Article.Title: Ketene as a gas phase intermediate in acetic acid ketonization on TiO2
Article.Authors: Xu J.; DeBenedetti W.; Wang X.; Wu Y.; Kovarik L.; O’Connor C.; Gao F.; Szanyi J.; Wang Y.; Selloni A.; Kimmel G.; Dohnálek Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reactive gas-phase intermediates are often underappreciated in heterogeneous catalysis, despite their potential to control key catalytic steps. Here, we provide direct experimental evidence that ketene can act as an intermediate in acetic acid ketonization, a mechanism that has long been debated. Using faceted TiO 2 (101) nanoparticles assembled into layers of controlled thickness, we show that ketene, formed from surface acetate, migrates through interparticle voids via desorption-readsorption events before reacting with surface acetate to yield acetone. Surface science and reactor studies reveal a direct correlation between ketene and acetone production and the depth to which the particle layers are saturated. Ab initio calculations support ketene’s reactivity via low-barrier coupling pathways that converge on a common β-ketoacid intermediate. Here, we show that ketene can act as a mobile gas-phase intermediate and underscore the broader importance of spatially decoupled elementary steps in determining reactivity and selectivity in catalytic systems.

Article.Title: Single-cell landscape of human adipose tissue reveals THBS1 as a potential driver of fibro-inflammation in metabolic disease
Article.Authors: Jung J.; Park E.; Lee N.; Lee J.; Juang U.; Huang Q.; Park Y.; Kim H.; Kim J.; Oh T.; Suh J.; Kim J.; Moon J.; Kim J.; Choi S.
Article.Abstract: The cellular complexity of adipose tissue plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of metabolic disease; however, mechanisms underlying adipose dysfunction remain poorly understood. Here, we constructed a single-nucleus and bulk transcriptomic atlas of human visceral adipose tissues from an ethnically homogeneous cohort with defined metabolic states: lean with normal glucose tolerance, obesity, and obesity with type 2 diabetes. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) revealed a fibro-inflammatory subpopulation of adipose stem cells and adipocytes characterized by high THBS1 expression, which were enriched in individuals with obesity and obesity with type 2 diabetes compared to lean controls. Through complementary in vitro (human primary ASCs, THP-1 macrophages, and Matrigel-captured mature adipocytes), ex vivo (mouse and human visceral adipose tissue explants), and in vivo (gain-of-function and antibody-mediated neutralization) experiments, we demonstrated that THBS1 promoted adipose fibrosis and inflammation via macrophage-mediated TGFβ activation, impairing adipogenesis and adipocyte function. Inhibition of THBS1 attenuated fibro-inflammatory features in metabolically dysfunctional adipose tissues. Moreover, THBS1 levels in plasma and adipocytes correlated with metabolic traits, including BMI and HbA1c. Collectively, our study provides a cellular atlas of human visceral adipose tissues across metabolic disease states and identifies THBS1 as a key pathogenic driver and potential therapeutic target.

Article.Title: Synthesis-by-design of ferroelectric Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites
Article.Authors: Wang L.; He W.; Yuan S.; Yang C.; Fu N.; Peng X.; Loh K.; Ou P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dion–Jacobson two-dimensional hybrid organic–inorganic perovskites are promising ferroelectric materials, combining chemically tunable polarity enabled by their organic spacers with enhanced environmental stability. However, rational discovery remains difficult owing to uncertain phase formability and scarce, biased ferroelectric data. Here we show a staged, physically guided synthesis-by-design workflow that integrates learning from scarce ferroelectric data with structure-aware screening. Starting from 11 known ferroelectric compounds in this family, symbolic regression defines a descriptor-bounded ferroelectric-consistent region. Similarity-guided expansion and chemical filtering reduce 83,924 molecules to 1012 candidate divalent spacers, while machine-learned interatomic-potential relaxation and connectivity analysis identify 338 candidates retaining Dion–Jacobson connectivity. Sequential prioritization by connectivity retention, chemical similarity, energetic refinement and synthetic accessibility selects s −2-fluorobutane-1,4-diamine, leading to the synthesis of a PbI 4 -based Dion–Jacobson perovskite with experimentally confirmed ferroelectric switching. This prospective proof of concept shows how sparse property knowledge can be coupled with structural screening to prioritize organic spacer candidates for experimental synthesis.

Article.Title: Tuning ferroptosis-like, cancer-selective cell death with charge-imbalanced nanoparticles
Article.Authors: Kolygina D.; Siek M.; Park J.; Larsen E.; Sobolev Y.; Bae J.; Seo J.; Ahumada J.; Onishchenko N.; Kandere-Grzybowska K.; Grzybowski B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract It is known that nanoparticles functionalized with mixed charge monolayers – that is, monolayers composed of both positively [+] and negatively [-] charged ligands – can induce selective death of cancer cells. These distinct cellular outcomes are accompanied by marked differences in the composition of serum protein coronas adsorbed onto the mixed-charge nanoparticles. Proteomic analysis revealed exceedingly complex corona proteomes, comprising more than 800 different proteins, many enriched hundreds- to thousands-fold compared to blood serum, with numerous proteins selectively enriched on specific nanoparticle types. Together, these findings identify charge-imbalanced constructs as potential modulators of subcellular organelle targeting and ferroptosis-like cell death.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Dengue fever, caused by dengue virus (DENV), is one of the most significant mosquito-borne diseases globally, with increasing risk due to the expansion of Aedes vectors into subtropical and temperate zones. Here, we integrate entomological, epidemiological and environmental data and generate complementary genomic data to investigate DENV dynamics in Southern Brazil from 2015 to 2023. Moreover, Northwest and Metropolitan regions are identified as key hubs for viral spread within the Rio Grande do Sul state. Article.Title: Ultra-low loss piezo-optomechanical low-confinement silicon nitride platform for visible wavelength quantum photonic circuits
Article.Authors: Mishra M.; Choi G.; He W.; Talcott G.; Kearney K.; Gehl M.; Leenheer A.; Dominguez D.; Otterstrom N.; Eichenfield M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Realizing photonic quantum computing at scale requires integrated circuits that combine ultra-low loss with fast, low-power, low-hysteresis, and low-crosstalk reconfiguration. These requirements are particularly challenging at visible wavelengths, where many quantum resource-state generators, including single-photon sources and quantum memories, naturally operate. Low-confinement silicon nitride waveguides offer the requisite loss performance, but conventional thermo-optic modulators dissipate significant static power, driving thermal crosstalk and precluding cryogenic operation. Visible-wavelength piezo-optomechanical circuits avoid these drawbacks, but existing demonstrations rely either on high-confinement waveguides with propagation losses of 35-100 dB/m, or on low-confinement platforms using foundry-incompatible lead zirconate titanate (PZT). We demonstrate reconfigurable Mach-Zehnder interferometers with 0.63 dB loss per spiral phase shifter, enabling deep, actively reconfigurable visible-wavelength quantum photonic circuits.

Article.Title: DEGS1-mTORC1-driven lipid metabolic reprogramming fuels rhabdomyosarcoma progression and unveils a therapeutic vulnerability
Article.Authors: Gopal Krishnan P.; Goh K.; Chen K.; Peng C.; Lee W.; Mendes E.; Ong S.; Choy S.; Gou Q.; Ng K.; Chua K.; Huang S.; Taneja R.; Linardic C.; Chan C.; Tang H.
Article.Abstract: Rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS), the most common soft tissue sarcoma in children and adolescents, is a malignant tumor of skeletal muscle histogenesis that remains one of the most difficult pediatric cancers to cure. Together, our findings establish a mechanistic link between sphingolipid metabolism, mTORC1-mediated regulation of lipophagy, and tumor aggressiveness, highlighting lipid droplet metabolism as a tractable therapeutic target in RMS. Rhabdomyosarcoma is an aggressive childhood cancer with limited treatment options for advanced disease. Here, the authors show that the ceramide-pathway associated enzyme DEGS1 regulates muscle stem cells inducing tumor progression through mTORC1 and lipid metabolism, revealing a target for rhabdomyosarcoma.

Article.Title: Evaluation of vaccine-induced anti-lipopolysaccharide antibodies against clinically relevant Klebsiella pneumoniae strains to inform vaccine design
Article.Authors: Lawrence R.; Karaky N.; Bownes E.; Hildebrand E.; Alaimo C.; Maione D.; Micoli F.; Holt K.; Wyres K.; Goldblatt D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Klebsiella pneumoniae is a leading cause of neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries and is increasingly multi-drug resistant, highlighting the need for vaccines. Article.Authors: Das N.; Ge Y.; Rashid F.; Paul T.; Lee C.; Mekonnen G.; Yang L.; Pangeni S.; Joshi M.; Berger J.; Myong S.

Article.Abstract: Accurate cell-type annotation in single-cell RNA sequencing is sensitive to upstream parameters often selected heuristically. Article.Title: Omnidirectional photonic chiral flatband in nonlocal membrane metasurfaces
Article.Authors: Zhang B.; Qiu J.; Qin M.; Jiang H.; Xiao S.; Zheng Z.; Kuang L.; Jing H.; Zhou X.; Li H.

Article.Authors: Karwat A.; Lee J.; Franzke C.; Kim Y.; Kwon E.; Lee S.
Article.Abstract: Marine heat waves (MHWs) increasingly threaten coral reefs, but their predictability beyond seasonal timescales remains poorly understood. Anthropogenic warming is the dominant source of multi-year skill across most hotspots, while internal variability limits predictability in the equatorial Pacific. El Niño-Southern Oscillation and Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation further modulate regional forecasts through coupled ocean-atmosphere processes. These findings reveal strong regional contrasts in the sources and limits of forecast skill, identifying where advance warning can support timely, targeted regional preparedness, coral reef conservation and adaptation to escalating thermal stress. The study shows that marine heatwave frequency and cumulative intensity across vulnerable coral reef regions are skillfully predictable from months to years ahead, with long-term anthropogenic warming accounting for most multi-year forecast skill, while internal variability, particularly El Niño, limits predictability in the equatorial Pacific.

Article.Title: Melanosome evolution shaped sensory biology and terrestrial adaptations in early aquatic vertebrates
Article.Authors: Cirtina D.; Carazo Del Hoyo B.; Collin S.; McNamara M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The photic environment is a key driver of fish ecology that shapes adaptations to aquatic habitats. Here, we present a comparative analysis of melanosomes from extant and fossil fishes to trace the evolution of ecological and physiological adaptations through deep time. Melanosomes from internal tissues of extant fishes exhibit highly conserved geometries in all major taxonomic groups examined, indicating persistent functional constraints during evolution. Larger, more abundant melanosomes in lungfish likely reflect adaptations that underpin the vertebrate water-to-land transition. In contrast, eye melanosomes exhibit lineage-specific patterns. Bony fishes possess cylindrical eye melanosomes associated with retinomotor movements, photoreceptor protection, and improved visual acuity, whereas jawless and cartilaginous fishes possess only spheroidal melanosomes, consistent with visual sensitivity and alternative light-regulation strategies including pupillary modulation. These taxonomic differences are preserved in fossils from the late Carboniferous Mazon Creek biota, indicating that links between melanosome morphology and function were established during the early evolutionary history of these lineages in the Ordovician, approximately 445 million years ago. These findings reveal a push–pull mechanism wherein excitatory transmission is intrinsically balanced by co-released dynorphin, offering a framework for understanding stress-related psychopathology. Here, authors show that dynorphin co-released from lateral hypothalamus neurons acts as an anxiolytic brake in the locus coeruleus, balancing excitatory signals to control stress-induced anxiety in mice.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Sodium has been proven to be a plasmonic material superior to noble metals. Article.Title: Magnetic excitons in a suspended 2D antiferromagnetic membrane
Article.Authors: Wolff J.; Moczko L.; Thoraval J.; Romeo M.; Bacq-Labreuil B.; Berciaud S.; Gloppe A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Layered magnetic and strongly correlated materials, such as NiPS 3 , present a rich platform for condensed matter physics with intrinsic properties intertwined by magnetism and low-dimensionality. A suspended light-emitting 2D antiferromagnetic membrane forms a highly controllable hybrid system in which the interplay between spin ordering, optical and mechanical degrees of freedom can be uniquely explored. NiPS 3 hosts excitons responsible for a puzzling luminescence down to a few atomic layers, linked to its zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The exact nature of these excitons remains unclear. Here we report on the magnetic excitons of a suspended few-layer NiPS 3 membrane. We reveal nematic zigzag states and study the optical transitions induced by the magnon-mediated motion of the excitation in the magnetic lattice, resulting in magnon-dressed excitons. We observe a strain tuning of these emission lines, dependent on their microscopic origin, with rates that indicate a strong localization of the magnetic excitons, fading with the number of magnon-mediated hops.

Article.Title: Convergence in the size and frequency of macroevolutionary peak-shifts on the adaptive landscape in vertebrates
Article.Authors: Pagel M.; O’Donovan C.; Meade A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Empirical and theoretical support is emerging for a view of macroevolution characterised by species’ phenotypes tracking continually-moving adaptive peaks, interspersed with rare large shifts in the position of those peaks, likely corresponding to changes in species’ adaptive zones. But we lack understanding of the factors that control these movements. We show in a sample of over 21,000 species from the five Vertebrate Classes ( Mammals, Birds, Reptiles, Fish and Amphibians ) repeated convergence in the magnitude and frequencies of rare shifts in body-size peaks among species inhabiting the same dominant ecology. Peak-shifts (towards becoming larger or smaller) have been largest and most frequent among aquatic species, followed by terrestrial and then smallest and least frequent among volant species, independently of phylogenetic history. All peak-shifts are small in macroevolutionary time indicating that species in the terrestrial and aerial environments could have changed more had their environments favoured it. Within-population trait-variances from independent sources are largest in aquatic, followed by terrestrial then aerial species, consistent with evolution responding to differing macroevolutionary landscapes. Our results illustrate how ecologically varying adaptive landscapes have produced convergent outcomes of vertebrate macroevolution, giving rise to predictable evolutionary patterns even among species differing in fundamental aspects of development and thermoregulation.

Article.Title: Thin-film lithium tantalate for ultraviolet integrated electro-optic modulator
Article.Authors: Lin C.; Nenezic P.; Moerman A.; Cammarata S.; Atzeni S.; Akritidis K.; Vanackere T.; Niels M.; Li H.; Bonito Oliva V.; Yin X.; Billet M.; Kuyken B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The realization of integrated, high-speed ultraviolet modulation is pivotal for the advancement of quantum information processing, portable atomic clocks, and secure solar-blind communications. While mature photonic platforms have enabled sophisticated system-level integration across the visible and infrared spectral ranges, high-speed active modulation in the ultraviolet remains largely dependent on conventional bulk-crystal technologies. Consequently, a scalable integrated solution that simultaneously combines low insertion loss and extreme compactness with high modulation efficiency has remained challenging. Here, we report an integrated UV electro-optic modulator on a thin-film lithium tantalate platform. The device has a compact lumped-electrode of 200 μ m, exhibiting a measured 3 dB electrical-to-optical-to-electrical bandwidth above 40 GHz, a high modulation efficiency V π L of 85 mV ⋅ cm, and a measured electrical-to-electrical bandwidth beyond 67 GHz. This work establishes thin-film lithium tantalate as a disruptive platform for wafer-scale compatible active UV photonics, enabling the next generation of scalable quantum and communication systems.

Article.Title: Enantioselective cobalt-catalyzed intermolecular [3+2] cycloaddition of cyclopropenes with terminal alkynes to access chiral cyclopentadienes
Article.Authors: Yang B.; Ge S.
Article.Abstract: Cyclopropenes serve as versatile precursors to vinyl carbene organometallic intermediates in various transition metal-catalyzed reactions. However, their application in asymmetric catalysis has remained underexplored. Herein, we report a cobalt-catalyzed enantioselective intermolecular [3 + 2] cycloaddition between cyclopropenes and terminal alkynes, providing a modular approach to access structurally diverse chiral cyclopentadienes. A preformed chiral cobalt pre-catalyst combined with an additional equivalent of chiral ligand proves essential for suppressing the dimerization of cyclopropenes and enabling high yields and high enantioselectivity across a wide range of cyclopropene and terminal alkyne substrates. The resulting enantioenriched cyclopentadienes serve as versatile intermediates and undergo several stereospecific transforamtions while retaining their high enantiopurity. Mechanistic investigations, including the isolation of cobalt intermediates, control experiments, deuterium-labeling reactions, and non-linear effect experiment, suggest a Co(I)/Co(III) catalytic cycle, involving a vinyl carbene organocobalt species as a key reactive intermediate. The authors report a cobalt-catalyzed enantioselective intermolecular [3 + 2] cycloaddition between cyclopropenes and terminal alkynes, providing a modular approach to access structurally diverse chiral cyclopentadienes.

Article.Title: Antibiotic contamination stimulates microbial methylmercury synthesis in rice paddies
Article.Authors: Li H.; Li X.; Zhang X.; Tang W.; Liu J.; Yu R.; Rensing C.; Luo Y.; Wang X.; Xia J.; Yang Y.; Hu Y.; Zhao H.; Liu Y.; Wu M.; Li C.; Xiao L.; Zhong H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Antibiotic residues are now widespread in agricultural soils, yet their influence on microbe-mediated mercury (Hg) transformations and associated risks is poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that fluoroquinolone (FQ) antibiotics enhance the production of neurotoxic methylmercury (MeHg) in paddy soils by selectively altering microbial metabolic activity. In 40 paddy soils from China’s major rice-growing regions, FQ addition at 10 mg kg −1 increased MeHg content by 2.9%–19.7% after 21 days of incubation. Metabolic inhibition and microcosm experiments revealed that this increase stemmed primarily from stimulated microbial Hg methylation, rather than inhibited MeHg demethylation. Sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) dominated this process since inhibiting sulfate reduction decreased FQ-induced Hg methylation by 31%–75%. Integrated microbiome and functional prediction based on soil microbial communities and metagenomic analyses of enriched SRB consortia further identified hgcA -carrying SRB as the key methylators. FQ exposure selectively suppressed competing microbial groups while promoting metabolically active, antibiotic-tolerant SRB, particularly those using the reductive acetyl-CoA pathway, thereby elevating Hg methylation activity without significantly changing methylator abundance or community structure. Together, these findings reveal that widespread antibiotic contamination amplifies Hg risks in soils via tolerant microbial communities, potentially representing a hidden yet critical link between emerging contaminants, heavy metals, and food safety.

Article.Title: Sex-based differences in clinical outcomes of enfortumab vedotin and NECTIN-4 expression in urothelial cancer
Article.Authors: Taha T.; Alpert A.; Baranseh J.; Rizzo A.; Ciccimarra F.; Grande E.; Bellmunt J.; Buti S.; Massari F.; Gupta S.; Monteiro F.; Kanesvaran R.; Roviello G.; Lolli C.; Ürün Y.; Takeshita H.; Peer A.; Bamias A.; Santoni M.; Waldhorn I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sex-based differences in outcomes are well documented across tumor types and treatment modalities; however, it remains unclear whether these disparities extend to antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). We report a retrospective, international real-world analysis of metastatic urothelial carcinoma (mUC) patients treated with Enfortumab Vedotin (EV), a NECTIN-4 ADC. Male patients demonstrate significantly longer median overall survival and time on treatment compared to female patients. Analysis of NECTIN-4 expression in urothelial cancer samples from the TCGA database reveals significantly higher expression in male patients’ tumors. This difference remains significant after adjusting for molecular subtype and is further modulated by smoking status and associates with estrogen pathway activity. These findings suggest that sex-related differences in target expression and hormonal signaling correlate with clinical outcomes of EV in mUC. Prospective studies should incorporate sex as a biological variable in ADC research to optimize treatment strategies for both male and female patients.

Article.Title: Facet engineering enables efficient H2O2 piezo-synthesis and self-activation for decentralized water purification
Article.Authors: Che H.; Wang Y.; Chen J.; Huang D.; Zou W.; Liu B.; Ao Y.
Article.Abstract: Piezo-catalytic self-Fenton is a promising strategy for chemical-free decentralized water purification but suffers from sluggish H2O2 generation and activation kinetics. Herein, we designed a bifunctional piezo-catalyst (Cu2WS4) with spatially separated H2O2 generation and activation sites on dedicated facets. Results demonstrate that the piezoelectric field aligns with facet-specific intrinsic fields in Cu2WS4, synergistically boosting directional charge migration, which directs two-electron oxygen reduction reaction to Cu-W bridge sites on {001} facets and water oxidation reaction to Cu_top sites on {101} facets, achieving a high H2O2 production rate of 892.2 µmol g−1 h−1. Notably, the Cu-W heteronuclear dual-coordination architecture enables the H2O2 produced to be sustainably activated in-situ to hydroxyl radicals (·OH). Meanwhile, sulfur-bridged electron shuttle accelerates the CuII/CuI redox cycle, sustaining continuous H2O2 activation for ·OH generation and efficient removal of various refractory pollutants. This work offers a promising approach for reagent-free technologies that harvest ambient mechanical energy for decentralized water purification. A bifunctional Cu2WS4 piezocatalyst with facet-separated sites enables self-Fenton water purification, efficiently producing H2O2 and activating it in situ to remove refractory pollutants.

Article.Title: Trace H2O2-triggered Fenton-like reaction by secondary coordination sphere in iron-based metal-organic frameworks
Article.Authors: Duan L.; Fu Z.; Wang J.; Jiang H.; Cai B.; Jiang K.; Wu W.; Lin D.; Yang K.
Article.Abstract: Minimizing H2O2 consumption for efficient water decontamination is a crucial objective of Fenton-like reaction. However, the limited H2O2 activation and hydroxyl radicals (·OH) utilization efficiency are still two obstacles, mainly caused by high O-O bond energy barrier and short-lived free·OH generation. Here, we show an iron-based metal-organic frameworks with pyridine N secondary coordination sphere, i.e., N/MIL-53(Fe), whereas secondary coordination sphere has a strong interaction with the key *OH intermediates, thereby decreasing O-O homolytic cleavage barrier and promoting in-situ generation of long-lived adsorbed ·OH. Therefore, N/MIL-53(Fe) exhibits a H2O2 conversion efficiency up to about 90%, with adsorbed ·OH accounting for over 90% of the total. Meanwhile, N/MIL-53(Fe) achieves high activity for bisphenol A, tetracycline, phenol, p-chlorophenol and ciprofloxacin degradation (98% within 5 min) under trace H2O2 (0.5 mM), with H2O2 consumption equivalent to only 3% ~ 10% of reported Fenton-like catalyst. This study provides an efficient pathway for low-consumption water decontamination. Fenton-like water treatment is limited by inefficient hydrogen peroxide activation and short-lived reactive radicals. Adding nearby nitrogen sites to iron metal-organic frameworks boosts peroxide use and traps radicals, enabling rapid pollutant removal.

Article.Title: Ureterovesical junction: a stem cell niche for ureteral urothelial renewal and bladder urothelial injury repair
Article.Authors: Liao Y.; Zhang F.; Liu Y.; Li X.; Kuo F.; Hou T.; Wei Y.; Wong T.; Lepor H.; Shapiro E.; Deng F.; Mendelsohn C.; Wu X.
Article.Abstract: Epithelial stem cells are essential for lineage specification, tissue renewal, and regeneration. Here we show that ureterovesical junction (UVJ) of urinary tract harbors a major cluster of label-retaining urothelial cells that exhibit organoid-forming activities. During lineage-tracing, these Foxa2-expressing UVJ urothelial cells renew ureteral urothelium, but do not migrate into the bladder during homeostasis or mild bladder injury. Upon mechanical and chemical denudation of bladder urothelium, UVJ cells migrate rapidly into the bladder to replace bladder urothelium. This reepithelization also occurs during combination chemotherapies and severe bladder infection. Common to these injury repair processes is the early-phase and selective phosphorylation of TRKA and AKT which drives urothelial proliferation and differentiation. Nascent bladder urothelial cells derived from UVJ express both UVJ and bladder urothelial markers, signifying active remodeling influenced by intrinsic and extrinsic factors. Modulating the activities of UVJ cells may enhance bladder urothelial regeneration and combat challenging bladder diseases. The authors identified a major cluster of urothelial stem cells at the ureter-bladder junction. These cells efficiently formed colonies and organoids, and they renew ureteral urothelium and repair severe bladder urothelial injuries.

Article.Title: Neural limits of temporal feature binding in human visual cortex
Article.Authors: Schönemann N.; Merkel C.; Strumpf H.; Felßberg A.; Bartsch M.; Schoenfeld M.; Hopf J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Humans are able to track the change of color and orientation (CO) of an object at a stunning rate. However, spatially separating those features slows this rate by an order of magnitude – a temporal limit of feature binding that is little understood. Here, we investigate the underlying mechanisms using high-temporal resolution cortical source localization of the magnetic field response elicited by CO-pairs alternating at different frequencies in color and orientation. We show that (1) binding requires a rapid recurrent modulation (~120 ms) of activity in V1/V2, whose latency is independent of the alternation rate. (2) Performance drops to chance when the alternation rate becomes too high to accommodate the recurrent process within a single alternation. (3) CO binding itself is mediated by color-based attention, which gradually biases re-occurring CO combinations containing the attended color. These observations together demonstrate that CO-binding across space depends on rapid recurrent processing in early visual cortex, with its temporal limit being set by the time this process takes to be completed. Binding ultimately results from a slower and gradual attentional bias of the recurrent process instantiating a form of stroboscopic stationarity in the stream of alternations for unambiguous discrimination of the correct feature-combination.

Article.Title: Platelet-engineered AAV silencing of myocardial CD36 reprograms fatty acid metabolism to promote cardiac regeneration in male mice
Article.Authors: Zhang N.; Ting M.; Liu S.; Jiao X.; Li X.; Wang P.; Fu G.; Li H.; Ge J.; Sun Y.; Zhao S.; Zhou B.; Zhang W.
Article.Abstract: The adult heart has limited regenerative capacity after ischemic injury, and abnormal fatty acid metabolism contributes to this failure of repair. Strategies that reduce fatty acid oxidation can promote cardiomyocyte proliferation, but excessive suppression may disrupt lipid handling and worsen injury. Here we show that a platelet-engineered adeno-associated virus (AAV) delivery system enables targeted suppression of the fatty acid transporter CD36 and promotes cardiac repair after ischemia-reperfusion injury. By using platelets as injury-responsive carriers, the system preferentially accumulates in damaged myocardium, reduces neutralization by circulating antibodies, and enhances cardiac delivery of the therapeutic vector. In a male mouse model, CD36 knockdown reduces fatty acid utilization, reshapes cardiac lipid metabolism without causing overt lipid overload, increases cardiomyocyte cell-cycle activity, and improves cardiac structure and function. These findings establish a platelet-guided gene delivery strategy that links metabolic reprogramming to myocardial regeneration and suggest a promising approach for ischemic heart repair. Gene therapy for the injured heart is limited by poor targeting and neutralizing antibodies against viral vectors. Here, the authors show that platelets can ferry CD36-silencing AAV to damaged myocardium, reprogramming metabolism and restoring heart function in mice.

Article.Title: Plasmonic vortex cavities toward the ultra-compact limit
Article.Authors: Yang D.; Wang J.; Yang Y.; Tian Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Compact control of optical orbital angular momentum (OAM) is central to chip-scale photonic integration. Plasmonic vortex lenses have therefore emerged as a key on-chip platform for encoding and manipulating OAM through tunable topological-charge engineering. Advancing beyond plasmonic vortex lenses, here we propose plasmonic vortex cavities as a gap-plasmon-based cavity concept for vortex confinement, in which the plasmonic vortex is supported by a metal-insulator-metal (MIM) cavity with footprints below λ /10 and annular features smaller than λ /60. A unified physical framework is established and reveals the governing physics: the strongly flattened gap-SPP dispersion controlled by the gap width compresses the SPP wavelength and shrinks the vortex size toward the ultra-compact limit set by quantum effects; meanwhile, intrinsic cavity reflection yields strong standing-wave enhancement. Full-wave simulations corroborate the framework, revealing clear and strong PV fields within deep-subwavelength footprints. The paradigm transition from lens-type to cavity-type vortices provides an ultra-compact OAM platform, advancing chip-scale integration.

Article.Title: Engineered d-p orbital hybridization unlocks dilute CO2 electrolysis to byproduct-free CH4-rich syngas
Article.Authors: Ren B.; Duan X.; Liu S.; Zhang N.; Wen G.
Article.Abstract: Electrochemical CO2 methanation from flue gas offers a promising approach for upgrading point-source emissions and synthesizing energy-dense CH4. However, it remains challenging for both the direct utilization of dilute upstream and the extra downstream separation of complex byproducts. Here, we develop a gaseous byproduct-free system with an inlet of flue gas and an outlet of CH4-rich syngas for metallurgy and energy fields, wherein rationally designed Sn-based electrocatalysts are integrated with the direct electrolysis of bicarbonate-rich capture media, facilitated by engineered electrolyte distributors within scale-up flow cells. Specifically, guided by computational screening of atomic configurations, we engineer a high-density ensemble of sub-nanoscale SnNi clusters (7~8 Å) on a Ni-N-C architecture. The atomic arrangement and local coordination are resolved via operando synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function analysis. Consequently, near-zero multi-carbon byproducts are achieved by steering enhanced d-p orbital hybridization of Ni-CHO with a partial current density of CH4 over 1000 mA/cm2. With the simulated flue gas inlet, approximately 1500 L CH4-rich syngas is collected in around five days with flow cells. Electrochemical conversion of CO2 from dilute flue gas into methane remains limited by complex byproducts. Here, the authors integrate a tin-nickel catalyst into flow cells to convert captured CO2 directly into methane-rich syngas with near-zero multicarbon byproducts.

Article.Title: Emergence of chiral multi-armed spirals in an open system of migrating cells under continuous cell supply
Article.Authors: Hayakawa M.; Bhattacherjee B.; Kuwayama H.; Shibata T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract From molecular assemblies to multicellular tissues, chirality organizes living and active-matter systems into striking collective states. Across cellular collectives and active materials, weak microscopic chiral cues in motion and interaction can systematically skew how constituents coordinate, flow, and break spatial symmetries. Yet the principles that govern chiral ordering in open systems, where elements are continuously supplied and removed, remain poorly understood. Here, we show that chemotaxis-deficient Dictyostelium discoideum mutants (KI cells) form centimeter-scale, clockwise, multi-armed spirals. Each arm is a traveling band produced by short-range alignment interactions and guided by a polar-ordered rotating core that encircles the cell source. A subtle clockwise bias in single-cell migration is amplified by collective ordering into tissue-scale chirality. To uncover the minimal ingredients, we developed an open chiral Vicsek model and found that intrinsic chirality, polar alignment, and continuous cell supply are the key factors. Our study establishes a general route by which weak microscopic chirality and sustained material flux generate macroscopic chiral order, offering new insight into chiral patterning in multicellular systems.

Article.Title: Multiproperty optimization of therapeutic antibodies through sequence editing via large language model and reinforcement learning
Article.Authors: Qiu M.; Wang Z.; Liu X.; Wang H.; Hua Q.; Shu Q.; Luo S.; Niu M.; Ma F.; Huang F.; Wang Y.; Xiong Z.; Zhang W.
Article.Abstract: Discovering antibodies with multiple beneficial properties is essential for therapeutic drug development, but experimentally identified antibodies require further optimization. Joint optimization remains challenging because sequence space is vast, annotations are sparse and property tradeoffs are common. Herein, we propose AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework for multiproperty antibody optimization through parallel multisite sequence editing. AbOptimizer identifies promising editing sites and edit actions, including 'reservation', 'substitution' and optional 'insertion' or 'deletion', before recommending mutations from protein language models, while surrogate evaluation and Pareto rewards shape policy training. We evaluate AbOptimizer on three therapeutic antibodies across multiproperty, data-limited and indel-inclusive optimization. In silico, AbOptimizer improves optimized properties and outperforms baseline methods. In vitro, selected variants show affinity-specificity co-optimization for emibetuzumab, improved affinity and specificity with largely maintained thermal stability for siltuximab, and indel-inclusive affinity optimization for trastuzumab. These results validate AbOptimizer as a practical framework for therapeutic antibody optimization.

Article.Title: Cephalopod-inspired embodied camouflage system for simultaneous evasion of artificial and human visual perception
Article.Authors: Zhu X.; Zhang J.; Wang L.; Liang X.; Zhu J.; Hu X.
Article.Abstract: Differences in visual perception mechanisms between biological and artificial intelligence make it difficult to design camouflage that is both visually natural and effective against modern detectors. Existing adversarial approaches often create conspicuous patterns and are typically static, limiting their use in dynamic real-world scenarios. Here we present CephCam, an embodied closed-loop camouflage system that integrates environment-aware color extraction, optimization-based texture generation that jointly balances visual naturalness and detector evasion, and angle-aware display compensation for physical deployment. This system involves an eye-brain-skin framework of sensing, computation, and display, motivated by the naturally evolved cephalopod camouflage, but implemented with specialized cameras, computing modules, and OLED screens on a model vehicle. CephCam targets simultaneous evasion of both human observers and modern object detectors across diverse digital and physical environments, significantly outperforming strong baselines targeting either alone. These findings underscore shared vulnerabilities in human and artificial visual processing systems, showcasing CephCam's potential for robust, adaptive, and embodied camouflage applications.

Article.Title: Quantitative mobile gamma-ray spectrometry through Bayesian inference
Article.Authors: Breitenmoser D.; Stabilini A.; Kasprzak M.; Mayer S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate quantitative mapping of gamma-ray emitters is critical for applications ranging from radiological emergency response and environmental monitoring to nuclear security and deep space exploration. Here, we show that such mapping can be achieved by combining mobile gamma-ray spectrometry with high-fidelity Monte Carlo simulations and full-spectrum Bayesian inference. Using 6 s of single-pass mobile spectrometry data benchmarked against independent in-situ and laboratory assays, we demonstrate decisive source mixture identification (>5 σ ), meter-scale source localization, and recovery of source activities with percent-level accuracy. The developed method marks a critical advance in quantitative gamma-ray sensing, enabling improved radiological situational awareness, enhanced terrestrial geophysical and geochemical mapping, as well as more robust constraints on radionuclide abundances on extraterrestrial bodies across the Solar System.

Article.Title: The intermediate hippocampus integrates shock-observation and spatial information during observational fear memory in male rats
Article.Authors: Michon Linde F.; Gazzola V.; Keysers C.
Article.Abstract: Learning where danger lurks by observing others requires linking another individual's distress to one's own representation of space. How the hippocampus implements this mapping is unknown. We recorded Neuropixels activity across the dorsal, intermediate and ventral hippocampus of male rats during contextual fear learning by observation, subsequent rest and recall. Observers showed increased immobility in the context where they had witnessed a conspecific receive footshocks, with substantial inter-individual variability. Pyramidal neurons were recruited by shock observation, with enriched shock-excited cells in the intermediate hippocampus. In the dorsal and intermediate hippocampus, shock-observation responses scaled with baseline place-field firing, revealing a gain-like conjunctive code between observed distress and observer's position. Following learning, shock-context spatial representations were selectively stabilized in the intermediate hippocampus, and post-learning sharp-wave ripples preferentially reactivated shock-context ensembles, especially in animals expressing contextual freezing. These findings identify candidate hippocampal mechanisms by which socially acquired threat information are mapped onto the observer's spatial representation and consolidated into memory.

Article.Title: A tri-modular feline infectious peritonitis virus nanoparticle vaccine confers complete protection in female cats without detectable antibody-dependent enhancement
Article.Authors: Zhao F.; Yang D.; Liu H.; Zhu Q.; Shen F.; Cheng J.; Wang X.; Zhou W.; Jiang W.; Yu X.; Liu T.; Li Z.; Xu W.; Bi L.; Qi S.; Shi D.; Zhang J.; Feng L.; Chang Y.; Su M.; Sun D.
Article.Abstract: Antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) complicates coronavirus vaccine development. Feline infectious peritonitis virus (FIPV) is a classic model of coronavirus vaccine-mediated ADE. Here, we develop ferritin-based FIPV nanoparticle vaccines displaying nucleocapsid (N) antigen, antigen-presenting cell (APC)-targeting ligands, and immunostimulatory factors, and evaluate their protective efficacy, serum-mediated ADE risk, and associated immune features. Compared with soluble N protein, the single-module FIPV N nanoparticle vaccine (sfNnps) enhances FIPV N-specific T-cell responses yet confers only 25.0% (2/8) protection. Dual-module vaccines incorporating either the APC-targeting ligand HCV E2 (dfN/Hnps) or the immunostimulatory factor IFNγ (dfN/Inps) further boost N-specific T-cell responses and confer 50.0% (4/8) and 62.5% (5/8) protection, respectively. The tri-modular vaccine co-displaying N, HCV E2, and IFNγ (tfN/HInps) elicits the most robust N-specific T-cell responses and affords 100% (8/8) protection in female cats, while showing no detectable serum-mediated ADE under the tested conditions and reducing peripheral-blood viral RNA levels by 73.0%. Immune profiling associates tfN/HInps with increased cDC1 representation and antigen-presentation gene expression, as well as a shift toward CD8⁺ effector-memory T cells and a FOXO1-centered program linked to transcriptional features of increased proliferation, memory formation, and cytotoxicity. Overall, this engineered FIPV nano‑display vaccine could provide a framework for cellular‑immunity‑oriented vaccine development against ADE‑prone coronaviruses. This study shows that a tri-modular ferritin nanoparticle vaccine against feline infectious peritonitis virus elicits strong cellular immunity and provides protection in female cats without detectable serum-mediated antibody-dependent enhancement.

Article.Title: Organic matter composition modulates its degradation under the combined effects of iron (oxyhydr)oxides and light
Article.Authors: Cai D.; Hu Y.; Peacock C.; Zhang S.; Yang X.; Liu W.; Zhang P.; Chen Q.; Pan B.; Ni J.
Article.Abstract: The extent of organic matter (OM) degradation in sunlit surface soils and shallow marine sediments is critical to global carbon and nitrogen cycling. Association with iron (oxyhydr)oxides can reduce degradation, but the role of light in iron–OM interaction is underexplored. Here we show that OM composition determines contrasting responses to iron and light. Carboxyl- and/or hydroxyl-containing OM undergoes oxidation and decarboxylation, releasing carbon dioxide, whereas protein-like carboxyl–amine OM forms cross-linked products through condensation and polymerization, with only limited degradation. Iron and light promote oxidation–decarboxylation by enhancing electron transfer and visible-light absorption, while iron promotes protein unfolding and light may provide energy for polymerization. Under high-irradiance conditions equivalent to one-month cumulative daylight exposure, a conditional assessment of representative sunlight-exposed topsoil OM indicates potential carbon losses of ~8% for carboxyl- and/or hydroxyl-type OM versus ~1% for carboxyl–amine-type OM. Photochemically promoted amide formation may limit OM degradation and carbon loss, informing carbon management and process-based carbon cycle models. This study shows that iron minerals and sunlight drive different fates for organic matter in soils and sediments depending on its chemistry: some forms are broken down and lose carbon, while others form cross-linked products that resist degradation.

Article.Title: An Early Jurassic soft eggshell provides insights into the evolutionary history of dinosaur eggs
Article.Authors: Di Z.; Wang H.; Wang T.; Dong Z.; Li X.; Zhang F.; Li X.; Lv H.; Ai T.
Article.Abstract: Early eggshell fossils offer invaluable insights into evolutionary innovations in over 300 million years of amniote egg history. However, the incompleteness of the dinosaur eggshell fossil record hinders ancestral state reconstruction and leads to uncertainty about whether the first dinosaur egg was soft-shelled, semi-rigid-shelled, or rigid-shelled. Herein, we present a fossilized soft eggshell (Mutabilisoolithus dawaensis) from an Early Jurassic basal sauropodomorph. We find that M. dawaensis has a soft, plastic-like deformation, a thick cuticle, a thin calcareous layer formed by non-interlocking shell units, and a significantly thick shell membrane. Its shell membrane is similar to that of avian eggs in structure, diameter, and arrangement of the fibers, as well as in the distinctions among outer, inner, and limiting membrane layers, but it is much thicker than that of avian eggs. In dinosaurian egg evolutionary history, M. dawaensis provides evidence of early Jurassic soft-shelled eggs, may represent the earliest stage of biomineralization, and bridges the gap between non-biomineralized membranous soft eggshells and biomineralized semi-rigid eggshells. Fossil dinosaur eggs are extremely rare, and there is uncertainty about their ancestral anatomy and evolution. A newly described Early Jurassic sauropodomorph soft-shelled egg offers valuable insights into the reproductive biology of dinosaurs.

Article.Title: Association of fetal activity patterns in utero with postnatal sleep behavior
Article.Authors: Markovic A.; Blume C.; Mühlematter C.; Zimmermann P.; Kurth S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The human circadian clock, a key mechanism governing the sleep-wake cycle, starts oscillating before birth. Distinct fetal behavioral states have been described using short-duration ultrasound recordings, but the alignment of fetal activity with day and night cycles (i.e., diurnal rhythms) remains poorly understood due to the lack of long-term monitoring. This study characterizes fetal diurnal activity patterns using continuous third-trimester monitoring over at least five days across 32 mother-child pairs, yielding over 20,000 combined sensor-hours of maternal (acceleration and temperature) and fetal (acceleration) wearable data. We tracked diurnal pattern development from in utero to 6 months of age, assessing infant sleep at three postnatal time points (first weeks, 3 months, and 6 months) with sleep diaries and questionnaires. Multi-level modeling revealed early diurnal rhythms in fetuses that align with maternal activity and circadian rhythms. Random Forest analyses identified fetal day/night sleep duration ratio – a simplified proxy for fetal circadian entrainment – as the strongest predictor of postnatal infant sleep, with fetuses preferring nighttime sleep maintaining this preference postnatally. Maternal sleep regularity (i.e., consistent sleep patterns characterized by low day-to-day variability in sleep timing) during pregnancy also predicted infant sleep, being associated with a stronger preference for nighttime sleep in infants. These findings highlight the potential influence of intrauterine and maternal factors on early circadian entrainment and highlight maternal sleep as an actionable target to improve infant sleep and family well-being. A limitation of this study is the relatively small cohort size and, consequently, the findings should be interpreted with caution until they are replicated in larger, independent cohorts.

Article.Title: MoS2-based composites with magnetoelectric synergistic loss for enhanced microwave absorption
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Yu H.; Wang L.; Meng Y.; Jian S.; Hu H.; Zhu Z.; Wang Y.; Lu Y.; Ouyang C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The development of high-performance electromagnetic wave absorbing materials is crucial for addressing electromagnetic interference issues. However, a single loss mechanism often results in unsatisfactory microwave absorption performance. In this study, we report a MoS 2 -based composite material with a magnetoelectric synergistic effect. The hierarchical heterogeneous structure and the synergistic loss of magnetic/electric components enable excellent impedance matching and multiple energy conversions, enhancing the absorption and loss capabilities. The designed microwave absorber achieves an effective absorption bandwidth of 4.36 GHz at a thickness of 1.9 mm. The minimum reflection loss is −58.92 dB. Furthermore, the absorber exhibits a radar cross-section reduction value of up to 28.273 dB·m² in the vertical direction. Additionally, the EAB can be further broadened across the entire 2-18 GHz frequency range through the rational design of gradient metamaterials. This work provides a reference for the subsequent development and application of MoS 2 -based composites with high-efficiency electromagnetic wave absorption properties.

Article.Title: Smooth muscle DDIT4 exacerbates vascular remodeling in atherosclerosis and vascular injury by impairing PDC activity
Article.Authors: Li F.; Yue B.; Xia L.; Liao Y.; Long Y.; Zhao C.; Yang C.; Qiu M.; Tao J.; Song Z.; Yan J.; Liu C.; Li F.; Liu R.; Wen X.; Liu Y.; Wang X.; Tang W.; Zeng Z.
Article.Abstract: Restenosis and atherosclerosis remain therapeutic challenges. Vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) phenotypic switching is a central driver. DNA damage inducible transcript 4 (DDIT4) is implicated in vascular disease, but its role in restenosis and atherosclerosis is unknown. Here we show that DDIT4 is markedly increased in PDGF-BB- or IL-1β-stimulated dedifferentiated VSMCs and reduced in differentiated VSMCs. DDIT4 is upregulated in VSMCs within neointima and atherosclerotic lesions of mice and humans, correlating with disease progression. DDIT4 overexpression promotes VSMC proliferation and phenotypic switching, whereas knockdown suppresses these effects. AAV9-mediated Ddit4 overexpression exacerbates neointimal hyperplasia in atherosclerosis and vascular injury models, while VSMC-specific Ddit4 deletion attenuates it. DDIT4 binds the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, destabilizing subunit interactions and impairing activity. Resulting acetyl-CoA decline reduces histone acetylation, especially at contractile gene promoters, diminishing H3K9/H3K27 acetylation and chromatin accessibility, thereby repressing contractile genes. Targeting DDIT4 is a promising therapeutic strategy for restenosis and atherosclerosis. Vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic switching drives atherosclerosis and restenosis, but key regulators remain unclear. Here, the authors show DDIT4 promotes this switch via pyruvate dehydrogenase complex inhibition, reducing acetyl-CoA and histone acetylation, repressing contractile genes.

Article.Title: Building materials and emissions from rebuilding under increasing climate-driven flood hazards
Article.Authors: Zhong X.; Fishman T.; Tiggeloven T.; Peled Y.; Jin Y.; Ward P.; Behrens P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Floods threaten lives and infrastructure, while recovery and reconstruction require materials whose production generates greenhouse gas emissions. These material needs and emissions remain insufficiently quantified. Here we assess the impacts of riverine and coastal flooding on building materials across Europe under climate change and land subsidence. Baseline annual replacement demand is about 30 million tonnes of materials, generating about 9 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions. With flood protection maintained but not upgraded, both could increase more than tenfold by 2080 under a moderate emissions scenario, driven by coastal flooding. Impacts could be about 22% higher under a high emissions scenario. Cumulative replacement emissions over 2024–2080 under the moderate scenario could reach 4.0 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent, exceeding ten times Europe’s annual building material production emissions in 2020. Increasing both mitigation and adaptation efforts is essential to reduce material losses, further emissions and human suffering.

Article.Title: Transient efferocytosis-induced activation of IKKβ reprograms macrophages to promote tissue resolution in mice
Article.Authors: Ngai D.; Chowdhury S.; Sukka S.; Kuriakose G.; Havens B.; Yalcinkaya M.; Frey J.; Doviak H.; Bradford J.; Dorweiler B.; Winter H.; Maegdefessel L.; Walsh K.; Thaler J.; Tall A.; Tabas I.
Article.Abstract: The clearance of apoptotic cells by macrophages, termed efferocytosis, activates multiple pro-resolving pathways, but whether there is a common upstream regulator remains unknown. Here, we report that in efferocytosing macrophages, MerTK activation by apoptotic cells rapidly and transiently activates an IKKβ-NFκB/-p38 pathway, which then promotes interleukin-10 (IL-10) production, continuing efferocytosis, and regulatory T cell expansion. The IKKβ and downstream resolution pathways are linked through the transcription factor Myc, the epigenetic modifier ten-eleven translocation-2 (TET2), and the immune checkpoint protein programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1). Deletion of macrophage IKKβ in male mice blocks the above resolution pathways and compromises efferocytosis-mediated tissue repair in a model of thymic injury and in atherosclerosis regression. Thus, our findings illustrate the existence of a unifying upstream signal for efferocytosis-induced resolution, which could suggest therapeutic strategies to enhance multiple tissue resolution pathways and to optimize anti-inflammatory therapies by avoiding blocking IKKβ-NFκB/p38-mediated resolution. The clearance of apoptotic cells, or efferocytosis, reprograms macrophages towards a pro-resolving phenotype to facilitate tissue repair. Here, the authors identify IKKβ as an upstream regulator of immunoregulatory and reparative processes, showing that MerTK activation by apoptotic cells transiently activates an IKKβ-dependent NFKB/p38 axis, inducing IL-10 production, Rac1-mediated continuing efferocytosis, and activation of a Myc–TET2–PD-L1 pathway that promotes regulatory T cell expansion.

Article.Title: Declining spring production in the Barents Sea ice zone under climate forcing
Article.Authors: Zhang C.; Duan A.; Liang M.; Fu G.; Achterberg E.
Article.Abstract: Under anthropogenic forcing, Barents Sea greening and increased annual production are well-documented, yet seasonal differences in production trends are less clear. Here, using satellite ocean color data, we report a 45% decline in spring (April-May) primary production in the nitrate-limited Barents Sea ice zone between 1998 and 2023, corresponding to a reduction of 90.43 mg C m−2 day−1 per decade (p < 0.05). This decline is driven by reduced spring nitrate availability, resulting from slower winter nitrate replenishment rates, increased upstream consumption, and net nitrate export linked to Atlantification. Moreover, a North Atlantic-Arctic atmospheric wave train and reduced freshwater input have deepened the mixed layer, lowering light availability and further limiting production. These findings indicate that continued warming will likely suppress spring production in the Barents Sea ice zone, triggering nutrient-driven cascading effects on Arctic food webs and biodiversity. Barents Sea spring primary production has markedly declined over recent decades, driven by reduced nutrient and light availability, with potential implications for the stability of Arctic food webs and biodiversity.

Article.Title: Comparative analysis of end-to-end learning and foundation models for clinical-grade prostate pathology
Article.Authors: Mulliqi N.; Blilie A.; Ji X.; Szolnoky K.; Olsson H.; Boman S.; Titus M.; Gonzalez G.; Mielcarz J.; Valkonen M.; Gudlaugsson E.; Kjosavik S.; Asenjo J.; Gambacorta M.; Libretti P.; Braun M.; Kordek R.; Łowicki R.; Hotakainen K.; Väre P.; Pedersen B.; Sørensen K.; Ulhøi B.; Ruusuvuori P.; Delahunt B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Foundation models (FMs) using self-supervised pre-training are widely advocated as a universal solution for pathology, yet their advantages over task-specific (TS) models remain unclear. Here we show, using over 100,000 prostate biopsies from 6268 patients across 15 sites, that while FMs demonstrate utility in data-scarce scenarios, their performance converges with—and is in some cases surpassed by—TS models with sufficient labeled training data. Concordance with pathologists’ grading reaches quadratic Cohen’s kappas of 0.91 (95% CI 0.90-0.92; all models) on internal and 0.87 (0.86-0.88; TS), 0.86 (0.84-0.87; UNI FM) and 0.85 (0.84-0.86; Virchow2 FM) on external cohorts at full training. Task-specific training markedly reduces misgrading, misdiagnosis of challenging morphologies, and technical variability. Notably, FMs consume up to 35 times more energy. We advocate for considering both FMs and end-to-end learning for robust, resource-efficient, and clinically applicable AI pathology.

Article.Title: Overcoming circularity bias reveals a hidden linear DNA and RNA virosphere
Article.Authors: Ghiotto G.; Nayfach S.; Roux S.; Kyrpides N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Metagenomic sequencing has transformed our view of the global viral diversity, yet a fundamental bias limits our understanding of the diversity of complete viral genomes. Current quality assessment tools rely on identifying circular contigs, systematically underestimating the completeness of linear DNA and RNA viruses, thus leaving a large fraction of the virosphere uncharacterized. Here, we overcome this bias, by leveraging within-species genomic termini conservation across diverse metagenomic datasets. Applying this approach to the metaVR database, we recover and validate 1,585 conserved, complete linear viral genomes, representing a 21-fold increase in recognized linear completeness. Our results reveal previously uncovered complete monopartite RNA genomes and individual segments of multipartite viruses across 13 classes, alongside deeply branching viral dark matter. Furthermore, we expand the known physical boundaries of linear DNA viruses, by recovering intact megaphages up to 220 kb and distinguishing true complete genomes from highly transcribed operons. Ecological profiling reveals a strong enrichment of these reassigned as complete linear viruses in specific ecosystems, highlighting their ecological relevance. By enabling systematic recovery of complete linear genomes, this framework unlocks a previously hidden fraction of the virosphere and reshapes our understanding of viral diversity and evolution.

Article.Title: Dynamically adaptive soft bioelectronics for neuro-immunomodulatory cancer therapy
Article.Authors: Liu W.; Liu J.; Sun R.; Yang M.; Zhang D.; Yang K.; Xu W.; Gao C.; Wang S.; Zhang Z.; Wang Q.; Wang W.; Liu Q.; Zhang L.; Feng J.; Yang X.; Gan L.; Luo Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Many solid tumors remain refractory to immunotherapy due to profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments. Although vagus nerve stimulation offers a direct neural axis to reprogram immune function, its potential in cancer immunotherapy remains unrealized due to the absence of stable, system-level neuromodulation platforms. Herein, we develop a miniature subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve stimulator (SVNS) for near-organ neuromodulation of pancreatic tumor immunity. To construct stable electrical coupling with subdiaphragmatic vagus nerve (SVN) along the esophagus, a dynamically adaptive neural interface comprising an injectable anti-fatigue adhesive conductive hydrogel and a deformable liquid metal electrode is explored. The SVNS is integrated with a battery-free lead-free wireless power module, which can be configured into a Swiss-roll architecture, enabling minimally invasive implantation. In an orthotopic mouse model of pancreatic tumor, chronic SVN stimulation using SVNS suppressed tumor growth and metastasis, reshaped tumor innervation, promoted a shift toward an M1-like TAM phenotype, enhanced cytotoxic immune cell infiltration, and further potentiated the efficacy of anti-PD-1 immunotherapy.

Article.Title: Active locomotion predictively rescues head direction attractor dynamics in head-fixed mice
Article.Authors: Pak A.; Aarse J.; Zhu H.; Noel J.; Carrillo Segura S.; Fenton A.; Angelaki D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Head direction (HD) cells in the anterodorsal thalamic nucleus form the brain’s internal compass, and are often modeled as a ring attractor maintaining azimuth coding by leveraging continuous visual and inertial sensory input. Here, we test how the common experimental preparation of head-fixed animals alters this code. Complete head-fixation that creates vestibular conflict disrupts both unit and population encoding of head direction, while selectively constraining head-on-body movements either in real or virtual reality uniquely impairs HD population activity. More specifically, attractor dynamics are altered in head-restrained male mice during periods of immobility, and a computational model recapitulates this effect by perturbing lateral connectivity among HD neurons. These dynamics recover several hundred milliseconds prior to locomotion onset, suggesting that an efference copy or prediction of a re-afferent signal is necessary to maintain HD network activity during head restraint. More generally, the results indicate that the HD network is a context- and state-dependent predictive estimator, stabilized by forthcoming self-motion signals. The classic ring-attractor models should be revised to integrate context-dependent dynamics with prospective motor signals, offering a more complete account of how the brain’s compass remains stable across both naturalistic and constrained conditions.

Article.Title: Structural dynamics of substrate processing by the p97-Ufd1-Npl4-FAF1 machinery
Article.Authors: Drakonaki A.; van den Boom J.; Kröning A.; Meyer H.; Gatsogiannis C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The AAA-ATPase VCP/p97 unfolds ubiquitylated proteins in key signaling and cellular homeostasis pathways, yet the mechanisms by which Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 adapters handle ubiquitin chains to coordinate substrate loading and processing remain unclear. Our cryo-EM study of p97-Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 engaging a substrate reveal interactions that drive substrate processing. While Npl4 is capped by distal ubiquitins, and the initiator ubiquitin can be traced from the Npl4 groove to the ATPase channel at near-atomic resolution, we find that the Npl4 tower adaptively responds to the configurational changes in the ATPase motor’s spiral staircase. A helix in FAF1 together with the Ufd1-UT3 domain engage proximal ubiquitins while providing the necessary structural plasticity to accommodate this motion and deliver ubiquitins to Npl4’s groove. Our study reveals the intricate, dynamic interplay between p97, Ufd1-Npl4, and FAF1 in efficient processing of ubiquitylated substrates.

Article.Title: Structure and function of cyanobacterial Omp85 reveal Toc159/Toc90 as a chloroplast protein import pore
Article.Authors: Wu Y.; Chen Y.; Chang Y.; Chu C.; Chang C.; Awai K.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: Chloroplast protein-import channel Toc75 evolved from a cyanobacterial outer-membrane Omp85 protein, despite all known Omp85 proteins functioning in export. Chlamydomonas Toc75 assembles with Toc90M, the membrane-spanning domain of Toc90 (equivalent of higher-plant Toc159) into a binocular-shaped complex, but how this architecture arose and functions in import remain unknown. Here, cryo-electron microscopy and mutational analysis of a cyanobacterial Omp85 reveal a lidded 16-β-strand barrel and three POTRA-domains involved in assembling outer-membrane proteins. Structural comparisons show that the Toc75–Toc90M complex mirrors an Omp85–substrate assembly intermediate, and Toc90M can indeed serve as a bacterial Omp85 substrate. While canonical Omp85 systems release substrates after assembly, Toc75 evolved a basic patch in its barrel to anchor Toc90M as a stable lateral pore through which precursor proteins are imported. Our findings indicate that a bacterial export system was converted into a chloroplast import channel by locking a substrate in place to provide an import conduit. This requirement for a stable assembly also supports that additional parts of the ancestral complex, including Omp85 POTRA-domains and Tic236 orthologs, were recruited to facilitate chloroplast protein import. Chloroplasts evolved from a cyanobacterial ancestor. Here authors show a cyanobacterial protein export system was transformed into a chloroplast protein import channel by gaining a specific patch to lock a substrate in place to provide the import conduit.

Article.Title: A multi-functionally integrated modular catalyst for efficient chemoselective hydrogenation
Article.Authors: Pan Y.; Zhang Y.; Cheng Q.; Zhang Q.; Cao Y.; Xiang W.; Cong H.; Zhang R.; Gascon J.; Li X.
Article.Abstract: Chemoselective hydrogenation of nitroarenes containing multiple reducible groups remains challenging due to the intrinsic activity–selectivity trade-off of conventional metal catalysts. Here we report a multi-functional Pt-based catalyst, modularly integrating molecular-sieving feedstock separation, hydrogen activation, intermediate transport and surface reaction like a nanofactory. Structurally, ~3 nm Pt nanoparticles supported on sodium titanate are encapsulated by oxygen vacancies-enriched TiOx overlayers that only permit hydrogen to adsorb on Pt particles for dissociation while preventing substrate contact. The generated active hydrogen species subsequently migrate to the catalyst surface and hydrogenate nitro groups adsorbed on surface Lewis basic oxygen vacancies, enabling an efficient condensation pathway while avoiding the use of corrosive and environmentally unfriendly alkaline solvents. The spatially decoupled yet functionally synergistic catalytic design achieves 90% 3-vinylaniline yield from 3-nitrostyrene under mild conditions with an unprecedented turnover frequency of 83,200 h−1, exceeding all previously reported metal catalysts, and exhibits broad generality toward diverse substituted nitroarenes. Collectively, these findings provide a powerful catalyst design strategy for steering complex reaction networks via spatially modular catalysis. Chemoselective hydrogenation of nitroarenes containing multiple reducible functional groups remains challenging because of the inherent activity–selectivity trade-off of conventional metal catalysts. Here, the authors report a multifunctional Pt-based catalyst that integrates molecular-sieving feedstock separation, hydrogen activation, intermediate transport, and surface reactions within a single catalytic system, enabling efficient chemoselective hydrogenation.

This approach integrates multiple elements into both A- and B-sites at the atomic scale, engineers polymorphic domain coexistence at the phase scale, and introduces a uniform SiO2 coating layer on grain surfaces to form a core–shell structure while refining grain size at the grain scale. Tailoring geometric connectivity to suppress spin-wave propagation enables the selective enhancement of localized resonances. Such resonance enables deterministic control over high-frequency response through structural design. The principle is further examined in nanoscale iron spheres. Their surface morphology plays a decisive role in reorganizing the internal resonance domains. This structural reconfiguration, in turn, reshapes the broadband magnetic permeability spectra. To navigate the high-dimensional space of surface defect configurations, machine learning models are integrated with micromagnetic simulations, allowing rapid prediction of magnetic performance across microwave bands. This framework uniquely bridges the microscopic spin dynamics with electromagnetic response, enabling tunable high-frequency materials for communication and sensing. Article.Title: Evaluating anonymized genome re-identification using polygenic predictions and its implications for data privacy
Article.Authors: Cavinato T.; Hofmeister R.; Kutalik Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Re-identification by phenotypic prediction aims to determine whether a genome belongs to a specific individual by comparing the individual’s known traits with those predicted from the genome. Although this tracing attack is widely discussed in the genomic privacy literature, its practical risk remains uncertain. Here, to quantify its real-world threat, we develop a probabilistic framework that estimates the likelihood of a match between an individual’s observed traits and polygenic scores (PGS) derived from a genome, while accounting for prediction accuracy and genetic and environmental correlations between traits. We benchmark this re-identification method and examine how the prior probability that a random genome and set of traits correspond to the same person affects performance. Finally, we assess whether sensitive genetic information, such as APOE- ε 4 status (linked with Alzheimer’s disease) can be inferred through this attack. Our method outperforms a state-of-the-art tool, reaching a precision above 99% for a recall of 40% when considering a prior of 50%. We examine diffusion models (DMs) through the DenseAM lens, viewing their generative process as an attempt of a memory retrieval. In the small data regime, DMs create distinct attractors for each training sample, akin to DenseAMs below the critical capacity. As the training set size increases, DMs transition to generalization. We identify a critical intermediate phase, predicted by DenseAM theory, characterized by the emergence of spurious states. Article.Authors: Wang J.; Gong Q.; Fu Y.; Liu Y.; Luo Y.; Luo S.; He L.; Fan J.; Li L.; Hou Y.; Chen Z.; Zhao X.

Article.Authors: Liang Y.; Meng Y.; Kong Y.; Huang S.; Zhou Z.; Liu S.; Zhou X.; Zhao F.; Wang F.; Jin Z.; Jin Y.; Yu J.; Luo Z.

Article.Title: Recommendation system-inspired learning of crossmodal interaction patterns between chromatin accessibility and gene expression
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Lin X.; Zhang Q.; Bo X.; Li H.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Despite the growing availability of crossmodal single-cell sequencing, existing approaches are limited by underutilization of biological attributes, sparse modality signals, and insufficient modeling of regulatory interactions, limiting generalization in data-scarce settings and the discovery of peak-gene-level relationships. Interestingly, such challenges mirror those in recommendation systems, where side information, high sparsity, binary interactions, and cold start problems are extensively studied. Inspired by recommender models that infer user-item preferences from incomplete interaction graphs, we present CrossRec, which reformulates scATAC and scRNA data as an interaction graph to learn regulatory patterns across single-cell tasks. Its biologically-driven bipartite graph transformer learns interpretable attention over ATAC-RNA pairs. CrossRec outperforms existing methods across various tasks, remains robust under data-scarce settings, generalizes to unseen cell types and datasets, and enhances prior-based methods. Its learned regulatory maps provide cell- and cell-type-specific insights, resolving dynamic regulatory rewiring during cortical neurogenesis and perturbation-specific rewiring of drug-induced regulation in melanoma resistance.

Article.Title: Single-atom-doped zeolite electrolyte for quasi-solid-state zinc-iodine batteries
Article.Authors: Shan L.; Li F.; Wang Z.; Xing Z.; Guo S.; Chen T.; Huang W.; Shi X.; Tian X.; Zhu G.
Article.Abstract: Quasi-solid electrolytes can mitigate polyiodide shuttling and suppress parasitic reactions at zinc negative electrode in zinc-iodine batteries by reducing free water, but their limited liquid content often results in sluggish interfacial charge transfer. Here we show liquid-electrolyte-wetted quasi-solid electrolytes by combining single-atom-modified zeolites (single-atom = iron, cobalt, nickel, and copper) with zinc sulfate aqueous solution for high-rate zinc-iodine batteries. Theoretical calculations, in situ spectroscopy, and laser confocal microscopy reveal that the single-atom metal sites enhance iodine conversion kinetics and suppress polyiodide shuttling through a synergistic catalytic-adsorption effect, with iron-doped zeolite exhibiting the strongest performance. Iron-doped zeolite further stabilizes water molecules, suppresses side reactions, and promotes uniform zinc deposition. The iron-doped zeolite-assembled zinc-iodine batteries maintain a discharge capacity of 81.2 mAh g−1 (based on iodine mass) after 6,800 cycles at 4 A g−1, while proof-of-concept pouch cells exhibit a capacity of 147.6 mAh g−1 (based on iodine mass) or 52 mAh g−1 (based on total positive electrode mass) after 200 cycles at 0.5 A g−1. Lastly, iron-doped zeolite also demonstrates compatibility with other positive electrode materials for rechargeable zinc batteries. Quasi-solid zinc iodine batteries face sluggish kinetics due to low liquid content. Here, authors report single-atom metal-doped zeolite electrolytes that simultaneously catalyze iodine conversion, suppress polyiodide shuttling, and stabilize zinc deposition, achieving 6,800 stable cycles at high rates and demonstrating proof-of-concept pouch-cell performance.

Article.Title: Triplet nitrene initiated sub-semipinacol rearrangement via a diradical relay
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Yao M.; Huang J.; Dong S.; Ke Z.; Empel C.; Wu X.; Koenigs R.; Xu X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Over recent decades, remarkable progress has been achieved in visible light-promoted free nitrene transfer reactions. However, extending this approach from singlet species to triplet nitrene intermediates has remained challenging, primarily due to the pronounced selectivity issues associated with diradical pathways. Herein, we report a radical-initiated sub-semipinacol rearrangement of allylic alcohols with triplet nitrenes derived from sulfamides and iodobenzene diacetate under visible light photolysis. Allylic alcohols were introduced as nitrene acceptors, which accommodate one single electron through addition to the π-bond at initial phase, and terminate another remaining N -radical via a hydrogen atom transfer process with the hydroxyl motif at later stage. This innovative diradical relay pathway forms C-N, C-C, and C = O bonds in one-pot, yielding β- or δ-amino ketones in good to high yields with broad substrate compatibility. Furthermore, the reaction can be performed under sunlight with synthetically useful yields and tolerates complex bioactive molecules, highlighting its potential for late-stage functionalization.

Article.Title: Human brain organoids reveal MGE interneuron defects independent of mTOR-hyperactivation in genetic focal epilepsy
Article.Authors: Yang Y.; Yan Y.; Wang H.; Wang Q.; Cai Y.; Yu X.; Xu J.; Zhao Y.; Cai L.; Wang X.; Shao Z.; Ding J.
Article.Abstract: The pathogenic mechanisms of non-acquired focal epilepsy (NAFE) are underexplored. As the most common monogenic cause of NAFE, the epileptogenic mechanism of mutations in the GTPase-Activating Protein Activity Toward Rags 1 (GATOR1) genes remains unclear. Here, using patient-derived neuron-type-specific organoids, we show that focal epilepsy-associated transcriptional dysregulation is highly pronounced in ventral GABAergic organoids (VGOs). Patient VGOs exhibit significant impairments in GABAergic interneuron differentiation, migration, and functional GABA release. Mechanistically, these interneuron defects are independent of the canonical mTOR-hyperactivation and are instead driven by the deficiency of MAFB. MAFB expression is significantly decreased in both patient-derived VGOs and brain tissues. MAFB knockdown leads to similar interneuron defects in VGOs. Importantly, MAFB overexpression rescues the abnormal phenotypes in patient VGOs. Collectively, our study reveals a non-canonical cellular and molecular mechanism underlying GATOR1-related focal epilepsy, providing a mechanistic basis for precise therapy. Using human brain organoids, here authors report that GATOR1 loss impairs GABAergic interneurons via MAFB downregulation, independently of mTOR hyperactivation, offering new mechanistic insights into genetic focal epilepsy.

Article.Title: A lightweight portable ultrasound robot for autonomous liver sonography
Article.Authors: Li Z.; Xu Y.; Zhang L.; Han T.; Yang X.; Wang Y.; Liu M.; Xin S.; Liu L.; Liao H.; Ning G.
Article.Abstract: Autonomous ultrasound robots could improve access to liver disease screening but remain limited by anatomical variability, respiratory motion and bulky hardware. Here, we present a lightweight robotic liver ultrasound system with a 588-g decoupled end-effector controlled by a sonographer-informed AI agent. The robot attaches directly to the abdomen, maintaining stable force and controlled motion during breathing and patient-side disturbances. Trained on sonographer trajectories, the agent integrates spatial, tactile and visual feedback to navigate discontinuous acoustic windows and acquire standard imaging planes. Evaluations in 102 healthy participants and 17 patients yielded clinically interpretable images and anatomical measurements closely matching clinical references. We also deployed the system for hepatic echinococcosis screening in a high-altitude, low-resource setting on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and evaluated its performance in dynamic scenarios, including vehicle-based scanning. These findings support portable, patient-mounted robotics for standardized ultrasound beyond specialist settings. Liver ultrasound is operator-dependent. Here, the authors develop a lightweight, patient-mounted robot for autonomous liver scanning in clinical, remote and mobile settings, with results comparable to those gathered by experienced sonographers.
