Article.Title: Pole-to-pole LOV-domain receptor diversity points to an early stramenopile origin and global dominance of aureochromes
Article.Authors: Misir M.; Kroth P.; Wohlrab S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Light regimes are a fundamental environmental cue for marine organisms. Yet molecular adaptations of photoreceptors to the extreme seasonality of polar regions remain poorly understood. We demonstrate that the diversity of candidate blue-light-sensing LOV-domain proteins increases at higher latitudes. We identify aureochromes, blue-light-sensitive transcription factors unique to stramenopiles, as the most frequent LOV-domain receptors across ocean latitudes. Phylogenetic reconstructions reveal early aureochrome diversification in the stramenopile lineage, originating in a heterotrophic ancestor before photosynthesis was acquired. This challenges the assumption that aureochromes are restricted to phototrophs, suggesting an ancestral role in spectral light signaling. We find that, despite changes in light quality and photoperiod by latitude, diatom aureochrome domain architecture remains conserved. This implies adaptation through regulatory tuning, such as altered expression dynamics or post-translational control. Our results emphasise the importance of spectral-light sensing in polar oceans and link the widespread dominance of aureochromes to their ancient origin and conservation.

Article.Title: Chronic exercise induces a pathway-dependent electrophysiological signature in the mouse hippocampus
Article.Authors: Muela P.; Makarova J.; Muñoz-Arnaiz R.; Aballay J.; Cintado E.; Herreras O.; Trejo J.
Article.Abstract: Chronic physical exercise enhances hippocampal function, yet its impact on network activity remains poorly defined. We explored whether treadmill running leaves durable imprints detectable through electrophysiological techniques and spatial transcriptomics. Field potentials (FPs) were recorded in anesthetized male C57BL/6 J mice after a chronic exercise protocol. Using machine learning to analyze FP generators, we were able to reliably classify animals into their correct group by Lateral Perforant Path (LPP) activity alone. Classification rested on a multifeatured signature rather than any single feature. Schaffer Collateral and Lacunosum-Moleculare generators showed changes that did not achieve statistical significance. Exploratory spatial transcriptomics identified a coordinated enrichment of calcium signaling and long-term potentiation programs in the dentate gyrus. These findings demonstrate that exercise-induced plasticity is not a global shift but a localized remodeling of specific synaptic inputs, with changes detectable at both circuit and molecular levels. These durable, pathway-specific imprints persist in the absence of active task engagement, suggesting a reorganization of the brain’s memory circuitry.

Article.Title: Specification of bone marrow sinusoids requires TIE2-mediated positive feedback involving COUP-TFII and VEGFR3
Article.Authors: Li X.; Jia X.; Sun Z.; Li T.; Xu B.; Cao X.; Ding K.; Wang Y.; Shi Y.; He Y.
Article.Abstract: The bone marrow (BM) vascular network drives bone development and hematopoiesis, but the mechanisms governing its specialized sinusoidal architecture remain poorly characterized. Here, we show that the angiopoietin receptor TIE2 is highly expressed by BM sinusoidal endothelial cells (BM-SECs). Its endothelial deletion triggers sinusoidal capillarization, characterized by reduced vessel diameter and aberrant mural cell coverage. Mechanistically, TIE2 insufficiency downregulates VEGFR3 in BM-SECs within 48 h of induced endothelial Tek deletion, while leaving hepatic sinusoidal VEGFR3 unaffected. RNA-sequencing reveals that TIE2 insufficiency suppresses sinusoidal development pathways while upregulating arterial and angiogenic genes. We validate this phenotype using inducible Tek deletion mainly in VEGFR3 + SECs and in Angpt1 -insufficient mice. Furthermore, endothelial deletion of the transcription factor COUP-TFII ( Nr2f2 ) recapitulates these defects, reducing both BM sinusoidal TIE2 and VEGFR3 expression. Finally, induced endothelial deletion of Flt4 produces a similar phenotype. Together, our findings imply that ANGPT1/TIE2 and COUP-TFII form a reciprocal regulatory loop essential for BM sinusoidal specification by sustaining VEGFR3 expression.

Article.Title: Evolutionary genomics of ancient and endangered Achnatherum breviaristatum on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
Article.Authors: Yang Y.; Zhang X.; Su X.; Wu G.; Yang Y.; Liu J.; Yuan L.; Ren G.; Chen W.
Article.Abstract: Climate change and human activities threaten biodiversity on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP), renowned for its endemic species. We examined genomic diversity and evolution of Achnatherum breviaristatum, an endangered grass species endemic to the QTP. A. breviaristatum diverged from its sister lineage ~15 million years ago, and contrasts with two widespread and ecologically dominant monotypic genera within the same lineage—Neotrinia splendens and Psammochloa villosa—which thrive in arid northwestern China. Using newly generated chromosome-level genome assemblies and population resequencing data for A. breviaristatum and N. splendens, together with publicly available genomic data for P. villosa, we reveal that A. breviaristatum exhibits lower genetic diversity and heterozygosity based on resequencing reads mapped to the respective reference genomes. All species experienced parallel demographic declines since the Quaternary glaciation, with reductions during the Pleistocene. The endangered status of A. breviaristatum likely results from weaker clonal reproduction relative to its relatives, combined with Pleistocene vegetation shifts and anthropogenic activities. A reduced genetic load in A. breviaristatum may mitigate the effects of its low genetic diversity and contribute to its persistence. This study highlights interactions among climatic shifts, reproductive strategy, and human impact in shaping endemic species’ fates, providing genetic insights for conservation in vulnerable ecosystems. A comparative genomics study on grasses from the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau reveals how demographic decline, reduced clonal reproduction, and Pleistocene climate shifts have driven low diversity in an endangered endemic species, while reduced genetic load may have enabled its persistence.

Article.Title: Developmental restriction of the jaw skeletal muscle cardiogenic potential
Article.Authors: Díaz-Díaz C.; Ocaña O.; Isern J.; Muñoz-Cánoves P.; Torres M.
Article.Abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are a leading cause of mortality worldwide and heart failure remains an end-stage disease with no other treatment than transplantation. A promising field to tackle heart failure is cardiomyocyte implantation. Whereas cardiomyocyte generation from pluripotent cells has shown promising results, direct derivation of cardiomyocytes from somatic stem cells is still challenging. Skeletal muscle progenitors have been extensively studied as a source of cardiac cells, due to their cellular and functional similarities. During development, the right ventricular myocardium and jaw skeletal muscles derive from a common pool of myogenic mesodermal progenitors. Previous studies have reported the derivation of cardiomyocyte-like cells specifically from adult mouse jaw muscle stem cell populations, but not from other skeletal muscles, suggesting that developmental origin endows cardiogenic potential. Here we evaluated the cardiogenic potential of satellite cells and mesenchymal progenitor cells from the masticatory muscle by reproducing, optimizing and diversifying previously described protocols. We consistently found that stem cells from masticatory muscles are unable to differentiate into cardiac cells under any tested cardiogenic environment. Furthermore, pharmacological erasing of repressive epigenetic marks did not activate cardiogenic potential, suggesting that barriers restraining lineage plasticity are profound and unlikely to be reversed by simple exposure to cardiogenic environments.

Article.Title: Cleavage of xanthone and flavone C–glycosidic bonds by the enzyme complex LaGME from gut Lachnospiraceae
Article.Authors: Liu W.; Tao X.; Fan S.; Li X.; Liu Z.; Zhang H.; Li J.; He W.; Zhang D.; Zhang T.; Zhang T.; Pang X.; Yang Z.; Ma B.; Xiang H.; Yu L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Aglycones, the bioactive metabolites of C– glycosides, can be obtained through the deglycosylation of naturally abundant C– glycosides. However, C– glycosides are more resistant to enzymatic and chemical degradation. Gut microbiota and its enzymes are known to cleave the C–C glycosidic bond, but only a limited number of active strains and functional enzymes have been identified. Here we show that a new C– deglycosylation gene cluster encoding the g lycoside- m etabolizing e nzyme from La chnospiraceae (LaGME), an enzyme complex consisting of a C – g lycoside o xidoreductase (LaCGO1) and a C – g lycoside e limination enzyme complex (LaCGE), was discovered using the DUF6379 domain-containing protein as a probe. LaGME demonstrates significant activities toward xanthone-type and flavone-type C– glycosides. After investigation into heterologous expression, structural determination and catalytic mechanism, a LaGME-mediated one-pot cascade enzymatic reaction system was developed for green production of aglycones. This research provides an approach to uncover C– glycoside-metabolizing enzymes in nature, as well as a preliminary basis for the sustainable production of value-added bioactive aglycones from glycosides.

Article.Title: Analysis of 515 human proteomes defines plasma extracellular vesicle core composition, corona and coisolated networks
Article.Authors: Carvalho A.; Falcón-Pérez J.; Beck H.; Matthiesen R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Plasma extracellular vesicles (EVs) are promising liquid biopsy biomarkers, yet their proteomic profiling remains confounded by massive co-isolation. Here, we resolve this heterogeneity through a meta-analysis of 515 human plasma EV proteomes. We demonstrate that the reproducible core proteome is overwhelmingly governed by predictable, surface-charge-driven mass-action that dynamically mirrors synthetic nanoparticle corona formation. By quantitatively decomposing the core isolate against pan-synthetic coronas and agonist-induced platelet EVs, we trace the core isolate to three main mechanistic origins: an electrostatic plasma corona, ex vivo platelet vesiculation and biological macromolecular co-isolates. Crucially, the residual vesicular cargo strongly correlates with thrombin-induced platelet degranulation, indicating that phlebotomy-induced trauma contribute to the bulk signal. We provide a modular atlas that mathematically distinguishes biophysical coronas from these cellular co-isolates, establishing a new framework for interpreting biological origin in plasma EV proteomics.

Article.Title: Tamoxifen targets Wisp2 to impair subcutaneous adipocyte progenitor self-renewal and adipogenic differentiation
Article.Authors: Thomas N.; Sankofi B.; Cen H.; Sekhri M.; Murguia S.; Cherian M.; Stout M.; Miller B.; Rudolph M.; Wellberg E.
Article.Abstract: Breast cancer endocrine therapy, including tamoxifen, systemically disrupts estrogen receptor signaling and increases type 2 diabetes (T2D) risk in women. Hyperplastic adipose tissue expansion, especially in subcutaneous depots, facilitates nutrient storage and attenuates inflammation during a chronic positive energy balance and is impaired in the absence of estrogen. Adipocyte progenitors are renewed through Wnt signaling pathway activation, however the the mechanisms that explain the depletion of these cells during endocrine therapy are not defined. Here we show the direct impact of tamoxifen on proliferation, renewal, and differentiation in subcutaneous adipose stromal cells from humans and adult mice. In obesity, the Wnt1 inducible signaling pathway protein 2 (Wisp2) was lost in adipocyte progenitors following endocrine therapy. Wisp2 gain and loss of function studies defined the link between estrogen signaling and adipocyte progenitor maintenance. We found that tamoxifen treatment disrupts the protection of adipocyte progenitors by estrogen, mediated through suppression of Wisp2. These studies reveal effects of tamoxifen therapy that precede and could influence T2D development in breast cancer survivors.

Article.Title: Assessing whole-cortex excitability from electromagnetic brain signals
Article.Authors: Pellegrino G.; Duma G.; Schuler A.; Daub M.; Marinazzo D.; Arcara G.; Soddu A.; Rasero J.
Article.Abstract: Cortical excitability is a core feature of brain function shaped by microcircuitry, large-scale networks, and neurochemistry. In humans, it can be inferred from indirect electrophysiological measures, yet it remains unclear whether these capture a single construct or multiple processes. We systematically compared established excitability metrics using whole-head magneto-encephalography (MEG) recorded at rest and during 40 Hz auditory stimulation in a large sample of healthy adults. These measures included stimulus-driven synchronization, spectral power, aperiodic (1/f) activity, signal complexity, long-range temporal correlations, and phase–gamma synchronization. Hierarchical clustering identified six distinct excitability dimensions with limited redundancy, indicating that cortical excitability is inherently multidimensional. Aperiodic and alpha-band measures were strongly coupled and most spatially aligned with stimulus responses, while temporal, complexity, and synchronization metrics were largely independent. Regional differences were most pronounced in integrative and internally oriented areas. Each dimension also related differently to cortical morphology and neurotransmitter receptor density, highlighting diverse neurobiological substrates and supporting multimodal approaches to studying excitability.

Article.Title: Single-cell atlas reveals NLRP2 associated mitochondrial dysfunction in estrogen induced Macrobrachium nipponense sex reversal
Article.Authors: Cai P.; Gao Z.; Jiang S.; Zhang W.; Xiong Y.; Qiao H.; Jin S.; Fu H.
Article.Abstract: Sex reversal is used in aquaculture breeding, but its cellular basis in crustaceans remains unclear. Here we combine estrogen induced feminization, single-cell RNA sequencing, histology and RNA interference to study gonadal development in the oriental river prawn (Macrobrachium nipponense). Feeding post-larval males with 17β-estradiol produced neo-females with ovary like gonads. Single-cell profiling of testes, ovaries and neo-female gonads resolved major oogenic and spermatogenic cell types and showed that neo-female gonads were enriched in early germ cells, whereas mature oocytes and spermatozoa were depleted. Cell type matched analyses identified oxidative phosphorylation as a consistently altered pathway. The gene MnNLRP2 showed primary spermatocyte specific and testis enriched expression. Knockdown of MnNLRP2 shifted sex ratios toward females in juveniles, altered sex hormone levels and caused spermatogenic arrest in adults. These results link MnNLRP2 to mitochondrial dysfunction during incomplete crustacean sex reversal. Single-cell analysis reveals incomplete estrogen induced sex reversal in Macrobrachium nipponense and identifies MnNLRP2 associated mitochondrial dysfunction in germ-cell development.

Article.Title: Breaking new ground into RAD51 BRC repeats interplay in homologous recombination
Article.Authors: Rinaldi F.; Franco P.; Veronesi M.; Romeo E.; Bresciani V.; Varignani G.; Catalano F.; Bernetti M.; Masetti M.; Langer J.; Girotto S.; Cavalli A.
Article.Abstract: Homologous recombination (HR) is a critical repair pathway involving numerous proteins that ensure error-free DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) repair. Dysfunction in HR components can compromise genome integrity. Despite advances, many aspects of HR remain poorly understood. Notably, even one of the earliest identified and most critical interactions, between RAD51 and BRCA2, remains incompletely characterized, mainly due to the lack of structural data. This study presents a comprehensive biophysical analysis of the RAD51–BRC repeats interaction, integrating computational and experimental approaches. Starting with assessing the correlation between the binding affinities of individual BRC repeats and their impact on RAD51 disassembly, our investigation extends to larger BRCA2 truncations, offering unprecedented insights into the molecular determinants of RAD51 recognition. As mutations in the BRC repeats impair RAD51 recruitment and are associated with cancer, these results provide a valuable framework for interpreting pathogenic variants and guiding precision medicine therapies.

Article.Title: Ultra large docking reveals novel chemotypes and a distinct binding mode for Porcupine inhibition
Article.Authors: Kim C.; Coria J.; Radchenko D.; Cheng H.; Li J.; Wang B.; Hu Q.; Moroz Y.; Li X.; Liu F.
Article.Abstract: Wnt signaling is essential for embryonic development and adult tissue homeostasis, and its dysregulation contributes to cancer and other human diseases. Porcupine (PORCN), a membrane-bound O-acyltransferase (MBOAT) required for Wnt palmitoylation and secretion, has emerged as an important therapeutic target. Despite promising preclinical results, PORCN inhibitors have shown limited clinical activity to date, motivating the search for new chemotypes and binding modes. Here, we docked a library of 1.3 billion molecules against PORCN and identified 16 novel compounds that inhibit Wnt signaling. These hits are structurally distinct from known PORCN inhibitors, and structure-based optimization of one series yielded sub-micromolar leads. Cryo-electron microscopy revealed that the lead inhibitor binds PORCN in an unreported mode within the palmitoleoyl-CoA chamber, positioned closer to the cytosol than existing inhibitors. Together, our findings expand the chemical and structural space available for targeting PORCN and provide new starting points for development of Wnt signaling antagonists.

Article.Title: Kidney-derived mitochondrial extracellular vesicles trigger acute lung injury in sepsis via mtDNA-cGAS-STING in pulmonary endothelium
Article.Authors: Jiao Y.; Zhang H.; Xie X.; Pi M.; Fu Q.; Zhu W.; Song J.; Bo J.; Zhang T.; Chen M.; Gu X.; Ma Z.
Article.Abstract: Sepsis often leads to multiple organ failure, but how injury in one organ propagates to another remains poorly understood. Here we show that the injured kidney releases mitochondria-rich extracellular vesicles (mitoEVs) into the circulation, which travel to the lung and trigger acute lung injury. In septic mice and cultured renal tubular epithelial cells, sepsis promotes the formation of mitochondrial-derived vesicles by upregulating sorting nexin 9. Blocking this process in kidney tubules reduces the release of mitoEVs and protects against lung injury. Once taken up by lung endothelial cells, the mitochondrial DNA carried by these vesicles activates an innate immune pathway involving cGAS and STING, with ZBP1 serving as a potential cooperative partner for this activation. This leads to endothelial barrier disruption, immune cell recruitment, and respiratory failure. In patients with sepsis, higher levels of circulating mitoEVs associate with lung injury and death. These findings identify a kidney-to-lung signaling axis that may be targeted therapeutically.

Article.Title: Genome-wide analyses reveal recent diversification and hidden diversity in Amazonian howler monkeys, including two new species
Article.Authors: Batista R.; Semedo T.; Beck R.; Bittencourt P.; Ceríaco L.; Cuadros-Espinoza S.; da Silva M.; de Melo F.; Deo R.; de Vries D.; Farh K.; Farias I.; Gibson M.; Goodhead I.; Gubili C.; Hermosilla-Albala N.; Hrbek T.; Janiak M.; Kuderna L.; Mahabir D.; Marqués-Bonet T.; Melin A.; Mendoza A.; Mittermeier R.; Nash S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Complex ecological and evolutionary patterns shaped the rich biodiversity of the Neotropics. Understanding how diversity emerges and is maintained is key to anticipating potential biotic responses to current anthropogenic changes. Howler monkeys ( Alouatta ) are one of the most successful radiations inhabiting this region. However, 11 of the 16 taxa currently recognised are classified as threatened by the IUCN Red List, and the genus faces increasing threats from deforestation, habitat fragmentation, and hunting. Here, we present a genomic-wide analysis covering 11 of the 13 recognised Alouatta species. Our results indicate that most of this genus’ diversity in Amazonia originated in the last million years, driven by major biogeographic and ecological factors, such as geographical barriers (e.g., Amazonian rivers, and the Andes), as well as by ecological gradients, including savanna-forest mosaics and ecotonal zones. Historical biogeographic reconstructions support a trans-Andean origin for Alouatta . Based on integrative taxonomy, including genomic and morphological evidence from numerous specimens, we formally identify groups and provide descriptions for two new species. Our findings underscore the power of genome-wide data to uncover hidden diversity and to inform conservation strategies, particularly in rapidly transforming tropical ecosystems where undescribed species may already be at risk.

Article.Title: Omega-3 PUFA supplementation promotes arthritis resolution by modulating joint cell phenotype involving E-series resolvins
Article.Authors: Cecconello C.; Claria-Ribas P.; Cartagena García C.; Busnel J.; Dalli J.; Perretti M.; Norling L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The cellular mechanisms of omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid (ω3 PUFA) supplementation were investigated in inflammatory arthritis. Mice fed a prophylactic ω3 PUFA-enriched diet displayed reduced arthritis and paw oedema, with a discrete regulation of innate and stromal cell phenotypes in arthritic joints. Lipid mediator profiling of arthritic paws identified a distinct repertoire of molecules in ω3-fed mice, with elevated EPA-derived resolvin E2 (RvE2) and RvE4, compared with increased TXB 2 and PGF 2α with a normal diet. Pharmacological treatment of mice with RvE2 and RvE4 concomitant with arthritis induction, attenuated arthritis and increased MerTK + CD206 + macrophages in arthritic joints. Synovial explant treatment revealed reduced pro-inflammatory mediator and enzyme release including IL-6, CCL2 and MMP-9. In arthritic patient blood, RvE2 and RvE4 (100 nM) lowered monocyte ICAM-1 expression. Collectively, these data identify cellular and molecular determinants of an ω3 diet in pre-clinical and human settings, highlighting therapeutic potential.

Article.Title: Myristic acid promotes in vitro maturation and developmental competence of porcine oocytes
Article.Authors: Yan J.; Zhang K.; Gao X.; Xu S.; Ning F.; Liu K.; Zhang X.; De Felici M.; Zhang T.; Wang J.; Shen W.
Article.Abstract: The present study examined how antral follicle size influences oocyte meiotic maturation and developmental competence from a metabolic perspective and explored strategies to improve the meiotic maturation and quality of oocytes derived from small antral follicles. In vitro, myristic acid (MA) improved meiotic maturation (polar body extrusion, spindle morphology, chromosome dynamics) and survival of oocytes from small follicles by reducing Annexin V expression and ROS levels. MA also enhanced their developmental competence after parthenogenetic activation. Molecular and cytochemical analyses showed that MA altered the transcriptional profile, increased lipid storage, and boosted mitochondrial number and function. Finally, MA upregulated SIRT1, activated PPARα, and increased CPT2 expression, suggesting a potential mechanism underlying its effects on these oocytes.

Article.Title: Structure-function tethering of human locus coeruleus connectivity reveals a noradrenergic cortical hierarchy
Article.Authors: Zhu Q.; Fan L.; Wu Y.; An S.; Li Y.; Wang H.; Yao N.; Li Y.; Huang Z.
Article.Abstract: The locus coeruleus (LC) is the primary source of cerebral norepinephrine and plays a broad role in cognition. Here, we show the macroscale organization of human LC connectivity using 7 T diffusion and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Structural and functional connectivity exhibit a dominant rostral-caudal gradient, with structure-function tethering lowest in the intermediate LC and increasing toward its rostral and caudal portions. In the neocortex, this pattern is expressed as steeply increasing tethering from the central sulcus toward anterior and posterior regions. Allen Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas tracing further reveals preferential LC projections to somatomotor cortex. The cortical expression of LC structure-function tethering exhibits a network-level hierarchy and aligns with a behavioral axis. Additionally, this cortical expression shows significant spatial covariance with norepinephrine transporter concentration, fiber length, and gray matter volume. Together, these findings provide MRI-based evidence for a hierarchical macroscale organization of human LC connectivity linking structural and functional architecture to cortical and behavioral variation.

Article.Authors: Zhu Y.; Chen X.; Deng X.; Zhang S.; Zhang J.; Meng F.; Zhou Q.; Gu Y.; Gong F.; Lu G.; Lin G.; Leng L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The blastocyst formation rate of human embryos cultured in vitro for assisted reproduction is approximately 50%, with most embryos arresting at the cleavage stage; however, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Collectively, these findings provide mechanistic insights into preimplantation embryonic development and reveal potential causes of blastocyst formation failure.

Article.Title: Aberrant RNA sensing and host-specific immunopathology in highly pathogenic influenza infections
Article.Authors: Dey A.; Patel A.; Chandra A.; Kesavardhana S.
Article.Abstract: Innate immune activation is critical for mounting protective host immune responses against viral infections. Viruses have evolved mechanisms to counteract host innate immune responses and restrict host defence. Intriguingly, growing evidence suggests that RNA viruses of zoonotic origin, particularly influenza viruses, trigger dysregulated innate immune activation leading to excessive inflammation and cellular damage. However, the host and viral mechanisms underlying the dysregulated innate immune responses that cause severe immunopathology remain to be fully unravelled. In this review, we discuss how aberrant RNA sensing contributes to innate immune responses during highly pathogenic influenza infections. Article.Title: Towards a sequential microbiome therapy for HPV-associated cervicovaginal dysbiosis
Article.Authors: Molina M.; Zhang Y.; Steenbergen R.; Melchers W.; Du J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infections are the principal cause of cervical cancer, and are increasingly associated with ecological instability of the cervicovaginal microbiome. Multiomics studies indicate that hrHPV persistence is linked to reduced Lactobacillus dominance, increased anaerobic taxa, and metabolic alterations that may compromise epithelial integrity and antiviral immunity. In this Perspective article, we introduce a sequential microbiome therapy (SMT) framework designed to restore cervicovaginal ecological balance and support viral clearance. SMT is a two-phase, strain-resolved strategy. The first phase targets dysbiotic communities using antimicrobials, biofilm-disrupting or microbiota-modulating approaches to create a window for ecological reset. The second phase introduces health-associated Lactobacillus species selected for their acidification capacity, competitive fitness, and ability to stabilize the mucosal environment. We outline the ecological principles underpinning SMT and discuss its development as a potentially scalable microbiome-directed strategy for restoring cervicovaginal health and managing hrHPV-associated disease within existing cervical cancer prevention frameworks.

Article.Title: Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data
Article.Authors: Nasr E.; Pechlivanis N.; Strepis N.; Amato P.; Bernt M.; Bhardwaj A.; Blankenberg D.; Brites D.; Cumbo F.; Do K.; Ferrari E.; Griffin T.; Grüning B.; Hiltemann S.; Hyde C.; Jagtap P.; Kumar A.; Malla M.; Mehta S.; Métris K.; Momin S.; Nelson T.; Oba A.; Pavloudi C.; Péguilhan R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The explosion of microbial omics data has outpaced the ability of many researchers to analyse it, with complex tools and limited computational resources creating barriers to discovery. To address this gap, we present the Microbiology Galaxy Lab (MGL): a free, globally accessible, community-supported platform that combines state-of-the-art analytical power with user-friendly accessibility. Supported by the Galaxy and global microbiology communities, this platform integrates over 315 tool suites and 115 curated workflows, enabling comprehensive metabarcoding, (meta)genomic, (meta)transcriptomic, and (meta)proteomic data analysis within a FAIR-aligned environment. It also supports research in the health and infectious disease sectors, as well as in environmental microbiology. The platform’s utility is exemplified through various use cases, including antimicrobial resistance tracking, biomarker prediction, microbiome classification, and functional annotation of key microbes. Built on reproducibility and community engagement, it supports the creation, sharing, and updating of best-practice workflows. Over 35 tutorials and learning paths empower scientists, fostering an ecosystem that keeps resources at the forefront of microbiological data analysis. The MGL enables collective analysis, democratising research, thereby accelerating discovery across the global microbiology community ( microbiology.usegalaxy.org , .eu , .org.au , . fr ).

Article.Title: BdCDPK5 is an essential regulator of Babesia divergens intraerythrocytic progression

Article.Title: Developmental and genetic modulation of evidence integration dynamics in zebrafish sensorimotor decision-making
Article.Authors: Garza R.; El Hady A.; Bahl A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Animals integrate information over time and maintain persistent internal representations of cues to guide decision-making. How the underlying behavioral algorithms of individual animals depend on factors such as experience, developmental stage, or genotype remains poorly understood. Drift-diffusion models provide a powerful theoretical framework to describe and predict performance metrics across a wide range of species. The stochastic nature of these models and the typically limited throughput of most experimental designs challenge the automatic inference of latent variables. Here, we combine high-throughput behavioral assays in larval zebrafish with drift-diffusion modeling, revealing that larvae progressively develop more persistent, self-reinforcing integration dynamics during early development. This effect is reduced in fish carrying mutations in genes linked to human epilepsy and schizophrenia. Our results show that behavior-based drift-diffusion modeling can offer a scalable, automated approach to generate experimentally testable hypotheses about the algorithmic implementation of sensorimotor integration in health and disease.

Article.Abstract: Abstract The capacity to regulate corticosterone release following a stressful event is an essential component of the physiological flexibility required to maintain homeostasis and ensure adaptive responses to environmental change. Hg blood concentrations were negatively correlated with corticosterone responsiveness, suggesting impairment of hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal axis function. These results demonstrate that environmental Hg contamination is associated with reduced stress responsiveness and physiological flexibility, which likely limits the ability of Hg-contaminated individuals to cope with novel environmental stressors. We found that a methylmercury-sensitive cysteine in the glucocorticoid receptor is highly conserved across vertebrates, suggesting a shared molecular mechanism for mercury effects on glucocorticoid signaling. Given the widespread Hg pollution in tropical ecosystems, these findings emphasize the role of Hg as an endocrine-disrupting chemical in crocodylians.

Article.Title: PDE10A identified by cross-hemisphere visual cortex proteomics restores adult ocular dominance plasticity involving cAMP/CREB signaling
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Zhu Z.; Xu J.; Dong S.; Mo E.; Li Q.; Li Z.; Zhao Y.; Chang P.
Article.Abstract: Ocular dominance plasticity (ODP) is robust during the critical period but is restricted in adulthood. Article.Authors: Vassal-Stermann E.; Berthollet C.; Zhang W.; Fenel D.; Ehrhardt A.; Lieber A.; Schoehn G.; Effantin G.; Fender P.

These findings establish the fiber knob apex as a vulnerable site for antibody-mediated neutralization and identify 5C5 as a candidate targeting pathogenic species B adenoviruses. Article.Title: Crocin alleviates renal fibrosis through inhibiting mitochondrial dysfunction via regulating HOXD8/PGC‑1α pathways
Article.Authors: Li X.; Ma T.; Han X.; Hai S.; Yin L.; Wang L.; Wang J.; Li H.; Yang Q.; Guan X.; Li Y.; Ding H.
Article.Abstract: Crocin, a key bioactive compound derived from saffron ( Crocus sativus L .), a traditional Chinese medicinal and edible herb, exhibits renoprotective effects against fibrosis, but the mechanisms remain unclear. HOXD8 overexpression increases PGC1-α expression, reduces reactive oxygen species, restores mitochondrial function, and suppresses profibrotic genes. DNMT1-mediated promoter hypermethylation drives HOXD8 downregulation, and crocin reduces DNMT1 enrichment and activity at this promoter. These findings suggest that crocin upregulates HOXD8 by inhibiting both its promoter hypermethylation and protein ubiquitination, thereby ameliorating mitochondrial dysfunction and fibrosis in chronic kidney disease (CKD).

Article.Title: SUMOylation and ubiquitination of Viperin dynamically regulate the type I interferon-mediated antiviral response
Article.Authors: Miao Y.; Cui Q.; Li Z.; Zhang T.; Zhang R.; Zhao Q.; Zhou H.; Zuo Y.; Wang Q.; Zhang Y.; Zheng Z.; He W.; Liu C.; Huang Q.; Zheng H.; Yuan Y.

Trait-based analysis showed long-term increases were mainly fine filter feeders, including many meroplankton larvae. Article.Authors: Zeng L.; Liu Y.; Zhang C.; Fan Y.; Sun J.; Liu Y.; Xu Z.; Cao Y.; Li O.; Zhang C.; Fan G.; Zhang J.; Zhao Y.; Liang X.; Liu Y.; Chen Y.; Lu H.

Article.Title: White matter fiber bundles enable robust conduction and time-critical signaling despite axon caliber variation
Article.Authors: Mordhorst L.; Weiskopf N.; Morawski M.; Mohammadi S.

We show in 450,000 3D axon reconstructions from male rats that—despite this individual variation—axon bundles possess stable radius distributions at the ensemble level. These distributions are faithfully captured by 2D cross-sections and yield robust conduction velocity predictions, as along-axon variability has only a modest effect. Conduction in large axons is particularly stable, supporting time-critical signaling. With 2D sampling validated, we leverage 46 million human corpus callosum axons from 2D histology to determine sample size requirements across neuroscience applications. Our findings show how axonal organization gives rise to stable ensemble statistics and conduction, explaining and reinforcing decades of 2D histology-based research.

Article.Title: Exceptional preservation in cherts reveals complex cuticular architecture in one of the earliest Cambrian ecdysozoans
Article.Authors: Zhang M.; Dong L.; Hua H.; Liu W.; Qin S.; Liu H.
Article.Abstract: Ecdysozoans, animals characterized by a periodically moulted cuticle, became major components of Cambrian marine ecosystems, yet the structural organization of their earliest non-mineralized cuticles remains poorly documented. This occurrence represents one of the earliest Cambrian ecdysozoan body-fossil records and may predate the classic Kuanchuanpu scalidophoran assemblages. The material preserves a terminal mouth with large circumoral spines and abundant cuticular fragments. Its cuticle comprises a fibrous mesh, short upright plate-like structures, and hollow ridged spines. Morphological and Raman data support an ecdysozoan affinity, whereas scalidophoran placement remains tentative. Spinosoma reveals a previously undocumented cuticular architecture, suggesting that early ecdysozoan ecological breadth and integument diversity are underestimated in the earliest phase of the Cambrian Explosion.

Article.Title: A NEST-based framework unlocks massively parallel simulation of networks of multi-compartment neurons with customizable subcellular dynamics
Article.Authors: Wybo W.; Ewert L.; Linssen C.; Babu P.; Pastorelli E.; Paolucci P.; Morrison A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract While subcellular mechanisms in the dendrites of neurons govern the implementation of learning and memory in the brain, large-scale network simulations featuring such processes remain challenging to achieve. This can be attributed to a lack of appropriate software tools, as neuroscientific simulators focus on the one hand on highly detailed models, and on the other hand on massive networks featuring point neurons. Here, we fill this gap by implementing a framework for the massively parallel simulation of simplified dendrite models with customizable subcellular dynamics. We leverage the NEural Simulation Tool (NEST), the neuroscientific reference with respect to efficient massively parallel simulations of point-neuron networks. By co-opting the model description language NESTML, we generate C++ code implementing user-configurable subcellular dynamics. We show that the generated models run efficiently, leading to scalable NEST network simulations. To showcase relevant functionalities, we provide a proof-of-concept demonstration that a key sensory computation – the association of top-down context arriving at distal dendrites in layer 1 and feedforward sensory input arriving perisomatically – can be achieved in a single-shot fashion through apical calcium dynamics. Article.Title: SQSTM1/p62-LC3A–mediated autophagic clearance of stress granules prevents apoptosis under hyperosmotic stress
Article.Authors: Yi Q.; Zhang C.; Hu S.; Wang Z.; He L.; Zhang M.; Man Z.; Bai Y.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: Stress granules (SGs) are transient, membraneless assemblies that form in response to cellular stress and typically disassemble when stress resolves. Their persistence has been linked to neurodegenerative disease. Here we show that LC3A has a selective role in the autophagic clearance of SGs formed during hyperosmotic stress. LC3A, but not LC3B or LC3C, associates with SGs, and depletion of LC3A impairs their removal. LC3A also promotes clearance of pathogenic inclusions containing TDP-43 or poly(GR) dipeptides from C9orf72 expansions. Proteomic analysis reveals enrichment of the autophagy receptor SQSTM1/p62 in SGs, supporting its role in SG degradation. SGs are also enriched in mitochondrial and apoptosis-related proteins, consistent with an anti-apoptotic function potentially linked to mitochondrial proximity. However, prolonged stress activates CASP3 and promotes apoptosis, which is exacerbated by defective SG clearance. These findings highlight the critical role of the SQSTM1–LC3A axis in SG turnover and cell survival under chronic stress.

Article.Title: Forced expression of UCP1 counteracts the compromised activity of NK cells in the tumor microenvironment
Article.Authors: Gu M.; Chen W.; Hu C.; Jia X.; Xiao W.; Lu G.; Gong W.; Lu D.
Article.Abstract: Uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) is a mitochondrial inner membrane protein that mediates non-shivering thermogenesis in brown adipose tissue. Natural killer cells are key effectors of antitumor immunity but are impaired in the tumor microenvironment. Here we show that UCP1 is downregulated in tumor-infiltrating NK cells (TINKs) from colorectal cancer patients and tumor-bearing mice and correlates with impaired effector function. Natural killer cell-specific UCP1 ablation accelerates tumor growth and reduces tumor infiltration. Transforming growth factor β1 and hypoxia repress UCP1 transcription through C/EBPβ downregulation. UCP1 deficiency increases CD36/FABP4-mediated fatty acid uptake and alters mitochondrial respiration, accompanied by mitochondrial damage, mitochondrial DNA release, NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation, and pyroptosis. Enforced UCP1 expression prevents tumor microenvironment-induced pyroptosis and maintains antitumor activity in murine models and patient-derived organoids. Genetically modified expression of UCP1 in NK cells is a potential therapy for patients with tumors. UCP1 loss in tumor-infiltrating NK cells drives CD36/FABP4-dependent fatty acid oxidation, mitochondrial DNA release and NLRP3-mediated pyroptosis. Restoring UCP1 preserves NK cell function and antitumor activity in mouse tumor models and patient-derived colorectal cancer organoids.

Article.Title: Sexually dimorphic transdifferentiation of endothelial cells in atherosclerosis
Article.Authors: Luo C.; Wang S.; Lyu Q.; Lyu Y.
Article.Abstract: Sex differences in atherosclerosis are clinically recognized, but the contribution of endothelial cell (EC) states and fates to these differences remain incompletely understood. Here, we used EC lineage tracing in male and female Apoe −/− /Cdh5-CreER T2 /Rosa26-mTmG mice fed a high-fat diet and performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing of plaque-bearing aortae. We identified nine sex-biased EC subpopulations, including capillary, lymphatic, Sox17 + , Myh11 + , Mki67 + , and Ly6a + ECs enriched in females and Col8a1 + and Fmo2 + ECs enriched in males. GeneTrajectory analysis and lineage tracing indicated that approximately one quarter of GFP⁺ EC-lineage cells transit into adipocyte-like, SMC-like, or fibroblast-like states. EC-to-SMC-like transitions were more prominent in females, whereas EC-to-adipocyte-like transitions were more prominent in males. Regulatory network analysis using pySCENIC implicated Klf2 and Creb5 in EC fate decisions. These findings reveal sex-specific EC-lineage trajectories associated with distinct plaque phenotypes and nominate candidates for sex-informed therapeutic investigation.

Article.Title: Quantitative imaging supports that endoskeletal mineralization in sharks is an adaptive trait
Article.Authors: Winkel E.; Hansen K.; Krøjer Westh C.; Nielsen J.; Rask Møller P.; Lauridsen H.
Article.Abstract: Modern sharks (Selachimorpha) exhibit a broad suite of adaptations that enable them to inhabit diverse marine environments. Notably, their cartilaginous endoskeleton displays varying degrees of mineralization, potentially reflecting adaptations for buoyancy, locomotion, and feeding. Here, quantitative computed tomography was applied to assess endoskeletal mineralization in representatives from all nine orders of sharks spanning 26 out of 35 families. Our findings reveal that skeletal mineralization is highly variable between species and is more closely associated with ecological factors such as depth distribution, than with phylogenetic relationship. We find that deeper-dwelling species generally exhibit lower degrees of mineralization, suggesting adaptations for buoyancy regulation and energy conservation. Our study provides insight into the variation of skeletal mineralization in the ecology and evolution of sharks.

Article.Authors: Song Y.; Newton J.; Abedi K.; Toukan S.; Zhang J.; Lam T.; Yang S.; Yang J.; Salih R.; Kanagarajah K.; Young E.; Wong A.
Article.Abstract: Human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-derived lung models remain limited by inefficient progenitor specification and incomplete alveolar maturation. Here, we present a robust and scalable differentiation strategy that reproducibly generates high-purity ( > 85%) fetal lung progenitors without cell sorting. These cells form distal bud tip organoids that recapitulate human fetal late tip and late stalk epithelial populations with multilineage potential. We show that direct co-culture with human lung fibroblasts, combined with Notch inhibition, promotes efficient differentiation toward fetal AT1- and AT2-like epithelial states, supported by transcriptional, protein, and ultrastructural analyses. Importantly, paracrine signaling alone is insufficient, highlighting a requirement for direct epithelial–mesenchymal interaction. We further integrated a microfluidic air-liquid interface culture system incorporating cyclic stretch. Under these conditions, we observed activation of mechanotransduction-associated and developmental signaling programs together with structural and transcriptional changes consistent with more mature alveolar-like epithelial states. This platform establishes a physiologically relevant model for human alveologenesis and provides a foundation for disease modeling and regenerative applications. hPSC-derived distal bud tip organoids that resemble fetal alveolar progenitors are developed and used to show that air-liquid interface culture and cyclic stretch enhance alveolar epithelial maturation and increased segregation of AT1- and AT2-associated cell states.

Article.Title: Targeting central thalamus with transcranial ultrasound reduces arousal in healthy volunteers
Article.Authors: Hopkins A.; Cain J.; White E.; Abakians S.; Monti M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Using low-intensity focused transcranial ultrasound stimulation, we test the causal roles of the central thalamus in arousal and the pulvinar in visuospatial attention in the healthy human brain. In a within-subjects, counterbalanced design, 27 healthy volunteers (two females) complete a vigilance task (Psychomotor Vigilance Task) and a visuospatial attention task (Egly-Driver Task) before and after sham, central thalamic, and pulvinar sonication. Targeting the central thalamus slows responses and increases lapses in attention during the vigilance task, indicating reduced arousal. Pulvinar sonication reduces (and slows) responses to visual stimuli presented contralaterally, suggesting a disruption of contralateral visuospatial attention. These results provide causal evidence linking the pulvinar to visuospatial attention and the central thalamus to arousal in the healthy human brain and demonstrate that ultrasound can elicit distinct behavioral changes in healthy volunteers when delivered to close but functionally distinct thalamic regions, underscoring its potential as a tool for noninvasive brain mapping.

Article.Title: Whole brain modeling reveals subtype specific regulation for adolescent major depressive disorder
Article.Authors: Zeng X.; Zhang G.; Wang F.; Xiong Y.; Zhang T.; Zhou C.; Biswal B.; Yao D.; Guo D.
Article.Abstract: Adolescent major depressive disorder exhibits substantial intrinsic subtype heterogeneity, necessitating the development of subtype-specific therapeutic strategies. Using the Boston Adolescent Neuroimaging of Depression and Anxiety dataset, we identified two subtypes with distinct clinical features. For each subtype, we constructed a whole-brain model and performed virtual stimulation to assess regulatory effects at global (whole-brain) and regional (classical depression-related targets) levels. Here we show that the two subtypes require different but stable stimulation modalities, excitatory or inhibitory, to normalize brain activity. Optimal stimulation intensities for restoring static and dynamic features vary across targets and subtypes, whereas the stimulation modality remains consistent within each subtype. Notably, localized stimulation of subtype-specific targets within classical depression-related regions produces more effective and stable outcomes than whole-brain stimulation. These findings provide a computational framework for identifying subtype-specific regulatory strategies in adolescent major depressive disorder, bridging whole-brain modeling with potential clinical translation.

Article.Title: A glutamatergic projection from the central medial thalamic nucleus to the red nucleus regulates states of consciousness during sevoflurane anesthesia in mice
Article.Authors: Dai X.; Wu J.; Liu L.; Song W.; Wu H.; Gao S.; Zhang L.; Liu D.; Zhou Y.; Tian B.; Zhang P.; Chen S.; Chen D.; Zhang P.; Mei W.; Tang Z.
Article.Abstract: General anesthetics like sevoflurane are clinically essential, yet the neural circuits governing their induction of unconsciousness and recovery remain incompletely defined. Here, we show the potential involvement of the vesicular glutamate transporter 2 (Vglut2)-expressing glutamatergic neurons in the central medial thalamus (CMT Vglut2 neurons) in modulation states of consciousness under sevoflurane anesthesia. Results show that CMT Vglut2 neuron activity revealed a reduction during the loss of consciousness and a subsequent elevation upon recovery of consciousness under sevoflurane anesthesia. Chemogenetic activation of CMT Vglut2 neurons delays induction and hastened recovery from sevoflurane anesthesia. Moreover, during sustained sevoflurane anesthesia at steady state, optogenetic activation of CMT Vglut2 neurons facilitates cortical activation and behavioral recovery. During burst suppression under sevoflurane, this stimulation elicits cortical arousal and declines the burst-suppression ratio. Conversely, inhibiting CMT Vglut2 neurons via chemogenetic or optogenetic methods produces greater sensitivity to sevoflurane anesthesia and deepens cortical suppression, respectively. Monosynaptic connections from CMT Vglut2 neurons to red nucleus glutamatergic neurons (RN Vglut2 neurons) are identified using combined retrograde and anterograde tracing. During sevoflurane anesthesia, optogenetic activation of CMT Vglut2 -RN terminals triggers cortical activation. Overall, these findings identify the CMT Vglut2 -RN pathway as a neural circuit regulating cortical activation and behavioral arousal under various stages of sevoflurane-induced anesthesia.

Article.Title: Efficient structural information integration into protein language models with implicit mixture-of-experts ProBEiT
Article.Authors: Li M.; He S.; Sang T.; Li R.; Jiang Y.; Ren Y.; Zhao Y.; Yao S.; Yang G.; Wang X.; Lu H.
Article.Abstract: Protein language models can now predict function and mutational effects directly from sequence, yet only a few incorporate function-deciding structural information with minimal additional effort. Trained on 1.7 million AlphaFoldDB proteins, the 400 million-parameter model surpasses larger baselines across six tasks of fitness prediction and functional annotation, demonstrating enhanced understanding of sequence-structure-function relationships. Unlike existing billion-scale models, ProBEiT attains strong accuracy early in continual training period, reducing computational cost. In an experimental thermostability engineering task on glycerol-3-phosphate oxidase, it correctly identifies optimized variants with positive epistatic effects. These results show that tightly coupling structural context with sequence modeling in a modality-specialized framework enables efficient, high-performance protein engineering. ProBEiT integrates protein sequence and tokenized structure with deterministic implicit MoE routing, enabling efficient sequence structure modeling and strong performance in fitness prediction and thermostability engineering.

Article.Title: Hierarchical distortions in structure-function coupling linked to multiscale neurobiological characteristics in autism
Article.Authors: Kim T.; Namgung J.; Park Y.; Kim C.; Yoo K.; Satterthwaite T.; Di Martino A.; Bernhardt B.; Park B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Autism spectrum disorder is associated with widespread alterations in brain connectivity, but how structural and functional networks are jointly reorganized remains unclear. Here, we show that autism is associated with altered structure-function coupling, particularly in the hierarchical organization of sensory and association systems. Using brain imaging data from 91 individuals with autism and 67 typically developing controls, we model functional connectivity from structural networks using Riemannian optimization and examine communication across multiple steps. In the resulting simulated networks, hierarchical organization is comparable between groups at lower communication steps but becomes less differentiated in autism as communication extends across multiple steps. These alterations are associated with excitation/inhibition alterations, neurotransmitter distributions, gene expression, and multisensory processing. We also identify atypical connectivity involving the thalamus and putamen. Importantly, greater hierarchical distortion predicts more severe autistic symptoms, linking macroscale network organization with neurobiology and behavior. These findings highlight hierarchical structure-function coupling as a potential framework for understanding biological and behavioral characteristics in autism.

Article.Authors: Han X.; Zuo L.; Zhang Z.; Yu Y.; Hu J.; Long Q.; Tian X.; Wei J.; Zhang R.; Luo F.
Article.Abstract: Oligodendrocyte lineage cells (OLLCs) are essential for myelination and neuronal homeostasis, yet the evolutionary conservation of their transcriptional programs remains unclear. Together, these findings provide a comparative framework for understanding mammalian myelin biology, brain aging, and disease.

Article.Title: A role for the BBSome in restricting the entry of non-ciliary proteins into cilia
Article.Authors: Cevik S.; Yenisert F.; Kantarci H.; Pucak D.; Gallrein C.; Stöckl S.; Dünninger X.; Cakici O.; Stigloher C.; Kirstein J.; Kaplan O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cilia possess the inherent ability to restrict the entry of non-ciliary components through the ciliary gate. This misloading allows them to bypass the ciliary gate. Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) suggests the gate remains largely functional, supporting a potential two-step model of ciliary composition control: cargo selection/loading and ciliary gating. We propose that defects in cargo selection/loading (and potentially export) alter ciliary composition, allowing unintended protein entry.

Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Yang M.; Li A.; Liu Y.; Guo K.; Yang Y.; Yao Y.

These findings demonstrate that spinal GPR177 contributes to NP by activating astrocytes and regulating the C3/C3aR signaling pathway, suggesting the GPR177/C3/C3aR axis as a potential therapeutic target for NP.

Article.Authors: Amano H.; Tanabe H.; Bruner E.; Ogihara N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Encephalization is a hallmark of human evolution, but how regional brain morphology changed during early hominin evolution remains unclear. Here, we show regional brain morphological differences between sampled Australopithecus and early Homo specimens. Our reconstructions suggest that the posterior cerebellum was enlarged in early Homo compared with the sampled A. africanus specimens. In contrast, relative frontal lobe volume remains largely unchanged among the sampled fossils. We also identify enlargement of temporoparietal regions that, in modern humans, are associated with functions including social communication and tool use. By integrating fossil endocranial morphology with comparative neuroanatomical information from extant primates, the present approach provides a quantitative framework for generating and testing hypotheses about regional brain evolution in extinct hominins.

Article.Title: Serum albumin maintains Wnt3a water solubility and activity
Article.Authors: Yeo J.; Chae J.; Kwon S.; Han J.; Kusen I.; Lim J.; Lee H.; Kim H.; Haam S.; Cheong J.; Kim T.; Moon S.; Jung Y.; Lee J.; Kim C.
Article.Abstract: Wnt proteins regulate adult tissue homeostasis and repair by driving stem cell self-renewal and differentiation. This approach enables the conversion of conventional detergent-solubilized pWnt3a (CHAPS-pWnt3a) into SA-pWnt3a through dialysis-mediated detergent removal. Together, these findings define a simple and robust SA-based strategy for preserving Wnt3a activity, addressing a long-standing challenge in both experimental and therapeutic settings.

These findings suggest that Hippo pathway alterations and associated YAP/TAZ hyperactivation may serve as potential prognostic factors for stratifying patients undergoing ICI therapy. Article.Authors: Coppi L.; Severi I.; Bonacina F.; Villa S.; Peri C.; Longo R.; Senzacqua M.; Perugini J.; Galli C.; Pedretti S.; Mitro N.; Catapano A.; Norata G.; Giordano A.; De Fabiani E.; Crestani M.

Article.Title: Relationship between X chromosome mosaicism, neuroanatomy and cognitive performance in females
Article.Authors: Karipidis I.; Klabunde M.; Jordan T.; Chromik L.; Hosseini S.; Reiss A.; Hong D.
Article.Abstract: Females have two X chromosomes, one of which is inactivated early in development with specific regions and genes ‘escaping’ inactivation. Thus, X chromosome loss putatively results in decreased ‘dosage’ of X chromosome escapee and pseudoautosomal genes, impacting downstream pathways. Evidence from Turner syndrome (TS) indicates that X chromosome monosomy results in consistent neuroanatomical and cognitive phenotypes. However, it remains unclear whether mosaic karyotypes, with mixed proportions of 45X and 46XX cells, attenuate these phenotypes. Thus, mosaicism partially ‘rescues’ phenotypes linked to full 45X monosomy and may explain the role of the X chromosome not only across heterogeneous phenotypic expression in females, but also in sex differences observed in neuropsychiatric conditions. X chromosome mosaicism in Turner syndrome partly mitigates the brain and cognitive effects of X monosomy. Higher proportions of 46XX cells predict more typical brain structure and better visuospatial, motor, language, and cognitive performance.

Article.Authors: Yang C.; Zhang X.; Chen J.
Article.Abstract: Spatial transcriptomics links gene expression to tissue architecture, but detecting spatially variable genes at atlas scale remains difficult because biologically relevant patterns are multiscale, sparse, and often non-parametric. Article.Title: A review of self-supervised imaging phenotypes for genome-wide association studies
Article.Authors: Patel K.; Zhao X.; Xie Z.; Zhi D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Biobank-scale imaging-genomic cohorts enable genome-wide association studies (GWASs) of organ structure and function. Traditional approaches rely on expert-defined image-derived phenotypes (IDPs), which capture only a fraction of the biological variation in high-content images. Powered by artificial intelligence, self-supervised learning (SSL) learns representations directly from intrinsic image structures, creating scalable, data-driven traits. Here, we review the technical frameworks and challenges of SSL-based imaging genetics and their applications in brain MRI, cardiac MRI, and retinal imaging. Early studies suggest that these data-driven approaches can complement traditional IDPs and may expand the phenotypic space available for discovery of heritable imaging traits, although broader validation across cohorts, ancestries, scanners, and imaging protocols remains needed.

We generated a multiplex immunofluorescence dataset of 345 TNBC samples that showed OSR proteins GCLC and NQO1 are differentially expressed across tumor, immune, and stromal cells, and elevated in inflamed regions. We identified a mesenchymal-like tumor cell state characterized by co-expression of GCLC and vimentin (GCLC⁺VIM⁺), with increased proliferation and reduced anastasis-associated signatures, suggesting a vulnerability to chemotherapy. Consistently, TNBC cell lines with higher GCLC expression showed increased sensitivity to cisplatin. Moreover, patients with higher proportions of GCLC⁺VIM⁺ tumor cells had longer overall survival. Article.Title: Anatid herpesvirus 1 US10 recruits TRIM13 to ubiquitinate STING for autophagic degradation and immune suppression

Here we show that AnHV-1 tegument protein US10 suppresses innate immunity by targeting stimulator of interferon genes (STING) for autophagosome-lysosome degradation. US10 associates with STING and binds the autophagy-related protein microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 beta (LC3B), enhancing delivery to lysosomes. Mechanistically, US10 recruits E3 ligase tripartite motif-containing protein 13 (TRIM13) and induces stress in the endoplasmic reticulum through the Protein kinase R-like Reticulum Kinase (PERK). These synergistic actions inhibit type I interferon (IFN-I) production and IFN-stimulated gene expression. Article.Title: Individualized morphometric-similarity deviations in autism linked to cortical hierarchy and microarchitecture
Article.Authors: Mamat M.; Chen Y.; Li L.
Article.Abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) shows marked interindividual variation that complicates efforts to identify coherent neuroanatomical signatures. Here we combine subject-wise morphometric-similarity networks with hierarchical Bayesian normative regression to map per-region, per-subject departures from expected cortical organization across 308 parcels in a large multisite cohort. Normative z-maps reveal that ASD individuals have a higher prevalence of extreme, spatially focal deviations than controls, yet fewer than 12% of cases show extreme deviation in any single region. These deviations are not random: they preferentially redistribute morphometric similarity from association and heteromodal cortex toward sensory and visual territories and align with canonical cortical gradients. Network-level analyses identify a spatially localized subnetwork of altered similarity (dominant in occipito-temporal/visual nodes). Semi-supervised clustering of individual z-maps resolves a reproducible continuous axis of deviation whose opposite ends carry opposite global polarity and distinct cortical-molecular couplings revealed by transcriptomic and neurotransmitter-receptor density maps, as well as divergent cognitive meta-analytic associations. Together, these findings reframe ASD neuroanatomy as gradient-constrained and molecularly tethered at the individual level and support normative, subject-wise approaches for mechanism-informed stratification. Normative models of morphometric similarity across 1,344 brains map where each autistic individual’s cortex departs from expectation. Article.Title: Maltreatment predicts centiles of individual variation from normative brain growth in children
Article.Authors: Mohn J.; Bauer M.; Hoffmann F.; Rasmussen J.; Tietze A.; Entringer S.; Winter S.; Buss C.; Heim C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Exposure to maltreatment in childhood is posited to profoundly disrupt brain development with adverse consequences for cognitive development and health across the lifespan. Here we use “brain charts” from the largest available neuroimaging database to quantify individual brain volumes relative to normative brain growth distributions in 299 children, aged 3 to 13 years, including 123 children with clinically verified maltreatment exposure. Using magnetic resonance imaging, we obtain volumes of cortical grey, total white, and subcortical grey matter and derive chart-based centiles for each child and tissue type. In our sample, children with maltreatment exposure exhibit lower mean brain centiles across tissues than unexposed children. Associations of greater maltreatment severity with lower brain centiles do not survive correction for multiple comparisons. Article.Title: Emerging links between gut dysbiosis, aryl hydrocarbon receptor activation, and Parkinson’s disease
Article.Authors: Aziz N.; Kortagere S.
Article.Abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD), the second most common progressive neurodegenerative disorder, is classically defined as a motor disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuron loss in the substantia nigra and motor dysfunction. Increasing evidence, however, identifies PD as a multisystem disorder with early non-motor features, including sleep, psychiatric, and gastrointestinal disturbances, implicating the gut-brain axis. Tryptophan metabolism through serotonin, kynurenine, and indole pathways generates bioactive metabolites, many of which regulate the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR). AhR is a ligand-activated transcription factor involved in xenobiotic metabolism through canonical signaling pathways; however, growing evidence supports its role in immune balance, glial responses, and barrier integrity. Altered AhR signaling may therefore connect gut dysbiosis and disrupted tryptophan metabolism to sustained, systemic and central inflammation in PD. This review examines gut dysbiosis, tryptophan metabolism, and AhR signaling as potential mechanisms underlying idiopathic PD and highlights their relevance to early diagnosis and disease-modifying therapies.

Article.Title: Predicting transcriptional burst kinetics from histone modifications with deep learning
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Zhang Z.; Huang Z.; Yu X.; Wang Z.; Qiu H.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: Transcription is inherently bursty, and burst frequency and burst size provide mechanistically informative phenotypes that are not uniquely determined by mean expression alone. DeepBurst uses self-attention to learn combinatorial, position-dependent predictive patterns, with training labels inferred from single-cell transcriptome data using mechanistic bursting models. Across three human cell lines and two label-inference procedures, DeepBurst achieves consistent performance under chromosome-based splits and shows strong cross-cell type generalization. Model interpretation shows that burst frequency benefits from broader chromatin context, whereas burst size depends more strongly on promoter-proximal signals. Model-constrained in silico perturbations further identify histone-profile changes predicted to shift bursting regimes. DeepBurst therefore enables genome-wide mapping from readily measurable histone-modification landscapes to hard-to-assay transcriptional bursting dynamics, while generating testable hypotheses for future perturbation studies.

Article.Title: Hepatitis E virus genome plasticity: a marker of chronicity and therapy failure?
Article.Authors: Janshoff S.; Sirkinti L.; Nocke M.; Bechtel T.; Gömer A.; Brüggemann Y.; Steinmann E.; Brown R.; Todt D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is a globally distributed zoonotic pathogen, spread by contaminated food and blood products, and a leading cause of acute viral hepatitis. Recent data indicate that the HEV genome contains a highly heterogeneous hypervariable region (HVR) that can tolerate extensive genomic rearrangements, especially among immunocompromised patients. These rearrangements can increase HEV replication in tissue-culture and have further been observed in HEV-infected patients. Insertions comprise either duplications of virus-derived sequences, or alternatively, host-derived sequence fragments and exhibit enrichment of specific amino acids and functional motifs. However, the molecular mechanisms driving these insertions, as well as their functional significance, remain largely unexplored. Given that sequences not required for infectivity or replication are typically rapidly eliminated in small RNA viruses such as HEV, the persistence of HVR insertions suggests a potential biological role in HEV replication and/or pathogenesis. This review summarizes our current understanding of the role of HVR insertions during HEV infection, as well as the potential mechanisms underlying these insertions. We further discuss the factors driving the selection of genomic insertions and speculate on their functional role by analyzing over 650 publicly available HEV genotype 3 genome sequences and systematically cataloging identified insertions.

Article.Title: Identification of candidate key genes involved in natural rubber biosynthesis in Periploca sepium
Article.Authors: Lu G.; Yong J.; An Y.; Lang S.; Zhang H.; Chen R.
Article.Abstract: Natural rubber is a critical industrial material facing supply shortages. Periploca sepium has emerged as a promising alternative for producing the rubber component cis-polyisoprene. To investigate its biosynthesis, we performed genome and transcriptome sequencing. Our results indicate that this plant possesses complete mevalonic acid (MVA), 1-deoxy-D-xylulose-5-phosphate/2-C-methyl-D-erythritol-4-phosphate (DXP/MEP), and polyisoprene pathways, as well as contains corresponding rubber particle membrane proteins. Using weighted gene co-expression network analysis, we identified 11 key genes positively correlated with levels of cis-polyisoprene and precursor allylic diphosphates (IPP/DMAPP, GPP, FPP, GGPP). Overexpressing acetoacetyl-CoA thiolase, 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA synthase, 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA reductase, and 1-deoxy-D-xylulose-5-phosphate reductoisomerase genes from the MVA and DXP/MEP pathways in P. sepium increased IPP/DMAPP levels. Molecular docking and enzyme assays indicated that cis-prenyltransferase exhibits the highest affinity for FPP, suggesting it is the dominant initiator of IPP condensation in cis-polyisoprene biosynthesis. Overexpressing the FPP synthase gene enhanced FPP levels, leading to increased cis-poly7isoprene content. Overexpressing cis-prenyltransferase, small rubber particle protein, and rubber elongation factor genes, especially in combination, significantly raised cis-polyisoprene content and high-molecular-weight proportions. These findings demonstrate that targeted gene up-regulation can improve both rubber yield and quality in P. sepium. The candidate key genes involved in rubber biosynthesis in P. sepium were identified via genome and transcriptome sequencing combined with WGCNA. Up-regulation of the key genes by overexpression, especially in combination, can improve both rubber yield and quality in P. sepium.

Article.Title: In vivo replication of a fully functional nerve net in a clonally reproducing animal
Article.Authors: Sakib E.; Hofacker L.; Noack C.; Ströbel F.; Giez C.; Wittlieb J.; Klimovich A.; Bosch T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Nerve nets are considered the evolutionarily oldest form of nervous system. How such networks develop and how complex nervous systems become fully functional is largely unknown. In a phylogenetically ancient animal, the freshwater polyp Hydra , we demonstrate how a nerve net consisting of distinct neuronal populations is precisely replicated over the course of asexual proliferation by budding. During this process, precursor cells first accumulate at the site of the emerging neural network, followed by a stepwise formation of functional neural circuits composed of distinct neuronal populations. These circuits become arranged according to an accurately controlled spatiotemporal pattern and take control of behaviors independently of the existing parental network. Since similar processes also govern the formation of more complex nervous systems in other invertebrates and vertebrates, we suggest that the basic requirements for a neuronal network to replicate were already in place at the beginning of the evolution of the nervous system.

Article.Title: Evolution towards higher unitary conductance in mammals makes BK channels more efficient and precise
Article.Authors: Hepburn I.; Hellemans S.; Taniguchi T.; Bourguignon T.; De Schutter E.
Article.Abstract: The large-conductance calcium-activated potassium (BK) channel plays a critical role in neuronal excitability and spike timing precision. We show that mammalian BK channels are activated more efficiently by calcium and generate stronger repolarizing currents than lower unitary conductance channels. Channels with lower unitary conductance require greater channel density in the cell membrane, leading to stronger competition for calcium and reduced activation. In contrast, high unitary conductance channels minimize competition, enabling more effective activation and repolarization. Incorporating these channel properties into a neuronal model revealed that mammalian-type BK channels enhance spike-timing precision, consistent with the evolution of fine motor control and advanced neuronal processing in mammals.

Article.Authors: Klaourakis K.; Kulkarni S.; Zvonickova K.; Kalisch-Smith J.; Smart N.; Sparrow D.; Jackson D.; Riley P.; Vieira J.

Article.Authors: Wang H.; Kroeschell G.; Zhu Y.; Mumm J.; Yi J.

Article.Authors: Krishna N.; Menon A.; Kumaran M.; Kesireddy D.; Venkatesh I.

Article.Abstract: Functional recovery after spinal cord injury (SCI) remains challenging, requiring therapeutic targets. In neurons, DCLK1 inhibited KATNA1-induced neurite outgrowth, whereas DCLK1 inhibition restored this effect. To address this, we propose a series of recommendations to establish the foundation for a future standardized framework for coral deoxygenation methodology. Such efforts are critical to establish a robust consensus of scientific data to support effective management of reef deoxygenation. Article.Title: SGLT2 inhibitors attenuate diabetic kidney disease by suppressing YAP dependent ferroptosis
Article.Authors: Feng L.; Feng C.; Li H.; Wang T.; Zhang H.; Zhao Y.; Liu H.
Article.Abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors provide renal protection in diabetic kidney disease (DKD) through mechanisms beyond glucose lowering, but these remain incompletely understood. Here we show that Yes-associated protein 1 (YAP)-dependent ferroptosis contributes to renal tubular injury in DKD and that suppression of this pathway underlies part of the renoprotective effects of dapagliflozin. In human DKD kidney tissues, nuclear YAP accumulation correlates positively with ferroptosis markers acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) and 4-hydroxynonenal, and negatively with renal function. In a diabetic rat model, dapagliflozin attenuates renal dysfunction, tubular injury, and fibrosis alongside reduced YAP activation and ferroptosis. In high-glucose-treated renal tubular epithelial cells, YAP promotes nuclear translocation, upregulates ACSL4 and transferrin receptor expression, induces iron accumulation and mitochondrial damage, and drives ferroptotic cell death. YAP knockdown and pharmacological inhibition both confirm an upstream regulatory role for YAP in ferroptosis. Mechanistically, YAP and TEAD4 enhance ACSL4 promoter activity through a conserved TEAD-binding motif, an effect suppressed by dapagliflozin. These findings identify the YAP/TEAD4-ACSL4 axis as a therapeutic target underlying glucose-independent renoprotection by SGLT2 inhibition.

Article.Title: Integrating corneal endophenotypes with classic GWAS approaches identifies novel keratoconus loci
Article.Authors: Shabani H.; Buch G.; Lee S.; van Camp G.; van den Biggelaar F.; Haudum C.; Smoor M.; Geerards A.; Ghanbari M.; Habeeb M.; Pfeiffer N.; Marx-Groß S.; N/A N/A.; Wesselius A.; van der Kallen C.; van Asten F.; A. M. Blokland G.; Wisse R.; Faro V.; Bergen A.; Berendschot T.; Koppen C.; Obermayer-Pietsch B.; van der Heide F.; Dickman M.
Article.Abstract: Keratoconus is a chronic progressive disorder characterized by corneal deformation. It usually affects adolescents and young adults, reducing vision and decreasing the quality of life. Here we show that integrating genetic analyses of corneal traits with large case-control studies improves the discovery and annotation of genetic factors underlying keratoconus. Analysing corneal imaging measurements from 16,464 individuals, we identify four informative corneal traits and use them in a multi-trait genetic analysis that uncovers 80 significant loci associated with one or more of the selected traits. Twenty-five of these loci (5 novel) are also associated with keratoconus (Bonferroni-corrected P ≤ 6.3 × 10 −4 ). A subsequent meta-analysis of 6,372 cases and 593,541 controls identifies 51 significant keratoconus loci ( P ≤ 5.0 × 10 −8 ), including eight not previously reported. Gene-set analysis implicates pathways involved in extracellular matrix integrity, glucosylceramidase regulation and cellular differentiation. These findings expand the genetic landscape of keratoconus, provide insight into the biological mechanisms underlying disease development, and support future efforts in genetic risk profiling and therapeutic target discovery.

Article.Title: Chronic XBP1s signaling promotes B cell dysfunction and anergy
Article.Authors: Deng B.; Zaleski O.; Hill M.; Seeto S.; Benson D.; Woyach J.; Hu C.; Liu B.
Article.Abstract: B cells are central mediators of humoral immunity, and their development is tightly regulated to prevent autoreactivity. The unfolded protein response (UPR) plays a crucial role in supporting the high biosynthetic demands of B cells. The transcription factor XBP1s, a key effector of the UPR’s IRE1α branch, has been implicated in plasma cell differentiation, but its role in early B cell development and tolerance remains unclear. Here we demonstrate that sustained activation of XBP1s shapes anergic B cell development and peripheral tolerance. We generated a B cell-specific XBP1s knock-in mouse model that induces chronic XBP1s expression. We find that chronic XBP1s overexpression drives the accumulation of anergic transitional 3 B cells, which exhibits attenuated activation responses to both BCR and TLR stimulation. Mechanistically, XBP1s overexpression upregulates the anergy-associated factor Egr2 and suppresses Irf4 expression. Our study provides insights into how dysregulated XBP1s expression may contribute to immune tolerance and dysfunction.

Article.Title: Molecular mechanisms of NLR proteins in inflammasome activation
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Ji K.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: Nucleotide-binding domain and leucine-rich repeat-containing proteins (NLRs) are central mediators of inflammasome signaling, activating caspase-1 to drive pyroptotic cell death and pro-inflammatory responses. Although NLR activation is generally thought to involve conformational rearrangements that oligomerize their N- or C-terminal death domains to nucleate ASC or pro-caspase-1 oligomerization, the molecular mechanisms that enable these transitions vary substantially among family members. Here, we highlight recent structural advances that reveal how distinct NLRs are activated and assemble into higher-order signaling platforms, providing mechanistic insights into the diverse activation mechanisms that converge on a common inflammatory outcome.
