Article.Title: Organelle associations and metabolic rewiring of size-defined hepatic lipid droplets
Article.Authors: Liao Q.; Fu X.; Wang Y.; Xu Y.; Cao Z.; Wang Y.; Pan B.; Wang J.; Liu P.; Yang Z.; Zhang S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lipid droplet (LD) size is a key determinant of hepatic lipid metabolism, yet the molecular programming routing size-defined subpopulations to distinct fates remains unclear. Here we show that a fractionation workflow resolves hepatic LDs by size and organelle association, defining a high-confidence intrinsic LD proteome. Moreover, comparative proteomics of fasted livers reveals a clear ‘division of labor’: Large LDs (L-LDs) function as specialized mitochondrion-coupled ‘putative fueling hubs’, whereas small LDs (S-LDs) serve as lysosome-coupled ‘putative trafficking and turnover hubs’. This interaction map is highly plastic; metabolic stress (fasting or steatosis) triggers a programmatic remodeling where lysosomal machinery is inducibly recruited to S-LDs. Crucially, in vivo stress recruits mitochondria to both pools, supporting a ‘parallel programs’ model where S-LD-associated mitochondria are hypothesized to power the energy-intensive degradative machinery. These findings establish that metabolic state leverages LD size to direct organelle partnerships, nominating the small-LD lysosomal axis as a critical regulatory node in metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD).

Article.Title: Vascular tree structure-based perfusion phantom fabrication using modified Hele-Shaw cell method
Article.Authors: Das S.; Rakshe M.; Sarkar S.; Paul R.; Marathe S.; Abraham N.; Gandhi P.; Varma H.
Article.Abstract: Tissue phantoms mimicking microvasculature and perfusion are essential for vasculature modelling and calibrating imaging systems, which require faithful replication of vascular geometry and flow. Conventional fabrication methods, including lithographic micromachining and additive manufacturing remain constrained by predefined designs, rectangular channel cross-sections, limited scalability, and high production costs. Here we present a lithography-free approach based on a modified lifted Hele-Shaw cell method where, unlike above-mentioned methods, random fractal-like vascular structures emerge naturally. This results in channels of widths 100-1000 μ m with smooth Gaussian cross-section and natural diameter tapering. We demonstrate this with four phantom designs: a planar vascular tree, a cerebral vasculature-mimicking guided tree network, a conformable curved substrate and a retinal vasculature-mimicking network. Flow visualisation with laser speckle contrast imaging shows close agreement with in vivo observations and consistency with the generalized Murray’s law. This approach uniquely combines fractal-like network formation leading towards realistic vascular geometry and flow characteristics, offering an in vitro alternative to small animal vascular models.

Article.Title: FOXO3 induces chromatin changes in a model of DNA damage-induced senescence
Article.Authors: Brown A.; Arevalo J.; Holcom A.; Finch A.; Maybury-Lewis S.; McNamara A.; Webb A.
Article.Abstract: FOXO transcription factors are critical for cellular homeostasis and the stress response and have been implicated in longevity in several species. Yet, how these factors function at the chromatin level in differing conditions in human cells is poorly understood. Here, we take an integrated multi-omics approach to identify the chromatin-level mechanisms by which FOXO3 coordinates transcriptional programs in replicating cells and in a model of cellular senescence. In a DNA-damage induced senescence, FOXO3 levels are elevated early in senescence entry. Increased FOXO3 expression induces expression of chromatin remodeling factors, and impacts chromatin accessibility across the genome together with SWI/SNF chromatin remodelers. As cells enter DNA-damage induced senescence, FOXO3 is essential for chromatin remodeling and reprogramming of a genomic network that functions to modulate cell stress and lineage-specific cellular functions. Altogether, we identify a FOXO3-SWI/SNF network that regulates key cellular processes including metabolism, proteostasis, epigenetics, and cell lineage, and is dynamically controlled under DNA damaging conditions.

Article.Title: Large-scale functional overlap between dorsal and ventral object-responsive networks
Article.Authors: Simmons C.; Behrmann M.; Ayzenberg V.
Article.Abstract: The processes of acting on and recognizing objects have traditionally been attributed to dorsal and ventral visual pathways, respectively. Although extensive evidence suggests that the two pathways interact, the extent and the strength of these interactions across whole-brain networks remain unclear. In two experiments, we characterized the whole-brain network connections of object-selective regions in each pathway using functional magnetic resonance imaging data acquired while participants viewed objects. Here, we show substantial spatial overlap in connectivity networks generated from the dorsal and the ventral seed region—with greater similarity between object networks within an individual than each network shows across individuals. This overlap persists across viewing of tools and non-tools and even after controlling for the shared variance between pathways. Together, these findings reveal that dorsal and ventral pathways form highly overlapping and distributed networks in the service of object perception.

Article.Title: Estradiol deficiency aggravates AngII-induced vascular remodeling by failing to inhibit GRK2 through ERα-mediated autophagy
Article.Authors: Ji M.; Song N.; Adu-Amankwaah J.; Liu C.; Wang G.; Zhou W.; Hao Y.; Shi Y.; Wu J.; Li K.
Article.Abstract: Hypertension acts as a critical cardiovascular risk factor that drives vascular remodeling, which manifests as vascular media thickening triggered by excessive proliferation and migration of vascular smooth muscle cells. Angiotensin II promotes vascular remodeling by upregulating G protein-coupled receptor kinase 2. Estradiol deficiency, particularly among postmenopausal individuals, increases susceptibility to hypertension by overactivating the renin-angiotensin system, while the precise mechanism remains unkown. Here we show that estradiol inhibits G protein-coupled receptor kinase 2 to ameliorate hypertensive vascular remodeling. Ovariectomy in spontaneously hypertensive rats exacerbate hypertension, while estradiol supplementation significantly reduced blood pressure and attenuated vascular remodeling. Mechanistically, Estradiol downregulated G protein-coupled receptor kinase 2 expression, leading to decreased β-arrestin2 recruitment and ERK signaling, thereby reducing vascular smooth muscle cell proliferation and migration. Additionally, Autophagy or estrogen receptor α blockade abolishes the effects of estradiol on G protein-coupled receptor kinase 2 degradation. This study provides a potential therapeutic strategy for hypertensive vascular remodeling. Ji and colleagues show that estradiol (E2) enhances autophagy and ERalpha-AMPK signaling in a mouse model of hypertension and vascular remodeling.

Article.Title: Phospholipid remodeling of the cardiomyocyte membrane affects cardiac function
Article.Authors: Bujo S.; Fujiwara T.; Kubota M.; Toko H.; Kawana H.; Kano K.; Ito M.; Ishizuka M.; Umei M.; Kadowaki H.; Zhai B.; Kishikawa R.; Takeda N.; Harada M.; Takeda N.; Aoki J.; Komuro I.
Article.Abstract: Membrane phospholipid (PL) remodeling has been linked to various mammalian metabolic and oncogenic pathologies, but its role in the heart remains elusive. Here, we investigated the role of PL remodeling in cardiac function. Lysophospholipid acyltransferase 7 (LPLAT7)/lysophosphatidylglycerol acyltransferase 1 (LPGAT1) remodels phosphatidylcholine (PC) and phosphatidylethanolamine (PE), two major cardiac membrane PL species. Public functional genomics data revealed downregulation of LPLAT7/LPGAT1 gene expression in failing human hearts and murine cardiomyocytes. Cardiomyocyte-specific Lplat7/Lpgat1-deficient male mice exhibited selective remodeling of cardiac PC and PE composition, including diminished stearic acid- and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA)-enriched species. LPLAT7/LPGAT1 suppression induced myocardial contractile dysfunction associated with cAMP-dependent protein kinase (PKA) activation and abnormal calcium handling, partially rescued by pharmacological PKA inhibition. Conversely, Lplat7/Lpgat1 overexpression partially improved pressure overload-induced cardiac dysfunction with selective restoration of PC(40:6), a major stearic acid/DHA-enriched PC species. These findings highlight the contributory role of LPLAT7/LPGAT1-dependent membrane PL remodeling in cardiac function and heart failure. Cardiomyocyte LPLAT7/LPGAT1 regulates membrane phospholipid composition and cardiac function. Its loss reduces stearic acid- and DHA-enriched phosphatidylcholine and causes PKA activation, abnormal calcium handling, and contractile dysfunction, whereas overexpression partially improves pressure overload-induced dysfunction

Article.Title: A Colletotrichum orbiculare-based fungal model recapitulates conserved cellular defects of Niemann–Pick type C disease and enables therapeutic evaluation
Article.Authors: Sano H.; Takezawa S.; Saomoto N.; Chiba A.; Tanaka C.; Kato N.; Nishiuchi T.; Nishisaka H.; Kitatani K.; Kodama S.; Kubo Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Niemann–Pick type C disease is a fatal lysosomal storage disorder caused by mutations in NPC1 or NPC2 , leading to lipid accumulation and progressive neurodegeneration. Current mammalian models recapitulate major pathological features but are limited by long disease courses and low throughput. Here, we establish the plant-pathogenic fungus Colletotrichum orbiculare as a scalable eukaryotic model of Niemann–Pick type C disease. Introduction of disease-associated mutations into fungal NPC1 or NPC2 homologs abolishes pathogenicity, showing that NPC dysfunction compromises lipid-dependent morphogenesis required for host penetration. Conversely, human NPC1 partially restores fungal infection. Together, these findings support functional conservation of NPC-dependent cellular processes across kingdoms. Miglustat and 2-hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin restore pathogenicity through distinct lipid pathways. These complementary modes of rescue indicate that NPC1 and NPC2 dysfunction converges on lipid-dependent morphogenesis closely linked to actin organization. By connecting lipid metabolism, actin organization, and pharmacological rescue to a measurable infection outcome, this fungal model provides a tractable and scalable platform for mechanistic and therapeutic exploration.

Article.Title: Flippability of Escherichia coli membrane proteins under lipid stress reveals a new job for old genes
Article.Authors: Sawasato K.; Bogdanov M.
Article.Abstract: Normally, the “flip-flop” motion is reserved for small lipid molecules which move from one leaflet of the membrane to the other, and even that process is very slow without the aid of specific enzymes. Unexpectedly, we recently found that despite a prohibitively high energy barrier, Escherichia coli cardiolipin (CL) synthase A (ClsA) flips its large catalytic domain across the inner (cytoplasmic) membrane (IM) when cells were fully or partially depleted of phosphatidylethanolamine (PE) and that this was necessary to support cell viability. Here, we demonstrated that production of the non-native phospholipid phosphatidylcholine (PC) in PE-depleted cells prevents ClsA flipping and halts cell growth, a phenotype rescued by constitutively inverted ClsA. Surprisingly, properly oriented lactose permease (LacY) acts as a multicopy suppressor, rescuing the growth defect in the -PE+PC cells. These data indicate that neutral PC regulates the membrane topology of ClsA and LacY, and subsequently the appearance of CL to the periplasmic leaflet required for viability. Therefore, ClsA and potentially LacY may achieve varied roles from the same amino acid sequence through an unusual flip-flopping mechanism. This fruitful “repurposing” of genetic material highlights the remarkable adaptability of living organisms and their membranes. Altering E. coli lipids disrupts growth, but controlled membrane protein flipping simulates natural selection and resemonstrates that membrane proteins can re-evolve under the selective pressure of an altered lipid bilayer.

Article.Title: The representation of order and randomness in the auditory cortex
Article.Authors: Bashari S.; Jankowski M.; Nelken I.
Article.Abstract: Perception fundamentally relies on the brain’s ability to extract structure from its sensory environment. The auditory cortex possesses significant sensitivity to statistical regularities in tone sequences. To examine this phenomenon at the single-neuron level, we used multitone sequences and recorded responses from the auditory cortex of awake adult female Sprague Dawley rats. Tones were presented in periodic sequences with a fixed, repeated cycle; in a fully random condition; or in an intermediate condition in which cycles were maintained, but tones were randomly permuted within each cycle (random cycle condition). Units showed a continuum of preferences between order-preferring neurons and randomness-preferring neurons. Unexpectedly, we found sensitivity to the position of sounds in the cycle (‘phase modulation’). The strongest and most consistent phase modulations were in the responses to the random cycle condition. Finally, we show how such phase sensitivity may emerge from a simple, biologically plausible computation. Neurons in the auditory cortex exhibit a continuum of preferences from order to randomness, and show sensitivity to the position of tones in abstract repeating patterns.

Article.Title: VASP cooperates with zyxin to organize mechanically competent adhesions
Article.Authors: Chung W.; Boujemaa-Paterski R.; Winograd-Katz S.; Eibauer M.; Geiger B.; Medalia O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Focal adhesions (FAs) are dynamic macromolecular assemblies that anchor the actin cytoskeleton to the extracellular matrix via integrin receptors, thereby regulating cell morphology and migration. Here, we show that the vasodilator-stimulated phosphoprotein (VASP) cooperates with the mechanosensitive scaffold protein zyxin to maintain FA during maturation under actomyosin-generated tension. Using sequential CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing and cryo-electron tomography, we resolved the in situ nanoarchitecture of the FA-stress fiber interface. We establish that tropomyosin decorates the dorsal aspect of adhesion-associated stress fibers independently of VASP and zyxin. VASP and zyxin are required for the assembly of dense, aligned actin bundles with uniform polarity, oriented with their barbed ends toward the cell edge. Live-cell imaging and quantitative analyses of cells confined on micropatterns reveal that VASP and zyxin cooperate to preserve the mechanical coupling between FAs and the actin cytoskeleton under contractile load. Our findings establish that VASP and zyxin perform distinct yet complementary functions to organize FA-associated actin into mechanically competent force-transmitting units.

Article.Title: BUB signaling in cancer and molecular insights into targeted therapies
Article.Authors: Baweja B.; Saini C.; Vats P.; Soni R.; Jangir K.; Patidar P.; Kumar A.; Nema R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Spindle Assembly Checkpoint (SAC) is vital for proper chromosome segregation during cell division and for maintaining genomic integrity; its disruption can cause aneuploidy and tumors. The BUB gene family ensures SAC fidelity by regulating kinetochore–microtubule attachments and mitotic progression. Dysregulation leads to chromosomal instability (CIN), contributing to cancer progression, heterogeneity, metastasis, and therapy resistance. Beyond mitosis, BUB proteins influence DNA repair, chromatin remodeling, transcription, and immune responses. They interact with cell cycle and genome stability pathways, impacting cancer prognosis and therapy response. Research is ongoing to validate BUB proteins as biomarkers and develop inhibitors, possibly combined with immunotherapies or DNA-damaging agents for resistant tumors. This review summarizes their functions, highlighting their potential in personalized cancer treatment.

Article.Title: A circRNA-microRNA-Pdcd1 axis drives microglial activation and retinal ganglion cell degeneration
Article.Authors: Sun L.; Ke X.; Yu J.; Wei J.; Gu J.; Zhou W.; Cen Y.; Huang J.; Zhang X.; Zhang J.; Zhang S.; Liu X.; Ji Y.; Yan W.; Pan S.; Zhou M.; Wu W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Retinal ganglion cell (RGC) degeneration is the primary cause of vision loss, driven by the complicated effects of intrinsic neuronal damage and neuroinflammation. However, current single-target therapies fail to address these dual pathological challenges. CircRNAs, functioning through ceRNA networks, represent a multi-target intervention due to their stability. Here we show that, using whole‑transcriptome sequencing of optic nerve crush (ONC), we bioinformatically predicted nine candidate ceRNA networks. Among these, the network centered on circAgtpbp1 was significantly up-regulated post-injury, independent of its host gene. Mechanistically, circAgtpbp1 functions as a ceRNA by sequestering miR-3098-3p, thereby de-repressing the translation of PD-1 ( Pdcd1 ). In the ONC model, this upregulation of PD-1 protein amplifies microglial activation, creating a pathogenic non-cell-autonomous inflammatory amplification loop that drives RGC degeneration. Our findings not only uncover a novel circRNA-mediated mechanism in neurodegeneration but also identify the circAgtpbp1-miR-3098-3p-Pdcd1-microglia axis as a promising therapeutic target for neuroprotective interventions.

Article.Title: Towards a comprehensive landscape and mechanism understanding of virus-disease associations
Article.Authors: Wu Y.; You R.; Feng Y.; Lu S.; Chen S.; Fu P.; Zhu Z.; Lu C.; Zhang Z.; Xu L.; Li H.; Wang X.; Wang X.; Huang Q.; Liu X.; Xu Z.; Dong G.; Li S.; Hu X.; Xiang Z.; Hu Y.; Mao L.; Miao Z.; Meng X.; Peng Y.
Article.Abstract: Viruses are linked to human diseases through complex molecular mechanisms, yet a comprehensive investigation of virus-disease associations and their molecular basis remains lacking. We curated 3,555 high-confidence virus-disease associations involving 267 viruses and 954 diseases through text-mining over 28 million PubMed abstracts followed by rigorous manual verification, establishing the most comprehensive resource in this field to date. We then developed AVD, a user-friendly online database to store, visualize, and analyze these associations and their molecular mechanisms. Our analysis revealed that virus-disease association patterns are significantly influenced by viral taxonomy, phenotype, and key biological traits such as transmissibility, transmission routes, and tissue tropism. Molecular analysis identified a core set of bridging genes involved in the majority of virus-disease associations. Notably, these bridging genes were extensively involved in viral infections and diseases, and exhibit distinct characteristics, including a high proportion of secreted proteins, elevated expression across human tissues, and high centrality in the human protein-protein interaction network. Furthermore, we developed a machine-learning model capable of accurately predicting virus-disease associations. Collectively, this study provides a valuable data resource and analytical framework for studying virus-disease relationships and offers novel insights into their molecular mechanisms. In this manuscript the authors analyze viral-disease associations and identified that virus-disease associations are significantly influenced by viral taxonomic, phenotype, and their biological traits. Genes that may mediate the viral-disease associations are also discovered. A database called AVD (Association of Virus and human Diseases) is also constructed to facilitate the storage and convenient analysis of the associations.

Article.Title: Metabolic characteristics and evolutionary history of the nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterial endosymbionts of pennate diatoms
Article.Authors: Cheung S.; Cornejo-Castillo F.; Bianchini G.; Coale T.; Vieyra-Mexicano C.; Sánchez-Baracaldo P.; Zehr J.; Turk-Kubo K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria are important sources of bioavailable nitrogen on Earth. Some nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria are endosymbionts of algae, and recently one of them, UCYN-A2, was shown to be an early-stage organelle (nitroplast) of haptophytes. These biological associations are important models for studying co-evolution and organellogenesis. Endosymbioses between Rhopalodiaceae diatoms and nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria (spheroid bodies, SBs) are widespread in marine and freshwater ecosystems, but their adaptation and evolution remain unclear. We found that the genomes and metabolic characteristics of marine and freshwater SBs are remarkably similar. Purifying selection pressures dominated SB diversification both within marine and freshwater habitats and across habitat boundaries. The metabolic characteristics and genome reduction of SBs are substantially different from UCYN-A, suggesting different evolutionary journeys for the endosymbionts influenced by different hosts. We estimated that the marine SBs diversified ~185 Mya (95% highest posterior density (HPD): 340-88 Mya), which was within a prolonged oligotrophic period in the ocean, during which UCYN-A also diversified. The freshwater SBs diversified from the marine SBs ~137 Mya (95% HPD: 258-66 Mya) and further diversified ~80 Mya (95% HPD: 157-31 Mya), when sea level was increasing. Our study reveals the genetic and metabolic underpinnings characterizing the nitrogen-fixing cyanobacterial endosymbionts of Rhopalodiaceae diatoms.

Article.Title: Conserved Core but Divergent Biochemical Features of RAS-MAPK Signalling in C. elegans
Article.Authors: Bernal Astrain G.; Strakhova R.; Amro J.; Banerjee R.; Teszner E.; Decorso I.; Reiner D.; Smith M.
Article.Abstract: Genetic studies in Caenorhabditis elegans have established core principles of RAS-MAPK signalling. These nematodes encode three RAS proteins: LET-60/KRAS is essential for vulval induction, while RAS-1 and RAS-2 are orthologs of RRAS/RRAS2 and MRAS, respectively, but remain biologically and biochemically uncharacterized. We here present a comprehensive biochemical analysis of all three C. elegans RAS proteins, defining nucleotide cycling and effector interactions. We show that conserved RAS scaffolds are tuned by sequence variation to balance signalling with developmental fidelity. LET-60 has significantly impaired nucleotide exchange and changing its sequence to match human KRAS induces a protruding vulva phenotype in vivo. RAS-1 rapidly exchanges GDP-to-GTP, whereas RAS-2 remains consistently GDP-bound. LET-60 engages the RAF ortholog LIN-45 through a divergent interface, and RAS-1 unexpectedly drives SOC-2:RAS:PP1C holophosphatase assembly in a nucleotide-independent manner. Our findings reveal both conserved and distinctive biochemical features underlying RAS signalling and suggest species-specific tuning of this key proliferation pathway.

Article.Title: Age-related shift towards feedforward motor control under uncertainty
Article.Authors: Kreter N.; Sager C.; Barany D.; Dundon N.; Marneweck M.
Article.Abstract: Humans perform movements in the face of uncertainty on a daily basis. To accomplish these tasks without error, young adults frequently rely on feedback-mediated motor strategies that allow them to update their movement as uncertainty evolves. However, it remains unclear how aging impacts the ability to plan and execute movement under uncertain conditions. Here we use a “go-before-you-know” pointing task completed during functional neuroimaging to examine how aging influences movement planning under uncertainty. Behaviorally, young adults employed a strategy consistent with feedback-mediated control, biasing their trajectories toward the more likely target when uncertainty was low, and intermediate to potential targets when uncertainty was high. Older adults employed a different approach, shifting away from an intermediate reaching strategy, particularly under high uncertainty, suggesting a shift toward feedforward control. Neuroimaging mirrored these behavioral patterns, revealing that young adults encoded task uncertainty and movement direction in sensorimotor regions more strongly than older adults. Overall, these findings suggest that aging diminishes the ability to flexibly encode task-related uncertainty, leading to a shift towards feedforward control strategies.

Article.Title: Distinct genetic perturbations at the endogenous Atf4 locus uncouple polyadenylation loss from transcriptional readthrough
Article.Authors: Zhang Z.; Wu T.; Chen Z.; Chen D.; Ye M.; Chen J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Transcription termination by RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) is coupled to co-transcriptional cleavage and polyadenylation directed by the canonical AAUAAA polyadenylation signal (PAS). However, the in vivo requirement of the canonical PAS for termination fidelity remains unclear. Here, we dissect PAS-dependent termination at the endogenous Atf4 locus using complementary mouse models. A previously characterized Atf4 ΔCDS + ΔPAS allele deleting exons 2-3 induces strong transcriptional readthrough, producing an Atf4 – Cacna1i fusion transcript that suppresses Rps19bp1 and causes severe cardiac defects. To isolate PAS function, we generated an Atf4 ΔCDS allele retaining the PAS and an Atf4 ΔPAS allele preserving the coding sequence but deleting the PAS. The ΔCDS allele produces modest readthrough, whereas ΔPAS does not produce detectable downstream readthrough. Instead, PAS loss permits utilization of a cryptic intragenic polyadenylation site within exon 3, generating a prematurely terminated transcript. These findings demonstrate that PAS loss does not necessarily cause transcriptional readthrough in vivo and can instead promote alternative polyadenylation at an endogenous mammalian locus.

Article.Title: Towards a unified biology of vertebrate number sense
Article.Authors: Zanon M.; Messina A.; Butterworth B.; Vallortigara G.; Brennan C.; Torres-Pérez J.; Miletto-Petrazzini M.
Article.Abstract: Number sense, the ability to estimate and compare numerical quantities, emerges early in development and is widespread across species. Despite decades of work on behavioural and neural correlates of numerosity, the genetic and mechanistic foundations remain poorly integrated. We propose a review and perspective that brings together evidence from vertebrates. Our unique focus relies on how genetic variation, brain lateralisation, and neural circuit organisation across development shape number cognition. We highlight zebrafish (Danio rerio) and chicks (Gallus gallus) as complementary comparative models that can uncover conserved principles and novel mechanisms, opening new avenues for studying the biological bases of numerical cognition and its disorders from the very early developmental stages.

Article.Title: Spi1 and Usp7 aggravate diabetic encephalopathy through regulating Ddx3x
Article.Authors: Zhao N.; Chen L.; Qin L.; Liu T.; Han G.
Article.Abstract: DEAD-box helicase 3 X-linked (DDX3X) can interact with NOD-like receptor protein 3 (NLRP3) to drive inflammasome activation. Nonetheless, the role of DDX3X on NLRP3 inflammasome activation in diabetic encephalopathy remains unidentified. Here, Ddx3x knockdown alleviates microglial NLRP3 activation, which reverses the increased permeability and decreased tight junction proteins induced by conditioned medium of lipopolysaccharide-stimulated microglia (LPS-CM) in bEnd.3 endothelial cells, and overturns LPS-CM-elicited apoptosis promotion in HT22 neurons. In male type 2 diabetes db/db mice, Ddx3x silencing mitigates microglial activation, blood-brain barrier disruption, neuronal apoptosis and cognitive impairment. Spi-1 proto-oncogene (SPI1) transcriptionally activates Ddx3x ; Additionally, ubiquitin-specific protease (USP)7 reduces DDX3X ubiquitination to increase its protein stability. Silencing Spi1 / Usp7 exerts beneficial effects in vitro and in vivo, which are neutralized when overexpressing Ddx3x . In conclusion, Spi1 / Usp7 knockdown downregulates DDX3X to inhibit microglial NLRP3 activation, alleviating BBB dysfunction and neuronal loss to ameliorate diabetic encephalopathy, which suggests prospective targets for diabetic encephalopathy.

Article.Title: Evolutionary transitions in social organization and the relationship between climate and queen number in ant societies
Article.Authors: De Gasperin O.; Silvestro D.; Helanterä H.; LeBoeuf A.; Downing P.; Chapuisat M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In about one fourth of ant species, multiple queens reproduce within the same colony (‘polygyny’), reducing relatedness and potentially fuelling evolutionary conflicts among colony members. Polygyny is more common at higher altitudes / latitudes in several species, suggesting that cold climates favour multiple queens. We tested this prediction with phylogenetic analyses comparing 263 ant species and modelled the evolutionary pathways between alternative social structures. Queen number was phylogenetically labile, with bidirectional transitions between single and multi-queen species passing through socially polymorphic species (with both types of colonies). Contrary to our predictions, polygyny was not more common at higher latitudes or altitudes. Socially polymorphic species tended to occur in environments with more uniform precipitation throughout the year, and queen number increased towards the tropics. We discuss how multiple queening may be favoured in warm climates due to competitive advantages of faster colony growth and higher genetic diversity. We also call for more studies in tropical regions, as most studies were performed in the northern hemisphere.

Article.Title: CircAbcc1-encoded ABCC1-677aa modulates DLX1 to suppress ferroptosis in chronic cerebral ischemia
Article.Authors: Yang J.; Yu Y.; Fan J.; Hong K.; Zhang N.; Zheng J.
Article.Abstract: Cerebral ischemia leads to progressive neurological dysfunction due to restricted blood perfusion in the brain. While circular RNAs are known to regulate pathological processes, their ability to encode functional proteins during ischemic injury remains unclear. Here, we show that the circular RNA circAbcc1 suppresses ferroptosis in mouse and cellular models of chronic cerebral ischemia‘. We found that circAbcc1 translates into a functional protein, ABCC1-677aa. This protein actively interacts with and phosphorylates the transcription factor DLX1, triggering its export from the nucleus to the cytoplasm. This translocation prevents DLX1 from transcriptionally repressing the crucial anti-ferroptotic genes, Gpx4 and Fsp1. The subsequent upregulation of Gpx4 and Fsp1 limits lipid peroxidation and iron accumulation, successfully protecting brain neurons from ferroptosis. These findings elucidate a regulatory mechanism driven by a circular RNA-encoded protein and identify the circAbcc1-DLX1 axis as a potential therapeutic target for cerebral ischemic injury. A circular RNA, circAbcc1, protects neurons from ferroptosis during chronic cerebral ischemia by encoding the protein ABCC1-677aa. This protein relieves repression of anti-ferroptotic genes, reducing neuronal damage and highlighting the circAbcc1-DLX1 pathway as a therapeutic target.

Article.Title: Uncoupling of seagrass host selection and succession for microbial guilds in meadow chronosequence
Article.Authors: Maithani P.; Sim C.; Srinivas S.; Kwek Z.; Case R.
Article.Abstract: Succession describes the predictable assembly of communities and habitats towards increasingly complex ecosystems. In marine meadows, the relative roles of succession and host selection in structuring microbial communities and functions remain unclear. Using chronosequences of the pioneering seagrass Halophila ovalis , we examined bacterial community succession (16S rRNA gene) and functional genes linked to nitrogen fixation and sulfur cycling ( nifH , soxB , aprA , dsrA ) across meadow sediments and seagrass microbiomes (rhizoplane and phylloplane). Sediment communities diversified progressively with distance from the patch edge, whereas host-associated microbiomes were differentially impacted from the meadow sediments, indicating strong host selection. For sulfur-cycling genes, taxonomic succession was decoupled from gene-sequence diversity, while only nifH exhibited successional patterns. Nevertheless, all communities displayed directional assembly trajectories despite being shaped by contrasting ecological processes. Our findings show that both succession and host selection predictably drive microbial community assembly in developing seagrass meadows, while functional gene potential responded in a niche-dependent manner.

Article.Title: Selective inhibition of IL-6 trans-signalling reveals distinct mechanisms of human classic and trans-signalling receptor-complex formation
Article.Authors: Rieneck E.; Haak J.; Asgarov K.; Pallandre J.; Wundrack N.; Ettich J.; Miri N.; Floss D.; Scheller J.; Garbers C.; Clark A.; Wijdenes J.; Schaper F.; Dittrich A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The cytokine interleukin-6 orchestrates inflammation through two distinct pathways of receptor activation: anti-inflammatory classic signalling via membrane-bound interleukin-6 receptor and pro-inflammatory trans-signalling via soluble interleukin-6 receptor. We here show a high-affinity, human-specific antibody that selectively inhibits interleukin-6 trans-signalling. This antibody maintains classic signalling-induced expression of hepatic acute phase genes while completely blocking trans-signalling-induced activation of endothelial cells. This selective blockade demonstrates that human interleukin-6 classic and trans-signalling proceed through distinct receptor assemblies. UbiBrowser 2.0 database prediction and validation experiments identify FBW7γ as an E3 ligase to promote NEDD1 K323 ubiquitination-mediated degradation, while hUTP14a facilitates FBW7γ degradation in a leucine-rich repeat (LRR)-dependent manner. Article.Title: Engineering T cell-selective chemokine inhibitors through network-level directed evolution
Article.Authors: Payne M.; Durães F.; Clark C.; Wilde E.; Karuppanan K.; Chandra S.; Brennan P.; Hodson D.; Smagurauskaite G.; Bhattacharya S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs) are sustained by chemokine-driven recruitment of effector T cells. Although direct suppression of T cell function can be effective, systemic immunosuppression and infection risk limit clinical utility. Targeting chemokine networks offers an alternative strategy, yet chemokine redundancy has hindered the development of clinically effective inhibitors. Tick evasins overcome chemokine redundancy by binding multiple chemokines. Here we show that network-level directed evolution of class B evasin-derived peptides generates T cell-selective chemokine inhibitors. In contrast to analogous class A-derived peptides, these preferentially bind and inhibit chemokines that drive T cell migration. Structural modelling of chemokine:peptide complexes and structure-guided mutagenesis suggest that evasin-derived peptides sterically occlude receptor-binding surfaces and that class B-derived peptides exhibit a more compact organisation of key interaction hotspots than a previously characterised class A-derived peptide. Together, these findings suggest that anti-chemokine peptide specificity can be engineered through scaffold choice and network-level directed evolution.

In contrast, humans exhibit a dominant reliance on pitch. Experience further modulates this bias, with trained human listeners recruiting secondary cues to preserve learned relational structure when pitch is unreliable. These findings imply a cross-species divergence in auditory representation, suggesting that auditory processing is shaped by an interplay of species-specific priorities and experience-dependent functional substitution.

Article.Authors: Cao D.; Cui J.; Yan X.; Zhang X.; Dang Y.; Zhao H.; Li J.; Zhang J.; Zhang Y.

These alternating and orthogonal activities of the resting-state networks may reflect the brain’s strategy to achieve both the integration and separation of visual and sensorimotor information via the default mode network. Furthermore, we reveal how these activities consecutively move between the default mode network and the visual/sensorimotor network in tens of milliseconds. They move in different ways depending on their direction, suggesting that distinct mechanisms generate the movements in different directions.

Article.Authors: Hadas N.; Xu H.; Neupane S.; Twan W.; Elgamal A.; Lunel A.; Mahjoub M.; Horani A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a genetic condition causing dysmotile cilia and abnormal mucociliary clearance. Using high-speed video microscopy, we captured fluorescent microsphere movement on cultured multiciliated cells from 14 individuals with primary ciliary dyskinesia and 10 healthy donors (602 videos). Quantitative and visual analyses reveal distinct motility profiles between PCD and non-primary ciliary dyskinesia and normal recordings. Classical machine learning models and a convolutional neural network classify recordings with 95-97% accuracy and differentiate affected from normal samples. Machine learning provides an objective, accurate framework for characterizing ciliary dysfunction, offering potential as a diagnostic tool for primary ciliary dyskinesia.

Article.Title: Balancing energy efficiency and functional demand via bimodal coupling optimization in biological rhythms
Article.Authors: Zhang J.; Han J.; Xie L.
Article.Abstract: Biological rhythms are governed by intricate interactions among oscillatory subsystems, yet how they balance functional demands and energy efficiency remains unclear. We present a bimodal coupling optimization strategy where physiological systems alternate between synchronized (energy-saving) and desynchronized (function-priority) coupling modes. Using the water-filling principle developed in communications engineering, we derive necessary optimality conditions showing that energy-efficiency (oxygen uptake per cardiac work) maximization requires synchronized heart rate(HR)-respiration oscillations. Then, system modeling confirms task/stress-induced oxygen demands enhance oxygen uptake at the cost of desynchronization and reduced efficiency. Experiments reveal a 70.36% decrease in HR-respiration synchronization during arithmetic versus relaxation, enabling 4.43% higher oxygen uptake but with 11.38% lower energy efficiency. This bimodal coupling optimization strategy is also evident in pancreatic islets, with their insulin/glucagon oscillator alternating between in-phase (energy-saving) and anti-phase (rapid glucose reduction) coupling. This framework, integrating engineering and life sciences, reveals a universal regulatory principle for biological oscillatory systems. Integrating optimization theory, physiological modeling and experiments, this study reveals a bimodal coupling strategy in which biological rhythms switch between synchronized energysaving and desynchronized function-priority modes.

Article.Title: Self-regulated emergence of heavy-tailed weight distributions in evolving complex network architectures
Article.Authors: Li J.; van Leeuwen C.; Bauer R.; Rentzeperis I.
Article.Abstract: The nervous system continuously adjusts connection strengths and reorganizes its structure to form and maintain complex connectivity patterns with heavy-tailed weight distributions. We propose a parsimonious model in which structural and synaptic plasticity are driven by common diffusion dynamics. Synaptic plasticity alone generates heavy-tailed weight distributions, but only when activity spreading remains predominantly local. However, when combined with structural plasticity through adaptive rewiring, the model also generates these distributions with more extensive activity flow. Furthermore, adaptive rewiring produces complex network structures with convergent-divergent circuits. These circuits contain motifs that are pervasive in nervous systems and are responsible for context-sensitive signal propagation and enhanced signal-to-noise ratios. Our model robustly reproduces these results across diverse dynamical regimes while capturing key connectivity features of both C. elegans and mouse brain networks. These findings suggest that the underlying principles are shared across species of varying complexity. We develop a diffusion-based model of evolving neural networks with adaptive weight adjustment and rewiring. Compared with weight adjustment alone, adding adaptive rewiring generates heavy-tailed weights over broader activity regimes.

Article.Title: Persistent impairment of spatial hearing and neural binaural interaction after “temporary” noise-induced hearing loss
Article.Authors: Mackey C.; Mondul J.; Conner A.; Peacock J.; Benson M.; Hackett T.; Tollin D.; Ramachandran R.
Article.Abstract: Many people have suprathreshold auditory processing difficulties despite normal audiometric thresholds, referred to as “hidden hearing loss.” Such difficulties are widely thought to originate from pathology of the inner hair cell ribbon synapse (cochlear synaptopathy) following noise-exposure-induced temporary threshold shifts. This pathology impairs the temporally-precise sound encoding necessary for spatial hearing, but direct evidence in primates, human or nonhuman, is lacking. Here, we show in macaques of both sexes that noise-exposure-induced temporary threshold shifts produced long-lasting alterations in synaptic morphology without synapse loss, and persistent spatial hearing deficits up to 11 months post-exposure, despite recovery of audiometric thresholds. These deficits were accompanied by a reduction in a neurophysiological measure of binaural processing - the binaural interaction component of the auditory brainstem response. Article.Title: Cellular and spatial context of genetic convergence between insomnia liability and DTI ALPS perivascular diffusivity
Article.Authors: Shen J.; Shen Y.; Yu G.; Pang L.; Xiao C.
Article.Abstract: Sleep has been linked to brain waste clearance and glymphatic/perivascular transport, yet whether insomnia shares genetic architecture with perivascular diffusivity remains unclear. Here we show that insomnia liability and diffusion tensor imaging measures along the perivascular space have little genome-wide genetic correlation but converge locally at chromosome 17q21.31. Polygenic enrichment, conjunctional false discovery rate, and Bayesian colocalization analyses support shared statistical signals in this region, which contains the MAPT inversion locus. Transcriptome-wide, gene-level fine-mapping, and summary-data Mendelian randomization analyses prioritize HEXIM1, ACBD4, EFTUD2, and MAPT. Tissue, cell-type, spatial transcriptomic, and sleep-perturbation analyses place these candidates in neuronal, glial, immune, vascular, and perivascular contexts, with effects varying by brain region and imaging phenotype. Together, these findings support localized genetic convergence rather than a genome-wide shared architecture and provide biological context for future studies of perivascular imaging phenotypes and neurodegeneration-related processes. Insomnia and MRI-derived perivascular diffusivity show little genome-wide genetic correlation but converge locally at 17q21.31, highlighting HEXIM1, ACBD4, EFTUD2 and MAPT.

Article.Title: Non‑monotonic reorganization of cortical neuron firing despite ongoing delta‑dominated activity
Article.Authors: Ge D.; Qin S.; Huang Z.; Chen L.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: Delta - dominated activity is a hallmark of anesthesia and non‑REM sleep, yet how neuronal firing evolves across these rhythms remains unclear. Here, by tracking cortical neuron firing in the ketamine‑xylazine model, we find that across continuing delta - dominated activity, population firing rates progress through successive epochs of excitation, suppression, and re - emergence. Concurrently, fine‑scale spike timing and burst dynamics exhibit non - monotonic modulation, revealing continuous reorganization beneath the ongoing delta-dominated oscillation. At the transition to theta - dominated activity, a restructuring of temporal patterning without a significant shift in the firing - rate distribution suggests that temporal structure, rather than firing rate, defines this transition. These population - level dynamics were firing - rate - dependent: high‑firing - rate neurons were more tightly modulated, whereas low‑firing-rate neurons exhibited more heterogeneous changes. Neither ketamine nor xylazine alone recapitulates these dynamics, suggesting their combined action creates a uniquely dynamic architecture. These findings reveal a continuous, firing - rate - dependent reorganization of single-neuron activity during ongoing delta-dominated states.

Article.Title: Linking centromere stretch to SAC signaling in mammalian oocytes with insights from modified kinetochore model
Article.Authors: Yun Y.; Lane S.; Guo Z.; Zheng Z.; Cai W.; Holt J.; Jones K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The spindle assembly checkpoint (SAC) monitors kinetochore-microtubule interactions to ensure accurate chromosome segregation. In mitosis, investigation of its silencing at anaphase centers on whether attachment or tension is the key signal, while in meiosis for mammalian oocytes it remains unclear whether centromere stretching contributes to SAC deactivation, because in this reductional division sister chromatids co-segregate during meiosis I. While previous studies have linked bivalent tension to SAC control in oocytes, this measurement cannot be directly equated with mitotic chromatin stretching. Here, by tagging the N-terminus of NDC80/HEC1, we developed a mouse oocyte model that features stable microtubule attachments, yet exhibits persistent SAC signaling at metaphase I. Our comprehensive analysis reveals a strong correlation between centromere stretching and SAC signaling. Furthermore, high-resolution live imaging demonstrates that these modified kinetochores impair their oscillatory movements, a process vital for error correction, while chromosome congression remains largely unaffected. Collectively, our data suggest that stable microtubule attachment alone is insufficient to silence SAC in mammalian oocytes; instead, centromere stretching may serve as a critical signal to deactivate the checkpoint. These findings underscore the adaptability of core cell-cycle surveillance pathways.

Article.Title: A modular constitutive single-plasmid platform for efficient production of a recombinant Strep A glycoconjugate vaccine
Article.Authors: Harrison M.; Flood T.; Reglinski M.; McNeil M.; Dorfmueller H.; Wren B.; Passmore I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Production of glycoconjugate vaccines has long relied upon chemical methods which are highly complex and expensive, resulting in vaccines that are not widely affordable. Heterologous bioconjugation methods, such as Protein-Glycan Coupling Technology (PGCT), have emerged as a path to significantly cheaper manufacture using safe host organisms, such as Escherichia coli , for recombinant glycoconjugate expression. PGCT glycoconjugate synthesis components are typically encoded across three plasmids and require the addition of exogenous chemical inducers for gene expression. In this study, we utilise modular DNA assembly to generate a single constitutive plasmid for biosynthesis of a Streptococcus pyogenes rhamnose polysaccharide glycoconjugate vaccine. This approach resulted in a greater than seven-fold glycoconjugate yield as well as simplified cell culture conditions compared to the traditional three plasmid inducible system. Importantly, given the modular nature of this method, this innovation could be applied to the manufacture of glycoconjugate vaccines against a range of pathogens.

Article.Title: Suppression of follistatin by spontaneous seizures dysregulates neurogenesis in a model of Alzheimer’s disease neuropathology
Article.Authors: Furuta Y.; Wang J.; Fu C.; Silva-Pérez M.; Al Faisal M.; Church C.; Hiniker A.; Rissman R.; Lee M.; Yu W.; Chin J.
Article.Abstract: Adult hippocampal neurogenesis is perturbed in neurological disorders accompanied by seizures, including Alzheimer’s disease (AD). We find that FST expression is reduced in the dentate gyrus of a mouse model of AD neuropathology that exhibits infrequent spontaneous seizures similar to those in individuals with AD. Treatment with an antiseizure drug improves FST expression in AD mice, whereas a seizure-inducing agent suppresses FST expression in wild-type mice. We identify c-Fos, whose expression is suppressed by the seizure-induced transcription factor ∆FosB, as a transcriptional activator of Fst . Article.Authors: Chan T.; Niroomand S.; Lim U.; Teo E.; Tulsian N.; Tumkaya T.; Parish C.; Simov V.; Yeo J.; Leong J.; Voleti B.; Marino M.; Klein R.; Fagegaltier D.; Fernandis A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a complex neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive loss of motor neurons and presents a critical need for effective treatments. The model successfully recapitulates functional deficits observed in ALS patients, including impaired neurite outgrowth, reduced axonal regeneration, and neuronal hyperexcitability. Proteomic and metabolomic profiling revealed early mechanisms underlying ALS neuronal pathophysiology, involving altered oxidative stress and neurotransmitter release. TDP-43 nuclear depletion led to mis-splicing STMN2 and KCNQ2 , defects characteristic of TDP-43-associated disease. Notably, a splice-switching antisense oligonucleotide successfully restored normal STMN2 splicing and function, demonstrating that directly correcting splicing defects can rescue motor neurons. Article.Authors: Baral K.; Spade L.; Shrestha S.; Thapa K.; Rohner R.; Li Y.; Majari G.; Xue Y.; Liu G.; Moroz K.; Yin X.; Khambu B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Post-translational modifications (PTMs) are essential for hepatic protein function and signaling. This acetylation loss results from decreased hepatic acetyl-CoA levels, independent of acetyltransferase or deacetylase expression. Mechanistically, NRF2 activation suppresses key acetyl-CoA biosynthetic enzymes (Acly, Acss, Mlycd, Pdha1), limiting substrate availability. Acetyl-CoA or acetate supplementation restores the protein acetylation and alleviates liver injury and inflammation in autophagy-deficient models. Article.Authors: Li L.; Peng M.; Yan Y.; Chen Q.; Liao H.; Yang J.; Yang X.; Pu X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rosa roxburghii ( RRT ) is a nutritionally and medicinally important Rosaceae species that accumulates diverse bioactive compounds, making it an excellent system for investigating the genetic basis and evolutionary diversification of specialized metabolism. Article.Title: Neural oscillations and network specialisation in early childhood captured with next-generation magnetoencephalography
Article.Authors: Rhodes N.; Bandhan J.; Vandewouw M.; Broeders E.; Sato J.; Safar K.; Coleman S.; Taylor M.
Article.Abstract: Early childhood sees very rapid brain development, reflected in substantial alterations in neural oscillations and reorganisation of functional networks. Global connectivity decreased from 1–5 years, driven by a broadband bilateral parietal and frontal network, while task-relevant occipital connections increased with age. Article.Authors: Xia J.; Pinto-Fernández A.; Damianou A.; Lee J.; Gumusdis E.; Kessler B.; Davis I.; Elliott P.; Vagnoni A.; Ligoxygakis P.

Article.Title: Global patterns are key to understanding macroevolution
Article.Authors: Guo Z.; Kiessling W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Regional diversification patterns are increasingly being used to investigate spatial heterogeneity in biodiversity evolution and its drivers. We show that immigrations and extirpations account for up to 76% of apparent plate-level generic turnover. Moreover, regional diversity fluctuations are more strongly shaped by preservation, sampling, and tectono-sedimentary history than global patterns. In widely distributed groups, global analyses integrate data across regions and environments, dampen region-specific biases, and recover a higher proportion of shared biological signal. Global analyses therefore remain indispensable for inferring macroevolutionary dynamics over deep time.

Here, we investigate whether this lipid-protein association also contributes to the late stages of regulated exocytosis. Using fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy combined with Förster resonance energy transfer, we find that CgA undergoes a stimulation-dependent association with PA at exocytic sites in living cells. Immunofluorescence and electron microscopy further show that CgA remains transiently associated with fused secretory granule membranes. Functional analyses reveal that disruption of the PABD alters secretory granule exocytosis by accelerating CgA release, modifying quantal catecholamine release and fusion pore dynamics, and changing the early kinetics of secretory granule membrane retrieval. Together, these findings support a model in which the CgA/PA association is not restricted to secretory granule biogenesis but also contributes to the temporal coordination of multiple post-fusion events during regulated secretion. This work identifies a lipid-protein interaction that links distinct stages of the secretory granule life cycle in neuroendocrine cells. Chromogranin A binds phosphatidic acid at exocytic sites, coordinating secretion beyond granule formation. Disrupting this interaction alters cargo release, fusion pore dynamics, and membrane retrieval, linking distinct stages of the secretory granule life cycle.

Article.Title: Single-cell chromatin maps of thymic carcinoma reveal a conserved malignant state and its immunosuppressive dependencies
Article.Authors: Lin F.; Kim S.; Hsiao T.; Peng Z.; Wang J.; Chen P.; Chen B.; Liao H.; Chung W.; Chou Y.; Hsu C.; Ko T.
Article.Abstract: Thymic carcinoma is a rare and aggressive malignancy with limited therapeutic options. Although recent single-cell transcriptomic studies have begun to resolve its cellular composition, its regulatory landscape remains poorly characterized. We present a single-cell chromatin accessibility resource comprising 26,661 high-quality nuclei from three tumors and two adjacent normal tissues, with annotated malignant and immune populations, cell-type-resolved peaks, and gene activity estimates. To illustrate its utility, exploratory analyses identified a recurrent tumor cluster, T3, in all three tumors examined, with shared accessibility at therapeutically relevant loci, including KIT , FGFR3 , and SYK , and an inferred regulatory program involving ELF2 , BCLAF1 , PBX3 , IKZF1 , NFKB1 , TFDP2 , and POU2AF1 , alongside exhaustion-associated CD8⁺ T-cell and M2-like macrophage chromatin programs. Article.Title: A dielectric spectroscopic measurement of single Saccharomyces pastorianus growth and heat-shock response
Article.Authors: Islam M.; Caldwell T.; Wang P.
Article.Abstract: Cell growth and heat shock response (HSR) are central to cellular adaptation, fate determination, and survival under fluctuating environments, yet their continuous quantification in individual suspended microbial cells remains challenging. Here, we present microwave dielectric spectroscopic cytometry (DiSC) for real-time, label-free monitoring of single-cell growth and HSR in budding yeast, Saccharomyces pastorianus , under physiological culture conditions. Integrated optical microscopy enabled simultaneous tracking of morphological dynamics during growth, heat shock, and apoptosis. At 32 °C, cells exhibited continuous biomass accumulation with fluctuating growth rates but relatively conserved molecular composition profiles (MCPs). Upon heat shock (from 32 °C to 42 °C), cells displayed discontinuous biomass accumulation, rapid mass fluctuations, and dynamically varying MCPs across all 17 cells analyzed. A subset of cells subsequently underwent apoptotic collapse, with onset times ranging from ~ 20 min during temperature ramping to more than 60 min at 42 °C or remaining absent throughout the 340 min observation window, revealing pronounced cell-to-cell heterogeneity. Post-apoptotic cells exhibited stabilized MCP dynamics. Analyses of two- to four-cell lineages further demonstrated divergent apoptotic outcomes among closely related progeny. These results establish DiSC as a promising platform for continuous single-cell quantification of growth, stress adaptation, and phenotypic heterogeneity while highlighting opportunities for further improvements in system performance and analytical capability.

Article.Title: Transient hemispheric lateralization is associated with intensity-dependent aftereffects of low-frequency rTMS
Article.Authors: Qiu S.; Gao Y.; Yi W.; Zhang C.; Liu C.; Zhu X.; Wang S.; He H.
Article.Abstract: Low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) can alter brain activity during and after stimulation, but the relationship between these immediate responses and subsequent effects remains unclear. In a randomized, single-blind crossover design, twenty healthy adults receive 1 Hz rTMS over the left motor cortex at sham, 80%, 100%, and 120% of resting motor threshold (RMT). electroencephalography (EEG) is recorded before, during, and after rTMS. Stimulation at and above threshold elicits robust transient responses, characterized by enhanced TMS-evoked potentials, increased beta-band power, increased beta-band lateralization and recruited bilateral cortical activities. Also, they induce significant aftereffect with a decrease in hemispheric lateralization after rTMS. Mediation analyses links stimulation intensity to this subsequent rebalancing through transient beta-band lateralization. In an exploratory stroke cohort, lower beta-band lateralization is associated with better motor function. These findings suggest that low-frequency rTMS induces intensity-dependent transient responses and aftereffects. Transient beta-band lateralization is associated with subsequent interhemispheric rebalancing and may serve as a marker for optimizing personalized neurorehabilitation.

Article.Title: An ensemble framework for robust drug response prediction and large-scale sensitivity profiling across cancers
Article.Authors: Feng Y.; Zhou S.; Luo S.; Feng B.; Wu H.; Zeng Y.; Feng J.; Wang Z.; Yang L.; Li S.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: Predicting how cancers respond to treatment remains difficult because tumors are diverse and computational models often perform poorly on unfamiliar drugs or samples. Here we show that the accuracy of deep learning models varies across molecular inputs, drug descriptions, model designs, and evaluation settings, with the largest losses when models are tested on previously unseen drugs or distinct datasets. We therefore develop Drug Response Integration and Voting Ensemble, a meta-learning framework that combines models using predictions from held-out data. A nine-model ensemble improves predictive accuracy, drug ranking, and stability over individual models and ensemble approaches. We implement the framework as a reproducible Nextflow workflow and use it to build a resource of measured and predicted drug responses across cancer cell lines, patient-derived samples, and compound libraries. In colorectal cancer, the framework identifies treatments with confirmed antitumor activity in cell and animal models. This approach provides a scalable strategy for therapeutic discovery. We benchmark drug response models and develop DRIVE, a meta-learning ensemble for large-scale cancer drug sensitivity prediction. DRIVE improves robustness and prioritizes compounds with validated antitumor activity in colorectal cancer.

Article.Authors: Linde J.; Yildiz C.; Vöhringer K.; Nabbefeld G.; Graff S.; Pensold D.; Reichard J.; Hermanns M.; Koch L.; Müller M.; Tanwar A.; Weber-Hamacher C.; Costa Filho I.; Stiehl T.; Spehr M.; Kampa B.; Urbach A.; Musall S.; Zimmer-Bensch G.

Together, our findings demonstrate that DNMT1 maintains inhibitory circuit stability through PV interneuron function, secondarily shaping glial states and extracellular scaffolds to support cortical network synchronization and affective behavior.

Article.Title: ESR1 mutations are associated with enhanced MTORC1 signaling in a context-dependent manner
Article.Authors: De Marchi T.; Kuras M.; Betancourt L.; Kjellström S.; Valcich J.; Vallon-Christersson J.; Brueffer C.; Saal L.; Malmström J.; Niméus E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract ESR1 mutations are a driver of endocrine therapy resistance in breast cancer, however their impact on protein signaling pathways and clinical outcomes remains poorly understood. Here we show that ESR1 mutated cancers exhibit a higher mutational burden associated with increased cell proliferation, and display enhanced activation of the mTOR pathway via MTORC1, suggesting an ER-driven amplification of existing oncogenic mechanisms. Analysis of an independent proteomic dataset from breast cancer cell lines further supported a convergence between MTORC1 and ER signaling programs. Integrative multi-omic data analysis incorporating features related to tumor grade, MTORC1 signaling, and ESR1 mutations, enabled the development of a predictive signature that distinguishes patients with ESR1 mutation and identified those at high risk of recurrence. This study provides insights into the mechanisms underlying tumor aggressiveness and poor clinical outcome modulated by ESR1 mutations and highlights the potential of proteogenomic approaches to identify signaling pathways and molecular signatures.

Article.Title: LSD reconfigures cortical dynamics through faster brain rhythms and increased fractal dimension
Article.Authors: Subramani V.; Nest T.; Pascarella A.; Brunel J.; Mantilla Ramos Y.; Harel Y.; Muthukumaraswamy S.; Carhart-Harris R.; Lioi G.; Farrugia N.; Jerbi K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD) profoundly alters conscious experience, yet the electrophysiological mechanisms by which it reshapes neural dynamics remain incompletely understood. A hallmark of psychedelic states is widespread cortical desynchronization, typically inferred from reductions in spectral power, but whether such effects reflect genuine weakening of neural oscillations or are confounded by shifts in oscillatory peak frequencies remains unresolved. We combine source-resolved magnetoencephalography (MEG), spectral parameterization, temporal complexity metrics, and interpretable machine learning in an LSD versus placebo design, with and without music. We show that LSD induces robust, spatially structured increases in alpha and beta peak frequencies alongside genuine attenuation of oscillatory power, with partly dissociable cortical patterns. Beyond rhythmic activity, LSD is associated with flattening of the aperiodic 1/f spectral slope and increased neural signal fractality and complexity, preferentially affecting sensory, language, emotion, and imagery-related networks while sparing motor cortex. Machine-learning analyses identify peak-frequency shifts, aperiodic parameters, and complexity measures as key discriminators of the psychedelic state. Music does not robustly amplify these neural signatures and instead shows a trend toward attenuation. These findings provide an electrophysiological account of how LSD reorganizes large-scale human brain dynamics and highlight features that may differentiate its neural signature from other psychedelics.

Article.Title: A scalable Zebrafish Platform for genetic validation and functional discovery of stage-specific breast cancer metastasis regulators
Article.Authors: Ruscitto F.; Priami C.; Roda N.; De Michele G.; Dalmasso A.; Bivacqua S.; Peccati G.; Rimoldi R.; Soriani C.; Rodighiero S.; Migliaccio E.; Pelicci P.
Article.Abstract: Metastatic disease accounts for over 90% of breast cancer-related deaths, yet scalable in vivo models for functional analysis of distinct metastatic steps remain limited. GAS5, LRRC75A-AS1 and FST displayed distinct context-dependent effects on tumor growth or metastatic progression. These findings establish zebrafish xenografts as a scalable platform that complements mouse models for quantitative functional analysis of breast cancer metastasis. Screening candidate genes identified distinct regulators of dissemination, extravasation, and metastatic growth, providing a powerful tool for studying metastatic mechanisms.

Article.Title: Daytime illumination shapes sex differences in sleep and circadian responses to nighttime light
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Chen C.; Deboer T.; Block G.; Paul K.; Colwell C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Light is the primary environmental cue regulating circadian rhythms and sleep–wake behavior, yet daylight intensity is rarely standardized or reported. This variability may contribute to inconsistent findings on sex differences in sleep regulation. In prior work, we observed no sex differences in sleep–wake architecture under relatively bright daylight, suggesting that daytime illumination may be a critical but underappreciated determinant of sex difference in sleep regulation. Here, we tested whether daylight intensity modulates sex differences in sleep–wake architecture and vulnerability to dim light at night (DLaN). Male and female C57BL/6 J mice were exposed to acute (one night) or chronic (two weeks) DLaN (10-lux) under daytime light intensities of 50-, 100-, or 300-lux. Sleep was assessed using electroencephalographic measures of vigilance states and slow wave activity (SWA). Dim daylight (50-lux) revealed marked sex differences in dark phase that were absent under brighter daylight (300-lux). Acute DLaN reduced early-night wakefulness in both sexes under low daytime light but had little effect under bright daylight conditions. Following chronic DLaN, males showed reduced wakefulness and dampened rhythm amplitude, whereas females exhibited larger phase shifts, rhythm attenuation, and altered SWA timing under 50- and 100-lux, and bright daytime light largely prevented these effects.

Article.Authors: Cai J.; Zhang S.; Chen K.; Xie X.; Zhang G.
Article.Abstract: The rational engineering of non-model microorganisms is often constrained by the scarcity of high-performance genetic regulatory tools. To overcome this limitation, we developed ARCANE – a reprogrammable circuit architecture for non-model engineering – featuring a cascaded design in which an inducer controls orthogonal bacterial transcription factors (bTFs), which in turn drive both activation and repression of endogenous promoters. This architecture provides strong insulation from host regulatory networks, minimizes leakage, and enables a broad dynamic range. As a proof-of-concept, we implemented ARCANE in the industrially significant non-model yeast, Yarrowia lipolytica . The resulting genetic switch exhibited exceptionally precise and tunable control over both single reporter genes and a multi-gene carotenoid biosynthesis pathway. Beyond providing a powerful regulatory tool for Y. lipolytica , ARCANE offers a versatile and transferable modular foundation for programmable gene control in emerging microbial platforms, paving the way for scalable synthetic biology in non-model systems.

Article.Title: Target-dependent routing of sensory information in the olfactory system
Article.Authors: Le-Jahns K.; Sireci S.; Mayland J.; Richter F.; Chamero P.; Schwarz M.; Brunert D.; Rothermel M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Parallel processing, the ability to split the information content of sensory stimuli and handle them simultaneously, is essential for sensory perception in many systems. Purely cell-type-derived properties did not explain the projection target-dependent differences in odor representation, as both mitral and tufted cells showed similar changes, and SVM classifier analysis demonstrated that classification by projection target outperformed classification by cell type. Our data suggests a prominent projection-defined separation of sensory information in the OB.

Article.Title: TDP-43 regulates mitochondrial dsRNA accumulation and chromosome territory formation during prophase I of Drosophila male meiosis
Article.Authors: R. St. Amand V.; Stilwell G.; Helfand S.; Reenan R.
Article.Abstract: TDP-43 is a conserved RNA/DNA-binding protein infamous for its pathological roles in numerous human neurodegenerative diseases. Article.Title: Climate change impacts flowering, pollinator interactions, and seed yield in canola
Article.Authors: Dzekashu F.; Hoover S.
Article.Abstract: Insect-mediated pollination is a crucial ecosystem service that significantly contributes to the fertilisation of crop plants. However, as extreme weather events become more frequent with climate change, environmental stressors such as heat waves and drought threaten this mutualistic interaction, posing risks to global food production. We examined how heat and water stress affect flowering phenology, traits (flower number and size, nectar volume, and concentration), pollinator visitation, and seed yield in three canola varieties. We found that plants in heat and drought stress conditions bloomed earlier, produced fewer flowers, and shortened their flowering period, making them less attractive to pollinators. Plants also produced smaller flowers with reduced volumes of highly concentrated nectar relative to those in ambient conditions. Reproductive output declined under water limitation, with drought‑stressed plants producing significantly fewer pods and seeds than well‑watered plants, while total seed weight was reduced under both heat and drought. We found that flower abundance positively influenced seed yield across treatments, whereas pollinator visitation was a key factor for seed yield under ambient conditions but not in hot/drought conditions. Our findings highlight the complex ways in which climate change affects plant phenology, floral rewards, and reproduction, potentially disrupting plant-pollinator interactions and threatening crop production.

Article.Authors: Pathmasiri K.; Cologna S.
Article.Abstract: Niemann–Pick Disease Type C1 (NPC1) is a fatal, neurodegenerative disorder, characterized by lysosomal lipid accumulation and dysmyelination. These findings offer critical insight into the lipid perturbations under the loss of NPC1, and highlight lipid targets that may be crucial for therapeutic intervention and biomarker development. A comprehensive LC-MS-based lipidomic investigation of the brain and isolated myelin in a Niemann–Pick Disease Type C1 mouse model reveals regional and progressive lipid dysregulations.

Article.Title: Adult hippocampal neurogenesis shapes ideomotor action control in mice
Article.Authors: Barde W.; Kempermann G.; Beste C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Humans select and learn goal-directed actions through the anticipation of their outcomes. While this ideomotor principle is well established in humans, its biological instantiation and relevance for organizing naturalistic behavior remain unclear, including its neurobiological substrates such as hippocampal plasticity. Here, we leverage high-resolution, continuous behavioral tracking in mice across a month-long series of automated learning tasks to test whether ideomotor principles generalize to naturalistic behavior and how they relate to adult hippocampal neurogenesis. Mice lived in a shared enriched environment and engaged in self-initiated learning tasks, allowing us to quantify how action–outcome associations are formed, maintained, and updated. Despite identical genetic background and environment, animals showed stable individual differences in how these associations were organized. These differences correlated with levels of adult hippocampal neurogenesis: higher neurogenesis was associated with broader, more variable exploration and greater flexibility in updating action–outcome relations, whereas lower neurogenesis was linked to more rigid behavior. Together, these findings link ideomotor theory to a cellular plasticity mechanism supporting flexible action control.

Article.Authors: Li C.; Han Y.; Zhou J.; Zhao L.; Zou Y.; Zhu H.; Zheng C.; Li Y.; Wu J.

Article.Authors: Jurdzinski K.; Latz M.; Torstensson A.; Brugel S.; Hedblom M.; Hu Y.; Lindh M.; Andersson A.; Karlson B.; Andersson A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Salinity has been identified as a primary factor structuring community composition in global diversity assessments of free-living bacteria in non-extreme environments. Conversely, marine-associated protists dominated across most of the salinity gradient, with fewer taxonomic units adapted to lower salinities. Overall, the diversity of protists but not bacteria followed patterns consistent with local adaptation as observed in other groups of organisms. Ultimately, the observed patterns form a baseline for environmental monitoring and suggest unexplored differences between bacterial and protist eco-evolutionary dynamics.

Article.Title: Cryo-EM structures of Mycobacterium tuberculosis pyruvate carboxylase reveal acetyl-CoA-mediated tetramer stabilization and carrier-domain coordination
Article.Authors: Singh A.; Singh S.; Das U.
Article.Abstract: Pyruvate carboxylase (PC) is a biotin-dependent enzyme essential for anaplerotic metabolism and intracellular survival of Mycobacterium tuberculosis , yet the structural basis by which allosteric ligand binding reshapes the conformational landscape of this dynamic multi-domain assembly has remained unresolved. Here we report four cryo-EM structures of MtPC in apo and acetyl-CoA-bound states, revealing that acetyl-CoA binding stabilizes a compact and structurally ordered tetrameric architecture while shifting the conformational ensemble toward catalytically competent states. In the absence of the effector, MtPC adopts a heterogeneous expanded assembly prone to interfacial dissociation. Acetyl-CoA binding enforces a compact quaternary organization through a reciprocal interfacial seam between adjacent pyruvate carboxylase tetramerization (PT) domains, absent from all characterized PC homologs. Through symmetry expansion, focused classification, and local refinement, we resolve intra-monomeric engagement of the biotin carboxyl carrier protein (BCCP) domain at both catalytic centers within the intact tetramer. Three-dimensional variability analysis reveals coordinated but non-synchronous hinge-centered domain motions that shift the population of accessible conformational states rather than enforcing a single active conformation. These findings provide structural insight into ensemble-based allosteric regulation and a species-specific quaternary architecture in a medically critical pathogen enzyme.

Article.Title: Championing neurodiversity and human potential: an interview with Lawrence Fung
Article.Abstract: Dr. Lawrence Fung is the director of the Stanford Center for Neurodiversity and Human Potential and an Associate Professor in the Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences at Stanford University. Article.Title: An ALLO-1–associated network links mitochondrial quality control to functional recovery in structurally compromised muscle
Article.Authors: Sarkar A.; Biriczová L.; Szulc N.; Thapa P.; Serwa R.; Pokrzywa W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Muscle function can recover before damaged contractile structures are fully repaired, but the mechanisms enabling this recovery remain poorly understood. Using a temperature-sensitive Caenorhabditis elegans model of UNC-45 dysfunction, in which impaired myosin chaperoning triggers muscle proteotoxic stress and reversible paralysis, we show that coordinated movement recovers while sarcomere disorganisation persists. Quantitative proteomics identified ALLO-1, a selective-autophagy receptor previously characterised for paternal organelle clearance during embryogenesis, as induced during recovery from UNC-45dependent muscle stress. Functional and proteomic analyses revealed an ALLO-1–associated regulatory network comprising IKKE-1, SIP-1, DIM-1 and CAR-1 that modulates mitochondrial stress responses and muscle recovery. Loss of ALLO-1 or its associated factors altered mitochondrial homoeostasis and delayed functional recovery, whereas muscle-specific ALLO-1a restoration improved recovery, preserved mitochondrial network integrity, and modulated mitochondrial turnover despite reduced respiratory capacity. These findings identify ALLO-1 as a regulator of mitochondrial stress adaptation that enables functional recovery before completing structural repair.

Article.Title: UCHL5 stabilizes ALK5 to promote autophagy dependent ferroptosis in osteoarthritis
Article.Authors: Jin R.; Li C.; Xiong M.; Wu Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ferroptosis is recognized as a key driver in the pathological progression of osteoarthritis (OA), but its regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely understood. To address this gap, we focused on the deubiquitinating enzyme UCHL5, which is implicated in OA progression, to elucidate its function in modulating ferroptosis within the OA context. Through in vitro experiments involving UCHL5 knockdown and overexpression in chondrocytes, and in vivo studies using UCHL5 knockout mice, we demonstrate that UCHL5 promotes OA pathogenesis by activating autophagy-dependent ferroptosis. Genetic suppression of UCHL5 significantly inhibited ferroptosis, enhanced chondrocyte survival, and facilitated functional recovery in OA models. Mechanistically, UCHL5 deubiquitinates and stabilizes ALK5 by specifically cleaving Lys48-linked polyubiquitin chains via its C185 catalytic residue. This UCHL5-ALK5 axis activates autophagy, promotes ferroptosis, and accelerates cartilage matrix degradation. Our findings identify the UCHL5/ALK5 pathway as a regulator of autophagy-dependent ferroptosis in OA, offering a potential therapeutic target for OA treatment.

Article.Title: Cancer-derived lactic acid as a potential upstream contributor to tumor hypoxia
Article.Authors: Kang N.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Hypoxia contributes to tumor progression, abnormal blood vessel formation, immune suppression, and therapeutic resistance. Although hypoxia is traditionally viewed as the primary driver of glycolysis, intrinsic oncogenic signaling, mitochondrial dysfunction, and epigenetic reprogramming also stimulate glycolysis independently of oxygen limitation, leading to substantial lactic acid accumulation under oxygenated conditions. Beyond its classic role in metabolism, lactic acid is a bioactive molecule that shapes tumor physiology by influencing immune responses, driving vascular remodeling, and mediating metabolic interactions among tumor and stromal populations. In this Perspective, we propose that cancer-derived lactic acid may contribute to the development and persistence of hypoxic tumor regions and sustain hypoxia-associated signaling. This framework positions lactic acid not only as a consequence of hypoxia but also as a potential upstream driver, forming a self-reinforcing glycolysis-lactic acid-hypoxia feedback loop that can be therapeutically disrupted by targeting lactic acid production or transport.
