Article.Title: Hippocampal theta states are linked to reconfiguration of population activity with respect to behavioural context
Article.Authors: Masaracchia L.; Oyarzo P.; Fredes F.; Vidaurre D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Neural activity reflects both external stimuli and the brain’s internal state, which shapes how information is processed and perceived. For example, in phase-precession in the hippocampus, the phase of theta oscillations affects the firing of single neurons (place cells) and its relation to the external world. Here, we examine a different form of relationship between oscillations and neural activity, where frequency and power of hippocampal oscillations, instead of phase, are associated with differential neural firing patterns at the population level. Using electrophysiological recordings of rats performing an odour-memory task and a data-driven model, we identify two distinct theta states: low-power-lower-theta and high-power-higher-theta. These states are associated to modulations in hippocampal neural ensemble activity representing trial outcome. Our findings suggest that power and frequency variations within theta oscillations may be linked to the reconfiguration of neural firing at the network level.

Article.Title: Spatiotemporal encoding signatures of covert speech revealed by source-localized EEG and fMRI
Article.Authors: Zhang W.; Jiang M.; Teo K.; Bhuvanakantham R.; Guo Z.; Zhang S.; Foo C.; Leong V.; Lu J.; Gulyás B.; Guan C.
Article.Abstract: Covert speech, the silent production of words without overt articulation, is fundamental to human cognition and a potential target for restoring communication in speech-impaired populations. Yet where, when, and how the human brain represents specific phrase content during covert speech remains largely unresolved. Here, we combine source-localized EEG (n = 57) with fMRI validation in the same cohort (n = 49) to map the encoding of five covert command phrases. Phrase-discriminative activity is concentrated before estimated articulation onset, peaking at 200–400 ms and strongest in the theta band. Cross-modal representational similarity analysis reveals convergent EEG–fMRI phrase representations in left sensorimotor cortex, while phase-lag connectivity identifies left postcentral gyrus as a phrase-sensitive functional hub within a parietal-somatosensory-temporal sequence during the speech planning period. Beyond these group-level signatures, individual-specific encoding patterns substantially exceed group-average effects. These findings provide a temporally precise, cross-validated cortical map of covert speech and identify targets for speech neuroscience and non-invasive brain-computer interfaces. Source-localized EEG with fMRI validation in the same cohort maps where and when the cortex encodes covert speech. Phrase information peaks 200-400 ms after the cue in left sensorimotor cortex, and individual-specific patterns exceed group effects.

Article.Title: Extracellular vesicle-encapsulated GDF15 alleviates doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity via the SUB1/TERT/TPP signalling axis
Article.Authors: Gu Q.; Chen Q.; Deng Y.; Deng L.; Huang J.; Wang J.; Ji Y.; Wang R.; Wang Q.; Sun L.
Article.Abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX) is a highly effective chemotherapeutic agent, but its clinical application is limited by cardiotoxicity. Mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis are key mechanisms underlying DOX-induced cardiomyopathy (DIC), while the role of telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) and its specific regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. An in vitro DOX-induced H9C2 cardiomyocyte injury model was established. TERT was overexpressed via adenoviral transfection or inhibited using BIBR1532. An in vivo mouse model of DOX-induced acute myocardial injury was constructed, with TERT expression regulated via intramyocardial adenoviral injection. Cardiac function was evaluated by echocardiography, and myocardial pathology was observed via staining. Additionally, exosome-encapsulated growth differentiation factor 15 (EXO-GDF15) was extracted and identified. Its regulatory mechanism on TERT was explored using DNA pull-down and luciferase reporter gene assays. Metabolomics was used to analyze the effect of TERT on mitochondrial metabolites in cardiomyocytes. TERT overexpression reduced DOX-induced apoptosis, increased mitochondrial membrane potential, and promoted autophagy in cardiomyocyte. In mice, TERT overexpression improved cardiac function and alleviated myocardial fibrosis, inflammation, and cardiomyocyte hypertrophy. Conversely, TERT inhibition exacerbated these injuries. EXO-GDF15 could be endocytosed by cardiomyocytes and alleviated DOX-induced myocardial injury by downregulating SUB1 to promote TERT transcription. Luciferase reporter assays showed that SUB1 binds to the BS4 site of the TERT promoter. Metabolomics showed that TERT increased the mitochondrial metabolite thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) in cardiomyocytes, which alleviated myocardial injury by participating in the tricarboxylic acid cycle. EXO-GDF15 alleviates doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity via the SUB1/TERT/TPP signaling axis, thereby providing advanced insights for future DIC treatment. TERT overexpression reduces DOX-induced cardiomyocyte apoptosis, preserves mitochondrial function, and enhances autophagy, while TERT inhibition worsens in vivo cardiac injury. Critically, exosome-encapsulated GDF15 (EXO-GDF15) alleviates DIC by promoting TERT transcription.

Article.Title: Early Ediacaran micro- and macro-fossils from South China provide insights into post-Snowball Earth marine ecosystem
Article.Authors: Ye Q.; An Z.; Chen S.; Long X.; Xiao S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Understanding of biological and ecological dynamics after the terminal Cryogenian Marinoan glaciation remains limited because the early Ediacaran fossil record is sparse and taphonomically biased toward microfossils. Here we show an early Ediacaran fossil assemblage from the Ancangping section of South China that co-preserves micro- and macrofossils in the same strata. It contains 17 genera and 35 species of acritarchs, including three new taxa, and six forms of macroscopic carbonaceous compressions. Integrated lithostratigraphic and biostratigraphic correlation with published astrochronologic and radiometric data indirectly constrains its age to approximately 620–610 million years ago, thus predating the hitherto oldest-known macrofossil assemblage (the Lantian biota at 602 million years ago) in the Ediacaran Period. The assemblage comprises cyanobacteria, phytoplankton, benthic macroalgae, and possible metazoans, indicating the co-occurrence of benthic and planktonic organisms in the aftermath of the Snowball Earth. This finding fills a temporal gap and provides insight into early Ediacaran biological communities across the Cryogenian–Ediacaran transition.

Article.Title: AAV-mediated inducible expression of OSK and OSKM ameliorates acute ischemic and chronic steatotic liver disease
Article.Authors: Maroto-Serrat C.; Rabadan-Ros R.; Montagud-Marrahi E.; Micó-Carnero M.; Rojano-Alfonso C.; Caballeria-Casals A.; Sanus F.; Lopez-Sanchez I.; Gracia-Sancho J.; Luque Y.; Peralta C.; Campistol J.
Article.Abstract: Short-term expression of the Yamanaka factors Oct4, Sox2, Klf4 and c-Myc (OSKM) has been shown to promote liver regeneration, whereas sustained in vivo expression has been linked to tumorigenesis. Here, we evaluated doxycycline-inducible AAV-mediated expression of OSKM or OSK in male Wistar rats subjected to warm hepatic ischemia, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), or MASH with cirrhosis. A single AAV dose was administered, with transgene expression activated intermittently by doxycycline once a week. Short-term OSKM expression in healthy rats did not induce liver tumors up to 12 weeks after administration. In warm hepatic ischemia, both OSKM and OSK reduced liver damage. In contrast, only OSK improved chronic liver disease, attenuating tissue injury and fibrosis in MASH and MASH-cirrhosis and increasing survival. OSKM provided no therapeutic benefit in either chronic model and, in MASH without cirrhosis, exacerbated liver injury and fibrosis, induced tumors, and reduced survival. These findings support transient OSK expression as a potential therapeutic strategy for hepatic ischemia and MASH-associated liver damage.

Article.Title: Sexual dimorphism shapes the plasma metabolome of the endangered Iberian lynx
Article.Authors: Llobat L.; Curtasu M.; Grande-Gómez R.; Cantos-Rubert A.; Flavel P.; Hedemann M.; Marín-García P.
Article.Abstract: Sexual dimorphism is a key but still incompletely resolved determinant of mammalian systemic metabolism, particularly in endangered species where physiological organization remains poorly characterized. Here, we integrate untargeted plasma metabolomics to dissect hierarchical determinants of systemic metabolic organization in the Iberian lynx ( Lynx pardinus ), one of the world’s most endangered felids. We show that plasma metabolic profiles exhibit distinct patterns associated with sex and age class ( n = 37). Sex is the dominant axis of variation, driving coordinated divergence across lipid remodelling, taurine-associated metabolism, fatty acid β-oxidation, amino acid turnover, and endocrine-related pathways. This separation is supported by consistent metabolite-level differences and clear system-level discrimination, indicating widespread metabolic divergence between females and males. Importantly, this sex-dependent architecture persists after sexual maturation and remains stable in adult-only analyses, indicating that the observed structure is not driven by age composition effects. Age shows limited explanatory power and does not yield interpretable systemic structure. Metabolic networks reveal a conserved lipid–taurine backbone, with sex shaping system architecture and metabolic organization persisting despite demographic constraints.

Article.Title: Predicting recovery trajectories and injury severity following partial crush spinal cord injury in mice
Article.Authors: Li K.; Hassan L.; Prasad H.; Omodia G.; Woods P.; O’Shea T.
Article.Abstract: The partial crush spinal cord injury (SCI) model enables preclinical testing of experimental therapies in mice, but substantial inter-animal variability in recovery outcomes confounds efficacy assessments. Here, we used open field behavioral data collected during the first 3 days post partial thoracic SCI to generate an Acute Functional Score (AFS) that defined three subgroups with divergent recovery trajectories. Applying latent class growth analysis and growth mixture modeling to open field and grid walk testing data, we demonstrated 83-92% prediction accuracy for AFS-defined recovery trajectories. The three subgroups differed significantly in treadmill kinematics and histological assessments of lesion size and astrocyte bridging. Applying the recovery trajectory framework to mice receiving saline or biomaterial vehicle injections at 3 days post-SCI revealed robust predictive accuracy while exposing disproportionate injury severity distributions between experimental groups. The approach enables individualized post-SCI recovery characterization that can neutralize procedural bias, minimize animal numbers, and provide a probabilistic basis for evaluating whether interventions enhance or suppress wound repair processes. Our findings establish a foundation for improving preclinical SCI study design and accelerating identification of effective therapies.

Article.Title: Assessment of the zoonotic spillover potential of SARS-CoV-2-related coronaviruses from Rhinolophus pusillus bats in Thailand
Article.Authors: Supataragul A.; Tan C.; Suksavate W.; Rattanatumhi K.; Noradechanon K.; Thippamom N.; Duengkae P.; Manee-Orn P.; Ninwattana S.; Sirichan N.; Panpuengkaew S.; Firth C.; Olival K.; Li H.; Daszak P.; Wang L.; Wacharapluesadee S.; Putcharoen O.
Article.Abstract: Proactive surveillance of wildlife has the potential to help prevent pandemics caused by coronaviruses spilling over into human populations, but the relative value of this approach versus early outbreak investigation has been debated. This study investigated bat coronavirus zoonotic potential in a high human-wildlife interaction site in Ratchaburi, Thailand. We sampled 261 Rhinolophus pusillus bats, a known reservoir for sarbecoviruses, and detected diverse alpha- and betacoronaviruses (prevalence = 16.47%), including SARS-CoV-2-related coronaviruses, alongside paramyxoviruses at a lower prevalence (5.36%). Notably, the detected paramyxoviruses were phylogenetically distinct from previously described paramyxoviruses, suggesting the presence of previously uncharacterized viral diversity. Five complete SARS-CoV-2-related coronavirus genomes were obtained, showing significant divergence in spike and ORF8 regions and diverse recombination patterns. One identified SARS-CoV-2-related coronavirus, RpuRB21065, exhibited high spike and receptor-binding domain similarities to SARS-CoV-2. The receptor-binding domain demonstrated binding to human ACE2 and the spike protein induced syncytia in vitro. However, human sera from SARS-CoV-2 vaccinated individuals effectively neutralized RpuRB21065, suggesting pre-existing SARS-CoV-2 immunity may minimize current spillover potential. Our study is a proof-of-concept that proactive viral discovery and wildlife surveillance in EID hotspots can provide information of direct public health relevance, even in the absence of viral isolation. This study investigates the zoonotic potential of bat coronaviruses at a human-wildlife interface in Thailand. Molecular analyses identify a SARS-CoV-2-related strain capable of human ACE2 binding, which is neutralized by post-vaccination immunity.

Article.Title: Tuned inhibitory control of neuronal firing thresholds explains predictive sensorimotor behavior
Article.Authors: Ahn J.; Kim S.; Park J.; Woo S.; Sohn H.; Lee J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Prior expectations guide sensorimotor behavior when sensory information is uncertain, yet the cellular mechanisms underlying this integration remain elusive. Here, we investigate how priors in sensory motion direction shape neural population dynamics by combining recurrent neural network (RNN) modeling with macaque smooth pursuit behavior and middle temporal area (area MT) electrophysiology. Our RNN model reveals that prior expectations are implemented by elevating firing thresholds in neurons tuned away from the expected direction. This selective inhibition sharpens population tuning and reduces behavioral variability under weak sensory information conditions. We validated this prediction in vivo : delta-band local field potentials in area MT, where the phase reflects neural excitability states, exhibited direction-specific phase shifts that scaled with the deviation from the expected direction. These findings demonstrate that prior expectations enhance behavioral reliability through tuned inhibitory control of neuronal excitability, providing a mechanistic link between Bayesian inference and cortical circuit dynamics.

Article.Title: Neural dynamics of reconstructing knowledge structure from temporally disordered inputs
Article.Authors: Xu X.; He X.; Zhou S.; Feng X.; Lu C.
Article.Abstract: Humans possess a remarkable ability to integrate fragmented experiences into coherent internal models. However, the neural dynamics supporting structure reconstruction from temporally disordered inputs remain poorly understood. Here, we show that knowledge reconstruction follows a delayed, two-stage neural trajectory. Two independent cohorts learned complex physics concepts from scrambled video lectures during behavioral testing or functional magnetic resonance imaging. Learners receiving disordered inputs required sufficient information accumulation before their internal models matched the expert-defined structure. The posterior cingulate cortex showed stronger correspondence with knowledge structure during updating, whereas the precuneus showed more sustained correspondence after reorganization. Functional coupling between these two regions predicted immediate learning success for disordered input, but this success did not fully translate into robust delayed retention. These findings reveal a two-stage neural mechanism for transforming fragmented inputs into coherent understanding, highlighting both the adaptive capacity and potential subsequent cost of learning from fragmented materials. Using behavioral ratings and functional magnetic resonance imaging, this study tracks how learners dynamically reconstruct coherent knowledge from temporally disordered lectures. The posterior cingulate cortex supports structural updating, the precuneus shows later sustained representation, and their coupling predicts immediate learning success.

Article.Title: Identification of a novel dependency between PRMT5 and APC-LOF in preclinical models of FAP disease
Article.Authors: Gaffney D.; Hulpia F.; Thuring J.; Vesely E.; Retzbach E.; Etwebi Z.; Jiang Z.; Francis A.; Mattson B.; Liddane A.; Clancy K.; Candelaria F.; Fan Y.; Smith-Monroy C.; Cowley G.; Wong V.; Gokare P.; Boj S.; Verissimo C.; Overmeer R.; Silva M.; ten Hag G.; Nicolaï J.; Hixon M.; Chu G.
Article.Abstract: Strategies for targeting adenomatous polyposis coli ( APC) loss-of-function ( APC -LOF) may provide an opportunity to intercept tumorigenesis in high-risk CRC patients, such as those with Familial Adenomatous Polyposis (FAP). Here, we uncovered a novel synthetic lethal dependency of APC -LOF on protein arginine methyltransferase (PRMT5). JNJ-64619178 (JNJ-9178), a potent clinical (PRMT5) inhibitor, demonstrated >800-fold more growth inhibition of engineered APC KO organoids compared to wild-type isogenic congeners. We further confirmed this PRMT5/APC dependency by testing other PRMT5 inhibitors with various chemotypes and mechanisms of action. Notably, less antiproliferative activity was observed with methylthioadenosine (MTA)-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitors, MRTX1719 and TNG462. Furthermore, we assessed the impact of JNJ-9178 on colon adenoma burden in the Apc min+ -DSS mouse model, where we started treatment either before (early interception) or after (late interception) measurable adenoma burden had been established. A 72% and 66% reduction in adenoma burden was observed, respectively, compared to vehicle-treated mice, suggesting that PRMT5 inhibition both suppresses polyp growth and reduces existing polyp burden. The data we present here suggests that PRMT5 inhibition in the colon offers a strategy to intercept tumorigenesis in patients at a high risk of developing APC -LOF-driven CRC.

Article.Title: Amygdala Oligodendrocyte <scp>MDH1</scp> Dysregulation and Mitochondrial Dysfunction in High Urea‐Induced Anxiety‐Like Behavior
Article.Authors: Hu J.; Zhang M.; Jiang S.; Bi H.; Tu B.; Zhang S.; Wan G.; Wang Q.; Liu Y.; Leng J.; Chen X.; Li J.; Chen D.; Li G.; Gui J.; Huang B.; Ran J.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT The high incidence and mortality rates of anxiety disorders in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) have drawn attention. Prior studies identified urea as an independent risk factor for mental disorders in CKD. While urea accumulation is known to impair synaptic plasticity, its effects on glial cells remain unclear. How urea influences oligodendrocyte lineage differentiation may represent a critical node in neuron–glia interactions. Previous studies have shown that OL‐lineage cells may be underrepresented in scRNA‐seq datasets. We selected amygdala tissue from wild‐type and high‐urea (UT‐B − / − ) mice and performed single‐nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA‐seq), behavioral tests, and cellular experiments to delineate the impact of urea on oligodendrocyte lineage dynamics. In UT‐B − / − mice, the relative abundance of oligodendrocyte subpopulations enriched for mitochondrial transcripts decreased, suggesting vulnerability to urea toxicity. Dlat and MDH1, genes associated with TCA cycle‐related metabolism, were downregulated alongside alterations in mitochondrial and oxidative phosphorylation‐related transcriptional programs. Urea dose‐dependently decreased MDH1 expression, mitochondrial membrane potential, and intracellular ATP content in MO3.13 cells. Regulatory analyses linked MDH1 to energy metabolism and neurodegenerative pathways. Trajectory reconstruction suggested altered differentiation‐ and myelination‐related transcriptional programs in mitochondria‐related oligodendrocytes (MitOLs). The cytoplasmic concentration and fate of oxaloacetic acid (OAA) are regulated by the reversible catalysis of MDH1. OAA supplementation partially restored amygdalar MDH1 expression and alleviated anxiety‐like behaviors in UT‐B − / − mice, while improving mitochondrial bioenergetics in urea‐exposed MO3.13 cells. These findings support a candidate metabolic–glial model linking elevated urea, MDH1 dysregulation, oligodendrocyte bioenergetic dysfunction, and anxiety‐like behavior, with potential relevance to CKD‐associated anxiety.

Article.Title: Brain PDGFR β + Cells Exhibit Diverse Reactive Phenotypes After Stroke Without Requiring KLF4
Article.Authors: Manrique‐Castano D.; ElAli A.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT The pathobiology of ischemic stroke is associated with the activation of brain platelet‐derived growth factor receptor (PDGFR) β + perivascular cells. While Krüppel‐like factor (KLF)4 is a well‐established mediator of peripheral PDGFR β + cell activation, its role in brain PDGFR β + cells remains elusive. Herein, we aimed to characterize the spatiotemporal reactivity of brain PDGFR β + cells, while assessing KLF4 contribution upon experimental ischemic stroke using transgenic mice that enable tracking PDGFR β + cells or conditionally depleting KLF4 in PDGFR β + cells. Moving beyond the qualitative descriptors, we sought to develop point pattern analysis (PPA) and topological data analysis (TDA) workflows to generate robust and reusable mathematical models to assess spatial cell responses and tissue scar topological changes. First, we report the emergence of phenotypically distinct reactive parenchymal PDGFR β + cells, which cannot be causally and exclusively linked, as it is currently proposed, to local cell proliferation or adjacent vascular detachment. Furthermore, we show that KLF4 is barely expressed in brain PDGFR β + cells under normal conditions and that it is only marginally induced in reactive PDGFR β + cells at the injured brain. Notably, the conditional attenuation of KLF4 expression specifically in reactive PDGFR β + cells does not alter spatial cellular distribution nor scar organization. This suggests that, in contrast to peripheral PDGFR β + cells upon ischemic insults, KLF4 is not a main regulator of the reactivity of brain cells in response to ischemic stroke. Ultimately, our findings supported by open‐source spatiotemporal models indicate that the reactivity of brain PDGFR β + perivascular cells is highly heterogeneous and fundamentally distinct from peripheral PDGFR β + cells.

Article.Title: sox17 Mutagenesis Reveals Compounding Effects ofMaternal and Zygotic Contribution on Microglia Abundance
Article.Authors: Spring C.; Dennen J.; Gan D.; Li J.; Smith C.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Embryonic development is shaped by maternal and zygotic factors but how the interplay between these factors contributes to phenotypic variability and impacts specific populations of brain cells, and subsequently neurodevelopment, remains largely unknown. Here, we reveal a double hit phenomenon that impacts microglia and microglia precursors during development. Using zebrafish, we identified a mutation in sry‐related HMG box gene‐17 (sox17) that exhibits a maternal effect phenotype presenting as a reduction of microglia in the brain and precursors in the yolk sac. We demonstrate that microglia deficits are exacerbated in homozygous offspring from homozygous parents compared to homozygous offspring from heterozygous parents, suggesting a compounding effect of maternal and zygotic sox17 mutation on microglia abundance. We observe that sox17 is expressed in microglia and yolk sac precursors and is maternally contributed. Injections of sox17 RNA during embryogenesis are sufficient to rescue microglia and yolk sac cell abundance. To identify additional genes interacting with sox17 , we perform a genetic screen using CRISPR mutagenesis and identify f11r.1, gas6 , and mpp1 as microglia regulators, which we demonstrate are expressed in zebrafish microglia. Transcriptional and mutant analyses with these genes suggest sox17 positively regulates mpp1 transcription. These results demonstrate that microglia are susceptible to additive effects of maternal and zygotic sox17 mutation, and that offspring greatly differ in their susceptibility to microglia deficits depending on the mother's genotype. Our findings highlight that both the maternal and offspring genotype should be considered when examining neurodevelopmental disorders that could arise from microglia dysfunction.

Article.Title: Disruption of Lactate Metabolism in the Peripheral Nervous System Leads to Motor‐Selective Deficits
Article.Authors: Bloom A.; Tendulkar S.; Hackett A.; Strickland A.; Sato‐Yamada Y.; Yuan L.; Dong W.; Ippolito J.; Schmidt R.; Sasaki Y.; DiAntonio A.; Milbrandt J.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Schwann cells (SCs) myelinate and provide trophic support to axons in the peripheral nervous system (PNS). Disrupted SC metabolism can lead to demyelination and axon degeneration, cardinal deficits in peripheral neuropathy. The lactate shuttle hypothesis proposes that glycolytic support cells supply lactate to axons to sustain their high metabolic demands. This transfer requires lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) to interconvert lactate and pyruvate in both SCs and neurons. To test the importance of lactate metabolism in the PNS, we selectively knocked out both LDHA and LDHB in ChAT‐positive neurons, including motor neurons (MNs), Nav1.8‐lineage sensory neurons (SNs), or SCs. Interestingly, motor axons and their synapses progressively degenerate when LDH is deleted from either MNs or SCs, but defects in Nav1.8‐lineage sensory axons and their terminals are not observed when LDH is excised from either SNs or SCs. Deletion of LDH in SCs leads to decreased ATP in peripheral nerves despite marked accumulation of pyruvate and glycolytic intermediates, consistent with energetic deficits due to failed conversion of pyruvate to lactate. Cholinergic neuron‐specific gene expression using ribosome affinity profiling (RiboTag) identified a strong response to metabolic compromise by activating axon‐injury stress programs in LDH‐deficient neurons. Finally, blocking axon degeneration in LDH‐deficient mice by SARM1 deletion preserves axon morphology without ameliorating behavioral and electrophysiological defects, demonstrating functional decline of lactate‐deprived axons that remain physically intact. These results show a differential requirement for SC‐derived lactate by motor vs. sensory axons, suggesting that lactate availability could influence the course of motor neuron diseases.

Article.Title: Astrocytic <scp>EAAT</scp> ‐2 Upregulation Supports Neuro‐Axonal Homeostasis in Chronic Inflammatory <scp>CNS</scp> Lesions
Article.Authors: Reukauf L.; Margineanu A.; Muinjonov B.; Chen J.; Cui Y.; Rosiewicz K.; Radbruch H.; Munro I.; Alisch M.; Siffrin V.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Neuronal loss in multiple sclerosis (MS) is a key factor in the progression of disability. Axonal degeneration within MS lesions is central to progressive MS pathology, yet its mechanisms are not fully understood. Excess extracellular l‐glutamate (GLUT) is neurotoxic due to overstimulation of GLUT receptors. Excitotoxicity, driven by GLUT, is a suspected contributor to several central nervous system (CNS) diseases. Astrocytic glutamate transporters EAAT‐1 and EAAT‐2 play crucial roles in managing extracellular GLUT, yet their role in chronic MS remains underexplored. Using the animal model experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) and advanced microscopy in live anesthetized mice, we examined GLUT‐mediated neurotoxicity and protective mechanisms in chronic CNS lesions. By employing genetically encoded fluorescent biosensors, we visualized extracellular GLUT levels and axonal Ca 2+ dynamics within the live mouse brain during EAE. In acute EAE, extracellular GLUT levels were high, while in chronic lesions, normalized GLUT levels together with sustained EAAT‐2 upregulation were consistent with a protective astrocytic response. EAAT‐2 inhibition in chronic lesions led to higher intra‐axonal Ca 2+ levels and morphological changes consistent with neuroaxonal injury, indicating that EAAT‐2 upregulation may counter excitotoxicity and support neuroprotection. Post‐mortem MS brain tissue analysis provided complementary evidence, showing elevated EAAT‐1 and EAAT‐2 expression in chronic MS lesions with expression patterns varying according to lesion type and cellularity. This study highlights astrocytic mechanisms that may contribute to neuroaxonal protection in MS tissue and suggests targeting GLUT transporters as a promising strategy to limit neurodegeneration in progressive MS.

Article.Title: Single‐Cell Integration of Mouse Models of Autism Reveals Conserved Transcriptomic Signatures of Excitatory‐Inhibitory Imbalance and Glial Dysfunction
Article.Authors: Nani J.; Duque V.; Muotri A.; Mecawi A.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT The etiological heterogeneity of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) complicates identifying core molecular mechanisms. We systematically integrated scRNA‐seq data from 11 diverse genetic and environmental mouse ( Mus musculus ) models, encompassing > 300,000 cells across multiple brain regions and developmental stages. Using advanced computational harmonization (RPCA), we identified robust convergent transcriptomic signatures that transcend model‐specific variability. Our findings reveal widespread alterations in neuronal communication pathways, specifically increased excitatory‐inhibitory signaling involving PTN, SLIT, and PTPR pathways. Furthermore, cell–cell communication analysis via NicheNet prioritized ligand‐receptor pairs associated with altered circuit excitability, offering a predictive blueprint of dysregulated intercellular crosstalk. Crucially, we identified significant glial involvement characterized by astrocyte function inhibition, marked by Aqp4 and Kcnj10 downregulation related to impaired water/potassium homeostasis and mature oligodendrocyte metabolic dysregulation through Olig family upregulation and enhanced oxidative phosphorylation. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) significantly overlapped with SFARI‐listed high‐confidence risk genes, particularly within excitatory neuronal subtypes. Comparison with human postmortem single‐nucleus data from the prefrontal and parietal cortices demonstrated conserved signatures related to impaired synaptic protein synthesis (GRIN2B, CAMK2A) and oligodendrocyte‐mediated neurodevelopmental deficits (NRXN, DLGAP). This study confirms that E/I imbalance and glial dysfunction are universal cellular pathologies in ASD, providing a robust, large‐scale reference for identifying novel therapeutic targets with single‐cell resolution.

Article.Title: A Müller Glia‐Retinal Pigment Epithelium Apical Network Surrounding Cone Outer Segments in Fish and Mouse
Article.Authors: Sharkova M.; Housset M.; Boudreau S.; Dworkind C.; Amidian S.; Cayouette M.; Hocking J.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Homeostasis of the vertebrate retina critically depends on two non‐neuronal cell populations, Müller glia and the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). Their opposing apical surfaces delineate the subretinal space, a specialized extracellular compartment housing the light‐detecting outer segments of photoreceptors. Although the individual interactions between these supporting cells and photoreceptors have been extensively characterized, Müller glia and the RPE have long been presumed to remain physically separate in the healthy retina. Here, we challenge this assumption and present a revised model of the subretinal space architecture based on detailed FIB‐SEM and confocal microscopy imaging of the zebrafish and mouse outer retina. We demonstrate that both Müller glia and the RPE extend long apical processes that not only contact one another but also collectively ensheath cone outer segments, forming a previously unrecognized tripartite interface. These contact regions are highly elaborated in fish and, while comparatively sparser, are still present in mouse. Developmentally, the growth and interdigitation of Müller glial and RPE apical processes follow the emergence of the outer segment in both species and, in mouse, coincides with the onset of visual function. Although glial–RPE interactions are enriched at cone‐associated sites, their presence is not strictly dependent on cone localization in either species, suggesting they represent a fundamental feature of the vertebrate subretinal space. Together, these findings revise our understanding of the subretinal space cytoarchitecture and reveal a previously unappreciated structural interaction between Müller glia, RPE, and photoreceptors that is conserved across vertebrate species.

Article.Title: <scp>CD47</scp> – <scp>SIRPα</scp> Axis as a Target for Neuroprotection
Article.Authors: Gómez‐López A.; Manich G.; Penas C.; Pampalona J.; Villacampa N.; Almolda B.; Viennois E.; Rojas S.; González B.; Castellano B.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Microglial “Off” signaling is crucial for maintaining microglia in a homeostatic state through the interaction of “Off” neuronal ligands with their corresponding microglial receptors. Dysregulation of “Off” signaling has been reported in both acute and chronic neuroinflammation; however, the influence of inflammatory mediators on this pathway remains underexplored. Here, we investigated whether chronic IL‐6 or IL‐10 overexpression modulates microglia–neuron “Off” signaling after FNA, thereby accounting for the previously observed differences in facial motoneuron (FMN) survival and microglial reactivity in transgenic mouse models (GFAP‐IL6Tg and GFAP‐IL10Tg). To this end, we examined the expression of the neuronal “Off” ligands CD200, CX3CL1, CD47, and CD22, as well as their corresponding microglial “Off” receptors CD200R, CX3CR1, SIRP‐α, and CD45 in non‐lesioned and axotomized GFAP‐IL6Tg, GFAP‐IL10Tg, and WT mice across multiple time points. Our analyses revealed the dynamic regulation of “Off” signaling in both neurons and microglia during microgliosis and FMN phagocytosis and showed temporally restricted strain‐specific differences in CD47 expression across genotypes. Chronic IL‐6 overproduction promoted a more phagocytic microglial phenotype, defined by downregulation of SIRPα and CX3CR1 alongside upregulated CD45 in the microglial population. In contrast, chronic IL‐10 overproduction did not alter the expression of microglial “Off” receptors but induced an IL‐10 dependent accelerated upregulation of neuronal CD47. Our findings highlight the CD47‐SIRPα axis as a key regulator of FMN death via microglial phagocytosis and emphasize IL‐10's neuroprotective potential role through enhanced neuronal CD47 signaling. Overall, this work positions the CD47‐SIRPα axis as a potential therapeutic target to mitigate neuroinflammation‐induced neuronal loss.

Article.Title: Microglial Labeling in Mouse Spinal Cord Injury: A Review of Timing, Efficacy, and Specificity
Article.Authors: Colbert R.; Di Stefano J.; Dooley D.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI) is a complex and disabling condition with no curative therapy currently available. The mechanical damage of the primary injury phase is followed and exacerbated by a secondary injury phase, characterized by the release of free radicals and pro‐inflammatory cytokines that lead to chronic inflammation. Microglia, as the resident immune cells of the central nervous system, play a critical role in orchestrating this inflammatory response. Studying their dynamics after SCI not only deepens our understanding of injury pathology but also advances the development of microglia‐targeted immunotherapies. However, trauma‐induced transcriptional and phenotypic changes mean that markers used to identify homeostatic microglia may be unreliable when applied to their reactive counterparts. Another major challenge lies within discriminating resident microglia from infiltrating monocyte‐derived macrophages (MDM), which permeate the blood‐spinal cord barrier (BSCB) after injury. In this review, we examine three key variables for selecting appropriate strategies for labeling microglia in mice: (i) time (in relation to injury); (ii) efficacy (within the chosen murine SCI model); and (iii) specificity (to microglia). We discuss the transcriptional landscape of murine microglia pre‐injury and its alteration post‐injury, evaluate the strengths and limitations of commonly used markers, and highlight emerging tools and approaches for studying microglia in preclinical murine SCI research.

Article.Title: Ifi27l2a Facilitates the Recruitment of Pathogenic T Cells by Retinal Microglia in the Initiation Phase of Experimental Autoimmune Uveoretinitis
Article.Authors: Gao W.; Wu P.; Xie K.; Zhou P.; Jin B.; Zhu H.; Li F.; Wang Y.; Lei B.; Jin X.; Du L.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT The mechanisms by which pathogenic T cells enter the immune‐privileged retina at the onset of uveitis remain unclear. To identify regulatory targets that promote retinal inflammation, we established an experimental autoimmune uveoretinitis (EAU) model by immunizing C57BL/6J mice with IRBP 651–670 and dynamically evaluated retinal inflammation after induction; fundus lesions were prominent, with the first 14 days representing the initiation phase, Days 14–28 the amplification phase, Days 28–35 the peak phase, and Days 35–42 the regression phase. We characterized retinal cellular alterations from the pre‐inflammatory stage to the peak stage using single‐cell transcriptomic analysis, and found that retinal immune cells changed in parallel with EAU severity, while immune‐cell interactions were strongest on Day 14, especially between microglia and T cells through multiple chemokine‐related pathways. We then identified key cell populations and candidate targets through integrated analyses and functional validation, and Ifi27l2a emerged as a core gene associated with inflammatory and immune responses in retinal microglia on Day 14. In vitro knockdown of Ifi27l2a in LPS‐activated BV‐2 cells reduced inflammatory mediator production and abolished Th1/Th17 induction. In vivo targeting of Ifi27l2a attenuated EAU severity and restored the balance of T‐cell subsets. These findings indicate that microglia are highly activated before retinal inflammation becomes prominent and that Ifi27l2a regulates this early pathogenic process.

Article.Title: Neuronal Overexpression of Glycogen Synthase Kinase‐3β Accelerates Age‐Related Glial, Vascular, and Inflammatory Remodeling of the Murine Dentate Gyrus
Article.Authors: Prádanos‐Senén A.; Rodríguez‐Moreno C.; Llorens‐Martín M.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Adult hippocampal neurogenesis (AHN)—the lifelong generation of new neurons in the dentate gyrus (DG)—depends on the integrity of the subgranular zone (SGZ) neurogenic niche, which comprises astrocytes, microglia, oligodendroglial cells, and a dense vascular network. Although AHN declines during aging and is impaired in Alzheimer's disease (AD), the cell‐type‐specific alterations within the DG underlying this decline remain poorly characterized. Given the critical role of glycogen synthase kinase‐3β (GSK‐3β) in AD pathogenesis and AHN regulation, we studied how the overexpression of this kinase in dentate granule cells (DGCs) remodels the cellular and vascular composition of the DG throughout life. Using a layer‐resolved approach (SGZ vs. granule cell layer (GCL)) and mice of distinct ages (4–30 months), we quantified glial densities, cellular contacts, vascular architecture, and cytokine profiles in wild‐type (WT) and GSK‐3β‐overexpressing (GSK‐3β‐OE) mice. In the former, aging was associated with a layer‐specific reorganization, characterized by progressive astrocyte loss in the SGZ, midlife increases in GCL microglia, a reduction in oligodendroglial progenitors, and enhanced SGZ vascularization. GSK‐3β overexpression accelerated age‐related changes, triggering premature SGZ astrocyte depletion by 4 months, broader disruption featuring reduced SGZ microglial and mature oligodendrocyte densities accompanied by increased microglial morphological complexity, vascular restructuring, and a shift toward a pro‐inflammatory environment. Therefore, neuronal GSK‐3β overexpression promoted a non‐cell‐autonomous reorganization of the DG, consistent with premature remodeling of the neurogenic niche. These results provide mechanistic insights into AHN failure in AD and point to the modulation of GSK‐3β activity as a strategy to preserve DG integrity.

Article.Title: Red Fluorescent Labeling of Myelin by Membrane‐Targeted <scp>tdTomato</scp> in Transgenic Mouse Lines
Article.Authors: Reinert A.; Winkler U.; Goebbels S.; Komarek L.; Möbius W.; Zanker H.; Schoknecht K.; Bornschein G.; Schmidt H.; Fledrich R.; Stassart R.; Hirrlinger P.; Nave K.; Werner H.; Saab A.; Hirrlinger J.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Myelin is a highly complex membranous structure wrapped around axons by oligodendrocytes or Schwann cells in the central and peripheral nervous system, respectively. Fluorescent labeling is widely used to study the structure and dynamics of myelin. However, in vivo tools enabling red fluorescent labeling of myelinating cells and their myelin sheaths remain limited. Here, we generated a set of seven transgenic mouse lines expressing a membrane‐targeted variant of the red fluorescent protein tdTomato in myelinating oligodendrocytes and Schwann cells throughout the nervous system. In the peripheral nervous system, the pattern of fluorescence in sciatic nerves indicates predominant localization of tdTomato to non‐compact myelin compartments including the inner and outer tongues, paranodal loops and Schmidt‐Lanterman incisures. In summary, our work provides a set of novel mouse lines with myelin labeled by red fluorescence, which are compatible with diverse imaging modalities in the green spectral range enabling integrated structural and functional imaging.

Article.Title: Schwann Cell‐Specific <scp>ATG7</scp> ‐Dependent Autophagy Protects Myelin in a Mouse Model of Krabbe Disease
Article.Authors: Dhimal N.; Sidharth A.; Zhang J.; Rudra T.; Hurley E.; Paez P.; Sim F.; Shin D.; Feltri M.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Krabbe disease (KD) is a lysosomal storage disorder characterized by severe peripheral demyelination caused by mutations in galactosylceramidase (GALC), leading to the accumulation of galactosylceramide and psychosine. Although psychosine toxicity is central to KD pathology, additional mechanisms likely contribute to myelin dysfunction. Because Schwann cells (SCs) play a critical role in myelin maintenance, and GALC deficiency disrupts lysosomal function, we hypothesized that autophagy is altered in SCs during KD progression. Using a SC‐specific Galc conditional knockout ( Galc SC cKO) mouse model, we identified early changes in autophagy‐related protein levels and increased autophagosome abundance during the pre‐symptomatic phase, prior to detectable myelin abnormalities. To assess whether autophagy contributes to disease progression, we selectively deleted Atg7 , an essential regulator of canonical autophagy, in SCs. Atg7 deletion alone did not affect myelin or behavior, but its loss in Galc SC cKO mice markedly worsened disease severity. Atg7‐Galc SC cKO mice exhibited significantly thinner myelin and pronounced deficits in motor performance and nerve conduction, accompanied by altered steady‐state levels of autophagy‐associated proteins and functional decline. Notably, Atg7 deletion in Galc SC cKO mice did not further increase macrophage abundance, suggesting that the worsened myelin phenotype occurs without additional macrophage recruitment at this stage. Together, these findings demonstrate that autophagy‐associated changes occur early in KD and ATG7‐dependent pathways play a protective role during disease progression. Modulating ATG7‐dependent pathways may therefore warrant further investigation as a strategy to support myelin maintenance in KD and related lysosomal disorders.

Article.Title: Myelin Maintenance and Addition Regulate Synaptic Plasticity in the Adult Mouse Cortex
Article.Authors: Pepper R.; Makowiecki K.; Pitman K.; Ricci R.; Nicoli A.; Nguyen P.; Blizzard C.; Emery B.; Cullen C.; Young K.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Myelin has the capacity to affect synapse number or plasticity across the lifespan. We report that disrupting oligodendrocyte (OL) and myelin maintenance from P57 ( Plp‐CreER T2 :: Myrf fl/fl mice) induces myelin loss and impairs action potential conduction and gross motor performance. By studying sparsely labeled layer V pyramidal neurons in the primary motor cortex of P57 + 60 mice, we determined that apical and basal dendritic spine densities were normal; however, more were large, stable mushroom spines that generated larger amplitude miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents. When we instead prevented OL and myelin addition from P57 ( Pdgfrα‐CreER:: Myrf fl/fl mice), action potential conduction velocity, gross motor performance, and spine densities were normal; however, basal dendritic spine morphology was changed. Without adult myelination, the basal dendrites of P57 + 60 mice retained the morphological characteristics of dendrites in P57 + 0 mice, which have a higher proportion of thin, plastic spines. These data indicate that existing myelin imposes limits on the proportion of spines that become mushroom spines, allowing neurons to remain plastic, while adult myelination is required for spine stabilization within the basal but not apical dendritic compartment. These data show that myelin regulates synaptic plasticity within the motor circuit and offer a potential mechanism by which myelination can influence motor skill learning and/or recall.

Article.Title: Molecular Control of Neural Stem Cell Quiescence in the Adult Zebrafish Telencephalon: Established Mechanisms and an Integrative Hypothesis
Article.Authors: Hoareau M.; Diotel N.; Rastegar S.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT The zebrafish telencephalon is an excellent model for adult neurogenesis under physiological and regenerative conditions, as many pathways regulating neural stem cell behavior are conserved with mammalian neurogenic niches. Resident radial glial cells (RGCs) serve as neural stem cells in the adult brain and are readily accessible in vivo, because forebrain eversion repositions the ventricular zone to the dorsal surface. Recent studies have revealed substantial heterogeneity among RGCs, including activation‐primed cells and deeply quiescent states during homeostasis. Here, we first review the evidence that four mechanisms control quiescence in pallial RGCs: Notch3‐mediated lateral inhibition, the neuronal bone morphogenetic protein (BMP)‐Id1 axis, the nuclear receptor Nr2f1b, and the secreted factor Midkine‐a. The evidence supporting them is unequal, and we state its level for each before asking whether they act together. Notch‐mediated lateral inhibition and neuronal BMP‐Id1 signaling converge on her4.1 , the clearest documented interaction among them, whereas Nr2f1b establishes a deeper dormancy program that resists Notch and BMP inhibition and protects a reserve stem cell pool. Midkine‐a is proposed to reinforce quiescence, pending functional validation. Finally, we propose as a hypothesis that these mechanisms act as partially redundant inputs whose relative contributions determine quiescence depth and vary along the antero‐posterior axis of the pallium. Together, these findings reframe quiescence as a spectrum of actively maintained conditions rather than a passive default state. These mechanisms are conserved across vertebrates, with implications for understanding why mammalian neural stem cell pools decline with age and injury.

Article.Title: Photobiomodulation Ameliorates Alexander Disease Through <scp>AMPK</scp> / <scp>mTOR</scp> ‐Mediated Mitophagy
Article.Authors: Qiu N.; Zhang J.; Yi H.; Dong S.; Han L.; Feng Z.; Gao S.; Shi J.; Liu J.; Wu Y.; Wei X.; Wei Y.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Alexander disease (AxD) is a rare neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the pathological accumulation of Rosenthal fibers (RFs) and astrocytic inflammation. Despite advances in elucidating its genetic basis, effective therapeutic strategies remain limited. Recent studies indicate that astrocytes in AxD exhibit excessive mitochondrial fragmentation, which may cause mitochondrial dysfunction and inflammatory response. Photobiomodulation (PBM) has been shown to improve mitochondrial function and exert anti‐inflammatory effects, suggesting it may be a promising candidate for the treatment of AxD. Here, we report that exposure to 1070‐nm infrared light exerts therapeutic efficacy in AxD. Specifically, using the astrocytes derived from AxD patients and a mouse model of AxD, we demonstrate that PBM regulates AMPK/mTOR signaling and promotes mitophagy, thereby attenuating reactive oxygen species production from fragmented mitochondria and subsequent inflammatory status. This study suggests PBM may serve as a novel, non‐invasive therapeutic approach for the treatment of AxD.

Article.Title: Advanced Cellular Models for Drug Testing and Discovery to Target Cardiac Fibrosis Progression
Article.Authors: Icolaro F.; Chimenti I.; Cozzolino C.; Bordin A.; Pontecorvi V.; Frati G.; De Falco E.; Floris E.; Picchio V.; Pagano F.
Article.Abstract: Cardiac fibrosis is a complex and dynamic pathological process, central for cardiac repair, characterised by continuous cell–cell and cell–matrix interactions. Three-dimensional (3D) models are gaining increasing relevance, compared with traditional two-dimensional (2D) cellular setups, due to their ability to recapitulate key features of the fibrotic microenvironment at different levels of complexity, including cellular heterogeneity, spatial organisation and tissue mechanical properties. These systems have enabled a deeper investigation of fibrosis mechanobiology and the mechanosensitive pathways involved in disease progression, contributing to the identification of potential therapeutic targets for cardiac repair. Increasing biological complexity can reveal therapeutic responses that remain undetected in conventional models; however, the predictive value of 3D systems has so far been confirmed in vivo only for a limited number of platforms and compounds. The role of 3D models is therefore expanding beyond disease modelling towards platforms for the screening and evaluation of antifibrotic strategies, pointing to increasingly functional cardiac reparative strategies. Here, we distinguish model complexity, biological fidelity and demonstrated predictive value, compare current platforms according to their validation level and limitations, and discuss the benchmarks and standards required for their routine use in antifibrotic drug discovery. From this perspective, the development of systems that are not necessarily more sophisticated, but progressively more informative and predictive, may help bridge the gap between conventional 2D in vitro models and animal studies, ultimately improving the translational relevance of preclinical evaluation.

Article.Title: Abuse of Anabolic-Androgenic Steroids: Molecular and Organ Dysfunctions—A Critical Narrative Review for Forensic Interpretation
Article.Authors: Morena D.; Marchesini D.; Manta A.; Caruso A.; Santori V.; Crusco P.; Sirello R.; Umani Ronchi F.; Scopetti M.; Fineschi V.
Article.Abstract: Anabolic-androgenic steroids (AAS) comprise testosterone and synthetic androgenic compounds that differ substantially in pharmacokinetics, receptor activity, route of administration, hepatic metabolism, and clinical risk. From a forensic perspective, the central problem is not simply to catalogue adverse effects but to determine how verified exposure, chronology, co-use of other substances, clinical and electrocardiographic findings, pathological alterations, and toxicological results should be integrated when evaluating an individual death. This critical narrative review therefore distinguishes therapeutic testosterone replacement from non-medical and supraphysiological AAS exposure and examines the evidence connecting exposure to endocrine, cardiovascular, hepatic, renal, musculoskeletal, neuropsychiatric, and immunological findings. Human prospective and observational data support associations between androgen abuse and endocrine suppression, erythrocytosis, adverse lipid changes, increased blood pressure, and left-ventricular structural or functional alterations, with recovery of selected measured parameters reported in the studied cohorts. Electrocardiographic studies also report prolonged repolarization indices and impaired heart-rate recovery in AAS-using bodybuilders; however, these intermediate markers do not by themselves establish an individual risk of fatal ventricular arrhythmia. Forensic autopsy series describe myocardial hypertrophy, fibrosis, coronary disease, and other lesions in AAS-associated deaths, but these findings are not specific and require correlation with toxicology, clinical history, circumstances, and alternative causes. The detailed immunological literature is predominantly mechanistic, in vitro, or experimental and currently provides limited direct forensic evidence in human AAS users. Similarly, Raman spectroscopy is best regarded as a developing adjunct for forensic trace or analytical applications rather than a validated method for confirming AAS accumulation or cause of death in post-mortem tissue. We propose a structured forensic framework in which exposure is first verified, the temporal and pharmacological context is reconstructed, findings are assessed for specificity and plausibility, co-exposures and competing causes are examined, and the final opinion explicitly communicates the degree of certainty and the limitations of the evidence.

Article.Title: Not All EVs Are Equal: Functional Heterogeneity of Extracellular Vesicles in Neuroregenerative Therapies
Article.Authors: Chodkowska-Michalowska M.; Hawryluk O.; Lakomy S.; Slysz A.; Sarnowska A.
Article.Abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are increasingly being investigated as cell-free therapies for neurological diseases. However, their clinical application remains limited by biological and functional heterogeneity. EVs should therefore not be considered as a single, uniform therapeutic product defined only by their cell of origin, size, or conventional vesicle classification. EV composition and activity are influenced by extrinsic factors, including donor and tissue source, culture conditions, and isolation procedures, as well as by intrinsic mechanisms of vesicle biogenesis and selective cargo loading. Some vesicles may have beneficial therapeutic effects, whereas others may show little biological activity or act on unintended cellular targets. For this reason, EVs may be better classified according to biological function rather than only physical properties or cellular origin. A functionality-based classification could improve potency assessment, dose selection, reproducibility, and the development of consistent EV-based products. EV properties can be modulated by selecting appropriate parental cells, modifying culture conditions, or using genetic or metabolic engineering to alter EV production and cargo. Single-vesicle approaches can reveal differences between EV subpopulations and identify those responsible for specific biological effects. Overall, understanding EV heterogeneity may provide a rational basis for developing reproducible and disease-specific EV therapies for neurological and neurodegenerative disorders.

Article.Title: IL-18 and NFE2L2/NRF2 in Adult ADHD: An Inflammation–Redox Framework for Salivary Biomarker Research
Article.Authors: Hurjui I.; Serban I.; Hurjui L.; Jipu R.; Hurjui I.; Tanase D.; Tarniceriu C.; Balcos C.; Dobrin I.; Dobrin R.
Article.Abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental disorder, and increasing evidence suggests that inflammatory and oxidative processes may contribute to its biological complexity. Despite these observations, no molecular biomarker has yet been established for clinical diagnosis. In this narrative review, we examine interleukin-18 (IL-18) and the NFE2L2/NRF2 antioxidant pathway as two potentially complementary components of the inflammation–redox landscape in adult ADHD, with particular attention to their possible assessment in saliva. For this purpose, we conducted a focused search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science, bringing together evidence from human ADHD studies, mechanistic and experimental research, and studies investigating the feasibility of salivary biomarkers. IL-18 is closely associated with inflammasome-mediated inflammatory signaling, whereas NFE2L2 encodes NRF2, a major regulator of antioxidant and cytoprotective responses. The evidence for these two targets in adult ADHD is not equally developed. Direct human data on IL-18 remain limited, while more recent studies have identified alterations in NRF2-related antioxidant defenses in adults with ADHD. Both IL-18 and NRF2 can be measured in human saliva, although the available evidence comes from clinical populations other than ADHD. Their detection in saliva therefore demonstrates analytical feasibility but does not establish their validity as ADHD biomarkers. At present, neither marker has been validated in the saliva of adults with ADHD. Studying them together may nevertheless provide a useful way to explore the relationship between inflammatory activity and antioxidant regulation. Future studies will require standardized saliva collection, careful assessment of oral health, and characterization of systemic inflammatory and metabolic conditions, medication use, and smoking. Initial studies should also include paired saliva and blood samples to determine how salivary measurements relate to circulating levels and whether they capture biologically meaningful variation in adult ADHD.

Article.Title: Chemical Mechanisms of Cerebral Ischemia–Reperfusion Injury and Neuroprotection in the Thrombectomy Era
Article.Authors: Panos L.; Chakif D.
Article.Abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy has significantly improved outcomes for patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke. However, restoring the artery does not always re-establish full microvascular blood flow, tissue rescue, or a good neurological outcome. Ischemia–reperfusion injury varies over time, with distinct biochemical mechanisms dominating during ischemia, early reperfusion, and the subsequent hours. During ischemia, factors like adenosine triphosphate (ATP) depletion, ionic imbalance, calcium overload, mitochondrial dysfunction, acidosis, and metabolic changes such as succinate build-up render brain tissue highly vulnerable. When blood flow resumes, oxygen delivery to this stressed tissue can induce rapid mitochondrial redox shifts, electron leakage, reactive oxygen and nitrogen species formation, iron-dependent radical generation, and lipid peroxidation. Damage may then persist for hours through ongoing mitochondrial dysfunction, phospholipid hydroperoxide accumulation, reactive aldehydes, ferroptosis, blood–brain barrier breakdown, microvascular issues, and inflammation. Much of the mechanistic evidence supporting these processes derives from experimental studies, and their relevance to clinical outcomes after thrombectomy requires further validation. This narrative review tracks these chemical changes across the main phases of cerebral ischemia–reperfusion injury and connects them to modern thrombectomy practices. It also explores how the timing of each process may inform neuroprotective strategies, drug delivery methods, patient selection via imaging, and future clinical trial approaches.

Article.Title: Oral 25-Hydroxycholesterol Suppresses 4T1 Tumour Growth in an Immune-Context-Associated Manner
Article.Authors: Liang S.; Xu J.; Wang Z.; Liu Y.; Xu Y.; Yao C.; Zhu Z.
Article.Abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive subtype with limited targeted-treatment options. 25-Hydroxycholesterol (25-HC) is an oxysterol involved in metabolic and immune regulation, but its antitumour effects remain context dependent. We examined whether oral 25-HC suppresses 4T1 tumour growth in immunocompetent BALB/c mice and whether host immune status modifies the response. Mice bearing 4T1 tumours received oral vehicle or 25-HC (1 or 10 mg/kg) daily for 14 days (n = 6 per group). 25-HC reduced endpoint tumour volume from 1510.6 ± 235.4 mm3 (vehicle) to 1147.2 ± 243.1 and 866.7 ± 206.6 mm3 (adjusted p = 0.027 and 0.0004); the 10 mg/kg dose also reduced tumour weight and Ki-67 positivity, increased CD8-positive T-cell infiltration and the granzyme B (GZMB)-positive fraction, reduced M2-like macrophages and raised the M1/M2 ratio. Tumour-tissue adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signalling was altered, with p-AMPK/AMPK increased to 1.23- and 1.57-fold of control and p-STAT6/STAT6 decreased to 0.81- and 0.46-fold. Serum 25-HC increased with dose, while intratumoral 25-HC was lowest at 10 mg/kg; no dose-associated reduction was observed in BALB/c nude mice. Oral 25-HC thus suppressed 4T1 tumour growth with immune-context-associated features; however, the treatment-by-host interaction did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.06), and immune-context association of the response remains suggestive rather than established. The reciprocal serum–tumour pattern, a descriptive observation from a single time point whose cause remains unclear, generates a testable hypothesis of immune-cell-associated 25-HC handling.

Article.Title: Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analysis Identifies a Translation/RBP-Related Fibroblast Signature for Drug Repurposing in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
Article.Authors: Qiao Y.; Cui C.; Han Y.; Tang X.; Yang Z.; Ge C.
Article.Abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is characterized by persistent fibroblast activation and excessive extracellular matrix deposition. However, transcriptional heterogeneity associated with translation- and RNA-binding protein (RBP)-related processes within IPF fibroblasts remains incompletely characterized. Here, we analyzed two independent human IPF single-cell RNA-sequencing cohorts to identify fibroblast states that differed in Translation/RBP-related transcriptional programs while sharing high fibrotic output. Donor-paired pseudobulk analysis in GSE136831 identified a transcriptional signature distinguishing these states, and genes showing consistent directional changes in the independent GSE135893 cohort were retained to derive a cross-cohort signature. Reverse-connectivity analysis across CLUE, L1000CDS2, and iLINCS was then used to prioritize compounds predicted to transcriptionally oppose this signature. Candidate compounds were subsequently evaluated in transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)-stimulated human fetal lung fibroblasts (HFL-1), with cell viability, α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), and collagen I used for initial phenotypic assessment. PP-1, PK-11195, dabrafenib, GSK-1059615, and dasatinib reduced both profibrotic markers within the tested concentration ranges, identifying them as candidates for further investigation. Together, these findings define a cross-cohort Translation/RBP-related fibroblast signature in IPF and support its use as a transcriptome-guided strategy for prioritizing compounds with antifibrotic phenotypic activity.

Article.Title: Biosilica from Agricultural Residues for Hazardous Contaminant Removal and Soil Remediation: Synthesis Routes, Structure–Property Relationships, and Environmental Relevance
Article.Authors: Latini V.; Wawrzyńczak A.; Feliczak-Guzik A.
Article.Abstract: The conversion of agricultural residues into functional silica materials offers opportunities to combine waste valorization with environmental remediation. This review critically examines biosilica production from rice husk and straw, corn, sugarcane, wheat, and selected fruit and potato wastes, focusing on sol–gel processing, hydrothermal synthesis, and acid leaching. To address feedstock heterogeneity, reported silicon and silica contents are distinguished according to their analytical basis, including biomass and ash fractions. Synthesis routes are compared using available quantitative indicators, including silica yield, purity, specific surface area, and processing conditions, while accounting for differences in reporting practices and incomplete datasets. Particular attention is given to the relationships between precursor composition, synthesis parameters, surface chemistry, and contaminant-removal performance. The analysis highlights the importance of accessible surface sites, functional groups, and contaminant speciation, demonstrating that specific surface area alone cannot predict adsorption efficiency. Although biosilica shows potential for water treatment and soil remediation, practical implementation remains constrained by feedstock variability, limited testing under realistic conditions, regeneration challenges, and uncertainties regarding long-term safety. The review identifies key research priorities for developing reproducible, economically viable, and environmentally sustainable biosilica technologies.

Article.Title: Alterations in the Expression of Tight and Adherens Junction Proteins in the Hen Oviduct Following Tamoxifen Treatment
Article.Authors: Frydrych K.; Wolak D.; Hrabia A.
Article.Abstract: Intercellular junctions are essential for maintaining epithelial integrity, barrier function, and tissue remodeling in the female reproductive system. However, their role in the avian oviduct is poorly understood. The aim of this study was to examine the effect of tamoxifen (TMX; an estrogen receptor blocker in birds) treatment on the histoarchitecture and the abundance of transcripts and proteins, as well as the immunolocalization of key tight junction proteins (occludin, claudin 1, and ZO1) and adherens junction proteins (E-cadherin and β-catenin) in the oviduct of hens. Tissue samples were collected from all oviductal segments (i.e., the infundibulum, magnum, isthmus, shell gland, and vagina) on day 8 of the experiment, from control (laying; n = 6) hens and hens treated (6 mg/kg body weight) daily with TMX (non-laying; n = 6). Following TMX treatment for 7 consecutive days, a pause in laying and partial oviductal regression was accompanied by segment-dependent alterations in mRNA transcript abundances (examined by qRT-PCR) and/or protein abundances (determined by Western blot) of the examined junctional molecules. Furthermore, TMX treatment altered the patterns of immunofluorescent staining within the oviductal wall, concomitant with the disorganization of the luminal epithelium and tubular glands. Our results suggest that the expression and localization of tight and adherens junction proteins in the hen oviduct depend strongly on estrogen signaling. Moreover, this study provides novel insights into the regulation of these proteins, indicating their potential involvement in the molecular mechanisms that orchestrate epithelial remodeling and functioning in the hen oviduct, which may affect poultry production.

Article.Title: Vitamin K3 (Menadione) Targets TBK1 to Enhance the Efficacy of Pirfenidone in a Mouse Model of Bleomycin-Induced Pulmonary Fibrosis
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Cao J.; Zhou Y.; Cao X.; Deng S.; Li Y.; Li C.; Tang S.; Chen P.
Article.Abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive and irreversible interstitial lung disease. Current antifibrotic drugs, exemplified by pirfenidone (PFD), only slow disease progression with limited efficacy and adverse effects, underscoring the need for novel therapeutic strategies. By integrating single-cell transcriptomics with the Drug2Cell algorithm, we performed drug prioritization at single-cell resolution and identified menadione (vitamin K3, VK3), a synthetic naphthoquinone and the minimal core of naturally occurring vitamin K, as a candidate preferentially active in alveolar epithelial cells. In bleomycin (BLM)-stimulated A549 cells and a mouse model of pulmonary fibrosis, therapeutic co-administration of low-dose VK3 and PFD reduced vimentin expression by 44.8% and collagen deposition by 50.3%, and decreased fibroblast abundance by 36.7%, thereby attenuating histopathological damage and restoring BLM-disrupted alveolar epithelial homeostasis. Experiments with VK3 alone further demonstrated that its antifibrotic activity is independent of conversion to vitamin K2. Mechanistically, thermal proteome profiling identified TANK-binding kinase 1 (TBK1) as the principal candidate target; molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations predicted a stable binding mode, independently confirmed by biolayer interferometry and differential scanning fluorimetry, demonstrating direct binding of VK3 to TBK1 with nanomolar affinity. TBK1 knockdown suppressed BLM-induced fibrotic responses, establishing TBK1 as a positive regulator of pulmonary fibrosis. In vitro signaling analysis revealed that VK3 plus PFD inhibits phosphorylation of TBK1 and STAT3, whereas PFD alone reduces phosphorylation of JAK1 and STAT3, suggesting that both agents converge on STAT3 through distinct upstream nodes. Although VK3 exhibits dose-dependent cytotoxicity precluding direct clinical use as monotherapy, its validated high-affinity target TBK1 and privileged naphthoquinone scaffold lay a rational foundation for lead optimization toward safer anti-IPF agents, and its ability to enhance PFD efficacy supports further development as an adjunct to existing antifibrotic therapy.

Article.Authors: Lewandowska K.; Pachura-Hanusek N.; Kuropka P.; Szumny A.; Kupczyński R.
Article.Abstract: Maternal dietary lipids may influence fatty acid availability across the maternal–placental–offspring axis. This study evaluated the effects of prepartum supplementation with flaxseed oil (FO), black soldier fly larvae (BSFL; Hermetia illucens) oil, or their 2:1 blend (Mix) in 32 pregnant Olkuska ewes. In lamb serum collected after colostrum intake, postnatal age was strongly associated with fatty acid composition, whereas nominal treatment-related differences did not withstand FDR adjustment. Placental architecture remained preserved across treatments, without inflammatory, degenerative, or vascular lesions. Lamb growth performance did not differ significantly among treatments. Overall, maternal lipid supplementation was associated with compartment-specific differences in relative fatty acid composition. Because placental fatty acid transport was not directly assessed, these findings do not demonstrate direct maternal-to-offspring fatty acid transfer.

Article.Title: An Explainable MRI-Conditioned Generative Framework for Gene-Feature Representations in Alzheimer’s Disease
Article.Authors: Huang X.; Shihab M.; Bhagchandani R.; Dong Y.; Wang Y.

IG-CVAE comprises a genetic branch encoding expression into 128-dimensional gene-feature vectors (GFV128), an imaging branch encoding MRI into 128-dimensional MRI-feature vectors (MFV128), and a conditional variational autoencoder that generates GFV128 from MFV128. Paired analyses included 289 ADNI and 98 ANM participants. Test area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) values in ADNI/ANM were 0.646/0.851 for the genetic branch, 0.942/0.752 for the imaging branch, and 0.939/0.869 for generated GFV128. Generated-observed GFV128 agreement was moderate (cosine similarity, 0.590/0.589; coefficient of determination (R2), 0.161/0.211). Molecular importance was cohort-specific at the gene level, with no significant pathway-level convergence, whereas MRI perturbation showed cross-cohort convergence in cerebral white matter linked to distinct disease-informative molecular features. Overall, structural MRI retained disease-relevant information sufficient to generate disease-informative molecular representations, supporting IG-CVAE as a participant-paired hypothesis-generating imaging–transcriptomic framework while providing only limited evidence of participant-specific molecular correspondence without implying raw transcriptome reconstruction. The ANM test estimates should be interpreted cautiously given the small paired independent test set (n = 20).

Article.Title: Beyond the Black Box: Physics-Based and Conservation-Informed Evidence for ACVRL1 Variant Classification in Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia and Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension
Article.Authors: Brusgaard K.
Article.Abstract: Missense variants in ACVRL1 (ALK1) cause hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia type 2 (HHT2), heritable pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), or both in the same patient, and many remain variants of uncertain significance. AlphaMissense classifies them accurately but does not show which evidence drives a call. I annotated 899 ACVRL1 missense variants with protein-stability estimates (FoldX, DynaMut2), a GREMLIN-style conservation score, and structural context. I then trained random-forest classifiers on 311 variants with labels traceable to ClinVar or a publication (296 pathogenic-like, 15 benign-like). A structural/conservation-only classifier (Model 1b) reached a cross-validated ROC-AUC of 0.954 (95% CI 0.916–0.984), and a model adding sequence-based predictors (Model 1) reached 0.979, versus 0.983 for AlphaMissense on the same variants. On variants first reported in 2025–2026, Model 1b scored 0.976, Model 1 0.992, and AlphaMissense 0.992; equivalence within ±0.05 AUC was supported for Model 1 only. Benign variants were the main weakness: Model 1b correctly classified 10/15, against 14/15 for AlphaMissense. Conservation drove most calls, with predicted destabilization contributing to a minority. An interpretable, gene-specific classifier can approach AlphaMissense for ACVRL1 while showing the structural or evolutionary evidence behind each call. Its calls are hypotheses, not functional evidence, and can prioritize VUS for functional testing.

Article.Title: The FGF23–Undercarboxylated Osteocalcin Axis in Predialysis Chronic Kidney Disease: Linking Mineral Homeostasis and Bone Turnover

In the multivariable regression models, Glu-OC was inversely associated with FGF23 (standardized β = −0.258, p = 0.024), whereas alkaline phosphatase was positively associated with FGF23 (β = 0.369, p = 0.001). In the model with Glu-OC as the dependent variable, FGF23 (β = −0.266, p = 0.020) and serum calcium (β = −0.366, p = 0.002) were inversely associated with Glu-OC. Significant inverse correlations between FGF23 and Glu-OC were observed in CKD stages G1–G3, but not in stage G4 or the control group. These findings support an association between FGF23 and Glu-OC in non-dialysis CKD and provide a rationale for further investigation of a potential FGF23–Glu-OC axis in CKD-associated mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD). Article.Title: Wide-Field Fundus Autofluorescence Patterns in a Polish Cohort of Genotyped Patients with Phenotype of Retinitis Pigmentosa, Usher Syndrome and Cone–Rod Dystrophy
Article.Authors: Pietras-Baczewska A.; Gajda-Deryło B.; Ognik K.; Rejdak R.; Nowomiejska K.
Article.Abstract: To investigate different wide-field fundus autofluorescence (FAF) patterns in a large cohort of Polish patients with inherited retinal dystrophies (IRDs) of different genotypes sorted into groups of at least 5 patients. A total of 103 patients with IRDs and phenotype of retinitis pigmentosa, Usher syndrome and cone–rod dystrophy were included and divided into groups of at least 5 patients based on the outcome of genetic analysis. Ultra-wide field FAF imaging was reviewed to determine patterns of FAF. Ten groups of the same genotype and three patterns of FAF have been distinguished. In the most prevalent USH2A group (26 cases), macular hyperautofluorescence (AF) ring combined with mottled hypo-AF in the periphery was present in 19 cases, the hyper-AF ring alone (including one double ring) was present in 5 cases, while the peripapillary sparing appeared in 2 cases. In the ABCA4 group (22 cases), mottled hypo-AF pattern in the posterior pole and mid-periphery was most prevalent (13 cases), additional peripapillary sparing was present in 4 cases, central hyper-AF ring was present in 3 cases, and characteristic flecks were present in 2 cases. In the RPGR group (15 patients), the most prevalent pattern was a combination of hyper-AF ring and mottled hypo-AF in the periphery (13 cases), while in 2 cases only hypo-AF mottling was present. In PROM1 gene variants (7 patients), mottled hypo-AF in the posterior pole was again the most dominant pattern (6 patients), and there was one case of combined hyper-AF ring and hypo-AF in the periphery. All NR2E3 (5 patients), RP1 (5 patients), RHO (7 patients), CDHR1 (5 patients), PRPF31 (5 patients) and EYS (6 patients) gene pathogenic variants also manifested with hyper-AF ring in the center and patchy hypo-AF spots in the periphery. Only one of the NR2E3 patients demonstrated a double ring. The most prevalent pattern across all groups, excluding ABCA4 and PROM1 groups, is central hyper-AF ring together with patchy hypo-AF in the periphery (72 cases—70%). ABCA4 and PROM1-related RP groups revealed mostly hypo-AF mottled patterns in the posterior pole and periphery, without hyper-AF ring. FAF patterns are very heterogenous, but there are some distinctive features in different genotypes of IRDs.

Article.Title: Protopanaxatriol Inhibits Listeria monocytogenes Infection Through a Multi-Target Virulence Suppression Strategy
Article.Authors: Liu J.; Lu J.; Liu L.; Liu R.; Lan B.; Qi Y.; Yang D.; Li H.; Wang G.
Article.Abstract: Listeria monocytogenes (LM) infection relies on the synergistic effects of multiple virulence factors, including but not limited to flagella-mediated bacterial motility, listeriolysin O (LLO)-mediated immune evasion and inflammatory response, multiple virulence proteins anchored to the cell wall by SortaseA (SrtA), and internalin-mediated adhesion and invasion. These virulence factors are critical potential targets for developing anti-LM infection inhibitors. This study found that protopanaxatriol (ptt) significantly inhibited the adhesion and invasion of LM into epithelial cells potentially by interfering with internalin A/InlB (InlA/InlB)-mediated host–cell interactions and reducing the transcription of inlA and inlB. InlA was anchored to the cell wall by SrtA, and in silico analysis predicted that ptt may interact with key active residues of SrtA. Additionally, ptt was predicted to interact with LLO and inhibited its oligomer formation, resulting in a loss of its pore-forming activity. Flagella, SrtA, and LLO all affect bacterial biofilm formation; ptt inhibited the formation of biofilms and disrupted mature biofilm without affecting the growth of LM. Finally, ptt protected Galleria mellonella from LLO and LM by increasing survival and alleviating tissue damage. These results indicate that ptt shows excellent potential for the prevention and control of LM infection.
