Article.Title: Regimen-Dependent Anti-Cytokine and Immune-Checkpoint Autoantibodies Are Associated with Immunotherapy Toxicity and Response in Melanoma
Article.Authors: Reschke R.; Zucht H.; Budde P.; Mangana J.; Dummer R.; Pföhler C.; Wistuba-Hamprecht K.; Weide B.; Meier F.; Hakim-Meibodi L.; Schulz C.; Richter J.; Enk A.; Bräutigam M.; Nguyen T.; Hassel J.
Article.Abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) efficacy and immune-related adverse events (irAEs) in melanoma are influenced by the pre-treatment immune state. We investigated whether baseline autoantibodies directed against cytokines, chemokines, cytokine receptors, and immune-checkpoint/costimulatory proteins were associated with outcome in a regimen-dependent manner. Baseline sera from patients with metastatic melanoma were profiled on a multiplex bead array of 86 cytokine, chemokine, cytokine-receptor and immune-checkpoint antigens, and associations with best overall response and irAE development were assessed within pre-specified treatment strata by label-permutation testing with Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate control (SAM as a sensitivity analysis). Associations differed by ICI regimen. Anti-IL17A and anti-CCL2 reactivity was higher in patients developing irAEs under ipilimumab monotherapy (both p = 0.003) and shifted in the opposite direction under pembrolizumab without prior CTLA-4 therapy. Higher anti-PD-L1/CD274 and anti-CCL5 and lower anti-KIT reactivity were associated with response to pembrolizumab without prior CTLA-4 therapy (p = 0.025, p = 0.002, p = 0.006), and lower anti-MCAM and anti-CSF3 reactivity with response under ipilimumab/nivolumab (p = 0.001 and p = 0.002). No association survived false-discovery-rate correction, so all findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating; higher baseline anti-IL10 reactivity was a leading irAE signal under pembrolizumab without prior CTLA-4 therapy (p = 0.027). These regimen-dependent humoral markers warrant prospective, regimen-stratified validation.

Article.Title: Transposable Element Dysregulation in Fetal Down Syndrome Mesenchymal Stem Cells: Insights from a Model of Premature Ageing
Article.Authors: Vaiasicca S.; Cianfruglia L.; Campagna R.; Cecati M.; Cardelli M.; Casoli T.; Olivieri F.; Fumarola S.
Article.Abstract: Down syndrome (DS) is associated with accelerated biological aging, but the molecular alterations linking trisomy 21 (T21) to early aging-related phenotypes remain incompletely understood. Transposable elements (TEs), particularly LINE-1 (L1) retrotransposons, are sensitive indicators of epigenetic and chromatin instability; however, their dysregulation during fetal development in DS remains largely unexplored. In this study, we performed a bioinformatic analysis of available RNA-sequencing data from chorionic villus-derived fetal mesenchymal stem cells (CV-MSCs) affected by T21 and compared them with data from euploid CV-MSCs. TE expression was quantified using TEtranscripts and analyzed across major TE classes, subfamilies, chromosomes, and evolutionary L1 groups, alongside curated gene-set analyses. At the class level, TE expression showed modest and heterogeneous differences between DS and CTRL samples. Among LINE-1 elements, ancient families, particularly HAL1 and L1M, showed a tendency toward higher expression, whereas L1PA2 and L1HS showed no evidence of increased expression. Pathway analysis revealed downregulation of pathways involved in heterochromatin maintenance and L1 repression, alongside alterations in DNA methylation, the DNA damage response, inflammatory/SASP pathways, nuclear architecture, and mesenchymal commitment. These findings highlight alterations in TE regulation and chromatin-related pathways in fetal DS cells, suggesting that molecular features potentially relevant to accelerated aging may be detectable early during development.

Article.Title: Metal-Based Anticancer Drugs: Integrating Pharmaceutical Perspectives with DFT-Based Quantum Chemical Topology (QTAIM and ELF)
Article.Authors: Al-Sahlawi F.; Al-Samydai A.; Hassan A.; Mayyas A.; Al-Remawi M.; Shakir H.; Mozafari M.; Maki M.
Article.Abstract: Anticancer metal drugs are presented with mechanistically different opportunities in therapeutic use that are not limited by conventional organic chemotherapeutics. Molecular structure not only regulates their clinical behaviour but also their electronic structure, coordination dynamics and metal speciation in complex biological conditions. Rational design of such agents is, nevertheless, a challenging task, even with the long-term interest given, because standard structure–activity relationships are not that effective at revealing such attributes. This review critically studies metal-based anticancer therapeutics in an integrated framework, with a combination of pharmaceutical sciences, density functional theory (DFT), and quantum chemical topology. Following the analysis of significant classes of platinum and non-platinum metal complexes in a structure–reactivity–limitation perspective, the main aspects of pharmacology, such as pharmacokinetics, cellular absorption, resistance, and toxicity, are discussed. The importance of DFT in the explanation of electronic structure is evaluated in addition to the conceptualisations and uses of the Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules and the Electron Localisation Function. The focus is on topology-supported relationships between structures and activities that can be integrated into pharmacological results according to electronic and topological measures. Through applications of computational and pharmaceutical knowledge, this review suggests a mechanistically based, multidisciplinary approach to the rational design of next-generation metal-based anticancer drugs.

Article.Title: Comparative Acetylation and Ubiquitination Profiling in Cervical Cancer-Cell Models Supports a Proposed Lysine-Fate Code
Article.Authors: Bastida R.; Reyes M.; Marko-Varga G.; Gil J.; Encarnación-Guevara S.
Article.Abstract: Post-translational modifications are rarely studied as an integrated system. Most studies have focused on acetylation or ubiquitination in isolation, despite both frequently targeting the same lysine residues on the same proteins. This study investigated whether the interplay between these modifications, rather than their individual effects, constitutes a meaningful regulatory layer in cervical cancer cells. Quantitative stoichiometric proteomics was applied to HPV-positive and HPV-negative cell models, with a non-cancerous keratinocyte cell line serving as the control. The results demonstrate that acetylation and ubiquitination form coordinated, context-dependent patterns rather than acting independently. In HPV-positive cells acetylation predominated and was enriched in transcriptional regulators. Conversely, the HPV-negative C33A line exhibited a substantially larger ubiquitinome, indicative of increased proteostatic surveillance. Site-specific stoichiometry analysis revealed that the relative occupancy of each modification at shared lysine residues determines regulatory outcomes, rather than their mere presence. This competition is proposed to constitute a “lysine-fate code” that integrates transcriptional regulation, metabolic adaptation, and immune signaling into a unified proteostatic logic. Beyond their implications for cervical cancer biology, these findings suggest that the acetylation–ubiquitination balance may represent a key regulatory principle. Targeting enzymes that modulate this balance could provide novel therapeutic strategies that surpass single-pathway inhibition.

Article.Title: Fractionation of Bioactive Polysaccharides from Volvariella volvacea and Their Ameliorative Effects on Hepatic Lipid Accumulation
Article.Authors: Xia W.; Zhao R.; Li S.
Article.Abstract: Volvariella volvacea is a widely consumed edible mushroom, yet the lipid-lowering potential of its polysaccharides remains poorly understood. In this study, two polysaccharide-enriched fractions, VVP-1 and VVP-2, were isolated from V. volvacea fruiting bodies, with weight-average molecular weights of 13,789 and 17,829 Da, respectively. Their lipid-lowering effects were evaluated in palmitic acid (PA)-challenged AML12 mouse hepatocytes and in high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obese male C57BL/6J mice. Both fractions reduced PA-induced intracellular triglyceride (TG) levels in a dose-dependent manner, with VVP-2 showing a trend of greater efficacy. At the molecular level, VVP-2 exposure was associated with downregulation of the lipogenic genes Acaca and Srebf1, upregulation of the fatty acid oxidation-related genes Cpt1a and Ppara, decreased secretion of TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β, preservation of mitochondrial signal, restoration of mitochondrial membrane potential, and enhanced ATP production. In HFD-fed mice, VVP-2 (100 mg/kg) attenuated body-weight gain by 38.9%, reduced liver weight by 28.9% and epididymal, inguinal, and perirenal fat weights by 50.3%, 47.5%, and 28.8%, respectively, improved the serum lipid profile (TG reduced by 39.1%, TC by 33.5%, NEFA by 56.2%, and LDL-C by 56.8%), and alleviated hepatic lipid accumulation and liver injury. These findings suggest that VVP-2 may improve mitochondrial function and modulate lipid metabolism-related gene expression, potentially reducing lipid accumulation and inflammation in hepatocytes. These results support the potential of VVP-2 as a lipid-lowering functional food ingredient for the prevention of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.

Article.Title: Adenomyosis and Its Impact on Reproduction, Pregnancy, Childbirth, and the Newborn
Article.Authors: Signorile P.
Article.Abstract: This narrative review covers the diagnosis of adenomyosis; its impact on fertility, assisted reproduction, pregnancy, childbirth, and the newborn; and its uterus-sparing management. Diagnosis is delayed by about 11 years, and no classification is universally accepted. After in vitro fertilization, adenomyosis lowers clinical pregnancy and live birth rates and doubles miscarriage risk. Because oocyte number and morphology are preserved and miscarriage remains increased with donor oocytes and euploid embryos, the deficit appears mainly uterine; however, age and coexistent endometriosis contribute. In pregnancy, it is associated with preeclampsia, preterm birth, placental malposition and placenta accreta spectrum, cesarean delivery, and postpartum hemorrhage, and newborns are more often small for gestational age, of low birth weight, and extremely preterm. The evidence is observational and of low to very low certainty, and defective remodeling of the junctional zone spiral arteries remains a hypothetical unifying mechanism. In selected observational cohorts, pregnancy was reported in approximately half of infertile women after uterus-sparing surgery, which has not been compared with medical treatment or assisted reproduction in randomized trials and carries a risk of uterine rupture. Management rests on individualized counseling; proposed preventive measures, including low-dose aspirin and correction of vitamin D or folate deficiency, remain untested in adenomyosis.

Article.Title: The p53 Super-Hub Architecture: From Planar to Volumetric Network Pharmacology
Article.Authors: Bazanov D.
Article.Abstract: The p53 protein is a central tumor suppressor; however, its status as an intracellular super-hub renders direct pharmacological reactivation via the traditional “lock-and-key” paradigm highly challenging due to systemic toxicity and the evolutionary plasticity of tumor networks. To address this translational barrier, we apply a systems engineering approach, deconstructing the p53 signaling architecture into seven hierarchical levels. By mapping current therapeutic strategies onto this framework, we illustrate that no ideal single-target strategy currently exists. While existing alternative approaches—such as activating redundant homologs, allosteric regulation, or exploiting synthetic lethality (e.g., WEE1 inhibition)—provide valuable bypass tactics, they frequently remain insufficient in isolation. Instead, we propose that a genuine therapeutic solution requires a comprehensive, multi-level intervention strategy that simultaneously modulates several layers of the network. We hypothesize that this concept of distributed signal load is biologically supported by natural evolutionary models: increased TP53 copy numbers in elephants and multi-tiered contact inhibition in naked mole-rats suggest the efficacy of peripheral network offloading. Ultimately, we advocate a conceptual shift from planar mono-targeting toward adaptive network management, aiming to identify tissue-specific local optima for coordinated multi-node interventions.

Article.Title: Through the Long COVID Looking-Glass: An Unremitting Conundrum of Mitochondria?
Article.Authors: Kononova S.; Bobkova N.; Leonov S.; Sukhikh G.
Article.Abstract: Plentiful data indicate a high post-COVID risk of developing pathologies that are long-term and result from disruption of multiple cellular processes. The significance of this data becomes increasingly clear as it links the pandemic’s effects to enduring health problems which could affect millions. These conditions are usually caused by different problems with mitochondria. These problems can include less efficient energy production and increased removal of damaged cells, showing how complex cell health is. Having other health problems such as high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, brain diseases, and cancer related to renin–angiotensin–aldosterone system (RAAS) imbalance worsened COVID-19 and its lasting effects. This highlights the importance of focused treatments for these at-risk groups. This review seeks to evaluate the information on this issue, carefully studying the features and symptoms often associated with mitochondrial disorders. What happens next in the pandemic is still to be seen, but we know there is much to learn. It is important to lessen the effects of the pandemic on people with comorbidities as much as possible.

Article.Title: Fine-Tuning the Processes of Steroid Hormone Biosynthesis: SULT2A1/1E1 and CYP21A2 Interaction
Article.Authors: Yablokov E.; Tumilovich A.; Gnedenko O.; Mednaia D.; Mezentsev Y.; Ershov P.; Konstantinov M.; Kaluzhskiy L.; Tsybruk T.; Grabovec I.; Shabunya P.; Gilep A.; Ivanov A.
Article.Abstract: The high physiological activity of steroid hormones requires multilevel regulation of their biosynthesis. Cytosolic sulfotransferases, specifically SULT2A1 and SULT1E1, convert steroid precursors into mobile sulfated depot forms, diverting them from key steroidogenic cytochromes P450. Given the previously demonstrated CYP17A1–SULT interactions, this study aims to verify the hypothesis that CYP21A2 can interact with SULTs and thereby potentially contribute to the regulation of steroid metabolism. Using surface plasmon resonance (SPR) biosensing, in vitro enzymatic activity assays, and in silico molecular modeling, we investigated the interplay between CYP21A2 and SULT2A1/1E1. SPR analysis revealed high-affinity binding between purified recombinant CYP21A2 and SULT2A1/SULT1E1 in vitro in the nanomolar range (9.5 × 10−9 M for SULT2A1 and 1.15 × 10−8 M for SULT1E1). Thermodynamic assessments indicated that the CYP21A2–SULT1E1 complex is entropy-driven, contrasting with the enthalpy-driven CYP17A1–SULT1E1 interaction. Enzymatic assays demonstrated reciprocal modulatory effects: CYP21A2 exerted a stimulatory effect on pregnenolone sulfation by SULTs, whereas SULT2A1 moderately inhibited CYP21A2 activity. Molecular modeling of binary complexes predicted structural interfaces and continuous intraprotein channels connecting the enzymes’ active sites. These findings suggest that CYP–SULT interactions may contribute to the fine-tuning of steroid hormone biosynthesis. These findings raise the possibility that CYP–SULT interactions may form part of a broader regulatory network, acting as metabolic switches that dictate the balance between downstream corticosteroid pathways and structural sequestration into sulfated pools.

Article.Title: Long-Term Propranolol Treatment Induces Anxiolytic-like Effects and Alters Hypothalamic Noradrenergic, Serotonergic and GABAergic Neurotransmission
Article.Authors: Witczyńska A.; Fijałkowski Ł.; Blecharz-Klin K.; Ziętal K.; Pyrzanowska J.; Piechal A.; Joniec-Maciejak I.; Machaj E.; Jastrzębska A.; Nowaczyk J.; Mirowska-Guzel D.; Nowaczyk A.
Article.Abstract: Propranolol is a non-selective β-adrenergic receptor antagonist widely used in cardiovascular medicine and anxiety-related conditions; however, its central neurochemical mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the effects of long-term propranolol administration on anxiety-like behavior and hypothalamic neurotransmission in rats. Adult male Sprague–Dawley rats received propranolol in drinking water at doses of 1, 2.5, or 5 mg/kg b.w./day for 33 days. Behavioral effects were assessed using the Open Field Test (OF) and Elevated Plus Maze (EPM). Hypothalamic concentrations of amino acids, e.g., γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) as well as monoamines, and their metabolites were determined by high-performance liquid chromatography with electrochemical detection (HPLC-ED). Long-term propranolol treatment induced a significant anxiolytic-like effect, reflected by increased exploration of open arms in the EPM, without affecting locomotor activity in the OF. Neurochemical analyses revealed a significant increase in hypothalamic GABA levels and a marked reduction in noradrenergic turnover, as indicated by decreased MHPG/NA ratios. Propranolol also increased hypothalamic serotonin concentrations, whereas dopaminergic turnover remained unchanged. These findings demonstrate that long-term propranolol administration produces neurochemical changes within the hypothalamus involving noradrenergic, serotonergic, and GABAergic signaling pathways. The results suggest that the anxiolytic-like effects of propranolol extend beyond β-adrenergic receptor blockade and may be mediated by coordinated modulation of multiple neurotransmitter systems involved in stress regulation and emotional processing. The study provides new evidence linking chronic propranolol exposure to selective hypothalamic neurochemical remodeling associated with reduced anxiety-like behavior.

Article.Title: Four Recombinase-Aided Amplification Assays for the Rapid Detection of Fowl Adenovirus Serotype 4
Article.Authors: Feng Q.; Lu S.; Cao Y.; Wu R.; Wang Y.; Xu L.; Wang Q.
Article.Abstract: Fowl adenovirus serotype 4 (FAdV-4) infection leads to serious damage to the poultry industry worldwide. Accurate and prompt diagnosis is essential for effective management of FAdV-4 outbreaks. In this study, we first designed a pair of specific primers based on the ORF19A gene of FAdV-4 strain NP for recombinase-aided amplification (RAA) and optimized the reaction conditions. The results revealed that the optimal conditions for a sensitive RAA reaction were at 39 °C for 40 min. The minimum detection amount of FAdV-4 genomes was 10−2 ng/μL using RAA. In order to facilitate the result presentation of RAA, which was visualized using a lateral flow dipstick (LFD), and the optimal reaction time of RAA-LFD was shortened to 30 min. However, the minimum detectable amount of FAdV-4 genomes was 50 ng/μL, which was lower than the sensitivity of RAA. Furthermore, to enhance the sensitivity of RAA-LFD, we designed LbaCas12a-FAdV-4-crRNA and incorporated it into RAA to develop the RAA-Cas12a-F and RAA-Cas12a-LFD methods, respectively. Based on the RAA reaction of 40 min, RAA-Cas12a-F and RAA-Cas12a-LFD only need an additional 15 min. The minimum detectable amounts of RAA-Cas12a-F and RAA-Cas12a-LFD were 10−6 ng/μL and 10−5 ng/μL, respectively. These results indicate a significant improvement in the sensitivity of two detection methods. A total of 192 fecal samples from chicks were collected from Fujian province. These samples were then detected using these four RAA rapid detection methods. The results showed that 57 positive samples were screened by both RAA-Cas12a-F and RAA-Cas12a-LFD, which was 4 more positive samples than the RAA method and 14 more positive samples than the RAA-LFD method. Overall, we developed four accurate and rapid RAA assays of FAdV-4, which is feasible and of certain value in the application of FAdV-4 in clinical practice.

Article.Title: Postnatal Immune Activation: A Hidden Trigger for Mood Disorders?
Article.Authors: Shen D.; Ji G.; Sun X.; Ma S.; Zhao T.
Article.Abstract: Postnatal immune activation (PIA) is linked to persistent CNS homeostatic imbalance, which may contribute to the emergence of neuropsychiatric disorders such as depression and cognitive impairment. This process involves multiple pathological changes such as abnormal activation of central glial cells, neuroimmune disorders, and abnormal neural development during the embryonic period and the early postnatal period. Currently, the specific molecular mechanism by which PIA leads to the occurrence of emotional disorders is still not fully understood. This review summarizes evidence from animal models linking early postnatal immune challenges with later cognitive, anxiety-like, depression-like, and social outcomes, and systematically elaborates on the regulatory role of PIA in the occurrence and development of emotional disorders, aiming to deeply analyze its potential pathological mechanism and provide a basis for early prevention and targeted intervention in mental diseases such as depression and anxiety.

Article.Title: Acid-Sensing Ion Channel 1 Deficiency Aggravates Cuprizone-Induced Demyelination, Axonal Damage and Microgliosis in Mice
Article.Authors: Öz A.; Wiemuth D.; Gründer S.; Clarner T.; Tillmann N.
Article.Abstract: White matter degeneration in multiple sclerosis (MS) is characterized by oligodendrocyte dysfunction and subsequent demyelination. To determine whether acid-sensing ion channel subtype 1 (ASIC1) contributes to oligodendrocyte-associated pathology under non-autoimmune conditions, the cuprizone model was used in wild-type (WT) and ASIC1-deficient (KO) mice. Axonal degeneration, microgliosis (IBA1), demyelination, and oligodendrocyte abundance were assessed in the medial Corpus Callosum. Cuprizone increased IBA1 positivity, axonal damage, and demyelination, and these effects appeared more pronounced in ASIC1 KO animals than in WT animals. ASIC1 deficiency was associated with increased APP+ axonal spheroid formation and reduced myelination scores. However, oligodendrocyte marker analyses did not indicate an additional reduction in oligodendrocyte survival after 3 weeks. Overall, these data support a role of ASIC1 in preserving myelin integrity, consistent with myelin maintenance rather than direct regulation of oligodendrocyte survival.

Article.Title: Thermoresponsive Gel for Sustained Nanoliposome-Mediated Nose-to-Brain Drug Delivery
Article.Authors: Mihailova L.; Shalabalija D.; Dodov M.; Mishonova M.; Koceva L.; Raikova N.; Mladenov M.; Gagov H.; Tchekalarova J.; Petkova-Kirova P.; Sazdova I.
Article.Abstract: Nose-to-brain drug delivery represents a promising non-invasive strategy for improving CNS targeting. However, conventional liquid formulations are limited by rapid mucociliary clearance and short mucosal residence time. This study developed a thermoresponsive in situ gel incorporating indocyanine green (ICG)-loaded nanoliposomes and evaluated its potential to enhance and modulate the ICG-associated brain distribution after intranasal administration of the formulation. ICG-loaded nanoliposomes were prepared using a modified thin-film hydration method and incorporated into a poloxamer-based gel containing hyaluronic acid and Carbomer 940 as mucoadhesive components. The nanoliposomes exhibited a mean particle size of 124 ± 3.25 nm, a unimodal size distribution, and a high ICG encapsulation efficiency of 93.33%. Rheological analysis confirmed a temperature-triggered sol-to-gel transition at the physiological nasal temperature (~32 °C), shear-thinning behavior, and rapid structural recovery suitable for intranasal application. Ex vivo fluorescence imaging in rats demonstrated distinct biodistribution profiles for the ICG-associated signal delivered via the liquid nanoliposomes and gel-incorporated nanoliposomes. Although the liquid liposomes showed faster early signal at 4 h, the gel formulation produced stronger and more sustained brain fluorescence at later time points. At 8 h and 24 h, whole-brain fluorescence was approximately twofold higher with the gel formulation than with the liquid liposomes formulation. These findings indicate that this thermoresponsive gel enhances nasal retention and may modulate the delivery profile of the nose-to-brain transport, supporting its potential as a platform for CNS-targeted delivery and the development of more effective therapies for neurodegenerative diseases.

Article.Title: Editing the Embryonic Brain: How In Utero Electroporation Reveals the Secrets of Cortical Development
Article.Authors: Anastasiia E.; Alexandr O.; Pavel K.; Assol’ D.; Victor T.; Maria G.
Article.Abstract: The development of the mammalian cerebral cortex follows a tightly regulated dynamic molecular program, the critical stages and key molecular players of which remain to be fully elucidated. Detailed visualization of these processes, along with functional genomic studies, will significantly advance our understanding of neurogenesis and its associated human disorders. Such developmental aberrations often entail irreversible changes that lead to congenital malformations of varying severity. In utero electroporation (IUE) has emerged as a widely utilized in vivo transfection and imaging technique. When coupled with advanced technologies such as genome editing and systems for spatiotemporal and tissue-specific gene expression, IUE offers unprecedented opportunities to dissect the molecular mechanisms underlying embryonic cortical development both under normal conditions and in various pathological processes. This review highlights the technical utility of IUE and provides examples of experimental designs used to investigate stages of neurogenesis. Particular attention has been paid to studying the cell cycle using thymidine analogues, the differentiation of neuronal progenitor cells, and axonal guidance.

Article.Title: ER Stress Induces Endothelial Dysfunction Linked to Mitochondrial Redox Imbalance and Enhanced Mitochondrial Bioenergetics in Penile Erectile Tissue
Article.Authors: Gómez del Val A.; Contreras C.; Olmos L.; Muñoz M.; Freire-Agulleiro Ó.; Mohamed M.; Benedito S.; Rivera L.; López M.; Sánchez A.; Prieto D.
Article.Abstract: Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress has been proposed as a link between insulin resistance, oxidative stress, and endothelial dysfunction in metabolic disorders. Penile erectile dysfunction shares risk factors with cardiovascular disease (CVD) including insulin resistance, diabetes, and obesity. In the present study, involvement of ER stress in penile endothelial and vascular dysfunction was investigated in an in vivo model of ER stress induced by tunicamycin. Endothelial function was assessed by using wire myography, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) by mitoSOX and Amplex Red fluorometry, mitochondrial bioenergetics by Seahorse XF Analyzer, and expression of ER-stress markers by Western blot. Tunicamycin increased expression of BiP, pPERK, ATF6α, and pIRE1α in penile erectile tissue. Endothelium-dependent relaxations to acetylcholine were impaired, while α1-adrenergic vasoconstriction was blunted in penile arteries from ER-stress rats. Selective NADPH oxidase 1 (Nox1) inhibition restored endothelial relaxations, while blockade of Nox2 and Nox4 revealed H2O2-mediated endothelial relaxations in control but not in tunicamycin-treated rats. ER stress reduced basal mtROS levels and mitoTEMPO- sensitive relaxant responses. On the other hand, enhanced mitochondrial respiration and glycolytic activity were found in penile arteries from tunicamycin-treated rats. These findings indicate that ER stress blunts adrenergic vasoconstriction, and induces endothelial dysfunction by enhancing Nox1-derived ROS and reducing mitochondrial vasodilator H2O2. Attenuation of ER stress emerges as a potential therapeutic target in the management of metabolic disease-associated erectile dysfunction.

Article.Title: A Transformers Analysis Pipeline (TrAP) to Evaluate LINE-1 RNA Sequence Content
Article.Authors: Chamorro-Parejo A.; Ramos K.
Article.Abstract: LINE-1 RNA has emerged as a potential regulator of chromatin organization and gene expression, as well as a candidate readout of cellular and disease-associated states. Accurate measurement of LINE-1 transcript abundance is therefore important for evaluating its regulatory, biomarker, and potential therapeutic relevance. AlbertSalmon agreed most closely with the synthetic insertion levels, ranking first in all insertion levels and deletion-probability strata. Agreement with the 5′RACE reference was also highest, although the locus-level gain there was only incremental. High-attribution k-mers were modestly over-represented within functional ORF2 coding regions rather than being uniformly distributed across LINE-1. These findings support TrAP as a transformer-assisted framework for improving LINE-1 quantification in short-read RNA-seq datasets, thereby supporting future regulatory and biomarker studies.

Article.Title: Construction of S-Scheme Heterojunction MoS2/TiO2 and Investigation of the Photocatalytic Inhibition Performance
Article.Authors: Lu Q.; Yang G.; Han T.; Nan H.
Article.Abstract: TiO2 possesses excellent photocatalytic antibacterial performance. Owing to its unique structural and physicochemical characteristics, TiO2 has been extensively applied in energy, environmental remediation, and biomedical fields. Herein, a hierarchical one-dimensional (1D) TiO2 architecture consisting of a well-distributed nanotube bottom layer whose surface nanowires interconnect into groove structures was fabricated on titanium foil via anodic oxidation, and molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) nanosheets were further grown in situ on the TiO2 surface to construct MoS2/TiO2 composite photocatalysts. The as-prepared composites exhibit superior hydrophilicity and prominent photocatalytic activity under full-spectrum simulated-solar irradiation, achieving a bactericidal efficiency of 86% against Staphylococcus aureus. Characterization results confirm that MoS2 nanoflower-like spheres are uniformly loaded on the surface of the 1D TiO2. An intimate S-scheme heterojunction is successfully fabricated between the two components, which significantly promotes the migration and separation of photogenerated charge carriers. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) tests demonstrate that superoxide radicals (·O2−) and hydroxyl radicals (·OH) are the dominant active species responsible for the efficient antibacterial behavior. This work reveals the significant application potential of MoS2/TiO2 composite photocatalysts and provides a feasible theoretical basis for the practical development and application of high-efficiency photocatalytic antibacterial materials.

Article.Title: Immune-Related Proteomic Profiling in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma: Tissue and Soluble Biofluid Biomarkers
Article.Authors: Anatoliotaki C.; Antonouli S.; Tzortzis V.; Vlachostergios P.; Zachos I.; Thodou E.; Giakountis A.; Samara M.
Article.Abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) shows complex interactions with the tumor microenvironment, involving a range of immune checkpoint proteins and circulating biomarkers that may influence disease progression and response to treatment. Recent technological advances have identified tissue-based and circulating immune-related proteomic targets such as programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1), cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4 (CTLA-4), and circulating interleukin-8 (cIL-8) as potential diagnostic, prognostic and predictive biomarkers. Despite significant progress, ccRCC remains a major clinical challenge due to its diverse molecular and immunological characteristics that hinder the clinical utility of these biomarkers. The present review provides an updated overview of the current evidence regarding immune-related proteomic biomarkers in ccRCC, including both tissue-derived and circulating proteins. Herein, we discuss the potential diagnostic, prognostic, and predictive value of such agents, emphasizing their biological significance and potential to guide personalized immunotherapeutic strategies. Particular attention is given to the developing liquid-biopsy-based techniques and their application as novel minimally invasive methods of identifying new targets for disease monitoring and treatment evaluation. Finally, we focus on emerging therapeutic approaches and combined strategies, highlighting how biomarker-driven precision oncology continues to reshape ccRCC management.

Article.Authors: Demchenko A.; Lopatina M.; Panchuk I.; Nazarova A.; Ivleva A.; Amelina E.; Voronina E.; Pozhitnova V.; Kochergin-Nikitsky K.; Balyasin M.; Kovalskaia V.; Ryzhkova O.; Lavrov A.; Smirnikhina S.

Chimeric organoids showed a dose-dependent increase in swelling with rising wild-type fractions, with a statistically significant FIS response first resolved at approximately 6% wild-type cells in the pooled analysis. Separately, ROC analysis of well-level data identified two area-ratio cutoffs for classifying organoid populations—1.16 (80% sensitivity, 80% specificity) and 1.21 (98% specificity, 70% sensitivity)—which the fitted mean response reaches at approximately 14% and 34% wild-type cells, respectively. The minimum statistically detectable fraction and the classification cutoffs are distinct quantities derived from different analyses and are not interchangeable; both describe the performance of the FIS assay in heterogeneous organoids rather than thresholds for therapeutic benefit and provide a practical reference framework for designing and interpreting gene editing and cell therapy studies in cystic fibrosis.

Article.Title: Computer-Aided Drug Design for Immunosuppressive Tumor Microenvironment Reprogramming: A Critical Review
Article.Authors: Moon J.; Rew J.; Shin H.; Song K.; Cho H.; Jung J.; Kyung M.
Article.Abstract: How can cellular interactions in solid tumors guide molecular interventions against immune suppression? This critical review examines how computer-aided drug design (CADD) connects immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) states to testable molecular hypotheses. We distinguish observational artificial intelligence (AI) predictions from molecular intervention hypotheses and examine the experimental evidence required to evaluate them. We reviewed patient-derived models, spatial and multi-omics profiling, molecular design, simulation, and pharmacology using the literature identified through to 15 October 2026. Adenosine-receptor antagonist discovery and generative protein-binder design illustrated how computational methods contributed to experimentally tested molecular candidates. Native-state structural studies, stromal delivery, and protein degradation broadened the approaches considered. We organized these findings into a proposed framework encompassing in vivo and patient-derived systems, multi-omics mapping, phenotyping of TME states, actionable AI integration, combination-therapy prioritization, and translational testing (IMPACT). A retrospective analysis of a phase III trial illustrated how the framework connects clinical outcomes to questions about mechanism, patient selection, and exposure. The synthesis clarifies the evidence required to connect molecular binding, target engagement, and exposure to patient benefit. IMPACT provides a structure for relating biological context to molecular design and specifying hypotheses for prospective evaluation.

Article.Title: Force-Induced Spiropyran–Merocyanine Interconversion: An Enforced Geometry Optimization Study
Article.Authors: Brzyska A.
Article.Abstract: Mechanically induced spiropyran (SP)–merocyanine (MC) interconversion was examined using the enforced geometry optimization (EGO) method at the B3LYP/6-311G(d,p) level. The calculations followed a complete mechanical cycle for the SP–CH3 model: tensile opening of the spiro ring, force removal, and subsequent compression. This allowed both SP → MC conversion and recovery of the closed SP structure to be considered within the same computational framework. Across eleven spiropyran derivatives, the first observed opening forces show a clear overall Hammett-like trend, with strongly electron-withdrawing substituents opening earlier and strongly electron-donating substituents opening later. A closer analysis of the H-, NH2-, and Cl-substituted systems showed that C–O cleavage is accompanied by loss of the localized spiro bond, Wiberg bond indices falling to values near zero, charge redistribution, and narrowing of the HOMO–LUMO gap. Calculations in the gas phase and in thirteen COSMO environments revealed a further feature: a low-force geometric reorganization precedes bond cleavage. The solvent also influences which relaxed MC conformer is reached, giving TTC, CTC, CCC, or CCT structures. Neither the calculated ring-opening point nor the final MC conformation is determined solely by the dielectric constant.

Article.Title: From Ethnomedicine to Pharmacological Evidence: Phytochemistry, Biological Activities, and Therapeutic Potential of the Genus Abutilon (Malvaceae)
Article.Authors: Rakhymbayev N.; Ibadullayeva G.; Mombekov S.; Kantureyeva A.; Azimkhanova B.; Amantayeva M.; Pazilov S.; Iskakova U.; Konash N.; Tjahjono D.; Yegizbayeva A.; Zhakipbekov K.; Daulbayeva A.
Article.Abstract: The genus Abutilon (Malvaceae) comprises taxonomically and phytochemically diverse medicinal plants with a long history of ethnomedicinal use. This critical narrative review integrates evidence on the taxonomy, traditional applications, phytochemical composition, pharmacological activities, molecular mechanisms, safety, and pharmaceutical potential of Abutilon species, incorporating the literature published through September 2026. Flavonoids, phenolic acids, triterpenoids, phytosterols, polysaccharides, and fatty acids represent major reported constituent classes, although the reliability of their identification and quantitative characterization varies among studies. A. indicum and A. theophrasti remain the most extensively investigated species. Experimental findings support preliminary antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, antidiabetic, hepatoprotective, gastroprotective, and other biological activities, predominantly in biochemical, cellular, and animal models. Mechanistic investigations have reported modulation of NF-κB/MAPK signaling, inflammatory mediators, glucose-regulatory processes, and oxidative stress-related responses; however, direct molecular target validation remains limited. Pharmaceutical studies have explored tablets, phytosomal formulations, and plant-mediated nanoparticles, but evidence of improved systemic bioavailability, therapeutic efficacy, and long-term safety remains insufficient. Toxicological findings indicate preparation- and dose-dependent responses, while controlled clinical evidence is extremely limited. Methodological heterogeneity, incomplete chemical standardization, and limited pharmacokinetic characterization further restrict cross-study comparisons and therapeutic translation. Future research should prioritize authenticated botanical materials, chemically standardized preparations, reproducible dose–response studies, direct mechanistic validation, comprehensive toxicological assessment, and appropriately designed clinical investigations. Overall, Abutilon represents a potentially valuable source of pharmacologically active natural products, but current evidence does not establish standardized clinical applications.

The workflow enabled same-day mutation profiling directly from diagnostic material, providing rapid sequence-level information on mutations associated with increased transmissibility and immune escape. These findings demonstrate that PSQ provides rapid and reliable screening of predefined spike mutations associated with early SARS-CoV-2 VOCs. The workflow may complement whole-genome sequencing in surveillance settings where rapid mutation-level information is required. In a broader sense, the study demonstrates a data-driven approach for developing and periodically adapting targeted molecular surveillance assays as viral populations evolve.

Article.Title: Rare-Earth Orthoferrites: Synthesis–Structure–Property Relationships, Functional Applications, and Future Perspectives
Article.Authors: Mataev M.; Abdraimova M.; Madiyarova A.; Raissova K.; Nurbekova M.; Keskin B.
Article.Abstract: Rare-earth-based RFeO3 orthoferrites are multifunctional materials distinguished by their structural flexibility, high chemical and thermal stability, and unique combination of magnetic, electrical, dielectric, optical, sensing, and catalytic properties. This review critically systematizes recent advances in the synthesis of RFeO3 orthoferrites, the development of their structural and morphological characteristics, and the targeted control of their functional properties. The effects of solid-state reaction, optical floating-zone growth, sol–gel processing, sol–gel auto-combustion, coprecipitation, hydrothermal synthesis, and microwave-assisted synthesis on phase purity, crystallinity, particle size, morphology, and defect structure are compared. The influence of A- and B-site cation substitution, oxygen vacancies, FeO6 octahedral tilting, and microstrain on charge transport, magnetic exchange interactions, and electronic structure is examined. The capabilities of X-ray diffraction (XRD), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Raman and Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, electron microscopy, vibrating-sample magnetometry (VSM), linear sweep voltammetry (LSV), and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) for elucidating structure–property relationships are assessed. The compiled evidence demonstrates that synthesis conditions and chemical modification produce interrelated changes in the phase composition, grain size, band-gap energy, dielectric and magnetic responses, and sensing and catalytic activity of orthoferrites. The application potential of RFeO3-based materials in magnetic refrigeration, spintronics, supercapacitors, gas sensors, solid oxide fuel cells, magnetic memory, capacitors, photocatalysis, and electrocatalysis is evaluated. The analysis identifies the systematic elucidation of the “synthesis–structure–morphology–property–function” relationship, quantitative characterization of defect chemistry, standardization of measurement protocols, and evaluation of long-term operational stability as key priorities for future research.

Article.Title: Frequent PRAME Expression in Ameloblastoma: Immunohistochemical Profiling, Clinicopathologic Correlations, and Interobserver Reproducibility in a 37-Case Cohort
Article.Authors: Popovic F.; Spasic D.; Boricic N.; Milanovic S.; Glumac S.; Dozic B.; Anicic B.
Article.Abstract: Ameloblastoma is a histologically benign odontogenic epithelial tumor with locally destructive growth and a clinically relevant risk of recurrence. Established molecular research has been largely focused on MAPK-pathway alterations, whereas markers capturing other dimensions of tumor biology remain limited. Preferentially expressed antigen in melanoma (PRAME) is a tumor-associated antigen implicated in retinoic-acid receptor signaling, altered differentiation, and antitumor immune recognition, but dedicated data in ameloblastoma remain limited. In this retrospective cohort, 37 histologically confirmed ameloblastomas were evaluated immunohistochemically for PRAME on tissue microarray sections by two independent pathologists. A four-tier extent score (0, 1+, 2+, 3+) and a four-tier intensity score (absent, weak, moderate, strong) were recorded. PRAME positivity was defined as nuclear staining in ≥25% of tumor cells for exploratory association analyses. Clinicopathologic variables included age, sex, anatomic site, side, mandibular subsite, histologic type, surgical approach, recurrence, and follow-up. Interobserver reproducibility was assessed using percentage agreement and Cohen’s κ statistics. Holm adjustment was applied as a post hoc sensitivity analysis across eight exploratory clinicopathological comparisons. PRAME was positive in 30 of 37 tumors (81.1%; exact 95% CI 64.8–92.0). Twenty-nine tumors (78.4%) received a 3+ extent score from both observers, seven (18.9%) were negative, and the remaining tumor was scored 1+ by one observer and 2+ by the other. Extent scoring agreed in 36 of 37 cases (97.3% agreement; Cohen kappa = 0.923). Intensity scoring agreed in 35 of 37 cases (94.6%); unweighted kappa was 0.905, with linear and quadratic weighted kappa values of 0.927 and 0.949. PRAME positivity was more frequent in women than in men (95.2% vs. 62.5%; unadjusted two-sided Fisher exact p = 0.029; Holm-adjusted p = 0.230). All 11 patients with documented recurrence had PRAME-positive tumors, compared with 19 of 26 patients without documented recurrence (unadjusted p = 0.080). PRAME positivity was also more frequent among conservatively than radically treated patients (91.7% vs. 61.5%; unadjusted p = 0.072). None of the eight clinicopathological comparisons met the 0.05 threshold after Holm adjustment. PRAME is frequently and extensively expressed in ameloblastoma and can be assessed with excellent interobserver reproducibility. The recurrence and treatment patterns are hypothesis-generating, but the small cohort, sparse PRAME-negative subgroup, and treatment imbalance preclude claims of independent prognostic value. Larger multicenter studies with standardized scoring, molecular validation, and time-to-event analysis are warranted.

Article.Title: From Fixed Lineage to Dynamic States: Fibro-Adipogenic Progenitors in Skeletal Muscle Regeneration, Fibrosis, and Fibrofatty Degeneration
Article.Authors: Sun J.; Ma F.; Yang D.; Chen S.; Wang L.; Li S.; Gu M.; Zhang W.
Article.Abstract: Skeletal muscle repair depends on coordinated interactions among muscle stem cells, immune cells, extracellular matrix, and resident stromal cells. A key stromal population, fibro-adipogenic progenitors (FAPs), has attracted considerable attention. Yet FAPs are not a fixed mesenchymal lineage. They form a plastic, heterogeneous compartment with context-dependent functional states that shift with injury stage, anatomical site, disease, and species. Understanding what drives this plasticity is essential. This review examines how biochemical, inflammatory, mechanical, and epigenetic signals shape FAP states. We synthesize evidence from multiple species, including mouse, human, bovine, porcine, and camel muscle systems. Four regulatory modules are considered: TGF-β/PDGFRα signaling and immune crosstalk, canonical and non-canonical Wnt pathways, epigenetic regulation, and extracellular matrix mechanotransduction. Through these pathways, FAPs adopt distinct functional programs. These include homeostatic maintenance, reparative support, fibrogenic activation, adipogenic differentiation, inflammatory response, and senescence. Each program differentially influences muscle stem cell function and tissue remodeling outcomes. These programs reflect context-dependent FAP states, not a uniform lineage with fixed functions. Several concepts require clarification. We emphasize that fibrogenic and adipogenic programs can be differentially regulated yet coexist within diseased muscle, and that pathological FAP states may retain context-dependent reversibility. These insights clarify the constraints on cross-species translation and inform the design of stage-matched, context-appropriate, or combinatorial FAP-directed therapeutic strategies for muscle disease.

Article.Title: Terpenoid Accumulation and Terpene Synthase Gene Expression Are Coordinately Modulated in Calabrian Pine (Pinus nigra subsp. laricio) Following Infestation by the Pine Processionary Moth (Thaumetopoea pityocampa)
Article.Authors: Alicandri E.; Sebastiani B.; Paolacci A.; Covino S.; Sorgonà A.; Manti F.; Castiglione E.; Bonsignore C.; Badiani M.; Ciaffi M.
Article.Abstract: Calabrian pine (Pinus nigra subsp. laricio) is an ecologically and economically important Mediterranean conifer increasingly exposed to the pine processionary moth (PPM; Thaumetopoea pityocampa). We investigated temporal differences in needle terpene metabolism between saplings maintained in a control enclosure and saplings exposed to prolonged PPM infestation in a separate, otherwise identical enclosure. Three-year-old saplings underwent semi-natural infestation for 195 days, and needles were sampled at 0, 21, 84, and 195 days post-infestation. Solvent-extractable monoterpenoids and diterpene resin acids (DRAs) were quantified through gas chromatography–mass spectrometry, while the transcript abundances of mono- and diterpene synthase (MTPS and DTPS, respectively) genes were analyzed through quantitative real-time PCR. During the whole experimental period, the terpenoid blend remained unchanged, qualitatively speaking, in both control and PPM-infested saplings, whereas the two experimental groups showed marked time-dependent quantitative differences among each other in terms of individual compound and transcript abundances. In PPM-infested plants, β-pinene, α-pinene, α-terpineol, and (−)-β-phellandrene accumulated mainly at 84 and 195 days, with changes in their putatively associated Pnl MTPS transcripts accompanying or preceding metabolite accumulation. Conversely, δ-3-carene and Pnl MTPS3 transcript abundance declined strongly. Abietane-type DRAs and dehydroabietic acid accumulated at later stages, together with higher Pnl DTPS1 transcript abundance. Multivariate analyses showed earlier divergence of TPS transcript profiles than metabolite profiles. Thus, Calabrian pine saplings infested by PPM exhibit selective, temporally structured reprogramming of mono- and diterpenoid pathways, rather than a generalized terpenoid induction.

Article.Title: Isolation, Identification, and Pathogenicity of Aeromonas veronii from Diseased Paracobitis variegatus
Article.Authors: Zhang Z.; Zhou Y.; Zhou Q.; Wang Y.; Xiao C.; Xu D.
Article.Abstract: Aeromonas veronii (A. veronii) is ubiquitous in aquatic habitats and infects diverse aquatic animals, causing high mortality and heavy economic losses in aquaculture. In this study, we initially isolated a Gram-negative bacterium (Pv001) from the visceral organs of naturally diseased Paracobitis variegatus. Based on morphological, biochemical, and 16S rRNA and gyrB gene sequence analysis, the isolated strain was accurately determined to be A. veronii. Virulence gene screening showed that the strain Pv001 carried multiple virulence genes, including Acg, Act, Alt, Exu, Lip, and Omp. In vitro antimicrobial evaluations revealed that ceftriaxone, chloramphenicol, ciprofloxacin, and tetracycline displayed significant inhibitory effects on Pv001, while ampicillin, penicillin, and lincomycin exhibited no detectable inhibitory action. The artificial challenge of Paracobitis variegatus with the isolated strain Pv001 via intraperitoneal injection reproduced the clinical signs observed in the affected farm, yielding a calculated LD50 of 8.61 × 105 CFU/fish. Histopathological analysis of the diseased fish indicated extensive intestinal mucosal destruction, vacuolar degeneration of liver cells, and localized necrosis, as well as a considerable number of melano-macrophage centers (MMCs) aggregating in the spleen. This study provides a scientific foundation for the prevention and control of epidemics by revealing the pathogenic features of A. veronii illness in P. variegatus.

Article.Title: Emerging Therapies in Pulmonary Fibrosis: A Common Pathway for the Action of Diverse Pharmacologic Agents
Article.Authors: Bolger G.
Article.Abstract: Fibrotic lung diseases are a heterogeneous set of disorders characterized by progressive infiltration of the pulmonary interstitium by inflammatory cells and fibroblasts, leading to destruction of normal pulmonary tissue and increased extracellular matrix deposition. Fibrotic lung disease can be initiated by numerous triggers—genetic, immunologic, pharmacologic, environmental, infectious—that share many downstream effectors, leading to injury patterns with substantial pathologic and clinical overlap. Recent preclinical studies have expanded our knowledge of the mechanisms of lung inflammation and implicated the key role of specific cytokines in the pathogenesis of lung inflammation. They reinforce the concept that inflammation is a key precursor of lung fibrosis. They have also identified specific intracellular signaling pathways that are modulated, at least in part, by cytokine signaling and that have been shown to be emerging targets for drugs that target inflammation in the lung. Recent advances in therapeutics have yielded two new drugs active in pulmonary fibrosis, the PDE4-selective inhibitor nerandomilast and the prostacyclin analog treprostinil. There is now compelling evidence that, despite their structural differences, these two drugs act through a common mechanism, the cAMP signaling pathway. The new clinical trial results have provided critical confirmation that these targets are indeed key regulators of lung fibrosis and inflammation and, in turn, have provided well-validated clinical evidence that these agents have therapeutic value in patients.

Article.Title: Combined Effect of Hadron Therapy and PCSK9 Inhibition Therapy on the Immune Response in STK11-Deficient Lung Adenocarcinoma
Article.Authors: Gantsova E.; Arutyunyan I.; Soboleva A.; Mikhailovskaia V.; Kananykhina E.; Artemova D.; Mironov K.; Vishnyakova P.; Elchaninov A.; Bao X.; Makarov A.; Gordon K.; Fatkhudinov T.
Article.Abstract: Lung cancer is the most common type of cancer worldwide. Tumors carrying a mutation in the STK11 gene are associated with severe prognosis and resistance to therapy. New treatments for pulmonary adenocarcinoma highlight the efficacy of High-LET neutron therapy, often combined with drug therapy. PCSK9, whose inhibitors are used to treat dyslipidemia, may also be a new target in lung cancer therapy. CRISPR-Cas9-mediated STK11 mutation was performed in murine LLC1 lung adenocarcinoma cells. Human A549 cells that naturally carry a homozygous loss-of-function mutation in the STK11 gene were also used. Cells were irradiated with protons, neutrons, and photons (2 Gy) and analyzed for survival, apoptosis, clonogenic survival assay, and evolocumab (PCSK9 inhibitor) sensitivity. In vivo xenograft (Nude) and syngeneic (C57BL/6) subcutaneous tumor models were neutron-irradiated (5 Gy). Tumor cell proliferation, microenvironment, and protein expression were assessed. High-LET irradiation confirmed the STK11-deficient lines radio resistance, which did not reduce under PCSK9 inhibitor treatment conditions in vitro. In animal models, the PCSK9 inhibitor decreased Ki67 index of tumor cells and infiltration of cancer-associated fibroblasts and macrophages in the combination therapy group. Particle therapy resistance serves as a crucial prognostic marker in the management of lung adenocarcinoma. Using cell lines and animal models, we successfully described this resistance phenotype and demonstrated the promising use of a PCSK9 inhibitor to enhance the efficacy of hadron radiotherapy against lung cancer.

Article.Title: Alpha-Lipoic Acid and Saxagliptin Attenuate Ferroptosis-Related Ovarian Injury and Modulate FGF21/NOX4–NRF2/HO-1 Signaling in Letrozole-Induced Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
Article.Authors: Yousef E.; Zohny M.; Abdel-lah E.; Metawee M.; Sakr H.; Salama M.
Article.Abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a complex endocrine-metabolic disorder characterized by ovarian dysfunction, hormonal imbalance, and emerging ferroptosis-related abnormalities. This study investigated the effects of alpha-lipoic acid (ALA), saxagliptin (Saxa), and their combination in a letrozole-induced PCOS model, with focus on the ovarian FGF21/NOX4–NRF2/HO-1 and ferroptosis-related pathways. PCOS was induced in female rats by oral letrozole administration for 21 days. Rats were allocated into control, PCOS, ALA, Saxa, and ALA/Saxa groups, followed by 14 days of treatment. Body weight, ovarian index, ovarian histopathology, reproductive hormones, oxidative stress markers, ovarian FGF21 and NOX4 expression, NRF2/HO-1 signaling, and ferroptosis-related markers, including Fe+2, GPX4, and SLC7A11, were assessed. Letrozole induced weight gain, ovarian hypertrophy, follicular disruption, endocrine imbalance, and ferroptosis-related alterations, marked by increased ROS, MDA, Fe2+, and NOX4, alongside reduced FGF21, NRF2/HO-1, GPX4, and SLC7A11. ALA or Saxa attenuated these alterations, whereas ALA/Saxa produced greater improvements in ovarian morphology, hormonal status, redox homeostasis, and ferroptosis-related markers. These effects were associated with FGF21 upregulation, NOX4 suppression, enhanced NRF2/HO-1 signaling, and preservation of GPX4 and SLC7A11. In conclusion, ALA/Saxa therapy markedly ameliorated letrozole-induced PCOS in rats, accompanied by restoration of ovarian FGF21/NOX4 homeostasis, associated with enhancement of NRF2/HO-1 antioxidant responses, and attenuation of ferroptosis-related alterations.

Article.Title: Nuclear Mechanotransduction in Cancer Radiation Response: Linking Nuclear Envelope Dynamics to DNA Damage Repair
Article.Authors: Xu F.; Xiang Y.; Huang W.; Hu P.; Wang S.; Cao K.; Wan Z.; Yang Y.; Gao F.; Chen Y.
Article.Abstract: Tumor mechanics influence radiation response, yet no single mechanical parameter predicts radiosensitivity, and nominally identical variables report opposite results. The gap is not a shortage of mechanisms but the absence of a validated link between a measurable nuclear state, the fidelity of damage processing, and long-term reproductive outcome. This review follows mechanical signals from adhesion and the cytoskeletal systems through the linker of nucleoskeleton and cytoskeleton (LINC) complex, nuclear pores and lamina to chromatin, the nucleolus and DNA repair, asking at each step whether the mechanical input could change how radiation damage is processed rather than how much is produced. Mechanical manipulation combined with irradiation in the same system remains uncommon; most evidence establishes mechanosensitive components without connecting them to a radiation outcome, and this asymmetry accounts for much of the apparent conflict in the literature. We therefore sort the evidence into three levels of support, propose a three-state framework of nuclear mechanical homeostasis (insufficient structural support, maladaptive structural constraint, coordinated integrity and plasticity), and specify the experiments that would falsify it. Nuclear mechanotransduction is better described as a context-dependent adaptive network than as a single determinant of radiosensitivity, and matrix-normalizing, Src-directed and ultrasound-based interventions remain unvalidated for radiotherapy.

Article.Title: Virtual Screening–Derived Computational Lead Candidates for MAO-B Inhibition in Parkinson’s Disease: Pathway-Informed Docking, Molecular Dynamics, DFT and ADMET Evaluation
Article.Authors: Khater I.; Elabed S.; Hussein M.; Alam-Eldein K.; Aly A.; Hamada S.; Elhendawy A.
Article.Abstract: Monoamine oxidase B (MAO-B) is a clinically validated target in Parkinson’s disease (PD), but docking rank alone is insufficient to establish a CNS-directed inhibitor. We integrated MAOB-related pathway context, domain-resolved structural annotation, GNINA virtual screening, predicted blood–brain barrier (BBB) permeation, molecular dynamics (MD), density functional theory (DFT) and ADMET assessment to nominate hypothesis-stage computational candidates. A pharmacophore-derived input collection 2870 entries was subjected to virtual screening; a curated BBB-positive, favorable Vina/CNN-affinity shortlist yielded PubChem CIDs 143667968, 42876521 and 1232631. The three candidates had similar reported GNINA scores. In single 100 ns MD trajectories, CID 42876521 displayed frequent protein–ligand hydrogen bonds, whereas CID 143667968 displayed almost none and reduced aromatic-cage fluctuation. CID 143667968 also had the smallest gas-phase HOMO–LUMO gap. All three compounds carried predicted mutagenicity, carcinogenicity and hERG alerts. CID 42876521 is therefore prioritized for validation, CID 143667968 is retained as a complementary hypothesis and CID 1232631 as a backup scaffold. These results define a preliminary, multi-parameter prioritization framework.

Article.Title: The Radiosensitizing Potential of CC-115, PIK-75 and M3814 DNA-PK Inhibitors for Breast Cancer Targeted Radiotherapy
Article.Authors: Niculae D.; Șerban R.; Drăgănescu D.; Niculae D.
Article.Abstract: NHEJ is one of the preferred DNA-damage-repairing mechanisms for human cells, due to its rapid onset and activity throughout the cell cycle. It is, nevertheless, error-prone and highly relevant in numerous oncological malignancies. In recent years, it has gained a lot of attention as a target either for cancer treatment or as pharmacological- and radio-sensitization approaches. This study evaluated the genotoxicity and radiosensitization potential of three DNA-PK inhibitors (PIK-75, M3814, and CC-115) in breast cancer by comparing MDA-MB-231 and MCF-7 breast cancer cell lines, selected based on reported differences in DNA-repair characteristics and relative NHEJ dependence. Cells were preincubated with the DNA-PK inhibitors, using four different concentrations either in monotherapy or in combination with a DNA damage inducer (doxorubicin or [64Cu]CuCl2). Viability was measured by MTS assays at 24, 48, and 72 h, while the DNA damage was measured by γH2AX and flow cytometry. DNA-PK inhibitor combinations produced greater reductions in MTS viability in MDA-MB-231 than in MCF-7 under experimental conditions when combined with doxorubicin and 64Cu. Combination treatments generally reduced viability relative to inhibitor monotherapy, with clearer concentration dependence and stronger effects in MDA-MB-231. In the case of [64Cu]CuCl2 alone, MDA-MB-231 viability was reduced to 70–75% at 24 h, whereas several inhibitor combinations reduced it further; MCF-7 showed weaker or inconsistent potentiation. The reduction in metabolic viability became more pronounced at 72 h, particularly in MDA-MB-231 cells. Overall, the results highlight the potential of exploiting repair-pathway dependence to improve targeted radiotherapy in breast cancer.

Article.Title: Evaluation of Dose-Dependent Efficacy and Mechanisms of Aspirin Combined with Intravenous Immunoglobulin in a Murine Model of Kawasaki Disease Vasculitis
Article.Authors: Chien K.; Huang S.; Wang W.; Huang C.; Kuo H.; Yeh Y.; Lin C.; Hsieh K.; Weng K.
Article.Abstract: The requirement and molecular contribution of acute high-dose aspirin (ASA) in the treatment of Kawasaki disease (KD) remain clinically controversial. This study aimed to investigate the dose-dependent mechanism and pharmacodynamics of adjunctive ASA in an experimental KD mouse model. Male C57BL/6 mice were injected with Lactobacillus casei cell wall extract (LCWE; 100 µg/day, Days 1–7) to induce systemic coronary arteritis. On Day 14, mice received intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) (2 g/kg, i.p.) monotherapy (G3) or IVIG combined with High-dose (100 mg/kg; G4), Medium-dose (50 mg/kg; G5), or Low-dose ASA (5 mg/kg; G6) daily via oral gavage for 3 days (Days 14–16), followed by a 5-day drug washout until sacrifice on Day 21. Coronary vasculitis and internal elastic lamina integrity were quantified using H&E and Verhoeff–Van Gieson (VVG) staining. Heart tissue activation of p-nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κB) and downstream matrix metalloproteinance-9 (MMP-9) expression were evaluated by Western blot. High-dose ASA combined with IVIG (G4) achieved statistically superior suppression of upstream NF-κB phosphorylation (p-NF-κB/NF-κB ratio) and perivascular leukocyte infiltration compared to IVIG monotherapy (G3) (p < 0.05). This acute upstream blockade directly preserved arterial wall architecture, with G4 demonstrating near-baseline structural restoration of the internal elastic lamina on VVG scoring (G4 vs. G3, p < 0.05). Following the 5-day drug washout, downstream MMP-9 expression in G4 converged with G3 levels due to pharmacodynamic waning, whereas suboptimal mid/low-dose ASA regimens (G5/G6) displayed lingering MMP-9 elevation, indicating persistent low-grade matrix remodeling. Acute high-dose ASA provides a non-redundant, synergistic anti-inflammatory effect alongside IVIG to prevent early elastolysis. Maintaining adequate acute ASA dose followed by careful post-withdrawal tapering is vital to prevent delayed arterial wall remodeling and coronary aneurysm progression.

Article.Title: LED Photobiomodulation at 630 nm Attenuates TNF-α-Induced Senescence-Associated Responses in Association with Mitochondrial Homeostasis
Article.Authors: Li X.; Zhang L.; Wang N.; Yang X.; Xie W.; Meng Q.; Hu L.; Liu H.; Song W.
Article.Abstract: Chronic inflammation can accelerate the aging of joint tissues, characterized by cellular senescence, inflammatory degeneration, and disrupted tissue homeostasis. The accumulation of senescent cells and the excessive release of senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) factors are accompanied by mitochondrial dysfunction, including increased oxidative stress, reduced mitochondrial membrane potential, and impaired mitochondrial quality control. Since TNF-α is a key inflammatory mediator in arthritic tissues, we used TNF-α-stimulated human fibroblast-like synoviocytes (MH7A) and chondrocytes (C28/I2), along with hTNF-α transgenic mice, to investigate whether 630 nm LED photobiomodulation therapy (PBMT) attenuates inflammatory and senescence-associated responses and whether these effects are linked to the restoration of mitochondrial homeostasis. Transcriptomic analysis, cell-based assays, and tissue immunohistochemistry were used to assess inflammatory and senescence-associated gene expression, mitochondrial features, autophagy-related proteins, and SIRT1/PGC-1α levels. PBMT reduced the TNF-α-induced expression of IL-6, IL-1β, IL-8, MMP-3, MMP-13, p16, and p21 in both cell models. Further experiments in C28/I2 cells showed that TNF-α increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, reduced mitochondrial membrane potential, disrupted mitochondrial ultrastructure, altered autophagy-related protein expression, and decreased SIRT1 and PGC-1α expression. These alterations were partially reversed by PBMT, accompanied by the restoration of mitochondrial homeostasis-related markers. Extending the in vitro findings, in vivo experiments using hTNF-α transgenic mice showed that PBMT enhanced the immunostaining signals of SIRT1 and PGC-1α in joint tissues. Overall, these findings indicate that PBMT attenuates TNF-α-induced inflammatory and senescence-associated responses in joint cells, which are associated with mitochondrial homeostasis, supporting further mechanistic and functional evaluation of this intervention.

Article.Title: Inositol-Dependent Alleviation of Lithium-Induced Embryonic Neurotoxicity in Mice Through the GSK3β/β-Catenin/CyclinD1 Pathway
Article.Authors: Li S.; Guo J.; Wang X.; Guan Z.; Zhu Z.; Yang A.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Lithium carbonate (Li2CO3) is a first-line pharmacotherapy for bipolar disorder (BPD) in female patients of childbearing age, although it is associated with embryonic teratogenicity. Lithium exposure in batteries and pharmaceuticals has been a toxicity factor for women’s reproductive health in energy, environment, and fitness fields. Neural tube defects (NTDs) are the severest reproductive outcome of maternal Li2CO3 exposure. Currently, there is a lack of effective prevention for Li2CO3 neurotoxicity. Our previous study revealed that lithium-induced murine NTDs correlated with enhanced proliferation and impaired inositol biosynthesis. In this study, 400 mg/kg inositol was used to treat the lithium-induced murine NTDs after calculating the toxicity using ADMETlab 3.0 and Deep-PK. We found that inositol supplementation ameliorated fetal neural phenotypes, crown-rump length, and body weight and rescued aberrant cell proliferation and dysregulated the GSK3β/β-catenin/CyclinD1 pathway in both animal and cellular models. The affinity of GSK3β-inositol interaction was analyzed and validated using molecular dynamics and surface plasmon resonance. GSK3β-edited cell models further revealed that inositol altered GSK3β post-transcriptional status and phosphorylation, consequently modulating the GSK3β/β-catenin/CyclinD1 signaling cascade. Overall, our study clarified that inositol alleviates lithium-induced NTDs via the GSK3β/β-catenin/CyclinD1 pathway, revealed the direct molecular interaction between inositol and GSK3β, and highlighted the potential of inositol as a therapeutic prevention against lithium-induced embryonic neurotoxicity for childbearing female BPD patients.

Article.Title: Sweeteners at the Water–Soil Interface and in Soil Matrices: A Brief Review of Ecotoxicological Impacts
Article.Authors: Tkach V.; Costa M.; Morozova T.; Ricardo Sousa J.; Ivanushko Y.; Martins J.; Gaivão I.
Article.Abstract: Sweeteners have become emerging contaminants in terrestrial and aquatic environments due to their extensive use in food, pharmaceutical, alternative smoking, and personal care products. They reach terrestrial ecosystems from both atmospheric and aquatic ecosystems, making the water–soil interface a critical zone governing their transport, persistence, and environmental fate, which remains mostly unknown, thus creating a gap that needs to be filled. This review aims to summarize current knowledge on the occurrence, mobility, persistence, and ecotoxicological effects of artificial and natural sweeteners in soils and at the water–soil interface, with emphasis on sucralose, saccharin, acesulfame potassium, aspartame, cyclamate, and steviol glycosides. The review covers seventy-two full papers, published from 2004 to 2026, involving sweetener intake and occurrence and environmental fate in soil and at the water–soil interface. Sweeteners may persist in terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, inducing, either individually or in combination, oxidative stress and influencing microbial communities and enzymatic activity at the soil–water interface, which affects invertebrates, plant roots, and the overall ecosystem. Their effects on soil biota are still poorly understood. These influences, as well as the effects of long-term persistence and differences in responses across soil types and climatic conditions, are mostly unknown. This review highlights the central role of the soil matrix and water–soil interface in understanding the environmental fate and ecological significance of sweeteners and identifies key gaps requiring further soil-specific research.

Article.Title: Endothelial Dysfunction in Psoriasis: A Comparative Analysis of Cutaneous, Inflammatory, and Metabolic Correlates
Article.Authors: Gkornik T.; Toma A.; Levai C.; Caraba A.; Borza C.
Article.Abstract: Psoriasis is associated with an elevated risk of cardiovascular disease, in which endothelial dysfunction, systemic inflammation, and insulin resistance are thought to interact. This study assessed endothelial function in 60 patients with psoriasis and 30 age- and sex-matched healthy controls, and examined its relationships with disease severity (PASI), insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α). Endothelial function was measured as brachial-artery flow-mediated dilation (FMD). Compared with controls, patients showed significantly reduced FMD together with higher TNF-α, HOMA-IR, renal resistive index, albumin-to-creatinine ratio, body mass index, and total cholesterol, and lower high density lipoprotein (HDL)-cholesterol (all p ≤ 0.002). Within the patient group, PASI correlated strongly and positively with TNF-α and HOMA-IR, and inversely with FMD, while both TNF-α and the renal resistive index correlated inversely with FMD (all p < 0.001). In separate multivariable regression models, a model containing TNF-α and HOMA-IR explained a slightly larger proportion of variance in FMD (R2 = 0.72) than a model containing PASI and HOMA-IR (R2 = 0.70); in both, HOMA-IR was the most consistently associated predictor, while PASI did not reach significance (standardized β = −0.18, p = 0.08). When all three predictors were entered simultaneously, strong collinearity between PASI and TNF-α (variance inflation factors 4.8 and 4.5, respectively) precluded reliable separation of their effects, and only HOMA-IR and TNF-α retained significance. These associations persisted after adjustment for age, sex, BMI, systolic blood pressure, and smoking status.These findings indicate that insulin resistance is the strongest independently associated factor of endothelial dysfunction in psoriasis, with systemic inflammation contributing additional explanatory value; however, the strong overlap between disease severity and circulating TNF-α prevents definitive separation of their individual effects, and formal mediation analyses in larger cohorts are warranted.

Article.Title: Emerging Computational Advances in Simulating PCSK9 Variant Dynamics for Therapeutic Design Against Hypercholesterolemia
Article.Authors: Opazo M.; Gallegos A.; Muñoz A.; Zapata R.; Rivera J.; Sepúlveda R.; Aguayo D.
Article.Abstract: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) is a premier model for precision medicine, having moved from genetic discovery to approved therapeutics within two decades. Yet despite the clinical success of monoclonal antibodies, small interfering RNA and the newly approved oral macrocyclic-peptide inhibitor class, targeting PCSK9 remains a demanding biophysical challenge. Clinical translation has concentrated almost entirely on the rigid, well-resolved subtilisin-like catalytic domain that interfaces with the low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR). By contrast, the C-terminal cysteine- and histidine-rich domain (CHRD), which governs allosteric regulation, protein trafficking and post-translational modification, is highly disordered and largely elusive in experimental structures, leaving a critical regulatory network therapeutically unexploited. This review examines how advanced computational biology is bridging that structural gap, organizing the computational landscape of PCSK9 around the biophysical mechanisms of gain- and loss-of-function variants. We detail how explicit-solvent molecular dynamics, free-energy calculations and cryptic-pocket detection expose the functional plasticity and allosteric networks that static crystallography cannot capture, and we evaluate the convergence of these physics-based approaches with artificial intelligence, including deep-learning structure prediction and generative design of de novo nanobody and peptide binders. Therapeutic development and the structural literature currently point in diverging directions: drug discovery remains focused on the crowded LDLR-binding interface, whereas computational methods are beginning to identify candidate sites beyond it. We argue that the next advance in PCSK9 therapeutics will come from integrating generative artificial intelligence with rigorous enhanced sampling in a unified pipeline, deliberately shifting focus toward the disordered regulatory domains that have evaded classical screening.

Article.Title: Exploration of Alternative Approaches to Citron Kinase Inhibition for Glioblastoma Treatment
Article.Authors: Ferraro A.; Lazzerini L.; Iegiani G.; De Bacco F.; Boccaccio C.; Di Cunto F.
Article.Abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains a highly aggressive brain tumor with limited therapeutic options, highlighting the need to identify novel tumor vulnerabilities. Citron kinase (CITK), a protein involved in cytokinesis and genome stability, is required for the proliferation and survival of neural progenitors and has previously emerged as a potential therapeutic target in medulloblastoma (MB). Here, we investigated the effects of CITK depletion and pharmacological inhibition in two patient-derived GBM stem cell models. CITK was depleted by siRNA or pharmacologically targeted using the first selective kinase inhibitor so far described, C3TD879 (c879). We also explored the polypharmacological inhibitor Lestaurtinib. Effects on spheroid growth, cytokinesis, cytotoxicity, DNA damage-associated proteins, apoptotic markers, and cell-cycle regulators were assessed. CITK depletion partially impaired spheroid growth, slightly increased multinucleation, and led to cytotoxicity in both GBM models, while effects on DNA damage-associated proteins were cell-line dependent. Selective CITK inhibition with c879 slightly reduced spheroid growth and only partially recapitulated the cellular and molecular effects of CITK depletion. Lestaurtinib produced stronger spheroid growth inhibition and cytokinesis defects, while inducing limited cytotoxicity and heterogeneous molecular responses. In summary, the tested GBM models were shown to be moderately sensitive to CITK depletion and selective catalytic inhibition, while Lestaurtinib showed the strongest effects, which mimicked only in part the effects of CITK loss.

Article.Title: Plasma PAH-like AhR Bioactivity, Homocysteine, and Subclinical Vascular and Haematologic Phenotypes in the SPES Biomonitoring Substudy
Article.Authors: Cerino P.; Rosa E.; Triassi M.; Montuori P.; Buonerba C.
Article.Abstract: Receptor-based bioassays measure mixture activity whose relationship with human physiology requires empirical assessment. We examined plasma polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH)-like aryl hydrocarbon receptor bioactivity in the selected cross-sectional SPES biomonitoring substudy in Campania, Italy. Out of 598 assay records, 591 had quantified PAH-CALUX results and 7 were below individual limits of quantification (LOQs). Primary models related log2 lipid-normalised benzo[a]pyrene-equivalent bioactivity to homocysteine and recorded seated systolic blood pressure (SBP), adjusting for age, sex, body mass index, current smoking, and sampling cluster fixed effects, with municipality-clustered inference. Holm correction covered the two primary tests; Benjamini–Hochberg correction covered two secondary families. Participants comprised 295 women and 296 men aged 20–50 years from 63 municipalities. Per exposure doubling, homocysteine differed by −0.12% (95% confidence interval [CI], −0.76% to 0.52%; Holm-adjusted p = 0.699) and SBP by −0.37 mmHg (95% CI, −0.80 to 0.06; Holm-adjusted p = 0.183). None of the eighteen secondary outcomes met the within-family false discovery rate threshold. Additional post hoc Akins lipid normalisation and three below-LOQ substitution analyses yielded similar interpretations. These findings describe small estimated contemporaneous associations in a selected population. Uncertainty remains concerning cumulative exposure, temporal variability, and generalisability; equivalence and environmental safety cannot be inferred.
