REBOSEP uses hierarchical clustering to uncover shared regulatory patterns among genes, revealing highly diverse expression changes that can shift sharply across just a few cell layers. Using this approach, the study generated the first resource of gene expression across tissue boundaries, covering five brain-meninges boundaries in the developing mouse brain. Analysis of the dorsal pallium-meninges boundary showed specific regulatory patterns in outer brain and meningeal layers, with strong links to developmental processes and distance-dependent regulation in major pathways, including those involved in neurodevelopmental disease and cancer. Functional assays demonstrated that PTTG1 knockdown impaired G2/M checkpoint regulation and reduced gastric cancer cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, whereas its overexpression enhanced organoid growth and altered mucin-related features. Article.Abstract: Cholinergic neurons exhibit functional and molecular heterogeneity across the basal forebrain (BF), midbrain (MB), and brainstem (BS), while the aging-associated transcriptional features remain poorly characterized. BF cells showed greater age-associated transcriptomic alterations than MB and BS cells, with pronounced region-specific divergence among cholinergic neurons. Intercellular communication analysis revealed BF-specific age-related changes in APP and ApoE signaling. Within this altered milieu, intrinsic transcriptional responses varied across brain regions. In aged BF cholinergic neurons, transcriptional responses were characterized by increased oxidative stress and inflammatory signatures and reduced expression of genes involved in neuronal structural maintenance. In contrast, MB and BS cholinergic neurons maintained relatively stable transcriptional profiles. Article.Abstract: We assessed the global burden of rare childhood neurological diseases from 1990 to 2021 and projected trends to 2050 using Global Burden of Disease data, alongside an analysis of the genetic burden from ClinVar. Article.Title: Enabling climate action: A nexus approach for delivering co-benefits across biodiversity, water, food, and health
Article.Authors: Singh P.; Gupta H.; Díaz-José J.; McElwee P.; Tirado M.; Cherubini F.; Duchková H.; Llope M.; Vale M.; Khan S.; Ito A.; Hori M.; Eriksen S.; Tiwari L.; Phang S.; Mason-D’Croz D.; Xu X.; van Huysen T.; Herrero M.; Ricketts T.; Harrison P.; Smith P.
Article.Abstract: Climate response options rarely affect biodiversity, water, food, and health in uniform ways. This comparative analysis examines why technically viable response options generate uneven cross-nexus outcomes, and how governance and justice conditions shape whether these outcomes become durable co-benefits. Anchored in the IPBES Nexus Assessment, the analysis synthesizes evidence from fifteen response options spanning land, ocean, energy, urban, industrial, and societal transitions. Ecosystem-centered and demand-side pathways more consistently produce synergies because they work through ecological functions that connect several nexus elements. Infrastructure- and technology-centered options deliver mitigation and health gains, but their wider effects are more context-dependent and often shaped by land use, water demand, biodiversity risk, tenure, access, and benefit-sharing. These patterns do not arise from technical design alone. By integrating nexus governance with Earth System Justice, the analysis indicates how cross-sectoral coordination, distributive equity, procedural inclusion, accountable finance, and knowledge pluralism can shape legitimacy and durability. Climate action is more likely to deliver sustained system-wide benefits when institutions align ecological interdependencies with social rights and responsibilities. Otherwise, promising interventions may remain partial, contested or short-lived.

Article.Title: Targeting host ferroptosis in cancer cachexia: Tumor-immune triggers, tissue wasting, and the therapeutic paradox
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Chen R.; Ding S.
Article.Abstract: Cancer cachexia is a systemic wasting syndrome driven by tumor burden, chronic inflammation, disrupted nutrient handling, and neuroendocrine stress. Supportive nutrition, exercise, and symptom management rarely restore lean mass, function, or treatment tolerance once wasting is established. Ferroptosis, iron-dependent cell death caused by phospholipid peroxidation, may connect inflammatory iron redistribution, lipid remodeling, mitochondrial stress, and impaired antioxidant defenses. This review critically evaluates ferroptosis in cachexia from a tumor-host pharmacology perspective, distinguishing causal evidence from associated oxidative signatures. We highlight two experimentally supported mechanisms: neutrophil-derived lipocalin-2 in lung cancer cachexia and tumor exosomal miR-203a-3p in pancreatic cancer-associated muscle wasting. We also examine the paradox that tumor ferroptosis induction may weaken host-tissue resistance and worsen muscle and adipose loss. We propose a "split-ferroptosis" strategy combining tumor sensitization with host-protective iron modulation, lipid peroxide scavenging, endogenous defense reinforcement, and biomarker-guided patient selection to expand the tumor-host therapeutic index.

Article.Abstract: Global warming-induced water scarcity threatens agricultural sustainability. This review synthesizes recent advances in the "water-plant-microbe" synergy to propose a bidirectional regulatory mechanism for climate-smart agriculture. We demonstrate that irrigation regimes function as a primary filter for rhizosphere microbial assembly, thereby defining the hydraulic niche for colonization. Conversely, functional microbes actively engineer the soil environment via exopolysaccharide production and hormonal modulation, thereby enhancing plant hydraulic status and water use efficiency (WUE). In contrast to previous reviews focusing on single factors, this review constructs an integrated framework linking soil hydrology with microbial ecology, supported by emerging comparative evidence. We conclude that future agricultural water management must shift from solely regulating water supply to managing the holobiont's hydrological interactions, offering a promising systems-level strategy to safeguard food security under climate stress.

Article.Authors: Guo Y.; Luo Y.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of childhood lower respiratory infections, but updated G20 burden estimates are lacking. Using the Global Burden of Disease 2023 database, we analyzed deaths and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) for RSV-associated lower respiratory infections in children aged 0-14 years across G20 members from 1990 to 2023, with stratification by sex, age, and country. In addition, an illustrative empirical application demonstrates the analytical utility of the dataset for examining associations between land allocation and urban economic development indicators. This dataset provides a comprehensive empirical foundation for future research on land governance, land finance, urban spatial development, and regional transformation in China.

Article.Authors: Sang X.; Dong X.; Bao M.

Article.Title: Offshore wind farm impacts on marine fauna across taxa and ecological levels: A global review
Article.Authors: La Manna G.; Merella M.; Crobu A.; Pansini A.; Ceccherelli G.
Article.Abstract: The expansion of offshore wind farms (OWFs) is central to global decarbonization strategies, yet their effects on marine biodiversity are only partially understood. This systematic review synthesizes 221 publications up to June 2025 to assess the ecological impacts of OWFs on marine fauna living below the sea surface. The evidence base is uneven, heavily focused on North European waters, fish, and invertebrates, while expanding OWF regions and marine mammals remain underrepresented. Most studies examine short-term, individual-level responses, limiting inference on long-term effects. Impacts vary widely by stressor, taxon, and biological outcome. Invertebrates often show positive responses linked to reef effects, though key functional traits are vulnerable. Fish responses are largely neutral except under noise, while marine mammals exhibit the most consistent negative impacts. The impact score developed here highlights taxon-specific vulnerability and offers a scalable risk-assessment tool for data-poor regions. The review calls for standardized, long-term field monitoring to support OWF expansion while safeguarding biodiversity.

Article.Authors: Halling A.; Goodson B.; Hirschmann A.; Wing B.; Simpson C.
Article.Abstract: During the 70-million-year Cryogenian Snowball Earth glaciations, low ocean temperatures beneath global sea ice increased water viscosity over 3-fold. We experimentally tested whether viscosity-induced metabolic constraints could have selected for multicellular phenotypes, potentially driving the origin or early diversification of multicellularity. Under Snowball Earth-like viscosities, populations of unicellular green algae evolved motile multicellular forms, along with other phenotypes that optimize size and speed. As oceans warmed and viscosities decreased, the diversity of multicellular phenotypes may have allowed early multicellular organisms to exert novel physical control over their local environments. This pivotal period in Earth's history could have shaped the emergence and eventual dominance of certain multicellular lineages, highlighting a potential ecological driver of one of life's major evolutionary transitions.

Article.Title: A phase 3 trial of GB-K02 pegfilgrastim biosimilar for preventing chemotherapy-induced neutropenia in breast cancer
Article.Authors: Lin J.; Peng H.; Zhang Y.; Yi Y.; Yang K.; Lin Y.; Li H.; Qin S.
Article.Abstract: Chemotherapy-induced neutropenia (CIN) constitutes a substantial disease burden globally. Although pegfilgrastim (a long-acting granulocyte-colony stimulating factor) has demonstrated efficacy in preventing CIN, it is not yet available in China. This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-controlled, phase 3 equivalence study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of GB-K02 (a pegfilgrastim biosimilar) in preventing CIN among 250 patients with breast cancer. The primary efficacy endpoint was the duration of grade 4 neutropenia (DG4N) in cycle 1 of chemotherapy. Overall, GB-K02 demonstrated proper equivalence to pegfilgrastim and might offer an option in preventing CIN in China.

Article.Title: Diversification and hybridization within the Spirochona gemmipara complex driven by gammarid host range shifts
Article.Authors: Bukovinská K.; Rurik I.; Vd'ačný P.
Article.Abstract: Hybridizing multispecies complexes represent understudied genetic systems within unicellular eukaryotes. Time-calibrated phylogenies indicate that its five main lineages originated in the Miocene through allopatric divergence on isolated European paleoislands colonized independently by freshwater gammarids. Subsequent reconnection of continental freshwater systems following the regression of the Paratethys Sea enabled secondary contact and hybridization among emerging S. gemmipara-like species, with later Pleistocene range shifts likely maintaining compatibility within the syngameon. Discordant mitochondrial signals within the syngameon are consistent with heteroplasmy and may also reflect phylogenetic noise or nuclear mitochondrial pseudogenes (NUMTs), and only tentatively suggest the possibility of mitogenome recombination. Article.Title: Context shapes action understanding in social interactions
Article.Authors: Keck J.; Sato K.; Cañal-Bruland R.
Article.Abstract: In social interactions, individuals anticipate what others are about to do next, enabling smooth social interactions and coexistence in daily life. Article.Title: Intelligent immunotherapy: AI-driven optimization of CAR-T therapy in hematologic malignancies
Article.Authors: Farhadzadeh F.; Borji A.; Aram C.; Alishvandi A.; Kamali M.; Rahimi M.
Article.Abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has transformed outcomes in selected hematologic malignancies, yet its delivery remains constrained by variable efficacy, acute and prolonged toxicities, and complex manufacturing logistics. Artificial intelligence (AI) is being applied across the CAR-T continuum at three distinct levels of evidentiary maturity. Externally validated parsimonious models built on routine clinical and laboratory data including CAR-HEMATOTOX, endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) and m-EASIX, MyCARe, and gradient-boosting cytokine release syndrome predictors provide deployable risk stratification today. Methodologically sophisticated tools using deep-learning positron emission tomography (PET) segmentation, attention-based digital-pathology analysis, and multimodal fusion of imaging with laboratory and circulating tumor DNA features have demonstrated technical promise but generally lack the multi-center external validation required for clinical-grade deployment. Forward-looking applications, including digital-twin frameworks, large language models, and closed-loop adaptive therapy, remain at the prototype stage and have not yet been validated for CAR-T. This review synthesizes these three tiers, summarizes 18 published AI and statistical-modeling tools in a comparative performance table, and compares data characteristics and AI modeling paradigms across large B cell lymphoma, B cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and multiple myeloma. We also identify the implementation realities-absent regulatory clearance, demographic and racial bias in training data, and post-deployment model drift-that condition the field's evolution. The contribution of AI to CAR-T therapy, as the evidence currently stands, is the calibrated quantification of established risk factors rather than the discovery of novel biology, but the methodological and data infrastructure foundations are now in place for the broader transformation that the next decade may enable.

Article.Abstract: Polyvinyl acetate (PVAc) is a highly polar, fluorine-free polymeric adhesive that combines strong interfacial adhesion with good processability. Despite this, PVAc has rarely been investigated as an active layer in mechano-electric nanogenerators, even though its strong adhesion facilitates effective interfacial contact, thereby eliminating the need for auxiliary conductive layers. Electrical measurements revealed that the electrical output of PVAc arises from the interplay of triboelectric charge transfer, electrostatic induction driven by residual polarization, and deformation-induced interfacial polarization. Article.Title: Climate change and sexual and reproductive health: A mixed methods scoping review of possible mechanisms
Article.Authors: Vahedi L.; Pradhan S.; Zaidi S.; Brizuela V.; Rashid S.; El Adawy M.; Hajjeh R.; Gaffey M.; Bhutta Z.
Article.Abstract: This scoping review synthesized empirical evidence on the relationships and possible pathways through which climate change could impact sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Eligible sources had to investigate climate change and SRHR using any study design. We identified 14 potential pathways and developed a typology of mediators and contextual moderators to inform the mechanisms. Five mediator domains were identified: (1) systems and infrastructure, (2) demographic shifts, (3) socioeconomic resources, and (4) behavioral and (5) biological. Article.Abstract: Neutrophil granule release is critical for host defense, yet its dysregulation underpins cytokine release syndrome (CRS) in both acute (such as sepsis) and sustained inflammatory states. Article.Abstract: Bone organoids offer three-dimensional systems for studying skeletal development, disease, and regeneration. Article.Authors: Castaldi E.; Anobile G.; Marazzi M.; Federici S.; Angelelli P.; Turi M.
Article.Abstract: Geometry is fundamental to mathematical thinking, yet its foundations and difficulties in learning disorders remain poorly understood. Article.Authors: Tang X.; Xu H.; Liu X.; Yang Y.; Li Z.
Article.Abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic disease affecting the entire joint, influenced by a combination of inflammatory, metabolic, immune, and environmental factors. Article.Abstract: To overcome physiological constraints during submergence, many air-breathing aquatic animals utilize an air store. Using a deep autoencoder, AE_EPI captures complex nonlinear relationships in high-dimensional, multi-region data and is benchmarked against a principal component analysis-based index (PCA_EPI). Linear Regression, Random Forest (RF), and XGBoost, combined with SHAP analysis, are used to identify key environmental drivers. Results show that AE_EPI outperforms PCA_EPI in reconstruction accuracy, stability, and robustness to noise, while RF yields the most consistent predictions. Globally, electricity access and renewable energy are the dominant drivers. Regionally, governance and innovation are most important in East Asia; urbanization in South Asia; renewable energy in Central Asia; digitalization in MENA; and economic capacity, electricity access, and governance in Sub-Saharan Africa. These findings support region-specific, data-driven policies that advance energy transitions, strengthen institutional capacity, and address local environmental priorities for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals.

Article.Title: β motifs and molecular flux promote fibril growth at condensate interfaces
Article.Authors: Biswas S.; Potoyan D.
Article.Abstract: Biomolecular condensates can age into gel-like or solid-like states, and their interfaces can promote amyloid fibril formation. Article.Authors: Joung J.; Na H.; Yoon S.; Jeong Y.; Lee M.; Majidi C.; Kim H.

Article.Abstract: Intergroup conflict poses asymmetric strategic demands: acquiring resources through offense benefits from behavior that opponents cannot easily anticipate, whereas protecting resources through defense requires monitoring opponents and adjusting to threats. These strategies aligned with sex-differentiated behavioral patterns: male participants showed greater variability and performed better in offense, whereas female participants showed stronger tracking and performed better in defense. Article.Title: Bridging soil resistome and clinical inference: A four-tier evidentiary framework

Article.Abstract: Soils support a varied range of microbial communities and are important repositories of antimicrobial resistance genes. This review contends that better clinical inference requires tying presence-based signals to function, mobility, and exposure routes, rather than just increasing survey volume. We offer a four-tiered evidentiary paradigm that distinguishes between detection, functional or expression-based evidence, mobile genetic element context, and exposure-linked evidence in environmental, animal, and human compartments. Article.Title: Senescence and tumor immunology: A multifaceted interplay of influence
Article.Authors: Xie Y.; Zhang J.; Wang S.; Rao D.; Zhang J.; Ao Y.
Article.Abstract: Medical advances and global population aging have propelled aging and cancer research into a new period of discovery. Senescent cells, which exert context-dependent tumor-suppressive and tumor-promoting effects, are central to this progress and engage in complex crosstalk with tumor proliferation. This review critically examines the multidimensional interplay between aging and cancer by synthesizing genetic, cytokine signaling, and tissue microenvironment evidence. We discuss how senescent cells influence immune surveillance, therapy response, tumor progression, metastasis, and age-related cancer risk, while cellular diversity, molecular complexity, immune balance, tumor heterogeneity, treatment resistance, and individual aging variability further complicate this relationship. We conclude that aging and cancer are intertwined through dynamic, context-specific mechanisms. By integrating these insights, this review aims to inspire novel research directions and transformative advances in cancer therapy and healthy longevity.

Article.Title: Distinct electrophysiological correlates of low- and high-level visual consciousness with minimized post-perceptual processing
Article.Authors: Hense A.; Peters A.; Dellert T.; Bruchmann M.; Straube T.
Article.Abstract: Conscious visual phenomenology comprises multiple representational levels, from basic features to integrated percepts, raising the question of how the neural correlates of consciousness (NCC) differentiate accordingly. Event-related potential (ERP) studies identified early occipitotemporal negativities as reliable NCC; yet, it remains unclear whether these capture conscious content beyond low-level features and extend to higher-order representations. Moreover, whether later ERP components index higher-level conscious percepts independent of task-related processing remains contested. The present study addresses this question using an inattentional blindness (IB) paradigm that isolates three representational levels of conscious perception (no, low- or high-level awareness) for an identical stimulus under minimized post-perceptual processing. Across 85 healthy participants, low-level line perception was indexed by an enhanced early occipital negativity, whereas high-level face perception additionally recruited a right-lateralized occipitotemporal negativity, followed by medial posterior positivities. These findings reveal systematic spatiotemporal differentiation of awareness-related potentials across representational levels of consciousness under task-irrelevant conditions.

Article.Title: Longitudinal associations of screen time with brain development and expressive language skills in early childhood

Article.Abstract: Screen-based media may reduce reciprocal social interactions that support expressive language development, but little is known about how early language abilities, later screen use, and brain structure are related during toddlerhood. Greater weekday and weekend screen time at age 2 were associated with poorer concurrent expressive language skills. Right pars triangularis volume did not explain additional variance in these cross-sectional associations. Longitudinally, right pars triangularis volume moderated the association between expressive language skills at age 2 and screen time at age 3. Among toddlers with relatively smaller right pars triangularis volumes, poorer expressive language skills were associated with greater subsequent weekday and weekend screen time. These findings support guidance to limit screen use during toddlerhood, a sensitive window for language and brain development.

Article.Title: Paleogenomics reveals leprosy at the late antique burial site of Fallward in northern Germany
Article.Authors: Myburgh D.; da Silva N.; Romeyer-Dherbey J.; Grefen-Peters S.; Jöns H.; Peek C.; Nebel A.; Krause-Kyora B.
Article.Abstract: The coastal settlement of Fallward in northwestern Germany (3rd-5th century CE) is renowned for exceptionally preserved wooden and textile grave goods, yet the genetic and pathogen landscape of its inhabitants has remained unstudied. We conducted metagenomic analyses on skeletal samples from 11 individuals to investigate their genetic affinities and infectious disease history. Three individuals yielded sufficient data for population genetic analysis: two clustered with northwestern European Iron Age and Anglo-Saxon groups, while one adult male might have originated from a Roman frontier population. This man was also infected with a strain of Mycobacterium leprae belonging to phylogenetic branch 4 and was buried in a boat accompanied by Roman-influenced grave goods, including carved furniture and a military belt. Together, these findings point to possible long-distance connections linking remote communities, such as Fallward, to the wider Roman world during Late Antiquity.

Article.Title: A hierarchical framework of representational emergence: From feature binding to supramodal emergence
Article.Authors: Paraskevopoulos E.; Bamidis P.
Article.Abstract: Multisensory integration is traditionally conceptualized as transient, stimulus-driven feature binding. Here, we propose a hierarchical framework that reconceptualizes multisensory processing as a continuum of representational emergence across three distinct levels: level I (multimodal binding), where features are integrated via probabilistic causal inference; level II (supramodal representation), where recurrent co-activation and value-guided selection establish consolidated, perceptual-semantic engrams that act as emergent modalities; and level III (amodal concepts), where meaning becomes increasingly detached from sensory form and is represented within transmodal semantic networks. Drawing on recent mammalian evidence for cross-modal associative memory neurons and experience-dependent network reorganization, this framework proposes how local synaptic selection may scale into increasingly autonomous cognitive modules. Finally, we delineate an empirical roadmap and outline implications for supramodal AI, toward architectures capable of more autonomous semantic representation and generation.

Here, we leverage a uracil-DNA-specific labeling assay, originally developed for modern DNA, to evaluate whether extracts contain ancient DNA molecules. Article.Title: Evidence for climate-mediated range expansion of hybrid wood ants
Article.Authors: Krapf P.; Heidbreder P.; Bruijning M.; Meirmans P.; Stankowski S.; Kulmuni J.
Article.Abstract: Climate change challenges many species. To persist, species can shift ranges, respond plastically, and adapt, which all require variation. Hybridization can quickly increase genetic variation, potentially facilitating climate adaptation; however, it is unclear how hybrids respond to climatic changes. Article.Abstract: Meniere disease (MD) is a rare inner ear disorder with a significant genetic contribution. Article.Title: Cortical substrates of perceptual confusion between pitch and timbre
Article.Authors: Ou Y.; Allen E.; Kay K.; Oxenham A.
Article.Abstract: Pitch and timbre, two fundamental perceptual attributes of sound, are critical for both speech and music. Although governed by different acoustic parameters, pitch, and brightness (one of the primary dimensions of timbre) can be perceptually confused. Here, we identify potential neural substrates of this well-known illusion by independently manipulating pitch and brightness while measuring fMRI responses. First, we show that the preferred pitch of individual voxels within auditory cortex decreases systematically as stimulus brightness increases, and vice versa, consistent with predictions from perceptual confusion. Second, we demonstrate that pitch and brightness share a common tuning gradient across auditory cortex, implying a shared trajectory of cortical activation for changes in each dimension. The pattern of results at both local and global cortical levels are consistent with the principle of efficient coding, with the brain exploiting correlations between pitch and brightness in natural sounds via a shared neural code.

Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Feng X.; Xu X.
Article.Abstract: To date, experimental development biology still faces challenges to efficiently model the morphogenesis of cross-species vertebrates, spanning from the embryonic development to postnatal growth. Article.Abstract: Ischemic stroke triggers profound, dynamic changes in the brain's cellular landscape. To systematically characterize these dynamics, we integrated single-cell RNA-sequencing data from 21 mouse stroke studies (103 samples; 414,359 cells) spanning multiple models and post-stroke intervals. Using a harmonized computational workflow, we constructed StrokeTime, a single-cell mouse brain atlas covering hyperacute, acute, subacute, and chronic stages post-ischemia. The atlas contains 17 major cell classes and 120 fine-grained transcriptional states within myeloid, lymphoid, vascular, epithelial, neuronal, and glial populations. Myeloid cells showed the greatest plasticity, including disease-associated microglia/macrophage programs shared across resident and infiltrating cells, whereas lymphocytes featured activation and regulatory signatures within lineage constraints. Vascular and mural cells shifted from early inflammatory and barrier-disruptive programs to later fibrotic and angiogenic states. StrokeTime delineates both convergent and cell type-specific injury responses, offering a resource for studying post-ischemic brain immunity, tissue remodeling, and benchmarking future single-cell and single-nucleus studies of cerebrovascular disease.

Article.Title: Factor H polymorphism elevates granzyme B and impairs complement inhibition in human and mouse models
Article.Authors: Chakravarthy H.; Xi J.; Yoo H.; Buss A.; Li B.; Bell R.; Haegert A.; Le Bihan S.; Granville D.; Matsubara J.
Article.Abstract: The complement factor H (CFH) Y402H polymorphism is a leading genetic risk factor for age-related macular degeneration (AMD). Here, we identify extracellular granzyme B (GzmB) as a crucial mediator connecting complement dysregulation to structural pathology. Using in vitro human retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells, we demonstrate that complement fragment C5a triggers GzmB secretion and zonula occludens-1 disruption. RNA sequencing of GzmB-stimulated RPE cells confirmed transcriptomic signatures of barrier dysfunction and cellular stress. Furthermore, GzmB-deficient mice displayed preserved choroidal vitronectin compared with wild-type controls, supporting a role for GzmB in cleaving this terminal complement inhibitor. These findings delineate a pathogenic C5a-GzmB pathway compromising extracellular matrix integrity, implicating extracellular GzmB as a critical downstream mediator linking genetic risk to early AMD onset.

Article.Title: Screening colorectal tumor-associated fibroblasts using dual-channel THz biosensor
Article.Authors: Xu H.; Gu R.; Serville Torvund A.; Grønlien I.; Xomalis A.; Nguyen H.; Yu Z.; Zhao Z.
Article.Abstract: In clinical oncology, label-free identification of colorectal tumor-associated fibroblast (CAF) subtypes is challenging. In this work, a terahertz (THz) metasurface exhibiting dual channels of probation, quasi-bound states in the continuum (q-BICs) and electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT), is used to screen CAF subtypes in colorectal tumors. When impinging light is polarized along x axis, the pro-tumorigenic myofibroblasts (myCAFs) cause frequency red-shift of q-BIC resonances compared to intestinal epithelial cells, while anti-tumorigenic antigen-presenting CAFs (apCAFs) result in blueshift. Similarly, for EIT modes, when light is polarized along the orthogonal polarization, myCAFs result in a frequency red-shift while apCAFs result in blueshift. These frequency shifts are attributed to the dielectric environment variation due to the surface hall-marks of CAFs. To validate our results, we conducted flow cytometry and gene expression analyses that confirmed distinct hallmarks of myCAFs and apCAFs, consistent with the resonance frequency shifts observed in THz metasurface measurements. Our findings demonstrate a label-free and cost-effective method for screening CAF subtypes using two-parameters-q-BICs and EIT-which can help speed up cancer diagnosis.

Article.Title: IgM monoclonal antibodies reduce IgG-mediated antibody-dependent enhancement of Zika and dengue virus infectivity
Article.Authors: Lingemann M.; McGee T.; Sidoti Migliore G.; DeLuca J.; Whitehead S.; Bonsignori M.
Article.Abstract: Zika virus (ZIKV) is an arthropod-borne flavivirus endemic to Latin America, Africa, and Southeast Asia for which IgG-mediated antibody-dependent enhancement of infectivity (ADE) is a phenomenon of concern. The dynamics between flavivirus-specific antibodies of the IgG and IgM isotypes are mostly unknown. Here, we used DH1017.IgM, a previously described human-derived, pentameric, ultrapotent neutralizing ZIKV IgM monoclonal antibody (mAb) and a recombinantly produced IgM version of neutralizing EDE1 mAb C8 (C8.IgM) to assess if IgM antibodies can interfere with IgG-mediated ADE in vitro. Both mAbs consistently reduced IgG-mediated ADE across a panel of ZIKV-binding IgG mAbs in a dose-dependent manner. ADE mitigation was achieved at DH1017.IgM sub-neutralizing concentrations. C8.IgM also mitigated IgG-mediated ADE for ZIKV and dengue virus (DENV), demonstrating generalizability. Finally, DH1017.IgM confirmed inhibition of ADE at sub-neutralizing concentrations in sera of ZIKV-infected individuals. In conclusion, mAbs of the IgM isotype may potently counter the adverse effects of IgG-mediated ADE.

Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Zhan J.; Mao W.; Han X.; Chen Y.; Chen J.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Type 2 diabetes is characterized by impaired glucose homeostasis and progressive pancreatic β cell dysfunction, highlighting the need for externally controllable strategies for metabolic regulation. Here, we combined low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) with the mechanosensitive channel MscL-G22S to establish a tunable sonogenetic system for glucose regulation. Graded ultrasound stimulation was evaluated in MscL-G22S-expressing β cells and diabetic db/db mice to define an effective acoustic dose range. Within an intermediate dose window, LIPUS increased intracellular Ca2+ levels and glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in vitro and improved glycemic control, insulin sensitivity, islet morphology, and systemic metabolic profiles in vivo. Serum metabolomics further identified metabolic pathway alterations associated with combined LIPUS and MscL-G22S activation. These findings establish a quantitative framework for relating ultrasound dose to sonogenetic metabolic responses and support further investigation of ultrasound-controlled regulation of glucose homeostasis.

Article.Title: Contralateral delay activity during dynamic spatial updates in working memory
Article.Authors: Chernik C.; van den Berg R.; Lundqvist M.
Article.Abstract: Working memory (WM) enables us to maintain and directly manipulate mental representations, yet we know little about the neural implementation of this privileged online format. We recorded electroencephalography data as human subjects engaged in a task requiring continuous updates to the locations of objects retained in WM as well as in a visually identical task with WM demands removed. Analysis of neural data suggested WM-related contralateral delay activity reversed polarity as objects held in WM moved to the opposite hemifield. The control task suggested this was partially but not fully explained by visual attention demands. Thus, the spatial location of activity related to both attention and WM was updated to meet behavioral demands as the spatial location of remembered objects changed.

Furthermore, SGK1 inhibition reduced TGF-β1-induced SMAD2/3 phosphorylation. Therapeutic administration of EMD638683, initiated after disease establishment, significantly ameliorated BO pathology. These findings demonstrate that SGK1 promotes BO-associated fibrosis through TGF-β1-mediated EMT and ECM deposition, identifying SGK1 as a potential therapeutic target for post-transplant BO intervention.

Article.Authors: Ding J.; Samvelian D.; Ying Z.; Diamante G.; Ahn I.; Palafox-Sanchez V.; Wang S.; Gomez-Pinilla F.; Yang X.

Article.Title: Early-warning signals of critical transitions in global ecoregions
Article.Authors: Hirsch E.; Koren I.
Article.Abstract: Terrestrial ecoregions represent coherent ecological units shaped by shared environmental conditions and biological communities. As ecosystems approach critical transitions, their resilience declines, showing slower recovery from perturbations and increasing temporal autocorrelation. Here, we analyze 22 years of global satellite vegetation data to detect early warning signals of structural ecological change across all terrestrial ecoregions. By combining spatial clustering, vegetation trend analysis, and resilience indicators, we identify ecoregions exhibiting both vegetation change and declining resilience. We find that approximately one-quarter of ecoregions, covering over one-third of Earth's land surface, show consistent signals of emerging structural transitions. Many of these occur in regions with low direct human modification, suggesting a strong role for large-scale environmental drivers. The detected patterns reveal increasing internal fragmentation within ecoregions and highlight regions potentially approaching critical transitions. This framework provides a scalable approach for identifying ecosystems at risk and supports targeted monitoring and conservation planning.

Article.Authors: Li H.; Zhang J.; Liu Z.; Li J.; Yin X.; Li H.; Lu Y.; Xu Q.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Ischemic heart disease (IHD), ischemic stroke (IS), type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), and lower-extremity vascular disease are leading causes of disability in Western Europe and North America, but their diet-attributable burden remains unclear. By 2023, Western Europe had a lower burden than North America. Processed meat and whole grain dominated T2DM and IHD burden, respectively. Joinpoint analysis revealed declining trends. Projections to 2035 indicated North America remains higher. MR identified several potential causal links. This study provides a basis for vascular/metabolic disease prevention policies and dietary interventions in Western Europe and North America.

Article.Title: Periodontitis as a potential contributor to lung cancer: Epidemiological evidence, proposed mechanisms, and clinical implications
Article.Authors: Dong H.; Xin H.
Article.Abstract: Periodontitis has been proposed as a potential contributor to lung cancer (LC), but the epidemiological, mechanistic, and clinical evidence remains heterogeneous. The absence of a clear association among lifelong never smokers and the lack of supportive Mendelian randomization evidence further limit causal inference. Human studies demonstrate oral-lower airway microbial overlap, while experimental LC models support microbiota-related inflammatory and oncogenic signaling; however, periodontal origin, directional microbial transmission, and a continuous causal pathway from periodontitis to LC have not been established. Clinically, periodontitis should not modify current eligibility for low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) screening, and oral or respiratory microbiome biomarkers remain investigational. Perioperative oral care has comparatively stronger evidence for reducing postoperative pulmonary infectious complications, but this benefit should not be extrapolated to tumor recurrence or survival. Overall, current evidence supports an observational association and biological plausibility, whereas independent causality and an oncologic benefit of periodontal treatment remain unproven.

Chitosan structurally stabilizes the fibers while modulating swelling and local pH to enhance Ag+ diffusion. The dressings achieved >99.9999% bacterial reduction in vitro and up to 99% ex vivo using freshly excised human skin. Crucially, the dressings maintained >90% viability of human keratinocytes and fibroblasts and showed no detectable impairment of short-term wound healing. Article.Abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the loss of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra. Article.Title: A single arm phase II trial of chidamide plus cisplatin in advanced adenoid cystic carcinoma

Patients received a short chidamide lead-in followed by combination therapy for up to six cycles. The study did not meet its prespecified objective response target, with a confirmed objective response rate of 13.6% among 22 efficacy-evaluable patients. However, disease control was observed in 86.4% of patients, median progression-free survival was 17.9 months, and median overall survival was 40.3 months. Toxicity was manageable, with no treatment-related deaths. Article.Title: FDX1 suppresses acute myeloid leukemia progression and reverses cuproptosis resistance via the ROS/p53/ME1 axis
Article.Authors: Yao L.; Zhong F.; Bai Q.; Zeng H.; Qiu Y.; Yao F.; Xu Y.; Zhang J.; Lin J.; Deng K.; Huang B.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: Cuproptosis, a copper-dependent cell death mechanism, holds therapeutic potential in cancer, yet its regulatory pathways in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) remain poorly defined. We demonstrate that elevated serum copper levels correlate with poor prognosis in AML patients. Screening reveals that ferredoxin 1 (FDX1) is significantly downregulated in AML and associated with adverse outcomes. FDX1 loss promoted AML cell proliferation and cuproptosis resistance. Mechanistically, FDX1 enhanced mitochondrial damage and ROS/p53 signaling, which transcriptionally suppressed malic enzyme 1 (ME1). ME1 disrupted mitochondrial NAD + /NADH homeostasis and modulated lipoylated DLAT delipoylation, thereby limiting cuproptosis. ME1 was highly expressed in AML and supported leukemic cell growth, while its inhibition restored cuproptosis sensitivity in FDX1-low cells. Given the elevated serum copper levels in AML and the capacity of ME1 inhibition to reverse cuproptosis resistance induced by low FDX1 expression, the combination of copper ionophores with ME1 inhibitors may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for AML.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: cuproptosis; acute myeloid leukemia; p53 pathway; ME1; reactive oxygen species; FDX1; copper ionophores; serum copper; dihydrolipoamide acetyltransferase

Article.Title: Pre-season bare-soil spectral proxies complement pod-filling canopy indices for field-scale soybean-yield prediction from UAV imagery
Article.Authors: Zhao Y.; Tian Z.; Ma R.; Liang Y.
Article.Abstract: Field-scale soybean-yield models based on canopy imagery may miss soil-surface variation. We evaluated a two-flight drone framework combining pre-season bare-soil and pod-filling multispectral imagery at 101 locations in four slope units in Northeast China. Five random-forest scenarios were compared using nested feature selection and repeated outer-test evaluation. Adding the bare-soil proxy pool to pod-filling vegetation indices increased mean outer-test predictive R 2 from 0.240 to 0.325 and reduced mean absolute error from 573.06 to 518.76 kg ha −1 ; this error decreased in all 10 repeats. Model attribution showed contributions from canopy and bare-soil predictors. Predictions overestimated low yields and underestimated high yields. For this combined scenario, pooled predictive R 2 declined to 0.161 when each slope unit was excluded from model development. Pre-season bare-soil imagery therefore provided modest complementary information beyond a pod-filling acquisition, but the framework remains a field-scale proof of concept requiring multi-year and multi-site validation.

Article.Title: Neural substrates related to memory consolidation of learning multiple motor sequences during wakeful rest
Article.Authors: Yoon S.; Caraballo A.; Kim S.
Article.Abstract: Motor learning has long been considered independent of the hippocampus, but recent evidence suggests that the hippocampus contributes to motor memory consolidation during wakeful rest. However, whether hippocampal reactivation supports consolidation during interleaved rest remains unclear. We investigated the fMRI evidence of motor memory consolidation of learning multiple motor sequences during wakeful rest. We found that while sensorimotor regions exhibited sequence-specific activity patterns during practice, these were not reliably discriminable in the sensorimotor regions and hippocampus during interleaved rest. In contrast, neural activity patterns in the right hippocampus, right putamen, and sensorimotor regions during interleaved rest showed greater similarity to post-learning rest patterns than pre-learning rest patterns. These findings suggest that under highly interfering, multi-sequence learning conditions, the consolidation of motor memories may not be related to a specific sequence but may instead reflect a generalized or abstract representation of sequences, potentially to stabilize and minimize interference among newly acquired skills.

Article.Title: HelixWings enables AI-driven enzyme engineering for biomimetic cofactor utilization
Article.Authors: Zhang C.; Feng Y.; Ji Y.; Rong M.; Zhang R.; Yuan Z.; Shen H.; Tong T.; Miao T.; Fang B.; Tong L.; Fang W.; Wang Z.; Wei H.; Gao B.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: Biomimetic nicotinamide cofactors, such as nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMNH), can substantially reduce synthesis costs compared with natural cofactors like nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate (NADPH). However, natural enzymes generally exhibit poor activity with these alternative cofactors. Existing engineering approaches, including directed evolution and rational design, remain limited by experimental uncertainty or computational complexity. Here, we developed HelixWings, an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven screening platform that integrates conformational dynamics analysis with static microenvironment analysis to identify enzyme variants compatible with biomimetic cofactors. Applied to P450BM3, a widely used biocatalyst for chiral synthesis and pharmaceutical precursor production, HelixWings identified a variant with a 404% improvement in catalytic efficiency toward cytochrome c under NMNH-supported conditions. The platform was further validated with CYP116B46, achieving a 217% improvement in NMNH utilization efficiency. HelixWings reduced screening time by 23-fold compared with rational design.

Article.Title: Metabolic regulation of ATM-KAT8-RPA1 axis in DNA damage repair and chemoresistance
Article.Authors: Ding X.; Yang J.; Wu J.; Jin M.; Wang Z.; Yang X.; Wang X.; Song Y.; Huang B.; Li R.; Li Y.; He Y.; Zheng W.; Wang Q.; Zeng Z.; Chen Y.; Yuan J.
Article.Abstract: Post-translational modifications are recognized as critical regulators of the DNA damage response. In this study, we determined that replication protein A1 (RPA1), a modulator of homologous recombination (HR) repair, is lactylated at lysine 167 (K167) in response to DNA damage. This modification is catalyzed by the histone acetyltransferase KAT8 and is dependent on ATM-mediated phosphorylation of KAT8. Lactylation at K167 enhances the DNA-binding capacity of RPA1, which in turn facilitates HR repair. The inhibition of KAT8 or lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), which increases intracellular lactate level, markedly reduces RPA1 lactylation, impairs HR repair, and increases the sensitivity of tumor cells to chemotherapy in patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models. Furthermore, a cell-penetrating peptide (CPP) that selectively disrupts this modification can sensitize tumors to genotoxic treatment. These findings establish RPA1 lactylation as a critical regulator of HR repair and reveal a potential therapeutic strategy in which this modification can be targeted to overcome chemoresistance.

Article.Title: An engineered α-1,3-glucanase-derived probe enables sensitive detection of α-1,3-glucan and reveals its soluble release by Aspergillus
Article.Authors: Suzuki K.; Kimura M.; Miyazawa K.; Adachi Y.; Yamanaka D.
Article.Abstract: α-1,3-Glucan is a major component of the Aspergillus cell wall. However, unlike β-1,3-glucan and galactomannan, α-1,3-glucan was not previously considered to be released in a soluble form. Therefore, its potential as a diagnostic biomarker has remained largely unexplored. In this study, we engineered α-1,3-glucanase mutants to develop α-1,3-glucan-specific binding proteins and detection systems. Mutants derived from the endo-type α-1,3-glucanases, AGN1 and AglKA, were generated, among which AglKA-CatD-D1090A lacked enzymatic activity but retained strong binding affinity for α-1,3-glucan. Using this probe, we established a split luciferase assay to detect α-1,3-glucan in Aspergillus hyphae and conidia without prior purification. Soluble α-1,3-glucan was substantially released by major Aspergillus species, as indicated by results of a sandwich ELISA-like assay with AglKA mutants. These findings suggest that soluble α-1,3-glucan has potential as a complementary diagnostic biomarker for aspergillosis.

Article.Title: Fault diagnosis of rotating machinery under imbalanced samples based on outlier-removal HCAB-SMOTE-LOF
Article.Authors: Liao Z.; Yan Z.; Jia B.; Song X.
Article.Abstract: In rotating machinery fault diagnosis, the original feature space often suffers from anomalous outliers, limited sample availability, and imbalanced class distributions. These issues significantly impede the accurate recognition of minority-class samples and lead to suboptimal diagnostic efficiency. To tackle these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid method of HCAB-SMOTE-LOF for diagnosing imbalanced fault diagnosis under outlier contamination. The core idea is not a simple combination of Local Outlier Factor (LOF) and Hybrid Clustering Affinity Synthesis Minority oversampling technique (HCAB-SMOTE), but a coupling mechanism in which LOF-based majority-class purification constrains the boundary region of HCAB-SMOTE, so that synthetic samples are generated in reliable minority-class clusters. To extract the fault-relevant time-frequency features, high-pass filtering is applied to the raw vibration signals to remove low-frequency components. The LOF is introduced to eliminate samples that are clearly abnormal or mislabeled in the feature space. On this basis, the HCAB-SMOTE algorithm is employed to synthetically generate minority-class fault samples, thereby improving the quality and distributional plausibility of the generated samples and alleviating the adverse impact of data imbalance on classifier performance. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated using both a laboratory dataset and the Ottawa motor dataset. Furthermore, a comparative analysis is conducted between the proposed method and several oversampling strategies applied during data processing, including the use of original data, SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, and HCAB-SMOTE. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms all existing oversampling methods across all evaluation metrics, confirming its marked advantages in outlier removal and sample-distribution optimization and thus its capability to effectively detect rotating machinery faults.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: rotating machinery fault diagnosis; outlier removal; time-frequency features; LOF; class imbalance; minority class samples; SMOTE; oversampling
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Control and Systems Engineering > Machine Fault Diagnosis Techniques; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Imbalanced Data Classification Techniques; Engineering > Control and Systems Engineering > Fault Detection and Control Systems

Article.Title: Recurrent latent dynamics in spinal circuits enable a digital twin of autonomic state transitions
Article.Authors: Choo M.; Cho M.; Lee J.; Oh C.; Hong S.; Heo C.; Shon Y.; Park S.
Article.Abstract: Physiological signals underlying homeostasis, such as blood pressure, are dynamic and nonlinear, shaped by interactions among diverse neurons. In the spinal intermediolateral nucleus (IML), neurons show heterogeneous, monotonic firing changes during blood pressure transitions, intrinsic to control yet difficult to decode. We introduce a manifold-based model reconstructing internal state dynamics from IML activity, beyond prior descriptive frameworks. Brief spinal stimulation lowering blood pressure showed that single-neuron responses could not explain the nonlinear trajectory, so we derived a low-dimensional circular manifold capturing its cyclical evolution. Embedding the manifold as a dynamic reservoir in a recurrent neural network reconstructed trial-to-trial variability and nonlinear blood pressure dynamics generated by the manifold, without a readout. Our results establish the neural manifold as a generative computational substrate for autonomic physiology, a capability that remains largely unexplored in spinal circuits, and a step toward closed-loop spinal neuromodulation.
Article.Topic: Heart Rate Variability and Autonomic Control

Article.Title: Design, modeling, and validation of a computer-vision-enabled 3D-printed soft robotic glove for stroke telerehabilitation
Article.Authors: Tawk C.; Saab G.; Abdallah G.; El Khoury J.; Aouad R.
Article.Abstract: Post-stroke rehabilitation for upper-limb mobility faces challenges such as limited availability, high costs, and insufficient insurance coverage. This work addresses these challenges by integrating soft robotics with computer vision. A lightweight soft robotic glove (159 g), featuring five three-dimensional (3D)-printed soft pneumatic actuators that function as fingers, is designed and optimized using finite element modeling (FEM) in terms of bending behavior and force output. The fingers demonstrated durability, bending deformation repeatability, force repeatability, and reliable holding force capability. The proof-of-concept system comprises a wearable robotic glove for the patient and a computer vision interface for the therapist. The therapist performs hand gestures captured by a camera to control the glove through the computer vision interface. The soft robotic glove and integrated computer vision interface were experimentally validated on healthy participants. This validation demonstrates the feasibility of controlling the glove using computer vision and its potential for future telerehabilitation applications.

Article.Title: Therapeutic HPV16 E7 vaccination with CD137 agonism induces tumor regression and durable immunity in mice
Article.Authors: Ou Y.; Lu W.; Zhao H.; Demetrious C.; Zhang Q.; Zheng Q.; Jiang Y.; Kok-Ting Wan P.; O’Neill E.; Zhang L.; Jiang S.
Article.Abstract: Prophylactic human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines prevent new infections but do not treat established HPV-associated lesions, highlighting the need for therapeutic strategies targeting viral tumor antigens. We developed a recombinant overlapping peptide-based HPV16 E7 vaccine (ROP-E7) and evaluated its immunogenicity and antitumor activity, alone or combined with CD137 (4-1BB) agonism, in C57BL/6 mice. In tumor-free mice, ROP-E7 induced greater helper and cytotoxic T cell responses than wild-type E7. In tumor-bearing mice, ROP-E7 reduced tumor burden and improved survival, while combination treatment induced complete tumor regression and tumor-free survival beyond 100 days. These effects were associated with increased intratumoral cytotoxic T cells and reduced regulatory and exhausted T cell populations. These findings provide preclinical support for combining therapeutic HPV16 E7 vaccination with T cell co-stimulation in HPV-associated cancers.

Article.Title: Efficacy and safety of trans-fornix conjunctival retrobulbar block in a prospective randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Chen R.; Xu T.; Chen C.; Liu K.; Shi G.; Xi C.; Yin M.; Chen R.; Hu K.; Chen B.
Article.Abstract: Retrobulbar block is widely used for vitreoretinal surgery, but the conventional transcutaneous technique advances a sharp needle blindly through the lower eyelid. We evaluated a trans -fornix conjunctival approach in which a curved blunt-tip needle is advanced into the muscle cone under the operating microscope. In a two-center randomized trial, 196 patients were stratified by expected surgical duration and allocated to the transcutaneous or the trans -fornix technique, and pain was graded at predefined procedural stages. The trans -fornix approach reduced pain during anesthetic injection in both cohorts and during scleral indentation in longer procedures, and fewer patients required supplemental anesthesia. Ocular akinesia was better with the trans -fornix technique, and periorbital hemorrhage and ecchymosis occurred only in the transcutaneous group. These findings support the trans -fornix block as a practical and reproducible option for regional anesthesia in vitreoretinal surgery.

Article.Title: Temporal patterns of melanopsin-evoked calcium signaling engage NF-κB-associated transcriptional and phosphoproteomic responses
Article.Authors: Nikpour P.; Varas-Godoy M.; Tenghamn J.; Uhlén P.; Smedler E.
Article.Abstract: Cells use oscillatory calcium (Ca 2+ ) signals to regulate diverse biological processes, with temporal dynamics providing a potential layer of intracellular information. We used optogenetic activation of the Gαq-coupled photoreceptor melanopsin to impose defined slow or fast temporal stimulation patterns in human non-excitable cells, evoking oscillatory Ca 2+ -associated signaling while preserving receptor-proximal signaling. Fast, regular melanopsin stimulation induced stronger nuclear factor κB (NF-κB)-associated tumor necrosis factor ( TNF ) and interleukin-8 ( IL8 ) expression than temporally irregular stimulation, while TNF and IL8 showed partly distinct responses to stimulation frequency. Transcriptomic analysis identified an MYC-associated gene expression program despite unchanged MYC transcript levels. Integration of transcriptomic and phosphoproteomic datasets identified candidate kinase networks involving PRKDC, CHEK2, and ATM, potentially linking temporally patterned signaling to cell-cycle and stress-response pathways. Together, these findings show that distinct temporal patterns of melanopsin-evoked signaling are associated with distinct transcriptional and phospho-signaling responses, highlighting temporal dynamics as a feature of intracellular information processing.

Article.Title: EEG-based deep learning estimates preterm infants’ cerebral age: Contribution of slow-wave and cross-frequency coupling
Article.Authors: Gallard A.; Billiot A.; Bourel-Ponchel É.; Brunel P.; Chazal C.; Kongolo G.; Ghostine G.; Wallois F.; Routier L.; Moghimi S.
Article.Abstract: Reliably estimating cerebral maturation in preterm newborns is crucial for early identification of atypical neurodevelopment. We developed a deep-learning framework using a convolutional neural network (CNN) to predict postmenstrual age (PMA) from spontaneous neural activity in EEG recordings of 165 healthy preterm infants (28–38 weeks PMA). The model achieved a mean absolute error of 0.75 ± 0.60 weeks, with 73.9% of prediction errors within one week. To identify key neurophysiological drivers, we systematically manipulated signal components. Results showed that removing low-frequency activity (<4 Hz) significantly degraded performance and disrupting phase-amplitude coupling selectively impaired prediction accuracy before 34 weeks PMA, while high-frequency activity (>12 Hz) had minimal impact. Our results demonstrate that maturation signatures are primarily driven by slow-wave dynamics and their hierarchical coupling with faster oscillations, which are fundamental hallmarks of early neurodevelopment.

Article.Title: Critical analysis of the new European framework for non-fossil flexibility and the questions left unanswered
Article.Authors: Mastropietro P.; Rodilla P.; Chaves Ávila J.
Article.Abstract: The 2024 Electricity Market Design Reform introduced a new European framework for non-fossil flexibility. The first national flexibility needs assessments were published in July 2026, and indicative objectives and support schemes for non-fossil flexibility will soon be introduced. However, we argue that this new framework, which will influence the development of European power systems as they transition to low-carbon resources, is based on a flawed theoretical foundation and exhibits significant overlap with the European resource adequacy framework. No flexibility metric has been defined for the flexibility needs assessment. No flexibility standard/target has been calculated based on the economic equilibrium between the cost of additional flexibility and the cost of not relying on it. We identify three underlying metrics for flexibility needs, we present alternative approaches to define flexibility products and identify open questions that need to be addressed before the new flexibility framework moves to the implementation phase.

Article.Title: Diatom-based treatment of geothermal brines to selectively remove silicon, retain lithium for downstream recovery, and produce omega-3 fatty acids
Article.Authors: Rehmanji M.; Skeffington A.; Hudson-Edwards K.; Newsome L.
Article.Abstract: The human blastocyst contains the pluripotent epiblast from which human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) can be derived. ACTIVIN/NODAL signaling maintains expression of the transcription factor NANOG and in vitro propagation of hESCs. It is unknown whether this reflects a functional requirement for epiblast development in human embryos. Here, we characterized NODAL signaling activity during pre-implantation human development. We showed that NANOG is an early molecular marker restricted to the nascent human pluripotent epiblast and was initiated prior to the onset of NODAL signaling. We further demonstrated that expression of pluripotency-associated transcription factors NANOG, SOX2, OCT4, and KLF17 were maintained in the epiblast in the absence of NODAL signaling activity. Genome-wide transcriptional analysis showed that NODAL signaling inhibition did not decrease NANOG transcription or impact the wider pluripotency-associated gene regulatory network. These data suggest differences in the signaling requirements regulating pluripotency in the pre-implantation human epiblast compared with existing hESC culture.

Article.Title: NR2F6 functions as a key transcriptional checkpoint enforcing dysfunction of human CD3+ T cells and limiting CAR-T cell potency
Article.Authors: Koutník J.; Gruber T.; Freimark D.; Humer D.; Schreiber D.; Hölzl I.; Lang V.; Tokic N.; Sajinovic T.; Wolf D.; Thuille N.; Siegmund K.; Klepsch V.; Baier G.
Article.Abstract: Although nuclear receptor subfamily 2 group F member 6 (NR2F6) regulates lymphocyte activation in murine models, its function in human T cells remains incompletely defined. Here, we identify NR2F6 as a T cell receptor (TCR)-inducible transcriptional checkpoint that limits effector potency in human CD3 + T cells, including chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells. In an anti-EGFR CAR-T cell-A549 co-culture model, enforced NR2F6 expression, mimicking its upregulation in tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, markedly impairs killing under repeated tumor challenge. In polyclonal T cells, NR2F6 overexpression and CRISPR-Cas9-mediated ablation produced directionally opposing effects, supporting its role as a negative regulator of activation, differentiation-associated programs, and cytokine production. Mechanistically, transcriptomic, epigenomic, and nuclear protein analyses are consistent with suppression of NFAT-, AP-1-, and NF-κB-associated pathways and reveal context-dependent changes in TCF-1-associated readouts. Collectively, these findings position NR2F6 as a signaling-integrated transcriptional checkpoint that contributes to dysfunctional T cell states and may promote tumor immune evasion in humans.

Article.Title: Frequency-dependent thalamocortical transfer limits sustained cortical expression of sensory drive
Article.Authors: Yu Z.; Wang H.; Zhuo Y.; Zuo Z.
Article.Abstract: Frequency-dependent sensory drive must pass through thalamocortical pathways before cortical expression, yet how high-frequency input is transformed into sustained cortical activity remains unclear. We combined 11.7-T fMRI, pathway-specific optogenetic stimulation, tuned-burst thalamic drive, and dynamic causal modeling (DCM) in dexmedetomidine-sedated rats to examine the ventral posterolateral thalamus (VPL)-to-primary somatosensory forelimb cortex (S1FL) pathway. Peripheral forepaw stimulation revealed intermediate-frequency cortical tuning, whereas thalamic nuclei remained responsive at high frequencies. Direct S1FL activation evoked sustained high-frequency blood-oxygen-level-dependent responses, indicating that cortex can express high-frequency drive when upstream relay is bypassed. In contrast, direct VPL activation produced strong thalamic responses but weak, onset-dominated high-frequency cortical responses, and tuned-burst stimulation showed temporal compression before cortical expression. DCM indicated preferential enhancement of VPL-to-S1FL effective connectivity at intermediate frequencies. These findings identify a frequency-dependent bottleneck in VPL-to-S1FL transfer, rather than local cortical responsiveness, as a constraint on sustained cortical expression of temporally dense sensory input.

Article.Title: Expanding the galactose oxidase substrate repertoire via a multi-modal computational strategy
Article.Authors: Miyajima J.; Tay D.; Yeo W.; Koo Y.; Supekar S.; Chen A.; Chia C.; Muthaliff N.; Teh T.; Fan H.; Lim Y.; Maurer-Stroh S.; Ang E.
Article.Abstract: Biocatalysis offers a greener alternative to chemical processes, yet industrial adoption is bottlenecked by the prohibitive cost of enzyme engineering. Here, we report a multi-modal computational framework that integrates synergistic descriptors of substrate binding, protein stability, and aggregation traits. Using galactose oxidase as a model system, this approach achieves 77% precision in identifying active variants across 13 structurally diverse secondary alcohols despite being trained exclusively on a single substrate. By implementing sequence conservation-based filtering, we demonstrate that training data can be reduced by 41% without compromising predictive fidelity. Furthermore, the multi-modal model generalizes to combinatorial variants (2–5 mutations) with 100% precision on a limited library. Experimental validation yields a curated panel of starting points for the synthesis of high-value functional ingredients, including optical brighteners and fragrance stabilizers. Our multi-modal approach facilitates more cost-effective enzyme engineering, supporting the development of biocatalytic routes for sustainable chemical manufacturing.

Article.Title: Ultrasound-based breast nodule malignancy diagnosis using CNN enhanced by knowledge distillation
Article.Authors: Hu T.; Ru R.; Ding Y.; Wang V.; Xu D.
Article.Abstract: Accurate discrimination of benign and malignant breast lesions is essential for early diagnosis, yet remains challenging due to lesion heterogeneity and interobserver variability in ultrasound assessment. We developed a deep learning (DL) framework integrating dual inverted bottleneck blocks (Dual-IB), adaptive hierarchical feature fusion, and knowledge distillation (KD) for breast ultrasound lesion classification. The model was trained and evaluated on public datasets and validated on an independent external cohort to assess its generalizability. Results demonstrated superior performance compared with baseline methods and resident radiologists, while maintaining robust performance across diverse datasets and imaging conditions. On the external validation dataset, the model achieved the best performance, with an accuracy (Acc) of 92.64% and an F1-score of 92.37%. Furthermore, class activation mapping (CAM) visualizations revealed focused and anatomically plausible attention patterns within lesion regions, aiding interpretation and suggesting its potential to assist in breast ultrasound lesion classification.

Article.Title: Targeting TRP channels in hearing loss from mechanisms to otoprotection
Article.Authors: Yang Y.; Li S.; Xie L.; Li J.; Wang C.; Li Z.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Hearing loss, a highly prevalent global disease with complex pathogenic mechanisms, poses significant challenges due to limited treatment options and secondary complications. Recent research highlights the crucial roles of transient receptor potential (TRP) channels in auditory physiology and pathology, including cochlear electrophysiology, endolymph ionic homeostasis, neurotransmitter release, inflammation, and sensorineural injury responses. Although previous reviews synthesized TRP-mediated pathological mechanisms in hearing loss, clinical translation and otoprotective drug discovery remain underexplored. This review characterizes inner ear TRP spatiotemporal expression, traces the hair cell mechanoelectrical transduction (MET) channel research trajectory, details their dual regulatory mechanisms, and compiles emerging TRP-targeting otoprotective candidates. It further highlights limitations including restricted preclinical models, scarce otoprotective drugs, and limited target diversity among existing agents. Finally, it proposes new research directions for future basic and clinical studies on TRP channels and auditory function.

Article.Title: miR-7a-5p attenuates hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy by suppressing PARP1-mediated parthanatos
Article.Authors: Chen D.; Kong X.; Zhong H.; Zhang Y.; Si C.; Kasimu A.; Qiao R.; Song Y.; Li B.
Article.Abstract: Hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) causes severe neonatal brain injury, with PARP1 hyperactivation implicated in neuronal death. Using a rat HIE model and glutamate-exposed HT22 neurons, we found that miR-7a-5p is significantly downregulated in both peripheral blood and the injured cortex of HIE rats. PARP1 hyperactivation triggered parthanatos, characterized by PAR polymer accumulation and apoptosis-inducing factor (AIF) nuclear translocation, without activating caspase-dependent apoptosis. Luciferase assays confirmed direct targeting of miR-7a-5p to the 3′ UTR of PARP1, suppressing its expression. Article.Title: The potential biomarkers of organ transplantation in the era of machine perfusion: Current status, challenges, and future directions
Article.Authors: Yang Z.; Ying X.; Guan Z.; Dong S.; Zhao Y.; Shi H.; Jiang J.
Article.Abstract: Machine perfusion (MP) is a technology that mimics the physiological state in an ex vivo environment to preserve organs and enable their dynamic assessment. Biomarkers measured during MP hold significant promise for predicting post-transplant outcomes and guiding decisions on organ utilization. However, the clinical translation of this field is currently hindered by a lack of robust research defining the relevant biomarkers, their types, and their clinically applicable thresholds. This review outlines the development and fundamental principles of MP devices and provides a definition and classification of biomarkers. We systematically summarize and categorize potential MP biomarkers for the liver, kidney, lung, heart, and pancreas. Current research into MP biomarkers remains insufficient, and its clinical application is constrained by factors including MP platform heterogeneity and donor variability. Further studies are needed to determine the sensitivity, specificity, stability, and reproducibility, while exploring dynamic monitoring for timely assessment and intervention during MP.

Article.Authors: Zhu S.; Köhler L.; Ergün B.; Meierhofer D.; Busch J.; Rabien A.

MMP-14 promoted proliferation and reduced apoptosis of bladder cancer cells and, in co-culture, suppressed T-cell-mediated killing. Mechanistically, MMP-14 was regulated by STAT3 and directly interacted with STAT3, promoting STAT3 phosphorylation at Y705 and upregulating PD-L1 expression. Article.Authors: Mammel M.; Matovu B.; Guirhem-Helican G.; Monteclaro H.; Beegum S.; Chimdo A.; Vasanthakumaran M.; Lee M.; Cheng L.; Ayyappan J.
Article.Abstract: Understanding species-habitat relationships is critical for marine ecosystem management. WUE showed an overall gradual decline and an intra-annual increase-decrease–increase pattern, with growth rates peaking in November and the lowest values occurring in June. Delayed drought responses occurred in 50.77% of vegetation, with a mean lag of 6.82 months; seasonally frozen soil mainly showed non-lagged and long-term responses, whereas permafrost mainly showed non-lagged and short-term responses. Cumulative effects affected 40.49% of vegetation, with a mean duration of 5.06 months. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for understanding drought impacts on vegetation WUE across contrasting frozen-soil environments.

Article.Authors: Soto G.; Dehmelt F.; Baumann M.; Tunç I.; Yu Y.; Malevich T.; Hafed Z.; Arrenberg A.
Article.Abstract: Active sensing requires integrating information about self-generated movements and afferent inputs. Here, we used a control theory model based on efficient state estimation to predict that optimal saccadic suppression strength depends on the time-dependent magnitude of unexplained sensory and motor variability. Using two drastically different species, macaques and zebrafish larvae, we experimentally measured saccadic suppression in the superior colliculus and the homologous optic tectum. Species-specific oculomotor noise was quantified experimentally, and sensory noise was estimated. We found that inter-species differences in sensory and motor noise levels, as well as their theoretically predicted impacts on visual sensitivity, are consistent with observed differences in saccadic suppression strength. Our results highlight the importance of computational resource limits of the brain for understanding performance differences that have evolved in homologous brain areas.

Article.Title: Axonal transcriptome remodeling during PGE2 induced sensitization identifies Tnfrsf12a/FN14 as a regulator of sensory neuron excitability

Article.Abstract: Axonal mRNA translation is a key regulator of neuronal plasticity, yet its contribution to inflammatory pain remains poorly defined. We identify a conserved axonal transcriptome across embryonic and adult neurons, enriched for ribosomal and mitochondrial functions, supporting sustained local translation and metabolic activity. Article.Title: Automated small-scale devices and robotic systems for analyzing the cellular impact of ambient aerosol particles
Article.Authors: Jeong S.; Kim K.; Han C.; Sung B.; Abelmann L.
Article.Abstract: In response to emerging threats associated with natural disasters, environmental pollution, and infectious diseases, the detrimental influences of airborne aerosols on humans have been investigated at the cellular level. Especially, intensive efforts have been devoted to system automation in order to enhance the efficiency, precision, and machine intelligence of aerosol cytotoxicity analysis. In this context, we combine the concepts of small-size automated and robotic platforms used for monitoring the harmful effects of aerosols. A conceptual framework is provided with a focus on mobile and field-deployable platforms that enable automated operation of (bio-)engineered systems on-site. Particular attention is given to the principles of biomimetic device design and the underlying physical and engineering mechanisms, to provide a system-level estimation on the complete "source-to-effect" workflow. Article.Title: Benchmarking of cell type deconvolution techniques for microarray data
Article.Authors: Kamali Z.; Snieder H.; Vaez A.
Article.Abstract: Cell type deconvolution algorithms have significantly advanced in recent years. However, a notable gap remains regarding the performance of these algorithms when applied to microarray data, which is widely available in numerous disease contexts. Here we compare the performance of existing cell type deconvolution algorithms across a spectrum of data preparation scenarios and diverse cell types within the context of microarray-based bulk transcriptome. Among the ten algorithms evaluated, MuSiC, qprogwc, and CIBERSORTx emerged as the top performers, demonstrating the highest correlation between the estimated and real cell type compositions ( r max = 0.74, 0.69, and 0.67, respectively). Such methods would unlock the full potential of the vast repositories of microarray data in public domains, facilitating deeper insights into cellular compositions in various disease states, and promoting translational research.

Article.Title: Unrealized optimal designs challenge models of constraint in early vertebrate evolution
Article.Authors: Leflaëc E.; Ballell A.; Sanisidro O.; Ferrón H.
Article.Abstract: Jawed vertebrates dominate modern vertebrate diversity, whereas most jawless vertebrate lineages disappeared during the Devonian. Hydrodynamic performance varied strongly across headshield morphospace, and later lineages tended to occupy more efficient regions. However, extensive areas containing highly optimal designs remained unexplored throughout the group's history. Evolutionary model fitting provided little support for hard phenotypic bounds preventing access to these regions. Pteraspidomorphs therefore retained substantial unrealized functional potential, suggesting that their extinction occurred before they fully explored the range of viable hydrodynamic solutions available to their body plan. Article.Authors: Kojima M.; Sato Y.; Hirayama A.; Ryuge A.; Imaizumi T.; Maeda K.; Kato N.; Kozaki Y.; Sugimura M.; Noda Y.; Shibata K.; Onogi C.; Tanabe K.; Takefuji M.; Terabe K.; Furuhashi K.; Kosugi T.; Tsuboi N.; Kadomatsu K.; Maruyama S.

Parametric Zwind simulations further revealed W- and M-shaped offline yaw-pitch response manifolds for the investigated typhoon and earthquake cases, respectively, providing simulation-derived references for parked-state comparison and hazard-region identification. Article.Authors: Tani K.; Okuuchi S.; Hirose S.; Kushiro K.
Article.Abstract: Humans routinely estimate whether an action can be completed within a limited time window, yet the mechanisms underlying such implicit evaluations are not fully understood. Article.Authors: Herz S.; Khan A.; Betancourt-Toscano I.; Tiron C.; Ton V.; Selley D.; Damaj M.

Adjuvant therapy with aromatase inhibitors (AIs), such as letrozole (LTZ), is the standard of care in ER + BC patients to prevent recurrence but many patients cease treatment prematurely due to the development of musculoskeletal side effects (i.e. arthralgia, myalgia, decreased grip strength) referred to as aromatase inhibitor-associated musculoskeletal syndrome (AIMSS). These findings identify S1PR1 as an important mediator to AIMSS and suggest that S1PR1 antagonists may be most effective as acute interventions to provide relief from the sensory and affective burden of AIMSS.

Neither acute nor repeated MDL 11,939 altered extinction in female mice. Article.Title: 3,4-Dimethoxyacetophenone ameliorates epileptogenesis by suppressing BDNF, c-fos, and JAK-2/ STAT-3 expression in a pentylenetetrazole-induced kindling model of epilepsy

Article.Abstract: Epilepsy is a neurological condition that affects approximately 50 million individuals worldwide.
