This underscores the urgent need for new drugs that can overcome these challenges. According to recent studies, the Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/STAT) pathway play an important role in epileptogenesis. Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and c-fos are also involved in neuronal excitability and seizure-induced neuronal changes. The purpose of the present study was to examine the anticonvulsant and antiepileptogenic activities of 3,4-dimethoxyacetophenone (3,4-DMA) in the acute seizure and pentylenetetrazole (PTZ)-induced kindling models of epilepsy and to elucidate related molecular changes of BDNF, c-fos, and JAK-2/STAT-3 signaling pathways. 3,4-DMA was first evaluated in an acute seizure model, followed by a kindling model of epilepsy in mice. The effects of 3,4-DMA on BDNF, c-fos, and JAK-2/STAT-3 were assessed by quantitative reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) and immunohistochemistry (IHC). The results showed that 3,4-DMA significantly reduced seizure scores in a PTZ-induced kindling model. BDNF, c-fos, and JAK-2/STAT-3 were significantly upregulated in both the cortical and hippocampal tissues in PTZ-control mice. Conversely, treatment with 3,4-DMA attenuated this overexpression in the cortex and hippocampus. In conclusion, 3,4-DMA has antiepileptogenic effect as evidenced by a reduction in the expression of BDNF, c-fos and the JAK-2/STAT-3 pathway components. So, it can be a promising therapeutic candidate in the treatment of epilepsy. However, future studies measuring p-JAK-2 and p-STAT-3 will be required to confirm pathway activation status.

Moreover, alcohol releases the stress signal norepinephrine (NE) into the adult CeA, leading to sex-dependent changes in its GABA transmission. Whether similar alcohol-induced changes in the adolescent CeA contribute to later-life vulnerability to AUD is unknown. In the present study, we used an intragastric gavage model of adolescent intermittent ethanol (AIE) exposure in Sprague-Dawley rats to examine the long-lasting effects on CeA synapses and noradrenergic regulation. Collectively, our data reveal that AIE produced a long-lasting reduction in adult CeA inhibitory tone, and this change is likely independent of the noradrenergic system. This developmental-specific shift in CeA activity reflects the heightened vulnerability of the adolescent brain to ethanol-induced neuroadaptation and may represent a neural substrate underlying the increased risk of AUD following adolescent alcohol use.

Article.Title: Profiling the effects of alcohol history on cognitive performance during abstinence: an examination of proenkephalin-A-derived peptides in the medial prefrontal cortex
Article.Authors: David E M.; Meera A.; Laura A A.; Stan B F.; Luis A N.
Article.Abstract: Cognitive impairments during abstinence may complicate recovery from alcohol use disorder, but their persistence across executive domains and accompanying cortical adaptations remain unclear. Neuropeptides are candidate mediators of persistent alcohol (ethanol; EtOH) effects, and emerging evidence implicates endogenous opioid peptides in cortical processing. Here, we examined cognitive function and medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) enkephalin profiles in rats with a history of chronic EtOH exposure. Using a longitudinal operant-based approach, we assessed cognitive flexibility during early abstinence and delay-dependent working memory during protracted abstinence. We then quantified methionine-enkephalin (Met-ENK) and leucine-enkephalin (Leu-ENK) and profiled the proenkephalin-A (PENK)-derived peptide pool in the mPFC. EtOH history did not alter overall trials or errors to criterion during strategy set-shifting or reversal learning. During reversal, however, EtOH rats showed greater perseverative bias, with response adjustments less aligned with recent feedback and more strongly influenced by prior reinforcement. During initial testing at the longest working memory delay, EtOH rats also showed lower accuracy. Performance across these tasks was correlated in EtOH rats, suggesting individual differences in cognitive susceptibility were maintained across abstinence. Targeted analyses showed comparable levels of Met-ENK and Leu-ENK between groups. Although individual PENK-derived sequences did not differ in abundance, compositional analysis showed a greater summed relative contribution of C-terminal fragments in EtOH samples. These findings indicate that EtOH history produces lasting cognitive vulnerabilities that emerge under greater task demands, with some animals remaining more susceptible than others. C-terminal PENK profiling may reveal novel targets associated with enduring mPFC adaptations during abstinence.

Article.Title: SV2A attenuates interictal anxiety in pharmacoresistant epilepsy via the SYT3–GluA2 axis
Article.Authors: Li C.; Pan T.; Ren M.; Wang X.; Shi Y.; Ren S.; Wu G.; Wang L.
Article.Abstract: Objective: Synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A (SV2A) is an established target of antiseizure therapy; however, its role in excitatory synaptic function and downstream postsynaptic machinery remains poorly defined. This study examined whether SV2A limits excitotoxic signaling by recruiting synaptotagmin-3 (SYT3), thereby modulating the α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor subunit GluA2. Methods: A multilevel strategy was used to define the contribution of SV2A to anxiety in a pharmacoresistant epilepsy (PRE) model. The phenobarbital/phenytoin-resistant PRE phenotype was established in rats using the lithium-pilocarpine paradigm. Lentiviral vectors were delivered to the hippocampal CA1 region for bidirectional manipulation of SV2A expression. Protein abundance and molecular interactions were examined using western blotting, immunofluorescence, co-immunoprecipitation, and molecular docking. Synaptic plasticity was assessed using long-term potentiation (LTP) recordings, and anxiety-related behavior was evaluated using the elevated plus maze and open field test. Results: A special interaction between SV2A and SYT3 was confirmed at the protein level. PRE rats exhibited pronounced anxiety-like behavior, increased seizure frequency, reduced SV2A expression, and aberrantly potentiated LTP in the CA1 region. Hippocampal SV2A overexpression reduced SYT3 levels, suppressed GluA2 internalization, and attenuated both exaggerated LTP and anxiety-like behavior. Conversely, SV2A knockdown increased SYT3 expression, promoted GluA2 endocytosis, and further aggravated aberrant LTP and anxiety-like behavior. Conclusion: SV2A plays a pivotal role in interictal anxiety associated with PRE. PRE downregulates SV2A and weakens the SV2A-SYT3 interaction, thereby driving aberrant LTP and the emergence of anxiety-like behavior.

Article.Title: Molecular mechanism of the interaction between kaempferol and human nicotinic acetylcholine receptors
Article.Authors: Yang J.; Moon M.; Yun J.; Yeom H.; Kamau V.; Lee M.; Lee G.; Lee J.
Article.Abstract: Kaempferol has been investigated for its potential neuroprotective properties and its ability to modulate mood-regulating pathways through the regulation of neurotransmitter systems. Evidence suggests that it may inhibit the reuptake of selective neurotransmitters, thereby enhancing their synaptic availability. Here, using two-electrode voltage-clamp recordings in Xenopus oocytes expressing five human nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (nAChR) subtypes, we found that kaempferol selectively and potently inhibits α3β4 nAChRs, with weaker inhibition of α3β2 receptors and no effect on α7, α4β2, or α4β4 subtypes. This inhibition was reversible, voltage-independent, and non-competitive with acetylcholine, indicating an allosteric mechanism of action rather than direct competition at the orthosteric binding site. To identify the structural basis of this subtype selectivity, molecular docking of kaempferol onto the α3β4 nAChR structure was performed, and candidate binding residues at the α3-β4 interface were prioritized based on binding energy for site-directed mutagenesis. The results showed that the inhibitory effect of kaempferol was abolished in the α3 W55A and β4 R151A double mutant. These findings confirm that kaempferol selectively and effectively inhibits the α3β4 nAChR subtype via an allosteric site formed by residues W55 (α3) and R151 (β4), supporting the hypothesis that it interacts with a specific region of this receptor distinct from the acetylcholine-binding site.

Article.Title: Distinct protein synthesis requirements for coupled excitatory and inhibitory long-term co-plasticity in mouse hippocampus
Article.Authors: Jabłońska J.; Orzoł D.; Ciurko D.; Wiera G.; Mozrzymas J.
Article.Abstract: The functioning of neuronal networks critically depends on the coordinated interaction between excitation and inhibition. The properties of glutamatergic and GABAergic synapses are finely tuned by network activity, and the heterosynaptic nature of inhibitory plasticity further emphasizes their functional coupling. Although the dependence of glutamatergic plasticity on protein synthesis is well established, the role of translation in inhibitory plasticity remains unclear. Herein, we investigated how protein synthesis supports the concurrent plasticity at inhibitory and excitatory inputs onto CA1 pyramidal neurons. To this end, we applied a high-frequency stimulation protocol of CA3-CA1 input combined with prolonged postsynaptic depolarization of principal cells. This induced both glutamatergic long-term potentiation (LTP) and inhibitory LTP (iLTP) at synapses formed by somatostatin-expressing interneurons onto pyramidal neurons. Although LTP was observed in slices from both juvenile (≤45 days) and adult (>45 days) mice, iLTP was only present in the adult group, revealing an unusual developmental profile. Moreover, in adult animals, excitatory LTP was required for the induction of iLTP but did not determine its magnitude. We found that bath application of translation inhibitor cycloheximide (CHX) strongly attenuated LTP and converted co-occurring iLTP into iLTD. However, when CHX was restricted to the recorded postsynaptic neuron, the initial phase of iLTP proceeded normally, but GABAergic currents gradually returned to baseline levels, indicating intact induction but impaired maintenance. In contrast, postsynaptic CHX left excitatory LTP unaffected. Together, these findings identify two distinct translational mechanisms: a postsynaptic one necessary for strengthening inhibition and a non-postsynaptic process required to potentiate excitation.

Article.Title: Route-dependent behavioral, dopaminergic, and transcriptomic adaptations to nicotine aerosol inhalation and systemic injection in male mice
Article.Authors: Ma Y.; Song Z.; Chen Y.; Liu G.; Li X.; Han S.; Fu Y.; Chen H.; Hou H.
Article.Abstract: Nicotine is one of the most widely used psychoactive substances, yet most preclinical studies rely on subcutaneous injection, which does not fully model inhalation-based exposure. How different nicotine delivery paradigms shape neurobehavioral adaptations remains unclear. Here, we compared subcutaneous nicotine injection and nicotine aerosol inhalation in male mice across behavioral, dopaminergic, and transcriptomic domains. Nicotine aerosol inhalation produced concentration-dependent modulation of conditioned place preference, accompanied by rapid nicotine absorption and delayed cotinine accumulation. Fiber photometry recordings in the nucleus accumbens revealed distinct dopamine dynamics during nicotine-associated contextual processing, with nicotine-paired contexts eliciting shorter time-to-peak but reduced amplitude and area under the curve. High-dimensional behavioral tracking under mecamylamine-precipitated withdrawal conditions demonstrated that nicotine exposure conditions reshaped behavioral organization rather than producing generalized hyperlocomotion. Subcutaneous nicotine and aerosol exposure produced partially overlapping but compositionally distinct behavioral profiles influenced by nicotine exposure, delivery paradigm, and aerosol formulation. Transcriptomic analyses further revealed region-specific molecular signatures, including metabolic pathways in the ventral tegmental area and synaptic/neuroimmune-related pathways in the nucleus accumbens after aerosol exposure. Together, these findings demonstrate that nicotine delivery paradigms shape distinct neurobehavioral and molecular responses, emphasizing the importance of inhalation-based models in preclinical nicotine research.

Article.Title: Effects of metabotropic 2/3-glutamate receptor agonism and antagonism on activity-based anorexia model in mice
Article.Authors: Varjelus T.; Oksanen A.; Kaljala L.; Ryazantseva M.; Aitta-aho T.
Article.Abstract: Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder disproportionately found in female teens and young adults. It is often resistant to treatment, has a significant chance of relapse and is more lethal than other eating disorders, such as bulimia nervosa or Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (ARFID). There is no specific medication for the treatment of anorexia nervosa. Treatment consists of psychosocial means, psychotherapy, psychoeducation, and nutritional counseling. Medication is usually used for treating comorbidities such as anxiety or to decrease obsessive-compulsive tendencies. These medications cannot help the patient regain weight or treat core symptoms. Metabotropic 2/3-glutamate (mGluR2/3) receptor agonist (LY379268) and antagonist (LY341495) are promising pharmacological agents to treat psychiatric disorders. Both have been reported to be anxiolytic, while antagonists have shown antidepressant-like effects in preclinical studies. The activity-based anorexia (ABA) paradigm is used to study mechanisms related to anorexia nervosa. It consists of giving mice access to a running wheel and restricting their feeding time. This causes mice to exercise more than mice without feeding time restriction and to eat less than mice without access to a moving running wheel. In this study, we subcutaneously injected female ABA model mice with a metabotropic 2/3-glutamate receptor agonist (LY379268) and antagonist (LY341495) in two experiments. Both compounds exacerbated weight loss by decreasing food intake as well as increasing physical activity. It can be concluded that the pharmacological manipulation of mGluR2/3 receptors is detrimental for the female ABA model and, therefore, might be potentially harmful for anorexia nervosa as well.

Article.Title: Altered hsa_circ_0005567 expression in schizophrenia: exploratory clinical associations and cellular evidence involving RPL7A
Article.Authors: Li J.; Zhong Q.; Long J.; Lu R.; Lv M.; Huang X.; Zhong Z.; Lan W.; Liao F.; Su L.
Article.Abstract: Background: Schizophrenia (SCZ) is a chronic mental disorder with unknown etiology and complex pathophysiology. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have emerged as important regulators in neuropsychiatric disorders. This study investigated the clinical relevance, functional role, and potential mechanism of hsa_circ_0005567 in SCZ. Methods: hsa_circ_0005567 expression was measured by qRT-PCR in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from 160 patients with SCZ and 160 healthy controls. Associations with clinical symptoms and laboratory parameters were explored. Functional studies were conducted in MK-801-treated SH-SY5Y cells after hsa_circ_0005567 knockdown or overexpression. Cell viability, apoptosis, and inflammatory cytokines were assessed. Candidate hsa_circ_0005567-interacting proteins were explored using chromatin isolation by RNA purification (CHIRP), mass spectrometry, RNA immunoprecipitation, and Western blotting. Results: hsa_circ_0005567 expression was significantly increased in PBMCs from patients with SCZ (P < 0.001) and in SH-SY5Y cells following MK-801 treatment (P = 0.026). Higher hsa_circ_0005567 expression remained associated with SCZ status after adjustment for age and sex. Exploratory analyses of PANSS scores and laboratory parameters showed only nominal associations, none of which remained significant after FDR correction. In vitro, hsa_circ_0005567 manipulation affected cell viability, apoptosis, and TNF-α expression in MK-801-treated SH-SY5Y cells. RPL7A was identified as a candidate hsa_circ_0005567-interacting protein, and its protein expression was altered following hsa_circ_0005567 knockdown or overexpression. Conclusions: hsa_circ_0005567 is upregulated in PBMCs from patients with SCZ and is independently associated with SCZ status. Functional experiments suggest that hsa_circ_0005567 may participate in cellular responses under MK-801-induced stress conditions, while RPL7A represents a candidate interacting protein. Further clinical and mechanistic validation is needed.

Article.Title: Suppression of ER stress underlies Montelukast's neuroprotective actions in D-gal/AlCl3-induced Alzheimer's disease in rats
Article.Authors: Mahmoud A.; Ibrahim S.; El-Yamany M.; Gowifel A.; Mohammed R.
Article.Abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative ailment characterized by neuronal and cognitive dysfunctions. Notably, cysteinyl leukotriene receptor 1 (CysLT1R) overexpression was detected in various AD models. It was closely associated with other hallmarks of AD, including increased oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, amyloid beta (Aβ) deposition, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress. Montelukast (MTK), a CysLT1R antagonist, is an anti-asthmatic drug possessing antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. Consequently, this study aimed to mechanistically investigate MTK's neuroprotective potential on D-galactose/Aluminum Chloride (D-gal/AlCl3)-induced AD in rats. This was accomplished by allocating thirty-six adult male Wistar rats into four equal groups as follows: Group I served as the control group, and Group II was orally treated daily with MTK (10 mg/kg) for eight weeks. At the same time, groups III and IV were administered D-gal (65 mg/kg/day, SC) and AlCl3 (200 mg/kg/day, p.o.), starting from week 3 until the end of the experiment, for the remaining six consecutive weeks, to induce AD. Group IV received MTK orally daily for eight weeks. The findings showed that dampening CysLT1R expression by MTK ameliorated D-gal/AlCl3-induced amyloidopathy. MTK rectified the behavioral outcomes, as evidenced by the improved parameters in the novel object recognition, Y-maze, and Morris water maze tests. MTK hampered oxidative stress (MDA and GSH), inflammatory (NF-κB and TNF-α), glial activation (GFAP and Iba1), apoptotic (Caspase-3), ER stress, and Aβ biomarkers. Additionally, MTK, as a CysLT1R antagonist, exerted these favorable actions via adjustment of PERK/IRE1-α/CHOP, NF-κB, mTOR, and apoptotic axes. In conclusion, this study underscored the use of MTK as a promising neuroprotective approach for mitigating AD via modulation of ER stress, neuroinflammatory, and apoptotic trajectories.

Article.Title: Adult-administered chronic nicotine remodels nigral dopaminergic and pedunculopontine cholinergic physiology
Article.Authors: Chen R.; Hosseini H.; Hall S.; Zhang S.; Evans R.
Article.Abstract: Nicotine is linked to neuroprotection and has been proposed as a potential preventative treatment for Parkinson's disease (PD). Because PD is an aging disorder, such a treatment would necessarily be administered to adults. However, previous studies examining the effects of chronic nicotine in neurons vulnerable to PD have primarily been conducted in juvenile animals. Here we administer chronic nicotine to adult mice of both sexes. We examine nicotine-induced functional adaptations in two brain structures vulnerable to PD, the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) and the pedunculopontine nucleus (PPN). Using whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology and two-photon calcium imaging, we observed changes in cellular properties that potentially contribute to reduced risk of PD associated with nicotine exposure. Chronic nicotine decreased pacemaking frequency, burst propensity, and rebound firing in SNc dopaminergic neurons, while decoupling tonic firing rate from dendritic calcium levels. These changes in the SNc occurred without altering L-type channel contributions, dendritic arborization, or excitatory synaptic drive. Although the PPN degenerates in PD and is the primary cholinergic input to the SNc, no previous studies have evaluated the effects of chronic nicotine on this structure. We find that chronic nicotine induced subregion-specific plasticity in the PPN. Rostral PPN neurons showed depolarized membrane potentials, broadened action potentials, and dendritic pruning, whereas caudal PPN neurons showed reduced spike frequency adaptation and accelerated excitatory postsynaptic current kinetics. While these PPN alterations do not have a previously established link with cellular vulnerability, synaptic and physiological changes in this region may have unexpected contributions to PD progression. In addition, these findings reveal novel mechanisms that could underlie nicotine's modulation of brainstem circuitry controlling arousal, sensory gating, and drug dependence.

Article.Title: 4-methyl-3-aminopyridine: A novel active blocker of voltage-gated potassium ion channels in the central nervous system
Article.Authors: Rodríguez-Rangel S.; Coronado O.; Ortega B.; Sun Y.; El-Saadi S.; Brugarolas P.; Sánchez-Rodríguez J.
Article.Abstract: Aminopyridines, including 4-aminopyridine (4AP), 3,4-diaminopyridine, and [18F]3-fluoro-4-aminopyridine, are voltage-gated potassium (KV) channel blockers used clinically to enhance conduction in neurological disorders and to image demyelination by positron emission tomography (PET). Developing new aminopyridines may yield improved therapeutics or imaging agents. Here, we characterized the physicochemical properties (pKa, logD), KV channel-blocking activity, toxicity (LD50), and pharmacokinetics of a novel compound, 4-methyl-3-aminopyridine (4Me3AP). 4Me3AP was less basic and more lipophilic than 4AP and showed greater blocking potency across multiple KV channels expressed in Xenopus oocytes. In mice, 4Me3AP exhibited lower acute toxicity (LD50 = 29.3 mg/kg) than 4AP (LD50 = 12.7 mg/kg) and a longer plasma half-life. These findings indicate that 4Me3AP is a potent KV channel blocker with favorable pharmacological properties, supporting its potential for symptomatic treatment of demyelinating diseases.

Article.Title: Molecular pathways implicated in antidepressant actions exhibits diurnal fluctuations in the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus of adult male and female mice
Article.Authors: González-Hernández G.; Rozov S.; Berrocoso E.; Rantamäki T.
Article.Abstract: Epidemiological and experimental studies have demonstrated a bidirectional relationship between mood disorders and the circadian system, with disrupted circadian rhythms contributing to depressive states, and their restoration playing a key role in antidepressants effects. In this context, we sought to examine whether selected molecular pathways implicated in antidepressant responses exhibit diurnal regulatory patterns. Naïve adult male and female C57BL/6 mice were euthanized at 3-h intervals beginning at Zeitgeber Time 0 (ZT0), and hippocampal (HC) and medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) tissues were collected for RT-qPCR and Western blot analyses. We observed statistically significant diurnal rhythmicity in all analyzed transcripts (cFos, Arc, Nr4a1, Dusp1, Dusp5, and Dusp6) in both HC and mPFC samples, with peak expression occurring during the dark (active) phase (ZT15-18). Phosphorylation levels of TrkBY816 (tropomyosin-related kinase) and GSK3βS9 (glycogen synthase kinase 3β) also showed patterns suggestive of temporal rhythmicity, peaking during the light (inactive) phase. Levels of p-ERK2T185/Y187 (extracellular-signal regulated kinase) did not display rhythmic fluctuations, but peaked during the light phase in the HC, especially in males. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that antidepressant-related signaling is subject to diurnal regulation, highlighting the importance of integrating circadian biology and time-of-day as relevant variables in the development of translationally relevant antidepressant research.

Article.Title: Structure-activity relationships of BnOCPA derivatives at native pre- and postsynaptic adenosine A1Rs
Article.Authors: la Mache C.; Preti B.; Wani M.; Lochner M.; Frenguelli B.; Wall M.
Article.Abstract: The addition of a benzyloxy group to the adenosine A1R agonist cyclopentyladenosine (CPA) produces a compound (BnOCPA) that selectivity activates A1R signalling via the G protein alpha subunit Gob. In rat hippocampus, BnOCPA inhibits CA3-CA1 synaptic transmission (IC50 65 nM) likely via Gob, with no effect on Goa-mediated postsynaptic membrane electrophysiology at concentrations up to 1 μM. We have investigated how modifications of the benzyloxy group of BnOCPA affects signalling: addition of methoxy group, MBnOCPA, substituting a phenoxy group, PhOCPA; and addition of bromide to the phenoxy group, BPhOCPA. These derivatives, previously shown to be selective A1R agonists, were assessed through inhibition of hippocampal CA3-CA1 synaptic transmission and postsynaptic effects on CA1 pyramidal neurons. All compounds inhibited synaptic transmission and increased paired-pulse facilitation, indicative of presynaptic actions. At a concentration that inhibited synaptic transmission (>75 %), none of the compounds hyperpolarised the resting membrane potential and thus retained the pre-vs postsynaptic selectivity of BnOCPA. Increasing their concentration allowed a measure of the selectivity range. BnOCPA hyperpolarised ∼40 % of neurons at 3 μM (∼50x the IC50 for synaptic inhibition). For PhOCPA and MBnOCPA, hyperpolarisation, occurred for some neurons, at 1 μM. For BPhOCPA, no hyperpolarisation occurred at concentrations up to 10 μM. Pre-application of the derivatives (at 300 nM) reduced adenosine-mediated hyperpolarisation, showing they bind but do not activate postsynaptic A1Rs. This data shows that modifying the structure of BnOCPA changes the discrimination between different native A1Rs, likely based upon selective activation of G-protein coupling.

Article.Title: Global Malat1 deletion in two genetic mouse models reveals sex-dependent effects on select ethanol-related behaviors
Article.Authors: Gil D.; Baratta A.; Ferguson C.; Miskanic M.; Iker A.; Homanics G.; Farris S.
Article.Abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a widespread psychiatric condition, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying its development remain poorly understood. While prior studies have largely focused on protein-coding genes, long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) remain underexplored in AUD. Malat1, a highly abundant and evolutionarily conserved lncRNA, is elevated in post-mortem brain tissue of human AUD subjects and rodents chronically exposed to ethanol; however, its causal contribution to AUD-relevant behaviors remains unknown. Using CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing, we generated two complementary global Malat1 knockout mouse models to assess its role in ethanol intake and related phenotypes. Constitutive knockout selectively attenuated acute functional tolerance rate and every-other-day two-bottle-choice (EOD-2BC) ethanol intake in females. These results were supported by an inducible adult conditional global knockout model, which reduced EOD-2BC ethanol consumption in females without altering taste preference. Together, our findings provide the first causal evidence that Malat1 regulates select ethanol-related behaviors in a sex-specific manner, supporting further investigation into its underlying mechanisms in AUD.

Article.Title: Psychoneuroimmunology of glioblastoma: How emotional states shape tumor biology
Article.Authors: de Melo M.; Bezerra T.; de Souza P.; Sales V.; da Rosa M.
Article.Abstract: Psychological states profoundly influence physiological processes, with growing evidence linking emotional dysregulation to cancer progression. Within the framework of psychoneuroimmunology, recent findings have shown that chronic stress, depression and anxiety disrupt immune surveillance and promote a pro-inflammatory environment that favors tumor growth. Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), the most aggressive brain tumor, appears particularly sensitive to these neuroimmune influences. Some stress mediators and neurotransmitters-such as glucocorticoids and catecholamines- modulate the GBM microenvironment, fostering tumor-supportive pathways and epigenetic changes. This comprehensive review synthesizes evidence connecting emotional disturbances and glioma biology, highlighting shared neuroimmune mechanisms and therapeutic opportunities. We propose that integrating psychosocial and neuropharmacological strategies into GBM care could improve patients outcomes by targeting both tumor biology and emotional well-being.

Article.Title: Thyrotropin-releasing hormone increases dorsal premammillary nucleus neuron activity and darting behavior
Article.Authors: Coletta C.; Laing B.
Article.Abstract: Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH) is classically recognized for its role in regulating the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid (HPT) axis; however, it also functions as a central neuromodulator influencing arousal, locomotion, and autonomic processes. Despite these established roles, the circuit-level mechanisms through which TRH modulates behavior remain poorly defined. The dorsal premammillary nucleus (PMd) is a hypothalamic structure implicated in high-imminence defensive states, yet whether TRH directly engages PMd circuits is unknown. Here, we assessed the role of TRH as a modulator of PMd neuronal activity and behavioral output using in situ hybridization, electrophysiology, calcium imaging, and behavioral assays in male and female mice. TRHR mRNA was co-localized with a subset of PMd CCK-positive neurons. TRH increased firing rate in a subset of PMd neurons in brain slices, revealing functional activation of a subset of the population. This finding was corroborated by calcium imaging that showed increased activity following TRH exposure. In vivo, intrahypothalamic administration of TRH produced darting and behavioral effects. Together, these findings identify a subpopulation of PMd neurons that serve as a functional hypothalamic target of TRH signaling associated with rapid locomotor behavioral output.

Article.Title: Deficiency of synaptotagmin 9 in the hippocampal region induces synaptic damage and cognitive impairment in Parkinson's disease mice via BDNF/TrkB signaling
Article.Authors: Xu N.; Du C.; Li Y.; Yang W.; Li W.; Perez R.; Yu S.; Lou H.
Article.Abstract: Cognitive impairment is a prominent non-motor symptom of Parkinson's disease (PD) that severely affects patients' quality of life, yet its underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the role of hippocampal Synaptotagmin 9 (Syt9) in PD-related cognitive deficits. We found that Syt9 expression was significantly downregulated in the hippocampus of both MPTP-induced subacute PD mice and A53T α-synuclein transgenic mice, concomitant with cognitive impairment and synaptic damage. To determine causality, we performed hippocampal Syt9 knockdown and overexpression using AAV-mediated gene delivery. Syt9 knockdown exacerbated, while Syt9 overexpression alleviated, cognitive deficits and synaptic structural abnormalities in PD mice. Proteomic sequencing and pharmacological manipulations revealed that Syt9 may regulate the BDNF/TrkB signaling pathway at the protein level, likely by influencing BDNF vesicular transport, release, or stability. Intra-hippocampal BDNF supplementation rescued synaptic damage and cognitive impairment, whereas the TrkB antagonist ANA-12 reversed the protective effects of Syt9 overexpression. Collectively, our findings identify the Syt9/BDNF/TrkB axis as a key mechanism in PD-related cognitive impairment and suggest that targeting this pathway may offer a novel therapeutic strategy for PD.

Article.Title: Gallic acid attenuates PTSD-like behavioral and hippocampal neuroplasticity deficits induced by single prolonged stress in male rats
Article.Authors: Meamar M.; Mohamadi Yarijani Z.; Parsaei H.; Vafaei A.; Rashidy-Pour A.; Raise-Abdullahi P.
Article.Abstract: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is associated with persistent cognitive and emotional disturbances linked to hippocampal dysfunction, oxidative stress, and impaired neuroplasticity. Gallic acid, a naturally occurring polyphenol, possesses antioxidant and neuroprotective properties, but its effects in trauma-related disorders remain incompletely understood. Male Wistar rats were subjected to single prolonged stress (SPS) to induce PTSD-like phenotypes and, beginning 24 h after SPS, received gallic acid (10 or 100 mg/kg) or saline for 14 days. Anxiety-like behavior, fear extinction, and spatial learning and memory were assessed using the elevated plus maze, contextual fear conditioning with extinction, and Morris water maze, respectively. Hippocampal oxidative stress markers (MDA, SOD, and TAC), BDNF protein expression, and CA3 dendritic morphology were evaluated. SPS exposure induced anxiety-like behavior, impaired fear extinction, and deficits in spatial learning and memory, accompanied by increased lipid peroxidation, reduced antioxidant capacity, decreased hippocampal BDNF expression, and CA3 dendritic atrophy. Early post-stress gallic acid administration attenuated these behavioral alterations and was accompanied by improvements in hippocampal oxidative status, BDNF expression, and CA3 dendritic morphology, without detectable effects on locomotor activity or relative adrenal gland weight. Collectively, these findings indicate that early post-stress gallic acid administration attenuates SPS-associated behavioral and hippocampal abnormalities and that these effects are associated with antioxidant and neuroplasticity-related changes rather than establishing a causal mechanism. Further studies using delayed treatment paradigms and pathway-specific approaches are needed to determine the efficacy of gallic acid after establishment of the PTSD-like phenotype and to clarify the mechanisms underlying its effects.

Article.Title: N-acetylcysteine decreases toluene conditioned place preference and modulates corticostriatal activity in adolescent rats
Article.Authors: Carampel A.; Asis J.; Munar J.; Gregorio C.; Medina P.; Quirk G.; Cena-Navarro R.
Article.Abstract: Inhalant (toluene) use disorder (IUD) continues to be a public health problem especially among Filipino adolescents. Animal models of IUD have not yet explored neurobiological changes from chronic toluene exposure, or possible treatments for long-lasting toluene-induced deficits. In rats repeatedly exposed to 3000 ppm of toluene vapor over 12 days, we report that daily administration of N-acetylcysteine (NACys; 100 mg/kg i.p. or 0.9 g/l oral), but not melatonin (10 mg/kg i.p.), during 8 days of abstinence reduced toluene conditioned place preference in both male and female adolescent Sprague Dawley rats. Using immunofluorescence, we found that toluene-exposed rats showed decreased c-Fos densities in the dorsomedial striatum (DMS), dorsolateral striatum, and ventrolateral orbitofrontal cortex (vlOFC) after 8 days of abstinence. NACys partially rescued c-Fos expression in vlOFC. We found that c-Fos densities in both vlOFC and prelimbic cortex were significantly correlated with CPP values and with c-Fos densities in the DMS across treatment groups, suggesting that a history of toluene exposure may act by reducing cortical modulation of the dorsal striatum to promote long-lasting drug context seeking. Our findings suggest that NACys may be a promising treatment for IUD in adolescent males and females.

Article.Title: Cholinergic-dependent metaplasticity in the amygdala–insula pathway during incubation of cocaine craving
Article.Authors: Salin A.; Lardeux V.; Dugast E.; Balado E.; Thiriet N.; Jaber M.; Solinas M.; Belujon P.
Article.Abstract: The time-dependent increase in drug seeking during abstinence, termed 'incubation of craving' is believed to play a major role in the persistent risks of relapse. This phenomenon is associated with synaptic plasticity changes across brain structures involved in reward processing, executive functions, emotion regulation and inhibitory control. The basolateral amygdala (BLA) and the anterior insular cortex (aIC) are two interconnected structures involved in processing internal and external drug-related cues and are known to play a role in drug craving. However, whether chronic cocaine alters synaptic plasticity within the BLA-aIC circuit and how these changes evolve during abstinence remains unclear. Here, using cocaine self-administration and in vivo electrophysiological recordings in anesthetized male rats, we demonstrate that, while long-term potentiation in the BLA-aIC pathway remains intact, long-term depression is disrupted throughout abstinence in both cocaine- and sucrose-rats, indicating a persistent impairment in synaptic weakening mechanisms. Importantly, a loss of depotentiation was observed after late but not early abstinence, and was specific to cocaine self-administration, identifying it as a hallmark of incubation of craving. Systemic, but not local intra-aIC, blockade of muscarinic receptors with atropine restored depotentiation and reduced cocaine-seeking behavior. Finally, qPCR analysis revealed region-specific transcriptional adaptations, with upregulation of muscarinic, NMDA and AMPA receptor transcripts in the BLA and a selective decrease of Grin2a in the aIC. Together, these findings point to cholinergic regulation of BLA-aIC metaplasticity as a candidate mechanism underlying incubation of cocaine craving.

Article.Title: zDHHC11 is a common palmitoyltransferase regulating microglia-mediated neuroinflammation across neurodegenerative diseases
Article.Authors: Luo H.; Jiang D.; Hao Z.; Bu J.; Wang J.; Xu N.; Nie X.; Zhang Y.; Yin Q.; Zhuang P.
Article.Abstract: Purpose: Microglia-mediated neuroinflammation is a shared feature across Alzheimer's disease (AD), Parkinson's disease (PD), and diabetic cognitive impairment (DCI), but the convergent molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated whether protein S-palmitoylation serves as a common regulator of microglial neuroinflammation across distinct neurodegenerative diseases etiologies and aimed to identify the key palmitoyltransferase involved. Methods: In vivo ND models (APP/PS1 for AD, MPTP for PD, STZ/high-fat diet for DCI) and in vitro BV2 microglial models stimulated with amyloid-β (Aβ), lipopolysaccharide (LPS), or high glucose (HG) were established. Microglial morphology, inflammatory responses, and the TLR4/MyD88 pathway were assessed by immunofluorescence, RNA-seq, RT-qPCR, and ELISA. Protein palmitoylation levels were evaluated using 2-BP and ABE assays. Palmitoyltransferase expression profiling was performed, and protein-level validation was conducted both in vitro and in vivo. Subsequently, the identified common enzyme, zDHHC11, was knocked down by siRNA to determine its functional role. Results: All three ND models showed robust microglial activation with a pro-inflammatory amoeboid morphology. Aβ, LPS, and HG each upregulated pro-inflammatory cytokines and activated the TLR4/MyD88 pathway in BV2 cells. Palmitoylation inhibition with 2-BP attenuated cytokine production, and all three stimuli increased total protein palmitoylation. Among all palmitoyltransferases screened, zDHHC11 was uniquely and consistently upregulated by all three stimuli. This upregulation was further corroborated at the protein level, with elevated zDHHC11 expression observed both in cultured cells and in brain tissue sections. Knockdown of Zdhhc11 suppressed cytokine expression/secretion and reduced TLR4/MyD88 levels, indicating that zDHHC11 acts upstream of this common pathway. Conclusion: Protein S-palmitoylation mediated by zDHHC11 is a convergent mechanism driving microglial pro-inflammatory activation across distinct ND etiologies. zDHHC11 represents a common regulator of TLR4/MyD88-dependent neuroinflammation and a potential therapeutic target for multiple NDs.

Article.Title: Therapeutic potential and toxicological trade-offs of nanoparticle-enhanced valproic acid in glioblastoma: Behavioral and oxidative insights
Article.Authors: Khodayari N.; Sedghy F.; Ranjbar M.; Pashazadeh Azari P.; Houshmand F.; Shahrokhi Raeini A.; Mahmoodi M.; Bashiri H.; Kheirandish R.
Article.Abstract: Background: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly aggressive brain tumor with a poor prognosis. In the current research, the therapeutic and behavioral efficacy of valproic acid (VPA) and its nanoparticles (Nano VPA) with or without temozolomide (TMZ) was investigated in the C6 glioblastoma rat model. Methods: We divided eighty-four adult male Wistar rats into seven groups (n = 12/group): sham, tumor, TMZ, VPA, nano VPA, VPA + TMZ, and nano VPA + TMZ. To induce tumors, C6 cells were injected into the brains of the rats. On days 12 to 15, behavioral performance was assessed using the social interaction test, elevated plus maze, open field, rotarod, and passive avoidance. On day 18, tumor size, edema, and histopathology were examined. Oxidative stress parameters in brain tissue and serum were measured by ELISA. Results: VPA and Nano VPA significantly inhibited tumor growth, either alone or with TMZ. All treatments except Nano VPA + TMZ improved survival compared with tumor controls. Treated groups showed enhanced anxiety regulation, sociability, learning, and memory. Motor coordination improved following VPA or Nano VPA therapy. Tumor induction reduced serum SOD, CAT, and TAC levels; treatments raised serum TAC and lowered brain MDA, but further reduced serum SOD. Conclusion: Our results suggest that oxidative stress modulation may contribute to the neurobehavioral and antitumor effects of both VPA and nano-VPA. While nano-VPA showed greater tumor reduction, conventional VPA was more effective in improving survival. Combining VPA with TMZ may enhance outcomes, and support further study of Nano VPA as an adjuvant therapy for GBM.

Article.Title: Subanesthetic ketamine modulates region-specific neural and endocrine responses to acute stress in rats
Article.Authors: Drozd U.; Bulygina V.; Shishkina G.; Kalinina T.; Dygalo N.; Lanshakov D.
Article.Abstract: Exposure to acute, inescapable stress triggers a coordinated neural and endocrine response across corticolimbic and brainstem circuits. Although subanesthetic ketamine has rapid antidepressant effects, it is unclear whether its modulation of the stress-response network depends on the presence of an acute stressor. In this study, naïve rats received subanesthetic ketamine (15 mg/kg) or a vehicle, and then underwent the tail suspension test (TST) or remained undisturbed in their home cages. Ketamine reduced immobility in the TST and attenuated the stress-induced increase in plasma corticosterone levels. Regional c-Fos expression, ascertained through quantitative real-time PCR and immunohistochemistry, revealed region-specific and context-dependent modulation. Ketamine selectively activated neuronal populations in the prefrontal cortex and potentiated stress-induced activation in the hippocampus and dorsal raphe nucleus. However, it suppressed stress-driven hyperactivation in the amygdala and elicited non-additive activation patterns in the brainstem. These findings suggest that subanesthetic ketamine modulates the regional balance of neuronal activation and attenuates hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis reactivity in a state-dependent manner. Furthermore, its effects on the stress-response network are influenced by the presence of an acute stressor.

Article.Title: Preoperative sleep deprivation prolongs postoperative hyperalgesia by downregulating spinal cord D2R expression via the PP2A/AKT-dependent NMDA receptor phosphorylation
Article.Authors: Liu Q.; Dong Q.; Xu T.; Jiao Y.; Yu J.; Zhang W.; Gu X.; Huang Y.; Xu R.; Ma Z.
Article.Abstract: Preoperative sleep deprivation (SD) is known to exacerbate postoperative pain, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Using a male mouse model of 48-h continuous SD followed by incisional surgery, we found that SD alone induced transient mechanical hyperalgesia, and when combined with surgery (SI group) it significantly aggravated and prolonged postoperative pain recovery until day 10. On postoperative day 7, SI mice showed marked downregulation of spinal dopamine D2 receptor (D2R) expression and decreased spinal dopamine concentration. D2R was predominantly expressed on spinal glutamatergic neurons. Overexpression of D2R on these neurons via intrathecal AAV injection effectively alleviated the prolonged hyperalgesia, normalizing pain sensitivity by day 7. Mechanistically, D2R downregulation led to increased phosphorylation of NMDA receptor subunits (p-NR1 and p-NR2B) without altering total NMDA receptor levels. Co-immunoprecipitation revealed an interaction between D2R and protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A). SI mice exhibited decreased PP2A expression but increased p-AKT, p-GSK3β, and β-catenin, indicating activation of the PP2A/AKT signaling pathway, which were reversed by D2R overexpression. Furthermore, pharmacological activation of PP2A with DT-061 not only downregulated p-AKT, p-GSK3β, β-catenin, p-NR1 and p-NR2B, but also produced significant analgesia in SI mice. Collectively, these results demonstrate that preoperative sleep deprivation prolongs postoperative hyperalgesia by downregulating spinal D2R on glutamatergic neurons, which disinhibits the PP2A/AKT pathway and enhances NMDA receptor phosphorylation. Targeting D2R or its downstream PP2A/AKT signaling may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for managing persistent postoperative pain caused by preoperative sleep deprivation in male mice.

Article.Title: Preconditioning induces ischemic tolerance by attenuating ferroptosis: involvement of the m6A-dependent FTO–IGF2BP1/3–ACSL4 regulatory axis
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Zhang L.; Liu X.; Li S.; Wang X.; Li S.; Ren X.; Zhou X.; Zhao C.; Zhao C.; Xian X.; Li S.; Hu Y.; Zhang J.; Zhang M.
Article.Abstract: Cerebral ischemic preconditioning (CIP) confers robust protection against subsequent ischemic stroke by enhancing brain ischemic tolerance. Although ferroptosis is increasingly recognized as a critical pathogenic mechanism in stroke, the role of N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA modification in its regulation remains poorly understood. This study investigated the involvement of m6A signaling in the anti-ferroptotic mechanism of CIP using complementary in vivo mouse middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) and in vitro oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) models. We found that CIP significantly attenuated ischemia-induced neuronal ferroptosis in vivo, whereas OGD preconditioning (OGDP) recapitulated these anti-ferroptotic effects in HT22 cells. Acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4), a key executor of ferroptosis, was markedly upregulated following ischemic injury, whereas CIP effectively suppressed this increase. Similarly, OGDP attenuated OGD-induced ACSL4 upregulation in HT22 cells. Importantly, ACSL4 overexpression significantly attenuated the protective effects of OGDP against OGD-induced ferroptosis. Mechanistic analyses in HT22 cells revealed that OGD downregulated the m6A demethylase fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) and upregulated m6A readers insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding proteins (IGF2BPs), including IGF2BP1 and IGF2BP3, thereby stabilizing ACSL4 mRNA and promoting ferroptosis. OGDP alleviated these effects by restoring FTO expression, reducing IGF2BP1 and IGF2BP3 levels, and enhancing m6A-dependent ACSL4 mRNA decay. Together, these findings demonstrate that CIP induces ischemic tolerance and attenuates ACSL4-associated ferroptosis. Mechanistic studies in neuronal cells further identify the m6A-dependent FTO-IGF2BP1/3-ACSL4 axis as a potential regulatory mechanism contributing to OGDP-induced ferroptosis resistance.

Article.Title: Lateral hypothalamic orexin→VTA projection regulates consolation via orexin receptor 1 in male mice
Article.Authors: Tian J.; Li W.; Zhang L.; Zheng M.; Zhao Q.; Liu Y.; Li L.
Article.Abstract: Consolation, a prosocial behavior in which individuals comfort distressed conspecifics, is regarded as a fundamental expression of empathy. Orexin (OX) neurons in the lateral hypothalamus (LH) have been implicated in empathic processes, but the specific circuitry and receptor subtypes through which they modulate consolation remain unknown. Here, we investigated the role of LHOX neurons and their projection to the ventral tegmental area (VTA) in regulating consolation-like behavior in male mice. We found that consolation toward a defeat induced stressed partner was accompanied by reduced c-Fos expression in LHOX neurons. Using chemogenetic manipulations, we demonstrated that activation of LHOX neurons, or specifically the LHOX→VTA projections, decreased consolation-like allogrooming. Furthermore, intra-VTA injection of the orexin receptor 1 (OX1R) antagonist SB-334867, but not the OX2R antagonist Seltorexant, rescued the allogrooming deficit induced by pathway activation, identifying VTA OX1R as the critical receptor subtype. These effects occurred without alterations in anxiety-like behavior or general sociability. Collectively, these findings reveal that the LHOX→VTA pathway, acting through OX1R, contributes to the regulation of consolation, establishing a receptor-specific circuit mechanism for orexinergic modulation of empathy-related prosocial behavior.

Article.Title: Modulation of postictal hypoxia: Sex- and route-specific effects of acute and chronic cannabidiol and Delta9-tetrahydrocannabinol
Article.Authors: Rha S.; Gom R.; Duran Bascope V.; Fick L.; Imoukhuede A.; Hume C.; Lightfoot S.; Hill M.; Teskey G.
Article.Abstract: Postictal hypoxia causes several consequences that are detrimental to the quality of life of people with epilepsy. Cannabidiol (CBD) and Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the primary phytocannabinoids from cannabis, have been shown to exhibit vasoactive and antioxidant properties that may mitigate the local oxygen deficiency observed after seizures. Here, we focus on the effects of CBD and THC on seizure-induced hypoxia. Adult Long-Evans rats of both sexes were assigned to drug-specific cohorts and the effects on local hippocampal oxygen were measured before and after seizure elicitation following either vaporized or oral administration of the two phytocannabinoids. Acute effects were assessed following a single administration of each drug, whereas chronic effects were evaluated over 28 days of daily treatment. In naïve rats, acute vaporized CBD significantly attenuated postictal hypoxia in both sexes, whereas acute oral THC attenuated postictal hypoxia in male rats. With chronic daily administration, phytocannabinoids produced time-dependent adaptations. Chronic vaporized CBD in females and chronic oral THC in males maintained attenuating effects on postictal hypoxia but exhibited partial tolerance, characterized by diminished effects on postictal oxygen decline in both sexes, recovery of postictal oxygen in females, and severity of hypoxia in males. These results demonstrate that acutely and chronically administered phytocannabinoids attenuate postictal hypoxia in a route-, sex-, and time-dependent manner. Together, these findings provide evidence that vaporized CBD and oral THC hold potential to treat the postictal hypoxia-induced comorbidities associated with seizures, potentially increasing the overall quality of life of people with epilepsy.

Article.Title: Adolescent social isolation drives sex-dependent shifts in medial prefrontal cortex endocannabinoid tone and excitatory/inhibitory balance: the protective role of a methyl donor
Article.Authors: Ricciardi F.; Mosca L.; Belardo C.; Bonsale R.; Fusco A.; Teweldemedhin M.; Piscitelli F.; di Marzo V.; Limongelli R.; D'Agostino E.; Zampelli A.; Guida F.; Luongo L.; Porcelli M.; Maione S.; Palazzo E.
Article.Abstract: Prolonged social isolation triggers neuropsychiatric impairments linked to brain neurotransmitter imbalances. This study investigated the impact of social isolation on sensory perception, affective states, and the levels of amino acid neurotransmitters and endocannabinoids within the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) of both male and female adolescent mice. Furthermore, we evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of S-adenosylmethionine (SAMe), a methyl donor with established antidepressant properties, in mitigating these alterations. Single-housed (SH) male mice developed mechanical allodynia, cold hyperalgesia, depression-like behavior, and general malaise, alongside significantly decreased GABA levels in the mPFC. SAMe treatment effectively ameliorated these symptoms, restoring GABAergic tone and increasing glycine and glutamate levels. In contrast, SH female mice exhibited anxiety-like behavior and pain hypersensitivity without depression-like traits. Their neurochemical profile was characterized by decreased GABA but increased levels of glutamate and specific endocannabinoids/acylethanolamides (2-AG, PEA, and LEA) in the mPFC. In females, SAMe treatment successfully reversed anxiety-like behavior and pain hypersensitivity, normalized glutamate, LEA, and GABA levels, and increased glycine and DHG. Our findings demonstrate that while social isolation-induced neuropsychiatric and neurochemical alterations are sex-dependent, the development of sensory hypersensitivity and the therapeutic responsiveness to SAMe are consistent across sexes. By restoring GABAergic homeostasis and modulating excitatory and endocannabinoid signaling in the mPFC, SAMe emerges as a promising pharmacological intervention for treating the complex psychiatric and sensory sequelae induced by chronic social stress.

Article.Title: Parthenolide reduces transgelin-2 expression in inhibiting glioblastoma malignancy through activating GSK3β-suppressing CREB signaling
Article.Authors: Liu A.; Kuo Y.; Shih C.; Cheng C.; Chen K.; Ho K.
Article.Abstract: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is a WHO grade IV brain tumor with aggressive growth and frequent recurrence, and temozolomide (TMZ) remains the standard first-line chemotherapy despite limited durable benefits. Parthenolide (Pt), a sesquiterpene lactone derived from the medicinal plant feverfew, has shown antitumor activity in multiple cancer types; however, its therapeutic potential and downstream mechanisms in GBM have not been fully defined. Herein, we demonstrate that Pt induces apoptosis, suppresses stemness, and reduces invasion in human U-87MG and T98G cells. Pt also potentiates TMZ's efficacy in vitro and in an orthotopic GBM model with male NOD-SCID mice. RNA-sequencing and pathway analyses revealed that Pt markedly represses epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-associated programs. Among the most significantly downregulated genes, transgelin-2 (TAGLN2) emerged as a key Pt-responsive target, and its high expression was correlated with poor survival in glioma cohorts. TAGLN2 overexpression rescued Pt-mediated suppression of malignant phenotypes and the EMT, supporting a functional role for TAGLN2 in Pt responsiveness. Mechanistically, inhibitor screening identified glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK3β) as a critical upstream regulator of Pt-induced TAGLN2 repression. Promoter-reporter and ChIP-qPCR assays further showed that Pt activates GSK3β, leading to reduced cyclic AMP response-binding protein (CREB) transcriptional activity and diminished CREB occupancy at the TAGLN2 promoter, thereby suppressing TAGLN2 transcription. Collectively, our findings define a Pt-driven GSK3β/CREB/TAGLN2 axis that restrains the mesenchymal transition and enhances TMZ sensitivity in GBM, highlighting TAGLN2 and its upstream regulatory pathway as potential therapeutic targets for this lethal disease.

Article.Title: Oleoylethanolamide modulates fear memory even after rapamycin infusion into the hippocampus of male Wistar rats
Article.Authors: Ceglarek V.; Czarnabay D.; Fontes G.; Sagae S.; Baldo G.; Blandina P.; Passani M.; Provensi G.; Benetti F.
Article.Abstract: Fear memory can become maladaptive, leading to stress disorders, which represent a significant global health challenge that requires alternative treatment approaches. Oleoylethanolamide (OEA), an endogenous lipid mediator, has demonstrated anxiolytic and pro-cognitive properties to address these conditions. This study investigated the role of OEA in fear memory attenuation and its interaction with hippocampal protein synthesis pathways during memory reconsolidation. Male Wistar rats were trained in a contextual fear conditioning paradigm. Twenty-four hours post-training, memory reactivation was induced through a 10-min context re-exposure, immediately followed by systemic intraperitoneal administration of OEA (1, 5, or 10 mg/kg) or saline. To examine downstream mechanisms, the protein synthesis inhibitor anisomycin or the mammalian target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1) inhibitor rapamycin was microinfused into the CA1 region of the hippocampus. Freezing behavior was assessed during a retention test conducted 3 h or 24 h later. Systemic OEA at 10 mg/kg facilitated the attenuation of fear memory 24 h post-reactivation, an effect that was dependent on memory reactivation. Intra-CA1 microinfusion of anisomycin blocked the behavioral effects of OEA, while rapamycin did not reliably prevent the behavioral effects of OEA under the present conditions. These results indicate that OEA-mediated memory attenuation requires de novo protein synthesis within the hippocampus, but that the precise involvement of mTORC1 remains unresolved, implicating alternative downstream cascades. Our findings highlight the potential of OEA as a therapeutic target for fear-related disorders and emphasize the need for further research to delineate the specific neural pathways involved.

Article.Title: Dual hypocretin receptor antagonism reduces oxycodone seeking and attenuates aberrant dopamine transporter function during abstinence
Article.Authors: Samson K.; Bashford A.; España R.
Article.Abstract: A major barrier in the treatment of opioid use disorder is persistent drug craving during abstinence. While opioid-based medications have been used to treat opioid use disorder for decades, there is an urgent need for novel, non-opioid-based pharmacotherapies. The hypocretin/orexin (hypocretin) system is a promising target for treating opioid use disorder due to its influence on motivation for drugs of abuse through actions on dopamine transmission. We recently showed that intermittent access to oxycodone promoted sustained oxycodone seeking and alterations in dopamine transmission during abstinence. In the current studies, we investigated to what extent suvorexant, an FDA-approved dual hypocretin receptor antagonist, reduces oxycodone seeking and restores dopamine function during abstinence in female and male Long Evans rats. Results indicated that intermittent access to oxycodone produced sustained cue-induced oxycodone seeking after a 14-day abstinence period, which was associated with reduced dopamine uptake in the nucleus accumbens core as we have previously shown. Treatment with suvorexant 24 h prior to a cue-induced seeking test significantly reduced oxycodone seeking and attenuated aberrant dopamine uptake. These findings suggest that targeting hypocretin receptors could be a promising strategy for reducing opioid craving and associated neuroadaptations, thus lowering the risk of relapse.

Article.Title: Cued unpredictable intermittent access exacerbates loss of control over ethanol drinking
Article.Authors: Mitten E.; Caldwell J.; Zambrano G.; Arce Soto N.; Glover E.
Article.Abstract: Background: Loss of control over drinking is a hallmark feature of alcohol use disorder (AUD) that is modeled preclinically through escalation of ethanol consumption and aversion-resistant drinking. Prior work with other reinforcers suggests that within-session unpredictable, intermittent access (uIntA) promotes these phenotypes. However, the effect of uIntA on voluntary ethanol consumption is unknown. Methods: Male and female Long-Evans rats (n = 9-10/group) underwent seven weeks of daily voluntary ethanol (20% v/v) drinking sessions under either a continuous access (ContA) or uIntA schedule. Following four weeks of baseline, rats were rendered dependent using a two-week chronic intermittent ethanol vapor exposure procedure. Daily testing was maintained through one week into withdrawal from vapor exposure. On the final day of testing, ethanol was adulterated with quinine (30 mg/L) to assess aversion-resistant drinking. Results: Rats drinking under ContA and uIntA exhibited similar levels of average daily ethanol consumption at baseline. However, uIntA elicited a more robust dependence-induced escalation of ethanol consumption compared to ContA, with uIntA sustaining escalation through early withdrawal. Additionally, while rats with ContA to ethanol remained sensitive to quinine even after chronic ethanol vapor exposure, uIntA promoted aversion-resistant drinking in ethanol dependent rats. Conclusions: These results demonstrate that, compared to ContA, uIntA maintains ethanol drinking and exacerbates dependence-induced escalation and aversion-resistant ethanol consumption. This work positions uIntA as a powerful tool to assess psychological and neurobiological factors that may underlie loss of control over drinking.

Article.Title: Activation and increased hippocampal GPR55 prevents cognitive deficits in male APP/PS1 mice
Article.Authors: Liang Y.; Zhi T.; Fan B.; Wu Y.; Wu L.; Xie Z.; YanYang N/A.; Mu R.; Wu X.
Article.Abstract: Background: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by progressive memory loss and cognitive decline. G protein-coupled receptor 55 (GPR55) has been linked to cognitive regulation, yet its precise role in AD pathogenesis remains unclear. Objectives: Here, we investigated the role of GPR55 in AD and its molecular mechanism. Methods: This study utilized APP/PS1 and GPR55 knockout (GPR55KO) mice to investigate the role and possible mechanism of GPR55 in AD. Results: We observed progressive reduction of GPR55 levels in the hippocampus of aging APP/PS1 mice. Conversely, hippocampal GPR55 overexpression rescued cognitive deficits, neuroinflammation, and impairment of synaptic plasticity in APP/PS1 mice. Moreover, GPR55 activation reduced neuronal death and memory impairments in APP/PS1 mice. In addition, aged GPR55KO mice showed cognitive deficits, but hippocampal GPR55 reexpression improved cognition. We also demonstrated that GPR55 activation mitigates Aβ1-42-induced synaptic damage and apoptosis in HT22 cells. Further studies revealed that in both animal and cell models, the levels of P-AKT/AKT and P-GSK3β/GSK3β were significantly decreased, and the level of P-ERK/ERK was markedly increased, while upregulation of GPR55 reversed this trend. Conclusions: These results indicate that hippocampal GPR55 may improve cognitive dysfunction by regulating the AKT/GSK3β and ERK signaling pathways, highlighting its crucial role in AD.

Article.Title: Sex-specific differences in endocannabinoid regulation of cocaine-evoked dopamine in the medial nucleus accumbens shell
Article.Authors: Gaulden A.; Chase K.; McReynolds J.
Article.Abstract: Endocannabinoid (eCB) signaling is a key regulator of reward-related dopaminergic signaling, particularly in response to drugs of abuse, such as cocaine. To date, our understanding of this mechanism has primarily been limited to male subjects. Prior work establishes that female cocaine users have more adverse outcomes, and female rats show greater sensitivity to cannabinoid type 1 receptor (CB1R) regulation of cocaine self-administration. Therefore, we hypothesize that female rats exhibit enhanced eCB regulation of cocaine-evoked dopamine (DA). We used in vivo fiber photometry recording of the dopamine biosensor, dLight 1.3b, in the nucleus accumbens medial shell (NAcms) in response to cocaine in male and female rats. Rats were pretreated with cannabinoid-targeting drugs to investigate the effects of CB1R inactivation or augmentation of the eCB 2-AG on cocaine-evoked DA. Our results revealed that CB1R inactivation attenuates cocaine-evoked DA in male and female rats, but females showed enhanced sensitivity for CB1R regulation of cocaine-evoked DA. Cocaine-evoked DA was enhanced by augmenting 2-AG levels, and females again showed increased sensitivity to this manipulation. Finally, females show greater cocaine-evoked DA when in a non-estrous cycle compared to estrous, reinforcing that estrous cycle is a determinant of cocaine-evoked DA. These data indicate that females show enhanced eCB regulation of cocaine-evoked DA signaling, underscoring the importance of sex as a biological variable in our understanding of endocannabinoid regulation of drug reward.

Article.Title: Inferior olive-selective amplitude suppression and progressive dentato-cortical decoupling during haloperidol-induced parkinsonism: a longitudinal multi-unit activity study
Article.Authors: Zarate-Calderon C.; Chi-Castañeda D.; López-Meraz M.; Beltrán-Parrazal L.; Morgado-Valle C.; García L.
Article.Abstract: Drug-induced parkinsonism (DIP) arises from competitive D2 receptor blockade, yet its cerebellar circuit-level dynamics remain poorly characterized. We recorded multi-unit activity simultaneously from four cerebellar structures (dentate nucleus, Crus II, inferior olive, and lobulus Sim B) across three weekly sessions in male Wistar rats receiving chronic haloperidol (1.5 mg/kg/day, subcutaneous) to characterize structure-specific and longitudinally evolving cerebellar population dynamics. Resting-state discharge amplitude was suppressed only in the inferior olive after FDR correction, where all six amplitude features fell sharply (d = -6, pFDR < 0.001); reductions in the same direction in Sim B were smaller and non-significant (d = -1.24 to -1.38), as was a concurrent increase in discharge rate (Hedges' g = +1.15, 95% CI [-0.07, 2.37]). During spontaneous tremor, all four structures showed elevated population amplitude alongside reduced discharge rate and irregularity, identifying temporally concentrated synchronized discharge rather than generalized hyperactivation as the mesoscopic tremor correlate. Phase coupling diverged anatomically: dentate-Crus II synchronization declined progressively across weeks (slope = -0.024 per week, p = 0.0006, Rm2 = 0.36) while olivocerebellar coupling remained robust and static. Week-1 Crus II activity alone predicted week-3 tremor burden in this single cohort with cross-validated accuracy (rLOO = 0.993, RLOO2 = 0.901, pFDR = 9.0×10-4), and unsupervised clustering revealed progressive neural state reorganization across all structures without behavioral escalation. These findings establish DIP as a longitudinally evolving cerebellar network state driven by pharmacodynamic changes beyond acute D2 occupancy, identifying the inferior olive, the dentate-Crus II axis, and Crus II as mechanistically and anatomically distinct nodes for future pharmacological and translational investigation.

Article.Title: M3 muscarinic receptor antagonism attenuates cocaine-induced hippocampal oligodendroglial changes and relapse-like behavior in male mice
Article.Authors: Yamada J.; Maeda S.; Okamura A.; Iinuma K.; Jinno S.
Article.Abstract: Acetylcholine (ACh) signaling regulates oligodendrocyte lineage progression via muscarinic ACh receptors (mAChRs), yet its role in cocaine-induced myelin-associated and relapse-like changes remains unexplored. Here, we examined whether hippocampal cholinergic and oligodendroglial alterations were associated with cocaine-related outcomes and pharmacologically sensitive to M3-preferential antagonism. Adult male C57BL/6J mice were subjected to cocaine-conditioned place preference (CPP), extinction, and cocaine-primed reinstatement, and treated with benztropine (BZT), the M1-selective mAChR antagonist VU0255035, or the M3-preferential mAChR antagonist solifenacin (SOL). Cocaine conditioning increased dorsal hippocampal ACh levels and reduced the expression of selected myelin-related genes and oligodendroglial transcription factors, including Mbp, Plp, Olig2, and Olig1, predominantly in the dorsal hippocampus. These changes were accompanied by reduced myelin basic protein (MBP) immunoreactivity, increased cholinergic terminal apposition to oligodendrocyte-lineage cells, and upregulation of Chrm3 in O4-sorted hippocampal oligodendrocytes. BZT reduced cocaine-primed reinstatement and increased Mbp and Plp expression and MBP immunoreactivity in several hippocampal layers. BZT also normalized cocaine-induced changes in Fosb, ΔFosb, Creb, and Slc6a3 in the dorsal hippocampus, whereas dorsal Bdnf remained different from vehicle-treated controls. SOL reduced reinstatement relative to both cocaine-conditioned and VU0255035-treated mice. SOL also increased open-arm time and entry ratio in the elevated plus maze test relative to cocaine-conditioned mice. In CD140a-sorted oligodendrocyte precursor cell-derived cultures, SOL increased MBP-positive oligodendrocyte volume relative to cocaine alone; however, the lack of a SOL-VU0255035 difference precluded conclusions about subtype specificity. These findings provide evidence consistent with a contribution of M3-sensitive muscarinic mechanisms to cocaine-associated oligodendroglial and behavioral alterations.

Article.Title: Digestion of perineuronal nets in the ventral CA1 suppresses methamphetamine-induced conditioned place preference acquisition by modulating PV interneuron activity in female mice
Article.Authors: Yao J.; Wu X.; Guo Z.; Wang X.; Liu X.; Li J.; Yang J.; Tang W.; Cui Y.; Li F.; Li C.
Article.Abstract: Methamphetamine (MA) addiction is characterized by persistent drug-associated memory and high relapse risk. Perineuronal nets (PNNs), which mainly surround PV interneurons, are specialized extracellular matrix structures involved in synaptic stabilization and memory regulation. Our previous studies have shown that PNNs in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) are essential for MA-induced conditioned place preference (CPP) memory, but the role of hippocampal PNNs in MA-associated contextual memory remains unclear. Here, a CPP paradigm was employed in female mice to investigate the role and underlying mechanisms of hippocampal PNNs in MA-induced reward memory. During MA-induced CPP acquisition, the number of c-Fos and PNNs in the hippocampal CA1 was significantly increased. Digestion of PNNs using chondroitinase ABC (ChABC) or knockdown of the key PNNs component Aggrecan in the ventral CA1 (vCA1) but not dorsal CA1 (dCA1) suppressed the acquisition of MA-induced CPP and reduced the immunoreactivity of PV and c-Fos. In addition, chemogenetic inhibition of PV interneurons in the vCA1 of Pvalb-IRES-Cre mice using the hM4D(Gi) DREADD strategy also suppressed CPP acquisition, supporting a critical role for PV interneuron activity in this process. Together, our findings indicate that MA-induced increased PNNs in the vCA1 promote the formation of CPP memory by regulating PV interneuron activity. This study provides new evidence for the region-specific role of hippocampal PNNs in drug-associated memory and suggests that targeting vCA1 PNNs and PV interneurons may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for MA addiction.

Article.Title: The positive feedback interaction between mast cell-derived tryptase and NETs formation in the pathogenesis of sepsis-associated encephalopathy
Article.Authors: Peng Y.; Mo L.; Zeng G.; Xu X.; Zhang X.; Cheng Y.; Jiang Y.; Yue J.
Article.Abstract: Background: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a serious neurological complication resulting from sepsis, marked by considerable neuroinflammation and deficits in cognitive function. While neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have been implicated in various neuroinflammatory conditions, the specific mechanisms underlying NETs formation in SAE, particularly the role of brain-resident mast cells (MCs) and their interplay with neutrophils, remain poorly understood. Methods: The cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) procedure was employed to create the SAE model in male C57BL/6 mice. Comprehensive methodological approaches included: 1) Pharmacological interventions using MC stabilizer (cromolyn), MC activator (C48/80), tryptase inhibitor (APC366), and Protease-activated receptor 2(PAR2) antagonist (AZ3451); 2) Establishment of MC-neutrophil co-culture systems with PMA/LPS stimulation; 3) Advanced imaging techniques including multiplex immunofluorescence and NETs visualization through Cit-H3/MPO/DAPI triple staining; 4) Molecular pathway analysis through Western blot, co-immunoprecipitation, and lactate quantification; 5) Functional assessments of MC activation through β-hexosaminidase release and tryptase activity assays. Results: MC activation significantly promoted neutrophil infiltration and NET formation in SAE mice. Investigations into the mechanisms have demonstrated that tryptase, derived from MC, activates the PAR2-MAPK signaling pathway in neutrophils, which results in an increased expression of LDHA and boosts lactate production. Subsequently, lactate-mediated lactylation stabilizes PAD4 protein by inhibiting its degradation, thereby facilitating NETosis. Furthermore, NETs promote a positive feedback mechanism by boosting MC activation and elevating the release and activity of tryptase, thereby creating a self-reinforcing cycle of inflammation. Conclusion: This study elucidates a novel bidirectional MC-NETs axis in SAE pathogenesis, wherein tryptase-PAR2-MAPK signaling and lactylation-mediated PAD4 stabilization drive progressive neuroinflammation. These findings not only advance our understanding of SAE mechanisms but also identify multiple potential therapeutic targets within this pathway for clinical intervention.

Article.Title: Dual MDM2 and PPARG regulatory axes mediate the antiepileptic effects of Gouteng: An integration of bioinformatics, network pharmacology, machine learning, molecular docking, and MD simulations
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Chen L.; Yuan X.; Luo Y.; Duan L.; Lin Y.; Wang R.
Article.Abstract: Gouteng is a traditional Chinese medicine widely used for the clinical treatment of epilepsy, yet the specific mechanism underlying its antiepileptic has not been elucidated. Network pharmacology, bioinformatics, machine learning, molecular docking, MD simulation, and ADMET druggability analysis were performed to systematically elucidate the molecular regulatory mechanism of Gouteng against epilepsy. The results showed that 29 active components of Gouteng collectively regulated 661 potential antiepileptic targets. Through screening with machine learning-based disease diagnostic model, MDM2 and PPARG as the core target genes mediating the antiepileptic effect of Gouteng were finally identified. Immune infiltration analysis confirmed that MDM2 and PPARG synergistically reshape the immune microenvironment of epileptic lesions, restrain excessive inflammatory responses, and maintain immune homeostasis and tolerance. Molecular docking and MD simulation revealed that the four core active components, namely Angustidine, Rhynchophylline A, vincoside lactam_qt, and coryincine, target the hydrophobic pocket of MDM2, with non-polar interactions serving as the primary driving factor for their interactions. ADMET analysis indicated that vincoside lactam_qt and coryincine exhibit favorable oral bioavailability, excellent blood-brain barrier permeability, and low hepatotoxicity, which make them potential antiepileptic candidate drugs with clinical translational potential. Most importantly, Gouteng exerts antiepileptic effects by targeting and regulating the dual MDM2-MDM4/TP53 and PPARG-NCOA1/RXRA regulatory axes, thereby mediating neuroinflammation inhibition and neuronal protection. Furthermore, TFAP2C as a common upstream transcription factor of both MDM2 and PPARG was identified. This study provides theoretical basis for the development of novel MDM2/PPARG-targeted antiepileptic drugs and for the clinical application of Gouteng.

Article.Title: Hippocampal teneurin-4 knockdown promotes depression-like behavioral phenotypes by disrupting oligodendrocyte differentiation in mice
Article.Authors: Sugimori Y.; Yano Y.; Asano T.; Suzuki S.; Kaigawa T.; Yokose J.; Shigetsura Y.; Muramatsu S.; Nitta A.
Article.Abstract: Depression is one of the most prevalent mental disorders worldwide. The limited clinical efficacy of current antidepressants highlights identifying new therapeutic targets. Emerging evidence suggests that dysfunction of oligodendrocyte lineage cells contributes to the pathophysiology of depression. Teneurin-4 (Tenm4), a transmembrane protein that promotes oligodendrocyte differentiation and myelination, has been implicated in psychiatric disorders in genome-wide association studies; however, its causal role remains unclear. To determine whether Tenm4 contributes to depressive-like behavioral phenotypes, we examined Tenm4 protein expression in mice exposed to repeated forced swimming stress and generated hippocampal Tenm4 knockdown (Tenm4KD) mice. Chronic stress reduced Tenm4 expression levels in the hippocampus. Mice with hippocampus-specific Tenm4KD exhibited depressive-like behaviors, accompanied by reduced hippocampal myelin basic protein. Importantly, administration of clemastine, a myelin formation promoter, inhibited the reduction of myelin and attenuated depression-like behavioral phenotypes. Immunohistochemical analysis showed that Tenm4KD significantly decreased the number of mature oligodendrocyte cells and increased in the number of oligodendrocyte precursor cells, without changes in the total number of oligodendrocyte lineage cells. This study provides the first evidence that hippocampal Tenm4 deficiency induces depression-like behavior phenotypes through impaired oligodendrocyte differentiation and promoting demyelination. Our results identify Tenm4 as a molecular regulator of stress-induced behavioral phenotypes and suggest that it might represent a potential therapeutic target for mood disorders associated with demyelination.
