Article.Title: Interpretable machine learning model based on radiomic features of hippocampal subfields for classifying zoster-associated pain
Article.Authors: Wen X.; Peng R.; Wang M.; Yu M.; Liu S.; Zhang D.; Ren C.; Chen G.
Article.Abstract: Postherpetic neuralgia (PHN), the most common complication of herpes zoster (HZ), is difficult to prevent due to limited understanding of the mechanisms underlying the transition from acute to chronic pain and the lack of objective neuroimaging biomarkers for individualized risk stratification. In this study, we aimed to develop interpretable machine learning models based on hippocampal subfield radiomics to classify zoster-associated pain (ZAP) patients and identify neuroimaging biomarkers reflecting microstructural alterations in hippocampus associated with ZAP. High-resolution 3D T1-weighted MR images were obtained from 28 PHN patients, 25 Hz patients, and 21 healthy controls (HCs). We extracted radiomic features of ten hippocampal subfields and used five machine learning classification algorithms to identify the most contributive subfield and robust model for classifying ZAP patients. Furthermore, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used to interpret the optimal model. In distinguishing ZAP patients from HCs, the SVM_Linear model based on the left subiculum radiomics achieved the highest performance with an AUC of 0.739, whereas the Logistic_L1 model based on the right CA4-DG and left SR-SL-SM radiomics showed the best performance with an AUC of 0.799 in distinguishing PHN patients from HZ patients. SHAP analysis revealed that SmallAreaEmphasis from the right CA4-DG subfield was the dominant feature for identifying PHN patients, followed by ClusterShade from the left SR-SL-SM subfield. Furthermore, both features showed strong associations with disease duration. These results suggest that hippocampal subfield radiomics can effectively stratify ZAP phases. Specifically, right CA4-DG radiomic features may serve as effective neuroimaging biomarkers associated with disease chronicity and have the potential for early risk stratification and intervention of ZAP.

Article.Title: Efficacy of eugenol against N, N′-Dimethyl-4,4′-bipyridinium dichloride (paraquat)-induced NA⁺/K⁺/CA²⁺ dysregulation and behavioral deficits in rat models
Article.Authors: Uchewa O.; Ibegbu A.; Chukwu V.; Igwe E.; Alobu E.; Cookey-Gam T.; Okoronkwo S.
Article.Abstract: Background: Ion level disruption causes mitochondrial aberration and alters cytochrome c activity. Purpose: To evaluate the efficacy of eugenol in Na+/K+/Ca2 + Cytochrome C dysregulation and behavioral deficits in Wistar rats. Methods: Forty male Wistar rats were acclimatised for two weeks and assigned to five groups of 8 rats. Group A received feed and normal saline. Groups B, C, D, and E received 10 mg/kg paraquat (PQ), and then C, D, and E received eugenol at graded doses of 200, 400, and 600 mg/kg. PQ was administered for 28 days at 1-day intervals, before the rats were treated with eugenol for 14 days via the oral route. Social interaction and depression-like behaviours were studied using a sociability chamber and a tail suspension box. Results: In Group B, interstitial Na+/K+ increased, while Ca2 + significantly decreased. In the treated groups, Na+/K+ and Ca2 + levels decreased and increased significantly, respectively. Cytochrome C, Caspase cleavage, and Full-length cytokeratin-18 were significantly increased in the untreated Group B and were reduced by eugenol (p < 0.05). In the PQ-untreated Group, social interaction and immobility were impaired, but eugenol attenuated these behavioral deficits. Dopamine levels and gamma-glutamyl transferase activities were lowered and increased in Group B, respectively, while eugenol increased and reduced them (p < 0.05). Microscopically, paraquat caused a significant loss of dopaminergic neurons, formation of Lewy bodies, and Pyknosis in the substantia nigra. Conclusions: Overall, eugenol shows valuable therapeutic potential against pesticide-induced neurotoxicity and associated ion dysregulation.

Article.Title: Epipharyngeal sensory stimulation is associated with changes in brainstem-cortical functional connectivity and circulating proteomic profiles
Article.Authors: Sakatani H.; Ueda R.; Tha K.; Murakami K.; Kitagawa M.; Kubota S.; Kono M.; Murakami M.; Hotomi M.
Article.Abstract: Neurostimulation has emerged as a potential approach for modulating autonomic and neuroimmune function. Because epipharyngeal mucosa receives sensory innervation from cranial afferents, mechanical stimulation of this region may engage neural pathways. Epipharyngeal abrasive therapy (EAT) involves mechanical and chemical stimulation of the epipharyngeal mucosa and is used clinically for chronic epipharyngitis; however, its central and systemic effects remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate whether epipharyngeal stimulation using EAT is associated with changes in brainstem functional connectivity and circulating proteomic profiles in healthy adults. Participants underwent five EAT sessions at 7-day intervals (Protocol A), with restingstate functional MRI performed before, immediately after, and four weeks after the first session. A subset also underwent a control protocol without EAT (Protocol B). Wholebrainstem seed-to-voxel functional connectivity was analyzed. Paired plasma samples collected before and after the first EAT session were analyzed using the SomaScan 11 K assay. Longitudinal analysis identified altered connectivity between the brainstem and subcallosal/medial frontal region, primarily immediately after EAT. A controlled withinsubject analysis identified an EAT-specific increase in connectivity between the brainstem and right temporal pole, extending into the inferior temporal gyrus. Proteomic analysis identified 13 proteins meeting exploratory screening criteria and significant pathway-level enrichment involving RNA metabolism, translation, and extracellular matrix organization. Mechanical and chemical stimulation of the epipharynx was associated with changes in brainstem-cortical functional connectivity and circulating proteomic signatures. These findings suggest that sensory stimulation of the epipharynx may engage cranial sensory afferent-brainstem pathways and contribute to coordinated central neural and peripheral molecular responses.

Article.Title: Neutrophil extracellular traps in ischemic stroke: Thrombolysis resistance, no-reflow, and hemorrhagic transformation
Article.Authors: Zhang S.; Cui Y.; Zhou X.; Wang D.; Cao Y.; Zhao H.; Sun Z.; Li Q.; Yin H.
Article.Abstract: Recanalization is central to acute ischemic stroke treatment. However, reopening an occluded artery does not always restore microvascular perfusion, and hemorrhagic transformation (HT) can occur regardless of recanalization success. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) may help explain these discordant outcomes because they act within occlusive thrombi, the downstream microcirculation, and the neurovascular interface. This review examines the roles of NETs in thrombolysis resistance, no-reflow, and hemorrhagic injury. Within thrombi, NET-associated chromatin reinforces clot architecture and limits fibrinolysis. Intravascular NETs may impede downstream microvascular flow after recanalization, while NET-related inflammatory signaling may aggravate blood-brain barrier disruption and HT. These findings implicate NETs in impaired recanalization, incomplete tissue reperfusion, and hemorrhagic injury and support their evaluation as an adjunctive target during reperfusion therapy.

Article.Title: S-equol mitigates anxiety-like behaviors associated with acute hyperuricemia by restoring neuronal excitability in the medial prefrontal cortex
Article.Authors: Sun Y.; Duan X.; Shi Y.; You W.; Tang Z.; Gao Y.; Lu H.; Wu X.
Article.Abstract: Hyperuricemia (HUA) is a prevalent metabolic disorder closely linked to neuropsychiatric symptoms, including emotional disturbances. However, the neural mechanisms underlying this association remain largely unexplored. We established a mouse model of acute HUA by administering potassium oxonate (PO) and hypoxanthine (HX) intraperitoneally to investigate its effects on emotional behaviors and neural activity in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC). The HUA mice exhibited typical hyperuricemia and renal morphological abnormalities, along with increased anxiety-like behaviors, but showed no alterations in mechanical/thermal pain sensitivity or depressive-like behaviors. Immunofluorescence c-Fos mapping revealed extensive activation in emotion-related brain regions, such as the mPFC, paraventricular thalamus (PVT), anterior insular cortex (aIC), lateral hypothalamus (LH), and basolateral amygdala (BLA). Whole-cell patch-clamp recordings demonstrated that HUA was associated with reduced intrinsic excitability of mPFC layer V/VI pyramidal neurons, indicated by a lower firing rate, higher rheobase, and decreased membrane input resistance. Additionally, it was associated with alterations in the excitatory/inhibitory (E/I) synaptic balance, including changes the frequency of spontaneous excitatory postsynaptic currents (sEPSCs). Notably, the reduction in mPFC neuronal excitability was comparable between sexes, although female HUA mice displayed less pronounced synaptic alterations in response to HUA. S-equol, a selective estrogen receptor beta ligand, ameliorated anxiety-like behaviors associated with HUA. Electrophysiological analyses revealed that S-equol appeared to restore the intrinsic excitability of mPFC pyramidal neurons in both sexes, although it did not significantly alter E/I synaptic balance. However, its behavioral effects exhibited sex-dependent differences: S-equol significantly ameliorated anxiety-like behaviors in both sexes, with the specific behavioral domains affected varying between males and females. The results suggest that HUA may be linked to anxiety-like behaviors, potentially involving reduced excitability of mPFC pyramidal neurons. Furthermore, S-equol may exert anxiolytic effects in association with restored neuronal excitability, independently of detectable changes in E/I synaptic balance. Together, this study offers new insights into the neurobiological mechanisms underlying HUA-related emotional disorders and identifies sex-specific potential therapeutic targets.

Article.Title: The PVN astrocyte–excitatory neuron functional axis mediates chronic stress-induced depressive-like behaviors
Article.Authors: Lv Y.; zheng T.; Chen J.; Lu B.; Chen Z.
Article.Abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a common psychiatric disorder, and accumulating evidence suggests that astrocytes play an important role in the regulation of emotional behaviors. However, the mechanisms by which astrocytes in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN) contribute to chronic stress-induced depression remain unclear. In this study, a chronic restraint stress (CRS) mouse model was established, and depressive-like behaviors were assessed using the sucrose preference test, open field test, tail suspension test, and forced swim test. Immunofluorescence staining, chemogenetic manipulation, fiber photometry, transcriptomic analysis, and quantitative real-time PCR were employed to investigate the role of PVN astrocytes and their interactions with excitatory neurons. CRS induced robust depressive-like behaviors and was accompanied by reactive astrocyte activation in the PVN, as evidenced by increased GFAP expression and morphological remodeling. Fiber photometry recordings revealed enhanced astrocytic calcium activity under both basal and stress-related behavioral conditions following CRS exposure. Chemogenetic activation of PVN astrocytes induced depressive-like behaviors in naïve mice, whereas inhibition of astrocytic activity alleviated depressive-like behaviors in CRS mice. Moreover, CRS increased c-Fos expression and calcium activity in CaMKIIα-positive excitatory neurons within the PVN. Bidirectional modulation of astrocyte activity correspondingly altered excitatory neuronal activity, indicating a functional coupling between these cell populations. Transcriptomic screening combined with qPCR validation further identified upregulated expression of the stress-responsive genes Timp4 and Manf in the PVN following CRS. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that PVN astrocytes are critical regulators of chronic stress-induced depressive-like behaviors and suggest that the PVN astrocyte-excitatory neuron functional axis represents a potential therapeutic target for depression.

Article.Title: High-fidelity and network-based spatio-temporal mathematical models of Alzheimer’s disease progression and their comparison with PET-SUVR imaging data
Article.Authors: Caon B.; Corti M.; Bonizzoni F.; Antonietti P.
Article.Abstract: Alzheimer's disease is the most common neurodegenerative disorder. Its pathological development is connected with the misfolding and accumulation of two toxic proteins: amyloid-β and tau proteins. Mathematical models provide a valuable quantitative tool for monitoring disease progression. In this work, we proposed and compare a novel framework where the spatio-temporal dynamics of amyloid-β and tau proteins is modeled based on employing either three-dimensional patient-specific geometries or through reduced network-based models defined on the brain connectome. More specifically, a high-fidelity biophysical model is proposed on three-dimensional brain geometries reconstructed from magnetic resonance imaging, whereas a network-based reduced formulation is defined on the brain connectome. For both approaches, a suitable numerical discretization is proposed. A sensitivity analysis is presented to quantify the influence of model parameters on protein concentration patterns as well as compare the quality of the predictions. For both approaches, the results are compared with group-level PET-SUVR clinical data using [18F]AZD4694 for amyloid-β and [18F]MK6240 for tau protein. The results indicate that the three-dimensional model provides the most accurate and biologically consistent description of the disease progression, but remains computationally demanding. On the other hand, the reduced graph-based model is cheaper, but it is not always able to achieve reliable results.

Article.Title: When Fakes Feel Real: Behavioral and Neural Mechanisms of Deepfake Hyperrealism in Younger and Older Adults
Article.Authors: Washburn S.; Lin T.; Zhu M.; Faulkner R.; Cahill B.; Lighthall N.; Ebner N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deepfakes are designed to mimic real people and constitute an emerging exploitation threat. They are potent methods of fraud as humans detect deepfake images at near or below chance levels, and deepfakes are frequently perceived as more real even than real images (deepfake hyperrealism). Anterior insula (aINS) function is implicated in processing salient, untrustworthy cues suggesting that low aINS recruitment during deepfake perception may underlie experiences of deepfake hyperrealism. Further, aging may confer increased experiences of deepfake hyperrealism, given increased susceptibility to deception and reduced aINS sensitivity to deceptive stimuli with age. Here, 156 participants (62 younger: 18-37 years, 94 older: 60-89 years) evaluated the realness of real and deepfake face images while undergoing fMRI. Behavioral results revealed deepfake hyperrealism in both age groups, with these effects more pronounced in older adults. Our imaging results indicated lower aINS activation was associated with higher realness ratings and aINS activity was also lower for deepfake than real images in both younger and older adults. These findings provide additional support for deepfake hyperrealism in perception, underscoring the threat of deepfakes as a method of exploitation across adulthood. Results also support that muted aINS response to deepfakes constitutes a neuromechanism in deception vulnerability.

Article.Title: mPFC-Dependent Valuation Shapes Information Sharing: Causal Evidence from tDCS and a Dyadic Social Media Paradigm
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Zhang Y.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Information sharing drives the spread of both accurate and misleading content, yet its psychological and neural mechanisms remain unclear. We investigated whether perceived self- and social relevance influence sharing through downstream content evaluations, and whether this process depends on medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) function. In a dyadic social media paradigm, 186 participants were assigned to anodal, cathodal, or sham tDCS over the mPFC. Senders judged 30 science news items (15 true and 15 false) on truthfulness, self-relevance, social relevance, interestingness, and importance before deciding whether to share each item with a real receiver. Structural equation modeling showed that self- and social relevance predicted sharing indirectly through evaluations of interestingness, importance, and truthfulness. mPFC stimulation did not reliably change sharing rates, but altered evaluative processing: it reduced perceived interestingness, and anodal stimulation produced a significant negative indirect pathway to sharing through reduced interestingness. Multi-group analyses indicated that these valuation pathways were invariant across true and false news. On the receiver side, social endorsement increased reading of shared items but had little effect on post-reading evaluations. Together, these findings support a causal contribution of mPFC-targeted neuromodulation to evaluative processing relevant to sharing, with limited evidence for a direct effect on sharing behavior.

Article.Title: Social relationship is associated with distinct patterns of inter-brain synchrony and directed connectivity during interpersonal coordination
Article.Authors: Han H.; Zhao Z.; Lin L.; Li C.; Jin X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract How social relationship and effector pairing relate to behavioral coordination and inter-brain interaction during joint timing remains unclear. Using functional near-infrared spectroscopy hyperscanning during a dyadic synchronization-continuation task, we examined 21 romantic couples and 23 stranger dyads performing hand-hand and hand-foot coordination. Romantic partners showed smaller tapping deviations than strangers during continuation, while hand–foot coordination was associated with greater tapping variability. Motor-region inter-brain synchrony (IBS) was greater in romantic partners than in strangers. True-dyad IBS exceeded the pseudo-dyad baseline in the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, corresponding differences were not detected in the motor cortex or left temporoparietal junction. Dynamic IBS analysis identified two recurrent configurations differing in synchrony strength and global efficiency, but state-transition frequency did not differ significantly between relationship groups. Granger-causality-based directed connectivity was stronger overall in stranger dyads, with female-to-male values exceeding those in the reverse direction. Together, these findings indicate that social relationship is associated with contrasting patterns of motor-region synchrony and directed connectivity, while effector pairing is associated with behavioral variability.

Article.Title: The gentle grip of beauty: Neural bases of motor inhibition during aesthetic appreciation
Article.Authors: Barbieri P.; Frascaroli J.; Varesio G.; Piovesan F.; Bechis L.; Sarasso P.; Ronga I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A century-old tradition characterizes aesthetic experiences as intense contemplative moments in which we suspend practical concerns and devote our full attention to the object at hand. In line with this tradition, recent theories suggest that aesthetic experiences involve heightened sensory processing accompanied by a suppression of motor activity. Yet, while the link between aesthetic appreciation and perceptual enhancement has received considerable attention, the role of motor inhibition remains largely unexplored. The present study addressed this gap by investigating whether the aesthetic appreciation of images can modulate behavioral and electrophysiological markers of motor inhibition. In Experiment 1, significantly slower reaction times following the observation of preferred images were found. In Experiment 2, EEG responses associated with motor preparation and execution were significantly reduced in trials involving preferred compared with non-preferred images. Time-frequency analysis revealed significantly decreased alpha power (associated with attentional engagement toward visual perception) and increased beta power (associated with inhibited motor preparation) for preferred than non-preferred images. Overall, our results provide new evidence for the existence of a relationship between aesthetic appreciation and motor inhibition and position aesthetic experience as a valuable case study for exploring the adaptive coordination of sensory and motor systems in response to environmental demands.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: beta power; aesthetic appreciation; motor inhibition; motor preparation; perceptual enhancement; sensorimotor coordination; aesthetic experience; alpha power

Article.Title: Hylocereus undatus peel extract and ZnO nanoparticles suppress cancer through apoptosis and Wnt/β-catenin inhibition
Article.Authors: Tawfik M.; Barakat L.; Elfeky H.; El-Zend M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cancer treatment faces the challenge of multidrug resistance and systemic cytotoxicity. This study explores the anticancer potential of Hylocereus undatus peel extracts and their biogenically synthesized zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs). Total phenolics, flavonoids and GC–MS profiles of the extracts were determined. Then, ZnO NPs were synthesized by using aqueous and n-hexane extracts and characterized by FTIR, Zeta Potential, XRD, SEM, EDX, and TEM. Among all tested formulations, ZnO NPs-AE (derived from the aqueous extract) showed the strongest antitumor activity, both in cell culture (Caco‑2 and HepG2) and in the Ehrlich ascites carcinoma mouse model. In MTT assays, ZnO NPs-AE was highly cytotoxic to Caco‑2 and HepG2 cells (IC₅₀ = 9.22 and 12.93 µg/mL, respectively) and performed on the same level as doxorubicin ( p < 0.05). It also showed a more favourable selectivity profile, being less toxic to normal colon fibroblasts (CCD‑18Co; IC₅₀ = 32.35 µg/mL) than to Caco‑2 cells (IC₅₀ = 9.22 µg/mL), which was better than doxorubicin. Consistent with this, ZnO NPs-AE reduced the proportion of cells in G2/M phase (7.39% compared with 12.65% in untreated cells) and increased total apoptosis to 25.98% in Caco‑2 cells. Molecularly, it up-regulated caspase-3 (6.15-fold), down-regulated topoisomerase II (0.33-fold) and suppressed the Wnt/β catenin axis. Consistently, ELISA quantification of Axin2 and Cyclin D1 in Caco‑2 cells confirmed down‑regulation of these Wnt/β‑catenin targets in parallel with the decrease in β‑catenin protein. In vivo, ZnO NPs-AE (5 mg/kg) reduced EAC volume to 89.36%, normalized hepatic/renal biomarkers, improved lipid profiles, and alleviated oxidative stress by elevating GSH, CAT, and SOD levels, while reducing MDA, alongside histopathological improvements. Overall, ZnO NPs-AE represents a promising, well tolerated biogenic nanoplatform for targeted cancer therapy.

Article.Title: Attributing compound flood impact from tropical cyclone Idai in Mozambique to climate and population change
Article.Authors: Vertegaal D.; van den Hurk B.; Couasnon A.; Paprotny D.; Muis S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Impacts of extreme weather events are a complex interplay of compounding climatic and socio-economic drivers. In this paper, we attribute the effect of climate and population change on the number of people exposed to flooding from tropical cyclone (TC) Idai, making landfall in Mozambique in 2019. We apply an extended storyline attribution framework based on a globally-applicable model chain to simulate compound flooding and exposed population as a proxy for impact under factual and counterfactual climate and population conditions. This enables impact attribution to both drivers, and disaggregation across flood depth categories and socio-economic groups. Under the selected storyline experiments, 84% of the exposed population is attributable to the combined effect of climate and population change since 1975, with population change alone accounting for 80% and climate change alone for 9%. Climate change increases flood extent and flood depth, whereas population change alters the number of people living in the flooded area. These drivers change the distribution of people exposed to flooding, leading to different attribution assessments per flood depth category. Our results indicate that the effect of climate change is not evenly distributed across socio-economic groups, which is masked when spatially aggregating the attribution assessment.

Article.Title: Randomized trial of pressure controlled versus volume controlled ventilation during robot assisted urological surgery in the clasp knife position
Article.Authors: Cai X.; Chen J.; Lin W.; Wen L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The combination of CO₂ pneumoperitoneum and clasp-knife position imposes substantial respiratory and hemodynamic challenges in Da Vinci robot-assisted urological surgery. Although volume-controlled ventilation (VCV) and pressure-controlled ventilation (PCV) are widely used, their comparative effects under these specific surgical conditions remain unclear. We hypothesized that PCV could reduce peak inspiratory pressure (Ppeak) and improve dynamic lung compliance (Cdyn) without compromising hemodynamic stability. The trial was retrospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06056401). We randomized 62 ASA I–II patients to VCV (n = 30) or PCV (n = 32). Study measurements were discontinued in two PCV patients after randomization because of intraoperative bleeding, leaving 60 participants for the following analyses. Ventilatory parameters, hemodynamic variables, and arterial blood gas values were recorded at five time points: T1 (15 min after induction), T2 (15 min after clasp-knife positioning), T3 (30 min after CO₂ pneumoperitoneum), T4 (60 min after CO₂ pneumoperitoneum), and T5 (15 min after pneumoperitoneum removal). Ppeak showed a significant ventilation mode × time interaction ( P < 0.001). Lower Ppeak was observed in the PCV group at T2–T5, with the largest differences during pneumoperitoneum at T3 and T4. Cdyn also showed a significant ventilation mode × time interaction ( P = 0.012), with higher values under PCV at several measurement points. No significant ventilation mode × time interactions were observed for the measured arterial blood gas variables. No significant ventilation mode × time interactions were observed for the principal hemodynamic variables. No severe postoperative complications occurred during the 72-hour follow-up. PCV and VCV showed different intraoperative respiratory-mechanical profiles, including lower Ppeak and different Cdyn trajectories under PCV. No differential arterial blood gas or hemodynamic trajectories were observed, and the clinical significance of these physiological differences remains uncertain.

Article.Title: Intelligent clinical decision support system for intracranial aneurysm lesion-based detection using biomedical imaging data
Article.Authors: Praveena S.; Murali Krishna V.; Sonthi V.; Gottumukkala D.; Pattanaik C.; Behera N.; Bansal K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract An intracranial aneurysm (IA) is a type of cerebrovascular condition that occurs due to focal bulging or expansion in the wall of a cerebral artery, most frequently affecting the internal carotid artery. An IA is seemingly connected with conditions such as fibrous dysplasia, adult-dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), and coarctation of aorta. A ruptured brain aneurysm can result in a severe and life-threatening subarachnoid hemorrhage if not treated early, often leading to long-lasting neurological damage and a higher chance of death. However, the traditional diagnostic technique is time-consuming, and it necessitates a trained and skilled medical practitioner. Hence, building an automated model to help physicians precisely detect IA can reduce the clinicians’ burden. Recently, deep learning has gained significant interest in the domain of medical imaging as it automatically learns patterns and accurately detects several types of diseases, such as IAs. Therefore, this article introduces a Clinical Decision Support System for Intracranial Aneurysm Lesion-Based Detection (CDSS-IALD). The main purpose of this work is to develop a robust system that can automatically detect and identify intracranial aneurysms using medical imaging data to assist clinicians with treatment decisions. Initially, the proposed CDSS-IALD model pre-processes the input biomedical images using image normalization, noise reduction, contrast improvement, and skull stripping to refine image quality and consistency for subsequent analysis. Following that, a ConvNeXt hierarchical model is employed for feature extraction, which effectively extracts local details and global context from pre-processed images. Finally, these extracted representations are then forwarded to a spiking neural network, which performs accurate aneurysm detection and classification. To ensure the enhanced performance of the CDSS-IALD system, extensive experiments were conducted on the benchmark Intracranial Aneurysm Dataset. The experimental outcomes clearly demonstrate the betterment of the proposed CDSS-IALD system over the other approaches in detecting and localizing intracranial aneurysms from biomedical imaging.

Article.Title: Surveillance epidemiology and an open machine-learning benchmark of antimicrobial-resistant healthcare-associated infections in a Chinese district hospital
Article.Authors: Han D.; Hu Y.; Shu X.; Zou H.; Wang C.; Peng X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) drives a growing share of healthcare-associated infection (HAI) mortality; however, data resources from Chinese hospitals outside university referral networks remain scarce. We conducted a retrospective analysis of 39 months of prospectively collected, hospital-wide HAI surveillance data (February 2023–April 2026) from a 1,100-bed district-level general hospital (accredited Class III Grade A) in Chongqing, China, comprising 1,240 episodes among 1,054 patients across 256,993 admissions and 1.14 million patient-days. The hospital-wide episode incidence was stable at 0.48 per 100 admissions and 0.82 per 1,000 patient-days, with no seasonal pattern or residual autocorrelation. Acinetobacter baumannii was the leading pathogen (19.4% of isolates), with carbapenem resistance reaching 92.0% hospital-wide and 98.5% in the intensive care unit, exceeding national benchmarks. Mechanical ventilation, bedridden status, central venous catheterization, and stroke were enriched among resistant infections (odds ratios 2.4–5.2; all Bonferroni-adjusted p ≤ 0.001). We then benchmarked three transparent machine-learning baselines on routinely collected, pre-infection variables using patient-grouped, 10 × 5-fold repeated cross-validation. AMR phenotype prediction achieved a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.74–0.75 (area under the precision–recall curve 0.55–0.56 against a prevalence of 0.31) for logistic regression and random forest, whereas infection-site classification was not clinically useful (accuracy 0.39–0.52 versus a 0.46 majority-class baseline). A previously reported AUROC of 0.91 was traced to two forms of leakage (patient overlap between partitions and inclusion of total length of stay) and is corrected here. The de-identified dataset, bilingual codebook, and complete reproducibility pipeline are deposited under permissive licences, providing an open, leakage-audited benchmark for AMR prediction research in an under-represented hospital tier.

Article.Title: A lightweight closed-loop adaptive intrusion detection framework for cyber resilience in critical infrastructure
Article.Authors: Al Ghamdi M.; Alghamdi I.; Alzahrani R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Most operators of energy, health, or transport facilities do not have at their disposal the kind of computational resources that large-scale deep-learning detectors require. Being energy and health care and transportation facility operators, they seek an intrusion detection approach that is responsive to environmental changes. We present one such lightweight alternative. At the core of such an approach is a regularized Logistic Regression-based detector, with the closed loop comprising context-aware thresholding, behavioral profiling, recent error-rate feedback, budget-limited incremental updates, and deception-derived observations from outside. None of these approaches is, in itself, novel. Our contribution lies in the coupling of these mechanisms to displace the decision threshold using contextual and behavioral signals and in detecting confirmed outcomes that are then fed back to update the classifier, the behavioral baseline, and future decisions. We conduct the model evaluation on two levels of abstraction. The confirmation dataset includes 39,919 SWaT instances segmented into 40 nonoverlapping time windows, validated over StratifiedGroupKFold with a per-instance allowance of no more than 256 analyst-validated instances. In an ablation study over 25 such splits comparing the full model to the Logistic Regression with the static threshold, the full model achieved an F1 of 0.7526 ± 0.1074 compared with only 0.5719 ± 0.1578 for the latter (Holm adjusted p < 0.001). Most of the contribution came from budgeted incremental learning; without it, F1 dropped by 0.1704. Feedback using error rates was less important but still significant, returning 0.0048 in F1 together with a lower false positive rate. Behavioral profiling did not affect the F1 and improved specificity. Context-aware thresholding increased the false positive rate while yielding no improvement in the F1; thus, this is reported as a trade-off rather than an improvement. There were no significant contrasts with respect to the Holm correction; hence, we do not claim any synergy. Batch Logistic Regression with matching scored 0.7065 ± 0.1254 in terms of F1 score compared with Decision Tree, Random Forest, Linear SVM, Extra Trees, and MLP, none being significantly different from batch Logistic Regression. Because the labels were equally split among 256, all feedback mechanisms outperformed the case with no feedback, going from an F1 of 0.5845 ± 0.1495 to between 0.7292 and 0.7676. The deception-prioritized proxy did not make it into the winners. It beat no feedback but lost to random sampling on all the metrics that we examined. We have, therefore, referenced the previously published simulation and emulation figures as exploratory studies illustrating the behavior of this architecture. In toto, the framework is efficient and competitive under the tested conditions, and nothing herein suggests classifier superiority or a deception-specific advantage or true zero-day detection or readiness for a live plant.

Article.Title: FS-VMADW: a frequency–spatial vision mamba framework for dual watermarking of medical MRI images
Article.Authors: Ur Rehman A.; Lee C.; Li L.; Khan F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Secure transmission and copyright protection of medical images require watermarking methods that preserve image quality and enable reliable payload recovery. However, the currently available deep watermarking architectures either encode only a single watermark or use convolutional networks with inherently restricted receptive fields, which limits their ability to capture long-range anatomical dependencies in medical images. Moreover, spatial modeling alone does not explicitly capture the frequency characteristics that influence watermark imperceptibility and robustness. This work proposes FS-VMADW - a Frequency-Spatial Vision Mamba Dual Watermarking architecture for abdominal MRI security. The proposed encoder combines the Vision Mamba spatial branch with a four-direction selective scan of state-space models applied with linear complexity, along with a two-stage Haar Discrete Wavelet Transform frequency branch, which are fused with a gating module generating location-specific weighting of spatial and frequency feature maps. Two independent spread-spectrum carriers encode two 64-bit binary watermarks, while an adaptively generated Vision Mamba mask controls their embedding. A two-phase training curriculum mitigates the gradient conflict between imperceptibility and extraction fidelity by decoupling the two objectives across successive training phases. Experiments on the CHAOS abdominal MRI benchmark demonstrate PSNR = 42.37 dB, SSIM = 0.9557, NC = 0.9511, BER = 0.0491, and BitAcc = 0.9509 under clean conditions. Controlled backbone comparisons further show that Vision Mamba outperforms CNN and Transformer alternatives, while the addition of DWT provides further improvements in both imperceptibility and watermark recovery. These results demonstrate that long-range spatial modeling and multi-scale frequency information provide complementary benefits for dual watermarking of medical images.

Article.Title: Sleep disturbances and their association with quality of life and depressive symptoms among elderly residents of long-term care facilities: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Wójcik-Pędziwiatr M.; Kontowicz E.; Dębska G.; Rudzińska-Bar M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sleep disturbances are common in later life and may be particularly relevant among residents of long-term care facilities, where multiple clinical and functional factors can affect sleep and well-being. Evidence concerning the relationship between sleep disturbances, depressive symptoms, and quality of life among institutionalized older adults in Central and Eastern Europe remains limited. This cross-sectional study included 80 residents aged ≥ 60 years from two long-term care facilities in Poland. Sleep was assessed using the Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS). Depressive symptoms, functional independence, cognitive functioning, and quality of life were evaluated using the 30-item Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS-30), Barthel Index, Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), and WHOQOL-BREF, respectively. Associations were examined using Spearman’s rank correlations and multivariable regression models accounting for available potential confounders. Insomnia symptoms (AIS ≥ 6) were present in 50 participants (62.5%), poor sleep quality (PSQI > 5) in 42 (52.5%), and increased daytime sleepiness (ESS ≥ 10) in 21 (26.3%). Depressive symptoms above the adopted GDS-30 cut-off were identified in 37 participants (46.3%). Greater insomnia severity and poorer sleep quality were associated with more severe depressive symptoms and lower scores in several WHOQOL-BREF domains in unadjusted analyses. After adjustment for depressive symptoms and available clinical and functional covariates, the associations between sleep measures and quality-of-life domains were attenuated. Sleep disturbances were common in this selected sample of long-term care residents with relatively preserved cognitive functioning and were associated with depressive symptoms and poorer quality of life in cross-sectional analyses. However, these relationships were attenuated after accounting for relevant covariates. Given the cross-sectional design, selected study population, and potential residual confounding, the findings should not be interpreted as evidence of causal relationships.

Article.Title: Evaluation of performance and emissions of a diesel engine using dual aqueous ammonia -diesel fuel
Article.Authors: El-Fakharany M.; Gad M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The carbon footprint of fossil fuel application is a crucial indicator of the overall quantity of greenhouse gases discharged into the atmosphere. Sustainable replacements, such as aqueous ammonia, are viewed as a good approach to solve the shortage of conventional fuel, low-carbon fuels and address climate change. Emissions and performance of diesel engine running on dual fuel of diesel and aqueous ammonia were investigated. Ammonia and water were combined in volumetric amounts of 5, 10, and 15% to get around these adverse effects. Adding aqueous ammonia of 5, 10 and 15% to diesel boosted brake specific fuel consumption by 4, 7, and 13% at 75% of engine output power. Thermal efficiency of diesel and aqueous ammonia were decreased by 4, 7 and 13% when aqueous ammonia was added by 5, 10 and 15%. Aqueous ammonia of 5%, 10% and 15% demonstrated increases of 17, 32 and 42% in CO emissions about diesel, whereas the decreases in nitrogen oxides were 5, 10 and 15% in relation to diesel, respectively. At 100% of output power, increases in hydrocarbon emissions for 5%, 10%, and 15% aqueous ammonia were 10, 23, and 31% but carbon dioxide values were decreased by 6, 12, and 17% for diesel with aqueous ammonia compared to diesel oil. Increases of oxygen concentrations for 5%, 10% and 15% aqueous ammonia were 6, 8 and 10%, respectively at 75% of output power. Engine performance penalties and emissions issues limit the use of aqueous ammonia, despite its potential as a carbon-reducing supplemental fuel.

Article.Title: Formulating a training strategy for tactical swimmers: an integrated approach using the modified Delphi method and an intuitionistic fuzzy three-dimensional eight-octant distribution
Article.Authors: Zheng C.; Lin K.; Chang K.; Tsai W.; Chu H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Tactical swimming enhances the operational effectiveness of military personnel in diverse maritime missions. Compared with conventional swimming, tactical swimming places greater demands on endurance, speed, and load-bearing capacity. Inadequate warm-ups or improper daily training may result in sports injuries, thereby compromising combat readiness. This study employed the modified Delphi method to develop stretching exercise evaluation indices specifically tailored to tactical swimming. Eighteen cadets from a Taiwan military academy were recruited as participants and provided intuitionistic fuzzy evaluations of stretching exercises, along with assessments of their swimming abilities. A three-dimensional eight-octant distribution was subsequently applied to formulate tactical swimming training strategies. The results identified 11 key stretching indices and revealed that two participants (M2 and M4) demonstrated the highest performance. This study identified inter-individual differences and provided recommendations for improving group performance and guiding future tactical swimming training.

Article.Title: Silencing of LOXL4 inhibits colorectal cancer progression via regulating GLS1-dependent glutamine metabolism
Article.Authors: Qu P.; Wang M.; Luo F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lysyl oxidase-like 4 (LOXL4) is frequently overexpressed in colorectal cancer (CRC) and associated with poor clinical prognoses. However, the metabolic mechanisms underlying LOXL4-driven CRC progression remain poorly elucidated. This study investigated the biological function of LOXL4 in CRC and its potential as a therapeutic target. We detected LOXL4 expression in paired CRC and normal tissues via western blot, qRT-PCR, IHC and flow cytometry. CRISPR-Cas9 was used to construct LOXL4 knockout SW480 and HT-29 cells, and multiple functional assays assessed cell proliferation, migration and invasion. Integrated proteomics and targeted metabolomics screened glutamine metabolic alterations, with the glutaminase 1 (GLS1) inhibitor CB-839 for functional validation. AOM/DSS-induced CRC mouse models were built to evaluate in vivo tumor growth. LOXL4 was significantly upregulated in clinical CRC samples. LOXL4 knockout suppressed malignant behaviors of CRC cells in vitro. Combined proteomic and metabolomic profiling confirmed GLS1 downregulation in LOXL4-knockout cells, accompanied by glutamine accumulation and glutamate reduction. Exogenous glutamate supplementation enhances the proliferative and migratory capacities of LOXL4-knockout tumor cells. LOXL4-knockout mice developed fewer, smaller intestinal tumors and milder weight loss. CB-839-mediated GLS1 inhibition synergistically strengthened the anti-tumor effect of LOXL4 deletion. LOXL4 silencing restrains CRC progression via a novel mechanism of GLS1 downregulation and intracellular glutamine accumulation. GLS1 pharmacological blockade further potentiates the anti-cancer efficacy of LOXL4 depletion, highlighting complex metabolic dependence in CRC.

Article.Title: Prevention of parasite infection in birds: adaptive advantages of anting behaviour
Article.Authors: Ohkawara K.; Kamei Y.; Akino T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Anting, the application of ants to plumage, has been reported in more than 200 bird species worldwide. The advantage of the peculiar behaviour is hypothesized to be self-treatment against parasites and bacteria because many ant species eject pungent fluids from their exocrine glands, which might help remove ecto- and microparasites from bird’s body. However, this hypothesis has not been well explored. In this study, by using thrush Turdus cardis and two ant species, Lasius spathepus and L. nipponensis , it was tested whether any chemical components on bird’s body surface were altered by anting and whether any ectoparasites were excluded or repelled from the bird’s body. Artificial ant treatments and GC analysis revealed the chemical components on body surface of T. cardis were remarkably altered by anting. Specifically, dendrolasin, a species-specific volatile chemical in the two ants, was added to the body. The anting treatments were significantly effective in removing ectoparasites, louse flies and dipteran insects. Insecticidal effects also were confirmed. Additional experiments showed dendrolasin and some chemical components had directly repellent effects on dipteran insects. It suggests the advantages of anting include the exclusion of harmful dipteran insects and preventive medication for the diseases they introduce, such as avian malaria.

Article.Title: No detectable BK polyomavirus or JC polyomavirus DNA in FFPE specimens from patients with advanced laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
Article.Authors: Doulaptsi M.; Tseliou M.; Karatzanis A.; Akoumianakis E.; Tzardi M.; Prokopakis E.; Velegrakis G.; Sourvinos G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Human polyomaviruses (HPyVs) exhibit oncogenic potential, and Merkel cell polyomavirus (MCPyV) is an established cause of Merkel cell carcinoma. While BK and JC polyomaviruses possess oncogenic properties, their etiological contribution to head and neck squamous cell carcinomas, specifically laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) remains highly controversial. This study aimed to evaluate the presence of BK polyomavirus (BKPyV) and JC polyomavirus (JCPyV) in advanced LSCC to clarify their potential role. Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tumor specimens were obtained retrospectively from 35 patients with advanced (pT3–pT4a) LSCC treated with total laryngectomy. BKPyV and JCPyV DNA was investigated by real-time PCR, with co-amplification of the human β-globin gene as an internal control for DNA amplifiability and PCR inhibition. Amplifiable genomic DNA was confirmed in all 35 samples. No JCPyV or BKPyV DNA was detected in any specimen (0/35 for each virus; 95% CI 0–10.0%). The absence of detectable JCPyV and BKPyV genomes in the examined specimens does not support a frequent or persistent presence of BKPyV and JCPyV in advanced LSCC. However, we cannot definitively exclude transient early-stage viral involvement, low-level infection or varying prevalence in different populations.

Article.Title: Landscape heterogeneity is structured by multidimensional components and land-cover proportion interactions
Article.Authors: Bae S.; Westphal C.; Ammer C.; Hostert P.; Hüttel S.; Kis-Katos K.; Kneib T.; Kreft H.; Paul C.; Plieninger T.; Putzenlechner B.; Rötter R.; Schlund M.; Seidel D.; Siebert S.; Wiegand K.; Knohl A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Landscape heterogeneity is a key driver of biodiversity, ecosystem functioning, and resilience. However, its multiple components—compositional, configurational, vertical, and temporal— are rarely analysed together at broad spatial scales. Compositional heterogeneity refers to the number and proportions of different elements, configurational heterogeneity to their spatial arrangement and shape, vertical heterogeneity to variation in vegetation height, and temporal heterogeneity to interannual variation in land cover and management. Here we examine relationships among these components across forests, croplands, and grasslands using nationwide geospatial data from Germany. We show that compositional and configurational heterogeneity (Shannon diversity vs. edge density) are positively correlated, although their relationship varied with land-cover proportions. Contrary to common assumptions, configurational heterogeneity does not enhance habitat connectivity. Vertical and temporal heterogeneity are largely independent from horizontal heterogeneity. Forests are the main contributors to landscape heterogeneity across land-cover types, whereas croplands contribute little or even negatively. These findings highlight the importance of considering land-cover proportions and multi-dimensional heterogeneity when assessing landscape structure. Our results have broad implications for environmental monitoring and planning for biodiversity and ecosystem assessments, offering a framework to avoid hidden collinearity and consider multi-dimensional perspective and socio-ecological context.

Article.Title: Genomic surveillance identifies shared Salmonella clusters and antimicrobial resistance across dogs, raw pet food and humans
Article.Authors: Chattaway M.; Painset A.; Martelli F.; Mackintosh A.; Jorgensen F.; Ismail Ahmed A.; Greig D.; Pulford C.; Wise G.; Snow L.; Lawes J.; Griffiths-Jones S.; Bottery M.; Hopkins S.; Godbole G.; Petrovska L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The emergence of antimicrobial resistant Salmonella poses growing public health challenges, with companion animals and their diets representing under recognised transmission routes. Despite increasing use of raw pet food (RPF) and statutory reporting of canine Salmonella infections, limited genomic data have been used to investigate potential transmission pathways and their implications for human health. In order to identify potential zoonotic links and characterise antimicrobial resistance, we conducted a genomic analysis of Salmonella spp. isolates from dogs ( n = 1,017) and raw meat pet food ( n = 206) collected between 2006 and 2024 through a collaborative surveillance programme. All isolates underwent whole genome sequencing (WGS), and comparative genomic analysis was performed against human clinical isolates. Among 1,223 sequenced isolates, 676 unique 5 SNP single linkage clusters, across 29 different Salmonella serovars were identified. Overall, 27.2% (148/545) of canine isolates and 23.7% (27/114) of RPF isolates were genetically related to human cases, with 88.2% (15/17) of shared dog–RPF isolates also clustering with human infections. Multi-drug resistant (MDR) strains, including those resistant to critically important antimicrobials, were detected in both dogs and RPF. Salmonella Typhimurium predominated across human and canine isolates including the distribution of MDR within multiple clusters. These findings highlight the zoonotic risk associated with dogs and raw pet food within domestic settings, underscoring the need for targeted public health messaging and strengthened One Health genomic surveillance.

Article.Title: Effects of hydrothermal aging on the wear behavior, mechanical properties, and microstructure of a multilayered zirconia
Article.Authors: Souza K.; Campos T.; Demachkia A.; da Cruz B.; de Carvalho Ramos N.; Thim G.; de Melo R.; Bottino M.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated the effects of hydrothermal aging on the wear, surface roughness, mechanical properties, and crystalline composition of multilayered zirconia. Blocks (14 × 14 × 1.5 mm) fabricated from multilayered zirconia (IPS e.max ZirCAD Prime, Ivoclar Vivadent) were divided into non-aged and aged groups and subjected to cyclic loading (150 N, 4 Hz, 600,000 cycles) with a horizontal sliding. The following analyses were performed: wear volume, surface roughness, XRD, EDS, SEM, Vickers hardness, and fracture toughness. Wear measurements were analyzed using Student’s t-test. Surface roughness was analyzed using ANOVA On ranks and Dunn’s test. Hardness and fracture toughness were evaluated based on the overlap of confidence intervals. XRD, EDS, and SEM were qualitatively analyzed. Hydrothermal aging significantly increased the wear volume of the multilayered zirconia to 27.8 × 10⁵±10.3 × 10⁵µm³, but decreased the surface roughness in the worn area. Aging induced phase transformation only in the 3Y-TZP layer and transition zone. Hardness was increased in the 3Y-TZP region, and fracture toughness increased in the transition zone and 3Y-TZP layer after aging. Overall, hydrothermal aging did not adversely affect the evaluated mechanical properties, indicating that the material has low susceptibility to hydrothermal degradation, which may be favorable for clinical application. However, the observed phase transformation may contribute to reduced wear resistance. Additionally, the distinct responses of the individual layers of multilayered zirconia to hydrothermal aging should be considered during clinical decision-making.

Article.Title: Progressive decline in EEG low frequency spectral power during overnight sleep
Article.Authors: Ghosn S.; Araujo M.; Bilal E.; Foldvary-Schaefer N.; Mehra R.; Beck K.; Rogers J.; Saab C.
Article.Abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a cornerstone in the analysis of sleep architecture and sleep disorders. Prior studies describe decreases in EEG power towards the end of overnight sleep. However, most of these observations are based on small samples, rely in part on qualitative analyses, do not characterize EEG power at intermediate stages, and do not examine all sleep stages. Importantly, the possible relation between a dynamic change in EEG power and health outcomes was not explored. We sought to compute power in sleep stages for the first, middle, and last instances of sleep using automated, quantitative EEG methods leveraging 10,000 high-resolution overnight polysomnography cases. Results confirm that power in the 1–20 Hz range during the last instances of all sleep stages is significantly decreased compared to first instances. However, power increases in the delta and theta bands during the middle instances of N1 and N2. For N1, the decline in power follows a linear trend. These changes were not uniform across brain regions, and correlations between the EEG power decrease and clinical outcomes were statistically significant albeit with modest effect size. Thus, our work provides a rigorous, large-scale analysis of temporal trends of EEG power across the overnight sleep period, revealing novel dynamics and a potential impact on health beyond sleep disorders.

Article.Title: Piracetam attenuates cyclophosphamide-evoked pulmonary injury in rats; the role of AMPK/NF-κB/NLRP3/caspase-1 and caspase-3 mediated apoptosis signaling cascades
Article.Authors: Mohyeldin R.; Sharata E.; Ibrahim A.; Attya M.; Kotb A.; Ali F.; Abdelzaher W.; Rofaeil R.; Abdelnaser M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cyclophosphamide (CP) is often employed in the treatment of numerous malignancies and autoimmune diseases, although it is accompanied by numerous side effects. Piracetam (PIRA) is used as a nootropic agent and reported to possess antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic properties in addition to its established cognitive-enhancing effects. This study aimed to investigate the potential protective effects of PIRA against CP-induced lung damage in rats. CP was utilized to provoke pulmonary damage. Molecular docking was performed to predict the binding affinity of piracetam for NF-κB p65, NLRP3, caspase-1, caspase-3, and AMPK. Arterial blood gas parameters (PaO₂ and PaCO₂) were assessed to evaluate pulmonary gas-exchange function. The lung contents of MDA, GSH, and CAT activity were measured. Levels of lung IL-18, IL-1β, TNF-α, and caspase-1 were evaluated using ELISA. Immunohistochemistry was employed to evaluate NF-κB p65 and caspase-3. The Western blot technique was utilized to evaluate the protein expression of NLRP3 and p-AMPK. Lung Bax and Bcl-2 gene expression was assessed using qRT-PCR. The histological examination of lung tissues was conducted. Molecular docking revealed favorable binding affinities of piracetam. CP caused a notable reduction in PaO₂ and elevation in PaCO₂, alongside a notable increase in lung MDA, IL-18, IL-1β, TNF-α, caspase-1, and Bax levels, with a substantial reduction in GSH, CAT, p-AMPK, and Bcl-2. CP administration also led to the upregulation of NLRP3 protein. Additionally, the immunopositivity of both NF-κB p65 and caspase-3 was elevated in the CP group. PIRA markedly ameliorated all previously described functional, biochemical, and histopathological anomalies. PIRA pretreatment significantly improved CP-induced pulmonary injury, an effect associated with suppression of NF-κB/NLRP3/caspase-1 and caspase-3 signaling and with increased p-AMPK expression.

Article.Title: Role of bio-polymeric binders on combustion and fire suppression performance of KNO3/KClO4–3,5 DNB pyrotechnic composite
Article.Authors: Kumar R.; Niringiyimana E.; Gautam N.; Rathee P.; Rana K.
Article.Abstract: Traditional pyrotechnic composites (PCs), often synthesized with epoxy or other synthetic binders, can combust at temperatures up to ​ 2100 °C, creating secondary fire and explosion risks. This study examines how renewable, cost-effective binders: starch, guar gum, tannic acid, and sodium carboxymethyl cellulose affect the combustion behavior, exothermicity, temperature profiles, and fire-suppression performance of PCs in a 4.57 kW n-heptane pool fire. Characterization of the aerosol particulates was performed using XRD, FTIR, and SEM. SEM-EDX and DSC for the PCs. PC-1, with a linear burning rate (LBR) of 10.05 ± 2.158 mm/s, extinguished the fire within 5 s and generated the highest ignition temperature (210 °C), whereas PC-4 and PC-5 with LBRs of 9.3 ± 0.742 mm/s and 9.7 ± 0.693 mm/s, respectively showed a noticeable decrease in ignition temperatures (184 °C and 182 °C, respectively) and suppressed the fire within 7 s and 5 s, respectively. It can be concluded that starch-based PC exhibited optimal fire performance parameters, making it a promising bio-based binder for the KNO 3 -KClO 4 -3, 5 DNB pyrotechnic composition.

Article.Title: Integrated recovery of rare earth elements and transition metals from spent NiMH batteries
Article.Authors: Kaplan S.; Dizdar B.; Emil-Kaya E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Spent nickel-metal hydride batteries are concentrated secondary resources rich in transition metals (TM) and critical rare earth elements (REE). This study compares two integrated hydrometallurgical routes exploiting different solution chemistries: (i) sulfuric-acid leaching followed by bulk REE precipitation and (ii) methanesulfonic-acid (MSA) leaching followed by targeted oxidative removal of Ce. In the sulfate route, TM dissolution was favored (approximately 98% Ni at 60 °C), whereas REE extraction remained within approximately 40–60% over the investigated temperature range. La extraction further decreased to approximately 42% at 3 mol.L −1 H 2 SO 4 , consistent with the limited solubility of REE sulfate species. Following leaching and pH adjustment, the precipitation percentages of La, Ce, and Nd exceeded 98%. In the MSA route, the high solubility of metal methanesulfonates prevented this sulfate related limitation and enabled approximately 95–99% extraction of La, Ni, and Co at 60 °C, together with near-complete La dissolution at a 1/30 g.mL −1 solid-to-liquid ratio. Subsequent addition of 6 vol.% H 2 O 2 at pH 4 resulted in 94% Ce removal, consistent with selective oxidative precipitation, while most other metals remained predominantly in solution. The sulfate route therefore introduces TM–REE selectivity during leaching and enables collective REE recovery, whereas the MSA route prioritizes comprehensive dissolution and postpones selectivity to a targeted downstream step. These results show that the preferred route depends on the desired product streams: early group separation and bulk REE recovery, or near-complete metal dissolution followed by Ce-first separation.

Article.Title: A statistical framework for laser-induced subsurface modification and cracking in 4H-SiC
Article.Authors: Mir H.; Schillinger-Engel K.; Nekarda J.; Preu R.; Meyer F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Laser slicing of 4H-SiC enables low-kerf wafer separation, but reproducible subsurface crack formation remains challenging because the modified layer is buried, defect-sensitive, and statistically variable. Here, nanosecond laser-induced subsurface modification and cracking in commercial n-type 4H-SiC are described probabilistically rather than through deterministic thresholds. Incident fluence, pulse-to-pulse pitch, and focal depth below the surface were varied systematically, and image-derived outcomes were classified as modification onset, crack onset, or stable crack formation. Weibull analysis was used to describe the probability of each outcome, while binomial confidence intervals and bootstrap resampling were used to quantify uncertainty. Modification formed within a comparatively narrow fluence band across all tested depths and pitches. Pulse pitch emerged as the primary parameter governing the transition from modification to cracking. At smaller pitch, stable cracking became probable within the same fluence interval as modification, whereas at larger pitch a statistically separable fluence range produced modification without subsequent cracking. Cross-sectional SEM supported the corresponding morphological progression from void-like or elliptical modifications to wedge-like, crack-forming inclusions. This combined statistical and morphological analysis captures both systematic parameter trends and excursions among nominally identical conditions, providing a basis for selecting more reproducible crack-forming process windows for 4H-SiC wafer slicing.

Article.Title: Fairness aware real time traffic signal control using vehicle detection under symmetric and asymmetric demand
Article.Authors: Rani N.; Vikramacholeswaran V.
Article.Abstract: Urban traffic congestion imposes measurable costs in travel time, fuel consumption and vehicular emissions. Fixed-time signal controllers, which remain the dominant form of intersection control, follow a schedule computed offline and cannot respond to instantaneous demand. Adaptive controllers address this, but are commonly reported on aggregate efficiency alone, without measuring how delay is distributed across approaches, so a controller may improve mean delay while starving a minor approach. This work presents an integrated framework combining camera-based sensing, a priority-based adaptive signal controller with an explicit anti-starvation constraint, and an asynchronous number plate recognition path for automated insurance verification, and subjects the controller to the quantitative evaluation that comparable systems generally omit. Sensing requires no in-road instrumentation. A YOLOv26 detection model classifies vehicles into four categories and produces occupancy-weighted lane densities; a second YOLOv26 model localises number plates for a recognition path that transcribes plate text using a Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network with Connectionist Temporal Classification decoding. The vehicle detector achieves an mAP@50 of 90.92% and the plate detector 97.21%. Among four recognition architectures trained on identical data the CRNN attains the highest accuracy at 96.61%, ahead of a Transformer encoder-decoder at 94.37%, a recurrent baseline at 91.84% and a convolutional baseline at 86.59%; every pairwise difference is statistically significant on the 1,020-image test split (two-proportion z-test, p < 0.05). The detection pipeline processes a frame in 7.6–11.9 ms, approximately 84–130 FPS. The controller was evaluated in Eclipse SUMO 1.27 against fixed-time and Webster’s-method baselines across low, moderate, congested and asymmetric demand, with ten-seed replication under stochastic arrivals. The results are scenario-dependent and are reported as such. Under symmetric demand the proposed controller does not improve on fixed-time control, recording higher mean waiting time and a lower Jain’s Fairness Index, because uniform loading offers no inequity for a demand-responsive policy to correct. Under asymmetric demand, the condition the controller is designed for, it records the lowest mean waiting time at 51.6 s against 55.4 s and 66.7 s for the baselines, improves throughput by 28.0% and 51.8% respectively, and serves 413.9 vehicles per seed against 311.7 and 278.4. The dominant approach’s delay falls by 59.1% against fixed-time control and its demand is fully served, where the baselines leave 98–136 vehicles per seed stranded. The explicit cost, disclosed rather than smoothed over, is that the two minor approaches wait 2.5–3.5 times longer, bounded just below the starvation threshold by the anti-starvation constraint, which activates in approximately 80% of cycles under skewed demand against 2.5–3.5% under symmetric demand. The contribution is a quantified characterisation of this exchange, together with an ablation establishing occupancy-weighted density as the component carrying the controller’s performance.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Control and Systems Engineering > Traffic control and management; Engineering > Building and Construction > Traffic Prediction and Management Techniques; Social Sciences > Transportation > Transportation Planning and Optimization

Article.Title: Bi-directional ANN framework for forward and inverse design of microstrip antenna in RF applications
Article.Authors: Routhu G.; Sarkar M.; Kumar R.
Article.Abstract: In this paper, a bidirectional machine learning (ML)-based framework is introduced to predict the performance parameters such as \(|S_{11}|\) , VSWR and radiation pattern in two planes (XZ and YZ), radiation efficiency, and total efficiency, as well as to estimate the design variables including the patch and feed line dimensions (L, W, L1, and W1) and the dielectric constant ( \( \varepsilon _r \) ) of a quarter-wave transformer (QWT)-microstrip patch (MSP) antenna at an operating frequency of 3 GHz. A Forward Artificial Neural Network (F-ANN) is developed to predict performance parameters based on given design variables. At the same time, an inverse artificial neural network (I-ANN) is implemented to estimate design variables from the desired performance parameter. This technique involves designing, training, and optimizing an MSP antenna in real time. The F-ANN architecture has five input features and one output, whereas the I-ANN has three input features and five outputs. Model evaluation is done using the R-squared (R 2 ) and mean squared error (MSE). The F-ANN and I-ANN achieve R 2 values of 0.99 and minimal MSE values. The estimated design variables from inverse modeling are further re-verified using retro simulation and compared with simulated and predicted results; the developed models \(|S_{11}|\) and VSWR parameters are also validated with measured performance. Both F-ANN and I-ANN predict and estimate parameters with higher accuracy. As a comparative model, the prediction of the ANN framework is compared with two other regression-based models, namely Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Machine (SVM). All the developed models are able to predict the performance with good prediction accuracy.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Aerospace Engineering > Antenna Design and Analysis; Engineering > Aerospace Engineering > Antenna Design and Optimization; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Microwave Engineering and Waveguides

Article.Title: TGF-β-induced ganglioside remodeling highlights GD2 as a dynamically regulated target in glioblastoma
Article.Authors: Tarnóczi K.; Siddi C.; Grember M.; Delannoy C.; Allain F.; Denys A.; Guerardel Y.; Krzewinski-Recchi M.; Paszternák A.; Tábi T.; Szökő É.; Groux-Degroote S.
Article.Abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by extensive cellular plasticity and dynamic interactions with the tumor microenvironment. The tumor-associated ganglioside GD2 is considered a promising therapeutic target, although its stability across different cellular states remains unclear. Here, we investigated whether transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β), a key regulator of glioblastoma progression and mesenchymal reprogramming, modulates ganglioside-biosynthetic gene expression and GD2 surface expression. Using U87-MG and U251-MG glioblastoma cell lines, we combined MALDI–TOF-MS glycosphingolipid profiling, flow cytometry, quantitative PCR, Western blot analysis, and migration assays to characterize TGF-β–induced phenotypic changes. Baseline analyses revealed marked differences in ganglioside composition between the two cell lines. TGF-β induced distinct mesenchymal-like phenotypic responses and differentially regulated ganglioside-biosynthetic gene expression, resulting in opposite effects on GD2 surface expression: GD2 levels increased in U251-MG cells but decreased in U87-MG cells. These changes were accompanied by cell line–specific alterations in migratory behavior. Pharmacological inhibition of UDP-glucose ceramide glucosyltransferase (UGCG) reduced GD2 expression and attenuated migration, supporting a broader contribution of glycosphingolipid biosynthesis to migratory behavior. Together, these findings demonstrate that GD2 expression is dynamically regulated by microenvironmental signaling and is associated with TGF-β-induced phenotypic changes in the glioblastoma cell models examined. Our results identify changes in ganglioside-biosynthetic gene expression and GD2 surface abundance as molecular features accompanying tumor cell plasticity and suggest that GD2 should be considered a context-dependent therapeutic target rather than a stable tumor-associated marker.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Genetics > Glioma Diagnosis and Treatment; Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Molecular Biology > Glycosylation and Glycoproteins Research; Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Molecular Biology > Sphingolipid Metabolism and Signaling

Article.Title: Dynamic survival prognosis and the role of radiotherapy in retroperitoneal liposarcoma
Article.Authors: Lin M.; Huang H.; Huang Z.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: Retroperitoneal liposarcomas (RPLSs) are rare and highly heterogeneous tumors, presenting unique clinical challenges. Despite surgical resection being the primary treatment, achieving complete resection with negative margins is difficult, and the role of adjuvant therapies, such as radiotherapy, remains unclear. The data for this study was sourced from the SEER (Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results) database. Conditional survival (CS) analysis was performed to evaluate survival outcomes over time. Machine learning techniques, including Random Survival Forest (RSF) and Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression, were used to identify prognostic factors and develop a CS-based nomogram. Propensity score matching (PSM) was employed to assess the survival benefit of radiotherapy. A total of 1,186 patients were analyzed (830 training, 356 validation). The CS analysis demonstrated improved survival probabilities with extended survival time; the probability of reaching 10 years rose from 41% at diagnosis to 87% after surviving 8 years. Based on machine learning and rigorous variable selection, the optimal prognostic indicator combination consists of age, histology, tumor grade, tumor size, SEER stage, AJCC stage and surgery. Based on the selected variable combination, the CS-based nomogram successfully predicted 3-, 5-, and 10-year overall survival and 10-year CS. The model was validated through calibration curves, ROC curve analysis, and decision curve analysis, and effectively stratified the cohort into risk groups. After propensity-score matching, radiotherapy was not associated with overall survival (HR 1.06, 95% CI 0.84–1.34; P = 0.62). CS analysis provided valuable insights into the evolving survival outcomes of RPLS, offering a more accurate prognostic tool for clinicians. Radiotherapy did not show a significant survival benefit, after adjustment for measured confounders; given the likelihood of residual confounding by indication, its role in RPLS treatment warrants further prospective investigation.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Pulmonary and Respiratory Medicine > Sarcoma Diagnosis and Treatment; Medicine > Epidemiology > Multiple and Secondary Primary Cancers; Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Cancer Research > Breast Cancer Treatment Studies

Article.Title: Deciphering leaf morpho-biochemical and mineral diversity in strawberry tree (Arbutus andrachne L.) genotypes through multivariate statistical approaches
Article.Authors: Yaman M.; Aydınlıoğlu C.; Karakoç Y.; Tunç Y.; Yıldız E.; Sümbül A.; Gönültaş M.; Güneş A.; Köse M.; Keçe Y.; Yılmaz K.
Article.Abstract: Strawberry tree ( Arbutus andrachne L.) leaves represent a sustainable source of bioactive compounds and mineral nutrients with considerable potential for pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and functional food applications. However, comprehensive information integrating leaf morphology, biochemical characteristics, mineral composition, and multivariate statistical analyses remains limited. This study aimed to characterize the leaf morpho-biochemical and mineral diversity of 30 naturally growing strawberry tree genotypes collected from Hatay, Türkiye, and to identify phenotypically promising plant materials for future evaluation in breeding, domestication, and industrial leaf biomass production. The evaluated variables were analyzed using Pearson correlation analysis, principal component analysis (PCA), hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA), heat map analysis (HMA), and multiple regression analysis (MRA). Leaf width, leaf length, petiole length, and petiole thickness ranged from 24.92 (‘ST-2’) to 54.28 mm (‘ST-5’), 45.48 (‘ST-28’) to 91.74 mm (‘ST-12’), 8.14 (‘ST-10’) to 23.14 mm (‘ST-29’), and 0.78 (‘ST-28’) to 1.72 mm (‘ST-16’), respectively. Total phenolic content, total flavonoid content, and antioxidant activity ranged from 53.95 (‘ST-13’) to 74.89 mg GAE 100 g⁻¹ FW (‘ST-2’), 13.59 (‘ST-26’) to 35.12 mg CAE 100 g⁻¹ FW (‘ST-7’), and 32.00% (‘ST-17’) to 64.50% (‘ST-13’), respectively. Calcium was the predominant mineral element, ranging from 5327.22 mg kg⁻¹ DW (‘ST-10’) to 27352.35 mg kg⁻¹ DW (‘ST-28’), followed by phosphorus and potassium. Pearson correlation analysis revealed strong positive associations among leaf morphological traits and among most mineral elements, whereas MRA showed that leaf width was primarily explained by leaf length ( R² = 0.95). In contrast, magnesium was identified as a significant predictor of phenolic and flavonoid contents, while both magnesium and potassium were significant predictors of antioxidant activity. PCA extracted six principal components, jointly explaining 79.62% of the total variation, confirming substantial multidimensional diversity among genotypes. Collectively, the results identified ‘ST-5’ and ‘ST-12’ for superior leaf morphology, ‘ST-2’, ‘ST-7’, and ‘ST-13’ for outstanding bioactive properties, and ‘ST-28’ for exceptional calcium accumulation as phenotypically promising plant materials for further evaluation in breeding, conservation, domestication, and sustainable industrial utilization of strawberry tree leaf biomass.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Biochemistry > Phytochemicals and Antioxidant Activities; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Agricultural Practices and Plant Genetics; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Berry genetics and cultivation research

Article.Title: A causality-aware and explainable intelligence framework for secure and resilient cloud systems
Article.Authors: Lakshmanan S.; Annamalai T.; Kamalesan T.; Venugopal S.
Article.Abstract: The cloud computing environment is becoming more vulnerable to advanced and dynamic cyber intrusions that take advantage of complex behavioural dependencies, dynamic access patterns, and vulnerabilities of shared infrastructures. Traditional cloud intrusion detection platforms are largely based on correlation-based machine learning or non-adaptive rule-based platforms that have problems generalizing when faced with changing attack plans and offer only limited interpretability of operations to give operational trust. The case of this paper consists of a causality-aware and explainable intelligence framework of secure and resilient cloud systems to address these challenges. The proposed framework will combine structural causal modelling with deep behavioural representation learning to reveal latent cause-and-effect relationships of malicious activities in cloud network traffic. Counterfactual reasoning is also used to increase resistance against low-rate and evasive attacks and a causal explainability module produces transparent and human interpretable security justifications. Experimental analysis is done over the UNSW-NB15 benchmark dataset which consists of various types of intrusion and realistic cloud traffic patterns. The proposed framework has the highest detection accuracy of 98.34, F1-score of 97.91 and a lower rate of false positive of 1.62, which is much better than traditional machine learning and deep learning baselines. Resilience analysis also illustrates that the training is resilient to adversarial perturbation and low-rate attack conditions and it is more resilient than correlation-based models, i.e., the resilience increases more than 12%. These findings substantiate the fact that incorporating causality and explainability in cloud security intelligence can enhance detection performances in addition to improving trust, transparency, and operational stability. The framework suggested is an interpretable and scalable tool that fits in the contemporary cloud structures and infrastructures that require a high level of security. Additional validation using the CICIDS2017 benchmark dataset further demonstrates the generalization capability and robustness of the proposed framework.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Computer Networks and Communications > Network Security and Intrusion Detection; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Adversarial Robustness in Machine Learning; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Internet Traffic Analysis and Secure E-voting

Article.Title: Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio as a low-cost triage marker for malaria in febrile patients in conflict-affected Southern Yemen
Article.Authors: Saleh K.; Ali N.; Ali G.; Ali H.; Alkubati S.
Article.Abstract: In many fragile and conflict-affected settings, access to reliable laboratory diagnostics for febrile illnesses remains limited. Malaria and other infectious diseases continue to impose a major burden in Yemen.
