Article.Abstract: Government target management, a core institutional tool for optimizing resource allocation and improving governance efficiency, plays a pivotal role in air pollution mitigation. Using panel data from 225 Chinese cities spanning 2006 to 2022, this paper employs a spatial Durbin model to investigate how economic growth targets and energy consumption constraints shape transboundary PM 2.5 pollution. The results show that economic growth targets significantly elevate local and neighboring pollution levels, whereas energy consumption constraints reduce pollution in both areas; their antagonistic interaction amplifies PM 2.5 spillovers. The joint effect of dual-target management exhibits spatial attenuation at approximately 500 km and a temporal breakpoint around 2013, marking a governance pattern transition from zero-sum games to win–win outcomes. Mechanism analysis identifies economic linkages and strategic interactions as core transmission channels, while heterogeneity tests reveal a west-to-east declining gradient in spillover effects. These findings provide actionable empirical support for local governments to set compatible economic and environmental targets and resolve the cross-regional pollution governance dilemma.
Article.TopicFields: Economics, Econometrics and Finance > Economics and Econometrics > Energy, Environment, Economic Growth; Environmental Science > Environmental Engineering > Environmental and Air Quality Management; Environmental Science > Health, Toxicology and Mutagenesis > Air Quality and Health Impacts

Article.Title: The growing burden of diabetes mellitus in Ethiopia: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Berhe B.; Negash H.; Legese H.; Belay G.; Mersha T.; Kidanu M.; Tedla M.
Article.Abstract: Despite significant progress and efforts, the global burden of diabetes mellitus has continued to increase. According to a report by the International Diabetes Federation, Ethiopia has the fifth highest number of adults with diabetes in the African region. In Ethiopia, which is a member of LMICs, there are no national data or studies to determine its burden, prevalence, complications and economic impact. A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following the PRISMA framework. R statistical software version 4.5.1 was used to obtain the pooled prevalence and odds ratio via a random effects model. Our analysis revealed that the pooled prevalence of diabetes mellitus in Ethiopia was 8%. The subgroup analysis on a regional basis revealed a prevalence of 15% and 10% in Dire Dawa and Addis Ababa, respectively. The overall prevalence of diabetes mellitus-related complications was 50%, and further classification analysis revealed that 29% of the complications were acute and 52% were chronic. Moreover, the odds of developing diabetes mellitus among males are 1.2 times greater than those among females. The estimated average individual medical cost of managing diabetes mellitus is reported to be approximately $294.00 USD per month. Diabetes mellitus and its associated comorbidities are a critical public health concern in Ethiopia and is characterized by a triple burden of prevalence, serious health complications and significantly high management costs. Therefore, we strongly recommend the implementation of early patient screening, the reduction of behavioral risk factors, and government policy reforms related to public health support and access to emergency care for individuals with low socioeconomic status.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism > Diabetes, Cardiovascular Risks, and Lipoproteins; Health Professions > Health Information Management > Global Health and Epidemiology; Medicine > Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism > Diabetes Management and Research

Article.Title: Machine learning-based classification of zeolite quantities for humidity and temperature control in fireworks storage safety
Article.Authors: Indumathi N.; Gnanavel S.; Sultanuddin S.; Vijayalakshmi V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accident occur in fireworks storage facilities are mainly caused by the variations in temperature and relative humidity that affect the instability of chemical mixes and hence leading to explosions. In this study, a machine learning decision-support system was suggested to estimate the right amount of zeolite to help achieve safe storage. Data concerning temperature and relative humidity were gathered from storage insert a space 5 kg, 10 kg, and 15 kg of wet and dry zeolites better as over a 10-day period. A total of 208 records were acquired from the experiments. Eight different classification algorithms available in the WEKA environment such as Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (SMO), Random Forest, BayesNet, k-Nearest Neighbor, J48, Multiclass Classifier, and Multilayer Perceptron were analyzed through stratified 10-fold cross-validation. Logistic Regression showed the best performance by achieving the highest classification accuracy of 78.41% followed by SMO that showed a classification accuracy of 77.24%. Humidity and state of zeolite proved to be the significant factors in the analysis. The results show the possibility of integration of zeolite-based humidity regulation and machine learning systems. Although the model requires further validation with use large datasets and deployment in the real-world situation, the suggested model provides a useful tool for decision.
Article.Topic: Data Mining and Machine Learning Applications
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Information Systems > Data Mining and Machine Learning Applications; Materials Science > Materials Chemistry > Machine Learning in Materials Science; Engineering > Mechanics of Materials > Energetic Materials and Combustion

Article.Title: Contradictory effects of basalt fiber on chloride transport in concrete: a scopus-centered systematic review and study-level quantitative synthesis
Article.Authors: Aslam F.; Javed M.; Sadiq M.; Durrani A.; Jameel M.; Alaskar A.; Ahmad F.
Article.Abstract: Basalt fiber (BF) can improve, worsen, or reverse chloride transport in concrete. We systematically assessed matched BF-only contrasts across rapid chloride permeability (RCPT), diffusion, migration, chloride-content, and penetration-depth outcomes, treating each experimental program as independent. Scopus was searched on 30 August 2026 with three queries (1,108 records); normalized exact-title deduplication left 874 records for screening. Reporting completeness and extraction provenance were appraised; no validated risk-of-bias tool was used. The final dataset contained 125 effects from 24 program clusters (26 reports); 17 sought reports were not retrieved. RCPT effects averaged B = 0.039 (14 clusters; 95% cluster-bootstrap interval − 0.142 to 0.209), and diffusion effects averaged B = 0.047 (7 clusters; −0.184 to 0.298); positive B = − ln(BF/control) indicates a lower measured chloride indicator. Smaller outcome families were descriptive. An exploratory normalized-dose model (12 studies, 79 rows) yielded a concave interior maximum in 52.3% of cluster-bootstrap samples, but coefficient and turning-point intervals were broad. One author screened and extracted data without independent duplicate review; within-condition variances were unavailable. The review was Scopus-only and not prospectively registered. Results support neither a transferable BF dosage optimum nor causal test-method effects. No external funding was received.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Civil and Structural Engineering > Concrete Corrosion and Durability; Engineering > Civil and Structural Engineering > Innovative concrete reinforcement materials; Environmental Science > Pollution > Smart Materials for Construction

Article.Title: Enhancing salinity resilience in horticultural systems through Portulaca oleracea PGPR phytoremediation with quantum dot biosensing
Article.Authors: Aghamir F.; Eghlima G.; Alvand Z.; Farzaneh M.
Article.Abstract: Soil salinity is a major constraint on productivity in greenhouse and horticultural systems, especially when saline irrigation is applied. In this study, we examined whether halotolerant plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) could alleviate saline–sodic stress in Portulaca oleracea . Eight PGPR strains were evaluated individually and as a multi-strain consortium in saline–sodic soil under greenhouse conditions, alongside uninoculated and 1% H₂SO₄-treated controls. Among the evaluated treatments, PGPR8 and the consortium were among the most effective in improving key plant physiological and soil biological parameters under salinity stress. Plants treated with the consortium reached about 29 cm in height, showed a shoot Na⁺/K⁺ ratio of 0.58, and had chlorophyll levels approximately ten times higher than those of acid-treated plants. Soil biological activity also improved, with microbial biomass carbon reaching about 268 µg C g −1 . In parallel, transcriptional analysis showed a 2.2–2.4-fold upregulation of SOS1 , NHX1 , SOD , and POD relative to the controls. We also applied anti-OmpA antibody-functionalized quantum dots as an exploratory approach to probe OmpA-associated bacterial surface responses. Although this assay produced a rapid, concentration-dependent fluorescence response, the results should be interpreted as preliminary surface-associated indicators rather than direct quantitative measures of PGPR activity. Overall, these findings suggest that PGPR inoculation can enhance plant resilience and improve soil function under short-term saline–sodic stress. Further field-scale validation is needed to determine the long-term agronomic relevance and sustainability of these biological treatments.
Article.TopicFields: Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Plant-Microbe Interactions and Immunity; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Plant Stress Responses and Tolerance; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Silicon Effects in Agriculture

Article.Title: An inductive content analysis of the multifaceted nature of educational support among Iranian patients with chronic diseases
Article.Authors: Kalani Z.; Kermanshahi S.; Ahmadi F.; Kazemnejad A.
Article.Abstract: Nurses should teach patients with chronic diseases how to manage their disease. While providing patient education is consistently considered a vital nursing intervention for patients with chronic diseases, what chronic patients expect from educational support is unclear. This study aimed to define educational support and identify its key elements as perceived by chronic Iranian patients and nurses’ perspectives. The participants with at least one chronic disease were selected through purposive sampling at the community level, focusing on health centers and clinics. The study was conducted in Yazd city, Iran, between October 2023 and August 2024. Eighteen participants were included. Semistructured interviews were conducted. A conventional inductive content analysis approach was used to analyze the data. Three themes emerged from the data: (1) the need for self-management, encompassing coping strategies and self-care behaviors; (2) the need for others, including the desire for family companionship, maintaining independence, and addressing feelings of helplessness; and (3) the need for education, encompassing knowledge acquisition, information seeking, and challenges related to medication adherence. The findings suggest that chronic patients’ educational support is a person-centered and multifaceted educational process that supports patients in meeting their needs. Nurses can play an important role in facilitating this process due to their extensive interaction with chronic patients.
Article.TopicFields: Health Professions > Pharmacy > Nursing care and research; Social Sciences > Education > Health Education and Validation; Medicine > Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism > Diabetes Management and Education

Article.Title: Ecological and human health risk assessment of heavy metals in sewage sludge to ensure safe agricultural use
Article.Authors: Alinejad N.; Armand N.; Torkashvand J.; Ansarizadeh M.; Yousefi M.; Badeenezhad A.
Article.Abstract: The use of sewage sludge in agricultural lands is one of the sludge management options that must be ensured to avoid environmental and health consequences. Considering the content of heavy metals in sewage sludge, the aim of this study was to measure the concentration of these elements in sewage sludge and assess the ecological and health risks resulting from its use in agricultural lands in southwestern Iran using Monte Carlo simulation. Eighteen two-liter samples of sewage sludge from Behbahan wastewater treatment plant were sent to the laboratory for analysis of heavy metal concentrations over a six-month period. The results were used to calculate ecological risk based on single-factor pollution index (PI) and Nemerow’s synthetic pollution index (PN), as well as to assess non-carcinogenic risk based on hazard index (HI) and carcinogenic risk based on total cancer risk (TCR). Concentration of the total studied heavy metals in the analyzed samples was 1871.89 mg/kg. The maximum and minimum concentrations detected were associated with iron (1093.26 mg/kg) and cadmium (0.40 mg/kg), respectively. The heavy metal content of the studied sewage sludge produced PI and PN values less than 1, indicating a safe ecological risk class. Also, calculated HI less than 1 indicated a insignificant non-carcinogenic risk level from the use of sewage sludge with the detected heavy metal content for adults and children. The calculated TCR (3.66E-06) indicated an acceptable carcinogenic risk. Under the exposure assumptions and toxicity benchmarks used in this screening assessment, the modeled non-carcinogenic and carcinogenic risks associated with the analyzed sludge concentrations were below the selected risk-management criteria and can be an option considered for sludge management by local policymakers. These results should not be interpreted as evidence that agricultural application is universally risk-free, particularly because long-term soil accumulation and food-chain exposure were not fully characterized. So, long-term monitoring of background concentrations of heavy metals in soil is necessary due to the persistence of these elements in environment.
Article.TopicFields: Environmental Science > Pollution > Heavy metals in environment; Environmental Science > Waste Management and Disposal > Wastewater Treatment and Reuse; Environmental Science > Health, Toxicology and Mutagenesis > Environmental Toxicology and Ecotoxicology

Article.Title: Blue and green LED light kills Meloidogyne javanica juveniles through cuticle damage and oxidative stress
Article.Authors: Nasab Z.; Mirafzali S.; Marashi S.; Mohammadi A.; Sadeghipour A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Root-knot nematodes ( Meloidogyne javanica (Treub, 1885) Chitwood, 1949) cause severe global yield losses. Chemical nematicides are effective but raise environmental and health concerns. Light-emitting diodes (LEDs) offer a non-chemical alternative, but wavelength-dependent effects are poorly understood. This study investigated the lethal effect of visible LED light on second-stage juveniles (J2) in water and, to our knowledge, documented early cuticular changes using atomic force microscopy (AFM) at 1, 2 and 3 h. Blue (440 nm), green (510 nm), red (635 nm), yellow (580 nm) and white LEDs were applied for 1–4 h at irradiances of 2.6–2.9 mW/cm² (radiant exposure 36–42 J/cm² after 4 h). Blue light caused 20–27% mortality after 1–3 h, while all other wavelengths (including dark control) gave ≤ 20% mortality. After 4 h, blue and green both achieved 100% mortality, red caused 60%, and yellow or white remained ≤ 25% (Fig. 1). A sham control (opaque filter) and a thermal control (27 °C, dark) showed 0% mortality, ruling out heating or hypoxia. AFM images (Figs. 2, 3 and 4 and Supplementary Fig. S1) revealed progressive cuticular damage (increased roughness and pores) exclusively under blue and green light, occurring before death. Red light induced moderate roughness only from 3 h onward, while yellow and white caused no significant change. Pre-treatment with 5 mM N-acetylcysteine (NAC) reduced blue-light-induced mortality from 100% to < 15% ( p < 0.01), supporting the involvement of reactive oxygen species (ROS). Blue and green LED light (≥ 4 h) are highly nematicidal to M. javanica J2, with cuticle damage starting from the first hour as an early lethal event. The wavelength dependence and NAC rescue support an oxidative stress pathway. LED technology offers a promising non-chemical, residue-free alternative for nematode management in hydroponics and greenhouses, though effects on non-target organisms require further study.
Article.TopicFields: Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Nematode management and characterization studies; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Plant Disease Management Techniques; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Insect Science > Insect-Plant Interactions and Control

Article.Title: A combined histopathological treatment response classification is associated with survival and pretreatment immune features in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma treated with neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy
Article.Authors: Koskenniemi A.; Huusko T.; Routila J.; Vainio P.; Ventelä S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A standardized system for assessing histopathological treatment response (HTR) in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is lacking, an issue of increasing relevance with growing interest in neoadjuvant therapies. In this retrospective study, paired pre- and post-treatment samples from 53 patients with HNSCC treated with curative-intent neoadjuvant radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy (RT/CRT) were analyzed histopathologically and immunohistochemically for CD8, CD68, CD206, Clever-1, and PD-L1. Post-treatment histiocytic multinucleated giant cell reaction (MGC) was associated with favorable overall survival (OS) and with the pre-treatment immune microenvironment. Based on these findings, a two-tiered combined HTR (cHTR) classification integrating tumor regression grade (TRG) and MGC was developed. Good cHTR was associated with a 5-year OS of 59% versus 16% for poor cHTR (HR 0.21; 95% CI 0.09–0.47, p < 0.001). High pre-treatment tumor-cell PD-L1 expression was associated with absence of MGC, while elevated pre-treatment PD-L1 expression and CD8⁺ intraepithelial tumor infiltrating lymphocyte (iTIL) density were potential predictive markers of poor cHTR. The proposed cHTR classification provided clear OS stratification in this cohort but should be considered exploratory and requires validation in independent cohorts. CD8⁺ iTILs and PD-L1 may represent predictive biomarkers of histopathological response to neoadjuvant treatment and warrant further prospective validation.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Otorhinolaryngology > Head and Neck Cancer Studies; Medicine > Oncology > Cancer Immunotherapy and Biomarkers; Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Cancer Research > Breast Cancer Treatment Studies

Article.Title: Biologically interpretable multi-scale feature engineering with two-stage pruning for tomato leaf disease classification
Article.Authors: Wang P.; Zhou Z.; Hu W.; Ma X.; Xu S.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Automated tomato leaf disease classification remains challenging when different diseases exhibit similar color, texture, and necrotic symptoms. To improve pathological interpretability while maintaining competitive classification performance, this study proposes a multi-scale feature engineering framework that explicitly represents disease symptoms at both global and local scales. A composite Excess Green (ExG)-Triangle segmentation strategy is first used to preserve green, chlorotic, and diseased leaf tissues, achieving a Dice coefficient of 92.45% and a Recall of 99.40% on manually annotated leaf masks. Color, multi-scale Local Binary Pattern (LBP), shape, and lesion descriptors are then integrated, with a Lesion Spatial Logic (LSL) descriptor introduced to characterize the relative allocation of necrotic tissue between the marginal and interior regions of the leaf. A two-stage pruning strategy based on permutation importance and Pearson correlation reduces the feature dimensionality from 296 to 164, corresponding to a 44.6% reduction. The pruned Support Vector Machine (SVM) achieves 96.44% accuracy on the independent PlantVillage test set, while Early Blight Recall increases from 88.50% to 92.00%. An exact McNemar test shows no statistically significant difference between the full and pruned SVM models ( \(\:p=0.644\) ), and five-fold cross-validation shows limited performance variability across training partitions. Modern pretrained CNNs achieve higher absolute accuracy on PlantVillage, whereas the proposed framework provides explicit pathological feature representation, a compact classifier, and lower memory and model-storage requirements. These findings support pathology-guided feature engineering as an interpretable approach for tomato disease classification under controlled conditions, while further validation under greenhouse and field conditions remains necessary.
Article.TopicFields: Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Smart Agriculture and AI; Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Advanced Neural Network Applications; Engineering > Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering > Industrial Vision Systems and Defect Detection

Article.Title: Hybrid GWO–GA optimized LSTM–MLP framework for highly accurate palmer drought severity index prediction
Article.Authors: Alhammad S.; Mohamed F.; Osman A.; Fouad Y.; El-Bakry H.; Elshewey A.
Article.Abstract: Accurate prediction of the Palmer Drought Severity Index (PDSI) is essential for drought monitoring, climate-risk assessment, and the effective management of water resources. This study proposes a hybrid Long Short-Term Memory–Multilayer Perceptron (LSTM–MLP) model for PDSI prediction, integrated with a Grey Wolf Optimizer–Genetic Algorithm (GWO–GA) optimization framework. The model is evaluated using a climate dataset comprising 864 observations characterized by scenario information and multiple climatic variables, including pr, tas, tasmin, tasmax, and srad. The predictive performance of the proposed approach is assessed using the mean squared error (MSE), root mean squared error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), median absolute error (MedAE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), and coefficient of determination ( $$R^2$$ ). Furthermore, its performance is compared with several deep-learning architectures, including convolutional neural network (CNN), LSTM, gated recurrent unit (GRU), bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM), and bidirectional GRU (BiGRU) models. The proposed LSTM–MLP model achieved an MSE of 0.0004, RMSE of 0.0201, MAE of 0.0169, MedAE of 0.0160, MAPE of 0.0018, and an $$R^2$$ of 99.97%. In comparison, the CNN, LSTM, GRU, BiLSTM, and BiGRU models achieved $$R^2$$ values of 94.58%, 90.84%, 88.70%, 87.39%, and 86.48%, respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed LSTM–MLP framework provides highly accurate PDSI predictions and consistently improves predictive performance relative to the investigated benchmark deep-learning models. The findings give a focus to the potential of the proposed hybrid modeling framework as an effective data-driven approach for PDSI prediction and drought-related climate analysis.
Article.TopicFields: Environmental Science > Environmental Engineering > Hydrological Forecasting Using AI; Environmental Science > Global and Planetary Change > Hydrology and Drought Analysis; Decision Sciences > Management Science and Operations Research > Stock Market Forecasting Methods

Article.Title: Numerals in news headlines act as an information-gateway signal, increasing engagement, perceived informativeness, and memory
Article.Authors: Peters E.; Markowitz D.; Shoots-Reinhard B.; Ely M.
Article.Abstract: People increasingly distrust news and engage with it irregularly. Can the presence of numbers in headlines encourage news engagement and, if so, why? We show that the presence (vs. absence) of at least one numeral (“3”) in tests of headlines increased click-throughs to associated articles by 3.6% at The Washington Post and 5.2% at Upworthy, after controlling for other engagement-related factors. A preregistered experiment (n=765) demonstrated causal effects: Participants selected headlines with numerals more than those with verbal labels (“several”) or similarly precise, logically identical written-out numbers (“three”), suggesting that numerals were not simply more precise. Participants also formed more positive impressions of numeric headlines and remembered their number-related and non-numeric information better. Font-fluency manipulations did not moderate number-type effects, although did increase numeric memory. We propose that the presence of numerals may act as a cognitive information-gateway signal influencing attention and encouraging engagement in noisy digital ecosystems.
Article.TopicFields: Social Sciences > Communication > Journalism and Media Studies; Social Sciences > Communication > Media Studies and Communication; Computer Science > Computer Science Applications > Digital Media and Philosophy

Article.Title: XAI-ECGNet: an explainable hybrid CNN-BiLSTM framework for multi-label cardiac diagnosis classification from 12-lead ECG signals using the PTB-XL dataset
Article.Authors: Metre P.; K V.; G D.; Kalnoor G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cardiovascular disorders cause approximately 17.9 million deaths annually, and the 12-lead electrocardiogram remains the primary non-invasive diagnostic tool, yet interpretable deep-learning ECG classifiers remain limited, restricting clinical adoption. We present XAI-ECGNet, which is based on 1D residual CNNs, squeeze-and-excitation (SE) channel attention on learned, lead-derived feature channels, and bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) temporal modelling. On PTB-XL (21,799 ECGs, 18,885 patients), XAI-ECGNet outperforms all of the top performing baselines in terms of macro-AUROC, which is 0.9337, within the range of the baselines’ bootstrap confidence intervals, and four of five diagnostic superclasses have AUROC above 0.90. Ablation results indicate that the full model is within five-seed variability (σ = 0.0023) of the CNN-only backbone (0.9333); per-class analysis reveals that SE attention is crucial for BiLSTM to offer benefit, as it recovers and surpasses CNN-only performance on four out of five classes after BiLSTM alone fails to do so. Three post-hoc methods (Grad-CAM, SHAP, Integrated Gradients) show the model learns clinically consistent representations without explicit clinical priors. We also report quantitative faithfulness evaluation, SHAP background-sample-size justification, and zero-shot cross-dataset validation on CPSC 2018, demonstrating genuine generalisation for NORM and CD, and interpretable label-taxonomy mismatch for STTC. XAI-ECGNet combines accurate multi-label ECG classification with a rigorously and quantitatively assessed explainability framework, but prospective cardiologist validation is required before any claim to clinical use can be made.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Cardiology and Cardiovascular Medicine > ECG Monitoring and Analysis; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI); Health Professions > Health Information Management > Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare

Article.Title: Pembrolizumab plus paclitaxel with optional bevacizumab for platinum-resistant recurrent ovarian cancer with PD-L1 CPS ≥ 1: a cost-effectiveness analysis
Article.Authors: Lin Y.; Chen K.; Ding D.
Article.Abstract: Patients with platinum-resistant recurrent ovarian cancer (PRROC) have limited therapeutic options. Pembrolizumab plus paclitaxel with optional bevacizumab (pembrolizumab group) has recently emerged as a promising therapeutic strategy for this population. Nevertheless, the high acquisition and treatment costs associated with this regimen raise important concerns regarding its economic value, making a formal cost-effectiveness evaluation essential. A three-state Markov model with a 15-year time horizon was constructed using clinical efficacy data from the KEYNOTE-B96 trial together with treatment-related cost inputs for estimating lifetime costs and health outcomes for PRROC patients with PD-L1 combined positive score (CPS) ≥ 1 receiving either the pembrolizumab regimen or placebo. Outcomes included total costs, quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), incremental net health benefits (INHBs), and incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs). Cost-effectiveness was assessed using willingness-to-pay (WTP) thresholds of $150,000/QALY for the USA and $40,500/QALY for China. In the USA, treatment with pembrolizumab resulted in an additional cost of $214,982 and a gain of 0.29 QALYs compared with placebo. In China, the corresponding incremental cost and QALY gain were $16,459 and 0.27, respectively. The resulting ICERs were $752,613/QALY in the USA and $61,777/QALY in China, with associated INHBs of -1.14 QALYs and -0.14 QALYs, respectively. Sensitivity analyses showed that when pembrolizumab prices were reduced by 10% in the USA and 30% in China, the ICERs declined to levels below the respective WTP thresholds. At current market prices, pembrolizumab plus paclitaxel with optional bevacizumab does not represent a cost-effective option for PRROC. However, price reductions for pembrolizumab could substantially improve its economic attractiveness.
Article.Topic: Health Systems, Economic Evaluations, Quality of Life
Article.TopicFields: Economics, Econometrics and Finance > Economics and Econometrics > Health Systems, Economic Evaluations, Quality of Life; Medicine > Reproductive Medicine > Ovarian cancer diagnosis and treatment; Economics, Econometrics and Finance > Economics and Econometrics > Economic and Financial Impacts of Cancer

Article.Title: A pilot study on individual differences in humor style and their associations with self-rated physical health and blood pressure
Article.Authors: Duane A.; Gianaros P.; Inagaki T.
Article.Abstract: Humor style, defined as the use and function of humor, may have implications for health. Indeed, research suggests certain humor styles are related to better mental health, but surprisingly little research assesses associations with physical health. Further, no studies assess both positive and negative humor styles as they relate to physical health. The current study, therefore, investigated associations between positive (affiliative, self-enhancing) and negative (aggressive, self-defeating) humor styles and indices of physical health, specifically self-rated physical health and blood pressure. Secondary analysis on an existing dataset was conducted in which participants ( N = 143, 77.6% women, mean age = 18.92) attended a laboratory session during which time we assessed individual differences in humor styles using the Humor Styles Questionnaire (HSQ). Resting blood pressure and self-rated health were assessed as indicators of physical health, followed by health-relevant covariates (depressive symptoms, body mass index (BMI), smoking status, prescription medication) and demographics. To test primary hypotheses, data was analyzed using Pearson and Bayesian correlations followed by hierarchical linear and Bayesian multiple regressions. Positive humor styles were not related to self-rated health or resting blood pressure. However, negative humor styles were both related to higher resting blood pressure such that use of more aggressive and self-defeating humor was related to higher resting systolic and diastolic blood pressure. Negative humor styles each accounted for additional variance in resting systolic blood pressure above and beyond BMI, suggesting the combination of negative humor styles might be particularly influential. Negative humor styles relate to higher resting blood pressure, suggesting individual differences in the use of humor may be another psychosocial risk factor for the development of hypertension. Future research is needed to investigate pathways linking humor styles with physical health and confirm the causal direction, as well as to establish clinical significance of the findings given the young, healthy sample.
Article.TopicFields: Psychology > Social Psychology > Humor Studies and Applications; Arts and Humanities > Literature and Literary Theory > American Literature and Humor Studies; Arts and Humanities > Literature and Literary Theory > Media Influence and Health

Article.Title: Hyaluronic acid–functionalized synergistic nanostructured lipid carriers for sustained release and enhanced bioavailability
Article.Authors: Butt A.; Ali Z.; Zahid F.; Khan D.; Mukhtiar M.; Alamri A.; Al Awadh A.; Amin M.; Alghamdi M.; Din F.
Article.Abstract: Breast cancer remains one of the most prevalent malignancies among women and is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality. This study was designed to develop and statistically optimized co-loaded tamoxifen (TMX) and letrozole (LTZ) nanostructured lipid carrier coated with hyaluronic acid (HA-TMX-LTZ-NLCs) for synergistic activity towards breast cancer. Melt emulsification-ultra sonication method was used for the preparation of TMX-LTZ-NLCs, followed by their statistical optimization via Design-Expert. TMX-LTZ-NLCs were subsequently coated with HA for improved biopharmaceutical performance. The coating was confirmed using Fourier Transfrom Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) analysis. The optimized HA-TMX-LTZ-NLCs were characterized for particle properties, polymorphic form, thermal behavior and morphology using Dynamic Light Scattering (DLS), Powder Xray Diffractometry (PXRD), Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) and Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), respectively. In vitro release analysis of HA-TMX-LTZ-NLCs was performed and in vitro antitumor potential was investigated in MCF-7 cells. Moreover, its synergistic activity was evaluated through CompuSyn software. Pharmacokinetic (PK) profile of HA-TMX-LTZ-NLCs was investigated after intravenous administration in rats. The optimized HA-TMX-LTZ-NLCs demonstrated a mean PS of 197.2 ± 5.9 nm, polydispersity index 0.192 ± 0.004 and zeta potential of -15.1 ± 0.60 mV. TEM, PXRD and DSC analysis respectively confirmed the spherical morphology and amorphous nature of the HA-TMX-LTZ-NLCs. Moreover, it demonstrated a sustained drug release and significantly higher antiproliferative effect. The HA-TMX-LTZ-NLCs exhibited a 2.4 ~ and 4.1 ~ fold reduced with IC 50 values when compared with HA-TMX-NLCs and HA-LTZ-NLCs, respectively. Furthermore, a strong synergistic effect was evident from the CompuSyn analysis. Additionally, PK study exhibited a 3.96 ~ and 3.65 ~ fold increased systematic exposure of TMX and LTZ, respectively. The sustained release, enhanced in vitro antitumor efficacy and improved bioavailability of HA-TMX-LTZ-NLCs suggests its therapeutic potential in breast cancer therapy.
Article.TopicFields: Materials Science > Biomaterials > Nanoparticle-Based Drug Delivery; Pharmacology, Toxicology and Pharmaceutics > Pharmaceutical Science > Advancements in Transdermal Drug Delivery; Pharmacology, Toxicology and Pharmaceutics > Pharmaceutical Science > Advanced Drug Delivery Systems

Article.Title: Response surface optimization and ANFIS Prediction of abrasive waterjet machining in areca nut biofiller epoxy composites
Article.Authors: Murugadoss P.; Vasanthkumar P.; Senthilkumar N.; Balakrishnan D.; Selvam R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Abrasive waterjet machining (AWJM) of epoxy-10 wt.% areca nut biofiller composite was investigated using a face-centred central composite design in response surface methodology (RSM). Waterjet pressure (WJP), traverse speed (TS), abrasive flow rate (AFR), and stand-off distance (SoD) were varied to assess surface roughness (SR) and kerf angle (KA). Measured SR and KA ranged from 3.55 to 5.43 µm and 3.08 to 4.42°. Analysis of variance identified SoD as the dominant factor for both responses. Backward elimination improved the RSM predicted R 2 from 0.8287 to 0.8553 (SR) and from 0.8954 to 0.9307 (KA). In the six-observation comparison, ANFIS achieved lower RMSE values (0.0313 µm and 0.0298°) than the backward-eliminated RSM models (0.0469 µm and 0.0462°) for SR and KA. ANFIS exhibited the lowest RMSE across all 30 observations (0.0859 µm and 0.0379°). Full-RSM desirability optimization identified 300 MPa WJP, 200 mm/min TS, 150 g/min AFR, and 1.5 mm SoD as the optimal conditions, with a desirability of 0.95. Confirmation experiments yielded 3.48 µm (SR) and 3.11° (KA), with prediction deviations of 3.53% and 2.81%. SEM observations revealed finer cutting tracks and fewer surface defects under optimized conditions. These findings highlight the complementary modelling capabilities of RSM and ANFIS for AWJM of biofiller-reinforced sustainable epoxy composites.
Article.TopicFields: Environmental Science > Ecological Modeling > Erosion and Abrasive Machining; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Advanced Machining and Optimization Techniques; Engineering > Mechanical Engineering > Advanced machining processes and optimization

Article.Title: Defining clinically relevant risk threshold for predicting sudden cardiac death
Article.Authors: Hernesniemi J.; Ahola R.; Uimonen M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract There is no consensus on a risk threshold for sudden cardiac death (SCD) that could be used in practical design and evaluation of prediction models and decisions regarding implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) therapy. Baseline assumptions for a simulation framework were derived from previous randomized controlled trials ( n = 18) to identify minimal average SCD risk threshold that would translate to mortality benefit by ICD therapy also considering the effect of competing non-sudden mortality. ICD efficacy to prevent SCDs and other data for simulations were estimated using inverse-variance weighted meta-analysis of included trials. Number needed to treat (NNT) was evaluated over a 5- and 10-year horizons (≤ 20 defined as clinically relevant). Correlation analysis confirmed average annual SCD incidence in trial populations as the key factor associating with ICD therapy effectiveness to reduce mortality (Pearson’s r = 0.653, p < 0.01). In a simulation assuming 5% annual non-sudden mortality (pooled estimate of included RCTs) and a 56% (48–62%) efficacy for ICDs to reduce SCDs or similar events, 3% average annual SCD risk (≈ 12% over 5 years) emerged as the lowest practical threshold even after controlling for excess (overlapping) mortality among those saved successfully from SCD by ICD therapy. In populations with very low incidence of non-sudden mortality (1%), the lowest practical threshold over a longer 10-year time horizon was 1.3% (assuming no overlapping mortality). Even under substantial competing risk, populations with an average 3% (or higher) annual SCD incidence most likely would benefit from ICD therapy. Lower threshold may be considered only in populations with very low non-sudden mortality.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Cardiology and Cardiovascular Medicine > Cardiac pacing and defibrillation studies; Medicine > Cardiology and Cardiovascular Medicine > Cardiac electrophysiology and arrhythmias; Medicine > Emergency Medicine > Cardiac Arrest and Resuscitation

Article.Title: Study on the fracture initiation mechanisms of supercritical carbon dioxide and radial branch borehole cooperative fracturing in methane-bearing coal seams
Article.Authors: Zhang L.; Meng X.; Chen J.; Huang X.; Zuo S.
Article.Abstract: Deep methane-bearing coal seams are difficult to stimulate because of high in situ stress, strong gas adsorption, and low permeability. This study develops a theoretical–numerical framework to predict fracture initiation pressure (FIP) during supercritical carbon dioxide (SC-CO₂) fracturing assisted by radial branch boreholes. The model couples stress transformation, borehole-induced stress concentration, fluid seepage, and thermal stress, and accounts for bedding and joints through three competing failure modes: coal-matrix tensile failure, structural-plane shear failure, and structural-plane tensile opening. Validation against published true-triaxial data yielded a mean absolute relative error of 7.69% and captured the lower FIP of SC-CO₂ relative to hydraulic fracturing (HF). Under baseline conditions, SC-CO₂ reduced FIP by 3.68 MPa. FIP was controlled primarily by the three-dimensional stress state, initial gas pressure, and radial branch borehole configuration, whereas wellbore orientation had little influence. Wellbore-induced perturbations decayed rapidly, and FIP stabilized beyond a radial distance r of 0.4 m from the wellbore centerline. Branch orientation controlled both FIP and failure mode, with a minimum near 90° under the adopted conditions; increasing temperature differences reduced FIP approximately linearly. These findings provide a quantitative basis for optimizing SC-CO₂ fracturing with radial branch boreholes in methane-bearing coal seams.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Mechanical Engineering > Hydraulic Fracturing and Reservoir Analysis; Engineering > Ocean Engineering > Coal Properties and Utilization; Engineering > Mechanics of Materials > Rock Mechanics and Modeling

Article.Title: A deep learning method for ECG heartbeat classification based on Gaussian features
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Liu J.; Shu L.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Electrocardiography (ECG) is a vital tool for diagnosing and screening cardiovascular diseases. Accurately extracting ECG signal features is key to improving the accuracy of arrhythmia classification. To address the limitations of traditional methods in terms of feature extraction precision and discrimination capability, this study proposes an ECG signal classification method based on Gaussian features. First, the R-peak is identified via the visibility graph algorithm, and its prominence is computed to locate the onset and offset of the P, Q, R, S, and T waves across the heartbeat waveform. Five Gaussian components are then fitted to the segmented signal, yielding 16 highly discriminative features for classification. Furthermore, an AMH–BiLSTM architecture is developed by integrating convolutional neural networks, bidirectional long short-term memory, and multi-head attention mechanisms, with two fully connected layers performing the final classification task. To address class imbalance in the MIT–BIH Arrhythmia Database, the SMOTE algorithm is employed to oversample minority classes. Moreover, over 10 independent random seeds, the proposed method achieves a mean classification accuracy of 97.93%, precision of 98.10%, recall of 97.92%, and F1-score of 97.99%, with a mean AUC of 99.90%. Compared to the baseline model under the same experimental setup, our proposed method has shown some improvements. In addition, we also provide reference comparisons with recent representative methods, and our method demonstrates competitive classification performance under comparable evaluation protocols.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Cardiology and Cardiovascular Medicine > ECG Monitoring and Analysis; Medicine > Cardiology and Cardiovascular Medicine > Cardiac electrophysiology and arrhythmias; Engineering > Biomedical Engineering > Non-Invasive Vital Sign Monitoring

Article.Title: Hybrid post-quantum explainable AI intrusion detection with SDN for heterogeneous IoT networks
Article.Authors: Li S.; He Y.; Xu Y.; Xie S.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Significant security concerns have been brought about by the fast growth of heterogeneous Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystems, especially in environments enabled by Software-Defined Networking (SDN), where centralized control increases network programmability but also generates high-value attack surfaces. This study presents HPQ-EAI-IDS, a unified intrusion detection system designed for various IoT networks, emphasizing explainable graph-oriented attack identification, and incorporating post-quantum-secured control-plane communication along with SDN-supported mitigation as supplementary architectural enhancements for future deployment validation. In order to detect attacks, the system uses a Graph Neural Network (GNN) to identify structural relationships between communicating entities by modeling IoT traffic as dynamic graph structures. By determining the most significant characteristics linked to identified attack classes, the explainability component enhances model transparency even more. The SDN-assisted mitigation mechanism is analytically evaluated as an architectural extension rather than through a physical SDN-IoT deployment, and the experimental evaluation concentrates on intrusion-detection performance using the CICIoT2023 dataset along with computational and cryptographic overhead analysis. As a result, network-level metrics like packet delivery improvement and throughput recovery represent anticipated operational gains that need to be validated in real-world testbeds in the future.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Computer Networks and Communications > Network Security and Intrusion Detection; Computer Science > Hardware and Architecture > Network Packet Processing and Optimization; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Internet Traffic Analysis and Secure E-voting

Article.Title: A geospatial decision-support framework for groundwater potential zonation and artificial recharge planning in the Bikkeru watershed, India
Article.Authors: Shekar P.; Shinde A.; Prasanth M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Groundwater, as a key natural resource held in aquifers, is important for the development of the economy, human health and ecological systems. With the increasing demand for water, it has become essential to extract groundwater. The development of geo-information technology has simplified the monitoring and management of these resources. This study presents a comprehensive methodology for identifying suitable artificial recharge locations in the Bikkeru Watershed, India, using geospatial tools and multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) techniques, including the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), Fuzzy-AHP, and Multi-Influencing Factor (MIF) methods. The novelty of this study lies in the comparative evaluation of AHP, Fuzzy-AHP, and MIF methods, followed by the selection of the best-performing model for identifying suitable artificial recharge sites. The framework took into account ten thematic layers: elevation, drainage density, land use and land cover, geology, rainfall, topographic wetness index, geomorphology, soil, distance from the river, and slope. Each layer had some weight assigned depending on how much it affects groundwater recharge potential. The research delineated groundwater potential zones (GWPZs), categorizing the region into high, moderate, and low recharge zones by the integration of these layers within a geospatial framework. Using ground truth data and the area under the curve (AUC) metric, the AHP model produced an accuracy of 73.4%, while the Fuzzy-AHP model achieved a higher accuracy of 87.5% and the MIF model achieved an accuracy of 70.2%. Lineaments and drainage networks were superimposed to identify artificial recharge site points. These points were then overlaid on the best-performing Fuzzy-AHP map to identify suitable artificial recharge sites according to the different groundwater potential zones. Furthermore, 186 possible sites for artificial recharge were found; suggestions to create check dams and percolation ponds would help to enhance groundwater replenishment. This study identifies and safeguards key groundwater recharge zones using integrated geospatial and decision-support methods, directly supporting sustainable development goal 6.
Article.TopicFields: Environmental Science > Environmental Engineering > Groundwater and Watershed Analysis; Environmental Science > Management, Monitoring, Policy and Law > Soil and Land Suitability Analysis; Decision Sciences > Management Science and Operations Research > Multi-Criteria Decision Making

Article.Title: Post-traumatic growth and its predictors in young and middle-aged coronary heart disease patients: a latent profile analysis
Article.Authors: Ren L.; Ahn S.
Article.Abstract: The prevalence and mortality of coronary heart disease among young and middle-aged adults are rising, and these patients experience substantial psychosocial impairment owing to the multifaceted and long-lasting symptoms of the disease. Post-traumatic growth, a positive psychological change arising from the struggle with illness, is associated with better health-promoting behaviors and prognosis. This study aimed to identify profiles of post-traumatic growth and their associated factors in young and middle-aged patients with coronary heart disease. This cross-sectional study was conducted from October 2023 to September 2024. In total, 513 young and middle-aged patients with coronary heart disease were recruited from a tertiary hospital in China. Self-reported questionnaires were used to collect data on demographic and clinical characteristics, resilience, and post-traumatic growth. Latent profile analysis and multinomial logistic regression were performed in R to identify profiles of post-traumatic growth and their predictors. Three profiles were identified: high (43.1%), moderate (44.2%), and low (12.7%) post-traumatic growth. Demographic, clinical, and psychological factors distinguished profile membership: higher growth was associated with a higher educational level, a middle-range family monthly income (1000–5000 RMB), the absence of comorbidities, fewer previous hospital admissions, longer disease duration, and higher resilience. More than half of the patients showed only moderate or low post-traumatic growth, and resilience specifically distinguished the highest growth profile. Profile-tailored, stepped psychosocial support, prioritizing recently diagnosed patients with heavier illness burden and lower resilience, may help foster growth in this population.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Cardiology and Cardiovascular Medicine > Cardiac Health and Mental Health; Medicine > Oncology > Cancer survivorship and care; Psychology > Clinical Psychology > Resilience and Mental Health

Article.Title: Technology acceptance mediates associations between pre-service physical education teachers’ AI-TPACK and study engagement and behavioral intentions in digital teaching
Article.Authors: Pan Z.; Ren Y.; Lin X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Against the backdrop of artificial intelligence (AI) reshaping the educational landscape, the digital transformation of physical education has placed greater demands on preservice physical education teachers’ (PSPETs’) capacity to integrate technology. However, research remains limited on the effects of pres-ervice physical education teachers’ artificial intelligence technological pedagogical content knowledge (PSPETs AI-TPACK) on their study engagement (SE) and behavioral intentions (BI) in digital teaching, as well as on the role played by technology acceptance (TA) in these relationships.This study involved 1,144 undergraduate and postgraduate students enrolled in physical education, physical education teaching, or physical education and training programmes at five higher education institutions in Guangzhou, Guangdong Province. Using adapted scales, data were collected on PSPETs AI-TPACK, TA, SE, and BI. Structural equation modelling (SEM) was then employed to examine the relationships among these variables and the mediating effects. The findings showed that PSPETs AI-TPACK significantly and positively predicted both SE and BI in digital teaching. TA played a significant partial mediating role in the relationships between PSPETs AI-TPACK and SE, and between PSPETs AI-TPACK and BI. These results indicate that PSPETs AI-TPACK can promote PSPETs’ SE and BI both directly and indirectly by enhancing their TA. This study extends the theoretical understanding of the relationships between PSPETs AI-TPACK and SE and BI in digital physical education teaching, while also providing empirical evidence for improving preservice physical education teacher education in higher education institutions. Higher education institutions should incorporate AI-based instructional design and practice into physical education teacher education curricula, implement tiered and progressive technology training, create authentic digital teaching contexts, and enhance PSPETs’ TA through resource provision and exemplary applications. These measures can, in turn, strengthen PSPETs’ SE and BI in using AI technologies to support physical education teaching.
Article.TopicFields: Health Professions > Physical Therapy, Sports Therapy and Rehabilitation > Physical Education and Pedagogy; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Educational Technology and Pedagogy; Computer Science > Information Systems > Artificial Intelligence in Education

Article.Title: Evaluation of 1-octadecyl-3-methylimidazolium bromide for enhanced oil recovery: interfacial behavior and pore-scale displacement in a glass micromodel
Article.Authors: Roosta Tasooji M.; Esfandiari N.; Nabipour M.; Arab Aboosadi Z.; Azizi M.
Article.Abstract: The efficiency of conventional surfactants in chemical enhanced oil recovery (EOR) is often limited by high salinity, elevated temperatures, and adsorption-related chemical losses, particularly in carbonate reservoirs. These limitations have motivated the investigation of alternative surface-active agents with favorable interfacial performance under challenging conditions. In this study, the interfacial and pore-scale displacement performance of the ionic liquid 1-octadecyl-3-methylimidazolium bromide ([C18mim][Br]) was investigated through a combination of interfacial tension (IFT) measurements and flooding experiments in a heterogeneous glass micromodel. A systematic experimental program was conducted to evaluate the effects of ionic liquid concentration, salinity, and temperature on oil–water interfacial behavior and displacement efficiency. The ionic liquid reduced the oil–water IFT from approximately 89 mN/m to below 2 mN/m as the [C18mim][Br] concentration was increased from 0 to 200 ppm, corresponding to a reduction greater than 97%. A pronounced salinity-dependent interfacial response was observed, with an IFT value of approximately 0.36 mN/m at 22,500 ppm NaCl and a nominal ionic-liquid concentration of 50 ppm in the salinity-focused experiments. Micromodel flooding experiments further showed that injection of a nominal 10 ppm [C18mim][Br] solution increased the final recovery factor to approximately 58% relative to conventional water flooding under the tested micromodel conditions. Temperature elevation also improved the observed displacement performance, with recovery increasing from 36.8% at 25 °C to 48.1% at 60 °C. The results further demonstrated that the lowest IFT condition did not necessarily correspond to the highest oil recovery, indicating that pore-scale displacement performance depends on coupled interfacial and flow-related mechanisms. Overall, the findings indicate that [C18mim][Br] provides strong interfacial modification and favorable pore-scale displacement performance at the tested concentrations under the controlled experimental conditions investigated. However, the present study did not quantify ionic-liquid adsorption or retention on carbonate minerals, glass surfaces, or within porous media, and therefore the reported concentrations should not be interpreted as field dosage or as evidence of low chemical consumption at reservoir scale. Accordingly, the results should be regarded as a pore-scale screening assessment that provides a basis for further carbonate-specific validation rather than direct evidence of carbonate-reservoir applicability.
