Article.Title: Machine learning predicts postoperative lung metastasis in upper tract urothelial carcinoma
Article.Authors: Wu H.; Xu T.; Cao H.; Li Y.; Zhou H.; Wang L.; Ye Z.; Shi X.; Zhang W.; Gao B.
Article.Abstract: Early detection of individuals at high risk for lung metastasis (LM) from upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) is important for postoperative risk stratification and surveillance planning. This retrospective study used five machine learning techniques to predict LM risk in UTUC patients. Data from the SEER database (2000–2017) were analyzed. The SEER cohort was randomly divided into a training set and an internal test set in a 7:3 ratio for model development and internal validation. No synthetic resampling technique was used in the final analysis. The Boruta algorithm and multivariable logistic regression identified key independent variables. The model’s performance was validated with data from 569 UTUC patients at the First Hospital of Jilin University. Evaluation included AUC, AUPRC, decision curve analysis, and SHAP interpretation. An online tool was developed for clinical use. Among the five machine learning models, RF showed strong apparent performance in some metrics, whereas LR demonstrated greater stability and generalizability across the internal test and external validation sets. Therefore, an LM-specific UTUC risk calculator was developed using LR for clinical application. This study developed a clinical prediction model for assessing LM risk in UTUC patients, offering potential support for clinical decision-making.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Surgery > Bladder and Urothelial Cancer Treatments; Medicine > Radiology, Nuclear Medicine and Imaging > Radiomics and Machine Learning in Medical Imaging; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > AI in cancer detection

Article.Title: DNA metabarcoding reveals that Galapagos pinnipeds might not be competing as thought
Article.Authors: Urquía D.; Anslan S.; Tedersoo L.; Moreira-Mendieta A.; Vences M.; Páez-Rosas D.
Article.Abstract: Interspecific competition is a key process shaping species distributions and biodiversity. In the western bioregion of the Galapagos archipelago, two endemic and endangered pinniped species coexist: the Galapagos sea lion (GSL) and the Galapagos fur seal (GFS). Previous studies reported marked dietary differences between these species and proposed niche partitioning as the mechanism allowing their coexistence. However, these works neither precisely identified prey at the species level, nor compared diets under conditions of coexistence versus non-coexistence, leaving trophic partitioning by interspecific competition largely untested. Here, we used DNA metabarcoding to analyze GSL and GFS diets across five settings encompassing coexistence and non-coexistence, and multiple Galapagos bioregions. Although we confirmed dietary differences between GSL ( N = 22 to 50 depending on setting) and GFS ( N = 12), our results provide little evidence that these differences arise from interspecific competition. Contrary to expectations under a competition-driven setting, GSL occurring alone did not exploit prey typically consumed by GFS when these coexisted. Instead, GSL diets remained diverse and similar across settings, regardless of GFS presence. Thus, rather than competition, spatial variation in the archipelago’s oceanographic conditions better explain the dietary patterns of both endemic pinnipeds.
Article.TopicFields: Environmental Science > Ecology > Marine animal studies overview; Environmental Science > Ecology > Environmental DNA in Biodiversity Studies; Environmental Science > Ecology > Isotope Analysis in Ecology

Article.Title: Chromosome-resolved genome of the rice blast fungus Magnaporthe oryzae KJ201 enables comparative analysis of genome architecture and pathogenicity-associated loci
Article.Authors: Chung H.; Nam Y.; Hue Y.; Kim J.; Choi B.; An S.; Ko J.; Lee Y.; Park S.; Kim K.
Article.Abstract: Rice blast, caused by Magnaporthe oryzae , threatens rice production and is a model for fungal pathogenicity. The Korean rice isolate KJ201 has supported extensive functional, transcriptomic, and epigenomic research, but its fragmented reference genome has limited chromosome-scale interpretation. PacBio HiFi and Hi-C sequencing produced a 44.8 Mb assembly comprising seven chromosome-scale scaffolds and three mini-scaffolds, with an N50 of 6.5 Mb and 98.5% complete BUSCOs. Comparative analysis with 17 public M. oryzae genomes grouped KJ201 with P131 and O-135, separately from the 70-15/Guy11-containing rice subclade. The seven core chromosomes were broadly conserved, whereas localized chromosome-terminal differences and variable breakpoint burdens characterized the sampled comparisons. Gene-family content was largely conserved. Secreted effector candidates showed elevated local repeat density, and 61 ORF-disrupting pathogenicity-associated loci from the KJ201 Agrobacterium-mediated insertional mutant collection were mapped across all seven major chromosomes. This assembly connects comparative chromosome organization, candidate effector genomic context, and legacy mutant phenotypes in a native KJ201 reference.
Article.TopicFields: Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Plant Disease Resistance and Genetics; Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Molecular Biology > Fungal and yeast genetics research; Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Cell Biology > Plant Pathogens and Fungal Diseases

Article.Title: Optimal transport-based synthetic histology generation using cytomorphological Wasserstein barycenters for rare cervical malignancy classification
Article.Authors: Roopa C.; Shanthi N.
Article.Abstract: Despite its potential, the automated cervical cytology analysis is severely limited by the lack of rare malignant cell samples and the class imbalance that is frequently associated with them, resulting in biased predictions and limited generalisation capabilities to clinically relevant abnormal categories. The existing augmentation based methods and generative methods, such as SMOTE, GANs, and variational autoencoders, have major limitations including unrealistic cellular morphologies, mode collapse, feature blur, and lack of biological or statistical assurance, which makes them less reliable for medical decision support. To overcome these problems, this work proposes a novel Optimal Transport based synthetic histology generation framework, Wasserstein Cellular Barycenter Optimal Transport (WCB-OT), that consists of entropic Sinkhorn regularized optimal transport, cytomorphological transport costs, Wasserstein barycenter synthesis and dynamical optimal transport interpolation, to create biologically consistent rare cervical malignancy samples. In contrast to GAN-based, VAE-based and diffusion-based augmentation methods, our proposed method contains no adversarial learning, latent reconstruction, or iterative denoising; instead, it synthesizes a representation by explicitly modeling a distribution transport based on the morphology, and Wasserstein barycentric interpolation. Experimental evaluation on the SIPaKMeD cervical cytology dataset demonstrated that WCB-OT achieved an F1-score of 0.94, AUC-ROC of 0.98, and FID of 1.05, compared with 0.78, 0.91, and 2.67, respectively, for StyleGAN2, the strongest GAN-based baseline, and 0.74, 0.86, and 4.26, respectively, for the SMOTE interpolation-based baseline. The improvements were statistically significant across five independent experimental runs ( p < 0.001). Moreover, the proposed framework offers interpretable transport mappings and biologically meaningful intermediate (cell to cell) transformations that facilitate explainable and clinically reliable synthesis of data. The results indicate that the proposed WCB-OT framework provides a biologically sound, clinically feasible, and theoretically sound approach to enhancing the reliability and diagnostic power of AI-based cervical cancer screening systems for rare cervical malignancies.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > AI in cancer detection; Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis; Medicine > Epidemiology > Cervical Cancer and HPV Research

Article.Title: Comparison of plastic stents and lumen-apposing metal stents in endoscopic ultrasound-guided gallbladder drainage for acute cholecystitis in high-risk surgical patients
Article.Authors: Okuno M.; Mukai T.; Kataoka F.; Iwata K.; Tezuka R.; Iwasa Y.; Koizumi T.; Shimojo K.; Ohashi Y.; Iwata S.; Mita N.; Maruta A.; Uemura S.; Ichikawa H.; Yoshida K.; Iwashita T.; Tomita E.; Yasuda I.; Moriwaki H.; Shimizu M.
Article.Abstract: Endoscopic ultrasound-guided gallbladder drainage (EUS-GBD) for acute cholecystitis (AC) has a high technical and clinical success rate and is beneficial for patients’ quality of life due to internal fistula drainage, especially for high-risk surgical patients. Two drainage devices (plastic stent [PS] and lumen-apposing metal stent [LAMS]) are available; however, suitable drainage devices remain unclear. Between 2016 and 2026, 20 PS and 20 LAMS placement high-risk surgical AC were compared. Technical and clinical success rates, the number of dilation cases for the puncture route, procedure time, adverse events (AEs), and hospital stay were evaluated. There was no significant difference in patients’ backgrounds, except for the number of prior percutaneous gallbladder drainage cases (75% in PS group vs. 10% in LAMS group; P < 0.01). The shortest gallbladder diameter tended to be larger in the LAMS (30-mm) than in the PS group (25-mm; P = 0.052). Dilation of the puncture site was required in all PS cases. The technical and clinical success rates were 100% in both groups. EUS-GBD procedure time was significantly shorter in the LAMS group (7 min. vs. 21 min.; P < 0.01). The AEs occurrence rate was significantly higher in the PS group (40% vs. 5%; P = 0.02), and the hospital stay was shorter in the LAMS group (10 vs. 34 days; P = 0.047). Technical and clinical success did not differ between LAMS and PS. In this exploratory analysis, LAMS was associated with shorter procedure time and hospital stay and fewer AEs, suggesting it may be a safe, useful option. Clinical trial registration : UMIN000060137.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Pulmonary and Respiratory Medicine > Gallbladder and Bile Duct Disorders; Medicine > Surgery > Minimally Invasive Surgical Techniques; Medicine > Surgery > Pancreatitis Pathology and Treatment

Article.Title: An adaptive polarization correction algorithm for mitigating time-varying amplitude and phase errors
Article.Authors: Ma Z.; Qi Z.; Xu H.; Shi Y.
Article.Abstract: In dual-channel polarization diversity reception systems, amplitude and phase errors exhibit temporal variations due to factors such as mechanical antenna vibration, local oscillator drift, and gain fluctuations, leading to the distortion of polarization characteristics. In this paper, by constructing a time-varying amplitude and phase error model for dual-channel systems and analyzing the underlying error mechanisms, we design a joint blind equalization model in the polarization domain. A two-stage polarization adaptive filtering correction algorithm, termed TPAF, is proposed. The first stage involves variable-step-size polarization amplitude-phase momentum adaptive filtering (VPM-NLMS), which dynamically adjusts the iteration step size based on phase concentration and amplitude variance, while introducing a momentum mechanism to accelerate transient convergence, thereby achieving preliminary noise reduction and bias correction of the polarization sequence. The second stage employs a multi-constraint polarization correction autoencoder (PC-AE) for feature reconstruction. A polarization amplitude-phase correction loss function is proposed, which combines reconstruction loss, temporal smoothing loss, and phase concentration loss to stabilize the polarization fingerprint and separate transient noise using a convolutional encoder-decoder architecture, thereby enabling polarization feature reconstruction. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can theoretically effectively suppress time-varying channel disturbances and significantly reduce estimation errors in polarization amplitude and phase. Real-world data results indicate that the algorithm presented in this paper exhibits a marked improvement over existing adaptive filtering algorithms, fully validating its reliability and practical value.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Computational Mechanics > Advanced Adaptive Filtering Techniques; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Advanced Signal Processing Techniques; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Advanced Power Amplifier Design

Article.Title: Plant-derived oxylipins modulate fumonisin production through transcriptional and lipid metabolic changes in Fusarium verticillioides
Article.Authors: Di Pasquale G.; Giorni P.; Campmajó G.; Bertuzzi T.; Leggieri M.; Marocco A.; Dall’Asta C.; Battilani P.; Lanubile A.
Article.Abstract: Plant-derived oxylipins play pivotal roles in plant immunity and have emerged as important mediators of cross-kingdom communication with fungal pathogens. Although several oxylipins exhibit antifungal activity, their impact on mycotoxin biosynthesis and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the effects of three maize-associated oxylipins, jasmonic acid (JA), trans-2-hexenal (T2H), and traumatic acid (TA), on mycotoxin production by Fusarium verticillioides , Aspergillus flavus and F. graminearum . Among the compounds tested, T2H and JA significantly reduced fumonisin (FB) accumulation in F. verticillioides , whereas aflatoxin and deoxynivalenol production remained unaffected in A. flavus and F. graminearum , respectively, highlighting species-specific responses to host-derived oxylipins. To elucidate the mechanisms underlying FB inhibition, transcriptomic and lipidomic analyses were performed on F. verticillioides following JA and T2H treatments. Both oxylipins induced extensive transcriptional reprogramming affecting genes involved in signal transduction, nutrient transport, chromatin remodeling, autophagy, fungal development, and endogenous oxylipin metabolism. Surprisingly, despite the marked reduction in FB accumulation, genes of the fumonisin ( FUM ) biosynthetic cluster were transcriptionally induced, suggesting that oxylipin-mediated inhibition occurs through regulatory networks acting upstream or independently of FUM gene expression. Lipidomic profiling further revealed substantial remodeling of fungal oxylipin metabolism, with pronounced accumulation of lipoxygenase- and linoleate diol synthase-derived metabolites, including hydroxyoctadecadienoic, dihydroxyoctadecadienoic and dihydroxyoctadecenoic acids, particularly following T2H treatment. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that host-derived oxylipins modulate FB production by reshaping fungal regulatory and metabolic networks rather than by directly repressing toxin biosynthetic genes. This work provides new insights into oxylipin-mediated cross-kingdom communication and identifies T2H as a promising candidate for sustainable strategies to mitigate FB contamination in maize.
Article.TopicFields: Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Plant Science > Mycotoxins in Agriculture and Food; Medicine > Pharmacology > Microbial Natural Products and Biosynthesis; Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Cell Biology > Plant Pathogens and Fungal Diseases

Article.Title: GIS-MCDA-based groundwater recharge potential zonation and artificial recharge site identification in coastal Ramanathapuram, India
Article.Authors: Velusamy P.; Rajakumar S.; Sashikkumar M.; Jino R.
Article.Abstract: In this study, an effort was made to demarcate the zones of groundwater recharge potential along with the identification of preliminary candidate locations for the construction of artificial recharge structures (ARS) in the coastal region of Ramanathapuram District, Tamil Nadu State of India through an integrated approach of GIS & MCDA technique. There are eight thematic layers like rainfall, lineament density, drainage density, geomorphology, lithology, soil, slope, and land use/land cover (LULC) used in this study depending upon the influence of each factor on the recharge of groundwater. The random forest technique was adopted to prepare LULC map. The recharge potential zones generated from the analysis were categorized into very high, high, moderate, low, and very low recharge potential zones. The very high potential zone occupies 38.94% (1621.38 km 2 ) of the district, followed by high (22.23%; 925.64 km 2 ), moderate (19.12%; 796.29 km 2 ), low (11.00%; 458.14 km 2 ) and very low (8.71%; 362.55 km 2 ). From the above spatial distribution, it can be seen that rainfall, lineament density, drainage density, geomorphology and favorable lithology and soil conditions have a strong influence on the recharge potential, where the relatively favorable zones occur in central, northern, coastal and deltaic areas of the district. Preliminary candidate locations for construction of artificial recharge structures like check dams, percolation tanks, nala bunds have been determined based on groundwater potential zones, hydrogeomorphological features and drainage conditions. The aforementioned sites are screening level locations that need to be validated through field hydrogeology before their application. The findings of this study are useful for spatial planning for conservation of groundwater and artificial recharge operations in the semi-arid coastal region of Ramanathapuram District.
Article.TopicFields: Environmental Science > Environmental Engineering > Groundwater and Watershed Analysis; Environmental Science > Management, Monitoring, Policy and Law > Soil and Land Suitability Analysis; Earth and Planetary Sciences > Geochemistry and Petrology > Groundwater and Isotope Geochemistry

Article.Title: Changes in adaptive behavior, gut microbiota and fecal metabolites following an integrative intervention in children with autism spectrum disorder
Article.Authors: Even C.; D’Amico F.; Andrawes J.; Marie A.; Mansour-Kassabri A.; Nimri L.; Horovitz O.; Karsh N.; Musa S.; Elias N.; Tamir S.; Turroni S.; Magzal F.
Article.Abstract: Emerging research suggests a link between gut microbiota, gut-derived metabolites, and autism spectrum disorder (ASD)-related behaviors and gastrointestinal issues. However, the clinical effectiveness and potential interactions of integrative interventions remain poorly understood. This pilot study compared TABAM, an integrative treatment, with conventional therapy for adaptive behavior in children aged 3–7 years with ASD. Participants received either TABAM or conventional therapy for 12 months. Adaptive behavior and autism symptom severity were assessed at baseline and follow-up using VABS-II and CARS2-ST. Stool samples were collected at both time points for gut microbiota profiling using 16 S rRNA amplicon sequencing and targeted metabolomics. Sixteen of 22 enrolled children completed the study (TABAM n = 10; control n = 6). VABS-II scores improved within the TABAM group, but the change did not differ significantly between groups. In the TABAM group, fecal serotonin increased and citrulline decreased; fecal propionate showed a significant between-group difference, decreasing in the TABAM group relative to controls. Other metabolite changes did not remain significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Gut microbiota beta diversity did not differ significantly between groups or over time, whereas the TABAM group was comparatively associated with the preservation of phylogenetic diversity, and some compositional changes, particularly an increase in Bifidobacterium . These exploratory findings suggest that TABAM may be associated with improvements in adaptive functioning and concurrent changes in gut microbiome composition and metabolite profiles, supporting larger studies to clarify its potential clinical benefit and explore possible gut-brain axis mechanisms.
Article.TopicFields: Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Molecular Biology > Gut microbiota and health; Neuroscience > Cognitive Neuroscience > Autism Spectrum Disorder Research; Medicine > Psychiatry and Mental health > Child Nutrition and Feeding Issues

Article.Title: Standard and decoupled knowledge distillation for lightweight radiographic knee osteoarthritis grading and triage
Article.Authors: Hasan U.; Nayeem M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This retrospective study compares standard knowledge distillation (KD) and decoupled knowledge distillation (DKD) fo​r lightweight artificial intelligence-based​ radiographic knee osteoarthritis grading. GhostNetV2 students learned five Kellgren–Lawrence grades from a Swin-Tiny teacher and were evaluated against a cross-entropy baseline using an Osteoarthritis Initiative-derived dataset of 8260 images from 4130 patients with patient-disjoint partitions. Across three​ runs, mean binary triage accuracy was 84.04%, 84.82%, and 84.82% for baseline, standard KD, and DKD. Thresholds targeting at least 90% validation specificity yielded test sensitivities of 72.77%, 76.56%, and 75.50%, with specificities of 92.09%, 90.94%, and 91.12%; these operating points are not specificity-matched. Mean five-class accuracy was 64.63%, 67.63%, and 67.71%. Separate illustrative checkpoints showed reduced KL-1-to-KL-2 overcalls with DKD (28.0 to 18.9%) but lower KL-0 recall (90.6 to 78.7%). Calibration, exploratory decision curves, and patient-cluster uncertainty intervals were evaluated. Each student contains 4.88 million parameters. Distillation improved mean performance internally, but decoupling did not demonstrate an additional sensitivity benefit over standard KD. No external cohort or clinician-supported decision policy was evaluated; clinical utility and population-level stability remain unestablished.
Article.Topic: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Health Informatics > Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education; Engineering > Biomedical Engineering > Medical Imaging and Analysis; Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Advanced Neural Network Applications

Article.Title: Mathematical analysis of a reaction-diffusion gambling information diffusion model
Article.Authors: Mandume M.; Nuugulu S.; Shikongo A.
Article.Abstract: This study develops and analyses a non-linear reaction–diffusion model for information spread, motivated by gambling-related information diffusion. The model is formulated as a susceptible–exposed–excessive–skeptical (SEIZ) system, in which individuals transition between information-related states through exposure, interaction, engagement, and resistance, while spatial diffusion captures heterogeneity across the population. The mathematical analysis establishes the existence, uniqueness, positivity, and boundedness of solutions, and derive both gambling-free and endemic equilibria. Two threshold quantities, \(\mathcal {R}_0^{ext} = \beta /\varepsilon\) and \(\mathcal {R}_0 = \alpha /\sigma\) , are obtained for the non-excessive and excessive states, respectively, yielding conditions for the persistence or elimination of these states. Diffusion-driven stability further assess how spatial effects modify the dynamics of the corresponding homogeneous system. For numerical analysis, the reaction–diffusion system is discretized using a semi-implicit Euler finite-difference method and the resulting non-linear system is solved by Newton’s method. The numerical experiments support the theoretical consistency, stability, and convergence of the method. Sensitivity analysis demonstrates that variations in the parameters entering the threshold quantities directly change the predicted qualitative dynamics. Although framed around gambling-related information, the main contribution of this work is the formulation and analysis of a general non-linear reaction–diffusion model that can be adapted to a broad class of spatial information and behavioral diffusion processes.
Article.Topic: Mathematical and Theoretical Epidemiology and Ecology Models

Article.Title: Aging of microplastics exposed to UV irradiation and its effect on the sorption of organic contaminants in freshwater
Article.Authors: Exojo-Trujillo S.; Hernández-Muñoz P.; Gavara R.
Article.Abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are recognised as vectors of hydrophobic organic contaminants in aquatic environments, yet their sorption behaviour can be strongly influenced by environmental aging processes. In this study, the effect of UV-induced photooxidative aging on the physicochemical properties and sorption capacity of common MPs was systematically investigated. Polymeric materials of different chemical nature, including polyolefins (HDPE, LDPE, PP), polyamides, PET, and PLA, were subjected to controlled UV irradiation to induce accelerated photooxidative aging under laboratory conditions. Photoaging induced significant surface modifications including increased roughness, microcrack formation, and changes in specific surface area, together with chemical oxidation evidenced by the formation of oxygen-containing functional groups. These changes resulted in altered surface polarity and reactivity. The sorption behaviour of aged MPs towards two representative polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), pyrene (PYR) and fluoranthene (FLU), was evaluated under freshwater conditions and compared with pristine materials. Results showed that UV aging generally increased the sorption capacity of these organic contaminants, although the extent of this effect depended on both polymer type and the specific PAH considered, being most consistently observed for pyrene sorption onto polyolefins. At environmentally relevant low concentrations, PAHs sorption followed a Henry linear isotherm. Kinetic analysis revealed fast sorption, reaching equilibrium within 20 h. Mechanistically, retention appeared to be governed by molecular diffusion of PAHs through the aqueous boundary layer surrounding the particles, while empirically, data were described by a pseudo-second order model, consistent with strong surface-mediated interactions rather than proof of a specific chemisorption mechanism. These findings demonstrate that photooxidative aging plays a key role in determining the environmental behaviour of MPs and their capacity to retain organic contaminants.
Article.TopicFields: Environmental Science > Pollution > Microplastics and Plastic Pollution; Environmental Science > Health, Toxicology and Mutagenesis > Toxic Organic Pollutants Impact; Environmental Science > Pollution > Pharmaceutical and Antibiotic Environmental Impacts

Article.Title: Wavelet denoising of inertial sensor input data for GNSS-INS integration: simulation approach
Article.Authors: Naik K.
Article.Abstract: Integrated Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) and Inertial Navigation System (INS) architectures are widely employed to achieve reliable and continuous navigation under conditions of signal blockage, interference, and degraded satellite visibility. Although GNSS provides long-term positioning accuracy, its performance deteriorates in challenging environments, whereas INS offers continuous navigation as a self-contained system but suffers from accumulated inertial sensor errors and drift over time. These limitations significantly affect positioning reliability, particularly during GNSS-denied operation. This paper presents a simulation-based investigation of wavelet-driven denoising techniques for preprocessing inertial sensor acceleration measurements in GNSS–INS integrated navigation systems. The study systematically evaluates and compares multiple wavelet-domain denoising strategies including decimated wavelet transform (DWT), un-decimated wavelet transform (UDWT), and least-square-method (LSM)-assisted adaptive thresholding integrated with UDWT for suppressing inertial sensor noise while preserving signal characteristics. Unlike conventional implementations that employ a single wavelet configuration, the proposed framework establishes a comparative methodology to analyze the trade-off between noise attenuation, reconstruction fidelity, computational complexity, and implementation constraints under practical navigation conditions. A realistic simulation environment incorporating inertial sensor error sources, GNSS observation uncertainty, and representative motion conditions was developed to evaluate denoising performance. The results demonstrate that DWT provides reduced memory usage and lower computational burden but may introduce reconstruction distortion due to coefficient down-sampling. In contrast, UDWT preserves temporal continuity and improves signal reconstruction quality at increased computational cost. The LSM-assisted UDWT approach further enhances denoising performance by reducing reconstruction artifacts and improving signal smoothness. The study demonstrates that wavelet-based preprocessing of inertial measurements can improve INS robustness and support more reliable GNSS–INS integrated navigation under real-time operational scenarios.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Aerospace Engineering > Inertial Sensor and Navigation; Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Image and Signal Denoising Methods; Engineering > Aerospace Engineering > GNSS positioning and interference

Article.Title: Heavy metals in road dust across contrasting urban settings and screening assessment of noncarcinogenic risk for adults and children
Article.Authors: Skorbiłowicz M.; Ofman P.; Łapiński D.; Sidoruk M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Road dust can retain metals from traffic and other urban sources and create repeated contact opportunities in pedestrian environments, yet evidence from smaller settlements remains limited. We compared Cr, Cu, Ni, Pb and Zn in 35 road-dust samples from four towns in north-eastern Poland selected as contrasting urban and transport settings. Pseudo-total concentrations were determined after aqua regia digestion, contamination was assessed using the geoaccumulation index (Igeo), contamination factor (CF) and pollution load index (PLI), and non-carcinogenic hazard was screened for adults and children using the United States Environmental Protection Agency (USEPA) framework. Zambrów had the highest median Cu, Zn, Cr and Ni concentrations, while statistically significant among-town differences were confined to Cr, Zn and Cu. Town-mean PLI values were below 1, but three Zambrów sites exceeded 1, indicating localised rather than town-wide multi-metal enrichment. The unrefined total hazard index across the five metals remained below 1 at all locations, reaching maximum values of 0.0238 for adults and 0.214 for children at Z11; among the metal-specific indices, median values were highest for Pb and maximum values for Cr, and ingestion was the dominant pathway. Because each town represented a unique combination of population size, transport function, road-network structure and local environmental conditions, the study could not estimate the independent effects of town size or transport pressure. The results therefore support an exploratory comparison of four case-study towns rather than causal source attribution, broad generalisation or site-specific risk prediction. Within this screening framework, transit-exposed towns and pedestrian-sensitive locations may warrant targeted repeated sampling, with Cu and Zn used as initial screening parameters followed by broader analysis where elevated concentrations persist.
Article.TopicFields: Environmental Science > Pollution > Heavy metals in environment; Environmental Science > Health, Toxicology and Mutagenesis > Heavy Metal Exposure and Toxicity; Environmental Science > Health, Toxicology and Mutagenesis > Environmental Toxicology and Ecotoxicology

Article.Title: Black hollyhock (Alcea rosea var. nigra) flower as a functional additive to enhance the quality characteristics of red velvet cake
Article.Authors: Beygmoradi M.; Mansouripour S.; Jafarpour A.
Article.Abstract: Red velvet cake is commonly prepared using synthetic food colorants. Given concerns regarding the adverse effects of synthetic colors on human health, using natural colorants in this product could be valuable. In this study, the effect of black hollyhock flower (BHF) at 0.1%, 0.3%, and 0.5% as a natural additive on the quality characteristics of red velvet cake was evaluated and compared with the synthetic colorant carmoisine. The BHF caused no significant difference in physicochemical properties (except for ash), L* value, and mold and yeast counts ( p > 0.05). The total phenolic content (TPC), flavonoids, anthocyanins, antioxidant activity, and a* value increased, while the b* value, peroxide value (PV), and free fatty acids (FFA) decreased ( p < 0.05). The highest levels of bioactive compounds were observed in cakes containing 0.5% BHF, with TPC (18.40 mg GAE/100 g), TFC (12.67 mg QE/100 g), and TAC (1.61 mg/100 g), which were increased by 22.16, 23.90, and 23 times, respectively, compared with the control. In addition, the PV and FFA values were reduced by 4 and 3.34 times, respectively, at the end of storage. The sensory characteristics were also acceptable with no significant difference between treatments ( p > 0.05). Therefore, BHF has potential as a natural functional additive and colorant in red velvet cake, with 0.5% BHF providing the most favorable overall quality characteristics.
Article.TopicFields: Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Food Science > Food Quality and Safety Studies; Chemistry > Analytical Chemistry > Dye analysis and toxicity; Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Food Science > Botanical Research and Applications

Article.Title: Open multi-year UAV surveys establish a reproducible seabird baseline for the Destruction Bay–North Foreland region, King George Island, Antarctica
Article.Authors: Fudala K.; Karaś P.; Kozakiewicz D.; Kurczaba T.; Bialik R.
Article.Abstract: Large sectors of the Antarctic Peninsula remain incompletely surveyed for breeding seabirds, while historical records often lack the spatial and methodological detail required to assess change. We combined broad uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) reconnaissance with targeted high-resolution mapping and repeated surveys to establish a spatially explicit contemporary baseline for surface-nesting seabirds in the Destruction Bay–North Foreland region of King George Island during the 2022/23–2025/26 breeding seasons. North Foreland was the principal breeding complex for Chinstrap Penguins and Southern Giant Petrels, with maxima of 53,310 and 560 active nests, respectively, while Cape Melville supported up to 493 Antarctic Shag nests. Independent annotations by three or four observers were highly reproducible: 45 of 49 survey–species combinations had coefficients of variation below 1% (median CV = 0.13%), and object-level matching showed strong spatial correspondence. Historical records corroborated the long-standing importance of the region but were too heterogeneous in survey timing, spatial extent and census units to support trend assessment. A published YOLOv6L Antarctic Shag detector retained high performance without retraining on later imagery and previously unseen colony settings (F1 = 94.7%). The released orthomosaics, observer-specific annotations and consensus products provide a transparent and reusable baseline for future monitoring, conservation assessment and automated image analysis.
Article.TopicFields: Environmental Science > Ecology > Avian ecology and behavior; Environmental Science > Ecology > Polar Research and Ecology; Environmental Science > Ecology > Marine animal studies overview

Article.Title: Pre-transplant cardiovascular risks and adverse outcomes in patients after receiving kidney transplantation
Article.Authors: Wan X.; Xu Z.; Wei R.; Liu H.; Gu L.; Shi Y.; Zhu Y.; Zeng X.
Article.Abstract: Kidney transplantation (KT) has been reported to significantly improve the survival rate of patients with end-stage renal disease, but the long-term risk for major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) or mortality remains uncertain. Our study aimed to evaluate the association between cardiovascular risk factors and adverse outcomes in patients after KT. Using raw data from the National Health Insurance Research Database in Taiwan, we included 3,562 adult patients (1997–2013) who underwent uncomplicated KT. The median follow-up was 7.7 years (IQR 4.8–10.6), with a total of 28,267 person-years. Patients were censored at the date of the primary event, death, or December 31, 2013, whichever occurred first. We evaluated adverse outcomes, including non-fatal acute myocardial infarction (AMI), non-fatal stroke, and/or all-cause death, as primary events during the observation period (up to 17 years). The association of cardiovascular risk factors before KT was assessed using multivariate Cox proportional hazards models, adjusted for age, sex, and other available baseline factors. We also performed Kaplan–Meier analysis to estimate the cumulative risk. Among these patients, 225 (6.3%) were aged over 60 years, and 1,895 (53.2%) were male. All-cause death occurred in 703 patients (19.7%), non-fatal AMI in 125 (3.5%), and non-fatal stroke in 104 (2.9%). Only 853 patients (23.9%) had a waiting time for KT of < 1 year. Logistic regression analysis showed that only diabetes (OR = 2.085, 95% CI: 1.749–2.484, P < 0.001), AMI (OR = 2.568, 95% CI: 1.621–4.070, P < 0.001), and stroke before KT (OR = 4.376, 95% CI: 2.720–7.041, P < 0.001) were significantly associated with primary events, whereas hypertension and dyslipidemia were not. Consistently, the fully adjusted Cox model showed that diabetes (HR = 1.560, 95% CI: 1.338–1.819, P < 0.001), AMI (HR = 1.692, 95% CI: 1.188–2.410, P = 0.004), and stroke before KT (HR = 2.226, 95% CI: 1.612–3.074, P < 0.001) were independently associated with the composite primary event. Pre-transplant diabetes, AMI, and stroke were associated with increased risks of MACCE and all-cause mortality after KT. These findings support preoperative cardiovascular risk stratification in KT candidates.

Article.Title: Perceived green-shipping knowledge and competency demands among Chinese enterprise respondents: an exploratory network analysis
Article.Authors: Lv C.; Zeng X.; Li J.
Article.Abstract: Workforce-needs surveys can conflate broad endorsement, uniform answering and specific relations among knowledge domains. We applied a measurement-aware diagnostic analysis to perceived green-shipping knowledge and competency demands. In a non-probability online survey, 93 Chinese enterprise respondents rated seven study-specific knowledge domains and selected six generic competencies; no invitation denominator was retained. Ratings were ceiling-concentrated (80.6–91.4% rated 4 or 5), and 41 respondents used one rating across all seven domains. A regularised network retained 15 of 21 positive edges, but centrality was unstable (CS = 0.10 for strength; CS = 0.20 for expected influence). We compared the observed edges with two post hoc simulation benchmarks, one reproducing a general importance factor and the other fixing the composition and margins of the 41 uniform-response records, using 20,000 datasets per benchmark under fixed-penalty and penalty-reselected estimation. Energy efficiency–clean fuels alone met the four-condition sensitivity criterion (q = 0.00105–0.00367); digitalisation–ESG was model-selection sensitive. No knowledge–competency correlation survived multiplicity correction. Thus, the survey does not establish a stable population network or observed task coupling. It identifies one association that persists under the specified sensitivity analyses and a diagnostic approach for separating survey-wide endorsement from candidate pair-specific workforce needs.
Article.TopicFields: Psychology > Social Psychology > Competency Development and Evaluation; Environmental Science > Environmental Engineering > Maritime Transport Emissions and Efficiency; Environmental Science > Management, Monitoring, Policy and Law > Sustainable Development and Policies

Article.Title: A predictive multi-agent learning framework for energy-constrained ultra-reliable edge systems under stochastic environments
Article.Authors: Ye Z.; Zhao X.; Jiang Y.; Wu X.; Wang W.; Shao X.; Hamian M.
Article.Abstract: Ultra-reliable low-latency systems operating at the network edge are increasingly constrained by stochastic environmental factors, including energy variability, dynamic workloads, and time-varying communication conditions. Existing learning-based resource management approaches predominantly rely on reactive decision-making and assume stable energy availability, limiting their applicability in energy-harvesting edge systems where uncertainty is intrinsic and future conditions critically influence system reliability. This study proposes a predictive multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for energy-constrained edge systems, designed to enable proactive and resilient decision-making under stochastic dynamics. The framework integrates a Transformer-enhanced graph attention predictor with a decentralized multi-agent learning architecture based on centralized training and decentralized execution. By jointly modeling energy harvesting processes, workload dynamics, and communication variability, the proposed approach allows agents to anticipate future system states and adapt resource allocation policies accordingly. A key contribution is the introduction of an energy-deficit-aware reward shaping mechanism, which incorporates both current and predicted energy conditions to guide agents toward proactive coordination and stability preservation. This mechanism enables emergent cooperative behavior without explicit inter-agent communication, improving robustness in non-stationary environments. Extensive simulations using trace-driven network environments demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly improves system reliability, energy efficiency, and latency performance compared to state-of-the-art reactive and optimization-based baselines. In particular, the approach reduces energy depletion events, stabilizes queue dynamics, and maintains ultra-reliable performance under severe environmental fluctuations.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Computer Networks and Communications > IoT and Edge/Fog Computing; Computer Science > Hardware and Architecture > Energy Efficiency in Computing; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Advanced Wireless Network Optimization

Article.Title: Modeling user attention continuity and interaction mechanisms in continuous interfaces of digital platforms
Article.Authors: Zhu J.
Article.Abstract: The paradigm shift from paginated to continuously scrolling interfaces has fundamentally altered how users interact with digital content. However, a theoretical framework for quantifying attention continuity in such environments remains absent. This study introduces the Attention Continuity Model (ACM), which quantifies users’ probability of sustained interaction through a composite metric—the Attention Continuity Index (ACI)—now formulated as a non-linear function incorporating quadratic terms for content similarity (S) and novelty (N) to capture their hypothesized inverted-U relationships, along with a linear term for interaction intensity (I). Furthermore, we propose, as a theoretical design specification for future empirical implementation, a Feedback Loop Mechanism (FLM) specifying how real-time user behaviors could dynamically inform content presentation. A 2 × 3 between-subjects controlled experiment ( N = 120) compared infinite scrolling versus paginated interfaces across three content types (similar, novel, mixed). Results demonstrated that infinite scrolling interfaces significantly prolonged session duration (18.5 vs. 12.3 min, t(118) = 11.47, p < .001, Cohen’s d = 2.10) and increased interaction frequency (45.2 vs. 28.7 actions, t(118) = 12.35, p < .001, d = 2.27). The ACI was substantially higher for infinite scrolling (M = 0.78, SD = 0.11) than paginated interfaces (M = 0.52, SD = 0.14). Mixed content (70% similar, 30% novel) yielded optimal attention continuity. The interface type manipulation significantly reduced bounce rates from 28.6% to 12.3%. The FLM’s real-time adjustments are proposed as a future direction rather than a validated empirical finding. This research provides a quantifiable framework for attention modeling in digital platforms, offering theoretical contributions to human-computer interaction and practical guidelines for ethical interface design.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Human-Computer Interaction > Innovative Human-Technology Interaction; Computer Science > Human-Computer Interaction > Usability and User Interface Design; Computer Science > Computer Science Applications > Digital Media and Philosophy

Article.Title: A federated learning framework for anomaly detection in electric vehicle charging networks
Article.Authors: Rehman A.; Ibrahim M.; Sarwar N.; Albahli A.; Hamdi M.; Hashmi M.
Article.Abstract: Charging networks for electric vehicles (EVs) are also coming under attack from cyber threats such as Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks, unauthorized access, load balancing the network, and sudden charging network disruptions. The traditional centralized anomaly-detection and authentication schemes are not suitable for large-scale, geographically distributed and privacy-focused charging infrastructure, as they include SPOF, high communication overhead and limited adaptability to the changing threats. This paper proposes a federated-learning (FL) framework, which is composed of (i) a dual-layer authentication architecture, namely a Global Authentication Protocol (GAP) using TLS with a fallback Local Authentication Protocol (LAP), and (ii) a heterogeneous pipeline of anomaly detections, such as supervised models (Random Forest, Decision Trees), unsupervised models (Autoencoders, Principal Component Analysis), and regression-based normal-behavior forecasters (Linear Regression, Support Vector Regression), with BERT-based log preprocessing. To ensure the parameters of the neural-network part of the model can be meaningfully aggregated, only the Autoencoder and the BERT-based log encoder are being aggregated using Federated Averaging. To achieve this aggregation for the other models, either the tree-based model or the PCA model are replaced by the global model after each round, which is referred to as a model-replacement strategy. A combined real-world dataset (ACN (Caltech and JPL sites) and ElaadNL (snapshot) was used together with a simulated dataset of 500 K events generated using ACN-Sim. DoS, unauthorized-access, load-balancing and abrupt-charging-disruption events were synthesized using a formal threat model and attack-injection procedure. To compare the baselines, all baselines (Hybrid IDS, System used in and a protocol-compliance reference implementation of ISO 15118) were re-implemented and tested using the same data splits, preprocessing and hardware. Across five repeated runs, the proposed framework achieved a mean detection accuracy of 95.4% (95% CI: 94.6–96.2%) on ACN, 92.1% (91.2–93.0%) on ElaadNL, and 90.3% (89.2–91.4%) on the simulated set, with mean latency of 205 ms (ACN), 223 ms (ElaadNL), and 248 ms (simulated). The framework has been tested to support an average of 1,500 concurrent charging sessions and achieved a measured 28.7% decrease in communication costs from a centralized baseline. We further study the framework’s ability to resist model-poisoning attacks through a secure aggregation mechanism (coordinate-wise median, with a fallback to a trimmed-mean algorithm). We also discuss the question of compatibility of the framework with Distributed Ledger Technologies (DLTs) for auditable federated updates. There are clear specifications and open discussion regarding the limitations of dataset diversity, real-time live-network validation, and lack of differential privacy.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Computer Networks and Communications > Network Security and Intrusion Detection; Engineering > Control and Systems Engineering > Smart Grid Security and Resilience; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Privacy-Preserving Technologies in Data

Article.Title: Study on properties, mechanism and carbon benefit of cementing tailings backfill with full solid waste binder
Article.Authors: Shu B.; Li Y.; Qiu W.; Zeng G.; Chen X.
Article.Abstract: The synergistic effects of full solid waste binder (FWB) on the performance of cemented tailings backfill (CTB) require in-depth investigation. In this study, the performance, mechanism and carbon emission benefit of FWB CTB are systematically investigated. Experimental results revealed that slurry fluidity is significantly reduced with increasing content of alkaline slag in FWB. Notably, ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBS) exhibited a more pronounced fluidity-reducing effect compared to steel slag. The compressive strength of CTB is gradually decreased as the FWB-to-tailings ratio decreases. Remarkably, at a 1:10 FWB-to-tailings ratio, the A4 CTB achieved 116% higher compressive strength than conventional cement CTB. Field trials confirmed the practical viability of FWB CTB, with engineering strength reaching 2.3 MPa, which exceeding the 1.8 MPa of design requirement. A4 CTB at a 1:6 FWB-to-tailings ratio demonstrated a 49% reduction in 14d drying shrinkage relative to cement CTB. More ettringite (AFt) was generated in A4 CTB, coupled with a substantial porosity reduction of 5.5%. A larger number of pores and unreacted particles was found in A7. The superior performance of FWB CTB is attributed to three synergistic mechanisms: (1) development of a denser CTB micro-structure, (2) increased formation of hydration, and (3) inherent shrinkage compensation capabilities. FWB exhibit a reduction of over 95% in carbon emission compared with Portland cement. A decrease in the FWB-to-tailings ratio, by contrast, results in a unexpected rise in carbon emission normalized to unit compressive strength.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Civil and Structural Engineering > Tailings Management and Properties; Engineering > Civil and Structural Engineering > Concrete and Cement Materials Research; Engineering > Civil and Structural Engineering > Geotechnical Engineering and Soil Stabilization

Article.Title: Dosimetric evaluation and energy optimization in proton therapy for Hodgkin’s lymphoma using a GATE-based Monte Carlo framework
Article.Authors: Anjomi M.; Sadeghi H.; Seif F.; Bayatiani M.
Article.Abstract: Proton therapy offers superior dose conformity because of the Bragg peak, which makes it particularly attractive for treating Hodgkin’s lymphoma (HL) in young patients. In this work, we aimed to (i) determine the optimal proton energy for a simplified spherical target (37 mm diameter, 5–42 mm depth) in a homogeneous water phantom consistent with clinical commissioning practice, and (ii) quantify the relative out-of-field doses to organs at risk (OARs) using a standardized anthropomorphic CIRS ATOM phantom. We used the GATE Monte Carlo (MC) toolkit to generate depth-dose curves in a water phantom for energies from 60 to 90 MeV. We selected the optimal energy by maximizing a weighted Target Coverage & Sparing (TCS) metric that accounts for both target dose coverage and sparing of normal tissue distal to the target. The 70 MeV beam maximized this metric for the investigated target geometry (5–42 mm depth), with a TCS value of 0.876 and 93.8% target coverage. We then calculated absorbed doses to OARs using a voxelized CIRS ATOM phantom. Relative organ doses showed an approximately exponential decrease with distance, ranging from 39.9 mGy (left lung) to 0.079 mGy (thyroid) per Gray of physical dose to the target. All simulations had statistical uncertainties below 2% in the target volume and below 3.2% in organs at risk. This methodological framework provides a standardized reference for comparing proton therapy plans and assessing secondary cancer risks in a standardized geometry for HL patients, upon further validation with patient-specific data.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Pulmonary and Respiratory Medicine > Radiation Therapy and Dosimetry; Physics and Astronomy > Radiation > Advanced Radiotherapy Techniques; Medicine > Radiology, Nuclear Medicine and Imaging > Radiopharmaceutical Chemistry and Applications

Article.Title: Temperature-dependent operating margins of proton-irradiated integrated 4H-SiC CMOS current mirrors
Article.Authors: Kwon T.; Yoon Y.; Moon J.; Woo S.; Seo J.
Article.Abstract: Integrated 4H-SiC CMOS current mirrors and co-fabricated MOSFETs were characterized at temperatures up to 180 °C and after 15 MeV proton irradiation. The SiC mirrors retain highly linear current transfer over the measured current ranges, with coefficients of determination of 0.99943–0.999996 across the reported conditions. Heating reduces the threshold-voltage magnitude of both NMOS and PMOS devices, whereas irradiation predominantly increases the PMOS threshold-voltage magnitude and the supply voltage required for stable mirroring. Using a common target current ratio of 2.47, the minimum measured supply voltage of the type 2 mirror increases from 7.5 V before irradiation to 10.5 V after a fluence of 5 × 10¹³ cm⁻² at room temperature, and decreases to 9.5 V when the irradiated circuit is measured at 180 °C. Devices annealed in hydrogen before irradiation require higher supply voltages: 12.0 V at room temperature and 10.5 V at 180 °C. These results demonstrate partial, temperature-dependent improvement of the circuit operating margin after irradiation. They do not establish thermal removal of radiation-induced defects. The device and circuit measurements identify threshold-voltage shifts and processing history as relevant considerations for the operating margins of this SiC CMOS platform.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Radiation Effects in Electronics; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Silicon Carbide Semiconductor Technologies; Physics and Astronomy > Nuclear and High Energy Physics > Particle Detector Development and Performance

Article.Title: Orally active aminosteroid RM-581 suppresses tumor growth and metastasis formation in a gemcitabine-resistant orthotopic xenograft pancreatic cancer model
Article.Authors: Poirier D.; Chen Q.; Maltais R.; Roy J.; Ahamed F.; Arnold S.
Article.Abstract: New agents with distinct mechanisms of action are urgently needed to overcome drug resistance and improve survival, particularly in highly lethal cancers. The estrane derivative RM-581, designed through structure–activity relationship studies, needed to demonstrate efficacy in poor-prognosis cancer models, such as pancreatic cancer, to validate its therapeutic potential. Oral administration of RM-581 (30 mg/kg) in female mice revealed improved pharmacokinetic parameters (C max , AUC, bioavailability) when formulated in Propylene glycol: DMSO, compared with Glycerol: DMSO. Plasma levels of RM-581 increased dose-dependently, and once-daily dosing produced exposure comparable to twice-daily administration. In an orthotopic PANC-1 human pancreatic cancer xenograft model with female nu/nu mice, orally administered RM-581 inhibited tumor growth in a dose-dependent manner by 11%, 54%, and 74% at 10, 40 and 80 mg/kg, respectively. RM-581 at 80 mg/kg suppressed tumor growth by 74–95% and prevented metastasis, whereas 33% of control mice developed metastatic lesions. The combination of RM-581 with Pravastatin also prevented metastasis. RM-581 was well tolerated during 35- and 48-day treatment periods, with no clinical signs of toxicity, including stable body weight, normal organ appearance, unremarkable histopathology, and normal animal behavior, indicating a favorable safety profile. Together, these findings position RM-581 as a promising preclinical candidate warranting advancement into clinical development.
Article.TopicFields: Medicine > Oncology > Pancreatic and Hepatic Oncology Research; Chemistry > Organic Chemistry > Synthesis and biological activity; Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Cancer Research > Cancer, Lipids, and Metabolism

Article.Title: Experiences of a food-based very low-calorie diet programme among Chinese adults with obesity and prediabetes or type 2 diabetes: a COM-B-guided qualitative study
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Guo R.; Ge J.; Chen G.; Xu S.; Liu C.; Li D.; Zhou Y.
Article.Abstract: Very low-calorie diets (VLCDs) can halt the progression of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and induce remission. However, they currently face significant adherence challenges, limited long-term efficacy, and acceptability issues among Chinese populations due to cultural differences. Aiming to explore the perceptions, experiences of individuals with obesity and prediabetes or T2DM who are consuming VLCDs, this descriptive qualitative study was conducted guided by the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation-Behaviour (COM-B) model. Purposeful sampling selected participants at two hospitals in China between July and August 2024. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed via a COM-B–guided framework analysis. Fourteen participants completed the interviews, revealing 8 subthemes: (1) Capability factors: A lack of self-control hinders adherence to dietary routines, whereas limited physical ability restricts engagement in daily exercise; (2) Opportunity factors: Supportive physical environments and strong social networks facilitate the maintenance of health behaviours, whereas competing life priorities often lead to the neglect of health management; (3) Motivation factors: The perceived threat of disease and positive treatment feedback enhance behavioural motivation, whereas discomfort and negative experiences related to dietary restriction undermine adherence sustainability. Future research should focus on developing targeted and sustainable lifestyle management programmes to enhance dietary compliance and diabetes management outcomes.

Article.Title: Seismic performance optimization analysis of HPEC beam to H-section column joints
Article.Authors: Yao Y.; Liu Y.; Sun S.; Wang W.; Dong J.
Article.Abstract: To fully exploit the advantages of steel-concrete composite structures and reduce material consumption and self-weight, this study proposes a novel prefabricated hollow-core partially encased composite beam (HPEC)-to-H-section column joint (PHHJ); however, its seismic performance and key detailing effects remain insufficiently understood. Six 1/2-scale specimens were tested under low-cycle reversed loading to evaluate the effects of hollow ratio, stiffener length, and cover plate length on failure mode, hysteretic behavior, energy dissipation, and ductility. Refined ABAQUS models were validated and used for parametric analyses of stiffener position, widened flange, and connection form. The primary failure modes were flexural failure and connection failure. The hysteretic curves exhibited a shuttle shape with good energy dissipation, and the maximum equivalent viscous damping coefficient reached 0.24. Initial stiffness degradation was mainly caused by buckling of the H-section steel beam flange, whereas later degradation was governed by steel yielding and concrete crushing. The maximum ductility coefficient was 1.61. Bearing capacity was relatively insensitive to stiffener length, cover plate length, and hollow ratio, and its degradation mainly depended on damage to reinforced concrete in the filling area. FEM results show that stiffeners relocate the plastic hinge away from the column face, while a widened flange alleviates stress concentration at the interface between the HPEC flange edge and the beam end plate. A connection combining stiffeners and a widened flange is recommended, with stiffener length > 200 mm, widened flange width matching the column flange width, and length ≥ 200 mm. These findings provide a reference for the seismic design and engineering application of HPEC beam-column joints.
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Civil and Structural Engineering > Structural Load-Bearing Analysis; Engineering > Civil and Structural Engineering > Seismic Performance and Analysis; Engineering > Building and Construction > Structural Behavior of Reinforced Concrete

Article.Title: Frequency-dependent electrical characteristic reconstruction with physics-based evaluation for interface-state analysis in CeO₂NPs-doped GQDs device
Article.Authors: Ersöz B.; Berktaş Z.; Orhan T.; Öter A.; Orhan E.; Sağıroğlu Ş.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Frequency-dependent capacitance–voltage ( C–V ) and conductance–voltage ( G–V ) measurements provide important information on charge transport and interface properties in semiconductor devices, but dense frequency sweeps increase experimental measurement requirements. This study systematically evaluates frequency-domain reconstruction strategies for a CeO₂NPs-doped PEI N-GQDs/n-Si heterojunction using physics-based post-reconstruction evaluation. Experimental C–V and G–V data acquired at 17 frequencies and 81 bias-voltage points per frequency (1377 measurement points) were analyzed using classical interpolation, ensemble machine-learning, recurrent deep-learning, and analytical equivalent-circuit approaches. Leave-one-frequency-out validation was complemented by sparse-frequency experiments using reduced subsets of 13, 9, 7, and 5 frequencies from the original 17-frequency dataset, separation of interior interpolation from endpoint extrapolation, and repeated stochastic-model evaluation. Reconstruction accuracy was assessed for C–V and G–V characteristics and physically derived R s , G p /ω , and N ss . Classical interpolation remained highly competitive and frequently outperformed machine-learning methods under reduced frequency sampling. With only five measured frequencies, PCHIP achieved R 2 = 0.9959 for G -V reconstruction, while Linear interpolation and Extra Trees achieved R 2 = 0.9869 and 0.9852, respectively, for C-V reconstruction. Sensitivity analysis further showed that reconstruction errors can be amplified during N ss extraction and that insufficient frequency resolution around the G p /ω peak can degrade physical-parameter recovery. These findings demonstrate that reconstruction performance depends on measurement density, interpolation versus extrapolation conditions, and the subsequently derived physical quantity. Accurate reconstruction of C–V and G–V characteristics therefore does not necessarily guarantee equally accurate recovery of interface-related parameters.
Article.TopicFields: Physics and Astronomy > Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Optics > Semiconductor materials and interfaces; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Semiconductor materials and devices; Engineering > Electrical and Electronic Engineering > Advancements in Semiconductor Devices and Circuit Design

Article.Title: A multicomponent biofeedback-informed programme reduces music performance anxiety in undergraduate music students a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Xie Y.; Ding W.
Article.Abstract: Music performance anxiety (MPA) can affect the physiological, psychological, and behavioral functioning of music students. This randomized controlled trial evaluated a 12-week multicomponent programme integrating physiological monitoring, biofeedback, breathing regulation, virtual-reality exposure, cognitive restructuring, progressive performance practice, and teaching adaptation. A total of 120 undergraduate music students were randomly allocated to an intervention group ( n = 60) or a control group ( n = 60). The prespecified primary analysis used analysis of covariance, with the post-intervention multidimensional total score as the outcome and the corresponding baseline score as a covariate. Adjusted post-intervention means were 69. 82 (SE = 0. 68) in the intervention group and 108. 14 (SE = 0. 68) in the control group; the adjusted between-group difference was − 38. 32 points (95% CI -40. 22 to -36. 42; P < 0. 001). Baseline-adjusted differences also favored the intervention group for the physiological (-17. 71, 95% CI -19. 47 to -15. 95), psychological (-16. 65, 95% CI -17. 92 to -15. 38), and behavioral (-3. 83, 95% CI -4. 40 to -3. 26) dimensions. Exploratory within-group analyses showed progressively higher HRV (SDNN) and lower electromyographic activity and respiratory rate across the three intervention stages (all P < 0. 001). The multicomponent programme was associated with improved outcomes in this sample, but the design cannot isolate the independent effects of biofeedback, virtual reality, additional contact time, or the other programme components. Trial registration : This study was not registered prospectively. It was initiated as an evaluation of a curriculum-embedded educational intervention, and the investigators did not recognize at study commencement that prospective registration is also recommended for non-clinical educational trials. The protocol was approved before recruitment (Approval No. SQYZ-2023-ETH-038; 18 August 2023), and the prespecified outcomes and analysis plan are documented in the approved protocol, which is available from the corresponding author on reasonable request.

Article.Title: Long-term spatio-temporal dynamics of sediment-associated heavy metals in a large river system
Article.Authors: Sidoruk M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Despite the widespread use of geochemical and ecological indices, our understanding of long-term heavy metal dynamics in large river systems is still limited, particularly when it comes to capturing temporal variability and interactions between multiple elements. In this study, we examine patterns of sediment-associated metal contamination and ecological risk in the Vistula River (Poland), using monitoring data collected between 2015 and 2022 from 23 sites distributed along the entire river course. Concentrations of eight metals (As, Cd, Cr, Cu, Hg, Ni, Pb and Zn) were analysed using a set of commonly applied geochemical and ecotoxicological indices, including Igeo, CF, PLI, PERI and the mean probable effect concentration quotient (mPEC-Q). To better capture changes over time, we also propose a Sediment Contamination Trend Index (SCTI) as a complementary metric that integrates proportional, toxicity-weighted changes in multi-metal contamination. The results show clear spatial variability in sediment contamination, with the highest enrichment observed for Zn, Pb, Cd and Cr. While classical indices indicate moderate to considerable contamination and generally moderate ecological risk, the inclusion of SCTI highlights pronounced year-to-year variability, with alternating periods of increasing and decreasing metal concentrations that are not fully reflected by conventional static approaches. Taken together, the results suggest that combining long-term monitoring data with both established indices and a simple trend-based metric can improve the interpretation of sediment contamination dynamics in large river systems. Such an approach may be particularly useful in supporting environmental monitoring and river basin management under changing environmental conditions.

Article.Title: Tapeworm foraging optimization algorithm: a novel approach to metaheuristic optimization of complex problems
Article.Authors: Betrabet P.; Vincent S.; Sahu U.; Niranjan U.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents an empirical investigation of the Tapeworm Foraging Optimization (TFO) algorithm, a nature-inspired metaheuristic search framework motivated by parasitic tapeworm attachment and reproductive segmentation. TFO combines a decaying Gaussian perturbation for exploratory diffusion with an inverted difference-vector displacement toward the current global best for local exploitation, governed by a probabilistic switching parameter. We evaluate TFO on classical unimodal and multimodal benchmarks (F1–F16) and four constrained mechanical engineering design problems: tension/compression spring, welded beam, 10-bar cantilever truss, and speed reducer design. Comparative evaluations against established metaheuristics - Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA), and Aquila Optimizer (AOA) reveal that GWO, WOA, and AOA converge faster and achieve objective values closer to theoretical minima on most benchmark functions, whereas TFO achieves comparable performance on F6 and F14 and competitive convergence on F11, F15, and F16. In constrained engineering optimization, TFO consistently identifies valid feasible configurations satisfying nonlinear stress, deflection, and geometric constraints, although it obtains higher objective costs than comparator methods on the spring (+ 7.14%), welded-beam (+ 8.57%), and 10-bar truss (+ 25.22%) problems, while securing an intermediate 3rd-place ranking on the speed reducer problem. Systematic parameter-sensitivity and ablation analyses across 1,980 independent runs indicate that balanced hybrid switching is essential for avoiding premature constraint entrapment, while the decay schedule exhibits robust stability. TFO’s structural simplicity, absence of velocity vectors or memory matrices, and low per-iteration overhead make it an accessible, transparent baseline for constrained engineering applications where computational simplicity and constraint feasibility are prioritized.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithms Research; Mathematics > Numerical Analysis > Advanced Optimization Algorithms Research; Computer Science > Computational Theory and Mathematics > Advanced Multi-Objective Optimization Algorithms

Article.Title: Validating therapy decisions by reasons for therapy switch in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis
Article.Authors: Sakr A.; Havla J.; Mansmann U.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Models for individualized treatment recommendations in relapsing–remitting multiple sclerosis often select therapies based on predicted risks of relapse and/or 3-month confirmed disability progression (3m-CDP). Recommendations should be interpretable, align with guidelines, and reflect patient perspectives. We validated recently developed prognostic algorithms in eight subgroups defined by reason for therapy switch: intolerance, lack of efficacy, pregnancy desire, serious adverse events, programmed stop, personal convenience, therapy initiation, drug-holiday end. From the OFSEP registry, we analysed 3768 therapy cycles from 3768 patients treated between 2017 and 2021 with interferon beta, glatiramer acetate, teriflunomide, dimethyl fumarate, fingolimod, natalizumab. One therapy cycle was randomly selected per patient. The algorithms produced ranked therapy lists per treatment cycle as switching option; certainty of the provided recommendation was quantified by entropy (0 = clear; 4.78 = maximal uncertainty). Recommendations were more consistent for relapse (median entropy 0.54, IQR 0.39–0.61) than for 3m-CDP (0.95, IQR 0.88–1.01). Across subgroups, natalizumab most often ranked highest for relapse, whereas teriflunomide or interferon beta frequently ranked highest for 3m-CDP. Calibration varied across switcher subgroups and outcomes, while discrimination was comparable to overall set: C-index 0.776 (95% CI 0.753–0.797) for 3m-CDP and 0.638 (95% CI 0.615–0.661) for relapse. Guideline and relapse-based recommendations did not always align, notably in the pregnancy desire subgroup. For 3m-CDP, guideline-based recommendations are scarce, precluding systematic comparison with model outputs. Agreement between the best-ranked therapy for relapse and 3m-CDP was zero (κ = 0), underscoring outcome-dependent divergence. Algorithm-generated recommendations depend on the chosen outcome and may diverge from guideline-based practice or patient perspectives. Transparent communication of uncertainty and outcome trade-offs is essential for shared decision-making.

Article.Title: Agreement between pelvic floor muscle assessment methods in women with stress urinary incontinence: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Demi̇rdöğen E.; Dağli S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Stress urinary incontinence (SUI) is associated with impaired pelvic floor muscle (PFM) function; however, the relationships and agreement among commonly used PFM assessment methods remain unclear. This study investigated the associations between digital vaginal palpation using the Modified Oxford Scale (MOS) and surface electromyography (sEMG) measurements, as well as the agreement between transperineal (TP-sEMG) and intravaginal (IV-sEMG) recordings in women with SUI. In this cross-sectional observational study, 25 women with SUI were recruited between December 25, 2025, and January 25, 2026. PFM function was assessed sequentially using MOS, TP-sEMG, and IV-sEMG. Associations between MOS scores and sEMG parameters were examined using Spearman''s rank correlation coefficient, whereas agreement between TP-sEMG and IV-sEMG was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) and Bland–Altman analysis. Moderate positive correlations were observed between MOS scores and selected sEMG parameters during the 5-s contraction protocol (ρ = 0.414–0.445, p < 0.05), whereas the remaining correlations were not statistically significant. Agreement between TP-sEMG and IV-sEMG was poor across the evaluated parameters (ICC = −0.136 to 0.162). Bland–Altman analysis revealed systematic bias for selected parameters and wide limits of agreement. These findings indicate generally limited associations between MOS scores and sEMG parameters and poor agreement between the two sEMG recording methods under the investigated conditions. However, they do not establish whether the methods assess distinct physiological constructs or provide complementary clinical information. Further studies with larger samples, standardized EMG acquisition and processing procedures, and validated reference methods are warranted to clarify their clinical relevance and potential interchangeability.

Article.Title: Designing a blockchain-enabled certification framework for food loss and waste reduction: a proof-of-concept in the fresh food supply chain
Article.Authors: Sainz N.; Amador M.; Alonso A.
Article.Abstract: Blockchain technology, supported by IoT, has proven essential for improving traceability in food supply chains, but its application to auditing and certifying food loss and waste (FLW) reduction remains largely unexplored. This paper addresses this gap by proposing the architectural design, data models, and audit workflow of a permissioned blockchain-enabled tool developed within the EU H2020 FOODRUS project. Focused on the Spanish fresh vegetable supply chain pilot, the proposed framework integrates Hyperledger Fabric to establish a decentralized and immutable ledger for recording audit evidence and verifying compliance indicators. Rather than assessing long-term operational impact, this study demonstrates the baseline technical feasibility of automating FLW certification workflows through a deployed proof-of-concept prototype. The implementation highlights key architectural contributions, such as standardized data schemas and an integrated 7-stage audit lifecycle, while identifying primary deployment hurdles, notably stakeholder reluctance toward ERP data sharing. The findings confirm that while a permissioned blockchain design effectively secures audit record integrity, broader adoption hinges on establishing legally recognized FLW certification schemes and granular data-governance mechanisms.

Article.Title: Dentists’ acceptance of artificial intelligence-assisted decision support for oral potentially malignant disorder detection: a structural equation modeling study
Article.Authors: Ghalwash D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) may support early detection and clinical decision-making of oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs), but clinical implementation depends on dentists’ acceptance of AI-assisted clinical decision support. This study aimed to identify structural associations of AI acceptance among dentists using an extended Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 500 dentists. Construct validity and reliability were assessed using confirmatory factor analysis. Hypothesized associations were evaluated using structural equation modeling with bootstrap mediation analysis. The extended TAM showed generally satisfactory measurement properties and good overall model fit. Attitude toward AI showed the strongest association with behavioral intention (β = 0.550), followed by AI-assisted clinical decision reliance (β = 0.220), perceived usefulness (β = 0.180), trust (β = 0.140), and perceived ease of use (β = 0.120). Significant indirect effects operated through attitude toward AI. The model explained 67.5% of the variance in behavioral intention. Dentists reported favorable behavioral intention toward AI-assisted decision support for OPMD detection. Attitude toward AI showed the strongest association with behavioral intention. The findings are consistent with the extended TAM. Successful implementation will require explainable systems, clinician education, trust-building, and effective workflow integration. Longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether these associations translate into actual clinical adoption. Understanding factors associated with dentists’ acceptance of AI may support the responsible integration of AI-assisted decision support into oral cancer screening pathways.

Article.Title: Mechanical deterioration and damage evolution of coal specimens under drying–wetting cycles
Article.Authors: Wang B.; Zhou D.; Liang B.; Zhang J.; Lei G.; Ma J.
Article.Abstract: Utilizing underground mine reservoirs for pumped hydroelectric storage (PHS) stations represents a highly promising approach for large-scale energy storage. However, the long-term exposure of coal pillar dams to drying-wetting cycles (DWC) poses a severe risk of structural instability. This study investigated the mechanical degradation and damage mechanisms of coal specimens, leveraging triaxial loading coupled with acoustic emission (AE) and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) monitoring. The results indicated that the compressive strength and cohesion underwent non-uniform, multi-stage degradation with increasing DWC, with the most acute deterioration occurring after the first cycle. AE monitoring revealed that with increasing DWC, the frequency of high-amplitude AE events escalated, and their peaks shifted forward. Concurrently, the overall b -value exhibited a downward trend. RA-AF analysis showed an increasing fraction of shear-related AE signals with increasing DWC. NMR testing revealed predominantly unimodal T 2 spectra dominated by small pores. With increasing DWC, the relative fraction of small pores decreased, whereas those of medium and large pores increased, indicating a shift toward larger pore structures. These findings provide laboratory evidence of DWC-related coal deterioration relevant to further material assessments for underground reservoirs and potential PHS applications.
