Article.Title: Molecular characterization of hepatitis B and hepatitis delta viruses in Mauritanian HBV chronically infected patients
Article.Authors: Abdawa M.; Toyé R.; Abdellahi M.; Hemeyine M.; Elbara A.; Chemin I.; Lunel-Fabiani F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) is highly endemic in Mauritania, and co‑infection with hepatitis delta virus (HDV) may worsen liver outcomes. We characterized circulating hepatitis B virus (HBV) and HDV strains and assessed the clinical impact of HDV co‑infection among HBsAg‑positive patients in Nouakchott. A total of 165 adults with CHB were enrolled at the National Institute of Hepato-Virology. Demographic/clinical data, serological and molecular tests, ultrasound, and fibrosis estimates (APRI, FIB-4) were collected. HBV DNA was quantified by real-time PCR; HDV RNA was measured mainly by RT-ddPCR. HBV and HDV were Sanger-sequenced. HBV DNA was detectable in 146/165 (88.5%) with median 2197.25 IU/mL; 75/165 (45.45%) exceeded 2000 IU/mL. Total anti-HDV antibodies were found in 68/112 (60.7%) tested; HDV RNA was quantified in 130/165 patients and detected in 34/130 (26.15%) with median 72,271 IU/mL, including 34/68 (50%) of anti-HDV–positive patients. HDV-RNA positivity was associated with symptoms, higher AST/ALT/AFP/APRI/FIB-4, lower HBV DNA detectability, and increased cirrhosis/HCC and treatment use ( p ≤ 0.004). HBV genotypes were D (36/65, 55.4%), including 11 isolates (16.9%) assigned to subgenotype D8, a D/E recombinant lineage first described in Niger; E (21/65, 32.3%); and A (8/65, 12.3%). HDV genotyping ( n = 21) showed mainly genotype 1 and two genotype 5 isolates. An rtA181S substitution in the polymerase reverse-transcriptase domain and a naturally occurring altered YMDD motif (rtY203N) were detected. Whole-genome analysis revealed co-circulation of HBV genotypes A (A1/A2), D (D1/D4), E, and recombinant D/E strains, with high conservation across coding regions and absence of widespread antiviral resistance in these Mauritanian patients’ samples. HDV co‑infection is frequent among Mauritanian patients with CHB and is associated with more severe liver injury. HBV genotype D predominates, with presence of inter‑genotype recombinations and HDV genotypes are mainly genotype 1. These findings support routine HDV screening, timely antiviral access, and improved HBV vaccination coverage- including the birth dose- to slow disease incidence and progression in Mauritania.

Article.Title: Identification of ferroptosis-related key genes influencing synovitis development in osteoarthritis based on machine learning
Article.Authors: Zhang Z.; Huang H.; Chen J.; Peng K.; Yang Y.
Article.Abstract: This study aims to explore the potential involvement of ferroptosis-related genes (FRGs) in osteoarthritis (OA) synovitis. Synovial tissue samples from 32 OA patients and 32 normal controls were obtained from the GEO database and analyzed to identify differentially expressed FRGs.Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) identified a gene module significantly associated with OA. To further prioritize candidate genes, three machine learning approaches—Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost)—were applied, among which the SVM model demonstrated the best predictive performance.Through integrated analysis, CARS was identified as a candidate key ferroptosis-related gene associated with OA synovitis. Further immune infiltration analysis revealed a significant positive correlation between CARS expression and follicular helper T cell abundance, suggesting a potential association between ferroptosis-related metabolic regulation and immune microenvironment alterations in OA synovial tissue.In addition, competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) network analysis indicated that CARS may be regulated by multiple non-coding RNAs, implying a complex post-transcriptional regulatory landscape. Experimental validation using qRT-PCR and Western blot analysis supported the bioinformatics prediction that CARS expression is elevated in OA synovial tissues at both mRNA and protein levels.Overall, this study provides a bioinformatics-based framework for identifying ferroptosis-related gene signatures in OA synovitis and suggests that CARS may serve as a potential candidate biomarker associated with ferroptosis and immune regulation in OA. Further functional studies are required to clarify its mechanistic role.

Article.Title: Hybrid deep feature fusion framework with maximum entropy based selection for accurate diabetic foot ulcer diagnosis from enhanced and segmented medical images
Article.Authors: Ali E.; Senan E.; El Hakim N.; Khan M.; Ahmed I.; Al-Omari O.; Fati S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Diabetic foot ulcers (DFU) pose significant risks, including delayed wound healing, infection, and, in severe cases, amputation. Early diagnosis is critical to mitigate these risks and enhance patient outcomes. Manual assessment may be affected by inter-observer variability and workflow delays, which motivates the investigation of AI-assisted methods for DFU image classification. In this study, several hybrid artificial neural network (ANN) strategies were developed incorporating features from various convolutional neural network (CNN) models for diabetic ulcer image diagnosis. The use of feature selection algorithms, specifically principal component analysis (PCA) and maximum entropy score based selection (MESbS), enhanced the discriminatory power of the models. Image quality was improved by using fused filters - average and Laplacian - to enhance the images and highlight the features of the diabetic ulcer and highlight the boundaries of the lesion. The geometric active contour (GAC) algorithm facilitated isolation of damaged areas from healthy areas. AlexNet, MobileNetV2 and VGG16 models processed these regions and extracted deep feature maps. These maps are later combined to create global feature vectors, namely, AlexNet-MobileNetV2, MobileNetV2-VGG16, AlexNet-VGG16, and AlexNet-MobileNetV2-VGG16. The fusion of features from multiple CNN models gives rise to high-dimensional vectors, prompting the application of PCA and MESbS for feature selection. The proposed hybrid strategies demonstrated strong diagnostic performance on the evaluated dataset. Among the evaluated configurations, the AlexNet-MobileNetV2-VGG16-ANN model with MESbS achieved the highest performance, reaching an AUC of 99%, sensitivity of 99.7%, accuracy of 99.5%, precision of 99.5%, and specificity of 99.75%. These findings suggest that combining complementary CNN feature representations with feature selection may improve DFU classification under the evaluated experimental conditions.

Article.Title: GLTF-FEDformer: an adaptive time-frequency fusion method for multivariate time series anomaly detection enhanced by prediction error embedding
Article.Authors: Nie H.; Tong Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multivariate time series are widespread in scenarios such as industrial IoT, smart manufacturing, energy systems, and medical monitoring. Their anomalous behaviors often involve complex patterns like long-range dependency changes, local dynamic shifts, transient spectral perturbations, and variable-association mismatches. Existing reconstruction-based and attention-based methods can learn the overall evolution of normal sequences but still lack fine-grained characterization of local time-frequency changes; moreover, relying solely on point-wise prediction errors for anomaly scoring struggles to fully reflect structural shifts in the error distribution. To address these issues, this paper proposes GLTF-FEDformer, a multivariate time series anomaly detection method that jointly models global and local time-frequency features. The method learns temporal dependencies, trend changes, and periodic candidate patterns from long-window contexts via a global temporal representation module, and enhances the modeling of temporal evolution through a continuous dynamic refinement mechanism. It also builds a lightweight local time-frequency feature extraction module that uses short-time Fourier transform, 2D convolutions, spectral gating, and inverse transforms to enhance the perception of local morphological changes, spectral perturbations, and time-frequency coupled features within local windows. A gated fusion mechanism performs data-dependent integration of global temporal information and local time-frequency information to obtain more discriminative prediction representations. Additionally, we design an anomaly scoring strategy based on a prediction-error-embedded profile, mapping prediction residuals into an embedding space and measuring structural deviations of test prediction-error embeddings from the normal error profile through variable-level standardized distances. The profile score is further combined with point-wise prediction errors to form anomaly responses with temporal localization ability. This strategy not only uses amplitude information of prediction errors but also captures structural shifts of the error distribution relative to normal patterns, thereby improving detection robustness in complex anomaly scenarios. Experimental results show the proposed method effectively enhances multivariate time series anomaly recognition and demonstrates strong detection performance and stability across various public datasets.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: multivariate time series anomaly detection; spectral gating; time-frequency feature fusion; gated fusion; short-time Fourier transform; anomaly scoring

Article.Title: Research on the mechanical properties and freeze resistance of geopolymer concrete
Article.Authors: Xing Z.; Chen H.; Kang Y.; Wang P.; Zhang B.
Article.Abstract: To investigate the mechanical properties and freeze resistance of fiber-reinforced geopolymer concrete, this paper uses kaolin, slag powder, and fly ash as the silicate-aluminate cementitious materials, sodium silicate and sodium hydroxide as the alkaline activators, The alkali activator dosage was adjusted to optimize the performance of different silica-alumina cementitious materials. Polypropylene fibers with lengths of 9 mm and 18 mm were blended as reinforcement to prepare geopolymer concrete. strength tests, rapid freeze-thaw tests, and salt freeze resistance tests were carried out. Combined with pore structure analysis and the establishment of a damage model, key conclusions were drawn. In terms of mechanical properties, fly ash is beneficial for the subsequent strength development of concrete, while slag promotes early strength development. Polypropylene fibers can enhance the flexural and compressive strengths. Among them, the P60F20S20M1.2N12 mix ratio has the best performance, with a 28-day flexural strength of 6.5 MPa and a compressive strength of 45.3 MPa. In terms of freeze resistance, concrete’s resistance decreases as porosity and the proportion of harmful pores increase. The incorporation of fibers can inhibit deterioration of the pore structure, reduce the quality loss and relative dynamic elastic modulus caused by freeze-thaw, and increase the freeze resistance cycles of the four mix ratios by 25 times, 25 times, 25 times, and 50 times, respectively. The anti-salt freeze test shows that deicing salt aggravates freeze-thaw damage, while fibers can effectively resist the temperature stress and permeation pressure induced by salt freeze, thereby improving the anti-salt freeze effect. Based on the Lemaitre effect of strain variation, a freeze-damage equation for P60F20S20M1.2N12 fiber geopolymer concrete was established and can be used for freeze-damage evaluation. This research achievement provides an excellent fiber geopolymer concrete mix ratio scheme and theoretical support for pavement repair in seasonally frozen areas and new construction projects.

Article.Title: Children with special educational needs and family polyvictimization in Hong Kong: a cross-sectional survey of families
Article.Authors: Wu C.; Chen Q.; Chan K.
Article.Abstract: Families raising children with special educational needs (SEN) may experience adversities. However, previous research has focused on individual children, and limited research has examined family polyvictimization (FPV) and SEN correlates from a family-centered perspective. This study analyzed data from a family-based survey conducted in Hong Kong between August 2022 and March 2023, comparing families with and without children with SEN. A total of 1,400 respondents participated (mean age = 39.75 years, SD = 6.99; 75.4% female), each representing one participating family. Of these respondents, 130 reporting children with SEN and 1,270 without. Respondents provided information on sociodemographic characteristics, family violence and FPV experiences, and health outcomes. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with having children with SEN. Lifetime FPV prevalence was higher among families reporting children with SEN than among other families (23.1% vs. 8.2%). After adjustment for sociodemographic, family-context, psychosocial-attitude, and social-support variables, FPV was associated with higher odds of SEN-reporting family status (aOR = 2.630, 95% CI 1.529–4.524). Other adjusted correlates included lower family income, male dominance, violence socialization, lower perceived social support, violence against adult parents, children, and older family members, poorer respondent physical health, and lower child quality of life. These findings underscore the importance of viewing families raising children with SEN as a window for identifying family violence and call for early detection, systematic screening, and family-centered interventions. Future research should examine these associations over time and strengthen family-based support.

Article.Title: Targeting M2 Macrophages Enhances the Efficacy of PD-L1 Blockade in Non-small Cell Lung Cancer
Article.Authors: Ma X.; Bae Y.; Murugan S.; Vadevoo P.; Li H.; Wu M.; Fan X.; Song Y.; Liu Y.; Lee B.; Joo K.
Article.Abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring KRAS G12D mutations and TP53 deficiency is associated with poor clinical outcomes, and effective therapeutic options remain limited. Immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis have made tremendous advances in lung cancer therapy over the last few years. Despite this, only a subset of patients receives durable clinical responses with PD-1/PD-L1 monotherapy. Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), especially M2 macrophages, play a critical role in shaping the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) and in resistance to PD-L1 blockade. In this study, we utilized an interleukin-4 receptor (IL-4R)-binding peptide conjugated to the pro-apoptotic peptide (KLAKLAK)₂ (IL4RPep-1-KLA) to induce apoptosis in IL4R-expressing M2 macrophages. We found that both anti-PD-L1 antibody and IL4RPep-1-KLA monotherapy exhibited antitumor effect in NSCLC-bearing mice. Although co-administration of these two agents did not show a significant survival benefit, the combination markedly enhanced the infiltration of CD8 + T cells and granzyme B + cells within the tumor core, promoted systemic CD8⁺ T cell activation in the periphery and reduced the proportion of M2 macrophages in the TME. Thus, targeting M2 macrophages may provide a novel approach to remodel the immunosuppressive TME and potentially contribute to developing a new therapeutic modality that can address limitations of PD-L1-based therapies.

Article.Title: Development and validation of a risk score to predict mortality in the pediatric intensive care unit using routinely collected data in Northwest Ethiopia: a retrospective study
Article.Authors: Alamirew Y.; Enyew T.; Zeleke M.; Altaye K.; Genet G.; Teshager N.
Article.Abstract: Early prediction of mortality in critically ill patients is essential for informed clinical decision-making, effective risk stratification, and optimal resource allocation. Most existing pediatric-specific mortality prediction models, however, depend on extensive laboratory testing and advanced monitoring and intervention tools, which limit their applicability in resource-limited settings. To develop and internally validate a mortality risk score for pediatric patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU). A retrospective cohort study of 565 pediatric patients in northwest Ethiopia was conducted. Data were extracted from medical records using a structured data abstraction tool developed in Kobo Toolbox V2024.2.S. Descriptive statistics, including mean, median, and standard deviation, were summarized and presented in text and tables. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) was used to select variables for the multivariable logistic regression model. The reduced model’s performance was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, Brier score, and area under the curve (AUC). Decision curve analysis was conducted to assess clinical utility, and results were presented in a nomogram. The observed mortality rate was 27.3% (95% CI: 23.6%, 30.9%). The final risk score incorporated nine predictors: rural residence, cardiac comorbidity, oxygen saturation (SpO2) at admission, temperature at admission, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS), urine output, vasopressor use, lowest hemoglobin, and thrombocytopenia. The model demonstrated an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.86 (95% CI: 0.83, 0.90) and exhibited good calibration. Sensitivity was 85%, specificity was 75%, the negative predictive value was 93.1%, and the positive likelihood ratio was 3.4. Decision curve analysis indicated a greater net benefit compared to the “treat-all” or “treat-none” strategies. A mortality risk score model for the pediatric intensive care unit was developed using readily available clinical profiles. The model demonstrated strong discrimination, calibration, sensitivity, and specificity, supporting its utility for predicting mortality in critically ill children. Following external validation, the model could be implemented in clinical practice and quality improvement programs.

Article.Title: A Markov transition analysis to study changes in HIV prevention strategies among men who have sex with men in the French ANRS-PREVENIR cohort
Article.Authors: Boutet C.; Hoyer M.; Van Huizen R.; Sow A.; Mora M.; Beniguel L.; Ghosn J.; Assoumou L.; Protière C.; Michels D.; Costagliola D.; Spire B.; Di Ciaccio M.; Molina J.; Sagaon-Teyssier L.
Article.Abstract: Despite various biomedical and behavioral prevention strategies, new HIV seroconversions are disproportionately higher among gay and bisexual men who have sex with men (GBMSM). Using data from the French PrEP cohort ANRS-PREVENIR, this study aimed to investigate prevention strategies among this population and to analyze factors that may shape GBMSMs’ sexual behaviors. We defined three protection states as follows: self-dependent protection (SDP), which covered condom and/or PrEP use, partner-dependent protection (PDP), whereby the partner self-declared being either seronegative or seropositive with an undetectable viral load, and no protection (NP). We constructed a composite variable reflecting the degree of concordance between actual and perceived risk. A continuous-time multi-state Markov model was used to determine transition probabilities between protection states over time. Hazard ratios and their 95% confidence intervals (HR(95%CI)) were computed to identify factors associated with transitions. Irrespective of the protection state at baseline (i.e., SDP, PDP, NP), the highest Markov transition probabilities were to transition from one state to the same state at the next follow-up visit over the entire study period; specifically, the probability [95%CI] was 0.920 [0.916,0.924] for SDP, 0.783 [0.769,0.797] for PDP, and 0.584 [0.546,0.615] for NP. Event-driven PrEP (3.34(2.89–3.85)) and PrEP naivety (1.19(1.04–1.36)) were associated with an increased probability of transitioning from SDP to PDP. PrEP naivety (1.44(1.23–1.69)) and event-driven PrEP (4.15(3.47–4.96)) were also associated with an increased probability of transitioning from SDP to NP. A higher actual/perceived risk concordance score, i.e., higher actual risk and either a greater level of discordance or not considering risk, was associated with a reduced probability to transition from SDP to PDP (0.96 (0.92–0.99)), and was not associated with the transition from SDP to NP. Most GBMSM in our study transitioned from one state of protection to the same state at the next follow-up visit over the entire study period, highlighting the need for close counselling when GBMSM adopt a protection strategy for the first time, as it will shape their future strategies. Our findings also suggest that PrEP-naive and event-driven PrEP users have an increased probability of transitioning to protection strategies that are not self-controlled, raising questions about their vulnerability to HIV acquisition.

Article.Title: High-temperature affects morphological, physiological, and biochemical traits in day-neutral strawberries
Article.Authors: Demirsoy L.; Cengiz M.; Ullah I.; Demirsoy H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract High-temperatures significantly constrain the growth and resilience of day-neutral strawberry ( Fragaria × ananassa ) varieties, affecting their morphological, physiological, and biochemical characteristics. In this study, frigo plants of six day-neutral strawberry cultivars (Albion, Monterey, Portola, Redlands Hope, San Andreas, and Sweet Ann) were initially grown for 5 weeks in 15 cm diameter plastic pots (3:1:1; garden soil, peat, perlite) under open conditions. After 2–3 weeks of acclimatization at 23/15 °C (day/night) in a climate chamber, the temperature in one chamber was maintained at 23/15 °C, while the other was subjected to high-temperature conditions at 30/25 °C. Temperature and cultivars significantly influenced most of the morphological, physiological, and biochemical characteristics of strawberries. High- temperature caused a significant decrease in root length, number of leaves, leaf area, leaf fresh and dry weight, root fresh and dry weight, plant fresh and dry weight, and membrane stability index, while increasing leaf surface temperature, Malondialdehyde content, starch content, sugar content, and total carbohydrate content of strawberry plants, indicating enhanced oxidative stress and metabolic reprogramming. Among varieties, the highest values of the number of leaves, leaf area, leaf fresh and dry weight, root fresh weight, and plant fresh and dry weight were recorded in the San Andreas variety. The Portola variety exhibited considerably higher values of root length and root dry weight. The leaf surface temperature was higher in Monterey, and the membrane stability index was higher in San Andreas. The highest values of MDA and sugar content were observed in the Albion strawberry variety, and the highest values of starch and total carbohydrate content were observed in Monterey. The findings highlight the detrimental effects of high-temperatures on day-neutral strawberry varieties and emphasize the importance of selecting heat-tolerant cultivars for sustainable strawberry production under changing climatic conditions.

Article.Title: Maternal and neonatal outcomes after French Ambulatory Cesarean Section (FAUCS): a prospective study
Article.Authors: Wolder D.; Błażuk-Fortak A.; Kwas-Sarnacka K.; Velemir L.; Michalska A.; Gładyś-Jakubczyk A.; Świercz G.; Hendler I.; Fauck D.; Ami O.
Article.Abstract: French Ambulatory Cesarean Section (FAUCS) has been proposed as a less invasive alternative to conventional cesarean section (CS), with the potential to enhance postoperative recovery. Evidence directly comparing maternal and neonatal outcomes between these techniques remains limited. This single-center observational cohort included 200 women (100 FAUCS and 100 conventional cesarean section [CS]). Five primary and seven secondary outcomes were analyzed, with Holm correction applied separately within each family. Unadjusted comparisons used available observations; archived multivariable and propensity-score analyses were treated as exploratory sensitivity analyses. FAUCS was associated with earlier first full meal (mean difference − 7.01 h, 95% CI − 7.54 to − 6.49), earlier mobilization (− 2.11 h, 95% CI − 3.31 to − 0.91), and lower WHO step-2-or-higher analgesic use (49% vs. 69%; OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.24–0.77); all remained significant within the primary family. Hospital stay was longer (+ 0.87 days, 95% CI 0.26–1.48; Holm p < 0.001). Among women with a recorded breastfeeding time, the mean difference was − 4.58 h (95% CI − 5.14 to − 4.02); this conditional comparison does not establish an effect on breastfeeding initiation in the full cohort. Mobilization and analgesic findings were not consistently supported across adjusted analyses. Blood loss and time to fetal extraction were lower and surgery duration longer (secondary Holm p < 0.001 for each). No neonatal endpoint was significant after correction: cord pH and Apgar < 10 each had Holm p = 0.129, pH < 7.20 p = 0.995, and recorded neonatal trauma/complication p = 1.000. FAUCS was associated with earlier postoperative recovery despite longer operative time, while neonatal outcomes were generally comparable between groups in this prospective observational cohort. These findings suggest that FAUCS may represent a promising alternative surgical approach in selected patients; however, confirmation in larger multicenter randomized studies is required before definitive conclusions regarding safety and effectiveness can be drawn.

Article.Title: Single-domain antibody-conjugated lipid nanoparticles for selective mRNA delivery to CD4⁺ T cells and Brec1-mediated excision of HIV-1 proviral DNA
Article.Authors: Wittner M.; Hartjen P.; Keil O.; Fehring V.; Gkionis L.; Dunne C.; Kaiser P.; Rothbauer U.; Hauber J.; Chemnitz J.; Beschorner N.; Schulze zur Wiesch J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Approaches to curing HIV infection aim to eliminate the latent viral reservoir — long-lived, resting CD4⁺ T cells harboring integrated but transcriptionally silent proviral DNA — which persists despite effective antiretroviral therapy. The HIV-1 LTR-specific designer-recombinase Brec1 can precisely excise integrated proviral DNA from infected cells. However, targeted delivery of therapeutic payloads to HIV reservoir-bearing CD4⁺ T cells remains a major challenge. Here, we present a proof-of-concept study of a modular platform combining CD4-specific single-domain antibody (sdAb)-conjugated lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) with Brec1 mRNA for targeted delivery to CD4⁺ T cells. In primary human PBMCs, sdAb-LNPs achieved 44% transfection efficiency in CD4⁺ T cells with pronounced specificity over CD8⁺ T cells (4:1 ratio) and B cells (9:1 ratio), without compromising cell viability. Brec1 recombinase activity was validated across three reporter cell systems of increasing complexity, confirming efficient translation of delivered Brec1 mRNA into a functional recombinase capable of precise, error-free loxBTR-mediated proviral excision. These findings provide proof of concept for sdAb-LNP-mediated Brec1 mRNA delivery as a candidate strategy for HIV reservoir reduction, with the modular platform design enabling flexible adaptation to other cell-specific therapeutic applications.

Article.Title: Co-retained intron retention on single RNA molecules marks fitness-critical genes
Article.Authors: Mathieu E.; Ritchie W.
Article.Abstract: Using published nanopore direct RNA sequencing from the SG-NEx consortium across six cancer cell lines, we characterize co-retention: the simultaneous retention of adjacent introns on individual transcript molecules. Where it occurs, co-retention is close to absolute (median phi 0.79). This mechanism is distinct from individual retention caused by weak splice sites. Co-retained introns have adequate splice sites, are enriched for TIA1 and U2AF2 binding, and are separated by short exons. Co-retained genes are enriched for fitness-critical components of the translation and splicing machinery.

Article.Title: An interpretable deep learning method for early hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis on multiphase CT
Article.Authors: Sarfati E.; Bône A.; Gori P.; Yang S.; Rohé M.; Nicolas F.; Lee J.; Yoon J.; Ronot M.; Bloch I.; Aubé C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Early diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma is critical to preserve access to curative treatment options. The Liver Imaging Reporting and Data System (LI-RADS) provides a standardized framework for non-invasive diagnosis on multiphase computed tomography, based on major visual imaging features. However, these features may be difficult to assess consistently, particularly in small liver lesions. We developed dLI-RADS, an interpretable artificial intelligence method designed to estimate the probability of hepatocellular carcinoma from multiphase computed tomography images of manually segmented liver lesions, while remaining aligned with LI-RADS-related imaging concepts. dLI-RADS combines neural network-derived predictions with handcrafted quantitative imaging measurements reflecting LI-RADS major features and integrates these inputs using logistic regression. In this multicenter retrospective study, patients with multiphase computed tomography and at least one liver lesion were included, while lesions larger than 40 mm were excluded. Histology served as the reference standard for hepatocellular carcinoma, and a composite reference standard was used for non-hepatocellular carcinoma lesions. The lesion-level accuracy of dLI-RADS and LI-RADS were compared on the internal evaluation set using 10,000-repetition bootstrap non-inferiority tests, with 5% margins and significance levels. On the external test set, sensitivities were similarly compared. A total of 143 (61 years ± 9, 125 men), 62 (61y ± 10, 49 men), and 133 (59y ± 10, 103 men) patients with 196, 84, and 171 lesions (mean diameter 17.7, 18.3, and 21.8 millimeters) were respectively included in the training, internal and external evaluation sets. dLI-RADS was non-inferior to LI-RADS for lesion-level accuracy in the internal evaluation set, achieving 80% accuracy compared with 74% for LI-RADS ( p = 0.04). On the external evaluation set, dLI-RADS achieved a sensitivity of 93% compared with 78% for LI-RADS (non-inferiority p < 0.001). On this same set, dLI-RADS also achieved 74% specificity, 86% accuracy, and an AUC of 84%. Because LI-RADS features were unavailable for non-HCC lesions, only sensitivity could be directly compared between dLI-RADS and LI-RADS. These findings suggest that dLI-RADS may provide interpretable decision support for hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis on multiphase computed tomography, particularly for small liver lesions.

Article.Title: Improving edible oil quality by low- and high-temperature selective adsorption on the example of walnut oil (Juglans regia L.)
Article.Authors: Czwartkowski K.; Nizio E.; Marcinkowski D.; Kmiecik D.; Grygier A.; Siger A.; Golimowski W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the effects of adsorbent type, dosage, and temperature on walnut oil quality and selected bioactive compounds. Adsorption efficiency depended on the combination of processing conditions, with statistically significant effects observed for individual factors and their interactions. Differences among adsorbents may be related to their composition and surface properties, which were not directly characterised in this study. The relative effects of temperature and adsorbent dosage varied depending on the adsorbent and parameter analysed. Treatment at a relatively low temperature (approximately 30 °C), combined with an appropriate adsorbent dosage, may help improve selected quality characteristics while retaining valuable bioactive compounds. However, carotenoid and tocopherol retention varied among adsorbents, and no single treatment condition was optimal for all parameters. Overall, walnut oil adsorption requires joint consideration of adsorbent type, dosage, and temperature. Further research should characterise adsorbent surface properties and evaluate the oxidative stability of treated oil to clarify the mechanisms underlying the observed changes and their implications for oil quality.

Article.Title: Camellia japonica callus–derived extracellular vesicles attenuate αCGRP-induced endothelial hyperactivation via cAMP-dependent signaling
Article.Authors: Roh K.; Park E.; Yu K.; Wang H.; Cho E.; Park D.; Jung E.
Article.Abstract: Menopausal vasomotor symptoms (VMS), such as hot flushes, are associated with neurovascular instability initiated by estrogen deficiency and characterized by excessive peripheral vasodilation. Calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), a potent vasodilatory neuropeptide, plays a pivotal role by activating adenylyl cyclase-cAMP signaling in endothelial cells, thereby stimulating nitric oxide (NO) production and angiogenic activity. This study investigated whether Camellia japonica callus–derived extracellular vesicles (CJEV) can modulate αCGRP-induced endothelial activation relevant to the vascular component of VMS. In human microvascular endothelial cells (HMEC-1), αCGRP markedly increased proliferation, cAMP accumulation, NO synthesis, and angiogenic behaviors through activation of the AKT-mTOR and CREB pathways. CJEV treatment significantly attenuated these responses without cytotoxicity, reducing cAMP accumulation, eNOS phosphorylation, and CREB-dependent gene expression, including VEGFA , BCL2 , and MMP9 . Functionally, CJEV reduced endothelial migration and tube formation, indicating attenuation of αCGRP-driven angiogenic responses. Collectively, these findings identify CJEV as a modulator of αCGRP-responsive endothelial signaling and provide a mechanistic basis for further investigating plant-derived extracellular vesicles as regulators of αCGRP-associated vascular signaling relevant to vasomotor physiology.

Among the conditions investigated, an inlet air temperature of 160 °C with 20% maltodextrin was associated with overall desirable powder characteristics under the fixed experimental conditions employed.

Article.Authors: Zhao X.; Qu H.; Neo C.; Sahrani S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Self-occlusion and external occlusion significantly affect the accuracy of monocular 3D dense face alignment (3DDFA). Although the 3D Morphable Model (3DMM) provides a simple and effective facial prior, existing 3DMM-based methods still suffer from limited robustness caused by the scarcity of facial occlusion data. In this work, we present M4Net ( M ulti-scale features, M ulti-head outputs, M ask Augmented, and based on 3D M orphable Model), a 3DDFA framework that integrates multi-scale feature extractors, multi-head prediction, and a mask augmentation strategy. The proposed framework improves robustness under occluded conditions without increasing training cost. Moreover, by learning decoupled semantic tokens, M4Net disentangles the pose, shape, and expression of the head region. This decoupled representation not only facilitates occlusion-robust alignment but also enables flexible 3D expression, pose, shape, and texture transfer across different subjects without any extra training. Quantitative evaluations show that our approach achieves comparable accuracy on AFLW2000-3D (68 pts) and AFLW (21 pts), and improves the MAEV by up to 0.88% on AFLW2000-3D for head pose estimation. Qualitative results on five different datasets demonstrate the generalization and robustness of M4Net. In particular, facial expression transfer is a major highlight of this work.

Article.Title: Serological and molecular evidence of an endemic presence of mpox and associated risk factors in semi-rural areas of southern Cameroon
Article.Authors: Lamare N.; Godwe C.; Thaurignac G.; Ouedraogo S.; Edoul G.; Kengne M.; Koudoum P.; Djuiessie H.; Tonfack L.; Atemkeng T.; Mba Djondzo F.; Elemva A.; Tidan H.; Ngueyo J.; Kinganda Lusamaki E.; Vidal N.; Delaporte E.; Peeters M.; Kouanfack C.; Ayouba A.
Article.Abstract: The mpox epidemic in Africa is maintained by zoonotic spill-over events and sustained human-to-human transmissions. In serology, 2 of the 5 samples of the household (index case and his 13-year-old son) were mpox antibody positive. This pilot work suggests endemic circulation of mpox in the studied semi-rural districts of southern Cameroon.

Article.Authors: Abdelhadi R.; Ahmed K.; Motawea M.; Younes A.; Mostafa Ahmed Hassan shanab M.
Article.Abstract: A magnetically recoverable binderless N-doped carbon/Fe 3 O 4 /nZVI composite was prepared from technical lignin through activation, nitrogen treatment, binderless granulation, Fe 3 O 4 deposition, and nZVI immobilization for heavy-metal adsorption and H 2 O 2 -assisted phenol removal. The Freundlich model provided a better empirical description of the available Pb(II) and Cd(II) adsorption data than the Langmuir model. Phenol removal reached approximately 75% without added H 2 O 2 and 98% with H 2 O 2 after 120 min, while aqueous-phase total organic carbon removal was approximately 77% in the composite/H 2 O 2 system. These results are consistent with an additional oxidant-assisted contribution, although the degradation pathway and extent of mineralization were not established. Pb(II) removal remained above 91% after five adsorption–desorption cycles. In battery and electroplating wastewaters, Pb(II), phenol, and TOC removal ranged from 90.3–92.5%, 93.8–95.0%, and 70.1–72.0%, respectively. Fixed-bed experiments also demonstrated Pb(II) removal under continuous-flow conditions. The findings support the composite’s potential for combined pollutant treatment, while its individual component contributions, catalytic synergy, and long-term stability require further validation.

Article.Authors: van den Berg J.; Marquering H.; Marquand A.; Reneman L.; Ruhé H.; Caan M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The turbulence dynamics (TD) framework has proven to be informative of whole-brain network synchronicity and rigidity, and is related to neuropsychiatric disorders and antidepressant response prediction. However, studies conducted so far have used small samples and have not accounted for individual differences in demographic and other confounding variables. We aimed to investigate whether demographics were associated with TD read-outs and -if so- built a Normative Model (NM) to account for such demographic variability. We analysed resting-state fMRI data from the UK Biobank ( N = 11,184) and extracted TD features. We analysed associations between TD and age, sex and head motion during scanning across 11 spatial scales (λ:0.01–0.31). We then evaluated the benefit of correcting for these covariates using Normative Modeling (NM) by its association with recent depressive symptoms using the RDS-4 questionnaire. Age, sex and motion during scanning were statistically significantly associated with all TD features, though with generally small effect sizes (η_p 2 < 0.01). Increased network rigidity was seen in older age. While NM-correction did not increase predictive power for depressive symptoms—likely due to a weak phenotype—it successfully shifted the most predictive spatial scale of Amplitude Turbulence to an intermediate scale (λ = 0.16), aligning with established literature. TD features show small but consistent, statistically significant associations with demographics and motion, warranting correction. After applying NM-correction, no improvement in overall depression prediction occurred. However, the most predictive scale of Amplitude Turbulence shifted by applying NM, aligning with previous findings on TD for health and disease. The proposed NM value lies in recovering a more disease-specific, literature-consistent signal, rather than in improving prediction.

Article.Authors: Ahmadi S.; Fridriksson J.; den Ouden D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Language impairments in aphasia are characterized by various representational disruptions that may be reflected in discourse production. This research examines the capacity of transformer-based language models, particularly GPT-2, to serve as a computational framework for analyzing variations in aphasic narrative speech. Pairwise Tukey HSD tests revealed consistent distinctions between Broca’s aphasia and both Anomic and Wernicke’s aphasia, suggesting a shared activation profile between the latter two. Longitudinal tests revealed significant changes over time, especially in the final three layers (10–12). These findings suggest that transformer-based activation patterns reflect meaningful variation in aphasic discourse and may align with clinical observations. Overall, GPT-2 provides a scalable tool to model representational dynamics in aphasia and may offer exploratory insights into language representation in aphasic discourse.

FAP knockdown represses VSMC migration in vitro and attenuates neointimal hyperplasia in vivo. RNA-sequencing implicates FAP in modulating the Net1–RhoA–ROCK axis, further validated by western blot. Collectively, FAP upregulation promotes VSMC migration to foster neointimal hyperplasia and restenosis, marking FAP as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for PAD-associated restenosis.

Article.Authors: Zhang Q.; Yu B.; Liu X.; Wang E.; Li W.; Zhu D.; Chen B.; Chao Y.; Ku X.

The 100:10:10 mixture achieved the minimum overall deviation of 7.85%, with measured-to-target ratios of 0.98, 1.00, 0.95, 1.17, and 1.01, respectively. The damage model reproduced the post-compaction response, peak transition, and post-peak softening, with R 2 values of 0.951–0.994 and normalized root-mean-square errors of 2.39%-6.54%. The framework advances rock-like material design from single-property matching to coordinated reconstruction of multidimensional mechanical response and progressive failure.

Article.Authors: Nayak S.; Nandi S.; McKenna F.; Henry S.; Duong T.
Article.Abstract: Long-term survivors of childhood cancer may experience neurocognitive late effects, yet how they engage neural systems during cognitive tasks remains poorly characterized. Whole-brain group comparisons were conducted for each condition, and group-by-condition interactions on reaction time and accuracy were examined. We also examined exploratory associations between this contrast and cognitive performance. Relative to controls, survivors showed longer reaction times in both conditions and lower NIH Toolbox Flanker scores, with comparable accuracy. Survivors showed reduced activation in the bilateral inferior frontal gyri, the supplementary motor area, and the bilateral caudate, and increased activation in the right inferior temporal and cerebellar regions. The incongruent > congruent contrast was associated with greater activation in the orbitofrontal cortex, inferior temporal gyri, and fusiform gyrus. The findings are hypothesis-generating and require replication in larger, treatment-informed, longitudinal studies before clinical inferences can be drawn.

Article.Title: A robust Pythagorean fuzzy OPARA decision making approach for evaluating hybrid machine translation in language education
Article.Authors: Wei Y.
Article.Abstract: The application of hybrid machine translation systems has become more and more crucial in language education in order to assist multilingual communication, language learning, and delivery of educational content. However, finding the most suitable hybrid machine translation system is a complex multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) problem, because there are many conflicting evaluation criteria and uncertainty in expert evaluations. Current MCDM methods are generally based on normalization procedures, which may alter the original information of the decision and make the ranking less reliable. To overcome these drawbacks, this research proposes a Pythagorean fuzzy objective pairwise-adjusted ratio analysis (PyF-OPARA) MCDM method for evaluating hybrid machine translation systems in language education. The proposed approach combines Pythagorean fuzzy sets (PyFS) and the OPARA methodology to handle uncertain expert judgments while preserving the original properties of the evaluation data via a normalization-free pairwise-adjusted-ratio mechanism. Three typical machine translation systems are considered as a case study and evaluated with three evaluation criteria. Computational results demonstrate the feasibility and usefulness of the proposed approach for obtaining a consistent ranking of competing alternatives, with the Hybrid Neural Translator being the most appropriate system. In addition, sensitivity analysis results show the stability of the proposed approach in rankings across various parameter values, and comparisons with existing MCDM approaches indicate that the proposed approach exhibits greater ability to handle uncertainty, preserve information, and achieve stable rankings. The PyF-OPARA framework is an effective decision-support tool for evaluating educational technology and can be applied to other complex decisions with uncertain information, which could be expanded.

Article.Authors: Mikolaskova I.; Zvarik M.; Gidron Y.; Durmanova V.; Jansakova K.; Kollarik B.; Bucova M.; Hunakova L.
Article.Abstract: Chronic stress and inflammation are potential contributors to tumor progression, yet their interplay with autonomic regulation remains under-explored in bladder cancer (BC). Conversely, higher values of DFA-α2 (per 0.1-unit increase: HR = 0.653, 95% CI 0.476–0.897, p = 0.005) and the SNS index (per 1-unit increase: HR = 0.709, 95% CI 0.535–0.941, p = 0.012) were associated with a lower hazard of recurrence (longer DFS). HRV moderated the association between cortisol and DFS: increasing cortisol levels were linked to a significantly higher recurrence hazard primarily in patients with high DFA-α2 ( p = 0.022) or low TINN ( p = 0.025). Exploratory indirect association analyses suggested that psychological stress and health satisfaction are linked to DFS through these autonomic parameters. These findings identify preliminary associations that position HRV parameters as potential candidate biomarkers for recurrence hazard in BC, although their clinical utility remains to be established in larger, independent validation studies.

Article.Title: The association between preceding birth interval and childhood stunting in Benin
Article.Authors: Agossou M.; Scarpa G.; Beňová L.; Boyi Hounsou C.; Sagastume D.; Agballa G.; Dossou J.; Wong K.
Article.Abstract: Stunting affects approximately 32% of children under five years in Benin. While birth intervals shorter than 33 months are a recognized risk factor for childhood malnutrition, the birth interval associated with the lowest odds of stunting in the Beninese context is still unclear. This study examined the association between preceding birth interval (PBI) and stunting among children aged 6–59 months in Benin. This study is a secondary analysis of nationally representative data from the cross-sectional 2017-18 Benin Demographic and Health Survey. We included 10,153 children aged 6–59 months. Stunting was defined as height-for-age z-score below 2 standard deviations from World Health Organization standards. Preceding birth interval (PBI), the interval between the index birth and the preceding live birth, was categorized into six groups: <24, 24–32, 33–44, 45–56 and > 56 months, and a separate category for first-born children with no preceding birth interval. Survey-adjusted multivariable logistic regression was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aOR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for the association between PBI and stunting, controlling for child, maternal, and household-level covariates. PBI categories were also compared directly with one another. Potential effect modification by child age group (6–23 vs. 24–59 months) was assessed with a design-based Wald test of the interaction terms. Compared with children born after an interval of < 24 months, those born after 45–56 months (aOR: 0.61; 95% CI: 0.49–0.74) and > 56 months (aOR: 0.63; 95% CI: 0.51–0.77) had significantly lower odds of stunting (both p < 0.001). Intervals of 24–32 months and 33–44 months were not significantly associated with stunting, nor was first-born status. Compared directly with one another, adjusted odds were similar for 33–44 vs. 24–32 months (OR: 1.03; 95% CI: 0.91–1.17) and for > 56 vs. 45–56 months (OR: 1.04; 95% CI: 0.83–1.31), whereas 45–56 months differed from 33 to 44 months (OR: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.55–0.79). No evidence of effect modification by child age group was found (design-based Wald test p = 0.363), and stratified analyses by age group are reported as exploratory. Longer preceding birth intervals, particularly of 45 months or more, were associated with lower odds of stunting. This cross-sectional analysis of a single child outcome supports further investigation into whether longer intervals may provide additional nutritional benefits. Alongside this, nutritional support for pregnant and breastfeeding women, including adequate dietary supplementation and counselling, may further contribute to improved child growth outcomes.

Article.Title: Spatial multicellular coordination networks are associated with neoadjuvant immunotherapy response in hepatocellular carcinoma
Article.Authors: Mittal P.; Chauhan J.; Philip D.; Singh P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The response to immune checkpoint blockade in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains highly variable, and the abundance of immune cells alone has been shown to be insufficient as a predictive biomarker. We analyse spatial transcriptomics data from seven neoadjuvant cabozantinib- and nivolumab-treated HCC patients to test whether the therapeutic outcome is associated with spatial coordination of multicellular programs rather than their presence. Modeling immune, stromal, and malignant transcriptional programs as continuous spatial fields, we introduce a graph-based framework that quantifies their organization using field energy and inter-program gradient coupling. Across tumors, immune exhaustion and cytotoxic programs display a comparable spatial structure irrespective of response, indicating that immune presence is not discriminatory. In contrast, responding tumors exhibit structured cancer-associated fibroblast organization and permissive malignant-stromal interfaces, whereas non-responders show pronounced malignant-CAF segregation and immune exclusion. Integrating three biologically motivated coupling terms, we define a Spatial Immune Coordination Index (SICI) that shows directionally consistent separation of response states across 21 of 27 coefficient parameterisations under sign-flip sensitivity testing, independent of immune abundance. Malignant–CAF coupling is the primary discriminating metric (Cohen’s $$d=2.40$$ , Cliff’s $$\delta =+1.00$$ , $$p_{\textrm{exact}}=0.029$$ , $$n=7$$ ). In an exploratory bulk RNA-seq analysis in TCGA-LIHC ( $$n = 533$$ ), coordination-informed composite scores show statistically significant but modest associations with overall survival. These hypothesis-generating findings suggest that spatial coordination topology is associated with the immunotherapy response in HCC and provide a principled graph-based framework for developing and evaluating future spatial biomarkers.

Article.Title: Mouse suppressyn-like 1 suppresses membrane fusion through envelope glycoprotein recognition
Article.Authors: Sugimoto J.; Schust D.; Nakagawa S.; Hiyoshi M.; Saito M.; Sugimoto M.; Nagamatsu T.; Takahashi H.; Sotomaru Y.; Jinno Y.; Kudo Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cell-cell fusion is essential for placental development and is mediated by endogenous retrovirus (ERV)-derived fusogens known as syncytins. However, how ERV-derived proteins negatively regulate membrane fusion remains largely unknown. Here, we identify a previously uncharacterized murine ERV envelope-derived protein, mouse suppressyn-like 1 (mSUPYNL1), that suppresses syncytin-mediated membrane fusion through a mechanism distinct from that of placental human suppressyn (hSUPYN). Unlike hSUPYN, which acts through receptor interference, mSUPYNL1 inhibits both murine and human syncytin-mediated fusion independently of receptor usage by associating with the surface (SU) subunits of multiple syncytin envelope glycoproteins, revealing a receptor-independent mechanism of fusion suppression. This mechanism extends beyond endogenous fusogens. mSUPYNL1 also associates with the SU glycoprotein (gp46) of Human T-cell Leukemia Virus type 1 (HTLV-1) and suppresses Env-dependent syncytium formation, whereas hSUPYN showed no detectable antiviral activity in this assay. These findings identify mSUPYNL1 as a broad-spectrum inhibitor of envelope glycoprotein-mediated membrane fusion. Analysis of mSUPYNL1 knockout mice revealed that, in contrast to the placenta-restricted expression of hSUPYN, mSUPYNL1 was broadly expressed, with its most prominent localization in decidual stromal and vascular endothelial cells of the pregnant uterus, as well as in hematopoietic tissues such as the spleen and thymus. Together, our findings uncover an evolutionarily distinct class of ERV-derived fusion suppressors that function through envelope glycoprotein recognition instead of receptor interference. Our study expands current models of ERV domestication by demonstrating that retroviral envelope proteins have been independently co-opted not only to promote membrane fusion but also to restrain it, thereby linking placental biology, antiviral defense, and host evolution.

Article.Title: Radiocarbon reveals depleted carbon in attached benthic assemblages of persistent pools in a tropical non-perennial river
Article.Authors: Tayer T.; Beesley L.; Meredith K.; Douglas M.; McFarlane D.; Rasmussen T.; Bourke S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Radiocarbon-depleted ("old") carbon can be bioavailable in aquatic ecosystems, but its role in persistent-pool food webs of non-perennial rivers is largely unknown. We measured hydrochemistry, environmental tracers and carbon isotopes in water and biota from four main-channel pools and one floodplain spring along the Martuwarra Fitzroy River, Western Australia, over two dry seasons. Dissolved inorganic (DIC) and organic (DOC) carbon remained near modern in all pools (97.6–103 and 95.1–101.0 percent Modern Carbon, pMC, respectively), yet attached benthic assemblages (periphyton and biofilm) were substantially more depleted, with periphyton as low as 57.1 pMC (~ 4,500 apparent radiocarbon years). Depletion did not track groundwater connectivity: the most depleted periphyton occurred where groundwater indicators were weakest. This biota–water mismatch suggests localised old-carbon sources of unresolved origin. Plausible sources include groundwater-derived DIC/DOC at connected sites, respired aged sedimentary organic carbon, methane-derived and rock-derived (carbonate or petrogenic) carbon. Pool consumers were near modern (~ 97.5–100.5 pMC). At the floodplain spring, strongly depleted DIC (30.4 pMC) co-occurred with depleted charophytes, aquatic insects and fish, although all biota were more modern than DIC. DIC and DOC radiocarbon may therefore fail to represent the 14 C composition of carbon incorporated into aquatic biomass, in either direction.

Article.Title: Head stabilization patterns reflect long-term postural stability alterations during gait associated with history of concussion
Article.Authors: Reilly N.; Prebor J.; Moxey J.; Schussler E.
Article.Abstract: Clinical gait testing following concussion is graded on overall performance rather than the neurological mechanisms contributing to postural control, including those designed to maintain stabilization of the head during movement. The objective of this study was to examine the influences of concussion history on the ability to stabilize the head during gait beyond clinical recovery. Sixteen healthy adults with a history of diagnosed concussion(s) and sixteen controls reporting no history of concussion were recruited for participation. Spatiotemporal metrics and triaxial accelerations at the levels of the head, neck, and lower trunk were collected during preferred and tandem gait across a six-meter path. Attenuation values between the trunk, neck, and head were calculated to assess the ability to reduce the magnitude of acceleration patterns as they ascended the spinal column during gait. Those with a history of concussion displayed greater mediolateral head accelerations compared to controls during both preferred and tandem gait despite no significant differences in spatiotemporal metrics. Individuals with concussion history also demonstrated decreased attenuation between the neck and head, suggesting an altered ability to mitigate ascending oscillations from the trunk. The overall results of this study indicate that concussion can negatively influence postural control during gait beyond the point of symptom cessation as determined by current clinical practices. The ability to stabilize the head during gait may be a valuable metric when assessing sensorimotor integration beyond the acute phase of onset concussion.

Article.Title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and future scenario simulation of farmland carbon sources and sinks patterns in the Guanzhong region, China
Article.Authors: Jiao W.; Zhang F.; Feng Q.; Wei Y.; Song Z.; Li G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Farmland ecosystems play a vital role in regional carbon cycling and are strongly influenced by climate variability and agricultural management.The Guanzhong region, a major agricultural area in northwestern China, is characterized by an intensive winter wheat–summer maize rotation and widespread irrigation.A refined assessment of cropland net ecosystem productivity(NEP) and its driving factors is therefore important for understanding the spatial heterogeneity of carbon sink capacity and for formulating carbon sequestration strategies.Accordingly, this study integrated multi-source datasets with an improved CASA model and a soil heterotrophic respiration model to estimate farmland NEP from 2000 to 2023.Trend, stability, and Pearson correlation analysis were used to investigate the spatiotemporal variation and management-related associations of NEP, while CMIP6 climate projections were used to simulate future NEP under the SSP126,SSP245,and SSP585 scenarios for 2030,2045,and 2060.The results showed that farmland NEP exhibited a fluctuating upward trend during 2000–2023,with a spatial pattern characterized by higher values in the west and lower values in the east.Human-related factors, including straw returning area, fertilizer application rate, and agricultural machinery power, generally enhanced farmland NEP, whereas excessive multiple cropping and improper irrigation exerted negative effects on NEP in certain areas; under future warming and wetting conditions, farmland NEP in the Guanzhong region is projected to decline overall, and the extent of carbon sink conservation areas is expected to decrease relative to the historical period.The findings provide scientific support for optimizing agricultural management, enhancing farmland carbon sequestration, and promoting sustainable agricultural development in the Guanzhong region.

Article.Title: Arboreal life supports slow and steady pace of life in the Pacific dry forest of Ecuador
Article.Authors: Stănescu F.; Cogălniceanu D.; Niculiță A.; Tănase T.; Székely P.; Székely D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Age and growth-related data provide key insights into life-history strategies, yet remain scarce for neotropical amphibians, particularly arboreal species inhabiting highly seasonal environments. We used skeletochronology to conduct the first empirical assessment of sex-specific aging and somatic growth patterns of an arboreal frog from the Pacific dry forest of Ecuador. We found limited support for the “breed fast, die young” pace of life that would be expected in highly seasonal environments. The studied species, Trachycephalus jordani , attained sexual maturity after two to three years, had a relatively long average lifespan (4.2 years in females, 3.9 years in males) and longevity (6 years in both sexes), and grew slowly compared to a sympatric fossorial species. We suggest that the higher longevity associated with arboreal life buffers the costs of delayed reproduction. Female-biased size dimorphism was established before sexual maturity and maintained after, while age structure and somatic growth were similar in both sexes. Our findings emphasize that the diversity of life-history strategies in the Neotropics is shaped at a fine (microhabitat, microclimate) scale. Expanding age and growth-related research across neotropical lineages and niches remains essential for refining life-history theory and guiding conservation in species-rich but data-poor ecosystems.

Article.Title: Insights on the adsorption of malachite green behavior using a bio-inorganic composite of chitosan-cellulose itaconate/nickel oxide
Article.Authors: Abd-elaty H.; Hamd A.; Osman A.; Ahmed S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The detrimental impacts of dye-containing wastewater discharge on aquatic ecosystems and water quality make it a major environmental concern. The newly synthesized matrix that composed of chitosan-crosslinked cellulose itaconate (CS–CLI) integrated with nickel oxide (NiO) nanoparticles was tested in the removal of malachite green (MG) dye from aqueous solutions. Both surface and core structure of all adsorbents were examined, moreover, different factors affecting the adsorption process such as pH, temperature, contact time, and initial dye concentration were assessed using batch adsorption mode. The findings showed that operating parameters had a significant impact on adsorption efficacy, with optimal removal occurring at pH 7 and 25 °C. At 5 mg/L MG, the removal percentages reached 91% for CS–CLI, 88.9% for NiO, and 81.8% for CS–CLI/NiO, under conditions of pH 7 and 25 °C. The composite's highest adsorption capacity was 11.56 mg/g. Chemisorption was a significant factor in dye uptake, according to kinetic tests that demonstrated the adsorption process followed the pseudo-second-order model. A multi-step adsorption mechanism comprising both surface adsorption and diffusion within the adsorbent structure was proposed by intraparticle diffusion studies. The Freundlich isotherm model provided a more accurate description of equilibrium data, suggesting multilayer adsorption on a heterogeneous surface. The Langmuir isotherm provided the best explanation for the equilibrium results, and adsorption kinetics strongly correlated with the pseudo-second-order model (R 2 = 0.999). It was discovered that the greatest adsorption capacities were 18 mg/g for CS–CLI/NiO, 23.4 mg/g for CS–CLI, and 36.1 mg/g for NiO. Overall, the results show that the CS–CLI/NiO composite is a viable, reasonably priced, and environmentally benign adsorbent for the treatment of dye-contaminated wastewater.

Article.Title: Mosquito community structure, host-feeding patterns, and molecular xenomonitoring of zoonotic Brugia in Klang Valley, Malaysia
Article.Authors: Hafizu M.; Junaid O.; Bakar N.; Phang W.; Ravi R.; Jeyaprakasam N.; Vythilingam I.; Ling L.
Article.Abstract: Lymphatic filariasis remains a public health concern in Malaysia, with zoonotic Brugia species occurring at the animal-human interface and presenting a potential risk of spillover to humans. This study investigated mosquito community structure, host-feeding patterns, and the presence of zoonotic Brugia in a non-endemic area of Malaysia. Entomological surveys were conducted in two locations; Bukit Gasing (forested area) and Pulau Carey (coastal area), between April–July 2024 and November 2024–February 2025 using Human Landing Catch and Mosquito Magnet traps. A total of 1584 mosquitoes representing 16 species were collected, morphologically identified, and analyzed using dissection and PCR targeting the cytochrome c oxidase I ( COX1 ) gene to detect Brugia pahangi and Brugia malayi . Community analysis revealed significant differences in mosquito assemblages between sites (stress = 0.015, F 1,6 = 4.11, R 2 = 0.41, p = 0.021). Pulau Carey was characterized by Culex and Mansonia species, whereas Bukit Gasing was associated with Aedes and Armigeres kesseli . Ar. subalbatus overlapped across the two sites. No significant difference in within-site variability was observed ( p > 0.05). Mosquito dissection showed one infective-stage (L3) of B. pahangi in Ar. subalbatus from Pulau Carey. Molecular screening detected B. pahangi in 5 of 68 pools of Ar. subalbatus (overall minimum infection rate = 3.16 per 1000 mosquitoes; 95% CI 1.0–7.4) from the same area. B. malayi was not detected in any of the samples. Two of the five positive pools yielded high-quality sequences (GenBank: PV611840, PV612037) and showed clustering with Southeast Asian B. pahangi strains from animal and vector sources. Blood meal analysis showed that 47.87% of mosquitoes contained detectable vertebrate DNA, with Ar. subalbatus (H′ = 1.01) and Cx. quinquefasciatus (H′ = 1.08) exhibiting the highest host diversity, feeding across multiple vertebrate hosts including humans, cats, dogs, and monkeys, suggesting their potential role as bridge vectors facilitating contact between human and animal hosts. Although evidence of sustained transmission was not established, the detection of B. pahangi DNA, an infective-stage larva, diverse vector blood meals, and clustering of isolates with sequences from human and animal hosts suggests the potential for zoonotic filarial transmission risk in non-endemic settings. These findings highlight the value of integrated entomological surveillance alongside molecular techniques for detecting early signals of zoonotic filarial circulation in at-risk regions.

Article.Authors: Massidda M.; Ashirov D.; Demkov A.; Sices A.; Baker A.
Article.Abstract: In this study, we developed a computational model of a cell being stretched on a flexible membrane, a configuration that matches many in vitro experimental systems studying the effects of mechanical stretch on cultured cells. Using this model, we explored the complex patterns of stresses and strains present in the cell during dynamic stretching. We linked these intracellular stresses to a simple model of chromatin deformation to provide a rough estimate of chromatin reconfiguration resulting from nuclear strain. Together, this multiscale model of cell stretching offers a first-order approximation of cellular strain responses to dynamic substrate deformation. Our simulations identified an optimal range of applied strain that induces chromatin distention without causing cellular damage. This computationally determined optimal strain range aligns with recent experimental findings from our laboratory, where the same strain levels were shown to maximize nuclear localization of Yap/Taz and reduce senescence in mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). These results provide a computational framework for understanding cellular responses to mechanical stimuli, potentially optimizing experimental designs and advancing the understanding of mechanobiology in stem cell research and tissue engineering applications.

Article.Title: Longitudinal associations between specific exercise components and depressive symptoms in Chinese older women
Article.Authors: Ding L.; Zhang W.; Li W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Physical activity is associated with mental health outcomes in older adults. However, longitudinal evidence regarding specific exercise characteristics and depressive symptoms in older Chinese women remains limited. This study examined the associations between baseline exercise characteristics and subsequent depressive symptoms in community-dwelling older Chinese women. Analysis of covariance was used to examine the associations between baseline exercise characteristics and follow-up SDS after adjustment for baseline SDS and demographic and health-related covariates. In the present study, higher exercise frequency at baseline was significantly associated with lower follow-up SDS scores after adjustment for baseline SDS and potential confounders ( p value < 0.001). Among participants who reported exercising at baseline (n = 637), longer exercise duration and longer exercise persistence were also associated with lower follow-up SDS scores; however, these associations were attenuated and were no longer statistically significant after additional adjustment for exercise frequency. No significant association was observed for exercise intensity. In conclusion, higher baseline exercise frequency was associated with lower depressive symptom scores at follow-up among older Chinese women. Although longer exercise duration and exercise persistence were associated with lower follow-up SDS scores among participants who exercised at baseline, these associations were not independent of exercise frequency. These findings should be interpreted as associations between baseline exercise behaviors and subsequent depressive symptoms.

Article.Authors: Sahal G.

Microbial colonization on BC discs was examined by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) analysis. Tz EO exhibited greater antimicrobial activity than Ss EO, with lower minimum inhibitory and microbicidal concentrations and larger inhibition zones. Notably, BC loaded with only 0.25% (v/v) Tz EO (2.5 µL/mL) inhibited the growth of all tested isolates, whereas BC containing Tz EO at 0.25×MIC reduced biofilm formation by more than 91% across all tested isolates. SEM observations, supported by EDX analysis, indicated reduced microbial colonization on Tz EO-loaded BC discs. These findings support the potential of Tz EO-loaded BC as an antimicrobial biomaterial with broad-spectrum antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity and warrant further evaluation for applications aimed at limiting biofilm-associated infections.

Article.Title: Magnoflorine alleviates experimental osteoarthritis and is associated with altered M1- and M2-associated macrophage markers and subchondral bone remodeling
Article.Authors: Wang C.; Wang H.; Tantai M.; Cui L.; Wang L.; Zhao R.; Yang H.; Liu X.; Cai Z.; Feng Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common degenerative joint disease characterized by cartilage degradation, abnormal subchondral bone remodeling, and macrophage-associated inflammation. Despite its high prevalence, effective disease‑modifying treatments remain lacking due to limited understanding of OA’s complex pathogenesis. Magnoflorine, an active compound from the traditional Chinese medicine formula San‑miao‑San, has reported anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, but its effects and the signaling changes associated with these effects in OA remain unclear. This study aimed to characterize the effects of magnoflorine in experimental OA and the signaling changes associated with these effects. In this study, an osteoarthritis model was induced in rats using medial meniscus destabilization (DMM), and magnoflorine was administered via intra-articular injection. The effects were assessed using micro-CT, histopathological staining, IF, and other techniques. Magnoflorine treatment was associated with improved joint degeneration scores, greater subchondral bone stability, better bone microarchitecture, improved cartilage morphology and matrix synthesis, and changes in osteogenesis-related markers. It was also associated with reduced M1-associated markers, increased M2-associated markers, and increased serum antioxidant enzyme activity. In vitro, magnoflorine showed no cytotoxicity at 25–100 µg/mL and was associated with restored cell viability, increased MC3T3-E1 cell migration, and reduced oxidative stress. It was also associated with reversal of osteoclast-conditioned medium-induced suppression of osteogenic differentiation. The observed effects of magnoflorine were associated with changes in a ROS-associated regulatory network. The observed effects were associated with changes in ROS-related signaling, including reduced ROS levels, attenuated MAPK and NF-κB activation, enhanced Nrf2-associated antioxidant responses, and changes in BMP2/SMAD-associated signaling. These associations may contribute to the anti-inflammatory and pro-osteogenic effects of magnoflorine; however, a sequential causal cascade was not established. These findings suggest that magnoflorine warrants further investigation as a potential disease-modifying candidate for OA and provide experimental context for understanding the modern scientific basis of traditional Chinese medicine in OA treatment.

Article.Title: A symmetry breaking swarm optimizer derived from the Landau theory of phase transitions
Article.Authors: Chen K.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: Metaheuristic optimization algorithms are widely used for high-dimensional non-convex problems, yet most are designed by analogy with biological or physical processes and govern their exploration–exploitation balance with heuristic schedules that lack an underlying theory. We introduce Symmetry-Breaking Swarm Optimization (SBSO), in which this balance is not a tuned schedule but a second-order phase transition derived from the Landau-Ginzburg free energy. Each agent carries a component of an order-parameter field that relaxes along the free-energy gradient while a computational temperature is lowered through the critical point; the field then breaks symmetry spontaneously, and the local order parameter schedules the search operator of every agent. A vector generalization with one field component per coordinate searches heterogeneous problems with coordinate-wise adaptive intensity and reduces exactly to the scalar algorithm when the differentiation strength vanishes. Against eleven optimizers from four families under one evaluation budget, SBSO ranks fourth of twelve on a classical suite, where separable unimodal problems favour methods that collapse the population onto a point, and second of twelve on five shifted and rotated IEEE CEC blocks, where it is consistently the runner-up. Controlled ablations attribute the benefit to the phase transition itself rather than to any individual search operator.

Article.Title: Intelligent fine-grained classification of tunnel surrounding rock mass by integrating tunnel face point clouds and measurement-while-drilling data
Article.Authors: Liu L.; Li Y.; Ding Y.; Han W.; Peng H.; Zhu Z.
Article.Abstract: Fine-grained rock mass classification is essential for support design and safety control in drill-and-blast tunnels. To address the limitations of conventional manual geological logging, including subjectivity, delayed feedback, and difficulty in continuous quantitative assessment, this study proposes an intelligent fine-grained rock mass classification method that integrates tunnel face point clouds and measurement-while-drilling (MWD) data from drilling jumbos. Tunnel face point clouds are used to identify the development characteristics of discontinuities and quantify rock mass integrity, while MWD parameters are employed to characterize the relationship between drilling responses and rock mass conditions. The structural geometric information and drilling-induced mechanical responses are further mapped into a unified probabilistic space for fusion-based classification, thereby improving the accuracy and reliability of rock mass classification. Engineering validation was conducted using typical construction cycles of a drill-and-blast tunnel. The results show that the proposed method can rapidly distinguish between Grade IV and Grade V rock masses, with the fusion-based classification results consistent with manual judgments. The complete workflow for a single construction cycle can be completed in approximately 12–19 min, meeting the requirements for rock mass classification and support decision-making during construction intervals. The findings provide an interpretable and deployable technical approach for intelligent construction and dynamic risk control in drill-and-blast tunnels.

Article.Title: Response characteristics of multi-source information and disaster evolution mechanism of roadway rockburst induced by dynamic stress waves
Article.Authors: Zhang Q.; Liu X.; Wang E.; Li W.; Li Z.; Zhu D.; Xie H.; Gui Q.
Article.Abstract: The high-energy dynamic load released by the fracturing of high-position thick-hard roof is a critical catalyst for inducing rockburst instability in deep roadways. In this study, a self-developed large-scale true-triaxial static–dynamic physical simulation system was used to conduct meter-scale physical model experiments under different impact energy levels. Multi-source monitoring data, including stress, strain, acoustic emission (AE), electromagnetic radiation (EMR), and electrical resistivity, were synchronously collected to unveil the response characteristics and the disaster evolution mechanism of roadway rockburst induced by dynamic stress waves. The results demonstrate that as the impact energy level increases, the macro-failure of the surrounding rock evolves from static-dominated fracture propagation to dynamic-static combined local damage, and eventually to dynamic-dominated global rockburst instability. Apparent resistivity inversion reveals a spatial evolution pattern where the damage zone expands from localized high-resistance areas to a model-wide interconnected network. Both dynamic stress and peak strain of the surrounding rock exhibit non-linear growth with increasing impact energy. Under high-energy impacts, the dynamic stress follows a “rise-plateau-sharp rise-fall” two-stage non-linear growth pattern, accompanied by an instantaneous transition from compressive to tensile strain. This reveals a tension-shear composite progressive secondary failure mechanism. Furthermore, AE and EMR signals evolve from single-peak instantaneous to double-peak continuous characteristics as the energy level rises, serving as characteristic indicators of the transition from local damage to global catastrophe. The response of the surrounding rock structure to dynamic stress is divided into two stages: plastic dissipation and progressive failure. A Rockburst Dynamic Failure Index η is defined as the ratio of the dynamic pressure to the static failure pressure of the surrounding rock, which is equivalent to the ratio of the impact kinetic energy to the plastic energy dissipated during the loading stage. Based on this, rockbursts are categorized into three types: high static load-dominated (1 ~ 2), dynamic-static coupled (2 ~ 100), and dynamic load-dominated (≥ 100). Finally, a feature-level and decision-level multi-source information fusion warning model, integrating stress, deformation, AE, EMR, and resistivity, was constructed. These findings provide essential experimental support and a theoretical basis for the mechanism analysis and monitoring of dynamic load-induced rockburst.
