Article.Title: Green synthesis of copper oxide nanoparticles using Arachis hypogaea shell extract and evaluation of its antioxidative, antidiabetic and antibacterial properties
Article.Authors: Islam M.; Obidul Huq A.; Moksud J.; Nahida U.; Islam S.; Miah M.; Islam D.; Mirza S.; Kazi M.
Article.Abstract: This investigation aimed to employ a green synthesis procedure to fabricate copper oxide nanoparticles (CuO-NPs) from peanut shell extract ( Arachis hypogaea ). Characterization of the synthesized CuO-NPs was conducted utilizing UV‒Vis spectroscopy, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), energy dispersive X-ray (EDX), and field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE‒SEM). The synthesized particles showed a color change pattern during synthesis and it showed a broad peak at 292 ɳm and analyzed using UV–Vis spectroscopy. The morphology of the sample was found to be spherical aggregated from the SEM and XRD, with an average grain size of 25.23 ɳm and 19.30 ɳm crystallite size, respectively. The FTIR data validated the presence of bioactive functional groups which are crucial in capping and stabilizing the CuO-NPs. At a concentration of 500 µg/mL, the produced CuO-NPs demonstrated strong antioxidant activity (scavenging activity was 66.47 ± 1.58%) in the DPPH experiment. An α-amylase inhibition assay was carried out using DNSA method, which showed anti-diabetic activity with maximum inhibition of 63.23 ± 1.36% at 100 µg/mL for CuO-NPs. The antibacterial evaluation showed that CuO-NPs was the most effective with zone of inhibition (mm) Escherichia coli (10.0 ± 0.50), Salmonella typhi (11.0 ± 0.15), Bacillus subtilis (18.5 ± 0.25), and Staphylococcus aureus (14.0 ± 0.50), at minimum inhibitory concentration of 0.2 g/mL Hence, the CuO-NPs prepared using peanut waste extract (PWE) can be used as potential candidates for biomedical applications.

Article.Title: Seed coating with a Serendipita indica–ZnO/Ag nanobiocomposite enhances growth and yield-related traits of rice (Oryza sativa L.)
Article.Authors: Chauhan A.; Tiwari A.; Attri M.; Khanuja M.; Singh M.
Article.Abstract: Rice ( Oryza sativa L.) productivity is constrained by nutrient deficiency and environmental stress, and nanotechnology-based delivery systems offer new options for crop improvement. Here we developed a nanobiocomposite (NBC) by growing the root endophyte Serendipita indica with biosynthesized ZnO (700 ppm) and Ag (100 ppm) nanoparticles (NPs) and applied it to rice as a seed coating. The NPs, synthesized with Azadirachta indica and Aloe vera extracts, had hydrodynamic diameters of 23.3 nm (ZnO) and 65.4 nm (Ag). Growth with the NPs increased fungal dry cell weight by 96.9% and radial growth by 27.8% relative to the control. In a pot experiment, NBC-treated seedlings had the longest shoots (31.8 vs. 11.1 cm in the control) and the highest root length and dry weights after 30 days. In a four-month field trial, NBC-treated plants at harvest were taller (126.0 vs. 98.0 cm), had greater shoot dry weight (49.9 vs. 33.0 g), longer panicles (35.2 vs. 24.0 cm), heavier grains (1000-grain weight 28.7 vs. 24.1 g) and higher chlorophyll and total carbohydrate contents than untreated plants (all P < 0.05). Roots of NBC-treated plants were colonized by the fungus. NBC seed coating is therefore a promising approach for improving rice growth and yield-related traits.

Article.Title: Synthesis and in silico evaluation of 1,2,4-triazolo[1,5-a]pyridines in a solvent-free manner over cellulose-based retrievable copper catalyst
Article.Authors: Salamatmanesh A.; Hosseini M.; Heydari A.; Tehrani S.
Article.Abstract: 1,2,4-Triazolo[1,5-a]pyridines have emerged as potential therapeutic agents for various diseases due to their diverse biological activities, including antiparasitic and anti-inflammatory effects. Recent advances have focused on developing efficient synthetic strategies for these compounds as potential drug candidates with improved efficacy and selectivity. In this study, a cellulose-based copper-amidoxime heterogeneous catalyst was successfully synthesized and applied for the solvent-free synthesis of 1,2,4-triazolo[1,5-a]pyridine derivatives from benzonitriles and 2-aminopyridines. The nanocatalyst exhibited high catalytic activity, easy separation, and good reusability over five consecutive cycles. The nanocatalyst was characterized using FT-IR, XRD, FESEM, TEM, TGA, EDX, VSM, ICP-OES, and BET analyses. The synthesized derivatives were characterized by NMR and mass spectrometry. Molecular mechanics (MM) calculations and geometric optimization of the structures were performed using Spartan software, and the absence of imaginary frequencies confirmed the stability of the structures. Subsequently, molecular docking studies were performed using AutoDock Vina to identify optimal interactions with the target protein. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, structural parameter studies (RMSD, RMSF, R g ), and binding free energy calculations (MM-PBSA) confirmed that, among the synthesized compounds, 2-(naphthalen-2-yl)[1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-a]pyridine (NTP) exhibited the highest compatibility with the drug Tolmetin (TOL). Furthermore, evaluation of binding efficiency metrics, including inhibition constant ( K i ) and ligand efficiency (LE), along with ADMET (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity) and toxicity predictions, suggested that NTP could potentially serve as a promising alternative to TOL.

Article.Title: Sulfuric acid activated water hyacinth root biosorbent for hexavalent chromium removal from synthetic aqueous solutions
Article.Authors: Sisay H.; Prasad D.; Abera M.; Tesema E.; Shams S.
Article.Abstract: Hexavalent chromium [Cr(VI)] discharged from tannery effluents poses severe environmental and human health risks. This study evaluates sulfuric-acid-treated water hyacinth root powder (TWHRP) as a low-cost biosorbent for Cr(VI) removal and recovery, using synthetic Cr(VI) solutions representative of the polishing/tertiary-treatment stage of tannery effluent. The biosorbent was characterised by proximate analysis, BET, point of zero charge, FTIR, and SEM before and after modification and adsorption. Batch experiments varying pH, contact time, adsorbent dosage, and initial Cr(VI) concentration yielded removal efficiencies of 16.98–97.11%. Response surface methodology with a face-centred central composite design identified the optimum as pH 2.01, dosage 0.59 g/100 mL, contact time 62.77 min, and 10.12 mg/L Cr(VI), giving 98.08% predicted removal (experimentally validated at 97.39 ± 0.14%). Equilibrium data fitted both Langmuir and Freundlich isotherms, and the pseudo-second-order model best described the rate data; the underlying mechanism is presented as proposed rather than experimentally demonstrated. Desorption with 0.5 M NaOH (30 mL) recovered 91.27% of the Cr(VI); subsequent reaction with BaCl 2 ·2H 2 O yielded a yellow precipitate consistent with, but not confirmed as, BaCrO 4 , pending XRD and SEM–EDS characterisation.

Article.Title: Experimental study on buckling behavior of corrugated steel arch support under tunnel surrounding rock pressure
Article.Authors: Zhou F.; Xie Z.; Deng T.; Zheng L.; Chen Z.; Xu J.; Zhou W.; Cao K.
Article.Abstract: Steel arch supports are widely used in tunnel construction, but their thin-walled nature makes them susceptible to buckling prior to strength failure. To investigate the evolution of buckling behavior and the spatial characteristics of deformation, physical model tests were conducted on steel arches. Two models were considered: flat steel arches and corrugated steel arches, along with two surrounding rock conditions: with or without sand filling. By analyzing the buckling deformations, strain and critical loads, the results demonstrated that the corrugation shape dramatically enhances structural stability, increasing the critical buckling load by approximately 20 times under identical sand-filled conditions, while reducing vault settlement by approximately 80% compared with flat steel arches. Lateral pressure from the surrounding rock further improves stability, with a lateral pressure coefficient of 0.7 yielding a 145.6% increase in the critical buckling load relative to the no-lateral-pressure condition. The results further revealed that the buckling evolution of the steel arch undergoes three stages: the elastic stage, the nonlinear plastic stage and the instability stage, where the plastic stage is dominated by tangential strain, with magnitude 1.5 to 3 times that of the longitudinal strain. Spatial differentiation of buckling deformation is identified: at the wave-peak, the vault flattens under compression, while at the wave trough, the haunch bulges outward. This study has revealed the evolutionary stages and spatial distribution of buckling in steel arches, and has identified critical early-warning indicators. The results provide practical references for both construction-stage stability control and long-term in-service safety monitoring.

Article.Title: Niosomal in situ gel enhances the ocular bioavailability of kaempferol and improves therapeutic efficacy in dry eye disease
Article.Authors: He X.; Liu Z.; Yao X.; Liang Z.; Wu T.; Ji Y.; Jiang M.; Li Y.; Zhou T.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Dry eye disease (DED) is a common ocular surface disorder characterized by inflammation and oxidative stress. Kaempferol (KAE), a natural flavonoid, exhibits potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, but its physical and chemical properties limit its clinical application. This study aimed to develop a ion-sensitive in situ gel loaded with kaempferol niosomes (KAE-NIO-ISG) for enhanced DED therapy. KAE niosomes were prepared from tween 80, span 60, cholesterol and kaempferol by the thin-film hydration method and incorporated into an ion-sensitive in situ gel matrix. The prepared KAE-NIO-ISG system exhibited favorable nanoscale properties with particle size of 177.27 ± 1.26 nm. The formulation’s viscosity increased from 27.24 ± 0.49 cp to 238.71 ± 1.75 cp, after adding simulated tear fluid. The storage stability study demonstrated that the formulation possessed good stability and irritation test revealed that the formulation was well tolerated. Ocular pharmacokinetic study indicated that the formulation improved the drug’s bioavailability. Therapeutic efficacy was conducted using a benzalkonium chloride-induced dry eye mouse model and the results demonstrated that the efficacy of KAE exhibited in a dose-dependent manner and the efficacy of high-dose KAE was equivalent to cyclosporine. KAE-NIO-ISG is a promising therapeutic strategy for DED, offering good tolerability and improved bioavailability

Article.Title: A matched-cohort study of treatment-requiring autoimmune rheumatic diseases after COVID-19
Article.Authors: Sada R.; Yamamoto S.; Minoda S.; Tajima R.; Miyazawa S.; Komeda T.; Kutsuna S.
Article.Abstract: Post-coronavirus disease-2019 (COVID-19) symptoms can resemble autoimmune and inflammatory rheumatic diseases (AIIRDs), and claims-based studies using diagnosis codes alone may misclassify transient or uncertain diagnoses. The combination of an AIIRD diagnosis and initiated disease-relevant therapy may more accurately identify patients requiring treatment. We aimed to determine whether a history of COVID-19 was associated with a higher 1-year incidence of treatment-requiring AIIRDs compared to matched individuals without COVID-19. We conducted a matched cohort study using the nationwide JMDC Claims Database in Japan, including inpatient, outpatient, and pharmacy data, from July 1, 2019, to August 31, 2023, with 12 months of observation after the index month. Individuals with confirmed COVID-19 and at least 12 months of claims data after the index month were matched 1:1 to individuals without COVID-19 on age, sex, severe-disease risk factors, and Charlson Comorbidity Index; individuals with COVID-19 or AIIRDs in the previous 6 months were excluded. The matched cohorts included 770,498 participants each, and the matched analysis population included 764,454 participants per group. The primary outcome was incident treatment-requiring AIIRD within 12 months, defined by an AIIRD diagnosis code plus initiation of immunosuppressants and/or disease-specific medications. The secondary outcome was AIIRD-related hospitalization. Risk differences and risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals were estimated. Among 1,528,908 participants, incident treatment-requiring AIIRDs occurred in 1,591 individuals (0.21%) with COVID-19 vs. 817 (0.11%) in those without COVID-19 (risk difference, 0.101% points [95% CI, 0.089–0.114]; risk ratio [RR], 1.95 [95% CI, 1.79–2.12]). AIIRD-related hospitalization occurred in 283 individuals (0.037%) with COVID-19 vs. 15 (0.002%) in those without COVID-19 (risk difference, 0.035% points [95% CI, 0.031–0.039]; RR, 18.87 [95% CI, 11.22–31.71]). In diagnosis-specific analyses, notably, risks were higher for rheumatoid arthritis (RR, 1.92 [95% CI, 1.71–2.15]), Sjögren’s syndrome (RR, 1.49 [95% CI, 1.24–1.79]), and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis (RR, 4.90 [95% CI, 2.48–9.67]). This study revealed a higher 1-year incidence of treatment-requiring AIIRDs and markedly higher AIIRD-related hospitalization associated with COVID-19. These findings support clinical vigilance for inflammatory rheumatic disease requiring treatment after COVID-19.

Article.Title: RA4KT: a causality-informed explainable reverse attribution framework for knowledge tracing
Article.Authors: Wang L.; Fu M.; Jian Z.; Tan J.; Zhou X.
Article.Abstract: With the global digital transformation of education, Knowledge Tracing, the core cognitive modeling module in intelligent tutoring systems, has become a key research focus in educational data mining. However, existing deep learning-based KT models are inherently black-box: while achieving high-accuracy answer performance prediction, they fail to clarify internal decision logic or translate outputs into actionable teaching guidance for students and teachers. Existing KT interpretability methods cannot simultaneously satisfy the core requirements of causality, actionability, pedagogical adaptability, and non-professional accessibility, severely limiting KT’s industrial deployment and compliant application of educational AI systems. To address these research gaps, we systematically establish the conceptual definition, mathematical formalization, and five core attributes of reverse attribution for KT sequence learning scenarios, and propose RA4KT, a model-agnostic post-hoc explainable framework specifically tailored to the sequential characteristics and pedagogical prior constraints of educational scenarios. RA4KT unifies attribution validity, modification minimalism, and pedagogical coherence via a multi-objective loss function integrating knowledge concept prior correlations, enforces intervention actionability through an Actionability Mask hard constraint mechanism, and connects model explanation to teaching intervention via a Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP)-variant post-processing module that generates cognitively aligned ordered teaching paths. Systematic experiments on two large-scale real-world educational datasets (XES3G5M and ASSISTments2017) show that RA4KT outperforms mainstream reverse attribution baselines (DiCE, CETD, CMKT, RCKT) on core metrics (Validity, Sparsity, Pedagogical Relevance, Robustness), with relative improvements of the best-performing RA4KT-gs variant over the strongest baseline on each core metric ranging from 2.1% to 16.6% (per-metric, per-dataset values and calculation details in Tables 2–3 and Section "Main experimental results and analysis"), maintains stable performance in long-sequence scenarios, and delivers significant knowledge mastery efficiency gains in offline intervention simulations, especially for students with low initial mastery levels. This work fills the technical gap between black-box KT prediction and actionable intervention schemes, providing a technical pathway toward interpretable engineering deployment of educational AI, with potential extensibility to high-stakes time-series scenarios including healthcare, financial risk control, and industrial predictive maintenance, subject to domain-specific validation.

Article.Title: Design and pilot usability study of a mobile self-care application supporting physical activity among low-risk pregnant women
Article.Authors: Hadizadeh M.; Afshar H.; Nourani A.; Parizad M.; Saleh S.
Article.Abstract: Pregnancy is accompanied by changes that may affect women’s physical activity and ability to maintain healthy self-care practices. Mobile health applications offer a promising approach to providing accessible education and support during pregnancy. The aim of this study was to design and pilot-test the usability of a mobile-based self-care application focused on physical activity for pregnant women. A comprehensive literature review, along with expert consultation with a gynecologist, was conducted to identify the essential requirements and core features of the self-care application. An initial prototype was developed using the Figma platform and reviewed by three domain experts. After iterative refinements, the application was implemented in the Android development environment. Sixteen low-risk pregnant women without medical contraindications to physical activity, recruited by consecutive convenience sampling at Al-Zahra Hospital in Tabriz, Iran, used the application for one month, of whom thirteen completed the final evaluation. User experience was evaluated using the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ). Following the one-month pilot period, semi-structured telephone interviews were conducted with the 13 participants who completed the evaluation to explore their experiences, patterns of use, perceived benefits, and suggestions for improvement. The findings demonstrated a generally positive user experience across all six UEQ dimensions (means ranging from 1.45 to 2.34 on a -3 to + 3 scale; Attractiveness = 1.85, Perspicuity = 2.34, Efficiency = 1.98, Dependability = 2.10, Stimulation = 1.45, and Novelty = 1.95), with all dimensions interpreted as positive evaluations. Participants reported perceiving improved awareness of self-care practices and found the application helpful for accessing educational content. Qualitative findings indicated perceived improvements in awareness of pregnancy-related physical activity and self-care. Participants appreciated the structured activity content and accessibility of the application, while the main recommendations for improvement, raised by a small number of participants, were more comprehensive nutritional information and medication-related precautions. This pilot study demonstrated the feasibility of deploying a Persian-language mobile self-care application integrating structured physical-activity content with complementary self-care information for low-risk pregnant women. The favorable UEQ results and qualitative findings suggest good preliminary usability and acceptability. However, the findings should not be interpreted as evidence of increased physical activity or clinical effectiveness because objective behavioral outcomes were not measured. The small single-site sample, short follow-up period, Android-only design, and absence of usage logs further limit generalizability. Future studies should evaluate the application in larger and more diverse populations using longer follow-up and objective measures of physical activity and relevant maternal outcomes.

Article.Title: Vaccination rates, facilitators and barriers for influenza, pneumococcal and SARS-CoV-2 vaccination among sepsis survivors: a Mid-German Sepsis Cohort survey
Article.Authors: Zimmermann C.; Born S.; Rose N.; Pletz M.; Scherag A.; Reinhart K.; Fleischmann-Struzek C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sepsis survivors often suffer from chronic immune dysfunction, leading to frequent rehospitalization and recurrent sepsis. Vaccinations are effective in preventing common infections in sepsis survivors. However, vaccination behavior in this vulnerable population remains unknown. Prospective interviewer-administered survey performed between 04/2023 and 04/2024 among sepsis survivors in Germany. Participants were recruited from the Mid-German Sepsis Cohort (MSC) 6 to 8 years after initial inclusion. We assessed risk perception, cues to action and barriers for vaccination against influenza, pneumococci and SARS-CoV-2. Predictors for the vaccination status of each of the three infections were identified by logistic regression analyses. Among 174 survivors, vaccination rates against influenza and pneumococci rose from 57.3 to 70.7% and from 31.4 to 60.5% 3 months to 8 years post-sepsis, respectively. A total of 135 patients (77.6%) had full vaccination coverage against SARS-CoV-2 at the time of the survey. Higher age and an intermediate vs. low education increased the odds for influenza vaccination. No associations between sociodemographic indicators and the vaccination status against pneumococci and SARS-CoV-2 were found. Vaccination counselling by a general practitioner increased the odds for vaccination between 5.5-fold (influenza) and 3.2-fold (pneumococci) in the multiple regression analyses. The review of general vaccination status was associated with a 4.7-fold increase of influenza vaccination rates and 3.1-fold increase of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination rates. Among patients with at least one missing vaccination (n = 92), impaired mobility (16.8%), long waiting times in the practice (14.8%) and fear of infection in the practice (14.7%) were the most relevant barriers. There are considerable vaccination gaps in sepsis survivors. Pro-active vaccination counselling and checks of vaccination status by general practitioners may offer a great potential to increase vaccination rates and thus should be considered as an important element of sepsis aftercare.

Article.Title: Medicinal fungal secondary metabolites as potential inhibitors of the Chikungunya virus nsP2 protease: an integrated computational study
Article.Authors: Siddiquee N.; Mueed K.; Faysal M.; Islam L.; Ragu M.; Aktery S.; Omor S.; Hosen M.; Anan A.
Article.Abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an emerging mosquito-borne alphavirus that causes millions of infections and severe arthralgia annually. Due to the lack of specific antiviral medications, analgesics and NSAIDs are used for symptomatic relief but are associated with potential hepatic, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, and renal toxicities. This study investigated natural fungal secondary metabolites selected to target nsP2 protease (PDB ID: 3TRK), a key protein involved in chikungunya virus replication. 1830 fungal secondary metabolites were screened using intensive in silico approaches to identify potential nsP2 inhibitors. Based on their binding affinity, ADMET profiles, and post-docking MM-GBSA, HOMO-LUMO, and QSAR analyses, three lead compounds (MSIDs 000670, 001323, and 001565) were selected for further investigation alongside the control (Withaferin A). The 200 ns MD simulations provided insights into their stability, while DCCM, PCA, and post-simulation MM-GBSA analyses further supported their favorable dynamic behavior and binding stability. Among these candidates, MSID000670 (Erinacerin Q) and MSID001565 (Caputmedusin F) exhibited optimal ADME properties, reduced toxicity, higher binding scores, and a consistently stable MD simulation profile. Since these compounds are reported here for the first time as promising drug candidates, they need special attention in chikungunya antiviral drug development. However, experimental validation is needed to confirm their therapeutic potential.

Article.Title: Joint communication, computation, and trajectory optimization for UAV-enabled mobile edge computing in smart city IoT networks
Article.Authors: Alruwaili F.; Alsolai H.; Aljaafari M.; Saeed M.; Alotaibi S.; Alamro S.; Ebad S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Smart-city Internet of Things (IoT) devices generate latency-sensitive computation tasks but have limited processing and energy resources. UAVs Computing (MEC) servers can serve them, yet probabilistic air-to-ground propagation, nonlinear rotary-wing propulsion, strict per-task deadlines, backhaul availability and finite onboard energy make the joint coordination of communication, computation and mobility difficult. We formulate a mixed-integer nonconvex problem that jointly determines task admission, binary edge/cloud execution, onboard Central Processing Unit (CPU) allocation and horizontal trajectory, minimizing a normalized combination of device and UAV mission energy under single-user Time-Division Multiple Access (TDMA) access, same-slot end-to-end deadlines, computation-capacity, backhaul-availability, mobility, minimum-completion and battery-reserve constraints. The optimal frequency is shown to admit a closed form, reducing the integer block to a binary linear program solved to proven optimality; the trajectory is updated by a constrained trust-region nonlinear program using the original expressions. Every accepted state satisfies the original constraints, and the best-so-far objective sequence converges. Over 50 realizations with 12 devices and 120 slots, the method attains a mean normalized objective of 0.334, reducing it by $$11.10\%$$ , $$7.16\%$$ , $$7.02\%$$ and $$0.98\%$$ against local-only execution, fixed CPU allocation, an estimation-of-distribution algorithm and a straight-line trajectory (Holm-adjusted $$p=3.02\times 10^{-9}$$ ); a cloud-only design is feasible in only 5 of 50 cases. Code and data are openly available.

Article.Title: Age-dependent threshold effect of reproductive lifespan on cardiovascular disease in chinese women: a CHARLS cohort study
Article.Authors: Chen Y.; Huang H.; Gongqiu B.; Gesang Y.
Article.Abstract: Reproductive lifespan (RLS) reflects lifetime estrogen exposure. Whether age modifies the nonlinear link between RLS and cardiovascular disease (CVD) is unclear. We investigated this age-dependent relationship in Chinese women. Data were from CHARLS. We included 4,443 women aged ≥ 45 years without CVD at baseline (2011). Incident CVD was defined as self-reported, physician-diagnosed heart disease or stroke. RLS = menopause age − menarche age. Participants were stratified by baseline age tertiles. We applied Cox models with restricted cubic splines and two-piecewise Cox regression to detect nonlinearity and thresholds, with subgroup and sensitivity analyses. Over 7.53 years of follow-up (33,442 person-years), 1,244 (28.0%) developed CVD. In the youngest tertile (age 45–55), RLS showed a U-shaped association with a threshold at ~ 31 years (LRT P = 0.027). Above 31 years, longer RLS increased CVD risk (HR = 1.08, 95% CI 1.03–1.13; P = 0.003). No thresholds were detected in older tertiles. Findings were robust in sensitivity analyses. In younger postmenopausal women, RLS beyond ~ 31 years was associated with higher CVD risk. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation; whether reproductive lifespan improves cardiovascular risk prediction remains to be formally evaluated.

Article.Title: MAP3K8 is associated with an immune-active tumor microenvironment and suppresses malignant phenotypes of NSCLC cells in vitro
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Song J.; Dong T.; Zhang W.; Li X.
Article.Abstract: MAP3K8, also known as Tpl2/Cot, participates in MAPK- and NF-κB-related signaling and plays important roles in inflammation and immune regulation. However, its expression pattern, prognostic value, and immune relevance in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remain unclear. Transcriptomic, clinical, pan-cancer, single-cell RNA-sequencing, and cell-line datasets were integrated to characterize MAP3K8 expression and its clinical and immune associations in NSCLC, particularly lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Survival, immune-infiltration, functional-enrichment, molecular-subtype, N6-methyladenosine (m6A)-related, Tumor Immune Dysfunction and Exclusion (TIDE), and exploratory computational drug-response analyses were performed. An independent institutional cohort of 114 patients with NSCLC was additionally analyzed to validate the association between MAP3K8 protein expression and overall survival. MAP3K8 protein expression and subcellular localization were evaluated by Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and immunofluorescence. To investigate the tumor-cell-intrinsic effects of MAP3K8, MAP3K8 was overexpressed in A549 cells and depleted in H1975 cells, followed by proliferation, migration, and invasion assays. MAP3K8 expression was reduced in LUAD tissues, and higher expression was associated with favorable overall survival. This association was further supported in an independent institutional cohort of 114 patients with NSCLC, in which high MAP3K8 protein expression was associated with significantly longer overall survival (log-rank P < 0.001) and remained significantly associated with survival after multivariable adjustment for the clinicopathological variables included in the model. Single-cell analysis showed that MAP3K8 was predominantly expressed in dendritic cells, monocytes/macrophages, and other immune-cell populations rather than malignant epithelial cells. Higher MAP3K8 expression was associated with an immune-active tumor microenvironment. Functional gain- and loss-of-function experiments further showed reciprocal effects of MAP3K8 manipulation on NSCLC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. MAP3K8 expression is associated with favorable prognosis and an immune-active tumor microenvironment in LUAD/NSCLC. The prognostic association observed in public transcriptomic data was further supported by an independent institutional cohort. Complementary gain- and loss-of-function experiments indicate that MAP3K8 can negatively regulate malignant phenotypes of NSCLC cells in vitro. However, because MAP3K8 expression in primary tumors is strongly influenced by immune-cell composition, further studies incorporating tumor purity, immune-cell fractions, and independent treatment-annotated cohorts are required to establish its independent prognostic and mechanistic significance.

Article.Title: Temporal changes in quadriceps tendon mechanical properties following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: an in vivo shear wave elastography study
Article.Authors: Pasurka M.; Falck T.; Söllner S.; Kubach J.; Strobel D.; Perl M.; Betsch M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In addition to hamstring and patellar tendon (PT) autografts, the quadriceps tendon (QT) has gained increasing popularity for anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR), partly due to lower reported graft re-rupture rates. However, postoperative changes of the residual quadriceps tendon and the relationship between tendon mechanical properties and clinical outcomes remain poorly understood. The purpose of this study was to evaluate in vivo QT mechanical properties following graft harvest for ACLR and to quantify tendon mechanical properties using shear wave elastography (SWE). Twenty patients (11 males, 9 females; mean age 29.8 ± 7.2 years; mean BMI 26.8 ± 3.8 kg/m²) with anterior cruciate ligament rupture who underwent ACLR using an ipsilateral QT autograft were prospectively enrolled. In addition to standardized clinical outcome measures, participants underwent a standardized multimodal ultrasound protocol of the bilateral QT consisting of B-mode-ultrasound (B-US), Color Doppler-ultrasound (CD-US) and a SWE examination. Measurements were performed preoperatively (t0) and at 3 (t1), 6 (t2), and 12 months (t3) postoperatively. For SWE values a two-way repeated-measures analysis of variance (RM-ANOVA) was performed to evaluate differences over time and between sides. The within-subject factors were time (preoperative, 3 months, 6 months, and 12 months) and side (operated vs. contralateral control). For ROM measurements and scores a one-way repeated-measures analysis of variance (RM-ANOVA) was performed to evaluate differences over time. Effect sizes were reported as partial eta-squared (ηₚ²). Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Post-hoc pairwise comparisons were adjusted using the Bonferroni correction. Relationships between variables were assessed using the Pearson correlation coefficient (r). A significant main effect of time (F(3,57) = 2.86; p = 0.045; partial η² = 0.131) and a significant time-by-side interaction (F(3,57) = 3.98; p = 0.012; partial η² = 0.173) were observed. On the operated limb, a significant time effect was observed (F(3,57) = 5.14; p = 0.003), characterized by a transient increase in mechanical properties from the preoperative baseline to 3 months (Δ = −0.421; p = 0.045), followed by a significant decline from 3 to 6 months (Δ = +0.447; p = 0.003) and from 3 to 12 months (Δ = +0.368; p = 0.030). No significant difference was found between the preoperative baseline and 12 months. On the control limb, QT mechanical properties remained stable throughout the entire follow-up period (F(3,57) = 0.38; p = 0.769); none of the pairwise comparisons reached statistical significance. Over the 12-month follow-up period, significant improvements were observed in knee flexion as well as in the IKDC and Lysholm clinical scores, with the greatest gains occurring between the preoperative baseline and 6 months postoperatively. The Öhberg score exhibited a biphasic course with an initial increase at 3 months and subsequent normalisation by 12 months. Extension showed only a non-significant trend toward improvement. No statistically significant correlations were found between QT mechanical properties and clinical scores, as well as between QT mechanical properties and range of motion. Moderate correlations were observed between QT mechanical properties and IKDC ( r = 0.30, p = 0.207) and Lysholm Score ( r = 0.39, p = 0.231), without reaching significance. No significant correlations were observed between QT mechanical properties and knee flexion ( r = 0.11, p = 0.335), extension ( r = 0.10, p = 0.373), or Öhberg score ( r = -0.02, p = 0.873). This study represents the first in vivo assessment of quadriceps tendon SWE-derived mechanical properties following ACLR using a QT autograft. The findings indicate a high adaptation capacity of the QT, with transient postoperative changes in stiffness that normalize over time. Future studies incorporating longitudinal histological evaluation are warranted to further elucidate the biological mechanisms underlying QT alterations after graft harvest.

Article.Title: Hemoglobin polymorphism and its association with morphometric traits of indigenous sheep populations reared in different agroecological zones of Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Woldeyohannes T.; Betsha S.; Melesse A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Analyzing blood protein polymorphisms helps in understanding population relationships, genetic structure, and their evolution. This study was conducted to assess hemoglobin polymorphisms and their association with morphometric traits of indigenous sheep population reared in the highland, lowland, and midland agroecological zones. Blood samples were collected from 198 sheep of both sexes, and hemoglobin types were determined by gel electrophoresis. Agroecological zone had a significant ( p < 0.05) effect on body weight and most other linear body measurements. The two hemoglobin variants, namely Hb A and Hb B , with frequencies of 0.30 and 0.70 in highland, 0.23 and 0.77 in midland, and 0.17 and 0.83 in lowland sheep populations, were observed, with the predominance of Hb B in all agroecological zones. The genetic distance at the hemoglobin locus between lowland and midland was estimated to be 0.004. Body length was significantly ( p < 0.05) affected by hemoglobin type, with the longest body being observed at Hb AB type. The studied sheep populations did not significantly deviate from Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium ( p = 0.05). These findings provide baseline information that may contribute to future genetic characterization and may support further investigations into selection and the design of cost-effective and sustainable genetic improvement programs for indigenous sheep populations in the Sidama region.

Article.Title: Experimental investigation into the influence of rock mechanical properties and etching patterns on acid fracture conductivity in the ilam carbonate formation
Article.Authors: Akbari M.; Ameri M.; Homayoun M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Acid fracturing represents a primary stimulation technique for unlocking commercial hydrocarbon productivity in tight carbonate reservoirs, yet predicting post-treatment fracture conductivity under closure stress remains challenging due to the coupled effects of dissolution geometry and rock mechanical deformation. In this study, we present an experimental methodology that decouples mechanical closure from stochastic dissolution kinetics by machining deterministic, idealized channel geometries onto standardized split core plugs (18.4 cm length × 4.75 cm width) of Cretaceous Ilam formation limestone from southwest Iran. Using an API RP-61 compliant high-pressure conductivity cell, tests were conducted across systematic variations in channel depth (0.6-1.6 mm), width (1.4-2.48 mm), and multiplicity (1–3 channels) under closure stresses spanning 1,321 to 5,283 psi (9.1–36.4 MPa). Two distinct mechanical facies were evaluated: compliant Ilam 1 (Young’s modulus E = 19.7 GPa, UCS = 50.0 MPa) and stiff Ilam 2 (E = 39.63 GPa, UCS = 78.8 MPa). Our results demonstrate that channel depth is the governing geometric control, providing 6- to 9-fold greater retained conductivity per unit volume of dissolved rock than channel widening or multiplicity. Classical linear superposition and parallel-plate cubic formulations fail systematically under closure due to sidewall compliance and inter-channel pillar stress concentrations. Notably, in multi-channel systems subjected to stresses exceeding 3,500 psi, stiffer rock undergoes accelerated conductivity loss via brittle pillar crushing, whereas compliant rock exhibits ductile stress redistribution that preserves conduit patency. Regularized third-degree polynomials accurately model this multi-stage closure behavior (R 2 > 0.98), providing physically grounded inputs for reservoir stimulation design.

Article.Title: Complete mitochondrial genome of six aphids (Hemiptera: Aphididae)
Article.Authors: Wang Z.; Zhao T.; Zhan D.; Fan J.; Wang C.; Wu S.; Duan Y.
Article.Abstract: Aphids represent an important group within Hemiptera, yet mitochondrial genomic data for this lineage remain relatively scarce. In this study, we newly sequenced and characterized the complete mitochondrial genomes of six aphid species, all of which contain the canonical set of 37 genes. Among them, two mitochondrial genomes supplement existing NCBI entries with additional validated data, while the other four are reported here for the first time. Evolutionary rate analysis revealed that nad6 exhibited the highest Ka/Ks ratio, whereas cox1 was the most conserved. Nucleotide composition skews varied among different codon positions. Phylogenetic trees reconstructed from a dataset comprising 107 aphid mitochondrial genomes consistently placed all six species with their respective congeners, supporting their taxonomic assignments. Overall, this study contributes six novel mitochondrial genome sequences to the existing genomic resources, providing a valuable reference for future phylogenetic and evolutionary investigations of Aphididae. The phylogenetic analyses presented here are intended to validate the taxonomic assignment of the newly sequenced species and should not be interpreted as resolving deep-level relationships within the family.

Article.Title: Predictive analysis of Drug concentration in drug release process via two-dimensional mechanistic model and machine learning integrated Grey Wolf optimization
Article.Authors: Alotaibi H.; Saleh K.; kumar Alisherov F.; Patel M.; Jayaprakash B.; Shakir A.; Ansari G.; Sharma S.
Article.Abstract: This research develops a machine learning framework to predict the spatial distribution of drug concentration (C) within a specific cylindrical biomaterial matrix at a fixed release time (t = 2400 s), using the radial (r) and axial (z) coordinates as inputs. The predictions are limited to the specific diffusion-reaction system described by the mass transfer equations, and the parameter set defined by Maxwell method, with no extrapolation beyond the training domain of r ∈ [0, 0.006] m and z ∈ [0, 0.009] m. Three distinct models, Kernel Ridge Regression (KRR), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), were employed to predict C based on the input parameters r and z. The data for machine learning were obtained by solution of mass transfer equations for this specific system. The effectiveness of each model was evaluated by considering essential metrics, such as the R² score, the Mean Squared Error (MSE), and the Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE). The findings suggest that the XGBoost model surpassed both GPR and KRR, attaining an R² score of 0.97322, showcasing its effectiveness in capturing the inherent patterns within the dataset. GPR also demonstrated good performance with an R² score of 0.95911, whereas KRR exhibited lower accuracy with an R² score of 0.75277. To enhance the models’ predictive capabilities, hyperparameter optimization was carried out using Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO). Within the specific simulated system investigated, this study demonstrates the efficacy of ML models with hyperparameter optimization for predicting spatial drug concentration. Extension to other systems requires additional validation.

Article.Title: Contribution of centrosymmetric lattice parameters to impeller response
Article.Authors: Jia D.; You Z.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates the mechanical response of centrosymmetric lattice-filled compressor impellers under inertial and combined inertial/aerodynamic loading. A multiscale homogenization framework is developed, and the effects of lattice configuration, volume fraction, and loading conditions are systematically examined. The centrosymmetric lattice reduces maximum deformation by approximately 25.5% and peak stress by approximately 42.2% compared to the parallel-array configuration, while achieving superior circumferential uniformity. For the full impeller, aerodynamic pressure reduces deformation and stress by only about 1.3% and 1.0%, respectively, indicating that inertia-only analysis is mildly conservative. A local minimum in the sampled volume-fraction range shifts from 14% under inertia-only loading to 22% under combined inertial/aerodynamic loading; this is a local minimum within the sampled range rather than a formal optimization result. These findings provide practical guidelines for the lightweight design of high-performance impellers.

Article.Title: Electric-field-induced fully spin-polarized current in ferromagnetic bipolar Ag, Cr, or Sc-decorated AlN monolayer at room temperature
Article.Authors: Mahmoodabadi M.; Mahdavinejad H.; Nasresfahani S.; Safaiee R.; Sheikhi M.
Article.Abstract: In this study, we systematically unveil the pivotal role of transition metal adatoms (Ag, Cr, and Sc) in the atomic configuration, electronic structure, and magnetic properties of the aluminum nitride(AlN) monolayer using spin-polarized density functional theory calculations. A pristine AlN monolayer is a direct p-type semiconductor with a non-magnetic nature. Decoration of the AlN monolayer with transition metal atoms induces a transition from non-magnetic to antiferromagnetic states. Bipolarity emerges in the decorated AlN monolayer once the temperature exceeds the magnetic transition temperature. Based on the first-principle calculations, the magnetic transition temperature turns out to be 21, 494.075, and 57.39 K for the AlN monolayers decorated with Ag, Cr, and Sc, respectively. The adatoms’ partially filled valence orbitals hybridizing with the host material is responsible for the ferromagnetic state of each compound. Further investigation demonstrates that stronger chemical adsorption and higher charge transfer are achieved for the Sc-decorated AlN monolayer. The tight bonding of the Sc atom, relative to other adsorbate species, is attributed to the formation of polar covalent bonds between the Sc atom and the nearest N atoms of the AlN monolayer. We further extended our investigation to explore the adsorption properties of decorated AlN monolayers under an external electric field. The energy band gap in all structures begins to decrease as the applied external electric field increases, and half-metallicity occurs when a threshold electric field is reached. These results underscore the significant potential of adatom embellishment of the AlN monolayer for future electronic and spintronic devices.

Article.Title: Ferroelectric-substrate coupling modulates hydrovoltaic droplet-induced electrical signals on graphene
Article.Authors: Jang Y.; Kim S.; Choi S.; Lee H.; Yang H.; Kum H.
Article.Abstract: Hydrovoltaic electricity generation at graphene-liquid interfaces is sensitive to both the electronic state of graphene and the electrostatic environment at the interface. However, how remanent ferroelectric polarization pre-conditions the electronic state of graphene before droplet contact, and how this state is related to the subsequent electrical response, remains unclear. Here, we use electrically pre-poled LiTaO 3 (LTO) and LiNbO 3 (LNO) ferroelectric substrates to electrostatically pre-condition graphene before liquid contact. Kelvin probe force microscopy reveals clear polarization-dependent shifts in graphene work function. Positive polarization produces a relatively electron-rich state, whereas negative polarization shifts graphene toward a more hole-rich state. Despite these distinct electronic states, the hydrovoltaic response does not follow a universal polarization-dependent voltage ordering across LiTaO 3 and LiNbO 3 , indicating that graphene carrier modulation alone cannot account for the generated response. Transient measurements further reveal strongly polarization- and substrate-dependent changes in the rise and decay time constant, indicating that ferroelectric polarization influences not only the signal magnitude but also transient interfacial charge dynamics. Repeated droplet exposure and subsequent cleaning produce partially reversible changes in the electrical response, while long-term ambient aging substantially reduces the polarization-dependent work-function contrast. Together, these results establish an experimental link between remanent ferroelectric polarization, the pre-contact electronic state of graphene, and the subsequent droplet-induced electrical response. Ferroelectric substrates therefore provide a substrate-side strategy for regulating graphene hydrovoltaic interfaces without continuous external bias or direct chemical doping.

Article.Title: Performance of the DxI 9000 Access immunoassay analyzer for the diagnosis of viral hepatitis B and C
Article.Authors: Le Glaunec J.; Luce D.; Pispisa V.; Safinia S.; Bouvier-Alias M.; Cappy P.; Roudot-Thoraval F.; Chevaliez S.
Article.Abstract: Reliable serological assays are essential for the screening and diagnosis of hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections. We evaluated the analytical and clinical performance of the DxI 9000 Access Immunoassay Analyzer for detecting HBV and HCV markers using over 1,000 serum and plasma specimens, including seroconversion panels and clinical specimens. Results were compared with those from established platforms, such as the VITROS ECiQ and Alinity i. The Access anti-HCV assay demonstrated 97.5% sensitivity and 97.0% specificity, with slightly delayed detection in some seroconversion panels. The Access HBsAg assay showed high sensitivity (98.8%) and specificity (99.2%), with robust detection of most HBsAg variants. Anti-HBc assays (total and IgM) achieved 100% sensitivity and demonstrated excellent concordance across platforms. Anti-HBs results showed good agreement, with minor discrepancies in samples with a low titer (< 10 mIU/mL). Overall, agreement with the comparator assays ranged from 84.7% to 100%. The Access assays on the DxI 9000 platform demonstrate high analytical and clinical performance for hepatitis B and hepatitis C serological testing, with strong agreement with established systems. These results support the use of the DxI 9000 Access Immunoassay Analyzer in the serological testing of viral hepatitis.

Article.Title: Six test exercises to assess weaknesses in four physical abilities related to fall risk
Article.Authors: Folke M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Weaknesses in physical ability related to fall risk need to be identified and reversed as early as possible. Eleven physical test exercises have shown to be able to assess weaknesses in four physical abilities related to fall risk. The aim of this study was to evaluate the applicability of predefined pass criteria for the 11 test exercises in older adults and to determine whether the number of test exercises assessing balance and strength could be reduced without loss of relevant information on weakness in physical ability related to fall risk. Fisher’s exact test was performed to evaluate if the number of test exercises can be reduced. The result shows that: (i) The predefined pass criteria for the test exercises are achievable in older adults, (ii) the number of test exercises assessing balance can be reduced but not those assessing strength. It can be concluded that six of the evaluated test exercises are achievable in older adults and can assess weakness in physical ability related to fall risk for them. These six test exercises can identify kinds of weaknesses related to fall risk and assess the severity of the weakness.

Article.Title: An episodic prototypical embedding modulated transformer (EPMT) for network intrusion detection
Article.Authors: Biswal U.; Mishra S.; Mahapatra S.
Article.Abstract: The rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) and Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) deployments has made intrusion detection harder, with high-dimensional flow representations, severe class imbalance, and attack families that appear with few labelled examples. This study proposes an Episodic Prototypical Embedding-Modulated Transformer (EPMT), which differs from prior work less in its components than in how feature relevance enters the model. A multi-criteria ranking stage combines correlation, ANOVA F -statistic, mutual information, and recursive feature elimination through the Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) to produce a continuous relevance score for every feature, and the resulting subset is combined with an episode-level context vector through a feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM) layer inside the transformer. Classification is performed by prototypical metric learning under an episodic meta-learning objective. We evaluate on RT-IoT-2022, CIC-IoT-2023, and CIC-IoMT-2024-WiFi-MQTT under a stratified cross-validation protocol, reporting macro-averaged precision, recall, and \(F_1\) alongside accuracy and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, since accuracy is dominated by majority classes in all three benchmarks. Under its selected sequence length and ADASYN configuration, EPMT reaches a macro \(F_1\) of 80.32% on RT-IoT-2022, 42.45% on CIC-IoT-2023, and 56.25% on CIC-IoMT-2024, consistently ahead of a plain transformer, a meta-learned transformer without FiLM, and a FiLM-conditioned transformer without episodic training on every dataset and every principal metric. We report this consistent ordering as evidence of a directionally robust improvement rather than definitive statistical superiority: under a three-fold cross-validation protocol with correspondingly limited statistical power, only one of nine pairwise comparisons, EPMT against the plain transformer on RT-IoT-2022, remains significant after Holm correction. Per-class confusion matrices and receiver operating characteristic curves are reported for the selected configuration on all three datasets, and show that the gap between accuracy and macro-averaged \(F_1\) has a different source on each benchmark. We additionally report a diagnostic finding of independent interest: two of the three benchmarks are distributed in class-contiguous record order, so sliding-window sequence construction over them aggregates same-class records rather than modelling traffic dynamics, which inflates measured performance under record-level cross-validation. We quantify this effect and discuss its implications for sequence-based evaluation on these datasets, and we report a substantially more conservative estimate of RT-IoT-2022 performance under a strict temporal hold-out. We treat the fixed, dataset-level feature-selection protocol, together with the comparison against published baselines evaluated under different protocols, as open points that bound the strength of the claims made here, and we discuss each explicitly rather than treating the reported numbers as a settled comparison.

Article.Title: Coupled electronic and phononic transport in O-terminated MXene nanoribbons within a unified TB-NEGF framework
Article.Authors: Soltani O.; Jafari M.; Shokri A.
Article.Abstract: Thermoelectric transport in oxygen-terminated MXene nanoribbons is investigated using a tight-binding nonequilibrium Green’s function (TB-NEGF) framework combined with phonon transport calculations. Ti₃C₂O₂ is considered as the primary system, and the effect of thermally induced bond-length fluctuations on electronic hopping parameters is incorporated through a temperature-dependent hopping-renormalization scheme. The present model is intended as a computationally efficient effective description, with the force constants and hopping-decay coefficients treated as effective parameters. At 300 K, the maximum electronic thermoelectric figure of merit changes from 2.9698 for the unrenormalized system to 2.9944 after hopping renormalization, indicating a relatively small effect of thermal lattice fluctuations on the electronic thermoelectric response. The phonon contribution is subsequently evaluated using phonon NEGF, yielding a lattice thermal conductance of 2.57 × 10⁻¹¹ W K⁻¹ and a corresponding thermal conductivity of 0.0411 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹. Including lattice thermal transport reduces the maximum ZT to 0.8361. Comparative calculations for Zr₃C₂O₂ show that the proposed treatment can also be applied to a different transition-metal-based MXene. These results demonstrate that lattice heat transport, rather than thermal hopping renormalization, plays a major role in determining the achievable thermoelectric performance of the investigated MXene nanoribbons.

Article.Title: Comparative and explainable deep learning for cherry (Prunus avium L.) cultivar classification using convolutional neural networks (CNN) and transformer architectures
Article.Authors: Demir B.; Ünal F.; Türk Ö.; Acar M.; Yaman K.; Gezer U.; Yaman M.; Tunç Y.
Article.Abstract: Accurate identification of cherry ( Prunus avium L.) cultivars is essential for automated sorting, postharvest management, and cultivar-specific quality control in modern horticultural systems. However, fine-grained classification remains highly challenging due to strong phenotypic similarity among cultivars and the influence of intra-class variability under imaging conditions. In this study, a comparative and explainable deep learning framework was developed to classify eight cherry cultivars, including both registered cultivars and selection cultivars, using three representative architectures: ResNet50, EfficientNet-B0, and Swin Transformer V2. A stratified five-fold cross-validation strategy was employed to provide a consistent fold-wise evaluation while preserving class balance. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, confusion matrices, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, area under the curve (AUC), and Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) for interpretability. Among the evaluated models, EfficientNet-B0 achieved the highest classification accuracy (0.970), followed by Swin Transformer V2 (0.955) and ResNet50 (0.895). EfficientNet-B0 achieved an AUC of 1.00 for all evaluated classes in the present dataset and exhibited the most stable training convergence among the evaluated architectures. Misclassification was primarily observed between phenotypically similar cultivars, particularly 10–22 and Lapins, highlighting the intrinsic complexity of fine-grained classification. Grad-CAM analysis revealed that EfficientNet-B0 produced the most spatially focused and fruit-centered attribution maps, whereas ResNet50 showed diffuse activations and Swin Transformer V2 captured broader contextual features. Overall, the results demonstrate the feasibility of deep learning-based fine-grained cherry cultivar classification under controlled imaging conditions. EfficientNet-B0 achieved the highest mean accuracy among the evaluated architectures in the present dataset; however, this result should be interpreted as dataset- and condition-specific rather than as evidence of general architectural superiority. The proposed framework provides an interpretable basis for future validation using independently acquired and more diverse datasets. The proposed framework provides a reproducible and interpretable comparative approach for cultivar-level image recognition and may support future intelligent sorting and precision-agriculture applications.

Article.Title: Improved Nix-Gao-Feng model considering the strain-rate effect on indentation size effect
Article.Authors: Wang P.; Gao Y.; Wang P.
Article.Abstract: The indentation size effect (ISE) and strain-rate effect are two fundamental phenomena in nanomechanical characterization; however, a model that can predict the influence of the strain-rate effect on hardness measurements across different ISE categories remains lacking. Here, we develop an improved Nix-Gao-Feng model considering the strain-rate effect on ISE, termed the INGF-SS model, by systematically identifying and formulating the strain-rate dependence of three key parameters: the lattice friction contribution, the dislocation hardening contribution, and the plastic-zone evolution parameter. The model is established by first modifying the relationship between the plastic zone size ratio and indentation depth, and then determining mathematical descriptions for the rate-dependent evolution of these key parameters. The descriptive capability of INGF-SS model is validated against experimental data covering three ISE categories, normal ISE (N-ISE), normal-to-reverse ISE (NR-ISE), and complex ISE (C-ISE), across different materials under various strain-rates. The validation shows that the INGF-SS model can describe the rate-dependent of three ISE categories. Compared with a simplified INGF‑SS model accounting only for rate effects on lattice friction, the INGF‑SS model yields a higher mean determination coefficient (DC) of 0.9630 and a lower mean root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.4648 GPa. Furthermore, the predictive capability of the model is evaluated via two extrapolation strategies: the strategy using both low and high strain-rate data for parameters calibration achieves acceptable medium-strain-rate predictions for most materials, while direct extrapolation to the highest strain rate shows larger deviations at large indentation depths. This work thus provides a semi-empirical theoretical model for describing coupled size and rate effects in different materials under dynamic indentation.

Article.Title: Comparison of subjective orofacial esthetic perception and objective malocclusion severity: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Beşer Gül B.; Pertek Hatipoğlu F.; Şahin R.; Hatipoğlu Ö.
Article.Abstract: This cross-sectional study aimed to compare subjective orofacial esthetic perception assessed using the Orofacial Esthetic Scale (OES) with objective malocclusion severity assessed using the Dental Aesthetic Index (DAI), and to identify demographic and occlusal factors associated with OES scores. A total of 263 participants (163 females and 100 males) were included. OES summary scores were calculated from seven items (range, 0–70), with higher scores indicating greater esthetic satisfaction. DAI scores were categorized according to established malocclusion severity thresholds. Associations with demographic characteristics were examined using appropriate non-parametric and categorical tests, the relationship between continuous DAI and OES scores was assessed using Spearman correlation, and factors associated with OES scores were evaluated using univariable and multivariable linear regression with HC3 robust standard errors. DAI category distribution was significantly associated with education level ( p = 0.010), but not with gender ( p = 0.235) or age group ( p = 0.080). Female participants had lower OES scores than males in the unadjusted comparison (median 44.0 vs 47.0; p = 0.034), whereas OES scores did not differ significantly across education levels ( p = 0.436). DAI and OES scores showed a moderate inverse correlation (Spearman’s ρ = − 0.407, p < 0.001). In the adjusted model, largest anterior maxillary irregularity (β = − 1.690, p < 0.001), maxillary overjet (β = − 1.337, p = 0.005), and mandibular overjet (β = − 3.182, p = 0.002) remained independently associated with lower OES scores, whereas gender, age, and education level were not independently associated with subjective esthetic satisfaction. These findings indicate that greater objective malocclusion severity is associated with poorer self-perceived orofacial esthetics and support incorporating patient-reported esthetic assessments alongside normative clinical indices in orthodontic evaluation and treatment planning.

Article.Title: Nanoscale imaging resolves canonical topology and intracellular dynamics of SUN5/SPAG4L during mammalian spermiogenesis
Article.Authors: Herold L.; Thoma H.; Thielemann N.; Strissel C.; Daube A.; Braune S.; Alsheimer M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract SUN-domain proteins are core components of LINC complexes that connect the cytoskeleton to the nucleus across the nuclear envelope. SUN5 is a testis-specific SUN-domain protein essential for anchoring the sperm tail to the nucleus, but its functional organization remained controversial, with previous reports suggesting that SUN5 represents an exception to the canonical topology of SUN-domain proteins. Here, we analyzed SUN5 organization during mammalian spermiogenesis using ultrastructure expansion microscopy (U-ExM), Tokuyasu immunogold labeling, and complementary biochemical assays. We show that SUN5 adopts a canonical SUN-domain protein topology at the head-to-tail junction and present a refined model of SUN5 positioning within the nuclear envelope. Stage-resolved U-ExM further reveals SUN5 redistribution including enrichment at the microtubule manchette and the perinuclear ring (PNR), suggesting additional roles in manchette-associated processes. Together, these findings clarify SUN5 topology and localization and provide a framework for understanding its function during mammalian spermiogenesis.

Article.Title: Inflammatory biomarkers, stroke severity, and 1-month outcomes in minor acute ischaemic stroke by small-vessel occlusion status
Article.Authors: Ünal E.; Kılıç C.; Bildirici S.; Aydın T.; Kızılkılıç E.; Issı E.
Article.Abstract: The prognostic value of systemic inflammatory biomarkers in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains controversial, particularly regarding whether these markers provide information beyond established clinical predictors. In addition, potential differences across stroke aetiological subtypes have not been fully clarified. We examined admission C-reactive protein (CRP), ferritin, and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) in predominantly minor acute ischaemic stroke (AIS), with exploration by small-vessel occlusion (SVO) status. This prospective single-centre study included 64 patients (36 SVO, 28 non-SVO; median admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS], 2). Correlations underwent Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment. Separate Poisson and Firth models assessed 1-month NIHSS and modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0–1 versus 2–6, with and without admission NIHSS. In SVO, CRP correlated with admission NIHSS (ρ = 0.431, q = 0.020), 1-month NIHSS (ρ = 0.439, q = 0.020), and admission mRS (ρ = 0.468, q = 0.012); CRP–1-month mRS did not meet the adjusted threshold (q = 0.058). In non-SVO, CRP correlated with ferritin (ρ = 0.507, q = 0.025), but no biomarker–clinical score correlation survived adjustment. Multivariable models detected no biomarker association with either outcome; 11 of 64 patients (17.2%) had a 1-month mRS score of 2–6. Admission NIHSS was associated with 1-month NIHSS (mean ratios, 1.30–1.32) and mRS 2–6 (odds ratios, 2.25–2.32; all p < 0.001). CRP correlated with baseline neurological severity and 1-month NIHSS within the SVO group, although this study could not establish whether these associations differed by TOAST subtype. Admission NIHSS was consistently associated with both 1-month outcomes. Article.Title: Eye-state-dependent reorganization of EEG microstates in a pediatric transdiagnostic cohort
Article.Authors: Xu O.; Sun X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Resting electroencephalography (EEG) is sensitive to eye condition, yet the reorganization of pediatric EEG microstates between eyes-closed (EC) and eyes-open (EO) rest remains incompletely characterized. Paired EC and EO recordings from 110 children in the Healthy Brain Network were analyzed using polarity-invariant two-level clustering, backfitting, and within-participant tests of microstate duration, coverage, occurrence, and transition measures. Eye opening shortened A and C segments, increased the occurrence of all four K = 4 classes, and redistributed coverage from C toward B. All eight significant K = 4 temporal effects retained their direction after participant-wise duration matching and template re-estimation, and broad state sensitivity was also observed at K = 6. Change-score and baseline-adjusted analyses yielded comparable EC-to-EO response profiles among the comparison group without the target diagnoses, ADHD-only group, and ADHD+Anxiety group. The association between posterior alpha reactivity and switching varied in magnitude and direction across segmentation specifications. A stable fourth K = 4 map showed little correspondence with adult microstate D, whereas a D-like map emerged at K = 6. Pediatric microstate measures reflect both physiological context and analytical definition; eye condition, model order, temporal smoothing, and analyzed duration should therefore be specified explicitly in developmental and clinical studies.

Article.Title: Enhanced dielectric properties and alignment behavior of ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals in the non-polar nematic phase.
Article.Authors: Stedman B.; D’Alessandro G.; Kula P.; Kaczmarek M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals (FNLCs) combine long-range orientational order with macroscopic polarization. While their ferroelectric nematic phase has attracted considerable attention, the extent to which its polar character influences the non-polar nematic phase is not yet fully understood. Here, we investigate the non-polar nematic phase of the ferroelectric nematic mixture (MIX NF-P1) that emerges above 44 $$^\circ$$ C. In particular, we determine this liquid crystal interaction with alignment substrates by characterising the pretilt and polar anchoring. The pretilt is found to decrease with increasing temperature, while the polar anchoring remains strong throughout the non-polar nematic phase. Through dielectric and optical characterization, we also extract the dielectric coefficients, birefringence, voltage threshold, and the splay and bend elastic constants as a function of temperature. The voltage threshold is shown to be up to 20 times lower than in the conventional nematic liquid crystal E7, because the large dielectric anisotropy is retained in the non-polar nematic phase. The birefringence monotonically decreases with increasing temperature, while the elastic constants show temperature dependent behaviour consistent with trends reported for other FNLCs. This behavior differs markedly from those observed in conventional nematics, with the splay elastic constant remaining relatively constant. Thus, we demonstrate that the nematic phase of FNLCs cannot be regarded as a conventional nematic state and instead retains signatures of the underlying polar interactions. The combination of strong dielectric response and a low threshold voltage highlights the potential of these materials for high-speed electro-optic and photonic applications.

Article.Title: Intermittent cyclophosphamide therapy exerts distinct cancer cell-intrinsic and stromal cell-dependent effects in a murine model of triple-negative breast cancer
Article.Authors: Zuo L.; Sun M.; Ge J.; Zhou C.; Wu T.; Zhou X.; Ni S.
Article.Abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) poses a formidable clinical challenge. Previous studies have suggested that intermittent cyclophosphamide (CTX) treatment can produce significant anti-tumor effects while minimizing adverse side effects; however, the underlying mechanisms are only partially understood. In this study, we established a therapeutic model of intermittent CTX treatment in a murine orthotopic model of TNBC (4T1) and investigated its impact on the tumor microenvironment (TME) in vivo. High-dose (HD) and low-dose (LD) intermittent CTX regimens were administered. While the LD regimen was better tolerated, it was less effective in inhibiting tumor growth. Integrated bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing of tumor tissues revealed that CTX treatment not only inhibited cancer cell proliferation but also remodeled the TME by recruiting and reprogramming various immune cells, thereby enhancing the anti-tumor immune response in a dose-dependent manner. Our findings elucidate both cancer cell-intrinsic and stroma-dependent mechanisms of CTX action, highlighting potential targets for overcoming the translational limitations of intermittent CTX regimens in TNBC chemo-immunotherapy.

Article.Title: Attitudes to genetic testing and reproductive interventions among patients with inherited retinal disease in Singapore
Article.Authors: Ng J.; Seah N.; Tang R.; See A.; Kee K.; Han N.; Li J.; Ng L.; Ang C.; Tan A.; Tan T.; Fenwick E.; Lamoureux E.; Willis T.; Fenner B.
Article.Abstract: This study assesses the understanding and attitudes of patients with inherited retinal disease (IRD) towards genetic testing and its application towards reproductive interventions in Singapore. This is a previously uninvestigated group, who may benefit from increased uptake of genetic testing. In this cross-sectional study, patients were recruited via Singapore National Eye Centre (SNEC) and its satellite clinics to answer closed- and open-ended questions about their understanding and attitudes towards genetic testing. Multivariable logistic regression models assessed the adjusted associations between patients’ attitudes towards different applications of genetic testing. Thematic coding and tabulation of frequency were performed for qualitative content analysis. Of 216 participants (median age 57.5 years; 50.9% male, 85.6% Chinese), most had a favorable view of genetic testing (62.5%), and its application to reproductive interventions (preimplantation genetic testing = 56.5%; prenatal testing = 58.8%), despite variable self-reported understanding. Better self-reported understanding was positively associated with support (OR 3.24; 95% CI 1.4, 7.5; p = 0.006), financial coverage (OR 3.29; 95% CI 1.4, 7.9; p = 0.008) and universal availability (OR 4.44; 95% CI 1.8, 10.7; p < 0.001) of genetic testing for patients with IRD. Chinese ethnicity (OR 2.50; 95% CI 1.1, 5.8; p = 0.033), younger age (< 50 years; OR 2.52; 95% CI 1.3, 4.7; p = 0.004), and positive family history (OR 2.03; 95% CI 1.1, 3.8; p = 0.025) were associated with increased support of genetic testing for preimplantation genetic testing. Singaporeans with IRD expressed broad support for genetic testing and its reproductive applications. Education and tailored genetic counselling for patients with poorer levels of understanding could increase uptake and perceived utility of genetic testing.

Article.Title: Effect of chitosan/graphene quantum dot/stem cell-derived exosome nanocomposite hydrogel on inflammation and neuronal preservation in spinal cord injury
Article.Authors: Karami F.; Pooyan P.; Akbari-Gharalari N.; Bayat K.; Zomorrod M.; Mahmoudifard M.; Nemati A.; Adibi A.; Zali H.; Niknam Z.; Hosseinzadeh S.
Article.Abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is associated with persistent inflammation, neuronal damage, and impaired functional recovery. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a thermosensitive chitosan/graphene quantum dot/stem cell-derived exosome (CS-GQD-Exo) nanocomposite hydrogel with potential for injectable application in SCI treatment. CS, CS-GQD, CS-Exo, and CS-GQD-Exo hydrogels were prepared and characterized for their physicochemical properties, cytocompatibility, swelling, degradation, mechanical properties, and exosome release. Their therapeutic effects were subsequently evaluated in a mouse model of SCI using behavioral, histological, immunofluorescence, and inflammatory assessments. All hydrogel formulations exhibited a porous structure and supported PC12 cell viability. The wet CS hydrogel exhibited compressive properties suitable for the spinal cord tissue environment. The CS-GQD-Exo hydrogel showed sustained exosome release over 21 days, with a cumulative release of 274.13 ± 1.06 µg/mL. In vivo, CS-GQD-Exo produced the greatest improvement in locomotor recovery, with significantly higher BBB scores than the other treatment groups. It also markedly reduced serum IL-6 and TNF-α levels to 82.09 and 1.17 pg/mL, respectively. Histological analysis demonstrated reduced lesion formation, while NeuN immunoreactivity was highest in the CS-GQD-Exo group, indicating enhanced neuronal preservation. The CS-GQD-Exo nanocomposite hydrogel demonstrated the most favorable overall therapeutic performance among the tested formulations by combining sustained exosome delivery with improved functional recovery, reduced inflammation, and enhanced tissue and neuronal preservation. These findings support its potential as an injectable platform for SCI repair.

Article.Title: Accelerated CO2 curing of fly ash–GGBS self-compacting geopolymer concrete: experimental, environmental and explainable machine learning assessment
Article.Authors: Joseph H.; Padavala S.; Flores E.; Maureira-Carsalade N.; Gashe A.; Avudaiappan S.
Article.Abstract: The construction industry is under increasing pressure to develop sustainable cement-free materials with lower carbon emissions and enhanced durability. In this study, a high-performance self-compacting geopolymer concrete (SCGC) was developed using Fly Ash (FA) and Ground Granulated Blast Furnace Slag (GGBS) as binder precursors, combined with accelerated CO 2 curing to improve engineering performance and environmental sustainability. Five binder compositions with varying FA-to-GGBS ratios were prepared under ambient and carbon curing conditions, resulting in ten experimental mixtures. The fresh properties of the developed mixtures were evaluated according to EFNARC guidelines, while mechanical performance was assessed through compressive, split tensile, and flexural strength tests at 7, 28, and 56 days. Durability performance was investigated using water absorption, sorptivity, acid resistance, and sulfate resistance tests. Carbon sequestration behavior was quantified through mass gain analysis, while microstructural evolution was examined using Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy (EDS), X-Ray Diffraction (XRD), and Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR). The environmental performance of the developed SCGC mixtures was evaluated through cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment (LCA) using openLCA. In addition, machine learning (ML) models including Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Random Forest (RF), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) were developed to predict compressive strength. The results demonstrated that accelerated CO₂ curing significantly enhanced the fresh, mechanical, and durability performance of SCGC. Among all investigated mixtures, the M3-C mixture exhibited the optimum performance, achieving a compressive strength of 68.4 MPa at 56 days along with significantly reduced water absorption and sorptivity. Microstructural investigations confirmed enhanced geopolymerization, pore refinement, and carbonate formation in carbon-cured mixtures. LCA revealed that M3-C exhibited the lowest global warming potential (148.8 kg CO 2 -eq/m 3 ), low embodied energy (2384 MJ/m 3 ), and the lowest carbon intensity (2.38 kg CO 2 /MPa·m 3 ) among all investigated mixtures. ML analysis demonstrated excellent predictive capability, with XGBoost showing the highest prediction accuracy (R 2 = 0.983). The integrated experimental, microstructural, environmental, and data-driven findings confirm that carbon-cured slag-modified SCGC has strong potential as a sustainable next-generation construction material for low-carbon infrastructure applications.

Article.Title: Multi-objective casualty distribution and real-time coordinated transportation scheduling of emergency medical materials
Article.Authors: Wan M.; Yang F.; Ye C.; Dong J.
Article.Abstract: In recent years, the frequent occurrence of emergencies has resulted in substantial casualties, rendering traditional unidirectional forward rescue models inadequate to cope with the sudden surge in demand for emergency medical materials. Differentiated rescue strategies for different casualty categories can mitigate the surge in emergency medical materials demand, while coordinated forward and reverse rescue integrating casualty allocation and emergency medical material scheduling can reduce deprivation cost and optimize resource allocation. This paper proposes a differentiated rescue strategy that accounts for various types of casualties. We also establish a multi-objective casualty distribution and coordinated transportation scheduling of emergency medical materials model for bidirectional rescue to minimize rescue costs, in which a multimodal transportation strategy is incorporated. To solve this multi-objective problem, we propose an improved hybrid multi-objective Harris hawks-whale optimization algorithm (HMOHH-WOA). Experimental results show that the HMOHH-WOA algorithm achieves better convergence and diversity in the solution set compared to the five multi-objective algorithms when solving this problem. Finally, we demonstrate through case studies that the proposed research problem and solution algorithm can improve the utilization efficiency of emergency medical materials and reduce deprivation cost through better resource allocation.
