Article.Title: Impact of medical law education based on the IRAC model on the medical law reasoning of internal medicine and surgery residents
Article.Authors: Abdi M.; Norouzi A.; Mafinejad M.
Article.Abstract: Medical-legal challenges have intensified over the past decade, leading to substantial financial burdens and psychological distress for physicians. Literature reviews indicate that the medical law skills of specialists and residents, particularly their medical law reasoning abilities, are insufficient, underscoring the necessity for appropriate educational interventions. This study aimed to determine the impact of medical law education based on the IRAC (Issue, Rule, Analysis, Conclusion) model on the medical law reasoning of internal medicine and surgery residents at Zanjan University of Medical Sciences. A quasi-experimental study employing a non-randomized control group with a pretest-posttest design was conducted. The ADDIE model guided the design of the educational intervention. Residents were non-randomly assigned to an intervention group ( n = 27) receiving IRAC-based training and a control group ( n = 27) receiving no such training. Attitudes toward medical law reasoning were assessed using the Medical Law Reasoning Attitude Questionnaire (MLRAQ), while cognitive medical law reasoning was assessed using the participant-completed, scenario-based Medical Law Reasoning Skill Test (MLRST), which measures respondents’ reasoning judgments in hypothetical medico-legal scenarios. Data were analyzed using independent t-test, paired t-test, Chi-square, and Welch. No statistically significant differences were observed between the groups in baseline total attitude scores ( P = 0.213) or total medical law reasoning skill scores ( P = 0.572). Posttest results, however, revealed significant differences favoring the intervention group in total attitude scores (101.48 ± 9.32 vs. 82.63 ± 13.08; P < 0.001) and all its subscales. Similarly, the intervention group demonstrated significantly higher total medical law reasoning skill scores posttest (79.00 ± 8.27 vs. 58.81 ± 7.39; P < 0.001) across all subscales. The primary between-group analysis of pretest-to-posttest change confirmed these improvements for both outcomes ( P < 0.001), and supplementary Welch’s tests on posttest scores were consistent. The IRAC-based medical law education intervention was associated with significant improvements in residents’ measured attitudes and cognitive reasoning scores. This model offers a practical framework for medical educators and curriculum planners to employ creative, integrated, model-based, and active learning strategies to enhance legal reasoning competencies. Ultimately, fostering these skills may help reduce future legal disputes, mitigate physicians’ criminal and civil liabilities, and ensure better adherence to patient rights.

Article.Title: Evaluation of cytotoxic potential of phytochemicals identified from Gymnostachyum febrifugum roots and deciphering the molecular mechanism using in vitro and in silico analysis
Article.Authors: Spandana K.; Chandana A.; Poojary B.; Bhagya N.
Article.Abstract: Gymnostachyum febrifugum , an ethnomedicinal plant with antioxidant, hepatoprotective, anti-inflammatory and cytotoxic potential against breast and lung cancers. The present study was planned to identify and characterise cytotoxic phytochemicals from the G. febrifugum root ethyl acetate extract and its fractions to understand the possible molecular mechanisms of action of these phytochemicals using in vitro and in silico analyses against breast cancer. The study involves the bioassay-guided fractionation of cytotoxic phytochemicals from the G. febrifugum root ethyl acetate extract using column chromatography. Cytotoxicity was evaluated using 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide, clonogenic and scratch assays. Additionally, induction of cell death, ROS production, and regulation of the cell cycle and apoptosis were assessed by fluorescent staining, flow cytometry, and immunoblotting. The phytochemicals in the cytotoxic fractions were characterised spectroscopically, and their molecular targets were identified from network pharmacology. The cytotoxic effect of the ethyl acetate fractions (GF1-GF4) evaluated against MCF7 cells showed IC 50 values ranging from 54.64 ± 1.99 to 84.47 ± 1.0 µg/mL. Clonogenic, scratch, and live-dead assay also confirmed the significant ( p < 0.001) cytotoxic potential of GF2 and GF3 fractions. The identification and characterisation of the phytochemicals in the cytotoxic GF2 and GF3 fractions using GC-MS/MS and HR-LCMS/MS analysis revealed the presence of 2,4-di-tert-butylphenol (2,4-DTBP) (GF2) and kalopanax saponin C (GF3), which might have contributed to generating cytosolic ROS, G1 phase arrest and enhanced level of caspase 3 as observed in the molecular mechanism-based studies. Further, the in silico analysis using a network pharmacology approach identified HSD11B1, NRIH3, PTGS1, UGT2B7, AR, BCL2L1, GLI1, JUN and F2 as the major protein targets for 2,4-DTBP and kalopanax saponin C, all of which require further experimental validation.

Article.Title: Mobile health application for adherence and symptom management in hemodialysis patients: a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Demir Ö.; Yılmaz Karabulutlu E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hemodialysis patients experience a heavy symptom burden that can undermine treatment adherence. This randomized controlled trial evaluated whether a mobile application-based training and counseling intervention reduces symptom burden and supports adherence. Sixty-eight patients at two hemodialysis centers in eastern Turkey were randomly allocated to intervention or routine care (n = 34 each). The application included five educational modules with text, images, and videos, two daily automated reminders, and researcher counseling provided within 8 h of a patient’s request. The primary outcome was symptom burden (Dialysis Symptom Index), the secondary outcome adherence (End-Stage Renal Disease Adherence Questionnaire); clinical, dialysis-related and biochemical parameters were exploratory. All 68 participants completed the 8-week follow-up. After adjustment for baseline values, symptom burden was lower (adjusted mean difference − 14.64, 95% confidence interval (CI) − 20.36 to − 8.92, P < 0.001) and adherence scores higher (75.24, 95% CI 28.04 to 122.44, P = 0.002) in the intervention group. Exploratory analyses favored the intervention for interdialytic weight gain (− 0.48 kg, P < 0.001), ultrafiltration volume (− 449.11 mL, P < 0.001), phosphorus (− 1.20 mg/dL, P = 0.017) and weight (− 0.62 kg, P = 0.003). Mobile application-based training and counseling may reduce symptom burden and support adherence; exploratory findings require confirmation in larger trials. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05322291.

Article.Title: GeoCTGAN generates privacy-aware geosynthetic event data
Article.Authors: Abdullah A.; Law J.; Sun S.; Hu B.; Layton A.; Chen H.
Article.Abstract: High-resolution spatial event data are valuable for urban research but difficult to release because of privacy and disclosure risk. GeoCTGAN combines road-network discretization, DeepWalk topology embeddings, globally pooled conditional CTGAN generation and Capacitated k -Nearest Neighbour (CaNN) reconstruction to produce privacy-aware geosynthetic data. Using crime data for the City of Toronto, GeoCTGAN-Full, prioritizing micro-scale spatial fidelity for restricted use, and GeoCTGAN-Priv, incorporating additional privacy protections for more open release, preserved broad spatial structure in the real data, as evidenced by KDE-surface correlations of 0.9976 and 0.9913 and Dissemination Area (DA) count correlations of 0.8919 and 0.8491, respectively. DA maps and LISA classifications were highly concordant with held-out data, while Global Moran’s I retained the same positive spatial-autocorrelation pattern. Temporal evaluation showed close preservation of crime-category and hour-of-day composition across month boundaries. Privacy diagnostics were also strong, with DCR Overfitting Protection score near 0.99 and Disclosure Protection Estimate near 0.73. GeoCTGAN provided a stronger spatial-fidelity and privacy balance than most tabular and spatial-resampling benchmarks. Ablations showed that capacity-constrained CaNN reconstruction was especially important, with topology-based components contributing to finer-scale structure. Multi-seed robustness and unchanged-configuration application to a supplementary second city analysis (City of Ottawa) supported reproducibility and cross-city transferability.

Article.Title: AIT2-FRL: offline PPO-optimized interval type-2 fuzzy scheduling for fair and sustainable fog–cloud systems
Article.Authors: Moazzami S.; Mirzaei A.; Aminian M.; Karimi R.; Mikaeilvand N.
Article.Abstract: Fog–cloud systems support latency-sensitive Internet of Things applications, but heterogeneous and time-varying resources make task scheduling a multi-objective problem. Nodes differ in processing speed, power demand, network delay, failure tendency, and carbon intensity, while tasks vary in urgency and resource requirements. Existing heuristics encode limited trade-offs, population-based optimizers may require repeated search, and direct reinforcement-learning schedulers can obscure deployment-time decisions. This study proposes AIT2–FRL, a two-phase scheduler for independent fog–cloud tasks that combines interval Type-2 fuzzy inference with offline proximal policy optimization. The fuzzy layer represents uncertainty in urgency, congestion, and carbon conditions, establishes a one-time task order, and generates context-dependent weights for makespan, energy, carbon emissions, unreliability, and load imbalance. PPO is used only during offline training to calibrate membership functions and weighting parameters; the validation-selected checkpoint is then frozen. During deployment, feasible nodes are ranked through a deterministic weighted score with linear complexity in the number of candidates. Evaluation covers six workload sizes, 17 matched holdout seeds, four baselines, ablations, sensitivity and convergence analyses, and resource pools up to 256 nodes under common traces and constraints. AIT2–FRL achieved the best mean value for all five primary objectives at every workload, with statistical support at all workloads except unreliability at the smallest size. Secondary response-time and runtime results show that these gains do not extend to every operational measure.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: proximal policy optimization; energy efficiency; offline reinforcement learning; multi-objective optimization; load balancing; CO2 emissions
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Computer Networks and Communications > IoT and Edge/Fog Computing; Computer Science > Information Systems > Cloud Computing and Resource Management; Computer Science > Hardware and Architecture > Energy Efficiency in Computing

Article.Title: Physiological and biochemical responses of facultative halophytes to differential hydroponic solution salinities
Article.Authors: Khan A.; Pukalskas A.; Samuolienė G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Salinity is a major abiotic stressor limiting crop production globally. Unlike obligate halophytes, facultative halophytes adapt to saline environments by enhancing their secondary metabolism, particularly under moderate salinity, offering great potential for Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA). However, the metabolic thresholds of specific edible halophytes under hydroponic salinity management remain unclear. To evaluate their growth performance, osmolytes, and antioxidant activity in CEA, we hypothesized that moderate salinity would stimulate antioxidant and soluble carbohydrate accumulation without severely compromising growth parameters: two facultative Amaranthaceae species, Chenopodium giganteum D. Don and Amaranthus tricolor cv. Red Aztec, were grown in a deep-water culture system tested with different salinity levels (0, 150, and 300 mM NaCl). Our study revealed that increased salinity resulted in declines in growth rate, leaf area, and dry weight, whereas leaf mass and leaf area mass increased, indicating structural adaptations. Salinity triggered metabolic processes to increase glucose and fructose concentrations, indicating salinity-associated metabolic responses. Moreover, the responses of maltose and raffinose were species-specific, and the antioxidant patterns varied on an individual basis. Organic acid profiles in response to salinity were also species-specific, revealing divergent metabolite adaptation. 150 mM NaCl partially maintained growth relative to 300 mM but did not fully preserve it compared with the control, and increased metabolite accumulation, whereas DPPH rose with increasing salinity level. TPC showed no significant change, while FRAP increased at 150 mM NaCl in A. tricolor . Our research findings revealed that the tested species exhibited salinity-dependent changes in selected metabolites and antioxidant activity, and that 150 mM NaCl was not lethal to either species.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: Amaranthus tricolor; facultative halophyte; maltose; organic acids; salt stress; Chenopodium giganteum; soluble sugars; osmolytes; raffinose; controlled environment agriculture; antioxidant activity; deep water culture

Article.Title: Antimicrobial effectiveness of passive ultrasonic irrigation following preparation with single-file and multi-file NiTi instrumentation systems in flattened root canals
Article.Authors: de Souza P.; Reddy D.; Machado R.; Camargo E.; Ignácio S.; Carneiro E.; da Silva Neto U.
Article.Abstract: Effective disinfection of the root canal system (RCS) depends on the interaction between mechanical preparation and irrigation protocols, particularly in anatomically complex root canals. The influence of passive ultrasonic irrigation (PUI) on antimicrobial outcomes following preparation with single-file nickel–titanium reciprocating file systems (SNTRFSs) or multi-file nickel–titanium rotary file systems (MNTRFSs) in flattened root canals remains unclear. The objective of this ex vivo study was to evaluate the antimicrobial effectiveness of PUI in flattened root canals previously prepared with an MNTRFS—ProTaper Universal (Dentsply-Maillefer, Ballaigues, Switzerland)—or an SNTRFS—Reciproc (VDW GmbH, Munich, Germany)—and contaminated with Enterococcus faecalis . Initially, 60 mandibular central incisors with flattened root canals were randomly allocated to two instrumentation groups ( n = 30 each). After 21 days of bacterial contamination, specimens from each instrumentation group were randomly assigned to one of three final irrigation protocols (FIPs) ( n = 10): (1) distilled water activated by PUI, (2) 2.5% sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) activated by PUI, or (3) conventional syringe irrigation (CSI) using 2.5% NaOCl. Bacterial metabolic activity before and after irrigation was assessed using an MTT assay, and the percentage reduction in bacterial metabolic activity was calculated from changes in optical density. Data were analyzed using one-way ANOVA and Tukey’s post hoc test (α = 0.05). Groups treated with PUI generally exhibited greater reductions in bacterial metabolic activity than those treated with CSI ( P < 0.05). The combination of the MNTRFS with 2.5% NaOCl and PUI yielded the greatest mean reduction in bacterial metabolic activity, whereas the lowest antimicrobial effect was observed in specimens instrumented with the SNTRFS and treated with 2.5% NaOCl using CSI. Although all the FIPs reduced bacterial metabolic activity, residual activity remained detectable in all groups. Within the limitations of this ex vivo study, PUI was associated with greater reductions in bacterial metabolic activity under standardized laboratory conditions, particularly after preparation with the evaluated MNTRFS. However, complete bacterial inactivation was not achieved with any of the evaluated FIPs.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: passive ultrasonic irrigation; antimicrobial efficacy; root canal instrumentation; root canal disinfection

Article.Title: An experimentally calibrated MBD–DEM framework for ice fracture, fragmentation, and dispensing in a refrigerator ice maker
Article.Authors: Park S.; Jeon S.; Park J.; Park M.; Kim Y.; Lee J.
Article.Abstract: In the highly competitive home appliance market, the dispensing and crushing performance of built-in ice makers has become a critical quality attribute affecting both user satisfaction and product competitiveness. However, conventional product development processes still rely heavily on reactive trial-and-error approaches, which may lead to substantial economic losses during the later stages of mass production. Ice is a complex material whose mechanical properties and failure behavior are highly sensitive to initial conditions, including temperature, geometry, and porosity. Therefore, a high-fidelity numerical model capable of accurately representing these characteristics is essential. This study proposes a discrete element method (DEM)-based modeling methodology for constructing an ice block model that captures realistic mechanical behavior. Physical property data were obtained from cubic ice samples produced using an actual ice maker, and the DEM model was subsequently refined through a systematic parameter validation procedure. Furthermore, a coupled simulation framework integrating multibody dynamics (MBD) and DEM was established to quantitatively predict the performance of two primary operating modes: Cube Mode, in which ice is dispensed without fragmentation, and Crush Mode, in which ice is fragmented prior to discharge. By evaluating ice mass flow and crushing characteristics in a virtual environment representative of actual operating conditions, the proposed framework enables predictive performance assessment during the product design stage. The developed approach provides a robust analytical basis for improving the design and performance evaluation of ice dispensing and crushing mechanisms.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: ice fragmentation; discrete element method; ice fracture; multibody dynamics
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Mechanics of Materials > Numerical methods in engineering; Engineering > Computational Mechanics > Granular flow and fluidized beds; Engineering > Mechanics of Materials > Rock Mechanics and Modeling

Article.Title: Deformation and failure mechanisms and active–passive coordinated support of roadways subjected to repeated mining disturbances
Article.Authors: Wei Y.; Li Z.; Shan R.; Wang H.; Wang H.; Yu S.; Chen L.; Cao C.
Article.Abstract: The failure mechanisms and support control of roadways subjected to repeated mining disturbances remain critical challenges in underground close-distance coal seam mining. This study investigates the effects of the mining coefficient and support resistance on the plastic zone distribution of surrounding rock in roadways subjected to repeated mining disturbances through field investigation, theoretical analysis, numerical simulation, similarity modeling, and engineering practice. An active–passive coordinated support system composed of bolt–cable support (active support) and a steel beam–concrete-filled steel tube (CFST) composite frame (passive support) is proposed and verified through field application. The results indicate that the plastic zone of surrounding rock continuously develops and expands under repeated mining disturbances. The mining coefficient is identified as a key parameter controlling the extent of the plastic zone, whereas increasing passive support resistance effectively restrains its development. Based on these findings, a steel beam–CFST composite frame is developed as the passive support structure. Parametric analyses using ABAQUS are conducted to evaluate the influence of steel pipe diameter, wall thickness, and steel beam length on the stress–strain behavior of the support system. Optimized design parameters suitable for engineering applications are proposed, forming an active–passive coordinated support system together with bolt–cable support. Similarity model tests of the active–passive coordinated support scheme demonstrate that the composite frame possesses adequate load-bearing capacity while accommodating controlled deformation of the roof and surrounding rock. Under the coordinated action of bolt–cable support and the steel beam–CFST composite frame, the stability of roadways subjected to repeated mining disturbances is significantly improved. Compared with the original support scheme, roof subsidence, sidewall convergence, and floor heave are reduced by 37.4%, 17.8%, and 40.4%, respectively. The proposed active–passive coordinated support system has been successfully applied in field engineering and achieved satisfactory control of roadway deformation.

Article.Title: Development and exploratory feasibility of a social cognitive theory-based family intergenerational support intervention for rural older adults with cognitive impairment
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Gong Y.; Hu D.; Yang X.; Wang J.; Duan Y.
Article.Abstract: Guided by Social Cognitive Theory (SCT) as the theoretical framework and family-based intergenerational support as the implementation pathway, this study developed a family-based intergenerational support intervention for rural older adults with cognitive impairment. An exploratory feasibility pilot study was subsequently conducted. It described recruitment and retention, completion of assessment procedures, family participation, and implementation challenges. The findings were used to inform further protocol refinement and future feasibility research. The intervention was developed based on the core mechanisms of Social Cognitive Theory, including self-efficacy, observational learning, behavioral reinforcement, and environmental support, through a literature review, research team discussions, and two rounds of Delphi expert consultation. The intervention comprised three modules: self-management, psychological intervention, and cognitive training. Representative activities included walking, looking at old photographs, everyday-life calculation tasks, and memory training. Under the guidance of healthcare professionals, younger-generation family members were intended to support patients’ participation in the planned activities through companionship, reminders, demonstrations, joint activities, and feedback recording. From June to July 2026, eight rural older adults with cognitive impairment admitted to Fuyang Third People’s Hospital were recruited using purposive sampling. Each participant was enrolled together with one younger-generation family member who was primarily involved in their care, and all dyads took part in a 2-week pilot study. Two nurses documented patient participation, available information on task implementation, and family-member feedback through WeChat communication, observations during intervention delivery, and follow-up. A researcher-developed four-item family feedback form was used to assess overall satisfaction, understanding and implementation of the intervention content, willingness to participate in future research, and satisfaction with the research staff’s service attitude. Open-ended questions were used to collect family-reported patient activity preferences and suggestions for intervention refinement. The Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), 15-item Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS-15), and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) were administered to document completion of the assessment procedures, and the data were analyzed descriptively. The effective response rates of the two rounds of expert consultation were 100.0% and 94.4%, respectively, and the coefficients of expert authority were 0.79 and 0.85, respectively. In the second round, the mean importance scores of items at all levels ranged from 4.53 to 4.94, and the mean operability scores of tertiary-level items ranged from 4.18 to 4.82. Kendall’s coefficients of concordance for the importance ratings of items at all levels and the operability ratings of tertiary-level items were 0.591 and 0.617, respectively (both P < 0.001). After two rounds of expert consultation, a modular pilot intervention protocol was developed, consisting of 3 primary items, 12 secondary items, and 34 tertiary items. During the recruitment phase, 10 eligible individuals were screened, of whom 8 were enrolled, resulting in an enrollment rate of 80.0%. All 8 enrolled participants remained in the 2-week pilot study period and completed pre- and post-pilot assessments, yielding a retention rate and assessment completion rate of 100.0%. All 8 younger-generation family members participated in the family support process during the 2-week pilot study and primarily provided assistance through companionship, reminders, task demonstrations, and process documentation. In the family feedback questionnaire, the mean scores for the four items—research staff attitude, overall satisfaction, understanding and implementation of intervention content, and willingness to participate in future studies—were 4.50 ± 0.53, 4.00 ± 0.53, 3.63 ± 0.52, and 3.88 ± 0.83, respectively. Feedback from implementing nurses indicated that the intervention protocol was characterized by modular design, integration of tasks into daily life, and family involvement. However, several implementation challenges were identified, including insufficient guidance strategies for family members, difficulties in understanding some tasks, and limited availability of family time. Based on pilot feedback, the research team refined the implementation methods, task difficulty, scheduling arrangements, and process documentation procedures for selected tertiary items while maintaining the overall intervention framework and primary intervention components unchanged. This study developed a preliminary family-based intergenerational support intervention for rural older adults with cognitive impairment and conducted an exploratory feasibility pilot study. The pilot study described recruitment and retention, completion of assessment procedures, family participation, and implementation-related challenges. Feedback from younger-generation family members and observations by implementing nurses indicated that further refinement is needed regarding task comprehension, family guidance strategies, and time arrangements. These findings only reflect the specific process indicators and implementation experiences observed in this sample and cannot establish the overall feasibility of the intervention, patient acceptability, or intervention effectiveness. The refined intervention protocol requires further examination in larger samples, diverse family contexts, and studies incorporating standardized process evaluations.

Article.Title: Kaiser window-based S-transform for vibration signal denoising in rolling bearing fault diagnosis
Article.Authors: Vaziri Sarashk M.; Shahnazari M.; Saeedi-Sourck H.
Article.Abstract: Vibration signal analysis is widely used for bearing fault diagnosis in rotating machinery, but the presence of strong background noise often masks fault-related features, reducing diagnostic accuracy. To address this issue, this paper proposes a noise removal method based on the Kaiser window S-transform (KST), in which the signal is windowed over time using a variable Kaiser window. The Fourier transform is then applied to the windowed signal, yielding a three-dimensional S-transform comprising time, frequency, and transform amplitude. Then, a soft thresholding method is applied to the S-transform for denoising, and finally, the denoised time-domain signal is obtained using the inverse transform. To evaluate the proposed denoising method, it is applied to the experimental bearing vibration signal from a rotating machine. Following denoising, kurtosis is used for fault detection, and the envelope spectrum is used to identify the fault type. Finally, the study compares soft and hard thresholding for noise removal using KST, compares KST with Wavelet Thresholding (WT) under various conditions—including colored noise at different Signal-to-Noise Ratios (SNRs)—and performs fault detection using a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier. The results show that the proposed method effectively removes noise while enhancing fault-related features in the signal.

Article.Title: TLR4/NF-κB signaling in polystyrene nanoparticle-induced endometrial injury: evidence from transcriptomic profiling and pharmacological inhibition
Article.Authors: Luo X.; Mu S.; Shen H.; Wang L.; Zhang Q.; Jia T.; Zhang X.
Article.Abstract: Polystyrene nanoparticles (PS-NPs) have raised concerns regarding female reproductive toxicity, yet their endometrial effects and underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Primary human endometrial stromal cells (hESCs) and a mouse exposure model were used to characterize PS-NP-associated injury and changes in receptivity-related markers. Exploratory transcriptomic profiling in hESCs was followed by targeted evaluation of TLR4/NF-κB signaling and pharmacological intervention with TAK-242. PS-NP exposure increased reactive oxygen species accumulation, induced mitochondrial membrane depolarization and apoptosis, and reduced HOXA10, FOXO1, and ITGB3 expression in hESCs. Mouse uterine tissue showed concordant apoptosis-related changes and reductions in these proteins, while implantation sites were reduced at the higher PS-NP doses. Transcriptomic profiling highlighted innate immune and inflammatory responses, including Toll-like receptor and NF-κB signaling. Targeted analyses showed increased TLR4 and PTGS2 expression and elevated p-IκBα/IκBα and p-p65/p65 ratios in both models. TAK-242 attenuated NF-κB activation and apoptosis and mitigated reductions in HOXA10, FOXO1, and ITGB3 in hESCs. These findings support a contributory role for TLR4/NF-κB signaling in PS-NP-induced endometrial stromal cell injury and disruption of a receptivity-associated molecular profile.

Article.Title: CCVS-3ASeg: a large-scale contextual auxiliary framework for road crack semantic segmentation in UAV imagery
Article.Authors: Yao C.; Wen N.; Zhang Z.; Chang Y.; Fan Y.
Article.Abstract: Existing road crack inspection using UAVs and vehicle-mounted systems often relies on local field-of-view observations, requiring repeated scanning in large road scenes. We present CCVS-3ASeg, a framework for a preliminary feasibility evaluation of UAV-based large-scale road crack semantic segmentation. Its design focuses on two coupled challenges: computational overhead from large-scale feature representation and loss of fine crack features during spatial compression. CCVS extracts road regions and performs direction-aligned slicing, while 3ASeg uses an Ultra-Lightweight Adversarial Attention Mechanism (Ultra-LAAM) to assist crack-feature representation. Evaluation comprised CCVS road processing on the Custom-Dataset, 3ASeg-assisted segmentation on Crack500 and a selected public-source Crack-Dataset, and a two-image G94 Expressway case study of the connected workflow. Across test images, CCVS achieved recall of 0.9377 ± 0.1517 and pixel accuracy (PA) of 0.9606 ± 0.1010. On Crack500, the largest observed mIoU gain among evaluated 3ASeg-assisted configurations was 6.93 percentage points, and Ultra-LAAM reached 1132.27 ± 18.15 FPS. These component‑level experiments preliminarily demonstrate that large‑scale road extraction to assist pavement crack segmentation is a viable direction for further exploration and optimization.

Article.Title: Balancing yield and wrapper leaf quality in cigar tobacco through data-driven nitrogen management
Article.Authors: Liao S.; Xiong L.; Wang B.; Li X.; Yu J.; Li H.; Yang C.; Rao X.
Article.Abstract: Nitrogen (N) is a vital macronutrient influencing both the yield and quality of cigar tobacco leaves, particularly the high-value wrapper leaves. However, the response of cigar wrapper yield and quality traits to N input remains inconsistent and underexplored. This study aims to identify an optimal N application rate that balances productivity and leaf quality for sustainable cigar wrapper cultivation. A two-year field experiment was conducted using the cigar tobacco cultivar Chuxue 26 to evaluate the effects of six N rates (0–270 kg N/ha) on yield and multiple quality parameters. Results showed that total yield, as well as wrapper and binder yields, increased with N rate, while filler yield declined. N also significantly influenced key quality traits. Apparent quality and oil content initially improved but declined beyond 180 kg N/ha. Leaf thickness increased with N application up to 135 kg N/ha and then declined, while stalk-containing rate and particulate matter content decreased with higher N input. Blade tension peaked at 135 kg N/ha. The potassium-chlorine ratio increased with N application, whereas the glycoalkaloid ratio declined. Using analytic hierarchy process and membership function methods, the optimal N application rate was identified as a local recommendation of 187.4 kg N/ha (recommended range: 170–200 kg N/ha) for the cigar tobacco cultivar Chuxue 26 under the agroecological conditions of northwestern Hubei Province. This rate provides a balanced, data-driven recommendation for enhancing both yield and wrapper quality in cigar tobacco production.

Article.Title: Normal-weight central obesity and cardiometabolic risk among adolescents and young adults in 70 countries
Article.Authors: Aychiluhm S.; Ross A.; Isaac V.; Thapa S.; Ahmed K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Body mass index (BMI) does not capture central adiposity, which raises cardiometabolic risk even at normal BMI. We estimated the prevalence of central obesity and normal-weight central obesity, and their cardiometabolic associations, among adolescents and young adults (15–29 years) in 70 countries using WHO STEPS data (2010–2023; n = 60,618). Central obesity was defined as a waist-to-height ratio ≥ 0.5, and normal-weight central obesity as central obesity with a normal BMI. Prevalence estimates were pooled using a random-effects meta-analysis; multilevel logistic regression examined associated factors and cardiometabolic associations. Pooled prevalence was 42.1% (95% CI 37.9–46.2) for central obesity and 18.8% (95% CI 16.5–21.0) for normal-weight central obesity, with substantial between-country heterogeneity (I 2 = 98.9 and 94.0%, respectively). Compared with normal BMI and no central obesity, normal-weight central obesity was associated with higher odds of hypertension (aOR 1.28, 95% CI 1.15–1.41), diabetes (aOR 1.36, 95% CI 1.08–1.71), and elevated cholesterol (aOR 1.90, 95% CI 1.70–2.13). More than two in five young people had central obesity, including nearly one in five with normal BMI; this phenotype was associated with cardiometabolic risk across income settings. Adding waist-based measures to BMI screening could help identify at-risk young people.

Article.Title: Environmental sensing-based assessment of trees outside forests and land use and land cover change patterns in the Bundelkhand agroforestry landscape
Article.Authors: Samant U.; Dobriyal M.; Sahu S.; Kumar P.; Srivastav M.; Pandey P.; Turyasingura B.; Tiwari P.
Article.Abstract: This study assesses land use and land cover (LULC) dynamics and Trees Outside Forests (TOF) in Lalitpur district, Uttar Pradesh, within the semi-arid Bundelkhand landscape. The study addresses the need to distinguish tree resources occurring outside officially defined forest areas from conventional LULC classes and to examine their spatial significance for land management. Landsat imagery was used to produce LULC maps for 2015, 2020 and 2025 using supervised Maximum Likelihood Classification (MLC), while high-resolution canopy-height data were used to derive total tree cover. A one-hectare circular neighbourhood and a 10% canopy-density threshold were then used to identify forest areas according to the operational framework applied from the Forest Survey of India (FSI), and TOF was estimated as tree cover outside that forest mask. The reported LULC results show an increase in agricultural area from 2,351.29 km² (47%) excluding the drought fallow land (1440 sq km) in 2015 to 3,776.26 km² (74%) in 2020, followed by 3,704.66 km² (72%) in 2025, while open forest declined from 1,383.43 km² (27%) to 417.97 km² (8%). The Forest & tree-cover assessment estimated 203,969 ha (40.34%) of tree cover, of which 63,697 ha (12.60%) met the applied forest-density criterion and 140,272 ha (27.74%) were classified as TOF. These findings indicate that a substantial share of mapped tree cover occurs outside the FSI-defined forest category. The combined LULC and TOF framework provides a spatial basis for agroforestry planning and sustainable land management, while the limitations of MLC, the canopy-height threshold, and the available validation information should be considered when interpreting the estimates.

Article.Title: Probabilistic representation learning of baseline transcriptomes enables prediction and pathway-level interpretation of anticancer drug responses
Article.Authors: Kim H.; Im S.; Kim S.; Han J.; Kim J.; Sim J.; Park S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Baseline transcriptomes can predict anticancer drug response, but their high dimensionality complicates pathway-level interpretation. We developed a probabilistic representation learning framework using a reusable variational autoencoder (VAE) latent space to prioritize response-associated factors by aggregate importance and drug preferentiality. Across five reference drugs, leakage-free repeated cross-validation showed that gene-level Ridge regression performed best, whereas 64-dimensional latent representations retained predictive signal after compression. In a separate interpretation VAE fitted to 939 cancer cell lines, six aggregate-importance candidates were bootstrap-robust within the fixed representation and were associated with immune/inflammatory, oncogenic, cell-cycle, stress-response, and cellular-processing programs. Drug-preferential candidates lacked factor-level bootstrap robustness, although several pathway associations remained supported after lineage adjustment. Five independent VAE refits showed partial gene-program concordance but seed-sensitive axes, while a principal component analysis baseline supported stable factor selection and pathway annotation. As an exploratory application, baseline transcriptomes from 15 QAL333-tested cell lines were projected into the fixed VAE without encoder retraining. QAL333-prioritized factors were associated with inflammatory, oncogenic, cellular-processing, and microenvironment-related pathways. The two-model zebrafish xenograft comparison remained descriptive and hypothesis-generating. These findings support reusable, stability-aware latent-space analysis as a framework for pathway-level hypothesis generation from high-dimensional transcriptomic drug-response data.

Article.Title: Recognising the first visible signs of leprosy and late case detection in a low endemic area of Benin
Article.Authors: Gbaguidi F.; Zanvo S.; Anagonou S.; Tossou Y.; Codjo-Seignon K.; Agbo S.; Houezo J.; Bédié V.; Jimenez C.; Toussaint A.; Velut P.; Fastenau A.; Gine-March A.; Hounkpatin A.; Johnson R.
Article.Abstract: Although Benin reports fewer than 100 new leprosy cases per year, 47–54% of those notified between 2022 and 2025 had grade 2 disability (G2D) at diagnosis. We examined whether affected individuals and their neighbours recognised the disease by its first recognisable sign, a persistent skin patch with loss or alteration of sensation, or by its perceived late consequences. An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted in the Plateau and Zou departments of Benin among 175 people with multibacillary leprosy (64.1% of 273 multibacillary cases registered there in 2013–2023; 89 paucibacillary cases registered over the same period, 24.6% of the 362 registered cases, were not eligible) and 746 residents randomly selected within 100 m of the patients’ homes. Because the diagnosis was never disclosed, residents were analysed as members of endemic rural communities rather than as traced contacts, with no claim of representativeness. Recognition of this sign was compared with the perception of late consequences, and associations with G2D were examined using logistic regression. Among residents, 66.9% had heard of leprosy. Among those aware, 62.5% cited death, whereas the patch with altered sensation (45.5%) and disability or impairment (47.5%) were cited at indistinguishable rates; across all residents, only 30.4% could name this early sign. G2D was recorded in 33.7% of affected individuals: 19.4% of those presenting with a patch, 50.0% with sensory loss and 80.0% with visible disability. Compared with presentation for a patch, presentation for sensory loss was associated with higher odds of G2D (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 3.85, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.64–9.05). No difference was observed between actively and passively detected cases (36.1% versus 33.1%; OR 1.14, 95% CI 0.53–2.46), a comparison limited by only 36 active cases. In principle, 96.4% of residents would accept preventive medication; however, acceptance fell to 73.9% once distance, time and side effects were taken into account. In these low-endemic rural communities, leprosy was more evident through its perceived late consequences than its initial manifestations, and disability at diagnosis tracked the stage at which patients entered care. The findings support communication centred on persistent patches with altered sensation, reinforced recognition skills among first-line workers, and integration of education with case finding and contact-based prevention. The observational design precludes causal inference.

Article.Title: Cultural adaptation and validation of Eye Frailty Self-Check List for middle-aged and older adult in China
Article.Authors: Deng M.; Zheng K.; Zheng Z.; Xu X.; Wu J.; Su Y.; Chang J.
Article.Abstract: Visual function is central to the health-related quality of life of middle-aged and older adults. As population aging accelerates, eye frailty has become a new focus in public health. This condition represents an early state characterized by increased vulnerability of the visual system due to aging, diminished accommodative capacity, and impaired visual function. This study translated the Eye Frailty Self-Check List into Chinese and to evaluate its psychometric properties in a Chinese middle-aged and older adult population. Based on Brislin’s translation model and cross-cultural adaptation guidelines, forward and back translation, cultural adaptation, and cognitive interviews were conducted for the scale. Using a convenience sampling method, middle-aged and older adults from a tertiary hospital and two communities in Shanghai were recruited as study participants from January to April 2026. The reliability and validity of the Chinese version were evaluated under classical test theory. A total of 749 valid questionnaires were collected, yielding an effective response rate of 96.77%. The Chinese version of the Eye Frailty Self-Check List comprises 10 items distributed across three dimensions. Exploratory factor analysis identified three common factors, which collectively accounted for a cumulative variance contribution rate of 76.604%. The item-level content validity index (I-CVIs) ranged from 0.87 to 1.00. Construct validity was established through correlation with the Visual Function Index Scale, resulting in a correlation coefficient of -0.639 ( P < 0.001). The overall Cronbach’s α for the scale was 0.765, with factor 1 at 0.819, factor 2 at 0.827, and factor 3 at 0.862. The test-retest reliability coefficient was 0.857. The Chinese version of the Eye Frailty Self-Check List showed satisfactory reliability and preliminary evidence of construct validity among middle-aged and older adults, recruited from one tertiary hospital and two urban communities in Shanghai.

Article.Title: Solvent-mediated synthesis and catalytic performance of oxalate gel-derived CuO/ZnO/Al2O3 catalysts for hydrogen production via methanol steam reforming
Article.Authors: Bagherzadeh S.; Haghighi M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The influence of solvent engineering during oxalate gel co-precipitation on the physicochemical properties and catalytic performance of CuO/ZnO/Al₂O₃ (CZA) catalysts for methanol steam reforming was systematically investigated. Catalysts were synthesized using ethanol, ethylene glycol, diethylene glycol (DEG), triethylene glycol, and propylene glycol, followed by characterization using XRD, FESEM, EDX-mapping, FTIR, and BET analyses. Solvent selection markedly affected catalyst microstructure, phase dispersion, morphology, and specific surface area. Among the prepared catalysts, the DEG-derived sample exhibited the smallest CuO crystallites, the highest specific surface area, and the most homogeneous morphology, resulting in superior catalytic performance. It achieved approximately 51% methanol conversion at 160 °C and nearly complete conversion above 220 °C, while maintaining CO selectivity below 1.5% up to 300 °C and excellent stability over 24 h. These findings demonstrate that solvent engineering provides a simple and effective strategy for optimizing Cu-based catalysts for efficient hydrogen production via methanol steam reforming.

Article.Title: Optimizing seismographic network strategies for earthquake surveillance under linguistic pythagorean fuzzy dynamic knowledge
Article.Authors: Kalsoom U.; Razaq A.; Alhamzi G.; Baidar A.
Article.Abstract: Global seismographic networks (GSNs) capture fine details of ground motion signals, assisting scientists and governments in detecting and characterizing earthquakes and other seismic events worldwide. Continued improvements in these networks enhance knowledge about Earth structure, atmospheric interaction, and geological hazards. Because seismic stations operate under changing environmental and operational conditions, decision-making for network optimization requires tools that can handle uncertainty, linguistic assessments, and time-varying information. This study develops dynamic Dombi aggregation operators within the linguistic Pythagorean fuzzy set (LPFS) framework to support multi-attribute decision-making in such evolving environments. Aggregation operators combine multiple pieces of information into a single representative assessment. Their dynamic versions allow the influence of past and present information to vary over time, reflecting changes in data reliability and expert preference. The Dombi formulation further introduces a flexible parameter that models the decision-maker’s risk attitude. Two new operators are proposed. The linguistic pythagorean fuzzy dynamic Dombi weighted averaging (LPFDyDWA) operator produces a time-adjusted average evaluation in which both attribute importance and temporal relevance are incorporated under linguistic uncertainty. The linguistic pythagorean fuzzy dynamic Dombi weighted geometric (LPFDyDWG) operator performs a similar integration using a geometric combination, which is particularly suitable when interactions among attributes are multiplicative or mutually reinforcing. Together, these operators provide adaptive and interpretable tools for aggregating uncertain, language-based evaluations across multiple time periods. We establish their structural properties, introduce a novel score function for ranking alternatives, and develop a systematic decision-making procedure. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is demonstrated through an application to the optimization of seismographic network performance for enhanced earthquake monitoring, along with comparative analysis against existing methods.

Article.Title: Material calibration-independent neutron scattering corrections for quantitative imaging
Article.Authors: Sans-Planell O.; Kardjilov N.; Markötter H.; Tötzke C.; Tengattini A.; Hilger A.; Krzyzagorski M.; Lenoir N.; Manke I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Neutron imaging is a fundamental technique for the study of light elements, indispensable for the study of lithium distribution in batteries, water dynamics in soil or hydrogen storage in materials. Its quantitative accuracy is limited by the presence of scattered neutrons at the detector, which reduces the image contrast and introduces systematic errors in the attenuation coefficient evaluation. Here we present a dual detector setup to correct the neutron scatter component. The first detector, placed close to the sample, captures the transmitted and scattered neutrons while the second, installed downstream, captures mostly transmitted neutrons, with the scattered neutrons strongly suppressed by distance. By combining both acquisitions, we obtain a scatter-free radiography with the superior resolution of the first detector, without any sample-dependent calibration. This method is validated on a standard resolution sample to assess that there is no degradation in image quality; and the performance is proven on a highly challenging 4D tomography experiment using H $$_2$$ O and D $$_2$$ O mixtures within a heterogeneous soil matrix. This method brings neutron tomography from a qualitative visualisation technique to a quantitative analysis of heterogeneous, dynamic systems containing strong scattering substances.

Article.Title: Severe vitamin D deficiency among pregnant women delivering at a governmental hospital in Nablus, West Bank, Palestine: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Ali I.; Nazzal Z.; Saabneh S.; Ali N.; Yassin R.
Article.Abstract: Vitamin D deficiency is common in pregnancy, but data from the West Bank, Palestine, are scarce. The primary objective was to estimate the prevalence of vitamin D deficiency and severe deficiency among women admitted for delivery; the secondary objective was to explore associations of severe deficiency with maternal characteristics and with delivery and neonatal outcomes. This cross-sectional study was conducted at Rafidia Governmental Surgical Hospital, Nablus, between December 2020 and May 2021, using convenience sampling. Data were collected through structured interviews and medical records, and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] was measured by electrochemiluminescence immunoassay before delivery. Vitamin D status was classified as severe deficiency (< 10 ng/mL), deficiency (< 20 ng/mL), insufficiency (20–29.9 ng/mL), and sufficiency (≥ 30 ng/mL). Prevalence was estimated with 95% confidence intervals (CIs); associations were explored using bivariate tests and modified Poisson and log-linear regression. Among 193 women (mean age 27.7 ± 5.5 years), the median 25(OH)D was 7.9 ng/mL (interquartile range 5.2–11.5). Overall, 94.8% (95% CI 90.7–97.2) were deficient, including 67.4% (95% CI 60.5–73.6) with severe deficiency; 4.1% were insufficient, and 1.0% were sufficient. Severe deficiency was not significantly associated with the sociodemographic, lifestyle, or obstetric characteristics examined. Supplement use (24.9% of women) was independently associated with higher 25(OH)D concentrations (adjusted geometric mean ratio 1.27, 95% CI 1.06–1.53). No statistically significant associations were detected between severe deficiency and cesarean delivery (adjusted prevalence ratio 1.18, 95% CI 0.90–1.56), low birth weight, neonatal oxygen requirement, or neonatal intensive care unit admission; these estimates were imprecise. Vitamin D deficiency was nearly universal among women delivering at this hospital, two-thirds had severe deficiency, and supplement use was low. These findings support improving vitamin D supplementation coverage during pregnancy; larger multicenter studies across seasons are needed to assess maternal and neonatal outcomes.

Article.Title: A rapid multiplex LC-MS/MS platform for simultaneous monitoring of eight antibiotics: clinical application and exploratory analysis of determinants of personalized dosing in critically ill patients
Article.Authors: Chen F.; Tan Y.; Yang X.; Li H.; Zhang W.; Man H.; Shi Z.; Jiang Y.; Qiu C.
Article.Abstract: Critically ill patients show significant variability in antibiotics pharmacokinetics, often leading to suboptimal dosing and increased risk of treatment failure or toxicity, and the development of drug-resistant bacteria. This study aimed to establish a rapid and reliable LC-MS/MS method for the simultaneous quantification of eight antibiotics (vancomycin, meropenem, linezolid, voriconazole, sulfamethoxazole, trimethoprim, piperacillin, and cefoperazone) in human serum. The secondary aim was to apply this assay to therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM), explore and analyze clinical factors associated with serum drug concentrations, and provide a reference for individualized antibiotic dosing. A multiplex LC-MS/MS method was developed using protein precipitation and validated per FDA/EMA guidelines. It was applied to 522 serum samples from critically ill patients undergoing TDM. Clinical and laboratory data were analyzed using Spearman correlation and multiple linear regression to identify factors affecting drug levels. The method demonstrated good linearity (r² > 0.98), recovery (63.4–110.6%), and minimal matrix effects (89.2–105.2%). Target attainment rates varied from 22.2% to 70.4%. Creatinine clearance negatively correlated with concentrations of vancomycin, meropenem, linezolid, and piperacillin (p < 0.05). Daily dose positively influenced levels of vancomycin, meropenem, sulfamethoxazole, and trimethoprim (p < 0.01). Sex significantly affected sulfamethoxazole, while red blood cells count was inversely correlated with exposure to meropenem and trimethoprim. A robust and rapid LC-MS/MS method was established for the simultaneous TDM of eight antibiotics and was successfully applied to TDM in critically ill patients. Preliminary analyses showed that renal function, dosing regimen, sex, and anemia may be associated with drug exposure in critically ill patients, potentially providing a preliminary basis for future studies on individualized dosing.

Article.Title: RehaBot: a user-centered design and usability evaluation of a chatbot-based platform for cerebral palsy telerehabilitation
Article.Authors: Saoudi H.; Antón-Rodríguez M.; de la Calle García B.; Simón-Martínez C.; González-Ortega D.; Martínez-Zarzuela M.
Article.Abstract: Cerebral palsy is a lifelong neurodevelopmental condition that often requires sustained, home-based rehabilitation to maintain functional gains. Telerehabilitation has been proposed to extend specialist support beyond the clinic, but prior literature reports that therapists face difficulties personalizing, monitoring, and documenting remote interventions. To address these challenges, we applied a user-centered design (UCD) approach to develop RehaBot, a conversational telerehabilitation platform that integrates structured exercise prescription, video-guided home sessions, automated reminders, and bidirectional communication within a single digital workflow. Iterative co-design sessions with clinicians and patients informed system requirements, prioritizing accessibility, workflow integration, and motivational support. We conducted a mixed-methods usability and feasibility evaluation with patients with cerebral palsy ( N = 10, via caregiver proxy report) and rehabilitation professionals ( N = 10). The platform achieved high usability, with mean System Usability Scale scores exceeding established industry benchmarks for both groups. Qualitative interview data from therapists highlight enhanced patient engagement and streamlined remote supervision, while identifying areas for automation and workflow optimization. These findings suggest that a chatbot-based architecture is a feasible, accepted interface for structured home neurorehabilitation, with perceived benefits for communication and monitoring beyond the clinic. Future work will focus on large-scale clinical validation, adherence monitoring, and long-term outcome assessment.

Article.Title: The litter decomposition dynamics under land-type conversion by microbial communities in the Yellow River floodplain
Article.Authors: Lin Q.; Huai Z.; Riaz L.; Huq M.; Yu F.; Sun C.; Xu T.; Ma J.
Article.Abstract: Land-type conversion contributes significantly to litter decomposition, yet microbial feedback mechanisms remain unclear in river-floodplain areas. The distinct roles of bacteria versus fungi in wetland litter decomposition remain a key unresolved issue requiring further investigation. Litter decomposition dynamics and microecological mechanisms of three diverse land-types (riparian higher-beach wetland (RHW), cultivated wetland (CW), mesophytic wetland (MW)) within the Yellow River tidal flat were studied via litter bag method and high-throughput sequencing method for 2 years. Results indicated that land-use conversion induced obvious changes in the dominant microbial community composition, thereby regulating the facilitative role of soil microbiota in wetland litter decomposition processes. Agricultural reclamation on wetland changed microbial habitat and accelerated the litter decomposition 35.7–38.05% and the net release of total carbon 4.15–9.78%. Mesophytization of wetland increased the bacterial species and OTU, and facilitates local carbon retention. Cellulose and lignin content of litter in RHW, CW and MW decreased exponentially over time (R 2 = 0.960, 0.775, 0.896 and 0.959, 0.822, 0.918). C/N ratio (MSE = 15.37%), litter carbon content (8.30%) and soil moisture (6.94%) best predict litter mass loss ( P < 0.01). Furthermore, the DOC, NH 4 + -N, NO 3 - -N etc. content in soil were correlated with microbial Chao1 index and Shannon diversity. Cellulose, lignin DRs were positively related to the DR of nitrogen, fungi Shannon-diversity and bacterial Chao1, with lignin DR being more susceptible to fungi. During the decomposition process, bacteria account for 77.44–84.49% and fungi 0.08–0.22% at kingdom level. Land-use change reduced moisture (r = -0.79) but didn’t significantly increases soil N, both lowering bacterial α-diversity (r = -0.49, -0.76) and accelerating decomposition (r = 0.81) (R 2 = 0.61). Soil N and environment enhance fungal diversity non-significantly. Conclusively, land-use conversion in the Yellow River wetland soil reshapes the microbial engines, mesophytization of natural wetland and anthropogenic reclamation enhance litter decomposition and carbon–nitrogen degradation.

Article.Title: Molybdenum trioxide and silver hybrid nanofillers enhance the capacitance of polyvinyl alcohol and polyvinylpyrrolidone blend electrodes for supercapacitor applications
Article.Authors: Ragab H.; Diab N.; Hamada F.; Aleid G.; Farea M.; Algethami R.; AlElaimi M.; Al-Hakimi A.; Farea M.
Article.Abstract: Polyvinyl alcohol/polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVA/PVP) blend nanocomposites reinforced with a hybrid MoO 3 /Ag nanofiller at 0, 1, 3, 5 and 7 wt% were prepared by solution casting and denoted PAM-x, where PAM stands for PVA/PVP–MoO 3 /Ag and x is the nanofiller content in wt%. X-ray diffraction confirmed the incorporation of both orthorhombic α-MoO 3 (JCPDS No. 05-0508) and metallic fcc Ag (JCPDS No. 04-0783) into a predominantly amorphous polymer matrix, with crystallinity increasing with nanofiller content and no secondary phases detected. SEM and TEM showed uniform dispersion of the hybrid filler in the matrix, with Ag nanoparticles (about 15–30 nm) attached to MoO₃ platelets. FTIR revealed hydrogen bonding between the polymer functional groups and MoO 3 together with the appearance of Mo–O bands, while UV–Vis spectroscopy showed enhanced visible absorption and a reduced optical band gap. Electrochemical tests were performed in a three-electrode cell in 3 M KOH over 0–0.7 V at a mass loading of 3 mg cm −2 . Cyclic voltammetry showed a transition from double-layer behaviour in the pristine blend to pseudocapacitive Mo 6+ /Mo 5+ redox behaviour in the loaded samples, and impedance spectroscopy indicated much lower series and charge-transfer resistance for PAM-5. PAM-5 delivered the highest specific capacitance of 545 F g −1 at 0.5 A g −1 , retained 485.7 F g −1 at 2.0 A g −1 (rate capability ~ 89%), and retained 79% of its initial capacitance after 1000 cycles at 2.0 A g −1 . This performance is attributed to the combined contributions of redox-active MoO 3 , conductive Ag, and the flexible PVA/PVP host. Future work will address extended cycling, post-cycling characterisation, and two-electrode device evaluation.

Article.Title: Evaluation of an extracurricular undergraduate ultrasound training program at a central European medical faculty
Article.Authors: Smaha J.; Sučák A.; Pekarčík M.; Vitovič P.; Hnilicová S.; Jackuliak P.; Payer J.
Article.Abstract: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is increasingly incorporated into medical training, yet structured undergraduate education remains limited in many European medical schools. We evaluated a four-session extracurricular ultrasound course using a mixed-methods design in 58 medical students. At course completion, students retrospectively self-assessed theoretical knowledge and practical skills on 0–10 scales, completed a 30-item course-specific theoretical knowledge test, and provided satisfaction ratings and qualitative feedback. Self-assessed theoretical knowledge increased from 3.34 ± 1.76 to 6.91 ± 1.26 and practical skills from 2.02 ± 1.58 to 6.95 ± 0.94 (both p < 0.001). The mean knowledge-test score was 24.64 ± 3.74/30 (82.1 ± 12.5%), with acceptable internal consistency (KR-20 = 0.775). Most students rated the course highly, and qualitative feedback emphasized clinical relevance, supervised hands-on learning, and support for broader curricular integration. This pilot evaluation suggests that extracurricular ultrasound training is feasible, well accepted, and associated with increases in retrospectively self-assessed theoretical knowledge and practical skills. Controlled studies using validated objective assessments are needed before conclusions regarding educational effectiveness, practical competence, and long-term skill retention can be drawn.

Article.Title: Effect of seaweed extract and foliar spray of smoked water on the growth of tomato under alkalinity stress
Article.Authors: Haq A.; Ashraf K.; Fatima S.; Hussain A.; Hassan A.; Ur-Rahman M.; El Sabagh A.; Al-Ashkar I.; Zaman Q.
Article.Abstract: Alkaline conditions inhibit plants growth, resulting in reduced yield and quality of field crops. Various soil and foliar amendments, such as seaweed extract (SWE) and smoked water (SW) are widely used as a biostimulant to improve plant growth and development and to enhance resistance to abiotic stress. In the current study, a pot experiment was comprising of two factors i.e., alkalinity stress (with 100 mM NaHCO 3 :Na 2 CO 3 in a ratio of 9:1), and six treatments of SWE and SW (control; seaweed extract 3%; smoked water 1:150; smoked water 1:300; seaweed extract and smoked water 1:150; seaweed extract and smoked water 1:300) was applied to the tomato plants. Results showed that the alkaline conditions had significant impact on growth, biomass, and photosynthetic characteristics of tomato plants. But combinatorial use of SWE and SW showed improvement in growth, biomass, photosynthetic properties, and decreased plant membrane damage and lipid peroxidation. These biostimulant combinations improved the carotenoids content (41.06%), soluble protein contents (98.23%), and decreased the electrolyte leakage (55.53%) as compared to control (no SWE and SW application). The optimal use of SWE and SW had significant effects on ionic homeostasis in tomato leaves. The combined effect of SW and SWE significantly reduced sodium (Na + ) ions (80.00%), chloride ions (Cl - ) (53.00%) and significantly increased in potassium ions (K + ) (311%) in leaves. Overall, the combined effect of SWE (3%) and SW (1:300) demonstrate the potential as an effective and sustainable approach for increasing alkalinity tolerance in tomato plants.

Article.Title: Modeling and prediction of cotton/polyester ring-spun yarn hairiness using Taguchi analysis, MLR, ANN and ANFIS
Article.Authors: Khadem-Ilkhechi S.; Shakersoureh A.; Safar Johari M.; Otaghsara M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Yarn hairiness affects downstream processing and fabric appearance. This study evaluated five machine variables, front-roller cot hardness, front-to-middle roller gauge, front-roller pressure, apron spacer (clip) size, and spinning angle, for 30/70 cotton/polyester ring-spun yarn using a Taguchi L27 design. S3 hairiness was measured in five repetitions per run and analyzed by mean response, smaller-the-better signal-to-noise ratio, and ANOVA. Cot hardness was dominant, followed by front-roller pressure and spacer size; roller gauge had a smaller significant effect, whereas spinning angle had the smallest effect (parametric p = 0.050; permutation p = 0.019). The preferred combination produced the lowest L27 response (18.3 hairs/m), while an independent confirmation production gave 18.5 ± 0.85 hairs/m ( n = 5; CV = 4.59%). MLR, ANN, and ANFIS were compared using a common 24-run training and three-run test split. ANFIS gave the lowest held-out RMSE (0.273 hairs/m), whereas ANN gave the highest test correlation. Repeated six-fold cross-validation over ten repetitions provided a more stable assessment across data partitions, with ANN showing the lowest mean RMSE (0.554 ± 0.194 hairs/m), compared with MLR (0.834 ± 0.064 hairs/m) and ANFIS (0.845 ± 0.543 hairs/m). Given the small test set, model differences are interpreted descriptively.

Article.Title: Molecular epidemiology of rifampicin-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis in Vietnam
Article.Authors: Solomon O.; Nguyen V.; Nguyen T.; Nguyen H.; MacLean E.; Fox G.; Behr M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Vietnam is a top 20 burden country for multi-drug resistant/rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (MDR/RR-TB), with nearly 10,000 cases a year. With the emergence of new diagnostic assays for M. tuberculosis detection and resistance, along with new drugs for both treatment and prevention, we sought to better understand the molecular epidemiology of RR-TB in this high-burden setting, through the study of clinical trial isolates from the VQUIN MDR trial. We assembled a sample of cultured isolates, collected from patients with RR- M. tuberculosis detected with Xpert MTB/RIF across 10 provinces, enriching for isolates from outside of the two major cities, Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City. We subjected these isolates to whole genome sequencing (WGS) and bioinformatic analysis, with a subset subjected to phenotypic drug susceptibility testing to evaluate phenotypic/genotypic concordance. New genome sequences were phylogenetically contextualised to publicly available M. tuberculosis genome sequences sampled in Vietnam from National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) Sequence Read Archive (SRA). Of 252 isolates classified as RR-TB by Xpert MTB/RIF, 244 (97%) were confirmed to have rifampicin-resistance mutations by WGS. A high proportion of these (235/244, 96%) had mutations associated with resistance to at least one other first- or second-line antibiotic. Phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (pDST) for rifampicin, isoniazid, and levofloxacin was completed for a random sample of 77 isolates, demonstrating a high concordance between pDST and genomic-based resistance predictions (67/77, 87% RIF; 76/77, 99% INH; 73/77, 95% LFX). In a phenotypic/genotypic comparison of 59 isolates to new and repurposed antibiotics, no resistance was detected to pretomanid or linezolid, whereas high concordance was observed for bedaquiline (56/59, 95%). RIF-resistant strains were more likely to be L2.2.1, compared to RIF-susceptible M. tuberculosis strains in Vietnam, particularly in the major cities. The high prevalence of secondary drug-resistance beyond RIF and INH, along with the dominance of one major lineage across geographic regions, provides insights into the spread of MDR/RR-TB in Vietnam and reinforces the importance of prompt and broad detection of drug-resistance to inform the timely initiation of effective drug regimens.

Article.Title: Unified description of Fano resonances in excitonic nanostructures across multiple geometries
Article.Authors: Hayashi S.; Sugimoto H.; Fujii M.; Nesterenko D.; Sekkat Z.
Article.Abstract: The optical properties of excitonic materials can be described by an excitonic dielectric function consisting of a background dielectric constant and a Lorentzian term associated with the exciton transition. In excitonic nanostructures, the background dielectric constant is expected to produce a nonresonant response, whereas the excitonic term is expected to yield a resonant response; interference between these contributions has been proposed as the origin of Fano line shapes across different geometries. To test this scenario and establish a unified description, we develop a general theoretical formalism and apply it to light-scattering spectra of excitonic spheres and cylinders, as well as the reflection spectra of excitonic slabs. Calculations for a sphere and a cylinder with radii of 40 nm and for a 40 nm-thick slab show that all these nanostructures show similar asymmetric line shapes superposed on monotonically increasing background spectra. When the spectra are normalized to the background spectra, they exhibit Fano profiles arising from interference between a constant background component and a resonant excitonic component described by a complex Lorentzian function. These results demonstrate that the general formalism provides a unified framework for identifying the common origin of the Fano resonances in excitonic nanostructures of different geometries.

Article.Title: Eight-beam wide coverage ridge waveguide slot antenna array based on 4×4 Butler matrix
Article.Authors: Jo S.; Lee K.; Yun S.; Lee J.; Kim K.; Cho Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multibeam antennas fed by Butler matrices (BMs) can effectively combine passive beamforming networks with antenna arrays. However, limited structural approaches exist for BM-integrated antennas to address the issues associated with scan loss and null regions. This paper presents a ridged waveguide slot antenna array integrated with a 4 $$\times $$ 4 BM that generates four dual-lobe radiation patterns, thereby expanding spatial coverage without increasing hardware complexity. By strategically configuring the grating lobes with appropriate element spacing, the architecture covers eight interleaved angular directions across four beam states. To mitigate inherent beam scan loss and crossover loss, periodic groove structures are integrated between adjacent arrays to optimize the mutual coupling. Furthermore, a vertically integrated center-fed ridged waveguide configuration is employed to miniaturize the footprint and suppress beam squint. At the center frequency of 62.5 GHz, the fabricated antenna demonstrated a peak gain of 19.7 dBi. The eight interleaved beams provided a wide angular coverage of $$\pm 79^{\circ }$$ with a gain imbalance of less than 1.9 dB. The prototype maintained a reflection coefficient below $$-10$$ dB over a 13.4% fractional bandwidth of 59–67.5 GHz. Thus, the proposed antenna has strong potential to be employed in future multiuser millimeter-wave wireless communication systems.

Article.Title: Latent-aligned scalable interpolant transformer for controllable chest X-ray synthesis
Article.Authors: Schlattner I.; Atlassov V.; Abdrakhmanov A.; Won D.; Lee M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Controllable chest X-ray (CXR) synthesis requires control over both semantic findings and their spatial relationship to thoracic anatomy. Text-conditioned generative models can specify disease labels or report-level descriptions but often provide limited control over pathology location and extent. We introduce LatAlignCXR, which represents anatomical layout, pathology location, and residual appearance within a structured latent space. Text prompts, reference radiographs, and user-defined coordinates are mapped to this representation, from which anatomical, pathology, and thoracic structural priors are decoded to condition a scalable interpolant transformer (SiT). The same representation supports text-, image-, and coordinate-conditioned synthesis. On MIMIC-CXR, LatAlignCXR achieved the highest anatomical Dice (0.6564), the lowest Fréchet distance in three of four feature spaces, and the highest pneumonia-localization consistency (Dice 0.1385, IoU 0.0741). In a blinded radiologist evaluation, LatAlignCXR received mean ratings of 4.63 for pathology consistency and 4.50 for spatial consistency, compared with 3.63 and 3.37 for Cheff, respectively. In downstream classification, synthetic augmentation increased accuracy from 69.0% to 76.0% with 1000 real images, with smaller and non-monotonic effects as real-data availability increased. These findings support structured latent conditioning for spatially controllable CXR synthesis, particularly for pathology representation and spatial consistency.

Article.Title: Caffeine-related exposure and dry eye disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis of epidemiological associations and tear-related outcomes
Article.Authors: Bao Y.; Xiao C.; Xu K.; Yu X.; Dai Q.; Wang C.
Article.Abstract: Caffeine intake has been described as a potential lifestyle factor in dry eye disease (DED), but evidence remains conflicting. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the association between caffeine-related exposure and DED and summarized clinical studies examining tear-film parameters. Web of Science, PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, Scopus and Google Scholar were searched from inception to March 31, 2026. Twenty-three studies were included: 14 epidemiological studies involving 117,736 participants and 9 tear-parameter studies involving 519 participants. Grouped analysis without separating caffeine sources showed no significant association with DED and substantial heterogeneity (OR 0.89, 95% CI 0.74–1.08; I² = 69%). Heterogeneity decreased in adjusted estimates (OR 0.92, 95% CI 0.80–1.05; I² = 40%). After excluding the tea-specific study, the remaining adjusted studies showed a significant inverse association (OR 0.85, 95% CI 0.75–0.96; I² = 0%). Tear-parameter studies suggested transient increases in tear secretion after pure caffeine, while beverage-based effects on tear stability were inconsistent. In summary, current evidence does not establish caffeine-related exposure as protective against DED. Future studies should distinguish caffeine from beverage constituents and evaluate topical caffeine or methylxanthine analogues.

Article.Title: Plasma metabolomics reveals systemic alterations associated with cardiac surgery and identifies candidate predictors of postoperative outcomes: a prospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Wehkamp L.; Radke D.; Bernardes J.; López-Agudelo V.; Schuchardt S.; Elke G.; Hummitzsch L.; Neu F.; Steinfath M.; Albrecht M.; Veluswamy P.; Huenges K.; Panholzer B.; Warnecke G.; Schädler D.; Rosenstiel P.; Schreiber S.; Aden K.; Lindner M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) is associated with systemic metabolic alterations related to stress and immune responses. We aimed to map these dynamics through perioperative metabolomics. Furthermore, we assessed whether baseline metabolites predict postoperative outcomes. Plasma was sampled pre- and post-surgery in a discovery (n = 98) and validation cohort (n = 24). Targeted metabolomics was performed with the Biocrates MxP Quant 500XL kit. Statistical analysis involved principal component analysis, linear mixed effects models, and machine learning-based approaches. The plasma metabolome exhibited marked pre- to post-surgery alterations, primarily driven by postoperative lipid reduction. Baseline metabolic profiles showed no global separation between outcome groups. Individual preoperative metabolites however demonstrated exploratory evidence of higher discriminative performance than established biomarkers (CRP, urea) and clinical risk scores for prolonged ICU stay (> 3 days) in the discovery cohort (n = 22 events). External validation showed discrimination comparable to conventional parameters, although precision was limited by only five outcome events. Our findings highlight substantial metabolic alterations following CPB and suggest baseline metabolites as candidate predictors of postoperative outcomes, supporting further evaluation as prognostic markers in larger cohorts. Trial registration: The study was registered in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS00016493, https://drks.de/search/en/trial/DRKS00016493 ) on 15 March 2019.

Article.Title: A systems analysis of barriers to effective national incident management in Iran
Article.Authors: Ahmadi E.; Marzaleh M.; Peyravi M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Iran’s high disaster risk necessitates a robust National Incident Management System (NIMS), yet its implementation faces deep-rooted barriers. This qualitative study explored these systemic challenges through thematic analysis of in-depth interviews with 33 senior managers and specialists from Iran’s key disaster management organizations in 2025. Analysis identified six interconnected themes: Governance & Strategy; Structure & Organization; Coordination & Communications; Human Resources; Equipment & Logistics; and Culture & Participation. These factors were found to form a self-reinforcing vicious cycle, where governance failures create structural and cultural deficiencies that perpetuate operational breakdowns, which in turn reinforcing weak governance. The study concludes that overcoming these interdependent barriers requires integrated, multi-level policy interventions targeting governance, culture, and coordination simultaneously. This framework offers critical insights for building resilient national systems in other high-risk, resource-constrained contexts globally.
