Article.Title: Deep learning classification of longitudinally defined 24-2 central- and peripheral-onset visual field phenotypes in glaucoma using baseline fundus photographs
Article.Authors: Lee E.; Im J.; Choi Y.; Chung M.; Han J.; Kim T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We aimed to determine whether a deep learning (DL) model trained on baseline color fundus photographs can identify the dominant locus of visual field (VF) damage in glaucoma, as defined by longitudinal VF follow-up. We performed retrospective analysis of a longitudinal cohort study on 1,464 patients with early glaucoma (baseline mean deviation > − 6 dB) followed for at least 5 years with a minimum of five reliable VF examinations. Eyes were classified into operationally defined central-onset or peripheral-onset VF damage patterns based on longitudinally consistent VF patterns. A retinal foundation model RETFound was fine-tuned in two configurations, unimodal (fundus image only) and multimodal (fundus image + gender via late fusion), to classify central-onset versus peripheral-onset phenotype. Model performance was assessed on a held-out test set. A total of 1,088 eyes from 871 patients were finally included in the analysis; 168 (15.4%) were classified as central-onset and 920 (84.6%) as peripheral-onset phenotype. At baseline, 175 eyes (16.1%) were preperimetric, whereas 913 eyes (83.9%) had a detectable VF defect. The mean follow-up duration was 9.0 ± 2.7 years and did not differ between groups. The multimodal RETFound model achieved the highest AUROC of 0.867, followed by the unimodal model (0.840) and ConvNeXt (0.839), while other backbone architectures ranged from 0.641 to 0.721. In conclusion, DL applied to baseline fundus photographs identified longitudinally defined patterns of central versus peripheral VF vulnerability in glaucoma.

Article.Title: Mathematical modeling and cross-salt validation of layer-by-layer deposition of cadmium sulfide thin films: correlating thickness, morphology, and functional relevance from sensor to photocatalytic applications
Article.Authors: Guminilovych R.; Deva L.; Lozynskyi V.
Article.Abstract: The paper presents a systematic study of the layer-by-layer chemical deposition of cadmium sulfide thin films. The research aimed to establish relationships among concentration parameters, the number of deposition cycles, morphological characteristics, and functional properties. The objective of the study was to develop a mathematical model to quantitatively describe film growth kinetics and predict film thickness from process parameters. A multifactor regression analysis was employed, with model coefficients determined using the least-squares method in matrix form. The construction of the design matrices enabled the inclusion of primary variables, as well as interaction and quadratic terms that capture the nonlinear nature of film growth. This approach ensured high accuracy in approximating experimental data and yielded a statistically significant model capable of reproducing and predicting deposition trends. The model’s reliability was verified through cross-salt validation, in which analogous deposition conditions were applied with various cadmium sources, including sulfate, chloride, iodide, nitrate, and acetate. The comparative analysis confirmed that the fundamental growth patterns are preserved across different salt-system compositions, demonstrating the model’s universality and transferability across various technological environments. To better understand film-forming patterns, 3D visualization of both experimental and modeled data was performed, enabling the spatial relationships among reagent concentration, the number of deposition cycles, and film thickness to be traced. The visualization confirmed the adequacy of the chosen model. The optical and morphological characteristics of the obtained films were analyzed, revealing that variations in film thickness directly influence the transmittance coefficient and the bandgap ( E g ). Thinner films exhibited high optical transparency, potentially relevant to sensing and optoelectronic applications, whereas thicker films showed enhanced optical absorption.

Article.Title: FedEAVE: federated evidence alignment and causal diagnosis for privacy-preserving personalized learning
Article.Authors: Zeng Y.; Wang X.; Kong L.
Article.Abstract: Reliable educational diagnosis requires evidence from multiple sources without exposing sensitive student records or assuming that recommended interventions are effective. We propose FedEAVE (Federated Evidence-Aligned Verification for Education), a federated framework combining contrastive evidence alignment, prerequisite-aware diagnosis, and retrospective intervention verification. Source-specific encoders map assessment, behavioral, peer-interaction, and temporal signals into a shared space; an availability-aware network weights the observed sources by their reliability. A graph-based diagnostic model estimates concept mastery and counterfactual responses under assumptions of an acyclic prerequisite graph and concept-level unconfoundedness. A matched difference-in-differences (DiD) procedure estimates intervention effects and provides feedback for diagnostic and policy updates. Federated optimization employs per-example clipping ( \(C{=}1.0\) ), Gaussian noise ( \(\sigma _\textrm{DP}{=}1.1\) ), and a reported privacy budget of \((\epsilon {=}2.0,\delta {=}10^{-5})\) over \(T{=}50\) rounds. On EdNet, FedEAVE obtains \(84.7\%\) response-prediction accuracy and an MAE of 0.113; it also improves predictive performance on ASSISTments and Junyi Academy. Intervention estimates remain retrospective and require prospective validation.

Article.Title: Comparative numerical analysis of ground-improvement techniques for embankment performance on soft soil: insights into rigid, semi-rigid, and drainage-based solutions
Article.Authors: Hosseinzadeh M.; Abdollahi M.
Article.Abstract: This study develops and validates a mechanistically consistent plane-strain finite-element framework to elucidate how stiffness contrast and drainage capacity interact in controlling embankment performance on soft clay. A column-wall formulation is combined with coupled deformation-consolidation analysis and benchmarked against full-scale field data, reproducing settlement and excess pore-pressure responses with deviations generally < 15% during construction and < 10% during consolidation. Under identical geometry, stratigraphy, and staged loading, the results demonstrate that serviceability is governed primarily by stiffness-driven load bypassing rather than drainage efficiency. Rigid and semi-rigid inclusions limit construction-stage settlement to 5.9–6.3 mm, compared with 10.9 mm for prefabricated vertical drains (PVDs) and 15.1 mm for granular columns, corresponding to reductions of approximately 46% and 42% relative to PVDs, and 61% and 58% relative to granular columns, demonstrating their superior short-term deformation-control performance. In contrast, excess pore-pressure response reveals an inherent trade-off: inclusions suppress peak construction-stage pore pressure to 24.6–25.8 kPa (15–19% lower than PVDs at 30.5 kPa) via stress redistribution, yet consolidate slowly (270–300 days), whereas drainage-based systems dissipate pore pressure within 45–55 days at the cost of higher initial buildup. Vertical stress partitioning is shown to be stiffness-controlled, with concrete piles attracting 85–90 kPa peak stress and unloading the soft clay by 40–60%, directly underpinning stability gains; construction-stage FS increases from 1.293 (PVDs) to 2.14–2.15 (65–66%). The findings reframe ground-improvement selection as a performance-based stiffness-drainage interaction problem, providing a quantitative basis for rational and material-efficient embankment design.

Article.Title: Structural perturbations and destabilizing mutations in RAD51C and RAD51D reveal mechanisms of cancer risk
Article.Authors: Gund V.; Sharma S.; Badhe S.; Pandey R.; kumar S.; Singh S.
Article.Abstract: Breast and ovarian cancers remain among the most prevalent malignancies affecting women worldwide, with only 20% of hereditary cases explained by BRCA1/2 mutations. This highlights the importance of alternative susceptibility genes such as RAD51C and RAD51D, which play essential roles in homologous recombination repair (HRR). In this study, a comprehensive in silico analysis was conducted to identify deleterious non-synonymous single nucleotide variants (nsSNVs) in RAD51C and RAD51D that may contribute to genomic instability and increased cancer risk. A total of 19,195 SNVs were retrieved and analyzed using multiple computational tools including SIFT, PolyPhen-2, PANTHER, PROVEAN, PhD-SNP, SNP&GO, I-Mutant, and MUpro. Eleven high-risk nsSNPs in RAD51C and several in RAD51D were identified, primarily affecting the ATP-binding and DNA repair domains. Structural modeling, docking, and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that mutations such as p.R212H, p.L219S, and p.L262V in RAD51C and p.S207L, p.S207P, and p.A210E in RAD51D significantly alter protein stability, flexibility, and binding affinity with interaction partners like XRCC2, RAD51B, and RAD51C. These alterations may compromise DNA repair mechanisms, contributing to carcinogenesis. Our findings underscore the utility of integrated computational approaches in identifying pathogenic variants and provide a molecular basis for understanding RAD51C/D-related cancer susceptibility. This work lays the groundwork for future experimental validation and supports the application of personalized medicine in HR-deficient tumors.

Article.Title: Nutritional values, phytochemical profiles and enteric methane mitigation potential of West African indigenous forage species for sustainable ruminant livestock production systems
Article.Authors: Montcho M.; Lesse P.; Salako V.; Dakpogan H.; Sinsin B.
Article.Abstract: Manipulating feed rations with forages containing specific natural phytochemicals that reduce enteric methane emissions is a sustainable strategy for cattle farming. This study aimed to select forages based on their secondary metabolites, nutritional value and methane production. A total of fifteen forage species identified by cattle farmers were studied. Phytochemical parameters were measured in line with the European Pharmacopoeia method. In vitro fermentation with bovine rumen juice was used to assess digestibility and methane production. Results showed that species with high tannin content: Acacia sieberiana (2.002%), Khaya senegalensis (1.939%) and Detarium microcarpum (1.665%) had the lowest digestibility values of Organic Matter Digestibility (OMD ranging from 30.0 to 47.1%) and metabolizable energy values (1281.6 to 1952.4 kcal/kg DM). These low energy values were also coupled with low methane production (185.0 to 282 mL CH 4 /kg DM). Furthermore, despite their high tannin contents, Anogeissus leiocarpa (4.556%) and Isoberlinia doka (2.486%) recorded good digestibility, good energy values, and moderate methane production. However, species that are poor in tannins and rich in nitrogen, such as Blighia sapida , Leucaena leucocephala , and Faidherbia albida , have high digestibility values (43.1% − 62.8%) and metabolizable energy above 2200 kcal/kg DM. Blighia sapida , in particular, stands out with an exceptional dMO content of 62.8% and an energy value of 2657.6 kcal/kg DM, combined with values of 0.93 UFL and 0.88 UFV. However, this performance resulted in the highest methane production (505 mL CH₄/kg DM). Species with moderate levels of secondary metabolites, such as Piliostigma thonningii , Daniellia oliveri , Combretum collinum , Annona senegalensis and Diospyros mespiliformis , have average digestibility (53.3%) and energy values ranging from 1868.3 to 2206.4 kcal/kgDM. These plants offer a good compromise between digestibility and methane production through the balanced presence of polyphenols and flavonoids. This study definitively demonstrates that the rational management of secondary metabolites in ruminant feed is a promising way to combine zootechnical performance with a more responsible environmental footprint. This research is the first study in Benin that provides data and tables to guide cattle farmers in ecofeed rations formulation.

Article.Title: An AutoML and GeoAI workflow for comparative landslide susceptibility assessment in high-relief mountain terrain
Article.Authors: Faisal R.; Shehab Z.; Mebrahtu G.
Article.Abstract: Landslide susceptibility mapping in complex mountain terrain demands modeling frameworks capable of resolving non-linear, high-dimensional conditioning factor relationships while maintaining spatial referencing integrity. This study applies and comparatively evaluates the AutoML and GeoAI tools implemented in ArcGIS Pro 3.5 for comparative LSM in Choman District, Kurdistan Region using LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, Random Trees, Extremely Randomized Trees, and a weighted Ensemble model. A spatially balanced training dataset of 2,384 samples was intersected with thirteen conditioning factors and partitioned into 75% training and 25% independent test subsets. On an independent holdout set the Ensemble model returned the lowest log-loss (0.0809) together with an accuracy of 97.15% (95% CI 95.48–98.21%), ROC-AUC of 0.9965, and KS of 0.943; its margin over the leading individual learners was not statistically significant, though it exceeded both bagging-based ensembles on every metric. Under five-fold spatial block cross-validation, adopted as the primary estimate of generalization performance, mean ROC-AUC was 0.993 ± 0.003 and mean accuracy 95.56 ± 1.20%. The three gradient boosting algorithms formed a coherent high-performance cluster, while Tree algorithms showed substantially higher log-loss and compressed probability distributions. Feature importance analysis identified NDVI, land cover, LS factor, and lithostratigraphic units as the four dominant predictors. Hot-spot stability analysis, perturbing the susceptibility index at 10%, 20%, and 30%, showed that 96.84%, 93.70%, and 88.90% of 1,373,610 terrain features respectively retained their original cluster classification, with interquartile ranges of 0 at the two lower magnitudes, indicating that the mapped clustering structure is robust to imprecision in the susceptibility values. This workflow provides a reproducible and uncertainty-aware methodology for similar mountain geohazard situations.

Article.Title: Quadratic thermal radiation effects on hybrid nanoliquid flow near saddle and nodal stagnation points over a Howarth wavy cylinder using mass‑based thermophysical relations
Article.Authors: Ramzan M.; Akram J.; Shahmir N.; Barakat N.; Saeed A.; Alkhrijah Y.; Koh W.
Article.Abstract: Flows near saddle and nodal stagnation points possess applications in solar collectors, high-performance systems, drag reduction systems, and catalytic reactors. Motivated by these applications, the primary objective of the present study is to investigate three-dimensional stagnation-point flow of a hybrid nanoliquid over a sinusoidal wavy cylinder, with potential relevance to thermal management and heat-transfer systems involving boundary-layer transport phenomena. The fluid consists of a water-based mixture of copper oxide ( CuO ) and zinc oxide ( ZnO ) nanoparticles and flows through a porous medium with spatially varying porosity. The novelty of the anticipated model is enhanced by considering the thermophysical properties using mass-based relations instead of conventional thermophysical relations involving volume fraction directly. Heat transfer is analyzed using a quadratic thermal radiation approximation, and the governing equations are solved numerically via the bvp4c approach. The results indicate that increasing the CuO nanoparticle mass parameter enhances both axial and transverse velocity profiles, while slightly reducing fluid temperature at both stagnation points. Axial velocity is higher at the saddle point, whereas transverse velocity is higher at the nodal point. The thermal radiation sensitivity is highly topology-dependent. The Nusselt number is almost independent of Rd at the nodal stagnation point, while it becomes significantly larger as Rd increases at the saddle stagnation point. The inclusion of 30 g CuO in 100 g of base fluid leads to a substantial increase in surface drag, whereas within the investigated range (Da = 1.0 − 1.2), the Darcy parameter produces only a marginal variation (below 0.2%) in the reported engineering quantity. Model validation is also provided.

Article.Title: Kaempferol attenuates secondary brain injury after traumatic brain injury in mice with reduced neuroinflammation
Article.Authors: Li T.; Wang D.; Li L.; Hao H.; Wang C.; Peng R.; Zhang G.; Wang H.
Article.Abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) triggers a secondary injury cascade characterized by neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption, cerebral hypoperfusion, and progressive neuronal loss, yet effective therapies remain limited. Here, we investigated whether kaempferol attenuates secondary brain injury after TBI in mice by suppressing neuroinflammation. Using a fluid percussion injury model, we performed transcriptomic, histological, behavioral, cerebral perfusion, flow cytometric, and protein analyses. Kaempferol treatment reduced lesion burden, tissue disruption, and Evans blue extravasation, and improved neurological, motor, and cognitive outcomes after TBI. It also decreased neuronal loss and neuronal apoptosis in the injured cortex and hippocampus. Notably, kaempferol reduced microglial accumulation and neutrophil infiltration and was associated with a less pro-inflammatory microglial cytokine profile, including reduced IL-1β and TNF-α expression and increased IL-4 and TGF-β expression. And in vitro, kaempferol attenuated LPS-induced pro-inflammatory activation of BV2 microglial cells. In addition, kaempferol increased CD31 immunoreactivity, restored ZO-1 immunoreactivity along CD31-positive microvessels, improved ipsilateral cortical blood flow, and was accompanied by increased expression of PI3K, p-AKT, HIF-1α, VEGF, HO-1, and Bcl-2, together with reduced Bax and cleaved caspase-3. These findings indicate that kaempferol attenuates secondary brain injury after TBI in mice, with reduced neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, BBB disruption, vascular dysfunction, and neuronal apoptosis as prominent associated features.

Article.Title: Loss of centriolar OFD1 activates the p53–DRAM1 pathway to remodel centriolar satellites and suppress ciliogenesis
Article.Authors: Izumi H.; Lei S.; Fukuoka M.; Hirota T.; Nakagawara A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Autophagy is a lysosome-based proteolytic system that is essential for cellular homeostasis. However, it remains unclear whether autophagy regulates the homeostasis of non-membranous organelles, such as centrosomes. We herein provide evidence to show that the depletion of centrosomes by centrinone, a PLK4 inhibitor, appears to activate autophagy. We then searched for centrosomal proteins whose loss promotes autophagy. Among the centrosomal proteins examined, the loss of OFD1, a centriole and centriolar satellite protein, was the most strongly associated with increases in autophagy markers. Mechanistically, OFD1 was found in close proximity to p53 at the distal ends of centrioles. The loss of OFD1 was associated with the redistribution of p53 from centrioles to the nucleus, leading to the transcriptional induction of the p53 target gene, DNA damage-regulated autophagy modulator 1 (DRAM1). DRAM1 localizes to the pericentrosomal region and is associated with reduced levels of centriolar satellites, including PCM1, CEP131, and CEP290, which are essential for ciliogenesis. Consequently, DRAM1 activation suppressed primary cilium formation. These results support a model in which the OFD1–p53–DRAM1 axis may contribute to linking centrosome integrity with the autophagy-mediated regulation of centriolar satellites and ciliogenesis.

Article.Title: Selection of the most appropriate semiconductor on the DC-DC buck converters by multi-criteria decision making methods
Article.Authors: Yildiriz G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The selection of suitable semiconductor is one of the most important factors affecting the performance of the power electronics circuits. The general characteristics of the circuit such as voltage, current, and switching frequency limit the switch selection. When choosing semiconductors that meet these constraints, the criteria such as switching speed, losses, cost etc. are be taken into consideration. The importance weights of the criteria may vary depending on the expert’s experience and the application conditions. Therefore, to make the best decision, it is necessary to make a choice based on all criteria. In this paper, the most suitable semiconductor selection for a 36–12 V DC-DC buck converter has been made using the multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) methods, MOORA and integrated AHP-TOPSIS firstly in the literature. GaN-transistor, IGBT and power MOSFET has been evaluated according to the four criteria. The consistency of the results obtained with both MOORA and the integrated AHP-TOPSIS methods demonstrates that these methods are successful in determining the most suitable semiconductor in power electronics applications where there is more than one option.

Article.Title: Chitosan from Penaeus monodon prawn shell waste by Bacillus subtilis fermentation-assisted deproteinization and its evaluation for turbidity removal from water and po​stharvest coating of grapes
Article.Authors: H. R.; Joshi K.; Navalgund L.; El Qada E.; Mubarak N.; AlGhamdi A.; Shet V.; K. S.; S. H.; Chandra S.
Article.Abstract: The crustacean shell waste generated by the shellfish industry poses a significant threat to the environment. Extracting chitin from invertebrate exoskeletons can reduce shell-waste disposal costs. This study aimed to convert Penaeus monodon shell waste into chitosan via a fermentation-assisted route and to test one batch of the product as both a coagulant for turbid water and a postharvest coating for grapes. Waste shells of the prawn Penaeus monodon were the starting material in the present study: conventional chemical extraction yielded chitin, fermentation with Bacillus subtilis removed the residual protein, and three days of deacetylation in 65% sodium hydroxide at room temperature then yielded chitosan. The chitin yield was 32% on dry raw shell, and the chitosan yield was 48% on the chitin charged to deacetylation, using two different bases. XRD showed crystalline peaks at 2θ = 11.38°, 18.04° and 22.6°; FT-IR showed the characteristic bands of chitosan, and SEM showed a smooth, compact surface without cracks. The as-prepared chitosan had moisture and ash contents of 4.1% and 1.9%, respectively. Viscosity was 55.933 cP, and the degree of deacetylation was 53.44%, below the range usually reported for commercial grades. In jar tests on silt-laden water, removal was greatest at pH 5, where a 0.2 mg/L chitosan solution removed 80.2 ± 1.2% of the turbidity and 76.1 ± 1.0% of the total solids (mean ± SD, n = 3); larger doses lowered removal through re-stabilisation. As a coating on grapes stored at ambient temperature, the chitosan cut the seven-day weight loss from 64.0 ± 0.9% to 41.7 ± 1.1%, about one-third less than in uncoated fruit, and limited the rise in juice pH (4.93 ± 0.02 against 5.26 ± 0.03). These results, from triplicate runs on one batch of chitosan, indicate that low-DD chitosan from prawn shell waste can act as both a coagulant and a postharvest coating.

Article.Title: Ultra-swelling pH-responsive hybrid hydrogel for oral heparin delivery
Article.Authors: Ashraf M.; Mahjub A.; Davachi S.; Nejad S.; Harandi D.; Harofteh M.; Mahjub R.
Article.Abstract: Oral delivery of heparin remains challenging because of poor stability and limited site-specific release within the gastrointestinal tract. Herein, an ultra-swelling pH-responsive hybrid hydrogel based on chitosan, acrylic acid, and 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate (HEMA) was developed through low-temperature redox-initiated graft copolymerization and statistically optimized using a Box–Behnken design. The effects of the monomer-to-chitosan ratio, initiator concentration, and crosslinker content on hydrogel performance were systematically evaluated. Structural, morphological, and thermal characteristics were confirmed by FTIR, XRD, SEM, DSC, and TGA analyses. The optimized hydrogel exhibited a highly porous architecture and an exceptional swelling ratio exceeding 4000% under near-neutral conditions while maintaining limited swelling in acidic media. Heparin loading and in vitro release studies demonstrated minimal drug release at gastric pH and rapid, sustained release at neutral to mildly alkaline pH, reflecting the transition from stomach to intestinal environments. The combination of statistical optimization, pronounced pH responsiveness, and selective heparin release highlights the advantages of this hydrogel over conventional formulations. These findings establish the optimized chitosan-g-poly(AA-co-HEMA) hydrogel as a promising platform for oral delivery of heparin and other pH-sensitive therapeutics requiring controlled gastrointestinal release.

Article.Title: Influence of different methods of sealer agitation on the quality of root canal obturation: a micro-CT study
Article.Authors: Campelo D.; Cordeiro R.; Limoeiro A.; Marceliano-Alves M.; Seckler I.; Lopes R.; de Almeida A.; Mehta V.; Carneiro R.; Frozoni M.
Article.Abstract: This study evaluated the effect of different agitation techniques for AH Plus Jet endodontic cement on the volume occupied, void spaces in the obturation mass in the cervical and apical 5 mm of the canal, and cement extrusion in oval canals of lower molars. Distal roots from 30 replicas of human lower molars were instrumented and analyzed using micro-CT. The samples were randomly divided into three groups (n = 10) based on the agitation technique: Group PA (control) – applicator tip attached to a 1 mL syringe; Group PUI – applicator tip attached to a 1 mL syringe with agitation using the Irrisonic ultrasonic tip (E1, Helse Ultrasonic, Brazil); and Group PS – applicator tip attached to a 1 mL syringe with agitation using the sonic tip 25.04 Perfect Clean (Microdont, Brazil). The teeth were obturated using the vertical compaction technique and the AH Plus Jet sealer, then rescanned via micro-CT to evaluate the volume filled, void spaces, and extrusion of sealer. The results showed no statistically significant differences in the volume occupied or void spaces between the groups, regardless of agitation method (p = 0.633). Sealer extrusion was also not influenced by agitation (p = 0.755). The agitation of AH Plus Jet sealer, whether using ultrasonic or sonic tips, did not improve the reduction of void spaces in the obturation mass or increase the extrusion of material, showing no added benefit to the root canal obturation process.

Article.Title: Exploring the neuroprotective potential of aprepitant against nicotine-induced molecular, histological, and behavioral sequels
Article.Authors: Asoudeh H.; Qomi M.; Maraashi S.; Hayes A.; Gholami M.; Motaghinejad M.
Article.Abstract: Chronic nicotine exposure causes molecular and behavioral impairments. APRE, a selective NK1R antagonist, has neuroprotective potential. This study investigated whether APRE could protect against nicotine-induced neurotoxicity and mood- and motor-related behavioral changes in adult male Wistar rats. Forty-eight male Wistar rats were randomly assigned to six groups (n = 8) and treated intraperitoneally once daily for three weeks: group 1 received normal saline (0.5 mL/rat), group 2 received nicotine (10 mg/kg), groups 3–5 received nicotine (10 mg/kg) plus APRE (20, 40, or 80 mg/kg), and group 6 received APRE alone (80 mg/kg). Mood- and motor-related behaviors were assessed using OFT, EPM, and FST. In the hippocampus, mitochondrial function, oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis-related JNK/Bcl-2/Bax signaling, Beclin-1, and qualitative and quantitative histopathological changes in the DG and CA1 regions were investigated. APRE significantly attenuated nicotine-induced mood and motor disturbances. It also increased SOD, GPx, GR activity, TAC, ATP, MMP, GSH, and unphosphorylated Bcl-2, while reducing ROS, MDA, H2O2, GSSG, TNF-α, IL-1β, both forms of JNK, Bax, Beclin-1, and phosphorylated Bcl-2. In nicotine-exposed rats, APRE also significantly improved qualitative and quantitative histopathological changes in the DG and CA1 regions of the rat’s hippocampus. APRE mitigated multiple untoward effects of nicotine exposure, including behavioral disturbances, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, cell death, and histopathological damage in the rat’s hippocampus.

Article.Title: Gender affirmation concerns of aging transgender women: findings from qualitative listening sessions
Article.Authors: Lau M.; Velazco N.; Arangure J.; Karris M.; Blumenthal J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Older transgender persons are a specific minoritized population with unique health and care concerns. The needs and priorities of older transgender adults are poorly understood, likely due to implicit biases surrounding age, sexuality, and gender. Four listening sessions were conducted with transgender women, ages 55 years old and above, in the San Diego and Palm Springs area between August and November 2023. Two sessions were held in-person in English, one was held virtually in English, and one was held in-person in Spanish. Individuals were recruited through local clinics, community-based organizations, and social media. All sessions were audio-recorded, transcribed, translated as needed, and analyzed using a rapid thematic analysis approach. Nineteen individuals participated (median age 62 years, range 55–87). Of the 16 who completed the demographics questionnaire, all identified as transgender female and/or female. Four identified as Hispanic/Latinx, 7 as White, 1 as Black/African American, 1 as American Indian/Alaska Native, and 3 as mixed race. Six were living with HIV and taking anti-retroviral therapy. Participants expressed concerns about aging, including companionship, financial security, access to routine healthcare maintenance screenings, and safe housing. These concerns were balanced by future aging goals like living authentically and mentoring younger generations. 75% were using gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT), and most shared frustrations with inconsistent provider guidance on GAHT duration, dosing, method of administration, and long-term risks. Many viewed GAHT as essential, despite potential risks. While all participants reported positive and negative healthcare experiences, many emphasized a desire for providers to address mental and sexual health more openly and to be better informed about community resources. Older transgender adults represent a heterogenous population with distinct medical, psychological, and social needs. Identifying their key concerns is essential to advancing patient-centered, transgender-informed research and improving care for this historically underserved population.

Article.Title: Changes in circulating biomarkers in symptomatic atrial fibrillation from before to one day after catheter ablation
Article.Authors: Jackson A.; Fröbert O.; Boye Larsen D.; Giordano R.; Arendt-Nielsen L.; Björkenheim A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Atrial fibrillation (AF) causes debilitating symptoms in some patients, whereas others remain asymptomatic; the biological basis remains unclear. In this prospective case–control study, we investigated whether circulating biomarkers were associated with symptom burden, differed between patients with symptomatic AF and controls, and differed between samples collected before catheter ablation and on the first post-procedural day. We enrolled 100 patients undergoing first-time AF ablation and 100 age- and sex-matched controls; one patient with AF was excluded because of compromised blood samples. Symptoms were assessed using the AF6 questionnaire and EHRA score. Ninety-two proteins were measured using the Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel, and six additional biomarkers were analysed locally. The median AF6 was 23 (IQR 14–32), and 46% had modified EHRA score III. No statistically significant biomarker–symptom associations were detected after Bonferroni correction. In age- and sex-adjusted comparisons, 12 biomarkers differed between patients with AF and controls, including higher NT-proBNP, CCL20, and CXCL10, and lower FGF-19. On the first post-procedural day, 51 biomarkers differed significantly from pre-procedural levels, with the largest increases observed for hs-TnI, IL-6, and hs-CRP. These findings demonstrate biomarker differences between AF patients and controls and an acute post-procedural response consistent with myocardial injury and inflammation. Clinical trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05201989 09/01/2022.

Article.Title: Quality and readability of large language model–generated responses on type 2 diabetes remission: a cross-sectional balanced factorial study
Article.Authors: Wu W.; Qin N.; Kang X.; Jiang L.; Gao Q.; Liu C.; Li Z.; Liao S.; Li G.; Li J.; Ji H.; Lian F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for patient education and medical information delivery. However, their outputs may involve trade-offs among medical accuracy, comprehensiveness, empathy, and readability. Type 2 diabetes remission is a clinically nuanced concept that is readily misunderstood by patients, making it a suitable context in which to evaluate both the medical quality and patient accessibility of artificial intelligence–generated health information. To systematically compare the medical quality and readability of responses concerning type 2 diabetes remission generated by different LLMs and prompting strategies, and to characterize their joint quality–readability profiles. We conducted a cross-sectional study using a balanced factorial design. Responses were generated for 16 core questions concerning type 2 diabetes remission using 4 LLMs—DeepSeek-V3.2,GPT-5.5,Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Sonnet 4.6—and 6 prompting strategies: Keyword, Question, 6th-grade, Guideline, Patient, and Doctor. This yielded 384 AI-generated responses. Two endocrinologists, each with more than 5 years of clinical experience, independently evaluated medical quality using a prespecified rubric. Five domains—Accuracy, Relevance, Comprehensiveness, Empathy, and Falsehood avoidance—were rated on 5-point ordinal scales. A descriptive Composite quality score was also calculated. Readability was assessed using the Flesch Reading Ease Score (FRES), Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL), Gunning Fog Index (GFOG), and Simple Measure of Gobbledygook (SMOG). Quality ratings were analyzed using cumulative link mixed models, whereas readability outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models; Question ID was included as a random intercept in all models. Exploratory analyses examined Spearman correlations between readability and quality and identified Pareto-efficient model–prompt combinations. All 384 responses were included in the analysis, with no missing data. The descriptive Composite quality score ranged from 4.175 for Gemini 3.1 Pro to 4.285 for DeepSeek-V3.2 across models and from 4.066 for the 6th-grade strategy to 4.350 for the Doctor strategy across prompting strategies. Cumulative link mixed models showed significant main effects of model across all 5 quality domains: Accuracy (LR χ² = 10.964, LR-based pseudo-R² = 0.0281, 95% CI 0.0015–0.0636, P = 0.012), Relevance (LR χ² = 54.042, LR-based pseudo-R² = 0.1313, 95% CI 0.0688–0.1974, P < 0.001), Comprehensiveness (LR χ² = 12.018, LR-based pseudo-R² = 0.0308, 95% CI 0.0025–0.0677, P = 0.007), Empathy (LR χ² = 50.905, LR-based pseudo-R² = 0.1242, 95% CI 0.0632–0.1890, P < 0.001), and Falsehood avoidance (LR χ² = 18.752, LR-based pseudo-R² = 0.0477, 95% CI 0.0107–0.0922, P < 0.001). Prompting strategy also showed significant main effects across the quality domains, with the largest effect observed for Empathy (LR χ² = 243.836, LR-based pseudo-R² = 0.4701, 95% CI 0.3786–0.5477, P < 0.001). Descriptively, GPT-5.5 had the numerically highest mean scores for Accuracy (4.448) and Falsehood avoidance (4.469), whereas DeepSeek-V3.2 had the numerically highest mean scores for Relevance (4.948), Comprehensiveness (4.427), and Empathy (3.615). Among prompting strategies, Patient had the numerically highest mean Empathy score (4.359), whereas Doctor had the numerically highest mean Comprehensiveness score (4.609). For readability, both model and prompting strategy showed significant main effects on FRES, FKGL, GFOG, and SMOG. DeepSeek-V3.2 had the numerically highest mean FRES (51.28), whereas Claude Sonnet 4.6 had the lowest (32.98); among prompting strategies, 6th-grade had the numerically highest mean FRES (69.70), whereas Doctor had the lowest (27.50). In an exploratory response-level correlation analysis that did not account for clustering within Question ID and was intended for hypothesis generation only, FRES was positively correlated with Empathy (ρ = 0.53) and negatively correlated with Comprehensiveness, Falsehood avoidance, and the Composite quality score (ρ = −0.46, − 0.40, and − 0.26, respectively; FDR-adjusted q < 0.001), indicating directionally divergent association patterns between readability and different dimensions of medical quality. In patient-education responses related to type 2 diabetes remission, LLM output performance was influenced by both model choice and prompting strategy. No single model–prompt combination consistently outperformed the others across all evaluated outcomes. Within the T2DM remission question set examined in this study, response optimization required trade-offs among accuracy, comprehensiveness, readability, falsehood avoidance, and empathy.

Article.Title: Humic acid–Fe–kaolinite composite for robust phosphate removal from complex wastewater matrices
Article.Authors: Al-Mur B.; Jamal M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Consistently achieving high phosphate removal across diverse water chemistries remains a significant obstacle in adsorption-based nutrient management. This study developed a humic acid–Fe–kaolinite (HA–Fe–Ka) composite integrating Fe-bearing reactive phases, humic functional groups, and a kaolinite mineral framework. The composite was generated via ferrihydrite coating followed by humic acid immobilization and characterized using FTIR, XRD, SEM–EDX, and BET analyses. Structural characterization indicated retention of the kaolinite framework together with Fe-bearing phases and humic functional groups, yielding a mesoporous material with a surface area of 52.7 m 2 g −1 . Batch adsorption trials showed phosphate removal of 88.1–96.7% across pH 3–11, with the highest removal at pH 7. Adsorption kinetics were best described by the pseudo-second-order model (R 2 ≈ 1.00). Langmuir fitting gave R 2 = 0.9956, qmax = 89.206 mg g −1 , and K L = 0.0749 L mg −1 . Thermodynamic analysis based on the reported distribution coefficients gave ΔG values of − 1.68 to − 4.91 kJ mol −1 for HA–Fe–Ka, with ΔH = + 10.36 kJ mol −1 and ΔS = + 43.77 J mol −1 K −1 , consistent with an endothermic adsorption process. Application to phosphate-affected waters in Saudi Arabia gave removal efficiencies of 79–84% in freshwater matrices and 55–61% in marine matrices. Overall, the results identify HA–Fe–Ka as a promising sorbent for phosphate removal from chemically complex waters.

Article.Title: Microscopic observation of magnetization response shaped by magnetic anisotropy in a single magnetic nanoparticle
Article.Authors: Urano S.; Ito H.; Yamazaki K.; Futagawa M.; Ota S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Magnetization response under a magnetic field with thermal fluctuations is important for designing magnetic nanoparticles, which are extensively studied for biomedical applications. The magnetic properties of magnetic nanoparticles have conventionally been measured as net magnetization. In this study, the magnetization distribution in a single magnetic nanoparticle under a static magnetic field was observed using magnetic force microscopy. After the easy axis of the particle associated with magnetic anisotropy was aligned, the effects of magnetic anisotropy, the applied magnetic field, and thermal fluctuations on the magnetization orientation were analyzed. The single-particle magnetization response was then compared with the net magnetization response obtained from the static measurement and numerical simulations. The effects of magnetic moment and anisotropy energy on the magnetization distribution were evaluated by measuring single-core magnetic nanoparticles with different core diameters. Our measurement approach for magnetization response in a single magnetic nanoparticle also contributes to the analysis of the dipolar field affecting surrounding particles.

Article.Title: Self-reported polysubstance use is negatively associated with prospective memory in university students
Article.Authors: Celaya X.; O’Rourke H.; Brewer G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The present study investigated self-reported patterns of substance use and prospective memory ability. Participants completed a self-report survey of their drug use history (ten substances and use-related behaviors), a self-report measure of prospective and retrospective memory failures, and a laboratory-based prospective memory task under one of two encoding conditions (standard or implementation intention). To better represent naturalistic patterns of substance use, a latent class analysis was applied to binary indicators of substance use. Class membership was then used as a categorical predictor of prospective memory. The latent class analysis revealed three classes: non-use, alcohol-cannabis use, and polysubstance use. Latent class was associated with both self-reported and laboratory-based prospective memory, and the polysubstance use class reported the most everyday memory failures. Implementation intention encoding improved task performance but did not interact with latent class. In sum, latent class analysis provided an ecological representation of how patterns of substance use can be classified and associated with prospective memory deficits.

Article.Title: Retrieval practice reshapes neighboring memories in a naturalistic continuous-recognition dataset
Article.Authors: Liu X.; Li Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Retrieval can facilitate or impair related memories, but most evidence comes from laboratory paradigms with experimenter-defined relationships. Here, we asked whether retrieval-related associations emerge in temporal neighborhoods of a large naturalistic continuous-recognition dataset. We analyzed 72,402 target tests from the Natural Scenes Dataset and modeled target recognition as a function of prior tests of neighboring images. Closest-neighbor analyses showed a local dissociation: accurate same-session neighbor retrieval predicted better target recognition, whereas accurate across-session neighbors and inaccurate same-session neighbors predicted poorer target recognition. Accumulated weighted-history models showed broader positive associations for accurate retrieval history and negative associations for inaccurate same-session history. These findings suggest that retrieval-related spillover in naturalistic memory depends jointly on retrieval success, session context, and neighborhood scale.

Article.Title: Validation of 2D video-based movement analysis tools for assessing human fall impact kinematics
Article.Authors: Lim K.; Park J.; Chun S.; Kim D.; Yoon S.; Choi W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) video-based pose estimation offers a low-cost complement to three-dimensional motion capture (MOCAP) for quantifying fall impact kinematics, yet few studies have compared the available tools under controlled conditions. We compared the accuracy and agreement of six 2D pose estimation tools, one manually digitized (Kinovea) and five AI-based (OpenPose, RTMPose, and MediaPipe-lite/full/heavy), against a MOCAP reference. Eighteen healthy young adults fell in three directions under two fall types, with each trial recorded simultaneously by MOCAP and an iPhone. We found that Kinovea showed the highest agreement for peak vertical velocity (ICC = 0.902), while OpenPose and RTMPose showed the lowest error among the AI-based tools. All six tools underestimated peak vertical velocity by 9% on average (13% in MediaPipe-heavy). Errors were smallest in forward falls for both outcomes. Among the AI-based tools, peak vertical velocity errors were greatest in sideways falls for four of five tools, but Kinovea showed its greatest error in backward falls. For horizontal velocity, all six tools showed agreement with MOCAP (ICC = 0.83 to 0.90); no pairwise differences between the AI-based tools were significant after Bonferroni correction. These findings may guide tool selection for fall kinematics research. Further validation is needed for surveillance footage.

Article.Title: Simultaneous correction of spectral-line bending across multiple slits in a slit recombination hyperspectral imager with multiple viewing angles
Article.Authors: Niu Y.; Wang L.; Zhang J.; Lin C.; Ji Z.; Fu Y.; Zheng Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Simultaneous spectral-line bending correction is required for the central and off-axis slit channels of a multi-angle slit-recombination hyperspectral imager. This study develops a modeling and optimization method using an oppositely oriented dual-material prism group. The model describes spectral-line bending as a function of wavelength, slit channel, and position along the slit. A prism-group merit function guides material screening, and a system-level merit function incorporating distortion guides genetic-algorithm optimization of the prism parameters. Complete-system optimization and numerical evaluation are performed in Zemax for a three-slit design operating over 410–900 nm, using the H-QF3/D-ZLaF81-25 prism group as the sole dispersive element. For the evaluated wavelengths and field positions spanning 410–900 nm, the maximum optical spectral-resolution bandwidths, quantified by the full width at half maximum (FWHM) of the wavelength-domain line-spread function (LSF), are 9.35, 9.43, and 9.75 nm for the + 15°, 0°, and − 15° viewing channels, respectively, all below the 10-nm requirement. The ray-tracing results show that the three slit spectra are geometrically separated on the detector plane. The spectral-line bending and keystone distortion of all slit channels are less than 0.5 effective pixel in the spectral and spatial directions, respectively. At 650 and 900 nm, the sagittal and tangential optical modulation transfer function (MTF) values exceed 0.7 at 25 lp/mm for the plotted field points in all three slit channels. Relative to a reference with two upright prisms, the optimized design reduces the maximum absolute spectral-line bending to 0.0012–0.0024 mm, with an average reduction of approximately 94%. This method provides a design reference for multi-angle hyperspectral imaging systems with low spectral-line bending and geometrically separated slit spectra.

Article.Title: Fuzzy adaptive PID attitude control of quadcopter unmanned aerial vehicle with airborne radar in autonomous flight mode
Article.Authors: Qian Y.; Yaowen C.; Nannan Z.; Lixia L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper studies a fuzzy adaptive PID control method for a quadcopter UAV equipped with an airborne three-coordinate radar operating in autonomous counter-drone mode. A mathematical model of the quadcopter is first established, and a cascade control architecture is adopted in which fuzzy adaptive PID is applied to the outer position control loops to adjust PID parameters online based on the relative attitude and distance deviation detected by the onboard radar. The horizontal position loops generate roll and pitch references tracked by fixed-gain inner PID controllers. Simulation compares outer-loop adaptation with fixed-gain PID and inner-loop fuzzy PID to assess its effect on attitude transients within the cascade. A universe-of-discourse sensitivity analysis is conducted to examine the effect of FIS input domain size on control performance, and a 21-state closed-loop stability verification with Monte Carlo robustness check under parameter uncertainties is presented. An experimental platform consisting of two quadcopters and an STM32-based flight controller is built for validation. The yaw and pitch MAPE values were 0.1235% and 0.1963%, respectively, for the tested trajectory. In addition, dynamic horizontal calibration tests are performed for the airborne radar, and the altitude measurement error characteristics at different ranges are quantitatively analyzed via segmented RMSE, providing empirical support for the sensing link of the countermeasure system.

Article.Title: An exploratory retrospective study of low bone density and perioperative D-dimer and Wells score after unicompartmental knee arthroplasty
Article.Authors: Hartono F.; Wangsa A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The present study aimed to examine the association between bone mineral density (BMD) and perioperative D-dimer levels and Wells scores in patients undergoing unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA), with adjustment for potential confounding factors including age and sex. The study was exploratory and was not designed to establish causality or to evaluate imaging-confirmed thrombotic outcomes. A retrospective cohort study of 97 consecutive UKA procedures was conducted. BMD was categorized as normal, osteopenia, or osteoporosis based on dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry. Serum D-dimer was measured preoperatively and on postoperative day 3 (POD 3), together with the Wells score. The primary analysis employed multivariable Gamma regression with log link, adjusted for BMI and preoperative D-dimer, withan extended model additionally incorporating age and sex. Model robustness was evaluated through non-parametric bootstrap resampling (10,000 iterations), permutation testing (10,000 permutations), and female-only sensitivity analysis. A further sensitivity analysis reclassified bone density using the femoral neck T-score alone, rather than the lowest T-score of the lumbar spine or femoral neck. Alternative outcome analyses included absolute D-dimer change, POD3/preoperative ratio, log-transformed ordinary least squares with heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors, and quantile regression. Propensity score inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) was performed with standardized mean difference balance diagnostics. Wells score was analysed using the Kruskal-Wallis test, pairwise Mann-Whitney U tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction, dichotomization at Wells score of 0 versus negative 1, and multivariable logistic regression. In the absence of duplex ultrasonography data, a composite DVT risk proxy was constructed based on established D-dimer and Wells score thresholds. Among 97 cases, 75 (77.3%) had low bone density. The primary Gamma regression showed a significant association between low bone density and POD 3 D-dimer (adjusted mean ratio 1.39, 95% CI 1.02 to 1.91, p = 0.040). The extended model incorporating age and sex gave a similar estimate (adjusted mean ratio 1.40, 95% CI 1.01 to 1.93, p = 0.043), as did bootstrap resampling (95% CI 1.10 to 1.76, bootstrap p = 0.004) and IPTW weighting (an adjusted increase of 380.7 ng/mL, 95% CI 136.9 to 624.5, p = 0.002). The Kruskal-Wallis test indicated significant differences in Wells score distribution across bone density groups (H = 7.32, p = 0.026). After Holm-Bonferroni correction, a significant difference was observed between the osteoporosis and osteopenia groups (adjusted p = 0.043). The proportion of patients meeting the composite DVT risk proxy was significantly higher in the osteoporosis group (47.4%) compared with osteopenia (25.0%) and normal BMD (13.6%) groups (p = 0.047). A sensitivity analysis reclassifying bone density using the femoral neck T-score alone attenuated the primary association to non-significance (AMR = 1.17, 95% CI 0.89 to 1.53, p = 0.268). Median quantile regression, the Wells score logistic regression and the adjusted composite proxy analysis did not reach statistical significance. Low bone density, defined by the lowest T-score of the lumbar spine or femoral neck, was associated with higher postoperative D-dimer levels and higher Wells scores following unicompartmental knee arthroplasty. That association disappeared once bone density was defined by the femoral neck alone, and several of the supporting analyses fell short of significance. The study was exploratory and its endpoints were surrogate markers, so these results are best read as a hypothesis for testing; prospective validation with imaging-confirmed endpoints is needed before they can inform clinical practice.

Article.Title: Concentrations and adsorption performance of heavy metals of microplastics from plastic sports fields
Article.Authors: Cheng Q.; Li Y.; Li Y.; Li J.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Plastic sports fields represent a significant source of microplastics (MPs) pollution, yet their heavy metal adsorption characteristics and associated ecological and human health risks remain poorly elucidated. This study investigated the MP release characteristics, heavy metal concentration, and adsorption performance of polyurethane MPs collected from campus plastic sports fields. Results revealed that a standard-sized stadium releases up to 5.96 × 10⁶ MPs per aging cycle, with heavy metal concentrations in MPs following the order: Zn > Mn > Cr > Ni > Pb > Cu > Co > Cd. Total carcinogenic risks (CR) of arsenic (As) and cobalt (Co) across all sampling plots exceeded the acceptable threshold of 1 × 10⁻⁶. Derived risk control values of As (1.85 mg/kg) and Co (7.67 mg/kg) were calculated to provide preliminary reference for pollution management. PU MPs exhibited high saturated adsorption capacity of metals, such as of Cu 2 ⁺ and Zn 2 ⁺. Cu 2 ⁺ displayed a distinct competitive adsorption advantage, especially at high temperatures. These findings highlight the urgent need for enhanced management and regulation of plastic sports facilities to mitigate the combined pollution risks of MPs and heavy metals.

Article.Title: Validation of a deep neural network workflow for fully automated dicentric chromosome analysis in biological dosimetry
Article.Authors: Bucher M.; Brown A.; Hänselmann S.; Moquet J.; Barnard S.; Oestreicher U.; Endesfelder D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence has recently found its way into biological dosimetry. This study validated the initial version of a deep neural network (DNN) workflow implemented by MetaSystems to detect dicentric and polycentric chromosomes in microscopy images. This was performed through parameter optimisation, calibration curve generation and independent testing. Optimisation of thresholds for the class score parameter defining the aberration classes was performed and brought DNN scoring closer to manual scoring ( 60 Co dataset) for low doses by reducing the number of false-positive dicentrics, while balancing the influence of false-negative detections, especially for higher doses. Although slightly higher, the DNN achieved an acceptable yield of dicentrics for the control. A comparison of the calibration curves showed that the DNN curve was between manual and semi-automatic curves. DNN curves based on two independent test datasets (X-ray) from different laboratories showed very good agreement, with dose estimations matching the reference doses for all 12/13 test samples precisely, even for low doses and for triage scoring. This DNN-workflow enables the establishment of calibration curves for different radiation qualities and successfully performs dose estimations. It could replace semi-automated scoring and enhance the capacity of biological dosimetry laboratories in the event of large-scale radiological or nuclear incidents.

Article.Title: Action-conditioned latent Kalman filtering for robust spatio-temporal state estimation of deformable object
Article.Authors: Gao D.; Melibary M.; Hu J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Robust spatio-temporal state estimation from noisy observations is a critical challenge in robotic manipulation. Current latent space representations derived from dynamic point clouds often suffer from severe perceptual noise and occlusions, leading to discontinuous trajectories and pronounced temporal jitter. To mitigate these artifacts, we propose an Action-Conditioned Latent Kalman Filter (AC-LKF) framework. Leveraging a hybrid architecture of PointNet++ and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), our method models non-linear temporal dynamics within a low-dimensional latent manifold. Instead of claiming to fully model the physical causality of deformable-object dynamics, AC-LKF incorporates the robot end-effector displacement as a low-dimensional, observable, and task-relevant kinematic prior to condition the latent state transition. Furthermore, a heteroscedastic latent filtering module adaptively estimates process and measurement uncertainties, balancing the action-conditioned prior with degraded visual inputs under noise and occlusion. Evaluations using quantitative temporal metrics and reconstruction errors, supplemented by principal component analysis (PCA) and t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) visualizations, show that AC-LKF improves latent trajectory smoothness, information retention, and dynamic robustness by reducing abrupt observation-induced state transitions. These results indicate that kinematic action conditioning can improve the temporal consistency and robustness of learned geometric state representations for interactive deformable-object manipulation.

Article.Title: Development and validation of a cell death gene signature for overall survival in clear cell renal cell carcinoma
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Li J.; Zhang Y.; Zhang M.; Hu X.
Article.Abstract: Kidney renal clear carcinoma (KIRC) is a common genitourinary malignancy with high morbidity and mortality rates despite multimodal therapies. Programmed cell death (PCD) is an active death process that occurs not only in the normal development of individuals but also in abnormal physiological states or diseases. PCD pathways dysfunction is associated with the formation and progression of cancers. Expression profiles of KIRC specimens and corresponding clinical information were obtained from the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and ArrayExpress databases. Single-cell transcriptome were collected from GEO database. Eight cell death pathways genes were downloaded from Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes database, Gene Set Enrichment Analysis website, Human Autophagy Database website and FerrDb website and the literature, respectively. Consensus clustering analysis, differential gene analysis, survival analysis, correlation analysis, immune cell infiltration analysis, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression analysis, univariate and multivariate Cox analysis were conducted using R software. Experimental validation was performed using RT-qPCR, Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, siRNA-mediated gene knockdown, and flow cytometry. We identified three cell death-relevant subtypes of KIRC based on 709 genes of eight PCD-related pathways. Each cluster displayed distinct clinical, cellular, and immunological characteristics. Moreover, a novel cell death related prognostic model was constructed in this research. Survival analysis and time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated that the model was reliable and robust not only in TCGA cohort, but also in an external validation dataset (E-MTAB-1980 cohort). In addition, RT-qPCR results confirmed the differential expressions of DEGs in the tissue samples, which was in line with the results of TCGA. Western blotting and immunohistochemistry further confirmed the elevated protein expression of IRF9, CXCL2, and EIF4EBP1 in KIRC tissues. In addition, siRNA-mediated IRF9 knockdown increased apoptosis in 786-O and A-498 cells. This study identified three cell death-relevant subtypes of KIRC based on the genes of eight PCD-related pathways, which were associated with OS and DSS of KIRC. We also defined a novel prognostic model of seven cell death-related genes, which was proven to be independently associated with the OS of KIRC, and the prognostic model was validated in an external dataset. The experimental findings further suggest that IRF9 may contribute to apoptosis resistance in ccRCC cells.

Article.Authors: Kim D.; Kim D.; Lee W.; Kim Y.; Lozanoff S.; Lee U.
Article.Abstract: Craniofacial reconstruction is a pivotal process in identifying unknown individuals by estimating facial feature positions and soft-tissue thickness from the skull. This study aimed to bridge this gap by establishing a relationship between the alveolar ridge and lip morphology within a Korean population. Under 10-fold cross-validation, the proposed sex- and age-specific regression equations achieved an overall mean absolute error of 1.445 mm, with 73.8% of predictions falling within the ± 2.0 mm forensic threshold. By replacing subjective estimations with objective, data-driven equations, this study offers a standardised reference for forensic facial approximation in Korean adults.

Article.Title: Multi-polarized nested metasurface antenna stacking for satellite-assisted Internet of Vehicles
Article.Authors: Gunasekaran S.; Anbazhagan R.; Chinnusami M.
Article.Abstract: A novel, multi-polarized, multi-band, metasurface stacked patch antenna has been developed for satellite-assisted Internet of Vehicles (IoV) communication. The antenna features an aperture-coupled, integrated dual-flipped L-slot patch (IDFLP) stacked layer. A patch is fed via a rectangular slot aperture. To optimize performance, the nested complementary dual split-ring (NCDSR) metasurface is integrated into the IDFLP layer. The NCDSR-IDFLP antenna has a footprint of 25 × 25 mm and operates at multi-band frequencies of 7.4 GHz, 11.51 GHz, and 14.15 GHz, with good impedance matching ( < −10 dB). The multi-band frequencies have peak gains of 3.8 dBi, 4.69 dBi, and 8.82 dBi, respectively. The simulated axial ratio (AR) is < 1.23 dB at the Ku band. A metasurface antenna is mounted on a vehicle rooftop to study real-time scenarios. The proposed nested metasurface antenna was fabricated and tested for satellite-assisted 6G autonomous vehicular networks.

Article.Title: Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy of buffy coat distinguishes acute myeloid and lymphoblastic leukemia
Article.Authors: Juntararuangtong T.; Tanthanuch W.; Kaarj K.; Artsang P.; Kreepala C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) are distinct hematologic malignancies requiring accurate differentiation. This proof-of-concept study investigated Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectral differences in peripheral blood buffy-coat specimens from 30 patients with AML, 24 with ALL, and 10 healthy controls. Spectra were preprocessed using extended multiplicative signal correction and Savitzky–Golay second derivatives and analyzed using peak-area analysis, hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA), principal component analysis (PCA), and partial least-squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA). Group-associated differences were observed in protein-, ester-carbonyl-, phosphate-, and carbohydrate-associated spectral regions. PCA and HCA showed exploratory clustering, with clearer separation between healthy-control and leukemia observations than between AML and ALL. Using a spectral-observation-level 67:33 model-development/held-out prediction split, PLS-DA achieved accuracies of 98.92–100.00%, sensitivities of 97.79–100.00%, and specificities of 98.02–100.00%. These findings demonstrate group-associated spectral variation and high internal spectral-level classification performance but represent analytical discrimination rather than patient-level diagnostic accuracy. Participant-wise model development and independent external validation in larger, demographically balanced cohorts are required before clinical utility can be established.

Article.Title: A weather integrated neural symbolic dispatch framework for power system operational security
Article.Authors: Dahal S.; Mishra S.; Hegglid G.; Chhetri B.; Jha S.; Øyvang T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Modern power systems face unprecedented challenges from rapid digitalization, electrification of new sectors, and increasing renewable integration. These changes demand real-time operational decisions based on accurate weather forecasting, as traditional dispatch methods cannot handle the speed and complexity of weather-driven variability in renewable generation. This paper thus proposes the Weather-Integrated Neural-Symbolic Dispatch System (WINDS), a novel methodological framework designed to incorporate weather-driven uncertainties into power system dispatch decisions. The WINDS framework combines weather forecasting and neuro-symbolic reasoning, where neural learning methods address weather-related uncertainties and symbolic methods enforce system security constraints, to provide operators with actionable dispatch strategies. Through a detailed set of study cases comprising normal operations, extreme weather events, missing data conditions, and multi-scenario risk analysis, evaluated on both a controlled experiment and measured wind and load data from the Danish DK1 bidding zone, WINDS reduces operational cost by 11.4% to 26.7% compared to static climatology-based dispatch depending on weather volatility, while reducing constraint-violation volume by more than 80% relative to forecast-only dispatch and substantially limiting violations during a measured extreme ramp-down event through adaptive uncertainty margins, with a novel L consistency metric quantifying the alignment between neural predictions and symbolic constraints. WINDS utilizes the strengths of both data-driven and symbolic approaches, enhancing system security and reliability, especially in renewables-rich regions sensitive to weather variability. This work presents a clearly defined methodological framework, and the results provide a proof-of-concept, paving the way for real-world implementation and operational enhancement in weather-sensitive power systems.

Article.Authors: Pande M.; Chaudhary A.; Rajput P.; Kumar S.; Mohanty A.; Singh V.; Patel A.; Sirohi A.; Kumar S.; Saha S.; Singh A.; Chand N.; Anjali N/A.; Divya D.; Biswas A.; Sachan V.; Mahajan S.

A total of 24 ejaculates collected from three clinically healthy bulls were incubated with Resiquimod at concentrations of 0.2, 0.4, and 0.6 µM, separated into upper and lower sperm fractions, cryopreserved, and subsequently evaluated for semen quality, cryosurvivability, and X/Y sperm enrichment. The 0.4 µM group showed the most pronounced enrichment, with significantly lower MAOA CT values in the lower fraction and lower SRY CT values in the upper fraction compared with the control. Following cryopreservation, semen quality declined in all groups; however, post-thaw functional parameters at 0.2 and 0.4 µM remained comparable to the control, whereas 0.6 µM significantly impaired sperm quality ( p < 0.05). Overall, the findings indicated that Resiquimod, particularly at 0.4 µM, may provide a practical, economical and less invasive approach for partial enrichment of X- and Y-bearing spermatozoa under routine semen processing conditions without markedly compromising cryosurvivability.

Article.Title: Comparative analysis of gate-dielectric effects on the analog and linearity performance of MoS2-, MoSe2-, and WS2-based FETs
Article.Authors: Ahmad M.; Imam M.; Mech B.; Askari S.; Awasthi M.; Sreenivasulu V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This work investigates the influence of gate dielectric engineering on the analog, RF, and linearity performance of transition metal dichalcogenide field-effect transistors (TMD-FETs). A self-consistent non-equilibrium Green’s function (NEGF)-based simulation framework is employed to analyze MoS 2 -, MoSe 2 -, and WS₂-based FETs integrated with different high-k gate dielectrics. The impact of dielectric materials on electrostatic integrity, carrier transport, transistor efficiency ( g m / I D ), quality factor (Q-factor), and RF linearity metrics is systematically examined. Key device parameters including ON current ( I ON ), OFF current ( I OFF ), current ON/OFF ratio ( I ON / I OFF ), subthreshold swing (SS), transconductance ( g m ), second-order transconductance ( g m2 ), and third-order transconductance ( g m3 ) are evaluated. The results demonstrate that high-k dielectrics significantly enhance gate electrostatic control, resulting in improved ON-state current, reduced SS, enhanced g m / I D efficiency, and superior Q-factor characteristics. Furthermore, the use of high-k dielectrics shifts the peaks of g m2 and g m3 toward lower gate voltages, indicating improved low-voltage RF linearity behavior. Among the investigated materials, WS₂-based FETs exhibit superior transconductance and RF performance characteristics, while MoS 2 -based devices provide an excellent trade-off between power efficiency, nonlinear distortion behavior, and analog/RF characteristics. The findings offer essential insights for optimizing dielectric–channel combinations in next-generation low-power, high-linearity, and RF-oriented nanoelectronic devices.

Article.Title: Audit-first rollback semantics for safety–critical deployment pipelines
Article.Authors: QIN X.; LUAN S.; YANG C.; LI Z.
Article.Abstract: Deployment runtimes for safety–critical embodied agents keep two records: the live state components execute and the audit chain operators and regulators read. When an upgrade crashes mid-flight, a runtime that fails open keeps the partial deployment running, so the audit chain misstates what runs. We propose audit-first rollback semantics: the revert is attempted before any terminal record is written, and the record states what it did. Provisional state machines with a rollback closure and a bounded soak budget realize the rule; a protocol design extends it to coordinated bridges. We implemented it in a robot-manipulator deployment runtime and compared it with fail-open at 23 enumerated fault sites plus a control and over 10 runs of a 12-point crash grid. The sweep exposed two writes the first implementation left outside its guard and a fallback that lost the divergence flag. With the guard widened, every audit-first trial ended in the specified state; under our stricter coherence check fail-open did so at 5 sites, the ones needing no revert. Over the guarded trials that ended ROLLED_BACK, a terminal record followed within 35.7 ms at the 99th percentile. A terminal record then states what is running or flags that it must be reconciled.

Article.Title: The laforin/malin E3-ubiquitin ligase complex ubiquitinates members of the Hsp70 and Hsp90 protein families
Article.Authors: Gende-Rodriguez P.; Kumarasinghe L.; Tena D.; Lopez-Cantero B.; Garcia-Gimeno M.; Sanz P.
Article.Abstract: The presence of misfolded and aggregated proteins presents a problem in cellular protein homeostasis. To avoid this, cells have evolved powerful protein quality control systems that ensure proper folding or disposal of misfolded and aggregated proteins. Some of these systems are the ATP-dependent chaperones, such as Hsp70s and Hsp90s. Through cycles of binding to substrates and ATP hydrolysis, and with the help of additional co-chaperones, these systems participate in the proper folding of misfolded proteins. The activity of the Hsp70s and Hsp90s is regulated by post-translational modifications, one of them being ubiquitination. In this work, we present evidence of the participation of the laforin/malin complex in the ubiquitination of several components of the Hsp70s and Hsp90s systems, such as HspA1L, Hsp90α, Hsp90β and the co-chaperone Hop/Stip1. In addition, we show that there is a physical interaction between HspA1L and both laforin and malin. In the case of Hsp90α, we observed an interaction with malin but not with laforin, and in the case of Hop/Stip1, both laforin and malin are needed for the interaction with this co-chaperone. Our work identifies the laforin/malin complex as a new E3-ubiquitin ligase that introduces post-translational modifications in these proteins, which may regulate their activity.

Article.Title: Acoustic analysis comparison and model optimization of Chinese ancient and modern oboes
Article.Authors: Niu Y.; Peng P.; Jia Z.; Niu Z.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: As a traditional Chinese double-reed woodwind instrument, the Suona has evolved through representative forms such as the Tang dynasty Bili and Qing dynasty Sunaiyi. However, systematic studies on its acoustic characteristics across historical evolution remain scarce. This work takes the Qing dynasty Sunaiyi and the modern standard Suona as samples, and adopts an integrated approach combining three-dimensional scanning, finite element simulation, and intelligent optimization. High-fidelity axisymmetric finite element models are built based on historical records and scanning data. The two instruments are compared in far-field sound pressure level, directivity, central-axis pressure distribution, and internal sound field, followed by parametric optimization of the modern Suona bell profile. Results show that the Sunaiyi has a longer tube and gentler bell flare and exhibits higher overtone frequencies and unstable high-order overtones. In contrast, the modern Suona, with a shorter tube and steeper bell flare, achieves a lower fundamental overtone, smoother far-field attenuation, and more concentrated directivity. Spectral measurements in a professional studio agree well with simulations, validating the numerical models. A surrogate-assisted K‑means clustering particle swarm optimization algorithm with diversity control (SAPSO‑BCM) is proposed and coupled with COMSOL for global optimization of bell curvature to obtain the optimal radian values under different sound pressure level targets. This work pioneers the integrated three‑dimensional scanning, FEM, and intelligent optimization workflow for Suona acoustics, investigating the influence of structural parameters on radiation performance and offering a generalizable engineering method for traditional wind instruments.

Article.Title: Evolution towards functional stability of buried wood in an anoxic Lab Wood Vault for durable carbon dioxide removal
Article.Authors: Zeng N.; Zapata C.
Article.Abstract: Wood harvesting and storage (WHS) via Wood Vaulting is an emerging carbon dioxide removal method. Its effectiveness hinges on long-term wood preservation but currently our process understanding is limited. A major type of Wood Vault aims to create anoxic (oxygen-free) condition to stop biological degradation. Here we study wood preservation inside a ‘Lab Vault’ where wooden discs are buried under a layer of clay to seal off air with subsequent monitoring of gas concentrations. Our results show 3 stages of gas evolution: (1) Aerobic decomposition: O 2 decreased from 21 to 0% by the consumption of a small amount of organic matter in 10 days, replaced by CO 2 ; (2) Anaerobic decomposition in the next 1.5 months, with CH 4 increased from 0.0002% to 0.2%; (3) A ‘deep anoxic state’ where both aerobic and anaerobic decomposition stop or slow down drastically with zero oxygen and negligible CH 4 generation while CO 2 remains high. The third stage signifies a ‘functional stability’ where wood degradation stops completely. However, long-term maintenance requirement of anoxic condition on millennial timescales cannot be directly inferred from the short-term experiment because anoxic condition was initially created by wood decay. Our experiment suggests that Wood Vault is fundamentally different from landfill, which is often used as a reference in commercial implementation standards. Our results provide direct observational evidence of the initial biophysical processes underlying durable wood preservation, as well as targets for engineering design and monitoring and verification for biomass burial as a climate solution.

Article.Title: Jacobi-enhanced dynamic hypergraph learning for graph-based fraud detection
Article.Authors: Li D.; Shen J.; Yang X.; Qin Z.
Article.Abstract: Financial and e-commerce fraud detection remains challenging because fraudulent entities often exploit structural camouflage, coordinated behaviors, and complex relational dependencies. Existing graph-based approaches mainly rely on pairwise message passing, which may fail to explicitly characterize hidden higher-order affiliations and can suffer from unreliable information propagation under heterophilous graph structures. We propose JK-DHGNN, a dual-view graph learning framework designed for fraud detection scenarios where both observed structural relations and latent higher-order interactions are important. A Top- K dynamic hypergraph generator learns sparse latent affiliations, a Jacobi spectral filter aggregates multi-order graph signals, and a Jacobi polynomial-based KAN-like classifier provides adaptive nonlinear prediction. Experiments on YelpChi, Amazon, and Elliptic demonstrate that JK-DHGNN achieves competitive performance against representative graph-based fraud detection methods. Extensive analyses, including component ablation, dynamic structure analysis, perturbation evaluation, temporal case study, and computational-cost analysis, further reveal that the effectiveness of different modules depends on dataset characteristics and relational structures. These results highlight the potential of combining observed topology, latent higher-order modeling, and adaptive nonlinear classification for graph-based fraud detection.
