Article.Title: Endotracheal application of Ultraviolet A light in Pseudomonas aeruginosa ventilator-associated pneumonia: a sham-controlled large animal study
Article.Authors: Llonch B.; Kiarostami K.; Galli F.; Cabrera R.; Vázquez N.; Rovira-Ribalta N.; Forin E.; Calabretta D.; Guzzardella A.; Bindo F.; Misuraca S.; Miralles C.; Soler-Comas A.; Martinez D.; Fernández-Barat L.; Rigol M.; Rezaie A.; Torres A.; Motos A.
Article.Abstract: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a serious complication in mechanically ventilated patients, with high mortality and costs, so its prevention is a key issue. The narrow-band ultraviolet A (NB-UVA) catheter, emitting UVA light, demonstrated in vitro antimicrobial activity and could help decrease airway bacterial burden and prevent VAP. We aim to evaluate the efficacy and safety of an endotracheally inserted NB-UVA catheter in preventing VAP caused by extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Pseudomonas aeruginosa in a porcine model. Therefore, 10 intubated, mechanically ventilated pigs (41.0 [38.5–43.5] kg) were inoculated with XDR P. aeruginosa and randomized to receive UVA therapy (20 min, twice daily) or sham treatment. Tracheal aspirates and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluids were cultured, inflammatory markers measured, and catheter safety monitored. After 100 h, lung and trachea samples underwent microbiological and histological analysis. Nine animals completed the study. Lung tissue P. aeruginosa burden was similar between the NB-UVA and sham groups (1.48 [0–2.00] log CFU/g vs. 3.37 [2.23–4.32] log CFU/g, p = 0.26). However, microbiologically confirmed pneumonia occurred in fewer lobes (4/25 vs. 15/25, p = 0.003). UVA-treated animals had significantly lower tracheal P. aeruginosa concentrations at 12 h and less neutrophil-mediated interstitial infiltration at histopathological examination. Analysis of ELF cytokines revealed increased levels of IL-10 and reduced levels of IFN-γ. No histological abnormalities, changes in p53 expression, or major adverse events occurred. In conclusion, UVA therapy via the NB-UVA catheter may transiently delay airway the colonisation of the airways by XDR P. aeruginosa and influence the early progession of pneumonia, supporting further research of its potential as an adjunctive strategy for VAP prevention.

Article.Title: Emotional and behavioral asymmetries in user responses to virtual versus human influencers
Article.Authors: Jagodnik K.; Bartal A.
Article.Abstract: As AI virtual influencers (AIVIs) proliferate, understanding human-AI emotional engagement is vital for advancing affective computing. To examine whether AIVIs evoke comparable affective responses to human influencers (HIs), we analyzed 156,918 Instagram comments that received 12+ million likes, integratinglarge language model (LLM)-derived knowledge graphs, emotion analysis, and machine learning. HI-directed discourse shows more differentiated emotional expression and a pattern consistent with more cohesive semantic networks than AIVI-directed discourse. AIVI-directed comments are less likely to express positive affect (24.8% vs. 41.5%) and also less likely to express negative affect (5.8% vs. 9.3%), indicating reduced affective expression of either valence rather than heightened negativity. This group-level tendency is not uniform: affective engagement varies substantially across AIVIs, and that variation is more closely associated with positive than with negative expression. Our Multi-Signal Embedding Network (MSEN), incorporating behavioral metrics and OpenAI semantic embeddings, classified influencer types from behavioral, affective and semantic features (F1 = 0.89), outperforming baselines including a state-of-the-art zero-shot LLM. These findings identify a boundary condition for the Computers Are Social Actors (CASA) paradigm: human-like appearance can elicit social responses without producing affective and semantic response patterns as rich as those elicited by HIs.

Article.Title: Comparing SHAP and distributed-lag model summaries of environmental associations with reported malaria cases in three Nigerian states
Article.Authors: Tanimu J.; Hamada M.; Mashi B.
Article.Abstract: Explainable AI is increasingly used to interpret machine-learning models in public health, but is rarely checked against models that estimate environmental exposure–lag relationships directly. We compared the two on identical inputs. We analysed ten years (2015–2024) of routine monthly confirmed malaria cases from three Nigerian states spanning a low-to-high transmission gradient. A regularised LightGBM model trained on lagged satellite rainfall, temperature and vegetation was interpreted with SHAP; a distributed-lag non-linear model fitted to the same predictors provided a reference. The two agreed on which drivers mattered. Agreement on direction was only partial: the mean-absolute SHAP summary is sign-free, and a signed SHAP check matched the reference model on the leading driver (vegetation, positive) but not on rainfall. Agreement on the timing of effects across monthly lags was not reproducible—across rolling-origin resamples it was centred near zero for every driver and, against a permutation null, was not distinguishable from chance. This is consistent with strong collinearity between neighbouring monthly lags, though with only three collinear drivers we cannot isolate collinearity as the cause. Environmental variables did not improve out-of-sample prediction over a seasonal baseline, suggesting gains lie in finer spatial resolution rather than more covariates.

Article.Title: Physico-mechanical and anisotropic performance of robotic large-scale additive manufacturing using sustainable wood-based PLA composites
Article.Authors: Ziada O.; Chystiakov A.; Čepčianska J.; Ahmed S.; Gomez-Gallegos A.; Kovacikova J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This research investigates large-scale additive manufacturing of functional components from wood–based polymer composite on polylactic acid, containing 20 wt% cellulose fibres derived from birch. The main physico-mechanical characteristics of the printed specimens were evaluated, including tensile strength, flexural strength, hardness, density, water absorption, deformation, and thermophysical properties, as well as the microstructure using optical and scanning electron microscopy. The study investigates printing orientation-dependent anisotropy, which remains insufficiently characterised for PLA-based wood composites produced by LSAM. The influence of printing strategy was assessed by varying the printing layer orientation at 0°, 30°, 45°, 60° and 90° relative to the loading direction. The results show a strong dependence of mechanical properties on layer alignment: tensile strength decreased from 18.61 MPa (0°) to 5.22 MPa (90°), and flexural strength from 23.98 MPa (0°) to 6.87 MPa (90°), corresponding to reductions of approximately 70–72%. Scanning electron microscopy linked this anisotropy to weak interlayer adhesion and elevated porosity relative to the feedstock granules, supporting the interlayer interface as a dominant factor governing off-axis strength. The results confirm that the studied composite provides sufficient strength and durability for applications in furniture, design elements, tools, and building structures fabricated by large-scale additive manufacturing.

Article.Title: Development and validation of an artificial intelligence model for automated classification of whole-body bone scintigraphy in oncology patients
Article.Authors: Kanokwongnuwat W.
Article.Abstract: Whole-body bone scintigraphy with Tc-99 m methylene diphosphonate (MDP) is widely used to detect osseous metastases, and artificial intelligence (AI) may support its interpretation. We developed and internally validated OsseoScan AI, a deep learning model classifying whole-body bone scans as normal or abnormal. In this retrospective single-center study at Phrapokklao Hospital, Thailand, consecutive oncologic scans from April 2021 to June 2026 were labeled using a two-tier composite reference standard. An ImageNet-21k-pretrained EfficientNetV2-B3 was trained on full-body anterior and posterior images from 5,040 scans of 4,313 patients (1,395 abnormal), partitioned at patient level into a training/validation pool (4,032 scans; 5-fold cross-validation) and a held-out test set (1,008 scans). Pooled out-of-fold AUC was 0.959 (95% CI 0.952–0.967). On the test set at the pre-specified threshold, AUC was 0.963 (0.946–0.977), sensitivity was 0.907 (0.868–0.944), specificity was 0.886 (0.862–0.910), and NPV was 0.961. Sensitivity was 1.000 for extensive, 0.925 for multifocal, and 0.725 for solitary metastases; a sensitivity-oriented threshold raised solitary-lesion sensitivity to 0.882 while flagging 40.7% of scans. Grad-CAM provided qualitative explainability. OsseoScan AI showed high discrimination in internal validation and may support worklist prioritization; external, multi-center, and prospective evaluation is required before clinical use.

Article.Title: CXRG-SVLM: a parameter-efficient small vision-language model for multi-view chest X-ray report generation in resource-constrained environments
Article.Authors: Fareed M.; Uddin J.; Sayyid A.; Ahmed A.; Sattar M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Automated chest X-ray report generation reduces reporting delays in resource-constrained clinical environments. Existing vision-language models often rely on large language models or full fine-tuning. This dependence causes high computational costs and limits on-premise deployment. We propose CXRG-SVLM. This small vision-language model combines a frozen RAD-DINO medical image encoder with a 4-bit quantized Qwen2.5-3B language model adapted using 4-bit QLoRA. A multi-view fusion module integrates frontal and lateral radiographs into a compact continuous visual representation. The resulting visual tokens are projected into the language-model embedding space and concatenated with clinical-indication embeddings to form a conditioning prefix. The decoder uses its native causal self-attention over this prefix and the generated tokens to produce the Findings report. The assembled implementation reports approximately 1.99 billion loaded parameter elements, of which approximately 38.1 million are trainable, corresponding to 1.91% of this framework-reported inventory. We evaluated the model on the Indiana University Chest X-ray dataset to generate the Findings section of the radiology report. The proposed model attains a ROUGE-L score of 0.3527 and a METEOR score of 0.2744. Automated entity-level agreement varies across findings, with the strongest F1 for normal descriptors and measurable agreement for pleural effusion, pneumothorax, and mediastinal mentions under the reported rule-based evaluation. Efficiency testing shows an average generation time of 5.27 seconds per report on a single graphics processing unit. These results establish the model’s computational feasibility and motivate subsequent radiologist evaluation of factual correctness, safety, and practical usefulness. Ultimately, CXRG-SVLM demonstrates that a parameter-efficient approach with less than 2% trainable parameters maintains competitive semantic fidelity, establishing an accessible foundation for future, prospectively validated on-premise clinical decision-support tools.

Article.Title: Prevalence of drug-related hospital admissions and associated factors among chronic internal medicine wards in Wolaita Sodo University Comprehensive Specialized Hospital
Article.Authors: Dana D.; Paulos G.; Dawit M.; Toma A.
Article.Abstract: Drug therapy is fundamental to clinical care, aiming to optimize outcomes while minimizing risks. However, increased medication use has raised the prevalence of drug-related problems (DRPs), which may lead to serious consequences, highlighting the need for proper management and monitoring. Therefore, the objective of this study was to assess the prevalence of drug-related hospital admissions (DRHA) among chronic care patients and its associated. An institutional-based cross-sectional study was conducted using a previously validated tool. Descriptive statistics summarized sociodemographic and clinical characteristics, while binary logistic regression identified associated factors. Variables with a p -value < 0.25 in bivariate analysis were entered into a multivariable logistic regression model to control for potential confounders. A p -value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant at a 95% confidence level. Out of 367 patients, 34.6% experienced DRHAs. Significant predictors included comorbidities, chronic kidney disease (CKD), younger age, and urban residence. Patients with ≥ 3 comorbidities had 3.25-fold higher odds (AOR = 3.25, 95% CI 1.75–6.04), 1–2 comorbidities nearly doubled the risk (AOR = 1.98, 95% CI 1.21–3.23), CKD increased risk (AOR = 2.41, 95% CI 1.41–4.13), young adults aged 18–35 had higher odds (AOR = 1.65, 95% CI 1.01–2.69), and urban residents had 54% higher odds (AOR = 1.54, 95% CI 1.01–2.35). DRHAs were considerably high in the study setting. The most common causes were noncompliance, untreated indications, unnecessary drugs, and adverse drug reactions, most of which were preventable.

Article.Title: Evaluation of housekeeping gene stability in placental tissues: comparative expression studies in first-trimester, preeclamptic and control placenta
Article.Authors: Pegoraro S.; Toffoli M.; Balduit A.; Zito G.; Fogar B.; Hervatich G.; Romano F.; Ricci G.; Bulla R.; Agostinis C.
Article.Abstract: Molecular studies of the human placenta may reveal gene expression alterations responsible for impaired placentation and the subsequent development of pregnancy complications ( e.g. , preeclampsia, fetal-growth restriction, pre-term birth) characterised by a significantly increased risk of maternal and newborn mortality. Accurate qPCR normalization is crucial in placental research; however, reference gene stability across different gestational stages, pathological conditions, and experimental models remains poorly validated. This study systematically evaluated six candidate housekeeping genes ( ACTB , GAPDH , HPRT1 , RPS18 , TBP , YWHAZ ) in human placental tissues (first/third-trimester, preeclampsia) and trophoblast cell lines (BeWo, HTR-8/SVneo, JAR, JEG-3). Expression stability was assessed using four algorithms: Delta-Ct, BestKeeper, NormFinder, and RefFinder. Validation was performed by analyzing target genes ( CD46 , PGF , HLA-G , CD93 ). Strong transcriptional divergence was identified between tissue samples and cell lines; restricting the analysis to placental tissue samples significantly improved stability values. Among the six candidate genes tested, the RefFinder comprehensive ranking identified GAPDH and HPRT1 as the most stable reference pair for placental tissues. Normalization with this pair successfully detected significant differences in CD93 expression across groups, whereas the least stable combination ( TBP/YWHAZ ) failed to do so. The geometric mean of GAPDH and HPRT1 provides a robust normalization strategy among the candidates evaluated here for qPCR studies in human placental tissues across physiological and pathological conditions.

Article.Title: Association of glycemic variability with delirium and mortality in critically ill patients with community-acquired pneumonia: a retrospective analysis
Article.Authors: Li M.; Zhang Y.; Zhang L.; Luo Y.; Tang X.; Dong Q.; Xiao Q.; He Z.; Zhang L.; Ma H.
Article.Abstract: Delirium frequently complicates the course of critically ill patients with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP). Nursing screening tools such as the CAM-ICU remain subjective and fail to capture underlying metabolic disturbances. Glycemic variability (GV) which can be calculated from routine glucose measurements collected by nursing staff, has been linked to delirium and poor outcomes in general ICU populations but has not been fully explored in CAP patients. This study evaluates whether GV is associated with delirium onset and one-year mortality in ICU-admitted CAP patients, with the goal of informing targeted, evidence-based nursing interventions. This retrospective cohort study analyzed 6,167 ICU patients with CAP from the MIMIC-IV database. GV was measured using the coefficient of variation of blood glucose values and divided into tertiles. The primary outcome was delirium, identified by at least one positive CAM-ICU assessment. Secondary outcomes included 1-year mortality and ICU length of stay. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate the association between GV and delirium, while Cox proportional hazards regression was used to evaluate the association between GV and 1-year mortality. Kaplan–Meier curves and restricted cubic spline analyses were used to examine the associations between GV and clinical outcomes, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate the discriminatory performance of multivariable models incorporating GV and prespecified covariates. A sensitivity analysis using a fixed 72-hour exposure window was performed to assess the robustness of the primary findings. Among 6,167 critically ill patients with CAP, 54.3% developed delirium, the overall 1-year mortality rate was 45.2%, and the median ICU length of stay was 4.30 days (IQR 2.37–9.08). After full adjustment, each unit increase in log-GV was independently associated with higher odds of delirium (OR, 1.328; 95% CI, 1.177–1.499) and a higher hazard of 1-year mortality (HR, 1.081; 95% CI, 1.006–1.162). The highest GV tertile (GV3) exhibited a delirium incidence of 58.40% and significantly greater mortality compared with GV1 ( P < 0.001). Kaplan–Meier analysis confirmed lower survival in GV3 (log-rank P < 0.001). Restricted cubic splines showed a nonlinear positive association with delirium (P nonlinearity = 0.002) and a linear relationship with mortality (P nonlinearity = 0.65). ROC curves yielded AUCs of 0.82 for delirium and 0.74 for 1-year mortality. GV was significantly associated with delirium and 1-year mortality in critically ill patients with CAP. GV may serve as a potential risk marker for identifying patients at higher risk of adverse outcomes. Further prospective studies are warranted to determine whether targeted assessment or modification of GV can improve clinical outcomes.

Article.Title: Effect of freezing rain-induced changes in dry deposition on particulate matter concentrations in Hubei, China
Article.Authors: Tian T.; Xia X.; Wang L.; Zhu B.; Zhu Z.; Zhang T.; Zhang M.; Huang Y.; Han W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Particulate matter (PM) pollution is a critical aspect of urban air quality degradation, and vegetation mitigates atmospheric PM concentrations via dry deposition, offering a natural, sustainable, and cost-effective strategy for pollution mitigation. Based on multi-source satellite remote sensing products, this study quantified the dry deposition effect of PM 2.5 and PM 10 on vegetation using a mathematical model, and evaluated its spatial and temporal changes in the long-term series in Hubei province, especially the impact of dry deposition changes induced by the extreme freezing rain process in early 2024 on particulate matter pollution. The key findings are as follows: (1) Leaf Area Index (LAI) showed a significant negative correlation with PM 2.5 and PM 10 , and modeled dry deposition flux (DDF) showed consistent coherence with LAI, Land Surface Temperature (LST), Wind Speed (WS), and Precipitation (PRE) at the one-month scale; (2) The physical damage caused by the freezing rain substantially diminished the vegetation’s capacity for particulate matter deposition, with the reduction of the deposition effect of PM 10 being more pronounced than that of PM 2.5 ; (3) A decadal spatiotemporal analysis of dry deposition on vegetation indicated an overall trend toward improving air quality in Hubei and further revealed stronger spatial heterogeneity in the long-term trend of PM 2.5 dry-deposition reduction than that of PM 10 , partly reflecting differences in regional socioeconomic and industrial activity and background PM concentrations. This study advances a deeper understanding of the influence of extreme weather events on vegetation-driven dry deposition and provides scientific support for air quality management and strategic development aimed at strengthening urban ecosystem resilience.

Article.Title: Pistacia khinjuk oil enhances oxidative stability of a corn-canola-sesame frying oil blend during six months of storage under repeated thermal treatment
Article.Authors: Khajeh-mehrizi R.; Ardakani S.; Alizadeh A.
Article.Abstract: The degradation of frying oils during thermal processing and storage poses a significant challenge to food quality. This study investigated the impact of blending frying oil with Pistacia khinjuk oil at concentrations of 5%, 10%, 15%, and 20% on oxidative stability and physicochemical properties over a six-month storage under thermal condition. The 20% P. khinjuk oil blend (TK20) exhibited superior oxidative stability, maintaining a high induction period (18.52 ± 0.01 h at month 1; 18.39 ± 0.00 h at month 6). Furthermore, the study investigates the influence of the fractional order on prediction accuracy and computational performance, providing a systematic numerical assessment of the proposed framework. These translational modes become the characteristic low-frequency excitations of SAF skyrmion chains. For skyrmion chains, we identify collective translational and breathing modes with standing-wave-like spatial profiles. Beyond ferromagnetic-like breathing modes, the SAF geometry supports breathing oscillations in which the two layers oscillate out of phase. We further demonstrate signal propagation along extended SAF skyrmion chains with propagation velocities about 15% larger than in ferromagnetic skyrmion chains. These results provide a systematic description of the collective dynamics of SAF skyrmions arising from the interplay of geometric confinement, intralayer, and interlayer coupling.

This clustering strategy promotes a more balanced distribution of energy consumption across the network, delaying early node failures caused by localized energy depletion. The GA component employs a custom fitness function designed to maximize the time to FND latency. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed scheme not only reduces energy consumption and extends the time to FND but also achieves near real-time performance. This makes it a promising alternative to traditional heuristic-based approaches, particularly in latency-sensitive RWSN applications. Together, these contributions mark a significant step toward the development of scalable, efficient, and resilient RWSN architectures.

SPAD and PRI were consistently higher under shade. Article.Title: Spatial multi-omics identifies regional immunometabolic remodeling and macrophage PCK2-associated T-cell activation in lupus nephritis
Article.Authors: Liu L.; Li A.; Guo Q.; Wen M.; Zhao L.; Tan S.; Peng M.; Kong M.; Xu Z.; Zheng L.; Tang Y.
Article.Abstract: Poor response of lupus nephritis (LN) to conventional therapies frequently results in persistent renal inflammation and progression of chronic renal insufficiency. The complex pathogenesis of LN, characterized by microregional immune heterogeneity and interregional crosstalk, greatly hinders identification of the core immune network initiating disease and development of effective therapeutic strategies. Given that metabolic reprogramming drives immune cell activation, exploring region-specific immunometabolic characteristics of LN kidneys is critical for clarifying disease mechanisms and therapeutic targets. This study integrated spatial proteomics, spatial metabolomics and multiplexed immunofluorescence to map the spatial immune landscape of three key regions (glomerulus, renal tubules, medulla) in LN kidneys and analyzed their distinct metabolic profiles. Significant region-specific immunometabolic dysregulation was observed. The glomerular region was enriched with neutrophils and exhibited purine metabolism disorder with upregulated ADCY4; the renal tubules showed obvious T cell aggregation and glycerophospholipid imbalance with elevated Shmt1; the medulla was characterized by macrophage accumulation and increased PCK2 expression within a pyruvate associated metabolic signature. In an inflammatory macrophage–T-cell co-culture model, PCK2 knockdown in macrophages reduced macrophage and T-cell activation readouts. This study delineates distinct region-specific immunometabolic landscapes and key regulatory molecules across different renal compartments in LN. Functional perturbation in vitro further indicated that macrophage PCK2 contributes to T-cell activation under inflammatory co-culture conditions. These findings reveal the heterogeneous immunometabolic pathogenesis of LN and provide promising region-specific metabolic targets for the precise treatment of refractory LN.

Article.Title: Two-stage generative adversarial networks for urban pocket park design assistance: effects of training-set size and input augmentation
Article.Authors: Dai Y.; Zhang Y.; Zhu Y.; Jiang Y.
Article.Abstract: This study develops a two-stage image translation workflow for urban pocket park design assistance, linking rough line drawings, fine line drawings and spatial semantic layouts. Four training-set sizes—180, 360, 540 and 720 triplets—and four input conditions are evaluated: original image pairs, geometric rotation augmentation, drawing-style perturbation and local information masking. Each setting is trained independently three times and assessed on a common test set using IoU, Dice, boundary F1 and supplementary image and road-representation metrics. Findings show: (1) increasing the number of original image pairs improves final layout reconstruction, with macro-IoU rising from 0.1222 to 0.1516 and Dice from 0.2053 to 0.2494; (2) augmentation provides task-specific benefits: geometric variation improves line-position agreement, while drawing-style perturbation improves selected road graphic properties, but these gains do not consistently translate into better overall layout reconstruction; and (3) comparing reference and automatically refined drawing inputs identifies distinct weaknesses in the transfer of planting information and the interpretation of water and structures. These findings support selecting augmentation according to the intended representation task and reviewing intermediate drawings alongside final layouts. The study provides an experimental basis for training-data organisation, augmentation selection and staged graphic review in generative design assistance for urban pocket parks.

Article.Title: Leakage-controlled multi-assay antioxidant QSAR with class-conditional learning and evaluation of geometric–arithmetic connectivity indices
Article.Authors: Alhaj Z.; Alsharafi M.; Altairi A.; AL Naggar N.
Article.Abstract: Reliable comparison of antioxidant potency is complicated by the strong dependence of measured activity on assay conditions. ABTS, DPPH, superoxide, lipid-peroxidation, and hydroxyl-radical tests capture different chemical environments and reaction mechanisms, making a single global model potentially misleading. We therefore evaluated a class-conditional quantitative structure-activity relationship framework for jointly predicting assay identity and antioxidant potency. The curated dataset comprised 1,059 compound-assay records from 898 standardized compounds and 330 Bemis-Murcko scaffolds. Models used 102 RDKit descriptors, 14 classical indices, and 14 geometric-arithmetic indices, with all preprocessing restricted to the training folds. Robustness was examined through repeated compound-grouped cross-validation, scaffold-grouped testing, descriptor-block ablation, architecture controls, response permutation, residual diagnostics, endpoint sensitivity, and applicability-domain analysis. Conditional XGBoost achieved a compound-grouped classification accuracy of \(0.718\pm 0.027\) and known-assay regression performance of \(R^2=0.718\pm 0.053\) . A Morgan ECFP4 random-forest comparator gave the best compound-grouped regression result ( \(R^2=0.739\pm 0.065\) ), but its performance declined under scaffold separation ( \(R^2=0.472\pm 0.303\) ). The connectivity-index blocks did not significantly improve the RDKit-only models after Holm adjustment. These findings support assay-aware modeling for related chemical structures, while showing that predictions for unfamiliar scaffolds require applicability-domain screening and prospective validation.

Article.Title: Rapid residual stress assessment in additively manufactured specimens via standard uniaxial tensile testing
Article.Authors: Voloskov B.; Karpov I.; Em V.; Firsov D.; Simonov A.; Karamov R.; Qian G.; Bryukhanov I.; Fedorenko A.; Evlashin S.; Sergeichev I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract High residual stresses (RS) in laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB) components present significant structural challenges, yet traditional characterization techniques are cost- and time-intensive. This study introduces three rapid mechanical testing methodologies to estimate longitudinal RS in PBF-LB 316 L stainless steel by using the premature micro-yielding of pre-tensioned near-surface regions in cylindrical geometries. The proposed methods evaluate RS through: (I) plastic work density calculated from cyclic loading-unloading, (II) virtual unloading mathematically projected from standard monotonic tensile data, which also allows the analysis of existing tensile test results, and (III) the detection of a macroscopic micro-yielding threshold (0.01% strain). The estimates were benchmarked against neutron diffraction (ND) measurements across multiple heat-treatment conditions (as-built to 1000 °C). The energy-based approaches (Proposed Methods I and II) demonstrated linear correlations with relative ND stress reductions (R 2 = 0.75 and 0.71, respectively). Furthermore, by subtracting the empirical micro-yielding threshold from condition-specific macroscopic yield strengths, Proposed Method III captured the relative RS relaxation trend. Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) analysis supported the proposed mechanistic interpretation by showing localized geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) accumulation prior to bulk yielding. These findings show that the proposed mechanical methods can serve as accessible tools for evaluating stress mitigation strategies in additive manufacturing.

Article.Title: Reuse of ESR-irradiated tooth enamel for amino acid geochronology: assessing the impact of gamma irradiation
Article.Authors: Dickinson M.; Duval M.; Penkman K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hominin and faunal fossil collections are valuable scientific resources for investigating past populations, making it critically important to preserve these rare materials and prioritise minimally destructive methods. Electron spin resonance (ESR) dating of tooth enamel typically requires laboratory irradiation of powdered subsamples; however, the effects of this treatment on organic biomolecules, and therefore their potential reuse for amino acid geochronology (AAG), remain largely unknown. This study investigates the impact of gamma irradiation on amino acids within tooth enamel, and its implications for reuse of leftover ESR-dated enamel for AAG from two palaeolithic sites: Hortus, southern France and Belle-Roche, Belgium (maximum laboratory gamma dose of 1500 and 3000 Gy respectively). Our results show that laboratory irradiation induces negligible racemisation in selected amino acids, although significant correlations between dose and D/L values emerge at higher doses (> 1200 Gy). This demonstrates that while low-level gamma irradiation (e.g. <500 Gy) does not substantially compromise the chemical integrity of amino acids in enamel, higher doses may alter racemisation patterns, potentially affecting AAG interpretation. Consequently, this supports cautious reuse of irradiated ESR powders, preferably those exposed to low laboratory doses, enabling effective reuse of finite fossil tooth enamel resources.

Article.Title: Differential temporal dynamics of Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional activity following minibeam and conventional irradiation
Article.Authors: Bertho A.; Martinez Vicente P.; Fernandez Rodriguez A.; Juchaux M.; Gilbert C.; Moros M.; Prezado Y.
Article.Abstract: Minibeam radiation therapy (MBRT) improves the therapeutic index by sparing normal tissues while maintaining tumour control, yet the biological mechanisms underlying these effects remain poorly understood. TOP-TCF luciferase reporter activity and cell viability were assessed following MBRT or conventional radiotherapy (CRT) in A431, RG2 and MDCK cell models. Dose- and time-dependent responses were evaluated at 24, 48 and 72 h post-irradiation. Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional activity showed delayed, dose-dependent and strongly cell-context-dependent responses. Across the three cell lines, MBRT generally produced lower reporter activity than CRT at later measured time points and/or higher doses. These differences were accompanied by distinct cytotoxicity profiles, with CRT generally inducing greater PI positivity than MBRT. MBRT and CRT were associated with different magnitudes and temporal profiles of Wnt/β-catenin transcriptional activity. Because the irradiation modalities also differed in dose rate and cytotoxicity, the present data do not establish that spatial dose heterogeneity itself caused these signalling differences. The findings provide an initial framework for further mechanistic and spatially resolved studies.

Article.Title: O-antigen deficiency in Porphyromonas gingivalis attenuates dendritic cell-driven Th1/Th17-associated CD4+ T-cell responses
Article.Authors: Pavez V.; Melgar-Rodríguez S.; Selman J.; González-Osuna L.; Díaz-Zúñiga J.; Cafferata E.; Carvajal P.; Bravo D.; Vernal R.
Article.Abstract: Porphyromonas gingivalis is a keystone periodontal pathogen whose lipopolysaccharide (LPS) contributes to immune dysregulation during periodontitis. Dendritic cells (DCs) link microbial recognition to adaptive immunity; however, how P. gingivalis LPS shapes DC activation and subsequent CD4 + T-cell responses remains incompletely understood. This study examined responses of human monocyte-derived DCs (hMoDCs) and downstream autologous CD4 + T lymphocytes to P. gingivalis strains that differ in complete LPS expression. hMoDCs were stimulated with the wild-type W50 strain, the isogenic O-antigen-deficient ΔPG1051 mutant, the complemented cΔPG1051 strain, or left unstimulated. We evaluated hMoDC maturation, cytokine responses, and expression of IRF4, IRF8, NOTCH2, and BATF3 by flow cytometry, RT-qPCR, and ELISA. We then co-cultured stimulated hMoDCs with autologous CD4 + T lymphocytes to assess cytokine and RANKL responses by RT-qPCR and ELISA and lineage-associated transcription factor expression by RT-qPCR. All P. gingivalis strains induced comparable maturation of hMoDCs. In contrast, W50 induced robust expression of Th1- and Th17-polarizing cytokines and increased IRF4 and NOTCH2 expression. Notably, ΔPG1051 markedly attenuated these hMoDC responses, and cΔPG1051 restored them. Consistently, CD4 + T lymphocytes co-cultured with ΔPG1051-stimulated hMoDCs showed attenuated Th1- and Th17-type responses, with reduced mRNA expression of Th1- and Th17-related cytokines, T-bet, RORC2, and RANKL, and lower protein levels of IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-6, IL-17A, IL-23, and RANKL. In contrast, Th2- and Treg-associated cytokines and transcription factors remained largely unchanged. These findings demonstrate that intact P. gingivalis LPS is a major determinant of DC inflammatory programming and its downstream capacity to promote Th1- and Th17-associated CD4 + T-cell responses.

Article.Title: Hemostatic efficacy and safety of oxidized regenerated cellulose hemostatic material in a multi-organ bleeding porcine model
Article.Authors: Li G.; Li Z.; Deng K.; Qiu X.; Zhu Y.
Article.Abstract: Oxidized regenerated cellulose (ORC) is a widely used absorbable hemostatic agent, but comparative data on its efficacy across different bleeding scenarios remain limited. This study compared the hemostatic efficacy, tissue compatibility, and safety of a domestically produced absorbable ORC (StypCel™) with an imported counterpart (Surgicel ® Fibrillar™) in minipig models of Liver, Gastric wall, and Mesentery bleeding. Sixteen male Bama minipigs were randomly assigned to the Liver bleeding model ( n = 8) or the gastrointestinal model ( n = 8). Within each model, animals were further allocated to the StypCel™ group ( n = 4) or the Surgicel ® Fibrillar™ group ( n = 4), with three bleeding sites created per animal per organ. Bleeding models were established for each organ, and outcomes including 10‑s blood loss, time to hemostasis, intraoperative blood loss, hematology, liver and kidney function, coagulation parameters, and histological changes were assessed. Both materials exhibited three‑dimensional porous network structures, with StypCel™ showing significantly finer fibers (9.82 ± 0.93 μm vs. 20.59 ± 1.88 μm, P < 0.001). In the Liver, Gastric wall, and Mesentery bleeding models, no significant differences were observed between groups in time to hemostasis ( P = 0.8759, P = 0.1578, and P = 0.9632, respectively), intraoperative blood loss ( P = 0.0805, P = 0.7673, and P = 0.4678, respectively), or any hematological, biochemical, or coagulation parameters at all time points (all P > 0.05). Histological analysis revealed similar degradation and absorption profiles, with inflammation essentially resolved by week 4 in both groups. StypCel™ demonstrated hemostatic efficacy and safety comparable to those of Surgicel ® Fibrillar™ across multiple bleeding models, supporting its use as an effective alternative.

Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Ni J.; Liang Y.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been prominent in our daily lives by means of mobile applications and web search engines. AI-based Automated Essay Scoring (AES) system is playing an increasingly important role in higher education field. This study investigated the relationship between Chinese private university EFL students’ perceived interactivity of iWrite AES system and perceived performance, confirmation, individual innovativeness of AES system, as well as their reflective thinking, and how the variables influence students’ criticism of AES system. Based on a sample of 442 students, the study used Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) for data analysis. The findings indicated that students’ perceived interactivity of AES system is positively related to perceived performance and confirmation. Students’ perceived performance of AES system has a significant influence on students’ confirmation. Furthermore, students’ confirmation of AES system positively affects individual innovativeness, reflective thinking and criticism of AES. And students’ individual innovativeness also positively influences students’ reflective thinking of AES. However, students’ individual innovativeness and reflective thinking of AES system doesn’t have a positive relationship with students’ criticism. This study not only reveals Chinese private university EFL students’ attitudes and experiences towards technological tools but also provide valuable support for enhancing teaching effectiveness and improving teaching methods.

Article.Title: Time to uptake of long-term postpartum family planning and factors associated with it among Ethiopian mothers: A shared frailty survival analysis
Article.Authors: Kabtyimer A.; Jemil H.; Endalkachew A.; Mankelkl G.; Kassaw A.; Abeje E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Long-term postpartum family planning (LTPPFP) involves the use of long-acting contraceptive methods within one year after childbirth. Delayed initiation increases the risk of unintended and closely spaced pregnancies, leading to adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. This study assessed the time to LTPPFP uptake and associated factors during the extended postpartum period among mothers in Ethiopia. A secondary analysis of data from the Performance Monitoring for Action (PMA) Ethiopia Cohort II, 2021 to 2023 was performed. A total of 2,167 postpartum mothers were included using a multistage stratified sampling technique. Data management and analysis were conducted using Stata 17 and R. Multicollinearity was checked using the variance inflation factor, while the proportional hazards assumption was assessed using the global Schoenfeld residual test. Three shared frailty survival models (cluster-level, region-level, and nested frailty models) were fitted and compared. Adjusted hazard ratios (AHRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were presented, and statistical significance was declared at p ≤ 0.05. During the one-year follow-up period, 396 women initiated LTPPFP. Among users, implants accounted for 94% of methods used, while female sterilization represented only 1%. The weighted prevalence of LTPPFP utilization was 14.8% (95% CI: 13.2–16.4). A total of 1,748.37 person-years were observed, yielding an incidence rate of 183.5 per 1,000 person-years. The cumulative survival probability for one year was 0.809. Earlier initiation of LTPPFP was significantly associated with having a plan to use family planning (AHR = 2.45; 95% CI: 1.58–3.81), previous family planning use (AHR = 1.90; 95% CI: 1.48–2.43), institutional delivery (AHR = 1.52; 95% CI: 1.03–2.26), postnatal care utilization (AHR = 1.63; 95% CI: 1.00–2.66), complications during delivery (AHR = 1.28; 95% CI: 1.02–1.60), and age at sexual debut > 18 years (AHR = 2.04; 95% CI: 1.20–3.46). LTPPFP initiation remains substantially delayed among postpartum mothers in Ethiopia. Key determinants of earlier uptake included prior family planning experience, service contact points (institutional delivery and postnatal care), and reproductive history characteristics. Strengthening integrated postpartum counseling during maternity care services is essential to facilitate timely LTPPFP adoption.

Article.Authors: Mante P.; Ntewusu J.; Danquah J.; Owusu G.; Dotse D.; Adomako N.
Article.Abstract: Drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) in children is associated with significant morbidity, yet the contribution of systemic inflammation to its clinical expression remains incompletely defined, particularly in low- and middle-income settings. This study investigated the relationship between systemic inflammatory markers, drug resistance and seizure severity in a paediatric cohort in Ghana. Although these markers were associated with NHS3 seizure-severity scores in pooled analyses, these relationships were substantially attenuated after accounting for DRE status. These findings demonstrate an association between selected systemic inflammatory markers and pediatric DRE and support further prospective evaluation of their clinical relevance.

Article.Title: Imaging shallow magma storage and fluid pathways beneath Aso volcano using ambient-noise tomography
Article.Authors: Tsuji T.; Chhun C.; Andajani R.; Ishikawa Y.; Nishizaka N.; Yano H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To investigate the high-resolution three-dimensional internal structure of the large caldera-type volcano Mt. Aso, we deployed a temporary seismometer network and applied ambient-noise surface-wave tomography. We resolve the shallow crustal structure with high spatial resolution and identify an ellipsoidal low S-wave velocity ( Vs ) anomaly at depths of 2.5–4.5 km beneath the Nakadake crater. The Vs within this zone is ~ 1.5 km/s, indicating a highly fractured and pressurized rock, which we interpret as a shallow magma storage zone. Considering the temperature conditions, supercritical fluids could transition to a gas phase beneath the storage zone, leading to volume expansion, fracture opening, and reduced Vs . Furthermore, combined with previously reported temporal variations in seismic velocity and geodetic modeling results, the low- Vs zone could behave as a pressure-sensitive fractured system, potentially connected to the overlying fluid-bearing pathway beneath Aso Volcano. Above the storage zone, we image a narrow, vertically elongated low- Vs structure interpreted as a hydrothermal conduit that likely transports the pressurized fluids to the surface crater and generates very long-period (VLP) tremors.

Article.Title: Network modeling of science teachers’ perceptions of artificial intelligence integration in science curriculum development
Article.Authors: Ibrahem U.; Alrashood J.; Diab H.; Alrosa T.; Alkhabra Y.; Alotaibi S.; Moussa M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study employs psychological network modeling to examine the interrelationships among science teachers’ perceptions of benefits, challenges, and attitudes toward integrating artificial intelligence (AI) tools in science curriculum development. The estimated network revealed a dense structure. Centrality analyses indicated that curriculum content generation and innovative pedagogical tools were most central, while data processing challenges and algorithmic bias emerged as prominent structural barriers. Centrality metrics identify AI-facilitated curriculum design and innovative pedagogical tools as primary benefits, while challenges such as data processing limitations and algorithmic biases emerge as significant barriers. Teacher attitudes demonstrate ambivalence, characterized by resistance to automating administrative functions alongside guarded optimism for interactive and adaptive learning applications. These insights underscore the imperative to address technical constraints, ethical considerations, and the evolving professional identities of educators to ensure effective AI integration. The study contributes a nuanced, systemic understanding that informs the development of tailored AI tools and support frameworks, ultimately advancing transformative innovation in science education.

Article.Title: HCVSOA: hybrid corona virus–snake optimization for hyperparameter-tuned kinematic handwriting analysis in Parkinson’s disease detection
Article.Authors: Ayus I.; Azad C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Working with machine learning models is challenging due to various complex factors such as high-dimensional temporal dependencies, control complexity and poor subject-independent performance. Researchers have identified that the conventional optimization strategies often fail to explore these complex factors fully which limits model robustness and subject-independent performance. The study introduces hybrid heuristic optimization strategy namely, Hybrid Corona Virus-Snake Optimization Algorithm (HCVSOA) which combines the exploratory strengths of Corona Virus Optimization Algorithm (CVOA) with the adaptive exploitation of the Snake Optimization Algorithm (SOA). The HCVSOA framework is capable of tuning model parameters for machine learning models which facilitates more effective temporal feature extraction and structured feature representation for strengthening accurate class-based classification. Experiments are conducted on both handwriting dynamics datasets with meander and spiral patterns. The HCVSOA + Convolutional 1D Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit framework demonstrates superior performance over other considered optimization strategies which records an accuracy of 96.25% on meander New HandPD signals, 97.86% on spiral New HandPD signals and 99.903% on spiral UCI dataset. The observed improvements in performance metrics confirm a well-balanced trade-off between sensitivity and specificity. Further, Area under the Curve and radar analyses confirm enhanced discriminative capability which highlights the consistent advantage across architectures and datasets for hybrid optimization techniques. The proposed HCVSOA significantly improves model subject-independent predictive performance for kinematic handwriting analysis.

Article.Title: Game theoretic modeling of blockchain–enabled dual-channel collection in closed-loop supply chains
Article.Authors: Sridhar J.; Unnissa M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Blockchain technology has emerged as an innovative digital solution aimed at enhancing transparency, traceability, and trust within closed-loop supply chains, particularly in the domains of remanufacturing and recycling operations. This study formulates a Blockchain-enabled Closed-Loop Supply Chain model that incorporates an original equipment manufacturer $$(M-R)$$ , a retailer-third party $$(R-3p)$$ , and a manufacturer-third party $$(M-3P)$$ . In light of Blockchain investment costs, privacy concerns, information transparency, and competitive dynamics in recycling, a Stackelberg game framework is developed to analyze optimal pricing strategies, collection decisions, and overall profitability. The research investigates the impact of collection competition and Blockchain-related parameters on supply chain performance. Through numerical analysis and sensitivity assessments, the findings reveal that the adoption of Blockchain technology enhances acceptance rates for remanufactured products and influences channel decision-making, whereas intensified competition in collection efforts tends to diminish individual collection performance. The results indicate that the $$M-R$$ model exhibits superior economic performance, while the $$M-3P$$ model demonstrates greater recycling efficiency in the context of intense competition. This research contributes theoretical insights and practical guidance for the design of sustainable Closed-Loop Supply Chains through the strategic integration of blockchain technology and optimized recycling channel selection.

Article.Title: Control of source–migration–trap coupling on hydrocarbon accumulation in the Shahejie Formation, Qikou Sag, Bohai Bay Basin
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Liu W.; Fu G.; Liang M.; Zhang D.; Shi Y.
Article.Abstract: Understanding the spatial heterogeneity of hydrocarbon accumulation in continental rift basins remains a major challenge in petroleum geoscience because the relative roles of hydrocarbon supply, migration pathways, and trap effectiveness are often poorly constrained. Focusing on the lower section of the first member of the Shahejie Formation (Es 1 L ), this study formulates a hierarchical control framework that synthesizes source supply, migration pathways, and trap effectiveness to elucidate the mechanisms of hydrocarbon accumulation. Integrating three-dimensional (3D) seismic, well logging, and geochemical data, this study delineates the distribution of effective source rocks, systematically characterizes vertical and lateral hydrocarbon migration pathways, and identifies the development locations of effective traps in the target interval combined with the evaluation of fault lateral sealing capacity to carry out coupled hydrocarbon accumulation analysis of source-migration-trap. A total of 18 migration pathways and 24 effective trap locations were identified. The hierarchical framework identifies source-rock expulsion intensity as the first-order control, defining the upper limit of hydrocarbon supply; migration-pathway architecture as the second-order control, regulating hydrocarbon focusing, dispersion, and charging efficiency; and trap effectiveness, particularly fault sealing capacity, as the third-order control, governing hydrocarbon preservation and final filling degree. The results indicate that hydrocarbons mainly accumulate in zones with optimal matching of source-migration-trap elements, characterized by sufficient hydrocarbon supply from source rocks, unobstructed migration pathways and effective trap conditions. Production-testing results from Well BS-4, located within one of the predicted favorable hydrocarbon accumulation zones, provide field-based support for the proposed coupling framework. The proposed hierarchical source-migration-trap framework provides a process-based approach for evaluating favorable hydrocarbon accumulation zones in lower-source upper-reservoir petroleum systems of mature faulted basins.

Article.Title: Multi-omics profiling of gene expression and chromatin accessibility in mouse hippocampal CA1 following adolescent social isolation
Article.Authors: Kubota A.; Shinohara Y.; Goto A.; Tajima A.
Article.Abstract: Social isolation (SI) during adolescence is associated with neurobiological alterations; however, its effect on the hippocampal epigenome and transcriptome remains unclear. ATAC-seq identified candidate SI-associated chromatin accessibility alterations, with nominal functional enrichment linking increased enhancer-associated regions to calcium transport and decreased promoter regions to synaptic organization. Motif analysis showed enrichment of the activator protein 1 (AP-1) motif among candidate regions with reduced accessibility. RNA-seq identified 106 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), including upregulated Fosl2 and Hdac9 and downregulated Fbxw7 , with enrichment of myelination-related pathways. Although global concordance between chromatin accessibility and transcriptional changes was limited, integrated analysis showed directional concordance between expression and nearby candidate accessibility changes for a subset of DEGs. Cell type analyses suggested that SI-downregulated transcriptional signatures were linked to excitatory neurons, whereas SI-upregulated signatures were enriched in non-neuronal populations, particularly oligodendrocytes. Deconvolution suggested higher estimated oligodendrocyte representation and lower estimated excitatory neuron representation in isolated mice. These findings suggest that adolescent SI is associated with significant transcriptomic remodeling and candidate chromatin accessibility changes within hippocampal CA1, accompanied by distinct neuronal- and glial-associated transcriptional signatures.

Article.Title: Comparative detection of multielement geochemical anomalies using PCA and Mahalanobis distance in artisanal gold mining soils in eastern Ghana
Article.Authors: Kazapoe R.; Kwaw A.; Sagoe S.; Sagru-Larr P.; Adam A.; Amoah B.; Fynn O.

PCA retained three components explaining 62.89% of the total variance and identified 60 anomalies (9.02%), compared with 51 (7.67%) for Classical MD and 120 (18.05%) for robust MD. Overall, at least one method identified 164 samples (24.66%), at least two methods identified 57 (8.57%), and all three methods identified 10 (1.50%). PCA showed the strongest spatial dependence, with a Global Moran’s I of 0.1474 (p = 0.002). Local spatial analysis corroborated 25.00% of PCA, 13.73% of Classical MD, and 10.00% of robust MD anomalies. The results indicate that PCA identifies more spatially coherent anomalies, whereas robust MD detects a broader range of unusual multielement compositions. Integrating these methods provides complementary evidence for prioritising locations for field verification and environmental monitoring in mineralised and mining-affected areas.

Article.Title: Interplay between immune cell damage and depletion, population size, ecological factors and Picornavirus infection in the Venice Lagoon (Italy)
Article.Authors: Carella F.; Feola A.; Romano G.; Aceto S.; Garcia-March J.; Tena-Medialdea J.; Prado P.; Mazzero G.; Sabino A.; Sigovini M.
Article.Abstract: We monitored the mortality of the fan mussel Pinna nobilis (L.) in the Venice lagoon (North of Italy) during a period of one and half year (2023–2024) in two areas named Ottagono Alberoni (OA) and Coffa Val Grande (CV) reporting the disease condition for the period time 2024. Host and environmental factors (e.g. pen shell state of infection, size, immune cell depletion with activation of caspase-3, oxygen, temperature, salinity) were investigated and shown to influence morbidity and mortality progressiveness in the two areas. During the study period, Pinna nobilis Picornavirus ( PnPV ) caused systemic hemic infections in all examined individuals (100%) compromising the organelle compartment of the cells activating cell death. Ultrastructure revealed widespread viral replication organelles (vROs) occupying most of the host immune cells that arose from a total rearrangement of cell cytoskeleton that were dedicated to the virus machinery. Our results show a positive correlation between mortality rates and host size, with higher mortality affecting bigger/older individuals, although with local differences. CV pen shell population was characterized by smaller/younger individuals affected by milder viral infections and suffering lower mortality rates. Conversely, OA population presented larger individuals (adults) of P. nobilis affected by heavy viral infections that suffering a 100% mortality rate, leading to the extinction of that population by October 2024. Total Hemocyte Count (THC) was lower in OA (1.77 × 10 4 ±0.16 cell/ml) compared to CV (1.65 × 10 5 ±0.8 cells/ml) showing a negative correlation with viral load, connected with percentage of dead cells percentage, in turn correlated with animal size, suggesting that number of immune cells is regulated by the level of infection, and also age. Collection of hemolymph from the adductor muscle is safe practice for P. nobilis and should be explored to the evaluation of PnPV presence in the fan mussel residual population in the Mediterranean Sea.

Oscillometric SAD was present in 145/533 (27.2%), spirometric SAD in 71/504 (14.1%), and fixed-ratio airflow obstruction in 18/504 (3.6%). Article.Authors: Gao Y.; Huang W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Physical appearance is an important form of social capital, yet limited longitudinal evidence exists on whether it can be shaped by modifiable behaviors such as physical exercise. Physical appearance is measured using interviewer evaluations on a 1–7 scale, and physical exercise is primarily measured by weekly exercise frequency. The results show that exercise frequency is positively and significantly associated with appearance ratings: each additional exercise session per week corresponds to a modest increase in interviewer-rated appearance. This positive association remains stable across sequentially adjusted model specifications. However, when total weekly exercise duration is used as an alternative measure, the estimated coefficient is no longer statistically significant. The estimated association is somewhat larger among women than among men, although the gender difference is not statistically significant. In addition, lagged exercise frequency is not significantly associated with current appearance ratings, suggesting that the appearance-related benefits of exercise may be more immediate than persistent. This study contributes to the literature by improving identification relative to prior cross-sectional research through panel fixed-effects estimation and by using interviewer-rated appearance. The findings provide longitudinal evidence that physical exercise is associated with external appearance evaluations in a manner that is relevant to real-world social interactions.

Article.Title: High stimulation rate ABR reveals auditory brainstem conduction abnormalities in vestibular migraine
Article.Authors: Li C.; Huang Y.; Wang Y.; Yang S.; Yu W.; Pan Q.; Wang D.
Article.Abstract: To explore the application value of high-stimulation-rate auditory brainstem response (ABR) in evaluating auditory pathway conduction in vestibular migraine (VM) patients and to analyze its correlation with clinical symptoms. A prospective case-control study was conducted, including 56 VM patients (56ears) and 56 healthy controls (56 ears). All subjects underwent acoustic immittance testing, pure-tone audiometry, and ABR testing at low (11.1/s) and high (51.1/s) stimulation rates. The interpeak latency variance of wave I–V (ΔI-VIPL) between high and low stimulation rates was calculated, and ≥ 0.28 ms was defined as the abnormal threshold. The Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and Dizziness Handicap Inventory (DHI) were used to evaluate headache intensity and dizziness-related handicap, respectively. The correlations between these scores and ΔI-VIPL were also analyzed. At the low stimulation rate, no significant differences in ABR parameters were observed between the control and VM groups ( P > 0.05). At the high stimulation rate, the latencies of waves III and V, as well as the I–III, I–V and ΔI-VIPLs, were significantly prolonged in the VM group ( P < 0.05). The prevalence of abnormal ΔI-VIPL was 69.64% (39/56), which was significantly higher than that in the control group 12.50%(7/56), P < 0.05. ROC curve analysis for discriminating VM patients from healthy controls showed that the optimal cutoff value of ΔI-VIPL was 0.265 ms (AUC = 0.791, sensitivity 73.2%, specificity 87.5%, P < 0.05). Internal validation with 1,000 bootstrap resamples supported its stability (bootstrap median 0.265 ms, 95% PI 0.215–0.285 ms). Spearman correlation analysis demonstrated that ΔI-VIPL was significantly positively correlated with the total DHI score ( r s =0.623, P < 0.05) and VAS score ( r s =0.534, P < 0.05). High-stimulation rate auditory evoked potential (ABR) can effectively identify abnormal auditory brainstem pathways in VM patients. The ΔI-VIPL parameters show differences among different clinical subtypes, and are closely related to dizziness-related handicap and headache intensity; however, these associations are cross-sectional and should not be interpreted as causal or independently predictive.Therefore, ΔI-VIPL may serve as an auxiliary electrophysiological metric reflecting brainstem auditory conduction stress in VM patients, although further studies with disease controls are required to confirm its clinical utility.

Article.Title: Generative AI-assisted design problem exploration in interaction design: response disclosure, prompt initiative, and cost-sensitive prompting behavior
Article.Authors: Liu X.; Ibrahim F.; Wang Y.; Liu J.; Liu Y.; Zhao S.

High prompt initiative showed the same pattern on these four self-reported measures but significantly fewer prompts, reversing the predicted direction; composition time accounted for 18% of the exploration window under high initiative and under 2% under low initiative. Both sets of main effects held after multiplicity correction and adjustment for task and period. An exploratory interaction for germane cognitive load did not survive correction. Article.Authors: Hany H.; Elashry A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fused Deposition Modelling (FDM) 3D printing is widely used in industrial and consumer applications, but printing failures are often detected only after substantial material and production time have been lost. All models were fine-tuned under identical conditions on 5793 annotated images covering six fault classes. Performance was evaluated on clean test images and under three types of synthetic camera degradation: Gaussian blur, directional motion blur, and additive Gaussian noise. Deployment-related metrics, including parameter count, GFLOPs, ONNX model size, GPU latency, and CPU inference latency, were also measured. On clean images, YOLOv8s achieved the highest mAP@0.5 of 0.7905, while YOLOv11n provided comparable nano-scale accuracy with 14% fewer parameters. Stringing remained the most difficult fault class, with AP@0.5 values of approximately 0.45–0.48. The robustness experiments showed that blur caused a gradual reduction in detection performance, while directional motion blur was more severe than Gaussian blur. Additive Gaussian noise produced the largest performance degradation. Across the extended degradation grid, YOLOv11n achieved the lowest Degradation Sensitivity Index (DSI) of 28.80%, and also provided the fastest CPU inference at 48.11 ms/image and the smallest model footprint at 10.61 MB. These results provide a practical benchmark for selecting lightweight YOLO models and designing robust FDM monitoring systems.

Article.Title: Phase-matched ion pre-acceleration by upstream magnetic dipole vortices in relativistic collisionless shocks
Article.Authors: Naseri N.; Turkakin H.; Shvets G.
Article.Abstract: Collisionless shocks are among the most efficient particle accelerators in the Universe, yet the physical mechanism responsible for energetic upstream seed ions remains poorly understood. Using two-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations of unmagnetized relativistic electron-ion shocks, we investigate ion pre-acceleration by self-generated magnetic dipole vortices (MDVs) in the upstream region of the shock. We identify two distinct ion populations: one remains phase-matched with the moving MDV, undergoes considerable energization, and returns toward the shock, whereas the other escapes upstream after gaining only modest energy. We show that the magnetic component of the Lorentz force reduces the ion’s longitudinal velocity relative to the moving MDV, extending the interaction time and allowing the transverse electric field to perform sustained positive work. Decomposition of the electric field shows that both the motional electric field associated with the moving MDV and plasma-generated fields contribute to the observed ion energization. Repeated interactions with successive MDVs can increase ion energy before the particles return to the shock transition region. These results identify MDV-mediated upstream ion pre-acceleration as a candidate mechanism for producing energetic seed ions that may facilitate subsequent shock acceleration.

Decision-curve analysis suggested potential net benefit at selected low-risk thresholds following recalibration. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of an interpretable prediction model based on routinely available clinical data, with potential for integration into ICU workflows to support individualized VTE risk stratification and targeted surveillance.

Higher levels of reported behavior were associated with greater symptom burden, consistent with behavior being partly driven by experienced heat strain. HRHB explained additional variance in symptoms beyond sociodemographic and cognitive factors, supporting its incremental validity. These findings identify behavioral adaptation as a distinct and measurable dimension of population-level heat resilience, enabling improved identification of vulnerable groups and more targeted public health interventions.

Prime MM-GBSA estimates also favored anabsinthin over absinthin, although the energetic difference relative to X77 was sensitive to the sampled trajectory window. In silico pharmacokinetic and toxicity predictions suggested generally favorable early drug-like characteristics without prominent predicted toxicity alerts. This integrated workflow combining extraction optimization, phytochemical profiling, purification, and computational assessment provides a rational strategy for prioritizing natural products for further investigation. Among the compounds examined in this study, anabsinthin emerged as the most promising A. absinthium -derived lactone candidate for subsequent experimental evaluation against Mpro. Average LC beam-to-pore-ratio was 2.06 ± 0.37. Significant associations existed between LC OCT quality and most LC microstructural parameters. Article.Title: Industrial defect image generation via structured latent-space interpolation
Article.Authors: Cang Y.; Rong H.; Zou R.; Ma J.; Zhou Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Industrial visual defect detection suffers from scarce defect samples, limiting generalization. First, we introduce UMAP-based dimensionality reduction to project VAE latent features onto a low-dimensional manifold while preserving local neighborhood structure, thereby enabling artifact-free sampling in the subsequent stage. Second, we design a PSO-optimized Gaussian mixture model to capture the sparse, multimodal distribution of defect features within this manifold, and sample new coordinates from high-likelihood regions to generate diverse yet realistic defect representations. Third, we employ a non-parametric radial basis function interpolator to map these sampled coordinates back to the original VAE latent space, preserving geometric continuity and restoring high-frequency defect details before decoding. Experiments on bearing-defect and public industrial datasets show that detectors trained with a synthetic-to-real ratio $$\le 1:3$$ achieve superior accuracy and robustness, validating each innovation’s effectiveness.

Article.Title: Simulation-based implementation of the developed system dynamics model for sustainable urban water supply systems
Article.Authors: Hassan Z.; Rehan R.; Khan F.; Khan M.; Ali A.; Nasery M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Water is an indispensable resource, underpinning not only domestic livelihoods, but also the social and economic fabric of nations. Climate change serves among the most formidable threats to the world’s freshwater reserves. Naturally, potable water serves as a finite and precious commodity, merely, 3% is fresh, 2% locked within glaciers and polar ice caps, leaving only 1% accessible for human use. As global water consumption increases at an average rate of 1% annually. Projections alarms need of adopting robust and advanced water management policies, as only 60% of the world’s required water supply will be available by 2030. This crisis is most acutely felt, in developing nations with rapid population growth and pervasive poverty compounds water scarcity. In Pakistan, groundwater serves as the cornerstone of the national domestic water supply infrastructure approximately, meeting 70% of drinking water demands nationwide. Moreover, the widening chasm between water demands and supply urgently required, innovative water management strategies. At present, in Pakistan, urban water supply planning, development, and maintenance remain heavily anchored in conventional engineering and demand-driven frameworks. This study develops the first tailored System Dynamics decision-support model for Peshawar’s urban water system, introducing a novel coupling of an age-band leakage formulation with proactive pipe replacement policies tailored for intermittent, groundwater-dependent utilities. At its foundation, lies meticulously on a constructed Causal Loop Diagram, serving as a comprehensive visual map. To capture, the intricate interdependencies in social, financial, and physical/technical sectors of urban water supply systems. The framework was operationalized and demonstrated on Tehsil Peshawar over a 50-year simulation horizon. Currently, the public water supply system in Peshawar, comprising of tube wells collectively discharging approximately 2 million gallons per hour. However, at baseline static conditions, the total water demand is 6.01 MGH with an estimated leakage rate of 1.703 MGH (28.3%). Crucially, comparing these requirements against the actual municipal abstraction capability of 2 million GPH reveals a 3-fold supply deficit. This structural gap highlights the disparity between standard design benchmarks (250 LPCD) and real-world supply capacities, demonstrating how operational intermittent supply acts as a forced rationing mechanism under current system constraints. Critically, energy costs constitute nearly 80% of total tube well operating expenses, positioning energy optimization as a linchpin of financial sustainability. The study advocates for solar-based energy alternatives, demand management interventions and proactive groundwater replenishment strategies as transformative interventions. This paper makes a compelling case of holistic and systems-thinking approaches, embracing full complexity of sustainable water governance, offering a replicable and scalable model for developing nations confronting analogous of water security challenges.

Article.Title: Predicting the number of infant deaths per woman in ethiopia using complementary count regression and machine learning approaches
Article.Authors: Aga M.; Dugasa S.; Chen D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Infant mortality remains a major public health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa. Understanding factors associated with cumulative infant deaths and improving their prediction may help identify populations with higher infant-death burdens. This study examined maternal-level counts of infant deaths ever experienced by women in Ethiopia using complementary count-regression and machine-learning approaches. Data from the 2019 Ethiopia Mini Demographic and Health Survey were analyzed among 5,846 women with complete birth histories. The outcome was the cumulative number of infant deaths experienced by each woman. Because the outcome is mechanically related to the number of births, the logarithm of the number of children ever born was incorporated as an exposure offset in the count-regression models and excluded from the machine-learning predictor set. Poisson, negative binomial, zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP), and zero-inflated negative binomial models were compared using Akaike and Bayesian information criteria. Poisson Random Forest, Extreme gradient boost (XGBoost)-Poisson, and Light Gradient-Boosting Machine (LightGBM)-Poisson models were evaluated using 70% training and 30% independent testing split, with five-fold cross-validation for hyper-parameter tuning. Predictive performance was assessed using mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE). The ZIP model provided the best fit among the evaluated count-regression models, with the lowest AIC (2503) and BIC (2544). In the count component, maternal age, household wealth, postnatal care, child vaccination status, maternal education, and place of delivery were statistically associated with the expected number of infant deaths. In the machine-learning analysis, XGBoost-Poisson achieved the best test-set predictive performance, with an MAE of 0.320 and RMSE of 0.570. Region had the largest relative predictive contribution (gain = 0.190), followed by marital status (0.167), maternal age (0.136), education level (0.125), and wealth index (0.117). These variable-importance measures represent predictive contribution and should not be interpreted as causal effects. Cumulative infant-death counts among women in Ethiopia were associated with demographic, socioeconomic, geographic, and maternal and child healthcare characteristics. The ZIP model provided interpretable adjusted associations, whereas XGBoost-Poisson provided the best out-of-sample prediction among the evaluated machine-learning models. The findings support the value of combining inferential count regression with count-specific machine-learning methods while emphasizing that predictive importance does not establish causality. Continued attention to maternal education, socioeconomic disadvantage, postnatal care, immunization, and access to appropriate delivery care may help inform child-survival strategies in Ethiopia.

Article.Title: Multi-environment evaluation of finger millet genotypes for agronomic traits, yield stability and adaptability for summer cultivation
Article.Authors: Mishra S.; Rajendran A.; Kumar S.; Thakur M.; Kishor K.; Singh M.; Chandra M.; Banoriya R.; Shivraj G.; Mundakochi M.; Dash P.
Article.Abstract: Identification and advancement of high yielding and early maturing finger millet genotypes for summer season is essential for crop diversification in the Indo-Gangetic flood plains to enhance food security and production efficiency. The current experiment studied 145 finger millet genotypes under six contrasting environments namely: E2, E4, and E6 (summer) and E1, E3, and E5 (rainy) in three consecutive years (2021–2024) to identify parents suitable for the development of specific varieties and superior genotypes for summer cultivation. An integrated analytical framework combining AMMI, GGE biplot, BLUP, WAAS and MTSI were employed to reveal greater insights. REML/BLUP analysis was employed to enhance the reliability of selection, which revealed that genotypic variance accounted for a larger proportion of the phenotypic variance (49.5%) than genotype × environment interaction variance (24.3%), coupled with moderate broad-sense heritability (0.49) and high selection accuracy (0.95). AMMI found C3, C2, C1, G120 and G11 to take the top high yielding genotypes and G111, G12, G7, G65 and G81 were the most stable. GGE mean vs. stability biplot indicated G120, G80 and G29 as broadly adapted and high-yielding, G120 topped as the best performer and G52 and G68 summer-specific adaptors (E2 and E4). BLUP predicted results with re-affirmation of G120, G29 and G80 as the good performers. C3, C2, C1, G120, G29, G28 and G85 were grouped by the WAAS index as ideal (high yield and stable). Multi-Trait Stability Index (MTSI) also identified eighteen genotypes that could be improved simultaneously for multiple traits. Overall, the elite genotypes (G120, G80, G29 and the check varieties C1, C2, and C3) are useful as parents for breeding climate resilient finger millet varieties adapted to summer climatic conditions in the Gangetic plains of India.

Article.Title: Bhallatakadi modaka induces apoptosis of cancer cells via activating ROS/p-ERK pathway
Article.Authors: Dixit A.; Mishra S.; Ghosh D.; Shrivastava N.; Sarkar M.; Paul M.; Bose S.; Kumar D.; Basak S.; Dey R.; Roy S.; Saha S.; Jagtap C.; Nair P.; Bora M.; Babu G.; YR S.; Srikanth N.; Acharya R.; Srivastava A.
Article.Abstract: Bhallatakadi modaka (BM) is an Ayurvedic formulation that has been traditionally used for various therapeutic purposes, but its anticancer effects and underlying molecular mechanisms remain insufficiently characterized.This study aimed to investigate the antitumor effects and underlying mechanisms of BM in cancer cell lines and a xenograft mouse model. In vitro assays, including MTT and clonogenicity assays, revealed that BM inhibited cancer cell growth and induced apoptosis in a dose-dependent manner. Flow cytometry, DAPI/PI staining, and Western blotting further confirmed apoptosis induction. Additionally, BM treatment reduced the cancer stem cell population, evidenced by a decrease in CD44+CD117+ cells and reduced sphere formation. Mechanistically, the formulation induced the generation of ROS, which activated the extracellular signal-regulated kinase (p-ERK) pathway, culminating in apoptosis. Increased expression of apoptosis markers such as cleaved caspase-3 and decreased total PARP1 further confirm the apoptotic effect. In vivo, treatment with BM in OVCAR-3 xenograft-bearing mice led to a significant reduction in tumor size compared to controls. Immunohistochemistry showed a marked decrease in Ki-67 expression, indicating suppressed tumor cell proliferation. Overall, the data suggest that BM may inhibit cancer cell growth through mechanisms involving ROS accumulation, p-ERK activation, and induction of apoptosis.
