Article.Title: Formononetin-loaded solid lipid nanoparticles attenuate inflammatory signaling in TNF-α-stimulated MH7A synoviocytes
Article.Authors: Faheem M.; Ahmad A.; Munawar N.; Ali M.; Akhtar B.
Article.Abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with persistent synovial inflammation induced by pro-inflammatory cytokines and matrix metalloproteinases. Formononetin (FN), a plant isoflavone, has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties with therapeutic potential for RA. This research aimed to prepare FN-loaded solid lipid nanoparticles (FN-SLNPs) and determine whether nanoencapsulation preserves chemical identity, increases antioxidant potential, and enhances anti-inflammatory activity in tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α)-stimulated MH7A synoviocytes. FN-SLNPs were characterized by particle size and zeta potential analysis, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), UV-visible spectroscopy, and antioxidant profiling, including total flavonoid content, total phenolic content, and 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) radical scavenging activity. In vitro biological activity in TNF-α-stimulated MH7A cells was evaluated using cytotoxicity analysis by MTT assay, protein quantification by ELISA, and gene expression analysis by qRT-PCR. FN-SLNPs showed a hydrodynamic diameter of 148 ± 42 nm and a zeta potential of − 27.3 ± 1.3 mV. SEM revealed crystalline lipid domains. FTIR confirmed the chemical retention of isoflavone functional groups. Flavonoid content and total phenolic content increased with FN-SLNP loading compared with pure FN. DPPH radical scavenging activity was highest for FN-SLNPs at 20 mg compared with pure FN. TNF-α increased MH7A cell viability to 145.2 ± 5.8%. FN-SLNPs at 100 µg/mL reduced viability to 85.4 ± 3.1%, decreased interleukin-1β (IL-1β) protein levels from 0.0182 ± 0.0015 to 0.0035 ± 0.0003 µg/mL, and reduced IL1B gene expression from 18.50 ± 1.20 to 2.90 ± 0.25. These findings indicate that FN-SLNPs preserve the chemical identity of FN, enhance its antioxidant activity, and potentiate anti-inflammatory responses in MH7A synoviocytes.

Article.Title: Development of an original PAm@P hydrogel for high-performance cationic dye removal from wastewater
Article.Authors: Nayl A.; Arafa W.; Ahmed I.; Alanazi A.; Alanazi M.; Mostafa A.; Akl M.; Bräse S.; Abd-Elhamid A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this study, an original and simple method was employed to modify polyacrylamide (PAm) with sodium phosphate (Na₃PO₄), yielding a sodium phosphate-modified polyacrylamide hydrogel (PAm@P) with promising swelling and adsorption properties compared to pristine, unmodified polyacrylamide. The PAm@P hydrogel was characterized using various advanced techniques to confirm successful modification of PAm and the formation of the PAm@P hydrogel. Swelling experiments demonstrated that phosphate modification significantly enhanced the swelling capacity of PAm@P hydrogel (%S = 7000 at t = 60 min and pH 9.5) compared to unmodified PAm. The adsorption performance of PAm@P was evaluated using methylene blue (MB) dye. The adsorption kinetics followed a pseudo-second-order model exhibiting the best fit with the highest value for the correlation factor (R 2 ) of 0.999, comparing with R 2 values obtained for the other investigated models (0.976, 0.976, 0.993, and 0.654 for Pseudo first order, Liquid film diffusion, and intra-particle diffusion (step1 and step 2) kinetic models, respectively. These results demonstrated that the investigated adsorption process may be explained as chemisorption is the dominant mechanism. Also, the Langmuir isotherm model illustrated the R² value (0.999) with a maximum monolayer adsorption capacity (q max ) of 746.26 mg g − 1 for MB dye. While the R² values for the other investigated adsorption isotherm models were 0.254, 0.672, and 0.704 for Freundlich, Tempkin, and Flory-Higgins models, respectively. Also, the highest experimental adsorption capacity (q max = 1490 mg g –1 ) was obtained under the optimum adsorption conditions with an initial MB-dye concentration of 300 mg L –1 , PAm@P hydrogel dosage of 0.005 g, solution volume of 25 mL, pH 7, contact time of 120 min, and temperature of 25 °C. Furthermore, the PAm@P hydrogel exhibited selective adsorption and separation of the cationic dye MB in the presence of other dyes, such as Rhodamine B (RhB) and Azorubine (E122). The adsorption selectivity of the fabricated PAm@P hydrogel was quantitatively evaluated by calculating the selectivity factor (SF) where it was 2.31 for MB/Rhodamine B and 3.10 for MB/E122, confirming the preferential adsorption of MB-due over the other investigate dyes under identical experimental conditions. Moreover, the PAm@P hydrogel exhibited good regeneration and reusability performance over three consecutive adsorption–desorption cycles. The adsorption efficiency decreased gradually from 96.56% in the first cycle to 62.63% after the third cycle, indicating that approximately 64.9% of the initial adsorption efficiency was retained. Finally, the application of the prepared PAm@P hydrogel to real wastewater samples demonstrated its practical feasibility and highlighted its potential as an efficient adsorbent material for industrial wastewater treatment applications. This confirms that the investigated hydrogel is economical, promising, and can significantly reduce wastewater pollutants.

Article.Title: Mathematical and machine learning analysis of high-density polyethylene thermal degradation
Article.Authors: S S.; M A.
Article.Abstract: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) is widely used to characterize polymer degradation, but repeated experiments and conventional single-step kinetic models can become inefficient or inadequate when degradation is nonlinear, multistage, atmosphere-dependent, or evaluated outside the conditions used for calibration. This study developed a machine learning (ML) regression framework to predict the percentage mass remaining during high-density polyethylene (HDPE) degradation. Twenty-five TGA specimens (8–20 mg) yielded 237,154 observations; time, temperature, and initial mass were used as predictors. Random Forest, Extra Trees Regressor (ETR), Support Vector Regressor (SVR), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Adaptive Boosting (AdaBoost), Categorical Boosting (CatBoost), Natural Gradient Boosting (NGBoost), and a multilayer perceptron artificial neural network (MLP–ANN) were compared with a hybrid NGBoost–ETR model. Performance was assessed using the coefficient of determination (R²), mean squared error (MSE), root mean squared error (RMSE), and mean absolute error (MAE). The hybrid model achieved R² = 0.999987, MSE = 0.027042, RMSE = 0.164446, and MAE = 0.015879 on the dataset. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) ranked time and temperature as the dominant predictors, while initial mass had a smaller contribution. The optimized point-prediction model was deployed through a Django web interface. The framework provides rapid within-domain interpolation of HDPE TGA profiles; external validation across polymer grades, heating programs, and laboratories remains necessary before replacing experimental TGA.

Article.Title: Social participation patterns are associated with distinct salutogenic and mental health profiles in older Japanese adults
Article.Authors: Hamada M.; Sawada Y.; Sakano J.; Okata H.; Yajima Y.; Sasahara S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Social participation is widely promoted as a key factor in healthy aging, but its configuration may matter beyond participation volume. This cross-sectional web-based study examined social participation patterns and their associations with psychosocial resources and mental health among 998 older adults in Japan. Latent class analysis identified three patterns: Low-engagement ( n = 550, 55.1%), Leisure-oriented engagement ( n = 408, 40.9%), and Broad multi-domain engagement ( n = 40, 4.0%). Covariate-adjusted BCH analyses showed that the Leisure-oriented class had a favorable psychosocial profile. The multi-domain class had the highest adjusted means for positive mental health and social well-being, although neither differed significantly from the Leisure-oriented class. Compared with the Leisure-oriented class, the multi-domain class showed lower sense of coherence, particularly comprehensibility and manageability, and higher psychological distress (|d| = 0.48). Sensitivity analyses provided partial support for this mixed profile, although class proportions and some distal-outcome contrasts varied across model specifications. These findings highlight the importance of social participation configurations beyond participation volume, revealing that favorable positive mental health can coexist with lower salutogenic orientation and elevated psychological distress relative to the Leisure-oriented profile. A person-centered approach may therefore provide a nuanced understanding of social participation and mental health in later life.

Article.Title: Graph-based multi-agent reinforcement learning for industrial supply chain efficiency optimization
Article.Authors: Yao J.; Aldawood M.; Daghistani A.; Alnowibet K.
Article.Abstract: Industrial supply-chain decisions are affected by variable demand, transportation delays, and inventory uncertainty. This study evaluates an integrated Graph-MAPPO framework that combines graph-based state representation with cooperative multi-agent policy learning in a data-informed supply-chain simulation environment. A deterministic mapping of 1,873 development-period DataCo records produced 140 proxy nodes and 2,626 transaction-induced directed links; the subsequent operational trajectories were generated by explicit simulation rules rather than replayed as observed industrial trajectories. Normal, Surge, Disruption, and Mixed demand/lead-time scenarios were evaluated with fully specified distributions and reserved random seeds. For the controlled comparison, all learning-based baselines used 1,000 training episodes, the same cooperative reward, equivalent tuning effort, and common evaluation seeds; a 10-step rolling-horizon MPC baseline was also implemented. Graph-MAPPO obtained a mean episode reward of − 24.2559, a mean backlog of 41.05 units, and a service level of 99.70%. Several baselines achieved higher reward or lower backlog, and rolling-horizon MPC achieved the strongest scalar reward-backlog score but required substantially greater online computation. The ablation results support a contribution from graph-aware representation within the evaluated architecture, but the findings demonstrate a specific coordination-computation trade-off rather than general superiority or validated industrial deployment.

Article.Title: Association between the Planetary Health Diet and foot ulcer size and renal biomarkers among diabetic patients with foot ulcers in a cohort study
Article.Authors: Geravand F.; Nasli-Esfahani E.; Jalalzadeh M.; Montazer M.; Kazeminejad S.; Javadi F.; Tanha S.; Azadbakht L.
Article.Abstract: Planetary Health diet index (PHDI) has been associated with chronic diseases and mortality. This study examines the relationship between PHDI and foot ulcer indices, as well as renal biochemical markers, in patients with type 2 diabetes and foot ulcers. We prospectively included 219 patients with type 2 diabetes and diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) aged 25–75 years in Tehran, Iran. This study took place at the Diabetes Clinic of Tehran University of Medical Sciences. To assess dietary intake, three 24-h dietary recalls were conducted. We evaluated adherence to the PHDI based on EAT-Lancet guidelines. Length, width, and depth of ulcers and biochemical renal biomarkers were obtained from medical records at baseline. Participants were followed for 1 year. Multivariable linear regression models, adjusted for potential confounders, were used to assess the relationship between adherence to PHDI and the outcomes. Our findings revealed that higher adherence to the PHDI was related to lower serum creatinine (Cr) (β = −0.18, 95% CI: −0.33, −0.03), blood urea (β = −14.18, 95% CI: −22.89, −5.46), and higher estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) (β = 17.18, 95% CI: 3.53, 30.82) in fully adjusted models. However, no significant relationship between PHDI and ulcer characteristics (length; β = −0.29, 95% CI: −1.15, 0.55, width; β = −0.07, 95%CI: −0.34, 0.49, and depth; β = −0.10, 95% CI: −0.60, 0.40) was observed. Each 10-point increase in PHDI was not significantly associated with ulcer indices. This study indicated inverse associations between adherence to the PHDI and Cr, urea, and eGFR in diabetic patients with foot ulcers. Further cohort research with larger sample sizes could yield more comprehensive insights.

Article.Title: Full-spectrum XGBoost framework for interpretable classification of femtosecond LIBS spectra
Article.Authors: Jang I.; Kim C.; Jang H.
Article.Abstract: Reliable classification of laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) spectra remains challenging when emission signals are weak and strongly fluctuating under low-pulse-energy femtosecond (fs) laser ablation. This study evaluates a full-spectrum machine-learning approach based on eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) using an Al/Si thin-film ablation dataset as a representative binary spectral-classification case. The full raw LIBS spectrum was directly used as the model input, and XGBoost was compared with support vector machine, multilayer perceptron, k-nearest neighbors, and Gaussian Naive Bayes classifiers. Model development and evaluation were performed using processing-point-level data separation, with hyperparameter optimization conducted exclusively on the training dataset using repeated five-fold cross-validation. XGBoost achieved a mean cross-validation accuracy of 99.55 ± 0.26%, an F1-score of 99.48 ± 0.31%, and an AUC of 0.99994 ± 0.00008. On the independent test dataset comprising 612 spectra from 68 processing points, XGBoost achieved 100% accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, with an AUC of 1.00000. The classification results remained unchanged at probability thresholds of 0.3, 0.5, and 0.7. The measured single-spectrum inference time was approximately 0.105 ms, substantially shorter than the 10 ms interval between successive laser pulses at 100 Hz. SHAP analysis showed that the most influential wavelength channels were concentrated within the 288–289 nm spectral region and were distributed across multiple neighboring channels rather than being confined to the nominal Si I 288.15 nm wavelength. These results demonstrate accurate full-spectrum classification of the investigated low-signal fs-LIBS dataset while retaining wavelength-level information for model interpretation.

Article.Title: Investigation of a modified multi soil layering system performance in the supplementary treatment of municipal wastewater
Article.Authors: Yazdekhasti M.; Shayannejad M.; Heidarpour M.; Hejazi S.
Article.Abstract: The discharge of untreated municipal wastewater poses significant risks to surface and groundwater resources, highlighting the need for sustainable treatment technologies. The Multi Soil Layering (MSL) system consists of soil block units and enclosed by permeable layers. The present study introduces a Modified Multi Soil Layering (MMSL) system, contain the soil blocks with geotextile cover and a composite of nano-alumina layer. The performance of six experimental treatments was evaluated using a split-plot factorial design with two replications. The first factor was the type of soil block covering (jute, geotextile, and geotextile with a nano-alumina layer), and the second factor was aeration condition (aerated vs. non-aerated). Effluent samples were collected at 2–3-weekly and analyzed for BOD, COD, TSS, TDS, nitrate, and phosphate. Aerated systems exhibited higher BOD and COD removal, with the aerated geotextile cover achieving the highest efficiencies (77% and 78%, respectively). Non-aerated systems showed superior TSS and TDS removal due to stable sedimentation and reduced resuspension, with the geotextile cover reaching 52% and 79%, respectively. Aeration enhanced aerobic activity and nitrate removal, whereas non-aerated conditions favored denitrification, suggesting that coupling aerobic and anaerobic zones may optimize nitrate removal. The geotextile with nano-alumina cover under non-aerated conditions achieved the highest phosphate and nitrate removal (78% and 57%, respectively). FESEM and EDS analyses confirmed that geotextile-based coverings provided more porous and reactive structures that improved pollutant capture, while jute supported primarily surface-level removal. Mineral deposition observed via EDS contributed to sustained system performance.

Article.Title: Machine learning–driven optimization of abrasive waterjet drilling of custom 450 steel
Article.Authors: Muniyappan K.; Nagarajan L.; Kumar M.; Salunkhe S.; Singh R.; Nasr E.
Article.Abstract: To enhance the performance of the abrasive waterjet drilling process for machining Custom 450 steel components, a combined strategy that incorporates evolutionary algorithms and machine learning with engineering aspects is proposed in this work, by selecting the ideal combination of drilling parameters, such as stand-off distance, abrasive flow rate and water pressure. The goal is to simultaneously minimize the erosion diameters at entry & exit and taper angle of the drilled holes. Biogeography based optimization, particle swarm optimization, salp swarm optimization, and tug of war optimization algorithms are used to construct the machine learning algorithm model. After adjusting its hyper parameters, the taper angle and erosion diameters are to forecasted. The results comparison confirmed tug of war optimization algorithm’s efficiency over other algorithms. Given the small percentage of variance, the results of the confirmation experiment are also consistent with the findings of tug of war optimization algorithm. This research strategy has the potential to greatly enhance industrial abrasive waterjet drilling operations especially on custom 450 steel material.

Article.Title: AI-driven secure traffic optimization in VANETs
Article.Authors: K. S. S.; D. K. S.; Mikali S.; P. Gowda V.
Article.Abstract: Vehicular Ad-hoc Network (VANET) and Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) face significant challenge in achieving efficient and secure traffic management in urban environments where prioritizing emergency vehicles is essential for public safety. This work presents a modular AI-driven traffic optimization framework for VANETs that integrates proximity-aware reinforcement learning and secure vehicular communication to enable adaptive and trustworthy traffic signal control. The primary contributions of this work lie in the unification of proximity-aware intelligent traffic control and security-aware VANET communication. The proposed framework integrates a proximity-based Deep Reinforcement Learning (DQN) signal control strategy which is triggered when an emergency vehicle is detected within approximately 250m of an intersection to enable adaptive signal preemption. The evaluation considers a network comprising 71 Roadside Units (RSUs) and 13 signalized junctions with DQN deployed at four high-traffic intersections using a 157 dimensional observation space and a 256 action joint control space. A mini Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) based hybrid RSA–AES cryptographic framework (RSA-OAEP, RSA-PSS, AES-GCM) is implemented that ensures authenticated and tamper-resistant V2V and V2I communications. The system uses the standard protocols IEEE 802.11p and WiMAX for vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) and vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) communications respectively, facilitated by Road Side Units (RSUs) and coordinated by a fog controller that validates nodes, enforces strict security and is responsible for decision-making. The system is simulated using SUMO-NS3 over 30 random seeds to model an urban environment. In the revised scaled-network evaluation comprising 13 signalized junctions the framework demonstrates an overall packet delivery ratio of 95.85%, V2I Packet Delivery Ratio(PDR) of 95.78% and average emergency message delay of 26.36ms. The results show that the proximity-based RL controller reduces emergency vehicle waiting time by around 40.9% as compared to fixed-time control achieving an average waiting time of 30.31s as compared with 51.28s for fixed-time control. Though the density based control has a slightly lower average emergency vehicle time of 28.46s, the proximity-based RL approach provides adaptive emergency preemption in the multi-intersection network. The work is strengthened by conducting security evaluations that achieved 100% blocking of the spoofing, replay, tampering and flooding attack scenarios at the same time maintaining approximately 96% V2V/V2I PDR. The proposed open-source framework is a work integrating VANETs, artificial intelligence and distributed computing for real-time, resilient and sustainable traffic management. The work contributes toward advancing intelligent urban transportation systems and aligns with the objectives of United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 11 for sustainable and safe cities.

Article.Title: Valenced moral contagion affects adolescents’ self-reported prosocial tendencies in a guided imagery experiment
Article.Authors: Li K.; Yang J.
Article.Abstract: Using a three-condition, class-based guided-imagery experiment, this study examined associations between contact-based moral contagion valence and self-reported prosocial tendencies among 207 Grade 7 students (106 boys and 101 girls) from six intact classes. Two classes completed each condition: positive moral contagion ( n = 66), negative moral contagion ( n = 82), or neutral control ( n = 59). Welch’s ANOVA showed significant differences across conditions, F (2, 110.61) = 30.49, p < 0.001, η² = 0.19, with scores highest in the positive condition, followed by the negative and control conditions. Relative to control, positive moral contagion showed a significant statistical indirect effect through moral elevation, effect = 6.73, 95% CI [3.92, 10.07], whereas the indirect effect for negative moral contagion was not significant, effect = − 2.13, 95% CI [− 5.22, 0.61]. Junzi personality negatively moderated the positive-versus-control contrast, Δ R ² = 0.0465, b = − 0.3085, p = 0.0023; the conditional effect decreased from 22.02 at low Junzi personality to 7.96 at high Junzi personality. These findings indicate valence-specific pathways and suggest that external positive moral cues have larger incremental associations among adolescents with lower Junzi personality.

Article.Title: Data-driven gait cycle decomposition based on multi-joint coordination dynamics
Article.Authors: De Luca M.; Demuru M.; Gallo E.; Angiolelli M.; Rabuffo G.; Tafuri D.; Sorrentino G.; Mandolesi L.; Sorrentino P.; Troisi Lopez E.
Article.Abstract: The study of human locomotion has long relied on descriptive frameworks of the gait cycle, which have provided essential insights into the functional phases of walking and their underlying biomechanical demands. While these models remain highly informative, they are largely based on observational analyses and may not fully capture the continuous, global coordination that characterizes human movement. The present study proposes an integrated framework to study multi-joint coordination. This framework combines network theory with non-negative matrix factorization (NNMF) to treat gait as a dynamic system of coordinated joint interactions. Using three-dimensional kinematic data from 60 healthy subjects, a representation of multi-joint coordination across time was constructed, named “dynamic kinectome”. It was then decomposed using NNMF to extract spatial patterns of joint coordination and their corresponding temporal activations, allowing for an interpretable characterization of locomotor organization whilst preserving physiological meaning. The analysis extracted six robust, highly consistent ( p < 0.001 across 240 gait cycles, with an 85% spatial and 83% temporal correspondence), and symmetrical coordination patterns (exhibiting cross-lateral similarity with r > 0.95) across participants, effectively capturing the primary functional subtasks of locomotion. Rather than challenging classical phase descriptions, these findings enrich them by showing how coordination emerges as a continuous, often proactive process that can extend across conventional phase boundaries and systematically integrates the upper limbs for dynamic stability. Overall, this study provides a holistic, data-driven perspective on human locomotion, offering a promising basis for future investigations in motor control and may provide a promising methodological framework to explore coordinative alterations in clinical and rehabilitative settings.

Article.Title: Digital tool use and teachers’ teaching enjoyment: evidence from China, Singapore, Finland, and Japan
Article.Authors: Qian M.; Ren K.; Fang Y.; Yan C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Digital teaching efficacy and innovative teaching practice offer complementary perspectives on the relationship between digital tool use and teaching enjoyment. We analysed Teaching and Learning International Survey (TALIS) 2024 data from 4,473 lower-secondary teachers in China (Shanghai), Singapore, Finland and Japan. Composite regression models used teacher weights and 100 Fay balanced repeated replication weights, adjusting for teaching experience and employment-hours status. Total associations between digital tool use and enjoyment were positive in all four primary adjusted models. Efficacy-only indirect associations also remained positive after multiplicity correction. Sequential associations through efficacy and innovative practice were small: intervals excluded zero in Shanghai and Singapore before correction, with Shanghai retaining support across twelve indirect tests. Japan’s total association was sensitive to covariate adjustment. Full measurement invariance was not supported, and all four sequential intervals included zero in latent response-style sensitivity models. The findings show a recurring efficacy-related association in the primary composite models and limited support for the proposed sequence. They place teachers’ perceived digital capability and emotional experience alongside reported technology use as priorities for further research.

Article.Title: Adaptive Knowledge Fusion Ensemble (AKFE) for Flow Zone Indicator prediction and Hydraulic Flow Unit classification from well logs
Article.Authors: Olya B.; Mohebian R.; Moradzadeh A.; Pahlavani P.
Article.Abstract: Accurate hydraulic flow characterization in uncored reservoir intervals remains challenging because the Flow Zone Indicator (FZI) requires core-derived porosity and permeability, which are available only at discrete depths. This study introduces an Adaptive Knowledge Fusion Ensemble (AKFE) for continuous FZI prediction and subsequent Hydraulic Flow Unit (HFU) classification from conventional well logs. AKFE integrates well-log features, heterogeneous model predictions, model-disagreement information, and ensemble consensus through a leakage-controlled meta-learning framework. Seven base learners are combined using a CatBoost meta-regressor, and the resulting FZI predictions are classified into four interpreter-defined HFUs using a Gaussian mixture model (GMM). The framework was developed using 1,072 depth-matched core observations from two cored wells and independently evaluated on three blind wells. AKFE outperformed Simple Averaging, Weighted Averaging, and Conventional Stacking, achieving an R² of 0.991, RMSE of 0.0374, MAE of 0.0291, and MAPE of 6.7936. Compared with conventional stacking, AKFE reduced RMSE, MAE, and MAPE by approximately 26.8, 29.7, and 50.0%, respectively. Blind-well application further demonstrated that the predicted FZI profiles preserved meaningful variations in hydraulic quality and yielded consistent HFU patterns supported by cumulative-FZI and porosity–permeability analyses. The results demonstrate that integrating geological context with collective model behavior can improve the transferability of machine-learning-based hydraulic characterization to uncored reservoir intervals.

Article.Title: Characterization of prolonged hospital stays on a Medical Oncology Department in Portugal
Article.Authors: Bruno T.; Kellen F.; Magno S.; Oliveira J.
Article.Abstract: Prolonged hospital stays represent a significant challenge in oncological care, consuming resources and potentially reflecting systemic inefficiencies in discharge planning and palliative care access. This study aims to characterize prolonged hospitalizations and identify independent predictors of prolonged stay through comparison with non-prolonged hospitalizations during the same period. This comparative cohort study includes all hospitalization episodes with discharge dates between January 1st and June 30th, 2023. Prolonged hospitalization was defined as hospital length of stay (LOS) ≥ 16 days (the definition of “prolonged hospitalization” was tailored to the specificities of the department enrolled - mean + 1 standard deviation). The non-prolonged group (LOS < 16 days) served as the control group. Univariate comparisons used Mann-Whitney U, chi-square, and Fisher’s exact tests. Independent predictors were identified by binary logistic regression. Of 434 eligible episodes, 138 (31.8%) were prolonged (mean LOS 34.5 ± 21.6 days) and 296 (68.2%) were non-prolonged (mean LOS 7.6 ± 3.5 days). Independent predictors of prolonged hospitalization included intra-hospital department transfer (OR 7.88, 95% CI 1.97–31.6, p = 0.004), Palliative Care Unit (PCU) referral (OR 5.33, 95% CI 1.66–17.1, p = 0.005), social services involvement (OR 4.71, 95% CI 2.47–9.0, p < 0.001), and family meetings (OR 3.00, 95% CI 1.41–6.4, p = 0.004). In this cohort, prolonged hospitalization was most strongly associated with systemic and organizational factors—including social support deficits and palliative care access—rather than with markers of irreducible clinical complexity. These associations highlight potential targets for coordinated intervention in discharge planning and palliative care resource allocation, pending prospective validation.

Article.Title: Ameliorating effects and mechanisms of therapeutic electrical stimulation on the recurrent laryngeal nerve injury model in rats
Article.Authors: Zheng W.; Han M.; Shi M.; Han J.; Tian J.; Zhang Y.; Tian M.
Article.Abstract: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) injury is a rare but serious complication of thyroid surgery and other neck surgery, leading to vocal fold paralysis. The aim of this study was to investigate the therapeutic effects and mechanisms of therapeutic electrical stimulation (TES) on RLN regeneration in a rat model of RLN crush injury. Sprague–Dawley rats were randomly divided into groups of RLN injury and RLN injury + TES, and received RLN injury operation. The RLN injury + TES group received daily recurrent laryngeal nerve electrical stimulation for 14 days. Functional recovery including vocal fold mobility scoring and electrophysiological measurements was assessed. Structural changes were evaluated using histology and transmission electron microscopy. In comparison with observation management, TES improved vocal fold mobility(p < 0.01) on direct observation, reduced latency and attenuated amplitude loss (p < 0.05) on electrophysiological analysis, promoted fibroblast activation and angiogenesis on histology, and enhanced remyelination and axonal integrity on ultrastructural analysis. The results show that TES accelerates the early phase of functional and structural recovery following RLN injury, as evidenced by improved vocal fold mobility, electrophysiological parameters, and ultrastructural organization at 14 days post-injury.

Article.Title: Optimizing oil selection for curcumin-based nanoemulsions formulation through molecular self-assembly
Article.Authors: Bahaman A.; Pongprayoon P.; Tejo B.; Abdul Rahman M.
Article.Abstract: Curcumin is a bioactive compound with anti-inflammatory and anticancer activity, which is poorly water solubility and stability that limiting its therapeutic potential. Curcumin delivery can be improved by oil-in-water nanoemulsions by providing a hydrophobic core, but it is challenging to develop stable systems due to oil-drug compatibility. Molecular dynamics simulations were used to compare two oil cores of linoleic acid (LA) from safflower oil and oleyl laurate (OL) from palm kernel oil esters for curcumin nanoemulsions. The LA structure exhibited smaller structural movements, reduced radius of gyration (Rg) and more persistent intermolecular hydrogen bonds than the OL system. The higher number of CC-LA hydrogen bonds suggest the curcumin molecules become more densely packed with LA to form a tightly ordered hydrophobic core with its amphiphilic character enables a closely packed self-assembly with curcumin. Based on these findings, an optimized nanoemulsion was formulated by adding lecithin (LC) and Tween 85 (T85) into CC-LA (CC-LA-LC-T85), with LC and T85 appearing to enhance the aggregation rate. In simulations, self-association of surfactants occurred at the droplet interface with exposed polar head groups, a uniform shell around a CC-LA core. The ultimate aggregate was near-spherical and structurally hard, as shown by a stable Rg and minimal molecular diffusion. The dense hydrophobic core formed by LA, stabilized by persistent interactions with LC and T85, demonstrated a compact and organised self-assembled structure. These intermolecular interactions collectively ensured effective encapsulation and well-defined nanoemulsion, rendering its potential suitability as a carrier for future curcumin encapsulation in drug delivery applications.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: curcumin; nanoemulsions; molecular self-assembly; oil selection; formulation optimization
Article.TopicFields: Agricultural and Biological Sciences > Food Science > Proteins in Food Systems; Chemistry > Organic Chemistry > Surfactants and Colloidal Systems; Biochemistry, Genetics and Molecular Biology > Molecular Medicine > Curcumin's Biomedical Applications

Article.Title: ESAD-Net﻿: an efficient steel adaptive detection network for real-time surface defect detection
Article.Authors: Xiaoshan L.; Mingming C.
Article.Abstract: Steel surface defect detection is a critical component of quality control in the steel industry. Traditional detection methods face technical challenges including low accuracy and poor real-time performance. This paper proposes ESAD-Net (Efficient Steel Adaptive Detection Network), which achieves an average inference latency of 8.7 ms per frame (115.3 FPS) while ensuring high precision. Through the serial integration of RegNet-X lightweight feature extraction and the ATSS adaptive training sample selection algorithm. RegNet-X constructs a lightweight backbone network based on design space optimization theory. It integrates edge enhancement module and multi-scale feature fusion mechanisms. This achieves computational efficiency optimization while ensuring feature representation capability. The ATSS algorithm adopts an adaptive IoU threshold selection strategy targeting geometric feature differences of steel defects. It dynamically adjusts the positive and negative sample selection mechanism. This effectively alleviates sample imbalance issues and significantly improves small target defect detection performance. Experimental results on the NEU-DET steel defect dataset demonstrate that ESAD-Net achieves 87.0% mAP@0.5 detection accuracy and 115.3 FPS processing speed. Compared to the baseline model YOLOv8n, it improves overall detection accuracy by 6.8 percentage points and small target defect detection by an average of 13.2 percentage points. The algorithm increases positive sample utilization from 15.2% to 24.8% and reduces false positive rate to 6.7%. Training convergence efficiency is improved by 29%. Meanwhile, model parameters are reduced by 25% and inference time is shortened by 17%. While performance benchmarking is conducted on an RTX 3070 GPU, the model is designed with high architectural efficiency aimed at potential industrial edge deployment. By minimizing parameter redundancy (2.4M) and computational complexity (2.4 GFLOPs), the framework establishes a theoretical foundation for operational feasibility on resource-constrained edge devices.

Article.Title: Metabolic and hormonal responses to nutritional ketosis across metabolic phenotypes and sex in adults
Article.Authors: Grabowski M.; Grabowska K.; Klonek G.; Michalczyk M.; Zydek G.; Panek M.; Małecki A.; Nowacka-Chmielewska M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ketogenic diets are increasingly used for weight management and metabolic improvement, but it remains unclear whether nutritional ketosis induces uniform adaptation across metabolic phenotypes and sex. This exploratory study examined phenotype- and sex-dependent responses to a 60-day ketogenic diet in adults with normal weight, overweight or obesity. Participants were stratified into six metabolic phenotype–sex groups and assessed at baseline, day 14, day 30 and day 60. Plasma biochemical and hormonal markers, appetite and perceived stress scores, and body composition were analyzed using repeated-measures models. During the ketogenic diet intervention, β-hydroxybutyrate increased in all groups, confirming nutritional ketosis, but the response differed between groups and was most progressive in men with obesity. Free fatty acids manifested in a heterogeneous manner, exhibiting distinct time-, phenotype-, and sex-dependent profiles. Glucose decreased after diet initiation, whereas insulin and HOMA-IR improved mainly in participants with overweight and obesity. Lipid profile changes were variable, while liver enzymes showed a sex-dependent temporal pattern. Appetite score differed by metabolic phenotype, leptin changed according to phenotype and sex, and ghrelin remained unchanged. Self-reported perceived stress scores showed group-specific changes, whereas cortisol changed over time and body mass, fat mass, visceral adipose tissue and subcutaneous adipose tissue decreased. These findings indicate that responses observed during the ketogenic diet intervention showed variable patterns across metabolic phenotypes and sex; however, given the limited sample size, these apparent between-group differences should be interpreted cautiously. Because of the single-arm design, these changes cannot be attributed to nutritional ketosis independently of weight loss or changes in energy intake.

Article.Title: Transcriptional and ultrastructural analysis of a pigmentation polymorphism in frog eggs
Article.Authors: Macías-Bazante H.; Vizuete K.; Carrillo A.; Salazar-Nicholls M.; Debut A.; Young R.; Romero-Carvajal A.
Article.Abstract: Melanin synthesis in gametes is exceptionally rare among vertebrates. Among amphibians, egg pigmentation patterns range from unpigmented or subtly melanic eggs, such as in foam-nesting frogs to the heavily pigmented eggs known from some poison frogs and salamanders. This diversity is hypothesized to improve the survivability of externally developing embryos through camouflage, temperature regulation, or protection from UV-induced DNA damage. However, the multifaceted adaptive role of egg pigmentation remains unresolved, and the genetic and molecular processes governing these patterns are largely unknown. Here, we investigate a pigmentation polymorphism in the variable glassfrog Espadarana prosoblepon (Boettger, 1892) 1 , where females lay either dark or pale eggs due to a recessive pale eggs like allele ( pel ) that is specifically associated with reduced oocyte cortical melanin, while late-stage embryos of both morphs develop normal melanocyte-derived pigmentation. We combined ultrastructural analysis of melanosomes and gene-expression profiling of ovaries containing oocytes to identify putative mechanisms underlying the pale phenotype. We found evidence of accelerated melanosome degradation and complex gene expression changes in pigmentation, melanosome biogenesis, transport, and processing pathways. Identifying these developmental and molecular origins provides new insight into the ecological and evolutionary determinants of reproductive diversity among amphibians.

Article.Title: Phylogenetic characterization of circulating bovine viral diarrhea virus subgenotypes 1b and 1l in cattle from the Mediterranean region of Türkiye
Article.Authors: Saltik H.; Atli K.; Hasircioğlu S.; Kale M.; Yildirim Y.; Usta A.; Avci O.; Kaplan O.; Koçlu O.
Article.Abstract: Bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV), a member of the genus Pestivirus within the family Flaviviridae , is a globally significant pathogen affecting livestock health and productivity. The genus includes Pestivirus bovis (BVDV-1), Pestivirus tauri (BVDV-2), Pestivirus ovis (BDV), and Pestivirus suis (CSFV), all capable of infecting multiple host species, including cattle, sheep, goats, and wild ruminants. In cattle, BVDV infection ranges from subclinical to severe respiratory, gastrointestinal, and reproductive disorders. Infection during early gestation may result in immunotolerant, persistently infected (PI) calves that shed virus throughout life, serving as reservoirs for transmission. BVDV-1 (Pestivirus A) and BVDV-2 (Pestivirus B) are the principal genetic species, while HoBi-like viruses represent emerging pestiviruses. BVDV-1 is genetically diverse, comprising at least 24 subgenotypes (1a–1x), with 1b being the most prevalent globally. In Türkiye, BVDV is endemic, with multiple BVDV-1 subtypes, BVDV-2, and HoBi-like viruses reported. Notably, subgenotype 1l has recently emerged as a predominant lineage in certain regions. To investigate circulating pestiviruses in the Mediterranean region of Türkiye, 444 serum samples were collected from unvaccinated cattle exhibiting compatible clinical signs in Burdur province during 2021–2022. Screening by conventional RT-PCR targeting the conserved 5′ untranslated region (5′-UTR) identified 83 of 444 samples (18.7%; 95% CI: 15.3–22.6%) as pestivirus-positive. Pestivirus detection rates differed significantly across clinical categories ( p = 0.011), with cattle presenting reproductive disorders (22.9%) and growth retardation (22.7%) showing higher positivity. Five representative isolates were successfully propagated in MDBK cells, confirmed by direct immunofluorescence assay, and subsequently characterized by phylogenetic analysis. All five isolates belonged to BVDV-1, clustering within subgenotypes 1b (n = 2) and the endemic lineage 1l (n = 3). These findings confirm the circulation of BVDV-1 subgenotypes 1b and 1l in southern Türkiye and highlight the value of continued molecular surveillance and targeted removal of persistently infected animals to support regional control programs.

Article.Title: Functional connectivity in cerebral visual impairment: implications for daily visual behaviors
Article.Authors: Nadvar N.; Kim C.; Drottar M.; Bauer C.
Article.Abstract: Individuals with cerebral/cortical visual impairment (CVI) often report challenges in the functional use of vision to perform daily activities. As the underlying neural mechanisms of functional CVIs remain unclear, this study evaluated resting state functional connectivity in individuals with CVI versus typically sighted controls and evaluated within-group associations with visual dysfunctions. Resting state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) connectivity profiles were calculated from 16 individuals diagnosed with CVI and 19 controls. Visuoperceptual profile was constructed using the Flemish CVI questionnaire (FCVIQ) for each participant with CVI. General linear models were used to evaluate between-group functional connectivity differences and regression analysis was used to determine the relationship between functional network connectivity FCVIQ outcomes. Significantly lower functional connectivity between groups was observed in two clusters involving the somatomotor, frontoparietal, orbito-affective, cingulo-opercular, and default mode networks. Within the CVI group, significant associations were observed for visual (dis)interest and clutter and distance viewing impairments in multiple networks. These results support that CVI and the severity of every day visual difficulties may be associated with changes to higher order executive and cognitive networks to interpret and/or provide top-down control over sensory processes.

Article.Title: Long COVID burden in healthcare workers: a 12-month survey of 771 cases
Article.Authors: Pagani E.; Fresi E.; Zuccaro V.; Asperges E.; Cutti S.; Klersy C.; Bruno R.
Article.Abstract: Long COVID syndrome represents a significant public health concern, with healthcare workers constituting a population at particularly high risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection and subsequent persistent symptoms. To evaluate the prevalence of Long COVID syndrome in healthcare employees of IRCCS Policlinico San Matteo Foundation over a four-year time window from the pandemic onset. An anonymous survey was conducted among healthcare workers with documented SARS-CoV-2 infection since February 2020. Long COVID syndrome was defined as persistent symptoms lasting beyond 12 weeks from the acute infection, extending to 12 months or more. The Fisher exact test and the McNemar test were used to compare prevalences between groups and over time, respectively. Unsupervised learning techniques were used for identifying patient aggregation. Among 771 respondents (response rate 41.41% of employees with previous SARS-CoV-2 infection), the overall Long COVID syndrome cumulative prevalence (participants experiencing symptoms at any time point) was 27.9% (215/771; 95% CI: 24.7–31.2%), with point prevalence decreasing over time: 26.0% (95% CI 23.0–29.0%) at 3 months, 20.0% (95% CI 17.0–23.0%) at 6 months, and 16.0% (95% CI 14.0–19.0%) at 12 months post-infection. Significant associations were found with job position ( p = 0.004), with nurses showing the highest prevalence (35.0%). Fatigue, joint and muscle pain, concentration troubles, and memory difficulties emerged as the most persistent symptoms over time. Long COVID syndrome affects more than one-quarter of healthcare workers with previous SARS-CoV-2 infection, with symptom persistence demonstrating a gradual decline over time. These findings have important implications for occupational health management and workforce planning in healthcare settings.

Article.Title: Prevalence, genotype distribution and associated factors of high-risk human papillomavirus among pregnant women in Eastern Ethiopia: a cross-sectional analysis nested within a population-based cohort study
Article.Authors: Weldegebreal F.; Van Eenooghe B.; Ayana D.; Himschoot L.; Wilfong T.; Yadeta T.; Dheresa M.; Negesa A.; Eticha T.; Geremew A.; Assefa N.; Negash A.; Tura A.; Cools P.
Article.Abstract: High-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection is the main cause of cervical precancer and cancer. Although Ethiopia introduced the quadrivalent Gardasil ® HPV vaccine (targeting HPV6, 11, 16, and 18), data on the distribution of HR-HPV genotype and the coverage provided by the vaccine remains limited. We assessed the prevalence, genotype distribution, theoretical vaccine coverage, and associated maternal factors for HR-HPV among apparently healthy pregnant women in eastern Ethiopia. This study was a cross-sectional analysis nested within the EthiOMICS cohort, a population based longitudinal study of pregnant women (12–22 weeks of gestation) recruited from the Hararghe Health and Demographic Surveillance System Site. A total of 217 vaginal swabs were collected, genomic DNA was extracted, and HR-HPV detection was performed using the Seegene HR HPV Allplex™ assay targeting 14 high-risk genotypes. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 28. Among the 217 pregnant women, HR-HPV prevalence was 12.9% (95% CI: 8.8–18.1). HPV16 and HPV66 were the most common genotypes (21.4% each), followed by HPV31, HPV58, and HPV51 (17.9% each); 35.7% of HPV-positive women harbored multiple HR-HPV genotypes. Participant-level theoretical genotype-based coverage among HR-HPV-positive women was 25.0% for the quadrivalent vaccine and 71.4% for the 9-valent vaccine. Detection of Ureaplasma parvum and Mycoplasma hominis was associated with HR-HPV in the adjusted exploratory analysis. More than one in eight pregnant women harbored HR-HPV, and more than one-third of these women had multiple high-risk genotypes. Theoretical participant-level genotype-based coverage of the quadrivalent vaccine currently used in Ethiopia was 25.0% among HR-HPV-positive women. These findings highlight the diversity of circulating HR-HPV genotypes among pregnant women in eastern Ethiopia and underscore the importance of continued molecular surveillance.

Article.Title: Machine learning for advancing gamma source localization in a human phantom using NaI (Tl) detector spectra in radiobioassay
Article.Authors: Moshkbar-Bakhshayesh K.; Lashani Z.; Mohtashami S.
Article.Abstract: This study introduces a machine learning (ML) based framework for the anatomical localization of gamma radiation sources in a human phantom (i.e., RMCII) using energy spectra from a NaI (Tl) scintillation detector, aiming to enhance internal dose assessment accuracy in radiobioassay. Spectra from Co-60, Cs-137, and Ba-133 placed in GI, lung, thyroid, and whole-body (WB) organs were recorded using a whole-body counter. After background subtraction and Min–Max normalization, ten statistical features (mean, skewness, kurtosis, entropy, interquartile range, etc.) have been extracted from each spectrum. A modular classification strategy trained four ML models (i.e., logistic regression (LR), decision tree (DT), support vector machine (SVM), multilayer perceptron (MLP)) for each isotope-detector configuration. LR achieved 100% localization accuracy when the detector was positioned in front of the GI organ with thyroid spectra excluded, while DT achieved up to 97.4% under the same conditions. However, performance dropped for Ba-133 due to spectral overlaps and attenuation, and for the WB detector position due to geometric symmetry. SVM and MLP performed poorly due to limited data and feature sensitivity. This modular, feature-based approach demonstrates the feasibility of ML for source localization in constrained radiobioassay settings, with LR and DT emerging as the most reliable classifiers, while highlighting challenges for low-energy isotopes and symmetric geometries that require future investigation.

Article.Title: A preliminary study on wound healing and scar reduction using platelet-rich fibrin matrix
Article.Authors: Bempah S.; Abaidoo C.; Bimpong S.; Okwan D.; Robertson J.; Atobiga C.; Diby T.; Appiah A.; Sarkodie F.; Nketsiah J.; Obeng P.; Owusu S.; Domfeh E.; Ampofo M.
Article.Abstract: Wound healing is a natural response to tissue injury. Many factors come into play during the process, leading the body to make compromises to ensure healing and, in turn, form scars. Over the years, several approaches have been developed to aid wound healing. Platelet-rich plasma is believed to have various important capabilities, such as serving as a source of growth and clotting factors, and possessing both chemotactic and mitogenic properties that aid wound closure and healing and minimise scar formation. This experimental animal study aimed to increase wound-healing rates and quality by using platelet-rich fibrin matrix, a derivative of platelet-rich plasma, with particular focus on reepithelialisation and scar tissue reduction. Platelet-rich fibrin matrix-treated wounds demonstrated faster closure primarily through contraction. They also showed superior histological reepithelialisation and scar resolution. The test group recorded a 73.18% reduction in wound diameter for the first week and 100% closure by day 14. The control group recorded a 65.32% reduction in wound diameter by the end of the first week, a 92.09% reduction by the end of the second week, and 100% closure by day 18. Wound closure was accompanied by reepithelialisation. The test group showed higher rates of scar resolution, with statistically significant differences compared to the control group. This can be attributed to the abundance of growth factors and other necessary chemicals provided by the platelets. Based on the results from the test group, it may be speculated that platelet-rich fibrin matrix may be potentially beneficial for wound treatment. The significance of this study is the provision of preliminary baseline data for wound healing, which will prove useful in the treatment and management of wounds in the clinical setting.

Article.Title: Association of antibiotic exposure with Kawasaki disease
Article.Authors: Suzuki T.; Yoshida J.; Michihata N.; Saito K.; Uchida H.; Kojima A.; Asai Y.; Hata T.; Yoshikawa T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Kawasaki disease (KD) is an acute febrile vasculitis of unknown etiology that primarily affects children under five years old. Emerging evidence suggests that gut microbiota alterations may contribute to KD pathogenesis. Because antibiotics modify intestinal microbial composition, their inappropriate or repeated use in early childhood may increase KD susceptibility. However, population-based evidence linking antibiotic exposure with KD onset remains limited, and the influence of antibiotic class, number of antibiotic prescriptions, and administration route has not been systematically evaluated. To examine the association between antibiotic type, number of antibiotic prescriptions, route of administration, and KD onset in a nationwide dataset. We conducted a matched case–control study using the JMDC database (2005–2024). Children aged 0–6 years were eligible. Newly diagnosed KD cases ( n = 17,410) and controls ( n = 68,621) were matched 1:4 by age, sex, and birth year. Antibiotic exposure from birth until one month before the index date was assessed by class (penicillins, cephalosporins, macrolides, quinolones, others), number of antibiotic prescriptions, and administration route (oral vs. intravenous). Multivariable conditional logistic regression estimated odds of KD onset adjusted for antiviral agent use, antifungal agent use, preterm birth, and low birth weight, with matching by age, sex, and birth year accounted for in the conditional analysis. Among 86,031 children, exposure to penicillins (OR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.21–1.34), cephalosporins (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.10–1.23), quinolones (OR, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.27–1.73), and macrolides (OR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.09–1.31) was associated with increased KD risk. Higher odds of KD were observed with increasing numbers of antibiotic prescriptions (≥ 5 prescriptions: OR, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.16–1.28). Oral antibiotic use showed a significant association (OR, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.16–1.27), while intravenous use did not. Repeated antibiotic prescriptions, especially via oral administration, were associated with KD. These findings support an association between prior antibiotic exposure and KD, warranting further mechanistic investigation.

Article.Title: Serum brain-derived neurotrophic factor response to maximal exercise in coronary artery disease and chronic heart failure
Article.Authors: Baladzhaeva S.; Fuertes-Kenneally L.; Sanz-Rocher A.; Manresa-Rocamora A.; Climent-Payá V.; Sempere-Ruiz N.; Pérez-González R.; Sellés-Climent E.; Alfayate-Guerra R.; Sirera-Sirera P.; Sarabia J.
Article.Abstract: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) has emerged as a prognostic biomarker in coronary artery disease (CAD) and chronic heart failure (CHF). While exercise is known to acutely elevate BDNF in healthy populations, evidence in CAD and CHF remains limited. The aims of the study were: to compare resting serum BDNF concentrations between patients with CAD, CHF, and healthy controls; to determine the acute effect of a maximal cardiopulmonary exercise test (CPET) on serum BDNF; and to explore potential moderating factors (i.e., sex, age, body mass index, lactate). Fifteen patients with CHF, 14 with CAD, and 14 age-matched healthy individuals (all male or postmenopausal females, 40–75 years) underwent a symptom-limited CPET with blood sampling pre- and post-exercise. Serum BDNF was quantified using ELISA. Repeated-measures ANOVA models and Pearson correlations were used to conduct data analyses. Resting serum BDNF levels were significantly lower in CAD patients compared to healthy controls (–11.38 ng·ml⁻¹; 95% CI = − 18.65, − 4.10). No statistically significant differences were found between the other groups ( p > .050). Maximal exercise induced a significant increase in serum BDNF (5.99 ng·ml⁻¹; 95% CI = 2.44, 9.54), with no significant differences between groups ( p = .987). Patients with CAD exhibit significantly lower resting serum BDNF than controls, while differences in CHF patients did not reach statistical significance. The BDNF response to maximal exercise in both patient groups was of similar magnitude to that of controls, although the limited sample size precludes firm conclusions. The response was independent of sex, though future research should explore inter-individual variability and the minimum intensity to increase BDNF.

Article.Title: Bidirectional cross-scale detail-semantic collaborative network (BCDS-Net) for vision-based waste recognition
Article.Authors: Yang X.; Xu C.
Article.Abstract: The continuous growth of global waste generation poses serious challenges to environmental protection, public health, and resource recovery. In intelligent sorting systems, vision-sensor-based waste recognition is a challenging core perception task, yet its reliability is often affected by scale variation, background clutter, and inter-class visual similarity. To address these challenges, we propose BCDS-Net, a Bidirectional Cross-Scale Detail-Semantic Collaborative Network combining a Hybrid Conv-MLP backbone, Scale-Aware Context Gated Fusion, Dilated Scanning Attention, and Bidirectional Cross-Scale Aggregation to enhance local details, model long-range dependencies, and fuse multi-scale features. This study focuses on single-label waste image classification. Each input image is assumed to contain one predominant waste category, and the model outputs one image-level category label. BCDS-Net does not perform object localization, multi-object detection, or instance segmentation. Evaluations on TrashNet, RealWaste, and TrashBox achieved accuracies of 96.73%, 92.15%, and 96.23% and recall rates of 96.87%, 92.26%, and 96.27%, respectively, outperforming representative baselines. Scale- and condition-stratified evaluations further demonstrate stable recognition under object-size variation, background clutter, occlusion, and degraded image quality. With 11.53M parameters and 2.52G FLOPs, BCDS-Net achieves a batch-size-one FP32 latency of 24.4 ms (41 samples/s) on an NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX at an input resolution of 224 $$\times $$ 224, and 3.2 ms on an NVIDIA RTX 3090. These results indicate that BCDS-Net provides a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off and has potential for edge deployment, although performance on a specific device remains hardware and implementation dependent.

Article.Title: Resting-state electroencephalographic characteristics in patients with atopic dermatitis accompanied by chronic pruritus
Article.Authors: Sun D.; Li W.; Liang N.; Liu S.; Zhu Z.; Yu P.; Zhao Y.; Yuan J.; Zhao Y.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated resting-state EEG alterations in patients with atopic dermatitis (AD) and chronic pruritus and their associations with clinical symptoms, aiming to provide insights into central neurophysiological mechanisms and identify candidate biomarkers. This case-control cross-sectional study recruited AD patients and matched healthy controls (HCs). All underwent eyes-closed resting-state EEG and clinical assessments. Frequency features and power spectral density were compared using t-tests. Functional connectivity was assessed using network-based statistics, and entropy measures using permutational multivariate analysis of variance. Spearman correlations examined relationships between EEG indices and clinical scores. The Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure was additionally applied to account for multiple comparisons. Thirty-seven AD patients and 38 HCs were included. Nominally significant between-group differences in right-hemispheric peak and mean frequencies across the delta and low-frequency beta bands did not survive FDR correction. Global EEG power was reduced in the theta, alpha, and beta bands (all FDR-adjusted P < 0.05). At the regional level, significant reductions were observed in the central region for the theta, alpha, and beta bands and in the occipital region for the beta band (all FDR-adjusted P < 0.05). No significant between-group differences were identified in functional connectivity or multivariate entropy measures. In AD patients, right-hemispheric delta peak frequency was positively correlated with anxiety symptoms ( r s = 0.511, FDR-adjusted P = 0.029). No significant correlations were observed between EEG power measures and clinical symptoms. Patients with AD accompanied by chronic pruritus exhibit alterations in resting-state EEG, characterized by reduced global power in the theta, alpha, and beta bands. Right-hemispheric delta peak frequency was positively associated with anxiety symptoms in AD. Resting-state EEG measures may represent candidate biomarkers warranting further investigation. Trial registration: This study was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (Registration No. ChiCTR2400093716).

Article.Title: Genetic variability and multi-trait analysis for enhanced yield stability under acid soil stress in common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.)
Article.Authors: Wirtu A.; Abtew W.; Fenta B.; Sandri M.; Nebiyu A.; Nigussie A.; Menamo T.
Article.Abstract: Soil acidity and low soil fertility are the bottlenecks to sustaining common bean production and productivity. Enhancing stable varieties needs understanding genetic variability and selecting genotypes based on multiple traits across environments for soil acidity tolerance. This study was aimed to determine genetic variability, trait associations, and identify superior genotypes for soil acidity tolerance via multi-trait biplot analysis. A total of 300 common bean genotype were evaluated using Alpha lattice Design with two replications across two locations under lime treated and lime untreated acidic soil conditions during the 2022 growing season. ANOVA revealed highly significant ( P < 0.001) genotypic variation and genotype-by-management interactions effects for all traits, indicating substantial genetic variability. Mean grain yield was 2331 kg/ha under lime treated conditions, ranging from 974.5 kg/ha (CB97) to 3464.4 kg/ha (CB81). Under soil acidity stress, mean grain yield declined to 1424 kg/ha, ranging from 309.96 kg/ha (CB97) to 2313.14 kg/ha (CB82), reflecting a 38.9% of reduction due to soil acidity stress. Phenotypic Coefficient of Variation ranged from 5.53 to 43.81%, while Genetic Coefficient of Variation ranged from 1.79 to 25.02%. Broad sense heritability ranged from 12.87 to 93.6% s and genetic advance as percentage of mean ranged from 1.46 to 51.69%. Genotype by traits and Genotype by Yield by Trait biplots analyses revealed positive associations for most traits across acidic soil environments, confirming the feasibility of selecting genotypes for balanced performance. Genotypes CB82 and CB231 were superior and stable, while CB151 (SMR241), CB82 (KSGPC25), CB57 and CB231 (CB170044-42-1) identified as promising candidates for breeding acid-tolerant, high-yielding varieties of common bean. In the future, the application of molecular markers to identify genes for soil acidity tolerance will be crucial for using the information to improve breeding efficiency in beans.

Article.Title: Skin transcriptome comparison of Changthangi Pashmina and Sirohi goats reveals fibre-barrier and skin remodeling expression signatures
Article.Authors: Bhat B.; Nazir F.; Yaseen M.; Syed M.; Assad A.; Shah R.; Ganai N.
Article.Abstract: Goat breeds have developed diverse phenotypic characteristics through natural selection and long-term exposure to different environments. In this study, we compared skin transcriptomes from the high-altitude, cold-adapted Changthangi Pashmina goat and the hot, semi-arid-adapted Sirohi goat. To our knowledge, this is the first comparative transcriptomic study of these two contrasting goat breeds, revealing distinct molecular signatures associated with skin biology, fibre production, breed-specific characteristics, and molecular response to contrasting climatic conditions. Differential expression analysis identified 420 significant DEGs (|log2FC| ≥ 1, FDR < 0.05), including 180 genes upregulated in Pashmina and 240 in Sirohi. Changthangi Pashmina goats showed enrichment of keratinization , formation of the cornified envelope , epidermal differentiation , lipid metabolism , and hair-follicle-development processes. Key upregulated genes in Pashmina goats including ASIP , AWAT1 , KLK6 , KRT77 , KRT79 , DGAT2L6 , LIPK , CES3 , CES4A , AADACL3 , TGM5 , and WNT4 were associated with white fibre formation, secondary hair-follicle development, fine-fibre formation, epidermal barrier maturation, lipid-rich skin and coat maintenance, and thermal insulation, features that are central to Pashmina production and survival under the cold, arid, high-altitude environment of Ladakh. Sirohi goats showed significant enrichment of signaling pathways like IL , TNF , chemokine , tyrosine , immune response , inflammatory , oxidative-stress and endocrine processes . These pathway-level changes were supported by upregulation of TYR , TYRP1 , DCT , PMEL , TRPM1 , SOX10 , IL6 , CXCL8 , CXCL10 , PTGS2 , CH25H , ACOD1 , and SLC7A11 . The upregulated genes were consistent with the characteristic dark pigmentation, heat tolerance, immune responsiveness and overall environmental robustness of Sirohi goats. These findings provide a strong foundation for livestock improvement related to fibre quality and climatic adaptation. Validation of these candidates in larger populations may support future breeding strategies for developing goats with better fibre traits, improved performance, and greater resilience to changing environmental conditions.

Article.Title: High alkalinity mitigates the negative impacts of high-CO2 ocean on foraminiferal calcification quantity and quality
Article.Authors: Kinoshita S.; Kuroyanagi A.; Hashimoto Y.; Suzuki A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ocean acidification threatens marine calcifiers, but the independent effects of seawater pH and total alkalinity on shell formation remain poorly understood. Here, we experimentally decoupled pH and alkalinity to examine their effects on shell growth and density in the large benthic foraminifer Amphisorus kudakajimensis . Low pH under present-day alkalinity substantially reduced shell weight, volume, and density, whereas simultaneously elevated alkalinity largely compensated for these negative effects. Shell weight and volume increased across the tested range of calcite saturation state, consistent with the balance between available inorganic carbon substrates and inhibitory protons. In contrast, shell density showed a more constrained response, suggesting physiological limits on further densification. These results provide experimental support for a carbonate-chemistry mechanism that may help explain how the low-pH but high-saturation conditions of Cretaceous oceans allowed calcifiers to persist. They also suggest that maintaining carbonate saturation through ocean alkalinity enhancement could help protect calcification under future acidification. Assessments of the vulnerability of marine carbonate producers to changing ocean chemistry should therefore distinguish between changes in shell growth and shell density.

Article.Title: Cometary impacts an unlikely pathway towards the origins of life on Earth
Article.Authors: Anslow R.; McDonald C.; Bonsor A.; Rimmer P.; Rae A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract An early period of cometary bombardment has long been speculated to provide an important source of prebiotic feedstock molecules, required for the origins of life on Earth. In support of this interpretation, comets boast a rich diversity of volatile organic molecules, with many thought to be limiting for prebiotic chemistry. Modelling studies suggest, however, that a significant proportion of these molecules will be destroyed during hypervelocity impact. Here, we revisit the ability of comets to deliver prebiotic feedstock molecules in the high concentrations required for prebiotic chemistry, leveraging recent advances in cometary impact simulations, comet-atmosphere interactions, and dynamical modelling of short-period comets’ origin and evolution. Taken together, the rapid decline in Earth’s cometary impact bombardment and the efficient destruction of fragile cometary organics indicate that the successful delivery of prebiotic feedstock molecules was an exceedingly rare event. Our results therefore challenge the long-held assumption that cometary impacts played an important role in the origins of life on Earth.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: short-period comets; origin of life; cometary impacts; prebiotic chemistry; hypervelocity impact; impact simulation

Article.Title: A 100-Gb/s hybrid PDM-DWDM system for simultaneous bidirectional LEO-to-LEO inter-satellite optical communication
Article.Authors: Bhutiani S.; Ye W.
Article.Abstract: Optical inter-satellite links (ISLs) have emerged as a key enabling technology for next-generation satellite communication networks due to their advantages over traditional radio-frequency (RF) based ISLs. However, practical high-capacity links must combine bidirectional operation, compact terminals and resilience to dynamic pointing errors. We present a unified design and performance analysis of a 100-Gb/s aggregate hybrid polarization division multiplexing (PDM) and dense wavelength division multiplexing (DWDM) bidirectional low-earth orbit (LEO) ISL. The design integrates a compact 10 cm common aperture on each satellite, dedicated forward and return wavelengths around the 1550 nm window, quantified local transmitter-receiver isolation and an optically pre-amplified receiver model. The system performance is evaluated using a detailed link budget and Monte Carlo framework that incorporates two-dimensional Gaussian pointing jitter together with varying transmitter power, link ranges, Mach–Zehnder modulator extinction ratio, polarization extinction ratio and optical aperture efficiency over $$\:{10}^{5}$$ independent realizations. Performance is quantified through signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), cumulative distribution functions (CDFs), average bit-error ratio (BER) and outage probabilities. Under conservative worst-case pointing conditions, our proposed system supports simultaneous 100 Gb/s aggregate bidirectional operation over separations up to 6000 km, yielding an average BER $$\:\le\:2.5\times\:{10}^{-2}$$ with $$\:\le\:\:2.58\%$$ SD-FEC outage at 37 dBm transmit power. These results indicate the proposed architecture’s viability for high-capacity bidirectional optical inter-satellite links using a single compact aperture per satellite, while establishing quantitative design requirements for compact LEO satellite terminals.

Article.Title: Hybrid feature pyramid attention and capsule network (FpaNet+CapsNet) for enhanced spatial and contextual feature extraction for improved brain tumor segmentation
Article.Authors: Aldakheel E.; Zakariah M.; Amin S.; Kashmeery T.; Dubey P.; Hakami N.
Article.Abstract: Gliomas are among the most dangerous brain tumors, and their treatment depends on accurately outlining the tumor in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). These outlines are hand-drawn, vary from expert to expert, and are time-consuming to create. Automatic techniques may help, but glioma boundaries are difficult to detect because of the wide variety of shapes, sizes, and contrast. While existing deep learning models address only part of this issue, attention-based networks can capture multi-scale information but may lose spatial relationships in parts of the tumor, and capsule networks can retain these relationships but lose broader context. This study therefore proposes a hybrid model, FpaNet+CapsNet, combining a Feature Pyramid Attention Network and a Capsule Network. The attention module will see the fine details and the context, and the capsule module will preserve the shape and structure of the tumor. Four MRI sequences (T1, T1Gd, T2, and FLAIR) were used for the BraTS2020 model. Patients were split into training (236), validation (59), and test (74) groups prior to pre-processing and augmentation. Both modules proved useful on the test set, achieving Dice scores of 99.05%, 98.05%, and 99.50% for enhancing tumor, tumor core, and whole tumor, respectively, with an overall accuracy of 99.6% and an average HD95 of 2.40 mm. Ablation and statistical tests confirmed the usefulness of both modules, and the model was successful with a Dice score of 0.962 on the unseen BraTS2021 set. These results indicate that the model can accurately and reliably segment gliomas, but requires further clinical validation.

Article.Title: Lifetime economic impact of pediatric cataract surgery in sub-Saharan Africa: a case study from Kinshasa
Article.Authors: Poschkamp B.; Guthoff R.; Ngoy J.; Hopkins A.; Faber H.; Steinau E.; Stahl A.; Fleßa S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Childhood cataract is a major cause of treatable childhood blindness in sub-Saharan Africa. Effective care requires case finding, surgery, and long-term follow-up. While economic evaluations largely focus on adult cataract surgery and report high cost-effectiveness, evidence for pediatric cataract care remains limited. We built a lifetime model for bilateral pediatric cataract care, comparing discounted present values of costs and benefits with and without intervention. Costs included case finding, preoperative assessment, bilateral surgery and follow-up; benefits were expressed as age-specific productivity (GDP proxy) and quality-adjusted life years (QALYs). Parameter ranges from local program data, expert input and published sources were tested in one-way and scenario analyses. In the base case, surgery generated a present-value GDP gain of US$23,409 and 5.4 QALYs, indicating cost savings with improved quality of life. The intervention remained cost-saving across most plausible ranges; only an extreme worst-case produced a small negative GDP balance (− US$2,269) while still gaining 1.8 QALYs, remaining strongly cost-effective. Results were driven mainly by the discount rate and post-operative working-age productivity rather than surgical or follow-up costs. High-quality pediatric cataract management can therefore represent a high-return investment, but affordability constraints and uncertainty in long-term outcomes underscore the need for prospective follow-up and financial protection.

Article.Title: Integrating bioinformatics analysis with molecular simulation to elucidate the therapeutic mechanism of Guizhi Fuling Wan for adenomyosis and endometriosis
Article.Authors: Wu J.; Li X.; Li S.; Luo Y.; Gao Y.; Tao Y.; Yang J.; Hong W.
Article.Abstract: To elucidate the mechanism of Guizhi Fuling Wan (GFW) against adenomyosis (AM) and endometriosis (EM) using an integrated approach combining network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation. GFW components and their targets were retrieved from the Traditional Chinese Medicine Systems Pharmacology Database and Analysis Platform (TCMSP) and SwissTargetPrediction databases, while AM and EM targets were obtained from GeneCards and Open Targets Platform. Intersection targets were identified, and a herb-ingredient-target network was constructed. Protein-protein interaction networks, Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses, and molecular docking were performed, followed by 200 ns molecular dynamics simulations. Seventy-six active ingredients and 480 potential GFW targets were identified, with 176 intersecting with AM and EM. Core ingredients included cerevisterol, kaempferol, and baicalein; hub targets comprised AKT1, MAPK3, HSP90AA1, BCL2, TP53, ESR1, and JUN. Enrichment analysis implicated PI3K-Akt, MAPK, focal adhesion, and apoptosis pathways. Molecular docking and dynamics confirmed stable interactions between core ingredients and AKT1. GFW may exert therapeutic effects against AM and EM through a synergistic multi-component, multi-target mechanism involving the neuro-endocrine-immune-metabolic axis and key signaling pathways, which may provide a systems-level rationale for its clinical application.

Article.Title: Delay-induced dynamics and Hopf bifurcation in a quarantined SEIQR epidemic model with nonlinear incidence
Article.Authors: Hussien R.; Hamodi R.; Al-Jubouri K.; Naji R.; Ali A.
Article.Abstract: Mathematical modeling provides a rigorous framework for analyzing infectious disease transmission and assessing control strategies, among which quarantine plays a central role in limiting disease spread. In this study, we propose a delayed SEIQR epidemic model incorporating quarantine measures and a nonlinear incidence rate, where the population is partitioned into five compartments: susceptible, exposed, infected, quarantined, and recovered. Initially, the positivity and boundedness of solutions are established to ensure the biological feasibility of the model. The basic reproduction number \(\:{R}_{0}\) is derived using the next-generation matrix approach, and the local stability of the equilibrium points is rigorously analyzed. In particular, the healthy equilibrium point (HEP) is shown to be locally asymptotically stable when \(\:{R}_{0}\:<\:1\) , while the unhealthy equilibrium point (Un-HEP) becomes locally asymptotically stable when \(\:{R}_{0}\:>\:1\) , based on the Routh–Hurwitz criterion. Furthermore, by considering the time delay \(\:\tau\:\) as a bifurcation parameter, sufficient conditions for the occurrence of Hopf bifurcation are established, and the direction and stability of the emerging periodic solutions are determined. Unlike existing studies, this work introduces a non-monotonic saturated incidence with delay within a quarantine-based SEIQR framework, and rigorously derives explicit analytical conditions governing the onset, direction, and stability of Hopf bifurcation, thereby uncovering critical delay-induced oscillatory dynamics that are often overlooked in classical epidemic models. Finally, numerical simulations with appropriately selected parameter values are provided to validate the theoretical findings and to illustrate the dynamical behavior of the proposed model.
