Article.Title: Biogenic synthesis of ZnO nanoparticles using Aspergillus flavus for sustainable removal of strontium ions from contaminated water based on bioremediation technology
Article.Authors: Mousa A.; Hussin L.; Kamal N.; Attallah M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Addressing the environmental risks associated with inorganic pollutants, such as heavy metals and radionuclides, requires a shift toward sustainable remediation strategies. The primary objective of this study is to investigate biosynthesized zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO NPs) using Aspergillus flavus for environmental bioremediation. Characterization verified the successful synthesis of crystalline (30–60 nm). Batch sorption experiments demonstrated selectivity for strontium, achieving a maximum equilibrium uptake (q e ) of ~ 30.5 mg g −1 under optimized conditions (pH of 8, 5 h, 0.05 g adsorbent, 25 mg/L initial concentration, 25 ± 2 °C). Isotherm and kinetic data followed the Langmuir model and pseudo-second-order kinetics, respectively, while thermodynamic analysis indicated an endothermic process. Furthermore, ZnO NPs (5–100 mg/mL) exhibited dose-dependent antibacterial, notably against K. pneumoniae and S. aureus , though they showed no effect on the tested fungal strains. Better sorption affinity of Sr rather than Cs is reported. These findings establish biogenic ZnO NPs as effective material for targeted wastewater treatment and promising candidates for antibacterial applications towards eco-friendly method based on bioremediation technology.

Article.Title: A multi-metric characterization of quantum convolutional neural networks: expressibility, trainability, and noise sensitivity
Article.Authors: Hossain T.; Ronggon A.; Uddin M.; Ohidujjaman N/A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Quantum convolutional neural networks (QCNNs) are structured variational quantum architectures for quantum machine learning(QML). This study examines their practical reliability through the balance between expressibility, trainability, optimization geometry, and noise resilience. We propose a multi-metric QCNN framework integrating Haar-based expressibility analysis, gradient sensitivity assessment, finite-size scaling, optimizer benchmarking, empirical Fisher information, Hessian spectral analysis, parameter efficiency evaluation, and depolarizing noise characterization. Our applied 6-qubit, 3-layer QCNN-inspired architecture, with 72 trainable parameters, achieved a Kolmogorov-Smirnov(KS) similarity of (0.8826±0.0144) and a Kullback-Leibler(KL) divergence of (0.05648±0.00578) relative to the Haar-random fidelity distribution. Increasing circuit depth improved expressibility, increasing KS similarity from (0.7400±0.0153) to (0.9471±0.0152) and reducing KL divergence from (0.1812±0.0363) to (0.01815±0.00702). However, 30 of 72 parameters exhibited near-zero sensitivity, and the gradient variance decreased from (0.13939±0.08380) to (0.00929±0.00429) across 2–8 qubits, indicating finite-size gradient suppression without establishing asymptotic barren-plateau(BP) behavior. Furthermore, Adam achieved lower mean squared error(MSE) than gradient descent (0.24388 vs. 0.44056), while Fisher and Hessian analyses revealed anisotropic optimization landscapes. The QCNN required 72 parameters compared with 906 for a dense neural network(DNN) baseline. Under depolarizing noise, MSE increased from 0.39506 to 0.63404 and purity decreased from 1.0 to 0.0893, demonstrating that expressibility alone does not ensure robust trainability.

Article.Title: Knowledge, perceptions, and associated factors of marburg virus disease in selected towns and districts of the South Ethiopia Region: an explanatory sequential mixed-methods study
Article.Authors: Guyo T.; Toma T.; Kebede D.; Ushacho A.; Gujo M.; Alto A.; Asegahegn E.
Article.Abstract: The effectiveness of risk communication and community engagement (RCCE) depends on the population’s baseline knowledge, perceptions, and the sources of information. Therefore, this study aimed to assess community knowledge, perceptions, and associated factors of Marburg virus disease in the South Ethiopia Region. A community-based explanatory sequential mixed-methods study was employed among 614 adults in MVD-affected areas of the South Ethiopia Region from February 16, 2026, to March 10, 2026. Quantitative data were collected using interviewer-administered questionnaires with the Kobo Toolbox data collection software. For qualitative data, focus group discussions were conducted. To identify study participants, a systematic random sampling technique was used. To identify factors associated with knowledge and perception towards MVD, a binary logistic regression was fitted. Statistical significance was declared at a P -value < 0.05. For qualitative data, thematic content analysis was conducted. Among 611 adults who participated in the study, 74.8% (95% CI 71.2%, 78.1%) had good knowledge, and 62.7% (95% CI 58.8%, 66.4%) had positive perception, respectively. Educational status (AOR = 4.40; 95% CI 2.45, 7.89), source of information (AOR = 0.42; 95% CI 0.21, 0.87), and perception (AOR = 2.05; 95% CI 1.28, 3.26) were associated with knowledge. Participants aged 25–59 years (AOR = 0.40; 95% CI 0.21, 0.75), social media utilization (AOR = 5.13; 95% CI 3.12, 8.44), and MVD knowledge (AOR = 2.00; 95% CI 1.31, 3.0) were associated with perception. Health education delivered in multiple channels contributed to increased knowledge, whereas official recognition corrected early misconceptions and changed attitudes. Targeted interventions that focus on lower educational status and wealth, advanced age, and sources of information are essential. Strengthening risk communication and community engagement via trusted platforms is crucial. Strategies that utilize social media for information dissemination, empower housewives, and build positive perceptions are highly recommended.

Article.Title: Robust finite-time speed regulation of SRM drive using improved sliding mode control with super-twisting load observer based on DITC for EVs
Article.Authors: Junejo A.; Hamouda M.; Elgamal M.; Abido M.
Article.Abstract: A robust control strategy combining full-order terminal sliding mode control (FOTSMC) with a super-twisting load observer (STLO) is proposed for the speed loop to enhance disturbance rejection and dynamic performance in switched reluctance motor (SRM) drive systems. Unlike existing FOTSMC methods that suffer from steady-state speed errors under sudden load changes due to the lack of integral action , the proposed approach introduces a novel gain-with-integrator modification to the reference torque, which minimize the steady-state error while maintaining fast transient response. The STLO estimates total disturbances within the direct instantaneous torque control (DITC) scheme for feed-forward compensation. The proposed method enhances robustness, ensures finite-time convergence, reduces chattering, and suppresses torque ripple. Closed-loop stability is verified via Lyapunov analysis, and experimental results on a 12/8 SRM prototype validate its superior performance.

Article.Title: Temporal mapping of the anti-tumor effects of nanobody-based MSLN.CAR-T cell therapy in metastatic solid tumors
Article.Authors: Stathopoulou C.; Zhao M.; Jiang Q.; Hong J.; Bian J.; Venugopalan A.; Zhang J.; Ho M.; Hassan R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Studies on the dynamic changes occurring in the tumor microenvironment (TME) following CAR-T cell therapy have been confounded by host lymphodepletion, multiple dosing and immunodeficient models. Therefore, CAR-T cell mediated changes in the TME contributing to solid tumor resistance to CAR-T cell therapy remain poorly explored. A nanobody-based, mouse mesothelin-targeting CAR-T cell (A101) was developed to study the changes occurring in the TME after single dose treatment in immunocompetent hosts. Flow cytometry, single cell and total RNA sequencing of tumor tissue were used for TME profiling. A101 CAR-T cells achieved effective primary tumor suppression, metastasis reduction, and improved survival after a single dose in immunocompetent, syngeneic mouse models without lymphodepletion. Temporal tumor profiling using RNA sequencing revealed initial downregulation of cell proliferation genes followed by upregulation of inflammation, epithelial-to-mesenchymal-transition (EMT) and extracellular matrix (ECM) modification genes in the CAR-T-treated tumors relative to mock-T-treated controls. This phenotype was reversed at a later timepoint which coincided with downregulation of immunosuppressive Cd274+ Lcn2+ neutrophils and upregulation of anti-tumor P2rx1+ Nrf2− neutrophils. At the same time, upregulation of Ccl2+ in fibroblasts and a more pro-tumorigenic Ptgs2+ macrophage phenotype was observed in CAR-T-treated tumors, indicating a tumor adaptation mechanism. This study demonstrates complex dynamic changes in the TME, and highlights time-dependent responses of solid tumors to CAR-T cell therapy. It further highlights Ptgs2+ macrophages, Lcn2+ neutrophils and Ccl2+ fibroblasts as potential therapeutic targets for improving CAR-T cell anti-tumor efficacy for solid tumors.

Article.Title: Heavy metal contamination and risk assessment with uncertainty analysis in agricultural soils at a rural–urban interface
Article.Authors: Xia F.; Yan X.; Jin C.; Dahlgren R.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract As traditional pollution risk assessments fail to comprehensively consider the conbined effects of individual element toxicity and pollutant species, a modified geoaccumulation index ( I geo ) was proposed to identify priority trace metals and assess pollution risk characteristics in agricultural soils at a rural–urban interface area. Seventy agricultural soil samples were collected and analyzed for 6 heavy metals (Cr, Ni, Cu, Zn, Cd, Pb). To account for uncertainty from spatial heterogeneity in soil heavy metals and model parameters in the risk assessment model, a health risk model coupled with probabilistic triangular fuzzy numbers (TFN) was utilized to evaluate human health risks from three primary exposure pathways. The average concentrations of Cr, Ni, Cu, Zn, Cd, and Pb (mg kg −1 ) were 75.3, 22.6, 44.0, 189, 0.63, and 106, respectively, indicating elevated accumulation of Cd and Pb. The proposed I geo index determined elevated pollution risk levels comparable to the conventional index. Notably, Cd was identified as a priority trace metal to control due to its severe contamination risk ( I m = 3.3). The health risk model revealed no significant non-carcinogenic or cancer risk for adults. However, health risk for children were determined to be unacceptable, with a hazard index (HI) value > 1.0 and a total carcinogenic risk (TCR) > 1.0E−04. Ingestion was identified as the primary pathway of exposure to soil heavy metals. The TFN-based probabilistic assessment indicated higher cancer risk for children than the deterministic method. This difference may be attributed to Cr, which has moderate spatial variability and contributes substantially to health risk. This study provides new insights into pollution and human health risk from soil heavy metals, which can be used to generate strategies to prioritize decision-making on soil heavy metal pollution remediation and risk management in soil environments.

Article.Title: Experimental and analytical investigation on shear mechanism of a novel composite shear connector
Article.Authors: Wu Y.; Liao W.; Zhou M.; Chai H.; Yu G.; Hu H.
Article.Abstract: This study proposes a novel composite shear connector (CSSP-type) for interfaces subjected to large longitudinal shear, in which transverse studs are welded on the side faces of a slotted Perfobond Leiste (PBL) rib. Five push-out specimens, comprising a stud-only, a PBL-only and three CSSP-type specimens, were tested under monotonic static loading following Eurocode 4 and were modelled by calibrated finite elements. All specimens used C40 concrete (46.2 MPa measured cube strength) and Q235 steel, with a constant hole diameter of 40 mm, a slot width of 20 mm and a transverse stud diameter of 16 mm; the stud length ranged from 72 to 82 mm and the through-reinforcement diameter from 12 to 16 mm. Within these ranges, the ultimate capacity of the CSSP-type connector was 92% to 99% higher than that of the stud-only specimen and 31% to 36% higher than that of the PBL-only specimen. Steel strength and rib-plate length most strongly affect the ultimate capacity and stiffness, whereas the through-reinforcement diameter has a moderate effect on both and the slot width and hole diameter have the least effect.

Article.Title: Nonlinear coupling between digital economy development and regional income inequality in a reproducible multi-agent simulation framework
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Hu D.; Song P.
Article.Abstract: As a core driver of global economic growth, the digital economy reshapes regional economic landscapes and income‑distribution patterns. Existing work mostly estimates linear or single‑threshold relationships under static‑equilibrium assumptions, limiting the understanding of feedback between technology diffusion, capital reallocation and regional heterogeneity. This work adopts multi‑agent simulation to build an “economic‑geographical” dual‑gradient coupling model for interacting heterogeneous enterprises, residents and governmental agents on a spatial lattice. Simulations rely on a fully documented synthetic benchmark generated with fixed seed (1642026), without observational statistical, survey or satellite data; parameters are configured rather than econometrically calibrated. Therefore, outputs provide a reproducible simulation framework and mechanistic hypotheses rather than empirical estimates. Simulation results show that inequality variation is primarily explained by the technology‑diffusion gradient (52.8–66.4%), followed by capital‑flow (25.3–31.8%) and institutional gradients (8.3–16.4%). The technology‑capital contribution gap narrows from 41.1 pp in the Pearl River Delta to 22.0 pp in the Northwest at lower development levels. The DEI‑Theil link is monotonic with no interior turning point; thresholds 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 are predefined model inputs, and the relationship disappears after first‑differencing (coefficient = 0.060, p = 0.262). Digital‑infrastructure investment stands out as the single policy tool reducing western inequality by 15.2% by 2040, while 0.5–50 km lattice‑resolution tests generate deviations below 0.054%. Owing to the synthetic benchmark, these results have no external validity.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: multi-agent simulation; regional income inequality; digital economy; nonlinear coupling; reproducibility

Article.Title: Life-years gained and cancer burden in kidney transplantation compared with dialysis: insights from a nationwide dialysis-based cohort
Article.Authors: Wu M.; Hsu P.; Tsai M.; Soong R.; Kao J.; Lee M.
Article.Abstract: Kidney transplant (KT) recipients require lifelong immunosuppression, whereas dialysis patients experience uremia-related immune dysfunction, both of which increase cancer risk. However, direct comparisons of cancer burden between these populations remain limited. We analyzed Taiwan’s National Health Insurance Research Database (1998–2022), including 9,378 KT recipients and 229,278 dialysis patients. Cancer incidence and mortality were identified through national cancer and death registries. During median follow-up periods of 9.6 years for cancer incidence and 11.1 years for mortality, kidney transplant recipients had a substantially lower all-cause mortality rate than dialysis patients (SMR, 0.39; 95% CI, 0.37–0.40), with an estimated survival advantage of 8–11 years. However, KT recipients had modestly higher cancer incidence (SIR = 1.10, 95% CI 1.05–1.15) and cancer-specific mortality (SMR = 1.12, 95% CI 1.04–1.20). Elevated risks were particularly observed for skin, kidney, bladder, and prostate cancers, as well as non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma. Overall, kidney transplantation was associated with substantially better survival than dialysis, despite a modestly higher long-term cancer risk. These findings support continued, risk-adapted cancer surveillance and prevention strategies for kidney transplant recipients.

Article.Title: Divergent user expectations of conversational AI: a comparative sentiment and thematic analysis of ChatGPT and Replika app store reviews
Article.Authors: Kausalya N.; Joy G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Conversational AI apps are increasingly serving two different purposes: instrumental productivity and emotional support. Although both are built on the same underlying language technology, users may evaluate these systems according to different instrumental and relational expectations. This study examines the differences in user evaluation of a task-oriented assistant (ChatGPT) and a companionship-oriented agent (Replika) through computational analysis of the sentiment scoring, NRC emotion analysis, topic modelling, and inferential tests of the 6,000 publicly available app store reviews (3,000 per application). The two applications differed only marginally in overall review polarity, and the direction of the difference depended on the method used: under the Bing lexicon Replika reviews scored slightly higher (M = 0.312 vs. 0.275), whereas under sentimentr ChatGPT scored higher (M = 0.135 vs. 0.102); aggregate polarity was therefore not a robust point of difference between the two corpora. The rating distributions differed significantly between the applications (χ² (4, N = 6,000) = 242.26, p < .001, Cramér’s V = 0.20), with ChatGPT ratings more polarised at both ends of the scale (36.8% vs. 21.7% five-star; 27.4% vs. 23.8% one-star) and Replika ratings more concentrated in the intermediate categories. Once scores were normalised for review length, Replika reviews contained more joy-, anger-, surprise-, and anticipation-associated language, with all effect sizes small; fear-, sadness-, and trust-associated language did not differ significantly between the applications. The coupling between review language and star rating was weaker for the companion application, though the difference was small (App × Rating interaction, partial η² = 0.016); because the two samples span different publication periods, this interaction is reported as provisional. Topic modelling yielded a six-topic solution in which conversation and companionship accounted for 53.6% of Replika reviews against 10.9% of ChatGPT reviews, while task assistance and usefulness accounted for 30.9% of ChatGPT reviews against 1.2% of Replika reviews. Together, the findings are consistent with differences in evaluative framing between the two applications examined in this study, illustrating two representative cases rather than establishing distinct categories of conversational AI systems.

Article.Title: Dose-response effects of sonified movement instability on perceptual-motor regulation in ballet dancers with body image vulnerability
Article.Authors: Valdez C.; Stambor Y.; Tajadura-Jimenez A.; Tentori M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Human sensorimotor control relies on detecting and regulating subtle movement fluctuations. Sonification, mapping these fluctuations into sound, makes normally imperceptible micro-instabilities accessible and supports real-time perceptual–motor regulation. However, it remains unclear how much feedback is beneficial, for whom, and under what conditions. In particular, body-image-related vulnerability may influence responses to such feedback. This study examined how different rates of auditory feedback on movement instability, treated as doses of sonification, affect perceptual–motor regulation in young adult ballet dancers classified into exploratory Low- and High-Vulnerability profiles. Twenty-two participants performed a standardized ballet sequence under three conditions: Active Control (ambience-only), Low-rate sonification (+2 SD threshold in changes in jerk), and High-rate sonification (+1 SD threshold). Micro-instabilities were detected in real time. Outcomes combined subjective measures of body experience (awareness, control, flexibility, and lightness) with objective measures of elbow-level movement instability (Instability Frequency and Cumulative Instability Duration). Results showed systematic differences across the tested feedback-density conditions. Low-rate sonification was generally associated with more favorable subjective body-experience ratings and lower movement-instability measures than High-rate sonification, with several outcomes showing non-monotonic patterns across the three tested Dose conditions.

Article.Title: Machine learning–enhanced label-free Raman spectroscopy for accurate serum-based detection of early-stage breast cancer via tumor-associated antigens
Article.Authors: Akhtar L.; Martínez-Zérega B.; Oseguera-Galindo D.; Jave-Suárez L.; Aguilar-Lemarroy A.; Torres-González L.; Palafox-Mariscal L.; De la Torre-Gutiérrez L.; González-Solís J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Early-stage detection of breast cancer remains a critical challenge for improving clinical outcomes. In this study, an experimentally label-free Raman spectroscopy approach combined with principal component analysis and supervised machine learning is reported for the detection of tumor-associated antigen signatures in serum samples. Raman spectra from early-stage and advanced breast cancer patients, as well as healthy controls, were analyzed alongside recombinant tumor-associated antigen proteins, including $$\alpha$$ -1 antitrypsin, peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase A, peroxiredoxin-2, and triosephosphate isomerase-1. Distinct spectral variations were observed in lipid-, nucleic acid-, and protein-related bands. In particular, a characteristic peak at $$\sim$$ 519 $$\mathrm {~cm}^{-1}$$ , associated with oxidized glutathione and oxidative stress-related structural alterations, was prominently observed in early-stage breast cancer and tumor-associated antigen spectra. Machine learning models trained on principal component analysis-reduced features, including linear discriminant analysis, support vector machine, decision tree, and Naïve Bayes, demonstrated high diagnostic performance, achieving ROC-AUC values above 0.94 for early-stage breast cancer versus controls and above 0.85 for early- versus advanced-stage discrimination. Furthermore, spectral and principal component analysis comparisons revealed partial clustering overlap between early-stage breast cancer samples and tumor-associated antigen proteins, supporting the biochemical relevance of the detected signatures. This integrated spectroscopic and computational approach provides a non-invasive and accurate strategy for early breast cancer detection and stage differentiation, highlighting its potential for clinical diagnostics.

Article.Title: Novel recyclable tridentate Schiff base Cr species based on Fe3O4 magnetic nanocatalyst for efficient multicomponent synthesis of mono and bis dihydro-benzoimidazopyrimidines
Article.Authors: Nik Bakht Azma M.; Zare Fekri L.; MirJafari Z.; Nikpassand M.
Article.Abstract: A novel magnetic nanocatalyst, Fe₃O₄@SiPr@OVASB@Cr, was synthesized, thoroughly characterized, and applied for the green synthesis of 2-amino-4-substituted-1,4-dihydro-benzo[4,5]imidazo[1,2-a]pyrimidine-3-carbonitriles. The catalyst was prepared via a multi-step strategy: Fe₃O₄ magnetic nanoparticles were functionalized with 3-chloropropyltrimethoxysilane, modified with a tridentate Schiff base ligand, and coordinated with Cr species as Lewis acidic sites. One-pot multicomponent cyclocondensation of aromatic monoaldehydes, malononitrile, and 2-aminobenzimidazole was efficiently carried out under solvent-free conditions at room temperature, providing excellent yields in short reaction times. Furthermore, symmetrical bis-aldehydes with flexible tetra- and hexa-methylene ether linkers were successfully employed, affording the corresponding two novel dihydro-benzoimidazopyrimidine derivatives in high yields. The catalyst was characterized by FT-IR, XRD, FE-SEM/TEM, EDX, VSM, TGA, and DSC, confirming its structure and properties. It exhibited good reusability over six cycles with minimal loss of activity, highlighting mild operational conditions, facile magnetic separation, and good efficiency. This work demonstrates a sustainable, economical, and environmentally friendly approach for the synthesis of functionalized heterocycles using magnetic nanocatalysis.

Article.Title: Evaluating hv-block cross-validation for dependence-aware model selection in reference evapotranspiration estimation
Article.Authors: Karimi S.; Sadeghzadeh M.; Shiri N.; Shiri J.
Article.Abstract: Reference evapotranspiration (ET o ) estimation by machine learning techniques, e.g. Random Forest (RF), requires reliable model selection under temporally autocorrelated hydro-meteorological conditions. The hv-block cross-validation procedure 1 has been proposed as an assumption-light, dependence-aware alternative to classical information criteria. On the other hand, its consistency has been criticized because the procedure’s block construction does not satisfy the combinatorial balance of a Balanced Incomplete Block Design (BIBD) on which the original consistency argument relied, so that its theoretical consistency remains unassessed. The present research addressed this gap through a two-phase empirical design. In the first phase, a controlled Monte Carlo simulation (R = 500 replications per autocorrelation strength \(\phi \) ) with a known linear data-generating process was performed to test whether hv-block’s over-selection bias is detectable, persists as sample size scales from n = 4,000 to n = 10,000 and then n = 20,000, and is related to the structural design of the procedure or to autocorrelated noise. In the second phase, the same hv-block framework, using both PACF-based and cyclical exclusion windows, was applied to a real-world, 4000-day ET o dataset from two weather stations in Iran. RF was employed as the base model, and out-of-bag error and 5-fold cross-validation were utilized as temporally naïve benchmarks. As the true input set is unknown for real data, this phase assessed the practical consequences of the criterion choice rather than over-selection. The obtained results revealed that hv-block showed a higher over-selection rate (23–30%) than BIC and AIC at all tested autocorrelation levels, and than 5-fold CV in most configurations. Further, no bias diminishing was detected within the investigated sample-size range ( n = 4000–20,000). Control experiments (ϕ = 0 and h = 0) indicated that the over-selection is mainly associated with the structural design of the procedure (the exclusion gap and the resulting fold geometry and replication imbalance), while the autocorrelated noise showed a secondary role. Nevertheless, the resulting performance accuracy losses were negligible in both the simulation (RMSE differences below 0.002) and real-data applications (RMSE differences lower than 0.01 mm day⁻ 1 at both stations). Overall, while the results partially confirmed the theoretical concern regarding the consistency of hv-block cross-validation, its practical consequences for operational ET o estimation and irrigation water management applications were minimal.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: reference evapotranspiration; spatial autocorrelation; evapotranspiration estimation

Article.Title: Using artificial intelligence for clinical trial quality assurance in a multi-institutional neurovascular-sparing prostate radiotherapy trial
Article.Authors: Doucette M.; Zhang Y.; Liao C.; Lin M.; Yan Y.; Dess R.; Tendulkar R.; Garant A.; Hannan R.; Jiang S.; Nguyen D.; Desai N.; Yang D.
Article.Abstract: Our study evaluated whether a deep learning auto-segmentation model combined with machine learning triage could support radiotherapy clinical trial quality assurance (QA). We analyzed 107 stereotactic ablative radiotherapy (SABR) cases from a multi-institutional phase II clinical trial of neurovascular sparing prostate SABR, focusing on physician contours of the internal pudendal artery (IPA) as a novel organ-at-risk with substantial interobserver variability. Contours were scored by the trial principal investigator as Per-Protocol ( n = 89) or Minor Deviation/Unacceptable ( n = 18). We applied a deep learning model for IPA auto-segmentation. Agreement between human and AI contours was then quantified using 14 overlap, distance, and surface metrics, and a supervised classifier was trained on these metrics to flag clinical trial protocol deviations. While AI segmentation achieved only modest geometric agreement with mean Dice similarity coefficient of 0.446 and 95th percentile Hausdorff distance of 14.23, when incorporating all 14 metrics, a machine learning classifier yielded an AUROC of 0.836 (95% CI, 0.552–0.949), flagging all Minor Deviation/Unacceptable cases with 100% sensitivity (95% CI, 56.6–100%) on the 27 case hold-out set with 6 false positives and no false negatives. AI segmentation combined with metrics-based machine learning can triage protocol deviations within a multi-institutional radiotherapy clinical trial, supporting prospective evaluation of AI-assisted trial QA. However, the small number of hold-out protocol deviation cases in this analysis limits generalizability, and the clinical acceptability of the AI contours and potential reductions in QA workload require further investigation.

Article.Title: AI enhanced multimodal sensor fusion framework for explainable drift-aware decision making in large-scale IoT and cyber physical environments
Article.Authors: Ignisha Rajathi G.; Barakkath Nisha U.; Yasir Abdullah R.; Mary Posonia A.; Mohamed Anwar M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A multimodal fusion system for explainable and drift-adaptive decision making is essential in the era of Internet of Things and cyber-physical systems. In this paper, we propose an AI-powered fusion system to alleviate performance degradations due to distributional drift and improve explainability of deep decision models. Specifically, using modality-specific quality-aware encoders along with temporal fusion backbone, we produce calibrated decision scores based on multimodal sensory inputs. Drift monitoring is performed in feature space and prediction space to detect drift with less latency and adaptation is utilized to recover decision quality with minimal drift overshoot. Under the 10-subject leave-one-subject-out evaluation on WESAD, the proposed framework achieved mean macro-F1 and AUROC values of 0.923 and 0.964, respectively, compared with 0.859 and 0.960 for the early-fusion baseline. In the case of SWaT, the framework resulted in a mean macro-F1 of 0.966 for attack category classification, which is 0.055 higher than the LSTM-AE baseline. For the SWaT framework, the AUROC score reached 0.999 while its AUPRC was 0.911, lower than the best baseline AUPRC of 0.975. At the same time, ECE dropped from 6.8 to 2.1%, and the perturbation-based explanation fidelity was above 92%. Meanwhile, the stage-wise SWaT detection rate was above 0.985 with a false alarm rate below 0.02. For deployments of up to 400 simulated nodes, the inference latency was still 43 ms per decision window, peak memory footprint was 472 MB, and communication load was reduced by 46.15% compared to the cloud-only processing option.

Article.Title: Present scenario on the effectiveness of Bollgard-II (BG-II) cotton expressing the insecticidal crystal proteins against Helicoverpa armigera (Hübner) in India
Article.Authors: Kumar R.; Chandra S.; Paul D.; Shankarganesh K.; Shah V.; Phuke R.; Thube S.; Das J.; Bhute N.; Matti P.; Behere G.; Manickam S.; Prakash A.; Singh S.; Kalyanvat P.; Waghmare V.; Prasad Y.
Article.Abstract: The present study evaluated the mortality of Helicoverpa armigera neonate larvae in laboratory bioassay on Bt ( BG-II ) cotton tissues (leaves, squares, flowers, and bolls) expressing Cry1Ac and Cry2Ab toxins, across phenological stages from three major cotton-growing zones of India (North, Central and South) under irrigated and rainfed conditions during 2018–2023. The hybrids proposed under the All India Co-ordinated Research Project (AICRP) on Cotton, grown in replicated field trials across all three zones, were evaluated. Results revealed both spatial and temporal variations in the H. armigera larval mortality under laboratory conditions. The mean larval mortality (%) observed on leaf tissue in the North zone, irrigated crops, recorded consistently high mortality (approaching 100% at early crop growth stages) from 2018 to 2020. However, a slight decline was observed from 2021 to 2023, with the lowest mean mortality of 93.38% recorded in 2021. All mortality values recorded in the North zone were numerically non-significant. In Central zone, mean larval mortality (%) recorded on leaf tissue was 94.76% under irrigation and 96.01% under rainfed conditions, while in South zone mortality averaged 96.85% (irrigated) and 95.61% (rainfed). Mann–Kendall trend analysis also showed a statistically significant declining trend in the Central zone under both irrigated (τ = − 0.50, p = 0.0064) and rainfed (τ = − 0.73, p = 0.0004) conditions over 2018–2023. Among plant parts, flowers consistently recorded the lowest mortality (up to 81.6%). Mortality in bolls was generally high but showed greater variability between irrigation regimes. A clear numerical reduction in mortality was observed during later crop growth stages (> 90 days), which may be attributed to sublethal exposure to Cry proteins. Over six years, the overall decline in mortality trend from 97.8% (2018) to 94.1% (2023) may not be statistically significant except in the Central zone. As a precaution, it provides information on the survival of H. armigera on BG-II cotton. Nevertheless, as a proactive measure, these observations provide important information on the survival of H. armigera on BG-II cotton. Future studies should therefore focus on continued monitoring of survival patterns to support the long-term sustainability of BG-II cotton.

Article.Title: A multivariate approach to understanding cognitive functioning in high-performance athletes
Article.Authors: Camilleri C.; Johnston K.; Wattie N.; Baker J.; Wojtowicz M.
Article.Abstract: With increasing recognition of cognitive functioning in high-performance athletes, understanding these processes may offer insights into training and performance. The current study adopted a multidimensional approach to characterize domain-general cognitive functioning in high-performance athletes by examining the frequency and distribution of high cognitive scores across multiple cognitive domains. The sample consisted of 188 athletes from a training/development organization (n Female = 109, n Male = 79; Mean age ± SD: 16.56 ± 1.95 years). Athletes completed a battery of computerized neuropsychological tests assessing a broad range of cognitive abilities, including aspects of working memory, inhibition, attention/concentration, and spatial processing (among others). 87.2% of athletes achieved at least one high score at or above the 75th percentile, 69.7% at or above the 84th, and 53.2% at or above the 91st, whereas only 46.3%, 21.8%, and 9.6% achieved three or more high scores at these thresholds. Moderate positive associations emerged among tasks assessing episodic memory, attention/concentration, verbal reasoning and visuospatial working memory ( p < .001). These findings provide a foundation for future research to advance our understanding of athlete cognition and to inform development strategies.

Article.Title: Energy and reserve markets-based energy management system in smart grid including integrated system of flexible resources and distributed generations
Article.Authors: Navesi R.; Akbarizadeh M.; Bahreini M.; Zendehboudi H.; Pirouzi S.
Article.Abstract: By coordinating generation units, storage systems, and responsive loads within a unified framework, virtual power plants (VPPs) can function as both energy producers and storage entities. This operational model enables the constituent components to generate favorable revenue when aggregated as a VPP. Furthermore, applying advanced energy management schemes to grid-connected VPPs can significantly improve both the economic viability and the technical operation of power systems. In line with this objective, this study introduces a comprehensive energy management structure for flexible renewable VPPs functioning within an active distribution network (ADN), while explicitly considering their involvement in day-ahead energy and reserve markets. The proposed approach is formulated as a bi-level optimization problem. At the upper level, the operational strategy of the ADN is determined by minimizing a weighted objective function that incorporates both the expected operational cost and the voltage deviation index, subject to AC optimal power flow constraints. At the lower level, a risk-aware framework is adopted to model the participation of renewable and flexible VPPs in both energy and reserve markets. The objective at this stage is to simultaneously maximize the VPP’s expected profit and its conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) in the respective markets. The associated constraints include the operational characteristics of generation units, storage technologies, and flexible loads, as well as the limits related to reserve provision and flexibility capacity of the VPP. The proposed model incorporates uncertainties associated with load variations, fluctuations in renewable generation, and volatility in electricity prices. To effectively handle these uncertainties while maintaining computational efficiency and accurately capturing flexibility behavior, the Unscented Transform (UT) technique is utilized. Subsequently, the Karush–Kuhn–Tucker (KKT) conditions are employed to reformulate the problem into an equivalent single-level optimization model. In order to determine the optimal solution, a hybrid metaheuristic method combining the Ant-Lion Optimizer (ALO) and the Red Panda Optimizer (RPO) is implemented. The main contributions of this study include: assessing the role and performance of bio-waste generation, hydrogen and compressed air storages within the VPP framework; defining the flexibility boundaries of the VPP; facilitating its concurrent participation in both energy and reserve markets; employing the UT method for uncertainty representation; and proposing a novel hybrid metaheuristic optimization approach. Numerical results confirm that the proposed scheme enhances the economic and technical performance of the ADN by approximately 45.3% and between 41.9% and 64.6%, respectively, relative to conventional power flow approaches, owing to optimal VPP energy management. Regarding the technical performance, energy losses and the voltage deviation index are reduced by approximately 44.9% and 48.9%, respectively. In addition, the VPPs achieve 100% flexibility. Furthermore, integrating flexibility resources, namely the demand response program, hydrogen storage, and compressed air, improves the economic performance of VPPs in the energy market by 1.04% and in the reserve market by 1.96%.

Article.Title: Betta agonistic optimization algorithm: A novel metaheuristic approach for photovoltaic power forecasting
Article.Authors: Deen Mohamed A.; Sakthivel B.; Sheik Mohammed A.; Jeyalakshmi M.
Article.Abstract: Accurate photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential for efficient renewable energy integration because of the nonlinear, dynamic, and uncertain characteristics of solar power generation. This paper proposes a novel Evolutionary Memory-Augmented MambaFormer (EvoMem-MambaFormer) optimized using the proposed Betta Agonistic Optimization Algorithm (BAOA) for short-term PV power prediction. The proposed EvoMem-MambaFormer combines selective state-space modeling with memory-guided attention to effectively capture both short-term and long-term temporal dependencies. A Dual Predictive Space Generator is introduced to learn observation-oriented and future-oriented feature representations, while an Error-Adaptive Selective State Evolution mechanism enables recursive memory updates through error feedback. In addition, a Memory Echo Attention Transformer integrates evolved memory states into the attention mechanism to improve temporal feature extraction, and a Quantum-inspired Phase Memory Resonance module enhances the learning of periodic solar generation patterns. The proposed BAOA, inspired by the territorial competition behaviour of Betta fish, is used to optimize the model hyperparameters, improving convergence and forecasting results. Experimental results on a real-world PV dataset demonstrate that the proposed BAOA-EvoMem-MambaFormer attains an RMSE of 7.448, MAE of 4.602, and R² of 0.948, outperforming existing state-of-the-art forecasting models. These outcomes shows that the model provides an accurate, robust, and efficient solution for photovoltaic power forecasting in renewable energy and smart grid applications.

Article.Title: Spatially heterogeneous restoration of spermatogenesis in the mouse testis following experimental cryptorchidism and orchidopexy
Article.Authors: Kurauchi D.; Nakata H.; Kamijima T.; Kano H.; Makino T.; Naito R.; Kadomoto S.; Iwamoto H.; Yaegashi H.; Nohara T.; Shigehara K.; Izumi K.; Mizokami A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Spermatogenesis is a highly temperature-sensitive process that occurs within the testis and is rapidly impaired upon exposure to abdominal heat. Although spermatogenesis may recover once heat stress is relieved, it remains unclear whether this restoration occurs uniformly within the three-dimensional architecture of the testis. In the present study, we combined experimental cryptorchidism and orchidopexy in adult mice with deep learning-based whole-organ three-dimensional reconstruction. Following 8 weeks of cryptorchidism, markedly impaired segments accounted for 94% of the total tubule length. Ten weeks after orchidopexy, although 87% of the tubule length returned to a normal state, the remaining impaired segments were preferentially located near the rete testis and immediately beneath the tunica albuginea. In the cryptorchid testis, type A spermatogonia were not reduced beneath the tunica albuginea. Incomplete restoration beneath the tunica albuginea was not detected in the vitamin A-deficient testis after the switch to a vitamin A-containing diet. These results suggest that the incomplete restoration beneath the tunica albuginea arises after orchidopexy and may be specific to cryptorchidism. This knowledge may help optimize sperm retrieval, although verification in the human testis is required.

Article.Title: Key considerations from intrinsic properties to context-dependent performance in the preclinical evaluation of crosslinked HA dermal fillers
Article.Authors: Yu R.; Cao J.; Zhang K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Current preclinical evaluation of crosslinked hyaluronic acid (HA) dermal fillers often treats individual assays—rheology, extrusion force, cohesivity, swelling—in isolation, making it difficult to relate intrinsic network properties to context-dependent performance. In this study, five crosslinked HA gels—three commercial BDDE-crosslinked fillers (Juvéderm VOLUMA, Restylane Defyne and Ifresh) and two laboratory-model spermidine-crosslinked HA (SPDHA) gels—were characterized using a multi-assay battery covering extrusion force measurement, rheological characterization (amplitude sweeps, frequency/time sweeps, thixotropy test and flow sweep), cohesivity assessment (drop weight test and dispersion time test), and water uptake evaluation (swelling factor and hydration test). We examined how these different metrics relate to each other. Our results reveal that intrinsic network properties—such as elastic modulus (G′), crossover strain (γ c ) and swelling factor—capture different aspects of gel behavior from context-dependent performance metrics—such as extrusion force, dispersion time (reflecting resistance to hydrodynamic shear), and confined hydration (simulating post-injection spatial constraint). For example, Restylane Defyne exhibited the highest γ c among all products, indicating superior intrinsic resistance to large deformation, yet it showed the shortest dispersion time—a context-dependent outcome. Such discrepancies demonstrate that no single intrinsic parameter can reliably predict context-dependent performance. Interpreting the two sets of metrics in conjunction provides a more comprehensive understanding of each gel’s behavior, which may assist clinicians in product selection and guide future clinical investigation. However, correlations obtained in vitro cannot substitute clinical evidence; further in vivo and clinical studies are necessary to validate these relationships.

Article.Title: Seasonality and the effect of a marine heatwave on the metabolism of Red Sea coral reefs
Article.Authors: Saderne V.; Galvao A.; Langner U.; Tietbohl Talas M.; Rich W.; Nieuwenhuis B.; Rossbach S.; Suggett D.; Johnson M.
Article.Abstract: Coral reefs are in global decline due to climate change, shifting reef ecosystems from 24-hour net heterotrophy to autotrophy, altering carbon cycles and reducing resilience to stressors. Red Sea coral reefs experience some of the warmest waters globally, exceeding 30 °C and reaching up to 38 °C on reef flats during summer. Despite these extreme environmental conditions, the metabolism of Red Sea coral reefs remains understudied. Here, we measured day/night Net Ecosystem Calcification (NEC) and Net Ecosystem Production (NEP) on two reefs using a semi-Lagrangian approach across different seasons, including the 2023 summer marine heatwave and bleaching event (11–12 °C-degree heating weeks). The heatwave caused a shift toward net heterotrophy and dissolution. Sampled Red Sea reefs exhibited high NEP relative to NEC compared to global averages, suggesting Red Sea reefs may be short-term CO 2 sinks.

Article.Title: OBiLSTM-AM: an optimized bidirectional LSTM model with attention mechanism for robust DDoS attack detection in network traffic
Article.Authors: Koroma M.; Fofanah M.; Sesay M.; Sawaneh I.
Article.Abstract: DDoS attacks pose a critical threat to global digital infrastructure, causing severe service disruptions and financial losses. Contemporary low-volume, multi-vector attacks tend to circumvent traditional signature-based protection. The major shortcoming of current machine learning and deep learning detectors is that they do not analyze network traffic bidirectionally and prioritize the most indicative attack signatures, resulting in suboptimal detection of stealthy threats. In this study, the authors propose a new framework, the Optimized Bidirectional LSTM-Attention Mechanism (OBiLSTM-AM), to help fill these gaps. It also comprises a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network that captures the temporal context of past and future traffic conditions, and an attention mechanism that dynamically selects the most significant time intervals for computational analysis. Bayesian optimization is an algorithm that uses machine learning to optimize a model’s hyperparameters (usually to achieve the desired performance level). On a stratified sample of the benchmark CIC-DDoS2019 dataset, using 48,712 windowed sequences (100 time steps each) partitioned into 34,098 training, 7,307 validation, and 7,307 test sequences, the model achieves 99.2% accuracy, 98.5% precision, and 98.3% F1-score, far above those of standard LSTM, GRU, and hybrid models. The OBiLSTM-AM framework therefore offers a highly precise, efficient, and robust solution for real-time DDoS detection, which represents a significant improvement over cybersecurity defense tools.

Article.Title: Grey wolf optimization of renewable hydrogen and electric vehicle refueling stations using pv wind and hybrid energy systems
Article.Authors: Ahmadullah A.; Abdirahman A.; Ali E.; Elazim S.; Karimi B.; Irshad A.; Eirgash M.; Zaray A.; Wali N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study develops and comparatively evaluates three fully renewable hydrogen-EV refueling station configurations powered by PV-only, wind-only, and hybrid PV-wind systems. A Grey Wolf Optimizer was coupled with an 8760-h chronological simulation to jointly determine renewable-generation capacity, electrolyzer size, and hydrogen-storage capacity while enforcing zero electrical and hydrogen supply shortages. The wind-only configuration achieved the lowest techno-economic indicators, requiring 1250 kW of wind capacity, a 594.29 kW electrolyzer, and 621.35 kg H 2 storage, with an NPC of $3.77 million, LCOE of $0.16/kWh, and LCOH of $6.73/kg-H 2 . The hybrid PV-wind system combined 393.68 kW PV and 950 kW wind with a 552.89 kW electrolyzer and 542.05 kg storage, achieving an NPC of $3.92 million, LCOE of $0.17/kWh, and LCOH of $6.99/kg-H 2 . The PV-only configuration required 1622.98 kW PV, a 999.72 kW electrolyzer, and 1869.11 kg storage, resulting in a $6.67 million NPC, $0.30/kWh LCOE, and $11.89/kg-H 2 LCOH. All scenarios achieved LPSP = 0 and LHSP = 0. The results demonstrate that renewable-source selection strongly affects system sizing, storage requirements, and lifecycle economics, while the hybrid configuration provides a diversified supply architecture with reduced dependence on fuel-cell support.

Article.Title: Identification of CRF-related molecular subtypes and a prognostic CRRS model in glioma: insights into immunotherapy response prediction and candidate biomarkers
Article.Authors: Xue J.; Xu J.; Yin Q.; Wang M.
Article.Abstract: Cancer-related fatigue (CRF) is a common symptom in glioma patients, significantly affecting their quality of life. The underlying mechanisms of fatigue in these patients are not fully understood. Using CRF-associated genes (CAGs), we identified two CRF-related subtypes in glioma patients. We evaluated differences in clinicopathological features, immune characteristics, and prognostic stratification between these subtypes. A CRF-related gene-based risk score (CRRS) model was developed using LASSO Cox regression analysis. A nomogram was created to facilitate clinical use. Expression assessment of CAGs was conducted utilizing tissue microarray (TMA) and single-cell sequencing data. Computer-aided screening of potential small-molecule compounds was performed via molecular docking (MD) and molecular dynamics simulation (MDS) to obtain candidate agents for glioma treatment, and their anti-glioma activities were subsequently assessed through in vitro experiments.‌ We identified two CRF-related clusters and constructed a CRRS model based on 10 key CAGs. CRRS was significantly associated with age, WHO grade, IDH mutation status, and 1p/19q codeletion status. High-risk and low-risk groups differed in prognosis, immune cell infiltration, expression of immune checkpoint inhibitors, major histocompatibility complex and T-cell stimulators, computational prediction of immunotherapy response, and drug sensitivity. TMA analysis revealed upregulated expression of IRF7 in glioma. Docetaxel and SNX-2112 can inhibit the proliferation and migration of glioma cells in vitro and promote their apoptosis.‌ CRRS is a potentially reliable prognostic biomarker for glioma and may be correlated with CRF symptoms in patients. IRF7 can serve as a potential biomarker for glioma. Docetaxel and SNX-2112 demonstrate promising prospects as candidate therapeutic compounds for glioma.

Article.Title: Toward trustworthy IoMT healthcare: federated learning and verifiable blockchain for secure edge-driven EHR systems
Article.Authors: Chhabra G.; Mahapatra A.; Mishra K.; Rajareddy G.; Majhi S.; Sarma G.; Sahu P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The advent of Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) has made it necessary to exchange electronic health records (EHRs) across distributed healthcare entities in a manner that ensures their authentication and preserves patients’ privacy. This paper proposes the Federated and Blockchain-enabled Electronic Health Record (FBEHR) framework whose major contribution is the Improved Universal Designated Verifier Signature Proof (IUDVSP). Different from all other pairing-based UDVSP schemes, the suggested solution uses elliptic curve arithmetic compatible with ECDSA to ensure signer authenticity, designated-verifier privacy, and verification control without employing bilinear pairings. According to our experiments in the × 86 edge-server environment, IUDVSP takes 0.22 ms to generate signatures and 0.28 ms to verify them. While these results are below 2-4 ms that we take as the cost of one pairing operation in the adopted reference architecture, they are not the result of a direct same-platform performance comparison of the suggested algorithm with a complete pairing-based UDVSP protocol. The framework also features blockchain-based EHR registration, validation, access, revocation and federated ANN-LSTM-based malicious-user detection. In an internal evaluation of the suggested system, activation of edge processing results in the mean registration and validation latency reduction from 9.87 to 3.59 s which corresponds to the 62.76% latency improvement relative to the same framework but without edge processing. Performance of the FBEHR relative to existing baselines is similar; thus, the primary benefit of FBEHR is its pairing-free designated-verifier security, not latency improvement over those systems. An estimation of the total cost of ownership for a month-long period of FBEHR deployment gives us USD 1850 for the considered FBEHR architecture and USD 12,500 for the same architecture but centralized. This difference of 85.2% is calculated based on a model and is not the experimental performance cost reduction.

Article.Title: Research on optimization of drilling pressure relief scheme for residual triangular coal pillars
Article.Authors: Zhang J.; Zeng Q.; Zhang Y.; Tu X.; Deng X.
Article.Abstract: Based on the residual triangular coal pillar at the 1305 working face of a mine, this study employed numerical simulation to compare two pressure relief schemes with borehole depths of 30 m and 50 m, with field validation conducted under site-specific conditions. The results indicate that the 30 m-deep boreholes achieved a significant pressure relief effect on the residual triangular coal pillar, substantially reducing both the stress and displacement deformation of the surrounding rock of the roadway. In contrast, the 50 m-deep boreholes induced overlapping secondary pressure relief zones in the central part of the coal pillar. This led to a reduction in the load-bearing capacity of the central zone, transferring high stress toward the edges and resulting in an unsatisfactory overall pressure relief effect. Compared to the stress state of the surrounding rock without pressure relief measures, the 50 m scheme not only failed to reduce the stress and displacement but even caused a certain degree of increase. This further underscores the critical importance of optimizing the design of pressure relief schemes in rockburst mines.

Article.Title: Evaporation cracking characteristics and mechanism of silt improved by microbial-induced calcium carbonate precipitation
Article.Authors: Hao J.; Liu D.; Zhang D.; Liu B.; Yuan S.; Wang Z.; Li X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Silt readily develops desiccation cracks under evaporation, degrading mechanical properties and triggering hazards like slope instability and foundation deformation. As an eco-friendly soil improvement technique, MICP lacks systematic study on its anti-cracking effect and mechanism. In this study, laboratory drying cracking tests, combined with orthogonal tests and SEM characterization, are performed to explore the evaporation pattern and crack evolution characteristics of MICP-treated silt, quantify the influence weight of process parameters, and reveal the microscopic improvement mechanism. The results demonstrate that MICP-generated calcium carbonate can block water migration pathways, reducing soil evaporation rate and enhancing the water retention capacity. Compared with plain silt specimens, the modified samples achieve a maximum absolute crack ratio reduction of 1.72% points (about 22% relative reduction, achieved by the A3B2C3 group as the optimal combination), a 16% decrease in average crack width, and a markedly delayed crack initiation time. Orthogonal test results indicate that cementation solution concentration is the dominant factor governing the crack ratio, and the bacteria-cementation solution ratio exhibits a noticeable trend, while bacterial suspension concentration has a negligible effect. The optimal parameters are identified as bacterial suspension at OD 600 =1.5, cementation solution at 1 mol/L, and a bacteria-cementation solution volume ratio of 2:1. Calcium carbonate plays a synergistic role via three occurrence modes, enhancing the anti-cracking performance of silt from both hydraulic and mechanical perspectives.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Seafood carries nutrients and persistent chemicals in the same meal, yet population studies have treated it as one food group. All six seafood categories entered the same models. Finfish dominated them. Each doubling of finfish intake corresponded to 4.4–14.1% higher serum PFAS, 4.8–13.0% higher levels of six of seven retained polychlorinated biphenyls, and 13.2% higher blood mercury. Shellfish added three PFAS: PFOA (+ 9.4%), PFOS and PFNA (both + 5.9%). Crustaceans and seaweed added no positive contribution. One quartile up across the PFAS mixture corresponded to 2.8% higher γ-glutamyltransferase (GGT; ψ = 0.028, 95% CI 0.011 to 0.042). We then split the null finfish–GGT association in two: a positive indirect effect through PFAS (+ 0.032; 0.015 to 0.051), and a negative non-mediated component whose interval included zero (− 0.054; − 0.133 to 0.026).

Article.Authors: Zhu Y.; Zhang Y.; Yin Y.; Cui R.; Zhang S.; Chen S.; Yu X.

This study developed an interpretable XGBoost–SHAP model for classifying LESS-defined high-risk bilateral jump-landing patterns. XGBoost achieved the greatest mean cross-validated AUC (0.991 ± 0.001) and, on the held-out test set, an accuracy of 0.983, recall of 0.976, precision of 0.988, F1-score of 0.982, and AUC of 0.997. SHAP identified foot contact symmetry (FCS), trunk flexion displacement (TFD), knee flexion at initial contact (KF-IC), ankle plantarflexion at initial contact (APF-IC), and trunk lateral flexion at initial contact (TLF-IC) as the five most influential features. Under dual-task conditions, asymmetric FCS increased from 14 to 36%. These findings support interpretable classification of LESS-defined landing patterns and highlight cognitive-task interference in movement screening. However, video-derived inputs remain observer-dependent.

Article.Authors: Li X.; Zhu S.; Wang Z.; Zhu H.; Xing C.; Wang Z.

The 35-gene signature formed two co-expression modules. The turquoise module, but not the blue module, was associated with inferior overall survival and distinct exploratory metabolic and immune-related patterns. We then developed a 10-gene-pair model from turquoise-associated genes. The model stratified survival in the derivation cohort and retained prognostic value in the external TARGET cohort using the same cutoff. In multivariable TARGET analysis, the model remained an adverse prognostic factor after adjustment for age, white blood cell count, and day 29 minimal residual disease. Exploratory analyses also identified distinct predicted drug-sensitivity associations. These findings indicate that a single-cell-informed MSC-associated transcriptional signal can support prognostic modeling, while the cellular source of this signal requires orthogonal validation.

Article.Abstract: Peatland carbon stability reflects the vertical distribution of organic-carbon fractions and their response to changing hydrothermal conditions. At D2, SOC remained within 104.14–117.36 g kg⁻¹ and POC within 11.42–19.09 g kg⁻¹, while MAOC constituted 75.47–94.40% of SOC. At D3, SOC decreased from 147.61 to 148.09 g kg⁻¹ in the upper 20 cm to 93.12 g kg⁻¹ at 60–80 cm; measured CSI reached 23.68 at 20–40 cm. Principal components 1 and 2 explained 41.9% and 14.3% of standardized variance. PC1 contrasted pH, electrical conductivity, bulk density, and moisture with LAP, NAG, and POC, whereas PC2 contrasted total phosphorus with N/P, total nitrogen, and SOC. Under SSP5–8.5, simulated SOC changed by − 23.29%, + 5.11%, and − 2.11% from 2025 to 2100 at D1, D2, and D3, respectively; corresponding SSP2–4.5 changes were − 13.45%, + 16.79%, and + 5.43%. Article.Title: Wave propagation in stochastic triple-porosity thermoelasticity
Article.Authors: Kedim I.; Moulahi T.; Elidy E.; Sayed H.
Article.Abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analytical framework for wave propagation in a generalized thermoelastic medium possessing a triple-porosity structure within the Lord–Shulman (L–S) theory, incorporating stochastic parameter uncertainty. The model extends classical double-porosity theory by adding a distinct third porosity network, enabling realistic representation of complex porous materials such as naturally fractured reservoirs, vuggy carbonate rocks, and biological tissues. We consider a homogeneous, isotropic half-space subjected to thermo-mechanical loading with stochastic variations in material properties. The coupled system of equations for displacement, temperature, and three pore pressure fields is solved analytically using normal mode analysis. Exact expressions for physical quantities are derived in the transformed domain, and the fields are returned to the physical time domain by the Durbin Fourier-series inversion algorithm, accelerated by the Korrektur method and the $$\varepsilon$$ -algorithm, whose parameters are stated explicitly in Section 4.3. The results are computed for silicon, which is used strictly as a well-characterised numerical testbed, with hierarchically ordered triple-porosity parameters. A novel stochastic analysis is introduced using Monte Carlo simulation and perturbation methods to quantify the uncertainty propagation from material parameters to field variables; the random material properties are represented as homogeneous random fields with a prescribed correlation length, which reduce to correlated random variables in the long-correlation limit relevant to the present half-space problem. The deterministic, first-order perturbation, second-order perturbation and Monte Carlo predictions are compared quantitatively, and the correct single- and double-porosity limits of the formulation are recovered as special cases. Graphical comparisons investigate the influence of the third porosity network on wave propagation and field distributions, contrasting behaviors with double- and single-porosity cases at different time instants. The analysis reveals significant quantitative differences induced by triple porosity and parameter uncertainty, particularly in stress concentration, wave attenuation, and thermal diffusion patterns.

Article.Title: A study to explore the physiological impact of AIR+ KN95 masks on children
Article.Authors: Sondarajan R.; Lee J.; Goh D.
Article.Abstract: Masks remain essential for prevention and control of disease, and they may also be the only intervention to provide protection from air pollution including haze. While disposable particulate respirators are commonly used to protect against PM 2.5 and pathogens, most commercially available masks are designed for adults and do not fit children properly. This study evaluated the safety and physiological impact of the AIR+ KN95 mask developed specifically for children aged 7 to 14 years. The study recruited 100 healthy participants and measured the physiological impact of mask use, focusing on end-tidal carbon dioxide (ETCO 2 ), oxygen saturation, heart rate, and respiratory rate. Results showed that ETCO 2 levels were within safe limits (below 50 mmHg) in both resting and mild exertion states, with minimal reported breathing discomfort. Additionally, the mask adequately fit all participants, passing the mask fit test. Although the study was limited in duration, its findings suggest that the AIR+ KN95 mask is safe, comfortable, and effective for routine daily activities in school-going children, without significant respiratory compromise. Further research could explore its long-term use and applicability to children with respiratory conditions. [Trial registration number: NCT07037381]. Article.Title: HDAR-CNet: hybrid deep learning based spectrum sensing and resource allocation model for cognitive radio networks
Article.Authors: Bino J.; Bhuvaneswari P.; Ramesh P.; Gowthaman S.
Article.Abstract: Cognitive Radio Networks require accurate spectrum sensing and resource allocation to efficiently utilize dynamically available spectrum for varying traffic conditions. To address the issues, this research proposed the Hybrid Deep Learning Based Spectrum Sensing and Resource Allocation model for Cognitive Radio Networks (HDAR-CNet) model. Initially, the Multi-size Kernel Recurrent Transformer Network (MKR-TNet) is proposed for spectrum sensing that is designed using Multi-size Kernel Attention and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) based feed forward network of the transformer. Then, the resource allocation strategy is employed using the proposed Sinusoidal Swift Flight Optimization based Deep Reinforcement Learning (2SO-DRL) model. In the proposed DRL model reward estimation is employed by considering the throughput, delay, user priority and penalty to achieve QoS-aware spectrum allocation. Here, the sinusoidal chaotic mapping incorporated in the proposed 2SO algorithm to improve the exploration, avoid the premature convergence and enhances global optimal solution acquisition. The experimental analysis of the proposed HDAR-CNet model based on End-to-End Spectrum Utilization Efficiency and Computation Time acquired the values of 98.9% and 5 s respectively. Thus, the proposed model provides the efficient, intelligent and reliable solution for next-generation wireless communication systems and Cognitive Radio Networks.

Article.Title: FedEdgeHealth: an uncertainty-aware federated edge intelligence framework for real-time multi-modal health monitoring
Article.Authors: Alsyouf A.; Al-Momani A.; Ayadi M.; Abouelkheir E.; Alkhowaiter M.; Alsaadi N.; Alqassim M.; Alazzam M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study introduces a sustainability-focused, uncertainty-aware federated edge intelligence framework for multimodal healthcare monitoring within simulated AIoT-edge environments. Unlike conventional healthcare AI systems that optimize predictive accuracy or latency in isolation, the proposed framework integrates probabilistic multi-task learning with adaptive federated coordination to enable selective client participation and risk-aware resource management across distributed edge nodes. The framework captures predictive uncertainty while learning from heterogeneous, multimodal healthcare data distributed across non-IID clients. Furthermore, an energy-aware workload management strategy is incorporated to minimize computational and communication overhead, thereby supporting sustainable edge-cloud healthcare infrastructures. Experimental evaluations using diverse public healthcare datasets in a simulated federated edge environment demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves superior predictive performance (AUC-ROC = 0.956), enhanced calibration reliability, and reduced estimated latency and modeled energy consumption compared to centralized and conventional federated learning baselines. These findings highlight the effectiveness, robustness, and resource efficiency of the proposed approach under controlled simulation conditions, establishing a reproducible methodological foundation for future physical hardware deployment and prospective clinical assessment.

Article.Title: COVID-19-associated pulmonary aspergillosis: clinical characteristics, species distribution, environmental fungal contamination, and antifungal susceptibility
Article.Authors: Borjian Boroujeni Z.; Hashemi S.; Khodavaisy S.; Daie Ghazvini R.; Salehi M.; Rahimi Foroushani A.; Rafat Z.; Raiesi O.; Hosseinpour L.
Article.Abstract: COVID-19-associated pulmonary aspergillosis (CAPA) is an important secondary fungal complication of severe and critical COVID-19, particularly among patients requiring intensive care. Distinguishing CAPA from Aspergillus airway colonization remains challenging because respiratory isolation of Aspergillus does not necessarily indicate invasive disease. This study aimed to evaluate the burden of CAPA, characterize Aspergillus species distribution, assess antifungal susceptibility, and investigate the role of hospital environmental fungal contamination. This cross-sectional study conducted on hospitalized COVID-19 patients admitted to intensive care units (ICUs). Demographic and clinical data, including underlying risk factors, were collected from medical records. All patients with Aspergillus-positive respiratory or tissue specimens were reassessed at the patient level according to the 2020 ECMM/ISHAM consensus criteria, taking into account clinical and radiological findings and specimen-specific mycological evidence. Aspergillus isolates recovered by culture were identified using molecular methods and tested for antifungal susceptibility. Environmental air sampling was also performed in ICUs. In total, 290 hospitalized COVID-19 patients were included. Aspergillus spp. were isolated from 60 of 290 patients (20.7%). Following patient-level assessment, 54 patients (18.6%) fulfilled the criteria for CAPA, including 3 (5.5%) with proven CAPA, 42 (77.8%) with probable CAPA, and 9 (16.7%) with possible CAPA. Six patients (10.0% of Aspergillus-positive patients) did not fulfill the criteria for CAPA and were classified as having Aspergillus airway colonization. The mean age of CAPA patients was 60.2 ± 12.8 years, and 36 patients (66.7%) were male, with an overall crude in-hospital mortality rate of 42.6%. Molecular identification showed among the 60 Aspergillus isolates, A. flavus as the predominant species (n = 48, 80%), followed by A. fumigatus (n = 9, 15%) and A. terreus (n = 3, 5%). Endotracheal intubation was the most common reported predisposing factor (n = 6, 11.11%). Environmental sampling in the ICU identified 21 fungal isolates, comprising Cladosporium spp. (n = 9), Alternaria spp. (n = 6), Fusarium spp. (n = 3), and Aspergillus niger (n = 3). Antifungal susceptibility testing showed generally low MIC values, with posaconazole (GM MIC 0.07 mg/L; MIC50 0.063 mg/L; MIC90 0.125 mg/L) demonstrating the greatest in vitro activity. The predominance of A. flavus highlights regional variation in Aspergillus species distribution, whereas the detection of multiple airborne fungal genera underscores the importance of environmental surveillance in high-risk hospital settings. Given the lack of strain-level molecular typing, the environmental isolates cannot be considered a demonstrated source of the clinical infections.

Article.Title: Quiet coping and mental health disclosure among university employees in the Philippines
Article.Authors: Mirote B.
Article.Abstract: University employees may recognize work-related mental health strain but still be careful about making it visible at work. This qualitative grounded theory study examined how 10 employees in a Philippine public state university handled workplace disclosure when support, trust, and professional consequences felt uncertain. Face-to-face semi-structured interviews were analyzed through systematic coding and constant comparison. Five interrelated themes were developed: recognizing mental health strain as part of academic work; appraising the professional risks of disclosure; testing relational safety through trusted colleagues; practicing quiet coping through limited visibility; and navigating unclear formal support pathways. The analysis presents quiet coping as a visibility-management strategy in which employees cope with mental health strain while regulating its audience, timing, degree, and professional meaning. Because the findings come from a small single-site sample, they should be interpreted cautiously. Even so, they suggest that employee mental health initiatives need clear confidential pathways and psychologically safer communication cultures, not awareness activities alone.

Article.Title: Correlation of optical coherence tomography and histology in a laser-induced mouse retinal injury model
Article.Authors: Smart T.; Charbit B.; Tian Y.; Love J.; Chu C.; Sarunic M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Understanding the origins of structural features observed in optical coherence tomography (OCT) is essential for improving interpretation of retinal biomarkers. We have developed a workflow to correlate in vivo OCT and OCT angiography with ex vivo histochemistry in a mouse model of laser-induced retinal injury. Adaptive optics OCT provided high-resolution volumetric imaging of lesions, while retinal tissues were subsequently cleared, stained, and imaged with confocal microscopy. A digital tissue-flattening procedure and a two-stage registration pipeline enabled mapping of confocal volumes to OCT datasets using the deep capillary plexus as a structural landmark. Across multiple lesions and animals, hyper-reflective foci (HRF) on OCT co-localised with IB4-positive structures, although inter-lesion variability in the degree of feature correspondence was observed. This framework provides an approach for validation of OCT features to enhance the biological interpretability of retinal imaging biomarkers.

Article.Title: Hierarchical orthogonal ESNs with adaptive signal decomposition for chaotic financial time series prediction
Article.Authors: Zareen S.; Qadri S.; Yan K.; Ikram A.; Ikram S.; Alsubaie N.
Article.Abstract: To improve multi-scale financial time series forecasting, still many challenges exist; specifically, the echo state networks (ESNs) are unable to involve non-stationary dynamics, chaotic behavior, and mixing of frequency components. This is critical concern in the field of fintech, where precise and sound forecasting of financial data is the core of risk management and making informed investment decisions. This work focused on such challenges and came up with a solution in the form of a Hierarchical Orthogonal Echo State Network (HO-ESN) with adaptive signal decomposition. This proposed HO-ESN model, consist of three main contributions, first, Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), to break down raw financial signals into certain frequency components that isolate noise, regularities, and periodicities; second, orthogonal reservoir learning through singular value decomposition (SVD) to obtain near-orthogonal spectral properties to maximize memory capacity and stability with respect to edge of chaos; and third is hierarchical learning with mode-specific inner updates and mode-to-mode outer coordination. This model is trained and tested on four datasets, FinMultiTime (Russell 3000 constituents), RedStone Terminal (cryptocurrency high-frequency trades), TrueFX (EUR/USD tick data) and Fama-French factor portfolios. HO-ESN demonstrates a significant improvement in performance compared with state-of-the-art baselines such as standard ESN, LSTM, GRU, and Transformer models, with an increase in multi-step forecasting accuracy of up to 23%, directional accuracy of up to 19%, and reduces mode interference by up to 47%. Ablation experiments and scalability are used to validate the significance of each part and the scalability of the model to real-time financial forecasting.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: adaptive signal decomposition; financial time series forecasting; echo state networks; chaotic time series; hierarchical networks
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Neural Networks and Reservoir Computing; Decision Sciences > Management Science and Operations Research > Stock Market Forecasting Methods; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Neural Networks and Applications

Article.Title: CalciumInsights enables interactive analysis of calcium transients and assessment of baseline sensitivity
Article.Authors: Suárez-Gómez D.; Perez-Rosas N.; Miranda-Contreras G.; Colom-Braña S.; Zhang W.; Mim M.; Tan S.; Gazzo D.; Tepole A.; Deng Q.; Reeves G.; Isaza-Brando C.; Staiger C.; Umulis D.; Zartman J.; Cabrera-Ríos M.
Article.Abstract: Calcium imaging enables quantitative characterization of calcium dynamics across diverse biological systems. However, measurements derived from fluorescence traces depend on analytical choices, including signal smoothing, event detection, baseline estimation, and metric definition. These analytical steps are often distributed across different software packages and can materially affect the resulting event measurements. Here we present CalciumInsights, an interactive R/Shiny application for post-processing calcium-fluorescence time series previously extracted from regions of interest (ROIs). CalciumInsights provides two complementary analysis workflows. The Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) + Baseline Analysis module supports low-frequency signal reconstruction, peak detection, baseline-dependent event quantification, and assessment of the sensitivity of metrics to alternative baseline definitions. The Wavelet Ridgewalking module provides multiscale event detection and quantification of wavelet-detected transients. Both workflows operate on tabular time-series data and provide interactive visualization and exportable event- and trace-level measurements. Using ROI-derived calcium datasets from Arabidopsis thaliana , zebrafish ( Danio rerio ), and Drosophila melanogaster , we demonstrate the application of a common trace-analysis framework across distinct organisms and imaging contexts. Comparison with published flg22 dose–response data in A. thaliana shows qualitatively consistent response trends, providing an external biological comparison without treating the published data as a ground-truth benchmark. CalciumInsights is available as an open-source online Shiny application that provides an accessible, transparent, and reproducible workflow for visualizing ROI-derived calcium traces, quantifying transient features, and evaluating how baseline and event-detection choices affect their interpretation.
