Article.Title: L-histidine metabolic reprogramming is associated with imipenem-relebactam resistance in carbapenem-resistant hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae
Article.Authors: Li J.; Wang H.; Wang Y.; Lu H.; Geng J.; Hu Y.; Wang H.; Xia F.; Zou M.
Article.Abstract: Although the emergence of imipenem-relebactam (IMR)-resistant carbapenem-resistant hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (CR-hvKP) is known, the mechanisms underlying IMR resistance remain unclear. Here, we elucidated the evolutionary mechanisms underlying IMR resistance. Seven bla KPC-2 -carrying ST11 CR-hvKP strains were subjected to in vitro IMR selection, of which two acquired resistance. In these two resistant strains, the MICs of IMR were dynamically monitored. Galleria mellonella infection model, biofilm formation assays, and growth curve analyses were used for evaluation. Whole-genome sequencing, RT-qPCR, and transcriptome sequencing were performed to analyze the mechanisms. An exogenous L-histidine supplementation experiment was conducted to determine potential reversal of the IMR-resistant phenotype. Two in seven (i.e., KP520 and KP214) strains developed resistance at the 15th (KP520-15) and 20th (KP214-20) passages, respectively, following which, their biofilm-formation capacity and virulence were enhanced. The IMR-resistant strains exhibited changes in rearrangements of insertion sequences surrounding bla KPC-2 and inversion of the core transposon orientation, and significantly increased in the expressions of bla KPC-2 . The differentially expressed genes identified before and after IMR selected were predominantly enriched in metabolism-related pathways, among which L-histidine biosynthesis was the most significantly enriched pathways. Exogenous supplementation with 10 mmol/L L-histidine restored IMR susceptibility in resistant strains and significantly increased the expression of hisG , a key gene involved in L-histidine biosynthesis. Thus, in the two strains that acquired IMR resistance increased bla KPC-2 expression and metabolic changes involving L-histidine biosynthesis were associated with the resistant phenotype. In conclusion, prolonged IMR exposure may lead to the development of resistance in CR-hvKP, with enhanced biofilm formation and pathogenic potential. In CR-hvKP strains that acquired IMR resistance under in vitro selection, this resistance was associated with increased bla KPC-2 expression and transcriptional changes involving L-histidine biosynthesis.

Article.Title: Bio-priming improves salt stress tolerance in Zea mays L. insights from phenotypic and metabolomic analysis
Article.Authors: Shafqat A.; Shahid M.; Akram W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Salinity is a major abiotic stress that severely limits crop productivity worldwide by disrupting plant physiological and metabolic processes. Maize ( Zea mays L.) is considered a moderately salt-tolerant crop; however, high salinity can substantially impair its growth and productivity. This study evaluated the potential of rhizosphere-derived plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) to mitigate salt stress in maize through a bio-priming approach integrated with phenotypic and metabolomic analyses. Soil samples were collected from two maize fields, and 15 bacterial strains were isolated. Based on plant growth-promoting traits and salt tolerance, four promising PGPR strains were selected and evaluated under 250 mM NaCl stress. Bio-priming treatments consisted of UC (untreated control), SU (salt stress only), SB1 (PPB1 + salt stress), SB2 (PPB4 + salt stress), SB3 (PPB8 + salt stress), and SB4 (PPB12 + salt stress). Under salinity stress, PGPR inoculation produced strain-specific improvements in maize growth. Compared with the salinity-stressed treatment (SU), SB3 showed the strongest overall growth-promoting response, significantly increasing shoot and root length by approximately 20% and 45%, shoot and root fresh weight by approximately 95% and 50%, and shoot and root dry weight by approximately 20% and 133%, respectively ( P ≤ 0.05). SB2 also significantly improved shoot and root fresh weight and root dry weight relative to SU. Physiological and biochemical responses were likewise strain dependent. Compared with SU, SB1 significantly enhanced total chlorophyll content, whereas SB1 and SB2 significantly increased carotenoid content. SB2 produced the strongest antioxidant response, significantly enhancing POD, CAT, and APX activities relative to SU ( P ≤ 0.05). For LC–MS-based metabolomic profiling, four treatments were selected: UC, SU, SB2 (SU + PPB4; Bacillus aerius ), and SB3 (SU + PPB8; provisionally identified as a member of the Bacillus cereus group based on 16 S rRNA analysis). Metabolomic profiling revealed treatment-specific changes following PGPR inoculation. Relative to SU, L-citrulline and UDP-N-acetyl-α-D-glucosamine showed approximately 1.54- and 7.70-fold higher abundance, respectively, in SB2, whereas L-methionine showed approximately 5.11-fold higher abundance in SB3. These changes, together with alterations in other plant-related metabolites, indicated metabolic reprogramming associated with improved salinity adaptation. However, because PPB8 was identified only by 16 S rRNA sequencing, genome-based taxonomic confirmation and screening for toxin- and virulence-associated genes are required before considering this strain for agricultural application.

Article.Title: The capability of very high-resolution satellite imagery for plot-level early wheat stem rust disease detection, monitoring, and phenotyping in Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Blasch G.; Gemechu A.; Regasa G.; Alemayehu Y.; Ndour A.; Firpo P.; Potgieter A.; Hodson D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Very high‑resolution satellites (VHRS) have potential for early crop disease detection and enhanced food security. The capability of multispectral SkySat and Pleiades‑Neo imagery for early-stage detection and monitoring was assessed for wheat stem rust (SR) at the plot level. In randomized trials with contrasting fungicide and irrigation treatments, six bread wheat varieties with differing SR susceptibility were monitored using VHRS. 113 multispectral features were evaluated for their association with SR progression and associated yield loss. Several features demonstrated moderate to strong correlations with SR disease levels. Across early stages (healthy, mildly diseased, and moderately diseased), spectral sensitivity was dominated by Blue (B)‑based features, with Red-Blue (R-B) and Green-Blue (G-B) two-band features at mildly and moderately diseased levels, respectively. During late stages (severely diseased and fully diseased), spectral sensitivity was driven by R-based features (e.g., R-B, R-G on both sensors) and by Deep Blue (DB), Red-Edge-DB (RE-DB), and R-DB combinations on Pleiades‑Neo. Early-stage SR detection under moderate disease pressure was possible using ratio (RSI) and normalized difference (NDSI) spectral indices with B-G combinations. SkySat features such as RSI(NIR,B), RSI(R,B), and RSI(G,B) were consistently associated with SR across multiple disease scenarios, trials, and disease metrics. This work delivers the first VHRS-based SR detection at the plot scale and provides a foundation for future investigations into SR monitoring across larger spatial scales.

Article.Title: Leveraging biased FedSDS as a federated learning strategy for research on non-IID multi-disorder studies
Article.Authors: Casadei F.; A. Apellániz P.; Carota L.; Asti G.; Della Porta M.; Parras J.; Giampieri E.; Castellani G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Federated learning is a powerful approach to overcome privacy and data sharing issues, especially in small sample healthcare settings. However, parameter aggregation strategies, such as FedAvg, are prone to fail in case of non-IID data distributions, which often arise in real-world scenarios. In fact, data provided by different institutions can exhibit systematic heterogeneity across cohorts, such as age, genotype, and life expectancy, reflecting institution-specific biases. Federated Synthetic Data Sharing (FedSDS) represents a valuable solution to the problem of non-IID data. It is a federated learning strategy based on locally generating synthetic datasets from real data and sharing them between the federated clients, avoiding the transfer of real sensitive data. FedSDS is applied to a survival prediction task, performed using a DeepSurv model architecture in 3 different healthcare use cases: Myelodysplastic Syndrome, Low Grade Glioma, and Breast Cancer. We demonstrate that this approach outperforms FedAvg and other strategies based on model parameters optimization in non-IID settings. In particular, the possibility to locally bias shared synthetic data allows preserving the local data distribution of each participating client and significantly improving the performances of federated models. This study shows that biased FedSDS is effective in three different healthcare use cases, such as Myelodysplastic Syndromes, Low Grade Glioma, and Breast Cancer. Our findings suggest that FedSDS may have potential relevance for healthcare applications, as it can support the selection and biasing of samples for dataset augmentation and improve the performance of federated models in non-IID multi-disorder settings. The potential use of this approach for clinical trial cohort selection, however, would require further investigation and dedicated validation.

Article.Title: Short-term exposure to nominal PFBS concentrations is associated with reduced isotopic food uptake in benthic foraminifera
Article.Authors: Lintner M.; Polovodova Asteman I.; Hylland K.; Sturve J.; Wanek W.; Goleń J.; Tyszka J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pollution caused by per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) is an urgent environmental issue, yet their effects on microbial eukaryotes remain poorly understood. We investigated the association between short-term exposure to nominal concentrations of perfluorobutane sulfonic acid (PFBS), a short-chain PFAS, and isotopic food uptake by five benthic foraminiferal taxa: Bulimina marginata , Cassidulina laevigata , Eubuliminella sp., Globobulimina turgida and Nonionella sp. T1. Foraminifera were exposed for three days and supplied with ¹³C- and ¹⁵N-labelled lyophilized diatoms. Only B. marginata was exposed to the full nominal concentration gradient (0, 0.1, 1, 10 and 100 µg L⁻¹); the remaining taxa were tested at 0 and 100 µg L⁻¹. Across taxa, nominal PFBS treatment was associated with lower pC and pN uptake, while species × treatment interactions were not significant. In B. marginata , both pC and pN uptake differed among concentrations and were significantly lower than the control at 1, 10 and 100 µg L⁻¹ after Tukey adjustment, but not at 0.1 µg L⁻¹. The response was non-monotonic, with partial recovery at 100 µg L⁻¹ relative to 1–10 µg L⁻¹. These results provide initial evidence that short-term exposure to PFBS-containing treatments is associated with reduced isotopic food uptake in benthic foraminifera. Because concentrations were not analytically verified, no methanol-free vehicle control was included, and replication was limited, these results should be interpreted as an acute laboratory hazard-screening study rather than evidence for a biological threshold or species-specific sensitivity.

Article.Title: Nonlinear bit-level image encryption method integrating DCGAN-derived dual-branch features and chaotic regulation
Article.Authors: Lu Y.; Song J.; Fu X.; Huang X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To address the core bottlenecks of insufficient nonlinear adaptive capability of chaotic systems and the difficulty in balancing security and computational efficiency in bit-level transformation for existing image encryption methods, this paper proposes a nonlinear bit-level image encryption scheme combining a dual-branch feature regulation mechanism based on Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks (DCGAN) and an adaptive chaotic system. First, a key-controlled dual-branch DCGAN fusion module is constructed to generate cipher keys tightly correlated with plaintext content adaptively. Second, an adaptive Chen chaotic system modulated by plaintext features is designed; comprehensive dynamical analysis verifies its outstanding nonlinearity and randomness. Third, a low-complexity nonlinear bit-level transformation is elaborated to simultaneously achieve powerful confusion-diffusion capability and low computation cost. Experimental results demonstrate that the key space of the proposed method reaches 2 256 , and its security performance outperforms mainstream comparative algorithms. Meanwhile, the computational efficiency is improved by 29.7% compared with traditional DNA-based bit-level schemes, which provides a new perspective for the collaborative encryption of nonlinear dynamics and deep learning.

Article.Title: Analysis of the proteomic profiles in serum of mice treated with RadioDefender, a novel radiation medical countermeasure
Article.Authors: Carpenter A.; Packer B.; Li X.; Kandhavelu J.; Li Y.; Petrus S.; Fatanmi O.; Wise S.; Zhou J.; Cheema A.; Singh V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Exposure to high doses of ionizing radiation arising from nuclear attacks or radiological emergencies can result in the development of acute radiation syndrome (ARS). Current treatments for ARS are limited to radiomitigators that help restore immune cell and platelet production along with bone marrow function. However, there are no radioprotectors available for use as a prophylaxis for military and first responders, although many are under investigation. RadioDefender is a candidate radioprotective agent derived from amifostine, a limited-use drug with radioprotective properties. Previous investigations in pre-treated human hematopoietic stem cells exposed to γ-radiation and mouse survival studies have shown that this candidate drug improves cell viability, supporting its potential for further development as a radioprotector. In this study, mice were treated with a single dose of either RadioDefender (250, 500, 600, or 700 mg/kg) or vehicle 24 hours prior to 9.2 Gy total-body γ-irradiation. Blood was collected at 30 days post-irradiation, and serum was isolated for proteomic analysis. As part of a larger investigation into the safety of RadioDefender, this study was performed to assess the efficacy of selected doses in combination with radiation exposure. Serum proteomic profiles of vehicle- and RadioDefender-treated animals were compared to healthy controls as an exploratory investigation of proteomic differences among animals surviving to 30 days post-irradiation. At 30 days post-irradiation, minimal differences in serum proteomic abundance were observed between any of the groups, suggesting that both irradiation- and drug-induced changes may have subsided by this time point.

Article.Title: Phenotypic and multiplex PCR-defined antimicrobial resistance in Ukrainian soldiers’ war-wound microbiota
Article.Authors: Sibińska E.; Avramenko V.; Pryshchepa O.; Bespalko O.; Złoch M.; Babenko Y.; Yaremchuk S.; Rudnicka J.; Furtat I.; Vakuliuk P.; Pomastowski P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigates antimicrobial resistance in combat-related wound infections from the ongoing armed conflict in Ukraine using combined phenotypic and molecular approaches. Gram-negative pathogens, predominantly ESKAPE organisms, exhibited high resistance rates, including 43% resistance to imipenem and frequent multidrug resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii , Klebsiella pneumoniae , and Pseudomonas aeruginosa . Molecular analysis revealed β-lactamase and carbapenemase genes in 22/37 isolates, with frequent co-carriage of multiple determinants such as blaCTX-M , blaSHV , blaTEM , blaKPC , blaNDM , and blaOXA-48 . While blaCTX-M strongly correlated with cephalosporin resistance, weaker genotype–phenotype concordance was observed for blaTEM and blaSHV , indicating the contribution of additional resistance mechanisms. Discrepancies between multiplex PCR and phenotypic susceptibility were particularly evident in P. aeruginosa . Additional WGS analyses of selected isolates provided a broader characterization of the resistome and identified resistance determinants not covered by the targeted PCR panel, helping to clarify several genotype–phenotype discrepancies. Less susceptible subpopulations observed for Gram-negative isolates and vanC-mediated intrinsic resistance in Enterococcus gallinarum further emphasized diagnostic complexity. Overall, the findings indicate a high burden and substantial diversity of antimicrobial resistance among the analyzed combat-related wound isolates. These results support the use of integrated diagnostic strategies combining rapid molecular detection with MIC-based phenotypic testing, with broader genomic analyses applied where clinically or epidemiologically justified, to support targeted therapy and antimicrobial stewardship.

Article.Title: Rotational behaviour and morphological associations of the CT-based distal ulnar centering and eccentricity (DUCE) method in cadaveric specimens
Article.Authors: El Barbari J.; Kordon F.; Kunze H.; Armbruster J.; Grützner P.; Vetter S.; Schnetzke M.; Swartman B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Non-invasive assessment of distal radioulnar joint (DRUJ) stability remains challenging because CT-based measurements, such as the radioulnar ratio (RR), depend on forearm rotation and notch anatomy. The CT-based Distal Ulnar Centering and Eccentricity (DUCE) method describes DRUJ articulation relative to individual notch geometry, separating rotational translation into direction and magnitude. Thirty cadaveric upper limbs underwent cone-beam CT in pronation and supination, 11 also in neutral rotation. Centering (ulnar head centre to a notch-derived reference axis) and Eccentricity (to the deepest notch point) were compared with RR. RR varied with rotation (28.7 ± 8.5% vs. 70.8 ± 13.6%; P < 0.001) and with notch morphology (R 2 up to 0.31); no such association was detected for DUCE. Signed Centering reversed systematically (+ 3.11 vs. − 3.10 mm; P < 0.001), while its magnitude remained equivalent. Averaged across both end positions, Centering was equivalent to zero (exploratory ± 0.6 mm equivalence margin; TOST P < 0.001), placing the notch-derived axis at the centre of the rotational arc at group level, though not in individual limbs. Eccentricity did not differ with rotation. Interrater reliability was good to excellent. DUCE provides an anatomically referenced description of rotational DRUJ behaviour. Clinical studies must show whether it improves assessment of pathological instability.

Article.Title: Decentralized plug-and-play control of grid-forming converters for resilient and scalable AC microgrids: a passivity-based unified architecture
Article.Authors: Chaturvedi A.; Nishad D.; Bharti K.; Tiwari R.; Mossie M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In low-inertia AC microgrids, voltage formation, frequency support, power sharing, and disturbance rejection are performed by grid-forming (GFM) converters. Current systems often design these functions individually for a fixed, cooperatively tuned converter population. Adding, removing, or losing a unit requires retuning, which may jeopardize stability. We present a generic decentralized plug-and-play (PnP) design for all grid-forming (GFM) converters by including the same kernel, i.e., droop primary regulation, adaptive virtual impedance, sparse consensus-based secondary restoration, and trust-weighted resilient coordination, under a local passivity-based admission test. Under explicitly stated assumptions (quasi-stationary lossy lines, a feasible equilibrium, a connected electrical network and a bounded admission rate), we prove that a converter with normalized passivity index exceeding a strictly positive margin can be admitted or removed without neighbor retuning, that stability is preserved during the finite-time admission ramp and not only at its end points, and that the conductive (R/X) coupling of real feeders enters the test as a bounded, locally computable defect. The same certificate bounds the perturbation that false-data-injection (FDI) attacks can cause through the trust-weighted consensus, with an explicit relation between attack magnitude, residual threshold, trust weight, and perturbation. Validation is software-only: a detailed averaged three-converter Simulink model, a small-signal model with the exact lossy Jacobian for $$\:N\:=\:2-128$$ converters, several electrical and communication graphs, heterogeneous ratings and lines, sequential and simultaneous multi-unit events, a documented Monte-Carlo campaign and a 15-scenario FDI campaign. In the detailed model, admitting a converter causes a peak PCC voltage deviation of 1.79% (settling in 58 ms), and the harmonic kernel (current feed-forward plus selective resonant feedback of the PCC voltage) lowers PCC voltage THD from 9.19% to 3.33%, within the 5% limit. The computed minimum passivity index during admission is 0.723 over $$\:N\:=\:2-8$$ and remains between 0.723 and 0.885 up to $$\:N\:=\:128$$ ; the Monte-Carlo violation probability is 0.002 for design tolerances ( $$\:M\:=\:1000$$ ). Real-time hardware-in-the-loop testing was not performed and is identified as future work.

Article.Title: SWT-ResNet-based internal material identification for impacted multilayered cylindrical structures with clearance
Article.Authors: Liao J.; Li T.; Liang J.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate identification of materials enclosed within multilayer cylindrical structures is challenging without structural disassembly, particularly when assembly clearances induce contact and impact nonlinearities and result in nonstationary vibration responses. To address this problem, a material identification framework integrating the synchrosqueezing wavelet transform and a residual neural network (SWT–ResNet) is proposed. First, vibration responses are measured externally through impact tests, and SWT is employed to generate highly concentrated time–frequency representations through frequency reassignment. A lightweight ResNet is then used to automatically extract multilevel time–frequency features and classify the internal materials. Four materials, namely MJ, AZ31B magnesium alloy, epoxy resin, and polytetrafluoroethylene, are investigated under four impact levels of 5, 10, 15, and 20 g. Three independent repeated tests are performed for each condition, producing 48 original experimental records. To prevent information leakage caused by overlapping sliding windows, the data are partitioned at the original-record level before sample segmentation. The proposed SWT–ResNet achieves an accuracy, macro-averaged precision, macro-averaged recall, and macro-averaged F1-score of 97.50%, 97.56%, 97.50%, and 97.50%, respectively, on the independent test set. Original-record-level three-fold cross-validation yields an accuracy of 96.88% ± 0.63%, demonstrating the stability of the proposed framework. Ablation experiments show that SWT–ResNet outperforms CWT–ResNet, STFT–ResNet, Raw-CNN, SWT–CNN, SWT–SVM, SWT–RF, and PCA–k-means, confirming the contributions of both the highly concentrated SWT representation and residual feature learning. Under Gaussian white-noise conditions of 20, 10, and 0 dB, the corresponding accuracies are 98.5%, 94.4%, and 69.3%, respectively, indicating a certain degree of noise robustness. These results demonstrate that SWT–ResNet can effectively identify internal materials in multilayer cylindrical structures with assembly clearances and provides a feasible nondestructive approach for identifying internal media in complex enclosed structures.

Article.Title: Shared genetic architecture between adhesive capsulitis and type 2 diabetes: a phenotype-specific cross-trait analysis
Article.Authors: Dong J.; Yang M.; Zhang Y.; Wang X.; Ning R.; Zhang J.; Liu T.; Xiao J.; Zuo J.
Article.Abstract: Adhesive capsulitis (AC) is over-represented in people with diabetes, but whether AC and type 2 diabetes (T2D) share inherited susceptibility remains uncertain. We analysed GWAS summary statistics for phenotype-specific FinnGen R12 M13_ADHCAPSULITIS (ICD-10 M75.0; 7372 cases and 357,549 controls), FinnGen T2D, and Pan-UK Biobank T2D using cross-trait LD score regression, MiXeR, and the official pleioFDR toolbox. AC was positively genetically correlated with T2D (Pan-UK Biobank: rg = 0.334, SE = 0.049, P = 1.4 × 10⁻¹¹; FinnGen: rg = 0.189, SE = 0.042, P = 7.0 × 10⁻⁶). Five bivariate MiXeR fits were compatible with partial overlap, but variation in the shared component and disagreement between the Akaike information criterion (AIC) and the Bayesian information criterion (BIC) for the minimum-overlap comparison precluded a precise quantitative overlap claim. Conditional and conjunctional FDR analyses statistically prioritised AC-associated and jointly associated regions, respectively, without establishing shared mechanisms, causal variants, or effector genes. An exploratory cross-resource contrast of broad Pan-UK Biobank M75 with phenotype-specific FinnGen M75.0 produced similar genome-wide correlations but different polygenicity and locus-level results; because the resource, cohort, ascertainment, GWAS construction, case count, and sample-overlap structure changed simultaneously, these differences cannot be attributed to phenotype breadth alone. These results support consistent population-level genetic sharing, not causality or individual-level clinical utility; fine-mapping, colocalisation, and functional validation remain required.

Article.Title: Hybrid semantic optimization with hierarchical spatial-wavelet synergy for zero-shot anomaly detection
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Wu C.; Lu J.; Liu X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Zero-shot anomaly detection offers a promising solution for privacy-constrained scenarios. However, the preference of the pre-trained visual encoder for global semantic consistency, together with globally aware prompts, tends to favor object-centric holistic representations, potentially making high- and low-frequency cues that have limited influence on object-level semantics but are important for anomaly detection less adequately represented. In this paper, we propose H2HCLIP, which integrates hybrid semantic optimization with hierarchical spatial-wavelet synergy to enhance frequency-domain visual modeling while introducing semantic guidance. For visual enhancement, we develop the frequency-aware refinement attention at intermediate encoder layers, refining deep-frequency patterns via Fourier transformation, while applying non-saliency completion and threshold-based enhancement to accentuate key representations. At the output stage, spatial-wavelet collaborative inference is conducted, where multiple wavelet transformations intricately merge local high-frequency subtleties with global low-frequency structures. To enrich semantic representations, we introduce image-level, sentiment-level, and region-level prompts to refine normal-abnormal semantic boundaries. We leverage a feature-guided hybrid fusion mechanism and an intra-inter contrastive loss to facilitate the interaction of semantic information from local to global, promoting the joint optimization of classification and segmentation. Extensive experiments on 11 datasets demonstrate that H2HCLIP achieves competitive performance compared with many existing methods, with improvements observed across several evaluation metrics.

Article.Title: Persistent differentiation in rural ecological resilience across functional village types in the Yangtze River Delta
Article.Authors: Zhang Z.; Sun X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Understanding ecological differences among functional village types can inform rural revitalization. We analysed 4,126 village units in the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) at five benchmark years from 2003 to 2023, using an ecological resilience index (ERI) integrating resistance, adaptability and recovery. Five overlapping functional types were examined through city-adjusted comparisons, spatially validated extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) models and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). In 2023, mean ERI was highest for ecological livability (EL; 0.371), followed by rural civilization (RC; 0.366), industrial prosperity (IP; 0.330), effective governance (EG; 0.312) and wealthy life (WL; 0.304). WL villages showed the largest 2003–2023 increase in mean ERI (15.360 × 10⁻³). Functional memberships explained 10.887% of variation remaining after city and year adjustment. Seven of ten city-adjusted pairwise contrasts were significant in all five years after Holm correction. Population and impervious cover were the leading predictive features for 2023 levels, while shortwave radiation, climatic water deficit and nighttime lights were prominent for trends. Spatial out-of-fold coefficients of determination (R²) ranged from 0.585 to 0.788 for levels and from 0.231 to 0.484 for trends. These findings reveal persistent functional differences alongside contrasting temporal trajectories. Integrating functional classification with assessments of resilience levels and changes provides a village-level framework for differentiated ecological assessment and long-term monitoring in rural revitalization.

Article.Title: High salt induces early metabolic and extracellular matrix remodeling in Dahl salt-sensitive rats that persists despite subdepressor ACE inhibition
Article.Authors: Schuller M.; Kiessling M.; Gindlhuber J.; Klötzer K.; Voglhuber J.; Pollheimer M.; Schabhüttl C.; Kolb D.; Hingerl K.; Habisch H.; Madl T.; Ljubojevic-Holzer S.; Eller K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Excess salt is a major contributor to hypertension and hypertensive kidney injury, yet the early molecular events linking salt exposure to kidney damage remain incompletely understood. The Dahl salt-sensitive rat is a well-established model of salt-induced hypertension, but early metabolic and transcriptional remodeling in the kidney has not been fully characterized. We investigated early kidney alterations in 35 Dahl salt-sensitive rats fed a high-sodium (HSD) or low-sodium diet (LSD). A subgroup of HSD-fed rats received the ACE inhibitor imidapril at a subdepressor dose (1 mg/kg/day) to examine blood pressure-independent effects. Kidney tissue from 12-week-old animals was analyzed using histology, electron microscopy, transcriptomics, metabolomics, and angiotensin peptide profiling. HSD-fed rats developed hypertension by week 9 and showed kidney remodeling by week 12, including metabolic and transcriptional alterations suggestive of disrupted tricarboxylic acid cycle activity and impaired oxidative phosphorylation in the absence of overt fibrosis. Intra-kidney angiotensin I, II, and angiotensin 1–7 levels were reduced under HSD. Subdepressor ACE inhibition did not significantly alter blood pressure, kidney injury, angiotensin peptide levels, or the transcriptional and metabolic alterations observed in HSD-fed animals. Article.Title: Prevalence of anaemia and Associated Factors among pregnant women attending antenatal care in a rural district of Northern Ghana: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Saeed N.; Abdul-Rahaman A.; Fusheini A.; Dawuda L.; Mensah R.; Achageba A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Anaemia in pregnancy contributes to maternal and perinatal morbidity in sub-Saharan Africa, but facility-level evidence from the Sawla-Tuna-Kalba district of the Savannah Region of Ghana is lacking. We conducted a facility-based cross-sectional study of 410 pregnant women attending antenatal care (ANC) at three health facilities, recruited through multistage simple random sampling. Data were collected through interviews. Haemoglobin concentration was determined with the use of venous blood specimens in an automated hematology analyzer, and anaemia was defined using World Health Organization (WHO) trimester-specific thresholds.Chi-square tests and binary logistic regression were used (two-sided p < 0.05). The prevalence of anaemia was 52.2% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 47.2–57.1) among women attending the three facilities. In the multivariable model, women with junior high/middle-level education had significantly lower odds of anaemia than women with no formal education (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 0.41, 95% CI: 0.21–0.80), and women who initiated ANC in the second trimester had more than twice the odds of anaemia compared with the first trimester (aOR = 2.11, 95% CI: 1.11–4.01). Dietary diversity and the other variables were not significantly associated with anaemia. Anaemia was common in this facility-based sample, but the representativeness of the wider population could not be established. These cross-sectional associations do not establish causation, and the findings support early ANC initiation and anaemia prevention counselling for all pregnant women.

Article.Title: Measurement properties of subscales in the work environment impact questionnaire (WEIQ)
Article.Authors: Yngve M.; Ekbladh E.; Melin J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Work ability arises from interactions between individuals, work tasks, and the work environment. Valid instruments for assessing self-perceived work ability are essential to reduce sick leave and optimize productivity. The Work Environment Impact Questionnaire (WEIQ) assesses key workplace factors across four subscales: Physical and Organizational Prerequisites, Work Tasks, Social Relations, and Motivational Aspects. The purpose of this study was to assess the measurement properties of the WEIQ subscales. Rasch analysis was conducted on data from 288 respondents representing three work settings: assisted living, vocational rehabilitation, and a research institute. All subscales showed good targeting and no disordered thresholds but exhibited issues with item fit, local dependency (LD), and/or differential item functioning (DIF). In Work Tasks , LD was identified in four item pairs; after removing one item and creating testlets, the refined scale showed no misfit, DIF, or LD and supported unidimensionality. In Motivational Aspects , three misfitting items and three LD pairs were identified; one item was removed and two testlets were created, resulting in acceptable model fit. Physical and Organizational Prerequisites showed one misfitting item, LD in two item pairs, and DIF in two items; testlets, including one split by workplace, resolved these issues. In Social Relations , misfit, DIF, and LD were identified; two items were removed, testlets were formed, and one DIF item was retained. Across refined subscales, person separation indices ranged from 0.63 to 0.74. The final WEIQ comprised 29 items. Through item removal, testlet formation, and item splitting, acceptable measurement properties and unidimensionality were achieved, supporting the use of common scales across workplaces while allowing for setting-specific differences.

Article.Title: Scan-sampling interval shapes the reliability of immersion-activity estimates in captive penguins
Article.Authors: Yamamoto T.; Kakizaki T.; Takashima Y.; Tsunesumi H.; Yoda K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Instantaneous scan sampling is widely used across behavioural observation settings, but sampling intervals are often chosen for practical reasons despite their influence on estimation accuracy. We evaluated how sampling interval affects estimates of immersion activity in captive Magellanic penguins ( Spheniscus magellanicus ) and whether errors differ between group- and individual-level analyses. Using biologging-derived immersion records, we reconstructed immersion-state sequences and simulated scan sampling at intervals of 30 s and 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 30 min, accounting for scan-start phase. Estimation error increased nonlinearly with sampling interval but was smaller and less variable at the group level. Median group-level error remained below 0.7% at 5-min intervals and reached 3.6% at 30 min. In contrast, individual-level error increased sharply beyond 4–5 min and reached 8.5% at 30 min. Sampling interval dominated estimation error, with smaller detectable seasonal effects. Frequent land–water transitions further amplified errors at longer intervals. These results indicate that group-level aggregation buffers error but may also conceal individual-level heterogeneity. For group-level summaries, intervals up to 5 min may provide stable estimates, whereas individual-level monitoring requires finer resolution, approximately 2–3 min. More broadly, our findings highlight that sampling interval, scan phase, state switching, and aggregation level jointly determine the reliability of scan-sampling estimates.

Article.Title: Evidence drift analytics for long-term malware investigations: A causal and survival-theoretic framework for forensic validity optimizations
Article.Authors: Patidar G.; Beg R.; Sahu A.; Joshi S.; Nigam N.; Pateriya R.; Tomar D.; Solanki S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Advanced malware investigations frequently extend over prolonged periods, during which operating-system updates, software patches, logging-framework modifications, benign software evolution, and adversarial adaptations continuously alter the statistical characteristics of digital forensic artifacts. These temporal changes introduce evidence drift that affects registry traces, process lineage structures, executable metadata, memory layouts, network flows, and system-call distributions, thereby reducing the reliability and long-term validity of forensic evidence. Although existing concept-drift approaches improve predictive performance under evolving data distributions, they rarely assess whether forensic artifacts remain evidentially valid, reproducible, and operationally reliable throughout extended investigations. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a five-stage Evidence Drift Analytics (EDA) framework for long-term forensic-validity optimization in evolving malware environments. The framework integrates the Temporal Forensic Evidence Divergence Field (TFEDF) for multi-resolution drift estimation, the Causal Artifact Lineage Graph Transformer (CALGT) for SCM-guided estimation of attribution confidence under explicit intervention assumptions, the Forensic Integrity Preservation Index using Bayesian Evidence Survival Modeling (FIPI-BESM) for evidentiary survivability forecasting, the Drift-Aware Counterfactual Re-Anchoring Engine (DACRE) for learning drift-invariant representations while preserving malicious behavioural semantics, and the Forensic Validity Optimization Network (FVON) for reinforcement-learning–based forensic decision optimization. The proposed framework was evaluated using five publicly available cybersecurity datasets, including CICIDS2017, EMBER, LANL authentication logs, Android API streams, and IoT telemetry datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves 94.8% drift sensitivity with a 4.2% false-positive rate, attains 91.7% accuracy for the operational drift-source attribution task under the stated SCM intervention assumptions, and maintains a survival stability index of 0.92 during long-term evidentiary forecasting. Furthermore, the proposed drift-aware representation learning reduces embedding variance to 0.062 while preserving 96.1% reconstruction fidelity across temporal windows. The integrated framework also achieves a cumulative forensic validity score of 0.95 and a reproducibility index of 0.94, indicating improved cross-temporal consistency, evidentiary robustness, and operational reliability under evolving cybersecurity environments. Overall, the proposed Evidence Drift Analytics framework provides a unified evidence-centric methodology for modelling temporal evidence drift, preserving forensic validity, and supporting reliable long-term malware investigations through the integration of temporal drift analysis, SCM-guided causal reasoning, Bayesian evidence survival modelling, drift-invariant representation learning, and reinforcement-learning–based forensic optimization. These performance results were obtained under the offline experimental settings evaluated in this study using temporally segmented benchmark datasets and may vary under real-time, high-throughput operational environments. The CALGT outputs represent estimated attribution confidence obtained under assumptions of temporal ordering, reliable metadata observability, and correctly identified operating-system update pathways; they should not be interpreted as definitive causal discovery or experimental proof of causality. .

Article.Title: Enlarged brain perivascular spaces in chronic schizophrenia but not in first-episode psychosis: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Morozova A.; Zach P.; Geier K.; Brabec M.; Škoch A.; Piyioti G.; Söderberg A.; Pasik N.; Kehail Y.; Bendová M.; Zaytseva Y.; Španiel F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Enlarged perivascular spaces (EPVS) are MRI-visible markers associated with glymphatic system function and brain waste clearance, and are thought to reflect neurovascular, neuroinflammatory, and age-related changes. While schizophrenia is associated with neuroinflammation and accelerated brain aging, little is known about metabolic brain waste clearance in the condition. Moreover, whether EPVS burden differs across stages of disease is unclear. This study aimed to compare EPVS in the centrum semiovale (CSO) and basal ganglia (BG) among individuals with schizophrenia, first-episode psychosis (FEP), and healthy controls, with a total of 174 subjects included. EPVS were quantified using high-resolution 3T MRI and a standardized rating scale, with assessments conducted by three independent raters. Ordinal logistic regression showed higher odds of being in a higher CSO-EPVS category in chronic schizophrenia versus healthy controls (OR 2.31, 95% CI 1.15–4.62, p = 0.02), as well as higher total EPVS burden (OR 2.02, 95% CI 1.04–3.93, p = 0.04), while no significant group differences were observed for BG-EPVS or between FEP and healthy controls. These findings suggest regional and group-specific differences in EPVS burden, with greater burden in chronic schizophrenia primarily reflected by CSO-EPVS rather than BG-EPVS. This study emphasizes the potential role of neurovascular and neuroinflammatory processes in schizophrenia, aligning with evidence of accelerated brain aging in the disorder.

Article.Title: Dynamic weather window-based multi-objective path planning for low-altitude logistics
Article.Authors: Xie Y.; Zhong J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper addresses the path planning problem of low-altitude logistics UAVs in dynamic weather environments by proposing a conceptual framework termed the "dynamic weather window". On this basis, a multi-objective optimization model incorporating delivery timeliness, operational energy consumption, and weather risk exposure is constructed, and a solution algorithm based on NSGA-III and rolling horizon re-planning is designed. Through simulation experiments, the proposed method improves the task completion rate from 19–78% achieved by baseline methods to 98% under severe weather scenarios, reduces the constraint violation rate from 22%-81% to 2%, and achieves a Hypervolume 38% higher than the optimal baseline. The research demonstrates that elevating weather from a "static constraint" to a "dynamic spatiotemporal window" can significantly enhance the adaptability of path planning to time-varying weather conditions; the rolling horizon re-planning mechanism strikes a balance between prediction and reaction, serving as an effective engineering approach to weather uncertainty; and the multi-objective Pareto front provides flexible safety-efficiency trade-off space for operational decision-making. The theoretical contributions of this paper lie in extending the theoretical boundary of the vehicle routing problem, establishing a coupled weather-flight performance relationship model, and providing a methodological paradigm that integrates multi-objective optimization with rolling horizon control.

Article.Title: Heightened gaze responsiveness and mutual gaze instability at close distances characterize dyadic coordination in a marmoset model of autism
Article.Authors: Nakamura M.; Sato T.; Kurotani T.; Sakai K.; Hadjiev A.; Sasai S.; Mimura K.; Kawai N.; Shimmura T.; Ichinohe N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is associated with differences in social interaction, including alterations in gaze behavior and interpersonal distance. Although most assessments of ASD remain individual-centric, emerging human studies indicate that social difficulties may arise from atypical dyadic coordination rather than from reduced social interest alone. We examined dyadic coordination in a non-human primate model of ASD, focusing on gaze and inter-individual distance during minimally constrained first encounters between prenatal valproic acid-exposed marmosets (VPA) and unexposed conspecifics (UE). Markerless pose estimation quantified frame-by-frame gaze direction and spacing, comparing VPA–UE with UE–UE dyads. VPA–UE pairs exhibited a higher proportion of mutual-gaze events than UE–UE pairs. VPA individuals showed more rapid looks in response to the partner’s gaze, yet exhibited a lower proportion of one-sided looking events. VPA–UE dyads maintained shorter inter-individual distances than UE–UE dyads, and closer spacing was associated with decreased stability of mutual gaze. These findings reveal a dyadic coordination pattern in VPA–UE pairs, with rapid responsiveness coupled with a distance-dependent reduction in time spent in mutual gaze, paralleling features reported in human ASD. Our dyad-centric, markerless framework yields ecologically grounded readouts and potential intervention targets that leverage intact social responsiveness while accommodating altered spatial coordination.

Article.Title: Clinical outcomes and predictors of poor prognosis among children with probable and confirmed bacterial meningitis in Northwest Ethiopia: a prospective multicenter cohort study
Article.Authors: Sisay T.; Mihrete K.; Hunie E.; Temeche A.; Fentie A.; Tenagne Y.; Berhan A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pediatric bacterial meningitis remains a major cause of mortality and neurological disability in low-resource settings despite improvements in vaccination. The majority of studies conducted in Ethiopia previously have been retrospective and single-center studies with little information about the prognosis of the disease. This prospective multicenter cohort study evaluated clinical outcomes and identified independent predictors of poor prognosis among children with bacterial meningitis. A prospective multicenter cohort study was conducted from June 3, 2024, to May 25, 2025, at Felege Hiwot Comprehensive Specialized Hospital and Tibebe Ghion Specialized Teaching Hospital. A total of 342 study participants aged 0–14 years with probable or confirmed bacterial meningitis were enrolled and prospectively followed from admission to discharge or death. Patients with probable bacterial meningitis had clinical presentation that was compatible with the disease together with either leukocytosis in the CSF (> 100 cells/mm³ or 10–100 cells/mm³ in conjunction with increased protein concentration (> 100 mg/dL) or decreased glucose (< 40 mg/dL). Poor outcome was categorized as mortality, neurological complications on discharge, or prolonged hospital stay (> 14 days). Poor outcomes occurred in 28.4% of patients (n = 97). Independent predictors included delayed hospital admission (AOR = 3.1, 95% CI: 1.9–5.2), coma at presentation (AOR = 4.6, 95% CI: 2.6–8.1), malnutrition (AOR = 2.8, 95% CI: 1.5–4.9), and positive CSF culture (AOR = 2.5, 95% CI: 1.1–5.8). Nearly one-third of children experienced poor discharge outcomes. Late presentation, severe neurological impairment, malnutrition, and positive bacterial culture results were strongly associated with poor outcome. Improved recognition, referral pathways, nutritional support, and diagnostic techniques could greatly decrease morbidity and mortality due to childhood meningitis in developing countries.

Article.Title: Nanomito enables amplification-free full-length analysis of mitochondrial DNA variants and deletions
Article.Authors: Desquiret-Dumas V.; Duverger S.; Amati-Bonneau P.; Dieu X.; Mirebeau-Prunier D.; Reynier P.; Ferré M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate analysis of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) requires reliable quantification of heteroplasmy and robust detection of large-scale deletions. However, routine PCR-based short-read workflows can introduce amplification bias and have limited structural resolution. Here, we developed Nanomito, an amplification-free long-read workflow for full-length sequencing of native mtDNA using Oxford Nanopore Technologies, and compared it with the routine long-range PCR-based Illumina approach in 15 retrospectively selected clinical samples previously characterized in mitochondrial diagnostics. The long-read workflow detected all clinically confirmed causal point variants and identified one low-level m.3243 A > G variant, present at 3.8% heteroplasmy by digital PCR, that was detected only among quality-filtered short-read calls. Relative to digital PCR, long-read heteroplasmy estimates showed a more stable quantitative relationship than the PCR-based short-read workflow. In deletion-positive samples, long-read sequencing confirmed the major deletions detected by routine testing with closely matching breakpoint coordinates and resolved a complex deletion spectrum in one sample. These findings support amplification-free full-length nanopore sequencing as a promising framework for integrated mtDNA variant and deletion analysis.

Article.Title: Effects of flood-induced transverse bed degradation on local scour around adjacent bridge piers using three-dimensional CFD modeling
Article.Authors: Fallahi H.; Kardan N.; Dini M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Local scour around bridge piers can be strongly affected by flood-induced changes in channel-bed morphology, yet most existing studies assume an initially horizontal bed. This study investigates local scour around two side-by-side cylindrical piers ( $$D=0.04\hspace{0.17em}m, S=3D$$ ) subjected to a pre-existing localized transverse degradation flank using a three-dimensional FLOW-3D morphodynamic framework. The selected numerical configuration was evaluated against laboratory measurements of single-pier scour on a horizontal bed and reproduced the measured maximum scour depth within approximately 2%. Controlled parametric simulations were then conducted for transverse bed slopes of $$15^\circ , 30^\circ $$ and $$45^\circ $$ , flow depths of 0.30–0.60 m, approach velocities of $$1.5-2.5 m{s}^{-1}$$ , and different sediment conditions. At $$U=2.0\hspace{0.17em}m\hspace{0.17em}{s}^{-1}$$ , and $$H=0.45\hspace{0.17em}m$$ , the maximum quasi-equilibrium scour depth increased from 0.058 m for the flat-bed reference to 0.0982, 0.1065 and 0.2377 m for slopes of $$15^\circ , 30^\circ $$ and $$45^\circ $$ , respectively, corresponding to a maximum amplification ratio of 4.10. Over the same slope range, the scour-localization index increased from 1.08 to 2.84, indicating a transition from relatively distributed erosion to strongly concentrated scour at the trough-side monitoring location (G3). Once this critical zone developed under the steeper degraded-bed configurations, G3 remained the location of maximum scour across the investigated flow-depth and sediment-sensitivity series. On the flat-bed reference, increasing the approach velocity from 1.5 to $$2.5\hspace{0.17em}m\hspace{0.17em}{s}^{-1}$$ increased the maximum scour depth at all investigated flow depths, while the free-surface regime at $$H=0.45\hspace{0.17em}m$$ changed from subcritical to supercritical under live-bed conditions. The $$45^\circ $$ case is interpreted as an extreme transient morphology rather than a typical equilibrium slope, and the associated absolute scour depth is reported for the selected numerical configuration rather than as a mesh-verified design value. Supplementary reduced-order hydrodynamic diagnostics were consistent with increases and spatial concentration in near-bed forcing, sediment mobility, modelled turbulent shear and rotational activity, and are treated only as exploratory indicators. Overall, transverse bed morphology primarily controls where scour becomes concentrated, whereas hydraulic and sediment conditions predominantly control how strongly the critical zone responds. These findings highlight the need to account for post-flood transverse bed morphology in bridge-scour assessment.

Article.Title: Association between sample entropy and cardiorespiratory events in preterm infants routinely immunized in the hospital
Article.Authors: Kaempfen S.; Sanchez C.; Delgado-Eckert E.; Schulzke S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Timely vaccination of preterm infants < 32 weeks gestation is essential for protection against vaccine-preventable diseases. Vaccination may temporarily challenge autonomic regulation and trigger cardiorespiratory events (CRE), sometimes requiring interventions such as tactile stimulation or respiratory support. Concerns about post-vaccination CRE may lead to delayed vaccination. Objective markers identifying infants at risk for post-vaccination CRE are lacking. We therefore assessed whether sample entropy (SampEn) of heart rate time series, a-non-linear measure of heart rate variability, is associated with post-vaccination CRE and related interventions. In this prospective observational single-centre study, conducted from 2018 to 2022, we recorded heart rate and oxygen saturation using standard monitoring at vaccination timepoints. SampEn was calculated from 90-minute ECG recordings. Of 188 enrolled infants, 103 (56%) underwent SampEn analysis at first vaccination during their primary hospital stay. Mean gestational age was 27.3 weeks (range: 23.3 to 31.3 weeks). We found that CRE increased after vaccination, but SampEn was not associated with occurrence of CRE. Lower SampEn and lower gestational age were independently associated with the need for clinical intervention following vaccination. SampEn may help identify infants requiring clinical intervention after vaccination, but its lack of association with CRE limits broader clinical utility.

Article.Title: Lightweight real-time messaging system for resource-constrained environments
Article.Authors: Kaur E.; Kaur E.; Sethi V.; Nikhil N/A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The growing number of technologies and computer processing nowadays makes it increasingly difficult for those people who have access to only a basic mobile phone and limited Internet connectivity to get access to more complex messaging applications/ computers. This paper will talk about GupShupGo, a lightweight real-time messaging application aimed at usage in resource-constrained environments. The scope of the paper will be limited in terms of sending/receiving audio/ video calls. Nevertheless, sending/ receiving text messages, participation in the group chat, getting push notifications, and presence management during message exchange will be included. On the basis of the conducted performance testing of GupShupGo, we have defined the maximum number of simultaneous users equal to 1,000; the average response time to send messages to users was less than 100 ms. Under controlled testing conditions, the average amount of memory utilized by each device was between 85 MB and 100 MB; the average percentage of the CPU used by devices was between 8% and 18%. It is worth noting there were no direct comparison tests conducted with the commercial messaging services such as WhatsApp, Telegram, because of the different methods utilized and messaging services provided. Generally, findings show that GupShupGo is usable as a messaging service under resource-limited and low bandwidth environments. Furthermore, because of its energy efficiency and modularity, GupShupGo will offer reliable text messaging services in economically deprived regions/businesses.

Article.Title: Selection of promising Iranian Alcea species as phenolic-rich medicinal plants based on micromorphological, phytochemical, and antioxidant traits
Article.Authors: Sharifi B.; Saeidi K.; Shiran B.; Shahbazi E.; Lorigooini Z.; Rahimifard M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reliable identification and phytochemical characterization of medicinal plants are essential for selecting suitable germplasm and developing standardized botanical materials. We investigated eight Iranian Alcea species ( A. koelzii , A. kurdica , A. lavateriflora , A. rechingeri , A. remotiflora , A. rufescens , A. schiraziana , and A. teheranica ) grown under common field conditions. Phytochemical traits were evaluated in 46 ecotypes, while SEM and HPLC studies were performed only on 14 selected ecotypes. Micromorphological features of leaves, mericarps, and seed coats were examined using scanning electron microscopy, while flower extracts were evaluated for total phenolic, flavonoid, and anthocyanin contents, antioxidant activity, and four selected phenolic compounds were determined by targeted HPLC analysis. Diagnostic micromorphological variation was observed in glandular and fascicled trichomes and seed-coat structures. Significant interspecific variation was also detected in phytochemical and antioxidant traits. Targeted HPLC analysis of the selected ecotypes detected and quantified caffeic acid, chlorogenic acid, quercetin, and rutin in the flower extracts. Total phenolic content was positively correlated with flavonoid and anthocyanin contents and FRAP activity, but negatively correlated with IC₅₀, indicating an association between phenolic accumulation and antioxidant capacity. Hierarchical clustering based on phytochemical traits separated the species into three major groups. These complementary structural and phytochemical findings may support the characterization of Alcea germplasm and help identify promising ecotypes for trait-specific cultivation and further development of standardized botanical materials.

Article.Title: Topology selection and power optimization of photovoltaic arrays with hybrid cross-tie retrofit under partial shading
Article.Authors: Lin J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Partial shading leads to uneven irradiance distribution within photovoltaic arrays and induces branch‑current mismatch and multi‑peaked power-voltage curves, thereby degrading the efficiency of distributed photovoltaic systems. Most static and dynamic reconfiguration schemes take the total‑cross‑tied topology as the optimization basis yet overlook wiring complexity and retrofitting costs, making them unsuitable for cost‑constrained small‑scale photovoltaic scenarios. This work systematically compares five conventional topologies and five hybrid topologies under ten typical partial‑shading conditions. A multi‑dimensional evaluation framework is built using metrics including global maximum power point, shading loss, mismatch loss, fill factor, conversion efficiency, performance ratio and the number of cross‑tie connections. Scenario‑specific topology‑selection criteria are summarized for permanent building shading, and average performance across all partial‑shading conditions quantifies each topology’s adaptability to stochastic temporary shading. Simulations on a 6 × 6 photovoltaic array show that the proposed hybrid topologies achieve 1.25–4.34% power gains versus conventional schemes with a good trade‑off between power output and wiring complexity. A localized cross‑tie retrofit strategy is further proposed, yielding 2.26–5.25% power gain without rearranging the original photovoltaic module arrangement. All conclusions are derived from numerical simulations and offer theoretical references for small‑scale photovoltaic array planning and retrofitting.

Article.Title: Solar photovoltaic module multi-class anomaly detection using MobileNet architecture with skip connections
Article.Authors: Bhetalam A.; Anil Naik K.
Article.Abstract: Reliable detection of photovoltaic (PV) module anomalies is essential for improving the operational reliability and maintenance of solar energy systems. Infrared thermographic imaging provides a non-invasive means of identifying abnormal thermal patterns associated with module faults. However, accurate multiclass classification remains challenging because of similarities between fault signatures, variations in thermal characteristics, and imbalanced distributions of defect categories. This study investigates a lightweight deep-learning framework based on MobileNet with conditional skip connections for automated PV module anomaly classification using infrared thermographic images. The architecture employs depthwise separable convolutions to support computational efficiency while learning discriminative features from thermal images. Conditional skip connections are incorporated to facilitate feature propagation where the input and output dimensions are compatible. The framework is evaluated across binary and multiclass classification settings, with its performance examined using classification accuracy, class-wise evaluation metrics, confusion matrices, and training and validation behaviour. The results indicate the potential of the proposed architecture to distinguish normal operating conditions from anomalous modules and classify multiple fault categories using a compact network. Nevertheless, similarities between certain defect classes and variations in class representation remain important challenges for reliable fault identification. This study contributes to the development of lightweight image-based diagnostic methods for PV inspection. Further validation using independent datasets, class-balanced evaluation metrics, controlled architectural ablation, and standardized computational benchmarks is necessary to establish generalizability and practical deployment suitability.

Article.Title: Evaluation of the feasibility of classifying various upper limb movements using multichannel upper-arm sEMG signals
Article.Authors: Kim D.; Choi S.; Kim J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Surface electromyography (sEMG)-based upper limb movement recognition studies have primarily focused on signals measured from the forearm or muscles around the wrist. However, the feasibility of using upper-arm sEMG signals as an alternative measurement site for classifying various upper limb movements remains insufficiently investigated. This study evaluated the feasibility of classifying eight upper limb movements, including elbow, forearm, wrist, and hand movements, using five-channel upper-arm sEMG signals. sEMG signals were collected from the biceps brachii long head, biceps brachii short head, triceps brachii long head, triceps brachii lateral head, and brachialis in seven healthy adult males under static and free conditions. Random Forest achieved the highest accuracies of 93.13 ± 0.70% under the static condition and 89.16 ± 1.21% under the free condition. The full feature set and five-channel configuration showed high performance, although lower recall and increased misclassification were observed for hand open and hand close movements under the free condition. These findings provide preliminary evidence for the feasibility of within-subject upper limb movement classification using upper-arm sEMG signals and suggest their potential as a complementary measurement site.

Article.Title: Distance-dependent fluorescence modulation under continuous flow in an LTCC-integrated plasmonic competitive immunoassay
Article.Authors: Abad N.; Czok M.; Gwóźdź K.; Fiedot M.; Malecha K.; Cabaj J.; Baluta S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We report an LTCC-integrated optofluidic plasmonic immunoplatform that enables sequential flow-through fluorescence measurements with real-time optical signal acquisition. The system combines graphene quantum dot donors and gold nanoparticle plasmonic quenchers within a competitive microfluidic immunoassay architecture designed to investigate distance-dependent fluorescence modulation at biofunctionalized nanointerfaces. Fluorescence modulation is associated with distance-dependent interactions between biofunctionalized nanoparticles. Competitive binding of cortisol increases donor–acceptor separation, resulting in concentration-dependent fluorescence recovery within the 10–200 µM range (R 2 = 0.96). Spectral and analytical results are consistent with coupled plasmonic, interfacial, and optical attenuation effects contributing to the observed fluorescence modulation. The LTCC-integrated architecture enables stable real-time optical measurements under confined flow conditions. This work provides a proof-of-principle demonstration of the platform; however, before clinical application could be considered, further optimization and validation are required at cortisol concentrations corresponding to physiological conditions and in biological matrices.

Article.Title: Persistent directional anisotropy in dynamic visual acuity and attenuated increase in saccadic eye movements with stroboscopic training
Article.Authors: Soh Z.; Tachihara A.; Mizuguchi T.; Kandori A.; Hama S.; Tsuji T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Strobe glasses are used for dynamic visual acuity (DVA) training, but evidence is based mainly on horizontal motion. We examined short-term training, stroboscopic training, and directional anisotropy in vertical and horizontal DVA and eye movements. Twenty participants were randomly assigned to strobe or control groups and completed three sessions on alternate days; sixteen were analyzed. DVA improved by 23.4 deg/s per session ( p < 0.001), while vertical DVA remained 36.8 deg/s lower than horizontal DVA ( p < 0.001). The group $$\times $$ session interaction was not significant ( p = 0.252). The saccadic component of the cumulative eye displacement was quantified, with saccade onset and offset defined from the velocity profile and the detected events assessed for consistency with the saccadic main sequence. Saccades accounted for approximately 95% of the cumulative eye displacement. Training increased saccadic displacement, and this increase was attenuated in the strobe group (group $$\times $$ session, $$- 1.82$$ deg per session, p = 0.020). Mean absolute eye–target position error (MAE) decreased by 1.67 deg per session ( p < 0.001) and was 1.45 deg greater for vertical motion ( p = 0.005). The session $$\times $$ group interaction was significant ( $$- 0.92$$ deg per session, p = 0.045), indicating a larger session-related decrease in the strobe group. Thus, short-term practice improved DVA, whereas stroboscopic training was associated with an attenuated session-related increase in saccadic displacement and a larger decrease in MAE, without a significant additional DVA gain. Article.Title: A hybrid statistical–machine learning framework for day-ahead electricity price forecasting in smart city environments
Article.Authors: Hassanpouri Baesmat K.; Farrokhi Z.; Regentova E.
Article.Abstract: Accurate day-ahead electricity price forecasting, particularly in the context of customer-centric services and emerging smart city infrastructures, is a cornerstone of efficient power market operations, supporting bidding strategies, hedging, and grid reliability. This paper proposes SSXLR, a fault-tolerant hybrid forecasting framework that combines Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with Exogenous variables (SARIMAX), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) within a 2-out-of-3 voting architecture to capture both linear seasonal trends and nonlinear temporal dynamics while reducing dependence on a single forecasting branch. The proposed method was evaluated using one year of historical data (July 1, 2024–July 1, 2025) from Duke Energy Ohio and Kentucky (DEO&K) within the PJM interconnection. The dataset integrates day-ahead market prices ($/MWh), corresponding load consumption (MW), eleven weather variables, and population growth indicators. The target is the day-ahead price profile for July 2, 2025, consisting of 24-hourly points. Results show that SSXLR achieves more than 30% reduction in Root Mean Squared Error over SARIMAX and XGBoost, respectively. The Mean Absolute Error (MAE) reached 1.196, demonstrating the ability of SSXLR to account effectively for external market drivers and temporal dependencies. These findings highlight the scalability of the proposed framework for regional electricity markets, where accurate day-ahead forecasting can improve operational planning, supply–demand balance, and economic efficiency. The proposed framework is dynamic and region-adaptable, allowing it to be transferred to other smart city or regional energy systems when electricity price, load/consumption, weather, and calendar data are available. Beyond improving predictive accuracy, the 2-out-of-3 voting mechanism provides a fault-tolerant forecasting layer by allowing the final output to be determined from the two most consistent forecasting branches when one branch becomes unavailable or produces an unreliable output.

Article.Title: Rare gems: researchers from unconventional departments provide greater brokerage in interdisciplinary science
Article.Authors: Dinh L.; Barley W.; Allan B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Interdisciplinary research institutes are widely implemented at research universities to support cross-disciplinary collaboration, but their impact on researchers’ collaboration networks may not be uniform. Variation in how academic departments are represented within an institute creates different opportunities for researchers to either broaden their networks or remain within their disciplinary boundaries. Using longitudinal publication data from 256 researchers over 17 years, we estimate whether researchers’ collaboration networks become more redundant (higher constraint) or more bridging (lower constraint) after joining one such institute. A significant moderation effect shows that, within our sample, departmental conventionality conditions the effect of membership: in less conventional departments, institute membership is associated with decreased network constraint, providing greater access to diverse and non-redundant co-authorship connections. These findings indicate that members joining the institute from less conventional departments experience a greater impact on research networks, suggesting the need for policies to support these researchers for their brokerage roles.

Article.Title: Coverage and connectivity aware node deployment using improved NSGA-II and MOSSA approach for UWSNs
Article.Authors: Kumari S.; Garg L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Underwater wireless sensor networks (UWSNs) are extensively utilized for monitoring of aquatic environments, oceanographic data gathering, target tracking, and disaster early warning, but their effectiveness depends on maintaining adequate sensing coverage and end-to-end connectivity in the presence of node displacement caused by ocean currents, mobility, natural disasters, and environmental interference. Under such conditions, deployed nodes drift from their intended positions and become trapped in regions where they can neither cover the area of interest nor reach the surface infrastructure, producing both interior coverage holes inside the monitored volume and boundary holes at its periphery. Most existing schemes consider only interior coverage holes and do not address boundary holes that arise after natural disasters or environmental disturbance, and most are single-objective formulations that do not jointly account for coverage, connectivity, and energy. To mitigate these gaps, a unified two-stage scheme is proposed. In the first stage, a hole-detection method based on layered delaunay triangulation (DT) and sensing-circle intersection points is used to enumerate both interior and boundary holes within the monitored volume. In the second stage, additional autonomous-underwater-vehicle (AUV) based mobile nodes are deployed at optimal positions using two complementary multi-objective metaheuristics: an improved Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-II (NSGA-II) with multi-point crossover and a probability-based adaptive mutation operator, and a Multi-Objective Salp Swarm Algorithm (MOSSA) augmented with non-dominated sorting. A novel multi-objective fitness function is optimized that simultaneously maximises coverage quality, connectivity, and network lifetime, evaluated under a realistic underwater acoustic channel model and a Meandering Current Mobility model. The proposed scheme additionally exploits the geometric structure of overlapping coverage holes to deploy a single mobile node to repair multiple overlapping holes whenever feasible, reducing the number of additional AUVs required. The two algorithms are compared against published baselines SHORT (spherical hole-repair technique), DABVF (distributed node deployment algorithm based on virtual forces), and improved NSGA-II. MOSSA achieves a higher coverage quality, reduces average per-node energy, and extends network lifetime compared to existing schemes. Averaged over 30 independent runs, MOSSA improves coverage quality by 2.4–19.3%, connectivity by 4.5–23.8%, convergence fitness by 14.0–46.7%, and energy efficiency by 23.5–43.2% compared with improved NSGA-II, DABVF and SHORT, where each range covers the three baselines from the strongest to the weakest. In the healing scenario, the additional AUVs increase coverage from 78 to 100% by repairing both interior and boundary holes. All pairwise differences are statistically significant at p < 0.05 using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Holm correction.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: underwater wireless sensor networks; NSGA-II; coverage holes; underwater acoustic channel; node placement; adaptive mutation; multi-objective optimization; Delaunay triangulation; autonomous underwater vehicles; energy efficiency; network lifetime; multi-point crossover

Article.Title: Implementation and performance of a 9-level switched-capacitor (SC) multilevel inverter (MLI) with 4 × voltage gain for grid-tied photovoltaic systems
Article.Authors: Pardhu B.; Babu N.; Raju C.; Rani K.; Awas T.
Article.Abstract: In this article, the details of the development and result analysis of a 9-level SC-MLI have been presented. The proposed system achieves a quadruple voltage gain (4 ×) and generates a 9-level waveform. The proposed system not only achieves a quadruple voltage gain (4 ×) as an advantage but also used minimal component-efficient architecture; it utilizes only three capacitors, diodes, and 9 power switches, thereby minimizing system cost and complexity while enhancing reliability. A Phase Disposition (PD) Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) is implemented for precise switching control. During the discharging and charging of the capacitor spike occurs. To address this inherent challenge, a small inductor was added, which effectively suppresses current inrush and extends component lifespan. A comprehensive comparative analysis was conducted to evaluate the proposed topology's superiority over existing9-level SC-MLIs in terms of component count, voltage gain, and efficiency. Moreover, the closed loop with PV tied to the grid was analysed, and the proposed system ensures MPPT of the solar photovoltaic. To verify the theoretical analysis, experimental verification through a 1.4 kW laboratory prototype, controlled via a dSpace 1103 platform, and simulations done in MATLAB SIMULINK, was conducted. Finally, the proposed efficiency of the proposed topology was exceeding 97%, and the THD of the grid current was below 2% and, confirming the theoretical analysis.

Article.Title: Scarcity, cognition, and health decision-making: evidence from a lab-in-the-field experiment in rural China
Article.Authors: Zhu H.; You F.; Liu E.; Gruber T.; Dong H.; De Bont C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Understanding how financial scarcity impacts health-related decision-making is vital for designing interventions to break the cycle between poverty and poor health. We conducted a lab-in-the-field experiment with 479 rural adults in two low-income regions of China, Yunnan and Shaanxi, to examine the cognitive and behavioural consequences for health-related preferences and choices. Participants were randomly assigned to an acute financial scarcity intervention consisting of three hypothetical scenarios featuring either a heavy financial burden (the Hard prime, e.g., raising 20,000 yuan within a week) or a minimal cost (the Easy control, 1,000 yuan). We measured cognitive function using a 12-item Raven’s Progressive Matrices task, time and risk preferences across monetary and health domains using multiple price lists and ordered lottery menus, and spending decisions using a 100-yuan budget allocation task. In the moderately poor region of Yunnan, the scarcity prime significantly reduced cognitive performance by 8.4% points and increased health-related risk aversion, driving individuals toward safer vaccine options. In contrast, no cognitive or behavioural preference shifts were observed in the more severely impoverished region of Shaanxi. Intertemporal time preferences remained stable across both regions and choice domains. Budget allocations showed limited overall shifts, though specific resource-scarce subgroups reallocated spending more toward health items. These findings demonstrate that the cognitive and behavioural consequences of scarcity are not universal but highly context-dependent, shifting with the chronic depth of underlying deprivation.
