Article.Title: Long-term drought assessment and climate change signals in Türkiye using SPI, SPEI and trend analysis (1930–2024)
Article.Authors: Ergüven R.; Avcı D.; Aydın A.
Article.Abstract: Drought is a complex and multidimensional phenomenon influenced by both precipitation variability and temperature-driven processes, particularly under evolving hydro-climatic conditions. A comprehensive assessment of long-term drought dynamics across Türkiye is presented using multi-timescale Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) and Standardized Precipitation–Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) based on data from 21 representative cities across seven geographical regions. Drought variability was evaluated at 1-, 3-, 6-, and 12-month accumulation periods, while long-term trends and regime shifts were analyzed using the Mann–Kendall test, Sen’s slope estimator, and the Pettitt test. The results indicate that short-term drought variability is dominated by high-frequency fluctuations, whereas longer accumulation periods, particularly at the 12-month scale, capture more persistent and spatially coherent drought patterns. At the 12-month scale, statistically significant trends were detected in a considerable proportion of stations, with SPEI indicating more widespread and spatially consistent drying patterns compared to SPI, which remains spatially heterogeneous and often statistically weak. These findings highlight the increasing role of temperature-driven evapotranspiration in intensifying drought conditions. Change-point analysis revealed that all stations experienced at least one statistically significant regime shift, with most change points clustering between the 1950s and early 2000s, indicating pronounced non-stationary hydro-climatic behavior. Teleconnection analysis further shows that drought variability is partially influenced by large-scale atmospheric circulation patterns, with statistically significant relationships ( p < 0.05) identified in several regions, particularly for the North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO), while the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) shows more spatially variable and moderate effects. Overall, the results demonstrate that drought dynamics in Türkiye are governed by the combined effects of precipitation variability, temperature-driven processes, and atmospheric circulation patterns. The combined use of SPI and SPEI with trend, change-point, and teleconnection analyses provides an integrated basis for interpreting long-term drought variability and may inform climate adaptation, water resource management, and drought risk assessment.

Article.Title: Effect of printing layer thickness and sintering time on the densification, microstructure and mechanical properties of binder-jetted Ti-6Al-4V alloy
Article.Authors: Huang S.; Qi C.; Cui X.; Li Z.; Guan D.; Zhang Y.; Jia W.; Li F.
Article.Abstract: This study examines how printing layer thickness and sintering time jointly affect the densification, microstructure, and tensile behavior of binder-jetted Ti-6Al-4V under a fixed jetting strategy. Specimens were printed with layer thicknesses of 40, 80, and 120 μm and sintered at 1300 °C for 1–5 h. Reducing the layer thickness increased green density and refined the initial pore structure, thereby accelerating pore closure during early sintering. The 40 μm specimens reached the best condition after 2 h, with 94.4% relative density, 4.4% porosity, and an ultimate tensile strength approaches the wrought benchmark. Larger layer thicknesses required longer holding times but showed lower maximum densities within the investigated process window. Prolonged holding also promoted grain growth and possible pore coarsening, which limited further improvement. These results indicate that improving the green-body state by reducing layer thickness is more effective than simply extending sintering time, although ductility and residual defect control remain important for further optimization.

Article.Title: Lycium barbarum polysaccharides protect ischemic brain injury through regulating RPLP1 expression on ischemia-reperfusion nerve cells
Article.Authors: Shao N.; Ma B.; Li Y.; Wang X.; Du Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ischemic stroke is a major neurological disorder characterized by the sudden interruption of blood flow to the brain, leading to neuronal injury and death. This study investigates the protective effects of lycium barbarum polysaccharides (LBP) on neurons subjected to ischemia-reperfusion injury and its regulatory role on ribosomal protein lateral stalk subunit P1 (RPLP1) expression. Using in vitro cell models, we demonstrated that LBP significantly inhibits apoptosis in ischemic-reperfused neurons. Additionally, LBP treatment resulted in a notable upregulation of RPLP1 expression, indicating its potential to restore ribosomal function compromised during ischemic events. Further mechanistic studies revealed that the neuroprotective effects of LBP may be mediated through the Akt/mTOR signaling pathway, which plays a crucial role in cell survival and metabolism. These findings suggest that LBP not only enhances neuronal viability but also promotes recovery by modulating key cellular pathways involved in neuroprotection. Our results highlight the therapeutic potential of LBP as a candidate for ischemic stroke management, providing insights into its mechanisms of action and paving the way for future research aimed at developing effective interventions for ischemic brain injury.

Article.Title: Non-target effect of fungicides on root endophytic fungus Microdochium bolleyi in barley
Article.Authors: Matušinsky P.; Antalová Z.; Šlajsová T.; Jarošová N.; Bleša D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fungicides are widely used in crop protection to control phytopathogenic fungi, yet their effects on non-target microorganisms inhabiting plant tissues remain poorly understood. Endophytic fungi are components of the plant microbiome, but assessing how fungicide applications influence their colonisation is challenging because these interactions are often asymptomatic. In this study, a simplified barley- Microdochium bolleyi model system was used to investigate the effects of fungicide exposure on endophytic colonisation. In vitro sensitivity assays revealed differences among fungicides, with prothioconazole showing the highest activity against sixteen M. bolleyi isolates (EC 50 = 0.11 µg mL⁻¹), followed by fluxapyroxad (0.31 µg mL⁻¹), mefentrifluconazole (0.37 µg mL⁻¹), and azoxystrobin (0.50 µg mL⁻¹). Based on these results, prothioconazole was selected for greenhouse experiments. Application of this systemic fungicide as either a seed dressing or foliar treatment significantly reduced root colonisation by M. bolleyi in barley. Greenhouse experiments were conducted using nine M. bolleyi isolates with 12 biological replicates per treatment. Reduced colonisation was confirmed by microscopic detection of chlamydospores and quantitative PCR analysis of fungal DNA. Compared with untreated inoculated plants, root colonisation was reduced by approximately 83% following seed dressing and 65% following foliar application. These results demonstrate that, under the tested conditions, prothioconazole suppressed root colonisation by the non-target endophyte M. bolleyi . The study establishes an effect on colonisation of this specific endophyte but does not determine whether reduced colonisation has beneficial, neutral, or detrimental consequences for barley or the wider root-associated fungal community.

Article.Title: In vitro antifungal effect of plant-based and Ulva sp. extracts on Aspergillus flavus growth and conidia germination
Article.Authors: Boscarol G.; Di Francesco A.; Braidot E.; Vuerich M.; Boscutti F.; Volpe V.; Fabro M.; Vrhovšek U.; Moret E.; Ballico M.; Petrussa E.
Article.Abstract: Mycotoxins in cereals, particularly maize, represent a major threat to food safety and agricultural sustainability, a challenge expected to intensify under climate change. In this context, the development of environmentally friendly and sustainable mitigation strategies is urgently needed. Plant waste materials and seaweed biomass represent promising renewable sources of bioactive phytochemicals that can be used as sustainable agricultural approaches to control fungal pathogens. This study investigated the in vitro antifungal activity and chemical composition of hydroalcoholic extracts from plant waste materials and seaweed ( Ailanthus altissima (Mill.) Swingle leaves, Humulus lupulus L. trub, Olea europaea L. leaves, and Ulva sp. thallus). Except for Olea europaea , all extracts inhibited the growth of Aspergillus flavus , with those from Ulva showing the highest efficacy (EC 50 = 14.2 mg/mL). Total Phenolic (TPC) and Flavonoid (TFC) contents were quantified, revealing distinct chemical profiles across the extracts. Despite a TPC nearly three times lower (3.80 µg GAE/mg DW) than that from Humulus trub and Ailanthus (~ 11 µg GAE/mg DW), the superior activity of Ulva extract was attributed to its unique chemical composition. While the plant-derived extracts were enriched in glycosylated flavonols, the Ulva extract was characterized by specific phenolics, such as rosmarinic and p -hydroxybenzoic acids, and a dominant polysaccharide fraction; 1 H and 13 C NMR analysis confirmed the presence of sulfated ulvans, identified by characteristic rhamnose, xylose, and uronic acid units. These findings highlight the potential of plant residues and seaweed biomass as sustainable sources of antifungal compounds. In particular, Ulva extracts emerge as promising candidates for the development of eco-friendly strategies to control Aspergillus flavus infections, supporting greener crop protection and future applications in agricultural and post-harvest systems.

Article.Title: Predicting 1-year outcomes after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction from preoperative physical performance using machine learning: an exploratory study
Article.Authors: Boo S.; Lee J.; Jang K.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to develop machine learning (ML) models to predict 1-year outcomes after primary anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) using preoperative variables. A retrospective cohort of 75 patients who underwent ACLR between 2016 and 2023 was analyzed. Preoperative features included demographic characteristics, treatment-related variables, isokinetic muscle performance, and patient-reported outcome measures. One-year outcomes were defined as return to pivoting sports (RTS; Tegner activity level ≥ 6) and achievement of the patient acceptable symptom state (PASS; International Knee Documentation Committee score ≥ 75.9). Variables identified in univariable logistic regression were used for ML model development. Multiple algorithms were trained and evaluated using 3-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration plots, and Brier scores. Among the models, the random forest algorithm demonstrated the best performance, achieving an AUC of 0.832 for RTS and 0.815 for PASS. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified younger age and greater preoperative flexor strength of the uninvolved limb as the most important predictors. In this exploratory study, ML models incorporating preoperative clinical and physical performance variables showed promising potential for predicting 1-year outcomes after ACLR. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the small sample size and lack of external validation. The models should therefore be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than ready for clinical implementation, and require further validation in larger, independent cohorts. Article.Title: Behavior of reinforced high and ultra-high strength concrete slabs under high mass low-velocity impact loading
Article.Authors: Fareed S.; Dar N.; Khalid F.; Khan A.
Article.Abstract: The reinforced concrete (RC) structural elements during its design life may be subjected to accidental dynamic loads produced as a result of vehicular impacts, heavy drop weights, and explosive impacts. The structural elements may have to withstand forces with higher magnitudes and intensities than the typical static loading. Given its remarkable mechanical properties and durability, Ultra-High Strength Concrete (UHSC) slabs offer exceptional compressive strength and load carrying capacity; however, their response under low velocity impact loading remains underexplored. The primary motive of this study is to establish a framework that quantifies the influence of slab geometry, boundary condition, reinforcement ratio, concrete compressive strength and impactor properties on maximum dynamic contact force and mid-span deflections. This paper presents an experimental and numerical investigation into the response of two-way simply supported RC slabs under high-mass, low-velocity impact loading. The experimental investigation evaluated ten specimens made of normal strength concrete (NSC), high strength concrete (HSC) to assess the influence of compressive strength and reinforcement ratio on peak impact force, failure patterns and displacement. Furthermore, a non-linear Finite Element (FE) model was developed in ABAQUS and validated against the experimental contact force–time history. The validated framework was subsequently extended to numerically predict the dynamic response of UHSC slabs under impact conditions. The numerical FE results indicate that UHSC slabs exhibit greater impact resistance, reduced the mid-span deflections and enhanced scabbing controls. Based on the FE parametric findings an Equivalent Static Factor was derived to predict the maximum load carrying capacity of two-way simply supported UHSC-RC slabs when subjected to low-velocity impact loading of upto 6 m/s. Furthermore, multi-regression analysis-based equations were also developed to estimate the maximum impact force and maximum mid-span deflection of two-way simply supported UHSC-RC slabs when subjected to low-velocity impact loading. The ESF factor and MRA equations were developed using limited dataset and are not intended for design use. The predictive equations and ESF offer simplified approximation to assess the impact resistance of two-way simply supported RC slab under low velocity (upto 6 m/s) impact load evaluated in this study and require further experimental validation before the broader application.

Article.Title: Impact of geomagnetic storm intensity on thermospheric density and orbital decay of LEO satellites: a G1–G5 per-event analysis
Article.Authors: Kim J.; Eom G.; Kwak Y.; Yang T.; Huh H.
Article.Abstract: Geomagnetic storms enhance thermospheric density and increase atmospheric drag on low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites, accelerating their orbital decay, as illustrated by the loss of 38 Starlink satellites in February 2022. Prior multi-event analyses have characterized this response primarily through superposed epoch analyses (SEA). Here we apply a per-event approach: for each of 22 storms spanning G1 to G5 (2003–2024), including the May 2024 Gannon storm, we compare the storm-peak orbit of Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) or GRACE-Follow On (-FO) with a matched quiet-time reference orbit. The mean orbital decay rate enhancement generally increases with storm intensity (77.2%, 98.5%, 138.1%, 149.6%, and 166.5% from G1 to G5), although the scatter within each category is large. Operation altitude is also important: low-altitude events produce strong drag responses even under weak geomagnetic forcing. An empirical multiple linear regression model using quiet-time decay rate, maximum Kp, and operation altitude reproduces the storm-time decay rate (R² = 0.91; root mean square error, RMSE = 12.3 m/day; leave-one-out RMSE = 15.1 m/day). Replacing Kp with the open-ended Hp30 index gives similar results. These per-event benchmarks complement SEA-based analyses, provide a reference for empirical thermospheric models, and support storm-time orbit prediction for LEO satellites.

Article.Title: TinyRoute: secure adaptive routing for intelligent transportation system using TinyML and few shot learning
Article.Authors: Jagadeesan S.; Suresh A.; Vetriselvi T.; Tamil Priya D.; Balaji N.
Article.Abstract: Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) needs secure and adaptive communication mechanisms for addressing the dynamic vehicular mobility, routing instability, and increasingly sophisticated cyber-attacks in Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V), Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I), and Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) environments in which the recent VANET routing and intrusion detection approaches have improved routing efficiency or attack detection individually. However, it generally lack an integrated framework capable of simultaneously supporting adaptive routing, lightweight edge intelligence, and reliable zero-day attack detection under highly dynamic traffic conditions. To address these issues, this paper proposes TinyRoute, a secure adaptive routing framework that integrates Geometric Deep Reinforcement Learning (Geo-DRL), Honey Badger Optimization (HBO), TinyML, and a CNN LSTM-based Few-Shot Learning Intrusion Detection System (FSL-IDS) in which the Geo-DRL performs mobility-aware route selection but HBO refines routing paths by avoiding malicious and congested regions. The lightweight on-device anomaly inference within autonomous vehicles is enabled by TinyML. With only the limited samples, the cloud based FSL-IDS detects both known and zero-day attacks respectively. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that TinyRoute achieves a routing latency of 28.4 ms, a Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR) of 96.7%, an intrusion detection accuracy of 95.2%, and a communication overhead of only 12.4 KB/s, outperforming recent state-of-the-art VANET routing and IDS approaches. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for secure, adaptive, and low-latency ITS communication.

Article.Title: Psychometric validation of the emotional creativity inventory in an Egyptian context
Article.Authors: Helali M.; Elwakeel S.; Elharony S.; Abdelshafy E.; Aldawsari H.; Bukhamseen A.; Aboud Y.; Abdel-Sattar R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The study aimed to evaluate the factorial validity, internal consistency, and reliability of the Shortened Emotional Creativity Inventory (ECI-S) among Egyptian university students. A total of 1084 undergraduate and postgraduate students from several Egyptian universities completed the Egyptian Arabic version of the ECI-S through an online survey. Confirmatory factor analysis was conducted to examine the three-factor structure comprising Preparedness, Novelty, and Authenticity. Reliability was assessed using McDonald’s omega coefficients, alongside item-total correlations. The results supported the hypothesized three-dimensional model, demonstrating acceptable model fit (CFI = 0.953, TLI = 0.949, SRMR = 0.067, and RMSEA = 0.012, with a 90% CI of [0.000, 0.028]). All items loaded significantly on their respective latent factors, providing evidence of factorial validity. McDonald’s omega coefficients indicated satisfactory internal consistency for each subscale and for the total score, supporting the reliability of the instrument. Moreover, substantial correlations between subdimensions and the overall emotional creativity score provided further evidence of structural coherence. These findings support the factorial validity and internal consistency of the Egyptian Arabic version of the ECI-S within the current sample. The evaluated scale offers researchers and practitioners a tool for investigating emotional creativity within the Egyptian university context.

Article.Title: Anatomy-guided U-Net deep learning for sparse-view chest CT reconstruction using spatially varying RTV regularization
Article.Authors: Veysi A.; Babapour Mofrad F.; Zayyani H.; Pouraliakbar H.
Article.Abstract: Sparse-view computed tomography (CT) reconstruction remains a challenging inverse problem due to severe undersampling artifacts, noise amplification, and the difficulty of preserving anatomical structures while reducing image degradation. Conventional regularization-based methods often require manual parameter adjustment and rely on spatially uniform priors, whereas deep learning approaches may provide limited interpretability or insufficient integration of physical constraints. In this study, we propose SvRTV-UNet, a physics-guided deep learning framework that integrates a U-Net architecture with spatially variant Relative Total Variation (SvRTV) regularization for adaptive sparse-view chest CT reconstruction. The proposed framework simultaneously performs anatomical segmentation and predicts reconstruction parameters, including the regularization strength (λ) and tissue-specific weighting parameters (A 1 and A 2 ), directly from image quality characteristics. A homoscedastic uncertainty-based multi-task learning strategy is employed to automatically balance segmentation, parameter estimation, and reconstruction objectives without manual loss weighting. In addition, anatomy-aware confidence maps derived from segmentation accuracy and edge information enable tissue-dependent regularization for improved structural preservation. Compared with conventional iterative reconstruction methods, model-based regularization approaches, and representative deep learning methods, SvRTV-UNet demonstrated improved reconstruction performance across quantitative metrics. The quantitative and qualitative results obtained demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method compared with the evaluated approaches. By integrating physics-based constraints with anatomy-guided adaptive regularization, SvRTV-UNet offers an interpretable framework that adapts to varying acquisition conditions without view-specific retraining.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: chest CT; anatomical priors; sparse-view CT reconstruction; U-Net; deep learning reconstruction

Article.Title: Aerodynamic optimization of Gurney flap parameters for a Formula 1 wing using experimental and coupled GA-ANN-CFD methods
Article.Authors: Shahrabi A.; Kazemi M.; Jahangirian A.; Mani M.
Article.Abstract: This study presents a comprehensive numerical and experimental investigation of the aerodynamic performance of Gurney flaps applied to an inverted multi-element airfoil representative of a Formula 1 front wing. A coupled Genetic Algorithm & Artificial Neural Network & Computational Fluid Dynamics (GA-ANN-CFD) framework is developed and applied to a three-element airfoil at a Reynolds number of 500 × 10 3 . Four baseline configurations, defined by flap orientation (vertical and surface-normal) and geometry (solid and slotted), are independently optimized, yielding eight optimal designs. The results demonstrate that flap height is the dominant parameter governing downforce generation, with maximum-height configurations increasing downforce by up to 11.24%, albeit with a moderate reduction in aerodynamic efficiency. In contrast, smaller-height slotted configurations provide a more favorable balance between downforce and drag. The experimental investigation evaluates nine Gurney flap geometries, combining three heights (1.5%, 3%, and 5% chord) and three installation angles (54°, 72°, and 90°), over Reynolds numbers ranging from 250 × 10 3 to 500 × 10 3 . Surface pressure measurements and wake velocity profiles reveal that increasing flap height significantly enhances pressure differentials and wake momentum deficit, leading to higher downforce. Overall, the results identify flap height as the primary design parameter governing downforce generation, while installation angle and slotting provide secondary control over aerodynamic efficiency and wake characteristics.

Article.Title: Hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning for operations and maintenance disruption recovery in high-end equipment manufacturing under compound risks
Article.Authors: Wei C.; Liu P.; Rao W.
Article.Abstract: Compound disruptions in high-end equipment manufacturing can simultaneously fragment operations and maintenance (O&M) resource networks and constrain critical resource flows. Using natural disasters and trade sanctions as representative compound risks of topology-based network fragmentation and capacity-constrained flow bottlenecks, this study addresses a recovery problem in which network reconfiguration changes the feasible space of downstream resource scheduling, while scheduling outcomes feed back through system-level evaluation to influence upstream reconfiguration. The problem is further complicated when multiple projects compete for heterogeneous, category-specific resources under contractually binding delivery requirements. An integrated recovery model based on a dual-layer business–resource network is developed to coordinate network reconfiguration and resource scheduling while balancing recovery cost, duration, and pending repair rate. To solve the coupled problem, a dual-agent algorithm based on hierarchical multi-agent proximal policy optimization (HMA-PPO) is proposed. Its main architectural feature is a hierarchical conditional coordination mechanism: the reconfigured network is transmitted forward to construct the state and feasible decision conditions of downstream resource scheduling, while the network-reconfiguration and resource-scheduling decisions are jointly evaluated as an integrated recovery solution, with the resulting system-level evaluation shared by both agents for policy updating. Numerical experiments show that HMA-PPO achieves the lowest mean objective value among the tested baselines, reaches the exact optimum on all three tested small instances, and requires approximately 0.24 s for post-training online decision making. Its relative solution-quality advantage becomes more evident as the tested decision space expands; on the large network, the mean objective value is 12.84% lower than that of Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO) and 7.21% lower than that of Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS). Scenario analyses further show that compound risks increase total O&M cost by 25.17% on average relative to the single natural-disaster scenario, while backup-supplier configuration and operating margins materially affect recovery resilience. These findings provide a unified perspective on coupled structural recovery and constrained resource allocation for resilience management in advanced manufacturing systems and operations research. Enterprises should diversify backup-supplier portfolios while jointly assessing supplier quality, usable capacity, transportation conditions, and delivery reliability rather than relying on supplier count alone. They should also use stress testing to identify scenario-specific operating buffers and prioritize scarce resources according to project urgency, resource criticality, and contractual delivery requirements.

Article.Title: Complementary medicine awareness, beliefs, and recent conventional CAM use among university students with and without self-reported previous physician-diagnosed IBS in Palestine
Article.Authors: Lahlouh M.; Khalaf L.; Malhis L.; Futian R.; Toukan N.; Karaki D.; Deeb T.
Article.Abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a common disorder of gut-brain interaction, and many affected individuals seek complementary and alternative medicine (CAM) or related self-care practices. Data on CAM awareness, beliefs, information sources, and recent practice use among university students in Middle Eastern settings remain limited. This cross-sectional survey assessed these outcomes among 400 undergraduate students at An-Najah National University, Palestine, in relation to self-reported previous physician-diagnosed IBS and sociodemographic characteristics. Recent practices were classified as conventional CAM, culturally embedded/traditional practices, lifestyle/wellness practices, and physical therapy. Modified Poisson regression with robust variance was used to estimate adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for CAM awareness, belief in CAM effectiveness, and recent conventional CAM use. Overall, 20.8% of participants reported previous physician-diagnosed IBS, 49.0% reported awareness of CAM availability for IBS-related symptoms, and 73.5% believed that CAM may be effective. Recent conventional CAM use during the previous month was reported by 58.5% of participants; 39.8% reported at least one lifestyle/wellness practice, 5.3% reported prophetic medicine, and 28.0% reported physical therapy. Self-reported previous physician-diagnosed IBS was associated with a higher adjusted prevalence of CAM awareness (aPR 2.22, 95% CI 1.87–2.63), belief in CAM effectiveness (aPR 1.41, 95% CI 1.27–1.56), and recent conventional CAM use (aPR 1.56, 95% CI 1.36–1.78). Because IBS status was not clinically confirmed and recent practices were not necessarily IBS-directed, findings should be interpreted as CAM-related awareness, beliefs, and general health behavior rather than evidence of IBS-directed treatment or CAM effectiveness.

Article.Title: Lipid profile and treatment results in adults aged 25–64 in Czechia: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Michalec J.; Lustigová M.; Žejglicová K.; Malinovská J.; Krollová P.; Goyal K.; Fahmy E.; Wasserbauer M.; Koželuhová M.; Michalcová N.; Janíčková Žďárská D.; Piťhová P.; Brož J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of death in Czechia. This is caused by the persistently high prevalence of several CVD risk factors, including dyslipidemia. Our goal was to establish the success rate of meeting the study-defined lipid control. We used data from the Czech cross-sectional study EHES 2019 (European Health Examination Survey), which is an epidemiological study with a stratified random sampling design. All parameters were assessed according to standardized criteria. The data were analyzed via descriptive statistics and group comparisons. A total of 1057 participants (426 men and 631 women) aged 25–64 years were included in the study. The most common risk factor was dyslipidemia, accounting for 71.7% of the studied population. The shares of participants with risk values of the lipid spectrum indicator were distributed as follows: 54.3% for total cholesterol; 52.3% for LDL-C; 8.7% for HDL-C; 41.1% for non-HDL-C; and 27.6% for TAG. The percentage of subjects with dyslipidemia who were aware of this disorder was 33.4%, while that of respondents with knowledge of dyslipidemia treated with lipid-lowering drugs was 27.7%. The measured lipid levels met the study-defined normal values in only 23.7% of the treated participants. The study revealed not only a low awareness among patients of their conditions but also a low efficacy in achieving lipid goals.

Article.Title: Engineering a water-compatible upconversion nanoink for NIR-readable covert printing and QR authentication
Article.Authors: Alsofyani N.; Alfahd A.; Alghannam F.; Alessa A.; Alromaeh A.; Albariqi A.; Almuqhim A.; Alkahtani M.
Article.Abstract: Lanthanide-doped upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) offer an innovative route to covert optical labels that become visible under near-infrared (NIR) excitation. Here, LiYF₄:Yb, Er@LiYF₄ core–shell (CS) nanoparticles were coated with poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) and used to create a printable nanoink for water-based printing. X-ray diffraction (XRD) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) supported retention of the tetragonal phase and particle morphology after PAA treatment, while FTIR measurements were consistent with altered surface chemistry. Photoluminescence studies revealed the increase in the intensity of the green emission by about 2.7 times upon LiYF4 shell formation. The background-corrected green peak intensity of inks with concentrations of CS-PAA of 1–20 mg mL − 1 increased by about 28 times. Four nanoink formulations were tested in this study, and the ink with the 65:35 volume ratio of 10% aqueous ethanol to glycerol was selected, and covert text was printed with a Canon PIXMA MG5320 printer. QR-code readout used NIR camera acquisition followed by smartphone decoding of the camera image displayed on a computer screen. Decoding success rates over 20 decoding attempts were 5%, 25%, and 85% for inks with concentrations of 1, 2.5, and 5 mg mL − 1 , and 100% for inks with concentrations of 7.5, 10, and 20 mg mL − 1 . These results highlight the potential of aqueous LiYF₄-based inks for NIR-readable covert printing, with promising applications in anticounterfeiting, product authentication, and covert information encoding.

Article.Title: Evaluating image embeddings and metadata for NFT price prediction using temporal validation
Article.Authors: Lee G.; Koo H.; Lee H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Images and categorical traits provide closely related descriptions of profile picture non-fungible tokens (NFTs), making the incremental predictive value of image embeddings uncertain. We compare metadata-only, image-only, early-fusion and weighted late-fusion models for Bored Ape Yacht Club (BAYC) and Mutant Ape Yacht Club (MAYC) using eight regression families and seven visual encoders. Models are selected on pre-2025 data and retrospectively evaluated from January 2025 to April 2026. Selected models in all four groups outperform a zero log-relative-price benchmark. Relative to metadata, early fusion reduces root mean squared error (RMSE) by 0.09% in BAYC and 0.95% in MAYC; late fusion increases BAYC RMSE by 0.07% and reduces MAYC RMSE by 0.70%. Sensitivity analyses assess unseen tokens, matched regression families, transaction-row versus count-weighted fitting, and full reselection under stricter cleaning. For unseen tokens, exploratory 95% fusion-versus-metadata intervals include zero in both collections. Metadata-only partial least squares (PLS) outperforms CLIP–PLS early fusion in MAYC. Across two stricter cleaning variants, 13 of 16 representative configurations change relative to a common base-clean control; fusion improvements are not consistently supported after reselection. Some tree-based comparisons are implementation-sensitive. The results do not establish consistent image gains, independent aesthetic pricing power, or superiority of either fusion strategy.

Article.Title: Automated segmentation and quantification of histological liver features for MASH/MASLD scoring
Article.Authors: Spirgath K.; Huang B.; Safraou Y.; Dahami M.; Kraftberger M.; Kiehl T.; Stockburger C.; Bayerl C.; Ludwig J.; Jaitner N.; Kühl A.; Asbach P.; Geisel D.; Hillebrandt K.; Wells R.; Sack I.; Tzschätzsch H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The increasing global prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) creates an urgent need for objective histopathological assessment. Conventional histological approaches are time-consuming and subjective. Therefore, we propose a fully automated, deep-learning-based pipeline for the segmentation and characterisation of histological liver features of MASH/MASLD. Segmentation was applied to H&E sections from 45 mice and 44 humans with MASH/MASLD. Our qHisto (quantitative histology) method, is nnU-Net-based and quantifies key histological components of the MASH-score, including steatosis, fibrosis, inflammation and ballooning. Additionally, we determined novel features that are inaccessible through manual histology, like the distribution of fat droplet sizes, nuclear aspect ratio and heatmaps. qHisto parameters showed strong positive correlations with conventional histology scores (fat: R = 0.91, inflammation: R = 0.70, ballooning: R = 0.47) and with hepatic fat fraction by magnetic resonance imaging ( R = 0.87). Our novel scores showed that nuclei deformation is driven by large fat droplets rather than the overall amount of fat. A key advantage of our method is spatially resolved, precise histological quantification to provide detailed assessment of disease severity. By automating time-consuming and repetitive readouts, qHisto improves standardisation and reproducibility of MASH/MASLD feature quantification and provides scalable, slide-wide analysis that supports histopathologists and enhances clinical assessment.

Article.Title: Experimental characterisation and transfer matrix modelling of first natural frequencies in axially graded fused deposition modelling-printed polylactic acid cantilevers with edge cracks
Article.Authors: Katı H.; Alhamdan N.; He F.; Khan M.
Article.Abstract: Beams with axially varying infill density produced by fused deposition modelling (FDM) offer a route to tailor vibration response through manufacturing parameters, but few studies combine experimental and analytical characterisation of such beams with edge defects. In this work, polylactic acid (PLA) cantilever beams were fabricated by FDM with three axial infill distributions, uniform 50%, ascending 10% to 100%, and descending 100% to 10% from fixed to free end and tested with single-edge notches of depth 0 to 2.5 mm at the fixed end, giving 18 cracked-beam configurations. A separate set of 13 specimens, in which a 14 mm wide 10% infill segment was translated along an otherwise uniform 50% beam, served as an independent validation set that was not used in calibration. First natural frequencies were extracted from impulse-excitation measurements processed by three complementary methods (amplitude spectrum, power spectrum, time-domain peak counting), with a mean impulse-to-impulse standard deviation of 0.04 Hz. An analytical model combining a phenomenological linear constitutive law, the transfer matrix method, a Tada-Paris-Irwin rotational spring at the notch, and a point tip mass representing the accelerometer was calibrated against the 18-configuration cracked-beam dataset. Calibration converged to α E = 0.476 and α ρ = 0.522 with a 0.71 Hz RMSE; a profile-likelihood analysis showed both parameters are practically identifiable within the adopted model, dataset and reference properties E s and ρ s . Applied without re-fitting to the 13 segment-position specimens, the model reproduces all 31 configurations with a 4.0% mean absolute error, placing 28 within a ± 8% envelope.

Article.Title: CAT-GAN-UKF: uncertainty-aware spatiotemporal reconstruction for resilient urban air-quality monitoring under partial observability
Article.Authors: Tobaly L.; Zalevsky Z.; Yaniv E.
Article.Abstract: Urban air-quality monitoring networks are inherently incomplete: measurements disappear intermittently, sustained outages occur, and the reliability of the remaining evidence changes with pollutant, location, temporal regime, and network state. We present CAT-GAN-UKF, an uncertainty-aware framework for multivariate reconstruction under partial observability that combines nonlinear spatiotemporal state propagation, adversarial learning of context-dependent uncertainty, and masked recursive Bayesian updating. Pollutant-specific conditional Wasserstein generative adversarial networks with gradient penalty (WGAN-GP) are trained on signed empirical process- and observation-residual distributions derived exclusively from the chronological training period. Monte Carlo variance of generated residuals defines time-varying diagonal \(Q_t\) and \(R_t\) , which are injected into a nonlinear network UKF. The primary model uses causal temporal, lagged, rolling, missingness, and spatial context; temperature and humidity are evaluated only in a sensitivity analysis because they did not improve reconstruction in this benchmark. The evaluation uses 153,260 hourly station-time records from an OpenAQ-derived 2024 New York City metropolitan-area dataset. After predefined quality control, 27 of 33 monitoring locations were retained. All learned parameters are fitted on training data only; a separate validation interval is used for pollutant-specific multiplicative interval calibration, and the held-out test period is never used for fitting or calibration. Robustness is assessed under four random-masking levels, four contiguous outage lengths, and an empirical-gap replay protocol whose outage-length distribution is learned from naturally occurring training-period gaps. Each stress test is repeated over 30 masking seeds. CAT-GAN-UKF is compared with matched linear KF, fixed-covariance UKF and heuristic adaptive UKF baselines, as well as Extra Trees, random forest, histogram gradient boosting, multilayer perceptron, ridge, lasso, persistence, and temporal means. CAT-GAN-UKF significantly improves RMSE over adaptive UKF in seven of nine scenarios, linear KF in all nine, Extra Trees in all nine, and persistence in eight of nine after Holm correction. Relative to a strong fixed-covariance UKF, point-estimation accuracy is generally comparable rather than uniformly superior; however, CAT-GAN-UKF reduces average 95% interval width by approximately 38% across the nine scenarios while retaining mean empirical coverage near 95%. Spatial coupling is the dominant structural contribution: removing it increases RMSE by approximately 5.9% under 10% random masking and by 42.7% under a 24-hour outage. Conversely, adding meteorological covariates worsens RMSE throughout the sensitivity analysis. These findings establish an uncertainty-efficient research framework for spatial reconstruction under degraded sensing; real-time latency, memory use, and resource-constrained deployment feasibility were not evaluated.

Article.Title: Decomposing the inequality of tobacco use between upper caste and scheduled caste/tribe men in India, 2005-06 to 2019-21
Article.Authors: Hemram A.; Ghosh P.
Article.Abstract: Tobacco use is significantly high among Indian men belonging to disadvantaged social groups, posing a major public health concern. This study measures inequality in tobacco consumption between Upper Caste (UC) males and socially disadvantaged men, specifically Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) men, from 2005-2006 to 2019–2021 using data from the National Family Health Survey-3, 4, and 5. The study also quantifies the relative contributions of socio-demographic factors, household and community characteristics, and geographical space to this social disparity in tobacco consumption using Fairlie decomposition. Findings show a consistently higher tobacco consumption among SC and ST men, than among UC men; however, the disparity has declined considerably between 2005-2006 and 2019–2021. Key contributors to inequality in tobacco consumption include household wealth, education, occupation, and newspaper exposure. Community-oriented initiatives that address economic disadvantages, provide culturally relevant health education, and enhance addiction prevention, treatment, and cessation through media campaigns are crucial for reducing the burden of tobacco consumption and enhancing the overall well-being of socially marginalized populations.

Article.Title: Context-aware intelligent colour design via multi-objective optimisation and vision–language models
Article.Authors: Liu F.
Article.Abstract: Selecting a colour palette that suits its design context (application domain, audience, and accessibility profile) affects usability, engagement, and accessibility, yet remains a difficult computational problem. Vision–language models (VLMs) have improved performance on this task but share three limitations: deterministic outputs cannot represent the variance inherent in a design brief, single-scalar training fixes the harmony–accessibility trade-off at training time, and post-hoc context filtering leaves the generator itself context-blind. We argue that these limitations stem from the output representation rather than the encoder. CAIM (Context-Aware Intelligent palette Modelling) represents palettes as a context-conditional Gaussian mixture in CIELAB whose parameters are predicted from frozen vision–language embeddings by a learned head. It refines sampled candidates under five objectives designed to target distinct and complementary mathematical features with reference-direction-based many-objective optimisation and ranks them with a context-conditioned selection rule. On four public datasets and a 3200-scenario context-rich dataset, CAIM achieves up to 23% higher predicted ratings than the strongest baseline, a 22-percentage-point gain in APCA readability over the strongest baseline, and a Pareto hypervolume 34% larger than the convex hull of baseline solutions, at 1.6 s per scenario. Modelling VLM-conditioned generation as a context-conditional distribution is promising for design tasks with inherently uncertain outputs.

Article.Title: A tumor purity-based gene signature predicts prognosis and shapes the immune microenvironment in PAAD
Article.Authors: Ma L.; Ji Z.; Zhu L.; Wang Y.; Liu S.; Xin J.; Li B.; Zhao J.; Wang X.; Liu R.
Article.Abstract: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PAAD) is characterized by extreme lethality and a dense stroma that masks tumor-intrinsic biology. Tumor purity—the proportion of malignant cells within tumor tissue—shapes both transcriptomic signals and therapeutic response, yet purity-driven molecular programs in PAAD remain poorly defined. Using TCGA bulk RNA-seq and single-cell RNA-seq dataset GSE155698, we identified purity-associated genes and constructed a prognostic model via differential expression, LASSO, and multivariate Cox regression. Predictive performance was assessed through Kaplan–Meier, ROC, and independent prognostic analyses. Cell–cell communication was used to characterize immune interactions within the tumor microenvironment. Protein-level expression was validated by IHC and multiplex IHC in an independent cohort ( n = 110). A three-gene signature (AMH, PHACTR1, C5AR2) stratified PAAD patients into risk groups with significantly different survival. AMH and PHACTR1 were associated with favorable prognosis, whereas C5AR2 predicted poor outcome. Integration with single-cell data revealed that low-risk tumors exhibited enhanced antigen presentation and stronger CD8⁺ T-cell activation, implicating tumor purity in shaping immune surveillance. Protein validation confirmed consistent expression patterns in clinical samples. We identify a tumor purity–linked three-gene signature that robustly predicts patient survival and reveals an immune modulating axis involving CD8⁺ T-cell activation. These biomarkers provide mechanistic insight into how tumor purity influences PAAD progression and may guide personalized therapy.

Article.Title: Green infrastructure investment prioritization for urban ecosystem services and resilience: a decision-support framework
Article.Authors: Ayyildiz E.; Sasmazturk B.; Karaca T.; Yalcin Kavus B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Green infrastructure (GI) investments are increasingly promoted as nature-based solutions that generate multiple ecosystem services and contribute to human well-being, climate adaptation, and urban resilience. However, prioritizing GI alternatives is a complex decision problem because different options provide diverse regulating, maintenance/habitat-related, cultural, ecological, technical, and socio-economic benefits under uncertainty. To provide a systematic ecosystem services basis, this study uses the Common International Classification of Ecosystem Services (CICES) as a guiding reference for screening the potential contributions of urban GI alternatives to human well-being. In particular, GI alternatives can be understood as ecosystem service bundles, where interactions and potential synergies among water regulation, biodiversity support, urban cooling, recreation, and public well-being shape their overall contribution to ecosystem management. To address this challenge, this study proposes an integrated Multi criteria Decision Aiding (MCDA) framework for prioritizing GI investment alternatives under uncertainty. The proposed framework combines the Modified Delphi approach, Intuitionistic Fuzzy Step-wise Weight Assessment Ratio Analysis (IF-SWARA), and Intuitionistic Fuzzy Multi-Attributive Border Approximation Area Comparison (IF-MABAC). The Modified Delphi approach is used to validate the criteria and alternatives and consolidate expert judgments, while IF-SWARA determines the relative importance of the evaluation criteria. IF-MABAC is then applied to rank GI investment alternatives. The findings show that Stormwater Management and Flood Mitigation receives the highest criterion weight (0.080), although the overall weight distribution is relatively balanced across the fifteen criteria. Following the IF-MABAC calculation, Constructed Wetlands emerge as the highest-ranked alternative (1.183), followed by Green Walls (0.309), Rain Gardens (0.173), Green Roofs (0.031), and Permeable Pavements (-0.220). Constructed Wetlands show positive relative performance on 12 of the 15 criteria, although trade-offs remain for cost-effectiveness, long-term replacement cost, and technical feasibility. The robustness analyses consistently preserve Constructed Wetlands as the leading alternative, while greater variation is observed among the lower-ranked options. The resulting prioritization is expert-based and context-specific and should therefore be interpreted as conditional on the selected criteria structure, consensus judgments, linguistic scale, and Kayseri planning context. Ultimately, the study contributes to ecosystem services research by offering a CICES-informed, transparent criteria architecture for supporting GI investment decisions rather than a purely methodological innovation.

Article.Title: Pollen and non-pollen palynomorph signals of cultivation-related disturbance in a preservation-limited tropical soil profile, northern Thailand
Article.Authors: Sattraburut T.; Vongvassana S.; Phutthai T.; Thasod Y.
Article.Abstract: This study examined pollen, spores, non-pollen palynomorphs, and associated microremains in a 118-cm tropical soil profile from Sri Nan National Park, northern Thailand, to evaluate depth-wise assemblage patterns and their relationship to surface disturbance. Nineteen subsamples yielded 691 observations, dominated by fungal remains (478; 69.18%), mostly Glomus -type morphotypes. Indeterminate morphotypes accounted for 95 observations (13.75%), helminth eggs for 53 (7.67%), and testate amoebae for 21 (3.04%). Terrestrial pollen was sparse, with only 25 grains recorded across the profile. The highest sample-level counts occurred in the upper sampled depths, which contained most helminth eggs and testate amoebae and all recorded spores, freshwater algal remains, rotifer remains, and indeterminate morphotypes, whereas several middle and lower samples yielded few or no remains. The upper assemblage is consistent with a disturbed terrestrial surface and, together with field observations and regional land-use evidence, is compatible with cultivation-related disturbance. However, the recovered proxies do not independently identify a specific crop or management practice. The absence of independent chronology, low terrestrial pollen recovery, and discontinuous recovery restrict interpretation to depth-wise patterns rather than a temporally resolved environmental history.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: testate amoebae; helminth eggs; non-pollen palynomorphs; fungal spores; land use history

Article.Title: Fourier multiscale analysis of bilateral breast asymmetry associated with breast cancer
Article.Authors: Heine J.; Fowler E.; Egan K.; Weinfurtner R.; Balagurunathan Y.; Schabath M.
Article.Abstract: A substantial body of evidence demonstrates that mammographic measurements are associated with breast cancer. Because left and right breasts typically exhibit similar parenchymal patterns, measurable departures from bilateral symmetry may capture localized lesions and broader parenchymal alterations associated with breast cancer. In this matched case–control study (n = 368 pairs), women with mammograms acquired approximately at the time of diagnosis were analyzed. The objective is to investigate bilateral breast asymmetry as a measure associated with breast cancer. Specifically, contralateral breast images were compared with measures derived in the Fourier domain; this technique summarizes power in concentric radial bands that cover the Fourier plane. Equivalently, this approach can be described as a multiscale characterization of the image. The summarized power difference between respective contralateral bands produces a bilateral asymmetry measure (ASM). Full field digital mammography (FFDM) and synthetic two-dimensional images from digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) were investigated for women that had both types of mammograms acquired at the same time. Conditional logistic regression modeling was used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) for the ASM in per standard deviation increment and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curves (Azs) with 95% confidence intervals; models included body mass index and ethnicity as controlling variables. Raw FFDM mammograms (70 µm pixel spacing) produced significant findings: OR 1.90 (1.58, 2.29) and Az = 0.72 (0.67, 0.76). Associations were significant but attenuated for both clinical FFDM (70 µm pixel spacing) and DBT mammograms (pixel spacing ranging from 90 to 110 µm): OR 1.31 (1.11, 1.54) and Az = 0.63 (0.58, 0.67); and OR 1.48 (1.25, 1.76) and Az = 0.65 (0.60, 0.70), respectively. Clinical FFDM and DBT images were inferior to raw FFDM images for capturing bilateral breast asymmetry. DBT images have lower spatial resolution than clinical FFDM images but produced stronger associations. These findings provide strong support for investigating this bilateral ASM as a component in early detection modeling outside of the case–control setting.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: full-field digital mammography; digital breast tomosynthesis; breast cancer; mammography; breast cancer early detection; breast parenchyma; spatial resolution

Article.Title: From wind-solar accommodation to potential coal-generation displacement: spatial coordination and operational CO2 mitigation in China’s power system
Article.Authors: Chi Y.; Zheng Y.; Zhang Y.; Zhang X.
Article.Abstract: Wind-solar accommodation does not necessarily yield equivalent reductions in coal generation or emissions. Using 2022 hourly output for 2880 county-level units, 8760-h loads for 31 provinces and data for 2985 coal units or project phases, we compare provincial self-accommodation, neighboring-province pairing, nationwide pairing and national aggregation. Absolute coal-generation displacement is measured against a constructed common reference excluding studied wind-solar generation under unchanged demand and resources: a model counterfactual, not observed 2022 dispatch. Under the benchmark assumptions, nationwide pairing increases direct accommodation by 310.59 TWh (39.04%), coal-generation displacement by 285.98 TWh (47.61%) and operational CO₂ mitigation by 250.36 Mt (41.29%) relative to provincial self-accommodation. Renewable supply, coal conversion and displaced emission intensity contribute 191.39, 90.66 and − 31.69 Mt, respectively. Although nationwide pairing and national aggregation both directly accommodate approximately 1106.15 TWh, aggregation displaces another 144.58 TWh of coal generation and avoids another 127.79 Mt of CO 2 . Additional sensitivity tests retain positive coordination benefits but show substantial dependence on matching assumptions, annual reduction allowances and eligible provincial connections. These estimates describe conditional coordination potential under fixed unit emission intensities and unrestricted transfers within coordinated domains. Renewable planning should jointly assess accommodation, access to reducible coal generation and unit-level emission differences.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: China power system; CO2 emission reduction

Article.Title: Structural uncertainty propagation analysis by sensitivity-modification based on second order Taylor series expansion with complex variables
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Uncertainties widely exist in engineering and inevitably affect the mechanical responses of structures. It is therefore necessary to develop an uncertainty analysis model for predicting structural mechanical behaviors. Among uncertainty propagation methods, the Taylor series expansion method is simple and efficient, yet it is not applicable to structural responses with non-monotonicity and strong nonlinearity. To address the significant accuracy degradation of the traditional Taylor series expansion for uncertainty propagation when structural response intervals exhibit strong nonlinearity and contain extreme points, this paper proposes an improved interval analysis method based on second-order Taylor series expansion (MSTEM). In the proposed method, the second-order Taylor series expansion is converted into a parabolic expression, and the locations of approximate stationary points are determined to eliminate the influence of non-monotonicity. On this basis, a sensitivity modification strategy is introduced to improve the prediction accuracy of structural response bounds under strongly nonlinear conditions. To enhance both the accuracy and efficiency of sensitivity computation, the complex-variable formulation of MSTEM is derived. Finally, numerical examples verify the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: second-order Taylor series expansion; strong nonlinearity; interval analysis; critical points; non-monotonicity; complex variable method

Article.Title: Dual-robust unscented Kalman filter for UAV state estimation under simultaneous model and measurement uncertainties
Article.Authors: Liu J.; Zhao X.; Tian J.; Jiao Z.; Wang Y.; Zou X.
Article.Abstract: Accurate position estimation is essential for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), yet conventional filters can degrade when model mismatch and non-Gaussian measurement disturbances occur simultaneously. This study proposes a dual-robust unscented Kalman filter, termed H∞-GMMC-UKF, combining an H∞-motivated prior-covariance modification with a generalized maximum mixture correntropy measurement update. The former improves tolerance to prediction errors caused by model uncertainty, whereas the latter reduces the influence of asymmetric, heavy-tailed, and impulsive measurement errors. The method was evaluated through four progressive simulation scenarios and two EuRoC real-trajectory stress tests using 100 paired Monte Carlo trials with ablation, sensitivity, and statistical diagnostics. Results show that the proposed filter remains competitive under benign conditions and provides its clearest improvement over the standard UKF when model and measurement uncertainties coexist. In the controlled dual-uncertainty simulation, mean position RMSE was reduced by 18.0%, while a 57.3% reduction was obtained in the contaminated EuRoC stress test. Ablation and sensitivity analyses further show that the two robust stages contribute through complementary mechanisms: GMMC directly attenuates contaminated measurements, while the H∞ covariance modification provides an additional prediction-side robustness margin whose effect is most evident in the tested adverse measurement-update settings. These findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed architecture for reliable UAV state estimation under challenging operating conditions.
Article.Topic: Target Tracking and Data Fusion in Sensor Networks

Article.Title: Biocontrol of Trialeurodes vaporariorum by Bacillus velezensis and Bacillus licheniformis through lipopeptide production and induction of tomato defense
Article.Authors: Rahimi-Kaldeh S.; Vahidinasab M.; Salehi Jouzani G.; Ahmadzadeh M.
Article.Abstract: The wide application of chemical pesticides has led to various environmental and human health concerns. Biological control is considered an eco-friendly alternative for pest management. This study evaluated the biocontrol effects of the wild-type strains Bacillus velezensis UTB96 and Bacillus licheniformis NBT-192, as well as the codY deletion strain B. velezensis UTB97, against Trialeurodes vaporariorum . The free-choice preference test showed that bacterial treatments reduced whitefly oviposition, with B. licheniformis NBT-192 causing the greatest reduction (91.65% in 8320 and 83.33% in Early Urbana) compared with the control. In the bioassay, B. licheniformis caused the highest mortality of whitefly nymphs and puparium, reaching 51.33%, which was significantly higher than the other bacterial treatments. Bacterial treatments significantly enhanced plant defense responses, including anthocyanin and phenolic accumulation and peroxidase activity. Peroxidase activity increased from 25.90 in control plants to 44.98 following B. licheniformis treatment, while B. velezensis UTB97 produced the highest anthocyanin concentrations (8.545 and 30.303 in 8320 and Early Urbana, respectively). Phenolic concentrations were highest in B. licheniformis -treated plants, reaching 1.117 and 1.180 in 8320 and Early Urbana, respectively. HPTLC analysis revealed that all three bacterial strains produced surfactin, iturin, and fengycin. B. velezensis UTB96 produced the highest levels of surfactin (129.91 mg/L) and iturin (370.55 mg/L), whereas B. licheniformis produced the highest level of fengycin (188.83 mg/L). Bacterial treatments also significantly increased the uptake of N, P, K, Ca, Mn, Zn, Fe, and B, whereas Mg was not significantly affected. Overall, B. licheniformis NBT-192 showed the highest whitefly mortality and was associated with enhanced peroxidase activity, phenolic accumulation, nutrient uptake, and fengycin production, supporting its potential as a biological control agent against T. vaporariorum .

Article.Title: Patterns of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome stages and prevalence of lifestyle risk factors in a nationally representative iranian population study
Article.Authors: Ataei-Goujani H.; Mirzad M.; Amini M.; Azizpour Y.; Hasanzad M.; Larijani B.
Article.Abstract: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome contributes substantially to mortality and places a substantial burden on healthcare systems. Despite the high prevalence of cardiac, renal, and metabolic disorders in Iran, nationally representative data describing the CKM stage distribution and associated unhealthy lifestyle factors are lacking. We aimed to investigate the national pattern of CKM stages and the prevalence of unhealthy lifestyle behaviors among Iranian adults. This secondary analysis used data from the 2021 STEPS survey. Sociodemographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, and renal, metabolic, and cardiovascular risk indicators were presented across CKM stages (0–4). Geographical variations in stage distribution were also assessed. Categorical variables were presented as weighted percentages with corresponding 95% confidence intervals (CIs). A total of 16,208 participants aged ≥ 25 years were analyzed. Overall, 94.26% of participants met the criteria for CKM stages 1–4, with stage 2 accounting for the largest proportion (65.73%, 95% CI: 64.68, 66.78), followed by stage 1 (13.08%, 95% CI: 12.35, 13.82). Hypertension and metabolic syndrome were the most prevalent cardiometabolic conditions, whereas moderate- to high-risk and very high-risk CKD were the least prevalent. Geographic variations were observed, with northwestern and southwestern provinces showing high stage 3 prevalence but relatively low stage 4 prevalence. Overall, 63.83% (95% CI: 59.74, 67.92) of participants in stage 3 and 57.89% (95% CI: 54.20, 61.58) in stage 4 reported at least two unhealthy lifestyle factors, while 10.19% (95% CI: 7.77, 12.61) and 11.85% (95% CI: 8.98, 14.72), respectively, reported three or more factors. Insufficient fruit and vegetable intake was the most prevalent unhealthy lifestyle factor across all CKM stages. CKM syndrome affects most Iranian adults, predominantly at stage 2. These findings provide descriptive evidence of the national and regional distribution of CKM stages.

Article.Title: Cell-surface expression of the RNA binding protein U5 snRNP200 on acute myeloid leukemia and other tumor cells is independent of FcγR-mediated interactions
Article.Authors: Mons D.; de Jongh R.; Yasuda E.; Grigorova S.; Ñahui Palomino R.; van der Kooi E.; Haverkate N.; Leusen J.; Cragg M.; Li Z.; Kapur R.; Spits H.; Blom B.; Beaumont T.; Vidarsson G.; Hazenberg M.
Article.Abstract: The development of novel immunotherapeutics for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is hampered by the limited knowledge of tumor-expressed targets absent on non-malignant cells. We recently identified the RNA binding protein U5 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein 200 kDa (U5 snRNP200) as a novel antigen that is overexpressed on AML blasts in 50% of cases. As a non-canonical membrane protein lacking a transmembrane domain, a cofactor is required for surface expression. Previous studies suggested the Fc gamma receptor (FcγR) IIa (CD32a) as a cofactor. Here we show that solid tumor cell lines, especially SKOV3 (ovarian carcinoma), express U5 snRNP200 in the absence of FcγRIIa. Moreover, CRISPR-Cas9 induced deletion of FcγRIIa from AML-derived THP-1 cells had no impact on U5 snRNP200 expression. However, binding of the U5 snRNP200 antibodies was enhanced when FcγRII or FcγRI were expressed, suggesting that U5 snRNP200 antibody binding is stabilized by co-binding to FcγR. Antibody binding was markedly reduced using Fab’ or F(ab’) 2 formats, Fc-silent antibodies, FcγR deficient cells, or FcγR-blocking antibodies. Other cell surface expressed RNA-binding proteins are tethered to the membrane via heparan sulfate, and reducing heparan sulfate expression decreased U5 snRNP200 expression. Together, these data demonstrate that cell surface expression of the U5 snRNP200 complex by tumor cells is independent of FcγRIIa co-expression, and suggest that cell surface expressed U5 snRNP200 may be tethered to the tumor membrane by heparan sulfate.

Article.Title: Genetic and circulating inflammatory cytokine signatures for renal cell carcinoma risk: a case-control study from Northwest China
Article.Authors: Zhu K.; Li J.; Xu F.; Zhang Q.
Article.Abstract: Immune responses driven by inflammatory cytokines significantly contribute to the onset and progression of renal cell carcinoma (RCC). This research aimed to explore the association between genetic variants and Serum concentrations of inflammation-related cytokine genes and susceptibility to RCC within a Chinese cohort. A case-control design was employed, enrolling 160 individuals diagnosed with RCC and 280 healthy controls. Genetic variants in inflammation-related cytokine genes were determined using PCR-RFLP. Serum cytokine concentrations were assessed via flow cytometry with fluorescence detection. Serum levels of IL-1β, IL-6, IL-10, IFN-γ, and TNF-α were significantly elevated in RCC patients compared with controls (all P < 0.05; median fold changes: IL-1β 1.6, IL-6 1.9, IL-10 1.4, IFN-γ 1.3, and TNF-α 1.5). After FDR correction, the IL-6 -174 G/C and IL-10 -1082 G/A polymorphisms remained significantly associated with RCC risk (IL-6 -174 CC vs. GG: OR = 2.81, 95% CI 1.52–5.19, q < 0.05; IL-10 -1082 AA vs. GG: OR = 2.12, 95% CI 1.21–3.71, q < 0.05). Associations for IL-1β -511 C/T, IFN-γ + 874 A/T, and TNF-α -308 G/A were suggestive but did not survive FDR correction (nominal P < 0.05, q > = 0.05). These inflammatory factors and their corresponding polymorphisms may serve as potential biomarkers for identifying individuals at risk for RCC and provide new avenues for personalized treatment approaches.

Article.Title: Investigation on the preventive effects of total flavonoids extract from Ziziphi Spinosae Semen on depression and associated liver injury
Article.Authors: Qi M.; Tan J.; Qin F.; Zhang J.; Wang R.; Zhang Y.; Yue X.
Article.Abstract: Ziziphus jujuba Mill. var. spinosa yields the desiccated seeds known as Ziziphi Spinosae Semen (ZSS), a botanical classified in China as medicine-food dual-purpose. For centuries, these seeds have been ingested to relieve insomnia and depression. Their total flavonoid fraction (ZSSF) is now recognized as the key active component that provides sedative-hypnotic, antidepressant, antioxidant, and hepatoprotective benefits. However, its therapeutic efficacy and the underlying mechanism have not been elucidated. In this study, we extracted ZSSF and predicted that the primary action of ZSSF is focused on the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway based on network pharmacology. We further explored the preventive effects of ZSSF and the underlying mechanisms against depression and associated liver injury through in vitro and in vivo experiments. In oleic-acid-challenged HepG2 cultures, ZSSF activated the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, concomitantly lowering AST, ALT, TC, TG, and MDA while elevating SOD, thereby alleviating oxidative stress and liver injury. Furthermore, within a murine paradigm of mood disturbance established through CUMS, ZSSF improved depressive behaviors, increased serum 5-HT levels, and mitigated hepatic steatosis, and oxidative stress. More importantly, Western blotting experiments verified that ZSSF promotes the phosphorylation of PI3K and AKT proteins, thereby regulating the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway to improve depressive symptoms and associated liver injury in CUMS mice. In summary, our results indicate that ZSSF attenuates the development of depression and related liver injury by activating the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, and its antioxidant effects may contribute to the alleviation of oxidative stress and liver injury during the progression of depression.

Article.Title: Optimization of vibration parameters for selective coffee fruit harvesting on the basis of branch energy transfer characteristics
Article.Authors: Yu Y.; Qin Q.; Zhou S.; Liu X.
Article.Abstract: To determine optimal vibration parameters for selective coffee harvesting, the vibration response and energy transfer of a coffee fruit–branch system were analyzed. A forced vibration model of the fruit–pedicel system was established to determine the critical acceleration for mature fruit detachment based on maturity-dependent connection forces. A rigid–flexible coupled dynamic model of the branch–vibrator system was developed by incorporating branch structure and mechanical properties. Single-factor simulations evaluated the effects of frequency, amplitude, and excitation position on kinetic energy transfer. The maximum kinetic energy increased from 0.162 to 0.987 J with increasing amplitude and reached 1.142 J at an excitation position of 47.98 mm. The 60–80 Hz frequency range provided high and controllable energy transfer while satisfying the critical acceleration required for ripe-fruit detachment. A test platform was then used to conduct a quadratic regression orthogonal rotational experiment, with the harvesting rates of ripe, semi-ripe, and unripe fruits as the response variables. Multi-objective optimization yielded optimal parameters of 75.75 Hz, 8.18 mm, and 109.54 mm for frequency, amplitude, and excitation position, respectively. Validation experiments conducted at 75 Hz, 8 mm, and 109 mm yielded harvesting rates of 94.62%, 8.84%, and 6.79% for ripe, semi-ripe, and unripe fruits, respectively, satisfying the predefined requirements. These results provide a theoretical basis for the design and parameter optimization of mechanized coffee harvesting equipment.

Article.Title: Untargeted metabolomics reveals a reproducible signature associated with fatal insulin intoxication
Article.Authors: Elmsjö A.; Söderberg C.; Tamsen F.; Green H.; Kugelberg F.; Ward L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fatal insulin intoxication remains difficult to diagnose because insulin rapidly degrades after death, limiting the reliability of direct biochemical measurements. We hypothesised that insulin excess induces systemic metabolic alterations that persist beyond insulin degradation and can be captured using postmortem metabolomics. High-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS)-based metabolomics was applied to a national cohort (2017–2024), including 51 fatal insulin intoxications and non-insulin deaths for comparison. Orthogonal partial least squares-discriminant analysis (OPLS-DA) models were trained on cases collected between 2017 and 2022. Performance was evaluated using two temporally distinct test sets (2023–2024), a matched validation cohort ( n = 59) and a heterogeneous cohort ( n = 154), with 14 insulin cases included. An insulin-associated metabolomic signature comprising 91 features demonstrated reproducible discrimination. In the matched cohort, insulin intoxication classification achieved 100% sensitivity and 73% specificity. In the heterogeneous cohort, 100% sensitivity was maintained with 72% specificity. No insulin false negatives were observed in either test set. Significant alterations were observed across acylcarnitines, fatty acids/lipids, and purine/nucleoside metabolites. Fatal insulin intoxication is associated with a reproducible metabolomic signature. While not suitable as a confirmatory diagnostic approach, the high sensitivity and absence of false negatives suggests potential utility in supporting exclusion of insulin intoxication in death investigations.

Article.Title: Effects of nectar and sugar on the longevity of the mosquito Anopheles gambiae s.l.
Article.Authors: Cissé-Niambélé K.; Koella J.; Koudou G.
Article.Abstract: Mosquitoes regularly feed on plant nectar, which provides energy for key life-history traits, including longevity. However, the effects of nectar quantity and sugar composition on mosquito longevity remain poorly understood. To address this, we conducted two experiments. First, adult Anopheles gambiae s.l. fed on flowers of Thevetia nerifolia , Malvastrum coromandelianum , Ixora coccinea , and Tabernanthe iboga , or fruit of Carica papaya . We measured sucrose, fructose, and glucose concentrations in nectar and fruit juice, as well as mosquito longevity and sugar meal size. Second, mosquitoes received glucose, sucrose, fructose, or trehalose solutions at two energy concentrations (1.97 or 19.97 kcal per 100 ml), and longevity was monitored. In the first experiment, longevity ranged from 8.2 days on C. papaya to 21.1 days on M. coromandelianum . Interestingly, mosquitoes took larger nectar meals from plant species associated with greater longevity, whereas total sugar concentration had little effect on longevity. In the second experiment, sucrose increased longevity, whereas trehalose reduced it, with mean longevities of 14.1 and 4.8 days, respectively. These findings highlight the potential role of nectar plants in mosquito longevity and suggest that nectar composition, beyond sugar content, may contribute to mosquito survival.

Article.Title: Influence of borehole diameter and attack angle on the flow around a perforated sphere
Article.Authors: Li J.; Wei J.; Lu C.; Yan M.; Lytvynenko D.; Xu P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Motivated by the potential safety hazards posed by cracks in flow around bluff bodies in ocean engineering applications, this study investigates incompressible viscous flow around a sphere containing a central cylindrical bore at Re = 300. The effects of borehole diameter and attack angle on vortex shedding, flow separation, and drag coefficients are systematically explored. Results indicate that at low attack angles, increasing the borehole diameter markedly influences the primary shedding frequency of vortex, thereby modifying their structural characteristics. Moreover, total drag is observed to increase with larger borehole diameters. At elevated attack angles, the borehole diameter affects the initiation of flow separation due to its proximity to the separation point. The impact of attack angle is most significant for larger borehole diameters, where pronounced alterations in both vortex shedding and flow separation are evident. Additionally, the magnitude of the borehole diameter amplifies the influence of the angle of attack on the drag coefficient. Due to the jet-like flow induced by the bore, flow instability around the sphere is intensified when the borehole diameter is sufficiently small. This instability initially escalates with increasing angle of attack, peaking at 45 degrees, and then diminishes as the angle of attack continues to increase.

Article.Title: Model selection in linear mixed-effects analysis of craving outcomes in a randomized controlled trial of medications for opioid use disorders
Article.Authors: Wang K.; Kazemi D.; Wright P.; Raynor P.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: Identifying an appropriate covariance structure is a critical step in modeling longitudinal changes in polysubstance cravings during medications for opioid use disorders (MOUD) treatment. This study analyzed data from the National Drug Abuse Treatment Clinical Trials Network trial CTN0051, in which participants with opioid use disorders (OUDs) were randomized to receive either buprenorphine-naloxone (BUP-NX; n = 287) or extended-release naltrexone (XR-NTX; n = 283). Cravings for opioids, alcohol, stimulants, and nicotine were assessed at baseline and every four weeks over 36 weeks. Repeated-measures linear mixed models (LMMs) were used to examine longitudinal craving trajectories, with treatment, visit, and treatment-by-visit interaction specified as fixed effects and within-participant correlations among repeated observations modeled through the residual (R-side) covariance structure. Ten commonly used covariance structures were compared using Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) and Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) to determine optimal model fit. AIC-based comparisons indicated that the unstructured (UN) covariance structure provided the best fit for alcohol, opioid, and stimulant cravings and the second-best fit for nicotine craving. Using the UN covariance structure, craving scores decreased significantly from baseline across all four craving domains during follow-up. Treatment-by-visit interactions were observed for stimulant craving at selected visits, indicating differences between treatment groups in changes from baseline over time. Baseline alcohol and amphetamine use disorders predicted higher alcohol cravings, while baseline depression, amphetamine, and cocaine use disorders predicted greater stimulant cravings; baseline cocaine use disorder also predicted elevated nicotine craving. In conclusion, the UN covariance structure most effectively captured craving trajectories. These findings identify clinical characteristics associated with differences in reported craving; however, their utility for guiding treatment selection or predicting relapse requires prospective validation. Clinical trial number : NCT02032433.
