Article.Title: InSAR observations from multiple tracks reveal rainfall modulation of post-failure reactivation of the Xiongwadashan landslide
Article.Authors: Zhang L.; Zhang X.; Li J.; Wang Y.; Zhang X.; Huang Y.; Liu X.
Article.Abstract: Large mountain landslides may remain active after major movement, yet the migration of dominant deformation zones, internal post-failure partitioning, and rainfall modulation remain insufficiently understood. We investigate the Xiongwadashan (XW) landslide on the northeastern Tibetan Plateau using Sentinel-1 LOS observations from selected pre- and post-event periods between 2017 and 2025, terrain-constrained three-dimensional displacement estimates for 2022–2024, CHIRPS rainfall data, and field observations. Before the September 2018 event, deformation was concentrated mainly in the middle–lower slope. After failure, the dominant deformation zone shifted to the middle–upper slope and later extended partially downslope toward the middle slope. Movement was dominated by horizontal, near-downslope displacement, with a peak cumulative east–west displacement of ~ 210 mm at XW1-3. Integrated LOS deformation, three-dimensional displacement, time series, and geomorphic evidence delineated high-deformation, transitional, and low-deformation kinematic zones. The high-deformation zone showed stronger displacement increases following concentrated rainfall, while deformation persisted during relatively low-rainfall periods. These results indicate that rainfall mainly modulated stage-wise acceleration rather than controlling long-term activity, and demonstrate the value of integrating temporal deformation-zone migration with internal kinematic zonation for post-failure landslide monitoring.

Article.Title: Shapley-guided token pruning for real-time remote sensing scene classification on edge devices
Article.Authors: Li C.; Zhou T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Vision Transformers (ViTs) excel at remote sensing scene classification, but the quadratic cost of self-attention hinders real-time inference on edge platforms such as on-board satellite and UAV payloads. Token pruning accelerates ViTs, yet mainstream methods rank tokens by attention scores, whose reliability is contested, so aggressive pruning may discard predictively important patches. We instead adopt the axiomatically grounded Shapley contribution as the pruning criterion. To keep its exponential cost out of inference, Shapley values are estimated offline as supervision, and a lightweight head (about 0.10 M parameters) is trained through ranking distillation to reproduce their ranking, so the deployed path performs no Shapley computation; pruning is hierarchical (layers 4/7/10) with a calibrated early-exit recalibrated after pruning. On NWPU-RESISC45 (DeiT-S backbone), the criterion learned by this head follows the offline Shapley ranking more faithfully than attention does (Spearman rho = 0.641 vs. 0.401), with a higher Insertion AUC and a lower Deletion AUC. On a Jetson Orin Nano with TensorRT, latency and per-image energy fall by 24.18% and 32.27% versus the unpruned model. Accuracy at 0.7 retention is 93.04%, 0.53% points above attention pruning; however, with only three paired seeds this comparison is marginal (paired t-test, p = 0.067), and an observed-effect diagnostic power calculation gives only 0.51 at alpha = 0.05. Accordingly, no statistically decisive accuracy improvement is claimed. The contribution is therefore framed as a more faithful pruning criterion and a favourable accuracy-latency trade-off under a single-backbone, single-remote-sensing-benchmark setting, rather than as a general accuracy advantage.

Article.Title: Effect of polypropylene fiber length and content on the wet–dry durability of xanthan gum-stabilized clayey sand: mechanical response and ultrasonic monitoring
Article.Authors: Abbasi F.; Janalizadeh Choobbasti A.; Roushan K.
Article.Abstract: Biopolymer soil stabilization offers environmental benefits, but susceptibility to moisture cycling may limit long-term durability. This study assessed the effect of polypropylene (PP) fiber reinforcement on the wetting–drying (W–D) durability of clayey sand stabilized with 0.25% xanthan gum (XG). Specimens containing 0.4% or 0.8% PP fibers, with lengths of 6–12 mm, were cured for 7 days and exposed to up to six W–D cycles. Degradation was evaluated using cumulative mass loss (CML), relative axial height change, unconfined compressive strength (UCS), and ultrasonic pulse velocity (UPV), while microstructural changes were examined by scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The XG-stabilized specimen without fibers disintegrated about 1 h after initial immersion, whereas adding 0.8% 6-mm fibers extended specimen integrity beyond 280 h. After six W–D cycles, this specimen exhibited a 7.84% wetting-induced height increase, a 2.2% drying-induced height reduction, a CML of 10.3%, and reductions of 62.5% and 88.9% in UCS and UPV, respectively. SEM images showed that fiber bridging and particle retention delayed disintegration. Overall, selecting an appropriate PP fiber length and content can improve the W–D durability of XG-stabilized soils.

Article.Title: Switching thermal cycle modulation and cycle feature fusion for mixed gas concentration prediction
Article.Authors: Wang W.; Xie Y.; Liu W.; Liu Y.; Qian Z.; Gao J.; Ren T.; Zhong L.
Article.Abstract: Accurate prediction of methane and acetylene concentrations supports insulation condition assessment and fault diagnosis in power equipment. Metal oxide semiconductor (MOS) sensors offer compact, low-cost sensing, but cross-sensitivity limits their accuracy in mixed-gas concentration prediction. To improve prediction accuracy while simplifying temperature modulation hardware, a Switching Thermal Cycle Modulation (STCM) device and a Cycle Feature Fusion Network (CFFNet) are developed. STCM uses a timer-based circuit to periodically switch the sensor heaters on and off, producing temperature variations that induce periodic changes in gas response waveforms. CFFNet uses cycle means and fixed cosine projections to represent response intensity and waveform shape, respectively, and a Transformer encoder to model their temporal relationships across cycles during gas exposure and recovery. Performance was evaluated using nested leave-one-batch-out cross-validation on STCM and constant-temperature (CT) datasets, each comprising five acquisition batches. On the STCM dataset, CFFNet achieved mean coefficients of determination (R 2 ) of 0.9973 for methane and 0.9974 for acetylene, outperforming all four baseline models on this metric for both gases. Compared with CT, STCM improved concentration prediction accuracy across all evaluated models, demonstrating the value of modulation-induced response information for distinguishing gas concentrations. Ablation experiments supported the complementary roles of cycle mean and shape features, with cross-cycle temporal modeling providing a greater improvement in methane prediction. These results support combining simplified temperature modulation with cycle feature modeling to improve gas concentration prediction under the evaluated conditions.

Article.Title: Evaluating the real-world accessibility of open-source deep learning models for retinal vessel segmentation in optical coherence tomography angiography
Article.Authors: Liu D.; Torcasso M.; Alonso-Caneiro D.; Untracht G.; Drinkwater J.; Li Q.; Ong E.; Lim J.; Turner A.; Chen F.; Sampson D.
Article.Abstract: Accurate segmentation of retinal vasculature in optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) images underpins disease diagnosis and monitoring. While numerous open-source segmentation algorithms are available, an optimal solution remains elusive. This study evaluates and compares the real-world usability and performance of open-source deep learning-based vessel segmentation models across a diverse dataset comprising healthy and diseased eyes. The selected models are standardised in training and performance settings. Model usability is assessed against a range of software engineering criteria defined by the International Organisation for Standardisation. Performance is evaluated on the publicly available OCTA-500 and ROSE-1 datasets using the Dice coefficient of similarity (Dice) and Intersection over Union (IoU). We show that, within the evaluated sample, considerable variability exists in the quality and usability of open-source models, which may limit the practical integration and adoption of some tools within clinical research workflows. Common shortcomings include incomplete or missing dependency documentation, limited portability across systems, hard-coded file paths, and missing scripts or modules. Among the reviewed models, FRNet most closely met the requirements of international software engineering quality standards. In addition to its strong usability profile, FRNet consistently achieved high Dice and IoU across all evaluated datasets. Beyond identifying a reliable OCTA vessel segmentation model, this study highlights a gap between open-source development practices and their practical use in clinical research. While open-source frameworks support reproducibility and translation, explicit usability and quality criteria are needed to ensure real-world adoption.

Article.Title: Vital sign analysis and correlation of physiological parameters using edge AI and IoT technology
Article.Authors: Manikanta P.; Kumar C.; Chimpineni M.
Article.Abstract: Individuals encounter discomfort in their lifestyle with vital signs and problems that lie in their ability to identify and respond to life-saving situations with advanced health care technologies. Vital signs are essential parameters that provide an early warning of a diagnosis before further deterioration in health. Progress in health care technologies, such as automated health monitoring systems and telehealth systems, which can detect, collect real-time data, and diagnose remotely. The present article aims to measure vital signs such as heart rate (HR), temperature (T), oxygen saturation (SpO 2 ), and blood pressure (BP) using a designed medical device by implementing a quantized Gradient Boosting (GB) model deployed on the ARM Cortex-A72 processor for automated clinical risk stratification. The proposed system was evaluated on two benchmark datasets: The Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care for Emergency Department (MIMIC-IV-ED v2.2) dataset and a real-world clinical dataset. The accuracy of measured parameters was evaluated using parametric statistical analysis of baseline metrics and Gaussian distribution fitting of the recorded data from MIMIC-IV-ED. The (GB) algorithm achieved an accuracy of 99.84%, precision of 99.40%, and attained a lower false positive rate (FPR) of 0.06%. The quantized edge AI (INT8) model, when deployed on the processor, attained a latency of 0.596 ms. Hence, the designed system provides an efficient, low-latency solution for real-time vital sign monitoring and clinical risk-based classification.

Article.Title: Enhancement effect of composite loquat and wolfberry juice on the quality characteristics and antioxidant activity of yogurt
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Yang W.; Zhou D.; Liu X.; Zhao X.; Pang J.
Article.Abstract: Process optimization, quality characteristics evaluation and in vitro antioxidant activity analysis of a novel yogurt enriched with composite loquat-wolfberry juice was systematically carried out in this study. After optimization through single-factor and response surface experiments, an experimentally observed sensory score (81.74) of the compound yogurt was achieved under the conditions of 8% composite raw material juice, 6.27% white sugar and 5.99 h fermentation time, which was close to the predicted maximum value of 79.60 given by the regression equation. Subsequently, the obtained compound yogurt showed significantly better sensory quality, higher titratable acidity, lower pH value, and greater water holding capacity than the plain yogurt. Moreover, the compound yogurt achieved improved apparent viscosity, textural and thixotropic properties. Additionally, the microstructural analysis revealed a denser network structure in the compound yogurt when compared to the plain yogurt. Furthermore, the compound yogurt had stronger in vitro 2,2’-azino-bis(3-ethylbenzothiazoline-6-sulfonic acid) diammonium salt, hydroxyl and 1,1-diphenyl-2-picrylhydrazyl free radical scavenging ability than the plain yogurt at each tested mass concentration. These results demonstrated that the composite loquat-wolfberry juice was an effective food ingredient for improving the quality characteristics and in vitro antioxidant activity of yogurt.

Article.Title: Visitors’ perceptions and demand preferences for cultural ecosystem services in urban parks for sustainable tourism management
Article.Authors: Fan M.; Xiao X.; Zhan X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Urban parks serve as vital public spaces for recreational activities. However, key scientific questions remain regarding how, and to what extent, socio-demographic characteristics influence visitors’ perceptions of different types of cultural ecosystem services (CESs). Two further questions concern how park visitor typologies and their characteristics can be systematically identified, and how the demand preferences of different visitor groups for CESs can be understood. Addressing these questions is essential for urban park tourism management. This study employed a questionnaire survey to analyze visitors’ perceptions of CESs provided by Zhujiang Park in Guangzhou, China. Multiple linear regression was used to examine the influence of socio-demographic factors on perceptions of CESs. Cluster analysis and correspondence analysis were applied to identify visitor typologies and their characteristics. Importance-Performance Analysis (IPA) was used to determine the perceptual preferences of different visitor groups for CESs. The results identified key socio-demographic factors affecting visitors’ perceptions of CESs. For example, while occupation had no significant effect on visitors’ perceptions of CESs, education showed the strongest positive association with the perceived importance of recreation and entertainment. Furthermore, three distinct visitor typologies were identified: individual, social, and family visitors. These groups exhibited significant differences in their demand for inspiration, educational value, recreation and entertainment, and safety. The findings confirm the diverse demand for CESs among urban park visitors and highlight the need for tailored management strategies. They also offer insights for policymakers seeking to foster a more inclusive and equitable park tourism environment in which urban green spaces meet the varied needs of different visitor groups.

Article.Title: Data-driven modeling and optimal compensation of FACTS devices for real-world performance assessment in the Adama-II wind farm
Article.Authors: Teshome A.; Molinas Cabrera M.; Fosso O.; Kahsay M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Wind power systems routinely face power quality challenges due to the stochastic nature of the wind resource. Effective reactive power compensation is therefore essential to ensure grid code compliance and maintain stable operation. This study presents a real-world performance analysis of FACTS devices, specifically Magnetically Controlled Reactor-type Static Var Compensator (MCR-SVCs) installed at the Adama-II Wind Farm in Ethiopia. It introduces TopFlow, a validated Python-based optimization framework for assessing the real-world performance of reactive power support in wind power systems. This model was cross-verified through PandaPower and DIgSILENT PowerFactory and further validated using SCADA data from the operational wind farm. The proposed model was employed to identify the discrete optimal reactive power compensation requirements to ensure compliance with the steady-state voltage limits of 0.95–1.05 p.u. and to validate the compensation threshold practice of the farm. The deployment of MCR-SVCs enhanced bus voltage by up to 1.4% and reduced reactive losses by more than 42.86% compared to the uncompensated operation. Model predictions closely reflected that the compensation threshold of 80 MW was a viable decision. By integrating real operational data with a rigorously validated analytical model, this study offers one of the few empirically grounded assessments of FACTS-based reactive compensation in operational wind power systems. The results confirm the effectiveness of MCR-SVCs in stabilizing wind farm operation and demonstrate the model’s robustness in identifying discrete optimal compensation thresholds and guiding improved grid-support strategies.

Article.Title: Psychological resilience and media-based indirect trauma: evidence from the Kahramanmaraş earthquakes
Article.Authors: Demiröz Yıldırım S.
Article.Abstract: The aim of this study is to investigate the association between psychological resilience and media-related indirect trauma following the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes. This quantitative study utilized a predictive correlational design with a sample of 318 adults aged 18–65 (68.6% female, 31.4% male). The largest proportion of the sample (58.5%) fell within the 18–27 age bracket. Multivariable linear regression analyses showed that the higher age category was independently associated with higher psychological resilience scores (β = 0.272, p < 0.001). Perceived psychological strength against disasters was independently associated with lower media-related indirect trauma scores (β = −0.414, p < 0.001). No significant association was found between total psychological resilience and total media-related indirect trauma scores, although several very weak associations were observed at the sub-dimension level. These findings indicate that psychological resilience and media-related indirect trauma are complex, multidimensional constructs, with specific variables showing independent associations after adjustment for other factors. Given the cross-sectional correlational design, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal or protective effects.

Article.Title: Food-level nutrient-to-price analysis and modelled costs of Thai dietary guideline baskets using prices from selected retail outlets in Bangkok, Thailand
Article.Authors: Boonchoo W.
Article.Abstract: Healthy diets can be difficult to achieve when food budgets are constrained, but food-based dietary guidelines rarely indicate which commonly consumed foods provide more nutrient value for their cost. This study combined market-price data from selected retail outlets in Bangkok, Thailand, with Thai food-composition data to calculate nutrient-to-price values for 283 commonly consumed foods and to model the costs of food baskets based on Thai Food-Based Dietary Guideline serving recommendations. Rice and starches provided the lowest-cost energy and carbohydrate per Baht. Foods ranking highly for selected micronutrients came from a wider range of groups, including legumes, organ meats, blood products, vegetables, and fruits. Base-case Thai FBDG baskets cost 142.63–204.12 THB/day, equivalent to 40.4%–57.8% of the Bangkok minimum daily wage of 353 THB/day. Nutrient-to-price informed practical baskets cost 73.08–95.12 THB/day and reduced modelled costs by 48.8%–53.4% without changing the Thai FBDG food-group serving structure. These estimates show that food-item choice within the same dietary-guideline structure can materially alter modelled basket costs, but they do not establish nutrient adequacy, household acceptability, or implementation feasibility.

Article.Title: An enhanced spotted hyena optimizer-based LSTM framework for accurate DDoS attack detection in internet of things networks
Article.Authors: Nanthiya D.; Manjula Devi R.; Gopal S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The proliferation of IoT devices has made modern networks more vulnerable to Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks, which may overwhelm systems and cause them to crash. Due to the complex structure, enormous volume and ever-changing behavior of IoT-generated network data, conventional detection algorithms often produce too many false alarms and fail to maintain accuracy, making the detection of such attacks very challenging. This paper proposes an integrated strategy of optimization-deep learning for improving detection of distributed denial of service threats in Internet of Things systems. The model includes Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network and Enhanced Spotted Hyena Optimizer (E-SHO) for effective hyperparameter tweaking and feature selection. The revised optimizer is integrated with adaptive control strategies, the Levy flight exploration, the inertia weight adjustment and the opposition-based learning to improve the search process and prevent the premature convergence. While the optimization section adjusts model parameters, the LSTM network learns network data’s temporal patterns. It is tested using CICDDoS2019 and N-BaIoT benchmark datasets. The experimental results showed accuracy of 92.21%, precision of 92.22%, recall of 92.22%, F1-score of 92.22% for CICDDoS2019 Dataset and accuracy of 93.1%, precision of 92.8%, recall of 92.8%, F1-score of 92.9% for N-BaIoT Dataset. It also offers reduced false alarm rates and more stability than previous techniques.

Article.Title: Vaccine handling practices and determinants in immunization centers of Gambella, Ethiopia: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Chilo D.; Dagnew L.
Article.Abstract: Failure to adhere strictly to recommended specifications for vaccine handling and storage can result in reduced vaccine potency at the time of administration and compromise the overall quality of immunization services. This study aimed to assess vaccine handling practices and determinants among immunization centers in the Gambella Region, Southwest Ethiopia. An institution-based cross-sectional study was conducted in 2022. Data were collected from 92 immunization centers using validated questionnaires and on-site observations. Statistical analyses were performed using SPSS version 20, and variables with a p-value < 0.05 were considered statistically significant. Proper vaccine handling practices were observed in 45.7% of immunization centers (95% CI: 37.0%–57.2%). Awareness and use of vaccine handling guidelines were significantly associated with vaccine handling practices (AOR = 6.82, 95% CI: 1.99–23.35). Regular maintenance of temperature monitoring charts was associated with lower odds of improper vaccine handling practices (AOR = 0.11, 95% CI: 0.03–0.36). Similarly, immunization centers with incomplete vaccine stock records had higher odds of improper vaccine handling practices compared with centers that maintained complete stock records (AOR = 0.19, 95% CI: 0.05–0.74). Vaccine handling practices in the Gambella Region were suboptimal and may compromise vaccine effectiveness. Strengthening adherence to vaccine handling guidelines, training, and monitoring systems is recommended to improve vaccine handling practices.

Article.Title: Wood and seagrass fibre-based materials including TPSea on hot sounding rocket structures
Article.Authors: Guenther R.; Hohn O.; Unbehaun H.; Drescher O.; Tajmar M.; Bach C.; Weihs H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In order to assess the applicability of wood- and seagrass-based materials as thermal protection system materials in space, a test with fin leading edges made of two solid woods (oak and mahogany) in the arc-heated wind tunnel L2K was conducted. The requirement analysis enabled the selection of three untreated, native solid woods (birch, oak and larch), and four wood-fibre materials (TPSea-0, -1, -C and I-WBM) for further tests. The materials from the TPSea family are developments of TUD. A more detailed screening of the materials was conducted, encompassing density, thermal conductivity, specific heat capacity, and thermogravimetric analysis. The evaluation of measurements under flight-relevant thermal loads in L2K is conducted through analysis of mass, cross-sectional area, and contour. The findings indicate that untreated solid woods are not a favoured natural material for fin leading edges, owing to substantial mass loss and uneven leading edge geometry degradation. It is evident that wood-fibre materials characterised by enhanced homogeneity, in conjunction with the incorporation of flame retardants and elevated mineral content, exhibit considerable promise with regard to optimisation. Under the single thermal load case and limited replication tested in this screening study, TPSea-C showed the most promising dimensional stability and thermal behaviour among the candidates evaluated. However, none of the investigated bio-based material variants fully meets the defined requirements. Further analyses of TPSea-C could help identify the underlying material-related limitations and provide a basis for targeted optimisation. The work demonstrates the potential of natural fibre-based materials for fin leading edges in the primary structures of sounding rockets on the highest thermally stressed components. The findings of this study offer a foundation for further application of wooden materials in space engineering levelling the path for a bioeconomy in space.

Article.Title: Distributed optimization for transactive energy management in interconnected multi-microgrid systems
Article.Authors: Alsinai A.; Ashfaq R.; Alfaifi B.; Niazi A.; Peters J.; Piqueira J.; Khan S.
Article.Abstract: The rapid proliferation of renewable energy resources, battery energy storage systems (BESSs), and flexible loads has increased the operational complexity of interconnected multi-microgrid systems, creating the urgent need for effective and decentralized energy management strategies. In this context, this paper proposes a framework for Distributed Transactive Energy Management (DTEM), leveraging the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM), aimed at transactive energy transfer to achieve coordinated operation of interconnected microgrids. The proposed framework simultaneously schedules dispatchable generators, battery energy storage systems, flexible loads, and peer-to-peer energy exchange, aiming to minimize the overall operating cost while preserving the operational privacy of individual microgrids through information exchange between neighboring grids. The convex optimization problem is formulated by incorporating generation costs, battery degradation costs, energy trading costs, and the utility associated with flexible loads, together with operational and grid constraints. This optimization problem is decomposed into independent local sub-problems, enabling each microgrid to determine its operating schedule without the need for a centralized coordinator. Furthermore, the convergence of the distributed algorithm to the optimal solution is demonstrated under standard convex optimization assumptions. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed DTEM framework effectively coordinates distributed energy resources, improves resource utilization, reduces reliance on utility-grid energy, and reduces the total operating cost while satisfying all operational constraints. These results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed approach as a scalable, computationally efficient, and privacy-preserving solution for distributed energy management in interconnected multi-microgrid systems.

Article.Title: Development of cinnarizine nanoemulsion for enhanced topical delivery with ex vivo permeation and in vivo pharmacodynamic evaluation
Article.Authors: Al-Hamwi R.; Zrir M.; El-Zein H.
Article.Abstract: Despite widespread clinical use for vertigo, cinnarizine (CIN) suffers from poor water solubility and unpredictable absorption, limiting its oral bioavailability to approximately 8% when given in liquid dosage forms. We hypothesized that formulating CIN as a nanoemulsion (NE) could enhance skin permeability and enable effective topical delivery for allergic skin conditions, as CIN exhibits antihistamine activity. In this work, we prepared a novel CIN‐NE using low-energy emulsification method. Nanoemulsions were characterized for various parameters, including transmittance, viscosity, refractive index, pH, drug content, mean droplet size, Zeta potential, in vitro drug release, and ex vivo drug permeation. The optimum formula (F19) (30% Smixd of 2:1 with 1% oil) exhibited small nanodroplets (down to 82.03 nm) with a Zeta potential of −16.1 mV and good physical stability in the thermodynamic stability study, which was further formulated as a nanoemulgel to facilitate application. The ex vivo permeation study, using rat skin as a model, showed that NE-F19 and NE-Gel-F19 increased permeability 16- and 5-fold compared with the control, respectively. Additionally, in the in vivo an‐hypersensitivity study, NE-F19 and NE-Gel-F19 effectively suppressed swelling and inflammatory responses.

Article.Title: Genomic changes revealed by repeated sampling of kelp exposed to an extreme marine heatwave
Article.Authors: Edgeloe J.; Wernberg T.; Starko S.; Wood G.; Minne A.; Vranken S.; Wheeler D.; Batley J.; Coleman M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Extreme climatic events are increasingly recognised as potent evolutionary forces, imposing sudden pressures on natural populations. Among these, marine heatwaves (MHWs) are major drivers of ecological change, causing mass mortality, range shifts, and community reorganisation, particularly in habitat-forming kelps. While their ecological impacts are well documented, the genomic consequences remain less clear. Specifically, MHWs can not only induce demographic bottlenecks but also potentially drive selection on loci associated with thermal tolerance, shifting allele frequencies in affected populations. Here, we leveraged historical samples to investigate temporal genetic changes in the kelp Ecklonia radiata (order Laminariales) at three locations in Western Australia over 16 years, spanning the severe 2011 MHW. Overall genetic diversity and composition remained largely stable before (2006, 2008) and after (2012, 2018, 2022) the event, likely reflecting population resilience. However, a subset of loci, including known temperature-associated loci, showed shifts in allele frequencies following the event. Moreover, the strongest and most numerous changes occurred at warmer, lower-latitude sites where ecological impacts of the MHW were greatest, potentially consistent with MHW-driven natural selection. These results demonstrate that MHWs, while not dramatically altering genome-wide diversity, may alter allele frequences at specific loci linked to thermal response, highlighting their role as episodic yet powerful drivers of evolutionary change in marine foundation species.

Article.Title: Metagenomic parasite detection trap: prevention with an Excel filter sheet based on CIGAR values
Article.Authors: Lee F.; Md Yusuf N.; Mohd Khalid M.
Article.Abstract: False positive mapping in metagenomic microbial detection is an underestimated and under-explored concern. It is more critical among parasites than among bacteria and viruses in metagenomic samples. We created an Excel filter sheet to minimize false mapping for metagenomic parasites, based on ratios of the first and last values of S, H and M in the CIGAR string retrieved from Minimap2 mapping. By applying a filter of S/M < 0.3, 88% to 95% of reads ‘mapped’ to ten pathogenic reference parasite sequences were eliminated from the Oxford Nanopore Sequencing data of three macaque stool samples. CZID annotation of the remaining reads detected Entamoeba , Cyclospora , Toxoplasma and Giardia . The majority of the eliminated ‘mapped’ parasite reads were bacteria. The sensitivity of the Minimap2 – S/M < 0.3 filter is between 56.12% and 74.92% for the metagenomic data, and 86% (43/50) for 50 randomly downloaded annotated parasite sequences from NCBI. Our Excel filter sheet provides a temporary solution for false positive mapping in metagenomic parasite detection. We advocate tools that would automate read filtration for metagenomic parasite detection based on the principle reported herein, so that workers unbeknownst to this false positive trap could avoid misinformed downstream analysis and public health interventions.

Article.Title: Feasibility and safety of stand-alone stent retriever thrombectomy for acute embolic mesenteric ischemia in a canine model
Article.Authors: Zhou Y.; Gan S.; Yuan Y.; Zhao B.; Gong M.; Kong J.; Su H.; Gu J.; Shi Y.
Article.Abstract: This pilot study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of stent retriever thrombectomy for arterial embolic acute mesenteric ischemia (AEAMI) in a canine model. The AEAMI model was created in 10 beagles by transcatheter administration of autologous thrombus into the superior mesenteric artery (SMA). Follow-up angiography was performed 2 h after thrombus administration to assess the model stability. SMA recanalization was graded with the thrombectomy in visceral ischemia (TIVI) score, which ranges from 0 to 4. Clinical success was defined as a TIVI score of 3 or 4. Procedure-related complications and vessel injuries were recorded. The AEAMI model was successfully established in all canines and remained stable at 2-hour follow-up angiography. After a mean treatment time of 45.5 ± 19.0 min, the mean TIVI score significantly increased after stent retriever thrombectomy (0.5 ± 0.7 vs. 3.1 ± 1.0, p < .001). Clinical success was achieved in 8 (80%) canines. Mild vasospasm and new distal branch embolization occurred in 4 (40%) and 1 (10%) canines, respectively. No other procedure-related complications or histologically evident vessel injuries were observed. Stent retriever thrombectomy with the Solitaire FR device achieved rapid recanalization with few complications in this canine AEAMI model. With device optimization and further validation, this approach may represent a promising endovascular revascularization technique for AEAMI.

Article.Title: Comparative evaluation of two automated magnetic-bead cfDNA extraction workflows in early colorectal cancer
Article.Authors: Denninghoff V.; Aznar-Peralta I.; Fresno C.; Mellado-Cuesta Á.; Innamorato S.; Molina-Vallejos M.; López-Hidalgo J.; Serrano M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reliable plasma cell-free DNA extraction is a key component of liquid biopsy testing and requires standardized preanalytical workflows. We conducted a paired comparison of 2 automated extraction methods, the Maxwell RSC ccfDNA LV Plasma Kit and the Maxwell RSC Rapid ccfDNA Kit, using EDTA plasma samples from 48 patients with early-stage colorectal cancer. For each patient, 4 mL of plasma was divided into two 2 mL aliquots and processed on the same instrument according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Cell-free DNA was measured by fluorometry and capillary electrophoresis, and outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models with extraction kit as a fixed effect and patient as a random intercept. Measurements obtained by the two analytical platforms were strongly correlated. Compared with the Standard workflow, the Rapid workflow showed significantly higher values across all evaluated concentration and fragment-distribution endpoints, including total DNA concentration and fragment recovery in the 50–700 bp and 100–300 bp ranges. In this early-stage colorectal cancer cohort, the Rapid workflow showed higher cfDNA recovery and a greater representation of fragments within the evaluated cfDNA size ranges than the Standard workflow. These findings are limited to upstream extraction and quality-control metrics and do not establish improved mutation detection, analytical sensitivity, or suitability for downstream molecular assays. The findings indicate that this simplified workflow may be a practical alternative for routine plasma cell-free DNA extraction, although local analytical verification remains advisable.

Article.Title: Automated facial analysis for working dog fatigue assessment
Article.Authors: Oren D.; Lazebnik T.; Martvel G.; Grinstein D.; Michaeli Y.; Elazar O.; Cohen Y.; Zamansky A.
Article.Abstract: Working dogs perform safety-critical tasks, yet field fatigue assessment relies on subjective handler observation or invasive, impractical instrumentation. We present a non-invasive, video-only framework that extracts 46 anatomically grounded (DogFACS-based) facial landmarks from short recordings and produces fatigue assessment. Unlike wearable physiological monitoring, it attaches nothing to the animal; unlike manual DogFACS coding, it is automated and scalable; and unlike raw-video deep learning, it uses a compact, interpretable representation robust to coat color and lighting and suited to small field datasets. Landmark trajectories were classified by a nested model-selection pipeline spanning tree-based models and deep sequence models. On 177 videos from four working dogs recorded under field conditions, the pipeline reached mean F1-scores of 0.781 for tree-based models and 0.789 for neural-network models in dog-specific nested cross-validation, and 0.676 and 0.740, respectively, under nested leave-one-dog-out validation. We also introduce a dog-specific Relative Facial-State Index, giving strong held-out before–after discrimination in three dogs, and a mouth-motion analysis whose aperture-magnitude features discriminated within all four dogs. To our knowledge, this is the first automated facial-landmark approach to working-dog fatigue assessment under operational conditions, motivating validation in larger, more diverse cohorts.

Article.Title: Tangeretin ameliorates osteoarthritis and suppresses synovial macrophage M1 polarization in association with suppression of NF-κB signaling
Article.Authors: Liu S.; Tang J.; Liu J.; Dai Y.; Ding Y.; Yang H.; Liu W.
Article.Abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic, degenerative joint disease that carries significant economic and clinical impacts. M1 polarization of synovial macrophages exacerbates synovitis progression, and thus, targeting M1 macrophage inhibition emerges as a promising therapeutic strategy for OA. Although Tangeretin exhibits anti-inflammatory properties, its impact on OA and the associated mechanisms remain unelucidated. Techniques such as in vitro ELISA, Western blot analysis, and immunofluorescence staining were employed to assess Tangeretin’s influence on macrophage M1 polarization and chondrocyte metabolism. Conversely, histopathological analysis and immunohistochemical staining were utilized to evaluate Tangeretin’s in vivo therapeutic effects on synovial inflammation and cartilage degeneration. Tangeretin was found to inhibit IL-1β-mediated secretion of inflammatory mediators and mitigate ECM degradation in chondrocytes. Additionally, attenuation of M1 macrophage polarization by Tangeretin was accompanied by suppression of the NF-κB signaling. Furthermore, Tangeretin decreased IL-1β and MMP13 levels in the conditioned medium of M1 macrophages, consequently enhancing glycosaminoglycan (GAG) synthesis in chondrocytes. In vivo, Tangeretin alleviated iodoacetic acid-induced cartilage degeneration and M1 macrophage polarization in the synovium. These findings indicate that Tangeretin inhibits OA progression by suppressing M1 macrophage polarization in association with suppression of NF-κB signaling pathway, suggesting its potential as an effective OA treatment.

Article.Title: Stem cell secretome-enriched hydrogels as a potential therapeutic approach for osteoarthritis
Article.Authors: Casado-Santos A.; Vilariño-Feltrer G.; González-Rodríguez Y.; González-Cubero E.; González-Fernández M.; Villar-Suárez V.
Article.Abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic degenerative joint disease characterized by progressive cartilage loss and synovial inflammation, for which current therapies are mainly symptomatic and fail to durably modify disease progression. Hyaluronic acid (HA) and chondroitin sulfate (CS) are widely used in viscosupplementation, but the rapid clearance of HA and limited bioactivity of simple mixtures restrict their long‑term benefit. In parallel, adipose‑derived mesenchymal stromal cell (ASC) secretome has emerged as a promising cell‑free therapeutic due to its pleiotropic anti‑inflammatory and regenerative actions. Here, we evaluated an injectable SH-HA-g-CS hydrogel as a sustained-delivery platform for the ASC-derived secretome and compared its biological performance with the corresponding soluble formulations in an in vitro model of OA. The ASC-derived conditioned medium (secretome) was characterized by nanoparticle tracking analysis (NTA) and LC-MS/MS proteomics. Human chondrocytes were treated with soluble HA, CS, HA + CS, ASC-derived secretome, SH-HA-g-CS hydrogel or SH-HA-g-CS loaded with secretome (2:1 hydrogel: secretome, v/v) under basal and TNF/IFN-γ-induced inflammatory conditions. Cell metabolic activity, wound closure, gene expression and multiplex proteomic profiles were subsequently evaluated. In the inflammatory model, soluble HA + CS and ASC-derived secretome preserved metabolic activity, supported wound closure, and reduced IL1A and IL6 gene expression, with the secretome producing the lowest expression levels of both cytokines. Multiplex proteomic analysis showed that HA + CS and ASC-derived secretome were associated with lower levels of several pro-inflammatory mediators, whereas the secretome-loaded SH-HA-g-CS hydrogel showed lower recovered levels of several pro-inflammatory mediators than the unloaded hydrogel at Day 14. The ASC-derived secretome-loaded SH-HA-g-CS hydrogel showed the potential to provide sustained immunomodulatory effects while maintaining good cytocompatibility, supporting its further development as a cell-free therapeutic strategy for osteoarthritis. Further in vivo studies are required to confirm its therapeutic efficacy and translational potential.

Article.Title: Experimental study on performance and durability of Guangzhou soft soil solidified by a new slag-fly ash based cementitious material
Article.Authors: Huang J.; Liang Z.; Yang F.; Huang H.; Wu L.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: The development of sustainable alternatives to Portland cement for soft soil stabilization is of great significance for reducing carbon emissions and enhancing infrastructure longevity. This study investigates a one-part slag-fly ash geopolymer binder containing solid sodium silicate for stabilizing Guangzhou soft clay. The optimal mix proportion was a slag-to-fly ash ratio of 90:10, a solid activator dosage of 14% relative to the precursor mass, and a water-to-binder ratio of 0.6, achieving a 28-day compressive strength of 2.01 MPa, 14.9% higher than the pure slag system. After 25 wetting-drying cycles, the geopolymer showed a strength loss of 6.5%, compared with 31.2% for cement. After 100 freeze-thaw cycles, the losses were 34.8% and 36.5%, respectively. After 100 days of sulfate immersion, the losses were 32.3% and 44.2%. Under the coupled sulfate immersion-drying-freeze-thaw protocol, the geopolymer remained intact after 100 cycles with a 47.3% strength loss, whereas the cement-treated soil disintegrated. SEM showed qualitative differences in apparent matrix continuity, visible voids, and particle morphology among the mixtures; morphology alone did not establish phase identity or a definitive damage mechanism. The results indicate that this one-part binder can improve the measured strength and durability of Guangzhou soft clay under the tested conditions.

Article.Title: Multi-objective incremental path planning with learning-guided sampling and heading-constrained expansion for autonomous vehicles in dynamic occupancy grid environments
Article.Authors: Du Y.; Liu X.; Bu P.; Li J.
Article.Abstract: Path planning for autonomous vehicles in dynamic grid environments must balance reliability, efficiency, smoothness, safety, and rapid recovery after map changes. We propose LKSD-PRRT*, a modular framework built on APF-PRRT* that integrates learning-guided sampling (LG), multi-objective incremental rewiring (KMO), three-stage smoothing (SMO), and dynamic path repair (DPR). The contribution is a modular integration of learned sampling, Pareto-aware rewiring, geometrically screened smoothing, and tree-based repair, evaluated through ablations and external comparisons. LG combines a baseline-trained heatmap, geometric priors, and random exploration; KMO evaluates path length, curvature, an energy-consumption proxy, and obstacle safety during rewiring; SMO improves geometric continuity with collision checks and quality screening; and DPR reuses valid tree structures after local map updates. In independent-test static ablations (90 runs per configuration), the complete static method achieved a 100% planning success rate and, relative to APF-PRRT*, reduced path length, arc-length mean absolute curvature, and total turning angle by 4.88%, 46.44%, and 49.04%, respectively. Pure search time also increased by 260.31%. In dynamic tests, adding DPR to the LG+KMO backbone increased dynamic path validity from 84.44 to 93.33% and reduced mean recovery time and full task life-cycle time by 77.25% and 71.50%, respectively. The framework provides an interpretable trade-off among path quality, safety, and dynamic responsiveness in two-dimensional geometric planning. Complete static planning averaged 0.2640 s. Vehicle dynamics and closed-loop tracking remain untested.

Article.Title: Discrete element analysis of deformation and failure mechanism and influencing factors of anti-dip rock slope
Article.Authors: Lan F.; Lei G.; Wang X.; Long Y.; Deng L.; Hu Q.; Nan G.; Liu K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The safety problems of anti-dip layered rock slopes are widely encountered in mines, highway slopes and other aspects. Due to the lack of understanding of the deformation characteristics and evolution mechanisms of such slopes, these engineering problems have arisen. This study uses the numerical simulation software PFC 2D to conduct numerical simulation analysis on a layered anti-dip rock slope in soft rock. This study uses the numerical simulation software PFC 2D to conduct numerical simulation analysis on a layered anti-dip soft rock slope. The deformation mechanism of the anti-dip layered soft rock slope is studied from three aspects: slope rock layer thickness, rock layer dip angle, and bedding shear strength. Furthermore, the stress evolution and displacement evolution of the slope are analyzed. The research results show that as the dip angle and thickness of the rock strata increase, the overall failure mode of the slope gradually changes from sliding to toppling, and during the deformation process, the upper part of the slope is subjected to tension, while the lower part is subjected to compression. The deformation of the anti-dip layered slope begins at the top of the slope, and then failure begins at the toe. The failure depth of the anti-dipping layered rock slope gradually increases with the increase of the rock stratum dip angle. The lower the stratum strength, the greater the degree of slope collapse deformation. Both horizontal and vertical stresses at the leading edge of the slope gradually increase with time, then tend to stabilize. Tensile stress appears in the horizontal direction in the later stages of slope deformation at the leading edge. Tensile stress exists on the surface of the trailing edge during deformation and failure, while compressive stress dominates at deeper levels. The stress level at deeper levels is higher than that at the surface. The displacements at both the leading and trailing edges generally increase gradually with time. Surface displacements at both the leading and trailing edges are greater than those at deeper levels. The closer the slope is to the free face during deformation, the more likely it is to experience displacement.

Article.Title: Performance analysis of a DSO-optimized fuel cell-fed DSTATCOM with high-gain boost converter for power quality enhancement
Article.Authors: Choudhury N.; Dash S.; Rajasekar N.; Mohanty S.; Chudjuarjeen S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The increase in the usage of nonlinear loads and highly sensitive industrial machinery has called for an effective design of power quality improvement apparatus which guarantees reliable output. An innovative design of an advanced three-phase distribution static compensator (DSTATCOM) topology is presented in this paper to fulfil the dual objective of providing reactive power support and reduction of current harmonics in the grid-connected system. Two distinct high-gain DC–DC converters are suggested as power sources to feed the DC-bus of the DSTATCOM; namely, floating interleaved boost converter (FIBC) and quadratic high gain boost converter (QHGBC). High gain can be achieved by the FIBC while reducing the input current ripples by employing a method called interleaving which utilizes the concept of interconnecting two boost converters in series on a single magnetic core hence protecting the source from high-frequency interference. The QHGBC, on the other hand, achieves the step-up ratio using a switched inductor-capacitor topology where two converters are interconnected in cascade form, resulting in quadratic voltage gain hence a smaller duty cycle needed to achieve the step-up ratio unlike that of the conventional topology. For proper synchronization of the DSTATCOM to the distorted supply voltage, a dual second order generalized integrator phase locked loop (DSOGI-PLL) is applied and controlled with a third order loop filter. DC-bus voltage level control is accomplished using a Fuzzy control strategy where Dolphin Swarm Optimisation (DSO) is used to obtain optimized control parameters. Tuning of the parameters was done using the integral transient time index. The simulation analysis of DSTATCOM with fuel cell source shows that the designed controller has been able to reduce the current distortion in the source from 26.01 to 2.19% with nonlinear RL load and from 31.84 to 2.83% with nonlinear RC load, which meets the IEEE-519 guidelines. Moreover, the optimal controller is capable of controlling the DC-link voltage to 700 V in 0.1 s with no overshoot. For the realtime performance analysis, a lab scale prototype with an emulated fuel cell DC input is developed in the laboratory. The experimental results are analyzed and the efficacy has been achieved by the proposed controller.

Article.Title: EdgeNetTF for lightweight time frequency representation learning in multiclass sEMG hand gesture recognition
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Kim J.; Choi S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Surface electromyography (sEMG)-based hand gesture recognition plays a critical role in human-machine interaction, rehabilitation, and myoelectric control. However, many deep learning models improve recognition performance by increasing architectural complexity, which limits their suitability for wearable and resource-constrained applications. This study proposes EdgeNetTF, a lightweight time-frequency representation-learning model for multi-class sEMG hand-gesture recognition. EdgeNetTF employs two compact one-dimensional convolutional branches to learn complementary temporal and fast Fourier transform (FFT)-based spectral representations, followed by feature concatenation and a lightweight classification module. Experiments were conducted on the NinaPro DB2 dataset using data from 40 subjects and 49 non-rest hand gestures under a repetition-based within-subject evaluation protocol. Repetitions 1, 3, 4, and 6 were used for training, whereas repetitions 2 and 5 were reserved for testing. With causal majority voting over five consecutive predictions, EdgeNetTF achieved a Causal5 accuracy of 87.01% ± 4.30% and a macro-F1 score of 87.41% ± 3.94% under the primary within-subject protocol while requiring only 0.1891 million trainable parameters and approximately 70.01 million FLOPs. Additional cross-subject and external-dataset evaluations revealed substantial inter-subject variability, indicating that subject-independent generalization remains challenging. Overall, the results support lightweight time-frequency representation learning as a computationally efficient approach to multi-class sEMG recognition, while highlighting the need for improved generalization across subjects and populations.

Article.Title: Investigating the effects of dexmedetomidine in cecal ligation and puncture‑induced septic rats
Article.Authors: Fakirullahoğlu M.; Tanyeli A.; Eraslan E.; Akdemir F.; Çelebi D.; Çelebi Ö.; Kalaycı S.; Özkaraca M.; Eser G.; Güler M.
Article.Abstract: Sepsis is a leading cause of mortality, and ferroptosis has been implicated in sepsis-associated organ injury. Dexmedetomidine (DEX), an α2-adrenergic agonist with anti-inflammatory properties, may modulate this process. We examined whether DEX protects against cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)– induced septic lung injury and alters ferroptosis-associated markers in rats. Thirty-two female Wistar rats were randomized to sham, CLP, and CLP pretreated with DEX (30–50 µg/kg, intraperitoneally, 30 min before CLP) groups ( n = 8 each) and euthanized 16 h after surgery. Lung injury was assessed histopathologically; ferroptosis and inflammation were evaluated by serum ELISA (MDA, ferritin, ACSL4, HO-1, IL-18, SLC7A11), immunohistochemistry (GPX4, TFRC), and immunofluorescence (AQP5, IL-1β). CLP produced severe lung injury, increased MDA, ferritin, ACSL4, HO-1, IL-18, TFRC, and IL-1β, and decreased SLC7A11, GPX4, and AQP5. DEX attenuated histopathological injury, with an ordered dose trend for the primary outcome (interstitial pneumonia; p < 0.001), and shifted these biomarkers toward sham; serum markers differed between doses, and normalization remained partial. These findings indicate that DEX mitigates CLP-induced lung injury, associated with reduced lipid peroxidation, iron-handling, and inflammatory markers, and partial restoration of SLC7A11 and GPX4; whether ferroptosis inhibition mediates this protection requires confirmation with ferroptosis inhibitors and inducers.

Article.Title: Lipid droplet occurrence in human leukocytes of peripheral blood is higher in males with recent-onset psychosis
Article.Authors: Vidal-Domènech F.; Ferrer-Quintero M.; Ochoa S.; Almodóvar-Payá C.; Fatjó-Vilas M.; Pomarol-Clotet E.; Torrebadell M.; Claro E.; Ramos B.
Article.Abstract: Aberrant immune mechanisms in central and peripheral nervous system might underlie the heterogeneity of symptoms in schizophrenia. Lipid droplets (LDs) are implicated in inflammatory processes and immune response. Previous studies have successfully quantified LDs in cell lines by Nile Red staining. Therefore, we hypothesized that LD abundance could be optimally quantified in leukocyte subpopulations and that LD occurrence in peripheral blood leukocytes could be altered in people with psychosis at early stages of the disorder. We optimized a method to detect and quantify LD occurrence in different leukocyte subpopulations using flow cytometry. We found that leukocyte subpopulations contain LDs, with lymphocytes showing the lowest LD content, followed by monocytes, neutrophils and eosinophils. Leukocytes were able to modulate their LD abundance upon oleate exposure in in vitro blood culture from controls. Moreover, LD content was significantly higher in all leukocyte subpopulations in recent-onset psychosis (ROP) compared to controls. When stratified by sex, these differences were maintained in males but not in females. Leukocyte subpopulations from males with ROP contain higher LD levels than controls, suggesting LD abundance as a potential male biomarker of a pro-inflammatory stage early in the disorder course. Further studies are required to confirm these findings in females.

Article.Title: Feasibility assessment of novel binocular eye alignment monitor device for intermittent exotropia
Article.Authors: Morris C.; Jenewein E.; Scheiman M.; Alvarez T.
Article.Abstract: Intermittent exotropia exhibits inherent variability in the percentage of time the eye deviates and the amount of exodeviation; therefore, assessing the magnitude and duration of the eye’s deviation is challenging. A portable monitoring device for longer assessments can enhance evaluation and management, providing an objective tool for assessing therapeutic rehabilitative interventions. The Binocular Eye Alignment Monitor (BEAM) was developed to objectively evaluate eye alignment over an extended period. Eye position was objectively recorded from 22 participants with binocularly normal vision and 15 with intermittent exotropia. Participants watched an age-appropriate movie of their choice on a television located 6 m away for 90 min after undergoing a strabismus evaluation in two sessions, each occurring on a different day. Test and retest sessions were analyzed for the percentage of test time deviated, as well as the maximum, mean, and median deviation magnitudes. Repeatability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient and Bland-Altman plots. The BEAM has a temporal resolution of 8 milliseconds and a conservative spatial resolution of 2Δ. A Mann-Whitney U-test revealed significant differences between groups for the percentage of time deviated and the maximum, mean, and median deviation ( p < 0.01). Bland-Altman plots indicated good repeatability and narrow limits of agreement in the binocular normal vision group, whereas the intermittent exotropia group showed greater variability. Linear regression analysis showed a significant correlation between the maximum deviation measured by a clinician and the BEAM ( p < 0.03). These feasibility results warrant further evaluation of the BEAM for future randomized clinical trials.

Article.Title: Interpretable prediction of peak particle velocity in tunnel blasting based on feature-enhancement-weighted WOA-XGBoost and SHAP analysis
Article.Authors: Zhao Y.; Li P.; Li H.; Yin L.; Wang H.; Bai Y.; Ren J.; Yan J.; Han B.; Chen J.
Article.Abstract: To improve the prediction accuracy of peak particle velocity ( PPV ) in tunnel blasting, enhance the model's sensitivity to high- PPV samples, and improve model interpretability, this study develops a hybrid prediction framework, FEW-WOA-XGBoost, that integrates feature enhancement, high- PPV sample weighting, and Whale Optimisation Algorithm (WOA)-based hyperparameter optimisation. Based on 125 sets of field blasting vibration monitoring data from the Chongli Tunnel, the distance from the blast centre, elevation difference, single-hole charge, total charge, and maximum charge per delay were selected as the original input variables. In addition, scaled-distance terms, logarithmic transformation terms, and charge-distance coupling terms were constructed to form an 11-dimensional input feature system. This study employs min–max normalisation to unify the feature scales and introduces a high- PPV sample-weighting strategy to enhance the model's sensitivity to high- PPV samples. On this basis, the FEW-WOA-XGBoost prediction framework is developed using XGBoost as the base learner, with WOA employed to globally optimise its key hyperparameters. To verify its performance, the proposed model was compared with benchmark models and empirical methods, including GBO-XGBoost, GWO-XGBoost, RUN-XGBoost, PSO-XGBoost, standard XGBoost, the modified Sadowski empirical formula and SVR. A comprehensive evaluation was further conducted using regression performance metrics, TOPSIS-based ranking, Taylor diagrams, PPV response-level classification, SHAP analysis, and partial dependence plot (PDP) analysis. The results show that FEW-WOA-XGBoost achieves R 2 , RMSE, MAE, VAF, and MBE values of 0.971, 0.134, 0.084, 97.16%, and 0.024, respectively, on the independent test set. Under the dataset and evaluation scheme used in this study, the model demonstrates better overall prediction performance than the benchmark models. In PPV response-level classification, the model achieves accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and Cohen's kappa coefficient values of 0.888, 0.911, 0.884, 0.895, and 0.843, respectively, indicating that it has good capability for PPV response-level classification. The SHAP analysis results show that the maximum charge per delay, the scaled distance based on total charge, the elevation difference, the ratio of total charge to blast centre distance, and the blast centre distance are the main factors affecting PPV prediction, with relative contributions of 27.5%, 21.8%, 20.9%, 13.8%, and 13.5%, respectively. The results show that, under the dataset and evaluation scheme used in this study, the integrated FEW-WOA-XGBoost framework can effectively characterise the nonlinear relationships between the selected blasting-related features and PPV. The developed model can provide a reference for blast-induced vibration prediction in tunnel blasting, PPV response-level classification, and construction-parameter optimisation.

Article.Title: Viral etiology and predictors of hospitalization in adults younger than 65 years with laboratory-confirmed respiratory viral infections in the pre-COVID era
Article.Authors: Davido B.; Annane D.; Saliba M.; Rottman M.; Mamona C.; Loubet P.; Lemarié B.
Article.Abstract: Respiratory viral tract infections (VRTIs) are generally considered more severe in older adults, while their clinical impact in younger adults remains less well characterized. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study of adults aged 18–64 years with RT-PCR-confirmed influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human metapneumovirus (hMPV), or parainfluenza virus (PIV) infection during the 2016–2018 respiratory seasons. Among 172 patients, 110 had influenza, 31 RSV, 17 hMPV, and 14 PIV infections. Hospitalization occurred in 64.0% of patients overall, with rates of 53.6% for influenza, 77.4% for RSV, and 87.1% for hMPV/PIV infections. Chronic respiratory disease, neutrophilia, and hMPV/PIV infection were independently associated with hospitalization. Chronic respiratory disease and previous respiratory tract infection were independently associated with lower odds of short-term favorable outcome, whereas detectable eosinophils were associated with improved recovery. Ninety-day mortality was low across viral groups. Age was not independently associated with hospitalization or short-term recovery within this restricted age range. These findings highlight substantial morbidity associated with VRTIs in adults younger than 65 years and underscore the need for greater attention to this population, which remains less well characterized than older adults.

Article.Title: Boredom in the museum: levels, antecedents, and consequences
Article.Authors: Goetz T.; Kraiger L.; Fries J.; Yanagida T.; Grandjean L.; Pessler M.; Pekrun R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Boredom has attracted considerable research interest, particularly boredom in learning and achievement contexts. However, boredom in learning outside of compulsory schooling and higher education has rarely been investigated. We therefore examined museum visits as such a context. Drawing on control-value theory (CVT), we used quantitative situated assessments and qualitative interviews to investigate the occurrence, antecedents, and consequences of museum boredom. Across three studies ( N = 1269, ages 18–91), we complemented individual findings with an internal meta-analysis. On a 1–5 scale, the meta-analytic mean level of museum boredom was $$\overline{M}$$ = 1.74. Consistent with CVT, museum boredom was positively related to feeling overchallenged ( $$\overline{r}$$ = .23) and underchallenged ( $$\overline{r}$$ = .35). As expected, boredom was negatively related to perceived value ( $$\overline{r}$$ = − .34/− .28 for personal/general value). Museum boredom was also negatively related to judgments of museum quality ( $$\overline{r}$$ = − .18) and to knowledge acquisition during the visit ( r = − .23). Qualitative interview data identified specific facets of over- and underchallenge (e.g., too much information, empty rooms) and value (e.g., importance for one’s life path) during museum visits. Directions for future research and practical implications are discussed.

Article.Title: Dementia risk heterogeneity across cognitive decline stages and age-defined cohorts of former professional association footballers
Article.Authors: Phillips I.; Harland A.; Mitchell S.; Hogervorst E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Former professional footballers have an elevated neurodegenerative disease development and mortality risk, relative to control populations. Whether this risk is uniform across cognitive decline stages, and through age-defined cohorts, remains unclear. This study investigated whether this risk was heterogeneous across both dimensions through a secondary analysis of a cross-sectional cohort of former professional footballers. Findings were contextualised with a detailed football technology timeline for the cohort. The null hypothesis was that footballers would demonstrate a consistent, unvarying elevated neurocognitive decline risk relative to matched control populations, across cognitive decline stages and age-defined subgroups. Hopkins Verbal Learning Test scores (HVLT, as a validated dementia screening tool), stratified for participants’ ages, were utilised to develop cumulative event curves, and age and education adjusted binary logistic regression models, to assess cohort differences in dementia risk, at different stages. Footballers’ relative dementia risk varied depending on the HVLT cut-off scores. Age-based stratification further revealed heterogeneity across cohorts, that did not follow any discernible pattern. Together, these findings did not support the null hypothesis and suggest the dementia risk landscape in professional footballers is more complex than a single population-level estimate implies. Poor cognitive performance in footballers extended beyond those exclusively exposed to highly hydrophilic laced uncoated leather balls, suggesting that dementia risk in footballers is not only an historic issue.

Article.Title: Modeling nitrate and potassium leaching in contrasting soil textures and rice husk biochar
Article.Authors: Mirsafi S.; Sepaskhah A.; Ahmadi S.
Article.Abstract: Rice husk biochar was applied at 0, 10, 20, and 30 Mg ha⁻¹ to three soil textures (loamy sand, loam, and clay loam) to evaluate its effects on nitrate (NO₃⁻) and potassium (K⁺) leaching under saturated column conditions. HYDRUS-1D inverse modelling and STANMOD were used to estimate solute transport parameters from breakthrough curves (BTCs) for nitrate and potassium. Biochar effects depended strongly on soil texture and application rate. The 10 Mg ha⁻¹ rate had no significant effect on water flux, whereas higher rates increased flow and reduced bulk density. Moderate biochar applications (10–20 Mg ha − 1 ) improved nutrient retention. In loamy sand, 10 Mg ha⁻¹ biochar reduced cumulative nitrate leaching by 28%, and in clay loam, 10 and 20 Mg ha⁻¹ reduced nitrate leaching by 21% and 33%, respectively. Similarly, for potassium, 10–20 Mg ha⁻¹ biochar reduced K⁺ leaching by 13–33% across the soils. In contrast, the highest rate (30 Mg ha⁻¹) often led to earlier breakthrough and increased leached fractions. Biochar amendments also influenced solute transport parameters, with the hydrodynamic dispersion coefficients for NO₃⁻ and K⁺ increasing by up to two to four times at moderate application rates but declining at the highest rate. Inverse modeling with HYDRUS-1D captured the overall leaching trends well (NRMSE approximately 16–24%, index of agreement d between 0.96 and 0.97), though it slightly underpredicted cumulative nitrate leaching (by 9%). Biochar rates of 10 Mg ha⁻¹ for loamy sand and 20 Mg ha⁻¹ for loam and clay loam were the most effective rates. These findings show that the effect of biochar on nutrient transport is rate- and texture-dependent and that excessive application may reduce its retention benefits.

Article.Title: Experimental validation of the limits of beam-based transverse vibration diagnostics in laboratory-scale pipe belt conveyor systems
Article.Authors: Ozdoba M.; Bortnowski P.; Król R.; Marasová D.; Moravič M.
Article.Abstract: Pipe belt conveyors enable enclosed bulk-material transport along complex routes, but their closed tubular cross-section and multi-point radial support create mechanical conditions that differ substantially from those of conventional flat or troughed conveyor belts. This study experimentally tests the transferability of a previously developed beam-based transverse-vibration frequency–tension methodology to a laboratory-scale pipe belt conveyor. A total of 72 steady-state acceleration records were acquired under empty-belt conditions for four axial-force levels (2000, 3000, 4000, and 5000 N), three belt velocities, and two consecutive measuring spans. The measured vibration signals were analyzed using Fourier-based peak detection, Rank-based frequency characterization, factorial statistical analysis, model-conditioned spectral correspondence, and cosine similarity of normalized power spectra. The amplitude-dominant Rank-1 frequency did not exhibit the monotonic increase with axial force predicted by the analytical beam model. The factorial analysis did not identify statistically supported main effects of axial force ( \(p=0.479\) ), belt velocity ( \(p=0.689\) ), or measuring span ( \(p=0.568\) ) on the Rank-1 frequency. Group-averaged spectra retained broadly similar spectral envelopes, with cosine similarities ranging from 0.890 to 0.972, whereas individual realizations exhibited substantially greater variability. Model-conditioned searches frequently identified spectral activity near the analytical reference frequencies, but these components were often secondary rather than amplitude-dominant and their proximity cannot be interpreted as independent model validation. The results show that, for the investigated empty-belt pipe-conveyor configuration, the global amplitude-dominant frequency alone does not provide a robust standalone indicator of axial force. The study establishes an experimental baseline for further investigations incorporating payload effects, contact-dependent boundary conditions, and larger-scale pipe-conveyor systems.

Article.Title: Molecular signatures of bone remodeling imbalance in type 2 diabetes and osteoporosis comorbidity: a multi-omics study with in vivo support
Article.Authors: Zhao Y.; Nguyen T.; Wang F.; Li Y.; Xia Z.; Cai Y.; Chen L.; Lin X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Type 2 diabetes (T2D) and osteoporosis (OP) frequently coexist, but the molecular features linking metabolic dysfunction to impaired bone remodeling remain incompletely defined. Here, we integrated public bulk transcriptomic datasets, a clinical serum proteomics cohort, and descriptive single-cell resources to prioritize candidates for investigation in a T2D-OP mouse model. The existing differential-expression screens, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and set intersections nominated TTC1. A documented TTC1 expression-stratified GSEA in the low-versus-high BMD dataset was used for exploratory pathway context; it was not a disease-case-control enrichment analysis and did not apply a p-value adjustment method. These analyses are hypothesis-generating: TTC1 met the nominal screening criteria but did not meet BH-FDR < 0.05 in the low-versus-high BMD transcriptomic or serum proteomic results, and the T2D bulk analysis did not account for longitudinal sampling. Pre-imputation serum TTC1 measurements were available in only 1/14 controls and 6/14 patients, and TTC1 was excluded by detection-coverage filters. Single-cell analyses provided cellular context without cross-study disease-effect inference. In the T2D-OP mouse model, bone microstructural deterioration and histopathological damage were accompanied by increased TTC1, TNF-α, iNOS, NFATc1 and TRAP expression and reduced RUNX2 and OCN expression in bone tissue. The combined observations motivate further study of TTC1 in abnormal bone remodeling; independent clinical validation and functional perturbation are needed to establish its biological role.

Article.Title: A hybrid CoordAttention model with focal loss for handling visual similarity in gastrointestinal endoscopic images
Article.Authors: Akram S.; Zafar B.; Hanif M.; Khan M.
Article.Abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) diseases represent a major global health challenge that requires timely and accurate diagnosis for effective treatment. Deep learning has shown promise in endoscopic image analysis. However, challenges such as class imbalance and visual similarity among classes degrade the prediction performance. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning framework that combines ResNet50 and VGG16 architectures with the Coordinate Attention (CoordAttention) mechanism to enhance feature representation and improve classification accuracy. Both architectures were individually optimized with CoordAttention before concatenating them into a feature-level hybrid model, which was further refined using focal loss to address class imbalance. Experiments on the 22-class GastroVision dataset showed that the proposed hybrid with CoordAttention achieved higher scores than the baseline and the compared state-of-the-art models, with a macro F1-score of 0.718, a micro F1-score of 0.897, and a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.886. The hybrid model without CoordAttention obtained a macro F1-score of 0.657, a micro F1-score of 0.835, and an MCC of 0.816 with the focal loss function. Focal Loss mitigates the effects of class imbalance by emphasizing difficult and underrepresented samples. The proposed approach did not apply any synthetic technique to handle imbalance, which may make it applicable to datasets with different class distributions. Although standard data augmentation was applied uniformly to improve the diversity of datasets, no specific class-balancing strategy was used to artificially balance class distributions. These findings suggest that the proposed framework is a useful approach for jointly addressing class imbalance and visual similarity in GI endoscopy image classification.

Article.Title: Study on construction deformation law and support forms of tunnels in high‑geostress sand‑mudstone interbedded strata based on model tests
Article.Authors: Gao Y.; Fang Z.
Article.Abstract: Aiming at the asymmetric large deformation encountered during the excavation of tunnels in sand–mudstone interbedded strata under high in-situ stress, this paper takes the Jianshan Tunnel along the Zhonglan section of the Yinlan High-Speed Railway as the engineering background and adopts a combined approach of discrete element numerical simulation and physical model testing to systematically investigate the surrounding rock deformation laws and support mechanical response of soft–hard interbedded tunnels under different bolt support forms. First, the control effects of symmetric and asymmetric arrangements of long–short bolts on surrounding rock displacement and crack distribution are comparatively analyzed using the discrete element method. Second, based on similarity theory and orthogonal tests, sandstone and mudstone similar materials satisfying the required physico-mechanical indices are prepared, and a self-developed model test system capable of three-dimensional high-geostress loading is established. Finally, under the most unfavorable condition of a 45° dip angle and 1:1 layer thickness ratio, model tests are conducted for two support schemes—systematic equal-length bolts and asymmetric long–short bolts—to monitor the evolution of surrounding rock deformation and circumferential stress during excavation. The results show that the asymmetric arrangement of long–short bolts reduces the maximum horizontal displacement difference between the left and right sides by approximately 40% and effectively restrains crack propagation. The surrounding rock deformation along the tunnel longitudinal direction can be divided into five zones—the unaffected zone, initial influence zone, tunnel face transition zone, deformation development zone, and stable zone—with the maximum excavation influence range extending from 0.5B ahead of the tunnel face to 1B behind it. Under asymmetric support, the circumferential stress range at each position is significantly narrowed and the tensile stress difference between the left and right spandrels tends to be balanced, indicating a notable improvement in the stress condition of the support structure. The findings provide reference for deformation control and support design of tunnels in soft–hard interbedded strata under high in-situ stress.

Article.Title: In vitro assessment of Sargassum platycarpum extract as a novel antimicrobial agent and functional prebiotics
Article.Authors: Zaghloul E.; Elsayed K.; Ismail A.; Gamal R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sargassum platycarpum is a brown macroalgae species commonly found in coastal areas. This macroalgae is a source of important bioactive compounds that can be utilized as functional food ingredients and pharmaceutical agents. In the current study, S. platycarpum collected from the Red Sea was dried and extracted with methanol . S. platycarpum methanolic extract (SME) was evaluated as a potent antibacterial agent and as a prebiotic for marine probiotic consumption. SME demonstrated significant antimicrobial activity, with Bacillus subtilis ATCC 6633 being the most affected pathogen, exhibiting a clear zone diameter of 25 mm. Conversely, Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 25,923 displayed the least susceptibility, with a clear zone diameter of 14 mm. Moreover, SME (0.1%, 0.5%) exhibited a significant increase in the marine probiotic Enterococcus faecalis H2 growth, indicated by a high OD value of 1.3 at 620 nm after 6 h of incubation and viable bacterial count > 300*10 2 CFU mL −1 , which is equivalent to inulin. Furthermore, the chemical composition of SME was determined through GC–MS analysis, demonstrating that it consists of forty-five phytochemical compounds, primarily terpenoids, fatty acids/lipids, steroids, carotenoids, and polyphenolic/aromatic derivatives. These results offer new perspectives on integrating SME into future research paths related to functional food and pharmaceutics.
