Article.Title: Responses of soybean–maize succession to increasing phosphate fertilization rates under phosphate-solubilizing microorganism inoculation
Article.Authors: Oliveira T.; Cantão V.; da Silva J.; de Castro Dias R.; Cabral J.; Duarte W.; Sarkar S.; da Silva Solino A.
Article.Abstract: Low phosphorus (P) availability constrains crop productivity in weathered tropical soils, particularly within soybean–maize succession systems. Combined application of phosphate fertilization and phosphate-solubilizing microorganisms has been proposed, but its field performance in soybean-maize succession systems remains poorly documented. This study evaluated the response of a soybean–maize succession to increasing rates of monoammonium phosphate (MAP) under seed inoculation with phosphate-solubilizing microorganisms (PSM), Bacillus subtilis (CNPMS B2084) and Priestia megaterium (CNPMS B119) in a Cerrado Oxisol, assessing soil P availability, plant nutritional status, physiological traits, yield, and soil biochemical attributes (glomalin, β -glucosidase, arylsulfatase, and acid and alkaline phosphatases).The field experiment followed a randomized complete block design with P 2 O 5 rates of 0, 19.5, 39.0, 59.5, and 78.0 kg ha⁻ 1 (all inoculated with PSM), plus an absolute control without P fertilizer and without PSM inoculation. In maize, grain yield increased linearly with P₂O₅ rate under PSM inoculation. Yield values in fertilized treatments under PSM inoculation were higher than those observed in the absolute control. In soybean, grain yield was not affected, whereas grain P concentration increased linearly with P 2 O 5 rate. Soil β -glucosidase activity also increased with P 2 O 5 rates under PSM inoculation, suggesting stimulated microbial C-cycling activity, while photosystem II photochemical parameters and arylsulfatase activity remained unaffected. The results indicate that increasing MAP rates under PSM inoculation were associated with higher maize grain yield, soybean grain P accumulation, and soil β -glucosidase activity. Because all fertilized treatments received PSM inoculation, the independent contribution of PSM could not be determined.

Article.Title: Field-based estimation of bulk and wall chlorine decay in continuous and intermittent water distribution systems: a study from Coimbatore, India
Article.Authors: Dhanabal G.; Chellaiah G.; Ramkumar M.; Ravi S.
Article.Abstract: Maintaining appropriate residual chlorine in drinking water distribution systems is crucial for ensuring disinfection protection. This study uses field data from two urban distribution zones in Coimbatore, India—Jayaram Nagar, operating under continuous water supply, and Gandhi Park, operating under intermittent water supply to develop a deterministic first-order kinetic-based web framework for estimating bulk and wall chlorine decay coefficients. During the summer of 2024, 96 locations were sampled, comprising 37 in Gandhi Park and 59 in Jayaram Nagar. Bulk ( \({k}_{b}\) ) and wall ( \({k}_{w}\) ) decay coefficients were estimated using first-order kinetic equations, with hydraulic contact time approximated from pipe length and flow velocity and empirical adjustments applied for selected water-quality parameters. Across both zones, \({k}_{b}\) ranged from 0.059 to 0.092 h⁻ 1 and \({k}_{w}\) from 0.015 to 0.034 h⁻ 1 . Gandhi Park exhibited mean \({k}_{b}\) and \({k}_{w}\) values of 0.078 and 0.026 h⁻ 1 , respectively, compared with 0.076 and 0.025 h⁻ 1 in Jayaram Nagar. The mean numerical ratio of the estimated bulk to wall decay coefficients was approximately 3:1 in both zones; however, this ratio is reported only as a comparison of coefficient magnitudes and does not represent the actual relative mass contribution of bulk and wall reactions to chlorine loss. However, the differences between the two zones were only 0.002 h⁻ 1 for \({k}_{b}\) and 0.001 h⁻ 1 for \({k}_{w}\) and were smaller than the corresponding within-zone variability; therefore, the observed differences were interpreted descriptively rather than as statistically established effects of the supply regime. The developed application supports CSV-based and manual data entry and provides transparent sample-level estimates for preliminary engineering assessment.

Article.Title: In vitro and in silico therapeutic potential of Nyctanthes arbor-tristis (L.) flower extract against prostate cancer
Article.Authors: Hussain A.; Rahman S.; Gogoi D.; Alam S.; Tiku A.; Ansari K.; Ramteke A.
Article.Abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is a serious clinical problem because of metastatic development and the adverse effect of conventional treatment. This paper explores the anticancer effects of Nyctanthes arbor-tristis (L.) flower extract (NAFE) against PC3 and LNCaP cells. NAFE was profiled by high resolution liquid chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry, which led to the identification of fourteen major phytochemicals of potential relevance. Computational Molecular Docking (MD), Molecular Dynamics Simulation (MDS) and ADME/T was used to predict the underlying probable mechanism of its anticancer properties. Assays showed that NAFE exerts a dose-dependent inhibition of cellular proliferation with a maximal inhibition level around 74% and has cytostatic activity based on a modest increase in the G1-phase cell population. Western blotting evaluation suggest the downregulation of key regulatory proteins such as Cyclin D1, CDK4/6, phosphorylated Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) and phosphorylated Akt. Furthermore, NAFE impedes migration and invasion of PC3 PCa cells which was revealed by a reduction of 73.7% in wound healing assays, accompanied by suppression of matrix metalloproteinases (MMP-2 and MMP-9). In silico MD analyses and MDS study identified Phloridzin as probable lead molecule targeting EGFR (-138.51 kcal/mol), CDK6 (-140.64 kcal/mol), CDK4 (-130.633 kcal/mol) and MMP2 (-138.028 kcal/mol) proteins supported by favorable ADME/T parameters. The present findings establish the potential of NAFE as a non-toxic, nutraceutical candidate having therapeutic potential for efficient management of metastatic PCa.

Article.Title: Molecular recognition of Atrazine, 2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid, and Chlorpyrifos by cyclodextrin-based adsorbents: insights into selective pesticide removal
Article.Authors: Asadian M.; Kiani-anbouhi R.
Article.Abstract: Cyclodextrin (CD)-based host–guest complexation represents an effective supramolecular approach for the selective capture of pesticide contaminants. In this study, the binding behavior of Atrazine, 2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D), and Chlorpyrifos with α-, β-, and γ-CDs was evaluated comparatively using molecular docking and interaction analysis. The results revealed that the balance between molecular size, polarity, cavity compatibility, and interaction diversity strongly governs pesticide affinity. Among the studied systems, β-CD showed the most favorable and versatile performance, particularly for Atrazine and 2,4-D, where its intermediate cavity size enabled balanced rim anchoring and hydrophobic inclusion. Atrazine was stabilized mainly through hydrogen bonding and distributed weak interactions, while 2,4-D benefited from carboxylate-mediated rim anchoring combined with partial cavity fitting. For Chlorpyrifos, the larger γ-CD cavity provided the strongest accommodation due to the bulky and hydrophobic nature of the molecule, supported by hydrogen bonding, carbon–hydrogen bonding, van der Waals contacts, and a distinctive π–sigma interaction. In contrast, α-CD mainly promoted rim-dominated binding because of its restricted cavity, whereas γ-CD showed loose-fit behavior for smaller pesticides. Overall, the findings indicate that β-CD is the most broadly applicable host, while γ-CD is especially suitable for bulky chlorinated pesticides. These molecular-level predictions provide a basis for prioritizing CD–pesticide combinations for further experimental validation and the subsequent development of CD-based remediation materials.

Article.Title: A multimodal framework for UAV-assisted wildfire detection and contextual alert generation using vision-language models and LLM fusion
Article.Authors: Eesaar H.; Abbas Z.; Rehman M.
Article.Abstract: The increasing frequency and intensity of wildfires pose a critical threat to ecosystems, property, and human life, creating a need for monitoring systems that combine rapid visual detection with interpretable and actionable reporting. This study presents an integrated multimodal framework for UAV-assisted wildfire monitoring that combines YOLOv12n-based wildfire and smoke detection, Moondream2-based vision-language captioning, and GPT-4o mini-based alert summarization. YOLOv12n is evaluated against six YOLO baselines on an aerial wildfire and smoke dataset and achieves a favorable balance between detection performance and computational efficiency, with an overall precision of 0.649, recall of 0.628, mAP@0.5 of 0.628, an inference time of 1.8 ms, and a model size of 2.52 million parameters. For semantic scene understanding, Moondream2 achieves the highest average BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, and METEOR scores among the evaluated vision-language models. GPT-4o mini similarly outperforms the evaluated summarization baselines in summary-reference alignment, achieving average BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, and METEOR scores of 0.1501, 0.5595, and 0.5461, respectively. Qualitative analysis across five wildfire video scenarios further illustrates the pipeline’s ability to generate contextually relevant descriptions and concise draft alerts under varied visual conditions. Computational measurements for the locally executed models were obtained on a backend workstation, whereas GPT-4o mini was accessed through an external API; therefore, embedded UAV performance and network-inclusive end-to-end latency remain to be validated. Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of combining lightweight visual detection, vision-language reasoning, and LLM-based summarization to support human-verified wildfire situational awareness and emergency decision-making.

Article.Title: Urolithin A mitigates cryopreservation-induced oxidative damage and improves sperm quality and fertilizing ability in Turkey semen
Article.Authors: Azadbakht K.; Malekifard F.; Hosseini S.; Baqerkhani M.; Soleimanzadeh A.
Article.Abstract: Turkey spermatozoa are highly susceptible to cryoinjury, and post-thaw fertility with frozen-thawed semen frequently remains below 40%. Urolithin A (UA), a gut microbiota-derived ellagitannin metabolite with mitophagy-inducing and antioxidant properties, improves sperm quality in other species, but its efficacy in avian semen cryopreservation has not been tested. Pooled semen samples from adult Bronze turkeys ( n = 7 independent pools) were extended in a glucose-based diluent supplemented with 0 (control), 1, 5, or 10 µM UA and cryopreserved by the vapor-freezing method. Post-thaw evaluations included computer-assisted sperm analysis (CASA), sperm viability, plasma membrane functionality, DNA integrity, and oxidative stress/antioxidant biomarkers (TAC, SOD, GPx, MDA), together with fertility and hatchability following artificial insemination of turkey hens. Supplementation with 1 µM and 5 µM UA significantly improved total motility (58.4 ± 0.82% and 56.7 ± 0.91%, respectively) and progressive motility and most velocity parameters relative to control and 10 µM UA. Sperm viability, plasma membrane functionality and DNA integrity were likewise higher in the 1 and 5 µM groups, and TAC, SOD and GPx activities were elevated while MDA was reduced, indicating mitigation of oxidative stress. The 10 µM dose provided little or no additional benefit and for some parameters showed values similar to or worse than the control, consistent with a non-monotonic dose–response. Fertility and hatchability were significantly higher in the 1 µM (71.7% fertility, 54.8% hatchability) and 5 µM groups than in the frozen control. These findings indicate that low micromolar concentrations of UA, particularly in the range of 1–5 µM, protect turkey spermatozoa against cryopreservation-induced oxidative damage and improve in vivo fertilizing potential, consistent with the mitochondria-protective mode of action reported for UA in mammalian species. Urolithin A is a promising natural additive for avian semen cryopreservation and germplasm banking.

Article.Title: CBAT-Net: a unified CNN–BiLSTM–MultiHead transformer architecture for joint Q3/Q8 protein secondary structure prediction
Article.Authors: Pandit R.; Dhatterwal J.; Panigrahi G.; Khomane R.
Article.Abstract: Protein Secondary Structure Prediction (PSSP) remains one of the core challenges in computational biology relevant to a variety of important applications such as drug design, protein engineering and understanding of disease mechanisms. Although some recent deep learning methods have shown remarkable performance, the simultaneous prediction of the 3-state (Q3) and 8-state (Q8) secondary structure with high accuracy is not achieved yet. A novel unified architecture of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory networks (BiLSTM) and Multi-Head Transformer mechanisms is demonstrated to effectively predict the Q3/Q8 protein secondary structure together. Our architecture is based on a hierarchical structure that combines features extracted by layers of attention mechanisms. We obtain full mathematical models for gradient flow optimization, and present a new dual-task loss function with adaptive weights. The performance of CBAT-Net is tested on benchmark datasets (CB513, CASP12, CASP13, CASP14 and TS115); it outperforms the existing methods by 23.8% and 4.7% in Q3 and Q8 accuracy (Q3 = 86.71%, Q8 = 78.42% on CB513), respectively. The performance is confirmed as better by the statistical significance test ( p < 0.001). Ablation studies have shown that the whole architectural composition has a significant impact on the final performance. CBAT-Net is an important improvement in the field of protein secondary structure prediction that shows that it is possible to successfully learn both local and global information from a protein sequence with hybrid architectures that indicate suitable inductive bias. It discusses Hyper Learning, deep learning architecture, convolutional neural network, bidirectional LSTM, multi-head attention, Transformer architecture, features of the dataset, and Protein Secondary Structure Prediction.

Article.Title: Sim-heuristic algorithm for solving bi-objective stochastic optimization problems
Article.Authors: Horng S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bi-objective stochastic constrained optimization problems (BSCOP) involve bi-objective stochastic functions and deterministic constraints. BSCOP is NP-hard because of exponential growth in computational complexity. A sim-heuristic algorithm can solve NP-hard problems, where the simulation addresses model uncertainty and interacts with the metaheuristic approach, which explores the search space to identify a near-optimal solution. A sim-heuristic approach that combines leaf in wind optimization with ordinal optimization (LWOO), is presented to solve BSCOP efficiently. The LWOO approach comprises three phases: surrogate model, universal exploration, and local exploitation. The Kolmogorov–Arnold Network (KAN) serves as a surrogate model to efficiently evaluate solution performance. In universal exploration, a refined leaf in wind optimization is developed to select N promising solutions from the whole search space. An advanced optimal computing budget allocation is utilized in local exploitation to identify a near-optimal solution from the N promising solutions. The LWOO approach is employed for production planning in reconfigurable manufacturing systems. The purpose is to find the optimal system configuration, task allocation to the workstation, and buffer allocation to simultaneously maximize expected throughput while minimizing the total buffer capacity. A reconfigurable manufacturing system consisting of 3 workstations with 2 inter-station buffers serves as a practical example. The LWOO approach was compared with four heuristic methods to validate the performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the LWOO approach consistently produces optimal and reliable solutions within a reasonable timeframe.

Article.Title: An explainable hybrid transformer–CNN framework for multi-class brain tumor classification from MRI images
Article.Authors: Babu B.; Rajesh V.; Thottempudi P.; Dilli R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The identification of brain tumors through magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) requires effective methods that provide precise results because these results determine clinical choices. The study presents a classification system based on hybrid Transformer-CNN technology which classifies brain tumors into multiple types by using tumor segmentation and deep feature extraction and explainable artificial intelligence. The preprocessing of MRI images involves several steps which include skull stripping and CLAHE-based contrast enhancement and normalization and data augmentation and resizing to create high-quality images that maintain uniformity for model input. The TransUNet architecture performs tumor region segmentation by integrating convolutional neural networks with transformer-based attention systems which enable it to recognize both nearby and distant contextual details. The system generates segmentation masks which enable region-of-interest (ROI) feature extraction through DenseNet121 that has been pretrained on ImageNet while the final classification layer gets removed and global average pooling produces discriminative feature representations. The system uses an attention-based feature refinement method to improve feature representation followed by a regularized fully connected deep classifier which includes batch normalization and dropout for four-class classification of tumors. Model interpretability is achieved using Grad-CAM++ and attention visualization, enabling clear identification of tumor-related regions and improving model transparency. Experimental evaluation demonstrates high classification performance, achieving accuracies of 98.54% for meningioma, 98.65% for glioma, 99.45% for pituitary tumors, and 99.56% for no-tumor cases. These results indicate that presented TransUNet–DenseNet121 approach offers an accurate, reliable, interpretable method for detection of brain tumors automatically from MRI scanned images.

Article.Title: ATP release and ectonucleotidase activity shape infected red blood cell adhesion in placental malaria
Article.Authors: Rivadeneira E.; Etcheverry T.; Deleschaux C.; Saffioti N.; Delas Y.; Chêne A.; Semblat J.; Gamain B.; Sévigny J.; Schachter J.; Schwarzbaum P.; Ostuni M.; Farina M.; Alvarez C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Placental malaria is characterized by the sequestration of Plasmodium falciparum –infected red blood cells (iRBCs) within the intervillous space through VAR2CSA-mediated adhesion to chondroitin sulfate A (CSA) expressed on trophoblasts. Although cytoadherence is a key pathogenic event, its impact on extracellular ATP (eATP) signaling remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated eATP dynamics during trophoblast–iRBC interactions using BeWo-derived cytotrophoblast (CTB) and syncytiotrophoblast (STB) models together with human placental explants. CSA-binding iRBCs induced significantly greater eATP accumulation than culture-matched RBCs or CD36-binding parasites. eATP accumulation required direct cell contact and was reduced by soluble CSA, indicating that it is closely associated with VAR2CSA-dependent adhesion. Degradation of eATP by apyrase markedly reduced cytoadherence, and pharmacological modulation of purinergic signaling similarly disrupted the adhesive interaction, indicating that eATP homeostasis contributes to efficient cytoadherence. CTB, STB and placental explants exhibited substantial ATP-hydrolyzing activity and expressed multiple ectoenzymes. Placental tissue displayed a markedly higher capacity to remove eATP than trophoblast cultures, which likely contributes to the absence of detectable eATP accumulation in explants exposed to iRBCs. A data-driven model fitted to the experimental eATP kinetics enabled estimation of the ATP efflux, showing that early eATP dynamics are dominated by ATP release, while ectoATPase-driven hydrolysis acts as a buffering mechanism whose contribution grows over time as eATP accumulates. Together, these findings identify eATP metabolism as a previously underappreciated component of trophoblast–parasite interactions and suggest that regulation of eATP availability contributes to host–parasite communication during placental malaria.

Article.Title: PRMT1 facilitates the renal ischemia-reperfusion injury by inducing the ferroptosis via mediating the arginine methylation of ACSL4
Article.Authors: Lin Y.; Zhu B.; Zhu X.; Xu X.; Zhu K.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: Renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) potentially results in chronic kidney disease. Protein arginine methyltransferase 1 (PRMT1) is an arginine methyltransferase involved in regulating various cellular processes by methylating arginine residues. Herein, the function of PRMT1 in renal IRI was studied, and the underlying molecular mechanism was explored. HK-2 cells were stimulated by hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R) to induce injury, and ferroptosis-related indicators were detected using commercialized kits and western blot. Renal ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) mouse model was established using PRMT1 knockout (PRMT1-KO) mice, and renal injury and ferroptosis were evaluated. The effect of PRMT1 on arginine methylation of acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) was evaluated using immunoprecipitation and western blot. The results showed that asymmetric dimethylarginine (ADMA) and PRMT1 levels were significantly increased in H/R-treated HK-2 cells. H/R reduced cell viability and induced ferroptosis in HK-2 cells, which was demonstrated by the use of deferoxamine (DFO), a ferroptosis inhibitor. Overexpression of PRMT1 facilitated ferroptosis, and knockdown of PRMT1 inhibited ferroptosis in H/R-induced cells. Moreover, knockout of PRMT1 attenuated I/R-induced renal injury and inhibited ferroptosis in the kidney tissues in mice, while overexpression of ASCL4 reversed these effects. Mechanistically, ASCL4 methylation level was upregulated by PRMT1 overexpressing, and R284 and R437 sites were the methylation sites in ACSL4. Furthermore, PRMT1 enhanced the stability of ACSL4 protein. In conclusion, PRMT1 facilitated the renal IRI by inducing the ferroptosis through promoting the arginine methylation of ACSL4. These findings indicate the therapeutic potential of PRMT1 for treating renal IRI.

Article.Title: A 3L2C2 DC–DC three-port converter with topology-level power decoupling: conduction loss optimization via improved Gray Langurs Optimizer-based triple phase-shift modulation
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Ma C.; Zhang C.; Lu P.; Zhang D.; Liu J.; Zhao Y.; Fu H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper presents a 3L2C2 multi-resonant-element three-port converter (3L2C2-TPC) that transfers power through the fundamental and third-harmonic components while realizing topology-level decoupling between ports 2 and 3. Because the converter conduction loss is dominated by the resonant RMS currents, a converter-specific optimization model is established for the five triple phase-shift variables under two prescribed power-transfer constraints. An application-oriented improved Gray Langurs Optimizer (IGLO) combines Logistic-map initialization with dynamic opposition-based learning to improve initial coverage and reduce search stagnation. The optimizer is assessed through independent-run statistics and comparisons with representative population-based algorithms. A laboratory prototype verifies topology-level power decoupling and the optimized modulation. At the same power command, the measured weighted RMS-current metric decreases from 71.27 A 2 at a feasible nonoptimal point to 58.70 A 2 at the IGLO-derived point, corresponding to a reduction of approximately 17.6%. The results support the proposed method for the reported converter, voltage, and operating-point range; universal superiority over other optimizers is not claimed.

Article.Title: Plasma retinol binding protein 4 improves survival of Klebsiella pneumoniae-induced pneumosepsis through stimulation of neutrophils
Article.Authors: Ma J.; Wang S.; Bai Y.; Xu C.; Yang Y.; Yin S.; Xu H.; Wang Y.; Chen N.; Zhang Y.; Wang Y.; Li W.
Article.Abstract: A decrease in plasma retinol binding protein 4 (RBP4) was seen in sepsis patients. It is unknown whether the reduction is a specific indicator of sepsis or plays a role in sepsis pathogenesis. We addressed these questions using human cohorts consisting of 80 healthy, 68 non-sepsis infection (control for sepsis) and 471 sepsis subjects, and a mouse model of Klebsiella pneumoniae (KP)-induced pneumosepsis (KPS). Compared with healthy group, plasma RBP4 was markedly decreased in non-sepsis infection and sepsis patients. However, no difference was found between non-sepsis infection and sepsis groups. Lower RBP4 in sepsis patients was associated with increased mortality. In KPS mice, RBP4 knockout resulted in decreased survival. Intravenous administrations of recombinant RBP4 (rRBP4) improved the survival. The protective effect of RBP4 was selectively associated with augmented function of alveolar neutrophils. In vitro, both endogenous and exogenous RBP4 exhibited stimulatory effects on myeloperoxidase expression, KP phagocytosis and killing in neutrophils. Immunoprecipitations revealed a selective association between bioactive RBP4 and TLR2. TLR2 antagonist C29 reversed the effects of rRBP4 in vitro and in vivo. We conclude that decreased plasma RBP4 reflects the occurrence of infection rather than sepsis. Plasma RBP4 is protective in KPS likely through TLR2-dependent stimulation of neutrophils.

Article.Title: [18F]FDG brain PET-MR versus PET/CT in a clinical cohort: intra-subject quantitative comparisons
Article.Authors: Martinez A.; Flaus A.; Heckemann R.; Dunn J.; Al-Ethawi S.; Jeljeli S.; McGinnity C.; Hammers A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract There is limited evidence on the advantages of brain 2-deoxy-2-[ 18 F]fluoroglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography (PET) with simultaneous magnetic resonance imaging (PET-MR) over PET with computed tomography (PET/CT). We quantitatively compared brain FDG PET/CT and PET-MR images from a large clinical cohort. Participants with refractory epilepsy or cognitive problems underwent PET/CT at approximately 30 min post-injection, followed by PET-MR at approximately 100 min. Standardized uptake values (SUVs) were extracted in anatomical regions using a multi-atlas method, and voxel-wise comparisons were performed with statistical parametric mapping. Fifty-five image pairs passed quality control. Within-subject correlations between modalities were very high (0.96, range 0.84–0.99); within-region, across-participant correlations were 0.82 (0.72–0.90). PET-MR SUVs were on average 20% higher than PET/CT, more so for higher-uptake regions. Voxel-wise, PET-MR showed relatively higher uptake in visual and auditory cortices, lower uptake in medial frontal and anteromesial temporal cortices, and better grey-white matter contrast. We found a very close correspondence between the two modalities with their respective attenuation correction methods and sensory activation between scans; the different uptake times explain differences in absolute SUV levels and grey-white matter contrast. With awareness of these differences, brain PET-MR can be used clinically.

Article.Title: Integrated oculomics and lipidomics characterise cross-sectional retinal–lipidomic associations in a generally healthy biobank population
Article.Authors: Ullah I.; Vidal Rosas E.; Razzak I.; Jameel S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cardiovascular disease remains the leading global cause of mortality, yet current risk stratification methods may fail to capture early, subclinical vascular changes. Previous studies have rarely integrated retinal microvascular characteristics with comprehensive serum lipidomic profiles as potential indicators of cardiovascular health. In this study, we applied an imaging–omics framework that combines deep learning-derived retinal microvascular traits with serum lipidomic data to explore retinal-lipidomic association patterns using higher-dimensional serum lipidomic profiling alongside quantitative retinal vascular phenotypes. To our knowledge, this represents one of the first large-scale, covariate-adjusted correlation analyses of retinal microvascular phenotypes and serum lipidomics in a generally healthy biobank population. Retinal phenotypes were quantified using automated image analysis tools, while serum lipid profiling was performed using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with electrospray ionisation high-resolution mass spectrometry. Modest but statistically significant age- and sex-adjusted partial correlations were observed, particularly between average artery width, vessel density, and lipid subclasses such as triacylglycerols, diacylglycerols, and ceramides. These relationships are biologically plausible in the context of microvascular–metabolic remodelling but should be interpreted as exploratory association signals rather than evidence of causality or clinical prediction. By linking quantitative retinal vascular phenotypes to annotated serum lipidomic features, this study characterises retinal–lipidomic association patterns relevant to microvascular–metabolic variation. This integration provides an imaging–omics workflow for identifying candidate association signals that connect automated retinal vascular phenotypes with circulating molecular profiles. Future longitudinal and outcome-linked studies will be important to assess the temporal stability and clinical relevance of these association patterns.

Article.Authors: Zhou Q.; Li G.; Zhang W.; Li X.; Zhang C.; Jie M.
Article.Abstract: This study develops a styling optimization method assisted by positive emotional granularity (PEG) for new energy SUV wheel hubs. Scenario-based expert screening, imagery-word refinement, principal component analysis, and user ratings establish three imagery dimensions; morphological analysis and the analytic hierarchy process identify eight inputs. The third-generation nondominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-III) and entropy-weighted TOPSIS support candidate generation and selection. Across 20 matched random splits, PSO-BP achieves the lowest equally weighted three-target test root mean square error (0.1896). After correlation adjustment and Holm correction, only its comparison with OLS for modern dynamic imagery is significant ( \(\it \:\text{p}\) = 0.0315). Ten searches yield a final hypervolume of 1.10825 ± 0.00360. Within a fixed 354-candidate set, equal weighting and six local weight perturbations preserve the baseline top-ranked candidate, whereas surrogate changes and prediction errors affect rankings. The implemented design exhibits a maximum radial static stress of 175 MPa, below the 252 MPa yield strength. The decoupling–mapping–optimization–verification method supports early styling decisions, subject to sample coverage, predictive uncertainty, and engineering conditions.

Article.Title: Lived experience of patients following eye enucleation: a phenomenological study in western Iran
Article.Authors: Rasad R.; Khatony A.; Jalali A.; Abdi A.; Abbasi P.; Vaisi-Raygani A.; Bestankar M.; Jalali R.
Article.Abstract: Eye enucleation is a life-altering procedure that profoundly disrupts patients’ psychological well-being, social functioning, and overall quality of life. While the resulting emotional distress is generally acknowledged, in-depth phenomenological explorations within specific cultural contexts remain scarce. This study explored the lived experiences of patients following enucleation in Kermanshah, Iran. A qualitative phenomenological approach was employed. Thirteen patients who had undergone enucleation at a teaching hospital affiliated with Kermanshah University of Medical Sciences were purposively selected and participated in in-depth, semi-structured interviews from September 2024 to March 2025. Data collection continued until data saturation was reached. Data were analyzed using Colaizzi’s seven-step method and managed with MAXQDA 2020. Credibility was ensured through Lincoln and Guba’s criteria, and reporting followed the COREQ checklist. Participants (mean age: 40.6; mean enucleation duration: 2.76 years) revealed four main themes (Denial and Initial Shock, Catastrophic Perception of Loss, Adaptation and Coping, and Ambivalence and Emotional Complexity, comprising 10 sub-themes. Eye enucleation causes intense but modifiable psychological distress, including stigma, burdens, and coping challenges. While patients adapt via prosthetics and support, clinical care must incorporate routine psychological screening, targeted pre-surgical counseling, and peer-support programs to facilitate prosthetic adjustment and mitigate stigma.

Article.Title: A Multiagent Reinforcement Learning-based Energy-Efficient Routing Algorithm for Submerged Optical Wireless Sensor Networks
Article.Authors: Dinesh P.; John Y.; Sridevi P.; Balaji M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The benefits of a rapid communication rate, ultrawide bandwidth, and reduced delay have made Submerged Optical Wireless Sensor Networks (SOWSNs) a popular topic of study. However, offering a low-consumption and dependable routing in SOWSNs is difficult because of the restricted power resources and highly fluctuating topologies induced by the water stream velocity. An Energy Efficient Routing Algorithm using Multiagent Reinforcement Learning (EERA-MRL) for SOWSNs has been presented as a solution to this problem. To better deal with the changing circumstances and promote the extension of network lifespan, the system is initially represented as a decentralized multiagent system. The remaining power and connection quality have been determined while designing the routing algorithm. A technique for assessing the entire network’s input through a decentralized reward system has been provided. Localized (direct) Reward (LR) is one of the incentive types to express the relationships among individuals or the data about two nearby nodes. A Universal Reward (UR) has been supplied to represent the efficiency of the network or the caliber of data transfer in SOWSNs. Three energy management strategies are suggested to extend the lifespan of SOWSNs. The first strategy uses reinforcement learning to navigate accurately to shorten journeys and minimize energy usage. The second strategy is to enhance node energy usage by utilizing a sleep scheduling algorithm. The last method limits each node’s information transfer depending on the received information variation rate. Simulation findings demonstrate that the suggested strategy significantly outperforms previously published methods regarding mean remaining energy ( $$\:{P}_{rem})$$ ; hop count; and throughput. The findings demonstrate the low energy usage and elevated throughput (98.5%) of the proposed EERA-MRL-based routing protocol for SOWSNs.

Article.Authors: Han D.; Shin M.; Lee S.; Ko J.; Lee J.; Kim Y.; Kwak B.; Sung J.
Article.Abstract: Ferroptosis-associated redox vulnerability represents a potential therapeutic target in hepatocellular carcinoma, yet the interplay between this process and antioxidant adaptation remains unclear. Here, we show that Tamarixetin preferentially reduces viability in HepG2 and Huh-7 cells relative to the HepaRG comparison model. Transcriptome profiling revealed enrichment of ferroptosis- and glutathione metabolism-related pathways, implicating redox-associated genes linked to the SLC7A11–GPX4 defense axis. Molecular docking supported a structural hypothesis for xCT interaction without establishing direct binding. Notably, Tamarixetin-induced lipid peroxidation was retained in three-dimensional hepatoma spheroids. These findings identify Tamarixetin as a context-dependent redox-active compound that promotes ferroptosis-associated injury alongside NRF2-associated antioxidant responses in hepatoma cells.

Article.Authors: Samee N.; Talaat R.; Raza A.; Shaiba H.; Meshoul S.; Salem D.
Article.Abstract: Promoters are vital for the initiation of gene transcription, and their accurate uncovering in bacterial genomes is crucial for the progression of genetic and biotechnological research. This research introduces an innovative approach for detecting promoters in Agrobacterium tumefaciens, integrating a large language model (LLM)-based GPT-Neo transformer with Random Forest (RF) feature engineering and traditional machine learning methodologies. The GPT-Neo model was initially used to tokenize nucleotide sequences and produce high-dimensional embeddings that include the structural and interactional characteristics of promoter regions. The embeddings function as input for the RF classifier, which conducts probabilistic feature extraction to provide augmented feature vectors, therefore enhancing the model’s prediction capabilities. The integration of LLM-based feature extraction with RF feature engineering results in substantial performance enhancements, with the model attaining an accuracy of 97% and an AUC of 0.99, surpassing conventional methods. Furthermore, the use of the Synthetic Minority Over-Sampling Technique (SMOTE) rectifies class imbalances, hence providing equitable sensitivity and specificity. This methodology signifies a considerable progress in promoter prediction, providing a solid foundation for prospective applications in bacterial genomics and bioinformatics.

Article.Title: Knowledge, attitudes, and physician engagement among hospitalized older adults using long-term sedative-hypnotics
Article.Authors: Lavon O.; Motes Y.
Article.Abstract: Sedative-hypnotics remain widely used in older adults despite safety concerns. We conducted a cross-sectional interviewer-administered survey of hospitalized patients ≥65 years with regular sedative-hypnotic use documented on admission to characterize use, knowledge of recommended duration and adverse effects, and clinician engagement in counseling and deprescribing. Among 88 participants (mean age 81.5; 60% women), only 18% reported any counseling on duration and/or adverse effects, and 1% were offered a nonpharmacological alternative. Deprescribing engagement was limited: 7% reported that a physician had offered stopping and 19% had tried to stop; fear of stopping was common (88%). Nevertheless, 35% said they would try to discontinue if their physician advised that they could stop, and 32% reported abnormal events since starting treatment. These exploratory findings suggest a potentially actionable care gap. Structured counseling, shared decision-making, deprescribing support, and access to behavioral insomnia therapies warrant prospective evaluation as strategies to improve sedative-hypnotic safety in older adults.

Article.Authors: Liao G.; Pettan-Brewer C.; Ladiges W.
Article.Abstract: Aging involves progressive changes across interconnected biological pathways, but minimally invasive approaches for assessing these processes remain limited. Differences were identified across inflammatory, vascular, intercellular communication, metabolism, and tissue maintenance pathways. After Benjamini-Hochberg correction, 45 proteins remained significant at FDR q < 0.05 in CB6F1J mice and none in C57BL/6J mice. Hallmark-level analyses were therefore based primarily on all mapped proteins, with FDR-defined subsets considered secondary. Hallmark categories showed substantial overlap, and analyses restricted to uniquely assigned proteins showed attenuated cross-strain concordance. These findings demonstrate that serum protein profiling can capture hallmark-level age-associated differences across genetic backgrounds. As this study compared only two age groups cross-sectionally, the findings do not establish aging trajectories but provide a framework for future longitudinal serum-based assessment.

Article.Title: Amh3MD multimodal dataset and deep learning model for information disorder detection in social media
Article.Authors: Woldegiorgis A.; Abebe M.; Jimma W.
Article.Abstract: Misinformation, disinformation, and mal-information have all become significantly more common due to the quick expansion of social media platforms. These forms of abusive content often appear in multimodal formats such as text, images, and memes, making their detection more challenging, particularly for low-resource languages such as Amharic. This study proposes a multimodal deep learning model for detecting information disorder by integrating textual and visual features through early fusion. A new multimodal dataset (Amh3MD) containing 8053 labeled samples sourced from the most popular social media platforms. and grouped into 4 classes: disinformation, misinformation, mal-information, and normal content. Textual features were extracted using contextual embedding models, including DistilBERT, while visual features were extracted using deep convolutional and transformer-based architectures such as ResNet, EfficientNet, and Vision Transformer (ViT). Several multimodal deep learning models, including CNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, CNN-LSTM, and transformer-based architectures, were evaluated using performance evaluation metrics. Experimental results demonstrate that early fusion approaches, which integrate visual and textual features, substantially enhance classification performance. Among the evaluated models, the CNN-BiLSTM multimodal model achieved the best performance in the CNN/LSTM group with an accuracy of 0.63, an F1-score of 0.58, and a recall of 0.57. In transformer-based experiments, the EF-ResNet50-mBERT-Attention model achieved the highest overall performance with an accuracy of 0.68 and an F1-score of 0.67, demonstrating the effectiveness of attention-based multimodal fusion. The results present the importance of contextual text embeddings and advanced visual representations for multimodal information disorder detection. This study contributes to the field by introducing the first publicly available Amharic multimodal information disorder dataset and proposing an effective fusion-based deep learning model for multi-class classification. The findings provide valuable insights for developing scalable and context-aware models to combat information disorders and harmful content in low-resource languages. Future research should focus on scalable, multilingual, multimodal transformer and vision-language models to improve performance and to develop a real-time social media monitoring system for detecting information disorder.

Article.Title: Antiviral activity of HSP90 inhibitors against Mumps virus and related paramyxoviruses
Article.Authors: Kato F.; Bae C.; Wakata A.; Kakizaki M.; Okura T.; Nakatsu Y.; Seki F.; Someya K.; Otsuki N.; Ryo A.; Matsumoto Y.; Fukuhara H.; Maenaka K.; Ishigami-Yuasa M.; Kidokoro M.; Ochiai M.; Ishii K.; Katoh H.; Takeda M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mumps virus (MuV), a member of the family Paramyxoviridae , continues to cause recurrent outbreaks worldwide despite widespread vaccination. Currently, however, no antiviral drugs have been approved for MuV or other paramyxoviruses. In this study, we screened approximately 1,000 small-molecule compounds using a recombinant MuV expressing green fluorescent protein and identified six compounds that significantly suppressed viral replication without detectable cytotoxicity. These compounds were known inhibitors of heat shock protein 90 (HSP90), a host chaperone involved in the assembly and function of viral polymerase complexes. These HSP90 inhibitors exhibited potent antiviral activity with submicromolar EC₅₀ values and high selectivity indices. Moreover, their antiviral efficacy extended to other paramyxoviruses, including measles virus (MeV), canine distemper virus (CDV), and Sendai virus (SeV). Time-of-addition assays demonstrated that these compounds act at a post-entry stage, primarily during viral RNA synthesis. Consistently, minigenome assays of MuV and Nipah virus (NiV) confirmed robust suppression of viral RNA synthesis without direct inhibition of reporter enzyme activity, indicating target specificity. Collectively, our findings highlight the potential of HSP90 inhibitors as host-directed antiviral agents against paramyxoviruses and support their further development for the treatment of emerging and re-emerging paramyxovirus infections.

Article.Title: Predictive modelling and optimization of material removal rate in WEDM of carbon fiber reinforced polymer composites
Article.Authors: Patil S.; Hatte P.; Kebede A.; Magdum R.
Article.Abstract: Wire electrical discharge machining (WEDM) is one of the few processes capable of cutting carbon fibre reinforced polymer (CFRP) laminates without direct mechanical contact, but predicting the material removal rate (MRR) remains difficult because removal proceeds through a combination of thermal and spark-erosion mechanisms in a highly heterogeneous, poorly conducting workpiece. This study reports an L18 Taguchi experimental campaign on a hand-laid woven-carbon/epoxy laminate and uses it to examine a question that is frequently overlooked in the WEDM modelling literature: how much model complexity a small orthogonal-array dataset can actually support. Five parameters were varied - pulse-on time (T ON ), pulse-off time (T OFF ), spark gap voltage (SV), wire feed (WF) and wire tension (WT). Analysis of variance on the 18 runs shows that MRR is governed by TON (35.6% of the total sum of squares, p = 0.006) and TOFF (34.8%, p = 0.018). Wire feed contributes 8.6% ( p = 0.24), while spark gap voltage (0.4%, p = 0.92) and wire tension (0.3%, p = 0.94) are not statistically significant over the ranges tested. A hierarchy of regression models was then fitted to the same data and assessed by leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) rather than by training fit alone. A three-parameter model in T ON and T OFF gives the best predictive performance (LOOCV R 2 = 0.51), whereas expanding the model to 12 or more coefficients raises the training R 2 above 0.86 while driving LOOCV R 2 negative - that is, the elaborate models predict a new observation less accurately than the sample mean does. A saturated 18-parameter model reproduces the data exactly (R 2 = 1.000) yet has a LOOCV R 2 of -59.1. The practical conclusion is that for an 18-run WEDM dataset, reporting high-order polynomial or multi-term models on the basis of training R 2 is not defensible, and model selection should be based on out-of-sample criteria. The dominance of T ON and T OFF is consistent with discharge energy per pulse and duty cycle controlling removal. The study is limited to a single laminate configuration and a three replicate per run; surface-integrity characterisation of the machined edges is identified as necessary further work and is not claimed here.

Article.Title: Emerging role of LncRNAs MMP2-AS1, FAM222A-AS1, and XIST as potential biomarkers in HIV patients receiving antiretroviral therapy
Article.Authors: Fatima M.; Shahid M.; Gulzar S.
Article.Abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play crucial roles in immune regulation and viral pathogenesis. However, their expression patterns and clinical relevance in HIV infection remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to validate differentially expressed lncRNAs in HIV-infected individuals and evaluate their potential roles in distinguishing viremic and ART-suppressed patients. Transcriptomic analysis was performed on the GSE235038 dataset from the gene expression omnibus. Differentially expressed lncRNAs were identified using GEO2R (log₂FC > 2/< −2, p < 0.05). lncRNAs MMP2-AS1, FAM222A-AS1, and XIST were experimentally validated in a Pakistani clinical cohort (195 HIV patients and 51 healthy controls) using quantitative real-time PCR. ROC curve analysis was used to assess the diagnostic performance of lncRNAs. Competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) networks were constructed, followed by Gene Ontology (GO) and KEGG pathway enrichment analyses. Significant lncRNA dysregulation was observed associated with HIV infection and ART status. MMP2-AS1 was upregulated in viremic patients, whereas FAM222A-AS1 and XIST were markedly downregulated. qRT-PCR validation confirmed these expression patterns. MMP2-AS1 and FAM222A-AS1 exhibited strong diagnostic performance in distinguishing viremic patients from healthy controls, XIST showed high discriminatory ability suggesting a potential association with treatment response. ceRNA network analysis revealed interactions with immune and signaling pathways related to miRNAs and mRNAs. Functional enrichment highlighted pathways involved in immune regulation, transcriptional control, and signal transduction. Distinct lncRNAs expression is associated with HIV disease activity and ART response. MMP2-AS1 and FAM222A-AS1 show potential as diagnostic biomarkers, while XIST may serve as a treatment-response–associated marker. However, interpretation of XIST requires consideration of its sex-specific expression and validation in balanced cohorts.

Article.Title: Standardizing in-hospital cause-of-death data using large language models and neural machine translation
Article.Authors: Lee J.; Ryu B.; Kim Y.
Article.Abstract: This study aims to expand the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model (CDM) by linking in-hospital mortality data with national mortality statistics. Specifically, we developed a pipeline utilizing large language models (LLMs) and neural machine translation (NMT) to standardize unstructured, bilingual cause-of-death text. From a cohort of 1,033,461 patients, 64,034 mortality records were identified. These records were converted into a standardized CDM format by mapping Korean Standard Classification of Diseases codes to the international standard, Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine—Clinical Terms. The pipeline structured 1,702 cases of unstructured, bilingual (Korean–English) free-text records containing medical abbreviations. The English translation performance of NMT- and LLM-based models was compared and subsequently validated against a ground truth reviewed by medical professionals. Finally, we employed retrieval-augmented generation-based LLM prompts to automatically assign International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) codes to the translated text, identifying neoplasms (35.89%) and circulatory diseases (17.70%) as the primary causes of death. Technically, Nllb-200-1.3B achieved the highest translation accuracy, whereas SOLAR-10.7B and Llama 3.1-8B demonstrated superior performance in ICD-10 code matching. We successfully established a comprehensive mortality database and demonstrate that LLM-based modules are highly feasible for standardizing clinical big data, offering a scalable solution for enhancing real-world medical data interoperability.

Article.Title: In silico assessment of barnyard millet and blue pea derived bioactive peptides against Salmonella enterica Serovar Typhi and Clostridioides difficile
Article.Authors: Kacha S.; Guchhait R.; Panickar A.; Ramaiah S.; Anbarasu A.
Article.Abstract: Natural food derived bioactive peptides have been increasingly recognised for their natural origin, improved biocompatibility, and potent antimicrobial activities. In the current study, a comprehensive computational framework has been employed to evaluate the potency of bioactive peptides against major GI causing pathogens such as Salmonella Typhi and Clostridioides difficile . A total of 519 candidate peptides were screened based on antimicrobial properties, toxicities, anti-inflammatory activity and allergenicity, which yielded two promising peptides (P1: biopep02815 and P2: biopep02950). Molecular docking against key pathogenic targets, TcdA, TcdB and OmpF revealed strong binding affinity with ClusPro docking scores ranging from − 706 to − 920. Subsequent molecular dynamics simulations and binding free energy analyses confirmed the structural stability and favourable interaction energies of the protein-peptide complexes that are primarily driven by van der Waals and electrostatic energy components. The present findings of the study underscore the antimicrobial potential of the food derived bioactive peptides against prevalent GI pathogens, paving their way to future experimental and clinical investigations.

Article.Title: Effects of thermal-saline coupled conditions on swelling properties of bentonite analyzed on the basis of the fractal model
Article.Authors: Lu H.; Xu G.; Xiang G.; Liu J.; Luan M.; Liu W.
Article.Abstract: Swelling deformation tests were conducted on bentonite in NaCl, KCl, and CaCl 2 solutions at 25, 50, and 80 ℃. Utilizing a fractal e-p e model, the swelling coefficient K was employed to quantify thermal-saline coupling effects. Results indicated a negative correlation between K and temperature, attributed to increased water molecule kinetic energy restraining crystal layer swelling. While K remained constant in NaCl, it decreased with rising concentration and temperature in KCl and CaCl 2 due to intensified cation exchange. The relative magnitude of K varied by concentration: the sequence was NaCl > KCl> CaCl 2 at 0.1 M, but shifted to NaCl> CaCl 2 > KCl at 1.0 M. This reversal is not a simple “synergy. ” It reflects a shift from Ca 2+ -dominated electrostatic suppression at low concentration to K + -dominated fixation and mineral alteration at high concentration. XRD analysis confirmed mineral stability in NaCl and CaCl 2 ; however, significant montmorillonite dissolution was observed in KCl at 80 ℃ and 1.0 M, leading to a marked reduction in K . The intrinsic cation exchange capacity ( CEC ) is a material property and does not change with ion type; however, the apparent CEC and exchangeable cation composition measured after reaction can change in KCl due to K + fixation and mineral alteration.

Article.Title: In vitro and in silico prediction of bioactive compounds extracted from rhizosphere soil bacterium of Cassia fistula against Salmonella Typhi
Article.Authors: T B.; M K.; Ulaganathan S.; S S.; Balaji M.; V M.; Sivashanmugam K.; C S.
Article.Abstract: The emerging risk of multidrug-resistant Salmonella Typhi emphasizes urgent focus towards the identification of novel antimicrobial compounds with new mechanisms of action. This article investigated the rhizosphere soil of Cassia fistula for bioactive bacteria that are rich in antimicrobial activities. Twelve bacterial isolates were collected and screened for antimicrobial activity; of these, VITBS7 showed the maximum activity. The strain VITBS7 was identified as Pseudomonas aeruginosa by 16S ribosomal DNA sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS) revealed six bioactive metabolites. Molecular docking of the metabolites extracted from the bacterial isolates against the S. Typhi penicillin-binding protein 1B (PBP1B), cross-validated with three independent scoring functions and a redocking control, showed that a coumarin carbonate derivative bound most strongly (-8.28 kcal/mol), exceeding the reference drug ampicillin (-7.77 kcal/mol); molecular dynamics simulations (3.0 µs aggregate) confirmed that this complex remained stable and specifically bound at the catalytic site over 300 ns. The majority of the compounds revealed desirable pharmacokinetic and bioavailability profiles from Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, and Excretion (ADME) and drug-likeness studies. Further, the in vitro antibacterial tests demonstrated the potent activity of the metabolites against S. Typhi, comparable to those of reference antibiotics. The results obtained from the current study confirmed the antibacterial activity of metabolites derived from P. aeruginosa VITBS7, isolated from the rhizosphere soil of C. fistula , and possess a valuable lead for developing novel drugs against drug-resistant S. Typhi.

Article.Title: Serologically analyzing blood samples from Mongolian livestock for zoonotic pathogens
Article.Authors: Takhampunya R.; Lamalee A.; Longkunan A.; Boldbaatar B.; Matulis G.; Cleary N.; Lindroth E.; Fiorenzano J.; Mann A.; Mena-Sanchez A.; Altantogtokh D.; Sukhbaatar L.; Gray G.; Ricks K.; von Fricken M.
Article.Abstract: Mongolia faces a significant risk from zoonotic diseases including tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV), Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV), Hantaan virus (HTNV), and Yersinia pestis due to its large livestock and pastoralist populations. Given the potential exposure risk from infected livestock for Mongolian herders and military personnel transiting on operation, we sought to characterize seroprevalence rates among livestock animals against these high-consequence vector-borne and rodent-borne diseases. Whole blood samples were collected from cattle, goat, horse, sheep, and camel from 2014 to 2015 in three aimags (provinces): Tuv, Selenge, and Dornogovi. Samples were tested for reactive antibodies against these pathogens using the MAGPIX ® system and an in-house multiplex assay. Based on an optimized 20-fold signal-to-noise threshold cutoff, the following positivity rates were detected: in Tuv- 0% (HTNV), 1.4% (TBEV), 0.5% ( Y. pestis ) and 0% (CCHFV); in Selenge- 0.6% (HTNV), 3.2% (TBEV), 0% ( Y. pestis ), and 0.3% (CCHFV); and in Dornogovi- 0.2% (HTNV), 0.7% (TBEV), 1.3% ( Y. pestis ), and 1.7% (CCHFV). The highest positivity by pathogen and animal group was observed for TBEV in horses from Selenge (9.4%) and CCHFV in camels from Dornogovi (11.4%). These findings highlight the value of livestock surveillance for identifying circulating zoonotic pathogens and assessing public and veterinary health risk in Mongolia.

Article.Title: Market-driven technology opportunity discovery by integrating trademark-based market signals and patent embeddings
Article.Authors: Lee D.; Lee B.; Yoon B.
Article.Abstract: This study proposes a market-driven technology opportunity discovery (TOD) framework that integrates trademark-based market signals with patent embeddings. Existing TOD studies have mainly relied on technology-oriented data, such as patents and scientific publications, to identify technological structures, trajectories, and vacant areas. Although these data are useful for understanding accumulated technological knowledge, they have limitations in capturing early market signals, product and service concepts, and firms’ commercialization intentions. To address this limitation, this study utilizes trademark designated goods descriptions as market-oriented textual data and links them with patent-based technological knowledge. The proposed framework consists of three main steps. First, trademark descriptions are transformed into sentence-level embeddings, and unsupervised anomaly detection algorithms are applied to identify trademark outliers that deviate from existing market patterns. Second, the identified trademark outliers are matched with semantically related patents in a shared embedding space to evaluate their technological relevance. Third, a patent-based generative topographic mapping (GTM) map is constructed, and trademark outliers are projected onto the patent-based technology space using the coordinates of their matched patents. Opportunity regions are then identified by comparing patent density and trademark signals at the cell level. Regions with strong trademark signals but low patent density are interpreted as market–technology imbalance areas and potential technology opportunities. The empirical results demonstrate that trademark data can complement patent-based analysis by revealing market-oriented signals that may not be captured from technological documents alone. This study contributes to technology opportunity discovery research by providing a systematic framework for linking early market signals with technological knowledge structures.

Article.Title: Multimodal ensemble machine learning pipeline for oocyte fertilization prediction using first polar body morphology and clinical factors
Article.Authors: Onthuam K.; Limsila T.; Sappakit T.; Vongsaisuwon M.; Chaichaowarat R.; Suebthawinkul C.
Article.Abstract: While machine learning has seen growing applications in in-vitro fertilization (IVF), existing research primarily focuses on embryo-level data, which represents the developmental stage following the fertilization of the oocyte and sperm. However, the study of such application on oocyte, which is the major contributing factor to the success of IVF, is limited. This study introduces an ensemble-learning pipeline designed to predict successful fertilization—defined as two-pronuclei (2PN) development—following Intracytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) by integrating morphological image data with clinical features. Furthermore, this study examines how the first polar body (PBI) influences the established analytical pipeline. Our pipeline input consists of a complete metaphase of meiosis II (MII) oocyte image, its PBI segmentation, and numerical clinical cellular features. We evaluated two prominent machine learning models: Random Forest and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), to predict outcomes based on numerical features. Our experimental results indicate that XGBoost demonstrates superior performance and is more suitable for this specific numerical dataset. Furthermore, our results demonstrate that integrating PBI imagery significantly enhances the pipeline’s predictive performance, achieving a peak AUC of 0.82. Subsequent analysis suggests that the morphological characteristics of the PBI provide a valuable predictive association within the ensemble framework.

Article.Title: Stress entropic load as an exploratory thermodynamic indicator of physiological activation during a laboratory gaming task
Article.Authors: Sebera M.; Zlámal F.; Svobodová L.; Bienertová-Vašků J.
Article.Abstract: This exploratory study examines physiological activation and adaptive load in esports players during a standardized laboratory gaming stressor using Stress Entropic Load (SEL), a thermodynamic indicator derived using the Entrant system. It explores differences between amateur and elite players and examines whether long-term esports experience is associated with a different temporal profile of physiological activation. Fifty-five players (35 amateur, 20 elite; ages 15–30) participated in the study. Anthropometric data, body composition, subjective stress (PSS), sleep quality (PSQI), and physical activity (IPAQ) were recorded. The laboratory protocol included 10 min of baseline rest, a 15-min standardized Trackmania task designed to induce time pressure and frustration, and a subsequent recovery period. Participants were not specialists in Trackmania; therefore, the task should be regarded as a laboratory gaming stressor rather than a simulation of title-specific esports competition. SEL was continuously monitored throughout the procedure using the Entrant system. SEL changed significantly across the experimental phases in both groups (main effect of time, p < 0.001). Mean SEL values were descriptively higher in elite players across protocol phases; however, the mixed-effects model showed no statistically significant overall group effect ( p = 0.107). The time × group interaction also did not reach statistical significance ( p = 0.056). Accordingly, the observed between-group pattern is exploratory and should be interpreted as a preliminary trend requiring replication in a larger sample, rather than robust evidence of group separation. These findings should be interpreted as preliminary evidence that SEL may capture changes in physiological activation during a laboratory gaming task; they do not establish SEL as a validated measure of psychological stress or demonstrate an advantage over established physiological markers.

Article.Title: Preoperative GLP-1 receptor agonist use is associated with lower 2-year emergency department utilization and all-cause mortality after total shoulder arthroplasty
Article.Authors: Lee K.; Ma H.; Tsai S.; Chiang E.; Su Y.; Chien C.; Wu T.
Article.Abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have demonstrated metabolic, anti-inflammatory, and cardiovascular benefits, but their effect on outcomes following total shoulder arthroplasty (TSA) remains unclear. This retrospective cohort study used the TriNetX global database to evaluate the association between preoperative GLP-1 RA use and postoperative outcomes after TSA. Adult patients who underwent TSA between 2008 and 2022 were identified and stratified according to GLP-1 RA use within 30 days before surgery. One-to-one propensity score matching was performed to balance demographic characteristics and comorbidities. Outcomes included 90-day medical complications and 2-year surgical outcomes. In the matched 90-day cohort (1,951 patients), no significant differences were observed between groups in medical complications, readmission, emergency department utilization, or all-cause mortality. In the matched 2-year (1,917 patient) cohort, GLP-1 RA use was associated with significantly lower rates of emergency department utilization (26.7% vs. 31.0%; RR 0.86; 95% CI 0.78–0.95; p = 0.012) and all-cause mortality (1.8% vs. 4.3%; RR 0.43; 95% CI 0.29–0.63; p = 0.008). In summary, preoperative GLP-1 RA use was associated with favorable outcomes following TSA at 2-year follow-up. Given the observational nature of this study, these findings should be interpreted as associations and require validation in prospective studies.

Article.Title: Genomic and phenotypic characterization of the Jeju Genome Project cohort in Korea
Article.Authors: Nam K.; Lee J.; Kim H.; Jeong W.; Huh J.; Jo J.; Lee J.; Park C.; Oh J.; Lee S.; Kang C.; Park J.; Chang S.; Cho A.; Yang J.; Kim J.; Kim J.; Joo J.; Kim Y.; Hyun C.; Oh J.; Kim M.; Park J.; Lee S.; Han N.
Article.Abstract: The Jeju Genome Project (JGP) is a genomic and phenotypic cohort established to provide a comprehensive resource for precision medicine on Jeju Island, South Korea. JGP integrates whole-genome sequencing (WGS), customized genotyping arrays, and detailed clinical and lifestyle phenotyping to characterize population-specific genetic architecture, disease determinants, and risk profiles among participants recruited on Jeju Island. The study enrolled 5307 participants, comprising 2999 community-based and 2308 hospital-based participants enriched for neurological, malignant, rheumatic, and ophthalmological disorders, reflecting the real-world disease burden in an aging population. Biospecimens, including blood and stool samples, were collected using standardized protocols and biobanked for planned molecular analyses. WGS and genotyping array data were available for 3466 and 3002 participants, respectively, with both sources available for 1161 participants. By enabling the discovery of population-relevant genetic variants and supporting the development of polygenic risk scores and individualized prediction models, JGP provides a scalable framework for region-specific precision health strategies, facilitating risk stratification, early disease detection, and targeted prevention in Jeju Island and East Asian populations.

Article.Title: Prognostic miR-1/-26a-1/-487b signature predicts glioma progression via SH3PXD2B/EFHD2 targeting
Article.Authors: Díaz Méndez A.; Di Giuliani M.; Sacconi A.; Allegretti M.; Ranazzi G.; Ramponi S.; Barresi V.; Stroppa A.; Silvani A.; Costantini A.; Astuccioni B.; Di Maio A.; Carosi M.; Regazzo G.; Garufi C.; Rizzo M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Gliomas are aggressive brain tumors that remain challenging to diagnose and treat. Despite standard-of-care therapies, most patients recur, underscoring an unmet need for novel biomarkers to elucidate tumor evolution. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) play crucial roles in glioma biology by modulating tumorigenesis. We previously identified a non-invasive diagnostic/prognostic miRNA signature (miR-1-3p/miR-26a-1-3p/miR-487b-3p) which exerts oncosuppressive functions in glioma cells, prominently effecting the inhibition of invading targeting SH3PXD2A/SH3PXD2B/EFHD2 genes. Here, we investigated the miR-1/-26a-1/-487b- SH3PXD2A/SH3PXD2B/EFHD2 network as a progression indicator using datasets of primary/recurrent gliomas. We found that the three-miRNA signature is upregulated in primary vs. recurrent patients, whereas SH3PXD2A/SH3PXD2B/EFHD2 are downregulated in primary patients. It is worthy to note that, this network correlates with improved survival. These findings were validated by RT-qPCR in tissues of a paired-primary/recurrent cohort ( n = 42). Univariate and multivariate Cox-regression analyses showed that high miR-1-3p/miR-26a-1-3p/miR-487b-3p signature expression independently correlated with prolonged progression-free-survival in this cohort. Additionally, we developed a digital PCR multiplex clinical research assay (G-SMART), for the simultaneous absolute quantification of miR-1-3p/miR-26a-1-3p/miR-487b-3p, which may provide a fast and sensitive tool in the clinical setting. In conclusion, the miR-1-3p/miR-26a-1-3p/miR-487b-3p and its targets are key axes that are progressively dysregulated upon glioma progression. Hence, this regulatory network might offer a prognostic tool for disease monitoring, leading us to hypothesize a translational value of our findings for a more precise and patient-tailored approach.

Article.Title: Effects of Rhizobium inoculation and integrated fertilization on the nutritional composition of maize (Zea mays L.) in northwest Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Mekonen H.; Adugna A.; Yirdaw G.; Hibistu Z.; Kassie M.; Hune Y.; Mengist A.; Aneley Z.
Article.Abstract: Micronutrient deficiencies remain a major public health challenge in Ethiopia, largely due to reliance on cereal-based diets with low nutrient density. Microbial biofortification using Rhizobium offers a sustainable strategy to enhance nutrient content in staple crops. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of Rhizobium inoculation and chemical fertilizer application on nutritional composition of maize in northwest Ethiopia. A randomized controlled field trial was conducted across three districts (Baso Liben, Debre Elias, and Womberma) during the 2024 cropping season. Seeds of the ‘BH-661’ maize variety were evaluated under three treatments: Treatment 1 (T1): recommended full-dose chemical fertilizer (100 kg DAP ha −1 + 50 kg urea ha −1 ; Treatment 2 (T2): Rhizobium inoculation without chemical fertilizer; and Treatment 3 (T3): Rhizobium inoculation combined with half-dose chemical fertilizer (50 kg DAP ha −1 + 25 kg urea ha −1 ). Proximate composition and micronutrient levels were analyzed using standard laboratory methods, including atomic absorption spectrophotometry. Data were analyzed using two-way mixed-effects analysis of variance, with statistical significance declared at p < 0.05. Compared to Treatment 1, Treatment 3 significantly increased crude protein (11.26 vs. 8.77%, F(2,4) = 45.970, p = 0.002, ηp 2 = 0.958), carbohydrate (58.26 vs. 56.68%, F(2,4) = 7.51, p = 0.044, ηp 2 = 0.790), crude fiber (2.14 vs. 2.07%, F(2,4) = 265.101, p < 0.001, ηp 2 = 0.993), ash (1.27 vs. 1.15%, F(2,4) = 5.84, p < 0.045, ηp 2 = 0.745), iron (20.67 vs. 18.92 mg/kg, F(2,4) = 3.77, p = 0.038, ηp 2 = 0.770), and zinc (18.13 vs. 14.75 mg/kg, F(2,4) = 52.24, p < 0.001, ηp 2 = 0.984). The combined application of Rhizobium inoculation and reduced-rate chemical fertilizer therefore improved selected macro- and micronutrient concentrations of maize grain, particularly, crude protein, carbohydrate, crude fiber, ash, iron and zinc contents. These results suggest that integrated microbial and mineral fertilization may serve as a promising agronomic biofortification strategy.

Article.Title: Signal processing technology of multi-user OTFS communication system based on spectrum cognition
Article.Authors: Nie L.
Article.Abstract: In high-speed mobile communication scenarios, time–frequency dual-selective fading induces severe inter-symbol interference in traditional orthogonal frequency division multiplexing systems, drastically degrading communication reliability. Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) modulation effectively avoids channel dynamic fading through delay-Doppler domain transmission, but still faces the problem of cross-domain interference and resource allocation in multi-user spectrum sharing scenarios. To this end, a spectral cognition-based MU-SISO-OTFS system signal processing technology is suggested by integrating signal detection optimization and intelligent power allocation techniques. First, grounded in the sparse quasi-cyclic structure of the OTFS channel matrix, a zero-forcing, minimum mean square error linear detection algorithm is designed, and a nonlinear iterative detection algorithm grounded in Message Passing (MP) is suggested. Secondly, in the underlay spectrum sharing mode, for bidirectional interference between the Primary User (PU) and the Secondary User (SU), an equal power allocation strategy under zero-forcing mechanism and a binary iterative power allocation algorithm with Successive Interference Cancellation (SIC) technology are designed. The outcomes reveal that the minimum mean square error detection block error rate is as low as 3.8 × 10 –4 at a signal-to-noise ratio of 25 dB, which is nearly an order of magnitude lower than the zero-forcing algorithm. The MP algorithm converges its bit error rate to 1.8 × 10 –4 with a relaxation factor of 0.6 and 8 iterations, taking only 12.4 ms. The total rate approximation of the suggested binary algorithm SU reaches 99.45%, and the execution time is only 8.35 ms. With the introduction of SIC, the reachable rate of SU at 40 dBm power is 15.1 bps/Hz and the outage probability is 0. Moreover, at a mobile speed of 500 km/h, the proposed SIC-assisted bisection scheme maintains a per-grid resource allocation fairness index of 0.84 while achieving an SU achievable rate of 11.2 bps/Hz, demonstrating a favorable balance between the system throughput and the resource allocation fairness in ultra-high-speed scenarios. The study provides a high-performance, low-complexity OTFS signal processing solution for high-speed mobile communication systems, which has significant engineering application value.

Article.Title: Germline variation across breast cancer predisposition genes: whole-exome evidence
Article.Authors: Alabdulaziz B.; Alabdulrahman K.; Abouelhoda M.; Al-Tassan N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Understanding the population-level spectrum of genetic variation in cancer-associated genes is critical for improving variant interpretation and informing precision medicine. However, most hereditary cancer research has been conducted in populations specific cohorts, with underrepresentation of Middle Eastern populations in global genomic databases. These important data can be enriched with studies from different underrepresented ethnic groups to ensure diversity and inclusion. This study aims to characterize pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants in selected cancer-associated genes in a large Saudi population cohort. The whole-exome sequencing (WES) of 11,093 individuals without documented cancer diagnosis from different parts of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA), was analyzed to identify protein-altering variants across 20 breast cancer-associated genes. Variant annotation and classification were performed using established databases and interpreted according to American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) guidelines. A total of 217 variants were identified across the 20 genes analyzed. Of these, 156/217 (71.9%) occurred in high- and moderate-risk breast cancer susceptibility genes. Most of the variants were detected in genes associated with hereditary breast cancer susceptibility and DNA repair pathways such as BRCA1 , BRCA2 , ATM , CHEK2 , PTEN , and PALB2 . A substantial proportion of the variants were not currently reported in ClinVar. Most variants were found in a heterozygous state, consistent with carrier status in the general population. This study provides population-level insights into the prevalence of pathogenic variants in breast cancer-related genes in the Saudi population. The findings highlight the importance of population-specific genomic data to improve variant interpretation and support the development of precision medicine and genetic screening strategies in underrepresented populations.

Article.Title: Authenticity-constrained generative image enhancement using semantic consistency and provenance metadata
Article.Authors: Liu L.; Lin C.; Akande O.; Egenti G.; Agarwal N.; Agarwal S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The use of digital image enhancement has advanced with recent developments in artificial intelligence (AI), resulting in image enhancements that are visually pleasing and can sometimes exceed the capabilities of traditional methods. In digital media systems, however, a number of current deep learning approaches focus on perceptual realism, rather than semantic authenticity, which can lead to contextual distortion, misinformation risk, and lack of traceability of the provenance of the media product. To address this limitation, we introduce an Authenticity-Constrained Generative Model (ACGM) that jointly balances perceptual enhancement, semantic authenticity, and provenance traceability. The architecture combines a U-Net-based generator with residual dense blocks, a CLIP/VGG-based authenticity-preservation module, and a provenance-aware traceability encoder. These components are jointly optimized using the Creativity–Authenticity Loss Function (CALF), which integrates adversarial, perceptual, authenticity, and traceability terms. Semantic authenticity is assessed through input–output feature consistency, whereas traceability is evaluated by embedding and recovering invisible, C2PA-inspired provenance metadata. The present implementation does not generate a formally signed C2PA manifest. The development set consisted of 1,500 paired samples from Flickr2K and MIT-Adobe FiveK, of which 1,050 were used for training, 225 pairs were used for validation, and 225 pairs were used for internal testing. Under the reported controlled conditions, ACGM obtained PSNR = 33.7 ± 0.58, SSIM = 0.937 ± 0.009, LPIPS = 0.071 ± 0.007, FID = 10.5, and CLIP-based semantic similarity = 0.91 ± 0.02. Overall, the results of human-centered evaluation showed that there were significant model effects within participants for perceived visual appeal, perceived authenticity, and trustworthiness (all p<0.001). Bonferroni-adjusted paired comparisons revealed that ACGM scored significantly higher than all the evaluated baselines on all three criteria. These findings remain preliminary because of the modest dataset scale, the controlled provenance-recovery experiment, and the absence of robustness testing under common image transformations.
