Article.Title: A comparative study of classic, evolutionary, and ensemble machine learning methods for pressuremeter modulus prediction
Article.Authors: Hasanpour M.; Bolouri-Bazaz J.; Mohammadzadeh S. D.; Karballaeezadeh N.
Article.Abstract: Accurate determination of the pressuremeter modulus (Ep) is essential for foundation design and settlement analysis in geotechnical engineering, while direct pressuremeter testing remains costly and time-consuming. This study develops and compares five machine learning models from three methodological families for predicting Ep: classic machine learning (Support Vector Regression (SVR) and k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN)), evolutionary computation (Multi-Expression Programming (MEP)), and ensemble learning (Random Forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost)). The models use four routinely measured index properties, including depth (H), moisture content (ω), bulk density (ρ), and fines content (FC), from 103 pressuremeter tests collected at 103 distinct sites in Mashhad, Iran. Baselines included a mean predictor, ordinary least squares (OLS) regression, and a depth-only linear model. Performance was assessed through three accuracy indices (correlation coefficient, Willmott’s index of agreement, and Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency) and two error-based indicators (mean absolute error and root mean square error), all reported in kg/cm 2 . Under repeated 5-fold cross-validation and leave-one-out cross-validation, OLS, SVR, RF, and XGBoost performed statistically equivalently (LOOCV R 2 ≈ 0.974–0.978), while the depth-only linear model achieved R 2 = 0.969. An ablation analysis excluding depth caused R 2 to collapse to 0.30–0.37 for all models, confirming that depth dominates Ep prediction in this region. MEP evolved a nonlinear depth-only equation (test R 2 = 0.964) that provides comparable accuracy with full transparency and spreadsheet-level implementation. SHAP analysis confirmed the dominance of depth (88.5% importance) and the approximate linearity of the underlying relationship. Jackknife+ conformal prediction produced well-calibrated 95% intervals with 93.5% empirical coverage for both SVR and MEP. The study provides a dual-outcome framework: practitioners can adopt the SVR for maximum accuracy or use the transparent MEP equation for routine engineering calculations, both within the investigated regional conditions.

Article.Title: Pine needles as an indicator of the spatial distribution of trace elements in an urban-industrial area
Article.Authors: Kozłowski R.; Ludew M.
Article.Abstract: Biomonitoring using needles, in particular two-year-old needles of the Scots pine ( Pinus sylvestris L.), is a recognised method for assessing the intensity of atmospheric deposition of trace elements in urban and industrial environments. The aim of this study was to characterise the spatial variation in pollution levels in Starachowice (SE Poland) by analysing the accumulation of ten trace elements in the needles. The study material was collected from a representative network of sampling sites covering zones with varying levels of anthropogenic pressure, including areas affected by industrial and transport emissions, as well as reference zones. Measurements were performed using a high-resolution spectrometric technique suitable for the analysed metals (ICP-MS/TOF), and the concentrations obtained were subjected to statistical analysis, including principal component analysis (PCA). The results showed significant variation in element accumulation, clearly indicating increased metal deposition in areas with intensive industrial activity, heavy road traffic, as well as in municipal and residential areas. Concentrations in peripheral zones were close to the reference levels, confirming the local nature of emission sources. These studies support the usefulness of Pinus sylvestris needles as a bioindicator of trace element deposition and may form the basis for delimiting zones with varying levels of anthropogenic pressure and potential impacts on environment. Furthermore, this research is significant from the perspective of implementing the principles of sustainable development (Goal 11 – sustainable cities and communities).

Article.Title: Synergistic valorization of oil palm empty fruit bunch and pome sludge for balanced erosion control and runoff quality
Article.Authors: Akhtar N.; Almanasir Y.; Syakir M.; Muhammad S.; Yusuff M.; Hussain R.; Husain P.; Alzahrani A.; Khan A.; Gunawan A.; Alghamdi A.
Article.Abstract: The palm oil sector confronts significant sustainability challenges due to massive biomass waste generation, particularly Oil Palm Empty Fruit Bunches (OPEFB) and Palm Oil Mill Effluent (POME). This study aimed to valorize OPEFB-POME materials into biodegradable soil pellets in three distinct ratios to determine the optimum sludge ratio and evaluate their efficacy in mitigating soil erosion, surface runoff quality, and environmental sustainability. Rainfall simulation experiments were conducted on loamy sand, utilizing standardized soil characterization within erosion control plots at five application rates (T1, T2, T3, T4, and T5 g/ft 2 ) to evaluate the balance between physical protection and runoff quality. The results revealed that Pellet II (40:60 OPEFB-to-sludge ratio) exhibited the optimal dimensional stability, while application rate T2 provided the best balance between erosion control and runoff quality. Despite maximal pellet coverage (T5) decreasing turbidity by 97.80%, it exceeded the environmental thresholds for chemical oxygen demand (192 mg/L) and phosphorus (4.59 mg/L). Despite this rate reducing the nutrient load relative to higher application rates, it still introduced phosphorus levels exceeding eutrophication thresholds, marking it as a best-compromise solution rather than a completely benign intervention and providing the highest degree of balanced performance between physical protection and chemical runoff loading. This study highlights that OPEFB-POME pellets reflect an effective by-product valorization pathway, providing an integrated option for enhancing resource recovery in the palm oil sector by balancing soil conservation with aquatic environmental protection.

Article.Title: Assessment of resting-state prefrontal haemodynamic fluctuation characteristics in male university students who have received curling training using fNIRS technology
Article.Authors: Zhu T.; Wang L.; Zhang Z.; Sun X.; Li J.; Wang C.; Qin Y.; Mu L.; Wu H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study compared the amplitude of resting-state low-frequency haemodynamic fluctuation over the prefrontal cortex between curling-trained and curling-naive young adults. Forty-two right-handed male undergraduates were included (21 trained, 21 controls). Functional near-infrared spectroscopy recorded 10 min of resting-state data across 22 prefrontal channels, of which the middle 8 min were analysed. Using oxyhaemoglobin as the principal indicator, three amplitude indices were compared, the absolute (ALFF), within-participant standardised (zALFF) and fractional (fALFF) values, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction and mixed-design models for spatial structure. First, overall prefrontal ALFF was lower in the trained group with no Group x Channel interaction, and right frontopolar channel CH13 survived correction. Second, the Group x Channel interaction was significant on zALFF, with greater relative prominence at left dorsolateral channel CH17 and a borderline reduction at CH13; decomposition showed that this difference was carried by hemispheric balance rather than by differentiation among prefrontal regions. Third, fALFF showed no group difference, and deoxyhaemoglobin effects were directionally consistent. Finally, an exploratory analysis found greater relative prominence at right ventrolateral CH14 among participants trained for seven or more years. Because the design is cross-sectional and no cognitive task was administered, these are associations and the functional labels are candidate interpretations.

Article.Title: Principal component analysis enhanced pigeon-inspired optimization for function optimization and multi-scenario UAV path planning
Article.Authors: Xu H.; Chen Y.; Lei M.; Li J.; Huang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Standard Pigeon-Inspired Optimization (PIO) suffers from premature convergence, low accuracy, and blind search direction on ill-conditioned and multimodal problems. This paper proposes a Principal Component Analysis enhanced PIO algorithm (PCA-PIO) that introduces PCA into the map-compass operator to extract principal directions from the advantageous population for anisotropic directional search, combined with an adaptive stagnation detection and restart mechanism. Experiments on 12 benchmark functions, the modern CEC2017 and CEC2022 test suites, and $$D=100$$ high-dimensional tests show that PCA-PIO significantly outperforms PIO and CPIO in convergence accuracy and robustness across all tested functions, and outperforms PSO on 10 out of 12 classical benchmark functions (with comparable performance on the remaining 2) (PSO attains lower average ranks on the CEC hybrid/composition suites). Although it still lags behind GWO on ill-conditioned and multimodal functions, it achieves up to three orders of magnitude improvement over PIO and CPIO on the Rosenbrock function, consistent with the No Free Lunch theorem. The improvements are statistically confirmed by Bonferroni-corrected Wilcoxon tests. UAV 3D path planning in mountainous, urban, and maritime scenarios under explicit kinematic feasibility constraints further demonstrates that PCA-PIO achieves optimal or near-optimal path length, minimal turning angles, and the highest success rates, showing excellent engineering practicality.

Article.Title: Decentralized handover authentication for internet of vehicles based on dual blockchains
Article.Authors: Son S.; Kwon D.; Kwon H.; Park Y.
Article.Abstract: In the Internet of Vehicles (IoV), vehicles communicate with roadside units (RSUs) over open wireless channels, and frequent handovers create a critical security surface. We propose a decentralized handover authentication scheme based on a dual-blockchain architecture that separates authentication state according to its scope and lifetime. A global blockchain maintains long-term identities and public keys, whereas local blockchains shared among geographically adjacent RSUs store short-lived handover tokens. This separation enables intra- and inter-group handover authentication without pre-shared inter-RSU keys or a secure inter-RSU channel, while avoiding global replication of temporary credentials. We analyse security informally against conventional and blockchain-specific threats under the practical Byzantine fault tolerance (PBFT) fault bound, prove session-key security in the real-or-random model, and verify the protocol using AVISPA. Performance is evaluated through computation and communication costs compared with blockchain-assisted handover schemes and recent authentication frameworks, PBFT latency simulations, and SUMO-based mobility simulations across 135 scenarios. The results show that intra-handover requires 9.721 ms and 1664 bits, that newly issued tokens can be confirmed before the next handover in all evaluable cases even under a 2.138-s consensus delay, and that per-RSU token storage decreases in proportion to the number of local blockchain groups.

Article.Title: Transparent sociodemographic inference on reddit from self-declarations
Article.Authors: Cinus F.; Monti C.; Bajardi P.; De Francisci Morales G.
Article.Abstract: Sociodemographic information provides critical context for interpreting digital behavior and its societal implications in many computational social science settings. However, the labels used to train and validate current inference methods frequently rely on researcher-defined proxies or opaque modeling assumptions. This can make demographic measurement difficult to audit, especially when inferred attributes are used to interpret population-level patterns. Here, we study sociodemographic inference on Reddit using over 850 000 public user self-declarations of age, gender, and partisan affiliation as an explicit source of supervision. We train models on sparse subreddit participation signals and compare simple probabilistic models with embedding-based baselines commonly used for Reddit analysis. Across coarse binary classification and aggregate quantification tasks, Multinomial Naive Bayes (NB) often performs better than more complex alternatives. Relative to the unsupervised state-of-the-art embedding method, NB improves ROC AUC by up to \(19\%\) . Under true supervision, it maintains quantification error below \(15\%\) for gender and year of birth. The models produce calibrated and interpretable outputs, thus supporting uncertainty estimation and subreddit-level feature importance analysis. These results position self-declarations as an explicit and auditable source of supervision for studying both user-level and population-level sociodemographic patterns on Reddit. By grounding labels in user-provided statements, the framework reduces reliance on researcher-selected proxies and supports transparent aggregate analyses of online communities.

Article.Title: Drug repurposing via high throughput 3D spheroids screening in rare cancer treatment
Article.Authors: Yonk M.; Nuszen H.; Tora M.; Du Y.; Lim M.; Federici T.; Hoang K.; Neill S.; Wang Y.; Li Y.; Yao B.; Boulis N.; Brat D.; Lei K.
Article.Abstract: Rare cancers comprise over 200 distinct types and account for 20–25% of U.S. cancer diagnoses yet receive limited therapeutic investment due to small patient populations and resource constraints. Drug repurposing offers a viable strategy, and large-animal models such as minipigs provide physiologically realistic platforms for preclinical evaluation. However, scalable systems for systematically screening large drug libraries in rare cancer models remain unavailable. We developed an integrated pipeline combining a minipig spinal cord glioma (SCG) model with miniaturized high-throughput screening (HTS). Primary SCG cells were cultured in 3D platforms for rapid screening of bioactive compounds. Lead candidates underwent validation through 3D spheroid assays, in vivo xenografting, RNA sequencing, immunohistochemistry, and histological analysis. Human SCG tissue samples and population-level datasets assessed translational relevance. HTS screening identified Clofoctol as a lead compound with potent glioma growth inhibition in both primary SCG cells and xenograft models. Studies revealed pleiotrophin (PTN) as a key target, with expression patterns in human SCG samples, establishing association and potential translational validity. Integration of large-animal cancer models with drug-repurposing pipelines and HTS platforms is feasible and effective for rare cancer drug discovery. This approach successfully identified Clofoctol, an FDA-approved compound with therapeutic potential for spinal cord gliomas and establishes a scalable model applicable to other orphan cancers.

Article.Title: TAGLN2-mediated ORAI1 stabilization promotes Ca2+-NF‑κB-dependent inflammatory responses in rifampicin allergy
Article.Authors: Dong Y.; Yao Y.; Wu L.; Li X.; Wang P.; Chen L.; Gao Y.; Li Y.; Zhou Z.; Liu J.; Bai C.; Liu Z.; Liang J.
Article.Abstract: Rifampicin-induced delayed-type hypersensitivity presents a significant challenge during standard anti-tuberculosis therapy, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly elucidated. This study investigates the role of the actin-binding protein Transgelin-2 (TAGLN2) in the pathogenesis of T cell-mediated rifampicin hypersensitivity. A clinical cohort comprising 12 rifampicin-hypersensitive patients and 12 rifampicin-tolerant controls was enrolled. High-resolution proteomic profiling of peripheral blood mononuclear cells revealed a distinct upregulation of TAGLN2, PRTN3, ANXA3, POU2F1, S100A8/A9, and PCNA in three rifampicin-hypersensitive patients compared to three tolerant controls. These findings were validated by Western blotting and RT-qPCR, which confirmed the overexpression of these candidates in allergic cohorts, alongside elevated serum levels of TNF-α and IL-1β. Functional enrichment highlighted calcium-dependent protein binding, cytoplasmic translation, and secretory granule lumen pathways. PPI network analysis revealed two synergistic modules: Inflammatory/Effector Hub and Biosynthetic Hub. In vitro experiments confirm that overexpression of TAGLN2 in patient-derived T cells potentiated NF-κB activity, and TAGLN2 levels exhibited a significant positive correlation with pro-inflammatory cytokine expression. Cell surface biotinylation and calcium flux assays further revealed that TAGLN2 facilitates the retention of the calcium channel ORAI1 at the plasma membrane, thereby amplifying intracellular Ca 2+ influx; Conversely, TAGLN2 knockdown abrogated these effects. Furthermore, knockdown or pharmacological inhibition of ORAI1 not only suppressed NF-κB activation and cytokine secretion but also downregulated TAGLN2 expression, suggesting the existence of a positive feedback loop. Collectively, our findings indicate that TAGLN2 drives rifampicin-associated delayed-type hypersensitivity by stabilizing membrane-bound ORAI1, enhancing Ca 2+ influx, and triggering NF-κB-dependent pro-inflammatory cytokine production. This study identifies TAGLN2 as a critical mechanistic node, highlighting its potential as both a diagnostic biomarker and a therapeutic target for drug-induced hypersensitivity.

Article.Title: A hybrid meta-heuristic optimisation and unsupervised learning framework for predictive stability enhancement of single-machine infinite-bus power systems
Article.Authors: Kumar G.; Singh M.; Nishad P.; Sayyad J.
Article.Abstract: Accelerating renewable penetration into modern interconnected grids has amplified low-frequency electromechanical oscillations, eroding the dynamic stability margins of synchronous generators. A unified two-phase framework is proposed to address Power System Stabiliser (PSS) parameter optimisation and real-time stability estimation for the Single-Machine Infinite-Bus (SMIB) benchmark. In Phase I, three nature-inspired meta-heuristic algorithms, namely Ant Colony Optimisation (ACO), Harris Hawks Optimisation (HHO), and Passing Thought-Based Optimisation (PTBO), tune the PSS lead-lag parameters $$\{K_{\textrm{PSS}},T_{1},T_{2}\}$$ by minimising the Integral of Time-weighted Absolute Error (ITAE) of rotor speed deviation across a 50 MVA SMIB benchmark. MATLAB/Simulink simulations over three disturbance severities confirm that HHO achieves the lowest settling time (3.5 s), while PTBO attains the lowest ITAE cost observed in these experiments (1514.5) within 10 iterations. In Phase II, the optimised SMIB dynamic-response dataset trains and cross-evaluates three unsupervised machine learning (ML) models, K-Means clustering, Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), and Self-Organising Maps (SOM), for real-time PSS parameter estimation under unseen operating conditions. Evaluation by Silhouette Score, Davies-Bouldin Index (DBI), and Calinski-Harabasz (CH) Score ranks GMM best across all three metrics (Silhouette $$=$$ 0.2485; DBI $$=$$ 1.458; CH $$=$$ 393.68), confirming its superiority in representing the non-spherical, correlated structure of the disturbance feature space. On closed-loop performance, however, SOM is the strongest model, giving the shortest settling time in two of the three disturbance cases and the largest mean settling-time reduction at 23.3%; SOM is accordingly identified as the best overall model for stabiliser parameter estimation, and GMM as the best representation of the feature space. Quantitatively, settling time falls from 9.5 s uncontrolled to 3.5 s, a reduction of 63.2%, and from 5.2 s under conventional tuning, a reduction of 32.7%; peak speed excursion falls from $$+1.68$$ to $$+1.20$$ relative to the conventional stabiliser, a reduction of 28.6%; the lowest observed ITAE is 1514.5 against 1519.0 and 1521.0 for the two competing optimisers; parameter estimation reduces settling time by 17.3%, 22.1%, and 23.3% on average for K-Means, GMM, and SOM respectively relative to a fixed nominal stabiliser; and estimation completes in approximately 0.3 ms against 30–45 s for a full re-optimisation. The framework is demonstrated on a single-machine infinite-bus benchmark under offline simulation, and the timing figure establishes computational feasibility for a real-time implementation rather than real-time capability itself.

Article.Title: Zhixin: dataset construction and instruction fine-tuning for LLM-based mental disorder diagnosis
Article.Authors: Zhao X.; Liu S.; Sun F.; Dong Y.; Wang Y.; Ge C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Automatic diagnosis of mental disorder from chief complaints is an appealing but challenging task. Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown rich knowledge and strong reasoning ability in medical domain. However, mental disorder diagnosis based on chief complaints requires highly specialised knowledge. Lack of corresponding resources hinders LLMs performance on this task. To address this problem, we collect 6,780 complaint-diagnosis pairs spanning 29 different types of mental disorders from a specialized hospital as the dataset. Meanwhile we conduct detailed data cleansing and manual proofreading to protect the privacy. On this basis, we propose the model named Zhixin , a LLM for mental disorder diagnosis fine-tuned on the proposed dataset. The experimental results show that Zhixin outperforms the state-of-the-art approaches in terms of automatic evaluation. It surpasses 3-shot DeepSeek-R1 by 18.54 $$\%$$ on Overall Accuracy . Meanwhile, human evaluation results show that the generated response from Zhixin ensures the Accuracy , Safety and Professionalism , which are critical to the diagnosis of mental disorder. In-depth analysis of category-wise performance sheds light on the future research direction, suggesting the focus on relatively rare metal disorders.

Article.Title: Tissue and plasma expression patterns and bioinformatic analysis of miR-15a-5p, miR-145-5p, miR-221-3p, and miR-455-3p in primary pterygium
Article.Authors: Dal A.; Özkan H.; Keçeli H.; Gül A.; Yıldız H.; Kutluksaman B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pterygium is a fibrovascular ocular surface disorder driven by proliferative, angiogenic, and fibrotic processes, with high postoperative recurrence and no established molecular markers. While several microRNAs (miRNAs) have been implicated in pterygium tissue, whether these alterations extend to the circulation has not been established. This exploratory study evaluated the tissue and plasma expression of miR-15a-5p, miR-145-5p, miR-221-3p, and miR-455-3p in primary pterygium and explored their candidate molecular targets through integrated bioinformatic analysis. In this prospective case-control study, 25 patients with primary, nasal, grade 3 pterygium and 25 cataract-surgery controls were enrolled. Paired tissue and plasma samples were obtained from each participant, and miRNA expression was quantified by RT-qPCR using the 2 −ΔΔCt method; statistical comparisons were based on − ΔCt values. Discriminatory performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Validated and predicted target genes were retrieved from miRTarBase and miRDB, followed by Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes pathway enrichment, Gene Ontology enrichment, and protein-protein interaction network analyses. All four miRNAs were significantly upregulated in pterygium tissue compared with control conjunctiva. miR-15a-5p showed the greatest tissue upregulation (approximately 11-fold) and the strongest discriminatory performance (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.919; sensitivity 0.72, and specificity 0.96). A concordant upregulation was detected in plasma, where miR-15a-5p and miR-455-3p retained significant, albeit moderate, discriminatory value (AUC = 0.723 and 0.722). The selected miRNAs showed different correlation patterns in the pterygium and control groups. Target genes were significantly enriched in cancer-associated, PI3K-AKT, cell cycle, apoptosis, and transforming growth factor-beta pathways, with MYC, PTEN, KRAS, BCL2, and VEGFA identified as candidate hub genes. The four miRNAs we examined were upregulated in pterygium tissue and a similar, though weaker, pattern was present in plasma. miR-15a-5p separated pterygium from control tissue well and in plasma both miR-15a-5p and miR-455-3p showed moderate discriminatory value. Their candidate targets cluster in pathways related to proliferation, apoptosis, angiogenesis, and TGF-β signalling. Given the cross-sectional design and the inclusion of grade 3 lesions only, these findings should be seen as hypothesis-generating. Larger studies covering different clinical grades, with longitudinal follow-up, are needed before any role in disease monitoring can be considered.

Article.Title: Prognostic value of systemic inflammation markers in advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma treated with second-line nivolumab: a real-world European study
Article.Authors: Martínez-Lago N.; González Villarroel P.; Carral Maseda A.; Fernández Montes A.; Covela Rúa M.; Costa Rivas M.; Reboredo Lopez M.; Cameselle García S.; De Dios Álvarez N.; Varela Ponte R.; Cousillas Castiñeiras A.
Article.Abstract: Nivolumab is a standard second-line therapy for advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), based on pivotal phase III trials largely conducted in Asian populations. Real-world evidence in Western patients remains limited. Systemic inflammation- and nutrition-based indices have been proposed as prognostic biomarkers in immunotherapy but remain scarcely validated in ESCC. We conducted a retrospective multicenter study across six institutions of the Galician Research Group on Gastrointestinal Tumors (GITuD). Eligible patients had histologically confirmed advanced or unresectable ESCC progressing after platinum-based chemotherapy or within six months of curative-intent therapy. All patients received nivolumab monotherapy between April 2019 and January 2023. Clinical outcomes were assessed using RECIST v1.1 and Kaplan–Meier estimates. Prognostic indices included NLR, PLR, SII, LDH, albumin, NAR, GIPI, and GRIm. Cut-off values for NLR, PLR, SII, and NAR were derived from cohort-specific ROC analyses and should be considered exploratory. NLR, PLR, SII, and NAR were additionally evaluated as continuous covariates. GIPI and GRIm were assessed in separate multivariable Cox models adjusted for ECOG PS and rapid-progressor status. Forty-five patients were included. Median age was 60.9 years, 80% were male, and 26.7% had ECOG PS 2. Rapid progressors accounted for 35.6% of the cohort. The objective response rate was 17.8% and disease control rate was 40.0%. After median follow-up of 37 months, median overall survival was 9.66 months (95% CI, 5.49–15.64) and progression-free survival 3.38 months (95% CI, 2.63–5.26). In univariate categorical analyses, NLR, SII, NAR, and GRIm were significantly associated with overall survival. When evaluated as continuous covariates, NLR and NAR remained significantly associated with overall survival, whereas PLR and SII did not. In separate multivariable models adjusted for ECOG PS and rapid-progressor status, both GRIm and GIPI were significantly associated with overall survival. No indices were significantly associated with progression-free survival. Safety findings were consistent with the known safety profile of nivolumab. Clinical outcomes associated with second-line nivolumab in this European real-world cohort were broadly consistent with those reported in pivotal clinical trials. Several systemic inflammation- and nutrition-based indices showed exploratory associations with overall survival, including GIPI and GRIm in separate clinically adjusted multivariable models. These findings require validation in larger independent cohorts.

Article.Title: Genome and methylome of the root crop table beet (Beta vulgaris)
Article.Authors: Holzweber T.; Dorn K.; Rasaki L.; Dohm J.; Himmelbauer H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Table beet ( Beta vulgaris subsp. vulgaris var. vulgaris ), also known as red beet, garden beet, or beetroot, is an important crop with both nutritional and agricultural value, yet high-quality genomic resources for this taxon are limited. We present the chromosome-scale genome assembly RefTab-1 based on PacBio and Hi-C data of the inbred table beet genotype W357B. The assembly has a size of 668.6 Mbp and an N50 of 72 Mbp, with 96% of the assembly anchored to nine pseudo-chromosomes. We annotated 64% repetitive DNA, 24,863 protein-coding genes, and 10,405 non-coding RNA loci including a 5S rDNA cluster on chromosome 4. Genome-wide methylation profiling using EM-seq revealed high levels of cytosine methylation in repeats and context-specific methylation in gene bodies and promoters. We propose three terpene synthase candidate genes based on functional annotation and based on their location near a genetic marker on chromosome 8 previously associated with geosmin concentration, responsible for the earthy aroma of table beet. Comparative analysis with sugar beet indicated overall structural conservation and a 9 Mbp inversion on chromosome 9. These high-quality resources for table beet will enhance genetic, epigenetic, and comparative studies in Beta vulgaris , advancing beet biology and breeding programs.

Article.Title: Study on freeze-thaw damage of antique-style bricks based on grey relational analysis
Article.Authors: Liu J.; Liu Y.; Yu D.; Yin S.; Li W.; Luo Y.
Article.Abstract: To comprehensively evaluate the damage evolution of six types of antique-style bricks under freeze–thaw cycling and to identify rapid indicators for assessing their frost resistance, 60 freeze–thaw cycles were applied to the bricks, and the mass loss, compressive strength loss, and pore-structure evolution were measured. The entropy weight method (EWM) was employed to integrate the mass loss rate and the compressive strength loss rate into a comprehensive freeze–thaw damage index, and grey relational analysis (GRA) was used to establish the relational degrees between this index and the mechanical properties, water absorption, total porosity, and the porosity growth rates of four pore-size intervals. The results show that the six brick types differ significantly in mechanical properties, water absorption, and post-freeze–thaw mass and strength losses, and that a high initial compressive strength does not necessarily correspond to high frost resistance. Among them, the large city-wall brick 03CZ from Shanxi exhibited the best frost resistance, with a mass loss rate of 0.37% and a compressive strength loss rate of 2.15%, whereas 04NT showed the poorest performance, with a mass loss rate of 3.67% and a compressive strength loss rate of 25.18%. After freeze–thaw cycling, micropores smaller than 20 nm decreased while mesopores of 20–50 nm and 50–100 nm increased in all six bricks. The grey relational analysis results show that, among the pre-freeze–thaw indicators, the flexural-to-compressive strength ratio (0.783) had the highest relational degree with the comprehensive freeze–thaw damage index, indicating that this ratio should be given primary attention in discriminating the frost resistance of antique-style bricks; among the post-freeze–thaw indicators, the growth rate of 50–100 nm pores (0.655) was the highest. The severity of brick damage depends more on the migration of micropores to mesopores than on the absolute increase in the total pore volume.

Article.Title: Performance enhancement of efficient clustering and routing protocol for wireless sensor networks using fuzzy with adaptive frilled lizard optimization
Article.Authors: Prakash N.; Maheswari R.; Vimalnath S.; Kumareshan N.
Article.Abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) have a multitude of applications, particularly in the surveillance and tracking of non-human activities. Sensor nodes (SNs) in WSNs are known for their limited lifespan, primarily due to continuous sensing, which leads to rapid battery depletion. Consequently, energy consumption is a significant research issue in applications facilitated by WSNs. Immediate energy conservation emphasizes accurate categorization and the most efficient path determination from the SN to the receiver. Current clustering and routing methodologies in wireless sensor networks often struggle to equilibrate energy consumption and maintain network performance, leading to suboptimal longevity and efficiency. The work proposes a fuzzy with adaptive Frilled Lizard Optimization (AFLO) for cluster head (CH) selection and a Cross-layer based Improved Dwarf Mongoose Optimization (CL-IDMO) routing algorithm to select the most efficient shortest route for reducing energy consumption in WSN. Fuzzy clustering is a method that categorizes SNs according to their data and energy levels, enabling the creation of clusters that are both adaptable and efficient. In the proposed framework, cluster head selection is performed using key parameters such as residual energy level, node centrality, cluster density, distance to the base station (BS), and cluster head selection probability to ensure balanced energy utilization and effective cluster management. AFLO improves the CH selection process by dynamically adapting to network conditions, maintaining equitable energy consumption allocation, and prolonging network longevity. Furthermore, CL-IDMO improves data routing by incorporating cross-layer parameters, optimizing routing paths to reduce energy consumption and enhance data transmission efficiency. The suggested method outperforms existing clustering and routing methods across multiple measures. The metrics include an 85% Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR), 0.08 Mbps throughput, 22% channel load, 5 seconds end-to-end delay (E2ED), a packet loss rate (PLR) of 5.8%, a communication cost of 0.12%, a buffer occupancy rate of 20.9%, a network life cycle (NLT) of 4000 rounds, and an energy consumption of 40 mJ for 500 nodes.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: wireless sensor networks; routing protocols; metaheuristic optimization; clustering protocols; network performance optimization
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Computer Networks and Communications > Energy Efficient Wireless Sensor Networks; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithms Research; Computer Science > Computer Networks and Communications > Mobile Ad Hoc Networks

Article.Title: Climbing ungulates as modifiers of tree morphology: a case from the Formosan serow
Article.Authors: Takada H.; Tezuka N.; Sun N.; Pei K.
Article.Abstract: Tree climbing is rare among ungulates because of morphological constraints, yet its ecological significance remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the characteristics of trees climbed by Formosan serows ( Capricornis swinhoei ) and the potential consequences of this behavior for tree morphology. We surveyed trees with bite marks and compared their structural traits and surrounding environments with those of non-climbed trees. Serows preferentially climbed trees with horizontally oriented trunks and numerous branches that can serve as footholds. Climbing also occurred more frequently in open environments with high light availability. The bite marks reached heights of up to 680 cm, indicating that serows can access a vertical range of foliage beyond that available to most terrestrial ungulates. In addition, climbed trees frequently exhibited bending structures in which trunks transitioned from vertical to horizontal orientations, suggesting that repeated climbing and browsing may contribute to modifications of tree morphology. These findings indicate that serows selectively use structurally accessible trees to exploit high-quality resources and may modify tree morphology through their climbing and foraging behavior. Our study highlights a previously underappreciated interaction between ungulates and forest structure and suggests that serows may function as ecosystem engineers despite their relatively small body size.

Article.Title: Development of anti-CCR4 scFv-photoabsorber Conjugate for Enhanced Near-infrared Photoimmunotherapy Targeting Adult T-cell Leukemia Cells
Article.Authors: Yang Y.; Maeda N.; Nakajima K.; Sugiura N.; Tadokoro T.; Miyamoto K.; Morioka H.; Ogawa M.; Maenaka K.
Article.Abstract: Near-infrared photoimmunotherapy (NIR-PIT) is an emerging, highly-selective, cancer-therapeutic modality that combines molecular targeting with photochemistry. The mechanism of NIR-PIT involves conjugating antibodies with the photosensitizer IRDye700DX (IR700), which is activated by NIR light to induce localized cell death. This approach offers several advantages, including minimal off-target effects, rapid immunogenic cell death, and precise tumor-antigen targeting. Conventional full-length antibodies are effective in many therapeutic applications; however, their Fc regions can trigger unintended immune responses and effector-function-mediated toxicity, thereby reducing safety and efficacy of antibody-based therapies. To overcome these challenges, we investigated the feasibility of using a mogamulizumab-derived, single-chain variable fragment (Moga-scFv) targeting CC chemokine receptor 4 (CCR4), a common marker in adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATL). The Moga-scFv–IR700 conjugate was successfully prepared and efficiently killed CCR4-positive cells upon NIR irradiation at levels similar to Moga-IgG. This study demonstrates the potential of Moga-scFv–IR700 in NIR-PIT for ATL treatment, supporting the feasibility of scFvs as alternative antibody format.

Article.Title: A generalizable pipeline for specialty-curated postmarket device surveillance: a reference implementation in neurosurgery
Article.Authors: Qureshi K.; Gok E.; Fayaz M.; Yangi K.
Article.Abstract: Spontaneous-reporting medical-device databases, including the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience (MAUDE) database, store most of their content as unstructured free text. A generalizable methodology for converting these narratives into structured, searchable data is needed for specialty-level surveillance. We developed a 4-layer AI pipeline and applied it to the complete neurosurgical-device subset of the FDA MAUDE database from inception through March 31, 2026. Neurosurgical device product codes were identified from the complete FDA Product Classification list using a dual large language model (LLM) classifier with human adjudication. Each report was processed by: (1) dual-LLM specialty filtering of FDA product codes; (2) schema-constrained narrative labeling using a 15-class failure-mode taxonomy and an 8-class outcome taxonomy, with identifier-based input-output joining; (3) asymmetric semantic embedding into a 768-dimensional vector space indexed with hierarchical navigable small-world (HNSW) graphs and 8-bit scalar quantization; and (4) precomputed device-, manufacturer-, and category-level aggregate roll-up. Outcomes included labeling coverage; inter-LLM agreement on the specialty filter (Cohen κ); semantic-retrieval quality (Jaccard@10 against exhaustive nearest-neighbor search; top-1 match rate); and population-level label-to-record alignment (content-keyword hit rate; random-baseline expectation, 6.7% under the 15-class taxonomy). The neurosurgical corpus comprised 2,086,176 reports filed against 10,102 distinct devices from 641 manufacturers across 9 categories. The specialty filter evaluated 7,058 candidate FDA product codes and, after adjudication, yielded 527 neurosurgical codes. Against the adjudicated reference, the primary classifier (gemini-2.5-flash) had a sensitivity of 0.42, a specificity of 0.996, and a positive predictive value of 0.89, and the second-opinion classifier (claude-sonnet-4-5) had a sensitivity of 0.39, a specificity of 1.00, and a positive predictive value of 1.00; the 2 models agreed on 6,947 of 7,058 codes (Cohen κ = 0.75), and human adjudication with a recall-validation pass resolved discordant codes and recovered false negatives. The pipeline produced complete, schema-valid labels for 2,072,457 of 2,072,722 narratives (99.99% labeling coverage). Semantic-retrieval Jaccard@10 against exhaustive search was 0.83 (top-1 match rate, 0.81). Population-level content-keyword hit rates ranged from 32.9% to 91.5% across keyword classes, against the 6.7% rate expected under random assignment. Against an adjudicated reference standard from 2 clinically qualified reviewers, failure-mode labels reached 67% accuracy and outcome labels 58% (both far above majority-class baselines; inter-reviewer κ 0.90 and 0.85), and clinician-rated semantic retrieval reached precision@10 of 0.85. A 4-layer AI pipeline, designed to be generalizable, structured the free-text content of a national device adverse-event database on a proof-of-concept specialty subset. The architecture may transfer to other MAUDE specialty subsets and to analogous spontaneous-reporting databases.

Article.Title: Regional immune zonation of the healthy human ileocolic mucosa and its disruption along the adenoma–carcinoma sequence
Article.Authors: Valciukiene J.; Lastauskiene E.; Laurinaviciene A.; Jakubauskas M.; Kryzauskas M.; Valkiuniene R.; Jasiunas E.; Augulis R.; Garnelyte A.; Stundiene I.; Kavoliunas J.; Silinskaite U.; Poskus T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Colorectal carcinogenesis evolves through a stepwise adenoma–carcinoma sequence accompanied by changes in mucosal immune surveillance. Yet the spatial organisation of healthy ileocolic immunity, and its change during dysplastic progression, remain incompletely defined. We quantified immune cell density (cells/mm²) by compartment-resolved immunohistochemistry for CD3, CD8, CD20, and CD68 with HALO digital image analysis in 820 tissue sections from 57 individuals (14 controls, 16 small [≤ 1 cm] and 17 large [> 1 cm] adenomas, 10 carcinomas). In health, T cells were strongly zonated: enriched in the terminal ileum, decreasing toward the distal colon, and more abundant in stroma than epithelium. This zonation became progressively disrupted across the sequence. Lesional CD3 + density was higher in small than large adenomas. Normal-appearing mucosa showed two additional changes: ileal CD8 + depletion and expansion of right-colonic epithelial CD68 + macrophages. Both followed significant stage-trends. The epithelial CD68 + expansion remained significant after adjustment for age and sex but not after multiplicity correction; the ileal CD8 + change was no longer significant after either adjustment and is hypothesis-generating. These data establish a quantitative reference map of healthy ileocolic immune zonation and suggest that disruption of this spatial organisation, including within normal-appearing mucosa, may represent an early feature of colorectal tumorigenesis.

Article.Title: Quality, reliability, and accountability of patellofemoral pain-related short videos on three Chinese social media platforms: a cross-sectional comparative study
Article.Authors: Ren J.; Lin J.; Zhao L.; Mou L.
Article.Abstract: Patellofemoral pain (PFP) is a common cause of anterior knee pain, but the quality of related short-video information remains unclear. This cross-sectional study evaluated PFP-related videos on BiliBili, Douyin, and Rednote. Using one formal Chinese query, we screened the first 100 default-ranked videos per platform on 5 March 2026. After removing six repeated URL occurrences and reconciling five duplicated URL clusters to single adjudicated values, 184 unique within-platform listings were analysed, of which 12 probable cross-platform repost clusters (26 listings) were retained in the primary analysis. Video characteristics and engagement were extracted, and two raters independently assessed quality, reliability, and accountability using the Global Quality Score (GQS), modified DISCERN (mDISCERN), and Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) criteria. Median GQS, mDISCERN, and JAMA scores were 2 (IQR 2–3), 2 (IQR 2–3), and 2 (IQR 2–2), respectively. Overall, 11.4% achieved a GQS of 4 or 5, and none met all four JAMA criteria. Douyin scored higher than BiliBili on GQS and mDISCERN; Douyin and Rednote scored higher than BiliBili on JAMA. Uploader subgroup findings were exploratory, and engagement–score associations varied by platform. Pre-adjudication agreement was strong for GQS (weighted κ = 0.869) and good for mDISCERN (ICC = 0.804) and JAMA (ICC = 0.847). The findings represent one query at one time point and do not assess factual accuracy.

Article.Title: A hybrid swarm intelligence and evolutionary approach for adaptive fuzzy segmentation in energy-efficient WSNs
Article.Authors: Vimalarani C.; Sangeetha K.; Nallakumar R.; Srihari K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Wireless Sensor Network have become popular in a variety of applications including environmental monitoring and healthcare systems. But the biggest problem in WSNs is still how to optimize the energy consumption to improve the network lifetime. In dynamic node conditions, the wireless sensor networks need energy-aware clustering to prolong the lifetime. The proposed research work is Adaptive Fuzzy Guided Segmentation which constructs a round-wise eligibility pool for cluster-head using residual energy and communication context, and constructs a stable cluster by refining the cluster stability using GA. The method is tested with various node density and random deployments, with typical radio models and named WSN baselines. Results show increased lifetime, lowered energy consumption, increased delivery reliability, and controlled latency. This hybrid algorithm makes use of fuzzy logic to adaptively cluster sensor nodes based on the dynamic parameters like energy, communication range etc., which is different from the conventional clustering algorithms. The framework uses Swarm Intelligence to optimize cluster formation, making sure that data is transmitted effectively and with a low energy cost. The Evolutionary Algorithm also optimizes iterative processes, making the trade-offs. To prove the proposed algorithm is better than the existing algorithms (PSO and GA), detailed simulations are done. It enhances its network lifetime, packet delivery ratio, and overall energy consumption. With fuzzy segmentation, the clusters are dynamically generated and the hybrid algorithm has a very good energy load distribution among nodes, as the network changes conditions. The proposed solution is innovative and presents a scalable solution that can be realized in the various network sizes and topologies and is suitable for usage in smart environments with limited energy resources.

Article.Title: Intelligent resource orchestration for large-scale cloud environments using hybrid AI models
Article.Authors: Singhal S.; Verma P.; Anushree N/A.; Rakesh N.
Article.Abstract: The importance of cloud computing lies in its provision as a critical infrastructure for large-scale applications and emerging technologies. Modern cloud computing infrastructures demand efficient resource orchestration for dynamic workloads and service-level agreement requirements. In this regard, traditional scheduling techniques are not efficient. This study proposes a novel intelligent resource orchestration framework based on hybrid artificial intelligence techniques that combine deep learning, reinforcement learning, and optimization algorithms for efficient resource management. The proposed architecture has different layers for analytics, decision engines, and orchestration functions that enable efficient resource management. Experimental results confirm that the proposed framework improves resource usage efficiency, task completion time, and operational cost efficiency for large-scale cloud computing infrastructures. The hybrid AI-based orchestration technique is efficient for scalability and adaptability for future cloud computing.

Article.Title: Improvement of germination properties in barley (Hordeum vulgare) seeds damaged by Sitophilus oryzae infestation via dielectric barrier discharge plasma treatment
Article.Authors: Fard M.; Martami M.; Mohajer M.; Obajemihi O.; Hamidi A.; Ebrahimi N.; Rashvand M.; Ghomi H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Insect‑damaged barley seeds typically exhibit poor germination and are often discarded. This study investigated whether dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) cold plasma could improve the germination of partially viable seeds of barley seeds severely damaged by Sitophilus oryzae , to our knowledge, no study has been conducted in this area. Damaged seeds were treated at 13–19 kV for 1–9 min. Although the highest germination potential was observed at 19 kV for 9 min, the 16 kV for 1 min treatment provided the best overall improvement across germination and seedling growth parameters. Under this treatment, germination potential increased by 80%, germination rate by 59%, and vigor index by 51% compared to untreated damaged seeds. Shoot and root lengths increased by 41% and 24%, respectively, while fresh and dry weights also increased significantly. Furthermore, electrolyte leakage decreased by 40%, indicating improved membrane integrity. Plasma treatment roughened the seed surface (SEM), altered O–H and C–H functional groups (FTIR), and reduced the water contact angle from 89.88° to 27.83°, making the surface highly hydrophilic. Color changes were minor (ΔE = 3.99). These results demonstrate that DBD cold plasma, particularly at 16 kV for 1 min, can improve germination and early growth of insect‑damaged barley seeds through surface physical and chemical modifications that enhance wettability and water uptake. This chemical‑free method can offer a practical strategy to add value to otherwise wasted seeds, reducing post‑harvest losses and supporting sustainable agriculture.

Article.Title: Music performance anxiety and restrictive dietary behaviors: a moderated serial mediation model
Article.Authors: Zhang C.; Tan F.; Feng Y.; Luo M.
Article.Abstract: Working in high-evaluation and competitive stage environments, music performers are prone to anxiety and physical-cognitive biases that are associated with maladaptive Restrictive Dietary Behaviors. Existing studies have not systematically examined the psychological correlates and protective boundary conditions of this association. Based on the Transactional Theory of Stress and Coping, this cross-sectional study examined the serial mediating roles of Multidimensional Perfectionism and Body Image Concern, as well as the moderating role of Trait Mindfulness, in the association between Music Performance Anxiety and Restrictive Dietary Behaviors, so as to provide theoretical and practical references for the psychological support and eating-health management of music performers. A total of 723 valid samples were collected from college music students and professional music practitioners in eastern China via anonymous online questionnaires. Participants completed scales measuring Music Performance Anxiety, Multidimensional Perfectionism, Body Image Concern, Restrictive Dietary Behaviors, and Trait Mindfulness. SPSS 26.0 and Mplus 8.3 were used to conduct common method bias test, reliability and validity analysis, correlation analysis, as well as serial mediation and moderation effect tests. (1) Music Performance Anxiety significantly positively predicted Restrictive Dietary Behaviors; (2) Multidimensional Perfectionism and Body Image Concern independently mediated the relationship between Music Performance Anxiety and Restrictive Dietary Behaviors; (3) a significant serial mediating effect existed via the path of Multidimensional Perfectionism to Body Image Concern; (4) Trait Mindfulness significantly and negatively moderated two of the three examined pathways (the direct Music Performance Anxiety to Restrictive Dietary Behaviors path, and the Body Image Concern to Restrictive Dietary Behaviors path); the moderating effect on the Multidimensional Perfectionism to Restrictive Dietary Behaviors path was in the same direction but did not reach statistical significance; (5) full measurement invariance between university students and professional musicians was not supported, and the two subgroups differed significantly in their mean levels of Music Performance Anxiety, Multidimensional Perfectionism, and Body Image Concern, indicating the pooled associations above should be interpreted with this heterogeneity in mind. Music Performance Anxiety is associated with higher Restrictive Dietary Behaviors, with this association statistically accounted for in part by individuals’ Multidimensional Perfectionism and Body Image Concern; Trait Mindfulness is associated with a weaker expression of this pattern. Given the cross-sectional design, these findings should be read as evidence of association rather than of a confirmed causal or temporal sequence. The results nonetheless point to Trait Mindfulness as a candidate protective psychological factor for music performers and offer preliminary ideas for psychological support and healthy-behavior management for art practitioners, to be tested more directly in future longitudinal and experimental work.

Article.Title: Muscle stem cell treatment mitigates stress-associated multiorgan dysfunction in D-galactose-induced accelerated aging mice and improves behavior in naturally aged mice
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Zhao S.; Xu Y.; Jiang G.; Li L.; Xu Z.; Zhang S.; Li D.
Article.Abstract: Muscle stem cells (MuSCs) support skeletal muscle repair, but whether systemic MuSC administration mitigates stress-associated multiorgan dysfunction remains unclear. We evaluated MuSCs in a D-galactose-induced accelerated aging model and performed additional behavioral validation in naturally aged mice. Female KM mice received D-galactose for eight weeks with or without weekly intravenous MuSCs. Behavioral performance, serum injury, oxidative and inflammatory biomarkers, multiorgan histopathology, and heart/skeletal muscle transcriptomes were assessed. Naturally aged mice were tested for motor and cognitive behaviors after MuSC treatment. MuSC administration improved motor endurance, foraging, and spatial learning/memory in D-gal-treated mice, reduced ALT/AST and BUN, increased SOD/GSH-Px, and decreased TNF-alpha/IL-6. Histology showed attenuation of hepatic lipid accumulation, renal/glomerular injury, dermal and gastrointestinal atrophy, pulmonary inflammation, sarcopenia, lipid deposition, and fibrosis, with lower p16/p21 in heart and gastrocnemius. Transcriptomics indicated partial restoration of metabolic, genomic-stability, and immune pathways. In naturally aged mice, MuSCs improved rotarod, food-maze, navigation, and spatial-probe performance. These data support MuSCs as a candidate transient cell-based modulator of oxidative stress-associated dysfunction and behavioral decline, while further work is required to define cell fate, sex-specific responses, cell specificity, and chronological aging mechanisms.

Article.Title: NMR reveals an ordered but conformationally exchanging N-terminus in the chemokine CCL11
Article.Authors: Jang J.; Bannister S.; van Aalst E.; Farshadfar C.; Wylie B.
Article.Abstract: The C-C motif Chemokine Ligand 11 (CCL11) is a promiscuous messenger for multiple C-C motif G protein-coupled receptors in the human immune system. Previously solved structures, including CCL11 bound to a truncated CCR3 peptide and apo-CCR3 bound to the heterotrimeric G protein, provide clues to the initiation of ligand-receptor interaction; however, a consensus on the full-length interaction has yet to be reached. Here, we present a structure of CCL11 solved utilizing liquid-state Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) data in buffered solution at pH 5.0 with 100 mM NaCl. The resulting ensemble exhibits not only secondary structural elements defined differently from past reports, but also a less dynamic N-terminus, showing local exchange correlated with the 30s-loop. Fast (ns) and intermediate (µs-ms) dynamics were measured via a combination of relaxation techniques, revealing that most N-terminal and 30s-loop residues exchange, while only a few residues at the N-terminal tip move freely. We hypothesize that this local exchange contributes to induced binding, and that N-terminal and 30s-loop dynamics could be related to chemokine promiscuity. Rigid-body docking to an AlphaFold2 CCR3 model generated candidate geometries in which the CCL11 N-terminus reaches orthosteric pocket residues previously implicated in the literature. In total, our results highlight that dynamics captured on two distinct timescales together show that the N-terminus of CCL11 is ordered as a tail but undergoes conformational exchange linked to the 30s-loop.

Article.Title: Artifact-resilient deep learning segmentation for enhanced structural and functional cardiac analysis
Article.Authors: Singh R.; Nagarajan N.; Thakur Y.; Nathiya D.; Praveena A.; Nagendra Kumar U.; Almubarak H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cardiac imaging is essential in diagnosing heart disease. Imaging methods like x-rays, ultrasound, computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can show the heart in great detail. Given AI’s superior learning capabilities, these imaging approaches can be greatly improved. It is critical to use methods that can withstand artifacts in cardiac MRI when segmenting the ventricle in order to guarantee accurate structural and functional investigation of those tissues. While many have focused on making algorithms better, very few have addressed the problem of artifacts in predictions and how they affect accuracy. To make earlier techniques more resistant to these phenomena, we investigate pretrained network fine-tuning in this work. Our suggested approach makes heavy use of data augmentations designed to resemble such objects. The findings significantly improved the baseline segmentations, with improvements up to 0.06 Dice score and 4 mm Hausdorff distance. Our proposed process consists of three steps: resampling and preprocessing of data and performing normalisation; loading and setting training parameters of a pretrained model; training the loaded model with the data, which is augmented by modifying it in various ways according to intensity and deformations.The 3D data is called volumes, and the pictures are the short-axis slices. We used 3D for data resampling, preprocessing, and normalization, and we used slices for data augmentation. During the segmentation job, our technique primarily focuses on fine-tuning an encoder. We resampled the volumes after orienting them to the canonical orientation. The area of interest was subsequently treated with a crop. After then, the data was divided into two parts: training and validation. Out of the total individuals, 20% were used for validation. Secondly, a histogram was generated from the training data and used to standardize the intensity. Using the aforementioned histogram, we standardize all sets. The data used in our research came from the Extreme Cardiac MRI Analysis Challenge, specifically the Respiratory Motion subset. The results showed a group of five people using the same four breathing intensity throughout the assessment. The ED and ES phases were recorded and labeled by a skilled radiologist for all individuals and breathing intensity.

Article.Title: Understanding sleep-related attentional failures while driving in young drivers and associations with motor vehicle crashes, near misses, and nocturnal sleep
Article.Authors: Schmickler J.; Eijkeme C.; Quan S.; Czeisler C.; Robbins R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sleep-related attentional failures are a significant contributor to road traffic fatalities, with young drivers disproportionately affected. This study explored psychological and behavioral correlates of attentional failures while driving among a geographically diverse sample of high school students. A cross-sectional survey of 923 licensed high school drivers across the United States assessed attentional failure-related behaviors, behavioral intentions, beliefs (attitudes, social norms, self-efficacy), sleep behaviors, and history of both a near miss and crash. Adjusted logistic regressions examined predictors of attentional failure-related behaviors and intentions, as well as associations between the behavior, sleep, and near miss/crash history. Participants were 50.9% female, 43.9% male, and 5.2% other. High school drivers were between 16 and 20 years of age or older, with the most commonly reported age being 18 years (50.5%). Most participants (80.1%) reported never having attentional failures, while 19.9% reported doing so with any frequency. Logistic regression revealed that unfavorable attitudes (aOR: 0.82, 95%CI: 0.75–0.88), social pressure to avoid falling asleep while driving (aOR: 0.58, 95%CI: 0.51–0.66), and self-efficacy beliefs regarding the ability to avoid falling asleep while driving (aOR: 0.64, 95%CI: 0.57–0.73) were inversely associated with reports of attentional failures. Surprisingly, long sleep (> 10 h) on school (aOR: 2.8, 95%CI: 1.6–4.8) and weekend nights (aOR: 4.1, 95%CI: 2.4–6.7) was associated with an increased risk for sleep-related attentional failures. Use of the snooze alarm on school days (aOR: 2.64, 95%CI: 1.71–4.09) and reports of obtaining insufficient sleep duration most nights per month (aOR: 1.78, 95%CI: 1.22–2.59) were associated with increased reports of attentional failures. Reports of attentional failures were associated with near misses (aOR: 2.28, 95% CI: 1.58–3.29) and crashes (aOR: 2.56, 95% CI: 1.69–3.87), with substantially stronger associations observed when attentional failures were due to sleepiness, for near misses (aOR: 5.01, 95% CI: 2.44–10.26) and crashes (aOR: 15.79, 95% CI: 4.61–54.11), respectively. Fortunately, approximately 80% of participants reported never experiencing attentional failures, yet those who did report sleep-related attentional failures were associated with poor sleep health and history of near misses and crashes. Future research is needed to support sleep health in young people.

Article.Title: The HBCCL panel provides a comprehensive resource of human B-cell cancer cell line data
Article.Authors: Haraldsdóttir H.; Brøndum R.; Høholt H.; Jakobsen M.; Bøgsted M.; Stensballe A.; Dybkaer K.; Due H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A more comprehensive characterization of the biological and molecular mechanisms underlying cancer cell lines remains essential. Despite the rise of complex experimental systems, cell line models persist as indispensable tools for high-throughput screening due to their robust proliferation kinetics and technical reproducibility with minimal ethical considerations. In this study, we introduce a data-comprehensive human B-cell cancer cell line (HBCCL) panel comprising 17 diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) cell lines and 18 multiple myeloma (MM) cell lines. Characteristics and disease-related molecular subtypes of the cell lines are presented as well as subclassification of DLBCL cell lines into LymphGen subtypes (BN2, MCD, N1, EZB, A53, and ST2). The panel includes integrated cell line datasets from drug dose–response screens (11 agents), genotyping, gene expression, miRNA, and proteomic profiling. The utility of this resource is illustrated with examples of analyses applicable to investigating molecular mechanisms and drug responses in B-cell malignancies.

Article.Title: Salivary cortisol measurements for reliable numerical maximum concentration after the low dose 1 µg ACTH intravenously in healthy individuals
Article.Authors: Grensman A.; Acharya B.; Nilsson G.; Sundquist J.; Wändell P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We examined the potential use of the 1 µg adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) stimulation test to identify the optimal timing for measuring the maximum response after stimulation and to assess whether salivary cortisol might replace serum cortisol at that time. Data were collected from a trial investigating yoga as a stress management intervention. We recruited healthy, working participants experiencing stress ( n = 36, including 8 men), aged 25–62, from the healthcare sector. We obtained simultaneous serum and salivary cortisol samples six times over 60 min following an intravenous injection of 1 µg ACTH. Data were analyzed with the Fisher-Pitman permutation test and the general estimation equation. Most peak responses in serum and saliva occurred at 30 and 40 min. Additionally, the median maximum response values at these times were similar to the medians across all sampling times ( P = 0.1 and P = 0.06, respectively). Cortisol response curves in serum and saliva were parallel at 30–40 min ( P = 0.83). Salivary cortisol may substitute for serum cortisol in the 1 µg ACTH stimulation test to assess maximum stress-response capacity in people at risk for stress-related disorders, as in this study, with sampling only at 30 and 40 min.

Article.Title: Monitoring of brown adipose tissue with β3-adrenergic receptor agonist using [18F]FDG PET/CT and [123I]mIBG SPECT/CT
Article.Authors: Choi Y.; Lee E.; Park J.; Baik J.; Chung H.; Kang J.
Article.Abstract: Brown adipose tissue (BAT) is a thermogenic organ regulated by sympathetic nervous activation via β3-adrenergic receptors (β3-AR) and serves as a target for metabolic imaging. This study evaluated BAT activation induced by the selective β3-AR agonist CL316,243 using [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT and [ 123 I]mIBG SPECT/CT in male BALB/c mice. Following daily intraperitoneal treatment with CL316,243, uptake of two tracers in interscapular BAT was quantified using volume-of-interest analysis and ex vivo biodistribution. Uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) expression in BAT was measured by Western blot. Both [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT and [ 123 I]mIBG SPECT/CT successfully monitored CL316,243 induced BAT activation. [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT demonstrated visually conspicuous and quantitatively higher CL316,243-induced uptake differences compared with [ 123 I]mIBG SPECT/CT. Conversely, ex vivo biodistribution revealed a higher relative fold increase in [ 123 I]mIBG uptake in interscapular BAT than in [ 18 F]FDG uptake following treatment. White adipose tissue also showed increased uptake of two tracers with CL316,243 treatment. Western blot confirmed elevated UCP1 expression in BAT after CL316,243 treatment. These findings indicate that under the imaging conditions used in this study, [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT showed greater visual and image-derived contrast than [ 123 I]mIBG SPECT/CT, demonstrating complementary roles for both tracers in evaluating BAT biology.

Article.Title: Low methane emissions following experimental bog rewetting
Article.Authors: Chimner R.; Keller J.; Kolka R.; Lilleskov E.; Stuart J.; Tarpey R.; Tucker C.; Zalman C.; Lamit L.; Kane E.
Article.Abstract: Peatlands cover only 3–4% of the world’s land surface, but store one-third of global soil carbon. Undisturbed peatlands act as long-term net carbon sinks, but draining peatlands can convert them into net sources of greenhouse gases. Rewetting drained peatlands can improve CO 2 sequestration; however, there is concern that rewetting produces additional CH 4 . Our experimental bog restoration project found that rewetting drained peat resulted in only a modest increase in CH 4 emissions, which was still lower than undrained natural peat at similar water table levels. We also saw an increase in CO 2 uptake. We hypothesize that peat chemistry is limiting CH 4 emissions after rewetting, with strong differences between the peat’s physical and chemical characteristics in the rewetted vs. reference treatments. Our results, and others, indicate that rewetting drained peatlands will likely increase CH 4 efflux, but post-restoration emissions typically remain below those of naturally occurring peatlands, suggesting that CH 4 concerns are not necessarily a barrier to restoration if done correctly.

Article.Title: A sequential dose-finding study of fentanyl during remimazolam induction for tracheal intubation in adults
Article.Authors: Lee M.; Koh H.; Cho S.
Article.Abstract: Remimazolam is associated with relatively stable hemodynamics during anesthetic induction but does not provide analgesia to attenuate the sympathetic response to endotracheal intubation. Although several adjunctive agents may attenuate this response, opioids are commonly used during induction. This prospective sequential study aimed to estimate the ED 50 of fentanyl associated with hemodynamic stability during remimazolam bolus induction. This prospective sequential dose-finding study used Dixon’s up-and-down method in adults undergoing elective surgery with bolus remimazolam 0.2 mg/kg. Success was defined as maintaining mean blood pressure and heart rate within 20% of baseline for 2 min post-intubation. The primary analysis used centered isotonic regression to estimate the ED 50 from the full sequential allocation. To evaluate the quality of induction, integrated hemodynamic indices including average real variability (ARV) and time in target range (TTR) were derived from hemodynamic data. Overall, thirty-one patients were included in the final analysis. The full-sequence centered isotonic regression estimate of ED 50 was 2.85 µg/kg (90% confidence interval [CI] 2.241–3.313). The ARV and TTR showed no marked variation across the observed fentanyl dose range. In this prospective sequential study, the full-sequence centered isotonic regression estimate of the ED 50 of fentanyl associated with hemodynamic stability during tracheal intubation under remimazolam bolus induction was 2.85 µg/kg. This preliminary, protocol-specific estimate requires confirmation in larger prospective studies and should not be interpreted as a recommended fentanyl dose for routine clinical practice.

Article.Title: Novel pathway for curcumin utilization found in diverse Gram-negative soil-dwelling bacteria with evidence of horizontal gene transfer
Article.Authors: Taylor C.; Nelson M.; Hamza M.; Switzer W.; Patrick T.; Biggs J.; Seward A.; Parks S.
Article.Abstract: Bacteria are known to contain complex pathways to metabolize a plethora of recalcitrant compounds, especially in soil and gut microbiomes. Plant-derived polyphenols are often considered to be non-pharmaceutical antimicrobials that exist within both the soil and gut. Curcumin is the polyphenol active compound in turmeric root ( Curcuma longa ) and demonstrates anti-inflammatory, antioxidative, and anti-cancer properties. The NADPH-curcumin/dihydrocurcumin reductase gene (curA), yielding curcumin-reducing enzymatic activity, was previously discovered in the genomic DNA of Escherichia coli strains isolated from stool samples. We hypothesized that curA may also be present within soil-dwelling bacteria. In the current study, we isolated 15 Gram-negative soil-dwelling bacteria with the highly conserved curA gene, using growth selection strategies including Winogradsky columns and Rapid Flask Cultures containing turmeric powder. Using in silico synteny analysis, we found that curA is one gene within a highly conserved synteny cluster of 13 genes (ydcU, ydcV, patD, yncL, ortT, ydcY, ydcZ, mnaT, curA, mcbR, yncD, yncE, and ansP) encoding metabolic-related proteins including enzymes, transport systems, and genetic regulators. Reverse-transcriptase quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) analysis showed curA and 12 genes within the synteny cluster were significantly upregulated during 48 h growth with 1% turmeric in E. coli str. K-12 substr. DC10B (positive control strain) and soil-isolated Chryseobacterium sp. Notably, ATR-FTIR data supported preferential cell-associated accumulation/retention of curcuminoid-derived material consistent with uptake. Metatranscriptomics analysis of soil-turmeric growth slurries identified active transcription of genes associated with central carbon metabolism and amino acid biosynthesis pathways, consistent with the transcriptional activation of the curA synteny cluster observed in vitro. In addition, within the same soil-turmeric slurries, we observed transcriptional activation of putative type IV and type VI secretion system genes, consistent with potential mobility of the synteny cluster. Collectively, the present study provides substantial genomic, transcriptional, and biochemical evidence consistent with a candidate curcumin utilization pathway in Gram-negative bacteria.

Article.Title: Predicting fluorinated gas solubility in deep eutectic solvents using machine learning and deep learning approaches
Article.Authors: Sheikhshoaei A.; Kazemi-Beydokhti A.; Weigand J.; Sanati A.
Article.Abstract: This paper introduces a data-driven framework by deploying machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) architectures to estimate fluorinated gas (F-gas) absorption capacities in deep eutectic solvents (DESs). The proposed approach aims to support the screening and design of DESs for gas capture applications by correlating thermodynamic and molecular descriptors with experimentally measured solubility data. Four predictive models, namely Gradient Boosting (GBoost) and Random Forest (RF) as ML techniques, and TabNet and GrowNet as DL architectures, were developed and compared using a dataset of 440 experimental data points, incorporating temperature, pressure, and critical molecular descriptors of both F-gases and DESs as input parameters. Further evaluation was conducted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis and the leverage approach. DL models, especially GrowNet, demonstrated high accuracy and strong generalization on test data. GrowNet outperformed all others, achieving the lowest test errors (MSE = 0.0046%, R² = 0.9985). SHAP analysis revealed pressure and temperature as the most important variables affecting the model predictions, with critical temperature and acentric factor of F-gases also playing significant secondary roles. The leverage method confirmed model reliability, with over 98% of data points lying within its applicability domain. The results demonstrate that ML- and DL-based methods can provide effective predictive tools for estimating F-gas solubility in DES systems.

Article.Title: Performance analysis of underwater wireless optical communication under egg turbulence and link orientation
Article.Authors: Shetty C.; Ramavath P.; Kumar P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Underwater Wireless Optical Communication (UWOC) is a promising technology for high-data-rate underwater communication due to its high bandwidth and low latency, with potential applications in Internet of Underwater Things (IoUT) systems. However, UWOC performance is significantly affected by underwater channel impairments such as turbulence, optical attenuation, and transmitter–receiver pointing errors. In this work, a comprehensive physical-layer performance analysis of UWOC systems is presented by considering Exponential Generalized Gamma (EGG) turbulence and different link orientations. Horizontal, vertical, and diagonal link configurations are investigated to characterize the influence of link orientation and depth-dependent turbulence on system performance. The EGG distribution is employed to model underwater turbulence over weak-to-strong turbulence regimes, while optical attenuation and pointing errors are incorporated into the channel model. Closed-form analytical expressions for average bit error rate (BER), outage probability (OP), and channel capacity (CC) are derived for the considered link configurations. For vertical and diagonal links, the underwater propagation path is modeled using multiple non-mixing layers with layer-dependent turbulence characteristics. The analytical results are validated through Monte Carlo simulations, showing good agreement between the analytical and simulation results. The obtained results demonstrate the effects of link orientation, depth-dependent turbulence, attenuation, and pointing errors on UWOC system performance, providing useful insights for the design of reliable underwater optical communication links for potential IoUT applications.

Article.Authors: Han W.; Seo W.; Kim D.; Lee H.; Kim S.; Kim J.
Article.Abstract: We propose an optical see-through glasses-type AR display that utilises an off-axis, multiplexed holographic optical element (HOE) as an optical combiner. Based on an anamorphic freeform optics approach, we optimise the optical path from the eye pupil to the holographic display panel, achieving a highly compact form factor with a diagonal field of view (FOV) of 60° and an eye relief of 21 mm. A prototype in the form of eyeglasses is fabricated, and its imaging performance is experimentally verified. In addition, we present an optical design that incorporates a multi-point-recorded HOE to expand the eyebox, addressing the inherent limitation of Maxwellian-view-type displays. The simulation-based design shows the feasibility of significant eyebox enlargement (7 mm by 7 mm) while maintaining the compact form factor. This study provides practical insights into the design and optimisation of compact, wide-FOV AR glass display systems using HOEs as combiners, and further suggests a viable path towards improved usability through eyebox expansion.
