Article.Title: A provenance-aware hybrid deepfake detection framework integrating perceptual hashing and explainable CNNs for robust multimedia forensics in social IoT environments
Article.Authors: Alshenaifi R.; Mishra S.; ALmutairi S.
Article.Abstract: The rapid advancement in generative AI technology have increased the problem of detecting deepfakes, especially in the decentralized social Internet of Things (Social IoT), where multimedia data gets modified constantly in various ways such as by compressing, resizing, and metadata removal. Conventional techniques usually attempt to solve either manipulation detection or provenance verification independently, lacking flexibility and efficient implementations capable of running on edge devices. This paper introduces a provenance-aware hybrid deepfake detection framework based on CNN and perceptual hashing (pHash) as an efficient approach for provenance validation. EfficientNet-B0 and ResNet50 are utilized as CNN-based detectors, while an adaptive and confidence-aware fusing technique helps determine the ratio between the confidence of detectors and provenances. Without valid provenance information, the hybrid technique switches to detector-based inference. Grad-CAM was used to visualize the reasoning of the proposed framework. Experiments were conducted on the Deepfake and Real Images dataset using different combinations with fixed train-validation-test splits over three random seeds. The proposed framework achieved a mean AUC of 0.9973 with EfficientNet-B0 under the hybrid setting, while maintaining highly competitive classification performance with ResNet50 across multiple experimental configurations. Cross-validation experiments on the Celeb-DF benchmark dataset further demonstrated strong generalization capability and robustness across multiple random seeds. Provenance survivability evaluation in the case of Social IoT transformations, like resizing, compression, and Gaussian blur, resulted in an average survival probability of 47.05%. It is crucial to note that adaptive hybrid inference should be applied for such tasks. The ablation study, statistical test of significance, computational complexity evaluation, and qualitative Grad-CAM visualization have provided additional proof of the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed approach. The proposed framework demonstrates strong performance across the evaluated benchmark datasets while maintaining computational efficiency, explainability, and provenance awareness. These findings indicate the potential of the proposed hybrid framework for robust multimedia forensic analysis in decentralized Social IoT environments; however, the results should be interpreted within the scope of the evaluated datasets and dissemination scenarios.

Article.Title: Phenotypic and genotypic screening for root-knot nematode (Meloidogyne incognita) resistance in tomato
Article.Authors: Jadhav R.; Selvakumar R.; Chaukhande P.; Kranti K.V.V.S K.; Hussain Z.; Yadav R.; Muthusamy V.; Kalia P.; Kumar J.
Article.Abstract: Tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum L.) productivity is severely constrained by the root-knot nematode Meloidogyne incognita , which can reduce yields by 20–40% and, under heavy infestation, by more than 50%. To identify consistent sources of host resistance, 137 diverse tomato genotypes (exotic and indigenous cultivated lines, wild Solanum accessions, cherry types and released varieties) were evaluated under controlled artificial inoculation (2 J2 g –1 soil) across two contrasting seasons at ICAR-IARI, New Delhi. The inoculum, maintained as M. incognita race 1, was confirmed as M. incognita by perineal-pattern morphology and species-specific PCR. Phenotypic screening using the standardized root-knot gall index identified four Solanum peruvianum accessions (LA-1481, LA-1481-2, LA-2862 and LA-2802) that remained within the combined highly resistant/resistant group in both seasons, LA-1481 being highly resistant in both trials and LA-2862 shifting from resistant to highly resistant, whereas more than 70% of cultivated backgrounds were susceptible or highly susceptible, indicating a narrow resistance base. Pooled analysis of square-root-transformed gall counts under a completely randomized design showed a highly significant genotype effect, whereas neither the season effect nor the genotype × season interaction was significant. Of eighteen Mi -linked SCAR/CAPS primer pairs attempted, sixteen were scored across the panel and eight of these recorded resistance-associated calls, which were concentrated in the wild accessions but also occurred in a few cultivated lines; the Mi-3 -linked marker TG-263 showed the highest recorded concordance with the phenotypic classes (κ = 0.853), detecting resistance-associated alleles in LA-2862, LA-2802 and LA-1481. These accessions are promising donors, and the recorded marker profiles support their prioritisation, meriting confirmation through reproduction-based assays and multi-environment field evaluation.

Article.Title: A system dynamics-based approach to multi-dimensional damage reduction mining regulation and strategy in open-pit coal mines
Article.Authors: Sheng S.; Wang Z.; Zhang X.; Guo Q.; Liu W.; Lu X.
Article.Abstract: The environmental damage caused by open‑pit coal mining—including land excavation and occupation, groundwater disturbance, dust emissions, and carbon cycle imbalance—is not a collection of isolated phenomena but rather a systematically coupled ecological damage process driven by mining activities and mediated through pathway interactions among subsystems. Elucidating the transmission pathways and coupling mechanisms of these multidimensional environmental impacts is essential for achieving damage‑reduction mining and promoting the green transformation of mining areas. This study uses the Heidaigou Open‑Pit Mine as a case study and employs system dynamics to develop a multidimensional dynamic model comprising four subsystems: land protection, low‑carbon development, dust control, and groundwater control. This model is used to simulate the dynamic responses of various environmental damage indicators under single‑factor adjustments and multiple combined scenarios, identify the key regulatory factors, and reveal the transmission pathways linking different subsystems. The results indicate that mining parameters such as mining depth, slope angle, and working bench length act as the primary drivers of environmental damage, simultaneously influencing land degradation, carbon emissions, dust emissions, and groundwater inflow through synergistic or opposing responses. Among these parameters, mining depth exhibits the highest sensitivity for damaged land area, carbon emission intensity, total dust emission, and mine water inflow. Scenario simulations demonstrate that the synergistic strategy of combined bench mining and deep working bench optimisation achieves the greatest overall reduction in environmental damage, reducing the damaged land area, total dust emission, and mine water inflow by 8.66, 7.71, and 13.41%, respectively, while providing only a limited reduction in carbon emission intensity. The three-tier elasticity analysis further indicates that the cross-system transmission from mining parameters to carbon emissions is dominated by the “dust generation - auxiliary diesel consumption” pathway, which accounts for 78.3% of the path weight - higher than that of rainfall runoff (19.0%) and groundwater inflow (2.7%). This indicates that dust load, rather than mine water inflow, is the key coupling pathway through which mining parameters drive carbon emissions. This study reveals the intrinsic mechanism through which common mining parameters drive multidimensional environmental damage in open‑pit mining and establish coupling among environmental subsystems through pathway interactions. It provides systematic and quantitative regulation methods and decision‑making support for damage‑reduced mining in open‑pit coal mines.

Article.Title: Combining ability and heterosis analysis for growth, yield, and yield-related traits in watermelon (Citrullus lanatus) under arid conditions
Article.Authors: Ram G.; Choudhary B.; Naruka I.; Kumar P.; Yadav L.; Singh K.; Ola A.; Kumar N.; Kaswan H.
Article.Abstract: Exploitation of heterosis has substantially enhanced watermelon productivity; however, information on the combining ability of genetically diverse parental lines under hot arid environments remains limited. Identifying superior parental lines and hybrid combinations through combining ability and heterosis analysis is essential for watermelon improvement, particularly under hot arid environments where such information remains limited. Analysis of variance revealed significant differences among genotypes for all thirteen traits across both seasons, indicating substantial genetic variability. Both additive and non-additive gene effects were shown to be involved by significant general combining ability (GCA) and specific combining ability (SCA) mean squares for every characteristic. BIL-53, AHW/YF Selection-1, AHW/YF Selection-2, and Thar Tripti were found to be valuable breeding parents due to their improved GCA impacts for marketable fruit yield per plant and other commercially significant features. The hybrids Thar Tripti × Arka Shyama, Arka Shyama × AHW/YF Selection-1, and Arka Shyama × AHW/YF Selection-2 recorded up to 71.6% better marketable fruit output per plant than the commercial control by combining high per se performance with significant SCA effects and superior standard heterosis. Additionally, these hybrids performed well in terms of fruit number, average fruit weight, and earliness, demonstrating their potential for hybrid production in hot, dry climates. The study demonstrated the importance of both additive and non-additive genetic effects in the inheritance of growth and yield traits in watermelon. The parental lines BIL-53, AHW/YF Selection-1, AHW/YF Selection-2, and Thar Tripti emerged as promising donors for hybrid breeding, while the hybrids Thar Tripti × Arka Shyama, Arka Shyama × AHW/YF Selection-1, and Arka Shyama × AHW/YF Selection-2 were identified as superior combinations for developing high-yielding, climate-resilient watermelon hybrids adapted to hot arid environments.

Article.Title: Stress induced semiconductor to semimetal transition and tunable optical anisotropy in puckered bilayer GeTe: a first-principles study
Article.Authors: Rizvee H.; Chand M.; Neher B.; Ahmed F.
Article.Abstract: In this study, Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were employed to investigate a comparative analysis of structural, electronic, chemical bonding, phonon-dynamical, and optical properties of puckered monolayer and bilayer GeTe under applied tensile and compression stress ranging from − 1 to + 3 GPa. The indirect band gap is reduced by 76% compared to the monolayer (0.693 eV) in case of bilayer formation (0.166 eV). Under increasing biaxial compressive stress, the bilayer band gap progressively decreases and reaches a calculated zero-gap semimetallic state at approximately 0.55 GPa, characterized by band touching near the Γ point and the system is dynamically stable up to at least 3GPa, which was confirmed by phonon calculations. Based on Mulliken population analysis, the microscopic origin of gap closure is found to be progressive orbital rehybridization of Ge-Te bond. Compression is systematically red-shifted and amplified broadband optical absorption in direction dependent hierarchy inversion, leading to a mechanically tunable three-dimensional optical anisotropy. The results unveil puckered bilayer GeTe as a stress tunable platform for narrow-gap optoelectronics and pressure engineered quantum device architectures.

Article.Title: Hybrid architectures of CNN-ViT and SE-CNN with grad-CAM for monkeypox disease detection
Article.Authors: Mohsen S.; Zayed M.; Ibrahim A.; Abdel-Aziz M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In the aftermath of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, the monkeypox virus (MPV) emerged as a significant global health concern, leading the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare it a public health emergency. Accurate detection of monkeypox (Mpox) is challenging due to its similarity to other pox viruses such as measles and chickenpox. Conventional diagnostic methods often struggle to distinguish between these diseases, necessitating the development of more advanced diagnostic tools. This paper presents a novel approach to detect Mpox using two efficient deep learning (DL) models: the first one is a hybrid architecture of a Convolutional Neural Network—Vision Transformer (CNN–ViT), and the second model is a Squeeze-and-Excitation Convolutional Neural Network (SE-CNN). These models are employed for the classification of medical images into two categories: Monkeypox and Others. The proposed models are applied to a dataset of 1140 images, and utilize fine-tuning for the models’ hyperparameters. Data augmentation techniques are implemented for training images to maximize the models’ performance. Additionally, a gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) visualization technique is applied to explain the decision of the models and aid doctors in clinical decision-making. Experimentally, the accuracy, error matrix, area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, Recall, F1-score, and Precision are used to measure the performance of the proposed models. The CNN–ViT and SE-CNN achieve a testing accuracy of 97.80% and 96.05%, respectively, while the micro-average area under the ROC curve is 97% for CNN–ViT and 99% for SE-CNN. The weighted F1-score, Precision, and Recall for CNN–ViT are all 97.26%, 97.33%, and 97.27%, respectively, while for SE-CNN are 96.04%, 96.13%, and 96.05%, respectively. The proposed models provide a rapid and accurate method to differentiate Mpox from other cases, offering a valuable tool for healthcare professionals in the screening and diagnosis of Mpox.

Article.Title: Deconstructing overdispersion: a generative variance budget for luminescence dating from single grains to aliquots
Article.Authors: Şahiner E.
Article.Abstract: Overdispersion, the spread of equivalent-dose estimates beyond their measurement uncertainties, is the most reported and least interpretable number in luminescence dating: grain response, beta-dose heterogeneity, incomplete bleaching, mixing, fading, saturation, and understated errors produce the same value. Rebuilt from its physics as a variance budget, it yields four findings. Correlated intrinsic and dose-rate variance cannot be resolved from one dose distribution without an independent constraint. A boundary-calibrated test improves routine practice, but the detectable overdispersion falls only as \(n^{-1/4}\) with grain count n : most published datasets cannot resolve a modest real dispersion, and a realistic instrumental floor nearly doubles the limit. Log-dose skewness separates added-dose from loss mechanisms, yet co-acting mechanisms and a natively skewed dose-rate field mimic either, so shape statistics are prompts, not classifiers. Multi-grain averaging divides the diagnosable dispersion by an effective grain number, about eight for fifty bright-dominated grains, but leaves additive bias in place: a clean aliquot is not a clean sample. Read without these limits, a dispersion value credits an age to a mechanism the data cannot support; which mechanism acted is a measurement question, not a computational one. The framework matches reference software to 0.01 percentage points on published quartz datasets.

Article.Title: Spatiotemporal evolution and influential indicators of coupling coordination between new quality productive forces and high–quality development of the construction industry
Article.Authors: Xiang Y.; Huang S.
Article.Abstract: Against the backdrop of China’s ‘Dual Carbon’ goals and the strategic opportunity to develop new quality productive forces (NQPF), coordinated development between NQPF and the high-quality development of the construction industry (HQDCI) has emerged as an important pathway toward regional sustainability. This study examines the coupling coordination degree (CCD) between NQPF and HQDCI across 30 Chinese provinces from 2014 to 2023 and constructs comprehensive evaluation systems for both subsystems. The combined weighting-TOPSIS method is used to measure their development levels. By integrating the CCD model, exploratory spatial data analysis (ESDA), random forest (RF) and SHAP interpretation, this study evaluates coordination levels, reveals spatiotemporal patterns, and identifies influential indicators and regional differences in their model-based contributions. The CCD increased from 0.352 (mild imbalance) in 2014 to 0.453 (near imbalance) in 2023 and displayed an ‘east-high, west-low’ spatial pattern. Moran’s I showed strengthening spatial agglomeration, particularly after 2021. LISA analysis indicated a persistent High-High cluster in the Yangtze River Delta and Low-Low clusters in parts of western China. The RF results show that the ten most influential indicators (e.g., robot installation density, per capita number of patents, number of urban bridges, and technology market turnover) collectively explain 76.69% of the total feature importance. Regional SHAP analysis further uncovers heterogeneous mechanisms: eastern regions rely on intelligent infrastructure integration, central regions on economic scale leveraging scientific-educational resources, western regions require endogenous R&D investment and digital infrastructure and northeastern regions prioritize connotative urban renewal.

Article.Title: Profiles of everyday executive functioning in relation to adaptive behaviour in children and adolescents with Down syndrome
Article.Authors: Rossi E.; Onnivello S.; Locatelli C.; Marcolin C.; Sperti G.; Platè A.; Catapano F.; Colaianni S.; Vione B.; Cicilloni M.; Ramacieri G.; Lanfranchi S.
Article.Abstract: Executive functions (EF) are higher-order cognitive processes that support goal-directed behaviour. Previous research has shown that individuals with Down syndrome (DS) often experience EF impairments, with a profile of strengths and weaknesses. However within-group variability remains underexplored. The present study aimed to explore EF profiles in 111 children and adolescents with DS aged 7–17 years using caregiver-reported data from the BRIEF-2 scales. A latent profile analysis was conducted to derive EF subgroups and it revealed a three-profile solution: a Clinically Elevated Profile, characterised by widespread EF difficulties; a Moderate Difficulties Profile, with milder and more selective impairments; and a Preserved Profile, with scores largely within the normative range. These profiles differed in both overall severity and domain-specific configuration of EF. Significant differences emerged between the profiles in adaptive behaviour, assessed using Vineland-II standard scores, but not in verbal or non-verbal cognitive abilities, evaluated using the WPPSI-III. The most consistent effects were observed in Socialization. These findings demonstrate meaningful EF heterogeneity in school-aged children with DS and underscore the value of person-centered approaches in assessment and intervention, with important implications for individualised educational and clinical support.

Article.Title: Triglyceride-glucose index combined with DAS28-ESR predicts cardiovascular disease risk in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a national multicenter cohort study
Article.Authors: Ma X.; Chang T.; Yang Y.; Shen Z.; Xu H.; Liu Z.; Yao C.; Tang X.; Xia C.; Jiang Q.; Gong X.
Article.Abstract: Patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) face a significantly increased risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD). This study aimed to evaluate the combined association of systemic inflammatory activity and glucose-lipid metabolic abnormalities on long-term CVD outcomes in RA patients and to elucidate the dynamic trajectories of these factors during follow-up and their prognostic implications. This prospective longitudinal cohort study included 4,902 RA patients without baseline CVD. Baseline and follow-up status matrices (G1–G4 groups) were constructed using the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and DAS28-ESR score. Multistage nested Cox proportional hazards regression models were employed to assess the adjusted association of combined status and dynamic trajectories on incident CVD. Restricted cubic splines (RCS) quantified nonlinear associations, and the Delta method was used to estimate additive interaction measures. During a maximum 6-year follow-up, 355 incident CVD events occurred (7.24%). In the fully adjusted multifactorial model (Model 3), the baseline dual-high immune-metabolic status group (G4) showed significantly elevated incident CVD risk compared to the dual-low control group (G1) (HR 9.46, 95% CI 3.90–22.96, P < 0.001). Additive interaction analysis indicated a positive additive interaction (relative excess risk due to interaction [RERI] of 3.55; 95% CI, 0.46–6.64), with an AP of 0.38 (95% CI 0.16–0.60), supporting a positive departure from additivity on the relative hazard scale. RCS analysis showed nonlinear associations between both continuous variables and CVD risk ( P < 0.05). Dynamic trajectory analysis showed that persistent dual-high status (G4 → G4) during follow-up was associated with a higher risk of incident CVD (HR 6.95, 95% CI 2.06–23.41, P < 0.001), whereas the G2 → G3 trajectory showed a nonsignificant trend toward an increased risk of CVD (HR 1.24, 95% CI 0.28–5.48; P > 0.05). Baseline dual-high immune-metabolic status and adverse longitudinal trajectories were associated with incident CVD events in patients with RA after multivariable adjustment, with a positive additive interaction observed between high TyG and high DAS28-ESR. These findings support moving beyond an approach focused solely on inflammatory control by jointly considering inflammatory and metabolic status in CVD risk assessment and management.

Article.Title: YOLO-MAG: an edge-preserving and bilateral dual-gated YOLO11 network for small object detection in UAV aerial imagery
Article.Authors: Zhang R.; Zhang H.; Li T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Small object detection in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery is severely hindered by low spatial resolution, faint boundaries, drastic scale variations, and complex background interference. To address these vulnerabilities, we propose YOLO-MAG, an edge-preserving architecture built upon YOLO11 for aerial surveillance. First, the existing MEIS operator is integrated into the C3k2 framework and deployed across both the backbone and neck, forming a continuous edge-preserving feature path. Second, ACmix is embedded into the C2PSA block to combine global contextual modeling with local convolutional inductive bias. Third, the original single-gated GAC is reconstructed as a bilateral dual-gated module and incorporated into a modified feature pyramid network, in which the two feature branches jointly participate in estimating the modulation weights. These task-oriented architectural adaptations constitute the YOLO-MAG framework. Evaluated on the VisDrone2019 benchmark, YOLO-MAG-n achieves 40.4% mAP@0.5 and 24.5% mAP@[0.5:0.95], outperforming the YOLO11n baseline by 6.9 and 5.0 percentage points, respectively, while sustaining real-time inference at 136 FPS on an NVIDIA RTX 4080 GPU. Additional evaluation on UAVDT demonstrates consistent performance gains on a second aerial traffic dataset.

Article.Title: Micro-CT analysis of the maxillo–lacrimal complex in Plecotus auritus (Linnaeus, 1758) and description of the processus intersuturalis maxillo–lacrimalis (nova structura)
Article.Authors: Kłys G.; Socha P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The morphological organization of the maxillo–lacrimal region in the bat Plecotus auritus (Linnaeus, 1758) was investigated using micro-computed tomography (micro-CT). A consistent, bilaterally symmetrical anatomical complex was identified at the junction between the os maxillare and os lacrimale . This configuration includes a previously undescribed bony structure, the processus intersuturalis maxillo-lacrimalis (nova structura), proposed here as a descriptive anatomical term, located within the maxillo-lacrimal suture between the adjacent processus frontalis maxillae and processus nasalis ossis lacrimalis . The complex also includes a distinct additional opening, the foramen orbitonasale accessorium , clearly distinguished from the foramen infraorbitale. Serial sections further revealed the presence of a continuous canal, here termed the canalis maxillolacrimalis , with its course and opening into the nasal cavity clearly identifiable. All structures were consistently present in the examined specimens, exhibiting stable topography and high morphological repeatability. Available comparative descriptions suggest that this arrangement differs from the generalized mammalian condition, although directly comparable three-dimensional data remain limited. These findings demonstrate a consistent and previously unrecognized osteological organization of the maxillo-lacrimal region in P. auritus . Its functional significance remains unclear and requires further investigation.

Article.Title: EDGRU: edge-guided dual graph reasoning U-Net with spatial graph attention for infrared small target detection
Article.Authors: Huang X.; Song J.; Fu X.; Lu Y.; Yuan L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Detecting infrared small targets continues to be difficult because of indistinct object contours, intense background interference, and restricted multi-scale feature extraction. To tackle such problems, this work introduces EDGRU, an edge-oriented dual graph reasoning U-Net which simultaneously utilizes edge information and dual graph logic, and spatial graph attention for robust feature representation. Specifically, a multi-directional multi-order gradient edge module is designed to preserve weak structural details and suppress background interference. A dual graph reasoning framework enhances both local spatial dependencies and long-range semantic relationships, while spatial graph attention further strengthens topology-aware feature interaction to improve target-background discrimination. Empirical evaluations conducted on the NUAA-SIRST and NUDT-SIRST benchmarks reveal that EDGRU achieves the highest detection probability of 96.58% and 98.84%, respectively, while remaining competitive on other metrics, demonstrating enhanced resilience against complex environments and target scale fluctuations. The source code for this project is accessible at https://github.com/Huang-1015/EDGRU.git .

Article.Title: Deciphering the probiotic potential of Limosilactobacillus reuteri S8 in broilers through phenotypic and genomic analyses
Article.Authors: Tabashiri R.; Mahmoodian S.; Pakdel M.; Meimandipour A.; Amirzakaria J.
Article.Abstract: The ban on antibiotic growth promoters in poultry has increased the need for probiotics. This study evaluates Limosilactobacillus reuteri S8, isolated from the gastrointestinal tract of broiler chickens, using in vitro assays, whole-genome sequencing and comparative pan-genomics. The strain showed a log-based survival rate of 85% at pH 3.0 (a 1.2 log₁₀ reduction in viable count over 3 h) and a relative growth of 50.5% in 0.3% bile salts, consistent with the presence of the atp operon and nhaC . It adhered to Caco-2 cells more densely than a low-adhesion reference strain, a favourable prerequisite for potential competitive exclusion that warrants further verification in vivo, and the genome encodes a sortase A homologue, a putative adhesin and exopolysaccharide biosynthesis genes. Under the in vitro conditions tested, it displayed antagonistic activity against all indicator organisms, including reference strains of Escherichia coli ATCC 25,922 and Salmonella enterica ATCC 14,028, consistent with multiple lactate dehydrogenase variants and a putative Class III bacteriocin locus. Pan-genome analysis with 62 reference genomes identified 155 strain-specific gene clusters, mainly associated with cellular biogenesis and DNA maintenance. The strain was resistant to tetracycline and ampicillin, and the genome carries the acquired antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) tet(W) , tet(L) and lnu(A) ; tet(L) lies next to a recombinase gene ( xerC ), which warrants investigation of its possible mobility. Therefore, while commercial application is cautioned against due to the presence of acquired ARGs, this strain remains a valuable biological model for investigating antimicrobial resistance reservoirs in avian commensals.

Article.Title: Nutritional quality and genetic differences of five amaranth cultivars revealed by metabolome profiling and whole-genome sequencing
Article.Authors: Sedeek K.; Zuccolo A.; Toor U.; Sanikommu K.; Kantharajappa S.; Rivera-Serna L.; Wing R.; Mahfouz M.
Article.Abstract: Amaranth ( Amaranthus spp.) is an emerging crop that combines outstanding nutritional value in both edible grain and leaves with strong agronomic resilience, positioning it as an attractive candidate for sustainable food systems. Comprehensive metabolomic and genomic resources are, however, still lacking for many cultivated amaranths, limiting targeted breeding and genome-editing efforts. Here we combine non-targeted ultra-performance liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC–MS/MS) metabolome profiling with PacBio HiFi whole-genome sequencing to characterise five widely grown grain amaranth cultivars: coral fountain (CF), emerald tassels (ET), golden giant (GG), hopi red dye (HR) and New Mexico (NM). Metabolite profiling identified 426 and 420 structurally known compounds in grain and leaf tissues, respectively, revealing cultivar-specific differences in sulfur amino acids, vitamins, chlorogenic acids, and potentially anti-nutritive compounds such as oxalate and raffinose-family oligosaccharides; on average, CF and ET showed the most favourable nutritional profiles. De novo assembly using PacBio HiFi data produced reference genomes of 465–484 Mb per cultivar (46.9–48.7% repetitive elements), with gene models supported by Iso-seq transcript evidence. Together, these resources accelerate trait discovery, marker-assisted breeding, and genome-editing-based improvement of amaranth as a future nutritional crop.

Article.Title: Color matching ability of single-shade resin-based composites: an in vitro study
Article.Authors: Akbaba M.; Barutçugil Ç.
Article.Abstract: Single-shade resin-based composites (RBCs) are marketed as matching a wide range of tooth shades, although supporting evidence remains limited. This in vitro study evaluated the color-matching ability of Omnichroma (OMN), Vittra APS Unique (VTR), and Charisma Diamond One (DIA) against four shade backgrounds. Molds were fabricated from a conventional composite in A1, B1, JE, and BW shades, and standardized cavities were restored with each RBC (n = 15; 180 specimens). Color was measured using a clinical spectrophotometer. Two CIEDE2000 (ΔE₀₀) outcomes were calculated: polymerization-induced color change and the difference between the background mold and restored specimen. Data were analyzed using two-way ANOVA, followed by Welch's ANOVA and Games–Howell tests. Polymerization-induced ΔE₀₀ ranged from 3.31 to 10.18, differed among materials in three of the four shade backgrounds ( p < 0.001), and exceeded the perceptibility (0.8) and acceptability (1.8) thresholds in all groups. Only VTR against JE produced clinically acceptable matching (1.29 ± 0.24), although the difference remained perceptible. All other combinations exceeded the acceptability threshold. Color matching was material- and background-dependent and poorest against the most chromatic backgrounds, indicating that universal color matching should not be assumed under the tested conditions.

Article.Title: Timing of acute kidney injury and outcomes in patients receiving veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation
Article.Authors: Jungteerapanich T.; Chiracharasporn N.; Chiarnpattanodom C.; Wanichwecharungruang N.; Puyati W.; Tasanarong A.; Thanapongsatorn P.
Article.Abstract: Whether the timing of acute kidney injury (AKI) relative to veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) carries independent prognostic value remains uncertain. We evaluated the association between AKI timing and clinical outcomes in a retrospective, two-center cohort of 172 adults receiving VA-ECMO in Thailand. Patients were classified as having AKI before ECMO, AKI after ECMO, or no AKI by KDIGO creatinine criteria. Overall, 81 patients (47.1%) had AKI before ECMO, 82 (47.7%) developed AKI after ECMO, and 9 (5.2%) had no AKI. Compared with the AKI after ECMO group, patients with AKI before ECMO had more severe renal dysfunction, greater need for renal replacement therapy, more frequent acute liver injury, and higher unadjusted ICU mortality (82.7% vs 69.5%, p = 0.048). This association was attenuated after adjustment for age, sex, chronic kidney disease, and center (adjusted HR 1.39, 95% CI 0.98–1.98), and further attenuated after adjustment for illness severity (HR 1.28, 95% CI 0.86–1.90); AKI developing after ECMO initiation was not significantly associated with ICU mortality. In conclusion, AKI preceding ECMO appears to reflect pre-cannulation shock and multiorgan dysfunction in addition to renal injury, a distinction that should inform, rather than restrict, ECMO candidacy assessment.

Article.Title: Cross-Validated Adaptive Grey–ARIMA Hybrid forecasting of annual municipal water consumption under structural change: a case study of Suez City, Egypt
Article.Authors: Hassan S.; Mohsen N.; Ahmed N.; Fouad Y.; Elshewey A.
Article.Abstract: Reliable forecasting of municipal water consumption is essential for infrastructure planning and sustainable resource management. However, annual water-consumption records are often short, non-stationary, and affected by structural changes, limiting the effectiveness of data-intensive machine-learning and conventional statistical models. This study proposes a Cross-Validated Adaptive Grey–ARIMA Hybrid (CVA-GAH) model for forecasting annual municipal water consumption from limited historical data. The proposed framework combines a metabolic GM(1,1) model, fitted using a rolling data window, with an autoregressive integrated moving average model in a parallel weighted architecture. Model order, metabolic window length, and combination weight are selected exclusively through walk-forward cross-validation. An Occam’s-razor validation gate is incorporated to retain the hybrid model only when its additional complexity produces a meaningful out-of-sample improvement. The framework was evaluated using a 28-year annual water-consumption dataset from Suez City, Egypt, covering 1997–2024. Data from 1997–2020 were used for model development, while observations from 2021–2024 were reserved as a strictly blind holdout period containing a post-2020 structural decline. Cross-validation selected an ARIMA(0,2,1) model, a six-year metabolic GM(1,1) window, and respective blending weights of 0.85 and 0.15. During the blind holdout evaluation, CVA-GAH achieved a mean absolute percentage error of 4.14%, a mean absolute error of \(3.88\times 10^{6}\) , and a root mean squared error of \(4.90\times 10^{6}\) . These results improved upon standalone ARIMA and conventional GM(1,1), while reducing error volatility relative to ARIMA. The findings demonstrate that CVA-GAH provides an interpretable and computationally efficient forecasting framework for small-sample municipal water-demand series, although its empirical performance remains characterized by the specific socio-demographic and structural dynamics of the Suez City case study.

Article.Title: Deep learning mitigates batch effects in Raman spectroscopy
Article.Authors: Sjöberg J.; Lita A.; Larion M.; Petre I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Raman spectroscopy is widely used for its ability to provide rich molecular-level information from biological samples. However, the high sensitivity of Raman spectra can also unintentionally encode extraneous information, such as patient identity, instrument-specific signatures, environmental conditions, and sample handling protocols. This hidden structure, referred to as the batch effect, poses increasing challenges in machine learning applications, where it can lead to model overfitting, poor generalization, and even privacy risks when datasets are shared. In this work, we investigate the presence and impact of the batch effect in a Raman spectroscopy dataset derived from glioma tumor samples. We show that deep learning can accurately predict patient identity from individual spectra, revealing strong bias patterns in the data. To mitigate this issue, we explore several approaches and introduce an algorithmic framework based on adversarial deep learning. Our method effectively reduces the influence of confounding sample-specific signals while preserving information relevant to tumor classification. These findings highlight the need for careful bias control in Raman-based AI pipelines and provide tools to support more robust applications in biomedical spectroscopy.

Article.Title: Lactylation-driven mitochondrial dysfunction promotes diabetic myocardial fibrosis via impairing mitophagy and activating TGF-β1
Article.Authors: Lian B.; Li J.; Guo Y.; Li X.; Han Y.; Zhang J.; Lv F.; Shen D.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to investigate the role and mechanisms of lactate-derived protein lactylation in promoting myocardial fibrosis in diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM). We hypothesized that lactylation contributes to fibrosis through dual pathways: impairing PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy and epigenetically activating the TGF-β1 profibrotic axis. Clinical analysis included 80 type 2 diabetes (T2DM) patients with fibrosis and 40 non-fibrotic T2DM controls. Experimental models included Streptozotocin -induced diabetic mice and primary cardiac fibroblasts exposed to high glucose/lactate. Molecular mechanisms were examined using co-immunoprecipitation, lactylation-specific assays, siRNA knockdown, and pharmacological inhibition of lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA) with GSK2837808A. Fibrosis, mitochondrial function, and mitophagy were assessed via histology, hydroxyproline assay, Western blot, ATP/ROS detection, and echocardiography. Serum lactate was elevated in fibrotic T2DM patients. Diabetic mice showed increased myocardial lactate, suppressed PINK1/Parkin mitophagy, mitochondrial dysfunction (reduced ATP, elevated ROS), and enhanced fibrosis. Mechanistically, lactate induced HSP90 lactylation, disrupting its interaction with PINK1 and thereby contributing to mitophagy impairment. Concurrently, histone H3K18 lactylation enriched at the TGF-β1 promoter, leading to increased transcription and activation of the TGF-β1/Smad3 fibrotic cascade, as evidenced by elevated p-Smad3, α-SMA, collagen I/III, and enhanced fibroblast migration. In vivo , LDHA inhibition with GSK2837808A reduced lactate, improved mitophagy‑related markers, attenuated fibrosis, and improved cardiac function. In vitro, siRNA-mediated knockdown of LDHA or HSP90 suppressed TGF-β1 expression and fibroblast migration. Lactate-driven lactylation is associated with diabetic myocardial fibrosis through dual mechanisms—impairing mitophagy via HSP90 modification and epigenetically activating TGF-β1 via H3K18 lactylation. Targeting the lactate-lactylation-mitophagy-fibrosis axis may represent a potential experimental therapeutic strategy for DCM, though further validation in translational models and assessment of safety and specificity are warranted.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: myocardial fibrosis; mitophagy; mitochondrial dysfunction; TGF-β1 signaling; diabetic cardiomyopathy; lactylation; diabetes mellitus

Article.Title: Age at type 2 diabetes onset, retinol binding protein 4 and risks of diabetic retinopathy: a real-world cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Zhou Q.; Li J.; Fan M.; Shao H.; Ni L.
Article.Abstract: To examine the association between serum retinol-binding protein 4 (RBP4) and diabetic retinopathy (DR), and to assess whether age at type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) onset modifies this association. This cross-sectional study included 6,996 adults with T2DM identified from electronic medical records at Lishui People’s Hospital, Zhejiang, between 2018 and 2023. Participants were stratified by age at diabetes onset (< 65 vs. ≥ 65 years) and serum RBP4 levels (< 40 vs. ≥ 40 pg/mL). DR was assessed using standardized fundus photography according to ETDRS criteria. Logistic regression models were used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with interaction analyses performed to assess effect modification. Higher RBP4 levels (≥ 40 pg/mL) were associated with higher odds of DR in both age-at-onset strata. In adjusted analyses, the OR was 1.28 (95% CI 1.12–1.45) among participants with T2DM onset < 65 years and 1.43 (95% CI 0.96–2.12) among those with onset ≥ 65 years. However, the formal interaction by categorical age at T2DM onset (< 65 vs. ≥ 65 years) was not statistically significant (P for interaction = 0.58). Participants with onset ≥ 65 years had a shorter diabetes duration than those with onset < 65 years, which may partly explain the lower burden of DR in the later-onset group. In subgroup analyses, diabetes duration showed a statistically significant interaction with RBP4, although the stratum-specific ORs were very similar. Higher serum RBP4 was associated with higher odds of DR in adults with T2DM. However, we found no clear evidence that this association differed materially between the categorical age-at-onset groups. These findings support serum RBP4 as a potential biomarker candidate for DR risk and underscore the importance of diabetes duration when interpreting retinopathy risk.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: diabetic retinopathy; retinol-binding protein 4; type 2 diabetes; age at onset of diabetes

Article.Title: Morphological and permeability changes of the intestine in patients nourished exclusively with parenteral nutrition: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Pérez-Cordón L.; Molina-Montes E.; Serra-Prat M.; Yébenes J.; Campins L.; Marin S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract While evidence from animal models suggests that total parenteral nutrition (TPN) induces alterations in the intestinal mucosa, effects on humans are not clearly established. To analyse alterations in morphology and permeability associated with TPN in human intestinal mucosa, we conducted a systematic review following PRISMA recommendations. MEDLINE and Embase databases were searched from inception to May 2025 for literature on adults receiving TPN for any condition irrespective of the nutritional comparator. Outcome measures were intestinal morphological and permeability assessments. Meta-analyses conducted to synthesise the evidence were based on the random effects model because of heterogeneity in design characteristics. Of 1071 studies identified, 20 were included (morphology:10, and permeability: 13). Synthesis showed no significant short-term changes in villus height, crypt depth, or mucosal thickness over time after TPN. Villus height (mean difference: -87.51 µm [95%CI: -106.56, -68.46]) and crypt depth (mean difference: -44.48 µm [95%CI: -77.62, -11.34]) were significantly lower in patients on TPN compared to healthy volunteers or patients with dyspepsia. The lactulose/mannitol (L/M) ratios were significantly increased during TPN compared to baseline values (mean difference: 0.04 [95%CI: 0.02, 0.07]), and were also significantly higher for TPN compared to the enteral diet (mean difference: 0.03 [95%CI: 0.02, 0.05]). The overall strength of the evidence was low to moderate. Clinical status may have influenced the inconsistencies found in morphological outcomes. A possible association between altered permeability and TPN was observed; however, surgery and inflammation may have also contributed. The clinical significance of these findings and the effects of TPN duration and composition remain unclear. Prospero registration number CRD42022265814.

Article.Title: Identification of NUDT6 and LINGO1 as candidate genes for nCRT-associated signatures to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy in rectal cancer patients
Article.Authors: Wang Q.; Shen G.; Wang J.; Zheng Q.; Qin X.; Yang Z.
Article.Abstract: Rectal cancer is a highly prevalent cancer worldwide and a common cause of cancer death. Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) is the first choice for advanced rectal cancer. In this study, we used bioinformatics approaches to explore candidate genes affected by nCRT in rectal cancer. A total of 26 samples of rectal cancer patients were collected and divided into the Treatment group (14 patients who received nCRT) and the Control group (12 patients who did not receive nCRT). candidate genes were selected by high-throughput sequencing, differential expression analysis, machine learning algorithms, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, and gene expression analysis. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) was used to trace the enrichment pathways of these candidate genes. Additionally, the relationship between immune cells and these candidate genes was explored. A nomogram and molecular regulatory network were constructed based on the selected candidate genes. The quality of sequencing data was high for all samples. Overall, 35 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were discovered. Among them, NUDT6 and LINGO1 were identified as candidate genes with high discriminative ability (both with area under the curve (AUC) > 0.8). A nomogram with satisfactory exploratory performance was constructed. NUDT6 was significantly enriched in the ribosome and oxidative phosphorylation pathways, and was significantly positively correlated with Megakaryocyte-Erythroid Progenitor (MEP) and T helper cell 1 (Th1 cells), and significantly negatively correlated with Myocyte cells. LINGO1 was significantly enriched in the proteasome pathway and significantly positively correlated with Erythrocytes. Additionally, drug prediction analyses indicated that valproic acid was most highly associated with NUDT6, while bisphenol A is most closely linked to LINGO1. In this study, NUDT6 and LINGO1 were identified as potential candidate genes significantly associated with the Treatment group (patients who received nCRT) compared to the Control group (patients who did not). These findings may offer exploratory insights into the molecular correlates of nCRT treatment in rectal cancer. Moreover, as this study relies on a single-center convenience sample, these findings require further validation in multi-center prospective cohorts.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: LINGO-1; neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy; candidate genes; rectal cancer

Article.Title: AI awareness relates to university students’ boundaryless career through the parallel mediation of intrinsic motivation and future job insecurity
Article.Authors: Liang S.; Jiang J.; Chen J.
Article.Abstract: The in-depth penetration of artificial intelligence (AI) technology has reshaped career forms and the structure of the labor market, exerting a profound impact on university students’ cognition and orientation towards career development. Based on the conservation of resources theory and self-determination theory, we conducted three studies—an experimental study and two survey studies—to explore correlational linkages between AI awareness and university students’ boundaryless career. Studies 1 and 3 consistently demonstrated that AI awareness is indirectly associated with boundaryless career through the parallel mediating pathways of intrinsic motivation and future job insecurity. Study 2 provided experimental evidence that heightened AI awareness increases both intrinsic motivation and future job insecurity. This research enriches the application scenarios of boundaryless career theory in the context of technological change, deepens the understanding of the mechanism linking technological perception to youth career psychology, and offers practical implications for career guidance in universities.

Article.Title: Development of an automated method for audiometric data extraction and analysis using voting optical character recognition
Article.Authors: Kwon D.; Jung D.; Son J.; Shon B.; Lee Y.; Jeong S.; Lee K.
Article.Abstract: Hearing loss affects over 1.5 billion people worldwide, significantly impacting language development, quality of life, and economic independence. Research on audiometric data, such as pure tone audiometry (PTA), the speech reception threshold (SRT), and the word recognition score (WRS), is essential for understanding and preventing hearing loss. However, this data is frequently stored as image files within electronic medical records (EMRs), thus requiring manual extraction for research use. Manual extraction is time-consuming, costly, and prone to errors, limiting data utility and impeding large-scale data acquisition. In this paper, we propose an automated extraction method for audiometric report images using Tesseract optical character recognition (OCR) and an improved voting OCR (VOCR) algorithm. VOCR mitigates OCR variability by removing symbols (e.g., “dB,” “%”) and using tabulated data, generating multiple OCR candidates per cell and utilizing a voting mechanism to select reliable values. Our results indicate that VOCR achieves an image-level accuracy of 97.60% and high accuracy across all audiometric data categories, including PTA (99.95%), SRT (98.95%), WRS % (98.05%), and WRS stimulus (99.80%). The voting-based accuracy metric allows for the assessment of reliability, enabling a targeted review of areas with low consensus. This method has the potential to be employed in web-based data collection services, supporting real-time, standardized data management and reducing the need for manual extraction, making it a valuable tool for otolaryngological research.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: automated data analysis

Article.Title: Unsupervised ensemble methods for non-wear detection from triaxial accelerometer data in children following continuous monitoring
Article.Authors: Gunturkun F.; Fiterau M.; Moore H.; Jensen A.; Haydel K.; Kam M.; Garrard L.; Potter A.; Schuette P.; Robinson T.; Desai M.
Article.Abstract: Accelerometer signals from non-wear periods are often misclassified as stationary time or sleep, potentially biasing interpretations of physical activity’s impact on health. Non-wear detection algorithms exist but their performance varies depending on the population and activity patterns. To address this, we developed and evaluated unsupervised ensemble algorithms using data from the Stanford Sleep Accelerometer Study (15 children, aged 4–18) and a simulated dataset (100 subjects) constructed from real-world pediatric data. We compared two unsupervised ensemble methods (SUMMA and BI) and a simple majority-voting ensemble against nine base classifiers derived from three algorithms: Choi, NHANES and a Hidden Markov Model (HMM). Non-wear was treated as the positive class throughout. Performance was evaluated using sensitivity, specificity, and balanced accuracy, and the variability of error across subjects. Individual algorithms exhibited performance trade-offs: Choi performed well for long stationary and sleep periods but often missed short non-wear intervals, while HMM identified short non-wear intervals but underestimated stationary time. Ensemble methods provided comparable balanced accuracy with a better balance between sensitivity and specificity. In the simulation dataset, SUMMA achieved 67.7% sensitivity, 87.1% specificity, and 77.5% balanced accuracy, compared to the best individual baseline algorithm, NHANES_VM (63.4%, 90.3%, 77.1%). Overall, the ensemble approach showed more stable performance across subjects and provides a useful alternative to relying on a single non-wear detection algorithm in settings with heterogeneous activity patterns and short non-wear periods.

Article.Title: Reservoir stress sensitivity and its influence on pressure response characteristics in deep fractured-vuggy reservoirs: a case study of the X deep fractured-vuggy reservoir
Article.Authors: Guan Y.; Dai M.; Wu H.; Wu Z.
Article.Abstract: Although stress sensitivity and bottom-hole pressure analysis have been investigated extensively, the inherent reservoir heterogeneity leads to variability in stress sensitivity behavior and pressure response behavior across different reservoirs. Therefore it is considerable importance to establish a stress sensitivity characterization method tailored to the X deep carbonate reservoir and to elucidate its characteristic bottom-hole pressure behavior. Our study adopts a combined research approach that integrates laboratory experimentation with theoretical derivation to systematically analyze the stress sensitivity characteristics of X deep carbonate reservoirs, and a well test model suitable for X deep carbonate reservoirs was established. The influence of reservoir stress sensitivity on the bottom-hole pressure behavior was further examined. It is found that the flow regime of a vertical well in X fractured-vuggy reservoir includes eight flow stages, which are the wellbore storage stage, the skin stage, the first radial flow stage, the transition stage, the vug storage stage, the second radial flow stage, the vug-fracture crossflow stage, and the boundary-controlled flow stage. Furthermore, stronger stress sensitivity leads to a greater decline in permeability. Meanwhile, the higher the stress sensitivity, the greater the attenuation of permeability caused by changes in effective stress, and the stress sensitivity effect also increases accordingly. The bottomhole pressure drop corresponding to the same dimensionless time increases significantly, and the pressure derivative curve shows a noticeable upward bend. These findings provide a theoretical basis for the efficient development of X deep carbonate fractured-vuggy reservoirs.

Article.Title: Integrating computational fluid dynamics and field experiments to optimize mixing and irrigation strategies for biogas slurry application in Chinese yam
Article.Authors: Lu J.; Gao Y.; Tian Y.; Shao Y.; Li J.; Li J.; Du L.; Chen Q.; Chen J.; Zhang H.; Zhong F.
Article.Abstract: Maximizing the agricultural value of biogas slurry while mitigating its environmental risks requires precise blending and irrigation, yet optimized methodologies remain underdeveloped. This study employs Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) numerical simulation to analyze the fluid dynamics of three designed mixed fertilizer pipeline structures. It investigates how mixing sequence affects fertilizer blending efficiency within pipes of identical diameter. The realizable k- ε model is used for fluid simulation, with the velocity-based coefficient of variation (CV) serving as the evaluation metric for blending uniformity. Results indicate that the stepwise mixing structure b (anaerobic liquid–water-trace elements sequence) achieves optimal fertilizer mixing uniformity with a flow velocity of 6.65 m/s and a relative standard deviation (CV) of 6.47%. Based on this structure, an integrated biogas slurry irrigation machine featuring high integration and intelligent control was assembled, incorporating components such as solenoid valves, centrifugal pumps, and smart controllers. A two-factor experiment was conducted with four concentrations (25%-100%) and three irrigation lower limits (65%-85% field capacity), statistical analysis using two-factor ANOVA revealed significant effects of slurry concentration, irrigation lower limit, and their interaction on crop performance indicators, and the entropy weight method was used to identify the optimal irrigation strategy. Field trial results indicate that irrigation at 75% slurry concentration + 75% field capacity (F3T2) yields superior Chinese yam production and starch content. The entropy weight method also confirms comprehensively evaluated five key indicators-soil moisture content, yam yield, soluble protein content, starch content, and economic returns-confirming F3T2 as the optimal irrigation scheme for Chinese yam (evaluation value: 0.97). This work establishes a coherent framework linking engineering optimization to precision agronomy, offering a replicable strategy for transforming agricultural waste into a resource with enhanced efficiency and economic return.

Article.Title: Lightweight SAR building segmentation via enhanced multi-scale context modeling and bidirectional guided feature fusion
Article.Authors: Wang Q.; Long Z.; Chen Z.; Liang X.; Xu X.
Article.Abstract: Accurate building extraction from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery is important for urban mapping, disaster assessment, and remote-sensing interpretation, but remains difficult because speckle noise, heterogeneous scattering, radar shadow, weak texture, and ambiguous building boundaries can degrade pixel-level predictions. At the same time, heavy segmentation networks are difficult to deploy in computation-constrained settings. This study presents a task-oriented lightweight SAR building segmentation framework derived from DeepLabV3+. MobileNetV3 is used as an efficient backbone, a depthwise separable atrous spatial pyramid pooling (DS-ASPP) module retains multi-scale context at reduced cost, and a bidirectional guided fusion module (BGFM) combines boundary-sensitive low-level information with deep semantic features. On SARBuD1.0, the model achieves 94.64% OA, 79.89% MIoU, and 76.45% Kappa with 11.3 M parameters and 58.12 FPS. Across five independent runs, the proposed model achieves 79.86 ± 0.17% MIoU compared with 78.52 ± 0.20% for HSB-Net, with a significant paired difference ( p < 0.001). On HR-SARBuD, the model achieves 79.75% MIoU; the five-run mean is 79.77 ± 0.15%, compared with 79.68 ± 0.16% for FPANet, and the difference is not statistically significant ( p = 0.214). Under the batch-1 complexity protocol, the proposed network requires 8.9 GFLOPs and 17.21 ms per image, versus 42.7 GFLOPs and 50.89 ms for DeepLabV3+. These results support a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off, while cross-dataset and edge-device limitations are explicitly discussed.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: synthetic aperture radar images; atrous spatial pyramid pooling; DeepLabV3+; speckle noise; lightweight neural networks; radar shadow; MobileNetV3; edge deployment

Article.Title: Effect of capillary refill time-guided resuscitation on early fluid administration and fluid balance in septic shock: a single-center randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Gao F.; Xu Y.; Li Z.; Xu H.; Hui J.; Liang C.; Chen Y.; Wang Q.; Liang F.
Article.Abstract: Septic shock is a common critical illness in the intensive care unit (ICU). Capillary refill time (CRT) and lactate are used to guide perfusion assessment in septic shock. Their effects on additional intravenous fluid exposure during hemodynamic optimization after initial resuscitation remain uncertain. This was a single-center, prospective, randomized, open-label trial. A total of 85 patients with septic shock were randomized to capillary refill time-targeted resuscitation (CRT-T; n = 44) or lactate-targeted resuscitation (Lac-T; n = 41) for 6 h during hemodynamic optimization after initial resuscitation. The CRT-T target was CRT ≤ 3 s, whereas the Lac-T target was arterial lactate ≤ 2 mmol/L or a decrease of > 10% per hour. Six-hour total intravenous fluid input was prespecified as a secondary endpoint in the written protocol and was subsequently prioritized as the main early resuscitation outcome of this report after the trial was under-recruited relative to the mortality-based sample-size target; accordingly, these analyses are interpreted as exploratory. Ethics/scientific review and a written protocol were completed before recruitment. Public registration was delayed because of synchronization and review delays on the registry platform and was ultimately completed retrospectively after enrollment had ended; the retrospective registry covers the broader SBRI/CRT program and does not establish prospective primacy of the 6-hour fluid-volume endpoint. The 6-hour total intravenous fluid input was 1135 (824–1480) mL in the CRT-T group and 1350 (990–1850) mL in the Lac-T group. The Hodges-Lehmann location-shift estimate for CRT-T minus Lac-T was − 250 mL (95% CI, -500 to -20 mL; P = 0.035). Positive fluid balance at 6 and 24 h was also lower in the CRT-T group (nominal P < 0.05). No significant between-group differences were observed in CRT, arterial lactate, or norepinephrine dose at 6–24 h. Twenty-eight-day mortality was 22.7% (10/44) versus 29.3% (12/41), corresponding to a risk ratio of 0.78 (95% CI, 0.38–1.60); the trial was not powered for mortality. Ventilator-free days within 28 days were 14 (6.75–21.25) versus 12 (0–12) days, with a Hodges-Lehmann estimate of + 4.0 days (95% CI, 1.0 to 8.5; P = 0.005). Renal replacement therapy-free days and vasopressor-free days did not differ significantly between groups. All downstream clinical outcomes are considered exploratory. In a post hoc sensitivity analysis excluding patients with baseline CRT ≤ 3 s, the location-shift estimate was − 240 mL (95% CI, -500 to 0 mL; P = 0.052; n = 77). The CRT-targeted strategy was associated with modestly lower 6-hour total intravenous fluid input during hemodynamic optimization after initial resuscitation. The clinical importance and fluid-component contribution of this difference remain uncertain. The study compares overall target-driven treatment strategies and does not isolate the effect of CRT versus lactate. All findings are exploratory and do not establish improved clinical outcomes. Clinical trial registration The trial was retrospectively registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry on August 5, 2025 (ChiCTR2500107145), after participant enrollment had been completed. Ethics and scientific review and a written protocol were in place before recruitment. Public registration was delayed because of synchronization and review delays on the registry platform; by the time the registration process was completed, enrollment had ended and the entry was therefore retrospective. The retrospective registry covers the broader combined SBRI/CRT research program and lists SVRI, SBRI, and CRT as primary indicators; it does not prospectively establish 6-hour total intravenous fluid input as the primary endpoint of the randomized comparison. Retrospective registration is therefore acknowledged as an important reporting limitation and cannot establish prospective specification of the outcome hierarchy.

Article.Title: Exploring the biomarker potential of LCN2 and MMP9 proteins in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
Article.Authors: Suri S.; Parsana M.; Garg H.; Boora G.; Chauhan A.; Goel K.; Gupta S.; Mitra S.; Bakshi J.; Ghoshal S.; Pal A.
Article.Abstract: Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (HNSCC) is a major cancer-related health problem in low-and-middle-income countries (LMICs). A significant number of HNSCC cases result in overall poor disease outcomes, majorly attributed to late diagnosis due to the unavailability of suitable biomarkers. In one of our previous studies, a number of dysregulated proteins were identified using salivary proteomics in HNSCC patients; Lipocalin2(LCN2) and Matrix Metalloproteinase 9(MMP9) were among the topmost upregulated candidates. In this current prospective case–control study, we explored the clinical utility of these proteins in 351 biopsy-proven treatment-naïve HNSCC patients analysing their saliva, serum and tumour tissue. We compared them with 26 Oral Premalignant Diseases (OPMDs) and 118 healthy controls. The protein levels were estimated by Sandwich ELISA in saliva and serum and by Immunohistochemistry (IHC) and Immunofluorescence (IF) in tumour tissue. The findings were clinically correlated; Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curves and survival curves were analysed to predict probable biomarker efficacy. The outcomes of the study were compared with The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database. The effect of their knockdown (KD) on cancer hallmarks was also studied in HNSCC cell lines. Collectively, our data demonstrate that baseline LCN2, MMP9, and the LCN2/MMP9 complex can be used as potential biomarkers for the diagnosis and prognostication of HNSCC patients.

Article.Title: An experimental investigation of photovoltaic array with mixed mono-facial and bi-facial modules
Article.Authors: Thangaraj H.; David P.; Murugan M.; Balachandran P.
Article.Abstract: Bifacial photovoltaic (PV) panels are widely favoured for their higher energy yield and improved power generation capability. However, their high-cost limits large-scale deployment. To achieve a balance between enhanced power output and economic feasibility, a hybrid PV array integrating mono-facial and bifacial modules is proposed in this work. The proposed scheme consists of a 3 × 3 PV array composed of six mono-facial and three bifacial panels, where the bifacial modules are strategically positioned within the array. The performance of the hybrid array is evaluated in terms of maximum power, voltage, and current under twelve distinct partial shading scenarios. Various bifacial placement configurations, including diagonal, first row, first column, and grouped arrangements such as (2 × 2), (3 × 1), and (3 × 3), are systematically analyzed. The results are compared using double-hybrid and triple-hybrid configurations to identify the most effective arrangement. A switching matrix circuit is incorporated to dynamically select the optimal hybrid configuration, enabling maximum power extraction across multiple shading conditions. The proposed approach achieves higher power output in 11 out of 12 shading cases, compared to only five cases in conventional configurations. The power output ranges from 95 W under no-shading conditions to 26 W under severe shading, with first-row and first-column bifacial placements, specifically (2 × 2), (3 × 1), and (3 × 3) delivering superior performance in the majority of shading scenarios. The proposed hybrid configuration demonstrates a cost-effective and robust solution for maximizing power generation under partial shading conditions.

Article.Title: Development and validation of an interpretable machine learning model for early prediction of refractory mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia: a multi-center study
Article.Authors: Sheng Y.; Tang H.; Guo Y.; Ding L.; Liu F.; Zhu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Early prediction of refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (RMPP) in children remains challenging with conventional approaches. Machine learning (ML) offers a promising approach to improve risk stratification by identifying patterns in multidimensional clinical data. This study aims to develop and externally validate an interpretable ML model for early RMPP identification. This multicenter retrospective study collected clinical data from pediatric patients with MPP across four medical centers between 2019 and 2023. Using data from two centers as the derivation cohort, we developed and compared six ML models to predict refractory outcomes. Model performance was assessed by discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis. The optimal model was externally validated in two independent cohorts and systematically interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to reveal individual-level and cohort-level risk drivers. The analysis included 6,587 children across four centers: 5,546 in the derivation cohort and 696 and 345 in two external validation cohorts. The random forest model showed the best overall performance, with an AUC of 0.809 in the untouched internal hold-out test set. In the two external cohorts, the model achieved AUROCs of 0.774 and 0.807, respectively. Calibration drift was observed in external populations with different baseline RMPP prevalence, and local intercept recalibration improved calibration. SHAP analysis identified fever duration before hospitalization, neutrophil percentage, and age as the leading predictors. This externally validated machine learning model demonstrated robust generalizability across multiple centers and provided individualized risk assessment for children with MPP at admission. Local recalibration may be needed when applied to populations with markedly different baseline risks.

Article.Title: DARF: direction-aware adaptive routing fusion for cross-modal detection
Article.Authors: Zhang S.; Zhao J.; Fan J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In complex scenarios such as low illumination and background clutter, visible-light images often suffer from missing target textures and degraded image quality. Although infrared images can complement target contour and edge information, they lack color and surface texture features. Existing visible-infrared cross-modal detection algorithms still exhibit two key shortcomings. First, the shallow features at the front end of the network lack sufficient ability to extract multi-directional and multi-scale details, resulting in weak fundamental feature representations. Second, most cross-modal fusion methods rely on feature concatenation or fixed-weight aggregation, making it difficult to effectively distinguish shared information from modality-specific complementary information and to dynamically adjust the contribution ratio of visible and infrared modalities according to scene conditions, thereby leading to significant inter-modal interference. To address these issues, this paper proposes DARF, a cross-modal detection algorithm based on YOLOv8, following the idea of front-end basic feature enhancement and back-end dual-modal adaptive fusion. Specifically, two core improvements are introduced: first, a Multi-branch Direction-Aware Feature module (MDAF) is embedded at the front end of the backbone network to enhance shallow feature representations and provide stronger support for subsequent fusion; second, a Dual-Modal Adaptive Routing fusion module (DMAR) is deployed between the backbone network and the detection neck to achieve fine-grained cross-modal adaptive feature fusion. Comparative experiments are conducted on the pixel-aligned LLVIP dataset and the KAIST dataset for cross-scene evaluation. The results show that DARF achieves higher detection accuracy than representative existing methods, thereby validating the effectiveness of the proposed modules and the overall framework.

Article.Title: Machine learning modeling of the volumetric overall mass transfer coefficient in a novel L-shaped pulsed sieve plate extraction column
Article.Authors: Rafiei V.; Moradi S.
Article.Abstract: The volumetric overall mass transfer coefficient is a key design parameter in liquid–liquid extraction columns, yet reliable prediction remains difficult for non-standard geometries. This study applied machine learning to simultaneously predict the volumetric overall mass transfer coefficient for both the horizontal and vertical sections of a novel L-shaped pulsed sieve plate extraction column — a task not addressed by any single correlation, since the two sections operate under distinct dispersion and mixer-settler hydrodynamic regimes — using artificial neural network, random forest, and support vector regression models trained on experimental data from two liquid–liquid systems. The artificial neural network model achieved the highest accuracy for both sections, with a test coefficient of determination above 0.98 and an average absolute relative error below 6% on a small hold-out set (four test conditions per section), outperforming published empirical correlations developed for conventional vertical columns. Sensitivity analysis identified dispersed phase holdup and drop size as the dominant predictive variables in both sections. Neural-network-based response surface analysis identified optimal operating conditions, with residual diagnostics showing no evident systematic bias across the range of predicted values. Given the limited dataset (36 operating conditions per section), the model is regarded as valid for interpolation within the investigated experimental domain, and its generalization capability remains to be confirmed with larger datasets.

Article.Title: Effect of guideline-assisted prompting on large language model performance in medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw–related endodontic decision-making
Article.Authors: Altunkum M.; Tartuk G.; Mavigöz T.; Kaya S.
Article.Abstract: Clinical decision-making in patients receiving antiresorptive medications requires balancing tooth preservation against the risk of medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ). This study compared the performance of ChatGPT, Claude, and DeepSeek in MRONJ-related endodontic scenarios and evaluated the effect of guideline-assisted prompting using the 2022 American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons Position Paper. Eighteen fictional and standardized MRONJ-related endodontic clinical scenarios were developed based on the 2022 AAOMS Position Paper and current scientific evidence. Three contemporary LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, and DeepSeek) were evaluated using a two-phase study design consisting of baseline and guideline-assisted assessments. In the second phase, the complete AAOMS Position Paper was provided before evaluation of the same scenarios. Two endodontic specialists independently scored the anonymized responses across five clinical decision-making domains using a six-point ordinal scale (0–5). The primary outcome was the mean of the five domain scores, yielding an overall clinical decision-making score ranging from 0 to 5. Inter-rater agreement was assessed using the initial ratings, and disagreements were resolved through consensus before analysis. Linear mixed models (LMMs) were used for the primary analyses, with cumulative link mixed models (CLMMs) performed as sensitivity analyses for the ordinal domain scores. Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc comparisons were performed where appropriate. At baseline, ChatGPT achieved a significantly higher mean overall score than Claude (4.68 ± 0.14 vs. 4.29 ± 0.38). Following guideline-assisted prompting, Claude’s mean score increased to 4.68 ± 0.28 (+ 0.39 points on the 0–5 scale), and the statistically significant difference between ChatGPT and Claude was no longer observed. DeepSeek consistently received lower overall scores than both models. A significant overall phase effect ( p < 0.001) and model-by-phase interaction ( p = 0.004) were identified. Domain-level CLMM sensitivity analyses generally supported the LMM findings, although the phase effect for consultation and medication management was not confirmed by the CLMM. The most pronounced model-specific increase in guideline-concordant scores was observed for follow-up recommendations, particularly for Claude. Guideline-assisted prompting was associated with higher concordance with the predefined reference standard, particularly for Claude, which showed the largest improvement in overall scores and follow-up recommendations. Although ChatGPT scored significantly higher than Claude at baseline, this difference was no longer statistically significant following guideline-assisted prompting. Because the clinical scenarios, reference standard, and guideline-assisted intervention were aligned with the same AAOMS guideline, these findings should not be interpreted as independent validation of clinical accuracy. Further studies using externally developed scenarios and real-world clinical cases are required before considering these models for clinician-supervised decision support.

Article.Title: First-day Braden score carries more prognostic information than vasoactive dose for pressure injury in ICU patients receiving early vasoactive support
Article.Authors: Huang Y.; Shao L.; Li Y.; Cai K.
Article.Abstract: Vasopressor exposure is a reported risk factor for intensive care unit (ICU)-acquired pressure injury, but its prognostic information relative to bedside risk assessment is unknown. In this retrospective single-centre MIMIC-IV cohort of 17,148 adult ICU stays that started vasoactive support within 24 h and remained in the ICU, alive and free of documented injury, at 24 h, 1,833 (10.7%) had a newly documented pressure injury. Peak norepinephrine-equivalent dose, duration of support, hypotension burden and the Braden Scale, measured in the first 24 h, were entered simultaneously in a cause-specific Cox model with death and discharge as competing events. The first-day Braden score had the largest standardized association (hazard ratio 0.77, 95% CI 0.73–0.81 per standard deviation), ahead of hypotension burden (1.10) and peak dose (1.07), and improved discrimination more than peak dose, although modestly. In exploratory analyses, associations were concentrated in the first week, and for lesions severe at first documentation, mostly deep tissue injuries, peak dose was no longer clearly associated after full adjustment including first-day illness severity, whereas duration of support was. In a 48 h landmark subset, whole-stay summarization inflated the Braden association by 58%. First-day bedside assessment carried more prognostic information than vasoactive dose.

Article.Title: Machine learning in predicting recurrence of self-inflicted neck trauma in young adults
Article.Authors: Alabi R.; Mäkitie R.
Article.Abstract: Self-inflicted injuries, particularly among young adults, are associated with an increased risk of subsequent suicide attempts and suicide. Injuries to the anterior neck present unique challenges in management due to the presence of vital anatomical structures and possibly complicated consequences. Therefore, this study employed machine learning (ML) techniques to predict injury recurrence in patients with self-inflected anterior neck injuries. The cohort comprised 167 individuals aged 18 to 30 years with self-inflicted injury to the anterior neck at the Helsinki University Hospital in 2005–2023. Patient records were systematically analyzed for patient demographics, clinical characteristics, psychiatric comorbidity, and clinical management for building a ML model. Class imbalance and feature selection were handled across three different models; logistic regression, easy ensemble, and extreme gradient boosting-based models. Furthermore, predictions were enhanced using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) for both global and local interpretability. Our results showed that the most important predictive variables for a recurrence were history of other trauma, patient age at presentation, and mode of arrival (walk-in versus brought in). All three injury recurrence models showed poor performance. The highest balanced accuracy between the three models was 60.0%, Brier score of 0.23, precision-recall area under curve (AUC) value of 0.30, receiver operating characteristic-AUC of 0.66, recall value of 0.75, F1 score of 0.32, and accuracy of 55%. Our models showed poor performance and therefore still require further training and validation and, currently, hold limited clinical usability. However, given the rising rates of self-harm among young adults, identifying patients at risk of injury recurrence may improve clinical management and intervention. Future research is needed with larger, diverse datasets and external validation to improve the predictive capabilities of these ML models, ultimately aiding in the development of effective prediction tools.
