Article.Title: Comparative micro-computed tomography assessment of left-sided septal pouch and left atrial appendage morphometry
Article.Authors: Hołda J.; Jaśkiewicz K.; Tarasiuk J.; Wroński S.; Bolechała F.; Walocha J.; Urbaniak P.; Hołda M.
Article.Abstract: The left-sided septal pouch (LSSP) is a blind-ending recess of the interatrial septum that opens into the left atrium and has been proposed as a potential site of blood stasis and thrombus formation. Although its clinical relevance has been discussed in relation to cryptogenic stroke, detailed three-dimensional morphometric data are limited. This study used high-resolution micro-computed tomography to compare the morphology and volume of the LSSP with those of the left atrial appendage (LAA), a well-established source of cardiac embolism, thereby contextualizing the size and spatial orientation of the LSSP. Forty structurally intact human hearts with an LSSP were examined. After controlled fixation and micro-computed tomography scanning, three-dimensional reconstructions of the LSSP and LAA luminal spaces were generated and used for morphometric analysis. The mean LSSP volume was 0.43 ± 0.16 ml, whereas the mean LAA volume was 3.81 ± 2.21 ml ( p < 0.001). The mean specimen-level LSSP/LAA volume ratio was 14.5 ± 7.6% (range: 4.2–59.3%). The mean left atrial cavity volume was 37.4 ± 10.2 ml, while the mean specimen-level LSSP/LA cavity and LAA/LA cavity volume ratios were 1.4 ± 0.6% and 11.3 ± 7.2%, respectively. The LSSP ostium was oriented superiorly, whereas the LAA orifice was arranged in a horizontal plane. The LSSP was smaller than the LAA reference structure across the assessed volumetric, ostial, and linear dimensions, including ostial or orifice area (39.7 ± 19.0 mm² vs. 121.7 ± 74.1 mm 2 ), depth or length (9.1 ± 4.2 mm vs. 23.6 ± 7.5 mm), and width (7.1 ± 3.6 mm vs. 17.7 ± 6.9 mm). In conclusion, our findings provide the first micro-computed tomography-based three-dimensional morphometric assessment of the LSSP and show that, despite its small size, it represents a measurable left atrial recess with distinct spatial anatomy and quantifiable volume.

Article.Title: A hybrid approach for early fault prediction based on resistance behavior and machine learning
Article.Authors: Charjan O.; Gajbhiye K.; Warhade J.; Wankhade S.; Mallick S.; Wankhade K.
Article.Abstract: Fault detection in electrical power systems at an early stage plays a vital role in ensuring high operational efficiency, reliability, and cost-effectiveness by preventing unexpected system breakdowns. However, traditional fault diagnosis techniques based solely on raw voltage and current measurements may be sensitive to measurement noise and variations in operating conditions. To address this issue, this paper proposes a resistance-based statistical feature engineering framework integrated with machine learning for electrical fault classification. Phase-wise resistances derived from voltage and current measurements are used to extract statistical features including mean, maximum, minimum, standard deviation, and range. The extracted features are evaluated using six machine learning classifiers: Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), CatBoost, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). The proposed framework is evaluated on two datasets: the Electrical Fault Detection and Classification dataset from Kaggle and the Hybrid Electrical Fault Detection Dataset (Real + Synthetic) from Mendeley Data. Using an 80:20 training-testing split, Random Forest achieved the highest accuracy of 97.75% on the Kaggle dataset and 95.82% on the Hybrid Electrical Fault Detection Dataset. The results demonstrate that resistance-derived statistical features provide an interpretable and computationally efficient representation for reliable electrical fault diagnosis across different datasets. The proposed framework further demonstrates its potential for predictive maintenance and intelligent electrical fault monitoring.

Article.Title: A pilot cohort study of blood brain barrier permeability in Alzheimer’s disease using dynamic contrast enhanced magnetic resonance imaging
Article.Authors: McCausland B.; Varatharaj A.; Huneke N.; Abraham S.; Abadalkareem R.; Thomas B.; Gee C.; Kunicki A.; Darekar A.; Teeling J.; Zetterberg H.; Galea I.; Amin J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Blood–brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction is implicated as a key link between neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Peripheral inflammation may exacerbate cognitive decline by promoting BBB breakdown and impairing clearance of amyloid and tau, yet in vivo evidence for this hypothesis remains limited. We conducted a pilot cohort study to assess the feasibility of utilising dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) to quantify BBB permeability in AD, and to explore associations with cognitive decline, peripheral inflammation, and neurodegeneration. Fourteen participants with clinically diagnosed AD and 16 matched controls underwent baseline clinical, blood, urine, and DCE-MRI assessments. Thirteen AD participants were clinically reassessed after 12 months. BBB permeability was quantified using Patlak modelling in whole brain, grey and white matter, and selected regions of interest. Serum cytokines, phosphorylated tau-181 (pTau-181), neurofilament light (NfL), and urinary neopterin were analysed. BBB permeability did not differ significantly between AD and controls across global or regional measures at baseline. However, higher baseline permeability in the left entorhinal cortex was significantly associated with greater cognitive decline over 12 months. AD participants exhibited elevated serum interferon-γ relative to controls, and higher baseline interleukin-6 was associated with faster cognitive decline. This pilot study supports feasibility of regional DCE-MRI measurement in people with AD. Larger biomarker-confirmed cohorts are warranted to evaluate prognostic utility and to clarify the interaction between peripheral inflammation, BBB dysfunction and clinical progression in AD.

Article.Title: Genetic and expression evidence supports FTO rs9939609 as a key susceptibility marker for type 2 diabetes and obesity in Thai adults
Article.Authors: Yaikwawong M.; Kamdee K.; Ek-eudomsuk P.; Sittithumcharee G.; Jirawatnotai S.; Chuengsamarn S.
Article.Abstract: Variants in the fat mass and obesity-associated ( FTO ) gene are widely linked to obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), yet their functional relevance in Asian populations remains unclear. This study examined the association of two common FTO intron-1 variants, rs9939609 and rs1421085, with T2DM, obesity, and cardiometabolic traits in a Thai cohort ( n = 798; 350 controls and 448 cases), and evaluated their relationship with FTO messenger RNA (mRNA) expression. Both variants showed significant additive associations with T2DM and obesity, with rs9939609 demonstrating the strongest effect (per-allele OR = 1.60, 95% CI: 1.17–2.19; P = 0.003). Associations with T2DM remained robust after stratification by obesity status. The two SNPs were in strong linkage disequilibrium, and conditional analyses indicated that rs9939609 represented the primary association signal. In a subset of 152 participants, rs9939609 risk-allele carriers exhibited significantly higher FTO mRNA expression in peripheral blood leukocytes, whereas rs1421085 showed no expression differences. These findings, based on population-specific criteria and genetic modeling, demonstrate the additive contribution of FTO variants to metabolic risk in Thai adults and highlight rs9939609 as the major genetic signal at this locus, potentially acting through increased FTO expression. However, the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

Article.Title: Development of a simple and robust absorbance-based carbon dot platform for rapid escherichia coli DNA detection
Article.Authors: Thi H.; Phan N.; Kraft M.; Nguyen S.; Tran M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reliable DNA-based detection of Escherichia coli is essential for monitoring bacterial contamination in food, water, and environmental samples. In this work, we developed a label-free and amplification-free UV-Vis absorbance biosensor using carbon dots (Cdots) as optical transducers for the detection of E. coli DNA. Cdots synthesized from chitosan, citric acid, and thiourea were functionalized with NH 2 -terminated DNA probes through carbodiimide-mediated covalent coupling, enabling stable attachment of amine-modified DNA probes to carboxyl-containing Cdots. Among the tested probe configurations, NH 2 -BL21 produced the strongest optical response, with a maximum absorbance change of 31.6%, highlighting the importance of both probe sequence and terminal functionalization in enhancing sensor performance. The optimized biosensor exhibited excellent linearity over the 200–2000 fM range, with an R 2 of 0.9992, a limit of detection of 147.53 fM, and a limit of quantification of 491.76 fM. In addition, the sensor exhibited sequence-dependent recognition and preferential selectivity toward the tested E. coli DNA target, while its response remained statistically unchanged over four weeks of storage, demonstrating short-term stability under the tested conditions. Mechanistic analysis suggests that the absorbance response reflects multiple hybridization-induced interfacial and optical effects, including increased nucleic-acid absorption near 258 nm and possible contributions from changes in surface charge, the local dielectric environment, particle organization, and light scattering. This label-free and amplification-free absorbance strategy provides a potentially accessible platform for E. coli DNA detection. However, matrix-specific calibration and further validation are required before practical environmental or food-safety deployment.

Article.Title: Self-reported workplace heat and cold exposure time and WHO-5 screen-positive depressive symptoms among Korean employees: a nationwide cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Kim S.; Kim J.; Kim J.; Yoon J.; Yong S.
Article.Abstract: Given limited prior research, especially with small samples, this study examined the association between abnormal workplace temperature exposure and depressive symptoms among Korean employees. Here, workplace temperature exposure was operationalized as self-reported heat or cold exposure time, and the outcome was WHO-5 screen-positive depressive symptoms. The fifth Korean Working Conditions Survey (KWCS), conducted in 2017, included 30,108 paid employees; the primary common complete-case analysis included 29,413 participants. Heat and cold exposure time were categorized as none, low, intermediate, or high, and a WHO-5 score ≤ 28 defined screen-positive depressive symptoms. Survey-weighted modified Poisson regression with respondent-level empirical sandwich covariance estimated prevalence ratios (PRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The survey-weighted prevalence was 11.07%. In the primary adjusted model (Model 2), the categorical patterns were non-monotonic. Compared with no exposure, adjusted PRs for high heat and high cold exposure time were 1.04 (95% CI 0.88–1.24) and 1.15 (0.95–1.39), respectively. Formal interaction tests provided no evidence of effect modification by sex or broad occupational group. Due to the cross-sectional design, causal relationships cannot be established. The high-exposure confidence intervals included one; the findings therefore warrant cautious interpretation. Workplace thermal comfort remains relevant to worker well-being, while prospective studies with objective exposure measurements are needed.

Article.Title: Structured human resource development with AI support is associated with higher expert rated recruitment task quality among education graduates
Article.Authors: He Y.; Haja Maideen M.; Liang Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Graduate employability programmes are usually evaluated with self-report measures. We compared a structured human resource development programme supported by generative AI with career guidance matched on topics, duration and facilitator contact. Twelve intact cohorts of graduates seeking education-sector posts in Guangdong, China (N = 186), were allocated as whole units, six per condition, crossed with institution, facilitator and schedule. Blinded experts gave a global rating (0–100) of recruitment-task materials produced on site, under invigilation and without AI, before and after the programme. Ratings were made without a pre-specified rubric, which limits their interpretation. Among 168 participants with post-test data (overall attrition 9.7%), the adjusted difference favoured the AI-supported programme by 5.38 points (95% CI 2.76 to 8.01; d = 0.60) and was stable across eight specifications. Four new self-report scales showed smaller differences (d = 0.12 to 0.29), none significant after Holm correction; each scale could detect only differences of about d = 0.4. The effect on expert ratings exceeded the mean effect on self-report by 0.37 standard deviations (95% CI 0.10 to 0.63). Component analyses were exploratory. The design cannot separate the contribution of AI from structured practice and feedback.

Article.Title: BMI–hepatic steatosis phenotypes and prevalent carotid plaque: a cross-sectional health examination study
Article.Authors: Qi H.; Zhang X.; Zheng K.; Wang X.; Jiang M.; Hu H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hepatic steatosis is frequently detected during health examinations, but its vascular relevance among individuals with normal BMI remains insufficiently characterized. This study examined the cross-sectional association of ultrasound-detected hepatic steatosis and BMI–hepatic steatosis phenotypes with prevalent carotid plaque, and further explored metabolic heterogeneity among normal-BMI individuals with hepatic steatosis. This cross-sectional retrospective study included 95,157 eligible health examination records from 68,761 adults. Ultrasound-detected hepatic steatosis was used as an operational imaging-based exposure and was not considered equivalent to formal metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Examination records were classified into four BMI–hepatic steatosis phenotypes: normal BMI without hepatic steatosis, normal BMI with hepatic steatosis, BMI ≥ 24 kg/m² without hepatic steatosis, and BMI ≥ 24 kg/m² with hepatic steatosis. Multivariable logistic regression with participant-clustered robust variance estimates was used to estimate adjusted odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals for prevalent carotid plaque. Among normal-BMI examination records with hepatic steatosis, associations of non-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL-C), triglyceride-glucose index, uric acid-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) ratio, and atherogenic index of plasma with prevalent carotid plaque were further evaluated. Ultrasound-detected hepatic steatosis was associated with higher odds of prevalent carotid plaque after multivariable adjustment (OR 1.167, 95% CI 1.111–1.226). Compared with normal-BMI examination records without hepatic steatosis, those with hepatic steatosis had higher odds of prevalent carotid plaque (OR 1.229, 95% CI 1.147–1.317), as did examination records with BMI ≥ 24 kg/m² and hepatic steatosis (OR 1.151, 95% CI 1.087–1.219). In the primary logistic regression model, BMI ≥ 24 kg/m² without hepatic steatosis was not significantly associated with prevalent carotid plaque. Among normal-BMI examination records with hepatic steatosis, marker-specific linear analyses identified associations of non-HDL-C, triglyceride-glucose index, uric acid-to-HDL-C ratio, and atherogenic index of plasma with prevalent carotid plaque. Sensitivity analyses using a stricter normal-BMI definition, modified Poisson regression, and restriction to the first eligible examination per participant yielded broadly similar association patterns; no statistically significant interaction by sex or age group was observed. Among adults undergoing health examinations, ultrasound-detected hepatic steatosis within the normal-BMI range was associated with higher odds of prevalent carotid plaque, suggesting that normal BMI alone may not exclude plaque-related cardiometabolic burden. Associations of metabolic markers with prevalent carotid plaque further indicated metabolic heterogeneity within this phenotype. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether these markers improve prediction of plaque progression and cardiovascular events.

Article.Title: Multidimensional recovery monitoring in elite female football: an ecological understanding of sleep–recovery relationship
Article.Authors: Di Pinto G.; Marcelli L.; Colombo A.; Bertollo M.; Sartor F.; di Fronso S.; Curzi D.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated the associations between objective actigraphy-based sleep, morning heart rate variability, perception of recovery and sleep quality in elite female football players during a competitive season. Fifteen elite players from one Italian Serie A team were monitored over 14 weeks, collecting sleep data using wrist-worn actigraphy and sleep diaries. Daily subjective sleep and recovery metrics were also collected using brief self-report scales. Morning heart rate variability was assessed using a 1-min seated recording, to account for an autonomic marker of recovery, specifically the natural logarithm of the root mean square of successive differences (LnRMSSD). Linear mixed-effects models were used to account for repeated observations within players. When modelled simultaneously, sleep efficiency emerged as a significant positive predictor of LnRMSSD (β = 0.008, p = 0.014), highlighting the importance of sleep continuity for autonomic recovery. Total sleep time, however, did not show a significant independent association with LnRMSSD (β = − 0.051, p = 0.158). Longer-than-usual total sleep time was associated with higher subjective sleep quality (β = 0.199, p < 0.001) and perceived recovery (β = 0.305, p = 0.003). Match days were associated with lower sleep quality (β = − 0.314, p = 0.007) and perceived recovery (β = − 1.583, p < 0.001) compared with training and rest days. Monitoring in elite female football should not rely only on single markers for recovery or stress, it should encompass multifaceted and integrated strategies accounting for different dimensions of fitness and performance.

Article.Title: Uncertainty-aware offline reinforcement learning for LLM inference serving with heterogeneous SLOs
Article.Authors: Feng E.; Wang G.; Li P.; Wang Y.; Huang S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Large language model (LLM) inference workloads are bursty, have output lengths that are unknown at arrival, expose two resource-distinct phases (prefill and decode), and serve requests carrying heterogeneous service-level objectives (SLOs) on time-to-first-token (TTFT) and time-per-output-token (TPOT). Prevailing schedulers rely on static heuristics that cannot adapt to this uncertainty, while online reinforcement learning (RL) is unsafe and sample-inefficient in production. We present URSA, an uncertainty-aware, risk-sensitive scheduler trained entirely offline , without interacting with a live serving system, on scheduling transitions generated by replaying historical request traces under existing heuristic schedulers. URSA (i) predicts a calibrated distribution over each request’s output length and derived key–value (KV) cache footprint rather than a point estimate; (ii) encodes the joint state of the waiting queue, heterogeneous GPU instances, and KV occupancy as a request–instance heterogeneous graph processed by a graph neural network; (iii) learns a dispatch policy with conservative, distributional offline RL whose reward jointly optimizes SLO attainment, goodput, and KV-overflow risk; and (iv) reserves memory at a class-dependent high quantile of the predicted footprint to bound out-of-memory events. Across the BurstGPT, Azure LLM inference, and Alibaba GPU-cluster traces, URSA raises overall SLO attainment from $$71.3\%$$ (FCFS) and $$84.1\%$$ (learning-to-rank) to $$90.4\%$$ , cuts P99 TTFT by up to $$3.3\times $$ , and reduces recompute/eviction events below $$1\%$$ , approaching an oracle that knows true lengths. We analyze limitations, robustness to prediction error, and transfer to other scheduling domains.

Article.Title: Hybrid retrieval–verification framework for hallucination reduction in medical LLMs
Article.Authors: Reddy S.; Samreen S.
Article.Abstract: Clinicians use Large Language Models (LLMs) for clinical decision support, medical question answering, and automated document writing. However, these models can hallucinate and pose safety risks. While Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) improves factuality, it does not always produce outputs consistent with supporting evidence. To address these issues, this study reframes NLI-based unsupported-response rate mitigation for generative models as a confidence-aware inference problem and proposes a unified CARE-Med framework for retrieval, generation, and verification. The framework ensures the reliability of its outputs by leveraging dense retrieval, natural language inference verifiers, and a confidence scoring mechanism. The authors validated the anti-NLI-based unsupported-response optimisation method for biomedical large models proposed in this paper against the MIMIC-III, PubMedQA, and BioASQ benchmarks. The method reduces NLI-based unsupported-response rate decreases from 32% for the Baseline LLM to 10% for CARE-Med, corresponding to a 22-percentage-point or 68.8% relative reduction. Compared with conventional RAG, NLI-based unsupported-response rate decreases from 21% to 10%, corresponding to an 11-percentage-point or 52.4% relative reduction. The authors leverage explicit verification and uncertainty reasoning to meet requirements for safe clinical deployment.

Article.Title: Headway switching, rather than feedforward loss alone, destabilises cooperative platoons under V2X dropout
Article.Authors: Haneesh K.; Jisha P.; Suresh K.; Aravind P.
Article.Abstract: Cooperative Adaptive Cruise Control (CACC) uses vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication to sustain short, string-stable headways, but real wireless links drop packets, eroding this guarantee. We show that at a representative moderate-loss point, discontinuous headway switching on packet loss, not feedforward loss itself, is the dominant destabilising mechanism: a canonical plant-inverting design remains string stable losing feedforward at fixed headway, but not when switching headway on loss. Continuous, non-learned scheduling recovers stability at moderate but not severe loss. We train a dropout-aware multi-agent reinforcement-learning (TD3) controller with a learned V2X reliability gate; four of five training seeds converge to a policy string stable at $$30\%$$ and $$60\%$$ loss, outperforming the strongest classical scheduler under V2X-only information. The comparison is not information-matched: the learned policy also observes an idealised, always-exact onboard predecessor acceleration no classical controller here uses, and a non-learned controller given that signal alone is competitive with it, limiting attribution to learning. Frequency sensitivity, severe-burst robustness, and training reliability are all seed-dependent. These results identify switching, not information loss, as a primary vulnerability of communication-dependent platooning, and give a candid account of how much a learning-based remedy owes to learning itself.

Article.Title: A global taxonomy and computational characterization of major sign languages for scalable AI recognition systems
Article.Authors: Harish M.; Rashmi B.; M. S.
Article.Abstract: Sign language is characterized as natural visual-gestural language with autonomous linguistic structures, varied orthographic influences, and legal status. Despite the recent advancements in deep learning-based recognition systems, these systems face the problem of regional biases, which limits the scalability of the systems and excludes millions of users from low-resource backgrounds. The study focuses on a comprehensive Global Taxonomy and Computational Characterization of several significant sign languages across five continents of the world. These languages are classified based on six crucial parameters: alphabetic adaptation, linguistic family, legal status, user population, manual spelling structures: one-handed or two-handed. The research proposes a Hierarchical Transformer Architecture capable of accommodating various linguistic variations. It follows a three-layer approach: a universal hand pose encoder, family-specific adaptation, and classifier head. Moreover, it presents a Global Sign Language Complexity Index (GSLCI) and a Fairness Index to measure the complexities of various sign language. Analysis of the proposed optimized framework indicates a maximum accuracy of 91% using the common features of various language families which can be considered a preferable mode of communication for people with hearing and speech impairments.

Article.Title: Peak-valley resource demand forecasting for enhanced data reliability
Article.Authors: Zhong L.; Jiang X.; Zheng K.; Lin G.; Wu H.; Yang J.; Sun Y.; Li S.
Article.Abstract: Accurate load demand forecasting serves as the fundamental prerequisite for data reliability analysis in multi-user heterogeneous load access scenarios. In such environments, the volume of data flows generated by industrial, residential, and commercial loads exhibits complex temporal variation patterns characterized by distinct periodicity and volatility. These patterns are governed by multiple factors including diverse user behaviors, operational schedules, and seasonal variations. However, conventional reliability assessment methods rarely account for the periodic nature of peak/valley load fluctuations and the volatility of sudden data surges, leading to inaccurate reliability evaluations, e.g., underestimated transmission risks during peak load periods or inefficient resource redundancy during off-peak intervals. To address this challenge, we propose a peak-valley load demand forecasting (TAPV-RDF) model. The core motivation is to model and fit the complex temporal variation patterns of heterogeneous load data flows, which demonstrate multi-scale periodicity mixed with surge components. Given the high complexity of these patterns, the proposed model first constructs a “user-load” characteristic mapping framework by integrating multi-dimensional user attributes with time-series load data. A Gated User-aware Temporal Fusion Variational Autoencoder (GUTF-VAE) is designed to extract periodic load characteristics and surge amplitude features; this component introduces gated fusion mechanisms and attention-driven latent space regularization. Subsequently, a Peak-Valley Multi-Scale Gated LSTM (PVMS-G-LSTM) is proposed to capture multi-scale temporal dependencies across varying load conditions. Experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate that TAPV-RDF consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Specifically, our framework achieves improvements across the three datasets. Ablation studies confirm the contribution of each architectural component, while statistical significance tests validate the reliability of improvements. The proposed framework provides a practical solution for load demand forecasting and resource provisioning in modern power grid systems.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: variational autoencoder; gated fusion; load forecasting; data reliability

Article.Title: Belief-integrated timed elastic band planning for robust indoor person following under intermittent observations
Article.Authors: Guan J.; Liu S.; Guan K.; Zheng H.; Hu W.
Article.Abstract: Indoor person-following robots routinely lose sight of their target at corners, doorways, and in crowds, and most local planners then stall at the last seen position. We present IO-TEB (Intermittent-Observation Timed Elastic Band), a local planner that maintains a probabilistic estimate of the hidden person’s position and its growing uncertainty, feeds this estimate directly into trajectory optimization, and actively searches likely paths when the person stays hidden. Across 4,320 simulated episodes covering eight indoor scenes, three occlusion durations, and real pedestrian trajectories, IO-TEB completed 87.36% of following tasks, versus 55.14% for the standard timed elastic band planner. It was statistically equivalent to a conventional design that handles the same estimate in a separate finite-state supervisor, indicating that embedding the estimate in the optimizer costs neither accuracy nor computation. Compared with model predictive control (MPC) using trajectory prediction and three recent person-following planners, IO-TEB was not the most accurate, but in our implementation it missed the 100 ms control-cycle deadline least often (3.32% of cycles versus 5.14–44.21%). Ablation shows that replacing the last observation with the predicted estimate as the following reference accounts for most of the gain, whereas the uncertainty-dependent terms added no consistent benefit.

Article.Title: Mapping soil salinity and prediction uncertainty across different depths using quantile regression forests
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Han D.; Wang X.
Article.Abstract: Accurate assessment of soil salinity across the soil profile is necessary for sustainable agricultural management, yet conventional surface-based observations often provide limited information about subsurface salinity conditions. This study developed a depth-resolved digital soil mapping framework to predict soil electrical conductivity (EC) across five standard depth intervals (0–25, 25–50, 50–75, 75–100, and 100–125 cm) in Shandong Province, eastern China. A total of 617 soil profiles were used, and continuous profile observations were harmonized into standard layers using equal-area quadratic spline functions. Environmental covariates representing spectral salinity characteristics, vegetation conditions, climate, and terrain attributes were compiled at a 30-m spatial resolution. Principal component analysis was applied to reduce multicollinearity among predictors, and Quantile Regression Forest (QRF) models were implemented to estimate EC and its 90% prediction intervals. Model accuracy was evaluated using repeated 10-fold cross-validation. The results showed a clear decline in predictive performance with increasing depth: the coefficient of determination decreased from 0.79 in the 0–25 cm layer to 0.51 in the 100–125 cm layer, whereas RMSE increased from 0.142 to 0.295 dS m⁻¹. Surface EC predictions were mainly driven by salinity-sensitive spectral indices, including SSIB, CSI, and SC, while the contribution of these variables weakened in deeper layers. Conversely, topographic wetness index, valley depth, relative slope position, and climatic variables became increasingly important below 50 cm, suggesting a shift from predominantly spectral controls near the surface to hydro-topographic and climatic regulation at depth. Higher EC values were generally predicted in the eastern and southeastern parts of the study area, whereas uncertainty was more pronounced in western and central transitional zones. The findings demonstrate the value of integrating depth-specific environmental information with probabilistic machine learning to produce spatially explicit, uncertainty-aware maps of soil salinity for improved monitoring and site-specific land management.

Article.Title: Tectonic regionality and geophysical controls of the fractal dimension and b-value of seismicity in the Chinese mainland
Article.Authors: Bi J.; Li Y.; Pan Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Seismicity exhibits complex spatiotemporal patterns that are critical for hazard assessment. Using the Chinese mainland earthquake catalog (1970–2025), we analyze seismicity parameters across 20 seismic belts. After estimating the completeness magnitude ( M c ) for each belt, we apply nearest-neighbor distance declustering and calculate b -value and spatial fractal dimension ( D c ) before and after declustering using the maximum likelihood and correlation integral methods. We examine their spatial distributions and relationships with heat flow and maximum shear strain rate. Declustering increases D c -value (from 1.30 to 1.65) while decreasing a - and b -values, confirming that aftershock removal diffuses spatial patterns and reduces the proportion of small events. The relationship between b -value and D c -value varies regionally: negative in the Tibetan seismic region, positive in the South China seismic region and Xinjiang seismic region, and weakly negative in the North China seismic region. Heat flow modulates seismicity parameters in a consistent manner. The b -value is positively correlated with heat flow both before and after declustering, whereas the D c -value is negatively correlated with heat flow before declustering but not after. These results suggest that thermal weakening promotes microcracking, raising the b -value, and facilitates strain localization along major faults, lowering the D c -value. The D c -value and maximum shear strain rate relationship is positive in eastern extensional regions and negative in western compressional regions, reflecting contrasting strain energy partitioning mechanisms. These findings provide quantitative constraints on deep controls of seismicity complexity and offer new criteria for seismic hazard assessment.

Article.Title: Grade determination from systematic color and fracture mapping enables smart quarrying of dimension stone
Article.Authors: Yarahmadi R.; Ranjbar G.; Sarikhani Khorrami M.
Article.Abstract: The dimension stone industry lacks a quantitative, real-time grade equivalent to that used in metallic mining, resulting in suboptimal resource utilization and production planning. This study proposes an operational grade for dimension stone defined by two intrinsic characteristics: color quality and structural integrity. Through a year-long case study at a marble quarry, these variables were systematically mapped in 205 large primary blocks, and a spatially explicit block value (BV) map was generated. The calculated BV ranged from 1 to 5 across the bench, with a mean of 2.8; only 6% of blocks attained the highest BV category, while 12% fell into the lowest. Discontinuity analysis revealed that the cutting direction could be aligned with the dominant joint set to improve block recovery. By applying this information to adjust the extraction sequence, the quarry achieved a 14% higher marketable block productivity and a 14% reduction in waste volume relative to the quarry-wide average. The BV grade map served as an internal benchmark, enabling real-time production decisions without requiring a pre-existing baseline. This framework provides a quantitative grade metric for dimension stone, filling a long-standing gap, and demonstrates how site-specific geological intelligence can drive more efficient, sustainable, and smart quarrying.

Article.Title: External observers’ and local users’ perceptions of vegetation and surface transformations in historic urban square renovations
Article.Authors: Kosno-Jończy J.; Suchocka M.; Jankowski P.; Błaszczyk M.; Dudek-Klimiuk J.; Pachnowska B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Historic urban squares in Poland have undergone extensive renovations involving changes in vegetation, biologically active surfaces, and paving materials. This study examined how these transformations are perceived by external observers and local users. It combined face-to-face surveys with local users in five cities ( n = 100) and a nationwide online survey ( n = 1,005), whose participants evaluated square functions and before-and-after photographs of renovations in seven cities. Respondents strongly preferred vegetation, particularly trees and flower beds. The combined practice of removing trees and replacing biologically active surfaces with impermeable materials was negatively evaluated by 84% of local respondents. Renovations retaining more existing vegetation and biologically active surfaces generally received more favourable evaluations, with the highest local satisfaction recorded in Bełchatów (82%). Local users also frequently identified insufficient shade as a problem affecting their comfort when using the squares. Differences between photograph-based assessments and local user evaluations were particularly evident in Ciechanów and Skierniewice, where relatively favourable external assessments contrasted with low resident satisfaction. These findings show that visual assessments do not fully capture the functional qualities experienced by everyday users. The results highlight the importance of retaining vegetation, providing shade, and involving local users in historic square renovations.

Article.Title: Practical prediction of concrete compressive strength using an interpretable enhanced linear regression model
Article.Authors: Sadeghi A.
Article.Abstract: Reliable estimation of concrete compressive strength is essential for quality control in civil engineering. While complex machine learning models offer high accuracy, their lack of transparency limits practical adoption. This study develops an interpretable linear regression model in which cement, slag, and fly ash are represented as total binder content and slag-to-binder ratio, raw age is replaced by its natural logarithm, and water-to-cement ratio is retained alongside superplasticizer and aggregate contents. Using a publicly available dataset of 1,030 concrete mixtures, the final model achieved a full-data R 2 of 0.821 and, under nested GroupKFold cross-validation grouped by unique mixture design, a mean outer-fold R 2 of 0.805 (SD = 0.018), RMSE of 7.30 MPa, and MAE of 5.62 MPa. Multicollinearity was controlled, with a maximum variance inflation factor of 6.35 and a condition number of 4.97. All predictors were statistically significant ( p < 0.001), and the maximum Cook’s distance was 0.0217. Benchmarking against tuned Random Forest (nested R 2 = 0.884) and XGBoost (nested R 2 = 0.882) indicated that while ensemble methods offer higher accuracy, the proposed linear model retains interpretable coefficients and provides a transparent screening tool for preliminary strength estimation within the range of the studied dataset.

Article.Title: Cytomorphological assessment of buccal mucosal epithelial cells in Sudanese children with sickle cell anaemia: a pilot case-control study
Article.Authors: Batran S.; Abdulatif S.; Mohamed Z.; Zakout Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sickle cell anaemia (SCA) is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by the presence of homozygous haemoglobin S. To compare the cytomorphological features of buccal mucosal epithelial cells in children with sickle cell anaemia (SCA) receiving treatment with those of healthy controls, in a pilot case-control study. Buccal smears were collected from 80 Sudanese children: 40 children with homozygous SCA (HbSS) receiving treatment (cases) and 40 clinically healthy children matched for age and sex (controls). Smears were fixed immediately in 95% ethanol, stained with the Papanicolaou (Pap) technique and examined qualitatively by a cytopathologist blinded to group allocation. Each smear was screened in its entirety for predefined features: nuclear enlargement, hyperchromasia, nuclear membrane irregularity and cytoplasmic changes. Data were analysed descriptively using SPSS version 26.0. Of the 40 cases, 22 (55%) were female and 18 (45%) were male, with a mean age of 9.48 years (range 3–15 years). No cytomorphological abnormalities were identified in the buccal smears of either cases or controls. In this pilot study, no cytomorphological differences were observed between treated children with SCA and healthy controls. Because no pretreatment assessment or untreated SCA group was available, these findings cannot be attributed to treatment. Larger prospective studies are needed.

Article.Title: New geophysical insights into gold mineralization at Gabal Abu Marawat, Central Eastern Desert, Egypt
Article.Authors: Nagy M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Abu Marawat district in the Central Eastern Desert of Egypt hosts significant gold mineralization, yet the deep structural and magmatic controls governing its distribution have remained poorly constrained. This study applies an integrated magnetic interpretation workflow to resolve the structural architecture of the mineral system. By combining reduced-to-pole (RTP) and upward-continued fields with advanced edge-detection filters (TAHG, LTHG) and automated lineament extraction, we document a deep-seated, regionally persistent N–S to NNE–SSW shear corridor. This D3-related structural framework overprints earlier NE–SW and NW–SE fabrics and exerts first-order control on gold localization along rheological contacts. Crucially, Circular Feature Transform (CFT) analysis identifies depth-persistent, ring-like magnetic anomalies coincident with felsic intrusions at Abu Marawat gold mine and G. Wae’ra. These CFT-defined circular magnetic anomalies, tentatively interpreted as possible intrusive centers, raise the hypothesis that Abu Marawat may host a hybrid orogenic–magmatic component, which requires independent verification. Depth estimations using Euler deconvolution and Source Parameter Imaging (SPI) define a vertically integrated architecture: shallow shear-hosted rock units (< 0.8 km) are connected via deep-rooted fault networks (resolved > 1.5 km depth). Finally, a fuzzy-logic prospectivity model was developed by integrating structural complexity, CFT anomalies, depth solutions, and lithologies. The model is spatially consistent with known deposits falling within high fuzzy-membership (high-favorability) zones, which were used, in part, to inform the model's lithological favorability criteria; this spatial coincidence should therefore be interpreted with caution rather than as independent validation and delineates several underexplored, high-favorability segments along the Semna–Miranda Gossans gold mines and Abu Marawat corridor. This study illustrates how combining advanced magnetic filtering with fuzzy logic to constrain exploration targets, and indicates a notable role of N–S deep-seated shears, and CFT-defined circular magnetic anomalies in the Arabian-Nubian Shield's gold metallogeny.

Article.Title: Sport-specific differences in DXA-derived bone outcomes persist after adjustment for lean mass in competitive female athletes
Article.Authors: Kaikkonen M.; Savolainen E.; Hackney A.; Alanko L.; Laatikainen-Raussi I.; Rikkonen T.; Sirola J.; Valtonen M.; Kröger H.; Ihalainen J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Bone mineral density (BMD) contributes to skeletal strength, and mechanical loading influences skeletal adaptation. This cross-sectional study compared total-body BMD, BMD Z-scores, and bone mineral content (BMC) between Finnish female athletes ( n = 207) and non-athlete controls ( n = 307) and across endurance, antigravitation, ball game and power sports. Outcomes were assessed using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Analyses were adjusted for age and total lean mass. Athletes had higher total-body BMD, BMD Z-scores, and BMC than controls in unadjusted comparisons (all p < .001). After adjustment, differences in BMD and BMD Z-scores remained, whereas the BMC difference was no longer significant. Lean mass was positively associated with all bone outcomes, with the strongest association observed for BMC. Bone outcomes also differed by sport category, with power athletes having the highest and endurance athletes the lowest mean values. Sport-category effects remained significant after adjustment for age and total lean mass. Although mechanical loading was not directly measured, sport-specific loading characteristics may provide useful context when interpreting DXA-derived measures in athletes.

Article.Title: Radial phase engineering for divergence control of OAM beams using a transmitarray metasurface
Article.Authors: Paramanik A.; Rao M.; Ukey A.; Venkata K.; Subramanian V.
Article.Abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams show more divergence with increasing mode number, which limits their use in communication and imaging. Existing phase engineering techniques modify the divergence by adding an axicon and a lens phase term and observing the resultant beam through trial and error. Here, we have used an inverse relationship between the prescribed target beam radius at a chosen propagation plane and the radial phase correction required for it. The radial phase correction is determined by a relationship between the phase gradient and the trajectory slope. This inverse design enables divergence control via phase-only modulation on a fixed-aperture metasurface (MS). To study the efficiency of the phase correction mechanism, a compact two-dielectric three-metallic-layer-based MS is used with 2 \(\pi \) phase coverage and transmission greater than −3 dB at 28 GHz. By modulating the phase of individual unit cells across the MS, OAM modes are generated. Then, the radial phase correction is applied to produce equal-radius OAM beams. Full-wave simulations confirm the theoretical prediction, MSs generate OAM modes with an identical radius. We achieve an equal radius of 4.6 \(\lambda \) for three OAM modes ( \(\ell \) = 1, 2, and 3) at z = 40 \(\lambda \) for 28 GHz. Also, the phase-correction method is used to generate perfect vortex beams for modes 1 and 2 up to a 40 \(\lambda \) distance. Experimental verification is performed to confirm the formation of equal radius beams. The presented approach provides a general framework for multimodal multiplexing and divergence-controlled beam engineering in millimeter and microwave systems.

Article.Title: Altered integrin αvβ3 and extracellular matrix-associated molecular profile in granulosa cells from women with polycystic ovary syndrome
Article.Authors: Gülüşür A.; Karaca Ç.; Kenan S.; Keklikçioğlu I.; Eroğlu S.
Article.Abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common endocrine disorder and a leading cause of infertility due to lack of ovulation in women of reproductive age. Despite the presence of numerous antral follicles, ovulation often fails to occur in women with PCOS. Interactions between granulosa cells and the extracellular matrix (ECM) play a key role in regulating the follicular microenvironment. This study aimed to evaluate integrin αvβ3 and ECM-related molecules in granulosa cells from women with PCOS. The study included 18 women undergoing in vitro fertilisation (IVF) treatment. Nine patients diagnosed with PCOS according to the Rotterdam criteria formed the PCOS group, while nine women undergoing IVF due to male factor infertility served as controls. The immunoreactivity of integrin αvβ3, VEGF, FGF-1 and MMP-9 was evaluated using immunocytochemistry on cumulus granulosa cells obtained during oocyte retrieval. In addition, integrin αv and integrin β3 gene expression levels were analysed using quantitative qRT-PCR. Integrin αvβ3, VEGF and FGF-1 immunoreactivity were significantly higher in the PCOS group than in the control group (p = 0.029, p < 0.001 and p = 0.010, respectively), whereas MMP-9 immunoreactivity did not differ between the groups (p = 0.167). qRT-PCR analysis revealed no difference in ITGAV and ITGB3 mRNA expression levels between the PCOS group and the control group. These findings suggest that altered immunoreactivity of integrin αvβ3 and ECM-associated molecules may be associated with changes in the follicular microenvironment in women with PCOS. This molecular profile may contribute to a better understanding of the mechanisms underlying ovulatory dysfunction.

Article.Title: RSM-based optimization of mechanical and moisture resistance properties of ternary polymer nanocomposites
Article.Authors: Wero A.; Yigezu B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Epoxy-based polymer Nanocomposites are widely investigated for electrical insulation applications due to their exceptional mechanical and dielectric properties; however, moisture absorption and brittleness remain major challenges. This study aimed to develop and optimize Epoxy/ Ethylene Propylene Diene Monomer (EPDM) /nano-silica ternary nanocomposites with increased tensile strength and reduced water absorption using Response Surface Methodology (RSM) based on Central Composite Design (CCD). The effects of EPDM concentration, nano-silica loading, and sonication time were evaluated through 20 experimental runs. Water absorption was measured according to ASTM D570 after 240-hour immersion, while tensile strength was determined using ASTM D638 standard. The statistical analysis showed that all three processing parameters significantly affected the measured responses within the investigated experimental ranges, with nano-silica loading showing the largest statistical effect. The developed linear models showed satisfactory fit and predictive statistics, with non-significant lack-of-fit results. Increasing nano-silica loading and sonication time was associated with increased tensile strength and reduced water absorption within the experimental design space. These response trends may be related to changes in the polymer–filler environment and the processing-dependent state of the silica-containing phase. The optimized formulation exhibited a tensile strength of 90.9 ± 0.46 MPa and water absorption of 0.0441 ± 0.0003% under the investigated test conditions. Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of the Epoxy/EPDM/nano-silica system as a candidate for further investigation in electrical-insulation applications.

Article.Title: Hybrid local–global vision transformer framework for robust plant disease detection in precision agriculture
Article.Authors: Sharma A.; Sharma C.; Sandhu R.; Prabha C.; Mapari S.
Article.Abstract: Correctly identifying plant diseases has significant consequences for sustainable agricultural productivity as well as for national and global food security. Even though traditional convolutional neural networks have achieved great success detecting diseases using images, the receptive field is inherently limited which in turn limits the ability simply to model long-range dependencies. However, vision transformers can capture global relationships but often fail to maintain fine-grained local texture information that may be critical for distinguishing subtle symptoms caused by diseases variably. To mitigate these issues, we introduce ViT-LGFNet, a Hybrid Local-Global Fusion Vision Transformer that uses local convolutional feature extraction along with global self-attention encoding. The proposed architecture is built with the following proposed modules: a Local CNN Stem module for learning fine textures followed by a Transformer Encoder module for modeling contextual features. We propose a dual Cross-Attention Fusion Module that performs bi-direction direction exchanges between local and global tokens to increase the discriminative ability for the hybrid representation. The PlantVillage dataset results demonstrate ViT-LGFNet mean validation accuracy of 95.15% ± 0.74 across multiple runs, with a best-case performance of 96.28%. Grad-CAM and Attention Rollout maps were placed for visualization purposes, demonstrating that the model accurately attends to the disease-affected part of an image. The proposed model offers a reliable and explainable benchmark for plant disease recognition and shows potential for application in smart farming systems and AI-based crop health monitoring applications.

Article.Title: Low-density workover fluid technology designed to lower the required sealing strength for operations in the fractured reservoirs of the Ordos Basin
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Liu G.; Yang B.; Yuwen X.; Zhai X.; Wei P.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The tight Upper Paleozoic sandstone reservoirs and Lower Paleozoic carbonate reservoirs in the Ordos Basin necessitate fracturing or acidizing to generate artificial fractures prior to production, classifying them as typical fractured reservoirs. During workover operations, the depletion of formation pressure results in a considerable loss pressure differential. Conventional sealing operations impose overly stringent requirements on plugging materials, giving rise to substantial risks of formation damage and slow post-workover production recovery rates. Laboratory investigations identified optimized components: modified lauramidopropyl betaine as the foaming agent, alcohol–ether modified polyhydroxy polymer as the foam stabilizer, modified hydroxyethyl starch as the viscosifier, and a xanthan gum derivative as the stabilizer. Aiming at a base fluid density of 0.85–0.95 g/cm³, an orthogonal experimental design produced a basic formula: (0.80–1.40%) viscosifier+(0.5–0.6%) stabilizer+(0.18–0.32%) foaming agent+(0.28–0.32%) foam stabilizer. Glass microspheres with a D90 particle size ≤ 70 μm, a density of 0.42–0.44 g/cm³, and a compressive strength ≥ 40 MPa were selected as the low-density particles. A low-density workover fluid system with an adjustable density range of 0.65–0.90 g/cm³ was developed. Laboratory tests indicated that increasing the low-density particle concentration from 0 to 50% led to a reduction in the system density from 0.85 to 0.65 g/cm³. After static aging for 48 h at room temperature and 90 °C, the density increments were less than 0.05 g/cm³ and 0.10 g/cm³ respectively. After repeated stirring at 3000 r/min for 5 min, the density increments were less than 0.01 g/cm³ and 0.03 g/cm³ respectively, demonstrating stable density under reservoir temperature conditions. Five fluid samples with densities ranging from 0.65 to 0.85 g/cm³ were injected at a constant rate of 0.5 mL/min into artificial fractures 0.1 mm wide. The pressure increase relative to water displacement ranged from 6.20 to 17.15 MPa, with lower-density fluids exhibiting higher pressure increases, indicating enhanced plugging performance with decreasing density. After plugging the core samples, 1.5 pore volumes of a 1% ammonium persulfate solution were directly injected and allowed to soak for 2 h to break the gel. The measured core permeability recovery rate ranged from 92.48 to 95.56%, demonstrating excellent formation protection. Field applications in two low-pressure gas wells, G-X and SN-X, completed in the tight Shanxi Formation sandstone and Majiagou Formation carbonate reservoirs with pressure coefficients of 0.76 g/cm³ and 0.43 g/cm³ respectively, involved the injection of 53.5 m³ and 34.3 m³ of the low-density workover fluid (densities 0.76 g/cm³ and 0.75 g/cm³). Fluid returns were observed at the wellhead with a loss rate below 0.01 m³/h. After workover, gas lift was directly initiated for fluid recovery. The post-workover gas production recovery rate reached 95.83% to 130%. This study confirms that the low-density workover fluid, by reducing the fluid column pressure in the wellbore, effectively mitigates the pressure burden on the fractured formation. This addresses the limitation of inadequate formation protection caused by excessive plugging strength during conventional workover operations.

Article.Title: Enhancing circular textile waste recycling: a comparative analysis of European countries and South Korea
Article.Authors: Chae C.; Kim K.; Chu B.; Kim T.; Kim D.; Lee S.; Kim I.
Article.Abstract: The rapid increase in textile waste has intensified the need for effective strategies to establish circular textile management systems. This study evaluates textile waste management policies in South Korea through a comparative analysis with selected European countries and examines multiple recycling pathways, including mechanical recycling, chemical recycling, and energy recovery. The comparative policy analysis showed that the European countries generally covered a broader range of life-cycle stages and included economic and communication instruments that were not identified in South Korea. Product quality analysis further confirmed that qualified recycled products can be obtained through selected recycling pathways, indicating the technical applicability of textile waste recycling. However, policy and technological improvements are still required to support practical implementation. To address these challenges, this study proposes integrated policy and technology measures, including textile extended producer responsibility (EPR), recyclable design, digital product passport (DPP)-based tracking, advanced sorting, recycled-content requirements, and financial incentives. A hierarchical prioritization framework based on material circularity, value retention, and environmental considerations is also suggested to support the development of circular textile management systems.

Article.Title: Global polynomial synchronization of uncertain fractional variable-order BAM neural networks with proportional delay via quantized control
Article.Authors: Pavithra G.; Dharani S.; Sivakumar M.
Article.Abstract: The objective of this work is to study the global polynomial synchronization (GPS) of fractional variable-order bidirectional associative memory neural networks (FVOBAMNNs) subjected to proportional delays and uncertain parameters. To deal with this challenge, a quantized controller incorporating linear error states and a non-smooth switching term is proposed. By leveraging this controller, GPS is attained by constructing an appropriate Lyapunov functional (LF) and applying suitable inequality-based techniques. The usefulness of the proposed synchronization approach is illustrated through two computational experiments.

Article.Title: Hyaluronic acid-functionalized polypyrrole nanoparticles with controlled oxidation for targeted chemo-photothermal therapy of prostate cancer
Article.Authors: Imani F.; Karkhaneh A.; Hossein-Khannazer N.; Karimi-Soflou R.
Article.Abstract: Combined chemo-photothermal therapy as a synergistic approach has emerged to overcome the limitations of conventional chemotherapy. In this study, multifunctional polypyrrole-based nanoparticles were developed for targeted chemo-photothermal therapy of prostate cancer. In the first stage, the effect of polypyrrole backbone oxidative defects on the photothermal properties of nanoparticles was evaluated by changing the oxidant concentration during polymerization or chemical reduction of the structure post synthesis. The results showed an inverse relationship between the density of oxidative defects and the near-infrared (NIR) light absorption of the nanoparticles. To introduce active targeting capability to the system, hyaluronic acid (HA) was then conjugated onto the nanoparticle surface as a CD44-targeting ligand. Thereafter, the anticancer drug doxorubicin was loaded onto the nanoparticles, and drug release studies confirmed the photothermal responsiveness of the system. Cellular evaluations were performed on three common prostate cancer cell lines PC-3, DU145, and LNCaP, which exhibit different levels of CD44 expression. Chemotherapy alone demonstrated a significant size-dependent cytotoxic effect in CD44 positive cell lines, indicating the capability of the system for selective CD44 targeting. However, photothermal therapy induced cell death independent of CD44 expression levels. Finally, combined chemo-photothermal therapy induced a strong enhanced therapeutic effect, reducing cell viability to below 15% in all three cell lines, which represents a significant improvement compared to either treatment alone. The overall findings demonstrate the potential of the designed nanoparticles as a multifunctional platform for combined chemo-photothermal therapy of prostate cancer, particularly in the context of tumor heterogeneity and phenotypic differences among cancer cells.

Article.Title: Identification and validation of key genes related to innate immune cell barrier in type 2 diabetes mellitus: transcriptome and single-cell combined analysis
Article.Authors: Wu F.; Zheng G.
Article.Abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) constitutes a significant global public health issue, characterized by insulin resistance and progressive functional decline of pancreatic β-cells. The regulatory role of innate immune cell barrier (ICB)-related genes (ICBRGs) in the progression of T2DM remains unclear. This study aims to identify the key ICBRGs associated with T2DM, elucidate their regulatory mechanisms and clinical significance, and provide molecular targets for precise therapeutic interventions. Initially, T2DM-related transcriptome datasets were downloaded from public databases, with GSE15932 serving as the training set and GSE26168 as the validation set, along with the single-cell dataset GSE268210. Candidate genes were obtained by screening the intersection with ICBRGs through differential expression analysis. Subsequent identification of key genes was conducted using various machine learning algorithms, such as XGBoost and Random Forest (RF). In-depth exploration of gene functions involved immune infiltration analysis, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis, encompassing aspects such as cell communication and pseudotemporal analysis. Finally, reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) was employed to validate the expression of the identified key genes. Three key genes were successfully identified: CEBPA, ELANE, and TGFB1. Immune infiltration analysis revealed significant correlations of these genes with immune cells, particularly monocytes and CD4 + memory T cells. GSEA results indicated co-enrichment of these genes in critical metabolic pathways, including the insulin signaling pathway. Single-cell analysis confirmed that monocytes play a pivotal role in T2DM, exhibiting the highest communication probability with B cells. Pseudotime analysis demonstrated dynamic expression patterns of the key genes during the differentiation of monocytes. RT-qPCR validation indicated significant upregulation of CEBPA and ELANE in T2DM blood samples, while TGFB1 exhibited an increasing trend that did not reach statistical significance. CEBPA, ELANE, and TGFB1 may contribute to the pathogenesis of T2DM through monocyte-related immune regulation. CEBPA and ELANE demonstrated consistent experimental validation, while TGFB1 is proposed as a candidate biomarker that warrants further confirmation in larger clinical cohorts.

Article.Title: Design of MIL-53/carbon aerogel/CoFe2O4 ternary composites with improved photocatalytic activity for water treatment
Article.Authors: Smith S.; Shanmugam P.; Gnanasekaran L.; Shanmugapriya D.; Zheng A.; Boonyuen S.
Article.Abstract: A novel MIL-53/CA/CoFe 2 O 4 ternary nanocomposite was successfully synthesized via a facile hydrothermal- in situ precipitation route, integrating the porous carbonaceous aerogel (CA) framework with MIL-53(Fe) and magnetic CoFe 2 O 4 nanoparticles. The structure and morphology of the composites were systematically analyzed using XRD, FTIR, FESEM/EDS mapping, HRTEM, and UV-DRS, confirming the formation of a well-crystallized composite structure in which MIL-53 and CoFe 2 O 4 nanoparticles were uniformly anchored onto the CA matrix. The synergistic interfacial coupling between MIL-53, CA, and CoFe 2 O 4 significantly enhanced charge transfer and suppressed electron-hole pair recombination, as evidenced by the improved photocatalytic performance. The MIL-53/CA/CoFe 2 O 4 composite exhibited excellent photocatalytic activity toward the percentage of degradation of methylene blue (MB) (97.75%) and Congo red (CR) (93.74%) dyes, following pseudo-first-order kinetics with rate constants of 0.0211 min − 1 and 0.0187 min − 1 , respectively. Recycling and scavenging studies revealed that the prepared composite maintained over 90% of its photocatalytic activity after five consecutive cycles, while electron-derived reactive species played a key factor. These results demonstrate that the rational combination of MIL-53, carbon aerogel, and magnetic ferrite components can yield highly efficient and magnetically separable photocatalysts, offering great potential for advanced environmental remediation and energy-related applications.

Article.Title: Brown sugar levels influence fermentation quality and microbiota of mixed wheat straw and Pennisetum giganteum silage
Article.Authors: Zhang J.; Wang L.; Mirizati A.; Ma Y.; Bayin B.; Hu Y.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated the effects of different levels of brown sugar addition on the fermentation quality and microbial community structure of mixed wheat straw and Pennisetum giganteum silage, aiming to provide a theoretical basis for optimizing ensiling techniques for Pennisetum giganteum . In this experiment, fresh Pennisetum giganteum and wheat straw were used as ensiling materials at a 7:3 fresh-weight ratio ( Pennisetum giganteum : wheat straw)were used as ensiling materials. A composite microbial inoculant, consisting of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (≥ 1 × 10 11 CFU/g), Lentilactobacillus buchneri (≥ 2 × 10 10 CFU/g), and cellulase (≥ 1 × 10 4 U/g), was added to all treatment groups at a uniform rate of 0.01 g kg −1 fresh weight. Five treatment groups were then established with brown sugar addition levels of 0 (T0), 2 (T2), 4 (T4), 6 (T6) and 8 (T8) g kg −1 fresh weight, respectively, with three replicates per group. The silage was fermented at room temperature for 60 days. The results showed that: (1) The contents of acetic acid ( P < 0.05)and lactic acid ( P < 0.01) in group T6 were significantly or highly significantly higher than those in the other groups; the butyric acid contents in groups T6 and T8 were significantly lower than those in T0 and T2 ( P < 0.05). (2) PCoA and NMDS analyses revealed a clear separation between the T0 and T6 groups, indicating that brown sugar addition significantly altered the overall microbial community structure of the silage. (3) Network structure analysis results show that the addition of brown sugar altered the network characteristics of the silage bacterial community, with the highest average degree and graph density observed in groups T4 and T6, indicating enhanced cooperativity among genera. In conclusion, the addition of an appropriate amount of brown sugar effectively improved the fermentation quality and optimized the microbial community structure of mixed wheat straw and Pennisetum giganteum silage, with the best fermentation outcome observed at a brown sugar addition level of 6 g kg −1 .

Article.Title: Dynamics of cell states and alternative splicing following kidney ischemia-reperfusion injury
Article.Authors: Markiewitz D.; Goldberger J.; Kalisky T.
Article.Abstract: The progression of kidney damage in chronic kidney disease (CKD) involves multiple post-injury stages and complex cellular and molecular mechanisms that are not yet fully understood. In our study we set out to characterize the dynamics of alternative splicing following kidney injury. To this end, we analyzed publicly available bulk RNA-seq data covering nine time points following a kidney ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) mouse experiment. Using topic modeling we discerned five distinct temporal phases corresponding to the following cell states: “early injury response”, “injury”, “repairing”, “failed recovery”, and “healthy proximal tubule”. Additionally, we discovered a set of genes that are alternatively spliced between selected time points associated with these cell states, some of which are related to injury, stress, EMT, and apoptosis. Finally, we found several putative splicing regulators that are differentially expressed between the different time points and whose binding motifs are enriched in the vicinity of alternatively spliced exons, indicating that they may play critical roles in alternative splicing dynamics following kidney injury and repair. These findings enhance our understanding of the molecular mechanisms involved in kidney injury and repair, offering potential avenues for developing targeted therapeutic strategies for acute kidney injury (AKI) and its progression to CKD.

Article.Title: Accuracy of guided endodontic access evaluated through a fully digital workflow with three-dimensional vector-based measurement: an in vitro study
Article.Authors: Klein E.; Carvalho A.; Nakaie D.; Kussaba I.; Kurihara E.
Article.Abstract: To characterize a fully digital, vector-based workflow for assessing the accuracy of static guided endodontic access and to determine the precision of access execution under controlled laboratory conditions, minimizing methodological bias associated with tomographic-based measurements. This in vitro experimental study used 18 three-dimensionally printed resin replicas of a standardized maxillary central incisor (tooth #11) model with a flattened apical surface allowing direct visual verification of the access point. Static guided endodontic access was performed by a single calibrated operator using a static guide planned in Implant Studio (3Shape, Copenhagen, Denmark) with a metal sleeve (1.5-mm internal diameter; 7.5-mm length). The dependent variable was the linear deviation (mm) between the planned and executed access centers, obtained by superimposing pre- and post-operative STL meshes in Medit Design software. Intra-operator reliability was assessed according to COSMIN standards (ICC 3,1 , standard error of measurement [SEM], minimal detectable change at 95% confidence [MDC95], and Bland–Altman analysis). The mean linear deviation was 0.260 ± 0.221 mm (95% CI 0.150–0.369 mm; median 0.249 mm). Bland–Altman analysis revealed a bias of 0.004 mm and narrow limits of agreement (− 0.024 to 0.032 mm). Intra-operator reliability was excellent (ICC 3,1 = 0.998; SEM = 0.0101 mm; MDC95 = 0.028 mm). Among the included samples, 88.9% showed a deviation ≤ 0.5 mm, all remained below the 0.7 mm inclusion threshold by definition. The deviation was statistically greater than zero (Wilcoxon signed-rank, p < 0.001), but a sensitivity analysis excluding the two largest observations confirmed the robustness of the findings. Under controlled laboratory conditions, static guided endodontic access demonstrated high accuracy, with deviations predominantly within clinically accepted limits. The proposed fully digital, vector-based workflow proved to be a precise and highly reproducible alternative to tomographic-based measurement methods for assessing procedural accuracy in experimental endodontic research.

Article.Title: A novel, multifunctional pyrrolopyrimidine-modified chitosan hydrogel for potential applications with enhanced electrical characteristics and antimicrobial activity
Article.Authors: El-Gwaad A.; Zidan T.; Karam E.; Mwafy E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A novel pyrrolopyrimidine-modified chitosan hydrogel ( 3 ) is synthesized and charcterized. Pyrrolopyrimidine compound ( 2 ) is firstly synthesized and then it is used to chemically modify chitosan through the formation of imine linkage. The synthesized compounds are characteized by Fourier transforms infra red spectroscopy (FTIR), proton and carbon nuclear magnetic resonance ( 1 HNMR and 13 CNMR), and Field emission scanning electron microscope (FESEM). The prepared hydrogel undergoes multifunctional studies including electrical properties and antimicrobial activity. This research examines the dielectric and alternating-current conductivity characteristics of the pyrrolopyrimidine-modified chitosan hydrogel across different frequencies and temperatures, compared with the pure chitosan sample. Dielectric and AC conductivity properties of pyrrolopyrimidine-modified chitosan hydrogel are systematically investigated across a frequency range and temperatures from 20–90 °C, benchmarked against pure chitosan networks. Pure chitosan exhibits high low-frequency dielectric loss and permittivity due to pronounced Maxwell–Wagner–Sillars interfacial polarization from mobile ions and trapped charges along polar groups, alongside frequency-dependent AC conductivity governed by ion hopping. Pyrrolopyrimidine modification significantly suppresses dielectric loss while preserving permittivity, introduces a characteristic conductivity minimum at intermediate frequencies indicating restricted long-range ion migration, and yields a thermally stable response with reduced dissipative pathways. These enhancements stem from heteroaromatic cross-linking, π–π interactions, and constrained segmental mobility, which limit charge accumulation and leakage. The tailored dielectric and conduction behavior positions pyrrolopyrimidine-chitosan hydrogels as promising materials for electroactive devices, sensors, and energy storage systems requiring balanced polarization and minimal losses. The synthesized compounds are investigated for their antimicrobial activity. They are examined against two gram-positive bacteria ( Bacillus cereus 33,018 and Bacillus subtilis 6633), two gram-negative bacteria ( Pseudomonas aeruginosa 9027 and Salmonella typhimurium 14,028), and two yeast-like fungi ( Candida albicans 10,231 and Candida tropicalis 750). The antimicrobial activity of the target compounds ( 1–3 ) is compared with Amoxicillin for bacteria and clotrimazole for yeast and fungi. The minimum inhibitory concentration for the prepared compounds is detected. The results show that the pyrrolopyrimidine compound ( 2 ) has high activity towards both bacterial and fungal strains. The antimicrobial activity of pure chitosan shows low activity. By modification of citosan by pyrropyrimidine compound, the activity increases towards bacterial strains but no activity towards fungal strains. Based on the results, the synthesized pyrrolopyrimidine derivatives and the modified chitosan hydrogel exhibit useful characteristics for biomedical applications, including potential use as antimicrobial wound-care and drug-delivery materials. Furthermore, the results obtained for the dielectric and AC conductivity properties of the modified hydrogel indicate its potential for use in selected sensing, bioelectronic, and electroactive systems where control of dielectric characteristics, minimal dielectric loss, and antimicrobial properties are required.

Article.Title: Study on the mechanical properties and resistance to wetting–drying cycles of red clay stabilized by enzyme-induced carbonate precipitation (EICP)
Article.Authors: Xu X.; Chen Z.; Wei J.; Chen C.; Wu S.; Guo X.
Article.Abstract: In view of the problem of strong water sensitivity and susceptibility to dry and wet alternating damage of red clay, this study proposes to use plant-source enzyme-induced carbonate precipitation (EICP) technology for eco-friendly stabilization. Through a series of tests such as ratio optimization, triaxial shear and dry and wet cycle, the mechanical properties and durability of cured red clay were quantitatively evaluated, and its microphysical curing mechanism was revealed in combination with SEM and EDS tests. The results showed that the maximum catalytic activity of soybean urease was achieved at pH 8.0 and an incubation temperature of 55 °C. When the optimal ratio of 60 g/L urease and 1.0 mol/L cementation solution was used, the calcium carbonate content produced was the highest, and the improvement of unconfined compressive strength (UCS) was the most significant. These two parameters exhibited a strong positive correlation. The mechanical property test results show that EICP treatment significantly improved the compression modulus of the stabilized soil. The shear damage pattern of the treated soil showed typical strain hardening characteristics, and the effective cohesion increased from 18.12 kPa for the untreated soil to 43.14 kPa for the stabilized soil. The evaluation of the durability of the dry and wet cycle shows that after 20 cycles, the surface crack ratio of the stabilized specimens was only 5.2%, and the total mass loss is less than 5%, showing excellent volume stability and anti-collapse ability. SEM and EDS analysis show that the micro-nanometer calcium carbonate crystals induced by biochemical reactions effectively fill the capillary seepage channel inside the soil and build a strong bonding network between the scattered clay particles. Based on detailed indoor test data, this study fundamentally clarifies the intrinsic mechanism of EICP technology to effectively enhance the mechanics and durability of red clay.

Article.Title: Land cover change and vegetation trends in South Darfur Sudan using dynamic world
Article.Authors: Ahmed A.; Adam A.; Mohammed M.; Czimber K.
Article.Abstract: Land use and land cover change (LULCC) in semi-arid regions provides important insights into environmental dynamics under climate variability and socio-political disturbance. This study investigated the spatiotemporal dynamics of land cover, vegetation greenness, and climate variability in Buram Locality, South Darfur, Sudan, using Dynamic World land-cover data (10 m; 2016–2025), Sentinel-2 Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), Landsat-derived Land Surface Temperature (LST), and long-term meteorological observations (1980–2025). Trend analysis was performed using the Mann–Kendall test and Sen’s slope estimator within Google Earth Engine and R. Tree cover increased from 12.95% in 2016 to 18.03% in 2025, while shrub–grass–scrub vegetation and bare ground declined, with bare ground decreasing from 4.55 to 1.96%. Cropland fluctuated, increasing until 2020 before declining in 2025. Annual NDVI showed a significant increasing trend (Sen’s slope = 0.002 year⁻ 1 , p = 0.032), with the strongest increase occurring during the dry season (0.005 year⁻ 1 , p = 0.004), whereas rainy-season NDVI remained stable. Long-term rainfall increased significantly (3.92 mm year⁻ 1 , p < 0.01), accompanied by a significant warming trend (0.01 °C year⁻ 1 , p = 0.01). Pearson correlation analysis showed the largest observed association between dry-season NDVI and dry-season LST (r = − 0.581, p = 0.079), but none of the examined NDVI–climate correlations was statistically significant at p < 0.05. These findings indicate increasing vegetation greenness and changes in mapped land cover during 2016–2025 alongside long-term climatic changes. However, the observed patterns cannot be attributed to specific climatic or socio-economic drivers based on the available data. The study demonstrates the value of integrating high-resolution Earth observation data with long-term climate records to monitor environmental change in data-scarce and conflict-affected semi-arid regions.

Increasing MCP or MgP concentrations from 0.5 to 1.5 w/v% led to a non-linear variation in fiber diameter, with the average fiber diameter initially increasing and then decreasing. The results reveal that incorporation of MCP and MgP modulates the physicochemical properties and biomineralization behavior of electrospun PVA nanofibers.
