Article.Title: Effects of lyophilized common buckwheat sprouts on cardiometabolic, hepatic and oxidative-stress biomarkers in male Wistar rats
Article.Authors: Chłopicka J.; Francik S.; Potok H.; Brzychczyk B.; Berkoz M.; Krośniak M.; Francik R.
Article.Abstract: High-fat dietary exposure can alter cardiometabolic and redox homeostasis. This exploratory study evaluated the effects of lyophilised common buckwheat sprouts on plasma lipid-related measures, liver parameters, redox markers and paraoxonase-1 (PON1) activity in adult male Wistar rats. Rats were randomly allocated to four dietary groups for five weeks: control, lard, buckwheat sprouts and lard plus buckwheat sprouts (six animals allocated per group). The individual rat was the experimental unit for body-weight and biochemical outcomes, whereas the cage was the experimental unit for food- and water-intake outcomes (two cages per group). After false-discovery-rate adjustment, the most robust signals included diet-dependent changes in PON1 activity, lower oxidative-damage markers with sprouts, changes in glutathione-related measures, and increased gravimetrically measured liver lipid content with both dietary factors. The findings indicate diet-dependent changes in selected biochemical and oxidative-stress biomarkers associated with cardiometabolic risk, but they do not demonstrate vascular protection, prevention of atherosclerotic lesions or a defined molecular mechanism.

Article.Title: AI chatbots showed higher response accuracy than dentists, medical doctors, and the general public on radiation safety questions
Article.Authors: karslıoğlu H.; Çetin F.; Altun H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Radiation is encountered in daily life through natural and artificial sources as well as in medical diagnostic and therapeutic applications, and its exposure may lead to adverse health effects. This study aimed to assess radiation-related knowledge among dentists, medical doctors, and the general public and to compare their response accuracy with that of AI-based chatbot systems. A 25-item multiple-choice questionnaire assessing radiation risks and radiation safety was administered to 344 individuals, including dentists, medical doctors, and members of the general public. The same questions were entered into seven selected AI-based chatbot systems (Claude, DeepSeek, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini, Perplexity AI, ChatGPT-5, and ChatGPT-4o). The response accuracy of the chatbots was compared with that of the human participants. In addition, the consistency of their performance across different users and time periods was comparatively analyzed. AI-based systems generally demonstrated higher accuracy rates compared to human participants. Accuracy rates ranged from 80 to 90.67% among AI-based systems, compared with 32–60% among human participants. Among the evaluated chatbot systems, Microsoft Copilot achieved the highest performance, while Perplexity AI exhibited the lowest. Among the human groups, dentists and medical doctors performed significantly better than the general public, with no significant difference between the two healthcare professional groups. Performance remained stable across morning, midday, and evening assessments for most AI systems; however, ChatGPT-5 showed a significant temporal difference ( p < 0.001). AI-based systems achieved higher response accuracy than human participants under the evaluation conditions used in this study. The overall performance of the human participant groups indicates room for improvement in radiation safety education. While AI-based tools may serve as valuable educational resources, their performance should not be interpreted as evidence of superior clinical judgment or decision-making ability.
Article.Topic: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

Article.Title: Retinal layer thickness prediction from smartphone fundus imaging for early glaucoma detection
Article.Authors: Prashanth R.; Rajan C.; Geetha K.
Article.Abstract: Glaucoma progression leads to the loss of ganglion cells, which results in the thinning of retinal layers. Retinal layer thickness is a biomarker for monitoring glaucoma progression. Glaucoma is detected using the thickness of OCT images based on the RNFL layer and fundus images based on optic nerve damage. Continuous glaucoma monitoring requires both screening methods for effective treatment. However, OCT devices are high-cost, non-portable, require specialized operators, and are susceptible to artifacts and media opacities, which reduce their suitability for routine, large-scale screening, particularly in resource-limited settings. To address this clinical accessibility gap, an MPIML framework is proposed. The framework uses the Glauco Twin dataset, which consists of both fundus and OCT image data features. From the dataset, RNFL layer thickness is predicted from fundus image data features. This method of prediction avoids frequent OCT screening. In this proposed study, a smartphone-based 2D fundus image is used for measuring RNFL thickness. As the current cohort comprises 23 patients, this work is presented as a pilot feasibility study intended to demonstrate technical and clinical feasibility rather than population-level clinical validity. In this study, a multimodal physics-informed machine learning (MPIML) framework is proposed for the measurement of retinal layer thickness. The framework uses (I) the Glauco Twin dataset, which consists of segmented OCT and smartphone-based fundus image features such as structural, vascular, and biomechanical features for the same glaucoma patient's left and right eye. The MPIML framework consists of Segmentation-Modified TransUNet, which segments OCT images with 2-layer boundary segmentation of RNFL and ILM. A Modified SegFormer algorithm segments the optic disc, optic cup, blood vessels, and macula region for estimating indirect RNFL measurements. Finally, the MPIML model is used to classify glaucoma progression as normal, suspect, and glaucoma. The MPIML framework achieves a classification accuracy of about 94.3%, an AUC of 0.95, and RNFL thickness prediction is done for 3.1–3.4 µm length. In this pilot feasibility study, smartphone-based fundus image data with the MPIML model effectively predicts RNFL thickness and improves the detection of early-stage glaucoma progression, motivating a larger, multicenter validation study.

Article.Title: Three-dimensional finite element simulation study on abnormal magnetic positioning signals inside perforated casing
Article.Authors: Zhao Y.; Qi X.; Wang B.; Ji Q.; Wang S.; Fu J.
Article.Abstract: Perforating operations induce changes in the physical state of well casings, and the resultant abnormal magnetic positioning signals severely interfere with downhole casing coupling identification and depth positioning. To address this issue, based on the principle of electromagnetic induction, this study constructed a three-dimensional numerical model incorporating casing couplings, perforation holes, perforation burrs and casing deformation using the COMSOL Multiphysics finite element method. Combined with field measurement data from 24-arm caliper imaging, the interference mechanisms and quantitative relationships of various influencing factors on magnetic positioning signals were systematically analyzed. The results show that the signal at an ideal casing coupling position presents a stable “single-peak double-valley” pattern. Within the model parameter ranges defined in this study (perforation diameter ≤ 20 mm, burr height ≤ 2.5 mm), the amplitude of signal disturbance induced by perforation holes and burrs is on the order of 10 − 5 V, approximately two orders of magnitude lower than that of the casing coupling signal (10 − 3 V), and thus its impact on coupling identification and depth positioning is negligible. However, the applicability of this conclusion is constrained by perforation diameter scale and perforation density. In contrast, casing deformation disrupts the uniformity of magnetic field distribution and acts as the key interference source leading to depth misjudgment. Its signal disturbance amplitude can reach the order of 10 − 3 V, and there is a highly linear positive correlation between deformation magnitude and anomaly intensity (R 2 = 0.9808).Field measurement data further verify that the magnetic positioning signal disturbances caused by perforation holes and burrs are characterized by low-amplitude irregular fluctuations, consistent with simulation predictions. The signal anomalies induced by casing deformation are comparable in magnitude to the casing coupling signal. This conclusion is mainly based on numerical simulation and is indirectly supported by field data from partial well sections. This study provides a theoretical basis and discrimination criteria for the interpretation of post-perforation magnetic positioning signals and the evaluation of casing integrity.

Article.Title: Statistical-Plausibility Oracles for Quantum Key-Recovery: A Corpus-Driven Complexity Analysis
Article.Authors: Santo A.; Lanziani G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The efficiency of a Grover-based quantum key-recovery attack is governed not only by the size of the key space, but by the fraction of keys the oracle accepts as plausible. For ciphers whose keys are judged by statistical plausibility, that fraction reflects how strongly the language constrains admissible character sequences and, as we show empirically, how long the intercepted ciphertext is. We study this through a corpus-driven experiment on the monoalphabetic substitution cipher, using character trigram language models trained on four Renaissance Italian texts. The oracle threshold is defined as a scalar fraction of the best observed decryption score ( $$S_{\max }/\tau$$ ), producing a threshold that scales naturally with cipher length. Over a 21-letter alphabet we estimate the plausible key fraction across combinations of cipher length and stringency parameter, and derive Grover oracle costs analytically. Full Grover statevector simulation over completely enumerated key spaces at two reduced alphabet sizes confirms that the oracle’s acceptance density varies with cipher length, driven by the interplay between score-distribution concentration and the best-observed-score anchor $$S_{\max }$$ , and that the Boyer iteration formula provides a reliable near-optimal stopping criterion throughout. Parallel QUBO annealing experiments under the same scoring function exhibit a contrasting failure pattern under alphabet compression, establishing the two attack paradigms as probes of complementary landscape properties. An analytical projection across alphabet sizes shows that Grover oracle call counts grow far more slowly than the key space, roughly three orders of magnitude against the sixteen-order growth in the key space cardinality, so that the quantum speedup over classical random search increases with alphabet size, reaching thousands times at the full 21-letter scale.

Article.Title: Comparative laboratory and field assessment of commercial and nanoformulated metaldehyde baits against Monacha obstructa
Article.Authors: Emara E.; Khalifa R.; Ayoob F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Metaldehyde is a widely used molluscicide for controlling land snails; however, reformulation of commercial molluscicides using nanoscale delivery systems may provide an alternative approach for modifying their biological performance. This study aimed to prepare and characterize a nanoformulation of the commercial metaldehyde bait and compare its molluscicidal performance with Gastrotox 5% against Monacha obstructa under laboratory and field conditions. Laboratory toxicity was evaluated using the toxic bait method at five concentrations (1, 2, 5, 8, and 10%) for 72 h. Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP) and Acid Phosphatase (ACP) activities were determined as biochemical indicators of physiological responses, and field performance was assessed based on population reduction percentages over a 21-day experimental period. The prepared nanoformulation exhibited favorable physicochemical characteristics, with spherical particles measuring 7.4–33.5 nm, a mean particle size of 44.06 ± 4.57 nm, a Polydispersity Index (PDI) of 0.40, and a zeta potential of − 27 ± 3.24 mV. The nanoformulation showed a lower numerical LC 50 value than Gastrotox 5% (1.60% and 2.80%, respectively); however, the overlap of the corresponding 95% confidence limits did not support a statistically significant difference between the two formulations. ALP activity differed significantly among treatments, with the highest activity recorded in the Gastrotox-treated group, whereas ACP activity showed no significant differences. Under field conditions, the nanoformulation showed higher population reduction than Gastrotox 5% at all assessment times, with values of (48.55 ± 6.33%), (90.39 ± 2.95%), and (96.90 ± 3.26%) after 7, 14, and 21 days, respectively, compared with (37.14 ± 12.10%), (74.14 ± 2.30%), and (83.73 ± 11.51%) for Gastrotox 5%, respectively. The difference between the two treatments was statistically significant only after 14 days ( P ≤ 0.05). The prepared nanoformulation showed molluscicidal activity comparable to Gastrotox 5% under laboratory conditions, with a numerically lower LC 50 that was not statistically different from that of the commercial formulation. Under field conditions, the nanoformulation produced numerically higher population reduction than Gastrotox 5%, with a statistically significant advantage observed after 14 days. The differential ALP response, together with the unchanged ACP activity, indicated different biochemical responses to the two formulations. Overall, the findings indicate that the prepared nanoformulation has potential as an alternative formulation of commercial metaldehyde bait for the management of M. obstructa under the evaluated experimental conditions.

Article.Title: Association of salivary function with oral health-related quality of life in patients with type 2 diabetes and xerostomia: cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Judesly S.; Krithika C.; Ganesan A.; Aniyan K.; Murugan A.
Article.Abstract: Xerostomia and alterations in salivary function are frequently reported in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and may be associated with oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL). This study evaluated the associations of xerostomia and salivary parameters with OHRQoL in adults with xerostomia and T2DM. This cross-sectional study included 60 adults with T2DM, HbA1c > 6%, and mild or moderate subjective xerostomia according to CTCAE v3.0. Xerostomia severity was subsequently assessed using the Xerostomia Inventory (XI). Unstimulated whole salivary flow (UWS), stimulated whole salivary Materials and Methodsflow (SWS), salivary pH, total protein concentration, and taste perception were assessed after enrolment. OHRQoL was assessed using OHIP-14. Associations were examined using Spearman rank correlation and multiple linear regression. HIP-14 was strongly inversely correlated with UWS (ρ = −0.874, p < 0.001), SWS (ρ = −0.857, p < 0.001), and total salivary protein (ρ = −0.721, p < 0.001), whereas XI, salivary pH, and composite taste score were not significantly correlated with OHIP-14. In the six-variable regression model, UWS (β = −0.490, p < 0.001) and SWS (β = −0.385, p < 0.001) remained significantly associated with OHIP-14. The model explained 85.4% of the variance (adjusted R² = 0.838).Lower UWS and SWS were associated with poorer OHRQoL after accounting for the other variables included in the multivariable model. These findings indicate an association between reduced salivary flow and poorer oral health-related quality of life among adults with T2DM and xerostomia; causality cannot be inferred from the cross-sectional design.

Article.Title: The impact of artificial intelligence on corporate innovation
Article.Authors: Bao X.; Wu D.
Article.Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a key driver of technological progress and industrial transformation, yet empirical evidence on how AI promotes corporate innovation remains limited. Using online job posting data of Chinese listed companies from 2014 to 2024, this study constructs a firm-level measure of artificial intelligence and examines its impact on corporate innovation. The results show that artificial intelligence significantly promotes corporate innovation. Further analyses indicate that artificial intelligence enhances corporate innovation by increasing R&D investment and enriching firms’ knowledge diversity, thereby facilitating knowledge creation and knowledge recombination. The positive effect is more pronounced among non-state-owned enterprises and firms operating in non-high-tech industries. Grounded in the knowledge-based view, this study demonstrates how artificial intelligence expands firms’ knowledge bases and promotes knowledge creation and recombination, thereby extending the knowledge-based view of corporate innovation and providing new firm-level evidence on the innovation effects of artificial intelligence.

Article.Title: Integrated single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing analysis reveals paraptosis-related biomarkers and immune microenvironment regulation in triple-negative breast cancer
Article.Authors: Song Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is the most aggressive subtype of breast cancer with limited targeted therapeutic options and poor prognosis. Paraptosis, a non-apoptotic programmed cell death modality characterized by endoplasmic reticulum dilation and mitochondrial swelling, plays a critical role in tumor suppression and chemosensitivity. However, the molecular mechanism of paraptosis-related genes (PRGs) in TNBC progression and immune microenvironment remodeling remains poorly defined. As a pivotal calcium release channel on ER, ITPR3 is speculated to participate in endoplasmic reticulum stress and paraptosis execution, but its diagnostic value and regulatory role in TNBC have not been systematically elucidated. Two TNBC datasets were downloaded from the GEO database. PRGs were intersected with TNBC differentially expressed genes, and six hub genes were screened using random forest, SVM-RFE and multivariate logistic regression. ROC curve, nomogram, calibration curve and decision curve analysis were applied to evaluate the diagnostic value of hub genes. Furthermore, external validation in the independent TCGA-TNBC cohort was performed to further verify the robustness and diagnostic efficacy of this six-gene diagnostic model. Consensus clustering was used to classify TNBC into subtypes, followed by immune infiltration and inflammatory cytokine correlation analysis. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was performed to identify key modules and perform Gene Ontology (GO) / Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analysis. Single-cell transcriptomics was used to explore the cell-type-specific expression patterns of ITPR3 . We used the TIMER and HPA databases to verify the mRNA and protein expression levels of ITPR3 across pan-cancers and breast tissues. Finally, qRT-PCR, CCK-8 and EdU assays were conducted to verify the expression and biological function of ITPR3 in TNBC cells. A total of 13 differentially expressed PRGs were identified, and six hub genes including ITPR3 , CASP3 , CCR4 , CDKN3 , LPAR1 and MYLK were finally screened. The six hub genes and the combined diagnostic model exhibited satisfactory diagnostic performance. TNBC was divided into two distinct subtypes with significant differences in clinical features, immune cell infiltration and inflammatory cytokine levels. WGCNA identified two core modules closely correlated with subtypes, which were enriched in cell cycle, DNA replication, p53 signaling pathway and platinum drug resistance. Single-cell analysis confirmed that ITPR3 was highly expressed in tumor epithelial cells. In vitro experiments confirmed that ITPR3 was highly expressed in TNBC cell lines, and knockdown of ITPR3 markedly inhibited cell proliferation. This study reveals the expression characteristics and immune regulatory roles of hub PRGs in TNBC. The constructed diagnostic model has good predictive value, and TNBC subtypes present obvious heterogeneity in clinical and immune landscapes. ITPR3 is upregulated in TNBC and can promote tumor cell proliferation, which may serve as a candidate diagnostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target for TNBC.

Article.Title: Genetic components and heterotic performance of yellow maize hybrids for morphological and yield traits
Article.Authors: Ali A.; Khan S.; Khalili A.; Ali N.; Ali S.; Hussain I.; Qayyum A.
Article.Abstract: Information regarding combining ability of the inbred lines is crucial for success in hybrid breeding of maize. The current study was designed to assess general combining ability (GCA) and specific combining ability (SCA) effects, and heterotic effects for morphological and yield related traits of yellow maize. Ten inbred lines and three testers were used to produce 30 F 1 crosses by using line × tester matting pattern. The resulting hybrids along with 02 checks were evaluated by using Randomized Complete Block Design (RCBD) with 03 replications at Cereal Crop Research Institute, Pirsabaq Nowshehra, Pakistan during Kharif 2022. Significant differences ( P < 0.05) were observed among the parents and crosses for all the studied traits suggesting that further selection is possible. GCA and SCA estimates of the parental lines and crosses were significant ( P < 0.05) for all the studied traits of yellow maize except ear diameter. The inbred lines YL-1, YL-2 and YL-8 RC were found to have desirable and negative GCA values towards earliness. The parental lines YL-1, YL-2 and YL-6 were observed to have desirable and significant positive GCA values for ear length, 100-grain weight and grain yield, indicating favorable additive genetic effects for these traits. Among the F 1 crosses, the cross combinations YL-2 × YD-4 (8629.5 kg ha -1 ), YL-6 × YD-4 (7617.5 kg ha -1 ), and YL-1 × YL-07 RC (7602.8 kg ha -1 ) were the high yielding hybrids having positive and significant SCA effects for grain yield. Among these crosses, YL-02 × YD-04 showed positive and significant economic heterosis (15.1%) and commercial heterosis (3.30%) for grain yield, highlighting its potential for further evaluation. Assessment of combining ability variances revealed a predominance of SCA variance over GCA variance for most traits, while Baker’s ratio values below unity indicated a greater contribution of non-additive genetic effects to the expression of the traits studied.

Article.Title: Development of a concise objective biometric triage model for identifying myopia defined by cycloplegic refraction in school-aged children
Article.Authors: Wang Z.; Hu X.; Sun B.; Wan X.; Li Y.; Wei R.; Chang F.
Article.Abstract: To develop a concise objective biometric triage model using non-cycloplegic ocular biometric parameters to identify school-aged children likely to have myopia defined by cycloplegic spherical equivalent (SE ≤ − 0.50 D). In this study, 2,851 children aged 6–10 years from Wuchang and Jiang’an Districts of Wuhan, China, were included. To avoid inter-eye correlation, only right-eye data were analyzed. Myopia was defined as cycloplegic SE ≤ − 0.50 D. Three objective non-cycloplegic predictors, age, sex, and axial length-to-corneal radius ratio (AL/CR), were entered into a logistic regression model. The dataset was randomly divided into training and validation sets at an 8:2 ratio. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration curve, decision curve analysis, and reclassification statistics. The combined model (age, sex, AL/CR) demonstrated high discriminative performance (AUC = 0.941, 95% CI: 0.921–0.960), significantly outperforming both the AL/CR-only model (AUC = 0.935) and the demographic baseline model (AUC = 0.655) (DeLong test, P < 0.001). At the default threshold, the model exhibited high specificity (97.99%) and precision (88.16%) but limited sensitivity (54.03%). Calibration was acceptable (Brier score = 0.102), and decision curve analysis indicated potential net benefit. The optimal AL/CR cutoff of 3.02 from the univariable analysis is presented merely as an unadjusted descriptive reference, as the combined model provides individualized risk estimation across all subgroups. A concise model based on age, sex, and AL/CR showed good discrimination for identifying myopia defined by cycloplegic refraction. However, because the model showed limited sensitivity at the default operating threshold, it should be considered an adjunctive biometric triage tool rather than a stand-alone replacement for established screening methods or confirmatory cycloplegic refraction. Further studies with direct comparison against non-cycloplegic autorefraction and UDVA-based screening strategies are warranted.

Article.Title: Association of neighborhood social vulnerability with cigarette dependence and abstinence in patients with cancer who smoke
Article.Authors: Thippana N.; Robinson J.; Karam-Hage M.; Beneventi D.; Minnix J.; Cinciripini P.; Blalock J.; Cui Y.; Kypriotakis G.
Article.Abstract: Tobacco use after cancer diagnosis is associated with reduced survival poorer treatment response, and higher recurrence risk. While individual-level predictors of abstinence are well documented, less is known about the role of neighborhood disadvantage in shaping abstinence outcomes among patients with cancer. We analyzed 4913 patients with cancer who smoked and enrolled in the MD Anderson Tobacco Research and Treatment Program between 2006 and 2021. Residential addresses were geocoded to census tracts and linked to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry Social Vulnerability Index (SVI). The primary outcome was self-reported 7-day point-prevalence smoking abstinence at 3 months under an intention-to-treat definition, and the secondary outcome was baseline nicotine dependence, assessed with the Fagerström Test for Cigarette Dependence (FTCD). Multivariable logistic and linear regression models adjusted for demographic, clinical, and socioeconomic covariates were used to estimate associations between SVI and outcomes. The overall 3-month intention-to-treat abstinence rate was 40.7%; rates were 43.8%, 40.8%, 39.2%, and 38.6% across SVI quartiles from lowest to highest vulnerability. In adjusted models, higher overall SVI was associated with lower odds of abstinence (full 0-to-1 scale OR = 0.76, 95% CI = 0.61 to 0.95, p = .018; per 0.10 increase OR = 0.97, 95% CI = 0.95 to 1.00). Housing/transportation vulnerability showed the strongest domain association with abstinence (OR = 0.74, 95% CI = 0.60 to 0.90, p = .003). Higher overall SVI was associated with greater FTCD scores (beta = 0.55, 95% CI = 0.29 to 0.82, p < .001), with a stepwise increase across SVI quartiles. Even among patients receiving comprehensive evidence-based tobacco treatment, higher neighborhood social vulnerability was associated with lower abstinence and greater baseline nicotine dependence. These findings support prospective evaluation of SVI-informed assessment and evidence-based treatment intensification to reduce disparities in tobacco treatment outcomes for patients with cancer.

Article.Title: Reference intervals for neutrophil reactive oxygen species production capacity in Japanese adults
Article.Authors: Takeuchi K.; Hattori N.; Akita K.; Hatano Y.; Makise R.; Inoguchi C.; Sugiho A.; Shinke T.; Yoshida H.; Kazumura K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Innate immunity provides the first line of defense against pathogens; however, quantitative benchmarks for assessing its function remain limited. We developed optical sensing systems that enable real-time measurement of neutrophil reactive oxygen species (ROS) production by simply diluting 3 µL of whole blood into a reaction mixture. Here, we estimated reference intervals for innate immune responses of circulating neutrophils in healthy Japanese adults, primarily those in their 40s–60s, using these optical platforms. Neutrophil superoxide production and hypochlorous acid production (myeloperoxidase activity) were measured simultaneously following chemical stimulation. Data were obtained from 329 rigorously screened individuals selected from 7,263 participants (predominantly Japanese) who underwent comprehensive health examinations between February 2020 and March 2025. Reference intervals were calculated for six neutrophil activity indices, including total ROS production, ROS production per unit neutrophils, balance between the two ROS species, and neutrophil responsiveness to stimulation. Two corresponding hypochlorous acid-related indices obtained using simplified optical systems were also evaluated. Although the existence of sex-based differences in neutrophil activity indices remains unclear, sex-specific reference intervals were calculated for indices showing statistically significant sex differences and the observed differences are discussed from the perspective of future research. We further examined relationships among the indices, and their associations with age and conventional inflammatory markers. These findings provide an assay-specific quantitative framework for assessing innate immune function and may support future studies on subclinical immune variation. The gap between the current laboratory-based assay and broader clinical application, as well as future challenges, are also discussed.

Article.Title: ABCC2 rs2273697, rs717620, rs3740066 polymorphisms and antiseizure medication resistance: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Daškevičiūtė A.; Zaboras E.; Navalinskas J.; Mameniškienė R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Genetic variations in the ABCC2 gene have been proposed to influence resistance to antiseizure medications, but published findings to date are inconsistent. We aimed to systematically review and meta-analyze the association of three ABCC2 polymorphisms, rs2273697 (c.1249G >A, p.Val417Ile), rs717620 (c.-24C>T, 5′ UTR), and rs3740066 (c.3972C>T, p.Lys1324=), with antiseizure medication (ASM) resistance and to evaluate the statistical power, effect sizes, and required sample sizes. Searches covered PubMed, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, and NCBI dbSNP publication records (from inception to May 2026). The review followed PRISMA guidelines, and study quality was assessed using the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale (NOS). Statistical power and effect sizes (Cohen’s w) were estimated using G*Power 3.1, and random-effects meta-analyses were performed for all polymorphisms. Twenty studies (2627 ASM-resistant and 2639 ASM-responsive patients) met the inclusion criteria. Rs717620 was significantly associated with ASM resistance under the allelic (OR 1.25, 95% CI 1.06–1.48), dominant (OR = 1.25, 95% CI 1.01–1.54), recessive (OR 1.63, 95% CI 1.13–2.37), and homozygous (OR 1.79, 95% CI 1.17–2.74) genetic models, with low-to-moderate heterogeneity and no evidence of small-study bias. The pooled estimates for rs2273697 and rs3740066 were null across the genetic models. Most included studies were underpowered. Estimated median sample-size increases of 348%, 322%, and 289% were required for rs2273697, rs3740066, and rs717620 studies, respectively, to achieve 80% statistical power. The rs717620 (c.-24C>T, 5′ UTR) polymorphism showed the most consistent association with antiseizure medication resistance across genetic models. Given the limited statistical power of many existing studies, future research should focus on large consortium-based cohorts to improve statistical power and incorporate haplotype analysis.

Article.Title: Language-based assessments for experienced well-being: accuracy and external validity across behaviors, traits, and states
Article.Authors: Nilsson A.; Boyd R.; Ganesan A.; Kjell O.; Mahwish S.; Huang H.; Rosenthal R.; Ungar L.; Schwartz H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract While language is central to human communication, psychological science has relied on self-reported rating scales for decades because it was difficult to quantify language effectively. Large language models (LLMs) have changed that in recent years. Here, we used LLMs with machine learning to compare traditional ratings against language-based responses (short essays and descriptive words) of experienced well-being over 12 weeks from 764 individuals from an overburdened population highly exposed to emotional experience, U.S. hospitality workers. While accuracies were comparable by internal criterion (across 9 affective traits; words r = .53 vs. .51 for ratings), both language formats doubled the ratings’ accuracy (up to r = .18 and .24 for words and essays, respectively) across 24 external criteria: traits, demographics, and behavior. Beyond improved accuracy, language responses offered psychological insights: words provided concise emotional nuances, whereas essays encompassed broad life contexts. Though each language-based format differed in strengths and weaknesses, both demonstrated greater information-richness than traditional rating scales.

Article.Title: Isoliquiritigenin inhibits TGF-β1-induced epithelial–mesenchymal transition in pulmonary fibrosis by promoting Nix-mediated mitophagy
Article.Authors: Ke S.; Liu T.; Hu Q.; Jiang S.; Ma H.; Chen P.; Ke S.
Article.Abstract: Nix-mediated mitophagy has been implicated in the regulation of pathological processes in cardiac and cerebral diseases; however, its role in pulmonary fibrosis (PF) remains insufficiently understood. Epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT), a key contributor to PF pathogenesis, is closely associated with autophagy and mitophagy. Isoliquiritigenin (ISL), the major active component of licorice, has been reported to exert anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and anti-EMT effects. However, whether the effects of ISL on EMT involve mitophagy regulation remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between Nix-related mitophagy and EMT and to elucidate the mechanism by which ISL regulates EMT through Nix signaling. Our results showed that ISL inhibited cell migration and modulated the levels of E-cadherin, N-cadherin, and fibronectin. ISL also significantly promoted Nix-induced mitophagy by upregulating Nix, Beclin1, and LC3 expression, downregulating p62 expression, and increasing mitophagy-positive fluorescent puncta. In addition, ISL alleviated mitochondrial dysfunction in A549 cells by improving mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP), reducing reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, and maintaining adenosine triphosphate (ATP) levels. The anti-EMT effects of ISL were further enhanced by Nix overexpression, which further upregulated Nix, Beclin1, and E-cadherin expression and downregulated N-cadherin and fibronectin expression. These findings suggest that ISL inhibits TGF-β1-induced EMT in PF by upregulating Nix-mediated mitophagy and support its potential as a candidate therapeutic agent for PF.

Article.Title: Intelligent P-cycle provisioning in elastic optical networks via energy-aware deep reinforcement learning
Article.Authors: Dave R.; Thankachan D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To accurately assess the service accessibility of networks using preset cycles (p-cycles), we construct a theoretical model in this research. Compared to earlier work, our model is able to predict service availability more accurately by taking into account the dependency across protection domains as well as all instances where a lightpath is accessible. We next provide an approach for dynamic elastic optical networks (EONs) that is directed toward service availability throughout the configuration cycle, based on the results of the availability study. In elastic optical networks, a hybrid strategy combining deep reinforcement learning (DRL) and an improved genetic algorithm (IGA) is introduced to mitigate spectrum fragmentation and excessive resource redundancy associated with traditional pre-configured cycle (P-cycle) protection. The DRL agent learns to identify optimal base cycles, while the IGA refines their combination to achieve efficient, network-wide protection coverage. To further reduce spectrum fragmentation, a link-based spectrum partitioning approach integrated with P-cycle configuration is proposed, enabling better organization of spectral resources. Additionally, a routing mechanism is designed to select working paths either by prioritizing minimal traffic load or by applying a first-fit strategy, considering both spectrum utilization and path length to enhance overall efficiency. The results of the simulation demonstrate that the suggested DRL may enhance spectrum resource use while decreasing the likelihood of bandwidth blockage. Two benchmark-cycle design techniques that utilize the protection effectiveness of -cycles are compared with the suggested approach in the simulations. The proposed method can effectively enhance service accessibility in EONs with near minimal alteration to blocking probability as indicated in the simulation outcomes.

Article.Title: A conformable-inspired two-parameter regularized Hermite curve family for airfoil geometry modeling
Article.Authors: Altay Suroğlu G.; Das B.; Akyol S.; Bektaş M.
Article.Abstract: We introduce a local two-parameter cubic Hermite-type interpolation family motivated by the conformable identity \(T_\alpha f(t)=t^{1-\alpha }f'(t)\) and the power-law change of variable \(s=t^\alpha \) . For differentiable functions, the conformable operator is local and, up to the factor \(\alpha \) , corresponds to an ordinary derivative with respect to s ; therefore, the proposed construction is not interpreted as a nonlocal fractional model. The parameters \(\alpha \in (0,1]\) and \(\varepsilon >0\) act, respectively, as a power-law tangent-scaling parameter and a displaced endpoint-constraint/asymmetry parameter. The construction yields explicit basis functions that interpolate the endpoint control points, preserve affine invariance, and satisfy a regularized conformable tangent-matching condition under the reparametrization \(s=t^\alpha \) . The displaced tangent constraint imposed at \(t=\varepsilon \) , however, does not generally guarantee classical \(C^1\) or geometric \(G^1\) continuity at the actual knot. Accordingly, knotwise continuity is assessed through diagnostics based on jumps in the classical derivative, tangent angle, and curvature. The limiting behavior is characterized by distinguishing fixed-parameter and coupled limits. Classical cubic Hermite recovery is obtained under the coupled condition \((1-\alpha (\varepsilon ))\log (1/\varepsilon )\rightarrow 0\) as \(\varepsilon \rightarrow 0^+\) . In contrast, for fixed \(0<\alpha <1\) , the initial tangent basis diverges as \(\varepsilon \rightarrow 0^+\) unless the associated tangent datum is suitably renormalized; the corresponding coefficient system also becomes ill-conditioned in this regime. Thus, an unconditional recovery of the classical Hermite structure as \(\varepsilon \rightarrow 0^+\) is not claimed. The regularization-induced loss of symmetry is quantified and interpreted as a bias-type shape effect. Moreover, for fixed admissible parameters, a uniform first-order consistency estimate is established, including the first mesh interval, without asserting an unqualified \(h^{2\alpha }\) convergence rate. Based on this theoretical formulation, we develop a comprehensive computational framework to evaluate the proposed model in airfoil geometry reconstruction. Although the conformable Hermite formulation introduces additional local shape flexibility, experimental observations indicate that it does not consistently outperform classical Hermite interpolation when used without parameter tuning. To exploit this flexibility effectively, the proposed interpolation family is coupled with the Improved Starfish Optimization Algorithm (ISFOA), which adaptively identifies suitable values of \((\alpha ,\varepsilon )\) for each airfoil geometry. The proposed framework is evaluated on 11 different airfoil profiles and assessed through both an initial comparison with Cubic Spline, Classical Hermite, and B’ezier interpolation and an extended equal-control-point-budget comparison including shape-parameter Hermite, TCB/Kochanek–Bartels, rational cubic Hermite, trigonometric Hermite, cubic B-spline, CST, PARSEC, and Natural Cubic Spline constructions. In the initial restricted comparison, the optimization-assisted conformable Hermite framework achieves lower reconstruction errors than Cubic Spline, Classical Hermite, and B’ezier interpolation under the adopted experimental protocol. In particular, it attains an average RMSE of 0.270314, compared with 0.420562 for Cubic Spline, 0.421578 for Bézier interpolation, and 0.423351 for Classical Hermite interpolation. However, the broader equal-budget comparison shows that several established shape-representation methods achieve substantially lower reconstruction errors, indicating that the proposed framework should not be interpreted as universally superior in reconstruction accuracy. In addition, the proposed framework retains the local controllability of classical Hermite interpolation while providing an efficient shape representation with fewer control points. Quantitative knotwise diagnostics confirm that classical \(C^1\) and geometric \(G^1\) continuity are not universally guaranteed, while conditioning analysis shows that the optimized parameter pairs remain in moderately conditioned regions of the investigated parameter domain. Complementary symmetric Hausdorff and Chamfer distances are additionally used to quantify worst-case and average bidirectional geometric discrepancies without requiring one-to-one point correspondence. A controlled mesh-refinement experiment further yields an observed convergence order approaching unity, consistent with the theoretically established first-order consistency. The numerical results are interpreted as a characterization of the capabilities and limitations of adaptive parameter identification within the proposed local shape family, rather than as evidence of universal reconstruction superiority, nonlocal fractional effects, or aerodynamic equivalence. The ISFOA stage therefore serves exclusively as a parameter-selection mechanism, whereas the primary scientific contribution is the formulation and theoretical analysis of the regularized conformable Hermite-type interpolation family.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: cubic Hermite interpolation; affine invariance; conformable fractional derivative; shape bias; G1 continuity

Article.Title: Identification of a shared PAX5-mediated B-cell regulatory axis in inflammatory bowel disease and rheumatoid arthritis
Article.Authors: Zheng J.; He J.; Tian J.; Liu J.; Zhai Z.; Li Y.; Zhang H.; Bian Y.
Article.Abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory disease characterized by intestinal inflammation. Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) can occur concurrently with IBD as a comorbidity. However, the common dysregulated node underlying both IBD and RA remains largely unexplored. We screened differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in IBD and RA datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus. Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analyses were performed for functional enrichment. Hub genes were identified by constructing a protein–protein interaction (PPI) network. We further identified transcription factors regulating the hub genes and validated the expression of the hub genes and the corresponding transcription factors in additional IBD and RA datasets. Finally, the transcription factor PAX5 was validated in IBD and RA tissues using multiplex immunohistochemistry (mIHC). A total of 54 common DEGs were shared between IBD and RA. GO analysis indicated that these genes were significantly enriched in immune response activation. KEGG analysis suggested that these genes may be involved in cytokine–cytokine receptor interaction. PPI network analysis identified 10 hub genes. Among the transcription factors regulating these hub genes, PAX5 was found to regulate CD19 and CD79A. PAX5 was identified as a prioritized candidate shared regulatory node linking IBD and RA. These findings were further supported by mIHC. Our integrated analysis identified PAX5 as a prioritized candidate linking IBD and RA through B-cell-associated pathways, suggesting its potential as a biomarker and therapeutic target that warrants further investigation.

Article.Title: Apatite fission track reveals uplift-denudation processes of granitoid mountains in East China: a case study of Mount Tianzhushan
Article.Authors: Ye Z.; Guo F.; Pang J.; Xin L.; Yuan W.
Article.Abstract: Mesozoic granitoid mountains are widely exposed across East China, and their uplift and denudation evolution remain a key challenging scientific issue in the tectonic geomorphology of orogenic belts. Low-temperature thermochronology serves as a powerful tool to quantitatively constrain such geological processes. This approach is adopted in this study to investigate the uplift-denudation history of Mount Tianzhushan. As a UNESCO Global Geopark in southern Anhui Province, China, Mount Tianzhushan is renowned for its eroded granitoid landforms. In this study, the regional uplift and denudation history has been reconstructed for the first time by using the fission track dating (FTD) method. The apatite fission track (AFT) central ages fall into the Paleogene period of the Cenozoic, ranging from 55 to 31 Ma. The positive correlation between AFT ages and sample elevations indicates a pattern of regional integral uplift. Thermal history modeling reveals that its cooling history can be generally divided into three stages: 95–65 Ma, 65–25 Ma, and 25 Ma to the present, characterized by slow cooling, rapid cooling, and moderate cooling, respectively. The average regional cooling rate is calculated at 1.86°C/Ma. The mountain uplift rates vary from 0.041 mm/a to 0.073 mm/a, and the estimated uplift amounts fall into three intervals: 3760–3500 m, 3301–3148 m, and 2840–2620 m, displaying a considerable spatial variability in uplift magnitudes across Mount Tianzhushan. Higher terrain experienced more intense uplift. Regionally, the average uplift rate of Mount Tianzhushan is 0.053 mm/a, with an average denudation rate of 0.034 mm/a, yielding a rate difference of 0.019 mm/a. The average uplift amount relative to eustatic sea level is 3195 m, while its total denudation reaches 2346 m. The 849 m discrepancy is exactly consistent with the modern average elevation of Mount Tianzhushan. FTD provides a solid framework for further research on similar granitoid landform evolution in East China.

Article.Title: Hypertension prevalence and risk factors in a retained high-risk cohort of rural Black adults: a five-year follow-up study in Limpopo Province, South Africa
Article.Authors: Ntimana C.; Mashaba R.; Mathopo K.; Seakamela K.; Tlouyamma J.; Choma S.; Maimela E.
Article.Abstract: Hypertension remains a significant public health concern in South Africa, particularly in rural areas where healthcare access is limited. This study aimed to longitudinally assess hypertension prevalence and associated risk factors among a retained cohort of rural Black adults in Limpopo Province. Prospective longitudinal cohort study of 518 participants followed from baseline (2014–2016) to follow-up (2019–2022). Data were analyzed using SPSS version 27.0, with binary logistic regression to determine factors associated with hypertension. Among the retained cohort ( n = 518), baseline hypertension prevalence was 43.8%, increasing to 46.9% at follow-up. Hypertensive participants were significantly older and more likely to be female. Adjusted analyses showed age ≥ 64 years (baseline aOR = 3.05; 95% CI:1.23–7.56; follow-up aOR = 2.72; 95% CI:1.43–5.18), central obesity (baseline aOR = 2.92; 95% CI:1.72–4.96; follow-up aOR = 2.60; 95% CI:1.69–3.99), and diabetes (baseline aOR = 2.92; 95% CI:1.38–6.17; follow-up aOR = 2.75; 95% CI:1.70–4.44) were consistently associated with hypertension. Notably, significant attrition bias was observed: baseline hypertension prevalence among retained participants was more than double that of those lost to follow-up (43.8% vs. 19.7%; p < 0.001), and retained participants had higher rates of obesity and diabetes but lower rates of kidney disease. In this selectively retained high-risk cohort, hypertension prevalence increased over five years, with age, central obesity, and diabetes as consistent risk factors. Due to substantial attrition bias, these findings should be interpreted as reflecting trends within a high-risk survivor sub-cohort rather than population-level prevalence estimates. The strong associations observed support targeted screening and intervention strategies for older adults, women, and individuals with obesity or diabetes in rural South African communities.

Article.Title: Stochastic multi-objective optimal placement and sizing of distributed generation in multi-microgrid systems using enhanced modified spider wasp optimization
Article.Authors: Mavuri S.; Reddy C.; Kumar D.; Alanazi A.; ELrashidi A.
Article.Abstract: The incorporation of Distributed Generation (DG) units into Multi-Microgrid (MMG) systems has significantly enhanced the operational flexibility, reliability and economic efficiency of modern smart grids. The nonlinear, constrained and stochastic nature of the optimization problem, in addition to the multi-objective nature, makes the determination of the optimum location and size of a DG unit a challenging task. In this paper, Enhanced Modified Spider Wasp Optimization (EMSWO) algorithm is proposed for the stochastic placement and sizing of DGs in interconnected MMGs. In order to promote population diversity, fasten convergence speed, avoid premature convergence and meet the network operation constraints, chaotic population initialization, adaptive exploration–exploitation strategy, elite preservation, repair-based constraint handling mechanism are proposed for the proposed EMSWO. The proposed stochastic planning framework aims at minimizing the Total Present Worth (TPW) and Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) while simultaneously meeting power balance, voltage deviation, DG penetration, and generation capacity constraints. Using Monte Carlo simulation, uncertainties in load demand, renewable generation and electricity prices are captured, and a scenario reduction technique is used to maintain the statistical properties in a lower dimensional space with less computational effort. The proposed EMSWO is tested on a benchmark MMG system for different operating scenarios. The simulation results show that the obtained TPW is reduced from 434.25 million USD to 404.52 million USD and LCOE is reduced to 0.174 USD/kWh which is better than the conventional Spider Wasp Optimization (SWO), Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO), Cyclonic Convergent Particle Swarm Optimization (CCPSO) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). In addition, the convergence and statistical results validate that the proposed EMSWO results in faster convergence, more stable solutions, better voltage profile and lower operating cost, which proves its effectiveness as a solid optimization framework for stochastic DG planning in interconnected MMG networks.

Article.Title: Computational prioritization of fungal-derived H1 receptor ligand candidates for allergy-related research
Article.Authors: Rahman M.; Rijvy M.; Biswas M.; Tabassum M.; Shimu S.; Rahad M.; Haque M.
Article.Abstract: Activation of the G-protein-coupled histamine H1 receptor (H1R) contributes to allergic responses such as bronchoconstriction, vasodilation, and pruritus. This study aimed to computationally prioritize novel fungal-derived compounds for H1R-targeted investigation based on predicted binding characteristics, pharmacokinetic and toxicity profiles, and BBB permeability. A comprehensive workflow incorporating SP and XP molecular docking, ADMET, SAR, DFT, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, MM/GBSA, and Dynamic Cross-Correlation Matrix (DCCM) analyses was employed. A total of 13,381 fungal-derived natural products from the NPAtlas database were screened using acrivastine as the control. The top ten docking-ranked compounds were further evaluated by ADMET analysis, leading to the prioritization of CID:145,975,830 and CID:145,976,597, which showed docking scores of − 13.654 and − 13.997 kcal/mol, respectively, compared with − 9.071 kcal/mol for the control. Post-docking and post-simulation MM/GBSA analyses provided complementary binding free-energy estimates for the prioritized complexes. PASS prediction associated the leads with anti-eczematic, antipruritic, and vasoprotective activities, while DFT analysis revealed broadly comparable electronic profiles. The 100 ns MD simulations showed differences in dynamic behavior and residue-level interaction persistence, while DCCM analysis indicated differences in correlated residue motions. Overall, CID:145,975,830 exhibited the most consistent computational profile and was prioritized as a candidate for further H1R investigation. Experimental validation is required to establish H1R binding, antagonistic activity, and therapeutic potential.

Article.Title: Modified BRICS sequential regimen in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma patients with BCLC C stage: a real-world study
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Wang J.; Peng Y.; Chen J.
Article.Abstract: Patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) have limited treatment options and poor prognosis. This study evaluates the efficacy and safety of a modified BRICS (Bifidobacterium-based probiotics, Radiotherapy, Immunotherapy, and anti-angiogenic therapy with a Stereotactic approach) sequential regimen in a real-world setting. In this retrospective study, 22 patients with advanced HCC (BCLC stage C) received the modified BRICS regimen, which included stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) to a single lesion, high-dose probiotics, anti-PD-1 immunotherapy, and anti-angiogenic agents. Efficacy endpoints included objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS). Safety was assessed per NCI-CTCAE v4.0. The ORR was 59.1% (95% CI: 36.4–79.3%), and DCR was 100%. Median PFS and OS were 9.5 months (95% CI: 7.78–11.22) and 22.4 months (95% CI: 8.24–36.57), respectively. Patients with <2 metastatic organs had significantly better outcomes (median PFS: 10.5 vs. 3.8 months; median OS: 26.4 vs. 5.2 months). Grade 3–4 adverse events occurred in only 4.5% of patients, with no treatment-related deaths. The modified BRICS regimen demonstrated promising efficacy and favorable safety in advanced HCC, particularly in patients with limited metastatic burden. These findings support further investigation of multimodal sequential therapy in larger prospective studies.

Article.Title: Characterization of a fixed reinforcement learning policy for aerial robot with suspended payload under variable flight conditions
Article.Authors: Karasahin A.; Wu Z.; Kocer B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Flights with suspended payloads are particularly challenging because of their coupled dynamics, which lead to instability and increased sensitivity to disturbances. Although reinforcement learning (RL) has successfully achieved controller performance, the generalization and robustness of a single policy remain significant areas of investigation. In this study, we characterized the performance and robustness of a single RL policy for an aerial robot with different trajectory profiles, including a smooth, feasible lemniscate curve and a sharp-turning, infeasible pentagram, under varying velocity references (0.5 m s $$^{-1}$$ and 1.0 m s $$^{-1}$$ ) and crosswind disturbances (1.0 m s $$^{-1}$$ ). We trained a single RL policy using proximal policy optimization with collective thrust and body-rate control using a high-fidelity physics simulator based on the SimpleFlight framework. Real-world experimental results on the Crazyflie 2.1 platform show that the single RL policy successfully generalizes to different trajectory profiles and velocity references and maintains stability under a crosswind disturbance of up to 1.0 m s $$^{-1}$$ which is a substantial challenge for this small class platform and even smaller payload underneath, where such aerodynamic forces are significant compared to the available control authority and system mass. Furthermore, the single RL policy was systematically evaluated using the mean Euclidean distance error, cable length transitions, and swing angle distributions. Although the single RL policy maintained a robust control performance, the experimental results indicated performance degradation at higher velocities owing to increased dynamic challenges such as nonlinear aerodynamic drag and actuator saturation. This study provides a detailed performance characterization that highlights the generalization capability of a single-payload-aware RL policy in real-world applications and the limitations arising from the hybrid dynamics of the system.

Article.Title: Caputo fractional-order differential equations for tuberculosis transmission and relapse dynamics with empirical validation
Article.Authors: Jiru M.; Kumaravel S.; Dharmalingam M.; Sangeetha T.; Behabtu D.
Article.Abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) mortality has declined by only 23% since 2015, far below the WHO End TB Strategy target. Classical integer-order models, rooted in Markovian assumptions, do not adequately capture the memory-driven nature of TB transmission, in which progression depends on cumulative infection history. We formulate Caputo fractional-order differential equations for TB transmission in a SELIT framework with two-stage latency, direct relapse from the treated to the infectious class, and waning immunity, where the fractional order α quantifies epidemiological memory. We establish positivity and boundedness of solutions, derive the basic reproduction number \(\:{R}_{0}\) via the next-generation matrix, and prove global asymptotic stability of the equilibrium using Lyapunov and Volterra-type functionals. Sensitivity and bifurcation analyses show that relapse rates above a critical threshold induce backward bifurcation with bistability for \(\:{R}_{0}<\) 1, so that \(\:{R}_{0}<\:\) 1 is necessary but not sufficient for elimination. The model is calibrated and validated with Ethiopian surveillance data (2005–2020), yielding α = 0.914 (95% CI: 0.882–0.941) and \(\:{R}_{0}\) = 1.67. The fractional model reduces validation error by 54.7% relative to its integer-order analogue (ΔAIC = 22.4), and thereby provides empirical evidence of memory in TB transmission and a rigorous basis for elimination planning.

Article.Title: Compound microbial fermentation of tofu whey wastewater enhances nutrient composition and growth performance in swine
Article.Authors: Shen X.; Xu Y.; Yin L.; Yin D.; Yang E.; Zhao R.; Dai Y.; Wang J.; Liu Y.; Hu X.; Hou H.; Zhou X.; Pan X.
Article.Abstract: Tofu whey wastewater (TWW) is nutrient-rich but commonly discarded in China, causing environmental pollution. Here, TWW fermented with Cyberlindnera jadinii , Lactobacillus plantarum , and Enterococcus faecalis (CMFTWW) was compared with naturally fermented TWW (NFTWW). CMFTWW showed lower pH, higher genistein and lactic acid, greater viable bacterial counts, enriched Lactobacillus and Streptococcus , and reduced Acetobacter . In weaned piglets, 15% CMFTWW improved weight gain and feed intake, reduced feed conversion ratio and diarrhea, elevated serum glucose, albumin, triglycerides, calcium, iron, and IgA, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and attenuated oxidative stress. Both CMFTWW and florfenicol enriched Clostridium_sensu_stricto_1 and Sutterella relative to controls, whereas CMFTWW further elevated Alloprevotella , Blautia and Terrisporobacter . In fattening pigs, CMFTWW increased weight gain and reduced feed conversion ratio, reduced diarrhea incidence and improved economic efficiency. This study provides preliminary evidence that compound microbial fermentation improves TWW quality and that CMFTWW can serve as a feed additive in healthy swine production.

Article.Title: Development and open-source release of a multi-cancer module for structuring pathology reports
Article.Authors: Park P.; Choi Y.; Park S.; Han J.; Kim J.; Ryu B.; Shin D.; Cho K.; Yoo C.; Choi K.; Kim H.
Article.Abstract: Pathology reports contain clinically critical information; however, their semi-structured or free-text format substantially limits secondary use in large-scale cancer research. Scalable, reproducible methods are therefore needed to transform these reports into structured datasets across institutions. This study aimed to develop, externally validate, and publicly release a scalable NLP (Natural Language Processing) framework for structuring multi-cancer pathology report and supporting reproducible, institutionally transferable research workflows. We developed a Clinical BERT-based NLP framework for the automated extraction of structured variables from pathology reports across five cancer types. The pipeline integrated data preprocessing, annotation, model training using a question-answering approach, and a public release of the trained models. The trained models were applied to independent datasets from two external institutions without retraining, enabling direct assessment of cross-institutional. In the internal validation, the model demonstrated consistently strong performance across cancer types, with mean F1 scores ranging from 0.945 to 0.977 and median F1 scores exceeding 0.99. In external validation, performance declined substantially across institutions, with mean F1 scores declining to 0.623 and 0.427 for breast cancer and similar reductions observed in kidney, thyroid, liver, and colorectal cancers (ΔF1 ranging from − 0.209 to − 0.518). Despite this decline, the model maintained clinically meaningful, moderate performance across external datasets. We developed and validated a scalable and reusable NLP framework for multi-cancer pathology report across institutional settings. By publicly releasing trained models and processing pipelines, this study advances reproducible, deployable NLP infrastructure for clinical data integration and multicenter cancer research.

Article.Title: The 3’UTR protects bone against menopause-induced osteoporosis via regulating CHD9 expression
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Huang S.; Guo Z.; Guo X.; Shen T.; Shang H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Osteoporosis is characterized by low bone mass, increased bone fragility, and elevated fracture susceptibility, with approximately one-third of postmenopausal women affected by this disease. Estrogen deficiency induces aberrant upregulation of microRNA (miRNA) expression, and the 3’-untranslated region (3’UTR) of mRNAs can bind to and sequester target miRNAs. This study aimed to identify target genes capable of sequestering and inhibiting miRNAs in postmenopausal osteoporosis (PMOP). Candidate differentially expressed microRNAs were screened by analyzing sequencing data from the whole blood and serum of PMOP patients. These candidate microRNAs were validated in the serum of PMOP patients, the serum and bone tissue of ovariectomized (OVX) mice, as well as in mouse osteoblasts and osteoclasts. Luciferase reporter assays were performed to verify the binding sites between the candidate microRNAs and their predicted target genes; argonaute 2 RNA immunoprecipitation (AGO2-RIP) assays were carried out to detect ceRNA binding at the cellular level, and in vivo therapeutic animal experiments were also implemented. We screened and cross-validated miR-144-5p and miR-532-5p, which were found to be highly expressed in the serum of PMOP patients, the serum and bone tissue of OVX mice, and mouse osteoblasts. The common target gene of these two miRNAs is chromodomain helicase DNA-binding protein 9 ( CHD9 ). Luciferase reporter assays confirmed that the p233-239 and p721-727 regions within the CHD9 3’UTR are the specific binding sites for miR-144-5p and miR-532-5p, respectively. In osteoblasts, CHD9 positively regulates the expression of runt-related transcription factor 2 ( RUNX2 ) by binding to the − 450 to -400 region of the RUNX2 promoter. In vivo experiments further demonstrated that the CHD9 3’UTR ameliorates ovariectomy-induced osteoporotic phenotypes. This study demonstrates that the CHD9 3’UTR offers a potential therapeutic strategy for postmenopausal osteoporosis.

Article.Title: Pressure-relief mechanism and strata-pressure response of surface L-shaped well hydraulic fracturing for thick hard roofs in deep extra-thick coal seams
Article.Authors: Zhang C.; Du P.; Yu S.; Li J.; Huang Y.; Ren J.
Article.Abstract: Rockburst hazards in deep extra-thick coal seams with thick hard roofs are closely related to high in situ stress, strong strata control, and energy accumulation in overlying key strata. This study investigates the pressure-relief mechanism and strata-pressure response of staged hydraulic fracturing through surface L-shaped horizontal wells, taking the 40,307 working face of Xiaozhuang Coal Mine as an engineering case. A comprehensive approach integrating in situ stress testing, key-stratum mechanical analysis, UDEC numerical simulation, microseismic monitoring, and strata-pressure observation was adopted to reveal the structural weakening mechanism of thick hard key strata and evaluate the effectiveness of hydraulic fracturing. The results show that the deep mining area is dominated by high horizontal stress, which promotes the formation of large-span suspended roofs and increases the potential for stress concentration and energy accumulation. Mechanical analysis indicates that surface L-shaped well hydraulic fracturing can weaken the integrity and continuous bearing capacity of thick hard key strata, promoting the transition from large-span integral failure to short-span segmented failure. Numerical results demonstrate that fracturing expands the overburden stress-relief range and reduces the periodic weighting interval from 59 to 82 m to 21–40 m. Field monitoring confirms that the four surface L-shaped horizontal wells generated continuous fracture networks in the target sandstone layer, and the average periodic weighting interval after fracturing decreased to 26.85 m. The integrated analysis indicates that surface L-shaped well hydraulic fracturing changes the roof failure behaviour from delayed concentrated failure to progressive failure and energy release, thereby achieving regional pressure relief and rockburst control. This study provides an effective approach for rockburst prevention in deep coal mines with high stress and thick hard roof conditions.

Article.Title: Mechanisms and measurement of attention in laboratory tasks versus naturalistic learning contexts
Article.Authors: Chang F.; Mao X.; Khalil M.; Rapport M.; Dillon A.; Loo S.; Grammer J.; Lenartowicz A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Translation of laboratory-derived metrics to quantify learning in naturalistic settings is an important goal in neuroscience. In the current study we tested if a common neural metric of visual attention, alpha-range (8–12 Hz) oscillations, generalizes from laboratory to naturalistic learning. We recorded electroencephalography (EEG) in eighty 6–10-year-old children while they participated in naturalistic learning activities and during a laboratory spatial working memory task ( n = 51 final sample). We found that alpha power during the activities did not correlate with event-related alpha power modulations (ERMs) during stimulus processing in the laboratory task, a common indicator of visual attention. By contrast, multiple control analyses showed the expected relationships among baseline activity, task-related modulation and behavioral performance. These results suggest that alpha ERMs during task processing reflect different neural processes of visual attention than alpha power during learning activities – potentially reflecting additional contributions from arousal, motivation or motor activity in naturalistic environments. These findings suggest that laboratory-derived neural metrics of visual attention may not directly generalize to naturalistic learning, highlighting the need to consider multiple contributing processes when translating laboratory-derived neural metrics to naturalistic learning.

Article.Title: Process effect prediction method based on visual generative models
Article.Authors: Zhao J.; Yang H.; Sui Y.; Wang P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study aims to develop a conditional visual generation model that maps process-structure relationships, generating scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images of metallographic microstructures under specified conditions based on input process parameters for process improvement reference. The Omni-loss is used to optimize the conditional discriminator/generator. A MAE-CGAN model was proposed to demonstrate the fidelity of generated microstructures and their correlation with applied processing methods. The model integrating visual transformer and Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (CGAN) offers several advantages: the CGAN framework theoretically supports modeling any material system; trained generators can produce specific microstructure images under designated process conditions. And the prediction datasets are evaluated using quantitative indicators proposed in previous work. The results showed that the pre-trained Masked Auto-Encoder (MAE) model demonstrated robust critical structural feature extraction capabilities with the relatively small image dataset. The quantitative analysis of existing samples yielded results consistent with the expert evaluations, and the generated samples hold great potential for guiding future experimental settings.

Article.Title: An integrated fuzzy–fractal geochemical index for gold exploration targeting in the Saqqez mineralization belt, Iran
Article.Authors: Mahdiyanfar H.; Seyedrahimi-Niaraq M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In complex geochemical environments, separating anomalies from background values remains a major challenge. This study proposes an innovative integrative framework combining concentration-number (C–N) fractal modeling and fuzzy c-means (FCM) clustering to improve gold geochemical anomaly mapping in the Saqqez mineralization area, Sanandaj–Sirjan Zone. While fractal modeling is used for data-driven anomaly identification and background suppression, FCM clustering identifies multielement patterns related to mineralization. The main novelty of this research is the development of the Integrated Fractal–FCM Anomaly Index (IFFAI). This continuous, dimensionless index integrates standardized fractal-based anomaly intensity and FCM membership degrees, enabling the simultaneous quantification of anomaly strength and classification confidence. The results demonstrate that while standalone fractal modeling and FCM clustering fail to fully delineate all mineralized zones, the integrated IFFAI approach successfully identifies all known gold mineralization zones in the Saqqez region with a coherent and continuous pattern. Furthermore, by combining fractal anomaly classes with FCM-derived mineralization affinity factors, geochemical samples were systematically prioritized, showing strong spatial correlation with active exploration targets. Compared to standalone methods, the proposed framework provides significant improvements in spatial resolution, anomaly continuity, and background noise reduction. Overall, this method serves as an effective decision-support tool for geochemical anomaly mapping and exploration target prioritization.

Article.Title: Engineered three-phase interfaces in porous electrodes for efficient in-situ H2O2 generation and synchronous removal of co-contaminants
Article.Authors: Li L.; Zhang X.; Shi Y.; Yang Z.; Chen P.; Hu H.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: The co-existence of toxic hexavalent chromium [Cr(VI)] and synthetic organic dyes in dyeing effluents is a prevalent issue, butthe simultaneous removal of these co-contaminants remains a great challenge. Electrocatalytic reduction of oxygen to hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) as reductant in the flow-through systems by achieving efficient generation and utilization of active sites is a promising strategy for Cr(VI) reducing detoxification. Herein, a microfluidic flow-through electro-Fenton-like system, incorporating a modified graphite felt (GF) electrode, was developed to enable the simultaneous degradation of Cr(VI) and methyl orange (MO) through in-situ H 2 O 2 generation. This synergistic removal system promoted the degradation of Cr(VI) and MO compared to those in individual contaminant systems (Cr(VI) reduction reached 99.9%, while MO removal efficiency reached 95% simultaneously at a flow rate of 2.5 mL/min、initial pH of 2 and current density 10.19 mA/cm 2 ). Simulation study indicated that the increased number of accessible active sites and its induced nanoscale convection in flow-through system accelerated the nanoscale interfacial mass transfer at PTFE-electrode-solution. Moreover, active species monitoring and the quantum chemical calculation were applied to explore the synergistic mechanism and detailed pathway on the degradation of co-existing contaminants. This work demonstrated the feasibility of simultaneously converting heavy metals and organic dyes, holding great promise for the removal of multiple contaminants in complex wastewater.

Article.Title: Temporal trends in hypersensitivity pneumonitis–coded mortality: a multinational analysis of 32 countries, 1999–2019
Article.Authors: Yoon H.
Article.Abstract: Contemporary evidence on hypersensitivity pneumonitis (HP) mortality trends remains limited. Using World Health Organization Mortality Database data (ICD-10: J67) from 32 countries, we analyzed 7,581 deaths in adults aged ≥ 20 years between 1999 and 2019. Age-standardized mortality rates (ASMRs) were calculated using the WHO World Standard Population; joinpoint regression estimated annual and average annual percent changes (APC, AAPC), and Kitagawa decomposition separated the contributions of population age structure and age-specific mortality rates. The pooled ASMR was 0.0394 per 100,000 (95% CI 0.0385–0.0403). HP-coded mortality was stable from 1999 to 2004 and rose thereafter (APC 7.34%; 95% CI 6.66–8.02), giving an AAPC of 5.43% (95% CI 4.35–6.52). HP-coded mortality was higher in men (0.0496 versus 0.0317 per 100,000), increased more steeply in women (AAPC 6.40% versus 4.45%) and rose with age to 0.2977 per 100,000 at ≥ 80 years. Among the 25 countries with ≥ 30 deaths, eight showed a significant increase and two a significant decrease. Population aging accounted for 12.2% of the increase in crude mortality among adults aged ≥ 40 years. HP-coded mortality increased across this multinational sample with substantial between-country heterogeneity, which may reflect changes in diagnostic recognition and certification practice as well as in disease occurrence.

Article.Title: Gelatinase activity is induced in renal vascular lesions of rats with malignant hypertension
Article.Authors: Hartner A.; Cordasic N.; Veelken R.; Schiffer M.; Woelfle J.; Daniel C.; Amann K.; Hilgers K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We previously reported a RNASeq analysis comparing kidney injury in malignant 2-kidney-1-clip hypertension versus the “benign” form of hypertension. RNAseq pointed to differential expression of many matrix metalloproteases (MMPs). We now investigated the regulation of MMP expression, immunohistochemistry and gelatinase activity in more detail. Mean blood pressure was elevated in benign hypertension (188 ± 10 mmHg) and even more pronounced in malign hypertension (236 ± 4 mmHg), compared to sham operated controls (128 ± 9mmHg). MMP2, 7, 12, 16 and 19 expression was significantly higher in malignant compared to non-malignant hypertension. The only exception was MMP9 mRNA which decreased by 0.2-fold. Gelatinase activity was detected in vascular lesions of malignant hypertension in kidneys exposed to high blood pressure. The number of gelatinase activity lesions correlated with MMP2 expression. There was no gelatinase activity in shams, or in left (post-stenotic) kidneys of hypertensive rats. MMP2 staining was detected at vascular lesions of malignant hypertensives. MMP9 staining was observed in tubules, interstitial cells, and intact vessels but absent from malignant vascular lesions. TIMP1 and 2 were detected in tubular cells. Thus, in malignant hypertension, most MMPs are upregulated. The gelatinases MMP2 and MMP9 exhibited a strikingly divergent regulation, with MMP2 localizing to malignant vascular lesions with gelatinase activity.

Article.Title: Inactivation of highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (H5N1) using a combination of Hatano-RCMF and naturally strongly acidic hot spring water
Article.Authors: Hatano T.
Article.Abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (H5N1) poses a serious threat to the global poultry industry, causing substantial economic losses while representing a significant challenge to public health and environmental hygiene [1,2]. The objective of this study was to develop a novel non-chemical water treatment technology by combining a unique Hatano Repulsive-Collision Magnetic Field (Hatano-RCMF), generated by opposing like-pole (N–N/S–S) permanent magnets, with naturally strongly acidic hot spring water, and to evaluate its physicochemical characteristics together with its virus- and pathogen-inactivating efficacy [S1-S4]. Physicochemical changes in the treated water before and after Hatano-RCMF exposure were investigated using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) analysis [S1,S2]. Biological evaluations were performed by assessing the inactivation of highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (H5N1) [S1], together with representative pathogenic microorganisms, including Escherichia coli O157 [S2] and Salmonella spp. [S2]. The combined treatment of Hatano-RCMF and naturally strongly acidic hot spring water induced measurable physicochemical changes in the water and demonstrated potent inactivation activity against H5N1 as well as representative pathogenic microorganisms [S1,S2]. These findings suggest that this technology represents a promising non-chemical approach for infectious disease control that may reduce dependence on conventional chemical disinfectants. The proposed system has potential applications not only in the poultry and livestock industries but also in the fields of food safety, public health, and environmental hygiene.
