Article.Title: Digital pathology approach for the classification of focal and segmental glomerulosclerosis
Article.Authors: Le Moal P.; Orieux A.; Verney C.; Esteve E.; Boffa J.; Brocheriou I.; Rigothier C.; Chauveau B.; Rabant M.; Knebelmann B.; Isnard P.; Buob D.; Galichon P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Focal and segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) refers to various diseases with different pathophysiological mechanisms and treatments. Primary FSGS (pFSGS) is dependent on immunological factors and is treated with immunosuppressants. However, the histological lesions by light microscopy are not specific and do not reflect a precise etiology. The aim of this study is to categorize FSGS biopsies into etiological groups using digital pathology combined with clinical parameters. This was a retrospective, observational, multicentre study. It involved three university hospitals in Paris and Bordeaux. A total of 58 patients with pFSGS and maladaptive FSGS (mFSGS) were included in a selected ‘ultra-phenotyped cohort’ based on kidney biopsies. Secondly, there was a ‘clinical cohort’ of 89 patients with non-selected FSGS. First, we evaluated the ability of histological morphometric parameters to discriminate pFSGS and maladaptive FSGS (mFSGS) on kidney biopsies in an ultraphenotyped cohort of normative pFSGS and mFSGS patients ( n = 58). We performed a multivariate analysis to identify variables associated with the type of FSGS, leading to the identification of the Mean Interglomerular Area (MIA) as a marker to distinguish pFSGS from mFSGS. Secondly, we evaluated the discriminative value of this parameter in a clinical cohort ( n = 89) including primary, maladaptive, and undetermined FSGS. High MIA classified mFSGS versus. pFSGS in the ultraphenotyped cohort, even after stratification by age, eGFR and proteinuria. In the clinical cohort, MIA was also significantly lower in primary FSGS. Although MIA was strongly correlated with serum albumin, a classical marker of pFSGS, they conflicted in 30% of patients. In this subset, relying solely on serum albumin frequently misclassified patients by FSGS subtype (27%), highlighting the usefulness of combining MIA with serum albumin to adjudicate FSGS subtypes. FSGS of uncertain origin segregated with either pFSGS or mFSGS cases on an MIA by albumin graph, suggesting that they do not constitute a different pathological entity. Digital pathology, in conjunction with simple biological features, is a useful tool for FSGS classification, suggesting that it might improve the design of future therapeutic and mechanistic FSGS studies.

Article.Title: Thermal-state transition pathways and spatial differentiation of permafrost in Northeast China
Article.Authors: Sun J.; Shan W.; Guo Y.; Zhang C.
Article.Abstract: The evolution of the thermal state of permafrost in Northeast China exhibits significant phase transitions and multi-path characteristics. The dominant regional direction has shifted from an earlier adjustment toward lower thermal grades to a later adjustment toward higher thermal grades, accompanied by grade persistence, gradual transitions, directional reversals, and localized spatial reorganization. This paper constructs grade sequences from PTC-2 to PTC-15 based on four periods of 30 m permafrost temperature products from 2003 to 2021, strictly within the four-period common-valid pixels. By combining the transition matrices between adjacent periods, four-period trajectory classification, 10 km area-proportion fields, and spatial error models, the study analyzes the pathways of thermal state transitions, the spatial reorganization of PTC-13, and their environmental linkages. The results indicate that from 2003–2007 to 2008–2012, pixels that maintained their level or transitioned to an adjacent lower level accounted for 57.7% and 38.9%, respectively. In the subsequent two stages, the proportions of transitions to an adjacent higher level were 52.8% and 25.3%, respectively, while transitions spanning two or more levels did not exceed 1.72%. The area of PTC–13 initially increased by 32.1%, followed by decreases of 29.3% and 20.2%, respectively. Under the 30% reference threshold, the area of its high-proportion PTC–13 area expanded from 4.208×10 4 km 2 to 1.151×10 5 km 2 , then subsequently shrank to 2.378×10 4 km 2 and 3.506×10 3 km 2 . The entry-exit decomposition indicates that the initial stage is characterized by expansion based on high retention, while the subsequent two stages transition to an exit-dominated rapid contraction. The Jaccard index decreases to 0.20 and 0.12, while turnover intensity increases to 0.67 and 0.79. The centroid direction varies with the area-proportion threshold, suggesting that changes are primarily manifested as spatial reorganization rather than stable migration. Results from trajectory partitioning, based on the magnitude and frequency of thermal state changes, indicate that the persistent, transitional, and high-dynamic thermal-trajectory zones account for 57.20%, 40.18%, and 2.62%, respectively. The association between long-term climate means and thermal state trajectory differences is stronger than that with interannual climate fluctuations. After environmental correction, the mean NDVI of different thermal trajectory zones shows no stable differences; however, the interannual variability of NDVI increases with the degree of trajectory dynamics. The research findings reveal a pattern of thermal state change within the common effective permafrost in Northeast China, characterized by phase transitions, multi-path evolution, and heterogeneous spatial reorganization. This provides a repeatable analytical framework for regional thermal state comparison and the subsequent identification of monitoring targets.

Article.Title: Comparing the pristine biochar and Zn-biochar composite for stabilizing Cd in a contaminated calcareous soil
Article.Authors: Boostani H.
Article.Abstract: The optimal pyrolysis temperature and feedstock type for producing a Zn-biochar composite tailored to Cd immobilization in calcareous soils remains unexplored. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of Zn-biochar composites derived from two agricultural residues (rice husk and wheat straw) pyrolyzed at three temperatures (300, 450, and 600 ° C) on Cd immobilization in a contaminated calcareous soil. Sequential extraction procedure, release kinetics experiment, and spectroscopic (FTIR, XRD) and microscopic (SEM) analyses were employed to identify the Zn-biochar composite most effective at reducing soil Cd availability. Zn-biochar composites outperformed pristine biochars in reducing labile fractions (soluble and exchangeable, carbonate, FeMn-oxides) while increasing the recalcitrant residual fraction across all pyrolysis temperatures. Among all treatments, Zn-rice husk biochar composite produced at 600 ° C (R60z) was the most effective. It caused the highest statistically significant increase in the Cd content of residual fraction relative to the control (28.9%) and showed the lowest mobility factor (25.08%). R60z also exhibited the greatest significant reductions compared to the control in the parameters of the simple Elovich kinetic model, corresponding to decreases of 17.8% in a e and 29.4% in 1/β. These findings identify R60z as the most effective amendment for suppressing both the initial magnitude of Cd release and the rate of Cd desorption into the soil solution. This superior performance was likely associated with the potentially greater accessibility of surface sites of the R60z, which may have enhanced the retention of Cd in less mobile soil fractions. Finally, it seems that high-temperature Zn-biochar composites derived from rice husk represent a promising amendment for mitigating Cd mobility in contaminated calcareous soils.

Article.Title: A double diamond model-based design and evaluation method for medical transfer beds
Article.Authors: Li H.; Qin L.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: This study aims to improve patient experience and healthcare professionals' operational efficiency during patient transfer by proposing an integrated design and evaluation method for medical transfer beds within the Double Diamond framework.First, initial user requirements were identified through User Journey Map (UJM) analysis and multi-stakeholder interviews to explore key challenges and potential design needs during the medical transfer process. Subsequently, the Kano model was applied to classify the attributes of user requirements, and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) was employed to determine the priority weights of critical design requirements. Based on these results, Quality Function Deployment (QFD) was adopted to establish the relationship between user requirements and product technical characteristics, thereby providing guidance for the development of innovative design solutions. Finally, an independent expert panel was invited to conduct a comparative evaluation between the proposed design and an existing medical transfer bed using the Fuzzy Comprehensive Evaluation (FCE) method.The evaluation results demonstrated that the proposed design achieved a higher overall score than the existing medical transfer bed. The integrated framework effectively transformed user requirements identified during the medical transfer process into prioritized technical characteristics and provided a systematic decision-making basis for the development of medical transfer bed concepts.

Article.Title: Direct and indirect impacts of COVID-19 vaccination in Slovenia in 2021: a retrospective modelling study
Article.Authors: Fafangel M.; Žibert J.; Fošnarič M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Country-specific estimates of vaccination impact are essential for public-health planning after the COVID-19 pandemic. Most national estimates rely on a static formula that captures direct protection only. We retrospectively quantified the direct and transmission-mediated indirect impacts of COVID-19 vaccination in Slovenia in 2021 using national surveillance data and an age-stratified extended SEIR model with vaccinated and unvaccinated compartments, age-specific mixing and observed vaccination uptake. The actual rollout reached 56% population coverage by the end of 2021 and was compared with counterfactual scenarios of no vaccination, lower and higher coverage, and vaccination restricted to people aged 65 years and older, under the assumption that nonpharmaceutical interventions and behaviour remained as observed. Compared with no vaccination, the model estimated that the actual rollout averted 35,936 hospital admissions (95% uncertainty interval [UI] 29,965–40,322), 8,137 intensive care unit admissions (7,263–9,027) and 5,248 deaths (4,170–6,356), corresponding to reductions of 71% (67–73), 73% (71–75) and 66% (61–70). Comparison with an older-adult-only strategy suggested transmission-mediated indirect protection for older adults, with 38% (19–45) fewer hospital admissions and 32% (23–38) fewer deaths under the actual rollout. These model-based, conditional estimates show what a calibrated transmission model adds to static estimates: healthcare burden, indirect protection and strategy comparisons.

Article.Title: Exposure to organochlorine pesticides via breastmilk and infant length-for-age in a cross-sectional study in the Lake Atitlán watershed, Guatemala
Article.Authors: Rodríguez Quintana S.; von Hippel F.; Orozco M.; Solomons N.; Salamova A.; Kong M.; Sans-Fuentes M.; Billheimer D.; Sneed S.; Beamer P.; Zamora A.; Rivera E.; Mora A.
Article.Abstract: Organochlorine pesticides (OCPs) are persistent and bioaccumulative, disrupt development, and are still used in some parts of the world despite local and global bans and restrictions. Guatemala has the highest prevalence of stunting (length-for-age that is two standard deviations below the median of childhood growth standards) in the Americas, affecting ~ 50% of children under five, and it has the sixth highest prevalence worldwide. This manuscript examines concentrations of OCPs and their degradation products (18 chemicals) in the breastmilk of Mayan women from the Lake Atitlán watershed in Guatemala to assess current exposures and to explore potential relationships among demographic parameters and stunting prevalence in infants. We conducted a cross-sectional study ( n = 80 mother/infant dyads, infants were 90–182 days in age) with 20 mothers/infants from each of four communities: San Juan La Laguna, San Pedro La Laguna, Panajachel, and Santiago Atitlán during June - July, 2022. We administered a survey based on the language preference of the mother with the help of a community translator to collect demographic information and assess exposure to pesticides. We measured the length of each infant to assess stunting (based on age) and plotted data on the World Health Organization (WHO) growth charts. We detected all 18 OCPs in at least one breastmilk sample and 11 were detected in at least five samples (2,4’-DDD, 4,4’-DDD, 4,4’-DDE, 4,4’-DDT, cis-heptachlor epoxide, HCB, heptachlor, pentachlorobenzene, trans-chlordane, trans-heptachlor epoxide, trans-nonachlor). Concentrations were the highest for 4,4’-DDE (mean ± SE = 60.6 ± 5 ng/g lipid weight, maximum = 313.1 ng/g lipid weight). No statistically significant associations were observed between OCP concentrations and stunting measures; however, exploratory analyses suggested an inverse trend between 4,4’-DDT concentration and stunting ( p = 0.08) that warrants future study. The detection of legacy pesticides demonstrates ongoing environmental exposure and supports further investigation of routes of exposure for the mother and potential health implications for the child. Our results also have policy implications for Guatemalan regulations and enforcement.

Article.Title: A hybrid machine-learning based security algorithm for improved detection of distributed-denial-of-services attacks in internet of things networks
Article.Authors: Baloyi C.; Mathonsi T.; Tshilongamulenzhe T.; Muchenje T.; Plessis D.
Article.Abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has emerged as a critical enabler of intelligent and autonomous systems, supporting applications across sectors such as agriculture, healthcare, education, and smart infrastructure. However, the increasing connectivity of IoT devices has significantly expanded the attack surface, making these networks particularly vulnerable to Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks. Existing detection approaches, including Decision Tree (DT), Linear Regression (LR), and K-means, are often limited by suboptimal classification accuracy, high response latency, and poor adaptability to evolving and zero-day attack patterns, thereby compromising their effectiveness in dynamic IoT environments. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Machine Learning-Based Security (MLBS) framework that integrates K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) to enhance the detection and mitigation of DDoS attacks in IoT networks. The proposed hybrid model leverages the temporal learning capability of RNNs and the instance-based classification strength of KNN to improve both detection accuracy and generalization. The framework was evaluated using the MATLAB simulation environment, where it achieved an accuracy of 98.72%, precision of 97.95%, recall of 98.94%, and an F1-score of 98.39%, outperforming conventional baseline models. Beyond performance improvements, the proposed MLBS framework demonstrates strong performance on previously unseen traffic patterns, indicating its suitability for real-time deployment. The key contribution of this work lies in providing a scalable, adaptive, and high-precision intrusion detection solution that enhances the resilience of IoT networks against both known and emerging DDoS threats.

Article.Title: Incision orientation and scar formation in the shoulder area: a prospective multicenter study
Article.Authors: Olsavszky V.; Ballo O.; Christ F.; Marquet P.; Kivelitz S.; Wachendorff A.; Reiners-Koch P.; Gauglitz G.; Bruning G.; Kunte C.; Felcht M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Optimal skin incision orientation in the shoulder remains debated: textbook guidelines recommend horizontal incisions, while the intraoperative pinch test suggests an upright orientation, and no consensus exists among tension-line concepts such as Langer’s, Kraissl’s, or more recent ones. In this prospective multicenter comparative study with partial randomization and blinded photographic assessment, we evaluated scar formation following horizontal, upright, and oblique incisions at 44 shoulder excision sites from 38 patients across three German centers (2020–2022), using the Patient and Observer Scar Assessment Scale (POSAS) at 3 and 6 weeks. For the primary endpoint, the 6-week observer-reported overall POSAS score, no significant differences were observed between orientations. In exploratory analyses, upright incisions were among the best-rated by patients and observers at 6 weeks and showed significant improvement over time in thickness, elasticity, and vascularity, while oblique incisions showed significant pigmentation improvement; horizontal incisions did not improve. Subregion analyses showed higher stiffness and thickness scores for upright incisions, and worse overall scores for oblique incisions, in the lateral versus medial subregion. As the primary endpoint was non-significant, these exploratory findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating, positioning upright incisions as a promising candidate for early scar improvement warranting confirmation in larger, adequately powered studies.

Article.Title: Development of surface modified Mg-2Gd-2Yb alloy through friction stir processing: corrosion behaviour and short-term anodic performance
Article.Authors: Balan P.; Vignesh R.; Dhanyanth P.; Hariesh S.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates the influence of friction stir processing (FSP) on the microstructural evolution, corrosion behaviour and electrochemical performance of Mg–2Gd–2Yb alloy shows potential for further evaluation in short-duration cathodic-protection applications. The as-cast base material (BM) was processed using two FSP conditions: FSP02 (2 passes, 33 mm/min, 1400 rpm) and FSP04 (4 passes, 33 mm/min, 1400 rpm). FSP significantly refined the coarse-grain structure of the BM from approximately 808 µm to 8–10 µm, producing a homogeneous and defect-minimized microstructure. FSP02 exhibited the most effective grain refinement, while FSP04 showed slight grain coarsening due to cumulative heat input during multiple passes. Transmission electron microscopy revealed improved particle dispersion and strong particle matrix interactions in the processed specimens. Corrosion behaviour was evaluated under thermo-static (− 20 to 80 °C) and thermo-cyclic conditions. The BM exhibited severe localized corrosion characterized by pitting, cracking, and unstable corrosion product layers. In contrast, FSP specimens developed more uniform corrosion morphologies owing to refined grains and enhanced elemental distribution. At elevated temperatures, corrosion mechanisms shifted from chloride-assisted attack to the formation of protective MgO/Mg(OH) 2 -rich surface layers. Rare-earth elements (Gd and Yb) promoted surface film stability and reduced chloride penetration. Corrosion performance varied according to temperature, in that BM had the minimum corrosion rate at − 20 °C, while FSP02 had the minimum corrosion rate between 0 to 40 °C and FSP04 had the minimum corrosion rate at 60 and 80 °C. However, FSP02 was found to perform better than BM in electrochemical polarization and making it a promising candidate for short-duration cathodic-protection applications.

Article.Title: Initial proton pump inhibitor choice and 6-hour heartburn severity in acute reflux exacerbation: a prospective two-centre cohort study
Article.Authors: Borazan İ.; Çalışkan H.; Çalı H.; Karaca B.; Şirin İ.
Article.Abstract: Acute exacerbations of gastro-oesophageal reflux disease commonly bring patients to emergency departments, where rapid symptom control matters more than mucosal healing, yet head-to-head data on symptom severity in the first hours after an oral dose are scarce. In this prospective two-centre cohort study, 189 adults with an acute reflux exacerbation and a Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease Questionnaire score of 8 or more received dexrabeprazole 10 mg, esomeprazole 20 mg or pantoprazole 40 mg, chosen by the treating physician before enrolment. The primary outcome was heartburn visual analogue scale (VAS) score six hours after the first dose, analysed by analysis of covariance adjusted for baseline VAS and nine covariates. The overall adjusted group effect was significant (F(2,171) = 6.32; p = 0.002). Adjusted six-hour VAS was lower with dexrabeprazole than pantoprazole (− 0.83 points, 95% confidence interval − 1.36 to − 0.30) and than esomeprazole (− 0.77, − 1.27 to − 0.27; both Holm-adjusted p = 0.007); comparators showed no detectable difference. In a post hoc exploratory analysis, adjusted probabilities of ≥ 50% heartburn reduction were 68.3%, 31.5% and 33.7%. Treatment was not randomly allocated and the analysis plan followed data collection, so these findings concern prescribing regimens rather than equipotent doses, are hypothesis-generating and require randomised confirmation.

Article.Title: Influence of eco-friendly diesel fuel additives on fuel properties, engine performance and exhaust emissions
Article.Authors: Krakowski R.; Gołębiowski W.; Zając G.
Article.Abstract: Diesel fuel used in transport, marine applications, and stationary power systems is vulnerable to storage-related degradation, especially in the presence of bio-components, which creates a need for environmentally benign additives that preserve fuel quality without compromising engine operation. This study investigates the effect of four eco-friendly diesel additives—liquid Effective Microorganisms EM(F), ceramic EM carriers EM(C), silver solution (SS), and colloidal nanosilver (CNS)—on fuel properties, engine performance, and exhaust emissions. Fuel blends were prepared at additive concentrations of 1, 2, and 5% v/v for physicochemical analyses, while engine tests were performed for selected blends at 2 and 5% using an SW 680/1 direct-injection diesel engine operating at 20 and 30 kW. The novelty of the study lies in the integrated assessment of environmentally oriented additives as potential alternatives to conventional fuel-treatment agents through combined evaluation of ignition quality, density, distillation characteristics, low-temperature behavior, corrosion tendency, fuel consumption, thermal efficiency, and exhaust emissions. The results showed that the additives did not adversely affect compliance with the evaluated EN 590 fuel-quality requirements (e.g., density, distillation, copper corrosion, cetane number, CFPP) and caused only negligible changes in density and volatility-related properties. At the same time, selected additives improved ignition quality, with the cetane number increasing from 54.73 for neat diesel to 55.83–55.97 for ceramic EM blends and to 55.70–55.83 for silver-solution blends at lower concentrations. Engine tests demonstrated reduced brake specific fuel consumption, from 421 to 408 g/kWh at 20 kW and from 366 to 358 g/kWh at 30 kW, together with an increase in brake thermal efficiency from 20.1 to 20.7% and from 23.1 to 23.7%, respectively. Simultaneously, reductions in NO x , CO, and CO 2 emissions were observed without deterioration of engine power output. These findings indicate that eco-friendly additives show potential to improve diesel-engine energetic performance while maintaining short-term fuel stability and physicochemical compatibility, which supports their further investigation for sustainable fuel management.

Article.Title: Dietary AAA/BCAA ratio and glycemic load are associated with obesity and novel anthropometric indices in Iranian adults
Article.Authors: Zeraati T.; Rivaz R.; Adibian M.; Salari S.; Khorasanchi Z.
Article.Abstract: Obesity remains a major public health issue in Iran, with adult prevalence of overweight ~ 35–38% and obesity ~ 17–22%, driven by dietary transitions toward energy-dense, low-quality foods. While macronutrient quantity has been linked to obesity, the independent role of quality and its relation to novel anthropometric indices is underexplored in Iranian populations. This cross-sectional analysis used baseline data from the first phase of the PERSIAN Organizational Cohort Study at Mashhad University of Medical Sciences. Dietary intake was assessed using a validated 130-item semi-quantitative FFQ; Macronutrient quantity was expressed as percentage of total energy. Macronutrient quality indices were calculated (GI, GL, CQI for carbohydrates, AAA/BCAA, PAR for proteins, MUFA/PUFA, SFA/PUFA, PUFA/SFA for fats). BMI, ABSI, BRI, AVI and VAI were subsequently calculated from anthropometric measurements. Associations were evaluated using crude and multivariable-adjusted logistic regression, controlling for age, sex, physical activity, socioeconomic status, and total energy intake. A higher dietary AAA/BCAA ratio was consistently associated with lower odds of obesity and high levels of BRI and AVI after multivariable adjustment. Associations of glycemic index and glycemic load with adiposity outcomes were less consistent and attenuated after adjustment. Fat-quality ratios and the PAR showed no significant associations. Among the anthropometric indices examined, associations with dietary composition were observed most consistently for BRI and AVI. In this cross-sectional analysis of Iranian adults, a higher dietary AAA/BCAA ratio was associated with lower odds of obesity and selected novel anthropometric indices. Associations of glycemic load and glycemic index were less consistent. Longitudinal studies are required to establish temporality and potential causality.

Article.Title: Simplex-centroid mixture design reveals pathogen-dependent interaction structure in a camphene–d-limonene–eucalyptol system against three phytopathogenic fungi and oomycetes
Article.Authors: Taibi M.; Elbouzidi A.; Mellal A.; Haddou M.; Baraich A.; Bellaouchi R.; Hawwal M.; Alqahtani A.; Almarfadi O.; Gharsallaoui A.; Asehraou A.; Addi M.; Guerrouj B.; Chaabane K.; Mothana R.
Article.Abstract: The increasing limitations of synthetic fungicides have intensified interest in sustainable, plant-derived alternatives. A simplex–centroid mixture design with Scheffé special-cubic modelling was used to optimize a ternary monoterpene system (camphene, d -limonene, eucalyptol) against three phytopathogenic fungi and oomycetes representing diverse infection strategies: Macrophomina phaseolina , Phytophthora infestans , and Verticillium dahliae . Twelve formulations (pure compounds, binary blends, and ternary mixtures) were assayed by broth microdilution. Individually, the three monoterpenes were weak antifungal agents (MIC 150–500 µg/mL); ternary formulations reduced MIC values markedly, to 12.5 µg/mL at two of the design points used to fit the M. phaseolina model. The fitted models were statistically significant for all three targets (R 2 = 0.8940, 0.9604 and 0.9400; R 2 adj = 0.7668, 0.9130 and 0.8680; p = 0.0023–0.0246); because the modal-MIC reporting convention yields zero pure error, lack of fit could not be tested, and the models are presented as descriptive representations of the response surface within the tested compositional region rather than as externally validated predictors. They revealed pathogen-dependent interaction structure: binary interactions dominated for M. phaseolina , a ternary interaction dominated for P. infestans , and both contributed for V. dahliae , indicating that antifungal activity is primarily driven by non-additive mixture effects, that is, significant departures from linear blending of the pure components, rather than by single-compound dominance. Desirability-based optimization identified an interior formulation (camphene 0.3643, d -limonene 0.2967, eucalyptol 0.3390) with a composite desirability of 0.998; because the individual desirabilities saturate once their targets are met, this composition lies within a broader domain of near-equivalent blends rather than being a unique optimum. At this composition the model predicted MIC values of 16 ± 45 µg/mL for M. phaseolina , 41 ± 22 µg/mL for P. infestans and 74 ± 11 µg/mL for V. dahliae (predicted value ± standard error of prediction). This composition was then prepared and assayed independently of the design runs, in three biological replicates on separate days; the experimentally determined MIC values were 15.625 µg/mL (modal) for M. phaseolina , 50 µg/mL (median of 31.25, 50 and 62.5 µg/mL) for P. infestans and 62.5 µg/mL (modal) for V. dahliae , each within one two-fold dilution step of its prediction (observed/predicted = 1.00, 1.22 and 0.85, respectively; t(6) = 0.861, p = 0.422; t(6) = 1.166, p = 0.288; t(6) = − 1.841, p = 0.115). Relative to the most active pure monoterpene assayed in parallel, the optimised blend was 16.0-fold more potent against M. phaseolina , 5.0-fold against P. infestans and 2.4-fold against V. dahliae , and the three pathogens differed in susceptibility to it (one-way ANOVA F(2,6) = 12.24, p = 0.0076). Overall, this study demonstrates that mixture-design-driven statistical optimization can identify monoterpene compositions with substantially lower in vitro MIC values than their individual components. These in vitro results provide a quantitative starting point for future greenhouse and field evaluation, phytotoxicity assessment, and formulation development, none of which is reported here.

Article.Title: Non-classical Mullins-Sekerka instability during mineralization at gas-liquid interfaces
Article.Authors: Wegner L.; Santoso R.; Chogani A.; Jennings J.; Bosbach D.; Poonoosamy J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Diffusion-driven morphological instability, described by Mullins–Sekerka theory, predicts amplification of interfacial perturbations and wavelength selection for idealized sharp interfaces. However, natural systems rarely satisfy these assumptions. Here, we investigate barite mineralization on the growing interface of CO $$_{2}$$ gas bubbles using 3D focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) tomography, quantitative surface analysis and reactive transport modelling. Bubble morphologies exhibit diffusion-driven instability, with dominant modes consistent with Mullins–Sekerka predictions. However, the interface violates key assumptions of the classical framework; it is porous, transport active, and evolves in pore space confinement, while crystallization proceeds via heterogenous nucleation, producing a polycrystalline interface. We show that diffusion-driven instability persists under these conditions but with modified mode selection, defining a non-classical Mullins–Sekerka regime for gas-liquid interface mineralization. Such dynamics influence pore structure evolution and transport pathways in the subsurface environment.

Article.Title: Design and implementation of an automated Drosophila locomotor assay using computer vision tracking
Article.Authors: Melkani D.; Harnwal N.; Desai S.; Patel D.; Melkani G.
Article.Abstract: Drosophila has long served as a powerful model for investigating locomotor behavior, using geotaxis assays to generate valuable insights into genetics, aging, and neurobiology. Nonetheless, its use has been constrained by subjective scoring, modest throughput, and challenges in reproducibility. We developed and validated an integrated hardware–software platform that enables automated, high-resolution locomotor analysis across 12 vials in parallel. The system integrates 3D-printed mechanical components, Raspberry Pi–based video acquisition, and programmable environmental controls to ensure standardized conditions. A deep learning pipeline segments vials with near-perfect accuracy (IoU > 0.95), while computer vision algorithms quantify climbing trajectories, velocity, and positional zone occupancy at 60 frames per second. The end-to-end workflow converts raw video into time-resolved metrics, supports sex-specific aggregation, and incorporates advanced statistical analyses, including Linear Mixed Effects regression, harmonic mean p-values, and Mann–Whitney U tests. Relative to manual scoring, this automated pipeline yields 2.8-fold faster processing and about 800-fold higher data density. Application of the platform uncovered reproducible phenotypes of multiple genotypes. For example, in circadian Clock out mutation, males displayed progressive climbing deficits with age, whereas females maintained age-resilient trajectories. Moreover, male Clock out exhibited a reduced locomotor performance compared to age-matched control ( w 1118 ) males; however, female Clock out showed subtle reduction in locomotor performance. Additionally, glial-specific knockdown of PolG , encoding the DNA polymerase gamma catalytic subunit, revealed striking sex-dimorphic aging patterns: females outperformed controls at older age in Glaz-driven line and at younger age in Elav-driven line, while males exhibited a marked decline. To promote broad adoption, a user-friendly Python interface (Tkinter GUI) enables accessibility independent of computational expertise. Collectively, this standardized, high-throughput framework advances the resolution of genotype-, age, and sex-dependent locomotor dynamics, offering new opportunities in aging, circadian biology, and neurodegeneration research.

Article.Title: A machine learning framework for solar cell design optimization and efficiency prediction
Article.Authors: Faizan M.; Ahmed G.; Khan M.; Ijaz S.; Namoun A.; Mehmood M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study applies machine learning (ML) to the design of tin-based perovskite solar cells (PSCs) to reduce dependence on exhaustive device simulation. Ten regression algorithms were trained on 4428 SCAPS-1D simulations covering 27 device architectures, predicting efficiency (η), open-circuit voltage (V OC ), short-circuit current density (J SC ) and fill factor (FF) from the absorber, electron and hole transport layer materials, absorber thickness, and band-edge densities of states. CatBoost performed best, reaching R 2 of 0.999990 and RMSE of 0.0126% points for η on a random 80:20 split. Accuracies of this kind are common in this literature, so we examined what they measure. The dataset is a dense sweep of a deterministic solver, so random partitioning, including ten-fold cross-validation, leaves near-identical configurations on both sides of the split. Withholding whole architectures raised the error by one to two orders of magnitude. The models are therefore reliable for interpolation within characterised architectures, not for extrapolation to unseen ones. Training on random subsets showed that 480 simulations, 10.8% of the grid, recovered the correct architecture and the optimum in all ten repeats. The best configuration, FASnI 3 with SnO 2 and Cu 2 O at 660 nm, reaches 28.87% efficiency (V OC 1.086 V, J SC 30.01 mA cm⁻², FF 88.55%).

These compounds were evaluated for cytotoxic activity, with doxorubicin as the control. Furthermore, molecular docking, density functional theory, ADME-T, and MD simulations were performed on the synthesized compounds. Compound 14 had a higher binding affinity (-10.3 kcal/mol) than doxorubicin (-7.3 kcal/mol) and other compounds. The pharmacokinetics of the newly synthesised derivatives were predicted using ADME analysis. According to the HOMO–LUMO study, compound 14 had a significant energy gap of 2.77 eV with an energy range of -8.027 eV and -5.258 eV. Simulations of the HER2 receptor (PDB ID: 5NQR) using compound 14 demonstrated stable binding, as evidenced by minimal fluctuations over 100 ns. After docking studies, compound 14 was evaluated for cytotoxicity activity against HepG-2 (IC 50 = 29.07 μg/mL), HeLa (IC 50, = 34.13 μg/mL), and MCF-7 (IC 50, = 25.40 μg/mL) cell lines. Compound 14 was moderately active in MCF-7 (IC 50, = 25.40 μg/mL) compared with other cancer cell lines. In addition to blocking cancer cell invasion, compound 14 promotes apoptosis via mitochondrial-dependent apoptosis and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. As a result of the aforementioned findings, vanillin derivatives may suggest useful as anticancer drugs in the future.

Article.Title: Decision-support modelling for liver paired exchange integrating clinical thresholds and operational feasibility
Article.Authors: Heydari M.; Li Y.; Shi V.; Tayerani Charmchi A.; Ghobadi F.
Article.Abstract: Living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) is limited by donor–recipient incompatibilities in blood type, graft-to-recipient weight ratio (GRWR), and future remnant liver volume (FRLV). Liver Paired Exchange (LPE), adapted from kidney exchange, offers a strategy to expand donor pools, but implementation remains constrained by surgical, logistical, and ethical challenges. We developed an integer linear programming (ILP) model, implemented in OPL/CPLEX, to optimise LPE under combined clinical and operational constraints. Clinical thresholds included ABO compatibility, GRWR ≥ 0.8, and FRLV ≥ 30%. Logistical feasibility was encoded through simultaneous or consecutive operating room scheduling, inter-centre travel distance ≤ 250 km, and surgical team availability. A synthetic cohort of 20 incompatible donor–recipient pairs was generated using clinically realistic parameter distributions derived from published LDLT and LPE programmes. Applying the optimisation model to this simulated dataset, we identified 6 feasible matches (30%), compared with a random allocation baseline of 12.5% (± 4.3%) under the same clinical thresholds and one-to-one assignment rules. All simulated matches complied with ABO, GRWR, and FRLV thresholds, as well as the imposed logistical feasibility filters. In this simulation study, we demonstrate that incorporating operational constraints into an optimisation framework can improve matching efficiency within a synthetic LPE pool. The work provides a transparent, replicable decision-support framework that transplant centres could adapt and prospectively evaluate. The main contributions are: (i) formalising logistical feasibility for LPE within an integer linear programming model, (ii) showing, in a simulated cohort, that optimisation can identify more clinically and logistically feasible exchanges than random allocation, and (iii) illustrating how such a tool could support, but not replace, multidisciplinary decision-making around donor safety, recipient viability, and institutional capacity.

Article.Title: Transformerless nine-level switched capacitor inverter with common-ground for grid-tied PV system
Article.Authors: Latha Devi M.; Babu M.
Article.Abstract: Transformerless multilevel inverters (MLIs) with voltage-boosting capabilities have become an attractive choice for utility grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) systems due to their compactness, high efficiency, and cost-effectiveness. However, leakage current caused by the absence of galvanic isolation remains a major concern, affecting both safety and power quality. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a single-phase nine-level (9 L) common-ground (CG) switched-capacitor (SC) inverter with a voltage gain of four. The main novelty of the proposed topology lies in integrating a CG configuration with a high-gain, self-balanced-SC structure to simultaneously achieve complete leakage current suppression, reduced component count, and low device voltage stress without compromising voltage gain. Comparative analysis with state-of-the-art 9 L topologies demonstrates that the proposed inverter offers reduced component count, low device voltage stress, high efficiency, zero leakage current, and lower implementation cost. Experimental validation using a 1.3 kW laboratory prototype under both stand-alone and grid-connected operating conditions confirms the effectiveness of the proposed topology. Owing to its compact structure and high voltage gain, the proposed topology requires a lower input DC voltage, making it particularly suitable for low-voltage PV systems.

Article.Title: Larval diet drives remodelling of the peritrophic matrix in the Australian sheep blowfly and influences vaccine efficacy
Article.Authors: Kerr E.; Briscoe S.; McNally J.; Acton G.; Driscoll D.; Schulz B.; Vuocolo T.
Article.Abstract: Flystrike, the infestation of the skin by larvae of predominately Australian Sheep Blowfly on Sheep, costs the Australian sheep industry more than $320 million annually. The peritrophic matrix (PM) is a chitin–protein barrier lining the insect midgut that is essential for digestion, protection, and host–parasite interactions. In Lucilia cuprina larvae, the PM is also a proven vaccine target, yet how diet influences its molecular composition remains unclear. Here, we used integrated proteomics, glycoproteomics, glycomics, and transcriptomics to examine diet-dependent PM structure. Larval diet strongly altered PM protein composition, particularly the abundance of peritrophins, while PM glycosylation remained highly conserved and dominated by oligomannose-type N-glycans. Transcriptomic data indicated that simplified diets induce ER-associated responses consistent with post-transcriptional regulation of PM assembly. Importantly, these compositional changes directly correlated with reduced vaccine efficacy. Together, our findings demonstrate that larval diet governs PM structure and immunogenic potential, with direct implications for vaccine antigen selection and PM production.

Article.Title: Machine learning model for predicting regional lymph node metastasis in acral melanoma
Article.Authors: Zhuang Y.; Liu D.; Deng X.; Lin J.; Wu X.
Article.Abstract: Acral melanoma (AM) is an aggressive subtype of cutaneous melanoma characterized by delayed diagnosis and poor prognosis. Accurately and non-invasively assessing regional lymph node metastasis (RLNM) remains a significant clinical challenge. This study aimed to develop an interpretable machine learning (ML) model to preoperatively predict RLNM in AM patients. Clinical, pathological and imaging data of 189 patients with histologically confirmed AM were analysed retrospectively. Patients were randomly assigned in a 7:3 ratio to a training cohort (n = 132) and an internal validation cohort (n = 57). Boruta and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression were used to screen candidate variables within the training cohort. Seven algorithms were compared by nested cross-validation performed exclusively inside the training cohort; the final algorithm was chosen by a pre-specified composite of out-of-fold discrimination and calibration. The decision threshold was fixed on the training out-of-fold predictions. The internal validation cohort was evaluated once, with the model and the threshold locked in advance. SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) analysis was used to interpret the locked model, and calibration, decision curve analysis (DCA) and DeLong tests against conventional Breslow/TNM-based models were performed on the untouched validation cohort. Five predictors were retained: Breslow thickness, lymph-node short-axis diameter, positive contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEU) finding, vascular invasion and positive positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET-CT) finding. In the training cohort, the pooled out-of-fold area under the curve (AUC) ranged from 0.850 to 0.877 across the seven algorithms. On the pre-specified composite rule, the GradientBoost model was selected and locked; it achieved a single locked AUC of 0.868 (95% CI 0.769–0.967) in the internal validation cohort, with a sensitivity of 0.889 (95% CI 0.762–1.000) and a specificity of 0.733 (95% CI 0.565–0.885). The locked model significantly outperformed the Breslow-only logistic model (AUC 0.610, DeLong p = 0.0002) and a categorical T-stage (TNM-T) logistic model (AUC 0.562, DeLong p < 0.001). Calibration was adequate (slope 1.02, intercept − 0.63, Brier score 0.156) and DCA demonstrated a positive net benefit over the conventional models across clinically relevant threshold probabilities. This study developed a machine learning-based non-invasive diagnostic model that effectively assesses the risk of regional lymph node metastasis in patients with AM. The locked gradient boosting model retained good discrimination and calibration and outperformed conventional Breslow/TNM-based models. This non-invasive model may assist in assessing the risk of RLNM in patients with AM.

Article.Title: Culture platform influences marker expression and morphology of human lung organoids
Article.Authors: Fletemeyer B.; Dichtl S.; Erckert S.; Wilflingseder D.; Posch W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The cultivation platform strongly shapes the development and phenotype of human lung organoids derived from adult stem cells. We compared three systems - animal-derived (AD), animal-free (AF), and scaffold-free (SF) - under basal-out, apical-out, and proximally differentiated conditions. Our goal was to assess how each platform influences epithelial cell-type-associated marker expression and morphology. AD and AF matrices yielded smaller, more uniform organoids, whereas SF cultures produced markedly larger structures, especially in apical-out and proximally differentiated conditions. Bulk RT-qPCR analysis revealed distinct platform-associated marker-expression profiles: the basal cell marker KRT5 peaked in AD basal-out organoids. Under proximal differentiation, KRT5 expression declined across systems, reaching the lowest levels in AF, and SCGB1A1 became undetectable in all systems. In contrast, SF cultures showed the highest expression of the AT1 cell-associated marker AQP5 (basal-out and apical-out) and of the ciliated cell-associated marker FOXJ1 (proximally differentiated), whereas MUC5AC was only slightly upregulated. Notably, ACE2 and TMPRSS2 - key mediators of SARS‑CoV‑2 entry - were induced by proximal differentiation: ACE2 was strongly upregulated in SF organoids, and TMPRSS2 increased under all proximal conditions, independent of platform. Immunofluorescence corroborated mature epithelial phenotypes, revealing robust ciliation across platforms and particularly advanced cilia maturation in AF cultures. Together, these data indicate that the cultivation platform strongly influences lung organoid growth, morphology, and cell-type-associated marker expression. Our findings provide an evidence-based guide for selecting systems to model human respiratory physiology, infection, and regeneration.

Article.Title: Association of KCNJ11 and TCF7L2 genetic variants with type 2 diabetes in a Mexican region with high disease prevalence and strong Mayan cultural heritage
Article.Authors: Fragoso-Bargas N.; Ruiz-Garcia L.; Pinto-Escalante D.; Escarcega-Castro V.; Valencia-Pacheco G.; Rubi-Castellanos R.; Valadez-Gonzalez N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Type 2 diabetes (T2D) affects up to 18.3% of Mexicans, surpassing the global prevalence of 11.1%. Among Amerindian groups, Mayan ancestry has been linked to a higher risk of T2D. Sisal, a southeastern Mexican town with strong Mayan heritage, reports a prevalence of 22%, providing a unique setting to study genetic factors in an underrepresented population. We examined associations of KCNJ11 (rs5215, rs5219) and TCF7L2 (rs7901695, rs11196205) genetic variants with T2D in 232 individuals, including 99 participants diagnosed with T2D and 132 metabolically healthy individuals. Both rs5215 (OR = 2.07 [1.20–3.58], p = 0.009) and rs5219 (OR = 1.89 [1.09–3.27], p = 0.023) showed association under the dominant model and remained robust after adjustment for age, sex, and adiposity measurements. Overdominant models for both variants also indicated increased risk. Therefore, for both KCNJ11´s variants, a copy of their C (rs5215) or T (rs5219) allele increases T2D susceptibility. Rs7901695 showed no association. Rs11196205 exhibited a protective effect under the overdominant model (OR = 0.37 [0.18–0.76], p = 0.007). A similar trend ( p = 0.051) in the same direction was observed in the dominant model. In contrast, the recessive model indicated increased risk for CC homozygotes (OR = 1.79 [1.10–2.91], p = 0.019). Both overdominant and recessive models remained robust after covariable adjustment. A joint model including both rs5219 (Dominant-coding) and rs11196205 (Overdominant-coding) SNVs showed that rs11196205 remained robustly associated with T2D, while the effect of rs5219 was slightly weaker. These findings suggest rs5215-C, rs5219-T (KCNJ11), and rs11196205-C ( TCF7L2 ) increase T2D risk, whereas a single G allele at rs11196205 may mitigate the effect of C in a southeastern Mexican population with prevalent Mayan ancestry.

Article.Title: Unveiling the potential of two different lactococcal glutamate decarboxylase enzymes and their application for producing GABA-rich soy beverages
Article.Authors: Abellán J.; Sabuquillo P.; Lazar R.; Langa S.; Benito-Ventoso J.; Peirotén Á.; Landete J.; Curiel J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) has been associated with health properties and has therefore attracted the attention of the food industry for the development of functional foods. Our previous studies elucidated the great capacity of Lactococcus lactis INIA Z108 strain, as well as the heterologous expression of the gadB gene from Lactococcus cremoris MG1363 in other strains to produce high yields of GABA. Because the biochemical properties of GadB enzymes from Lactococcus cremoris MG1363 and Lactococcus lactis INIA Z108 are still unknown, this study describes their characterization, stabilization on food-grade supports and their application for the production of plant-based beverages enriched in GABA. The recombinant GadB_MG1363 and GadB_Z108 enzymes were purified at yields of 18.12 and 20.53 mg per liter of culture, respectively. Both enzymes exhibited similar architecture and biochemical properties, exhibiting optimal activity at pH 5.0 and 40 °C, heat sensitivity at temperatures above 30 °C and similar catalytic efficiencies. Although multipoint covalent immobilization on agarose supports activated with N-hydroxysuccinimide groups drastically reduced the catalytic activity of both GadB enzymes, their stabilization was achieved by encapsulation in food-grade gellan gum. The resulting derivatives retained more than 70% of glutamate decarboxylase activity, improved their heat resistance to 50 ℃ and their tolerance to metal ions and higher pH levels. Since the application of these derivatives enabled the production of a non-fermented soy beverage enriched in GABA up to 9.27 mM, this study demonstrates the potential application of stabilized recombinant GadB enzymes for the production of GABA-enriched plant-based beverages.

Article.Title: A multi-phase task scheduling with NSGA-II integrated ant colony optimization in fog-cloud environment
Article.Authors: Tahira U.; Verma A.
Article.Abstract: Efficient task scheduling in fog-cloud environments has become a critical challenge in modern healthcare systems due to the increasing demand for data-intensive medical applications and real-time service delivery. Managing computational tasks under heterogeneous resource constraints while maintaining balanced workload distribution, low latency, reliability, and high system performance remains a significant issue in healthcare fog-cloud infrastructures. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a prediction-aware multi-layer intelligent scheduling framework for healthcare fog-cloud environments. Initially, a rule-based scheduling layer performs preliminary task filtering based on deadline, budget, VM resource availability, and healthcare-specific constraints to generate feasible task-to-VM mappings. Subsequently, a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)-based prediction model forecasts near-future virtual machine workloads using historical workload observations and temporal dependencies, enabling prediction-aware and adaptive resource allocation. Finally, a hybrid optimization framework combining Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) and Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) generates near-optimal scheduling solutions by jointly minimizing execution cost, makespan, and latency while maximizing throughput and resource utilization. Under multi-objective constraints, experimental evaluation using synthetically generated healthcare-oriented workloads demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves an execution cost of 25,842.61 and a makespan of 21,846.73. The framework further achieves 98.40% emergency task priority satisfaction, 98.90% reliability, and 98.10% fault tolerance, while reducing the critical deadline violation penalty to 2.15. Compared with the corresponding framework without LSTM-based workload prediction, the proposed approach reduces execution cost by 12.37%, makespan by 4.91%, and average latency by 73.93%, while improving throughput by 89.15% and the resource utilization score by 82.69%. Comparative analysis against ACO, NSGA-II, Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO), Hummingbird Algorithm (HBA), and NSGA-III demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework across multiple scheduling and healthcare-oriented performance measures. Statistical analysis using the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank test, paired t -test, Friedman test, and ANOVA further supports the statistical robustness and effectiveness of the proposed framework.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: ant colony optimization; NSGA-II; cloud computing; hybrid metaheuristic; fog computing
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Information Systems > Cloud Computing and Resource Management; Computer Science > Computer Networks and Communications > IoT and Edge/Fog Computing; Engineering > Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering > Scheduling and Optimization Algorithms

Article.Title: Field surveys and soil metabarcoding recover largely non-overlapping nivicolous myxomycete diversity in Ile-Alatau and Katon-Karagay National Parks (Kazakhstan)
Article.Authors: Shchepin O.; Schnittler M.; Azirakhmet Z.; Daniyarov A.; Rakhimova S.; Akilzhanova A.; Kussainova A.; Abayev B.; Nursafina A.; Bersimbaev R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Nivicolous myxomycetes fruit at snowmelt in mountains, while their amoeboid trophic stages persist unseen in soil. To assess to what extent different approaches capture their diversity, we combined 18S rDNA barcoding of 172 fruiting body collections (48 ribotypes) with soil metabarcoding of the same marker (187 samples, 730 myxomycete amplicon sequence variants, ASVs) along elevational and canopy gradients in Ile-Alatau (IANP, Tian Shan) and Katon-Karagay (KKNP, Altai) National Parks, Kazakhstan. Only 7.2% of nivicolous barcode variants were recovered by both methods; a second fruiting body survey of IANP added no further soil matches and shared only 26% of its ribotypes with the main IANP survey, so the approaches are complementary and neither alone provides an adequate inventory. Soil communities were hyperdiverse, dominated by ASV replacement and compositionally distinct between parks. Per-sample richness did not differ significantly between parks, but fine-scale turnover was higher in KKNP; canopy shaped composition in both parks but richness only in IANP, where open-canopy positions were richer. Nivicolous richness showed no elevational trend within the sampled gradients, whereas that of other myxomycetes declined with elevation in IANP. The largely park-specific ASV and ribotype pools support regional structuring of myxomycetes over unlimited gene flow.

Article.Title: Causal landscape of the circulating proteome in systemic iron overload revealed by Mendelian randomization and experimental validation
Article.Authors: Wang M.; Ying Q.; Lou X.; Li Q.; Li C.; Dai S.; Du X.; Wang J.; Li L.; Liu Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Systemic iron overload precipitates progressive and often irreversible organ dysfunction, yet the clinical toolkit for non-invasive, organ-specific monitoring of iron accumulation remains inadequate. This study leverages a proteome-wide causal inference framework to identify circulating biomarkers that drive or reflect iron deposition in the liver, spleen, and pancreas. We integrated large-scale plasma pQTL data (n = 35,559) with GWAS summary statistics of organ-specific iron content using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR). Candidate proteins were prioritized through Bayesian colocalization to identify shared genetic etiologies. The findings were validated in a systemic iron-overload mouse model, assessing the concordance between genetically predicted effects and experimental protein expression, histopathology, and systemic iron markers. MR analysis identified PRSS1 as a high-confidence causal mediator and prioritized BGLAP, FTMT, and ZHX3 as candidate proteins associated with tissue iron homeostasis. Genetically predicted BGLAP levels exhibited a negative causal effect on liver iron content (β = -0.294, P = 6.35 × 10⁻⁶), while FTMT and ZHX3 were positively associated with splenic iron accumulation. Notably, PRSS1 demonstrated a robust negative association with pancreatic iron (β = -0.217, P = 1.28 × 10⁻⁵) and showed strong evidence of genetic colocalization (PP.H4 = 0.982), suggesting a direct regulatory role. These MR-prioritized protein targets exhibited directionally concordant in vivo associations with organ iron accumulation and pharmacological iron chelation in mouse models of systemic iron overload. Our study establishes a genetically anchored proteomic map of systemic iron variation, prioritizing PRSS1 alongside BGLAP, FTMT, and ZHX3 as candidate proteins associated with organ-specific iron homeostasis. Rather than providing definitive clinical tools, these findings offer hypothesis-generating insights that warrant rigorous prospective validation in clinical iron-overload patient cohorts and dedicated functional models.

Article.Title: Prioritizing ArtTech trends in Vietnam using a T-spherical fuzzy bounded-rationality decision framework
Article.Authors: Anh T.; Nhieu N.
Article.Abstract: The integration of art and technology is reshaping cultural production and audience experience, but ArtTech development in Vietnam remains constrained by uneven infrastructure, institutional capacity, accessibility, and regulatory uncertainty. Eight ArtTech trends were prioritized across six evaluation factors through an expert-based multi-criteria decision-making framework. Linguistic assessments from 15 experts were represented using T-spherical fuzzy numbers and aggregated through a weighted Einstein interactive operator. Criterion weights were derived using the Method based on the Removal Effects of Criteria, and the alternatives were ranked using a prospect-theory-informed extension of the Evaluation based on Distance from Average Solution method. Market Readiness received the greatest relative weight, followed by Innovation Potential, Cultural Relevance, Accessibility, Ethical Considerations, and User Engagement. Virtual Cultural Spaces was ranked first, followed by AR/VR Exhibitions and Creative Coding for Interactive Installations. Sensitivity analysis showed that the first, second, and lower-ranked positions were stable, while only the third and fourth positions changed under one gain–loss balance scenario. Standard and prospect-theory-informed MEREC–EDAS produced identical rankings, although appraisal-score magnitudes differed. The behavioral extension therefore refined the representation and spacing of favorable and unfavorable deviations rather than restructuring the complete ordering. The findings represent structured expert perceptions of strategic viability under Vietnamese conditions and should not be interpreted as direct evidence of realized adoption, market performance, or audience demand.

Article.Title: A geographic information system-based assessment of asphalt road network inventory, condition, and maintenance needs in Jimma City, Ethiopia
Article.Authors: Abafogi A.; Fufa F.; Jemal A.; Teshome G.
Article.Abstract: Urban road infrastructure is critical for economic development and mobility, yet municipalities in developing nations like Ethiopia face substantial challenges in infrastructure management and maintenance. In Jimma City, the absence of a systematic and complete inventory of its asphalt road network has resulted in inefficient maintenance, accelerated pavement deterioration, and subsequent economic losses. This study addresses this critical gap by developing a comprehensive GIS-based framework to assess the asphalt road network’s inventory, condition, and maintenance needs. A cross-sectional study was conducted within the administrative boundaries of Jimma City, with primary data on road geometry and attributes collected through GPS surveys and direct visual inspection, focusing on distress types, severity, and extent. This information was integrated into a centralized GIS database using ArcGIS Desktop 10.8 version. Pavement conditions were evaluated and categorized, and spatial analysis was employed to identify the distribution of road conditions and distress hotspots. Subsequently, a maintenance needs forecast was developed, prioritizing interventions based on road condition and hierarchy. The assessment revealed that 69.3% of Jimma City’s asphalt road network is in poor (62.9%) or very poor (6.4%) condition, while only 12.1% are in good or very good condition. Potholes were identified as the most dominant distress, affecting 48.6% of the surveyed network. Other significant distress types included wash-away damage (16.4%), edge drop-off (12.6%), and alligator cracking (9.3%). Notably, statistical analysis revealed a severe decoupling between road assets and expenditures, with a near-zero correlation ( r ≤ 0.07) between maintenance costs and all asset metrics, despite strong internal asset valuations ( r ≥ 0.91). This structural disconnect highlights an inefficient, reactive maintenance regime where funding is allocated independently of deterioration rates or asset values. The GIS-based approach proved effective for creating a detailed inventory, evaluating conditions, and forecasting maintenance needs. The findings highlight an urgent need for a shift from reactive to proactive, data-driven maintenance strategies.

Article.Title: Subacute oral exposure to Fumaria parviflora aromatic water (hydrosol) is associated with 2,4-DTBP-related toxicity in rats, with molecular docking suggesting a potential pro-oxidant role
Article.Authors: Keshavarz V.; Saffari M.; Rahmani F.; Mohseni R.; Abolhasanzadeh Z.; Zarei M.
Article.Abstract: Fumaria parviflora is widely used in traditional Iranian medicine, commonly in the form of hydrosol. Despite its therapeutic applications, data regarding its safety, particularly following repeated exposure, remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the subacute oral toxicity of F. parviflora hydrosol in a rodent model and to investigate the potential role of its major constituent, 2,4-di-tert-butylphenol (2,4-DTBP), using molecular docking analysis. Hydrosol was prepared via traditional distillation and analyzed by GC–MS to identify its chemical constituents. We administered different doses of hydrosol (0.5, 3.2, and 10 mL/kg) to 40 male and female Wistar rats over a subacute period (28 days). Phytochemical analysis identified seven compounds, with 2,4-DTBP as a major component. High-dose administration (10 mL/kg) resulted in significant histopathological alterations in the liver and kidney, elevated blood urea nitrogen levels ( P < 0.05), and reduced triglycerides ( P < 0.01). White blood cells were significantly ( P < 0.05) decreased, and Mean Corpuscular Hemoglobin was significantly ( P < 0.05) increased in all treated groups. Molecular docking revealed strong binding affinities of 2,4-DTBP toward RXR-α, PPARα, and TNF-α, suggesting a potential pathway to the observed toxic effects. F. parviflora hydrosol exhibits dose-dependent toxicity, with higher doses inducing significant hepatorenal damage. The presence of 2,4-DTBP may contribute to these effects through interactions with key molecular targets. These findings highlight the necessity for dose regulation, safety assessment, and standardization in the use of herbal hydrosols.

Article.Title: Near-infrared optical losses induced by rear contacts in four-terminal perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells
Article.Authors: Zulhafizhazuan W.; Sepeai S.; Rohaizar M.; Shaikh G.; Shafian S.; Chelvanathan P.; Umar A.; Syafiq U.; Su’ait M.; Ludin N.
Article.Abstract: Four-terminal (4T) perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells offer a promising architecture to surpass the theoretical efficiency limits of single-junction photovoltaics; however, achieving high performance requires simultaneously optimizing top cell efficiency and sub-bandgap photon transmission. This study presents an experimental and computational deconvolution of near-infrared (NIR) optical losses in 4T tandem devices. Experimental characterization demonstrates that integrating a commercial silicon bottom cell (15.60%) beneath a perovskite top cell with a conventional silver (Ag) rear electrode drastically suppresses the bottom cell short-circuit current density ( J SC_EQE ) from 37.85 to 1.18 mAcm − 2 . This 89.7% loss in NIR photon harvesting stems primarily from metallic opacity and parasitic plasmonic absorption. Replacing the Ag layer with a semi-transparent perovskite top cell restores the bottom cell ( J SC_EQE ) to 11.46 mAcm − 2 , achieving a cumulative tandem efficiency of 15.90% alongside an optimized 11.18% (top cell). To eliminate remaining optical shielding, Monte Carlo Wafer Ray Tracer simulations and admittance analysis reveal that a 70 nm indium tin oxide (ITO) rear contact provides an optimal phase shift \(\:({\phi})\) at 1000 nm while maintaining minimal free-carrier absorption (4.49%). This computationally optimized transparent conductive oxide recovers the bottom cell J SC_WRT to 19.73 mAcm − 2 , projecting a total 4T tandem efficiency of 19.82%.

Article.Title: Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel triazolopyrimidine–1,2,3-triazole–acetamide hybrids as potent α-glucosidase inhibitors supported by in silico studies
Article.Authors: Peytam F.; Biglar M.; Bayati B.; Norouzbahari M.; Gülcan H.; Mojtabavi S.; Ghasemi F.; Tehrani M.; Firoozpour L.; Foroumadi A.
Article.Abstract: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a global metabolic disorder characterized by chronic hyperglycemia, and inhibition of α ‑glucosidase is an established strategy to manage postprandial blood glucose. However, current inhibitors such as acarbose are associated with gastrointestinal side effects and variable efficacy, necessitating the development of novel agents. To this aim, a new series of poly-substituted triazolo[1,5- a ]pyrimidines 13 conjugated with 1,2,3-triazol and substituted N -arylacetamides was designed and synthesized as potential α ‑glucosidase inhibitors. All compounds were evaluated for their inhibitory potency, and structure–activity relationship (SAR) studies were conducted. The most potent compound, 13n , was further assessed through enzyme kinetics, α ‑amylase inhibition, cytotoxicity (MTT assay), CD spectroscopy, fluorescence spectroscopy, thermodynamic analysis, molecular docking, 500 ns molecular dynamics simulations, and ADME analysis. Our findings identify the triazolo[1,5- a ]pyrimidine scaffold as a promising lead for the development of potent α -glucosidase inhibitors with selectivity over α -amylase, offering a potential pathway toward more effective antidiabetic agents.

Article.Title: Frequency-domain characterization of a fractional-order armature DC motor via a modified integral transform: a comparative analysis with the Laplace transform
Article.Authors: K J.; Saratha S.; Premalatha K.
Article.Abstract: Integral transforms play an essential role in the transfer-function analysis of dynamical systems. In this work, a recently introduced integral transform is investigated for the analysis of fractional-order electromechanical systems. The formulation of this transform includes a parameterized kernel, which allows controlled modification of the associated transform domain and consequently, influences the pole distribution. To illustrate its applicability, a fractional-order model of an armature-controlled DC motor is considered. The transfer functions obtained using the Laplace transform and the proposed transform are compared through pole analysis and Bode frequency responses. The analysis demonstrates that the proposed transform preserves the stability and dynamic characteristics of the original system while providing additional flexibility in the transformed domain through systematic pole relocation and frequency-response adjustment. The fractional-order model exhibits improved phase margins and faster transient responses compared with the corresponding integer-order model. Furthermore, experimental validation confirms that the fractional-order model with $$\vartheta =0.8$$ provides the closest agreement with the measured motor response, demonstrating the capability of fractional-order modeling to capture the memory-dependent dynamics of the system. These results indicate that the proposed transform constitutes an effective framework for the transfer-function analysis of fractional-order dynamical systems without compromising their fundamental physical characteristics.

Article.Title: Test-time fine-tuning of large-scale vision foundation models for data-efficient electronic waste segmentation
Article.Authors: Senanayake A.; Harandi M.; Kunananthaseelan N.; Arashpour M.
Article.Abstract: Electronic waste (e-waste) recycling is crucial for resource conservation and environmental sustainability. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, have shown strong potential to advance waste recognition and recycling. However, deep learning-based e-waste recognition remains challenging due to heterogeneous, cluttered images and limited labeled data. Model adaptation is further constrained by high computational costs and lengthy adaptation times. Large-scale vision foundation models (LVMs) provide strong generalization across visual domains, but their direct application to e-waste imaging remains limited for fine-grained segmentation. Here, we present a deep learning-based segmentation approach that integrates test-time fine-tuning with LVMs for automated e-waste recognition. The proposed approach adapts LVMs at inference time using a small, diverse, and contextually relevant support set, avoiding the need for offline domain-specific fine-tuning. To construct this support set, we introduce active retrieval , which combines cosine similarity-based preselection with an informativeness acquisition function to identify query-specific, non-redundant support images. Evaluated on a curated e-waste dataset, the method reduces end-to-end processing time by approximately sixfold compared with parameter-efficient fine-tuning, while maintaining reliable segmentation accuracy using less domain-specific data. This scalable approach supports practical AI deployment for e-waste management and improved resource recovery.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: vision foundation models; image segmentation; electronic waste; data-efficient learning
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Advanced Neural Network Applications; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Domain Adaptation and Few-Shot Learning; Engineering > Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering > Industrial Vision Systems and Defect Detection

Article.Title: Paclobutrazol improves physiological traits and seed yield in sesame genotypes under rainfed Pothwar conditions
Article.Authors: Ahmed J.; Jhanzab H.; Darwish M.; Khalili A.; Saeed M.; Khalofah A.; Qayyum A.
Article.Abstract: Climate change is increasing temperatures and causing drought conditions, along with fluctuations and unpredictable rainfall patterns, which are reducing crop yields. In the rainfed Pothwar region, sesame productivity is further constrained by terminal drought and heat stress, yet the potential of plant growth regulators such as paclobutrazol (PBZ) to mitigate these effects in sesame genotypes remains largely unexplored. To investigate the effect of paclobutrazol (PBZ) concentrations on the yield and physiological traits of sesame genotypes under rainfed conditions of the Pothwar region, experiments were conducted at two locations: NARC-Islamabad and URF-Koont, Chakwal. The study included ten exotic genotypes and two indigenous varieties and was carried out over two years, 2020 and 2021. Paclobutrazol was applied as a foliar spray, with treatments consisting of T 0 = Control without paclobutrazol, T 1 = 150, T 2 = 300, T 3 = 450, and T 4 = 600 mgL -1 paclobutrazol were employed. Results indicated that PBZ significantly enhanced physiological characteristics, and all variables examined (genotypes, locations, and PBZ concentrations). With the lowest intercellular CO 2 concentration, the sesame genotypes PI-175907 and PI-154304 had the highest relative water content (RWC), SPAD value, leaf area, net photosynthetic rate, transpiration rate, stomatal conductance, proline content, epicuticular wax content, and maximum seed yield. In both years of the experiment, PBZ treatments at 600 and 450 mgL -1 had the highest RWC, SPAD value, net photosynthetic rate, transpiration rate, stomatal conductance, proline content, epicuticular wax content, and seed yield. However, the PBZ concentration reduced the leaf area and intercellular CO 2 concentration. Regarding environments, NARC-Islamabad generated highest transpiration rate, intercellular CO 2 concentration; however, the URF-Koont produced the highest seed yield with the highest RWC, SPAD value, leaf area, transpiration rate, stomatal conductance, proline content and epicuticular wax content. Therefore, it is concluded that paclobutrazol could dramatically improve physiological characters while increasing economic returns through better seed productivity. Based on the findings, the genotypes PI-154304 and PI-175907 with paclobutrazol level 450 mgL −1 may be suggested for cultivation in Pothwar farming community under rainfed conditions, with improved physiological characters as well as enhanced growth and yield.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: paclobutrazol; sesame; plant growth regulators; rainfed agriculture; Pothwar region; seed yield; physiological traits

Article.Title: Twenty years of sports venue provision in China: National evidence from official statistics, 2004–2024
Article.Authors: Liu Z.; Zhang A.; Zhou Y.; Jin Q.; Zhu Z.; Yang X.
Article.Abstract: Long-term surveillance of sports venue provision can help document changes in national infrastructure and provide a baseline for future spatial, behavioural, and public health research. China has expanded its sports infrastructure substantially, and the official observation series provides a national administrative record that can complement regional and population-specific empirical studies. This study described changes in national sports venue provision in China across the available official observations from 2004 to 2024. A longitudinal descriptive ecological analysis was conducted using official national sports venue statistics published by the General Administration of Sport of China. The series comprised the fifth national sports venue census reported in 2004, the sixth national sports venue census reported in 2014, and annual national sports venue statistical surveys reported from 2015 to 2024. Three indicators were analysed: number of sports venues, total sports venue area, and per-capita sports venue area. Descriptive measures included absolute increase, relative increase, endpoint-based average annual increase, endpoint compound annual growth rate (CAGR), indexed values (2004 = 100), and period-specific growth rates. Between the 2004 and 2024 observation endpoints, the number of sports venues increased from 850,000 to 4.842 million (+ 469.6%; endpoint CAGR: 9.09%). Total sports venue area increased from 1.33 to 4.23 billion m² (+ 218.0%; endpoint CAGR: 5.96%), while per-capita sports venue area increased from 1.03 to 3.00 m²/person (+ 191.3%; endpoint CAGR: 5.49%). The number of venues increased faster than the two area-based indicators, and this divergence became more apparent after the 2014 observation. All annual observations from 2015 to 2024 were higher than the preceding observation, although the annualised growth rates varied across intervals. The findings provide a national descriptive baseline for the 2004–2024 study window and show that venue number, total area, and per-capita area capture distinct dimensions of recorded infrastructure provision. These statistics do not directly measure accessibility, public availability, quality, utilisation, physical activity, or health outcomes; future research can integrate them with spatial, behavioural, and facility-level data.

Article.Title: Cryopreservation techniques for adult and pediatric glioblastoma organoids and their effects on stem cell self-renewal
Article.Authors: Shakya S.; Joseph E.; A M.; Shukla P.; Nwachukwu T.; Ho S.; Miller T.; Hubert C.
Article.Abstract: Organoids are advanced three-dimensional in vitro models that faithfully recapitulate tumor architecture, cellular heterogeneity, and microenvironmental interactions, making them valuable tools for cancer research, including for the lethal primary brain tumor glioblastoma (GBM). However, organoid generation is time- and resource-intensive, necessitating reliable cryopreservation techniques to enable long-term storage, biobanking, and sample sharing. Cryopreservation of small spheroids and organoids has been reported, but such methods have not been directly compared, and preservation of larger multi-millimeter-scale organoids has remained largely unexplored. Additionally, existing cryopreservation methods containing FBS, which induces differentiation in neural-lineage culture, have not been systematically benchmarked for their ability to maintain GBM self-renewal. We evaluated multiple custom-made and commercial cryopreservation containers and media on GBM self-renewal, as well as cell viability, structure, and stem cell preservation in large matrix-based GBM organoids and organoids directly from patient tissue. Common non-commercial cryopreservation media containing 10% DMSO, either serum-free or supplemented with 80% FBS, preserved GBM stem cell viability and self-renewal as well or better than commercial cryopreservation formulations tested. Cryopreserved organoids maintained post-thaw viability, self-renewal capacity, and histological characteristics following outgrowth. These findings demonstrate feasible methods to cryopreserve large GBM organoids, supporting their broader use in biobanking, collaborative studies, and experimental workflows.
