Article.Title: Integrated experimental and machine learning analysis of nano-MQL assisted turning of AA7075-T6
Article.Authors: Binali R.; Ayrancı E.; Kuntoğlu M.; Çetin T.; Aslan A.; Parlakyigit A.; Kul B.
Article.Abstract: This study comprehensively investigates the machinability performance of dry cutting, minimum quantity lubrication (MQL), and nanoparticle-modified minimum quantity lubrication (nano-MQL) methods in turning AA7075-T6 aluminum alloy. Tool wear mechanisms were evaluated using SEM/EDS analyses; surface roughness, cutting forces, and energy consumption were compared under different cutting parameters. In addition, the obtained data were predicted and evaluated using machine learning-based correlation maps and random forest models. The results demonstrated that the cutting environment plays a decisive role in machining performance. The nano-MQL application reduced the build-up edge (BUE) height at the cutting edge by approximately 29% compared to dry cutting and presented a more stable wear morphology compared to MQL. Surface roughness values ​​were measured at their lowest levels under nano-MQL conditions for all cutting parameters; an improvement of 12–20% compared to dry cutting and 3–10% compared to MQL was achieved. The cutting forces were reduced by an average of 8–19% in the nano-MQL environment compared to dry cutting, while energy consumption savings ranged from 10–53%. The nano-MQL strategy demonstrated high performance and energy efficiency in turning AA7075-T6 alloy by reducing tool wear, improving surface quality, and lowering cutting forces and energy consumption.

Article.Title: Association of dietary total antioxidant capacity, dietary inflammatory index, and dietary phytochemical index with sarcopenia in middle-aged and older Iranian women: a case-control study
Article.Authors: Nabizadeh K.; Sohrabi Z.; Zare M.; Faghih S.
Article.Abstract: As life expectancy increases worldwide, the older population and age-related diseases such as sarcopenia are increasing. Although some studies have examined the effects of inflammation or antioxidants on muscle health, evidence in this area remains limited. Given the impact of diet on muscle health, this study investigated the relationship between the Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII), Dietary total Antioxidant Capacity (DTAC), and Dietary Phytochemical Index (DPI) with sarcopenia in middle-aged and older Iranian women. In this case-control study, a total of 120 participants (60 cases and 60 controls), frequency-matched case-control study (by age and physical activity), were studied. Body composition was assessed using bioelectrical impedance analysis (BIA), and gait speed and handgrip strength were assessed for all participants. Sarcopenia was identified according to the Asian Working Group on Sarcopenia (AWGS) criteria. Dietary intake was assessed using a validated 168-item semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire (FFQ), and DII, DTAC, and DPI scores were calculated. Multivariate logistic regression was used to determine the associations, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant. In the adjusted models, higher DTAC was associated with lower odds of sarcopenia (OR = 0.744; 95% CI = 0.588–0.942), while higher DII was associated with increased odds (OR = 2.35; 95% CI = 1.51–3.63). DPI also remained significantly associated with lower odds (OR = 0.516; 95% CI = 0.322–0.828). In conclusion, an inflammatory diet was associated with higher odds of sarcopenia, while diets rich in antioxidants and phytochemicals were associated with lower odds.

Article.Title: Structured generative AI preparation and classroom belonging in a six-class randomized trial
Article.Authors: Wang R.; Sun J.; Wen S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) may support independent preparation without necessarily strengthening students’ connections to the classroom. We examined a structured instructional protocol combining AI exploration, confidence reflection, unresolved question generation, and instructor responsiveness. Following baseline assessment, six intact undergraduate class sections at one Chinese university were randomized equally, with three sections and 110 students assigned to each condition. Assessments were conducted in Weeks 1, 6, and 12, and the intervention began in Week 2. Recomputed item means were analyzed using equally weighted section-level contrasts with four degrees of freedom, supplemented by exact randomization tests. At Week 12, the between-condition difference in classroom belonging change was 0.361 (95% CI 0.145 to 0.576; Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.029). The corresponding differences were 0.282 for emotional engagement, − 0.497 for reactance to teacher guidance, and − 15.24 points for the confidence–performance discrepancy index (CPDI). Exact two-sided randomization p values were 0.100 for all primary contrasts, the minimum attainable with six balanced sections. Exploratory individual-level pathway and effect-modification analyses were treated as hypothesis-generating because only six sections were observed and the pathway estimates were sensitive to measurement timing. Overall, the structured protocol showed promising differences in classroom belonging and related outcomes, but inference remains limited by the small number of randomized sections, parametric model assumptions, and the preliminary discrepancy measure. The findings therefore concern the combined instructional protocol rather than an isolated effect of GenAI or an established psychological mechanism.

Article.Title: Ex-vivo magnetic resonance elastography detects inflammation-associated biomechanical changes in a mouse model of Salmonella-induced colitis
Article.Authors: Maisch N.; Kühl A.; Tzschätzsch H.; Hussein S.; Bereswill S.; Siegmund B.; Heimesaat M.; Paclik D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Inflammation alters the mechanical properties of soft tissues, yet the biomechanics of the inflamed intestine remain poorly characterized. Using magnetic resonance elastography (MRE), we characterized colonic biomechanical properties in a murine colitis model. CBA/J mice infected with Salmonella Typhimurium were sacrificed at days 5, 16 and 30 post infection alongside uninfected controls. Ex-vivo tabletop MRE and the Springpot model yielded shear modulus µ (stiffness) and powerlaw exponent α (structure). Collagen, hyaluronic acid and periostin content, immune-cell infiltration, epithelial apoptosis and histopathological scoring were assessed histologically. Colonic stiffness decreased at day 5 (1.7 ± 0.7 kPa) versus controls (5.5 ± 4.0 kPa; p = 0.0002), concurrent with development of edema, immune-cell infiltration and apoptosis, without concomitant ECM changes. Stiffness normalized by day 30 and correlated negatively with the histopathological score ( r = − 0.40, p = 0.002) and the total cell count ( r = -0.47, p = 0.002). At day 5, µ discriminated infected from control colons with an AUC of 0.93 (sensitivity 89%, specificity 90%). Ex-vivo MRE thus detects reversible, inflammation-driven biomechanical changes, indicating that MRE-derived stiffness may serve as a biomechanical readout of acute intestinal inflammation.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: periostin; hyaluronic acid; epithelial apoptosis; magnetic resonance elastography; tissue stiffness; colitis; Salmonella typhimurium; shear modulus; intestinal inflammation; immune cell infiltration; ex vivo imaging

Article.Title: A new weight function representation for one-dimensional edge cracks: application to mode I stress intensity factor evaluation for a radial edge-crack in a solid circular disk
Article.Authors: Mokarrami M.; Kaklar J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate evaluation of stress intensity factors (SIFs) is fundamental to many fatigue and fracture mechanics analyses. The weight function method (WFM) provides a simple and computationally efficient approach for evaluating SIFs under complex loading conditions. In this study, a new representation of the one-dimensional WF for edge cracks is proposed and applied to derive the Mode I WF for a radial edge-crack in a solid circular disk subjected to tensile loading. Given the availability of SIF solutions and several approximate WF formulations for this geometry, the primary objective is to assess the effectiveness of the proposed representation in constructing approximate WFs from reference SIFs. To this end, reference SIFs for three tensile stress distributions were calculated using finite element analysis (FEA) and used to determine the WF coefficients. Fitting expressions were then developed to represent these coefficients as continuous functions of the relative crack length, enabling efficient SIF evaluation within the investigated range. The derived WF was validated using three independent, complex nonlinear stress distributions, and its predictions showed good agreement with FE results. Furthermore, comparisons with previously published WF formulations for radial edge cracks demonstrated the capability of the proposed representation to construct accurate one-dimensional approximate weight functions from reference SIFs.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: weight function method; mode I stress intensity factor; nonlinear stress distribution; tensile loading; edge cracks

Article.Title: A feature optimized machine learning framework for solar radiation prediction in the high-altitude Western Himalayan region
Article.Authors: Dogra A.; Sharma G.; Thakur D.; Kumar A.; Bahadur J.; Singh V.
Article.Abstract: Accurate prediction of solar potential is essential for efficient integrating photovoltaic system particularly in geographically complex regions where meteorological variability poses challenges to grid stability. This study focuses on improving the solar potential estimation in arid and semi-arid Himalayan regions through feature selection and machine learning approaches. The study evaluates seven feature selection methods such as Pearson Correlation, Mutual Information, XG Boost Importance, LASSO, Random Forest Importance, Permutation Importance and SHAP to identify most influential parameters for solar radiation. The results showed that temporal variable is most important followed by temperature in prediction accuracy of solar radiation. K-based feature selection results show that the selected five feature subset provides an effective accuracy–complexity trade-off, reducing RMSE by approximately 17.5% (from 75.17 to 62.01 W/m²) while maintaining competitive predictive performance compared with the full-feature models. Out of all the models tested, MLP and XGBoost yield optimal results with all features used (RMSE is about 59.86 W/m² and R² is around 0.953). Interestingly, even after using just five selected features, XGBoost and LSTM still provide accurate predictions (RMSE is about 62.46 W/m² and R² is roughly 0.949). The results depict that the model framework has managed to provide highly accurate predictions (R² > 0.95) while reducing input dimensionality, showing the potential of the approach for practical solar energy prediction scenarios.

Article.Title: Additional effect of pain neuroscience education to neuromuscular exercise in chronic low back pain: a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Letafatkar A.; Alvani E.; Sheikhi B.; Hadadnezhad M.; Amirizadeh F.; Khazaei O.; Rossettini G.
Article.Abstract: Pain Neuroscience Education (PNE) and Neuromuscular Exercise (NME) are commonly used in chronic low back pain (CLBP) rehabilitation. However, evidence remains limited and inconsistent regarding whether adding PNE to exercise provides incremental benefits beyond exercise alone across pain, disability, and psychosocial outcomes. To determine whether adding PNE to a structured NME program provides additional improvements in pain intensity, disability, and psychological outcomes compared with NME alone in individuals with CLBP. A single-blind, two-arm randomized controlled trial was conducted in Iran involving 60 adults with CLBP. Participants were randomized to either PNE (10–20 min/session, three times weekly for eight weeks, delivered immediately before exercise using verbal, visual and interactive methods) followed by NME (experimental group) or NME alone (control group). Both groups attended supervised sessions three times per week for eight weeks. The primary outcome was pain intensity (VAS). Secondary outcomes included disability (ODI), fear-avoidance beliefs (FABQ), pain self-efficacy (PSEQ), and kinesiophobia (TSK). Outcomes were assessed at baseline, post-intervention, and six-month follow-up. Sample size was determined a priori based on the primary outcome. Data were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA with intention-to-treat principle, with Greenhouse–Geisser correction when required. Pain intensity and disability showed no significant Group × Time interactions (VAS: p = 0.13, \({\eta}_{p}^{2}\) = 0.04; ODI: p = 0.11, \({\eta}_{p}^{2}\) = 0.05), and mean changes did not reach minimal clinically important difference (MCID) thresholds. Significant Group × Time interactions were observed for FABQ ( p < 0.001, \({\eta}_{p}^{2}\) = 0.16), PSEQ ( p < 0.001, \({\eta}_{p}^{2}\) = 0.21), and TSK ( p < 0.001, \({\eta}_{p}^{2}\) = 0.15). However, only the reduction in kinesiophobia exceeded the published MCID, whereas improvements in the other psychosocial outcomes did not reach established thresholds for clinical relevance. Adding PNE to a structured NME program did not provide additional benefits for pain intensity or disability compared with NME alone. Although the combined intervention was associated with statistically significant improvements in several psychosocial outcomes, clinically meaningful benefit was demonstrated only for kinesiophobia. These psychosocial findings should therefore be interpreted cautiously, considering that they were secondary outcomes and that the trial was powered for the primary outcome. PNE may represent a useful adjunct to exercise-based rehabilitation when targeting movement-related fear. Trial Registration: IRCT20190427043384N2 (registered on 17 March 2023).
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: neuromuscular training; chronic low back pain; pain neuroscience education; exercise therapy

Article.Title: A generative adversarial network with enhanced feature extraction for intelligent interface generation
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Han P.
Article.Abstract: Automatic intelligent interface generation is a critical task in human-computer interaction, yet traditional generative models suffer from issues such as poor semantic consistency, insufficient component-level structural accuracy, and a trade-off between generation quality and computational efficiency. To address these challenges, this paper proposes DCS-GAN, a novel generative adversarial network tailored for intelligent interface generation. The model integrates three core modules with complementary functions: a ConvNeXt-Tiny-based feature extraction module for hierarchical interface representation learning, a DG parallel generation module to balance global layout optimization and component-level structural preservation, and an SE-AdaIN perceptual calibration module to enhance the consistency between generated interfaces and real samples in terms of perception and semantics. Comprehensive evaluations on the RICO and WebUI datasets demonstrate that DCS-GAN outperforms mainstream comparative models in generation quality, noise robustness, and computational efficiency. The model exhibits strong generalization ability across datasets and maintains stable performance under noisy input conditions, while achieving a favorable balance between generation efficiency and resource consumption. This work provides a feasible solution for high-quality and efficient automatic intelligent interface generation, and offers practical reference for the application of generative models in interface design scenarios.
Article.Topic: Generative Adversarial Networks and Image Synthesis

Article.Title: Urban living and dementia risk: associations with perceived green space qualities and traffic noise annoyance
Article.Authors: Alzhrani A.; Mattisson K.; Stockfelt L.; Xu Y.; Harari F.; Gustafsson S.; Björk J.; Nägga K.; Hansson O.; Oudin A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dementia is a major public health concern, and ambient air pollution is increasingly recognized as a plausible risk factor. Green space and traffic noise have also been proposed as environmental determinants of dementia but have received less attention. We examined whether novel, perception-based measures of urban green space and traffic noise annoyance were associated with dementia risk. We included around 30,250 participants from the Malmö Diet and Cancer cohort, followed from 1991 to 2014. Neighborhood-level perceptions of serenity, wilderness, and species richness (Perceived Sensory Dimensions [PSDs]), as well as road and train noise annoyance, were derived from regional surveys and linked to participants' annual residential addresses. We also constructed a combined PSD index as the sum of z-scores. Time-varying Cox models were used to estimate associations with clinically validated all-cause dementia (ACD), Alzheimer's disease (AD), and vascular dementia (VaD), adjusting for demographic, lifestyle, and health factors. In sensitivity analyses, we additionally adjusted for air pollution. Higher neighborhood PSDs were associated with lower risks of ACD and AD (ACD: hazard ratio [HR] per interquartile range [IQR] increase in the PSD index, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.88–0.99). Road traffic noise annoyance was associated with a higher risk of ACD (HR, 1.07; 95% CI, 1.00–1.14), whereas train noise annoyance showed no clear association. Patterns for VaD were similar but less precise. Neighborhoods perceived as more serene, wild, and species-rich were associated with lower dementia risk, while greater road traffic noise annoyance was associated with higher risk. These findings support the relevance of the residential environment for dementia risk and highlight the value of perception-based exposure measures in environmental epidemiology.

Article.Title: Green synthesis of copper oxide nanoparticles using Illicium verum Hook. f.: phytochemical characterization, apoptosis-mediated cytotoxicity activity, antioxidant potential, and metabolic enzyme inhibition
Article.Authors: Almutairi H.; Aljarba N.; Al-Otaibi W.; AlMotwaa S.; Soliman M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigated the plant-mediated synthesis, physicochemical characteristics, and in vitro biological activities of copper oxide nanoparticles (CuO NPs) prepared using an ethanolic extract of Illicium verum Hook. f. (star anise). GC–MS profiling showed anisaldehyde (29.83%), anethole (20.72%), and anisyl methyl ketone (12.84%) as the predominant volatile constituents, while the available HPLC records provided retention-time-based assignments and concentration estimates for phenolic and flavonoid compounds, with the highest estimated values reported for apigenin (2651.60 ppm), pyrocatechol (685.89 ppm), and quinic acid (481.70 ppm). The synthesized material was characterized using UV–Vis spectroscopy, FTIR, XRD, TEM, SEM–EDX, and elemental mapping. An absorption maximum was observed at 353 nm, and XRD analysis indicated predominantly crystalline monoclinic CuO with a mean crystallite size of 11.18 ± 1.00 nm. TEM analysis of 70 particles revealed predominantly spherical to quasi-spherical morphologies with a mean particle diameter of 25.75 ± 8.57 nm. The CuO NPs produced concentration-dependent cytotoxicity against SKOV3 ovarian cancer and Vero cells, with IC₅₀ values of 196.08 and 395.54 µg/mL, respectively, corresponding to a selectivity index of 2.02. Exploratory flow-cytometric analysis showed apoptosis-associated changes and an increased G2/M DNA-content population following treatment. RT-qPCR analysis showed increased relative expression of caspase-3 and BAX and decreased Bcl-2 expression. The CuO NPs also exhibited cell-free antioxidant activity, with DPPH and ABTS IC₅₀ values of 154.15 and 342.94 µg/mL, respectively. In addition, they inhibited α-amylase, α-glucosidase, and pancreatic lipase in vitro, with IC₅₀ values of 323.78, 234.17, and 257.86 µg/mL, respectively. These findings provide an integrated phytochemical, physicochemical, and preliminary biological evaluation of I. verum -mediated CuO NPs while emphasizing the need for additional mechanistic, safety, and independently replicated studies.

Article.Title: Evaluation of health and economic impacts of atmospheric PM₂.₅ in Tabriz, Iran, using BenMAP-CE and AirQ+
Article.Authors: Mohammadi A.; Vagheei R.; Ashrafi K.; Bayat R.; Firozjaee T.; Kardel F.
Article.Abstract: Air pollution poses a major threat to public health and carries the highest burden of environmentally related diseases. This study evaluated mortality associated with long-term exposure to PM₂.₅ and the corresponding economic burden in Tabriz city. The analysis was conducted using the BenMAP-CE and AirQ⁺ software. We evaluated five scenarios concerning the annual average PM₂.₅ concentration: increases to 35 and 25 µg/m³, decreases to 15 and 10 µg/m³, and a reduction to the theoretical minimum risk level of 2.4 µg/m³. Applying the Global Exposure Mortality Model (GEMM) to produce modelled estimates of attributable burden, we estimate that 886 deaths (95% CI: 814–935) among adults are associated with long-term exposure to PM₂.₅ at concentrations exceeding 2.4 µg/m³. Among these, the highest mortality was attributed to ischemic heart disease (435 deaths; 95% CI: 419–446), followed by stroke (102; 95% CI: 79–118), lower respiratory tract infections (71; 95% CI: 53–80), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (45; 95% CI: 33–53), and lung cancer (33; 95% CI: 28–36). This modelled mortality corresponds to an estimated loss of 14,086 years of life lost (YLL). Using a central value of statistical life (VSL) of USD381,212, the mortality-related economic burden was approximately USD338 million. A separate exploratory10% morbidity uplift gives approximately USD372 million; sensitivity to VSL income elasticity and mortality uncertainty is reported separately. These findings highlight the substantial health and economic benefits of improved air quality management in industrial cities. Keywords: Air pollution, PM 2.5 , Economic assessment, Health effects, BenMAP-CE, AirQ+.

Article.Title: A study on the configurational effects of multidimensional attributes on the continuance intentions of Chinese smart home app users
Article.Authors: Qi X.; Fan L.; Wu F.
Article.Abstract: Smart home apps are an important interface through which users manage devices and configure services. Users’ continuance intention may be associated with different combinations of experiential attributes. This study used a mixed-methods approach combining online review mining, PLS-SEM, and fsQCA. We extracted eight experiential attributes from 3,667 reviews and examined their relationships with user satisfaction and continuance intention using 553 survey responses. PLS-SEM showed that system operational stability ( β = 0.192) and smart scenario and service automation ( β = 0.183) were significantly positively associated with satisfaction, whereas the paths from visual aesthetics and interaction simplicity and from voice and multimodal interaction to satisfaction were not statistically significant. Satisfaction was significantly positively associated with continuance intention ( β = 0.775). The R ² values for satisfaction and continuance intention were 0.807 and 0.687, respectively. fsQCA identified 13 configurations associated with high continuance intention and grouped them into three patterns. All five pathways in Pattern 1 included the absence of commercial information intrusion (~ CII); the pathways in Pattern 2 did not specify whether CII was present or absent; and those in Pattern 3 included its presence. The necessity analysis identified no single necessary condition. These findings show that different combinations of attributes can be associated with high continuance intention, providing configurational evidence for understanding smart home app users’ continuance intention and informing differentiated design.

Article.Title: Accuracy evaluation of railway track irregularity inspection using bogie-mounted IMUs of different grades
Article.Authors: Guan Y.; Li H.; Wang H.; Sheng Y.; Chai J.; Chen Q.
Article.Abstract: Railway track irregularity inspection is critical for operational safety and ride comfort. As inspection time windows become increasingly constrained, onboard inspection systems mounted on in-service trains have attracted growing attention because they can improve inspection efficiency. In such systems, inertial measurement units (IMUs), when integrated with laser sensors, provide an effective solution for dynamic track geometry measurement, especially for high-grade IMUs. However, the high cost of high-grade IMUs limits large-scale deployment. In this study, we evaluated the measurement accuracy of onboard track irregularity inspection systems based on 2D laser sensors and IMUs of different grades, together with different processing schemes. The results show that, under the adopted semi-physical evaluation framework based on signal grafting and after constant bias calibration, the system combining a tactical-grade IMU with 2D laser sensors has the potential to achieve measurement accuracies for gauge, cross level, and lateral/vertical irregularities comparable to those obtained using a navigation-grade IMU, satisfying the requirements of the relevant Chinese national standards. For micro-electro-mechanical system (MEMS) IMUs integrated with the same laser sensors, the accuracy of cross level measurement is inherently constrained by attitude estimation accuracy. However, for the other track geometry parameters, acceptable measurement accuracy can still be maintained after removing constant biases and omitting attitude-based gravity compensation, which mitigates attitude-error amplification but should be regarded as a trade-off that may reduce waveform fidelity. These results clarify the achievable measurement capability of IMUs of different grades within the adopted semi-physical evaluation framework and provide practical guidance for the design of cost-effective onboard track irregularity inspection systems.

Article.Title: RNA processing factors are associated with microglial heterogeneity and intercellular communication in ischemic stroke
Article.Authors: Gong J.; He Y.; Zhang Y.; Xu J.; Lin H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ischemic stroke (IS) is a leading cause of death and long-term disability globally, with dysregulated RNA processing implicated in its pathogenesis. This study aimed to identify the key genes associated with RNA processing factors (RNAPF) in IS using integrated transcriptomic analyses. Microarray data from human blood (GSE16561 and GSE58294) and single-cell RNA sequencing data from mouse brain tissue (GSE174574) were analyzed. Candidate genes were screened via differential expression analysis and intersected with RNAPF-related genes. Machine learning algorithms identified feature genes, followed by diagnostic validation and functional characterization. Immune infiltration was characterized at the transcriptomic level, whereas cellular heterogeneity was examined at single-cell resolution. To avoid pseudoreplication, all statistical inferences from single-cell data were elevated to the biological replicate level (n = 3 per group). Cell type and microglial subtype proportions were compared using sample-aggregated Wilcoxon rank-sum tests. Using RT-qPCR technology, we conducted a preliminary assessment of expression differences in key genes in a small-scale clinical sample set (n = 5 per group), providing preliminary support for this bioinformatics finding. A total of 12 candidate RNA processing-related genes were identified, with RNASEL and SRPK1 established as potentially key genes via machine learning and validation cohorts. A nomogram integrating both genes demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy. Functional enrichment linked key genes to neuroinflammation pathways, such as Toll-like receptor and chemokine signaling. Immune dysregulation was observed, with RNASEL/SRPK1 positively correlating with M0 macrophages and neutrophils. Single-cell analysis revealed microglia as a cell type of interest. At the sample level (n = 3 per group), microglia showed a decreasing trend in IS (24.40% vs. 21.51%,). Microglial subtype analysis revealed a marked reduction in MG_Homeostatic_Slc2a5 (88.50% → 15.60%) and significant expansion of MG_IEG_Egr1 (3.75% → 46.74%) and MG_Postnatal-PAM_Spp1 (0.05% → 21.22%) in IS. Pseudobulk DESeq2 analysis demonstrated that RNASEL was significantly downregulated (log2FC = − 1.127, padj < 0.001) while SRPK1 was significantly upregulated (log2FC = 0.599, padj < 0.001) in IS microglia. Cell–cell communication analysis highlighted enhanced monocyte–microglia interactions. RT-qPCR analysis in a small but clinically characterized cohort (n = 5 per group) preliminarily supported the key gene-expression patterns observed in the bioinformatics analyses, although these findings require validation in larger cohorts. RNASEL and SRPK1 may serve as candidate RNAPFs whose altered expression is associated with immune dysregulation and microglial reprogramming in IS. Microglial subtype-specific changes and altered intercellular communication networks provide hypotheses for further mechanistic investigation.

Article.Title: Predicting hypertension risk using machine learning, deep learning, and quantum neural network models: a comparative evaluation
Article.Authors: Aslam M.; Xu S.; Hussain S.; Arif U.; Ibrahim M.; Saeed M.; Abiodun N.
Article.Abstract: Hypertension is a major public health problem and an important risk factor for cardiovascular disease. Early identification of patients at risk of hypertension can support timely prevention and clinical assessment. This study developed and compared statistical, machine learning, deep learning, and quantum neural network (QNN) models for hypertension prediction using clinical data from 624 patients at District Headquarters Hospital, Faisalabad, Pakistan. The proposed framework involved data preprocessing, K-nearest neighbor imputation, chi-square-based feature selection, feature scaling, and synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE) for class balancing. Logistic regression was used as a statistical reference, while SVM, random forest, XGBoost, Naive Bayes, ANN, SVM with PCA, DNN, and QNN were evaluated. Stratified 10-fold cross-validation was used to assess model performance using accuracy, F-measure, AUC, precision, recall, specificity, and maximum probability of correct decision (MPCD). The DNN model achieved the highest accuracy (95.77%), while the QNN achieved the highest AUC (95.40%), precision (96.26%), and recall (94.76%). Naive Bayes showed the lowest accuracy (83.40%). The QNN was included as an exploratory hybrid quantum-classical approach using a simulated quantum circuit, and the results do not imply a quantum advantage over classical models. Overall, the evaluated models showed promising predictive performance for hypertension classification in the study population. Further evaluation using independent populations, external validation, and prospective clinical studies is needed before considering their use in routine clinical practice.

Article.Title: Enhancing urban water resilience through green infrastructure in Kathmandu, Nepal
Article.Authors: Dhakal A.; Lim N.; Arifeen H.; Chowdhury M.
Article.Abstract: Rapidly growing cities in developing countries, including Kathmandu, Nepal, are struggling to handle water issues driven by both urban growth and climate change. Conventional grey infrastructure is unable to address the rising problems of flooding, polluted water, and declining groundwater recharge. This work evaluates how Green Infrastructure (GI) might help make Kathmandu Valley more sustainable and enhance ecosystem resilience through better water management. This study develops an integrated urban water resilience framework for Kathmandu Valley by combining geospatial analysis, hydrological modelling, field-based assessment of GI interventions, and stakeholder-driven policy evaluation. The interdisciplinary approach enables simultaneous examination of environmental performance, spatial vulnerability, and institutional implementation challenges associated with GI adoption in a rapidly urbanising Himalayan city. GI interventions reduced surface runoff by up to 40%, improved water quality by reducing nutrient loads (BOD, nitrate, phosphate) by over 60%, and mitigated urban heat by 3–4 °C. Spatial analysis identified priority zones for GI implementation along the Bagmati River corridor and in low-lying urban areas of Kathmandu Valley. Stakeholders expressed strong public support for GI initiatives but highlighted weak institutional coordination and limited maintenance capacity as major implementation challenges. This research helps build evidence for ecological adaptation and suggests useful steps to make Kathmandu’s infrastructure more resilient, livable, and ecologically adaptive.

Article.Title: Item analysis and evaluation on chronic obstructive pulmonary disease quality of life scale based on classical test theory and item response theory
Article.Authors: Wan K.; Qiao L.; Xiong Y.; Zhao Z.; Wu B.; Liu T.; Ren Y.; Wan C.
Article.Abstract: In recent years, the incidence of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) has been increasing and the quality of life of patients with COPD has received more and more attention. The QLICD-COPD (V2.0), a widely used quality of life scale for patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, warrants rigorous item-level analysis to evaluate its psychometric properties, and to inform future scale refinement and potential item reduction. 321 patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease were investigated by QLICD-COPD (V2.0) scale. The items of the QLICD-COPD (V2.0) scale was evaluated by some statistical methods based on CTT including correlation coefficient method, variance method, factor analysis method and Cronbach’s α coefficient method. Meanwhile, Samejima hierarchical response model of item response theory was utilized to calculate the difficulty, information amount and differentiation coefficient of each item in the scale. CTT results showed that 6 items failed meet at least three or more statistical requirements, including 5 items in the general module and 1 item in the disease specific module. IRT results showed that the range of item differentiation was 1.03 ~ 1.41, which was suitable. The difficulty coefficient increases monotonously with the increase of the difficulty level (B1→B4), and some items exceed the standard value range. The average information amount of each item ranges from 0.250 to 0.546. It concluded that most items of the QLICD-COPD (V2.0) scale have good performance and good differentiation, but a few items still need further revision.

Article.Title: PIM-like additive manufacturing and characterization of a MnZn ferrite magnetic core
Article.Authors: Sqalli G.; Martin V.; Gillon F.; Soupremanien U.; Najjar D.; Witz J.; Benabou A.; Hecquet M.
Article.Abstract: Additive manufacturing offers flexibility in terms of shapes, and currently enables the printing of a variety of materials for electrical engineering. This article presents the fabrication and magnetic characterization of a MnZn soft ferrite toroidal core produced by additive manufacturing. The parts are manufactured using the PIM-like process for which the 3D printing step is performed using powder filled polymer pellets. After debinding and sintering steps, a dense core with magnetic performance comparable to that of a conventional ferrite is obtained. The process is an original one for the production of soft ferrite parts. Microstructural and magnetic characterizations were carried out to obtain its grain size and main magnetic properties, i.e. its hysteresis loops and associated power losses as a function of induction and frequency. The evolution of the temperature behavior of the ferrite is also presented.

Article.Title: Quadruple isotope dilution versus conventional calibration methods for accurate urinary hippuric acid quantification with a synthesized isotopically labelled material
Article.Authors: Bodur S.; Atakol A.; Eroğlu K.; Günkara Ö.; Bakırdere S.
Article.Abstract: Hippuric acid is a key biomarker in toxicological and metabolic investigations. This study presents an accurate UHPLC-MS/MS method for the quantification of hippuric acid in urine matrix. A quadruple isotope dilution (ID 4 ) strategy was utilized to compensate possible matrix effects and variations in calibration and increase accuracy. Hippuric acid– d₅ was synthesized in-house from glycine and benzoyl chloride– d₅ , lowering material costs to easily affordable levels. The mass spectrometry and chromatographic parameters were optimized for improved sensitivity and separation. After the optimization experiments, the analytical performance of the UHPLC-MS/MS system was evaluated. The developed method exhibited a wide linear range from 55.80 ng/kg to 530.10 µg/kg, with limit of detection (LOD) of 15.6 ng/kg and limit of quantification (LOQ) of 52.1 ng/kg. The method was validated with a certified reference material and gradient spiked recovery runs in the same matrix, resulting in excellent agreement with the certified value and consistent recoveries. Results were put into comparison with more conventional techniques of external standard (ES) calibration and single–point isotopically labelled standard addition which demonstrated the superiority of the ID 4 method. The proposed method is intended as a candidate reference procedure for hippuric acid in urine, and it can be used to assign values to quality control and calibration materials for routine LC-MS/MS methods. In addition, the in-house synthesis of hippuric acid- d 5 makes this approach affordable for laboratories outside metrology institutes.

Article.Title: Zero-trust cybersecurity framework for AI-driven Energy Internet and smart grid systems
Article.Authors: Mumbaikar T.; Alohali M.; Sharma G.; Almutairi A.; Assiri M.; Nawaz M.
Article.Abstract: The Energy Internet extends the classical power grid into a densely interconnected system of distributed energy resources, advanced metering infrastructure, and machine-learning-driven control loops, and this extension enlarges the attack surface at the same rate that it improves efficiency. Perimeter-based security models, which implicitly trust any device or control message that has already crossed the substation firewall, are a poor match for this environment because a compromised remote terminal unit or a spoofed measurement stream sits, by construction, inside the perimeter. This paper develops a zero-trust cybersecurity framework for AI-driven Energy Internet and smart grid systems that treats every measurement, device, and control action as unverified until it is continuously re-evaluated. The framework combines four elements: a continuous trust-score recursion with an evidence-driven decay dynamic; an artificial-intelligence risk engine that fuses residual-based anomaly scores with a federated-learning classifier trained across substations without centralising raw telemetry; a tiered false-data-injection detector that partitions the network into observability zones and exploits tie-line flow measurements the attacker does not control, building on and extending an existing tiered detection and distributed partitioning method; and a policy decision engine, formalised as a Stackelberg game between defender and attacker, that converts trust and risk scores into access decisions. The framework is evaluated through reproducible simulations on the IEEE 14-, 30-, and 118-bus test systems, using a from-scratch alternating-current weighted least squares state estimator, physically grounded false-data-injection attacks restricted to a realistic compromised-measurement subset, and extensive Monte Carlo campaigns on each system. The results show a sharp, theoretically predicted transition in detectability governed by the ratio between the number of measurements an attacker controls and the redundancy of the measurement set; a consistent detection advantage for the tiered partitioned detector precisely in the narrow operating region attackers would rationally target; area under the receiver operating characteristic curve above 0.98 for the combined detector across all three test systems; sub-second state-estimation solve times even on the 118-bus system; and a trust-score policy engine whose false-revocation rate and detection delay trade off predictably with the memory parameter of the trust recursion.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: energy internet; smart grid; zero-trust security; cybersecurity framework; artificial intelligence
Article.TopicFields: Engineering > Control and Systems Engineering > Smart Grid Security and Resilience; Social Sciences > Sociology and Political Science > Access Control and Trust; Computer Science > Computer Networks and Communications > Cybersecurity and Information Systems

Article.Title: Coupling coordination relationship and optimization strategies of tourism industry and human settlement environment in Xinjiang
Article.Authors: Zhang F.; Hou J.; Sun G.
Article.Abstract: Xinjiang is characterized by a typical arid–oasis geographical setting, with complex interactions between tourism development and improvements in the human settlement environment. Taking 14 prefecture-level administrative units in Xinjiang as the study units, this study constructs panel data on the tourism industry and human settlement environment from 2013 to 2025. The entropy weighting method, coupling coordination degree model, spatial autocorrelation analysis, and obstacle degree model are employed to examine the spatiotemporal characteristics and obstacle factors of coordinated development between the two systems. The results show that: (1) From 2013 to 2025, the overall development levels of Xinjiang’s tourism industry and human settlement environment improved, although pronounced regional disparities remained. (2) The coupling coordination degree increased from 0.2406 in 2013 to 0.3512 in 2025. During the COVID-19 pandemic period, most regions experienced fluctuations, with the tourism industry system exhibiting greater variation than the human settlement environment system. (3) Spatial analysis indicates that no significant overall spatial clustering pattern has formed across Xinjiang, although local high-value clusters are present in Urumqi and its neighboring areas. (4) Indicators including the urban water supply coverage rate, urban sewage treatment rate, passenger turnover, operating revenue of catering enterprises above the designated size, and inbound tourism revenue consistently rank among the major obstacle factors, with differences in obstacle characteristics across regions. This study concludes that the coordinated development of Xinjiang’s tourism industry and human settlement environment is jointly influenced by resource and environmental conditions, regional development foundations, and the operational capacity of the tourism industry. Accordingly, regional differences should be taken into account when improving infrastructure, enhancing the quality and efficiency of the tourism industry, and implementing differentiated optimization strategies.

Article.Title: Real time small target fire detection in photovoltaic plants using attention enhanced multiscale fusion
Article.Authors: Guo W.; Meng X.; Wang J.; Cai C.; Cui H.
Article.Abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power plants concentrate flammable polymers and arc-prone electrical components, making early fire detection a safety-critical condition-monitoring task. Yet incipient fires appear as small, weakly contrasted smoke or flame, while specular reflections from glossy module surfaces fabricate fire-like cues, jointly degrading conventional detectors. We cast this as an applied computational-intelligence problem and propose PVFire-YOLO, a real-time neural detection framework. A patch-aware parallel attention block amplifies weak small-target responses against reflective backgrounds; a gather-and-distribute neck performs intelligent information fusion across four feature-pyramid levels to close the semantic gap of conventional necks; and a four-scale adaptive spatial feature-fusion head learns per-pixel scale weights, adding a high-resolution branch for sub-100-pixel targets. To enable training and evaluation, we built PV-Fire, the first annotated flame-and-smoke corpus with a PV-specific background distribution. Against fourteen baseline detectors, PVFire-YOLO attains 87.4% mean average precision at intersection-over-union 0.5 on PV-Fire and 84.4% on the public D-Fire benchmark, raises small-target average precision by 5.2 points over its baseline, and lowers the reflection-induced false-positive rate to 3.1% at higher recall. It runs at 79 and 21 frames per second on a desktop graphics card and an embedded edge device, supporting real-time deployment.

Article.Title: Spatial patterns and environmental suitability of traditional Tibetan villages in Ganzi Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, China
Article.Authors: Liu X.; Li X.; Zhang B.; Li Y.; Ran D.
Article.Abstract: The acceleration of global urbanization and industrialization since the 20th century has drawn increasing attention to the quality of human settlements. Ganzi Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture, located on the southeastern Tibetan Plateau, is characterized by rugged terrain, fragile ecosystems, and cultural diversity. Its traditional villages exhibit strong adaptation to local environmental conditions in site selection, spatial configuration, and construction practices; however, rapid modernization and environmental change have increasingly affected their spatial distribution and living conditions. In this study, 274 traditional villages listed by the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development and the Sichuan Provincial Government were selected as research samples. An integrated framework combining spatial pattern analysis, environmental suitability assessment, and factor detection analysis was applied. ArcGIS spatial analysis, multi-index evaluation, and the GeoDetector model were employed to examine spatial distribution patterns, environmental suitability, and associated factors. The results indicate that traditional villages in Ganzi are significantly clustered, forming a “two cores–multiple scattered points” pattern, primarily concentrated in Danba and Litang. Clear inter-county disparities are observed, showing a general “south-dense and north-sparse” tendency. Most villages are located in unsuitable, critical, or low-suitability zones, accounting for 63.60% of the total sample. GeoDetector results indicate that the Temperature–Humidity Index shows the strongest individual association with village clustering intensity, while the interaction between the Temperature–Humidity Index and Water Resources Index exhibits the highest explanatory power (q = 0.518). The Land Cover Index shows no statistically significant association (q = 0.035, p = 0.214). These findings are robust under different weighting scenarios with ± 20% parameter perturbation. This study provides empirical evidence on the spatial patterns of traditional Tibetan villages and their relationships with environmental conditions in a high-altitude region.

Article.Title: Optimized reversible QCA full adder subtractor for low latency and energy efficiency
Article.Authors: Kumar A.; Ganesh C.; Kumar S.; Priyanka S.; Kumar V.; Tripathi S.
Article.Abstract: Quantum-dot Cellular Automata (QCA) offer a promising beyond-CMOS platform for ultra-low-power and high-density nanoscale logic. However, existing reversible full adder/subtractor (FA/FS) designs typically suffer from high cell count, multilayer routing, multiple garbage outputs, and increased latency, limiting their practical integration into larger reversible systems. This paper presents a compact and fully reversible QCA-based FA/FS architecture constructed using a Feynman gate and a Reversible Quantum Gate (RQG), both optimized for single-layer implementation. The proposed design minimizes overhead by requiring only one constant input and producing a single garbage output while avoiding complex wire-crossing structures through the use of rotated cells. To demonstrate scalability, a 2-bit FA/FS architecture is also developed by cascading the proposed 1-bit unit. Functional verification was performed using QCADesigner, and energy dissipation was evaluated using QCAPro. The comparative analysis demonstrated that the proposed reversible FA/FS architecture provides substantial improvements over state-of-the-art reversible FA/FS designs. Specifically, the proposed circuit achieves reductions of up to 70.1% in cell count, 75% in occupied area, 57.14% in latency, and 95.4% in computational cost. In addition, the proposed architecture exhibits the lowest leakage energy and switching energy among the considered designs across the evaluated operating conditions. These improvements indicate enhanced area and computational efficiency while reducing energy-related overheads. These results highlight the suitability of the proposed FA/FS unit for future energy-efficient QCA-based arithmetic and logic systems.

Article.Title: Environment-adaptive Acoustic–Optical sensing for fish abundance estimation in complex aquaculture waters
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Cheng X.; Lu Y.; Zhao Q.; Zhu H.; Wang Y.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reliable fish abundance estimation is essential for the operation and management of aquaculture systems, but remains challenging under turbidity, bubble interference, target occlusion, and acoustic reverberation. This study develops an Acoustic–Optical fusion sensing framework for robust fish monitoring in complex aquaculture waters. An environment-aware geometric fusion network, termed EAGF-Net, is proposed to integrate optical appearance information with sonar-derived geometric features. The network employs modality-specific feature extraction with an orthogonality constraint, sonar-guided spatial compensation, and adaptive gating to regulate modality contributions according to environmental conditions. Asymmetric cross-attention is further introduced to reduce semantic inconsistency and suppress unreliable acoustic or optical responses. For densely distributed fish, a keypoint-based topological association method uses fish-eye features and geometric constraints to separate overlapping individuals. The resulting observations are incorporated into Kalman-filter-based trajectory management to reduce missed and repeated counts. Fish abundance is then inferred by combining trajectory flux with the effective sensing volume determined by the Acoustic–Optical field of view and survey path. Experiments covering clear water, dense schooling, turbidity, and bubble disturbance show that the proposed fusion network achieves an F-measure of 0.924 and an average counting accuracy of 96.40%. Field-scale tests in eight aquaculture ponds estimate 1,939 fish against a reference count of 1,975, corresponding to a relative error of 1.80%. These results demonstrate the potential of environment-adaptive Acoustic–Optical sensing for non-invasive fish abundance monitoring in aquaculture engineering applications.

Article.Title: Admission-time prediction of hospital length of stay in diverticular disease using explainable machine learning models
Article.Authors: Güneri G.; Dandıl E.; Andıç K.; Ünal M.; Emre Ö.; Çorbacı K.; Kurular D.; Gönüllü M.
Article.Abstract: Acute diverticulitis (AD) is a leading cause of emergency department admissions and hospitalizations worldwide. Accurately predicting hospital length of stay (LOS) at the time of admission is essential for optimizing the utilization of resources, planning discharges and managing patients. The aim of this study was to develop and validate an explainable machine learning framework for predicting LOS at the time of admission in patients with diverticulitis and diverticulosis. A retrospective dataset comprising 148 hospitalized patients was analyzed. Advanced feature engineering techniques were applied, including interaction terms, nonlinear transformations, logarithmic scaling and clinically derived inflammatory indices. Multiple regression-based and machine learning model such as Linear Regression, Ridge Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost and a Voting Regressor ensemble were trained using log-transformed LOS values. Model performance was evaluated using five-fold cross-validation, bootstrap-based stability analysis, calibration assessment, SHAP-based explainability and Kaplan-Meier-based risk stratification. The mean LOS was 2.08 ± 2.5 days. Tree-based ensemble models demonstrated better predictive performance compared to linear models. XGBoost performed best in the full cohort (mean absolute error (MAE) = 0.03; R² = 0.99), while Random Forest and ensemble approaches showed comparable or improved performance in the diverticulitis subgroup with MAE of 0.74 and R² of 0.77. XGBoost showed exceptionally high apparent performance in the full cohort. However, stricter internal validation produced more conservative estimates. Patient-level nested out-of-fold (OOF) evaluation resulted in an R² of approximately 0.57, while bootstrap optimism correction yielded an optimism-corrected R² of 0.8314 and MAE of 0.3512 days. SHAP analysis indicated that Hinchey class and inflammatory characteristics contributed substantially to model predictions. Calibration and residual analyses indicated acceptable agreement between predicted and observed LOS, while prediction intervals provided clinically relevant uncertainty estimates. Subgroup analysis revealed decreased predictive performance and increased variability, reflecting the challenges associated with reduced sample size and heterogeneity. Combining explainable machine learning with clinically informed feature engineering provides a promising framework for estimating LOS at the time of admission for diverticular disease. However, the more conservative nested cross-validation results highlight the need for larger, independent cohorts in order to establish the generalizability and potential utility of the proposed approach.

Article.Title: Enhancing energy efficiency and thermal comfort in residential towers through multi-objective optimization and energy hub systems
Article.Authors: Moazzen E.; Zare-Anbouhi M.; Hayati M.; Guarino F.; Abapour M.; Haghparast F.
Article.Abstract: Existing high-rise residential buildings often exhibit high energy consumption and inadequate thermal comfort, while building retrofit decisions are rarely coordinated with subsequent district-scale energy-system operation. This study develops a two-stage framework that links building retrofit optimization with multi-energy hub scheduling. First, a validated EnergyPlus model of a residential unit in a 17-story tower is coupled with NSGA-II to optimize insulation, glazing, external shading, and heating and cooling setpoints with simultaneous consideration of energy use and thermal comfort. The model is validated against three years of measured electricity and natural-gas consumption, with deviations of − 6.18%, − 2.87%, and + 1.49% for 2022–2024, respectively. The selected retrofit solution reduces annual energy consumption from 33,336.28 kWh to 28,384.04 kWh (14.85%) and decreases the average predicted percentage dissatisfied (PPD) from 29.51 to 18.69%. Second, the optimized demand profile is scaled to 816 residential units and integrated into a MILP-based energy hub incorporating CCHP generation, renewable energy, electrical and thermal storage, and demand response. Relative to the baseline, storage reduces operating cost by 12.14%, while storage combined with demand response achieves a 19.90% reduction. The results demonstrate that coordinating long-term retrofit decisions with short-term multi-energy scheduling can simultaneously improve building efficiency, thermal comfort, and district-scale operational flexibility.

Article.Title: An MMD-weighted ensemble for multi-source cross-domain intrusion detection in heterogeneous IoT systems
Article.Authors: Liu C.; Yi T.; Jing X.; Ling Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cross-domain intrusion detection is essential for securing heterogeneous Internet of Things (IoT) deployments. However, detectors trained in one environment degrade sharply under domain shift, which arises from systematic differences in protocols, device types, and network architectures across IoT domains. Existing approaches typically focus on single-domain training or require explicit feature alignment, both of which limit practical deployment. To address this, this paper presents a systematic multi-domain benchmark on a public IoT adaptation dataset comprising 7,000 labeled traffic samples with 39 features spanning six domains, and proposes the Maximum Mean Discrepancy-Weighted Ensemble (MMD-WE), a multi-source ensemble that weights per-domain XGBoost classifiers by Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD)-derived similarity scores without any explicit feature alignment. CORAL (Correlation Alignment), a widely used second-order domain adaptation method, serves as a baseline for comparison. In-domain detection reaches 92.86% accuracy and an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.9825; single-source cross-domain transfer yields off-diagonal accuracies ranging from 89.6% to 93.7%; and in leave-one-domain-out multi-source adaptation, MMD-WE attains 92.80% average accuracy, marginally exceeding a pooled multi-source baseline of 92.69% and significantly outperforming a CORAL-aligned variant of 92.22%. Analysis with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) further shows that adaptation-aware features, led by communication reliability and payload entropy, dominate predictions, and that the dataset’s adaptation status stratifies risk: attack prevalence rises from 2.9% under low shift to 81.8% under high shift. These findings support shift-aware alert triage and label-free deployment of robust IoT intrusion detectors.

Article.Title: Flawed policies in dam construction and their hydropolitical ramifications: a case study of the Atatürk Dam
Article.Authors: Bozorg-Haddad O.; Moghaddam N.; Salar-Khorasani S.; Loáiciga H.
Article.Abstract: Large dams can produce significant environmental, geological, and geopolitical impacts, particularly in transboundary river basins. This study examines the Atatürk Dam on the Euphrates River, one of the largest components of Turkey’s Southeastern Anatolia Project (GAP), to evaluate its potential geological, environmental, and governance implications across the Euphrates and Tigris basin. An integrated analytical framework was employed by combining seismological analysis, satellite-based land use assessment, and governance evaluation. Historical seismic records (1905 to 2020) were analyzed to investigate potential reservoir-induced seismicity, while remote sensing data (2001 to 2023) were used to assess long-term land cover changes. Governance performance was evaluated using indicators aligned with the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) water governance principles, including transparency, stakeholder participation, accountability, and transboundary coordination. Results suggest that reservoir impoundment may have contributed to increased pore pressure and reduced fault stability, correlating with increased seismic activity in the region, including two moderate earthquakes (Mw 5.5 and 5.1) recorded after 2004. Remote sensing analyses reveal significant environmental transformations across the basin between 2001 and 2023, including a 30 to 40% reduction in vegetation cover, an 88% decline in evergreen needleleaf forests, a 33% loss of mixed forests, and a decrease of more than 15,000 km 2 of croplands. Concurrently, barren lands expanded by more than 33,000 km 2 , indicating accelerating land degradation trends. Downstream impacts include reduced water availability and associated ecological and agricultural stress in Syria and Iraq. Governance assessment further indicates systemic weaknesses in transparency, data sharing, environmental compliance, and formal transboundary agreements, suggesting that institutional limitations may amplify environmental and political pressures within the basin. The findings highlight the importance of integrating seismic risk assessment, environmental sustainability, and cooperative transboundary water governance in large-scale hydraulic infrastructure planning. The Atatürk Dam provides an important case study illustrating how large dam projects may generate complex environmental and governance challenges when implemented without sufficiently integrated regional risk management.

Article.Title: Integrated microbiome and metabolomic analysis reveals associations between vaginal microbiota composition and psychological profiles
Article.Authors: Castellano P.; Conti S.; Foschi C.; Djusse M.; Camboni T.; Ceccarani C.; Consolandi C.; Severgnini M.; Laghi L.; Prinelli F.; Marangoni A.; Mazzetti M.
Article.Abstract: The vaginal microbiota plays a key role in women’s health and is increasingly linked to psychobiological processes, although underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study investigated the relationship between vaginal community state types (CSTs), psychological dimensions, and vaginal metabolites in 105 reproductive-aged women. Vaginal microbiota composition was characterised through 16 S rRNA gene sequencing and classified into CSTs; metabolomic profiling was performed using NMR spectroscopy. Participants completed validated questionnaires assessing trait anxiety, emotion regulation, behavioural inhibition/activation, depressive symptoms, perceived stress, and somatisation. Women with polymicrobial CST IV profiles showed significantly lower Behavioural Activation System (BAS)-Reward Responsiveness and BAS-Drive scores, whereas those with Lactobacillus iners -dominated CST III exhibited lower Behavioural Inhibition System (BIS) scores. Limited direct correlations between bacterial taxa and psychological variables emerged, but psychological dimensions strongly correlated with specific vaginal metabolites. Exploratory mediation analyses indicated that aminobutyrate and valine partially or fully mediated the associations between CST IV and BAS dimensions, while phenylalanine partially mediated the relationship between CST IV and BIS inhibition. These findings suggest that the vaginal metabolome may represent a functional interface linking microbial community structure and psychological functioning, supporting a biopsychosocial perspective of vaginal health and the importance of integrating microbiome, metabolomic, and psychological assessments in women’s health research.

Article.Title: Matrigel scaffold, alone or with human placenta-derived mesenchymal stromal cells, improves histological repair of murine excisional wounds
Article.Authors: Saeedifar R.; Darehbagh R.; Jafarian A.; Moradveisi B.; Parvizpour F.
Article.Abstract: Impaired cutaneous wound healing remains a major clinical challenge, particularly when excessive inflammation disrupts tissue regeneration and extracellular matrix remodeling. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs; the term recommended by the International Society for Cell & Gene Therapy in preference to “mesenchymal stem cells”) have been proposed as therapeutic agents on the basis of their immunomodulatory and paracrine properties. Human placenta-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (hPMSCs) are of particular interest because of their accessibility, proliferative capacity and low reported immunogenicity. Whether their benefit in cutaneous wounds is attributable to the cells themselves, to the delivery vehicle, or to both, has not been resolved. In this preclinical study, two full-thickness excisional wounds were created on the dorsum of female BALB/c mice and treated by intradermal injection with hPMSCs alone, hPMSCs incorporated within a Matrigel scaffold, Matrigel alone, or vehicle (DMEM) control. Separate cohorts were euthanized on days 7, 14 and 21 post-wounding ( n = 5 mice, 10 wounds, per group per time point). Wound repair was assessed by histological and histomorphometric analysis of haematoxylin and eosin and Masson’s trichrome-stained sections. Collagen density was quantified morphometrically from Masson’s trichrome-stained sections, and re-epithelialization was graded on a five-point ordinal scale. Inflammatory cell infiltration and skin appendage regeneration were described qualitatively and were not quantified; inflammatory cells were not counted, and serial macroscopic wound-area measurements were not performed. Serum interleukin-10 (IL-10), interleukin-17 (IL-17) and interferon-γ (IFN-γ) were measured by ELISA on days 7, 14 and 21 as indices of the systemic inflammatory response. All three treatments improved histological repair relative to vehicle control. At day 21, collagen density was 86.1 ± 7.5% in the hPMSC + Matrigel group, compared with 77.8 ± 6.6% for Matrigel alone, 68.4 ± 5.1% for hPMSCs alone and 45.1 ± 4.1% for vehicle control. Across the three time points, the improvement in collagen density observed with Matrigel alone was 80–93% as large as the combination-versus-vehicle difference when the group means were compared descriptively. Adding hPMSCs to the scaffold gave a modest further increase of 5.8, 3.8 and 8.3% points at days 7, 14 and 21, which remained significant after Bonferroni adjustment only at day 7. The combination showed the highest re-epithelialization grade and the most organized dermal architecture on qualitative histological assessment at day 21. Systemically, hPMSC administration was associated with elevated serum IL-10 and reduced IFN-γ relative to control, with little difference in IL-17. In this model, a Matrigel scaffold improved histological wound repair relative to vehicle; adding hPMSCs to the scaffold gave a modest further increase in collagen density, and the combination performed best of the conditions tested. Because the study includes no non-MSC cellular control, the incremental benefit of the cells over the scaffold cannot be attributed specifically to hPMSC identity; and because no local (wound-bed) immunological or angiogenic analysis was performed, the accompanying serum cytokine changes represent a systemic association rather than a demonstrated local immunomodulatory mechanism. These findings should be regarded as an initial preclinical observation supporting combined cell–scaffold delivery, which requires confirmation with an appropriate cellular control and direct assessment of the wound microenvironment.

Article.Title: Effects of vertebral shortening during corrective osteotomy for spinal deformity on spinal cord biomechanics and cerebrospinal fluid-anterior spinal artery fluid-structure interaction
Article.Authors: Yusufu A.; Abulaiti A.; Haibier A.; Ma Y.
Article.Abstract: Corrective osteotomy for severe spinal deformity requires vertebral shortening, but the safe degree of shortening remains uncertain. This study used fluid-structure interaction finite element analysis to investigate how graded vertebral shortening affects cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) dynamics and anterior spinal artery (ASA) perfusion. A three-dimensional T1-T12 model was reconstructed from computed tomography data obtained from a 16-year-old male with scoliosis. Posterior vertebral column resection at T8/T9 was simulated in four conditions: no shortening and shortening by one-third, one-half, and two-thirds. Coupled CSF-dura and blood-vessel wall models were used to quantify pressure, wall shear stress, flow velocity, structural stress, and displacement. With shortening of up to one-half, CSF wall shear stress (~ 0.04 Pa) and velocity (~ 0.014 m/s) remained stable, whereas ASA luminal pressure and velocity declined gradually together with vessel-wall stress and displacement, indicating preserved hemodynamic compensation and mechanical unloading. At two-thirds shortening, CSF wall shear stress (0.4998 Pa) and velocity (0.16009 m/s) increased by approximately 12-fold and 11-fold, respectively; dural stress increased by approximately 34%, whereas displacement increased by only 1.2%, demonstrating nonlinear stress-displacement decoupling. ASA luminal pressure, velocity, vessel-wall stress, and displacement also rebounded to their highest values. In this patient-specific model, shortening up to one-half was associated with relative stability of CSF dynamics and progressive vascular unloading, whereas two-thirds shortening produced marked nonlinear changes in CSF and ASA-related biomechanical variables. These findings suggest a model-derived biomechanical transition between one-half and two-thirds shortening; however, this transition should not be interpreted as a clinically validated safety threshold.

Article.Title: Enhanced CO2 absorption and reduced regeneration energy in Si-ZIF-8/Sulfinol-M nanofluid: experimental and thermodynamic evaluation with data-driven modeling
Article.Authors: Bahadori M.; Shokouhi M.; Golhosseini R.; Zoghi A.
Article.Abstract: The study investigated the CO 2 absorption/desorption characteristics of a nanofluid comprising Sulfinol-M (base solvent), γ-Al 2 O 3 nanoparticles (0.1 wt. %), super actived carbon (SAC) (0.1 wt. %), and silica-2-methylimidazole zinc salt (Si-ZIF-8; 0.02 wt. %). Experiments were conducted by a static method at T = 313.15, 323.15, 333.15, and 393.15 K and pressures up to 1.2 MPa. The results show that all three nanofluids increase absorption capacity; notably, Si‑ZIF‑8 nanoparticles exhibited average enhancement factors of approximately 40% at 323.15 K and 44% at 333.15 K. Desorption studies at 393.15 K showed poor performance for SAC and γ-Al 2 O 3 nanoparticles, while Si-ZIF-8 nanoparticles successfully reduced CO 2 loading by 22%. The ΔH abs values were determined by the Clausius–Clapeyron equation. Accordingly, the heat of CO 2 absorption for Si-ZIF-8 base nanofluid exhibited 21% reductions at a loading of 1 wt.% compared to the base solvent. Furthermore, data modeling by genetic programming yeilded an average absolute relative deviation ( AARD ) of 10.8%, a root-mean-square error ( RMSE ) of 0.042, and a coefficient of determination of R 2 = 0.979.

Article.Title: Anthropogenic groundwater declines may exert far-reaching climatic impacts
Article.Authors: Paldor A.; Paldor N.
Article.Abstract: Past studies of climate change focused on effects such as greenhouse gas emissions, land-use changes, and ocean circulation. From the hydrogeological standpoint, several other studies have examined the impact of climatic changes on groundwater. However, the reverse impacts, of groundwater exploitation on climate, remain unexplored. We hypothesize that when shallow groundwater tables decline, evaporative heat loss diminishes, which leads to ground surface temperature increase. We explore this effect theoretically by developing a novel, physics-based framework that quantifies the relationship between groundwater declines and the resulting surface temperature increase. We further perform geospatial analyses to map and quantify the scale and scope of shallow groundwater declines in the contiguous United States. Results show that groundwater table declines from the surface to depths of order 1 m could have a potent heating effect of over ten degrees, depending on porosity. The geospatial analysis suggests a spatial correlation between regions where such declines have been occurring on decadal scales, and temperature rises. Particularly, California and Florida are found to be regions of excess vulnerability to this effect. These results may have far-reaching implications for the future of climate-change research and for groundwater management worldwide.

Article.Title: Cleistanthin A and diphyllin derivatives as putative EGFR-binding compounds: an integrated computational and biophysical study
Article.Authors: Panasawatwong B.; Lohawittayanan D.; Chabang N.; Charoensutthivarakul S.; Kuhaudomlarp S.; Munyoo B.; Tuchinda P.; Morales N.; Mangmool S.; Reabroi S.; Sanvarinda P.; Nutho B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cleistanthin A (CTA) is an arylnaphthalide lignan glycoside that exhibits anticancer activities through diverse molecular mechanisms. This study used an integrated computer-aided drug design (CADD) workflow, including target prediction, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, binding free-energy calculations, and surface plasmon resonance (SPR), to identify a potential molecular target for CTA and its derivatives. SwissTargetPrediction identified protein kinases as potential molecular targets. Molecular docking against targetable non-small cell lung cancer-associated kinases revealed that CTA and its derivatives exhibited stronger binding to wild-type EGFR than erlotinib. MD simulations indicated the stability of the protein–ligand complexes, whereas Molecular Mechanics Poisson-Boltzmann (generalized Born) Surface Area (MM/PB(GB)SA) analyses identified van der Waals interactions as the primary driving force for binding at the ATP-binding pocket. Incorporation of a benzoyl ester moiety to this pharmacophore increased nonpolar binding energy contribution. SPR confirmed concentration-dependent binding of CTA, MUC-853, MUC-858, Compound 1, and Compound 2 to the EGFR kinase domain, with Compound 1 and MUC-858 exhibiting good dissociation constants (K D ) of 6.4 and 9.5 µM, respectively. Collectively, these findings denote arylnaphthalide lignans as a potential scaffold for EGFR-targeted drug discovery and provide structure–interaction insights for rational design of inhibitors with improved potency and selectivity.

Article.Title: An explainable and fair TabNet framework for remote employee performance prediction using multidimensional workplace data
Article.Authors: Zhu Z.; Wei G.; Bian X.; Yu S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The prediction of performance by remote employees has become more important as organizations try to make their workforce data-driven when distributed. Existing approaches, however, tend to be non-interpretable, non-robust, and non-fair. In this study, an Explainable TabNet Framework for predicting employee performance remotely from a workforce dataset with 100,000 employee records is proposed. This framework incorporates attention-based deep tabular learning, explainability through SHAP values, robustness evaluation via cross-validation, statistical significance testing, and fairness auditing of subgroups in this field. Multiple regression analysis metrics were computed for the predictive performance of the model and compared with four other baselines: Linear Regression, Ridge Regression, Random Forest, Extra Trees, Gradient Boosting, Model XGBoost and LightGBM. The proposed framework outperformed all baseline models with better predictive performance, as evident in the R 2 score, RMSE, MAE, and PCC values, which were 0.9880, 0.1549, 0.1223, and 0.9956, respectively. The most significant predictors of employee performance as determined by ex-ante analysis were employee satisfaction, monthly salary, project involvement, participation in training, and tenure in the organization. Cross-validation and statistical testing ensured model robustness and significance, and fairness testing confirmed that the prediction was similar across groups of demographic and organizational individuals. The Explainable TabNet Framework is an accurate, interpretable, robust, and fair solution for employee performance prediction in remote work, which will enable transparent workforce analytics and human resource decision making based on evidence.

Article.Title: FTO-mediated m6A regulation modulates hepatic stellate cell activation through the IGF2BP1–TRIB3 axis and mitochondrial homeostasis
Article.Authors: Guo H.; Li Y.; Li C.; Duan H.; Mao J.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Liver fibrosis represents a critical pathological stage in chronic liver diseases, though its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood—particularly the role of N 6-methyladenosine (m6A) methylation. This study investigates the mechanism by which the m6A demethylase fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) regulates hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation and liver fibrosis. A murine liver fibrosis model was established using bile duct ligation (BDL), and human hepatic stellate LX-2 cells were transfected with specific shRNAs or overexpression plasmids to modulate FTO and IGF2BP1 expression. Techniques included histology (H&E, Sirius Red, Masson’s trichrome), immunohistochemistry (IHC), immunofluorescence, Western blotting, qRT-PCR, RNA dot blot, MeRIP-qPCR, and mitochondrial functional assays to assess collagen deposition, HSC activation, m6A methylation levels, and mitophagy. BDL mice exhibited significant inflammatory infiltration and collagen deposition, indicating HSC activation. Western blot and qPCR revealed downregulated FTO expression in HSCs. FTO deficiency promoted HSC activation by elevating m6A levels, increasing expression of α-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA), collagen type I (Collagen I), and transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β). Mechanistically, FTO depletion was associated with increased TRIB3 expression through an m6A–insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding protein 1 (IGF2BP1)-dependent regulatory mechanism, accompanied by mitochondrial dysfunction, mitophagy-related alterations, and HSC activation. These findings suggest that dysregulation of the FTO–m6A–IGF2BP1–TRIB3 axis contributes to hepatic stellate cell activation and liver fibrosis, highlighting this pathway as a potential target for epigenetic intervention and the development of mechanism-based therapeutic strategies for liver fibrosis.
