Article.Title: The relationship between genetic bone mineral density and spinal stenosis: a Mendelian randomization and cohort study
Article.Authors: Adegbenro T.; Carr M.; He J.; Polimanti R.; Margetis K.
Article.Abstract: To evaluate whether genetic liability to higher bone mineral density (BMD) is associated with spinal stenosis and primary lumbar decompression surgery. We integrated two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR), multivariable MR, MRlap, reverse MR, and longitudinal UK Biobank analyses. The primary exposure was UK Biobank heel estimated BMD (eBMD); lumbar spine and total body DXA BMD were evaluated as sensitivity exposures. The primary outcome was FinnGen R12 spinal stenosis (26,090 cases; 353,224 controls), and decompression GWAS summary statistics were generated in UK Biobank (1,215 cases; 155,913 controls). Multivariable MR adjusted for body mass index and height. Cox models included 157,128 European-ancestry UK Biobank participants with valid baseline heel eBMD. Genetically proxied higher heel eBMD was associated with stenosis before (OR = 1.097, 95% CI: 1.01–1.191, p = 0.028) and after (OR = 1.09, 95% CI: 1.010–1.175, p = 0.026) MR-PRESSO outlier removal. The final instruments included 462 independent SNPs with mean F-statistic 46.3. Associations persisted after adjustment for BMI and height. Lumbar spine BMD showed stronger associations with stenosis (IVW OR = 1.23, 95% CI: 1.14–1.33, p < 0.001), but reverse MR also associated stenosis liability with higher lumbar BMD, suggesting local remodeling or disease-site contamination. Heel eBMD was not associated with decompression in MRlap, and lumbar BMD was similarly non-significant. Observationally, baseline heel eBMD was modestly associated with incident stenosis (HR = 1.04, 95% CI: 1.00-1.09, p = 0.037), but not decompression. Higher genetically proxied BMD was associated with lumbar stenosis but not decompression. Findings support skeletal remodeling biology as a contributor to stenosis susceptibility while highlighting surgery as a downstream clinical endpoint.

Article.Title: Multi-scale vision transformer model with UAV-based hyperspectral imagery for early identification of pine wilt disease infected trees
Article.Authors: Shi H.; Zhang R.; Chen M.; Liu H.; Zhang D.; Chen L.
Article.Abstract: Pine Wilt Disease (PWD), caused by the pine wood nematode ( Bursaphelenchus xylophilus ), is a devastating forest disease characterized by rapid spread and high mortality. During its pathogenesis, the green attack and early stage are critical for disease control. However, RGB UAV images lack obvious visual features at these stages, which limits the accuracy of existing identification methods. This study aims to develop a Multi-Scale Vision Transformer Model specifically designed for UAV hyperspectral data. The primary objectives are to improve the identification capability for the green attack and early stages of PWD. To accurately capture subtle changes in the spectral and spatial features of pine trees during the green attack stage, an efficient spectral-spatial feature fusion module was designed. Meanwhile, an improved Gaussian self-attention mechanism was introduced to enhance the modeling of spectral differences between central pixels and their neighboring pixels. Furthermore, by integrating a lightweight Transformer architecture with a multi-scale feature pyramid, the proposed method not only fuses features ranging from the pixel level to the canopy level but also reduces the number of parameters. Experiment results show that the model achieves an identification accuracy of 87.40% and 88.21% for the green attack stage and the early stage of PWD, respectively. The model achieves an OA of 87.90% and a Kappa coefficient of 83.25%, both of which outperform those of traditional machine learning methods and other deep learning models. In terms of efficiency, the model has only 2.45 M parameters, a FLOPs of 112.42 M, a training time of 114 min, and a testing time of 25 min, demonstrating high efficiency. The model improves the recognition accuracy for the green attack stage and early stage through targeted design, providing important technical support for the large-scale monitoring and scientific prevention and control of PWD-infected trees.

Article.Title: Disrupted glial-mediated synaptic refinement in Fragile X syndrome
Article.Authors: Starr L.; Lee M.; Vo A.; Weisenhaus M.; Cheadle L.; Yadav A.; Paryani F.; Shirasu-Hiza M.; Menon V.; Mason C.
Article.Abstract: Fragile X syndrome (FXS), the most common inherited cause of intellectual disability and autism, results from the loss of the RNA-binding protein fragile X mental retardation protein (FMRP). FMRP is a translational regulator and is highly expressed in glial cells, where its role in neural circuit development remains poorly defined. Here, it was observed that Fmr1 knockout mice exhibit reduced synapse size and accelerated eye-specific segregation. To examine which cell-types participate in this process, a multi-omic framework was applied to FXS model mice at postnatal day 7, a critical window for synaptic remodeling in the retinogeniculate pathway, an established model system utilized to study synaptic pruning. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed coordinated alterations in microglia, astrocytes, and neurons in genes linked to synaptic pruning. Computational modeling further demonstrated enhanced astrocyte-to-microglia signaling, particularly through Ephrin A (EphA)- and semaphorin-mediated pathways, while preliminary lipidomic profiling revealed reductions in EphA-associated lipid species required for lipid raft stability and receptor localization. Consistent with these observations, a glial engulfment assay indicated that FXS microglia and astroglia over-engulf synaptic material in the lateral geniculate nucleus, supporting the transcriptomic profile. Together, these findings identify impaired glial-driven synaptic refinement as an early feature of FXS pathogenesis, highlighting the genes involved in this process as candidate targets for future investigation.

Article.Title: Foot-specific health status in a large convenience sample of adults living in Spain: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Navarro V.; Chicharro-Luna E.; Gijon-Nogueron G.; Fernández-Ehrling N.; García-Martínez M.; Ferrer-Torregrosa J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Introduction Podiatric health is crucial to people's overall well-being and independence but is often underestimated. Foot injuries are common, affecting mobility and increasing the risk of falls. This study aimed to evaluate podiatric health using the Foot Health Status Questionnaire (FHSQ) in the constructs of pain, function, general health and footwear. Material and Methods. Observational, analytical, cross-sectional and prospective study with 2,424 people over 18 years of age in Spain. The FHSQ questionnaire, which measures foot pain, foot function, footwear and general foot health, was applied. Results Of the participants, 1.998 were women and 426 men, with a mean age of 37.86 years. Significant differences were found between sex, with men reporting better results in “footwear”. Geographic and age differences were also significant, with older adults reporting worse podiatric health. Discussion Podiatric health significantly affects quality of life. Differences by sex, age, and region indicate the need for personalized approaches to podiatric care. Promoting podiatric health should be a priority to improve overall well-being. Conclusion Foot health is fundamental. It is crucial to recognize its importance and improve podiatric education and services, focusing on the needs of different demographic groups.

Article.Title: Comparative evaluation of energy efficiency strategies for green and low-carbon e-commerce logistics operations
Article.Authors: Xie P.; Hu L.; Lu C.; Huang J.; Alizadeh M.
Article.Abstract: This study evaluates five energy-efficiency and low-carbon strategies for e-commerce last-mile logistics using 120 calibrated simulated operating scenarios distributed across five metropolitan regions and three delivery-density classes. Each scenario was evaluated under a conventional internal-combustion baseline (S0), route optimization (S1), consolidation (S2), electrification (S3), and an integrated strategy (S4). Paired scenario-level comparisons, controlled-response analysis, factorial decomposition, grid-carbon break-even analysis, Monte Carlo simulation, and robustness tests were applied. Relative to S0, S1 and S2 reduced mean final energy use by 11.07% and 14.58% and route-operational CO₂e emissions by 11.06% and 14.56%, respectively. After accounting for 90% charging efficiency, S3 reduced grid-purchased final energy use by 66.43% and route-operational CO₂e emissions by 61.15%. S4 achieved the strongest central performance, reducing grid-purchased final energy use by 74.13% and route-operational CO₂e emissions by 70.05%, while increasing productivity from 29.34 to 33.81 deliveries per vehicle-hour. Factorial and alternative-combination analyses showed that S4 retained its first-place ranking after removal of the 0.99 integration multiplier and under the examined alternative combination rules. Both electrified strategies remained lower-carbon under average grid factors, although S3 retained this advantage in only 91 of 120 scenarios under nonbaseload factors. Strategy ordering remained unchanged across all ordinary-uncertainty simulations but frequently reversed under deliberately severe implementation stress. The findings support condition-dependent strategy selection but remain limited to calibrated simulated operations and route-level energy and emissions.

Article.Title: Daily physical activity on days with and without tennis lessons among adults in beginner and advanced classes
Article.Authors: Kawakami R.; Yamakawa S.; Hasegawa R.; Yokoyama T.; Horie S.; Hirayama Y.; Nakata K.
Article.Abstract: This observational repeated-measures study compared accelerometer-derived physical activity on tennis-lesson and non-tennis days among 47 adults enrolled in pre-existing coach-assigned beginner (n = 26) or advanced (n = 21) classes at one commercial tennis school; no standardized skill test was used. Monitoring occurred over two 15-day periods. Valid tennis-lesson-day data were available for 41 participants (median, 3 days; range, 1–9), and valid non-tennis-day data for 44 participants (median, 18 days; range, 2–27). Participant-level day-type means were analyzed using linear mixed models adjusted for accelerometer wear time. Participants in the advanced class were younger and included a higher proportion of men; sensitivity analyses additionally adjusted for age, sex, and body mass index. Group × Day interaction estimates were − 80.91 min/day for sedentary behavior (95% CI − 128.59 to − 33.23), − 104.27 min/day for light physical activity (95% CI − 138.54 to − 70.00), and − 19.96 min/day for moderate physical activity (95% CI − 38.85 to − 1.07). On tennis-lesson days, the beginner class showed lower light and higher moderate physical activity, whereas the advanced class showed higher light and moderate physical activity. Both classes also had higher step counts. These findings indicate class-associated differences in daily activity patterns, although causal and minute-for-minute substitution interpretations are not supported.

Article.Title: A deformation measurement method for discontinuous Timoshenko beams
Article.Authors: Guo Z.; Qian X.; Ren J.; Ma L.; Huang C.; Chen K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Based on the frame of the traditional inverse finite element method (iFEM) with global continuity, an enhanced IGA-iFEM method for handling the real-time shape sensing of beam structures with multiple stiffeners is proposed in this study. This method compensates for the defect of existing iFEM in engineering applications which segmental monitors displacement and strain in discontinuous structures. The number of strain sensors required in classical iFEM would greatly increase due to the changes in material properties. In this study, discrete real-time experimental strains were collected and processed by the enhanced iFEM algorithm, and finally, full-field displacement and strain monitoring were carried out for discontinuous structures. To this end, the distribution theory and sign function are used to reconstruct the neutral axial strain field, and the corresponding constitutive formulations are given. Meanwhile considering the abrupt change of strain field at the stiffener, the IGA analysis is used as a shape function to describe the integral beam element. Furthermore, the univariate equation is used to simplify the equation of motion of the Timoshenko beam. Finally, an experimental platform for UAV wing is built to verify the effectiveness of the above method on discontinuous beam deformation reconstruction. Overall, compared with the existing iFEM, the significant advantage of this method is that the number of sensors is greatly reduced under the premise of ensuring accuracy and greatly expanding the engineering application field of iFEM.

Article.Title: A multi-source earth observation and artificial intelligence framework for unsupervised water-use anomaly screening in Mediterranean agriculture
Article.Authors: Kakoulli E.; Antoniades A.; Neophytides S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reliable screening of agricultural water-use anomalies over large areas remains challenging because verified event labels and field observations are rarely available. We present AI4WaterGuard, a multi-source Earth Observation and artificial intelligence framework for unsupervised water-use anomaly screening across Cyprus. Using 617,862 records from 1,974 centroids across six hydrological years, six primary detector families were assessed under nested temporal cross-validation with training-consistent scaling, validity-aware scoring, and harmonised temporal support. Among the five centroid-sequence detectors, the convolutional neural network autoencoder showed the strongest response to the strong-reference controlled synthetic proxy, achieving Average Precision of $$0.893\pm 0.130$$ and Proxy F1 of $$0.880\pm 0.100$$ . The spatially explicit convolutional long short-term memory variational autoencoder was evaluated at finer land-pixel-sequence granularity and interpreted descriptively. Across five perturbation patterns and three severities, the convolutional neural network autoencoder achieved an equal-scenario mean Average Precision of 0.342, declining to 0.088 for weak perturbations. These synthetic metrics quantify controlled-proxy sensitivity, not field-validated detection performance. Operational post-processing on 1,157 WorldCover-eligible centroids combined threshold sensitivity, 1,000 exact-count randomisations, a primary Top-50 inspection-prioritisation queue with a nested Top-20 high-priority subset, and common-cadence spatiotemporal events. The resulting screening priorities require independent administrative and field evidence to establish physical cause or legal status.

Article.Title: Experimental enhancing drug solubility in supercritical CO₂ using modifiers: Modeling and machine learning prediction
Article.Authors: Sajadian S.; Askarizadeh M.; Sheikhshoaei A.; Noubigh A.
Article.Abstract: The experimental determination of the solubility of aripiprazole (APZ) in supercritical carbon dioxide (SC-CO 2 ) containing ethanol and dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) was conducted at temperatures ranging from 308 to 338 K and pressures from 12 to 30 MPa. The measured mole fraction solubility of ethanol ranged from 2.95 × 10 − 5 to 1.03 × 10 − 4 , while that of DMSO ranged from 4.59 × 10 − 5 to 1.38 × 10 − 4 . These results demonstrate that DMSO provides superior solubility enhancement. The maximum enhancement factor achieved was approximately 33 relatives to pure SC-CO₂. The experimental were then correlated using six semi-empirical models: The Sodeifian-Sajadian, González et al., Jouyban et al., Garlapati-Madras, MST, and Soltani-Mazloumi models. The Sodeifian-Sajadian and González et al. models were found to give the best correlations in terms of AARD%, R adj, and AICc, respectively, for DMSO and ethanol. In addition, multilayer perceptron (MLP) and support vector regression (SVR) models were developed to predict APZ solubility. The MLP model demonstrated superior predictive capabilities, with AARD values of 0.85% and 1.30% for the ethanol and DMSO systems, respectively. The experimental data and predictive models provide a reliable foundation for designing and optimizing supercritical pharmaceutical particle engineering processes.

Article.Title: Oceanic atoll in southern Maldives offers refuge for elasmobranch species amidst global declines
Article.Authors: Zerr K.; Hilbourne S.; Gregr I.; Zareer I.; Stevens G.; Baum J.
Article.Abstract: Despite their ecological and socioeconomic importance, oceanic and reef-associated elasmobranchs (sharks and rays) have experienced widespread declines. Within the Indian Ocean, Fuvahmulah Atoll, a highly exposed oceanic atoll in the southern Republic of Maldives, was recently designated as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, partly due to its extraordinary marine megafauna. However, Fuvahmulah’s elasmobranch populations have been little studied. Using remote timelapse cameras at three shallow forereef sites on the atoll, we quantified elasmobranch sightings during daylight hours between March and August 2022 ( n = 1,629,756 images analyzed). Elasmobranchs were sighted almost every day (95%, n = 60) and most hours (72%, n = 550). Of the four ray and seven shark species sighted, whitetip reef sharks were seen on the most hours ( n = 327) and days ( n = 56), but pelagic thresher sharks were sighted in the most images ( n = 27,447), reflecting the long periods this species spent at one site known to be a cleaning station. We document significant differences in species’ occurrences, relative abundances (MaxN), and frequency of occurrences diurnally, across sites, and seasons. The highest shark sighting rates overall, and for grey reef, whitetip reef, and tiger sharks, were observed within the Farikede marine protected area, for which management plans are in development. Our findings, which represent the first quantitative reports of Fuvahmulah’s elasmobranchs, underscore the atoll’s importance and that of protected areas for ensuring the persistence of these megafauna.

Article.Title: Contributing factors for surgically treated Hallux Valgus: a nationwide population-based cohort study in Taiwan
Article.Authors: Kuo T.; Chen Y.; Chung C.; Cho D.; Wang S.; Kuo C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hallux valgus (HV) is a prevalent deformity of the first metatarsophalangeal joint that can progress from a cosmetic concern to a painful, function–limiting condition requiring surgical correction. However, population-based data focusing on severe HV in Taiwan remains limited. Therefore, this study aims to examine national trends and systemic disease associations among patients undergoing HV surgery. Data from the National Health Insurance Research Database of Taiwan (2008–2021) were analyzed. Severe HV was defined by receipt of corrective surgery (procedure codes 64132 and 64133). Exposures were claims-defined comorbidities (≥ 10 outpatient visits or ≥ 1 hospitalization), and individuals with prior HV surgery were excluded. A non-exposed cohort was assigned random index dates. Propensity-score matching (1:1) was applied, and hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models. Of 25,767,574 individuals in the NHIRD, 2,392,429 with index dates outside 2008–2020, 9,065 with prior HV surgery, and 8 men in the breast cancer analysis were excluded, leaving 23,366,072 eligible individuals (3,377,791 with and 19,988,281 without the study comorbidities). After 1:1 propensity-score matching, the matched cohort comprised 6,755,582 individuals (3,377,791 per group) with excellent post-matching covariate balance. The annual prevalence of severe HV increased steadily over the study period and was consistently higher among women and older adults. Several comorbidities were associated with significantly higher risk of HV surgery, most notably anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury (adjusted HR 7.37, 95% CI 2.62–20.75), rheumatoid arthritis (RA; adjusted HR 5.31, 95% CI 3.52–8.00), Sjögren’s syndrome (adjusted HR 4.25, 95% CI 1.94–9.30), and osteoporosis (adjusted HR 3.52, 95% CI 2.90–4.27). Increased risks were also identified for obesity (adjusted HR 2.51, 95% CI 1.42–4.44), gout (adjusted HR 2.58, 95% CI 1.93–3.45), thyroid disease (adjusted HR 1.71, 95% CI 1.46–1.99), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD; adjusted HR 2.44, 95% CI 1.83–3.25), and breast cancer (adjusted HR 1.46, 95% CI 1.10–1.93). Severe HV requiring surgery was associated with multiple systemic comorbidities, suggesting that factors beyond a localized forefoot deformity may be involved. A surgery-based case definition identifies clinically meaningful disease but may be influenced by healthcare access and treatment preferences. These findings may inform risk-stratified counseling; however, causal relationships and the benefit of early preventive strategies require confirmation in prospective studies.

Article.Title: Diagnosis and causal-chain-based treatment of water-leakage in in-service mountainous highway tunnels: an engineering application
Article.Authors: Deng W.; Liu X.; He S.; Ma J.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Water leakage in in-service mountainous highway tunnels is difficult to diagnose due to concealed geological conditions, coupled seepage processes, and frequent recurrence after local repair. This study proposes a causal-diagnosis and causal-chain-based treatment framework for tunnel water leakage. The water-leakage mechanism is interpreted as a progressive process involving groundwater recharge, fracture-controlled seepage transport, drainage obstruction, water-pressure accumulation behind the lining, and failure at weak points in the waterproofing system. A diagnostic method integrating leakage characteristics, groundwater conditions, geological anomalies behind the lining, drainage performance, and waterproofing defects is established, followed by a three-stage treatment strategy. The framework was applied to the Dashiling Tunnel on the Shenzhen–Cenxi Expressway (G2518), China, using leakage surveys, seismic reflection imaging, and visual inspections. A total of 312 leakage defects were identified, with 48.1% occurring at secondary-lining construction joints and 37.8% occurring in wall-foot-to-sidewall zones. Fracture-related anomalies behind the lining and severe blockage in 50.0% of the inspected side drains revealed a compound leakage mechanism. After targeted treatment, two years of monitoring showed that the total area of pavement leakage was reduced to approximately 3.9% of its pre-treatment level. The number of tunnel water-leakage defects exhibited an approximately linear decreasing trend, with an overall reduction of more than 70%. The densities of tunnel water-leakage defects in all statistical sections were less than 0.3 points per linear meter, demonstrating good treatment effectiveness. The proposed framework provides a practical approach for the systematic diagnosis and treatment of water leakage in comparable in-service mountainous highway tunnels with similar hydrogeological and drainage conditions.

Article.Title: Predicting creativity in everyday life: an additional HRV reduction algorithm simulation and its Bayesian replication
Article.Authors: Rominger C.; Fink A.; Perchtold-Stefan C.; Benedek M.; Weber B.; Schwerdtfeger A.
Article.Abstract: Creative ideas happen in everyday life; however, some may be better than others, and we know little about the dynamics of idea quality as life unfolds. Research suggests that situations of reduced heart rate variability (HRV) might indicate moments of higher (verbal) creative performance. Therefore, this study investigated appropriate settings of an additional HRV reduction (AddHRVr) algorithm to predict creative performance in everyday life. In the first sample of 76 participants, who worked on verbal creative ideation tasks during five consecutive days, we simulated potential AddHRVr algorithm settings to identify higher creative performance. The simulation showed that short-lived periods of AddHRVr predicted higher creative performance in a given moment. In a second independent sample ( n = 65), the very same algorithm setting predicted higher creative performance, indicating robustness. This study provides first evidence for the predictive value of an AddHRVr algorithm to forecast creative performance in real life. As the next step, real-time field applications of these specific AddHRVr algorithm settings via wearables are needed to establish causality in the relationship between HRV reductions and creativity.

Article.Title: Enhancing ferric-reducing antioxidant activity through terpene mixture optimization
Article.Authors: Qasem A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The present study investigated the antioxidant potential of three terpenes p -cymene, thymol, and β-ionone—through their ferric reducing power (FRAP). Individually, p -cymene demonstrated the strongest activity with an EC 50 of 123.03 ± 2.05 µg/mL, followed by thymol (EC 50 = 153.16 ± 2.84 µg/mL), whereas β-ionone exhibited the lowest ferric reducing capacity (EC 50 = 931.46 ± 5.37 µg/mL), revealing significant variation in their antioxidant efficacy. To assess combinatorial effects, twelve randomized mixture trials were performed, each representing the mean of three independent repetitions, yielding FRAP EC 50 values ranging from 79.76 to 931.46 µg/mL. Statistical analysis identified significant contributions from linear terms (β 1 , β 2 , β 3 ), binary interactions (β 12 , β 13 ), and the ternary interaction term (β 123 ), indicating that both individual and combined effects shaped the overall antioxidant response. Analysis of 2D and 3D mixture plots suggested that an EC 50 around 79.70 µg/mL could be obtained by combining all three terpenes. Furthermore, desirability analysis predicted an optimal FRAP EC 50 of 58.23 µg/mL, achieved with a mixture comprising 17% β-ionone, 42% p -cymene, and 41% thymol, with a global desirability of 99.9%. These findings demonstrate that strategic blending of structurally related terpenes can substantially enhance ferric reducing capacity, providing a robust framework for the development of potent natural antioxidant formulations.

Article.Title: Blockchain-assisted revocable capability credential authentication for cross-domain UAVs
Article.Authors: Xu S.; Guan Y.; Li S.; Li J.; Zhao Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cross-domain UAV operations require secure and privacy-preserving authentication across multiple administrative domains. However, existing schemes still suffer from centralized authorization, exposure of mission attributes, insufficient revocation consistency, and limited auditability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a blockchain-assisted revocable capability credential authentication protocol for cross-domain UAV edge networks. The main innovation is to shift cross-domain UAV authentication from identity- or location-centric verification to revocation-aware lifecycle verification of mission capabilities. In the proposed framework, a Domain Authority committee jointly issues blinded capability credentials through distributed key generation and threshold BLS signatures. UAVs then prove mission-policy compliance using Groth16 zero-knowledge proofs without revealing sensitive capability attributes. Meanwhile, the blockchain maintains credential active states, revocation versions, and audit-root evidence for cross-domain consistency and accountability. A ticket-based AuthResume mechanism is further designed to reduce repeated authentication overhead while preventing outdated tickets from bypassing revocation. Formal security analysis, BAN logic, and Scyther verification show that the protocol supports credential unforgeability, revocation enforcement, auditability, mutual authentication, freshness, and session synchronization. Solidity smart contracts were deployed on the Sepolia testnet, and experimental results demonstrate acceptable FullAuth overhead and lightweight repeated access through AuthResume.

Article.Title: In vitro evaluation of the osteogenic associated cellular response and antibacterial activities of Vitex negundo leaf aqueous extract
Article.Authors: Liao Y.; Qiu B.; Albaqami A.; Mawkili W.; Alnassfan T.; Mireani M.
Article.Abstract: Plant-derived bioactive compounds have emerged as promising candidates for enhancing osteoblast function and bone formation because of their osteogenic potential and with minimal cytotoxicity. This study investigated the osteogenic associated activity and antibacterial properties of Vitex negundo leaf aqueous extract (VNL-AE) using osteoblast-like SaOS-2 cells and pathogenic bacteria. LC/MS analysis was employed to profile the phytochemicals of VNL-AE, revealing the presence of 31 highly active phytocompounds. VNL-AE exhibited marked antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa , with minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC) of 25 and 100 µg/mL and minimum bactericidal concentrations (MBC) of 50 and 200 µg/mL, respectively, along with significant inhibition of biofilm formation (P < 0.0001). Concentration-dependent effect on cell viability of SaOS-2 cells was observed in cytotoxicity assay. VNL-AE enhanced cell viability at concentrations up to 200 µg/mL, whereas higher concentrations (≥ 300 µg/mL) reduced viability, with an IC₅₀ of approximately 500 µg/mL after 72 h of exposure. Increased alkaline phosphatase activity was observed in dose-dependent manner (2.41 ± 0.03 in control vs. 2.58 ± 0.04 at 200 µg/mL) with enhanced mineralized matrix formation (0.44 ± 0.01 in controls vs. 3.14 ± 0.11 at 200 µg/mL; P < 0.0001) was observed. Quantitative PCR analysis showed significant up-regulation of osteogenic markers RUNX2 and BGLAP at 100 and 200 µg/mL. Additionally, VNL-AE preserved normal nuclear morphology, and increased the S-phase cell population from 21.16% in the control to 25.22% at 200 µg/mL. Overall, these finding suggest that VNL-AE may influence osteogenic associated response and cellular redox status in SaOS-2 in vitro model while exhibiting antibacterial activity. Further studies using primary human osteoblasts, mesenchymal stem cells, and appropriate in vivo models are necessary to validate these observations and elucidate the underlying mechanisms and translational relevance of VNL-AE.

Article.Title: Palmatine as a topical candidate for psoriasis targeting LCK to inhibit NF-κB signaling with computational prediction of Wnt pathway involvement
Article.Authors: Wang T.; Zhang X.; Wang H.; Ni Q.; Zhang X.; Chen H.; Yu W.; Fang G.; Wang Y.
Article.Abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder characterised by immune dysregulation and aberrant keratinocyte hyperproliferation. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formulae are widely used to alleviate psoriatic symptoms; however, their complex chemical compositions have long impeded the identification of core bioactive constituents. This study aimed to screen for anti‑psoriatic components from two representative TCM formulae using network pharmacology, and to further validate the therapeutic efficacy and molecular mechanism of palmatine—a major alkaloid derived from Phellodendron chinense—against psoriasis. Network pharmacology was used to construct a drug-component-target-disease network, identifying palmatine as the principal anti-psoriatic constituent of P. chinense. An IL-17A-induced HaCaT cell model was established. Cell viability was measured to determine working concentrations, and psoriasis-associated markers were quantified by RT-qPCR. Transcriptomic profiling with bioinformatics analysis identified key signalling pathways. Molecular docking and 100-ns MD simulations prioritized core targets, and CETSA validated target engagement. NF-κB activation was assessed by Western blotting. Palmatine shared a substantial number of targets with psoriasis-related genes. In IL-17A-stimulated HaCaT cells, palmatine significantly reversed the upregulation of psoriasis-associated markers and inhibited NF-κB activation, with efficacy comparable to methotrexate. Transcriptomic analysis identified 736 differentially expressed genes enriched in the NF-κB and Wnt signalling pathways, with Wnt involvement computationally predicted. Molecular docking and MD simulations prioritised LCK as the core target, and CETSA further confirmed that palmatine preferentially engaged LCK over LYN in intact cells. Palmatine exhibits considerable anti‑psoriatic activity in the in vitro setting, potentially through targeting LCK and modulating the NF‑κB signalling pathway. This study provides a novel candidate compound and a precise molecular target for the research and development of anti‑psoriatic therapeutics.

Article.Title: Robotic-assisted knee arthroplasty methods provide insight into Homo neanderthalensis gait and the evolutionary origins of modern human knee variation
Article.Authors: Pott H.; Savov P.; Stauss R.; Watson L.; Kullmer O.; Ettinger M.; Webb N.; Chapman T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lower-limb alignment is central to human bipedal locomotion and a key determinant of joint kinematics and osteoarthritis risk in modern clinical practice. However, its significance in hominins, and therefore its evolutionary implications, remain poorly understood. Advances in robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty (TKA) provide highly precise measurements of lower-limb alignment, joint morphology and soft-tissue balance that can elucidate these understudied aspects of hominin functional morphology. Here, we perform a proof-of-concept robotic-assisted TKA on an anatomically accurate model of the Spy II Neandertal. Using a robotic-assistance system, we registered bony morphology and replicated soft-tissue laxity extrapolated from a modern patient with a comparable alignment phenotype. We confirmed a pronounced constitutional varus alignment, classifying Spy II as a CPAK type I knee. This phenotype resembles that of modern athletes engaged in significant weight-bearing sports or intense physical activity during growth. The demonstration of constitutional varus in a hominin fossil thus suggests a deep evolutionary origin for this alignment pattern in modern humans, contextualizing normal knee variation and supporting an individualized alignment approach to modern TKA.

Article.Title: Integration of multi-trait stability indices for selection of nutrient-dense and yield-stable pearl millet genotypes across environments
Article.Authors: Hemanth S.; Singh S.; Singhal T.; Naveen A.; Yadav S.; Kapoor C.; Sharma S.; Bhargavi H.; Jangala D.; Singh N.; Satyavathi C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Addressing micronutrient malnutrition through pearl millet biofortification remains challenging because of complex trait interactions, anti-nutritional factors, and genotype × environment interactions. This study comparatively evaluated four multi-trait selection indices—SHI, FAI-BLUP, MTSI, and MGIDI for identifying pearl millet genotypes with improved nutritional composition, reduced anti-nutritional factors, and desirable yield-related performance. A diverse PMiGAP panel of 218 genotypes was evaluated across four contrasting environments representing the A, A₁, and B pearl millet-growing zones of India. The traits comprised iron, zinc, manganese, and phosphorus, total tannin content, phytic acid content, grain filling duration, tiller productivity, spike size, sink capacity, thousand-seed weight, and seed yield per plant. Combined analysis of variance revealed highly significant effects of genotype, environment, and genotype × environment interaction for all evaluated traits, indicating substantial genetic variability and differential environmental responses. Correlation analysis revealed positive associations among nutritional and yield-related traits, whereas anti-nutritional traits showed antagonistic relationships. At 15% selection intensity, MGIDI produced gains of 8.78% for Fe, 3.85% for Zn, and 3.01% for Mn, while reducing PAC and TTC by 6.31% and 10.70%, respectively. MTSI produced the greatest gains for several yield-related traits, including tiller productivity (21.55%), seed yield per plant (14.63%), spike size (11.98%), and sink capacity (16.51%). SHI achieved the largest reductions in PAC (17.90%) and TTC (13.40%), whereas FAI-BLUP showed substantial gains for several yield traits but increased PAC (8.96%) and TTC (13.40%). Four genotypes—IP 15,872, IP 19,584, IP 3757, and IP 6310—were consistently selected by all four indices, demonstrating strong concordance among selection approaches. These consensus genotypes represent promising genetic resources for the development of pearl millet with improved nutritional quality, reduced anti-nutritional factors, and desirable yield-related attributes.

Article.Title: Antimicrobial activity, physicochemical properties, antioxidant capacity, and elemental composition of yerba mate (Ilex paraguariensis)
Article.Authors: Hallaç B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Yerba mate ( Ilex paraguariensis ) has attracted considerable interest because of its diverse bioactive properties. To provide an integrated characterization beyond the evaluation of a single biological property, this study investigated the antimicrobial and physicochemical characteristics of water, ethanol, and methanol extracts, together with the antioxidant capacity and elemental composition of yerba mate. Antimicrobial activity was evaluated against foodborne pathogenic bacteria ( Bacillus subtilis , Escherichia coli , Enterococcus faecalis , and Staphylococcus aureus ) and yeast species ( Candida albicans and Saccharomyces cerevisiae ) using the agar well diffusion method. The water, ethanol, and methanol extracts were tested at their experimentally determined extract concentrations rather than after normalization to a common dry-extract concentration. The results revealed that the extracts exhibited no antifungal activity but showed varying levels of antibacterial effects among the tested extracts and microorganisms. Under the tested experimental conditions, the methanol extract produced the largest inhibition zones, particularly against S. aureus (18.67 mm) and B. subtilis (18.33 mm), and showed the lowest MIC value (43.75 µg/mL). Physicochemical analyses showed that the methanol extract had the highest pH (5.31) and the lowest oxidation–reduction potential (113.83 mV), whereas the ethanol extract had the lowest pH (4.86) and the highest oxidation–reduction potential (137.13 mV). For the single analyzed extract condition at 5 mg/mL, the total phenolic content was 12.80 µg GAE/mL, with a ferric reducing antioxidant power of 0.89 µM FeSO 4 ·7H 2 O equivalents and a DPPH radical scavenging activity of 59.07%. Because solvent-specific antioxidant measurements were not available, these results do not permit comparison among the water, ethanol, and methanol extracts. Elemental analysis by ICP-MS showed that potassium (3320.54 ppm), magnesium (1079.60 ppm), and calcium (726.35 ppm) were the most abundant measured elements, while Pb, Cd, and As were detected at relatively low concentrations in the dried plant material; however, dietary exposure was not assessed. Overall, extracts prepared from the analyzed commercial yerba mate material using different solvents exhibited different levels of in vitro antibacterial activity under the tested experimental conditions; however, because the extracts were not evaluated at an identical dry-extract concentration, these differences cannot be attributed exclusively to the extraction solvent. However, because no food-matrix or shelf-life experiments were performed, further validation using food-compatible extracts in real food systems is required before preservative applications can be proposed. Further studies should focus on identifying the bioactive compounds responsible for the observed activities and evaluating concentration-dependent responses using food-compatible extracts.

Article.Title: Depressive symptoms increase during follow-up and are associated with phenoconversion in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder
Article.Authors: Baltassis S.; Pascazio A.; Houot M.; Leu-Semenescu S.; Peter-Derex L.; Leclair-Visonneau L.; de Cock V.; Abril B.; Lanvin L.; Livia Fantini M.; Arnulf I.; Dodet P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Depressive symptoms are common in synucleinopathies, emerging during prodromal stages such as isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD), yet their association with phenoconversion remains unclear. Among 167 patients with iRBD from the FranceRBD cohort with at least two yearly Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) assessments, we examined the clinical correlates and longitudinal trajectory of depressive symptoms and their association with phenoconversion using linear regression and joint models for longitudinal and survival data. At first assessment, 13% of patients had depressive symptoms (HADS-D > 7), which were associated with apathy, daytime sleepiness, and abnormal visual perception. HADS-D scores progressively increased over time, with a later increase than that observed for apathy. Each additional point in HADS-D score was associated with a 27% higher hazard of phenoconversion (HR 1.27, p < 0.05). These findings suggest that depressive symptoms evolve dynamically across the prodromal phase of synucleinopathies and are associated with phenoconversion, supporting their longitudinal assessment in iRBD.

Article.Title: Automated terminology enhancement for domain-specific translation using large language models
Article.Authors: Huang Y.; Liu W.; Wang J.; Zhu H.
Article.Abstract: This paper proposes an Automated Terminology Enhancement Translation (ATET) Framework that integrates Large Language Models (LLMs) with a terminology enhancement mechanism to improve the accuracy and consistency of domain-specific translations. LLMs often struggle with errors in translating specialized terminology. The ATET Framework addresses this issue by introducing an automated process for identifying and correcting terms during translation, thereby reducing reliance on manual intervention and minimizing translation errors. Experimental results demonstrate that the ATET Framework significantly improves translation quality across multiple language pairs (zh-en, de-en, en-cs, en-zh, en-de, cs-en), particularly in handling domain-specific terms. Fine-tuning further enhances the accuracy of terminology translation, validating the Framework’s applicability and potential in multilingual translation tasks. This research offers an effective solution for advancing machine translation technology and highlights its practical value in specialized translation scenarios.

Article.Title: Paleoenvironmental and vegetational controls on tar yield in the Jurassic Xishanyao Formation coals of southern Junggar Basin, China
Article.Authors: Zhang L.; Gan H.; Gong S.; Wang H.; Xie W.; Ning C.; Chen Z.; Lu B.; Cao Z.; Ma W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Tar-rich coal is an important resource for coal-measure oil and gas exploration and clean energy conversion, yet seam-scale variations in tar yield and their controlling mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study investigates the Middle Jurassic Xishanyao Formation coals in the southern Junggar Basin by integrating organic petrography, palynology, geochemistry, and molecular-structure analyses. Results show an upward increase in tar yield, volatile matter yield, and hydrogen index, indicating relatively enhanced liquid-product potential during pyrolysis in the upper coal interval. Palynological analysis identified two assemblages, characterized by a shift from gymnosperm-pollen dominance in the lower seams (55.00–58.33%) to higher fern-spore proportions in the upper seams (50.00–58.82%). The lower coal seams were mainly formed in delta-plain forest swamps during the lowstand systems tract (LST), accompanied by stronger clastic input and water-level fluctuations. Their coal-forming materials were dominated by woody gymnosperms, while fluctuating water tables and greater oxygen exposure were associated with relatively abundant inertinite and more aromatic molecular structures. With progressive lake transgression, peat-forming mires evolved into lakeshore swamps characterized by more stable water coverage and more reducing conditions, which favored the preservation of labile organic matter. FTIR results show that high-tar-yield coals have higher CH 2 /CH 3 ratios and A-factors, but lower aromaticity and aromatic condensation, indicating molecular structures enriched in aliphatic chains and weakly condensed aromatic units. These features suggest that long-chain aliphatic side chains and bridge bonds provide a favorable molecular basis for liquid-product release during low-temperature pyrolysis, whereas highly condensed aromatic structures and certain oxygen-containing functional groups tend to inhibit tar generation. Overall, the higher tar yields of the upper coals were associated with changes in vegetation input and improved preservation of aliphatic-rich organic matter under more persistently water-covered, oxygen-restricted mire conditions during lake transgression. These findings provide a geological basis for interpreting tar-rich coal and identifying high-tar-yield intervals in comparable low- to medium-rank humic coal successions formed in terrestrial lacustrine settings.

Article.Title: Inhibitors for a conserved filarial catechol-O-methyltransferase with potent efficacy against all life-stages of Brugia malayi infection in gerbils
Article.Authors: Mia M.; Sk M.; Paudel B.; Azam A.; Allaie I.; Zhang X.; Tajkhorshid E.; Witola W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Filarial nematodes of genus Brugia cause lymphatic filariasis, with over 36 million chronically debilitated people, and 885 million at risk in Asia and sub-Saharan Africa. Current drugs have limited efficacy. Herein, we unveil a unique catechol- O -methyltransferase (COMT) called BmMT that is conserved in filarial nematodes with a lethal RNAi phenotype in Caenorhabditis elegans and absence of orthologs in mammals. COMTs catabolize catecholamines that if left to accumulate are lethal in nematodes. BmMT possesses core structural functional features of COMTs, but is divergent from mammalian COMTs. Three compounds (NSC17783, NSC133100, and NSC56410) with inhibitory activity against BmMT showed potent activity against all life stages of B. malayi . The inhibitors bind within BmMT’s catechol substrate-binding fold with high-occupancy (> 80%) of residues, indicating they target blocking catecholamine binding. As proof of principle for mode of action of BmMT inhibitors, treatment of B. malayi worms with NSC56410 elevated catecholamines, consistent with observations using morpholino-mediated knockdown of BmMT in B. malayi . Importantly, infection-and-treatment of gerbils showed that 4 days treatment with NSC133100 (100 mg/kg/day) or NSC56410 (10 mg/kg/day) eliminated both microfilariae and adult worms. Together, our studies unveil and validate a molecular target and its optimizable selective inhibitors for development of novel efficacious anti-filarial drugs.

Article.Title: Agricultural chemical intensification and ecological footprint comparative analysis of pesticide and insecticide consumption
Article.Authors: Akadiri S.; Awosusi A.; Abdallah I.
Article.Abstract: This study examines how agricultural chemical intensification affects environmental sustainability in Nigeria by comparing the ecological footprint impacts of pesticide and insecticide consumption from 1990 to 2024. The analysis incorporates economic growth, renewable energy consumption, financial development, and energy use as control variables, and tests the Environmental Kuznets Curve (EKC) hypothesis. To capture nonlinearities and gradual structural shifts, the study uses the BDS nonlinearity test, Fourier-augmented unit root procedures, the Fourier Bootstrap ARDL approach for long-run estimation, and the Fourier Toda–Yamamoto causality framework. The empirical results reveal that both pesticide and insecticide consumption are positively and significantly associated with Nigeria’s ecological footprint in the long run, consistent with chemical intensification contributing to environmental pressure. Renewable energy consumption reduces ecological pressure, whereas financial development exhibits mixed effects. The results are consistent with an inverted-U relationship, although the evidence is weaker for some specifications. Fourier Toda–Yamamoto results indicate predictive causality between chemical use and ecological footprint in both directions, with the INSECT → EF link strongest at the 5% level and the others significant at the 10% level. The study suggests that Nigeria’s input-intensive agricultural growth pattern is environmentally unsustainable and underscores the need for cleaner energy systems, sustainable agricultural practices, and environmentally aligned financial development. The findings provide policy insights for balancing agricultural productivity and ecological sustainability in developing economies.

Article.Title: How physical activity relates to college students’ prosocial behavior through psychological capital and social connectedness
Article.Authors: Ke W.; Chen J.; Li G.; Wu M.; Wu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Against the backdrop of accumulating psychological stress and challenges in social adaptation, physical activity is widely recognized as an important daily behavior associated with the physical and mental health of college students. However, the pathways linking physical activity to prosocial behavior remain insufficiently understood. Drawing on conservation of resources theory, this study develops a resource transformation framework incorporating physical activity, psychological capital, social connectedness, and prosocial behavior, and examines their differentiated relational pathways in the accumulation of psychological and social resources. Using survey data from 1244 college students, partial least squares structural equation modeling and necessary condition analysis were combined to examine the relationships among physical activity, psychological capital, social connectedness, and prosocial behavior. The results indicated no significant direct relationship between physical activity and prosocial behavior. However, significant indirect relationships were identified through psychological capital and social connectedness separately, as well as through the sequential pathway from psychological capital to social connectedness. Necessary condition analysis further indicated that psychological capital was identified as a necessary condition for achieving higher levels of social connectedness, while physical activity, psychological capital, and social connectedness were all identified as necessary conditions for achieving higher levels of prosocial behavior. Theoretically, this study extends the understanding of physical activity from an outcome-oriented health behavior perspective to a resource perspective on the development of social behavior, broadens the explanatory scope of conservation of resources theory in prosocial behavior research, and further elucidates the potential sequential association between psychological and social resources. Practically, the findings provide resource-oriented insights into the use of physical activity to support social adaptation and the development of prosocial behavior among college students, with implications for college physical education and public health practice.

Article.Title: Multi-objective artificial pedosphere intelligence for microbial homeostasis-oriented governance of functional nanoparticle systems in complex ecosystems
Article.Authors: Vidap R.; Nadialli R.; Teriveedhi V.; Suresh Babu K.; Pulluru S.; Manohar A.; Thondapu S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Soil microbial homeostasis is fundamental to sustainable agriculture and ecological resilience, yet existing machine learning approaches primarily emphasize prediction accuracy while overlooking microbial interactions, uncertainty quantification, ecological homeostasis, and decision-support for nanoparticle governance. This study proposes an Artificial Pedosphere Intelligence framework to predict the Microbial Homeostasis Deviation Score (MHDS) by integrating a Microbial Co-occurrence Graph Attention Network (MC-GAT), homeostasis-constrained learning, a Deep Kernel Gaussian Process (DKL), Bayesian Multi-Objective Optimization, and SHAP-based explainability within a unified ecological intelligence pipeline. The framework first constructs an ecological feature graph, learns biologically informed representations, estimates predictive uncertainty, and subsequently performs simulation-based optimization to identify environmentally balanced nanoparticle governance strategies. The model was implemented using Python 3.10 with PyTorch, PyTorch Geometric, GPyTorch, BoTorch, and SHAP, and evaluated on the Kaggle Soil Microbe Dataset containing 100,000 soil samples. The proposed framework achieved R² = 0.962, MSE = 0.007, and MAE = 0.016, representing an approximately 2.3% improvement in R² over the strongest baseline (0.94). These findings demonstrate that biologically informed graph intelligence combined with uncertainty-aware optimization provides accurate, interpretable, and scalable ecological decision support for sustainable soil management. .

Article.Title: Externally validated and explainable QSAR for ready biodegradability: KNIME–H2O AutoML with RDKit descriptors and Morgan fingerprints
Article.Authors: Elsayad A.; Elsayad K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ready biodegradability is an important endpoint for environmental chemical assessment. We developed an externally validated QSAR workflow using KNIME, RDKit descriptors, Morgan fingerprints and H2O AutoML to classify readily biodegradable (RB) and not readily biodegradable (NRB) compounds. The benchmark contained training (n = 837), internal test (n = 218) and external validation (n = 670) subsets. Preprocessing and RF feature screening reduced 119 RDKit descriptors and 1024 Morgan bits to 311 predictors. Four model families were evaluated: GLM, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting (GB) and a neural network. Reported external ROC–AUC values were approximately 0.91 for the tree ensembles. Recalculation from the deposited GB predictions gave ROC–AUC = 0.911, accuracy = 0.866, RB recall = 0.754 and MCC = 0.668. A paired bootstrap of the external prediction table gave a 95% ROC–AUC interval of 0.886–0.935. Global and local explanation outputs highlighted surface-property descriptors, topology and selected fingerprint bits. Direct comparison of feature ranks distinguished broadly shared signals, such as smr_VSA10, from method-dependent rankings. Applicability-domain assessment and conservative interpretation of hashed fingerprint bits provide additional context for screening. The workflow supports prioritization and model auditing; it does not replace experimental biodegradability testing or establish causal degradation mechanisms.

Article.Title: Contrast-enhanced ultrasound in assessment of testicular injury based on different degrees of testicular torsion in rabbits
Article.Authors: Yang L.; Peng C.; Zhu X.; Yao W.; Deng Y.; Luo Y.
Article.Abstract: Early detection of testicular torsion (TT) and accurate evaluation of testicular injury are clinically critical for guiding appropriate interventions. This study aimed to investigate the feasibility of Contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) for assessing the degree of testicular injury after torsion. CEUS quantitative parameters were obtained from fifty rabbits with different degrees of TT (0°, 180°, 360°, and 720°) at 2 h, 4 h, 6 h post-operation. With reference to histopathological changes, significant correlations were observed between time to peak (TTP) /relative peak intensity (R-PI) and spermatogenic cell apoptotic index, with corresponding correlation coefficients of 0.61( P = 0.004) and − 0.74 ( P < 0.001), respectively. In early diagnosis of TT, both TTP and R-PI demonstrated good diagnostic capability with the areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUROCs) of 0.87 (95% CI, 0.71-1.00) and 0.75 (95% CI, 0.53–0.96), respectively. In identifying ischemia/ hypoxia injury, the AUROCs were 0.83 (95% CI, 0.72–0.94) for TTP and 0.80 (95% CI, 0.68–0.92) for R-PI, respectively. The corresponding sensitivity and specificity values of TTP were both above 80%. In identifying severe injury/necrosis, the AUROC of TTP was 0.81 with a diagnostic sensitivity of 94.1%. Relatively lower diagnostic performance was observed for R-PI with an AUROC of 0.74 (95% CI, 0.59–0.89). In conclusion, the CEUS quantitative parameters TTP and R-PI demonstrate promising diagnostic performance for the early diagnosis of TT and the assessment of testicular injury following TT.

Article.Title: Continuous fixed-bed adsorption of cationic dyes by starch nanocrystals with breakthrough modeling of competitive interactions in multicomponent systems
Article.Authors: Bahrami M.; Amiri M.; Rahsepar Chargi Z.; Mahmoudi M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The removal of synthetic dyes from industrial wastewater remains a major environmental challenge due to their persistence and toxicity. This study investigated starch nanocrystals (SNCs), a carbohydrate-based biological macromaterial, as a sustainable biosorbent for the continuous removal of malachite green (MG), methylene blue (MB), and crystal violet (CV) from single-, binary-, and ternary-component systems using fixed-bed column adsorption. Breakthrough behavior was evaluated using six models, including Thomas, Yoon–Nelson, Adams–Bohart, mass-transfer, dose–response, and bed-depth service time (BDST) models. Model performance was assessed using the coefficient of determination (R 2 ) and normalized root mean square error (NRMSE). SNCs exhibited high adsorption affinity toward all three dyes under single-component conditions, with removal efficiencies of 70.87–71.88% and saturation capacities ranging from 5.16 to 5.44 mg/g. Competitive adsorption in binary and ternary systems reduced removal efficiency (59.24–73.01%), adsorption capacity (3.67–4.95 mg/g), and column service time (1772.73–1942.86 min) relative to single-component systems. However, the extent of performance reduction varied among different dye combinations, with systems containing MB and CV exhibiting less severe reductions than other mixed-dye systems, indicating composition-dependent competitive interactions rather than net synergistic effects. Among the evaluated models, the dose–response and BDST models provided the most accurate predictions across all adsorption systems (R 2 > 0.99, NRMSE = 3.00–6.02%). The Thomas model also showed good fit quality (R 2 = 98.78–99.46%) but exhibited variable NRMSE values (5.25–9.21%), with the highest errors observed in binary systems, indicating that its accuracy is system-dependent and its parameters have limited interpretability under competitive conditions. The Yoon–Nelson model showed moderate predictive capability (R 2 = 97.92–99.15%, NRMSE = 6.10–12.51%), while the Adams–Bohart and mass-transfer models exhibited the highest NRMSE values (8.65–32.89% and 21.03–25.71%, respectively), indicating limited applicability under multicomponent conditions. A statistical regression framework incorporating dummy variables and interaction effects was developed to quantify the combined influence of adsorption time (quantitative variable) and system composition (qualitative variable: single-, binary-, and ternary-component systems) on breakthrough behavior. The model structure includes linear and quadratic time terms, categorical dummy variables representing different dye systems, and interaction terms (time × system composition) to account for composition-dependent adsorption kinetics. This framework successfully described competitive adsorption behavior and explained more than 98% of the variability in the experimental data (R 2 = 98.02%, adjusted R 2 = 97.72%, NRMSE = 0.053%), with the interaction terms revealing that the effect of adsorption time on breakthrough behavior was significantly modulated by system composition, particularly in mixed-dye systems containing MB and CV. The results demonstrate the potential of SNCs as environmentally friendly adsorbents for dye-contaminated wastewater and provide useful insights for the design and optimization of fixed-bed adsorption systems operating under realistic multicomponent conditions.

Article.Title: Impact of access cavity design on the filling ability of two obturation protocols evaluated by micro-computed tomography
Article.Authors: Alhwieti A.; Alnahawi D.; Howait M.; Abulhamael A.; Al-Habib M.; Alsofi L.; Alamoudi R.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated the effects of traditional access cavity (TAC) and contracted access cavity (CAC) designs on the filling ability of two obturation protocols, single cone obturation (SC) and continuous wave compaction (CWCT), using micro-computed tomography (micro-CT). Twenty standardized 3D-printed mandibular first molar replicas were allocated according to access cavity design ( n = 10). All canals were prepared with the EdgeFile X7 rotary system to size 30/0.04 and scanned using micro-CT. The specimens were then allocated to four groups according to access design and obturation protocol: TAC/CWCT, TAC/SC, CAC/CWCT, and CAC/SC ( n = 5). Filling quality was assessed by percentage of voids (POV), isthmus filling, and residual filling-material volume in the pulp chamber. Gaussian generalized estimating equation analysis of POV demonstrated a significant access cavity design × obturation protocol interaction (Wald χ² = 6.37, P = 0.012), with an estimated interaction contrast of 1.903% points (95% CI, 0.426–3.381). The highest descriptive apical POV values were observed in the CAC/CWCT group, reaching 8.810 ± 1.082% in the mesiobuccal canal and 12.069 ± 0.768% in the mesiolingual canal. Residual filling-material volume also showed a significant access design × obturation protocol interaction ( P < 0.001), with CAC/CWCT showing the greatest residual volume (0.409 ± 0.064 mm³). Isthmus filling was absent in all CAC/CWCT specimens; however, differences between TAC and CAC were not statistically significant within either CWCT ( P = 0.167) or SC ( P = 1.000). Overall, filling outcomes depended on the combination of access cavity design and obturation protocol, with the CAC/CWCT combination showing the least favorable pattern. Because different sealers were used with CWCT and SC, these findings reflect the complete obturation protocols rather than the obturation techniques alone.

Article.Title: Dynamic distribution of volatile organic compounds emitted by lilac at various developmental stages
Article.Authors: Tuo Y.; Bai S.; Dai X.; Bai Y.; Bao W.
Article.Abstract: Lilac flowers emit diverse volatile organic compounds (VOCs) that contribute to their characteristic fragrance. However, limited research has been conducted on the characteristics of VOCs emitted by naturally grown lilac flowers from the bud to withering stages. To investigate the variations in the VOCs of lilacs across different developmental stages, dynamic headspace sampling combined with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) detection was adopted to collect and identify VOCs emitted by Syringa oblata , Syringa meyeri and Syringa vulgaris at various developmental stages, and statistical methods were applied to screen key differential compounds. A total of 73 VOCs belonging to 7 categories were emitted by the three lilac species across all developmental stages, and the VOCs content differed significantly among developmental stages. For Syringa oblata , 2-butenal and octanal peaked at the full flowering stage. While 2-ethyl-2-hexenal and (Z)-3,7-dimethyl-1,3,6-octatriene were the most abundant substances in Syringa meyeri at the flowering stage, most VOCs in Syringa vulgaris exhibited a U-shaped trend, which is opposite to the development of the other two lilacs. Terpenoids, including camphene, Limonene, and β-pinene, were observed to change considerably during flower development. These results revealed the dynamic distribution of VOCs in lilacs at different developmental stages.

Article.Title: Rice starch–activated carbon composite films for potential cosmetic facial sheet mask applications: physicochemical and mechanical characterization
Article.Authors: Jain S.; Shahapur S.; Pooja N.; Madhusree J.; Mal S.; Gunathilake T.; Bhavanari M.; Singh B.; Prasad A.; Mazumder N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The widespread use of synthetic facial sheet masks has raised concerns about their environmental impact. In this study, rice starch (RS)–activated carbon (AC) composite films were prepared by solution casting and characterized to assess their potential as biodegradable cosmetic mask substrates. The surface morphology of the films changed after AC incorporation, with thicknesses ranging from approximately 0.2 to 0.3 mm and the moisture content increasing with increasing AC loading. The water contact angles ranged from 48.95° to 63.85°, indicating hydrophilic surfaces, with the RS + AC (0.4 g) film exhibiting the lowest measured contact angle. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy suggested predominantly physical interactions between the RS and AC, whereas differential scanning calorimetry and X-ray diffraction characterized their thermal transitions and structural features. Compared with the neat RS film, the RS + AC (0.4 g) film exhibited lower tensile strength and elongation at break. MTT assays performed on AC powder revealed that the cell viability of L929 fibroblasts and HaCaT keratinocytes was above 90% under the tested conditions; the complete composite films were not evaluated for cytotoxicity. Soil burial testing revealed approximately 68.7% mass loss for the RS + AC film after 30 days. These findings support further investigations of RS + AC films as biodegradable cosmetic mask substrates. Their biocompatibility, water uptake, serum retention, and performance during skin application remain to be established.

Article.Title: Dental aesthetics moderate the association between negative views of aging and psychological distress
Article.Authors: Nangle M.; Henry J.; Kerr B.; Coundouris S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In late adulthood, a positive body image has been shown to moderate the association between broader ageist attitudes and psychological wellbeing. An important aspect of body image often overlooked in this age group is how attractive and healthy one’s teeth appear. Since age-related declines in oral health negatively impact orofacial appearance and are also associated with poorer mental health, this study provided the first test of whether perceived dental aesthetics also moderates the relationship between negative views of one’s own aging and psychological distress. A representative sample of 604 adults with the same proportion of participants as the national United Kingdom population across three core demographics (age, sex, ethnicity) completed a survey that included validated measures of subjective age, body image and perceived dental aesthetics. Correlational and moderation analyses revealed that, as predicted, not only was holding more negative views of one’s own aging linked to poorer mental health, but this relationship was moderated both by body image in general, and perceived dental aesthetics specifically. Thus, the adverse association between age-based self-perceptions and mental health was strongest for those who held a poorer body image, and/or who reported more negative perceptions about their orofacial appearance. Thus, while extensive literature reveals that how attractive or healthy one’s teeth appear contributes to self-esteem and self-worth in young adulthood, the current study reveals that this aspect of body image remains important at later stages of the adult lifespan: perceived dental aesthetics moderates the association between negative views of one’s own aging and psychological distress.

Article.Title: Identification of artificially ripened banana by chemical agent using gas sensor array
Article.Authors: Jim A.; Rahman M.; Charoenlarpnopparut C.; Talukder K.
Article.Abstract: Fresh fruits are consumed for the necessary vitamins, minerals, fiber, and proteins to keep ourselves healthy. The banana is a common and healthy fruit produced around the year in Bangladesh and many countries in the world. Bananas are often artificially ripened by chemical agents, which is injurious to health. Therefore, detecting artificially ripened bananas (ARB) has become important in ensuring food safety and quality. A novel non-destructive approach to identify ARB by analyzing electronic signals acquired by a gas sensor array in response to volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emitted from bananas is proposed in this paper. An automated data collection system is designed, which consists of a gas sensor array, a data acquisition device, and LabVIEW. Four machine learning (ML) models, namely logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM), decision tree (DT), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), have been utilized to analyze the sensor data and classify the bananas into both binary and day-wise (ripening stages) classification of artificially and naturally ripened banana (ANRB) tasks. Among the four models, XGBoost achieved the best performance on binary classification of ANRB with 97.03% and 95.05 ± 2.98% test and 10-fold cross-validation (CV) accuracy while incorporating important features. As for the day-wise classification, the SVM model performed best, obtaining 99.94% test accuracy and 99.92 ± 0.05% CV accuracy (utilizing all features). Moreover, this study is the first investigation of ANRB detection using VOC response, which also outperforms existing hyperspectral imaging-based ANRB classification in a substantially cost-effective manner. Overall, this study contributes to the advancement of food safety technologies by providing a non-destructive technique, an alternative to destructive solutions, for ARB detection.

Article.Title: Interpretable machine learning for predicting intraoperative oxygenation impairment during one-lung ventilation in thoracic surgery: a retrospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Deng Y.; Chen J.; Liu W.; Zhu F.
Article.Abstract: Intraoperative oxygenation impairment during one-lung ventilation poses significant challenges in thoracic anesthesia. Traditional statistical models often fail to capture complex non-linear clinical relationships. This study aimed to evaluate machine learning algorithms for predicting this impairment and interpret potential feature associations using the SHAP method. Clinical data from 519 patients undergoing thoracic surgery were retrospectively analyzed. Five algorithms were evaluated. Model performance was measured using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. SHAP was applied to explore non-linear associations and feature interactions, without implying biological causality. The random forest model exhibited the highest area under the curve (0.924), performing better than logistic regression (0.790). SHAP analysis identified positive end-expiratory pressure, preoperative arterial oxygen partial pressure, and body mass index as the primary predictors. Moreover, the analysis revealed potential U-shaped protective associations for positive end-expiratory pressure (4 to 6 cm of water) and tidal volume, alongside synergistic interactions between baseline pulmonary conditions and mechanical ventilation settings. The random forest algorithm may provide superior discriminative performance for predicting oxygenation impairmen in this retrospective cohort. Interpretable machine learning provides exploratory hypothesis-generating insights into complex non-linear thresholds and interactions, which may serve as preliminary reference information for future prospective studies on individualized anesthetic management.

Article.Title: Herpes zoster and major vascular events in a general population without prior cardiovascular event from Shizuoka Kokuho database
Article.Authors: Ikegami S.; Takeuchi M.; Nishimura S.; Kumamaru H.; Nakamaru R.; Kohsaka S.; Ieda M.
Article.Abstract: Herpes zoster (HZ) is associated with a risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD), but findings may differ according to baseline risk profiles. We evaluated the association between HZ and CVD among adults without prior CVD. We used a municipal-level health insurance database in Japan. Adults aged 50–84 years without prior CVD were included. HZ was defined using ICD-10 diagnostic codes with concurrent antiviral prescription. The primary outcome was a composite of unstable angina pectoris, myocardial infarction, or stroke requiring hospitalization. Propensity score matching was performed and Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs). Sensitivity analyses were conducted in individuals with Charlson Comorbidity Index ≥ 1. After propensity score matching, 94,269 individuals (20,575 HZ cases and 73,846 controls) were included. During a median follow-up of 58 months, 1,214 (1.3%) experienced the primary outcome. HZ was not significantly associated with increased risk (HR, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.90–1.18; p = 0.66). In a sensitivity analysis, HZ showed a non-significant trend toward higher risk (HR, 1.33; 95% CI, 0.90–1.96). In adults without prior CVD, HZ was not significantly associated with CVD events. However, a possible excess risk among individuals with comorbidities could not be excluded, supporting further evaluation in higher-risk populations.

Article.Title: Multi-scale representation contrastive learning for multivariate time-series anomaly detection
Article.Authors: Liao P.; Cheng R.; Bai X.; Chen Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In recent years, multivariate time series anomaly detection has received growing attention due to its broad relevance in real-world applications. Nevertheless, accurately identifying anomalies in large-scale time series remains challenging. Many existing methods partition time series into patches to model temporal information, but single-scale patching cannot simultaneously capture complex dynamics at multiple granularities. Moreover, multivariate time series often exhibit strong coupling and complex interactions across sensor channels, such that anomalies may propagate across channels and disrupt dependency structures. To address these challenges, we propose a multivariate time series anomaly detection method based on Multi-scale Representation Contrastive Learning (MsRCL). Specifically, MsRCL performs multi-scale patch decomposition and learns complementary representations from two views, multi-scale intra-patch and multi-scale inter-patch, to capture local dynamics at different temporal scales, cross-segment dependencies, and temporal patterns such as trends and periodicity. In addition, we design a channel-aware attention mechanism that strengthens salient channel correlations and suppresses weakly correlated noise, enabling adaptive modeling of cross-channel dependency structures and improving the representation of cross-channel coupled anomalies. Experiments on five real-world multivariate time series datasets show that MsRCL delivers effective performance gains over the mainstream alternatives.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: contrastive learning; multivariate time series anomaly detection; temporal patterns; multi-scale representation

Article.Title: Health information in Bangladesh: sources, trust, and perceived effectiveness of digital communication technologies
Article.Authors: Nakib S.; Rahman T.; Biswas S.; Rahat M.; Yeasin S.; Chowdhury T.; Husna M.; Noor J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study responds to the urgent need to understand the role that digital communication technologies play in shaping health information consumption in Bangladesh, a country that is grappling with persistent health crises, where common diseases often escalate to epidemic levels, resulting in substantial loss of life. Despite these challenges, public awareness of health issues remains suboptimal, compounded by a lack of preparedness, inadequate health infrastructure, and limited disease control programs. Data were collected between December 2024 and March 2026 through online surveys (n=191) and one-to-one interviews (n=65) conducted in both Bengali and English. Our diverse demographic includes both socio-economically privileged individuals and marginalized populations, such as those residing in the Korail slum of Dhaka. The findings expose a notable gap in awareness regarding the health information aspects of digital technologies, despite their widespread accessibility. Google and YouTube emerged as the most commonly used digital health information sources, followed by Facebook. ChatGPT appeared as an emerging supplementary source, while Arogga, DocTime, and Wikipedia were reported less frequently. Arogga is an online pharmacy and healthcare platform in Bangladesh, while DocTime provides online doctor consultation services. Although less frequently reported, these platforms were included to capture diverse digital health-information pathways beyond general search and social media platforms. Trust in these sources hinges on authenticity, information accuracy, medical reliability, popularity, verifiability, selective visual trust dynamics, and convenience.

Article.Title: Relationship of weather and plant microclimate parameters to rhizoctonia aerial blight development in soybean
Article.Authors: Bhamra G.; Gayithri M.; Deka R.; Das R.; Borah M.; Chand S.; Nayak J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rhizoctonia aerial blight (RAB), caused by Rhizoctonia solani Kühn, is a major constraint to soybean production. This study evaluated weather and plant microclimate effects on RAB development using a split-plot design (two genotypes as main-plot, five sowing dates as sub-plot) over two kharif seasons (May-October, 2022–2023) at Jorhat, Assam, in India. Minimum temperature and evaporation showed the strongest negative correlations with disease severity ( r = − 0.86 to − 0.87, p < 0.01); soil moisture was positively correlated ( r = 0.68–0.91, p < 0.01). Disease severity, AUDPC, infection rate, weather, and microclimatic parameters were monitored weekly. Disease severity increased progressively with crop age ( p < 0.001) and was higher under early sowing. The highest severity occurred in JS 335 sown on 17 May (35.61% PDI; AUDPC 237.90), while the lowest occurred in KDS 753 sown on 1 and 16 July (16.34% and 14.73% PDI; AUDPC 102.92 and 105.16; p < 0.001). Treatment-specific stepwise regression equations explained 73.3–92.7% of the observed severity variability (adjusted R² = 0.706–0.900), but they were fitted and evaluated using the same two-season, single-location dataset and therefore represent exploratory fitted relationships rather than independently validated forecasting models. Lower disease severity in late-sown treatments is interpreted as reflecting a shorter epidemic window and altered weather exposure across phenological stages rather than an independent causal effect of sowing date. This study would support in the development of forecast models to assess soybean RAB risk in the hot and humid areas.
