Article.Title: Robust design of air chamber to enhance impact connection strength of magnetic connectors on modular truss robots
Article.Authors: Kim J.; Shin W.; Go Y.; Choi M.; Seo T.
Article.Abstract: The connection mechanisms between neighboring modules are crucial subsystems in modular reconfigurable robot (MRR) systems. Magnetic connectors have been widely used for docking and undocking because of their mechanical simplicity and ease of use. However, they suffer from lower maximum tensile strength compared with mechanical docking mechanisms. This limitation is critical when modular truss robots are subjected to impact forces during locomotion, reconfiguration, docking, and undocking. To address this challenge, this paper presents a comprehensive parametric study and establishes design guidelines to maximize the impact resistance of magnetic connectors. As a core component of this approach, we investigate a mode-switching silicone air chamber designed to enhance impact absorption while mitigating the degradation of undocking capabilities. To evaluate the performance of the air chamber, we introduce an experimental evaluation method inspired by the Charpy impact test. Because the transient response of the soft structure is highly complex, the Taguchi and full factorial design method were employed to optimize the design parameters and derive the design guidelines. In the case of parameters, four factors were selected that could be judged to have an impact on the pneumatic stiffness, structural flexibility, and fluid damping of the air chamber. Also, each design parameter was divided into three levels, and five replicate experiments were conducted for each combination using an \(L_9(3^4)\) orthogonal array. The performance metrics consist of the sum of weighted values of \(M_1\) , which indicates the air chamber’s resistance to impact, and \(M_2\) , which reflects the indicator of mode switching between opening and closing the air chamber’s bottom hole. To explore the vicinity of the optimal value identified in the first experiment, a second experiment was conducted to pinpoint the final optimal parameter configuration, achieving a metric improvement of 0.051969 over the worst-case scenario. Finally, the practical feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed design guidelines were demonstrated through a hardware model using a prototype connector within a configured MRR system, demonstrating connection retention under selected impact conditions.

Article.Title: A hybrid antlion and hunter prey optimization paradigm for optimal allocation of distributed generation in radial distribution system
Article.Authors: Rajakumar P.; Sahoo B.; Senthil Kumar M.; Thangaraj D.; Sabarish P.; Vijayakumar G.; Mohanapriyaa N.; Mwanandiye E.
Article.Abstract: Optimal selection of distributed generation (DG) locations and sizes is essential for improving the performance of radial distribution systems (RDSs). This paper proposes a hybrid Ant Lion Optimizer–Hunter-Prey Optimizer (ALO–HPO) for optimal DG placement and sizing, combining the global search capability of ALO with the local refinement characteristics of HPO to achieve an improved exploration–exploitation balance. The proposed approach is formulated for both single-objective and multi-objective DG allocation, considering real power loss (RPL), voltage deviation, and voltage stability. Loss sensitivity factor (LSF) analysis is employed to identify candidate buses, thereby reducing the search space for DG placement. The proposed method is evaluated on the IEEE 33-bus RDS under static-load conditions, with additional assessment under 24-h time-varying load and peak-demand conditions. The investigation is further extended to the IEEE 136-bus RDS to demonstrate its robustness for large-scale power networks. The simulation results demonstrate that the hybrid ALO–HPO consistently reduces RPL while improving voltage profiles. For a single-objective DG allocation study, the hybrid ALO–HPO achieved an RPL reduction of 70.97% and 83.76% with the optimized inclusion of Type-I and Type-III DGs in the 33-bus RDS under static-load conditions. Comparatively, the ALO and HPO algorithms delivered only 66.60% and 68.22% power loss reductions for Type-I DGs and 71.39% and 78.14% for Type-III DGs, respectively, with optimal connections. Further, the hybrid algorithm converged in less computational iteration and required less computational time than the ALO and HPO. Similar performance was observed under time-varying load and peak-demand conditions, demonstrating its applicability to DG planning across different operating conditions.

Article.Title: Altered cellular phenotypes and a limited yet inflammation-focused transcriptional response induced by dexamethasone in caprine dermal papilla cells
Article.Authors: Ma S.; Liu M.; Ge C.; Zheng Y.; Wang S.; Gao T.; Shi Y.; Sun Y.; Xu Z.; Wang X.; Wang L.; Fu T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Glucocorticoids (GCs) serve as first-line immunosuppressive therapy for alopecia areata (AA), yet physiologically suppress hair growth and cycling. The molecular basis of this paradoxical effect remains incompletely understood, hindering optimization of GCs as.effective depilatory agents. Using transcriptomic data and immunofluorescence staining, we detected robust expression of the glucocorticoid receptor (GR, encoded by NR3C1 ) in caprine dermal papilla cells (DPCs) in vitro. At the cellular level, high-dose (10 − 4 M) dexamethasone (Dex), a synthetic GC, reduced metabolic activity and proliferation, increased the proportion of cells displaying apoptotic nuclear morphology, and skewed the cell cycle toward S-phase with concomitant G 2 decrease. At the transcriptomic level, RNA-seq identified a limited set of 373 Dex-responsive genes, including canonical GR targets (e.g., FKBP5 , PER1 , LEP ), which substantially overlapped with putative conserved targets of GR and/or the NF-κB p65 subunit ( RELA ) identified from cross-species ChIP-Atlas data. Upregulated genes featured inflammatory-response modulators (e.g., IL1R2 , CD163 , PTX3 ) and the entire cholesterol biosynthetic pathway (from HMGCS1 to DHCR24 ), whereas downregulated genes included well-characterized pro-inflammatory mediators (e.g., IL6 , CXCL8 , GROα , HGF ). Functional enrichment analysis identified both inflammatory pathways (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis) and cholesterol biosynthesis-related terms as significantly enriched. Notably, directional enrichment confirmed that inflammatory pathways were predominantly represented among downregulated DEGs, while cholesterol biosynthesis-related pathways were exclusively associated with upregulated DEGs. In addition, vascular development-related GO terms were also significantly enriched, with the contributing genes largely comprising the same set of inflammation-associated mediators-a pattern recapitulated in the PPI network, where classic inflammation genes (e.g., CXCL8 , IL6 , IL1R2 , CD163 ) clustered in a single independent network. These findings identify inflammation-associated gene expression as the predominant transcriptional signature in Dex-treated caprine DPCs. The concomitant enrichment of vascular development-related terms, driven by the same inflammation-associated mediators, represents a candidate correlate for future functional investigation. These observations provide a cellular and transcriptomic data-based insight for exploring GCs action in HF and for optimizing GCs-based depilatory strategies.

Article.Title: The secretory peptidase inhibitor R3HDML fine-tunes p38 MAPK signaling to maintain glomerular basement membrane architecture during renal aging and disease
Article.Authors: Rogg M.; Schell C.; Scherzinger A.; Keller J.; Meyer C.; Tholen S.; Kark C.; Boerries M.; Helmstädter M.; Schilling O.; Huber T.; Bechtel-Walz W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Serine proteases and their inhibitors are the most abundant class of proteolytic enzymes, involved in numerous biological processes such as cellular crosstalk. However, their role in renal diseases remains controversial. In this study, we identified the putative serine peptidase inhibitor R3HDML as a podocyte-specific expressed and secreted protein. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated generation of a novel floxed- R3hdml allele, demonstrated a regulatory function in renal aging and diabetic nephropathy. R3hdml knockout mice developed hump-like collagen IV deposits in the glomerular basement membrane (GBM), as well as mesangial expansion. These deposits induced the retraction of podocyte protrusions and the formation of a clustered, synaptopodin-positive actin cytoskeleton via integrin adhesion signaling. Despite the development of these key podocytopathy features, renal function was not severely impaired by the loss of R3hdml in aging, diabetic nephropathy, and during ischemia-reperfusion induced tubular injury and regeneration. Interaction proteomics revealed p38 MAPK signaling-related kinases, collagen modifiers, and N-terminal signaling peptide containing proteins, as potential R3HDML interactors. Consequently, Thr180/Tyr182 phosphorylation of p38 MAPK and downstream collagen IV deposition were suppressed by R3HDML in podocytes. In summary, we demonstrate a cell type specific mechanism by which podocytes maintain the composition and structure of the GBM in ageing and disease.

Article.Title: Thermal load responses of a large assembly workshop to envelope and ventilation design in a severe cold region
Article.Authors: Chu Q.; Wang H.; Wang J.; Liu H.; Ming Y.; Zhu S.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates thermal load responses to envelope and ventilation parameters in a large assembly workshop in Shenyang, China, using controlled DeST simulations. Reducing the wall U value from 1.0 to 0.1 W/(m 2 K) decreased annual heating load by 10.6%, compared with 1.85% for the same roof change, identifying wall insulation as the more influential measure. Lower shading coefficients reduced cooling load but increased heating load, indicating that thermal and daylight performance should be considered together. Increasing outdoor air exchange reduced cooling load while raising winter heating demand, and boundary analysis showed that sensible heat recovery can moderate this penalty. The interval from 3 to 4 ACH marks a transition in modeled cooling response and can inform ventilation design when combined with indoor air quality and production requirements. Because operational measurements and reliable production schedules were unavailable, the model was not calibrated and internal heat gains remained fixed. The results therefore represent comparative thermal responses rather than operational energy predictions. The findings establish a hierarchy of insulation, solar control, ventilation, and heat recovery measures for industrial buildings in severe cold regions.

Article.Title: Deep-learning-based electrode action potential mapping from annotation-free unipolar electrograms for substrate characterization in atrial fibrillation
Article.Authors: Seno H.; Kojima T.; Oshima T.; Yamagata K.; Yamazaki M.; Sakuma I.; Fujiu K.; Tomii N.
Article.Abstract: Catheter ablation for non-paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (non-PAF) remains limited by difficulty in identifying abnormal conduction regions, and current mapping relies on excitation-timing annotation that is unreliable under complex conduction. We developed Deep-learning-based Electrode Action Potential Mapping (DEAP Mapping), which reconstructs membrane potential distributions from unipolar intracardiac electrograms (EGMs) without local activation-time annotation. A convolutional neural network was trained on 13,824 in silico samples from a fibrotic human atrial bidomain model. In ex vivo porcine hearts ( N = 6), DEAP Mapping reconstructed conduction delays and blocks with high similarity to optical mapping (phase-variance-map SSIM 0.87 ± 0.07), outperforming conventional activation maps (0.36 ± 0.14). In a retrospective clinical study ( N = 12 non-PAF patients), the conduction patterns reconstructed by DEAP Mapping partly differed from those of existing methods, and phase-variance analysis revealed spatially continuous conduction heterogeneity with interpatient variability. DEAP Mapping provides annotation-free, optical-comparable substrate visualization from clinical catheter signals, potentially supporting personalized ablation.

Article.Title: Identification of a natural product derived NaV1.5 sodium channel modulator through integrated machine learning and molecular modeling
Article.Authors: Khosravi S.; Yarmohammadi F.; Hatamipour M.; Hoseini B.; Nejabat M.; Farokh S.; Hadizadeh F.; Karimi G.
Article.Abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common cardiac arrhythmia, and the voltage-gated sodium channel NaV1.5 represents a key therapeutic target. However, currently available sodium channel blockers are associated with proarrhythmic liabilities, underscoring the need for safer alternatives. This study aimed to develop an integrated computational framework to identify novel natural product–derived NaV1.5 modulators. A curated dataset of 1512 NaV1.5 inhibitors from ChEMBL was used to train LightGBM, XGBoost, and Random Forest classification models using optimized hybrid feature selection strategies. Model performance was evaluated using scaffold-based splitting and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC). The optimized models were applied to virtually screen 100,404 natural compounds from the COCONUT database. Top-ranked hits were further analyzed using molecular docking, 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations, MM/GBSA binding free energy calculations, and in silico ADMET profiling. The best-performing model (LightGBM) achieved an MCC of 0.66 on the external scaffold-based test set. Virtual screening identified 10 candidate compounds. Among them, Piperaduncin C exhibited favorable docking scores, stable interactions during molecular dynamics simulations, and a more favorable predicted binding free energy compared to quinidine. ADMET analysis suggested comparatively low predicted hERG liability and limited CYP2D6 inhibition. This integrated computational strategy identified Piperaduncin C as a potential NaV1.5 modulator. While experimental validation is required, these findings support its consideration as a natural product–derived scaffold for further antiarrhythmic drug development.

Article.Title: Multiscale mechanical behavior of the Qiongzhusi Formation shale
Article.Authors: Peng H.; Wang C.; Li Z.; Liu Y.; Chen Y.; Jia S.; Wang Q.; Lv Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Qiongzhusi Formation shale has attracted significant attention due to its vast mining potential; its macroscopic failure behavior is fundamentally governed by its microstructural characteristics and compositional evolution. This study employs a combined approach of laboratory testing and theoretical analysis to investigate the cross-scale mechanical correlations of the Qiongzhusi Formation shale. First, the mineral composition of the Qiongzhusi Formation shale was determined through XDR testing. Next, nanoindentation tests were conducted to obtain the mechanical properties of the minerals, and a Gaussian probability-based mineral deconvolution classification method was proposed to classify the nanoindentation dataset based on mineral mechanical properties. Finally, the macro- and micro-scale mechanical properties of the Qiongzhusi Formation shale were correlated using the Mori-Tanaka method. The results indicate that: (1) XDR mineral composition analysis revealed that the Qiongzhusi Formation shales exhibit high hardness and high brittleness; (2) the nanindentation curves of different minerals vary significantly; framework minerals such as quartz demonstrate strong brittle energy storage characteristics, whereas muscovite exhibits an extremely high proportion of plastic work; (3) A Gaussian probability-based mineral deconvolution classification method proposed in this paper can effectively classify minerals in nanindentation datasets based on their mechanical properties. (4) The macroscopic elastic modulus of shale exhibits significant sensitivity to changes in muscovite content, and an increase in quartz content significantly enhances the mechanical properties of the Qiongzhusi Formation shale. Furthermore, by integrating environmental geology with sustainable development needs, multiscale analysis techniques can reveal the mechanical response mechanisms of minerals and rocks under complex environmental conditions, thereby further expanding their application prospects in shale gas exploration and development engineering.

Article.Title: Adaptive active learning and metaheuristic-optimized transformer framework for robust intrusion detection in software-defined networks
Article.Authors: Shareef S.; Chinthakunta M.; Vijayan A.; Aditya C.; Lella K.; Mantena S.; Koteswararao C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Existing intrusion detection systems largely rely on static supervised learning models that require extensive labeled data and periodic retraining. Such approaches struggle to adapt to evolving attack patterns in dynamic software-defined networks. To address these limitations, this study proposes an adaptive intrusion detection framework that integrates uncertainty-driven active learning, metaheuristic-based feature selection, Transformer-based attack classification, and adaptive hyperparameter optimization within a unified software-defined networking architecture. Unlike conventional adaptive intrusion detection systems that rely on static feature representations or fixed learning strategies, the proposed framework continuously refines both the training data and model configuration to improve robustness against evolving cyberattacks. The proposed framework iteratively identifies informative samples for annotation, optimizes feature subsets using adaptive search, and continuously updates the classifier to maintain high detection performance under changing traffic distributions. The proposed system was evaluated using the ToN-IoT dataset and additional real-world traffic traces. Experimental evaluation on benchmark and real-world network traffic datasets demonstrated a detection accuracy of up to 97.92% and an F1-score of 97.10%. Although the optimization stage increases offline training time, the optimized model maintains efficient inference during deployment, making it suitable for practical software-defined network environments. Performance was evaluated over five independent runs using different random initialization seeds. Although the optimization and active-learning stages increase offline training time, the optimized model maintains efficient inference during deployment. Performance was evaluated over five independent runs using different random initialization seeds. The results demonstrate that the complementary use of adaptive sample acquisition, feature selection, and hyperparameter optimization provides an effective intrusion-detection framework for software-defined network environments.

Article.Title: Association of MALAT1 and TUG1 transcript levels and cardiometabolic diseases according to cholesterol saturated fat index
Article.Authors: Rasaei N.; Samadi M.; Shiraseb F.; Gholami F.; Tavakoli A.; Mohamadi A.; Khadem A.; SaeedYekaninejad M.; Clark C.; Mehrvar A.; Mirzaei K.
Article.Abstract: Cardiometabolic diseases in obese people, are influenced by the interactions of environment and genetics. Irregular expression of ”Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs)” is linked to several metabolic diseases. Therefore, we aimed to investigate the interaction between lncRNAs Metastasis-Associated Lung Adenocarcinoma Transcript 1 ( MALAT1 ), Taurine Upregulated Gene 1 ( TUG1) gene expression with dietary fatty acid quality indices (DFQI) on cardiometabolic risk factors among overweight and obese women. A total of 346 overweight and obese women (18–50 years), were included. Anthropometric measurements and biochemical determination were assessed. A validated and reliable 147-item semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) was used to evaluate food intake. The cholesterol-saturated fat index (CSI) was used as a measure of DFQI. A real-time polymerase chain reaction (real-time PCR) was performed to evaluate lnc-RNAs MALAT1 and TUG1 gene expression. The mean ± standard deviation (SD) of the age and body mass index (BMI ) of our participants were 36.568 ± 8.978 years and 31.215 ± 4.182 kg/m2 respectively. After controlling for confounding variables, significant positive interactions between lncRNAs MALAT1 and second tertile of CSI were observed on triglyceride (TG) (β = 6.268, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.760 to 11.776, p = 0.026), homeostasis model assessment insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) (β = 0.121, 95%CI = 0.013 to 0.230, p = 0.029). Similarly, a significant positive interaction between TUG1 expression and the second tertile of CSI was observed for HOMA-IR (β = 0.063, 95% CI: 0.017 to 0.108, p = 0.007). In addition, total cholesterol differed significantly across MALAT1 expression tertiles after adjustment (p = 0.046). No significant correlations were observed between MALAT1 or TUG1 expression and CSI. No adjustment for multiple testing was performed. In this exploratory, cross-sectional study, it appears that there might be a positive interaction between lncRNA MALAT 1 and CSI on cardiometabolic risk factors in overweight and obese women. However, due to methodological limitations, larger prospective studies are necessary to elucidate this concept.

Article.Title: Improving low-cost NO₂ sensor reliability under real-world air quality conditions by calibrating distributions instead of data points
Article.Authors: Sánchez D.; Schalm O.; Delgado L.; Rodríguez E.; Laguardia A.
Article.Abstract: Low-cost electrochemical NO₂ sensors enable dense air-quality monitoring, but their quantitative reliability depends strongly on calibration under field conditions. Laboratory calibration often fails to transfer to the field because temperature, humidity, cross-sensitivities, drift, ageing, and memory effects alter sensor response. Timestamp-paired co-location calibration addresses some of these effects but remains vulnerable to micro-scale heterogeneity: the sensor and reference analyser may not sample exactly the same air mass, resulting in scatter and weak point-wise agreement. This study introduces distribution-alignment calibration (DAC), which shifts the calibration target from individual timestamp-paired observations to the statistical structure of the complete co-located time series. Frequency distributions are constructed for the sensor signal and reference NO₂ concentrations, after which linear regression between matched descriptors—the mode, mean ± standard deviation, and selected percentiles—defines a transfer function that maps the sensor-signal distribution onto the reference-concentration distribution. DAC was evaluated using four NO₂ monitoring campaigns conducted at the same reference station over nearly three years. Compared with laboratory and conventional timestamp-paired co-location calibration, DAC improved the representation of baseline concentrations, short-term variability, and peak magnitudes. Descriptor-stability analysis indicated that approximately one month of continuous monitoring was sufficient for most descriptors to reach a relative variability below 10%.

Article.Title: Experimental and computational evaluation of antiproliferative, antioxidant, and antibacterial activities of Commiphora terebinthina aerial parts
Article.Authors: Nigussie G.; Zaib S.; Dekebo A.; Abebe M.; Tegegn M.; Zegeye A.; Meressa A.; Negassa T.; Abebe A.; Degu S.; Gemechu W.; Woldemariam M.; Niukalova M.; Hunsen M.; Endale M.; Chanyalew M.
Article.Abstract: Commiphora terebinthina Vollesen is a drought-tolerant species widely distributed in the Acacia-Commiphora woodlands of southern Ethiopia. The species plays a significant ecological and socio-economic role in pastoral communities by providing medicinal resin with antiseptic and insect-repellent properties, serving as an important dry-season browse for camels and other livestock, and generating household income through the harvesting and trade of incense. However, to date, no scientific study has been conducted on its chemical composition and pharmacological properties. Therefore, the present study aimed to isolate and characterize the chemical constituents from the aerial parts of C. terebinthina and evaluate their pharmacological activities. Silica gel chromatographic separation of the methanol extract afforded eleven compounds 1 – 10 , identified herein for the first time from this species using NMR and IR. Among them, compound 7 exhibited notable antibacterial activity with an MIC of 0.625 mg/mL against Staphylococcus aureus . Compound 4 showed antibacterial activity with an MIC of 0.625 mg/mL against Listeria monocytogenes . Compounds 7–10 demonstrated potent antioxidant activities in the DPPH assay, with IC₅₀ values ranging from 2.63 to 7.99 µg/mL. The methanol extract showed significant cytotoxicity against MCF-7 breast cancer cells (27.05% viability at 200 µg/mL). Molecular docking revealed that compound 6 exhibited higher predicted binding affinities with DNA gyrase B of E. coli (-7.4 kcal/mol) and S. agalactiae topoisomerase IV receptor (-9.8 kcal/mol) compared to ciprofloxacin (-7.1 and − 8.7 kcal/mol, respectively). Compound 8 showed stronger predicted binding affinity to Prdx5 (-5.8 kcal/mol) than ascorbic acid (-4.2), while compounds 7 – 10 bound more strongly to human myeloperoxidase (-6.4 to -9.6) than ascorbic acid (-5.0). Compounds 7 – 10 satisfied Lipinski’s Rule of Five, indicating favorable predicted drug-likeness. Additionally, compounds 8 and 9 were predicted to be non-mutagenic and non-toxic, with safety profiles comparable to ascorbic acid. These findings indicate that Commiphora terebinthina is a promising source of bioactive compounds warranting further experimental validation.

Article.Title: Transmission line bird hazard detection and tracking based on LBIT-YOLO
Article.Authors: Pei S.; Fu C.; Hu C.; She Y.; Pei Z.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: This paper proposes a lightweight detection-tracking integrated model LBIT-YOLO to solve the engineering problems in intelligent bird hazard monitoring for transmission lines. These problems include insufficient multi-category bird recognition, weak multi-target tracking, poor lightweight adaptability for edge devices, high false-triggering rate of bird repellent equipment and difficult field deployment. Based on YOLOv11, the model adopts PConv, SimAM attention and PIoU loss to improve detection performance, and integrates Bytetrack to realize continuous multi-bird tracking. Experimental results show that the model achieves 76.3% mAP@50 and 59.7% mAP@50–95, with 5.2 and 8.9% points higher than the original YOLOv11. The IDF1 score of multi-object tracking reaches 80.073%, increased by 15.458% points. With 5.18 MB weight and 39.9 FPS edge inference speed, the model can be deployed on Jetson Xavier NX terminals efficiently. Field tests verify that the model greatly reduces the false actuation rate of bird repellent systems and meets the engineering requirements of transmission line operation. It provides a practical solution for precise bird hazard prevention and control of power transmission infrastructure.

Article.Title: Neonatal bilirubin trajectory phenotypes and composite adverse outcomes: a two-database latent-class analysis (MIMIC-III and PIC)
Article.Authors: Lu J.; Wang M.; Xu H.; Zhu S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Total serum bilirubin (TSB) is measured routinely in neonates, but whether its trajectory over the first postnatal week adds prognostic value beyond a single measurement is unclear. In this preregistered two-database retrospective cohort study, we fitted latent-class trajectory models separately within each database (primary analysis) and on the pooled population (secondary analysis), including neonates admitted at < 28 days of age with at least three TSB measurements on postnatal days 0–7 (MIMIC-III, n = 2,951; PIC, n = 1,817). Site-specific models identified four classes in MIMIC-III and two in PIC; agreement with pooled classes was low (adjusted Rand index 0.23 and 0.25). High-risk classes were associated with the composite outcome of in-hospital death, necrotizing enterocolitis, or late-onset sepsis in both databases (MIMIC-III: OR 5.66 [95% CI 3.72–8.61] and 3.16 [2.10–4.77]; PIC: OR 2.13 [1.40–3.24]). Outcome drivers differed: MIMIC-III associations reflected necrotizing enterocolitis and late-onset sepsis, whereas the PIC association reflected death. In MIMIC-III, birth-weight adjustment substantially attenuated the associations (Class 4 3.05→1.16; Class 1 5.47→1.85), whereas in PIC, where birth weight was unavailable, admission-weight adjustment strengthened the Class 1 association (OR 2.45→3.81). The trajectory model did not exceed the peak TSB value in MIMIC-III (AUC 0.825 vs. 0.827) and performed poorly in PIC (AUC 0.582; corrected calibration slope 0.719), indicating failed external validation. The hour-specific Bhutani nomogram comparison was applied outside its validated ≥ 35-week population. Bilirubin trajectories largely mark underlying immaturity and illness severity rather than a bilirubin-specific effect; these hypothesis-generating findings require prospective validation, particularly in infants born at ≥ 35 weeks.

Article.Title: Attention specialized multi-view vision transformer for physics interpretable rolling element bearing fault diagnosis
Article.Authors: Vishal P.; Sahani S.; T. N.
Article.Abstract: Rolling element bearing fault diagnosis remains challenging because different fault conditions produce complex and overlapping vibration characteristics. This study proposes a physics-guided Multi-View Vision Transformer (MV-ViT) that converts raw vibration signals into six complementary image representations: Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT), Constant-Q Transform (CQT), Spectral Kurtosis (SK), Teager Energy Map (TEM), and Envelope Spectrum (ES). The six representations are jointly processed using a shared Vision Transformer with multi-head self-attention to learn cross-view relationships among time-frequency, spectral, impulsive, and nonlinear energy characteristics. The proposed framework is evaluated for five-class bearing fault diagnosis, including combined faults. MV-ViT achieves a maximum test accuracy of 99.62%, with a mean accuracy of 98.72 ± 0.70% across five random seeds, demonstrating consistent performance across independent training runs. The class-wise results further show F1-scores above 0.96 for the combined-fault class. Transform-level attention analysis identifies the Envelope Spectrum as the most influential representation, accounting for approximately 42.8% of the measured attention energy, followed by CQT at 20.3%. This observation is verified using leave-one-view ablation, where removing the Envelope Spectrum leads to a decrease in the test accuracy by 1.12% points, going from 99.62% to 98.50%, while removing the CQT, CWT, or TEM view results in a decrease in accuracy of 0.75% points. The ablation study on the architecture of the network also shows that decreasing the depth and embedding dimension of the Transformer does not cause noticeable changes in the accuracy, which implies that representation diversity plays a more important role in diagnosis than increasing the model capacity. In Leave-One-Working-Condition-Out experiments, the accuracy for unseen working conditions is achieved at levels of 97.92%, 98.01%, and 97.23%, respectively. The statistical comparison of the results of five repeated experiments shows no significant differences between the validation and test accuracy ( p = 0.3125). Finally, post-training quantization leads to a decrease in the size of the model from 77.9 MB in FP32 to 19.7 MB in INT8 and 9.9 MB in FP16Q4, preserving high classification accuracy.

Article.Title: Human dignity and its associations with self efficacy and treatment adherence in adults with type 2 diabetes in Iran
Article.Authors: Fallah Y.; Hashemi N.; Keshvari M.; Mardanian Dehkordi L.
Article.Abstract: Human dignity is a foundational ethical construct in chronic illness care, yet its relationship with self-efficacy and treatment adherence in type 2 diabetes remains insufficiently understood. This cross-sectional descriptive-analytical study examined the associations between perceived human dignity, diabetes self-efficacy, and treatment adherence among 200 adults with type 2 diabetes attending comprehensive health service centers in Isfahan, Iran. Data were collected using validated Persian versions of the Patient Dignity Inventory, Diabetes Management Self-Efficacy Scale, and Modanloo Treatment Adherence Questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression. Participants had a mean age of 58.70 ± 9.10 years, and 55.5% were female. The regression models had adjusted R 2 values of 0.111 for total self-efficacy and 0.248 for total treatment adherence. These findings indicate that perceived human dignity is associated with self-efficacy and treatment adherence among adults with type 2 diabetes. Longitudinal and interventional studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationships and potential explanations for these associations.

Article.Title: Trajectories of leisure-time physical activity behavior and risk of incident cardiovascular disease in middle-aged and older adults
Article.Authors: Li J.; Luo L.; Zhao Y.; Dallakoti N.; Peng Z.; Luo Y.; Miao Y.; Wu F.; Wu Y.
Article.Abstract: Leisure-time physical activity (LTPA) behaviors in later life are highly dynamic, yet the cardiovascular impact of these longitudinal trajectories remains unclear. This study aimed to characterize distinct trajectories of LTPA behaviors and investigate their association with incident cardiovascular disease (CVD) among middle-aged and older adults. This longitudinal study included 5,412 participants from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing. LTPA was assessed via a questionnaire at Wave 1 (2002-03), Wave 2 (2004-05), and Wave 3 (2006-07). Trajectories of LTPA behavior were identified using Group-Based Trajectory Modeling. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models estimated the associations between these trajectories and Incident CVD. A total of 5,412 participants (mean age 65.9 ± 9.31 years; 41.4% male) were followed for a median of 11.8 years, and 571 incident CVD events were recorded. Compared with the Stable Low trajectory, the Increasing group (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.44–0.92) and the Stable High group (HR 0.61, 0.43–0.86) were associated with lower CVD risk. Conversely, the Decreasing group was not associated with lower CVD risk (HR 1.03, 0.74–1.44). Notably, maintaining moderate activity was associated with lower CVD risk among those with hypertension (HR 0.65, 0.47–0.91) and ever-smokers (HR 0.67, 0.49–0.93). In this national, long-term cohort study of middle-aged and older adults, stable high or increasing trajectories of LTPA behavior were associated with a lower risk of Incident CVD compared with persistently low activity. Among participants with hypertension or a history of smoking, sustaining even moderate levels of LTPA was associated with a reduced CVD risk.

Article.Title: Micro-CT-informed Monte Carlo and experimental dosimetry of transcranial photobiomodulation devices
Article.Authors: Enam S.; Saint-Martin L.; Manwar R.; Avanaki K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Transcranial photobiomodulation (tPBM) is being investigated as a noninvasive strategy for modulating neural metabolism, neurovascular signaling, inflammation, and network activity; however, the field still lacks a quantitative framework that links nominal device parameters to delivered intracranial dose. Here, we combined micro-CT-informed Monte Carlo light transport with ex vivo phantom measurements to determine how wavelength, skull anatomy, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) thickness, commercial device design, delivery route, and thermal behavior govern tPBM dosimetry. Two human skull models were embedded in four-compartment scalp-skull-blood-filled diploic pore-CSF models and simulated at 23 wavelengths from 610 to 1267 nm using an LED-like source geometry. Experimental benchmarking used a porcine skin-human skull-artificial CSF gelatin phantom measured regionally with a spectroradiometer for three commercial helmet devices, complemented by intranasal-style 810 nm irradiance mapping, brain-gelatin transmission measurements, and infrared thermal imaging. Monte Carlo results showed that transmitted photon weight was highly sensitive to skull thickness, CSF depth, and diploic microstructure, and generally favored the 1064–1070 nm range under controlled source-detector conditions, whereas 1267 nm decreased due to increased long-wavelength absorption. In contrast, commercial-device phantom measurements showed that delivered post-stack output was not determined by wavelength alone: the 810 nm helmet produced substantially higher region-resolved transmittance than the two longer-wavelength devices, while a paired 810 versus 1070 nm comparison showed higher instantaneous post-stack irradiance/transmittance for 810 nm but comparable detector-plane fluence after accounting for the longer 1070 nm exposure duration. Intranasal mapping demonstrated route-dependent redistribution of irradiance, and thermal measurements revealed marked differences in device self-heating despite modest skin-surface temperature changes. These findings show that meaningful tPBM evaluation requires wavelength, anatomy, source geometry, irradiance, exposure time, transmission, fluence, and thermal response to be reported as distinct but interdependent parameters.

Article.Title: Renal hyperfiltration dynamics as a cardiovascular risk stratification marker
Article.Authors: Kim J.; Jeong S.; Yoon S.; Kim J.; Lee Y.; Jeong K.; Hwang H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Renal hyperfiltration (RHF) is a precursor to adverse clinical outcomes. However, RHF is a dynamic condition that can develop or disappear over time, and the prognostic implications of this transition remain unclear. This nationwide cohort study included 1,022,062 individuals of Korean ethnicity who underwent consecutive health screening examinations between 2012 and 2015. RHF was defined as an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) exceeding the 95th percentile after multiple adjustments. The participants were categorized based on their RHF transitions (RHF-free, developed, disappeared, and persistent), and risks of mortality and cardiovascular (CV) events were assessed. Compared with RHF-free individuals, those with persistent RHF had the highest risks of mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 1.61; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.24–2.10) and CV events (1.39, 1.13–1.71). Mortality risk increased across all other transition patterns regardless of exposure duration or the slope of hyperfiltration excess. Conversely, CV risk increased primarily in the RHF-disappeared, particularly with longer RHF exposure and declining hyperfiltration excess, but not with RHF-development. RHF dynamics showed distinct outcome-specific associations. Compared with the RHF-free pattern, mortality increased across all other RHF transition patterns, whereas CV events increased only in the RHF-disappeared and RHF-persistent patterns.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: renal hyperfiltration; cardiovascular events; estimated glomerular filtration rate; cardiovascular risk stratification; mortality

Article.Title: Fuzzy logic-based controller strategy for a single-input dual-output DC–DC converter for DC homes
Article.Authors: Ramesh D.; Poli T.; Siva Krishna Rao K D.; Bonthagorla P.; Ravi Varma C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Effective power management systems in DC household applications have raised interest in the analytical study of specialized converter topologies and control algorithms. This Article presents the design of a Single-Input Dual-Output (SIDO) converter with control strategies, including a Fuzzy Logic (FL) controller and a Proportional-Integral (PI) controller for voltage control. The proposed SIDO converter has a 48 V input and regulated 24 V and 12 V outputs. The experimental results are validated on the TMS320F28379D Microcontroller by maintaining the output voltage at a constant level in a closed-loop configuration with sensor-based feedback. The PI controller demonstrated a settling time of 5.83 ms and a voltage regulation of 4.7%, whereas the FL controller achieved a settling time of 3.24 ms and a voltage regulation of 0.5% for the 24 V output. The FL controller achieved a settling time of 5.29 ms and a voltage regulation of 1.25% for the 12 V output, significantly improving over the PI's 19.95 ms settling time and 2.16% voltage regulation. These results show that the FL controller has a better dynamic response in terms of rise time, settling time, overshoot, undershoot, and reduced ripple during load surges than the PI controller.

Article.Title: Explainable hybrid ensemble framework for lung cancer classification using deep CNNs and random forest
Article.Authors: Suzon M.; Shohan M.; Islam M.; Abdullah M.; Aktaruzzaman M.; Rahman M.
Article.Abstract: Lung cancer is still a significant cause of cancer death in the world. Thoracic computed tomography (CT) classification can be helpful in earlier diagnosis and better patient management. However, many deep-learning techniques require large annotated datasets, large amounts of computational resources and the techniques are not easily interpretable. This manuscript introduces a comprehensible hybrid approach to multiclass lung cancer classification based on two different transfer-learning backbones, DenseNet169 and MobileNetV2. They used several ensemble techniques to combine their class-probability outputs. For qualitative visual explanations of the image regions contributing to each prediction, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) was applied to the image after inference. The framework was evaluated with two publicly available thoracic CT datasets that include both benign and malignant, normal and non-small-cell lung cancer categories. The accuracy of the Random Forest stacker for the Chest CT dataset was 99.50% and 99.54% for the IQ-OTH/NCCD dataset. The results show that DenseNet169 and MobileNetV2 complementary probability outputs could be used as an effective decision-fusion method in lung cancer classification from different datasets with different class structures and diagnostic categories. The Grad-CAM technique also made the model predictions more transparent by identifying image areas that influenced the prediction. In general, the proposed framework presents a practical and comprehensible method for automated lung cancer classification, and serves as a valuable guideline in future studies regarding the development of robust, explainable, and clinically relevant computer-aided diagnosis in medical imaging.

Article.Title: Study on gas flow characteristics and pulse blockage removal regulation in unstable collapsed boreholes
Article.Authors: Song S.; Liu G.; Ma R.; Xiao P.
Article.Abstract: Gas drainage boreholes easily suffer hole wall collapse and coal particle blockage under in-situ stress and mining disturbance, drastically lowering gas extraction efficiency. To avoid the drawbacks of traditional dredging technologies, including drainage interruption and borehole wall damage, a gas pulse blockage removal method is proposed to achieve non-contact dredging using transient high-pressure gas. By establishing a gas pulse dredging test system for collapsed and blocked boreholes, the flow resistance characteristics under the coupling effect of collapse position and coal particle size are revealed. The regulation mechanisms of pulse pressure and frequency on blockage removal performance are clarified, and prediction models for pore response and structural penetration degree are developed, considering energy attenuation and coal structure evolution. The results indicate that collapse position and particle size jointly determine borehole flow resistance. Fine coal blockage at the borehole opening creates a global flow bottleneck, bringing the lowest extraction peak concentration and serious gas retention in surrounding coal seams. Pulse energy decays exponentially with transmission distance: bottom-blocked boreholes show weak unblocking effect with response lag over 10 s, while orifice blockage responds rapidly and achieves prominent concentration growth. Pulse pressure presents a marginal diminishing promotion effect on dredging efficiency. Under the conditions of this experiment, 0.4 MPa is the optimal pressure for most conditions, with gas concentration increment ΔC reaching 110–186%; further increasing pressure to 0.6 MPa limits ΔC growth below 20.3%, and fine coal at the opening undergoes turbulent secondary deposition to weaken dredging effect. Pulse frequency dominates cumulative energy input, and unblocking performance evolves following a three-stage rule of slow growth, accelerated breakthrough and decelerated growth. The optimal frequency is 4 cycles per 10 min for middle-borehole collapse (ΔC increment of 94.7%) and 3 cycles per 10 min for orifice collapse (ΔC increment up to 168.0%). The model developed quantifies key parameters, showing that the comprehensive reaction coefficient A decreases as particle size increases, whilst the energy accumulation index B rises with increasing propagation distance. Based on this, a differentiated pulse strategy of ‘high-frequency, short-duration pulses near the source and low-frequency, cumulative pulses far from the source’ is proposed, which provides a theoretical basis and guidance on parameter design for the efficient and precise unblocking of gas extraction boreholes.

Article.Title: Quality of life among community-dwelling older adults receiving primary care in the Podkarpackie region (Poland): a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Dziechciaż M.; Kuczek-Gaweł N.; Goniewicz K.; Khorram-Manesh A.; Al-Wathinani A.; Goniewicz M.
Article.Abstract: Quality of life (QoL) in older adults is influenced by a complex interplay of sociodemographic characteristics, multimorbidity, and medication burden. Understanding these relationships among community-dwelling older adults receiving primary healthcare may support more targeted approaches to care. To assess quality of life among community-dwelling older adults and examine its associations with sociodemographic characteristics, multimorbidity, and polypharmacy. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 101 community-dwelling adults aged ≥ 60 years receiving primary healthcare in the Podkarpackie region of Poland. Quality of life was assessed using the validated Polish version of the WHOQOL-BREF questionnaire. Sociodemographic characteristics, self-reported health conditions, and regular medication use were collected using an author-designed questionnaire. Bivariate analyses were complemented by multiple linear regression models assessing the independent associations of multimorbidity and polypharmacy with each WHOQOL-BREF domain after adjustment for age, marital status, and education. Polypharmacy was defined as the regular use of five or more medications. The highest mean quality-of-life score was observed in the social relationships domain (66.09 ± 16.88), whereas the lowest scores were observed in the physical health (51.41 ± 17.39) and environmental (51.58 ± 16.01) domains. In bivariate analyses, age, education, marital status, multimorbidity burden, and medication use were associated with quality of life in one or more WHOQOL-BREF domains. A greater number of reported health conditions and higher medication use were associated with lower scores across all four domains. In multivariable analyses, a greater number of reported health conditions remained independently associated with lower physical health scores (B = − 3.57, 95% CI −6.40 to − 0.74; p = 0.014) and lower social relationships scores (B = − 5.10, 95% CI −8.22 to − 1.98; p = 0.002). Polypharmacy was not independently associated with any WHOQOL-BREF domain after adjustment. Quality of life among community-dwelling older adults receiving primary healthcare varied across WHOQOL-BREF domains and was associated with both sociodemographic and health-related characteristics. Multivariable analysis indicated an independent association between greater multimorbidity burden and poorer outcomes in selected quality-of-life domains, whereas the associations observed for polypharmacy in bivariate analyses were attenuated after adjustment for disease burden and sociodemographic factors.

Article.Title: Development and validation of a postoperative prognostic nomogram for early-stage pancreatic cancer
Article.Authors: Cai P.; Luo C.; Zhao L.; Wu Z.; Yang X.
Article.Abstract: Our study aims to develop and validate individualized risk prediction models for all-cause mortality (ACM) and cancer-specific mortality (CSM) following surgery for early-stage pancreatic cancer (ESPC). Patients with pathologically confirmed stage I–II pancreatic cancer (PC) who underwent curative surgery between 2010 and 2019 were identified from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database. To identify the optimal predictor, the integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) and net reclassification improvement (NRI) indices were calculated to compare the predictive performance of the log odds of positive lymph nodes (LODDS) with that of other lymph node (LN)-related measures. LODDS demonstrated superior incremental discriminative ability for predicting ACM and exhibited a nonlinear association with ACM. The Cox regression-based nomogram for predicting ACM yielded area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.751 (95% CI 0.732–0.769), 0.799 (95% CI 0.784–0.813), and 0.824 (95% CI 0.808–0.840) for 1-, 3-, and 5-year survival, respectively, in the internal validation cohort. The competing risk model-based nomogram for predicting CSM achieved AUC values of 0.746 (95% CI 0.728–0.765), 0.808 (95% CI 0.794–0.823), and 0.832 (95% CI 0.816–0.847) for 1-, 3-, and 5-year CSM, respectively, in the validation cohort. The nomograms developed using Cox regression and competing risk models demonstrated favorable predictive performance based on internal validation. However, these findings should be interpreted with caution, as the nomograms remain preliminary prediction tools that require further validation. In the future, we will continue to incorporate additional external validation data to further validate and update the model.

Article.Title: An improved polarization-sensitive semi-analytic monte carlo simulation method for bathymetric lidar considering complex water-column stratification
Article.Authors: Li C.; Sun J.; Chen C.
Article.Abstract: Bathymetric lidar simulation has long treated seawater as an optically uniform medium, so existing models cannot reproduce how a thermocline, a turbidity layer, or a subsurface chlorophyll maximum reshapes the polarized echo. This paper develops an improved polarization-sensitive semi-analytic Monte Carlo (SMC) method for vertically stratified water. Earlier semi-analytic treatments either keep the polarization state but collapse the column to a homogeneous medium, or resolve the vertical structure but carry only a scalar photon weight; here the photon engine itself is rebuilt around layer-aware free-path marching and a layer-resolved local estimate, the forced-scoring weight is rederived so that it remains unbiased where the attenuation coefficient and the Mueller matrix change discontinuously, and the full Stokes state is carried through every scattering event. Importance sampling, adaptive step control near boundaries, and a GPU-mapped multiple-scattering synthesis keep the cost within reach of parameter sweeps. Against an analytic small-angle solution the method agrees to better than 1% inside the quasi-single-scattering window where that solution is valid, and against a converged conventional Monte Carlo reference it holds waveform and degree-of-polarization errors below 1% at roughly a tenth of the photon budget. Under stratified scenes it reproduces the layer-specific pulse broadening, peak delay, and co- and cross-polarized depolarization signatures that homogeneous models cannot generate. Reading the two polarization channels jointly reduces the stratification-induced bottom-detection bias from about 0.34 m to about 0.10 m once the waveform signal-to-noise ratio exceeds 25 dB, and it supports a preliminary retrieval of layer depth and optical contrast, although absorption and scattering remain strongly correlated. The evidence is entirely numerical, and the flat-layer geometry, the static sea surface, the neglect of wave-facet refraction, and the absence of any comparison with field-measured airborne waveforms bound what can be claimed from it.

Article.Title: Development and internal validation of a nomogram for predicting mechanical ventilation requirement in adult tetanus patients: a dual-center retrospective study
Article.Authors: Zhang B.; Wang H.; Kang J.; Liu J.; Liu X.; Zhong Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Objective This study aimed to develop and internally validate a nomogram model for predicting the risk of mechanical ventilation (MV) requirement in adult patients with tetanus, based on routine clinical and laboratory indicators, to facilitate early identification of high-risk patients and optimize allocation of critical care resources. Methods A retrospective cohort of 227 adult tetanus patients admitted to two largest tertiary hospitals in Southern Jiangxi between January 2012 and December 2024 was included. Patients were stratified into a MV group and a non-mechanical ventilation (NMV) group based on MV implementation. Independent predictors of MV requirement were identified through LASSO regression and multivariate logistic regression analyses. A nomogram prediction model was subsequently constructed. Internal validation was performed using the Bootstrap method with 1,000 resamples and 10-fold cross-validation. Model performance was comprehensively evaluated through ROC curves, calibration plots, and Decision Curve Analysis (DCA) to assess discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility. Results Five independent predictors of MV requirement were identified: age (OR = 1.032, 95% CI :1.011–1.054), chronic kidney disease (CKD,OR = 4.939, 95% CI :1.621–18.681), neutrophil count (NEUT,OR = 1.187, 95% CI :1.078–1.321), D-dimer (DD,OR = 1.089, 95% CI :1.019–1.182), and creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB,OR = 1.034, 95% CI :1.015–1.057). The nomogram demonstrated robust predictive performance, with AUC of 0.813 (95% CI :0.757–0.868), excellent calibration (mean absolute error = 0.029), and clinical net benefit across threshold probabilities of 0.1–0.8 confirmed by DCA. Conclusion We successfully developed a nomogram incorporating five readily available clinical parameters to predict MV risk in adult tetanus patients. The model exhibited favorable discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility, offering a practical tool for early risk stratification and targeted management of critical care resources. Future multicenter external validation is warranted to promote its clinical application.

Article.Title: Exploring the thermal and mechanical performance of hybrid bio composites reinforced with agro waste fibers and Turbinella pyrum shell powder
Article.Authors: Maniraj J.; Arunkumar A.; Deeban B.; Venkatesh S.; Baranitharan P.; Sriariyanun M.; Elaiyarasan U.; Yeshachew M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The use of sustainable natural fiber-reinforced polymer composites has attracted considerable attention mainly because they are environmentally friendly and can replace heavy components in engineering. The present work involves making hybrid epoxy composites reinforced with banana stem fiber (BSF), sugarcane bagasse fiber (SCF), and Turbinella pyrum shell (TPS) powder by the vacuum-assisted resin infusion technique. Nine composite samples (S1-S9) were made by changing fiber and TPS filler amounts to study the mechanical, thermal, moisture resistance, and morphological properties of the composites. The study found that the addition of the TPS filler might be the biggest reason for the composite’s better performance, which increased with filler content up to a maximum of 3 wt%. S6 showed the best tensile strength (20.0 MPa), tensile modulus (2.95 GPa), flexural strength (49.8 MPa), flexural modulus (4.48 GPa), and impact strength (8.1 kJ/m 2 ); these properties were 332.9%, 136.0%, 255.7%, 250.0%, and approximately 523.1% better than the unfilled S1 formulation. S5, in contrast, has the highest compressive strength (9.40 MPa), compressive modulus (1.34 GPa), and minimum moisture absorption (1.95%), which indicates very good resistance to water. The composite formulation with the lowest weight and highest strength was selected, based on different performance criteria (mechanical, thermal, and moisture resistance), by multi-response optimization. It was revealed that S6 was the composite formulation showing the most balanced characteristics. Thermogravimetric studies showed that the composites with TPS filler have better thermal capability, and SEM imaging revealed discrepancies among composite samples for fibre pull-out, void presence, filler dispersion, and the nature of the crack. EDX analysis was used to detect the calcium carbonate (CaCO 3 ) enriched material of the TPS filler, and its contribution towards the increase of composites’ stiffness and thermal resistance was acknowledged. These results portray the possibility of using TPS-filled hybrid epoxy composites as green products for lightweight structural and engineering applications.

Article.Title: Evaluating anatomy-constrained GWO-assisted non-negative matrix factorization for muscle synergy extraction in cowboy-dance kicking across synergy numbers
Article.Authors: Dong X.; Liang T.; Han R.; Luo W.; Zheng W.; Li D.; Ma Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cowboy-dance kicking is a rapid, multi-joint lower-limb task that requires coordinated activation of multiple muscles, resulting in complex electromyographic patterns for which low-dimensional muscle-synergy analysis can provide a compact description of the recorded coordination structure. Conventional non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) is widely used for such decomposition, but its solutions can be sensitive to initialization and local convergence, and solutions with similar reconstruction quality may still differ in their internal muscle-loading structure. This study therefore evaluated an anatomy-informed Grey Wolf Optimization-assisted NMF framework (GWO-NMF) designed to refine low-dimensional synergy structure while balancing anatomical guidance against reconstruction fidelity. Surface EMG was recorded from eight muscles of the dominant left kicking limb in 12 sports-dance students during metronome-paced cowboy-dance kicking, with 83 valid trials retained for analysis. Following EMG preprocessing and time normalization to a common 0–100% movement cycle, conventional NMF and anatomy-constrained GWO-NMF were compared across synergy numbers k = 3–6. Outcomes included synergy-weight sparsity ( Δsparsity w ), anatomy adherence, global VAF, RMSE, R 2 , cross-trial stability, and computational runtime. Trial-level outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models with algorithm, synergy number, and their interaction as fixed effects, while accounting for repeated trials within participants; planned contrasts were adjusted using the Holm procedure. GWO-NMF largely preserved the dominant muscle-weight composition and temporal activation patterns while increasingly modifying secondary loadings as k increased. Synergy-weight sparsity was significantly higher under GWO-NMF at k = 4 (Δ = 0.01295, p = 0.003), k = 5 (Δ = 0.03161, p < 0.001), and k = 6 (Δ = 0.06356, p < 0.001), but not at k = 3. Anatomy adherence improved significantly only at k = 6 (Δ = 0.02636, p < 0.001). No significant reconstruction differences were detected at k = 3–4, whereas GWO-NMF showed lower VAF and R 2 and higher RMSE at k = 5–6 (all Holm-adjusted p < 0.001).Cross-trial stability showed a lower directional estimate at k = 5 but did not reach statistical significance (Δ = − 0.03267, Holm-adjusted p = 0.077); a significant reduction was observed at k = 6 (Δ = − 0.06165, p < 0.001). Computation time was approximately 133–138 times longer for GWO-NMF across the tested synergy numbers. GWO-NMF should be regarded as a k -dependent, anatomy-guided refinement framework rather than a universal replacement for conventional NMF. At lower decomposition orders, particularly k = 4, it increased structural compactness without a detectable reconstruction penalty, whereas stronger structural modification at higher k was accompanied by reduced reconstruction fidelity, lower cross-trial stability, and substantially greater computational cost. Improvements in sparsity and anatomy adherence therefore describe structural properties of the extracted decomposition and should not be interpreted as direct evidence of specific biomechanical functions or greater neurophysiological validity without independent kinematic, kinetic, or neural validation.

Article.Title: Depth-dependent inter-pixel distance in trench-isolated LGADs for shallow radiation detection
Article.Authors: Zareef F.; Mianroodi P.; Rebarz M.; Fernandez-Martínez P.; Bates R.; Maneuski D.; Bullough M.; Obłakowska-Mucha A.; Szumlak T.; Moffat N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The fill factor of finely segmented low-gain avalanche detectors (LGAD) is limited by the effective inter-pixel distance (IPD), particularly when charge is generated far from the gain layer. In this work, 200 $$\mu $$ m thick trench-isolated LGADs (TI-LGADs) fabricated by Micron Semiconductor Ltd. were characterized using single-photon and two-photon absorption transient current technique measurements at ELI Beamlines to determine the dependence of IPD on interaction depth, illumination direction, and gain-layer doping. The measurements show that the effective IPD is smallest near the trench side of the device and increases as charge generation occurs deeper in the sensor bulk, with a minimum measured IPD of approximately 7 $$\mu $$ m. Devices with higher gain-layer doping exhibit larger IPD, indicating a trade-off between gain and effective fill factor, while depth-resolved measurements reveal enhanced charge collection at the trench edge consistent with a localized high-field region at the gain-layer/trench interface. These results show that, in thick TI-LGADs, back-side shallow absorption corresponds to charge generation far from the multiplication region and can therefore lead to an increased IPD, which may limit the performance of small-pixel designs. The findings identify an important design constraint for TI-LGADs intended for applications involving shallow energy deposition under back-side illumination.

Article.Title: VDAC1 regulates disulfidptosis susceptibility and associates with the immune microenvironment via multi-omics analysis in lung adenocarcinoma
Article.Authors: Chen C.; Yang Y.; Fu W.; Wu H.
Article.Abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), the predominant subtype of non‑small cell lung cancer, continues to exhibit high incidence and mortality due to tumor heterogeneity and therapy resistance, underscoring the need for novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets. This study aimed to systematically characterize the expression, prognostic value, immune‑microenvironment modulation, and functional role of VDAC1 in LUAD, with a focus on its regulation of glucose‑deprivation–induced disulfidptosis. By integrating multi‑omics data from public resources, we performed differential expression, copy‑number variation, survival, immune‑infiltration, pathway‑enrichment, and single‑cell/spatial transcriptomic analyses. Findings were validated using immunohistochemistry on 15 paired LUAD samples and functional assays in A549 and PC‑9 cell lines. VDAC1 was significantly upregulated at mRNA and protein levels in LUAD, and its high expression correlated with poor prognosis and therapy resistance. Genomic copy‑number amplification and promoter hypomethylation cooperatively drove VDAC1 overexpression. Single‑cell and spatial transcriptomics confirmed VDAC1 enrichment specifically in malignant epithelial cells. Immune‑microenvironment analysis revealed a positive correlation with antigen presentation and a negative correlation with CD4 + T‑cell recruitment, suggesting a role in fostering an immunosuppressive niche. Pathway analysis linked VDAC1 to pro‑tumor processes including cell‑cycle progression, hypoxia response, and DNA‑damage repair. Transcriptomic analysis further showed that VDAC1-high tumors were preferentially enriched for disulfidptosis core genes—including SLC7A11—distinguishing this program from ferroptosis and apoptosis. Functionally, VDAC1 knockdown suppressed cystine uptake, partially restored GSH/GSSG balance and NADPH levels, attenuated mitochondrial ROS accumulation, and ameliorated ultrastructural damage, thereby alleviating glucose‑deprivation–triggered disulfidptosis. In summary, this integrated multi‑omics and experimental study establishes VDAC1 as both an independent adverse prognostic factor and a key regulator of disulfidptosis in LUAD, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for selectively inducing tumor cell death.

Article.Title: Deficiency of non-muscle myosin IIA promotes neuroinflammation by impairing autophagic degradation of VCAM-1 in brain endothelium
Article.Authors: Zhang H.; Li Y.; Zhao X.; Zhao Y.; Gu J.; Pan H.; Liu A.; Lin J.; Peng Y.; Wang L.; Zhang H.; Cao J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Endothelial cell dysfunction is a major driver of neuroinflammation, a critical contributor to neurological disorders. Non-muscle myosin IIA (NMIIA), a key cytoskeletal protein, has been implicated in cerebrovascular pathology, but its role in endothelial-mediated neuroinflammation remains unclear. This study reveals that NMIIA expression is downregulated in brain microvascular endothelial cells during aging. Using in vitro knockdown and endothelial-specific conditional knockout mouse models, we demonstrate that NMIIA deficiency specifically upregulates VCAM-1 protein without affecting its mRNA or other inflammatory mediators. Mechanistically, NMIIA loss impairs autophagic flux, particularly the autophagosome-lysosome fusion, leading to inhibited autophagic degradation and subsequent accumulation of VCAM-1. Proteomic analysis and biochemical assays identified Caveolin-1 (Cav-1) as a direct binding partner of NMIIA. NMIIA deficiency promotes the redistribution of the autophagy-related protein ATG5 into Cav-1-enriched lipid raft domains, a process known to suppress autophagy initiation. Functionally, soluble VCAM-1 released from NMIIA-deficient endothelial cells promotes pro-inflammatory polarization of microglia and induces neuronal apoptosis in vitro. In vivo, NMIIA iECKO mice exhibit increased microglial activation, impaired hippocampal neurogenesis, neuronal loss, and significant deficits in learning and memory behaviors. Collectively, our findings define a novel NMIIA–Cav-1–autophagy–VCAM-1 regulatory axis in brain endothelium, positioning NMIIA as a crucial maintainer of neurovascular homeostasis by preventing VCAM-1-driven neuroinflammation. This pathway provides new mechanistic insights into aging-related cerebrovascular dysfunction and offers potential therapeutic targets for neuroinflammatory diseases.

Article.Title: Privacy-accuracy trade-off optimization in sensitive surveys through regression estimation
Article.Authors: Ali M.; Khan M.; Hussain S.
Article.Abstract: Collecting reliable information on sensitive quantitative characteristics remains a big challenge in social and behavioral surveys, as respondents often hesitate to answer truthfully. The Randomized Response Technique (RRT) helps protect privacy, but many existing models do not balance privacy and efficiency well. To resolve this problem, this study proposes a novel regression estimator designed to accurately estimate the sensitive population mean. The strength of this approach lies in incorporating non-sensitive auxiliary variables into data collected under strict privacy protocols. To thoroughly evaluate the behavior of this estimator, we apply it to data collected through existing distinct randomized response models. Theoretically, the proposed regression estimator is unbiased and benefits from a straightforward, closed-form variance expression, allowing for practical application. We assess privacy protection using a deviation-based metric, while efficiency is assessed through in terms of sampling variance. To capture the overall performance of the models, we also employ unified, weighted, and log-weighted composite measures that balance both privacy and precision. Extensive numerical examples and Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate that the proposed estimator usually has lower variance and offers a better balance between privacy and efficiency than other existing mean estimators. These results indicate that the proposed estimator provides a practical, efficient, and privacy-preserving tool for surveys involving sensitive quantitative data.

Article.Title: Construction of a leak detection and pressure regulation system for municipal water distribution networks integrating digital twin technology
Article.Authors: Li P.; Gao F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Aging municipal water networks lose a substantial share of treated water to leakage, yet detection and pressure control are still pursued on separate models, so neither can inform the other. This paper builds an integrated system in which both functions read from and write to one continuously synchronized digital twin. The twin couples an open-source hydraulic kernel, a pressure-dependent demand closure and emitter-based leakage to an ensemble Kalman filter and a weighted least-squares recalibration step, so that heads, flows, Hazen–Williams roughness coefficients and demand multipliers are updated from multi-source telemetry rather than frozen at commissioning. Detection normalizes twin residuals against diurnal demand patterns and combines a sliding-window CUSUM statistic with a Mahalanobis joint test; the residual field then feeds a graph attention network that scores each junction and aggregates node posteriors into ranked suspect pipe segments. Regulation solves a bi-objective program over valve settings and pump speeds, weighting nodes by their leak posterior so that head is reduced hardest where water actually escapes, subject to service-head, switching and resilience constraints. Results are reported network by network rather than pooled alone. The pooled F1 reaches 0.916 and the Top-5 hit rate 0.816, against 0.836 and 0.573 for the strongest baseline, with per-network F1 ranging from 0.903 on C-Town to 0.932 on Net3 and mean detection latency falling to roughly four hours. On the official BattLeDIM 2019 scenarios, held out as an independent validation set, the same model retains an F1 of 0.818 but sheds about twenty points of Top-5 hit rate, which bounds how far the in-house training distribution generalizes. Closing the loop on C-Town raises leakage reduction from 24.6% under uniform depressurization to 37.5% while holding service compliance at 99.4%. Ablations identify state assimilation as the load-bearing component. Code and result records accompany the paper; scalability beyond a few thousand nodes, transient hydraulics and the capital cost of dense instrumentation remain open limitations.

Article.Title: Parental attitudes toward myopia prevention: insights from an Australian survey
Article.Authors: Wang B.; Watt K.; Chen Z.; Jalbert I.; Kang P.
Article.Abstract: Prevention or delay of myopia onset has emerged as a promising strategy to reduce the long-term burden of myopia and associated ocular complications. However, little is known about parental awareness of myopia and acceptance of interventions aimed at preventing myopia onset in children. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among Australian parents and guardians of children aged 4–18 years. Participants completed questions assessing myopia awareness, knowledge, personal and child myopia status, and willingness to participate in pre-myopia intervention programs. Associations between participant characteristics and willingness to engage in pre-myopia intervention were evaluated using multivariable ordinal logistic regression. A total of 800 responses were included in the analysis. Participants with myopia and those with a myopic child demonstrated significantly greater myopia awareness and knowledge than other participants. Overall willingness to consider pre-myopia intervention was high, with 76.8% of participants responding Yes, 19.5% Maybe, and 3.8% No. Greater myopia knowledge was independently associated with increased willingness to participate in pre-myopia intervention (OR 1.34, 95% CI 1.25–1.43, p < 0.001). Participants with both myopic and non-myopic children demonstrated lower willingness compared with participants with no myopic children. Cost, evidence of treatment effectiveness, and recommendation from an eye-care professional were the most influential factors affecting participation and adherence to intervention. Australian parents demonstrated high willingness to engage in pre-myopia interventions. Myopia knowledge was the strongest independent predictor of willingness, whereas direct experience with myopia was not. These findings suggest that improving parental understanding of myopia may be critical for successful implementation of future pre-myopia prevention programs in Western populations.

Article.Title: Hot-ion modes in the high-field compact spherical tokamak Globus-M2
Article.Authors: Kurskiev G.; Miroshnikov I.; Minaev V.; Sakharov N.; Gusev V.; Petrov Y.; V. Chernyshev F.; N. Bakharev N.; Kiselev E.; Telnova A.; Tkachenko E.; Tukhmeneva E.; Shchegolev P.; Skrekel O.; Zhiltsov N.; N/A N/A.; Bakharev N.; Balachenkov I.; Buts M.; Chernyshev F.; Ermakov N.; Goryainov V.; Gusev V.; Kavin A.; Khromov N.
Article.Abstract: The development of the next generation of spherical tokamaks (STs) or fusion neutron sources based on STs depends on achieving high-temperature plasma regimes with enhanced energy confinement. Here, we report the realization of hot-ion modes in the Globus-M2 compact ST (R = 0.36 m, a = 0.24 m), where ion temperatures reach 50 million Kelvin (> 4 keV) at high plasma densities (> 10 20 m -3 ). By doubling the toroidal magnetic field from 0.5 T to 1 T, we observed a threefold improvement in thermal energy confinement. Our analysis reveals that high-torque neutral beam injection effectively suppresses ion-scale turbulence, enabling ion heat transport to approach the fundamental neoclassical limit at low collisionality. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the increased magnetic field plays a critical role in suppressing turbulent heat fluxes, ensuring robust thermal insulation. These results provide firm experimental validation for the high-field compact ST potential as a fusion neutron source or an essential testbed for fusion technology development as well as for plasma physics studies under low collisionality conditions demonstrating that record-level plasma parameters can be maintained in a compact device through the synergy of strong magnetic confinement and rotation-induced turbulence suppression.

Article.Title: Effects of tomato leaf handling methods on growth performance and chemical composition of Schistocerca gregaria
Article.Authors: Luo Y.; Förster N.; Mewis I.; Schulz S.; Bogdanova M.; Grebenteuch S.; Rohn S.; Ulrichs C.; Yakti W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Tomato leaves are an abundant agricultural waste stream; however, their use as feed is limited due to their high fiber content and the presence of toxic glycoalkaloids. This study evaluated the feasibility of utilizing tomato leaves for rearing Schistocerca gregaria (desert locust) as a source of insect protein. Locusts were fed freshly harvested leaves, leaves stored for different durations, and leaf cuttings maintained in water to preserve freshness. The results showed that storage and water-based maintenance reduced the need for daily harvesting without negatively affecting growth performance or survival, while affecting the accumulation of Cu and Zn. Notably, although tomato leaves maintained in water contained high levels of α-tomatine and dehydrotomatine, their accumulation in the locusts was reduced. Crude protein content ranged from 59.37% to 60.51%, and α-linolenic acid (C18:3, n-3) was the predominant fatty acid, accounting for 40.63% to 43.12% across treatments. Overall, tomato leaves can be stored or appropriately handled as an alternative to freshly harvested leaves without compromising locust growth, while enhancing the accumulation of Cu and Zn and reducing the frequency of daily harvesting and feeding operations.
