Article.Title: A SHA-256 driven multi-PWLCM image encryption scheme with adaptive image-dependent permutation-diffusion
Article.Authors: Nagarad P.; Patro K.; Das S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract With the rapid growth of digital image transmission over open and insecure communication channels, the need for robust and computationally efficient image encryption techniques has become increasingly important. This paper presents a SHA-256-driven multi-PWLCM image encryption scheme with adaptive image-dependent permutation–diffusion for secure visual data protection. Rather than constructing a new chaotic system, the proposed framework adopts three conventional Piecewise Linear Chaotic Map (PWLCM) instances within a plaintext-dependent, functionally role-separated architecture. Plaintext-derived SHA-256 information diversifies the operational initial conditions and control parameters of the three PWLCMs, while the PWLCM instances are explicitly assigned to row permutation, XOR diffusion, and column permutation, respectively. An adaptive hash-dependent flipping mechanism further introduces image-dependent spatial transformation, while the same processing framework supports both grayscale and color images. The security behavior is evaluated through histogram and chi-square analysis, adjacent-pixel correlation, global and local information entropy, differential analysis, key sensitivity, chosen-plaintext and ciphertext-based cryptanalytic evaluations, noise and cropping robustness, and statistical randomness testing. Direct randomness evaluation of the PWLCM-generated sequences and finite-precision analysis under IEEE-754 double-precision arithmetic are additionally performed to assess the numerical behavior of the underlying chaotic generators. The experimental results show near-uniform ciphertext distributions, information entropy close to the theoretical value for 8-bit data, low adjacent-pixel correlations, and NPCR and UACI values close to their expected levels. Chosen-plaintext experiments further show substantial plaintext-dependent changes in the generated row-permutation indices, column-permutation indices, and diffusion-key elements, limiting direct reuse of the tested equivalent permutation–diffusion information across different plaintexts. Computational analysis indicates that the principal pixel-wise operations are linear, while sequence sorting determines the conservative overall complexity bound of $$O(P\log P)$$ . Overall, the results demonstrate the feasibility of combining plaintext-dependent parameter diversification, explicit functional separation of lightweight PWLCMs, and unified grayscale/color processing within a comparatively compact image-encryption architecture.

Article.Title: ASC-MAPPO: attention-based communication and safety-constrained multi-agent proximal policy optimization for cooperative path planning and dynamic obstacle avoidance of connected autonomous vehicles
Article.Authors: Liu B.
Article.Abstract: Fleets of connected autonomous vehicles have to solve two problems at once: they must agree on who goes first, and each of them must stay clear of traffic that nobody controls. This paper presents ASC-MAPPO, an attention- and safety-constrained variant of multi-agent proximal policy optimization designed for exactly that coupling. The planning task is cast as a decentralized partially observable Markov decision process and solved with centralized training and communication-enabled distributed execution. Each vehicle encodes its own observation into a 128-dimensional embedding, broadcasts it inside a 50 m radius, and aggregates the messages it receives through a masked four-head attention module that weights neighbours by situational relevance rather than treating them alike. A shared-parameter actor emits continuous steering increments and longitudinal accelerations; agent-wise critics and a monotonic mixing network resolve credit assignment during training only. Safety is enforced on two levels. A differentiable Gaussian risk surrogate shapes the reward and supplies smooth gradients, and a projection layer confines every executed action to an admissible set defined by obstacle clearance, road boundaries, lane keeping and friction-limited vehicle dynamics. Collisions themselves are always decided by a binary contact test, never by the surrogate. In CARLA experiments covering highway merging, a four-way intersection and a curved rural road, with four cooperative vehicles and three obstacle densities, ASC-MAPPO reaches a 99.2% avoidance success rate in the dedicated avoidance suite, shortens the mean fleet arrival time in the high-density intersection by 18.2% relative to MAPPO (11.6% when averaged over all scenarios and densities) and attains a cooperative efficiency of 0.93. Ablations separate the contributions of communication, attention, value decomposition and the projection layer; transfer tests, a complexity analysis and latency measurements for up to twelve vehicles delimit the operating envelope of the method.

Article.Title: Combined application of biochar and silicon on physiological and antioxidant defense mechanism of wheat against plastic induced stress
Article.Authors: Kapoor R.; Hasanuzzaman M.
Article.Abstract: The exponential rise in plastic waste has become a major problem for the environment and public health because of its high stability, non-biodegradable nature and long-term persistence. This investigation analyzed the effects of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) on wheat plants and the alleviation of its adverse effects using jackfruit shell biochar (JSBC) and potassium silicate (Si). The pot experiment was conducted to evaluate the individual and combined effects of PET, JSBC, and Si treatments on the growth of wheat plants. After treatment, wheat plants were harvested for analysis of morphological and biochemical variables, oxidative stress markers, enzymatic and non-enzymatic antioxidants and glyoxalase enzyme activities. Exposure of wheat plants to PET treatment decreased morphological traits and relative water content, caused photosynthetic damage and increased lipid peroxidation and electrolyte leakage. The combined treatment of JSBC and Si in PET-treated pots reduced electrolyte leakage, levels of H 2 O 2 and O 2 ·− by 29%, 53%, and 31%, respectively, as compared to the PET treatment. Application of JSBC and Si, individually or combined, enhanced growth attributes of wheat plants and alleviated PET-induced oxidative stress by modulating activities of antioxidant and glyoxalase enzymes. The findings of the present study underscore the beneficial effects of the combined applications of biochar and potassium silicate for enhancing growth of wheat plants under plastic stress. Thus, the combined application of JSBC and Si acts as a promising strategy for plastic contaminant mitigation and reutilization of waste materials as renewable assets to combat plastic pollution in the soil ecosystem.

Article.Title: Machine learning based distribution mapping of gold in soil samples using aqua regia digestion and solid phase extraction
Article.Authors: Rezazadeh M.; Esmaeily D.
Article.Abstract: In the present work, aqua regia followed by solid phase extraction using activated carbon was developed for soil sample treatment. The analytical approach was further integrated with machine learning algorithms enabling the prediction of gold potential zone. Some modifications such as roasting the samples and hydrofluoric acid addition for silicon structure removal of the samples have also been investigated. The analytical performance of the method was evaluated via certified reference materials and geological samples, at different concentration levels. Random Forest, Gaussian Process Regression and Ordinary Kriging models were subsequently used considering nonlinear spatial relationships, uncertainty prediction and generate predictive gold distribution map. Despite the significant effect of sample roasting, HF addition had only a minor and negligible effect (according to t-test at 95% confidence level) and the proposed method was able to detect gold concentrations ranging from 18.0 ng/g to 53,000 ng/g in soil samples and down to 0.01 µg/mL in aqueous samples with correlation coefficients greater than 0.9991. The method accuracy and precision were in the range of 3.7–9.6 and − 9.5-+7.4, respectively. Comparison of responses obtained for the analysis of 40 different geological samples via fire assay and aqua regia digestion shows a good compatibility which verified the aqua regia as a simple, low cost and reliable treatment technique.

Article.Title: Econometric-prior-guided multi-head attention with application for interpretable multi-horizon financial forecasting
Article.Authors: Fu J.; Abdulabbas A.
Article.Abstract: Reliable financial forecasting requires both predictive accuracy and transparent model behavior. This study presents Economic-Loss Guided Multi-Head Self-Attention (ELG-MHSA), a transformer framework that regularizes three attention heads toward distinct econometric and statistical priors: GARCH-based conditional variance, a trailing moving-average target for mean reversion, and a one-sided trend estimate. The priors are constructed separately within each causal input window and are normalized over eligible historical positions only, preventing future information from entering training or evaluation. The proposed losses are optimized jointly with the forecasting objective without changing the transformer encoder structure. Experiments on VIX Futures, FRED-MD, and Binance BTC-USD compare ELG-MHSA with GARCH(1,1), EGARCH, a standard multi-head transformer, and the Temporal Fusion Transformer. The reported results are interpreted as descriptive performance differences unless accompanied by formal uncertainty estimates. The framework is intended to improve the economic interpretability of attention while retaining multi-horizon predictive capacity.

Article.Title: Roadbase performance and modification mechanisms of TBM-excavated gneiss muck utilizing a fiber–geopolymer synergistic stabilization system
Article.Authors: Zheng H.; Wei M.; Shang Q.; Tong X.
Article.Abstract: The disposal of TBM muck has become a pressing issue in tunnel construction. This study addresses the utilization of 295,000 m 3 of gneiss muck excavated from the DXL Tunnel in western China by modifying it with low‑calcium fly ash (FA), ground granulated blast‑furnace slag (GGBS), carbide slag (CCS), and basalt fiber (BF) to produce a roadbase material. The optimal mix, designated X‑FGC (FA:GGBS:CCS = 9:4:1 with 0.3% 12‑mm BF), was determined via response surface methodology. Mechanical and durability properties were assessed through unconfined compressive strength (UCS), splitting tensile strength (STS), wet‑dry cycling, and sulfate attack tests; the modification mechanisms were investigated using FTIR, XRD, and SEM. The results show that, after 7 days of curing, the modified muck achieves a UCS of 7.22 MPa and an STS of 0.764 MPa. After 20 wet‑dry cycles and 40 days of sulfate exposure, the UCS loss rates are 11.3% and 4.53%, respectively. Performance enhancement is attributed to the formation of a multi‑gel system (N‑A‑S‑H, C‑A‑S‑H, and C‑S‑H), which cements particles, fills pores, and promotes fiber bridging. However, although increasing the X‑FGC content generates more gels and improves mechanical strength and wet‑dry resistance, it also retards polymerization, reduces the degree of gelation, and impairs sulfate resistance. Overall, X‑FGC exhibits promising mechanical performance and durability as a roadbase material, while incorporating a high proportion of TBM‑excavated gneiss muck (approximately 79% of the total wet‑dry mass in the optimal mixture).

Article.Title: LVAERMIL: enhancing multiple instance learning robustness via latent variational autoencoders
Article.Authors: Sáez-Maldonado F.; García L.; Cooper L.; Goldstein J.; Molina R.; Katsaggelos A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) has become widely used in medical imaging classification, where precisely annotated data is scarce. MIL methods treat whole slide images as bags of instances (the patches), and only bag labels are required for training. Recently, MIL methods have shown extraordinary results in both classification and tumor localization benchmark tasks. However, in real-world scenarios, slides may be contaminated by tissue from other specimens or artifacts that can extrapolate MIL models and produce medical errors. This presents a challenge for widespread use of MIL in pathology labs. In this work, we propose Latent-VAE-Robust-MIL (LVAERMIL), a novel probabilistic module that learns the instance-level data distribution using a Variational Autoencoder trained on the latent space produced by a feature extractor. This enables the detection of out-of-distribution patches and their elimination from MIL bags, improving the robustness of any MIL model to whole slide image contaminants. The extensive evaluation performed by contaminating two datasets using four foreign tissues and using two scanner-induced artifacts shows that LVAERMIL maintains or improves the accuracy of the eight state-of-the-art MIL models on contaminated datasets, especially when the amount of contamination in the slides is high.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: multiple instance learning; whole slide images; out-of-distribution detection; robustness

Article.Title: Entropy guided spectral phenological feature engineering using Sentinel-2A data for Pan-Arctic vegetation classification
Article.Authors: Huo S.; Shuai Y.; Qu G.; Ma X.; Oke S.; Rafaelg R.
Article.Abstract: Arctic vegetation plays a critical role in regulating terrestrial ecosystem structure and function. Existing remote-sensing classification products are often limited in thematic detail and accuracy because of the region’s inaccessibility and the underuse of high-dimensional spectral and phenological information. This study established a Pan-Arctic vegetation classification system comprising Barren Tundra (BT), Sparse Tundra (ST), Cyperaceae Tundra (CT), Graminoid Tundra (GT), Wet Tundra (WT), Grass, and Shrub. A total of 161 homogeneous samples were selected across the Pan-Arctic domain through multi-source consistency filtering and visual verification. These samples were used for spectral–phenological feature development, entropy-based feature evaluation, threshold definition, and model construction. We introduced spectral characteristic information entropy (SCIE) and spectral characteristic information weight coefficients (SCIWC) to characterize spectral information content and relative feature importance. The entropy-guided feature set improved inter-class separability; for example, green-band information helped distinguish BT from ST, whereas red-band information contributed to the separation of CT and GT. Final map accuracy was assessed independently using 761 reference points in Yamal’skiy Rayon, which were not used for feature development or model construction. The classification achieved an overall accuracy of 90.67% and a Kappa coefficient of 0.88. A comparison with CALC-2020 indicated broad spatial consistency, while differences reflected the finer thematic detail and differing class definitions of the two products. These results demonstrate the potential of entropy-guided spectral–phenological feature engineering for fine-scale Arctic vegetation mapping, while further multi-region and multi-year validation is needed to assess Pan-Arctic transferability.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: wet tundra; Sentinel-2A; Shannon entropy; pan-Arctic

Article.Title: Machine-learning prediction of freezing temperature in Pb-contaminated soils remediated with biochar
Article.Authors: Safi L.
Article.Abstract: Throughout the Pb-contaminated soil rehabilitation procedure, biochar may change the structure of the soil, which has a significant impact on soil freezing. This study examined the change in freezing temperature ( \(ToF\) ) during the biochar remediation of Pb-contaminated soils using machine learning techniques, such as Light Gradient Boosting ( \(LGB\) ), Extreme Gradient Boosting ( \(XGB\) ), Extra Tree Regression ( \(ETR\) ) and Random Forest Regression ( \(RFR\) ). The data used in this research is derived from previously conducted trials. The system's reliability is significantly impacted by hyperparameters, which must be selected using metaheuristic optimization approaches. To accomplish this, a variety of algorithms are used, including the Catch Fish Optimization ( \(CFO\) ). The information, which includes 360 ToF data points, came from studies that were submitted for publication. After studying each element, the study group came to the decision that 80% (288) of the dataset would be utilized for training and model construction, while the other 20% (72) of the dataset would be utilized for validating the model. Randomization, normalization, cross-validation, scaling, and feature significance evaluation were some of the pre-processing methods used to the dataset. The prediction efficacy of \(ETR(CFO)\) and \(RFR(CFO)\) in predicting ToF was assessed using metrics. With the data, ToF can be reliably predicted by both \(ETR(CFO)\) and \(RFR(CFO)\) over other baseline models. The assessment process assessed the reliability and plausibility of each model using evaluation criteria, logical analysis, ranking score, and model difference percentage. In achieving its primary target, the \(RFR(CFO)\) model performs better than the alternative model.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: lead-contaminated soil; extra trees regression; machine learning prediction; random forest regression; hyperparameter optimization

Article.Title: De novo transcriptome analysis reveals the effects of abiotic and biotic elicitation on naphthoquinone and flavonoid production in Lawsonia inermis L
Article.Authors: Das D.; Mullick R.; Mallick B.; Samanta D.; Roy D.
Article.Abstract: Lawsonia inermis L. is a medicinally and commercially important plant, contributing to 9% of India’s medicinal exports. The growing demand for its principal phytochemical (lawsone) is difficult to be met through traditional farming. Although elicitation can help in augmentation of phytochemicals, the absence of a reference genome limits our understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms leading to enhanced secondary metabolite production. This study amalgamates elicitation and transcriptomics in understanding the augmentation of lawsone, rutin, and kaempferol. Salicylic acid(50 µM) was the best abiotic elicitor, followed by yeast extract (biotic elicitor), enhancing the secondary metabolite content. In vitro plants, treated with salicylic acid (50 µM) showed 1–2 times more accumulation of lawsone, rutin, kaempferol, 5–10 time more secondary metabolite accumulation, as compared to control in vitro plants. Transcriptome assembly generated 23,648 unigenes. Further analysis revealed genes involved in phenylpropanoid, flavonoid, terpenoid and lawsone biosynthetic pathways to be upregulated in salicylic acid treatment. RT-qPCR showed enhanced expression of PAL, CHS, HST, COQ4, FQRL, MenE, MenB and MenD genes, responsible for the enhanced secondary metabolite in the plant. Collectively, these findings provide an elicitor-induced production of secondary metabolites, which can pave the way for future manipulation and sustainable production of these phytochemicals for industrial need.

Article.Title: Empagliflozin attenuates ISO-induced myocardial injury through PGC-1α-mediated mitochondrial biogenesis and improved fatty acid metabolism
Article.Authors: Zhang C.; Jin X.; Wei L.; Bian Y.; Qi X.
Article.Abstract: Empagliflozin, as a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor (SGLT2i), has demonstrated beneficial cardioprotective effects in patients with heart failure. However, the cardiac benefits of empagliflozin are not entirely dependent on the classical SGLT2 receptor-mediated mechanism and may also be associated with the improvement of cardiomyocyte mitochondrial function and fatty acid metabolism. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of empagliflozin on cardiac function and elucidate its potential targets and underlying mechanisms. Rats with ISO-induced myocardial injury were subsequently treated with empagliflozin by intragastric administration. Compared with the model group, empagliflozin improved cardiac function and alleviated pathological changes, including myocardial hypertrophy and fibrosis. Empagliflozin significantly reduced the expression levels of cytochrome c (Cyt c), Bax, and cleaved-caspase-3, increased Bcl-2 expression, attenuated cardiomyocyte apoptosis, and decreased serum levels of BNP, sST2, and cTnT. Empagliflozin preserved mitochondrial morphology and cristae structure, reduced myocardial ROS levels, significantly increased mitochondrial membrane potential and mtDNA copy number, and upregulated the expression of PGC-1α, NRF1, NRF2, and TFAM. Following empagliflozin intervention, the expression levels of PPARα, CPT1, CPT2, and MCAD were increased, promoting fatty acid utilization in myocardial tissue and enhancing ATP production. In the ISO-induced H9c2 cell model, empagliflozin exerted biological effects similar to those of a PGC-1α agonist, promoting mitochondrial biogenesis, facilitating the utilization of accumulated fatty acids in cardiomyocytes, improving energy metabolism, and reducing apoptosis. Importantly, siRNA-mediated knockdown of PGC-1α attenuated the effects of empagliflozin on mitochondrial biogenesis, fatty acid utilization, energy metabolism, and cardiomyocyte apoptosis. Empagliflozin improves cardiac function and attenuates myocardial remodeling in ISO-induced HF rats. Its cardioprotective effects may involve PGC-1α-mediated mitochondrial biogenesis, which promotes fatty acid utilization and oxidation, improves energy metabolism, and reduces cardiomyocyte apoptosis. This study provides new experimental evidence for the cardioprotective mechanisms of empagliflozin.

Article.Title: Hematologic and biochemical prognostic indicators of influenza disease severity in naïve and preimmune ferret (Mustela putorius furo) models
Article.Authors: Barkes A.; Kieran T.; Daggett G.; Maines T.; Jean S.; Pulit-Penaloza J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ferrets ( Mustela putorius furo ) are widely used to evaluate influenza virus pathogenicity and pandemic risk, but hematologic and biochemical parameters are not routinely included in these assessments. In this study, we performed a comparative analysis of complete blood count and serum chemistry profiles in immunologically naïve and preimmune ferrets following intranasal inoculation with different influenza virus strains. Seasonal A(H1N1)pdm09 and A(H3N2) viruses and a less virulent A(H5N1) virus caused mild, nonfatal disease with limited or transient bloodwork changes in naïve ferrets. In contrast, naïve ferrets challenged with a highly virulent A(H5N1) virus showed virus detection beyond the upper respiratory tract, rapid disease progression accompanied by pronounced metabolic and biochemical disruption, necessitating humane euthanasia. Pre-existing immunity altered disease progression following challenge with this virus, with A(H1N1)pdm09-preimmune ferrets displaying reduced viral replication, less severe disease, and less pronounced biochemical disruption compared to A(H3N2)-preimmune ferrets. Overall, lymphopenia was common during acute infection in both ferret models; however, it did not distinguish nonfatal from fatal disease. Conversely, worsening biochemical changes, including hyperglycemia, increased alanine aminotransferase, total bilirubin, amylase, globulin, and electrolyte disturbances, were most evident in ferrets with severe A(H5N1) disease. These findings support the use of serial hematologic and serum chemistry analyses as complementary endpoints for evaluating disease severity, immune-mediated protection, and humane endpoint decisions in naïve and preimmune ferret models.

Article.Title: Attacking visual foundation depth estimation model with adaptable adversarial patch
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Wang J.; Yin J.
Article.Abstract: Vision foundation models (VFMs) have demonstrated strong generalization ability across various downstream tasks and scenes. However, their vulnerability to adversarial examples, particularly in safety-critical applications, remains insufficiently understood. This paper investigates the attack effect of physical adversarial patches on monocular depth estimation (MDE) models, specifically the foundation model Depth Anything, widely used in fields such as autonomous driving and robotic navigation. First, we introduce a universal patch attack pipeline and present the following key observations: 1) Attack effectiveness : In the pixel-wise dense prediction task of MDE, adversarial effects are largely confined to the patch area and do not spread to other regions, indicating that foundation models have enhanced adversarial robustness compared to traditional models. 2) Attack interpretability : The learned adversarial patches often contain semantically meaningful content, such as forests or buildings, leading to corresponding erroneous depth predictions, which adds interpretability to the attack’s behavior. Based on the observations, we focus on improving the applicability of adversarial patches in real-world environments by proposing a plug-and-play augmentation method, termed MixCrop, that enhances attack effectiveness, especially when patch semantics are incomplete or repetitive. Extensive experiments including physical attacks demonstrate that the patched objects can effectively vanish from the predicted depth map. The learned patches also have strong generalization ability across various objects and scenes.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: vision foundation models; monocular depth estimation; adversarial robustness; adversarial patches; autonomous driving safety; physical assault

Article.Title: Taphonomy and early diagenesis of a semi-articulated dinosaur tail from the late maastrichtian of southwestern Europe
Article.Authors: Torrent M.; Parra S.; Sellés A.
Article.Abstract: Articulated dinosaur remains are extremely rare in Upper Cretaceous alluvial deposits of southwestern Europe, limiting detailed reconstructions of post-mortem processes in these settings. We present a taphonomic, sedimentological, and early diagenetic analysis of a semi-articulated mid-caudal segment of a lambeosaurine hadrosaurid, recovered as a detached sandstone block from the Planta del Mestre locality (Late Maastrichtian Tremp Basin, South-Central Pyrenees). The specimen comprises eleven middle caudal vertebrae and associated neural spines and four haemal arches preserved in close anatomical association. Semi-articulated arrangement, lack of abrasion, and mineralized intervertebral fibrocartilage indicate short residence time following minimal transport. Stage 2 subaerial weathering on centra and stepped displacement of distal elements reflect differential exposure during partial entombment and post-depositional settling. Parallel grooves on neural and haemal spines record early biological interaction by a medium-sized ziphodont theropod, likely an abelisaurid, during initial decay stages. Petrographic analysis reveals early ferruginous impregnation under oxidizing conditions promoted sediment stabilization and sealing bone pores, preserving delicate structures against decay. Associated planktonic foraminifera suggest episodic marine influence within the floodplain. These results highlight the role of localized geochemical pathways in generating high-fidelity preservation within otherwise unfavourable floodplain taphonomic settings.

Article.Title: Risk model for predicting mortality risk in patients with cerebral infarction: a cohort study using the MIMIC-IV database
Article.Authors: Zhang J.; Lin Y.; Liu M.; Yan H.
Article.Abstract: Cerebral infarction represents a significant health threat, causing mortality and long-term disability. This study investigated prognostic variables associated with cerebral infarction and developed a risk model to predict mortality, thereby offering new strategies to enhance patient care and improve overall outcomes. Participants were selected from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database, covering the period 2008–2019. The study population comprised patients with cerebral infarction admitted to the intensive care unit. Univariate Cox regression analysis, proportional hazards assumption testing, machine learning (least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression), and multivariate Cox regression analysis were performed to identify prognostic variables. Based on these variables, a risk model was developed and subsequently evaluated. After excluding ineligible individuals, 109 patients with cerebral infarction were included. The anion gap [hazard ratio (HR) = 1.1040, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 1.0070–1.2110, P = 0.0356], platelet count (HR = 0.9965, 95% CI = 0.9939–0.9990, P = 0.0072), and glucose concentration (HR = 1.0050, 95% CI = 1.0000–1.0090, P = 0.0483) were identified as prognostic variables. A risk model utilizing these prognostic variables classified patients into high- and low-risk cohorts, with high-risk patients displaying lower survival probabilities. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis demonstrated the strong predictive performance of this risk model, with all areas under the curve exceeding 0.7. The study identified the anion gap, platelet count, and glucose concentration as prognostic variables for cerebral infarction. The findings underscore the potential of the risk model to enhance clinical decision-making and management for patients with cerebral infarction.

Article.Title: Solar-powered VANET architecture for sustainable and smart traffic management in arid regions
Article.Authors: Hajlaoui R.; Filali A.; Mahfoudhi S.; Alghazi S.; Moulahi T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Energy-autonomous roadside communication is essential for sustainable intelligent transportation systems (ITS), particularly in arid regions that combine abundant solar resources with highly dynamic traffic demand. Existing solar-powered vehicular ad hoc network (VANET) approaches typically treat roadside unit (RSU) placement, activation scheduling, and traffic prediction as separate problems, limiting their ability to coordinate long-term infrastructure siting with short-term communication demand and energy availability. This paper presents an integrated solar-powered VANET framework that coordinates these spatial and temporal decisions within a unified architecture. A Discrete Grey Wolf Optimization (D-GWO) method performs spacing-aware RSU siting by maximizing traffic coverage, network centrality, and solar harvesting potential while penalizing redundancy. A Traffic-Aware Duty Cycling (TADC) controller regulates RSU operation through traffic hysteresis, battery state-of-charge guards, and minimum dwell times. A Joint Activation Score (JAS) couples long-term site utility with runtime activation, and a Random Forest-based traffic anticipation module enables proactive scheduling; the Activation Timeliness Gain (ATG) metric quantifies the resulting improvement in activation timing. Trace-driven simulations on the Ha’il City road network, using measured solar irradiance and real traffic data, demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves packet delivery ratios (PDR) of 94.5–97.9%, reduces end-to-end delay (E2ED) by 7–35 ms, and lowers per-RSU energy consumption by 20–33% relative to representative baselines, while maintaining fully off-grid operation under the evaluated conditions. Predictive assistance further advances RSU activation by up to 2.1 min during traffic surges without additional energy cost. These results show that coordinated spatio-temporal design can simultaneously enhance communication reliability, responsiveness, and energy efficiency, supporting the feasibility of energy-autonomous VANET operation under the evaluated Ha’il topology, traffic densities, irradiance trace, and log-distance radio model.

Article.Title: Fuzzy relation-aware graph role clustering for sentiment-augmented fake news detection
Article.Authors: Zhang F.; Zhang P.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: Existing research on fake news detection shows that sentiment information in social media comments can provide important clues for judging the authenticity of news. However, existing sentiment enhancement methods usually treat comments as independent samples and mainly rely on the semantic representation and sentiment features of individual comments for role clustering, ignoring the potential relationship structure between comments. In fact, the user roles in the comment section are not entirely determined by the sentiment polarity of individual comments. Comments expressing the same negative sentiment may come from blind followers, skeptics, or debunkers. To address this issue, we propose a fuzzy relation-aware graph role clustering framework, FRGC. Specifically, FRGC models comments under the same news event as nodes and constructs an event-level comment graph based on semantic similarity to capture latent comment relations beyond individual representations. It further introduces sentiment probability distributions and their uncertainty to calibrate semantic edge weights, avoiding the direct use of unreliable sentiment polarity for relation modeling. Through this design, sentiment information is incorporated as an uncertain auxiliary signal while preserving the dominance of semantic relations. Furthermore, a graph encoder layer and a weak graph regularization term are introduced to obtain relation-enhanced comment representations and improve the stability of latent role clustering. Experimental results on multiple datasets validate the effectiveness of FRGC. Specifically, FRGC achieves an F1-score of 97.1 on Weibo-comp and obtains a Macro-F1 of 36.5 and RMSE of 74.3 on RumourEval-19, outperforming existing methods and demonstrating the effectiveness of fuzzy relation-aware graph modeling for sentiment-enhanced fake news detection.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: fake news detection; social media comments; fuzzy relations

Article.Title: Estimated built-up surface increase within water-related lowland screening areas in Vietnam from 2000 to 2025
Article.Authors: Pham A.
Article.Abstract: We estimate built-up surface increase within water-related lowlands across Vietnam using Global Human Settlement Layer (GHSL) estimates, Joint Research Centre surface-water history and Shuttle Radar Topography Mission terrain data accessed through Google Earth Engine. A 1 km equal-area grid supports reporting for 710 fixed districts over five five-year intervals from 2000 to 2025. Positive GHSL differences measure estimated surface increase rather than verified construction. National built-up stock rose from 2,943.50 to 5,681.95 km². In 2020–2025, the screened share reached 14.53%, and screened increase was 78.72% above 2015–2020. The Mekong River Delta contributed 78.24% of the national net rise in screened increase between these intervals. A historical-only water-screen sensitivity gave a 25.62 km² increase (+ 83.52%), supporting the direction of the latest change. Exact district-boundary weighting changed the latest screened amount by − 0.06 km². Dynamic World change showed modest agreement with GHSL increase (Spearman ρ = 0.312). A modelled 50-year river-flood benchmark showed stronger national correspondence (ρ = 0.845) than within the Mekong (ρ = 0.368). The findings identify districts for local hydrological and planning assessment. Estimated GHSL epochs, static screening and unknown co-location within grid cells limit interpretation as flood exposure.

Article.Title: Dance course participation is associated with reductions in anxiety sensitivity physical concerns in college students
Article.Authors: Price M.; Bradford D.; Jha A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract College students face heightened risk for anxiety. Anxiety sensitivity (AS), the fear of anxiety-related sensations, is a key vulnerability factor for anxiety. Dance courses, which incorporate aerobic exercise, may provide interoceptive exposure to anxiety-related sensations, which may correspond with reductions in AS. The current quasi-experimental study investigated the association between participation in university dance courses relative to non-dance courses, and changes in AS over time. Undergraduate students were recruited from dance courses, including traditional dance and mindfulness-infused dance, and non-dance courses. Consented students ( N = 271) completed a testing battery online at the beginning of the academic semester (T1) and 7 weeks later (T2). This battery included the Anxiety Sensitivity Index-3 (ASI-3), demographic and engagement information, and other metrics outside the current scope. Multilevel models revealed greater reductions in AS physical concerns in students enrolled in dance courses, relative to those in non-dance courses, even after accounting for out-of-class exercise engagement and intensity ( b = -1.13, SE = 0.36, t (227.81) = -3.15, p = .002, 95% CI [-1.84, -0.42]). Our findings suggest that university dance courses may warrant further investigation as a promising, pragmatic, and scalable curricular approach associated with reductions in AS physical concerns.
Article.Topic: Anxiety, Depression, Psychometrics, Treatment, Cognitive Processes

Article.Title: Numerical study on combined regeneration cooling of supercritical kerosene and supercritical CO₂ considering cracking effect
Article.Authors: Zhong X.; Jiang Y.; Liu J.
Article.Abstract: To meet the efficient heat transfer demand of thermal protection systems for hypersonic vehicles at extremely high thermal environment (Ma ≥ 8), this work numerically investigates the thermo-hydraulic characteristics of composite cooling of supercritical RP-3 kerosene pyrolysis and supercritical CO₂ regeneration cooling channels. Three channel sections (circular, triangular, rectangular) and two flow arrangements (co-current flow and counter flow) are studied. Based on the SST k-ω model and a 24-steps 18-components cracking reaction mechanism, the coupling rules of cracking reaction, flow behavior and heat transfer are systematically revealed. Compared with the single-kerosene baseline, the dual-fluid configuration suppresses the peak wall temperature by about 25–30%, and the sCO₂ side absorbs 39–49% of the total heat load. Counter-current flow yields higher local Nusselt numbers, whereas co-current flow gives lower and more uniform wall temperatures together with a higher cracking rate, revealing a trade-off between heat-transfer intensity, wall-temperature suppression and fuel conversion. The circular channel provides the best temperature uniformity and the highest overall performance index η that balances heat-transfer enhancement against flow-friction penalty. The combination of a circular section and co-current flow is found to be optimal. This study provides a reference for the structural design and optimized operation of active thermal protection systems for hypersonic aircraft.

Article.Title: Scalable binary-to-gray and Gray-to-Binary code converters using atomic silicon dangling bonds: hierarchical physical design, complexity analysis, and robustness evaluation
Article.Authors: Bathula N.; Misra N.
Article.Abstract: The atomic silicon dangling bond (ASDB) technology platform holds promise as an efficient solution for atomically precise digital circuits with extremely high integration density, low energy operation, and compatibility with silicon technology manufacturing processes. However, scalable and functional code conversion systems based on ASDB technology are still unknown. In this work, scalable architectures for binary-to-gray (B2G) and Gray-to-Binary (G2B) code converters are suggested based on hierarchical physical design approach within the SiQAD simulation framework. Physical layouts are synthesized and verified through SimAnneal simulations for 3-bit, 4-bit, and 8-bit converters, while the analytical scalability model is built to evaluate the physical resource requirements of large scale 16-bit, 32-bit, 64-bit, 128-bit, and 256-bit converters. Performance evaluation is performed with respect to the number of dangling bonds, physical size, propagation delay, area-delay product (ADP), computational complexity, and energy consumption of ground state configurations. For the directly simulated 8-bit converters, the B2G and G2B architectures require 300 and 418 dangling bonds, respectively, with G2B requiring approximately 39.3% more dangling bonds than B2G. Binary-wire routing accounts for 66.3% of the total dangling bonds in the 8-bit B2G converter and 73.4% in the corresponding G2B converter, confirming routing as the dominant physical resource. The analytical scalability model further projects 9461 dangling bonds for the 256-bit B2G converter and 13175 dangling bonds for the corresponding G2B converter, indicating a consistent increase in physical resource requirements with converter width. It is shown that there exists a fundamental computational asymmetry between the two code conversion architectures. The proposed B2G converter relies on parallel XOR operations and its computational depth remains constant with O (1) complexity. In contrast, due to the recursive XOR relationship, the propagation delay of G2B converter increases linearly with O ( N ) computational complexity. Dangling bond decomposition demonstrates that binary-wire routing becomes the scalability bottleneck for larger code conversion architecture due to dominant contribution to the physical realization cost. Analysis of fabrication-induced geometric variations, including dangling bond misalignments, proves the stability of logical function and electrostatic charge configuration. The presented hierarchical design methodology provides a scalable approach for atomic code converters and sets practical design guidelines for ASDB-based digital systems in beyond-CMOS computing.

Article.Title: A machine learning-based web application aids Kawasaki disease diagnosis and predicts its outcomes
Article.Authors: Nagao Y.; Kita N.; Fujii S.; Sameshima S.; Nishimura Y.; Okubo H.; Endo H.; Yamane I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Unless Kawasaki disease (KD) is promptly treated with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), patients may develop IVIG-unresponsiveness and aneurysm. We analysed 628 KD and 155 KD-like cases to develop machine learning models for having KD (i.e., being diagnosed with KD), IVIG-unresponsiveness and aneurysm formation. We applied LASSO logistic regression to illness-day-indexed data incorporating family/previous histories and laboratory variables (e.g., neutrophils, total bilirubin, C-reactive protein, and AST). Optional inputs included BNP, IgG, fibrinogen, and echocardiographic Z scores. On Day 4, all models achieved AUCs > 0.7 in the test dataset: having KD (0.779), IVIG-unresponsiveness (0.772), and aneurysm formation (0.710). On Day 5, the model achieved a positive predictive value > 90% for having KD. When combined with predictions of unresponsiveness or aneurysm, 90% of complicated KD cases were identified. These models were implemented in a web-based and intranet-integrated application, enabling early diagnosis and risk stratification of KD across resource-limited and resource-rich settings.

Article.Title: Seaweed-derived biostimulants differentially enhance growth, nutritional composition, antioxidant capacity, and sensory quality of cultivated Caulerpa racemosa
Article.Authors: Windarto S.; Lee M.; Zhou Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Seaweed-derived biostimulants offer a promising strategy to enhance the productivity and functional quality of edible seaweeds. This study evaluated the effects of aqueous extracts from Halymenia sp., Halimeda sp., Sargassum sp., Kappaphycus sp., and Gracilaria sp. on the growth, biochemical composition, nutritional quality, antioxidant properties, and sensory acceptance of cultivated Caulerpa racemosa under controlled 35-day laboratory culture conditions. All extracts contained detectable phytohormones (indole-3-acetic acid, kinetin, zeatin, and gibberellic acid) as quantified by HPLC. Among the treatments, Halymenia extract produced the highest absolute growth (155.02 ± 25.00 g), specific growth rate (4.02 ± 0.35% day −1 ), chlorophyll accumulation, total amino acids (50.12 mg g −1 DW), protein level (11.37% DW), mineral enrichment, and sensory acceptance, which correlates strongly with growth-oriented primary metabolism. In contrast, Sargassum and Gracilaria extracts were more strongly associated with secondary metabolic and antioxidant-related responses, including higher total phenolic content, carotenoids, polyunsaturated fatty acids, and radical-scavenging activity. Crucially, Halymenia extract optimized the dietary Na/K ratio to 1.12 (compared with 3.72 in control), highlighting its potential to produce health-beneficial, low-sodium edible sea grapes. These findings demonstrate that species-specific seaweed extracts correlate with distinct physiological and biochemical responses in C. racemosa , providing baseline evidence of biostimulatory potential for cross-phylum macroalgal biostimulation in controlled aquaculture systems.

Article.Title: Integrated in vitro cytotoxicity and in silico safety profiling of glycerol-derived ethers based deep eutectic systems
Article.Authors: Garralaga M.; Zuriaga E.; Giner B.; Pires E.; Sánchez N.; Lomba L.
Article.Abstract: Toxicity studies of Deep Eutectic Systems (DES) are of particular importance for their application in various fields, such as biomedicine and pharmaceuticals. This study evaluated the cytotoxicity of 14 DESs composed of choline chloride (ChCl) and N,N,N-triethyl-N-(2,3-dihydroxypropyl)ammonium chloride (N00Cl) as HBA, paired with structurally modified glycerol-derived ethers as HBD. Cell viability was assessed using Prestoblue and Crystal Violet assays, and protein quantification was also performed when these systems were exposed to HaCat, HepG2, and HK-2 cell lines. Furthermore, in silico ADMET predictions were performed for the individual HBA and HBD components using SwissADME and ProTox. The results obtained show that there is a dose-dependent relationship. Furthermore, analysis of the different families studied reveals that the toxicity of DESs increases with the length of the HBD chain in the case of the ChCl family, whilst an odd–even effect is observed in the N00Cl family. Additionally, the correlation between EC 50 values and XLogP3, Log Kp (sking permeation) and polarizability values was investigated, yielding direct correlations. The in silico predictions provided preliminary information for the individual components but did not fully reproduce the experimental cytotoxicity pattern of the complete DES. These findings highlight the need to assess each DES experimentally and indicate that component-based computational predictions should be interpreted as complementary to, rather thatn predictive of, the cytotoxicity of the complete euctecit systems.

Article.Title: Altered brain-body activity during emotional mental imagery in major depressive disorder
Article.Authors: Al Latheef A.; Flasbeck V.; Juckel G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Major depressive disorder (MDD) has been associated with alterations in emotional processing, brain activity, and autonomic regulation, potentially reflecting impaired coordination between neural and autonomic systems. This study examined whether these alterations are more clearly reflected in distinct measures of brain activity or autonomic nervous system measures (HRV) during emotional mental imagery and investigated associations with mood and cognitive functioning. Therefore, thirty-seven healthy controls and 35 patients with MDD completed an auditory-guided imagery paradigm including positive, negative, neutral, and abstract conditions during EEG and ECG recording. EEG data were analyzed using event-related potentials (ERP), spectral power, and event-related synchronization/desynchronization (ERS/ERD), alongside heart rate variability (HRV) indices derived from ECG. All participants completed mood questionnaires and cognitive assessments. Patients showed higher depressive symptom severity, more negative current mood, and reduced executive performance. Further group differences emerged in alpha, gamma, and delta bands, whereas ERP amplitudes did not differ between groups. Altered neural oscillations were associated with reduced cognitive efficiency and greater depressive symptom severity. HRV measures indicated higher sympathetic nervous system and stress indices in patients, suggesting altered autonomic regulation. Importantly, correlations between delta ERS/ERD activity and HRV indices were observed in healthy controls but not in patients with MDD. These findings suggest that depression-related alterations are more strongly reflected in neural oscillations and autonomic regulation than basic emotional response patterns. Neural and autonomic markers may therefore provide clinically relevant information on cognitive difficulties, stress regulation, and disrupted brain–body interactions in MDD.

Article.Title: Higher risk does not necessarily produce greater expected value in football passing
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Shen L.; Xing J.; Xie C.; Qin Y.
Article.Abstract: Passing performance is often summarized by completion rate, which can obscure differences in pass difficulty, decision value, and execution. We developed an interpretable risk–reward framework combining a calibrated expected pass-completion model with a cross-fitted pass-chain continuation threat model. The framework separates expected success value, expected failure cost, and execution relative to completion probability. The analysis included 3,396,912 open-play passes from 3,926 matches. On a locked independent test set of 390 matches, the Full xPass model outperformed constant and geometry-only comparators (ROC-AUC 0.872; failure-class PR-AUC 0.646) and showed close calibration, with modest overprediction in the highest-risk tail. Across the full sample, expected success value and expected failure cost increased at different rates as risk rose, producing a nonlinear relationship between risk and expected net value. Under-pressure and non-ground passes were associated with less favorable net-value profiles, although these comparisons were descriptive. Three team-season applications showed distinct risk-allocation patterns. Among role-matched players with similar completion rates, modeled difficulty, and passing volume, decision-value profiles differed because expected success value and expected failure cost were combined differently. Results were broadly stable across alternative horizons, xPass specifications, and event filters, but player rankings changed when failure exposure was restricted to opponent-transition threat alone. The framework provides a transparent decomposition of short-horizon decision value rather than a universal risk threshold or overall measure of player quality.

Article.Title: Effects of biochar and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi on growth and water status of Chrysanthemum (Chrysanthemum morifolium Ramat.) in outdoor green walls
Article.Authors: Karimzadeh A.; Zarei H.; Jozay M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract With the increasing adoption of green walls as a sustainable approach to improve air quality, mitigate urban heat, and enhance space-use efficiency in cities, the need to produce ornamental plants that are resilient and require fewer chemical inputs has become increasingly important. In this context, the use of biochar and mycorrhizal fungi has emerged as an environmentally friendly strategy. This study was conducted to evaluate the synergistic effects of biochar and mycorrhizal fungi on the growth and physiological traits of chrysanthemum ( Chrysanthemum morifolium Ramat.) using a factorial experiment arranged in a randomized complete block design with three replications during 2024–2025. Treatments consisted of four biochar levels (0, 2, 3, and 5% w/w of the substrate) and four mycorrhizal inoculation treatments (non-inoculated control, Glomus intraradices , G. mosseae , and a combination of the two strains). The results showed that increasing biochar levels and mycorrhizal inoculation significantly improved growth and morphophysiological indices of chrysanthemum. The treatment consisting of 5% biochar combined with G. intraradices produced the highest leaf number (29.43), leaf dry weight (11.07 g), and growth index (145,559.83 cm 3 ), representing increases of 54%, 103%, and 722%, respectively, compared with the control. The greatest plant height (68.1 cm) was observed in the treatment with 5% biochar combined with G. mosseae . The combined application of 5% biochar and the two fungal strains also resulted in a significant increase in leaf fresh weight (75.15 g) and leaf area (1233.18 mm2). In terms of physiological traits, the highest relative water content (83.71%) was recorded in the 3% biochar treatment with G. intraradices , while the lowest electrolyte leakage (64.01%) was observed under 5% biochar combined with G. mosseae . In addition, chlorophyll a and b concentrations reached their maximum values in the 3% and 0% biochar treatments, respectively, when combined with G. intraradices . In contrast, the highest chlorophyll a/b ratio (2.42) and total pigment content (1.3 mg g −1 fresh weight) were recorded in the 5% biochar treatment with the combined fungal inoculum. Overall, the results demonstrated that biochar application—particularly at the 5% level—when combined with G. intraradices or dual mycorrhizal inoculation, markedly enhanced growth, physiological efficiency, and plant water status in chrysanthemum. This approach can therefore be considered an effective strategy for improving plant performance in outdoor green wall systems while reducing reliance on chemical inputs in urban green infrastructure.

Article.Title: Exploring clinician interpretability of AI decision support systems for surgical anatomy recognition
Article.Authors: Khan D.; Adams T.; Wijekoon A.; Ramirez Herrera R.; Bano S.; McCulloch P.; Stoyanov D.; Clarkson M.; Costanza E.; Blandford A.; Marcus H.; N/A N/A.; Adawi M.; Almeida J.; Ang J.; Borg A.; Bošnjak R.; Boukas A.; Chari A.; Daggubati L.; Dorward N.; Emerson S.; Glancz L.; Gwammache P.; Hanrahan J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) decision support systems for surgery hold promise but face barriers to adoption, particularly around the interpretability of their outputs. We conducted an international cross-sectional survey of 47 neurosurgeons to evaluate perspectives on literature-derived explanatory techniques for AI-generated anatomical segmentations, using endoscopic pituitary surgery as a high-risk exemplar. Participants ranked certainty scores, certainty maps, saliency maps, scene similarity scores, and nearest-neighbour illustrations, and rated them using a modified Explanation Satisfaction Scale alongside free-text feedback. Certainty-based techniques were consistently ranked and rated highest - valued for aligning with surgical decision-making by conveying confidence (via scores) and anatomical boundaries (via maps). Saliency- and similarity-based methods were judged less clinically relevant and better suited to educational settings. Therefore, certainty-based techniques appear most acceptable to surgeons for improving the interpretability of AI-assisted anatomical navigation systems, though their impact on trust calibration and performance requires prospective evaluation across surgical domains.

Article.Title: CAR T cells targeting fibroblast activation protein-α for the treatment of pulmonary fibrosis
Article.Authors: Chen Y.; Zhang Q.; Wu J.; Xu D.; Wei C.; Gao X.; Chen S.; Li C.; Gao S.; Bian H.; Liu S.; Li F.
Article.Abstract: Pulmonary fibrosis, a progressive and irreversible manifestation of interstitial lung disease, leads to severe respiratory dysfunction. Although current therapies can slow disease progression, they cannot eliminate pathogenic fibroblasts, thereby limiting clinical efficacy. Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has shown success in hematologic malignancies and autoimmune diseases and is being explored for non-malignant disorders. Here, we identified fibroblast activation protein (FAP) as highly and selectively expressed in myofibroblasts and fibroblasts within fibrotic lung tissues via single-cell RNA sequencing analysis, indicating its potential as a therapeutic target. Using a bleomycin-induced mouse model, we confirmed FAP upregulation in fibroblast populations. Furthermore, we generated murine CAR T cells targeting FAP for the treatment of pulmonary fibrosis. The results showed that FAP-targeted CAR T cells significantly reduced fibrotic burden and improved pulmonary function, including mid-tidal expiratory flow (EF50), minute ventilation (MV), and tidal volume (TV). These results demonstrate the feasibility and therapeutic potential of FAP-targeted CAR T cells in eliminating pathogenic fibroblasts and provide a promising strategy for pulmonary fibrosis treatment.

Article.Title: Experimental and numerical analysis of foamed concrete as a damping interlayer in metro sub-track systems
Article.Authors: Safa M.; Chakeri H.; Darbor M.; Khodaei S.
Article.Abstract: The use of various materials like flexible mats, polyurethane (PU) carpets, isolator compositions and etc. as a sublayer material in urban metro tunnels, while common in many countries, presents several challenges, including difficulties in material procurement, increased construction costs, and performance degradation over time. To address these issues, the present study introduces a novel foam concrete (FC) mixture as a replacement material. Owing to its multi-phased internal structure comprising interconnected pores and voids, foam concrete effectively attenuates train-induced vibrational energies. Experimental mechanical, physical, and numerical investigations demonstrate that a foam concrete specimen composed of 450 kg/m 3 cement, a water-to-cement (W/C) ratio of 0.5, 60% foam content, and 50 kg/m 3 silica fume achieves a 11.3% damping of applied stresses and reduces applied energy by 2.53 J per 50 m of length. A second mixture, composed of 600 kg/m 3 cement, a W/C ratio of 0.5, and 50% foam content, exhibits a damping ratio of 10.8% and reduces applied energy by 5.05 J per 50 m of length. Collectively, the integrated multi-method experimental and numerical investigations confirm the suitability of foam concrete for sublayer construction applications. This material substantially reduces induced vibrations, dynamic energies, and mechanical stresses.

Article.Title: Security and reliability constrained power management of virtual power plant considering ancillary services and energy markets models in smart grid
Article.Authors: Abdoli M.; Shamim A.; Abedini M.; Moradi M.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates the operation of a flexible renewable virtual power plant (VPP) with inverter-based system in a smart distribution network while considering the technical and economic objectives of the distribution system operator and maximizing the VPP’s participation in energy, reactive power, and reserve markets. A bi-level optimization framework is proposed in which the upper level minimizes a weighted combination of voltage security, power loss, and expected energy not supplied by incorporating AC optimal power flow and network security constraints. The lower level maximizes the VPP’s profit subject to inverter capabilities and operational and reserve constraints. The bi-level problem is transformed into a single-level formulation using the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions. To address uncertainties in load, renewable generation, mobile storage characteristics, market prices, and equipment availability, a hybrid stochastic-robust optimization framework is employed. Equipment availability is modeled stochastically to accurately assess reliability, whereas the remaining uncertainties are handled through robust optimization to improve resilience against forecasting errors. The proposed approach is distinguished by its inverter-based VPP model, integration of multiple technical performance indices, hybrid uncertainty modeling, and coordinated use of flexible resources for energy management. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework enhances both network performance and VPP profitability. Compared with conventional load flow analysis, it significantly improves operational performance, voltage security, and reliability through coordinated inverter control. Even under the worst-case uncertainty level of 17%, the proposed method achieves improvements of approximately 36–43%, 8.6%, and 90.5%, respectively.

Article.Title: Optimizing water and nutrient delivery through precision drip fertigation boosts fennel productivity and resource-use efficiency in arid agroecosystems
Article.Authors: Singh R.; Choudhary S.; Ravi Y.; Meena N.; Meena R.; Kumar S.; Shekhawat P.; Verma A.
Article.Abstract: Fennel ( Foeniculum vulgare Mill.) is a vital seed spice crop cultivated in arid and semi-arid regions of India, where water scarcity and nutrient inefficiency constrain productivity. To address these challenges, a comprehensive three-year field study (2016-17, 2017-18 and 2018-19) was conducted to assess the effects of drip fertigation under varying irrigation regimes and fertilizer levels on fennel growth, yield, Water-Use Efficiency (WUE), and economic returns. The experiment comprised ten treatments, including surface irrigation (T 1 /control) and nine drip fertigation combinations structured across three IW/CPE levels (0.4, 0.6, and 0.8) and three fertilizer levels (60, 80 and 100% of RDF i.e. 90:40:30 N: P:K). Drip fertigation at 0.8 IW/CPE with 100% RDF (T 10 ) significantly enhanced plant height (195.3 cm), primary and secondary branches, umbels per plant (71.4), umbellets per umbel (71.34), seed yield (2,705 kg ha − 1 ), essential oil content (1.63%), and net returns (₹1,78,628 ha − 1 ), with a benefit-cost ratio of 2.84, along with significantly higher test weight reflecting improved seed filling and quality under optimized drip fertigation. Although the highest WUE (7.24 kg/ha-mm) was recorded under T 4 (0.4 IW/CPE with 100% RDF), T 10 offered the best balance between seed productivity and economic returns. Correlation and regression analyses revealed strong positive associations between growth parameters and seed yield, validating their role as reliable indicators for agronomic optimization. Multivariate analyses further showed that T 10 was associated with consistently high productivity and economic performance across the three seasons. Overall, the findings underscore the potential of drip fertigation particularly at 0.8 IW/CPE with full nutrient supply as a sustainable, water-efficient, and economically viable strategy for enhancing fennel cultivation in water-limited environments.

Article.Title: Social network based fuzzy decision-analytic model for hydrogen vehicle selection toward sustainable transportation systems
Article.Authors: Bhoopalan R.; Parthasarathy T.; Krishnan V.; Bhavana S.; Athira T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The selection of an effective hydrogen vehicle technology is a multi-criteria decision making (MCDM) problem with conflicting evaluation criteria and uncertainty in experts’ judgments. To tackle this challenge, this study presents an integrated social network analysis based fuzzy MCDM approach to hydrogen vehicle selection. First, in the present work, Social Network Analysis (SNA) is used to calculate the relative influence of experts using degree centrality. Second, the uncertainty and imprecision in experts’ linguistic assessments are captured in terms of Interval-Valued Fuzzy Sets (IVFS). Third, the Entropy method is used as an objective weighting method to give relative importance of the evaluation criteria. Finally, the Evaluation based on Distance from Average Solution (EDAS) technique is used to evaluate and rank the alternatives. The suggested methodology is used in four hydrogen vehicle alternatives, with the evaluation criteria of eight. The results indicate that $$O_1$$ (FCEV) is the most suitable option, with an EDAS appraisal score of 0.9992 followed by $$O_3$$ (H2Hybrid), $$O_4$$ (H2REEV) and $$O_2$$ (H2ICE). The proposed approach is further tested the effectiveness by comparing four existing hybrid MCDM approaches, and O1 is consistently determined as the best alternative. In addition, Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis with 1,000 random perturbations of the criterion weights demonstrates that rank-1 probability for $$O_1$$ is 100% in all simulations. No rank reversal is observed in the investigated ranges for the sensitivity analyses when using criterion weights and expert weights as sensitivity factors. The quantitative results show the robustness and stability of the proposed approach for hydrogen vehicle selection under uncertain decision-making conditions.

Article.Title: Predicting fish spoilage through adsorption and detection of volatile sulfur compounds on B2N monolayers: a computational study
Article.Authors: Rahimi R.; Solimannejad M.
Article.Abstract: In the present work, a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation was conducted to elucidate the adsorption behavior of two key sulfur-containing volatile compounds generated during fish deterioration, namely dimethyl sulfide (DMS, CH₃–S–CH₃) and dimethyl disulfide (DMDS, CH₃–S–S–CH₃). The calculated adsorption energies are significantly negative, revealing strong yet reversible adsorption characteristics suitable for both sensing and capture applications. The obtained E ads (%ΔE g ) values for DMS/B₂N and DMDS/B₂N are − 0.47 eV (40%) and − 0.45 eV (39%), respectively. Adsorption induces substantial modulation of the B₂N electronic band gap, generating distinct electronic responses for each analyte. As a result, the monolayer exhibits distinct electronic and φ-type sensing responses, arising from substantial band-gap modulation and charge transfer between the adsorbed species and the B₂N substrate, thereby providing a pronounced and readily detectable electrical response. The pristine B₂N surface exhibits high sensitivity toward both DMS and DMDS, while the short recovery times and ultrafast desorption confirm excellent reversibility. Therefore, the B₂N monolayer serves as a multifunctional nanomaterial, acting as both a high-performance sensor and an efficient adsorbent for sulfur-based spoilage compounds, and presents a promising strategy for real-time seafood freshness monitoring.

Article.Title: GGE biplot and WAASB assessment of seed-purpose watermelon for fruit yield and 100-seed weight across hot semi-arid environments of India
Article.Authors: Shekhawat N.; Gowthami R.; Yadav S.; Kumar S.; Prajapati N.; Kumar M.; Patidar A.; Narolia R.; Singh P.; Singh G.
Article.Abstract: Watermelon [ Citrullus lanatus (Thunb.) Matsum. & Nakai] belongs to the Cucurbitaceae family and is widely cultivated for both fruit and seed-purpose. In India, indigenous seed-purpose watermelons, locally known as Mateera, Kalingada, or Karingada are predominantly grown in semi-arid regions such as Rajasthan and Gujarat. Unlike sweet dessert types, seed-purpose watermelons are less sweet but are valued for their edible, oil-rich seeds, culinary uses, medicinal properties, and use as animal feed. The present study was conducted using a randomized complete block design with twelve seed-purpose watermelon genotypes across four locations, namely Sardarkrushinagar (Gujarat), Sihori (Gujarat), Mandor (Rajasthan) and Jobner (Rajasthan), over the kharif seasons of 2023 and 2024, to identify stable and high-yielding seed-purpose watermelon genotypes using GGE biplot and WAASB analyses. Fruit yield and 100-seed weight were selected for stability analysis because they represent overall productivity and seed size, respectively. Combined analysis of variance revealed highly significant ( p < 0.001) effects of genotype, environment, and genotype × environment interaction (GEI) for both traits. In the GGE analysis, the first two principal components explained 78.63% (41.46% and 37.17%) of the G + GE variation for fruit yield and 59.69% (36.51% and 23.18%) for 100-seed weight. GGE biplot analysis integrating mean performance and stability identified SKNK-1704 as the most desirable genotype for fruit yield, followed by RMK-2. For 100-seed weight, SKNK-1407 achieved the best combined rank primarily because of its highest mean performance, despite intermediate stability, whereas GK-2 exhibited the greatest stability. The genotype NBPGRK-1 exhibited near-average performance for fruit yield and 100-seed weight, indicating its potential as a consistent performer across diverse environments. Additionally, genotype SKNK-2007 demonstrated broad adaptability for both fruit yield and 100-seed weight. The WAASB (50:50) index further confirmed SKNK-1704 and NBPGRK-1 as the superior genotypes for fruit yield, while NBPGRK-1, SKNK-1407, SKNK-2007, RMK-4, GK-2, and CAZJK-13-2 for 100-seed weight. Collectively, the integrated GGE biplot and WAASB analyses identified SKNK-1704 as a promising genotype for fruit yield, SKNK-1407 showed the highest combined performance for 100-seed weight, whereas NBPGRK-1 emerged as a promising dual-purpose candidate genotype across environments. These findings provide a basis for prioritizing genotypes for further validation and breeding evaluation in seed-purpose watermelon under hot semi-arid environments.

Article.Title: Quantum similarity estimation with hybrid discrete-continuous encoding: algorithm and application to atomtronics precision measurements
Article.Authors: Jana S.; Raghav S.; Mehta V.; Roy U.
Article.Abstract: We introduce a quantum similarity estimation algorithm which employs an entangled discrete-continuous representation and a modified SWAP-test protocol using conditional displacement and controlled-SWAP operations. The corresponding exact form of the similarity metric is analytically derived and its feasible circuit implementation is provided. We apply this result to interferometric images, which are numerically generated from an experimentally viable atomtronics setup. A ring-shaped potential, confining a localized Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC), is considered where the BEC manifests fractional revivals during its confined time-evolution. We perform a precise identification of nonlinearity, originated from interatomic interactions, which can be tuned by Feshbach resonance and thus, the presented method paves the possibility for a magnetic field sensor. Moreover, we perform quantum simulation with Shot-noise of the proposed quantum circuit with public benchmark datasets and analyse the resource and computational complexities of the proposed algorithm.

Article.Title: Dynamic event-triggered fractional-order super-twisting control for practical fixed-time quadrotor tracking under DoS attacks
Article.Authors: Li W.; Zhang Z.; Wan H.
Article.Abstract: Denial-of-service (DoS) attacks interrupt controller-to-actuator communication in quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), preventing timely control updates and degrading trajectory-tracking accuracy. External disturbances and limited communication bandwidth further complicate precise tracking under such attacks. To address these problems, a dynamic event-triggered fractional-order super-twisting control strategy is proposed to achieve practical fixed-time trajectory tracking under DoS attacks. First, a fractional-order sliding surface with nonsingular dual-power feedback is designed to improve the tracking performance of the position and attitude subsystems. Subsequently, a generalized super-twisting controller is constructed to enhance disturbance rejection and alleviate chattering. Considering the limited communication bandwidth during remote control, a dynamic event-triggered mechanism (ETM) with a strictly positive threshold floor is developed to reduce unnecessary command transmissions. An acknowledgment-based retry strategy is introduced to restore command updates after communication interruptions, while the actuator retains the most recently received command during the outage. Within the prescribed operating domain, Lyapunov analysis establishes practical fixed-time stability under DoS attacks for the closed-loop system on a prescribed compact set of initial conditions. Moreover, a strictly positive lower bound on successive transmission attempts is derived to exclude Zeno behavior. Finally, numerical simulations verify the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

Article.Title: Ex vivo IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-8 responses 2 years after critical COVID-19 are associated with age and innate immune activation
Article.Authors: Hiti L.; Kandušer M.; Burnik T.; Karas Kuželički N.; Farkaš Lainščak J.; Miholič M.; Pal E.; Lainscak M.; Mlinarič-Raščan I.; Markovič T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A cytokine storm drives critical COVID-19, yet the determinants and long-term consequences of this exaggerated inflammatory response remain unclear. We investigated whether cytokine responsiveness remains altered 2 years after recovery from critical disease. In a cohort of 117 individuals with mild, severe, or critical COVID-19, acute-phase clinical and laboratory parameters were analyzed in moderate–severe and critical cases. Long-term immune function was assessed by ex vivo stimulation of whole blood with PMA/ionomycin, lipopolysaccharide (LPS), and phytohemagglutinin (PHA), followed by cytokine quantification and correlation with clinical parameters. A biobank of 76 patient-derived lymphoblastoid cell lines (LCL cells) was established to evaluate the stability of cytokine responses. During acute illness, critically ill patients exhibited marked inflammatory dysregulation, including lymphopenia (72%), neutrophilia (51%), elevated neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratios, and increased C-reactive protein (median 91 mg/L) and ferritin (median 1,153 μg/L), consistent with a hyperinflammatory–hypercoagulable phenotype. Two years post-infection, individuals with prior critical disease showed more than threefold higher secretion of IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-8 following PMA/ionomycin (p < 0.0001) and LPS stimulation (p < 0.05) compared with younger mild cases, whereas PHA-induced responses remained comparable. PBMC counts were also higher in the moderate–severe and critical groups 2 years post-infection (p < 0.001), highlighting differences in cellular composition. LCL cells from critically ill donors secreted 79% more IL-8 and TNF-α than those from mild cases (p < 0.05). Collectively, these findings indicate differences in cytokine responsiveness 2 years after COVID-19 which correspond to prior disease severity and are associated particularly with age and innate immune activation.

Article.Title: Dynamic construction behavior recognition through domain-adaptive multimodal evidence fusion
Article.Authors: Liu C.; Zhong C.; Li L.; Lian J.
Article.Abstract: Construction behavior recognition must remain reliable when acquisition conditions or participants differ from the training data. Existing adaptation can admit unsupported target samples, while multimodal fusion can become overconfident when streams are degraded, missing, or temporally misaligned. We propose reliability-coupled domain-adaptive evidence fusion (RDAEF), which derives a shared diagnostic state from signal quality, class-prototype distance, evidential uncertainty, open-set risk and, when multiple streams are available, temporal lag and opinion conflict. The shared state is mapped to a target-admission weight during training and modality-specific evidence discounts during inference. Evaluation uses two complementary configurations: the Construction Meta Action (CMA) benchmark supplies RGB clips for cross-condition adaptation, whereas the Scaffolding Worker IMU Time-series (SWIT) benchmark supplies synchronized pose and inertial sequences for cross-participant adaptation and multimodal fusion. RDAEF achieved target-domain macro-F1 scores of 0.798 on CMA and 0.783 on SWIT, exceeding the strongest unsupervised baselines by 3.4 and 5.9 percentage points, respectively. Removing conflict discounting increased the risk–coverage area (RCA) from 0.118 to 0.198, indicating poorer selective decisions.

Article.Title: Climate change adaptation barriers among beekeepers across agroecological zones in Gedeo, Ethiopia: evidence from problem confrontation index and multinomial regression
Article.Authors: Mengistu E.; Kenea T.; Asfaw N.
Article.Abstract: Climate change increasingly threatens apiculture by reducing floral resources, water availability, and colony productivity. Although beekeepers adopt various adaptation measures, barriers to effective adaptation remain poorly understood across different agro ecological settings. This study examined the determinants and severity of climate change adaptation barriers among beekeepers across three agro ecological zones in Gedeo Zone, southern Ethiopia. A cross-sectional mixed-methods design was employed using data from 398 beekeeper households, complemented by 15 focus group discussions and key informant interviews. The Problem Confrontation Index (PCI) was used to prioritize adaptation barriers, while the Kruskal–Wallis H test assessed differences across agro ecological zones. Multinomial logistic regression identified socioeconomic and institutional determinants of perceived adaptation barriers. The most severe adaptation barriers were lack of improved beekeeping technology (PCI = 1056), lack of credit (PCI = 1047), water scarcity (PCI = 939), lack of training (PCI = 934), and shortage of bee-forage plants (PCI = 921). Significant agro ecological differences were observed for water scarcity ( p = 0.011), pests and diseases ( p = 0.017), and lack of finance ( p = 0.025), whereas most institutional and technological barriers were common across zones. Multinomial logistic regression revealed that age, sex, education, income, climate information, and particularly beekeeping practices significantly influenced the likelihood of experiencing different adaptation barriers ( p < 0.05). Climate change adaptation barriers in apiculture arise from interacting technological, financial, institutional, and environmental constraints. Strengthening access to improved beekeeping technologies, affordable credit, climate information, extension services, and training, while implementing agro ecology-specific interventions, is essential for enhancing the climate resilience and sustainability of beekeeping livelihoods in Ethiopia.
