Article.Title: FARABI: fuzzy-assisted routing for adaptive blockage-resilient 6G IoV
Article.Authors: Sedaghat S.
Article.Abstract: High-frequency millimeter-wave (mmWave) and Terahertz (THz) communications are promising for 6G Internet of Vehicles (IoV) services but remain vulnerable to dynamic vehicular mobility, bursty heterogeneous traffic, and heavy-tailed physical blockage. Conventional routing approaches often rely on memoryless channel models, non-differentiable soft-computing heuristics, or centralized optimization that may not adequately capture blockage persistence and tail-latency risks. This paper presents FARABI (Fuzzy-Assisted Routing for Adaptive Blockage-Resilient 6G IoV), a cross-layer Software-Defined Networking (SDN) routing framework that integrates a three-state semi-Markov blockage model, multi-class Markov-Modulated Poisson Process (MMPP) traffic, a seven-dimensional differentiable fuzzy inference system, and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR)-based risk-aware routing optimization. The framework tracks blockage age to estimate residual interruption duration and incorporates queueing, link reliability, route sustainability, and traffic-class requirements into an online hierarchical primal-dual optimization process. Extensive simulation-based evaluation under dynamic blockage, mobility, and bursty traffic conditions shows that the FARABI control-plane execution time increases from 0.5 ms to 1.85 ms as the decision space grows from 450 to 18,000 variables, corresponding to up to 42.08× lower computational time than a centralized interior-point solver. Under increasing obstacle density, FARABI sustains an effective service rate from 4.62 to 1.88 Gbps, while conditional outage reaches 54.2% at a blockage age of 180 ms. Under severe blockage dynamics, 58.4% of packets are delivered within 1.6 ms, 94.1% within the 3.2-ms tail-latency target, and the median end-to-end delay is 1.48 ms. Across burstiness levels from 1.5 to 5, safety, cooperative-perception, and infotainment packet-loss rates remain within 0.002–0.098%, 0.045–0.98%, and 0.42–10.15%, respectively. These results indicate that FARABI can improve the robustness of SDN-based 6G IoV routing against stochastic blockage and bursty traffic while maintaining bounded computational and QoS performance.

Article.Title: A methodological approach for land use planning in hill towns of India: a case of Shoghi special area of Shimla
Article.Authors: Sharma S.; Saini A.; Shrivastava B.; Kumar A.; Dhiman V.; Sharma S.
Article.Abstract: Land is a finite, immovable, and valuable resource that supports diverse societal needs. Rapid population growth and consequent changes in land use have intensified development pressures, making systematic land use planning essential, particularly in India’s environmentally sensitive hilly regions. Topographical constraints, limited developable land, climatic variability, and high exposure to geohazards further complicate development planning in hill towns. However, contextual land use planning for Indian hill towns remains relatively under-researched. This study develops a systematic framework for land use planning and allocation in hill towns by integrating environmental, infrastructural, and hazard-related considerations. An integrated Analytic Hierarchy Process–Geographic Information System (AHP–GIS) framework was applied to the Shoghi Special Area, Shimla, using 20 criteria grouped into natural setting, built environment, and hazard proneness. Expert judgments were used to derive criterion weights, with all pairwise comparison matrices satisfying the consistency requirement Consistency Ratio (CR) ≤ 0.10; goal-level Consistency Ratio (CR) = 0.0%; group consensus = 96.9%. Category weights were 37.6% for hazard proneness, 33.8% for natural setting, and 28.6% for the built environment. Earthquake, landslide, and flood susceptibility received the highest individual weights. Criterion layers were prepared in ArcGIS 10.4.1, standardized using a five-level rating scale, and aggregated through weighted linear combination across 443 land facets delineated according to IS 14,496 (Part 2): 1998. Results indicate that 55.53% of facets scored above 50, while only 16.03% exceeded 60. No facet attained the Most Suitable or Extreme Suitability classes. The findings demonstrate that natural setting constitutes the principal constraint on development capacity, highlighting the need for context-sensitive, risk-informed, and sustainable land use planning in Indian hill towns.

Article.Title: Detection-aware disparity refinement for weak-texture pavement target reconstruction in stereo vision
Article.Authors: Li W.; Yan F.; Qin X.; Dong K.; Yin Z.; Luo Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate detection and depth perception of pavement targets from close-range remote sensing observations are important for intelligent road monitoring and transportation infrastructure assessment. However, existing stereo matching methods often produce unstable disparity estimates in weak-texture and low-height pavement regions, such as manhole covers and speed bumps, where the disparity distribution is easily affected by matching ambiguity and image noise. To address this issue, a detection-guided disparity post-processing strategy named Detection-Aware Disparity Refinement (DADR) is proposed. A custom pavement dataset containing approximately 3000 annotated images is first constructed from a binocular vision-based remote sensing platform, covering five pavement target categories, including manhole covers, speed bumps, road damage, storm drains, and iron plates. YOLOv11 is employed to detect target regions, while FoundationStereo is used to generate initial disparity maps from calibrated stereo images. Instead of modifying the stereo matching network, the proposed method performs a rule-based post-processing operation that combines detection bounding boxes, a local ground-reference disparity, and confidence-weighted fusion to stabilize the disparity representation within detected target regions. Experimental results show that the YOLOv11 detector achieves a Precision of 0.89, a Recall of 0.88, and an mAP@50 of 0.895, and compares favourably with other one-stage detectors trained under the same protocol. Visual analysis with magnified regions of interest shows that the proposed strategy produces more spatially coherent disparity responses for weak-texture pavement targets, and an ablation study identifies the local ground reference and the adaptive confidence weighting as the main contributing components. Quantitative evaluation indicates that the within-region disparity standard deviation decreases from 3.81 px to 1.25 px after refinement. Because no independent depth ground truth is available, this result is reported as improved local disparity consistency rather than improved absolute depth accuracy. The proposed approach offers a lightweight, detector-agnostic disparity stabilization strategy for low-height pavement targets in close-range remote sensing scenarios and provides useful geometric cues for subsequent road-condition assessment, while its reliance on a locally planar ground reference and on detector reliability is discussed as a limitation.

Article.Title: Micro-computed tomography analysis of root and canal morphology in maxillary primary molars
Article.Authors: Eldehna A.; Elzahar S.; Ahmad A.; El Kharadly D.; Salem N.; Abdel-Ghany D.; Abd-Allah N.; Abd-Allah M.; Ahmed H.; Abdelkafy H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Effective pulpectomy of maxillary primary molars depends on a clear understanding of their complex internal root canal anatomy, yet high-resolution data on the second mesiobuccal (MB2) canal in the primary dentition remain scarce. Using micro-computed tomography (micro-CT; SkyScan 1172; 13.61 μm isotropic voxel size), the three-dimensional root and canal morphology of 60 extracted maxillary primary molars were charaterized, focusing on the prevalence, location, and morphometry of the MB2 canal, along with inter-orifice distances, canal diameters, and dentin wall thickness. Three-rooted molars predominated (83.3%). An MB2 canal was present in 43.3% of mesiobuccal roots and, when present, was consistently located palatal to the main mesiobuccal (MB1) canal, originating predominantly in the coronal third. Long-oval and oval cross-sections together accounted for almost all canals. The MB1–MB2 inter-orifice distance was the shortest of any canal pair (mean 1.12 mm), and buccolingual diameters exceeded mesiodistal diameters in the mesiobuccal, MB2, and distobuccal roots but not the palatal root. Apical dentin was thinnest in the palatal roots (0.10 mm). Maxillary primary molars therefore combine a frequently overlooked MB2 canal with thin apical walls. These findings may help clinicians plan access cavities, select instruments, and perform conservative apical preparation during pulpectomy procedures.

Article.Title: Hierarchical Mg/Ag2O nanostructures as multifunctional biomedical agents with potent antimicrobial, mosquitocidal, and anticancer efficacy
Article.Authors: Mostafa W.; Mahmoud M.; Elshanawany S.; Elgazzar E.; Ayoub H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Magnesium silver oxide nanostructures were synthesized via a straightforward co-precipitation method and characterized using various analytical techniques. The morphological analysis revealed a 2D/3D sheet hierarchical architecture decorated with ultrafine spherical nanoparticles, providing distinctive characteristics include large specific surface area and high porous network that may facilitate enhanced interaction with microbial cells. The nanohybrid showed remarkable antimicrobial activity against Proteus vulgaris with an inhibition zone diameter of 20 mm as well as moderate antibacterial activity against Bacillus subtilis and Staphylococcus aureus with inhibition zone diameters of 14.33 and 11.67 mm, respectively. In contrast, no detectable antibacterial activity was observed against Escherichia coli . The Mg/Ag₂O nanostructure also demonstrated pronounced antifungal activity against Aspergillus fumigatus and Candida albicans producing inhibition zones of 10.50 and 12 mm, respectively. Moreover, the nanostructure exhibited remarkable adulticidal efficacy against Culex pipiens at a concentration of 300 ppm. In biomedical field, Mg/Ag₂O nanocomposite revealed strong antioxidant and anticancer activities achieving an IC₅₀ value of 2.80 ± 0.37 µg/mL and a maximum inhibition rate of 99.05%, highlighting its promising potential for diverse biomedical applications.

Article.Title: Development and psychometric validation of a multidimensional menstrual hygiene scale
Article.Authors: Aydın A.; Ocakoğlu F.; Şirin Gök M.; Çiftçi B.
Article.Abstract: This study was conducted methodologically to develop a valid and reliable measurement tool for assessing women’s menstrual hygiene behaviours. The study was conducted between June and December 2025. The scale development process was carried out in three stages: creating an item pool through a literature review, assessing content validity, and conducting analyses of construct validity and reliability. The item pool was submitted for expert review to assess content validity. The study sample comprised 522 women aged 18 years and older who had experienced menarche, residing in Erzurum city center and recruited from the community using convenience sampling through face-to-face interviews conducted in public areas, parks, streets, and hospital settings: 297 for Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) and 225 for Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA). Data were collected via face-to-face interviews. The scale’s construct validity was examined using EFA and CFA, whilst reliability was assessed using Cronbach’s Alpha. According to the EFA results, the data set was suitable for factor analysis (KMO = 0.863; Bartlett’s Test, χ² = 2262.657, p < 0.001). The analysis revealed that the scale exhibited a multi-factor structure and explained 63.53% of the total variance. The highest factor loadings were observed for items related to awareness of menstrual hygiene, the ability to maintain proper hygiene, handwashing practices after changing menstrual products, and storing menstrual materials under hygienic conditions. The Menstrual Hygiene Scale is a 5-point Likert-type scale (1 = Never, 5 = Always). Scale scores are calculated based on the mean item score, with higher scores indicating better menstrual hygiene. CFA results indicated that the model demonstrated an overall acceptable fit when all fit indices were considered together (χ²/df < 5; CFI > 0.90; GFI > 0.90). The scale’s internal consistency coefficient was found to be quite high (Cronbach’s α = 0.855). It was determined that item-total correlations were adequate and that all items contributed meaningfully to the scale. The developed Menstrual Hygiene Scale is a valid and reliable instrument for assessing the cognitive, behavioral, and environmental dimensions of menstrual hygiene management in community and clinical settings. This scale may be useful for assessing menstrual hygiene management and evaluating educational and community-based interventions.

Article.Title: Cost estimate for the procurement and preparation of donated corneas for transplantation in an eye bank
Article.Authors: Maidana G.; Ferreira Júnior M.; Frota O.; de Azevedo I.; da Silva Martins M.; Santos V.; Mota F.; Menezes B.; da Silva A.; de Oliveira M.; Ribeiro K.; da Silva J.; de Oliveira Ferreira G.; Shinohara G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Corneal diseases are among the leading causes of blindness, and transplantation may be the only treatment option. Studies providing a comprehensive economic analysis of the corneal tissue processing chain, from procurement to release for transplantation by eye banks, are scarce. This study aimed to estimate the cost of preparing donated corneal tissue for transplantation at an Eye Bank. We performed a cost analysis using the Time-Driven Activity-Based Costing (TDABC) method based on data from the stages of corneal tissue preparation. The study population consisted of data from corneal donors collected in 2023. The median cost per donor was estimated at USD 454.65. Supplies (43%), human resources (32%), and operational costs (23%) were the costliest components. Multiple regression analysis identified predictors influencing costs. This study highlighted critical stages in the process and resource consumption. Investing in domestic pharmaceutical production, improving interinstitutional communication, training healthcare professionals, and providing logistical support may reduce costs and contribute to the management and sustainability of Eye Banks.

Article.Title: Trust and power-aware group shilling attacks on multi-criteria top-N recommendation systems
Article.Authors: Kaya T.
Article.Abstract: Multi-Criteria Collaborative Filtering (MCCF) systems improve recommendation quality by considering users’ preferences across multiple criteria. However, the rich multidimensional structure of MCCF systems also makes them vulnerable to sophisticated shilling attacks. In particular, coordinated group shilling attacks can generate behaviorally informed fake profiles capable of significantly manipulating recommendation results. Although various attack generation methods have been proposed in the literature, existing approaches generally rely on random filler item selection and fail to effectively exploit the behavioral characteristics of influential users in multi-criteria environments. To address this limitation, this study proposes a novel trust- and power-aware group shilling attack model called Group Shilling Attack Power Attack (GSAGenPA) . Unlike traditional attack models, the proposed approach identifies powerful users based on user influence metrics and generates attack profiles by imitating their preference behaviors. In addition, new trust-oriented target item selection strategies are introduced for both push and nuke attack scenarios. The proposed framework is evaluated on multi-criteria recommendation datasets under different attack configurations. Experimental results demonstrate that GSAGenPA provides a strategically informed attack-generation mechanism that consistently improves recommendation manipulation performance over the random filler-selection baseline ( \(GSAGen_{l} Ran\) ). However, the proposed power-aware variants do not generally surpass the average-based filler-selection baseline ( \(GSAGen_{l} Avg\) ) in terms of absolute attack success, highlighting a trade-off between power-aware profile construction and maximum manipulation effectiveness.
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Information Systems > Recommender Systems and Techniques; Computer Science > Information Systems > Spam and Phishing Detection; Social Sciences > Sociology and Political Science > Access Control and Trust

Article.Title: Terrain-induced aerodynamic disturbances and wind sector management of a wind turbine in complex terrain: a SCADA–CFD cross-validation study at the Tetouan wind farm
Article.Authors: Bousla M.; Haddi A.; El Mourabit Y.; Samkari H.; Allehyani M.; Bossoufi B.; Yessef M.
Article.Abstract: Wind turbines operating in complex terrain are exposed to terrain-induced aerodynamic disturbances, such as strong vertical wind shear, wind veer, turbulence and flow deviation, which increase asymmetric rotor loading and can degrade operational reliability. The quantitative link between such disturbances, the operational response recorded by the Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system, and the parameterisation of Wind Sector Management (WSM) strategies remains insufficiently documented for real turbines. This study analyses a 3.0 MW turbine (WTG 30, 80 m hub height) of the Tétouan wind farm (Morocco), located 300 m west of a hill that overlaps 72.8%–99.9% of the rotor-swept area. The methodology combines long-term-corrected wind-resource characterisation (WDA, WAsP 11 and WindPRO 3.4), a sector-binned analysis of SCADA data from WTG 30 and its two neighbouring turbines, steady Reynolds-Averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) and unsteady Detached Eddy Simulation (DES) of the flow at rotor top, hub and rotor bottom for ten inflow sectors (50°–140°), and quasi-steady rotor-load indicators derived from the simulated inflow. The DES results identify two critical regimes: for 50°–80°, the whole rotor lies in the hill wake (mean rotor-top speed 2.7–5.5 m/s for a 14.7 m/s undisturbed reference), whereas for 90°–130° the upper rotor remains exposed to 14.6–15.6 m/s while the rotor bottom experiences only 2.2–3.9 m/s. This produces rotor shear exponents of 1.08–1.52 (versus 0.2 for the IEC normal wind profile), wind veer of 43°–95° across the rotor, and blade-root 1P flapwise and rotor-tilt load indicators 2.1–3.2 times higher than for a uniform IEC reference inflow. The SCADA data independently show that, for easterly winds, WTG 30 deviates from its neighbours by a mean absolute direction of 24°–36° (versus 4°–7° for westerly winds), and the sector-wise SCADA wind-speed reduction correlates with the CFD rotor-equivalent wind-speed ratio ( r = 0.81, p < 0.01). On this basis, the WSM settings of WTG 30 are revised (stop at all wind speeds for 35°–85°, above 10 m/s for 85°–135° and above 12 m/s for 180°–200°), at the cost of an estimated annual energy production loss of 37.6% (3.19 GWh/year) compared with 20.5% (1.74 GWh/year) for the current settings. The results show that combining CFD and SCADA data provides a quantitative, physics-based basis for identifying critical sectors and setting reliability-oriented operating strategies in complex terrain, while component-level aeroelastic validation remains necessary.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: complex terrain; computational fluid dynamics; SCADA data; wind farm performance; wind turbine aerodynamics

Article.Title: FusionSwinUNETR: A multimodal deep learning model for abdominal mass segmentation in pediatric CT
Article.Authors: Moon S.; Ko D.; Park S.; Kim Y.; Youn J.; Yang H.; Kim H.; Kim K.
Article.Abstract: Research on computational methods for pediatric solid tumors is constrained by data scarcity, a focus on single tumor types, and the limits of imaging alone. We present FusionSwinUNETR, a multimodal segmentation model that conditions a SwinUNETRv2 backbone on patient metadata and clinician-written findings alongside CT images, and we evaluate it on a multi-center paired dataset of 750 pediatric patients spanning 12 mass types — a considerably broader diagnostic range than previous single-tumor studies. Against an image-only baseline evaluated on the same 60 held-out patients, the fusion model improved every metric: DSC 0.900 ± 0.044 versus 0.882 ± 0.064, precision 0.928 ± 0.051 versus 0.913 ± 0.062, recall 0.880 ± 0.081 versus 0.866 ± 0.110, and HD95 4.79 ± 3.31 versus 8.93 ± 6.22 mm, a 46% reduction in boundary error. Paired within-patient testing with correction for multiple comparisons confirmed these gains: HD95 improved significantly for all three multimodal configurations, and the fusion model was the only configuration whose DSC improvement survived correction (Hodges–Lehmann + 0.012, q = 5.6 × 10⁻ 4 ) and the only one to improve precision and recall concurrently, indicating that metadata and clinical findings contribute complementary rather than redundant information. Incorporating clinical information already available at the time of image interpretation therefore yields more accurate and more reliable segmentation across a wide range of pediatric abdominal masses.

Article.Title: Sleeve gastrectomy is associated with a higher incidence of rheumatoid arthritis and spondyloarthritis compared to gastric bypass
Article.Authors: Paccou J.; Letarouilly J.; Cailliau E.; Delettrez C.; Ficheur G.
Article.Abstract: To compare the incidence of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and spondyloarthritis (SpA) following three bariatric procedures—gastric bypass (GB), sleeve gastrectomy (SG), and adjustable gastric banding (AG)—using the French National Health Insurance Database. We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study of adults aged 18–65 years with morbid obesity (BMI ≥ 40 kg/m 2 ) who underwent primary bariatric surgery between 2012 and 2016. Patients with prior immune-mediated inflammatory disorders, disease-modifying antirheumatic drug use, or previous rheumatology consultations were excluded. Follow-up extended up to 10 years. Incidence rates (IRs) of first RA and SpA diagnosis were calculated per 1,000 person-years (PY). Time-to-event analyses used Fine and Gray competing-risk models with time-dependent coefficients (< 6 years vs ≥ 6 years), adjusted for age, sex, obesity class, and Charlson Comorbidity Index. Hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) compared SG and AG with GB. Among 46,137 patients (SG, 28,431; GB, 13,438; AG, 4,268), 418,759 PY of follow-up were accrued and 244 incidents RA or SpA identified (0.58/1,000 PY). IRs were lowest after GB (0.43/1,000 PY), intermediate after AG (0.51/1,000 PY), and highest after SG (0.67/1,000 PY). Compared with GB, SG was associated with a significantly increased RA or SpA risk during the first 6 years (sHR 2.76; 95% CI 1.67–4.55; p < 0.001). No significant difference was observed between AG and GB during this period (sHR 1.53; 95% CI 0.67–3.52). After 6 years, no between-group differences were observed. SG was associated with a higher risk of incident RA and SpA compared with GB. Given the observational nature of the study, further research is needed to confirm these findings and better understand the factors underlying this association.

Article.Title: Sex differences in the association between body mass index and recent suicide attempts in treatment-naïve young adults with major depressive disorder
Article.Authors: Zhu Q.; Xu J.; Lang X.; Lu Y.; Zhang X.
Article.Abstract: Although sex differences in suicidal behavior among young patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) are well documented, whether the association between elevated body mass index (BMI) and suicide attempts (SA) varies by sex remains inconclusive. This study examined, with stratification by sex, the associations of BMI with SA in the past 3 months and related factors in young patients with MDD, and further tested for a sex × BMI interaction. A total of 520 patients with MDD aged 18–25 years were enrolled and underwent comprehensive biochemical assessments, including measurements of glycemic parameters, lipid profiles, and thyroid hormone levels. Psychiatric evaluations were conducted using standardized scales for depressive, anxiety, and psychotic symptoms. SA was defined as a suicide attempt occurring within the past 3 months. Binary logistic regression was used for sex-stratified analyses, and a sex × overweight/obesity interaction was tested in the full-sample model. Among 520 young patients with MDD, the prevalence of overweight/obesity did not differ significantly by sex ( P > 0.05). Among males, SA was more prevalent in those without overweight/obesity than in those with it (24.5% vs. 12.5%, P < 0.05), whereas no such difference was observed among females (18.7% vs. 15.0%, P > 0.05). After adjustment for SBP, DBP, TSH, and education level, overweight/obesity was independently associated with lower odds of SA in males (OR = 0.32, P = 0.005, 95% CI 0.15–0.71), but not in females. After stratification by sex and BMI, the factors associated with SA differed across subgroups: HAMD score in males with overweight/obesity (OR = 1.32, P = 0.049, 95% CI 1.002–1.73); age (OR = 1.73, P = 0.01, 95% CI 1.12–2.68), HAMA score (OR = 1.91, P = 0.002, 95% CI 1.27–2.87), and BMI (OR = 0.38, P = 0.01, 95% CI 0.19–0.77) in males without overweight/obesity; HAMA score (OR = 1.32, P = 0.02, 95% CI 1.05–1.66) and TPOAb level (OR = 2.29 per 1-SD increment, P = 0.02, 95% CI 1.13–4.62) in females with overweight/obesity; and HAMD score (OR = 1.38, P = 0.04, 95% CI 1.01–1.89) in females without overweight/obesity. However, the sex × overweight/obesity interaction was not significant ( P = 0.24), so these stratified differences should be interpreted as descriptive rather than definitive sex-specific findings. This study suggests that, among young patients with MDD, the association between elevated BMI and SA and the related factors show different patterns when stratified by sex. Larger-scale and specifically designed studies, incorporating formal interaction tests and mechanistic measures, are warranted to further validate these descriptive observations.

Article.Authors: Vaitinadapoule H.; Decoeur F.; Aouimeur I.; Travers G.; Perrache C.; Svahn I.; Marais S.; Maucort G.; Gain P.; Thuret G.; Mascarelli F.; Gontier E.
Article.Abstract: Late-onset Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy (FECD) is marked by progressive thickening of Descemet’s membrane (DM), accumulation of guttae, and endothelial dysfunction, primarily affecting the central cornea. We studied the regional variability of FECD specimens using multiscale electron and surface imaging, along with shotgun proteomics. The central surface showed large, coalescent guttae within curly fibers and amorphous matrix with low roughness, while the deeper layer had buried guttae in a multilaminar matrix. Conversely, the paracentral surface had fewer, small round guttae on a thin matrix enriched with wide-spaced collagens and higher surface roughness. Molecular analysis revealed overexpression of fibril-forming collagens and key regulators of collagen organization and fibrillogenesis in the centre compared to the paracentral region, correlating with structural differences. These findings provide insight into FECD’s regional molecular dynamics and may help to develop biomarkers and therapies.

Article.Title: Numerical analysis of coal seam spontaneous combustion effects and preventive berm design for composite slope stability in arid open-pit mines
Article.Authors: Ru X.; Du W.; Zhang L.; Huang M.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates the spontaneous combustion of shallowly buried coal seams at the toes of dump–end-wall composite slopes in open-pit mines and its implications for slope stability. An integrated approach combining theoretical analysis, numerical simulations, and field investigations was employed to identify the mechanism of coal-fire initiation, assess its influence on slope stability, and develop a mechanism-informed prevention strategy. The results reveal a mechanism whereby stress redistribution, shear deformation, fracture evolution, and oxygen migration collectively govern coal-fire initiation in composite slopes. The interaction between waste-dump and end-wall slopes induces significant shear stress concentration and deformation within the slope toe, promoting fracture propagation and coalescence. Under hot and arid conditions, the resulting fracture networks provide oxygen pathways that enable spontaneous combustion of shallowly buried coal seams without direct outcrop exposure. Coal burning further reduces slope stability through coupled thermo-mechanical degradation, decreasing the factor of safety from 1.668 to 1.560. A counterweight berm strategy was developed to regulate toe stress conditions, suppress fracture connectivity, and interrupt oxygen transport pathways, increasing the factor of safety from the initial unbermed value of 1.668 to 1.758. The findings provide a geomechanical basis for the assessment and proactive prevention of coal-fire hazards in composite slope systems.

Article.Title: FDG PET evidence suggests the left insula may be a hub for cognitive reserve in mild cognitive impairment
Article.Authors: Liperoti R.; Cipriani M.; Di Tella S.; Anzuino I.; Testa C.; Clemente E.; Calvani R.; Lo Monaco M.; Calcagni M.; Cocciolillo F.; Silveri M.
Article.Abstract: Cognitive reserve (CR) refers to the ability to cope with the detrimental effects of ageing or brain pathology on cognition. Individuals with higher CR may maintain cognitive performance despite a greater burden of underlying brain pathology. This study aimed to characterize cerebral metabolic patterns associated with CR in subjects with amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI) using [18]F-FDG PET/CT, and to identify brain regions associated with higher CR. Sixty-three subjects with aMCI were included in this cross-sectional study. Based on the Cognitive Reserve Index questionnaire (CRIq), 29 participants were classified as having high CR (HCR) and 34 as having low CR (LCR). Brain [18]F-FDG PET/CT scans were obtained in all participants and compared with those of 19 cognitively healthy subjects (HS). Voxel-wise analyses and volume-of-interest analyses were performed to assess regional metabolic differences, and multivariable regression models evaluated the association between CRIq and insular metabolism after adjustment for age and sex. Both HCR and LCR groups exhibited the characteristic temporo-parietal pattern of Alzheimer’s disease-related hypometabolism compared with HS. Direct voxel-wise comparison between HCR and LCR identified a significant difference in the left anterior insula, where metabolism was relatively preserved in HCR. Left insular metabolism was positively associated with CRIq score independently of age and sex. These findings suggest that relatively preserved left insular metabolism is associated with higher CR in aMCI and identify the left anterior insula as a candidate neural substrate of CR. Future longitudinal studies will be important to confirm these findings and clarify the mechanisms possibly linking left insular metabolism to CR.

Article.Title: Tracking spatial variations of CO2 isotopologues, NH3 and H2O in urban air: a case study from the Campi Flegrei Caldera
Article.Authors: Di Martino R.; Gurrieri S.; Caliro S.; Santi A.
Article.Abstract: Anthropogenic CO 2 emissions are a major driver of greenhouse gas accumulation in the atmosphere, whereas natural sources, including volcanic degassing, can locally modify atmospheric composition. Since the onset of renewed bradyseismic activity at Campi Flegrei in 2005, the Solfatara area has released ~ 5,000 tons of CO₂ per day. Recent reports of elevated indoor CO₂ concentration in Pozzuoli prompted an in situ survey using a portable laser-based spectrophotometer. Measurements of stable isotope compositions (δ¹³C-CO₂, δ¹⁸O-CO₂, δ¹⁷O-CO₂) combined with NH 3 and H 2 O concentrations, enabled the identification of distinct atmospheric contributions despite the limited spatial variability of CO 2 concentrations. Atmospheric CO 2 in Pozzuoli exhibited distinct isotopic signatures consistent with contributions from soil degassing, dispersal of volcanic CO 2 from the Solfatara area, and fossil fuel combustion. In particular, atmospheric CO 2 showed a measurable 13 C-enrichment relative to the atmospheric background. This isotopic shift is incompatible with a simple dilution process and instead indicates admixture with an isotopically heavier geogenic CO 2 endmember, characterized by a δ 13 C-CO 2 value of approximately − 1.8‰ vs. VPDB. Spatial variations in H 2 O were related to distance from the marine shoreline, whereas NH 3 concentrations provided evidence of an anthropogenic influence on the atmosphere within the densely inhabited area. Concentrations of air CO 2 remained well below short-term exposure limits along the entire survey transect, although these thresholds are primarily intended for indoor environments. This study provides a combined characterization of carbon and triple oxygen isotope composition in atmospheric CO 2 for volcanic source attribution, and can establish a basis for the development of future high-resolution monitoring strategies. Continuous surveillance integrating CO 2 concentration and isotope compositions could therefore complement existing volcano monitoring approaches and strengthen environmental monitoring in densely populated volcanic areas.

Article.Authors: Banoocy N.; López-López D.; Oliveira R.; Nobari H.
Article.Abstract: This longitudinal observational study examined associations between accumulated weekly training load, match load and next-day muscle-specific force in elite male football players. Nineteen players contributed observed force measurements; five had no force measurements in the included microcycles. Missing outcome values (18.0–30.9%) were handled using 50 two-level predictive-mean-matching imputations. Random-intercept models were fitted separately to each completed dataset and pooled. Higher match PC1 had a negative association estimate for Nordic force (β = − 9.39 N per SD; model-based 95% CI − 19.44 to 0.66; p = 0.067). The player-cluster-robust interval was wider (− 25.31 to 6.53 N; p = 0.211). All 12 retained load-force associations had confidence intervals spanning zero under both approaches. The results did not establish the hypothesized association between higher match load and lower next-day Nordic force. Missing force measurements, limited cluster numbers and unmeasured contextual factors constrain interpretation. These data do not establish individual fatigue or injury-risk thresholds.

Article.Title: Determining association between metabolic syndrome and its components and oral-dental health among participants in fasa adult cohort study (FACS)
Article.Authors: Rezazadeh A.; Dahi A.; Rakhshani T.; Golab F.; Dehghan A.; Jeihooni A.
Article.Abstract: In recent years, the relationship between metabolic syndrome (MetS) and oral and tooth health status has been broadly addressed. Yet, lots of challenges have raised concerning this relationship. Although some cross-sectional studies have verified the existence of a relationship between these two health challenges, the results in some epidemiological studies have been contradictory. Thus, the present study was developed and executed targeting to outline the association between metabolic syndrome and its components and oral status in the participants in the Fasa Adult Cohort Study (FACS). This cross-sectional study was performed on 10,092 participants in the Fasa (Persian) Adult Cohort using baseline data from the cohort study. The data were collected via a questionnaire including demographic characteristics, health indicators, the history of underlying diseases, and the history of medication taking, which was conducted by interviewing a trained expert. After the data were included in SPSS-24, independent t-tests and multivariable binary logistic regression were utilized to analyze the data. A metabolic syndrome prevalence was 24.6%. Distribution of individual metabolic syndrome components defined per harmonized ATP III criteria—was as follows: hypertension (20.1%), diabetes mellitus (12.3%), hypertriglyceridemia (28.2%), reduced high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (26.8%), and elevated waist circumference (3.2%). Oral health status was quantified using the Decayed, Missing, and Filled Teeth (DMFT) index and its constituent components. Mean ± standard deviation values were: sound (healthy) teeth, 17.33 ± 10.05; decayed teeth, 9.20 ± 7.22; missing teeth, 14.67 ± 10.05; and filled teeth, 0.63 ± 1.64. Bivariate analysis demonstrated statistically significant associations between metabolic syndrome status and all DMFT components: sound teeth ( P = 0.038), decayed teeth ( P = 0.001), missing teeth ( P = 0.045), and filled teeth ( P = 0.001). In multivariable logistic regression analysis, after adjustment for demographic and lifestyle covariates, dental indicators were not independently associated with MetS status (all P > 0.05). Results from this study demonstrate significant unadjusted associations between metabolic syndrome and compromised oral health status. However, these associations were not independent after adjustment for confounders. These findings support attention to oral health in the clinical assessment of metabolic risk, but do not establish dental indicators as independent screening markers for MetS.

Article.Title: Parameter estimation of single, double, and three-diode photovoltaic cell models using an advanced optimization algorithm
Article.Authors: Belaala H.; Guezouli L.; Hamouma M.; Zaitsev I.; Antonenko A.
Article.Abstract: With the rising worldwide need for green power sources, dependable and efficient photovoltaic (PV) systems are emerging as one of the most promising choices among sustainable energy supplies. Precise modeling of solar generators is crucial to improve their energy conversion efficiency, rendering this necessity even more critical. The precise extraction of photovoltaic (PV) model parameters is crucial for the assessment of the PV system. Many current techniques for obtaining photovoltaic parameters exhibit poor precision and are susceptible to local optima. A Circulatory System Based Optimization (CSBO) is developed to address these flaws. This research presents an innovative approach for extracting essential characteristics of the single diode model (SDM), double diode model (DDM), and three diode model (TDM) of RTC FRANCE silicon solar cells utilizing the recently discovered CSBO, which has not been previously employed in this context. A CSBO utilizes the root mean square error (RMSE) to precisely compute the current of a PV unit and is examined. Non-linear equations are employed for the accurate resolution of the I-V curve in RTC FRANCE silicon solar cells. Comprehensive simulations are performed to assess the efficacy of the suggested strategy and its efficacy relative to other metaheuristic techniques. The findings indicate that CSBO markedly decreases the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), achieving optimal RMSE values of 9.860218 × 10 − 04 , 9.824848 × 10 − 04 ,9.803370 × 10 − 04 , and 2.425074 × 10 − 03 for SDM, DDM, TDM, and Photowatt-PWP-201 module respectively, with a smaller RT (Running Time) for all the PV cell models. The findings validate the enhanced performance and precision of CSBO which is adopts circulation-inspired search strategies to enhance the global exploration, local exploitation, population diversity, convergence speed, and premature convergence avoidance, relative to current methodologies, demonstrating that it yields more dependable parameter estimations and contributes to increased energy conversion efficiency in solar systems.

Article.Title: Effects of a cognitive training program on cancer-related cognitive impairment in breast cancer patients in active treatment: a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Sánchez-González J.; Jiménez-Sánchez S.; Sánchez-Gómez C.; Fonseca-Sánchez E.; Arroyo-Garrapucho N.; Pérez J.; Vaszquez-Carrasco E.; García-Tizón S.; Fernández-Rodríguez E.
Article.Abstract: Cancer-related cognitive impairment (CRCI) is a frequent and distressing complication in women undergoing active treatment for breast cancer. Although cognitive training has shown promise as a non-pharmacological strategy, evidence on ecologically valid interventions during active treatment remains limited. To evaluate the efficacy of an everyday cognition-based training program on cognitive function and related psychological and functional outcomes in women with breast cancer receiving active treatment. In this randomized controlled trial, 50 women newly diagnosed with breast cancer (within 6 months) were allocated (1:1) to either an Intervention Group ( n = 25; receiving a 4-month structured home-based daily cognitive training program of 80 real-life activities plus Health Education) or a Control Group ( n = 25; receiving Health Education alone). The control group received a health education program. Co-primary outcomes were objective cognitive performance (MoCA) and subjective cognitive function (FACT-Cog). Secondary outcomes included everyday cognition (PECC), anxiety (Hamilton scale), sleep quality (PSQI), functional independence (Lawton & Brody), performance status (ECOG), and subjective memory complaints (MFF). Assessments were conducted at baseline and post-intervention (4 months). After adjusting for baseline scores using ANCOVA, the intervention group demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in perceived cognitive abilities (FACT-Cog PCA domain; \(\:F=24.60\) , \(\:p<0.001\) , \(\:{\eta\:}_{p}^{2}=0.35\) ) compared to the control group. In contrast, no significant between-group differences were observed for objective global cognitive performance (MoCA; \(\:F=0.03\) , \(\:p=0.856\) ) or other FACT-Cog subscales. Everyday cognition (PECC) showed a positive unadjusted trend ( \(\:p=0.066\) , \(\:d=0.57\) ), which did not remain statistically significant in baseline-adjusted models ( \(\:p=0.614\) ). No significant intervention effects were detected for anxiety, sleep quality, functional independence, performance status, or subjective memory complaints after baseline adjustment. A structured everyday cognition-based training program improves perceived cognitive abilities during active breast cancer treatment. However, no significant effects were confirmed for objective cognitive screening scores or general functional outcomes.

Article.Title: Protease-sensitive antibacterial activity from tilapia gut-derived Enterobacter ludwigii is associated with a colicin V-like genomic candidate
Article.Authors: Chatterjee A.; Sinha K.; Mondal K.; Sanyal S.
Article.Abstract: Fish-associated intestinal bacteria are promising sources of antimicrobial compounds that may reduce reliance on conventional antibiotics in aquaculture. Here, 64 intestinal bacterial isolates from apparently healthy tilapia were screened against bacterial indicators, and isolate A1 was selected because its cell-free supernatant (CFS) showed antibacterial activity. Neutralization and catalase treatment did not abolish activity, and heat treatment reduced but did not eliminate the inhibitory effect, whereas trypsin and proteinase K abolished detectable inhibition. This profile supports a protease-sensitive, partially heat-tolerant bacteriocin-like inhibitory substance (BLIS). Ammonium sulfate precipitation and dialysis enriched the active fraction, increasing specific activity to 10.604 AU \(\mu\) g \(^{-1}\) against the Gram-positive bacterium Listeria monocytogenes and 9.643 AU \(\mu\) g \(^{-1}\) against the Gram-negative bacterium Aeromonas hydrophila . Whole-genome sequencing yielded a curated 4.96-Mb draft genome with 61 contigs, 54.31% GC content, 100% coverage breadth, and a weighted mean depth of 392.6-fold. Average nucleotide identity (ANI) assigned A1 to Enterobacter ludwigii , with 98.8048% ANI to the type strain EN-119. Gene prediction and antimicrobial-domain mining identified ELUD_A1_000009_42 , encoding a 162-amino-acid colicin V/microcin V-like protein, as the strongest candidate determinant. The candidate showed a Proteins family (Pfam) Colicin_V hit and full-length similarity to publicly available colicin V proteins. These results associate a protease-sensitive antibacterial phenotype with a specific, testable genomic candidate.

Article.Title: Development and comprehensive characterization of hybrid chicken meatballs formulated with a ternary blend of green pea, chickpea, and peanut flours
Article.Authors: Jahan I.; Akter L.; Sinthiya N.; Al Noman M.; Nijhum A.; Hossain I.; Rahman A.; Mazumder M.
Article.Abstract: Alternative meat products have been developed in response to consumer demand for healthy food. This study aimed to develop and evaluate hybrid chicken meatballs (HCB) by partially substituting chicken meat with a mixture of plant-based flours. Three HCB formulations (T 1 –T 3 ) were prepared by replacing chicken meat with increasing levels of green pea flour (15–25%) and chickpea flour (10–20%), along with constant 5% peanut flour. Proximate composition, physicochemical characteristics, microstructure, amino acid profile, and sensory properties were evaluated. Increasing plant flour substitution significantly ( p < 0.05) increased protein, ash, fibre, and carbohydrate content while reducing moisture and fat content. Cooking yield, moisture retention, and juiciness all improved progressively with plant flour addition. Textural properties, including hardness, springiness, cohesiveness, and chewiness, decreased with increasing substitution levels. Microstructural analysis confirmed that T 2 (20% green pea flour + 15% chickpea flour) formed the most cohesive and uniform protein matrix. Essential amino acid analysis confirmed that T 2 exceeded the control in most essential amino acid concentrations and met FAO/WHO reference values. Sensory evaluation confirmed T 2 as the most preferred formulation overall. These results indicate that moderate substitution of chicken meat with plant-based flours is an effective strategy for developing nutritionally enhanced, consumer-acceptable hybrid meatballs.

Article.Title: A comparative study of diaphragm ultrasound using multimodal parameters in healthy adults
Article.Authors: Du M.; Ye R.; Ning C.; Zhou H.; Li C.; Lai M.; Wu S.; Chen X.; Sun L.
Article.Abstract: To compare multimodal ultrasonographic parameters for diaphragmatic assessment across different intercostal spaces (ISs) in healthy adults, and to evaluate the feasibility and inter-method consistency of various measurement approaches. This cross-sectional study enrolled 337 healthy volunteers at Zhejiang Provincial People’s Hospital(November 2024–June 2025). Diaphragmatic thickness (DT), thickening fraction (TF), and shear-wave elastography (SWE) were evaluated at the 7th–9th ISs by 2D and M-mode ultrasonography. Statistical analyses included Paired t-tests and Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. No significant differences in echogenicity classification were observed between the 8th and 9th ISs ( p = 0.09). However, end-inspiratory thickness (Tei) and TF differed significantly between ISs ( p < 0.05) and between 2D and M-mode measurements ( p < 0.001). SWE image quality was superior at the 9th IS (76.55 ± 7.17% vs. 74.97 ± 9.15%, p = 0.012), though elastic modulus values did not differ ( p = 0.105). A standardized protocol for diaphragmatic ultrasonography was developed and meticulously outlined. Both the 8th and 9th ISs demonstrate adequate feasibility for routine diaphragmatic assessment, though thickness measurements require level-specific reference ranges due to significant inter-level variability. The 9th IS is recommended for SWE given its superior image quality. Notably, 2D imaging may be preferred in routine practice due to its lower dependence on high image quality.

Article.Title: Identification of complement system-related biomarkers in immunoglobulin A nephropathy through machine learning and single-cell data analysis
Article.Authors: Yang S.; Bai L.; Zhang X.; Meng Z.; Yalikun D.; Ha X.; Jiang H.
Article.Abstract: Immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) is associated with complement dysregulation, but complement-related molecular markers remain incompletely defined. We integrated bulk transcriptomic datasets (GSE93798 training; GSE37460 validation), a single-cell RNA-seq dataset (GSE171314), machine-learning feature selection, functional enrichment, immune deconvolution, and a preliminary qRT-PCR assessment to identify candidate complement-system-related biomarkers. Among 25 differentially expressed complement-related genes, LASSO, SVM-RFE, and Boruta jointly prioritized A2M, C3AR1, COLEC11, SERPINA1, and IL1B; A2M, C3AR1, and SERPINA1 showed consistent cross-cohort expression patterns and AUCs > 0.7. A three-gene ANN classifier achieved an apparent training AUC of 1.000 and an external-validation AUC of 0.959, although overfitting remains possible. Functional analyses associated the candidates with ECM-receptor interaction and propionate-metabolism signatures. CIBERSORT and exploratory single-cell analyses suggested macrophage-related associations, but the single-cell dataset included only one healthy control. Archived summary-level qRT-PCR measurements from 5 patients with IgAN and 5 living-donor controls showed higher mean A2M and C3AR1 expression in IgAN tissue; these measurements are presented descriptively because participant-level raw values and the original statistical-test output were not available for independent reanalysis. These findings support A2M, C3AR1, and SERPINA1 as candidate IgAN biomarkers requiring validation in larger, clinically annotated cohorts.

Article.Title: IoT-enabled individual poultry monitoring with lightweight step-counting for health assessment
Article.Authors: Sun X.; Zeng W.; Shi B.; Liang X.
Article.Abstract: To address the challenges of quantifying individual physical activity, delayed detection of health anomalies in high-density environments, and the lack of objective data supporting welfare-oriented farming in large-scale floor-rearing poultry farms, this paper proposes and implements an Internet of Things-based system for individual poultry behavior monitoring and digital management. The system consists of three core components: an energy-efficient smart anklet, a solar-powered multi-modal communication base station, and a cloud management platform. At the edge node, the smart anklet utilizes a CH582M microcontroller and an ADXL362 three-axis accelerometer to achieve precise acquisition of poultry gait signals. The base station integrates Bluetooth Low Energy and an ML307A LTE Cat.1 cellular module, featuring a custom SL3795-based solar power management circuit to overcome the challenges of device power supply and data relay transmission in expansive rearing facilities. Algorithmically, a lightweight step-counting algorithm based on the signal amplitude features and an adaptive dynamic threshold is proposed to minimize computation overhead. Furthermore, integrated with cloud-based time-series logic, multi-dimensional strategies are developed for daily activity evaluation, abnormal resting early warning, and out-of-bounds anti-loss alarming. Field tests indicate that the proposed algorithm achieves a high average step-counting accuracy of 97.19% under complex activity states, and the multi-dimensional state warning model reaches an overall accuracy of 96.33%. This solution provides objective and reliable data support for the digital logging of high-quality poultry behaviors and the advancement of animal-centric precision livestock farming.

Article.Title: Intelligent educational agent-based collaborative scaffolding for STEM interdisciplinary project-based learning: a multi-dimensional framework and empirical evaluation
Article.Authors: Zang J.
Article.Abstract: STEM interdisciplinary project-based learning (PBL) asks students to knit together knowledge their courses have kept apart, and to do so while absorbing the ordinary friction of group work. Scaffolding designed for single-discipline tasks rarely keeps pace with either demand. This paper proposes an intelligent educational agent-based collaborative scaffolding model comprising four architectural layers—data perception, intelligent analysis, strategy decision, and interaction execution—supported by three specialized functional agents targeting cognitive guidance, process coordination, and reflection facilitation. A multi-dimensional feature fusion approach employing scaled dot-product attention diagnoses collaborative states in near real time, reaching a macro-averaged $$\:{F}_{1}$$ of 0.83 on a test set split by team, and a timing policy trained with Proximal Policy Optimization decides when to intervene while a fading rule decides when to withdraw. Twenty-four five-member teams (120 undergraduates) completed two interdisciplinary projects over six weeks under agent-based scaffolding, teacher-led scaffolding, or unsupported collaboration. Because students were nested in teams and several outcomes are defined at team level, condition effects were estimated with baseline-adjusted, cluster-robust models rather than treating the 120 students as independent. Agent-based scaffolding exceeded unsupported collaboration on posttest achievement (adjusted contrast 14.67 points, 95% CI [10.38, 18.96]) and on team-level interdisciplinary integration (0.33, 95% CI [0.20, 0.46]), with teacher-led scaffolding intermediate. Scaffold type and intervention timing were selected by the system rather than randomized, so their comparative effectiveness is reported as process evidence, and the collaboration-quality pathway is reported as an exploratory association rather than a demonstrated causal mechanism. Protocol, analysis and model code, rubrics, prompts, thresholds, and a clearly labelled synthetic demonstration data set are archived with the paper; the empirical derived observations stay restricted under the ethics approval and are available for controlled verification.

Article.Title: Digital video watermarking algorithm integrating 3D convolution and DT-CWT
Article.Authors: Li D.; Li G.
Article.Abstract: With the widespread application of digital video in copyright protection and multimedia security, embedding robust and imperceptible watermarks while preserving video quality remains a critical challenge in digital video applications. Therefore, this study proposes a digital video watermarking algorithm that integrates three-dimensional convolutions with the dual-tree complex wavelet transform (DT-CWT). Unlike existing convolutional neural network DT-CWT watermarking methods, which mainly use DT-CWT as a static frequency domain preprocessing method, this method models DT-CWT sub-band features across frames and spacetime through a three-dimensional convolutional network. Based on the synergistic effects of dense feature fusion and an attention guidance mechanism, it achieves adaptive watermark embedding in the frequency domain and temporal consistency dimensions. A differentiable compression simulation is used for H.264 encoding during training to perceive the actual encoding distortion distribution. This improves the stability of the watermark in real compression environments. The experimental results on the publicly available UVG dataset showed that the proposed algorithm achieved significant performance improvements in multiple indicators. In ablation experiments, the complete model achieved a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 41.8 dB and a structural similarity index of 0.985, validating the importance of key modules. Comparative experiments revealed that after 100 training epochs, the proposed algorithm achieved a bit error rate of 0.22 on the test set while maintaining a recognition rate above 96% under various typical attacks. This method was more resistant to attacks such as scaling, cropping, rotation, and Gaussian noise. The peak signal-to-noise ratio of this method was improved by an average of about 2–4 dB compared to the comparison method. The structural similarity index was improved by about 0.03–0.06. Moreover, the video multi method evaluation fusion index was improved by about 6–12 points. The proposed algorithm significantly enhances the robustness and stability of watermarks while maintaining video quality, providing a high-performance practical solution.

Article.Title: An experimental and numerical study on drillstring stick-slip oscillations in ultra-deep wells
Article.Authors: Wang W.; Wang H.; Zhang H.; Xu B.
Article.Abstract: Severe drillstring stick–slip oscillations can substantially reduce drilling efficiency and accelerate bit wear in ultra-deep wells. In this study, full-scale downhole measurements are first obtained during drilling of an ultra-deep vertical well using a 333.4-mm PDC bit. The measured tri-axial accelerations reveal severe low-frequency stick–slip oscillations, with a period of approximately 10.0 s, consisting of about 3.0 s of stick phase and 7.0 s of slip phase, and a maximum estimated downhole angular velocity of approximately 350 rev/min at a surface rotary speed of 120 rev/min. A nonlinear finite-element model considering coupled axial and torsional motions, axial–torsional geometric nonlinearity, drilling-fluid damping, and a non-regularized velocity-weakening bit-rock interaction law is then developed. The resulting nonlinear equations of motion are solved numerically using the Newmark time-integration method. The key bit-rock interaction parameters are calibrated against the field measurements by reproducing the maximum downhole angular velocity and the characteristic stick–slip period and phase durations. The calibrated model reproduces the measured maximum angular velocity of approximately 350 rev/min and the 10.0-s stick–slip period. Parametric analyses further show that increasing WOB intensifies stick–slip oscillations, with the stick–slip severity index increasing from approximately 0.52–1.46 as WOB increases from 60 to 160 kN at 120 rev/min, whereas increasing surface rotary speed reduces the severity index from approximately 1.75–0.78 as rotary speed increases from 60 to 160 rev/min at a WOB of 120 kN. The results provide a physics-based framework for understanding stick–slip behavior and evaluating drilling-parameter effects in ultra-deep wells.

Article.Title: Orally bioavailable CB2 receptor agonists attenuate neuroinflammation and stabilize the blood–brain barrier
Article.Authors: Rom S.; Zuluaga-Ramirez V.; Gajghate S.; Grether U.; Guba W.; Reichenbach N.; Van der Stelt M.; Ullmer C.; Pacher P.; Persidsky Y.
Article.Abstract: Neuroinflammation and blood–brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction are key contributors to the pathogenesis of many neurological disorders. Cannabinoid receptor 2 (CB 2 ) agonists possess anti-inflammatory properties and may represent promising therapeutic agents for preserving BBB integrity. This study evaluated the effects of orally bioavailable CB 2 receptor agonists on leukocyte–endothelial interactions and BBB function using in vitro and in vivo models of neuroinflammation. Novel CB 2 receptor agonists were tested in an aseptic localized encephalitis mouse model and in a lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced systemic inflammatory response model. Leukocyte adhesion and migration within cerebral microvessels were assessed in vivo. BBB permeability was evaluated in LPS-treated mice, while barrier integrity was measured in primary human brain microvascular endothelial cells (BMVECs) using transendothelial electrical resistance (TEER). Cytokine release, adhesion molecule expression (vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 [VCAM-1] and intercellular adhesion molecule-1 [ICAM-1]), and inflammatory gene expression in isolated cerebral microvessels were also analyzed. Statistical significance was determined using comparative analyses between treatment and control groups. Among the compounds tested, RO6839828 and HU-910 appeared most effective in reducing leukocyte adhesion to and migration across the BBB, although direct statistical comparisons between compounds were not performed. CB 2 receptor agonists significantly attenuated BBB hyperpermeability in LPS-treated mice and improved endothelial barrier integrity in vitro, as reflected by increased TEER values. Treatment also reduced cytokine release and decreased mRNA expression of VCAM-1 and ICAM-1. In addition, CB 2 agonists attenuated dysregulation of multiple inflammation- and endothelial injury-related genes in cerebral microvessels isolated from LPS-treated mice. Pre-treatment of either BMVECs or primary human monocytes reduced monocyte adhesion to and transmigration across endothelial monolayers in vitro. When administered before the inflammatory challenge, orally bioavailable CB 2 receptor agonists prevented neuroinflammation-associated BBB dysfunction and leukocyte trafficking in both in vitro and in vivo models. Because all models were prevention paradigms, these data establish prophylactic rather than therapeutic efficacy. They support further investigation of CB 2 receptor agonists for the treatment of neurological diseases associated with neuroinflammation and BBB disruption.

Article.Title: Role of CB1 receptors in the gastrointestinal tract after microbiota depletion and natural recolonization
Article.Authors: Beraldi E.; Habibyan Y.; Keenan C.; Wallace L.; Sharkey K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The endocannabinoid system is involved in the control of gastrointestinal motility and function, with increasing evidence of its interactions with gut microbiota. We investigated if cannabinoid (CB) 1 receptors participate in the enteric nervous system (ENS) response to microbiota depletion and natural microbial recolonization. We characterized enteric neurons and glia in the ileum and colon of CB 1 receptor knockout mice (CB 1 -KO), showing their ENS is identical to wild type (WT) mice. Next, WT and CB 1 -KO mice were treated for 2 weeks with antibiotics followed by 2 or 4 weeks of natural microbial recolonization, compared to mice on water or continuous antibiotic treatment. CB 1 -KO mice lost significantly more body weight than WT mice during antibiotic treatment, and both genotypes had slower whole gut transit with antibiotic treatment. Compared to WT mice, CB 1 -KO mice had faster whole gut transit, but slower colonic motility after recolonization. Gut microbiota diversity was similarly affected by antibiotic treatment in both genotypes. CB 1 -KO mice showed the same ENS neuronal and glial density as WT mice in all populations, with neuronal loss after antibiotic treatment and recovery after natural microbial recolonization. Altogether, this study reveals new insights in the interactions between the endocannabinoid system and gut microbiota in gastrointestinal function.

Article.Title: Evaluation of the comparative biofilm removal properties of four cleansing and debridement tools, in an ex vivo porcine wound model
Article.Authors: Doherty C.; Baqader S.; Mercer S.; McBain A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The effectiveness of four mechanical debridement devices for removing ex vivo porcine wound biofilms was assessed. Devices comprised a one-sided straight monofilament fibre pad, a one-sided looped monofilament fibre pad, a two-sided foam pad with distinct loosening and absorptive surfaces (TSFP), and traditional cotton gauze. Dual-species Staphylococcus aureus / Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms were cultivated in an ex vivo porcine wound model. Debridement was standardised using a mechanical simulator and performed at a single time point (24 h, 72 h, or 7 d post-inoculation) to represent differing biofilm maturities, or repeatedly over seven days (once, twice, or three times) to simulate outpatient dressing-change schedules. Biofilm removal was quantified using colony counting and viability mapping. In the model-derived percentage-removal analysis following single debridements, OSLMP and TSFP demonstrated significantly greater removal than gauze at 24 h. TSFP consistently achieved > 90% model-derived reduction in viable CFU/wound across all single-debridement time points and demonstrated significantly greater removal than gauze at 24, 72 and 168 h. PrestoBlue staining revealed corresponding reductions in PrestoBlue-positive wound-surface coverage. Following repeated debridements, TSFP maintained > 90% model-derived reduction in viable CFU/wound and demonstrated significantly greater removal than gauze following each debridement schedule. Hedges’ g effect sizes frequently exceeded 2.0 for TSFP relative to gauze and the single-sided devices, indicating pronounced effects under the predefined interpretation thresholds.

Article.Title: An explainable swarm-optimized hybrid GRU–Transformer framework with wavelet-based spatial–temporal feature modeling and activation function analysis for rainfall classification across Pakistan’s climatic regimes
Article.Authors: Farman H.; Hussain M.; Laila U.; Alam M.; Su’ud M.; Saaludin N.; Khan T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate rainfall occurrence prediction is essential for climate risk management, flood preparedness, and water resource planning, particularly in climatically diverse regions such as Pakistan. This paper develops and compares a multi-phase classification of rainfall based on daily IMERG precipitation data over six representative Pakistani cities spanning very low-, moderate-, and high-rainfall regimes, i.e., Gharo, Gilgit, Islamabad, Karachi, Swat, and Turbat. The research follows a four-stage modeling process: (i) a baseline set of ensemble-learning models; (ii) a hybrid GRU–RNN model on 30-day temporal sequences with 19 engineered features; (iii) a GRU–RNN optimized with Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) and the Tiki-Taka Algorithm (TTA); and (iv) a swarm-optimized hybrid GRU–Transformer using wavelet-based spatio-temporal features (W-ST). Four ensemble methods, namely Bagging, Boosting, Voting, and Stacking, were used in the initial phase to classify next-day rainfall. Findings show ensemble models perform well in low-rainfall cities in terms of overall accuracy because of the effect of class imbalance, while predictive performance is more balanced in moderate- and high-rainfall areas. In the second stage, a hybrid GRU–RNN model on 30-day temporal sequences and 19 engineered features showed good discrimination ability across the climatic regimes, with better rainfall-event classification in Karachi and Gharo among the low-rainfall cities and balanced classification in Gilgit and Swat. The analysis of activation functions also showed that ReLU is more effective in highly imbalanced low-rainfall conditions, whereas Tanh is more stable and balanced in moderate and heavy rainfall conditions. The third stage involved optimization of the GRU–RNN using the proposed TTA framework to improve the stability of the classification process, achieved by adding VMD-based multi-scale signal decomposition and adaptive hyperparameter tuning. The optimized framework achieved strong performance across cities, including Karachi (ACC = 0.944, F1 = 0.624, ROC–AUC = 0.885), Gharo (ACC = 0.927, F1 = 0.596), Gilgit (ACC = 0.772, F1 = 0.589, ROC–AUC = 0.834), and Swat (ACC = 0.656, F1 = 0.556). In the fourth stage, to enhance predictive performance, a swarm-intelligence-based hybrid deep-learning system combining W-ST, STFM, HGRA, DTGAM, GRU, and Transformer modules was developed using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Glowworm Swarm Optimization (GSO). Empirical findings show that PSO offers greater performance stability in most cities, especially Gharo, Karachi, Islamabad, and Swat, whereas GSO can offer better localized performance in Gilgit and Turbat. The activation-wise assessment shows that Tanh-based networks consistently generate better F1-scores and ROC–AUC values, whereas ReLU provides slightly more accurate results in extreme class-imbalance situations. In general, the proposed PSO/GSO hybrid framework achieved high classification performance across a variety of climatic regimes. The highest overall performance was achieved with GSO–Turbat in the Tanh configuration (ACC = 0.9617, F1 = 0.754, ROC–AUC = 0.956), followed by PSO–Turbat (ACC = 0.9583). PSO-based configurations in Gharo and Karachi were highly stable, with accuracies of 0.9392 and 0.9351, respectively. In moderate-rainfall regions, Gilgit achieved optimal performance with GSO–ReLU (ACC = 0.9064, F1 = 0.806, ROC–AUC = 0.953), while Islamabad performed best with PSO–Tanh (ACC = 0.8838, F1 = 0.782, ROC–AUC = 0.927). In all cities, ROC–AUC values were high (≈ 0.90–0.95), indicating strong discrimination ability between rain and non-rain events. The explainability analysis conducted using SHAP revealed wavelet-derived components, lagged rainfall variables, persistence measures, and seasonal encodings as the top predictors, suggesting that the proposed framework captures physically significant rainfall dynamics rather than spurious ones.

Article.Title: TiO2 nanocrystalline microspheres as an effective scattering layer in bilayer photoanodes for DSSCs
Article.Authors: More P.; Mujawar A.; Salunke S.; Kim J.; Bulakhe R.; Pathan H.
Article.Abstract: Among emerging solar technologies, Dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) stand out for their scientific and technological attention for indoor and outdoor light harvesting applications. However, their efficiency is often hindered by limited light harvesting and recombination losses of electrons. To address these challenges, TiO 2 microspheres synthesized by the hydrothermal technique were utilized as a light scattering layer (LSL) in bilayer photoanode configuration. We report on the characterization of TiO 2 along with its utilization in an LSL using the microsphere structure. TiO 2 (P25), which ensures improved dye uptake and efficient electron transport, while the microsphere-based scattering layer redirects unabsorbed photons back into the photoanode. This design significantly improves light-harvesting efficiency using ruthenium-based sensitizing dyes like N3, N719, 520 DN, and Black, resulting in elevated J sc and overall power conversion efficiency (η) compared to conventional single-layer electrodes. Which is in good agreement with the Incident Photon to Current Conversion Efficiency (IPCE) spectra data. The highest J sc of 4.308 mA/cm 2 , 1.59% efficiency, and 43.53 ms mean electron lifetime was achieved for the bilayer photoanodes with N3 dye. These results demonstrate the potential of TiO 2 microspheres to enhance light harvesting in DSSCs and may be explored for future T-DSSC applications.

Article.Title: Effects of an 8-week core stabilization exercise program on respiratory function, trunk muscle endurance, and postural stability in individuals receiving basic acting education
Article.Authors: Çelik H.; Badilli Hantal F.
Article.Abstract: Efficient breathing, trunk muscle endurance, and postural stability are important physical components of acting performance. This study examined whether an 8-week core stabilization exercise (CSE) program could improve respiratory function, trunk muscle endurance, and postural stability in individuals receiving basic acting education. Thirty-three eligible individuals receiving basic acting education were randomly assigned to the Exercise Group ( n = 17) or the Control Group ( n = 16). Two participants in the Exercise Group withdrew for personal reasons before completion of the intervention. Therefore, 31 participants (Exercise Group, n = 15; Control Group, n = 16) completed the study and were included in the final analysis. Both groups received diaphragmatic breathing training, while the Exercise Group additionally participated in core stabilization exercises twice weekly for 8 weeks. Respiratory function, trunk muscle endurance, and postural stability were assessed before and after the intervention. Thirty-one participants completed the study (Exercise Group, n = 15; Control Group, n = 16). Between-group comparisons of changes showed greater improvements in FVC (mean difference = 1.31 L, p < 0.001), FEV1 (mean difference = 0.68 L, p = 0.040), and PEF (mean difference = 3.43 L/s, p < 0.001) in the Exercise Group compared with the Control Group. The corresponding between-group effect sizes were large for FVC (Cohen’s d = 1.73), FEV1 (d = 0.77), and PEF (d = 1.40). Significant between-group differences were also observed in selected trunk muscle endurance and dynamic balance outcomes. Adding CSE to diaphragmatic breathing training may be associated with greater improvements in respiratory function, trunk muscle endurance, and selected components of dynamic balance compared with diaphragmatic breathing training alone. These findings provide preliminary evidence that core stabilization may be a useful component of physical conditioning programs for individuals receiving basic acting education; however, the effects of CSE on acting performance should be investigated in future studies using direct measures of acting performance. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier NCT06625164, retrospectively registered on 24 April 2024.

Article.Title: A network science approach to granular time series segmentation
Article.Authors: Kesić I.; Fortuna C.; Mohorčič M.; Bertalanič B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Time series segmentation assigns a label to each part of a sequence. We formulate dense univariate segmentation as node classification on a graph whose nodes are the original time points. A local window provides node features without setting output granularity. We evaluate the approach on a TSSB-derived inductive benchmark built from disjoint UCR training and test instances. Under one fixed Graph Attention Network (GAT), visibility-based transformations achieve the highest mean ranks among eleven graph constructions. WDPVG, directed NVG, and weighted NVG form a statistically indistinguishable top group after Holm correction. On the 59-dataset Time Series Segmentation Benchmark, WDPVG+GAT reaches a weighted F1 of 0.916, below seq2point at 0.951 and statistically indistinguishable from same-feature MLP, random-forest, and 1-NN controls , because at this downsampled resolution each segment is short and the fixed 81-sample window already spans most of it. At native resolution , where each segment is longer than that window, WDPVG+GAT is less sensitive to feature-window width and remains above the same-feature MLP at every tested window. The graph’s advantage over these point-wise classifiers comes from context beyond the local window, which the visibility graph’s long-range edges can supply, rather than from better features within it. In a separate resolution sweep, it is statistically tied with a window-searched seq2point while using about $$70\times $$ fewer parameters and $$46\times $$ less measured peak memory, although seq2point moves ahead after downsampling. This identifies a practical operating regime for finely sampled series when model size and repeated window tuning matter.

Article.Title: Experimental analysis of AISI 304 stainless steel machinability utilizing TiO₂ and ZnO nanoparticle-infused emulsifier oil-based cutting fluids
Article.Authors: Shanmugam T.; Kandasamy V.; Janakiraman R.; Subramanian R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigates the effectiveness of nanoparticle-dispersed cutting fluids in minimizing temperature rise and improving machining quality. During the precise turning of AISI SS304 stainless steel, excessive heat generation at the work-tool interface can undermine tool durability and surface finish. Two types of nanoparticles, TiO₂ and ZnO, were mixed with SAE30 emulsifier oil at concentrations of 1.5% and optimized 2.25% by weight to improve the thermal and tribological properties of the base fluid. A DCMT-120,404 cutting insert was employed on a production-grade CNC lathe for turning operations. Cutting forces were measured using a lathe tool dynamometer, while interface temperatures were monitored with a pyrometer. The cutting fluid containing 2.25% by weight of TiO₂ and ZnO nanoparticles demonstrated superior performance compared to the other fluids tested, significantly reducing both cutting force and interface temperature. This improvement was attributed to enhanced heat dissipation and lubrication, which is expected to reduce frictional interaction at the tool-chip interface and better surface roughness characteristics.

Article.Title: Co-localized optical and acoustic defect modes enable resonantly enhanced photoelastic readout in a one-dimensional phoxonic multilayer
Article.Authors: Aly A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Efficient acousto-optic transduction in compact multilayer platforms requires the coexistence of a spectrally confined optical resonance and a mechanically responsive acoustic mode with strong spatial and spectral overlap. In this work, a shared-geometry one-dimensional phoxonic multilayer is numerically investigated for enhanced photoelastic readout through defect-mediated optical–acoustic coupling. The proposed architecture consists of a responsive central defect layer embedded between reversed periodic bilayers, with optical and longitudinal acoustic characteristics modeled using transfer-matrix formulations. Candidate structures are screened based on the formation of localized defect states within the corresponding optical and acoustic Bloch stop bands, while a first-order photoelastic model is applied to quantify the conversion of acoustic strain into optical resonance modulation. The optimized configuration, consisting of five bilayers on each side of a 494.13 nm defect layer, supports an optical defect resonance at 1521.83 nm with a quality factor of 1.51 × 104 and an acoustic defect mode at 3.22425 GHz with a quality factor of 833.2. The predicted displacement sensitivity reaches 2.724 pm/nm, corresponding to a strain sensitivity of 0.409 pm/µε. Field-energy analysis demonstrates simultaneous localization of optical and acoustic modes within the defect cavity, while frequency-domain calculations reveal a 21.67-fold enhancement of the first-order photoelastic response when the acoustic excitation is resonantly matched to the defect mode. Further assessments, including defect-free reference structures, deterministic thickness perturbations, passive-loss evaluations, and Monte Carlo parameter analysis, characterize resonance robustness, fabrication-related variability, and the consistency of the proposed transduction mechanism. These results establish a calibration-aware numerical framework for designing compact one-dimensional phoxonic structures with enhanced defect-assisted acousto-optic readout capabilities.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: defect modes; strain sensitivity
