Article.Title: An edible capacitive tilt sensor towards sustainable autonomous robotics
Article.Authors: Qi Q.; Kumaresan Y.; Keller A.; Garrad M.; Rossiter J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Edible transient robots can be eaten, digested, and metabolized by human, and are a rapidly emerging technology towards sustainable autonomous robotics. Among numerous developments of edible robotic components, edible tilt sensors can inform the self state of the robot such as orientation and tilt angle, representing a key technology for autonomous robotic control. However, the only existing fully edible tilt sensor in the literature generates binary output and is hard to monitor the continuous inclination angle change. Additionally, the resistive sensing principle is strongly affected by heat and humidity, hindering its application to wet environments such as in the human body. To bridge the gap, we present the first edible tilt sensor capable of monitoring continuous change of tilt angle. Our tilt sensor is based on capacitance variance, which by principle minimizes the effects of temperature and humidity. The sensor is composed of a gelatine compartment coated with wax, graphite electrodes and an edible dielectric sensing liquid. We present the concept, design, fabrication, and characterization of our sensor, and demonstrate its application in robotic control. The sensor has a large working range (0 $$^\circ$$ to 80 $$^\circ$$ ) with a high sensitivity (2.34 %/ $$^\circ$$ ) and repeatability. This device paves the way for future development of sustainable autonomously navigable edible soft robotics.

Article.Title: Central sensitization-related measures and peripheral treatment outcomes in patients with chronic pain: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Santiago D.; Fischer-Jbali L.; Reyes del Paso G.; Montoro C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Central sensitization may contribute to persistent pain and unfavorable outcomes following interventions targeting peripheral pain mechanisms. However, clinical studies use heterogeneous approaches to assess central sensitization-related phenomena, most commonly the central sensitization inventory (CSI), alongside psychophysical measures of pain processing. To systematically review the association between central sensitization-related self-report or psychophysical measures and clinical outcomes following invasive peripheral procedures in adults with chronic pain conditions, including low back pain, knee and hip osteoarthritis, endometriosis-related pain, shoulder pain, and abdominal nerve entrapment, and to quantitatively synthesize their association with post-intervention pain intensity. This systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines and was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD42024592591). PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect were searched between October 1 and November 10, 2025, for original studies published between 2015 and 2025. Eligible studies included adults with chronic pain who underwent an invasive peripheral procedure and were assessed using a central sensitization-related self-report or psychophysical measure related to central pain processing; non-original reports and studies not meeting these eligibility criteria were excluded. Risk-of-bias was assessed using the quality in prognosis studies tool. Findings were synthesized narratively, and post-intervention pain intensity was quantitatively synthesized using a random-effects meta-analysis with Cohen’s d and 95% confidence intervals. Statistical heterogeneity was assessed using I 2 . Twenty-four studies comprising 3494 participants were included. Higher central sensitization-related scores or psychophysical findings were generally associated with less favorable clinical outcomes, particularly greater post-intervention pain intensity. Twelve studies contributed to the quantitative synthesis. Higher CSI scores or enhanced temporal summation were associated with greater post-intervention pain intensity (Cohen’s d = 1.1074, 95% CI [0.7060, 1.5089]; I 2 = 88.35%). Under a conservative overall classification rule, 21 studies were rated as having a high risk of bias and three as moderate. Substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity was also observed across studies. Higher CSI scores and psychophysical findings related to nociceptive facilitation may be associated with less favorable outcomes in patients with chronic pain, particularly greater pain intensity, following invasive peripheral procedures. These findings should not be interpreted as evidence that central sensitization itself was directly measured or that central sensitization-related measures uniformly predict treatment outcomes across chronic pain conditions and invasive peripheral procedures. Further prospective studies using standardized and multimodal assessments of central pain processing are required. Article.Title: Risk of orofacial clefts in offspring following maternal exposure to anti-seizure medications in a UK CPRD GOLD observational study
Article.Authors: Jain K.; Davies A.; Lewis S.; Zhong C.; Forbes H.; Rast J.; Martin F.; Ahlqvist V.; Davies N.; Tomson T.; Magnusson C.; Lee B.; Rai D.; Madley-Dowd P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Orofacial clefts (OFC) are complex congenital anomalies characterised by a gap in the upper lip and/or palate, causing speech and feeding difficulties in children. Studies suggest inconsistent findings for an association between anti-seizure medications (ASM) and OFCs. Our study evaluated the association between ASM prescription during pregnancy and OFC in offspring using a United Kingdom primary care-based cohort of 393,281 mothers and 518,050 babies. 3651 and 3199 women were prescribed ASMs during preconception and first trimester respectively, irrespective of indication. Valproate prescription during preconception and first trimester was associated with higher odds of OFCs, with limited evidence after adjustment for potential confounders. Carbamazepine, pregabalin, and levetiracetam showed limited evidence for increased odds of OFCs, and no evidence was found for gabapentin or lamotrigine. No OFC cases were found in children born to mothers exposed to topiramate or phenytoin. Children exposed to ASM polytherapy during first trimester were 6 times as likely to have OFC as compared to ASM monotherapy. While ASMs may contribute to the risk of OFCs, our findings suggest they are unlikely to be a major cause, given that most exposed pregnancies did not result in a cleft and most children with OFCs were not exposed to ASMs.

Article.Title: Prioritising emotional experience in pocket parks: towards human-centred design through Kano-based needs assessment
Article.Authors: Zhou Z.; Wang M.; Chen Q.; Yuan S.; Mo S.
Article.Abstract: As a key component of sustainable urban planning, the emotional design of pocket parks warrants further investigation. Drawing on case studies of four typical pocket parks in Shanghai and 400 valid questionnaire responses, this study developed emotional need indicators based on emotional design theory and combined the Kano model, Better–Worse coefficients, and non-parametric tests to classify and prioritise users’ emotional needs and examine differences across user groups. The results show that Must-be qualities, such as Safety and Security Assurance, establish the baseline conditions for use; One-dimensional qualities, such as Environmental Restorativeness, have a strong capacity to enhance satisfaction; and Attractive qualities, such as Social Interaction, foster deeper emotional experiences. Qualities such as Accessibility of Digital Services and Biodiversity were classified as Indifferent. Based on these needs priorities, this study proposes emotional design strategies that prioritise securing Must-be qualities, focus on developing One-dimensional qualities, and moderately expand Attractive qualities. The findings provide context-specific guidance for the design and renewal of pocket parks in Shanghai and other comparable high-density built environments, while offering empirical insights into the shift of public-space design from a function-oriented approach towards a human-centred and emotion-oriented approach.

Article.Title: Room temperature synthesis of novel azine-linked covalent organic framework: molecular docking, theoretical investigation studies, and antimicrobial activity
Article.Authors: Abdelnasser E.; Fahim A.; El-Hendawy M.; Oyekunle D.; Ramadan A.; Khodair A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this study, an azine-linked covalent organic framework (COFTH) was synthesized via a Schiff base reaction between terephthaldehyde and hydrazine hydrate at room temperature. COFTH was promoted in dioxane at room temperature, compared with traditional solvothermal reactions in organic solvents. This synthesis has the advantages of large-scale production, simplicity, safety, low cost, and short reaction time. The synthesized COFTH has a large surface area, excellent thermal and chemical stability. It has a large surface area of 118.358 m 2 g −1 with a pore size of 1.80 nm and a pore volume of 0.113 cm 3 /g. It showed higher sensitivity as an antibacterial agent than tobramycin against, gram‐negative bacterial ( Escherichia coli and Pseudomonas aeruginosa) and gram-positive bacteria ( Staphylococcus aureus , Enterococcus faecalis). Moreover, molecular docking analysis of COFTH was performed to understand the molecular interaction with different proteins and their reactivity with COFTH. In addition, the computational calculation studies of COFTH, terephthaldehyde, and NH 2 NH 2 were performed to elucidate their physical properties, FMO, ESP, and MEP. Furthermore, the correlation of 1 H NMR and 13 C NMR was confirmed via DFT/WB97XD/6–311(G) basis set.

Article.Title: Efficient real-time vehicle tracking via lightweight YOLO and DeepSORT integration
Article.Authors: Xu W.; Liu J.; Cheng M.; Huang Y.
Article.Abstract: Detecting and tracking vehicles ahead during driving is a critical technology for ensuring driving safety and enhancing the driving experience. However, traditional detection and tracking models often suffer from high computational intensity and large parameter sizes, making them unsuitable for resource-constrained mobile devices. This paper introduces a lightweight vehicle tracking model that integrates YOLO and DeepSORT. By incorporating GhostConv and C3GhostV2 modules into the backbone and neck networks of YOLO, we enhance detection accuracy while reducing model size. The Focal-EIoU function is utilized to improve the recognition of small, distant target vehicles. Additionally, ShuffleNetV2 replaces DeepSORT’s feature extraction network, further reducing model parameters. Experimental results demonstrate that among the latest models in the YOLO series, YOLOv5 offers more stable and accurate performance, making it a more suitable baseline for vehicle detection and tracking tasks. Based on this foundation, experimental results show that, compared to the baseline model implemented using the Ultralytics framework, the proposed model reduces GFLOPs by 37.1%, decreases the number of parameters by 34.5%, and achieves mAP@0.5 by 0.3%. The overall model size is only 13.62 MB, 44.8% smaller than the original. Validated on the SODA10M dataset, the model exhibits improved detection accuracy and maintains performance compared to other models, making it suitable for deployment on mobile devices during vehicle driving.

Article.Title: Hybrid KarcıFANN–EEFO controller for adaptive speed control of BLDC motors in electric vehicles
Article.Authors: Anish S.; Kebila Anns Subi L.; Suthanthira M.
Article.Abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) have gained significant attention in recent years and are rapidly emerging as a sustainable alternative to fossil fuel-based transportation due to their efficiency and environmental benefits. Maximizing energy efficiency and increasing driving range are the main goals of EV development, and both of these goals rely significantly on improving motor performance. The Brushless Direct Current (BLDC) motor is the best option for EVs among different motor types because of its strong performance, high efficiency, and excellent speed and position control capabilities. To achieve accurate and adaptive speed regulation, this study proposes a Hybrid Karcı Fractional Artificial Neural Network (KarcıFANN) controller. The KarcıFANN architecture integrates fractional calculus with artificial neural networks, providing enhanced learning adaptability and memory characteristics for dynamic system control. To further optimize the KarcıFANN’s performance, Electric Eel Foraging Optimization (EEFO) is employed for weight and bias tuning. The EEFO algorithm improves convergence speed and prevents premature stagnation during training, ensuring optimal controller performance. Simulation results obtained in the MATLAB/Simulink environment demonstrate superior performance over conventional controllers, achieving a settling time of 0.0321 s and a rise time of 0.0201 s under the high-inertia condition, together with low overshoot and accurate reference-speed tracking. Consequently, the integration of KarcıFANN with EEFO presents a robust and efficient solution for BLDC motor speed control, marking a substantial advancement in intelligent EV propulsion systems and contributing to the evolution of sustainable and responsive transportation technologies.

Article.Title: Foundation model-driven framework for human–object interaction prediction with segmentation mask integration
Article.Authors: Park J.; Lee K.; Chang H.; Cho J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this work, we introduce Segmentation to Human–Object Interaction (Seg2HOI), a novel framework that integrates segmentation-based vision foundation models with the human–object interaction (HOI) task, distinguished from traditional detection-based HOI methods. Our approach enhances HOI detection by not only predicting the standard triplets but also introducing quadruplets, which extend HOI triplets by including segmentation masks for human–object pairs. More specifically, Seg2HOI inherits the properties of the vision foundation model (e.g., promptable and interactive mechanisms) and incorporates an implicit relation-learning decoder that applies these attributes to the HOI task. By freezing the vision foundation model, Seg2HOI preserves its original capabilities while using pixel-level mask guidance to support high-level relational reasoning. Despite being trained only for the HOI task, without additional training mechanisms for these properties, the framework demonstrates that such features still operate efficiently. Extensive experiments on two public benchmark datasets demonstrate that Seg2HOI achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods, even in zero-shot scenarios. Lastly, we propose that Seg2HOI can generate HOI quadruplets and interactive HOI segmentation from novel text and visual prompts that were not used during training, making it versatile for a wide range of applications by leveraging this flexibility.

Article.Title: HAFI-DTA: an interpretable multimodal framework for drug-target affinity prediction based on hierarchical attention guidance and feature iterative interaction
Article.Authors: Wang Y.; Song S.; Tian W.; Zhu B.
Article.Abstract: Accurate prediction of drug-target affinity (DTA) is a core technical step in high-throughput drug screening and targeted drug discovery, which directly affects the efficiency of candidate compound mining and the control of research and development costs. Traditional experimental methods are difficult to meet the requirements of high-throughput screening, while existing deep learning-based models generally suffer from bottlenecks such as shallow fusion of multi-source heterogeneous features, insufficient mining of interactive features, and inadequate generalization robustness. To address these issues, we propose HAFI-DTA (Hierarchical Attention-Guided and Feature Iterative Interaction for Multimodal Drug-Target Affinity Prediction). Specifically, our framework employs a hierarchical attention mechanism to guide the fusion of multi-source heterogeneous features, and combines a two-layer GRU with iterative interaction to capture the deep correlations among features. Experimental results on the KIBA and Davis datasets demonstrate that the proposed HAFI-DTA model achieves overall performance comparable to the current state-of-the-art, while delivering stable and modest improvements in both CI and MSE metrics. Moreover, under the most challenging drug–target double cold-start scenario, our model attains the best performance, exhibiting excellent generalization robustness. In addition, interpretability analysis shows that the model can automatically focus on the key residues of the real binding pockets of proteins, providing an important basis for subsequent drug design and binding mode research.

Article.Title: Hokkaido brown bear-related human injuries: a public-record cohort with nested clinical characterization
Article.Authors: Mitamura S.; Oide S.; Hayashi S.; Shirane Y.; Tsuruga H.; Takafumi H.; Miura K.; Mitamura M.; Watanabe A.; Ishikawa K.; Osawa M.; Maeda T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Human injuries caused by Hokkaido brown bears have been described in fragmented public and clinical records. We conducted a retrospective descriptive public record cohort study of Hokkaido brown bear attack episodes from 2019 to 2024, supplemented by linked clinical records for selected episodes. The primary aim was to characterize publicly recorded episodes and victims; exploratory analyses compared fatal episode proportions by attack time grouping and broad activity context, and the linked clinical subset was used for descriptive clinical characterization only. Among 28 episodes involving 36 victims, seven (25.0%) were fatal. At the victim level, 17 injuries were minor, 12 severe, and seven fatal. Fatal episodes occurred in seven of 16 solo-coded episodes (43.8%) and none of 11 group-coded episodes (0.0%; two-sided Fisher exact P = 0.0216), an exploratory, noncausal association. Seven victims from five episodes were linked to clinical records. Their injuries included complex craniofacial and soft tissue trauma, ocular injury, open fractures, major vascular injury, and thoracic trauma; all received plastic and reconstructive surgical care, with additional specialty involvement in selected cases. This study describes recent Hokkaido brown bear attack episodes using a public record cohort with transparent source documentation and linked clinical details for selected cases. Because of the small number of episodes, potential public record ascertainment bias, and the nonrepresentative clinical subset, the findings should be interpreted descriptively and as hypothesis generating.

Article.Title: Histopathology image classification based on ensembles of highly compact features
Article.Authors: Łażewski S.; Cyganek B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this paper, we present a method for extracting highly informative yet compact features from histopathological images, which at the same time enable their classification with high accuracy. These types of concise features are very valuable due to the ever-increasing size of datasets as well as the sheer size of histopathology scans. To meet these requirements, we propose new methods for extracting features from the combinations of inner layers of deep neural networks DenseNet-161 and ResNet-152, as well as DINO derived from vision transformers. This is followed by the construction of the subspaces with the help of the principal, as well as neighborhood component analysis. This method creates new features: PCA/NCA-DenseFeats, PCa/NCA-ResFeats, and PCA/NCA-DINO. We then further improve their performance through domain-trained extraction models. The collected results show that the classification accuracy of these features becomes stable even after several-fold reduction of the dimensionality of the baseline features. This means that there is no need to use long representation vectors, and features even several times shorter can be used for classification with almost no information loss. In addition, we propose the multi-architecture ensemble of classifiers orchestrated by the error-correcting output codes method, which utilizes features extracted from three different domain-finetuned models with different architectures: ViT Small, ResNet-152, and DenseNet-161. The proposed solution allows for an increase in accuracy by up to almost 7pp compared to the baseline. The classification vector consumes only 180 float16 values, which is significantly smaller than many other published methods. This reduces the memory required to store features and enables faster classification of these representations. The proposed method was evaluated on the BreakHis breast cancer dataset (achieving 95.39% at 40X, 92.07% at 100X) and the Kather colorectal cancer dataset (97.1%), demonstrating its generalizability and applicability.

Article.Title: Sustainable valorization of tea waste for promoting plant growth, secondary metabolites production and environmental sustainability in tea cultivation
Article.Authors: Thapa P.; Agarwal S.; Anand J.; Jaiswal D.; Pandey A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Camellia sinensis (L.) Kuntze, represents a commercially significant crop, primarily recognized for its pharmacologically active secondary metabolites, including catechins and caffeine. However, excessive reliance on agrochemicals threatens both soil fertility and the biochemical quality of tea leaves, underscoring the urgent need for sustainable agronomic alternatives. The present study evaluates the agronomic and biochemical efficacy of Tea Waste Manure (TWM), an organic amendment derived from post-industrial tea processing residues, as a sustainable substitute for synthetic agrochemicals. Field experiments were conducted from July 2023 – October 2024 at two distinct tea-growing areas of Uttarakhand, India. Pre-and post-treatment assessments encompassed quantitative analysis of vegetative biomass, photosynthetic pigment concentrations (chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b, and total carotenoids), as well as targeted metabolite profiling, including total phenolic content, total flavanol content, catechins, and caffeine content. The research additionally emphasizes on evaluating the impact of TWM on soil health via enumerating bacterial load, determining physicochemical and nutritional properties, and enzymatic activity of soil. Application of TWM resulted in statistically significant enhancements in plant growth, pigment biosynthesis, and metabolite accumulation with an increase in catechin and caffeine concentration in leaves. Additionally, soil analyses demonstrated enhanced fertility attributes, including optimised pH, elevated macronutrient levels, and increased microbial proliferation, as well as increased enzymatic activity. In conclusion, the findings reaffirm the viability of converting agro-industrial waste into organic inputs, not only enhancing resource efficiency but also promoting environmentally sustainable tea cultivation practices, paving the way for a greener and more environmentally friendly agricultural future.

Article.Title: Screening and characterization of endophytic bacterial isolates associated with Echinops kebericho M. and Lepidium sativum L. and evaluation of their potential role
Article.Authors: Senbeta D.; Dekebo A.; Ebu S.
Article.Abstract: Endophytic bacteria (EB) associated with medicinal plants contribute to plant growth by enhancing nutrient availability, stress tolerance, and phytohormone production. This study aimed to isolate and characterize potential endophytic bacterial isolates (EBIs) from Echinops kebericho Mesfin and Lepidium sativum L., two traditional Ethiopian medicinal plants, and to evaluate their ability to utilize various growth substrates. Roots of E. kebericho and seeds of L. sativum were collected for bacterial isolation. Biochemical and enzymatic assays were performed to characterize the isolates. Phosphate solubilization, zinc solubilization and indole acetic acid production were determined based on standard in vitro assays. Characterization and identification of Endophytic bacterial isolates were carried out using Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization Time-of-Flight Mass Spectrometry mass spectrometry and 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Endophytic bacteria belonging to Bacillus , Paenibacillus , Proteus , and Pseudomonas genera were identified, with Bacillus being the most frequently detected genus. The isolate Ls5I1 showed 98.29% 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity with Lysinibacillus capsici PB300 T , suggesting that Ls5I1 may represent a novel endophytic bacterium. The isolate demonstrated strong phosphate and zinc solubilization activities and produced IAA. Molasses served as cost-effective and low-cost growth carbon source for growth and yielded the highest cell biomass of Lysinibacillus sp. Ls5I1. In conclusion, the study highlights Lysinibacillus sp. Ls5I1 as promising plant growth-promoting bacteria capable of utilizing agro-wastes like molasses, producing phytohormones and solubilizing insoluble minerals. These findings suggest its potential application as a sustainable biofertilizer in agriculture.

Article.Title: From hard carbon to activated carbon: influence of surface area and pore structure on the electrochemical performance of coconut rachis-derived supercapacitor electrodes
Article.Authors: Bindhu D.; Gayathri M.; Ramachandran A.; Jinchu I.; Jose R.; Sreekala C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The performance of supercapacitors depends on the structural characteristics of electrode materials and their interactions with electrolytes. In the present work, hard carbon (HC) and chemically treated coconut rachis-derived activated carbon (AC) are comparatively studied for understanding the role of porosity, surface area and electrochemical performance. Through chemical activation, the compact structure of HC was converted to a hierarchically porous AC, resulting in an increased specific surface area from 32 to ~1025 m² g⁻¹. Such AC provided rich electrochemical active sites along with efficient transport of electrolyte ions. Structural and compositional changes induced by activation were characterised using FESEM, BET, EDX, XRD, FTIR, and Raman spectroscopy. Electrochemical performances of HC and AC were analysed using different aqueous electrolytes. In all electrolytes, AC showed better capacitive behaviour than HC due to the developed hierarchical pore system and high surface area. AC in 6 M KOH showed a maximum specific capacitance of 201 F g⁻¹. Besides, the supercapacitor assembled using AC in 6 M KOH showed a high specific capacitance with ~93% capacitance retention after 2000 cycles of charge-discharge. These findings demonstrate that engineering the pore structure and surface area of biomass-derived carbon is essential for enhancing supercapacitor performance.

Article.Title: A novel preclinical model of cDCD lung transplantation with implications for necroptosis
Article.Authors: Sakurai T.; Kanou T.; Matsui T.; Nagata H.; Kimura K.; Fukui E.; Kimura T.; Ose N.; Shintani Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study established a novel rat model that simulates controlled donation after circulatory death (cDCD) lung transplantation (LTx), and investigated necroptosis as a therapeutic target to improve graft quality using a three-phase experimental design. First, we established a model that reproduced the agonal phase in the donor (Phase I). Second, prolonged warm ischemic time progressively worsened graft function, as evidenced by reduced oxygenation, increased pulmonary edema, and increased necroptosis-related signals in pretransplant samples (Phase II). Accordingly, necrostatin-1 (Nec-1), an inhibitor of receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1), was administered during the pre-mortem, graft-flushing, and peri-transplant periods, which improved graft quality, reduced neutrophil infiltration after reperfusion, and decreased the ratio of phosphorylated mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein to total MLKL (pMLKL/MLKL) in pre-transplant samples, consistent with the attenuation of necroptosis-related signaling. These findings suggested that necroptosis-related signaling during the ischemic phase is associated with graft injury in cDCD LTx, and that RIPK1 inhibition may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for attenuating graft injury under prolonged warm ischemia.

Article.Title: Benchmarking machine-learning surrogates for rapid prediction of the reflectance-defined stopband width of finite dielectric Bragg reflectors
Article.Authors: Bouazzi Y.; Esmail M.; Touahmia M.; Elleuch Z.; Alshammari S.; Selmi F.; Kanzari M.; Bouandas H.; Soliman S.
Article.Abstract: Predicting the stopband width of finite one-dimensional dielectric Bragg reflectors requires a transfer-matrix calculation followed by spectrum-level edge extraction for each candidate stack. Although an individual wavelength-vectorized TMM evaluation is inexpensive, this calculation is repeated throughout large screening campaigns. Five supervised regressors are benchmarked as surrogates for the reflectance-defined stopband width Δλ Stop of finite multilayers at normal incidence, in the lossless, non-dispersive limit. TMM spectra were generated for stacks parameterized by the refractive indices n L and n H , the layer thicknesses d L and d H , and the number of bilayers N. For each spectrum, Δλ Stop was taken as the widest continuous interval with R(λ) ≥ 0.95. Designs with no such interval, or with a widest interval below 5 nm, were excluded, retaining 1660 of 2000 sampled designs. Hyperparameters of RF and SVR were selected by 10-fold cross-validation on the 1411-structure development set, while MLP depth was examined from one to ten hidden layers under the same test-isolated protocol. The selected six-hidden-layer MLP (128,64,32,16,16,16) achieved R 2 = 0.9862, RMSE = 10.47 nm, and MAE = 5.92 nm on the independent 249-structure test set. On a structured external set of 120 quarter-wave designs from four dielectric pairs, the final MLP achieved R 2 = 0.9688, RMSE = 5.67 nm, and MAE = 4.44 nm against the TMM reference; 94.17% of the cases had absolute errors below 10 nm and all 120 cases remained below 20 nm. Under an accuracy-controlled benchmark, the wavelength-vectorized TMM required 0.856 ms per structure at the selected 201-point spectral grid, whereas end-to-end single-sample inference with the final MLP, including input standardization, required 0.328 ms, corresponding to a 2.60× speedup. The surrogate is intended as a bounded-domain screening tool complementing, not replacing, full TMM analysis.

Article.Title: Carrier-selective dimensional crossover from bulk stibnite Sb2S3 to the single-chain limit
Article.Authors: Ulian G.; Valdrè G.
Article.Abstract: Low-dimensional materials display physical properties markedly different from their bulk counterparts because of quantum confinement. Chain-based chalcogenides provide pre-formed structural motifs for exploring one-dimensional (1D) electronic behaviour without cutting or passivating an extended two-dimensional lattice. In the present work, we use hybrid density functional calculations and semiclassical Boltzmann transport theory to characterize the mineral stibnite (Sb 2 S 3 ) across its structural hierarchy, from the bulk (3D) crystal to the natural (100) cleavage layer (2D) and finally to the unsupported single-chain limit. Phonon dispersions show that both 2D and 1D models are dynamically stable, while the energy analysis quantifies the progressive removal of inter-chain interactions. The 2D layer retains a slightly enlarged indirect gap and exhibits the most dispersive chain-direction conduction band, giving the lightest electron mass among the three systems. By contrast, complete chain isolation opens a wider direct gap and produces an exceptionally flat, strongly non-parabolic valence-band edge together with finite full-zone dispersion. Transport calculations at equal carrier loading reveal a carrier-polarity-dependent crossover: hole transport evolves comparatively regularly from bulk to layer to chain, whereas the electron branch is non-monotonic because the highly dispersive 2D conduction band combines high conductivity with weak energy selectivity. Water adsorption weakly perturbs the isolated chain, while oxygen produces structural activation and an in-gap hybrid state. These results define the intrinsic single-chain reference for Sb 2 S 3 and clarify how partial and complete inter-chain decoupling reorganize its frontier electronic states.

Article.Title: Knowledge and attitudes of Egyptian medical students towards artificial intelligence application in medical practice: a multicenter cross‑sectional study
Article.Authors: El-Helaly M.; Hussein A.; Taman A.; Farrag N.; Elfeky A.; Elhelaly A.; Essam N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly impacted various fields, including medicine. As AI integration in medicine expands, medical students and professionals need to develop a comprehensive understanding of its applications. This study aimed to explore the self-reported knowledge and attitudes of undergraduate Egyptian medical students regarding artificial intelligence application in medical practice. A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted between June and August 2025 among undergraduate medical students from seven Egyptian medical schools. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling. Data were collected via a validated structured web-based questionnaire distributed through social media to assess students’ demographics, knowledge, and attitudes toward AI applications in medical practice. This study included 1438 medical students with a mean age of 20.3 years ± 1.9 years. Overall, 55.3% demonstrated good knowledge and 66.8% showed a positive attitude toward AI applications in medical practice. Good knowledge was significantly higher among students in higher academic years (3rd year AOR = 1.88, P = 0.006; 4th year AOR = 2.02, P = 0.007; 5th year AOR = 1.86, P = 0.034) and among those reporting peers and mentors (AOR = 1.35, P = 0.017), scientific papers and books (AOR = 1.71, P < 0.001), training courses (AOR = 1.43, P = 0.004), and mass media (AOR = 1.32, P = 0.036) as their main sources of AI information. A positive attitude toward AI was significantly more common among male students (AOR = 1.50, P = 0.001), 4th-year students (AOR = 1.97, P = 0.014), and those willing to enroll in an AI course (AOR = 1.30, P = 0.039). YouTube was perceived as the most valuable social media source for AI-related information (90.4%), followed by Telegram (86.6%) and WhatsApp (65.2%). Although the Egyptian medical students who participated in this study demonstrated generally positive attitudes toward AI and a willingness to learn, they may be navigating this transition with limited institutional guidance. These findings suggest that medical schools should consider integrating AI-related technical literacy and ethical reasoning into the core curriculum.

Article.Title: An integrated wireless sEMG framework with Bayesian-optimized machine learning for multi-task locomotor classification and neuromuscular characterization
Article.Authors: Wagdy D.; Rashad S.; Malek A.; Anwar H.; Kandil A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Wearable surface electromyography (sEMG) systems show strong potential for real-time gait analysis, yet few frameworks combine wireless acquisition, standardized normalization, and optimized machine learning within a single validated pipeline, leaving their joint contribution to subject-independent locomotor recognition unclear. This study developed and validated a custom wireless sEMG framework combining hardware design, normalization evaluation, and Bayesian-optimized machine learning for locomotor-task classification and neuromuscular characterization. An ESP32-based system recorded tibialis anterior, soleus, and gastrocnemius lateralis activity in 25 healthy participants during level walking, stair ascent, and ramp ascent. Signals were bandpass filtered (20–500 Hz), rectified, and used to extract 120 time-, frequency-, and time–frequency-domain features. Three normalization strategies, three feature-selection methods, and eight Bayesian-optimized classifiers were evaluated via an exploratory participant-level split, nested 5 × 5 cross-validation, leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) validation, and an independent test set. Task-dependent EMG differences were significant with large effect sizes (η 2 = 0.183–0.708, p < .001). Level walking was the most electromyographically distinct task, while stair and ramp ascent were similar yet separable; ramp ascent showed multi-muscle co-activation at mid-stance and peak soleus activity at toe-off (50.7 ± 6.2% MVC). Genetic Algorithm feature selection with Z-score normalization gave the best single-split performance (logistic regression: 98.33% accuracy; SVM: 96.33%). Under the stricter LOSO regime, random forest reached 89.02% accuracy with 44 features, while a correlation-pruned 17-feature subset matched or exceeded this across all classifiers—best with SVM (92.40%)—achieving an 85.8% dimensionality reduction from the original feature space (61% relative to the 44-feature set) with no loss in mean accuracy. Two deep-learning baselines (1D-CNN, BiLSTM) achieved comparable LOSO accuracy (91.39% and 87.72%), confirming the feature-based pipeline captures the signal’s discriminative structure without end-to-end deep architectures. These findings support an interpretable, compact, subject-independent framework for multi-task locomotor classification, though broader clinical validation is still needed.

Article.Title: Integrated markov state-space framework for reliability evaluation, failure analysis, and maintenance strategies for high-tension power transmission lines
Article.Authors: Kumar A.; Kumar P.; Kumar P.; Kamila P.
Article.Abstract: Overhead transmission lines and high-tension wires represent the critical infrastructure of the world’s electrical power systems. These systems facilitate the bulk transfer of electrical power over vast distances. A significant percentage of the world’s existing power transmission infrastructure has reached an age where it has become increasingly vulnerable to environmental degradation, corrosion, mechanical stress, and thermal effects. These effects may cause critical component failure in power systems, resulting in economic losses. These components include the main transmission line, conductor strands, insulator discs, and insulator strings. The current paper proposes a sophisticated probabilistic mathematical model through Markov state-space modeling that allows for assessment of the efficiency, risk, reliability, and economic feasibility of transmission line systems. Moreover, the paper introduces economic break-even points that define the exact relationships in the form of linear inverse functions between the expected profit and the costs of maintenance in terms of repair, maintenance, and outage cost penalties in comparison with the basic revenues. Therefore, the current paper links the field of reliability engineering with that of economics in relation to the power grid system operation. The numerical results presented in this study are based on hypothetical parameters for demonstrative purposes. The model is analyzed using the regenerative point technique, assuming exponentially distributed failure and repair times, to derive various reliability measures.

Article.Title: Distinct estrogenic transcription programs of estetrol and 17β-estradiol across mammary, uterine, and vaginal cell types of pseudomenopausal mice
Article.Authors: Crevet L.; Dias Da Silva I.; Wuidar V.; Bouvencourt G.; Fioramonti M.; Destrebecq C.; Song Y.; Blacher S.; Foidart J.; Péqueux C.; Van Keymeulen A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Menopause results from a marked decline in estrogen production and leads to symptoms that impair quality of life. Menopausal hormone therapy is effective in alleviating these symptoms; however, it is associated with an increased risk of estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer. Estetrol (E4), a natural fetal estrogen produced by the liver, has emerged as a promising alternative, relieving menopausal symptoms while remaining neutral on tumor growth in mouse models. To further assess its potential, we compared the transcriptional effects of E4 and estradiol (E2) in three estrogen-sensitive tissues: the mammary gland, uterus, and vagina. Ovariectomized adult mice, used to model menopause, were treated for two weeks with either a therapeutic dose of E4 (E4low), a tenfold higher supratherapeutic dose (E4hi), or E2. In mammary luminal cells, E2 induced a proliferative gene signature that was absent following E4 treatment. E4 did not elicit a distinct transcriptional profile, supporting the notion that it acts as a weaker estrogen in this tissue. In contrast, in the uterine and vaginal epithelium, E2, E4low, and E4hi similarly regulated most genes, and all treatments produced comparable morphological effects. However, in fibroblasts of the uterus and vagina, E2 induced a specific transcriptional signature that was not reproduced by E4. Additionally, comparison of gene signatures following E2 treatment across different organs revealed that, beyond proliferative genes, the sets of upregulated genes differed markedly between tissues, both in epithelial and fibroblast compartments, with the exception of a small inflammation-related gene set shared between uterine and vaginal fibroblasts. Overall, this study refines our understanding of estrogen downstream effects and highlights key differences between E2 and E4, supporting the idea that E4 may represent a safer alternative for menopausal hormone therapy in clinical settings.

Article.Title: The clinical and imaging comparisons between sellar extraventricular neurocytoma and nonfunctional pituitary macroadenoma
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Ran C.; Li W.; Liu L.; Luo Y.
Article.Abstract: We aimed to explore the clinical and imaging features of sellar extraventricular neurocytoma (EVN) through a comparison between sellar EVN and nonfunctional pituitary macroadenoma. 19 cases of EVN and 27 cases of nonfunctional pituitary macroadenoma were retrospectively included, and their clinical and imaging findings were analyzed. Compared with sellar EVNs, nonfunctional pituitary macroadenomas were more common with cystic changes (51.9% vs. 21.1%, P = 0.035), intratumoral hemorrhage (29.6% vs. 0, P = 0.027), and vesicle signs (33.3% vs. 0, P = 0.015). Compared with nonfunctional pituitary macroadenomas, sellar EVNs were common with solid lesions (78.9% vs. 48.1%, P = 0.035), obvious MR enhancement (89.5% vs. 55.6%, P = 0.014), eccentric cavernous sinus involvement (84.2% vs. 44.4%, P = 0.007), and dural tail sign (68.4% vs. 22.2%, P = 0.002). Compared with nonfunctional pituitary macroadenoma, sellar EVN was more common with subtotal resection (37.0% vs. 68.4%, P = 0.036) and postoperative radiotherapy (14.8% vs. 78.9%, P < 0.001). However, there was no significant difference in recurrence and progression-free survival between the two groups, although the gross total resection rate of nonfunctional pituitary macroadenomas was higher (59.3% vs. 21.1%, P = 0.010). Solid lesions with obvious MR enhancement, dural tail sign, and eccentric cavernous sinus involvement could suggest sellar EVN in the condition of negative pituitary hormone. The clinical and imaging comparisons between sellar EVN and nonfunctional pituitary macroadenoma were helpful for clinical diagnosis and treatment.

Article.Title: A multidirectional extradural corridor for pretemporal endoscope-assisted orbitozygomatic–anterior petrosectomy
Article.Authors: Yuncu M.; Bilgin B.; Kartum T.; Karadag A.; Bozkurt B.; Tanriover N.
Article.Abstract: Surgical exposure of the ventral petroclival region remains technically challenging because of the complex three-dimensional relationships among the middle cranial fossa, petroclival junction, cavernous sinus, brainstem, and surrounding neurovascular structures. The orbitozygomatic (OZ) approach, anterior transpetrosal approach (ATPA), and pretemporal corridor are well-established approaches that provide complementary anatomical perspectives. This study aimed to define the continuous ventral petroclival corridor created by integrating extradural OZ–ATPA exposure with the intradural pretemporal corridor under endoscopic assistance. Five silicone-injected human cadaveric heads (10 sides) underwent standardized OZ craniotomy followed by extradural ATPA. The dissection was sequentially extended through a pretemporal intradural corridor and supplemented with 0° and 30° endoscopic inspection to evaluate anatomical continuity beyond the microscopic line of sight. Stepwise dissections were performed to characterize anatomical visualization during the sequential dissection along the ventral petroclival axis. Following anterior petrosectomy and dural opening, the ventrolateral brainstem between the dorsum sellae and the internal auditory canal (IAC) was visualized. Through the combined OZ–pretemporal trajectory, the optic tract, crural cistern, interpeduncular cistern, and mammillary bodies were identified from an inferior-to-superior perspective. Endoscopic inspection demonstrated deep and contralateral petroclival structures, including the contralateral abducens nerve and petrous apex, as well as inferior structures toward the cerebellopontine angle beyond the IAC. These findings document qualitative anatomical visualization; surgical freedom and the safety of instrument manipulation around the inferior and contralateral structures were not assessed. Stepwise integration of extradural OZ–ATPA exposure with the intradural pretemporal corridor and endoscopic inspection provides complementary anatomical views from the mammillary bodies to the cerebellopontine angle. This framework may support three-dimensional anatomical orientation and operative planning, but endoscopic visualization does not establish a safe working corridor to all visualized structures.

Article.Title: Advanced statistical modeling of loading waveform, frequency, temperature, and SBS modification effects on asphalt concrete resilient modulus
Article.Authors: Ghanizadeh A.; Safi Jahanshahi F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Resilient modulus (Mr) is one the most important parameter for designing flexible pavements based on different damage criteria. The resilient modulus test measures the recoverable elastic strains of asphalt concrete under repeated loading, and therefore provides a stiffness-related parameter which is affected by temperature and loading conditions. The Mr of asphalt concretes is typically measured at specific temperatures and loading frequencies because of the high cost and time-consuming nature of testing; therefore, predictive models are necessary to predict the Mr at other temperatures and loading frequencies. The aim of this study is to present a framework for modeling and predicting the Mr of asphalt concretes by considering four parameters: loading waveform, loading frequency, temperature, and SBS modification. SBS, loading waveform, temperature, and loading frequency were used as the input parameters. The statistical comparison of developed models reveals that the MARS-POA method outperformed the others. The R 2 values for training and testing data were 0.9973 and 0.9732, respectively. Temperature has the greatest relative importance, while waveform has the least influence on Mr. In addition, master curves corresponding to waveform type and to SBS-modified or control mixture were calibrated in order to compare the results of MARS-POA model with those of master curves.

Article.Title: Research on fault diagnosis and control strategies for battery packs
Article.Authors: Ye Z.; Zhu Q.; Fu X.; He G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract With the rapid electrification of the automotive industry, the traction battery pack has become the most safety-critical subsystem of an electric vehicle, and any insulation or communication fault must be identified and managed reliably. This work proposes a fuzzy-theory-based diagnosis and control strategy for battery packs that detects and confirms unpredictable faults under diverse operating conditions. The method couples a fuzzy inference system (FIS) with a calibrated expert database: an adaptive fuzzy matching mechanism continuously adjusts the process and observation noise in the state-of-charge and terminal-voltage correction, while triangular membership functions, an IF–THEN rule base, Mamdani inference and centroid defuzzification convert the diagnostic signals into graded fault levels, with rule weights being refined after each confirmed event. Fault confirmation follows the debounce intervals and consecutive-cycle counts defined in the unified threshold tables, and the resulting fault levels activate power-limitation responses. Validation through simulation and vehicle experiments reveals that the judgment time for insulation faults lengthens by 4.6 s (from 3.0 s to 7.6 s), whereas the corresponding accuracy climbs from 81.1% to 92.3%; for communication faults, the accuracy rises from 91.4% to 97.7%, and the interval between fault confirmation and completed power limitation is 16.1 s in simulation, 8.2 s on the test bench, and 24 s under real-world driving. Article.Authors: Aldhahri E.; Almazroi A.; Alkinani M.; Alghamdi E.; Janbi N.; Ayub N.; Al-Sulami Y.
Article.Abstract: Disasters affect citizen safety, municipal infrastructure, and the economy, making disaster management vital and difficult. Rapid urban expansion and climatic extremes have increased big catastrophe frequency and complexity. Situational awareness and quick decision-making are needed. Due to these restrictions, this research offers an AI system for real-time catastrophe assessment and response using drones and the Adaptive Convolutional-Transformer Fusion Network. Convolutional feature extraction and attention-based temporal modeling allow ACTF-Net to grasp sequential interactions and dynamic spatial patterns in high-dimensional catastrophic data. Article.Authors: Kala K.; Pathak R.; Shahi N.; Patil P.; Chatterjee N.; Nadella R.; Patiyal R.; Pande V.; Mallik S.

Among these, 88.2 mg kg − 1 day − 1 is suggested as the minimum effective therapeutic dose for rainbow trout under the present experimental conditions. Residue depletion analysis further indicated a muscle withdrawal period of 35.89 days following administration at 80 mg kg − 1 day − 1 . Article.Title: Risk of biases in estimating storm surge extremes: a global study

Article.Abstract: Abstract Extreme sea levels (ESLs) threaten coastal zones, and global assessments suggest that future ESLs grow with rising mean sea level (MSL) as the main driver. Bayesian model comparison and posterior coefficient support classify 200 of the 386 analysed series (52%) as non-stationary and 186 as stationary. At some stations, ESLs increase more than MSL; at others they increase less than MSL or even decrease. Article.Authors: Taşyürek M.; Mutlu O.; Kaygısız Ö.; Teke M.; Adıgüzel Ö.; Şevik U.

Corresponding mAP@0.5 values were 0.91 for YOLOv11 and 0.90 for YOLOv12. Article.Title: Climate-related shifts in fire-weather regimes across heterogeneous mountain ecosystems: long-term spatiotemporal assessment in the Alborz mountains
Article.Authors: Roshan G.; Saman A.; Arbabi M.; Dogar M.; Ali T.
Article.Abstract: Climate change is intensifying fire-weather activity globally, yet the extent to which ecosystem structure modulates fire-weather regimes in complex mountain environments remains insufficiently understood. These differences are consistent with the combined influence of contrasting land-cover environments and the prevailing climatic and topographic gradients across the Alborz Mountains, with forested regions generally experiencing lower fire-weather exposure under their current environmental setting. Spatial analyses reveal persistent and intensifying hotspots concentrated in the western Alborz, alongside a marked west–east gradient in fire-weather evolution. Abrupt shifts detected during the mid-to-late 1990s, particularly around 1996 and 1999, indicate potential transitions in regional fire-weather regimes, although their relationships with large-scale climatic variability require further investigation. As a supplementary analysis, historical fire-weather patterns were statistically extrapolated to 2026–2035, indicating relatively higher frequencies in non-forested summer landscapes. These estimates represent statistical continuation of historical temporal patterns rather than climate projections or deterministic predictions of future wildfire occurrence. Overall, the results highlight pronounced spatial contrasts in climate-driven fire-weather conditions among different land-cover environments. These patterns reflect the combined influence of land-cover distribution, regional climatic gradients, and topographic setting rather than the independent effect of land cover alone.

Article.Title: Creep behavior of lightweight concrete containing fly ash ceramsite aggregate after exposure to high temperatures
Article.Authors: Xiao D.; Chen S.; Wen L.; Dou Y.; Liu H.; Zhao J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To investigate the influence of aggregate types on the long-term deformation performance of concrete after disasters, this paper takes normal-weight aggregate concrete (NWAC) and light weight aggregate concrete (LWAC) as the research objects, and conducts uniaxial step-wise compression creep tests after being subjected to high-temperature treatment ranging from 20 °C to 800 °C. LWAC can maintain a longer steady-state creep period compared to NWAC. SEM confirmed that at high temperatures, the ITZ of NWAC developed tensile cracks of several micrometers, while LWAC maintained a relatively intact structure. Moreover, the fitting degree of the Burgers model for the creep data of LWAC was high ( R 2 = 0.99), verifying the applicability of this model in describing the deceleration and constant-speed creep behavior of LWAC after high-temperature treatment. These results demonstrate that combining short-acquisition measurements with intra-domain spectral averaging through the co-addition of spectra within each classified domain can substantially accelerate spatially resolved ARPES while preserving classification accuracy.

To address this issue, an automatic unloading control system for a corn-field residual-film baling device is developed based on an HZC-H1 load cell. By monitoring film-bale mass, the system determines the unloading timing, alerts the driver to stop the machine, and executes automatic unloading. Mechanical analysis is first carried out to calculate the elastic deformation of the baling belt and thus determine the sensor mounting position, ensuring that the baling belt fully contacts the load-cell sensing surface and that the film-bale weight is transmitted to the sensor in a timely and accurate manner. A Wheatstone full-bridge circuit is then used to convert the applied external force into a voltage signal, and a CYBSQ-12 multi-channel signal amplifier converts the weak electrical signal output by the load cell into an analog signal recognizable by the main controller. Finally, with this analog signal as the control input, an Arduino UNO R3 acts as the main controller to achieve precise start–stop control of the electric push rod, thereby realizing automatic film-bale unloading and driver alerting. Field tests indicate that the relative error between the measured film-bale mass and the preset value is no greater than 4%, demonstrating that the proposed system meets the operational accuracy requirements. This work provides both theoretical support and a practical reference for the intelligent upgrading of residual-film recycling equipment and the standardization of recovered film bales.

Article.Title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa modulates Staphylococcus aureus biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance
Article.Authors: Helal Z.; Elshaer S.; El-Mowafy M.; Habib E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigated how co-existence between bacterial species affect virulence and antimicrobial resistance of each other. The effects of co-culturing with Pseudomonas aeruginosa ( P. aeruginosa ) on Staphylococcus aureus ( S. aureus ) virulence and survival under sub-MIC antibiotic exposure were assessed in vitro using 12 bacterial combinations. These combinations were divided into three groups: standard, co-isolated (from the same patient), and random combinations. The effect of these interactions on pathogenicity was also evaluated using a mouse model. Co-culture significantly enhanced S. aureus survival following exposure to azithromycin (100%), gentamicin (91.7%), cefepime (91.7%) and ciprofloxacin (58.3%). Likewise, biofilm formation and clot lysis activity were significantly enhanced in 83% and 67% mixtures, respectively. Gene expression analysis revealed significant upregulation of icaD and sspA in 100% and 89% of the tested combinations, respectively, compared with mono-culture. Overall, the results demonstrate an interspecies interaction between the two pathogens which increased antimicrobial tolerance and virulence in S. aureus . Consistent with these findings, co-infected mice exhibited higher mortality rates and elevated bacterial counts in lung and liver tissues. Taken together, these findings highlight the effect of polymicrobial interactions in evaluating bacterial pathogenicity and resistance to antimicrobial agents.

Article.Title: Electric wind and fibrous flow development near the active electrode in alternating field electrospinning
Article.Authors: Stanishevsky A.
Article.Abstract: Electric wind generated in AC electric field-enabled electrospinning (or alternating field electrospinning, AFES) of nanofibers is considered a critical parameter of the process but it remains unexplored. In this study, the electric wind in proximity of active electrode (AC-spinneret) in AFES process is investigated using customized cantilevers to detect the x- and y-components of the electric wind force and calculate the electric wind distribution around the spinneret. The cantilever approach is dependable and accurate, and it can be refined to expand the measurement range. Electric wind data were correlated with observations of fibrous flow initiation, development, and propagation in AFES process. The interaction between the time-dependent structure of fibrous flow and electric wind velocity spatial distribution strongly affects the initial stages of fibrous flow development and propagation as well as the overall process efficiency. It is suggested that known AFES processes may utilize only a fraction of available electric wind energy. Future studies are needed on fibrous flow structure analysis and electric wind - fibrous flow interaction in AFES depending on the AC spinneret design and process parameters to advance the AC electric field-enabled electrospinning instrumentation and technology.

Article.Title: Potential zoonotic transmission and environmental factors associated with Blastocystis sp. occurrence in wild roe deer (Capreolus capreolus) from Central Poland
Article.Authors: Korycińska J.; Lepczyńska M.; Kloch M.; Świątek M.; Klich D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Blastocystis is one of the most common protists colonizing the gastrointestinal tract of humans and animals worldwide. The aim of this study was to analyze the occurrence of Blastocystis in wild roe deer ( Capreolus capreolus ) from Central Poland, as well as to determine its zoonotic potential and the influence of selected environmental factors on the infection level. A total of 151 fecal samples were collected and analyzed using PCR amplification followed by DNA sequencing. To identify predictors of Blastocystis occurrence, data on animal characteristics, season, and landscape structure were compiled. Variables were analyzed using a binary generalized linear model with AIC selection. Blastocystis was detected in 49 samples (32.5%). Sequence analysis revealed three subtypes: ST14 (53.1%), ST13 (32.7%), and ST10 (10.2%), while two samples (4.0%) remained classified at the genus level. Roe deer present on wind farms (p = 0.016) and in areas with a higher percentage of settlements (p = 0.035) had a significantly lower probability of colonization. Conversely, the probability of Blastocystis presence increased with a higher proportion of arable land (p = 0.012) and surface water (p = 0.024). Although a zoonotic risk exists, its potential in the studied population appears to be low. The transmission risk may be influenced by factors related to landscape structure and anthropogenic pressure.

Article.Title: The yeast checkpoint kinase Mec1p promotes Nrd1p-Nab3p-Sen1p-mediated transcription termination and attenuation
Article.Authors: Mehta R.; Sadia F.; Reddy S.; Vancurova I.; Vancura A.
Article.Abstract: Transcription cycle of RNA polymerase II (RNAPII) features three stages: initiation, elongation, and termination. Termination, closely linked with RNA 3’ end processing, dissociates RNAPII from DNA and releases the nascent RNA transcript. Efficient termination is required for maintaining a pool of RNAPII that is available for re-entry into new transcription cycle. RNAPII transcription termination of most mRNAs and non-coding RNAs in S. cerevisiae occurs via polyadenylation-dependent and Nrd1p-Nab3p-Sen1p (NNS)-dependent pathways, respectively. Previous results showed that checkpoint kinase Mec1p in the absence of exogenous genotoxic stress promotes transcription termination by the polyadenylation-dependent pathway by facilitating recruitment of termination factor Pcf11p and torpedo exonuclease Rat1p to 3’ ends of genes. We report here that Mec1p is required also for efficient NNS-mediated termination. Mec1p inactivation causes transcription read-through of snoRNAs, downregulates the efficiency of NNS-mediated transcription termination, and enhances growth defect in cells with compromised NNS complex. Mec1p also promotes the NNS-mediated transcription attenuation. However, Mec1p is not required for phosphorylation of the carboxy-terminal domain of the largest RNAPII subunit Rpb1p at Ser5 and for recruitment of Nrd1p to 5’ ends of genes. Together, our data reveal a new role for checkpoint kinase Mec1p in NNS-mediated transcription termination and suggest that during S phase, Mec1p enforces efficient transcription termination of both mRNAs and non-coding RNAs, perhaps to limit transcription-replication conflicts.

Article.Title: ACSS2 phosphorylation at Ser659 attenuates neuronal apoptosis induced by cerebral ischemia-reperfusion by initiating autophagy
Article.Authors: Hadierbieke A.; Buerlike A.; Xia H.
Article.Abstract: Acetyl-CoA synthetase 2 (ACSS2), as a key enzyme regulating the synthesis of acetyl-CoA, has been proven to be involved in various metabolic and epigenetic regulatory processes. However, the specific mechanisms by which ACSS2 functions in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (CI/R) injury have not yet been fully elucidated. The middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model was established in C57BL/6 mice, and an in vitro model was generated using oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R). The dynamic expression of ACSS2 mRNA and protein was assessed by RT-qPCR and Western blot, respectively. The subcellular localization of ACSS2 was analyzed by immunofluorescence staining and Western blot. TTC staining and TUNEL/NeuN double immunofluorescence were applied to assess cerebral infarct size and neuronal apoptosis, respectively. To investigate the biological functions of ACSS2 and its Ser659 phosphorylation, we adopted pharmacological interventions with the ACSS2 inhibitor AD-8007 and the AMPK inhibitor Compound C, as well as the overexpression of wild-type ACSS2 (ACSS2-WT) and its Ser659 phosphorylation-deficient mutant (ACSS2-Mut). In the MCAO model, CI/R injury markedly upregulated ACSS2 expression and induced robust phosphorylation of ACSS2 at the Ser659 site. Subcellular localization analysis revealed that ischemic stress drove prominent nuclear translocation of total ACSS2 and p-ACSS2. Pharmacological suppression of ACSS2 activity by AD-8007, or blockade of Ser659 phosphorylation by Compound C, obviously restrained I/R-triggered autophagy, accompanied by impaired LC3-II conversion and inhibited p62 degradation. This suppression further aggravated neuronal apoptosis and enlarged cerebral infarct volume. Consistent with in vivo findings, in vitro neuronal OGD/R challenge rapidly elevated ACSS2 Ser659 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation, and enhanced nuclear acetyl-CoA production, which subsequently increased H3K27 acetylation at the LC3B promoter. Functional validation demonstrated that ACSS2-WT effectively activated autophagy and alleviated neuronal apoptosis under OGD/R, while the ACSS2-Mut lost such protective capacity. Moreover, Compound C administration abolished OGD/R-elicited ACSS2 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation, thereby repressing autophagic activation and worsening neuronal damage. ACSS2 confers neuroprotection against cerebral ischemia via Ser659 phosphorylation and subsequent nuclear translocation, which further activates autophagy-related gene expression. In contrast, blockade of ACSS2 activity or its phosphorylation compromises protective autophagy and exacerbates ischemic brain damage. ACSS2 Ser659 phosphorylation is therefore essential for modulating autophagic activity in ischemic neurons, and targeting ACSS2 may provide a promising therapeutic approach for ischemic brain injury.

Article.Title: Tourism urbanization and landscape fragmentation in Taiwan’s Yilan Plain: an integrated analysis of intensity and landscape metrics
Article.Authors: Chiu H.; Chen Y.
Article.Abstract: Tourism urbanization prioritizes tourism consumption over traditional residential-focused development, reshaping land use patterns in destination areas. This research examines how tourism urbanization is associated with agricultural landscape change in Taiwan’s Yilan Plain from 1995 to 2020. Using intensity analysis and moving-window landscape metrics, results show that the agricultural landscape in Yilan underwent substantial change over the study period. Hotel land expanded from 0.8 to 5.9 km 2 between 1995 and 2020, with the highest interval change rate (177%) occurring in 1995–2006, partly reflecting growth from a very small base. Meanwhile, farmland decreased 14.5%, primarily converting to built-up areas. Intensity analysis identified accelerated change during 1995–2006 and 2015–2020, while hotels showed the highest gain intensity in every interval despite their small area. Landscape fragmentation intensified, with patch density increasing 57% while the aggregation index declined 9%, indicating a less clustered landscape. Moving-window and transect analyses revealed spatial heterogeneity in this change, with the landscape becoming more aggregated around urban peripheries but more fragmented across the outer plain. Land use planning should prioritize agricultural landscape integrity and minimize fragmented development patterns to balance tourism growth with environmental sustainability.

Article.Title: Self-heating effect analysis of a dual cavity AlGaN/GaN MOS-HEMT biosensor with AlN/diamond substrate
Article.Authors: Prasanna R.; Kiran T.; Vijaya P.; Chandrika G.; Bolisetty V.; Sreenivasulu V.; Kondavitee G.; Karumuri S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this paper, we have designed and analysed the dual cavity AlGaN/GaN Metal oxide semiconductor high electron mobility transistor (MOS-HEMT) heterojunction biosensor for biomolecule detection. The proposed biosensor uses triple-metal work functions (M 1 , M 2 and M 3 ) to improve electric field distribution and electrostatic control. The proposed biosensor is evaluated using MCF-10 A (K = 4.5), Keratin(K = 8), Gelatin (K = 12), Hs578T (K = 22), MCF-7 (K = 27.5) and T47D (K = 32) biomolecules using Atlas Silvaco TCAD. The temperature dependent behaviour is examined at different temperatures (250 K, 300 K, 350 K and 400 K) to evaluate its electrical stability and sensing performance. In addition, Self-Heating Effect (SHE) is analysed using Sapphire and Diamonds substrate configurations. Self-heating increases the lattice temperature, leading to enhanced carrier scattering and reduced 2DEG mobility that can affect the electrical and sensing performance. A Diamond substrate AlN/Diamond substrate is used to improve heat dissipation and supress self-heating. The proposed device analyses the lattice temperature, DIBL, drain-current sensitivity and subthreshold swing (SS) sensitivity for different biomolecule effective dielectric constant. The Diamond substrate reduces the lattice temperature from 422 K to 324 K and increases the drain current sensitivity from 5.392 × 10 1 to 9.99 × 10 1 at K = 32. These results demonstrated that the proposed AlN/Diamond substrate device provides improved thermal management and sensing performance, making it suitable for biomedical applications.

Article.Title: Serum relaxin and beta hCG levels in pregnant women with prior recurrent pregnancy loss and composite adverse pregnancy outcomes
Article.Authors: Eleje G.; Ugwu E.; Onah C.; Igbodike E.; Malachy D.; Nwankwo E.; Ugboaja J.; Ikechebelu J.; Onwuegbuna A.; Egbuniwe M.; Edokwe E.; Egwim U.; Umeononihu O.; Ekwuazi K.; Ogelle O.; Okafor C.; Nweze S.; Ezenwaeze M.; Odugu B.; Ortuanya K.; Onah N.; Ezeora N.; Ofojebe C.; Ezeigwe C.; Enechukwu C.
Article.Abstract: To analyse maternal serum relaxin and β-hCG in pregnant women with a history of recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) and compare them with a healthy control group without a history RPL. A prospective cohort study was conducted among pregnant women with prior RPL ( n = 47) and healthy controls ( n = 94). Serum relaxin and β-hCG concentrations were measured between 8 and 20 weeks of gestation. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were generated across the entire study population followed up till birth ( n = 136, combining RPL and control groups) to evaluate the predictive performance of relaxin and beta-hCG for composite adverse pregnancy outcomes. Multivariable binary logistic regression was performed to adjust for potential confounding variables. Mean levels of relaxin and β-hCG were significantly lower in the RPL group (95.28 ± 24.90pg/mL and 425.24 ± 147.57mIU/mL) than in controls (111.61 ± 41.43pg/mL and 542.26 ± 97.97mIU/mL, respectively; p < 0.001). Across all participants, a serum relaxin cutoff < 109.14pg/Ml was a statistically significant predictor of composite adverse pregnancy outcomes (AUC = 0.63; sensitivity = 72.00%; specificity = 55.00%; p = 0.01). Conversely, β-hCG < 540.48mIU/mL was not predictive (AUC = 0.55; sensitivity = 59.00%; specificity = 58.00%; p = 0.30). In multivariable logistic regression, repeat miscarriage (aOR = 31.01, p < 0.01) and caesarean birth (aOR = 3.92, p = 0.01) remained significantly associated with prior RPL after adjusting for maternal age, BMI, gestational age at sampling, and socioeconomic status. Although maternal serum relaxin levels are significantly lower in women with prior RPL, their predictive performance across the general cohort is modest (AUC = 0.63). Relaxin represents a potential candidate biomarker that warrants validation in larger, longitudinal cohorts.

Article.Title: System dynamics evidence of sub-additive carbon reduction from combined mitigation strategies in multi-echelon logistics networks
Article.Authors: Chen Y.; Li L.; Pang Y.; Gu G.; Huang W.
Article.Abstract: The transition of multi-echelon logistics networks toward carbon neutrality is constrained by the inability of traditional static models to capture complex emission dynamics and time-delayed effects. To bridge this critical gap, this study develops a comprehensive system dynamics framework that captures non-linear feedback mechanisms, nonlinear interactions and temporal delays across transportation, inventory, and ware-housing operations. By simulating multiple mitigation strategies on a stylized regional distribution network, the analysis reveals strongly asymmetric temporal patterns: annual emissions in the base scenario rise from 2,736 to 3,453 t CO 2 e over five years, an increase of 26.2%. Transportation mode optimization delivers a 21.3% reduction with a 9.8% saving in five-year total cost, network reconfiguration a 22.4% reduction with a 6.5% saving, and technology upgrading a 25.9% reduction at an 8.4% cost increase. Combining all three yields a 47.5% reduction while lowering cumulative expenditure by 9.8%, so the deepest reduction is obtained together with a net cost saving rather than in exchange for one. The combined effect is markedly sub-additive, since the three single strategies sum to 69.6% points against a simulated 47.5. The emission response to modal shift is near-linear in the shifted volume over the range a programme can plausibly reach, and a shift of 57.6% of road line-haul tonne-kilometres is required merely to hold year-five emissions at the base-year level. Theoretically, these findings challenge prevailing static optimization paradigms by reframing logistics networks as complex adaptive systems. Practically, the study provides a transparent and reproducible simulation framework with which logistics managers can examine the sequencing and interaction of decarbonization measures before committing capital.

Article.Title: Quantifying external root resorption associated with various orthodontic tooth movements in clear aligner treatment: a retrospective clinical study
Article.Authors: Kurnaz S.; Buyukcavus M.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated associations between tooth movements and external root resorption (ERR) during clear aligner (CA) orthodontic treatment (OT). Forty-eight patients who underwent non-extraction OT using ClearCorrect aligners were included. Maxillary and mandibular incisors and canines were assessed, comprising 576 teeth. Pre- and post-OT digital models were superimposed to quantify intrusion, extrusion, crown tipping, crown torque, rotation, buccolingual translation, and mesiodistal translation. Root length, projected root surface area (PRSA), and ERR were measured on pre- and post-OT panoramic radiographs. Associations between tooth movements and root length, PRSA, and ERR were evaluated using correlation and multivariable linear regression analyses, with correction for multiple comparisons where appropriate. Significant movement-specific associations were observed in the maxillary lateral incisors and canines, with crown torque associated with root length and ERR changes and crown tipping associated with ERR in the lateral incisors, while extrusion was associated with PRSA changes in the canines. No significant movement–resorption associations were observed in the mandibular teeth. The magnitude of the observed resorptive changes was generally limited. Overall, the findings suggest that root responses during CA treatment may vary according to both the type of tooth movement and tooth group; however, the observed movement-specific associations should be interpreted cautiously.

Article.Title: A reconfigurable architecture for CNN acceleration using line buffers
Article.Authors: Sarnala B.; Pillutla S.
Article.Abstract: Computer vision (CV) is experiencing a rapid increase in real-time applications driven by neural network (NN) processing. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are the core architecture of advanced CV applications based on artificial intelligence (AI) for autonomous driving, facial recognition, object detection, and information decryption. However, huge computational complexity and continuous memory bandwidth requirements restrict the efficient hardware implementation of CNNs on FPGA platforms. In this paper proposes a reconfigurable systolic CNN architecture using line buffers for enhancing the resource utilization and reducing delay. The proposed architecture dynamically reconfigured to CNN layer requirements, and line buffers improve the data reuse and reduce redundant memory access. In addition, reconfigurable adder and pooling structures are designed to increase the flexibility of accumulation and down sampling operations, supporting various kernel sizes and layers in CNNs. The proposed reconfigurable architecture is hardware-efficient through control signals and adapts to all CNN layers. FPGA implementation of this proposed reconfigurable architecture is performed using LeNet CNN architecture layers. This flexible and low-cost reconfigurable systolic CNN architecture achieves a 15.25% reduction in LUTs utilization, 75% improvement in throughput, and 2.44% reduction in computational delay in LeNet CNN. The implemented LeNet CNN using proposed reconfigurable architecture is suitable for high performance and hardware efficient CNN applications.

Article.Title: Robust federated learning for detecting false data injection attacks in advanced metering infrastructure under non-IID data
Article.Authors: Wei Y.; Gong G.; Cao L.
Article.Abstract: Advanced metering infrastructure exposes fine-grained residential consumption to false data injection attacks that tamper with meter readings while evading conventional bad-data screening. Federated learning keeps raw measurements on the device, yet real smart-meter populations are naturally non-independent and identically distributed and the distributed training loop is open to malicious clients that poison model updates. This study proposes a dual-robust federated detection framework that couples a lightweight two-branch gated recurrent detector with a server-side aggregation pipeline built from exponential moving average smoothing, client-level trimmed filtering, and deviation-aware cosine weighting. Real non-IID scenarios are constructed from the public Low Carbon London dataset by ACORN group, and generalization is checked on the Spanish GoiEner dataset across a different region and period. Under a strict fixed false-positive operating point the framework holds balanced accuracy near 61% from zero to thirty% malicious clients, whereas standard federated baselines collapse toward chance, confirming the value of client-level robust aggregation for edge-deployable attack detection.
