Article.Title: Optimized deep learning based digital twin architecture for system management in heterogeneous IoT system
Article.Authors: Jebasingh G.; Amsaprabhaa M.
Article.Abstract: The rapid explosion of heterogeneous Internet of Things (IoT) deployments has introduced significant challenges in network traffic, device reliability, energy efficiency and Quality of Service (QoS) management due to the diversity of devices, communication protocols and application requirements. The existing methods of network management methods are gateway-centric and rule-based approaches that lacks in the intelligence for dynamic and large-scale environments. To address the challenges, this research introduced Digital Twin (DT) based intelligent gateway system for heterogeneous IoT networks, which is the synchronized virtual replica of the physical IoT environment for continuous maintained and analysis of networks. In the proposed DT framework, deep learning–based decision-making based on Cross-Stage Gated Transformer Network (CSG-TNet) is proposed to enable proactive system management. Here, the loss function associated with the CSG-TNet is supplemented by using the proposed Chaotic Blood sucking Leach Optimizer (CBSL) algorithm. The DT model aggregates and harmonizes heterogeneous IoT data related to network traffic, device health, energy consumption and service performance that allows the CSG-TNet to learn complex spatio-temporal correlations across multiple system dimensions. The experimental evaluation demonstrates that the proposed DT–enabled gateway significantly improves network efficiency, reliability and service quality for next-generation heterogeneous IoT systems.

Article.Title: A hybrid ANN-metaheuristic framework for vibration-based identification of orthotropic parameters in GFRP laminated plates
Article.Authors: Adimass S.; Żak A.; Doliński Ł.
Article.Abstract: Glass-fibre-reinforced polymer (GFRP) composite plates are widely used in engineering structures, yet their numerical modelling is challenging because their material properties can vary due to anisotropy, manufacturing variability, and uncertainty in input parameters. This study develops a fast numerical framework for vibration-based finite element model updating and inverse identification of orthotropic material properties in GFRP composite plates using analytical modal reference data. A baseline finite element model was developed in Abaqus and compared with modal results obtained using Classical laminate plate theory. To reduce the high computational cost of repeated finite element simulations during model updating, an artificial neural network (ANN) surrogate model was trained on parametric FE data and coupled with genetic algorithm (GA), particle swarm optimisation (PSO), and slime mould algorithm (SMA) optimisation methods. The novelty of the study lies in comparing these ANN-assisted optimisation frameworks with direct GA-Abaqus-Python updating under the same modal identification problems. Pearson correlation-based sensitivity analysis showed that the longitudinal elastic modulus E x was the dominant parameter affecting the modal response, with sensitivity values ranging from approximately 0.62 to 0.80. In the representative updated model, ANN-SMA achieved the lowest average frequency-prediction error of 2.289%, compared with 3.821% for the conventional GA-Abaqus-Python updated model. However, statistical analysis over 50 independent runs showed that ANN-PSO provided the best robustness, with the lowest mean frequency error, smallest standard deviation, and lower runtime than ANN-SMA. The ANN-assisted methods reduced the computational time from approximately 5.830 h to 6.617–42.409 s. These results show that ANN-assisted model updating provides an efficient numerical approach for vibration-based material-property identification in composite structures.

Article.Authors: Putri I.; Kusumiyati K.; Hadiwijaya Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Quality control in cayenne pepper fruit is important for maintaining product consistency. The research aimed to evaluate lycopene content and antioxidant capacity as the main indicators of cayenne pepper quality. Visible-near infrared (Vis-NIR) spectroscopy is an emerging technology that can predict lycopene content and antioxidant capacity non-destructively, accurately, and quickly. Spectral data (381–1065 nm) were analyzed using support vector machine regression to develop the calibration model. Reference data on lycopene and antioxidant capacity were determined using spectrophotometry method. The results displayed a robust association between spectra and reference data. The calibration model for lycopene content and antioxidant capacity generated sufficient performance in terms of accuracy. For both parameters, the models showed correlation coefficient ( R ) ≥ 0.85, root mean square error of calibration (RMSEC) ≥ 17.61, root mean square error of cross validation (RMSECV) ≥ 42.01, and ratio of prediction to deviation (RPD) ≥ 1.95. Based on these results, it further strengthens that Vis-NIR technology was able to non-destructively assess lycopene content and antioxidant capacity. In the food and postharvest industries, the developed method shows promise for fast quality screening, automated grading, and real-time monitoring. Additionally, Vis-NIR spectroscopy’s rapidity and non-destructive nature make it scalable for industrial uses, especially in precision agriculture and contemporary quality control systems. These findings support the potential of non-destructive technology as an alternative for the quality control system of cayenne pepper quality in the agricultural and food industries.

Article.Title: Differences in self-stigma and help-seeking among individuals reporting a history of childhood maltreatment: a multi-country study
Article.Authors: Haim-Nachum S.; Pfaltz M.; Jansson B.; Fisch C.; Ayas G.; Şar V.; Lazarov A.; Balle S.; Jenkins D.; Sela Y.; Ahmed F.; Seedat S.; Schnyder U.; Oe M.; Amsalem D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Self-stigma is a significant barrier to help-seeking among survivors of childhood maltreatment (CM). Although context, including cultural context, shapes the way stigma-related beliefs are experienced and translated into help-seeking intentions, most evidence derives from Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic (WEIRD) countries/cultures. This multi-national study examined cross-national differences in self-stigma dimensions and help-seeking intentions among CM survivors spanning both WEIRD (United States, Sweden, Switzerland) and non-WEIRD (Japan, South Africa, Türkiye) countries. Young adults with a retrospectively self-reported history of CM ( N = 2,691) completed online self-report measures assessing self-stigma dimensions (alienation, stereotype endorsement, secrecy, and perceived recovery) and help-seeking intentions. Group (WEIRD vs. non-WEIRD) differences were examined using ANCOVAs controlling for age, gender, education, subjective social status, and extent of CM exposure. Pearson correlations assessed associations among stigma-related constructs and help-seeking intentions at both group (regional; WEIRD vs. non-WEIRD) and country levels. Participants from non-WEIRD countries reported lower alienation alongside higher secrecy, perceived recovery, and help-seeking intentions compared to participants from WEIRD countries. Stereotype endorsement did not differ between groups. Correlational patterns among stigma-related constructs were broadly similar across contexts, but associations were descriptively stronger and more interlinked in WEIRD countries. Country-level analyses revealed substantial mean-level variation across countries. Self-stigma-related patterns among CM survivors varied descriptively across countries, with differing configurations of stigma-related dimensions observed across contexts. These findings underscore the importance of moving beyond WEIRD-centric models and support culturally sensitive approaches to stigma reduction and help-seeking promotion.

Article.Title: Single-cell transcriptomics-based analysis of cellular heterogeneity in aggrephagy in gastric cancer and development of a prognostic model
Article.Authors: Wan T.; Yang P.; Xu Y.; Shu P.
Article.Abstract: Aggrephagy maintains protein homeostasis through selective autophagy, but its cellular heterogeneity and immune associations in gastric cancer (GC) remain unclear. We integrated GC single-cell RNA sequencing data with TCGA and GEO transcriptomic cohorts to identify aggrephagy-associated genes and develop a prognostic signature. Analyses included immune infiltration, somatic mutations, predicted drug sensitivity, pseudotime trajectories, and virtual gene knockout. Expression of VIM, TUBA1A, and CST3 was examined using quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) in GC cell lines and Human Protein Atlas immunohistochemical data. Aggrephagy-associated AUCell score distributions varied across the seven major cell types, with overlaps. The VIM–TUBA1A–CST3 signature showed moderate prognostic discrimination in public transcriptomic cohorts and was associated with immunosuppressive microenvironment features, immune checkpoint expression, and predicted drug sensitivity. Virtual VIM knockout predicted network perturbations involving macrophage antigen-presentation and lysosomal pathways, suggesting potential links to the GC immune microenvironment rather than established causal regulation. These findings characterize aggrephagy-associated cellular heterogeneity and provide a basis for further investigation of prognostic stratification and immune-associated mechanisms in GC.

Article.Title: A novel ISSA-GRNN approach for efficient camphor extraction from Artemisia argyi
Article.Authors: Ji P.; Wang D.; Li R.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Efficient extraction of bioactive compounds from plant matrices is essential for pharmaceutical, functional food, and agricultural applications. However, process optimization is often challenged by nonlinear interactions among multiple parameters and limited experimental data. This work presents an optimization framework that combines an improved sparrow search algorithm (ISSA) with a generalized regression neural network (GRNN) to model camphor extraction from Artemisia argyi leaves. The ISSA incorporates three modifications: hybrid chaotic-opposition population initialization, a dual-adaptive discoverer update rule, and a stagnation-triggered hybrid mutation operator. The GRNN leverages its small-sample tolerance to establish a nonlinear relationship between five extraction parameters and camphor yield using 50 experimental runs. Under 5-fold cross-validation, ISSA-GRNN outperformed PSO, GA, and SSA-optimized GRNN models, achieving an R² of 0.931, RMSE of 0.0140, and MAPE of 4.65%. Experimental validation under optimized conditions (58 °C, 0.7% cellulase, 3.8 h hydrolysis, pH 6.0, 32 min ultrasonication) produced a camphor yield of 0.2368 mg/g, an 11.5% increase over RSM, with an RSD of 1.05% (3.74% for RSM). The findings of this study contribute to a better understanding of small-sample nonlinear process modeling and provide a practical framework for bioactive compound extraction under data-scarce conditions, readily extendable to other plant matrices and data-limited regression problems.

Article.Title: The prediction model of social alienation trajectory in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis patients based on social ecosystem theory: a prospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Huang L.; Zang J.; Chen Z.; Li J.; Ren Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Social alienation can adversely affect the psychological well-being, social functioning, and longer-term adjustment of adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis (AIS). However, longitudinal patterns of social alienation after diagnosis and prediction frameworks integrating multilevel factors remain insufficiently studied. This study aimed to identify distinct social alienation trajectories during the first year after AIS diagnosis and to develop a prediction model for trajectory-group membership. In this single-centre prospective cohort study, 276 patients with AIS completed assessments at diagnosis and at 3, 6, and 12 months. Growth mixture modelling (GMM) was used to identify social alienation trajectories. Trajectory classes were subsequently grouped to define a binary outcome for prediction modelling. Candidate predictors underwent univariable screening followed by forward likelihood-ratio logistic regression. Internal validation was performed using 1000 bootstrap resamples, with the selected predictor set held fixed and the regression coefficients re-estimated in each resample. Three trajectories were identified: lower-score increasing ( n = 144), moderate-score increasing ( n = 91), and persistently higher-score ( n = 41). The latter two classes were combined as the elevated-score trajectory group ( n = 132), with the lower-score increasing class as the reference. The final model retained seven predictors: age > 12 years (OR = 6.461; 95% CI, 2.019–20.678), presence of comorbid health conditions (OR = 8.535; 95% CI, 1.803–40.394), positive self-esteem (OR = 0.876; 95% CI, 0.771–0.995), negative self-esteem (OR = 1.243; 95% CI, 1.117–1.383), intra-family support (OR = 0.829; 95% CI, 0.747–0.920), extra-family support (OR = 0.891; 95% CI, 0.826–0.962), and economic discrimination (OR = 2.003; 95% CI, 1.420–2.824). The apparent AUC was 0.913 (95% CI, 0.878–0.948). Fixed-predictor-set bootstrap correction yielded an AUC of 0.902, a Brier score of 0.124, a calibration intercept of − 0.004, and a calibration slope of 0.907. Participants with AIS followed heterogeneous social alienation trajectories during the first year after diagnosis. The model with seven predictors showed promising performance after bootstrap correction and may inform further research on psychosocial risk assessment. However, predictor selection was not repeated during bootstrap validation, and independent external validation is required before routine clinical use.

Article.Title: Nonlinear distortion compensation for high-speed ADC using a diffusion model
Article.Authors: Yan H.; Qian X.
Article.Abstract: To address the amplitude/phase distortion and intermodulation distortion caused by nonlinearity of the sampling switch and front-end amplifier, clock jitter, and frequency coupling in high-speed ADCs (Analog to Digital Converters), this paper proposes a conditional Diffusion framework based on physical constraints for nonlinear distortion compensation in high-speed ADCs. The study uses a one-dimensional time series Temporal-UNet as the denoising backbone and fuses the calibrated hardware parameter vector with jitter spectrum estimation through a conditional encoder. FiLM is used to inject conditional information into the residual block to guide progressive inverse diffusion. Then, in each step of the inverse process, a data consistency projection based on a memory polynomial physical forward model is embedded. The Gauss-Newton approximation solution is used, combined with STFT (Short Time Fourier Transform)-L1 and spectral convergence term to constrain the network output to suppress intermodulation and phase distortion. Finally, in the deployment link, low-latency engineering implementation is achieved through methods such as few-step deterministic sampling, progressive distillation, model pruning, and quantization. Parallel multi-sample uncertainty estimation and lightweight online fine-tuning ensure domain adaptability and reliability. A comprehensive evaluation based on a hybrid simulation and experimental dataset — comprising single-tone sweep, two-tone intermodulation, multi-tone, and modulation signal scenarios over an input frequency range of 10 MHz to 450 MHz and a normalized input amplitude range of 0.1 to 1.0 full scale, with an uncompensated baseline ENOB of 4.37 bits at full-scale high-frequency input — shows that the proposed method achieves suppression of THD (Total Harmonic Distortion) and IMD (Intermodulation Distortion) of approximately 73.04% and 78.15% respectively in the high-frequency band above 300 MHz. The ENOB (Effective Number of Bits) increased by 3.21 ± 0.16 bits, the SNDR (Signal-to-Noise and Distortion Ratio) increased by 11.07 ± 0.76 dB, and the SFDR (Spurious Free Dynamic Range) increased by 9.57 ± 0.99 dB. Experimental results demonstrate that this method can achieve high-fidelity signal reconstruction in different frequency bands and under complex operating conditions, providing a reliable technical solution for accurate measurement and communication link optimization in high-speed ADC systems.

Article.Title: Oxidative stress contributes to persistent pain and central sensitization in a repeated PGE2-induced hyperalgesic priming model
Article.Authors: Arai Y.; Koyama Y.; Kobayashi Y.; Takahashi A.; Kobayashi H.; Yoshida T.; Shimada S.
Article.Abstract: Chronic pain is a global health concern that impairs physical and psychological well-being. Recently, nociplastic pain, characterized by the absence of overt inflammation or nerve injury, has gained attention as a distinct chronic pain condition. Central sensitization is considered a primary mechanism underlying nociplastic pain and the persistence of chronic pain states. Emerging evidence suggests that oxidative stress contributes to central sensitization, through increased neuronal excitability and glial activation; however, its role in nociplastic pain remains unclear. In this study, we investigated the involvement of oxidative stress in a prostaglandin E2 (PGE2)-induced hyperalgesic priming mouse model with features resembling nociplastic pain. Additionally, we examined the effects of modulating oxidative stress on pain progression using a silicon (Si)-based antioxidant agent. Repeated PGE2 administration induced mechanical allodynia and increased circulating reactive oxygen metabolites (d-ROMs), effects that were attenuated in mice treated with the Si-based agent. In the spinal dorsal horn, neuronal activity and astrocyte activation increased in the chronic pain model but not in mice treated with the Si-based agent. These findings support an association between systemic oxidative stress and spinal sensitization in this repeated PGE2-induced hyperalgesic priming model and provide insight into mechanisms underlying persistent pain that may share features with nociplastic pain.

Article.Title: Germline missense variants in FBXW11 differentially affect its subcellular localization and protein interactome
Article.Authors: Tibbe D.; Volbracht R.; Biabani A.; Siebels B.; Schneeberger P.; Alawi M.; Shenoy R.; Shetty V.; Girisha K.; Kutsche K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The neurodevelopmental, jaw, eye, and digital syndrome shows high clinical variability and is caused by heterozygous FBXW11 missense variants. FBXW11 encodes an F-box protein containing a WD40 domain that forms a seven-bladed β-propeller. FBXW11 is part of the SKP1-CUL1-F-box (SCF) E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, which mediates the ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of numerous substrates, thereby regulating diverse cellular processes and pathways. Here, we report a de novo FBXW11 missense variant, NM_033644.3:c.1100 C > T; p.(Ser367Phe), in an infant with developmental delay and severe skeletal phenotype characterized by multisuture craniosynostosis with turricephaly and postaxial polysyndactyly. We studied the functional consequences of the reported FBXW11 variants p.(Gly229Arg), p.(Arg350Trp), and p.(Glu431Lys), as well as p.(Ser367Phe), all located within the WD40 substrate-binding domain, by ectopic expression of HA-tagged wild-type and variant FBXW11 β-isoforms. Subcellular localization studies revealed FBXW11 WT mainly in the nucleus. HA-FBXW11 E431K showed either nuclear or nucleo-cytoplasmic distribution, whereas FBXW11 G229R and FBXW11 S367F were excluded from the nucleus. Using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry and independent co-immunoprecipitations, we identified variant-specific and shared alterations in FBXW11 interaction networks. Decreased complex formation with the SCF components was observed for FBXW11 G229R . Both FBXW11 G229R and FBXW11 S367F showed reduced binding to the nuclear substrate SUN2. Enriched complex formation of FBXW11 G229R and FBXW11 S367F with the chaperonin-containing TCP-1 (CCT) subunits suggests that both FBXW11 protein variants are trapped by CCT, potentially delaying or arresting folding of FBXW11’s β-propeller. Together, our data show that FBXW11 missense variants differentially affect binding to specific substrates and/or interaction partners, providing a molecular explanation for the clinical variability.

Article.Title: Optimizing hypertrophic strength training: electromyographic effects of forearm position on biceps brachii activity
Article.Authors: Pakosz P.; Konieczny M.; Domaszewski P.
Article.Abstract: This study examined the acute effect of three forearm positions (supination, neutral, and pronation) on biceps brachii sEMG amplitude during a standardized hypertrophy-oriented resistance exercise. While the optimal forearm position for maximizing muscle engagement in dumbbell exercises remains debated, this research utilizes surface electromyography (sEMG) to provide practical insights for coaches, athletes, and rehabilitation specialists. Fifty-six right-handed male participants with strength training experience performed elbow flexion exercises with dumbbells while biceps brachii activity was recorded using surface electrodes. Two predefined sequences with reversed order were used to reduce potential order and fatigue effects. sEMG analysis revealed significant differences in biceps brachii activation across forearm positions. In pronation, right-arm EMG activity averaged 215 µV, increasing by 106 µV in neutral and an additional 100 µV in supination. On the left side, pronation resulted in 249 µV, rising by 188 µV in neutral and 93 µV in supination. Cohen’s dz effect sizes indicated moderate-to-large differences in recorded sEMG amplitude between forearm positions. Forearm rotation significantly affected biceps brachii sEMG amplitude, with the highest values observed during supination and the lowest during pronation. These findings suggest that forearm position may be an important factor to consider when selecting dumbbell exercises aimed at increasing biceps brachii muscle activity. Future research should explore additional muscle groups and exercise variations to refine training strategies and enhance performance outcomes.

Article.Title: Safety and efficacy of lacnotuzumab, a colony-stimulating factor 1 antibody for the treatment of tenosynovial giant cell tumors: a randomized phase II trial
Article.Authors: Cheng E.; Schramm U.; Mirzaei A.; Saxer F.; Laurent D.; Lowcock R.; Peters T.; Valentin M.; Wiesmann M.; Pinot P.; Praestgaard J.; Zou H.; Abraham J.; Block J.; Batus M.; Gitelis S.; Henshaw R.; Wilky B.; Krieg A.; Khachatrian A.; Trent J.; Correa H.; Beckmann E.; Roubenoff R.; Schieker M.
Article.Abstract: Tenosynovial giant cell tumors (TGCT) are locally aggressive tumors that are often difficult to treat surgically due to their size and diffuse growth. Systemic therapies targeting the colony-stimulating factor-1 (CSF-1) pathway have emerged as alternatives. This study assessed the safety and efficacy of lacnotuzumab, a monoclonal antibody against CSF-1. This prospective, placebo-controlled, double-blind phase II study had three parts introduced sequentially: Part A: 7 participants received a single dose of lacnotuzumab (10 mg/kg) or placebo. Part B: 11 participants received 10 mg/kg lacnotuzumab or placebo for the first dose, followed by up to six monthly open-label doses (10 mg/kg). Part C: 18 participants were randomized to 3, 5, or 10 mg/kg lacnotuzumab for the first three doses, with possible escalation based on tumor response. Tumor volume was assessed by MRI every 4 weeks. Safety was monitored via laboratory assessments and adverse event (AE) reporting. The most frequent treatment-emergent AEs were periorbital/facial swelling (64%) and peripheral swelling (22%), mostly mild and self-limiting. Four weeks after a single dose, median tumor volume reductions were − 8.6% (3 mg/kg), -17.7% (5 mg/kg), and − 33.3% (10 mg/kg), versus − 10.1% for placebo. Eight weeks after the last dose, reductions were − 29.7% (3 mg/kg), -56% (5 mg/kg), and − 55.7% (10 mg/kg). Dose escalation further reduced tumor volume. Lacnotuzumab reduced TGCT volume, especially with multiple and higher doses. Edema was the most frequent AE but was self-limiting. While not curative in most cases, lacnotuzumab could be explored as neoadjuvant option to reduce tumor volume. Clinical trial number : ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT01643850.

Article.Title: A privacy-preserving adaptive pricing and coordination framework for decentralized prosumer energy systems with demand response and EV/V2G-inspired flexibility
Article.Authors: Bhavana G.; Mainali A.; Adhikari R.; Anand R.; Ramprabhakar J.; Padmanaban S.
Article.Abstract: Distributed energy resources (DERs), electric vehicles (EVs), and the involvement of prosumers are turning distribution-level energy systems into decentralized, flexibility-driven markets. However, these systems are hindered by interrelated issues such as stochastic supply–demand mismatch, DR rebound, EV/V2G availability constraints, coordination effects (represented through a coalition proxy), network stress, and privacy-preserving settlement. These components tend to be studied separately in existing research, and their combined operational and settlement-level trade-offs have not been assessed. In this paper, a simulation-grade Adaptive Pricing and Coordination (APC) framework for decentralized prosumer energy trading called Zenergy is presented. The framework combines price-responsive DR with curtailment and shifting/rebound; EV/V2G-inspired flexibility with availability and travel-energy constraint, required departure SOC, willingness, and degradation-cost constraint; locality and matching effect represented by a coalition proxy; simplified network-stress proxies; and ZK-aware settlement overhead modelling. To separate out the contribution of each of these components, a conventional double-auction benchmark, transparent No ZK settlement case, centralized coordination proxy, ablation scenarios, sensitivity analysis, and scalability sweep are provided. Monte Carlo simulation experiments (500 prosumers, 1440 time steps) reveal that DR is the primary factor to improve adequacy (by 11.62% compared to the fixed-tariff case), while EV/storage and coordination proxy boost the adequacy improvement to 12.64%. The no-network case for full APC-ZK achieves a 12.68% reduction, while the case with the network-stress proxy enabled for APC-ZK has a smaller reduction of 2.04% because the proxy activates modeled curtailment. Compared with transparent settlement, the metadata-leakage proxy is reduced by roughly 49.85% with ZK settlement, and latency is increased from 1.8228 s to 2.0921 s, and gas cost from 0.0003 to 0.0006. The results show that Zenergy can be used to assess the trade-offs between the adaptive pricing, DR, EV/V2G flexibility, coalition locality proxy, network-stress proxies and privacy-aware settlement.

Article.Title: The relationship between the quality of the shared decision-making process and hope in patients with multiple sclerosis: an analytical cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Nikboresh R.; Mohamadi M.; Dadkhah B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Background Multiple sclerosis (MS) profoundly impacts patients’ psychological and social well-being. This study investigated the relationship between the quality of the shared decision-making (SDM) process and hope among patients with MS in northwest Iran. Method This correlational study selected 300 patients with MS covered by the Ardabil MS Association via stratified random sampling. Data were collected using a sociodemographic questionnaire, the AGA-25 scale, and Snyder’s Adult Hope Scale. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent t-tests, analysis of variance, and a linear regression model in SPSS 26. Results In this analytical cross-sectional study of 300 patients with multiple sclerosis (mean age = 32.20 ± 10.20 years; 66.3% women), most participants had a relapsing–remitting disease course (76%) and a moderate level of both hope (mean = 38.97 ± 6.33) and shared decision-making (SDM) quality (mean = 75.0 ± 9.72). The mean scores of hope and its subscales were significantly below the established criteria (p < 0.01), while the SDM total score exceeded its criterion (p < 0.01). The quality of SDM was significantly associated with patients’ education, occupation, age, number of children, and disease duration (p < 0.05). A positive correlation was found between SDM quality and hope (r = 0.37, p < 0.001). Regression analysis identified satisfaction with information during SDM (β = 2.85, p = 0.004), DMT convenience (p < 0.001), and information reliability (p = 0.047) as significant predictors of hope, collectively explaining 12.2% of its variance. Conclusion The findings demonstrated a positive and significant relationship between the quality of the SDM process and hope in patients with MS. These results underscore the importance of enhancing patient participation in therapeutic decision-making to improve the psychological well-being of individuals with MS and develop targeted interventions.

Article.Title: CNN model-based image classification for canine brain MRI abnormalities
Article.Authors: Abani S.; Laue M.; Dickinson P.; De Decker S.; Gutierrez-Quintana R.; Ghiasvand S.; Tahmasebi S.; Spohn F.; Sabbotin A.; Hänsch A.; Janisch J.; Ulrich R.; McLarty E.; Nessler J.; Volk H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Diagnostic imaging represents one of the most promising clinical applications of artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the customised convolutional neural network (CNN) SepNetDense for distinguishing between normal and abnormal canine brain magnetic resonance images (MRIs), with the aim of enhancing diagnostic efficiency and assisting radiologists in identifying abnormal images. The dataset comprised T1-weighted (T1w) pre- and post-contrast sequences in transverse, sagittal, and dorsal planes from 550 dogs, collected from four universities. Dogs were included if they had a complete clinical diagnosis confirmed either through histopathology or in accordance with current clinical consensus. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n = 444), a validation set (n = 53), and a test set (n = 53). Each MRI was labelled on a slice-by-slice basis as normal or abnormal. The model was trained on 205 normal imaging datasets (e.g., extracranial aetiologies, idiopathic epilepsy, paroxysmal dyskinesia) and 239 abnormal ones (e.g., neoplasms, inflammatory lesions, other pathologies). The model correctly predicted 74% of the true normal slices in the test set as normal and 73% of the true abnormal as abnormal. A ROC analysis of the model’s prediction at the patient level revealed that, at a threshold of 51% abnormal slices per patient, the model reached an optimal balance of 83% sensitivity (95% CI 67–91%) and 78% (95% CI 54–91%) specificity, with a balanced accuracy of 80% (95% CI 69–92%). ANCOVA revealed that the CNN’s classification performance was influenced by multiple biological, technical, and institutional factors. Lesion diagnosis, institutional setting, and breed size had significant large effects, whereas body weight showed a significant medium effect. Significant interactions with large effect sizes were also observed between diagnosis and institute, as well as between breed size and weight. Additionally, a distinct pattern was observed in the distribution of prediction categories along the anatomical axes, with a trend towards better CNN performance in the central quartiles across all MRI sequences. Overall, the results demonstrate the feasibility of CNN-assisted triage of canine brain MRI studies and highlight diagnosis, institutional setting, breed size, and body weight as key determinants of model performance, emphasising the importance of heterogeneous datasets for the development of robust veterinary AI applications.

Article.Title: Exploring the potential of hybridized metaheuristic algorithms for photovoltaic model parameter estimation
Article.Authors: Khouili O.; Wardi F.; Louzazni M.; Hanine M.; Obidallah W.; Alhulayyil H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Proper modeling of photovoltaic (PV) cells is a highly non-linear and multidimensional problem whose optimization using standalone meta-heuristic techniques faces premature convergence due to the large number of parameters. This paper seeks to fill in a major gap in the literature through a permutation study of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Differential Evolution (DE), Simulated Annealing (SA) and Nelder-Mead (NM) simplex method to determine the optimal "hand-off" scheme for balancing exploration and exploitation. The proposed approach has been evaluated using SDM, DDM, and TDM using R.T.C. France silicon cell, Photowatt-PWP 201 module and an independent set of data on flexible dual junction amorphous silicon cell. To ensure state-of-the-art robustness of the hybrid approach, it was also benchmarked against CEC 2017 test suite. Statistical analysis from 30 runs has been performed using Wilcoxon signed-rank test ( $$p<1.86\times {10}^{-9}$$ ), demonstrate that a sequential "Global-to-Local" transition (PSO–NM) achieves superior precision and stability, yielding a mean RMSE of $$9.32 \times 10^{ - 4}$$ for the SDM and $$1.16 \times 10^{ - 3}$$ A for the 9-parameter TDM, with coefficients of determination ( $${R}^{2}$$ ) exceeding 0.9999. Complexity analysis via the Number of Function Evaluations (NFE) shows that this hybrid method is computationally worth the effort since it produces results of great decimal accuracy and at the same time remains consistent in physical parameters. This research establishes a well-founded model for high accuracy photovoltaic simulation crucial for smart energy management and diagnosis.

Article.Title: Machine learning-driven inverse design of high-hardness multi-principal element alloys through symbolic regression
Article.Authors: Li P.
Article.Abstract: Conventional trial-and-error metallurgical approaches fail to efficiently develop high-hardness multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs), limited by poor physical interpretability of existing machine learning (ML) hardness prediction models and the lack of targeted inverse composition optimization. This work establishes a closed-loop physics-informed ML framework integrating symbolic regression (SR), CatBoost surrogate modelling and multi-metaheuristic optimization to address the two core bottlenecks. A comprehensive descriptor library is constructed by integrating elemental fractions, pymatgen-derived atomic physicochemical properties and classical Hume-Rothery metallurgical parameters, which quantitatively captures lattice distortion, electronic effects and phase transformation mechanisms governing alloy hardness. Genetic programming-based symbolic regression automatically extracts three nonlinear descriptors that encode standardized physicochemical variables, reducing the original 39-dimensional feature space by 33% and remarkably elevating predictive accuracy. The SR-enhanced CatBoost model achieves a test-set coefficient of determination R 2 = 0.885 and RMSE = 77.2 HV, far outperforming traditional semi-empirical formulas and baseline ML models. SHAP analysis verifies that the three SR features contribute 52% of total predictive weight, explicitly elucidating non-monotonic hardening responses including hardness saturation under excessive atomic size mismatch and the trade-off between bulk modulus and dislocation storage capacity. A triangulated inverse design pipeline combining genetic algorithm, particle swarm optimization and whale optimization algorithm is deployed to maximize Vickers hardness under four- and five-principal-element constraints. Cross-algorithm convergence shows stability of the search under a shared surrogate rather than global optimality. The 22 candidates that clear the physical screen and the domain test span 716.6-783.1 HV. Refractory W and Mo act as primary strengthening elements, while moderate Al addition enables simultaneous lightweighting and possible precipitation hardening. This integrated framework unifies interpretable forward hardness prediction, mechanistic analysis and targeted compositional inverse design, drastically cutting experimental screening costs. Future research will incorporate processing and microstructural variables to realize multi-objective optimization balancing hardness, density and ductility.

Article.Title: Comparison between metformin and intermittent fasting for renoprotective effects through mitophagy modulation in a rat cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury model
Article.Authors: Elmorshdy S.; Genedy D.; Helal N.; Moustafa A.; Emam R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The current study investigated the effects of metformin versus intermittent fasting as modulators of mitophagy in cisplatin-induced acute renal injury in rats. Twenty-four adult male rats were divided into four groups: control, cisplatin, metformin-treated, and intermittent fasting groups. Cisplatin (8 mg/kg, intraperitoneal) was administered once on day eight, while metformin (200 mg/kg) was given orally for 12 days. Renal function parameters including serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), fractional excretion of sodium (FENa), and serum sodium and potassium levels were measured, along with urinary neutrophil gelatinase associated lipocalin (NGAL) and renal oxidative stress markers malondialdehyde and superoxide dismutase (MDA and SOD). Mitophagy was assessed by immunohistochemical evaluation of Microtubule-Associated Protein 1 Light Chain and Nucleoporin p62 (LC3 and p62) expression, measurement of PTEN-induced kinase 1(PINK1) levels, and Parkin gene expression, along with histopathological examination of renal tissues. Cisplatin administration significantly impaired kidney function, increased oxidative stress and p62 expression, and reduced SOD, LC3, PINK1, and Parkin gene expression, accompanied by marked histopathological renal damage. Treatment with metformin or intermittent fasting significantly improved renal function tests, reduced oxidative stress and p62 levels, and restored LC3, PINK1, and Parkin expression, with corresponding improvement in renal histopathology. These findings suggest that metformin and intermittent fasting exert protective effects against cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury, potentially through modulation of oxidative stress and mitophagy pathways.

Article.Title: Instruction-tuning large language models with medical classification data improves ICD coding of German tumor diagnoses
Article.Authors: Lenz S.; Ortiz Rosario L.; Vollmar G.; Ustjanzew A.; Alickovic F.; Kindler T.; Panholzer T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate coding of tumor diagnoses, with the German Modification of the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10-GM), and the International Classification of Diseases for Oncology, Third Edition (ICD-O-3), is essential for structured cancer documentation. Large language models (LLMs) offer opportunities for automating such tasks, but locally deployable, open-weight models often lack sufficient domain-specific coding expertise. This study investigates whether instruction-based fine-tuning on public classification resources improves the coding accuracy of open-weight LLMs for German tumor diagnosis texts. Eight models from the Qwen, Llama, and Mistral families (7–70 billion parameters) were fine-tuned on over 500,000 question-answer pairs based on the ICD-10-GM, ICD-O-3, and German procedure classification. The evaluation uses coded diagnoses from the local tumor documentation system as test data. ICD-10-GM accuracy rose from 1.4 to 24 to 41–58%, and partial (three-character codes only) accuracy from 31 to 74 to 73–83%. The accuracy of ICD-O-3 topography coding also improved but started and remained considerably lower. Malformed code outputs dropped to nearly 0% for almost all models. Tumor-diagnosis recognition reached 99%. A data quality analysis showed that incomplete diagnosis descriptions limited achievable test performance. Accuracy correlated positively with model size, but gaps between small and large models narrowed after fine-tuning. The reasoning mode in Qwen3 generally yielded lower performance than fine-tuning and was over 100 times slower. Our findings highlight the potential of leveraging public catalogues to build instruction datasets that improve LLMs in medical documentation tasks. To support reproducibility and further research, we publicly release the complete training dataset and the best-performing fine-tuned model checkpoints.

Article.Title: Mild thermal elevation phase-advances metabolic and matrix transcriptomic programs during koi scale regeneration
Article.Authors: Liu L.; Bai J.; Zhang R.; Li H.; Wang X.; Zhu H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mild warming can alter regeneration kinetics in ectotherms, yet its influence on temporal coordination of transcriptional programs remains incompletely characterized. Using a scale-removal model in koi scale ( Cyprinus carpio ), we compared spontaneous healing at 22 °C (SI), waterborne vitamin C exposure at 25 mg/L at 22 °C (VC), and mild thermal elevation at 24 °C without vitamin C supplementation (TF) over two weeks using histology and time-series RNA sequencing. Histologically, TF showed earlier scale-forming cell aggregation at the pocket base and advanced collagen organization relative to SI and VC. Transcriptomically, SI followed three phases: early amino acid metabolism and inflammatory modulation (Days 1–3), mid-stage lipid oxidative metabolism and extracellular matrix (ECM) assembly (Days 5–7), and late ECM remodeling with autophagy signatures (Days 10–14). Under TF, metabolic and matrix modules typically emerging in the SI mid-window appeared earlier (Days 1–3), indicating a selective forward shift rather than uniform acceleration. Time-series clustering identified nine gene modules; Cluster 8 showed sustained upregulation under TF but not SI, with enrichment for cell differentiation, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, ATPase activity, and ion channel regulation. Machine-learning feature selection prioritized LOC109073349 as the top candidate, with maximal TF–SI divergence at Day 14. These findings support a temporal phase realignment model for thermal management in aquaculture wound care.

Article.Title: A prescription-computable pharmaco-ecological exposure score for predicted drug-induced gut-microbiome disturbance and its association with heart failure in chronic kidney disease
Article.Authors: Fukuoka K.; Yoshida Y.; Uehara Y.; Sakagami S.; Tsukamoto R.; Kawano S.; Kawabe R.; Satake M.; Tanihara T.; Hamamura K.; Mayanagi K.; Yoshii K.; Watanabe D.; Kunisawa J.; Ohdo S.; Matsunaga N.
Article.Abstract: Polypharmacy is pervasive in chronic kidney disease (CKD); however, the cumulative burden of non-antibiotic drugs on the gut microbiota is not captured by host-centric medication indices and is rarely measurable at scale. We developed the cumulative disturbance score (CDS), a prescription-computable exposure metric that scores the predicted drug-induced disturbance of 40 core gut taxa, integrating in vitro growth-inhibition data for 1,197 drugs with duration-weighted prescription records. In 179,591 patients with incident CKD, a higher CDS for a core taxon was associated with incident heart failure in weighted Cox models. Using the internally estimated polypharmacy (≥ 8 drugs) hazard ratio 1.228 as the selection rule, four taxa were prioritized ( Bacteroides fragilis enterotoxigenic, Eggerthella lenta , Bacteroides vulgatus , and Bacteroides uniformis ; 1.262–1.286), whereas a negative-control taxon was null. Taxon-level effects are not separately identified, the scores deriving from shared prescription histories. Whether the association reflects microbial mediation or residual confounding by disease severity cannot be determined without microbiome measurement. Empirical calibration against 15 negative-control outcomes attenuated the estimates to 1.111–1.157. Chronically prescribed cardiovascular and gastrointestinal agents contributed most for Bacteroides taxa, antibacterials for E. lenta . CDS is a prescription-level exposure indicator instead of a microbiome measurement: a scalable pharmaco-ecological index for prioritizing drug–microbiome risks, applied here to heart failure in CKD.

Article.Title: DAMSeg: degradation-aware modulation network for robust semantic segmentation of road scenes under adverse conditions
Article.Authors: Zhang Z.; Wu J.; Zhang D.; Yan X.; Wang Q.; Xia H.; Cai C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Semantic segmentation models for autonomous driving suffer significant performance degradation under adverse weather and lighting conditions such as fog, rain, snow, and nighttime illumination. Existing approaches include restoration before segmentation and robustness-oriented adaptation or generalization; comparatively few use an image-derived degradation estimate as an explicit conditioning input to the segmentation network. We propose DAMSeg, a degradation-aware modulation framework that treats degradation characteristics as conditioning signals within a unified end-to-end model. DAMSeg comprises an implicit degradation encoder that extracts a compact conditioning vector directly from the input image, a conditional feature modulation module that applies stage-specific channel transformations with spatially adaptive fusion, and degradation contrastive regularization (DCR), which structures the projection space used during training. Scene-level condition annotations are used to construct DCR pairs when they are available; the network itself receives only the RGB image and requires no condition label at inference. Experiments on ACDC, Foggy Cityscapes, and BDD100K show that DAMSeg achieves 75.9% mIoU on the ACDC test set with a MiT-B2 backbone, improving the SegFormer-B2 baseline by 5.7 percentage points with gains across all four adverse conditions. On the evaluated dataset transfers, the performance benefit persists without target-domain fine-tuning.

Article.Title: Deciphering the prognostic and immunological landscape of NFKBIA across human cancers
Article.Authors: Guo Z.; Ding X.; Zhang C.; Jiang Y.; Liao D.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to explore the pan-cancer expression, prognostic significance, and immune relevance of NFKBIA , with a specific focus on BRCA, GBM, KIRC, and SKCM. NFKBIA expression was analyzed across multiple cancers using the GEPIA2 and TCGA databases. Survival analyses for BRCA, GBM, KIRC, and SKCM were performed, including overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS). Immune cell infiltration and immune checkpoint gene expression were evaluated in high and low NFKBIA expression groups. The TIMER2.0 database was used to investigate immune cell correlations, and single-cell data from TISCH was analyzed for NFKBIA expression in tumor subpopulations. Pan-cancer analysis revealed that NFKBIA expression was significantly dysregulated across multiple cancers. In BRCA and KIRC, high NFKBIA expression correlated with improved OS and DFS. In contrast, in GBM, elevated NFKBIA expression was not associated with prognosis. In SKCM, higher NFKBIA expression predicted better OS. Additionally, NFKBIA expression showed correlations with immune cell infiltration levels, including CD8 + T cells, macrophages, and dendritic cells, particularly in BRCA, GBM, KIRC, and SKCM. Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis confirmed that NFKBIA was highly expressed in specific immune cell subsets within the tumor microenvironment (TME), indicating its role in regulating immune responses across these cancers. NFKBIA expression is a critical factor in the prognosis of pan-cancer, particularly in BRCA, KIRC, and SKCM, with its effects may contribute to the immune microenvironment.

Article.Title: Computationally efficient stokes-domain phase demodulation for polarization-diversity coherent $$\phi$$-OTDR with apache flink stream processing
Article.Authors: Demise A.; Nur A.; Muanenda Y.
Article.Abstract: Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) based on phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry ( \(\phi\) -OTDR) enables distributed vibration detection over long optical fibres. We investigate a computationally efficient Stokes-domain demodulation approach for polarization-diversity coherent \(\phi\) -OTDR. The Stokes representation provides access to the polarization phase, orientation, and ellipticity, which depend on different combinations of the Stokes parameters and therefore exhibit different conditioning under polarization variations. The state-of-polarization (SOP) evolution is further characterized using the degree of polarization (DOP) and Poincaré-sphere representation, enabling visualization of the polarization behaviour under vibration-affected, silent-fibre, and noise-floor conditions. The polarization phase, derived from the ratio of two Stokes parameters, is demonstrated to be equivalent to the differential phase between orthogonal polarization components while requiring only a single Stokes-domain phase computation, thereby reducing computational complexity. The method is experimentally evaluated over a 10.15-km fibre using 100-ns pulses with a 120- \(\mu \text {s}\) repetition period, providing approximately 10-m spatial resolution and a Nyquist-limited maximum detectable vibration frequency of 4.17 kHz. Experimentally investigated vibrations from 400 Hz to 3 kHz yielded spectral SNRs of 29.50 dB and 23.98 dB, respectively, while a 2-kHz vibration was localized near 10.11 km with a peak SNR of 27.14 dB. A proof-of-concept Apache Flink implementation demonstrates reduced processing time for Stokes-domain phase extraction relative to differential-phase processing under the same local execution environment. The three Stokes-derived angular observables exhibit different conditioning under polarization imbalance, while deep Rayleigh interference fading can degrade all of them as the total backscattered signal approaches the receiver-noise level.

Article.Title: Baseline adipokine profiles have limited predictive value for weight-loss outcomes after laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy: a prospective longitudinal cohort study
Article.Authors: Dohnal R.; Schovánek J.; Cibičková Ľ.; Popelková K.; Karásek D.; Vaverka P.; Radvanský M.; Kučerová V.
Article.Abstract: Bariatric surgery is the most effective treatment for severe obesity, yet postoperative weight-loss outcomes vary considerably between individuals and reliable preoperative predictors remain lacking. Adipokines regulate energy homeostasis, inflammation, and insulin sensitivity, making them promising candidates for predicting surgical outcomes. Here, we evaluated whether baseline circulating adipokine profiles predict weight-loss magnitude, weight-loss velocity, and weight-loss plateau after laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG). We performed a prospective longitudinal study of 83 patients with severe obesity undergoing LSG. Clinical and metabolic parameters together with a panel of eight circulating adipokines were assessed before surgery and during 12 months of follow-up. Associations with postoperative outcomes were evaluated using multivariable regression and survival analyses with false-discovery-rate correction and bootstrap validation. LSG induced substantial improvements in anthropometric and metabolic parameters accompanied by marked remodeling of circulating adipokines. However, baseline adipokines showed limited and inconsistent predictive value for postoperative weight loss. Higher baseline adiponectin was independently associated with lower percentage total weight loss only at 6 months, whereas no adipokine consistently predicted long-term weight loss or weight-loss plateau after correction for multiple testing. In contrast, baseline HDL cholesterol demonstrated a stable inverse association with postoperative weight loss across multiple follow-up time points, outperforming all adipokines as a preoperative predictor. These findings suggest that routine preoperative adipokine profiling has limited clinical utility for predicting weight-loss outcomes after LSG and that conventional metabolic markers may provide greater prognostic value.

Article.Title: Copy number variants (CNVs) interfere with human accelerated regions (HARs) in neurodevelopmental disorders: a large-scale cohort study
Article.Authors: Iuditskaia M.; Semina E.; Pankratova E.; Kurinnaia O.; Guldan E.; Abasov E.; Iourov I.; Chaika Y.
Article.Abstract: ABSTRACT Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs) represent a heterogeneous group of conditions affecting the central nervous system, the etiology of which involves a wide range of factors, including genetic contributors. A proportion of this genetic component is mediated by copy number variations (CNVs) - deletions and duplications of genomic segments that are associated with a broad spectrum of neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric phenotypes. In recent years, there has also been growing interest in studying Human Accelerated Regions (HARs) in relation to these disorders. HARs are highly conserved genomic elements across mammals that have accumulated human-specific sequence changes. These regions are thought to contribute both to the evolution of higher cognitive functions in humans and, paradoxically, to an increased susceptibility to NDDs. Thus, both HARs and CNVs are expected to play key roles in the genetic architecture and pathogenesis of NDDs. However, despite active research on HARs and CNVs separately, integrative studies examining copy-number–driven disruptions specifically within HARs in patients with neurodevelopmental disorders have been extremely limited. This is the first study to assess the contribution of CNVs affecting HARs in 821 children with NDDs. Our bioinformatic evaluation of CNV profiles in this clinical cohort demonstrated that HARs are indeed susceptible to structural alterations in the form of deletions and duplications, supporting the notion that CNVs have shaped the evolution of these regions. Our findings further indicate that HARs, overall, are less frequently affected by duplications compared to other genomic regions. We identified three recurrent HAR loci most strongly associated with neurodevelopmental impairment: HAR_Merge50-02702, HAR_Merge50-02080, and HAR_Merge50-02689. Additionally, we found that HARs disrupted by CNVs form coordinated functional clusters corresponding to genomic regions that harbor extremely rare or entirely absent CNVs in the general population (e.g., HARs associated with RBFOX1, DOC2B, ZMYND11, AFF2, OPHN1 ). These same genes exhibit a high haploinsufficiency index (HI = 3) according to ClinGen, highlighting their dosage sensitivity. Analysis of the most frequently affected HARs confirmed that their associated genes are significantly enriched for core NDD phenotypes. The absence of a direct correlation with genomic instability suggests that HARs represent functionally vulnerable elements and that compensatory mechanisms may restrict the accumulation of additional structural damage in these regions. Taken together, our study reinforces the importance of HARs in the evolution and functioning of the human central nervous system and provides new evidence supporting the functional relevance of HAR-associated disruptions in neurodevelopmental disorders. We anticipate that future research will further elucidate the complex regulatory processes within the genome and help identify specific HAR regions that may be informative for diagnostic purposes and the development of targeted therapeutic approaches.

Article.Title: Fear of falling in parkinson’s disease: a qualitative exploration of patient experiences and coping strategies
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Zheng Z.; Ma Y.; Wu X.; Li J.; Kong X.; Lan M.
Article.Abstract: To explore the psychological experience of fear of falling (FOF) in patients with Parkinson’s disease (PD) and examine their coping behaviors. Sixteen patients with PD, admitted to the Department of Neurology at a tertiary hospital in Hangzhou between July and September 2024, participated in in-depth interviews. The collected data were analyzed, summarized, and refined using a content analysis approach. Two overarching themes with ten subthemes were identified. The first theme, experiences of fear of falling (FOF), revealed profound impacts on daily life, family responsibilities, social activities, and self-esteem, while also highlighting the vicious cycle between recurrent falls and heightened risk perception. The second theme, responses to FOF, encompassed both active coping strategies—such as modifying the home environment, seeking family support, and anticipating professional guidance—and passive avoidance behaviors that further limited independence. Healthcare providers should recognize the psychological burden of fear of falling (FOF) in patients with Parkinson’s disease and consider interventions tailored to their needs. Our findings highlight the importance of addressing FOF in clinical practice and support the development of culturally sensitive, family-centered, and individualized fall-prevention strategies. Future research is needed to evaluate the implementation of these approaches and their potential impact on patients’ quality of life and negative impacts.

Article.Title: Pseudo-label optimization and DIoU-NMS for semi-automatic annotation in scrap steel detection
Article.Authors: Sun S.; Chen J.; Ding Y.; Geng M.; Pan H.; Li H.; Li Z.; Yin W.
Article.Abstract: Industrial scrap steel detection is challenged by dense stacking, fine-grained morphological differences, and severe category imbalance, which make fully manual annotation prohibitively labor-intensive and leave even carefully labeled datasets with missing or imprecise objects. To address this bottleneck, we propose a Semi-Supervised Pseudo-Label YOLO11 detector (SSPL-YOLO11). Built on an offline teacher–student pseudo-labeling framework, SSPL-YOLO11 applies a three-level pseudo-label quality control mechanism—confidence thresholding, DIoU-NMS deduplication, and lightweight manual verification—to recover unlabeled objects at a small manual cost. Controlled experiments quantify the impacts of the confidence threshold, the deduplication strategy, and the pre-trained weight initialization. On the public Scrap Steel Image Dataset (SSID), SSPL-YOLO11 achieves 88.25% $$\text {mAP}_{50}$$ and 65.58% $$\text {mAP}_{50--95}$$ on the independent test set, surpassing the fully supervised YOLO11 baseline by 3.92 and 7.74 percentage points, respectively. The proposed workflow substantially reduces manual annotation cost and provides a practical route toward intelligent scrap steel sorting and recycling.

Article.Title: Rasagiline suppresses glioblastoma cell survival through oxidative stress-mediated modulation of TLR4/NF-Κb signaling and apoptosis
Article.Authors: Akcay G.; Anakok O.; Ozkaraca M.; Yesilyurt F.; Akcay S.; Suicmez M.; Hacimuftuomglu A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most aggressive primary brain tumor in adults and remains associated with poor prognosis despite multimodal treatment. The identification of clinically approved drugs with novel antitumor activities has emerged as a promising strategy for accelerating therapeutic development. Rasagiline, an irreversible monoamine oxidase-B inhibitor widely used for the treatment of Parkinson’s disease, has demonstrated neuroprotective properties; however, its effects on glioblastoma biology remain largely unknown. The present study investigated the concentration-dependent effects of rasagiline on oxidative stress, inflammatory signaling, and apoptotic responses in two human glioblastoma cell lines, U87-MG and T98G. Cells were treated with 2.5, 5, 10, 20, and 40 µM rasagiline for 24 h. Cell viability was evaluated using the MTT assay, while membrane integrity was assessed by lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) protein concentration. Oxidative stress biomarkers (superoxide dismutase, reduced glutathione, and malondialdehyde), inflammatory mediators (IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α), TLR4, NF-κB, and caspase-3 levels were determined by ELISA. Immunofluorescence staining was performed to assess TLR4 and NF-κB expression. Rasagiline produced concentration-dependent effects on glioblastoma cell viability and cellular injury, with more pronounced responses observed at intermediate-to-high concentrations. Treatment with rasagiline disrupted intracellular redox homeostasis, as evidenced by increased SOD protein concentration and MDA levels together with depletion of GSH. At intermediate concentrations, particularly around 10 µM, rasagiline produced coordinated alterations in oxidative stress-related and inflammatory parameters, accompanied by modulation of TLR4/NF-κB-related responses. IL-1β and TNF-α levels increased at selected intermediate concentrations, whereas IL-6 levels progressively decreased with increasing rasagiline concentrations. Caspase-3 protein levels increased particularly at higher concentrations, suggesting an association between rasagiline-induced cellular stress and apoptotic signaling. Immunofluorescence findings further supported the concentration-dependent modulation of TLR4 and NF-κB. Although the magnitude of the responses differed between U87-MG and T98G cells, both models demonstrated broadly similar concentration-dependent response patterns, with 10 µM representing a biologically active intermediate concentration for mechanistic interpretation. In conclusion, rasagiline produced concentration-dependent cytotoxic effects in glioblastoma cells, accompanied by alterations in redox homeostasis, inflammatory signaling, and caspase-3-associated apoptotic responses. These findings provide a basis for further investigation of rasagiline as a potential drug-repurposing candidate in glioblastoma, particularly through mechanistic and in vivo studies.

Article.Title: Quantum key distribution over a three-user fiber network with passive optical circulator
Article.Authors: Jeong Y.; Kim S.; Baek I.; Hong C.; Kwon D.; Jang J.; Ji S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We report the implementation of a quantum key distribution (QKD) system over a three-user fiber-optic network in which each user employs an identical bidirectional transceiver, with a single asymmetric interferometer shared between the encoding and decoding paths to reduce duplicated optical resources at the node level. The three users-Alice, Bob, and Charlie-are interconnected through a passive circulator-based hub built from 3-port optical circulators, which enables secure key exchange between any pair of them without active switching or a trusted intermediary. Each user is connected to the central circulator via standard telecom fiber links of 10-15 km, resulting in effective inter-user distances of 20-25 km. We employed the BB84 protocol with a two-decoy-state method (weak and vacuum) for secure key generation. For each user pair, sifted keys of $$10^6$$ bits were processed with a composable security parameter $$\varepsilon \sim 10^{-8}$$ . Secret key lengths were evaluated using three approaches: (1) theoretical estimation based on measured quantum bit error rate (QBER) and gains, assuming an error correction efficiency of 1.16; (2) experimental post-processing using Winnow; and (3) experimental post-processing using Cascade. All links achieved low QBERs and yielded positive secret key lengths. Cascade consistently produced longer final keys due to its higher reconciliation efficiency. These results demonstrate the feasibility of a resource-sharing bidirectional node architecture for secure multi-user quantum communication using passive circulator-based routing.

Article.Title: Integrating causal knowledge with satellite and glider data: a novel framework for marine water quality simulation
Article.Authors: Hashemi M.; Mahjouri N.; Nikoo M.
Article.Abstract: This study presents a causally informed machine-learning framework for jointly estimating coastal marine variables by incorporating prior structural assumptions into model training. The causal-informed neural network (CINN) uses an expert-specified directed acyclic graph (DAG) and model-based feature-perturbation effects as regularization targets; it is designed for prediction and does not identify causal effects from the observational data. The framework combines satellite remote sensing data with high-resolution in-situ glider measurements from the upper 0–2 m to jointly estimate temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, and chlorophyll-a. Under acquisition-date-blocked five-fold cross-validation, in which all observations from the same acquisition date were kept in the same fold, CINN achieved R² values of 0.961, 0.905, 0.898, and 0.725, respectively, and a uniform-average multi-output R² of 0.872. Regularization-weight, matched-input, and output ablations assess predictive sensitivity, while bootstrap intervals and Diebold–Mariano tests quantify uncertainty in the reported observation-level comparisons.

Article.Title: The cervical microbiome in hispanic populations in Texas and Puerto Rico with and without cervical dysplasia
Article.Authors: Walters D.; El Alam M.; Harris T.; Lo D.; Diaz J.; Napravnik T.; Lynn E.; Boatright L.; Figueroa D.; Judge A.; Bhaskar C.; Fontillas A.; Ehsan S.; Wang R.; Jansen Aref S.; Ajami N.; Sastry J.; Sims T.; Romaguera J.; Dorta-Estremera S.; Klopp A.; Godoy-Vitorino F.; Colbert L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Within the United States, Hispanic women, especially those in Puerto Rico, face an increased risk of cervical cancer development. The objective of this study was to explore the cervical microbiota of Hispanic women at high risk of developing HPV-induced cervical dysplasia or with cervical dysplasia treated in Texas and Puerto Rico. Cervical swab samples were collected from 296 participants (N = 80 Texan Non-Hispanic White, N = 98 Texan Hispanic, and N = 118 Puerto Rican Hispanic) during each patient’s initial visit and subjected to 16S V4 rRNA gene sequencing for microbiome profiling. HPV types were grouped as HPV 16, other high-risk HPV types, and other using HPV genotyping. Among participants, 71% (N = 211) were classified as high-risk normal, and 29% (N = 85) had cervical dysplasia. HPV 16 was detected in 15% (N = 45), other high-risk HPV types in 33% (N = 98), while 52% (N = 152) of patients were classified as “other”. Comparative analysis of microbial community structures across locations revealed distinct compositions, with Texan Hispanic women showing higher alpha diversity for two alpha diversity metrics (Pielou evenness and Shannon Diversity Index). The prevalence of CSTs varied across locations and disease states, with CSTs III and IV-B being among the most common in the study cohorts. Overall, this descriptive study provides a better understanding of cervical microbiome in Hispanic women across multiple geographic locations, in order to guide future interventions.

Article.Title: Health literacy and medication beliefs in adults with type 2 diabetes enrolled in therapeutic patient education: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Odic P.; Nardi O.; Mutlu G.; Blackwell F.; Gainet A.; Foucault-fruchard L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Therapeutic patient education is a cornerstone of type 2 diabetes management. Medication beliefs, as conceptualized by the Necessity–Concerns Framework, influence how patients perceive and engage with long-term treatment. Health literacy may shape these beliefs, yet its relationship with medication beliefs remains insufficiently explored in adults with type 2 diabetes, particularly in real-world therapeutic patient education settings. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from the DIABREVAL cohort, a structured therapeutic patient education programme conducted in primary care in France. Medication beliefs were assessed using the Beliefs about Medicines Questionnaire-Specific (BMQ-Specific). Health literacy was measured using the Newest Vital Sign (NVS), socioeconomic deprivation using the EPICES score, and educational attainment using three predefined categories. Linear regression models with progressive adjustment for deprivation, age and educational attainment were performed using multiple imputation, with complete-case sensitivity analyses. A total of 494 adults with type 2 diabetes were included (mean age 64.4 ± 10.1 years; 54.0% men). Limited health literacy was common, with 62.8% of participants scoring below 4 on the NVS. Higher health literacy was independently associated with lower medication concerns (β = −0.28, p = 0.047), whereas no independent association was observed with perceived necessity of treatment. Educational attainment and socioeconomic deprivation were not independently associated with medication beliefs, while older age was independently associated with stronger necessity beliefs. These findings suggest that health literacy may be more closely associated with how patients perceive treatment-related risks than with their perceived necessity of treatment. Integrating the assessment of health literacy and medication beliefs into therapeutic education and routine clinical care may help healthcare professionals identify medication-related concerns and support more personalised communication and counselling strategies.

Article.Title: Methodological audit and empirical evaluation of a lightweight whole-volume 3D CNN for preterm brain injury classification
Article.Authors: Yuan B.; Lu J.; Zhang W.; Wu B.; Wang T.; Wang C.; Sun C.; Guo L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study uses methodological auditing to evaluate a proof-of-concept engineering pipeline for classifying radiological severity groups of preterm brain injury (BI) from T2-weighted MRI in the dHCP cohort. Its primary contribution is methodology-driven empirical discovery rather than a new neural-network architecture. GloResNet combines a standard ResNet-10 backbone, MedicalNet initialization, whole-volume array resizing, mixup, and array-axis-0-reversal probability averaging, hereafter referred to as axis-0-reversal averaging; no new CNN block is proposed. The audit identifies concrete mechanisms by which small-cohort imaging results can be overstated, including unit-of-analysis drift, fold-assignment non-traceability, post hoc model-selection bias, and ranking across incompatible evaluation protocols. Building on this framework, we report the first fair, traceable comparison between a de novo trained Vision Transformer (ViT) and a domain-adapted lightweight 3D CNN on a public preterm brain injury dataset. When all sources of bias are controlled, the lightweight CNN achieves comparable or superior performance to ViT, challenging the prevailing assumption that larger, more complex architectures are always preferable in low-data regimes. Applying the audit to the historical evidence also showed that the archived GloResNet mean fold accuracy of $$69.12 \pm 7.42\%$$ was calculated over 180 scan records from 128 subjects, including repeated scans, without retained subject identifiers or out-of-fold predictions. The historical archive is therefore reported separately from the fair, traceable server-side comparison. A separate, auditable subject-level input-representation experiment did not demonstrate superiority of whole-volume input. The resulting minimum reporting standard requires an explicit statistical unit, traceable subject-level folds, retained out-of-fold predictions, prespecified selection rules, and transparent comparator conditions. These internal estimates do not establish clinical screening performance or external generalizability. The source code is available at https://github.com/ICL-SUST/GloResNet-Preterm-Brain

Article.Title: A dual-expert social bot detection model based on R-GCN and LLM fusion reasoning
Article.Authors: Song J.; Gao H.; Xu N.; Guan J.; Shan S.
Article.Abstract: With the rapid development of social media platforms, automated accounts have become an important factor affecting information dissemination, public opinion governance and platform ecology. This paper takes TwiBot-20 as the research object, focusing on the study of social bot detection based on textual semantic information and social topological information. The research objective of this paper is to combine detection performance with readable expert evidence for social bot detection through a data-driven dual-expert model. Firstly, a textual semantic expert based on supervised fine-tuning large language model is constructed. User description, follower count, following count, tweet count, verification status and active years are organized as user profile input, and the textual semantic expert outputs the semantic-side prediction label and evidence summary. Secondly, a topological structure expert based on relational graph convolutional network is built. The construction of this expert includes the construction of user nodes, the construction of Following and Followers relation edges, and the construction of node features by combining account attributes and textual semantic embeddings. Thirdly, a dual-expert fusion reasoning model based on large language model is constructed. The outputs of textual semantic expert and topological structure expert are organized as structured evidence, and user-specific decision weights computed by a model fitted on the development split are used to guide the large language model to generate the final detection result and explanation report. The proposed model achieves 82.76% accuracy and 84.14% bot F1 on TwiBot-20, improving on the stronger single expert by 2.20 and 1.54% points. Its accuracy matches stacking, while the calibrated ensemble achieves a slightly higher bot F1. The model also produces readable reports of expert disagreement and decision cues, illustrated through correct and incorrect arbitration cases.

Article.Title: Construction of a five-gene prognostic model involving T cell exhaustion and metabolic reprogramming for predicting hepatocellular carcinoma risk using LASSO: insights into immune infiltration and drug sensitivity
Article.Authors: Wang S.; Chen Y.; Mao Y.; Chen Z.; Zhang X.; Zhang T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hepatocellular carcinomas (HCCs) ranks as the most commonly seen and deadly tumor in the world, whose pathogenesis has a close correlation with T cell exhaustion and metabolic reprogramming, which are two critical yet underexplored mechanisms and can profoundly shape the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) to drive disease progression. This study was designed for constructing a prognosis risk model for HCCs and elucidating its correlations with immune infiltration and drug sensitivity via combined use of these two biological axes. An integrated bioinformatics analysis was performed by leveraging data from two datasets such as Cancer Genome Atlas Liver Hepatocellular Carcinoma (TCGA-LIHC) and Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO, including GSE76427 and GSE10186). Fifty seven overlapping genes associated with both T cell exhaustion and metabolic reprogramming were screened out. Thereafter, the protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analyses and Cox regression model analyses were conducted for identifying five core genes as follows: EZH2, FOXO1, SMARCA2, KPNA2, and SLC2A1.According to the calculated risk scores, HCC patients in the TCGA-LIHC training set were assigned into two groups respectively with high and low risks, which indicated an obvious difference in overall survival (OS) (P<0.0001). This model demonstrated a good performance in predicting one-and three-year OS, with an area under the curve (AUC) of greater than 0.7, which was further confirmed by external validation.Furthermore, the risk scores had correlations with distinct immune cell infiltration patterns and different sensitivities to anticancer drugs, and the low-risk group displayed an enhanced immune activity and greater drug sensitivity.To sum up, the present study has constructed a creative five-gene prognostic model involving both T cell exhaustion and metabolic reprogramming, which can be used as a reliable prognosis biomarker, and guide personalized therapy. These findings offer new and deeper insights into synergistic effects of metabolic alterations and immune escape on HCC progression.

Article.Title: DAF-EfficientNetV2: distribution-aware feature enhancement for plant leaf disease recognition in complex environments
Article.Authors: Du L.; Ma Y.; Xue R.; Zhao Y.; Xie X.; Yu H.
Article.Abstract: Plant leaf diseases in complex natural growing environments are characterized by significant scale variation and morphological heterogeneity, which pose severe challenges to the feature representation capability and inference efficiency of recognition models. Although existing convolutional neural networks have achieved certain progress in disease recognition tasks, they are still constrained by inherent local inductive bias, resulting in limited capability in modeling long-range dependencies and bridging the semantic gap across hierarchical features. To address these issues, this paper proposes a plant leaf disease recognition model termed DAF-EfficientNetV2 (Distribution-Aware Feature-enhanced EfficientNetV2) based on the EfficientNetV2-S backbone. Under the premise of maintaining parameter efficiency and fast inference of the backbone network, the proposed model introduces an integrated Global–Local Semantic Fusion Module (GMSF). Through a spatially orthogonal global modeling strategy, the module efficiently captures cross-region lesion correlations within a single computational unit, and, together with an adaptive semantic calibration mechanism, effectively alleviates the semantic inconsistency among features from different levels. As a result, the model’s panoramic perception capability for scale distortion and complex lesion morphologies is significantly enhanced. In addition, a Shuffle Attention feature re-calibration mechanism is incorporated, which jointly optimizes channel-wise and spatial responses through a “group–parallel–reassemble” strategy, guiding the model to focus on diagnostically valuable lesion regions while suppressing redundant noise from complex field backgrounds in a computationally efficient manner. Furthermore, a lightweight cross-scale aggregation strategy is adopted to achieve efficient integration and alignment of features at different resolutions. Experimental results on the Plant Pathology 2020-FGVC7 and Plant Pathology 2021-FGVC8 datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves classification accuracies of 95.43 ± 0.51% (best 96.14%) and 88.39%, respectively, outperforming existing mainstream approaches and validating the effectiveness and robustness of DAF-EfficientNetV2 in complex plant disease recognition tasks. The code is publicly available at: https://github.com/mayue0606/DAF-EfficientNetV2 .
