Article.Title: Performance evaluation of laser diffraction and sieve-pipette techniques for grid-scale hydraulic characterization of lateritic vadose zones
Article.Authors: Biswal S.; Jha M.; Senapati D.
Article.Abstract: The vadose zone plays a vital role in sustaining society and ecosystems on the Earth. The complexity of vadose zones, coupled with expensive and laborious field investigations pose a formidable challenge in their characterization, and hence they are neglected in hydrogeologic studies. This study demonstrates a novel scientific framework for the grid-scale hydraulic characterization of vadose zones using the laser diffraction (LD) technique and grain-size analysis (GSA) models. To demonstrate the proposed methodology, a total of 126 vadose zone samples and 95 core samples were collected from four layers across 33 grids in a lateritic terrain of Eastern India. Thereafter, the efficacy of the advanced LD technique and the conventional sieve-pipette analysis (SP) was compared by generating grain-size distribution curves (GSDCs) and estimating vadose-zone hydraulic conductivity (K vz ) by using selected GSA models at four different depths (0–50 cm, 50–100 cm, 100–150 cm, and 150–200 cm), followed by an uncertainty analysis. Finally, the estimates of K vz based on the SP-GSA and LD-GSA models were verified using field-measured K vz . The analysis of GSDCs for different depths revealed that the LD technique yields smoother S-shaped GSDCs than the SP technique. Consistently, low uncertainty was found in the K vz estimated by the LD-GSA models (0.0002–1.203 m/day) compared to the K vz estimated by the SP-GSA models (0.0008–2.171 m/day). The verification results based on statistical and graphical indicators revealed that the K vz yielded by most of the LD-GSA models for all layers of the vadose zone are in close agreement with the measured K vz values [MAE: 0.38 to 0.89 m/day and RMSE: 0.6 to 0.98 m/day]. On the other hand, the performance of SP-GSA models was also found to be reasonable, yielding K vz values with MAE and RMSE ranging from 0.36 to 1.45 m/day and 0.64–1.74 m/day, respectively, across all the vadose-zone layers. It is concluded that the LD technique provides more reliable GSDCs, whereas both SP and LD techniques yield reliable K vz (using suitably selected GSA models), thereby offering a useful scientific framework for estimating K vz at a grid scale. The proposed framework provides a basis for transferability and future evaluation at a larger spatial scale under different hydrogeologic and hydro-climatic conditions.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: vadose zone; grain size distribution; uncertainty analysis; hydraulic conductivity; laser diffraction; Eastern India

Article.Title: Association of pre-existing cardiovascular disease with cardiovascular and clinical outcomes in patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors
Article.Authors: Alfehaid L.; Alanazi A.; Alomran M.; Skouri H.; Alsuhebany N.
Article.Abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer therapy but are increasingly associated with cardiovascular complications. The association between pre-existing cardiovascular disease (CVD) and cardiovascular outcomes among patients receiving ICIs remains incompletely characterized, particularly in real-world settings. To evaluate the association between baseline CVD and cardiovascular and clinical outcomes among adult patients treated with ICIs. We conducted a retrospective multicenter cohort study at two tertiary hospitals in Saudi Arabia, including adult patients who received at least one ICI dose between January 2017 and January 2023. Baseline CVD was defined as documented cardiovascular disease before ICI initiation. The primary outcome was a composite of new cardiovascular events occurring after ICI initiation. The secondary outcome was all-cause mortality. We used multivariable logistic regression to identify factors independently associated with cardiovascular events, with sensitivity analyses incorporating additional cardiovascular risk factors. Among 608 patients, 54 (8.9%) had baseline CVD. Patients with baseline CVD were older and had a greater burden of comorbidities than those without baseline CVD. During follow-up, 69 patients (11.3%) experienced at least one cardiovascular event. Cardiovascular events occurred in 27 of 54 patients (50.0%) with baseline CVD compared with 42 of 554 patients (7.6%) without baseline CVD ( p < 0.001). Baseline CVD was independently associated with higher odds of cardiovascular events (adjusted OR, 9.46; 95% CI 4.92–18.17; p < 0.001), and increasing age was also independently associated with the outcome (adjusted OR per year, 1.04; 95% CI 1.01–1.06; p = 0.001). The association remained significant after additional adjustment for hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and dyslipidemia (adjusted OR, 6.64; 95% CI 3.28–13.47; p < 0.001). All-cause mortality was higher among patients with baseline CVD (64.8% vs. 46.4%, p = 0.010), and unadjusted median overall survival was shorter (11.5 vs. 23.8 months; log-rank p = 0.022). Cardiovascular events were predominantly ischemic and heart failure-related, whereas myocarditis was rare, occurring in only one patient overall. In this multicenter cohort, pre-existing CVD was independently associated with higher cardiovascular event odds among ICI patients, even after adjusting for risk factors. These patients also had shorter OS, though survival analysis was unadjusted. Findings suggest baseline CVD patients are vulnerable and may benefit from thorough risk assessment and cardio-oncology care. However, as an observational study without a non-ICI comparator, these associations do not prove ICI caused or worsened CVD.

Article.Title: Hierarchical dual-timescale deep reinforcement learning for mechanically rotatable STAR-RIS assisted mobile edge computing networks
Article.Authors: R D.; K. S P.
Article.Abstract: The integration of Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) with Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) has emerged as a promising paradigm to address the challenges of latency-sensitive applications in dynamic wireless environments. This paper proposes a multi-rotational Simultaneously Transmitting and Reflecting RIS (STAR-RIS) assisted MEC framework that considers both mechanical reorientation and electronic control. Unlike conventional STAR-RIS systems with fixed orientations, the proposed architecture enables physical rotation of STAR-RIS panels to dynamically adjust spatial coverage and achieve improved geometric alignment with mobile users. A comprehensive system model is developed incorporating rotatable STAR-RIS panels, dual-region users, task offloading decisions, and wireless channel dynamics. To address the resulting mixed-timescale, non-convex stochastic optimization problem, a hierarchical dual-timescale Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) - based framework is proposed, where a slow-timescale agent controls mechanical rotation while fast-timescale agents jointly optimize electronic STAR-RIS parameters and MEC offloading decisions. A formal non-stationarity analysis demonstrates the superiority of dual-timescale DRL and a convergence rationale is established through two-timescale stochastic approximation theory. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves stable convergence and significantly outperforms benchmark schemes in terms of task completion rate, fairness, sum rate, and energy efficiency. The findings highlight that mechanical rotation introduces an additional spatial degree of freedom and enhances the MEC performance in dynamic mobile environments.

Article.Title: Prevalence and functional impact of musculoskeletal pain among university students in seven Arab countries and its sociodemographic and lifestyle associations
Article.Authors: Samir A.; El-Ashry A.; Tawfik A.; El-Sayed M.; Abdelaziz O.; Mosali T.; Hamdy A.; Soliman E.; Tiryag A.; Mousalawi I.; Hatem N.; Hemida M.; Alzeer D.; Hachim O.; Howireth A.; Ahmed G.; Al-shayeb L.; Ghazy R.; Kabbash I.
Article.Abstract: Musculoskeletal pain (MSP) represents a major public health challenge globally, particularly among university students who are in a critical transitional phase of life characterized by intense academic demands, lifestyle changes, and increasing reliance on digital technologies. Sedentary behavior (SB) has been identified as a potential risk factor for MSP; however, evidence from the Arab region remains limited. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of MSP in nine body regions (neck, shoulders, upper back, elbows, wrists/hands, lower back, hips/thighs, knees, and ankles/feet) across four time points (lifetime, past 12 months, past month, and today), to assess the impact of MSP, and examine the association between SB and MSP. A multinational cross-sectional study was conducted among 4300 university students in seven Arab countries (Egypt, Yemen, Iraq, Sudan, Jordan, Syria, and Palestine), using an online Arabic self-administered questionnaire. Convenience and snowball sampling methods were used to recruit eligible study respondents. MSP was assessed using the Arabic version of the Extended Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ-E). SB was assessed using sedentary behavior questionnaire (SBQ). Chi-square tests were used for univariate associations. Binary logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with any MSP in the past 12 months, and to identify predictors of high SB. Adjusted odds ratios (aOR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were reported, and a p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. The prevalence of MSP in at least one body region was 84.0% (lifetime), 71.3% (past 12 months), and 64.9% (past month). The neck (49.3%) and lower back (37.3%) were the most affected regions in the past 12 months. Among those affected, preventing usual activities (range: 48.8%–71.7%) and taking medication (range: 37.6–48.2%) were the most reported impacts, while hospitalization remained relatively low (3.2–14.2%). Female sex (aOR = 1.98, 95% CI 1.69–2.31), chronic diseases (aOR = 1.90, 95% CI 1.44–2.49), MSP family history (aOR = 1.96, 95% CI 1.56–2.47), moderate SB (aOR = 1.56, 95% CI 1.32–1.84), and high SB (aOR = 1.42, 95% CI 1.16–1.72) were significantly associated with MSP in the past 12 months, while sleeping 6–8 h was protective (aOR = 0.79, 95% CI 0.67–0.92). This study found a high prevalence of MSP among university students in Arab countries, particularly affecting the neck and lower back. Higher SB, chronic diseases, and a family history of MSP were associated with MSP, whereas adequate sleep appeared to be protective. These findings support the need for university-based strategies that reduce prolonged SB and promote musculoskeletal health, including ergonomic education, active breaks, adjustable study stations, and more active learning environments.

Article.Title: p300 activity and subcellular localization associate with tumor aggressiveness and clinical outcome in triple-negative breast cancer
Article.Authors: Fermento M.; Clemente V.; Gallardo G.; Masciovecchio M.; Villegas M.; Alonso E.; Ferronato M.; Coló G.; Arévalo J.; Juri M.; Jung M.; Facchinetti M.; Curino A.
Article.Abstract: Hormone-independent breast cancers are aggressive malignancies with limited targeted therapeutic options. Epigenetic regulators such as the transcriptional cofactor p300 (EP300), which possesses histone acetyltransferase (HAT) activity, have been implicated in tumor progression; however, the contribution of p300 functional activity and subcellular localization to tumor aggressiveness and clinical outcome remains incompletely understood. Here, using triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) as a model of hormone-independent aggressive tumors, we investigated the role of p300 activity and intracellular distribution through genetic silencing and pharmacological inhibition approaches. p300 depletion or HAT inhibition reduced tumor cell viability, induced apoptosis, and impaired metastatic dissemination both in vitro and in vivo. These effects were associated with alterations in epithelial–mesenchymal transition–related markers and cytoskeletal organization. Analysis of human TNBC specimens revealed a predominant cytoplasmic localization of p300 in tumor cells. Notably, exclusive cytoplasmic localization was associated with lower tumor stage and improved overall survival, independently of mutations affecting the HAT domain. Together, these findings identify p300 functional activity as a regulator of tumor aggressiveness and demonstrate that its subcellular localization provides clinically relevant prognostic information. Our results underscore the importance of considering both the activity and intracellular distribution of epigenetic regulators when evaluating their role as biomarkers and therapeutic targets in aggressive cancers.

Article.Title: Prediagnostic GERD is associated with mortality among patients with gastric cancer in a nationwide cohort
Article.Authors: Choi J.; Song J.; Kim Y.; Kim J.; Han Y.; Lee H.; Lee J.; Park Y.; Yang S.; Han K.
Article.Abstract: We investigated the survival outcomes of patients with newly diagnosed gastric cancer with prior gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). In this nationwide population‑based cohort study using the Korea Central Cancer Registry database (2012–2017), patients with gastric cancer aged ≥ 30 years with national health screening records were classified into the GERD and non-GERD groups. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality, with secondary analyses including stage-specific outcomes and cause of death. Among 108,350 patients with gastric cancer, 14,237 (13.1%) were classified into the GERD group. Patients with GERD were diagnosed with gastric cancer at earlier disease stages than were those without GERD. However, all-cause mortality was higher in the GERD than in the non-GERD group (19.78% vs. 17.85%, P < 0.0001), including both gastric cancer-related and non-cancer-related deaths. The association remained after multivariable adjustment (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.13; 95% confidence interval, 1.08–1.17). The association was stage-specific, being strongest in the regional stage, followed by in the localized stage; no significant difference was observed in the distant stage. Presence of GERD in patients with gastric cancer was associated with earlier-stage diagnosis but higher mortality, suggesting that GERD may be associated with prognostic heterogeneity. Further studies should verify its potential role in risk stratification.

Article.Title: Climate-resilient tomato production: potassium nanoparticles regulate carbohydrate metabolism and oxidative defense under nanoplastic stress
Article.Authors: Bengisu G.; Atay U.; Durul M.; Khalofah A.; Faizan M.; Habib Y.
Article.Abstract: Nanoplastics are emerging environmental contaminants that threaten sustainable crop production and food safety by disrupting mineral nutrient homeostasis, impairing physiological processes, and inducing reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated oxidative stress. Nanoparticle-based interventions have emerged as a promising strategy for mitigating nanoplastic-induced phytotoxicity and enhancing plant stress resilience. In the present study, the protective effects of potassium nanoparticles (K-NPs; 10 mmol L⁻ 1 ) against nanoplastic-induced stress (4 mg kg⁻ 1 soil) were investigated in Solanum lycopersicum using a randomized complete block design with five biological replicates per treatment. Nanoplastics were applied to the soil, whereas K-NPs were administered as a foliar spray at 30 days after sowing (DAS). Nanoplastic exposure markedly inhibited plant growth and physiological performance, significantly reducing root length (68.81%), shoot dry weight (20.53%), SPAD chlorophyll value (70.85%), net photosynthetic rate (46.67%), protein content (13.82%), and Ca 2 ⁺ content (41.01%) relative to the control. In contrast, foliar application of K-NPs effectively alleviated these adverse effects, significantly enhancing shoot length (17.25%), leaf area (10.89%), and glucose content (18.62%) under nanoplastic stress. Furthermore, nanoplastic exposure markedly increased oxidative damage, as evidenced by elevated malondialdehyde (40.47%), hydrogen peroxide (26.87%), and superoxide anion (42.35%) levels, indicating severe membrane lipid peroxidation and excessive ROS accumulation. K-NP treatment substantially suppressed the accumulation of these oxidative stress markers while enhancing the activities of key antioxidant enzymes, including superoxide dismutase, catalase, and peroxidase, thereby strengthening the cellular antioxidant defense system. In addition, K-NPs restored mineral nutrient homeostasis and improved physiological and biochemical performance under nanoplastic stress. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that foliar application of K-NPs effectively mitigates nanoplastic-induced phytotoxicity by enhancing antioxidant capacity, maintaining nutrient homeostasis, and preserving physiological functions, highlighting their potential as a sustainable nanotechnology-based strategy for improving crop resilience under emerging nanoplastic pollution.

Article.Title: TAS-VANET: a trust-aware clustering and misbehavior management architecture for vehicular networks with whale-optimized deep detection
Article.Authors: Abdulkadhim F.; Abbas S.; Alashour G.; Mohammed M.; Hashim H.; Tang C.
Article.Abstract: Reliable operation of vehicular ad hoc networks (VANETs) requires more than detecting individual falsified messages: misbehaving vehicles must be identified over time, excluded from privileged roles such as cluster head, and prevented from degrading routing performance. This paper presents TAS-VANET, a trust-aware clustering and misbehavior management architecture that couples (i) a weighted clustering scheme (WCS) for stable cluster-head election, (ii) a per-vehicle trust model updated by detector verdicts, and (iii) a compact supervised sparse autoencoder (SAE) with a skip connection, whose hyperparameters are tuned by the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA). The detection component is validated on a public consolidation of the VeReMi Extension benchmark (88,029 records, 17 attack variants) under sender-disjoint 10-fold cross-validation, reaching a mean F1 of 0.8831 (held-out test F1 \(=\) 0.9036); WOA tuning contributes \(+9.34\) F1 points over the default-configured SAE (one-sided Wilcoxon \(p=9.77\times {10}^{-4}\) , paired across identical folds). The integrated system is evaluated in OMNeT + + /SUMO against two trust-based clustering protocols (TACR and QMM-VANET): at 195 vehicles TAS-VANET attains a packet delivery ratio of 89.0%, exceeding TACR by 2.0 percentage points and QMM-VANET by 14.0 percentage points (18.7% relative), with the margin over TACR widening from 2.0 to 3.5 percentage points at 90 km/h; deploying the tuned rather than the default configuration lowers end-to-end delay by 14.3% at the 10% malicious-vehicle ratio. We additionally report two transparent negative findings: strong tabular ensembles remain competitive per-message detectors on this benchmark, and constant-position-offset attacks are essentially undetectable from single-message kinematics alone (AUC \(\approx \) 0.529), which we frame as an open research problem. All reported values trace to released simulation and training artifacts.

Article.Title: Non-suicidal self-injury is linked to mind-body intuitions: an exploratory study
Article.Authors: Berent I.; Boccagno C.; Hooley J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) presents a pressing mind-body conundrum: why does the infliction of physical pain alleviate psychological suffering? We suggest that NSSI might arise, in part, from a difference in intuitive Dualism. We hypothesize that the tacit mind-body divide typically guides the conscious differentiation of physical and psychological pain. If, in NSSI, the mind-body divide is attenuated, psychological pain would be harder to recognize and differentiate from physical pain. Here, we evaluate this prediction in an exploratory online study of mind-body intuitions among individuals with NSSI engagement ( N = 47) and Controls ( N = 52). Results show that people with more severe lifetime NSSI view the psyche as more physical—more likely to persist by duplicating one’s body and desist upon the body’s demise. Furthermore, among participants with more severe NSSI, those who manifested a weaker mind-body divide were less likely to endorse established NSSI functions as explanations for their self-injury. Our results cannot determine whether intuitive Dualism plays a causal role in NSSI or NSSI motivations. Nonetheless, in this exploratory online sample, the mind–body judgments of people with more severe lifetime NSSI suggested stronger Physicalist intuitions. Thus, individual differences in intuitive Dualism could shed light on NSSI, and potentially, psychopathology more broadly.

Article.Title: Comparative evaluation of long-term corona- and environmentally-aged high-temperature vulcanized silicone rubber nano-composites
Article.Authors: Saleem M.; Noorden Z.; Salem A.; Amer A.
Article.Abstract: This study presents an aging evaluation of high-temperature vulcanized silicone rubber nanocomposites subjected to corona-induced deterioration over different durations, as well as their retardation through the incorporation of nanosized fillers to improve high-voltage insulation performance. In addition to performing corona aging using a multi-needle electrode test system for 72, 172, and 272 h, the test samples were aged in a specially constructed chamber for 5040 h under AC voltage and different environmental stresses, including temperature, humidity, ultraviolet radiation, and acidic and salt fog. Following these different aging treatments (corona/environmental stress), diagnosis based on surface partial discharge and volume/surface current was performed to determine modifications in the electrical properties of the materials under investigation. As a result, the deterioration of the tested samples’ surface properties was indicated by an increase in the mean partial discharge magnitude. Furthermore, a significant change in surface conductivity was noticed at high ambient temperature and test voltage. The results showed that under the given experimental arrangement, corona discharge for about 272 h is adequate to cause considerable degradation of the material properties. Overall, the sample containing 5 wt% of boron nitride demonstrated consistent performance under all investigated conditions, leading to improved aging resistance against different stresses.

Article.Title: ENDOPAIN4D assesment and platelet mediators in adenomyosis insights from thromboxane A2 and platelet activating factor
Article.Authors: Anwar R.; Aprialdi D.; Rachmawati A.; Permadi W.; Syam H.; Ritonga M.; Annas J.; Trianasari N.; Nisa A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Adenomyosis is a common benign uterine disorder in women of reproductive age, often associated with pelvic pain, abnormal uterine bleeding, and infertility. Platelet-derived mediators such as thromboxane A2 (TXA 2 ) and platelet-activating factor (PAF) have been implicated in disease pathophysiology. However, their relationship with pain perception in adenomyosis remains incompletely understood. The cross-sectional nature of the available evidence limits conclusions regarding temporal or causal relationships between platelet-derived mediators and pain. This study aims to compare TXA 2 and PAF levels in adenomyosis and non adenomyosis uterine tissue. This cross-sectional study included 64 women aged 20–49 years, divided into an adenomyosis (n = 32) and non-adenomyosis uterine tissue (n = 32) groups. The comparison group consisted of women undergoing gynecological surgery whose uterine tissue showed no histopathological evidence of adenomyosis. Pain perception was assessed using the ENDOPAIN-4D questionnaire. Tissue levels of TXA 2 and PAF were measured using ELISA. Statistical analyses included t-tests or Mann–Whitney tests for group comparisons. TXA2 levels were significantly higher in adenomyosis tissue (287.26 ± 29.57 ng/L) compared to non-adenomyosis uterine tissue (177.33 ± 15.75 ng/L; p = 0.0001). PAF levels were also significantly higher in adenomyosis tissue (200.97 ± 22.83 ng/mL) compared to non-adenomyosis uterine tissue (128.52 ± 24.68 ng/mL; p = 0.0001). The observed differences indicate an association between adenomyosis and higher tissue levels of TXA2 and PAF but do not establish causality. TXA2 and PAF levels are elevated in adenomyosis tissue compared with non-adenomyosis uterine tissue. These findings suggest that TXA2 and PAF may be involved in the pathophysiology of adenomyosis; however, further studies are needed to clarify their mechanistic roles.

Article.Title: Positive-unlabelled learning for recorded damp and mould risk in UK housing
Article.Authors: Nguyen M.; Butt U.; Farag S.; Khan A.
Article.Abstract: Operational housing records identify damp-and-mould complaints and repairs, while dwellings without recorded events remain unlabelled rather than verified negatives. We formulate recorded damp-and-mould risk prioritisation as a Positive-Unlabelled (PU) learning problem using anonymised UK housing administrative data. The dataset contains 65,214 dwellings described by 291 property-level and household-level snapshot features, with 8,580 recorded positives and 56,634 unlabelled cases. We develop and evaluate a two-stage sample-selection PU framework: an out-of-fold XGBoost scorer first identifies conservative reliable negatives, and weighted Stage-2 classifiers then combine positives, reliable negatives, and weakly weighted residual unlabelled cases. The Stage-1 scorer achieved an out-of-fold development-set PU-AUC of 0.7547. The selected Stage-2 XGBoost model achieved a held-out PU-AUC of 0.7760 and average precision of 0.2981, and increased Recall@20% from 44.0% to 47.0%, retrieving 51 additional recorded positives compared with the Stage-1-only scorer. Supervised XGBoost baselines achieved similar recorded-label performance, while Stage-1 learner ablation showed that the framework supported alternative reliable-negative selectors. Grouped SHAP analysis connected the fitted scores to heating and fuel systems, household and occupancy context, assessment status, dwelling characteristics and energy performance. Targeted predictor exclusion reduced PU-AUC to 0.7648 and Recall@20% to 43.6%, quantifying dependence on selected inputs without resolving their temporal availability. These findings provide an empirical basis for PU-based recorded-risk prioritisation in housing, combining improved ranking over the initial scorer, explicit control over unlabelled training data and interpretation through housing-domain feature groups.

Article.Title: Investigation of multi-DOF WEC S-shaped buoy configurations in the nearshore region of East China
Article.Authors: Ali Mohieldin H.; Sun Z.; Sun Y.; Han P.; Kang J.; Abdelrahman M.
Article.Abstract: This study proposes a multi-DOF WEC employing S-shaped buoy profiles and a mechanically integrated PTO system tuned for site-specific nearshore wave conditions. The system uses heave and coupled surge/pitch motions, while the proposed PTO mechanism mechanically synthesizes the corresponding modal responses into a unified transmission path and represents their damping contributions through a single equivalent PTO damping coefficient. The hydrodynamic responses were calculated using ANSYS AQWA, whereas the PTO dynamics and absorbed power have been evaluated in Matlab/Simscape. The natural multi-mode periods have been tuned to align the system response with the most frequently occurring peak-period interval at the selected site. Site-specific performance has been subsequently determined using the normalized joint probability distribution to account for the complete location wave distribution, including the high-probability design range and all off-resonance sea states. The results demonstrate that all multi-DOF configurations outperform their corresponding single-DOF heave only models, although the improvement is strongly dependent on buoy geometry since the normalized occurrence weighted mean absorbed-power enhancement ranges from 14.8 to 40.6%. The optimum configuration achieved a mean absorbed power of 4.95 kW and a mean capture width ratio of 23.14%, compared with 3.52 kW and 16.50%, respectively, for its single-DOF counterpart. The findings demonstrate that combining site-specific hydrodynamic tuning, buoy-shape optimization, and multi-mode PTO integration can substantially improve wave energy capture over realistic operating conditions.

Article.Title: Evaluating and enhancing the geotechnical properties of clay–wood ash and clay–sawdust composites using RSM and ANN
Article.Authors: Chaouche Y.; Bencheikh M.; Aidoud A.; Boumaaza M.; Belaadi A.; Bourchak M.; Ercetin A.; Ghernaout D.; Mukalazi H.
Article.Abstract: This study examines the mechanical and geotechnical performance of expansive clayey soil stabilized with sustainable agro-industrial by-products. The experimental program evaluates the effects of incorporating wood sawdust (WS) and wood ash (WA) at dosages of 2% to 10%, both individually and in combination with a fixed 2% addition of Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC). Comprehensive laboratory characterization included Atterberg limits, methylene blue value, hydrometer analysis, compaction characteristics determined by the Standard Proctor test. Direct shear testing was conducted to determine cohesion (c) and the internal friction angle Φ), while California bearing ratio (CBR) and unconfined compressive strength (UCS) were evaluated as key mechanical properties. Soil responses were modeled using response surface methodology (RSM) and artificial neural networks (ANNs). The mixture containing 8% WA and 2% OPC showed the greatest mechanical improvement relative to the untreated natural clay baseline, increasing CBR by 389.34% and UCS by 335.50%. while significantly enhancing shear strength parameters. Both ANN/Genetic Algorithm (GA) and RSM/Desirability function effectively identified mixes that maximized CBR and UCS, although ANN/GA provided superior prediction accuracy and closer alignment with the model-based optimum. These findings support the use of optimized clay-based biocomposites incorporating WA, WS, and OPC for sustainable foundation engineering, soil stabilization, and pavement subgrade enhancement.

Article.Title: Field testing the influence of settlement recesses and nighttime feeding lights on coral recruitment
Article.Authors: Jorissen H.; Reichert J.; Dixon S.; Madin E.; Madin C.; Asbury M.; Nims A.; Rottmueller M.; Rova L.; N/A N/A.; Grottoli A.; Madin J.
Article.Abstract: Previous studies show that two promising technologies can increase recruitment probability and survival: (i) helix recesses for entraining coral larvae and (ii) night-time feeding lights for improving subsequent survival. We evaluated whether these technologies can be combined to improve coral settlement and survival under in situ reef conditions on concrete restoration modules designed for a large-scale hybrid reef deployment in Hawaiʻi. During a 6-month experiment in Kāneʻohe Bay, recesses dramatically improved initial natural larval entrainment, but specific recess depths and light intensities had little effect on survival of settlers 2 months after settlement. After 6 months, survival was significantly higher in deeper recesses. Higher survival was likely associated with increased protection from algal competition and predation; although increased heterotrophic food availability in shaded microhabitats may contribute to recruit persistence, this mechanism could not be confirmed due to experimental limitations. Integration of these technologies is straightforward and can be incorporated into coastal engineering structures to accelerate coral growth in local, high-value coastal areas.

Article.Title: Antimicrobial resistance and pathogenicity islands in mucosa-associated Escherichia coli in colorectal cancer patients
Article.Authors: El-Gendy Y.; El-Farrash M.; Eldesoky M.; El-Mahdy R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most prevalent adult cancers. Escherichia coli may contribute to CRC development and progression through its virulence factors and inflammatory pathways. E. coli acquires antibiotic resistance easily; however, the antibiotic resistance in mucosa-associated E. coli in CRC is still undefined. This study aims to determine the prevalence and distribution of pathogenicity islands (PAI) and antibiotic resistance in mucosa-associated E. coli i solated from CRC patients compared to colorectal adenoma (CRA) and the healthy control group. This cross-sectional study included 63 mucosa-associated E. coli isolated from colorectal biopsies of 21 CRC, 7 CRA and 35 healthy control individuals. Antibiotic susceptibility was performed by the disk diffusion method. PAI (pks, PAI I-IV536, PAI I-IICFT073 and PAI I , IIJ96 ) and Beta-lactamase genes (carbapenemase genes, CTX-M gene) were detected by PCR. More than one PAI was detected in (90.5%, 57%, 68.5%,) of mucosa-associated E. coli isolated from CRC, CRA, and control, respectively. The pks and PAI IV536 were the most common PAI among our isolates. There is no significant difference in antibiotic resistance between pKs- positive E. coli isolates and the pks- negative -E. coli isolates. Resistance to Ampicillin, Ceftazidime, Aztreonam, Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and Cefepime was significantly higher in mucosa-associated E. coli in CRC patients than in normal subjects. NDM and OXA48 were the most common carbapenemase genes detected in all studied groups. The CTX-M gene was detected in 41.3% of all the isolated mucosa-associated E. coli . High prevalence of multiple PAIs and multiple drug resistance in mucosa-associated E. coli in both colorectal neoplasia and normal individuals. Significantly higher prevalence of PAI IV536 and resistance to Ampicillin, Ceftazidime, Aztreonam, Cefuroxime, Trimethoprim- sulfamethoxazole and Cefepime in mucosa-associated E. coli of CRC compared to healthy subjects. We recommend raising awareness of antibiotic resistance, strategies to prevent the spread of antibiotic resistance, such as surveillance, improving sanitation and further study to assess the effect of antibiotic use on colonic E. coli in CRC.

Article.Title: Seizure quality in bilateral electroconvulsive therapy: the influence of hyperventilation, electrode placement, and anesthesia
Article.Authors: Paetow R.; Frodl T.; Hill A.; Grözinger M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is an effective psychiatric treatment and relies on an iatrogenically induced, generalized seizure. Seizure quality scores have been developed to predict treatment outcomes of ECT. Its intensity can be governed by various parameters like electrode placement, anesthesia, and the systemic levels of CO₂. The aim of this retrospective study was to investigate whether reducing end-tidal CO₂ (etCO₂) through hyperventilation prior to ECT seizure would improve seizure quality score considering electrode placement and anesthetic agent. Case notes from 2023 were reviewed and seizure quality scores, pre-seizure etCO₂, electrode placement, and anesthetic agent were obtained. The resulting 732 ECTs from 68 patients were analyzed. Lower etCO₂ and its interaction with main anesthetic agent and different bilateral electrode placement were not significantly associated with improved seizure quality overall. Higher age was associated with a decrease in seizure quality (β = -0.03, SE = 0.01, z = − 5.58, p < .001). Post-hoc power analysis indicated sample sizes of at least 400 patients to detect isolated etCO 2 effects. Seizure quality should be understood as a complex interplay of technical, neurophysiological, and patient-related factors. Large and standardized multicenter studies are needed to explore the influence of treatment protocols on seizure quality.

Article.Title: Latent tuberculosis infection among hemodialysis patients in a national multi-governorate screening initiative in Egypt
Article.Authors: Amin W.; Ashmawy R.; Hassan M.; El-Maradny Y.; Elsawy N.; Gebili S.; Ghazy R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Patients with end-stage renal disease receiving maintenance hemodialysis are at increased risk of developing active tuberculosis (TB) and are therefore, considered a priority population for latent tuberculosis infection (LTBI) screening and management. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of LTBI and identify factors independently associated with QuantiFERON-TB Gold Plus (QFT-Plus) positivity among patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis in 13 selected governorates in Egypt. A retrospective registry-based cross-sectional study was conducted using records from the Egyptian Tuberculosis Health Initiative collected between November 2022 and December 2023 from designated screening facilities. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize the data, and between-group comparisons were performed using the Chi-square test and analysis of variance (ANOVA), as appropriate. Multivariable logistic regression and generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) were applied to identify factors independently associated with QFT-Plus positivity. Geographic distribution was visualized using a choropleth map generated with ArcGIS Desktop version 10.8. Among the 18,060 screened individuals, 3668 (20.31%) had positive QFT-Plus results when calculated using all tested participants as the denominator. Among participants with determinate results ( n = 16,477), the QFT-Plus positivity rate was 22.26%, while 1583 (8.77%) had indeterminate results. In the GLMM analysis, older age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.03, 95% CI 1.02–1.03; p < 0.001), male sex (aOR = 1.59, 95% CI 1.47–1.72; p < 0.001), and smoking (aOR = 1.21, 95% CI 1.05–1.41; p = 0.011) were significant factors associated with QFT-Plus positivity after adjustment for diabetes, hypertension, infection with human immunodeficiency virus, hepatitis C virus, and hepatitis B virus, region, and patient load, while accounting for clustering at the governorate level. Descriptive geographic mapping showed substantial geographic variation in LTBI prevalence across governorates. Regional QFT-Plus positivity among participants with determinate QFT-Plus results was similar in Nile Delta (22.5%) and Upper Egypt (21.7%), although marked heterogeneity was observed. The highest positivity rates were reported in Luxor (27.1%) and Sharqiya (25.7%). Geographic variation was also observed in indeterminate QFT-Plus results. These findings support further evaluation of structured LTBI screening and follow-up pathways within renal care services, particularly for older male patients and smokers. Targeted surveillance strategies may facilitate identification of individuals at increased risk and help inform future TB prevention policies in this population. Additional prospective studies should evaluate treatment uptake, progression to active TB, clinical benefit, cost-effectiveness, and optimal screening strategies.

Article.Title: Development of a clinical prediction model for overall survival in locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
Article.Authors: Koide Y.; Ishihara S.; Wakabayashi K.; Abe S.; Hanai N.; Ozawa T.; Ito M.; Shimizu H.; Aoyama T.; Noguchi M.; Tachibana H.; Kodaira T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To develop and validate a machine-learning–based prediction model for overall survival (OS) in locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (LA-HNSCC) that integrates both surgery-based and chemoradiotherapy (CRT) cohorts within a single framework. A total of 1,005 LA-HNSCC patients receiving curative-intent surgery-based treatment or CRT were retrospectively assembled from a domestic multicenter cohort ( n = 678) and publicly available datasets from The Cancer Imaging Archive ( n = 327). Candidate predictors were pre-specified from routinely available clinical variables. Elastic net regularization with 10-fold cross-validation was applied for variable selection and weighting, followed by a multivariable Cox proportional hazards model. Elastic net selected 12 variables, of which p16 status, performance status, nodal stage, serum albumin, T stage, and age were most influential. The model showed good discrimination (C-index 0.73), with time-dependent AUCs of 0.78–0.73 across 1–5 years and good calibration at 1 and 3 years. Decision curve analysis confirmed clinical utility across relevant threshold probabilities in both cohorts. By relying on prognostic factors common to both surgery-based treatment and CRT, this interpretable model demonstrated stable performance and may support prognostic risk stratification applicable across treatment modalities in LA-HNSCC.

Article.Title: Urinary kisspeptin as a non-invasive reproductive biomarker in crossbred cattle and black Bengal does
Article.Authors: Gogoi J.; Mondal M.; Karunakaran M.; Reena Y.; Kuri P.
Article.Abstract: Kisspeptin is an upstream regulator of the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis and plays a critical role in the estrous cycle and pregnancy in domestic animals. The KISS1 gene, also known as the "metastatin" gene, has emerged as a promising diagnostic biomarker in reproductive physiology across livestock species. This study aims to explore the dynamics of urinary/plasma kisspeptin and their creatinine-normalized ratio during the bovine and caprine estrous cycle and pregnancy. Experimental animals comprised two groups (cyclic and pregnant). The cyclic group consisted of 12 cyclic crossbred cows and 12 cyclic black Bengal does, and the pregnant group consisted of 12 pregnant crossbred cows and 12 pregnant black Bengal does. Early-morning fresh urine and blood samples were collected from each cyclic animal group on Day 0, 6, 12, and 21 of the estrous cycle, and at fortnightly intervals from each pregnant animal group for estimation of urinary and plasma kisspeptin. Urinary and plasma kisspeptin were estimated using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and urinary and plasma creatinine values were estimated using the alkaline picrate method. Two-way repeated-measures analysis ofvariance was used to analyze the samples, followed by regression analysis and student’s t-test to assess significant differences between non-pregnant and pregnant animals. Further receiver operating curve analysis was used to assess the diagnostic performance of urinary and plasma kisspeptin and their creatinine-normalized ratios. The results obtained for the said objective revealed that urinary kisspeptin levels showed a qualitatively similar trend to plasma kisspeptin (r=0.99) during the estrous cycle in crossbred cattle and black Bengal does. The highest concentration of UKP (2.45 ± 0.21ng/ml and 2.44 ± 0.08 ng/ml) was recorded during the proestrus stage of the estrous cycle of both crossbred cows and black Bengal does. The highest plasma kisspeptin-to-creatinine ratios were also observed on Day 21 (14.49 ± 0.91 and 16.22 ± 1.53), whereas the corresponding urinary kisspeptin-to-creatinine ratios reached 11.84 ± 0.70 and 7.47 ± 0.34, respectively, in crossbred cattle and black Bengal does. Plasma and urinary kisspeptin concentrations were found to increase significantly (P<0.05) from early through late pregnancy (4.28 ± 0.19 to 33.40 ± 0.78; 2.01± 0.10 ng/ml to 23.01 ± 0.54 ng/ml) in crossbred cows and black Bengal goats (3.49 ± 0.53 to 30.50 ± 1.26 ng/mL; 1.68 ± 0.01 to 19.84 ± 0.82 ng/mL), respectively. The PKP/PC ratio (134.9 ± 10.96; 127.30 ± 6.62) was found to be significantly higher (P < 0.01) during late pregnancy than the UKP/UC ratio (71.94 ± 10.63; 68.4 ± 6.70 ng/ml) in crossbred cattle and black Bengal goats. The results of our study revealed that kisspeptin can be detected in the urine of cyclic and pregnant domestic animals, such as crossbred cattle and black Bengal does, and that its ratio to creatinine can serve as a reliable diagnostic marker for predicting ovulation and pregnancy in crossbred cows and black Bengal does.

Article.Title: Effects of clinically available HIF-PH inhibitors on retinal Vegfa transcription
Article.Authors: Hoshino J.; Irie K.; Konishi A.; Akiyama H.; Minamishima Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) plays a central role in the cellular response to hypoxia and is negatively regulated under normoxic conditions by prolyl hydroxylase domain-containing proteins (PHDs), also referred to as HIF prolyl hydroxylases (HIF-PHs). HIF-PH inhibitors induce erythropoietin (EPO) expression by activating HIF and are widely used for the treatment of renal anemia; however, their effects on intraocular vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) expression remain unclear. In this study, we examined the effects of all five HIF-PH inhibitors (roxadustat, daprodustat, vadadustat, enarodustat, and molidustat) on Vegfa expression in the retina in mice. C57BL/6 J mice were orally administered each inhibitor. Six hours after administration, the kidney, retina, and liver were collected, and transcription levels were quantified by real-time reverse transcription PCR (real-time RT-PCR). Renal Epo transcription was significantly increased by molidustat (P < 0.01), roxadustat (P < 0.01), and enarodustat (P < 0.05) significantly increased renal Epo transcription. Retinal Vegfa transcription was significantly increased by four inhibitors (P < 0.01), with molidustat showing no significant effect. In the liver, Vegfa transcription was increased by daprodustat (P < 0.05) and vadadustat (P < 0.01). No significant correlation was observed between renal Epo and retinal Vegfa transcription levels for any of the HIF-PH inhibitors. These findings indicate that HIF-PH inhibitors differentially regulate hypoxia-responsive genes across tissues and suggest that their potential effects on retinal Vegfa transcription should be considered when evaluating their ocular safety.

Article.Title: Dissecting genomic regions and candidate genes for root traits at the seedling stage under cold stress in rice
Article.Authors: Singh G.; Mondal S.; Iqbal R.; Shaik R.; Jyoti S.; Debsharma S.; Lakshmi V.; Harper C.; Talukder S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Root system architecture (RSA) is crucial for plant growth under abiotic stress including cold stress (CS) in rice and capturing RSA variation under CS is a key strategy for improving cold tolerance (CT). This study aims to identify the genomic regions associated with RSA traits under CS in 204 diverse rice germplasms. Two growth environments were used: growth chamber (E1; 10°C in 1–2 weeks, followed by 17°C during weeks 3–4) and controlled greenhouse (E2; 28–30°C night/day). A total of 2448 roots were harvested four weeks after planting, and four plant biomasses, along with eight RSA traits, were measured using WinRhizo Pro. Significant phenotypic variations were observed for study traits. 8,54,832 polymorphic SNPs were used for GWAS using the FarmCPU model within the ‘rMVP’ package and 143 QTNs were identified (87 in E1 and 56 in E2) associated with the studied traits. Among the identified QTNs, 49 novel QTNs were multi-trait (≥ two traits), which were further used for candidate genes identification, resulting in 74 putative genes within ± 100 kb genomic regions. Key candidate genes ( OsBRD1/OsDWARF , MHZ11 , and OsSNDP1 ) supporting the rice root adaptation under CS by coordinated brassinosteroid biosynthesis, ethylene signaling, and phospholipid-mediated root hair development, whereas OsPP2C27 , OsNIP1;2 , OsNAR2.1 , OsMYB305 , OsSWEET3a , and OsHMA7 genes play important roles in stress signaling, nutrient uptake, growth regulation, and root development. Overall, this study provides the foundation of novel insights for improving rice CT by RSA.

Article.Title: External validation of a machine learning model for predicting liver injury in children with mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia
Article.Authors: Yu Y.; Jing Y.; Tang Y.; Liu F.; Wei H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP) is associated with a high risk of liver injury, which adversely affects clinical outcomes and healthcare costs. Early identification of at-risk children remains challenging, and no validated predictive tool is currently available. This multicenter retrospective study included 1321 children with MPP from two centers in Nanjing, China. The development cohort was randomly split into training (67%) and test (33%) sets, with an independent external validation cohort (n = 640) from another hospital. Liver injury was defined as alanine aminotransferase (ALT) > 80 U/L. Feature selection was performed using the boruta algorithm, and ten machine learning algorithms were developed and evaluated. Model performance was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy (ACC), sensitivity, specificity, calibration metrics, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The SHAP method was used for model interpretation. Among 1321 patients, 55 (4.2%) developed liver injury. The boruta algorithm identified six predictors: LDH, D-dimer, CK, age, IL-6, and CK-MB. The neural network (nnet) model demonstrated optimal performance, with AUC values of 0.914 in the training set, 0.829 in the test set, and 0.755 in the external validation set. The model showed acceptable calibration and modest clinical utility on decision curve analysis. SHAP analysis revealed LDH as the most important predictor. An interactive web-based application was developed to facilitate clinical implementation. We developed and validated a machine learning-based model using six readily available predictors that identifies children with MPP at risk for liver injury. The accompanying web-based tool may assist clinicians in early risk stratification and timely intervention.

Article.Title: Clinical features, epidemiology, and survival of patients with core binding factor acute myeloid leukemia in the SEER database
Article.Authors: Liu S.; Lin Y.; Shen J.
Article.Abstract: Core binding factor acute myeloid leukemia (CBF-AML) (RUNX1::RUNX1T1 or CBFB::MYH11) is a favorable-risk but heterogenous subtype of acute myeloid leukemia (AML). However, understanding of its epidemiology, clinical characteristics, and prognosis is limited. A total of 70,912 records of adults with AML, including 947 with CBFB::MYH11 and 1,285 with RUNX1::RUNX1T1 CBF-AML were extracted from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database (2000–2023) and analyzed. Incidence trends were assessed using the annual percent change (APC); prognostic factors were identified using multivariable Cox regression; and survival was compared between groups using the Kaplan–Meier method. The CBFB::MYH11 and RUNX1::RUNX1T1 subtypes accounted for 1.3% and 1.8% of cases of AML, respectively, and incidence was higher in men and adults aged < 60 years. The incidence of CBF-AML increased significantly during the study period (APC 2.84% for CBFB::MYH11 and 2.89% for RUNX1::RUNX1T1 subtypes). Sex, age, and chemotherapy were independent predictors of overall survival (OS) in both subtypes. Second malignant neoplasm (SMN) was associated with poorer cancer-specific survival (CSS), and radiotherapy was associated with poorer OS in patients with RUNX1::RUNX1T1 AML. Patients with CBFB::MYH11 AML had longer OS and CSS than those with RUNX1::RUNX1T1 AML, but CSS did not differ significantly by subtype in patients aged ≥ 60 years. Untreated patients had a median OS of 1 month. The prognosis of CBF-AML is generally favorable but differs by subtype. Age, chemotherapy, and SMN are key predictors of survival. Timely diagnosis and initiation of chemotherapy is critical, especially in older patients.

Article.Title: A disentangled CNN–transformer framework for big data-driven intelligent brand visual generation
Article.Authors: Jiang Y.; Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: Big data has driven the rapid growth of brand visual design demand, yet existing intelligent generation methods suffer from detail distortion and poor cross-cultural adaptability. This study proposes a style-disentangled Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-Transformer framework for intelligent brand visual generation. A dual-branch architecture extracts local details via CNN and global style via Transformer, with an embedding mixer enabling balanced feature fusion. A regional gating and style calibration module further enhances structural fidelity. Evaluated on a self-constructed 10-brand multimodal dataset, the model outperforms state-of-the-art methods on Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity (LPIPS) (0.186) and Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) (0.924), with style consistency exceeding 85% across cross-cultural scenarios. Ablation studies have shown that, compared with the full model, only the CNN branch increases LPIPS by 54.3%, confirming the contribution of key modules. This work provides an effective solution for big data-driven intelligent brand design and extends computational creativity applications.

Article.Title: Integral resonant filter-based chattering reduction in switched human-robot interaction with hybrid admittance-adaptive impedance control
Article.Authors: Haruna A.; Abdullahi A.; Chaichaowarat R.
Article.Abstract: Physical human-robot interaction (pHRI) is a type of interaction that implies that robots should demonstrate dynamic and compliant behavior that is dependent on the interaction environment. A prominent solution is compliant control, which includes either Admittance Control in the case of soft contact or Impedance Control for stiff contact. However, if the nature of the environment is unknown or dynamic, then a hybrid control scheme that switches between the admittance and impedance regimes is adopted. However, switching from admittance to impedance and vice versa results in discontinuity in the control signal. The discontinuity inherent in the abrupt switching mechanism causes high-frequency oscillations (chattering) in the control signal. The effect of this phenomenon is poor performance of the system, mechanical stress, and high energy consumption. To effectively attenuate this chattering and its negative effects, this work proposes an Integral Resonant Control (IRC) command filter, which is incorporated into the switching loop of the hybrid admittance and adaptive impedance control. The IRC filter, normally employed to damp structural vibrations, is designed here to act as a command filter for robust signal smoothing by damping the high-frequency components of the control signal introduced by the switching action. The proposed hybrid controller is compared to a standard hysteresis (dead-zone) chattering mitigation strategy. Comparative simulation results indicate that the proposed filtering technique can reduce the Chattering Index on average by over 76% for both joints of a planar rehabilitation robot while maintaining trajectory tracking accuracy. The results obtained indicate that the proposed switched hybrid control is Lyapunov stable and can be employed to achieve effective, energy-efficient, and compliant robotic rehabilitation in uncertain environments.

Article.Authors: Yang N.; Mu J.; Liu Y.; Guo W.; Sun C.; Peng B.; Xiang J.; Deng L.; Fan W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate intraocular lens (IOL) power selection remains challenging in cataract eyes with long axial length, altered corneal geometry, or previous corneal refractive surgery. SHAP analysis identified target refraction, axial length, and IOL power as dominant predictors. Post-refractive eyes, very long eyes, and flat corneas remained difficult. These findings support cautious, locally validated use of AI-based formulas and interpretable machine learning in refractive cataract surgery.

Participants ( N = 2,576, aged 35–45) completed online tests and questionnaires, while students rated occupational requirements. For each occupation, the population sex composition of people with traits in line with requirements was estimated, using trait sex differences and occupational requirement profiles. Estimates were highly predictive of actual population sex ratios, with the model assessing interest and cognition in conjunction explaining the most variance ( R 2 = .49), followed by the interest model ( R 2 = .46) and the cognition model ( R 2 = .18). Among individual traits, sex differences in interest in things were by far the most predictive ( R 2 = .42). Notably, sex differences in cognition were more predictive of high proportions of men in occupations than high proportions of women. Given lifespan trait stability, these results suggest that cognition and interests matter in occupational choice, with sex differences consequently contributing substantially to occupational sex segregation.

Article.Title: Empagliflozin does not rescue nor exacerbate doxorubicin-induced skeletal muscle wasting and metabolic dysfunction in male mice
Article.Authors: Van Asbroeck B.; Dombrecht D.; Dalle S.; Van Craenenbroeck E.; Guns P.; van Breda E.
Article.Abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX) can induce skeletal muscle and white adipose tissue (WAT) wasting, contributing to treatment-related body mass loss, functional decline and compromised treatment efficacy. Impaired protein turnover and energy metabolism have been proposed as contributing mechanisms. Sodium–glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) induce glucosuria and systemic metabolic adaptations that may improve skeletal muscle protein homeostasis and metabolic regulation. Concurrently, the glucosuria-induced caloric loss associated with SGLT2is may interfere with tissue wasting. This study investigated whether empagliflozin (EMPA) modifies DOX-induced tissue wasting in male mice. C57BL/6J mice ( n = 36) were randomized to control, EMPA, DOX, or DOX-EMPA groups. DOX (4 mg/kg/week, intraperitoneally) and EMPA (10 mg/kg/day, oral gavage) were administered for 6-weeks. Whole-body energy metabolism was assessed by indirect calorimetry, followed by tissue weight and molecular analyses in skeletal muscle and WAT. EMPA neither attenuated nor exacerbated DOX-induced body weight, skeletal muscle, or WAT loss. Despite effective glucosuria, EMPA did not increase non-fasted circulating β-hydroxybutyrate levels or meaningfully modify DOX-associated alterations in whole-body energy metabolism, tissue wasting, molecular markers of skeletal muscle protein turnover and metabolic regulation, or metabolic and stress-related gene expression in WAT. In conclusion, EMPA did not protect against DOX-induced tissue wasting and associated metabolic dysfunction, nor did it aggravate these effects.

Article.Authors: Cosentino J.; Tassino B.; Estevan I.
Article.Abstract: Shift work disrupts sleep patterns and is associated with adverse health outcomes, yet the role of chronotype in shaping shift workers’ sleep behavior remains underexplored. We assessed sleep timing, duration, napping, and chronotype using an abbreviated Munich Chronotype Questionnaire for shift workers. Night and morning shifts produced the largest shifts in sleep timing and the greatest restriction in sleep duration. Workday sleep was shorter, and napping was more frequent, during morning and night shifts than during the afternoon shift and days off. Participants were predominantly evening-oriented. Chronotype strongly modulated sleep patterns: evening-oriented workers slept longer during night and afternoon shifts and days off, and napped longer on morning workdays. A 1-hour delay in chronotype was associated with 6–25 min of additional sleep. Weekly average 24-hour sleep duration remained below recommended levels during morning and night shifts (~ 7 h) but exceeded 8 h during the afternoon shift, with longer sleep among later chronotypes. These findings identify chronotype as a key factor shaping sleep under shift work and support its consideration in shift scheduling to improve sleep health and reduce the adverse effects of shift work.

Averaged across seasons and plant densities, fresh herbage yield increased from 4.98 to 8.97 t ha −1 and dry herbage yield from 2.15 to 4.76 t ha −1 between the control and 150 kg N ha −1 treatments (nitrogen main effects: P < 0.0001). Conversely, leaf essential oil content decreased from 0.47 to 0.35%, and flower essential oil content from 2.43 to 1.84% ( P < 0.0001). Fresh leaf ratio was not significantly affected by nitrogen dose ( P = 0.6233), although dry leaf and flower ratios increased. Significant season × density × nitrogen interactions for herbage yield indicate that treatment responses depended on the combination of these factors. The 2022 season generally produced greater biomass and higher organ-specific essential oil contents than 2021. The results indicate contrasting responses of biomass production and organ-specific oil content to nitrogen supply within the tested treatments; the underlying physiological mechanisms were not measured.

Article.Title: Plasma-treated porous carriers for modulating clove essential oil release against Tropilaelaps mites in Apis mellifera colonies
Article.Authors: Boonmee T.; Sinpoo C.; Wongthaveethong L.; Kamyo T.; Songsri S.; Pettis J.; Chaimanee V.
Article.Abstract: Tropilaelaps mites are among the most destructive ectoparasites of Apis mellifera. The application of essential oil-based acaricides to control their populations is limited by rapid volatilization and short persistence under hive conditions. This study investigated pumice and ceramic balls treated with argon or helium non-thermal atmospheric pressure plasma (NTAPP), with or without water vapor, to modify the evaporation profile of clove essential oil for Tropilaelaps mite control. Plasma treatment did not significantly affect clove essential oil adsorption capacity (0.0072–0.0092 μL mg −1 and 0.0049–0.0065 μL mg −1 for pumice and ceramic balls, respectively). However, the He + H 2 O-treated ceramic ball exhibited significantly slower evaporation during days 2–8, although all treatments reached approximately 52–54% cumulative evaporation after 14 days. In laboratory bioassays using 5% clove essential oil, mite mortality differed between plasma-treated and untreated ceramic balls during the initial 30 min of exposure for the 0 and 24 h evaporation periods. However, both treatments resulted in 100% mite mortality after 3 h of exposure across all evaporation periods (0, 6, and 24 h). Adult bee survival was comparable between the two treatments but differed from the control. During the 28-day field trial, colonies treated with 5% clove essential oil-loaded ceramic balls showed numerically lower mite infestation than those treated with formic acid, with comparable adult bee populations and no significant differences among treatments. Overall, plasma surface modification modulated the evaporation profile of clove essential oil without compromising its acaricidal activity, supporting the potential use of plasma-treated porous carriers as delivery systems for Tropilaelaps mite management.

Article.Title: Causal-enhanced federated transfer learning framework for privacy-preserving cross-organizational strategic collaboration
Article.Authors: Fu G.
Article.Abstract: Cross-organizational strategic collaboration increasingly demands data-driven coordination while confronting stringent privacy constraints and heterogeneous data distributions. This paper proposes a coupled framework integrating causal inference with federated transfer learning to enable effective knowledge sharing across organizational boundaries without centralizing sensitive data. The framework comprises three core components: a distributed causal discovery algorithm that reconstructs inter-organizational causal structures through secure aggregation protocols, a causal-enhanced federated transfer learning mechanism that identifies invariant features transferable across heterogeneous enterprise contexts, and an adaptive privacy computing architecture that dynamically allocates protection resources according to data sensitivity profiles. Experimental validation across multi-enterprise ecosystems demonstrates that the causal enhancement mechanism improves cross-domain generalization robustness by 43% compared to conventional federated transfer learning, while maintaining predictive accuracy within 6.2% of centralized approaches. The adaptive privacy architecture retains 93.7% of collaborative utility under meaningful privacy constraints, with membership inference attack success rates near random baseline. These results establish that properly designed federated frameworks can approach centralized performance while preserving organizational autonomy, enabling broader participation in data-driven strategic alliances across regulatory and competitive boundaries.

Article.Title: Inter-individual variation in cisplatin-induced liver injury is associated with hepatic platinum accumulation and GSH/GST-dependent defense in male mice
Article.Authors: Jeon S.; Nam K.; Park Y.; Ryu D.
Article.Abstract: Cisplatin is a platinum-based chemotherapeutic agent whose clinical use is limited by toxicity in non-tumor tissues. Even among genetically homogeneous mice receiving the same dose, hepatic responses to cisplatin vary considerably, but the biochemical basis of this variability remains unclear. Male mice received a single intraperitoneal dose of cisplatin, and hepatic injury was evaluated using serum alanine aminotransferase (ALT) activity. Cisplatin significantly increased serum ALT activity, with marked inter-individual variability among treated mice. Within the cisplatin-treated group, higher serum ALT activity was associated with higher hepatic platinum retention and oxidative protein damage, whereas lower serum ALT activity was associated with higher glutathione S -transferase (GST) activities toward multiple substrates, increased GSTP1/2 expression, higher reduced glutathione (GSH) content and GSH/GSSG ratio, and greater glutamate-cysteine ligase (GCL) activity and GCLC expression. Notably, several parameters, including reduced GSH content and GCL activity, showed no significant differences between the control and cisplatin-treated groups, highlighting biochemical patterns that were apparent primarily at the individual level. These findings suggest that inter-individual differences in hepatic platinum handling and GSH/GST-dependent defense capacity are associated with variability in cisplatin-induced hepatotoxicity and emphasize the biological significance of within-group variability in experimental toxicology.

Article.Title: Neuropsychiatric symptom clusters across the cognitive impairment spectrum in advanced age: a data-driven analysis integrating AD biomarker and clinical profiling
Article.Authors: Chatzikostopoulos A.; Moraitou D.; Pateras K.; Manafi G.; Tsolaki A.; Papantoniou G.; Katsouri I.; Sofologi M.; Tsentidou G.; Papadopoulos E.; Tsolaki M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Neuropsychiatric symptoms (NPS) are among the most common manifestations of cognitive impairment, yet their heterogeneity complicates understanding of how they relate to Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathology. While individual NPS have been linked to AD biomarker burden, the interplay between co-occurring neuropsychiatric profiles and AD biomarkers in shaping cognitive and functional outcomes remains insufficiently understood. This study used data-driven clustering to identify NPS clusters in 300 individuals (156 mild cognitive impairment, 112 AD dementia, 32 non-AD dementia) using the 12 domains of Neuropsychiatric Inventory. K-means clustering identified three clusters: Minimal/No NPS (55.7%), Apathy-Behavioral Dysregulation (17.7%), and Depression-Anxiety/Affective (26.7%). Clusters differed significantly in age, sex, education, cognitive status, and diagnostic composition (all p < .05). The Apathy-Behavioral cluster showed advanced cognitive impairment and AD/non-AD dementia predominance, whereas the Depression-Anxiety cluster showed preserved cognition, female predominance, and highest vascular risk factor prevalence. Measured AD pathology (plasma pTau217, CSF amyloid and tau) did not differ across clusters, whereas APOE ε4 carriership was higher in the two symptomatic clusters (both 44.4% vs. 26.0%; p = .032), an association that did not persist after multivariable adjustment. Hierarchical regression revealed five of eight biomarker-outcome associations were largely independent of NPS clusters (change < 10%), with exceptions involving functional outcome: pTau217 (11.4%), tau (17.7%), and APOE ε4 (29.6%). Findings are consistent with a parallel-pathway hypothesis: measured AD pathology and NPS clusters showed largely independent associations with cognition, with only partial overlap in their associations with functional status.

Article.Title: Integrated transcriptomics and network toxicology suggests core targets and potential mechanisms of aspartame-related breast carcinogenesis
Article.Authors: Wang Z.; Bao H.; Zhan X.; Ma Q.; Wei J.; Wu J.
Article.Abstract: Aspartame (APM) is a globally prevalent low-calorie artificial sweetener. Although its long-term health risks have garnered increasing attention, the potential molecular targets and pathways linking APM exposure to breast cancer remain largely unexplored. In this study, we integrated network toxicology and transcriptomics with multiple computational approaches, including machine learning, molecular docking, and clinical validation, to predictively prioritize candidate targets and pathways potentially involved in APM‑related breast carcinogenesis. We acquired 226 APM targets and 1973 breast cancer genes, from which 46 overlapping potential targets were extracted. Functional enrichment analyses revealed that these targets were mainly enriched in biological processes related to cell proliferation and migration, as well as multiple cancer‑associated signaling pathways, including transcriptional misregulation in cancer, TNF, and IL-17. Using a multi-algorithm machine learning model, we further prioritized 5 core targets with favorable diagnostic performance and stable predictive ability. SHAP analysis was performed on the core targets, and virtual gene knockout was conducted for the gene with the most significant contribution. Finally, TCGA datasets further confirmed the differential expression of these core targets across breast cancer subtypes and normal tissues. Collectively, these computational findings provide a prioritized list of molecular candidates and a hypothesis‑generating basis for future experimental and mechanistic studies on APM and breast cancer.

Article.Title: Early Nrf2/HO-1 signaling activation following surgical decompression in a rat model of lumbar spinal stenosis-induced neurogenic intermittent claudication
Article.Authors: Liu D.; Wen H.; Fu M.; Gao J.; Gao C.; Li L.; Li J.; Feng M.; Sun W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lumbar spinal stenosis is a prevalent degenerative disease globally. The hallmark symptom is neurogenic intermittent claudication, characterized by lower extremity pain during walking that is relieved by resting.Although mechanical constriction initiates the primary pathology, the precise molecular orchestration underlying this transient, rest-induced symptomatic resolution has not yet been fully characterized. We established a cauda equina compression model in Sprague-Dawley rats using epidural silicone implants. Multiple groups were designed to evaluate behavioral, histological, and molecular changes across the acute and chronic compression phases, as well as designated post-decompression recovery windows. Chronic compression induced functional impairment, structural injury, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammation. At 2 h after surgical decompression, Nrf2 showed increased nuclear localization together with early upregulation of Ho-1, Nqo1, and Gclc. Under continued compression, SFN improved selected functional and molecular injury indices, whereas ML385 treatment was associated with worsened neurological, inflammatory, and apoptotic outcomes. Nrf2/HO-1 signaling may contribute to the early antioxidant response following surgical decompression and may represent a potential pharmacological target for compression-associated cauda equina injury.

Article.Title: Deviation of bovine milk leukocyte functions against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus after co-stimulation with Weissella paramesenteroides
Article.Authors: Keeklangdon P.; Srithanasuwan A.; Intanon M.; Chaisri W.; Saipinta D.; Chuasakhonwilai A.; Suriyasathaporn W.
Article.Abstract: Weissella paramesenteroides (WP) is a lactic acid bacterium found in the bovine udder microbiota, and some strains have been proposed as probiotics in the food industry. However, its immunomodulatory effects, particularly in the presence of mastitis pathogens, remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the effects of two W. paramesenteroides isolates (WPI1 and WPI2) on bovine milk white blood cell (mWBC) functions following co-stimulation with Escherichia coli (EC) or Staphylococcus aureus (SA). mWBC were isolated from 12 quarters of 12 cows (one quarter per cow; CMT = 2) in two independent experiments. Milk-derived mWBC were isolated and stimulated with EC, SA, WPI1, WPI2, or their co-stimulations. Leukocyte migration, phagocytosis, bacterial killing activity, and neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation were assessed, and data were analyzed using repeated linear mixed models ( p < 0.05). Both WP isolates induced stronger migration and phagocytosis than the mastitis pathogens alone. WPI1 maintained these responses during co-stimulation and demonstrated enhanced bacterial killing activity against S. aureus . In contrast, WPI2 showed reduced migration and phagocytosis in co-stimulation. Although both strains stimulated extracellular DNA release individually, WPI2 co-stimulation with S. aureus induced the greatest NET release, whereas WPI1 co-stimulations achieved superior bacterial killing with lower NET production. These findings support further investigation of selected W. paramesenteroides strains as potential adjunctive candidates for mastitis-control strategies.

Article.Title: Attentive temporal patch filtering for explainable streaming intrusion detection in medical IoT traffic
Article.Authors: Palaniappan S.; Sengan S.
Article.Abstract: Network traffic in the Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) forms an unbounded multivariate temporal sequence whose statistics shift across devices, protocols, and acquisition environments; detecting malicious segments within it is a streaming time-series classification problem constrained by bounded per-window latency, essential for temporally localized explanations, and robustness to distribution shift. This research work presents TAPX-Net, a window-local classifier that decomposes each traffic window into temporal patches, applies channel-attentive depthwise convolutional filtering, and models the patch sequence with stacked bidirectional recurrent layers before attention pooling and dual classification and reconstruction heads. Each window is classified independently, with recurrent states reset at every window boundary, making the model window-causal. A temporal attribution module (TAM) produces patch- and feature-level explanations through Integrated Gradients (IG), validated against a causal input-level ablation. A feature-harmonized adaptation stage transfers the trained model to new network environments through limited-label fine-tuning with Maximum Mean Discrepancy alignment. On the CICIoMT2024 benchmark, TAPX-Net reaches a recall of 0.9541 at an FPR of one percent and a zero-day recall of 0.8963 across ten held-out attack classes, exceeding 7 baselines on every detection metric, and under CPU-only inference on the tested configuration processes a continuous stream at 108.7 windows per second with 98.8 percent of decisions within a 10 ms per-window bound. IG tracks the causal ablation more closely than attention weights (AW) across all attack classes, and cross-dataset transfer (CDT) to the general-purpose UNSW-NB15 and ToN-IoT benchmarks recovers most of the achievable performance gain with 5,000 labeled target windows. The reconstruction head contributes a 7.46 percentage point improvement in zero-day recall, focused on the generalization regime.

Article.Title: A glycolysis-associated four-gene risk model for prognosis and immune microenvironment characterization in hepatocellular carcinoma
Article.Authors: Xu S.; Xiang H.; Xiang M.; Zhang C.; Luo C.; Luo C.
Article.Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has a dismal prognosis and profound metabolic reprogramming, yet the role of glycolysis-associated genes (GRGs) remains incompletely defined. This study aimed to develop a glycolysis‑associated prognostic model and explore its association with the tumor immune microenvironment (TME). We curated 760 GRGs from MSigDB and performed consensus clustering to identify molecular subtypes. Using WGCNA integrated with three machine learning algorithms (LASSO, Random Forest, and SVM-RFE), we constructed a GRGs risk score model and validated it across multiple independent cohorts. Its correlation with prognosis, genomic alterations, immune infiltration, and in silico drug sensitivity was comprehensively evaluated. Experimental validation was conducted in clinical specimens and HCC cell lines. Two distinct GRGs-based subtypes were identified, with cluster B exhibiting worse prognosis and significant enrichment of cell cycle, glycolysis, EMT, and PI3K‑AKT‑mTOR pathways. A four-gene risk model ( CBX1 , DNMT1 , GAS2L3 , KPNA2 ) was constructed. The risk score demonstrated moderate prognostic performance as an independent prognostic factor and correlated with advanced AJCC stage, higher tumor mutational burden, and an immunosuppressive TME characterized by increased Tregs and M0 macrophages. A nomogram incorporating the risk score showed moderate predictive accuracy and clinical net benefit. Experimental validation supported upregulation of all four genes in HCC tissues, and knockdown of CBX1 or GAS2L3 markedly suppressed cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in vitro. The GRGs risk model demonstrates clinical applicability and net benefit in terms of prognostic stratification and immunophenotype characterization in HCC patients, offering a potentially useful tool for risk assessment and personalized management.
