Article.Title: YOLO-FWF: a lightweight frequency–wavelet feature fusion network for robust scene text detection
Article.Authors: Zhao M.; Zheng Z.; Ye Q.; Fan J.; Zhao J.
Article.Abstract: Scene text detection remains challenging due to large scale variations, slender stroke structures, complex backgrounds, low contrast, and arbitrary text orientations. To address these issues, this paper proposes YOLO-FWF, an improved lightweight scene text detection model based on YOLO11n. First, a C3k2_FrequencyCM module is introduced into the backbone to enhance fine-grained text representation by combining Fourier-domain amplitude compensation with spatial high-frequency feature enhancement, thereby improving the sensitivity of the network to text strokes, edges, and weak texture cues. Second, a C2PSA_WDAM module is designed to replace the original C2PSA structure. By decomposing features into low-frequency semantic components and high-frequency detail components through wavelet transform, the module uses high-frequency information to guide attention modeling and suppress background interference. Third, a Fourier Angle Alignment Fusion module is proposed for multi-scale feature fusion. It estimates dominant local orientations in the frequency domain and aligns high-level semantic features with low-level structural features before fusion, improving the detection of inclined, curved, and irregular text instances. Experiments on two Roboflow-hosted scene text datasets demonstrate that YOLO-FWF achieves superior detection accuracy while maintaining a lightweight structure. On the text scene computer vision dataset, YOLO-FWF reaches 86.8% mAP50 and 64.2% mAP50:95 with only 2.89 M parameters and 6.7 GFLOPs. On the text detection dataset, it achieves 54.7% mAP50 and 34.6% mAP50:95, outperforming YOLO11n and other mainstream detectors under the same evaluation setting. These results verify the effectiveness of frequency-domain enhancement, wavelet-guided attention, and direction-aware feature fusion on the evaluated datasets. Because the current experiments do not include standard public scene-text benchmarks, broader generalization remains to be further verified.

Article.Title: Athlete-AI: a multi-modal artificial intelligence framework for personalized athlete monitoring and injury risk forecasting
Article.Authors: Kanthavel R.; Dhaya R.; Jondhale S.; Jondhale A.; Sharma G.
Article.Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) provides opportunities for computational athlete monitoring, adaptive training analysis, and injury-risk modelling. This study presents Athlete-AI, a multimodal AI framework that integrates wearable sensor data, human motion information, pose features, and literature-derived athlete variables into a unified computational architecture. The framework combines multimodal feature fusion, reinforcement learning for adaptive training simulation, and machine-learning-based injury-risk modelling. The evaluation was conducted using publicly available benchmark datasets, including PAMAP2, Human3.6 M, and Microsoft COCO, together with literature-derived parameters used to construct simulated athlete profiles, workload, fatigue, recovery, and injury-risk scenarios. The framework was evaluated through computational experiments and simulation-based athlete-monitoring scenarios to examine multimodal integration, injury-risk classification, and adaptive training behaviour. Repeated-run evaluation across five random seeds, probability-calibration analysis, component ablation, comparison with multimodal fusion baselines, and a leakage-controlled analysis of the dependence on label-defining variables were also performed. When the workload, fatigue, recovery, and biomechanical-risk variables used to define the simulated labels were removed from the predictors, the F1-score decreased from 86.6 to 72.8%. Negative-control analyses showed that the benchmark-derived features-only model produced performance comparable to the shuffled-label control. The results demonstrate the computational feasibility of integrating heterogeneous athlete data and evaluating adaptive training and injury-risk modelling within a unified simulation environment. The reported performance values represent preliminary computational results and do not constitute real-world, clinical, or prospective athlete validation. Therefore, the proposed framework should be regarded as a computational research framework that requires validation with longitudinal data from real athletes before practical or clinical deployment.

Article.Title: Data-driven and physics-guided neural approaches for LCR circuit modeling: a comparative analysis
Article.Authors: Gopi Sai Ram T.; Sarkar N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this paper, a comparative study is carried out between Recurrent Neural Network Long Short Term Memory (RNN LSTM) models and Physics Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for modeling the dynamic response of an LCR circuit. The circuit dynamics are first formulated in the form of an integro differential equation to capture the memory characteristics of the system. An approximate analytical solution for the charge response is obtained using the Sumudu Transform combined with the Adomian Decomposition Method. The obtained charge profile is then used as training data for both RNN LSTM and PINN models to predict the exact temporal evolution of the circuit charge. The performance of the models is evaluated using prediction accuracy, convergence behaviour, and error analysis. Simulation results show that the RNN LSTM model provides better prediction accuracy and more stable learning compared to the PINN model for the considered LCR system. The study demonstrates that data driven sequential deep learning approaches can effectively model complex electrical circuit dynamics and may offer practical advantages in real time prediction and intelligent circuit analysis.

Article.Title: Anxiety symptoms across menopausal stages: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Mehta A.; Spector A.; Bahhar N.; Desai R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To compare the odds of reporting anxiety symptoms across the pre, peri and post-menopausal stages. Medline, PsycInfo, Embase and Web of Science were searched until 16th August 2024. Inclusion criteria were (1) a cross-sectional or longitudinal design (2) a female population aged 18+ (3) assessed anxiety across menopause stages using validated measures. Exclusion criteria were (1) intervention studies (2) systematic reviews (3) studies with samples who had co-morbid physical or psychiatric conditions. Study quality was assessed using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme tool. 21 studies met the inclusion criteria and 15 studies were included in the meta-analysis. Compared to pre-menopause, women in peri-menopause and post-menopause had higher odds of reporting anxiety symptoms (Pre vs. peri: OR = 1.59, 95% CI: 1.26-2.00; pre vs. post: OR = OR = 1.63, 95% CI: 1.19–2.25). Post-menopausal women had lower odds of anxiety symptoms compared to those in peri-menopause (peri vs. post: OR = 0.79, CI: 0.65–0.96). This review suggests that women in peri-menopause and post-menopause report higher levels of anxiety symptoms compared to pre-menopause, with the highest odds observed during peri-menopause. The menopause transition may represent a period associated with increased reporting of anxiety symptoms, but longitudinal research is needed to clarify directionality, underlying mechanisms, and the role of confounding factors.

Article.Title: Prediction of asphaltene onset pressure and precipitation amount using tree-based stacking–blending ensemble meta-learners: a flow assurance perspective
Article.Authors: Nazeri P.; Khamehchi E.; Ebrahimzadeh A.
Article.Abstract: Flow assurance is critical to reliable oil production, and asphaltene precipitation is among its costliest threats, damaging the near-wellbore region, cutting output, and forcing expensive remediation. Equation-of-state models describe it rigorously but need detailed fluid characterization and heavy computation. This study aims to predict asphaltene onset pressure (AOP) and precipitation amount, as two separate regression tasks, from routinely available reservoir data. We compiled 483 AOP and 408 precipitation measurements from the literature, trained XGBoost, Random Forest, LightGBM, and Extra Trees, and combined them through stacking and blending with a Huber meta-learner. Tuning used 5-fold cross-validation on training data only, and all metrics come from a held-out test set. An ensemble performed best in each task: Stacking-Huber for AOP (R2 = 0.991, MAPE = 1.65%) and Blending-Huber for precipitation amount (R2 = 0.988, MAE = 0.0298), though margins over the best base learners were small. C1 and C5 mattered most for AOP, and pressure and bubble point pressure for precipitation amount, in line with thermodynamic expectations. These findings support rapid screening of asphaltene risk when detailed equation-of-state characterization is unavailable and can inform inhibitor design. When coupled with the pressure and temperature profile along the wellbore, the models can be used to estimate the depth at which precipitation begins and the amount of asphaltene precipitated, within the compositional range of the training data. The main challenge is generalization: records from one source may fall in both training and test sets, so scores reflect the compiled data, not unseen oils. Future work should use source-wise validation on independent datasets, cover gas-injection conditions, and embed thermodynamic constraints through physics-informed models.

Article.Title: An informatics workflow for label-scarce cross-domain segmentation of geological outcrop fractures from UAV photogrammetric imagery
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Li G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate extraction of geological outcrop fracture networks from UAV photogrammetric imagery supports rock-mass characterization, discontinuity mapping, and geotechnical interpretation. However, automated segmentation remains challenging because fractures are often thin, low-contrast, discontinuous, and visually confused with heterogeneous textures, weathering patterns, and shadows. Pixel-level annotation is also labor-intensive, resulting in limited labeled data for newly surveyed areas. This study develops a label-scarce cross-domain segmentation workflow using GeoCrack as the source domain and RockCrack, a small, site-specific UAV dataset, as the target domain. GRNet, the segmentation model used in the workflow, combines Deformable Large-Kernel Attention at the bottleneck with Spatial-Channel Squeeze-and-Excitation in the encoder. Feature-space analysis identifies a measurable discrepancy between the two domains. On GeoCrack, GRNet achieves an IoU of 66.84% and an F1-score of 80.12%. When trained from scratch on RockCrack, it achieves a five-fold mean crack-class IoU of 56.69 ± 4.34% and an F1-score of 72.28 ± 3.61%. Following GeoCrack pretraining and target-domain fine-tuning, the best-performing configuration achieves a mean IoU of 58.96 ± 3.64% and an F1-score of 74.13 ± 2.93%. Fine-tuning substantially outperforms direct source-only deployment, although differences between the leading strategies are small and fold-dependent. The workflow provides pixel-level fracture maps that can support subsequent skeletonization, trace vectorization, and fracture-network characterization; however, further spatial calibration, uncertainty assessment, and geological validation are required before the outputs can be used for quantitative rock-mass analysis or engineering decisions.

Article.Title: Virtual monoenergetic imaging trade-offs in postoperative spectral head CT: a two-center reader study
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Yang J.; Zhong J.; Wu H.; Zheng Q.; Liang H.
Article.Abstract: Postoperative non-contrast spectral head CT permits retrospective virtual monoenergetic imaging (VMI), but the energy level that best balances objective and reader-rated image quality is uncertain. We evaluated 93 patients who contributed 120 postoperative examinations using conventional images and VMIs at 60, 70, 80, 90, and 100 keV. Image noise, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), and independent ratings by two neuroradiologists were analyzed with mixed-effects models reflecting the hierarchical data structure. CNR was highest at 60 keV (1.62 ± 0.39), whereas image noise was lowest at 100 keV (4.27 ± 0.49 HU). The 70-keV VMI had the highest reader scores for overall image quality, operative-bed parenchymal conspicuity, and diagnostic acceptability, whereas 100 keV had the highest artifact-suppression score. Quadratic-weighted kappa values ranged from 0.859 to 0.986. Thus, no single VMI energy optimized all image-quality properties: 60 keV maximized measured CNR, 70 keV produced the most favorable reader ratings across three routine-review domains, and 100 keV minimized noise and maximized artifact suppression. Diagnostic-performance validation is required before these findings inform a task-specific clinical workflow.

Article.Title: Cutting-edge trends in drought prediction and mitigation using ensemble learning and augmented XAI: a meteorological study
Article.Authors: Rathi M.; Mishra S.; Alshammari N.; Agrawal H.; Ashraf E.
Article.Abstract: Drought affects more than 60% of India's population, reducing agricultural productivity, straining water resources, and threatening socioeconomic stability. This study proposes an interpretable one-month-ahead meteorological drought prediction framework by integrating class-weighted ensemble machine learning with SHAP and LIME explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). Historical meteorological observations (1972–2022) obtained from the Zenodo climate database were analyzed for 49 districts across five drought-prone Indian states (Bihar, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka). After generating lagged meteorological features (t − 1 to t − 6) and addressing severe class imbalance (7.07% drought events), multiple machine learning classifiers were evaluated. The class-weighted XGBoost model (scale_pos_weight ≈ 11.90, without SMOTE) achieved the best overall performance on the independent 2016–2022 test dataset, with an accuracy of 95.7%, macro precision of 84.7%, macro recall of 81.0%, macro F1-score of 82.7%, and a PR-AUC of 0.647 on the highly imbalanced test set (outperforming both unweighted training and SMOTE-based approaches). SHAP and LIME consistently identified lagged Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI), lagged precipitation, vapour pressure, and wet-day frequency as the most influential drivers of drought occurrence. Exploratory temporal analysis further revealed declining wet-day frequency in Karnataka, increasing vapour pressure in Andhra Pradesh, and substantial climatic variability across the study regions. The proposed framework combines accurate drought prediction with transparent model interpretation, providing a practical decision-support tool for district-level drought early warning, water resource management, and climate-resilient agricultural planning in India.

Article.Title: A lightweight YOLO based framework for real-time seat belt detection in intelligent traffic surveillance
Article.Authors: Nayak P.; Dash R.; Muduli D.; Kanade A.; Rawat A.; Zamani A.; Khilari P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Road accidents remain a major cause of fatalities worldwide, and proper seat belt usage significantly reduces the risk of severe injuries and death. Ensuring compliance through automated traffic surveillance systems is therefore essential; however, reliable real-time detection remains challenging due to illumination variations, occlusions, windshield reflections, and low contrast between seat belts and vehicle interiors. This paper presents a task-oriented lightweight detection framework, termed as ECA-BiFPN-YOLO, designed specifically for robust seat belt detection under real-world conditions. The proposed approach systematically integrates efficient feature generation, lightweight attention, adaptive multiscale fusion, and visibility enhancement to address the unique challenges of thin-object detection in degraded environments. The framework incorporates GhostC2f modules and depthwise convolutions for computational efficiency, Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) for improved channel-wise feature discrimination, and a Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network (BiFPN) with learnable weighted fusion for stable multiscale representation. Additionally, a Dark Channel Prior (DCP)-based preprocessing pipeline is employed to enhance visibility in low-light and hazy scenarios. Extensive experiments conducted on the SeatBelts-V1 dataset and a cross-domain dataset demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an mAP@50 of 95.6% while maintaining real-time inference performance (11.5 ms per image, $$\sim$$ 85 FPS) on an NVIDIA T4 GPU. Comparative and ablation studies confirm that the proposed design provides an effective balance between accuracy, efficiency, and robustness. These results highlight the practical applicability of the proposed framework for large-scale intelligent traffic surveillance systems, particularly in resource-constrained and real-world deployment scenarios.

Article.Title: Electrochemotherapy in large and deep-seated soft tissue sarcomas: a pilot study on tumor control, limb preservation, and symptom relief
Article.Authors: Ghale H.; Mahmoodzadeh H.; Bayat M.; Berhanegard E.; Mansouri S.; Naamvari A.; Mohamadian A.; Ghanaati H.; Miri S.; Abdolahad M.
Article.Abstract: Electrochemotherapy (ECT) is a locoregional treatment that combines reversible electroporation with chemotherapy to enhance intracellular drug delivery. Clinical evidence for ECT in large, deep-seated, recurrent, or locally advanced soft tissue tumors remains limited. This pilot study primarily evaluated symptom palliation following bleomycin-based ECT, with objective tumor response and treatment-related toxicity assessed as secondary outcomes. Twenty-five patients with recurrent, locally advanced, or metastatic STS tumors resistant to conventional treatments underwent ECT between 2022 and 2025. Bleomycin (15,000 IU/m²) was administered intravenously, followed by electroporation using variable electrode configurations according to tumor characteristics. The primary outcome was symptom palliation. Secondary outcomes included objective tumor response and treatment-related toxicity, while additional clinical outcomes included quality-of-life changes, limb preservation, local progression-free survival (LPFS), and overall survival (OS). The study population had a median tumor size of 87 mm (range 35–320 mm), and 92% of tumors were ≥ 5 cm. Overall symptom palliation was achieved in 16 of 18 symptomatic patients (88.9%), with pain reduction reported in 12 of 14 patients with severe baseline pain (85.7%) and complete cessation of bleeding and tumor-associated discharge in all eight affected patients. EORTC QLQ-C30 scores improved across all evaluated domains, including Global Health, Physical Function, and Role Function, while Pain and Other Symptoms scores decreased significantly (all P < 0.001). ECT enabled conversion to operability in selected unresectable tumors, and long-term limb preservation was achieved in four of the six patients who were initially considered candidates for amputation. An objective response was observed in 21/25 patients (84.0%, 95% CI: 63.9%–95.5%). After a median follow-up of 13.7 months, the 1-year LPFS and OS rates were 56.0% and 76.0%, respectively. The most frequent adverse events were skin reactions and soft tissue necrosis, which were generally manageable with conservative wound care or outpatient debridement. No serious ECT-related systemic adverse events were reported. ECT was associated with symptom palliation, objective tumor response, and manageable treatment-related toxicity in this pilot cohort. These preliminary findings warrant further evaluation in larger prospective controlled studies. Clinical trial registration number : The clinical trial registration code number was (IRCT20190904044697N8, Registration Date: 2022-10-02).

Article.Title: Prevalence and fragmented populations of submicroscopic Plasmodium vivax in Vanuatu from 2017 to 2019
Article.Authors: Chan C.; Kagaya W.; Kalkoa M.; Yaviong J.; Iata H.; Kalkoa K.; Taleo G.; Kaneko A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Vanuatu had experienced a remarkable decrease in malaria since the mid-2000s but transmission hotspots remained on several islands. We conducted cross-sectional surveys in known hotspots on seven islands between 2017 and 2019. Among 6,943 participants we found low prevalence of exclusively submicroscopic Plasmodium vivax infections on Epi (4.3%; 95% CI 3.0–6.0%), Malekula (4.8%; 95% CI 4.0-5.7%), Santo (6.5%; 95% CI 5.3–7.7%), Maewo (0.4%; 95% CI 0.1–1.2%), and Vanua Lava (1.2%; 95% CI 0.5–2.8%). Regression analysis revealed significant association between P. vivax infections and age (OR = 1.07, p = 0.007) and enlarged spleen (OR = 5.36, p < 0.001) among 2,407 children ≤ 12 years. Microsatellite genotyping of 53 P. vivax samples showed that parasites on Epi had lower heterozygosity ( H E = 0.173) and haplotype diversity ( h = 0.731) than those on Malekula ( H E = 0.638; h = 0.990) and Santo ( H E = 0.751; h = 0.984). P. vivax effective population size estimates on Epi were an order-of-magnitude smaller than those on Malekula and Santo. Significant genetic differentiation (F ST = 0.018–0.138, p < 0.01) and apparent population structure were observed among these three islands. P. vivax populations had shown evidence of fragmentation at the island level in Vanuatu by 2019.

Article.Title: Reducing boundary conditions for the Thomas–Fermi equation using a hybrid q-deformation and neural network method
Article.Authors: Güvercin F.; Özavşar M.
Article.Abstract: This study introduces a hybrid \(q\) -calculus and artificial neural network framework for the Thomas–Fermi equation of free positive ions. Its contribution is a construction in which \(q\) -deformation combines the terminal derivative and terminal-value conditions, representing three classical boundary conditions by two constraints in the deformed problem. A boundary-compatible trial solution embeds the transformed constraints, allowing training to focus on the \(q\) -differential residual. For fixed \(q<1\) , the result is a deformed approximation with a classical limit as \(q\rightarrow 1\) . Experiments across nine ionization degrees and five seeds compared the \(q\) -ANN with a benchmark, a soft-constrained PINN, and an undeformed hard-constrained classical ANN. The \(q\) -ANN produced lower RMSE than the PINN in 42 of 45 matched runs and a lower median RMSE ( \(0.004127\) versus \(0.015044\) ), although two outlying outcomes caused mean RMSE to favor the PINN and paired tests did not establish a difference. Against the hard-constrained classical ANN, the \(q\) -ANN produced lower RMSE in 44 of 45 comparisons, indicating that the observed performance is not attributable solely to exact constraint embedding. The pointwise \(q\) -ANN was approximately \(102\) times slower than the vectorized PINN. The framework provides a new boundary-transformation strategy while retaining initialization sensitivity and computational cost as limitations.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: q-deformation; Thomas-Fermi equation; degree of ionization; q-calculus; physics-informed neural networks; boundary conditions; artificial neural networks

Article.Title: Transcriptomic profiling and immune gene expression analysis of canine DH82 cells (co)infected by Leishmania infantum, Leishmania tarentolae and their hybrid
Article.Authors: Latrofa M.; Louzada-Flores V.; Cafferati Beltrame L.; Pierri C.; Mendoza-Roldan J.; Otranto D.
Article.Abstract: The co-occurrence of Leishmania infantum and Leishmania tarentolae in sympatric geographic areas raises questions about their immunological interactions in vertebrate hosts, suggesting a protective effect of the latter species in the course of canine leishmaniasis. This study aimed to characterize the transcriptome profile and cytokine gene expression of canine DH82 macrophage cells infected in vitro by L. infantum , L. tarentolae , their hybrid strain (i.e., Linf/Ltar ) and with both Leishmania species. The transcriptional profiles of cells infected were assessed at 72 h post-infection by RNA-seq analysis and RT-qPCR (reverse transcriptase qPCR) assay. All strains established cell infection with a progressive decline in parasite burden rate over time points. Transcriptomic analysis indicated that L. infantum (i.e., padj < 0.01; gene count = 19) and Linf/Ltar hybrid strains (i.e., padj < 0.01, gene count = 16) induced a transcriptional changes involving gene of inflammatory pathways, while L. tarentolae elicited a weaker response, associated with metabolic processes (i.e., padj > 0.05), reflecting a less transcriptional changes in genes associated with macrophages and inflammatory responses. The coinfection with both Leishmania species resulted in the largest number of differentially expressed genes and the strongest enrichment of inflammatory pathways (i.e., padj < 0.01, gene count = 21). These findings were further supported by moderate to strong IL-6 gene expression induced by L. infantum (up to 1.13 relative fold change), Linf/Ltar hybrid (up to 1.30 relative fold change), and coinfection with both Leishmania species (up to 2.26 relative fold change), as well as by a relatively high IL-12 gene expression (up to 1.74 relative fold change) for L. tarentolae . Overall, the results provided evidence that L. infantum and L. tarentolae may induce distinct transcriptional response in canine macrophages, and particularly in genes associated with immune and inflammatory processes.

Article.Title: Longitudinal evaluation of video assistant referee implementation on goal timing distributions and card statistics in Turkish Super League
Article.Authors: Çiftçi M.; Gökalp H.; Yarayan Y.
Article.Abstract: The Video Assistant Referee (VAR) system has become an integral component of modern football, yet its long-term influence on disciplinary outcomes and goal-scoring patterns remains debated. Therefore, this study examined the association between VAR implementation and changes in disciplinary rates and goal-scoring dynamics in the Turkish Super League across twelve seasons (2012–2013 to 2023–2024). Match information from all Turkish Super League games played during this period was aggregated at the season level, yielding six pre-VAR and six post-VAR observations. Data were analyzed using generalized linear models with a negative binomial distribution. To account for unequal seasonal match volumes, all count-based models incorporated log-transformed seasonal match totals as exposure offsets. A quasi-binomial regression model was additionally employed to examine the occurrence of goals during added-time periods. Sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate the consistency of the findings under alternative historical specifications. The results revealed significant reductions in yellow cards (IRR = 0.87, p < .001), total cards (IRR = 0.88, p < .001), and card points (IRR = 0.88, p < .001) following VAR implementation. In contrast, direct red cards and second yellow-to-red cards showed no statistically significant differences between periods. While overall goal productivity remained unchanged (IRR = 0.97, p = .555), a greater proportion of goals occurred during added-time periods in the post-VAR era. Significant increases were observed in first-half added-time goals (IRR = 2.92, p < .001), second-half added-time goals (IRR = 1.41, p = .003), and total added-time goals (IRR = 1.71, p < .001). Quasi-binomial regression analyses further indicated that the association between VAR period and the conditional probability of an observed goal occurring during added time differed by match half, with higher odds in the post-VAR period during both the first half (OR = 3.15, 95% CI [2.03, 4.91], p < .001) and second half (OR = 1.56, 95% CI [1.21, 2.02], p = .001). Sensitivity analyses demonstrated consistent directional associations across multiple model specifications. Overall, VAR implementation was associated with lower rates of caution-related disciplinary actions and with changes in the temporal distribution of goals, while overall goal productivity remained stable. The findings indicate that a greater proportion of goals occurred during added-time periods following VAR implementation. However, because actual added-time durations were unavailable, these results should be interpreted as a redistribution of goal occurrence rather than definitive evidence of increased scoring intensity during stoppage time.

Article.Title: From reconstruction to interpretation: zero-setup deployable model for multi-phase segmentation of X-ray tomography data
Article.Authors: Elavarthi P.; Bhattacharjee A.; Lisabeth H.; Ralescu A.; Zwart P.; Parkinson D.; Clark E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract X-ray tomography enables the nondestructive characterization of materials, and recent advances in micro-CT imaging technology have accelerated the acquisition and reconstruction of volumetric data. However, rapid scientific interpretation remains limited by image segmentation, which typically requires manual thresholding, user prompting, or material-specific model training before meaningful analysis can begin. We present a zero-setup deployment framework for multi-phase segmentation of synchrotron X-ray tomography data that produces interpretable segmentations of previously unseen tomography datasets without user prompting or additional retraining during deployment. The framework combines a material-agnostic mask preparation strategy based on common structural concepts in tomography data such as background, sample, bright regions, dark-gray regions, light-gray regions, and porosity, with a pretrained semantic segmentation network to generate diagnostic-quality segmentations within minutes of reconstruction. Unlike conventional deep learning pipelines that require dataset-specific annotations and retraining, the proposed approach can be applied immediately to new scans, enabling rapid assessment of experimental quality and preliminary microstructural analysis during ongoing beamline experiments. Users can subsequently refine or fine-tune the generated masks when application-specific segmentation is required. Experiments on held-out and qualitatively evaluated synchrotron micro-CT datasets suggest that the framework produces consistent and physically meaningful segmentations on new tomography datasets while substantially outperforming conventional intensity-based thresholding. By bridging the gap between high-speed data acquisition and immediate interpretation, the proposed framework enables near real-time beamline feedback and provides a practical foundation for scalable AI-assisted scientific imaging workflows.

Article.Title: Cross-corpus consensus feature selection for language-invariant Parkinson’s disease detection: a dual-stream acoustic and spectrogram-attention framework
Article.Authors: Hossain R.; Banu A.; Chowdhury M.
Article.Abstract: Speech-based biomarkers of Parkinson’s disease (PD) routinely achieve high within-corpus accuracy yet degrade sharply when transferred to an unseen dataset, language, or recording protocol. We argue that this fragility is primarily a feature-stability problem rather than a modelling problem, and we propose a dual-stream cross-corpus consensus feature-selection framework that explicitly enforces inter-corpus agreement. The first stream operates on 156 interpretable handcrafted acoustic descriptors: within each training corpus a heterogeneous set of classifiers performs recursive feature elimination, features are retained by intra-dataset model agreement, and a strict cross-dataset intersection isolates a compact set of cross-corpus stable candidate biomarkers, a subset of which additionally exhibit consistent effect-size direction across derivation languages. The second stream operates on log-Mel spectrogram images, where the spatial attention of a CBAM-augmented ResNet, the attention rollout of a Vision Transformer, and Grad-CAM saliency are combined into a consensus saliency mask whose agreed-upon salient regions yield pooled, file-level image features that are likewise stabilised across corpora. The two consensus streams are fused and classified under monolingual, multilingual, and cross-lingual paradigms. Crucially, three corpora (English, Italian, Bengali) are used only for feature derivation, while three disjoint corpora (Spanish, English, Spanish) are withheld for external validation, so that feature-level invariance is measured independently of model-specific adaptation. The framework advances the transition from language-specific PD models toward scalable, language-agnostic, and interpretable speech-based screening. Cross-corpus stability, per-feature effect-size consistency, and leave-one-language-out validation are reported as the evidentiary basis for these claims, and we explicitly quantify the corpora and margins by which dataset-specific optimisation still outperforms the consensus representation.

Article.Title: Serum molybdenum and right ventricular remodeling after durable left ventricular assist device implantation
Article.Authors: Urbanowicz T.; Wojewódzki F.; Tomaszewska M.; Ładzińska M.; Kaczmarek J.; Straburzyńska-Migaj E.; Kowalewski M.; Grywalska E.; Bojarski K.; Jemielity M.; Hanć A.
Article.Abstract: Left ventricular device (LVAD) implantation has become a standard of care for patients with heart failure (HF). Right ventricular remodeling remains one of the major determinants of late outcome after left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation, whereas biomarkers reflecting postoperative right ventricular adaptation remain poorly defined. Because molybdenum is an essential cofactor regulating oxidative and inflammatory pathways, we investigated whether circulating molybdenum concentrations are associated with right ventricular remodeling following durable LVAD support. There were 25 male patients in median (Q1 – Q3) age of 56 (51 – 62) years treated with left ventricular assist device implantation (HM3, Abbott Corp. USA) due to end-stage heart failure. Patients presented with NYHA status I (12 (48%) patients) and II (13 (52%) patients) on the control follow-up check-ups, with a median (Q1 – Q3) time of 421 (296 - 1277) days. Right ventricular diameter dilatation was observed in 7 (28%) patients, and RV reduction in basal diameter in 8 (32%) more patients. In the subset with concurrent trace-element and follow-up RV data, molybdenum showed the strongest nominal association with reduction in RV basal diameter (3.227 [2.918–3.609] vs. 2.000 [1.734–2.187] µg/L; p = 0.018), although the association did not remain significant after correction for multiple trace-element comparisons (FDR q = 0.327). Circulating molybdenum emerged as a candidate trace-element signal associated with postoperative RV structural remodeling; however, the association was exploratory and did not withstand multiplicity correction. Larger prospective studies are required to determine its reproducibility and biological relevance.

Article.Title: Early dose stratification 4 h after ionizing radiation exposure using a peripheral blood transcriptional gene panel
Article.Authors: Biolatti L.; Ausas M.; Leberle J.; Hernández D.; Negrin L.; Mazzitelli-Fuentes L.; Cascon A.; Choudhury A.; Bellora N.; Ibañez I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Biodosimetry is essential for absorbed-dose estimation following occupational radiation accidents where early clinical decisions determine whether individuals require hospitalization or can be managed on an outpatient basis. Radioinduced transcriptomic alterations are a promising tool for rapid dose estimation. We established a gene expression panel for dose classification at 4 h post-exposure, reducing the time typically required for cytogenetic assays. Peripheral blood leukocytes from healthy individuals were X-ray irradiated and cultured for 4 h. RNA was sequenced and reads were mapped to the human hg38 genome (STAR software). Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified using DESeq2 (false discovery rate, FDR, < 0.05). Radiation specificity was confirmed using eight independent microarray datasets from multiple disease conditions. DEGs were validated by RT-qPCR. A total of 215 DEGs were identified; hierarchical clustering separated samples by absorbed dose. AEN, CD70, CDKN1A, DDB2, FDXR, PCNA, and VPREB3 showed strong dose-dependent transcriptional changes across multiple disease conditions, demonstrating specificity to IR. A LASSO logistic regression model discriminated between low-dose (0–100 cGy) and high-dose (≥ 200 cGy) exposures, achieving AUC-ROC = 0.88 with CDKN1A and CD70, and AUC-ROC = 1.00 with CDKN1A, CD70, and DDB2. This gene panel offers a reliable tool for early classification of radiation exposure, supporting improved treatment of exposed individuals.

Article.Title: Morphological, molecular, and pathogenic characterization of five Fusarium species associated with coffee berry rot in Malaysia
Article.Authors: Tang X.; Mohd M.
Article.Abstract: Coffee berry rot has emerged as an important disease affecting coffee production in Malaysia; however, information on the Fusarium species associated with this disease remains limited. This study aimed to identify and characterize Fusarium species associated with coffee berry rot affecting Coffea arabica , C. canephora , and C. liberica in Malaysia. Surveys conducted during 2023–2024 across eight coffee plantations yielded 30 Fusarium isolates from symptomatic berries exhibiting irregular brown to black lesions that progressed to berry rot. Species identification was performed using morphological characterization and phylogenetic analyses based on the translation elongation factor 1-alpha ( tef1-α ) and β-tubulin ( tub2 ) genes. Integrative analyses identified the isolates as Fusarium proliferatum , F. fujikuroi , F. lateritium , F. incarnatum , and F. solani . Pathogenicity tests on healthy coffee berries confirmed that all five species were capable of causing typical coffee berry rot symptoms, and Koch’s postulates were fulfilled through successful re-isolation of the inoculated pathogens. Among the identified species, F. solani was the most virulent, inducing the highest disease severity in pathogenicity tests, while C. arabica and C. canephora showed greater susceptibility to infection under the experimental conditions. The occurrence of multiple Fusarium species associated with coffee berry rot highlights the complexity of the disease and the importance of accurate pathogen identification for disease management. To our knowledge, this is the first report of Fusarium species causing coffee berry rot in Malaysia.

Article.Title: Quantifying nonlinear thresholds of grey-green space morphology on urban carbon metabolism across local climate zones: a machine learning study in Changchun city
Article.Authors: Gong Y.; Qin W.
Article.Abstract: Urban grey-green spaces play a critical role in regulating carbon metabolism by influencing atmospheric CO₂ concentration (XCO₂) and net primary productivity (NPP). However, the heterogeneous drivers of carbon metabolism across different Local Climate Zones (LCZs) remain insufficiently understood. This study investigated Changchun, China, by integrating LCZ classification, multidimensional morphological indicators, and interpretable machine learning. Based on typical urban development patterns and morphological contrasts, LCZ 1–3 were aggregated into a compact built-up group (hereafter the LCZ 1 group), while LCZ 6 (open low-rise) was retained as an independent group; these two groups were selected as representative zones. CatBoost-SHAP models were developed to reveal nonlinear relationships between urban morphology and carbon metabolism. Results showed that grey-space characteristics (B_CORE, BD, BH) dominated carbon metabolism in LCZ 1, contributing over 55%, whereas green-space and climatic factors (VFC, ACH, MAT) played greater roles in LCZ 6. Context-dependent nonlinear turning-point characteristics were identified: in LCZ 1 group, response changes occurred around B_CORE ≈ 2.0 and over BH range of 10–40 m; in LCZ 6, VFC around 0.65 and B1 around − 0.25 showed distinct turning points. Identical indicators showed different association across LCZs, highlighting context-specific planning. This study provides an integrated LCZ-based interpretable machine-learning framework to characterize localized nonlinear responses and support low-carbon urban planning.

Article.Title: Stability-aware hybrid optimisation-based feature selection and stacking classification for PCOS prediction
Article.Authors: Reka S.; Praba T.; Selvam P.; Kumar B.; Ivković N.; Cengiz K.
Article.Abstract: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is one of the most common endocrine diseases in women of reproductive age all over the world. It is estimated that 6–13% of women are affected worldwide, and a significant percentage of them go undiagnosed because of their heterogeneity. The increased rate of PCOS is directly associated with lifestyle transition, metabolic stress, and hormonal imbalance. PCOS is linked to infertility, metabolism, and cardiovascular risks, which are long-term. Machine learning provides data-driven approaches for identifying patterns associated with PCOS from clinical and related patient characteristics. Such approaches may support predictive modelling by identifying informative features and combining them to distinguish between PCOS and non-PCOS cases. Feature selection is therefore used to identify a compact and stable subset of input variables, with the aim of improving predictive performance and model reliability. This study presents a hybrid optimisation approach for selecting a compact and stable subset of features for PCOS prediction. First, an ensemble wrapper-based approach is implemented, and then a combination of hybrid Optimisation strategies is examined with several combinations and ends with an ACOBO (Ant Colony Optimisation - Butterfly Optimisation) technique. Additionally, robustness of feature selection methods, a most common issue when algorithms run on the same dataset multiple times or with small modification has been checked with the help of rank-based Spearman and Kendall correlations, and distribution-based Jensen Shannon divergence using 10-fold cross-validation. Additionally, SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique) has been used to address the class imbalance issue. Finally, multiple stacking configurations were evaluated with SMOTE by varying the meta-classifier while using the remaining candidate classifiers as base learners. Among the evaluated configurations, the stacking model with AdaBoost as the meta-classifier achieved the highest accuracy of 95.64%.

Article.Title: The actual sky of Van Gogh’s Starry Night: a multidisciplinary reconstruction
Article.Authors: Kim E.; Kang S.; Song J.; Jin H.
Article.Abstract: The Starry Night : whether its sky represents spontaneous fantasy or a realist depiction has gone unanswered for over a century. Earlier astronomical readings, constrained by the conventional June dating, reached mutually exclusive conclusions, and the painting’s celestial arrangement was never quantitatively tested. In contrast, this study narrows the dates on which the Moon and Venus fall within the painter’s field of view, confirms that selection by Procrustes fitting of the asterism, and cross-checks it against meteorological and bioclimatic records and the original letters. The procedure is first applied to night paintings by Elsheimer and Millet, and validated on two 1888 night paintings whose sites survive. The painter’s narrow frame, recovered from an earlier sketch of the same terrain, is then applied to the 1889 sky. At dawn around 22 July 1889, the waning-crescent Moon, Venus, and the Hyades cluster gather within that narrow frame, while the asterism’s geometry, contemporary weather records, and the letters independently converge on the same date. These findings suggest that the night sky in The Starry Night originated from observation of a specific celestial arrangement, and call for reconsidering the June dating. This framework can extend to historical night paintings as a reproducible scientific art history.

Article.Title: Regional synergetic effects of ice and snow consumption based on a BERT neural network
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Zhi S.
Article.Abstract: This study takes Harbin Ice-Snow World as a key case and develops an integrated framework based on a BERT neural network and regional economic analysis to quantify and analyze regional synergy associated with ice-snow consumption. The framework integrates semantic features with structured indicators to construct a regional synergy intensity model using approximately 12,000 consumer reviews and multidimensional statistical data from 15 regional nodes. Five-fold cross-validation and a three-expert consistency assessment (Fleiss’ Kappa = 0.84) were conducted. The results showed that the model achieved strong performance in predicting synergetic relationships, with an F1-score of 0.87, significantly outperforming baseline models based on advanced large language models such as Llama-3-70B and the ablation variants. Harbin was identified as the “absolute core” of the network, with a weighted centrality of 4.52. Based on quantitative topological indicators, including network density and path strength, the synergetic patterns were classified into the “Heilongjiang Core Agglomeration Zone,” the “Jilin-Liaoning-Hebei Functional Complementarity Zone,” and the “Long-Distance Characteristic Linkage Zone.” This study provides a new perspective for understanding the spatial organization of the ice-snow industry and offers data-driven decision support for formulating cross-regional collaboration policies.

Article.Title: An advanced hybrid aquila optimizer with DE–QOB–elite strategies for precise PEMFC parameter extraction
Article.Authors: Alharbi A.; Zaki Diab A.
Article.Abstract: The Aquila Optimizer (AO) is a metaheuristic optimization algorithm widely applied to solve complex nonlinear problems. However, its original formulation suffers from slow convergence and a tendency to be trapped in local optima when applied to Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell (PEMFC) parameter identification. In this work, several enhanced variants of AO are developed, including the Super Aquila Optimizer (SAO), Hyper Super Aquila Differential Evolution (Hyper_SAO_DE), Hyper Super Aquila Differential Evolution with Quasi-Opposition-Based Learning (Hyper_SAO_DE_QOB), and Hyper Super Aquila Differential Evolution with Quasi-Opposition and Elite strategy (HyperSAODE_QOB_Elite), aiming to improve the exploration–exploitation balance, convergence speed, and robustness. The reported Reinforced Learning Quantum-inspired Fully Adaptive Aquila Optimizer (RLQFAO), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) are also considered for comparison. All algorithms are applied to estimate the unknown parameters of PEMFC models using the sum of squared errors (SSE) between the estimated and experimental output voltages as the objective function. The implementation is carried out in MATLAB using 30 independent runs. For the BCS 500 W PEMFC case, Hyper_SAO_DE_QOB achieved the lowest SSE of 0.011556306, corresponding to reductions of approximately 99.29% and 51.05% compared with AO and PSO, respectively. It also achieved a mean SSE of 0.011556 with a standard deviation of 3.77 × 10⁻⁸, indicating highly consistent performance across independent runs. Hyper_SAO_DE and RLQFAO produced statistically comparable results, while Hyper_SAO_DE_QOB achieved the best Friedman average rank. In addition, its average computational time was 253.61 s, substantially lower than the 1194.40 s required by RLQFAO. The estimated PEMFC parameters provide close agreement between the simulated and experimental voltage characteristics, demonstrating the effectiveness and robustness of the enhanced optimization framework for PEMFC parameter estimation.

Article.Title: Multi-bitplane edge detection of skin lesion contours in dermoscopic images
Article.Authors: Li D.; Pang P.; Lam C.; Chao P.
Article.Abstract: In dermatological medical image analysis, edge detection is critical for skin disease diagnosis. Precise edge information provides a vital basis for subsequent disease assessment. However, existing grayscale gradient-based edge detection methods exhibit poor visual effects when extracting features of complex skin textures, often due to interference from noise and inability to obtain complete, clear edge images, while deep learning-based methods suffer from heavy reliance on large annotated datasets and high computing costs. To improve the visual quality of edge detection for skin images and extract clear, complete skin edges, we propose the training-free, lightweight Skin Lesion Contour Detection (SLCD) method. It integrates Haar wavelet transform denoising and 3 × 3 circular structuring element morphological processing for two-stage preprocessing of skin images. The processed image uses 3 Most Significant Bit (MSB) planes, and edge detection is performed on each bit plane separately. Each bit plane is processed by the 3 × 3 neighborhood adaptive analysis based on local standard deviation and average gradient to get the edge image, and the resulting edge images are fused to generate the final detection result. Experiments on the Skin Image Edge Detection Test (SIEDT) dataset show that SLCD achieves an average F1-score of 0.718, Jaccard index of 0.575, and Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) of 0.733. All of which are the best among the compared methods. The SLCD can effectively extract true skin edges and mitigate noise interference in skin images, providing a training-free and lightweight alternative that offers better edge detection performance than traditional operators while avoiding the heavy data and computational requirements of deep learning models in resource-limited skin image analysis scenarios. This study provides multi-bitplane fusion-based novel concepts and methods for edge detection in skin images. It delivers diagnostic value by providing high-precision lesion contours, supporting analysis of skin lesions, early diagnosis, and surgical planning, and improving the reliability of clinical decision-making in dermatology.

Article.Title: Neutral versus Trendelenburg position for ultrasound-guided internal jugular vein catheterization: a randomized, controlled non-inferiority trial
Article.Authors: Bae J.; Yoo J.; Heo J.; Park S.
Article.Abstract: The Trendelenburg position is traditionally regarded as the standard maneuver for enhancing the success of internal jugular vein (IJV) catheterization, but its necessity under real-time ultrasound (US) guidance is unclear. We aimed to determine whether the neutral (supine) position is non-inferior to the Trendelenburg position for catheterization success under real-time US guidance. In this randomized, controlled non-inferiority trial, 216 adults undergoing elective surgery requiring central venous catheterization were randomly assigned to the Trendelenburg (10° tilt) or neutral position. Ultrasound-guided IJV catheterization was performed by experienced anesthesiologists using a short-axis out-of-plane approach. The primary outcome was the first-attempt success rate; secondary outcomes were catheterization time, complication rate, and IJV dimensions. The non-inferiority margin was prespecified at an absolute 5% in the approved study protocol. First-attempt success was 95.33% in the Trendelenburg group and 99.07% in the neutral group. The between-group difference (neutral − Trendelenburg) was + 3.75% (95% CI, − 1.2% to + 9.6%); the lower bound remained above the − 5% non-inferiority margin, confirming non-inferiority ( P = 0.001). Non-inferiority was maintained in the intention-to-treat analysis and in sensitivity analyses using margins of 3% and 7%. Although the Trendelenburg position produced significantly greater IJV vertical length and cross-sectional area, this did not affect clinical success. In elective adult surgical patients under general anesthesia in whom catheterization is performed by experienced operators under real-time US guidance, the neutral position is non-inferior to the Trendelenburg position, and routine use of the Trendelenburg position may not be necessary in this setting.

Article.Title: Pupillary signs are associated with subsequent Hirschsprung disease diagnosis and malignant adrenal neoplasm in congenital central hypoventilation syndrome
Article.Authors: Eleiwa T.; Bayoumy A.; Azhari J.; Abboud I.; Malek D.; Gaier E.; Phillips P.; Elhusseiny A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To evaluate the association between pupillary signs and the risk of late-diagnosed Hirschsprung disease (HD) and Malignant Neoplasm of the Adrenal Gland (MNAG) in pediatric patients with Congenital Central Hypoventilation Syndrome (CCHS), and to systematically review ocular manifestations in CCHS. We performed a retrospective cohort analysis with integrated systematic literature review. A cohort of 680 pediatric CCHS patients (2004–2024) was identified from the TriNetX US Collaborative Network. Patients with pre-existing HD or MNAG were excluded. CCHS patients with pupillary signs (ICD-10 codes H21.56, H57.0, G90.2) were compared to those without. Primary outcomes were subsequent HD diagnosis or MNAG at 3 and 5 years, assessed using adjusted Hazard Ratios (aHRs). A PRISMA-compliant systematic review of CCHS ocular findings was also performed. Among 680 CCHS patients (mean age 3.4 years), 38 (5.6%) had pupillary abnormalities. The presence of pupillary signs was significantly associated with an increased risk of subsequent HD diagnosis [5-year aHR, 4.93 (95% CI: 2.72–8.84; p < .001)] and MNAG [5-year aHR, 5.72 (95% CI: 2.31–14.33; p < .001)]. The systematic review (8 studies, n = 32 patients) found pupillary signs were present in 100% of tumor-positive patients and co-occurred with HD in 56%. Pupillary signs in pediatric CCHS were significantly associated with increased risk of subsequent HD diagnosis and MNAG. These findings are hypothesis-generating and support the incorporation of structured pupillary assessment into the multidisciplinary evaluation of pediatric CCHS patients, pending prospective validation.

Article.Title: Ontology-guided neuro-symbolic convNeXtV2–swin transformer for explainable cytological classification of papillary thyroid carcinoma
Article.Authors: Ahmed I.; Senan E.; Alyousef A.; Khan M.; Ali E.; Othman E.; Fati S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The cytological assessment of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) relies on microscopic evaluation of cellular and nuclear morphology. Subtle cytomorphological differences, interobserver variability, and specimen heterogeneity can complicate interpretation. This study developed an explainable hybrid ConvNeXtV2–Swin Transformer framework that integrates fine-grained cytological representation with broader spatial-context modeling for PTC classification. ConvNeXtV2 provides fine-grained nuclear and cellular representations, whereas Swin Transformer captures broader contextual relationships across cytological regions. These complementary representations support classification and subsequent pathology-informed interpretation of nuclear, architectural, and stromal evidence. Interpretability combines Biomarker-Guided Attention Modeling, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM)-style quantitative attribution analysis, and ontology-guided post-classification semantic interpretation. On the independent test set, the hybrid framework achieved 96.19% accuracy, 96.16% sensitivity, and 96.16% specificity. Precision was 95.27%, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) reached 0.9702. External testing achieved 91.4% accuracy, 91.0% sensitivity, 92.0% specificity, and 94.0% precision. Quantitative attribution analysis showed greater activation heterogeneity and stronger localized responses in PTC tissue. Non-PTC tissue showed broader and more uniform responses associated with preserved follicular morphology. The neuro-symbolic component subsequently organized compartment-level responses according to predefined thyroid cytopathology relationships. These outputs provide pathology-informed computational interpretation without constituting independent biomarker detection or expert-equivalent pathological reasoning.

Article.Title: Artificial Intelligence, climate policy uncertainty, and renewable energy transition: nonlinear evidence on sustainable energy resilience
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Grace S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The transition toward renewable energy is central to achieving sustainable development and climate mitigation objectives. At the same time, artificial intelligence (AI) and climate governance have emerged as critical forces shaping the pace and resilience of clean energy transformation. Despite growing attention to these factors, limited evidence exists regarding their nonlinear and asymmetric influences on renewable energy performance. This study investigates the asymmetric effects of AI development and climate policy uncertainty (CPU) on renewable energy transition using monthly data spanning 2013 to 2023. Employing a nonlinear autoregressive distributed lag (NARDL) framework, AI and CPU are decomposed into positive and negative partial shocks to capture heterogeneous short-run and long-run responses. The empirical results reveal pronounced asymmetries in the renewable energy transition process. Negative shocks to AI development generate larger and more persistent adverse effects on renewable energy performance than positive AI shocks generate benefits, indicating that disruptions in digital innovation substantially weaken the resilience of sustainable energy systems. Likewise, adverse climate policy uncertainty shocks exert stronger and longer-lasting impacts than favorable policy developments, increasing investment risk, delaying clean energy deployment, and weakening confidence in long-term low-carbon planning. Dynamic multiplier analysis confirms gradual adjustment toward long-run equilibrium, highlighting the presence of transition costs and delayed adaptation mechanisms within renewable energy markets. Furthermore, financial conditions and conventional energy prices significantly influence renewable energy performance through market-based transmission channels. Overall, the findings demonstrate that resilient renewable energy transitions depend on sustained technological innovation, stable climate governance, and supportive financial environments. By uncovering the asymmetric interactions between AI, policy uncertainty, and renewable energy dynamics, this study contributes to the emerging literature on sustainable development and offers policy insights for strengthening energy transition resilience and accelerating progress toward long-term decarbonization goals.

Article.Title: Spatial heterogeneity in PM₂.₅ mitigation from a 25% biomass burning scaling over northern Thailand using WRF-Chem
Article.Authors: Chakhamrun N.; Thepanondh S.; Sooktawee S.; Sirithian D.; Keawboonchu J.; Malakan W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Northern Thailand experiences severe PM₂.₅ pollution during the dry season from biomass burning, yet the response to incremental emission reductions remains poorly quantified. Using WRF-Chem v4.4, we simulated a 25% biomass-burning emission reduction scenario (Red25, i.e., fire emissions scaled to 75% of Base) over northern Thailand during 1–15 February 2020, evaluated against 15 Pollution Control Department (PCD) stations at 07:00 LT within a two-domain nested system (12 km and 4 km; analyzed at 4 km). The Base simulation showed limited quantitative skill (normalized mean bias − 42.9%, station-averaged correlation 0.25) and substantial meteorological biases, including warm (+ 3.58 °C), dry (− 35.23%), and wind-speed (+ 423%) biases, which constrain confidence in the modeled response magnitude. The Red25 scenario revealed pronounced spatial heterogeneity in the modeled, upper-bound decrease: station-level reductions ranged from 92.1% to 95.5% (station-averaged: 25.1 µg m⁻³, 93.8%), largest in high-fire-density provinces and smallest in urban centers. Across the gridded domain, ΔPM₂.₅ ranged from − 0.5 to − 80.6 µg m⁻³ (domain-averaged: −20.5 µg m⁻³, 88.4%). The mitigation signal showed a suggestive, though not statistically significant, association with temperature bias ( r = − 0.40, p = 0.22) and humidity bias ( r = − 0.46, p = 0.15) at 11 co-located stations. This heterogeneity indicates that uniform emission targets would likely yield heterogeneous benefits, and spatially differentiated strategies may be more effective for policy. However, given the model’s limited skill and exploratory design, the simulated reduction magnitude should be interpreted as an upper-bound diagnostic of model sensitivity, not a validated prediction of real-world air-quality improvement.

Article.Authors: González-Fernández R.; García-Díaz J.; Timbilla A.; Kuneš J.; Jenčo J.; Bokhari S.; Heredia-Díaz Y.; Escalona-Arranz J.; Janďourek O.; Konečná K.; Malaník M.; Rojas-Vargas J.; Havelek R.; Cahlíková L.; Chlebek J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Zanthoxylum flavum subsp. pistaciifolium (Griseb). Reynel (Rutaceae) is an endemic Cuban plant traditionally used for respiratory infections. This study evaluates the antimycobacterial and cytotoxic potential of its leaves, leading to the isolation of six known compounds characterized by LC-MS, 1D/2D NMR, and ECD spectra. The crude ethanolic extract ( ZPE ) exhibited moderate activity against M. kansasii (MIC = 31.25 µg/mL), while the hexane-butanone fraction ( A ) was active against M. kansasii and M. tuberculosis H37Ra (MICs of 31.25 and 62.5 µg/mL). From the fraction A , skimmianine ( 1 ), γ -fagarine ( 2 ), ( S )-clausenaside G ( 3 ), ( S )-marmesin ( 4 ) were isolated. Compound 2 was identified as the main bioactive constituent, exhibiting good activity against M. kansasii (MIC = 3.91 µg/mL) and moderate effects against M. tuberculosis H37Ra (MIC = 31.25 µg/mL), M. aurum , and M. avium (MICs = 62.50 µg/mL). In contrast, the fraction ethyl acetate ( B ) and its isolated flavonoid glycosides ( 5 and 6 ) were inactive at the highest concentration tested (MICs ≥ 250 µg/mL). An additive effect was observed when γ -fagarine was combined with rifampicin against M. kansasii using the checkerboard assay, which could be considered as a basis for adjuvant therapy. Molecular docking suggested potential interactions of γ -fagarine with several mycobacterial proteins, particularly DprE1, MmpL3, and DNA gyrase. These computational predictions provide hypotheses for subsequent target-based studies but do not establish direct protein inhibition or a mechanism of antimycobacterial action. Moreover, γ -fagarine exhibited cytotoxicity against the carcinoma cell lines A549, A2780, and MCF‑7 at 10 µM, while no toxicity was observed against MRC-5 (the non-carcinoma cell line of lung fibroblasts). These findings support the traditional medicinal use of this species and highlight its potential as a source of metabolites with dual‑interest scaffolds for antimycobacterial and anticancer drug development.

Article.Title: A framework to determine the optimum number and configuration of wastewater treatment plants
Article.Authors: Mansour D.; Mahdi I.; Ebid A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Clean water is essential for life, ecosystems, and economic development. As water treatment technologies advance and sewage systems grow more complex, wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) are essential for protecting public health and water resources. However, constructing these plants—particularly in developing countries—remains economically and technically challenging. This research investigates the optimum number and configuration of wastewater treatment plants (WWTP) for certain zones considering their served area, aspect ratio, and population density. The research methodology is developed to evaluate six different plant configurations, ranging from a single WWTP to four WWTPs. A parametric study is conducted to assess the impact of these three key factors on the total cost of the system, including pipes networks, pump stations, and treatment facilities, and excluding land acquisition and operational costs and considering plant cost model depending on number of buildings. The results clarify that land area is the strongest predictor of total system cost, while population density has a weak effect. The aspect ratio of the service area plays a secondary role, with ratios between 1.0 and 1.5 minimizing costs. Among the six configurations, Alternative 1 (Single WWTP) delivers the lowest total cost when WWTP cost is relatively high compared with network cost. On the opposite side, Alternative 6 (four WWTPs) becomes optimal when WWTP cost is relatively low. These findings provide engineers and urban planners with a practical framework for making early-stage decisions about wastewater infrastructure.

Article.Authors: Khan M.; Fayaz A.; Mobin J.; Alam A.; Shah A.; Elhenawy A.; Shah S.; AlAsmari A.; Alasmari F.; Alam A.
Article.Abstract: In this research, a new series of thiazole-based hydrazone derivatives (9–14) was designed, synthesized, and evaluated for α-amylase inhibitory activity as a strategy to manage postprandial hyperglycemia in type 2 diabetes (T2DM). Compound 10 , bearing an ortho -nitro substituent, was the most active (IC 50 = 1.04 µM), while the dimethoxy analogue 14 showed the weakest activity. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations at the B3PW91/D3/6 31G** level revealed that the high potency of 10 correlates with the highest electrophilicity index (ω = 4.04 eV) and the most negative chemical potential (μ = –3.816 eV). Molecular docking against human pancreatic α-amylase (PDB ID: 3BAJ) demonstrated that compound 10 establishes favorable binding interactions through hydrogen bonds with Asp197 and Tyr62, and electrostatic contacts with Glu233. The combined experimental and computational approach identifies the ortho -nitro-substituted thiazole scaffold as a promising preliminary hit for further development as α-amylase inhibitors.

This pioneering effort in preparing stable hilsa mince stock highlights its potential as a nutrient-rich value-added product from oily fish mince, supporting its commercial viability and contribution to fish-based food innovation.

Article.Abstract: In the quest to improve crash safety in automotive structures, lightweight energy absorbing lattice architectures have gained considerable attention. This study presents a combined numerical and experimental investigation of additively manufactured uniform and functionally graded (FG) lattice structures for automotive crash-box applications. Four lattice topologies Body-Centered Cubic (BCC), Body-Centered Cubic with vertical stiffeners (BCCz), Octet Truss, and Re-entrant Auxetic are evaluated under quasi-static and dynamic loading conditions. The novelty lies in the comparative analysis of multiple lattice topologies and the development of functionally graded Re-entrant auxetic lattices under identical loading conditions. Parametric models with varying unit cell size, strut thickness, and re-entrant angle are developed and analysed using finite element simulations. Among all configurations, the Re-entrant Auxetic lattice shows superior deformation stability and specific energy absorption behaviour. Uniform lattices with different packing factors and FG lattices with layer-wise density variation are further investigated under quasi-static compression and impact loading. The functionally graded re-entrant auxetic lattice exhibited approximately 17.9% higher specific energy absorption (SEA) than the corresponding uniform lattice, indicating improved crashworthiness performance. Finally, the optimized FG lattice is integrated into a crash box, which absorbs more energy (72,343 J vs. 69,654 J) and has a higher specific energy absorption (38.54 vs. 37.39 kJ/kg) than the uniform-lattice crash box, with a smoother force response, although at the cost of a higher peak crushing force and a lower crash force efficiency (0.61 vs. 0.72). These results indicate the potential of FG lattices for lightweight automotive crashworthiness applications.

Algebraic active-power balances coordinate grid-connected, interconnected, islanded, and self-healing modes according to generation–load imbalance and neighboring support capability. Battery operation is constrained by a 20–90% state-of-charge (SoC) range, 0.6 C charge/discharge limit, 70% depth-of-discharge constraint, and SoC-dependent derating. Small-signal converter models verify closed-loop stability across the four modes, including platform latency. Implementation uses a Real-Time Digital Simulator (RTDS) with 50 µs network and 2.5 µs converter time steps. Validation covers mode transitions, unbalanced and nonlinear loading, irradiance transients, prolonged islanding, and severe fault-plus-( N − 1) outage conditions. Over the 20 s sequence, PV supplies 72.95% of load energy, with battery storage, diesel generation, and grid support contributing 14.73%, 5.14%, and 7.19%. The maximum frequency excursion is 0.260 Hz, with primary arrest in 0.25 s and full restoration in 1.71 s. Current THD is 1.604% under nominal conditions and 2.492% with 30% nonlinear loading. During 90 min of islanding, 100% of critical-load energy is served with a final SoC of 21.66%. Under the severe-disturbance sequence, self-healing provides 12.4–17.6 kW of inter-MG support without load disconnection and reduces frequency restoration time by 39.0%. Energy not served is zero and the load-energy service ratio reaches 98.37%, confirming the dynamic, power-quality, storage-aware, and resilient real-time performance of the proposed HMLCS.

Article.Title: Residual-triggered active sensitivity estimation for topology-change detection and voltage control with MAPO-SOP
Article.Authors: Zheng Y.; Xu Y.; Yang Y.; Lu Y.; Weng D.; Jiang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Distribution-network reconfiguration changes the equivalent feeder impedance seen from a soft open point (SOP), thereby invalidating fixed-parameter analytical voltage-control models. This paper proposes a residual-triggered active sensitivity estimation method for model-assisted power optimization using an SOP (MAPO-SOP). An analytical point of common coupling (PCC) voltage model is first formulated to coordinate active and reactive power under the converter apparent-power constraint. Persistent voltage-prediction residuals are then used to identify potential model mismatch. Once triggered, a safety-oriented feedback controller returns the PCC voltage to a prescribed recovery band, after which a one-sided coordinated perturbation is applied to estimate the updated voltage–power sensitivity. The equivalent feeder parameters are subsequently reconstructed under the assumption that the X / R ratio remains approximately unchanged. In a 10-kV two-feeder system, the measured sensitivity-feature change indices were 33.58% and 57.44% for the two switching directions, with corresponding parameter errors of 2.8% and 0.2%. PV-only fluctuations did not trigger active estimation, whereas the combined PV/topology-change case was correctly identified with a parameter error of 0.42%. The proposed method enables temporary voltage containment and lightweight parameter adaptation without continuous probing or real-time topology communication.

Article.Title: Evaluating the effectiveness of coal bottom ash on the mechanical durability and microstructural characteristics of lightweight cellular concrete
Article.Authors: Al-Sodani K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Coal bottom ash (CBA), a byproduct of coal-based power plants, offers a potential route for reducing the environmental footprint of cement-based materials used to produce lightweight cellular concrete. This study experimentally investigates the influence of CBA as a partial cement replacement on the fresh, mechanical, durability, non-destructive, and microstructural properties of lightweight cellular concrete. For this purpose, six mixtures were developed at a target density of 1600 kg/m 3 . The whole experimental procedure includes a control mix, a mix having 5% silica fume (SF) only (S5CB0) and other mixes containing a constant 5% SF with 0–20% CBA replacement. Compressive strength (CS) and splitting tensile strength tests were performed along with ultrasonic pulse velocity (UPV) to assess the destructive and non-destructive properties. Furthermore, water absorption and rapid chloride permeability were measured to assess durability performance. In addition, scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive spectroscopy were evaluated for evaluating microstructural morphology. Based on the results, 10% CBA replacement achieved 8.85% and 10.59% increases in CS over the S5CB0 mix at 28 and 56 days, respectively. The same mix recorded UPV improvements of 11.74% and 8.52%, respectively. Furthermore, the chloride-ion charge passed decreased by 11.55% and 10.87% at 28 and 56 days, respectively, for 10% CBA replacement over the mix having 5% SF only. Microstructural observations and EDS results further supported the formation of a comparatively compact aluminosilicate-rich matrix at moderate CBA content. In addition, the 10% CBA and 5% SF combination reduced embodied CO 2 emissions by almost 8.95% relative to the S5CB0 mix. Overall, under the investigated conditions, 5% SF with 10% CBA combination provided balanced mechanical, durability, microstructural, and environmental performance.

Article.Title: Estimating chronological age from flicker-induced retinal vascular reactivity: a machine learning approach
Article.Authors: Assaf A.; Alsaify B.; AlJarrah O.; Li S.; Schmidt-Trucksaess A.; Kilani A.; Kotliar K.; Lanzl I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study proposes a novel, non-invasive approach to chronological age (CA) estimation by leveraging the Extra Trees Regressor to analyze retinal vessel reactivity to flicker light stimulation as a unique biomarker. By capturing and interpreting the dynamic responses of retinal blood vessels, we aim to develop an accessible and reliable tool for assessing chronological age, contributing to the emerging field of personalized anti-aging medicine through individualized insights into aging. Our method focuses on vascular function analysis using non-invasive dynamic vessel response measurements, offering a unique contribution compared to existing techniques. In this paper, multiple machine learning and deep learning models are employed to conduct experiments that estimate patient age using retinal arterial and venous vessel diameter changes across three flicker cycles. The best-performing model achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 9.3, a root mean squared error (RMSE) of 12.4, and a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) value of 17.7%, demonstrating acceptable reliability and accuracy. Additionally, the application of Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) to our time series age estimation model provided valuable insights into the key features influencing predictions. To our knowledge, this is the first study to demonstrate that retinal vascular reactivity can serve as a functional biomarker for estimating chronological age, providing a foundation for future research on non-invasive markers of aging.

Article.Title: Ultrasonic welding of Cu/Al cables: a study on the finite element model and characteristics of the gaps
Article.Authors: Cheng X.; Liu F.; Pan X.; Yang K.
Article.Abstract: A thermomechanical coupling model for the ultrasonic welding of Cu/Al cables was developed using Abaqus software. The effects of ultrasonic softening and thermal softening on the yield strength of Cu/Al cables are evaluated within the finite element model. By incorporating heat flux equivalent to frictional heat generation and the heat generated by plastic deformation at the weld interface, a highly efficient and accurate thermomechanical coupling model for the ultrasonic welding of Cu/Al cables was established. The accuracy of the model was verified by the temperature measurements and morphological analysis of the welded joints. The simulation results indicate that the stress concentration at the edges of the Al wire, leading to a reduction in the effective load-bearing area, is the primary cause of joint degradation. In addition, the results of the joint gap analysis indicate that the joint quality is optimal when the gap volume is approximately 2.36 mm 3 , with the tensile strength reaching 398.6 N (300 J).

Article.Title: Failure investigation and degradation study of long term hydrothermally stressed PVC reinforced with ZnO nanocomposites for cable insulation applications
Article.Authors: Faiza F.; Butt S.; Khattak A.; Mahmood A.; Khan Y.; AlKhalid K.
Article.Abstract: Water and temperature are critical environmental stresses that significantly affect the performance and longevity of insulation systems, particularly polymeric insulators. These factors lead to the degradation of the physical and chemical properties of polymers, ultimately resulting in failure. To investigate this, ZnO-based PVC nanocomposites (PZ0, PZ2, PZ4, and PZ6) were developed with varying concentrations of ZnO (0, 2, 4, and 6 phr). These nanocomposites were subjected to hydrothermal aging for 5000 h, divided into five cycles of 1000 h each, to assess their structural stability and performance over prolonged exposure to harsh conditions. Characterization of the nanocomposites was performed using techniques such as X-ray diffractometry (XRD), Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The analyses revealed that the nanocomposites generally outperformed neat PVC in terms of structural integrity and resistance to aging. Notably, PZ2 exhibited the highest contact angle of 78° after the aging period, indicating improved hydrophobicity. Additionally, surface roughness measurements showed that PZ2 had significantly less roughness compared to the other composites, suggesting better durability and performance against environmental stresses. The FTIR analysis highlighted substantial degradation of the polymer structure, with all samples experiencing over 80% chain scission after 5000 h of aging. In particular, PZ4 demonstrated 56% and 86% degradation in specific absorption bands related to -CH2 stretching and C–C bending. Thermal stability was assessed using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), which indicated that hydrothermal aging affected the melting points of the composites. Despite this, effective dispersion of the ZnO nanofiller within the polymer matrix provided enhanced stability, mitigating some adverse effects of aging. The failure analysis showed that PZ0 experienced 77% degradation after the first aging cycle, while PZ4, PZ0, and PZ6 exhibited 55%, 50%, and 66% degradation, respectively, underscoring the critical role of nanocomposite formulation in enhancing performance under environmental stress.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: zinc oxide nanocomposites; cable insulation; polymer nanocomposites; degradation; hydrothermal stress
