Article.Title: The role of boswellic acid/selenium nanocomposite in mitigating γ-irradiation testicular damage
Article.Authors: Sobeh E.; Salman F.; Kortam L.; Monir A.; Saleh H.; Ali A.; Elfeky S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract γ-radiation is widely used in human and veterinary medicine for diagnostic imaging and radiotherapy; however, exposure to ionizing radiation may induce oxidative stress, DNA damage, apoptosis, and reproductive dysfunction in both humans and animals. This study investigated the radioprotective efficacy of a boswellic acid–selenium nanocomposite (BA–Se NC) against γ-radiation–induced testicular injury in male Wistar rats as an experimental animal model. Selenium nanoparticles (Se NPs) were synthesized and conjugated with 3-O-acetyl-11-keto-β-boswellic acid, and then characterized by TEM, XRD, DLS, zeta potential analysis, and FTIR spectroscopy. Adult male rats were exposed to a single sublethal dose of γ-radiation (6 Gy) and treated orally with Se NPs, boswellic acid (BA), or BA–Se NC before and after irradiation. γ- irradiation caused marked testicular damage, evidenced by a significant reduction in testicular weight from 1.72 ± 0.05 g in controls to 0.55 ± 0.05 g in irradiated rats, accompanied by a decline in serum testosterone from 2.8 ± 0.057 to 0.58 ± 0.09 ng/mL and acid phosphatase activity from 34.6 ± 0.40 to 26.0 ± 0.19 U/L ( p ≤ 0.05). Irradiation also markedly increased DNA fragmentation, with testicular DNA damage rising from 6.46 ± 0.32% in controls to 36.76 ± 2.42%, accompanied by severe histopathological degeneration and altered apoptotic signaling characterized by upregulation of Bax and mTOR expression. Furthermore, irradiation caused a significant decline in sperm motility, viability, and morphology. Treatment with BA–Se NC significantly ameliorated these effects, restoring testicular weight to 1.34 ± 0.05 g, testosterone level to 2.9 ± 0.057 ng/mL, and acid phosphatase activity to 34.86 ± 0.54, while reducing testicular DNA damage to 9.16 ± 0.46% ( p ≤ 0.05). Histological examination further demonstrated near-normal preservation of seminiferous tubules and enhanced BCL-2 immunoexpression in BA–Se NC-treated rats. The nanocomposite exhibited superior radioprotective efficacy compared with either Se NPs or BA alone. These findings demonstrate that BA–Se NC exerts potent radioprotective effects against γ-radiation induced testicular damage through modulation of oxidative stress and apoptosis-related pathways. The combined nanotherapeutic approach offers mechanistic insight and promising translational potential for preserving reproductive function in animals exposed to ionizing radiation during veterinary and biomedical applications. This innovative study investigates the synergistic radioprotective potential of a BA–Se NC against γ-radiation induced testicular injury through integrated biochemical, molecular, genotoxic, histopathological, and immunohistochemical analyses.

Article.Title: Comparative evaluation of unilateral anterior crossbite and monoiodoacetate injection models for temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis in rats
Article.Authors: He Z.; Xiao Y.; Xie Q.; Jiang X.
Article.Abstract: To systematically compare unilateral anterior crossbite (UAC) and monosodium iodoacetate (MIA) models for temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJOA) research. This study used healthy adult male SPF-grade Sprague–Dawley (SD) rats, aged 6–8 weeks and weighing 180–200 g, with a total of 24 rats. After a 7-day acclimatization period, the rats were randomly and equally allocated into three groups: a normal control group (NC), an occlusion intervention group (UAC), and a drug injection group (MIA). Condylar height at the anterior, central, and posterior regions was quantitatively measured via a computer-aided image analysis system to elucidate the observed morphological alterations. Pathological assessments of the TMJ were conducted using Safranin O-Fast Green staining, hematoxylin and eosin (HE) staining, and immunohistochemistry (IHC). Both occlusion intervention and drug injection models exhibited cartilage degeneration with subchondral bone alterations evident on histological examination, a substantial reduction in chondrocyte count, and altered cellular morphology characterized by shrinkage. Furthermore, significant increases were observed in the Mankin score, OARSI score, and the number of positive inflammatory markers in both experimental groups compared to the control group. Notably, the drug injection group exhibited a more pronounced increase in these parameters compared to the occlusion intervention group. Under the tested conditions and observation period, the intra-articular MIA model produced more rapid and severe condylar degeneration than the UAC model, whereas the UAC model induced milder, progressively developing changes. Both models showed model-, dose-, and time-dependent characteristics, and neither fully recapitulates the complex pathogenesis of human TMJOA. Model selection should therefore be guided by the specific research question and the disease stage of interest, rather than by a general ranking of superiority.

Article.Title: Adaptive multi-scale YOLOv8s framework for defect detection in photovoltaic facilities
Article.Authors: Zuo X.; Dai Y.; Zhuang Y.; Chen J.; Almutairi A.; Zhou Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Photovoltaic (PV) modules are widely used in building-integrated photovoltaic systems and renewable energy infrastructure. Accurate defect detection is essential for improving the reliability, energy efficiency, and sustainable operation of PV systems. However, existing deep learning-based inspection methods still suffer from missed detections, imprecise localisation of small defects, and limited robustness under complex operating conditions due to variations in defect scales and background interference. This study proposes an adaptive multi-scale attention-enhanced YOLOv8s framework (AMA-YOLOv8s) for intelligent PV module defect detection. Compared with the baseline YOLOv8s, the proposed framework incorporates three newly designed modules specifically developed for PV defect detection: the Adaptive Bottleneck Attention Mechanism (ABAM), Multi-scale Adaptive Fusion Module (MSAFM), and Adaptive Pooling Fusion Module (APFM). ABAM is introduced to enhance defect-related feature representation and suppress irrelevant background information, whereas MSAFM and APFM are designed to strengthen multi-scale feature fusion and improve the detection of small and irregular defects. In addition, a comprehensive PV defect dataset was constructed by integrating publicly available images, field-collected samples, and data augmentation strategies. Experimental results show that AMA-YOLOv8s achieves a precision of 93.2%, an F1-score of 92.7%, and an mAP@0.5 of 93.5% on the current evaluation dataset. Compared with the YOLOv8s baseline, the AMA-YOLOv8s provides incremental improvements in detection performance while maintaining a comparable real-time inference speed. Its overall performance is competitive with the evaluated detectors, although recent lightweight YOLO variants retain advantages in some individual metrics and computational complexity. These results demonstrate the practical effectiveness of the proposed coordinated attention and multi-scale feature-fusion design for PV defect detection.

Article.Title: Amplified trunk-head contribution to whole-body angular momentum under perturbed conditions
Article.Authors: Nikolaidou M.; Theodorakis C.; Mademli L.; Mersmann F.; Bohm S.; Arampatzis A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The study’s objective was to establish whether and how the contributions of different body segments to whole-body angular momentum are modulated during unperturbed level walking, unpredictable and adapted drop-like perturbations and hole negotiation gait. Whole-body kinematics were recorded for 18 participants using an infrared motion capture system (250 Hz) and segmental and whole-body angular momentum were calculated in the sagittal, frontal, and transverse planes across three consecutive steps: preparation, perturbation, and recovery. Compared to level walking, trunk-head segment contributions significantly increased ( p < 0.001) and lower limb contributions significantly decreased ( p < 0.001) across all planes following both drop-like perturbations and hole negotiation gait, with the greatest modulation observed during unpredictable perturbations. Furthermore, the trunk-head segment’s contribution was associated with the increased peak-to-peak range of whole-body angular momentum ( p < 0.001), indicating functionally relevant involvement in regulating whole-body angular momentum under perturbed conditions. Given that the trunk-head segment contributes most to frontal plane whole-body angular momentum (~ 50%) and considering the rapid increase in frontal plane angular momentum following unpredictable drop-like perturbations, trunk movement may be important for controlling whole-body angular momentum in the frontal plane during perturbations . The findings could be used to develop preventive treatments by implementing trunk coordination strategies to enhance stability control.

Article.Title: Co-inoculation with Lactiplantibacillus plantarum and Bacillus amyloliquefaciens enhances the fermentation quality and in vitro ruminal digestibility of whole-plant millet silage
Article.Authors: He S.; Pei S.; Lv L.; Xiong F.; Li B.; Wu L.; Cao Z.; Li S.; Yang H.
Article.Abstract: Whole-plant millet is a climate-resilient alternative forage requiring ensiling optimization. This study evaluated single and combined bacterial inoculants on the fermentation quality and in vitro ruminal degradability of millet silage. Forage harvested at the grain-filling stage was ensiled for 60 days with sterile water (Negative Control), Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (L), Lactobacillus mucosae (M), or their combinations with Bacillus amyloliquefaciens (LB, MB) at 1 × 10 6 colony-forming units/g fresh matter, followed by a 72-h in vitro rumen assay. Compared with the control, bacterial inoculation significantly reduced silage pH (4.876 vs. 4.683–4.788, P < 0.001) and increased lactic acid concentration (2.543 vs. 2.938–3.450% of dry matter, P < 0.001) after 60 d ensiling. Inoculated silages also showed lower ammonia nitrogen concentrations (4.731 vs. 3.868–4.055 mg/dL, P < 0.001) and reduced neutral detergent fiber contents (59.675 vs. 58.213–58.574% of dry matter, P < 0.001). Consequently, inoculated silages yielded higher in vitro dry matter and fiber digestibility, alongside elevated volatile fatty acid concentrations. Notably, co-inoculating L. plantarum and B. amyloliquefaciens exhibited greatest fermentation efficiency, showing the highest asymptotic gas production and average gas production rate (AGPR) among all treatments ( P < 0.05). While a transient reduction in the proportion of ruminal methane occurred during early incubation (24–48 h, P < 0.05), it was not sustained by 72 h. Overall, multispecies bacterial inoculation improves the fermentative efficiency and nutritional degradability of whole-plant millet silage, optimizing sustainable roughage resources.

Article.Title: An AIoT-enabled framework for real-time predictive analytics and sustainable optimization in urban waste management systems
Article.Authors: Ullah H.; Kanwal A.; Ashraf N.; Gillani S.; Alazmi M.; Zalah I.; Alqahtani F.; Khan S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The high rate of urbanization and population growth has led to an increased generation of municipal waste, which poses challenges for environmental sustainability and efficient waste management. Most waste management systems are still manual, inefficient, non-scalable and can’t support intelligent real-time decision making, which are increasing costs, fuel consumption and environmental pollution. Despite recent developments in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT), current waste management systems have yet to achieve intelligent levels of predictive ability, interpretability and adaptability to complex urban conditions. The study suggests an AIoT based smart waste management system that fuses the features of the IoT based real-time sensing, cloud-edge computing, deep learning based predictive analytics, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), and sustainable route optimization approaches. The proposed framework uses smart bin sensors to constantly record waste levels and environmental conditions, and a stacked Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model is used to predict waste level and collection need in real time. Moreover, explainability techniques are integrated with SHAP analysis to enhance the transparency and trustworthiness of the model. Experimental evaluation was performed on those publicly available datasets of smart waste management, and synthetically generated IoT sensor data to create realistic urban waste scenarios 97.1% prediction accuracy, 96.8% precision, 97.0% recall, 96.9% F1-score, and a ROC-AUC score of 0.978, which outperforms the conventional machine learning methods like Random Forest, Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, KNN, and XGBoost. Further sustainability analysis shows that the fuel consumption has been reduced by 32% and that there were 35% fewer unnecessary collection trips and 72% fewer overflow cases. By combining real-time IoT sensing, explainable Artificial Intelligence and intelligent route optimization, the proposed AIoT-based framework enables smart city waste management with high accuracy, interpretability, scalability and eco-friendly operation for next-generation smart cities.

Article.Title: Hybrid optimization of multimodal SLAM for underground robots with seismic vibration geomagnetic and tactile sensing
Article.Authors: Fan X.; Sun B.; Zhang B.; Gao M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reliable underground SLAM remains difficult when GPS, visual features, LiDAR, or external anchors are unavailable or degraded, while non-visual sensors exhibit noise, drift, and environment-dependent uncertainty. We propose a hybrid-optimized seismic/vibration-geomagnetic-tactile SLAM framework that combines complementary sensor factors in a robust factor graph and uses staged COA-PSO-GSA optimization for automated parameter calibration. Evaluation covered 23 complete trajectories (10.2 km; approximately 7.5 h) from simulation, controlled underground corridors, and field tunnel/mine environments, with non-overlapping trajectory-level optimization, validation, and testing subsets. On the test trajectories, mean absolute trajectory error was 0.53 m, convergence occurred in approximately 37 iterations, and error growth remained between 1.81% and 4.09% under the evaluated magnetic, vibration, and tactile degradation conditions. Loop-detection AUC was 0.76, but its difference from the strongest GWO-SLAM baseline (0.74) was not statistically significant after Holm correction (adjusted p = 0.184). The measured foreground update latency was 57 ± 10 ms (approximately 17.5 Hz), indicating near-real-time online operation on the tested platform rather than hard real-time performance. These results support technical feasibility under the tested conditions, while broader claims require larger multi-site validation.

Article.Title: Associations of serum phosphate levels and intravenous phosphate exposure with mortality in patients with sepsis: a multi-database retrospective study
Article.Authors: He J.; Sheng Y.; Liao X.; Chen J.; Li F.; Xu S.; Zhang D.
Article.Abstract: Abnormal phosphate concentrations are common in sepsis, but the prognostic relevance of serum phosphate and the association between recorded intravenous phosphate exposure and mortality remain uncertain. This retrospective cohort study used MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, and a single-center database from the First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University. Adults with ICD-coded sepsis, a first ICU admission, and an ICU stay longer than 24 h were included. Admission phosphate was evaluated with restricted cubic spline regression for 28- and 90-day mortality. Recorded intravenous phosphate exposure was assessed using multivariable logistic regression in the 48- and 72-h landmark populations. Propensity-score matching and inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting were performed at both landmarks. A target-trial emulation was also performed. Cohorts 1 and 2 included 15,426 and 967 patients, respectively. Admission phosphate was nonlinearly associated with 28- and 90-day mortality (overall P < 0.001 for both outcomes). Recorded intravenous phosphate exposure by 48 h was associated with lower adjusted odds of 28-day mortality (OR, 0.799; 95% CI 0.704–0.907; P < 0.001). The 72-h estimate was similar (OR, 0.814; 95% CI 0.720–0.920; P < 0.001). The 48- and 72-h PSM and IPTW estimates were similar (OR, 0.801–0.847; all P < = 0.007). In cohort 2, the association was not statistically significant (OR, 0.766; 95% CI 0.441–1.328; P = 0.342). Admission serum phosphate provided nonlinear prognostic information for 28- and 90-day mortality in critically ill patients with sepsis. Recorded intravenous phosphate exposure at fixed landmarks was associated with lower 28-day mortality in MIMIC, but this association was not significant in cohort 2. These findings suggest that serum phosphate monitoring and individualized phosphate management should receive greater attention in patients with sepsis. Prospective studies are needed to further validate causality and determine the optimal intervention strategy.

Article.Title: SRT-YOLO11: a lightweight network for shortwave signal classification under low SNR conditions
Article.Authors: Xu S.; Guo J.; Zhu R.; Zhang Y.; Wang F.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Automatic classification of shortwave communication signals at low signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs) remains challenging because discriminative time-frequency features are readily masked by strong noise, particularly in spectrum monitoring and non-cooperative communication reconnaissance. Here, we propose SRT-YOLO11, a lightweight classification model built upon the YOLO11n-cls backbone. Three complementary modules—Spatial Pyramid Pooling Fast (SPPF), RepVGG-DW, and Triplet Attention—are sequentially embedded after the C2PSA block, enhancing multi-scale time-frequency perception, local texture representation, and noise suppression via cross-dimensional recalibration, respectively. The model is evaluated on a nine-class spectrogram classification task covering typical shortwave signals and a BACKGROUND noise class for false-alarm assessment. In the reported seed-2026 run, across the SNR range of -20 to -2 dB, SRT-YOLO11 achieves an average accuracy of 36.66% and a macro-averaged F1-score of 35.13%, surpassing the baseline by 0.90 and 0.94% points, respectively, with only 0.18 M additional parameters. The ablation results quantify module interactions. Across four training seeds (2026–2029), the mean accuracy is 36.72% for SRT-YOLO11 and 35.89% for the baseline; the paired improvement is + 0.82% points (95% CI: +0.44 to + 1.20, p = 0.006). These results demonstrate that SRT-YOLO11 provides an effective and parameter-efficient solution on the evaluated synthetic AWGN benchmark; generalization to operational channels remains to be established.

Article.Title: Effect of occlusal loading and crown material on stress and strain distribution in bone around 4-mm ultra-short implants: a 3D-FEA
Article.Authors: Renno F.; Gasparro R.; Mariniello M.; Aliberti A.; Garcia-Godoy F.; Lanzotti A.; Ausiello P.
Article.Abstract: Ultra-short (4-mm) dental implants represent a minimally invasive solution for the rehabilitation of posterior atrophic regions; however, concerns remain regarding stress and strain concentration in bone around implants under functional loading. This study aimed to evaluate the influence of occlusal loading conditions, prosthetic configuration, and crown material on stress and strain distribution using three-dimensional finite element analysis (3D-FEA). Three-dimensional finite element models of single-crown restorations and the splinted two-crown configuration supported by 4-mm ultra-short implants were developed. Zirconia and composite resin crowns were evaluated under vertical and 30° oblique loading, with and without a simulated food bolus. The bolus was assigned a Young’s modulus of 10 MPa and a Poisson’s ratio of 0.30. Primary outcomes were volume-weighted mean von Mises stress and equivalent elastic strain within a fixed 0.50-mm peri-implant volumetric region of interest (ROI). Mesh convergence was assessed using three nominal local refinement levels and a 5% acceptance threshold. In single-crown models without bolus, oblique loading increased cortical ROI stress from approximately 10.01 to 43.02 MPa and trabecular ROI stress from approximately 4.95 to 12.35 MPa. With bolus interposition, corresponding oblique values decreased to approximately 19.57 and 5.63 MPa. In models of the splinted two-crown configuration, cortical ROI stress under oblique loading ranged from 8.63 to 10.43 MPa. Zirconia and composite resin produced nearly identical ROI outcomes in the single-crown configurations, whereas a modest configuration-specific difference was observed under oblique loading in the splinted two-crown configuration. All primary outcomes met the 5% convergence criterion. Within the assumptions of this finite element model, loading direction and prosthetic configuration had greater effects on peri-implant stress and strain than crown material. Bolus interposition reduced the ROI outcomes under oblique loading. Under the modeled oblique conditions, the splinted two-crown configuration was associated with lower peri-implant ROI outcomes than the single-crown configuration; however, the different total loads prevent isolation of splinting as an independent causal factor. These comparative findings do not establish clinical superiority or biomechanical reliability and require experimental and clinical validation.

Article.Title: Kinematic modeling and dual-strategy heuristic screening of ductile hinge layout for multi-body coordinated incremental launching of spatial curve bridges
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Xiao L.; Li M.; Chen L.; Wang M.; Zheng H.; Zhu H.
Article.Abstract: Multi-body coordinated incremental launching (MCIL) provides a construction route for spatially curved bridges under constrained sites, but full-stage geometric posture and ductile-hinge layout still require efficient pre-construction evaluation. This study develops a geometric-kinematic framework based on composite rigid bodies (CRBs) and couples it with a dual-strategy heuristic for ductile-hinge layout. The CRB system is updated through chainage-based boundary lookup, and spatial posture is obtained with a safeguarded endpoint-based Rodrigues transformation. The heuristic combines a proximity rule for lateral-deviation exceedance with global candidate assessment for height-difference exceedance; it seeks a feasible low-cardinality layout. For a 1991 m, 36,000 tonne steel box-girder viaduct, one 772 state simulation required approximately 14 s. Five hinge additions reduced the maximum lateral deviation from 2.997 to 0.911 m and the maximum height difference from 1.727 to 0.586 m. Internal geometric and convergence checks support numerical consistency. In 100 fixed-layout simulations with independent 10 mm coordinate perturbations, the fixed layout remained within the 1.0 m and 0.8 m constraints. This study links kinematic simulation to hinge-layout screening, providing a quantitative design tool for MCIL of spatially variable curve bridges.

Article.Title: Effect of impaction on the performance of the CBCT-based third molar maturity index (I3M) for the 18-year age threshold
Article.Authors: Diricanlı M.; Akkaya N.; Zengin H.
Article.Abstract: The third molar maturity index (I3M), the ratio of the summed open-apex widths to tooth length of the mandibular third molar, assesses whether an individual has reached 18 years. We examined how impaction affects the classification performance of the I3M at the 18 year threshold. The I3M measurements were performed on 744 mandibular third molars on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) scans. Sensitivity, specificity, and AUC were compared between impacted and non-impacted molars, and the effect of impaction on correct classification was tested using age-adjusted generalized estimating equations. Discrimination did not differ significantly between groups (AUC, p = 0.12); instead, impaction shifted the error pattern. At the 0.08 cut-off, impacted molars showed lower sensitivity (0.68 vs 0.91) and reduced odds of correct classification (adjusted OR 0.34, 95% CI 0.19–0.59; p < 0.001), misclassifying adults as minors, whereas non-impacted molars more often misclassified minors as adults. Specificity reached the ≥ 90% level required in criminal contexts for impacted (0.95) but not non-impacted molars (0.54), although the latter was based on only 24 molars from minors. Impaction status should be considered when applying the I3M; a lower cut-off may be needed for non-impacted molars, but larger, age-balanced studies are required to establish it.

Article.Title: A semantic-conditioned multi-modal behavior cloning framework for terrain-specific behavior isolation in humanoid locomotion
Article.Authors: Ahmed A.; Doss A.; Hency V.
Article.Abstract: Humanoid locomotion across heterogeneous terrains requires terrain-specific behaviors to be selected without unwanted interference between learned skills. This work investigates whether a semantic terrain label can act as a deterministic condition for selecting pre-trained terrain-specific behaviors while preserving behavioral isolation. Two terrain-specific reference policies were independently trained using Proximal Policy Optimization for flat-ground and stairway locomotion of the Unitree H1 humanoid. Their demonstrations were collected as trajectories and used to train a Unified Multi-modal Behavior Cloning (UMBC) policy with dedicated encoders for proprioception, terrain geometry, and semantic terrain identity. The semantic terrain identity is represented using a learned embedding and explicitly conditions a shared policy head for joint-action prediction. The proposed policy achieved an overall test-set action MAE of 0.016349 and RMSE of 0.025733, with a best validation loss of 0.000367. In simulator-only closed-loop deployment, the UMBC policy recovered $$94.73\%$$ and $$93.07\%$$ of the reference-policy rewards on flat-ground and stairway terrains, respectively. Counterfactual terrain-label analysis produced non-zero action changes across the independent test-set, with mean $$L_2$$ prediction distances of 0.5019 and 0.5187 for flat-to-stairway and stairway-to-flat label changes, respectively. Deployment experiments demonstrated terrain-transition capability and evaluated transition delays and locomotion robustness under external perturbations. Ablation experiments showed that adaptive terrain-dependent weighting slightly improved performance on the more difficult stairway terrain but reduced performance on flat-terrain, while one-hot, no-label, and encoder-free concatenation variants resulted in reduced terrain-specific performance relative to the proposed architecture. These results support semantic terrain conditioning as an explicit mechanism for selecting terrain-specific behaviors within a single policy.

Article.Title: Antibacterial activity of ferrocene-derived multi-walled carbon nanotubes synthesized by chemical vapor deposition against Escherichia coli
Article.Authors: Ahmed S.; Taay Y.; Ahmed A.; Khudhayer H.; Hussein S.; Abbas Z.
Article.Abstract: Multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) were synthesized by chemical vapor deposition (CVD) using ferrocene as the carbon and iron-catalyst precursor and were evaluated for antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli ATCC 25,922. The as-grown material was characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman spectroscopy, field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX). The characterization results confirmed the formation of graphitized multi-walled nanotube structures and the presence of iron-containing residues derived from the ferrocene precursor. Antibacterial activity was assessed by agar well diffusion, broth microdilution, and viable-count plating. A concentration-dependent reduction in bacterial growth was observed over the tested range of 1–512 µg/mL. The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) was determined to be 256 µg/mL based on the absence of visible bacterial growth, with blank-corrected quantitative measurements providing supplementary confirmation of the inhibitory endpoint. Viable-count analysis on drug-free Mueller–Hinton agar showed no recoverable colonies at 256 and 512 µg/mL, supporting a minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) of 256 µg/mL under the experimental conditions. In the agar well-diffusion assay, inhibition-zone diameters were 26, 21, 19, 9, and 7 mm at 512, 256, 128, 64, and 32 µg/mL, respectively, whereas no inhibition was observed in the negative control. These findings demonstrate concentration-dependent antibacterial activity of the as-grown ferrocene-derived MWCNT preparation against E. coli ATCC 25,922. Because the material was evaluated without post-synthesis purification, the observed activity represents the response to the as-grown preparation, including potential contributions from synthesis-derived components.

Article.Title: Platelet to white blood cell ratio and short term mortality in critically ill patients with HFpEF
Article.Authors: Cao Z.; Chen Z.; Wei Y.; Liu S.; Li Y.; Liu Y.; Dong G.
Article.Abstract: Critically ill patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) require early and practical risk assessment. The platelet-to-white blood cell ratio (PWR), derived from routine blood counts, may reflect the balance between platelet availability and leukocyte-driven inflammatory stress. Its prognostic value in ICU patients with HFpEF remains uncertain. Methods: We performed a retrospective cohort study using MIMIC-IV v3.1 for derivation and primary analyses and eICU v2.0.1 for exploratory external assessment. Eligible participants were adult ICU patients with HFpEF. PWR was defined from the first platelet and white blood cell measurements recorded within 24 h after ICU admission. The primary endpoint in MIMIC-IV was 28-day all-cause mortality. Because eICU did not provide uniform post-discharge follow-up for determining 28-day mortality, in-hospital mortality was used only for an exploratory external assessment and was not considered an endpoint-matched validation outcome. Analyses included Kaplan–Meier curves, Cox models, restricted cubic splines, subgroup testing, Boruta selection, machine learning and SHAP interpretation. Incremental prognostic value was evaluated using nested fixed-horizon logistic models, repeated cross-validation, discrimination, calibration, reclassification and decision-curve analysis. Results: MIMIC-IV contributed 5774 patients, including 632 deaths within 28 days (10.95%). After full adjustment, mortality risk was lower in higher PWR quartiles than in Q1: Q2, hazard ratio (HR) 0.79 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.64–0.96, P = 0.020); Q3, HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.46–0.72, P < 0.001); and Q4, HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.49–0.76, P < 0.001; P for trend < 0.001). Restricted cubic splines supported a nonlinear pattern. Among the five machine-learning approaches, random forest showed the highest discrimination in the internal holdout test set, with an AUROC of 0.813 and an AUPRC of 0.387. Conventional unpenalized logistic regression using the same 15 predictors achieved an AUROC of 0.792 and an AUPRC of 0.389, indicating only a modest difference between the two modelling approaches. After the locked model specification was refitted using the complete MIMIC-IV cohort and applied to eICU (n = 685; in-hospital mortality, 13.3%), the AUROC was 0.767 (95% CI 0.715–0.817). Although adding nonlinear PWR to the clinical baseline improved full-sample model fit (likelihood-ratio P = 0.012), the cross-validated AUC changed only from 0.763 to 0.764. Calibration remained comparable, and decision-curve analysis showed no consistent gain in net benefit. Conclusions: Among ICU patients with HFpEF who survived and remained in the ICU for at least 24 h, higher PWR was independently associated with lower 28-day mortality, and the association was nonlinear. Its incremental predictive contribution beyond comprehensive severity indicators was modest. Because PWR is derived from routine blood counts, it may provide an accessible complementary risk signal.

Article.Title: Bacterial–fungal shifts and functional reprogramming in CDI: insights from matched metagenomic and metatranscriptomic profiling
Article.Authors: Rossman S.; See J.; Khedekar M.; Tong L.; Yalcinanahtar S.; Misra M.; Johnson E.; Watt D.; Chheda K.; Wright J.; Ramakrishnan P.; McMullen B.; Roth K.; Lamendella R.
Article.Abstract: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a leading cause of antibiotic-associated diarrhea, yet most microbiome studies have focused on bacterial composition, overlooking fungal contributions and transcriptionally active functions. Here, we applied matched metagenomic (MG) and metatranscriptomic (MT) sequencing to diarrheal stool from 100 adults (50 CDI+, 50 CDI−) to characterize taxonomic structure, functional potential and expression, predicted metabolites, and bacterial–fungal interactions. CDI− samples exhibited relatively greater taxonomic evenness, whereas CDI+ samples showed relatively higher MT KEGG Ortholog richness, indicating broader transcriptional activity. Beta diversity analyses demonstrated significant separation by CDI status, strongest in MT functional profiles. CDI+ microbiomes were enriched for opportunistic and transcriptionally active taxa, including C. difficile , Lactococcus cremoris , Nitratidesulfovibrio vulgaris , and fungi such as Candida albicans and Nakaseomyces glabratus , while CDI− communities were relatively enriched for obligate anaerobic commensals (e.g., Faecalibacterium , Roseburia , Subdoligranulum ). Functionally, CDI+ communities were relatively enriched in transport, stress-response, motility, quorum sensing, and amino acid metabolism pathways, whereas CDI− retained core metabolic functions. Network analyses identified significant enrichment of fungal-commensal co-exclusion relationships in the CDI+ metatranscriptomic network relative to CDI-, and predicted metabolites implicated bile acid disruption and lipid remodeling. Together, these findings define CDI as a trans-kingdom, functionally reprogrammed ecosystem and highlight the importance of integrating fungal ecology and transcriptional activity in CDI pathogenesis.

Article.Title: CT radiomic features detect mineral, collagen, and water contributions to cortical bone texture
Article.Authors: Lee Y.; Bandara W.; Jalaie P.; Hong S.; Chin C.; Jain S.; Kasumarthi N.; Warden S.; Surowiec R.
Article.Abstract: Without knowing which compositional properties drive specific features, radiomics cannot move from empirical association toward mechanistic interpretation. This gap is particularly relevant in several metabolic bone diseases where collagen and water abnormalities contribute to skeletal fragility despite sometimes preserved bone mineral density. Ten cortical cross-sections from a single fresh human cadaveric femur underwent stepwise selective removal of mineral (hydrochloric acid), collagen (sodium hypochlorite), and free and bound water (thermal treatment). Specimens were imaged by high-resolution peripheral quantitative computed tomography (HR-pQCT) at baseline, halfway, and full removal. Compositional loss was confirmed by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry and thermogravimetric analysis. Radiomic features were selected through variance filtering, correlation thresholding, and bootstrap stability ranking, with group comparisons by one-way ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis test. Each compositional component produced distinct, reproducible radiomic signatures. Mineral removal drove the largest radiodensity change, with Maximum intensity decreasing 13.5% at full demineralization accompanied by a greater than twofold increase in Contrast. Collagen removal generated biphasic responses in surface geometry, with Mesh Surface expanding 2.8% at halfway removal before contracting below baseline at full removal. Despite CT’s limited sensitivity to organic matrix, both water compartments produced measurable texture changes: free water removal progressively narrowed grayscale Range by 6.4%, while bound water removal produced distinct shifts in spatial Complexity and intensity Range. CT radiomic features are sensitive to mineral, collagen, and water contributions to cortical bone texture, including components conventionally considered invisible to density-based imaging. These preliminary findings suggest that individual cortical bone matrix components may produce distinct radiomic feature behaviors in a controlled ex vivo model, providing an initial compositional basis for interpreting bone texture in HR-pQCT images and informing the development of composition-aware imaging biomarkers for metabolic bone diseases.

Article.Title: Development and validation of a machine learning-based diagnostic model for depression in young populations: a retrospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Shi K.; Guo Y.; You T.
Article.Abstract: Depression in 10–26 years is often subtle but can greatly affect their physical and mental development. This study aims to develop a machine learning model for the diagnosis of depression. Data were collected from 600 patients aged 10–26 years between 2019 and 2025, including 350 non-depressed patients and 250 depressed patients. A gradient boosting machine (GBM) was used to build the model, shapley additive explanations (SHAP) plots employed for model interpretation and visualization. Based on Boruta feature selection, nine variables were identified for machine learning model construction: S100β, platelet(PLT), lactate dehydrogenase(LDH), white blood cell(WBC), creatinine kinase-mb(CK-Mb), gender, and LDH/PLT Ratio, LDH/WBC Ratio, LDH/HGB Ratio. The GBM showed the best performance with a threshold of 0.591, Accuracy of 0.878, Specificity of 0.941, and Precision of 0.913. It also demonstrated high levels of Sensitivity (0.797) and F1 Score (0.851). The decision curve analysis and calibration curve assessed the clinical validity and consistency of the model, indicating that the GBM model outperformed others. The most significant features identified were S100β, PLT, and LDH/PLT. By utilizing machine learning, key factors such as S100β, PLT, and LDH/PLT were identified, providing preliminary evidence for the diagnosis of depression in patients aged 10–26 years.

Article.Authors: Martínez-Gómez L.; Valle-Rivera E.; Martinez-Armenta C.; Vidal-Vázquez R.; Ramírez-Hinojosa J.; Vázquez-Cárdenas P.; Rodríguez-Pérez J.; Mata-Miranda M.; Vázquez-Zapién G.; Martínez-Cuazitl A.; de Martínez-Ruiz F.; Zayago-Angeles D.; Ordoñez-Sánchez M.; Segura-Kato Y.; Ramos-Tavera L.; Suarez-Ahedo C.; Herrera-López B.; García-Chávez D.; Flores-Robles D.; Madrigal A.; Pineda C.; Martínez-Nava G.; López-Reyes A.

The T allele (rs1769793) showed a lower oxygen saturation distribution. In addition, after Bonferroni correction, the rs1769793 CT allele of the codominant model showed an OR = 3.2 (95% CI = 1.42–7.5; P = 0.005), and the CT + TT allele of dominant model had an OR = 3.01 (95% CI = 1.37–6.58; P = 0.006), both were associated with an increased risk of death. Article.Abstract: This study introduces a physics-informed and climate-responsive optimization framework of Double Skin Façade (DSF) design to reduce the operational CO 2 emissions and preserve thermal and ventilation functions. The PI-GAT model outperforms conventional machine learning methods (ANN, RF, and XGBoost) by achieving higher accuracy and improved robustness, particularly under nonlinear and extreme design conditions, due to the incorporation of physical constraints governing airflow and heat transfer. The model is tested on two opposite climates: Tashkent (cold-dominant) and Najran (hot-arid). Findings show that optimum DSF schemes are capable of decreasing operational CO 2 emissions by 13–23% and 8–20% in comparison with baseline scenarios, respectively. Pareto analysis shows that there are unique climate-dependent trade-offs in which ventilation needs to be tightly regulated in cold climates but improved in hot climates to attain carbon-efficient operation. Article.Title: The chain mediating roles of career planning and future time perspective between AI literacy and employment anxiety among higher vocational college students
Article.Authors: Xiong Y.; Yu J.; Wu H.
Article.Abstract: Against the background of artificial intelligence (AI) reshaping the labor market, employment anxiety among higher vocational college students is becoming increasingly prominent. Grounded in Career Construction Theory, this study aims to explore the relationship between AI literacy and employment anxiety among Chinese higher vocational college students, with a specific focus on the chain mediating roles of career planning and future time perspective. A total of 1,234 students from five industry-featured higher vocational colleges in Jiangxi Province, China, were surveyed using self-report scales measuring AI literacy, employment anxiety, career planning, and future time perspective. The relationships among these variables were tested using the PROCESS macro (Model 6) for SPSS. The results indicated that (1) all variables were significantly correlated with one another; (2) AI literacy exhibited a significant positive total association with employment anxiety, which decomposed into a substantial positive direct association and a negative total indirect association; (3) AI literacy exerted a significant negative indirect association on employment anxiety through three pathways, namely, the independent mediating roles of career planning and future time perspective, and their chain mediating role, while the total association remained positive. These findings suggest that while higher AI literacy may heighten students’ awareness of labor-market disruptions, its negative indirect associations with employment anxiety operate through enhanced career planning and future orientation. It is recommended that higher vocational colleges consider integrating AI literacy education into career guidance programs, strengthening students’ career planning competencies, and cultivating a long-term future orientation, so as to potentially strengthen the anxiety-buffering pathway associated with AI literacy.

Article.Title: Moisture-dependent strength and microstructural response of clay stabilized with unsaturated polyester resin
Article.Authors: Yurtcan U.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study examines how initial water content influences the strength and microstructural response of a low-plasticity clay stabilized with unsaturated polyester resin (UPR). At LL, UCS reached a maximum of 5.52 MPa at 10% UPR and then decreased at higher dosages. SEM–EDX observations indicated polymer-rich domains and a more integrated fabric in the 0.5LL specimens, whereas the LL specimens showed a more heterogeneous structure. XRD patterns showed no distinct new crystalline reaction products, and FTIR confirmed a polyester-related ester carbonyl response near 1720 cm⁻ 1 . These results indicate that initial water content strongly influences the efficiency of UPR stabilization in the tested clay–polymer system by affecting the continuity and effectiveness of polymer-associated binding.

Article.Title: A resilient-sustainable assessment framework for prioritization of generation expansion projects
Article.Authors: Khaksefidi M.; Esfahanipour A.; Gharehpetian G.
Article.Abstract: Renewable-integrated generation expansion requires project prioritization that recognizes interdependent resilient-sustainable drivers under disruption. Existing approaches treat effective criteria as independent or retain fixed importance structures, limiting their ability to connect causal interdependence, disruption severity, vulnerability, and final project priority. This study develops a novel assessment framework called Scenario-Adjusted Resilient-Sustainable Assessment and Comprehensive Distance-Based Ranking (SARSA-COBRA) to address this gap. Its central innovation is a causal-to-priority mechanism that converts the interdependent structure of resilient-sustainable variables into coalition-based marginal contributions. Single-Valued Neutrosophic DEMATEL identifies the causal structure, and the proposed Causal-Synergy Shapley Game transforms it into weights reflecting systemic prominence, causal dominance, and internal causal synergy. Scenario activation makes these contributions responsive to Normal, Mild, Moderate, and Severe disruption conditions. The Integrated Power System Resilience and Vulnerability Index are combined with capital cost and renewable share through the COBRA method to prioritize predefined generation expansion projects. Applied to 74 alternatives in Sistan and Baluchestan, Iran, the framework shows that excluding sustainability contributions increases apparent resilience by 9.88% and vulnerability by 20.26%. Only 20% of the top-ten performance-ranked alternatives remain in the COBRA-prioritized expansion projects. The framework supports planning-oriented prioritization by jointly considering disruption-responsive performance, severe-stress vulnerability, investment burden, and renewable contribution.

Article.Title: Mechanical characterisation of Dendrocalamus asper bamboo and examination of idealised bamboo glulam joints in sustainable materials
Article.Authors: Aduldejcharas R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this study, mechanical tests are performed on three-year-old Dendrocalamus asper , while the research focuses on conducting an exploratory finite-element study of five idealized bamboo-glulam joints. Compression samples (n = 15) were examined using an adjusted protocol referenced to withdrawn ISO 22157–1:2004; the archived H/D ≈ 2 geometry, deliberate node inclusion, and missing moisture/density records are not equivalent to ISO 22157:2019. Meanwhile, ASTM D3039-type tabbed dog-bone coupons (n = 5) were employed to measure longitudinal tension for practical gripping. However, that composite-material method does not equal the bamboo-specific ISO process. The findings highlighted mean nominal compression and tension strengths of 56.99 and 77.88 MPa, respectively, while the bottom-node group exhibited the highest descriptive compression mean (66.54 MPa). Nonetheless, these findings and not characteristic design values and are not condition-specific. The FE models employ literature-based orthotropy, homogeneous node-free materials, bonded contacts and assumed friction without matched glulam/joint examinations. Meanwhile, model-specific global mesh-sensitivity reruns resulted in adjacent mesh differences of less than 5% in maximum total deformation and equivalent stress at the finest refinement step. Nonetheless, local interface stresses and failure modes have not yet been validated. Thus, numerical contours identify probable hotspots and priorities for future validation.

Article.Title: RiceExtent v1.0: a global rice-specific land cover product from multi-source data integration
Article.Authors: Patel A.; Bawa A.; Park S.; Chawanda C.; Jun S.; Choi S.; Himanshu S.; Srinivasan R.; Jeong J.
Article.Abstract: Accurate land cover information is fundamental for monitoring land-use dynamics, supporting sustainable agriculture, and informing environmental and climate-related decision-making; however, detailed and globally consistent crop-specific datasets, particularly for rice, remain limited. The study presents RiceExtent v1.0, a harmonized global rice-specific land cover dataset athigh (10 m) and moderate (250 m) resolution, developed by integrating verified local, national, and regional rice maps with ESA WorldCover v200 using a hierarchical multi-criteria dataset ranking and spatial merging approach that prioritizes source accuracy and spatial detail. Using an extent-based merging strategy that aggregates multi-source rice data, RiceExtent derives a maximum observed rice cultivation extent rather than annual mean estimates, thereby capturing double and triple cropping patterns, fragmented smallholder fields, and inter-annual variability often underrepresented in other products. The final product was evaluated using area-based statistical comparison metrics against Spatial Production Allocation Model (SPAM), RiceAtlas, and GloRice, along with USDA rice production statistics. Validation using independent ground-truth samples was performed using True Positive Rate (TPR). The developed dataset captures an estimated global rice area of ~ 1.67 million km² and shows broad agreement with official statistics and improving representation in Southeast Asia, South Asia, Africa and the Americas. RiceExtent v1.0, provided through an open repository ( https://dataverse.tdl.org/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18738/T8/JYAEHV ) with accompanying Python script, offers a robust resource for agricultural monitoring, crop and hydrological modeling, and climate impact assessments, while enabling collaborative refinement of global rice mapping.

Article.Authors: Selmi V.; Afghan M.; Taspinar M.; Sari S.; Caniklioglu M.; Isikay L.
Article.Abstract: Urinary stone disease is a global health concern where surgical planning often relies on surgeon experience. This study aims to quantify the relationship between stone characteristics and total Thulium Fiber Laser (TFL) energy consumption and to derive a predictive energy coefficient to optimize operative efficiency. This prospective, observational clinical trial included 61 patients undergoing ureterorenoscopy or retrograde intrarenal surgery between June 2025 and January 2026. Preoperative stone volume (V) and density (Hounsfield Units, HU) were measured using non-contrast CT. Intraoperative parameters, including total energy (Joules) and ablation time, were recorded. A Specific Energy Coefficient (Jx10 3 /mm 3 xHU) was calculated, and a multiple linear regression model validated via bootstrapping (1000 resamples) was developed to predict energy requirements. The median stone volume was 417.50 mm 3 , and the mean density was 944.21 HU. The median total energy used was 22,079 J. The median Specific Energy Coefficient, scaled for practical clinical utility, was 48.13 Jx10 3 /mm 3 xHU. A very strong positive correlation was found between stone volume and total energy (rho = 0.961, p < 0.001). The regression model (E = -1190.917 + 39.694 x V + 0.666 x D) demonstrated excellent predictive power (Adjusted R 2 = 0.934). Bootstrapping validation confirmed the stability of the predictors, identifying stone volume as the primary independent driver. Thulium Fiber Laser lithotripsy demonstrates promising preliminary predictability driven primarily by preoperative stone volume. The developed model serves as a preliminary framework for forecasting energy requirements using CT parameters; however, multi-center studies with larger independent validation cohorts are strictly required before widespread clinical application.

Article.Authors: Ford A.; Pilgeram N.; Wang A.; Alvarado M.; Jonesteller T.; Wesson J.; Bailey K.; Ginsberg S.; Karur P.; Sanchez M.; Bachevalier J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Visual attention to others in our immediate environments serves as an adaptive mechanism for early learning across primate species. The distribution of oculomotor movements that index the extent of infant attention to the video stimuli – fixations, saccades, and inattention, i.e., data lost to offscreen looks or movement – stayed constant during this developmental period. Attention to different body areas – mouth, head and body - showed subtle and progressive changes from birth to six months, except for attention to the eyes of conspecifics, which showed two distinct periods of significant increase. Rank was significantly associated with the percent of time infants spent making saccades, such that low-ranking infants spent more viewing time making saccades than their high-ranking peers. This association was established by five weeks of age. Collectively, these results provide insight into processes of social attention related to social status in rhesus macaques during infancy.

Article.Authors: Lin T.; Lian Q.; Zhong B.; Lin C.

This method achieved purification factors of 7564 and 10,679 for MS and AK, respectively, with high purity (> 90%, determined by an HPLC calibration curve on a weight basis). These findings represent highly competitive MS and AK productivities in Monascus submerged fermentation using non-genetic engineering approaches. providing a potential basis for industrial-scale production. Although this study explored the optimization of MS and AK production through Monascus submerged fermentation, many critical influencing factors are difficult to adequately investigate in shake-flask cultures. Building upon the findings of this study, future research should employ bioreactors for more in-depth investigations into fermentation production.

The blue-spotted wood-dove is an African equatorial forest inhabitant that defends long-term, stable territories and exhibits different responses to known neighbours and unknown strangers. Males repeat their single song with a highly repetitive structure, including frequency parameters. Although the limited sample size reduced our power to detect subtle associations, our results do not provide evidence for a within-species relationship between body size and song frequency. Song frequency may nevertheless influence territorial interactions through mechanisms other than signalling body size. Hypothesizing that these doves tune their response to unknown rivals based on the perception of their song frequency, we predicted that males differentiate the strength of their response to intruders characterised by relatively low or high song frequency and should respond stronger or more cautious to songs of intruder which are lower than their own song frequency, in comparison to the songs which have higher frequency. A total of 25 males were tested twice, in random order, with either a low- or a high-frequency song of the unknown intruder. Birds differed significantly in their responses and avoided approaching the playback in the low-frequency treatment, which we interpreted as more cautious response, as staying at a greater distance from the speaker decreases the chance of a physical fight. We also observed a single male attempting to lower the frequency of his song in response to low-frequency playback, which, however, resulted in distortion of the phrase structure. The findings of this study enhance our understanding of how birds, especially doves, perceive differences in song frequency. They clearly indicate that birds take this characteristic into account even when it is not strongly linked to simple body features associated with size. Repeatability of song structure and rare attempts to change the frequency suggest that the change in frequency is constrained by a production mechanism or by vocal-tract characteristics.

Consequently, differential settlement increased from 0.052 to 0.132 m and the differential settlement ratio from 20.8 to 37.8%. In the cohort study, over 7144 person-years of follow-up, 145 individuals developed moderate-to-severe AS. A significant overall association was observed between UCa/Cr and the risk of moderate-to-severe AS ( P overall = 0.014). Compared with the lowest UCa/Cr group (< 0.049), the highest group (≥ 0.109) had more than a two-fold higher risk of incident moderate‑to‑severe AS (aHR = 2.12, 95% CI: 1.18, 3.82). Further adjustment for continuous SBP and DBP attenuated both associations, which were no longer statistically significant. Ninety participants (93.8%) would use telemedicine again, and 91 (94.8%) reported overall satisfaction. Article.Title: Statistical mechanics of restroom choice
Article.Authors: Franckart A.; Luyckx A.; Araújo N.; Delens M.; Opsomer E.; Vandewalle N.
Article.Abstract: Human behavior is influenced not only by social interactions but also by the way people interact with their environment. We introduce a web-based platform that enables the collection of large-scale data on sequential occupancy choices in controlled restroom layouts. We analyze transition probabilities between configurations using a statistical physics framework inspired by the Ising model, from which we infer effective interpersonal interactions and site-dependent biases. We further develop a kinetic model describing individual arrivals and departures, which allows us to predict site usage as a function of the utilization factor. Finally, we demonstrate that the model generalizes across restroom of different sizes, enabling prediction of usage and dynamics from limited data. Beyond this specific system, our results demonstrate how simple local rules can generate predictable collective behavior in constrained environments, with implications for a broad class of public spaces such as waiting room or public transportation.

Article.Authors: Laska E.
Article.Abstract: Spinal tumors constitute a heterogeneous group of neoplasms that may lead to neurological deficits, pain, and functional impairment. Disease stage correlated negatively with QoL across domains (ρ = −0.54 to − 0.89). Exploratory regression showed that AIS and MSPSS were independently associated with several QoL domains, while I-ADL was independently associated only with the psychological domain. These findings indicate that three months after spinal tumor surgery, QoL is associated with disease stage, illness acceptance, functional independence, and perceived social support, supporting psychosocial and functional screening in early postoperative rehabilitation.

Article.Title: Biochar and PGPR co-application mitigates salinity stress in Malabar spinach (Basella alba L.) by modulating growth, stress markers, and antioxidant defense

Article.Abstract: Soil salinity is a major problem for agricultural productivity, adversely affecting plant growth, physiology, and biochemical performance. Malabar spinach ( Basella alba L. ), an important leafy vegetable with high nutritional value, is sensitive to salinity stress, leading to reduced yield and market quality. For example, 150 mM NaCl reduced plant height by approximately 36% and chlorophyll content by 30% compared with the control. The combined biochar + PGPR treatment improved plant height by 54% and chlorophyll levels by 39% relative to the salted control, while also lowering Na⁺ accumulation by 41%. Both amendments individually improved growth, RWC, K⁺/Na⁺ balance, and antioxidant enzyme activity under salinity, while the combined biochar + PGPR treatment produced the strongest recovery, showing the greatest improvements in pigment stability, ionic balance, and oxidative stress reduction. This work provides one of the first detailed evaluations of biochar–PGPR co-application in B. alba , demonstrating a practical biological strategy for improving crop tolerance in salt-affected systems.

PID retained rank one in 99.95% of paired-bootstrap replicates but only 63.16% and 43.06% under two weight-variation analyses. Post-review sensitivity analyses showed that the principal practical-separation conclusion was robust to the tested CRI coefficient, realization-specific median normalization, and heavier-tail dependence models, while command delay altered separation among near-tied controllers. Article.Abstract: This study aimed to examine the association between early warm and safe memories and healthy eating among college students, and to delineate the statistical mediating pathways involving anxiety and subjective well-being. Article.Authors: Esmeli R.; Abdullahi H.

At matched achieved NDCG, semantic control also produced lower mean SPE at every non-baseline utility target, while neighbourhood ablations showed that random-neighbour, category-mean and count-based signals were substantially weaker than semantic-neighbour signals. Across the five dataset-level units, the slope-based count-to-semantic transfer closely tracked the pre-intervention correlation between count popularity and semantic popularity (Pearson \(r=0.873\) ; mean absolute deviation \(=0.029\) ), supporting \(T\approx r\) as a descriptive first-order approximation rather than an exact law. These findings show that interaction-count popularity and semantic popularity represent distinct exposure dimensions in text-aware recommender systems, and suggest that semantic neighbourhood structure should be audited alongside conventional popularity measures when designing popularity-control mechanisms.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Rabbits are widely employed as ophthalmic models due to their favorable corneal geometry and biomechanical properties; however, intraocular pressure (IOP) measurements in both clinical and experimental settings are frequently performed under non-ideal body positions that may introduce off-axis spatial orientations relative to gravity. A motorized mechanical assembly facilitated multi-angle positioning of the eyes at seven distinct angles from 0° to 90° using 15° increments. An adjustable lead screw was used to gradually increase pressure to generate a physiologically relevant IOP range (8–50 mmHg). Simultaneous measurements were acquired using the iFalcon V700 tonometer (in rabbit-specific mode) and the implanted sensor, with precise synchronization ensured by a host computer program. Data distribution, linear regression, and Bland-Altman analyses were performed. IOP measurement agreement, correlation, and range-dependent biases between the rebound tonometer and the implanted sensor across various angles. Violin plot distributions of the iFalcon V700 closely mirrored the implanted sensor across all angles, with absolute median differences (|Δ Median|) remaining clinically negligible (range: 0.34–1.35 mmHg) and no significant measurement differences detected ( P = 0.398–0.973). Regression analysis revealed a strong positive correlation (R² = 0.962–0.989). However, range-dependent biases were present; a negative intercept suggested underestimation at lower IOP, whereas a slope > 1 (range: 1.00–1.11) indicated systematic overestimation at higher pressures. Bland-Altman analysis corroborated this slight overestimation bias, demonstrating mean differences ranging from 0.05 mmHg (at 0°) to 1.12 mmHg (at 90°), with 95% limits of agreement tightly confined, reaching a maximum width of -4.46 to 5.89 mmHg at 45°. Validated against an implantable pressure sensor, the iFalcon V700 rebound tonometer demonstrated high agreement across the 8–50 mmHg range and maintained robust mechanical and algorithmic stability throughout 0–90° multi-angle measurements under controlled ex vivo conditions. Despite range-dependent overestimation at higher pressures, this study, heavily constrained by its small sample size ( n = 4 eyes), must be interpreted strictly as a preliminary pilot study and an engineering proof-of-concept for multi-angle tonometry. Therefore, adequately powered, large-scale validation in living animals and clinical populations is definitively required before any translational claims regarding dynamic positional monitoring can be established.

Article.Title: Concurrency aware artificial intelligence for real-time intrusion detection in software-defined networks
Article.Authors: Kanimozhi R.; Padmavathi V.; Latha M.
Article.Abstract: Contemporary software systems are now being used in environments that are highly concurrent, data-intensive, and latency-sensitive. Software-Defined Networks (SDNs) applications like real-time intrusion detection need fast pattern recognition in large amounts of data streams through time. Although deep learning models have impressive detection capabilities, failure to perform well in real-world deployments is usually limited by poor concurrency management, inflexible scheduling, centralized learning pipelines, and fault tolerance. In this study, the authors suggest a concurrency-aware artificial intelligence (CA-AI) framework that directly incorporates actor-based concurrency control, workflow-based load-aware scheduling, deep long short-term memory (LSTM)-based temporal learning, agent-based parallel feature extraction, and feedback loops based on monitoring. The framework is evaluated for SDN-oriented intrusion detection workloads, where concurrency management is implemented at the system architecture level through actor-based execution, workflow scheduling, and asynchronous inference and tested on real network traffic data samples (NSL-KDD, CIC-IDS2017, and UNSW-NB15). Experimental results demonstrate that concurrency-aware system design leads to a significant improvement in the detection accuracy achieving up to 98.9% detection accuracy across multiple benchmark datasets, including NSL-KDD, CIC-IDS2017, and UNSW-NB15, throughput improved by 2.1 × compared with the centralized IDS baseline, while throughput increased by approximately 1.19 × when concurrency increased from 10,000 to 100,000 flows within the proposed CA-AI framework, average latency was reduced by approximately 57.5% compared with the centralized IDS baseline (146 ms to 62 ms), while maintaining high reliability under concurrent workloads. The proposed framework establishes concurrency as a fundamental architectural principle for scalable AI-driven pattern recognition systems.

Article.Abstract: Abstract Variable-diameter sections are widely used in industrial gas transmission, exhaust, and collection pipelines; however, their effects on deflagration-induced pressure loading remain insufficiently understood. In this study, a validated large eddy simulation (LES) scheme integrated with a premixed turbulent combustion model was adopted to investigate the effects of different variable-diameter configurations on propane-air deflagration and transient pressure loading. Four typical configurations were investigated, including contraction-then-expansion, expansion-then-contraction, continuous expansion, and continuous contraction, and their influences on flame propagation dynamics, transient pressure-rise characteristics, and turbulent flow-field evolution were comprehensively examined. The results demonstrate that pipeline geometric parameters dominantly control deflagration hazard evolution via jet flow generation, shear layer intensification, flow recirculation, and vortex-flame interaction. In contraction-then-expansion pressurized pipelines, the contraction segment markedly exacerbates early-phase deflagration. Across the LML and LSL contraction-expansion configurations, the peak flame velocity increases from 44.03 to 112.56 m/s, while the contraction-stage peak pressure-rise rate increases from 10.37 to 61.37 MPa/s. The highest overall pressure-rise rate, 67.48 MPa/s, occurs in the MSL configuration, where the downstream expansion receives the high-momentum flow generated by the upstream contraction. In expansion-then-contraction pressurized pipelines, the expansion segment enhances initial flame fluctuation, whereas the downstream contraction restrains late-phase flame propagation and pressure accumulation. Among the continuous configurations, continuous expansion generates persistent vortical disturbances and induces the most severe overall deflagration hazard, whereas continuous contraction sustains persistent flow confinement and reduces the peak pressure-rise rate to 6.89 MPa/s. These results reveal that expansion-dominated configurations can significantly elevate transient explosion-induced pressure loads, whereas contraction-dominated configurations exhibit superior performance in attenuating pressure-rise intensity. This study offers key engineering guidance for configuration optimization and hazard risk control of industrial pressurized pipelines in explosion-prone process facilities.

Article.Title: JARID2 promotes prostate cancer progression associated with TET3-mediated activation of the FAK/PI3K/AKT signaling pathway
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Liu Y.; Li Y.; Xu L.; Ning J.; Li H.
Article.Abstract: JARID2, a regulatory Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2) component, has diverse roles in cancer development, yet its function in prostate cancer (PCa) remains unclear. We analyzed JARID2 expression using TCGA-PRAD data and clinical samples. Functional assays, including CCK-8, wound healing, and Transwell assays, were conducted to assess the influence of JARID2 overexpression or knockdown in PCa cell lines. The JARID2-TET3 interaction was validated by co-immunoprecipitation, and rescue experiments were performed to evaluate TET3’s functional role. Pathway enrichment was analyzed by GSEA and KEGG while assessing in vivo tumor growth employing a xenograft model. JARID2 exhibited a significant overexpression in PCa tissues and cell lines, and was related to advanced N stage and escalated Gleason scores. Functionally, JARID2 enhanced cell proliferation and invasion in vitro, while its knockdown impeded tumor growth in vivo. Mechanistically, JARID2 interacted with and upregulated TET3, which activated FAK/PI3K/AKT signaling. TET3 knockdown attenuated the oncogenic effects of JARID2 overexpression, whereas TET3 overexpression restored the phenotypes induced by JARID2 silencing. Our findings identify JARID2 as a novel oncogenic factor in PCa that drives tumor progression associated with TET3-dependent FAK/PI3K/AKT signaling activation, highlighting a new epigenetic regulatory axis with potential diagnostic and therapeutic implications.

Article.Title: Cross-sectional associations with symptomatic gallstones among women in Chile
Article.Authors: Daniels M.; Jebai R.; Argirion I.; Pfeiffer R.; Cortés S.; Van De Wyngard V.; Curry M.; Mardones N.; Hildesheim A.; Cook P.; Araya J.; Ferreccio C.; Koshiol J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Gallstones (GS) affect 10–20% of adults around the world with a prevalence of around 40% in Chile. Most individuals with GS are asymptomatic, which may reflect underlying differences in disease severity and associated health risks. Few studies have comprehensively assessed factors associated with GS symptomatology. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from the Chile Biliary Longitudinal Study (Chile BiLS), a prospective cohort of middle-aged Chilean women with ultrasound-diagnosed GS. Symptomatic GS (sGS) was defined as self-report of ever having biliary colic or acute cholecystitis. Associations between sGS and personal and clinical characteristics, socioeconomic status, ultrasound characteristics, medication use, occupational pesticide exposure, and key lifestyle factors were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Among 4,328 women with gallstones, 40% had symptomatic gallstones (sGS). Compared to women with asymptomatic gallstones (aGS), those with sGS were younger, had lower educational attainment, reported more frequent and intense nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms, and had a higher prevalence of several gallbladder ultrasound abnormalities ( P < 0.05). Current occupational pesticide exposure was positively associated with sGS (aOR: 2.26; 95% CI 1.26, 4.06). In this cross-sectional study of women with ultrasound-confirmed gallstones in the Araucanía region of Chile, sGS were associated with younger age, lower educational attainment, greater gastrointestinal symptom burden, several gallbladder ultrasound abnormalities, and current occupational pesticide exposure. These findings characterize differences between symptomatic and asymptomatic gallstone disease in this population and warrant confirmation in longitudinal studies, particularly for occupational pesticide exposure.

Article.Title: Environmental distribution of African swine fever virus DNA in pig farm wastewater and Amblyomma javanense ticks in Vietnam
Article.Authors: Mai T.; Duong D.; Dong V.; Tran T.; Cao T.; Huynh T.; Bui T.; Dao V.; Nguyen T.; Hoang T.; Bui T.; Nguyen T.; Yamazaki Y.; Yamazaki W.
Article.Abstract: African swine fever virus (ASFV) is a major threat to pig production, yet its environmental distribution in Southeast Asian farming systems poorly understood. We investigated ASFV DNA in pig farm wastewater and Amblyomma javanense ticks collected from rescued Sunda pangolins in Vietnam. A polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based concentration protocol followed by p72 -targeting real-time PCR (rPCR) improved analytical detection of ASFV DNA in spiked wastewater compared with direct DNA extraction. In field samples, ASFV DNA was detected more frequently after PEG concentration, and additional detections were supported by an independent p54 -targeting rPCR. Infectious virus was not recovered from rPCR-positive wastewater. ASFV DNA was also detected in a small proportion of the examined ticks, with independent-target testing providing additional molecular support in available material. These findings broaden information on the environmental distribution of ASFV DNA and support further evaluation of wastewater and wildlife-associated ticks as complementary molecular surveillance matrices, without demonstrating environmental transmission or tick vector competence.

Article.Title: Effects of podcast supported multicomponent education on treatment adherence and self care management in patients with hypertension
Article.Authors: Bahçecioğlu Turan G.; Alanoğlu M.
Article.Abstract: Podcast-supported education may provide flexible and repeated access to health information; however, evidence regarding its use in hypertension remains limited. This study aimed to determine the effect of a podcast-supported multicomponent educational intervention on treatment adherence and self-care management in patients with hypertension. This study employed a randomized controlled experimental design. The study included patients with hypertension attending the internal medicine outpatient clinic of a university hospital in eastern Türkiye. Participants were randomly assigned to the intervention ( n = 47) or control ( n = 47) group. The intervention group received eight podcast episodes over four weeks, with two episodes delivered per week. Participants were asked to listen to each episode at least once during its initial delivery, once again during the second month, and once during the third month. Repeated engagement was supported through scheduled reminders and monitored using participant-coded Google Forms and available Spotify analytics. The control group received conventional face-to-face education and a printed booklet covering the same core educational content. Treatment adherence and self-care management were assessed at baseline, 1 month, and 3 months. Significant time × group interactions were observed for treatment adherence, F(1.74, 160.30) = 10.108, p < .001, ηp² = 0.099, and self-care management, F(1.70, 156.01) = 40.870, p < .001, ηp² = 0.308. At 1 month, treatment adherence scores were lower in the intervention group than in the control group (10.32 ± 5.18 vs. 15.98 ± 7.79, p < .001), while self-care management scores were higher (129.74 ± 12.15 vs. 113.15 ± 21.80, p < .001). At 3 months, treatment adherence scores remained lower in the intervention group (8.83 ± 5.00 vs. 17.89 ± 7.51, p < .001), whereas self-care management scores remained higher (132.23 ± 11.29 vs. 97.94 ± 14.94, p < .001). The improvements observed at 1 month were maintained at 3 months. The podcast-supported multicomponent educational intervention was associated with greater improvements in treatment adherence and self-care management than conventional education among patients with hypertension. Because podcast delivery was combined with repeated access, reminders, engagement monitoring, and technical support, the findings reflect the overall intervention package rather than the independent effect of the podcast component.

Article.Title: Automated grain-size characterization of GTAW Ti-6Al-4 V weldments using OpenCV and comparison with ASTM-based intercept methods
Article.Authors: Gudisi M.; Talari M.; Gopal A.; Nagallapati V.
Article.Abstract: Quantitative measurement of grain size in the fusion zone (FZ) of Ti-6Al-4 V GTAW weldments is difficult because the large, uneven grain morphologies can introduce operator bias in conventional metallography. In this study, a calibrated openCV based image-processing workflow was developed, and its results were compared with those of the Jeffries planimetric, the Heyn linear-intercept, and Abrams three-circle methods of ASTM E112. Four GTAW conditions were considered: conventional DC, pulsed DC, ultrasonic vibration-assisted (UAV) DC, and UAV pulsed DC. The workflow comprises grayscale conversion, filtering, boundary detection, segmentation, morphological operations, grain identification and spatial calibration at approximately 3.03 μm/pixel for the FZ micrographs. The OpenCV mean linear intercepts (± standard deviation) were 421.0 ± 21.0, 300.0 ± 20.6, 261.0 ± 31.9 and 243.9 ± 10.4 μm for DC, pulsed DC, UVA DC and UVA pulsed DC, respectively, showing progressive grain refinement with pulsing and ultrasonic vibration. Relative to the planimetric, linear-intercept and three-circle methods, the OpenCV mean biases were − 20.18, -65.13, and − 128.12 μm, with mean absolute percentage errors (MAPE) of 6.47%, 17.04%, and 29.60%, respectively. Although the OpenCV approach enables consistent grain-size determination, it should not be regarded as an exact replacement for ASTM E112 analysis.
