Article.Title: Experimental enhancement of a double-slope solar still using external reflectors and nano-coated absorber plates for solar desalination
Article.Authors: Agegnehu B.; Sinte Y.; Ali H.; Kebede M.
Article.Abstract: Freshwater scarcity, particularly in arid and off-grid regions, demands efficient and low-cost desalination technologies. While solar stills offer a sustainable solution, their low productivity remains a key limitation. Studies on the combined effect of external reflectors and nanoparticle-coated absorber plates in double-slope solar stills are scarce, and no such investigation has been conducted under the climatic conditions of Gondar, Ethiopia. This study addresses this gap by experimentally evaluating a double-slope solar still integrated with four externally mounted aluminum reflectors and interchangeable absorber plates coated with black paint, black paint + CuO nanoparticles (0.443 wt%), and black paint + Al 2 O 3 nanoparticles (0.443 wt%). Experiments were conducted in December 2023 and May 2024 at water depths of 2 cm, 2.5 cm, and 3 cm to optimize performance. A water depth of 2 cm consistently produced the highest distillate output across all configurations. The CuO-coated absorber plate with reflectors achieved the maximum productivity of 4.95 L day −1 (3.30 L m −2 day −1 ) with a thermal efficiency of 38.38%, substantially exceeding the typical efficiency range for conventional double-slope stills (25–34%). Reflectors alone increased productivity by 130.7% (1.37 to 3.16 L day −1 ), while the combined use of reflectors and CuO coating improved productivity by 261.3% (1.37 to 4.95 L day −1 ) and thermal efficiency by 27.10% points. The CuO coating outperformed Al 2 O 3 by 6.7% after normalization for irradiance variations. Theoretical predictions agreed closely with experimental results for the CuO configuration (difference < 0.5 L day −1 ), though the model over-predicted the black-paint case by 49%, highlighting the importance of accurate absorptance inputs. The proposed system offers a passive, low-cost solution for decentralized water production in off-grid communities, with demonstrated potential for significant productivity enhancement. Water quality testing is recommended to confirm compliance with drinking water standards in future studies.

Article.Authors: Erez T.; Osabutey A.; Bonda E.; Otmy A.; Levin-Nikulin S.; Hesketh-Best P.; Ferreira C.; Spivak M.; Schroeder D.; Chejanovsky N.; Soroker V.
Article.Abstract: The Varroa destructor (Varroa) and its vectored viruses are major drivers of honey bee ( Apis mellifera ) colony losses. Hygienic behavior, activated by olfactory cues from diseased brood, enables bees to cope with some pests and pathogens. Expression of immune genes was lower in pupae injected with IAPV-enriched inoculum-and lower immune gene expression than in the DWV+IAPV co-infected pupae, suggesting IAPV suppresses the immunity. Volatile profile of virus-injected pupae differed from controls. The ultimate consequence of such differences might lead to virus specific hygienic responses.

Article.Abstract: This study introduces a prior knowledge-informed neural network (PKiNN) for predicting material fatigue life. Article.Authors: Liu C.; Hideki T.; Lin T.; Chen C.; Lee I.; Lee R.; Chen S.
Article.Abstract: Outcomes after yttrium-90 (Y-90) transarterial radioembolization (TARE) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain heterogeneous, and blood-based biomarkers that capture dissemination biology are limited. Absolute total and stem-like CTC counts showed weak and imprecisely estimated relationships with tumor burden and showed limited ability to stratify progression-free survival (PFS). In contrast, the stem-like CTC-to-lymphocyte ratio, termed the Tumor–Immune Balance Index (TIBI), showed stronger apparent prognostic separation in exploratory analyses, and a combined CLR/TIBI schema identified a particularly high-risk group. Peripheral and hepatic venous sampling showed strong concordance, supporting peripheral blood as a practical sampling alternative. These findings support an exploratory, research-stage tumor–immune balance framework for risk stratification after radioembolization and provide a rationale for validation of CTC/lymphocyte-based biomarkers in contemporary HCC cohorts.

Article.Abstract: Millions of patients surviving COVID-19 infection develop post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC), a debilitating condition that severely disrupts quality of life. State-of-the-art mass spectrometry and next-generation leukocyte RNA sequencing were conducted in the blood samples of these participants. PASC status was associated with failure to regain a healthy baseline molecular status in these patients and aberrations in multiple biological pathways, including sphingolipids, chromatin-associated processes, and others. This work provides new mechanistic insights into PASC through integrated multi-omic and machine learning analyses, establishing a robust exploratory framework and data resources to guide future biomarker validation and clinical meta-analyses.

Article.Title: Mamba-enhanced RT-DETR for ship detection in optical remote sensing images
Article.Authors: Zhao Q.; Zhi D.; Wu Y.
Article.Abstract: Ship detection from optical remote sensing images remains challenging due to cluttered sea–land backgrounds, large scale variations, low-contrast small targets, and dense ship occlusion. Existing detectors struggle to balance global modeling capability, detection precision, and computational efficiency. This paper proposes a Mamba-enhanced Real-Time Detection Transformer (RT-DETR) framework for high-precision ship detection and identification. First, a Mamba-based Deformable Spatial Attention (Mamba-DSA) backbone is proposed to integrate linear-time state-space feature modeling and deformable spatial attention, which strengthens ship-specific feature representation and suppresses background interference. Second, a Context-Guided Spatial Feature Reconstruction Feature Pyramid Network (CGRFPN) is designed to enhance multi-scale context awareness and rectangular region calibration, effectively reducing missed detections in dense ship scenes. Third, a Spatial-to-Depth Depthwise Convolution (SPD-DWConv) module is developed to enhance small-target features without introducing excessive computation overhead. Experiments on HRSC2016, NWPU VHR-10, and DOTA-v1.5 datasets show that the proposed method outperforms the baseline RT-DETR by 9.0% in precision, 16.5% in recall, 19.0% in mAP@50, and 14.1% in mAP@50:95. The proposed method achieves strong robustness and efficiency, showing high practical value for maritime monitoring, port security, and emergency response.

Article.Authors: Wassenaar L.; Crann C.; Murseli S.
Article.Abstract: As the Suess effect drives atmospheric radiocarbon (Δ 14 C) below zero, biological 14 C archives are increasingly biased by carbon-storage physiology. A two-endmember mixing model constrains the product of the stored fraction ( f ) and the mean age of stored carbon ( \({{\bar{\uptau }}}\) ) to ≈ 1.3–1.7 year, and for \({{\bar{\uptau }}} \) = 2–3 year, f = 0.5–0.7 (0.70 ± 0.27 for an exponential-age pool). The leaf Δ 14 C zero-crossing in 2024 lagged the atmospheric crossing by 2.2 ± 0.3 year, and the offset re-opened to + 11‰ in 2024 as the Suess-effect decline steepened. NSC storage must therefore be accounted for explicitly when interpreting leaf 14 C as an atmospheric proxy.

STs were corrected from 5.4mm ± 1.3 to 1.0mm ± 1.3, with no patients experienced neurological complications postoperatively. Article.Authors: Suliman L.; Zhong Z.; Liu X.; Zhou X.
Article.Abstract: Tunnel excavation through fill slopes under extreme rainfall involves complex hydro-mechanical interactions among excavation-induced stress redistribution, rainfall infiltration, slope deformation, and adjacent infrastructure. This study investigates the response and stability of a tunnel–fill slope system using integrated physical model testing and numerical simulation. The physical experiments examined rainfall infiltration, ground settlement, stress redistribution, and pore-water-pressure evolution during excavation. The validation test simulated an upper-range heavy-rainfall event of 200 mm/day for 12 h at prototype scale, corresponding to approximately 16.67 mm/day applied for 1 h in the 1:120-scale model. Agreement between the experimental and numerical results confirmed the model’s ability to reproduce the principal hydraulic and deformation responses. Two parametric investigations were subsequently conducted. The first evaluated the effects of adjacent buildings and foundation systems under rainfall and dry conditions, focusing on building settlement and slope-supporting pile displacement. The second assessed riprap, geocell reinforcement, and vegetation under rainfall without building loads by examining slope deformation and pore-water-pressure development. The results demonstrate that rainfall intensifies hydro-mechanical responses and structural deformation, while the effectiveness of protection measures varies according to their hydraulic and mechanical functions. These findings support the selection of suitable foundation systems and slope-protection strategies in complex urban fill-slope environments.

Important physical phenomena such as activation energy, chemical reactions, variable thermal conductivity, electric forces, and viscous dissipation are incorporated into the model. The problem is formulated as a system of nonlinear partial differential equations with appropriate boundary conditions, which are then transformed into a dimensionless form using suitable scaling techniques. The dimensionless equations are solved numerically using an efficient RKF45 computational method. The effects of key physical parameters are analyzed and illustrated through graphical and tabular results. The final outcomes of this study provide valuable insights for the development of biomedical devices, including drug delivery systems, artificial blood flow models and may more.

Article.Abstract: Unhealthy lifestyle behaviors (ULBs) are major contributors to non-communicable diseases, yet nationally representative evidence among Iranian older adults remains limited. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence, clustering, and determinants of ULBs in this population. This cross-sectional secondary analysis included 5,650 participants aged ≥ 60 years from Iran’s 2021 STEPS survey. Among 5,960 participants who met the age criterion, 310 were excluded due to missing data on lifestyle or other key variables. This study assessed five ULBs: inadequate fruit/vegetable intake (< 5 mean servings/day), insufficient physical activity (< 150 min/week moderate-to-vigorous activity), current smoking (any use in the past year), current alcohol consumption (any use in the past year), and abnormal BMI (underweight < 18.5 or overweight/obese ≥ 25 kg/m²). The number of ULBs was summed and categorized as 0–1, 2, 3, or ≥ 4. Weighted prevalence estimates were calculated, and sex-stratified multinomial logistic regression models were used to identify factors associated with the number of ULBs. Overall, 98.8% of participants had at least one ULB, and 53.4% had ≥ 3. The most prevalent behaviors were inadequate fruit and vegetable intake (87.3%), insufficient physical activity (77.6%), and abnormal BMI (69.3%). The prevalence of multiple ULBs was higher among individuals with hypertension, diabetes, and cardiovascular diseases. Among females, age ≥ 80 years and a middle wealth index were associated with higher relative risk ratios (RRR) for having both 2 and 3 ULBs versus 0–1 ULBs, while a history of hypertension was associated with a higher relative risk ratio for having 3 ULBs versus 0–1 ULBs. Among males, a history of hypertension was associated with higher RRRs for having both 2 and 3 ULBs versus 0–1 ULBs. Age 70–79 years was associated with lower RRRs for having 3 and ≥ 4 ULBs, while age ≥ 80 years was associated with a lower RRR for having ≥ 4 ULBs. Higher wealth was generally associated with lower RRRs, particularly for ≥ 4 ULBs. ULBs are highly prevalent and frequently co-occur among Iranian older adults, with distinct sex-specific patterns. Integrated, multi-behavioral interventions leveraging existing primary healthcare systems are needed to promote healthy aging.

Article.Title: Machine learning-based ensemble model for the risk stratification of myocardial injury in physical examination data
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Wang Q.; Lu S.; Gu J.; Zhou S.; Li P.; Jin Z.; Zhao T.; Tian F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Inflammatory diseases such as myocarditis, which can be caused by a variety of factors, severely impact cardiac function and may lead to heart failure and death. Myocardial injury is widely recognized as an early and common pathological manifestation in the progression of myocarditis. With the widespread adoption of health check-ups, physical examination data has become a valuable resource for the early detection of diseases. This study aims to develop a machine learning-based model for assessing the risk of myocardial injury using routine physical examination data. Participants recruited in 2024 and 2025 were used for model development and temporal validation, respectively. Variable and sample selection were performed based on missing values, followed by multiple imputation via chained equations. A hill climbing algorithm was utilized to optimize model selection and parameter tuning, resulting in the integration of five ML models: Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), Classification and Regression Trees (CART) Classifier, and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LGBM) Classifier. Model performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, AUC, calibration plot and Brier score. Feature importance was assessed using the SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP) method. Performance evaluation results demonstrated that the ensemble model showed modest but statistically supported improvement over all individual classifiers in risk prediction of myocardial injury, as verified by paired DeLong test for AUC and McNemar’s test for classification discordance. The ensemble model achieved 81.8% AUC (0.2-2.0 increase), 89.7% accuracy (0.2%-2.7% improvement), 70.1% recall (2.9%-15.2% increase), and 75.8% F1-score (1.7%-8.2% higher) on the test set, while it retained stable performance on the temporal validation cohort with an AUC of 0.812 (95% CI: 0.768–0.856) and accuracy of 88.8% (95% CI: 0.847–0.929). Ablation experiments confirmed that each base classifier contributed predictive gain to the integrated framework, and our hill climbing-based weight adjustment strategy yielded highest overall performance compared with fixed equal-weight fusion. The ensemble model proposed in this study provides support for the risk stratification of biochemical myocardial injury. High-risk individuals identified by this model allows targeted further myocarditis-related examinations, facilitating early screening and timely early intervention. The final prediction model was implemented into a web application to enhance its practicality in clinical settings.

Article.Title: Improving prenatal thalassemia carrier detection with a combined MCV and MCH strategy: a 24-year retrospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Chen H.; Lin S.; Li C.; Ko T.; Yang Q.; Tai Y.
Article.Abstract: Carrier screening for thalassemia conventionally uses a mean corpuscular volume (MCV) cutoff ≤ 80 fL. However, silent carriers harboring mild mutations often present with borderline indices, which, if missed, may result in offspring with hemoglobin H disease or other significant hemoglobinopathies. Thus, we aimed to evaluate whether alternative hematological cutoffs could reduce this detection gap. Of 15,212 prenatal samples collected in Taiwan between 2000 and 2024, this retrospective cohort study analyzed 9,949 genetically confirmed thalassemia carriers (α-thalassemia, n = 7,473; β-thalassemia, n = 2,476) and 3,025 genotype-negative individuals, who served as the noncarrier reference group. The sensitivity and specificity of the conventional MCV threshold and alternative strategies incorporating higher MCV cutoffs and mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH) ≤ 27 pg were calculated and compared, stratified by sex. -- SEA deletion (78.71% of α-thalassemia carriers) and IVS-II-654 mutation (34.65% of β-thalassemia carriers) were the predominant genotypes. Under the conventional MCV threshold, approximately 5.3% of carriers were missed, including 6.3% and 2.3% of α- and β-thalassemia carriers, respectively. Among the predefined candidate thresholds evaluated, the MCV ≤ 82 fL or MCH ≤ 27 pg criterion achieved sensitivity exceeding 99% in both sexes in this cohort and reduced the missed-carrier rate to < 1%, with lower specificity and more false-positive classifications. Because the preferred MCV threshold was selected after examination of the observed candidate performance, these findings are exploratory, apply to initial screening rather than diagnosis, and require prospective validation in an unselected prenatal population.

Article.Title: A supportive intervention on infertile couples for continuing infertility treatments: a randomized trial
Article.Authors: Ghorbani M.; Keramat A.; Yunesian M.; Salehin S.; Talebi S.; Hoseini F.
Article.Abstract: Infertility affects 10-15% of couples globally, with high treatment dropout rates (22-72%) due to psychological, financial, and cultural barriers. Despite evidence supporting psychosocial interventions, few address post-failure continuation in resource-limited settings like Iran, where stigma and costs disproportionately impact adherence. The aim of this RCT was to evaluate a tailored intervention for improving treatment continuation intention, reducing infertility-related stress, and enhancing mental health among Iranian couples with prior treatment discontinuation. Parallel-group RCT (CONSORT-compliant) with block randomization (1:1 allocation, block size = 4) was done on 130 women (18–42 years) who discontinued IVF/ICSI/FET after at least one unsuccessful infertility treatment in Jahad Daneshgahi Infertility Center, Qom, Iran (June–December 2021). Primary outcome was treatment continuation intention (assessed by researcher-made questionnaire based on the Transtheoretical Model). Secondary outcomes included infertility stress (assessed by Newton’s Fertility Problem Inventory (FPI)), mental health (assessed by General Health Questionnaire-28 (GHQ-28)), and communication skills (assessed by Queendom Communication Skills Test (CSTR)). The Intervention included four weekly online sessions (psychoeducation, CBT techniques, and communication skills) plus six asynchronous modules. Controls received an assessment-only control condition. Study questionnaires were completed by participants at baseline (pre-intervention) and two weeks’ post-intervention. The intervention group showed 11.5-fold higher odds of treatment continuation (aOR = 11.49, 95% CI: 2.24–58.77, p = 0.003), with 84.2%of initially reluctant participants opting to continue vs. 28.0% in controls ( p < 0.001). There were no significant improvements in infertility stress or mental health and communication skills. While the intervention significantly improved continuation intentions, its limited psychological impact suggests that infertility-related stress in this population of treatment-discontinued couples may be more closely related to decisional conflict and motivational barriers to re-engaging with treatment than to clinical psychiatric symptoms. Cultural stigma and economic burdens emerged as critical, under-addressed dropout drivers. Brief, low-cost psychoeducation can enhance treatment adherence in high-stigma settings, but integrated financial support and culturally adapted mental health care are needed for holistic impact. Trial registration: The study is registered in the Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials with the IRCT20210516051315N1 (30/05/2021).

Article.Title: Integrating dft-based spectroscopic analysis, molecular docking, admet prediction, and natural biosorbent adsorption studies of flupyradifurone
Article.Authors: Türköz Altuğ D.
Article.Abstract: Using Density Functional Theory calculations, the molecular structure, molecular electrostatic potential surface analysis, boundary molecular orbital analysis, chemical reactivity, nonlinear optical properties, UV-Vis analysis, FTIR and Raman spectra of flupyradifurone were comprehensively investigated. The experimentally obtained UV-Vis, FTIR, and Raman spectra were compared with theoretical results. The interaction mechanisms of flupyradifurone with human DNA and p53 protein were theoretically investigated. Risk predictions regarding human health were also made using ADMET calculations. Adsorption experiments were conducted using natural materials such as walnut, peanut, and cherry seed shells to minimize the potential environmental impacts of flupyradifurone. Changes in FTIR and Raman spectra were observed in the ranges of 3000–2800 cm⁻¹ and 1600–1400 cm⁻¹ in untreated and flupyradifurone-treated insecticide-containing samples. The SEM images showed that flupyradifurone accumulated around the pore regions of the treated samples. According to the EDS results, N, F, and Cl atoms were identified as weight percentages after the treatment with flupyradifurone. In the adsorption spectra, the vibrational bands of these elements were most clearly observed around 1600 cm⁻¹. Molecular docking studies indicated that flupyradifurone can interact with human DNA and p53 protein. ADMET predictions gave probabilities of 0.77 for drug-induced liver injury and 0.24 for carcinogenicity, and the docking runs gave best binding affinities of -5.6 kcal mol⁻¹ for DNA and − 6.8 kcal mol⁻¹ for p53. FTIR, Raman, SEM, and EDS findings showed that walnut, peanut, and cherry seed shells could adsorb flupyradifurone.

Article.Title: Assessment of the technical, economic, and carbon reduction potential of recycled concrete aggregate for sustainable roads in Saudi Arabia
Article.Authors: Alharbi F.; Almoshaogeh M.; Jamal A.; Alhuthayl J.; Almijmaj M.; Shafiquzzaman M.
Article.Abstract: Construction and demolition (C&D) waste has been creating significant environmental and economic challenges associated with landfill disposal and depletion of natural resources. In Saudi Arabia, the growing volume of C&D waste highlights the need for sustainable recycling strategies that support the objectives of Vision 2030 and circular economy principles. This study evaluated the feasibility of utilizing recycled concrete aggregate (RCA) as a substitute for natural aggregate in both hot-mix asphalt (HMA) and base layer applications for road construction. RCA was obtained from a landfill in Buraidah, Saudi Arabia, processed, and evaluated through aggregate suitability tests, Marshall mix design, Proctor compaction, and California Bearing Ratio (CBR) testing. Economic performance was assessed using construction and life-cycle cost calculations, while construction-stage CO₂ emissions were estimated using a scenario-based carbon-screening approach. A multi-criteria ranking framework integrating engineering, economic, and carbon-performance indicators was also applied to compare RCA alternatives. The RCA satisfied the specified aggregate requirements, although its water absorption (7.83%) and abrasion loss (40.55%) were higher than those of the natural aggregate. In HMA mixtures, RCA contents up to 20% showed comparatively favorable volumetric and mechanical performance within the tested binder range, whereas mixtures containing 30–50% RCA exhibited elevated air voids and reduced VFA, indicating the need for further binder optimization. For base layers, increasing RCA content reduced maximum dry density from 2.29 to 1.73 g/cm³ and increased CBR from 96.8% for the control to 172.5% at 100% RCA, while swell decreased from 0.45 to 0.004%. Economic analysis indicated net savings of 2.35–9.73% for HMA mixtures, with the highest savings at 10% RCA, while base-layer costs decreased by up to 25.1% at 100% RCA. The estimated construction-stage CO₂ reduction increased from 4.67% to 23.37% for HMA and from 23.07 to 79.02% for base layers with increasing RCA content. Under the adopted equal-weight multi-criteria framework, 10% RCA provided the most favorable HMA option considering technical feasibility and overall performance, whereas 100% RCA ranked highest for the base layer. Overall, the findings indicate that RCA has substantial potential for sustainable pavement construction in Saudi Arabia, particularly in base-layer applications, while higher RCA contents in HMA require further optimization and durability validation.

Article.Title: Pro-vaccination communication requires tailoring: Evidence from an experimental and longitudinal comparison of communication strategies on vaccination-related cognition and intentions
Article.Authors: Damnjanović K.; Ilić S.; Kušić M.; Mišić K.; Ninković M.; Paunovic D.; B. Petrović M.
Article.Abstract: Effective vaccination communication requires evidence-based strategies, yet direct comparisons are scarce. In a longitudinal experiment (N = 901, four time points), participants were exposed to six pro-vaccination communicative texts, all centered on the concept of herd immunity to maintain consistency in information content while varying the communication style — nudge, boost, psychological inoculation (PI), patient-concerns-centred communication (PCCC), dismissive informational load (DIL), and neutral informational load (NIL) — compared against a control. We assessed the immediate and sustained, i.e., after a period of 7 and 14 days, impact on vaccination intention (personal and proxy), information-seeking habits, and vaccine-related biased reasoning. No single communication strategy was universally superior; effectiveness depended on the decision context and pre-existing attitudes. PCCC most effectively increased immediate personal vaccination intention. Pre-existing attitudes and beliefs were strong moderators of the effect (e.g., PI and NIL were more effective for individuals reporting higher levels of vaccine conspiracy beliefs when making proxy decisions). Critically, our findings reveal what these brief interventions can and cannot achieve: while initial gains in intention from PCCC remained stable, the impact on information-seeking habits was modest, and these brief-exposure interventions were insufficient to alter ingrained cognitive processes, such as vaccine-related biased reasoning. While brief communication can shift immediate intentions, changing how people think requires more sustained efforts. We argue that communication must be tailored to the audience and decision type, emphasizing the importance of considering patient concerns and suggesting abandoning the DIL approach given its tone and ineffectiveness.

Article.Title: Vision impairment, depressive symptoms, and risk of incident coronary events: a prospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Ling J.; Sun G.; Yu F.; Zhu J.
Article.Abstract: Vision impairment (VI) is a common yet underrecognized age-related condition, but its association with coronary heart disease (CHD) risk remains unclear. Using data from 6,906 adults aged ≥ 50 years in the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (2004–2023), we examined the associations of baseline self-reported vision status and vision transitions between Waves 2 and 3 with incident CHD and explored whether depressive symptoms statistically accounted for part of these associations. During a median follow-up of 12 years, 502 incident CHD cases were identified. Participants with baseline VI had a 40% higher risk of CHD (hazard ratio [HR] 1.40; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.08–1.80), and those whose vision deteriorated had a 55% higher subsequent risk (HR 1.55; 95% CI 1.12–2.15). Each one-point higher mean vision score was linked to a 21% lower CHD risk (HR 0.79; 95% CI 0.69–0.90). Exploratory mediation analyses suggested that depressive symptoms statistically accounted for a modest proportion of the baseline VI–CHD association. Poorer self-reported vision and deterioration were associated with a higher subsequent risk of CHD. Depressive symptoms statistically accounted for a modest proportion of the baseline association, suggesting that perceived visual decline may mark broader cardiovascular vulnerability in later life.

Article.Title: Relationship between autistic traits, emotional symptoms and adverse life events in Chinese adolescents: mediating effects of resilience
Article.Authors: Zeng L.; Liu Y.; Wang H.; Cao Q.; Ji Z.; Gong X.; Su X.; Zhao L.; Yin T.; Liu Q.; Sun B.; Han G.; Liu Y.; Jin Y.; Tang X.; Li X.; Liu J.
Article.Abstract: Few studies have explored links between autistic traits and multifaceted adverse outcomes with culturally specific mediators. This study aimed to examine associations of autistic traits with emotional symptoms and adverse life events, and analyze the mediating effect of resilience in Chinese adolescents. A total of 5666 Chinese adolescents were enrolled to assess autistic traits using the Autism Spectrum Screening Questionnaire, emotional symptoms using the Child Depression Inventory and the Screen for Child Anxiety Related Emotional Disorders, adverse life events using the Adolescent Self-Rating Life Events Checklist, and resilience using the Resilience Scale for Chinese Adolescent. Spearman correlations and multiple linear regression analyses were conducted to examine the associations between autistic traits and both two types of outcomes. The Bootstrap percentile confidence interval method was adopted to analyze the mediating effect of resilience. Autistic traits were correlated with emotional symptoms and adverse life events, among which the social interaction showed the strongest correlations. Relationship pressure and being punished were the adverse life events with the largest effect sizes. Resilience significantly mediated the associations of autistic traits with both emotional symptoms and adverse life events. Specifically, individual power exerted a stronger effect on the link with emotional symptoms, whereas supportive power had a stronger effect on the link with adverse life events. The association between autistic traits and mental health among Chinese adolescents is multidimensional. Culturally distinctive resilience with dual layers should be incorporated into targeted intervention design.

Article.Title: High-speed FPGA implementation of the CORDIC algorithm using carry lookahead adders
Article.Authors: Kanadal K.; Pradhan A.; S A.; Roy C.
Article.Abstract: This paper presents an efficient hardware architecture for sine and cosine generation using the CORDIC (Coordinate Rotation Digital Computer) algorithm. The design employs a pipelined scale-free CORDIC datapath integrated with a carry look-ahead adder (CLA) to reduce critical path delay and improve computational speed compared to conventional ripple-carry adder (RCA) implementations. To achieve an optimal balance between performance and hardware cost, hybrid CLA–RCA configurations are introduced, where CLAs are selectively used in timing-critical stages while RCAs are retained in non-critical paths. Furthermore, mutually exclusive micro-rotation techniques are utilized to reduce the number of iterations and eliminate the need for scale-factor compensation, thereby enhancing efficiency. The proposed architecture is implemented and synthesized on both FPGA and ASIC platforms to validate its performance and portability. FPGA implementation on Xilinx Artix-7 confirms accurate sine and cosine outputs with low power consumption of 0.175W, while a standard-cell ASIC realization on the open SkyWater 130 nm (Sky130) PDK using the Yosys–OpenROAD flow further demonstrates a core area of \(0.88 \textrm{mm}^{2}\) , an achievable clock frequency of \(32 \textrm{MHz}\) , and a total power of \(10.2 \textrm{mW}\) , confirming successful timing closure with zero violations across all sign-off corners.

Article.Title: Performance evaluation of recycled cement-stabilized gravel strengthened with multi-source solid-waste-based composite slurry and its mixtures
Article.Authors: Jia S.; Ding J.; Gao H.; Wen P.; Wang C.
Article.Abstract: To improve the mechanical performance of cold-recycled cement-stabilized gravel and address practical problems including poor mechanical properties and high dispersion of recycled cement-stabilized gravel (RCSG), a strengthening method for RCSG coated with multi-source solid-waste-based composite slurry was proposed. A multi-source solid waste-based composite slurry containing slag powder, steel slag powder and carbide slag was developed. The recommended paste-to-aggregate mass ratio and slurry concentration for RCSG strengthening were determined. The mixing proportion of slurry raw materials together with the strengthening procedure for RCSG were recommended. The effects of strengthening procedure and RCSG replacement content on the performance of cold-recycled cement-stabilized gravel mixtures were evaluated. The results show that the recommended mass ratio of ground granulated blast-furnace slag, steel slag powder, carbide slag, and sodium silicate was 60:40:4:1. A slurry concentration of 50%, a paste-to-aggregate mass ratio of 1:8, and mechanical mixing for 5 min were recommended as the strengthening parameters based on the experimental results. After treatment with this procedure, the 7 d and 28 d interfacial bonding strengths of fine RCSG reached 0.71 and 0.96 MPa, respectively, with the 7 d interfacial bonding strength increased by 77.5% compared with the untreated group. The crushing and abrasion values of coarse RCSG decreased to 19.09% and 8.98%. At a 30% replacement rate, the 7 d and 28 d unconfined compressive strengths of the strengthened cold-recycled cement-stabilized gravel mixtures increased by 104.4% and 103.8%, respectively. The proposed multi-source solid-waste-based composite slurry effectively improved the mechanical performance of RCSG and cold-recycled cement-stabilized gravel mixtures. This study provides experimental support for the strengthening and reuse of RCSG in pavement base applications.

Article.Title: Endophytic fungi-mediated biosynthesis of titanium dioxide nanoparticles: characterization and evaluation of their antimicrobial, antioxidant, and anticancer activities
Article.Authors: Alsharif S.; Alemam A.; Albalawi A.; Abdel-Rahman M.; Bukhari D.; Eid A.; El-Din Hassan S.; Alhujaily A.; Almutrafy A.; Fouda A.
Article.Abstract: Herein, the different biological activities of green-fabricated titanium dioxide nanoparticles (TiO 2 -NPs) were assessed. The cell-free filtrate (CFF) of the endophytic fungus Penicillium chrysogenum was utilized as a biocatalyst for the green production of TiO 2 -NPs. GC-MS was used to identify CFF metabolites containing alkaloids, terpenoids, organic compounds, carotenoids, and steroids. The characterization of the nanoscale structure was achieved by UV analysis, TEM, FT-IR, EDX, XRD, zeta potential, and DLS. The colorless CFF was transformed into a white precipitate as an indicator of TiO 2 -NPs synthesis, which showed maximum surface plasmon resonance at 360 nm. TEM exhibited spherical shapes with sizes ranging from 10 to 40 nm. EDX confirmed that the main components of the nanoscale sample were oxygen (weight% of 15.32%) and titanium (weight% of 44.1%) ions. XRD and DLS showed the formation of an anatase crystalline structure and a negative surface charge with a ζ-value of − 28.42. The biological applications of TiO 2 -NPs, including antimicrobial, antioxidant, and cytotoxic activities, were concentration-dependent. Different strains of Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, as well as unicellular and multicellular fungi, were inhibited by the formed nanostructure, with low MIC values ranging from 25 to 50 µg mL −1 . The synthesized nanostructure exhibited DPPH scavenging activity with a percentage of 90.4 ± 0.6% compared to 96.1 ± 0.8% for ascorbic acid (positive control) at 1000 µg mL −1 . Myco-fabricated TiO 2 -NPs targeted the cancer cells Caco-2 and MCF7 to inhibit their viability, with low IC 50 and selectivity index (SI) values of 242 and 287 µg mL −1 and 1.67 and 1.41, respectively, compared to their activity toward the normal cell line WI38, which had an IC 50 value of 405 µg mL −1 . Overall, these results highlight the efficacy of the endophytic fungal strain Penicillium chrysogenum in producing TiO 2 -NPs with multifunctional activities, including inhibition of microbial growth, scavenging of free radicals, and selective activity against cancer cells.

Article.Title: Image encryption algorithm integrating multi-chaotic key fusion and bipolar fuzzy diffusion
Article.Authors: Elmannai H.; Zafar Abbasi A.; Aiyaz M.; Daba I.; D. Algarni A.; Thamer Alsahle W.
Article.Abstract: The rapid growth of digital communication and cloud-based multimedia applications has significantly increased the demand for secure image encryption techniques capable of protecting visual information from unauthorized access and malicious attacks. In this study, a novel image encryption framework based on triple-chaotic key fusion and bipolar fuzzy based diffusion is proposed. The encryption scheme integrates three nonlinear chaotic systems, namely the Logistic map, Chebyshev map, and Circle map, to generate highly random pseudo-random sequences for key construction. The generated chaotic sequences are fused through modular arithmetic to enlarge the key space and enhance unpredictability. Furthermore, a bipolar fuzzy sets mechanism is introduced to construct an additional diffusion layer that strengthens encryption complexity and improves resistance against statistical and differential attacks. The proposed cryptosystem employs a permutation-diffusion architecture in which chaotic permutation destroys pixel correlations, while multi-stage XOR diffusion and bipolar fuzzy transformation provide strong confusion and diffusion properties. Experimental evaluations are conducted using benchmark grayscale images, including Flower and Leaves images. The encrypted images achieve entropy values of 7.999834 and 7.999990, respectively, which are extremely close to the theoretical maximum entropy value of 8. The correlation coefficients between adjacent pixels in the original uncoded images are around 0.998, whereas the correlation coefficient of adjacent pixels in the coded images are near zero; therefore, adjacent pixels are effectively decorrelated through this encrypting process. The histogram, entropy, correlation, NPCR, and UACI analysis results confirm the good security performance of our proposed method. The decrypted images accurately recover the original images with little or no distortion to support the claim of reversibility and reliability of the scheme. The results indicate that our proposed triple chaotic acoustic fuzzy image encryption framework has very high security, very strong randomness, and very strong resistance to statistical and differential attacks using cryptanalysis methods.

Article.Title: Decoding the anti-adenoviral potential of Ocimum volatile organic compounds: linking chemical fingerprints to molecular targets via docking
Article.Authors: Refaey M.; El-Haggar M.; Kutkat O.; Rashedy A.; Elhawary E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ocimum species are globally recognized for their pharmaceutical utility, yet a comparative mapping of their volatile architecture against viral pathogens remains incomplete. This study evaluated the chemical profiles and antiadenoviral (ADV) potential of Ocimum basilicum (Local), O. basilicum var. minimum (French), and O. africanum (Kafory). Volatiles from three extraction techniques; hydrodistillation, n -hexane, and headspace—were analyzed via GC/MS. One hundred fifty-seven compounds were quantified and subjected to Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and clustered heat mapping. Biological efficacy was assessed via IC 50 determination, supported by molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. PCA effectively discriminated against species, with PC1 and PC2 accounting for 88% of total variance. Oxygenated monoterpenes emerged as the dominant class. Notably, O. africanum hydrodistilled oil exhibited exceptional antiadenoviral potency (IC 50 of 1.72 µ g/ml), significantly outperforming the French (IC 50 of 54.26 µ g/ml) and Local varieties. This superior activity is hypothesized to be linked to the high relative abundance of methyl cinnamate and cadinol, while in silico molecular docking predicted 1,3-dimethyladamantane as a key potential bioactive candidate. MD trajectories (RMSD, RMSF, Rg, and SASA) support the hypothesis that this ligand forms a stable, rigid complex with the viral protein, effectively reducing structural flexibility. This study establishes a high-resolution chemical-to-biological workflow for Ocimum validation. By identifying a high-potency lead with a predicted binding mechanism, these findings move Ocimum from traditional usage into evidence-based antiviral drug discovery. These results provide a strategic blueprint for developing standardized, plant-derived therapeutics against adenoviral infections.

Article.Title: Enhanced multiclass intrusion detection on imbalanced IoT NetFlow traffic using a three-tier stacked time-distributed LSTM with SMOTENC-based class balancing
Article.Authors: Kwari M.; Rajkumar N.; Selvarathi C.; Abdulkadir R.; Jiru M.
Article.Abstract: The network-based attack surface has flourished abruptly with the unveiling of Internet of Things (IoT) devices. As a result, there is a pressing demand for automated intrusion detection systems (IDS) that can reliably identify a variety of attacks with severe class imbalance. Deep recurrent models are suitable for NetFlow traffic, however, a single-layer long short-term memory (LSTM) network is often inadequate for separating minority attack classes, and the effect of oversampling and model size is not well quantified. This study presents a three-tier stacked Time-Distributed long short-term memory network (ST-LSTM) evaluated on NF-BoT-IoT (600,100 flows, four attack classes and one benign class) under a leakage-free protocol. Ten flow features serve as predictors, while the class label and host identifiers are excluded. The data are divided into training, validation and test partitions before any fitting, and mixed-type oversampling (SMOTENC) is applied to the training partition only, at a ratio selected on validation data. On the untouched test set of 120,020 flows, the model reaches 83.98% accuracy, 0.8500 weighted F1, 0.6609 macro F1 and 0.9678 weighted ROC-AUC, the highest values among classical, shallow recurrent and stacked-ensemble baselines, and five-fold cross-validation gives 83.94 ± 0.19% accuracy. Standard SMOTE, by contrast, creates invalid protocol and flag codes and suppresses DDoS detection. A label-conflict analysis shows that 99.9% of DDoS and DoS flows share identical feature vectors with other classes, which limits attainable five-class accuracy to 84.91%, the model reaches 98.9% of this bound, and nearly all of its remaining errors fall on these ambiguous flows.

Article.Title: Integrated hierarchical fusion of GRU and meta-features for enhanced identification and interpretation of calcium ion inhibitors
Article.Authors: Hassan M.; Gaffar S.; Ahmad W.; Lee S.
Article.Abstract: The flow of calcium ions across cell membranes is essential for a wide range of physiological processes, including hormone secretion, epithelial function, the maintenance of electrochemical gradients, and the generation of electrical impulses. Calcium ion inhibitors have emerged as promising therapeutic agents for the treatment of various conditions such as cancer, muscle weakness, renal dysfunction, endocrine disorders, impaired cell function, and cardiac arrhythmias. Therefore, accurate identification and characterization of these inhibitors is crucial in regulating ion flow through calcium channels. In this study, we develop a neural network-based model for the identification of calcium ion inhibitors. To construct a comprehensive predictive framework, we employed seven peptide-encoding strategies and five distinct machine learning classifiers, resulting in 35 baseline models. From each, we extracted 35-dimensional probabilistic outputs and 35-dimensional predicted class labels, which were concatenated into a unified 70-dimensional meta-feature vector. In addition, we used the AAindex matrix to encode the physicochemical and biostructural properties of the peptide sequences. A gated recurrent unit (GRU) model was applied to capture long-range dependencies within this matrix, producing another 70-dimensional feature vector. The two 70-dimensional vectors were then concatenated into a final 140-dimensional representation, integrating physicochemical, biostructural, biochemical, and sequence-derived features. This 140D feature vector was used to train a two-layer multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier. On the independent test set, our proposed model (PredCaII) achieved an accuracy of 0.941, MCC of 0.883, and AUC of 0.990, outperforming the state-of-the-art Multi-Branch-CNN method (accuracy: 0.751, MCC: 0.431, AUC: 0.766) and all individual baseline models. Furthermore, we assessed the interpretability and robustness of the model using Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) and Integrated Gradients. These interpretability analyses provided deep insight into the model’s decision-making behavior, highlighting the most influential compositional and physicochemical characteristics. The experimental results demonstrated the proposed method offers a powerful and interpretable computational framework for the discovery and screening of potential calcium ion inhibitors.

Article.Title: Combined effects of 450, 635 and 980 nm LASER wavelengths on proliferation and migration of human periodontal ligament mesenchymal stem cells
Article.Authors: Yousefi-Koma A.; Shamszadeh S.; Azadi A.; Nashibi S.; Amid R.; Chiniforush N.; Kadkhodazadeh M.
Article.Abstract: This in vitro investigation was conducted to compare the efficacy of various wavelengths individually [450 nm (G1), 635 nm (G2), 980 nm (G3)] or in combination [450 nm + 635 nm (G4); 450 nm + 980 nm (G5); 635 nm + 980 nm (G6); and 450 nm + 635 nm + 980 nm (G7)] on cellular viability, proliferation, and migration of human periodontal ligament stem cells (hPDLSCs). In combined-wavelengths groups (G4, G5, G6, G7), laser irradiation was performed simultaneously through a single probe. All groups received 10 uninterrupted seconds of irradiation with each wavelengths set at 4 J/cm 2 energy density and 200 mW power. MTT assay, DAPI staining, scratch migration assay, Ki67 marker expression, Annexin V/PI assay (apoptosis), and proliferatory/migratory factors through ELISA (SDF-1, VEGF and TGF-β1) were utilized from 1 to 6 days post-irradiation. All groups were compared against each-other and a control negative (no laser therapy) group. The statistical analysis was evaluated using Two-way ANOVA ( P < 0.05). MTT and DAPI assays showed significantly higher metabolic activity/viability rates for G1, G5 and G7. The expression rate of Ki67 and its mean fluorescent intensity were both superior in G7. G7 had the most stable outcomes in apoptosis tests. hPDLSCs had the greatest migratory capability in G6 and G7 in the first 2 days. The highest concentrations of SDF-1, VEGF and TGF- β1 were observed in G1, G5 and G7, respectively. It is worth noting that combined-wavelength groups had overall higher energy densities and powers than individual-wavelength groups. Given the outstanding proliferative and migrative outcomes of blue light (450 nm) individually or in combination with red and near-infrared wavelengths on hPDLSCs, further studies must incorporate blue light lasers in photobiomodulation therapy. All wavelengths were set at 4 J/cm 2 ; further dose-matched studies must be conducted to reach firm conclusions.

Article.Title: Integrating transcriptomics and network biology to identify candidate genes against Conopomorpha cramerella in Theobroma cacao
Article.Authors: Akram S.; Vengatharajuloo V.; Muhammad N.; Hassan M.; Shah R.; Rahman M.; Goh H.; Mohamed-Hussein Z.; Harun S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cocoa pods suffer significant damage from the cocoa pod borer (CPB, Conopomorpha cramerella ), a major pest affecting cocoa ( Theobroma cacao ) crops in Southeast Asia, severely diminishing yield. The mechanisms underlying the genetic resistance of cocoa varieties to this pest are not yet fully elucidated. This study aims to identify key candidate genes associated with cocoa responses to CPB infestation through an integrative approach combining de novo transcriptomic profiling and gene co-expression network analysis to evaluate the genetic basis of CPB resistance in two contrasting T. cacao cultivars: KKM22 (CPB-moderately resistant; ADSI = 1.45) and PBC123 (CPB-susceptible; ADSI = 2.98). The de novo sequencing of husks and pulps from control and CPB-infested plants produced 70,073 transcripts. Functional annotation identified genes in diverse biological processes and pathway-related categories. For WGCNA, gene-level expression data were used following low-expression filtering and variance-stabilizing transformation (VST). Co-expression analysis identified 32 modules, from which key modules were prioritized based on module size, eigengene expression patterns, and functional enrichment. bisque4 was associated with cell-wall-related functions, including plant-type secondary cell wall biogenesis, while chocolate4 showed enrichment of defense-associated functions. Network analysis further identified highly connected genes within these key modules as candidate genes associated with the cocoa response to CPB infestation. These findings provide an exploratory framework for understanding tissue and cultivar-associated transcriptional responses to CPB and for prioritizing candidate genes for future functional validation.

Article.Title: Prevalence of intestinal parasitic infections and their association with academic achievement indicators: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Chipa L.; Salazar S.; Valderrama A.
Article.Abstract: Intestinal parasitic infections in children have been associated with learning difficulties, cognitive delays, nutritional deficiencies, impaired physical development, and lower academic performance. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of intestinal parasitic infections and their association with academic performance among school-age children in high-altitude Andean schools. A cross-sectional, observational, and analytical study was conducted in the district of Tamburco (Abancay, Apurímac, Peru). Stool samples from 265 schoolchildren aged 6 to 12 years (mean age: 8.9 ± 1.8 years; 51.3% female, 48.7% male) were selected via simple random sampling. Laboratory diagnostic procedures were performed at the Micaela Bastidas Micronetwork using direct microscopic examination with Lugol’s iodine and physiological saline, along with the Lumbreras rapid spontaneous sedimentation technique. Academic performance was evaluated using official 2018 achievement records across four core curricular domains: science and technology, physical education, mathematics, and communication. The overall prevalence of intestinal parasitic infection was 84.5% (95% CI = 80.1–88.9%). The most prevalent organism was Blastocystis spp. (53.2%), followed by Giardia duodenalis (36.6%), the non-pathogenic commensal protozoan Entamoeba coli (22.3%), and the helminth Ascaris lumbricoides (21.5%). The majority of students achieved the "expected performance" rating in science and technology (78.5%), physical education (88.3%), mathematics (72.8%), and communication (74.0%). Initial unadjusted bivariate analysis showed a nominal association between Entamoeba coli carriage and academic performance in communication (p < 0.05); however, this association did not sustain statistical significance after false discovery rate adjustment (q > 0.05). Although most schoolchildren achieved expected academic levels, the high prevalence of intestinal parasitic infection represents an unmistakable bio-indicator of persistent environmental sanitation exposure and social vulnerability, rather than a direct driver of domain-specific academic failure.

Article.Title: Health risks and lag effects of ambient PM2.5 exposure on respiratory and cardiovascular mortality and morbidity in Ratchaburi, Thailand
Article.Authors: Pengjan S.; Bonnet S.; Garivait S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Exposure to ambient PM 2.5 is a well-established risk factor for respiratory and cardiovascular diseases. In terms of air quality, Ratchaburi, Thailand, faces increasing concerns concerning particulate pollution. This study investigated the health risks associated with PM 2.5 exposure in Ratchaburi from 2015 to 2019, specifically focusing on respiratory and cardiovascular diseases. An exposure–lag–response model was employed to assess health risks on the day of exposure and throughout a seven-day lag period. The results indicate that the risks associated with PM 2.5 exposure vary by age and gender across different lag periods. The elderly and adults were identified as the most vulnerable groups, exhibiting significantly higher risks for respiratory mortality and respiratory morbidity, respectively. Regarding gender, females were found to be significantly more vulnerable to respiratory morbidity. In terms of cardiovascular risks, adults represented the most vulnerable demographic for both mortality and morbidity, while males showed a significantly higher risk for cardiovascular mortality. The findings of this study highlight the necessity of conducting similar investigations in other regions, especially across different provinces of Thailand. These findings provide critical evidence to support policymakers in developing targeted public health interventions and adequate air quality management strategies aimed at enhancing the well-being of the population and safeguarding against the impacts of air pollution, specifically PM 2.5 .

Article.Title: Distal Ulnar Centering and Eccentricity (DUCE) grading: assessing the degree of instability in the distal radioulnar joint
Article.Authors: El Barbari J.; Kordon F.; Kunze H.; Armbruster J.; Grützner P.; Vetter S.; Schnetzke M.; Swartman B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Distal radioulnar joint (DRUJ) instability is challenging to diagnose. The Distal Ulnar Centering and Eccentricity (DUCE) method was introduced as an anatomy-based assessment of DRUJ articulation to reduce rotation-related variability of existing metrics. This study evaluated its responsiveness to increasing instability, developing a point-based grading system. Twelve cadaveric forearms were scanned in stable condition and underwent stepwise induction of instability (TFCC lesion, Galeazzi, Essex-Lopresti). Cone-beam CT scans were obtained in pronation and supination at each stage of instability. DUCE parameters Centering (distance from ulnar head centre C to a notch-derived axis), and Eccentricity (distance from C to deepest notch point) were measured. Responsiveness of DUCE parameters to instability was analysed using a mixed-effects model and compared to radioulnar ratio. Thresholds for DUCE Grading were derived via linear regression. Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using ROC analysis, Youden’s Index, and weighted kappa. RR showed no significant change with increasing instability, whereas DUCE parameters increased progressively (P Centering = 0.005, P Eccentricity <0.001). The DUCE Grading showed good discrimination between stable and unstable joints (AUC 0.78, 95% CI 0.69 to 0.88), with 76.0% overall accuracy (95% CI 66.6 to 83.5) and moderate agreement with the true instability grade (quadratic weighted κ = 0.42). In this cadaveric proof-of-concept study, DUCE Grading provided an anatomy-referenced quantification of DRUJ instability and allowed preliminary severity stratification. As the thresholds were derived and internally validated within a single cohort, they require prospective external validation before the system can support clinical decision-making.

Article.Title: Mild heat treatment ameliorates PCOS by activating PI3K/Akt signaling and inhibiting granulosa cell apoptosis
Article.Authors: Yang Z.; Zhang Q.; Ou X.; Zhang M.; Ji R.; Zhang Z.; Xia J.; Yang Y.; Wu G.
Article.Abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is commonly accompanied by insulin resistance (IR), ovarian dysfunction, and granulosa-cell injury. We investigated whether mild heat treatment (MHT) alleviates PCOS-like reproductive and metabolic abnormalities and explored the potential involvement of PI3K/Akt signaling. A dihydrotestosterone (DHT)-challenged KGN cell model and a dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA)-induced rat model were used. In vitro, KGN cells were exposed to MHT at 40 °C for 1 h, with or without the PI3K inhibitor LY294002. Cell viability, mitochondrial membrane potential, apoptosis, and proliferation were assessed. In vivo, estrous cyclicity, ovarian morphology, androgen levels, fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, glucose tolerance, and insulin tolerance were evaluated. Ovarian IRS-1, GLUT4, PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling, RNA-seq profiles, and inflammatory cytokines were also examined. In DHT-challenged KGN cells, MHT improved cell viability, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, reduced apoptosis, and promoted proliferation; these effects were attenuated by LY294002, suggesting partial dependence on PI3K/Akt signaling in vitro. In DHEA-induced PCOS rats, MHT improved estrous cyclicity, reduced cystic and atretic ovarian changes, and lowered hyperandrogenemia. MHT also improved glucose homeostasis, as shown by reduced fasting insulin and HOMA-IR and improved glucose and insulin tolerance. At the ovarian level, MHT increased IRS-1 and GLUT4 expression and enhanced PI3K/Akt/mTOR phosphorylation, suggesting improved insulin-related signaling activity. RNA-seq indicated partial remodeling of insulin secretion, glycolysis/gluconeogenesis, AMPK, and PI3K/Akt-related transcriptional programs. MHT also reduced serum and ovarian IL-6, IL-1β, and TNF-α levels. MHT improved PCOS-like metabolic and ovarian phenotypes, reduced granulosa-cell apoptosis, and restored PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling. In vitro PI3K inhibition further indicated that the protective effects of MHT in KGN cells were partly dependent on PI3K/Akt signaling. These findings suggest that MHT may represent a potential non-pharmacological strategy for improving insulin resistance and ovarian dysfunction in PCOS models.

Article.Title: Identifying prevalent multimorbidity and its correlates in a low- and middle-income country: a machine learning analysis
Article.Authors: Uthman O.; Hazell M.; Hill J.; Uthman M.; Wahab K.; Saravanan P.; Gill P.; Kengne A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Multimorbidity, the coexistence of two or more chronic conditions, presents growing challenges for health systems in low- and middle-income countries. Neighbourhood socioeconomic conditions are widely assumed to contribute to multimorbidity risk beyond individual characteristics, but this contribution has not been quantified in sub-Saharan Africa. We estimated how much neighbourhood socioeconomic context adds to the identification of prevalent multimorbidity, over and above individual characteristics and place of residence, and compared machine learning with conventional regression for this task. We analysed cross-sectional data from 6,177 adults aged 15 years and older in 691 primary sampling units in the 2016 South Africa Demographic and Health Survey. Multimorbidity was defined as two or more of twelve chronic conditions ascertained by biomarker measurement, self-reported diagnosis or reported treatment. Predictors were classified by temporal status as structural, behavioural, or illness-concurrent; the primary model excluded illness-concurrent variables because current medication use is itself a criterion for ascertaining two of the outcome conditions. We compared 18 supervised algorithms with three regression comparators using repeated ten-fold cross-validation grouped by primary sampling unit, with sampling weights applied in the evaluation of all algorithms and in the fitting of those that accept observation weights. Discrimination was estimated from pooled out-of-fold predictions with cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals. We assessed subgroup sensitivity, false-negative rate and calibration across wealth, age, sex, residence and province. Multimorbidity affected 2,628 participants (weighted prevalence 40.0%). The primary model achieved an area under the curve of 0.776 (95% CI 0.760–0.793), sensitivity 0.599 (0.568–0.631) and specificity 0.785 (0.764–0.804). Adding neighbourhood socioeconomic indicators to a model already containing individual characteristics, province and urban/rural residence changed discrimination by 0.001 (95% CI -0.001 to 0.002); the neighbourhood-level intraclass correlation was 0.027. Machine learning offered no advantage over conventional regression: multilevel logistic regression with a primary-sampling-unit random intercept achieved an identical area under the curve of 0.776 (0.761–0.793), and the total spread across the five best-performing algorithms was 0.004. Including illness-concurrent predictors inflated discrimination by 0.031 (0.025–0.036). Although accuracy was similar across subgroups, sensitivity ranged from 0.00 in adults aged 15–24 years to 0.95 in those aged 65 and over. In a weighted analytic sample drawn from a nationally representative South African survey, neighbourhood socioeconomic context contributed negligibly to identifying prevalent multimorbidity once individual characteristics and place of residence were accounted for, and flexible machine learning offered no discriminative advantage over an appropriately specified multilevel regression. Reported performance of multimorbidity models is materially inflated by predictors that reflect existing disease. Because these data are cross-sectional, the model identifies prevalent rather than incident multimorbidity, and comparable subgroup accuracy conceals near-total failure to identify affected younger adults.

Article.Title: Predicting walking recovery after traumatic cervical spinal cord injury with machine learning: a multicenter cohort study
Article.Authors: Yang S.; Zhou W.; Wan H.; Wu A.; Huang S.; Wang C.; Wang G.; Ding Z.; Li M.
Article.Abstract: This study aims to investigate the effectiveness of various ML models—Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Logistic Regression (LR), Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), and Decision Tree (DT)—in predicting walking recovery after TCSCI. The goal is to develop a robust, personalized predictive model using demographics, injury characteristics, peripheral inflammatory blood biomarkers, and neuroimaging factors metrics. A retrospective cohort of 468 TCSCI patients treated between 2016 and 2022 was included. Patients were divided into training (235), testing (99), and validation (134) groups. Key prognostic features, including demographic data, injury characteristics, peripheral inflammatory blood biomarkers, and MRI features were collected. Several ML models were developed and validated using the training cohort, and performance was assessed in both internal (testing cohort) and external (validation cohort) validation cohorts. Model performance was evaluated using area under the curve (AUC) with 95% DeLong confidence intervals, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), and Brier score for calibration. The study demonstrated that all six ML models successfully predicted walking recovery after TSCI. Among the models, the RF model exhibited the highest performance in the training cohort, achieving perfect AUC, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, and NPV. However, its performance slightly decreased in the validation cohort, AUC of 0.990 (95% CI 0.977–1.000). The LR model showed stable and reliable performance across all cohorts, making it a solid option for predicting recovery. The SVM, DT, and LASSO models also exhibited strong predictive abilities, though with slight variations in performance across cohorts. However, the KNN model showed the lowest overall accuracy and NPV. ML models, particularly RF and LR, offer robust tools for predicting walking recovery in patients with TCSCI. While the RF model performed best in the training cohort, the LR model demonstrated consistent and reliable results across all cohorts, suggesting its potential for clinical application. Meanwhile, the SVM, DT and LASSO models also showed strong performance. These models could aid in personalized rehabilitation planning, improving clinical decision-making and patient prognostication.

Article.Title: Inclination-dependent fracture evolution and critical instability of echelon-grooved boreholes for coalbed methane recovery in low-permeability coal
Article.Authors: Meng W.; Zhang T.; Tian J.; Yan B.; Pang M.; Pan H.
Article.Abstract: Improving coalbed methane recovery from low-permeability coal requires permeability-enhancement structures that promote fracture connectivity without compromising borehole stability. Echelon guide grooves provide a controllable defect configuration for inducing directional cracking around coalbed methane recovery boreholes; however, the inclination-dependent fracture evolution and critical instability mechanism remain unclear. In this study, coal-like specimens containing a central coalbed methane recovery borehole and echelon guide grooves were prepared with groove inclinations of 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, and 90°. Uniaxial compression tests were conducted, and VIC-3D digital image correlation was used to monitor full-field strain localization, crack initiation, crack propagation, and borehole deformation. The results show that, as the guide-groove inclination increases from 0° to 45°, the peak strength, residual strength, and deformation modulus decrease significantly; when the inclination further increases to 90°, these mechanical parameters gradually recover. Crack evolution results reveal that cracks mainly initiate from the borehole wall and propagate as anti-wing cracks under small inclination angles, whereas they mainly initiate from the guide-groove tips and propagate as wing cracks at inclinations of 45°-90°. The 45° specimen exhibits the largest number of cracks, the widest main crack, and the most severe circumferential damage. Furthermore, the borehole damage degree first increases and then decreases with increasing guide-groove inclination, reaching its maximum at 45°, identifying 45° as the most unfavorable inclination among the five angles investigated under the present testing conditions. These findings reveal the dual role of echelon guide grooves in enhancing fracture connectivity and weakening borehole integrity, providing a quantitative basis for optimizing directional slotting parameters for stable and efficient coalbed methane recovery from low-permeability coal.

Article.Title: Beyond the maximum gradient: a consecutive-threshold criterion for nitracline detection in the Northwestern Indian Ocean
Article.Authors: Princy M.; Nandakumar K.; Vrinda P.; Kalita R.; Lotliker A.
Article.Abstract: Depth of the nitracline is an important indicator of the vertical distribution and availability of nitrate in the upper ocean. While the conventional definition of the nitracline as the depth of maximum nitrate gradient (dN/dz) has been widely accepted, this study introduces a complementary consecutive-gradient criterion to detect the onset of a sustained nitrate gradient zone. A total of 358 profiles from five Bio-Argo floats in the northwestern Indian Ocean, were analysed. Further, the nitracline depth was derived using three different methods: maximum gradient, single threshold, and consecutive threshold method. Of the three, the consecutive-threshold method provides a consistent approach for detecting the onset of a sustained nitrate gradient zone. It maintains a continuous nitrate gradient and is less affected by random spikes or noise. Hence, a consecutive gradient criterion is proposed for nitracline detection, defining the depth where dN/dz ≥ 0.1 µmol kg− 1 m− 1 is sustained over a 14 m continuous vertical span. Further, nitracline depth showed a strong association with the 26 °C isotherm (D26), which was used as an empirical thermal proxy when D26 > MLD. Under strong mixing, when D26 < MLD, the 23.5 °C isotherm (D23.5) showed a stronger association and was used as an alternative proxy. This will provide a practical thermal proxy for estimating nitracline depth in regions where direct nitrate measurements are unavailable.

Article.Title: Cell-type and donor-level epigenetic variation shape intestinal inflammatory responses to SARS-CoV-2 spike protein
Article.Authors: Chen H.; Bailey J.; Mezghanni E.; Sztein M.; Bafford A.; Salerno-Goncalves R.
Article.Abstract: Although coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) is associated with gastrointestinal symptoms and systemic hyperinflammation, the epigenetic mechanisms linking SARS-CoV-2 to intestinal immune activation remain poorly understood. We investigated histone modifications in human ileum immune cells following ex vivo exposure to the recombinant SARS-CoV-2 spike protein using mass cytometry. Cytokine expression (TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-17A, IL-6, and IL-10) and 14 histone marks were evaluated across eight major immune cell subsets, including B cells, T cells, resident T cells, natural killer (NK) cells, NKT cells, γδ T cells, mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells, and macrophages (MФ). Spike protein exposure induced coordinated inflammatory cytokine responses accompanied by extensive cell-type-specific epigenetic remodeling. MAIT cells, resident T cells, conventional T cells, and MФ exhibited the greatest chromatin remodeling. In contrast, NK cells, NKT cells, B cells, and γδ T cells showed no or few significant epigenetic changes. Linear mixed-effects modeling indicated that epigenetic associations with inflammatory responses were primarily attributable to differences between donors rather than variation among cell subsets within the same donor. Cell-subset identity remained independently associated with inflammatory response, with resident T cells showing significantly higher inflammatory scores, while the other cell subsets did not differ significantly. Together, these findings suggest that interindividual epigenetic variation and cell-subset identity are key determinants of intestinal inflammatory responses to SARS-CoV-2 spike protein.

Article.Title: Chronic stress-associated growth and metastasis of triple-negative breast cancer potentially involves β-adrenergic/p38 MAPK signaling
Article.Authors: Teng F.; Wu T.; Li X.; Li S.; Li K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Chronic stress is known to facilitate the progression of breast cancer. The p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (p38 MAPK) pathway is involved in multiple stress-related cascade reactions, but its role under chronic stress in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains unclear. In this study, a nude mice model bearing TNBC was established. Chronic stress was induced via the restraint method, and its effects on epinephrine (E) and norepinephrine (NE) release, tumor growth and metastasis, and p38 MAPK phosphorylation were investigated. In parallel, the effects of E and NE on the proliferation, migration, and p-p38 MAPK levels of TNBC cell lines (MDA-MB-231 and MDA-MB-468) were examined in vitro. In vivo findings revealed that chronic stress promoted TNBC growth and metastasis, increased plasma E and NE levels, and reduced p-p38 MAPK expression. Notably, β₂-AR expression was higher in TNBC tissues than in normal breast tissues, and was also higher in TNBC cells than in normal mammary epithelial cells. In vitro, E and NE enhanced TNBC cell proliferation and migration, suppressed p38 MAPK phosphorylation, and upregulated PCNA and MMP-9. However, Propranolol (Pro) partially attenuated these effects by inhibiting TNBC cell proliferation and migration, restoring p38 MAPK phosphorylation, and decreasing PCNA and MMP-9 levels. These results suggest that chronic stress promotes TNBC progression, potentially involving β-adrenergic/p38 MAPK signaling, and support further investigation of this pathway in chronic stress-associated TNBC progression.

Article.Title: PINK1 agonist MTK458 attenuates cerebral edema by protecting blood-brain barrier integrity in intracerebral hemorrhage mice
Article.Authors: Ma P.; Yang J.; Zeng G.; Xu X.; Huang N.; Tang J.; Cheng Y.
Article.Abstract: Secondary blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption and vasogenic edema drive neurological deterioration after intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), but targeted therapies remain lacking. PTEN-induced putative kinase 1 (PINK1) is a neuroprotective kinase, yet its role in ICH-induced BBB damage is unclear. This study investigates whether MTK458, a novel PINK1 agonist, protects BBB integrity after ICH and elucidates mechanisms. An ICH mouse model was employed and MTK458 (10, 50, 100 mg/kg) were administered intraperitoneally. The effects of MTK458 were evaluated using brain water content measurements, BBB integrity detection and neurological impairment assessments. A hemoglobin-stimulated BV2 microglia-bEnd.3 endothelial cell co-culture system was established to assess the effects of MTK458 on microglia-mediated tight junctions loss of BBB in vitro. PINK1 expression was significantly downregulated after ICH, with its lowest level observed at 72 h. MTK458 (50 mg/kg) reduced Evans blue extravasation and brain edema, attenuated microglial activation and neuroinflammation, decreased neuronal apoptosis, and improved both acute and subacute neurological function in vivo. MTK458 reversed hemoglobin-induced PINK1 loss in BV2 cells and reduced BV2-mediated damage to bEnd.3 tight junctions in vitro. Mechanistically, MTK458 restored microglial PINK1 expression, inhibited ROS production and cytosolic mtDNA leakage, and thereby suppressed activation of the cGAS-STING-NF-κB signalling pathway, leading to MMP-9 suppression and ZO-1/occludin protection. Consistent with this, the STING agonist dimeric amidobenzimidazole (diABZI) reversed the inhibitory effect of MTK458 on MMP-9, abolished its protection of tight junctions, and compromised BBB integrity. MTK458 activates PINK1, inhibits the cGAS-STING-NF-κB pathway, reduces microglial MMP-9 release, protects BBB integrity, alleviates edema and neuroinflammation, and improves neurological outcomes, providing a novel therapeutic strategy for secondary ICH injury.

Article.Title: Dysbiosis of the cervical lymph node microbiome associated with lymphadenitis in guinea pigs (Cavia porcellus)
Article.Authors: Barrientos N.; Del Solar J.; Mauri J.; Fernandez-Castro P.; Polveiro R.; Da Silva Vieira D.; Bardales W.; Quintana J.; Frias H.; Murga L.; Lapa R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cervical lymphadenitis is a significant infectious disease in guinea pig (Cavia porcellus) production, although the microbiota associated with affected lymph nodes remains poorly characterized. This study compared the microbiota of cervical lymph nodes from healthy guinea pigs and those with lymphadenitis using 16S rRNA gene sequencing, bioinformatics analysis, and molecular validation by PCR. The results showed that healthy lymph nodes harbor diverse bacterial communities, while infected lymph nodes exhibit a marked reduction in microbial diversity and a dominance of Streptococcus equi subsp. zooepidemicus. Furthermore, a subset of samples revealed an alternative etiology characterized by the dominance of the genus Caviibacter, suggesting etiological heterogeneity of the disease in this study. Taken together, these findings suggest that cervical lymphadenitis in guinea pigs is associated with dysbiosis of the lymph node microbiome and support the use of metagenomic approaches for etiological characterization.

Article.Title: Plant-mediated green synthesis of silver nanoparticles using Amaranthus spinosus L. extract: antimicrobial, antioxidant and nano-seedling enhancement
Article.Authors: Khalil D.; Kamel N.; Darwish D.; Ayed F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Amaranthus spinosus is a medicinal plant rich in bioactive metabolites with potential biomedical applications. Our present study was designed to investigate Egyptian-grown A. spinosus as a sustainable biological source for silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) synthesis and to characterize the resulting nanoparticles and evaluate their biological properties. In the current investigation, AgNPs were successfully biosynthesized using the plant extract of A. spinosus as a natural stabilizing and reducing agent. Phytochemical screening proved the presence of phenol, flavonoids, saponins, and terpenoids in the plant extract. The synthesized AgNPs were evaluated by UV–Vis spectroscopy, FTIR, TEM, FE-SEM, EDX, and XRD analyses. Morphological observations revealed predominantly spherical and well-dispersed nanoparticles with nanoscale dimensions and crystalline cubic-phase geometry. Comparative analyses demonstrated that AgNPs displayed relatively higher antioxidant, antimicrobial, and cell viability assessment than the plant extract. The nanoparticles also revealed strong antibacterial activity against Acinetobacter baumannii , Enterobacter cloacae , Staphylococcus aureus , and Staphylococcus haemolyticus . Pronounced antifungal activity was also observed against Cochliobolus specifier , Fusarium oxysporum , and F usarium solani . The plant extract exhibited good cellular compatibility, with viability exceeding 100%, but the manufactured AgNPs showed severe cytotoxicity toward RAW264.7 macrophages, with cell viability falling to about 1% at both tested dosages (10 and 25 µg/mL). Furthermore, the AgNPs showed very little NO inhibition (0.74% and 2.85% at 10 and 25 µg/mL, respectively), which was linked to significant cytotoxicity and cannot be regarded as conclusive proof of anti-inflammatory efficacy. These results suggest that the plant extract has a better cytocompatibility profile than the synthetic AgNPs. To prove the plant extract’s anti-inflammatory efficacy, more research employing non-cytotoxic doses and additional inflammatory biomarkers is needed. Furthermore, AgNPs treatment significantly promoted seed germination and seedling growth of Hordeum vulgare in a concentration-dependent manner. These findings highlight the prospect of green-synthesized AgNPs as multifunctional nanomaterials for agricultural, pharmaceutical, and biomedical applications.
