Article.Title: Waterborne eDNA metabarcoding of the upper Llano River watershed (Texas, USA) detects regionally unreported green plant taxa
Article.Authors: Hurtado L.; Sanbonmatsu K.; Kruse D.; Spalink D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Environmental DNA (eDNA) represents a promising tool for documenting biological diversity in locales where intensive field surveys are challenging, as in the case of west-central Texas. Its utility is amplified in lotic systems, which can transport eDNA several kilometers from its source and often contain signals from both aquatic and nearby terrestrial organisms. In the present study, we employed waterborne eDNA metabarcoding to characterize the extent and distribution of green plant (Viridiplantae) diversity in two west-central Texas rivers: the North Llano River and the South Llano River. We detected taxa from 51 green plant families, including both streptophytes and chlorophytes, and elucidated patterns of green plant diversity across the study area. Some taxa were not previously documented where we detected them, representing novel distributional data that can be leveraged in other ecological research contexts. Collectively, our findings highlight the utility and limitations of eDNA metabarcoding for broad-scale biodiversity characterization and provide insights into the floristic composition of Texas streams.

Article.Title: Spatial fairness in taxi demand prediction: a hybrid approach leveraging district profiles
Article.Authors: Eslami G.; Ghaderi F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate taxi demand forecasting is essential for efficient and equitable urban transportation management. This study proposes a hybrid framework for spatio-temporal taxi demand prediction, evaluated on a large-scale dataset from Chicago. The proposed approach consists of three main components. First, missing demand data are reconstructed using a combination of Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) and White Shark Optimization (WSO), enabling the recovery of latent spatial-temporal structures. Second, a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network is employed to capture temporal dependencies in demand patterns. Third, a fairness-aware regularization mechanism based on Relative Hardship Proximity (RHP) is introduced to control disparities in prediction errors across demographically similar regions. This mechanism explicitly penalizes unequal error distributions, guiding the model toward more balanced performance across urban areas. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 5.1 and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 3.8. Importantly, the improvement in fairness is obtained with only a marginal cost in accuracy, reflected by a Price of Fairness (PoF) of approximately 2%. These findings demonstrate that incorporating structured fairness constraints into demand forecasting models can significantly enhance equity while maintaining high predictive performance, offering a practical and scalable solution for fair urban transportation planning.

Article.Title: Blockchain-enhanced SDN framework with deep unfolding spatial frequency attention network and pine cone optimization for smart city IoT cybersecurity
Article.Authors: Vasumathy M.; Roselinkiruba R.; Shrestha S.; Jude Moses Anto Devakanth J.; Kavitha J.; Jothi C.
Article.Abstract: The rapid expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) in smart cities has revolutionized services by connecting numerous devices to deliver intelligent applications. However, this interconnected environment also exposes IoT networks to severe cybersecurity risks, including data breaches, intrusions, and advanced persistent threats. Traditional detection mechanisms often struggle with high-dimensional traffic, noisy data, missing values, and evolving attack patterns, which significantly reduce their reliability. Moreover, ensuring secure and tamper-proof storage of detection outcomes in large-scale IoT system s remains a major challenge. To address these issues, this paper proposes a blockchain-enhanced IoT cybersecurity framework for smart cities, utilizing a software-defined networking framework with a Deep Unfolding Spatial-Frequency Attention Network and Pine Cone Optimization (DUSFAN-PCO). Initially, input data is collected from UNSW-NB15 and CIC-IDS2017 datasets. The collected data are pre-processed using Diffusion Models for Missing Value Imputation (DMMVI) to handle noise and missing values. Next, Carpet Weaver Optimization (CWO) is applied to select the most informative attributes. These selected features are then fed into the Deep Unfolding Spatial-Frequency Attention Network (DUSFAN), which classifies IoT network traffic into normal and multiple attack categories through real-time anomaly detection. To further enhance detection accuracy, Pine Cone Optimization (PCO) is used to fine-tune DUSFAN’s weight parameters. Finally, the results are securely stored and managed using a Blockchain-Based Secure PBFT Lightweight Consensus (SPBFT-LC), ensuring immutability, transparency, and trust among IoT nodes. The proposed DUSFAN-PCO framework achieves an accuracy of 99.20% on UNSW-NB15 and 99.48% on CIC-IDS2017, with F1-scores of 99.52% and 99.50%, and ROC values of 0.99–1.00 across both datasets. Coupled with high blockchain-based security integrity (> 99%), it ensures robust, real-time, and reliable detection of IoT network intrusions, making it highly suitable for secure and resilient smart city IoT environments.

Article.Title: Technology topic mining and evolution path analysis based on dynamic topic modeling: a case study of hydrogen energy vehicle technology
Article.Authors: Quan Y.; Jie S.; Wei P.; Ji D.; Zhao L.
Article.Abstract: Technology topic evolution analysis and convergence trend prediction constitute important research directions in technological intelligence. Addressing the identity drift and threshold dependency issues inherent in conventional topic models for cross-period topic matching, as well as the limited capacity of existing technology evolution studies to quantitatively predict technology convergence trends, this paper proposes an integrated framework for technology evolution analysis and convergence prediction that combines the Dynamic Topic Model (DTM), technology lifecycle theory, and Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN). The framework first employs a Logistic growth model to delineate technology lifecycle stages, subsequently applies DTM to dynamically model time-series patent texts for continuous topic tracking and multi-dimensional evolution identification, and further constructs a topic co-occurrence network to perform link prediction and evaluation of potential technology convergence relationships using GCN. Based on patent data from the Derwent Innovation Index covering hydrogen energy vehicles from 2001 to 2024 (11,872 valid patents) as a case study, a dynamic evolution map of 50 technology topics was constructed and technology convergence trends were predicted. The findings reveal that: (1) hydrogen energy vehicle technology exhibits a three-stage evolutionary pattern characterized by “single-point breakthrough—system expansion—intelligent convergence,” with core technology topics progressively shifting from fuel cell stack R&D toward membrane electrode integration, from high-pressure hydrogen storage toward diversified storage and transportation, and from power control toward intelligent energy management; (2) topic persistence analysis indicates that technology differentiation and reorganization intensified significantly during 2017–2024, with newly emerging topics predominantly oriented toward vehicle-level integration and thermal management, reflecting a shift in innovation focus from the “component level” to the “system integration level”; (3) the GCN-based technology convergence prediction model outperforms all four baseline models across four of the five evaluation metrics (AUC = 0.8925), and the prediction results reveal two differentiated convergence pathways—“emerging–emerging” and “mature–emerging”—providing forward-looking references for technology deployment. The proposed integrated “evolution analysis–convergence prediction” framework offers a systematic and quantitative methodology for technology evolution research, supporting technology planning and strategic decision-making in the hydrogen energy industry.

Article.Title: Multi-criteria prioritized reinforcement learning for autonomous underwater vehicle navigation in 3D multi-node environments
Article.Authors: Yan L.; Zhang Q.; Huangfu Z.; Shangguan D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) are increasingly used as mobile data collectors in underwater wireless sensor networks, where navigation must balance task completion, obstacle avoidance, communication performance, and energy efficiency. This study develops a Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient framework with Multi-Criteria Prioritized Experience Replay (MC-PER-TD3). The replay priority combines normalized temporal-difference error with a goal-proximity heuristic; energy consumption is incorporated into the reward and data-collection evaluation rather than the replay priority. A soft potential-field reward and a time-window-based waypoint escape-transition mechanism are further used to guide continuous navigation. Across six training seeds and 60 deterministic-policy evaluation episodes per seed, MC-PER-TD3 achieved 100% mission success with zero observed collisions. Relative to uniform-replay TD3, the mean successful path length decreased from 13.188 ± 3.885 m to 10.985 ± 0.436 m and task time from 6.911 ± 1.511 s to 5.654 ± 0.257 s. A standard TD-error-only PER-TD3 baseline achieved 50% mission success, whereas the combined TD-error-plus-goal replay achieved consistent completion across all six training seeds. Additional zero-shot tests under observation noise, current perturbations, fixed and randomized obstacle layouts reveal condition-dependent robustness and clear failure boundaries. In UWSN evaluation, MC-PER-TD3 achieved the highest mean energy efficiency, while TD3 retained the highest throughput, indicating a throughput-energy trade-off rather than universal dominance.

Article.Title: Driving pressure, simplified elastic mechanical power, and time to liberation from mechanical ventilation: a competing-risks and time-anchored observational study
Article.Authors: Pan X.; Chen S.; Yu X.; Yang D.
Article.Abstract: Driving pressure ( \(\Delta\) P) and mechanical power are associated with liberation from mechanical ventilation, but the temporal interpretation of measurements obtained late in the ventilation course is uncertain. We analysed adults ventilated \(\ge\) 24 h in the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV). \(\Delta\) P and simplified elastic mechanical power (MP el ) were calculated from contemporaneously charted variables in the final 6-h controlled-mode window before the end of the first invasive-ventilation episode. The primary competing-risk analysis was landmarked at the end of this exposure window; successful liberation was extubation without reintubation, non-invasive ventilation, or death within 48 h, with death as a competing event. Binary outcome associations were examined in the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD). A separate time-zero-aligned, entropy-balanced analysis compared observed \(\Delta\) P \(\le\) 14 versus >14 cmH 2 O at the first operational low-support time point. Of 7,126 MIMIC-IV patients with measurable \(\Delta\) P, complete-case landmark models included 6,316 ( \(\Delta\) P) and 6,296 (MP el ); higher values were associated with slower successful liberation (cause-specific hazard ratios per standard deviation [SD]: 0.90 and 0.76; Fine–Gray subdistribution hazard ratios 0.85 and 0.68). In eICU-CRD (n=1,260), higher \(\Delta\) P was associated with 48-h failure (adjusted odds ratio per SD 1.79), although 419 of 420 failures were deaths. In the weighted comparison, the 28-day difference in area under the cumulative-incidence curve for successful liberation was \(-1.12\) d (95% confidence interval [CI] \(-1.70\) to \(-0.58\) ) for \(\Delta\) P >14 versus \(\le\) 14. These findings support a prognostic association but do not establish the effect of actively lowering \(\Delta\) P.

Article.Title: A LiDAR-driven urban energy benchmarking framework for mapping building energy intensity and carbon emissions in hyper-arid cities
Article.Authors: Hzami A.; Abu-Rayash A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rapid urbanization and intensifying heat extremes are accelerating building energy demand and associated carbon emissions in hyper-arid cities. However, quantifying building-level energy performance at high spatial resolution remains challenging because building morphology, floor area, and energy-consumption data are rarely integrated within a comprehensive framework. This study develops an integrated geospatial framework that integrates LiDAR-derived three-dimensional building morphology, high-resolution building footprints, and electricity-consumption data to quantify building-level energy use intensity (EUI), operational carbon emissions, and energy-performance patterns across Qatar. LiDAR-derived building morphology, deep-learning-based building footprints from high-resolution Pléiades imagery, and 14,186 electricity meter records were integrated with forest-based regression to estimate EUI across the mapped building stock. The analysis reveals pronounced sectoral and spatial disparities in building energy performance. Residential villas account for 35.5% of estimated operational building carbon emissions, while commercial, industrial, and governmental buildings collectively contribute 56.02%. Between 2020 and 2024, electricity consumption increased by 8.52% in the residential sector and by 25.0% in commercial and industrial buildings. Annual ean EUI rose from 158 ± 15 to 206 ± 20 kWh/m 2 , and total operational CO 2 -equivalent emissions increased from 19.3 to 22.7 MtCO 2 e. Annual mean carbon emission intensity also rose from 111.5 to 130.7 kgCO 2 e/m 2 , a 17.22% increase. Building-level clustering identified substantial heterogeneity in energy performance, with only 18% of buildings classified in the lower-EUI group (Cluster 1), compared with 50% in the higher-EUI group (Cluster 3), which had a mean EUI of 455 kWh/m 2 /year. The results identify substantial opportunities for spatially targeted energy-efficiency interventions and carbon reduction across building sectors. The proposed framework provides a high-resolution baseline for building-energy benchmarking and supports evidence-based prioritization of energy-efficiency and decarbonization strategies in hyper-arid urban environments.

Article.Title: Structural diversity of human urinary N-glycans revealed by reversed-phase LC/MS/MS toward a resource for biomarker discovery
Article.Authors: Makino R.; Natsuka S.
Article.Abstract: Glycan microheterogeneity sensitively reflects biological changes and represents a promising source of biomarkers for early disease detection. However, the high structural diversity, isomeric complexity, and wide dynamic range of glycans remain major obstacles to comprehensive glycomic analysis, particularly for low-abundance species. To overcome these limitations, we developed an isomer-resolved N -glycan dataset that supports automated structural assignment. The platform is based on pyridylamination, which enables precise separation of glycan isomers according to reversed-phase HPLC. Furthermore, by quantifying the contribution of individual monosaccharide residues to retention behavior, unknown structures can be inferred from the retention times of structurally related known glycans. By integrating normalized reversed-phase HPLC retention times with detailed structural information obtained through chemical derivatization and MS/MS analysis, we established a framework for accurate isomer-discriminative analysis in a single reversed-phase LC/MS run. We applied this strategy to pooled urine samples of healthy individuals and comprehensively characterized urinary N -glycans, including structures carrying N -acetylneuraminic acid, sulfate group, phosphate group, glucuronic acid, Lewis antigens, blood group antigens, Sda antigen, and HNK-1 antigen. This dataset provides a foundation for detecting low-abundance disease-associated urinary glycans and may accelerate glycan biomarker discovery.

Article.Title: Chain mediating effect of resilience and disease acceptance on social support and self-management behavior in patients with liver cirrhosis
Article.Authors: Sui S.; Wu M.; Yu Q.; Yue M.; Ju B.; Yan N.; Liu H.; Zhang H.; Sun Y.
Article.Abstract: To explore the chain mediating effects of psychological resilience and disease acceptance on the relationship between social support and self-management behavior in patients with cirrhosis. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 187 patients with cirrhosis hospitalized from January 2024 to January 2026. Relevant data were collected using general information questionnaires and standardized scales. SPSS 26.0 with the PROCESS plug-in was used for statistical analysis and chain mediation modeling to explore the mediating effects of psychological resilience and disease acceptance on the association between social support and self-management among cirrhotic patients. Baseline scale scores of 187 cirrhotic patients: BRS-6 (15.74 ± 2.44), AIS (20.32 ± 2.65), social support (27.53 ± 4.59), self-management (43.60 ± 4.51). All indicators showed significant positive pairwise correlations ( P < 0.05). Social support showed a prominent total statistical association with self-management (adjusted β = 0.542, t = 8.701, P < 0.001) and retained a significant direct correlational link after accounting for mediators and covariates (β = 0.425, t = 5.792, P < 0.001). The chained pathway of social support-resilience-disease acceptance-self-management was statistically significant (β = 0.047, Boot 95% CI : 0.020-0.074). Total standardized indirect effect was 0.434 (Boot 95%CI: 0.294-0.579), occupying 50.60% of the total effect.Summary statistics for the regression model predicting self-management were reported: R = 0.711, R²=0.506, F = 24.742, P < 0.001, indicating the model explained 50.6% of the total variance in self-management behavior. Social support was associated with self-management behavior among patients with liver cirrhosis, both directly and indirectly, through psychological resilience and disease acceptance, acting independently and in sequence. Interventions that strengthen social support, psychological resilience, and disease acceptance may improve self-management, although their effects on long-term clinical outcomes remain to be established.

Article.Title: Codon bias analysis in the chloroplast genome of Warburgia ugandensis (Canellaceae) and phylogenetic analysis within magnoliids
Article.Authors: Zhang S.; Ling L.
Article.Abstract: The complete chloroplast genome of Warburgia ugandensis , an endangered medicinal tree in East Africa, was sequenced and characterized. The genome is 157,374 bp in length with a typical quadripartite structure, comprising a large single-copy region of 87,235 bp, a small single-copy region of 17,873 bp, and two inverted repeats of 26,133 bp each. The overall GC content is 36.5%, and the genome encodes 113 unique genes. Phylogenetic analysis of 74 magnoliid species from five orders and 12 families robustly places W. ugandensis as the earliest-diverging lineage within the order Canellales, forming a sister clade to Tasmannia lanceolata , Drimys granadensis , and Pseudowintera colorata . Codon usage bias analysis reveals pronounced AT-richness and deviation from mutation-driven expectations. Neutrality plot, ENC-plot, and PR2-plot collectively demonstrate that natural selection plays a major role in shaping codon usage patterns. Seven candidate optimal codons, predominantly ending in A or U, were identified. Ka/Ks ratio analysis indicates pervasive purifying selection across most protein-coding genes, with only rpl23 showing a ratio > 1 suggestive of positive selection. RSCU-based clustering and Ka/Ks-based clustering are both consistent with the basal phylogenetic position of this species indicated by the phylogenetic tree. This study provides the first foundational chloroplast genomic resource for W. ugandensis , which may be useful for future conservation genetic studies of this threatened species.

The formulation produced concentration-dependent cytotoxicity, with an estimated IC 50 of 13.47 µM. At 20 µM for 48 h, the percentage of CD206-positive cells changed from 76.8 ± 2.31% to 21.7 ± 1.98%, whereas the percentage of CD80-positive cells changed from 18.6 ± 1.72% to 68.3 ± 2.54%. Because 20 µM exceeded the estimated IC 50 , these observations may partly reflect selective cell loss. Flow-cytometric measurements were performed in triplicate (n = 3), but confirmation in independent biological experiments remains necessary. Additional viability-matched and functionally validated experiments are required.

Article.Authors: Sollazzo K.; Karran A.; Rolon-Merette T.; Ruiz-Segura A.; Coursaris C.; Léger P.; Sénécal S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Digital learning systems rarely adapt to momentary cognitive state, creating risk of underload or overload. The current study testes whether EEG-based closed-loop pacing can regulate task load dynamics during a digital constellation-learning task. Fifty-one participants were randomly assigned to adaptive, reward, or control conditions. In the adaptive condition, a task loas index derived from frontal theta and parietal alpha adjusted feedback duration between 3 and 8 s; fixed 5s feedback was used in reward and control conditions, with reward participants receiving performance-contingent draw entries. Accuracy increased across blocks in all groups, with no significant group or group-by-block effect. In contrast, EEG indices showed group-specific trajectories: task load decreased over time in the adaptive condition, and frontal theta and parietal alpha showed significant group-by-block interactions. The adaptive condition also showed reduced ate-session feedback duration, while reward participants reported higher satisfaction. intrinsic motivation did not moderate group effects, although perceived competence predicated final-block performance and interest and effort predicted engagement. These findings suggest that EEG-based feedback pacing can regulate neurophysiological task load dynamics despite lack of immediate accuracy gains under the present task constraints. The results support neuroadaptive scaffolding as a state-regulation mechanism for digital learning.

Article.Title: Effects of waveguide tube geometry and surrounding medium conditions on acoustic emission signal attenuation
Article.Authors: Chen F.; Duan S.; Zhang G.
Article.Abstract: Deep-seated deformation in landslides is typically concealed and exhibits a time lag; reliably obtaining information on internal deformation through acoustic emission (AE) technology remains a key challenge in landslide early warning. Metal waveguides can reduce the impact of strong soil attenuation on AE signal acquisition; however, the mechanisms of propagation attenuation within the metal waveguides themselves remain unclear. To address this, this study conducted controlled laboratory experiments on wave propagation in waveguide tubes to systematically investigate the differences in propagation attenuation caused by waveguide diameter, wall thickness, and the state of the surrounding medium. By analyzing time-domain waveforms, frequency-domain characteristics, time–frequency representations, and fitting exponential attenuation models, the study examined the attenuation changes with increasing propagation distance under different operating conditions. The results indicate that the amplitude of AE signals generally exhibits exponential attenuation as the propagation distance increases. When comparing individual factors, the surrounding-medium condition produced the largest change in attenuation, followed by outer diameter, whereas wall thickness had the weakest effect. Attenuation was also frequency selective. These findings provide a basis for selecting components for active waveguide systems (AWS), determining sensor spacing, and establishing effective monitoring ranges.

Article.Title: Local-tele coupling coordination of land use pressure and urbanization based on multi-source remote sensing data
Article.Authors: Li W.; Deng K.; Zhang B.; Gu Y.; Zhao J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Assessing land use pressure is fundamental to understanding regional sustainability. This study constructs a comprehensive Land Use Pressure Index (L) using remote sensing and socio-economic data from 2000 to 2019 across three dimensions—carbon effects, ecological risks, and landscape stability—with weights objectively determined by the entropy weight method. An Urbanization Composite Index (U) is also developed across demographic, economic, spatial, and social dimensions. We further introduce a local-tele coupling coordination framework incorporating an Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) spatial weight matrix to capture inter-city spillover effects, extending traditional coupling analysis to include both local and tele-coupling interactions. When applied to the Middle Reaches of the Yangtze River Urban Agglomeration, the framework reveals: (1) the coupling degree (C) remained consistently high throughout 2000–2019; (2) the coupling coordination degree (D) transitioned from predominantly “barely coordinated” to “primary coordinated,” with four cities (Wuhan, Changsha, Nanchang, and Xinyu) achieving “intermediate coordinated” status by 2019; and (3) the three major urban agglomerations exhibited distinct evolutionary pathways. This study offers a spatially explicit perspective on urbanization–land use interactions and provides empirical evidence for differentiated land management in urban agglomerations.

Article.Title: Automatic segmentation of histological zones in rat distraction osteogenesis using a self-configuring deep learning pipeline
Article.Authors: Dittrich L.; Ramge J.; Neunaber C.; Wolff D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Distraction osteogenesis regenerates bone by gradually separating bone segments and inducing new tissue formation within the distraction gap. Although histologic assessment of regenerate composition is essential for evaluating tissue maturation, manual delineation of tissue compartments is labor-intensive and subject to observer variability. This study evaluated a deep learning-based workflow for the automated segmentation of three histologic zones in a rat distraction osteogenesis model: the fibrous interzone, the microcolumn formation zone, and the remodeling zone. High-resolution hematoxylin and eosin- and pentachrome-stained sections were used to train two-dimensional U-Net models in multi-class and single-class settings with five-fold cross-validation and a held-out test set. Performance was assessed using the Dice score, precision, and recall, and was supplemented by a qualitative review of the prediction overlays. On the test set, segmentation was most reliable for the fibrous interzone (Dice 0.76 in H&E; 0.75 in pentachrome), followed by the microcolumn formation zone (Dice 0.63; 0.57). The remodeling zone (Dice 0.29; 0.44) was the most challenging compartment due to its variable and late-stage appearance. Due to incomplete and partly ambiguous ground truth, quantitative metrics were interpreted alongside qualitative histologic assessment. Under this combined evaluation, the pentachrome multi-class configuration yielded the most coherent results. These findings suggest that deep learning-assisted segmentation is a reproducible approach for histologic compartment analysis in distraction osteogenesis. Beyond this application, the evaluated pipeline provides a practical workflow for related histologic segmentation tasks. Implementation in 3D Slicer enables inference, visualization, and area-based quantification in an accessible format for translational research.

Article.Title: mRNA vaccines expressing Plasmodium falciparum CSP with distinct antigen localisation profiles induce differential humoral immunity and partial protection in a mouse sporozoite challenge model
Article.Authors: Alhareth Z.; Truby A.; Taylor W.; Salman A.; Hill A.; López-Camacho C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pre-erythrocytic malaria vaccines aim to prevent infection at the earliest stage of parasite entry by blocking Plasmodium falciparum sporozoites before hepatocyte invasion, thereby halting progression to symptomatic blood-stage disease. The circumsporozoite protein (CSP), the dominant surface antigen of sporozoites, remains the leading target for pre-erythrocytic vaccine development. Here, we investigated the use of an mRNA vaccine platform to express CSP and examined how antigen localisation influences immunogenicity and protective efficacy. We compared mRNA constructs encoding soluble CSP with versions engineered for membrane anchoring using either a mammalian glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) sequence derived from placental alkaline phosphatase or a heterologous transmembrane (TM) domain from influenza H1N1 haemagglutinin. Immunisation with CSP mRNA-LNP formulations showed that membrane association altered the magnitude and profile of antibody responses, with distinct effects observed across the NANP repeat and C-terminal regions of CSP. Following intravenous challenge with transgenic Plasmodium berghei sporozoites expressing P. falciparum CSP, both soluble and membrane-associated vaccines delayed parasitaemia and conferred partial protection, but membrane targeting did not consistently improve protective efficacy. These findings show that antigen localisation can shape the immune response to mRNA-expressed CSP, while also highlighting that enhanced immunogenicity does not necessarily translate into greater protection.

Article.Title: Laboratory evaluation and field observations of plastic-concrete cutoff walls for seepage control in earth-dam foundations
Article.Authors: Faridmehr I.; Sahraei M.; Wamuziri S.
Article.Abstract: Plastic-concrete cutoff walls require low hydraulic conductivity and sufficiently low stiffness, and the wall must accommodate foundation deformation. Twenty-five laboratory mixtures of Type V Portland cement, sodium bentonite, water, and graded aggregates with a 16 mm nominal maximum size were evaluated. The study measured slump, 28-day compressive strength, static chord modulus, flexural response, and hydraulic conductivity; field observations were qualitative and noted slurry loss and surface boiling. The slump, from 50 to 220 mm, included 21 mixtures (84%) in the target range of 160–220 mm, while approximately 0.9 to 3.0 MPa, 0.63 to 1.05 GPa, and $$\:1.5\:\times\:\:{10}^{-9}$$ to $$\:1.3\:\times\:\:{10}^{-8}$$ m/s were the reported ranges for compressive strength, static chord modulus, and hydraulic conductivity, respectively. In the plotted results, only R19 and RK1 exceeded the specified compressive-strength threshold of 2.9 MPa; the latter was below the slump target. The hydraulic conductivities of the R- and QC-series were below $$\:1\:\times\:\:{10}^{-8}$$ m/s, while RA8-2 reached approximately $$\:1.3\:\times\:\:{10}^{-8}$$ m/s. Higher water–cement and bentonite–cement ratios in the tested mixtures were associated with lower stiffness, but the individual effects could not be isolated. These results support comparative mixture screening at 28 days, although the small-specimen tests and qualitative field observations do not establish wall-scale deformation compatibility.

Article.Title: Research on the vibration frequency range of vibratory soil cutting system and experimental verification
Article.Authors: Qiu Y.; Guo Z.; Chen X.; Zhang K.; Xu L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To address the wide variation in vibration frequencies used in existing vibratory soil cutting tools and the lack of a unified frequency selection criterion, this study investigated the natural vibration characteristics of soil in an indoor soil bin. Based on single-degree-of-freedom (SDOF) resonance theory, the empirical method, half-power bandwidth method, and amplitude magnification factor method were used to analyze the resonance bandwidth and vibration-energy proportion of the first-order soil vibration mode. On this basis, a frequency selection method for vibratory soil cutting tools was developed. The results show that the first-order natural vibration frequency f 0 of the soil is 29.492 Hz, with a damping ratio of 0.142. The resonance frequency bands determined by the empirical method and the amplitude amplification factor β = 2 are 0.75 f 0 ∼ 1.25 f 0 and 0.717 f 0 ∼ 1.207 f 0 , respectively. These bands strike a balance between vibration intensity and frequency adaptability, though their ranges are relatively limited. The effective vibration frequency band corresponding to an amplitude amplification factor β = 1 is the widest, ranging from 0 ∼ 1.414 f 0 , which can significantly enhance the equipment’s adaptability to variations in soil parameters, although the vibration response intensity is somewhat reduced. Balancing vibration intensity and engineering applicability, the recommended vibration frequency range for vibrating soil cutting equipment is proposed to be 0.75 f 0 ∼ 1.414 f 0 . To verify the validity of the proposed frequency range, 15 spatial spectrum bulldozing plate prototypes were designed and fabricated using five spatial spectrum excitation frequency levels and three amplitude levels, and soil bin cutting tests were conducted. The test results indicate that spatial spectrum bulldozing plates within the recommended frequency range generally exhibit good drag reduction and detachment performance, with the best drag reduction effect observed when the excitation frequency is close to the soil’s natural vibration frequency. Compared with traditional parabolic bulldozing plates, the relative drag reduction rate of the bulldozing plates reached 14.66% under the optimal parameter combination. The test results validated the rationality of the proposed vibration frequency selection range and selection principles. The research findings provide a theoretical basis for the design of vibration parameters for vibratory soil cutting implements and the optimization of the spatial spectrum structure of soil-engaging components.

Article.Title: A system-based abstraction hierarchy framework for seismic risk assessment of urban transportation networks
Article.Authors: Harandi V.; Ashtiany M.; Komendantova N.
Article.Abstract: Urban transportation networks are critical infrastructure for post-earthquake emergency response, making proactive seismic risk assessment essential. However, existing frameworks often examine transportation components, interdependencies, and cascading effects separately, making it difficult to integrate them into a unified seismic-risk framework for transportation systems. This study introduces the Urban Transportation System Abstraction Hierarchy (UTSAH), a directed graph–based framework integrating abstraction hierarchy theory with network analysis across five hierarchical levels. Within this framework, UTSAH identifies dominant risk drivers and critical transmission chokepoints within a unified hierarchical structure, enabling simultaneous diagnosis of where risk originates and how it propagates. By determining weighted interdependencies among 131 transportation-specific parameters spanning physical, functional, social, governance, economic, and environmental dimensions, UTSAH provides a unified multi-dimensional assessment of seismic risk propagation and cascading effects in urban transportation networks. Based on graph-based analysis, interventions are classified into three strategic objectives: (i) mitigating cascading effects by seismic retrofitting of vulnerable bridges and tunnels and strengthening construction quality control and periodic inspections; (ii) preserving system connectivity by maintaining emergency transportation network continuity and enhancing route redundancy; and (iii) strengthening vulnerable high-level goals by improving accessibility to critical service centers such as hospitals and fire stations. Overall, UTSAH provides a system-oriented decision-support tool for identifying and classifying candidate seismic risk mitigation strategies in urban transportation networks.

Article.Title: Silicon-mediated modulation of physiological performance, nutrient status and yield formation in winter wheat under field conditions
Article.Authors: Radkowski A.; Kępka W.; Kluwak K.; Kuc P.; Bujak H.; Prośniewski S.; Gwóźdź K.
Article.Abstract: Foliar silicon-containing formulations may modify wheat physiology, mineral nutrition, and canopy traits under field conditions. This study evaluated two commercial formulations in winter wheat cv. Chevignon: Silicon Complex 1 (SC1; 200 g SiO \(_2\cdot \) dm \(^{-3}\) , based on mono- and oligomers of stabilized orthosilicic acid) and Silicon Complex 2 (SC2; 260 g SiO \(_2\cdot \) dm \(^{-3}\) , 39 g N \(\cdot \) dm \(^{-3}\) and 156 g K \(_2\) O \(\cdot \) dm \(^{-3}\) ). Both were applied twice at 0.5 L \(\cdot \) ha \(^{-1}\) in a field experiment with three independent plots per treatment. Treatment effects were evaluated using one-way ANOVA on plot-level means with Bonferroni-adjusted pairwise comparisons. SC1 significantly increased \(F_\textrm{v}/F_\textrm{m}\) at both assessment dates and SPAD after the second application, and produced the highest tissue Si concentration and the largest flag-leaf area, length, and width. Both formulations significantly increased tissue Si relative to the Control at both sampling dates. Nitrogen concentration was numerically higher under SC1 but was not significantly affected. Grain yield averaged 65.0, 70.4, and 71.3 dt \(\cdot \) ha \(^{-1}\) in the Control, SC1, and SC2 treatments, respectively, but the treatment effect was not significant ( \(p=0.094\) ). The results indicate distinct physiological,mineral,and morphological responses to the tested formulations, whereas the numerical yield response requires confirmation in larger,multi-season field experiments.

Article.Title: Fuzzy logic based hybrid load balancing for solar–grid supply with tiered load shedding: a simulation study
Article.Authors: Wanzala J.; Byamukama M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hybrid installations that combine a solar inverter and battery with the utility grid are increasingly common in Uganda, yet they are typically managed by threshold-based automatic transfer switches (ATS) that ignore solar availability, grid quality, and load criticality. This paper presents the design, modelling, and simulation-based evaluation of a multi-input fuzzy logic based hybrid load balancing controller. The framework fuses four inputs (solar output, battery state of charge (SOC), grid status, and load demand) through a Mamdani-type fuzzy inference system to produce two coordinated outputs: a source-priority signal and a tiered load-shedding signal spanning three load classes (critical, flexible, and non-essential). The study is entirely simulation-based. The system was implemented in Python at one-minute resolution over a synthetic but representative 24-hour scenario featuring two grid outages, a brownout, and cloud-induced solar variability, and was benchmarked against a conventional threshold-based transfer switch, an ATS with critical-load priority, and a crisp rule-based tiered controller; it was further tested on seven stress cases and a 100-run Monte Carlo evaluation. In the headline scenario the fuzzy controller sustained 100% availability of critical load against 91.9% for the baseline, which suffered 67 minutes of complete blackout; raised solar utilisation from 47.1% to 100%; cut grid energy from 13.43 kWh to 7.95 kWh (40.8%); and reduced source-switching events from four to two. These gains came from deliberately curtailing all non-essential load and 4.6% of flexible load, so they are not a pure efficiency gain: total unserved energy rose from 1.84 to 3.18 kWh, although a criticality-weighted reliability index still favoured the fuzzy controller (96.4% versus 92.6%). Broader testing confirmed the solar-utilisation and grid-energy advantages over the threshold baseline, but showed that an ATS with simple critical-load priority protected critical load at least as well under stress, identifying rule-base tuning as the main need. The results support a simulation-based proof of concept. A real-time embedded demonstration, in which the controller and plant model ran on a Raspberry Pi 5 with an external touch display using emulated inputs, reproduced the simulated behaviour; testing with live sensors and relays and field validation remain future work.

Article.Title: Short-term effects of the peer teaching model on specialized content knowledge of pre-service physical education teachers
Article.Authors: Pan Y.; Wang W.; Zhang D.; Bu X.; Ling Q.
Article.Abstract: Pre-service physical education teachers often possess strong technical skills yet struggle to translate those skills into effective instruction. Grounded in the theoretical framework of specialized content knowledge (SCK), this study examined the short-term effects of the peer teaching model on teaching competence among pre-service physical education teachers. Using a quasi-experimental crossover design, 24 male physical education teacher education students completed two 60-minute basketball-focused instructional sessions, one employing a peer teaching model and one using conventional teacher-led instruction. Groups alternated between teacher and learner roles across the two sessions. Independent observation assessments of basketball shooting and chest passing were used to evaluate changes in common content knowledge (CCK; movement description and demonstration) and SCK (pedagogical key points). Two-factor repeated-measures ANOVAs were conducted for the eight outcome measures, with statistical significance set at α = 0.05. Significant group × time interactions were found for the pedagogy scores of both the chest pass and the overhead shot and for the chest passing total score, and students who assumed the teacher role showed greater SCK gains than those who acted as learners; no significant interaction effects were found for demonstration or description scores (CCK). These findings suggest that the peer teaching model has preliminary promise for promoting teaching competence in pre-service physical education teachers, particularly by providing structured opportunities for students to verbalize and demonstrate technical content to peers, and may inform the design of more authentic learning experiences within professional skill courses. However, the brief intervention duration and small sample warrant caution, and further longitudinal research is needed before broad implementation.

Article.Title: CFD-based analysis of load-independent power losses in high-speed cylindrical roller bearing considering internal geometry effects
Article.Authors: Moon D.; Kim B.; Kim J.; Lee M.; Park Y.
Article.Abstract: Predicting load-independent power losses in cylindrical roller bearings (CRBs) under high-speed operating conditions is essential for enhancing system efficiency. However, traditional empirical models often fail to account for the influence of internal geometry of bearings. This study investigates the effects of rotational speed and variations in internal geometry on load-independent power losses in bearings using computational fluid dynamics (CFD). A single phase model using an equivalent-fluid approach and the moving reference frame (MRF) method was applied to investigate internal flows of bearings. The results showed that load-independent power losses increase non-linearly with speed, from 0.030 kW at 10,000 rpm to 0.709 kW at 30,000 rpm. Comparative analysis showed that while CFD results were consistent with the ISO/TR 14179–1 trends, the results diverged significantly from the SKF model at high speed. Furthermore, internal geometry variations significantly affected load-independent power losses. The N-type bearing exhibited the highest losses (40.4% higher than the NU type) due to rib-induced shear stress concentration, whereas cage #3 minimized losses (10.9% lower than cage #2) by reducing the pressure acting on the cage bridges. This method can be utilized for predicting load-independent power losses, providing insights for optimizing high-speed CRB designs.

Article.Title: Predictive MRI signatures of alcohol-related risk diverge from group-level structural differences in firefighters
Article.Authors: Kim D.; Jang M.; Yoon S.; Lee H.
Article.Abstract: Group-level structural differences may not identify features most relevant to individual prediction. The primary stratified 70/30 split was fixed at seed 42 before held-out performance was examined. In this prespecified split, multimodal CatBoost achieved an AUC of 0.743 (95% CI 0.666–0.819), higher than the clinical-only and radiomics-only representative models. Across 10 training-stage runs on the same held-out test set, its mean AUC was 0.681 (SD 0.054; range 0.555–0.743), and it ranked highest in 6 of 10 runs; 0.743 was the maximum. Cortical features showed larger group differences, whereas SHAP-derived importance highlighted distributed subcortical features in the primary model; thalamic, ventral diencephalic, and ventricular features were among stable repeated-run contributors. Structural effect sizes and SHAP importance showed weak feature-level correspondence ( r = 0.22, p = 0.044) and no detectable region-level correspondence ( r = 0.03, p = 0.844). Within the selected radiomics set, these findings support evaluating group-level association and model-dependent predictive contribution as complementary properties of candidate imaging biomarkers.

Article.Title: Pexidartinib modulates pro-inflammatory cytokines in a co-culture model of stromal-immune cell crosstalk in tenosynovial giant cell tumor
Article.Authors: Zavoriti A.; Miossec P.
Article.Abstract: Tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT) is driven by CSF1 translocation, leading to chronic inflammation within the joint microenvironment dominated by CSF1R-expressing macrophages. Although pexidartinib successfully achieves tumor-volume reduction, its role in modulating the inflammatory component and stromal-immune cell crosstalk remains poorly characterized. We utilized a model where TGCT synoviocytes were stimulated with TNF + IL-17 or co-cultured with activated peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). Cultures were treated with varying pexidartinib doses (0–50 µM). Cytokine profiles were analyzed via ELISA, and PBMC aggregate formation was qualitatively assessed by light microscopy. In isolated synoviocytes, pexidartinib showed minimal cytotoxicity in the localized subtype, whereas higher doses selectively reduced the viability of diffuse TGCT synoviocytes. The treatment significantly suppressed IL-6 and IL-8 secretion across both subtypes. In co-cultures, IFNγ was the most sensitive cytokine to pexidartinib, showing significant reduction starting at 10 µM, whereas higher doses (25–50 µM) were required to suppress IL-6, IL-17, and IL-1β release. Conversely, TNF levels increased significantly at 25 µM and failed to decline at 50 µM. Additionally, microscopic examination revealed a qualitative reduction in PBMC aggregation at higher pexidartinib doses, though formal image quantification and underlying mechanisms remain to be established. Pexidartinib modulates the TGCT secretory profile and requires high concentrations to effectively inhibit synovial-immune crosstalk. The unexpected elevation in TNF raises the hypothesis that pexidartinib may trigger immune reprogramming with possible consequences for long-term joint integrity.

Article.Title: Morphometric analysis of the root canal system in three-rooted mandibular first molars: a micro-CT study in a Malaysian subpopulation
Article.Authors: Hussain S.; Mohd Noor N.; Ibrahim N.; Hasnan H.; Ahmed H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Three-rooted mandibular molars show wide variations in the root and canal anatomy. This study aimed to investigate the root canal configuration, the prevalence and location of accessory canals in three-rooted mandibular first molars in the Malaysian subpopulation using micro-computed tomography (micro-CT). A total of 70 extracted three-rooted mandibular first molars were scanned using micro-CT. The segmentation and 3D reconstruction of the acquired images were done using MIMICS software. Vertucci et al. (1974) and Ahmed et al. (2017) systems were used to classify the root canal configuration. The location and type of accessory canals were classified using complementary system introduced by Ahmed et al. (2018). Chi-square test was used for data analysis ( p = 0.05). Results showed that Vertucci Type I was the most commonly recorded configuration in mesial (12.9%), distal (92.9%) and distolingual (100%) roots, while 50% of the reported configurations in mesial root were non-classifiable by Vertucci system. According to Ahmed et al. coding system, the most recorded code for the mesial, distal and distolingual roots was M 1 , D 1 , and DL 1 , respectively. The most predominantly identified code for the tooth was 3 MFM M 1 D 1 DL 1 (11.4%), followed by the 3 MFM M 1–2 D 1 DL 1 (7.1%). The Ahmed et al. coding system was able to classify all canals in the mesial root. The chi-square test revealed a significant association between root type and root canal configuration ( p < 0.001) in both systems. The accessory canals were recorded in 92.9% of the samples, these were predominantly located in the apical third (86.9%), with the patent type being the most frequently encountered (66.3%). Three-rooted mandibular first molars in the studied Malaysian subpopulation demonstrate a wide range of variations in root canal configuration with high prevalence of accessory canals. In comparison to the Vertucci system, the coding system developed by Ahmed et al. provides a precise and practical classification of all canals, irrespective to their complexity.

Article.Title: A CLAHE–Gabor–vision transformer pipeline for palmprint image enhancement and deep feature extraction
Article.Authors: Kaliaperumal R.; Anandan S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Palmprint enhancement is a suitable technique for recognizing, a biometric modality, provides a dependable means of identifying individuals; however, poor-quality image capture, such as non-uniform illumination, low contrast, and ridge discontinuities, has made this technology difficult to implement in practice. Existing handcrafted descriptors do not adapt well to these capture variations, and while deep learning models learn highly discriminative features from large datasets, they remain sensitive to input image quality and generalize poorly on degraded palmprints. To address these challenges, this study proposes an integrated approach combining image enhancement with deep feature representation through Vision Transformers (ViTs). The pipeline first applies Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) to boost local contrast while limiting noise amplification, then applies multi-orientation Gabor filtering on the CLAHE output to enhance ridge and texture structures. The filtered outputs are fused using a weighted superposition method to produce an enhanced image that balances contrast fidelity with texture preservation. A Custom Vision Transformer (ViT) then extracts globally discriminative features from the enhanced palmprints, using multi-head self-attention to capture fine-grained texture detail and long-range pixel associations, evaluated on a dataset of 100 original grayscale palmprint images (512 × 512 pixels). The proposed technique achieved an average MSE of 440.24, PSNR of 22.01 dB, SSIM of 0.8481, and MS-SSIM of 0.8211, significantly outperforming five benchmark enhancement methods (Fuzzy Enhancement, Gamma Correction, Homomorphic Method, Multi-Scale Retinex with Color Restoration, and a Traditional Baseline Method), including a 78.6% reduction in average MSE and a 38.2% increase in average PSNR over the best-performing alternative.

Article.Title: Environmental chemicals cause changes in animal personality that can destabilize populations
Article.Authors: Tierney K.; Wang T.; Gao S.; Philibert D.; Steffler M.; Torwalt E.; Shahriari A.; El-Din M.; Lewis M.; Wang H.
Article.Abstract: Life is shaped by its chemical environment. An animal’s personality, for example, can be developmentally altered by foreign chemicals. We produced a data-based model to study how contaminant-mediated changes in personality affect predator and prey abundances. Increasing contaminant concentrations led to a greater proportion of bold vs. shy phenotypes in offspring, which shifted predator-prey populations from stable coexistence to periodic dynamics with large oscillations. The addition of a secondary stressor, which reflects a multi-stressor environment, led to a biphasic response in predator populations. A modest increase in boldness improved predator survival rates, while a more drastic increase, one consistent with the experimental data, led to a greater risk of extinction. This study indicates that subtle neurophysiological alterations from exposure to diverse and common environmental chemicals may have cascading effects that challenge ecosystem stability.

Article.Title: Experimental and life cycle assessment of reclaimed asphalt pavement modified with nano Fe2O3 and waste cooking oil admixtures
Article.Authors: Abdelsalam M.; Li J.; Khater A.; Ghazy M.; Eisa M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Thermal cracking, rutting, and moisture damage are common pavement distresses caused by heavy traffic growth, construction deficiencies, and environmental effects, reducing service life and performance. Asphalt additives can improve pavement behavior; however, a single modifier rarely enhances all properties simultaneously. This study investigates a composite modification approach using dual additives in reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP). In the current study, nine mixtures were prepared and evaluated to determine the optimum dosages of Nano Fe 2 O 3 and waste cooking oil (WCO). Subsequently, five mixtures were evaluated: the control mixture, RAP mixture, RAP modified with WCO, RAP modified with nano-Fe 2 O 3 , and RAP modified with a composite of WCO and nano-Fe 2 O 3 . Marshall immersion, low-temperature splitting, and wheel tracking tests were conducted to assess moisture resistance, low temperature stability, and rutting performance. Environmental performance was evaluated using life cycle assessment (LCA) with SimaPro software. The results showed that the optimum contents were 4% nano-Fe 2 O 3 and 9% WCO based on the Marshall properties. Compared with the control mixture, the composite-modified mixture (M8) achieved a 38.60% reduction in rutting depth and a 30.21% increase in indirect tensile strength, while its Marshall residual stability ratio increased by 8.24%. From the LCA perspective, the 20% RAP mixture (M1) exhibited the best overall environmental performance among the modified mixtures, whereas the nano-Fe 2 O 3 -modified mixture (M4) achieved the lowest weighted environmental impact.

Article.Title: Nutritional profiling and nutrient quality scoring of microgreens cultivated in India
Article.Authors: Punasiya M.; Singh H.; Panda A.; Pradhan J.; Agnihotri R.
Article.Abstract: Micronutrient deficiency remains a major public health challenge in India, where dietary diversity is often limited among low-income populations. Microgreens, young edible seedlings harvested at the two-true-leaf stage (7–21 days post-germination), have recently gained traction as potentially nutrient-dense functional foods. However, systematic compositional data for commercial varieties of Microgreens grown in India remain scarce. In this study, sixteen commonly consumed vegetable species from five botanical families (Brassicaceae, Amaranthaceae, Asteraceae, Apiaceae, and Compositae) were cultivated under controlled polyhouse conditions in Bihar, India. They were evaluated for vitamin C, crude fiber, protein, total phenolic content (TPC), DPPH (2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl) radical scavenging activity, FRAP (ferric reducing antioxidant power) assay, and mineral content (calcium, iron, zinc, and potassium), as well as oxalate, an antinutritional factor. All analyses were conducted in three independent replicates. Data were expressed as mg 100 g −1 fresh weight (FW) for vitamin C, protein, oxalate, and TPC, and mg 100 g −1 dry weight (DW) for minerals. The data were statistically analyzed using a Completely Randomized Design with three replicates. Radish, kale, broccoli, and fenugreek were the richest sources of vitamin C (85.77–97.88 mg 100 g −1 FW), while celery, parsley, palak, and spinach were the richest sources of calcium (320.14-410.15 mg 100 g −1 DW). The crude fiber content of broccoli microgreen (11.95 g 100 g −1 DW) and cabbage microgreen (11.48 g 100 g −1 DW) was good. Low oxalate content across all microgreen species (15.89–55.14 mg 100 g −1 FW) suggests safe consumption levels. The composite Nutrient Quality Score (NQS) and Antioxidant Index (AI) were calculated using Min-Max normalized values to enable cross-species comparison. Palak, broccoli, fenugreek, and kale ranked highest in NQS, driven primarily by their vitamin C, crude fiber, and iron content. These findings provide a systematic nutritional reference for microgreens grown in India and illustrate how NQS can be applied to comparative dietary assessment.

Article.Title: Dynamic modeling, simulation, and analysis of solar/wind-based hybrid renewable energy system for rural residential building: a case study
Article.Authors: Alao O.; Dagbasi M.; Abid M.; Shefik A.; Adebayo V.; Adun H.
Article.Abstract: In this paper, a hybrid renewable energy system (HRES) is designed and analyzed for a rural residential building in northern Nigeria to meet electricity demand, cooling load and hot water requirement of the building. Photovoltaic/thermal (PVT) collectors are coupled with a wind turbine alongside other primary components. The hybrid system was analyzed in the dynamic TRNSYS environment to supply an average annual electrical load of 2,056.78 kWh, annual cooling load of 4,343.06 kWh and domestic hot water demand. Simulation results indicate that the HRES provides a technically feasible and economically viable solution. Result shows delivery of 5,162.62 kWh of useful thermal energy by the thermal subsystem over the year, cooling production of 4,960.46 kWh, and electrical production of 2,029.88 kWh, with the baseline system meeting 98.7% of the electrical demand, and the optimal configuration achieving a surplus. The system economic analysis shows Net Profit Value (NPV) of 2,190.24 USD, a Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) of 0.155 USD/kWh and payback period of 8.3 years, indicating a feasible HRES for residential homes in rural northern Nigeria. The optimized system achieved an LCOE of 0.1488 USD/kWh, indicating a 3.87% reduction, while also reducing CAPEX by 16.67% and carbon emissions. Uncertainty analysis performed indicates a mean Loss of Power Supply Probability of 0.0336. These findings highlight the potential of tailored HRES solutions for energy poverty reduction and improved living standards, as well as support for broader clean energy transition in Nigeria, with 3,518.14 barrels of diesel fuel being avoided throughout the system’s lifetime.

Article.Title: Development of a transparent reporting tool for AI-based diagnostic prediction models of disease and syndrome in Chinese medicine (TRAPODS-CM): a Delphi study
Article.Authors: Li J.; Seetoh W.; Lim J.; Xiao X.; Lu C.; Yang K.; Yeo S.; Sun B.; Jiao W.; Liu J.; Xu Z.; Lu J.; Zhong L.
Article.Abstract: In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) prediction models have gained traction in Chinese medicine (CM) diagnostics. However, existing reporting guidelines, largely based on modern medicine diagnostic frameworks, have limited applicability to CM due to fundamental differences in diagnostic approaches. This highlights the need for a tailored reporting standard. This study develops a transparent reporting guideline for CM diagnostic AI models using the Delphi consensus method. An initial checklist was created by a steering committee and core working group, drawing on a prior systematic review, existing guidelines, and the unique characteristics of CM diagnostics. A multidisciplinary panel of 31 experts evaluated each domain and item on a 1–5 Likert scale across multiple Delphi rounds. In the first round, domain consensus was decent (Kendall’s W = 0.498), but item consensus was low (W = 0.271), prompting substantial revisions, including 5 modifications and 1 addition for domains, and 20 modifications, 13 deletions, and 4 additions for items. In the second round, domain consensus remained strong (W = 0.487), while item consensus improved significantly (W = 0.349), indicating convergence on the checklist. A final consensus meeting led to the refinement and finalization of the Transparent Reporting Tool for AI-Based Diagnostic Prediction Models of Disease and Syndrome in Chinese Medicine (TRAPODS-CM). This guideline aims to provide a reporting framework for CM diagnostic AI prediction models where the unique diagnostic principles of CM are specifically addressed, ultimately fostering more transparent, reliable and reproducible AI-driven clinical applications in this field.

Article.Title: Integrated network pharmacology, in vivo experiment, computational biology, and metabolomics to explore the mechanism of astragaloside IV against spinal cord injury
Article.Authors: Sun Z.; Hu B.; Wang L.; Pang X.; Shen X.
Article.Abstract: Spinal cord injury has become a global public health challenge. Astragaloside IV has been shown to have neuroprotective effects. However, the underlying mechanism of astragaloside IV against spinal cord injury remains poorly understood. An integrated approach combining network pharmacology, in vivo experimental validation, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and metabolomics was used to investigate the underlying mechanism of astragaloside IV against spinal cord injury. Network pharmacology results indicated that IL6, IL1B, AKT1, TNF, and PTGS2 might be the key targets, while the TNF signaling pathway, IL17 signaling pathway, and C-type lectin receptor signaling pathway might be the critical signaling pathways involved in the mechanism of astragaloside IV against spinal cord injury. In vivo studies indicated that astragaloside IV significantly improved BBB scores and Rivlin inclined plane test performance in spinal cord injury mouse models, while reducing TNF-α, IL1B, IL6, and PTGS2 levels and increasing AKT1 expression. Molecular docking results revealed that astragaloside IV exhibits strong binding affinity with IL1B, IL6, PTGS2, and AKT1. Molecular dynamics simulation further indicated that astragaloside IV could form stable complexes with AKT1 with a binding free energy of -27.17±3.21 kcal/mol. Metabolomic analysis further elucidated that the mechanism of astragaloside IV against spinal cord injury might involve up-regulating energy metabolism, nucleotide metabolism, amino acid metabolism, etc., and down-regulating lipid metabolism including linoleic acid metabolism, fatty acid biosynthesis, and α-linolenic acid metabolism. Astragaloside IV can improve spinal cord injury through multiple targets, multiple signaling pathways, and multiple metabolic pathways, providing a new perspective on the molecular and metabolic mechanism network of spinal cord injury and strong experimental evidence for the use of astragaloside IV in treating spinal cord injury.

Article.Title: Estimation of priority PAHs during potato frying and associated health risks
Article.Authors: Qasemi M.; Zarei A.; Alami A.; Shams M.; Afsharnia M.
Article.Abstract: Frying and cooking are important sources of indoor air pollution which contribute significantly to the release of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in the environment. This experimental study investigated 16 US EPA listed priority PAHs released from potato frying using two oils. In order to quantify the potential health threats due to inhalation exposure from the PAHs, Hazard quotients (HQ) and lifetime cancer risk (LTCR) were also calculated for the exposed groups. Levels of the PAHs ranged from 0.032 to 2.464 (mean 0.642) and 0.032 to 1.1 (mean 0.371) μg/m 3 , during sunflower and frying oil use, respectively. Total PAHs were in the range of 3.377–14.126 (8.345) and 2.807–8.145 (5.387) μg/m 3 , respectively during sunflower and frying oil use. Overall, sunflower oil generated higher levels of PAHs. Levels of LMW, MMW, HMW and carcinogenic PAHs increased with temperature increase. BaPeq levels ranged from 0.00003 to 2.464 (0.503) and 0.00003 to 1.10 (0.301) μg/m 3 . Some of the samples had HQ > 1, showing non-cancer risk. When frying potato with sunflower oil, the LTCRs associated with PAHs ranged from 5.8E−05 to 4.5E−04 (mean 2.3E−04), 1.2E−05 to 9.2E−05 (mean 4.7E−05) and 3.2E−06 to 2.5E−05 (mean 1.3E−05) for cooks, adults and children, respectively. For potato frying using frying oil, the LTCRs were estimated to be varied from 1.8E−05 to 3.2E−04 (mean 1.4E−04), 3.8E−06 to 6.6E−05 (mean 2.9E−05) and 1.02E−06 to 1.79E−05 (mean 8.02E−06) for cooks, adults and children, respectively. Overall, cooks could develop cancer over a lifetime due to inhalation of PAHs. Therefore, the formation of PAHs during potato frying could be reduced by choosing appropriate cooking methods.

Article.Title: A descriptive three-domain limitation count is associated with incident cardiovascular disease across three longitudinal ageing cohorts
Article.Authors: Shou R.; Li L.; Zhu S.
Article.Abstract: Ageing populations experience functional and psychological limitations, but their accumulated cardiovascular relevance across settings is uncertain. We analysed 31,535 adults aged ≥ 50 years without baseline cardiovascular disease in three cohorts. A descriptive three-domain analytic count (0–3) comprised daily-function, walking-distance mobility and elevated depressive-symptom limitations. Cohort-specific Cox models used a common adjustment set across cohorts; estimates were pooled using random effects. During follow-up, 8,950 participants developed cardiovascular disease. Each additional domain was associated with incident cardiovascular disease; the pooled hazard ratio was 1.214 (95% confidence interval 1.109–1.330; 95% prediction interval 1.043–1.414). Compared with no domains, pooled hazard ratios were 1.250 for one domain and 1.517 for ≥ 2 domains. After expanded adjustment for available socioeconomic, behavioural and multimorbidity-related factors, the pooled hazard ratio attenuated to 1.163 (95% confidence interval 1.064–1.271). Findings were similar in sensitivity analyses using common comparable ADL/IADL items and leave-one-cohort-out analyses. Competing-risk estimates differed in HRS, and findings at ≥ 75 years were heterogeneous. The primary estimate is not independent of broader measured factors; the descriptive count is not intended for causal inference, clinical prediction or decision-making.

Article.Title: Multi-scenario-based optimization with CVaR risk control for renewable energy participation in electricity spot markets
Article.Authors: Yan Z.; Huang F.; Liu J.; Wang W.; Liang L.; You Z.
Article.Abstract: Electricity spot-market participation by renewable producers is exposed to coupled uncertainty in generation, demand, and prices. This study develops a day-ahead bidding framework that combines multi-scenario stochastic optimization with Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) control of downside revenue shortfall. A large pool of temporally correlated trajectories is reduced by fast-forward selection, and the resulting fixed bids are evaluated on an independently generated sample. A deterministic forecast bid and a risk-neutral stochastic model provide explicit benchmarks. The out-of-sample evaluation shows that stochastic bidding reduces deviation penalties relative to the deterministic baseline, while the CVaR model accepts a small expected-revenue concession relative to the risk-neutral solution in exchange for lower tail shortfall and less volatile profit. These findings support the internal revenue-risk logic of the proposed method under the constructed data-generating process; validation with measured market data remains necessary before practical deployment.

Article.Title: Association of the VExUS score with right atrial pressure and organ dysfunction in acute heart failure and cardiogenic shock
Article.Authors: Filomia S.; Del Buono M.; Pedicino D.; Saponara G.; d’Aiello A.; Morini S.; Brecciaroli M.; Ricci M.; Simonini C.; Pinnacchio G.; Genuardi L.; Montone R.; Sanna T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Background Venous congestion is a major determinant of organ dysfunction in acute heart failure (AHF) and cardiogenic shock (CS). The Venous Excess Ultrasound Score (VExUS) provides a noninvasive assessment of systemic venous congestion, but its physiological correlates in the cardiac intensive care unit (CICU) remain incompletely characterized. Methods In this prospective single-center study, 94 patients with AHF or CS underwent simultaneous VExUS assessment and invasive right atrial pressure (RAP) measurement within 24 hours of CICU admission. VExUS (graded 0–3; Low 0–1 vs High 2–3) was evaluated for correlation with RAP and associations with hemodynamic, echocardiographic and organ dysfunction indices. Prespecified RAP–VExUS phenotypes (RAP ≤ 10 vs > 10 mmHg; Low vs High VExUS) were used to assess differences in hepato–renal biochemical markers, with adjustment for positive pressure ventilation and SCAI stage. In-hospital mortality was explored using univariate logistic regression. Results High VExUS was present in 29 patients (31%). VExUS correlated with RAP (ρ = 0.67), inversely with the MAP–RAP gradient, and was associated with impaired right ventricular function and higher hepato–renal dysfunction biomarkers, but not with lactate or urine output. RAP–VExUS discordance occurred in 30.9% of patients. Among patients with elevated RAP (> 10 mmHg), those with High VExUS showed greater hepato–renal biochemical dysfunction than those with Low VExUS (p < 0.01). The incremental contribution of VExUS beyond RAP was mainly evident for bilirubin. In-hospital mortality was numerically higher in High versus Low VExUS patients, without reaching statistical significance (24% vs 15%, p = NS). Conclusions In patients with acute heart failure or cardiogenic shock, VExUS was associated with invasively measured RAP and hepato-renal biochemical dysfunction, suggesting a complementary role in congestion phenotyping alongside invasive hemodynamic assessment.

Article.Title: Improved human development index may mitigate drought risk under the changing climate and socio-economic conditions
Article.Authors: Indraja G.; Maity R.
Article.Abstract: Drought is a recurring hydroclimatic hazard that significantly affects water resources, ecosystems and economic activities. Its overall risk is influenced not only by climate change but also by evolving population exposure and socio-economic vulnerability. This study develops an integrated framework to construct the Relative Drought Risk Index (RDRI) by integrating hazard with time-varying vulnerability and exposure. With the developed framework, the relative contributions of climate change and socio-economic conditions to drought risk are investigated. Drought hazard is quantified through the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI). Vulnerability is quantified using the Human Development Index (HDI), with values subtracted from 1, so that higher values correspond to higher vulnerability. Exposure is represented by population density of a grid. Both of these indices are time-varying and contrast this study with previous studies that are mostly based on a time-invariant approach. Considering the entire Indian mainland that spans across a wide range of climatic and socio-economic conditions, the developed framework is applied for the period 1991 to 2015. It is found that drought risk is higher in the Indo-Gangetic plain, eastern and north-eastern India compared to other parts of the Indian mainland. The findings reveal the combined role of frequent droughts, dense population, and low HDI in identifying high-risk regions compared to others. Temporal analysis reveals a clear spatial shift in drought risk between 1991 and 2003 and 2004–2015, with an overall reduction across 80% of regions, but intensified risk in eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Madhya Pradesh in the later period. Notably, southern India shows a decline in risk, despite experiencing increased drought frequency, primarily due to improvements in socio-economic conditions. The analysis to investigate the relative contributions of climate and socio-economic conditions to drought risk change reveals that, in areas with rising drought risk, climate change and socio-economic conditions contribute approximately 73% and 27%, respectively. On the other hand, in regions where risk has decreased, the contributions are approximately 34% and 66%, indicating a higher contribution from socio-economic conditions. These findings indicate that socio-economic development can substantially reduce drought risk, underscoring the need for region-specific, hotspot-targeted development strategies to manage drought risk.

Article.Authors: Yu J.; Song W.; Kang M.; Jeon H.; Jeong B.; Seo S.; Jeon S.; Sung H.
Article.Abstract: Non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) requires long-term surveillance, but cystoscopy is invasive and urine cytology has limited sensitivity. We evaluated the diagnostic performance of a urinary dual-site proenkephalin methylation (ds-me PENK ) test (EarlyTect Bladder Cancer Detection Plus) for detecting high-grade or invasive recurrence during NMIBC surveillance. This prospective longitudinal study included 82 patients with histopathologically confirmed NMIBC who underwent transurethral resection followed by cystoscopic surveillance. Serial urine samples were analysed using ds-me PENK testing, the nuclear matrix protein 22 (NMP22) assay, and urine cytology. The primary endpoint was diagnostic accuracy for histopathologically confirmed high-grade or invasive recurrence. During a median follow-up of 12.3 months, 22 patients experienced recurrence. The ds-me PENK test detected 9 of 11 high-grade/invasive recurrences (sensitivity, 81.8%; 95% CI, 48.2–97.7%) and 6 of 11 Ta low-grade recurrences (54.5%). Urinary methylation levels declined after resection and remained low through follow-up in recurrence-free patients, whereas levels remained persistently elevated in those who later recurred. Its negative predictive value (NPV) for high-grade/invasive recurrence was 96.4% (95% CI, 87.5–99.6%). Corresponding sensitivities were 45.5% and 30.0%, and NPVs were 91.5% and 90.9%, for NMP22 and urine cytology, respectively. The ds-me PENK test detected five of the six observed stage/grade progression events. Urinary ds-me PENK testing showed high NPV for high-grade/invasive recurrence during NMIBC surveillance. It may complement cystoscopy as a molecular rule-out adjunct, but larger multicentre studies are required before the test can be used to modify cystoscopic surveillance schedules.

Article.Title: Electroencephalographic gamma correlates with pain intensity attenuation in a prospective longitudinal study using an AI-powered digital device for pain self-management
Article.Authors: Bie B.; Klement M.; Ghosn S.; Lattouf E.; Schut S.; Xu J.; Cheng J.; Ezell J.; Borrebaeck C.; Saab C.
Article.Abstract: Chronic low back or neck pain is one of the most common neurological disorders in the US. Electroencephalogram (EEG) is a leading noninvasive approach to identify biomarkers for chronic pain, but its validation in clinical settings remains limited by methodological challenges, including variable feature selections, subjective removal of EEG artifacts, and reliance on population-level analyses. In this single center, prospective, longitudinal study, we investigated the relationships among EEG features, patient-reported clinical outcomes via validated Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMS) questionnaires, and daily self-management of pain-associated physical activity via a newly developed AI-powered mobile application Paindrainer PDCC (Paindrainer AB, Lund, Sweden) in patients with chronic pain undergoing standard care. In total, twenty patients with chronic lower back or neck pain were enrolled and evaluated during 3 visits over a 12-week period. Results show significant improvements in pain score, physical function, and pain interference scores over time, whereas mean EEG power spectral density across all electrodes and frequency bands was statistically insignificant at the group level between the three visits. However, logistic regression analysis revealed significant nominal inverse correlations between pain score reduction and gamma power changes (averaged globally and localized to the right temporal and left frontal regions), though these failed to retain significance after multiple comparison correction. Logistic regression showed a statistically significant correlation between increased EEG gamma oscillations (1 Hz bins) and decreased pain intensity in the right temporal EEG electrodes. These exploratory analyses suggest that improvements in self-reported pain outcomes in chronic pain patients undergoing standard treatments and complemented with digital-based behavioral interventions correlate negatively with measurable changes in EEG spectral features, which need further validation in future studies with larger cohorts.

Article.Title: Global context integration for pharmacologically robust preclinical sleep stage classification
Article.Authors: Brejtr V.; Aleksić K.; Šíchová K.; Vejmola Č.; Páleníček T.; Lhotská L.
Article.Abstract: Sleep stage classification from electrophysiological signals is essential for studying brain function in preclinical neuroscience, yet models often fail to generalize across subjects and experimental conditions, particularly under pharmacological interventions that alter neural and muscular activity. We propose a robustness-oriented deep learning framework that integrates multi-branch feature extraction, global contextual representation, sequence modeling, and training strategies designed to reduce sensitivity to subject- and treatment-specific variability. The approach is evaluated on a large rodent dataset comprising over one million annotated EEG and EMG segments collected from multiple animals across several pharmacological conditions. It achieves strong classification performance, substantially outperforming both classical methods and standard deep learning baselines. Notably, the model maintains stable performance across treatments, showing minimal degradation when trained on limited conditions, and remains effective even with relatively small amounts of annotated data. These findings demonstrate that accurate and robust sleep stage classification is achievable despite pronounced experimental variability. The proposed framework reduces reliance on extensive annotation and improves the reliability of automated sleep analysis, supporting more scalable and reproducible preclinical research.
