Article.Title: Anti-HER2 immunotoxin scFv-PE35KDEL internalizes via receptor-mediated endocytosis and induces apoptosis in ovarian cancer cells
Article.Authors: Saeidi M.; Gheisari Z.; Shafiee F.; Chou C.; Akbari V.
Article.Abstract: Ovarian cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide, highlighting the need for more effective targeted therapies. Immunotoxins have emerged as promising therapeutic agents for recurrent and metastatic ovarian cancer. In this study, we evaluated the binding, cellular uptake, cytotoxicity, and pro-apoptotic activity of an anti-HER2 immunotoxin, anti-HER2-scFv-PE35KDEL, composed of an anti-HER2 single-chain variable fragment (scFv) derived from pertuzumab fused to a modified 35-kDa fragment of Pseudomonas exotoxin A containing a KDEL sequence. The binding activity and cellular uptake of anti-HER2-scFv-PE35KDEL were evaluated in two ovarian cancer cell lines, SK-OV-3 and OVCAR-3, using flow cytometry, fluorometric analysis, and fluorescence microscopy. Cytotoxicity was assessed using MTT assay, while apoptosis induction was analyzed by Annexin V/PI staining and Western blot analysis of apoptosis-related proteins. The immunotoxin demonstrated significantly greater binding and cellular uptake in HER2-overexpressing SK-OV-3 cells compared with HER2-low OVCAR-3 cells, suggesting receptor-mediated internalization. Chlorpromazine treatment reduced cellular uptake, indicating the possible involvement of clathrin-mediated endocytosis. MTT analysis revealed concentration-dependent cytotoxicity against SK-OV-3 cells with an IC50 value of 10.90 nM, whereas OVCAR-3 cells exhibited substantially lower sensitivity with an IC50 value of 76.79 nM. Furthermore, treatment with anti-HER2-scFv-PE35KDEL induced apoptosis in SK-OV-3 cells in a concentration-dependent manner and increased the Bax/Bcl-2 ratio. These findings suggest that anti-HER2-scFv-PE35KDEL may exert preferential cytotoxic and pro-apoptotic effects against HER2-overexpressing ovarian cancer cells and support further preclinical investigation of this immunotoxin as a potential targeted therapeutic agent.

Article.Title: Integrating single-cell RNA sequencing and transcriptome analysis to explore uric acid–related biomarkers and regulatory mechanisms in preeclampsia
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Hou L.; Xie C.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is a pregnancy-specific syndrome that occurs after 20 weeks of gestation. Abnormal uric acid metabolism may play a pivotal role in the onset and progression of PE. This research aimed to extensively analyze and pinpoint biomarkers related to uric acid in PE and elucidate their potential molecular mechanisms. Data related to PE and uric acid were obtained from the public databases. Biomarkers were selected and validated through differential expression analysis, machine learning algorithms, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, and expression level validation. Moreover, a nomogram was applied to construct a uric acid-related predictive model for PE. Enrichment analysis, immune infiltration analysis, molecular regulatory network, drug prediction, and molecular docking were performed to further verify the regulatory roles of biomarkers. Furthermore, the expression patterns of biomarkers in core cells were investigated using dataset GSE173193. Finally, validation of biomarkers expression was performed by western- blotting and qRT-PCR. Overall, four biomarkers (ENG, JAK1, LEP, and SLC6A8) were identified as significantly associated with uric acid in PE. A predictive nomogram based on these biomarkers showed promising apparent diagnostic performance in the GSE35574 cohort. The biomarkers were significantly enriched in the “housekeeping genes”, “mitochondria”, and “signaling by Robo receptors”. Notably, JAK1 was positively correlated with gamma delta T cells, while SLC6A8 was negatively correlated with gamma delta T cells. Subsequently, 348 microRNAs (miRNAs) (like hsa-miR-4486) and 25 transcription factors (TFs) (like CTCF, TBP, and MAFK) were associated with the biomarkers. Molecular docking predicted favorable interactions for the reported biomarker-compound pairs. Moreover, ENG, JAK1, and SLC6A8 exhibited relatively high expression in extravillous trophoblasts (EVT). Finally, the results of qRT-PCR and Western blot showed that the mRNA and protein expressions of ENG, SLC6A8, and LEP in placental tissues from the PE group were higher than those in the control group, while the mRNA and protein expressions of JAK1 were lower in the placental tissues of the PE group compared to the control group, which is consistent with the expression patterns observed in the RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) datasets. Four uric acid-related biomarkers (ENG, JAK1, LEP, and SLC6A8) were identified in PE, providing preliminary molecular clues and a theoretical reference for further mechanistic exploration and the screening of potential therapeutic targets of PE.

Article.Title: The photosynthetic efficiency and heavy metals levels in Silybum marianum L. treated with azoxystrobin
Article.Authors: Adamczyk-Szabela D.; Krakowiak D.; Wolf W.
Article.Abstract: Silybum marianum L. (milk thistle) is valued worldwide for its medicinal properties. Currently, there is growing interest in the organic cultivation of this herb under controlled conditions. Unfortunately, its plantations are often exposed to fungal diseases, which pose a significant threat. The aim of the present study was to determine the effect of the fungicide azoxystrobin on photosynthesis and the uptake of manganese, copper, cadmium, lead, iron, and zinc by milk thistle. Moreover, using the Folin-Ciocalteu method, we determined changes in the level of phenolic compounds, which may reflect the potential response of plants to stressors. The concentrations of metals either in soil or plant samples were determined using ICP-OES technique. In general, azoxystrobin stimulated photosynthesis as indicated by the increase of gas exchange parameters which returned to initial values after 42 days of cultivation. Notable, the decrease of chlorophyl index was observed 28 days after the fungicide application. Nevertheless, the total phenolic content in milk thistle was gradually increasing over the time of cultivation. The highest influence of azoxystrobin was observed for lead and zinc which uptake by roots was significantly reduced after the fungicide application.

Article.Title: Documented preoperative statin exposure and short-term mortality after aortic valve replacement: a multicohort observational study
Article.Authors: Kang M.; Sohn S.; Choi J.; Hwang H.; Kim K.; Kang Y.
Article.Abstract: Whether documented preoperative statin exposure is associated with short-term mortality after aortic valve replacement (AVR) is uncertain. This retrospective multicohort study included 5,291 AVR records from SNUH, MIMIC-IV, and eICU. The primary analysis compared no documented versus any documented statin exposure for recorded 30-day mortality in SNUH and MIMIC-IV using overlap weighting and fixed-effect pooling. Exposure-window, recorded 365-day, IPTW, and SNUH available-follow-up analyses were sensitivity analyses; eICU and agent-specific analyses were exploratory. Overlap-weighted 30-day risks with versus without documented exposure were 1.29% versus 2.55% in SNUH and 1.18% versus 2.36% in MIMIC-IV; the pooled HR was 2.01 (95% CI, 0.98 to 4.11; P = 0.056). A 1-day MIMIC-IV window reclassified seven records and, pooled with the SNUH 24-h definition, yielded an HR of 2.29 (95% CI, 1.14 to 4.61; P = 0.020) at 30 days; the recorded 365-day HR was 1.76 (95% CI, 1.00 to 3.09; P = 0.050). Thirty-day IPTW estimates and the SNUH available-follow-up estimate were significant but remained sensitivity analyses. Absence of documented exposure showed consistently higher adjusted mortality estimates, but the primary analysis was inconclusive. Residual confounding, exposure misclassification, and incomplete death ascertainment limit causal interpretation.

Article.Title: Psychological distress is associated with early ultrasound-detected median nerve changes in asymptomatic young adults
Article.Authors: Marini A.; Iliou K.; Stergiou A.; Kitsouli N.; Chatzoglou T.; Kitsoulis P.; Varvarousis D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) is a common compressive neuropathy, caused by entrapment of the median nerve within the carpal tunnel. CTS has a vast range of symptoms, resulting in sensory and motor dysfunction of the hand. Whether psychosocial factors are associated with CTS remains obscure. The present study examined the relationship between median nerve ultrasonographic cross-sectional area (CSA) and stress and depression among asymptomatic young individuals. The study involved 169 healthy Greek medical students (67 men and 102 women). Age, gender, dominant hand, medical history, daily hours of computer use, and family background were recorded. Two validated psychiatric questionnaires estimating stress and anxiety were self-completed. Median nerve status was examined using ultrasonography. A CSA of < 10 mm² was considered normal and > 12 mm² pathological. Data were analyzed using Pearson linear correlation and t-test. Mean CSA of the median nerve was 0.082 cm (SD = 0.018). Total daily time of computer use was positively correlated with CSA ( p = 0.012). Mean Zung Scale Score for depression was 38.89 (± 8.76), while STAI-Y1 and STAI-Y2 for anxiety estimation were 37.28 (± 9.78) and 41.14 (± 11.21) respectively. CSA of the median nerve was positively associated with ZUNG ( p = 0.001), STAI-Y1 ( p < 0.001) and STAI-Y2 ( p < 0.001) scores. The daily hours of computer use, depression and anxiety are positively associated with median nerve CSA among healthy young adults. The correlation between anxiety, depression and CSA highlights the need for both biomechanical and psychiatric interventions in asymptomatic subjects with psychological distress.

Article.Title: Traits associated with novel foraging success in urban mesopredators
Article.Authors: Stanton L.; Caspi T.; Estien C.; Huber G.; Schell C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Urbanization is transforming ecosystems worldwide, creating novel environmental conditions that wildlife must adjust to. Because urban species differ markedly in ecological strategies, functional traits, and societal perceptions, they experience divergent pressures that shape their responses to the challenges associated with city living. A comparative framework can therefore reveal how both individual and species-level differences influence behaviors such as risk-taking and problem solving, even among related taxa in the same habitat. Here, we challenged free-ranging mesopredators with a novel foraging task and predicted a gradient of species-specific behavioral responses, hypothesizing that boldness, exploration, and effort would influence problem-solving success within and across species. We collected data from 110 locations across the East Bay of California for five mesopredator species: raccoons, opossums, striped skunks, coyotes, and domestic cats. Individuals from all species solved the task multiple times, but raccoons and coyotes emerged as the most successful despite divergent approaches. Across species, effort was the strongest predictor of success, whereas within species, exploratory individuals were most likely to solve. In contrast, boldness did not predict success. These results illustrate how trait differences within and among a taxonomic guild shape behavioral responses to novel challenges, offering insights on the strategies that facilitate urban persistence.

Article.Title: Automated optimization of solar energetic particle acceleration and transport parameters against five-spacecraft observations of the 9 October 2021 event
Article.Authors: Ishikawa H.; Fujita N.; Kato Y.; Kurihara M.; Minoshima T.; Shiota D.; Iwai K.; Pinto M.; Gomes A.; Murakami G.; Kusano K.; Mitsuda C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Solar energetic particle (SEP) events threaten space infrastructure, yet physics-based prediction models depend on numerous poorly constrained free parameters. We introduce the Fujitsu Solar Energetic particle Intelligent Tuning and Evaluation Network (SEITEN), which couples the MHD model of CME propagation to , a diffusive shock acceleration and focused transport model, through the shock conditions supplies, and automatically optimizes the free parameters of the particle model against the SEP event of 9 October 2021. The mean free path and the injection efficiency vary independently along each magnetic field line and heliolongitudinal bin, giving a 19-dimensional problem solved by quasi-Monte Carlo sampling followed by a Tree-structured Parzen Estimator. The optimized model reproduces proton flux profiles at five spacecraft with a mean absolute error of $$\approx 0.45$$ in log10 flux, and the inferred mean free paths show a clear east–west structure; these are effective parameters conditional on the assumed transport geometry. Six independent runs show that whether mean free paths or injection efficiencies dominate depends on the MHD shock strength, and that injection efficiencies differ by orders of magnitude between MHD configurations despite nearly identical fit quality. Joint MHD–SEP parameter estimation is therefore a necessary next step toward generalized, operational SEP forecasting.

Article.Title: Modeling of peak shear strength of rock joints based on a three-dimensional roughness index
Article.Authors: Wang H.; Man C.; Qi J.; Gao W.; Zheng J.; Chen Y.; Li X.; Ban L.
Article.Abstract: Rock joints are widely present in engineering rock masses, and their peak shear strength directly governs the stability of jointed rock masses. To investigate the influence mechanism of joint surface morphology on the peak shear strength, this study fabricated 35 sets of joint specimens with five distinct morphological types using a combination of three-dimensional laser scanning and CNC engraving technologies. Based on the scanning results, an improved 3D apparent dip angle distribution function was proposed, which more accurately captures the spatial distribution characteristics of joint surface morphology. By integrating this function, a new 3D roughness index was developed. This index exhibits a clear linear relationship with the sampling interval and decreases as the interval increases. Subsequently, a series of constant-normal-load direct shear tests on rock joints was conducted. Test results revealed a strong linear correlation between this roughness index and the initial (zero-normal-stress) peak dilation angle. Moreover, the degradation trend of the peak dilation angle with increasing normal stress can be effectively described by an exponential function. On this basis, a peak dilation angle degradation model was defined, which enables accurate prediction of peak dilation angles under varying normal stress conditions. By incorporating this model into the Mohr-Coulomb criterion, a peak shear strength model was established. Comparative analysis with existing models, including validation against published data on granite joints, demonstrates that the proposed model offers the highest prediction accuracy ( R 2 = 0.978; mean relative error = 4.25%), making it suitable for reliably estimating the peak shear strength of rock joints.

Article.Title: Privacy-preserving collaborative transfer learning with generative adversarial networks (CTL-GAN) for classification of dry eye disease
Article.Authors: Kim B.; Won Y.; Kim H.; Cha J.; Lim D.; Jeon J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigated whether a collaborative transfer learning generative adversarial network (CTL-GAN) can generate synthetic fluorescein corneal images and enhance multiclass dry eye disease (DED) grading across institutions. We retrospectively included 1,600 fluorescein-stained anterior segment images from patients with DED at Samsung Medical Center (SMC) and 260 images from the public Sun Yat-sen University (SYSU) dataset, graded on the Oxford scale. A StyleGAN3 generator trained on SMC data produced synthetic images. Pretrained generator weights were transferred to a simulated site represented by the SYSU dataset and fine-tuned on local images, without exchanging raw images. DenseNet classifiers trained with GAN-based augmentation were compared with a benchmark model trained on real images only. GAN-based augmentation improved validation accuracy on SMC data from 64.2% to 75.5%, and transferring pretrained weights increased SYSU validation accuracy from 41.4% to 66.3%. Peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR 13.95 ± 1.54 dB), structural similarity index (SSIM 0.428 ± 0.111), and learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS 0.510 ± 0.047) showed low similarity to real images. In a blinded 10-item multiple-choice realism survey, 37 ophthalmologists answered correctly in 28.4% of cases, against a 20% chance level. CTL-GAN indicates that image synthesis from shared generator weights can improve external DED grading without exchanging patient images.

Article.Title: Enhanced surface hydrophobicity in the combined treatment of chaplins and rodlins from Streptomyces griseus
Article.Authors: Shamsol Anuar N.; Suhaimi N.; Suzuki K.; Sunagawa N.; Ohnishi Y.; Tezuka T.; Hara H.
Article.Abstract: Many microorganisms depend on their hydrophobic hyphal surfaces to grow into the air and disperse their spores. In Streptomyces species, this property is conferred by chaplin and rodlin proteins. In the present study, we examined the potential of chaplins and rodlins from Streptomyces griseus IFO 13350, focusing on their contributions to surface hydrophobicity. In vitro assays with recombinant chaplins (ChpC and ChpH) and rodlins (RdlA and RdlB) demonstrated that ChpH alone increased the hydrophobicity of glass slides. The combination of ChpH with RdlA/RdlB enhanced water repellency, yielding a contact angle of 66.7 ± 2.6°, which was significantly greater than that of either ChpH or RdlA/RdlB alone. The long chaplin, ChpC, did not show such an enhancement with RdlA/RdlB. Gene disruption experiments supported the assumption that short chaplin ChpH plays a dominant role in generating hydrophobic surfaces and acts cooperatively with RdlA and/or RdlB to produce strongly water-repellent surfaces. We showed that hydrophobicity can be maintained even in the absence of rodlet structures, highlighting the flexibility of the chaplin–rodlin system. Based on these findings, we propose a hypothetical model in which rodlins act as molecular scaffolds that align short-chaplin fibrils into ordered rodlet arrays, thereby amplifying surface hydrophobicity. This study also suggests that chaplins in combination with rodlins have potential as effective additives for surface hydrophobicity.

Article.Title: Performance evaluation of Spar equipped with solitary and double heave plate for use in east coast of India
Article.Authors: Sudhakar S.; Lavanya V.; Ramshankar P.; Devi T.; Sunagar P.; Dharek M.
Article.Abstract: Numerical techniques which are effective and affordable can be used to model and solve complex situations in ocean engineering problems. Either the time domain or the frequency domain can be used to solve the fluid structure interaction problems involving regular and random waves. The ANSYS AQWA program which is built on three-dimensional panel method which falls under the category of Boundary Element Method is designed to analyze the interaction between surface waves and offshore structures using diffraction radiation phenomenon. Heave plates have been extensively employed on Spar as dampening mechanisms to minimize its motion responses. These plates are effective in offering viscous damping and considerable added mass in heave mode. This hybrid approach began with 1:100 scale free-decay tests of the Spar, run both bare-hulled and with a damping plate fitted, to capture its physical heave behaviour. The resulting hydrodynamic response of the Spar carrying twin heave plates was then simulated under regular and irregular sea states in ANSYS AQWA, a potential-flow-based solver. Because AQWA cannot capture viscous effects on its own, the gap between the total damping measured experimentally and the radiation damping predicted numerically was treated as non-linear viscous damping and fed back into the model as an external user-defined input. The role of relative spacing on Spar’s motion response was assessed and subsequently presented in the analysis. The simulated results revealed that the Spar featuring a pair of heave plates with a relative spacing ranging from 30 to 40% greater than that of Spar integrated with a solitary heave plate possessing a diameter ratio of 1.3 was highly effective in reducing responses under both regular and random wave conditions. The adoption of motion-reduction technologies in these platforms facilitates the development of clean energy solutions, thereby contributing to the achievement of United Nations Sustainable Development Goals on affordable and clean energy.

Article.Title: A robust deep learning framework for smart grid stability classification using statistical validation
Article.Authors: Kalyankumar K.; Saraswathi P.; Vanitha C.; Robin L.; Zewdu M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The classification of smart-grid stability is difficulty due to nonlinear interactions among the participant reaction-time, elasticity of power consumption and electricity-price. This paper proposed a comparative deep-learning model of classifying stable and unstable operating conditions based on 10,000 observations of simulated four-node electrical-grid stability dataset. To avoid deterministic redundancy and target leakage, we omitted p1 and the continuous stability variable stab, making 11 input predictors. They were data-quality assessment, training, standardization, stratified data partitioning and five-fold cross-validation. Four traditional machine-learning models (Logistic Regression, RBF-SVM, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting) and five deep-learning models (DNN, AutoEncoder-DNN, 1D-CNN, CNN1D-LSTM and FT-Transformer) were tested using a similar conditions. The DNN achieved the best overall test performance, with an accuracy of 97.10%, precision of 97.28%, recall of 98.20%, F1-score of 97.74%, ROC-AUC of 0.9963 and PR-AUC of 0.9980. AutoEncoder-DNN and RBF-SVM had the accuracy of 96.90% and 96.05, respectively. Precise paired McNemar tests with Holm correction indicated that the DNN performed better in comparison to the other tested networks with the exception of the AutoEncoder-DNN where the difference was not statistically relevant. The analysis of SHAP and feature-group ablation showed that the most impactful predictor groups were reaction times and price-elasticity coefficients of participants. The DNN achieved 95.60% accuracy with standardized Gaussian noise with a value of 0.10, but dropped to 90.90% in the case of 10% of measurements random and median-imputed. These results indicate that the DNN is effective on the studied simulated benchmark. However, it needs to be validated with actual PMU or SCADA measurements and larger and more heterogeneous grid topologies prior to operational implementation.

Article.Title: Mitochondrial diversity and demographic history of Arctica islandica (Bivalvia: Venerida) in the German waters of the Baltic Sea
Article.Authors: Schulz L.; Kniesz K.; Stuckas H.; Wolf F.; Zettler M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The semi-enclosed Baltic Sea is a comparatively young brackish ecosystem characterised by strong environmental gradients that can shape genetic diversity and demographic history in marine species. The amphi-Atlantic bivalve Arctica islandica (Linnaeus 1767) inhabits the southwestern Baltic Sea, where populations experience environmental conditions distinct from fully marine habitats. We analysed mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit I ( COI ) and cytochrome b ( CytB ) sequences to assess mitochondrial diversity and infer historical demographic patterns of A. islandica in the German waters of the Baltic Sea. Mitochondrial diversity was high, with haplotype diversity of 0.82–0.84 and nucleotide diversity of 0.69–0.74%. Widespread haplotype sharing and no evidence of regional structuring were observed. Most genetic variation occurred within rather than among regions (F ST = − 0.025, p = 0.99). Demographic analyses supported a history of population expansion, while comparison with previously published CytB haplotypes showed that specimens from the German waters of the Baltic Sea predominantly shared common haplotypes with samples from multiple regions across the species’ distribution. Overall, the mitochondrial data indicate that A. islandica populations in the German waters of the Baltic Sea retain substantial shared mitochondrial diversity despite inhabiting environmentally distinct brackish habitats. These patterns are consistent with relatively recent colonisation or expansion within the Baltic Sea and a shared demographic history and provide a baseline for future genome-wide studies of population connectivity and adaptive variation.

Article.Title: Design and development of a full-scale oxygenator model for future biohybrid lung application
Article.Authors: Singh A.; Janning K.; Simbolon D.; Mouzakis F.; Kashefi A.; Mottaghy K.; Neidlin M.; Olmer R.; Jockenhoevel S.; Cornelissen C.; Thiebes A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Use of conventional oxygenators is typically limited to 10–14 days due to poor hemocompatibility. Endothelialization of gas exchange membranes can create a natural non-thrombogenic surface and has proven effective in small laboratory models, but this approach requires a specific oxygenator design that can support both effective gas exchange and future membrane endothelialization. Thus, we developed a modular spiral-coil oxygenator using a fabrication approach that enables the production of a large membrane surface area with integrated blood channels. We designed and fabricated multiple oxygenator prototypes using a rolled flat-sheet PDMS/spacer/PDMS membrane structure and evaluated their gas exchange and fluid flow. Prototypes were tested for gas exchange performance following ISO 7199:2016 standards. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations were performed to assess flow distribution and wall shear stress (WSS). Among the tested prototypes, two designs provided the most promising results. They achieved surface areas of 0.20 m² and 0.34 m² with priming volumes of 348 mL and 312 mL, respectively. Both models showed quantifiable gas exchange supporting the feasibility of the proposed concept. CFD simulations revealed no stagnant areas and low WSS. These results demonstrate the feasibility of a modular spiral-coil oxygenator with a large-area flat-sheet membrane and millimeter-scale blood channels. While gas transfer requires improvement before clinical applicability for extracorporeal CO 2 removal, the fabrication approach provides a foundation for future endothelialization and development of long-term biohybrid lung support devices.

Article.Title: Synergistic integration of graphene-CNT-doped stearic acid PCM and graphene–metal oxide hybrid nanofluids for enhanced photovoltaic thermal–electrical performance
Article.Authors: Kumar N.; Barik D.; Tudu K.; Ranjan A.; Resmi S.; Ashok N.; Shanmugapriya D.; Gnanasekaran L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To enhance the durability of the solar PV systems, it is necessary to use novel materials and methods for cooling and disposal of unwanted heat. In this perspective, phase change materials (PCMs) with hybrid nanofluids are one of the best choices for efficient thermal management. This experiment proposes a novel PV cooling system that uses graphene and CNT nanoparticles (1:1) and (6 w/w%) added stearic acid as a PCM with hybrid nanofluids to maximize heat dissipation and system overall efficiency. The novelty lies in the synergistic combination of graphene-CNT-doped PCM (melting point 59 °C) with graphene-metal oxide hybrid nanofluids. Three hybrid nanofluids were prepared: G-TiO₂, G-Al₂O₃, and G-SiO₂, at a volume concentration of 0.5%, and different flow rates of 2, 4, 6, and 8 LPM were tested. The results proved that the 6 LPM flow rate, with the G-Al₂O₃ nanofluid, gave the best thermal and electrical results. In that, the enhanced absolute electrical efficiency was 4.5%, thermal efficiency by 8.3%, and the Nusselt number was 295 in comparison with the base fluid (DI water). Although the pressure drop and friction factor increased by 0.3 N/m² and 0.08, respectively, with G-SiO₂, it is still controllable with normal pumping. The proposed solar PV cooling system is highly applicable in building-integrated systems, hot climates, and hybrid renewable micro-grid systems.

Article.Title: Efficient removal of fusidic acid from aqueous solution using synthesized zinc magnesium aluminum layered double hydroxide adsorbent
Article.Authors: Asmel N.; Alwared A.; Sulaiman F.; Mohammed N.; Kalla R.; Knani S.; Ansari A.; Lakkaboyana S.
Article.Abstract: Pharmaceutical residues in the water have become a growing environmental concern because of their potential ecological and human health effects and their persistence. The Zn-Mg-Al layered double hydroxides (LDH) were prepared by the co-precipitation method, and their efficiency was tested as an adsorbent for the elimination of fusidic acid (FA) from aqueous solution. Characterization of the synthesized material was done by FTIR, SEM, XRD, EDS, BET, and TGA. The parameters affecting adsorption performance, such as pH, dosage of the adsorbent, contact time, initial concentration of FA and temperature, were investigated by batch adsorption experiments. The most efficient removal was obtained in 210 min at the optimum conditions of FA adsorbent dosage (1.25 g/L), agitation speed (250 rpm), concentration (20 mg/L), pH 5, and temperature (20 ± 1 °C), and showed the best agreement with the PSO model. Kinetic analysis suggested the PSO model best fitted the experimental data, while isotherm studies showed good agreement with the Freundlich model, indicating a heterogeneous adsorption behavior. Thermodynamic analysis shows that adsorption process was thermodynamically favorable. Besides, the reusability and structural stability of the adsorbent improved after calcination treatment, whereas the adsorption rate was slightly decreased. The results indicated that the Zn-Mg-Al LDH is a promising and economical adsorbent for the removal of pharmaceutical contaminants from aqueous stream.

Article.Title: Liquid neural network-driven intelligent topology perception and path anomaly diagnosis for Ipv6 smart grids
Article.Authors: Hu F.; Huang Y.; Lin X.; Huang G.
Article.Abstract: The deployment of Segment Routing IPv6 (SRv6) in smart grids introduces highly dynamic topologies and continuous-time telemetry streams. Traditional discrete-time Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) struggle to process these asynchronous, irregularly sampled data streams without suffering from severe discretization information loss, limiting their real-time diagnostic capabilities. To resolve this, this paper proposes an intelligent topology perception and path anomaly diagnosis framework driven by Liquid Neural Networks (LNNs). The novelty of this work lies in formulating network state transitions as continuous-time dynamics governed by Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs). This approach natively accommodates irregularly sampled telemetry data without discretization, allowing the network’s internal states to dynamically adapt to transient anomalies. Furthermore, we design a multi-task learning architecture that unifies real-time topology inference and probabilistic fault forecasting into a single end-to-end framework. Experimental evaluations on a simulated IPv6 smart grid demonstrate the objective superiority of the proposed model over state-of-the-art baselines. Specifically, the LNN framework achieves a 98.0% F1-score in topology awareness (outperforming Informer by 2.5%), reduces the False Positive Rate (FPR) in anomaly detection to 4.7%, and provides an Early Warning Time (EWT) of 8.5 s, which is a 13.3% improvement over the best baseline model. Comprehensive ablation and scalability studies further validate the computational feasibility and robustness of the LNN framework under high data-missing rates, providing a highly reliable monitoring mechanism for mission-critical power networks.

Article.Title: Probiotic potential of lactic acid bacteria isolated from a maize-based fermented beverage (kwete) consumed by ethnic communities in Northern Uganda
Article.Authors: Nassanga P.; Mauriello G.; Ochaya S.; Fassinou F.; Ongeng D.
Article.Abstract: Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) from traditionally fermented beverages are widely recognized for their health-promoting effects and probiotic potential. This study compared LAB isolates from kwete in two sub-regions of Northern Uganda (Acholi: seven isolates; Lango: nine isolates) with the reference strain Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus ATCC 7469. The isolates were evaluated for tolerance to gastrointestinal stress, functional properties, and antimicrobial activity. A one-way analysis of variance was conducted to compare the performance of isolates from the two sub-regions and the reference strain across probiotic parameters, with a significance level set at p < 0.05. Tukey’s HSD test was used for mean separation analysis. Results revealed distinct differences in probiotic performance between the isolates from the two sub-regions and the reference strain. Principal Component Analysis and Hierarchical Cluster Analysis were used to identify the most promising isolates. Notably, several isolates exhibited significantly higher values than Lb . rhamnosus ATCC 7469 for specific probiotic characteristics, including phenol (isolates 114,45,51); cell surface hydrophobicity (isolates 147, 104, & 99), survival under simulated gastric conditions (isolates 104 and 105) and survival under simulated pancreatin conditions (isolates 89 and 115) for 2 and 3 h. According to multivariate analyses (PCA and HCA), isolate 51 and 147 from Acholi sub-region and isolate 111 and 115 from the Lango sub-region showed the strongest overall associations with multiple probiotic attributes and were therefore identified as the most promising probiotic candidates. These results highlight that LAB from traditional fermented beverages in Northern Uganda are a valuable source of novel probiotic candidates for potential applications in health and nutritional interventions. The LAB isolates demonstrated several promising in vitro probiotic characteristics and one ex vivo characteristic; however, in vivo studies are required to validate their efficacy, safety, and functional performance before their application as probiotic candidates.

Article.Title: Study of the influence of hard interlayers on seismic parameters via shaking table tests
Article.Authors: Qiao F.; Chang C.; Zhao Y.; Cao Y.; Wang L.
Article.Abstract: According to the third theorem of similarity, a layered physical model was established using two types of materials with different shear stiffnesses. This model was used to represent the prototype in shaking table tests, and the influences of the burial depth and thickness of the hard interlayer on the amplification factor and on the characteristic parameters of the response spectrum were analysed and studied. The study revealed the following: (1) The influence trends of the burial depth and thickness of the hard interlayer on the amplification factor and on the characteristic period of the response spectrum obtained from the shaking table tests were found to be consistent with those obtained from a one-dimensional equivalent linearization calculation. This comparison serves as a verification of the experimental results rather than as an independent conclusion. (2) When the interlayer was located in the upper layer, the amplification factor gradually decreased with increasing thickness, with a maximum decrease of 6.6%. (3) When the input seismic motion was 0.1 g, the platform value of the response spectrum decreased linearly with increasing burial depth of the interlayer.(4) With increasing input seismic motion, the influence of the interlayer thickness on the characteristic period of the response spectrum remained almost unchanged when the interlayer was located at the bottom, whereas it varied considerably when the interlayer was located at the top. The results clarify the influence of the burial depth and thickness of hard interlayers on the amplification factor and on the characteristic parameters of the response spectrum, and provide a reference for the seismic response analysis and the seismic suitability evaluation of sites containing hard interlayers.

Article.Title: Electronic opacity in double bilayer graphene junctions

Article.Abstract: In this paper, we examine the transmission probability through a symmetric double bilayer-graphene junction modulated by Fano-type interference. At oblique incidence, two trajectories generated by Fano resonances and a quasi-bound well state are combined to generate perfect Fano interference resulting in null electron transmission. Interestingly, the transmission can be changed between normal and anomalous simply by adjusting the relative phase of the Fano resonances due to the appropriate modulation of the incidence angle, height of potential, and barrier and well width. This phenomenon is similar to electromagnetically induced absorption or to phase control of light propagation in quantum wells via Fano interference.

Article.Title: Failure analysis and improvement measures of tunnel drainage system in cold regions
Article.Authors: Zhao X.; Su X.; Sun Y.; Guan B.; Fu X.; Sun H.; Zhao K.; Zhang Q.
Article.Abstract: Tunnel construction in cold regions is particularly susceptible to frost damage, which is often caused by drainage system failures. To address this critical issue, it is essential to study the failure phenomena of the drainage system. This paper summarizes the characteristics of tunnels in cold regions and identifies channel clogging and channel frost heave as the main reasons for drainage system failure. Three factors contributing to drainage system failure are also identified. Furthermore, this paper explores the corresponding failure mechanisms. In response to these challenges, this paper has studied the reported and published engineering cases, and has summarized two drainage. the connection mode of frost protection drainage ditch and the addition of a drainage channel. Additionally, two temperature-control measures are reviewed: the insulation layer and ground source heat pump. These reviewed measures can help preventing frost damage and improving the durability of tunnels in cold regions. Finally, this paper discusses the potential for future drainage system failures in cold regions, highlighting the need for ongoing research and innovation in this area.

Article.Title: Molecular and biochemical insights after non-thermal plasma treatment during the germination process in maize grains
Article.Authors: Haranzová D.; Kostoláni D.; Kováč J.; Ličková P.; Zahoranová A.; Švubová R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Non-thermal plasma has been identified as a promising tool for the pre-sowing treatment of agriculturally important crops, with a multitude of studies reporting its positive effects on early germination processes. This study investigates the impact of plasma treatment generated by diffuse coplanar surface barrier discharge (DCSBD) on the initial and post-germination stages in maize grains. The relative expression of key hydrolytic enzymes, namely α-amylase , β-amylase , and zein-degrading protease ( ZDP ) was analysed. The subsequent activity of proteases and α-amylase was observed separately in the embryo, scutellum, and in the starch endosperm. Concurrently, the mobilisation of storage compounds within these tissues was observed. As a result of DCSBD treatment, the efficacy of the decontamination effect of maize grains was demonstrated. Furthermore, the genus of the present microorganism was also detected. Overall, this study provides a comprehensive characterisation of plasma-induced treatment in maize grains during the germination period, with a view to determining, on molecular and biochemical levels, as well as on morphological and surface properties of maize grains.

Article.Title: Feature driven machine learning framework for accurate and computationally efficient remaining useful life prediction of lithium-ion batteries
Article.Authors: Singh S.; Jain M.; Bhagirath S.
Article.Abstract: Accurate estimation of the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries is essential for improving the reliability, safety, and cost-effectiveness of electric vehicles (EVs). Although several machine learning models have been reported for RUL prediction, many require extensive feature engineering or high computational effort, which limits their practical use in battery management systems. This work presents a predictive machine learning framework that balances prediction accuracy with computational efficiency. The proposed framework uses sensor-derived features from the NASA battery degradation dataset. The data are first preprocessed through exploratory data analysis and normalization to improve their quality. Feature analysis identifies the maximum discharge voltage and the minimum charge voltage as the two most influential indicators of battery degradation. These features are then used to train three regression models, namely k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and Random Forest (RF). The models are evaluated using multiple statistical performance metrics. Among them, the RF model delivers the best overall performance with a coefficient of determination ( \(R^{2}\) ) of 0.9421 and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 77.47. The kNN model achieves comparable prediction accuracy while requiring less training time. However, the SVR model exhibits lower prediction accuracy incurring higher computational cost. The proposed framework is further validated using independent battery datasets, where the predicted RUL closely follows the observed degradation trend. These results demonstrate that the proposed approach provides accurate, reliable, and computationally efficient RUL estimation, making it suitable for real-time battery health monitoring and predictive battery management in electric vehicles. In the future, this framework has the potential to contribute to effective and scalable battery health management systems. Furthermore, it could be extended to deep learning and adaptive models to be used under diverse operating conditions.

Article.Title: Development of a gel-based temporary blocking agent: tuning activation temperature, degradability, and integrated pressure-resistance assessment using a dynamic simulation
Article.Authors: Faqfoory M.; Sharifi M.; Nasiri A.; Fahimpour J.
Article.Abstract: Workover operations frequently require temporary wellbore isolation to control formation fluid inflow; however, conventional lost-circulation materials and mechanical isolation assemblies often exhibit limited sealing efficiency, poor post-treatment removability, or severe formation damage potential. An integrated laboratory-scale wellbore simulation framework was developed to systematically evaluate Temporary Plugging Agent (TPA) gel-plug (GP) performance by integrating precursor injectivity, apparent activation temperature, static gel strength, confined differential pressure resistance, geometric confinement effects (H/D ratio), contaminant sensitivity, acid-triggered degradation behavior, and formation-damage potential. Two distinct synthesis pathways were investigated: (1) in-situ free-radical copolymerization of acrylamide (ACM) monomer using polyethylene glycol diacrylate (PEGDA) as a difunctional crosslinker with thermal persulfate initiators, and (2) ex-situ chemical post-crosslinking of linear polyacrylamide (PAM) using hexamethylenetetramine (HMTA). Ten distinct formulations were prepared and systematically evaluated. While ex-situ formulations failed to establish mechanically stable, self-supporting gel networks, in-situ formulations yielded robust three-dimensional covalently crosslinked hydrogel networks. The optimized in-situ formulation displayed excellent injectivity with a pre-gel viscosity below 5 cP (25 °C) and a tunable activation temperature ranging from 54 °C to 63 °C depending on the persulfate initiator used. Dynamic tube pressure assessments demonstrated a maximum differential pressure resistance of 1,410 psi. Contamination with sodium chloride (NaCl), potassium chloride (KCl), and crude oil reduced pressure resistance by 31%, 18%, and 14%, respectively. Controlled degradation assessments demonstrated a 78% mass reduction within 30 days in 20 wt% hydrochloric acid (HCl), while post-degradation core-flooding tests showed a 3.50% permeability reduction under the conditions of this study (96.5% permeability recovery ratio). The developed in-situ gel plug system successfully combines high precursor injectivity, substantial pressure-bearing capability, controlled chemical removability, and minimal formation damage, making it a promising temporary isolation technology for severe fluid-loss and workover applications.

Article.Title: Quality of life of patients with autoimmune bullous disease in Kabul, Afghanistan
Article.Authors: Aalemi A.; Habib K.; Wright A.; Hwang S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Autoimmune bullous diseases (AIBDs) are chronic, potentially life-threatening disorders that significantly impair patients’ quality of life (QoL). Despite increasing global recognition of this burden, data from Afghanistan remain lacking. This study aimed to evaluate QoL and its association with disease severity among patients with AIBDs in Kabul Afghanistan. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted at Maiwand Teaching Hospital, Kabul, between December 2024 and March 2026. A total of 105 patients aged ≥ 16 years with dermatologist-confirmed AIBDs were included. QoL was assessed using the Persian versions of the Autoimmune Bullous Disease Quality of Life (ABQOL) and Treatment Autoimmune Bullous Disease Quality of Life (TABQOL) questionnaires (ABQOL/TABQOL score range 0–51, higher scores represent worse QoL). Disease severity was measured using the Autoimmune Bullous Skin Disorder Intensity Score (ABSIS) (score range 0-206, higher scores represent greater disease severity). Independent t-tests and Spearman correlation coefficients were used to compare quality of life scores. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. The mean age of participants was 54.60 ± 11.98 years, with a slight female predominance (54.3%). Pemphigus vulgaris was the most common diagnosis (80.0%). The mean ABQOL and TABQOL scores were 23.85 ± 7.15 and 21.05 ± 6.26, respectively, indicating moderate QoL impairment. Patients with comorbidities had significantly higher ABQOL scores ( P = 0.007). ABQOL differed significantly by diagnosis, with worse scores among pemphigus vulgaris patients ( P < 0.001). No significant differences were observed by sex or educational status. ABQOL and TABQOL were moderately correlated ( r = 0.520, P < 0.001). Both scores showed significant positive correlations with ABSIS ( r = 0.705 and r = 0.528, respectively; P < 0.001), indicating that greater disease severity was associated with poorer QoL. Patients with AIBDs in Afghanistan experience moderate impairment in QoL, strongly associated with disease severity and comorbidities. These findings highlight the importance of disease control and comprehensive management strategies to improve patient outcomes in resource-limited settings.

Article.Title: Bridging the deployment gap in automated moth monitoring through biodiversity foundation models
Article.Authors: Wei Y.; Shih L.; Lai Y.; Lin C.; Lu S.; Shiao M.
Article.Abstract: Automated monitoring enables biodiversity surveys across broader spatial and temporal scales, but developing robust species recognition models requires large annotated image datasets that are often unavailable from field monitoring systems. Consequently, models are often trained using large citizen-science image repositories, creating a substantial domain gap between training and deployment images. Here, we developed a fine-grained moth classifier using approximately 363,000 citizen-science images representing 2727 species and evaluated it across two contrasting field monitoring systems encompassing 526 species. To improve deployment transferability, we optimized three components of the transfer-learning pipeline: biodiversity-specific pretrained representations, parameter-efficient model adaptation, and data augmentation. Biodiversity-specific pretrained representations with BioCLIP2.5 substantially improved deployment performance, outperforming conventional convolutional and generic vision-language models. Parameter-efficient adaptation improved deployment transferability, whereas deployment-oriented augmentations consistently enhanced robustness across both monitoring systems. The optimized pipeline achieved 85.0% Top-1 accuracy and 58.1% Macro F1 on the commercial monitoring system, and 89.5% Top-1 accuracy and 68.6% Macro F1 on the low-cost edge device. Optimization increased field performance relative to the source domain from 38.9 to 69.7% on the commercial system and from 62.3 to 82.3% on the low-cost edge device. Our study provides a practical framework for reducing the deployment gap between citizen-science training images and automated field monitoring, facilitating scalable species recognition in automated biodiversity monitoring.

Article.Title: Effects of cholecalciferol on cardiac electrical function autonomic regulation lipid peroxidation and myocardial injury in isoproterenol induced myocardial ischemia
Article.Authors: Farokhipour M.; Dehghanian A.; Ketabchi F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Myocardial ischemia is characterized by electrical instability, oxidative stress, and inflammation. This study investigated whether short-term cholecalciferol treatment attenuates cardiac electrical and autonomic dysfunctions and biochemical disturbances in a rat model of isoproterenol (ISO)-induced myocardial ischemia. Male Sprague–Dawley rats were allocated to Sham, cholecalciferol (CAL), ISO, and CAL + ISO groups. Cardiac electrical activity, autonomic function, and hemodynamics were assessed using electrocardiography, heart rate variability (HRV) analysis, and arterial pressure recordings under basal conditions, during phenylephrine-induced baroreflex activation and sustained elevation of arterial pressure, and following inhibition of endothelial nitric oxide synthase with L-NAME. Plasma malondialdehyde (MDA), NO metabolites, lactate dehydrogenase, total and differential leukocyte counts, and cardiac histopathology were also evaluated. ISO-induced myocardial ischemia increased heart rate, prolonged QT and QTc intervals, elevated the ST segment, and reduced HRV indices. These changes were accompanied by increased plasma MDA and NO metabolite levels, neutrophil percentage, and myocardial injury, along with decreased lymphocyte percentage and myocardial edema. Cholecalciferol treatment attenuated tachycardia and ST-segment elevation, reduced QTc prolongation during baroreflex activation, partially restored HRV responses during baroreflex activation, and altered autonomic balance. In addition, cholecalciferol reduced plasma MDA and NO metabolite levels and attenuated hematological alterations and myocardial structural damage. Short-term cholecalciferol administration improves cardiac electrical function and autonomic regulation and attenuates alterations in circulating leukocytes, plasma MDA and NO metabolite levels, and markers of myocardial injury. Our findings suggest that cholecalciferol may exert protective effects on cardiac electrical and autonomic function and mitigate biochemical and hematological alterations associated with isoproterenol-induced myocardial injury.

Article.Title: Effect of infill density and geometry of direct ink written 3D Ni-based electrodes on their oxygen evolution reaction performance
Article.Authors: Rodríguez-Lagar P.; Blanco C.; Santamaría R.; Menéndez J.; Montes-Morán M.; Rocha V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this work, Direct Ink Writing (DIW) is used to develop novel complex 3D electrodes for water splitting, specifically for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). The main advantages of using 3D electrodes for this application are to maximise catalyst surface area and facilitate gas products evacuation. High-solids-load (79 wt%), water-based pastes based on micrometer Ni powders were processed by a sequence of DIW, sintering and NiFe electrodeposition. Three different complex geometries, i.e., two rectilinear infills (40% and 55% infill density) and one gyroid infill (50% infill density), were developed as proof of concept to determine the influence of the electrode design on the OER performance. The study has demonstrated that lower infill rates (40% rectilinear infill) clearly enable OER efficiency optimisation. In addition to the higher mesh size, the superior performance of this particular electrode is enhanced by the filament orientation at 45° to the gravity vector, which facilitates buoyancy-driven bubble release, and by the inner porosity of the filaments, which is expected to favour the electrode wettability and aerophobicity.

Article.Title: Comparative hepatoprotective efficacy of spirulina polysaccharides and crude spirulina against metalaxyl-m toxicity via modulation of oxidative stress and Nrf2/NF-κB gene expression
Article.Authors: Alraheem E.; R. Sleem F.; Abdallah A.; Ibrahim I.; Ateya A.; Habotta O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The liver stands as the central metabolic hub of the body, acting as the primary frontline defense against systemic toxins and xenobiotics. However, this relentless detoxification role renders it uniquely vulnerable to the escalating threat of modern agrochemicals. Among these, metalaxyl-m, a widely utilized chiral pesticide, poses a significant risk, as the global shift toward sophisticated chemical synthesis continues to increase the prevalence of such bioactive compounds. This study was designed to investigate the hepatotoxic mechanisms of metalaxyl-m and explore the potential of spirulina platensis, along with its bioactive polysaccharides, in neutralizing this damage. Our findings revealed that metalaxyl-m exposure triggered severe hepatotoxicity by disrupting the Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway, leading to a collapse in the antioxidant defense system (GSH, CAT, SOD), profound oxidative stress (elevated MDA), and a sharp rise in liver enzymes (ALT, AST). At the molecular level, toxicity was driven by the upregulation of inflammatory and apoptotic markers, including TNF-α, TLR4 and NF-kB. Conversely, the administration of spirulina and its isolated polysaccharides effectively counteracted these pathological shifts. Notably, spirulina polysaccharides effectively preserved hepatocyte integrity and markedly upregulated tissue immunohistochemical expression of SIRT1. These findings highlight their protective potential as a natural candidate for mitigating pesticide-induced hepatotoxicity.

Article.Title: Chia (Salvia hispanica L.) shoot cultures as a scalable source of bioactive metabolites: from agar cultures to bioreactor systems
Article.Authors: Motyka-Pędrak S.; Kusznierewicz B.; Tomaś K.; Mesa T.; Bermejo N.; Korona-Głowniak I.; Munné-Bosch S.; Pomierny-Chamioło L.; Szopa A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents a comprehensive biotechnological characterization of Salvia hispanica (chia) shoot cultures as a scalable source of antioxidant and antimicrobial compounds. Cultures were established in agar, agitated, and temporary-immersion systems (TIS, Plantform bioreactors), with phenylalanine (Phe) supplementation to enhance secondary metabolism. Agitated cultures with 3 mmol/L Phe showed the highest rosmarinic acid production (8621.77 mg/100 g DW), over 40-fold higher than control cultures. LC–Q-Orbitrap HRMS analysis identified 127 metabolites, including phenolic acids, flavonoids, and terpenoids, revealing significant shifts in phenolic biosynthesis upon Phe treatment. Bioreactor cultures achieved the highest biomass yield (8.43-fold increase) and elevated levels of vitamins C and E. Extracts obtained from agitated and bioreactor micorshoot cultures exhibited antibacterial and antifungal activity. The highest antibacterial activity was observed for extracts from agitated cultures supplemented with 3 mM Phe, particularly against Staphylococcus aureus and Micrococcus luteus , whereas extracts from bioreactor cultures generally showed lower antimicrobial activity. These findings demonstrate that combining precursor feeding, culture optimization, and metabolomics enables efficient production of rosmarinic acid-rich biomass with potential applications in food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic industries.

Article.Authors: Daňková K.; Kasović M.; Višić G.; Gimunová M.; Vespalec T.
Article.Abstract: Carrying school bags represents a routine mechanical exposure for school-aged children and may influence posture, gait, and musculoskeletal health. Current recommendations commonly express school bag weight as a percentage of body weight; however, relationships among relative load, anthropometric characteristics, perceived heaviness, carrying duration, and back pain remain unclear. This cross-sectional study examined these relationships in 221 schoolchildren aged 6–15 years. Anthropometric characteristics, school bag weight, carrying duration, perceived heaviness, and self-reported back pain were assessed. Mean relative school bag load was 14.49 ± 3.79% of body weight. Relative load was inversely associated with BMI, body weight, and body height. Carrying duration showed a weak positive association with perceived heaviness. Exploratory cluster analysis identified three descriptive profiles characterized by higher BMI/lower relative load, lower BMI/higher relative load, and longer carrying duration. Still, the cluster membership was not significantly associated with back pain. These findings indicate that relative load, carrying duration, perceived heaviness, and reported back pain capture partly distinct aspects of school bag carriage. Preventive recommendations should therefore remain proportionate to the evidence and should interpret the effect of a single school bag parameter on musculoskeletal pain cautiously.

Article.Authors: Vahedian Z.; Ahmadi A.; Abdi P.; Rahmani E.
Article.Abstract: To evaluate anterior corneal higher-order aberrations (HOAs) and inter-device agreement among Pentacam HR, ACE, and iTrace in primary congenital glaucoma (PCG). This cross-sectional study evaluated 37 eyes of 23 treated PCG patients at 3-, 4-, and 5-mm optical zones. Agreement was assessed with pairwise intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Bland-Altman analysis, using patient-level cluster-bootstrap confidence intervals and distribution-free limits of agreement. Mean age was 9.4 ± 2.8 years. Coma agreement ranged from poor to excellent (ICC 0.34–0.91), improving at larger zones for Pentacam HR–ACE; trefoil agreement was poor for most pairs (ICC ≤ 0.47). Keratometric agreement was excellent for Pentacam HR–ACE (ICC ≥ 0.93) and, after excluding one implausible iTrace acquisition, good to excellent for both iTrace comparisons (ICC 0.88–0.92; n = 21–22 eyes). Restricting to pupil-adequate eyes improved Pentacam HR–ACE horizontal coma agreement at 3 mm (ICC 0.34→0.83; overlapping confidence intervals), suggesting undilated pupil size partly explains disagreement. In this exploratory analysis, the devices did not demonstrate interchangeable performance in PCG eyes. Coma agreed best, though its clinical acceptability is uncertain. Inferential conclusions are limited to Pentacam HR versus ACE at 4–5 mm; ACE at 3 mm and all iTrace comparisons are descriptive. Larger-cohort validation is warranted.

Fe 2 O 3 nanoparticles were biosynthesized using Punica granatum seed extract as potential alternative reducing and stabilizing agent under mild conditions, while CuO nanoparticles were prepared by thermal decomposition of CuCO 3 at 500 °C for 2 h. The synthesized nanoparticles were characterized using SEM, XRD, FTIR, and EDX analyses. Their molluscicidal activity was assessed against the target snail species under laboratory conditions using the leaf-dipping technique. The results demonstrated that CuO nanoparticles exhibited higher toxicity than Fe 2 O 3 , as indicated by lower LC 50 values (455.32 ppm for CuO and 703.61 ppm for Fe 2 O 3 ). Mortality increased with concentration and exposure time. These findings highlight the greater molluscicidal activity of CuO nanoparticles and suggest their potential integration into integrated pest management (IPM) programs for the control of terrestrial snails.

Article.Title: Natural-language prompting builds and operates an open-source software workflow for virtual drug-discovery
Article.Authors: Seo J.; Zhang Y.; Yoon E.; Wang Y.; Su S.; Kim H.
Article.Abstract: Virtual docking and free-energy calculations can accelerate drug discovery, but practical use requires structural chemistry expertise, complex parameter selection and software integration. Here we show that iterative dialogue with an artificial intelligence (AI) coding assistant, OpenAI Codex, can guide a non-specialist scientist to build and operate a scripted, auditable computational workflow without direct coding. The assistant provided structural chemistry guidance and assembled an integrated pipeline for structure retrieval and preparation, binding-site definition, ligand preparation, virtual docking, interaction analysis, molecular dynamics (MD) and alchemical relative binding free-energy calculations. It also built a script generator for launching, monitoring and interpreting workflow runs. We tested the workflow on public cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2) benchmarks. After primary docking and multi-seed hit refinement, the active-ligand fraction increased from 1.73% in the input library to 80% in the ten-candidate handoff set (46.4-fold over input); a short MD stage acted as a structural quality-control gate on the leading candidates. Docking and hit refinement also generalized to human immunodeficiency virus reverse transcriptase and kinesin family member 11 benchmarks. In a CDK2 free-energy benchmark, the workflow achieved root-mean-square error = 0.66 kcal/mol and Pearson r = 0.90. Prompt-guided AI can orchestrate computational drug-discovery workflows for non-specialists while the underlying calculations remain the work of established external software and every run remains auditable.

Article.Abstract: This study presents a two-stage framework for binary plasterboard quality inspection that combines edge-region-of-interest (ROI) segmentation with lightweight classification. The proposed MobileNetV2-MobileViT classifier contains 3.91 million parameters and was evaluated on a held-out set of 838 images, achieving 97.37% overall accuracy and 96.99% balanced accuracy. It achieved the highest accuracy among the evaluated transfer-learning baselines under the shared test protocol. Raspberry Pi 4 was used for image acquisition only; on-device inference, latency, memory, and power were not evaluated. Accordingly, the system should be interpreted as a compact, deployment-oriented framework that requires device-level validation before claims of real-time operation can be made.

Article.Title: Associations of longitudinal blood pressure with cerebral amyloid angiopathy in older adults
Article.Authors: Mehta R.; Capuano A.; Baumgartner N.; Barnes L.; Bennett D.; Arvanitakis Z.
Article.Abstract: Blood pressure (BP) and cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) are both risk factors for age-related cognitive decline, yet their associations are incompletely investigated. Here, we investigated the associations between longitudinal BP and neocortical CAA scores in 2107 older adults (mean age, 89.63 years) who were followed in one of five longitudinal cohort studies of aging. Systolic BP (SBP), diastolic BP (DBP), mean arterial pressure (MAP) and pulse pressure (PP) were collected at baseline and annual clinical visits whereas CAA and Alzheimer’s disease (AD) were assessed at autopsy. This study is a secondary analysis of the prospectively collected clinical and postmortem data from the five cohort studies. Logistic regression was used to analyze the association of mean BP across time with moderate-to-severe CAA. In primary analyses, we evaluated CAA in composite neocortex. In secondary analyses, we explored CAA in specific neocortical brain regions (i.e., frontal, temporal, parietal, and occipital) and controlled for cohort as well as CAA risk factors including APOE genotype and presence of AD pathology. All models adjusted for age at death, sex, and education. Primary regression analyses demonstrated no association between mean BP and moderate-to-severe CAA in the composite neocortex. However, secondary analyses revealed a weak inverse association between mean PP and moderate-to-severe CAA in the frontal neocortex (OR, 0.991 [95% CI, 0.983–0.998]) that remained after controlling for presence of AD and APOE genotype. We conclude that mean BP is not associated with CAA in composite neocortex, however further research into the associations of specific BP values with CAA severity may be warranted and should consider specific brain regions.

Article.Abstract: All-cause, cardiovascular, and stroke mortality are major public-health burdens, but mortality-status classifiers require rigorous validation and cautious calibration interpretation. We analyzed 4,137 sampled participants with linked binary mortality labels: 1,473 all-cause deaths, including 821 cardiovascular deaths and 223 stroke deaths. Single-task Elastic Net, Random Forest, XGBoost, and support vector machine models, together with an exploratory joint multinomial Elastic Net, were evaluated using 5-fold outer and 3-fold inner nested stratified cross-validation. Imputation, encoding, normalization, and class up-sampling were restricted to training folds, and performance was calculated from pooled out-of-fold predictions. For all-cause mortality, Elastic Net and the support vector machine achieved similar AUROC values of 0.925 after rounding, whereas Elastic Net achieved the highest AUPRC (0.886). Elastic Net performed best for cardiovascular mortality (AUROC 0.873; AUPRC 0.550). For stroke mortality, the support vector machine achieved both the highest AUROC (0.837) and AUPRC (0.189). The joint model did not improve discrimination and performed worse than single-task Elastic Net for cardiovascular mortality. Calibration curves and statistics showed meaningful deviations from ideal calibration; therefore, class-rebalanced probabilities should not be interpreted as validated absolute-risk estimates. SHAP beeswarm and dependence plots identified age and lactate dehydrogenase as prominent nonlinear model-attribution features. These models provide internally validated mortality-status classification, but clinical risk prediction requires outcome dates, fold-contained recalibration, and external validation.

Biochemical indices were categorized into predefined domains reflecting metabolic status, oxidative/antioxidant balance, and electrolyte–osmotic homeostasis. Associations were assessed using correlation analyses with false discovery rate (FDR) adjustment to control for multiple testing. Results Weak inverse correlations were observed between semen volume or motility and age, BMI, diastolic blood pressure, glucose, and triglycerides. Serum globulin levels demonstrated a small positive correlation with normal morphology. Serum osmolality exhibited consistent associations with DNA fragmentation index (DFI), high DNA stainability (HDS), and morphology. Most effect sizes were small, and associations not surviving FDR adjustment were interpreted as exploratory. Conclusion In this health-check population, routine systemic biochemical indices showed modest correlations with semen parameters. Given the cross-sectional design, findings should be interpreted as associative rather than causal. These results are hypothesis-generating and warrant longitudinal validation to clarify temporal relationships and biological mechanisms.

Article.Title: Shadow fading-aided path loss modeling in street canyons at 18 GHz
Article.Authors: Rifo F.; Chávez-Caipe E.; Celades-Martínez J.; García J.; Diago-Mosquera M.
Article.Abstract: Accurate propagation modeling is essential for network planning and performance evaluation. This paper presents a measurement-based analysis of large-scale path loss (PL) and shadow fading (SF) at 18 GHz in a line-of-sight (LoS) street-canyon scenario, using three receiver heights. Several PL models are evaluated, and a height-dependent close-in model (CI-H) is identified as a suitable baseline, achieving a global root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 2.48 dB while preserving physical interpretability. Based on CI-H, SF is extracted and statistically characterized, exhibiting near-zero mean and a global standard deviation of 2.47 dB, with increasing variability at larger distances. Using the spatial structure of SF, spatial interpolation and machine-learning (ML) models are tested under both dense-route interpolation and spatially blocked validation. Under random grouped interpolation, Ordinary Kriging (OK) and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) reduce the PL RMSE to 1.35 dB and 1.21 dB, respectively. When continuous 5–20 m route segments are excluded, GPR yields 2.21–2.38 dB, improving upon the corresponding 2.51–2.53 dB CI-H values by 0.15–0.32 dB. Under nested spatial cross-validation, GPR yields 2.32 dB, 0.21 dB below the 2.53 dB CI-H baseline. Thus, the large gains obtained with nearby measurements decrease substantially as spatial separation increases, although GPR retains a modest and consistent advantage on unseen route segments.

Article.Title: Enhancing performance of massive MIMO communication systems using iterative regularized zero-forcing precoding
Article.Authors: Gawo T.; Tiba I.; Yetneberk Z.; Ayenew T.; Woldesenbet M.
Article.Abstract: Massive multiple-input multiple-output (massive MIMO) has become a key technology in modern cellular networks because it can improve spectral efficiency, data rate, and coverage. These gains, however, require efficient precoding algorithms. Conventional precoding schemes such as regularized zero-forcing (RZF) precoding offer a useful trade-off between interference suppression and noise amplification, but their direct matrix inversion becomes computationally expensive when the number of base-station antennas is large. In this paper, we propose an iterative regularized zero-forcing (IRZF) precoding method that replaces direct inversion with a Richardson-type iterative algorithm to perform precoding with low complexity. We have compared the performance of the proposed method with conventional Gauss-Seidel (GS), Jacobi (JA), Joint Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel (Jac-PCG), Truncated polynomial expansion (TPE), and Regularized zero-forcing (RZF) in terms of achievable rate, spectral efficiency, computational complexity, and energy efficiency. The results show that the proposed IRZF achieves high performance with low complexity. Therefore, IRZF is most attractive in operating regimes where the required number of iterations is moderate and the regularized Gram matrix is well-conditioned.

Article.Title: AI-based smart waste collection route optimization system
Article.Authors: Shree J.; Chowdary T.; Jaraut P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Efficient collection of solid waste has become a significant challenge in urban areas due to increasing population density and waste generation. Conventional waste collection approach followed a rigid path and time based strategy resulting in heavy utilization of fuel, high operation cost, improper resource utilization, delay in waste collection in critical places. Intelligent data driven waste collection approach is thus required. This paper demonstrates an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based smart waste collection route optimization system combining machine learning based prediction and classical vehicle routing approach. The framework is built to predict the waste bin fill-levels using an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) regressor which identifies bins which require collection. Based on the projected demands for collection a Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP) is built and solved using Google OR-Tools to develop an efficient route that is also optimized in terms of fuel utilization while satisfying vehicle capacity constraints. The entire framework is developed using geospatial information data set of 11,058 waste bins and various waste processing facilities provided by Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC). The system is compared using metrics namely, collection distance, fuel consumption and its environmental impact. The current framework overcomes the problem of a reactive traditional system with inefficient prediction by presenting an intelligent and dynamic waste management system, proving that scalable AI-driven route optimization can help in supporting efficient smart city waste management.

Article.Title: Collaborative reasoning framework integrating multimodal large language models and knowledge graphs for dragon and lion dance technical action semantic understanding
Article.Authors: Yang A.; Ge Q.; Zhu M.
Article.Abstract: Dragon and lion dance occupies an unusual position: a nationally recognised item of intangible cultural heritage that is at the same time a codified competitive sport. Judging it is correspondingly hard, because one scored element carries temporal, spatial, dynamic and cooperative meaning at once. This study couples a multimodal large language model (MLLM) with a domain-specific knowledge graph (KG) so that technical actions can be recognised, scored and explained against the rulebook. The graph encodes 100 action types, 224 technical elements, 135 scoring criteria and 83 common error patterns, all distilled from official regulations, expert interviews and historical competition records. A perception-retrieval-reasoning pipeline drives the framework: the MLLM proposes a preliminary label, that label triggers structured subgraph retrieval, and the retrieved triples then constrain multi-hop reasoning. A cross-modal anchoring module aligns visual action embeddings with KG entity representations through contrastive learning with rule-aware hard negatives, while a path verbaliser converts the winning traversal into a rule-referenced adjudication report. We evaluate on 4,659 clips split disjointly by competition, so that no routine, team or venue appears in more than one subset. Measured against skeleton-based recognisers, recent video MLLMs, graph-augmented retrieval pipelines and a dedicated action quality assessment regressor, the framework reaches 82.7% classification accuracy, 44.2 BLEU-4 and 61.5 ROUGE-L; it predicts execution scores with a Spearman correlation of 0.812 and a relative L2 distance of 0.681, identifies deduction items at 79.4% F1, and cites the correct rule clause 85.6% of the time. Ablations, hyper-parameter sweeps, efficiency profiling and degraded-video tests indicate that knowledge grounding, perceptual anchoring, structured explanation and conflict-driven re-retrieval each address a different failure mode. Two clips traced end to end, one handled correctly and one not, show that every sentence of a generated report maps onto a graph edge that a reviewer can inspect. The framework is offered as a design for adjudication support that informs a judging panel rather than replacing it; whether it transfers to sports governed by other rulebooks has yet to be tested.
