Article.Title: Quality, reliability, and content coverage of pleural effusion–related short videos on Douyin (TikTok) and Bilibili: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Ji W.; Wang C.; Xie F.; Xu L.
Article.Abstract: Pleural effusion is a common clinical finding with heterogeneous causes, including infection, malignancy, heart failure, tuberculosis, pulmonary embolism and systemic disease. Because patients often encounter pleural effusion as an imaging finding rather than as a diagnosis, short-video platforms may shape early understanding, anxiety and care-seeking behaviour. Evidence on the quality of this content is lacking. We conducted a cross-sectional content analysis of publicly available pleural effusion–related short videos on Douyin and Bilibili. The Mandarin search term “胸腔积液” (pleural effusion) was entered on 15 May 2026 and the first 150 results returned under each platform’s default ranking were screened. Video duration, engagement metrics, uploader category, coverage of six content domains, Global Quality Score (GQS), modified DISCERN (mDISCERN) and Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) benchmark scores were extracted. Each video was scored independently by two reviewers, with discrepancies resolved by consensus with a third senior reviewer. Platform comparisons used two-sided Mann–Whitney U tests; uploader comparisons used Kruskal–Wallis tests with Holm-adjusted pairwise Mann–Whitney U tests. Proportional-odds ordinal logistic regression was used to estimate platform and uploader effects, with adjustment for uploader type and additional adjustment for log video duration and the number of coded content domains. All pairwise correlations were adjusted for multiplicity using Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate and Bonferroni corrections. The study is reported in accordance with the STROBE checklist for cross-sectional studies. The final sample comprised 200 videos (100 per platform). Overall quality was moderate and reliability limited, with median GQS 3 (IQR 2 to 3), mDISCERN 2 (IQR 1 to 2) and JAMA 2 (IQR 1 to 3). Specialists uploaded 51.00% of videos. Treatment (57.00%) and diagnosis (48.00%) were the most frequently covered content domains, whereas epidemiology (6.00%) and follow-up (5.50%) were the least; 14 videos (7.00%) covered none of the six coded domains. Unadjusted platform comparisons showed no difference in GQS or mDISCERN ( P = 0.961 and P = 0.603) and a higher JAMA score on Douyin ( P = 0.008). After adjustment for uploader type, however, Douyin videos had significantly lower overall quality (GQS adjusted OR 0.39, 95% CI 0.20 to 0.75, P = 0.005) and the apparent JAMA advantage was no longer present (adjusted OR 0.81, 95% CI 0.45 to 1.46, P = 0.479). The GQS difference was fully attenuated after further adjustment for video duration and content coverage (adjusted OR 1.06, 95% CI 0.48 to 2.32, P = 0.891), whereas log duration (OR 1.67, P = 0.002) and the number of coded content domains (OR 3.56, P < 0.001) remained associated with GQS. Uploader category showed the largest quality gradient (GQS epsilon-squared 0.423, 95% CI 0.294 to 0.557). After adjustment for multiple comparisons, none of the engagement metrics was associated with any quality instrument: likes, collections and shares showed no association, and the weak negative associations of comments with GQS (rho = − 0.20) and mDISCERN (rho = − 0.21) did not survive Bonferroni correction. Pleural effusion–related short videos on Douyin and Bilibili are widely accessible but medically incomplete. Platform identity was not independently associated with reliability or transparency once uploader composition had been accounted for, and the residual platform difference in overall quality was explained by shorter video duration and narrower content coverage rather than by the platform itself. Engagement metrics should not be read as indicators of information quality. Future short-video health education on pleural effusion should emphasise differential diagnosis, red-flag symptoms, thoracentesis and imaging pathways, malignancy and infection risk, and follow-up after initial treatment.

Article.Title: Physics aware joint low light and color correction for underwater image enhancement
Article.Authors: Vani P.; Suresh G.
Article.Abstract: The underwater images suffer from low illumination, absorption and scattering varies with the wavelength, poor visibility, low contrast and severe color distortion. These degradations have a negative impact on applications for underwater vision like marine exploration, object recognition and autonomous navigation. To overcome these difficulties, a Physics-Aware Joint Low-Light and Color Correction (PA-JLCC) framework to enhance underwater images has been developed. The proposed approach is lightweight, interpretable and does not require extensive training, in contrast with deep learning-based approaches. The framework estimates ambient light level, builds a depth-aware attenuation proxy by using the logarithmic color ratio, and computes a preliminary transmission map from an underwater image formation model, which is further improved by a total variation regularization. The radiance of the scenes is then reconstructed by model-based inversion, enhanced by multi-scale local contrast enhancement and Gray-World color balancing to improve the visual clarity, maintain structural details and restore natural color appearance. Extensive experiments are conducted on synthetic and real-world underwater benchmark datasets to evaluate the visual and quantitative performance of the proposed PA-JLCC framework. Specifically, the proposed approach achieves the reported Underwater Image Quality Measure (UIQM) and Underwater Color Image Quality Evaluation (UCIQE) results, which not only reflect improved perceptual image quality but also improved color fidelity and underwater contrast in various underwater environments. In addition to this, the computational complexity of the proposed algorithm is linear, O(N), where N denotes the number of pixels, making the framework computationally efficient for image enhancement applications. The efficiency and interpretability of the proposed approach make it applicable to underwater image enhancement systems.

Article.Title: Dietary inflammatory index in relation to metabolic health status, serum levels of brain-derived neurotrophic factor and adropin in Iranian adults
Article.Authors: Moradmand Z.; Shahdadian F.; Rouhani P.; Saneei P.
Article.Abstract: There was little evidence for the association of dietary inflammatory index (DII) and metabolic health status, and no evidence on DII and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and adropin. Thus, this study assessed the association between DII and metabolic unhealthy (MU), regarding the interactive roles of BDNF and adropin in Iranian adults. This observational study was conducted on 527 Iranian men and women living in Isfahan. Dietary intakes and DII were estimated by using a validated 168-item food frequency questionnaire. Anthropometric, blood pressure, and biochemical parameters were assessed using appropriate standard methods. The criteria defined by Wildman et al. were used to classify individuals into participants with and without MU. Mean age of participants was 42.66 years, and 224 of them (42.50%) were recognized as participants with MU. In the fully adjusted model, no significant association was observed between DII score and MU in the overall population or in normal-weight individuals; however, among participants with overweight or obesity, those in the third tertile of DII had significantly higher odds of MU compared with the first tertile (OR = 2.76; 95% CI: 1.16, 6.57). Furthermore, a positive association was found between DII tertiles and hyperglycemia (OR T3 vs. T1 = 3.41; 95% CI: 1.43, 8.17) and hypertriglyceridemia (OR T3 vs. T1 = 2.13; 95% CI: 1.06, 4.28). A nonsignificant association was observed between DII, BDNF, and adropin ( P > 0.05). In this adult population, a higher DII score was associated with a higher probability of MU in individuals with obesity or overweight. A higher DII score was associated with hyperglycemia and hypertriglyceridemia. No other remarkable association was found in the subgroup analysis or between DII score and BDNF, or adropin.

Article.Title: Reported performance differences on the ann-thyroid benchmark reflect class labelling rather than method choice
Article.Authors: Eray O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Machine-learning studies on the ann-thyroid benchmark routinely report near-perfect discrimination, yet the sources of that performance are rarely isolated and the benchmark’s own class labels are rarely questioned. We report a controlled audit of this benchmark, separating what a conventional pipeline contributes from what is inherited from the data. Ten classifiers were evaluated across ten stratified splits in a leakage-free pipeline. A 2 × 2 factorial ablation separated feature selection from class balancing; nine feature-selection methods and seven balancing strategies were compared; a parameter sweep tested the hybrid selector; and a simple threshold rule on TSH and TT4 served as a clinical baseline. Differences between methods were assessed by Friedman tests with Nemenyi post-hoc comparisons and by two one-sided tests against equivalence margins fixed before the tests were run. Class labels were verified against the hormone panel and, at record level, against the diagnosis codes distributed with the same archive. The UCI files do not name their classes, and the accompanying documentation describes a hyperfunction class the data do not contain; matching against the diagnosis codes distributed in the same archive yields 3597 one-to-one correspondences with no discordance, establishing three hypothyroid-spectrum strata (overt hypothyroid, subclinical hypothyroid, euthyroid) instead, and locating 89 diagnosed hyperthyroid records inside the majority class. A majority-class baseline reaches 92.6% accuracy at macro-F1 0.320, so accuracy is uninformative. The principal clinical gain, macro-specificity rising from 0.905 to 0.987, is attributable predominantly to class balancing rather than feature selection. Feature-selection methods span a ROC-AUC range of only 0.0018 and balancing strategies a macro-F1 range of 0.0098; Friedman tests detect a reproducible ordering in both comparisons, but every pairwise difference falls within an equivalence margin fixed before the tests were run, so the ordering is not clinically informative. Reporting ROC-AUC alone conceals this: the pipeline significantly reduces minority-class PR-AUC in five of ten classifiers while the corresponding ROC-AUC changes remain near 0.002. A three-line threshold rule whose two cutoffs are fitted on training folds attains macro-F1 0.885 in 0.2 s, comparable to tuned logistic regression; the fitted values converge on the data owners’ own documented cutoffs in all ten splits. On this benchmark the marginal value of algorithmic refinement is small and difficult to demonstrate; the labelling of the data warrants more scrutiny than the choice of method.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: hyperthyroidism; feature selection; data balancing; hypothyroidism; data leakage

Article.Title: Influence of particle size and flow conditions on retention in vuggy porous media
Article.Authors: Saeed M.; Khan H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigates the effect of particle size and flow conditions on particle retention in vuggy porous media by monitoring the changes in the rock porosity using temporal computed tomography (CT) scans during the injection of a glass bead suspension. Synthetic glass bead cores are fabricated by sintering glass beads to create a proxy core sample with known petrophysical properties. The core is vertically mounted in a dynamic core flooding setup which is placed inside a medical CT scanner, and fine-sized particles (40 and 125 $$\upmu $$ m diameter) are injected at different flow rates (40 and 60 cm 3 /min) and injected particle concentrations (0.5 and 1.0 wt%). Unlike previous studies that rely primarily on initial and final petrophysical characterization, this study systematically examines the coupled effects of flow rate, particle size, and particle concentration on the spatiotemporal evolution of particle retention in a controlled vuggy pore structure. A baseline CT scan is conducted on the core, and subsequent temporal scans are conducted to determine the evolution of porosity and the spatial distribution of the trapped particles. Results indicate that the injected particle size is the primary factor governing the porosity change of the system, with the larger injected particle size creating an external filter cake and resulting in $$\sim $$ 50% reduction in porosity at the inlet. The porosity loss is focused at the vug inlet, with the region before the vug exhibiting double the porosity loss of the region after the vug. A faster injection rate and higher injected particle concentration cause higher particle-particle collisions, resulting in porosity loss of up to 6% near the inlet. Retention is focused at the vug inlet at the high flow rate and at the vug outlet at the lower flow rate. The vug volume is observed to decrease continuously with time, with volume reduction of up to 3% observed. A lower injected particle concentration results in slower, and generally, lower total retention. The temporal CT observations reveal that particle retention and the associated pore-space alteration are highly non-uniform and evolve dynamically with injection conditions, demonstrating the importance of spatially and temporally resolved characterization for understanding particle transport in heterogeneous vuggy media. Furthermore, sample-to-sample variability was observed, most notably in the inlet porosity in sample 40-1.0-60, highlighting the variability that can occur even under controlled experimental conditions.

Article.Title: Dynamic volatolomic profiling reveals treatment-induced metabolic state transitions during radiosensitization in colorectal cancer
Article.Authors: Youssef O.; Mshaly M.; Soliman M.; Awaad A.; Mohamed E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Radiotherapy resistance remains a major challenge in colorectal cancer (CRC), necessitating strategies that not only enhance radiosensitivity but also enable real-time monitoring of treatment-associated biological responses. Here, we present an integrated systems-level framework combining network pharmacology, in silico target analysis, in vitro validation, and dynamic volatolomic profiling to investigate metabolic adaptations associated with curcumin-mediated radiosensitization. Network-based analyses identified curcumin as a multi-target modulator of key radiation-response pathways, including PI3K/Akt, EGFR, STAT3, and apoptosis-related signaling. Functional validation in Caco-2 cells demonstrated enhanced radiosensitivity following curcumin treatment, evidenced by increased radiation-induced cytotoxicity and apoptosis, together with reduced clonogenic survival and migratory capacity. Dynamic volatolomic profiling using an electronic nose (eNose) revealed that treatment-associated metabolic changes could be continuously monitored through volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions. Time-resolved trajectory analysis, vector-field modeling, Hidden Markov Model state inference, and Markov transition analysis demonstrated that VOC signatures encode dynamic metabolic-state evolution and probabilistic state transitions during treatment response. Curcumin reduced baseline VOC emissions, whereas irradiation induced dose-dependent metabolic perturbations associated with nonlinear VOC trajectories. Combined treatment generated distinct state-dependent VOC signatures consistent with enhanced metabolic reprogramming during radiosensitization. By integrating molecular signaling, cellular phenotypes, and dynamic VOC outputs, this study extends volatolomics beyond conventional classification-based applications and establishes a systems-level framework for monitoring treatment-induced metabolic-state transitions. These findings support the potential of eNose-based volatolomics as a non-invasive platform for real-time assessment of radiosensitization and therapeutic response in CRC.

Article.Title: Multi‑PTM landscape of four lysine acylations at shared residues in oral squamous cell carcinoma
Article.Authors: Tao X.; Huang G.; Li L.; Li Z.; Zeng Z.; Qin Y.; Tang D.; Dai Y.; Yan Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Posttranslational modifications (PTMs) are central regulators of cellular signaling and play critical roles in cancer biology. While individual PTMs have been implicated in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), the crosstalk and coregulatory patterns among different PTM types in this malignancy remain largely unexplored. Integrated proteomic analysis via liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) was performed to profile four lysine acylations (2-hydroxyisobutyrylation (Khib), crotonylation (Kcr), acetylation (Kac), and malonylation (Kma)) in OSCC tissues and matched adjacent tissues. Proteins harboring at least one differentially modified peptide or site were defined as differentially modified proteins (DMPs) and subsequently subjected to functional enrichment analysis via Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway enrichment. Protein protein interaction (PPI) networks were constructed via STRING and Cytoscape to screen hub modified proteins, and Spearman correlation analysis was applied to evaluate the regulatory relationships among the four PTMs. Eighty proteins were identified as being commonly modified by at least three of the studied PTMs. KEGG pathway analysis, which maps proteins to pre-defined pathway categories, indicated that these DMPs were annotated to pathways related to Salmonella infection, motor proteins, focal adhesion, and proteoglycans in cancer. A key finding was the identification of specific lysine residues that were found to be modified by multiple PTM types across samples. Notably, the modification levels of Khib, Kcr, and Kac at the FLNA-K837 and DCN-K164 site differed between OSCC tissues and adjacent tissues ( P < 0.05). This study describes the co-modification patterns among multiple PTMs in OSCC. These combinatorial modifications may contribute to regulating key metabolic and signaling pathways. These preliminary observations warrant validation in larger cohorts and functional studies. The identified PTM sites may serve as candidates for further investigation as potential biomarkers. These findings identify key PTM site hubs such as FLNA and DCN, whose site‑specific acylation patterns show alterations in OSCC. Further studies are needed to determine whether these modifications have clinical utility. The current findings should be considered hypothesis-generating rather than definitive.

Article.Title: Integrated melissopalynological and phenolic profiling reveals antioxidant and antimicrobial potential of Turkish honeys
Article.Authors: Sahin H.; Bektas E.; Sahin P.; Ozkok Saban A.; Inan Bektas K.; Egrioglu E.
Article.Abstract: This study provides a comprehensive characterization of 23 Turkish honey samples through an integrated approach involving melissopalynological, chemical, antioxidant, and antimicrobial analyses. Fourteen phenolic compounds were quantified by HPLC, while total phenolic content (TPC), FRAP, and DPPH radical-scavenging assays were used to assess antioxidant-related properties. Antimicrobial activity was evaluated against six pathogenic microorganisms using minimum inhibitory concentration values. To explore multivariate patterns, the dataset was standardized using Z-score normalization and subjected to two-way hierarchical clustering using Euclidean distance and average linkage, visualized through a Viridis-scaled heatmap. The integrated analysis revealed distinct sample groupings and co-distribution patterns among phenolic constituents, antioxidant-related parameters, and antimicrobial MIC profiles, demonstrating substantial compositional and bioactivity heterogeneity among the studied honeys. Overall, this integrated approach provides a robust framework for characterizing Turkish honey diversity and underscores the importance of botanical origin in shaping phenolic composition and bioactivity.

Article.Title: A small-area and power-efficient reversible full adder based on a two-transistor multiplexer applicable in image addition
Article.Authors: Deymad S.; Parvanehnezhad Shirazian S.; Heydarian S.; Shiri N.
Article.Abstract: This study presents an innovative 10-transistor reversible full adder (FA) architecture featuring two garbage outputs (GOs) and no constant inputs (CIs). The design integrates three reversible logic gates across two operational stages, implemented using the gate diffusion input (GDI) methodology. Specifically, it employs two Feynman gates alongside a newly developed GDI-based reversible multiplexer (R-MUX-GDI) to produce the Sum and Carry-out (C out ) signals. The 3 × 3 multiplexer, with two GOs and only two transistors, substantially minimizes the circuit’s footprint. The input configuration is strategically designed to limit excessive GOs. When incorporated into a ripple carry adder (RCA) for image processing, the proposed FA demonstrates exceptional performance in terms of area efficiency, power consumption, and output image quality. Simulations conducted using 32 nm carbon nanotube field-effect transistor (CNTFET) technology at a 0.9 V supply voltage (V DD ) reveal that the proposed circuit achieves a power consumption of 1.0388 µW, which is minimal compared to its counterpart. The power delay product (PDP) of the FA is 6.744 aJ, which makes it a candidate for low-power reversible computing and room-temperature quantum-adjacent control circuitry. Furthermore, implementing the FA in 4-bit, 8-bit, 16-bit, and 32-bit ripple carry adder (RCA) configurations requires 48, 96, 192, and 384 transistors, respectively, underscoring its substantial area savings and effective image processing capabilities.

Article.Title: EEG-based Alzheimer’s disease detection using two-branch multi-scale deep learning with integrated gradients-guided channel selection
Article.Authors: Shin J.; Hassan N.; Miah A.; Nishimura S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is critical for timely intervention and clinical monitoring. Electroencephalography (EEG) offers a non-invasive, low-cost, and portable alternative to neuroimaging. However, existing traditional and deep learning (DL)-based methods often face challenges related to computational cost, representational complexity, and practical deployment. In this work, we propose Fused-MSCA-2B, a two-branch multi-scale channel-attentive 1D convolutional neural network (CNN) for EEG-based AD detection. The model processes broadband multichannel EEG directly as temporal sequences and combines multi-scale temporal convolution, residual learning, squeeze-and-excitation channel attention, and feature-level branch fusion. Specifically, Branch A uses MSCA blocks with kernel configurations $$(3,5,9)$$ and $$(3,5,7)$$ to capture local and medium-range temporal dependencies, whereas Branch B uses $$(5,9,15)$$ and $$(3,5,9)$$ to capture broader and higher-level temporal patterns. The branch-level embeddings are fused and passed through dense classification layers to generate AD/HC posterior probabilities. A key component of the proposed model is an explainable AI-guided reduced-channel selection strategy. Integrated Gradients (IG) is used to rank EEG channel relevance from validation data, enabling the EEG montage to be reduced from 19 to 12 channels. We evaluated the proposed model using two benchmark datasets. The IG-guided Top-12 configuration achieved 98.60% ± 1.18% recording-level accuracy while reducing the EEG montage from 19 to 12 channels. As a supporting ablation analysis, the Fixed Top-12 configuration achieved 98.40% ± 0.73% accuracy, further confirming the effectiveness of the IG-guided reduced-channel selection strategy. The results demonstrate that the proposed XAI-guided Fused-MSCA-2B framework supports robust EEG-based AD detection with a compact and practical electrode configuration, showing strong performance with reduced channel sets.

Article.Title: Emotional valence and musical factors associated with music-evoked memories in Alzheimer’s disease
Article.Authors: Salakka I.; Kaila L.; Toiviainen P.; Särkämö T.; Pitkäniemi A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Music is a powerful tool for evoking emotions and memories in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and is commonly used in dementia care. In healthy older adults, music-evoked memories vary depending on the experienced valence (pleasant vs. unpleasant) of songs, show a reminiscence bump (RB) for mid-childhood/adolescence, and are linked to certain musical features (e.g. rhythm). However, little is known how these factors change from healthy ageing to advanced AD. This study combined ratings of emotional valence, familiarity, and autobiographical salience and Music Information Retrieval (MIR) features from 70 excerpts of traditional folk and popular songs from the 1950–1970 s. Participants included healthy older adults ( n = 40) and persons with mild ( n = 29) and moderate/severe ( n = 32) dementia. Compared to healthy older adults, AD groups showed lower familiarity and autobiographical salience but comparable valence. Relationships between valence and familiarity and autobiographical salience became increasingly linear with advancing AD. The RB peaked earlier in childhood as disease severity increased. Across groups, lower harmonic complexity predicted higher autobiographical salience and weaker pulse predicted higher familiarity, with stronger valence dependency in AD. These findings highlight how music-evoked memories change along the AD continuum and may support individualizing music interventions in dementia care.

Article.Title: Risk propagation in counter-terrorism security at large-scale events
Article.Authors: Fu L.; Li X.; Wang X.; Zhao B.; Chen T.
Article.Abstract: The complex interactions among human and organizational factors within the counter-terrorism security system at large-scale events drive risk propagation. This study integrates association rule mining, link prediction, directed weighted network theory, and a modified SIR model to explore risk propagation mechanisms from both structural and dynamic perspectives. The factor interaction network is sparse and modular, with small-world properties, enabling rapid propagation of local perturbations. Factors associated with the event organizer and external environment serve as primary risk sources, playing critical roles in both initiating and containing propagation. Factors from the temporary headquarters, venue manager, customs and border protection, dangerous goods administration, police, intelligence, and network operations department exert moderate influence, while those from the on-site security department exhibit limited influence on propagation dynamics. This study provides a propagation-aware foundation for designing terrorism risk mitigation strategies.

Article.Title: Physicians’ perspectives on the impact of echocardiographic feedback: a qualitative interview study
Article.Authors: Behzadi A.; Tasdighi H.; Kiani M.; Fatahpour A.
Article.Abstract: Echocardiography is a widely used non-invasive imaging modality central to diagnosing and monitoring heart failure, valvular disease, congenital heart disease, and cardiomyopathy. However, inappropriate requests, variability in reporting quality, and limited follow-up of diagnostic performance remain concerns, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Audit and feedback is an established strategy for improving professional practice, but its application in echocardiography remains underdeveloped. This study aimed to explore physicians’ perspectives on how the impact of echocardiographic feedback on clinicians can be assessed in Iran. A qualitative study was conducted using semi-structured interviews with an inductive approach and reflexive thematic analysis, following Braun and Clarke’s six-phase framework. From August 2022 to September 2023, 30 semi-structured interviews were conducted with purposively sampled participants, including cardiologists, university faculty in statistics, biostatistics, and health sciences, health insurance experts, and physicians working in health insurance organizations and research centers. The average interview duration was 49 min. Data saturation was reached after interview 27. Transcripts were coded by two independent researchers using MAXQDA 20 software. Trustworthiness was ensured using Lincoln and Guba’s criteria. The analysis generated five main themes and twelve subthemes: (1) indications for performing echocardiography; (2) diagnosing a patient’s need for echocardiography; (3) components of a complete echocardiography report; (4) sample selection and control group; and (5) data recording and analysis method. Participants emphasized the importance of guideline-based indications, standardized reporting, a before-and-after design with a control group, and the Difference-in-Differences (DID) technique for evaluating feedback. A cross-cutting finding regarding the role of body habitus and thoracic morphology in echocardiographic interpretation was integrated into the framework. The findings provide a comprehensive qualitative basis for a proposed framework for future quantitative evaluation of echocardiographic feedback. Future studies should operationalize these domains into valid and reliable indicators and prospectively evaluate whether feedback can improve the appropriateness, quality, and consistency of echocardiographic practice.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: audit and feedback; difference-in-differences; echocardiography; low- and middle-income countries; Iran; physicians' perspectives

Article.Title: Efficient fully convolutional network for real-time semantic segmentation
Article.Authors: Cărunta C.; Popa C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Considering the increased interest for deploying semantic segmentation models in real-world applications, including autonomous driving, robotics, video surveillance, researchers are developing ultra-lightweight segmentation frameworks, comprising approximately 1 million trainable parameters. Therefore, in this study, we propose an efficient convolutional segmentation network, termed as ECSNet, which achieves a good trade-off between segmentation accuracy, inference speed, computational cost, and parameter count. Particularly, we design the dilated convolutional feature module (DCFM), that is integrated within the encoder structure, and it effectively captures the local details and the global information. The decoder design is lightweight, comprising group convolutional layers, concatenation operation, upsampling operation, and the segmentation head, without any additional context extractor module. Comprehensive experiments are conducted on two autonomous driving datasets, namely Cityscapes and CamVid, demonstrating that the proposed framework attains an effective accuracy-speed trade-off. With only 1.06M parameters, ECSNet achieves $$70.98\%$$ mIoU and $$73.45\%$$ mIoU at an inference speed of 294.22 FPS and 234.48 FPS on the Cityscapes and CamVid test sets, respectively.

Article.Title: Relation of serum electrolytes and left ventricular functions in patients with STEMI undergoing primary PCI
Article.Authors: Bastam L.; Zare F.; Haddadi H.; Roshani S.; Naghdian M.; Fayazi S.; Alizadeh M.; Amirikar F.; Separham A.; Javanshir E.; Banisefid E.
Article.Abstract: Electrolyte disturbances are common in STEMI patients. However, the association between admission serum electrolyte levels and echocardiographic findings after primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PPCI) remains incompletely understood. This study investigated the relationship between serum electrolyte levels, echocardiographic parameters, angiographic findings, and ST-segment resolution (STR) in patients with first anterior STEMI. In this observational study, 138 patients with first anterior STEMI undergoing PPCI were enrolled. Admission serum sodium, potassium, magnesium, total calcium, and ionized calcium levels were measured. Before hospital discharge, transthoracic echocardiography was performed to evaluate left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), regional wall motion abnormality index (RWMAI), and left ventricular end-systolic volume index (LVESVI). Angiographic findings and STR were also assessed. Multivariable logistic regression was performed after adjustment for age and sex. Results at an exploratory level, lower serum potassium was associated in age- and sex-adjusted analyses with reduced LVEF (aOR = 2.984, 95% CI: 1.285–6.926; P = 0.011) and increased RWMAI (OR = 3.103, 95% CI: 1.338–7.196; P = 0.008); and patients with ionized calcium ≥ 1.05 mmol/L demonstrated significantly greater STR than those with lower levels ( P = 0.028). Serum sodium, magnesium, total calcium, and ionized calcium were not significantly associated with echocardiographic parameters. After Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons, none of the observed associations remained statistically significant. Admission lower serum potassium is suggested to be associated with impaired left ventricular systolic function and more extensive RWMAI in patients with first anterior STEMI undergoing PPCI. However, these associations should be considered exploratory, particularly given the multiple electrolyte-outcome comparisons and the lack of statistical significance after Bonferroni correction.

Article.Title: Understandability and implementability of enterostomy care short Chinese videos on TikTok and Kwai: cross-sectional content analysis study
Article.Authors: Chen C.; Deng X.; Xu A.; Luo S.; Huang Q.; Ma X.; Xie L.
Article.Abstract: As one of the most prevalent malignant tumours of the digestive tract, colorectal cancer poses a serious threat to human health. While enterostomy procedures offer new hope for colorectal cancer patients, they also present new challenges to their ability to manage enterostomy care. Health information on enterostomy care is widely disseminated through short-video platforms such as TikTok and Kwai, which are popular for their strong dissemination power and interactive advantages. However, the understandability and implementability of enterostomy care short videos on these platforms had not been evaluated. This study evaluated the understandability and implementability of Chinese-language short videos on TikTok and Kwai about enterostomy care. From February to April 2025, we used the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Audiovisual Materials (PEMAT-A/V) to evaluate the understandability and implementability of 92 Chinese enterostomy care short videos (41 on TikTok and 51 on Kwai). We employed the Kruskal-Wallis H test, Mann-Whitney U test, and Spearman correlation analysis to explore factors potentially influencing comprehensibility and implementability. The results of the PEMAT-A/V evaluation showed that short videos on TikTok and Kwai about enterostomy care were more understandable (85.71 (71.76, 100.00) points) but poorer in implementability (66.67 (33.33, 66.67) points). Kwai was better than TikTok in terms of understandability and implementability. Short videos published by for-profit organisations (100.00 (85.71, 100.00) points), featuring live demonstrations (90.00 (85.71, 100.00) points), patient appearances (100.00 (85.71, 100.00) points), and background music (86.61 (81.37, 100.00) points) demonstrated superior understandability ( P < 0.05). Short videos featuring the patients themselves or nurses/enterostomy therapists/caregivers were more implementable ( P < 0.05). The understandability of enterostomy care short videos on TikTok and Kwai was generally satisfactory, though their implementability was suboptimal. To address issues identified during the quality assessment, targeted improvement strategies are proposed from the perspectives of creators and social media platforms. These aim to enhance both the understandability and implementability of enterostomy care short videos, thereby increasing their utility for audiences and providing a reference for creating health science popularisation short videos.

Article.Title: Multimodal urban park service accessibility and spatial distributional inequality through a multiscale assessment
Article.Authors: Wu P.; Liu M.; Wang Z.; Miao X.
Article.Abstract: Urban park planning requires attention to both service accessibility and its spatial distribution. This study assessed 420 parks and 488 residential communities in Nanjing using Multi-G3SFCA, population-weighted Gini coefficients, sensitivity analysis, and spatially validated RF–SHAP. Travel impedance was calibrated using 320 route records obtained from the Amap Route Planning API. Mean Overall accessibility was 17.3005 hm² per 100 persons, with a Gini coefficient of 0.4931. Comprehensive parks contributed 87.67% of mean Overall accessibility, whereas Community parks had the lowest mean accessibility and the highest Gini coefficient of 0.9603. Under the baseline 10-min threshold, 32 communities, representing 6.56% of the sample and 5.83% of estimated residential demand, had zero Community park accessibility. Overall accessibility rankings and the identification of low-accessibility communities remained comparatively stable under changes in travel speeds, service thresholds, modal weights, population demand, and entrance-allocation rules. RF achieved an R 2 of 0.5701 under conventional ten-fold validation and 0.2016 under leave-one-district-out validation, indicating weaker transferability to districts excluded from model training. Spatially cross-fitted SHAP identified older-adult proportion and district-level income context as the leading predictors.

Article.Title: Observation-contract auditing for valid modality comparison in robot manipulation benchmarks
Article.Authors: He Y.; Wang Q.; Xu J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Robot manipulation benchmarks compare observation modalities such as low-dimensional state, red-green-blue (RGB) images, and point clouds to guide policy design, yet are valid only when each pathway delivers semantically identical state. We show that switching observation pathways silently alters the state content, dropping fields and re-sorting dictionary keys without error or warning, a failure mode we call observation-contract mismatch. We formalize the observation contract as the ordered list of state fields a pathway delivers, define a contract-diff operator, and give a four-step audit that detects mismatches from source code before training. Static analysis of ManiSkill3, RLBench, and the Diffusion Policy robomimic integration shows each silently loses 31 to 53 percent of its observable state. Under one matched protocol the state-only control (0.606 mean success) matches a default-pathway Diffusion Policy (0.600) and beats a retrained action chunking transformer (ACT) baseline (0.400), since the state pathway’s contract is already complete. A contract-controlled factorial crossing state completeness with point-cloud availability then shows that removing object geometry collapses mean success from 0.606 to 0.016, while point clouds neither rescue it nor help under full state. Within the tested regime the state contract dominates policy success, making observation-contract auditing a prerequisite for credible modality comparison
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: RLBench; RGB images; modality comparison; diffusion policy; point clouds; static analysis

Article.Title: Deformation and energy absorption mechanisms in steel/CFRP hybrid square tubes under axial compression
Article.Authors: Yang C.; Yang J.; Huo Y.; Zhao Y.
Article.Abstract: Steel/carbon fiber-reinforced plastic (CFRP) hybrid square tubes are promising lightweight energy-absorbing members for railway crashworthy structures, but their crushing response depends strongly on material arrangement, thickness distribution and fiber orientation. This study investigates the axial crushing behavior and energy absorption mechanisms of Q345 steel/T300 CFRP hybrid square tubes under quasi-static compression. Material tests were first conducted to obtain the mechanical properties of Q345 steel and T300 CFRP. Quasi-static compression tests were then performed on standalone steel tubes, standalone CFRP tubes and steel/CFRP hybrid tubes with different material arrangements. A finite element model was established and validated against the experimental results, with a maximum deviation of 5.91% in the main crashworthiness indicators. The results show that placing CFRP inside the steel tube improves interfacial constraint, suppresses premature outward tearing and promotes more stable cooperative deformation. Compared with the C1S1 configuration, the S1C1 configuration exhibits higher energy absorption and more favorable crushing stability. Increasing the steel-to-CFRP thickness ratio from 0.5 to 2.0 increases the total energy absorption from 3458.5 J to 5091.8 J, but decreases the specific energy absorption from 15.35 J/g to 14.28 J/g. The CFRP layup angle also affects crushing performance: small layup angles provide limited energy-dissipation contribution, whereas changes beyond approximately 50° have only marginal influence on the deformation mode and energy absorption. These findings provide design guidance for steel/CFRP hybrid square tubes used in train front-end energy-absorbing structures and other space-constrained crashworthy components.

Article.Title: Cellulose-based hydrogels derived from wastepaper for slow release of urea in chilli pepper cultivation
Article.Authors: Mohamed B.; Chin S.; Wasli M.
Article.Abstract: Conventional fertilizers often release nutrients too rapidly, leading to nutrient leaching, reduced fertilization efficiency, and environmental pollution of nearby water sources. To address this challenge, this study developed a slow-release urea system using hydrogels synthesized from recycled wastepaper. Cellulose fibers derived from wastepaper were blended with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) as a network-forming component, carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) as a binder, and epichlorohydrin (ECH) as a crosslinking agent to prepare cellulose-based hydrogels. Among the tested formulations, the cellulose/CMC/PVA hydrogel with a 3:3:4 ratio (CCP334) showed the highest swelling capacity and was selected for urea loading studies. Urea, used as a model fertilizer, was incorporated at different concentrations to determine the optimal loading conditions. The cellulose hydrogel exhibited a maximum loading capacity of 54.10% at 2.5% urea concentration. Release studies conducted in distilled water, topsoil, and coco peat demonstrated a sustained nutrient delivery: 86.25% release in water (10 days), 63.13% in coco peat (20 days), and 86.88% in topsoil (60 days). The release behavior followed the Korsmeyer–Peppas model with n values < 0.45, indicating Fickian diffusion.

Article.Title: Thermal descriptor extraction through reciprocal residual attention learning for construction worker unsafe condition detection and localization
Article.Authors: Choi J.; M S.; Preethaa K.; Natarajan Y.; Mi Y.
Article.Abstract: Unsafe worker actions in elevated construction environments remain a leading cause of occupational accidents, particularly under low-visibility and complex environmental conditions where conventional RGB-based monitoring systems exhibit limited robustness. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel Thermal Context-Guided Dual-path Reciprocal Network (TCDRNet) for intelligent detection of unsafe thermal actions. Initially, a novel Thermal Adaptive Gradient (TAG) preprocessing filter is introduced to enhance thermal image quality via local normalisation, gradient-based thermal boundary enhancement, adaptive thermal weighting, feature amplification, and edge-preserving smoothing. The generated TAG images are subsequently processed utilising the proposed TCDRNet, which incorporates a Cross Stage Partial Dual-path Reciprocal Network (CSPDRNet) backbone integrated with Thermal Global Descriptor Extraction (TGDE), Reciprocal Attention Generation (RAG), and Residual Reciprocal Fusion (RRF) modules to facilitate reciprocal thermal feature learning. Furthermore, Spatial Pyramid Pooling (SPP) is employed for multi-scale contextual extraction. Concurrently, the Path Aggregation Network (PANet) performs hierarchical feature aggregation to generate low-level localisation features, mid-level boundary information, and high-level semantic representations. Finally, a Thermal Context-Aware Residual Attention (TAR) module is introduced to refine the multi-scale features via channel attention, spatial attention, and residual fusion, thereby emphasising discriminative unsafe regions. Experimental evaluation on a thermal unsafe action dataset comprising no-helmet, no-shoes, mobile-phone utilisation, safe and unsafe posture classes demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework. TCDRNet achieves an accuracy of 96.60%, precision of 96.41%, and recall of 95.96%, outperforming several state-of-the-art models.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: construction worker safety; occupational accident prevention

Article.Title: Comparative dielectric and physicochemical assessment of surfactant-free TiO2 and SiO2 nanofluids for high voltage transformer mineral oil
Article.Authors: Alshammari M.; Omar A.; Eltlhawy B.; Waly H.; Qenawy S.
Article.Abstract: This study compares semiconductive TiO 2 and insulating SiO 2 nanoparticles as separate, surfactant-free additives to the same transformer mineral oil under a matched preparation and testing framework. The novelty is not the first use of nanofluids, but the controlled head-to-head evaluation of two electronically distinct oxide classes while minimizing the protocol differences that commonly prevent direct comparison across published studies. Five low loadings (0.01–0.10 wt%) were screened for kinematic viscosity, moisture content, and room-temperature AC breakdown voltage; relative permittivity and DC conductivity were additionally characterized from 30 °C to 90 °C. TiO 2 produced the largest measured AC breakdown improvement, 22.16% at 0.10 wt%, whereas SiO 2 reached its maximum improvement, 15.00%, at only 0.01 wt%. At 0.10 wt%, TiO 2 also produced a larger viscosity and DC-conductivity penalty than SiO 2 , revealing a clear performance trade-off between dielectric strengthening and charge transport. The results therefore provide a comparative concentration-selection map: semiconductive TiO 2 favors higher-loading breakdown enhancement, while insulating SiO 2 achieves its optimum response at trace loading with a smaller conductivity increase. These conclusions are restricted to the investigated concentration and test windows; quantitative long-term stability, temperature-dependent breakdown, thermal/oxidation performance, and oil-paper ageing remain necessary before transformer implementation.

Article.Title: Synergistic efficacy of chitosan nanoparticles and salicylic acid in mitigating charcoal rot (Macrophomina phaseolina) in soybean
Article.Authors: Yagoubi A.; Moosawi-Jorf S.; Safaie N.; Kazemi R.; Fathi-Qarachal J.
Article.Abstract: Macrophomina phaseolina is a devastating fungal pathogen of soybean, causing charcoal rot and resulting in significant reductions in both yield and grain quality. Conventional control approaches are limited by environmental concerns and the development of fungal resistance, necessitating the development of biocompatible, sustainable alternatives. This study evaluated the individual and interactive efficacy of chitosan nanoparticles (CNPs) and salicylic acid (SA) in managing M. phaseolina infection. CNPs exhibit strong antifungal activity and enhance plant basal immunity, whereas SA acts as a signaling molecule to activate defense responses. Two soybean cultivars, Golestan and Saba, were evaluated under greenhouse conditions using a randomized complete block design. Foliar applications of CNPs, SA, or their combination were administered 72 h before fungal inoculation. CNPs were synthesized and fully characterized for particle size, crystal structure, and FTIR spectra, and their in vitro inhibitory concentration against M. phaseolina was established. Morphological and physiological parameters, including fresh/dry biomass, plant height, greenness index, and the activities of peroxidase and polyphenol oxidase, were comprehensively assessed. Enzyme assays revealed significantly higher peroxidase and polyphenol oxidase activities 72 h after inoculation in treated plants compared to the control. Three weeks post-inoculation, treated plants showed increased shoot and root biomass and plant height, alongside reduced disease severity. Importantly, the optimal CNPs–SA combination for disease suppression differed between cultivars, with 100 mg L⁻¹ CNPs + 250 mg L⁻¹SA being most effective in Saba and 250 mg L⁻¹ CNPs + 100 mg L⁻¹ SA in Golestan. Both individual and combined applications of CNPs and SA significantly suppressed fungal growth and enhanced soybean resistance. These results indicate that CNP- and SA-based treatments offer a sustainable, safe, and effective strategy for controlling charcoal rot in soybean.

Article.Title: Response-surface optimization of high-performance GO-PET-PEG forward osmosis membranes for bentazone removal
Article.Authors: Sarlak M.; Shirzad-Siboni M.; Mohagheghian A.; Saeedi-Jurkuyeh A.
Article.Abstract: In this work, a single-layer forward osmosis (FO) nanocomposite membrane was developed and tested for bentazone removal from aqueous systems. Unlike conventional dual-layer thin-film composite membranes, this architecture, incorporating graphene oxide (GO) as a nanofiller and polyethylene glycol (PEG) as a pore-forming agent in a recycled PET matrix, eliminates interfacial defects between layers while simplifying fabrication. The membrane was prepared with recycled polyethylene terephthalate (PET, 16.5 wt%), PEG-400 (4 wt%), and N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP, 79 wt%), with 0.5 wt% GO added to enhance hydrophilicity, mechanical strength, and water transport. The homogeneous solution was processed via phase inversion to yield the optimized GO–PET–PEG membrane, showing FO water flux of 35.8 L m −2 h −1 (0.4 M NaCl draw solution), water permeability (A) of 4.04 L m −2 h −1 bar −1 (RO mode), salt permeability (B) of 1.00 ± 0.11 L m −2 h −1 , and RSF of 1.14 ± 0.08 g m −2 h −1 . Structural characterization was performed via FTIR, XRD, FE-SEM, EDX-MAP, AFM, and contact angle measurement, with conditions optimized using RSM. Effects of purge gases, hydrogen peroxide, organic compound type, anions, and membrane reusability were investigated. Under optimal conditions (pH = 7, bentazone = 25 mg/L, NaCl = 0.4 M, flow rate = 0.3 L/min, time = 35 min, temperature = 20 °C), 99.9% bentazone removal was achieved. For drinking water, efficiency reached 91.7%, reflecting the influence of other anions. Daphnia magna toxicity testing indicated a significant reduction in toxicity after treatment under the investigated conditions, supporting further evaluation of the environmental compatibility of the FO process. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of the GO-PET-PEG membrane for bentazone removal under the investigated laboratory conditions.

Article.Title: Optimized machine learning approach for intelligent dust contamination prediction in solar photovoltaic systems
Article.Authors: Sairaj K.; Pasi D.; Sheela M.; O.V. G.
Article.Abstract: Solar photovoltaic systems suffer significant losses in their performance due to contamination by dust, bird droppings and other pollutants, resulting in reduced power output and greater regular maintenance requirements. Thus, the key requirement for the proper functioning of a PV system is correct prediction of contamination which allows performing timely maintenance for better working of the PV system. In this paper, an approach based on the combination of machine learning and particle swarm optimization presented with the aim to predict contamination conditions in a solar PV system. A thorough validation of the proposed model done using SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost, CatBoost, PSO-SVM, PSO-RF, PSO-XGBoost and CNN-PSO models. The methodology consists of feature preparation and implementation followed by machine learning models that compared in terms of performance features. Among all the assessed models, the CatBoost model showed the best performance with a prediction accuracy of 99.43%.The findings demonstrate the potential of ensemble-based ML, particularly CatBoost, for intelligent PV contamination monitoring and predictive maintenance, enabling earlier identification of contamination conditions and supporting improved energy-generation performance and reduced operational losses.

Article.Title: Association of phubbing with fear of childbirth and early maternal–infant bonding: a prospective observational study
Article.Authors: Soysal C.; Başarı H.; Taşçı Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study aimed to evaluate the associations of phubbing with fear of childbirth and early maternal–infant bonding among term pregnant women who delivered vaginally. This single-center prospective observational study included 75 women with term pregnancies (37–42 weeks) who delivered vaginally. The Wijma Delivery Expectancy/Experience Questionnaire-A (W-DEQ A) and Generic Scale of Phubbing (GSP) were administered before active labor, and the Mother-to-Infant Bonding Scale (MIBS) was completed on postpartum day 2. MIBS items were recoded so that higher scores indicated more favorable bonding. Associations were assessed using Spearman correlation and multiple linear regression with heteroskedasticity-consistent HC3 standard errors. The mean age was 27.1 ± 4.3 years. Phubbing was negatively correlated with the recoded MIBS total score ( ρ =− 0.543, p < 0.001) and positively correlated with W-DEQ score ( ρ = 0.821, p < 0.001). In the adjusted bonding model, higher phubbing remained independently associated with lower MIBS scores (B = − 0.254, β = − 0.704, p < 0.001), whereas age, multiparity, BMI, and W-DEQ score were not significant. The model explained 49.9% of the variance in MIBS scores. In the fear-of-childbirth model, higher phubbing scores remained independently associated with higher W-DEQ scores (B = 1.153, β = 0.674, p < 0.001). Multiparous women had lower W-DEQ scores than nulliparous women (B = − 8.036, β = − 0.203, p = 0.035), whereas age and BMI were not statistically significant. The revised model explained 58.2% of the variance in W-DEQ scores. In this preliminary observational study, higher phubbing was associated with greater fear of childbirth and less favorable very early postpartum maternal–infant bonding. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger longitudinal studies with later postpartum assessments before clinical implications can be established.

Article.Title: Genotype-dependent growth and essential oil responses of Salvia officinalis under combined elevated CO2 and heat stress
Article.Authors: Tursun A.
Article.Abstract: Global climate change involves simultaneous increases in atmospheric CO 2 concentration and temperature, imposing complex constraints on plant performance. This study examined the interactive effects of elevated CO 2 (400–1000 ppm) and temperature (26/16, 29/19, and 32/22 °C day/night) on growth, essential oil yield, and chemical composition of four Salvia officinalis genotypes. A significant CO 2 × temperature × genotype interaction was detected for growth parameters ( P < 0.05) and essential oil ratio ( P < 0.05), revealing that CO 2 induced growth stimulation was strongly modulated by thermal conditions. Elevated CO 2 enhanced biomass and oil yield under moderate temperatures, whereas heat stress (32/22 °C) markedly constrained this fertilization effect, particularly in the thermosensitive genotype A1. In contrast, genotypes A3 and A4 maintained relatively stable biomass and metabolite production, indicating superior phenotypic plasticity and metabolic buffering capacity. Climate stress also induced substantial shifts in essential oil composition, with oxygenated monoterpenes showing pronounced genotype-dependent sensitivity to temperature × CO 2 interactions. Multivariate analyses confirmed that temperature was the primary driver of chemical divergence, while genotype determined overall chemotype stability. These findings suggest that genotype-specific differences in growth stability and chemical composition under combined CO 2 and heat stress reflect differential capacity for physiological adaptation, highlighting genotype selection as a key strategy for sustaining both productivity and phytochemical integrity under future warming scenarios.

Article.Title: Academic performance of large language models across an undergraduate physiotherapy curriculum: a subset analysis
Article.Authors: Acar A.; Öztürk S.; Çağrı Arslan D.; Alaca N.
Article.Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in physiotherapy for information retrieval, educational support, and assistance in assessment and rehabilitation-related decision-making. Although their performance has often been evaluated using isolated examinations or domain-specific question sets, less is known about how these models perform across the breadth of an undergraduate physiotherapy curriculum. This study examined LLM performance using a curriculum-based academic assessment framework reflecting how theoretical knowledge is formally evaluated in physiotherapy education. Written exams from a subset of 34 of 54 eligible courses within an undergraduate Physiotherapy and Rehabilitation program were analyzed. Two LLMs, GPT-5.0 and Claude 4.5 Sonnet, were queried using a standardized zero-shot prompting approach, and responses were graded according to official answer keys and institutional criteria. Course-level examination scores, letter grades, and cumulative grade point averages were calculated for standardized comparison. Under the institutional grading system, both models achieved passing-level performance, with GPT-5.0 reaching a mean total score of 85.7 ± 10.4 (GPA-equivalent: 3.28/4.00) and Claude 4.5 Sonnet a mean total score of 87.3 ± 11.2 (GPA-equivalent: 3.39/4.00), both satisfying the institutional graduation threshold; Claude 4.5 Sonnet showed modestly but significantly higher overall performance. Both models performed better in basic science courses than in clinically oriented courses. These findings suggest that LLMs perform well on knowledge-based assessments in undergraduate physiotherapy education, while revealing relative limitations in clinically integrated domains.

Article.Title: Eriocitrin promotes apoptosis and inhibits invasion and proliferation of androgen-independent prostate cancer via the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway
Article.Authors: Liu G.; Wang X.; Yang Y.; Gui D.; Zhang T.; Liang C.
Article.Abstract: Androgen-independent prostate cancer represents a highly aggressive malignancy with limited therapeutic options, during which the hyperactivation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway plays an important role in disease progression, presenting a critical target for therapeutic intervention. Eriocitrin, a natural flavonoid compound, has exhibited potential bioactivities; however, its specific anti-tumor efficacy and underlying mechanisms in prostate cancer remain poorly characterized. Our initial screening across multiple prostate cancer cell lines revealed that androgen-independent DU145 cells were particularly sensitive to Eriocitrin. Subsequent investigations demonstrated that Eriocitrin significantly suppressed DU145 cell proliferation and induced apoptosis in a concentration-dependent manner. Furthermore, Eriocitrin effectively impaired cell migration and invasion, which was mechanistically driven by the reversal of the epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) process, notably through the upregulation of E-cadherin. Molecular analyses revealed that Eriocitrin exerted these anti-tumor effects by inhibiting the activation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling cascade. Taken together, this in vitro study provides novel preclinical evidence that Eriocitrin restrains the aggressive phenotypes of androgen-independent prostate cancer via the PI3K/AKT/mTOR axis. These findings highlight Eriocitrin as a biologically active plant-derived compound that warrants further comprehensive in vivo and pharmacokinetic investigations to determine its true therapeutic potential.

Article.Title: GLP-1 receptor agonist initiation and newly recorded ankylosing spondylitis diagnoses in type 2 diabetes: a target trial emulation
Article.Authors: Lu Y.; Li T.; Liu Y.; Tsai M.
Article.Abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have broad cardiometabolic benefits, but their comparative association with ankylosing spondylitis diagnoses is uncertain. We emulated a target trial in the TriNetX US Collaborative Network among adults with type 2 diabetes who initiated GLP-1 RAs or dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors between 2018 and 2022. The new-user, active-comparator design used 1:1 propensity score matching and Cox models; the Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure covered six outcomes. After matching, 208,970 patients (104,485 per group) were included. GLP-1 RA initiation was associated with more newly recorded ankylosing spondylitis diagnoses (0.15% vs. 0.10%; hazard ratio, 1.49; 95% confidence interval, 1.16–1.91; P = 0.001). Polyosteoarthritis showed a nominal association (1.80% vs. 1.73%; hazard ratio, 1.07; 95% confidence interval, 1.01–1.15; P = 0.031) that was not significant after FDR adjustment (P = 0.093); rheumatoid arthritis, other rheumatoid arthritis, gout, and Sjögren’s syndrome did not differ. The primary association was directionally consistent across prespecified sensitivity analyses. These findings identify a potential comparative safety signal that warrants independent confirmation.

Article.Title: High concordance in molecular profiles between primary tumors and matched lymph node metastases in differentiated thyroid carcinoma: implications for clinical sample selection
Article.Authors: Pan Y.; Sun Y.; Shi C.; Li R.; Xu L.; Zhu C.; Lin Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Genetic testing guides personalized management of differentiated thyroid carcinoma (DTC). However, tumor heterogeneity, including spatial and temporal heterogeneity, has created an unresolved clinical problem. It remains unclear whether molecular profile of the primary tumor (PT) can reliably reflect the genetic characteristics of paired lymph node metastases (LNM) to reduce redundant testing costs. We analyzed 63 paired primary tumor-lymph node metastasis (PT-LNM) samples from 55 Chinese patients with DTC using a 10-gene real-time PCR assay to evaluate spatial heterogeneity. To assess the impact of temporal heterogeneity, we further stratified pairs into synchronous groups (≤ 6 months between PT resection and LNM detection, n = 41) and asynchronous groups (> 6 months interval, n = 22). The overall molecular concordance rate between PT and LNM was 88.9%. Concordance rates for core driver alterations ranged from 92.1% to 100%, with Cohen’s Kappa values of 0.79–1.00. Specifically, BRAF V600E mutation showed 92.1% concordance, TERT promoter mutation showed 98.4% concordance, and RET / NTRK3 fusions showed 98.4%-100% concordance. No statistically significant differences were detected between PT and LNM in overall or subgroup analyses (all P > 0.05). Our findings indicate high and time-independent molecular concordance between PT and LNM in Chinese DTC patients. This supports the clinical utility of PT-only genetic testing to guide LNM management.

Article.Title: In vitro and in vivo evaluation of liposomes constructed with Rg3 as a cholesterol substitute for tumor therapy
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Chen N.; Xie Z.; Huo T.; Wang W.
Article.Abstract: Conventional cholesterol liposomes have poor stability, rapid clearance, and toxicity. This study used Rg3 to replace cholesterol for constructing curcumin-loaded liposomes (PCRL) and evaluated their potential for enhanced hepatocellular carcinoma therapy. Curcumin-loaded liposomes were prepared with Rg3 (PCRL) and cholesterol (PCCL) via thin-film hydration. Physicochemical properties, protein corona, in vitro behavior, in vivo tumor targeting, antitumor efficacy, and biosafety were assessed in H22 tumor-bearing mice. PCRL exhibited smaller particle size, superior storage/plasma stability, and comparable membrane packing to PCCL. Protein corona analysis showed reduced adsorption of immunoglobulin-like and complement proteins, prolonging blood circulation > 24 h and enhancing tumor accumulation. In vitro, PCRL showed good biocompatibility, reduced curcumin cytotoxicity, enhanced cellular uptake, and the slowest drug release. In vivo imaging demonstrated stronger and more persistent tumor fluorescence with lower liver/spleen retention. PCRL significantly inhibited tumor growth. Safety assessment revealed low hemolysis, no hepatorenal toxicity, normal spleen index, and good body weight tolerance. Curcumin-loaded liposomes with Rg3 substituting cholesterol maintain membrane integrity while prolonging circulation, improving tumor targeting/efficacy, and enhancing biosafety, offering a promising strategy for next-generation stealth liposomal delivery systems.

Article.Title: Gingival recession type and related clinical problems are associated with oral health-related quality of life in adult Egyptian dental patients
Article.Authors: Abou-Bakr A.; Ahmed E.; Hussein R.; Hassanein F.; Sarhan S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Gingival recession (GR) is a frequently encountered mucogingival disorder that may be associated with aesthetic problems, dentin hypersensitivity, and root caries, which may be associated with poorer oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL). This study investigated the association between Cairo recession type, recession-associated problems, and overall OHRQoL among adult Egyptian dental patients, for whom evidence remains limited. A multicenter cross-sectional study included 1000 Egyptian adults attending periodontal clinics for dental treatment. Patients' sociodemographic, behavioral, and medical information was gathered through structured interviews. The clinical examination included assessment of gingival recession according to the Cairo Classification (RT1-RT3), plaque index, bleeding on probing (BOP), and gingival biotype, as well as recession-associated problems such as root caries, dentin hypersensitivity, and esthetic problems. OHRQoL was assessed using the Oral Health Impact Profile-14 (OHIP-14), a generic measure of oral health-related quality of life, with higher OHIP-14 scores indicating poorer OHRQoL. Poorer OHRQoL was independently associated with esthetic problems (IRR = 1.49), root caries (IRR = 2.51), dentin hypersensitivity (IRR = 2.52), and multiple recession-associated problems (IRR = 2.55) after full adjustment (all p < 0.001). In the fully adjusted primary model, RT2 and RT3 were associated with higher expected OHIP-14 scores than RT1 (IRR = 1.13 and 1.21, respectively; both p < 0.001). A prespecified interaction analysis indicated that this association differed according to the presence of recession-associated problems: among participants with recession-associated problems, RT2 and RT3 were associated with higher expected OHIP-14 scores than RT1 (IRR = 1.32 and 1.36, respectively), whereas these associations were not statistically significant among participants without recession-associated problems. Most demographic and behavioral factors were not independently associated with the total OHIP-14 score after multivariable adjustment, although the 31–40-year age group showed a modest association. Root caries and dentin hypersensitivity were more strongly associated with poorer OHRQoL among adult Egyptian dental patients. The association between Cairo recession type and poorer OHRQoL was modified by the presence of recession-associated problems, with higher recession types associated with poorer OHRQoL among participants with recession-associated problems but not among those without them. These findings support assessing recession-associated problems alongside Cairo recession type in patient-centered care.

Article.Title: Experimental and numerical study of RC beam joints to steel-encased RC columns with a transitional part
Article.Authors: Rezaifar O.; Taklymi S.; Kheyroddin A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The use of composite columns has attracted considerable attention due to their enhanced load-carrying capacity and ductility. However, the comparative behavior of reinforced concrete (RC) beam and RC column connections and, RC beam and steel encased in reinforced concrete columns (SRCC) incorporating a transitional part, aimed at improving load capacity, ductility, relocating the plastic hinge formation zone, and preventing shear failure of the RC beam under combined axial and cyclic loading, has not been comprehensively investigated. In this study, five specimens were tested, including RC beam RC column connections and RC beam and steel encased in reinforced concrete columns (SRCC) joints with a transition part employing different longitudinal reinforcement anchorage details. The specimens were subjected to quasi static cyclic loading under a constant axial load ratio of 0.08 of the column compressive capacity. Furthermore, a nonlinear finite element model was developed and validated against the experimental results. The experimental results demonstrated that the use of steel encased in reinforced concrete column enhanced the ultimate load-carrying capacity by an average of 35% compared to the conventional reinforced concrete beam to column specimen. In addition, a significant improvement in ductility and crack propagation control was observed. The incorporation of a transition part in the joint region not only increased the load capacity but also effectively relocated the plastic hinge formation from the joint core to the beam span, thereby reducing the likelihood of shear failure in the reinforced concrete beam. The numerical results showed good agreement with the experimental data, with the prediction error of the ultimate capacity remaining below 10% for all specimens. Based on the findings of this study, the application of steel-encased reinforced concrete columns combined with a transitional part and different anchorage details of beam longitudinal reinforcement can be considered an effective strategy for enhancing the seismic performance of beam–column connections. Furthermore, the proposed nonlinear finite element model provides a reliable tool for further analytical investigations and parametric studies.

Article.Title: Association between ambient relative humidity and accelerated aging among middle-aged and older adults: a cross-sectional study of CHARLS
Article.Authors: Ye D.; Xu C.; Lin C.; Ye S.
Article.Abstract: The accelerating global population aging necessitates a deeper understanding of environmental factors influencing the aging process. This cross-sectional study examined the association between ambient relative humidity and accelerated aging among adults aged 45 years and older in China. Utilizing data from the 2011 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) alongside annual average relative humidity data from the National Meteorological Administration, we performed logistic regression analyses to evaluate the association between relative humidity and accelerated aging, defined as biological age exceeding chronological age. The study included 6,529 participants, with adjustments for demographic variables, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities. Higher relative humidity was associated with greater odds of accelerated aging. In the fully adjusted model, each one-percentage-point increase in relative humidity was associated with approximately 2% higher odds of accelerated aging (OR = 1.02, 95% CI: 1.01–1.03). Exploratory restricted cubic spline analyses provided evidence of a nonlinear association but did not establish a humidity threshold or change point. Furthermore, urban residents demonstrated heightened susceptibility, indicating the complex interplay between environmental and lifestyle factors. This study provides evidence of a positive association between environmental relative humidity and accelerated aging among middle-aged and older adults in China, particularly among urban residents. Given the cross-sectional design and potential for selection bias and residual confounding, the findings should be interpreted cautiously. These findings indicate an association between ambient relative humidity and accelerated aging in this cross-sectional sample, particularly among urban residents. Because exposure and outcome were assessed within the 2011 survey period and the study was cross-sectional, the findings do not establish temporality or causality. Longitudinal studies are needed to confirm this association.

Article.Title: A machine learning model for early season wildfire risk in Ghana’s Guinea savannah assessing discrimination, operational prevalence, spatial transferability, and CMIP6 climate scenarios
Article.Authors: Tema W.; Bradshaw S.; Arya E.; Nuakoh B.; Awuah-Mensah Y.; Tan W.; Fouedjio F.; Afrifa-Yamoah E.
Article.Abstract: Tropical savannas account for most of the world’s burned area, and West Africa is a centre of both current fire activity and projected future risk, yet the northern Guinea Savannah of Ghana still lacks a locally calibrated early season fire risk tool. This study develops and critically evaluates a machine learning fire risk model for the November to January window on a 1 km grid over 2001 to 2024, using MODIS fire products, ERA5-Land reanalysis, CHIRPS precipitation, FLDAS multi-depth soil moisture, MODIS vegetation indices, SRTM topography, drought indices, and human access layers into 123 engineered features. Five algorithms were compared under a temporal split with spatial cross-validation. Discrimination was high on the held-out period, with tree ensemble AUC of 0.960 to 0.962 and overlapping bootstrap confidence intervals, and pairwise DeLong tests showing the leading gradient boosting models to be statistically comparable. Three methodological findings frame the contribution. First, because fire is rare at the cell month scale, threshold-dependent skill measured on a class balanced sample overstates operational performance: a base rate correction to the operational prevalence of about 1.7% reduces precision to roughly 0.12 to 0.14, so the model is a screening rather than an alerting tool. Second, feature attribution does not identify a single dominant driver; temperature range, population density, precipitation and soil moisture memory, and vegetation state jointly govern predicted risk, and a spatial ablation experiment shows that removing the five most influential static predictors lowers AUC by only about 0.013, indicating that most skill derives from time varying environmental variables rather than spatial memorisation. Third, CMIP6 scenario experiments suggest higher late century risk under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 but are reported as illustrative because tree ensembles cannot extrapolate beyond their training envelope and human drivers were held fixed. The framework offers a transferable template for evidence based, honestly evaluated fire risk screening in West African savanna landscapes.

Article.Title: Benchmarking the responsiveness of LLM-based agentic systems under controlled mid-task perturbations
Article.Authors: Balyan A.; Sharma S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed where tools fail, objectives change, and constraints tighten while a task is in progress. Prevailing benchmarks score only static end-task accuracy and therefore miss mid-episode responsiveness, which is the ability to adapt and recover after a controlled change. We present a responsiveness evaluation framework that pairs three agent architectures (ReAct, Reflexion, and Plan-and-Execute) with three deterministic synthetic environments (tool planning, debugging, and constraint planning) and injects tool denial, goal modification, or constraint injection at graded severity. Across two matched factorial grids of 4,320 episodes each—one with an explicit perturbation notice and one silent. ReAct attains the highest pooled reward (0.544), yet Plan-and-Execute leads on tool planning (0.711 vs. 0.532) while collapsing on constraint planning (0.114). Tool denial uniquely depresses behavioural recovery, and severity within [0.1, 0.9] yields no monotone dose–response. Explicit notices do not improve mean reward for any architecture. Code, logs, and analysis pipelines are released for extension.
