Article.Title: Sex-specific associations of ACE2 variants with COVID-19 hospitalization, viral load, and mortality: an Iranian hospital-based case-control study
Article.Authors: Baghershiroodi M.; Fattahi S.; Shiadeh A.; Akhavan-Niaki H.; Tayefeh-Arbab M.; Yahyapour Y.; Sadeghi F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 ( ACE2 ) is the cellular receptor for SARS-CoV-2, and its genetic polymorphisms may influence COVID-19 susceptibility. This hospital-based case-control study investigated the association between three ACE2 SNPs (rs2285666, rs4646127, rs971249) and normalized viral load, as well as risk of hospitalization for SARS-CoV-2 infection (comparing hospitalized COVID-19 patients versus hospitalized SARS-CoV-2-negative patients with other severe acute conditions), in 441 participants (226 cases, 215 hospital controls). Genotyping was performed by PCR-RFLP, and viral load was quantified by qRT-PCR and normalized to the RNase P gene. Associations were assessed using sex-stratified logistic regression with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple testing. In females, the rs971249 T allele showed a trend toward higher frequency in controls (48.9% vs. 39.5%; raw p = 0.007), but this association did not remain significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (q = 0.12). In males, the T alleles of rs971249 and rs4646127 were associated with reduced infection risk and remained significant after correction for multiple testing (raw p = 0.003, q = 0.048 and raw p = 0.002, q = 0.036, respectively). No significant associations were observed for rs2285666. While no ACE2 polymorphism was significantly associated with normalized viral load after correction for multiple testing (all q > 0.05), rs971249 showed a trend toward higher viral load in heterozygous females that did not reach statistical significance (raw p = 0.052; q = 0.18). For mortality analysis, the reported associations for rs971249 and rs4646127 in females (adjusted OR = 2.54 and 2.73, respectively) are based on covariate-adjusted logistic regression (age, comorbidities, sampling time) but did not undergo Benjamini-Hochberg correction due to the exploratory nature of this subgroup analysis; these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and are clearly labeled as ‘nominally significant’ in the Results section (raw p < 0.05). However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously due to the limited sample size and the exploratory nature of the subgroup analyses and because the rs971249 variant deviated from Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium in female controls ( p = 0.010). These findings suggest that the rs971249 and rs4646127 T alleles may confer sex-specific protection against hospitalized SARS-CoV-2 infection in this cohort of hospitalized patients. However, because controls were hospitalized patients with severe non-COVID-19 conditions, these associations reflect differences between two hospitalized groups rather than population-level susceptibility. Therefore, large-scale studies with population-based controls and diverse ethnic groups are warranted to validate these sex-specific associations and to clarify the role of ACE2 variants in population-level COVID-19 susceptibility.

Article.Title: Heterologous expression of the membrane protein OmpA from bovine Pasteurella multocida and establishment of an indirect ELISA for antibody detection
Article.Authors: Hao D.; Han S.; Wang Y.; Li J.; Liu L.; Liu Z.
Article.Abstract: Reliable serological tools are needed for surveillance of Pasteurella multocida antibodies. Four P. multocida membrane proteins were expressed in a prokaryotic system and screened by Western blotting and indirect ELISA. Among them, a dilution-refolded OmpA preparation retained serum immunoreactivity and met the antigen-selection criterion under the tested conditions. The optimized assay used a nominal total-protein coating concentration of 1 µg/mL, 1% skim milk blocking at 37 °C for 1 h, serum diluted 1:400, secondary antibody diluted 1:25,000, and 15 min colour development. In the preliminary analytical-specificity panel, the available PmB-positive serum and positive sera against eight other bovine respiratory pathogens remained below the lower decision threshold. PmA-positive serum remained test-positive at a dilution of 1:1280, and the intra-assay and inter-assay coefficients of variation were below 5%. Within the vaccination-defined 60-serum development panel, ROC analysis yielded an AUC of 0.969 and apparent sensitivity and specificity of 95.00% each relative to the predefined serum groups. These estimates are preliminary because the panel was derived from a single ranch, the same 20 predefined negative-reference sera were also used to establish the decision thresholds, and no independent reference method was applied.

Article.Title: Station-specific variability and short-term forecasting of a particulate air-quality index using machine learning in Charleroi, Belgium
Article.Authors: Bennis M.; El Morabet R.; Hallot E.; Abad Khan R.; Youssfi M.
Article.Abstract: Air-quality management in urban–industrial environments require reliable assessment of particulate pollution and realistic evaluation of forecasting performance. This study examined temporal variability and short-term predictability of a particulate air-quality index at Marchienne-au-Pont, Charleroi and Lodelinsart in Belgium. The analysis included 206,184 half-hourly observations collected during 2020–2023. Quality control identified a probable inconsistency in the recorded PM 2.5 and PM₁₀ fields, which was addressed through a reproducible provisional reconstruction. k-nearest neighbours, Random Forest, Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost and a Neural Network—were evaluated using expanding-window validation and an independent 2023 test period. The four-year mean particulate index was highest at Marchienne-au-Pont (35.13), followed by Lodelinsart (31.62) and Charleroi (28.60). PM 2.5 determined the index in 67.63–74.84% of observations, whereas PM 10 determined 25.16–32.37%. Tree-based models produced contemporaneous testing R 2 values above 0.999 because the target was mathematically derived from the simultaneous particulate predictors. Separate future-forecast experiments therefore provided the principal operational assessment. One-hour forecasts achieved R 2 values of 0.857–0.920, decreasing to 0.551–0.641 at 6 h and 0.270–0.335 at 24 h. Compared with persistence, Gradient Boosting reduced RMSE by 5.80–6.29% at 1 h, 15.31–17.19% at 6 h and 12.41–12.96% at 24 h. These findings demonstrate the importance of data-quality verification, chronological validation and explicit separation of contemporaneous index estimation from genuine future forecasting. Because monitoring-agency confirmation of pollutant identity and processing history was unavailable, the reconstructed concentrations and derived results remain provisional.

Article.Title: Pan-cancer analysis identifies ANGPT4 as a potential prognostic biomarker associated with the tumor microenvironment in kidney renal clear cell carcinoma
Article.Authors: Chen P.; Tong K.; You L.; Chen X.; Ye L.; Guo G.
Article.Abstract: As a pivotal member of the angiopoietin family, angiopoietin-4 (ANGPT4) is critically implicated in tumor initiation, progression, metastasis, and angiogenesis. However, systematic investigations into its impact on the tumor microenvironment (TME) and pan-cancer prognosis remain substantially lacking. Our comprehensive pan-cancer analysis and immunohistochemical results revealed that ANGPT4 expression was dysregulated across various cancers, with notably elevated levels in Kidney Clear Cell Carcinoma (KIRC) that were predictive of favorable clinical prognosis. Functional and gene set enrichment analyses revealed that ANGPT4 expression was positively correlated with diverse immune and stromal cell populations and inversely correlated with multiple tumor-promoting signaling pathways in KIRC. Furthermore, based on single-cell sequencing and spatial transcriptomic analyses, ANGPT4 expression was primarily detected in fibroblasts within the TME. Moreover, integrated computational analyses combining drug sensitivity profiling and Connectivity Map (CMap) screening revealed that three candidate compounds (clofibrate, MS.275, and AH.6809) were computationally predicted to reverse transcriptional signatures associated with ANGPT4 dysregulation in KIRC. In conclusion, we established ANGPT4 as a potential prognostic biomarker and a candidate molecule associated with the tumor microenvironment in KIRC.

Article.Title: Simple calls to increase effort influence attention, mind wandering, and learning during online lectures
Article.Authors: Albert D.; Heitzner J.; Smilek D.
Article.Abstract: Mind wandering is a prevalent contributor to poor retention of lecture content. This study examined whether simply directing students to “try harder” can enhance attention and learning in recorded lectures. In two experiments ( N = 113 and N = 100), participants watched a 45 min recorded lecture while periodically responding to probes measuring attention (Experiment 1) or intentional and unintentional mind wandering (Experiment 2). Two-thirds through the lecture, half of participants received a prompt directing them to “try harder” to learn from the remaining portion of the lecture (experimental, try harder condition), while the other half received a neutral prompt (control condition). The try harder prompt significantly increased self-reported attention (Experiment 1) as well as decreased intentional and unintentional mind wandering (Experiment 2). In Experiment 2 (but not in Experiment 1), the try harder prompt also led to a nominal improvement in retention of post-prompt lecture content, a change that was statistically different from the corresponding change for controls, which was nominally in the opposite direction. These effects occurred without explicit incentives or between-group differences in motivation, suggesting that directly targeting effort mobilization may be sufficient to enhance learning outcomes. These findings endorse directing students to try harder as a practical technique for improving attention and retention in recorded lectures.

Article.Title: Spatial–temporal coupling coordination and multi-scenario simulation of the urban resilience complex systems in the Yellow River Basin
Article.Authors: Zhang L.; Long T.; Yang J.
Article.Abstract: Enhancing urban resilience (UR) is critical for sustaining urban development and safeguarding resident well-being, particularly in ecologically fragile regions exposed to climate change and natural hazards. This study constructs an integrated framework that combines multidimensional assessment, coupling coordination, and scenario prediction to evaluate UR across the Yellow River Basin (YRB). Using a comprehensive indicator system, we quantify UR, trace its spatiotemporal evolution from 2010 to 2021, calculate the coupling coordination degree (CCD) among its economic, ecological, infrastructure, and social subsystems, and project UR under four development scenarios up to 2035. Three key findings emerge. First, UR improved markedly in most cities over the study period, with downstream cities gradually overtaking the middle and upper reaches after 2010, and non-resource-based cities ranking above resource-based ones. Second, by 2021, CCD in most cities had reached a good coordination level, with a significant positive spatial correlation across the basin. Third, projections show that by 2035, relative to the 2021 baseline, the sustainable resilience development pathway would raise UR by approximately 11.5%, while the other three pathways would yield gains ranging from 7.2% to 7.5%. This framework offers methodological guidance for resilience research in ecologically fragile basins and supports policy efforts to meet the UN Sustainable Development Goals.

Article.Title: Transforming mosquito surveillance LarvaFormer as a hybrid deep learning tool for rapid and accurate larval recognition
Article.Authors: Imtiaz A.; Karmaker D.; Bhowmik A.; Islam M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Mosquito-borne diseases represent a significant global health threat, causing over 700,000 deaths annually. Traditional control methods targeting adult mosquitoes are often ineffective and environmentally harmful. This paper proposes LarvaFormer, a novel hybrid deep learning framework that integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers with specialized attention mechanisms for the automated classification of mosquito larvae. Leveraging two benchmark datasets MosquitoLarvae-7400 (four species) and MLMI-2024 (anatomical-level imaging) the model achieves state-of-the-art accuracies of 98.97% and 99.50%, respectively. LarvaFormer incorporates cross-modality feature fusion, a lightweight attention module, and a neural architecture search (NAS)-guided optimization scheme to enhance discriminative capability and generalization. Comprehensive evaluations, including ablation studies and Grad-CAM visualizations, demonstrate its robustness, interpretability, and efficiency. The proposed system enables rapid, accurate larval identification, supporting targeted and environmentally sustainable mosquito control strategies.

Article.Title: Estimating the areal yield of forage nutritive components in a Mediterranean Sulla (Hedysarum coronarium L.) sward using UAV multispectral imagery
Article.Authors: Furnitto N.; Mammarella F.; Ramírez-Cuesta J.; Avondo M.; Bognanno M.; Biondi L.; Failla S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate information on pasture nutritive resources is essential for improving grazing management and supporting precision livestock systems, particularly in Mediterranean environments characterized by strong seasonal variability and heterogeneous pasture conditions. In this study, UAV multispectral imagery was evaluated for estimating the areal yield of key forage quality components in a Mediterranean pasture dominated by Hedysarum coronarium L. over two growing seasons under pre- and post-grazing conditions. Forage biomass and laboratory-derived quality traits were collected from 28 georeferenced plots across four sampling dates. Crude protein (CP), neutral detergent fibre (NDF) on an organic matter basis, acid detergent fibre (ADF), digestible NDF after 48 h incubation, undigested NDF after 240 h incubation and ash content were converted into areal yields (g m −2 ) by integrating forage quality concentration with dry biomass availability. UAV multispectral surveys were performed using DJI Mavic 3 Multispectral and MicaSense Altum-PT sensors, and 30 vegetation indices were evaluated through empirical single-index regression models. Among the tested vegetation indices, EVI2 provided the most consistent and interpretable relationships for fibre-related components yields, whereas green-based indices such as GI and GRVI were particularly informative for CP and ash yields. Calibration and location-grouped hold-out validation showed that UAV-derived spectral responses associated with canopy greenness, red–green contrast and structural development were associated with spatial variability in biomass-weighted forage nutritive component yields. Spatial prediction maps highlighted pronounced within-field heterogeneity and revealed clear differences between pre- and post-grazing conditions, particularly for protein and fibre-related components. Overall, the results highlight the potential of UAV multispectral imagery for estimation and spatial mapping forage nutritive component yields in Mediterranean grazing systems. The proposed approach may contribute to the future development of precision grazing strategies by providing spatially explicit information on pasture nutritional heterogeneity using simple and interpretable spectral models.

Article.Title: Structure-based computational analysis of quercetin and withaferin A as prolactin receptor inhibitors for male breast cancer therapy
Article.Authors: Yang F.; Ren S.; Shi C.; Tian Z.; Naz R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Male breast cancer (MBC) is a rare malignancy that is frequently diagnosed at advanced stages and managed using therapeutic strategies largely extrapolated from female breast cancer despite important biological differences. Notably, prolactin receptor (PRLR) expression has been reported in approximately 60% of male breast carcinomas compared with only approximately 20% of benign gynecomastia specimens, highlighting aberrant PRL–PRLR signaling as a potentially relevant molecular feature of MBC. PRLR activates JAK/STAT, PI3K–Akt, and MAPK signaling pathways involved in tumor-cell proliferation and survival, providing a strong rationale for exploring PRLR-directed therapeutic strategies in MBC. This study therefore employed computer-aided drug design (CADD) to identify plant-derived phytochemicals as potential PRLR inhibitors. The PRLR crystal structure (PDB ID: 4I18) was retrieved and validated (3.24 Å resolution, ERRAT score 79.78, 98.8% of evaluated residues in favored or allowed Ramachandran regions). Protein–protein interaction analysis and KEGG pathway mapping confirmed PRLR’s central role in oncogenic signaling. Eighteen phytochemicals were screened via AutoDock Vina and HDOCK; withaferin A (AutoDock Vina: –8.8 kcal/mol; HDOCK score: –226.80, confidence score: 0.8229) and quercetin (AutoDock Vina: –8.7 kcal/mol; HDOCK score: –199.25, confidence score: 0.7281) emerged as top binders. Interaction analysis revealed quercetin forming multiple hydrogen bonds (ASN60: 2.15 Å, SER112: 2.73 Å) and π–π stacking with TRP23 (3.83 Å, 4.53 Å), while withaferin A engaged hydrophobic contacts (ILE55: 4.26 Å; TYR117: 5.15 Å, 5.19 Å) and key hydrogen bonds (SER57: 1.96 Å; LEU47: 2.47 Å). Integrated docking and 500-ns MD simulations identified withaferin A and quercetin as stable predicted PRLR binders, with withaferin A showing superior pose persistence and interaction energy, warranting experimental validation. Pharmacophore mapping showed quercetin’s balanced polar-aromatic profile (3 aromatic rings, 5 donors, 6 acceptors, 3 hydrophobic regions) versus withaferin A’s hydrophobic-rich profile (2 donors, 5 acceptors, 8 hydrophobic regions). DFT analysis yielded small HOMO–LUMO gaps for quercetin (0.16436 eV) and withaferin A (0.18065 eV), indicating high reactivity. ADMET predictions indicated good gastrointestinal absorption, non–BBB permeation, and zero Lipinski violations for both, with bioavailability scores of 0.55; quercetin exhibited a cleaner toxicity profile than withaferin A, which showed AMES mutagenicity and hERG inhibition risks. In conclusion, Quercetin showed greater early conformational adjustment before converging toward a stable bound pose, whereas withaferin A maintained closer and more persistent proximity to the predicted binding pocket and exhibited stronger van der Waals stabilization, together indicating greater predicted dynamic stability of the PRLR–withaferin A complex.

Article.Title: A spatio-temporal graph neural network model for predicting economic impact of sports events and analyzing regional synergy effects
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Major sporting events reshape economic activity in host cities and their surroundings through channels that input-output, computable general equilibrium, and spatial econometric tools capture only in part, because each of these tools fixes multipliers or adjacency rules before it sees the data. This study develops ST-GAT, a spatio-temporal graph attention network that forecasts a monthly regional activity index around event cycles and learns inter-regional coupling from data, with gravity-based priors entering as side information rather than as fixed weights. The forecasting target combines card-transaction consumption with night-time light intensity at the prefecture-month level; the model therefore predicts event-period activity and does not estimate welfare or causal effects. Its architecture couples attention-weighted graph convolution with multi-scale gated temporal convolution and a synergy-regularized objective, and a downstream routine turns the learned attention into a directional synergy matrix. We evaluate the framework on eight Chinese host environments, which involve fourteen host or co-host prefectures among 96 prefectural nodes observed monthly from 2014 to 2024. Averaged over five random seeds, ST-GAT lowers RMSE by approximately 25% relative to STGCN at a six-month horizon. The margin narrows against DCRNN, ASTGCN, and Graph WaveNet: the Graph WaveNet comparison ( p = 0.032) survives a Holm adjustment across seven baselines but not a Bonferroni bound, so we treat it as provisional. The advantage widens at longer horizons and persists when the pandemic window is excluded. Three exploratory patterns follow, each a property of the fitted model rather than an estimated effect. Legacy half-life rises monotonically with pre-event fixed-asset investment across the eight environments, although part of this association may be mechanical because investment is also a model input. Suzhou, Foshan, and Langfang act as predictive hubs in the attention network without hosting an event. Perturbing policy-alignment information moves the synergy output roughly twice as far as perturbing transport accessibility, a contrast that motivates, but cannot substitute for, a causal test. We therefore present ST-GAT as a forecasting and hypothesis-screening tool that indicates which co-hosting, industrial, and infrastructure relationships deserve dedicated causal evaluation.

Article.Title: Comparative evaluation of Allplex RV master assay and biofire respiratory panel 2.1 plus for detection of respiratory viruses
Article.Authors: Abdel-Hamid S.; Ismail G.; Omar N.; Sherif B.; Rashad S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Respiratory tract infections are among the most prevalent diseases worldwide, causing significant morbidity and mortality, particularly in children, the elderly, and immunocompromised individuals. Early and accurate diagnosis is essential to reduce their health burden. Diagnostic methods include culture, serology, and rapid antigen tests; however, nucleic acid amplification assays, particularly multiplex PCR, are considered the gold standard due to their high sensitivity and specificity. This study aimed to compare the diagnostic performance of open-PCR multiplex platform Allplex RV Master Assay for the detection of respiratory viruses using a cartridge-based syndromic platform BioFire Respiratory Panel 2.1 plus (RP2.1plus) as a comparator. A cross-sectional study was conducted on 65 positive nasopharyngeal swabs, which were analyzed using both systems. Positive percent agreement ranged from 75 to 100%, negative percent agreement from 92.59 to 100%, and kappa values from 0.48 to 1.00. The good concordance between the two assays supports the use of Allplex Respiratory Panel 1 as a reliable alternative for rapid and accurate diagnosis of viral respiratory infections.

Article.Title: Effects of variable-speed operation on the tip leakage vortex and pressure pulsations in a vane-type multiphase pump
Article.Authors: Pei Q.; Shi G.; Chen Z.; Rui G.; Tongde F.; Wang S.
Article.Abstract: As a key component of oil–gas transportation systems, the off-design operating characteristics of multiphase pumps directly affect system stability and transport efficiency, while variable-speed transients are a key factor governing internal flow and energy conversion. This study numerically investigates the transient flow-field response of a vane-type multiphase pump under a prescribed variable-speed condition at a fixed inlet flow rate, focusing on the evolution of tip leakage vortex (TLV) and pressure pulsation characteristics. The results show that changes in rotational speed significantly affect the vorticity distribution within the impeller: during acceleration, the circumferential vorticity component strengthens and the axial and radial components extend over a wider region; during deceleration, the overall vorticity intensity decreases and the axial and radial components gradually weaken, with a delayed adjustment observed in the early deceleration stage. In the blade-tip region, the pressure-pulsation response varies markedly with monitoring position, with the strongest pulsations occurring near the pressure-surface inlet; the suction surface exhibits higher spectral amplitudes than the pressure surface. In the impeller passage, pressure-pulsation amplitude generally decreases along the flow direction, and the response exhibits a time lag relative to rotational-speed variation during both acceleration and deceleration. This study reveals the transient vorticity and pressure-pulsation characteristics of a multiphase pump under fixed-inlet-flow and prescribed variable-speed conditions, providing a reference for understanding the internal flow behavior of multiphase pumps during speed transients.

Article.Title: Shaking table investigation into seismic failure mechanisms of bedrock-underlain stratified slopes: influence of soil layer configuration
Article.Authors: Yang B.; Hu X.; Liu Y.; Li F.; Pan Y.; Cai H.
Article.Abstract: Soil layer configuration governs the seismic failure characteristics and dynamic responses of layered slopes. However, the seismic damage evolution and mechanical mechanisms of clay-over-sand and sand-over-clay slopes remain poorly understood. This study integrates shaking table tests and cyclic triaxial tests to investigate how soil layer distribution controls slope failure mode, acceleration amplification, and dynamic stress evolution. The results indicate that: (1) Differences in soil mechanical properties across layers give rise to distinct seismic damage patterns. The upper-clay/lower-sand slope exhibits progressive plastic sliding with significant accumulated deformation, whereas the upper-sand/lower-clay slope undergoes brittle failure characterized by surface tensile cracking and shallow instantaneous sliding. (2) The acceleration amplification factor increases nonlinearly with peak ground acceleration (PGA), peaking no later than the critical state and decreasing sharply once the slope fails, thereby serving as a precursor to seismically-induced slope instability. (3) Soil layer configuration governs the spatial evolution of dynamic stress. In the upper-clay/lower-sand slope, the soft clay layer in the upper-middle section exhibits large stress fluctuations and frequent redistribution, forming the primary damage zone. In the upper-sand/lower-clay slope, the lower clay layer serves as a stable basal boundary, intensifying dynamic stress responses in the middle-lower section; slope stability is governed by basal restraint. (4) Quantitative stress–volumetric strain constitutive models were developed from triaxial tests at varying confining pressures, elucidating the transition from dilative behavior at low pressures to contractive behavior at high pressures and revealing how confining pressure governs soil deformation and failure. This study advances the understanding of seismic instability mechanisms in layered soil slopes and informs seismic reinforcement strategies, hazard prediction, and slope protection engineering.

Article.Title: Nano-formulated humic acid modulates growth, antioxidant status, and intestinal architecture in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)
Article.Authors: Sharaf A.; Saleh N.; Ali F.; Abdelkhalek N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The growing demand for sustainable aquafeeds has intensified the search for eco-friendly alternatives to synthetic antibiotics. This study evaluated conventional and nano-formulated humic acid (HA) as promising feed supplements for Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ). Six isonitrogenous diets were formulated: control, bulk HA (H4; 4 g kg⁻ 1 ), two nano-HA supplemented diets (NH50/NH100; 50/100 mg kg⁻ 1 ), and two chitosan-loaded nano-HA supplemented diets (C-NH50/C-NH100; 50/100 mg kg⁻ 1 ). After a 60-day feeding trial, growth performance, hepatic biomarkers, immune and growth gene expression, intestinal histomorphology, antioxidant status, and digestive enzyme activities were assessed. At the end of the experiment fish were stressed by Aeromonas hydrophila injection. The results indicated that nano-HA supplementation, particularly C-NH100 significantly enhancing feed utilization efficiency ( P < 0.05 ). ALT and AST activities increased progressively across supplemented groups, with C-NH100 exhibiting the highest values. SOD and CAT activities were maximized in C-NH100 (5.04 & 3.76, respectively). In contrast, MDA levels were significantly reduced in all supplemented groups relative to control, attaining the lowest value in C-NH100 (4.62). Moreover, intestinal digestive enzymes were significantly modulated by HA supplementation. Intestinal histomorphology examination revealed that C-NH100 dietary supplementation increased the villus height by 46%, villus width by 138%, epithelial thickness by 221%, and goblet cell density by 157% relative to the control. Immune-related genes (IL8, CXC2, CC chemokines, and IgM) and growth hormone (GH) expression were markedly upregulated in C-NH100, whereas IGF-I expression exhibited a treatment-dependent response, increasing in H4 and NH100 but decreasing in NH50, C-NH50, and C-NH100 while NH100 showed comparatively lower immune expression. In contrast, the antioxidant-related gene GST showed the highest expression in C-NH100 and the lowest expression in C-NH50. Following bacterial challenge, supplemented groups descriptively exhibited lower cumulative mortality (~ 6.7% vs. 73.3% in control), consistent with a treatment-level trend toward enhanced physiological resilience. Collectively, chitosan-loaded nano-HA at 100 mg kg⁻ 1 provided improvement in feed utilization, intestinal morphology, antioxidant status, immune responses, and physiological stability under pathogenic challenge. These findings indicate that nano-HA formulations exert treatment-specific effects on growth- and immune-related molecular pathways. Collectively, these findings suggest the potential of chitosan-loaded nano-HA at 100 mg kg⁻ 1 as a sustainable functional feed additive to support health management in tilapia aquaculture.

Article.Title: Association of the TyG-grip index with incident stroke and all-cause mortality in middle-aged and older adults: a longitudinal analysis
Article.Authors: Zhang C.; Li K.; Song W.
Article.Abstract: Insulin resistance and declining physical function commonly coexist in middle-aged and older adults. Triglyceride-glucose (TyG)-derived composite indices, such as the TyG-frailty index, can capture this metabolic and functional risk, but require the assessment of multiple components, limiting their suitability for routine clinical use. In contrast, the TyG-grip index provides a single, objective, and readily accessible method. The TyG-grip index was defined as the TyG index divided by maximum grip strength, and its association with incident stroke and all-cause mortality was examined among participants in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study. Using propensity-score overlap weighting, we fitted weighted Cox models with baseline and updated exposure, and a causal survival forest to explore heterogeneity of the association. During follow-up, 636 participants developed stroke and 837 died. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest quartile of the TyG-grip index carried higher risks of stroke (time-varying model: HR 1.64, 95% CI 1.05–2.55) and all-cause mortality (HR 1.75, 95% CI 1.19–2.58), corresponding to 5-year absolute risk differences of 1.37% and 3.32%. Associations were consistent across sensitivity analyses, and heterogeneity in the mortality association was borderline. The TyG-grip index was associated with both stroke and all-cause mortality.

Article.Title: Molecular and functional characterization of a highly mosquitocidal Bacillus thuringiensis strain VCRC-B669
Article.Authors: Dhotre A.; Ashokkumar M.; Mandodan S.; Vijayakumar A.; Irudayaraj G.
Article.Abstract: Mosquito-borne diseases (MBDs) continue to pose a significant public health burden, and controlling mosquito populations remains a key strategy for reducing disease transmission. Extensive use of chemical insecticides causes environmental issues and leads to the development of resistance in mosquito populations. Entomopathogenic bacteria are increasingly being explored as environmentally safe alternatives for mosquito control. In the present study, a mosquitocidal bacterial strain was characterized and evaluated for its larvicidal potential against medically important mosquito vectors. The mosquitocidal bacterial isolate was identified using MALDI-TOF MS, 16 S rRNA gene sequencing, housekeeping genes, and detection of Bacillus thuringiensis ( Bt) crystal-insecticidal protein genes, viz., cry4A , cry4B , cry10 , cry11 , and cyt1 , cyt2 . Growth dynamics and protein production were monitored over a 96-h cultivation period. Larvicidal efficacy was evaluated against late third-instar larvae of Aedes aegypti , Anopheles stephensi , and Culex quinquefasciatus . SDS-PAGE was used to examine insecticidal crystal proteins, whereas conserved toxin domains in Cry4A and Cyt2 were analyzed using InterProScan. The isolate was identified as Bt strain VCRC-B669 and exhibited potent larvicidal activity, with LC₅₀ values of 0.0014, 0.0036, and 0.0070 µg/mL against Ae. aegypti , An. stephensi , and Cx. quinquefasciatus , respectively. SDS-PAGE consistently revealed major protein bands at approximately 130, 70, and 27–30 kDa, InterProScan analysis identified conserved protein domains and sequence features within the translated Cry4A and Cyt2 sequences. These findings indicate that B. thuringiensis VCRC-B669 has considerable potential for development as a microbial larvicide for integrated mosquito vector management.

Article.Title: Integrating disulfidptosis patterns and machine learning identifies a novel diagnostic signature for endometriosis
Article.Authors: Li Q.; Zhao B.; Yuan Y.; Lai L.
Article.Abstract: Endometriosis (EM) is a heterogeneous gynecological disorder with incompletely understood molecular mechanisms. Disulfidptosis, a recently identified form of programmed cell death, has not been systematically explored in EM. Gene expression profiles from the GSE51981 dataset were analyzed to investigate disulfidptosis-related genes (DRGs) and immune characteristics in EM. Consensus clustering identified molecular subtypes, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was performed to screen subtype-associated genes. Four machine-learning algorithms were subsequently compared to establish an optimal diagnostic model, which was further evaluated in two independent external datasets and validated at the expression level using RT-qPCR experiments. EM tissues showed abnormal DRG expression patterns and immune infiltration. Two disulfidptosis-associated molecular subtypes with distinct immune features and biological pathways were identified. The Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB) algorithm showed the best performance and generated a five-gene signature comprising BTBD2 , SLC4A2 , SSC5D , LPPR2 , and SRGAP2C . External validation, calibration, decision curve analysis, and nomogram evaluation provided complementary evidence supporting the potential diagnostic utility of the signature. RT-qPCR provided partial expression-level validation of selected genes within the five-gene signature in EM patients. Disulfidptosis-related molecular heterogeneity is associated with immune remodeling in EM. The five-gene signature provides a potential diagnostic tool and new insights into EM mechanisms.

Article.Title: The mediating role of social media addiction in the relationship between usage time and physical activity attitudes among adolescents: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Öztürk M.; Erdoğan R.; Bozkurt E.; Yıldırak A.; Yılmaz E.; Tümen T.; Tel M.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to examine the associations among social media addiction, social media platform preferences, and physical activity attitudes in adolescents. The study included 742 volunteer high school students (473 males and 269 females) aged 14–17 years attending schools in Bitlis, Türkiye, during the 2024–2025 academic year. Data were collected using a personal information form, the Social Media Addiction Scale–Short Form (SMAS-SF), and the Physical Activity Attitude Scale for Children and Adolescents (PAAS-CA). Independent samples t-tests, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), Bonferroni-adjusted post hoc comparisons, Pearson correlation analyses, and mediation analysis (PROCESS macro Model 4) were performed. Effect sizes were calculated using Cohen's d and eta-squared (η 2 ). Significant differences in social media addiction and physical activity attitudes were observed based on gender, age, grade level, family income, physical activity status, platform preference, and daily usage time (p < .05). Male students reported higher social media addiction and more positive physical activity attitudes than females. TikTok users exhibited less positive physical activity attitudes, whereas YouTube and Twitter users showed more favorable profiles. Mediation analysis indicated that social media addiction statistically mediated the association between daily social media use time and physical activity attitudes however, given the cross-sectional nature of the data, this mediation model represents an associative pathway rather than a confirmed causal mechanism. Correlation analyses indicated low but significant positive associations between social media addiction and physical activity attitude scores (r = .21–.25). Social media addiction and physical activity attitudes among adolescents are associated with socio-demographic characteristics and digital behavioral patterns. The findings suggest that social media addiction is statistically linked to the association between daily social media use time and physical activity attitudes, functioning as an associative bridge within the tested model. Because of the cross-sectional design, these findings should be interpreted as associative rather than causal. Future studies should incorporate objective measures of physical activity and longitudinal designs to clarify causal pathways.

Article.Title: BMSVP: Blockchain-based message signing and verification protocol for security enhancement in smart grids
Article.Authors: Kabier M.; Abduljabbar Z.; Hussain M.; Nyangaresi V.; Ma J.; Al Sibahee M.; Ali A.; Aldarwish A.; Hussien Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The transformation of traditional power grid systems towards smart grids is driven by factors such as the expansion of vehicle charging infrastructure, rapid technological advancements, demands for energy efficiency, as well as the surge in distributed energy generation. However, the smart grid system integrates with numerous internet of things (IoT) devices and legacy systems, most of which have inherent vulnerabilities or do not support current cryptographic protocols. In addition, the communication among the myriad of smart grid devices takes place over the public internet, further exposing the smart grids to security threats. Although numerous security techniques have been presented to mitigate these threats, the provision of perfect security at low overheads remains elusive. In this paper, we leverage blockchain, bilinear pairings, and elliptic curve cryptography to develop a provably secure protocol for smart grids. Its formal security is performed using the widely deployed Real or Random (RoR) model, while its semantic security analysis demonstrate its resilience against threats such as side-channeling, replays and privileged insiders. In addition, it is shown to offer authentication, untraceability, anonymity, and perfect key secrecy. In terms of performance evaluation, it is shown to reduce communication costs by 22.36% while maintaining fairly low computation overheads. There is therefore a need to further optimize this protocol to lessen the incurred computation overheads.

Article.Title: Genetically determined metabolite variation identifies a heat related pathway in workers at risk of Mesoamerican Nephropathy
Article.Authors: Leone D.; Raines N.; Amador J.; Delgado I.; Embade N.; Gil-Redondo R.; Gordo C.; Leibler J.; Lopez-Pilarte D.; Millet O.; Pitsillides A.; Ramirez-Rubio O.; Scammell M.; Johnson W.; Brooks D.; Friedman D.
Article.Abstract: Mesoamerican nephropathy (MeN), a regional chronic kidney disease of unknown etiology (CKDu) in Central America, is a leading cause of death among young agricultural workers and other manual laborers. MeN has both strong environmental and genetic components. Genetically-determined variability in urine metabolite concentrations may provide insight into causal factors driving kidney injury in MeN. We investigated the associations between nucleotide variants and levels of 93 urine metabolites in 313 Nicaraguan workers with normal renal function from an area with exceptionally high MeN prevalence. Of genetically-influenced urinary metabolites, one of the strongest relationships was between genetic variants in AGXT2 and metabolites on a pathway related to brown fat differentiation and thermogenesis. Nicaraguans at risk of MeN had higher urinary levels of one of these metabolites, ß-aminoisobutyrate, compared to similar workers in the Mediterranean. Longitudinal studies will be needed to determine the effect of these metabolites on development of MeN. Our study illustrates how genetics could be useful for understanding factors such as heat stress and energy metabolism in populations at risk for CKDu.

Article.Title: Acceptability and delivery of an offer of access to EMDR for depression, posttraumatic stress, and burnout in healthcare workers exposed to COVID-19: a randomized controlled trial within a cohort
Article.Authors: El-Hage W.; Mansy L.; Gissot V.; Blanchin M.; Chami L.; Bray A.; Hingray C.; Birmes P.; Bergey C.; Gohier B.; Fakra E.; Sauvaget A.; Lemogne C.; Krebs M.; Aouizerate B.; Jalenques I.; Vidailhet P.; Prieto N.; Bui E.; Caille A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Healthcare workers (HCWs) were highly exposed to COVID-19 and often experienced anxiety, depression, burnout, and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). The HARD trial assessed the effect of being offered access to EMDR therapy on HCWs with COVID-19-related psychological symptoms. This cohort-embedded randomized trial enrolled 849 HCWs exposed to COVID-19. Participants completed online assessments every 3 months for 12 months. Those scoring above predefined thresholds for PTSD, depression, or burnout were randomized (1:1) to an offer of access to EMDR or to usual care alone. Outcomes compared 6-month changes in PTSD, depression, and burnout symptoms, and EMDR compliance was evaluated. A total of 237 eligible cohort participants were randomized in the HARD trial. Among the 118 subjects of the intervention offer, 73 (62%) consented to EMDR sessions, and of these, 38 (52%) received EMDR sessions (median 7, IQR 4 to 12 sessions). Primary analysis estimated a mean difference between groups from baseline to 6 months post-randomization of -0.61 (p = 0.77) for the PTSD score, -1.17 (p = 0.18) for the depression score, and 0.32 (p = 0.72) for the burnout subdimension. Improvements favoring the intervention offer group were observed for depressive symptoms and PTSD avoidance at 12 months. In this pragmatic trial, uptake and adherence to an offer of EMDR among symptomatic HCWs were limited. No statistically significant between-group differences were detected in the prespecified six-month primary outcomes, although the study recruited substantially fewer participants than planned and was therefore underpowered, treatment exposure varied substantially, and the intervention was not subject to systematic fidelity monitoring. These findings primarily provide information about real-world acceptability (a modest 62% consent rate) and delivery (only 52% of consenting participants used the intervention). Our ability to draw conclusions about potential effectiveness of EMDR, if used, however, was limited by the law rate of consent to access the intervention among those offered program access and the law rate of usage among those who did not consent.

Article.Title: Radiographic fractal analysis of mandibular trabecular bone in children with down syndrome: a matched case-control study
Article.Authors: Tasdemir T.; Tassoker M.
Article.Abstract: Down syndrome (DS) is associated with systemic skeletal abnormalities; however, to the best of our knowledge, mandibular trabecular bone microarchitecture has not previously been evaluated in pediatric patients using fractal analysis (FA). This study assessed mandibular trabecular radiographic architecture in children with DS on panoramic radiographs and compared fractal dimension (FD) values with healthy age- and sex-matched controls. Thirty-six children with DS and 36 matched controls were retrospectively included. FA was performed on bilateral condylar, gonial, and dentate regions using ImageJ. Between-group comparisons used the Mann–Whitney U test, with Holm adjustment for six regional comparisons. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was restricted to regions remaining significant after correction. After Holm adjustment, FD values were significantly lower in the right condylar (adjusted p = 0.035) and right dentate (adjusted p = 0.003) regions in children with DS. The right dentate region showed the highest exploratory discrimination (AUC = 0.738, 95% CI: 0.624–0.851), followed by the right condylar region (AUC = 0.684, 95% CI: 0.557–0.810). These findings suggest region-specific differences in mandibular trabecular radiographic texture in children with DS. The observed discriminatory performance was moderate and requires independent validation in larger prospective studies.

Article.Title: Electrochemical performance of BN – Me (Ti, Cr, Al, Zr) composite nanopowders synthesized under concentrated light with reduced surface-driven contributions
Article.Authors: Sartinska L.; Fomanyuk S.; Staryk S.; Kolbasov G.; Borovyk D.; Frolov G.; Ievtushenko A.
Article.Abstract: BN–Ti, BN–Cr, BN–Al, and BN–Zr composite nanopowders were synthesized under concentrated light in nitrogen and tested as cathodically polarized electrodes in 0.1 M H₂SO₄. The ultrafast heating route produced structurally heterogeneous, partially oxidized composites, which were heat-treated at 400 °C to reduce surface-defect effects. XRD and Raman revealed amorphous/turbostratic BN domains with boron oxides (B₂O₃, H₃BO₃) and dispersed metal oxides (TiO₂, ZrO₂, Cr₂O₃, γ-Al₂O₃), without bulk nitride/boride phases. TEM showed additive-dependent architectures: BN–Cr formed fibrous networks of high surface area, while BN–Ti/Zr produced agglomerated nanoparticles. Electrochemically, BN–Cr delivered the highest instantaneous currents and earliest polarization onset, BN–Al the largest integrated charge via acid-induced restructuring of γ-Al₂O₃, and BN–Ti/Zr intermediate capacitive responses. Cycling confirmed BN’s stabilizing role, suppressing oxide dissolution and enabling beneficial surface reconstruction. These results establish BN–metal composites as durable, composition-tunable electrodes in acidic environments, with additive choice governing architecture, kinetics, and charge-storage behavior.

Article.Title: Psychomotor disturbances in neuronal growth regulator-1-deficient (Negr1−/−) mice are associated with alterations in hippocampal and skeletal muscle signaling
Article.Authors: Muthuraman S.; Jayaram M.; Lavogina D.; Pilve B.; Reinsberg A.; Mikheim K.; Vasar E.; Philips M.; Singh K.
Article.Abstract: The motor domain has emerged as a fundamental transdiagnostic dimension of neuropsychiatric disorders, reflecting dysfunction in neural circuits underlying movement, cognition, and behavior. Neuronal growth regulator 1 (NEGR1) is a synaptic cell adhesion molecule genetically linked to multiple neuropsychiatric disorders. Despite its function in neural development and widespread expression in the central and peripheral nervous systems, its involvement in the motor domain remains unknown. Here, we investigated the motor domain by comprehensively characterizing psychomotor function and associated molecular alterations in adult male and female Negr1 −/− mice. Negr1 deficiency produced a motor phenotype characterized by altered run characteristics, gait dynamics, including swing speed, stride length and muscle strength, with molecular changes in the hippocampus and skeletal muscle. Male Negr1 −/− mice exhibited increased casein kinase 2 (CK2) activity in the hippocampus and skeletal muscle, whereas females showed reduced activity of CK2 and Rho-associated coiled-coil-containing protein kinase (ROCK) only in the hippocampus. Skeletal muscle further exhibited transcript-level alterations in genes encoding proteins involved in mitochondrial biology and contractility. Together, these findings indicate co-occurring central and peripheral molecular alterations underlying the multisystem psychomotor phenotype associated with Negr1 deficiency.

Article.Title: An interpretable synthetic benchmark for machine learning in low-strain pile integrity testing
Article.Authors: Öztürk Ö.; Özacar V.; Canbula B.; Özacar T.
Article.Abstract: Low-strain pile integrity testing (LSPIT) is widely used for rapid pile screening, but reflectogram interpretation remains difficult because defect morphology, axial extent, signed relative cross-sectional change, attenuation, and wave propagation jointly shape the response. This study reformulates a synthetic archive of 90,900 reflectograms as a physically stratified machine-learning benchmark. Nine benchmark views (A0–A8) isolate neutral cases, axial-domain restrictions, severity thresholds, defect-length regimes, and sign regimes. Four objectives are considered: morphology classification, sign classification, absolute-severity regression, and signed-severity regression. In addition to the representation-specific baseline grid, a controlled five-fold grouped comparison was added in which logistic/ridge models, random forests, and a profile multilayer perceptron used the same 68-dimensional reflectogram-profile vector and identical train/validation/test groups. Under this matched condition, random forests achieved morphology accuracy of 0.810±0.010 and sign accuracy of 0.858±0.002; the corresponding profile-MLP values were 0.756±0.008 and 0.850±0.007. For signed severity, random forest and profile MLP obtained $$R^2$$ values of 0.626±0.008 and 0.622±0.014, with mean absolute errors of 10.82±0.10 and 12.22±0.14 percentage points. A sample-size- and target-matched A5–A6 experiment confirmed that short defects consistently facilitate morphology recognition, but showed that severity difficulty is non-monotonic and depends jointly on axial length, morphology, and limited identifiability under the profile representation. A fourfold tail-weighting sensitivity analysis reduced severe-loss miss rates but increased central-range error, indicating both loss-driven and representation-limited causes of tail compression. The study is explicitly limited to synthetic benchmark evaluation; it provides a transparent basis for future, independently grounded field or high-fidelity numerical validation rather than evidence of deployment readiness.

Article.Title: Heteroatom–connectivity engineering of benzofused oligomers for hydrogen fluoride capture
Article.Authors: Noohi B.; Shahnoorian M.; Arabieh M.; Zahedi M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hydrogen fluoride (HF) is a hazardous industrial gas, motivating molecular strategies for its capture and detection. Dispersion-corrected density functional theory was used to examine HF adsorption on O-, N-, S-, P-, ON-, and SN-containing benzofused oligomers with 2,5-, 2,6-, and 4,7-connectivities. Mixed-heteroatom ON and SN motifs exhibited stronger adsorption than single-heteroatom analogues, a trend retained after counterpoise adjustment for the monomeric complexes and supported by QTAIM analysis. Heteroatom composition and connectivity generally affected adsorption more strongly than oligomer length. The 2,5-ON and 2,6-SN series showed diminishing adsorption-energy changes upon chain extension, whereas the shorter 4,7 series was not regarded as chain-length converged. Among selected systems, 2,5-ON maintained nearly linear N···H–F geometries, 4,7-ON exhibited pronounced electrostatic-potential separation, and 2,6-SN showed the largest F–H vibrational redshift. Changes in charge distribution, dipole moment, polarizability, and electrostatic potential indicated localized polarization responses, with comparatively modest frontier-orbital effects. Arrhenius-based recovery times decreased with increasing temperature but constitute model-dependent estimates, not experimental evidence of reversibility. Because these results derive from isolated finite oligomers, validation using extended models and competitive adsorption under humid conditions remains necessary.

Article.Title: Potential role of PDLIM1 in the tumorigenesis of acute myeloid leukemia: a comprehensive bioinformatics and in vitro study
Article.Authors: Liu A.; Yu C.; Peng X.; Liu J.; Chen W.; Li X.; Zhang Y.; Lu C.; Liu Y.; Lai Y.
Article.Abstract: PDLIM1 has been associated with the development of multiple malignancies, but its expression profile and clinical relevance in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) have not been fully characterized. In this study, publicly available datasets were analyzed to assess differences in PDLIM1 mRNA expression between AML samples and healthy controls, while its protein abundance was preliminarily examined by immunohistochemistry. CCK8 and Transwell assays were used to evaluate the effects of PDLIM1 on the proliferation, invasion, and migration of AML cells. The molecular functions of PDLIM1 were investigated using an integrated multi-omics framework that included weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), machine learning, single-cell RNA sequencing, immune cell infiltration assessment, and functional enrichment analysis. Molecular docking was also performed with AutoDock Vina to estimate the binding affinities of PDLIM1 for candidate compounds, and the highest-ranking binding conformations were visualized using PyMOL. PDLIM1 was markedly upregulated in AML tissues compared with healthy control tissues, with a standardized mean difference of 0.91 (95% CI, 0.53–1.29). This result was preliminarily validated by immunohistochemistry (IHC) staining. Clinicopathological analysis indicated that elevated PDLIM1 expression was associated with greater proportions of blasts in the bone marrow and peripheral blood, as well as increased peripheral white blood cell counts. CCK8 and Transwell assays revealed that overexpression of PDLIM1 significantly enhanced the proliferation, invasion, and migration abilities of AML cells. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis demonstrated that PDLIM1 was primarily enriched in leukemia stem cell (LSC) and AML cell populations, indicating that it may serve as a molecular marker for LSCs. WGCNA identified 332 genes related to PDLIM1 expression. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes analysis further revealed significant enrichment of these genes in several biological pathways, including focal adhesion. Potential small-molecule agents associated with PDLIM1 expression were subsequently screened through the Gene Set Cancer Analysis database. The highest-ranked compounds were A-770041, afatinib, WZ-1-84, dasatinib, erlotinib, gefitinib, saracatinib, and WH-4-023. Among these compounds, A-770041 exhibited the lowest predicted binding energy, and local docking visualization identified multiple intermolecular interactions at favorable distances, suggesting that it may be the most promising candidate ligand among those evaluated. Collectively, these findings indicate that PDLIM1 is markedly upregulated in AML and LSCs and may represent a potential therapeutic target.

Article.Title: Assessing the feasibility of up-scaling grapevine physiological trait estimation using multispectral UAV imagery
Article.Authors: Lutz M.; Heßdörfer D.; Ullmann T.; Brandmeier M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Scalable grapevine physiological assessment is relevant for precision viticulture, but direct physiological measurements are labor-intensive and leaf-specific. This study evaluated whether a machine-learning framework developed for leaf-level hyperspectral measurements can be applied to UAV-derived multispectral imagery. In situ hyperspectral observations from 2024 and 2025 were combined and restricted to the visible and near-infrared (VNIR) range from 350 to 1000 nm to align with common UAV spectral coverage and assess multi-temporal performance and spectral resampling. UAV-derived multispectral observations from 2025 were analyzed for sunlit, shaded, and combined canopy extraction strategies. First-derivative preprocessing improved in situ performance, yielding best $$\textrm{R}^{2}$$ values of 0.811 for net assimilation rate $$ A $$ , 0.792 for electron transport rate ETR, and 0.890 for effective quantum yield of photosystem II $$ \Phi _{\text {PSII}} $$ . Moderate spectral resampling caused limited performance losses for $$ A $$ and ETR. UAV-based models yielded $$\textrm{R}^{2}$$ up to 0.765 for $$ A $$ , 0.768 for ETR, and 0.901 for $$ \Phi _{\text {PSII}} $$ . Shaded and combined observations improved $$ A $$ and ETR predictions relative to sunlit observations, whereas $$ \Phi _{\text {PSII}} $$ remained robust across extraction strategies. Plant-grouped validation supported generalization to unseen vines, whereas leave-one-date-out validation failed to demonstrate robust generalization to unseen measurement dates, highlighting temporal generalization as a key limitation of the UAV-based approach.

Article.Title: Alcohol and acute kidney injury—prospective evidence from the UK Biobank in 250,791 alcohol consumers
Article.Authors: Schutte R.; Zhang J.; Pierscionek B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The relationship between alcohol consumption and acute kidney injury (AKI) is controversial. Current understanding is AKI develops secondary to alcohol-induced liver disease. However, in vitro and in vivo evidence suggests alcohol could cause renal damage directly. We investigated associations between incident AKI and consumption of spirits, beer, red wine and white wine, independent of liver disease. We also investigated associations between these drink types and neutrophils and C-reactive protein (CRP), as well as their interactions in association with AKI. UK Biobank involved baseline data collection from 22 assessment centres across the United Kingdom. The cohort consisted of 250,791 current alcohol consumers. Participants were followed for a median 14.0 years capturing incident AKI events. Alcohol intake (units/week), C-reactive protein (mg/L) level and neutrophil count (cells/µL) were captured at baseline. Alcohol intake was reported as units per week. After adjustment for covariables and/or potential confounders in Cox proportional hazard regression analyses, spirits (HR, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.30 to 1.50) and beer (HR, 1.24; 95% CI, 1.17 to 1.32) consumption were associated with AKI, while associations were absent for red wine (HR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.90 to 1.02) and white wine (HR, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.98 to 1.14). Neutrophils and CRP increased by tertiles of spirits (both P -trend ≤ 0.001) and beer (both P -trend < 0.001) consumption, while decreases were observed by tertiles of red wine (both P -trend < 0.001) and white wine (both P -trend < 0.001) consumption. CRP (HR, 1.41; 95% CI, 1.34 to 1.47) and neutrophils (HR, 2.60; 95% CI, 2.25 to 3.01) associated with AKI and interactions existed with spirits (both P < 0.001) and beer (both P < 0.001) in association with AKI. Alcohol captured from spirits and beer consumption was associated with AKI, independent of liver disease. The significant interactions between inflammatory markers and spirits and beer consumption in association with AKI supports current in vitro and in vivo evidence proposing a direct mechanistic link.

Article.Title: Neonatal mortality prediction under extreme class imbalance: calibrated supervised models and exploratory phenotype analysis in a population-based Iranian registry
Article.Authors: Alamdarloo S.; Kanafchian A.; Barzegar H.; Cisakht H.; Asadi N.; Asghari F.; Montaseri A.; Bahrami R.; Bazrafshan K.; Hashemi A.; Haghighi A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Neonatal mortality remains a leading contributor to under-five deaths, yet early, individualized risk prediction is hampered by the rarity of the outcome and by limited attention to calibration and interpretability in prior models. We developed and stress-tested machine learning (ML) models for neonatal mortality prediction in a large, population-based cohort, integrating probability calibration, explainable AI, and exploratory unsupervised phenotyping. The development cohort of 61,517 neonates (131 deaths; class imbalance 1:469) was used to train L2-regularized logistic regression (LR) and LightGBM models on 60 routinely available perinatal features. performance was assessed by discrimination (AUROC, AUPRC), calibration, and decision-curve analysis, while SHAP and four unsupervised methods (UMAP, K-means, Isolation Forest, Apriori) characterized the underlying risk structure. Locked models then underwent a one-time case-only external stress test on 604 deceased neonates from a separate center and later period. LR achieved an AUROC of 0.955 (LightGBM, 0.944); at the optimal threshold (τ*=0.004) it captured 87.8% of deaths at 97.3% specificity, and positive net clinical benefit. In the external stress test, LR flagged 69.5% of deaths. Exploratory unsupervised analyses, fitted without outcome labels and evaluated post hoc against mortality, described a single high-risk phenotype; a K-means cluster comprising 6.7% of neonates contained 89.3% of all deaths. In this large, heterogeneous cohort, well-regularized ML models provided calibrated, interpretable, and early neonatal mortality risk stratification. The case-only design of the external cohort permits assessment of sensitivity only; external discrimination and calibration remain to be established, and prospective evaluation is warranted before clinical deployment.

Article.Title: Study on the enrichment of refractory oxidized lead ores from mining stockpiles using combined electrochemical polarization
Article.Authors: Dospayev М.; Figurinene I.; Jashibekova А.; Dospayev D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Man-made oxidized nonferrous metal ores accumulate in large quantities in mining plants, causing environmental problems and polluting the soil, groundwater, and atmosphere with toxic heavy metals. Traditional flotation is often ineffective and fails to yield acceptable levels of nonferrous metal recovery. This study aims to use refractory oxidized lead ore electrochemical enrichment to increase lead recovery into flotation concentrates to 93–95% from mining stockpiles. Cerussite is the primary lead mineral in the ore. Voltammetric measurements established that cerussite reduction proceeds partly via decomposition, with the formation of Pb 2+ ions, and partly through the direct solid-state discharge of mineral particles to elemental lead. To convert the mineral cerussite to an easily floatable sulfide form, the traditional flotation reagent sodium sulfide was used. Under microelectrolysis conditions in a weakly alkaline solution of sodium sulfide, lead cations formed during the solid-phase decomposition of cerussite interact with sulfide ions and form lead sulfides. The electrode mechanisms of cerussite mineral sulfidization were used for the electrochemical enrichment of oxidized lead ore. Sulfidization of ore from the Alaigyr deposit (Republic of Kazakhstan) was carried out by electrolysis under galvanostatic conditions in a specially designed electrolyzer with separated cathodic and anodic compartments. A multifactorial model of lead recovery into sulfide concentrate was obtained, indicating that a high degree of recovery of 98.56% was achieved under the experimentally determined optimal conditions. The chemical and phase compositions of the initial oxidized lead ore, cerussite, lead sulfide, and sulfide concentrate were determined using chemical analysis, X-ray diffraction, and electron microscopy.

Article.Title: Balancing nutritional quality and consumer acceptance in boiled beetroot (Beta vulgaris L.): effects of household boiling time on bioactive compounds, color, texture, and sensory attributes
Article.Authors: Bahi A.; Yousif N.; Kaleem S.; Sabbagh N.; Alzarouni D.; Maraqa Y.; Niroula A.; Nazir A.; Ranneh Y.; Shahbaz H.; Fadel A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Boiling is a common household method for preparing beetroot, but the boiling duration associated with higher measured bioactive compound concentrations may not correspond to that associated with consumer preference. This study investigated the effects of household-relevant boiling times (0–60 min) on the proximate composition, total phenolic content, DPPH radical-scavenging activity, betalain content, color parameters, peak puncture resistance, and consumer acceptance of beetroot ( Beta vulgaris L.). Boiling time significantly affected the physicochemical and sensory characteristics of beetroot. At 30 min, total phenolic content, DPPH radical-scavenging activity, and betalain content reached 7.61 mg GAE/g FW, 35.68%, and 0.54 mg/g FW, respectively, compared with 2.21 mg GAE/g FW, 13.35%, and 0.21 mg/g FW in raw beetroot. At 60 min, the corresponding values were 5.06 mg GAE/g FW, 34.06%, and 0.25 mg/g FW, indicating non-linear responses to boiling duration rather than a uniform decline after 30 min. Overall liking increased from 1.85 for raw beetroot to 5.08–6.88 among the cooked treatments, although the cooked samples did not differ significantly from one another in overall liking. Redness and chroma were highest at 30 min, although both increased again at 60 min after declining at 45 min. Peak puncture force decreased after reaching its highest value at 15 min, and the 60-min treatment showed the lowest numerical value. All cooked treatments were preferred to the raw sample; the 60-min treatment received the highest numerical overall-liking score, although overall liking did not differ significantly among the cooked treatments. Sweetness, firmness, and juiciness were the sensory attributes most clearly associated with liking. The boiling duration associated with the highest measured chemical and color values differed from that associated with the highest numerical consumer preference. Under the conditions of this study, 30 min produced the highest measured total phenolic and betalain concentrations, redness, and chroma, whereas the 60-min sample received the highest numerical overall-liking score. These findings demonstrate trade-offs among quality attributes and highlight the importance of considering multiple responses when recommending domestic boiling conditions for beetroot.

Article.Title: Structural, supramolecular and computational insights into the ALS inhibitor pyroxsulam: crystal structure, reactivity and bioactivity
Article.Authors: Potla K.; Vankayalapati S.; Nathaniel C.; Adimule S.; Kailasam K.; Shanthi J.; Alam M.; Tawfeek A.; Bilal H.; Islam M.
Article.Abstract: Triazolopyrimidine-2-sulfonanilides, recognized as bioisosteres of sulfonylurea herbicides, represent an important class of acetohydroxyacid synthase (AHAS/ALS) inhibitors widely employed for the selective control of broadleaf and grass weeds in cereal crops. Despite their extensive agricultural applications, detailed understanding of the structural, electronic, intermolecular, and biological characteristics governing their inhibitory behavior remains limited. In this context, the present work reports a comprehensive experimental and computational investigation of Pyroxsulam (PS; IUPAC name: N-(5,7-dimethoxy-[1,2,4]triazolo[1,5-a]pyrimidin-2-yl)-2-methoxy-4-(trifluoromethyl)pyridine-3-sulfonamide) to elucidate its structural stability, reactivity, sensitivity, and molecular interaction properties. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis reveals that Pyroxsulam adopts an “L”-shaped conformation with two nearly planar fragments connected through the sulfur atom, exhibiting a dihedral angle of 78.42(5)° and a gauche C–S–N–C torsion angle of 55.9(2)°. The crystal packing is stabilized by C–H···O, N–H···N, C–H···π, and π···π interactions, forming one-dimensional supramolecular ribbons. Hirshfeld surface and energy framework analyses confirm the dominant role of dispersion and hydrogen-bonding interactions in crystal stabilization. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations performed at the B3LYP/6–311++ G(d,p) level provided optimized geometrical parameters and electronic descriptors consistent with the experimental observations. Molecular electrostatic potential (MEP), reduced density gradient (RDG), ELF, and QTAIM analyses identified electrophilic and nucleophilic regions and highlighted the significance of weak intermolecular interactions. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated favorable binding affinity of Pyroxsulam toward ALS with a binding energy of − 6.69 kcal mol −1 , stabilized through hydrogen bonding and π–π stacking interactions within the active site. The combined findings provide deeper insight into the structural and electronic behavior of Pyroxsulam and contribute to advancing the understanding of triazolopyrimidine-based ALS inhibitors as selective agrochemical agents.

Article.Title: Odorant profiling in beer: a detailed evaluation of often overlooked SPME extraction parameters
Article.Authors: Wieczorek M.; Olczyk A.; Jeleń H.
Article.Abstract: Solid Phase Microextraction coupled with gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (SPME–GC–MS) has become a widely used tool for food, including beer volatilome analysis; however, critical extraction parameters influencing reproducibility, representativeness, and data interpretation are often insufficiently considered. In this study, we systematically investigate the impact of selected, frequently overlooked SPME parameters on the profiling of beer aroma compounds, using a commercial lager beer as a model matrix. The effects of sample volume, extraction time, degassing procedure, and repeated extractions from a single vial were evaluated using representative volatile analytes differing in polarity and volatility, as well as through non-targeted aroma profiling. This work provides experimental evidence that seemingly minor SPME parameters can profoundly influence beer aroma analysis. The findings emphasize the necessity of deliberate experimental design and a thorough understanding of SPME fundamentals to ensure reliable qualitative and quantitative interpretation of volatile profiles in complex food matrices.

Article.Title: Broadband multi-functional graphene-MoS$$_2$$ polarization conversion metasurface for biomolecular refractive index sensing at the THz band
Article.Authors: Zakeri H.; Moradi G.; Tavakoli A.
Article.Abstract: A tunable multifunctional reflective metasurface is proposed and numerically studied for mid-terahertz (THz) polarization conversion and refractive-index sensing. The unit cell comprises two orthogonally arranged elliptical resonators with rectangular cross-slots, integrated with a graphene layer, a MoS \(_2\) layer, a SiO \(_2\) spacer, and a gold ground plane. The electromagnetic characteristics of the structure are investigated using the frequency-domain finite-element method (FEM), with graphene and MoS \(_2\) described by the Kubo and Drude models, respectively. Owing to the hybrid graphene–MoS \(_2\) configuration, the metasurface supports dual-band linear-to-linear (LP-to-LP) polarization conversion in the ranges 1.233–1.409 THz and 2.172–2.215 THz, as well as broadband linear-to-circular (LP-to-CP) polarization conversion from 1.574 to 2.105 THz. The polarization-conversion performance remains high across the operating bands and is maintained for incident angles up to 45 \(^\circ\) . In addition, the proposed metasurface demonstrates high-performance refractive-index sensing capability through analyte-induced spectral resonance shifts. Across the biological refractive-index range ( \(n = 1.33\) –1.49), the sensor exhibits average sensitivities of 380.5 GHz/RIU and 748.2 GHz/RIU for the first and second resonance modes, respectively, reaching peak local sensitivities of up to 1.25 THz/RIU and 1.45 THz/RIU for high-index biological analytes. Furthermore, the device achieves maximum figure-of-merit (FOM) values of 6.41 RIU \(^{-1}\) and 6.04 RIU \(^{-1}\) , quality factors ranging from 6.6 to 10.8 (first resonance) and 9.2 to 15.4 (second resonance), and a minimum limit of detection (LOD) of 0.0078 RIU. The enhanced field confinement and dynamic electrostatic tunability make the proposed metasurface a promising platform for biomedical diagnostic applications-such as distinguishing blood components, including proteins, glucose, urea, lipids, and collagen-as well as compact, multifunctional THz polarization control.

Article.Title: Channel characteristics of long-distance magnetic induction based through-the-earth communication and performance analysis
Article.Authors: Ma C.; Zhu Y.; Sun L.; Zhu B.; Cheng H.; Jia X.; Wang Y.; Dai M.; Yang W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Magnetic induction (MI) based through-the-earth (TTE) communication has low path loss, no multipath effect and stable transmission channel. The generation and propagation of magnetic fields in MI based TTE communication do not have the strict requirements of antenna size than that in electromagnetic wave based TTE communication, which is conducive to achieving bidirectional communication between the ground and underground. An equivalent circuit of the receiving and transmitting circuit has been established for long-distance MI based TTE communication, and the transmission function of MI based TTE communication channel can be characterized using the equivalent circuit of the receiving and transmitting circuit. The noise of receivers of MI based TTE communication mainly includes thermal noise on the receiving circuit and electromagnetic noise in the environment where the receiving coil is located. The noise characteristics of receivers of MI based TTE communication were analyzed. The channel characteristics of MI based TTE communication such as amplitude frequency response, impulse response and bandwidth were analyzed by simulation under different TTE medium parameters and TTE communication distance. The amplitude spectrum of the received signal was compared with the amplitude spectrum of the noise. A simulation platform of MI based TTE communication was built, and the performance with BPSK and QPSK modulation was compared under different TTE medium parameters and TTE communication distance. The maximum modulation order that can be adopted by MI based TTE communication under different TTE medium parameters and TTE communication distance was given. These play an important role in improving the performance of long-distance MI based TTE communication systems.

Article.Title: IκB kinase epsilon deficiency attenuates osteoarthritis-associated pain and synovitis with limited cartilage protection in complementary mouse models
Article.Authors: Sakai M.; Akasaki Y.; Hyodo Y.; Kurakazu I.; Uchida T.; Hirose R.; Kuwahara M.; Kita T.; Kato K.; Ziyang L.; Eto G.; Nakashima Y.
Article.Abstract: Osteoarthritis is a whole-joint disease characterized by cartilage degeneration, synovial inflammation, and chronic pain, yet the causal role of IκB kinase epsilon (IKKε) in these distinct disease components remains unclear. We therefore investigated whether IKKε contributes to structural joint degeneration, synovial inflammation, and OA-associated pain using complementary in vitro and in vivo analyses in IKKε-deficient mice. IKKε deficiency reduced c-Jun phosphorylation, decreased Mmp13 expression in primary chondrocytes, and decreased Ccl2 expression in synovial cells, whereas p65 phosphorylation did not differ significantly between genotypes. In vivo, IKKε deficiency attenuated synovitis and mechanical hypersensitivity in the MIA model. In the DMM + MCLT model, inflammatory and catabolic markers in cartilage were reduced, whereas no statistically significant reduction in histological cartilage degeneration was detected. IKKε-deficient chondrocytes also showed increased Ikkβ and Tbk1 expression, which may represent a potential adaptive response, although functional compensation was not established. Together, these findings show that IKKε deficiency attenuates OA-associated synovitis and pain-related behavior and alters cartilage inflammatory and catabolic signaling, while its effect on structural cartilage degeneration remains uncertain, supporting the potential of IKKε as a therapeutic target for OA pain and synovial pathology.

Article.Title: Loneliness, social support, and depressive symptoms among men who acquired HIV through sexual transmission in China
Article.Authors: Chen R.; Que J.; Zeng J.; Lin Y.; Wei W.; Huang Y.; Zheng C.; Zheng Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Loneliness and social support are important psychosocial correlates of depressive symptoms among people living with HIV, but their interrelationships remain insufficiently understood. This cross-sectional study examined associations among loneliness, social support, and depressive symptoms in 436 men living with HIV who acquired infection through sexual transmission. Participants completed an online questionnaire including sociodemographic information, the Patient Health Questionnaire-9, the Social Support Rating Scale, and the UCLA Loneliness Scale. Correlation, multivariable logistic regression, and bootstrap mediation analyses were performed. Loneliness was positively associated with depressive symptoms, whereas social support was inversely associated with loneliness and depressive symptoms. In adjusted logistic regression, high loneliness was associated with greater odds of depressive symptoms, while higher total social support, subjective support, and support utilization were associated with lower odds. Mediation analysis showed that social support partially mediated the association between loneliness and depressive symptoms, accounting for 21.3% of the total effect. These findings suggest that interventions addressing both loneliness and social support may help improve mental health outcomes in this population.
