The synthesized nanocomposites were characterized by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), simultaneous thermal analysis (STA), field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) to elucidate their functional groups, crystal structure, and morphological features. The experimental results demonstrated that the concurrent use of bicarbonate and ammonium significantly influenced the morphology of the nanocomposites and, consequently, their adsorption performance. Furthermore, with increasing ZnO content, the morphology of the nanocomposites evolved from platelet-like to aggregated structures. Under the optimized conditions of pH = 5, initial dye concentration of 10 mg L⁻¹, and a nanocomposite dosage of 0.02 g (40 wt% Al₂O₃–60 wt% ZnO), a maximum methyl orange removal efficiency of 98% was achieved.

Article.Title: Monolithically integrated photonic beamforming for a phased array receiver antenna
Article.Authors: Rama L.; Rodrigues C.; Santos J.; Vaz D.; Rodrigues F.; Teixeira A.; Varum T.; Nogueira R.; Drummond M.
Article.Abstract: We present, to the best of our knowledge, the first monolithically integrated RF-in/IF-out photonic beamformer for a phased-array receiver antenna, fabricated on an \(8\times 4~\text {mm}^2\) Indium Phosphide die. The beamformer is designed to receive four input RF signals and one RF local oscillator, convert them to the optical domain, apply complex weighting, and down-convert the added signals to a beamformed IF output. The presented photonic beamformer is enabled by a novel laser generation stage requiring no isolation, injection locking, or optical filtering. A conversion loss of 79 dB was measured, primarily dominated by lossy passive devices. Despite the significant conversion loss, beamforming was demonstrated for three beam orientations, \(0^\circ\) and \(\pm 30^\circ\) , for \(f_{\text {RF}}=10\) GHz, \(f_{\text {LO}}=14\) GHz and \(f_{\text {IF}}=4\) GHz, using three out of four designed channels, and considering a virtual linear phased array antenna receiver.

Article.Title: The impact of a synchronized multimodal AI interface configuration on consumer experience journey and satisfaction
Article.Authors: Pan Z.
Article.Abstract: With the rapid integration of multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) into digital interfaces, understanding how combined visual, auditory, and textual cues influence consumers' experience journeys and satisfaction has become critically important for both scholars and practitioners. While prior research has examined individual modalities in isolation, the comparative effects of a specific rich multimodal interface configuration versus a minimal-modality baseline across different stages of the consumer journey remain underexplored. This study draws on cue utilization theory, presence theory, and the customer journey framework to investigate how exposure to a synchronized multimodal AI interface (text + voice + animated avatar) versus a text-only interface affects consumer satisfaction through three experimentally induced journey stages: search, evaluation, and post-purchase. A between-subjects online experiment (N = 320 recruited; 312 retained after screening) was conducted using a simulated e-commerce platform where participants interacted with an AI shopping assistant featuring either text-only or synchronized text-voice-avatar cues. Results from SEM indicate that the synchronized multimodal interface was associated with higher perceived diagnosticity and immersion, which in turn were related to higher satisfaction across all three stages. The configuration–satisfaction contrast was largest for evaluation satisfaction (Cohen’s d = 1.58, 95% CI [1.33, 1.83]); the indirect-effect patterns via perceived diagnosticity and immersion were statistically consistent with, but not demonstrative of, the proposed pathways. We emphasize that the two conditions differ not only in synchronization but also in modality count, anthropomorphic cues, and social presence; accordingly, all findings are interpreted as pertaining to the interface configuration as a whole, not to integration quality as an isolated construct. Theoretical contributions include extending cue utilization theory in the form of a speculative conjecture and identifying stage-specific patterns. Managerial implications suggest that e-commerce platforms should consider synchronized multimodal cue design, particularly during product comparison phases in simulated and early deployment contexts, and should be regarded as preliminary pending field validation.

Article.Title: Meteorological forecasting of respiratory diseases incidence with geospatial and machine learning methods
Article.Authors: Arroquia-Cuadros B.; Marqués-Mateu Á.; Fdez-Arroyabe P.; Sebastia L.
Article.Abstract: Weather conditions play a significant role in shaping human health, particularly in the incidence of respiratory diseases. This study proposes a workflow to predict hospital admissions related to respiratory conditions by integrating heterogeneous environmental and health data sources. A 15-year time series of meteorological data was combined with geographic and demographic information to derive biometeorological indices associated with hypoxia and hyperoxia. To account for spatial variability, three clustering techniques—k-means, Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA), and Spatial ’K’luster Analysis by Tree Edge Removal (SKATER)—were applied to define intra-provincial regions for targeted data extraction from raster models. These approaches were compared with conventional aggregation at the provincial level. Interpretable machine learning models, specifically tree-based algorithms, were used to evaluate predictive performance. The proposed spatial clustering strategies achieved comparable or improved performance relative to the baseline approach. Experiments conducted in three Spanish provinces (Cantabria, Madrid, and Valencia) yielded mean absolute errors ranging from approximately 5.4 to 8.2 cases per million inhabitants, depending on the province. Results highlight the relevance of spatially refined environmental data in improving predictive accuracy. The integration of geospatial data, meteorological models, and machine learning provides an effective framework for forecasting respiratory disease incidence. This approach supports the development of early warning systems and risk management strategies based on environmental monitoring. In this article we present how to gather, transform and model datasets from several data sources to predict hospital admissions of respiratory diseases. We also draw the importance of geographical distribution of population in order to determine the appropriate method to extract meteorological data.

Article.Title: CDA-YOLO: an improved YOLOv11 model for PCB defect detection
Article.Authors: Yuan A.; Li J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Printed circuit boards (PCBs) are fundamental to modern electronic systems, and their manufacturing quality directly determines the performance and reliability of the final product. However, existing YOLO‑based defect detection models still face critical challenges, including high miss rates for tiny defects and frequent false positives caused by complex background textures. To address these issues, we propose CDA‑YOLO, an enhanced YOLOv11 framework incorporating three key innovations. First, a Cross-level Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network (CBiFPN) is designed, which effectively alleviates the loss of fine-grained details of small targets as features propagate through deep layers. Second, a lightweight Dual-Scale Convolution module (DualScaleConv) is proposed, which employs a parallel branch structure to simultaneously capture local details and global contextual information. Finally, a parameter-free average attention mechanism (PfAAM) is integrated into the C3k2 module to enhance the feature response in defect-related regions and suppresses background noise. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves competitive performance on the PCB defect dataset, with mAP@0.5 reaching 96.1% and mAP@0.5:0.95 reaching 56.0%, corresponding to improvements of 2.8% and 3.4% over the baseline YOLOv11, respectively. These results validate that CDA-YOLO offers an efficient and robust solution for industrial-grade PCB defect detection.

Article.Title: Advancing automatic classification of single fine particles via multimodal deep learning framework
Article.Authors: Khadgi J.; Lee H.; Park K.; Choi S.; Kim Y.; Shin H.; Park K.
Article.Abstract: The accurate identification and classification of single fine particles are essential for understanding emission sources, atmospheric processes, and their subsequent impacts on climate and health. However, this task remains challenging due to the highly diverse and overlapping physicochemical characteristics of various particle types. Conventional single particle analysis relies heavily on manual interpretation, which is inherently slow, subjective, and limited in scalability. To overcome these limitations, this study implemented a multimodal deep learning fusion framework that classifies fine particles into seven distinct types: dust (206), fly ash (64), metals (164), organic-rich (551), sea spray (91), soot (299), and sulfur-rich (247), by simultaneously fusing three modalities (morphology, size, and elemental composition). A comprehensive dataset of 1,622 single particles, collected from diverse emission sources and ambient environments, was utilized for model development and evaluation. Three multimodal fusion strategies were systematically evaluated: early fusion (concatenating all modalities at an early stage), traditional joint fusion (integrating independently extracted features), and attention-based fusion (dynamically focusing on the most informative features within and across modalities). The attention-based fusion architecture achieved the highest predictive performance, yielding an overall accuracy of 89.6%, a sensitivity of 0.90, and a specificity of 0.98. Furthermore, an interpretability analysis revealed that the model’s classification decisions were predominantly governed by distinctive elemental composition and morphological patterns. By rapidly classifying thousands of individual particles within minutes, this automated, high-throughput framework provides a highly scalable solution for single-particle analysis, thereby facilitating a more profound understanding of atmospheric aerosol sources, transformation mechanisms, and their broader climate and health impacts.

Article.Title: A calibrated-domain DEM–machine learning assessment of asphalt concrete stiffness and micromechanical response
Article.Authors: Imoh U.; Movahedi Rad M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Asphalt concrete is a heterogeneous composite whose stiffness and damage response depend on aggregate contacts, binder-mediated bonding, air voids, force chain evolution, and progressive bond failure. This study presents a calibrated-domain assessment of an AC-16C mixture using three two-dimensional Discrete Element Method contact/bond formulations: the linear parallel bond, soft-bond, and contact-bond models, together with a machine-learning stiffness surrogate. The 160 records constitute a hybrid laboratory–DEM/parametric dataset within a single AC-16C domain, rather than 160 physically distinct mixtures. The DEM outputs were used to interpret the contact forces, particle displacement, bond breakage, coordination number, energy dissipation, and fracture localization. The Linear Parallel Bond Model produced the stiffest response because it transferred both force and moment; the Soft-Bond Model represented gradual softening and energy dissipation and the Contact-Bond Model exhibited earlier localized bond failure. The machine learning models used uniaxial compressive strength, indirect tensile strength, dynamic modulus, and Poisson’s ratio to predict the experimental elastic modulus; DEM-derived descriptors were not included as predictors. Using a 112/24/24 training, validation, and holdout partition, Random Forest and XGBoost achieved holdout R 2 values of 0.940 and 0.928, respectively, whereas the ANN/MLP was less stable, with an R 2 of 0.847. Because the dynamic modulus dominated the feature importance, the high predictive accuracy primarily reflected the stiffness-variable collinearity within the calibrated domain. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted as internal calibrated-domain interpolation rather than external validation or evidence of a general microstructure–property relationship. Broader application requires physically independent mixtures, complete DEM reproducibility information, three-dimensional verification, raw data disclosure, and measured runtime comparisons.

Article.Title: In situ evaluation of 3D polymeric microstructures integrated into a microfluidic channel
Article.Authors: Rekštytė Paipulienė S.; Paipulas D.; Mizeikis V.
Article.Abstract: We investigate the applicability of photoluminescence (PL) mapping technique for in situ evaluation of the polymeric microstructures fabricated by direct laser writing in pre-polymers (DLW-PP), both in open and closed (fully three-dimensional) microfluidic channels, where conventional characterization is often challenging. The technique utilizes quenching of photo-initiator emission in polymerized regions, enabling visualization of fabricated features prior to development. PL mapping enables accurate three-dimensional localization before sample development and can be repeatedly applied during fabrication without damaging the structures. The detected PL signal consistently exhibits a footprint smaller than the final developed structure. These results extend the applicability of PL mapping to fused silica microfluidic platforms and demonstrate its potential as a practical in situ tool for monitoring, alignment, and quality assessment of DLW-PP-fabricated microstructures.

Article.Title: Sensor-fused EKF-based navigation and kinematic modelling of a remotely controlled mobility vehicle in GPS denied agricultural environments
Article.Authors: Patle R.; Sahni R.; Ravuri S.; Harshavardhan K.; Saroj S.
Article.Abstract: Accurate row-following is essential for precision agricultural operations such as fertilizer application, inter-row cultivation, and site-specific crop management. However, reliable navigation in agricultural fields remains challenging under GPS-denied conditions caused by dense crop canopy, uneven terrain, and environmental disturbances. This study presents the development and validation of a low-cost sensor-fusion navigation framework for a remotely controlled agricultural mobility vehicle operating in GPS-denied environments. The system integrates wheel encoders and an inertial measurement unit within an extended kalman filter (EKF) for vehicle-state estimation, while ultrasonic sensing is used independently for obstacle detection and occupancy-grid mapping. A differential-drive kinematic model was employed for vehicle motion estimation, while Dijkstra-based path planning and closed-loop trajectory tracking enabled navigation during straight-row traversal and headland turning. Simulation studies in Gazebo and SolidWorks validated the kinematic behaviour and navigation performance before field implementation. Field experiments demonstrated that odometry-only navigation resulted in lateral-deviation RMSE values greater than 0.40 m, whereas the EKF-based framework achieved lateral-deviation RMSE values of 0.031 m for straight-row trials and 0.034 m for headland U-turn trials relative to an independent taut-line reference under the tested GPS-denied maize-field conditions. These results demonstrate consistent row-following and navigation performance under the tested field conditions.

Article.Title: Making informal religious representations visible in Japanese YouTube comments on Apple’s Crush advertisement
Article.Authors: Tsunematsu A.; Komiya A.; Takano R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract While formal religious representations have long been a central focus in psychology and cognitive science, informal religious representations remain understudied because their religious dimension is often embedded in everyday practices, values, and norms. This study examines how such representations may become visible in language on social media, focusing on Japan. We analyzed over 7,000 Japanese- and English-language YouTube comments on news coverage of Apple’s 2024 “Crush!” advertisement, which was criticized in Japan as conflicting with beliefs and values concerning respect for objects. Using a combination of dictionary-based and topic modeling approaches, we examined how emotion- and religion-related language appeared across linguistic contexts. The results showed that, in Japanese-language comments, terms related to respect for objects (e.g., mottainai ) appeared in topics linked to both religion-related and negative emotional language. A comparable pattern was not observed in the English-language corpus, although emotional expressions were prominent in these comments. Together, these findings suggest that informal religious representations can surface in everyday digital discourse through expressions concerning respect for objects that, in some contexts, carry religious resonance.

Article.Title: Prevalence of 406 rare diseases by ethnicity and recorded COVID-19 infection rates among 62.5 million people in England
Article.Authors: Gu Q.; Hasheminasab S.; Pineda-Moncusí M.; Chilala C.; Thygesen J.; Wu H.; Khalid S.; N/A N/A.; Coombe A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rare diseases (RD) are individually uncommon but collectively affect millions of people. Yet national estimates of their prevalence, especially across ethnic groups, are limited, and how the COVID-19 pandemic affected people with RD across ethnic groups is unknown. We aimed to estimate the prevalence of 406 RD by ethnicity, and to describe recorded COVID-19 infection across these RD and ethnic groups, in England. We conducted a cross-sectional study within the National Health Service (NHS) England Secure Data Environment, accessed via the British Heart Foundation (BHF) Data Science Centre’s CVD-COVID-UK/COVID-IMPACT Consortium, linking primary care, hospital, and mortality records for individuals alive on 31 July 2023. We calculated age- and sex-standardised prevalence for 406 RD, and recorded COVID-19 infection rates for the overall group, for each RD, and across the six-group Office for National Statistics (ONS) and 19-group NHS ethnicity classifications. Of 62.5 million people, 1.05 million (1.7%) had at least one of the 406 RD. Recorded COVID-19 infection was higher in the RD group than in the non-RD population (32.8% vs. 29.0%). Within the RD group, infection rates varied by ethnicity (e.g. 27.7% in the Pakistani and 23.8% in the Black African groups, versus 33.7% in the White British group) and by specific RD (24.6–41.2% among the 25 most common). Age- and sex-standardised prevalence also varied widely across ethnic groups, with substantial heterogeneity emerging only when broad categories were disaggregated into the more granular NHS classifications (for example, markedly elevated discoid lupus erythematosus prevalence in Black Caribbean but not Black African individuals, obscured within the aggregate “Black” category). This national, ethnicity-resolved map shows that rare-disease prevalence varies substantially across ethnic groups, with differences largely hidden within broad categories, and that recorded COVID-19 infection among people with RD varied across ethnic groups, with the highest rates observed in the ONS White and NHS White British groups. These findings provide a baseline to support earlier, fairer diagnosis and more targeted care.

Article.Title: Integrating bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing to identify mitochondrial quality control-related key genes in rheumatoid arthritis
Article.Authors: Xiao Y.; zhang J.; Su J.; Wu J.
Article.Abstract: Mitochondrial quality control (MQC) dysfunction contributes to rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but MQC-related genes in RA remain incompletely characterized. We integrated two bulk blood transcriptomic datasets and one peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset (248 RA and 88 control bulk samples; 11,719 cells from 3 RA and 3 healthy donors). Weighted gene co-expression network and differential expression analyses, combined with three machine-learning algorithms, identified candidate genes. Functional enrichment, immune infiltration, regulatory network, single-cell, cell–cell communication, pseudotime, metabolic, and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) analyses were performed. Nine MQC-related candidate genes were identified; CDC42 and RBBP7 emerged as key genes, with CDC42 upregulated and RBBP7 downregulated in RA. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) linked CDC42 to JAK–STAT signaling, while translation initiation showed opposite enrichment patterns. After multiple-testing correction, 15 immune-cell subsets differed between RA and controls; monocytes positively correlated with CDC42 and negatively with RBBP7. Single-cell analysis showed relatively high RBBP7 expression in B cells, motivating exploratory analyses of B-cell trajectories, metabolism, and predicted CCL5–CCR1 communication with monocytes. RT-qPCR confirmed the mRNA expression patterns. These findings identify CDC42 and RBBP7 as MQC-related key genes associated with distinct immune and metabolic features in blood-derived samples from patients with RA.

Article.Title: Adaptive entropy-guided access point selection for robust multi-floor Wi-Fi fingerprinting
Article.Authors: Bahy El-Din A.; Nafea H.; Samra A.; Abozied M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Wi-Fi fingerprinting is widely used for indoor localization. Although a large number of observable access points (APs) can provide richer spatial information, retaining all APs introduces significant computational overhead, increased scanning latency, and reduced generalization under heterogeneity across floors, devices, and contexts. This paper presents an entropy-guided dimensionality reduction framework that selects the most informative APs while preserving localization accuracy. First, each AP is ranked using Shannon entropy computed from its empirical RSSI distribution. The approach is evaluated on the multi-floor JUIndoorLoc dataset (172 AP features, three floors, four devices, and multiple contextual conditions) using a Random Forest classifier with stratified 5-fold cross-validation, and robustness is further assessed under additive RSSI noise and random AP dropouts. Across floors, the proposed adaptive entropy selection achieves substantial dimensionality reduction with negligible accuracy loss: it selects 17 APs on F3 ( $$\approx $$ 90.11% reduction) with only $$-0.41\%$$ accuracy change, 8 APs on F4 ( $$\approx $$ 95.34% reduction) with $$-0.51\%$$ change, and 26 APs on F5 ( $$\approx $$ 84.88% reduction) with $$-0.42\%$$ accuracy loss compared to the baseline configuration using all APs. Robustness experiments show that entropy-based selection can improve resilience under measurement noise on certain floors (e.g., on F5, at $$\sigma $$ =1–3 dB the selected subset achieves 0.8472/0.7748/0.7070 versus 0.7674/0.7084/0.6659 for using all APs), while also revealing floor-dependent trade-offs where extremely compact subsets may become more noise-sensitive under strong perturbations. Overall, the proposed adaptive entropy framework provides a lightweight, floor-aware AP selection mechanism that reduces inference cost and scanning burden while maintaining competitive accuracy and improving robustness in realistic degradation scenarios. The generalizability of these findings to more complex and dynamic real-world environments warrants further investigation.

Article.Title: Comparative performance analysis of adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system, fuzzy logic, and neural network-based maximum power point tracking controllers for permanent magnet synchronous generator-based variable-speed wind energy conversion systems
Article.Authors: Hadush G.; Gebremariam S.; Meresa S.; Alemu B.
Article.Abstract: In this study, the performance of MPPT based Fuzzy Logic Controllers (FLC), Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference Systems (ANFIS) for a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) based variable speed wind energy conversion system (WECS) is evaluated. Controllers are designed in MATLAB/Simulink and subjected to stepwise and time-varying wind speed settings to determine mechanical power extraction, boosted peak voltage, transient response, voltage regulation and steady-state stability. The stepwise wind speed is changed from 5 to 12 m/s and then to 9 and 10 m/s to assess the controller performance under dynamic operating conditions. The results show that all three intelligent controllers are able to successfully track the maximum power operating point, extracting 16.8 kW under the examined conditions, and get a maximum power coefficient of \(C_p=0.48\) . But large differences are observed in their electrical and dynamic responses. ANFIS achieves the best overall performance with maximum boosted voltage of 600 V and steady state DC-link voltage of 480 V with minimum oscillation. It also has the best damping properties, fastest transient response and least settling time compared with FLC and ANN. FLC provides intermediate dynamic performance with less computing complexity. ANN has relatively strong transient oscillations and longest settling response. The results demonstrate that ANFIS offers better dynamic stability and voltage regulation while all three controllers deliver similar maximum power extraction. Thus, ANFIS is proposed as a promising intelligent MPPT technique to enhance the performance and reliability of PMSG based variable-speed WECS under fast varying wind conditions.

Article.Title: Missed nursing care and associated factors among nurses working in critical care units in northern Ghana
Article.Authors: Wuni A.; Ibrahim M.; Sisala I.; Iddrisu M.
Article.Abstract: In high-pressure clinical environments, essential nursing tasks may be unintentionally omitted, a phenomenon known as missed nursing care. Despite its implications for patient safety and care quality, empirical evidence on missed nursing care in Ghana remains limited. This study aimed to determine missed nursing care and identify factors associated with its occurrence among nurses working in critical care units at a tertiary hospital in northern Ghana. A hospital-based cross-sectional survey was conducted among 217 registered nurses in one tertiary hospital in northern Ghana, selected using proportionate stratified and simple random sampling. Data were collected using the 24-item version of the Missed Nursing Care Questionnaire (MISSCARE Survey), which assesses the frequency of missed nursing care activities using a 4-point response scale (1 = “I miss rarely” to 4 = “I miss always”). The total composite score ranged from 25 to 86, with higher scores indicating more frequently missed nursing care. Participants reported missed nursing care activities in their unit during routine nursing practice. For robust regression, the average missed nursing care score was used as the continuous outcome. Robust regression using an MM-type estimator was used to examine factors associated with missed nursing care. The mean total missed nursing care score was 41.78 ± 12.52. The most frequently missed nursing care activities were participation in interdisciplinary care conferences (75.6%), patient ambulation (70.0%), meal setup for patients able to self-feed (64.5%), mouth care (62.2%), and bathing/skincare (61.8%). In the multivariable robust regression analysis, compared with nurses working in the Medical High Dependency Unit (HDU), those working in the Accident and Emergency (A/E) Unit had higher missed nursing care scores (β = 0.16, 95% CI: 0.01–0.33, p = 0.049), as did those working in the Obstetrics/Gynaecology Emergency Unit (β = 0.61, 95% CI: 0.23–0.99, p = 0.002). Conversely, nurses who reported supportive leadership in addressing patient safety concerns had lower missed nursing care scores (β = −0.17, 95% CI: −0.33 to − 0.01, p = 0.041). Nurses who perceived that they could make a meaningful impact on patient safety also reported lower missed nursing care scores (β = −0.30, 95% CI: −0.53 to − 0.06, p = 0.015). Missed nursing care varied across clinical units and was associated with organizational and professional factors, particularly leadership support and nurses’ perceived ability to make a meaningful impact on patient safety. Strengthening supportive leadership and improving organizational conditions may help reduce missed nursing care. However, given the cross-sectional design and single-hospital setting, the observed associations should not be interpreted as causal, and the findings may have limited generalizability beyond the study setting.

Article.Title: Multi-task deep learning framework for brain tumor classification and segmentation using ensemble feature extraction
Article.Authors: Singh R.; Prabha C.; Abdulla S.
Article.Abstract: Brain tumors are one of the most severe neurologic diseases, and their early and proper diagnosis is critical in developing treatment plans. MRI is often used in tumor detection; however, the manual examination is time-consuming and susceptible to human error. While deep learning algorithms have contributed to more automated brain tumor detection, there have been challenges in their implementation. For example, most methods implement classification and segmentation operations separately which increases the computational burden. In light of this challenge, this paper presents a multi-tasking deep learning architecture to detect brain tumors while incorporating both tumor segmentation and classification into one framework. Specifically, the model adopts an ensemble feature extraction technique through the use of ResNet-50, EfficientNet-B5, and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) along with attention-based modules to extract a wide range of features. A dynamic weighting process will be used to achieve effective fusion of the extracted features. In addition, classification will be the first step, and if a tumor is detected, then the U-net++ segmentation will be initiated. Experiments conducted using public MRI dataset yielded impressive results with a classification accuracy rate of 99.84%, dice coefficient of 91.22%, and IoU of 89.01%.

Article.Title: Detection of Helicobacter pylori in dental plaque among children with gastrointestinal disorders in a hospital-based cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Sadredinamin M.; Jamshidi Z.; Samani R.; Dara N.; Soleymani A.; Hakemi-Vala M.
Article.Abstract: Helicobacter pylori is responsible for gastritis and peptic ulcers, as well as gastric cancer. This bacterium can also be isolated from dental plaque, suggesting that the oral cavity may serve as a reservoir, contributing to reinfection after systemic antibiotic therapy. The present study was conducted to determine the presence of H. pylori and associated virulence genes in dental plaque from children with gastrointestinal disorders using PCR, and to investigate the relationship between the infection and dental caries experience (DMFT/dmft), tooth-brushing frequency, and dental visit frequency. In this cross-sectional study, 100 children with gastrointestinal disorders who were referred to Mofid Children’s Hospital in Tehran between 21 March 2023 and 19 March 2024 were included. A questionnaire was administered to collect data on gender, lifestyle, dental visit frequency, socio-economic status, and toothbrushing frequency. Oral and clinical examinations were performed before dental plaque samples were collected from the first molars or central teeth. During endoscopy, gastric biopsy specimens were obtained. The presence of gastric H. pylori was evaluated histopathologically in endoscopic biopsy specimens. Furthermore, dental plaque samples were analyzed for the presence of the 23 S rRNA , cagA , and sabA genes by polymerase chain reaction (PCR). H. pylori was detected in 54% of biopsy and 41% of dental plaque samples, respectively. All plaque-positive children were also biopsy-positive, although 13 biopsy-positive children were plaque-negative. H. pylori was not significantly associated with gender, age, parental education, or food consumption. Children who never brushed their teeth and those who visited the dentist only when they had a problem had higher odds of plaque H. pylori than those who brushed at least once daily and those with regular dental visits, respectively. Decayed teeth were more numerous in plaque-positive children. cagA was detected in 4.9% of plaque-positive samples, while no sample harbored the sabA gene. The results suggest that the oral cavity may serve as a potential reservoir for H. pylori infection in children and may be associated with dental caries, highlighting the importance of regular tooth brushing, routine dental visits, and timely treatment of dental caries in the management of H. pylori -related oral and gastric health.

Article.Title: Challenges in cancer diagnosis in Somalia through 35 years of instability (1991–2025): a pathologist’s experience
Article.Authors: Abdullahi I.; Farah F.
Article.Abstract: Somalia’s long-term instability since 1991 has severely disrupted pathology services, the cornerstone of cancer diagnosis, resulting in delayed and inaccurate diagnoses. This study provides a firsthand account of the evolution, current capacity, and systemic challenges of cancer diagnostic pathology in Somalia over 35 years of instability. A convergent mixed-methods study was undertaken to evaluate limitations of cancer diagnostic pathology services in south Somalia between 1991 and 2025. The quantitative component included all nine operational histopathology laboratories and assessed laboratory infrastructure, workforce, workload, and diagnostic capacity using standardised data abstraction from institutional records. The qualitative component consisted of semi-structured interviews with 14 practising pathologists exploring barriers, diagnostic limitations, and priorities for strengthening pathology services. Quantitative and qualitative findings were analysed independently and integrated during interpretation. Nine operational pathology laboratories employing 14 practising pathologists were identified, collectively processing an estimated 25,000–30,000 histopathology specimens annually, increasing the number of operational laboratories from one to nine between 2015 and 2025. Pathology services expanded substantially following the establishment of the Mogadishu Somali-Türkiye Training and Research Hospital (MSTTRH) in 2015. However, immunohistochemistry (IHC) was available in only one laboratory, while frozen section and molecular diagnostic services were unavailable nationwide. Qualitative analysis identified four major themes: inadequate laboratory infrastructure and recurrent reagent shortage; workforce and specialist training limitations; restricted access to advanced diagnostic technologies; and the need for improved quality assurance, multidisciplinary collaboration, and national coordination. In 2024, the Banadir region, Somalia, established its first histopathology-based cancer registry, providing the foundation for systematic national cancer surveillance. Somalia has made substantial progress in rebuilding cancer diagnostic pathology services despite decades of conflict. However, major investments in advanced diagnostics, workforce development, laboratory quality systems, and cancer surveillance remain essential to achieve equitable, high-quality cancer diagnosis. The findings provide evidence to inform national cancer control planning and offer insights relevant to strengthening pathology services in other resource-constrained and conflict-affected settings.

Article.Title: Bilateral M1 tDCS selectively modulates dynamic large-scale brain states associated with sensorimotor control relative to sham stimulation
Article.Authors: Salameh H.; Muffel T.; Serhan Y.; Samara M.; Nenning K.; Hertz U.; Villringer A.; Sehm B.; Ovadia-Caro S.
Article.Abstract: Transcranial direct current stimulation of the primary motor cortex is widely used to influence sensorimotor performance, yet its large-scale neural mechanisms remain unclear. This study examined how unilateral and bilateral stimulation of the primary motor cortex affect sensorimotor behavior and whole-brain dynamics. Twenty healthy adults participated in a double-blind crossover study that combined robotic motor tasks performed during stimulation (on-task) with resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging acquired during stimulation (off-task). We found that both unilateral and bilateral stimulation improved bimanual coordination compared to sham, with no difference between montages. Bilateral stimulation additionally increased proprioceptive variability in the left hand. On the neural level, only bilateral stimulation, as compared with sham, altered large-scale dynamics, increasing the occurrence rate of a frontoparietal and dorsal attention state and reducing transitions from a default mode-frontoparietal state to a thalamic-subcortical state. These brain dynamics were associated with sensorimotor performance in an exploratory analysis, thereby potentially linking stimulation-sensitive CAPs to motor performance.

Article.Title: Psychological (in)flexibility as a mediator between resilience and psychological outcomes in patients with cancer
Article.Authors: Sauer C.; Sajjad T.; Zinndorf L.; Weißflog G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Resilience and psychological flexibility are protective factors for mental health and well-being in the general population as well as in patients with cancer. Additionally, psychological inflexibility is a risk factor for poor wellbeing and psychopathology. Research suggests that psychological flexibility constitutes a resilience factor and mediates the association between resilience and psychological outcomes across various contexts. However, there is only sparse evidence regarding the mediating role of psychological inflexibility and flexibility processes in the relationship between resilience and psychological outcomes in patients with a chronic health condition. This study examined psychological inflexibility and flexibility processes as mediators of the relationship between resilience and psychological outcomes in patients with cancer. A total of N = 222 patients completed an online survey assessing resilience (Resilience Scale-11), psychological inflexibility (Acceptance and Action Questionnaire-2), distress (National Cancer Center Network distress thermometer), depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-8), anxiety (General Anxiety Disorder-7), and mental health-related quality of life (Short Form Health Survey-12). Across all bootstrapped mediation models, psychological inflexibility mediated the relationship between resilience and all psychological outcomes. Secondary analyses of acceptance of versus struggle with illness and value-based living versus obstruction showed partial mediation, with distinct patterns of association for each process. Our findings highlight psychological (in)flexibility as a key mediator between resilience and psychological outcomes in cancer patients. Obstruction showed the strongest association, suggesting that ACT-based interventions targeting psychological barriers may be particularly effective in enhancing resilience and mental health.

Article.Title: Fuzzy-adaptive MPPT and Kalman-filter SOC estimation for Lyapunov-stable predictive energy management in solar-integrated EV charging stations
Article.Authors: Santhoshkumar R.; Suresh S.; Peramanan A.; Sathishkumar P.
Article.Abstract: This research develops a coordinated control, estimation, and dispatch framework for a solar-photovoltaic-integrated electric-vehicle charging station (EVCS) with battery storage and grid backup, and reports four contributions. First, a fuzzy-adaptive-step perturb-and-observe (P&O) maximum-power-point-tracking (MPPT) algorithm varies its perturbation step with the local power–voltage sensitivity and reaches 98.1% ± 0.1% tracking efficiency over 15 randomised irradiance scenarios with a single fixed parameter set, compared with 95.0% ± 0.6% for fixed-step P&O and 97.8% ± 0.2% for a linear-adaptive law re-tuned for each scenario (Welch’s t-test, t = 5.2, p < 0.0001, fuzzy-adaptive vs. re-tuned). Second, an extended Kalman filter (EKF) fuses Coulomb counting with a second-order Thevenin battery model to estimate state of charge (SOC), the pair is shown observable by a Popov–Belevitch–Hautus (PBH) test and, across 20 Monte Carlo trials, reduces mean SOC estimation RMSE from 2.45% to 0.118%. Third, a model-predictive-control (MPC) energy-management system (EMS) replaces static rule-based dispatch with receding-horizon optimisation, lowering operating cost by 6.8% under a perfect-forecast assumption while revealing an explicit trade-off against grid independence. Fourth, a switched-system stability analysis constructs mode-dependent Lyapunov functions and derives an average-dwell-time bound (τ_a* = 2.31 ms) that certifies exponential stability of the linearised converter dynamics for any mode-switching sequence respecting this bound. The complete simulation delivers 93.6% system efficiency, DC-bus regulation within ± 5%, and grid dependency of 14.2%. Of the four contributions, only the fuzzy-adaptive MPPT and EKF-SOC layers were implemented on an ESP8266 hardware prototype, on that subset, hardware-measured system efficiency (91.2%) agrees with simulation (93.6%) to within 2.4 percentage points. The MPC-EMS dispatch result and the Lyapunov stability proof remain simulation-level findings, and hardware validation of both is set out as a priority for future work.

Article.Title: A novel, synergy-based kinematic model of the foot and ankle for gait analysis
Article.Authors: Conconi M.; Modenese L.; Barbieri G.; Leardini A.; Belvedere C.; Sancisi N.
Article.Abstract: Investigating foot biomechanics in musculoskeletal modeling is challenging. Multi-segment foot models, the most common approach in the literature, simplify the foot into a chain of a few rigid segments, neglecting many bone-to-bone motions and typically requiring several markers to track the various segments. This study aims to develop and characterize a synergy-based multibody kinematic optimization (SB-MKO) model that allow to reconstruct the kinematics of all the bones using a minimal number of degrees of freedom and markers. A novel kinematic model was developed by exploiting experimentally derived kinematic coupling among bones, or motion synergies, identified from weight-bearing CT scans through principal component analysis. The model describes the foot–ankle complex using five degrees of freedom (one at the ankle, three in the foot and one for toe motion). The intrinsic baseline accuracy of this modeling strategy was quantified against in-vitro CT-based bone kinematics, and robustness was evaluated by reducing the number of skin markers. The model was also preliminarily tested on clinical gait data from healthy, flat, and diabetic feet and compared with a standard multi-segment foot model. In the in-vitro test, the SB-MKO achieved average errors below 7° and 4 mm for rotations and translations, matching or improving the accuracy of existing models. Similar results were obtained using only four foot markers. In clinical gait analysis, the model showed superior discrimination between populations and enabled assessment of transverse arch deformation, which is not accessible with conventional models. The proposed SB-MKO provides a sound, low-complexity framework for reconstructing bone-level foot and ankle kinematics, substantially simplifying gait analysis and showing strong potential for clinical applications.

Article.Title: Optimization of conductivity for MXene polymer nanocomposites by the number and diameter of contacts among adjacent nanosheets
Article.Authors: Boomhendi M.; Munir M.; Soudmand B.; Zare Y.
Article.Abstract: In this study, a model for the conductivity of MXene-based samples is developed by simultaneously considering the percolation threshold, inter-nanosheet interfacial contacts, contact geometry, and electron tunneling effects. The percolation onset volume fraction and the network portion are demonstrated by interphase dimensions as well as the diameter and thickness of the MXene nanosheets. Accordingly, the proposed model is constructed based on physically meaningful and measurable parameters, providing an efficient framework for estimating the conductivity of MXene system. Parametric analysis and experimental conductivity facts from representative systems are employed to validate the method. The highest conductivity as 5.1 S/m is gained when nearly all MXene nanosheets participate in the conductive network and the interphase thickness is 40 nm. Furthermore, when the number of contact points reaches 40 and the contact circle diameter is 50 nm, the conductivity increases significantly, approaching 6.2 S/m. Overall, larger interphase region, shorter tunneling distance, larger contact area, higher contact number, and a greater fraction of networked nanoparticles lead to improved conductivity.

Article.Title: Precision risk stratification for perioperative safety of minimally invasive versus open TLIF in elderly patients with lumbar degenerative disease
Article.Authors: Wu H.; Fu H.; Qian J.; Yang C.; Wang X.; Xu G.
Article.Abstract: Lumbar degenerative disease is highly prevalent in elderly patients, and transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF) is a standard surgical treatment. However, the comparative safety of minimally invasive (MIS-TLIF) versus open TLIF in this vulnerable population remains incompletely defined, particularly regarding effect modifiers and underlying mechanisms. This retrospective cohort study included 728 patients aged ≥ 60 years who underwent primary TLIF, with 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) performed to balance baseline characteristics. Perioperative outcomes were compared, and 30-day complications were analyzed using the Fine-Gray competing risk model. Subgroup analysis, mediation analysis, and a gradient boosting machine learning predictive model were conducted to explore effect heterogeneity, mechanisms, and risk stratification. After PSM, all baseline variables were well balanced (all standardized mean differences < 0.05). The MIS-TLIF group exhibited significantly shorter operative time, less intraoperative blood loss, lower transfusion rates, faster postoperative recovery, and reduced 30-day and 90-day unplanned readmission rates (all P < 0.001). After adjusting for competing risks, MIS-TLIF was associated with a 52% lower risk of any 30-day complication (adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR] = 0.48, 95% CI 0.34–0.68, P < 0.001) and a 61% lower risk of major complications (adjusted SHR = 0.39, 95% CI 0.21–0.72, P = 0.003). Subgroup analysis revealed significant interactions between treatment effect and age (P for interaction = 0.007) and frailty index (P for interaction < 0.001), with exponentially greater benefits observed in patients aged ≥ 72 years and frail patients. Intraoperative blood loss and operative time mediated 41.3% and 18.9% of the total protective effect, respectively, with a total mediating effect of 60.2%. The predictive model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.83 in the validation set, and the relative risk reduction of complications with MIS-TLIF reached 78% in the very high-risk group. MIS-TLIF significantly improves perioperative safety in elderly patients with lumbar degenerative disease, with the greatest benefit in high-risk subgroups. The developed risk prediction model can facilitate personalized surgical decision-making for this population.

Article.Title: Impact of proposed wind turbines on seismic monitoring stations at the Xiaolangdi Reservoir
Article.Authors: Wei L.; Cao C.; Gan X.; Wang W.; Wang H.; Lv J.; Dong H.
Article.Abstract: This article simulates the operation vibration of a proposed wind turbine project, analyzes its impact on existing earthquake monitoring stations in the Xiaolangdi Reservoir. It selects 2 existing wind turbines with the same power and similar surroundings as the proposed one, and uses short period seismometers, strong motion meters, and wideband seismometers to monitor vibration at different positions from the wind turbines. Based on continuous waveform recording data from each measuring point, it calculates the root mean square of vibration acceleration at short period seismometer points, ground noise acceleration at strong motion meter points, and ground noise velocity at wideband points under the start - up and shutdown states of the wind turbine. Then it compares with seismic station construction standards and evaluates if the environmental ground noise level after wind turbine operation meets regulatory requirements. The test results show that a 5.6 MW wind turbine significantly impacts within 225 m of a station with a short period digital seismometer, and impacts beyond 315 m meet relevant seismic station standards. This study provides reference for site selection, detection and analysis of new wind power generation and other vibration equipment around existing earthquake monitoring stations of the same type.

Article.Title: Multivariate computational strategies for mechanisms involving gut microbiome metabolite targets of Astragalus in diabetic sarcopenic obesity
Article.Authors: Wang J.; Shen Y.; Hu Y.; Wang H.; Gu Y.; Zheng H.; Ren X.; Wang Y.; Yang X.
Article.Abstract: Diabetic sarcopenic obesity (SO) is a complex metabolic condition characterized by the coexistence of obesity, diabetes, and sarcopenia, leading to poor prognosis. Astragalus, is a key herb in spleen-strengthening formulas, but its pharmacological mechanisms against diabetic SO remain unclear. Drug- and disease-related genes for Astragalus, obesity, diabetes, and sarcopenia were retrieved from public databases. Overlapping genes were weighted by CytoNCA to identify core targets, which were expanded via GMFA network analysis to form core-plus genes. Gut microbiota metabolites and targets were obtained from gutMGene v2.0, with metabolite targets predicted using SEA and Swiss Target Prediction. Herb-active ingredient-target and drug–disease–gut networks were constructed via STRING and Cytoscape. Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes enrichment analyses identified key pathways, and molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations validated binding affinity between core ingredients and hub targets. A total of 31 drug-disease genes, 8 core genes, 87 core-plus genes, 6 drug-disease-gut genes and 11 final core genes were identified. Kaempferol and jaranol, the main active ingredients of Astragalus, were predicted to interact with AKT1, ESR1, MMP9, APP, and IGF1R, with these targets being associated with insulin resistance, the AMPK signaling pathway, the HIF-1 signaling pathway, and the TNF signaling pathway. Astragalus may alleviate diabetic SO through multi-target and multi-pathway mechanisms, highlighting its promise as a therapeutic candidate.

Article.Title: An innovative framework for student adaptability prediction using discriminant-based classification, feature selection, and sensitivity analysis
Article.Authors: Mao L.; Alkayid K.; Shreenidhi H.; Mostafa S.; MGM J.; Parhi M.; Wasson V.; Mohammed M.; Ansari G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurately predicting student adaptability is essential for enhancing academic performance and personal development. The present study presents a classification-based approach utilizing Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) to predict student adaptability. To enhance model performance, the Turbulent Flow of Water-based Optimization (TFWO) and Giant Armadillo Optimization (GAO) algorithms are employed. The dataset, consisting of 1,205 student records with demographic, educational, and socio-economic attributes, is split into training and test sets. The two best-performing hybrid models undergo a sensitivity analysis using the FAST approach. Experimental results demonstrate that the QDA model optimized with GAO (QDGO) achieves the highest classification accuracy of 0.975, outperforming other model configurations. These findings underscore the potential of optimized classification models in student adaptability prediction, providing valuable insights for educational institutions. Future studies can explore additional hybrid models and larger datasets to further refine predictive accuracy.

Article.Title: Source characterization and ecological risk of heavy metals in urban dust from two Iranian cities
Article.Authors: Ebrahimzadeh F.; Ahmady-Birgani H.; Dahmardeh Behrooz R.; Sheidai-Karkaj E.; Iram Batool A.
Article.Abstract: Urban dust can accumulate potentially toxic elements (PTEs) and may reflect differences in anthropogenic activities among urban environments. This study comparatively evaluated the concentrations, potential sources, and ecological risks of 13 heavy metals in urban dust from Urmia (northwestern Iran) and Abadan (southwestern Iran). Temporally integrated dust samples were analyzed using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Contamination and ecological risk were assessed using the contamination factor (Cf), enrichment factor (EF), pollution load index (PLI), and modified ecological risk (mRI) indices. Spearman correlation analysis and principal component analysis (PCA) were further applied to examine inter-element relationships and identify potential source patterns. The results indicated differences in metal contamination between the two cities, with higher overall contamination and ecological risk indices observed in Urmia than in Abadan. Among the analyzed elements, Cd and Cr contributed substantially to the observed contamination patterns, while Cd showed the highest potential ecological risk in both cities. The combined PLI and mRI results indicated higher contamination and ecological risk levels in Urmia. The findings demonstrate spatial variation in heavy-metal contamination and suggest differences in potential sources between the two urban environments. Continued monitoring and source-oriented management may help track changes in metal concentrations and reduce potential ecological risks associated with urban dust.

Article.Title: Tangerine peel as a sustainable biomass precursor for carbon quantum dots with photocatalytic application for dye removal from water and wastewater
Article.Authors: Sheshmani S.; Abedirad B.; Ghiyasi N.; Tarlani R.
Article.Abstract: Carbon quantum dots (CQDs) were synthesized via a green hydrothermal route using tangerine peel as a renewable carbon precursor. Structural characterization confirmed an amorphous carbon network (XRD broad peak at 2θ ≈ 20–25°) with a moderate degree of graphitization ( ID/IG ≈ 0.61–0.84). FT-IR spectroscopy revealed abundant surface functionalities, O–H stretching (~ 3400 cm⁻¹), C–H stretching (2850–2920 cm⁻¹), C = O stretching (~ 1730 cm⁻¹), and C–O–C/C–O stretching (1050–1150 cm⁻¹), alongside a newly formed aromatic C = C band at ~ 1600 cm⁻¹ after carbonization. The CQDs exhibited a mesoporous structure (~ 5 nm diameter) with a near-neutral, slightly negative zeta potential. Strong UV absorption (center ~ 275 nm; shoulder 320–380 nm) corresponded to an optical band gap of ≈ 3.18 eV (absorption edge ~ 389 nm). Under a 400 W Hg lamp, the CQDs displayed excitation-dependent photoluminescence (400–600 nm) and efficiently decolorized four textile dyes (Basic Blue 7, Acid Blue 56, Acid Blue 113, Acid Blue 128). Application to real textile wastewater achieved ≈ 88% removal efficiency, with BOD reduced from 1900 to 19 mg/L and COD from 600 to 27 mg/L.

Article.Title: An improved YOLOv8 framework fused with attention mechanism and gold-YOLO neck for abnormal driving behavior detection in automobiles
Article.Authors: Xu Z.; Chen Y.; Lu X.; Zhang S.; Xie K.; Zhang S.; Li P.; Shao X.
Article.Abstract: Vision-based detection of abnormal driving behaviors has become essential in the automated-vehicle era, playing a critical role in safeguarding vehicle occupants. By identifying unsafe actions early, this approach has demonstrated significant improvements in driving safety, accident reduction, and traffic condition management. However, existing research has primarily concentrated on facial expression recognition, overlooking a comprehensive analysis of overall driver postures. Common abnormal driving behaviors targeted in this study include eye closure, yawning, head turning, and phone use. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the Gold-YOLO-v8 variant achieves highly robust and competitive performance. Relative to the baseline YOLO-v8n (precision = 93.496%, F1 = 0.9404, mAP@0.5 = 0.97345), Gold-YOLO-v8 improves precision to 94.387% (+ 0.891%), F1-score to 0.9449 (+ 0.0045), and mAP@0.5 to 0.97598 (+ 0.00253). These results validate that the integration of the Gather-and-Distribute (GD) mechanism provides an optimized architectural balance, effectively capturing fine-grained driver anomaly features while still meeting the real-time detection requirement. After systematic validation of the GD multi-scale fusion architecture, this model is suitable for deployment on lightweight vehicle edge equipment for real-time abnormal driving monitoring, and subsequent work will carry out multi-vehicle real-scene field verification based on richer diversified driving datasets.

Article.Title: Resilience assessment and prediction of fresh agricultural product supply chains using variable fuzzy recognition and machine learning
Article.Authors: Gao S.; Bai A.; Sun X.; Peng A.; Li S.; Zhao W.; Ma S.
Article.Abstract: Fresh agricultural products are highly perishable and sensitive to transportation, storage, and handling conditions, which makes their supply chains particularly vulnerable to disruptions. Such disruptions can interrupt product flows and reduce both quality and availability. Traditional risk analysis methods mainly focus on uncertainty and the probability of adverse events, but they do not adequately capture the ability of supply chains to recover and adapt following disruptions. To address this limitation, this study develops a resilience evaluation and prediction framework for fresh agricultural product supply chains (FAPSCs). The framework is structured around three dimensions: production, transportation, and consumption. A hybrid modeling approach is proposed by integrating variable fuzzy set theory with machine learning. The variable fuzzy set model is used for dynamic resilience assessment, while a convolutional neural network (CNN) is employed to capture temporal dynamics and perform prediction. Indicator weights are determined by combining the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and the CRITIC method to improve robustness and interpretability. Using panel data from 31 provinces in China from 2009 to 2023, the results show that the proposed framework effectively distinguishes different resilience levels across regions. The CNN model captures temporal variations, including peak and off-peak fluctuations, and outperforms baseline models such as Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Linear Regression, particularly in modeling nonlinear patterns and high-resilience cases. Overall, the proposed approach demonstrates strong robustness under limited or noisy data conditions and provides practical support for early warning, risk mitigation, and decision making in FAPSC management.

Article.Title: Computational DFT and docking investigation of isoproterenol delivery using Al₁₂N₁₂ and Al₁₂O₁₂ inorganic nanocarriers
Article.Authors: Al Omari R.; saraswat S.; Abosaoda M.; Rekha M.; Ray S.; Chennakesavulu K.; Sharma R.; Kashyap A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The development of efficient nanocarriers for catecholamine drugs remains a critical challenge in cardiovascular therapeutics. This study presents the first comprehensive computational investigation of aluminum-based nanoclusters (Al₁₂N₁₂ and Al₁₂O₁₂) as drug delivery vehicles for Isoproterenol, a synthetic catecholamine used in managing bradycardia, heart block, and cardiac arrest. Using density functional theory (DFT) at the B3LYP/6-311 + G(d) level, the adsorption of Isoproterenol onto these nanoclusters was systematically evaluated through geometric, electronic, and spectroscopic analyses. The calculated binding energies ranged from ‒29 to ‒33 kcal/mol for Isoproterenol/Al₁₂N₁₂ complexes and from ‒61 to ‒88 kcal/mol for Isoproterenol/Al₁₂O₁₂ complexes in gas phase, and ranged from ‒25 to ‒28 kcal/mol for Isoproterenol/Al₁₂N₁₂ complexes and from ‒54 to ‒75 kcal/mol for Isoproterenol/Al₁₂O₁₂ complexes in water phase, suggesting favorable adsorption interactions, with Al₁₂O₁₂ exhibiting stronger interactions due to the higher electronegativity of oxygen. A substantial increase in dipole moment upon complexation suggests which may contribute to improved aqueous solubility and potentially facilitate cellular uptake, favorable attributes for drug delivery applications. Molecular docking against the β₁-adrenergic receptor (β₁AR) revealed that the Isoproterenol/nanocluster complexes achieved docking scores of‒15.98 and ‒16.56 kcal/mol for Al₁₂N₁₂ and Al₁₂O₁₂ complexes, respectively, markedly superior to free Isoproterenol (‒7.41 kcal/mol). Ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations at 300 K further supported the thermal and structural stability of the most stable Isoproterenol/Al₁₂N₁₂ and Isoproterenol/Al₁₂O₁₂ complexes under the simulated conditions, with no apparent dissociation or major structural distortion during the 10 ps trajectories. These findings suggest Al₁₂N₁₂ and Al₁₂O₁₂ nanoclusters as promising, previously unexplored carriers for Isoproterenol, offering a foundation for experimental validation and future development of inorganic nanocarrier-based delivery systems for cardiovascular drugs.

Article.Title: Interfacial control and evaporation pinning of nanocapillary filling from ambient to serpentinization temperatures
Article.Authors: Cihan A.; Gilbert B.; Bhuvankar P.; Hu M.; Steefel C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fluid transport in nanometer-scale channels underlies nanofluidic technologies and geological systems, yet measured capillary filling rates in hydrophilic channels are often far slower than classical theory predicts. Here we show, using a coupled flow model based on classical density functional theory combining hydrodynamics, electrokinetics and capillarity, that electrokinetic resistance and locally elevated viscosity near the channel walls jointly suppress flow, capturing the measured slowdown across independent experiments. At higher temperatures relevant to serpentinization (around 200 degrees Celsius), the model predicts a regime of evaporation-driven pinning: once relative humidity falls below saturation, classical capillary scaling breaks down and evaporation, orders of magnitude faster than at ambient conditions, balances capillary inflow and pins the meniscus inside the channel. Depending on wettability, humidity and channel length, transport may continue through thin liquid films and vapor migration. These predictions await experimental testing but identify a high-temperature flow regime, to our knowledge not previously described in nanochannels, relevant to nanodevice design, subsurface fluid modeling, and geologic hydrogen generation.

Article.Title: Organic amendments enhance aggregate stability of yellow soils in southwest China: roles of SOC characteristics and Fe oxides
Article.Authors: Zhan K.; Li J.; Long J.
Article.Abstract: Soil structure is the foundation of soil functions, and its widespread degradation poses significant threats to soil health. By 13 C nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and PLS-PM model, this study aimed to investigate how soil binding agents (SOC and Fe oxide) dynamically reshape soil structure after organic materials incorporation. Four treatments were implemented in a one-year field trial: conventional fertilization (CK), charcoal + rapeseed cake + husk (BC), rapeseed cake + husk (RS), and N fertilizer reduction (DP). Results show that treatments incorporating organic materials significantly improved the soil structure during maize maturity, RS treatment was more effective, resulting in increases of 27.15%, 32.26%, and 9.12% in aggregate MWD, GMD, and R 0.25 , compared with CK. And organic amendments enhanced aggregate-associated OC during the silking and maturity stages, particularly within the 8–2 mm aggregates (17.05–104.23%). In addition, organic amendment effects on aggregate‑associated OC accumulation differed across growth stages: RS outperformed BC at jointing and silking, while BC was superior at maturity. Compared with free-form Fe oxides (Fed) and complex Fe oxides (Fep), amorphous Fe oxides (Feo) exhibited a stronger influence on aggregate stability. We further observed that, apart from SOC quantity, the inherent characteristics of SOC also play a key role in aggregate stability. A/OA, aliphaticity, hydrophobicity, and alkyl C abundance of SOC favored the formation of 8 –2 mm aggregates, whereas O-substituted aromatic C, O-alkyl C, and SOC aromaticity were more strongly associated with the formation of 2–0.25, 0.25–0.053, and < 0.053 mm aggregates. This study provides new insights into SOC characteristics and aggregate formation in the yellow soils of southwest China.

Article.Title: Machine learning modeling and interpretation of saline soil thermal conductivity
Article.Authors: Abbasi M.
Article.Abstract: Soil thermal conductivity is a key parameter in geothermal design, buried infrastructure, frozen-ground engineering, agricultural heat-transfer assessment, and subsurface energy systems. This study developed an interpretable multi-model machine-learning framework for predicting soil thermal conductivity from 903 literature-derived observations and 15 predictors describing temperature, texture, bulk density, volumetric water content, salt concentration, salt molar mass, and ionic identity. Eleven regression algorithms were optimized by five-fold cross-validation within a common 90% development subset and compared on an untouched 10% random hold-out. Extra Trees yielded the lowest observed random-holdout error (R² = 0.9816, RMSE = 0.0625 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, MAE = 0.0446 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, AARE = 3.93%, and A20 = 98.90%), with CatBoost and XGBoost providing similarly high point performance. Because the database was assembled from 20 independent literature sources, source-aware validation was added. Pooled leave-one-study-out prediction decreased to R² = 0.2367 and RMSE = 0.3983 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹. A stricter retrospective external source validation was then performed by withholding all 100 observations from the two 2024 sources before any refitting or tuning and developing Extra Trees only on the remaining 803 observations from 18 earlier sources. The resulting external-source performance was R² = −3.3720, RMSE = 0.5855 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, MAE = 0.5438 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, AARE = 51.14%, and A20 = 12.00%, demonstrating substantial between-study domain shift. Feature ablation showed that a physical-only Extra Trees model achieved test R² = 0.9551; adding salt concentration increased R² to 0.9679, adding salt molar mass increased it to 0.9813, and the full chemistry representation reached R² = 0.9816. The results therefore support high-accuracy interpolation within represented experimental domains but do not support universal transfer to unseen studies. Source-specific or local validation is required before engineering deployment.

Article.Title: Integrated architectures for IFC interoperability and legacy BIM migration with a deterministic IFC2X3 data-quality pilot
Article.Authors: Lal R.; Sharif M.; Bashir M.; Khishe M.; Sorsa A.; Khan M.; Zaland A.
Article.Abstract: Interoperability remains a persistent limitation in Building Information Modelling (BIM) because Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) exchanges can preserve file syntax while losing or misrepresenting geometry, properties, quantities, and relationships. This study makes an architectural contribution by defining two proposed systems: the Globe-IFC framework for core-schema and regional rule governance, and the Legacy-IFC Bridge for traceable migration of legacy information into IFC. Evidence combines a structured 95-study review, a cross-industry comparison, a deterministic data-quality pilot, and a de-identified practitioner survey (n = 26). The pilot evaluated 300 seeded elements from three professional IFC2X3 steel models. Class-matched LoadBearing properties were present in 255/300 elements, positive Length properties in 200/300, recognized material grades in 210/300, and identifiers and relationship participation in 300/300. The structural-class check served as the sampling eligibility filter and was therefore satisfied by all 300 sampled elements by design. Two investigators independently annotated every sampled element and the retained manual dataset is the reconciled consensus baseline, which the automated implementation matched exactly. The manual–automated agreement is interpreted only as implementation consistency rather than validation of the proposed AI components. For C1280, no positive Length was returned through the R5 extraction pathway, but inspection of six sampled elements confirmed dimensional Span properties in Pset_BeamCommon and Pset_MemberCommon. Therefore, the 0/100 R5 result reflects how dimensions were represented and extracted rather than absence of dimensional information from the model. Survey respondents primarily used IFC for coordination (12/26), rated legacy integration highly (mean 4.31/5), and rated automated error-resolution tools highly (mean 4.46/5). The findings support the relevance of the proposed integrated IFC-interoperability workflow for infrastructural development and building design, while showing that AI regulatory updating, machine-learning validation, and blockchain provenance remain future components requiring separate empirical evaluation.

Article.Title: An underwater object detection method based on generative degradation simulation and hard-sample learning
Article.Authors: Wang F.; Zhan B.; Liu S.; Deng F.; Li L.
Article.Abstract: Underwater images are affected by spectral attenuation, particulate scattering, and nonuniform illumination and therefore often exhibit color shifts, reduced contrast, blurred edges, and local darkening. Existing public datasets provide limited coverage of degradation types and intensities, while frame extraction from continuous videos introduces many similar backgrounds, making it difficult for detection models to fully learn object variations in complex waters. To address these problems, an underwater object detection method based on generative degradation simulation and hard-sample learning, termed GDH-Det, is proposed. The method extracts degradation conditions related to water color, turbidity, and blur level from real images. A conditional diffusion network combines these conditions with bounding-box masks to generate degraded images at continuously varying intensities, and candidate samples suitable for training are selected using structural constraints on object regions and detection-based credibility scores. During detector training, sample difficulty is computed from classification uncertainty, localization deviation, and perturbation response, the sampling probability is then determined jointly by the generation credibility score and the training epoch, allowing difficult and credible samples to receive more training opportunities. Degradation conditions further participate in multi-scale feature computation, while a paired-feature loss preserves class-related information between object regions in real images and their corresponding generated images. Experiments are conducted on four public datasets, URPC2020, DUO, UODD, and Brackish. GDH-Det achieves mAP@0.5 values of 85.3%, 79.6%, 66.2%, and 84.7%, respectively. As degradation severity increases, GDH-Det shows a smaller performance drop. At degradation level 5, mAP@0.5 on URPC2020 remains 74.8%, 6.7% points higher than AGW-YOLOv8. In the ablation study, the complete method improves by 4.9% points over the baseline trained only on real samples. GDH-Det contains 31.8 M parameters and requires 18.7 ms per image for inference. The experimental results show that the method maintains high detection accuracy in turbid, low-light, dense small-object, and partially occluded scenes and exhibits good adaptability under complex underwater imaging conditions.

Article.Title: Parkinson’s disease is associated with increased 90-day readmission and reoperation after elective total hip arthroplasty
Article.Authors: Maman D.; Steinfeld Y.; Berkovich Y.
Article.Abstract: Patients with Parkinson’s disease (PD) undergoing total hip arthroplasty (THA) may be at increased risk for postoperative complications due to neuromuscular dysfunction and medical frailty. Contemporary national data on short-term outcomes following elective primary THA in this population remain limited. This study evaluated index hospitalization complications and 90-day readmission with procedural escalation after elective primary THA in patients with PD. We performed a retrospective cohort study using the Nationwide Readmissions Database (2020–2022). Adult patients undergoing elective primary THA on hospital day 0 were identified. A variable-ratio propensity score-matched cohort of up to 1:5 (PD: non-PD) was constructed using demographics, payer, hospital characteristics, calendar year, and comorbidities (all standardized mean differences < 0.1). Index complications, 90-day readmission, and readmission-associated procedural escalation (any procedure, reoperation, and revision) were assessed. The matched cohort included 12,143 elective primary THAs (2,043 PD; 10,100 controls). PD was associated with higher rates of perioperative complications, including blood transfusion, pneumonia, urinary tract infection, and hip dislocation (all p ≤ 0.015), while in-hospital mortality remained low and similar between groups. Within 90 days, PD patients had higher readmission (10.3% vs. 5.8%; OR 1.86; p < 0.001) and markedly increased procedural escalation, including reoperation (3.3% vs. 0.9%) and revision (3.0% vs. 0.7%) (all p < 0.001). Length of stay was longer in PD patients, with no significant difference in hospital charges. Elective primary THA in patients with Parkinson’s disease is associated with increased perioperative complications and substantially higher 90-day readmission with early revision and reoperation. These findings highlight increased post-discharge vulnerability in this population and underscore the need for enhanced perioperative optimization and postoperative surveillance.

Article.Title: Integration of multi-source hydroclimatic variables for enhanced drought monitoring
Article.Authors: Salman M.; Khalefa M.; Ismael W.; Hussain I.; Basheer A.
Article.Abstract: Agricultural drought monitoring requires integrated indicators that capture the coupled variability of soil moisture and TerraClimate Actual Evapotranspiration (AET) while accounting for uncertainty in multi-source datasets. However, using existing drought indices and model-based indicators alone can be constrained by scale differences, heterogeneous errors, and incomplete representation of drought-related processes, particularly in climatically heterogeneous agricultural regions. To address this gap, we develop the Soil Moisture and Evapotranspiration Revealed Drought Index (SERDI) by integrating ERA5 and GLDAS soil moisture with TerraClimate AET, using Triple Collocation(TC) as the primary uncertainty-weighted formulation and Scaled Triple Collocation (STC) as a domain-based sensitivity analysis of spatial scaling effects. This framework is evaluated at seven selected locations—Bahawalpur, Faisalabad, Gujranwala, Lahore, Multan, Sargodha, and Sialkot—spanning contrasting hydroclimatic conditions along the south-to-northeast agroclimatic gradient of Punjab, Pakistan, using monthly data from 2000 to 2023. Internal consistency and TC-based diagnostics showed that ERA5-SM had the lowest estimated error variance and consequently received the largest merging weights, while SERDI_TC retained strong correlation \(\left(r=0.93-0.99\right)\) with its standardized inputs and coherent spatiotemporal drought patterns, including comparatively stronger drought signals at the sampled southern locations. The domain-based STC sensitivity analysis produced a drought signal highly consistent with SERDI_TC \(\left(r=0.9927;RMSE=0.1205;MAE=0.0615\right)\) , indicating that spatially varying scaling did not materially alter the integrated signal under the sampled conditions. External benchmarking against six literature-based drought indicators showed the strongest correspondence with SMDI \(\left(lag-0r=0.89-0.95;ROC-AUC=0.973\right)\) , followed by ESI \(\left(r=0.66-0.78;ROC-AUC=0.854\right)\) , while the meteorological and vegetation-based benchmarks showed moderate to weaker and more spatially variable relationships.

Article.Title: Particle characteristics of recycled cement-stabilized gravel under abrasion treatment and evaluation of pretreatment effect
Article.Authors: Yang F.; Zhang X.; Dang W.; Wen P.; Huang Q.; Wang C.
Article.Abstract: To promote the reutilization of recycled cement-stabilized gravel (RCSG) in road base courses, the influence of abrasion parameters on the abrasion effect of virgin aggregate was analyzed. A treatment scheme for RCSG was then proposed. The changes in morphology, gradation, agglomeration rate, and abrasion value of RCSG before and after abrasion treatment were evaluated. A multi-index comprehensive evaluation system based on data envelopment analysis (DEA) was used to recommend the optimal abrasion cycles and size fraction for RCSG. The pavement performance of corresponding cold recycled cement-stabilized mixtures was verified. The results indicated that the agglomeration rate of RCSG of all sizes generally exceeds 20%. Abrasion tests on virgin aggregate verify that steel-ball abrasion increases fine aggregate content. They also determine a preliminary recommended upper limit of 500 abrasion cycles for RCSG pretreatment. The optimal pretreatment condition is determined as 6 steel balls and 400 rotation cycles for RCSG. Under this condition, the overall agglomeration rate of full-size RCSG drops from 30.7% (100 cycles) to 7.9%. Compared with the coarse fraction, the full-size fraction RCSG showed a 54.1% higher abrasion value and an 11.2% lower agglomeration rate. The DEA evaluation shows that the abrasion pretreatment effect on full-size fraction RCSG is superior to that on coarse and single-size fractions. Abrasion pretreatment of full-size fraction RCSG with 6 steel balls and 400 cycles achieves the best balance between particle shaping and energy consumption control. At 30% RCSG replacement, the 7 d and 28 d unconfined compressive strength (UCS) of the cold recycled cement-stabilized gravel mixture increased by 115.6% and 121.2%, respectively, compared with the untreated group.
