Article.Title: Single‑cell and bulk RNA sequencing identifies T cell marker genes to predict the prognosis of ovarian cancer
Article.Authors: Sun H.; Huo X.; Li S.; Guo L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Background: Ovarian cancer, with high mortality and often late diagnosis, shows high recurrence despite treatment. The variable effectiveness of immunotherapy highlights the urgent need for personalized, advanced therapeutic strategies. Methods: To investigate T-cell marker genes, single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) data were sourced from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Additionally, bulk RNA-sequencing data along with clinical information from ovarian cancer patients were retrieved from the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) database to establish a prognostic signature. This study involved survival analysis to evaluate associations between different risk groups, and explored cellular communication and relevant pathway analyses, including metabolic pathways. Results: We identified 41 genes showing varied expression between two T-cell subclusters, marking subcluster 0 with CCL5 and GZMA, and attributing the rest to subcluster 1. These markers delineate four prognostic groups within the TCGA OV dataset, with T-cluster 2 exhibiting the poorest survival, in contrast to T-cluster 3, which shows the best. Analysis suggests subcluster 1 T-cells might be dysfunctional, potentially exacerbating ovarian cancer progression. We also developed a T-cell scoring model using eight significant genes, showing improved survival in the low-score group. Moreover, cellular and metabolic pathway analyses underscored the importance of CCL, IL2 and MGMT pathways in these subclusters. Conclusions: The study identifies CCL-5 as a biomarker for T-cell subtypes in ovarian cancer using scRNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq data. A T-cell scoring model based on eight genes predicts survival and progression rates, independent of clinical features. This model could be a prognostic indicator and CCL-5 a potential immunotherapy target in ovarian cancer.

Article.Title: Performance-based evaluation of hyperbolic and parabolic vertical curves for highway geometric design
Article.Authors: Shahvarani M.; Kordani A.; Shirini B.; Moradi F.
Article.Abstract: Vertical curves play a fundamental role in highway geometric design by influencing vehicle dynamics, ride comfort, and safety. Although parabolic curves are widely adopted in current practice, alternative curve formulations may exhibit different dynamic-performance characteristics. To the authors’ knowledge, limited research has examined the vehicle-dynamics implications of hyperbolic vertical curves using multi-body simulation under standard highway-design constraints. Therefore, this study compares the dynamic performance of hyperbolic and parabolic vertical curves using a CarSim-based vehicle model. The analysis covered crest and sag curves designed according to stopping sight distance (SSD) and passing sight distance (PSD) criteria under identical geometric boundary conditions. Vehicle responses were evaluated using four indicators: maximum vertical acceleration, dynamic wheel load, pitch angle, and suspension deflection. The results revealed substantial differences between the two curve formulations. Vertical acceleration was the most sensitive indicator, with hyperbolic curves producing peak responses of up to 0.590 m/s², compared with approximately 0.030 m/s² for the corresponding parabolic curves. Conversely, under sag-curve conditions, hyperbolic curves reduced peak wheel loads by approximately 20–30% and suspension deflections by approximately 15–20% relative to the parabolic alternative. Pitch-angle responses showed only negligible differences between the two formulations. The findings demonstrate a clear performance trade-off between the investigated curve geometries. While the parabolic profile consistently produced lower vertical acceleration, the hyperbolic profile reduced peak wheel load and suspension deflection under the investigated sag-curve conditions. These benefits were accompanied by substantially increased vertical acceleration. The proposed framework provides a performance-based approach for evaluating alternative vertical-curve formulations and supports the integration of vehicle-dynamics considerations into future highway geometric-design studies.

Article.Title: XCAT-UIR: explainable cross-attention guided ConvNeXt-transformer framework for underwater image restoration systems
Article.Authors: Veeramakali T.; Sayeed M.; Yogarayan S.
Article.Abstract: Underwater images play a significant role in ocean exploration, but they frequently suffer from major loss of image quality due to light absorption and scattering in underwater conditions. However, underwater image restoration remains a challenging issue because of various distortions. The primary cause of information degradation includes wavelength-dependent color attenuation, light scattering effects, and blurring of objects. Currently, deep learning methods are widely utilized for image enhancement, leveraging the concept that hidden features can be learned to improve the image quality. Nevertheless, the black-box nature of deep learning methods limits the understanding of how the model produces its restoration outputs. This study presents an Explainable Cross-Attention Guided ConvNeXt-Transformer for Underwater Image Restoration (XCAT-UIR) model. The major objective of the proposed XCAT-UIR approach is to increase the visibility, correct color distortions, preserve fine details, and improve the overall quality of degraded underwater images. The proposed approach initially performs preprocessing to improve image quality for further analysis. Subsequently, ConvNeXt and Swin Transformer techniques are employed to extract local texture and global contextual information from the preprocessed images to enhance the feature understanding. The integration of convolution-based and transformer-based feature extraction networks improves the representation capability of the restoration model. Besides, the Cross-Attention Fusion model is used to integrate local features from ConvNeXt and global features from Swin Transformer to generate discriminative fused feature representations. Furthermore, Residual Reconstruction Blocks reconstruct the enhanced underwater image from the fused features while preserving important details and reducing information loss. Lastly, Grad-CAM and cross-attention maps are used to enhance visual evidence for restoration-relevant areas and local-global feature interactions. To ensure the improved performance of the proposed model, a widespread experimental analysis is performed using a benchmark dataset. An extensive comparison study emphasized that the proposed model has gained significant performance over recent methods in terms of different measures, indicating its superiority in underwater image restoration.

Article.Title: A phase 2 trial evaluating polysomnography outcomes and safety of lemborexant in Korean adults with insomnia disorder
Article.Authors: Cho Y.; Yoon I.; Pyo Y.; Takase T.; Kubota N.; Moline M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lemborexant (LEM), a dual-orexin-receptor-antagonist, was evaluated in this study of Korean participants with insomnia disorder. Study E2006-J082-204 (Study 204), a 1-month, multicenter, double-blind, placebo (PBO)-controlled, parallel-group study, evaluated LEM 5 mg (LEM5) or LEM 10 mg (LEM10) in participants aged 19–80 years with insomnia disorder (sleep efficiency [SE] ≤ 85%; latency to persistent sleep [LPS] ≥ 30 min). Korean participants were randomized (2:2:1) to LEM5, LEM10, or PBO, respectively, and received study drug immediately before bedtime for 30 days. Polysomnograms were conducted during an ~ 14-day single-blind PBO run-in (baseline) and after 1 month (Day 30). Changes from baseline in LPS (min; log-transformed; primary endpoint [LEM5 only]; secondary endpoint [LEM10 only]), SE (%; secondary endpoint), wake after sleep onset (WASO; min; exploratory endpoint), and total sleep time (TST; min; exploratory endpoint) were evaluated. Safety data were collected. The full analysis set comprised 64 participants (PBO, n = 13; LEM5, n = 25; LEM10, n = 26). At Day 30, decreases (improvements) from baseline in LPS and WASO were larger with LEM versus PBO. Increases from baseline in SE and TST were larger with LEM versus PBO. LEM was well tolerated. These findings support the clinical applicability of LEM as a therapeutic option for insomnia management in South Korea. Article.Title: Explainable machine learning for identifying nonlinear associations between street vitality and the built environment in a Historic District
Article.Authors: Xi X.; Qian Y.; Ao G.; Zhang H.; Wang H.
Article.Abstract: Historic districts exhibit fine-grained spatial variation, while street vitality may relate nonlinearly to the built environment. Using 213 micro-sampling points in the Lihuangpi Road Historic District, Wuhan, this study integrates heritage location, functional facilities, transport accessibility, street networks, frontage characteristics, and streetscape visual features. OLS, GAM, and XGBoost were compared, while SHAP, LOWESS, and spatial validation were used to assess nonlinear associations, model interpretation, and reliability. Under nested random validation, XGBoost achieved R² values of 0.474, 0.490, and 0.460 for overall, weekday, and weekend vitality, respectively, outperforming GAM and OLS. However, spatial GroupKFold reduced these values to 0.012, 0.084, and 0.052, with further deterioration as training–test separation increased. In the original ten-predictor models, Distance Heritage Core ranked first (29.7%–30.0%); after adding X and Y coordinates and distance to the study-area boundary, its importance decreased to 10.6%–11.3% and its rank fell to third or fourth, indicating that part of its apparent contribution reflected general spatial position. The results show that explainable machine learning can reveal nonlinear within-area associations, but random-validation performance should not be interpreted as spatial transferability. The framework supports micro-scale diagnosis and cautious, heritage-compatible renewal in historic districts.

Article.Title: Directional magnetic field detection with zero-bias surface acoustic wave sensors
Article.Authors: Nowak M.; Weisheit F.; Spetzler E.; Meyer-Strenzke J.; Lofink F.; McCord J.; Quandt E.; Meyners D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Surface acoustic wave magnetic field sensors are promising candidates in detecting low-amplitude magnetic fields over a broad frequency range. For sensor arrays and portable systems, operating without an external magnetic bias field is essential for reducing system complexity and power consumption. One approach to achieve an internal magnetic bias is to intentionally tilt the magnetic anisotropy of the sensing layer relative to the acoustic wave propagation direction. In this work, we present two types of internally biased surface acoustic wave magnetic field sensors based on exchange-biased multilayer structures. These consist of two multilayer stacks of Ta | (Fe 90 Co 10 ) 78 Si 12 B 10 | Ni 81 Fe 19 | Mn 80 Ir 20 | Ta layers that enable a stable magnetic configuration with low magnetic noise in a nearly single magnetic domain state. The best fabricated sensor reaches a detection limit of 69 pT/Hz 1/2 at 10 Hz and 22 pT/Hz 1/2 at 100 Hz, which is to our knowledge the lowest detection limit reported for SAW magnetic field sensors operated without an external bias field. The sensors exhibit a sinusoidal directional response fitting to an analytical magnetic model that includes magnetic energy contributions from magnetostatic interactions and unidirectional anisotropy.

Article.Title: A robust and reliable method for malware classification using hybrid features and gradient boosting
Article.Authors: Maqsood A.; Mirza H.; Muskan A.; Akram A.; Rashid J.; Alharthi R.; Sarwar N.
Article.Abstract: The most significant problem facing software security firms in the current cybersecurity system is the fact that new strains of malware keep on appearing. The achievement of successful detection of malicious software based on both static and dynamic data remains unmet despite the further realization of different approaches to deep learning and machine learning. Defects in encryption, packaging, and distribution, the discrepancies between the distribution of malware samples in families, make this issue even worse. To do actual malware research that utilizes deep learning methods, you will require data scientists of appropriate competence, large amounts of computer power (particularly GPUs) and time. In order to overcome such issues, this approach involves a hybrid approach to feature extraction that integrates wavelet and other statistical features based on benchmarked malware image sets. A classification model based on gradient-boosting can be used reliably to classify different types of malwares. Further, this paper examined the capability of the machine learning system to Classify in-distribution test samples well. This method is properly tested on the two benchmarked datasets MelVis and MALIMG to ensure its effectiveness. By joining these two sets of data it is possible to test the suggested technique using varied array of samples. The proposed approach outperforms the state-of-the-art techniques with an incredible accuracy rate of 100% using MALIMG and 98.10 and 98.40% using combined datasets. Its value extends far beyond cybersecurity in such spheres as sustaining IoT ecosystems to assist in improving networked devices and systems.

Article.Title: Identification of a natural product inhibitor of SARS-CoV-2 Mpro through integrated virtual screening, DFT, and molecular dynamics simulations
Article.Authors: Paudel D.; Shrestha P.; Lamichhane S.; Tripathi G.; Khanal S.; Koirala R.; Aryal P.; Adhikari N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The emergence of vaccine-resistant SARS-CoV-2 variants demands the development of novel antivirals targeting conserved viral proteins, like the main protease (M pro ). For expediting drug discovery, CADD approach of integrating different computational tools have been employed in drug candidate identification. Based on computational analysis, our study aimed to identify potential M pro inhibitors from natural product databases by combining virtual screening, DFT calculations and MD simulations. From 224,205 molecules from ZINC15 natural product database, N-[[(2R,3S,4R,5S)-5-(2-anilino-2-oxoethyl)-3,4-dihydroxyoxolan-2-yl]methyl]-4-methoxybenzamide (Lig14) was a prospective candidate against SARS-CoV-2 M pro . It exhibited binding energy of − 8.2 kcal/mol (Paxlovid with − 7.6 kcal/mol). It showed dipole moment of 12.70 D, HOMO/LUMO energy gap of 123.00 kJ/mol. MD simulations revealed a consistent contact area interference of ~ 360 Å 2 . The binding free energy (MM-GBSA) of − 31.82 ± 6.64 kcal/mol suggested in proper binding. Moreover, MD analysis also exhibited strong sub-diffusive motion (α = 0.49) with 35.2 Å confinement within the M pro active site, demonstrating sustained binding interactions characteristic of competitive inhibitors. The alchemical free energy perturbation calculation gave solvation free energy (ΔG solv ) in water (− 41.22 to − 40.70 kJ/mol) across four methods indicating solubility. The C145Y and π-sulfur bonding with C145 in G143S, G143D, G143N and E166K could disrupt catalytic dyad formation with H41, potentially compromising enzymatic function. Through an integrated computational approach, we identified Lig14 as a promising lead compound for the inhibition of SARS-CoV-2 M pro . While these in silico methods are highly credible for initial screening, their inherent limitations warrant subsequent experimental investigation to validate these findings.

Article.Title: Coupled analytical and finite element investigation of dynamic and cyclic response in cracked functionally graded beams
Article.Authors: Anusha N.; Pachaiappan S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Offshore and marine structures increasingly utilise Functionally Graded Materials (FGMs) because of their superior stiffness and enhanced resistance to damage under combined vibration and cyclic loading induced by waves, wind and operational conditions. This study presents a combined analytical and finite element investigation into the dynamic behaviour of a cracked FGM cantilever beam compared with eight conventional offshore structural steels. A fracture-mechanics-based analytical model, incorporating crack-induced flexibility and stiffness degradation under cyclic loading within a continuum damage mechanics framework, was developed to predict the beam’s natural frequencies and validated against finite element results, with deviations below 2%. The postulated cracks were represented by predefined notches to simulate pre-existing structural damage or defects, with crack depth ratios of a/h = 0.233, 0.333, 0.4, & 0.5 introduced at different locations along the beam length. A nonlinear finite element model developed in ABAQUS was subsequently used to evaluate stress evolution, strain accumulation, and hysteretic force-displacement response under displacement-controlled cyclic loading. As the crack depth ratio increased, both the natural frequency and stiffness decreased, whereas stress concentration, strain accumulation, and hysteresis loop width increased, indicating greater energy dissipation and progressive stiffness degradation. Compared with conventional offshore steels, the FGM beam consistently exhibited higher natural frequencies, lower displacement amplitudes, and stable cyclic behaviour without significant strength degradation. The proposed analytical-numerical framework was further validated against published experimental results, confirming its reliability for assessing the coupled vibration and cyclic behaviour of cracked FGM beams for offshore structural applications.

Article.Title: Hydrogeochemical characteristics, controlling processes, and irrigation suitability assessment of groundwater in the Sanjiang Plain, China
Article.Authors: Wang L.; Liu X.; Xu P.; Guo X.; Hu H.; Su Y.; Wang L.; Wang W.; Xu D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Groundwater is vital for global irrigation water supply, and its quality directly affects sustainable agricultural development. However, studies on irrigation water quality and its dominant controlling factors in semi-humid regions remain limited. Therefore, taking the Sanjiang Plain as a case, hydrochemical analysis, irrigation water quality assessment, and multivariate statistical methods were employed to systematically reveal the hydrogeochemical characteristics, irrigation suitability, and their dominant controlling mechanisms. The results indicate that the main hydrochemical type of groundwater is HCO 3 -Ca, and most ions exhibit moderate to significant spatial variability. Its hydrochemical composition is mainly controlled by rock weathering, dominated by the dissolution of carbonate minerals, silicate minerals, and evaporite rocks, with significant cation exchange and limited contribution from gypsum dissolution. The groundwater in the study area is generally suitable for agricultural irrigation. However, EC, Na%, RSC, and MH values are relatively high in the Jiansanjiang area in the northeast, while the EC and RSC values are high in the southeast, which poses a potential risk of soil salinization. This spatial variation is mainly controlled by natural geological conditions. Carbonate mineral weathering controls the spatial distribution of MH and RSC. The dissolution of halite and silicate minerals affects variations in SAR and Na% and indirectly influences MH by inhibiting cation exchange processes. RSC shows relatively low correlations with various hydrochemical parameters, indicating that its spatial distribution is regulated by multiple coupled factors. These findings can provide a scientific basis for the rational utilization of groundwater resources, irrigation management, and salinity hazard prevention and control in similar regions.

Article.Title: Simulation of compressible flow and convergence enhancement in finned porous medium PCM systems considering non-linear material properties
Article.Authors: Liu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fin enhanced melting of phase change materials (PCMs) is widely used to mitigate the inherently low thermal conductivity of PCMs in thermal energy storage systems. In this study, lauric acid is selected as the PCM, and numerical models are developed for four configurations: unfinned, single-fin, triple-fin, and triple-fin structures with porous media. The governing equations are derived based on the compressible Navier Stokes equations framework, incorporating nonlinear, temperature-dependent variations in dynamic viscosity, thermal conductivity, and density throughout the melting process. To improve physical fidelity, solid and liquid transition zones and buoyancy driven volume force terms are incorporated. A thermos melting based correction is applied to adjust the specific heat capacity and Prandtl number, while empirical relations are introduced to improve numerical convergence and stability. Numerical simulations are conducted at inclination angles of 0°, 45°, and 90°, and the predicted liquid phase distributions and temperature fields are validated against available experimental data. The results indicate that the modified formulation substantially enhances convergence under strong nonlinear and multiphysics coupling conditions, with improvements of up to 71.9% and an average gain of 65.3% in porous media configurations. The root mean square error for temperature was merely 0.96 K, while the relative error for melting time stood at just 4.4%. The proposed methodology provides a more accurate and stable framework for simulating fin enhanced PCM melting under compressible conditions, offering useful insights for heat transfer analysis in viscous compressible fluids.

Article.Title: Carbon accounting method for industrial sectors at prefectural level: the case of Shanxi Province
Article.Authors: Li Z.; Huang G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurately quantifying carbon dioxide (CO₂) generation from industrial sectors at the prefectural level is both critically important and highly amenable to methodological improvement. This study develops a systematic, machine learning–enhanced framework for precise sectoral CO₂ generation estimation and robust imputation of missing data. Utilizing this framework, an extensive carbon accounting analysis is performed for Shanxi Province, a major energy production hub in China, encompassing 30 industrial sectors across its 11 prefectural regions during the years 2007 to 2022. Furthermore, the resulting dataset is used to characterize the spatial distribution and sectoral heterogeneity of industrial CO₂ generation. This study advances the existing literature along four dimensions: (i) it achieves carbon accounting at a significantly finer spatial and sectoral resolution; (ii) it introduces a more sophisticated, algorithm-driven accounting framework grounded in state-of-the-art machine learning techniques; (iii) it incorporates a broader spectrum of energy types and explicitly accounts for sector-specific variations in carbon emission factors across energy sources; and (iv) it implements a rigorous reclassification of industrial sectors alongside nuanced, deflation-adjusted treatments of monetary indicators to ensure temporal consistency and comparability of industrial carbon dioxide generation estimates over time.

Article.Title: Effectiveness of local infiltration analgesia and femoral nerve block in primary total knee arthroplasty: A prospective, participant and outcome-assessor-blinded randomized trial
Article.Authors: Kocon M.; Fleming M.; Grzelecki D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Postoperative pain following total knee arthroplasty (TKA) can delay mobilization and increase the need for opioids. Local infiltration analgesia (LIA) and femoral nerve block (FNB) are widely used methods in postoperative multimodal analgesia, but the added value of combining these techniques remains uncertain. In this prospective, participant- and outcome-assessor-blinded randomized trial (ISRCTN11696218), 125 patients undergoing primary TKA for idiopathic osteoarthritis (Kellgren–Lawrence grades II–III) were randomized into five groups: (1) Control (no additional intervention), (2) Placebo (periarticular infiltration with 100 mL saline), (3) LIA (periarticular infiltration with ropivacaine 300 mg + epinephrine 1 mg + piroxicam 20 mg diluted with saline to a total volume of 100 mL), (4) FNB (ultrasound-guided, bupivacaine 25–50 mg + epinephrine 25–50 mcg, dosed according to the attending anesthesiologist’s preference, + 100 mL saline infiltration), and (5) LIA + FNB. Outcomes were assessed preoperatively and on postoperative days (POD) 1–5. Primary outcomes included mean opioid consumption converted to morphine milligram equivalents (MME). Secondary outcomes included pain intensity measured by a visual analog scale (VAS), and passive knee range of motion (ROM). Statistically, to exclude the influence of confounding factors in the form of contralateral knee surgery, a longitudinal linear mixed-effects model was constructed. A total of 125 patients were randomized and analyzed. Baseline demographics were comparable across groups. On POD 1, the LIA + FNB group had lower mean opioid requirements (93.7 mg MME) compared to the Placebo group (138.6 mg MME; mean difference − 44.9 mg MME), the isolated FNB group ( 123.7 mg MME; mean difference − 30.0 mg MME), and the isolated LIA group (116.8 mg MME; mean difference − 23.2 mg MME, $$\:\text{p}=0.027$$ ), but there was no difference compared to the Control group (107.4 mg MME) Opioid use dropped sharply after POD 1 and remained relatively low across all groups from POD 2 to POD 5, with minor fluctuations. Early postoperative pain scores remained moderately high (mean VAS 5.5–6.9) on POD 1 across all interventions. The LIA+FNB group demonstrated an early ROM advantage on POD 1 (mean 66.7°); however, from POD 3 onward, LIA alone provided comparable mobility benefits (POD 5 mean 97.6°). Combining LIA and FNB provides a modest, time-limited reduction in early opioid consumption on POD 1 compared to a placebo infiltration or isolated FNB but lacks overall superiority over a standard control or LIA administered alone. LIA utilized as an independent strategy optimizes mobility recovery without the added interventions of peripheral blocks. The addition of FNB to LIA does not substantially alter the overall recovery trajectory. Article.Title: A multi task deep learning framework for automated health condition prediction from retinal fundus images using hybrid attention and explainable AI
Article.Authors: Tenali R.; Potnuri A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Although retinal fundus imaging is a non-invasive tool to assess systemic and fundus pathology, current deep learning algorithms are mostly single-task, lack clinical interpretability and are unable to handle acquisition variation between different domains. These constraints limit their clinical utility: when a patient comes to the clinic for fundus screening, they could also be diabetic, have glaucoma, AMD, and increased cardiovascular risk, with each disease having retinal vascular biomarkers that require a patient to be tested for in the clinic, which must be managed within a framework of common, interpretable, and generalizable models rather than a pipeline of independent models. To solve these problems, we suggest a multi-task deep learning network that simultaneously classifies DR severity (five-class), glaucoma likelihood (binary), AMD stage (four-class) and cardiovascular risk (binary) from a single retinal fundus image using a single forward pass. It adopts an EfficientNet-B4 convolutional backbone pretrained on the ImageNet dataset, a six-layer multi-head self-attention Transformer encoder (d_model = 512, h = 8), a novel dual-branch spatial-channel attention module that builds on, but significantly expands, the CBAM module, and four task-specific output heads that are optimized using the homoscedastic uncertainty-weighted multi-task loss following the formulation of Kendall et al. Per-task anatomical explanations are produced by back propagating the CNN backbone via Grad-CAM in the anatomical space. The proposed model was evaluated on EyePACS, APTOS 2019, Messidor-2 and RIM-ONE v3 and achieved an accuracy of 94.7%, AUC = 0.978, sensitivity = 93.2% and specificity = 95.8% while being statistically better than all single task models (DeLong test, p < 0.01, Bonferroni corrected). Under the reported experimental setting, the zero-shot cross-dataset evaluation achieves AUC ≥ 0.951, which is promising for its performance across datasets. Grad-CAM saliency maps are anatomically similar to established clinical grading criteria for each disease. The four task-specific heads share a single architecture and produce four outputs in one forward pass, but no individual patient in the training corpora had verified ground-truth labels for all four conditions simultaneously; the model is trained on partially labelled, multi-source data via a masked multi-task loss, and the cardiovascular output is an AVR-derived image-based surrogate rather than a validated clinical cardiovascular diagnosis. This proposed framework could be considered for an additional potential step toward the future when it comes to multi-disease fundus screening with an interpretable single-model solution, if it is assessed and approved at an independent multi-centre level and by regulatory bodies.

Article.Title: Multi-timescale voltage optimization and control for distribution networks based on regional priority evaluation and deep reinforcement learning
Article.Authors: Zhao S.; Jiang H.; Xiong T.; Dou X.; Bu Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract With the increasing penetration of distributed photovoltaic (PV) generation, energy storage systems, and other flexible resources in distribution networks, conventional voltage regulation methods struggle to address both overvoltage and undervoltage violations and to coordinate heterogeneous devices operating at different timescales. Existing region-based multi-agent control methods typically treat partitioned regions as homogeneous decision-making units and lack an explicit mechanism to characterize spatiotemporal variations in regional regulation capability and available flexibility. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a multi-timescale voltage optimization and control method for distribution networks based on regional priority evaluation and deep reinforcement learning. First, a coordinated voltage regulation architecture spanning long and short timescales is established. At the long timescale, a double deep Q-network (DDQN) is employed to centrally schedule discrete voltage regulation devices from a system-wide perspective. At the short timescale, a comprehensive regional voltage regulation evaluation index is introduced to quantify the regulation capability and potential of each region and thereby determine its regulation priority. A priority-aware state feature encoding (PASFE) module equipped with a learnable gating mechanism then adaptively fuses regional physical information with coordination information broadcast by the upper-level controller. The resulting priority-aware representations are incorporated into the regional actor and centralized critic networks, enabling the multi-agent algorithm to perform fine-grained regulation of individual continuously adjustable devices. Case studies on the IEEE 33-bus and 141-bus systems demonstrate that the proposed method effectively eliminates bus-voltage violations and outperforms the benchmark strategies in mitigating voltage deviations and reducing network losses, thereby confirming the effectiveness of regional-priority guidance in enhancing coordinated multi-timescale voltage regulation.

Article.Title: An integrated bidirectional LSTM and adaptive cubature Kalman filter estimation method for accurate state-of-charge estimation of lithium-ion battery
Article.Authors: Kondru J.; Obulesu Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Model-based observers for lithium-ion battery state-of-charge (SOC) estimation lose accuracy under strong nonlinearities and sensor noise, while purely data-driven estimators lack physical consistency and generalise poorly outside their training distribution. Existing hybrid designs address this gap only partially: neural-network outputs are typically fused with an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) as a loosely coupled correction term, so first-order linearisation error and static noise statistics still limit performance under aggressive drive cycles. This paper proposes a tightly coupled Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory-Adaptive Cubature Kalman Filter (BiLSTM-ACKF) framework that resolves these limitations through three distinct mechanisms. First, the BiLSTM output is reformulated as a scalar pseudo-measurement of SOC, rather than a terminal-voltage correction, so the innovation is expressed directly in SOC units and is independent of the open-circuit-voltage-SOC slope. Second, an innovation-driven adaptive covariance law continuously re-weights the measurement noise covariance according to the real-time agreement between the BiLSTM output and the model-predicted SOC, self-regulating the filter’s trust in the data-driven channel. Third, cubature-point propagation replaces Jacobian linearisation in a single-RC Thevenin equivalent-circuit model, eliminating first-order truncation bias under strongly nonlinear transients. A sliding window sequence of voltage and current measurements were used to train the BiLSTM. Validation was conducted with four different driving cycles (DST, FUDS, UDDS and US06), at three temperatures (5° C, 25° C and 45° C), and six levels of Gaussian white voltage noise (0 mV, 30 mV, 80 mV) using two datasets provided by the TU-Berlin repository (LA92 and US06). Comparison results show that BiLSTM-ACKF significantly outperformed both the stand-alone BiLSTM (with a range of 40–60% lower RMSE values than BiLSTM) and BiLSTM-AEKF (with a range of 30–52% lower RMSE values than BiLSTM-AEKF) across all four driving cycles and all six levels of noise. With respect to error magnitude, BiLSTM-ACKF also demonstrated a consistent upper bound of less than 1.5% over all test cases.

Article.Title: Frequency and duration of BIS values outside 40–60 during blinded BIS recording in paediatric anaesthesia: a prospective observational study
Article.Authors: Bönischová T.; Klabusayová E.; Kondé A.; Klincová M.; Kramplová T.; Harazim H.; Fabián D.; Kašová V.; Obermannová L.; Latinovič M.; Klučka J.; Štourač P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This prospective observational study included 104 paediatric patients aged 1–19 years undergoing elective surgery under sevoflurane-based general anaesthesia and combined anaesthesia (general anaesthesia combined with a regional anaesthetic technique) between January 2022 and March 2024. BIS was recorded continuously while anaesthesiologists were blinded to the readings. Episodes of BIS < 40 or > 60 lasting ≥ 30 s were analysed. Postoperative outcomes included emergence delirium (ED) (PAED score), postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), and other complications in patients admitted to the PACU. Overall, 85.6% of patients experienced at least one episode outside the recommended BIS range. The median time spent outside BIS 40–60 was 22 min (35.1% of the duration of surgery). Episodes of BIS < 40 were observed in 61.5% of patients, and BIS > 60 occurred in 51.9% of patients. Blinded BIS monitoring revealed frequent and prolonged deviations from the conventionally recommended anaesthetic depth range in paediatric patients, even when anaesthesia was managed according to conventional physiological and clinical parameters. However, the clinical significance of these findings and their relationship to postoperative outcomes remain uncertain.

Article.Title: A primary cell culture platform for studying venom gland and brain tissue in octopus
Article.Authors: Parziale J.; Attarde S.; Khalid F.; Sangana P.; Holford M.
Article.Abstract: Coleoid cephalopods, squids, cuttlefish, and octopuses, have emerged as powerful model organisms for studying neurobiology, development, and behavior, however, cellular tools for investigating their specialized tissues remain limited. In particular, their venom producing gland, the posterior salivary gland (PSG), has been extensively described anatomically and histologically, yet remains largely inaccessible to experimental investigation at the cellular level. Here, we report the first establishment of primary cell cultures derived from both the optic lobe (OL) and PSG tissues of Octopus bimaculoides . Building on recent advances in cephalopod brain cultures, we adapted and optimized dissociation and culture conditions to support short-term survival and attachment of cells in vitro. We show that passive cell release during tissue handling, rather than enzymatic treatment, yields viable cultures from both tissues, and poly-D-lysine markedly improves the adherence of PSG-derived cells. Morphological analyses and fluorescent staining confirm the presence and viability of distinct cell populations, while cell cycle analysis indicates that the majority of cells reside in G 0 /G 1 phase. Notably, O. bimaculoides OL cultures share several features with the recently described squid brain cultures, including passive cell release, and an adherent fibroblast-like cell population, but additionally contain a predominant population of spherical cells, suggesting both conserved and species-specific coleoid cell behavior in vitro. Together, our findings establish a foundational in vitro platform for studying octopus venom and neural cell biology, providing a tractable system for probing venom biosynthesis, secretion, and neural regulation in coleoid cephalopods.

Article.Title: Physics-guided deep learning inference of intramural slow-conduction depth from simulated epicardial optical mapping
Article.Authors: Maciūnas K.; Marozas V.; Williams S.; Williams M.; Guimaraes A.; Bodagh N.; Klis M.; Vigneswaran V.; Gharaviri A.; Kietzell A.; Mačianskienė R.; Jurevičius J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Epicardial optical mapping integrates fluorescence over depth, making intramural slow conduction difficult to localize from surface signals alone. We present a simulation-based proof-of-concept study coupling monodomain electrophysiology and Monte Carlo photon transport to generate epicardial optical action potentials (OAPs) from slow-conduction layers in a 5 mm ventricular wall. In an initial 71-case depth sweep with fixed layer properties, 5-fold cross-validation of a one-dimensional residual network gave $$r=0.963$$ , $$R^2=0.916$$ , and RMSE $$=0.298$$ mm, with reduced performance beyond approximately 3 mm. We then varied start depth (0.5–3.5 mm), thickness (0.15–0.50 mm), and conductivity multiplier (0.15–0.4) in a 279-case factorial study. Training the same architecture on this expanded dataset and using grouped-depth cross-validation, in which every substrate variant at each test depth was withheld, retained predictive depth information across all tested combinations ( $$r=0.852$$ , $$R^2=0.717$$ , RMSE $$=0.476$$ mm), although accuracy varied with layer thickness and conductivity. Previously acquired rabbit optical and depth-stepped microelectrode recordings showed behaviour consistent with the simulated signals but were not used to train or quantitatively validate the estimator. These results demonstrate that simulated OAP morphology contains recoverable information about slow-layer depth across the tested variations in layer thickness and conductivity.

Article.Title: Risk-zone-stratified occurrence and antimicrobial resistance of E. coli and Salmonella spp. in ready-to-eat foods sold near elementary schools in urban Bangladesh
Article.Authors: Rahman A.; Khan S.; Amin A.; Islam A.; Islam M.; Remon M.; Sumi S.; Uday Z.; Hasan M.; Chy M.; Khan S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ready-to-eat foods sold near schools may contribute to children’s exposure to enteric bacteria, particularly in urban settings where informal food vending occurs near wastewater, animal markets, slaughter-related activities, and poorly managed solid waste. This study assessed the prevalence and antimicrobial resistance profiles of Escherichia coli and Salmonella spp. in ready-to-eat foods sold near elementary schools in an urban area of Bangladesh, comparing school areas with different environmental risk conditions. A comparative cross-sectional study was conducted from November 2025 to February 2026 in urban area of Bangladesh. A total of 210 ready-to-eat food samples were collected from vendors within 200 m of 30 elementary schools, including 105 samples from high-risk school areas and 105 from low-risk areas. High-risk schools were located within 500 m of predefined potential contamination sources, while low-risk schools were at least 1.5 km away. E. coli and Salmonella spp. were isolated using culture-based methods and confirmed by polymerase chain reaction. Antimicrobial susceptibility was assessed using the Kirby–Bauer disk diffusion method. Prevalence estimates were calculated with 95% confidence intervals. Associations were examined using chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests and multivariable logistic regression with school-cluster-adjusted standard errors. Overall, 89 of 210 samples were contaminated with at least one target organism, giving a prevalence of 42.4%. E. coli was detected in 41 samples (19.5%), and Salmonella spp. was detected in 57 samples (27.1%). Contamination was higher in high-risk than low-risk areas for E. coli (34.3% vs. 4.8%), Salmonella spp. (41.0% vs. 13.3%), and any contamination (66.7% vs. 18.1%). In adjusted models, high-risk areas remained strongly associated with E. coli contamination, Salmonella contamination, and any contamination. All tested isolates were resistant to amoxicillin. Multidrug resistance was more frequent among Salmonella isolates than E. coli isolates. Ready-to-eat foods sold near elementary schools in this urban setting showed substantial contamination with E. coli and Salmonella spp., with higher contamination in environmentally high-risk school areas. These findings highlight the need for One Health food-safety surveillance integrating school health, municipal sanitation, animal-market hygiene, vendor practices, and AMR monitoring. Article.Title: Spatial and temporal patterns of human-elephant conflict and compensation in Nagaon District, Assam, India
Article.Authors: Bhuyan C.; Bora C.; Das M.
Article.Abstract: Human-elephant conflict (HEC) threatens both biodiversity and rural livelihoods. Forest departments in affected districts hold decades of compensation-claim records, but these archives are seldom analyzed for the spatial and temporal insights they contain. This study analyses twenty-one years of compensation-claim records from Nagaon District, Assam, India (1999–2020) to identify the spatial, seasonal, and institutional structure of conflict, and to assess whether compensation is allocated in proportion to the burden it addresses. Getis-Ord Gi* and Local Moran’s I statistics were applied to 1,915 georeferenced incidents across 1,032 villages, and 1,788 records with complete financial data were examined using non-parametric correlation, Theil-Sen regression, and segmentation by policy regime. Conflict was reported in 241 villages (23.35%), with hotspots concentrated along the Karbi Anglong foothills and human casualty clusters localized in the northeastern part of the district. Incidents peaked in December (23.29%), coinciding with the Sali rice harvest. Property and crop damage together accounted for over 88% of claims but under 28% of disbursed funds, while human fatalities represented 6.26% of claims and 68.37% of funds. Claim volume explained only 31.8% of the variation in payouts, with compensation rate revisions accounting for most of the remainder. Mitigation should be spatially targeted and seasonally adaptive, and compensation restructured into a tiered, need-based model that recognizes chronic livelihood loss alongside catastrophic outcomes.

Article.Title: Numerical simulation and structural optimization of electrostatic precipitators for particle purification in space capsules
Article.Authors: Meng L.; Wang H.; Su N.; He M.; Mo F.; Liu C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To address the demand for performance optimization of electrostatic precipitators (ESPs) for space applications, this study numerically solves and analyzes the electric field characteristics and microparticle flow behaviors of ESP structures by coupling the discrete phase model (DPM) with the user-defined scalar (UDS) transport equation. Taking the structural optimization of electrodes and dust collection plates as the core entry point, four types of ESP structures were established for comparative research, namely the conventional Flat-type, W-type, W1-type (wave plate‑auxiliary electrode composite type) and Single-type (horizontal single-electrode type). The research focuses on investigating the synergistic effect of the pre-installed filter screen, the flow field distribution inside the ESP structure, the characteristics of electric field and charge density, as well as the correlation between particle motion trajectories and dust collection efficiency.The results show that after adopting strategies including expanding the area of dust collection plates, optimizing electric field distribution and extending the corona discharge region, the dust collection efficiency of particles with sizes ranging from 0.2 to 1.0 μm in the W1-type and Single-type structures both exceeds 92%. Compared with the Flat-type structure, the dust collection efficiency of the W1-type and Single-type structures for 0.5 μm particles is increased to over 90%, representing an improvement of approximately 40% relative to the conventional structure. In addition, the pre-installed filter screen enables the synergistic purification of mechanical interception and electrostatic collection, further enhancing the dust removal efficiency, which verifies the feasibility of the multi-stage purification mode. This study provides a theoretical basis for the design and optimization of electrostatic precipitators in the aerospace field.

Article.Title: Dispositional pessimism selectively predicts engagement with system-blame conspiracy theory around COVID-19 on social media
Article.Authors: Piksa M.; Kunst J.; Gundersen A.; Krysinska I.; Wojtowicz T.; Morzy M.; Piasecki J.; Rygula R.
Article.Abstract: Understanding why some individuals engage with conspiracy theories online remains a central challenge in misinformation research. In this study, we analyzed data from 2,506 U.S.-based Twitter users linked to over 7.7 million of their social media engagements, focusing on six COVID-19-related conspiracy theories. Using machine learning classification of ecologically valid behavioral tracking and multilevel modeling, we investigated whether self-reported dispositional optimism and pessimism, along with experimentally measured judgment bias, could predict interest in conspiracy-related content. Our results revealed that dispositional pessimism was selectively associated with engagement with one of the six conspiracy theories examined - specifically, the narrative that “ The virus and response to it are aimed at creating economic instability and benefiting large corporations .” The remaining five theories showed no such association, and neither dispositional optimism nor judgment bias predicted engagement with any of the six narratives. These findings suggest that dispositional pessimism may increase susceptibility to conspiracy theories that emphasize systemic threats, while leaving others unaffected. This underscores the role of affective-cognitive dispositions in shaping engagement with conspiratorial narratives and real-world digital behavior.

Article.Title: Transformer-based architectures for anomaly detection in solar-wind integrated energy infrastructures
Article.Authors: Asati R.; Khare V.
Article.Abstract: The growing incorporation of variable solar and wind power in electrical grids leads to serious issues concerning reliability due to the complexity of spatial and temporal behavior caused by factors like variations in environmental conditions, degradation of equipment, failures of sensors, and exceptional operating conditions. Therefore, we develop an innovative transformer-based deep-learning approach for anomaly detection in integrated solar-wind energy systems using real-life multivariate time series datasets from a renewable energy facility situated in Kayathar, Tamil Nadu, India. The framework proposed in this paper consists of data preparation and normalization, sliding window conducted as a set of sequences, anomaly data creation based on domain knowledge, transformer encoder enhanced with multi-head self-attention technology and the attention mechanism-based data interpretation. The effectiveness of the framework is compared with LSTM, GRU and CNN-LSTM using MSE, accuracy and ROC-AUC. The obtained results indicate the sufficient performance of the transformer model with the lowest MSE value of 0.00641 in comparison to 0.00831, 0.00859 and 0.00792 achieved for LSTM, GRU and CNN-LSTM respectively. The transformer model has also achieved the value of accuracy equal to 95% together with ROC-AUC of 0.89. However, at the default classification threshold, this accuracy was driven almost entirely by the majority (normal) class, and the model failed to identify any of the 10 labelled anomalies in the confusion-matrix evaluation (recall = 0% for the anomaly class), reflecting a severe 18.8:1 class imbalance in the test set. The correlation and attention analysis performed in the study shows that the model is capable of revealing significant interdependence among various environmental parameters and renewable power generation rates such as solar radiation and solar energy production ( r = 0.84) and wind speed and wind energy production ( r = 0.90).

Article.Title: Digital application literacy as a mediator of GAI-TPACK among non-STEM teachers after year-long professional development
Article.Authors: Dai Y.; Ye Z.; Du M.; Zhai X.
Article.Abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) can produce and revise instructional content through probabilistic, conversational interaction, creating demands that extend beyond routine use of digital tools. This study examined how digital technology knowledge and skills (DL-S) and digital application literacy (DL-A) relate to GAI-integrated technological pedagogical content knowledge (GAI-TPACK) among 224 Chinese primary and secondary teachers in general-subject settings. Participants completed a year-long professional development program and a post-intervention survey. Structural equation modeling showed positive paths from DL-S to DL-A (β = 0.300) and GAI-TPACK (β = 0.317), and from DL-A to GAI-TPACK (β = 0.453). The indirect effect of DL-S through DL-A was 0.137 (95% bootstrap CI [0.069, 0.219]), consistent with partial mediation. The larger point estimate for DL-A was not tested directly against the DL-S coefficient and is therefore interpreted descriptively. These findings position DL-A as a plausible practice-oriented mechanism linking foundational digital capability with subject-specific GAI integration. Because competence was self-reported at one post-intervention time point, the model does not establish causal development. The study offers a bounded operational account of GAI-TPACK for non-STEM professional development and identifies priorities for multi-wave and performance-based research.

Article.Title: Optogenetic modeling of wake-like transcriptional progression in human SH-SY5Y neuronal cells
Article.Authors: Yamazaki S.; Gee W.; Valekunja U.; Reddy A.
Article.Abstract: Sleep deprivation induces widespread transcriptional remodeling in the brain, but the extent to which this response arises from sustained neuronal excitation rather than systemic confounders remains unclear. Here we establish a reductionist human neuronal model to isolate the cell-autonomous effects of prolonged depolarization. Optogenetic stimulation of SH-SY5Y cells produced controlled calcium influx and robust induction of activity-dependent genes, enabling precise manipulation of excitation history. Time-resolved RNA sequencing revealed that sustained excitation partitions transcriptional responses into discrete temporal modules, including early-, mid-, and late-peaking, sustained, biphasic, and suppressed patterns, each with distinct functional signatures. At the pathway level, these modules combine into sequential transcriptional states that evolve directionally across stimulation and recovery. Transitions were asymmetric, indicating excitation-history-dependent reorganization rather than simple reversal. Cross-dataset comparisons revealed selective concordance between defined temporal modules and in vivo sleep deprivation signatures. Together, these findings demonstrate that sustained neuronal excitation alone can drive staged, wake-like transcriptional progression, linking gene-level temporal dynamics to higher-order regulatory states.

Article.Title: Improved HCV genotyping based on sequence encoding and feature integration
Article.Authors: Fahmy A.; Hammad M.; Al-Atabany W.; Mabrouk M.
Article.Abstract: Genomic sequence classification is an important task for understanding viral genetic variability and supporting genotype identification, particularly for viruses such as the Hepatitis C Virus (HCV). In this study, we evaluate the effectiveness of different sequence encoding techniques, supplementary genomic descriptors, and class-balancing strategies for HCV genotype classification under a stricter CD-HIT-EST cluster-aware evaluation protocol designed to reduce sequence-identity leakage. Four encoding methods were investigated, namely Frequency Chaos Game Representation (FCGR), k-mer encoding, one-hot encoding, and label encoding. These representations were evaluated using multiple machine learning models, including XGBoost, Random Forest, Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). To address class imbalance, SMOTE was applied, while GC content and GC skew were included as supplementary compositional descriptors. Overall, FCGR and k-mer encoding outperformed one-hot and label encoding. The best result was achieved using k-mer encoding with XGBoost and SMOTE, obtaining a macro F1-score of 0.890, accuracy of 0.922, macro precision of 0.866, macro recall of 0.925, macro specificity of 0.990, and MCC of 0.893 under the CD-HIT-EST cluster-aware evaluation setting. The statistical analysis showed that SMOTE had a clear positive effect on classification performance, particularly for the Random Forest model, while GC-based descriptors provided additional interpretability but did not show a statistically significant improvement in the k-mer-based experiment. Overall, this study demonstrates the importance of selecting appropriate sequence encodings and class-balancing strategies for machine-learning-based HCV genotype classification. The findings provide a comparative basis for future work on sequence-based classification tasks in virology and computational genomics.

Article.Title: A virulent and temperate phage cocktail synergizes with antibiotics against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Article.Authors: González-Gómez J.; Elizalde-Flores E.; Aispuro-Leal C.; Rodríguez-Arellano S.; Gomez-Gil B.; Ruíz-Ramírez A.; Castro-del Campo N.; Chaidez C.
Article.Abstract: The rapid emergence of multidrug-resistant bacteria necessitates antimicrobial strategies that constrain resistance while preserving efficacy. Phage cocktails are typically composed exclusively of virulent phages, whereas the therapeutic potential of temperate phages remains largely unexplored. Here, we evaluate a two-phage cocktail combining a virulent (ARP5) and a temperate (ARP3) phage against a multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical isolate (PaAK08). While ARP5 alone achieved strong bacterial suppression and ARP3 displayed limited efficacy, the combined cocktail sustained > 98% suppression across multiplicities of infection for 30 h. Resistance profiling revealed no cross-resistance between phages, consistent with receptor independence. Phenotypic and genomic analyses of resistant mutants identified alterations in surface-associated structures, including glycosyltransferase-linked loci, and ARP3 prophage integration events. Phage ratio optimization maintained suppression at reduced concentrations, with statistical analysis supporting additive interactions. Notably, co-administration with subinhibitory tobramycin or ofloxacin produced synergistic suppression, achieving complete inhibition for 48 h with ofloxacin. Together, these findings demonstrate that virulent–temperate phage combinations can function compatibly, expand therapeutic design frameworks, and potentiate antibiotic activity against multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa .

Article.Title: Deployment of edge-lightweight AI vertical models in multimodal anomaly detection and energy optimization of tech-long production line
Article.Authors: Wu X.; Tao X.; Cheng Y.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: Aiming at the problems that the abnormal state of high-speed liquid packaging production lines is difficult to identify in time, the computing power of edge controller is limited, and the energy consumption regulation and condition monitoring are separated from each other, a multimodal lightweight artificial intelligence (AI) system embedded in Tech-Long production controller is constructed; this realizes the collaborative optimization of abnormal operation window identification and energy consumption of the whole line. First, this study collects vibration, acoustic, and thermal signals from the bottle blowing, filling, and packaging sections; it also constructs cross-sectional anomaly characterization through time synchronization, feature-level alignment, and hierarchical fusion. Subsequently, Feather Convolutional Neural Network (FeatherCNN) is reconstructed using kernel fusion, channel compression, and 4-bit Integer (INT4) quantization to reduce model computation and storage load; thus, the network can adapt to resource-constrained Advanced RISC Machine (ARM) edge controllers. Finally, a dual-layer control chain is built, composed of continuous basic energy-saving and anomaly risk-weighted correction, so that anomaly scores influence the updates of temperature zones, valve openings, and heat-sealing parameters via dynamic weights and adjustment gains. The experimental results demonstrate that the anomaly window recognition accuracy of multimodal FeatherCNN reaches 0.931, which is superior to traditional machine learning models, deep learning baselines and various single-modal structures. The lightweight processing reduces Floating-Point Operations (FLOPs) from 3.42×10⁹ to 0.58×10⁹, a decrease of approximately 83%. The inference latency of the complete model on the ARM controller is shortened from 18.63 milliseconds (ms) to 7.41 ms. Under the controlled conditions of fixed production line speed, material specifications, and statistical windows, the dual-layer collaborative control has reduced the overall energy consumption of the whole line by 26%. The results show that multimodal anomaly identification, model lightweighting, and energy-saving parameter tuning can work together in the same edge decision chain. The framework verifies the feasibility of resource-constrained controllers supporting abnormal monitoring and energy consumption regulation of the entire packaging line; meanwhile, it provides an engineering reference for edge intelligent deployment of similar high-speed liquid packaging lines.

Article.Title: Ethnotaxonomy and phenotypic evidence for a zone of high common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris L.) diversity in northeastern Amazonian Peru
Article.Authors: Vecco-Giove C.; Barrera-Lozano M.; Tuesta-Chichipe E.; Rivera J.; Pinchi M.; Ortiz R.; Tobaru J.; Blas R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The common bean ( Phaseolus vulgaris L.) is a key crop in the Americas, yet its diversity in the Peruvian Amazon Basin remains poorly documented. We examined geographic and ethnographic patterns in vernacular naming and phenotypic diversity of common beans across three biomes: the inter-Andean Marañón Valley, the Highland Rainforest, and the Amazonian lowlands. Using lexical sources, ethnobotanical interviews, and phenotypic evaluation of seeds, we recorded 152 specific vernacular names and 20 generic terms for P. vulgaris across 26 ethnic groups. Naming categories relied primarily on morphological criteria, complemented by references to origin, growth habit, culinary properties, and historical events. Vernacular name richness and phenotypic diversity exhibited a congruent geographic concentration, with the highest values recorded in the Highland Rainforest biome. These results suggest a geographically continuous zone of high common bean diversity in the northeastern Peruvian Amazon, spanning the inter-Andean Marañón Valley, the Highland Rainforest, and adjacent Amazonian regions. While the observed congruence between vernacular and phenotypic diversity is consistent with historical diversification processes, the present evidence does not establish a historical diversification axis. Linguistic and ethnobotanical evidence thus provide a useful framework for documenting and conserving common bean diversity in this bioculturally dynamic region.

Article.Title: Nanobody-based lateral flow assays for the detection of α-bungarotoxin in Bungarus snake venoms
Article.Authors: Thumtecho S.; Belfakir S.; Christensen T.; Rivera-de-Torre E.; Burlet N.; Ljungars A.; Ross G.; Laustsen A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate snake identification is critical for effective antivenom treatment following snakebite envenoming, but remains a major diagnostic challenge. Here, we developed a prototype lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA) designed to distinguish krait ( Bungarus ) from cobra ( Naja ) envenoming in Southeast Asia. To enhance point-of-care utility, the assay employs variable domains of heavy-chain-only antibodies (V H Hs). The V H Hs target α-bungarotoxin (α-BuTx), a neurotoxin unique to Bungarus , with negative selection strategies to minimize cross-reactivity with α-cobratoxin in Naja venom. Our prototype LFIA detected α-BuTx with a visual limit of detection of 0.5–5 ng/mL in running buffer and spiked urine and serum samples. Additionally, the assay detected Bungarus whole venom at 50–500 ng/mL in running buffer. No cross-reactivity with Naja venom was observed at clinically relevant concentrations, with signals detected only at supraphysiological concentrations (≥50,000 ng/mL). These results support the feasibility of using V H H-based LFIAs for guiding timely, targeted antivenom administration in resource-limited settings.

Article.Title: Effect of nursing care program on healthy lifestyle behaviours and quality of life in women with endometriosis: a randomised controlled trial
Article.Authors: Bursa A.; Sahin N.
Article.Abstract: This study was conducted to determine the effect of Endometriosis Nursing Care Program (ENCP), developed in line with Health Promotion Model for women with endometriosis, on women's quality of life and healthy lifestyle behaviours. This prospective, single-centre, randomized controlled trial was conducted with 46 women diagnosed with endometriosis who applied to the Endometriosis Outpatient Clinic of a training research hospital. Women with an Endometriosis Health Profile Questionnaire-5 (EHP-5) score ≥ 22 indicating reduced quality of life were included. Participants were randomly assigned to an intervention group (n = 23) receiving Endometriosis Nursing Care Program (ENCP) or a control group (n = 23) receiving routine care. The ENCP consisted of two individual 60-min sessions delivered two weeks apart. The primary outcome was change in quality of life measured by EHP-5. Secondary outcomes included healthy lifestyle behaviours measured by Health Promoting Lifestyle Profile II (HPLP-II). Data were analysed using parametric or non-parametric statistical tests, as appropriate. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Forty-six women completed the study (23 intervention, 23 control). The mean EHP-5 score in the intervention group decreased significantly from 61.8 ± 11.4 to 32.1 ± 18.7; Cohen's d = − 1.71, p < 0.001 after the intervention, while no significant change was observed in the control group ( p > 0.05). HPLP-II total scores significantly increased in the ENCP group (132.04 ± 19.81 vs 164.17 ± 18.83; Cohen's d = 1.58, p < 0.001). ENCP significantly improved quality of life in women with endometriosis and resulted in increased scores on healthy lifestyle behaviours. Structured nursing interventions may play an important role in comprehensive endometriosis care. Article.Title: Stochastic SEIR dynamics via graph Laplacian diffusion under transmission uncertainty
Article.Authors: Achankunju P.; Barman M.; Mishra N.; Dash S.
Article.Abstract: Epidemic spatial spread across interconnected populations depends on both mobility between locations and random fluctuations in transmission. We extend the Susceptible-Exposed-Infected-Removed (SEIR) epidemic model to a network setting by introducing graph Laplacian diffusion to capture population mobility, and further incorporate stochastic perturbations in the transmission rate to capture environmental noise. Using Lyapunov function analysis, we first establish that the stochastic system admits a unique global solution which remains non-negative for all time, so that the model is mathematically well-posed and its state variables retain their epidemiological meaning as population counts. Building on this well-posedness, we then apply Lyapunov techniques a second time to analyse the long-term behaviour of the solution. The disease-free equilibrium is shown to be globally asymptotically stable when the basic reproduction number does not exceed one, indicating disease extinction. When the basic reproduction number exceeds one, the disease instead persists, in the sense that the stochastic solution exhibits a bounded time-averaged deviation from the endemic equilibrium of the corresponding deterministic system. Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) methods are further employed for parameter estimation and uncertainty quantification, applied to COVID-19 incidence data across all 47 prefectures in Japan. The proposed framework brings together network-driven mobility, stochastic transmission dynamics, and Bayesian uncertainty quantification within a SEIR model. Finally, computational experiments on a small-world Watts-Strogatz network are used to validate and visually illustrate the theoretical results.

Article.Title: DashGuard: spatio-temporal deep learning for dashcam-based road accident anticipation
Article.Authors: Pullur Somasekar L.; Sinha A.; Chintaluri N.; Madasamy B.
Article.Abstract: Road traffic accidents claim roughly 1.35 million lives each year, with delayed hazard perception rather than mechanical failure implicated in most collisions. Dashcam-based accident anticipation offers a low-cost complement to sensor-heavy ADAS, yet controlled comparisons across architectures remain rare. We present DashGuard, which trains and evaluates six spatio-temporal models a 3D CNN, CNN+LSTM, CNN+Transformer, and three two-stream variants (lightweight CNN, ResNet-18, and Transformer) on the Car Crash Dataset (1500 crash and 2000 normal videos) under a consistent, leak-free protocol. A video-level 70/15/15 split prevents clip-level contamination; four-level soft labels encode temporal distance to the accident frame; and a two-clip temporal consistency gate substantially cuts false-positive alerts. On the held-out test set, the Two-Stream Transformer achieves AUC = 0.981 and F1 = 0.870, with recall of 0.991. The lightweight 3D CNN (AUC = 0.949, \(\approx \) 180 K parameters) is a viable option for edge hardware. A React/FastAPI web interface supports interactive evaluation. The results show that explicitly separating motion and appearance via two-stream attention gives the clearest gains over single-stream designs on this task.

Article.Title: Integrated bioinformatic analysis identifies distinct neddylation-associated proteasome genes and immune-related features in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
Article.Authors: Wang S.; Xu J.; Ge H.
Article.Abstract: Neddylation contributes to cancer progression, but its relationship with proteasome-related genes and the immune microenvironment in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) remains unclear. We aimed to identify neddylation-associated genes in LSCC and characterize their molecular, metabolic, and immune features. Transcriptomic data from The Cancer Genome Atlas and Gene Expression Omnibus were analyzed using differential expression, functional enrichment, and machine-learning approaches. Key genes were further evaluated by survival, pathway, immune infiltration, and somatic mutation analyses and validated by quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) in five paired LSCC and adjacent tissues. Seventy-four differentially expressed neddylation-related genes were identified. Four genes, KCTD6, PSMB2, PSMB4, and PSMD2, were selected by both LASSO and SVM-RFE. KCTD6-associated genes were enriched in bile acid metabolism, while macrophage M0 and resting CD4 + memory T cells were associated with prognosis. Lower PSMB4 and PSMD2 expression was associated with immune escape-related features. qRT-PCR in five paired specimens confirmed the predicted direction of expression change for all four genes (KCTD6 lower, and PSMB2, PSMB4, and PSMD2 higher in tumor); given the small paired sample, this provides directional confirmation only and does not establish biomarker performance. We identified a distinct set of proteasome-related neddylation-associated genes associated with metabolic and immune characteristics in LSCC. These findings suggest potential links between neddylation-associated proteasome genes and the immune microenvironment in LSCC.

Article.Title: Genomic diversity, population structure, and relatedness of critically endangered Philippine eagles under conservation management
Article.Authors: Pascual F.; Perdon D.; Tablizo F.; Lapid C.; Egana J.; Mantaring R.; Punayan K.; Araiza S.; Llames J.; Abad M.; Gonzalez J.; Ibañez J.; Palmes-Saloma C.
Article.Abstract: The critically endangered Philippine eagle ( Pithecophaga jefferyi ) faces severe threats to its population from habitat loss, naturally slow reproduction cycles, and human encroachment. Thus, 38 years ago, the Philippine Eagle Foundation (PEF) was established for the conservation of the endangered Philippine eagle and its rainforest habitat. To support the PEF’s captive-breeding and rehabilitation efforts, this study investigates the genome-wide single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) profiles of 20 wild-captive and 15 captive-bred individuals under the foundation’s care. Sequence reads were quality-filtered and aligned to a previously generated Philippine eagle reference genome. Identified SNPs across the 35 individuals were then further analyzed to assess population structure, isolation by distance (IBD), inbreeding, and relatedness. Population structure analysis revealed that genetic distance tended to increase with geographic distance, suggesting that the wild-captive eagles follow an pattern. Inbreeding analysis meanwhile showed significantly higher levels among wild-captive eagles compared to those bred in captivity, suggesting limited access to genetically diverse mates in the wild, and highlighting the success of the foundation’s breeding strategy in minimizing inbreeding. Finally, kinship analysis confirmed known first-degree relationships among captive-bred eagles and uncovered novel kinships among wild-captive individuals that reinforce the IBD model. These results represent the first comprehensive conservation genomics study on the Philippine eagle, providing insights into the diversity of its captive and wild populations, as well as valuable information that can guide future breeding and conservation efforts.

Article.Title: Identification of kinematic motifs in crouch gait of children with cerebral palsy
Article.Authors: K S.; Poojari M.; Kumar A.; Krishnan C.; Unnikrishnan B.; Joshua A.; Figarado S.; Nayak M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Crouch gait is among the most disabling gait deviations in cerebral palsy (CP). Powered exoskeletons can supply the extensor thrust orthoses cannot, but their control depends on repeatable kinematic patterns, and crouch gait is perceived as irregular. Five children with CP (8–14 years; Gross Motor Function Classification System [GMFCS] I–III) walked at self-selected speed wearing bilateral shank inertial measurement units, knee goniometers and insole pressure sensors at the heel and forefoot. Signals were filtered with a two-state Kalman filter, adaptively segmented into gait cycles using plantar-pressure events (heel or toe strike), and time-normalised to 101 points. A kinematic motif was defined as a limb’s ensemble waveform and validated using the coefficient of variation, ICC(3,1), dynamic time warping, autocorrelation and 1,000-iteration permutation testing; symmetry was quantified with the Symmetry Index. Repeatability tracked the signal measured rather than functional severity: mean ICC(3,1) was 0.76 for forefoot loading, 0.61 for heel loading and 0.29 for knee kinematics. Full criteria were met in 12 of 30 limb–signal combinations, 12 met one or two, and 6 met none. Five of the six failures were knee channels, also the only channels indistinguishable from a permuted null, yet the knee met all criteria bilaterally in the least affected participant. These preliminary findings establish feasibility in a heterogeneous cohort ( n = 5); no gait-phase classifier was trained or evaluated here.

Article.Title: Development and internal validation of a clinical risk score for early delirium detection in older emergency department patients
Article.Authors: Sanguanwit P.; Sotakul P.; Wangviboonchai V.
Article.Abstract: Delirium is a common but frequently underrecognized neuropsychiatric syndrome among older adults in the emergency department (ED), associated with prolonged hospitalization and increased mortality. To develop a clinical risk score for early delirium detection in older emergency department patients. We conducted a prospective cohort study in the ED of a tertiary hospital from July 2024 to July 2025. Patients aged ≥ 65 years who remained in the ED for > 4 h were assessed using the Thai version of the Confusion Assessment Method intensive care unit (CAM-ICU) within 12 h of arrival. Demographic data, comorbidities, functional status, medications, presenting features, vital signs, laboratory values, and ED diagnoses were collected. Multivariable logistic regression was used to derive a clinical risk score, which was evaluated area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AuROC). Among 380 enrolled patients, 102 (26.8%) were identified with delirium. Five independent variables were included in the final model: age 70–79 years (1 point); age 80–89 years, CKD stage III–V, or prior cerebrovascular accident (12 points); age ≥ 90 years (29 points); cirrhosis (24 points); and dementia (41 points), yielding a total score range of 0–118. The score demonstrated good discriminative performance (AuROC 0.79; 95% CI 0.74–0.84). Delirium occurred in 17.97% of patients with low-risk scores (0–24) and 57.65% of those with high-risk scores (≥ 25). This simple, clinically applicable risk score, based on five readily available variables, shows good ability to identify older ED patients at risk for delirium. Early risk stratification using this tool may support timely preventive and monitoring strategies in the ED. Article.Title: Barriers to living walls implementation in Saudi Arabian sustainable construction projects: A PLS-SEM approach
Article.Authors: Alaboud N.
Article.Abstract: To maximize financial benefits and sustainability throughout a project’s lifecycle, the construction industry must move beyond the partial implementation of living wall (LW). While the existing literature has focused on LW drivers, there is a lack of comprehensive evidence regarding implementation barriers. This study prioritizes and assesses the LW implementation barriers in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) building industry. Data were collected via an expert survey and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The model demonstrated robust internal consistency, with Cronbach’s alpha and composite reliability meeting the required thresholds, and average variance extracted values exceeding the 0.50 (50%) requirement. Based on the second-order analysis, the identified LW barriers were found to be formative, but collinearity was assessed and found to be within the acceptable thresholds (VIF < 3.5), ensuring the distinct contribution of each formative indicator. The path model results showed that awareness and economic barriers ( β = 0.278), integration and complexity barriers (β = 0.303), operational and behavioral barriers (β = 0.380), and resource and structural barriers (β = 0.372) significantly impede LW implementation (all p ≤ 0.001). Conversely, maintenance and technical barriers (β = 0.097) were not significant ( p = 0.227), indicating their minimal impact compared with the other model constructs. These findings provide policy guidance concerning LW adoption in the KSA and other Gulf nations, facilitating the completion of projects by removing the barriers to LW implementation and enhancing their overall success.

Article.Title: SpecLLM: LLM-based VNIR spectral interpretation
Article.Authors: Romaszewski M.; Strzoda A.; Halama M.; Głomb P.; Masłowski P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Visible and near-infrared (VNIR) spectroscopy identifies materials from characteristic spectral bands, and spectroscopists interpret spectra by features such as peak positions and intensities. Recent machine-learning and foundation models for hyperspectral data are highly effective but return numerical outputs or latent representations rather than such feature-level descriptions. Meanwhile, LLM-based spectral approaches have mostly provided raw numerical sequences. We present a method for making spectroscopic data accessible to large language models (LLMs) through compact, feature-based representations. Instead of supplying full spectra as comma-separated values (CSV), JavaScript Object Notation (JSON), or extensible markup language (XML), the proposed approach extracts summary statistics and discriminative extrema. It serialises them as either natural language or structured JSON. We evaluate prototype-based substance classification in two complementary scenes from an open-access VNIR hyperspectral blood dataset. For the selected models, compact feature representations were substantially more effective than raw numerical encodings, but less effective than a Random Forest operating on raw spectra. The natural-language format provides a human-readable, inspectable serialisation of compact spectral evidence and reduces prompt length compared with full-spectrum encodings. We also compared natural language and JSON feature representations and found them broadly comparable.
