Article.Title: Seed persistence of nine weed species in silage, manure, and slurry and implications for dispersal through organic fertilizers
Article.Authors: Nikolić N.; Massaro S.; Tagliapietra F.; Schiavon S.; Masin R.
Article.Abstract: Weed seed contamination of cattle feed can contribute to weed dispersal within crop–livestock systems when viable seeds survive digestion and are returned to fields through manure or slurry applications. However, the persistence of weed seeds from feed preservation to waste recycling remains poorly understood. This study aimed to evaluate the viability of common agricultural weed seeds after exposure to silage fermentation, simulated rumen digestion, and storage in cattle manure and slurry. Seeds of nine weed species ( Abutilon theophrasti , Alopecurus myosuroides , Amaranthus retroflexus , Avena sterilis , Chenopodium album , Datura stramonium , Echinochloa crus-galli , Lolium multiflorum , and Sorghum halepense ) were incubated for one, four, and six months in three silage types (maize, sorghum, and grass) and subsequently incubated in cattle manure and slurry following simulated rumen digestion. Silage fermentation significantly reduced seed viability, although the response varied among weed species and silage types. During storage in cattle waste, seed viability declined progressively, with slurry degrading seeds faster than manure. Nevertheless, seeds of C. album , D. stramonium , A. retroflexus , and E. crus-galli remained viable after six months in manure. These findings suggest that cattle manure may be an important pathway for weed seed persistence and dispersal in agricultural soils, whereas slurry may pose a much lower risk. The results provide practical guidance for manure management strategies aimed at reducing weed spread while supporting sustainable crop–livestock production systems.

Article.Title: Association of perioperative etomidate exposure and mortality after hip fracture surgery: a matched cohort study
Article.Authors: Hung K.; Chang L.; Chen I.
Article.Abstract: Etomidate is often used for anesthetic induction in hemodynamically unstable patients because of its cardiovascular stability, but its transient adrenal suppression raises concern about possible adverse postoperative outcomes. We performed a cohort study using the TriNetX Research Network to examine the association between perioperative etomidate exposure and postoperative outcomes in adults undergoing hip fracture surgery. Patients receiving etomidate were matched 1:1 with controls. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality. Secondary outcomes included pneumonia, sepsis, venous thromboembolism, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs), and acute kidney injury (AKI). After matching, 6,246 patients were included in each group with balanced baseline characteristics. Etomidate exposure was associated with higher risks of 30-day mortality (OR 1.35, 95% CI 1.15–1.60; P < 0.001), pneumonia (OR 1.23, 95% CI 1.03–1.47, P = 0.019), and MACEs (OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.04–1.40, P = 0.014), but a lower risk of AKI (OR 0.83, 95% CI 0.71–0.96, P = 0.014). No significant associations were observed for sepsis or venous thromboembolism. All associations attenuated and became non-significant during extended follow-up (30–180 day). In conclusion, perioperative etomidate exposure was associated with worse short-term postoperative outcomes except for a lower AKI risk. These findings warrant prospective confirmation.

Article.Title: Dynamic weighted federated contrastive learning for robust medical image classification under heterogeneous data
Article.Authors: Yang L.; Wu Q.; Li J.; Guan Q.; Zhao Q.; Xu B.; Yang T.; Yang L.; Zhou T.
Article.Abstract: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence technologies, AI-driven medical image classification has attracted considerable attention in recent years. However, increasingly stringent data privacy regulations have significantly restricted data sharing among medical institutions, making it difficult for traditional centralized learning frameworks to effectively exploit distributed medical data resources. As a privacy-preserving distributed machine learning paradigm, federated learning enables multiple institutions to collaboratively train models without directly exchanging raw data. Nevertheless, federated learning still faces several critical challenges in practical applications, including heterogeneous data distributions and model bias caused by non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a dynamic weighted learning method based on federated contrastive learning. Different from approaches that focus solely on local representation optimization or employ fixed aggregation weights, the proposed framework couples supervised contrastive local training with loss-feedback-based multi-factor client weighting, thereby jointly controlling local representation drift and server-side model aggregation. Specifically, contrastive learning is integrated into the federated learning framework by jointly leveraging local and global model representations for supervised contrastive optimization. This strategy effectively mitigates the distribution discrepancy among different clients and gradually aligns local models with the global model as communication rounds progress. Furthermore, during global aggregation, a loss-feedback rule is introduced to accept the candidate global model parameters and aggregation weights only when the candidate loss-feedback value decreases. In addition, a multi-factor weighted aggregation mechanism is introduced to comprehensively evaluate client contributions based on multiple factors, thereby assigning larger aggregation weights to local models that are more beneficial to global model optimization. Experiments were conducted on an osteoporosis knee X-ray dataset and a COVID–Pneumonia–Normal chest X-ray dataset under IID and different Non-IID settings. Under severe Non-IID conditions, the proposed method achieved accuracies of 92.12% and 96.27%, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 98.31% and 97.68%, and F1 scores of 90.92% and 93.22% on the two datasets, respectively. Comparisons with representative federated learning methods and the static-weighting ablation setting demonstrate that the proposed method maintains competitive classification performance and stable training behavior under heterogeneous client distributions.

Article.Title: Comparison of systemic inflammatory indices and periodontal parameters in patients with rheumatoid arthritis and gouty arthritis with periodontitis
Article.Authors: Beder M.; Yemenoğlu H.; Arpa M.; Cüre O.; Aktürk Ş.
Article.Abstract: The aim of this study was to compare systemic inflammatory indices—including the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR)—and clinical periodontal parameters in systemically healthy patients with periodontitis and patients with periodontitis and concomitant rheumatoid arthritis (RA) or gouty arthritis (GA). 66 participants were divided into three groups: systemically healthy patients with periodontitis (SHP, n = 22), patients with RA and periodontitis (RAP, n = 22) and patients with GA and periodontitis (GAP, n = 22). Periodontal parameters and systemic inflammatory biomarkers SII, SIRI, AISI, NLR, PLR and MLR were assessed. The GAP group exhibited significantly lower probing pocket depth (PPD) and clinical attachment loss (CAL) values and neutrophil counts but higher lymphocyte counts than the other groups (p < 0.05). SII, SIRI, and NLR values were significantly lower in the GAP group compared to the SHP and RAP groups, while AISI and MLR were significantly lower in the GAP group compared to the SHP group (p < 0.05). SII and NLR were positively correlated with BOP, PPD, and CAL (p < 0.05). SII and NLR were positively associated with BOP, PPD, and CAL. However, these findings demonstrate associations rather than diagnostic or prognostic utility and should be confirmed in larger prospective studies.

Article.Title: Controlled nucleation of hopfions with field pulses
Article.Authors: Castillo-Sepulveda S.; Saéz G.; Corona R.; Altbir D.; Carvalho-Santos V.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We demonstrate a mechanism for the deterministic nucleation of magnetic hopfions in cylindrical nanopillars via transient magnetic field pulses. By exploiting a chiral magnetic cylinder with engineered surface uniaxial anisotropy, we show that field pulses trigger a non-equilibrium magnetization dynamics. Depending on the pulse amplitude, the system relaxes into distinct topologically protected energy minima, stabilizing either isolated hopfions or coexisting states with other three-dimensional solitons. This approach offers a framework for manipulating 3D topological textures without requiring localized spin-polarized currents, broadening the understanding of three-dimensional nanomagnetism.

Article.Title: Optimizing fixation and staining to reduce cell detachment in wet-fixed direct smears, a quantitative evidence-based quality improvement study
Article.Authors: Zou Y.; Wang X.; Chen Y.; Wu Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Wet-fixed cytologic smears are inherently prone to cell detachment, which causes cross-contamination and reduces smear cellularity, potentially leading to false-positive diagnoses and diagnostic uncertainty. This study evaluated the effects of the intermediate alcohol step, fixation duration, and slide type on detachment to establish an evidence-based optimized protocol. We evaluated: (i) the necessity and optimal concentration of the intermediate alcohol step; (ii) fixation duration from 30 min to 24 h; and (iii) slide type (ordinary vs. positively charged). Detachment was scored semi-quantitatively using a streak-wiping method. Wilcoxon and Friedman tests were used for paired and block comparisons, respectively. The intermediate alcohol step significantly reduced detachment ( p < 0.05), with 50% ethanol superior to 75% ( p = 0.012). Prolonged fixation progressively decreased detachment ( p < 0.001), with no further statistically significant reduction beyond 3 h. Under optimized conditions, ordinary and positively charged slides performed comparably ( p = 0.811). An evidence-based strategy for laboratory quality improvement—extending fixation toward 3 h, including an intermediate alcohol step (preferably 50% ethanol) at each transition between water and 95% ethanol, and using ordinary slides—substantially reduces detachment. By preserving cellularity and helping to reduce the risk of cross-contamination, this protocol offers an implementable quality improvement tool for cytology laboratories, potentially enhancing diagnostic reliability and patient safety in wet-fixed cytologic preparations.
Article.Topic: Clinical Laboratory Practices and Quality Control

Article.Title: Association of low parental mental health literacy with adolescent depression and anxiety: a large-scale cross-sectional study in Guangdong, China
Article.Authors: Wang X.; Wan Q.; Liu Y.; Jiang Z.; Qiu Q.; Jiang W.; Zhou F.; Kong X.; Zhao F.; Wu H.; Wang S.
Article.Abstract: Adolescent depression and anxiety symptoms are major health concerns, and the family environment plays a critical role. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between parental mental health literacy (PMHL) and adolescent depression and anxiety scores. Based on cross-sectional data from the 2023 Guangdong Adolescent Mental Health Survey, the study included 4,697 pairs of adolescents and their primary caregivers. Questionnaires were used to assess PMHL and adolescents’ levels of depression and anxiety, and weighted linear regression, restricted cubic splines, and subgroup analyses were employed. For every 1-point increase in PMHL, adolescents’ depression scores decreased by 0.033 and anxiety scores by 0.034 (both P < 0.05). The high PMHL group had significantly lower depression and anxiety scores than the low PMHL group. The dose-response relationship was linear. Subgroup analysis revealed interaction effects involving boarding status, mobile phone usage duration, and educational level. Higher PMHL is significantly associated with a lower risk of depression and anxiety among adolescents. Enhancing PMHL may help prevent and intervene in adolescent emotional problems; longitudinal studies are needed to verify the causal relationship.
Article.Topic: Child and Adolescent Psychosocial and Emotional Development

Article.Title: Distribution-based canonical correlation residual monitoring for industrial processes fault detection
Article.Authors: Kini K.; Harrou F.; Madakyaru M.; Sun Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reliable fault detection is essential for safe, efficient, and sustainable industrial processes. This paper proposes a Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA)-based fault detection framework with distribution-based residual monitoring using Hellinger Distance (HD), Kullback–Leibler Distance (KLD), and Kantorovich Distance (KD). Specifically, the proposed approach evaluates residual distributions within a moving window and determines decision thresholds nonparametrically using Kernel Density Estimation (KDE), avoiding restrictive Gaussian assumptions. A key advantage is that the framework requires only fault-free data for model construction and threshold calibration, making it suitable when labeled fault data are scarce or unavailable. The framework detects faults that disrupt the CCA cross-correlation structure, including faults affecting variables in either the predictor or response variables. The proposed approach is evaluated on the Williams–Otto reactor and a Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) under bias, intermittent, drift, and freezing faults. Additional experiments examine faults in CCA input variables, sensitivity to moving-window and KDE settings, and different fault magnitudes. The proposed approach is also compared with CCA-based Squared Prediction Error (CCA-SPE), Principal Component Analysis (PCA), and Support Vector Regression (SVR) monitoring under identical fault scenarios and evaluation conditions. The results show that distribution-based CCA indicators generally outperform conventional CCA-SPE and the considered PCA- and SVR-based strategies. Among them, CCA-KD achieves the best overall performance, with high detection and low false alarm rates. Overall, integrating CCA with distribution-based monitoring provides effective multivariate fault detection.

Article.Title: Microplastic contamination in commercially important marine fishes from the Sohar Coast, Sea of Oman: occurrence, characterization, and polymer composition
Article.Authors: Al Kharusi I.; Dutta S.
Article.Abstract: Microplastic (MP) pollution is an increasing concern in marine environments because of its persistence, bioavailability, and potential implications for marine ecosystem health and seafood safety. Despite growing global attention, information on MP contamination in commercially important marine fish from the Sea of Oman remains limited. This study assessed the occurrence, abundance, and characteristics of MPs in four commercially important fish species from the Sohar coast and tested whether MP contamination differed among species and tissues and was associated with habitat group, sex, and biometric characteristics. A total of 120 fish representing Epinephelus areolatus , Lethrinus microdon , Nematalosa arabica , and Rastrelliger kanagurta were examined for MPs in the gastrointestinal tract (GIT) and gills. Microplastics were extracted using alkaline digestion and visually identified under a stereomicroscope. All 316 recovered particles were subjected to ATR-FTIR spectroscopy; 313 (99.1%) met the ≥ 70% spectral-match criterion and were successfully assigned to polymer types. Microplastics were detected in 79.2% of the examined fish, with a mean total abundance of 2.63 ± 2.60 items individual⁻1. Frequency of occurrence ranged from 66.7% to 90.0% among species. Total MP abundance did not differ significantly among species, whereas GIT MP concentration differed significantly among species. GIT–gill differences were significant only in E. areolatus and R. kanagurta . No significant associations were detected between total MP abundance and habitat group, sex, total length, body weight, or condition factor. Fibers were the dominant particle type, most particles measured < 2 mm, and polyester was the predominant identified polymer, followed by polypropylene and ethylene-propylene diene polymer (EPDM). The predominance of fibers and polyester indicates that fibrous synthetic materials constitute an important component of MP exposure in these commercially important fishes. However, specific environmental sources cannot be determined from polymer identity alone, highlighting the need for integrated assessment of fish alongside seawater, sediments, and other potential environmental sources.

Article.Title: Habituation and housing interact to shape the magnitude and consistency of post-operative recovery after kidney imaging window implantation in mice
Article.Authors: Askar R.; Weidner P.; Peuckert C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Abdominal imaging windows enable longitudinal intravital microscopy but require surgical implantation, which induces physiological stress and may influence experimental outcomes. Although pre-operative habituation is widely used as a refinement strategy, its effects on post-operative physiological responses remain incompletely understood. Here, male and female BALB/c mice underwent kidney abdominal imaging window implantation following either a two-week handling habituation protocol or standard husbandry and were housed either in groups or individually after surgery. Post-operative recovery was assessed using clinical health scores, body weight, peripheral leukocyte counts, urinary corticosterone, and renal immunohistochemistry. Habituation altered both the magnitude and the consistency of post-operative physiological responses. Mean effects were primarily observed in males, including greater transient post-operative weight loss, delayed body weight recovery, and reduced urinary corticosterone concentrations. Across immune and endocrine endpoints, however, the predominant effect was a change in inter-individual variability. Under group-housed conditions, habituated mice showed reduced variation in leukocyte counts, urinary corticosterone concentrations, and renal CD68-positive cell infiltration, whereas these effects were absent or reversed in individually housed animals. Females were affected predominantly through changes in inter-individual variability. These findings demonstrate that pre-operative habituation reshapes the physiological response to surgery in a manner that depends on both post-operative housing and sex. More broadly, they identify inter-individual variability as a biologically meaningful outcome of peri-operative refinement, suggesting that refinement strategies should be evaluated not only by their effects on average physiological responses but also by their ability to promote more consistent responses across individual animals.

Article.Title: ZAPP: a zero-aware photovoltaic power prediction framework
Article.Authors: Gürhanlı A.; Esen V.
Article.Abstract: Predicting photovoltaic power generator outputs is not easy, especially when the values are near zero, because even very small errors can lead to large percentage errors. We introduce a new forecasting framework, ZAPP (Zero-Aware Photovoltaic Power Predictor), that handles near-zero errors while maintaining high prediction accuracy. The model does not rely on a single unified regression model but instead attaches two refinement stages to a base regression model. The first stage, called ZeroGate, predicts whether the output should be zero. The second refinement stage, the low-power MAPE reducer, fine-tunes the non-zero outputs near the zero level without significantly affecting scale-dependent regression metrics. The datasets are divided into training, validation, and test sets in chronological order, ensuring that test data is not used during model development, threshold tuning, ensemble weighting, or calibration. Experimental evaluation included base models such as Persistence, Ridge, XGBoost, LSTM, Transformer, and a hybrid Ridge–XGBoost model. Two separate datasets are employed to strengthen the quality of the results. For the hybrid model, sMAPE fell from 60.57% to 11.07% on Dataset 1. Its final MAE, RMSE, and R 2 were 22.37, 60.72, and 0.9637, respectively. On Dataset 2, sMAPE decreased from 63.30% to 11.92%, with MAE = 52.24, RMSE = 144.60, and R 2 = 0.9559. The zero-aware correction mainly reduced percentage errors without weakening the overall regression results.

Article.Title: Antimicrobial activity and ADMET analysis of novel coumarin-based pyridine and pyran hybrids
Article.Authors: Ahmed G.; Hessein S.; El haleem A.; Shmiess N.; Fouad S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A series of novel pyridine and pyran incorporated chromene moiety have been synthesized using 6-(2-(4-nitrophenyl) diazenyl)-3-acetyl-2 H-chromen-2-one 1 as the starting material. The chemical structures of the newly synthesized derivatives were characterized using different spectroscopic techniques (FT-IR, 1 HNMR and 13 CNMR) and elemental analysis. All derivatives were assessed for their in vitro antimicrobial activity against six clinically isolated multi-drug resistance strains, including Gram-positive ( Bacillus pumilis , Streptococcus faecalis ) and Gram-negative ( Escherichia coli , Enterobacter cloacae ) bacteria and fungi ( Saccharomyces cerevisiae , Candida albicans ) using broth microdilution and agar well-diffusion technique assays. The synthesized compounds exhibited moderate to good antimicrobial activity against the tested strains, with several derivatives approaching, and in one instance matching, the potency of the reference drugs. Notably, 2a , 5a , 5b , 6b , 7b , and 8a derivatives merged as the most promising bactericidal and fungicidal agents Compound 5a demonstrated an excellent activity toward S. faecalis which is equal to Penicillin G. with MIC value (3.91 µg/ml) and MBC value (31.3 µg/ml). Furthermore, compounds 5b , 6b , 7b and 8a revealed an excellent potency against S. faecalis with MIC value (7.81 µg/ml) and bactericidal activity with MBC value from 15.6 to 62.5 µg/ml Furthermore, in-silico ADMET analysis of compounds 6a , 6b , 8a , and 8b demonstrated adherence to Pfizer’s guidelines, reflecting favorable physicochemical properties.

Article.Title: Mitigation of bacterial spot disease of pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) using diseased plant-recruited microorganisms to modulate the rhizosphere microbiota
Article.Authors: Song H.; Yang S.; Cho Y.; Choi M.; Yang H.; Seo M.; Lee J.
Article.Abstract: Plants and their rhizosphere microbial communities actively interact with each other to create optimal growth and defense conditions. It is known that when a plant becomes diseased, the plant secretes various metabolites or signaling substances that can attract protective beneficial or helpful microorganisms from the surrounding soil as a response. This is the basis of the 'cry for help' hypothesis, which proposes that stressed roots emit distress signals that recruit beneficial microbes able to mitigate the stress. Here we hypothesized that the bacterial diseased pepper plants might harbour some rhizosphere microorganisms which could be distinctively different from the healthy pepper plants. In this study, we investigated the structural shifts in the pepper ( Capsicum annuum L.) rhizosphere microbiota following infection by the spot disease pathogen Xanthomonas euvesicatoria . Through microbial community analyses, we identified specific bacterial taxa such as Rhodanobacter and Arachidicoccus that appeared to influence or contribute to community differentiation. To validate the protective roles of these recruited microbes, we applied the selected strains as targeted inoculants together with known plant growth-promoting bacteria (PGPB). Microbial treatments, particularly the single-strain Rhodanobacter treatment (T2) and a four-strain consortium (T4), significantly reduced the proportion of diseased leaves by 72%. Furthermore, microbiome analysis of the treated rhizosphere showed a partial recovery of Mucilaginibacter , an indicator of plant health that had been depleted under disease conditions. This study suggests that the pepper plant actively recruits beneficial rhizosphere microbes in response to X. euvesicatoria infection to support its immunity. Utilizing the plant-recruited microorganisms provides a sustainable and targeted biocontrol approach that both inhibits pathogen proliferation and reestablishes ecological balance in the rhizosphere. This microbiome-informed approach presents an environment-friendly alternative to conventional chemical pesticides in managing pepper bacterial spot disease.

Article.Title: An interpretable hierarchical deep learning framework for lung and colon cancer detection
Article.Authors: Talukder M.; Rafeh R.; Chu N.; Uddin M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate and interpretable classification of lung and colon cancer from histopathological images remains challenging because of substantial inter-class similarities, morphological heterogeneity, and the limited transparency of conventional deep learning (DL) models. Most existing methods treat the problem as a flat multiclass classification task, requiring a single model to distinguish normal tissue and multiple cancer subtypes simultaneously. In this study, we propose an interpretable hierarchical DL framework that decomposes the five-class classification problem into clinically motivated coarse-to-fine decision stages. The framework initially separates normal tissue from cancerous tissue and then directs each sample to a specialized classifier for either normal tissue categorization or cancer subtype identification. Candidate DL architectures are independently evaluated at each stage, allowing the most suitable model to be selected for each specific classification task. The framework is evaluated on the LC25000 benchmark and further assessed on the independent LungHist700 dataset, which presents a distinct evaluation setting with different image characteristics and class distributions. The proposed approach achieves an accuracy of 98.50% on LC25000 and 82.01% on LungHist700. To improve model transparency, Grad-CAM, Grad-CAM++, LIME, and Occlusion Sensitivity are employed to highlight the image regions that contribute to the hierarchical predictions. The results show that the framework combines strong classification performance with a structured coarse-to-fine decision process and complementary interpretability techniques. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of hierarchical decision decomposition and explainable DL to provide a more transparent and task-specific approach to computer-aided histopathological cancer classification, particularly for distinguishing normal tissue from lung and colon cancer subtypes.

Article.Title: Use of microstream capnography in sedation practices for pediatric patients undergoing magnetic resonance imaging
Article.Authors: A. Akgün A.; Yılmaz C.; Sayan H.; Karasu D.; Balkaya A.; Güvenç G.; Uçar M.; Çevikkalp E.
Article.Abstract: In pediatric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), there is a need for more advanced monitoring methods in addition to routine pulse oximetry to ensure safer nonoperating room anesthesia (NORA). The integrated pulmonary index (IPI) available in the Microstream capnography device provides an early indicator of a patient’s respiratory functions. In this study, we aimed to investigate the feasibility of using the IPI as an early indicator for detecting cardiorespiratory events. A prospective, observational study was conducted on pediatric patients aged 1 month to 18 years who were to undergo sedation for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The respiratory rate (RR), end tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO 2 ), oxygen saturation (SpO 2 ), heart rate (HR), complications, and EtCO 2 changes (∆EtCO 2 ) were recorded. IPI values at induction and at the end of the scan were evaluated. The primary outcome was the diagnostic performance of the post-induction IPI value in predicting cardiorespiratory events; secondary outcomes included the incidence of cardiorespiratory events and of hypopneic hypoventilation, and the diagnostic performance of EtCO 2 for these outcomes. A total of 159 patients were included in the study. ROC analysis revealed the diagnostic significance of EtCO 2 induction in predicting hypoxia and apnea. While 31.44% of all patients had ∆EtCO 2 , only 6.3% of these patients had SpO 2 ≤ 93% (hypoxia) at the same time. The induction EtCO 2 median in patients who developed hypoxia was 26 mmHg (IQR: 14–29), compared to 33 mmHg (IQR: 28–36) in those without hypoxia ( p = 0.001). EtCO 2 The optimal threshold value was found to be 29 mmHg in patients who developed hypoxia, whereas it was 18 mmHg in those who developed apnea. A total of 27.7% of all patients had hypopneic hypoventilation, and hypoxia was detected in %15.9 of these patients. IPI, EtCO 2 , and ∆EtCO 2 have a statistically significant effect on ‘induction cardiorespiratory events’. Patients with cardiorespiratory events had an IPI ≤ 6 and EtCO 2 ≤ 33. Each one-unit increase in IPI was calculated to reduce the probability of a cardiorespiratory event by approximately 46.3%. Severe respiratory complications are frequently observed in young pediatric patients undergoing NORA. Early diagnosis of respiratory complications, particularly hypopneic hypoventilation, is possible through EtCO 2 monitoring. Low EtCO 2 and IPI are considered potential risk factors for the development of cardiorespiratory events. The routine use of capnography, a method that allows continuous and noninvasive monitoring of respiration, enhances patient safety in procedural sedation outside the operating room. Intervention in pediatric patients with an IPI value < 6 who develop cardiovascular events is considered necessary. Because EtCO 2 is sampled outside the airway, continuous auscultation of breath sounds is recommended as a complementary monitor in this setting. Registry : ClinicalTrials.gov, TRN: NCT04622436, Registration date: 03 November 2020.

Article.Title: Molecule-aware machine learning for predicting absorption and emission of benzothiadiazole derivatives
Article.Authors: Truong D.; Hong P.; Pham P.; Trinh T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Predicting the absorption and emission wavelengths of 2,1,3-benzothiadiazole (BTD) derivatives across diverse solvents from molecular structure alone remains challenging, and conventional random-split validation can obscure whether models truly extrapolate to new chemical structures or merely interpolate solvent effects for known ones. By enforcing a molecule-aware train–test split, in which all solvent measurements of any given chemical structure are held out together, we show that champion-model $$R^2$$ falls by approximately 27–29 percentage points relative to random splitting, revealing that high random-split accuracy primarily reflects reliable prediction of solvent-induced spectral shifts rather than generalisation to unseen BTD structures. Within this framework, replacing binary with count-based Morgan fingerprints raises single-split $$R^2$$ from 0.747 to 0.941 for absorption and from 0.797 to 0.916 for emission, an improvement rooted in the ability of count fingerprints to encode the recurrence frequency of donor substructures, a key determinant of intramolecular charge-transfer character. A systematically optimised deep neural network reaches $$R^2 = 0.954$$ for absorption on its best of twenty random initialisations (mean $$0.83 \pm 0.12$$ ), the highest value reported for this dataset, yet the molecule-aware benchmark confirms that this performance does not translate to structure-level extrapolation. Comparative evaluation of graph neural networks, multi-task learning, extended descriptor sets, and ensemble methods confirms that none outperforms the count-fingerprint approach at this dataset size. Feature-importance analysis identifies tertiary amine substitution as the dominant structural driver and solvent polarity as the strongest single feature for emission (ranked first or second in all four model/encoding combinations examined, versus 8th–13th for absorption), an asymmetry consistent with the stronger solvatochromism of relaxed charge-transfer states. These results offer practical guidance for computational screening: the models are well suited to solvent selection for known dyes, whereas the design of genuinely new structures demands expanded structural diversity in the training set.

Article.Title: A cell-based multivariate blood test (iCAP) for early detection of Alzheimer’s disease capturing non-amyloid-β biology
Article.Authors: Qi Y.; Miller L.; D’Ascenzo M.; Berndt J.; Whitney G.; Duffy F.; Danziger S.; Peskind E.; Li G.; Masters C.; Fowler C.; N/A N/A.; Milicic L.; Vacher M.; Bourgeat P.; Doré V.; Shishegar R.; Maruff P.; Rowe C.; Villemagne V.; Porter T.; Laws S.; Rainey-Smith S.; Bomke J.; Brown B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The indicator cell assay platform (iCAP) is a blood-based diagnostic approach that uses standardized cells as biosensors to transduce complex circulating signals into cell-based gene-expression profiles for multivariate disease classification. We developed an iCAP for early detection of Alzheimer’s disease (AD-iCAP) by incubating plasma from patients with early-stage AD (mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia) and non-affected controls with standardized neurons and training classifiers on transcriptomic responses. Modeling features were restricted to a predefined 84-gene panel derived independently by analyzing 5xFAD mouse plasma in the AD-iCAP. In this exploratory study, a model was trained and tested using 191 retrospectively collected human plasma samples across three cohorts. The classifier achieved AUC = 0.64 (95% CI 0.51–0.78) in an external validation set during model development (n = 82) and AUC = 0.77 (95% CI 0.57–0.96) in a blind test set (n = 23). The multivariate model incorporated 5 genes including AKT3 , GPR50 , PALLD , RGMA , and PCDH10 , implicated in AD, neuronal signaling and/or cytoskeletal dynamics. The cell-based approach is orthogonal to direct detection of circulating amyloid and tau, and these exploratory findings support further evaluation of AD-iCAP in prospective studies for combinatorial diagnostics and patient stratification for clinical trials.

Article.Title: Physics-constrained generative digital twin for early leakage detection in nitrogen accumulators in governor control systems at hydroelectric power plants
Article.Authors: Ustun T.; Sinha P.; Butuner M.; Koc E.; Gezer D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Nitrogen pre-charge loss in hydropower governor accumulators is a slow but critical degradation process that weakens hydraulic energy storage, reduces pressure-retention time, increases pump cycling, and accelerates thermal–mechanical stress. Conventional pressure-threshold SCADA alarms can miss the early stage because oil pressure may remain inside the operating band while waveform dynamics deteriorate. This paper proposes a SCADA-calibrated physics-constrained generative digital twin for early nitrogen leakage diagnosis. Limited anonymized field-SCADA observations are used only as calibration anchors for pressure set-points, pump-ON duration, pump-OFF retention, temperature range, and the fast-rise/slow-decay waveform; they are not presented as a complete labeled leakage dataset. The evaluation uses 80,000 physics-constrained synthetic training records and 20,000 independently generated synthetic test records per run, balanced across eight degradation months. Train and test records are produced with disjoint seeds and no shared cycles or residual draws. Across five independent generation-and-training runs, Random Forest gives the best pressure-prediction performance, with R 2 = 0.999731 ± 0.000004, MAE = 0.0856 ± 0.0007 bar, RMSE = 0.1074 ± 0.0007 bar, and 96.78 ± 0.18% of samples within 1% of the 23-bar operating span (0.23 bar). The corrected health index is bounded by 1.0, and cycle-level indicators identify the Month-4 warning transition before a conventional pressure-threshold response. The framework therefore supports earlier inspection and nitrogen-recharge planning, helping operators reduce avoidable pump cycling, maintenance escalation, and the risk of unplanned governor-system outages, while explicitly distinguishing SCADA calibration from synthetic diagnostic evaluation.

Article.Title: Optimization and mechanistic analysis of high-temperature aerobic composting process for dynamic sludge in rotary drums
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Zhang H.; Xiao Z.; Xv H.; Jia B.; Li Y.; Diao G.; Song H.; Wu C.
Article.Abstract: This study addresses challenges in high-temperature aerobic sludge composting using a rotary drum, particularly material adhesion to the drum wall and low efficiency. Response surface methodology (RSM) was used to develop predictive models for composting period time and seed germination index (GI). The models showed high reliability (R²≥ 0.95, p < 0.001) with validation errors of 6.67% for composting period and 1.04% for GI. The optimal conditions identified were 55% moisture content, 10 mm auxiliary material dimensions, 7 L·min⁻¹·kg⁻¹ TS aeration rate, and 1.5 r·min⁻¹ rotational speed. These conditions reduced the composting period to 15 days, increased GI to 86%, and met the GB/T 23,486 − 2009 standards for heavy metal concentrations. The bioavailability of heavy metals decreased significantly, ensuring environmental safety. Microbial community analysis revealed a two-stage succession pattern, with thermophilic Bacillus and Aspergillus dominating the high-temperature phase. The process efficiency was influenced by synergistic parameter interactions. Through comparative analysis of processes, it was found that rotating drum composting achieves an optimal balance among efficiency, environmental performance, and engineering feasibility, making it highly suitable for large-scale municipal sludge valorization.

Article.Title: When SHAP explains a leaked target: a cautionary study of an XGBoost and multi-level SHAP pipeline for S&P 500 direction prediction
Article.Authors: Yuan L.; Leng Y.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: Accurate prediction of stock price movements is of substantial importance to investors, portfolio managers, and financial regulators, and although machine learning models are increasingly deployed in quantitative finance, the limited transparency of many such models remains a non-trivial barrier to broader adoption in high-stakes decision-making environments, particularly where auditability and accountability are required. This study presents an end-to-end interpretable prediction pipeline that integrates multi-category technical indicator engineering, XGBoost gradient boosting classification, and comprehensive SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis for daily direction forecasting of the S&P 500 index, together with a rigorous diagnostic evaluation of that pipeline. A systematic feature engineering stage constructs 32 technical features organized into six categories—returns, trend indicators (moving average ratios, MACD, RSI, Bollinger Bands), multi-scale volatility, volume dynamics, momentum oscillators (ROC, ATR, Stochastic Oscillator, Williams %R, CCI), and lagged returns—which are fed into an XGBoost classifier trained on a sequential 80/20 train–test split to prevent look-ahead bias. On the hold-out set the classifier attains 63.84% accuracy and a macro-averaged F1-score of 0.6110. Contextualizing this figure, however, overturns its interpretation. The majority-class (“always-Down”) rule already attains 59.32% on the same split, and a data-provenance audit reveals that the widely used public source file contains every calendar day, with 31.1% of rows being exact forward-filled copies of the previous trading session. Because the target is defined by the strict inequality \(P^{\textrm{c}}_{t+1}>P^{\textrm{c}}_{t}\) , every session whose successor is a forward-filled copy—each Friday and each Saturday—is labelled “Down” by construction, rendering 31.0% of all labels independent of market behaviour. Consequently a one-bit rule that never observes a price (“predict Up iff the previous return is exactly zero”) reaches 63.84%, and a calendar-only rule reaches 71.19%, both matching or exceeding the classifier. Decomposing the model’s accuracy shows it scores 95.37% on rows whose label the calendar had already fixed but only 49.19% on the 246 rows carrying a genuine next-day move—below that subset’s own 58.54% majority rule. Once the forward-filled rows are removed, discriminative power collapses to chance (AUC 0.527 on a single split; 0.476 pooled across six walk-forward folds with per-fold hyper-parameter re-optimization), the model falls below the majority baseline, and a cost-aware backtest yields a Sharpe ratio of \(-0.24\) at 10 bps against \(+0.59\) for buy-and-hold. SHAP attributions are further shown to be unidentified within a volatility cluster whose pairwise correlations reach \(r=0.947\) : the members’ individual credits sum to 2.64 times the cluster’s joint contribution, and retraining on one representative per correlated group—discarding fourteen of the thirty-two features—does not degrade performance. The multi-level SHAP machinery faithfully explains this leakage rather than any market mechanism—most visibly, 108 of 354 test observations pile up at exactly zero lagged return and receive systematically positive attributions. The contribution of this work is therefore methodological rather than predictive: it provides a reproducible, auditable SHAP-on-XGBoost pipeline, and uses it to demonstrate how a routinely used public dataset combined with a strict-inequality target manufactures label leakage that post-hoc explanation methods will rationalize with apparent precision. We distil the analysis into a validation checklist for interpretable machine learning on financial tabular data.

Article.Title: Evaluating the performance of the surface water and ocean topography (SWOT) mission for monitoring reservoirs across the conterminous United States
Article.Authors: Huber J.; Abbaszadeh P.; Chang H.
Article.Abstract: Remote sensing provides critical insights into reservoir operations at sites with minimal in-situ data. The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission improves upon previous satellite altimetry missions with two-dimensional water surface representations, enhanced discharge estimates, and simultaneous water surface elevation (WSE) and surface area/width data. We found median agreement (Spearman rho) greater than 0.9 between SWOT and 773 United States Geological Survey (USGS; ρ = 0.96) and US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE; ρ = 0.94) WSE time series at Conterminous US reservoirs. At USGS sites, 68% of observations had relative errors compared to in-situ observations (after adjusting for bias using time series average WSE) with an absolute value under 10 cm, versus 22 cm at USACE sites. However, low agreement clusters appeared in the Pacific Northwest and Southeastern US. For SWOT-derived downstream discharge, agreement (ρ) with in-situ data was lower (USACE: 0.57, USGS: 0.39) with a low performance cluster in the Pacific Northwest and a high performance cluster in the central US. At USGS sites, 68% of observations had relative errors with an absolute value under 108 cubic meters per second (m 3 /s), compared to 133 m 3 /s at USACE sites. This research supports the ability of SWOT to accurately represent reservoir water levels at ungauged sites while recognizing potential for improvement on downstream discharge estimates.

Article.Title: Lifestyle factors associated with biofunctional age in a cross-sectional study of adults aged 35 and older
Article.Authors: Theis S.; Heller V.; Bitterlich N.; von Wolff M.; Frühwein H.; Stute P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ageing is a complex process influenced by chronological age, gender, genetics, lifestyle and environment leading to intra- and inter-individual variability in vitality and the trajectory of healthy ageing. This study aimed to identify key lifestyle factors and to develop a Lifestyle Index (LI) for low-threshold, practical assessment of Biological Functional Status (BFS) in routine health evaluations. A monocentric, cross-sectional, observational study including 630 participants; BFS and LI were derived for a subgroup of 312 participants aged ≥ 35 years, consistent with the age threshold required by the validated BFA model. Data collection comprised demographic, lifestyle and functional health parameters. Statistical analysis identified modifiable lifestyle factors most strongly linked to BFS and BFA forming the basis of the LI. Five lifestyle factors form the basis of the primary Lifestyle Index (LI): high physical activity (≥ 3 x /week), r = − 0.212), satisfaction with sexual life (r = − 0.156), normal Body Mass Index (18.5–22 kg/m 2 , r = − 0.120), very good sleep (r = − 0.099) and never /past smoking (r = 0.128). The constructed LI (0- 10 points) correlated with lower BFA (r = − 0.233; p < 0.001), indicating a healthier lifestyle profile. Mean LI score was 5.7 points (SD = 1.7; median = 5.5). Alcohol consumption also appears to exert an influence; however, this aspect warrants separate discussion. Accordingly, alcohol consumption was examined in a separate sensitivity analysis (see results “Sensitivity analysis: alcohol consumption” section). Active ageing should not be conceptualized as alignment with a normative biological age, but rather as the optimization of functional capacity within the context of individual variability and life circumstances. We developed a simple, cost-effective and user-friendly LI, intended as a preliminary, low-threshold tool for the assessment of BFS. Before it can support routine clinical use and personalized strategies for healthy aging, external validation and confirmation in more diverse populations is needed.

Article.Title: Surgical waste from stereotactic glioma biopsies contains clinically relevant tumor DNA
Article.Authors: Wadden J.; Adam T.; Lau B.; Cartaxo R.; Wink K.; Niculcea M.; Kong S.; John V.; Aittaleb R.; Pearson A.; Becker N.; Tripathy A.; Mortazavi A.; Serhan H.; Merrill N.; Merajver S.; Franson A.; Upadhyaya S.; Ranjan P.; Dickson R.; Heth J.; Muraszko K.; Garton H.; Marupudi N.; Ferris S.
Article.Abstract: Stereotactic needle biopsy is an established approach for sampling gliomas in deep, midline, or eloquent brain regions, but tissue acquisition remains constrained by the need to preserve material for histopathology, molecular testing, and research. During routine specimen handling, needle rinse fluid, expelled aspiration material, and gauze-associated debris are discarded as waste. This waste could contain diagnostically relevant tumor material. To evaluate this hypothesis, we collected 32 waste samples from 31 stereotactic needle biopsy procedures and evaluated whether they contained recoverable tumor-derived DNA. Among 28 samples with a clinically identified, testable tumor-associated alteration available for comparison, one failed targeted amplification after low DNA recovery. Review guided by clinical findings detected at least one corresponding alteration in all successfully sequenced samples (27/27), yielding an overall detection rate of 96% (27/28). In paired clinical and waste TSO500 analyses, waste sequencing identified all eligible reported variants in 12 of 15 samples. Waste sequencing also identified relevant mutations that matched marker-positive IHC findings, providing sequence-level context for IDH1 , ATRX , and TP53 alterations. These findings show that material routinely discarded during stereotactic needle biopsy can be a recoverable source of tumor-derived DNA for research, retrospective molecular analysis, and ancillary profiling when tissue is limited or unavailable.

Article.Title: QUBO sampling for mixed binary quadratic programming without continuous variable binarization
Article.Authors: Takabayashi T.; Ohzeki M.
Article.Abstract: Quantum annealing and related combinatorial optimization methods typically accept quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) problems as input, whereas many practical models include constraints and continuous variables. Standard QUBO conversions discretize continuous variables, increasing the binary dimension and often making feasible low-energy states harder to sample. We develop a Lagrange-multiplier method for a separable class of mixed-binary quadratic programs (MBQPs) without discretizing continuous variables. The method is based on a finite-temperature free-energy formulation and uses QUBO sampling for the binary sector. At fixed Lagrange multipliers, the continuous sector is integrated out analytically and enters only the multiplier update, leaving a QUBO over the original binary variables. We evaluate the method on the continuous relaxation of the quadratic p -median problem. Compared with a penalty-based QUBO formulation, it generates feasible solutions more reliably. At an appropriate inverse temperature, its conditional relative error is comparable to that of local search for small instances and often lower for the larger tested instances. In the time-to-target comparisons, the proposed method maintains high target-reached rates for stringent fixed-accuracy targets. For the larger instances within the tested range, it also reaches the prescribed targets faster than a commercial mixed-integer optimization solver.

Article.Title: Multimodal AI refines EAU risk stratification in patients undergoing radiotherapy for prostate cancer
Article.Authors: Camilloni A.; Micoli C.; Falagario U.; Mulliqi N.; Palm E.; Palsdottir T.; Szolnoky K.; Ji X.; Boman S.; Discacciati A.; Egevad L.; Grönberg H.; Kartasalo K.; Nordström T.; Eklund M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The European Association of Urology (EAU) risk groups guide treatment decisions in prostate cancer using prostate-specific antigen (PSA), ISUP grade, and clinical stage, but do not incorporate histopathological image information. We evaluated a locked multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) model that integrates routinely available clinical variables (age, PSA, and ISUP grade) with deep-learning features extracted from diagnostic biopsy whole-slide images for predicting outcomes after radiotherapy (RT). The model was originally trained to predict biochemical recurrence (BCR) following radical prostatectomy and was applied without retraining to 353 patients from the population-based STHLM3 trial (ISRCTN84445406) treated with RT. Study endpoints included BCR (Phoenix definition), high-risk BCR (HR-BCR), and prostate cancer-specific mortality (PCSM). Model performance was assessed using Harrell’s C-index and cumulative incidence analyses and compared with EAU risk groups. The continuous AI score showed C-indices of 0.65 (95% CI 0.55–0.74) for BCR, 0.84 (0.72–0.95) for HR-BCR, and 0.81 (0.63–1.00) for PCSM, compared with 0.60, 0.82, and 0.80, respectively, for EAU risk groups. Although paired differences in C-index between AI and EAU were not statistically significant, adding the continuous AI score to EAU classification improved model fit for BCR, HR-BCR, and PCSM. Exploratory AI risk stratification classified 18.9% of EAU intermediate-risk patients as AI high-risk and 28.2% of EAU high-risk patients as AI low-risk. Within the EAU high-risk group, patients classified as AI low-risk ( n = 24) experienced no BCR events during 10 years of follow-up, compared with a 10-year cumulative incidence of 28.7% (95% CI 17.3–41.2%) among AI high-risk patients ( n = 61). These findings suggest that multimodal AI may refine EAU risk stratification by identifying distinct prognostic subgroups within established risk categories, although prospective validation is needed before its potential role in individualized treatment decision-making can be established.

Article.Title: Integrated assessment of carbon stability and environmental performance of sewage sludge-derived biochar from a small wastewater treatment plant
Article.Authors: Gusiatin M.; Zaborowska M.; Bernat K.; Kulikowska D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Municipal sewage sludge (MSS) from small wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) is difficult to manage because decentralized facilities often lack economically viable treatment options. This study evaluated biochar produced by slow pyrolysis of MSS from a small WWTP (< 10,000 population equivalent) treating exclusively domestic wastewater. Pyrolysis at 400 and 600 °C progressively increased carbonization and structural stability, as indicated by a decrease in the H/C org ratio from 1.84 to 0.31, an increase in the thermostable fraction from 14% to 79%, and an increase in the recalcitrance index from 0.41 to 0.56. Carbon sequestration estimates were method-dependent: the R 50 -based carbon sequestration potential (CS R50 ) was higher for B400 (17.5%) than for B600 (15.3%), whereas the H/C org -based 100-year permanence approach predicted greater long-term carbon retention for B600 (0.12 vs. 0.10 kg C/kg dry MSS). These estimates should therefore be regarded as method-dependent predictions. Although total heavy metal concentrations increased during pyrolysis, their mobility decreased markedly, reducing the ecological risk index from 940 to 20. Among priority PAHs, only phenanthrene was detected in B600 at 0.011 mg/kg. Pyrolysis also strongly reduced the phytotoxicity of raw MSS. Overall, slow pyrolysis improved carbon stability and environmental performance. These findings indicate that pyrolysis can provide a locally applicable sludge valorization route for small decentralized WWTPs, combining waste reduction with carbon stabilization and reduced environmental risk.

Article.Title: CYB5R1 drives stemness and malignant progression via STAM2/STAT3 in chemotherapy-enriched triple-negative breast cancer
Article.Authors: Wang Z.; Li J.; Geng L.; Zhao Y.; Ma K.; Ma X.; Dong Y.; Lu Y.; Liu J.; Gasong Z.; Yuan M.; Yu Y.; Luo W.; Ruan X.
Article.Abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) frequently develops chemoresistance, but the mechanisms supporting tumor persistence remain incompletely understood. We integrated single-cell transcriptomic data with clinical cohort analyses to identify genes associated with chemotherapy exposure and prognosis. Malignant epithelial populations enriched after chemotherapy occupied terminal branches of the inferred pseudotime trajectory and exhibited higher stemness scores. CYB5R1 was enriched in these populations and associated with poor survival. Functional experiments showed that CYB5R1 promoted proliferation, migration, invasion, epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT), and stem cell-like properties in TNBC cells. CYB5R1 depletion suppressed these phenotypes and reduced STAM2 expression and STAT3 phosphorylation. STAM2 re-expression partially restored STAT3 phosphorylation and malignant phenotypes, supporting its role as a downstream mediator of CYB5R1. CYB5R1 depletion also increased cellular sensitivity to gemcitabine and selumetinib. Combined treatment produced greater antitumor effects than either agent alone in vitro and in vivo. These findings support a role for CYB5R1 in TNBC progression and EMT- and stemness-associated phenotypes, mediated partly through STAM2/STAT3 signaling. They also support further evaluation of gemcitabine plus selumetinib in TNBC and investigation of CYB5R1 as a candidate biomarker of prognosis and drug sensitivity.

Article.Title: Association of TyG-related indices with cardiometabolic multimorbidity across early cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome stages 0–3: a prospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Chen A.; Pan H.; Liu G.; Dong X.; Chen X.; Sun F.; Ahn S.; Ren L.; Miao M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic (CKM) syndrome is a systemic condition characterized by interrelated cardiac, renal, and metabolic disturbances. The triglyceride–glucose (TyG) index and several of its anthropometry-based derivatives have been increasingly recognized as surrogate markers of insulin resistance and potential predictors of cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM). However, whether their predictive performance differs across CKM stages 0–3 remains unclear. This prospective cohort investigation enrolled 646 participants without established CMM at baseline. CKM stages were classified according to AHA criteria based on obesity, metabolic abnormalities, kidney dysfunction, and subclinical cardiovascular disease. Five surrogate indicators of insulin resistance were examined, including the TyG index and four anthropometry-based TyG-derived indices. To evaluate model discrimination over time, Harrell’s time-dependent C-statistics were calculated. Improvements in predictive performance were further assessed by estimating the net reclassification index (NRI) and the integrated discrimination index (IDI). Restricted cubic spline functions were additionally fitted to depict potential dose–response relationships between each TyG-related measure and incident CMM. During a four-year follow-up, 21.36% of participants developed CMM. All TyG-related indices were significantly associated with increased CMM risk, displaying clear linear dose–response patterns. Among participants classified as CKM stage 3, TyG-WWI (TyG–weight-adjusted waist index) showed a robust association with CMM. Among all indicators, TyG-WWI and TyG-WHtR (TyG–waist-to-height ratio) showed relatively better discrimination, with meaningful improvements in NRI and IDI compared with the TyG index alone. Across CKM stages 0–3, the TyG index and its derivative markers showed consistent and independent associations with incident CMM. TyG-WWI and TyG-WHtR exhibited relatively better discrimination, highlighting their potential utility for early identification of high-risk individuals in community screening contexts, though their direct clinical applicability requires further validation.

Article.Title: Peptide-modified nanocellulose from dairy waste for organic compound removal in dairy wastewater
Article.Authors: Rastgar S.; Hanachi P.; Walker T.
Article.Abstract: Dairy effluent with a high organic loading demands efficient and sustainable treatment solutions. This work aimed to produce a peptide-modified crystalline nanocellulose (PCN C ) bio-adsorbent from dairy sludge and crustacean waste to remove organic compounds from industrial dairy wastewater. To optimize operational variables for maximum removal of chemical oxygen demand (COD), 5-day biochemical oxygen demand (BOD₅) and total organic carbon (TOC), response surface methodology (RSM) was applied based on a central composite design (CCD). Operational variables were pH (3–10), adsorbent dosage (100–500 mg L⁻1), contact time (15–55 min), peptide-to-cellulose mass ratio (0.5:1–3:1) and temperature (15–55 °C). The effective functionalization of the peptide and formation of a mesoporous structure with good thermal stability were validated by characterization using FESEM, XRD, FTIR, BET and TGA/DTG. Under the optimal conditions (pH 6.5, PCN C dose of 300 mg L⁻1, contact time of 35 min, peptide-to-cellulose mass ratio of 3:1 and temperature of 25 °C), the maximum removal efficiencies were 97.80%, 93.60% and 96.40% for COD, BOD₅ and TOC, respectively. The most significant factors were pH and PCN C dose according to analysis of variance (ANOVA) ( p < 0.0001). The quadratic models showed high predictive ability (R2 = 0.9519) and were experimentally validated with a relative error of < 0.50%. Furthermore, PCN C showed good reusability, with removal efficiencies of nearly 95% for COD, 92% for BOD₅ and 89% for TOC after five successive adsorption–desorption cycles. Generally, our results highlight the potential of PCN C as a bio-based adsorbent for dairy wastewater treatment while promoting waste valorization and circular economy concepts.

Article.Title: Evaluating the accuracy and efficiency of Cloud-to-IDA for drift-based collapse assessment of steel frames under near- and far-field motions
Article.Authors: Shemshaki E.; Asgarian B.; Monirvaghefi Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate estimation of seismic collapse capacity is essential for performance-based earthquake engineering and fragility assessment. Incremental Dynamic Analysis (IDA) is widely regarded as a reliable benchmark for collapse capacity evaluation; however, its high computational cost limits its application in large-scale or rapid assessment studies. This study evaluates the accuracy and computational efficiency of conventional Cloud Analysis and the Cloud-to-IDA procedure compared with IDA for steel moment-resisting frames subjected to near-field and far-field ground motions and investigates the influence of structural height and ground-motion characteristics on the accuracy of each assessment method. Three two-dimensional steel moment-resisting frames with 3, 5, and 9 stories were modeled in OpenSees and analyzed using 22 far-field and 28 near-field ground motion records from the FEMA P695 suite. Spectral acceleration at the fundamental period, Sa(T1), was adopted as the intensity measure, and maximum inter-story drift ratio was used as the engineering demand parameter. A drift-based collapse limit state was defined using HAZUS inter-story drift thresholds to provide a consistent comparison basis among the three methods. The results show that conventional Cloud Analysis can produce height- and record-dependent bias, with the bias diminishing as frame height increases from 3 to 9 stories, in estimating median collapse capacity. The largest discrepancy was observed for the 3-story frame under far-field records, where Cloud Analysis overestimated the IDA-based median collapse capacity by approximately 20%. In contrast, Cloud-to-IDA closely reproduced the IDA results across all studied frame heights and ground-motion categories, with median collapse capacity errors limited to only a few percent. Dispersion estimates from Cloud-to-IDA were also more consistent with IDA than those obtained from conventional Cloud Analysis. In terms of computational demand, Cloud-to-IDA substantially reduced the number of nonlinear dynamic analyzes and achieved approximately 86–91% reduction in computational time relative to IDA, while maintaining close agreement in both median capacity and dispersion. These findings indicate that Cloud-to-IDA can provide an efficient and reliable alternative for drift-based collapse fragility assessment of steel moment-resisting frames, provided that its applicability is carefully limited to the structural systems, ground-motion sets, and collapse criteria considered in the study.

Article.Title: Hydration-induced strengthening and progressive failure of grouted sandstone under water immersion
Article.Authors: Yu M.; Zhang C.; Ma D.; Zuo Y.; Wang L.; Li D.; Yu X.
Article.Abstract: Water immersion commonly causes mechanical weakening and deterioration of intact sandstone, whereas the continued hydration of cementitious grout may induce a contrasting strengthening response in grouted sandstone. To quantify this distinct water–grout interaction, cyan sandstone specimens with a central grouting structure were prepared and subjected to uniaxial compression tests coupled with digital image correlation (DIC) observations after immersion for 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20 days. The results show that, within the investigated 0–20 d immersion period, grouted sandstone exhibited hydration-induced strengthening rather than the conventional water-induced weakening observed in intact sandstone. The peak strength and elastic modulus increased progressively with immersion time, from 86.79 MPa to 117.52 MPa and from 10.95 GPa to 12.43 GPa, respectively. This strengthening trend is consistent with a contribution from continued hydration of the cementitious grout during immersion. Energy evolution analysis reveals that the turning point of dissipated energy effectively marks the transition from compaction to stable crack propagation. DIC observations demonstrate a systematic transition in failure mode from axial tensile splitting to tensile–shear composite failure and ultimately to X-shaped conjugate shear failure with increasing immersion duration. Based on these findings, a hydration-strengthened Drucker–Prager constitutive model is established by introducing hydration and elastic modulus strengthening coefficients, which successfully captures the time-dependent evolution of yield strength and elastic stiffness. The proposed model provides a quantitative framework for describing the early-stage mechanical evolution of grouted sandstone subjected to water immersion within the investigated 0–20 d period.

Article.Title: Artificial intelligence-based prediction of hepatocellular carcinoma in individuals without HBV or HCV infection in the MASLD era
Article.Authors: Choi H.; Kim L.; Yoo J.; Kim S.; Kim Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Current surveillance guidelines for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) primarily target individuals with liver cirrhosis or viral hepatitis. We developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-based model to predict HCC risk in individuals without viral hepatitis. Using the South Korean National Health Insurance Service database, we analyzed 7,961,075 individuals aged 20–79 years who underwent health screening in 2017 and were followed through 2023. Twelve AI models were compared. The best-performing model was retrained and evaluated in an unmatched validation cohort reflecting the original HCC prevalence and an independent non-selected validation cohort. Multi-Head Attention with Deep Neural Network (MHA_DNN) achieved the highest performance (AUC 0.9385, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.9312–0.9455 In the unmatched validation cohort, the model demonstrated excellent discrimination (AUROC 0.9450; AUPRC 0.0503), improved calibration after logistic recalibration, and superior clinical utility. Performance remained consistent in the independent non-selected validation cohort (AUROC 0.8848; AUPRC 0.0293). SHAP analysis identified fatty liver index (FLI) and triglycerides (TG) as the most influential predictors. TG increased HCC risk in individuals with FLI < 60 but showed the opposite association in those with FLI ≥ 60. MHA_DNN provides robust population-level prediction of HCC in individuals without viral hepatitis and supports personalized surveillance based on metabolic risk factors.

Article.Title: Radionuclide identification for plastic scintillation detectors by backward cumulative channel sum
Article.Authors: So J.; Jeon B.; Moon M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Large-area plastic scintillation detectors are widely used in radiation portal monitors, but their Compton-dominated spectra provide limited radionuclide-specific information. We evaluated backward cumulative channel sum (BCCS) combined with non-negative least-squares (NNLS) decomposition and compared it with raw-spectrum NNLS using an explicit background template and detector-specific five-window NNLS. A measured background and fixed reference spectra for Am-241, Cs-137, and Co-60 were used to analyze 18 independent spectra: nine single-radionuclide measurements, eight binary mixtures, and one ternary mixture. The mixed-source compositions were concealed during the primary BCCS analysis. All three methods ranked the actual radionuclide first for every single-radionuclide spectrum and the two constituents first and second for every binary mixture; the ternary mixture yielded positive coefficients for all three radionuclides. For the nine mixed-source spectra, method-specific relative residuals were 0.48–1.31% for BCCS-NNLS, 0.88–1.60% for raw-spectrum NNLS, and 0.11–0.50% for five-window NNLS; these values were calculated in different representation spaces and should not be compared as equivalent goodness-of-fit measures. Parametric Poisson resampling supported stable coefficient rankings under counting-statistical variation. These results support BCCS-NNLS as a simple, linear, and interpretable approach for static, unshielded measurements within a fixed radionuclide library, without hardware modification or data-intensive training. The study does not address open-set identification, activity quantification, or formal detection limits.

Article.Title: Multiscale surface-texture characterisation of heritage paintings using reflectance transformation imaging and completed local binary patterns
Article.Authors: Zhou Y.; Gao B.; Zeng W.
Article.Abstract: Reflectance transformation imaging provides a non-contact means of recording the illumination-dependent appearance of cultural heritage objects and can assist in the visual examination of brushwork, cracks, surface irregularities, and material-texture variations. However, the large number of directional-light images produced during RTI acquisition creates challenges for extracting stable and interpretable surface-texture information. This study presents a multiscale computational framework for characterising the visible surface features of heritage paintings using physically acquired RTI image sequences. The proposed framework first normalises the directional-light observations and generates relightable representations under controlled illumination directions. Discrete wavelet transform (DWT) is subsequently employed to decompose the RTI observations into multiscale frequency components representing coarse surface structures and fine textural variations. Completed local binary patterns (CLBP) are then extracted from the wavelet sub-bands to describe local intensity differences, neighbourhood relationships, and directional texture characteristics. The resulting descriptors are combined to produce surface-detail maps and quantitative texture representations for different regions of the paintings. The framework is evaluated using real multi-light RTI datasets and compared with conventional local binary patterns, wavelet-only descriptors, gradient-based methods, and standard texture-analysis approaches. Evaluation considers descriptor repeatability across lighting directions, texture separability, edge preservation, local contrast, computational cost, and robustness to illumination variation. The framework is intended for computational surface visualisation and texture characterisation. The study provides a reproducible and physically grounded approach for analysing visible painting-surface characteristics from real RTI measurements and establishes a basis for subsequent evaluation with conservator-annotated heritage datasets.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: Reflectance Transformation Imaging; local binary pattern; surface texture
Article.TopicFields: Arts and Humanities > Archeology > Cultural Heritage Materials Analysis; Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition > Image Retrieval and Classification Techniques; Engineering > Computational Mechanics > Surface Roughness and Optical Measurements

Article.Title: Intraoperative intravenous lidocaine for analgesia after oral cancer surgery with free perforator flap reconstruction: a randomised controlled trial
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Li Y.; Yue X.; Feng Z.; Song Z.; Zou W.
Article.Abstract: Intravenous lidocaine is effective in various surgical procedures, but its efficacy in oral cancer surgery is uncertain. We hypothesised that intraoperative intravenous lidocaine infusion can reduce 24-hour postoperative opioid consumption and reduce postoperative pain in patients undergoing oral cancer surgery with free perforator flap reconstruction. In this blinded, randomised, placebo-controlled trial, a total of 64 patients scheduled for elective oral cancer surgery with free perforator flap reconstruction were enrolled and randomly assigned to either the lidocaine group receiving intravenous lidocaine, or the control group receiving normal 0.9% saline. The primary outcome was the cumulative consumption of opioids at the first 24 h postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included the cumulative consumption of opioid drugs intraoperatively within 48 h and 72 h postoperatively, NRS scores at 24, 48, and 72 h postoperatively, lidocaine-related adverse events, incidence of chronic pain and neuropathic pain at 3 months postoperatively. From August 2024 to December 2024, a total of 102 patients were screened for eligibility, 64 patients were included. Baseline characteristics and surgery-related data were similar between the two groups. Median (IQR) 24-h morphine equivalent consumption was 43.38 (37.60, 47.45) mg in the lidocaine group vs. 35.15 (29.13, 47.60) mg in the control group (median difference, 5.31 mg; 95% CI, -3.45 to 11.95 mg; P = 0.295). There were no significant differences in pain scores at 24, 48, and 72 h, or in the incidence of chronic pain or neuropathic pain at 3 months follow-up ( P > 0.05). Among patients undergoing elective oral cancer surgery with free perforator flap reconstruction, intraoperative intravenous lidocaine infusion did not demonstrate a benefit in reducing 24 h postoperative opioid consumption (median difference, 5.31 mg; 95% CI, -3.45 to 11.95 mg; P = 0.295), acute pain (median difference, 0.00; 95% CI, -1.00 to 0.00; P = 0.762), or chronic pain at 3 months postoperatively (relative risk, 1.13; 95% CI, 0.50 to 2.55; P = 0.777). Trial registration : This trial was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400088614) on August 22, 2024 ( https://www.chictr.org.cn/ ).

Article.Title: Genomic landscape of antimicrobial resistance genes in Bacillus anthracis
Article.Authors: Medina Cordoba L.; Chivukula V.; Overholt W.; Bugrysheva J.; Maxson T.; Michel P.; Kongphet-Tran T.; Cherney B.; McLaughlin H.; Rishishwar L.; Conley A.; Villarma A.; Marston C.; Gee J.; Gulvik C.; Beesley C.; Hoffmaster A.; Weiner Z.; Sue D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Detection of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is critical for an effective public health response to anthrax, but a complete catalog of AMR markers in Bacillus anthracis is lacking. Here we characterized the landscape of AMR-associated B. anthracis genes using complete CDC and public genomes (NCBI RefSeq, SRA). We identified 33 candidate AMR genes from literature analysis and AMR gene databases, and surveyed them for variants. All predicted AMR genes were chromosomal; twenty were relevant to antibiotics recommended for anthrax treatment, while 13 were associated with other antibiotics. Across candidates, conventional broth microdilution susceptibility testing only confirmed penicillin resistance (linked to sigP , rsiP variants). As expected, few markers predicted functional resistance since AMR in B. anthracis is exceedingly rare. Variant frequencies were generally low, but slightly higher in genes presumptively linked to tetracycline-, penicillin-, and macrolide-resistance. Variation across all 33 regions is reported and intended to establish non-AMR conferring natural variation across the sample sets. The results from this study were integrated in a previously published bioinformatics pipeline, PiMA, expanding the set of genes analyzed as well as providing context for natural variation unlikely to confer AMR phenotypes. While B. anthracis is largely clonal with limited genetic variation, the AMR gene catalog linked to functional susceptibility results offers a valuable, evidence-based resource that strengthens resistance prediction and anthrax readiness.

Article.Title: Spermidine combined with resistance exercise ameliorates myocardial injury and mitochondrial dysfunction via AMPK-SIRT1-PGC-1α in D-galactose-induced aging rats
Article.Authors: Yang K.; Sun L.; Cheng Y.; Liang K.; Huang N.; Liu Y.; Zhang Y.; Liu C.; Peng L.
Article.Abstract: Age-related decline in myocardial structure and function is closely linked to dysregulated mitophagy, impaired mitochondrial biogenesis, and elevated apoptosis. Spermidine (SPD), a naturally occurring polyamine, and resistance exercise (RE) are both known to induce autophagy and exert cardioprotective anti-aging effects. In the present study, we investigated whether combined SPD and RE intervention ameliorates myocardial injury and mitochondrial dysfunction in D-galactose-induced aging rats, and explored the underlying mechanisms. With the exception of a control group, all rats received 6 weeks of daily intraperitoneal D-galactose injections to induce aging. Successful model establishment was verified by quantifying expression of the senescence-associated genes p53, p21, and p16, and by conducting hematoxylin–eosin (H&E) and Masson’s trichrome staining. Following model validation, rats in the aging cohort were assigned to three intervention groups treated for 8 weeks: RE alone, RE + vehicle (VRE), and SPD + RE. Myocardial tissues were assessed using H&E staining, Masson’s trichrome staining, and transmission electron microscopy. Myocardial levels of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), citrate synthase (CS), cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COX I), and mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) were quantified. Markers of mitochondrial biogenesis, mitophagy, and apoptosis were also quantified. Molecules of the AMPK-SIRT1-PGC-1α pathway were measured using reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. Combined SPD + RE intervention significantly ameliorated pathological myocardial structural alterations, mitochondrial morphological abnormalities, and functional impairment. It elevated myocardial ATP, CS, COX I, and MMP levels, and activated the AMPK-SIRT1-PGC-1α pathway. Specifically, it upregulated p-AMPK, SIRT1, PGC-1α, NRF1, and TFAM to promote mitochondrial biogenesis. Enhanced mitophagy was confirmed by an increased LC3B-II/LC3B-I ratio and reduced p62 expression, while suppressed apoptosis was verified by upregulated Bcl-2 and downregulated Bax. In conclusion, combined SPD and RE intervention ameliorates age-related myocardial injury and mitochondrial dysfunction by activating the AMPK-SIRT1-PGC-1α signaling pathway, promoting mitochondrial biogenesis and mitophagy, and inhibiting apoptosis.
