Article.Title: Deep learning-assisted sustainable design of a multi-substrate 2.4 GHz wearable IoT antenna
Article.Authors: Mersani A.; Mekki K.; Necibi O.; Altaieb M.; Abdalrahman A.; Hamid O.; Chouaib H.; Khaldi K.; Gharsallah A.
Article.Abstract: Wearable antennas are essential components of modern Internet of Things (IoT) systems, enabling wireless communication for body-centric, healthcare, environmental-monitoring, and smart-textile applications. Deep learning provides an effective means of accelerating antenna design and optimization under complex material and operating conditions. This paper presents a deep learning-assisted and sustainability-oriented framework for designing a compact 2.4 GHz wearable IoT antenna implemented on three representative substrates: FR4, Rogers laminate, and felt-based textile. A unified slotted microstrip patch topology is adopted to enable a consistent comparison between rigid and flexible antenna realizations while highlighting trade-offs among impedance matching, bandwidth, mechanical flexibility, and material characteristics. A multi-substrate full-wave electromagnetic dataset containing approximately $$1.09\times {10}^{5}$$ samples is generated in CST Microwave Studio by varying the principal geometrical parameters, substrate descriptors, and operating frequency over the 2.0–3.0 GHz range. A fully connected deep neural network surrogate is trained to predict the reflection coefficient from antenna geometry, substrate properties, and operating frequency, achieving an RMSE of 0.8500 dB and $${R}^{2}=0.9553$$ on the held-out sample-level test partition. A separate geometry-level holdout evaluation is also conducted using six antenna configurations whose complete frequency responses are excluded from training and validation. The optimized antenna designs are fabricated on the three substrates and experimentally evaluated through calibrated reflection-coefficient measurements. For the felt-based textile prototype, additional measured reflection-coefficient responses under on-arm bending and progressive surface-wetting conditions demonstrate stable impedance matching around the 2.4 GHz ISM band. Radiation patterns, realized gain, radiation efficiency, on-body behavior, and specific absorption rate are evaluated using full-wave simulations only; no experimental over-the-air radiation validation is claimed. The simulations predict broadside radiation behavior and simulated SAR values below the applicable international safety limits. An equivalent parallel RLC model is also introduced to support the physical interpretation of substrate-dependent impedance behavior. The results indicate that the proposed surrogate-assisted framework enables rapid, substrate-aware antenna design and reduces dependence on repeated full-wave simulations. The felt-based implementation provides a practical compromise among simulated electromagnetic performance, flexibility, reduced substrate mass, and wearable suitability.

Article.Title: Localized enteric neural deficiency and reduced nerve-mediated anorectal contractility in immunodeficient RetS812F/+ mice
Article.Authors: Komoike Y.; Yamashita T.; Nakajima T.; Goto M.; Yamamoto M.; Sunardi M.; Matsumoto H.; Enomoto H.; Ikeya M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Evaluating cell-based therapies for the enteric nervous system (ENS) requires an in vivo environment with a localized enteric neural-deficient region. However, preclinical studies using human cells are limited by the lack of suitable animal models; conventional aganglionic models often suffer from early lethality, and there are few immunodeficient strains with a defined enteric neural-deficient segment for xenotransplantation. In this study, we established the B6RGS- Ret S812F/+ mouse, a novel immunodeficient strain with a localized deficiency of enteric nerves and reduced nerve-related anorectal contraction. While these mice did not exhibit overt defecation defects or stool congestion, this phenotype allowed for the survival period necessary to perform transplantation experiments. Using the B6RGS background, we observed the short-term retention of human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived vagal neural crest cells within the distal anorectum. Our results suggest that the B6RGS- Ret S812F/+ mouse may serve as a practical recipient for evaluating the initial engraftment of human-derived cell therapies for enteric nerve deficiencies.

Article.Title: Differences in larval survival and development among three Chilean decapods are consistent with their southern range limits
Article.Authors: Soto J.; Rojas-Hernandez N.; Bruning M.; Cid M.; Vega-Retter C.; Pardo L.; Parada C.; Veliz D.
Article.Abstract: In marine organisms with complex life cycles, the planktonic larval stage is among the most sensitive to environmental variation, affecting dispersal potential in early life. We compared larval mortality and development at 10, 13, 16, and 19 °C among three Chilean decapods with contrasting southern range limits: the brachyuran crabs Cancer porteri (38°S) and Metacarcinus edwardsii (55°S), and the anomuran Petrolisthes violaceus (46°S). Metacarcinus edwardsii completed development across the full range, whereas C. porteri presented complete mortality in zoea III at 10 °C and in zoea V at 13 °C, and P. violaceus had complete mortality in zoea I at 10 °C, with partial survival to the megalopa at 13 °C. Development in M. edwardsii was less affected at low temperatures. At the cold end of the range, the probability of reaching the megalopa followed southern range limits, although spring sea temperatures near those limits were lower than the temperatures that constrained development in our cultures. Laboratory values therefore indicate a relative ordering among species rather than the temperatures that set a range edge. This consistency between larval performance and geographic distribution suggests that early-life thermal constraints may contribute to biogeographic patterns along the Chilean coast.

Article.Title: Exploring foot pressure patterns for skiing experience classification in a simulator-based environment
Article.Authors: Ono S.; Atsumi R.; Kanai H.; Koike H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigated whether deep learning can distinguish groups of ski experience based on plantar-pressure distributions measured during simulator-based training and whether classifier outputs change during repeated training. Weight-shift images from 27 participants were classified into beginner, novice, and intermediate groups, operationally defined by self-reported skiing exposure, using a YOLO11-based image classifier. Participant-wise generalization was explored using leave-one-participant-out (LOPO) cross-validation, with performance summarized at the participant and session levels. The classifier showed moderate discrimination between the beginner and novice groups but limited generalization to the intermediate group. Session-level classification achieved an accuracy of 0.667, macro-F1 of 0.489, and balanced accuracy of 0.524. Longitudinal changes in classifier outputs were subsequently examined in six beginner participants using fixed participant-dependent models trained only on baseline data. Mixed-effects analyses provided tentative evidence of nonlinear changes in classifier outputs across repeated training sessions, although the results were sensitive to model specification, and substantial inter-individual variability was observed. Qualitative Eigen-CAM visualization and biomechanical analyses further indicated that the classifier responded to distributed plantar-pressure characteristics. These findings support the feasibility of using plantar-pressure patterns to characterize skiing-experience groups and to track longitudinal changes in simulator-derived pressure patterns, while highlighting the need for larger sample sizes and independently validated skiing-skill criteria before such models can be used for objective proficiency assessment.

Article.Title: Analytical and clinical validation of SYBR Green- and TaqMan-based multiplex real-time PCR assays for quantitative detection of intestinal protozoa in India
Article.Authors: Garg P.; Khandelwal V.; Bhasin S.; Malhotra P.; Singh Rana S.; Sehgal R.; Datta P.
Article.Abstract: Intestinal protozoa such as Entamoeba histolytica , Giardia lamblia , and Cryptosporidium spp . are major causes of diarrhoeal disease worldwide, yet their accurate detection remains challenging because of the limitations of microscopy and antigen-based assays. This study developed and validated multiplex real-time PCR assays using SYBR Green and TaqMan chemistries for simultaneous detection and quantification of these pathogens in stool samples. A total of 540 patients with gastrointestinal disorders were examined using multiplex conventional PCR, SYBR-based qPCR, and probe-based qPCR. The TaqMan multiplex assay demonstrated the highest analytical sensitivity, with a limit of detection corresponding to the 10⁻⁸ serial dilution of the recombinant DNA standards with excellent linearity (R² ≈ 0.99) and diagnostic specificity (100%). Overall detection was 24.4% by probe-based and 23.1% by SYBR-based assays, with near-perfect inter-assay concordance (κ = 0.93–0.97). The probe-based assay additionally identified low-intensity and mixed infections confirmed by Sanger sequencing. These findings establish a sensitive, quantitative, and clinically applicable multiplex qPCR platform that improves the detection of intestinal protozoa, particularly in immunocompromised patients. By enabling simultaneous detection of three pathogens in a single reaction, the assay reduces reagent and consumable use, hands-on processing, instrument occupancy, and turnaround time compared with performing three separate single-plex qPCR assays. Under our laboratory conditions, the multiplex assay reduced reagent costs from approximately ₹1,800 per sample for three individual single-plex reactions to approximately ₹900 per sample, while decreasing the total assay time from approximately 4.5 h to 1.5 h, making it a practical and economical option for routine molecular diagnosis and surveillance in high-burden settings.

Article.Title: Regimen selection for combined immunotherapy in non-small cell lung cancer with PD-L1 < 1%: a multicenter, retrospective study from Japan (SPIRAL-LT1)
Article.Authors: Murata D.; Azuma K.; Murotani K.; Ito K.; Nomizo T.; Yamada K.; Imabayashi T.; Iwanaga K.; Chibana K.; Ota T.; Nishii Y.; Nakao A.; Okada A.; Hamai K.; Tanimura K.; Yoshimine K.; Tamura Y.; Takaki R.; Goto Y.; Hibino M.; Oba T.; Sumi T.; Kaneda H.; Nishioka N.; Yamada T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This multicenter retrospective study at 22 centers in Japan using electronic medical record data aimed to compare the effectiveness and safety of CTLA-4 regimens (ipilimumab plus nivolumab with or without chemotherapy) versus non-CTLA-4 regimens (pembrolizumab or atezolizumab plus chemotherapy) as first-line treatment for patients with advanced or recurrent NSCLC expressing PD-L1 < 1%. Dual primary endpoints were PFS and OS after propensity score matching (PSM) incorporating age, gender, PS, stage, histology, driver mutations, smoking, liver metastasis, and brain metastasis. Safety was assessed by the incidence and onset timing of ≥ grade 3 drug-related AEs. A total of 124 patients each were analyzed for both regimens. PFS and OS did not differ between CTLA-4 and non-CTLA-4 regimens, and exploratory subgroup analyses showed no substantial differences in treatment effect across patient characteristics. The CTLA-4 regimen had a higher incidence of ≥ grade 3 irAEs, particularly hepatic and gastrointestinal disease, and a lower incidence of ≥ grade 3 chemo-AEs. Onset of grade ≥ 3 irAEs also differed between regimens, and late-onset events with CTLA-4 regimens showed longer OS. In conclusion, while first-line CTLA-4 and non-CTLA-4 regimens showed comparable effectiveness in patients with NSCLC expressing PD-L1 < 1%, distinct toxicity profiles were observed, suggesting careful consideration of safety profiles is warranted.

Article.Title: Classification of chiral domain-wall dynamics through symmetry analysis
Article.Authors: Han G.; Shim W.; Kim K.; Jeon S.; Mok Y.; Kim D.; Yu J.; Kim T.; Kim K.; Choe S.; Kim D.
Article.Abstract: We report the discovery of a previously unreported type of chiral domain-wall (DW) dynamics and establish a symmetry-based framework for classifying the observed types of chiral DW dynamics. In this newly identified type, the symmetric component of the DW speed exhibits a concave-down curvature, in sharp contrast to the conventional concave-up response associated with the equilibrium DW-energy contribution. Sample-specific micromagnetic calculations reproduce only the conventional response and fail to account for this reversed curvature, indicating an additional even contribution beyond the conventional equilibrium DW-energy picture. By incorporating this new response, we show that the chiral DW dynamics observed to date can be classified into three distinct types, all of which are quantitatively described by symmetric and antisymmetric components having the same respective functional forms. This classification provides a systematic framework for investigating diverse chiral DW dynamics and their underlying physics.

Article.Title: Disturbance resilient fuzzy variable gain super twisting sliding mode control for underactuated Furuta pendulum systems
Article.Authors: Mengistu M.; Adane K.; Yosef E.
Article.Abstract: The Furuta pendulum, also known as a rotary inverted pendulum, is a representative underactuated nonlinear system widely used for evaluating advanced control strategies. Its inherent instability, nonlinear dynamic coupling, and limited actuation make accurate stabilization particularly challenging, especially in the presence of model uncertainties and external disturbances. Conventional controllers, such as PID and fixed gain sliding mode controllers, may suffer from limited robustness, excessive control activity, or chattering when subjected to system uncertainties and disturbances. To address these limitations, this study proposes a disturbance resilient fuzzy Logic Based variable gain super twisting sliding mode controller (FLBVGSTA) for the stabilization of an underactuated Furuta pendulum. A state based sliding surface is formulated using the rotary-arm and pendulum states, while a fuzzy inference mechanism dynamically adjusts the super twisting gains according to the magnitude of the sliding variable. The nonlinear dynamics of the Furuta pendulum are derived using the Euler Lagrange formulation, and the finite time stability of the closed-loop system is investigated using Lyapunov based analysis under bounded disturbances. The proposed controller is evaluated through MATLAB/Simulink simulations and compared with FBSTSA and PID-STA controllers under identical simulation conditions. The results show that the proposed FLBVGSTA reduces the pendulum-angle RMSE by 5.0% compared with FBSTSA and by 78.05% compared with PID-STA. For the rotary-arm angle, the RMSE is reduced by 85.0% compared with FBSTSA and by 64.8% compared with PID-STA. In addition, the convergence time is reduced by 87.21% and 86.35% compared with FBSTSA and PID-STA, respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed fuzzy variable gain super twisting strategy provides improved stabilization accuracy, faster convergence, and enhanced disturbance rejection while reducing unnecessary control activity.

Article.Title: Commonly traded anurans are susceptible to the emerging fungal pathogen Batrachochytrium salamandrivorans
Article.Authors: Masecar S.; Tavarez-Jimenez E.; Horan S.; Draculan M.; Sheley W.; McCartney J.; Woodhams D.; Piovia-Scott J.; Bletz M.
Article.Abstract: Batrachochytrium salamandrivorans (Bsal), a deadly fungal pathogen of amphibians, can spread via animal trade. Bsal is an emerging pathogen and is not yet in North America, which is a global center for urodelan biodiversity. While Bsal was initially thought to only infect urodelans, anurans can also develop infections. Anurans are more commonly traded than urodelans and therefore could pose a greater risk of facilitating the spread of Bsal. Determining the susceptibility of commonly traded anuran species is important for estimating the risk anurans pose of spreading Bsal via trade. Here, we investigate Bsal susceptibility in four species of commonly traded anurans ( Litoria caerulea, Bombina orientalis, Hymenochirus spp., Kaloula pulchra ) via pathogen exposure experiments. We measured morbidity, mortality, and infection prevalence, intensity, and duration. Eight of ten L. caerulea and 8/11 Hymenochirus spp. developed Bsal infections, with infections persisting beyond 6 and 12 weeks, respectively. No mortality was attributable to Bsal, but we did observe reduced weight gain in L. caerulea . These findings expand understanding of Bsal susceptibility across species and highlight the role anurans may play as asymptomatic carriers. Expanding Bsal mitigation strategies to include anurans could help prevent the introduction of this dangerous pathogen into North America.

Article.Title: Metabolome and microbiome analysis of human milk from women with lactational mastitis during remission
Article.Authors: Chen C.; Zhou Y.; Yu Y.; Xu Y.; Shi A.; Ju P.; Xu X.; Xiao Z.; Wu G.; Gu X.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lactational mastitis is a disease that brings pain to mothers and interrupts breastfeeding. After remission, mothers and doctors care about whether the milk is suitable to continue breastfeeding or not. However, relevant research, particularly multi-omics studies focusing on the remission phase of lactational mastitis, remains scarce. 16S rRNA sequencing was used to acquire the microbiome. LC–MS/MS was used to acquire the untargeted metabolome and lipidome of the milk samples from lactational mastitis patients in remission period (LMR) and control mothers. The results revealed that there were no significant differences between the milk from the LMR and control mothers in alpha and beta diversity, and the reported lactational mastitis related genera like Staphylococcus and Streptococcus . Significant differences were found in metabolomic and lipidomic profiles, differentially abundant metabolites especially enriched in some important lipid species like ceramides, triglyceride, O-acyl-hydroxy fatty acids, phosphatidylcholine and lysophosphatidylcholine. In addition, KEGG analysis showed arachidonic acid metabolism and α-linolenic acid metabolism were primarily associated with the aforementioned lipid changes. This study demonstrates that despite being in the remission period of lactational mastitis, the produced milk exhibits lipid dysregulation.

Article.Title: Atomistic insights into spermidine-mediated stabilization of paranemic crossover DNA motifs
Article.Authors: Alkhafaji A.; Zheoat A.; Alsaadi M.; Sawaran Singh N.; Mohammedsaeed A.; Jasim D.; Hamedinia M.
Article.Abstract: The polyamine spermidine (Spd³⁺), which is naturally abundant in cells, influences the architecture and stability of nucleic acid assemblies through multivalent electrostatic interactions. In this study, we investigated how Spd³⁺ affects the paranemic crossover (PX) motif, a key structural element in DNA nanotechnology. Quantum mechanical calculations (HF/6‑31G*) combined with RESP‑derived partial charges were used to optimize the molecular geometry of Spd³⁺ and obtain a reliable electrostatic description. We then performed all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations in GROMACS under two ionic conditions, neutralizing the systems with either Na⁺ or Spd³⁺. Radial distribution functions (RDFs) and minimum‑distance analyses showed that Spd³⁺ binds more strongly and persistently to the DNA backbone than Na⁺. Energy decomposition revealed more favorable electrostatic and van der Waals interactions in the presence of Spd³⁺, whereas Na⁺ exhibited weaker binding. Mean‑square displacement (MSD) analysis further confirmed the localized behavior of Spd³⁺ compared with the higher mobility of Na⁺. Global structural metrics, including principal component analysis (PCA) and root‑mean‑square deviation (RMSD), indicated a more confined conformational landscape under Spd³⁺ conditions. Analysis of base‑pair step parameters characterized the local helical geometry within the crossover region. In parallel, backbone fluctuation analysis showed reduced flexibility in the presence of Spd³⁺. Overall, these computational findings suggest that spermidine enhances the structural stability of the PX motif and provide molecular-level insights into the potential robustness of DNA‑based nanomaterials.

Article.Title: Genetic basis of phase amplitude coupling entrained by working memory
Article.Authors: Nazari A.; Treue S.; Esghaei M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Working memory (WM) is a core determinant of cognitive functions, and its impairment is a hallmark of several psychiatric conditions. Here, we investigated whether genetic factors contribute to WM performance. Analyzing magnetoencephalography (MEG) data from the Human Connectome Project (82 healthy adults: monozygotic [MZ] and dizygotic [DZ] twin pairs and unrelated [UR] pairs) performing WM tasks, we observed that WM accuracy is markedly more similar within MZ twin pairs than in DZ or UR pairs, indicating a genetic contribution to WM performance. To uncover a candidate neural mechanism for this genetic influence, we quantified phase-amplitude coupling (PAC)—the modulation of high-frequency amplitude by low-frequency phase—and compared PAC patterns across individuals. We define PAC alignment as the between-individual similarity of PAC temporal patterns. PAC alignment was significantly higher in MZ than in DZ or UR pairs and positively correlated with similarity in WM behavioral accuracy, linking PAC to behavior. Together, these findings support PAC alignment as a candidate genetically influenced neural feature related to individual differences in WM.

Article.Title: Green synthesized silver nanoparticles from floral waste of Tagetes patula for mitigation of Meloidogyne incognita stress in tomato plants
Article.Authors: Singh A.; Singh A.; Kapoor N.; Ohri P.
Article.Abstract: Meloidogyne incognita ( M. incognita ) is a destructive plant parasitic nematode causing severe crop losses worldwide. This study aims to evaluate the potential of Tagetes patula - mediated silver nanoparticles (TP@Ag NPs) as an eco-friendly nematicidal and plant growth-promoting agent against M. incognita infection in Solanum lycopersicum L. seedlings. Silver nanoparticles were synthesized using T. patula petal extract and characterized by UV–visible spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, high-resolution transmission electron microscopy with selected area electron diffraction, dynamic light scattering and zeta potential analysis. The synthesis process produced a yield of ~ 42.4 mg NP per g biomass (including both metallic silver and phytogenic components), resulting in stable silver nanoparticles with no detectable residual silver nitrate. Mortality bioassays revealed that TP@Ag NPs induced a clear dose- and time-dependent nematicidal response, with maximum juvenile mortality of 97.66% observed at 50 ppm within 24 h ( p < 0.01). Nematode-infested seedlings treated with TP@Ag NPs showed improved growth as well as biochemical attributes, enhanced photosynthetic pigment levels (~ 240% increase in chlorophyll a, b and total chlorophyll content at p < 0.01) and elevated antioxidant enzyme activities as compared to untreated infected controls. Confocal microscopy indicated increased glutathione levels, reduced hydrogen peroxide accumulation and improved cell viability. This study demonstrates the potential of green-synthesized silver nanoparticles from T. patula petals to simultaneously manage M. incognita stress and promote plant growth in tomato.

Article.Title: Identification of adventitious lung sounds in children with respiratory illnesses in Bangladesh using artificial intelligence and digital auscultation
Article.Authors: Ahmed S.; Khan A.; Nair H.; Cunningham S.; McLane I.; Islam M.; Islam A.; Tabassum R.; Chowdhury N.; Sultana N.; Githinji L.; Justin M.; Jahan I.; Wahiduzzaman M.; Mitra D.; Hasan M.; Chowdhury M.; Shahidullah M.; Baqui A.; McCollum E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Integrated management of childhood illness (IMCI) guidelines have high sensitivity but low specificity for pneumonia diagnosis. Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled digital stethoscopes capable of analyzing lung sounds may improve IMCI diagnostic performance. We evaluated the performance of an AI algorithm trained to identify normal and adventitial lung sounds in children. Non-physician health workers recorded lung sounds from four chest positions using a digital stethoscope in under-five-year-old children with suspected pneumonia at community clinics in Bangladesh. A trained paediatrician listening panel classified chest position recordings as normal, abnormal (crackles and/or wheeze), or uninterpretable. The AI algorithm similarly classified chest position recordings except for the uninterpretable category. AI algorithm and listening panel comparisons were made at the child-level, and included chest positions considered interpretable, uninterpretable, and high- and low-confidence by the panel. Compared to the panel, AI algorithm sensitivity and specificity for detecting abnormal sounds were 61.8% and 60.7% among all children, and 63.5% and 66.8% in IMCI pneumonia cases. Overall, the AI algorithm achieved moderate classification performance. Classification performance will benefit from further AI algorithm training to categorize recordings as uninterpretable.

Article.Title: Mesenchymal stem cells modulate pancreatic and splenic inflammation through PI3K/AKT/mTOR and TGF-β signalling in diabetic rats
Article.Authors: Ahmed S.; El-Ghaiesh S.; Eltrawy A.; Jaber F.; Alderbas R.; Rizk N.; Gad N.; Dawood A.
Article.Abstract: Bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (MSC) can attenuate diabetic organ damage through immunomodulatory and paracrine mechanisms, yet the specific signalling pathways engaged in the pancreas and spleen remain poorly characterized. This study investigated the effects of a single dose of undifferentiated MSC on PI3K/AKT/mTOR and TGF-β signalling, apoptotic gene expression, and tissue architecture in the pancreas and spleen of streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic rats. Female rats were divided into four groups: control, diabetic (induced by streptozotocin), insulin-treated diabetic, and MSC-treated diabetic. Gene expression levels of SRY, C-Jun, P53, BCL2, P38, and Caspase3 were assessed using quantitative PCR and normalized against GAPDH. Tissue histopathology of the spleen and pancreas using H&E and immunohistochemistry (IHC) staining for PI3K, AKT, mTOR, and TGF-β were investigated. MSC-treated group showed a significant downregulation of pro-apoptotic markers Caspase3 and P53, and stress response genes P38 with upregulated anti-apoptotic gene BCL2 compared to the untreated diabetic rats. Pancreatic and splenic PI3K and AKT protein were restored following MSC treatment. Conversely, elevated TGF-β protein expression was reduced by MSC therapy, whereas mTOR remained elevated in MSC-treated tissues while lowered toward control levels by insulin. These molecular changes were accompanied by partial restoration of islet architecture and splenic histology. To our knowledge, this is among few studies concurrently characterized PI3K/AKT/mTOR and TGF-β signaling in both pancreatic and splenic tissues from the same diabetic animal. MSC therapy demonstrates a potential therapeutic role by modulating inflammatory and cell apoptotic pathways of PI3K/AKT/mTOR and TGF-β signalling with partial preservation of pancreatic and splenic tissue. A differential mTOR response was observed, whereby insulin, but not MSC treatment, restored mTOR expression toward control levels. Our findings support MSC further investigation as a regenerative adjunct to conventional diabetes management.

Article.Title: Identification of stable reference genes for quantitative real-time PCR in human fibroblasts from lymph nodes and synovium
Article.Authors: Rasouli S.; van Ansenwoude C.; Semmelink J.; van Baarsen L.; de Jong T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) is a widely used method for gene expression analysis; however, its accuracy depends on the selection of stable reference genes for normalization. To date, no study has systematically identified suitable reference genes for primary human fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS) and lymph node stromal cells (LNSCs) in the context of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), despite the critical role of these stromal cells in disease pathogenesis. We evaluated the expression stability of 12 candidate reference genes in FLS and LNSCs subjected to various in vitro conditions, including inflammatory stimulation, senescence induction, and differentiation. Candidate genes were selected based on common usage and Genevestigator analysis of publicly available transcriptomic datasets. Expression stability was assessed using Clarida and RefFinder software, integrating geNorm, NormFinder, BestKeeper, and the comparative delta Ct method. The number and identity of recommended reference genes depended on cell type and experimental condition. In LNSCs, two genes, RPLP0 and POLR2G , were recommended across all tested conditions. In contrast, FLS exhibited condition-dependent variability, with POLR2G and TBP being recommended for untreated FLS. In contrast, combinations of three genes were recommended for FLS subjected to TNFαLTαβ stimulation ( EEF1A1 , NFIC and POLR2A ), senescence-related conditions ( EEF1A1 , GAPDH and NFIC) and adipogenesis ( POLR2G , EEF1A1 and TBP) . Comparison of normalization strategies in untreated FLS showed that reference gene choice influenced relative target gene expression patterns and their interpretation. This study provides the first systematic evaluation of reference genes for RT-qPCR normalization in human FLS and LNSCs. Our findings highlight the necessity of condition- and cell type-specific validation of reference genes to ensure accurate and reproducible gene expression analysis in studies of fibroblast biology and inflammatory disease.

Article.Title: Depression, functional disability, and cardiovascular disease in adults with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome stages 0–3: a nationally representative cohort study
Article.Authors: Chen J.; Zhou Y.; Yu C.; Chen Y.; Zheng D.; He Z.
Article.Abstract: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome (CKM) has emerged as an integrated framework for identifying individuals at increased cardiovascular risk before clinical cardiovascular disease (CVD) develops. However, whether psychological and functional vulnerabilities further refine risk stratification in earlier CKM stages remains unclear. Using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, we examined the joint association of depression and functional disability with incident CVD among 7217 adults with CKM stages 0–3. Participants were categorized into four groups according to baseline depression and functional disability status. During follow-up, incident CVD, heart disease, and stroke were assessed. Compared with participants with neither depression nor functional disability, those with depression only, functional disability only, and both conditions had higher risks of incident CVD in fully adjusted Cox models, with the highest risk observed among participants with both conditions. Similar patterns were observed for heart disease and stroke. No statistically significant additive or multiplicative interactions were found between depression and functional disability. Adding depression and functional disability to conventional risk factors modestly improved CVD risk prediction. These findings suggest that depression and functional disability should be considered as important dimensions in CVD risk assessment for adults with CKM stages 0–3, supporting a more comprehensive approach to early cardiovascular risk stratification.

Article.Title: Metabolic syndrome prevalence and correlates among university and hospital staff in southwestern Uganda
Article.Authors: Chuwa A.; Kangwagye P.; Agaba D.; Omolo R.; Migisha R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Background Metabolic syndrome (MetS) increases the risk of cardiovascular disease and diabetes; however, data among professional workforces in Uganda are limited. We assessed the prevalence and associated factors of MetS among university and hospital staff in Mbarara, southwestern Uganda. Methods We conducted an institution-based cross-sectional study among 231 university and hospital staff. Participants were selected using stratified simple random sampling with proportional allocation by institution and staff category. MetS was defined using the harmonized Joint Interim Statement criteria as the presence of ≥ 3 of five components: central obesity, elevated triglycerides, reduced high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, elevated blood pressure, and dysglycemia. We described component clustering as 0, 1–2, or ≥ 3 components and used modified Poisson regression to identify factors associated with MetS Results Among 231 participants, 139 (60.2%) were male, the mean age was 41.1 years, and 164 (71.0%) were university staff. Overall, 68 participants had MetS, giving a prevalence of 29.4% (95% CI 23.6–35.8). Low HDL-C (65%) and dysglycemia (51%) were the most common components. Only 9% of participants had no MetS components, whereas 62% had 1–2 components MetS was independently associated with age 35–49 years (adjusted prevalence ratio [aPR] 2.24, 95% CI 1.10–4.54), age ≥ 50 years (aPR 2.75, 95% CI 1.27–5.97), female sex (aPR 3.16, 95% CI 2.05–4.88), and alcohol use (aPR 1.78, 95% CI 1.20–2.63). Conclusions MetS and subthreshold cardiometabolic risk clustering were common among academic and healthcare workers. The predominance of low HDL-C and dysglycemia, together with higher MetS prevalence among older staff, women, and alcohol users, supports workplace-based screening, targeted prevention, and longitudinal follow-up in similar low-resource professional settings.

Article.Title: The dynamic changes of rumen bacterial and fungal microbiota in free-ranged Gangba plateau sheep
Article.Authors: Zhang L.; Xu H.; Wu Y.; Yang X.; Da W.; Li K.; Kiani F.; Li M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Gangba sheep is an important sheep breed in Xizang plateau; however, little information is available about its rumen microbiota. This study revealed the composition and characteristics of rumen bacterial and fungal microbiota in free-ranged Gangba sheep. For bacterial and fungal microbiota sequencing, rumen fluid samples were collected from free-ranged Gangba sheep from four age groups (6, 18, 30, and 42 months; n = 6 each). There were 2 421 684 and 2 463 063 filtered bacterial and fungal reads (bp), respectively in Gangba sheep. No significant differences were observed in the bacterial and fungal alpha diversity indices among Gangba sheep across different age groups. The predominant bacterial phyla were Bacteroidota and Firmicutes A , while Ascomycota and Basidiomycota were the dominant fungal phyla across all age groups of Gangba sheep. A total of seven bacterial phyla and thirty-nine genera, including UBA1711, Treponema D , CAG 41, CAJPSE01, Ruminococcus D , and Denitrobacterium exhibited significant age-related differences in Gangba sheep. Additionally, five fungal genera, Paraphaeosphaeria , Trichocladium , Dictyosporiaceae gen. incertae sedis , Entyloma , and Coprinopsis , showed marked variation among different age groups. Our study provides novel insights into the rumen microbiota, highlighting age related variations influencing microbial ecology. The functional roles and environmental interactions of these microbes may be explored in future studies to enhance sheep health and productivity in plateau regions.

Article.Title: Generic context-dependence governs clonal emergence of ciprofloxacin resistance mutations
Article.Authors: Ghosh A.; Deb P.; Bose P.; Sk I.; Biswas S.; Mukhopadhyay A.; Ganguly D.; Chattopadhyay S.
Article.Abstract: Ciprofloxacin is widely used against enterobacterial infections, where primary resistance-determinants are the mutations in DNA gyrase (GyrA) and topoisomerase IV (ParC) proteins. Bioinformatic analyses on 2734 isolates representing prominent enterobacterial species deciphered a high-resolution (with > 96% accuracy) septatype scheme, involving both nonsynonymous and synonymous mutations in five codon positions of gyrA , parC , and recN (encoding recombination protein N), and presence/absence of two plasmid-mediated resistance genes ( qnrB2 and qnrS1 ). Such a typing scheme should provide a framework for rapid point-of-care assays to optimize ciprofloxacin use against enterobacterial, and potentially other bacterial, infections. As expected, four amino acid positions of the topoisomerases were the most powerful contributors. Despite species-specificity, and also habitat-specificity owing to distinct intra-species clonal emergence, their tetratype combinations strictly followed a generalized context-dependence syntax, where conformational change owing to increased hydrophobicity disrupted ciprofloxacin binding to GyrA and ParC, leading to drug resistance. Moreover, in some Salmonella isolates, codon ctg over the consensus cta for leucine at codon 346 of the recN gene, owing to its drastically high usage preference, suggested better codon optimization. This might lead to higher RecN production, potentially aiding to antibiotic escape property of the organism, thereby indicating contribution of synonymous mutations in antibiotic resistance.

Article.Title: Representation learning for low-data protein fitness prediction using sequence–structure embeddings and graph neural networks
Article.Authors: Phunnasorn C.; Hongdilokkul N.; Laesanklang W.; Modchang C.; Krityakierne T.
Article.Abstract: Accurate prediction of mutational fitness effects remains challenging in low-data protein engineering settings, where experimentally characterized variants are limited. Although recent protein language models and structure-aware neural networks have demonstrated strong performance on large-scale datasets, the relative importance of structural information, pre-trained embeddings, and optimization strategies under data-constrained conditions remains insufficiently understood. In this study, we investigate a graph-based framework that integrates AlphaFold2-derived protein structures, Masked Inverse Folding with Sequence Transfer (MIF-ST) embeddings, and graph neural networks for protein fitness prediction using a dataset of 152 TEM \(\beta \) -lactamase variants. Through controlled ablation experiments, we systematically evaluate the effects of structural quality, feature richness, pre-trained embeddings, and automated hyperparameter optimization across both random train–test splits and mutation-specific splits requiring generalization to unseen mutations. Under standard random splits, simpler feature representations perform competitively because training and test samples follow similar distributions. In contrast, under mutation-specific distribution shift, models incorporating structural information and pre-trained sequence–structure embeddings achieve considerably stronger predictive performance and improved generalization. Among the evaluated configurations, the full framework combining AlphaFold2, MIF-ST, and Optuna achieved the highest overall performance across the evaluation datasets. These findings demonstrate that the effectiveness of structure-aware representations depends strongly on the evaluation regime and highlight the importance of mutation-specific generalization when designing data-efficient protein fitness prediction frameworks.

Article.Title: Distinct contributions of expertise and automatization to higher dual-task performance: A cognitive–motor dual-task study in pianists
Article.Authors: Worschech F.; Losch H.; Raab M.; Lee A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Dual-task studies consistently find that experts are better at performing two tasks at the same time than non-experts. Usually, this effect is explained by the high degree of skill automatization in experts, given that skills become increasingly automatized during later stages of learning. However, it is not yet clear whether expertise and task automatization following extensive practice exhibit identical or independent mechanisms for reducing dual-task costs. In this study, we investigated how expertise, the learning stage, and higher cognitive abilities contribute to motor–cognitive dual-task interference. Thirty-eight conservatory-level pianists practiced two novel piano sequences. Each sequence involved the same practice time for all participants (i.e., 20 trials) for which individual learning rates—proxies of the learning stages by the 20 th trial—were computed. Subsequently, they performed the sequences either at maximal speed or to a fixed metronome tempo while concurrently solving a mental arithmetic task (counting in steps of 7). Using Bayesian hierarchical modeling, dual-task costs were estimated as the change in piano performance between single- and dual-task performances while statistically controlling for cognitive dual-task costs. Results showed that higher piano expertise and later learning stages robustly reduced dual-task costs. Further, higher piano single-task performance, successful memorization of the piano sequence and better cognitive abilities, such as processing speed and switching ability, were also found to reduce dual-task costs. Finally, mediation analyses indicated that expertise and task automatization had largely independent effects on dual-task costs, suggesting distinct mechanisms. Therefore, future studies should avoid equating task automatization with expertise when interpreting dual-task costs.

Article.Authors: Ueda E.; Nakamura D.; Ohara T.; Honda T.; Shibata M.; Fujiwara K.; Furuta Y.; Sakata S.; Oishi E.; Tsuda Y.; Nakamura S.; Hata J.; Nakao T.; Sonoda K.; Ninomiya T.

After internal validation, the shrinkage-adjusted ORs were 2.31 and 2.52, and C-statistics were 0.707 and 0.688, respectively. Thus, hyperspectral imaging, particularly when considered alongside OCT, may capture retinal alterations associated with dementia in older adults.

Article.Title: Network pharmacology and metabolomics analysis of ginsenosides in fibrinolysis balance after hip arthroplasty
Article.Authors: Yao X.; Du Y.; Cao S.; Tan L.; Hu Y.; Mao Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Total hip arthroplasty (THA) is an effective treatment for end‑stage hip disease. However, postoperative fibrinolytic imbalance is common and increases the risks of bleeding and thrombosis. Ginsenosides, the main active constituents of Panax ginseng , exhibit multiple pharmacological activities, including anti‑inflammatory and anti‑apoptotic effects. Nevertheless, their role in fibrinolytic balance after THA remains unclear. Ginsenoside active components were screened from databases such as TCMSP and BATMAN-TCM and further filtered based on ADME parameters. Key targets were obtained via network pharmacology, and a protein–protein interaction (PPI) network was constructed. GO and KEGG enrichment pathway analyses were performed. Venous blood samples were collected from the same patient undergoing THA at 2 h before and 24 h after surgery and subjected to untargeted metabolomics analysis by LC-MS/MS. Multivariate statistical analysis was used to screen differential metabolites and perform pathway enrichment. By integrating network pharmacology and metabolomics results, a “component–target–metabolic pathway” association network was constructed. In vitro validation was performed using techniques such as qRT-PCR and Western blot. A total of nine active ginsenoside components were screened, yielding 351 component targets and 428 fibrinolysis-related targets. Sixty-five key targets were obtained by intersection. PPI network analysis identified AKT1, PTGS2, JUN, and others as core targets. KEGG enrichment analysis showed significant enrichment of complement and coagulation cascades, platelet activation, and the HIF-1 signaling pathway. Metabolomics identified 292 differential metabolites, mainly enriched in pathways such as arachidonic acid metabolism, purine metabolism, and glycerophospholipid metabolism. Based on VIP scores, the top 20 differential metabolites were subjected to exploratory correlation analysis with changes in hemoglobin and platelet counts before and after surgery. Adenosine, sphingosine, and arachidonic acid were positively correlated with changes in hemoglobin and platelet counts. Integrated analysis revealed that arachidonic acid metabolism, cGMP-PKG, cAMP, and sphingolipid signaling pathways were common key pathways. Molecular docking was performed between the core target AKT1 and ginsenoside Rh7, JUN and ginsenoside Rg3, PIK3CA and ginsenoside Rh1, and PTGS2 and ginsenoside F2. The results showed good binding affinity. Further qRT-PCR and Western blot (WB) experiments showed that in LPS-stimulated venous endothelial cells (VECs), intervention with ginsenosides Rh7, Rg3, Rh1, and F2 significantly inhibited the mRNA and protein expression levels of AKT1, JUN, PIK3CA and PTGS2, respectively. WB analysis further revealed that Rh7 intervention in LPS-stimulated VECs significantly promoted the expression of tissue-type plasminogen activator (t-PA) and reduced the expression of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1). These findings further suggest that ginsenoside Rh7 may affect fibrinolytic balance after total hip arthroplasty. This study explored the possibility that ginsenosides Rh7, Rg3, Rh1, and F2 may affect multiple pathways, such as arachidonic acid metabolism and the complement and coagulation cascades, by regulating targets including AKT1, PTGS2, JUN, and PIK3CA. Among them, ginsenoside Rh7 may improve fibrinolytic balance after THA, providing a theoretical basis for its perioperative clinical application.

Article.Title: Machine learning and Weibull-based reliability analysis of impact-resistant geopolymer concrete with construction demolition waste and natural fibers
Article.Authors: Murali G.; Chaudhary L.; Raju P.; Kurpińska M.; Wong L.; Górski J.; Abdelgader H.; Philip S.; Avudaiappan S.
Article.Abstract: This study presents a novel impact-resistant geopolymer concrete (GPC) incorporating construction and demolition waste powder, brick waste powder, slag, recycled concrete aggregates (RCA), and natural fibers (banana, jute, and pineapple) to simultaneously enhance its mechanical performance, impact resistance, and sustainability. Unlike previous studies that primarily focused on compressive strength, this study integrates experimental evaluation, microstructural characterization, machine learning, and Weibull reliability analysis to assess both the impact strength performance and reliability of GPC. By addressing the brittleness and performance variability associated with high RCA content, this study provides a practical strategy for developing durable, low-carbon concrete within the framework of a circular economy. This study examined the strength of natural-fiber-based geopolymer concrete using slag, construction demolition waste powder, brick waste powder, and RCA (0, 25, 50, 75%, and 100%). Banana, pineapple and jute fibers were used at 0.75% by volume. These combinations were mixed and tested for the compression and impact strengths of a total of 20 mixtures. In addition, microstructural analysis was performed on the GPC. Machine learning and the Weibull distribution were used to analyze the performance and reliability of the impact strength. The results showed that increasing RCA content substantially reduced impact resistance, with reductions of 45.6–57.3% in first-crack impact resistance and 54.4–62.7% in failure impact resistance for the fiber-reinforced mixtures. Pineapple-fiber-reinforced GPC exhibited comparatively stable post-cracking performance, with the ductility index remaining within 1.81–2.01 across the investigated RCA levels. The Weibull analysis demonstrated that fiber incorporation reduced the variability of impact resistance and provided more stable reliability characteristics under repeated impact loading. The XGBoost model showed good predictive capability, achieving a coefficient of determination of 0.80 on the testing dataset, with root mean square error, mean absolute error, and mean absolute percentage error values of 11.05, 9.39, and 19.54%, respectively. Shapley additive explanations analysis indicated that natural coarse aggregate and pineapple fiber were the most influential variables affecting the predicted impact resistance, followed by superplasticizer dosage, RCA content, and fiber volume fraction.

Article.Title: RailMASDet: a 3D object detection method for railway LiDAR point cloud foreign object detection
Article.Authors: Ning S.; Li H.; Chen Y.; Guo P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To address the issues of easy loss and inaccurate localization of distant small targets in railway LiDAR point cloud foreign object detection, this paper proposes a 3D object detection method named RailMASDet. The method constructs a cross-scale semantic spatial feature reassembly strategy. By employing transposed restoration of deep features and aligned compression of shallow features, it resolves the problem of spatial detail loss of distant targets in deep BEV feature maps. Furthermore, a railway-oriented channel modulation strategy based on existing channel attention mechanisms is introduced. By jointly exploiting global average and maximum statistics, the strategy adaptively enhances object-sensitive responses and suppresses structured-background interference in railway BEV features. Meanwhile, a foreground probability-driven non-Euclidean distance sampling paradigm is established, embedding point-level foreground priors into the distance metric function to shift keypoint sampling from uniform coverage to semantically guided targeted focusing. On the OSDaR23 dataset, RailMASDet achieves AP 0.7 of 80.59% for pedestrians and 70.05% for car, and an mAP 0.5 of 76.56%, outperforming the baseline model by 4.95, 3.78, and 3.21 percentage points, respectively. The average center localization error of detection boxes is 0.86 m, which is 57.5% lower than that of the baseline. The inference latency is 276.5 ms per frame, demonstrating reasonable computational efficiency. Ablation studies and visualization analyses validate the individual contributions of the three modules and their synergistic enhancement effects, confirming that the proposed method can effectively solve the problems of small target loss and insufficient localization accuracy in railway foreign object detection, thereby demonstrating its potential for long-range foreign object detection in sparse railway LiDAR scenes.

Article.Title: Evolution law of bed separation and mining-induced fractures during mining under thick limestone in the Changxing Formation
Article.Authors: Xu G.; Li C.; Ma Z.; Li H.; Zhao M.; Niu B.; Zhang Y.
Article.Abstract: To address the challenge of roof bed separation water inrush in the Northern Guizhou Coalfield, a study was conducted on the evolution mechanisms of bed separation cavities and mining-induced fractures during the development process of such water disasters. By focusing on the typical working face, we examined the structure and movement processes of the key strata in the overburden roof, along with the expansion of mining-induced fractures and the development of separation spaces, through theoretical analyses and similarity simulation tests. Taking a specific longwall panel in this mining area as the research subject, this study investigates the structure and movement of key strata, as well as the development of bed separation cavities and the propagation of mining-induced fractures, through key strata theoretical analysis and physical similarity modeling tests. The results show that: (1) During the uncoordinated movement of the subkey strata of the Changxing Formation limestone and the underlying strata, bed separation occurs at the bottom boundary of the strata, providing storage space for water enrichment. (2) Before the collapse of the subkey strata of the Changxing Formation limestone, the development of bed separation space and the height of the water-conducting fracture zone are synchronous. The height of the water-conducting fracture zone increases in a step-like manner along with the fracture of the overlying strata, and the maximum value is 51.45 m, which is the distance between the bottom boundary of the Changxing Formation limestone and the coal seam. The mining-induced fractures on the surface of the experimental model exhibit parallel patterns in the transverse direction, with the spacing between parallel lines being the periodic collapse step distance of the roof, with an average value of 21.98 m. The average fracture angle above the mined-out area is 66.2°. The distribution pattern of mining-induced fractures reveals that the two sides of the goaf are dominated by through-type longitudinal fractures, while the central area is dominated by bed separation fractures. Due to the re-compression effect of the overlying strata in the central part of the goaf, some fractures have closed, and the number of fractures in the central part of the mined-out area is less than that on both sides of the mined-out area, resulting in a “saddle” distribution of mining-induced fracture density.(3) The bed separation boundary angle θ is not significantly different between the open-off side and the working face side, and the overall shape of the bed separation is an isosceles regular trapezoid with a base angle of approximately 60°. During the advancement of the working face, the length of the bed separation l s appears to increase linearly, whereas the growth rate of the bed separation height w s tends to first increase but then decrease. When the mined-out area reaches a certain extent, the bed separation height tends to stabilize. The above research results provide important theoretical guidance for the design of bed separation water drainage holes to prevent and control water hazards caused by roof bed separation in coal mines in the region.

Article.Title: Probabilistic tsunami risk assessment based on submarine active faults and their possible interactions in the sea of Japan
Article.Authors: Kikuta H.; Miki Y.; Cheng A.; Suppasri A.; Imamura F.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Sea of Japan coastal areas have experienced tsunami damage caused by submarine active seismic faults. Large uncertainties remain regarding seismic activity of these faults and the following tsunami. Probabilistic tsunami risk assessment (PTRA) enables the evaluation of tsunami risk accounting for such uncertainties. In this study, the tsunami risks of a thermal power plant located in Joetsu on the Sea of Japan coast were evaluated using PTRA based on submarine active faults, including coupled faults, across the Sea of Japan. The results indicate that coupled fault models had large impacts on risk levels, especially for severe damage states. For the most severe damage state, the median expected annual probability of experiencing this damage state among the structures increased by 154% when coupled fault models were considered. In addition, the risk levels varied depending on the structures, even within the same site. The spatial distribution of tsunami risk revealed that structures with high risk levels existed not only along the coast but also inland. The findings of this study provide practical insights into reliable tsunami risk assessment, which are useful for the development of disaster resilience measures, especially for infrastructure.

Article.Title: Microhabitats are associated with bacterial and archaeal community structure in acid mine drainage from an abandoned mine
Article.Authors: Kim M.; Kim S.; Park S.
Article.Abstract: Acid mine drainage (AMD) is a severe environmental problem and a heterogeneous low-pH ecosystem containing diverse microbial communities. Microbial community structure across visually distinct AMD microhabitats remains poorly understood, particularly in South Korea, where field-based microbial studies are scarce and AMD research has mainly focused on contaminated soils and remediation. Here, in an exploratory survey, we analyzed 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing data from water, wall-attached biofilm, and AMD precipitate-associated biofilm microhabitats in AMD from the abandoned Ilgwang mine, Korea. The final dataset comprised 716,915 reads assigned to 663 ASVs across seven samples. Alpha diversity did not differ significantly among microhabitat types (all Kruskal-Wallis P > 0.10). A Type-constrained principal coordinates analysis of square-root-transformed Bray–Curtis dissimilarities, rarefied to the minimum library size, accounted for 50.3% of total variation (adjusted R² = 25.4%, P = 0.025 by exact permutation), although multivariate dispersion differed among Types. The largest genus-display category was Unclassified Gammaproteobacteria (24.96% of pooled reads); the dominant ASV in this category exactly matched a SILVA V4 sequence annotated as Ferrovum but remained formally unclassified at genus because its bootstrap support was 46%, below the 80% threshold. Overall, 57.91% of pooled reads remained unclassified at genus; among confidently assigned genera, Metallibacterium and Leptospirillum were the most abundant. The descriptive compositional summaries are consistent with visible AMD sample matrices being associated with shifts in the relative abundance of a partially shared acidophilic bacterial–archaeal assemblage, rather than with fully discrete communities. These exploratory findings suggest that sample matrix is an important context for interpreting AMD community composition and highlight candidate bacterial and archaeal lineages for future genome-resolved and activity-based studies.

Article.Title: Improving deep neural network prediction of hydraulic fracturing initiation pressure in hydrate-bearing sediments through feature engineering and architecture search
Article.Authors: Ho T.; Trinh T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of hydraulic fracturing initiation pressure ( $$P_b$$ ) in natural gas hydrate-bearing sediments provides screening-level support for laboratory-scale hydraulic fracturing design in NGH-bearing sediments. This study demonstrates that systematic feature engineering and neural architecture search yield substantial improvements for predicting $$P_b$$ on a 114-sample published dataset. The framework first expands the feature space from 12 to 208 variables via polynomial transformations, interaction terms, and domain-specific features, followed by deduplication. Multi-method feature selection identifies a 14-feature subset, and extended evaluation identifies a verified 12 $$\times $$ 32 model as the best-performing saved configuration. The reproducible-by-retraining reference is R $$^2$$ $$\approx $$ 0.87; the verified 12 $$\times $$ 32 saved model achieves R $$^2$$ = 0.92 on its original held-out split and is reported as an upper bound on the dataset. The best of 60 retraining runs reaches 0.85—none reproduces 0.92, confirming that 0.92 is a saved-artifact result, not a reproducible target. The verified 12 $$\times $$ 32 model reduces MSE from 19.34 to 8.22 MPa $$^2$$ and MAE from 3.16 to 2.14 MPa compared to the best prior reported result (R $$^2$$ = 0.81). Feature importance and SHAP analysis show that the model assigns highest importance to stress-composition interactions and stress-derived statistical terms, consistent with known geomechanical controls on fracture initiation. Generalization is modest (CV mean R $$^2 \approx $$ 0.50), and simpler models (RandomForest, SVR) are recommended as production-ready baselines; the 12 $$\times $$ 32 DNN is retained as the best verified saved artifact. These findings confirm that the dataset contains untapped predictive capacity, and that methodological refinement through domain-informed feature engineering combined with systematic architecture search provides an effective pathway for improving prediction fidelity in small-sample geomechanical problems.

Article.Title: Valorization of cotton waste into cellulose nanocrystals and their incorporation into electrospun poly (vinyl alcohol) nanofibrous membranes with enhanced thermal and structural properties
Article.Authors: Dagher W.; Alassod A.; Al Hinnawi M.; Alghoraibi I.; Abdur-Rahman E.
Article.Abstract: Cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) were extracted from cotton waste using alkaline treatment, bleaching, and sulfuric acid hydrolysis. Increasing the sulfuric acid concentration from 40% to 62% was associated with an increase in CNC yield from approximately 19.20 ± 3.9% to 41.30 ± 3.1%, indicating the influence of acid concentration on the recovery of the nanocrystalline fraction under the conditions employed. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) showed carbon and oxygen as the predominant elements, at 62.39 and 34.33 wt%, respectively, with trace amounts of sulfur and sodium. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) revealed snowflake-like aggregated structures composed of branched rod-like features, with an average width of 56.5 ± 8.7 nm . Atomic force microscopy (AFM) showed broadly consistent nanoscale morphological features, with snowflake-like structures ranging from approximately 120–200 nm and protruding branches of approximately 63.2 ± 10.9 nm in diameter. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) showed characteristic cellulose bands, including the band at 872.9 cm⁻¹ associated with β-(1→4)-glycosidic linkages. CNCs were incorporated into poly (vinyl alcohol) (PVA) nanofibrous membranes at concentrations of 0–40 wt% via electrospinning. Field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) of the 40 wt% CNC membrane revealed a relatively uniform fibrous network with a mean fiber diameter of 104.3 ± 38.6 nm, with CNCs distributed on the fiber surfaces. FTIR analysis of the prepared nanofibers showed the characteristic 916 cm⁻¹ band, supporting the presence of the cellulose component. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) showed an increase in residual mass with increasing CNC content, from 1.28% for the neat PVA membrane to 24.88% for the 40 wt% CNC membrane. Derivative thermogravimetry (DTG) indicated changes in thermal degradation behavior with increasing CNC content. The 40 wt% CNC formulation exhibited the highest residual mass among the studied formulations. The study highlights the successful conversion of cotton waste into CNCs and their incorporation into PVA nanofibrous membranes, with potential applications in advanced packaging and biomedical membranes.

Article.Title: Falsification tests distinguish frequency-aligned separation from α-lactose-specific detection in processed continuous-wave terahertz pellet spectra
Article.Authors: Kim C.; Kim J.; Ji T.; Lee M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Low-amplitude features near known absorption bands may be interpreted as analyte detection, although pellet and reference effects can generate similar structures. Using a previously described continuous-wave terahertz platform, we prepared α-lactose-containing and matrix-only control pellets and acquired separate datasets. Two separately prepared matrix-only controls exchanged reference and held-out comparator roles. Two independently prepared nominal 0.1 wt% pellets were evaluated at the pellet level, with repeated scans treated as nested technical measurements. Template and training-derived spectral consistency criteria were established from 0.5–8 wt% concentration-level means without the 0.1 wt% spectra. Under a constrained matrix-reference scaling correction, both 0.1 wt% pellet endpoints at 0.532 THz exceeded their fold-specific held-out control endpoints under both reciprocal reference roles, and their centers lay within the higher-concentration frequency range. However, the residuals failed the locked shape and width criteria, did not dominate matched off-peak responses, persisted after target-region masking, and were not jointly sign-stable under an unconstrained affine adjustment. These results support frequency-aligned spectral separation across two independent preparations under constrained comparison, but not α-lactose-specific detection, formally established limits of detection or quantification , validated quantification, population-level reproducibility, or generalizability. This study shows how post-acquisition falsification analysis can retain positive spectral evidence while bounding stronger analytical assertions.

Article.Title: Spatiotemporal evolution and driving factors of ecological risks in the Wujiang River Basin over the past four decades
Article.Authors: Li W.; Jiang X.; Huang L.; Lv S.; Zhao W.; Wu J.
Article.Abstract: Elucidating the spatiotemporal changes in ecological risk is theoretically and practically significant for advancing regional ecological civilisation development and achieving watershed ecological security. A landscape ecological risk (LER) assessment model based on land use data spanning eight periods from 1990 to 2023 was established for the Wujiang River Basin. Through this model, the spatiotemporal differentiation and evolutionary characteristics of the intrabasin LER were systematically analysed. By integrating spatial autocorrelation analysis with the optimal parameterised geographic detector method, the dominant drivers of global and local spatial differentiation in ecological risk were identified. Between 1990 and 2023, the Wujiang River Basin LER was significantly positively spatially correlated with the drivers, demonstrating overall risk reduction. The high/medium–high-risk area proportion decreased from 11.48 to 4.02%. The low-risk area proportion increased from 5.75 to 52.68%. Temporal analysis revealed three distinct phases of ecological risk evolution: disturbance (1990–2000), reduction (2000–2015), and stabilisation (2015–2023). Landscape pattern changes influenced risk across phases. Socioeconomic factors dominated the spatial pattern of ecological risk. The combined effect of multiple drivers was greater than the effects of individual factors. This study provides systematic references and decision-making support for establishing ecological barriers, managing ecological risks, and optimising ecological spatial patterns in the upper Yangtze River territorial space.

Article.Title: Cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP) inhibition and high-density lipoprotein particle composition: consequences for atherogenesis and neurodegeneration
Article.Authors: Niesor E.; Ditmarsch M.; Rezzi S.; Hodgson A.; Haenggi P.; Dicklin M.; Hsieh A.; de Kleer M.; Scheltens P.; Vijverberg E.; Szarek M.; Davidson M.; Kastelein J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP), required for transferring triglyceride from very-low-density lipoprotein in exchange for cholesteryl ester from high-density lipoprotein (HDL), is also involved in lipophilic antioxidant exchange. We aimed to determine the effects of the next generation potent CETP inhibitor, obicetrapib, on concentrations and plasma distributions of lipophilic antioxidants, apolipoproteins (apo), and sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) in an 8-week, Phase 2 trial of placebo and 2.5, 5, and 10 mg/d obicetrapib in Japanese participants (n = 12 per group). Obicetrapib robustly increased all antioxidant levels in the HDL fraction and decreased plasma levels of oxidized low-density lipoprotein. In specific analyses of the low-dose group, obicetrapib also raised HDL2 cholesterol, apoA1, S1P, apoM, and apoE. Increased levels of monomeric-apoA1 were found in the HDL2 and HDL3 fractions and these correlated with apoM and S1P. Furthermore, we analyzed the relationship between plasma and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) lipophilic antioxidants in a proof-of-concept study of obicetrapib 10 mg/d in early Alzheimer’s disease patients (n = 13) and demonstrated that HDL2 and CSF carotenoid and tocopherol levels were increased by obicetrapib. These results offer a first insight into the mechanism of action for obicetrapib in terms of HDL metabolism and function, with implications for both atherogenesis and neurodegeneration.

Article.Title: Depressive symptoms and fatigue are independently associated with myasthenia gravis-specific quality of life beyond neurological severity: a cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Ķēniņa V.; Krutovs V.; Glāzere I.; Roddate M.; Ķauķe G.; Renemane R.; Žukova V.; Renemane L.
Article.Abstract: Neurological examination and myasthenia gravis (MG)-specific functional scales may not fully capture the psychological and fatigue-related burden of MG. This cross-sectional registry-based study included 75 adults with MG. Depressive and anxiety symptoms were assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) and Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) with validated Latvian- and Russian-language thresholds. Fatigue, quality of life, functional impairment and clinical severity were assessed using the Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS), 15-item Myasthenia Gravis Quality of Life Questionnaire (MG-QOL15), Myasthenia Gravis Activities of Daily Living (MG-ADL) and MG Composite Score (MGCS). Analyses included group comparisons, Spearman correlations, and exploratory multivariable linear regression. Positive depression and anxiety screens were identified in 32/75 (42.7%) and 38/75 (50.7%) patients using language-specific thresholds, compared with 25/75 (33.3%) and 18/75 (24.0%) using conventional thresholds, despite low-to-moderate disease activity (median MGCS 3; MG-ADL 1). Depressive symptoms were associated with poorer MG-QOL15, higher MGCS, greater functional impairment and higher anxiety scores, whereas anxiety correlated only weakly with MG-QOL15 (rho = 0.270). Neurological severity alone may underestimate patient-perceived disease burden. Depressive symptoms and fatigue contribute independently to MG-specific quality of life beyond conventional clinical severity assessment, supporting psychological and fatigue screening even in patients with apparent clinical stability.

Article.Title: ZFPM2 deficiency is associated with oxidative stress and autophagy via FoxO pathway suppression in cardiac development and heart failure
Article.Authors: Zhang R.; Su Y.; Jiang N.; Dai H.; Jiang T.; Zhang Y.; Lin J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To investigate the role of zebrafish zfpm2a in cardiac development and maintenance of cardiac function, and to explore its potential mechanisms in heart failure (HF). The evolutionary conservation of ZFPM2 and the spatiotemporal expression patterns of zebrafish zfpm2a were analyzed. A zfpm2a knockout zebrafish line ( zfpm2a −/− ) was generated to assess developmental and cardiac phenotypes. Cardiac tissue transcriptome sequencing was performed to identify pathways regulated by zfpm2a . Resveratrol treatment was administered to H9C2 cells subjected to siRNA-mediated Zfpm2 knockdown to further elucidate the underlying mechanisms. ZFPM2 was highly conserved, and zebrafish zfpm2a was maternally expressed, with expression increasing after 48 h post-fertilization (hpf) and being enriched in the brain, heart, and swim bladder. zfpm2a knockout resulted in reduced hatching rates, impaired swimming ability, increased mortality, and significant cardiac dysfunction, including decreased heart rate, cardiac fluorescence intensity, stroke volume, fractional shortening, and ejection fraction. Transcriptome analysis indicated suppression of the FoxO signaling pathway in the hearts of zfpm2a −/− zebrafish. In H9C2 cells, Zfpm2 knockdown reduced cell viability and increased apoptosis, malondialdehyde (MDA) content, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, whereas resveratrol reversed these effects. Resveratrol also increased the expression of Sirt, Foxo1/3, Bnip3, and Atg8 at both the mRNA and protein levels. ZFPM2 is essential for cardiac development and the maintenance of cardiac function. Its deficiency may contribute to HF progression by modulating the FoxO signaling pathway and altering oxidative stress and autophagy, thereby providing potential therapeutic targets for HF.

Article.Title: Gui Gan Shen Mai Yin attenuates cardiac hypertrophy and dysfunction in association with mitochondrial homeostasis and the PI3K/AKT1 signaling pathway
Article.Authors: Hou H.; Shi W.; Song J.; Lei S.; Yan M.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of Gui Gan Shen Mai Yin (GGSMY) on cardiac hypertrophy and dysfunction and to explore associated mechanisms. The chemical profile of the GGSMY aqueous extract was characterized using UPLC-MS. Candidate active ingredients and potential targets were analyzed by network pharmacology, and molecular docking was used to evaluate predicted interactions between representative components and AKT1. A mouse transverse aortic constriction (TAC) model was established, and mice received different doses of GGSMY for 4 weeks. Cardiac structure and function were assessed by echocardiography, while myocardial morphology and collagen deposition were evaluated using HE, WGA, and Masson staining. In primary neonatal rat cardiomyocytes stimulated with angiotensin II (Ang II), cell size was assessed by α-actinin immunofluorescence. The expression of hypertrophy-, fibrosis-, and inflammation-associated markers (BNP, MYH7, COL1A1, TGF-β, TNF-α, and IL-18) and AKT/p-AKT (Ser473) was measured by qRT-PCR and Western blotting. Oxidative stress and mitochondrial-related indices were assessed using ROS and MDA assays, JC-1, and MitoTracker Red. Network pharmacology identified 70 overlapping targets between GGSMY-associated targets and cardiac hypertrophy-associated targets, with the PI3K/AKT pathway emerging as a candidate regulatory axis. Molecular docking predicted potential interactions between several representative components and AKT1. In TAC mice, GGSMY attenuated the reductions in LVEF and fractional shortening and reduced cardiac hypertrophy, collagen deposition, and the expression of hypertrophy-, fibrosis-, and inflammation-associated markers. In Ang II-treated cardiomyocytes, GGSMY reduced cell enlargement and marker expression, attenuated mitochondrial membrane depolarization, increased MitoTracker Red fluorescence intensity and area-related readouts, and decreased ROS and MDA levels. GGSMY was also associated with lower p-PI3K/PI3K and p-AKT/AKT ratios, while SC79 partially counteracted selected GGSMY-associated effects. GGSMY attenuated pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy and dysfunction, potentially through improved mitochondrial function-related changes, reduced oxidative stress, and modulation of PI3K/AKT signaling.

Article.Title: The economic value of urban soil carbon under competing carbon pricing perspectives in Prague
Article.Authors: Procházka P.; Soukupová J.; Červený J.; Roubík H.; Kandel G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Urban soil carbon is increasingly incorporated into ecosystem service and climate policy assessments, yet its economic value is commonly reported without an explicit uncertainty range. In this paper, we quantify this uncertainty in urban soil valuation for the Prague Functional Urban Area (rectangular study area centred on Prague) and examine how its sources vary across carbon pricing regimes. The soil organic carbon stock of the upper 0 to 30 cm layer is estimated at 4.15 million tonnes of carbon, with a 90% prediction interval of 1.68 to 8.90 million tonnes. Its estimated median economic value ranges from 0.09 billion EUR under the voluntary carbon market regime to 1.02 billion EUR under the European Union Emissions Trading System and 1.82 billion EUR under the social cost of carbon. Because the value distributions are right-skewed, the expected values, which are the relevant measure for risk-neutral decisions, are higher, at 2.58 to 5.34 billion EUR under two alternative estimates of the social cost of carbon. The source of valuation uncertainty varies markedly across regimes. Soil carbon stock uncertainty accounts for up to 96.7% of the variance under the European Union Emissions Trading System, whereas carbon price uncertainty accounts for at least 52.9% under the social cost of carbon (67.4% under a meta-analytic synthesis). These results suggest that the priority for reducing valuation uncertainty depends on the carbon pricing perspective: improved soil measurements are most informative under market-based pricing, whereas improved carbon damage and price estimates become more important under a social cost of carbon framework. Explicit uncertainty propagation can therefore improve the interpretation and use of urban soil carbon valuations in climate and land-use planning.

Article.Title: 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride based polymer electrolytes for supercapacitor applications
Article.Authors: Ghashal A.; Bi S.; Aldosari S.; Singh P.; Aldbea F.; Rawat S.; Dhapola P.; Srivastava M.; Singh A.; Alheety M.; Diantoro M.
Article.Abstract: The aim of this work was to investigate the effect of 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride (BMIMCI) on the structural, electrical, and electrochemical properties of PVDF-HFP/NaI solid polymer electrolyte for supercapacitor applications. In this work, solid polymer electrolyte films were prepared using the solution casting method with Polyvinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene (PVDF-HFP) as the host polymer. Sodium iodide salt (NaI) and an ionic liquid, 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride (BMIMCI) was incorporated in different weight percentages to improve ionic conductivity. The maximum conductivity of 8.07 × 10 − 4 S/cm was achieved at 4% BMIMCI. The ionic transference number (t ion ) was found to be 0.92, indicates that the ions mainly take part in the conduction process. Linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) revealed a wide electrochemical stability window of 3.67 V, making the electrolyte suitable for practical applications. Surface morphology of the films was studied using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and Polarized Optical Microscopy (POM), which showed a more uniform and less crystalline structure after the addition of the ionic liquid, supporting enhanced ion movement. Differential scanning calorimetry study showed a decrease in crystallinity and an increase in amorphous nature, helping easier movement if ions inside the polymer electrolyte. The optimized solid polymer electrolyte films was further used to fabricate a supercapacitor device. The device exhibited a specific capacitance of 26.3 F/g. Galvanostatic charge-discharge analysis gave a maximum specific capacitance of 10.1Fg − 1 , a coulombic efficiency of 98%, an energy density of 3.9 Whkg − 1 , and a power density of 2650 Wkg − 1 . The device retained about 95% of its initial specific capacitance after 1000 charge-discharge cycles, indicating good cycling stability, showing good electrochemical performance.
