Article.Title: Multiplexed intravascular molecular imaging using dual-channel near-infrared fluorescence integrated with optical coherence tomography
Article.Authors: Kim Y.; Kang D.; Lim Y.; Nam H.; Kim H.; Kim R.; Kim J.; Song J.; Park K.; Kim J.; Yoo H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate characterization of high-risk atherosclerotic plaques requires both structural and molecular information. While integrated optical coherence tomography (OCT)/near-infrared fluorescence (NIRF) imaging enables simultaneous assessment of plaque morphology and biological activity, single-target molecular detection may be insufficient to characterize the multifactorial plaque progression. Multiplexed intravascular molecular imaging remains technically challenging due to fluorescence crosstalk between emission channels, which compromises signal specificity. Here, we present a temporally modulated dual-channel NIRF/OCT catheter system designed to suppress spectral crosstalk and enable simultaneous multiplexed molecular imaging with structural information within the vessel wall. Time-interleaved excitation synchronized to the OCT trigger generates two NIRF excitation signals with a half-cycle phase difference, enabling crosstalk-free detection of two distinct molecular targets, as verified by phantom experiments. In vivo imaging in a rabbit model of atherosclerosis, using probes targeting calcified regions associated with osteogenic activity (ALN-PEG-Cy5.5) and mannose receptor (MMR)-expressing cells, including specific macrophage subset (MMR-PEG-Cy7), enabled simultaneous visualization of distinct molecular signatures within OCT-defined plaque structures. Ex vivo fluorescence imaging and immunohistochemistry supported the biological relevance of each NIRF channel. This integrated multimodal catheter system advances intravascular imaging from single-marker detection toward multiplexed molecular assessment of plaques, which could enable a more comprehensive evaluation of plaque pathobiology.

Article.Title: Comparison of Dynamic Imaging Grade of Swallowing Toxicity (DIGEST) estimates and segmentation-derived measures of pharyngeal residue severity
Article.Authors: Dharmarathna I.; Gandhi P.; Panes V.; Alvarez C.; Barbon C.; Valencia D.; Warneke C.; Steele C.; Hutcheson K.
Article.Abstract: The Dynamic Imaging Grade of Swallowing Toxicity (DIGEST) grades swallowing efficiency based on visuoperceptual estimates of the percentage of bolus in the pharynx after the primary swallow (DIGEST-PR). We compared DIGEST-PR ratings with segmentation-based metrics of % residue to characterize agreement and patterns of discrepancy across approaches. We analyzed 188 initial swallows from videofluoroscopies with available DIGEST-PR criterion-reference scores. Blinded raters segmented bolus area on three frames: (A) before bolus transfer into the pharynx (preswallow residue); (B) one frame before upper esophageal sphincter (UES) opening; and (C) one frame after UES closure. Measures of total bolus area (B), new bolus area (B − A), total residue area (C) and new bolus residue area (C − A) were used to derive four metrics: Bolus Clearance Ratio (“BCR” = C/B); new-bolus-residue-as-%-new-bolus (“NBRPNB” = [(C − A)/(B − A)]); new-bolus-residue-as-%-total-bolus (“NBRPTB” = [(C − A)/B]); and total-residue-as-%-new-bolus (“TRPNB” = [C/(B − A)]). These metrics were mapped to DIGEST-PR severity categories (0%-9%, 10%-49%, 50%-90%, > 90%). Agreement with DIGEST-PR was assessed using prevalence- and bias-adjusted kappa. Generalized estimating equations evaluated the odds of discrepant segmentation-derived metrics relative to DIGEST-PR using ordinal logistic regression. The sample consisted of 20 patients who performed a total of 114 thin liquid, 38 pudding, and 36 cracker swallows. Severity was skewed toward lower severity ratings. Across all consistencies, the NBRPNB metric showed the strongest correspondence with DIGEST-PR. Discrepancies were greatest when metrics did not distinguish the new bolus from preswallow residue. Preswallow residue increased across successive swallowing tasks in the protocol, contributing to the largest disagreement for cracker stimuli, which also had the smallest new bolus areas. Segmentation-based measures that express residue as a percent of the new bolus show good concordance with DIGEST-PR ratings, particularly for thin liquids and lower levels of residue (DIGEST-PR < 50%). Further work is needed to evaluate agreement for thick liquid and solid stimuli and in cases with greater residue severity.

Article.Title: Use of corticosteroids in nonsevere community acquired pneumonia a propensity score matching study
Article.Authors: Hernández Puentes J.; Bastidas Goyes A.; Sánchez L.; Quintero E.; Córdoba J.; Nuñez L.; Alzate L.; Bayona S.; Rincón Y.; Charry A.; Salcedo G.; Tovar N.; Parra L.; Martínez L.; Castro D.; Sanchez I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Community acquired pneumonia (CAP) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality. Although corticosteroids have shown benefits in severe CAP, their usefulness in non severe cases remains uncertain. This study assessed the association between systemic corticosteroids and 30-day mortality in adults hospitalized with non severe CAP. A multicenter retrospective cohort was conducted including adults hospitalized with non severe CAP between 2010 and 2020 in Colombia. Patients whose index episode was nosocomial pneumonia, as well as those with immunosuppression or connective tissue disease and those requiring vasopressors or mechanical ventilation, were excluded. Propensity score matching (1:1) was applied, and survival was analyzed using Kaplan Meier curves, including evaluations by corticosteroid type, dose and duration. A total of 2821 patients were included, with an overall 30-day mortality of 7.6%. Of these, 507 patients (18.0%) received corticosteroids, with a mortality rate of 10.4%, whereas the remaining 2314 patients who did not receive corticosteroids had a mortality rate of 7.0%. The propensity score-matched cohort included 448 patients (224 in each group). In the matched analysis, 30-day mortality was 14.3% among patients who received corticosteroids compared with 10.7% among those who did not. Before matching, patients treated with corticosteroids were older and had a higher burden of respiratory symptoms and comorbidities. After matching, baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups. After propensity score matching, no significant association was observed between corticosteroid use and 30-day mortality (average treatment effect on the treated [ATET] 0.031, 95% CI − 0.040 to 0.102; p = 0.389). The ATET estimates the absolute risk difference; an ATET of 0.031 corresponds to an absolute difference of 3.1 percentage points in 30-day mortality. Additionally, no significant differences in survival were found according to corticosteroid type, dose, or treatment duration. In adults with non-severe CAP, the use of systemic corticosteroids did not demonstrate a statistically significant difference in 30-day mortality.

Article.Title: A BERT-based multi-task learning framework for social media opinion mining with risk detection
Article.Authors: Liu W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a BERT-based multi-task learning framework for social media mining and risk detection. Unlike traditional open-loop architectures, the proposed system establishes a closed-loop feedback mechanism among crawling, analysis, and alerting modules, focusing on high-accuracy negative sentiment detection for social risk detection. A dataset of 4,238 texts is constructed, covering eight topic categories and three sentiment labels. A BERT-based multi-task framework with shared encoder and two task-specific heads jointly optimizes topic classification and sentiment analysis. Training uses AdamW (learning rate 2e-5, batch size 16, max length 128) for three epochs. The multi-task BERT model achieves 97.97% F1 for topic classification and 99.89% F1 for sentiment analysis. Negative sentiment detection reaches 100% accuracy. Compared to single-task models (98.34% and 99.76%), the multi-task model maintains comparable topic performance while improving sentiment analysis. Removing pre-training fine-tuning reduces training time by 7.9% with stable performance. The model performs two tasks in one inference, reducing deployment complexity while enabling reliable negative sentiment detection for social media opinion monitoring.

Article.Title: Cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment of pasteurized milk production in Uzbekistan identifies environmental hotspots and improvement opportunities
Article.Authors: Samanian N.; Hesarinejad M.; Sadullayev U.; Egamberdieva D.
Article.Abstract: Dairy production is an important component of Uzbekistan's food system but is associated with environmental burdens. This study presents a cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment (LCA) of pasteurized milk production in Uzbekistan to quantify environmental impacts, identify hotspots, evaluate uncertainty, and assess environmental improvement options. A case-based inventory informed by farm records and national production data was developed for 1000 kg of pasteurized milk at the factory gate, covering feed production, dairy farming, transport, processing, and packaging. Environmental impacts were assessed using ReCiPe 2016 Midpoint (H). Global warming potential (GWP), characterized water consumption, terrestrial acidification, freshwater eutrophication, and fossil resource scarcity were 1537.8 kg CO 2 -eq, 1509.5 m 3 , 13.40 kg SO 2 -eq, 0.775 kg P-eq, and 158.1 kg oil-eq, respectively. Dairy-farm activities were the largest GWP contributor (46.6%), while feed production accounted for all characterized water consumption and dominated freshwater eutrophication (81.8%). Feed production and dairy-farm activities contributed 52.9% and 47.1% of terrestrial acidification, respectively, whereas packaging dominated fossil resource scarcity (65.8%). Monte Carlo analysis quantified model uncertainty, while sensitivity analysis identified methane/manure emissions as the main GWP uncertainty driver, irrigation demand for water consumption, fertilizer nutrient losses for acidification and eutrophication, and packaging factors for fossil resource scarcity. The integrated inventory-level sustainability scenario reduced GWP, water consumption, acidification, eutrophication, and fossil resource scarcity by 23.9%, 47.5%, 25.0%, 25.0%, and 4.5%, respectively. These findings support impact-specific strategies for improving the environmental sustainability of the assessed dairy production system and provide evidence relevant to dairy-sector improvement in Uzbekistan.

Article.Title: Field evaluation of biodegradation of boscalid and kresoxim-methyl in grape leaves by plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria
Article.Authors: Kayaaslan Z.; Balkan T.; Belguzar S.; Dag S.; Sadighfard S.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated the potential of plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) to enhance the dissipation of boscalid and kresoxim-methyl residues in grape leaves under field conditions. The experiment was conducted in a vineyard in Tokat, Türkiye, using the ‘Narince’ ( Vitis vinifera L.) grape variety. Boscalid and kresoxim-methyl were applied prior to harvest, followed by the application of A cinetobacter calcoaceticus , Enterobacter cloacae , Pseudomonas putida , and their combined treatment. Pesticide residues were determined using a validated QuEChERS extraction method coupled with LC–MS/MS analysis. Dissipation kinetics were evaluated using the double first-order in parallel (DFOP) model. PGPR application enhanced pesticide residue dissipation, with the combined bacterial treatment showing the shortest overall DT50 for both active ingredients. The overall DT50 of boscalid decreased from 24.97 days in the control to 18.42 days with the combined treatment, while that of kresoxim-methyl decreased from 3.17 to 1.68 days. At the 14-day pre-harvest interval, the combined treatment resulted in significantly lower residues of both boscalid and kresoxim-methyl than the control. These findings indicate that PGPR application, particularly the combined bacterial treatment, has potential as a complementary approach for enhancing pesticide residue dissipation in grape leaves under vineyard conditions. Further studies are required to elucidate the underlying mechanisms, characterize transformation products, and evaluate their toxicological significance and the consistency of the approach across different seasons and vineyard conditions.

Article.Title: Effects of organic nutrient sources and NPK fertilizer on soil fertility, yield, and rhizome quality of ginger
Article.Authors: Hsu C.; Al-Assi G.; Peyghan A.; Mahariq I.; Latipova M.; Begmatova D.; Imanov H.; Natarajan V.; Bhutto J.; Islam S.; Agbede T.
Article.Abstract: Soil fertility improvement using locally available nutrient sources is essential for sustainable ginger production in low-input tropical agroecosystems. A two-year field study was conducted in 2023 and 2024 at two sites in Owo, Ondo State, southwestern Nigeria, to evaluate the comparative effects of animal manures, green biomass amendments and NPK fertilizer on soil properties, growth, yield and rhizome quality of ginger ( Zingiber officinale Roscoe). Eight treatments comprising pig manure, cow dung, poultry manure, goat manure, Tithonia diversifolia , Chromolaena odorata , NPK 15-15-15 fertilizer and an unfertilized control were arranged in a randomized complete block design with three replications. All nutrient sources were applied at an equivalent rate of 120 kg N ha − 1 . Data were subjected to analysis of variance, and treatment means were separated using Duncan’s multiple range test at p ≤ 0.05. Organic amendments generally increased soil pH, organic matter, total N, available P and exchangeable K, Ca and Mg, while reducing bulk density and improving soil moisture compared with the control and NPK fertilizer. Poultry manure produced the highest rhizome yields of 20.5 and 21.8 t ha − 1 in 2023 and 2024, respectively, and generally recorded the highest growth, dry matter, leaf nutrient concentrations and rhizome protein, ash, fat, oleoresin and mineral contents, whereas carbohydrate and fibre contents were greatest in the control. Tithonia diversifolia and Chromolaena odorata generally ranked next to poultry manure. Organic amendments therefore improved soil fertility, ginger productivity and rhizome quality more effectively than sole NPK fertilizer in the forest-savanna transition zone of southwest Nigeria.

Article.Title: Musculoskeletal disorders and ergonomic risk factors among petrochemical control room operators with health promotion and intervention strategies
Article.Authors: Rahgoshay N.; Nodooshan H.; Rezaeikhah A.; Daneshmandi H.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to assess musculoskeletal and ergonomic risk, identify demographic, occupational, lifestyle, and biomechanical characteristics associated with these outcomes, and develop and prioritize ergonomic intervention strategies for petrochemical control room operators. This cross-sectional study was conducted in 2025 among 210 male control room operators from an Iranian petrochemical complex using census sampling. Data were collected using the Demographic/Occupational Questionnaire, Persian International Physical Activity Questionnaire (P-IPAQ), Persian Örebro Musculoskeletal Pain Screening Questionnaire (P-ÖMSQ), and Persian Ergonomic Screening and Priority Tool (P-ESPT), complemented by objective postural and plantar pressure assessments. The P-ÖMSQ was used to classify participants according to P-ÖMSQ risk categories, with scores ≥ 90 categorized as moderate-to-high risk. Data were analyzed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) software, version 20.0, with descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression. A P-ÖMSQ score within the moderate-to-high risk categories (≥ 90) was observed in 27% of participants, while 78% were classified as having moderate-to-high ergonomic risk. Multivariable logistic regression showed that older age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 1.09, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.02–1.17, p = 0.014), higher body mass index (BMI) (aOR = 1.15, 95% CI = 1.04–1.27, p = 0.006), and longer job tenure (aOR = 1.98, 95% CI = 1.01–3.89, p = 0.047) were independently associated with higher odds of being classified in the moderate-to-high-risk P-ÖMSQ category. Lower physical activity was significantly associated with a higher prevalence of forward head posture, thoracic hyperkyphosis, lateral pelvic tilt, and pes planus ( p < 0.05). Objective biomechanical abnormalities were also significantly associated with higher P-ÖMSQ-based and P-ESPT-based risk categories ( p < 0.05). Based on the study findings, 20 ergonomic intervention strategies were proposed and prioritized through a stakeholder-informed participatory process. Older age, higher body mass index, and longer job tenure were associated with higher odds of being classified in the moderate-to-high-risk P-ÖMSQ category, while lower physical activity was associated with selected postural abnormalities among petrochemical control room operators. Several objective biomechanical abnormalities were also associated with P-ÖMSQ-based and P-ESPT-based risk categories. These findings may inform the prioritization of workplace ergonomic interventions; however, the proposed interventions were not evaluated in the present study, and their effectiveness should be assessed in future longitudinal and interventional studies.

Article.Title: Securing real-time traffic analytics with a privacy-preserving edge and cloud computing framework
Article.Authors: Avazov K.; Kalpeyeva Z.; Uskenbayeva R.; Kassymova A.; Tursunova S.; Kurbonalieva D.; Abdusalomov A.; Cho Y.
Article.Abstract: The recent demand for real-time traffic management in urban environments has led to the adoption of edge and cloud computing, which improve the efficiency, scalability, and security of traffic analytics. Nevertheless, the privacy and confidentiality of traffic data remain important issues. In this study, a privacy-sensitive real-time traffic analytics system is proposed that combines edge computing for local-area data processing and cloud computing for large-scale analytics. This system uses blockchain, encryption, and differential privacy to safeguard sensitive traffic information and ensure information integrity and confidentiality. The proposed system was evaluated through a set of simulation experiments and compared with existing models, namely BFRT, FedTSE, FLAGCN, and VehiCast. The results indicate that the suggested system is more successful at reducing latency, power consumption, and load balancing, and at improving data security, achieving 30% latency reduction and 15-30% power reduction. In addition, the system was highly scalable, able to process an increasing number of edge devices and cloud servers without significant performance impairment. The work overall offers a scalable, robust real-time traffic control platform and insight into integrating the edge-cloud computing system into intelligent transportation systems (ITS) with privacy-preserving technologies.

Article.Title: Spatial, spatiotemporal, and epidemiological patterns of animal bites in the population covered by Torbat Heydariyeh University of Medical Sciences, Iran, 2015–2025
Article.Authors: Maleki Z.; Dehghani A.; Etesamirad M.; Yazdansetad Z.; Khatibi R.
Article.Abstract: Animal bites pose a significant public health concern due to rabies risk and associated health and economic burdens. This study aimed to characterize the epidemiological, spatial, and spatiotemporal patterns of animal-bite cases among the population covered by Torbat Heydariyeh University of Medical Sciences, Iran, from 2015 to 2025. This retrospective registry-based epidemiological study included all recorded animal-bite cases ( n = 12,079) at rabies prevention and treatment centers in Torbat Heydariyeh County, Razavi Khorasan Province, Iran, over a 11-year period. Data on demographics, animal type, incident location, and anatomical site were analyzed using SPSS 26. Independent t-tests, chi-square tests, one-way ANOVA, and the Cochran–Armitage trend test were used to assess incidence trends. The Significance level was set at 0.05. The crude incidence rate of animal bites showed an overall increasing trend during 2015–2025, with fluctuations over the study period. After a decline during 2020–2021, the incidence rate increased substantially, reaching its highest level in 2024 (513.36 per 100,000 population), followed by a slight decrease in 2025 (475.83 per 100,000 population). Dogs accounted for 83.70% of bites, followed by cats (15.70%). Seasonal incidence peaked in spring (31.80%), followed by summer (29.80%), and was lowest in winter (17.20%). Thighs and legs were the most common anatomical sites (57.50%), and single injuries accounted for 59.60% of cases. Males accounted for 78.00% and rural residents for 65.60% of the cases. Among 11,469 animal-bite cases, six deaths (0.10%) were recorded. Annual incidence increased by 16.33 cases per 100,000 population per year (β = 16.33; 95% CI: 7.13–25.53; p = 0.003). Animal bites remain an important public health concern, with an overall increasing trend in incidence during the study period. Males and rural residents accounted for a higher proportion of reported cases, and dogs were the main biting animals. These findings highlight the need for sustained preventive strategies, public education, and targeted interventions to reduce the burden of animal bites.

Article.Title: Integrated risk prediction for opioid overdose: combining genetic and socioeconomic factors
Article.Authors: Lei M.; Yuan Y.
Article.Abstract: A multidimensional prediction model integrating genetic and socioeconomic factors was developed and validated to assess the risk of opioid overdose, aiming to facilitate individualized risk estimation and inform early clinical identification and preventive strategies. In this retrospective study, 340 patients with a history of opioid use were enrolled. Participants were randomly allocated to a training set ( n = 238) or a validation set ( n = 102) in a 7:3 ratio. Candidate variables, including genetic variants, socioeconomic determinants, clinical parameters, and comorbidities, were initially screened using univariate analysis. Subsequently, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression and multivariable logistic regression were applied for variable selection and identification of independent predictors. Four machine learning models—random forest, support vector machine, k-nearest neighbors, and gradient boosting machine –were constructed using the final seven predictors. Model performance was evaluated based on the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Model interpretability was enhanced using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values. Seven independent risk factors for opioid overdose were identified ( P < 0.05). Among these, a history of prior overdose showed the strongest association (odds ratio = 3.192). The random forest model demonstrated superior performance, with an AUC of 0.879 in the training set and 0.774 in the validation set. Its calibration curve was closest to the ideal line. Furthermore, DCA indicated a higher net benefit for the random forest model across a 10–30% risk threshold range. SHAP analysis confirmed daily morphine milligram equivalents and prior overdose history as the most contributory features, aligning with the logistic regression results. An integrated risk prediction model for opioid overdose was successfully developed and validated. The random forest algorithm exhibited optimal discriminative ability, calibration, and clinical utility, providing a tool for individualized risk assessment to guide precision prevention.

Article.Title: A machine learning-based platform for predicting the potential energy of small molecules
Article.Authors: Farcas A.; Pernes P.; Baloi A.; Belean B.
Article.Abstract: Accurate estimation of molecular potential energy after energy minimization is vital for the rational design of targeted therapeutics. In this study, we present a machine learning platform that leverages sophisticated neural network architectures to predict the potential energy of small molecules. Accurate prediction of molecular potential energy can facilitate the computational characterization of drug- and gene-delivery-related molecules and support molecular modeling workflows. Our methodology involves designing and evaluating deep learning models, including convolutional neural network–bidirectional long short-term memory architectures, with and without multihead attention mechanisms. These models are trained on a comprehensive dataset comprising small molecules structures. By utilizing atom-wise sequential representations that preserve key geometric and chemical information, our approach effectively estimates potential energies and surpasses traditional descriptor-based machine learning methods. The integration of attention mechanisms enhances model generalization by capturing complex structural relationships, thereby streamlining virtual screening processes. Comparative analyses against existing benchmarks demonstrate the efficacy of sequence-based neural networks in molecular energy prediction, paving the way for more efficient drug discovery and polymer informatics. This platform offers a robust, computationally efficient tool for virtual screening and energy estimation of candidate molecules, supporting the advancement of targeted therapeutics through rapid molecule prioritization based on predicted potential energies.

Article.Title: Contextualizing CNN attribution maps using predefined image-derived descriptors in medicinal plant seed classification
Article.Authors: Chin S.; Park Y.; Jung D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deep learning classifiers can achieve high predictive performance in medicinal plant seed image classification, but prediction accuracy alone does not clarify which visual properties are linked to model responses. This issue is particularly relevant for visually similar medicinal plant seeds, related taxa, and potential substitutes that may share overlapping morphology. Here, we analyzed RGB images from five medicinal plant seed classes by comparing CNN attribution maps with predefined image-derived descriptor maps within the seed foreground. ResNet50, EfficientNet-B0, and ConvNeXt-Small showed near-ceiling classification performance under controlled imaging and preprocessing conditions, and zero-baseline absolute Integrated Gradients (IG) maps from ConvNeXt-Small were used as the primary attribution reference. Among the tested descriptor maps, LAB L, Brightness, and fast Fourier transform (FFT) low-pass showed the highest positive foreground-restricted spatial associations with IG attribution maps. Descriptor summary feature classification further showed that foreground-level descriptor statistics contained class-discriminative visual information. The analysis organizes CNN attribution patterns within reproducible image-derived visual contexts in medicinal plant seed image classification.

Article.Title: Integrated transcriptomic and clinical analyses reveal the prognostic relevance of GPC3 and a putative ceRNA-associated relationship in gastric cancer
Article.Authors: Li Z.; Liu Y.; Chen G.; Sun L.
Article.Abstract: To investigate the expression pattern and prognostic significance of glypican-3 (GPC3) in gastric cancer (GC) and identify its potential upstream non-coding RNA regulatory network. Transcriptomic data from TCGA-STAD and GEO datasets were used to compare GPC3 expression between GC and non-tumor gastric tissues, with validation using GEPIA. The prognostic value of GPC3 was evaluated using TCGA-STAD, GEPIA, and Kaplan–Meier Plotter. An independent clinical cohort from our center was included for immunohistochemical validation, and associations between GPC3 expression and clinicopathological features were assessed using chi-square or exact tests, as appropriate. Upstream miRNAs targeting GPC3 were predicted using starBase and screened by correlation and survival analyses. Candidate lncRNAs were further identified by integrating starBase and miRNet to identify a putative non-coding RNA regulatory relationship. GPC3 was significantly upregulated in GC tissues compared with non-tumor gastric tissues in TCGA-STAD, GSE33335, GSE54129, and GEPIA. High GPC3 expression was associated with worse overall survival and progression-free survival. In the independent cohort, GPC3 protein expression was elevated in GC tissues and showed exploratory associations with advanced T stage (P < 0.001), N stage (P = 0.014), TNM stage (P = 0.013), and perineural invasion (P = 0.041). Among 15 candidate miRNAs, hsa-miR-96-5p showed the strongest negative correlation with GPC3 (r=-0.32614, P < 0.001). LINC02381 was positively correlated with GPC3 (r = 0.30255, P < 0.001), negatively correlated with hsa-miR-96-5p (r=-0.15184, P < 0.01), and its high expression was associated with poor prognosis. GPC3 is overexpressed in GC and associated with poor prognosis. Bioinformatic analyses further suggested a putative LINC02381/miR-96-5p/GPC3 regulatory relationship associated with GPC3 expression in GC.

Article.Title: Application of computer simulation technology in the optimization and performance evaluation of smart sports teaching systems in universities
Article.Authors: Zhao Y.; Khayatnezhad S.
Article.Abstract: This study proposes a computer-simulation-driven framework for optimizing and evaluating smart sports teaching systems in universities. Using MHEALTH as the main multimodal wearable-sensor dataset, and UCI HAR Smartphone and Daily and Sports Activities as external validation datasets, the framework integrates wearable-sensor preprocessing, window-level feature construction, activity recognition, teaching-state indicator construction, sensor-ablation analysis, scenario simulation and optimization, ...statistical validation, and computational implementation-feasibility assessment. Activity Load Index, movement stability, and a sensor-derived safety proxy were constructed to translate acceleration, gyroscope, magnetometer, and ECG signals into interpretable teaching-state representations. To address subject-dependence and potential overestimation from a fixed train/test split, classification performance was re-evaluated using leave-one-subject-out validation. In the realistic MHEALTH setting including the dominant null class, Gaussian Naive Bayes achieved the highest mean Macro F1 of 0.652, while tuned Extra Trees achieved an accuracy of 0.819 and a Macro F1 of 0.563. In the activity-only setting, Random Forest and Extra Trees achieved mean Macro F1 scores of approximately 0.95, indicating strong but not universally perfect subject-independent recognition. External validation produced Extra Trees accuracies of 0.941 on UCI HAR and 0.964 on Daily Sports. Sensitivity analyses showed that the principal high-load activity assignments remained stable under plausible variations in Activity Load Index weights and thresholds. Formal constrained optimization identified a 25% low, 65% moderate, 8% high, and 2% very-high state allocation as the utility-maximizing solution, corresponding to a 13.7% simulated utility gain over the observed baseline. These results support the use of the proposed framework as an interpretable, subject-independent decision-support approach for evaluating wearable-sensor-based sports teaching scenarios.

Article.Title: Oriented SAR ship detection with scattering-inspired cross-scale fusion and localization quality estimation
Article.Authors: Li W.; Wang L.; Gao X.; Xue G.; Pang J.
Article.Abstract: Oriented ship detection in complex nearshore and harbor SAR imagery is challenged by nonhomogeneous sea clutter and land-based strong scatterers, attenuation of weak ship structures during downsampling, and mismatch between classification confidence and oriented-box localization quality. We propose PSF-LQE, a scattering-inspired intensity-domain network with four functionally complementary modules. SCS extracts absolute scattering residuals against a locally smoothed background and reconstructs features via confidence gating, suppressing sea clutter before false responses propagate to deeper layers. PTE jointly encodes local residuals, channel-wise intensity contrast, and directional responses, preserving the scattering centers, contours, and heading-dependent structures of small weak ships throughout hierarchical encoding. A bidirectional neck built on MPCA and MPCA-Down generates channel gates from concatenated adjacent-scale descriptors before upsampling and downsampling fusion, calibrating channel reliability so that deep clutter semantics and shallow noise do not contaminate each other. LQE derives a localization-quality bias from four-side discrete boundary distributions and uses it as an additive re-ranking cue on the classification scores, so that candidates whose boundary distributions are more concentrated tend to rank higher, without claiming that the scores themselves are calibrated. The network requires no polarimetric channels, scattering matrices, or decomposition features and has a compact 3.8 million parameters. Experimental results show that PSF-LQE achieves 93.8% $$mAP_{50}$$ on HRSID, corresponding to absolute gains of 19.6 percentage points over the evaluated baseline. On SRSDD, it achieves 73.6%, corresponding to gains of 14.9 percentage points. Cumulative ablations and qualitative response visualizations are consistent with the intended roles of the modules.

Article.Title: Autonomous labeling of surgical resection margins using a foundation model
Article.Authors: Yang X.; Aydin M.; Lu Y.; Selcuk S.; Bai B.; Zhang Y.; Birkeland A.; Haran T.; Atlan K.; Ehrlich K.; Bec J.; Marcu L.; Pillar N.; Ozcan A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Assessing resection margins is central to pathological specimen evaluation and has profound implications for patient outcomes. Failure to achieve clear margins significantly increases the risk of local recurrence and may necessitate adjuvant therapies such as chemotherapy or radiotherapy. However, margin assessment faces multiple procedural challenges, including human error during manual tissue margin labeling (physical inking), tissue shrinkage and distortion from fixation and processing, and thermal damage from cautery that obscures cellular features, all of which can compromise accurate margin identification. We demonstrate a virtual inking network (VIN) that localizes the resection margin on whole-slide images (WSIs), producing a standardized, ink-free margin map that helps mitigate limitations of physical inking and enables accurate and reproducible margin measurements. VIN uses a frozen foundation model as the feature extractor and a compact two-layer multilayer perceptron trained for patch-level classification of cautery-consistent features. The dataset comprised 120 hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained slides from 12 human tonsil tissue blocks, resulting in ~ 2 TB of uncompressed raw image data, where a board-certified pathologist provided boundary annotations. In blind testing with 20 slides from previously unseen blocks, VIN produced coherent margin overlays that qualitatively aligned with expert annotations across serial sections. Quantitatively, region-level accuracy was ~ 73.3% across the test set, with errors largely confined to limited areas that did not disrupt continuity of the whole-slide margin map. Our results suggest that VIN is capable of capturing cautery-related histomorphology, offering a potential ink-free margin delineation for digital pathology workflows. These proof-of-concept results warrant further validation of VIN as a tool for margin localization in larger, clinically representative cohorts.

Article.Title: Longitudinal metal mixture interactions and dyslipidemia in a prospective nested case control study
Article.Authors: Qiao G.; Jia J.; Di Y.; Bai Z.; Xiong L.; Fu J.; Zhang Y.; Geng X.; Wang Y.; Gao C.; Hu H.; Guo M.; Ma J.; Hu M.; Zhang X.; Wang G.; Sun J.
Article.Abstract: Dyslipidemia affects over 40% of adults aged 50 years or older and contributes substantially to cardiovascular mortality, yet prospective evidence on metal mixtures, nonlinear dose–response relationships, and metal–metal interactions in community-dwelling older adults remains limited. In this prospective nested case–control study (2019–2023) within the Yinchuan Community-Dwelling Elderly Cohort, 436 incident dyslipidemia cases and 872 age-, sex-, and BMI-matched controls were included, and 13 urinary metals were quantified by microwave-assisted acid digestion followed by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS), expressed as µg/g creatinine. Single-metal logistic models showed positive dose–response trends for copper and cadmium (P for trend < 0.05), elevated risks for molybdenum (OR = 1.44) and arsenic (OR = 1.43) in the third quartile, and a protective association for zinc in the second quartile (OR = 0.68). Machine learning prioritized zinc, copper, cobalt, strontium, and vanadium, and SHAP revealed nonlinear patterns, including J-shaped associations for copper and vanadium and a biphasic pattern for cobalt. Weighted quantile sum regression indicated that low-concentration metal mixtures were associated with increased dyslipidemia risk, and Bayesian kernel machine regression suggested potential Cu–Sr and V–Zn interactions, which generalized additive interaction models supported on an exploratory basis; these models also suggested that exercise attenuated zinc-associated risk, whereas smoking and alcohol amplified copper and zinc toxicity and meat-based diets exacerbated strontium and cobalt risks. Collectively, metal exposures, individually and as mixtures, are associated with dyslipidemia risk in older adults through nonlinear and interactive mechanisms, supporting their potential relevance to precision public health.

Article.Title: Analysis of nine years of safety monitoring data from a roller-compacted concrete gravity dam in a high-altitude cold region
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Zhao J.; Yan Y.; Zhang X.; Zhu Z.; Zhang F.
Article.Abstract: Long-term monitoring records from roller-compacted concrete (RCC) gravity dams in cold regions are scarce, although freeze–thaw cycling and large seasonal temperature ranges act there together with hydrostatic loading. This study analyzes 9.1 years of daily records (2016–2025) from 190 instruments on a 71 m RCC gravity dam in Xinjiang, China. Correlations are reported with seasonality controls and a significance criterion that allows for serial correlation, and the monitored changes are related to the sliding stability of the dam. Maximum downstream displacement is 18.71 mm. Its seasonality-controlled association with reservoir level is moderate (partial r = 0.26–0.58), and its multi-year baseline, after rising by about 3–4 mm over 2017–2021, has not risen since. Foundation uplift head stays below the reservoir level, decreases downstream and shows no upward trend, and no monitored change points to reduced sliding stability. Concrete strain follows local concrete temperature (raw r = 0.82–0.94). Stresses estimated with a code-specified modulus, no material tests being available, are order-of-magnitude values (1.1–3.7 MPa compression), and one tensile strain excursion is flagged for inspection. The annual response is reversible, and no monitored quantity shows cumulative deterioration; surface freeze–thaw damage is beyond the reach of the embedded instruments.

Article.Title: Integrating ventilation assessments with IoT monitoring to evaluate indoor air quality in elementary schools of San Luis Potosí, México
Article.Authors: Ruiz-Correa S.; López-Revilla R.; Riego-Ruiz L.; Díaz G.; Boussetta K.; Gómez-Hernández N.; Dandoush A.; Amour L.; Marmolejo-Cossío F.; Rosales C.; Cárdenas-Juárez M.; Rivera-Aguilar J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Indoor air quality (IAQ) is neglected in schools of the Global South. Carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) and particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) are indicators of ventilation and exposure risk to airborne infections, respectively. We deployed Air Sentinel , a decentralized mobile-driven IoT network, to monitor these indicators across 106 spaces in 53 elementary schools in the San Luis Potosí Metropolitan Area, Mexico. Machine learning was used to forecast CO 2 and PM 2.5 concentrations one hour in advance, and the Wells-Riley model, based on CO 2 concentration, to estimate airborne infection probability (AIP). IAQ was poor, acceptable, and excellent in 27.3%, 36.4%, and 67.2% of the classrooms, respectively. During the cold season, 97.67% of the classroom CO 2 levels were typical (400–1000 ppm); in the hot season, 67.67% of the classroom CO 2 levels were typical, and 1.19% exceeded the high exposure threshold (> 2000 ppm). Classroom CO 2 dynamics exhibited low temporal synchrony. The strongest forecasting performance for CO 2 occurred in the hot season, but the PM 2.5 forecast failed in either season while AIP increased during the first two hours of class in both seasons. The successful CO 2 forecasting model has potential for real-time IAQ management in the cold season. The failure to forecast PM 2.5 levels suggests that localized sources drive their dynamics. We conclude that the Air Sentinel network is a convenient classroom IAQ monitor in the Global South.

Article.Title: Dysregulated nitric oxide signaling and its association with arginase-2 and fatty acid synthase in obesity and related comorbidities
Article.Authors: Taha A.; El-Bassossy H.; Eassa S.; Sabry S.; Elbatreek M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Obesity is a global health epidemic, projected to affect 38% of adults as overweight and 20% as obese by 2030, usually accompanied by comorbidities such as hypertension and diabetes. This study aimed to identify a disease module related to nitric oxide (NO) signaling in obesity and its comorbidities. We used computational network analysis to identify a nitric oxide synthase (NOS)-related module using NOS2 and NOS3 as seeds. A case-control study ( n = 125) categorized participants into healthy controls and four obese groups: obesity alone, and obesity with diabetes, hypertension, or both. Groups were balanced for age, gender, and smoking. Plasma NO (nitrite via colorimetry), arginase 2 (ARG2), and fatty acid synthase (FASN) were measured via ELISA. In silico analysis identified FASN and ARG2 as key proteins interacting with NOS enzymes. Clinical data revealed significant differences in plasma NO (as nitrite), ARG2, and FASN across groups. Notably, Patients with obesity, diabetes, and hypertension had the lowest median (IQR) nitrite levels at 26.09 (25.31–26.99) µmol/L ( p < 0.001). The obese-diabetic group exhibited reduced median (IQR) ARG2 [5.18 (4.49–7) mU/ml] and FASN [13.8 (10.91–15.43) ng/ml], whereas the obese-diabetic-hypertensive group showed elevated levels of both markers. Nitrite correlated negatively with ARG2 and FASN, while ARG2 and FASN correlated positively. Multivariate regression identified that plasma nitrite is significantly associated with the coexistence of obesity, diabetes, and hypertension. These findings highlight the intricate interplay between NO signaling, ARG2, and FASN in obesity-related comorbidities. Modulating these interconnected pathways may offer novel therapeutic targets for metabolic diseases.

Article.Title: Knowledge distillation-based lightweight generative large language models for standardized quality control of Chinese radiology reports
Article.Authors: Jiang D.; Han X.; Xu K.; Li C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Radiological reports, which document radiologists’ imaging observations and diagnostic conclusions from CT, X-ray and MRI scans, deliver core imaging evidence for clinical diagnosis and therapeutic planning. Inaccurate or disordered reports may lead to misdiagnosis and delayed intervention, posing risks to patient safety. Radiological reports are essential for clinical decision-making, yet Chinese radiology reports frequently exhibit logical inconsistencies, incomplete content, non-standardized descriptions, and formatting errors, while manual quality control remains time-consuming and inconsistent. Large teacher models can provide task-specific supervision but are difficult to deploy locally, whereas smaller models require adaptation to this clinical text task. We developed a teacher-supervised, locally deployable 4B language-model system for rule-based textual quality control of Chinese radiology reports.Among the three evaluated teacher APIs, Doubao-seed1.6-non-thinking achieved the highest macro-precision ,0.94, under the study's precision-prioritized selection.Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 emerged as the optimal student model, achieving an average precision of 0.90, recall of 0.49, and F1 score of 0.62, with inference speed improved by over 40-fold. Real-world clinical validation demonstrated that the lightweight model attains a precision of 0.74 in authentic clinical scenarios while retaining high overall performance, satisfying the deployment demands of on-site clinical institutions.

Article.Title: CAUSE: a context-aware user security enhancement model for trustworthy consumer immersive applications
Article.Authors: Sharma S.; Singh J.; Gupta A.; Alzubi A.; Sehra S.; Ali F.
Article.Abstract: Consumer-focused virtual immersive environments including AR and VR metaverse applications are creating new ways for people to interact, collaborate, and engage in commerce. Simultaneously, user privacy, trust, and security are also at great risk in these environments. This paper proposes the Context-Aware User Security Enhancement (CAUSE) model, which is a policy-based, user-centric, comprehensive, and real-time protection mechanism against such threats. For proactive threat detection and user interaction management, CAUSE incorporates a personalized AI agent. Fine-grained control is exercised by the user through user-defined security policies, interpreted by the policy engine to support context-aware, scenario-based controls. To ensure interoperability across diverse immersive platforms, it envisages user-defined security policy migration and consistent enforcement. The simulation results show that CAUSE effectively addresses threats, caters to complex interaction scenarios and improves user safety in virtual immersive environments. In the simulated evaluation, the Decision Tree risk classifier achieved 94.45% overall accuracy for three-class risk classification and a High-Risk recall of 90.83%. CAUSE addresses some of the key issues with current user-security methods and contributes to the development of safer and more trustworthy consumer immersive environments.

Article.Title: Psychometric validation of the perceived digital well-being scale and digital well-being questionnaire among adolescents receiving psychiatric care
Article.Authors: Vera Cruz G.; Terzioğlu M.; Da Rosa C.; Khan R.; Khazaal Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Research on adolescents’ digital media use has largely focused on risks and negative mental health outcomes, while comparatively little attention has been paid to digital well-being, defined as individuals’ subjective experience of the benefits and drawbacks of digital engagement. Empirical validation of digital well-being measures remains scarce, particularly among adolescents receiving psychiatric care and in non-Western contexts. This study aimed (a) to examine the construct validity, internal reliability, and gender invariance of the Perceived Digital Well-being Scale (PDWS) and the Digital Well-being Questionnaire (DWBQ) in a clinical adolescent sample, and (b) to assess their convergent validity, including associations with problematic social media use. A total of 481 Turkish adolescents (aged 14–18 years) receiving psychiatric care completed self-report measures of digital well-being (PDWS, DWBQ), problematic social media use (Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale), anxiety and depression (PHQ-4), and life satisfaction (KIDSCREEN-10). Confirmatory factor analyses were conducted to test factorial structure and gender invariance. Internal consistency was assessed using Cronbach’s alpha and McDonald’s omega and other indicators; convergent validity was examined via correlation analyses. Confirmatory factor analyses supported the proposed multidimensional structures of both the PDWS and the DWBQ, with good/excellent model fit indices. All dimensions demonstrated satisfactory internal reliability. Gender invariance analyses indicated stable factor structures across male and female participants. Mean digital well-being scores were above the scale mid-points, despite participants’ clinical status. PDWS and DWBQ dimensions were positively intercorrelated and most dimensions were significantly and negatively associated with problematic social media use, supporting convergent validity. The findings demonstrate that digital well-being can be reliably and validly assessed among adolescents receiving psychiatric care. Results challenge deficit-oriented assumptions about clinical adolescents’ digital lives and support a more nuanced understanding of digital engagement that integrates both risks and resources.

Article.Title: Multi-view context learning for human-object interaction detection
Article.Authors: Abdusalomov A.; Xudoynazarov U.; Ruziev U.; Mukhiddinov M.; Nosir N.; Kutlimuratov A.; Oğurlu C.; Buriboev A.; Jeon H.
Article.Abstract: Understanding how humans interact with objects in complex visual scenes is fundamental to human-centric artificial intelligence. Yet, current Human-Object Interaction (HOI) detection frameworks often falter when faced with visual occlusions, vague interaction semantics, and scenarios that extend beyond predefined categories. We present Multi-View Context-Aware Disentangled Interaction Network (MCD-Inet), a unified framework designed to robustly detect HOIs under these challenging, open-world conditions. Our approach integrates a novel Multi-View Context Fusion mechanism that synthesizes fine grained spatial cues and broad semantic information across instance, interaction, and global levels. To decouple the learning of object localization from interaction semantics, we introduce a Disentangled Interaction Decoder, enabling clearer task specific representations. Complementing this, our Bilateral Knowledge Adaptation module bridges high-resolution spatial features from the visual backbone with abstract semantics from a pre-trained vision language model. To overcome the challenge of occluded interactions, we design an Occlusion-Robust Enhancement module, which extrapolates missing regions and mines contextual cues to recover interaction evidence. Finally, MCD-INet leverages multi-modal prompts incorporating both textual templates and visual exemplars to extend its detection capabilities to unseen HOI triplets. Extensive evaluations on HICO-DET, V-COCO, and the HICO-Ambiguous datasets confirm the superiority of our approach, achieving a new state-of-the-art mAP of 40.7% and demonstrating significant resilience in occluded and zero-shot scenarios. MCD-INet offers a powerful step toward generalizable, context-aware HOI detection in real-world visual environments.

Article.Title: Numerical approximation of nonlinear fractional dynamical systems for coastal wave modeling: rigorous analysis of convergence and computational efficiency
Article.Authors: Sidaoui R.; Damag F.; Saif A.; Alsharafi M.
Article.Abstract: In the present work, we study a family of nonlinear fractional dynamical systems and propose a numerical procedure based on the power series iterative method (PSIM). The proposed framework is based on the Atangana-Baleanu-Caputo (ABC) fractional derivative which is able to capture memory and nonlocal effects in dynamic processes. The method transforms the original fractional system into an equivalent integral representation and generates approximate solutions through an efficient iterative scheme. We also discuss the analytical properties of the proposed method such as convergence to the exact solution under appropriate conditions and stability to small perturbations. To illustrate its practical utility, we apply the method to the fractional Whitham-Broer-Kaup system (WBKS) for the purpose of coastal wave modeling, analyzing wave propagation, surface elevation dynamics and memory effects in shallow-water environments. The obtained results show that PSIM provides accurate approximations with fast convergence, thus serving as an efficient and reliable computational tool for nonlinear fractional dynamical systems and their applications in coastal hazard assessment.

Article.Title: A study of the mediating role of early maladaptive schemas in the effects of occupational stress on cognitive failures among mine workers
Article.Authors: Teimori-Boghsani G.; Asilian-Mahabadi H.; Fouladi-Dehaghi B.; Ahmadi O.; khavanin A.
Article.Abstract: Cognitive failures can be an important link between occupational stress and the occurrence of work-related accidents. On the other side, early maladaptive schemas can fundamentally affect cognitive processing and individuals' reactions to stressors. This study modeled the effects between occupational stress and cognitive failures using early maladaptive schemas as a mediating variable among mine workers. This cross-sectional study was carried out on 285 mine workers of eastern Iran. Data were collected by the Osipow occupational stress inventory, Occupational Cognitive Failure Questionnaire (OCFQ), and Young Schema Questionnaire Short Form. This study employed Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) techniques using SmartPLS 3 to analyze data. The results revealed that occupational stress had a significant positive direct effect on cognitive failures (β = 0.375, P < 0.001) and on most early maladaptive schemas domains, with the strongest effect on impaired autonomy and performance (β = 0.459, P < 0.001). Notably, occupational stress showed a significant negative association with impaired limits (β = -0.172, P = 0.004 ). In turn, cognitive failures were most strongly predicted by disconnection and rejection (β = 0.396, P < 0.001) and impaired autonomy and performance (β = 0.278, P < 0.001). Mediation analyses indicated that disconnection and rejection (β = 0.144, P < 0.001) and impaired autonomy and performance (β = 0.127, P < 0.001) served as significant indirect pathways linking occupational stress to cognitive failures. The findings confirmed that occupational stress increases cognitive failures. Moreover, by activating early maladaptive schemas of disconnection and rejection and impaired autonomy and performance, it also indirectly affects these failures. Therefore, mining work environments should pay attention to workers' mental health, as neglecting it can exacerbate maladaptive thought and behavioral patterns. It is recommended that organizational interventions, in addition to reducing workplace stressors, focus on identifying and modifying these schemas and enhancing workers' sense of competence to prevent the occurrence of cognitive failures.

Article.Title: Selenium nanoparticles enhance anticancer effects by modulating LAMP1, autophagic machinery and P53 expressions in colon cancer cells
Article.Authors: Al-Eidan A.; Tabl A.; Daha M.; Elawdan K.; Elakkad H.; Elshamy A.; Fatahy N.; Shoaib H.; Bassiouny K.; Guirgis A.; Khalil H.
Article.Abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most prevalent malignancies worldwide, with its incidence continuing to rise due to changes in lifestyle and dietary habits. Selenium, an essential trace element, possesses antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer properties, making it a promising therapeutic candidate for CRC. This study aimed to synthesize nanomodified Selenium (Nano-Selenium), compare its anticancer efficacy with conventional Selenium and Sorafenib, evaluate its cytotoxicity toward normal colon epithelial cells, and investigate its underlying molecular mechanisms in colon cancer cells. Nano-Selenium was synthesized by dissolving Selenium in an oil phase containing Span 80 as a stabilizing emulsifier, followed by high-pressure homogenization to generate nanoparticles with diameters below 100 nm. Automated microscopic analysis demonstrated particle sizes ranging from 10 to 50 nm for Nano-Selenium, whereas conventional Selenium particles measured approximately 1–3 μm. Zeta potential analysis confirmed the superior physicochemical stability of Nano-Selenium over a 24-hour period. The antiproliferative activity of Selenium, Nano-Selenium, and Sorafenib was evaluated using MTT assays in Caco-2, HT-29, and HCT-116 colon cancer cell lines and the normal colon epithelial cell line NCM-460. Nano-Selenium exhibited significantly greater antiproliferative activity against all colon cancer cell lines while displaying lower cytotoxicity toward normal cells than conventional Selenium and Sorafenib. The IC₅₀ values of Nano-Selenium were below 5 µM in all cancer cell lines, compared with approximately 10 µM for conventional Selenium. In contrast, the IC₅₀ values in NCM-460 cells were approximately 27 µM for Nano-Selenium, 16 µM for conventional Selenium, and 14.5 µM for Sorafenib. Sorafenib exhibited IC₅₀ values of 12.2, 9.25, and 7.5 µM in Caco-2, HT-29, and HCT-116 cells, respectively. Unlike Selenium and Sorafenib, treatment of Caco-2 cells with 5 µM Nano-Selenium markedly reduced cell viability while inducing only minimal membrane damage, as evidenced by limited lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release. Nano-Selenium significantly enhanced apoptosis by increasing early and late apoptotic populations, activating Caspase-3, upregulating the tumor suppressor p53, and downregulating lysosomal-associated membrane protein-1 (LAMP1). Furthermore, Nano-Selenium increased the expression of the autophagy-related proteins ATG5 and LC3B and disrupted autophagic flux, suggesting inhibition of lysosome–autophagosome fusion. ELISA analysis further demonstrated a time-dependent reduction in TNF-α levels accompanied by a marked increase in IL-6 levels. In conclusion, Nano-Selenium demonstrated superior anticancer efficacy and selectivity compared with conventional Selenium and Sorafenib by suppressing lysosomal function, disrupting autophagic flux, and activating p53-mediated apoptotic pathways while exerting minimal toxicity toward normal colon epithelial cells. These findings highlight Nano-Selenium as a promising therapeutic strategy for CRC. Keywords : Colon cancer, Nanomodified Selenium, LAMP1, P53, autophagy.

Article.Title: Fitting device-free crowd size estimation models using area-ratio scaled synthetic labels
Article.Authors: Janssens R.; Berkvens R.; Bellekens B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract As urbanization accelerates, the ability to accurately monitor crowd densities in public spaces has become essential for enhancing city efficiency, safety, and sustainability. Collecting reliable ground truth data on people counts in large-scale urban environments can be challenging. In this paper, we evaluate an experimental setup that uses device-free wireless sensing to estimate the number of people in an area by analyzing the attenuation of the communication link between the battery-powered sensor nodes of a Wireless Sensor Network (WSN). In this work, we propose a technique that synthesizes count labels based on manual ground truth counts in a smaller portion of the environment to fit a model for the entire environment, thereby simplifying the ground truth gathering process. When comparing the Mean Absolute Percentage Errors (MAPE) for the transformed “subzone-to-total” models, we observe a mean increase of 4.49 % compared to evaluations of models directly fitted on data from the total zone. When transforming between adjacent subzones, we observe a mean increase of 9.65 % compared to evaluations of models fitted directly on the target subzone’s ground truth data. When collecting ground truth data for the total zone is too difficult, labels synthesized via area-ratio scaling from one or more subzones can provide a viable alternative for fitting the estimation model.

Article.Title: Seasonally divergent early-warning indicators of Amazon hydrological change
Article.Authors: Poveda G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Variance, lag-1 autocorrelation, skewness, kurtosis and entropy are used as early-warning indicators of critical transitions, on the premise that systems losing stability fluctuate more widely and recover more slowly. We computed them for about 45 years of precipitation, evapotranspiration, soil moisture and extreme streamflow records across the Amazon Basin and its eight sub-basins, in wet (December–February) and dry (June–August) seasons, against the fraction expected by chance under stationary surrogates. Wet-season change concentrates in the south: precipitation along the western Solimões–Juruá–Purus–Madeira corridor, and root-zone soil moisture in Purus and Tapajós, where 60% and 44% of the area show four or more concordant indicators against 6% expected by chance. Dry-season change shifts eastward: the Xingu–Tapajós arc, least affected in the wet season, becomes the most affected in precipitation, while minimum streamflows give the strongest result of all, five indicators aligning at 14% of gauges, twenty-six times chance. Evapotranspiration is weakest in both seasons. Resolving the soil column by layer places the soil moisture signal at 7–100 cm depth, and the areas flagged in the two seasons avoid one another, overlapping over 2.9% of the basin against 3.8% under spatial independence. Soil moisture declines over most of the basin in the dry season; in the wet season, the areas where it now fluctuates least are not those drying fastest. The flagged areas are smaller than in an aggregated, sign-based analysis because each indicator is gated on a significant trend, the seasons are resolved separately, and every fraction is read against chance; this stricter accounting narrows the flagged area while sharpening its location, and should not be read as indicating a lesser degree of change where indicators do converge.

Article.Title: A quantum-informed gradient catalyst layer architecture for freeze-resistant proton exchange membrane fuel cell cold startup via DFT guided machine learning
Article.Authors: Aurangzeb M.; Li J.; Shusheng X.; Xinwei L.; Khalid M.; Dafalla A.; Abbas Z.; Qazi H.; Haq M.; Rehman A.
Article.Abstract: Cold start represents a critical barrier to automotive PEMFC commercialization, as product water from the oxygen reduction reaction freezes rapidly at sub-zero temperatures, blocking catalyst active sites and transport pathways. This work proposes a quantum-mechanically guided hydrophilic-hydrophobic gradient catalyst layer architecture optimized for freeze-resistant cold startup at − 20 °C. We utilize the Density Functional Theory (DFT) results to use N-doped carbon and MoS 2 quantum dots useful interfaces to perform a systematic analysis of the water binding energies, ice nucleation barrier, and diffusion coefficient of a surface on the material. The Q-ICE-CL framework follows a five-stage workflow: (1) DFT quantum-mechanical calculations establish water-surface interaction descriptors for N-doped carbon/MoS₂ interfaces; (2) hybrid XGBoost-GNN machine learning models trained on DFT data enable inference-time composition screening within the established design space; (3) gradient catalyst layer architecture is designed using DFT-derived wettability parameters; (4) COMSOL Multiphysics simulations pre-validate the design before physical fabrication, substantially reducing experimental iterations; and (5) experimental cold-start testing validates the fabricated gradient catalyst layer. The calculated values of quantum parameters inform the design of a three-zone gradient architecture in which the membrane-side and proton-transport zone is mildly hydrophilic (1.5% N-doped), the core zone compartment offers mixed-wettability microchannels (3% N + 8% MoS \( {\text{}}_{2}\) ) and the gas diffusion interface is hydrophobic (5% N -doped). The hybrid XGBoost-GNN ensemble achieves R² = 0.881 (MAE = 2.14 s, n = 126 test compositions) using composition-structural inputs only, representing genuine independent predictive capability; the full-feature ensemble including DFT-linked descriptors that also participate in label construction achieves R² = 0.946 (MAE = 1.24s, n = 126 test compositions) and functions as a physics-informed emulator of the DFT-to-device performance chain rather than an independent predictor. Simulations of the gradient design using COMSOL Multiphysics has been performed for future time saving purpose which reveal that the gradient design provides a 108% increase in the freeze-delay time (17.1s) compared to baseline (8.2s), and a 52% decrease in time-to-0 °C self-heating threshold (12.0s) compared to baseline (25.0s), reduce ice formation (41.7% reduction in ice area fraction, and a 97% cold-start success rate at − 20 °C (29 of 30 trials), and tolerate is 5% of performance loss after 200 freeze-thaw cycles (compared to conventional Pt/C catalyst layers). These findings establish quantum-controlled microarchitectures as a significant advance toward reliable sub-zero PEMFC operation. This multi-scale pipeline represents one of the first frameworks to integrate DFT-computed ice nucleation descriptors with ML-accelerated screening specifically for cold-start catalyst layer optimization.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: cold start; proton exchange membrane fuel cells; density functional theory

Article.Title: A multimodal machine learning framework for assessing moisture and thermal damage in asphalt binder aggregate systems
Article.Authors: Lu Q.; Yang Q.; Ghasemi M.; Elattar S.; Ali H.; Escorcia-Gutierrez J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Moisture and thermal degradation of asphalt binder and aggregate interfacial bonds is a major precursor to stripping, adhesion loss, and premature pavement deterioration, but conventional mixture level indicators often fail to capture early interface damage. This study develops a multimodal learning framework for post-conditioning diagnostic assessment of durability loss by integrating binder rheology, aggregate surface characteristics, conditioning variables, contact angle measurements, and image derived damage descriptors. A 720-record experimental dataset was assembled using eight asphalt binders, six aggregate sources, five conditioning states, and three replicates. Target outputs included pull off adhesion strength, retained adhesion index, moisture damage probability, failure mode, interfacial durability score, and critical conditioning class. Mean pull off adhesion strength decreased from 722.0 kPa to 453.1 kPa after saline thermal aging, while retained adhesion declined from 100.0% to 61.7%. Contact angle increased from 77.4° to 101.9° and debonded area ratio increased from 5.0% to 31.8%, confirming progressive wetting related and morphological damage. For post test diagnostic inference, the Multimodal Transformer and CatBoost fusion model achieved R² values of 0.984 and 0.968 for adhesion strength and retained adhesion, moisture damage classification accuracy of 0.96, and failure mode macro F1 of 0.90. The reported multimodal performance therefore characterizes already conditioned interfaces and should not be interpreted as prospective prediction before environmental exposure or mechanical testing.

Article.Title: Multiphysics framework for sustainable iron ore reduction–softening–melting: high-energy X-ray computed tomography and moving particle hydrodynamics
Article.Authors: Natsui S.; Adema A.; van der Stel J.; Yang Y.; Kano K.; Kondo M.; Hayasaka M.; Ito A.; Iwama T.; Nogami H.
Article.Abstract: The steelmaking industry is one of the most difficult industrial sectors to decarbonise, with blast furnaces projected to play a dominant role in global iron production during this energy transition period. Iron ore behaviour remains largely unpredictable, given the uncertainty in the softening, deformation, and melting of iron-ore pellets in the cohesive zone, where small changes in gas permeability can significantly reduce furnace stability. Herein, we combine high-energy X-ray computed tomography, micro-chemical analysis, and moving particle hydrodynamics to link the internal transformation of reduced pellets with the mechanical collapse of a packed bed. Interrupted reduction–softening–melting experiments showed a progressive transition from a load-bearing metallic-iron shell at 1300 °C, to iron–slag coexistence and oxide enrichment in the core at 1400 °C, and finally to melting and dripping at 1550 °C. Three-dimensional tomography results quantified how the pellet-rich layer densifies and narrows, while particle simulations reproduced its displacement and collapse using a yield-stress formulation constrained by experimental data. This inverse calibration helped translate the observed deformation into a temperature-dependent shell-strength law. Our multiphysics framework converts tomographic images from static descriptors into predictive inputs for multi-scale furnace models, thereby offering a method to evaluate raw materials and operational strategies for low-carbon ironmaking.

Article.Title: Evaluation of segmental skin temperature cooling responses in a summer electric vehicle cabin using a thermophysiological model
Article.Authors: Ruhyanto M.; Suhaimi M.; Kim W.; Cho C.; Lee D.; Lee H.
Article.Abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) cabins create transient and uneven cooling conditions, but cabin average and whole-body indicators cannot show how cooling is distributed across body regions. This study evaluated segmental skin temperature cooling responses in a summer EV cabin by combining human skin temperature measurements from ten participants, thermal manikin based local boundary conditions, and a thermophysiological model. The model reproduced segmental skin temperatures with root-mean-square error values of 0.12–0.69 °C. A trend-based no-cooling reference was then constructed to estimate the cooling effect of active HVAC operation for each body segment. The analysis distinguished sustained low intensity cooling from stronger accumulated cooling, showing that cooling duration alone can misrepresent segmental cooling performance. The left arm showed the strongest accumulated cooling, with a cumulative cooling effect of 168.34 °C·min and an effective period equivalent cooling intensity of 3.77 °C, whereas the back showed the weakest response (44.69 °C·min; 0.82 °C). The right foot remained above the 0.5 °C threshold throughout the exposure, but its effective period equivalent cooling intensity was only 1.17 °C. These findings provide a compact framework for evaluating non-uniform cabin cooling and identifying body regions where conventional airflow may require complementary localized cooling strategies.

Article.Title: A lightweight photovoltaic panel defect detection model based on YOLO
Article.Authors: Liu Y.; Cao S.; Liu M.
Article.Abstract: To tackle the trade-off between lightweight deployment and high precision for photovoltaic panel defect detection, this paper proposes a lightweight photovoltaic panel defect detection model, LPD‑YOLO. This model performs deep compression and optimization based on YOLOv8. It embed Ghost HGBlock into the backbone and adopt GSConv and VoVGSCSP in the detection head to cut model parameters. Additionally, an adaptive scale fusion attention module is integrated to achieve weighted fusion of multi-scale features by combining Zoom-Cat scale alignment, ScalSeq serialization and reorganization, and multi-branch attention, thereby enhancing the model’s feature extraction capability for small targets and complex defects. Finally, the model is compressed and fine-tuned using network slimming and hybrid knowledge distillation, significantly reducing computational overhead while preserving detection accuracy. Experimental results on the GB_HSP_ modified dataset show that the LPD‑YOLO model has only 0.44 M parameters and 0.9 GFLOPs computational complexity, while maintaining a competitive detection accuracy (mAP50) of 76.8%. Compared to mainstream lightweight models, its parameters and computational cost are reduced by more than 80%. It outperforms baselines including Faster R-CNN and YOLOv6–v12 with a well-balanced trade-off among accuracy, speed, and model lightweighting, demonstrating strong potential for efficient photovoltaic panel defect detection on resource-limited devices.

Article.Title: Multi-class Alzheimer’s disease classification using VGG19 transfer learning with hybrid Harris Hawks Optimization and random forest
Article.Authors: Anbu Selvi G.; Karthick T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate cognition-state classification of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI), and Cognitively Normal (CN) is essential for early evaluation of the disease. Existing deep-learning approaches often retain redundant features, depend on dataset-specific configurations, and provide limited methodological optimization. This study proposes a transfer-learning-based MRI classification framework integrating spatial and intensity normalization, histogram equalization, double bilateral filtering, VGG19-based deep feature extraction, Harris Hawks Optimization with Simulated Annealing (HHO-SA) for feature selection, and Random Forest (RF) classification. The framework was implemented using Python and PyTorch and evaluated on the ADNI1 Complete 1Yr 1.5T dataset, containing 2,294 MRI observations from 639 subjects. Subject-level partitioning was employed to minimize data leakage. The proposed framework achieved 98.70% accuracy, 98.55% macro-precision, 98.93% macro-recall, 99.28% macro-specificity, 98.73% macro-F1, and 99.40% macro-ROC-AUC. Compared with the strongest reported benchmark accuracy of 98.20%, this study developed into 0.50%. The findings demonstrate effective retrospective three-class MRI classification and provide a reproducible computational framework for AD research.

Article.Title: Heterogeneous graph transformer with slot-based message passing for node classification
Article.Authors: Xie Y.; Zheng W.; Ming Y.; Lin K.; Xiong B.
Article.Abstract: As a widely utilized data structure, heterogeneous graphs can accurately model complex structures and multi-typed relationships, finding extensive applications in social network analysis, recommendation systems, knowledge graphs, and biomedical analysis. Node classification supports these applications by identifying entity categories or functional roles. However, during the message-passing process, mapping different types of nodes into a unified representation space often leads to cross-type feature confusion, resulting in the loss of type-specific semantic information. To address this issue, this paper proposes the HGT-Slot model. First, the model employs a type-aware Slot initialization to construct type-specific representation spaces for different node types, preserving their unique semantic attributes. Subsequently, a Slot attention mechanism is employed during the message-passing phase to preserve heterogeneous semantic information through different Slot channels. Meanwhile, the Transformer architecture is leveraged to enhance interactions among node representations, thereby improving the representation capability of the model. Finally, a Slot aggregation mechanism integrates the Slot representations for local prediction, which is fused with the global prediction from the Transformer branch for classification. Experiments on three datasets show that HGT-Slot achieves the best mean Macro-F1 and Micro-F1 scores among the compared methods for node classification.

Article.Title: Dynamic fusion and robust downsampling for remote sensing object detection
Article.Authors: Hong Y.; Lian J.; Wan Z.; Zhang C.
Article.Abstract: In remote sensing imagery, complex backgrounds and scale variation make small objects difficult to detect. To address this issue, we propose an SRFD-CAFM (Shallow Robust Feature Downsampling - Convolution and Attention Fusion Module) framework, which is an improved RT-DETR (Real-Time Detection Transformer). It integrates CNN and Transformer to balance local and global information. A dynamic weight allocation (DWA) module adaptively regulates feature contributions, while the Shallow Robust Feature Downsampling (SRFD) module preserves fine-grained shallow information to mitigate small-object feature loss. Experiments on multiple datasets show a 1.6-point mAP50–95 improvement over the baseline, confirming the model’s capability in complex scenes and small object detection.

Article.Title: An automata-machine learning integrated framework for intelligent mental health diagnostics
Article.Authors: Pawar L.; Bajaj R.; Mengist Y.; Kumar N.; Pant R.; Kumar A.; Pandey P.
Article.Abstract: Depression among the students has critical impact on student’s life and it needs to be predicted at an early stage. The unstructured nature of self-emotions are going to undetected and emerged as a critical mental health concern. Integration of machine learning (ML) with behavioural modelling address the concern and connects with student emotional state and helps to predict the depression among students at early stage. An automata-machine learning integrated approaches including ensemble of lazy and eager classifiers, behavioural modelling, minimization of finite automata are evaluated and compared in three scenarios where in the first case predictive performance on original dataset is evaluated. The second case in sighting the real life scenario student specific emotions are extracted with automata-based behavioural states to generate meaningful patterns and feature vectors for each student and these automata generated features are statistically tested and signified then embed with original dataset. Further the ML feature selection Gini index applied on automata integrated dataset to select the prominent features to enhance the predictive performance. In the third case automata based feature merging is applied which maintain the credibility of each feature and merged systematically with related features and preserve the equivalence and reduce the feature redundancy. Unlike the traditional ML based feature selection, Automata based feature merging retains the interpretability and behavioural traceability of all features. Lastly, eager learning (random forest) and lazy Learning (kstar) are ensemble and deployed to take advantage of the automata based optimized feature sets. The automata assisted scenario performs well and improves the accuracy with 14.86% where the baseline accuracy is 82.02% evaluated with random forest classifier and the accuracy with automata based behavioural modelling is recorded 96.88% and shows proposed framework is an interpretable, dynamic solution for mental health interventions in educational settings. The main contributions of the proposed framework is to extract automata based features that behaviourally connects to student emotions and mental state. The minimization of finite automata reduces the redundant factors and maintained the credibility of each feature. Further multi-metric statistical validation determines the applicability of automata extracted features.
