Article.Title: Combinatorial impact of sanguinarine on doxorubicin induced HSPA5 mediated ER stress in triple-negative breast cancer cells
Article.Authors: Bhamidipati P.; Malla R.
Article.Abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX) is a widely used chemotherapeutic for incredibly aggressive triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). However, its clinical utility is partially limited due to multiorgan toxicities and development of resistance. This study investigated the combinatorial impact of sanguinarine (SAN) on the DOX-induced ER stress and mRNA expression patterns in TNBC cells at sub-optimal concentration. This study evaluated dose-response profile on individual and combination treatments. The potentiated combination was explored to perform different functional assays, RNA-Seq and RT-qPCR analysis and HSPA5 expression analysis. The results showed that the duo combination induced a synergistic cellular toxicity after 48 h of exposure at sub-optimally lower concentrations on MDA-MB-231 cells. The synergistic combination inhibited viability, proliferation and cell cycle, and significantly induced cell death, ER stress, and ROS generation, with elevated caspase 3 activity. Gene ontology (GO) analysis of data from the RNA-Seq analysis revealed that downregulated genes were mapped mainly to protein modifications in the ER, cell cycle, metabolic pathways, and ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis. In contrast, upregulated genes were mapped to mitophagy, the MAPK pathway, and apoptosis, and showed differential expression of prominent ER stress-related genes. RT-qPCR analysis further confirmed the downregulation of HSPA5 and ATF4 and upregulation of XBP1 and DDIT3. Furthermore, combination treatment reduced the total and csHSPA5 protein expression. These insights highlight a novel mechanism by which the SAN-DOX combination synergistically promotes ERS mediated cell death in TNBC.

Article.Title: Three-year longitudinal safety surveillance following COVID-19 vaccination in individuals with underlying medical conditions
Article.Authors: Sadat Larijani M.; Eybpoosh S.; Ghaseminejad Kermani S.; Sofian M.; Hasannezhad M.; Ashrafian F.; Zali M.; Azerang P.; Bavand A.; Faridpour A.; Tahmasebi Z.; Moradi L.; Javadi A.; Ramezani A.
Article.Abstract: Individuals with chronic comorbidities are at increased risk of severe COVID-19 outcomes. Although post-vaccination adverse events are generally mild and comparable to those in the general population, rare events and limited longitudinal data highlight the need for condition-specific long-term safety surveillance. To address these critical evidence gaps, this study conducted a longitudinal analysis of various COVID-19 vaccine platforms within the Iranian population with comorbidities three years post - vaccination. The research evaluated the safety profiles of different vaccine platforms across these patient cohorts using a researcher-made questionnaire composing of short-term and long-term vaccine adverse events as well as cases’ medical profiles. Furthermore, an exploratory immunogenicity sub-study was performed among participants with HIV to characterize vaccine-induced humoral immune responses. A total of 1115 participants were enrolled; 43.9% had a history of COVID-19 infection, with significantly higher incidence among participants with several comorbidities. Body pain, fever, and weakness were the most frequently reported early adverse events (AEs). During long-term follow-up, 23.8% experienced at least one post-vaccination event, most commonly cardiovascular (5.4%) and neurological (4.8%) conditions. Multiple analysis identified obesity and liver disease as the strongest independent risk factors for a broad range of AEs, while increasing age was associated with higher odds of overall and several organ-specific events. After adjustment for age, sex, previous COVID-19 infection, and number of comorbidities, AstraZeneca recipients had higher rates of early AEs after the first dose and first booster. PastoCovac and Sputnik were associated with lower odds of early AEs after the second dose, whereas Bharat, Barkat, and PastoCovac were associated with higher odds of late AEs. While AEs were frequent in cases with underlying conditions, most of them were mild and transient. However, cardiovascular and neurological symptoms were the most frequently reported long-term events during follow-up. Although some kinds of comorbidities showed a higher prevalence of complains after specific vaccine types, the casual association is not possible yet.

Article.Title: A mixed-methods study of knowledge, attitudes, and practices related to gluten-free diets in india
Article.Authors: Moitra P.; Qureshi B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Recent evidence suggests a growing popularity of gluten-free diets (GFDs) beyond clinically indicated contexts in low middle income countries. However, a comprehensive investigation of public perceptions, motivations, and professional challenges related to both medically and non-medically indicated GFD adoption remains limited. Therefore, we conducted a mixed method study to explore the perspectives of dietetic professionals and assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) related to gluten and GFDs among adults aged 18–45 years in India. The clinical and nutritional considerations for GFD were examined through in-depth interviews (n = 9) and an online survey was conducted among adults (n = 285) to assess their KAP. Thematic analyses revealed fragmented public understanding, symptom-led self-diagnosis, influence of “anti-inflammatory” narratives, concerns regarding nutritional adequacy of GFDs, and the need to leverage traditional food systems. Data highlighted limited knowledge regarding gluten (50.9%), and GFDs (38.6%). Reasons for GFD adoption included perceived health benefits (19.8%), weight loss (26.4%) and no reasons (32.1%). Consumption of naturally gluten-free staples such as rice (58.9%), lentils (55.8%) and millets (30.9%) was higher than that of oats (7.7%), barley/ quinoa (2.8%), and speciality flours (2.1%). The study provides timely insights into the drivers of the GFD trend within India’s rapidly evolving urban nutrition landscape.

Article.Title: PGTNet: a physiology-guided parallel Graph-Transformer network for multimodal fatigue recognition of aviation maintenance engineers
Article.Authors: Li G.; Yang T.; Cai H.; Dai C.; Huang P.; Guo R.
Article.Abstract: Fatigue severely degrades operational reliability in high-risk operational settings such as aviation maintenance. Although multimodal physiological signals support objective fatigue assessment, many existing models emphasize temporal patterns without explicitly modeling dependencies among physiological features across modalities. We propose a Physiology-Guided Parallel Graph–Transformer Network (PGTNet) for multimodal fatigue recognition, which incorporates physiologically motivated fatigue-related features derived from multimodal physiological signals. Parallel DGCN and Transformer branches jointly model physiological feature relationships and long-range temporal dependencies, and their representations are integrated through a bidirectional cross-attention mechanism. Under the predefined subject-independent partition, PGTNet achieves an Accuracy of 0.8778 and a Macro-AUC of 0.9648. Eight-fold subject-wise cross-validation yields an average Accuracy of 0.8592 ± 0.0112 across the eight held-out subjects. These results support the effectiveness of PGTNet within the present dataset.

Article.Title: Optimized energy efficient cluster based routing protocol for real time communication in 5G enabled VANETs using reinforcement learning
Article.Authors: Arun Kumar M.; Somisetty R.; Pradeep M.; Arunkumar C.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The combination of 5G networks and Vehicular Ad-hoc Networks (VANETs) has transformed real-time communication to smart transportation systems, but challenges such as high energy usage, changes in topology, and rigid latency requirements still exist. This work offers a 5G-enabled VANET Optimized Energy-Efficient Cluster-Based Routing Protocol (OEECRP), which combines dynamic clustering, reinforcement learning (RL)-based routing, and 5G network slicing to provide sustainable, low-latency communication and therefore addresses these problems. Ensuring network lifespan, the protocol initially uses a weighted clustering technique to choose Cluster Heads (CHs) depending on residual energy, mobility, and 5G link reliability. A Q-learning model then dynamically adapts to traffic density, node energy levels, and latency limitations to achieve the best routing decisions, with a reward mechanism that balances energy efficiency and real-time performance. The Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency Communication (URLLC) that 5G network slicing provides priority to important traffic also reduces the reliance on centralized cloud infrastructure. The protocol is tested in the urban environment with the number of cars of 50–200 and is implemented in MATLAB R2023a and the 5G Toolbox and Communications Toolbox. Experimental results show that OEECRP beats five conventional models such as AODV, DSR, DSDV, GPSR and LEACH by approximately 30 percent reduction of energy consumption, less than 50ms end-to-end delay and increased packet delivery ratio (PDR). These results prove the reliability and scalability of OEECRP, thus offering a powerful solution to real-time, energy-conscious VANET communication.

Article.Title: Optimizing the synthesis of imine-linked covalent organic frameworks for high surface areas
Article.Authors: Hosseini F.; Amiri A.
Article.Abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) continue to attract attention for their structural precision and tunable porosity, yet reliably achieving high surface area remains difficult. In this work, we clarify how common reaction parameters actually influence the formation of imine‑linked COFs. Using COF‑SDU1 as model system, we show that a straightforward open-reflux synthesis, one that does not require degassing or specialized equipment, can produce materials with a high specific surface area of 2163 m 2 g −1 , nearly twice the highest value previously reported for comparable template-free COFs (1125 m 2 g −1 ). A more elaborate, multi-step procedure yields only a slight improvement (2241 m 2 g −1 ), demonstrating that the increased complexity and energy use offer little practical benefit. By directly comparing these approaches, we identify which synthetic choices truly matter and which can be safely simplified. These insights provide experimentally grounded guidance for the rational and reproducible preparation of high surface area imine-linked COFs.

Article.Title: Global analysis reveals persistent land-cover thresholds for river water quality across climates and decades
Article.Authors: Costa D.; Baulch H.; Jarvie H.; Liu J.; Macrae M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Agricultural and urban land uses are widely recognized as major drivers of global surface water quality. However, it remains unclear whether the magnitude of the impacts scales universally and consistently across contrasting climatic and geographical settings based on the intensity of land-use change. Here we analyse more than 19 million river water quality observations from 117 countries over 28 years, linking $$\sim$$ 101,000 monitoring stations to upstream basin land cover derived from ESA CCI. Cropland and urban areas reveal the strongest global positive correlations with nutrient and sediment concentrations, while forested landscapes are consistently associated with lower pollutant levels. A dose-response analysis (term borrowed from toxicology) based on 1.7 million basin–year records shows that land-cover impacts on water quality are not merely categorical but scale progressively across the full gradient of land-cover intensity. Nutrient concentrations increase by up to 10-fold for nitrate and 5.7-fold for total nitrogen with expanding agricultural and urban land use, whereas forest cover is associated with reductions of up to 12-fold in both nitrogen and phosphorus. Importantly, these relationships are strongly non-linear: the conversion of the first 20–40% of a basin to cropland drives disproportionately large increases in nutrient loads, revealing critical and actionable land-use thresholds for watershed management.

Article.Title: The ameliorative effects of gastrodin on cognitive impairment in STZ-treated mice are associated with the modulation of hippocampal neurogenesis-related proteins and inhibition of the AGEs–RAGE axis
Article.Authors: Li R.; Gao R.; Zhao R.; Yang J.; Du Y.; Yuan H.; Wu M.; Pei L.; Chen H.; Zhao G.
Article.Abstract: Hippocampal neurogenesis has been implicated in diabetic cognitive impairment (DCI). Gastrodin (Gas), the major bioactive ingredient of Gastrodia elata, has anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and neuroprotective activities. This study investigated whether Gas protects against DCI and whether this is associated with the AGEs–RAGE axis and hippocampal neurogenesis-related proteins. DCI was induced in mice by a high-fat diet plus streptozotocin. Mice received 25, 50, or 100 mg/kg Gas daily for four weeks, with metformin as positive control. Fasting blood glucose was monitored weekly. Gas attenuated hyperglycemia and cognitive deficits in DCI mice. Gas treatment was accompanied by upregulation of neurogenesis- and synaptic-related proteins (C-Myc, Cyclin D1, NGN2, NeuroD1, PSD95, MAP2) and downregulation of AGEs, RAGE, GFAP, and pro-inflammatory factors. These findings suggest that Gas may alleviate HFD/STZ-induced cognitive impairment, possibly via AGEs–RAGE axis suppression and enhanced hippocampal neurogenesis-related protein expression. However, this study was limited to a single animal model, relied mainly on correlative molecular data, and did not include pathway-blocking experiments. Further studies are needed to confirm causality and clinical relevance.

Article.Title: Conservation guided reverse vaccinology for the design of a broadly immunogenic multi-epitope vaccine against monkeypox virus
Article.Authors: Sajal H.; Mohan A.; Raju R.; Nadh A.
Article.Abstract: Mpox, caused by the Monkeypox virus (MPXV), has emerged as a global public health concern following outbreaks beyond its traditional endemic regions. Although existing smallpox-derived vaccines provide partial protection, their limitations and declining population immunity highlight the need for safer and more targeted vaccine strategies. This study aimed to identify conserved antigenic targets and design a multi-epitope vaccine candidate against MPXV using a conservation-guided immunoinformatics approach. A dataset of 27 complete MPXV genomes (2001–2025) from diverse geographic regions was analyzed to identify highly conserved viral genes. Conserved surface-exposed proteins were prioritized for epitope prediction, including cytotoxic T-lymphocyte, helper T-lymphocyte, and B-cell epitopes. High-confidence epitopes were selected based on binding affinity, antigenicity, immunogenicity, toxicity, allergenicity, and absence of human sequence homology. Promiscuous epitopes with broad human leukocyte antigen (HLA) binding were curated to maximize population coverage. Three multi-epitope vaccine constructs were designed using appropriate linkers and adjuvants. Structural modeling, molecular docking with innate immune receptors, immune response simulation, and codon optimization were performed to evaluate the constructs. All constructs were predicted to be stable, antigenic, and non-allergenic. Molecular docking indicated strong interactions of vaccine construct 2 (VC2) with TLR2 and the TLR4–MD-2 complex, achieving the highest binding affinities (ΔG = − 19.6 and − 27.8 kcal/mol, respectively). Immune simulations predicted robust humoral and cellular responses, including strong antibody production and interferon-γ induction for VC2. Population coverage analysis estimated 99.27% global coverage, and codon optimization suggested efficient expression in Escherichia coli . Overall, VC2 emerges as a promising multi-epitope vaccine candidate with strong predicted immunogenic and structural properties. While these computational findings lay a solid foundation, VC2 require further experimental validation and preclinical development as a targeted vaccine strategy against MPXV.

Article.Title: Probing collectivity in nuclear binding energies from the viewpoint of the F-spin formalism
Article.Authors: Emami H.; Sabri H.
Article.Abstract: We aim to investigate binding energies of fp-shell nuclei using the supersymmetric model within the Interaction Boson Model-2, emphasizing the role of F-spin symmetry as a classification tool for collective dynamics. Since nuclear binding energies are strongly influenced by pairing correlations, an algebraic framework capable of distinguishing proton and neutron collective pairs is required. F-spin symmetry provides this framework by organizing bosons into multiplets according to their degree of proton–neutron coherence. In this work, we extended a supersymmetric Hamiltonian expressed as a linear combination of Casimir operators of the relevant subalgebras, supplemented by pairing contributions and explicit F-spin–breaking interactions. Ground-state energies and binding energies are evaluated, and deformation is analyzed using the quadrupole parameter β 2 . Color-mapped scatter plot visualizations of β 2 as a function of mass number and root mean square deviations demonstrate a satisfactory agreement with experimental data and reveal the influence of shell structure. This study also examines quantities sensitive to nuclear structure, including two-neutron separation energies and neutron-proton pairing gaps, to probe underlying nuclear properties. The results highlight F-spin as the key algebraic symmetry for describing the impact of pairing and collectivity on nuclear binding energies in the fp-shell.

Article.Title: Phenotypic screening and molecular marker-based identification of resistant apple genotypes to Eriosoma lanigerum in Kashmir, India
Article.Authors: Tarasing P.; Mohi-ud-din S.; Malik A.; Dar S.
Article.Abstract: Phenotypic screening of nine apple genotypes (Shireen, Chamura, American Apirouge, Red Delicious, Vance Delicious, Royal Delicious, Lal Ambri, Akbar and Top Red) revealed significant variation in susceptibility to woolly apple aphid ( Eriosoma lanigerum ) infestation during April–October 2025. Infestation peaked in mid-summer, with Vance Delicious and Akbar showing extreme susceptibility, while American Apirouge consistently maintained low colony counts. Cumulative infestation scores ranged from 595 in Vance Delicious to 315 colonies of WAA in American Apirouge. The findings highlight substantial genotypic differences in resistance. American Apirouge emerges as a promising genotype for resistant to woolly apple aphid among the nine genotypes. Molecular marker analysis of nine apple cultivars revealed key genetic determinants of resistance to woolly apple aphid ( Eriosoma lanigerum ). Conserved markers NZsc_GS327, NZsc_O05, NZms_EB145764, NZms_EB106753, NZsc_E01 and NZsc_A01 were consistently detected across most genotypes, underscoring their strong association with resistance. A distinct finding was the presence of NZsc_C20, linked to the Er1 gene, exclusively in ‘American Apirouge’, suggesting a unique resistance pathway. In contrast, NZsn_O05 was absent in all cultivars, confirming its lack of relevance in resistance determination. The combined genotypic and phenotypic evaluation demonstrated a strong correlation between marker presence and field resistance, with ‘American Apirouge’ showing the lowest infestation, while ‘Vance Delicious’ and ‘Akbar’ recorded higher susceptibility despite carrying most markers. These results highlight the importance of both conserved and cultivar‑specific alleles in shaping resistance and provide valuable insights for aimed at durable woolly aphids’ control.

Article.Title: Machine learning-based prediction of 90-day tensile strength in geopolymer concrete under varying input-variable scenarios
Article.Authors: Mehravar P.; Bahrami H.; Ghazvinian H.
Article.Abstract: Accurate prediction of the long-term tensile strength (TS) of geopolymer concrete remains a complex challenge owing to the nonlinear and interactive nature of the governing parameters. This study develops and comparatively evaluates four machine-learning models linear regression (LR), decision tree (DT), random forest (RF) and support-vector regression (SVR) to predict 90-day tensile strength from a suite of physicochemical and mixture-related variables. Eleven systematically designed input scenarios were formulated to quantify the influence of different feature combinations on predictive performance. The results demonstrate a pronounced dependence of model accuracy on input configuration. Early scenarios that employed limited variable sets yielded only moderate performance (R² ≤ 0.885, with most models below 0.86), whereas the optimal configuration (S11), which incorporates water absorption (WA), ground-granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBS), nano-silica, pH and bulk density (BD), substantially enhanced predictive capability. Among the models, DT achieved the highest test accuracy (R² = 0.984, RMSE = 0.751) together with the smallest generalisation gap (training R² = 0.988), indicating strong predictive performance within the investigated dataset and limited evidence of overfitting under the applied validation procedures. RF and SVR also delivered high predictive performance (R² = 0.964 and 0.956, respectively), while LR exhibited comparatively lower accuracy, underscoring the importance of nonlinear modelling approaches. Permutation-importance sensitivity analysis identified WA as the dominant influential parameter (mean ΔR² = 0.911), followed by GGBS (0.588) and nano-silica (0.277), indicating that WA and GGBS were the strongest predictors of TS within the trained model, consistent with though not a direct proof of their established physical roles in porosity and geopolymeric gel formation. Collectively, the findings indicate that the integration of advanced tree-based learning algorithms with comprehensive input characterisation provides a promising and computationally efficient framework for modelling the long-term tensile behaviour of geopolymer concrete within the range of mixtures examined; broader industrial application will, however, require external validation on independent datasets and formal uncertainty quantification.

Article.Title: Drag reduction and degradation behavior of polyethylene oxide (PEO) solutions in hydraulic fracturing applications
Article.Authors: Yang Y.; Yuan H.; Zhu Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study systematically investigates the rheological properties, drag reduction performance, and degradation behavior of polyethylene oxide (PEO) solutions under turbulent flow conditions relevant to hydraulic fracturing. Using Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV) and Dynamic Light Scattering (DLS), complemented by rheological testing, we analyzed the flow characteristics of PEO solutions at various concentrations. Results show that a 150 ppm PEO solution achieved a maximum drag reduction (DR) rate of 52% at a Reynolds number (Re) of 5085, significantly lowering frictional resistance and enhancing fluid transport efficiency. PIV analysis revealed that PEO effectively suppresses turbulent eddies and reduces velocity fluctuations, leading to a more stable flow profile and decreased energy dissipation. DLS measurements quantified the molecular degradation, demonstrating that under continuous turbulent shear, the average hydrodynamic radius of PEO molecules decreased from approximately 351 nm to 211 nm within 10 min, representing a 39.8% size reduction. Most importantly, this reduction in molecular size strongly correlates with the decline in drag reduction efficiency ( R 2 = 0.95), providing evidence that the reduction of molecular‑scale hydrodynamic size is strongly correlated with impaired drag‑reduction performance, consistent with polymer mechanical chain scission. By integrating macroscopic flow visualization with microscopic structural analysis, this study establishes a quantitative relationship between molecular-scale degradation and macroscopic performance loss, offering valuable insights for the development of high-performance, shear-resistant drag reducers in hydraulic fracturing applications.

Article.Title: Biochanin A suppresses ferroptosis after traumatic brain injury via the Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway
Article.Authors: Hu Y.; Zhang M.; Zhao H.; Ruan Y.; Liu T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Traumatic brain injury can induce ferroptosis, which plays an important role in TBI progression. Therapies targeting ferroptosis are beneficial for TBI recovery. Biochanin A can be isolated from Huangqi, which has been shown to exert anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. Nevertheless, the underlying mechanism of BCA on secondary injury after TBI remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the mechanism by which BCA regulates ferroptosis after TBI. The mouse TBI model and HT-22 cells were utilized to study the protective effect of BCA on the injury induced by ferroptosis after TBI. Through in vivo experiments, a mouse TBI model was established to determine that BCA could reduce post-TBI injury and exert neuroprotective effects as determined by the Modified Neurological Severity scale, brain water content, Nissl staining, hematoxylin-eosin staining, TUNEL staining. BCA was proven to be capable of inhibiting the changes in post-TBI ferroptosis-related proteins, activating the Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway, and reducing oxidative stress, as confirmed by Western blotting. In vitro, erastin-induced ferroptosis in HT-22 cells was attenuated by BCA, as shown increased cell viability, reduced reactive oxygen species and and lipid peroxidation, and restored antioxidant levels. BCA suppressed protein levels of multiple ferroptosis-associated markers in this cell model. In conclusion, BCA had a neuroprotective effect after TBI by inhibiting ferroptosis via activating the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway. These findings may provide potential therapeutic strategies for TBI.

Article.Title: Clinical and genetic characteristics of patients with disorders of sex development in a large unselected cohort of China
Article.Authors: Yang H.; Lin H.; Tian H.; Yuan J.; Tang D.; Wu D.; Dong G.; Sun L.; Gu W.; Li H.; Wang Z.; Pi Y.; Liu L.; Shan X.; Wei H.; Xu R.; Yang Y.; Li G.; Chen X.; Feng M.; Ma X.; Su Z.; Li Y.; Xu X.; Chen R.
Article.Abstract: Disorders of sex development (DSD) encompass a range of congenital conditions characterized by atypical chromosomal, gonadal, or anatomical sex development. Accurate diagnosis and management of DSD are crucial for optimal patient outcomes. This research aims to characterize the clinical and genetic characteristics of a large Chinese cohort of children with non‑chromosomal DSD, with particular focus on the most frequently implicated genes and their diagnostic implications. Index cases of non-chromosomal DSD from 24 Chinese DSD centers were enrolled. Individuals were initially classified clinically following the 2006 Chicago consensus and its modifications. Targeted next generation sequencing was performed to identify possible pathogenic variants. We enrolled 494 individuals with 46,XY DSD and 45 individuals with 46,XX DSD. A likely genetic diagnosis was established in 35.44% of patients (36.44% in 46,XY and 24.44% in 46,XX). The most frequently implicated genes were SRD5A2 , AR , FGFR1 and NR5A1 , which together accounted for more than half of all molecularly diagnosed cases in 46,XY DSD. In total, 59 DSD‑related genes were found to harbor pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants, and 144 of the 495 identified variants (29.09%) had not been previously reported, substantially expanding the mutational spectrum of DSD. Diagnostic rates varied considerably across clinical subtypes, with the highest yield observed in cases presenting with severe undermasculinization or syndromic features. This study, conducted in the largest reported collection of non‑chromosomal DSD cases, demonstrates a genetic diagnostic rate of 35.44% and highlights SRD5A2 , AR , ANOS1 , FGFR1 and NR5A1 as the most frequently implicated genes in 46,XY DSD. These findings underscore the clinical utility of targeted gene panel testing in DSD and provide a valuable reference for genetic counseling and clinical management in diverse DSD subtypes.

Article.Title: The relationship between positive childhood experiences and flourishing via self-compassion and gratitude
Article.Authors: Çağış Z.
Article.Abstract: From ancient times to the present, the concept of happiness has consistently occupied a significant place in philosophical discourse and religious doctrine. People have pursued a “good” and “happy” life and have thought about the reasons behind such a life. Although existing literature suggests that positive childhood experiences (PCEs) are positively linked to flourishing, the underlying psychological processes remain relatively unexplored. Therefore, this study aims to address this limitation by examining associational relations between PCEs and flourishing, including self-compassion and gratitude as potential associated variables, as well as their sequential association. The participant group consisted of 499 Turkish adults aged between 18 and 52 years ( M = 27.11, SD = 8.14), representing a broad range of adulthood stages. The results revealed that PCEs were positively related to self-compassion, gratitude, and flourishing. Similarly, self-compassion was positively linked with gratitude and flourishing, and gratitude was positively correlated with flourishing. It was also found that both self-compassion and gratitude indicated significant associative relations in the relationship between PCEs and flourishing. The results also indicated a smaller but significant sequential association involving self-compassion and gratitude. The present study contributes to the expanding literature by providing a more comprehensive understanding of the link between childhood experiences and adult psychological outcomes. It also highlights the significance of childhood experiences for practitioners and identifies critical psychological factors that may be important to foster to improve flourishing in adulthood.

Article.Title: 2S-CFE: a two-stage contourlet-domain framework for contactless fingerprint enhancement
Article.Authors: Siddiqui M.; Iqbal S.; Khan T.; AlShammari B.; Alhaqbani B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Contactless fingerprint recognition offers significant advantages over contact-based sensing in terms of hygiene, faster acquisition, and reduced pressure-induced distortion. Nevertheless, contactless images typically exhibit low ridge-valley contrast, uneven illumination, perspective variation, and unreliable local ridge-frequency estimation, all of which degrade minutiae extraction and matching. Therefore, we propose a novel two-stage contactless fingerprint enhancement framework. The first stage performs contourlet-domain Block Matching and 3D Filtering (BM3D) denoising, while the second stage estimates local ridge orientation and frequency, applies adaptive Gabor filtering, and performs region-quality-aware minutiae selection, encoding, and matching. Experiments conducted using the Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU) contactless fingerprint database prove the effectiveness of the proposed enhancement technique, with a consistent decrease in Equal Error Rate (EER) across both contactless-to-contact-based and contactless-to-contactless matching scenarios. In the contactless-to-contact-based scenario, the Equal Error Rate decreases from 49.18 to 21.97% for M1, from 48.86 to 26.73% for M2, from 38.90 to 11.22% for M3, and from 24.76 to 17.50% for M4. In the contactless-to-contactless scenario, the Equal Error Rate decreases from 42.91 to 13.10% for M1, from 43.25 to 12.74% for M2, from 41.90 to 11.90% for M3, and from 31.00 to 9.05% for M4. These results demonstrate that the proposed enhancement framework consistently improves the performance of all evaluated matchers in both matching scenarios.

Article.Title: Drug repurposing and African natural product screening, targeting the Parkinson‘s-associated LRRK2 G2019S mutant kinase using molecular docking and molecular dynamics approaches
Article.Authors: Saeed O.; William M.; Salama M.; Ibrahim T.; Ramadan R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The G2019S mutation in leucine-rich repeat kinase 2 (LRRK2) is the most prevalent genetic contributor to Parkinson’s disease and is associated with increased kinase activity. Targeting this mutation remains a key therapeutic strategy; however, structure-guided identification of repurposable inhibitors remains limited. In this study, we implemented an integrated computational pipeline combining structure-based virtual screening, pharmacophore modeling, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and MM-GBSA free-energy calculations to prioritize candidate inhibitors of the LRRK2 G2019S mutant. A total of 9,407 compounds from DrugBank and African natural product libraries were screened against the ATP-binding pocket of the recently resolved cryo-electron microscopy structure of the mutant kinase (PDB ID: 8TZC). A structure-based pharmacophore model derived from the co-complex inhibitor MLi-2 was used for complementary screening. Selected candidates were further evaluated using 300-ns MD simulations, binding stability metrics, and per-residue energy decomposition. Virtual screening of 9,407 compounds (2,614 FDA-approved drugs, 4,923 East African and 1,870 North African natural products) against the ATP-binding pocket of LRRK2 G2019S, validated by MLi-2 redocking (RMSD = 0.095 Å); identified 14 candidates with docking scores more favorable than the reference inhibitor MLi-2 (− 10.1 kcal/mol) and hinge-region hydrogen bonding with GLU1948 and/or ALA1950 (four DrugBank, six East African, and four North African compounds). A complementary structure-based pharmacophore model derived from the LRRK2 G2019S–MLi-2 co-complex was screened against the DrugBank subset, yielding 81 pharmacophore-matched hits, of which four compounds, Rimonabant, Amlexanox, Bromocriptine, and Cilostazol, showed strong convergence across pharmacophoric fit, docking affinity, and hydrogen bonding at GLU1948/ALA1950. Representative top-ranked candidates from both approaches included, among FDA-approved drugs, Acalabrutinib (-10.6 kcal/mol), Atovaquone (-10.6 kcal/mol), Belumosudil (-10.4 kcal/mol), Rimonabant (-9.8 kcal/mol), and Bromocriptine (-9.2 kcal/mol); and, among natural products, Gallagic acid (-11.0 kcal/mol), 7,7′-dihydroxy-6,8′-bicoumarin (-10.7 kcal/mol), 10-hydroxy-10,7′-(chrysophanol anthrone)-chrysophanol (-10.7 kcal/mol), Anastatin A (-10.7 kcal/mol), and 5,7,2′,4′-tetrahydroxy-6-(3-methylbut-2-enyl)isoflavanone (-10.3 kcal/mol). Across the 300-ns MD simulations, Acalabrutinib and the chrysophanol anthrone dimer maintained the most stable backbone conformations, with mean RMSD values of approximately 1.066 and 1.022 nm, respectively, closely approaching the stability profile of the reference inhibitor. MM-GBSA calculations confirmed MLi-2 as the strongest overall binder (ΔG = − 46.91 ± 3.44 kcal/mol), while Rimonabant showed the most favorable binding free energy among repurposed drugs (− 36.61 ± 5.53 kcal/mol) and Gallagic acid was the top-performing natural product (− 33.18 ± 8.70 kcal/mol), sustaining a persistent hydrogen-bonding network throughout the simulation. These convergent docking, pharmacophore, dynamic stability, and binding free-energy analyses identify Rimonabant, Gallagic acid, Acalabrutinib, and Atovaquone as the most promising repurposable candidates against LRRK2 G2019S. Collectively, this study utilizes the recently resolved cryo-EM structure of the LRRK2 G2019S mutant to implement an integrated structure-based screening strategy and prioritize multiple repurposable drug candidates and natural scaffolds with favorable structural and energetic profiles. The findings provide mechanistic insight into mutation-specific ligand binding and establish a computational foundation for future experimental validation and LRRK2-targeted drug discovery in Parkinson’s disease.

Article.Title: First successful of embryo development after artificial insemination using frozen sperm in Okinawa rail (Hypotaenidia okinawae)
Article.Authors: Kaneko T.; Nakagawa Y.; Nakaya Y.; Tamanaha S.; Mukai S.; Nakashima E.; Ueda K.; Onuma M.; Nagamine T.
Article.Abstract: Okinawa rail ( Hypotaenidia okinawae ) is listed as endangered species with a population of approximately 1,500 individuals. Reproductive technology is an effective ex situ conservation method to prevent species extinction by increasing population size. Sperm preservation is useful for artificial insemination and maintenance of genetic resources. In this study, ejaculated sperm were collected and frozen in a solution containing N-methylacetamide as a cryoprotectant. Thawed sperm were inseminated into the oviducts of the female. The fertilized egg was collected and placed in an incubator. One embryo in one egg developed normally until day 21 after egg-laying whereafter the embryo died. This embryo contained genetic information derived from the frozen sperm. This result shows that frozen Okinawa rail sperm could potentially fertilize oocytes via artificial insemination. This protocol also contributes to the maintenance of the populations of other endangered avian species.

Article.Title: The quality assessment of asphalt pavement in the expressway engineering based on the gray target model with combination weights
Article.Authors: GU X.; LI Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The evaluation of pavement performance holds immense significance in the realm of engineering construction. To conduct this assessment, several indices have been carefully selected, namely Road Quality Index $$RQI$$ , Pavement Condition Index $$PCI$$ , Surface Strength Index $$SSI$$ , and British pendulum value $$BPN$$ measured by a pendulum apparatus. Additionally, a gray target model incorporating combination weights is introduced for enhanced analysis. Subsequently, a gray target model tailored specifically for the asphalt pavement of the Weiwu Expressway section is established. By employing the combination weighting method, the weight coefficients for each index are meticulously calculated. Then, utilizing the gray target model, the synthetic target center distances for each sample are determined. Based on these calculations, the quality levels of the asphalt pavement are ultimately ascertained. The proposed model excels in maximizing the exploitation of small-sample data and, to a certain degree, mitigates the issue of information scarcity inherent in small sample sizes. Moreover, it enables a quantitative evaluation of the final quality grade of the asphalt pavement. Consequently, this approach offers a novel perspective and methodology for the future quality assessment of asphalt pavements.

Article.Title: Links between La $$N_{4,5}$$-edge RIXS probed A-site covalency, structural parameters and superconducting properties in optimally doped La$$_{1.84}$$M$$_{0.16}$$CuO$$_4$$ (M = Ca, Sr, Ba) epitaxial films and the La$$_{2}$$CuO$$_4$$ host lattice
Article.Authors: Kusch M.; Siewierska K.; Liu C.; Kliem M.; Ruotsalainen K.; Decker R.; Schwiddessen R.; Logvenov G.; Christiani G.; Benckiser E.; Di Castro D.; Föhlisch A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We investigate La-site bonding by La N $$_{4,5}$$ -edge RIXS together with structural parameters and the superconducting transition temperature $$T_c$$ of optimally doped La $$_{1.84}$$ M $$_{0.16}$$ CuO $$_4$$ (M = Ca, Sr, Ba) epitaxial films and the La $$_2$$ CuO $$_4$$ host lattice. La and M in the A-site have been considered to be part of the axial hybrid state formed by Cu 4 s , apical O 2 $$p_z$$ , and rare earth (La) states. In La $$_{2-x}$$ M $$_{x}$$ CuO $$_4$$ (M = Ca, Sr, Ba) these states have been proposed as contributing to the superconducting transition temperature $$T_c$$ . We observe a systematic decrease of the La $$5p^54f^1$$ $$^3D_1$$ RIXS energy loss across the Ca–Sr–Ba doped film series. Based on previous La N $$_{4,5}$$ -edge RIXS studies, this trend is consistent with a La-site response to enhanced hybridization and local screening. The trend follows increasing A-site ionic radius and c -axis expansion, but these quantities are coupled to tetragonal distortion, unit-cell volume, epitaxial strain, relaxation, and possible symmetry changes. The undoped LCO host lattice shows a La $$^3D_1$$ energy close to the Sr-doped film, suggesting that its La-site environment cannot be described by ionic radius alone. However, because the LCO film differs in thickness and relaxation state from the doped films, this comparison is treated as qualitative. The superconducting transition temperature does not follow the La $$^3D_1$$ trend monotonically: the Sr-doped film has the highest $$T_c$$ , whereas the Ba-doped film shows a reduced $$T_c$$ despite the lowest $$^3D_1$$ energy loss. This indicates that the local A-site bonding response probed by La N $$_{4,5}$$ -edge RIXS is only one contribution among broader structural and electronic effects.

Article.Title: Federated digital twin framework for spectrum handover management in vehicular THz ORAN
Article.Authors: Gupta A.; Nisar A.; Khan M.
Article.Abstract: Vehicular Terahertz (THz) Open Radio Access Networks (ORAN) face severe challenges due to ultra-high mobility, rapid channel dynamics, spectrum scarcity, and frequent handovers, which limit the effectiveness of existing reactive and centralized management strategies. This paper proposes a Federated Blockchain-Assisted Digital Twin framework for proactive spectrum sharing and seamless handover in vehicular THz ORAN systems. The framework employs a Contrastive Denoising Spatio-Temporal Autoencoder (CD-STAE) to refine multi-source telemetry while preserving transient anomalies, followed by a Federated Multi-View Neural State-Space Twin (FMNSS) that constructs a privacy-preserving digital replica of the network. A Spatio-Temporal Transformer with Heteroscedastic Uncertainty (ST-TrH) enables confidence-aware forecasting of load, interference, and mobility-driven congestion, while On-Chain Verifiable Reward Shaping (OVRS) integrates blockchain-derived trust scores into federated aggregation and proactive spectrum leasing. Building on these predictions, a Reinforced Graph Trajectory Encoded DiffNet (R-GTEDiffNet), comprising EM-ST-GAT, Causal Trajectory Encoder (CTE), and Differentiable Handover Cost Layer (DHCL), is introduced to perform mobility-aware spectrum slicing and predictive handover optimization. Simulation results demonstrate superior performance over state-of-the-art models, achieving up to 94.1% spectrum utilization, 6.2 ms leasing delay, 10.5 ms handover latency, 1786 Mbps throughput, and an average classification accuracy of 98.68%, showing the framework’s strength in high-speed vehicular THz ORAN scenarios.

Article.Title: A unified multi-domain framework for hallucination detection and reliability evaluation in large language models
Article.Authors: Nagappan K.; Bhuvana M.; Khan A.; Bharath C.; Brijesh S.; Awasthi P.; Maity R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Large Language Models which consist of models like GPT5 from OpenAI, Claude Sonnet from Anthropic, Google’s Gemini are known for their reasoning capability, ability to summarize, cybersecurity analysis and other features. However, their reliability could be an issue particularly when dealing with ambiguous or hostile user input prompts. These kinds of attacks could lead to soft failures like false citations, hallucinations, and problematic suggestions. Current benchmarks (eg: TruthfulQA, AdvGLUE, and JailbreakBench) assess discrete aspects of robustness but are unable to identify multi-domain, conversational vulnerabilities that come up in practical applications. This paper introduces a novel dataset called MDH-Bench, a benchmark comprising 400 prompts that were specifically created to assess how reliably Large Language Models perform when they are provided with adversarial but natural and even tricky real-world queries. The benchmark covers eight types of challenges. They are numerical reasoning traps, security-sensitive defaults, historical and temporal inconsistencies, fictional research scenarios, contradictory context mixing, ethical provocations, and prompt-injection attempts. To monitor reliability in a holistic way, we present a Unified Multi-Domain Reliability Evaluation Framework that brings together several key metrics like accuracy, hallucination rate, hallucination degree (HD), unsafe output rate, and contradiction rate. A systematic assessment of four high-performance LLMs (GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4, Gemini 2.5 Pro, DeepSeek V3.1) was conducted under controlled, manual, multi-annotator settings. The findings indicate that although overall accuracy is more than 88% in all models, hallucinations are still present both at high frequency and severity level. The results of our investigation showed that solely relying on accuracy is not enough for evaluating the reliability of a system. MDH-Bench and the combined reliability scoring system give a wide-ranging, adaptable base for the assessment and enhancement of trust in future LLMs for real-world applications.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: hallucination detection; adversarial prompts; prompt injection; hallucination severity

Article.Title: SURF4 regulates RRM2 to activate the PI3K/AKT pathway and promote malignant progression in hepatocellular carcinoma
Article.Authors: Chen Z.; Zhao M.; Li Y.; Sun J.; Liu Z.; Zhao B.
Article.Abstract: Abstract SURF4 , a member of the Surfeit gene cluster, is widely expressed and localizes to the endoplasmic reticulum membrane. As a cargo receptor, it is involved in the transport of various proteins between the endoplasmic reticulum and the Golgi apparatus, and is closely associated with the progression of multiple tumors. However, the role and potential molecular mechanisms of SURF4 in the proliferation, migration, invasion, and apoptosis of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain unclear. First, the protein expression of SURF4 was evaluated in HCC tissues and their paired adjacent non-tumor counterparts utilizing a tissue microarray platform combined with immunohistochemical (IHC) analysis. SURF4 was knocked down by lentivirus-mediated short hairpin RNA (shRNA) in PLC/PRF/5 and Huh-7 cell lines. The effects of SURF4 knockdown on HCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion were evaluated through a series of experiments. A subcutaneous xenograft model in nude mice was established to investigate the effect of SURF4 knockdown on in vivo tumor growth. Subsequently, quantitative proteomic analysis was conducted, which identified RRM2 as a key differentially expressed protein. For functional rescue assays, cells were transduced with Lenti‑RRM2 or control vectors. Results showed that RRM2 overexpression reversed the proliferative, migratory, and invasive phenotypes induced by SURF4 knockdown in HCC cells. Finally, we examined the expression changes of key downstream signaling molecules and apoptosis-related proteins, thereby elucidating the role of SURF4 in HCC cell apoptosis. SURF4 protein was highly expressed in HCC tissues, and its expression level was significantly correlated with tumor size, differentiation grade, and microvascular invasion. Cytological experiments confirmed that SURF4 was highly expressed in HCC cell lines, promoting cell proliferation, invasion, and migration. SURF4 knockdown effectively inhibited the growth of HCC cells in nude mouse xenograft experiments. Quantitative proteomics, bioinformatic analyses, and Western blot assays demonstrated that SURF4 promoted proliferation, migration, and invasion while inhibiting apoptosis in HCC cells by upregulating RRM2 expression and activating the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. SURF4 was highly expressed in HCC tissues and cell lines. Its overexpression promoted HCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, while inhibiting apoptosis, by upregulating RRM2 and thereby regulating the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway.

Article.Title: Tariffs, FDI, and tourism drive transport CO2 emissions: evidence from SCO countries
Article.Authors: Imran M.; Zhang H.; Wei N.; Alzuman A.; Liu Q.; Mamirkulova G.; Zhang X.; Du S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) includes fast emerging member states with their trade, investment and industrial policies affecting trans boundary ecosystem. The study examines how tariff laws, tourism, direct foreign investment, industrialization, and inflation affect CO 2 emissions in the transport sector in the SCO members from 1994 to 2024. The study is the first inclusive analytical research of tariff regimes on transport CO 2 emissions in SCO countries using principal component analysis, dynamic panel autoregressive distributed lag-error correction mechanism and kernel regularized least squares models as one unified analytical model. There is a relationship between FDI, ITA, TRM, TRA, and CO 2 emissions that are in equilibrium in the long term, and that CO 2 emissions are highly persistent. Despite the fact that it decreases over time, FDI reduces the CO 2 emissions; however, industrialization is the most prevalent source of CO 2 emission. The causative effects of ITA on CO 2 emissions are more pronounced in the medium- and long-run, though the short-term effects depend on the individual policies. TRA affects tourism in China positively whilst negatively affecting tourism in India and Pakistan; however, the opposite is true of TRM. The study also enhances to the trade-environment theory by showing that the tariff mechanisms toil through assorted channels and so contest the assumption of a uniform impact of the tariffs. Instead of limiting the flow of investments in the SCO countries, policymakers should offer special relief on tariffs and focus on FDI as the way to facilitate transfer of clean technology.

Article.Title: Exploring the potential of cold plasma for nitrogen enrichment in diverse soil types of Kerala
Article.Authors: P. D.; Philip P.; K.P. S.; P.S. P.; V.I. B.
Article.Abstract: Atmospheric cold plasma is a novel green technology which generates highly reactive species at room temperature. Cold plasma exposure converts inert atmospheric nitrogen to plant available nitrates and ammonium ions in the soil. The present study aims to standardise voltage levels in major soil types of Kerala for achieving sufficient nitrogen enrichment with minimal impact on soil microbial activity. Selected soils were subjected to atmospheric cold plasma at low (5 kV), medium (10 kV) and high (15 kV) voltage levels for 10 min duration. Results have shown significant increase in available, total, ammoniacal and nitrate nitrogen content in all the studied soils with highest enrichment at 15 kV in most of the soils. Coastal sandy soil has shown the highest per cent increase in available nitrogen at 5 kV (214 per cent) and 10 kV (457 per cent), and black soil has exhibited the highest per cent increase at 15 kV (269 per cent). Optimum voltage level was found to be 5 kV for all the selected soils except coastal sandy soil, at which more than two-fold increase in available nitrogen content was observed with low energy consumption. Applied voltage level and inherent soil properties can play a decisive role on the effect of cold plasma treatment in all the soil types.

Article.Title: Acute effect of immersive VR technology on postural control and reaction time in young adults: a randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Kochman M.; Krućko M.; Niekurzak I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Immersive virtual reality (VR) has become a promising tool for sports training and rehabilitation due to its potential in modulating sensorimotor function. However, the acute effects of a single VR session on sensory organization and reaction time remain unclear, especially when both outcomes are assessed simultaneously. In this randomized controlled trial we investigated whether an acute VR intervention changes sensory organization and reaction time (LOS RT) in healthy young adults. Eighty-one healthy adults aged 18–25 years were randomly assigned to an immersive VR group ( n = 41) or a passive control group ( n = 40). The VR group completed a physically active 20-minute immersive VR motor task using an HTC VIVE Cosmos head-mounted display, whereas controls rested in a seated position for the same duration. Computerized dynamic posturography was performed before and immediately after the intervention using the Neurocom SMART EquiTest system. The primary outcome was the Sensory Organization Test (SOT) Composite Score. Secondary outcomes included the somatosensory (SOM), visual (VIS), vestibular (VEST), and visual preference (PREF) indices, as well as reaction time (LOS RT) measured during the Limits of Stability test. The primary intervention effect was assessed using ANCOVA adjusted for the corresponding baseline value. At baseline, the VR group had lower Composite Score and VEST values than the control group. After adjustment for baseline values, no significant between-group difference was observed for Composite Score (adjusted mean difference 0.51, 95% CI − 1.53 to 2.55; p = 0.623). Similarly, no significant between-group differences were observed for SOM (1.29, 95% CI − 1.59 to 4.17; p = 0.380), VIS (− 1.01, 95% CI − 4.96 to 2.94; p = 0.615), VEST (− 1.20, 95% CI − 6.00 to 3.59; p = 0.623), PREF (0.55, 95% CI − 2.97 to 4.07; p = 0.761), or LOS RT (0.004 s, 95% CI − 0.049 to 0.058; p = 0.872). A sensitivity analysis based on group × time interactions yielded a consistent pattern, with no statistically significant between-group differences in change over time. Under the conditions of this randomized controlled trial, a single 20-minute session of immersive VR did not produce statistically detectable between-group effects on postural control or LOS reaction time in healthy young adults. Although some within-group changes were observed, these did not differ significantly from changes in the passive control group and may therefore reflect nonspecific factors such as repeated testing or familiarization. Article.Title: A SMOTE enhanced multi stream deep learning ensemble for credit card fraud detection
Article.Authors: Alharbi L.; Alsulami F.
Article.Abstract: Credit card fraud detection is highly imbalanced, making minority-class metrics and deployment efficiency more informative than accuracy alone. This study proposes SMOTE-EnsembleNet (SENet), combining CNN, BiLSTM, and Transformer streams through learnable cross-attention fusion. Among 100%, 200%, and 500% SMOTE ratios with focal loss, 200% SMOTE achieved the best overall balance. SENet obtained AUC-ROC values of 0.9967 (95% CI 0.9955–0.9979), 0.9567 (95% CI 0.9542–0.9592), and 0.9923 (95% CI 0.9911–0.9935) on ULB, IEEE-CIS, and PaySim, respectively. Compared with no SMOTE, AUC-ROC improved by 1.55, 1.55, and 1.34 percentage points, while cross-attention improved AUC-ROC by 0.22 percentage points over concatenation. Fold-level significance testing ((p < 0.05)) was conducted against all tuned baselines. SENet achieved 12.4 ms inference latency per transaction on an NVIDIA A100 GPU while supporting interpretable error and feature-importance analyses. AUC-ROC and AUC-PR are threshold-independent, whereas precision, recall, and F1-score are reported separately in the experiments. The 12.4 ms latency applies only to the stated NVIDIA A100 configuration. Cross-attention additionally improved AUC-PR by 1.3 percentage points over concatenation, and the small differences between 200% and 500% SMOTE are interpreted together with fold-level statistical tests.

Article.Title: Performance optimization of cement-modified bajra mortar for sustainable heritage masonry conservation in Nepal
Article.Authors: Sapkota S.; Sahani K.; Bhusal B.; Kunwar A.; Dhakal P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Traditional Bajra mortar, widely used in Nepal’s Malla- and Rana-era monuments, is highly compatible with historic masonry but exhibits low mechanical strength and limited documented performance, restricting its use in modern heritage conservation. This study investigates the mechanical performance of eight mortar mixes spanning cement, cement–surkhi, lime, and Bajra-based systems, with particular focus on enhancing Bajra mortar through a 10% addition of cement in lime-based mortar along with indigenous additives, namely surkhi (brick powder), chaku (concentrated jaggery), and maas (black lentil paste). All mixes were evaluated for workability, water absorption, and 35-day compressive strength following IS 2250:1981, ASTM C1403-00, and IS 6932 (Part VII):1973, respectively. Compressive behaviour was further validated using finite element analysis in ABAQUS based on the Concrete Damaged Plasticity model calibrated with the Kent–Park constitutive relationship. The incorporation of chaku and maas increased compressive strength from 2.10 to 3.14 MPa (≈ 50%), while the 10% cement-modified mix (1 L:2Su:0.05 Ma:0.4Ch:0.1 C) achieved the strength of 4.21 MPa, representing a 34.24% improvement over conventional Bajra mortar, along with a 47.9% reduction in water absorption. Numerical predictions agreed well with experimental results, with differences ranging from 3.81 to 7.72%. Life-cycle and cost analyses showed that the 10% cement-modified bajra mortar retained an embodied carbon of 316.49 kg-CO₂/m³, which was 53.66% lower than that of conventional cement mortar, while reducing masonry construction costs by approximately $8.32 per cubic meter. These findings demonstrate that limited cement addition, combined with traditional additives, produces a stronger, more durable, breathable, low-carbon, and cost-effective mortar suitable for sustainable heritage conservation in Nepal.

Article.Title: Multicopter-assisted acoustic surveys complement ground-based transects in assessing bat activity and species group composition
Article.Authors: Huamán Roswag M.; Fietz J.; Roswag A.; Taefi T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We evaluated multicopter-based acoustic transects as a complement to traditional ground-based bat surveys, which cannot reach the airspace in which wind turbines operate. We compared species group composition and activity levels acoustically recorded along the same transect routes, surveyed simultaneously at ground level and at 104 m height with two multicopter types, across three habitat types (forest, meadow, and waterbody). Overall bat activity was almost eight times higher at ground level than at 104 m. Myotis species were virtually absent at 104 m, Pipistrelloid activity declined strongly with height, and Nyctaloid activity did not differ significantly between the two heights. Activity at 104 m was largely unrelated to the habitat structure at ground level. The two multicopter types did not differ in recorded activity when the recording device was positioned sufficiently below the multicopter and oriented away from it. Multicopter-based acoustic transects therefore extend the vertical reach of bat surveys into the risk area around wind turbine nacelles and can inform conservation and mitigation planning.

Article.Title: Social environment and entrepreneurial intentions among college students: the mediated effect of proactive personality
Article.Authors: Ye M.; Lv A.
Article.Abstract: Entrepreneurial intention is associated with both students’ social environments and individual characteristics, but their connection is not yet fully discussed. Drawing on social cognitive theory, we take university support, family background, and peer influence into a social-environment framework and examine the mediating role of proactive personality. We use data from 1,058 university students surveyed in China and apply partial least squares structural equation modeling to test the proposed relationships. The results show that university support, family background, and peer influence are all positively associated with entrepreneurial intention. They are also positively related to proactive personality. Proactive personality partially mediates the relationship between each social-environment dimension and entrepreneurial intention, while the direct relationships remain significant. The results further show that the three social environments are related but do not operate in exactly the same way. Overall, this research connects social context and individual characteristics within one framework and provides a more integrated explanation of how university students form entrepreneurial career intentions.

Article.Title: Integrated analysis of DNA repair and neuroendocrine marker expression in large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma with external small cell lung cancer reference data
Article.Authors: Put A.; Schwarzerová J.; Krystofova H.; Švecová P.; Mate E.; Weckwerth W.; Mitták M.; Černeková R.; Megyesfalvi Z.; Skarda J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lung cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) represents a rare and highly aggressive subtype that combines features of small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), creating challenges for diagnosis and therapy. Its molecular heterogeneity, particularly regarding DNA repair and neuroendocrine differentiation, remains poorly understood and limits the development of targeted treatment approaches. We performed an integrated analysis of patient-derived LCNEC samples, combining quantitative gene expression profiling with curated pathway databases. Boolean network modeling and rule-based simulations were employed to explore signaling and DNA repair pathway dynamics in LCNEC and SCLC. Clinical and histopathological parameters were correlated with gene expression data to identify potential biomarkers and regulatory mechanisms. Gene expression profiling revealed substantial heterogeneity across LCNEC tumors. Exploratory correlation analysis identified a moderate positive association between RAD51 and ASCL1 expression (Pearson r = 0.56, n = 17, P = 0.021), whereas the association between BRCA1 and RAD51 expression was weak and non-significant ( r = 0.15, n = 17, P = 0.573). The previously reported association between BRCA1 and BRCA2 expression was re-evaluated in the quality-controlled TaqMan subset and is reported separately together with the corresponding sample size and statistical significance. Peritumoral inflammation showed a strong positive correlation with vascular invasion ( r = 0.68, n = 16, P = 0.0035), whereas neither feature was significantly associated with tumor size. Boolean network simulations revealed that SCLC maintained multiple attractor states, consistent with phenotypic plasticity, whereas LCNEC displayed a more constrained attractor profile, in line with its distinct phenotype characteristics. Overall, these exploratory findings highlight potential relationships between neuroendocrine phenotype, DNA repair–associated gene expression, and tumor microenvironment features, while requiring validation in larger cohorts. Our study suggests that LCNEC displays marked transcript-level heterogeneity in selected DNA repair–associated and neuroendocrine lineage–associated genes. External SCLC reference data and in-silico modeling provide additional context for potential differences in regulatory network behavior between LCNEC and SCLC. Rather than demonstrating a causal RAD51–DLL3 regulatory mechanism, these findings generate hypotheses regarding possible interactions between DNA repair and neuroendocrine differentiation programs in LCNEC. Functional validation will be required to determine whether these transcript-level and model-derived associations translate into altered DNA repair capacity, DLL3 regulation, or proliferative behavior. Integrated molecular profiling and systems biology modeling may support future stratification approaches for this rare lung cancer subtype.

Article.Title: Sustainable agro-waste ash reinforced aluminium matrix composites with emerging potential of nano-banana peel ash in Al7075
Article.Authors: Prasad C.; Rao N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The development of sustainable aluminium matrix composites using agricultural waste-derived reinforcements provides an alternative approach to utilizing biomass residues in advanced engineering materials. In this study, nanoscale banana peel ash (Nano-BPA) was synthesized through dehydration, calcination, and high-energy ball milling and incorporated into an Al7075 alloy by stir casting. Nano-BPA was characterized using particle size analysis (PSA), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). The Al7075 base alloy and composites containing 2 and 4 wt% Nano-BPA were fabricated and evaluated under dry sliding wear, Charpy impact, and immersion corrosion conditions. Particle size analysis yielded a D50 value of 20.2 nm, with D10 and D90 values of 12.4 and 33.8 nm, respectively. The specific wear rate decreased from 1.160 × 10⁻⁴ mm³/(N·m) for Al7075 to 8.456 × 10⁻⁵ and 3.315 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m) for the 2 and 4 wt% Nano-BPA composites, respectively. The absorbed impact energy increased from 5.5 ± 0.20 J for Al7075 to 7.0 ± 0.25 and 8.0 ± 0.30 J for the 2 and 4 wt% Nano-BPA composites, respectively. After 72 h of immersion in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution, the measured corrosion rate decreased from 0.649 ± 0.027 mm/year for Al7075 to 0.460 ± 0.027 and 0.203 ± 0.014 mm/year for the 2 and 4 wt% Nano-BPA composites, respectively. Among the investigated compositions, the 4 wt% Nano-BPA composite exhibited the best overall measured performance. These results demonstrate the feasibility of Nano-BPA as a sustainable reinforcement for improving the experimentally evaluated wear, impact, and corrosion performance of Al7075 composites.

Article.Title: Lightweight BGS-YOLOv8 for surface crack detection in civil engineering infrastructure
Article.Authors: Fang Q.; Li W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To address the problems of false detection and excessive parameters in surface crack detection for civil infrastructure inspection, we propose an improved BGS-YOLOv8 method. First, we incorporate singular value decomposition based on cumulative contribution rate into the C2f modules to reduce model parameters while preserving important crack features. Second, we design a multi-dimensional channel importance evaluation model and an adaptive backtracking recovery method to compensate for the accuracy loss caused by over-compression. Experimental results on the RDD2022 dataset demonstrate that BGS-YOLOv8 improves mAP@0.5 by 2.33% over YOLOv8, while reducing parameters by 22.92% and GFLOPs by 18.29%. Although the current validation is conducted on road-surface images, the lightweight design is intended to be applicable to other surface crack inspection tasks, such as concrete structures.

Article.Title: Contemporary cardiometabolic and inflammation targeting therapies reduce residual cardiovascular risk in an endpoint harmonized meta analysis
Article.Authors: Bashir M.; Chen C.; Mohammad A.; Ahmed R.; Wang Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Residual cardiovascular risk remains substantial despite contemporary preventive therapy. Multiple pharmacological strategies targeting metabolic, lipid-related, cardiorenal, and inflammatory pathways have shown cardiovascular benefit in randomized trials, but differences in endpoint definitions and composite outcome structures complicate cross-trial interpretation. We aimed to evaluate whether contemporary cardiometabolic and anti-inflammatory therapies are associated with lower major adverse cardiovascular event risk using an endpoint-harmonized framework. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials evaluating sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 inhibitors, omega-3 fatty acid-based therapies, and anti-inflammatory agents. Databases were searched from inception through February 2026. The primary outcome was endpoint-harmonized major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as the trial-reported cardiovascular composite endpoint judged most comparable across studies according to prespecified harmonization rules. A prespecified sensitivity analysis was restricted to strict 3-point MACE, defined as cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, and nonfatal stroke. Hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled on the log scale using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung–Knapp adjustment. Seventeen randomized trials involving 157,278 participants and 15,815 events contributed to the primary endpoint-harmonized analysis. Active therapy was associated with a lower risk of MACE than control (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.79–0.88; I²=51%). In the sensitivity analysis restricted to strict 3-point MACE, 10 trials involving 98,973 participants and 9,067 events yielded a consistent pooled estimate with no observed heterogeneity (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.80–0.86; I²=0%). Directionally consistent benefit was observed for sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, and anti-inflammatory therapies. Estimates for proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 inhibitors and omega-3 fatty acid-based therapies were based on limited trials and should be interpreted cautiously. No statistically significant effect modification by therapeutic class was detected, although the analysis was not designed to establish comparative equivalence across classes. Across randomized trials, contemporary cardiometabolic and anti-inflammatory therapies were associated with lower major adverse cardiovascular event risk. The consistency of findings in the strict 3-point MACE sensitivity analysis supports the robustness of the overall association. However, differences in heterogeneity and precision across therapeutic classes suggest that these therapies should not be assumed to be clinically interchangeable.

Article.Title: Physics-guided residual inverse-transition modeling for continuum robots with simulation and ordered experimental evaluation
Article.Authors: Morakchi M.; Talhi A.; Ghoul A.; Djeffal S.; Bendriss B.; Latreche A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study distinguishes two levels that were conflated in the original submission: a tendon-driven mechanical dynamics model used only in simulation, and an ordered one-step inverse-transition estimator used for the recorded experiment. The experimental estimator does not identify force-level inverse dynamics because the supplied dataset contains no verified sampling interval, velocity, acceleration, tendon tension, actuator torque, pneumatic pressure, or contact-force channel. Instead, it predicts the next measured six-channel length-state increment from the present Cartesian state, desired Cartesian increment, and a structured representation of the measured length state. The first-order prior is a global empirical differential map, $$\widehat{{\bf J}}\in \mathbb {R}^{3\times 6}$$ , estimated only from the training block; it has rank 3, condition number 3.49, and singular values 1.425, 1.317, and 0.409. Reviewer-driven ablation further showed that the Clarke-like $$3\times 3$$ transform is a full-rank coordinate change rather than a dimensionality reduction, that appending both raw channels and deterministic modes reweights Gaussian-kernel distances, and that the one-step history term does not improve the held-out experimental prediction. The revised experimental instantiation therefore retains only the four bending coordinates $$(q_{\alpha ,1},q_{\beta ,1},q_{\alpha ,2},q_{\beta ,2})$$ in the nonlinear residual learner and excludes both the common mode and duplicated raw/mode features. On the chronologically held-out 39-transition test block, this bending-mode residual KRR obtains a task-space RMSE of 0.365 mm and a cable/length-state RMSE of 0.745 mm, compared with 0.469 mm for a validation-tuned direct KRR, 0.596 mm for ridge regression, 0.654 mm for the NARX-feature model, and 0.795 mm for the global empirical prior. A four-sample moving-block bootstrap gives a within-trajectory 95% interval of approximately 0.282–0.437 mm for the revised task-space RMSE. A paired sign-randomization test against direct KRR gives $$p\approx 0.060$$ , so the small test block does not justify a claim of statistically conclusive superiority over that strongest nonlinear baseline. The independently learned forward evaluator has a test component RMSE of 0.139 mm and vector RMSE of 0.240 mm, but its larger validation error also reveals chronological distribution shift. Accordingly, the revised claims are restricted to free-space, one-step inverse-transition prediction on the recorded trajectory family; no cross-speed, cross-platform, force/contact, or closed-loop hardware generalization is claimed.

Article.Title: Musculoskeletal pain, functional impact, and associations with recorded sex in an adult sample from Mashhad, Iran: a cross-sectional secondary analysis
Article.Authors: Nazary-Moghadam S.; Ziaee A.; Mirinezhad S.; Jafarzadeh S.
Article.Abstract: We conducted a cross-sectional secondary analysis of musculoskeletal data collected within a parent survey in Mashhad, Iran, between May 2024 and March 2025. Descriptive analyses included all 1,074 participants with musculoskeletal data; recorded-sex comparisons included 1,049 participants (624 men and 425 women), and age-adjusted models included 1,037. A study-specific Persian questionnaire recorded pain in nine anatomical regions during the previous 12 months and 7 days, difficulty with normal activities, and physician consultation. In a post hoc exploratory analysis, multisite pain (at least two regions) affected 78.8% over 12 months and 62.3% over 7 days. Twelve-month knee and lower-back pain were reported by 65.5% and 57.8%, respectively. In exploratory age-adjusted analyses, women had lower prevalence than men of knee pain (prevalence ratio 0.71, 95% confidence interval 0.64–0.78; marginal prevalence difference −22.1 percentage points, −28.2 to −16.1) and lower-back pain (0.69, 0.61–0.78; −20.1 percentage points, −26.4 to −13.8). The direction of all 36 regional associations persisted after adjustment for available covariates. Estimates were unweighted and not adjusted for the intended sampling design. These findings describe the analyzed subset; selective participation, residual confounding, and sparse representation of younger and oldest adults restrict generalizability.

Article.Title: RBM39 regulates malignant progression in lung adenocarcinoma cells through alternative splicing of NRG1-206
Article.Authors: Li S.; Li Y.; Tursun I.; Zhang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To investigate the function of RBM39 in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), with a particular focus on its regulatory effect on the alternative splicing of NRG1-206 and its role in tumor progression. Differential expression analysis of RNA binding proteins (RBPs) in LUAD samples was performed using TCGA datasets. RBM39 expression levels were validated by RT-qPCR and western blot. Functional assays, including cell proliferation, apoptosis, invasion, and migration were conducted using A549 cells with RBM39 or NRG1-206 overexpression. RNA-seq was employed to explore RBM39-mediated gene expression and alternative splicing regulation, and iRIP-seq combined with bioinformatics tools was used to identify binding motifs and downstream targets. Our results indicated that RBM39 expression was significantly downregulated in LUAD tissues and was associated with poor prognosis. Overexpression of RBM39 in A549 cells significantly inhibited proliferation and invasion while promoting apoptosis (all p < 0.05). Transcriptomic profiling revealed that RBM39 regulated gene expression and alternative splicing, with enrichment in immune and transcriptional pathways. iRIP-seq confirmed direct binding of RBM39 to pre-mRNAs including NRG1. Notably, RBM39 modulated the alternative splicing of NRG1, particularly suppressing the oncogenic NRG1-206 isoform. Functional rescue experiments showed that overexpression of NRG1-206 reversed the tumor-suppressive effects of RBM39. Overall, RBM39 exerts an antitumor effect in A549 cells by regulating gene expression and alternative splicing, largely by inhibiting the generation of the oncogenic NRG1-206 isoform to suppress malignant progression, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for LUAD.

Article.Title: Sustainable signal-processing spectrophotometric approaches for synchronous analysis of novel antiallergic combination: evaluation via multi-metric sustainability indices
Article.Authors: Abd El-Hadi H.; Fawzy M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents the development and validation of six sustainable signal-processing spectrophotometric approaches designed for the synchronous analysis of a novel antiallergic combination: Doxylamine succinate (DOX) and Phenylephrine hydrochloride (PHE). To resolve spectral overlap without chemical separation, various mathematical frameworks were employed, including: dual wavelength (DW), fourier self-deconvolution (FSD), first derivative (D 1 ), derivative ratio (DD 1 ), amplitude modulation (AM), and the amplitude summation (A-sum) method. The analytical procedures were conducted within linear ranges of 8.0–56.0 µg/mL for DOX and 20.0–180.0 µg/mL for PHE. Several processing parameters and wavelengths selection were optimized for each approach. DW approach is utilized ΔA 263.0–284.0 for DOX and ΔA 274.0–254.0 for PHE. The FSD method is applied at 286.0 for DOX and 278.0 nm for PHE. While D 1 amplitude is measured at 273.0 and 263.0 nm for DOX and PHE, respectively. The DD 1 approach utilized 237.0 nm for DOX and 287.0 nm for PHE. AM method was carried out at 277.0 nm while, A- sum method was applied at 288.0 nm for estimation of both DOX and PHE. All six methodologies showed excellent accuracy and precision according to ICH guidelines. Statistical comparison with established reference methods revealed no significant differences in performance. The environmental and practical impact of the methods was evaluated via multi-metric sustainability modern tools. The analytical greenness metric for sample preparation, the spider method, the green solvent selection too, Blue Applicability Grade Index, Click Analytical Chemistry Index, and Violet Innovation Grade Index were among the twelve newly created assessment metrics. Additionally, the Carbon Footprint Reduction Index, the Analytical Green Star Area, the Sustainability of Analytical Methods Index, the Modified GAPI, the Whiteness Evaluation for Chemical Analysis, and the Analytical Method Reliability Index. The results demonstrate that these signal-processing approaches offer a highly efficient, eco-friendly, and cost-effective alternative for the quality control of DOX and PHE in both raw materials and commercial tablets.
