Article.Title: Development and psychometric evaluation of the halal food and nutrition literacy scale (HFNLS) in Turkish adults
Article.Authors: Şahin Bayram S.; Karademir E.; Büyükdere Y.; Arı Gedik B.; Ersoy Yalçın S.
Article.Abstract: Religious beliefs, particularly Islamic halal principles, influence food preferences and consumer behavior. This study highlights the global significance of halal certification and the halal industry. Furthermore, it aimed to clarify the definitions of halal food and nutrition literacy-terms that are not well-defined in the current literature, and to develop the Halal Food and Nutrition Literacy Scale (HFNLS) to assess this concept among Muslim adults. This methodological study was conducted in three stages: (1) literature review and item pool generation, (2) expert evaluation and optimization of items, and (3) psycometric evaluation. Data were collected through a web-based, interviewer-administered method. The study sample size consisted of 552 adults aged 20 years or older. An exploratory factor analysis (EFA) was conducted in 285 participants, and a confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) was performed using data from an independent sample of 267 Muslim adults. EFA yielded a 28-item scale with three dimensions that together explained 52.764% of the total variance. As a result of CFA, the fit indices showed an acceptable and near-good fit of the data to the hypothesized model (χ 2 /df = 2.657, p < 0.001, root mean square error of approximation (RMSEA) = 0.053, standardized root mean residual (SRMR) = 0.047, goodness-of-fit index (GFI) = 0.913, comparative fit index (CFI) = 0.927, incremental fit index (IFI) = 0.925, Tucker Lewis index (TLI) = 0.906, and normed fit index (NFI) = 0.880). The Cronbach’s alpha (α) coefficient was 0.917 for the total scale, indicating excellent internal consistency. The Cronbach’s α coefficients for each dimension exceeded 0.80. The developed HFNLS demonstrated satisfactory construct validity and high internal consistency as a multidimensional instrument for assessing halal food and nutrition literacy among Muslim adults. The three-factor structure identified by EFA was supported by CFA, indicating that functional, interactive, and critical literacy represent related but distinct dimensions of the construct. These findings support the use of the HFNLS in research and practice; however, further validation in culturally, geographically, and religiously diverse Muslim populations is warranted.

Article.Title: Spatial heterogeneity and driving mechanisms of tourism resources vary across county types in Central China
Article.Authors: Jun L.
Article.Abstract: This paper selects Xinxian County (mountainous revolutionary heritage area), Linzhou City (mountainous complex landscape), and Huaxian County (plain-linear heritage) in Henan Province as representative cases exhibiting pronounced geomorphic and cultural contrasts. The study systematically applies four spatial analytical methods: the Voronoi polygon coefficient of variation, kernel density estimation, standard deviation ellipse, and the Geodetector model. Through this integrated methodological framework, the study reveals the distinct spatial differentiation patterns of tourism resources across the three counties and uncovers their underlying, context-specific driving mechanisms. The findings demonstrate that: (1) While tourism resources in all three counties are spatially concentrated, their configurations diverge markedly: Xinxian County manifests a balanced “multi-core network” structure; Linzhou City is characterized by a terrain-constrained “mountain strip” pattern; and Huaxian County follows a “canal-radiation” corridor structure shaped by historical waterway infrastructure. (2) The dominant spatial drivers differ, representing distinct evolutionary pathways: Xinxian’s development is strongly associated with capital and transportation support; the distribution pattern of Linzhou is closely related to its rugged terrain and ecology; and Huaxian’s distribution is highly correlated with historical heritage inertia coupled with high-density population adherence. (3) Factor interactions exhibit significant synergistic enhancement. By introducing a multidimensional analytical framework comprising a “foundational natural basis,” a “socioeconomic supporting guarantee,” and an “animating socio-cultural core,” this study offers a contribution to the literature beyond single-factor determinism. It suggests that county-level tourism spatial configurations are the outcome of non-linear spatial coupling among geographic constraints, economic investments, and historical legacies. The findings provide empirically grounded, place-sensitive insights that may inform spatial governance to support the differentiated, high-quality development of county-level human-environmental systems.

Article.Title: Self-assembling peptide hydrogel SPG-178 effectively prevents postoperative pancreatic fistula compared with polyglycolic acid mesh with fibrin glue in rats
Article.Authors: Kado T.; Tomimaru Y.; Akita H.; Uesugi K.; Tahara K.; Ueda H.; Sakano Y.; Gotoh K.; Mukai Y.; Sasaki K.; Hasegawa S.; Yamada D.; Noda T.; Takahashi H.; Kobayashi S.; Doki Y.; Eguchi H.
Article.Abstract: Postoperative pancreatic fistula (POPF) is a common and potentially life-threatening complication after pancreatectomy. Although various methods have attempted to prevent POPF, none have proven to be fully effective. This study used a rat model to compare the efficacy of a self-assembling peptide hydrogel, SPG-178, in preventing POPF with that of polyglycolic acid mesh combined with fibrin glue (PGA + FG). A rat model of POPF was created by pancreatic transection. The rats were randomly assigned to groups in which the pancreatic stump was untreated (control) or treated with SPG-178 or PGA + FG. The groups were compared based on ascitic amylase levels, macroscopic findings at relaparotomy (saponification and adhesion), and histological examination of the resected specimens. Three days after transection, the mean (± standard deviation) ascitic amylase level was significantly lower in the SPG-178 group (109 ± 58 IU/L) than in the control (283 ± 126 IU/L) and PGA + FG (219 ± 128 IU/L) groups ( p < 0.0001). On relaparotomy, saponification around the pancreatic stump and intra-abdominal adhesions were markedly reduced in the SPG-178 group compared with the other groups. Histological analysis also found milder edema, necrosis, hemorrhage, and inflammatory cell infiltration in the SPG-178 group than in the PGA + FG group. SPG-178 demonstrated favorable sealing performance compared with PGA + FG in this rat model. These findings support further preclinical and clinical evaluation of SPG-178 as a novel sealant for preventing postoperative pancreatic fistula.

Article.Title: Enhanced UV-assisted quartz wafer bonding: unveiling the critical role of humidity gradient in surface hydroxylation and interfacial strength
Article.Authors: Wan Y.; Zhan C.; Peng K.; Zhou L.; Wu F.
Article.Abstract: Relative humidity (RH) is a critical but frequently overlooked variable that significantly impacts the reliability of ultraviolet (UV)-activated quartz-crystal wafer bonding. This study examined how relative humidity during UV activation influences hydroxyl- and water-related surface chemistry and measured interfacial strength. Exposing quartz-crystal wafers to combined 185/254 nm UV irradiation under controlled relative humidity (15–90%) revealed a non-monotonic humidity dependence of hydroxyl- and water-related spectroscopic responses, with the largest response at 45% RH. The mean measured tensile strength increased from 2.64 MPa at 15% RH to a maximum of 9.88 MPa at 45% RH. It then decreased with further increasing humidity, reaching 2.01 MPa at 90% RH. This decline is consistent with excess adsorbed water hindering intimate interfacial contact and subsequent silanol condensation. Cross-sectional TEM and EDS compared local interfaces formed at 30%, 45%, 60% and 75% RH, revealing differences in interfacial contrast and Si/O signal profiles. These findings identify a practical humidity-control window for improving the reproducibility and strength of atmospheric-pressure UV-assisted quartz-crystal wafer bonding, supporting its development for wafer-level packaging of quartz crystal resonators.

Article.Title: Interactive effects of moisture level, lactic acid bacteria, and ensiling duration on fermentation and microbial communities in barnyard millet silage
Article.Authors: Jeong S.; Soundharrajan I.; Han O.; Jung J.; Choi K.
Article.Abstract: The present study evaluated the effects of lactic acid bacteria (LAB), moisture content, and ensiling duration on nutrient composition, fermentation quality, and microbial dynamics in barnyard millet (BM) silage. BM forage was ensiled under different moisture conditions using single inoculants ( Lactiplantibacillus plantarum -TC, Lactobacillus brevis 5 M, and Lactobacillus buchneri 6 M) or combined LAB inoculants for 10, 20, and 30 days. LAB inoculation improved fermentation quality by increasing lactic acid and acetic acid production, lowering pH, and inhibiting butyric acid production. Crude protein content remained stable, whereas reductions in neutral detergent fibre (ADF) and acid detergent fibre (NDF) varied with inoculant treatments. Microbial community analysis showed that L. plantarum became the dominant bacterial species, while mixed inoculants promoted greater LAB diversity. Yeast communities were influenced by inoculum, moisture level, and ensiling duration, with Issatchenkia orientalis and Ustilago davisii predominating under different treatments. Fungal communities showed distinct temporal and treatment-dependent patterns, with Ustilago spp. and Mucor circinelloides as major taxa. Correlation analysis revealed positive associations between L. plantarum and lactic acid production, while L. buchneri was associated with acetic acid accumulation. Overall, LAB inoculation was associated with improvements in fermentation quality, microbial stability, and nutrient preservation. However, the inoculants showed significant effects under low-moisture conditions throughout the ensiling period.

Article.Title: Adaptive deanonymization of blockchain transactions leveraging integrative neural architectures in decentralized networks
Article.Authors: Saxena R.; Chaurasia B.; Awasthi A.; Upadhyay L.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The pseudonymous nature of decentralized networks like Bitcoin presents tremendous obstacles for regulatory compliance, forensic auditing, and cybercrime investigation. Traditional heuristics and single-modality machine learning (ML) frameworks provide partial transparency but usually suffer from the modality isolation problem, which fails to consider spatial graph structure, temporal transaction velocity, and local metadata patterns simultaneously. To break these limitations, in this paper, we propose an adaptive behavioral deanonymization method for blockchain transactions at the entity level based on an integrative neural architecture (CNN → LSTM → GNN) that dynamically focuses on spatial, temporal, and structural signals based on the behavior of the entity. The integrative neural uses a Disjoint Set Union (DSU) algorithm to combine temporary address artifacts into 140,235 resolved actor clusters, lowering ledger noise by 67.2%. The proposed architecture uses 1D-Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for extracting local structural fingerprints, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for capturing temporal sequence velocity, and Graph Neural Networks (GNN) over a dynamic k-Nearest Neighbor (k-NN) adjacency matrix for aggregating neighborhood context. The architecture uses cost-sensitive learning (weighted cross-entropy) to tackle the significant class imbalance (1:500) to maintain analytical authenticity and forensics standards without synthetic distortion. The proposed architecture is assessed on a sample of a dataset of 427,625 transactions, achieving an overall classification accuracy of approximately 97%, which is better than the baseline models, and generating a transparent, explainable audit trail using SHAP and LIME feature attribution.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: cost-sensitive learning; pseudonymity; Bitcoin; class imbalance; SHAP feature attribution
Article.TopicFields: Computer Science > Information Systems > Blockchain Technology Applications and Security; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Privacy-Preserving Technologies in Data; Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence > Internet Traffic Analysis and Secure E-voting

Article.Title: BioInteract combines residue-level cross-attention with protein-language and physicochemical priors for interpretable drug–target interaction prediction
Article.Authors: Wang S.; Zhang Q.; Liu X.; Wang Z.; Cheng J.; Huang Z.
Article.Abstract: Accurate prediction of drug–target interactions (DTIs) can support the prioritisation of candidate pairs, yet published models are usually compared through numbers quoted across papers whose protocols differ, and their attribution outputs are rarely accompanied by an explicit statement of where the model may be trusted. We present BioInteract, a DTI framework combining a chemistry-aware molecular graph encoder, an ESM-2/physicochemical protein residue encoder with a configured domain-label channel, and bidirectional cross-attention, and we evaluate it inside a matched-protocol benchmark on the Davis kinase inhibitor dataset in which every model is trained with one shared partition, seed, optimiser, schedule and threshold rule. The comparison is a three-model ladder that changes one component at a time, so that adding the frozen ESM-2 representation and then replacing concatenation with cross-attention can be read separately. Both steps help, but by protocol-dependent amounts: the protein language model adds 0.120 and 0.063 AUPRC under the random and Target-ID-held-out protocols, whereas cross-attention adds 0.067 and 0.201 AUPRC under the same two protocols. A breadth check across two further architecture families places these differences in context: on the random split the five architectures tested fall within a narrow band, so the controlled Target-ID-held-out ladder carries the informative contrast. We audit chemical and sequence similarity across all partitions, evaluate exact-sequence-grouped cold-start protocols, and report leakage-aware diagnostic controls. On a strict exact-entity-novel BindingDB cohort, whose construction is documented as a complete row-level filtering waterfall for both the curated-articles snapshot and the full BindingDB release, the frozen Davis checkpoint achieved an AUROC of 0.560 and an AUPRC of 0.340; an applicability-domain analysis attributes this limited transfer principally to ligand and target novelty relative to Davis. The attribution analyses generate hypotheses about model-relevant atoms and residues, but, in line with evidence from models trained with explicit non-covalent interaction supervision, unsupervised attention is not treated here as a recovered interaction mechanism. BioInteract therefore contributes an audited, reproducible and domain-of-applicability-aware DTI reference rather than a new architectural principle.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: drug-target interaction prediction; cross-attention; interpretability

Article.Title: Tuning the mechanical integrity and corrosion performance of open-cell copper foams: identification of an optimization threshold
Article.Authors: Hassan M.; El-Kady O.; Ata M.; Najih I.; Ali A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract In this work, Porous copper foam samples were fabricated by a space-holder technique with water-atomized copper powder and sodium chloride (NaCl) particles in weight fractions ranging from 10 to 35 wt%. The powders were mechanically mixed at a 10:1 ball-to-powder ratio and 150 rpm for 2 h. The effects of space-holder content on the physical, mechanical, tribological, and electrochemical performance were systematically investigated. Increasing the NaCl fraction precisely controlled the total porosity, from 39.15% to 57.76%, and reduced the bulk density from 5.452 to 3.785 g/cm³. XRD and SEM analyses confirmed a single-phase FCC copper matrix and a structural transition from isolated pores to a highly interconnected open-cell network. Consequently, Vickers hardness, compressive yield strength, energy absorption capacity decreased from 52.12 to 29.23 HV, 18.25 to 1.65 MPa, and 35.73 to 10.46 MJ/m³, respectively, following a modified Gibson–Ashby model (R 2 = 0.95). Concurrently, the coefficient of friction and specific wear rate increased (reaching a maximum of 0.73 mm³/N·m under 15 N for 35 wt% NaCl) due to strut thinning and localized delamination. Electrochemical evaluation in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution revealed an optimization threshold for sample fabricated with 25 wt% NaCl, which exhibited the lowest corrosion rate of 0.918 mm/y, and the highest polarization resistance (Rp) of 267.28 Ω, due to a stable Cu 2 O passive film. Exceeding this threshold at 30 and 35 wt% NaCl led to structural instability and stagnant electrolyte zones, accelerating corrosion kinetics. Overall, lower-porosity porous copper foam architectures offer superior structural energy absorption, whereas the 25 wt% NaCl configuration achieves an optimal balance between mechanical integrity and corrosion resistance.

Article.Title: Intelligent MPPT in PV Systems using metaheuristic-optimised deep neural networks
Article.Authors: Sheela M.; Swathika O.
Article.Abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) systems face problems with multiple local maxima, poor tracking efficiencies and unstable maximum power point tracking (MPPT) when the irradiance changes rapidly or when there is partial shading on the panels. Traditional MPPT methods including Perturb and Observe (P&O) and Incremental Conductance display slow convergence and oscillation around the steady state in the changing environment. This paper proposes a Digital Twin-based Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO-Deep Neural Network) intelligent MPPT system for solar PV systems to overcome these two issues.This paper proposes a hybrid Grey wolf optimization –Deep neural Network (GWO_DNN) based MPPT technique for photovoltaic systems. The comparison between hybrid deep neural network (DNN)-based controllers for maximally tracking MPPs through Grey Wolf Optimisation (GWO), Golden Eagle Optimisation (GO) and Moth-Flame Algorithm (MFA) are evaluated by comparing relative effectiveness based upon converging performance, prediction accuracy, computational efficiency and stability. The proposed method improves tracking efficiency, reduces steady-state oscillations and achieves faster convergence under varying irradiance conditions. Computational models show GWO-DNN controllers achieving lower test mean absolute distance from the true MPP compared to the other controllers with mean absolute mean square errors (MAE) reported as 0.6138 V (GWO-DNN), 0.3506 V (MFA-DNN) and 0.4978 V (GO-DNN). The GWO-DNN controllers also have a lower degree of oscillation in steady-state conditions, showing faster convergence than all other controllers as well as significantly lower prediction errors. In contrast, Moses-DNN performs more reliably with respect to optimal positioning, but its predictive capabilities will limit its effectiveness for practical real-time implementation. Although GO-DNN provides lower inference time than both the GWO app and MFA model as is a whole, the standard deviation of how far down the MPP would be estimated will increase for the time taken to make the prediction. A traditional CNN-LSTM model has demonstrated to consistently underperform under dynamic operating conditions. Thus, the results demonstrate that GWO-DNN represents a superior balance of MPPT controller characteristics across dynamic operating ranges, as such, GWO-DNN will provide the most robust and predictable MPP capability for use in smart solar energy applications. This initiative helps meet the UN Sustainable Development Goals through the past improvements made in renewable energy extraction efficiency, the creation of more intelligent energy infrastructure and ultimately the contribution to greater levels of solar energy production, while also reducing wasted energy through better designs. Specifically, it contributes to SDG7 - Affordable and Clean Energy; SDG9 - Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure; and SDG13 - Climate Action by facilitating the creation of sustainable, resilient and low-carbon energy systems.

Article.Title: Acute transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation is associated with lower baroreflex sensitivity without detectable Mayer-wave coherence change: an exploratory study
Article.Authors: Katahara Y.; Iijima A.; Tainaka K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) delivers afferent inputs, but cardiovascular responses are heterogeneous and autonomic outcomes are not interchangeable. In this exploratory, non-randomised, open-label study, 18 healthy men completed fixed-order five-minute Pre, left-cymba Stim, and Post phases without sham. Spontaneous sequence baroreflex sensitivity (BRS seq, all ; designated centrally post hoc) was lower during Stim than Pre (8.54 ± 5.57 versus 6.49 ± 3.89 ms/mmHg; paired mean difference − 2.05, BCa 95% CI − 3.81 to − 1.10; Wilcoxon p = 2.29 × 10 − 5 ; Cohen’s d z = − 0.74), with negative differences in 17/18 participants. Mayer-band coherence and representative heart rate variability indices showed no detectable Stim–Pre differences. Systolic blood pressure was higher during Stim. Recovery of BRS was not established. No adverse events were reported after the sessions. Sequence BRS estimates blood pressure–R–R interval gain, whereas heart rate variability and coherence quantify different properties. This pattern supports prospective evaluation of sequence BRS as a session-level physiological response measure. The design does not establish stimulation-specific engagement, direct vagal inhibition, clinical utility, or a monitoring threshold. Sham-controlled replication is required. Trial registration: Japan Registry of Clinical Trials (jRCT), jRCT1032230440. Registered on 9 November 2023.

Article.Title: Correction of the transient thermal analysis model for the solar extreme ultraviolet imager based on in-orbit data
Article.Authors: Kang Z.; Chen L.; Liu S.; Li Y.; Zhao M.
Article.Abstract: After obtaining experimental or in-orbit temperature data, the finite element model must be corrected to align the simulation results with the actual measurements. Current research primarily focuses on steady-state corrections, considering only the average temperature. Transient model corrections additionally account for temperature fluctuations. The present study focuses on the correction of transient thermal analysis models for complex satellite systems. Initially, parameter sampling is executed based on an enhanced Latin Hypercube design, thereby enhancing fitting accuracy by improving sample orthogonality. Sensitivity analysis is then employed to select parameters for subsequent correction. Secondly, a transient surrogate model was constructed to link correction parameters and simulated temperatures. The model was created using a multi-layer perceptron. Finally, the Animated Oat Optimization and StarFish Optimization algorithms are employed to optimize the error function between simulation and in-orbit temperatures at β = 57.4° (the angle between the solar vector and the orbital plane). This approach traverses the corrected parameters, thereby determining the true values of thermal-physical parameters. The surrogate model and optimization algorithms further enhance the efficiency and accuracy of the correction process. The correction results demonstrate a reduction of 6.64 °C in the maximum temperature deviation under the β = 57.4° operating condition. Furthermore, the efficacy of the correction was substantiated under the β = 88.6° condition, where the maximum simulation deviation diminished by 3.67 °C. This correction method enhances the accuracy of future in-orbit temperature forecasts and provides valuable reference for the thermal design of second-generation imagers.

Article.Title: Blood flow restriction of sport-specific repeated-sprint training enhances acute physiological responses in elite female boxers: a randomized, crossover trial
Article.Authors: Li S.; Wang D.; Morouço P.; Chen C.; Zhou Z.
Article.Abstract: This study investigated the acute physiological responses during sport-specific repeated sprint training with different levels at blood flow restriction (BFR) in elite boxing athletes. Sixteen female boxers participated in this randomized, cross-over study. All boxers conducted four tests under different conditions, each consisting of 3 sets of 6 repetitions of 10-sec all-out punches in non-BFR, BFR-45%, 60%, 80% arterial occlusion pressure (AOP 45 , AOP 60 , and AOP 80 ). The intervals separating repetitions and sets were 20 s and 1 min, respectively. We assessed muscle activation, muscle oxygenation saturation, Serum hormonal changes, muscle discomfort, level of perceived exertion, and punch performance. BFR induced higher levels of muscle activation and changes in muscle oxygenation saturation compared with non-BFR ( p < 0.05), especially under the AOP 80 condition. BFR can also induce an increase in serum growth hormone and nitric oxide concentrations ( p < 0.05). Although these acute physiological changes are accompanied by increased muscle soreness and impaired punching performance, boxers typically recover within 48 h. Applying blood flow restriction during punching trainings can enhance acute physiological responses in elite boxers. AOP 80 may serve as an effective strategy to enhance high-intensity punching capacity in boxers.

Article.Title: External cervical spine joint moments in pilots during high +Gz real–flight: a biomechanical analysis using individual opensim models
Article.Authors: Goell F.; Braunstein B.; Lingscheid R.; Nüsse R.; Hartmann D.; Rein R.; Albracht K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The cervical spine of fast jet pilots is exposed to high +Gz accelerations during large range of head movements which may lead to biomechanical impairments. The objective of this study therefore was to quantify and analyze the resulting external cervical spine joint moments experienced by fast jet pilots during standardized head movements in real–flight during +5Gz, +7Gz and +9Gz maneuvers. The in– flight helmet orientation recordings and additional ground based motion capture recordings of isolated head movements of seven Eurofighter pilots were processed using a custom made pipeline. Subsequent inverse kinematics and inverse dynamics simulations of the in–flight head movements using individual OpenSim pilot models showed a significant reduction in the head extension angle with increasing +Gz acceleration. Cervical spine joint moments did not change significantly with increasing +Gz acceleration. However, theory–based model analysis indicated that constant head positions under higher +Gz acceleration would lead to an increase in joint moments. The pilots seemed to exhibit reduced head extension at higher +Gz levels, while external joint moments remained relatively constant. Furthermore, the designed pipeline may support individual cervical spine health assessment and monitoring, as well as to inform strength training or rehabilitation programming.

Article.Title: Citrus leaf pathology multi-class image dataset and a hybrid multi-branch attention fusion network for lemon leaf disease classification
Article.Authors: Abir C.; Biswas S.; Sahoo P.; Samantaray A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The productivity of lemon (Citrus lemon) crops is severely undermined by foliar diseases, which constitute the leading cause of global harvest degradation. The conventional reliance on manual identification by experienced specialists poses a significant bottleneck, as these methods are both time-consuming and prone to human error under field conditions. Recently, deep learning techniques have been employed to identify and diagnose citrus foliar diseases from digital images, automating the classification process and providing non-experts with accessible diagnostic tools. While several deep learning applications have been used to classify lemon diseases with the aim of improving classification accuracy, most of these studies fail to achieve high accuracy and rely on datasets with an insufficient number of disease classes. In this paper, we introduced a dataset named “Citrus Leaf Pathology Multi-Class Image Dataset” with 14 different classes, and we proposed a Hybrid Multi-Branch Attention Fusion Network (HMAF-Net). The architecture consists of four parallel feature extraction branches, each incorporating branch attention and channel attention, followed by classification using a Neural Network (NN). A DenseNet121 backbone is combined with lightweight convolutional branches, refined through squeeze-and-excitation channel attention and a learnable branch-weighting fusion mechanism to adaptively integrate complementary feature representations. The model attains 96.63% precision and 95.59% accuracy on the proposed dataset. The model further demonstrates strong generalization, achieving 97.48%, 95.89%, and 98.23% accuracy on three independent external lemon and citrus leaf datasets, with statistical significance confirmed through paired t-tests across five independent runs. Explainable AI visualizations further confirm that the model’s predictions are grounded in disease-relevant leaf regions, supporting its potential for reliable deployment in real-world agricultural diagnostic systems.

Article.Title: Polymer-modified MXene thin-film nanocomposite membranes for forward osmosis
Article.Authors: Bashardoust A.; Georgopanos P.; Shakeri A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Water scarcity demands novel solutions to address the challenges posed by increasing societal needs. This study presents a novel strategy for fabricating MXene-based thin-film nanocomposite forward osmosis (TFN-FO) membranes with enhanced permeability and selectivity, offering a promising advancement in water treatment technologies. The approach involves synthesizing MXene-functionalized polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP-g-MXene) additives through a facile chemical grafting method, where hydroxyl groups serve as linkers to covalently bond PVP onto the surface of 2D MXene nanosheets. Subsequently, PVP-g-MXene is incorporated into a polyamide (PA) thin film via interfacial polymerization (IP) to produce the innovative TFN-FO membranes. Characterization of MXene and PVP-g-MXene was performed using FT-IR, XRD, TGA, and FE-SEM. The fabricated membranes were analyzed for surface morphology, roughness, and hydrophilicity using FESEM, AFM, and water contact angle (WCA) measurements. The results indicate that incorporating PVP-g-MXene significantly alters the physicochemical properties of the membranes, including morphology, roughness, hydrophilicity, and overall performance during the IP process. All modified membranes demonstrated improved water flux compared to the pristine TFC membrane, with TFN-PgM1 and TFN-PgM2 exhibiting superior selectivity. Notably the representative TFN-PgM2 membrane exhibited a water flux of 18.5 LMH, which is approximately 72% higher than that of the TFC membrane, and demonstrated a Js/Jw ratio of 0.167, indicating an 18.1% improvement in selectivity performance. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of polymer-modified MXene for the development of high-performance FO membranes.

Article.Title: Longitudinal gut microbiome changes during the chemoradiotherapy component of total neoadjuvant therapy for rectal cancer
Article.Authors: Gal K.; Mikolas M.; Barabas M.; Fauszt P.; David P.; Szilagyi-Tolnai E.; Balogh K.; Solymosi D.; Miklos S.; Mikaczo J.; Trasi K.; Csiki E.; Simon M.; Remenyik J.; Kovacs A.; Paholcsek M.
Article.Abstract: Total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT), including fractionated external-beam radiotherapy (EBRT), may alter the gut microbiome, yet treatment-associated temporal patterns remain incompletely characterised in rectal cancer (RC). Thirteen patients with locally advanced RC were prospectively followed during the chemoradiotherapy component of TNT, with faecal samples collected before treatment (Fx0), midway through radiotherapy (Fx14), and immediately after the final fraction (Fx28). Aggregate relative frequency was lower in patients than in controls and declined across treatment, whereas Shannon diversity followed a V-shaped pattern, decreasing at Fx14 and increasing again at Fx28. Low-abundance taxa accounted for most detected species despite contributing only a small proportion of cumulative relative abundance. The relative bacterial signal declined transiently at Fx14, accompanied by an increased proportional representation of eukaryotic reads. The rectal cancer-associated taxon Fusobacterium nucleatum declined by Fx28, while the relative representation of SCFA-associated taxa shifted toward acetate-associated and away from butyrate-associated groups, particularly in samples from patients with diarrhoea. Resistome composition also changed over time, with Bacteroides fragilis identified as a prominent inferred ARG carrier. Among the three sampled time points, Fx14 showed the greatest concurrent deviation across several microbiome features, suggesting that mid-treatment may represent a period of increased ecological instability.

Article.Title: TFEB drives ER stress-induced apoptosis and limits cyst growth in polycystic kidney disease
Article.Authors: Nakamura J.; Matsui S.; Yamamoto T.; Kawai H.; Kubota T.; Takabatake Y.; Namba-Hamano T.; Takahashi A.; Minami S.; Sakai S.; Yonishi H.; Matsui I.; Yamamichi G.; Kato T.; Takenaka S.; Nonomura N.; Nishio S.; Yoshimori T.; Isaka Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) is characterized by the progressive growth of renal cysts and loss of renal function. Here, it was demonstrated that transcription factor EB (TFEB) activation in cyst-lining epithelial cells enhances their susceptibility to apoptosis via endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress-induced signaling, ultimately restricting cyst expansion. Single-cell RNA sequencing in Pkd1 -deficient mouse models identified G-protein coupled receptor family C group 5 member A (GPRC5A)-positive cyst-lining cell clusters originating from the loop of Henle and proximal tubules. These cells exhibited dysregulated Hippo signaling and enhanced unfolded protein response (UPR). With this change in UPR, nuclear localization of TFEB and C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP) was observed, and expression of pro-apoptotic target genes of CHOP, such as Ppp1r15 and Pmaip1 , increased. TFEB deficiency attenuated apoptosis, resulting in accelerated cyst growth. Human ADPKD kidney samples mirrored these findings, showing nuclear TFEB and CHOP accumulation in cyst-lining cells. These results indicated that TFEB is a key modulator of ER stress-induced apoptosis in cyst-lining cells, suggesting that TFEB activation paradoxically limits cyst expansion through apoptosis in ADPKD.

Article.Title: Behavioral characterization of 5xFAD mice using standardized decision-making and open field assays
Article.Authors: Imomdodova N.; Korde S.; Lee Y.; Cinquemani S.; Hwang E.
Article.Abstract: The 5xFAD mouse is a widely used transgenic model of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), characterized by early and aggressive amyloid-β plaque accumulation. However, the extent to which plaque burden in this model predicts functional impairment remains unclear, particularly during early to mid stages of pathology when substantial plaque deposition is already present. To further characterize behavior in this model using standardized assays, we systematically evaluated feedback-based associative learning, choice-switching behavior, and open field behavior in 5xFAD and wild-type mice (2–9 months of age) using the International Brain Laboratory decision-making task, a rigorously standardized behavioral paradigm, together with the commonly used open field test. Despite robust, age-dependent plaque accumulation, 5xFAD mice did not differ from age-matched controls in associative learning, choice-switching behavior, anxiety-like behavior, or locomotor activity. These results indicate that substantial amyloid plaque accumulation was not associated with measurable deficits in the behavioral domains examined during the early to mid stages of pathological progression. Our findings provide a standardized behavioral characterization of the 5xFAD model and highlight the need for more sensitive functional assays to further clarify the relationship between early amyloid pathology and behavioral outcomes in AD research.

Article.Title: Serine-threonine kinase 38 exerts a cancer-promoting role in hepatocellular carcinoma by stabilizing the Notch intracellular domain
Article.Authors: Mu Y.; Zhang T.; Li X.; Guo W.; Ma C.; Wang R.
Article.Abstract: Serine/threonine kinase 38 (STK38) has been increasingly recognized as a tumor-associated kinase across multiple human cancer types. Nevertheless, its potential contribution to the malignant progression of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains unexplored. The present study was therefore designed to characterize the expression landscape of STK38 in HCC and to delineate its regulatory impact on HCC cell behaviors and the underlying molecular circuitry. STK38 was robustly overexpressed in HCC tumor specimens, and this upregulation showed a clear association with unfavorable clinical outcomes. Silencing STK38 in HCC cell lines substantially attenuated cellular proliferation, migratory capacity, and invasive potential, while concomitantly augmenting the chemosensitivity of the cells. Further mechanistic dissection uncovered a tight functional link between STK38 and the Notch pathway in HCC. STK38 silencing provoked a marked reduction in the protein abundance of NICD1 as well as the canonical Notch downstream effectors HEY1 and HES1. The use of proteasome inhibitors reversed the decline in NICD1 expression induced by STK38 silencing, and overexpression of STK38 significantly reduced the degradation rate of NICD1 protein. Additionally, expressing NICD1 in STK38-silenced cells largely neutralized the tumor-suppressive effects of STK38 silencing. In a subcutaneous xenograft model, STK38 silencing significantly compromised the tumorigenic capacity of HCC cells in vivo, concomitant with suppressed Notch1 pathway activity within the tumor mass. Collectively, these findings position STK38 as a pivotal oncoprotein in HCC, acting at least in part through post-translational stabilization of NICD1 and the consequent activation of the Notch signaling axis. This work not only advances our mechanistic understanding of HCC pathogenesis but also highlights the STK38–NICD1–Notch axis as a candidate therapeutic target for this disease.

Article.Title: Application of hierarchical thermo-mechanical modelling and development of a generalized heat-source trajectory for an aluminium WAAM component
Article.Authors: Anikin P.; Bastos F.; Shilo G.
Article.Abstract: Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing enables cost effective production of metallic components, however accurate prediction of the thermo-mechanical behaviour remains computationally demanding because of complex thermal interactions, repeated heating and cooling cycles and thousands of sequentially deposited beads. This work presents an application of a three-level hierarchical thermo-mechanical modelling framework for WAAM and its experimental validation through the fabrication of an aluminium circular nozzle-like component. The methodology consists of bead layer and wall level analyses, solving the thermo-mechanical phenomena at each stage for the subsequent pass to the next level. the present framework combines transient heat transfer and structural finite element analyses to predict temperature evolution, heat accumulation, residual stress development and geometric distortion throughout the manufacturing process. The complete particular wall level simulation consists of 27 deposited layers comprising 1,431 sequentially activated beads, requiring the solution of approximately 1.7 billion of equations and 1.6 TB output database. A generalized heat source trajectory formulation based on the deposition geometry is introduced to represent transient deposition behaviour. At the bead level, it can be represented by a constant position path, at the layer, by sinusoidal trajectory, and at the wall level, by an oscillated sinusoidal function with progressively decreased amplitude. Experimental validation using a robotic GMAW-CMT WAAM system has demonstrated excellent agreement between numerical and experimental results, with fabricated component closely resemble the desired geometry and temperature peaks deviation of only 1.05 \(\%\) . The developed methodology provides a computational framework for automated WAAM process planning and optimization, establishing a basis for subsequent integration of real-time sensing and closed-loop process control.

Article.Title: Renoprotective effects of dapagliflozin and montelukast for diclofenac induced acute kidney injury through network pharmacology and experimental validation
Article.Authors: Kamal N.; Nour O.; Nader M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Diclofenac (DIC)-prompted acute kidney injury (AKI) is associated with inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and dysregulated autophagy, all of which contribute to renal impairment. Using a network pharmacology approach followed by experimental validation, this study evaluated the reno-protecting actions of dapagliflozin (DAPA) and montelukast (MON) against DIC-induced AKI in rats, both alone and in combination. DisGeNET, GeneCards, and OMIM databases were used to identify AKI targets, whereas Swiss-Target-Prediction, Super-PRED, and SEA databases were used to identify expected DAPA and MON targets. Protein–protein interaction (PPI) network, gene ontology (GO), and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment studies recognized significant pathways such as TNF-α, PI3K/AKT signalling, T-cell receptor signalling, microRNA regulation, and ROS. Experimental validation was conducted on thirty male SD rats, separated arbitrarily into five groups. A sole injection of DIC (100 mg/kg; i.p.) provoked AKI. Renal function markers, biomarkers for early kidney injury, oxidative stress, inflammatory mediators, indicators of mitochondrial biogenesis, and autophagy-related proteins were all evaluated. DIC resulted in significant renal dysfunction, oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial impairment, DNA damage, and autophagy activation. While DAPA and MON alone partially mitigated these effects, their combination, even at lower doses of both drugs, provided greater renoprotection, most likely through multi-target regulation of inflammation, oxidative stress, and autophagy pathways. These findings emphasized that combining DAPA with MON allowed dose reduction of each agent, minimizing potential side effects while achieving superior renoprotection via managing inflammation, oxidative stress, and autophagy.

Article.Title: Perceptions of aging and ageism among young adults
Article.Authors: Sütlü S.; Arslan B.
Article.Abstract: Ageism is defined as prejudice or discrimination against a person or a group of people because of their age. Ageism is recognised as an important social determinant of health. It was aimed to investigate the relationship between ageism and fear of aging among young adults and to identify the sociodemographic and psychosocial factors associated with both constructs. The population of the cross-sectional study consisted of 430 people aged between 20 and 40 years living in a province in Türkiye. Data were collected using a sociodemographic data form and the Fear of Old Age Scale and the Fraboni Older Adults Discrimination Scale. t-tests and ANOVA tests were used for analytical evaluations based on scale scores. To determine influencing factors, a forward linear regression analysis was conducted by creating a model with variables found to be significant in univariate analyses. Income status, frequency of visiting the older adults, and nursing home visits were identified as factors influencing both fear of aging and ageism. Both ageism and fear of aging were found to be lower in those who described their income as adequate and who visited the elderly weekly. Conversely, participants who had previously visited nursing homes were found to have higher levels of ageism and fear of aging.

Article.Title: Admission-time prediction of 7-day mortality in clinician-attributed hypertensive intracerebral hemorrhage: development and external validation against the ICH score
Article.Authors: Chen Q.; Zhong T.; Liu J.; Feng D.; Gao H.
Article.Abstract: Early mortality after intracerebral haemorrhage remains difficult to estimate at admission. We developed models for recorded mortality within 7 days after admission in two retrospective cohorts of clinician-attributed hypertensive intracerebral haemorrhage. Qingyuan records ( n = 1,433; 369 events) were used for grouped nested cross-validation, and Yunfu records ( n = 924; 182 events) for external validation. The models used 28 admission-time predictors. Predictions were averaged across 20 imputation-specific pipelines. Elastic-net logistic regression was selected from the development data. Its development and external areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0.848 and 0.893, respectively. In external validation, the ICH score had an area under the curve of 0.860, giving a difference of 0.0324 (95% CI 0.0126–0.0523; DeLong P = 0.00135). The external Brier score was 0.103, with a calibration intercept of − 0.504 and slope of 1.149. At the development-selected threshold of 0.1976, sensitivity was 0.901 and specificity was 0.706. The model modestly improved discrimination over the ICH score, but overprediction, differences between centres, and unavailable treatment and outcome-ascertainment details limit clinical interpretation.

Article.Title: Quality of online mastitis management information for dairy farmers in India: an evaluation of Hindi language YouTube videos
Article.Authors: Reddy D.; Bhargavi D.; Tiwari R.; Cariappa A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract YouTube has become a primary informal extension channel for livestock health information in India, yet quality is unregulated and algorithmically driven by popularity rather than accuracy. This study systematically evaluates the quality of Hindi language YouTube videos on Mastitis which is one of the most economically significant dairy diseases in India, using four validated instruments modified DISCERN (mDISCERN), JAMA benchmark criteria, Global Quality Scale (GQS), and a purpose-built Mastitis Video Content Scoring (MVCS) tool. We searched YouTube using the YouTube Data API v3 with four Hindi language queries on 6 March 2026, screened 200 videos, and analysed 63 that met inclusion criteria. Most videos were low quality: mean GQS was 1.98/5, mean JAMA was 1.21/4 and mean mDISCERN was 1.96/5. Independent creators produced 52% of videos and achieved the highest audience reach (Video Power Index: 2.32), yet scored lowest on clinical comprehensiveness. Veterinary professionals produced fewer videos but achieved the highest quality scores and engagement ratios (4.26), suggesting trust driven rather than algorithm driven audiences. A weak positive correlation between video duration and MVCS (r = 0.265, p = 0.036) indicates that longer run time is not a prerequisite for comprehensive content. These findings reveal a critical popularity-quality gap in digital veterinary extension and highlight the need to build digital communication capacity among field-level veterinarians.

Article.Title: Critical soil and leaf zinc toxicity thresholds in field-grown maize cultivated on a clayey oxisol
Article.Authors: da Silva Santos J.; Rocha A.; Campos C.; Cotrim M.; Silva A.; de Mello Prado R.
Article.Abstract: Zinc (Zn) is one of the most important micronutrients for maize cultivation and, when applied in excess, may cause physiological damage to plants. However, studies on the critical toxicity levels of Zn in clayey Oxisol under tropical conditions are still scarce, limiting the establishment of safe corrective fertilization practices. We hypothesized that: (i) Zn rates and critical soil toxicity levels would be relatively high due to the strong adsorption in clayey soils, reflected in the low Zn recovery rate by plants, and that the critical foliar toxicity level would also be relatively high, indicating a relative tolerance of maize to Zn toxicity under field conditions; and (ii) the damage caused by Zn toxicity would be more associated with oxidative stress and photosynthetic limitation than with nutritional imbalances. The objective of this study was to determine the critical toxicity levels of Zn in soil and leaves, as well as to evaluate the physiological, nutritional, and productive responses of maize. The experiment was conducted under field conditions in Jaboticabal, Brazil, using a randomized complete block design with five Zn rates (0, 12, 24, 48, and 96 kg ha⁻¹), applied as zinc sulfate in a clayey Oxisol. Soil and leaf Zn concentrations, nutrient accumulation, gas exchange, malondialdehyde content, and grain yield were evaluated. The application of 80 kg ha⁻¹ Zn reduced maize productivity by inducing toxicity and was associated with critical Zn toxicity levels of 9.9 mg dm⁻³ in soil and 74 mg kg⁻¹ in leaves. The results indicated a relative tolerance of maize to Zn toxicity in clayey soil, evidenced by the low Zn recovery rate by plants (< 1.3%) and by the high critical toxicity levels observed in both soil and leaves. In addition, the damage caused by excess Zn was mainly associated with oxidative stress and reduced photosynthetic rate, whereas the nutritional changes were not sufficient to impair the nutritional status of the crop. This study contributes to the establishment of critical Zn toxicity levels for maize and provides a scientific basis for safer corrective Zn fertilization practices through soil incorporation in tropical agricultural systems.

Article.Title: Morpho-physiological and biochemical diversity assessment of low-chill peach genotypes for germplasm conservation
Article.Authors: Akram M.; Ahmed A.; Ali I.; Abbas S.; Haider M.; Elmenofy W.; İbrahimova U.; Rzayeva A.; Mammadova R.; Muslumova Z.; Suleymanova Z.; Stanciu A.; Nampala P.
Article.Abstract: Peach ( Prunus persica L. Batsch) is an important temperate fruit grown globally for its nutritional value. There is a worldwide interest in assessing low-chilling germplasm that is well-adapted to warm regions. Exploiting diversity is essential to conserve existing germplasm and evaluate elite genotypes for breeding. The northern areas of Pakistan are rich in various local peach accessions but are rarely explored. Therefore, there is a need to characterize these accessions based on morphological and biochemical traits to improve local cultivars with better nutrition and adaptation to climate change. A field experiment was conducted during 2024-25 to evaluate the morphological and biochemical characteristics of 22 peach accessions collected from various areas of Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. The data was subjected to the multivariate analysis technique of principal component analysis. The results revealed substantial morphological and biochemical variations among the evaluated peach accessions collected from diverse agroecological regions of Pakistan, with genetic and environmental effects potentially contributing to the observed variation. There was a huge diversity among the selected peach genotypes for fruit length (29.7–63.8 mm), fruit width (40.3–58.2 mm), seed length (17.3–36.1 mm), seed width (15.3–35.4 mm), fruit weight (33–162 g), and seed weight (3–9 g). In addition, these genotypes contained high nutritional values a range of total soluble solids (5.2–13.3 ºBrix), vitamin C (98.0–182.2 mg/100 g), total sugars (39.4–74.6%), non-reducing sugars (22.5–64.4%) and reducing sugars (10.9–26.6%), total phenolic content (185.51–406.67 mg 100 g − 1 ) and total flavonoid content (87.4–149.7 mg g − 1 ). Principal component analysis (PCA) explained 84.7% of the total variation in the first six principal components, with PC1 (23.9%) mainly associated with seed weight, fruit length, fruit weight, seed length, and pH, while PC2 (18.7%) was primarily influenced by fruit weight, fruit width, total sugars, and non-reducing sugars, indicating these traits as the major contributors to genotype discrimination. Among qualitative traits, the highest coefficient of variation (CV) was observed for anthocyanin coloration of flesh (87.3%), fruit over color (75.2%), and flesh type (60.3%). Based on agro-morphological and biochemical assessments, the dendrogram generated through agglomerative hierarchical clustering (AHC) categorized peach into three main clusters, with six accessions in cluster one, five in cluster two, and 11 in cluster three. The accessions ‘CTRU’, ‘TIA’, ‘PCH’, and ‘SWT1’ exhibited superior fruit weight, total soluble solids and phenolic content, antioxidant activity, and vitamin C content, respectively, indicating their potential as promising germplasm for future peach improvement; however, their genetic potential should be validated under common garden or multi-environment trials to distinguish genetic effects from environmental influences before their use in breeding programs.

Article.Title: Simulation and analysis of strongly asymmetric swirl distortion flow fields
Article.Authors: Li Y.; Cheng B.; Han J.; Yin Z.; Yu Y.; Liu J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Driven by the growing demand for stealth and super-maneuverability in modern advanced aircraft, multi-bend inlets such as S-shaped and buried inlets have been widely adopted. While enhancing performance, the swirl distortion induced by such inlets severely restricts engine performance and operational stability. To accurately replicate the complex swirling inlet conditions at the engine face under actual flight, this study uses numerical simulation to investigate the asymmetric multi-vortex flow field at the engine inlet under three typical operating conditions. By rationally designing the turning vanes and supporting structure of the swirl distortion screen, a distortion screen model with high replication accuracy and strong adaptability is constructed, and its simulation results are verified. The results show that the designed swirl distortion screen can effectively reproduce the complex swirl flow field generated by the S-shaped inlet. Under the three typical conditions, the simulated swirl angle curves are close to the real swirl angle curves in overall trend and show high agreement, with average errors of swirl intensity of 7.34%, 3.28%, and 6.02%, respectively.

Article.Title: Implementation of i‑PARIHS-guided pulmonary rehabilitation in patients receiving oxygen by high‑flow nasal cannula
Article.Authors: Li M.; Lv D.; Yu W.; Li X.; Lu X.; Yang J.; Liu Y.; Huang L.
Article.Abstract: Patients receiving high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) oxygen therapy often experience dyspnea-related exercise fear, which limits adherence to pulmonary rehabilitation (PR). The integrated Promoting Action on Research Implementation in Health Services (i-PARIHS) framework provides a structured approach to evidence translation, yet its application in HFNC-based PR remains limited. This study evaluated the feasibility and preliminary effectiveness of an i‑PARIHS–guided strategy in reducing dyspnea and exercise fear while improving functional outcomes among patients receiving oxygen by HFNC. A two-cycle implementation project with historical controls was conducted in a tertiary hospital respiratory department, involving forty-five nurses and two cohorts of sixty patients each (one cohort receiving usual care as historical controls and one receiving the intervention). Twenty-two best-evidence publications were synthesized into seven topics and translated into fifteen review indicators across five audit domains—personnel structure, readiness assessment, exercise timing, training content, and education. Interventions included structured PR training, motivational interviewing, goal setting, individualized education, and fixed multidisciplinary teams, implemented over four months. The primary outcomes were dyspnea (mMRC) and six-minute walk distance (6MWD); secondary outcomes were exercise self-efficacy and quality of life (SF-36). At baseline, adherence was below 80% for seven of the fifteen review indicators (implementation outcomes); after implementation, adherence exceeded 90% for all fifteen, with four reaching 100%. Relative to the historical control cohort, significant improvements were observed in dyspnea, 6MWD, self-efficacy, and quality of life (all P < 0.05), and gains were sustained at three-month follow-up. Although the quasi-experimental, historical-control design precludes definitive causal attribution, these findings suggest that i‑PARIHS–guided PR may enhance functional outcomes, reduce exercise fear, and strengthen engagement by patients who are receiving oxygen by HFNC.

Article.Title: Comparative physicochemical and mineral profiling of multifloral honeys from Apis mellifera in Himachal Pradesh, India: implications for export and GI tagging
Article.Authors: Sharma R.; Thakur M.; Devi S.
Article.Abstract: This study examined the physicochemical, mineral, and bacterial profiles of multifloral honeys from Apis mellifera L. collected from different agro-climatic zones of Himachal Pradesh, India. Of the total honey samples, 26 were identified as multifloral based on melissopalynological analysis. The commonly occurring and prominent pollen types identified in the multifloral honey samples included Eucalyptus sp., Brassica sp., Acacia sp., Cassia sp., Dalbergia sp., Syzygium sp., Albizia sp., Bombax sp., Jacaranda sp., Prunus sp., Trifolium sp., Robinia sp., Adhatoda sp., Plectranthus sp., Thymus sp., and Fagopyrum sp. reflecting the diverse floral resources contributing to honey production in the region. The physicochemical parameters varied considerably among the multifloral honeys, with pollen density ranging from 42,000 to 545,000 pollen grains per 10 g, pH from 3.97 to 5.96, electrical conductivity from 0.13 to 0.74 mS/cm, moisture content from 14.34 to 20.13%, optical density from 0.12 (Extra White) to 2.41 (Amber), density from 1.35 to 1.61 g/cm 3 , glucose from 25.23 to 37.06%, fructose from 31.70 to 40.66%, sucrose from 2.74 to 5.78%, F:G ratio from 0.93 to 1.50, acidity from 17.40 to 49.36 meq/kg, vitamin C from 7.67 to 38.49 mg/100 g, ash from 0.02 to 0.42%, hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) from 6.59 to 86 mg/kg, diastase from 4.53 to 30.48 DN, phenol from 12.96 to 108.54 mg GAE/100 g, proline from 18.19 to 113.98 mg/100 g, and 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl activity from 16.49 to 78.84%. Calcium, magnesium, phosphorus, potassium, zinc, sodium, iron, and manganese were detected in the honey samples. No significant signs of adulteration were detected, and all multifloral honey samples met FSSAI safety standards, confirming their purity and compliance with recommended quality parameters. Furthermore, principal component analysis and hierarchical cluster analysis indicated variation in honey quality parameters according to geographical origin. The studied regions exhibited rich floral diversity, facilitating the production of distinctive multifloral honeys with potential for geographical indication recognition specific to the region.

Article.Authors: Demirtaş Z.; Arslan N.; Yılmaz F.; Arslan S.; Çelebi C.; Kayıhan Ş.
Article.Abstract: The association between digital addiction and adolescents’ psychological well-being and academic life has attracted growing scholarly interest. This study examines the association between digital addiction and school engagement among high school students, focusing on the statistically significant serial indirect association through anti-mattering and life satisfaction. A quantitative research design was adopted, using data collected from 437 high school students. Digital addiction was found to have a positive correlation with anti-mattering and a negative correlation with life satisfaction and school engagement. According to the findings of structural equation modeling, digital addiction was not significantly associated with school engagement. Nevertheless, the indirect association was suggested by the serial mediation analysis, indicating that digital addiction was associated with higher anti-mattering, and anti-mattering was associated with lower life satisfaction, which was, moreover, associated with lower school engagement (indirect association: B = – 0.031, 95% CI [– 0.051, – 0.014]). The results emphasize the links between digital addiction, mental health, and academic achievement, as well as the need for intervention programs designed to target students’ life satisfaction and anti-mattering.

Article.Title: A strain-aware electromechanical framework for III-nitride axial nanowire heterostructures toward an energy-efficient high-frequency tunnel FET
Article.Authors: Khodabakhsh A.; Amini A.
Article.Abstract: A polarization-engineered III-nitride nanowire tunnel field-effect transistor (TFET) is investigated for low-energy, high-frequency operation under strain relaxation. Unlike approaches that optimize polarization-assisted tunneling primarily from an electrical perspective, the proposed framework introduces mechanical strain retention and critical structural dimensions as explicit constraints before electrical optimization. A coupled Wentzel–Kramers–Brillouin tunneling analysis and finite-element electromechanical framework evaluates multiple heterostructures in terms of critical thickness, strain relaxation, polarization degradation, and tunneling strength. The InN/In \(_{0.65}\) Ga \(_{0.35}\) N/InN axial nanowire is identified as a balanced structure with strong tunneling under both coherent and relaxed strain conditions. Device simulations show steep switching with a subthreshold swing of 11.3 mV/dec at 300 K, suppressed leakage, and transconductance of 723–997 \(\upmu \) S over 225–400 K. Femtofarad-scale gate capacitance enables cutoff frequencies of 268–76 GHz, indicating potential for millimeter-wave operation. Zero-bias rectification is enabled by polarization-induced built-in electric fields, which enhance band-to-band tunneling without an externally applied DC bias. The device exhibits high intrinsic gain, low noise, and high power gain across the Ka-, V-, and early W-band ranges. System-level operation is validated using a non-quasi-static compact model for a differential power detector with high-responsivity drain-biased detection and polarization-driven zero-bias rectification, demonstrating strain-aware polarization control for strain-tolerant millimeter-wave TFET operation.

Article.Title: Vibration amplification mechanism and theoretical mitigation strategy for feedwater flow meter brackets in nuclear power plants
Article.Authors: Jiang S.; Gu B.; Wang S.; Zhao B.; Li Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the vibration amplification mechanisms and theoretical mitigation strategies for safety-class feedwater flow meter brackets in a nuclear power plant. Initial field surveys revealed excessive low-frequency (10–50 Hz) vibration energy at the transmitter installation node, posing significant long-term fatigue hazards. To elucidate this phenomenon, an equivalent cantilever beam model and a single-degree-of-freedom (SDOF) isolation model were established. Guided by the Euler-Bernoulli beam theory and vibration transmissibility analysis, a theoretical forward-design methodology was implemented to decouple structural resonance from external excitations. A composite optimization scheme—comprising localized stiffness reinforcement, a targeted 250 mm reduction in effective cantilever length, and specific elastic mounting—was formulated via numerical parameter optimization. Both laboratory and on-site experimental validations demonstrated that the optimized structure successfully shifted the natural frequency and strictly satisfied the critical isolation condition (\(\:{T}_{r}<1\)) in dominant frequency bands. Consequently, the overall vibration acceleration levels at the transmitter were remarkably suppressed by 18.4 to 26.4 dB across the 10 Hz to 8 kHz spectrum, providing a rigorously validated paradigm for vibration control in critical nuclear instrumentation.

Article.Authors: Hassan N.; El Shebini S.; Ahmed N.; El-Masry S.; Moaty M.; Khalil A.; Hammad D.; Kamal A.; Ismail A.; Alian K.; Afify M.; Megahed S.; Elashry G.; Ebrahim E.; Rasheed E.; Kishta M.; Selim M.; Aboud H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Obesity is a complex condition associated with increased levels of inflammatory markers, leading to chronic low-grade inflammation. To investigate the association between the intake of selected amino acids and fatty acids and immune dysregulation, as reflected by IL-10, IL-17, and TH17 responses, in Egyptian women with obesity. This observational cross-sectional study included 60 obese and 30 normal-weight women aged 25–60 years. Anthropometric measurements, dietary intake (3-day 24-hour recall), lipid profile, and cytokine levels (IL-10, IL-17, TH17) were assessed. Branched-chain amino acids were positively associated with IL-17, while glutamine correlated positively with IL-10 ( r = 0.325, p ≤ 0.001). Total fat intake showed a positive correlation with IL-17 ( r = 0.335, p ≤ 0.001) and a negative correlation with IL-10 ( r = − 0.416, p ≤ 0.001). Saturated fatty acids exhibited pro-inflammatory associations, while unsaturated fatty acids, particularly omega-3 (EPA, DPA), showed anti-inflammatory effects. Dietary composition plays an important role in immune dysregulation in obesity. Diets rich in BCAAs and saturated fats may exacerbate inflammation in obesity, whereas higher consumption of omega-3 fatty acids appears to have a protective, anti-inflammatory effect. These findings suggest that dietary fatty acid and amino acid profiles are associated with inflammatory marker.

Article.Title: Radiotherapy and anatomically defined pelvic second primary malignancies in 10-year rectal cancer survivors
Article.Authors: Huang K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Second primary malignancy (SPM) associations after rectal cancer may depend on anatomical endpoint definitions. Using Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results data, we examined 24,551 patients who survived at least 10 years after surgery for rectal adenocarcinoma diagnosed during 2000–2012. First SPMs diagnosed at least 11 calendar years after the index year were analyzed using competing-risk methods with approximate year-based event times. Radiotherapy was not independently associated with all-site first SPMs. After correcting broad site categories, 277 events met a conservative anatomical pelvic definition excluding prostate cancer. Radiotherapy was associated with this endpoint (adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio 2.36, 95% confidence interval 1.48–3.75). At 10 years after the landmark, unadjusted cumulative incidence was 2.80% with recorded radiotherapy and 1.07% with no/unknown radiotherapy, a difference of 1.73 percentage points (95% confidence interval 1.22–2.25). Including prostate cancer attenuated the association (1.43, 0.99–2.07). These exploratory findings are definition-dependent associations among selected long-term survivors, not evidence of radiation-induced carcinogenesis or a basis for a new screening policy.

Article.Title: A single-phase high step-up common-ground direct AC–AC converter with reduced switches stress
Article.Authors: Bairami M.; Sedaghati F.; Shayeghi H.; Mousavi-Aghdam S.; Padban S.; Mohajery R.
Article.Abstract: This paper introduces a single-stage boost AC–AC converter based on a switching-cell configuration. The suggested topology is designed to achieve high voltage gain while reducing the size and weight of magnetic components, and also, minimizing overall conduction losses. By providing continuous input and output current waveforms, the converter reduces current ripple, while the experimentally measured THD values confirm the limited distortion of the input current and output voltage waveforms. The proposed design provides a duty-cycle-controlled voltage gain while preserving the phase and frequency of the input voltage at the output. This operating principle enables direct high step-up AC voltage conversion without requiring a bulky line-frequency transformer. Additionally, the simplified circuit, fewer bidirectional switches, and reduced voltage stress on semiconductor devices enhance efficiency, and implementation feasibility. A detailed theoretical analysis is presented, including operating principles, mode analysis, component design considerations, and performance evaluation. The effectiveness of the introduced converter is validated experimentally. The laboratory test is conducted at an input voltage of 20 V, a duty cycle of D = 0.7, a switching frequency of 50 kHz, an output voltage of 110 V, and an output power of 250 W. The obtained results confirm the capability of the converter to provide high voltage gain and enhanced performance, making it suitable for inductive power transfer systems, AC power conditioning applications, and low voltage AC energy interfaces.

Article.Title: Fungicides influence pseudoephedrine bioaccumulation and stress response in Cucurbita pepo
Article.Authors: Urbaniak M.; Tomczyk P.; Shams M.; Wyrwicka-Drewniak A.; Kózka B.; Giebułtowicz J.; Inui H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pharmaceuticals in agricultural soils are emerging contaminants, yet their interactions with edible crops remain poorly understood. This study examined the uptake, translocation, and physiological effects of pseudoephedrine (PSE) in Cucurbita pepo cv. Atena Polka and the influence of co-applied fungicides (benomyl, B; chlorothalonil, D). Plants were grown for 28 days in soil spiked with 1 mg kg −1 PSE alone or combined with B or D. PSE concentrations in plant tissues, bioaccumulation (BAF), and root-to-leaf translocation factors (TF) were determined, along with major latex-like protein ( MLP ) gene expression, antioxidant responses, and oxidative damage. The highest PSE concentrations occurred in stems (7.89 µg g −1 ), followed by roots (4.18 µg g −1 ), with limited leaf translocation (0.42 µg g −1 ; TF = 0.10). Benomyl (B) increased root (5.56 µg g −1 ) and leaf (1.33 µg g −1 ) concentrations, whereas chlorothalonil (D) reduced root (3.10 µg g −1 ) and leaf (0.38 µg g −1 ) levels while leaving stem concentrations unchanged. MLP expression followed similar trends: it was downregulated by PSE, strongly upregulated by PSE + B, and restored near control levels by PSE + D. Plant biomass remained unaffected. PSE alone induced moderate antioxidant responses, while PSE + B was associated with stronger oxidative stress responses; in contrast, PSE + D did not significantly affect glutathione S-transferase (GST), ascorbate peroxidase (APX), or guaiacol peroxidase (POX) activities and maintained membrane integrity. Fungicides differentially influence PSE uptake, translocation, and plant stress responses illustrating complex interactions between pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and crops with implications for phytoremediation and food safety.

Article.Title: The effect of various fiber surface modification on the microstructure and strength of sisal-reinforced mortar
Article.Authors: Alemu D.; Dada O.; Menzi L.; Tedla T.; Chabalala D.; Ikotun B.
Article.Abstract: This study investigates the mechanical performance, workability, and durability of sisal fibre-reinforced mortar (SFRC) modified through alkali treatment (NaOH) and combined alkali-paraffin treatment. Three mortar mixes were evaluated: untreated sisal fibres (USFRC), alkali-treated fibres (ATSFRC), and paraffin-alkali-treated fibres (PATSFRC). Mechanical properties were assessed at 3, 7, 14, 28, and 56 days, while durability was evaluated through sorptivity and chloride conductivity tests at 28 and 56 days. Microstructural characterization using SEM, FTIR, and EDX revealed treatment-dependent morphological and chemical modifications that directly influenced composite behaviour. Workability improved progressively with fibre treatment, with PATSFRC achieving the highest slump value (85 mm) compared to USFRC (65 mm). Setting times increased from USFRC (initial: 75 min, final: 135 min) to PATSFRC (initial: 165 min, final: 255 min), indicating that paraffin coating delays hydration by creating a hydrophobic barrier. Mechanical testing showed that all fibre-reinforced mixes outperformed the control mortar, with ATSFRC exhibiting the highest compressive (37 MPa), tensile (3.4 MPa), and flexural (5.3 MPa) strengths at 56 days—representing increases of 19%, 26%, and 20%, respectively, over the control. The improved mechanical performance of ATSFRC correlates with SEM-observed surface roughening and FTIR-confirmed removal of hydrophilic components, which enhanced fibre-matrix interfacial bonding. Durability assessments revealed significant treatment-dependent differences. PATSFRC exhibited the lowest sorptivity (0.08 mm/min¹/² at 28 days; 0.05 mm/min¹/² at 56 days) and chloride conductivity (760 C at 28 days; 500 C at 56 days), representing 64% and 17% reductions, respectively, compared to USFRC at 56 days. These improvements are attributed to the paraffin coating’s hydrophobic barrier effect, which limits moisture ingress and alkali degradation. Microstructural analysis confirmed that paraffin-treated fibres maintained structural integrity with minimal mineral deposition, while untreated fibres showed extensive degradation. XRD analysis revealed increased cellulose crystallinity in alkali-treated fibres, while paraffin treatment created a composite diffraction pattern indicating surface-level modification without altering the crystalline core. FTIR spectroscopy confirmed successful removal of hemicellulose and lignin in alkali-treated fibres and the presence of hydrophobic hydrocarbon chains in paraffin-coated fibers. This study establishes clear correlations between fiber surface modification, microstructural characteristics, and macroscopic performance. The results demonstrate that combined alkali-paraffin treatment provides an optimal balance between mechanical enhancement and durability, offering a sustainable reinforcement strategy for cementitious composites.

Article.Title: A low-voltage half-select free static memory with hybrid inverters for low-power and reliable WSN-based IoT architecture
Article.Authors: Rao Y.; Venkatakrishnamoorthy T.; Dharani M.; Murthy P.; Basha S.; Garg P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The rapid development of wireless sensor network (WSN)-enabled Internet of Things (IoT) systems increases the necessity of designing SRAM cells with very low power dissipation, excellent stability, and reliable low-voltage operation. Nevertheless, traditional SRAM cells have problems of insufficient read/write stability, half select disturb, and higher susceptibility to process variations in nanometer technology nodes. In this paper, a CNTFET-enabled 10T SRAM cell with independent read/write paths, Schmitt trigger storage inverter, virtual ground write assistance, and half select disturb free operation is proposed to enhance the stability and energy efficiency. The new design is analysed in HSPICE by using the Stanford 32 nm CNTFET model and compared with the state-of-the-art CNTFET SRAM cells. Simulation results show that the proposed cell has 81% increase in read static noise margin (RSNM), 94% increase in write static noise margin (WSNM), 80% reduction in write power, 76% reduction in read power, 74% reduction in leakage power, 29% reduction in minimum operational voltage, and 109% increase in critical charge over the traditional 6T SRAM cell. Also, the RSNM and WSNM yields of the 1000 samples in Monte Carlo analysis are the largest, indicating immunity to process variations.

Article.Title: Pharmacological adherence in Type 2 diabetes mellitus, social inequalities and technological influences in Barbados
Article.Authors: Mandeville E.; Greaves N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Background Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) represents a critical public health burden in Barbados, with a prevalence of 18.7% — nearly double the global average of 10.5%. Despite a universally accessible public healthcare system, pharmacological non-adherence among low socioeconomic patients remains a persistent challenge. Social inequalities, climate-related events, and the evolving role of technology each intersect with T2DM management in complex ways that are poorly understood in the Caribbean context. Objectives This study aimed to explore the phenomenological experiences of low socioeconomic patients living with T2DM (PLWT2DM) and their healthcare providers regarding adherence to pharmacological treatment, climate events, and the use of smartphone technology. Methods A qualitative research design was employed. Purposive sampling was used to recruit 52 participants across five polyclinics in the highest-poverty parishes of Barbados, identified using the 2016 Barbados Survey of Living Conditions. Thirty PLWT2DM (7 male, 23 female) and 22 healthcare professionals (including doctors, nurses, pharmacists, podiatrists and nutritionists) participated in semi-structured in-depth interviews conducted via WhatsApp during the COVID-19 pandemic. Interviews were transcribed using a modified verbatim technique and analysed using thematic content analysis with constant comparison, supported by ATLAS.ti software. Results Four basic themes emerged: (1) the bio-psycho-social behaviour of T2DM patients, (2) factors affecting treatment, including physical symptoms and use of herbal therapies, (3) barriers to treatment, and (4) recommendations for a patient-centred health system. Two organising themes were identified: the need for patient-centred care models grounded in social and behavioural theory, and a greater systemic focus on T2DM management. The global theme established that patient-centred T2DM management is the optimal mechanism for improving pharmacological adherence among low socioeconomic patients. Social inequalities — including financial limitations, relative isolation, and psychological distress — were major drivers of non-adherence. Both patients and healthcare workers demonstrated limited knowledge regarding the impact of climate events on T2DM. While technology was perceived as beneficial, elderly patients faced significant barriers to adoption. Conclusions Patient-centred T2DM management that addresses social inequalities, enhances health education, and leverages appropriate technology is essential for improving pharmacological adherence in Barbados. Future research should integrate climate-related factors, age-targeted technological interventions, and health policy reform to ensure equitable and effective chronic disease management.
