Article.Title: VR-FOCUS: evaluating eye tracking during a virtual reality N-back task as a marker of cognitive load in chronic pain
Article.Authors: Tsigarides J.; Bowler J.; Dainty J.; Bagnall A.; Macgregor A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Immersive virtual reality (VR) is a promising medium for adaptive pain therapeutics, but objective markers of cognitive load suitable for real-time adaptation remain insufficiently characterised in people living with chronic pain. This study evaluated whether eye tracking embedded within a consumer-available VR system provides signatures of cognitive load during a VR N-back task in healthy controls and a pragmatic chronic musculoskeletal pain cohort. A total of 84 participants (42/group) completed five levels (Baseline to 4-Back) while ocular responses were recorded. Performance declined and subjective workload increased with higher N-back levels, confirming successful manipulation of cognitive demand. In mixed-effects models, larger pupil diameter and higher blink rate were associated with higher task level and workload ratings after covariate adjustment. Logistic regression using summary pupil and blink features showed limited discrimination of load (1-Back vs 4-Back), with near-chance accuracies (0.51–0.60). In contrast, time-series classifiers exploiting temporal structure achieved higher participant-level accuracy in healthy controls (0.81–0.87) and in chronic pain (0.60–0.66) using pupil diameter alone. Adding blinks produced small, reproducible improvements in model accuracy for the chronic pain group. These findings support VR-embedded eye tracking for cognitive load estimation, but suggest closed-loop applications in chronic pain will require personalised models.

Article.Title: Investigating depth-dependent transformation of vibroacoustic signals originating from tissue interactions during needle insertions
Article.Authors: Steeg K.; Gawron J.; Oran H.; Strama K.; Krombach G.; Friebe M.; Rzepka D.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Clinical needle placement requires accurate information about tissue boundaries and transitions, which are often not reliably resolved by standard imaging modalities due to limited spatial resolution. Vibroacoustic signals can encode such information and could complement existing modalities with real-time feedback, but their signal composition and the influence of insertion depth remain unclear. By applying physical concepts from established force-based needle insertion models we assess whether tip-related excitations contribute characteristics relevant for tissue classification and whether shaft-interactions alter these components with insertion depth. A ResNet-18 model was trained on tip-dominated interactions and tested on the same tissue at the bottom of a stacked phantom, to assess the shaft contributions and depth-dependent effects. The model failed to classify similar tissues beneath an overlying layer. However, augmentation with shaft-dominated recordings elevated classification performance over 90%, indicating that tissue-discriminative information remained present. As augmented signals did not reproduce spectral characteristics of depth-affected signals, shaft interactions alone were insufficient to explain observed transformations, suggesting additional modification by depth-dependent propagation effects including attenuation and damping. This study proposes a conceptual model in which vibroacoustic needle signals are interpreted as a depth-dependent superposition of tip- and shaft-related excitations, which are modified during propagation along the shaft.

Article.Title: Systematic investigation of cationic monomeric, dimeric, and trimeric surfactants for self-assembly, adsorption thermodynamics, and enhanced oil displacement
Article.Authors: Al Bustanji S.; Kumar R.; Beemkumar N.; Ali B.; Mishra A.; Gill H.; Khdyr A.; Yadav N.; Hoseini S.
Article.Abstract: Tailoring surfactant topology offers a powerful route to govern interfacial phenomena and fluid displacement in harsh subsurface environments. Herein, we systematically examine the influence of headgroup multiplication across three homologous tetradecyl quaternary ammonium architectures: single-chain MC14, dimeric GC14, and trimeric TC14. Spectroscopic characterization ( 1 H/ 13 C-NMR, FTIR) and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) validated the target chemical frameworks and their thermal robustness, while XRD confirmed the predominantly calcitic, highly crystalline matrix of the evaluated carbonate substrate. Increasing the oligomeric degree substantially boosted surface activity and self-assembly propensity at 25 °C, lowering the critical micelle concentration (CMC) by two orders of magnitude from 3.50 mM (MC14) down to 0.114 mM (GC14) and 0.035 mM (TC14), alongside superior counterion association and surface packing efficiency. Dynamic light scattering (DLS) confirmed architecture-controlled supramolecular aggregation, tracking hydrodynamic sizes from 4.15 nm to 8.12 nm. Thermodynamic evaluations indicated spontaneous, increasingly exergonic micellization and elevated halotolerance against NaCl from monomeric to trimeric configurations. Under harsh thermal conditions (80 °C), TC14 outperformed lower-order homologues by reducing oil-water interfacial tension to a nadir of 0.21 mN/m and effectively reversing oil-wet carbonate wettability (contact angle shifted from 153° to 56° at 2 ×CMC). Synergistic tuning with sulfate ions further decoupled conditions required for minimal interfacial tension from those favoring maximal hydrophilicity. Crucially, capillary-dominated spontaneous imbibition experiments revealed that wettability-tailored TC14 solutions yielded a peak recovery of 22.1%, outperforming baseline seawater (12.7%). These insights elucidate the mechanistic advantages of multivalent trimeric surfactants as ultra-low-dosage, salt-tolerant agents for interfacial engineering and enhanced hydrocarbon recovery in carbonate formations.

Article.Title: Inflammatory and metabolic dysregulation in a murine model of COPD-like lung injury with acute Aspergillus fumigatus challenge
Article.Authors: Feng Y.; Tang F.; Yang Y.; Liao R.; Ma Q.; Tao S.; Guo J.; Guo R.
Article.Abstract: Patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are susceptible to Aspergillus-related disease, but associated host-response alterations remain incompletely understood. We conducted an exploratory study in male C57BL/6 mice ( n = 3/group) assigned to control, COPD-like lung injury, acute Aspergillus fumigatus challenge, or combined challenge. COPD-like lung injury was induced by cigarette-smoke exposure and intranasal lipopolysaccharide administration, whereas acute A. fumigatus challenge was established by repeated intranasal inoculation of conidia. Cytokines, secretory IgA (sIgA), MAPK-related transcripts and proteins, histopathology, and lung metabolomes were assessed. The combined-challenge group showed numerically greater changes in inflammatory, mucosal immune, and MAPK-related measures, including higher levels of IL-17, IL-23, and TNF-α and lower levels of IL-10, IFN-γ, and sIgA in lung tissue and oral fluid. Untargeted metabolomics identified alterations involving glycerophospholipid, nucleotide-sugar, and energy-related pathways; ferroptosis-pathway enrichment was observed without assessment of canonical ferroptosis markers. Exploratory two-way ANOVA identified main effects of COPD-like injury and/or fungal challenge for multiple outcomes, but no interaction remained significant after Benjamini–Hochberg correction. Correlations between selected metabolites and inflammatory or MAPK-related markers were exploratory and non-causal. Overall, acute A. fumigatus challenge in mice with COPD-like lung injury was associated with concurrent inflammatory, mucosal immune, MAPK-related, and metabolic alterations. Given the absence of a consistent statistically significant interaction, these group-level differences are interpreted as descriptive and hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of a combined-condition-specific mechanism or causal relationship. Larger studies with adequately powered factorial designs and functional validation are required to determine whether the combined condition induces a distinct biological response.

Article.Title: Waste-to-resource geopolymer technology: mechanical, durability, and microstructural performance of red Mud–fly ash-stabilized black cotton soil
Article.Authors: Raj R.; Yadav B.; Kumar S.; Yadav A.
Article.Abstract: Black cotton soil is highly expansive and moisture-sensitive, resulting in low strength, poor bearing capacity, and volume instability in transportation infrastructure. This study adopted a two-stage approach to optimize a red mud–fly ash geopolymer binder and subsequently evaluate its effectiveness for black cotton soil stabilization. Geopolymer binders containing red mud-to-fly ash ratios of 90:10, 80:20, and 70:30 were activated using 10 M NaOH and Na₂SiO₃/NaOH mass ratios of 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0. The optimum binder, 80RM + 20FA at a Na₂SiO₃/NaOH ratio of 2.0, achieved 28-day compressive strengths of 5.81 MPa under ambient curing and 6.59 MPa at 60 °C. When incorporated into black cotton soil, an optimum dosage of 30% geopolymer produced the best overall engineering response. The 70BCS + 30GP mix achieved 28-day UCS values of 315 and 365 kPa and STS values of 118 and 132 kPa under ambient and 60 °C curing, respectively, representing increases of 80.0% in UCS and 126.9% in STS relative to untreated soil under ambient curing. The optimum mix also achieved unsoaked and soaked CBR values of 5.90% and 3.71%, respectively, while reducing the free swell index from 52.17% to 21.74%. After twelve wet–dry cycles, it exhibited only 1.82% mass loss and retained approximately 87% of its original UCS. XRD, SEM, and EDX observations confirmed amorphous aluminosilicate reaction-product development, matrix densification, pore filling, and improved particle bonding. Overall, the 70BCS + 30GP mix demonstrated promising laboratory-scale potential for selected low-volume road, shoulder, embankment, and subgrade-improvement applications, subject to further long-term and field-scale validation.

Article.Title: Peer bullying in adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis treated with bracing: a case–control study
Article.Authors: Altın Y.; Korkmaz M.; Demir B.; Yüksel T.; Akgül T.; Korkmaz M.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to evaluate peer bullying in patients with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) treated with bracing and to examine associated self-esteem and social anxiety compared with age- and sex-matched healthy controls. This case-control study was conducted at a tertiary university hospital between January 2023 and June 2025. The brace group consisted of 31 adolescents (22 girls, 9 boys) with AIS treated with a Chêneau brace, of whom 24 were current and 7 were former brace users. The control group comprised 32 age- and sex-matched healthy adolescents (21 girls, 11 boys). Psychosocial assessment was performed using the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES), the Child and Adolescent Bullying Scale-9 Short Form (CABS-9), and the Social Anxiety Scale for Adolescents (SAS-A). Intergroup comparisons were analyzed with the Mann-Whitney U test, and correlations within the brace group were examined using Spearman’s correlation analysis. Current and former brace users were also analyzed separately in an exploratory analysis. The mean duration of brace use was 17.1 (± 10.2) months, the mean Cobb angle was 31.1° (± 4.4°), and the mean self-reported daily brace-wear time was 21.2 (± 1.2) hours. Adolescents in the brace group had significantly higher CABS-9 scores than controls (19.6 ± 5.9 vs. 12.5 ± 6.3, p < 0.001). CABS-9 scores were similar in current and former brace users ( p = 0.981), and both subgroups scored higher than controls. In contrast, RSES and SAS-A scores did not differ significantly between groups (RSES, p = 0.238; SAS-A, 50.8 ± 11.0 vs. 51.3 ± 10.2, p = 0.826). Within the brace group, brace duration was positively correlated with CABS-9 scores ( r = 0.397, p = 0.027), while age was negatively correlated with SAS-A scores ( r =-0.396, p = 0.027). Adolescents with AIS treated with bracing had significantly greater exposure to peer bullying than healthy controls, while social anxiety and self-esteem did not differ significantly between groups. In exploratory analyses, longer brace duration was associated with greater bullying exposure, and younger age was associated with higher social anxiety within the brace group. Because no non-braced AIS group was included, these findings cannot distinguish the effect of bracing from that of scoliosis itself. These findings support specific attention to peer bullying during routine follow-up of adolescents receiving brace treatment for AIS.

Article.Title: Data-driven static position modeling of a parallel tendon-actuated soft continuum robot using artificial neural networks
Article.Authors: Hanna S.; Abdelhaleem A.; El-Naggar S.; El-Hussieny H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Parallel soft continuum robots combine the compliance and adaptability of soft structures with the structural advantages of parallel mechanisms, offering promising capabilities for complex robotic applications. However, their highly nonlinear behavior presents significant challenges for accurate and computationally efficient modeling. This study presents a data-driven approach for static end-effector position modeling of a parallel tendon-actuated soft continuum robot using an artificial neural network (ANN). A physics-based model of the robot is developed in the SoRoSim MATLAB framework using the Geometric Variable-Strain (GVS) formulation, with gravity incorporated into the static simulations. Simulation data are then used to train the ANN to learn the nonlinear mapping between the tendon actuation forces and the Cartesian position of the end effector. The trained ANN demonstrates close agreement with the SoRoSim-generated positions over the investigated input domain while providing considerably faster position predictions than direct SoRoSim evaluations. This computational advantage highlights the potential of the proposed data-driven model for applications requiring repeated and rapid model evaluations, particularly in future control-oriented implementations. The presented results establish the ANN as an efficient surrogate for the considered SoRoSim-based static position model, while the current evaluation remains simulation-based.

Article.Title: Land suitability analysis for taro (Colocasia esculenta) cultivation based on topo-edaphic variables in a smallholder farming system
Article.Authors: Mlambo B.; Mutanga O.; Matongera T.; Odindi J.
Article.Abstract: Taro ( Colocasia esculenta ), one of the neglected and underutilized crop species (NUCS), is regarded as a climate-smart crop due to its ability to tolerate harsh environmental conditions associated with climate change. The crop plays a critical role in enhancing food and nutritional security while promoting resilience through crop diversification, particularly in smallholder farming systems in developing countries. Despite its recognized potential, a substantial knowledge gap exists regarding the identification of optimal areas for maximizing yield in local contexts. Hence, this study employed the Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) machine learning algorithm to conduct a Land Suitability Analysis (LSA) for taro within rural landscapes dominated by smallholder farmers. To quantify the area suitable for cultivation, we evaluated topographic and edaphic influences at 0-20 and 20-50 cm using five models: (1) topographic- variables, (2) edaphic variables at 0-20 cm, (3) a combined model using topographic + edaphic variables at 0-20 cm, (4) edaphic variables at 20-50 cm, (5) a combined model using topographic + edaphic variables at 20-50 cm. Model 5 achieved the highest mean AUC (0.821 ± 0.083 SD) based on 10 replicated validations, although paired t-tests revealed that this improvement was statistically significant only when compared to the lowest-performing Model 1 (p = 0.005), while comparisons with Models 2, 3, and 4 were not significant (all p > 0.05). The results from Model 5 indicated that 7.92%, 11.04%, 16.80%, and 26.64% of the study area were classified as highly suitable, suitable, moderately suitable, and marginally suitable for taro cultivation, respectively. Based on the MaxEnt Jackknife test, slope, Topographic Wetness Index (TWI), and the soil’s calcium, iron, and phosphorus were the most important variables for taro growth. These findings provide practical information to support improved land-use planning, promote the integration of NUCS into local farming systems, and contribute to food and nutritional security, particularly within smallholder farming communities in rural areas.

Article.Title: Mechanistic assessment and control of poloxamer activity: exploiting bulk hydration to maximise solubilisation capacity
Article.Authors: Stewart R.; Sandhu M.; Shah S.; Kirby D.; Mohammed A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Although literature describes pluronic micellisation behaviour in solution, it does not elucidate the associated solubilisation capacities achieved nor how this capacity changes with micellisation potential, particularly when considering the impact of changes in the composition of the bulk media. This study, for the first time, employed differential scanning calorimetry, supported by micrometric analysis and drug loading studies, to mechanistically investigate the behaviour and impact of bulk hydration on changes in polymer chain-bulk interactions of Pluronic F-127. Employing a model hydrophobic drug (1,6-Diphenyl-1,3,5-hexatriene (DPH)) and pharmaceutically relevant carbamazepine, Pluronic F-127 solubilisation activity was shown to significantly increase up to 18 folds once the threshold of 2.5 times its critical micellisation concentration (CMC) is crossed. Particle properties such as size, polydispersity and drug loading were studied to understand the relationship between polymer behaviour and drug solubilisation. This study provides a paradigm for controlling loading capacity of poorly soluble drugs, that can be carefully tuned through the selection of well hydrated excipients that indirectly influence polymer behaviour.

Article.Title: Heliocide H2 and cadinatriene glucopyranoside as promising dual β-lactamase inhibitors against antibiotic resistance: an integrated computational study
Article.Authors: Noor S.; Mishra V.; Zaman A.; Ahmad I.; Perveen A.; Ahmed S.; Asif U.; Sherwani A.; Alasmari S.; Dib H.; Ali A.; Altwaim S.; Shah M.
Article.Abstract: Antibiotic resistance mediated by β-lactamase enzymes poses a major obstacle to the effective treatment of bacterial infections. Among these enzymes, serine β-lactamases and metallo β-lactamases are of particular concern, as they hydrolyze β-lactam antibiotics, rendering them ineffective. This study aimed to identify putative dual β-lactamase inhibitor candidates with predicted activity against both classes of β-lactamases using a comprehensive in silico approach. A curated library of 163 phytochemicals from Gossypium hirsutum L. was compiled from literature and chemical databases. Of these, 32 compounds exhibited higher docking scores than the standard inhibitors (boronic acid and meropenem) against both targets. The top 10 dual inhibitors, selected based on Lipinski’s rule of five and additional drug-likeness criteria, were subjected to further pharmacological evaluation. Heliocide H2 and Cadinatriene Glucopyranoside emerged as lead candidates based on their favorable predicted binding interactions, pharmacophoric features, and medicinal chemistry profiles. Interaction analysis revealed that both compounds formed key active-site interactions in both enzyme classes, including hydrogen bonding with SER-64 and zinc coordination in metallo β-lactamases. Pharmacokinetic profiling predicted high gastrointestinal absorption and no blood-brain barrier penetration, while PASS predictions suggested possible broad-spectrum antibacterial potential. The 200ns Molecular dynamics simulations suggested comparatively greater stability of Heliocide H2, as evidenced by lower radius of gyration (Rg), stable solvent accessible surface area (SASA) profiles, and a greater number of hydrogen bonds. Principal component analysis (PCA) and free energy landscape (FEL) analyses further demonstrated that Heliocide H2 maintained a stable conformational state throughout the simulation. Moreover, MM/PBSA binding free energy calculations showed that the Heliocide H2–metallo β-lactamase complex exhibited the most favorable binding energy (ΔG = − 21.2 kcal/mol). These findings support the prioritization of heliocide H2 and cadinatriene glucopyranoside as putative dual β-lactamase inhibitor candidates with predicted interactions with both serine and metallo β-lactamases. However, further in vitro and in vivo studies are required to validate their inhibitory activity, safety, pharmacological properties, and therapeutic potential.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: antibiotic resistance; beta-lactamase inhibitors; dual enzyme inhibition

Article.Title: Developmental exposure to green synthesized silver nanoparticles induces placental and fetal brain stress in Wistar rats
Article.Authors: Abdelaziz M.; El-Dakdoky M.; Ahmed T.; Mohamed A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract As the use and manufacture of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) continue to grow, there is a risk that they may be released into the environment, exposing humans to them in the form of air, water, and soil. Based on this, the present research examined the genotoxic, physiological, and histological effects of green biosynthesized AgNPs on fetal and maternal tissues using two methods. From the 1 st to the 19 th day of gestation, 28 pregnant female rats were divided into 4 groups (7 per group) and given the appropriate treatment doses orally once daily. As a control, distilled water was given to the first group. Saponin was administered to the second group. AgNPs were administered to the third. Silver nanoparticles loaded with saponin (Sn-AgNPs) were administered to the fourth. Treating with AgNPs and Sn-AgNPs revealed minimal adverse effects in pregnancy outcomes, gross external and skeletal examination. Although placental tissue showed elevated malondialdehyde level, significant increases in the Ag concentration, and DNA damage. Furthermore, AgNPs and Sn-AgNPs induced histopathological alterations in both the placenta and the fetal tissues. Green-produced AgNPs did not significantly affect pregnancy outcomes or fetal development; however, they induced placental alterations and elevated the fetal brain stress.

Article.Title: A systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies on body mass index and leukemia incidence and mortality
Article.Authors: Abdolkarimi M.; Hajifathali A.; Amiri Khosroshahi R.; Jowshan M.; Parkhideh S.; Mehdizadeh M.; Mofidi F.; Zahedi H.; Shadnoush M.
Article.Abstract: The relationship between body mass index (BMI) and leukemia is still unclear, especially across various leukemia subtypes and mortality. We conducted an updated systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies to quantify categorical, linear, and nonlinear associations between BMI and leukemia incidence and mortality. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for eligible prospective cohort studies. Twenty-one prospective cohort studies were included, of which 18 contributed leukemia incidence outcomes and three contributed leukemia mortality outcomes. To prevent duplicate counting, only one independent cohort-level risk estimate was included for each outcome, and pooled relative risks (RRs) were estimated using random-effects models fitted by restricted maximum likelihood (REML). Linear dose-response associations were standardized to a 5-kg/m² increment in BMI, and nonlinear associations were modeled using restricted cubic splines. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I, and the certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Higher BMI was associated with higher overall leukemia incidence in both categorical analyses comparing the highest available estimable BMI category with the study-specific reference category (9 studies; RR = 1.235, 95% CI 1.084–1.408; I²=49.8%) and linear dose-response analyses (10 studies; RR per 5 kg/m²=1.098, 95% CI 1.053–1.144; I²=82.4%). In categorical analyses, higher BMI was associated with higher incidence of ALL, AML, and CML, whereas the association with CLL was not statistically significant. In linear analyses, higher BMI was associated with higher incidence of AML and ALL; however, the ALL estimate was based on only two independent studies and should be considered exploratory. The associations for CML and CLL were not statistically significant. Higher BMI was also associated with leukemia-related mortality in both categorical (3 studies; RR = 1.870, 95% CI 1.372–2.550) and linear analyses (3 studies; RR per 5 kg/m²=1.329, 95% CI 1.121–1.575), although these estimates were derived from general-population cohorts with mortality linkage and should not be interpreted as evidence of higher post-diagnosis mortality among patients with leukemia. Restricted cubic spline analyses provided no evidence of nonlinear associations within the supported BMI ranges. The certainty of evidence was rated as low for overall leukemia incidence and very low for leukemia mortality. Higher BMI was associated with a modestly higher overall leukemia incidence and with leukemia-related mortality in prospective cohort studies. However, subtype-specific and mortality estimates were limited by the small number of independent studies, residual confounding, and between-study heterogeneity. No evidence of nonlinear associations was observed within the BMI ranges supported by the available data. These findings should be interpreted as epidemiological associations rather than evidence of causality.

Article.Title: Deep dynamic coronary roadmap guidance in percutaneous coronary intervention: a deep learning approach
Article.Authors: Lee C.; Lin Y.; Wu C.; Hsu S.; Hsieh Y.; Tseng P.
Article.Abstract: A dynamic coronary roadmap (DCR) serves as an intra-procedural navigation aid in percutaneous coronary interventions. However, the current technology relies on single-frame coronary artery segmentation through filtering, which struggles to adjust for positional shifts from heartbeat and respiratory movements, resulting in incomplete roadmap alignment of the coronary arteries and guidewire segments. To address these challenges, we propose a deep DCR method that integrates three models: deep-learning-based segmentation of coronary arteries and catheters, catheter tip detection, and optical-flow-based heart rate prediction. By leveraging optical flow, the system extracts heartbeat-related information directly from coronary artery angiography (CAG) images, without requiring ECG input during operation in sequences that meet the applicability conditions. Deep DCR uses a semi-supervised-learning-based segmentation model to generate a vascular roadmap, which is overlaid on the coronary artery for catheter segmentation. This overlay aligns the roadmap by capturing the relationship between the catheter and coronary artery motion during the transition from contrast medium injection to dissipation. This approach significantly enhances alignment accuracy, as demonstrated through case evaluations and guidewire coverage experiments. Our method provides a more precise and reliable DCR for intra-procedural navigation.

Article.Title: ANN-GA-based optimization of a hybrid battery thermal regulation system with helical liquid cooling, PCM, and copper foam
Article.Authors: Mahjoub S.; Vajdi M.; Vaferi K.; Moghanlou F.; Aghdam E.
Article.Abstract: Effective thermal management is essential for ensuring the safety, performance, and longevity of Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). In this study, an optimized hybrid Battery Thermal Regulation System (BTRS) is proposed, integrating helical liquid cooling mini-channels and phase change material (PCM) embedded in a copper foam matrix (CPCM) to enhance heat dissipation. To efficiently explore the complex design space, a coupled framework integrating numerical simulations, a Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) was developed. The approach successfully identified an ideal configuration (OCD1) characterized by a 10 mm PCM thickness, a 0.08 m/s inlet velocity, and a \(65^\circ \) helical angle. Under a severe 3C discharge condition, this optimal design achieved a maximum temperature reduction of 21.27 K, representing an 82.25% improvement over a standalone cell. Furthermore, the optimized hybrid system demonstrated superior cooling efficacy compared to individual strategies, outperforming case A (liquid cooling) by 33.67%, case B (pure PCM) by 69.35%, and case C (CPCM) by 45%. The developed ANN model exhibited high predictive accuracy, with R 2 values exceeding 0.99 for both thermal responses. These findings provide a high fidelity and scalable framework for advanced thermal management of next-generation electric vehicle battery systems.

Article.Title: Joint association of the cholesterol–high-density lipoprotein–glucose index and waist-to-height ratio with incident cardiovascular disease in a high-risk Chinese cohort
Article.Authors: Yang W.; He Y.; Wang F.; Ma X.; Ma S.
Article.Abstract: Insulin resistance (IR) and visceral obesity have been recognized as important risk factors for cardiovascular disease. Insulin resistance (IR) is quantified by the cholesterol–high-density lipoprotein–glucose (CHG) index, and visceral obesity is assessed by the waist-to-height ratio (WHtR). However, the combined impact of these two indicators on cardiovascular disease risk has not been thoroughly investigated. Our study aims to investigate the joint association of the CHG index and WHtR with incident cardiovascular disease. This study is based on data from the Ningxia region of the China Cardiovascular Disease High-Risk Population Screening and Comprehensive Intervention Project, including 3141 high-risk cardiovascular individuals without a history of CVD at baseline, for a prospective cohort analysis. Participants were categorized based on the median values of the CHG index and WHtR. Cox proportional hazards model and restricted cubic spline (RCS) were used to analyze the association of the CHG index and WHtR with the risk of CVD, evaluate the model’s predictive performance using C-index, Brier score, NRI, and IDI, and conduct subgroup analysis and sensitivity analysis. Among 3141 participants aged 45 years or older, the mean age was 58 years. Females accounted for 60.74% of the population. The median follow-up duration was 6.7 years, during which a total of 536 (17.06%) participants experienced CVD events. Compared with participants with low CHG and low WHtR, those in the high CHG and high WHtR group had a 52% increased risk of CVD ( HR = 1.52, 95% CI 1.15–2.00, P = 0.003), with a significant increasing trend. When examined separately, participants with high CHG alone had a significantly increased risk of cardiovascular disease ( HR = 1.33, 95% CI 1.11–1.58, P = 0.002), whereas those with high WHtR alone did not ( HR = 1.19, 95% CI 0.96–1.49, P = 0.114). Neither of the two discordant groups, namely high CHG and low WHtR ,and low CHG and high WHtR, showed a statistically significant association with cardiovascular disease. The RCS regression analyses demonstrated a positive linear association of the CHG index and WHtR with the incidence of CVD ( P for non-linear > 0.05). Interaction analysis did not detect statistically significant multiplicative or additive interactions. The C-index was 0.613 for the joint grouping model and 0.608 for the baseline model, with an NRI of 0.041 ( P = 0.152) and an IDI of 0.005 ( P < 0.001). Subgroup analyses showed that the effect of the combined grouping was consistent across various subgroups, and sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the main findings. This study based on a cohort of high-risk cardiovascular disease populations in the Ningxia region, found that individuals with both high CHG and high WHtR had an increased risk of incident CVD. However, this joint association is mainly driven by CHG, with WHtR making a limited independent contribution, and the incremental predictive value of the joint assessment is weak. Although CHG and WHtR are both simple, economical, and non-invasive clinical indicators, their combined assessment may provide some supplementary information for risk stratification in high-risk cardiovascular populations, but this finding needs to be further validated in general population cohorts.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: waist-to-height ratio; incident cardiovascular disease; cardiovascular risk

Article.Title: Individual perching, a potential reproductive strategy of Melipona stingless bee males
Article.Authors: Quezada-Euán J.; Guerrero-Herrera R.; Aragón-Pech R.; Ancona-Lizarraga L.; Fleites-Ayil F.; Moo-Valle H.
Article.Abstract: There is a wide gap in the knowledge of the reproductive behaviour of males of the Meliponini or stingless bees, the richest group of species within the corbiculate bees. To date two general reproductive strategies have been reported in the males of stingless bees, both involving the formation of large congregations of individuals. Here, we describe a newly observed potential reproductive behaviour of stingless bee males, that contrast with the large clustering reported in all species studied so far: individual perching. Across ten months we documented the frequency of Melipona beecheii males perching nearby colonies. We performed bioassays to verify sexual activity and the capacity of perching males for detecting and mating with gynes. We also assessed body size differences, comparing perching males and males produced in colonies. Males perching were present across the study. In controlled bioassays, they detected gynes and attempted mounting, which has not been observed at congregations. These evidences indicate that this behaviour is not occasional and may represent a mating strategy. Noteworthy, the thorax width of perching males was not different to colony males, suggesting that unlike other bees, this behavior may not be driven by body size differences. We discuss possible explanations and implications of this newly reported behaviour.
Article.Topic: Insect and Arachnid Ecology and Behavior

Article.Title: A differentiable multi-physics learning model for robust single-image dehazing under complex atmospheric conditions
Article.Authors: Alhawarat M.; Alotaibi M.; Aljuaidi R.; Alshreef B.; Shaban E.; Alawad W.; Alnuwaiser M.
Article.Abstract: Restoring clear visibility from a single hazy image remains a challenging inverse problem when multiple atmospheric phenomena jointly affect image formation. In real environments, light propagation can be influenced not only by particle scattering but also by turbulence-induced blur and wavelength-dependent attenuation. Most existing dehazing approaches primarily address scattering, which limits their physical consistency and robustness in heavy haze or long-range scenes. In this work, we introduce a differentiable multi-physics learning framework that is designed to integrate scattering, turbulence, and spectral attenuation within a unified image formation model. The degradation process is expressed as a compact linear observation equation, where turbulence is represented through a spatial convolution operator and spectral effects are modeled via channel-dependent attenuation. Since the governing parameters cannot be directly inferred from a single observation, the formulated as an iterative refinement process guided by a learned approximation of the physical model. A lightweight neural estimator predicts the observation operators, while a learnable spectral module captures wavelength-dependent behavior. An iterative regularization network stabilizes the reconstruction process and prevents error propagation. Experiments conducted on the RESIDE-SOTS benchmark show competitive performance, achieving PSNR/SSIM values of 27.3/0.94 for indoor scenes and 30.2/0.94 for outdoor scenes with only a few optimization steps. Additional analyses confirm improved robustness under noise perturbations and severe illumination variations, highlighting the effectiveness of differentiable learning with physics-inspired constraints for real-world atmospheric image restoration.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: single image dehazing; multiphysics simulation; atmospheric conditions

Article.Title: Empowerment and resilience through a behavioural intervention among pregnant women facing domestic violence in India
Article.Authors: Mahapatro M.; Roy S.; Nayar P.; Jadhav A.; Panchkaran S.; Chandhok G.; Srivastav D.; Prasad S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Background Women empowerment programs may reduce domestic violence (DV) by taking control of their lives. In a cognizant effort to empower pregnant women who have experienced DV, a Behaviour Intervention Package (BIP) was developed and used. It incorporates yoga-based techniques for self-development, interpersonal skill development, and awareness sessions. The study aims to assess the effects of a BIP on empowerment and resilience among pregnant women who have experienced violence and were attending antenatal care at a tertiary care hospital in India. Methods A randomised controlled trial was conducted with 211 pregnant women recruited between 18 to 20 weeks of pregnancy and randomly assigned to intervention (n = 105) or control (n = 106). The intervention group received behavioural intervention and standard care, while the control group received only standard care for 28 weeks. The study tools were completed once before the intervention and again at six weeks postnatal. The assessments were compared using methods as appropriate to estimate the effect size at baseline and post-intervention. Results The results showed that at a personal, relational, and socio-environmental level, the BIP intervention effectively improved quality of life, reduced DV, reduced stress and depression, and all parameters enabled women to develop a positive self-perception. They also reported being resilient and hopeful about their future. Conclusion The BIP may effectively empower pregnant women from low socioeconomic backgrounds facing DA in India, enhancing their quality of life. With no standardized intervention currently available, the BIP can be implemented in supportive settings to address the psychosocial health needs of women in distress and protect their health. Trial registration The Indian Registry of Clinical Trials number is CTRI/2019/01/017009 dated 9.1.2019.

Article.Title: Isoform-selective modulation of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors by quercetin and apigenin revealed through molecular simulations
Article.Authors: Balcan E.; Irani M.
Article.Abstract: This study employed an integrated computational workflow, including molecular docking, 1 µs molecular dynamics simulations, and binding free-energy calculations, to elucidate the isoform-specific interactions of the natural flavonoids apigenin and quercetin with human peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARα, PPARδ, and PPARγ). The results revealed distinct and strongly isoform-dependent interaction profiles. In PPARα, both flavonoids reduced the mobility of the activation function 2 (AF2) helix relative to the unliganded receptor, to an extent intermediate between the antagonist and the agonist, and apigenin sampled a region of the shared conformational space adjacent to that of the agonist. In PPARδ, all ligands rigidified the binding pocket to a similar degree, but apigenin alone increased the fluctuation of the AF2 helix. In PPARγ, apigenin was the only ligand that measurably increased receptor flexibility, while quercetin, the agonist, and the antagonist could not be separated on that metric. Neither flavonoid reproduced the behavior of a reference ligand across all three isoforms. Binding free-energy estimates were consistently less favorable for the flavonoids than for the reference ligands in every isoform, while physicochemical profiling indicated generally favorable drug-likeness for both compounds. Overall, these results provide a high-resolution structural framework for how apigenin and quercetin differentially engage PPAR isoforms and support testable hypotheses regarding isoform-dependent receptor modulation, without implying direct functional outcomes.

Article.Title: Melanin-concentrating hormone inhibits PVN oxytocin neurons through barium-sensitive inwardly rectifying potassium channels and MCH-neuron ablation alters pup-directed aggression
Article.Authors: Xiong T.; Saitow F.; Inutsuka A.; Onaka T.; Yamada K.; Orikasa C.
Article.Abstract: Interactions between melanin-concentrating hormone (MCH) neurons and oxytocin neurons are crucial for parental care. Whole-cell patch-clamp recordings demonstrated that MCH inhibits paraventricular hypothalamic nucleus (PVN)-oxytocin neurons through activation of barium-sensitive inwardly rectifying potassium channels, potentially G-protein coupled inwardly rectifying potassium channels, and pup-directed aggression was positively related to loss of MCH neurons. Our findings offer a glimpse into the neural mechanisms underlying the evolutionary regulation of offspring caregiving and abuse in males.

Article.Title: Adipocyte-specific mitochondrial intermediate peptidase (Mipep) deficiency protects against LPS-induced lethal inflammation through GDF15- and FGF21-independent mechanisms
Article.Authors: Fukuoh T.; Nozaki Y.; Nagasawa K.; Ayabe S.; Yokoyama M.; Mizunoe Y.; Ogawa S.; Okazaki S.; Goitsuka R.; Kobayashi M.; Higami Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sepsis is a life-threatening organ failure driven by an abnormally uncontrollable inflammatory response to systemic infection. Recent studies have demonstrated that mild mitochondrial stress confers protection against lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced septic shock; however, the precise mechanisms linking mitochondrial dysfunction to sepsis tolerance remain elusive. Here, we demonstrate that adipocyte-specific knockout of mitochondrial intermediate peptidase (MIPEP), termed aMKO, reduces susceptibility to LPS-induced mortality in mice. In MIPEP-deficient white adipose tissue (WAT), LPS-induced inflammatory responses were not uniform; selected proinflammatory and inflammasome-related responses were enhanced. By contrast, Mipep deficiency blunted the LPS-induced increase in circulating inflammatory cytokines. Consistent with this systemic attenuation, LPS-induced inflammatory cytokine expression was also less pronounced in nontargeted organs, including the liver, lungs, and spleen, where MIPEP remains intact. Although mitochondrial stress induces expression of growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15) and fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21), which have been implicated in LPS tolerance, neither GDF15 deficiency nor pharmacological inhibition of FGF receptors affected the LPS resistance acquired in aMKO mice. Together, these findings suggest that MIPEP deficiency-induced remodeling of WAT inflammatory responses attenuates LPS-induced systemic cytokine amplification and lethal inflammation through mechanisms not fully dependent on endogenous GDF15 or FGF21.

Article.Title: Planar covariation: a new key for the early detection of Duchenne muscular dystrophy walking behaviour
Article.Authors: Ruiz P.; Cheron G.; Deconinck N.; Cebolla A.
Article.Abstract: Three-dimensional gait analysis objectively quantifies lower-limb function and has been used to describe the gait pathomechanics in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) and to assess treatments. However, elevation angles, non-redundant sagittal-plane measures relative to the vertical axis, have not been examined in children with DMD, nor have gait differences between overground and treadmill walking been investigated in this population. This study investigated elevation angle profiles, planar covariation, spatiotemporal parameters, and joint kinematics in young children with DMD and typically developing (TD) children walking overground and on a treadmill. Kinematics were recorded using a Vicon motion capture system during self-selected overground and treadmill walking in twenty-five age-matched boys (fourteen with DMD; mean age 6.43 ± 1.45 years). Results showed that normalized step length and walking velocity were higher overground than on the treadmill in both groups. DMD children showed consistently wider normalized step width than TD peers. Joint kinematics did not distinguish groups across conditions, whereas elevation angles and planar covariation revealed significant overground differences in DMD children who exhibited reduced foot elevation angles bilaterally during terminal swing. They also showed smaller percent of variance on the first principal component (PV1) and larger percent of variance of the second principal component (PV2) values, with shorter, wider loops, suggesting weaker primary coordination and greater compensatory adjustments. These findings indicate that planar covariation can detect subtle gait alterations in young DMD children during overground walking, highlighting early compensatory coordination strategies not observable under treadmill pacing. Foot elevation angle modulation might serve as a sensitive marker for disease progression and treatment evaluation.

Article.Title: Sex- and age-related heterogeneity in obstructive sleep apnea phenotypes in a predominantly Afro-Caribbean population
Article.Authors: Agossou M.; Metanmo S.; Simo N.; Edoh Coffi M.; Inamo J.; Andreu M.; Awanou B.; Provost M.; Ahouansou N.; Duféal M.; Tabué-Teguo M.; Dramé M.
Article.Abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) shows wide variability in clinical presentation. Sex-related differences in symptom expression are increasingly recognized, but the contribution of age and respiratory event composition remains insufficiently explored in underrepresented populations. To describe sex- and age-related heterogeneity in clinical and respiratory phenotypes of OSA in a predominantly Afro-Caribbean population referred to a tertiary sleep center. We conducted a cross-sectional study of consecutive adults evaluated for suspected OSA at a tertiary sleep center (July 2024-June 2025). Clinical characteristics, symptom profiles, and respiratory indices were compared by sex and age (< 65 vs ≥ 65 years). Multivariable models adjusting for BMI and age assessed whether sex differences were independent of these factors. Among 213 patients evaluated, 189 had OSA (women: 61.4%, n = 116). Women had a higher BMI than men (31.4 vs 27.6 kg·m −2 , p < 0.001) and a lower respiratory event burden, with a lower apnea index and oxygen desaturation index but a higher relative contribution of hypopneas to the AHI (all p ≤ 0.045). Women also reported more insomnia (68.1% vs 49.2%, p = 0.02) and higher fatigue scores ( p = 0.02), with no significant difference in daytime sleepiness. After adjustment for age and BMI, these sex differences in respiratory indices persisted (all p ≤ 0.002), while the fatigue association was attenuated ( p = 0.08). Age ≥ 65 years was independently associated with a higher AHI, apnea index and ODI, a lower hypopnea/AHI ratio, and lower odds of excessive daytime sleepiness (adjusted OR 0.32, p = 0.002), patterns masked in unadjusted comparisons. A sex × age interaction was significant only for insomnia ( p = 0.007): the sex difference was confined to patients ≥ 65 years (adjusted OR 9.12) and absent in younger patients (adjusted OR 1.20). OSA phenotypes in this Caribbean population show marked heterogeneity by sex and respiratory event composition, largely independent of BMI and age. Age modulated daytime sleepiness, respiratory composition, and the sex-related difference in insomnia, which was concentrated among older patients. Reliance on daytime sleepiness alone may underestimate OSA burden in women, older patients, and hypopnea-dominant phenotypes, supporting a more phenotype- and age-based approach to screening.

Article.Title: Genome-based taxonomy reveals hidden diversity within the reorganized Stenotrophomonas genus and supports the proposal of a novel species
Article.Authors: Laço J.; Riesco R.; Gomila M.
Article.Abstract: The genus Stenotrophomonas comprises globally distributed bacteria of increasing clinical relevance, characterized by intrinsic multidrug resistance and remarkable ecological versatility. Species-level identification within this group remains challenging as formal classifications in public databases continue to underestimate its true diversity. A recent genome-based reclassification proposed the division of the genus into five distinct genera: Allostenotrophomonas , Parastenotrophomonas , Pedostenotrophomonas , Pseudostenotrophomonas , and Stenotrophomonas , introducing further taxonomic uncertainty in an already complex and clinically important lineage. In this study we performed a comprehensive genome-based analysis of 146 genomes, previously classified as Stenotrophomonas , including 22 isolates recovered from hospital sink drains. Using average nucleotide identity (ANI), digital DNA–DNA hybridization (dDDH), and average amino acid identity (AAI), we identified 31 species-level clusters within the redefined Stenotrophomonas sensu stricto lineage, including sixteen potential new species. Our findings support the proposal of a novel species, Stenotrophomonas balearica sp. nov. (type strain GM_D5_149 T = CCUG 78226 T = CECT 31222 T ). Pan-genome analysis revealed an open pan-genome with a highly diverse accessory genome, reflecting the genus’s genetic plasticity and ecological adaptability. Putative resistance and virulence determinants were unevenly distributed across lineages, with enrichment within the S. maltophilia complex, reinforcing its clinical significance. Overall, our findings clarify species boundaries, reveal extensive cryptic diversity, and provide a genome-resolved framework for accurate taxonomic assignment within this increasingly relevant bacterial group. These results underscore the importance of genome-based systematics for improving diagnostic accuracy, epidemiological surveillance, and antimicrobial resistance monitoring.

Article.Title: Effects of feedstock and pyrolysis temperature on carbon stabilization and mineral functionality of biochars
Article.Authors: Bivareh M.; Mahmoudi N.; Younesi H.; Safari O.
Article.Abstract: Understanding how feedstock composition and pyrolysis conditions regulate carbon stabilization, mineral transformation, and surface characteristics is critical to predicting biochar evolution across biomass resources. This study examined how feedstock type and pyrolysis temperature influence physicochemical, mineralogical, and surface properties of biochars from sugarcane bagasse (SB), pistachio branches (PB), and cattle manure (CM) at 300, 500, and 700 °C. Increasing pyrolysis temperature reduced yield, zeta potential, moisture, volatile matter, hydrogen, oxygen, H/C, O/C, and cation exchange capacity (CEC), while increasing fixed carbon, pH, pHpzc, EC, ash, and organic carbon content. At 700 °C, lignocellulosic biochars showed higher carbon and fixed-carbon contents and lower H/C and O/C ratios, indicating greater carbonization and aromatic condensation. In contrast, CM biochars generally showed higher yields, pH, CEC, ash content, and mineral concentrations than lignocellulosic biochars, whereas their EC values were lower. Their elemental and oxide compositions were richer, with more pronounced crystalline structures. These features indicate pronounced mineral inheritance from the mineral-rich feedstock. These findings provide a physicochemical framework for biochar evolution, linking carbon structure, mineral composition, surface chemistry, and porosity to feedstock–temperature-dependent characteristics. Such insights provide a basis for future environmental and agricultural application-oriented studies, while direct performance evaluations remain necessary before practical recommendations can be made.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: pyrolysis temperature; biochar; carbon stabilization; feedstock effects

Article.Title: REAMP: a stochastic resonance approach for multi-change point detection in high-dimensional data
Article.Authors: Shi X.; Jin B.; Liu X.; Li Q.
Article.Abstract: Detecting multiple structural breaks in high-dimensional data remains a challenge, particularly when changes occur in higher-order moments or within complex manifold structures. In this paper, we propose REAMP (Resonance - Enhanced Analysis of Multi-change Points), a novel framework that integrates optimal transport theory with the physical principles of stochastic resonance. By utilizing a two-stage dimension reduction via the Earth Mover’s Distance (EMD) and Shortest Hamiltonian Paths (SHP), we map high-dimensional observations onto a graph-based count statistic. To overcome the locality constraints of traditional search algorithms, we implement a stochastic resonance system that utilizes randomized Beta-density priors to “vibrate” the objective function. This process allows multiple change points to resonate as global minima across iterative simulations, generating a candidate point cloud. A double-sharpening procedure is then applied to these candidates to pinpoint precise change point locations. We establish the asymptotic consistency of the resonance estimator and demonstrate through simulations that REAMP outperforms state-of-the-art methods, especially in scenarios involving simultaneous mean and variance shifts. The practical utility of the method is further validated through two real-world applications: time-lapse embryo monitoring and automated bee exit event detection, where REAMP provides both accurate detection and intuitive visualization of structural state transitions.

Article.Title: Amblyopia treatment outcomes did not differ in a multi-regional binocular treatment trial between Chinese Han and White children
Article.Authors: Yehezkel O.; Kushner B.; Liu R.; Jaffe N.; Belkin M.; Wygnanski-Jaffe T.; N/A N/A.; Sala N.; Cox W.; Sala N.; Hodde R.; Zeto L.; Crouch E.; Kun A.; Bejarano L.; Ventura G.; de Veer C.; Hamric I.; Khuddus N.; Toskes T.; Troiano B.; Jenewein E.; Scombordi B.; Campbell J.; Myung J.
Article.Abstract: To date, no study has compared amblyopia treatment outcomes between White and Chinese Han children treated using a similar protocol, and data are lacking on whether treatment efficacy differs by race/ethnicity. This post-hoc exploratory analysis compared two methods of amblyopia treatment outcomes (patching and binocular treatment (CureSight, NovaSight, Israel) between Chinese Han and White children enrolled in a prospective, multicenter, evaluator-masked randomized clinical trial. A total of 186 children aged 4 to < 9 years (137 White; 49 Chinese Han) with anisometropic, strabismic, or mixed-mechanism amblyopia were randomized in 1:1 ratio to home-based binocular treatment (90 min/day, 5 days/week) or patching (2 h/day, 7 days/week) for 16 weeks. Overall amblyopic-eye visual acuity (VA) improvement was similar in White and Chinese Han participants (0.25 ± 0.13 and 0.24 ± 0.11 logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution (logMAR) (mean ± standard deviation), respectively; both p < 0.0001); the between-race least-squares mean difference was -0.026 logMAR (95% CI -0.209 to 0.157; p = 0.777). No significant between-race differences were found in stereoacuity improvement (p = 0.15) or binocular VA improvement (p = 0.856). Adherence exceeded 85% in both groups (monitored objectively via eye-tracking logs for binocular treatment and via parental diaries for patching); no serious adverse events were reported. These findings suggest that amblyopia treatment outcomes may not differ meaningfully by race/ethnicity, though the small Chinese Han sample (n = 49) limits definitive conclusions. Larger prospective studies are warranted.

Article.Title: Factors associated with protective behaviors against pesticide exposure: a study of rice farmers in Northern Iran
Article.Authors: Sharifzadeh M.; Hashemi M.; Abdollahzadeh G.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Background : Rice farming in Mazandaran Province, Iran, relies heavily on chemical pesticides, posing significant health and environmental risks. Despite efforts to promote pro-environmental practices, farmers’ adoption of protective and sustainable behaviors remains limited. This study investigates the determinants of rice farmers’ preventive awareness and protective behaviors, focusing on the sequential progression from awareness to preparation and eventual recognition of the need for alternative pest management strategies within an enabling environment framework. Methods : A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 388 rice farmers across three major counties of Mazandaran Province. Data were collected through structured questionnaire and analyzed using exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and multiple linear regression (MLR). Results : Findings revealed generally low levels of preventive awareness and protective behavior. EFA identified four behavioral stages: awareness of pesticide impact, avoidance of pesticide poisoning effect, Preparation for protective behavior, and recognition of regent need for alternative pest management alongside three enabling environment factors: social support, institutional incentives, and information flows. Education, gender, and household labor participation significantly influenced behavioral outcomes, while higher income and yield were negatively associated with protective actions. Among enabling environment variables, information flows exerted the strongest and most consistent influence across all behavioral stages, followed by institutional incentives and social support. Conclusion : This study advances understanding of behavior change in pesticide use and pest management by conceptualizing protective behavior as a multi-stage process influenced by individual, economic, and institutional factors. The inclusion of enabling environment variables fills a key research gap and offers a comprehensive analytical framework. Policymakers should strengthen information networks, institutional support, and targeted training programs to facilitate gradual behavioral transformation toward sustainable pest management in Mazandaran’s rice sector.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: institutional incentives; rice farmers; pesticide exposure; protective behavior; social support; sustainable pest management; alternative pest control; Mazandaran; information flow; enabling environment

Article.Title: Parental attitudes toward the vaccination of children diagnosed with congenital heart disease: a cross-sectional comparative study
Article.Authors: Yıldız Cengiz R.; Akın A.; Ture M.; Öz D.; Demir Pervane V.; Akar A.; Erten Bucaktepe P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Background The presence of chronic disease in children is one of the important factors affecting vaccination status. The aim of this study was to evaluate the attitudes to childhood vaccinations of the parents of children diagnosed with congenital heart disease (CHD) on presentation at the Paediatric Cardiology Polyclinic of Dicle University Medical Faculty Hospital, and the vaccination status of the children through comparisons with the parents of healthy children. Method This case-control study included a case group of parents of children who presented at the Paediatric Cardiology Polyclinic of Dicle University Medical Faculty Hospital between 01.06.2022 and 01.06.2023 and were diagnosed with CHD. The control group was formed of parents of children not diagnosed with CHD. The Parental Attitude to Childhood Vaccination (PACV) scale and a questionnaire to elicit sociodemographic characteristics and the vaccination status of the children were used to collect data. Results Evaluations were made of a total of 731 parents, as 274 in the case group and 457 in the control group. No significant difference was determined between the groups in respect of the rates of application of the vaccinations included in the childhood vaccination schedule of the Health Ministry of the Turkish Republic (p > 0.05 for all variables). The rates of rotavirus and meningococcus vaccinations was determined to be significantly higher in the control group (p < 0.001, p < 0.001). In the comparisons between the case and control groups, vaccine hesitancy was determined at a significantly higher rate in the control group (p = 0.006). The total raw points obtained from the PACV scale, converted points, and general attitude points were found to be statistically significantly higher in the control group (p < 0.001, p < 0.001, p = 0.019, respectively). In the case group, the rate of vaccine hesitancy of the parents of children with cyanotic heart disease was found to be higher (p = 0.038). Conclusion The results of this study showed that the rates of vaccine hesitancy were lower for the parents of children diagnosed with CHD than for the parents of healthy children. However, the presence of cyanotic heart disease emerged as a medical factor that significantly increased vaccine hesitancy. The rates of vaccine hesitancy in both groups were determined to be affected by sociodemographic characteristics, level of knowledge about vaccinations, trust in doctors, and economic factors.

Article.Title: Decade-long data highlight medium-sized, fast-flowing cold-water streams as important recruitment habitats for European river and brook lampreys
Article.Authors: Abersons K.; Elferts D.; Raibarte P.; Dimante-Deimantovica I.
Article.Abstract: European river lamprey Lampetra fluviatilis is a migratory (anadromous) species, spawning in freshwater rivers where it co-occurs with its non-migratory paired species, European brook lamprey L. planeri . Both species are listed under Annex II of the EU Habitats Directive, requiring habitat protection and sustainable management across their distribution ranges. Yet, both species have experienced declines and spatial drivers of larval recruitment remain poorly quantified. Lamprey larvae are known to occupy low-velocity depositional microhabitats, but how these requirements scale across river networks remains unclear. Here, we analysed size-structured populations of lamprey larvae across 177 sites in 32 Latvian rivers using data collected between 2014 and 2025. Higher proportions of smaller larvae, likely corresponding to the youngest age classes, were associated with river reaches of medium-size and small catchment area, moderate and high riverbed gradient and colder temperature. In contrast, larger individuals dominated low-gradient, warm river sections with large catchment area. These findings suggest that the observed longitudinal recruitment pattern may be driven by downstream larval dispersal across river networks and highlight small- and medium-sized, relatively fast-flowing cold-water reaches as important recruitment habitats. However, recruitment potential in these important habitats may be reduced by anthropogenic pressures, particularly migration barriers and channelization. Our findings highlight the importance of protecting and restoring small- and medium-sized streams and mitigating anthropogenic pressures to support the favourable conservation status of European river and brook lampreys.

Article.Title: ESR1 bridges GNGT1 to CLDN6 in promoting gastric cancer stemness and development
Article.Authors: zhang Y.; chen S.; zhuang Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Gastric cancer (GC) remains a major global health burden, and the molecular determinants driving its progression are incompletely understood. In the present study, G protein subunit gamma transducin 1 (GNGT1) was identified as a clinically relevant oncogenic driver that promotes GC growth, stemness, and metastatic traits. Transcriptomic analysis of the stomach adenocarcinoma cohort of The Cancer Genome Atlas revealed that GNGT1 was significantly upregulated in GC tissues and that its high expression predicted markedly shorter overall (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). These findings were validated at the protein level using immunohistochemistry on a GC tissue microarray, where elevated GNGT1 expression was associated with higher histological grade and poorer survival. Functional experiments demonstrated that GNGT1 silencing impaired cell proliferation, migration and clonogenicity, induced G 2 -phase arrest, enhanced apoptotic signaling and increased GC cells sensitivity to 5-fluorouracil. Mechanistically, interaction profiling and chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assays revealed that GNGT1 interacted with estrogen receptor 1 (ESR1) and contributed to maintaining its protein abundance and nuclear accumulation, thereby enhancing ESR1-dependent transcriptional activation of claudin 6 (CLDN6). Upregulated CLDN6 in turn promoted epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) -associated signaling and elevated the expression of stemness markers Nanog and OCT4. Furthermore, the CLDN6/Wnt/β-catenin axis was implicated in GNGT1-mediated cancer stem cell properties, whereas pharmacological inhibition of Wnt/β-catenin signaling attenuated GNGT1-induced proliferation and migration. In vivo, GNGT1 depletion significantly reduced tumor growth, stemness marker expression and cell proliferation in xenograft models. Collectively, the present study identified GNGT1 as a previously unrecognized regulator of GC progression and stemness, acting via the GNGT1-ESR1-CLDN6-Wnt/β-catenin signaling axis to promote malignant phenotypes. These findings suggest that GNGT1 may represent a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in GC.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: epithelial-mesenchymal transition; CLDN6; therapeutic target; gastric cancer; Wnt/β-catenin signaling; 5-fluorouracil sensitivity; cancer stemness; estrogen receptor 1; prognostic factors; stem cell markers

Article.Title: Designing novel fly ash proppant with high buoyancy and high durability for hydraulic fracturing: an experimental investigation
Article.Authors: Haydar R.; Fakher S.
Article.Abstract: Proppants are essential components in hydraulic fracturing, ensuring that fractures maintain conductivity. In high-pressure, harsh environments, high-strength, durable proppants are used, which are expensive and require costly fracture fluids. This research evaluates the ability to develop a new type of proppant using fly ash, a waste material, and assess the proppant’s durability under harsh conditions. Fly ash-based proppant is durable, environmentally friendly, buoyant, and cost-effective. To develop the fly ash-based proppant, an alkaline solution was used as an activator and binder. The proppant samples were tested under high temperature and pressure, as well as in acidic, alkaline, saline, and crude oil environments to evaluate their durability. Density was also assessed to determine the buoyancy of the proppant, which affects the fracturing fluid. The mix designs included weight ratios of 20%, 22%, and 25% binder, with a fixed 25% water content in all mixtures. After environmental testing, the B20W25 mix design was the best performing, showing minor erosion and deterioration. Conversely, the increasing binder concentration in the mix did not withstand the more aggressive environmental conditions. The density of the samples ranged from 1.33 to 1.36 g/cc, making them lighter than sand and thus highly buoyant.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: fly ash; hydraulic fracturing; buoyancy; proppant

Article.Title: Standardised procalcitonin monitoring and antibiotic duration in community-acquired sepsis: a pragmatic randomised controlled trial
Article.Authors: Meensuk T.; Chavapradit N.
Article.Abstract: Prolonged antibiotic therapy drives antimicrobial resistance, yet most evidence for procalcitonin (PCT)-guided stewardship in sepsis comes from protocol-driven trials in intensive care. We conducted a pragmatic, open-label, randomised controlled trial at a tertiary emergency department in Bangkok, Thailand (February 2025–March 2026). Adults with community-acquired sepsis (infection plus two or more systemic inflammatory response syndrome criteria) were randomised 1:1 to scheduled PCT measurement on days 0, 2 and 5, with results returned through routine channels, or to standard care; treating physicians retained full discretion. The primary outcome was total antibiotic duration. Of 182 randomised participants, 130 were analysed after post-randomisation withdrawals (PCT n = 62, control n = 68). Antibiotic duration was shorter with PCT monitoring (median 7 days, interquartile range 6–10, versus 9 days, 7–12.5; Mann–Whitney exact P = 0.028; mean difference − 1.34 days, 95% confidence interval − 2.60 to − 0.08). Twenty-eight-day mortality was 4/62 (6.5%) versus 3/68 (4.4%) (risk ratio 1.46, 95% confidence interval 0.34 to 6.28) and, among all randomised participants with known status, 12/87 (13.8%) versus 16/92 (17.4%) (risk ratio 0.79, 0.40 to 1.58); the trial was not powered for mortality and cannot exclude harm. Guidance-only PCT monitoring shortened antibiotic duration in emergency department sepsis; its safety requires confirmation in a larger trial. Trial registration: Thai Clinical Trial Registry no. TCTR20250216013 (https://www.thaiclinicaltrials.org)
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: antibiotic duration; procalcitonin; community-acquired sepsis; sepsis; antimicrobial stewardship

Article.Title: Unveiling the diversity of avastroviruses in tropical wild birds from the Atlantic Forest, Brazil
Article.Authors: Haisi A.; Schunck F.; de Azevedo L.; Cunha M.; de Almeida R.; Silva V.; Luchs A.; Araújo Junior J.
Article.Abstract: Astroviruses are widespread RNA viruses that infect a broad range of animal hosts, with avastroviruses (AAstVs) primarily infecting avian species. While AAstVs are well-documented in domestic birds, their presence in wild birds, particularly in tropical ecosystems like Brazil’s Atlantic Forest, has been underexplored. This study investigated the prevalence and genetic diversity of AAstVs in wild birds from the Serra do Mar State Park, São Paulo. A total of 417 fecal samples were collected from birds representing 89 species between 2022 and 2023. During a parallel investigation of Reovirales -related viruses, NGS unexpectedly revealed a potential novel AAstV strain in one sample, here named Passerine Avastrovirus (PasAstV M1580). Conventional RT-PCR, targeting the conserved RdRp gene, detected AAstV in 7.67% (32/417) of the samples. AAstV was repeatedly detected in recaptured individuals of Troglodytes musculus and Hylophilus poicilotis at multiple time points. Immune status was not assessed, limiting interpretation of shedding versus natural infection. Complete genome analysis of PasAstV M1580 revealed typical AAstV genomic features and suggests that it may represent a putative novel species within the Avastrovirus genus, displaying amino acid identity ranging from 25.18% to 33.23% in the ORF2 region compared to prototype strains. The genomic characterization of PasAstV M1580 expands the known diversity within the genus Avastrovirus and provides new insights into ecology of AAstVs in tropical wild bird populations of the Brazilian Atlantic Forest.

Article.Title: Evaluating the multi-scale performance and mechanical behavior of reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) mixtures incorporating waste-derived oils and vacuum bottom rejuvenators
Article.Authors: Amini S.; Akbari M.; Shafabakhsh G.; Vamegh M.
Article.Abstract: Maximizing the utilization of reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) while maintaining long-term fatigue durability is essential for sustainable pavement infrastructure. To address this challenge, this study aims to establish a multi-scale framework for evaluating and optimizing rejuvenator performance in high-RAP mixtures. Accordingly, the efficacy of three distinct rejuvenators—Waste Engine Oil (WEO), Lubricant Oil (LU), and Vacuum Bottom (VB)—was investigated in restoring the chemical and mechanical properties of bitumens and mixtures incorporating 30%, 45%, and 60% RAP. Using a viscosity-matching approach, rejuvenator dosages were optimized to target virgin PG64-22 bitumen rheology. SARA analysis showed that LU and VB restored colloidal balance by reducing asphaltenes from 27.0% to 17.5–18.1% and restoring aromatics to 44.3–45.2%, whereas WEO provided only partial chemical recovery. Linear Amplitude Sweep (LAS) testing revealed that LU and VB extended bitumen fatigue life by 21% and 29% at 2.5% and 5.0% shear strains, respectively. At the mixture scale, 4-point bending fatigue resistance improved by 76–85% at 500 µɛ and by 34–40% at severe 700 µɛ for 60% RAP mixtures with LU and VB. Furthermore, moisture durability was increased, with R60LU reaching a superior Tensile Strength Ratio (TSR = 90.7%) compared to the control (80.7%). These quantitative findings demonstrate that chemical rejuvenation via LU or VB provides 60% RAP mixtures with comparable or superior laboratory fatigue and moisture resistance relative to the virgin mixture.

Article.Title: Human motor and economic decisions show common risk-seeking bias under asymmetric gains
Article.Authors: Tsunoda K.; Onagawa R.; Kudo K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To plan actions optimally, it is essential to take one’s own variability into account. The outcome of an action is determined by the target of the action plan, the variability of the action, and the gain/loss function of the outcome. In previous studies, we demonstrated that humans make risk-seeking, suboptimal motor decisions under gain functions characterized by an asymmetry, where higher gains are associated with a higher risk of zero gain. However, it remained unclear whether such suboptimal and risk-seeking behavior stems from the motor decision-making process. Here, we examined whether this bias also arises in economic decision-making which does not include a motor variance component. In Experiment 1, we investigated the response distribution in an experiment where participants pressed a key within a specified time window to earn points based on their reaction time, using a gain function characterized by the asymmetry. Consistent with previous studies, we observed risk-seeking, suboptimal decision-making in this motor task. In Experiment 2, using the same gain function, participants made a numerical selection, with the chosen number serving as the mean from which values were sampled from a normal distribution with variance similar to that in the motor task. As in Experiment 1, we observed risk-seeking, suboptimal decision-making in this economic task. Trial-by-trial analyses revealed that the compensation strategies depending on error size were similar, but a task-dependent difference emerged when the error size was large. These results indicate a robust bias in both motor and economic decision-making under gain functions with asymmetry, highlighting that optimality in human decision-making under risk is limited.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: economic decision-making; motor decision-making; suboptimal decision making; compensatory strategies; reaction time

Article.Title: Investigating the control of subsurface structures on rainfall-induced ground instability using integrated geophysics and remote sensing in Jixi, China
Article.Authors: Fan Z.; Shi F.; Gao Z.; Teng M.; Luo J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Landslides are common geological hazards worldwide, often associated with by heavy rainfall. Jixi City, located in southeastern Heilongjiang Province, experiences frequent rainstorms from July to September. Long‑term unregulated quarrying has destroyed vegetation and reduced slope toe stability in the area. In early August 2023, Typhoon Doksuri increased rainfall. The Jixi landslide occurred on August 10 following this heavy rainfall. This study integrates aeromagnetic data, electrical resistivity tomography (ERT), multi‑temporal satellite and UAV remote sensing, borehole data, and surface displacement monitoring. Aeromagnetic anomalies support a magnetically quiet basement without deep magmatic activity. ERT 2D and quasi‑3D inversions, calibrated by six boreholes, reveal a three‑part electrical structure: a shallow discontinuous high‑resistivity landslide deposit, a continuous low‑resistivity slip zone interpreted as mudstone with elevated moisture content and fault fracture zones, and a deeper blocky high‑resistivity slip bed. Steeply dipping low‑resistivity belts are interpreted as possible water‑bearing faults. Multi‑temporal images show progressive quarry expansion. Post‑landslide UAV orthophotos indicate that the main landslide body showed approximately 20 m of cumulative displacement toward the southwest between 2020 and 2023, with a fan‑shaped morphology exhibiting apparent retrogressive geomorphic characteristics. Surface monitoring from August 17 recorded horizontal displacements of 0.2–35.2 cm, with the dominant direction toward the southwest and elevation changes showing rear subsidence and frontal uplift. Boreholes support the transition from intact slip bed to fractured landslide mass. Based on these results, a possible evolutionary chain is proposed as an evidence‑supported interpretation: quarrying disturbance, typhoon‑induced rainfall infiltration, fault‑controlled water conduction, slip zone softening, and retrogressive sliding. The multi‑method approach provides cross‑scale constraints from regional background to shallow detailed structures, offering a scientific basis for post‑disaster identification, investigation, and mitigation of similar landslides.
