Article.Title: Lightweight multimodal fusion for UAV classification with explicit missing-modality modeling
Article.Authors: Feng Y.; Li N.; Wu D.; Ma X.; Yu X.; Bao H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Fine-grained unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) type classification benefits from complementary sensors, yet real deployments face incomplete observations and heterogeneous stream reliability. We present a missing-aware fusion framework for RGB detections (YOLO11-S), Livox Avia LiDAR, 360° LiDAR, and radar-enhanced point clouds on MMAUD. Confidence–density scores are masked and renormalized so fusion weight is assigned only to observed streams (Eq. (2)); each absent stream still occupies a classifier slot via a learnable missing embedding that is not multiplied by the zero weight (Eq. (1)), keeping absence as a trainable signal rather than a numerical zero. On a time-stratified split, Tiny MLP (≈ 0.1 M fusion parameters) reaches 96.12% test accuracy in a representative seed-42 run. Over seeds 42–46, final test accuracy is 95.29 ± 0.60% without training-time modality dropout and 95.77 ± 0.90% with 30% training ModDrop (mean ± sample s.d.). Under matched 30% test missingness, accuracy remains 83.68% (seed 42). Protocol-aligned baselines and orthogonal ablations support the slot rule. Fusion-stage inference is about 2.1 ms per sample with pre-extracted features on an RTX 4090. Under our fixed split and frozen features—not as a challenge-leaderboard claim—compact missing-aware fusion is practical for heterogeneous UAV sensing under partial sensor availability.

Article.Title: Vessel-associated microglia contribute to blood-brain barrier disruption via a Notch-IL-1β axis in the diabetic brain
Article.Authors: Lee D.; Jung M.; Jeong H.; Kim S.; Kim G.; Shin H.; Cho C.
Article.Abstract: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is associated with central nervous system (CNS) complications, including cognitive impairment and an increased risk of neurodegenerative diseases. However, the cellular mechanisms underlying blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption in the diabetic brain remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the contribution of microglia to diabetes-induced BBB dysfunction. Using a streptozotocin (STZ)-induced mouse model of type 1 diabetes, we observed increased BBB permeability and an accumulation of vessel-associated microglia. Transcriptomic analysis of isolated microglia revealed upregulation of genes associated with migration, angiogenesis, and vascular permeability, alongside activation of Notch signaling. We found that endothelial cell (EC)-derived CCL20, upregulated by TNF-α, promotes microglial migration via AKT signaling. Furthermore, direct interaction with ECs activates Notch signaling in microglia, inducing IL-1β expression and disrupting EC tight junctions. Treatment with minocycline attenuated microglial activation, restored endothelial Tjp1 expression, and reduced vascular leakage. These findings identify a novel microglia-EC signaling axis that contributes to BBB impairment in diabetes and suggest that targeting microglial activation may offer therapeutic potential for protecting neurovascular integrity in diabetic neuropathology.

Article.Title: Structurally coupled cooperative inversion of ERT and SRT data with sequential cluster analysis for integrated imaging of an Andean rock glacier
Article.Authors: Yazdanpanah A.; Abedi M.
Article.Abstract: Integrating diverse geophysical datasets is paramount for characterizing complex geological formations, such as relict rock glaciers, where inherent heterogeneities pose significant challenges. This study showcases the efficacy of a structurally coupled cooperative inversion (SCCI) framework applied to electrical resistivity (ERT) and seismic refraction tomography (SRT) data, validated through a detailed synthetic modeling phase designed to test the method’s stability, sensitivity to structural information, and practical applicability in heterogeneous near-surface environments. Both forward and inverse modelling phases are conducted using unstructured triangular meshing. This method enables numerical stability for high topographic reliefs and local refinements (e.g., near sensors). For enhanced subsurface interpretation, we implemented Mean shift clustering, facilitating an automated analysis and seamless integration of the ERT and SRT inversion outputs. The subsequent application of SCCI to field data, augmented by the sequential clustering stage, successfully recovered expected subsurface anomalies and revealed intricate layering. Critically, this integrated SCCI approach significantly advanced the complexity of subsurface structures that could be accurately delineated, offering a more profound understanding of the relict rock glacier’s architecture and properties. Together, these components provide a coherent workflow that advances structurally coupled geophysical inversion and offers a reproducible basis for multi-method subsurface characterization.

Article.Authors: Amirrajab S.; Vehof V.; Bietenbeck M.; Yilmaz A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We investigated the utilization of privacy-preserving, locally-deployed, open-source Large Language Models (LLMs) to extract diagnostic information from free-text cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) reports. Performance was quantified using standard classification metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. We also employed confusion matrices to examine patterns of misclassification across models. Most open-source LLMs demonstrated exceptional performance in classifying reports into different diagnostic categories. Google’s Gemma 2(27B) model achieved the highest average F1 score of 0.98, followed by Qwen2.5(32B) and DeepSeekR1(32B) with F1 scores of 0.96 and 0.95, respectively. All other evaluated models attained average scores above 0.93, with Mistral(7B) and DeepSeekR1(7B) being the only exceptions. The top four LLMs outperformed our board-certified cardiologist (F1 score of 0.94) across all evaluation metrics in analyzing CMR reports. Our findings demonstrate the feasibility of implementing open-source, privacy-preserving LLMs in clinical settings for automated analysis of imaging reports, enabling accurate, fast and resource-efficient diagnostic categorization.

Article.Title: Association of sarcopenia with 9-year trajectories of depressive symptoms in middle-aged and older Chinese adults
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Huang X.; Zhao Y.; Han J.
Article.Abstract: Sarcopenia is linked to depressive symptoms, but its long-term impact on the trajectories of depressive symptoms in middle-aged and older Chinese adults is unclear. We analyzed five waves of longitudinal data (2011–2020) from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), involving 7,200 adults aged ≥ 45. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D). Group-based trajectory modeling (GBTM) identified distinct depressive symptom trajectories over 9 years. Multinomial logistic regression analyzed associations between sarcopenia status and its core indicators (muscle mass, muscle strength, and physical performance) with these trajectories. Four depressive symptom trajectories were identified: low and stable, low-moderate and stable, high and rapidly increasing, and moderate and increasing. In the fully adjusted model, compared with the non-sarcopenia group, possible sarcopenia was associated with higher odds of belonging to the high-rapidly increasing trajectory (OR = 1.59, 95% CI: 1.30–1.95), the moderate-increasing trajectory (OR = 1.55, 95% CI: 1.32–1.81), and the low-moderate stable trajectory (OR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.01–1.38). Similarly, sarcopenia was associated with higher odds of belonging to the high-rapidly increasing (OR = 2.18, 95% CI: 1.52–3.13), moderate-increasing (OR = 1.84, 95% CI: 1.35–2.49), and low-moderate stable (OR = 1.39, 95% CI: 1.03–1.89) trajectories compared with the low-stable group. Among the sarcopenia components, poor physical performance was associated with all adverse trajectories, whereas low muscle strength and low muscle mass were associated with only some of these trajectories. Sarcopenia and its core components are associated with adverse depressive symptom trajectories over a 9-year span. Incorporating physical function assessments into geriatric care may help identify individuals at higher risk of chronic mental distress during the aging process.

Article.Authors: Imani M.; Hasannejad M.; Imani A.; Shafiekhani M.
Article.Abstract: Large language models may support clinical information tasks, but hallucination, limited evidence traceability, and inconsistent workflow integration remain barriers to clinical deployment. We evaluated Dr.Copilot, a multilingual retrieval-augmented clinical AI framework combining hybrid evidence retrieval, specialized tools, and model-directed orchestration. During a 70-day deployment, 835 registered users generated 956 conversation threads; the analytics log contained 22,574 events and 4,226 tool-use events. In the original 64-prompt expert benchmark, Dr.Copilot and GPT-5.5 had comparable weighted scores (4.607 vs. 4.561; paired difference 0.046, 95% CI -0.064 to 0.140; p = 0.103). In a new independent 75-case, fixed-backbone external validation, Dr.Copilot scored 4.557 versus 4.217 for GPT-5.5 (difference 0.340, 95% CI 0.181 to 0.519; p = 0.00023), with fewer clinically important errors (5/75 vs. 16/75; p = 0.00098). A 30-case four-arm GPT-5.4 ablation found the highest mean score with standard RAG (4.813), while additional prespecified-tool and model-directed routing conditions did not yield uniform further gains. Targeted safety, pediatric, multilingual, citation, temporal, and abstention analyses identified both strengths and important failure modes. These findings support retrieval as the clearest incremental contributor in this evaluation, while underscoring that agentic tool orchestration requires direct validation and does not itself establish clinical benefit or patient-safety improvement.

Article.Title: Short-term thromboembolism risk and coagulation profiles among Thai transmasculine individuals receiving testosterone therapy: a quasi-experimental study
Article.Authors: Nimitpanya P.; Panyakhamlerd K.; Suwan A.; Uaprasert N.; Panichaya P.; Chavaengkiat S.; Rungruxsirivorn T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract While the use of gender-affirming hormone therapy is steadily increasing, safety data specific to Asian transgender populations remain limited. Blood samples were collected at baseline and week 13 (mid-interval) to assess median change in APC sensitivity ratio (APCsr), coagulation markers and natural anticoagulant levels, alongside hematological, biochemical, and hormonal assessments. The overall hemostatic shift was heterogeneous. Subgroup analysis according to total testosterone levels did not exhibit significant trend toward procoagulative change. APCsr did not significantly correlate with hormonal profiles. In predictive modeling, estradiol positively correlated with factor IX and fibrinogen levels, whereas rising hematocrit predicted natural anticoagulant levels. Short-term administration of testosterone enanthate did not alter the baseline risk of venous thromboembolism among Thai transmasculine population. Article.Title: Effects of storage temperature and delayed analysis on routine biochemical and haematological test results
Article.Authors: Yağan A.; Akpolat Z.; Yalçın D.; Şahin H.; Yağan M.; Doğan M.; Kalay Z.; Soylu Ü.; İncecik Ş.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Blood samples collected in primary care may be transported to central laboratories, creating variable intervals between collection, processing and analysis. This study evaluated the effects of delayed analysis and storage temperature on routine biochemical and haematological test results under controlled laboratory conditions, with relevance to specimen handling and transport in primary care. This prospective, controlled, repeated-measures laboratory study included 32 healthy volunteers (16 women and 16 men) at Van Yüzüncü Yıl University Dursun Odabaş Medical Centre, Türkiye. Serum and ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid whole-blood specimens were stored at room temperature (18–24 °C) or 4 °C. Twenty-seven biochemical and 26 complete blood count parameters were measured at a common baseline and after 4, 8 and 24 h. Time effects were assessed separately for each storage condition using Friedman tests, followed by Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Holm adjustment. Storage conditions were compared at each follow-up time using paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction was applied to multiple testing. Statistical analyses were performed using Python and the SciPy scientific computing library. Delayed analysis produced time-dependent changes in several biochemical and haematological parameters, with the magnitude of change varying according to storage condition. At 24 h at room temperature, haematocrit increased by 7.61%, mean corpuscular volume by 7.51% and red cell distribution width-standard deviation by 15.95%, whereas mean corpuscular haemoglobin concentration decreased by 7.11%. Corresponding changes in these erythrocyte-related indices were substantially smaller at 4 °C. Platelet indices changed under both conditions, with mean platelet volume increasing by 4.85% at room temperature and 6.85% at 4 °C, and platelet large cell ratio increasing by 17.34% and 23.72%, respectively. Among biochemical analytes, triglycerides increased by 14.75% at room temperature and 11.55% at 4 °C, while total iron-binding capacity increased by 11.15% and 8.86%, respectively. Delayed analysis and storage temperature were associated with measurable changes in several routine biochemical and haematological test results. Refrigerated storage generally reduced time-dependent changes in several haematological parameters compared with room-temperature storage, although changes were also observed at 4 °C. These findings highlight the importance of considering both storage temperature and analysis delay when handling specimens collected in primary care. The statistically significant changes observed should not be interpreted as formal analytical or clinical stability thresholds.

Article.Title: An agentic multi-drone framework for autonomous multi-accident detection, reasoning, and response
Article.Authors: Ahmed A.; Eesaar H.; Farhan M.; Yoo Y.; Lee D.
Article.Abstract: Rapid and effective response to highway accidents is critical for reducing response delays and improving situational awareness. In this study, we present an agentic multi-drone, end-to-end incident management framework, developed and validated in the Gazebo simulation environment, in which specialized planning, coordination, perception, scene-description, and dispatch agents communicate through ROS/MAVROS and MQTT interfaces. A simulated emergency call transcript is processed by a GPT-4o mini-based planning agent to extract incident coordinates and mission intent, which the coordination agent resolves into an optimal drone-to-incident allocation. Up to four autonomous drones, each managed via MAVROS and ArduPilot, navigate under GUIDED mode to their assigned sites, where a custom-trained YOLOv11n perception agent performs real-time accident and fire recognition on live aerial imagery. Detected events trigger a fine-tuned BLIP-2 description agent, which converts visual evidence into structured natural-language incident reports. When multiple reports correspond to the same incident, confidence-prioritized fusion selects the highest-confidence view as the primary description and supplements it with non-duplicated salient information from secondary views. A Piper TTS-based dispatch agent then converts these summaries into audio alerts and autonomously routes them to the nearest rescue center based on drone proximity. The description agent was fine-tuned on 1,783 image–caption pairs derived from the curated incident dataset, with reference captions generated using moondream2, holding its visual encoder and Q-Former frozen to preserve pre-trained feature representations, and evaluated on a held-out set of 254 samples using BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, METEOR, CIDEr, and SPICE. Results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed modular agentic architecture for autonomous multi-incident perception, reasoning, and coordinated drone-based emergency response in the evaluated four-drone, four-incident simulation configuration. The framework provides a basis for future validation in larger-scale and real-world emergency-response scenarios.

Article.Title: Exploration the influence of electron donor engineering on frequency-dependent nonlinear optical properties of anthraquinone-based chromophores: a DFT-ML approach
Article.Authors: Asghar M.; Sadiq H.; Khan M.; Sohail A.; Alhokbany N.; Ojha S.
Article.Abstract: Recently, non-linear optical materials (NLO) have gained significant attention due to their applications in photonics, optical communication, and signal processing. Herein, anthraquinone core-based chromophores (APCD1–APCD7) were designed via donor engineering for efficient nonlinear optical materials. Their structural and optoelectronic properties were calculated by density functional theory and time dependent density functional theory (DFT/TD-DFT) at M06/6-311G (d, p) level. The designed chromophores (APCD1–APCD7) showed red-shifted absorption spectrum (380.89–466.58 nm ) and reduced HOMO LUMO energy gap of 1.99 − 3.81 eV . The density of states (DOS), transition density matrix (TDM) and natural bond orbital (NBO) analyses revealed efficient charge redistribution. Moreover, the designed compounds exhibited enhanced NLO responses, with APCD1 showing the strongest second-order NLO response, including β(− 2ω;ω,ω) of 7.11 × 10⁻²⁷ esu , whereas APCD5 exhibited the most pronounced third-order NLO response, with γ DFWM of 3.10 × 10⁻³¹ esu and n₂ of 5.01 × 10⁻¹⁴ cm²/W at 532 nm . Machine learning analysis established the structure–property relationship of the energy gap, identifying PEOE VSA 11, EState VSA 10, and BCUT2D VSA 11 as the most influential descriptors. Synthetic accessibility analysis indicates the practical feasibility of the designed chromophores, highlighting their potential for advanced photonic and optoelectronic applications.

Article.Title: Potential involvement of S100A8/S100A9 and neutrophil extracellular traps in rheumatic heart disease valvular injury
Article.Authors: Wen J.; Wang L.; Wu G.; Huang Y.; Zeng Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Rheumatic heart disease (RHD) causes immune-mediated valvular inflammation and fibrosis, but the contribution of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) remains unclear. We integrated mitral valve transcriptomics with histological, molecular and echocardiographic assessments in a rat RHD model. Transcriptomic analysis included four rats per group; each subsequent experiment included three rats per group. RHD valves showed inflammatory infiltration, collagen remodeling and increased S100A8/S100A9 expression, alongside enhanced myeloperoxidase (MPO) and citrullinated histone H3 (citH3) staining. S100A8/A9 and MPO showed partial local colocalization, whereas the measured echocardiographic parameters did not differ significantly between groups at the terminal assessment. Exploratory screening using nominal P < 0.05 and |log₂ fold change| > 1 identified 89 genes, nine of which overlapped a NET-related gene set. These included S100A8 and S100A9, with nominal P values of 0.009565 and 0.002586 and Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted P values of 0.419214 and 0.297275, respectively. The combined findings support a possible contribution of S100A8/S100A9-associated NET responses to valvular inflammation and remodeling. However, the exploratory transcriptomic evidence, small experimental groups and absence of functional perturbation leave the proposed causal pathway in RHD unconfirmed.

Article.Title: An integrated organic geochemical assessment and oil-source rock correlation of the cretaceous chichali formation, Kohat Basin, Pakistan
Article.Authors: Siyar S.; Gharib A.; Ali F.; Ahmad J.; Jahandad S.; Kontakiotis G.; Besiou E.; Antonarakou A.
Article.Abstract: The Cretaceous Chichali Formation in the Chanda-01, Chanda-02, Chanda-03 and Mela-05 wells, along with crude oil from Chanda-01 and Chanda-02 wells located in the Kohat Basin, Pakistan, was investigated to evaluate organic content, depositional environment, thermal maturity, hydrocarbon generation potential, and oil-source correlation using Rock-Eval pyrolysis, organic petrography, gas chromatography (GC), and GC–MS biomarker analyses. Organic matter content in the Chichali Formation is generally low, with the average total organic carbon (TOC) content of 0.54 wt% for the Chanda-02 well, 0.66 wt% for the Chanda-03 well and 0.96 wt% for the Mela-05 well, corresponding to poor to fair quality of source rock in Chanda wells and fair to good quality in the Mela-05 well. Rock-Eval data (Tmax = 432–447 °C for samples considered reliable), hydrogen index values of 42–117 mg HC/g TOC and vitrinite reflectance values of 0.97–1.10% Ro indicate that the organic matter is dominated by Type III kerogen and has reached the main oil window. The non-biomarker and biomarker parameters used for oil–source rock correlation and thermal maturity include the carbon preference index (CPI), pristane/phytane (Pr/Ph), pristane/n-C17 (Pr/n-C17), phytane/n-C18 (Ph/n-C18), the terrigenous-to-aquatic ratio (TAR), C29 sterane 20 S/(20 S+20R), C29 ββ/(ββ + αα), moretane/C30 hopane (M29/H30), Ts/(Ts + Tm), and C31 homohopane 22 S/(22 S+22R), as well as sterane distributions and methylphenanthrene index (MPI). The Chichali Formation is characterized by low TAR values (0.025–0.08), CPI values of 0.9, Pr/Ph ratios of 0.40–0.61, C29 sterane 20 S/(20 S+20R) values of 0.50–0.52, ββ/(ββ + αα) values of 0.50–0.53, Ts/(Ts + Tm) values of 0.43–0.45, and MPI values of 0.78–0.92, whereas the oils exhibit higher Pr/Ph ratios (1.07–1.78), higher TAR values (0.17–0.71), ββ/(ββ + αα) values of approximately 0.50–0.56, Ts/(Ts + Tm) values of 0.48–0.55, and MPI values of 0.92–0.95, indicating slightly greater thermal maturity and a stronger terrestrial organic matter contribution. The integrated biomarker and non-biomarker evidence demonstrates that the investigated oils are not genetically related to the analyzed Chichali Formation. Rather, the oils were probably formed from a more terrestrial-rich source rock located elsewhere in the regional petroleum system.

Article.Title: CSwinFK: a bidirectional cross-attention CNN-Swin Transformer fusion model for fungal keratitis classification in in vivo confocal microscopy images
Article.Authors: Hu M.; Liang L.; Chen L.; He W.; Lan Q.; Jiang L.; Huang H.; Wei X.; Liu D.; Cai J.; Tong H.; Li K.; Chen Q.; Siu S.
Article.Abstract: Fungal keratitis is a corneal infection caused by filamentous fungi or yeasts. It can progress rapidly and, if not diagnosed and treated promptly, may lead to irreversible visual impairment or blindness. In this study, we developed CSwinFK, a classification model for distinguishing fungal keratitis from negative cases using in vivo confocal microscopy images. This model is based on a novel bidirectional cross-attention fusion of the CNN architecture and Swin Transformer. Through deep interactions between the two branches, the model aims to achieve high sensitivity to local structural details while effectively capturing long-range global dependencies in the image. Experiments were conducted on a curated set of 3,612 clinical IVCM images from the fungal keratitis and negative groups using a subject-level data split. The model achieved a test accuracy of 97.23%, with a sensitivity of 97.05% and a specificity of 97.42%. Comparative experiments with representative architectures and existing deep learning models showed that CSwinFK achieved favorable classification performance. Grad-CAM analysis further showed that the model focused on regions exhibiting patterns consistent with fungal hyphae in IVCM images.

Article.Title: Effects of growth media modulation on cytotoxicity, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities of postbiotic metabolites produced by Lactiplantibacillus plantarum I-UL4
Article.Authors: Rehman A.; Cho M.; Song A.; Saad N.; Chia S.; Loh T.; Wu R.; Foo H.
Article.Abstract: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum I-UL4 produces various postbiotic metabolites with known anticancer and antioxidant activities, but its anti-inflammatory effect remains unclear. In this study, we compared postbiotic metabolites produced by L. plantarum I-UL4 with commercial de Man, Rogosa and Sharpe (MRS) medium (PMM) and a reported refined formulation (PMF) for their volatile compound profiles, cytotoxicity, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects on LPS-stimulated THP-1 leukaemia cells. Volatile compound profiling was performed by GC–MS and cytotoxicity was determined by 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium Bromide assay. Subsequently, antioxidant effects were determined for cellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels (DCFDA assay) and inflammatory responses at the gene (nuclear factor kappa B, cyclooxygenase-2, IL-6, IL-18, TNF-α, IL-1β and IL-10) and protein levels via qPCR and cytokine antibody arrays. GC–MS analysis revealed that L. plantarum I-UL4 produced distinct volatile compound profiles from MRS and refined formulation media. Nonetheless, lactic acid predominating (≈ 89–92% peak area), alongside other unique bioactive compounds in PMM and PMF, as compared to MRS and the refined formulation media. Notably, PMM was more cytotoxic, with the lowest IC 50 (2.57 ± 0.2) at 72 h. Interestingly, both PMF and PMM reduced ROS levels at 48 h. Importantly, PMF showed significantly stronger ( P < 0.05) anti-inflammatory effects by inhibiting nuclear factor kappa B and cyclooxygenase-2 and simultaneously modulating both pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokine genes and protein expression compared with PMM, suggesting that PMF could be a promising biotic preparation for modulating inflammation-related diseases. In conclusion, this study reveals how fermentation media affect the volatile composition, bioactivity and functionality of postbiotic metabolites, including cytotoxicity, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities.

Article.Title: Family accommodation is associated with childhood social anxiety disorder and anxiety symptom severity
Article.Authors: Vietmeier N.; Phan D.; Fassot E.; Hauffe V.; Rauschenbach A.; Schmitz J.; Tuschen-Caffier B.; Asbrand J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Parenting processes are thought to shape children’s emotional development and may be particularly relevant once childhood social anxiety disorder (SAD) is clinically established. This study examined two distinct parenting processes—family accommodation (FA), a symptom-linked response to child anxiety, and challenging parenting behavior (CPB), a broader autonomy-promoting parenting dimension. Cross-sectional questionnaire and diagnostic interview data were drawn from three clinically characterized samples comprising youth with SAD ( n = 121), specific phobia ( n = 65), and healthy controls ( n = 147; total N = 333). Parents reported on FA and CPB using validated measures. Parents of youth with SAD reported greater FA than parents of healthy children, whereas CPB did not differ between groups. Higher FA was consistently associated with greater child SAD/anxiety severity, whereas CPB was unrelated to symptom severity. In two-parent families, FA and CPB showed little evidence of cross-parent coupling. Exploratory comparisons did not indicate that either parenting process differentiated SAD from other anxiety disorders. Overall, among the two parenting processes examined, symptom-linked accommodation showed the more consistent pattern of association with clinically established childhood SAD and anxiety severity, supporting its relevance for parent-focused assessment while leaving causal direction and broader diagnostic specificity beyond anxiety disorders unresolved.

Article.Title: Accuracy and clinical performance of conventional versus digital impressions for maxillary complete dentures: a randomized controlled clinical trial
Article.Authors: Habash M.; Almustafa A.; Alzoubi H.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to compare the three-dimensional trueness of digital impressions with conventional impressions for maxillary complete dentures and to evaluate the clinical performance of denture bases fabricated from each technique. Twenty completely edentulous participants received both conventional impressions and digital impressions using an intraoral scanner in a randomized crossover design. Conventional impressions were digitized and used as reference models. Trueness was assessed by root mean square (RMS) deviations for the entire surface and predefined anatomical regions. Denture bases were fabricated using stereolithographic 3D printing. Retention, stability, and support were clinically evaluated by blinded examiners. Statistical analyses included parametric and nonparametric tests (α = 0.05) with effect size estimation. Mean RMS deviation for the entire digital impression was 234.63 ± 43.87 μm and was significantly below the 300-µm reference threshold (Cohen’s d = − 1.49, representing the standardized difference from this threshold). The palatal vault (d = − 3.03) and ridge crest (d = − 2.88) showed the largest standardized differences below the 300-µm threshold, whereas the peripheral border (d = 1.47) and posterior palatal seal (d = 0.85) showed standardized differences above the threshold ( P ≤ 0.001). Conventional denture bases showed significantly higher posterior retention, lateral and anteroposterior stability, and anteroposterior support ( r = 0.60–0.77; P ≤ 0.007). No significant differences were observed for anterior retention or lateral support. Digital impressions demonstrated region-dependent trueness relative to conventional reference impressions, with lower deviations in the palatal vault and ridge crest regions and greater deviations in peripheral and posterior sealing regions. However, conventional impressions provided superior clinical performance for several retention, stability, and support parameters.

Article.Title: A cascaded probabilistic framework for stealth-aware MITRE ATT&CK path prediction in active directory adversary emulation
Article.Authors: Youssef M.; Badr N.; Abo-alian A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Proactive adversary emulation requires anticipating multi-step attack trajectories, yet existing approaches rely on static attack graphs or single-signal models that cannot jointly satisfy coherence, tactical realism, and evasiveness. We propose a cascaded probabilistic framework for MITRE ATT&CK technique-path prediction in Active Directory environments, where exhaustive enumeration is intractable. Its contribution is a three-stage architecture that decouples these objectives instead of blending them. Stage 1, a two-layer unidirectional LSTM trained on observed threat-actor chains, emits a five-candidate pool rather than one technique. Stage 2, an empirical Markov tactic-transition gate, admits only attested transitions, including self-loops and backward moves a strict linear kill chain excludes. Stage 3 re-ranks survivors against a detection-rule corpus, favoring evasive over merely probable techniques. Candidates are masked at inference to Windows-applicable techniques, so outputs are technique chains, not instantiated paths. Under a prefix-disjoint protocol in which no evaluation context occurs in training, the true continuation is retained in the five-candidate pool more often than by a first-order predictor or an exact prefix-lookup table on identical pairs. Because Stage 3 both selects on and is scored by detection-rule density, the chains are re-scored against independently maintained corpora the selector never accesses; the exposure reduction persists there, and it is that transferred result that carries the evasiveness claim. Novel here is that structural admissibility is a hard constraint rather than a soft weight, so tactical realism cannot be traded away for likelihood or stealth. A case study initiated from a single initial-access technique further indicates that all tactic transitions within the returned path portfolio have attested support in the corpus transition matrix, and that no predicted step violates the ATT&CK-declared phase set of its technique.

Article.Title: Association of self perceived clinical decision making with perceived importance of caring behaviors among ICU nurses in the West Bank
Article.Authors: Ayed A.; Eqtait F.; Anabtawi R.; Daibes M.; Hammad B.; Ejheisheh M.; Fashafsheh I.; Farajallah M.; Batran A.
Article.Abstract: To examine the association between self-perceived clinical decision-making (CDM) and the perceived importance of caring behaviors among intensive care unit (ICU) nurses in the West Bank, Palestine. ICU nurses make rapid, high-stakes decisions while providing technically complex and person-centered care. How CDM relates to perceived importance of caring behaviors in resource-constrained ICU settings in the West Bank, Palestine, remains insufficiently understood. A convenience sample of 244 ICU nurses from ten public hospitals completed the Clinical Decision-Making in Nursing Scale (CDMNS) and the Caring Behaviors Assessment Tool-Nursing Version-Short Form (CBAN-SF). Internal consistency was acceptable in the current sample (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.88 for CDMNS and 0.90 for CBAN-SF). Hospital-level clustering was not modeled in the regression analysis; adjusted estimates were therefore interpreted as exploratory. The mean CDMNS total score was 142.5 (SD = 16.1). Among the four CDM domains, canvassing of objectives and values had the highest mean score (M = 38.4, SD = 4.7), and search for and unbiased assimilation of new information had the lowest (M = 33.5, SD = 6.9). The mean CBAN-SF perceived-importance score was 105.8 (SD = 14.2). CBAN-SF domain item means ranged from 3.8 to 4.0; humanism/faith-hope/sensitivity and expression of positive/negative feelings had the highest item means, whereas helping/trust and teaching/learning had the lowest. Higher self-perceived CDM scores, membership in the master’s-degree-or-higher group compared with the combined diploma/bachelor’s group, and longer ICU experience were associated with higher CBAN-SF perceived-importance scores. Because the study was cross-sectional and the outcome measured perceived importance rather than observed or enacted behavior, the findings indicate statistical association rather than causal or behavioral effects. Future multicenter research should account for hospital-level clustering, use theory-informed covariate selection, and incorporate observed, patient-reported, or other performance-based measures of caring.

Article.Title: Ultrasound stimulation of hindlimb skeletal muscle is associated with selective differences in splenic metabolites during hindlimb unloading in mice
Article.Authors: Inoue T.; Nishimura N.; Dachs M.; Kawamoto Y.; Yamaguchi A.; Ma X.; Xing J.; Uemura M.; Matsuda M.; Hasunuma T.; Fujino H.; Maeshige N.
Article.Abstract: Physical inactivity and unloading induce skeletal muscle atrophy and systemic metabolic and immune dysregulation. HU and HUUS had lower body weight, gastrocnemius weight, spleen weight, and muscle fiber cross-sectional area than control. Exploratory analysis showed numerically higher particle concentrations in polymer-precipitated plasma EP-containing fractions in HUUS than in HU, although the difference was not statistically significant ( p = 0.050). In gastrocnemius muscle, gene sets for endoplasmic reticulum protein processing and proteostasis were positively enriched in HUUS versus HU. In the spleen, HU showed nominally higher upstream glycolytic intermediates and nominally lower flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD), whereas erythrose 4-phosphate (E4P) and GDP were lower and cis-aconitate was higher after FDR correction. Compared with HU, HUUS showed lower glucose 1-phosphate (G1P) after FDR correction and nominal differences in F6P, fumarate, and FAD. Overall, US stimulation under HU conditions was associated with pathway-level transcriptional remodeling and selective splenic metabolite differences.

Article.Title: ActiNet: an open-source tool for activity intensity classification of wrist-worn accelerometry using self-supervised deep learning
Article.Authors: Acquah A.; Chan S.; Doherty A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The use of accurate and reliable open-source human activity recognition (HAR) models on passively collected wrist-accelerometer data is essential in large-scale epidemiological studies that investigate the association between physical activity and health outcomes. While self-supervised learning has generated considerable excitement in improving HAR, the extent to which these models, coupled with hidden Markov models (HMMs), would make a tangible improvement to classification performance and the effect this may have on the predicted daily activity intensity compositions is unknown. Using up to 24 h of wrist-worn accelerometer data from 151 CAPTURE-24 participants (aged 18–91, mean age 42, 66% female), we trained the ActiNet model, consisting of HARNet, a self-supervised, 18-layer, modified ResNet-V2 model, followed by hidden Markov model (HMM) smoothing, to classify labels of activity intensity. The performance of this model, evaluated using fivefold stratified group cross-validation, was then compared to a baseline random forest (RF) + HMM, established in existing literature. Differences in performance and classification outputs were compared with different subgroups of age and sex within the CAPTURE-24 population. The ActiNet model was able to distinguish labels of activity intensity with a mean macro F1 score of 0.82 and a mean Cohen’s kappa score of 0.86. This exceeded the performance of the RF + HMM, trained and validated on the same dataset, with mean scores of 0.76 and 0.80, respectively. The improvements in performance were consistent across subgroups of age and sex. These findings encourage the use of ActiNet for the extraction of activity intensity labels from wrist-accelerometer data in future epidemiological studies.

Article.Title: Machine learning-based association analysis and cross-sectional classification of physical exercise behaviors and mental health among vocational medical students
Article.Authors: Tian S.; Meng S.
Article.Abstract: Psychological distress is common among vocational medical students, yet how multidimensional exercise behavior relates to their mental health remains coarsely described. This cross-sectional study surveyed 1,127 students at three vocational medical colleges in China between September and November 2024, applying machine learning to two analytically separate tasks: describing association patterns between exercise profiles and psychological status, and classifying concurrent psychological risk. Random forest ranking, Apriori rule mining and K-Means profiling agreed on three points: weekly frequency carried the most information among behavioral variables; frequent moderate-intensity aerobic activity co-occurred most often with low anxiety and depression; and four partially overlapping profiles emerged. XGBoost classified best on an internal hold-out test set of 226 students, one fifth of the full sample (accuracy 0.889, 95% CI 0.842 to 0.924; macro-averaged AUC 0.943), yet reached only 0.769 sensitivity for severe distress, and accuracy fell to 0.858 under leave-one-college-out validation. Because the design is cross-sectional and validation internal, these findings describe associations rather than supply a screening tool.

Article.Title: Genetic profile of P. falciparum strains in villages around Soum irrigation Dam, Burkina Faso: insights from targeted sequencing of drug resistance markers in Pfkelch13, Pfubp1, Pfcoronin, Pfcrt, Pfmdr1, Pfdhps and Pfdhfr genes
Article.Authors: Ouare N.; Sorgho H.; Rouamba T.; Natama H.; Some G.; Wellmann L.; Stauning M.; Ilboudo H.; Kaboré B.; Derra K.; Tahita M.; Magnussen P.; Zida A.; Alifrangis M.; Tinto H.; Hansson H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hydro-agricultural settings may sustain high and prolonged malaria transmission and increase antimalarial drug use, potentially intensifying selection pressure on P. falciparum strains. Molecular surveillance in these settings is essential to detect changes in markers associated with resistance to artemisinin, Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine (SP), and Artemisinin-Based Combination Therapy (ACT) partner drugs. This study characterized the genetic profile and seasonal distribution of P. falciparum strains circulating in villages surrounding the Soum irrigation dam in Burkina Faso. A prospective monitoring approach was implemented through monthly repeated cross-sectional household surveys in five villages around the Soum dam in the Nanoro health district from March 2022 to February 2023. Dried blood spots from microscopy-positive samples were randomly selected by village and transmission season. Illumina technology was used to sequence molecular markers of partial resistance to artemisinin ( Pfkelch13 , Pfcoronin , Pfubp1 ), Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine ( Pfdhfr , Pfdhps ), and Artemisinin-Based Combination therapy (ACT) partner drugs ( Pfmdr1 , Pfcrt ). Allele and haplotype prevalences were compared across villages, transmission seasons, and age groups using chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests, as appropriate. A total of 712 P. falciparum -positive samples were selected for the sample size for molecular analysis. No validated or candidate mutations associated with artemisinin partial resistance were detected in Pfkelch13 and Pfcoronin. Pfubp1 D1525E and E1528D mutations, suspected to be associated with delayed parasite clearance, were each detected at 18.5% and 19.1%, respectively. Mutant alleles of Pfdhfr , including 51 I (73.7%), 59 R (88.6%) and 108 N (91.4%), were highly prevalent. In Pfdhps , the mutant 437 G allele was highly detected (88.4%), whereas 431 V , 540 E and 581 G occurred at low frequencies (< 2%). No significant variation was found between villages and transmission season for Pfdhfr and Pfdhps ( p > 0.05). The wildtype 86 N allele of Pfmdr1 was predominant (95.2%), while mutant allele 184 F (49.31%) was higher and differed significantly between villages ( p = 0.029) with the highest frequency in Séguédin (57.4%) and the lowest in Soala (40.5%). The Pfcrt wildtype CVMNK haplotype (97.4%) remained dominant. This study found no validated Pfkelch13 mutation and no candidate Pfcoronin mutation associated with artemisinin partial resistance. However, the emergence of D1525E and E1528D mutations of Pfubp1 may suggest early signals adaptation of P. falciparum to artemisinin in the study area. The relatively high and expected frequency of Pfdhfr and Pfdhps without significant variations between villages and transmission period suggests homogeneous circulation of these mutations across the study area and reflects continued pressure of SP. The emerging Pfdhps 431 V and 540 E and high frequency of Pfmdr1 184 F allele reinforced the need for regular surveillance to anticipate any resistance of SP and Lumefantrine.

Article.Title: Body appreciation and regulatory emotional self efficacy in the association between physical exercise and social anxiety among Chinese college students
Article.Authors: Zhang X.; Han Y.; Li H.; Li Y.; Li L.; Gao W.
Article.Abstract: Social anxiety is a salient psychological concern among college students and is closely related to interpersonal adjustment and emotional well-being. This cross-sectional study examined the association between physical exercise and social anxiety among Chinese college students, focusing on the statistical indirect roles of body appreciation and regulatory emotional self-efficacy. A total of 1,869 students mainly from Henan Province, China, completed self-report measures of physical exercise, body appreciation, regulatory emotional self-efficacy, and social anxiety. Pearson correlation analysis and PROCESS Model 6 with 5,000 bootstrap samples were used to examine direct and indirect associations. Physical exercise was negatively associated with social anxiety and positively associated with body appreciation and regulatory emotional self-efficacy. Body appreciation and regulatory emotional self-efficacy were separately involved in significant indirect associations between physical exercise and social anxiety. A sequential statistical indirect association involving body appreciation and regulatory emotional self-efficacy was also observed. These findings suggest that positive body image and emotion-regulation beliefs are relevant psychological resources in the association between physical exercise and social anxiety. Given the cross-sectional design, the findings should be interpreted as statistical associations rather than evidence of temporal or causal ordering.

Article.Title: A functionally divergent paralog of the tRNA splicing ligase required for cell division but not tRNA maturation in Trypanosoma brucei
Article.Authors: Casius A.; Kumar B.; d’Almeida G.; de Graffenried C.; Paris Z.; Alfonzo J.
Article.Abstract: In eukaryotes a varying number of tRNAs undergo splicing, rendering them functional for protein synthesis; tRNA splicing is thus essential. Trypanosoma brucei ( T. brucei ) has a single intron-containing, tRNA Tyr , still requiring a fully functional splicing machinery. Splicing involves intron cleavage by the splicing-specific tRNA endonuclease complex, followed by exon ligation, which in some eukaryotes (including T. brucei ) is performed by the multi-domain enzyme tRNA Ligase (TRL1). Using phylogenetic comparative analysis, we and others showed the existence of a paralog of TbTRL1, which lacks the conserved ligase residues but maintains apparently intact kinase and phosphodiesterase domains. Here, we demonstrate that down regulation of the paralogous protein (we termed TbKCPD) by RNAi causes a growth defect, which cannot be rescued by providing a spliced version of tRNA Tyr . We also tested the functionality of the kinase and phosphodiesterase domains by genetic rescue with a recoded copy of the gene impervious to RNAi. We show that both domains are essential for viability. Global proteomics comparing RNAi induced to control cells unexpectedly revealed effects on proteins primarily involved in flagellar biogenesis and in line with this observation, we also show that TbKCPD leads to defects in cell division; an essential function that goes beyond splicing.

Article.Title: Reliability and validity of the Chinese version of the spouse response inventory in individuals with chronic pain
Article.Authors: Jia H.; Xia L.; Tao R.; Jiang E.; Wang Y.; Yang G.
Article.Abstract: Chronic pain is a significant global health challenge. Spousal responses to pain behaviors substantially influence patients’ pain perception and psychological adjustment. Therefore, the Spouse Response Inventory (SRI) was developed based on the operant behavioral framework to assess the spouse responses of individuals with chronic pain. To assess this construct in Chinese populations, we translated and culturally adapted the scale into Chinese. In our study, the SRI was translated and culturally adapted using Brislin’s model. A pilot test was first conducted, followed by a formal investigation from December 2025 to January 2026. A total of 517 chronic pain patients from a tertiary hospital in Henan, China, were recruited via convenience sampling. To evaluate the validity and reliability of the Chinese SRI, several statistical methods were employed: content validity was assessed using the Content Validity Index (CVI); construct validity was examined through confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), with model fit evaluated using the root mean square error of approximation (RMSEA) and comparative fit index (CFI); convergent validity was assessed using composite reliability (CR) and average variance extracted (AVE); Cronbach’s α measured internal consistency; and item analysis was performed using the critical ratio (CR) method and item-total correlation. The Chinese SRI consists of 33 items across four subscales. The item-level CVI ranged from 0.875 to 1, and the scale-level CVI was 0.97. CFA showed standardized factor loadings from 0.586 to 0.882 (all P < 0.001). CR ranged from 0.866 to 0.941, and AVE from 0.472 to 0.644. The four-factor model fit was acceptable (RMSEA = 0.064, CFI = 0.894). Item-total correlations ranged from 0.278 to 0.685. Cronbach’s α for the total scale was 0.934, and for subscales, 0.862–0.941. The Chinese SRI may be considered a suitable tool for assessing spousal responses in individuals with Chronic Pain in China.

Article.Title: Obesity partly explains the effect of socioeconomic position on multiple long-term conditions in UK Biobank
Article.Authors: Steell L.; Pereira S.; Hillman S.; Witham M.; Sayer A.; Cooper R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The mechanisms through which lower socioeconomic position (SEP) leads to increased risk of multiple long-term conditions (MLTC) are poorly understood. Using data from UK Biobank (n = 194,038), we applied four-way decomposition to investigate the mediating and moderating roles of overall (body mass index [BMI] > 30 kg/m 2 ) and central (waist-to-hip ratio > 0.85 [females]/ > 0.9 [males]) obesity in the association between SEP (indicated by educational attainment) and incident MLTC. Incident MLTC was defined as the diagnosis of two LTC of interest from linked healthcare data. Over five-years follow up, 11,071 participants developed MLTC. Socioeconomic inequalities in MLTC were observed and partly mediated by overall and central obesity. For example, compared with degree educated participants, those with no qualifications had an approximately 71% (95%CI 59%, 77%) higher rate of MLTC. The proportion mediated by overall obesity was 8% (6%, 11%) and central obesity was 13% (10%, 16%). Approximately one fifth of this total effect was attributable to interaction between SEP and central obesity. A hypothetical intervention eradicating central obesity could eliminate around one third of socioeconomic inequalities in incident MLTC. Obesity partly mediated the association between SEP and incident MLTC and targeting different indices of obesity could reduce socioeconomic inequalities in MLTC.

Article.Title: A meteorological big data-driven method for generating chaotic time-series curves of power supply loads for wind-solar-storage hybrid systems
Article.Authors: Qiu J.; Ren Z.; Fan Q.; Feng Z.; Zhang C.
Article.Abstract: The wind-solar-storage hybrid system represents an efficient and clean energy supply mode. However, its power supply load is influenced by multiple factors and exhibits complex chaotic time-series characteristics, which pose significant challenges to system operation scheduling and load forecasting. To address this issue, this paper proposes a method for generating chaotic time-series curves of the power supply load in such hybrid systems based on meteorological big data. Specifically, the empirical mode decomposition (EMD) technique is employed to decompose the load sequence into intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) with distinct scale characteristics, while the collected meteorological big data are subjected to dimensionality reduction. Subsequently, the chaotic time-series phase-space reconstruction method is applied to reconstruct in real time the various IMF components and the reduced meteorological data, thereby revealing the correlations between each meteorological factor and each IMF component. On the basis of these correlations, the chaotic time-series curve of the power supply load is generated using a method grounded in the maximum Lyapunov exponent. Experimental results show that the proposed approach exhibits strong capability in decomposing the load sequence and reducing meteorological data dimensionality. Moreover, it can effectively generate chaotic time-series curves of the power supply load for the hybrid system under cloudy weather conditions, driven by big data, achieving favorable application outcomes.

Article.Title: Semi-analytical investigation of fin configuration effects on PCM solidification in cylindrical thermal energy storage systems
Article.Authors: Kumar A.; Abdullah M.; Venkadeshwaran K.; Purohit B.; Thatoi D.; Singh R.; Bisht Y.
Article.Abstract: Thermal energy storage systems (TES) employing phase change materials (PCMs) are often constrained by the inherently low thermal conductivity of PCMs, resulting in slow heat transfer and prolonged charging and discharging processes. This study investigates the influence of fin configuration and fin number on the solidification behavior of PCMs in TES systems using a semi-analytical model based on Green’s function and the Megerlin method. The proposed framework predicts the evolution of the solidification front under different thermal boundary conditions while providing a computationally efficient alternative to conventional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations. The thermal performances of radial and longitudinal fin configurations are systematically compared to identify the most effective design for accelerating solidification. The results demonstrate that fin geometry has a greater influence on heat transfer enhancement than simply increasing the fin surface area. Among the investigated configurations, the two-radial-fin arrangement reduces the total solidification time by 21.38% compared with the unfinned tank and achieves an additional 12.37% reduction relative to the longitudinal-fin configuration. Moreover, the predicted solidification contours show that radial fins promote more effective heat extraction and suppress the formation of large unsolidified liquid regions. The proposed semi-analytical framework provides an accurate and computationally efficient tool for analyzing PCM solidification and offers practical design guidelines for optimizing fin configurations in high-performance LHTES systems.

Article.Title: Assessment of environmental and radiological risks in mining-affected areas of Minna, Niger State, Nigeria
Article.Authors: Kwaghhua F.; Adetona A.; Olarinoye I.; Ejepu J.; Adewumi T.
Article.Abstract: Mining is a human activity that perturbs radionuclide distribution in the natural environment. Minna area of Nigeria is rich in gold deposit and mining activity is active in the area. In this study, radiological impact of mining on human and non-human biota was assessed using airborne gamma ray spectrometric data of study area. The elemental concentration of naturally occurring radioactive materials (NORMs) in (%) for potassium, (ppm) for equivalent thorium and uranium were converted to activity concentrations in (Bq Kg −1 ). The activity concentrations were used to evaluate the human risk factors and estimate dose on non-human biota. Estimated absorbed dose rate \((\text{A}\text{D}\text{R})\) range from 20.78 to 86.62 \({\text{n}\text{G}\text{y} \text{h}}^{-1}\) with an average value of 43.00 ± 14.9 \({\text{n}\text{G}\text{y} \text{h}}^{-1}\) , annual effective dose equivalent for indoors and outdoors \({(\text{A}\text{E}\text{D}\text{E}}_{\text{i}\text{n}},{\text{A}\text{E}\text{D}\text{E}}_{\text{o}\text{u}\text{t}})\) were estimated ranging from 0.102 to 0.425 \({\text{m}\text{S}\text{v} \text{y}}^{-1}\) and 0.025–0.106 \({\text{m}\text{S}\text{v} \text{y}}^{-1}\) respectively. Annual gonadal dose equivalent \((\text{A}\text{G}\text{D}\text{E})\) and excess lifetime cancer risk \((\text{E}\text{L}\text{C}\text{R})\) were estimated ranging from 145.24 to 612.66 \({\upmu \text{S}\text{v} \text{y}}^{-1}\) and (0.36–1.48) × 10 −3 respectively. The peak values of estimated radiological hazards indicators exceeded the world average value of 59.00 \({\text{n}\text{G}\text{y} \text{h}}^{-1}\) , (0.41, 0.07) \({\text{m}\text{S}\text{v} \text{y}}^{-1}\) , 300 \({\upmu \text{S}\text{v} \text{y}}^{-1}\) and \({0.29\times 10}^{-3}\) for ADR, \({(\text{A}\text{E}\text{D}\text{E}}_{\text{i}\text{n}},{\text{A}\text{E}\text{D}\text{E}}_{\text{o}\text{u}\text{t}})\) , \(\text{A}\text{G}\text{D}\text{E}\) and \(\text{E}\text{L}\text{C}\text{R}\) respectively. The results imply averagely low radiological risk for human populace; however, a potential risk is anticipated for areas of peak occurrence of estimated parameters. Risk quotients below the hazard threshold value of 1.0 were estimated in the assessment of radiation dose impact on non-human biota, indicating low risk. The radiological parameters mapped with elevated values were within Nabi, Nadna, Buslimi, Shiroro, Barga, Guni, Dandawa and Fuka. This study showcases a baseline of moderate radiological impact in the study area. Periodic monitoring is advised as mining activities are predicted to intensify.

Article.Title: Cellular and tissue compatibility of quaternary ammonium silane for endodontic applications
Article.Authors: Bapat R.; Pang J.; Ilyas M.; Parveen T.; Raja H.; Banavar S.; Pichika M.; Mak K.; Khoo S.; Seow L.; Bijle M.; Blum I.; Daood U.
Article.Abstract: Quaternary ammonium silane (K21) is an innovative antibacterial agent with prospective endodontic applications. This study assessed the cytocompatibility of K21 in comparison to sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) and chlorhexidine (CHX). Murine macrophages (RAW 264.7) and human periodontal ligament stem cells (hPDLSCs) were subjected to saline (S ct ), 2% chlorhexidine (CHX), 6% sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl), 0.5% K21, and 1% K21. Cell viability was evaluated using MTT and Alamar Blue assays at 1 min, 5 min, 15 min, 30 min, 1 h, and 4 h. Mitochondrial staining intensity was assessed with MitoTracker Green (MTG) fluorescence as a surrogate marker of mitochondrial mass integrity. Cellular structures were analysed utilising scanning and transmission electron microscopy (SEM/TEM). Relative gene expression (IL-1β, TNF-α, TGF-β, VEGF-α) was measured by real-time PCR after macrophage polarisation. Biocompatibility was additionally assessed using a rat subcutaneous implantation model, with histological analysis performed at 2 h, 2 days, and 2 weeks. K21 exhibited significantly improved cell viability compared with 6% NaOCl, and a comparable or modestly improved viability profile compared with 2% CHX, in both macrophages and hPDLSCs across the time intervals tested (p < 0.05). Mitochondrial imaging revealed better preserved MTG staining intensity in K21-treated cells compared to NaOCl and CHX groups. SEM and TEM showed largely maintained cellular features with K21; these were the morphological observations and do not by themselves confirm cellular function. Gene expression analysis demonstrated lower fold-induction of pro-inflammatory markers (IL-1β, TNF-α) and higher fold-induction of angiogenic mediators (TGF-β, VEGF-A) relative to 6%NaOCl and 2%CHX. I n vivo , K21 elicited only mild, temporary inflammatory reactions, with swift tissue normalisation in contrast to the moderate to severe inflammation associated with NaOCl. Within the limitations of this preclinical cytocompatibility evaluation, 0.5% and 1% K21 demonstrated favourable cytocompatibility relative to 6% NaOCl and comparable or slightly better performance than 2% CHX; however these findings do not establish clinical efficacy or applicability, which would require dedicated orthotopic and clinical investigation.

Article.Title: Resistance training prevents the development of sarcopenia induced by chronic cholestatic liver disease
Article.Authors: Cabello-Verrugio C.; Valero-Breton M.; Tacchi F.; Portal-Rodriguez M.; Cifuentes-Silva E.; Salgado-Valdovinos J.; Martínez-Pérez M.; Elorza A.; Matamoros A.; Feijoo C.; Soto J.; Castro-Sepúlveda M.; Simon F.
Article.Abstract: Sarcopenia secondary to chronic cholestatic liver disease (CCLD) is linked to activation of the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) and autophagy-lysosome system (ALS), impaired mitochondrial dynamics, and diminished mTOR signaling. This study investigated the effects of RT in a mouse model of CCLD-induced sarcopenia. Male C57BL/6J mice developed CCLD-induced sarcopenia via a six-week diet containing the hepatotoxin 3,5-diethoxycarbonyl-1,4-dihydrocollidine while performing RT. RT markedly enhanced muscle strength, mass, and performance in CCLD mice. It maintained muscle fiber diameter and CSA, prevented loss of sarcomere proteins, and improved ultrastructure. RT preserved mitochondrial density, dynamics (DRP-1, mitofusin-2, OPA-1), PGC-1α levels, and oxygen consumption, normalized MuRF-1 and atrogin-1 expression, prevented transcriptional and protein induction of autophagy markers (LC3B, p62), and restored mTOR phosphorylation. These results demonstrate that RT prevents CCLD-related sarcopenia by inhibiting proteolytic systems and reactivating anabolic and mitochondrial pathways, offering a promising non-drug approach to protect skeletal muscle in this condition.

Article.Title: Effect of the C = C double bond in biodiesel compounds on copper corrosion
Article.Authors: Orea D.; Velazquez M.; Larios A.; Morelos J.; Arteaga A.; Sesenes R.; Rodriguez J.; Calderon J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Biodiesel is a mixture of fatty acid methyl esters in which the chemical structure, hydrocarbon chain length, saturation or unsaturation, and position of the C = C double bond in each methyl ester influence the biodiesel’s properties. In this study, pure mixtures of short-chain methyl esters (methyl acrylate and methyl propionate, methyl 3-butenoate and methyl butyrate) were selected as model systems to evaluate the effect of the C = C bond on copper corrosion behavior. These methyl esters allowed the study of unsaturation as representative structures of some compounds present in commercial biodiesel. Mass loss tests, electrochemical measurements such as open-circuit potential, linear polarization resistance, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and electrochemical noise were performed over a 6-week exposure period, along with surface analysis using scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The results showed that adding a high concentration of unsaturated methyl esters increases the copper corrosion rate as exposure time increases. The chemical structure and electronic conjugation of the methyl esters influence the polarization resistance (R p ), charge transfer resistance (R ct ), and noise resistance (R n ) values. SEM analysis revealed a greater tendency toward localized pitting corrosion on the copper surface.

Article.Title: Breeding emperor penguins show interannual recurrence in shelf-break associated foraging areas across contrasting sea ice conditions in the northwestern Weddell Sea
Article.Authors: Guímaro H.; Fretwell P.; Pütz K.; Xavier J.; Warwick-Evans V.; Day G.; Vianna J.; Pizarro E.; Krüger L.; Osborne N.; Ratcliffe N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The emperor penguin Aptenodytes forsteri is highly sea ice dependent and vulnerable to climate change, yet the at-sea distribution and habitat associations of breeding adults remain poorly understood for colonies in the western Weddell Sea. We tracked nine breeding adults from Snow Hill Island, the northernmost known colony, during chick-rearing in 2023-24 and 2025-26, and analysed 38 foraging trips using kernel utilisation distributions, habitat-selection models and hidden Markov models. Penguins repeatedly used a region east and northeast of the colony aligned with shelf-break-associated waters, with a smaller westward component towards waters close to glaciated coastal margins along the Antarctic Peninsula. Space use was broader and trips were longer in 2025-26, when core-use areas occurred under much higher sea ice concentration, yet overlap metrics indicated broad fidelity to the same geographical foraging region. Habitat use was associated with distance to the colony, mean sea ice concentration, with responses differing between study years, and the combined influence of shelf-break position and distance to glaciated coastal margins. Behavioural states varied with diel cycle and sea ice concentration, with foraging and resting associated with higher sea ice concentration than transit. The proposed Weddell Sea Marine Protected Area encompassed 57.9–75.1% of study-year foraging distributions, while smaller overlap occurred with the proposed Western Antarctic Peninsula and South Scotia Arc Marine Protected Area, highlighting the relevance of these areas for spatial conservation planning.

Article.Title: Phenology-driven dynamic threshold iot control for hydroponic garlic sprout production
Article.Authors: Chen S.; Li Y.; Liu P.; Lu S.; Guo H.; Xu Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To address the problem that traditional facility agriculture environmental control relies on fixed environmental thresholds and cannot adapt to the dynamic environmental requirements of crops at different growth stages, a crop phenology-based Crop Growth Dynamic Threshold Strategy (CGDTS) was proposed. An Internet of Things (IoT)-based intelligent greenhouse control system was developed, which integrates multi-source sensing, Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) control, edge computing, and cloud coordination. The proposed strategy incorporates real-time Growing Degree Days (GDD) as an indicator of crop developmental status into the greenhouse closed-loop control system. The crop phenological stages are automatically identified through cumulative GDD, and the environmental setpoints are switched according to the identified phenological stage, achieving coordination between environmental regulation and crop growth. A 24-day comparative cultivation experiment was conducted on hydroponic garlic sprouts. The results demonstrated that the proposed system achieved stable environmental monitoring, stage-based control, and remote management. Compared with the conventional fixed-threshold strategy, the CGDTS treatment was associated with an 11.7% higher marketable fresh weight, an 11.6% higher average plant height, and a 51.2% lower coefficient of variation of plant height in this single-cycle experiment, along with a lower observed developmental deviation ratio. These preliminary results suggest that the application of CGDTS in hydroponic garlic sprout production is feasible, and that stage-switching environmental regulation based on crop developmental status has the potential to improve crop growth performance and population uniformity; further studies with independently replicated treatments are needed to confirm these findings.

Article.Title: Systemic inflammation induces a myocardial inflammatory transcriptional signature without cardiac dysfunction in murine arthritis
Article.Authors: Tønnessen T.; Ahmed M.; Domanska D.; Umu S.; Melleby A.; Ueland T.; Espe E.; Zhang L.; Attramadal H.; Sjaastad I.; Vinge L.
Article.Abstract: Patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) face an elevated risk of developing heart failure, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Plausible causes include cardiac structural and molecular alterations attributable to sustained chronic inflammation. The present study investigates such putative cardiac alterations in a modified delayed-type hypersensitivity arthritis (DTHA) mouse model of sustained, RA-like inflammation. An RA-like inflammatory phenotype was induced in male BALB/c mice (n = 13) using a modified DTHA protocol, while control mice received vehicle injections (n = 13). The standard DTHA protocol consists of (1) immunization towards methylated bovine serum albumin (mBSA), (2) intravenous administration of a mixture of anti-collagen II antibodies, and (3) induction of arthritis via subcutaneous hind-leg injection of mBSA. In the modified DTHA protocol, steps 2 and 3 were repeated weekly for eight consecutive weeks to sustain inflammation. Analyses included serial cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI, days 15 and 57), plasma inflammatory markers, the left ventricular (LV) myocardial transcriptome, and assessment of hypertrophic and fibrotic remodelling. Fluctuating, yet sustained local and systemic inflammation was demonstrated. Despite this, no structural or functional differences were detected by cardiac MRI, and no gross fibrotic or hypertrophic alterations were observed. However, RNA-sequencing of bulk LV myocardial tissue revealed a distinct transcriptional profile with marked enrichment of inflammatory signalling pathways. Despite preserved cardiac structure and function, mice subjected to sustained DTHA-driven systemic inflammation displayed a pronounced myocardial inflammatory transcriptional signature. Whether this observation represents an early state of cardiac vulnerability preceding overt dysfunction, possibly requiring additional cardiac stressors, remains a hypothesis to be tested.

Article.Title: A unified stochastic random walk theory for Kolmogorov spectrum, halo mass functions, and halo density profiles
Article.Authors: Xu Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract We develop a unified stochastic framework for a broad class of nonequilibrium systems and apply it to turbulence and cosmic structure formation. Spectra and distributions in these systems are modeled as transport processes in an appropriate “scale space”, described by random walks and Fokker–Planck equations with scale‑dependent waiting times. Reformulating the turbulent cascade as a random walk in wavenumber space with a k-dependent waiting time, we recover the Kolmogorov -5/3 law and obtain the full energy spectrum including the inertial-dissipation crossover, exponential cutoff, and spectrum constant without invoking dimensional arguments. For a bottom-up hierarchical halo structure formation, low-mass haloes collapse early and retain strong primordial imprints, while prolonged assembly of large haloes near the characteristic mass $m_h^*$ tends to erase this memory and establishes a universal spectrum. We model this process as an analogous random walk of dark matter haloes in mass space $m_h$ with a mass-dependent waiting time $\tau_g\propto m_h^{-\lambda}$. The model yields a stretched Gaussian halo mass function that reproduces the Press–Schechter form, with both small‑scale scaling $f_M\propto m_h^{-\lambda}$ and exponential cutoff at $m_h>m_h^*$ set by exponent $\lambda$. The framework naturally produces a double‑$\lambda$ mass function, where $\lambda$ reflects the primordial spectrum at low masses and approaches $\lambda$=2/3 near $m_h^*$ where gravity dominates. For individual haloes, a spatial random walk with waiting time $\tau_{gr}\propto r^{-\gamma}$ generates a double‑$\gamma$ density profile that reproduces the Einasto profile, with both small-scale scaling $\rho_r\propto r^{-2\gamma}$ and exponential cutoff at $r>r_s$ set by exponent $\gamma$. In this case, $\gamma$ is fixed by the initial spectrum in the inner regions and approaches $\gamma$=2/3 in the outer regions and for haloes near $m_h^*$. Our results demonstrate that this simple stochastic framework provides a common theoretical description of both turbulent cascades and cosmic structure formation.

Article.Title: Mechanical stabilization of non-vascular catheters using a low-profile suture-anchored device
Article.Authors: Naidu S.; Zhou C.; Ma Q.; Bercu Z.; Li H.; Moon J.; Chen Y.
Article.Abstract: To evaluate the mechanical performance of AnchorDoc, a novel, low-profile, two-piece, suture-anchored device, against standard securement methods. We hypothesized that AnchorDoc would provide superior mechanical stability without compromising catheter patency. Using a custom anatomically-informed gelatin phantom of the human flank with porcine-skin overlay, we compared the performance of AnchorDoc against a standard adhesive device (StatLock) and a suture-tape technique (Roman sandal) for 8.5, 10.2, and 12 French (Fr) catheters. We conducted: (1) static tensile testing under dry and wet conditions to measure peak force to catheter slip (≥ 5 mm); (2) dynamic gait simulation to assess time-to-failure; and (3) static flow testing to evaluate for lumen compromise. In tensile testing, AnchorDoc required a significantly higher dislodgement force than both StatLock and Roman Sandal under dry (e.g., 10.2 Fr: 31.1 ± 1.4 N vs. 20.5 ± 2.4 N and 18.8 ± 2.3 N, respectively; p < 0.0001) and wet conditions (25.5 ± 1.0 N vs. 10.9 ± 1.3 N and 18.7 ± 1.0 N; p < 0.0001). The adhesive device’s retention strength degraded by nearly 50% when wet, while AnchorDoc maintained its superiority. In dynamic gait simulation, Kaplan-Meier analysis showed that AnchorDoc had a significantly higher survival probability (fewer failures) while tested over 12,000 cycles compared to both comparators (p < 0.05). Flow testing confirmed that AnchorDoc did not cause a statistically significant reduction in flow rate or lumen diameter across all catheter sizes (p > 0.05). The AnchorDoc device provides significantly greater resistance to both static and dynamic dislodgement forces than common adhesive and suture-tape techniques, particularly in a laboratory-simulated wet environment, without impairing catheter function. This suture-anchored, two-part platform represents a promising solution to mitigate the risk of non-vascular catheter dislodgement.

Article.Title: A multidimensional proteomic framework of circulating inflammation identifies outcome-specific cardiovascular risk axes in 39,494 UK biobank participants
Article.Authors: Song X.; Zhang H.; Liu G.; Shen Z.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Inflammation is central to cardiovascular disease, yet conventional biomarkers do not resolve the underlying organisation of circulating inflammatory biology. Among 44,787 UK Biobank participants passing proteomic quality control, 736 inflammation-related proteins were used to derive orthogonal proteomic dimensions in a White Development sample (n = 20,830), with definitions fixed and applied unchanged in White Validation (n = 20,831). A CVD-free multimodal cohort of 39,494 participants provided the source population for downstream analyses; primary prospective associations were evaluated in White Development complete cases (n = 17,334) and replicated in White Validation (n = 17,190). Eight dimensions showed high structural stability and distinct protein, pathway, metabolic, imaging, and cardiovascular profiles. In the primary analysis, 23 of 48 RC outcome associations were FDR significant; RC2 was positively associated with all six outcomes, with the strongest association for heart failure (HR 1.395, 95% CI 1.273–1.527), while RC8 showed a more moderate but similarly broad pattern. RC4 was mainly associated with coronary outcomes, RC6 showed inverse associations with several endpoints, and RC7 was most clearly related to heart failure and atrial fibrillation. Major patterns reproduced in White Validation. Adding RC1–RC8 improved discrimination across all six outcomes (ΔC-index 0.0055–0.0136), with incremental gains retained beyond CRP, GlycA, and NLR. These findings support a reproducible multidimensional proteomic architecture of inflammation with heterogeneous cardiovascular relevance.

Article.Title: Network-compartmental modeling for assessing core drivers of fascioliasis dissemination in definitive hosts
Article.Authors: Philipo H.; Hugo A.; Kung’aro M.; Shinzeh J.
Article.Abstract: Fascioliasis is a neglected zoonotic disease caused by Fasciola species, affecting livestock and humans worldwide and imposing substantial economic and public health burdens. Conventional compartmental models commonly assume homogeneous mixing and therefore may not adequately represent the heterogeneous contact patterns characteristic of smallholder farming systems. This study develops a network-informed multi-host compartmental model that integrates a Watts–Strogatz small-world contact network with effective exposure coefficients representing local and long-range connectivity among cattle, humans, snails, and environmental metacercariae. The framework incorporates short-range transmission within local communities and long-range transmission between geographically separated farming communities. Analytical results establish the basic reproduction number ( \(R_0\) ), demonstrate global asymptotic stability of the disease-free equilibrium when \(R_0<1\) , and provide a Jacobian-based criterion for local asymptotic stability of the endemic equilibrium. Numerical simulations characterize the temporal dynamics of infection and quantify the effects of treatment, environmental sanitation, network connectivity, and local exposure structure on transmission. Increased network connectivity and long-range interactions facilitate wider spatial dissemination, whereas reductions in transmission and environmental contamination suppress infection. The results demonstrate that incorporating network structure into fascioliasis transmission models provides a more realistic representation of heterogeneous contact processes and offers a quantitative framework for evaluating targeted control strategies in interconnected livestock and human communities.

Article.Title: Extraction, chemical fingerprinting, and dyeing-process evaluation of fungal pigments from Phaeolus schweinitzii
Article.Authors: Alotaibi N.; Umar A.; Alosaimi A.; Huseynova L.; Dufossé L.; Khalifeh A.; Alzahrani K.; Bhardwaj N.; Ghosh S.
Article.Abstract: Colors have capacity to elicit human emotions in philosophy, arts, science, and many industrial areas. There is a lot of interest in natural color substitutes due to rising concerns about the detrimental effects of synthetic colorants on consumers and the environment. Although, plants serve as major non-viable sources of natural pigments with several limitations. In contrast, fungi thrive in diverse environments also exhibit adaptive metabolisms and catalytic pathways, make them valuable for natural pigment production. Furthermore, there is a growing demand for more sustainable and cost-effective extraction methods. Therefore, under suitable condition, extraction technique was carried out. In this study, Phaeolus schweinitzii was identified using morphological and ITS-based molecular approaches and investigated as a source of yellow, red, and reddish-brown fungal pigments. The effects of pH, agitation speed, sodium sulfate concentration, temperature, and dyeing time on pigment uptake were evaluated sequentially using a one-factor-at-a-time (OFAT) experimental approach. The highest observed responses within the investigated ranges were generally associated with mildly acidic conditions, moderate-to-high agitation, low sodium sulfate concentrations, elevated temperatures, and intermediate dyeing times. However, because the variables were not studied simultaneously in a factorial design, these conditions are interpreted as preliminary operating ranges rather than a global multivariable optimum. Interactions among the process variables could not be estimated from the present design.
