Article.Title: The effect of appearance features of sidewalk autonomous delivery robot on perception of pedestrian
Article.Authors: Xu F.; Liu D.; Zhou C.; Hu J.; Zhang Z.; Sun S.
Article.Abstract: Sidewalk autonomous delivery robots (SADRs) are increasingly appearing on urban sidewalks and sharing public space with pedestrians. This study aims to investigate how different appearance features of SADRs influence four dimensions of human perception: Likeability, Competence, Perceived Safety, and Existence Acceptance. In Study 1, an affinity diagram method was used to classify the appearance features of existing SADRs into four categories—contour, proportion, facial features, and color scheme—which were then used as the design variables in Study 2. In Study 2, 100 participants completed an online questionnaire after viewing AI-generated videos of SADRs and evaluated the robots on the four perceptual dimensions. The statistical results showed that rounded contours and the presence of facial features significantly increased Likeability, Perceived Safety, and Existence Acceptance. White–black and yellow color schemes generally received higher ratings for Likeability, Perceived Safety, and Existence Acceptance than black–gray and red color schemes. In addition, a tall proportion significantly reduced Likeability. Study 3 used online semi-structured interviews to further examine the reasons underlying these evaluations and to explore participants’ subjective perceptions of SADRs. The findings provide practical guidance for designing SADR appearances that can foster more positive pedestrian perceptions and acceptance.

Article.Title: WebXR-based mobile point cloud rendering and semantic segmentation using depth data and voxel fusion
Article.Authors: Yang M.; Yeh C.; Tsai H.
Article.Abstract: A novel framework was developed for interactive, on-device visualization and user-triggered semantic segmentation of point clouds on mobile devices by integrating WebXR, THREE.js, and WebGL. Despite advances in mobile hardware, these tasks remain computationally intensive. The proposed framework leverages the WebXR API to acquire camera pose and depth data for efficient point cloud generation using BufferGeometry, followed by two-dimensional image recognition. A dynamic voxel fusion buffer was developed to construct voxel-based point clouds by aggregating semantic segmentation results from multiple frames. Segmentation results are further refined using a buffer voxel-counting algorithm and rendered in real time within a web browser using ShaderMaterial. Shaders are used to visualize public indoor datasets and convert them into depth maps, creating data compliant with WebXR constraints. The framework was trained and evaluated using the Stanford 3D Indoor Scene Dataset (S3DIS), and a lightweight 2D semantic segmentation model—trained on annotated real-world indoor scenes—achieved 89% accuracy and a mean Intersection over Union of 76%. The system was deployed and demonstrated in indoor scenes on a WebXR-capable mobile device. Under the tested configuration, the framework supports interactive visualization and user-triggered semantic segmentation; comprehensive latency, resource-use, cross-device, and environmental-robustness benchmarks remain subjects for future work.

Article.Title: Cumulative ecological risk and depression in college students: the mediating role of self-esteem and the moderating role of psychological resilience
Article.Authors: Zhang J.; Zheng S.; Fang M.; Long R.
Article.Abstract: This study proposes a moderated mediation model examining self-esteem as a mediator between cumulative ecological risk (CER) and depression among college students, and tests whether psychological resilience (PR) buffers the initial stage of this pathway (i.e., the CER–self-esteem link). A cross-sectional study was conducted among 1363 Chinese university students using self-report questionnaires. CER was assessed through a composite index measuring five ecological domains. Self-esteem was evaluated using the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale, PR with the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC-10), and depressive symptoms with the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). Data were analyzed using SPSS 26.0, with moderated mediation examined through the PROCESS macro (v4.2, Model 7). (1)CER significantly and positively predicted depression.(2) Self esteem partially mediates the relationship between CER and depression.(3) PR moderates the initial stage of the mediation pathway—specifically, the relationship between CER and self-esteem. For college students with high PR, CER has a far smaller detrimental effect on self-esteem. This study identified self-esteem as a potential mediator in the association between CER and depression among college students, and further indicated that PR plays a “protective shield” moderating role in the initial stage of this pathway, namely the process by which CER is associated with diminished self-esteem. These findings provide a theoretical basis for psychological interventions targeting high-risk college students, particularly those centered on enhancing PR.

Article.Title: Association between TyG-VAI and hypertension in children and adolescents based on machine learning algorithms
Article.Authors: Zhu J.; Zhang C.; Zhang Q.; Tian G.; Zhao J.; Wang M.; Liu Z.; Liu M.; Hao Y.
Article.Abstract: Hypertension in children and adolescents is increasingly prevalent, and effective risk indicators are needed. The triglyceride-glucose index combined with visceral adiposity index (TyG-VAI) has proved useful in adults, but evidence in the paediatric population remains limited. In this cross-sectional survey, 27,991 children and adolescents were enrolled in Henan Province, China, between 2023 and 2024 using multi-stage sampling. Multivariate logistic regression, subgroup and mediation analyses, and 11 machine learning models were used to examine the association between TyG-VAI and hypertension and to assess its predictive value. TyG-VAI was positively associated with hypertension (odds ratio [OR] = 2.36 for the highest quartile, P < 0.001), with greater sensitivity in males. Waist-to-height ratio was the main mediator (62.2%), followed by uric acid and the creatinine index. The multi-layer perceptron model incorporating TyG-VAI showed the best predictive performance (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.7518). TyG-VAI was independently associated with hypertension in children and adolescents and improved risk prediction, providing a basis for early intervention in this population.

Article.Title: Data-driven fault detection in wind turbine systems using support vector machines and artificial neural networks
Article.Authors: Bentata A.; Echiheb F.; Taj M.; Oproescu M.; Hussien S.; Mosaad M.; Bossoufi B.
Article.Abstract: Efficiency and reliability of wind turbine systems are very important in the production of clean sustainable energy sources. Malfunctioning of sensors, actuators, or other system components may affect system functionality and increase maintenance costs. This study presents a data-driven approach to fault detection in wind turbine systems using Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques, including Support Vector Machines (SVMs) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs), with Random Forest (RF) included as an additional baseline for comparison. A comprehensive benchmark model of a variable-speed wind turbine system is implemented using the FAST/Simulink environment under realistic turbulent wind conditions. The key system variables, namely generator speed, generated power, and blade pitch angles, were monitored. Multiple fault scenarios are introduced to evaluate system performance. A five-fold blocked temporal cross-validation strategy was used to evaluate the generalization performance of the models while preserving the temporal ordering of the simulated data. Simulation results show that fault-detection performance depends strongly on the fault type, with SVM and ANN generally providing stronger performance than RF, while ANN shows advantages for some nonlinear and challenging fault patterns, particularly in terms of recall and robustness under noisy conditions. This research highlights the effectiveness of AI-based, data-driven approaches in enhancing fault detection capabilities and improving the reliability of wind turbine systems.

Article.Title: Oral health status and navigation of care among first nations peoples with kidney failure in South Australia
Article.Authors: He I.; Budden T.; Jensen E.; Kaur S.; Hedges J.; Jamieson L.; Sethi S.
Article.Abstract: First Nations peoples in Australia experience a disproportionate burden of chronic diseases such as kidney disease and chronic gum disease or periodontitis. This study aims to describe a relationship between periodontal disease and kidney failure in a cohort of First Nations peoples in South Australia. A cross-sectional mixed-methods study was conducted, involving the recruitment of First Nations adults from South Australia who had been diagnosed with kidney failure. The participants underwent clinical oral examinations, which included assessments of dentate and periodontal status, using the CDC/AAP 2012 and AAP/EFP 2018 classifications. Periodontitis was reported if detectable interdental attachment loss at two or more non-adjacent teeth, or buccal/oral attachment loss ≥ 4 mm with pocketing > 4 mm at two or more teeth was observed. Furthermore, a structured, validated self-report questionnaire was administered to collect data on general health conditions and oral health behaviours. A total of 36 participants were enrolled in the study; the average age was 57.4 years, including 15 (41.6%) edentulous and 21 (58.3%) partially dentate individuals. All partially dentate participants were diagnosed with periodontitis. Over a third of participants (37.1%) self-rated their oral health as very good or good. Findings indicate a high burden of edentulous or severe periodontal disease amongst First Nations peoples with kidney failure. Integrating oral health care into primary kidney disease management strategies could mitigate health-related disparities and reduce adverse oral health outcomes among individuals with kidney disease.

Article.Title: Integrated stress indices, GGE biplot and physiological approaches reveal superior pre-released genotypes of linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.) for drought tolerance at reproductive stage
Article.Authors: Sharma P.; Kumar M.; Sharma V.; Kumar S.; Gangwar V.; Singh B.; Panwar G.; Singh C.
Article.Abstract: The present investigation was undertaken to assess genetic variability and identify the drought tolerant pre-released genotypes of linseed. Forty-two genotypes were evaluated under irrigated and managed drought stress conditions across the two years, followed by multi-location validation of selected genotypes under field and rainout shelter using GGE biplot approach. Further, validation was performed through root system architecture (RSA), leaf physiology, histo-chemical staining and DNA fingerprinting using EST marker was done for its exploitation in breeding programmes. Moreover, EST-derived markers provided a targeted assessment of genetic diversity and should be interpreted as a proof-of-concept. The significant genetic variability was observed for yield and key morphological traits. Traits such as plant height, number of branches per plant, number of capsules per plant, biological yield per plant, relative water content, membrane stability index and chlorophyll content were identified as reliable morphological traits under drought stress. Among stress indices, stress tolerance index, harmonic mean and yield index were proved as most effective for identifying high yielding genotypes with enhanced drought tolerance, resulting six genotypes were found drought tolerant. Among them two genotypes i.e. G32 (BLS 2022-28) and G28 (BLS 2022-24) exhibited superior yield and stability over the environments. Based on multi-environments validation, these two genotypes were confirmed as drought tolerant, supported by robust RSA and their relative ability to limit ROS accumulation. The DNA fingerprinting of selected genotypes showed the significant diversity among the reference panel of linseed, indicating their potential for targeted genotype fingerprinting and locus specific diversity assessment. These genotypes have strong potential for including in drought resilient linseed breeding programs.

Article.Title: Morphological and vascular assessment of mandibular nutrient foramina using cone beam computed tomography and Color Doppler ultrasonography
Article.Authors: Kaya M.; Doğan M.; Kotanlı S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract One of the anatomical variations found in the mandible is the presence of nutrient foramina. Failure to correctly identify these structures and understand their characteristics may lead to complications during surgical procedures. The aim of this study was to evaluate the presence and morphological characteristics of nutrient foramina using cone beam computed tomography and to assess the presence of detectable colour-flow signals using color Doppler ultrasonography. This observational study consisted of a retrospective cone beam computed tomography assessment of 538 eligible patients, followed by a prospective color Doppler ultrasonography examination of all 45 patients in whom at least one nutrient foramen was identified, comprising a total of 73 nutrient foramina. No statistically significant difference was found in the distribution of nutrient foramina according to sex. A significant association was observed between right- and left-sided nutrient foramen presence ( P < 0.001). In the primary analysis, nutrient foramina diameter analyzed as a continuous predictor was significantly associated with the presence of a detectable colour-flow signal, with each 0.1-mm increase in diameter associated with higher odds of signal detection (OR = 5.22, 95% CI: 2.75–9.93; P < 0.001). Nutrient foramina may be clinically relevant structures. While cone beam computed tomography enables detailed morphological evaluation, color Doppler ultrasonography may provide complementary information regarding detectable colour-flow signals under the applied imaging settings. The combined use of these methods provides complementary morphological and colour-flow information regarding nutrient foramina, while the potential surgical relevance of these findings requires prospective clinical validation.

Article.Title: Mouse Cardiac Regeneration Database (MCAREDB): a single-cell atlas of neonatal cardiac regeneration in mice
Article.Authors: Shea A.; Cui J.; Li M.; Leonard R.; Bartz J.; Nguyen T.; Zhang J.; Garry D.; Dong X.
Article.Abstract: Adult mammalian hearts exhibit minimal regenerative capacity, limiting most cardiac repair. In contrast, neonatal mice retain the ability to regenerate cardiac tissue for a brief period after birth. Although single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (sc/snRNA-seq) has deepened our understanding of this regenerative window, existing datasets remain dispersed across studies, hindering integrative and comparative analyses. To address this gap, we developed the Mouse CArdiac REgeneration DataBase (MCAREDB), the first freely accessible, web-based resource that consolidates and visualizes sc/snRNA-seq datasets from multiple mouse cardiac regeneration studies. MCAREDB enables cell-type-specific exploration of differential gene expression and pathway enrichment across key biological contexts, including regenerative versus non-regenerative stages and sham versus myocardial infarction. Core features include an interactive genome browser with epigenetic tracks, comparative gene expression visualization, spatial transcriptomics interface, pathway enrichment analysis, and bulk data download options. By integrating diverse datasets into a unified and interactive framework, MCAREDB lowers technical barriers to data exploration and accelerates hypothesis generation in cardiac regeneration research.

Article.Title: Development of machine learning and integrated design for prediction of pharmaceutical solubility in dense solvent at different temperature levels
Article.Authors: Alsaab H.
Article.Abstract: This research explores the solubility behavior of Nystatin in a ternary system of supercritical carbon dioxide (SCCO 2 ) and ethanol, focusing on the effects of temperature and pressure. The study employs three distinct machine learning models, Gradient Boosting (GB), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), and Polynomial Regression (PR), to predict the ternary solubility of Nystatin in SCCO 2 and ethanol. The hyper-parameter tuning for these models is accomplished using the Dragonfly Algorithm (DA), enhancing their predictive accuracy. The dataset, comprising temperature, pressure, and corresponding ternary solubility values, is analyzed using these models, and their performance is assessed through key evaluation metrics. The GB model achieves a score of 0.863 in R 2 metric. The RMSE and MAE both exhibit values below 0.1, thereby indicating the model’s high level of precision. The K-nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm demonstrated a high level of accuracy, as evidenced by its impressive coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.978. This result suggests that the KNN model exhibited a strong alignment with the underlying data. The performance of the PR model is outstanding, by its high R 2 score of 0.991, indicating its precise representation of solubility trends. The low RMSE and MAE values further confirm its precision.

Article.Title: Identification of model-ranked candidate medical interventions for pediatric atopic dermatitis using Dempster-Shafer evidence theory
Article.Authors: Na R.; Yang Y.; Li W.; Wang Y.; Yue S.
Article.Abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is common in infants and children, but comparative evidence for ranking drug combinations at the individual-patient level remains limited. Pathological and diagnostic data from 1,736 pediatric patients with AD were collected. After major measured confounding factors were screened, 455 patients with relatively low EASI scores were retained. CLIQUE subspace clustering was used to identify groups defined by similar medication patterns, and Dempster-Shafer evidence theory (DSET) was used to construct mass functions under prespecified clinical constraints. EASI improvement per hospitalization day was treated as an exploratory constructed surrogate outcome. Nested fivefold cross-validation was the sole primary validation strategy; all preprocessing, parameter selection, clustering, mass-function construction, safety-weight application, and prediction were performed within the corresponding training folds. Proportional calibration and expert-panel agreement were treated only as secondary descriptive analyses. In the primary nested fivefold cross-validation analysis, the clinically constrained framework generated model-ranked candidate combinations for held-out patients and yielded a mean hospitalization-duration difference of 1.57 days relative to experience-based selection. The highest-ranked candidates included topical fluticasone propionate with complementary adjuncts. A secondary proportional calibration analysis suggested an average difference of approximately 1.68 days across the three leading candidates. These values are internally validated associations or descriptive estimates, not causal treatment effects. The clinically constrained CLIQUE-DSET framework generated interpretable candidate rankings and showed a modest internally validated association with shorter hospitalization duration than experience-based selection. Because the endpoint was an exploratory surrogate and the study was retrospective, single-center, and focused predominantly on mild cases, the findings are hypothesis-generating and do not support direct prescribing or causal claims.

Article.Title: Graph-based ransomware propagation modelling and early interception in enterprise networks using dynamic attack surface analysis
Article.Authors: Al Khater N.
Article.Abstract: Ransomware incidents consistently bypass endpoint detection due to their rapid lateral movement through shared drives and remote services before detonating encryption payloads. Existing detection systems react to encryption activity rather than intercepting propagation. This study models enterprise network topology as a dynamic knowledge graph where node attributes represent device vulnerability scores and edge weights encode lateral-movement probability based on historical authentication logs. A graph attention network (GAT) trained on historical ransomware campaigns predicts high-risk propagation paths in real time, enabling proactive isolation of vulnerable nodes before encryption initiates. A simulation environment built on MITRE ATT&CK ransomware scenarios validates that the proposed interception strategy reduces the mean encrypted file value by 85% compared to endpoint-only detection (median reduction 98%, reflecting a heavy-tailed outcome distribution we characterise in full), even when encryption begins on the first affected host. We further report three results obtained for this extended study. First, the GAT already achieves a 76.2% reduction when trained on a single enterprise network and reaches 89.6% with four, after which it plateaus, indicating the learned propagation cues are not network-specific. Second, and most importantly for an adversarial domain, we introduce and evaluate an abstract “patient” attacker that delays visible encryption to deny the defender its primary dynamic signal: at short silent dwell the proposed defense retains a large advantage, but as the silent dwell grows all detonation-reactive defenses, including ours, converge toward the no-defense outcome, exposing a genuine and previously uncharacterised limitation of detection-triggered interception that we discuss together with complementary mitigations. Third, a GCN baseline slightly outperforms the GAT on interception (89% versus 85%) and an ensemble of the two performs best (91%), confirming that the gains come from the graph formulation and the isolation policy rather than from the attention mechanism itself. The model runs entirely on-premise with no dependence on external threat feeds. We position the contribution deliberately: rather than a new graph-neural-network primitive, it is a problem formulation (early interception as hidden-front prediction on a dynamic enterprise graph), a containment-aware isolation policy with proved structural guarantees, and, most importantly for an adversarial domain, a characterisation of when detonation-triggered defence works and when it provably fails against an adaptive, patient adversary. Ransomware propagation throughout is represented as an abstract probabilistic contagion on a graph.

Article.Title: A double-blind randomized controlled trial comparing intranasal dexmedetomidine with and without fentanyl for pediatric premedication
Article.Authors: Lapmahapaisan S.; Koopredechat P.; Jindawatthana I.; Maisat W.
Article.Abstract: Intranasal dexmedetomidine is effective for pediatric premedication but has a relatively slow onset. We investigated whether adding intranasal fentanyl accelerates sedation in children undergoing elective surgery. In this randomized, double-blind controlled trial, 60 children aged 1–5 years were assigned 1:1 to intranasal dexmedetomidine 1 μg/kg alone or dexmedetomidine 1 μg/kg plus fentanyl 1 μg/kg. The primary outcome was time to adequate sedation, defined as a sedation score of at least 3, assessed every 5 min until operating-room entry. Adequate sedation was observed in 28/30 and 30/30 children, respectively. Median time to sedation was 23.0 and 23.5 min (hazard ratio 0.91, 95% CI 0.54 to 1.53; p = 0.74). Complete-case mean onset times were 22.0 and 23.5 min, respectively (mean difference 1.5 min, 95% CI -3.7 to 6.6; p = 0.57). Sedation at mask introduction, mask acceptance, parental separation and parental satisfaction were similar between groups. No child developed oxygen desaturation below 95% or bradycardia requiring intervention. Adding fentanyl did not accelerate sedation or improve preoperative cooperation, providing no support for its routine addition solely to shorten sedation onset. Trial registration: Thai Clinical Trials Registry, TCTR20250812007, 12 August 2025.

Article.Title: Prevalence, severity, and associated factors of thrombocytopenia among pregnant women attending antenatal care clinic in North West Ethiopia,2024: cross-sectional study
Article.Authors: Berhan A.; Almaw A.; Legese B.; Damtie S.; Solomon Y.; Sharew B.; Tiruneh T.; Kiros T.; Asmare G.; Abeje G.; Getie B.; Assefa A.; Erkihun M.
Article.Abstract: Thrombocytopenia during pregnancy poses risks such as excessive bleeding during or after childbirth, wound leakage at cesarean sites, and neonatal thrombocytopenia. This study aimed to assess the prevalence, severity, and associated factors of thrombocytopenia among pregnant women who visited the Antenatal Care Clinic at Debre Tabor Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, North West Ethiopia. A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted from January 1 to April 30, 2024. Data were analyzed using Stata version 14.0. Descriptive statistics, along with bivariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses, were performed, with a P-value of ≤ 0.05 considered indicative of statistical significance. The overall prevalence of thrombocytopenia among pregnant women was 20.14% (95% CI: 16.6–24.3). Multivariable logistic regression revealed that older age (AOR = 6.5,95%:2.19–9.6, p-value = 0.001), increase in gestational age (AOR = 5.2, 95% CI: 3.92–6.65, p < 0.001), lack of iron supplementation (AOR = 2.4, 95% CI: 1.24–4.58, p = 0.009), lower antenatal care follow-up (AOR = 1.3,95% CI: 1.13–3.51, p-value = < 0.001), and history of heavy bleeding (AOR = 1.5, 95% CI: 1.29–3.84, p = 0.010) were significantly associated with higher odds of thrombocytopenia. The prevalence of thrombocytopenia was 20.14%, and it affects approximately one in five pregnant women in the study area, predominantly manifesting in mild forms. Key factors associated with thrombocytopenia include older maternal age, advanced gestational age, lack of iron supplementation, history of heavy bleeding, and lower antenatal care follow-up. Target interventions optimizing nutritional care and antenatal care compliance are recommended.

Article.Title: ISMC-based system-level coordinated control of Active Front-End converter and DSTATCOM for transient stability enhancement in shipboard hybrid AC/DC microgrids
Article.Authors: Barzegar A.; manthouri M.; Pahlavani M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Shipboard hybrid AC/DC microgrids (MGs) are increasingly deployed to integrate advanced propulsion systems and pulsed power loads while maintaining high power quality and reliability. However, rapid load fluctuations can induce severe transient disturbances that threaten system stability. This paper proposes a system-level coordinated control strategy for an Active Front-End (AFE) converter and a Distribution Static Compensator (DSTATCOM) to enhance transient stability and power quality in shipboard hybrid AC/DC MGs. The pulsed loads on the DC side are supplied through the AFE converter, which regulates the DC bus voltage and manages real and reactive power exchange between the DC and AC sides. To ensure precise dynamic response, an Integral Sliding Mode Control (ISMC) scheme is designed for the AFE to accurately track DC voltage and the dq-axis​ current components under severe disturbances. Similarly, the DSTATCOM is employed to correct the power factor at the Point of Common Coupling (PCC) and stabilize AC bus voltage, with an ISMC-based controller designed to achieve accurate tracking of its DC-link voltage and dq-axis current components. The performance of the proposed ISMC-based system-level coordinated AFE and DSTATCOM control is compared with conventional PI, Non-singular Terminal SMC (NT-SMC), and Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC) approaches under various dynamic scenarios, including pulsed load steps, propulsion load variations, and combined disturbances. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed ISMC method reduces DC-link voltage deviation by 45% compared to conventional PI control and improves transient settling time by nearly 30% under severe pulsed load conditions. Furthermore, the THD of voltage and current at the AC bus are limited to 3.36%, 4.38%, respectively, while maintaining a near-unity power factor. The findings confirm that ISMC-based system-level coordinated control of AFE and DSTATCOM provides an improved solution for enhancing transient stability and power quality in shipboard hybrid AC/DC MGs under model and parameter uncertainties.

Article.Title: Secure automation of CI/CD pipelines for cloud infrastructures
Article.Authors: Borghol R.; Zoghlami R.; Sarraj H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The paradigm shift towards cloud-native applications and microservices architectures has introduced significant complexities in software deployment and management. Traditional manual deployment processes are inadequate, being error-prone, slow, and insecure. This paper presents a comprehensive case study on the design and implementation of a fully automated, secure, and intelligent CI/CD pipeline for a cloud-based infrastructure. Leveraging a suite of modern DevOps tools, we demonstrate an end-to-end workflow for a microservices-based application deployed on Microsoft Azure. Unlike purely theoretical models, this work focuses on practical implementation, this work focuses on a practical implementation carried out in an academic engineering environment. The architecture integrates Jenkins for Continuous Integration, SonarQube for static code analysis, and Trivy for container security scanning. Continuous Deployment is achieved through a GitOps approach, orchestrated by ArgoCD on an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster. The results validate the efficacy of this model, showcasing a 95.6% pipeline success rate, an 87.5% reduction in deployment time, and the enforcement of stringent quality and security gates. These results were obtained in an academic environment; performance may vary in large-scale industrial deployments. This study aims to share concrete implementation insights that may support organizations and academic institutions seeking to improve the reliability, traceability, and security of their software delivery lifecycle.

Article.Title: Tracing working capital pressure in concentrated supply chains with temporal graph transformers
Article.Authors: Mu C.; Song D.
Article.Abstract: Concentrated trading relationships can improve coordination, yet they can also amplify operational stress when inventories, delivery commitments, and short-term obligations become misaligned. Conventional concentration ratios summarize dependence at the firm level but reveal little about how this pressure develops over time or travels through multi-tier supplier–buyer relations. This study presents SC-GraphTransformer-Press, a temporal graph framework that combines upstream and downstream concentration, product-specific transaction structure, recurrent firm states, and attention-based propagation to forecast working capital pressure. Pressure is operationalized as an inventory-backed stress proxy derived from unmet inventory-related obligations and available inventory, with firm-scale and network controls used to distinguish firms that have similar relative pressure but different operating capacities. The forecasting experiments use three SupplySim-derived benchmarks in which the required inventory and backlog states are observable. Under chronological multi-horizon evaluation, the proposed model achieves the strongest predictive performance among econometric, machine-learning, static graph, and temporal graph baselines, with its advantage increasing at longer horizons and under supply disruption. Network diagnostics further associate concentrated dependencies with persistent downstream pressure, while model-based scenarios indicate that supplier exits and supply shocks produce larger predicted responses than customer concentration and that product substitution can moderate these responses. Chronological audits and robustness tests across concentration assignments, shock locations, and simulator settings support the stability of these findings. The framework therefore offers a practical route from static concentration measurement to forward-looking diagnosis of working capital stress in dynamic supply-chain networks.

Article.Title: Antibody discovery from phage libraries lacking clear target-cell-selective enrichment through NGS-guided search space definition and cloning-free binding screening
Article.Authors: Wada K.; Watanabe T.; Nishida Y.; Kotera J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Antibody discovery targeting primary cells or transient cellular states remains challenging because conventional cell-based phage display relies on clonal enrichment, which may fail when specific binders do not become dominant. Here, we present an antibody discovery workflow for phage libraries lacking clear target-cell-selective enrichment that integrates next-generation sequencing (NGS)-guided definition of a candidate search space with cloning-free antibody reconstruction and screening. Using disease-associated CD11c⁺F4/80⁺ macrophages isolated from a diet-induced MASH mouse model, we found that conventional panning did not produce clear target-cell-selective enrichment at the phage-pool level, even after selection stringency was increased. Although NGS analysis revealed reduced library diversity and subtle shifts in clone frequencies, no dominant clones emerged. Applying predefined selection criteria to the NGS data instead enabled the identification of a tractable set of candidate antibodies. The selected sequences were directly reconstructed and screened using a cloning-free workflow, yielding antibodies with measurable target-cell binding. Selected antibodies showed modest target-cell-preferential binding after IgG conversion, and two antibodies additionally stained MASH-associated inflammatory lesions. This study provides a practical NGS-guided framework for candidate prioritization and functional screening when clear pool-level enrichment is not observed.

Article.Title: Timing of recurrent acute kidney injury is associated with mortality and chronic kidney disease progression in very elderly patients
Article.Authors: Bai Y.; Wang Y.; Ding X.; Lyu Q.; Ao Q.; Li Q.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Acute kidney injury (AKI) recurrence is common in elderly patients, but whether the timing of recurrence influences clinical outcomes remains unknown. We hypothesized that early and late recurrence represent two distinct phenotypes with opposing outcomes—early recurrence being associated with short-term mortality, and late recurrence being associated with chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression. This multicenter retrospective cohort study included patients aged ≥ 75 years who recovered from an index AKI episode between January 2017 and December 2024. Recurrent AKI was defined as a new serum creatinine rise (≥ 26.5 µmol/L within 48 h or ≥ 50% within 7 days) after complete recovery from the preceding episode. Recurrence timing was categorized into four intervals: 8–14 days, 15–21 days, 22–28 days, and more than 28 days. Among 2,382 patients, 51.7% (1232/2382) experienced a second AKI episode. Recurrence occurred within 8–14 days in 10.4% (248/2382) of patients, within 15–21 days in 13.3% (316/2382), within 22–28 days in 13.8% (328/2382), and after 28 days in 13.2% (340/2382). Early recurrence (8–21 days) was characterized by acute severity markers (sepsis, mechanical ventilation, advanced AKI stage), whereas late recurrence (> 21 days) was characterized by chronic vulnerability markers (lower baseline eGFR, nephrotoxicity). New-onset CKD occurred in 17.1% (24/140) of those with early recurrence (8–14 days), rising to 36.3% (114/314) in those with late recurrence (> 28 days) ( P < 0.001). Compared with a single AKI episode, recurrence at any time window was independently associated with higher 90-day and 1-year mortality. The adjusted HRs for 90-day mortality were 7.826 (95% CI: 4.051–13.106) for 8–14 days, 5.965 (95% CI: 3.087–11.526) for 15–21 days, 4.484 (95% CI: 2.276–8.835) for 22–28 days, and 2.506 (95% CI: 1.206–5.204) for > 28 days; for 1-year mortality, the HRs were 2.713 (95% CI: 1.942–3.786), 2.654 (95% CI: 1.917–3.687), 1.965 (95% CI: 1.396–2.765), and 1.583 (95% CI: 1.108–2.264), respectively (all P < 0.01). AKI recurrence at any time window independently increases mortality. However, early recurrence (≤ 21 days) is independently associated with higher mortality, whereas late recurrence (> 21 days) is associated with higher CKD progression in descriptive analyses. Recurrence timing, not just frequency, may help guide post-discharge risk stratification and follow-up planning.

Article.Title: Research on optimization of radial uncoupled charge parameters based on the mechanical characteristics of step-type partitioning
Article.Authors: Wang T.; Ren G.; Wang Z.; Kang P.
Article.Abstract: Abstract To investigate the influence mechanism of a radial uncoupled charge structure using mixed emulsion explosives on the blasting fines generation rate, a typical granite mine was selected as the research case. a systematic study was conducted by integrating theoretical analysis, transparent tube simulations, and on-site industrial trials. First, by comparing coupled and uncoupled charges, we demonstrate the advantage of radially uncoupled charges in achieving peak detonation stress attenuation and uniform energy release through the annular gap. Second, variable-diameter radial decoupled spaced sinking charge simulations were conducted to optimize spacer installation and isolation measures. Finally, field trials were carried out on a weakly weathered (+ 30 m) and a moderately weathered (+ 45 m) granite bench within the same mine, where different decoupling coefficient schemes were applied to the upper, middle, and lower sections of bench-zoned areas and compared with traditional rock-slag spacers and continuous charging. Results show that in weakly to moderately weathered granite, this radially uncoupled configuration-with a 125 mm bottom charge and 110 mm middle/upper spacers-reduces unit explosive consumption by over 16%, yields a uniform block size distribution, lowers fines generation, and produces a moderately loose muckpile favorable for subsequent excavation and loading. This proposed structure effectively controls the pulverization rate in granite blasting, offering a technical reference for similar granite quarries.

Article.Title: Hemoglobin-to-red blood cell distribution width ratio and in-hospital mortality in patients with non-traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage: a retrospective cohort study
Article.Authors: Xu W.; He W.; Zhai H.; Liu Q.; Huang J.; Min F.; Lin C.; Liang R.
Article.Abstract: Non-traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) carries a high in-hospital mortality rate, and reliable biomarkers for early risk stratification are lacking. This study investigated the association between the hemoglobin-to-red blood cell distribution width ratio (HRR) and in-hospital mortality in patients with non-traumatic SAH. A total of 1,161 patients were identified from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database. Multivariable logistic regression, subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses were performed to assess the association between HRR and in-hospital mortality. An exploratory analysis of hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) was further conducted using competing risk models. Lower HRR was significantly associated with increased in-hospital mortality. In the fully adjusted model, each 0.10 increase in HRR was associated with reduced mortality risk (OR = 0.873, P = 0.005). This association remained consistent across subgroup and sensitivity analyses. Incorporating HRR into the clinical model improved risk discrimination and reclassification. In the exploratory HAP analysis, although conventional regression indicated an inverse association, competing risk analysis showed that HRR was not independently associated with HAP, whereas its association with in-hospital mortality remained significant. HRR is independently associated with in-hospital mortality in patients with non-traumatic SAH and may serve as a readily available biomarker for early risk stratification.

Article.Title: An automated pipeline for adult and developmental neuropsychological assessment of executive functions and metacognition based on a multi-layer neuropsychological digital-twin framework
Article.Authors: Granato G.; Di Giulio J.; Manzi G.; Puzzo C.; Mattera A.; Giocondo F.; Adriani W.; Capobianco M.; Baldassarre G.
Article.Abstract: An efficient and standardised neuropsychological assessment of higher-order cognition is central to both research and clinical practice. However, existing tools are typically limited to isolated tasks, manual scoring, aggregated analyses, with little or no integration of computational modelling. These constraints reduce reproducibility, scalability, and translational potential across research and clinical contexts. We present an automated pipeline grounded in a multi-layer neuropsychological digital-twin framework that unifies task administration, automatic scoring, extended data analysis, computational modelling, and readable reporting. Specifically, the pipeline provides (I) administration of standard neuropsychological tasks of executive functions and metacognition, including the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test (WCST), the metacognitive WCST (Meta-WCST), and an original developmental version (Dev-Meta-WCST), (II) fully automated scoring of classical indices and trial-by-trial trends, (III) computational modelling of individual traits and dynamics, (IV) generation of individual multi-layer neuropsychological digital twins, made inspectable through human-readable reports presenting aggregated data, trial-by-trial dynamics, temporal data, and model-based profiles, alongside group-level reports. We illustrate the pipeline functionalities (task-specific automation, individual-profile differentiation, developmental applicability, and model-based interpretability) using five representative single cases: one adult performing the WCST, two adults performing the Meta-WCST, and two children, with typical development and Attention Deficit with or without Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), performing the Dev-Meta-WCST. The pipeline, of which a preliminary version is already shared on the IRIN platform (‘Italian Research Infrastructure for Neuroscience’, formerly EBRAINS-Italy), represents a starting point for the development of an enabling technology for individualized neuropsychological profiling across adult and developmental populations and multiple application contexts.

Article.Title: Semantic quality control of cervical cancer RTSTRUCT data through threshold stress-testing and technical DVH executability assessment
Article.Authors: Lin W.; Xiao L.; Lu S.; Liang C.; Zhou Y.; Lin X.; Fang J.; Xiao C.; Fang Y.
Article.Abstract: Technically readable radiotherapy structure sets do not necessarily contain structures suitable for organ-specific dose analysis. We developed a purpose-aware framework for pre-analytic semantic quality control (semantic QC) of real-world RT Structure Set (RTSTRUCT) data and evaluated threshold-dependent review workload and technical dose-volume histogram (DVH) executability. This single-centre retrospective framework-development study included 134 cervical cancer radiotherapy cases and 4311 regions of interest. Cases were assigned to rule-derived QC Levels 1–3, and four empirical cut-points were varied in a complete factorial design of 81 configurations. Technical DVH executability was evaluated across 670 case-OAR tasks. Essential OARs accounted for 1127 ROI records, whereas auxiliary optimisation and dose-shell/isodose-like objects accounted for 1376. The review set ranged from 16 to 107 cases, with review status changing in 91/134 cases. Moderate unmapped-ROI and suspected-duplicate thresholds accounted for 85.0% of the total review-workload sum of squares. Of 670 case-OAR tasks, 545 had a standardised-name candidate, 520 had non-empty multi-slice contours, and all 520 passed technical checks. Technical DVH executability was 77.6% overall and 95.4% among named candidates. Within this internal framework-development cohort, these findings support traceable pre-analytic triage and failure localisation but do not establish semantic accuracy, expert-confirmed structure identity, TPS agreement, clinical dose validity or external generalisability.

Article.Title: Sustainable behavior among students: the role of pollution risk perception and environmental policies in Romania and the United States
Article.Authors: Puiu S.; Amarie D.; Zăvăleanu M.; Udristioiu M.
Article.Abstract: Understanding the factors associated with sustainable behavior is important for developing effective environmental policies and educational strategies. However, only a few studies have simultaneously examined pollution risk perception, beliefs regarding environmental public policies, and sustainable behavior within a comparative cross-national framework. This study investigates the relationships among these constructs using data collected from a cross-sectional survey of 555 university students (294 from Romania and 261 from the United States). The proposed conceptual model was evaluated using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), complemented by bootstrapping, the measurement invariance of composite models (MICOM) procedure, and multi-group analysis (MGA). The results support all three hypothesized relationships. Pollution risk perception showed the strongest positive association with beliefs about environmental public policies and was also positively associated with sustainable behavior. The three hypothesized structural paths were positive and statistically significant in both national samples. The exploratory multi-group analysis did not detect statistically significant differences between the estimated path coefficients. These results do not demonstrate formal cross-country equivalence because compositional invariance was not established for RISKP and SUSTB. The country-specific estimates are therefore interpreted independently. By integrating psychological and institutional factors within a single analytical framework and providing exploratory evidence from student samples in an emerging and a developed economy, this study contributes to a better understanding of sustainable behavior among university students. The findings offer practical implications for higher education institutions, environmental agencies, and policymakers seeking to strengthen environmental awareness and promote sustainable practices through evidence-based educational and policy interventions.

Article.Title: PURE healthy diet score associated with lower asthma odds: a case–control study
Article.Authors: Liu X.; Zhong Y.; Luo Q.; Ma Q.; Xiang Y.; Huang Y.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Asthma is a chronic inflammatory airway disease. Diet may influence asthma through oxidative stress, inflammation, and gut–lung axis interactions. Evidence on the PURE Healthy Diet Score (PHDS) remains scarce. This study investigated PHDS adherence in relation to asthma odds, pulmonary function, asthma control, biomarkers, and quality of life in adults. This age‑matched case–control study included 200 adults with physician‑diagnosed asthma and 200 healthy controls. Dietary intake was assessed using a validated food frequency questionnaire, and PHDS (0–24) was calculated from fruits, vegetables, legumes, nuts, fish, and dairy. Spirometry, Asthma Control Test (ACT), Asthma Quality of Life Questionnaire (AQLQ), and biomarkers of inflammation, oxidative stress, and gut–lung axis were measured. Logistic regression and mediation analyses were performed. Healthy controls had a significantly higher PHDS than asthma cases (14.4 ± 2.7 vs. 10.4 ± 2.7, P < 0.001). Higher PHDS was associated with significantly lower odds of asthma (per 1‑point increase: OR = 0.89; 95% CI 0.83–0.96; P < 0.001), with a significant inverse quartile-based pattern across PHDS quartiles (fully adjusted model, Q4 vs. Q1: OR = 0.28; 95% CI 0.12–0.57; P-trend < 0.001). Higher PHDS also correlated with better lung function (FEV₁, FVC, PEF), higher ACT and AQLQ scores (all P‑trend < 0.05), and lower FeNO. Gut–lung axis biomarkers (zonulin, LPS, and TMAO) were significantly lower across higher PHDS quartiles, indicating an inverse association with circulating zonulin, LPS, and TMAO concentrations (all P-trend < 0.05). Exploratory mediation analyses identified statistical associations of systemic inflammatory and gut–lung axis-related biomarkers with the PHDS–asthma association; these model-based findings are exploratory and do not establish causal mediation or biological mechanisms. Higher adherence to the PURE Healthy Diet Score was associated with lower asthma odds, better respiratory health, and improved asthma control, together with a more favorable inflammatory and gut–lung axis-related biomarker profile; these observational associations do not establish causal pathways.

Article.Title: High rabies mortality and barriers to effective management in Tigray during prolonged war and deadly siege
Article.Authors: Nigusse A.; Gebregergs G.; Amaha M.; Hailu T.; Monti M.; Alemayohu M.
Article.Abstract: Global efforts has been undertaken to eliminate dog mediated human rabies deaths by 2030. This target was proposed to undertake various prevention and control measures including the integrated surveillance system and optimal dog vaccination. However, the impact of a collapsed healthcare system during the prolonged war and siege in Tigray, Ethiopia, remains poorly understood on the status of the surveillance system, and the burden of rabies. Therefore, this study assessed clinical rabies mortality patterns and explored challenges in rabies prevention and control methods. A mixed method approach with retrospective analysis of surveillance data (2017–2023) and in-depth interviews with human health and animal health experts were conducted in Tigray region of the Northern Ethiopia. Surveillance data from 2017 to 2023 were analyzed across the pre-war period (2017–2019), the transition year in which the war began in November (2020), the wartime period (2021–2022), and the early post-war recovery period (2023), when health and surveillance services had not yet been fully restored. Data were analysed using MS Excel and Arc GIS, while qualitative data were thematically examined. During the pre-war period (2017–2019), 8384 suspected rabies exposures and eight clinical rabies deaths were reported. In the 2020 transition year, 1881 exposures and two deaths were reported. During the wartime period (2021–2022), reported exposures declined to 501 while 49 deaths were recorded. In the early post-war recovery period (2023), 1481 exposures and 20 deaths were reported. Rabies deaths were notably higher in Central, North-western, and Southern zone of Tigray during the war while reporting completeness declined to below 12% in 2021. Qualitative data revealed significant disruption of rabies control were identified such as, decreased health-seeking behaviour, disruption of rabies prevention and control measures, and weak coordination among the One Health sectors. Reported clinical rabies deaths increased markedly during the wartime period and remained elevated during early post-war recovery, when healthcare, surveillance, PEP provision, and rabies-control services had not yet been fully restored. Strengthening surveillance, restoring PEP access, and enhancing One Health collaboration are essential.

Article.Title: Ononin suppresses proliferation and glycolysis in hepatocellular carcinoma via the EGFR/PI3K/AKT signaling pathway
Article.Authors: Zhang D.; Gong Z.; Li H.; Cai N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigated the inhibitory effect of Ononin on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and to elucidate its molecular mechanisms. CCK-8, EdU, colony formation, and Transwell assays were used to assess HCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. Western blotting and RT-qPCR analyzed protein and gene expression. Rescue experiments were conducted using EGFR knockdown, overexpression, and IGF-1. A xenograft mouse model evaluated the in vivo efficacy. Ononin dose-dependently suppressed the proliferation, colony formation, migration, and invasion of HCC cells. Mechanistically, Ononin treatment reduced the phosphorylation levels of EGFR, PI3K, and AKT, downregulated the expression of several key glycolytic enzymes including HK2 and PKM2, and concurrently decreased cellular glucose consumption, lactate production, and ATP generation. EGFR knockdown enhanced these inhibitory effects of Ononin, whereas EGFR overexpression or IGF-1-mediated pathway activation partially reversed them. In vivo experiments confirmed that Ononin significantly inhibited xenograft tumor growth and reduced the levels of p-EGFR, p-PI3K, p-AKT and glycolytic enzymes within the tumor tissues. Ononin may exert anti-HCC effects by inhibiting the EGFR/PI3K/AKT signaling pathway and subsequently interfering with downstream glycolytic metabolism. This study provides experimental evidence supporting Ononin as a potential candidate compound for HCC therapy.

Article.Title: TEPI: A transferable street-level framework for assessing urban thermal equity under data constraints
Article.Authors: Luo Y.; Luo J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Assessing urban thermal equity at the neighborhood level requires integrating physical exposure, demographic vulnerability, and adaptive capacity, yet many cities lack the longitudinal demographic data that established vulnerability frameworks assume. This paper presents the Thermal Equity and Population Index (TEPI), a diagnostic framework designed specifically for data-constrained contexts where only a single census cross-section, satellite-derived thermal variables, and current service-facility records are available. TEPI combines three dimensions—thermal exposure from Landsat imagery, population vulnerability from census age structure, and adaptive capacity from point-of-interest data—through a multiplicative composite that flags streets where multiple disadvantages co-occur. To evaluate the framework’s properties, we apply TEPI to 269 street-level units in Beijing and 74 in Shenzhen across three observation years (2015, 2020, and 2025), test its structural sensitivity against three alternative aggregation schemes, decompose its internal composition through OLS and GWR, and assess its cross-city transferability using 108 streets in Shanghai. Rank correlations between the baseline multiplicative specification and the alternative formulations exceed 0.97, and quintile overlap for the highest-burden streets ranges from 0.84 to 1.00, indicating that priority identification is robust to aggregation design. The transferability test shows strong ranking consistency (Pearson r > 0.90) but limited absolute portability (transferred R² = 0.22–0.26), establishing that TEPI is better suited as a comparative screening tool than as a plug-in prediction model. The framework also reveals a substantive pattern: in Beijing, mean TEPI declined over the decade while the Gini coefficient rose from 0.26 to 0.31 and Moran’s I increased from 0.29 to 0.39, demonstrating that average improvement in thermal equity can coexist with widening spatial inequality. TEPI provides a transparent, replicable screening tool for street-level thermal equity assessment in cities where comprehensive longitudinal social data are unavailable, while its documented structural and transferability properties help practitioners judge where the framework can and cannot be applied.

Article.Title: Cybersecurity for sustainable product performance through management quality, innovation intensity, and board risk oversight
Article.Authors: Arhinful R.; Mensah L.; Gyamfi B.
Article.Abstract: Cybersecurity plays a critical role in protecting digital systems and enabling organizations to deliver reliable, innovative, and sustainable products. Effective cybersecurity regulations strengthen product functionality and support long-term organizational resilience. This study explores the impact of cybersecurity on sustainable product performance and analyzes the moderating effects of management quality, innovation intensity, and board risk oversight. Using purposive sampling with predefined selection criteria, the study analyzes 25 years of data (2000–2025) from 482 non-financial firms listed on the London Stock Exchange, obtained from the Bloomberg database. Diagnostic test results require the application of advanced estimation techniques, including the Common Correlated Effects Mean Group (CCEMG), Augmented Mean Group (AMG), and two-step difference Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) estimators. The findings indicate a positive and statistically significant relationship between cybersecurity and sustainable product performance. Management quality, innovation intensity, and board risk oversight significantly and positively moderate this relationship, strengthening the relationship between cybersecurity and sustainable product performance. The results suggest that firms should strengthen cybersecurity frameworks to protect digital assets, improve product outcomes, support innovation, ensure regulatory compliance, and enhance long-term competitiveness and sustainability.

Article.Title: Optimizing metro and BRT transfer design in Isfahan using passenger generalized cost and ant colony optimization
Article.Authors: Nakhaie N.; Naderan A.; Afandizadeh Zargari S.; Rahimi H.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study presents a revised framework for screening and optimizing local Metro and BRT transfer connections in Isfahan using a state-separated passenger network, fixed-OD evaluation, explicit transfer screening, and ant-colony-based search. The formulation prevents implicit intermodal switching and holds the OD matrix constant between baseline and intervention networks, thereby separating modeled network-design effects from demand regeneration. Because the available empirical demand information does not provide a complete observed spatial OD matrix, the gravity deterrence coefficient is treated as a sensitivity parameter rather than as an empirically calibrated behavioral coefficient. Coordinate and network screening retained 29 feasible transfer candidates. Candidate 22, a 249.2 m pedestrian connection, produced the largest modeled improvement in the central case. System passenger generalized cost decreased from 6,265,519.636 to 6,258,241.797 passenger-min, a reduction of 7,277.839 passenger-min (0.116157%). Exhaustive evaluation of all 406 candidate pairs and targeted triple screening found no additional benefit beyond the best single link. I-ACO, standard ACO, and greedy search identified the same one-link solution, although the fast benchmark does not establish statistical superiority of any stochastic algorithm. Given the small system-wide effect and limitations in observed OD validation, route-choice behavior, and service-parameter calibration, the result is interpreted as a localized model-based screening outcome that requires empirical and site-level validation before implementation.

Article.Title: Proof carrying agent actions enable verifiable licensing of language model tool use
Article.Authors: Kadyrbek N.; Mansurova M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract LLM agents increasingly call tools and take irreversible actions, yet the reasoning that licenses an action is rarely checked before execution. We present Proof-Carrying Agent Actions (PCAA) : each governed action carries a typed Action Certificate that a planner-independent checker must accept before execution. A trusted execution shim derives the obligation set and the irreversibility classification from an authoritative tool contract and binds the certificate to the exact invocation with a canonical SHA-256 commitment. The checker compares that context with the certificate, re-derives typed support (proof, belief, hypothesis, contingency, conflict, or no-progress), and validates formula-level inference rules. Irreversible actions require Proof for every declared licensing obligation. The checker accepts the two valid certificates and rejects all fifteen unsafe certificates in a semantic battery; four additional structural cases confirm rejection of argument substitution, precondition omission, and risk-flag downgrade. A microbenchmark of a three-obligation payment certificate measures 53.7 μs median and 65.7 μs p95 for construction, checking, serialization, and buffered local persistence. A stateful guardrail with the same certified-state predicate matches PCAA on safety; PCAA’s distinct contribution is a typed, replayable decision artifact. Guarantees are relative to trusted tool contracts: PCAA checks their use, not their real-world semantic correctness.

Article.Title: Rapid response of choroidal thickness to outdoor light exposure in children
Article.Authors: Yu Z.; He J.; Lin Z.; Luo Z.; Jiang Y.; Wu H.; Wen L.; Yang Z.; Lan W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The objective of this study was to explore the rapid changes in choroidal thickness across a wide area of the eye after exposure to intense outdoor light in children.Thirty-five Chinese participants aged between 7 and 15 years old were allowed to acclimate to indoor light (300 lx, “normal light”) for 30 min and then exposed to bright outdoor light (10,000–20,000 lx, “bright light”) for 30 min. Choroidal thickness was measured by optical coherence tomography at five timepoints (completion of the acclimation to normal light and at 2, 5, 15, and 30 min after the completion of outdoor bright light exposure). All post-exposure measurements were obtained after participants had finished the full 30-min outdoor exposure and returned indoors. All experimental data were collected from 8 to 10:00 am. Choroidal thicknesses in each of the nine Early Treatment of Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) macular regions were compared between before and after bright light exposure and among these regions. At 2 min after bright light exposure, the choroidal thicknesses of the ETDRS 1-mm zone, the temporal and nasal quadrants of the ETDRS 3-mm zone, and the temporal quadrant of the ETDRS 6-mm zone decreased significantly compared with the baseline measurements. At 5 min, the same was found in all quadrants of the ETDRS regions. At 15 min, the same was found in all except for the superior quadrant of the ETDRS 6-mm zone and the temporal quadrant of the ETDRS 3-mm zone. After 30 min, the same was found in the superior quadrant of the ETDRS 3-mm zone. These findings indicate that exposure to intense outdoor light resulted in rapid and unexpected thinning of the choroid in children over the short term.

Article.Title: A dia-PASEF workflow improves proteome coverage and quantitative performance in repeated-measures analysis of cervicovaginal fluid from a preconception cohort (EARLY-PREG)
Article.Authors: Hernandez M.; Saldivia P.; Latapiat V.; Antilef B.; Nourdin G.; Castro F.; Vargas C.; Koch E.
Article.Abstract: Cervicovaginal fluid (CVF) represents a valuable source of molecular information reflecting time-dependent proteomic changes across the menstrual cycle. However, the large-scale discovery of CVF biomarkers remains challenging because of limitations in the sensitivity, reproducibility, and data completeness of mass spectrometry-based workflows, particularly within repeated-measures longitudinal study designs. Here, we evaluated a standardised data-independent acquisition (DIA)-based proteomics workflow (dia-PASEF) for longitudinal proteomic analysis of serial CVF samples collected across an ovulation-anchored seven-day window (d0-d6) from a prospective preconception cohort (EARLY-PREG). The performance of this dia-PASEF approach was compared with that of a dda-FracOffline strategy. Across the time window, 2,817 quantifiable proteins were detected with dda-FracOffline, whereas 4,229 quantifiable proteins were detected with dia-PASEF, with mean coefficients of variation of 9.37 ± 1.75% and 5.27 ± 0.68%, respectively. Using day 0 (ovulation) as a reference for day-to-day comparisons, more differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) were identified with dia-PASEF than with dda-FracOffline across pairwise comparisons (952–1,116 DEPs for dia-PASEF versus 161–460 DEPs for dda-FracOffline). Pathway analyses demonstrated broader biological coverage with dia-PASEF. In conclusion, dia-PASEF is a sensitive and reproducible approach for longitudinal repeated-measures proteomic analysis of CVF. This method is adaptable to other biofluids and supports the investigation of time-dependent molecular signatures and associated biological pathways under physiologically relevant conditions in female reproductive system research.

Article.Title: On the possibility of deep seabed permafrost to occupy Ca. 7 million km2 in the Arctic Ocean
Article.Authors: Dobiński W.; Saito K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Arctic Ocean (AO) shelf permafrost is the most popular and best-known type of subsea permafrost. Genetically, it is analogous to the ordinary subaerial permafrost. Today, the following types of subsea permafrost are also known: i) ice-bearing sediment layers formed from porewater freshening of terrestrial origins, ii) thermokarst lake taliks refreezing under cryotic seabed conditions, iii) bottom-fast ice preserving permafrost due to efficient heat conduction from atmosphere-ice-sediment coupling in winter, and iv) similar permafrost aggradation processes occurring beneath small islands and spits evolving with sediment dynamics. Here, we propose another type of marine permafrost: a deep seabed permafrost (DSP) underlying AO bottom sediments in a cryotic but not frozen state because of salty, supercooled seawater. Primary calculations indicate that the area of DSP deeper than 150 m may reach about 7.0 million km 2 , with the contacting seawater temperature ranging from − 2.5 °C to 0 °C. The formation and persistence of DSP or, almost equivalently, the negative-temperature regime of the AO seawater at the deeper layers may have begun at the Pliocene–Pleistocene border, ca. 3.5–2.4 Ma ago.

Article.Title: Positive-unlabeled graph ranking for assembly-center-oriented resilience-green sustainability evaluation of China Railway Express node cities
Article.Authors: Wang W.; Zhang K.
Article.Abstract: China Railway Express (CR Express) has become an important rail-based logistics corridor for improving Eurasian connectivity, regional openness, and sustainable freight organization. However, evaluating its node cities remains challenging because assembly-center labels are incomplete, city performance is network-dependent, and logistics development is increasingly shaped by resilience and green-sustainability requirements. This study proposes a positive-unlabeled graph ranking framework for CR Express node-city evaluation. The framework integrates statistical indicators, logistics operation variables, railway logistics relation structures, ecological governance indicators, and policy-text semantic representations. Existing assembly centers are treated as observed policy-designation positive anchors, while other node cities are modeled as unlabeled samples rather than negative cases. Accordingly, the model output is interpreted as relative assembly-center-oriented planning suitability under the observed operational, network, resilience, green-sustainability, and policy characteristics rather than as a causal estimate or a probability of future official designation. To reduce post-treatment information leakage, both ex-ante validation using 2011–2019 data and current assessment using 2011–2023 data are conducted. Experiments on 33 CR Express node cities show that the proposed model achieves an NDCG@5 of 0.932 ± 0.025, with auxiliary AUC and macro-F1 values of 0.948 ± 0.015 and 0.875 ± 0.021, respectively. Changsha, Wuhan, Jinan, Shenyang, and Hefei are identified as unlabeled cities with relatively high model-based planning suitability. The results indicate that railway logistics node evaluation benefits from jointly modeling incomplete labels, composite logistics relations, operational resilience, policy semantics, and green-sustainability constraints.

Article.Title: Investigation of the crystal structures and electronic features for trivalent praseodymium doped KY(WO4)2 crystal: a theoretical study
Article.Authors: Zhang D.; Jiang Z.; Wang J.; Kong P.; Xu Y.; Ju M.
Article.Abstract: Potassium yttrium tungstate (KY(WO 4 ) 2 ) doped with rare-earth ions exhibits efficient continuous laser activities in the near-infrared spectrum, suggesting its great potential as the new-generation of laser crystals. In this work, we report the structural evolution of KY(WO 4 ) 2 doped with Pr 3+ using the CALYPSO structure search method in combination with first-principles calculations. A novel structure of KY(WO 4 ) 2 :Pr crystal with P 2 space group is identified for the first time. The impurity Pr 3+ ion can naturally occupy the Y 3+ site in the host crystal. The doping concentration of Pr 3+ for the system is equal to 12.5%. The electronic features of the KY(WO 4 ) 2 :Pr is calculated by LDA + U method. The results show a gap of 3.106 eV in the electronic band structure, which implies that the KY(WO 4 ) 2 :Pr possesses a semiconductor character. The analysis of the partial density of states demonstrates that the introducing of impurity Pr 3+ ion into KY(WO 4 ) 2 leads to a transformation of the electronic states. Based on the electron localization functions and Bader charge analyses, the ionic bonding character of Pr–O in KY(WO 4 ) 2 :Pr structure are clarified. The absorption coefficient spectra of the KY(WO 4 ) 2 :Pr indicate a blue shift toward higher energies. These results could not only enrich the fundamental understanding on the structural evolution of rare-earth doped KY(WO 4 ) 2 , but also provide information for designing the new laser materials.

Article.Title: Genetic variation and trait selection in ryegrass (Lolium multiflorum Lam.) across dry and rainy seasons in Peru
Article.Authors: Bobadilla L.; Castillo M.; Matias F.; Ortiz R.; Castillo G.; Tenorio-Galvez O.; Altamirano-Tantalean M.; Vásquez H.
Article.Abstract: Ryegrass ( Lolium multiflorum Lam.) is an important forage species in Peruvian livestock micro-watersheds; however, increasing climatic variability underscores the need to identify promising germplasm for breeding programs. Twenty-three accessions, including three widely used checks in the area, were evaluated under an augmented block design across three livestock micro-watersheds in the Amazonian Andes of Peru, using mixed linear models with REML/BLUP for the dry and rainy seasons and a combined analysis. The study aimed to determine variance components, Cullis heritability, and correlations across fifteen selected traits, as well as to identify promising accessions through the Elston index and principal component analysis for plant height, basal coverage area, dry matter concentration, crude protein, neutral detergent fiber, and in vitro digestibility. The results revealed significant variation among accessions for most agronomic traits, with the exception of stem diameter. Heritability for in vitro digestibility was zero during the dry season. Plant height, basal coverage area, spike and spikelets number exhibited high heritability (> 0.60) in both seasons, while crude protein showed moderate heritability (dry season = 0.54; rainy season = 0.51). Dry matter concentration displayed high heritability during the rainy season and moderate heritability during the dry season. Principal component analysis indicated greater phenotypic differentiation during the rainy season (73.6%) than during the dry season (58.1%). Furthermore, the Elston index identified LM20 as the most promising accession in the combined analysis and dry season, outperforming the checks. LM5 showed performance comparable to the check varieties, whereas LM18 exhibited the most balanced profile during the rainy season. These findings provide a quantitative foundation for future breeding programs targeting the conditions of the Amazonian Andes.

Article.Title: Growth, hydrogen production, and community dynamics of Rhodopseudomonas palustris cultivated in forward osmosis-concentrated municipal sewage
Article.Authors: Nagashima S.; Nomura Y.; Nonaka I.; Sonoda K.; Nagashima K.; Sato T.; Kitashima M.; Hidaka T.; Fujiwara T.; Inoue K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Municipal sewage represents a sustainable resource for biohydrogen production; however, its direct application is hindered by low concentrations of soluble organic matter and elevated ammonium levels, which suppress nitrogenase activity. In this study, municipal sewage was concentrated approximately 20-fold by forward osmosis (FO) prior to cultivation experiments. While FO substantially increased organic matter availability, the resulting alkaline concentrate inhibited growth and hydrogen evolution. Adjustment of the medium to near-neutral pH restored robust growth and enabled detectable hydrogen production. Full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing enabled improved taxonomic resolution of microbial dynamics. Anaerobic FO concentration enriched for fermentative taxa, specifically Campylobacteria (> 50%), while subsequent illuminated cultivation demonstrated that Rhodopseudomonas palustris was able to utilize dissolved organics (27.1–34.7% relative abundance), as confirmed by specific high-fidelity read counts. These results demonstrate that the integrated FO–PNSB process effectively transforms municipal sewage into a concentrated substrate capable of supporting biohydrogen production without external organic supplementation.

Article.Title: Latent profiles of physical and psychological symptoms in patients following rectal cancer surgery: Associated demographic and clinical characteristics
Article.Authors: Hu C.; Chen Y.; Li Y.; Yang C.; Hu T.; Liu H.; Yang L.; Wang Q.; Song Z.; Niu N.
Article.Abstract: Patients following rectal cancer surgery frequently experience multiple co-occurring physical and psychological symptoms; however, heterogeneity in the patterns and severity of these symptoms remains insufficiently understood. This study aimed to identify latent profiles of postoperative physical and psychological symptoms and examine the demographic and clinical characteristics associated with profile membership. A single-center cross-sectional study was conducted among 272 patients who underwent rectal cancer surgery at a tertiary hospital in Nanjing, China, between November 2023 and March 2024. Participants were recruited using convenience sampling. Symptom assessments were performed during postoperative hospitalization, generally on postoperative day 7 after patients’ clinical conditions had stabilized. Fatigue, pain, sleep disturbance, anxiety, and depression were assessed using the Chinese versions of the corresponding Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System short forms, and raw scores were converted into standardized T-scores. Latent profile models containing one to six profiles were estimated using Mplus 8.3. Demographic and clinical characteristics were compared across profiles using univariate analyses, and factors associated with profile membership were examined using multinomial logistic regression in SPSS 26.0. Three distinct profiles were identified: a low physical and psychological symptom burden profile comprising 141 patients (Profile 1, 51.8%), an intermediate physical and psychological symptom burden profile comprising 81 patients (Profile 2, 29.8%), and an intermediate physical-high psychological symptom burden profile comprising 50 patients (Profile 3, 18.4%). Compared with Profile 1, patients with a stoma, preoperative intestinal symptoms, or a first hospitalization for rectal cancer were more likely to be assigned to Profile 2, whereas patients who had received neoadjuvant therapy were less likely to be assigned to Profile 2. Compared with Profile 1, self-paying patients, patients with a family history of rectal cancer, patients with a stoma, and those hospitalized for the first time were more likely to be assigned to Profile 3. Patients undergoing laparoscopic surgery were less likely to be assigned to Profile 3 than those undergoing other surgical approaches. These findings indicate substantial heterogeneity in physical and psychological symptoms during the early postoperative period among patients with rectal cancer. Concurrent assessment of physical and psychological symptoms, together with sociodemographic and clinical characteristics, may help healthcare professionals identify patients who could benefit from more comprehensive symptom assessment and individualized postoperative management.

Article.Title: An explainable AI framework using wearable IMU-based motion sensing for estimating and explaining motor skill improvement in school-based Baduanjin education
Article.Authors: Li J.; Zhang Y.; Sun Y.
Article.Abstract: Estimation of individual skill improvement within specific school-based physical education units remains methodologically underdeveloped, with existing approaches typically lacking external validation and interpretability. Because the full model incorporates training-load features aggregated across the same temporal window as the outcome, it is epistemologically retrospective; readers should not interpret it as a prospectively deployable prediction tool. This study aimed at developing and externally validating an explainable machine learning ensemble to retrospectively explain and estimate standardized skill gain (Δz) in Baduanjin (eight-section brocade) qigong, a mandatory traditional martial arts skill in the Chinese national PE curriculum, among students from four schools ( n = 727). A stacking meta-learner composed of five candidate algorithms, including XGBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, LASSO, and MLP, was trained using biomechanical, psycho-cognitive, and semester-aggregated training-load features obtained from the development cohort (Schools A + B, n = 486) and then validated against two geographically independent but regionally situated cohorts (Schools C + D, n = 241). Because the training-load features were aggregated across the full 16-week semester, the model functions as a retrospective semester-level estimation framework rather than a prospective early-warning tool. The model yielded an external validation R² of 0.691 (95% CI: 0.661–0.718), with robust subgroup performance across gender, initial skill quartiles, and sport types. SHAP-based interpretability analysis identified exercise self-efficacy as the highest-ranking modifiable feature in model-derived importance, with its predictive contribution predominantly associated with the training-response component rather than baseline level. A baseline-only sensitivity model excluding semester-aggregated training-load variables retained moderate external validity (R² = 0.573), indicating that prospective application at semester onset is feasible in principle but at substantially reduced precision. These findings suggest that, within this dataset and model specification, psycho-cognitive features contributed more strongly to model estimations than biomechanical features.
