Article.Title: Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of novel 4,5-diaryl-1,2,3-thiadiazole derivatives: anticancer activity and molecular docking studies
Article.Authors: Ghasemi M.; Ghadbeigi S.; Ostad S.; Kalhor H.; Amini M.
Article.Abstract: Malignancies remain a major global health challenge. Microtubule-targeting agents (MTAs) have emerged as a significant therapeutic class, effectively suppressing cancer cell proliferation by interfering with the normal dynamics of microtubules. Combretastatin, particularly combretastatin A-4, is a natural compound with anti-angiogenic and anticancer properties that interacts with the colchicine-binding site at the α/β-tubulin interface. A new series of 4,5-diaryl-1,2,3-thiadiazole analogues, based on the SAR of combretastatin A-4, were designed and synthesized. The anticancer activity of the synthesized derivatives was assessed on human gastric adenocarcinoma (AGS), human colorectal adenocarcinoma (HT-29), human breast adenocarcinoma (MCF-7), and mouse embryo fibroblast (NIH3T3) cell lines by MTT assay, along with known drugs (paclitaxel and doxorubicin) as references. Among the synthesized compounds, compound 5g demonstrated the highest cytotoxic activity in most of the tested cell lines and exhibited superior cytotoxic effects against AGS and HT-29 cells compared with paclitaxel. Doxorubicin remained the most potent compound across all tested cell lines. Particularly, compounds 5d , 5f , and 5h exhibited high safety toward normal NIH-3T3 cells (IC₅₀ > 600 µM), with selective activity against some cancer cell lines. Docking studies showed that all compounds were predicted to bind within the colchicine-binding site of tubulin with more favorable predicted scores than combretastatin A-4. Molecular dynamics supported complex stability, with 5i showing greater stability than 5d . Compound 5g emerged as a promising potential tubulin inhibitor, requiring further experimental and in vivo validation.

Article.Title: Phytochemical screening as an inhibitor of β-lactamases to overcome the carbapenem-resistant of Klebsiella pneumoniae
Article.Authors: Azmal M.; Paul J.; Shohan M.; Haque A.; Mrinmoy M.; Talukder O.; Mishu M.; Mia M.; Ghosh A.
Article.Abstract: The global emergence of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) poses a major health challenge due to its resistance to carbapenem antibiotics, such as imipenem and meropenem, primarily mediated by β-lactamases, including NDM and KPC carbapenemases. This study aimed to identify phytochemicals predicted to interact with NDM-1 and KPC-2 β-lactamases, and to determine whether the most promising candidate could enhance carbapenem activity against CRKP. A library of phytochemicals selected for their reported potential to inhibit resistance enzymes rather than for direct antimicrobial activity was screened through ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, Toxicity) profiling, followed by molecular docking against β-lactamase enzymes. Quercetin, eriodictyol, and luteolin showed favorable docking scores of − 9.1, − 8.32, and − 8.66 kcal/mol against KPC-2 and − 8.74, − 8.72, and − 8.73 kcal/mol against NDM-1, respectively. Molecular dynamics simulations were performed to evaluate the conformational behavior of the quercetin–NDM-1 and quercetin–KPC-2 complexes. In vitro assays showed that quercetin, at 2 µg/µL, enhanced the antibacterial activity of carbapenems against a CRKP isolate carrying both bla NDM-1 and bla KPC-2. However, these assays did not directly assess β-lactamase inhibition. These findings support the preliminary potential of quercetin as a carbapenem adjuvant, while the mechanism underlying the observed potentiation requires biochemical confirmation.

Article.Title: Reservoir eutrophication prediction with explainable framework integrating temporal convolutional networks and bidirectional sequence modeling
Article.Authors: Sharafi M.; Behmanesh J.; Rezaverdinejad V.; Samadianfard S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of total nitrogen (TN) concentration in dam reservoirs is recognized as one of the significant challenges in water resources management. In this regard, the present study, to develop an intelligent and robust modeling framework, introduced the integrated model, which consists of the combination of the improved variational mode decomposition algorithm (IVMD), the attention mechanism-based temporal convolutional neural network (AttTCN), the bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU), and the grasshopper optimization algorithm (GOA), which is used to predict the total nitrogen of Mahabad Dam. The results of this study suggest that the proposed framework has a significant advantage over conventional models, as the analysis of the indices indicated that, with each layer of complexity added to the model, prediction accuracy improved significantly. The 80% reduction in the mean absolute error value from the basic BiGRU model to the final IVMD-GOA-AttTCN-BiGRU model, along with the improvement of Willmott’s index of agreement from 0.75 to 0.99, confirms the superiority of the proposed integrated approach. This significant improvement in accuracy demonstrated that the intelligent combination of data preprocessing, an attention mechanism, and hyperparameter optimization can yield models with greater reliability in water quality prediction. The use of interaction terms such as turbidity × pH corrected the systematic bias of the model, which is hydrologically justified. In summary, the proposed framework shows promise as an accurate prediction tool and provides a useful analytical basis for better understanding water quality dynamics in the Mahabad reservoir, subject to further validation with larger datasets.

Article.Title: Adipose tissue-derived stromal vascular fraction and xanthosine independently promote canine surgical wound healing
Article.Authors: Grewal N.; Sharma V.; Sharma P.; Sethi R.; Kumar A.; Nameirakpam U.; Sherley J.; Choudhary R.
Article.Abstract: Adipose tissue-derived stromal vascular fraction (SVF) and cultured stem cells have been applied in the treatment of wound healing and many other diseases of dogs. However, these cells are difficult to obtain in large amounts for therapy. Xanthosine (Xs) is a nucleoside that has been shown to increase stem cell numbers when used in vivo. This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy of SVF along with xanthosine (Xs) on surgical wounds in dogs. Randomly, but age-matched, 24 dogs were allocated into four groups: a control group and three treatment groups (SVF, Xs, and SVF + Xs). The therapeutic effects of treatments on wound healing were assessed at days 7 and 14 by gross observation, photographs, and by measuring levels of angiogenic (VEGF) and inflammatory (TGFB1) markers. Results showed that SVF enhanced hair regrowth by day 7 and maintained its effects at day 14 (p ≤ 0.05). Compared to control, wound redness was visibly low in Xs, SVF, and SVF + Xs groups on day 7, and further reduced on day 14 (p ≤ 0.05) in the Xs group. VEGF expression peaked at day 7 in the SVF group (p ≤ 0.001), whereas the Xs group showed delayed elevation at day 14 (p ≤ 0.01). TGFB1 was mildly upregulated in SVF at day 14 (p ≤ 0.001) and strongly upregulated ( p < 0.001) in the Xs group. A combination of SVF and Xs demonstrated improved wound healing, maintaining a controlled range of TGFB1, which facilitates enhanced tissue regeneration. In conclusion, both SVF and Xs can independently promote wound healing. Furthermore, the combined SVF + Xs therapy was shown to modulate the surgical wound healing process in dogs.

Article.Title: A longitudinal study of perceived employability and psychological health among Chinese college students
Article.Authors: Zhang Y.; Liu B.; Liu J.
Article.Abstract: The decline in psychological well-being among students in higher education has been increasingly documented. Despite growing recognition of perceived employability as consequential for employees’ well-being in the labor market, less is known regarding its specific association with psychological health among college students approaching the school-to-work transition. This study examined the association between perceived employability and psychological distress among Chinese college students and further explored the variation of this association by gender and family economic condition. Data were from three consecutive waves of the Panel Survey of Chinese University Students (PSCUS, 2020–2022), tracking 2552 students from their first to their third year. Fixed-effects models were employed to account for unobserved time-invariant characteristics. Interaction models were used to investigate how gender and family economic condition would shape the relationship between perceived employability and psychological distress. Results showed that higher perceived employability was significantly associated with lower psychological distress. Interaction models further indicated that the association was primarily driven by female and economically disadvantaged students. These findings highlight the need for policymakers to develop career-related programs that enhance students’ perceived employability as a vital means of promoting the psychological well‑being of college students, with particular attention to vulnerable socioeconomic and gender groups.

Article.Title: Integrative chemometric profiling of biochemical composition, fatty acids, minerals, organic acids, and carbohydrates in wild olive (Olea europaea L. subsp. oleaster) genotypes for quality-oriented selection
Article.Authors: Tunç Y.
Article.Abstract: This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the compositional diversity of wild olive ( Olea europaea L. subsp. oleaster ) genotypes through an integrated analysis of biochemical traits, fatty acid composition, mineral elements, organic acids, and carbohydrates, and to identify superior genotypes using chemometric approaches. A total of 150 genotypes collected from the Eastern Mediterranean region were analyzed, revealing significant genotypic variation across all evaluated traits ( p < 0.05). Wild olive genotypes exhibited striking biochemical diversity, with up to 2.4-fold variation in total phenolics, 20-fold variation in flavonoids, and substantial differences in fatty acid profiles (oleic acid: 55–83%). Genotype-specific differences in antioxidant capacity, tocopherol content, and primary metabolites were also observed. Multivariate analysis identified ‘Oleaster-39’, ‘Oleaster-133’, and ‘Oleaster-140’ as promising genotypes based on their favorable oil quality- and stability-related compositional profiles. Overall, the findings reveal extensive biochemical and metabolic diversity within wild olive germplasm and demonstrate the value of integrated compositional profiling and chemometric analysis for identifying promising genotypes with desirable quality attributes. However, the identified superior genotypes should be further validated across different environments, growing seasons, maturity stages, and clonal propagation trials before their large-scale utilization in breeding programs. The selected genotypes may serve as promising germplasm resources for future breeding and conservation efforts targeting improved oil quality, nutritional value, and functional properties, pending further genetic and multi-environment validation.

Article.Title: A multifunctional Tb3+–salicylic acid hydrazide phosphor for anti-counterfeiting, forensic fingerprint visualization, and biological applications
Article.Authors: Nasser H.; Abdelrhman E.; Saif M.; Kamal R.; Shebl M.; Fouad R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract A novel terbium(III) complex, Tb(SAH) , derived from salicylic acid hydrazide ( SAH ), was successfully synthesized and fully characterized. Stoichiometric analysis confirmed a 1:2 metal-to-ligand ratio. X-ray diffraction and microscopic studies revealed a polycrystalline structure with micro- and nanodomain features. Photoluminescence investigations demonstrated intense monochromatic emissions: blue for SAH and green for Tb(SAH) , with relatively long excited-state lifetimes in dimethylformamide (DMF), solid state, and polymeric matrices (PVA (polyvinyl alcohol), PMMA (polymethyl methacrylate), and silica xerogel). An efficient ligand-to-metal energy transfer mechanism under ultraviolet (UV) excitation was confirmed, indicating a strong antenna effect responsible for enhanced luminescence. Both SAH and Tb(SAH) were successfully applied in latent fingerprint visualization, clearly resolving level I–III ridge details on diverse porous, non-porous, and multicolored substrates. Additionally, transparent luminescent security inks prepared from the compounds exhibited excellent storage stability and humidity resistance, highlighting their suitability for anti-counterfeiting applications. Biological evaluation revealed that Tb(SAH) exhibits significantly greater in vitro cytotoxicity against the hepatocellular carcinoma (HepG-2) cell line than the free ligand. Significant antioxidant activity was observed for SAH and Tb(SAH) (IC 50 = 0.38 and 0.78 μM, respectively), surpassing ascorbic acid. The Tb(SAH) complex also exhibited improved antidiabetic activity (IC 50 = 14 μg/mL) compared with SAH (IC 50 = 44 μg/mL), with potency comparable to that of acarbose (IC 50 = 35 μg/mL). Antimicrobial studies indicated marked enhancement upon Tb 3 ⁺ coordination, particularly against Staphylococcus aureus . Molecular docking against DNA gyrase B (PDB ID: 6TCK) supported strong binding interactions, corroborating the experimental antimicrobial findings.

Article.Title: Hybrid rank fusion of a group-token transformer with gradient boosting improves detection of evasive and novel-family malware
Article.Authors: Tawfik M.; Al-sellami B.; Heshmat M.; Fathi I.; Shaban W.
Article.Abstract: Static machine-learning malware detectors report near-perfect closed-set accuracy, but the malware that matters operationally is the malware that slips past detection and the malware that belongs to families never seen in training. We study both on three longitudinal benchmarks: EMBER2024 (3.2 M Windows, .NET, APK, ELF and PDF files, 52 training weeks and 12 test weeks, plus a challenge set of 6,315 files that evaded every antivirus engine at first sight), LAMDA (1.0 M Android applications, 2013–2025, with an IID/NEAR/FAR drift protocol) and BODMAS (134 K PE files, 2019–2020, monthly evaluation). We make five contributions. First, an operational evaluation protocol: true-positive rate at 1% and 0.1% false-positive rate, challenge-set detection at fixed FPR, novel-family, singleton and low-consensus strata, week-by-week and year-by-year drift, thresholds calibrated on time-aware validation data, and paired-bootstrap confidence intervals. Second, three new deep architectures for static feature vectors, trained jointly across formats: GT-Former, a Group-Token Transformer over the semantic feature groups, whose hyper-parameters are tuned with Optuna on a time-aware validation window and which is evaluated with five seeds on every benchmark; FR-MoE, a format-routed mixture of experts; and ProtoCon-Net, a prototype classifier with family-aware supervised-contrastive training. Third, three metadata-driven objectives that use antivirus consensus and family labels at training time only (a consensus-aware margin loss, a consensus-regression head and a family-adversarial gradient-reversal head), with full ablations. Fourth, explainability with SHAP and CLS attention. Fifth, benchmark-hygiene findings, including that the public EMBER2024 release lists every record twice. The results are sobering and useful: the EMBER2024 LightGBM benchmark remains the strongest single model at strict operating points (Win32: 90.0% TPR at 0.1% FPR versus \(88.1 \pm 0.4\) % for the tuned GT-Former over five seeds), and the metadata-driven objectives do not pay for themselves: on LAMDA, with five seeds per variant, no objective activated on its own is distinguishable from the plain model, and only their combination degrades the strictest operating point (NEAR TPR at 0.1% FPR falls from \(10.1 \pm 2.3\) % to \(4.4 \pm 3.7\) %). The seed spread on this benchmark is large enough that single-seed ablations are unreliable, which we regard as a methodological finding in itself. The deep models are nevertheless complementary to gradient boosting: a rank average of the tuned GT-Former and LightGBM raises Win32 challenge-set detection from 63.2% to 68.8% at 1% FPR (95% CI \(+4.7\) to \(+6.6\) points), novel-family detection from 89.1% to 91.8% (CI \(+1.5\) to \(+3.9\) ) and test TPR at 1% FPR from 96.8% to 97.3%, with significant challenge-set gains also on .NET ( \(+1.6\) ) and APK ( \(+3.9\) ); on LAMDA a rank average of an MLP and LightGBM raises far-future (2018–2025) detection from 40.5% to 54.4% at 1% FPR (CI \(+13.7\) to \(+14.0\) ) and singleton-family detection from 34.6% to 53.3% when the threshold is calibrated on the benign files of the test region ; under a threshold fixed on validation data and applied unchanged, twelve years of drift move both models far below their nominal budget and the advantage falls to 0.1 points (Section Retrospective and deployment operating points), which we regard as the honest deployment figure; and on BODMAS the tuned GT-Former/LightGBM fusion matches LightGBM at 1% FPR (99.85%) and improves detection at 0.1% FPR (98.9% to 99.5%) and novel-family detection at 0.1% FPR (94.7% to 97.1%). SHAP shows why the benchmark misses evasive files: its strongest evidence is structural sloppiness (suspicious section flags, missing signatures), and evasive malware is exactly the malware that avoids it. Code, de-duplication masks, models and all score files are released.

Article.Title: Effects of a hand sanitizer formulation on upper respiratory symptoms and work restrictions: a double-blind household cluster-randomized controlled trial
Article.Authors: Yamanaka N.; Mizukoshi K.; Asaoka K.; Morikawa T.; Nakashima Y.; Hayase A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Conventional hand sanitizers provide immediate but short-lived bactericidal and virucidal effects, necessitating their frequent use to reduce contact transmission. This double-blind, parallel-group, cluster-randomized controlled trial evaluated the effect of repeated use of the study formulation. Healthy employees and their cohabiting family members (clusters) were assigned to use either the study formulation or a commercially available 79.7% ethanol-based sanitizer 5–10 times daily for 72 days (December 2023–February 2024). The primary outcome was the cumulative incidence of upper respiratory symptoms, defined as fever ≥ 37.8 °C with cough, sore throat, and/or nasal discharge. Among the 568 participants (study-formulation group, 285; ethanol-based sanitizer group, 283) across 417 clusters, upper respiratory symptoms occurred in 35 and 58 participants, respectively. The study-formulation group showed significantly lower risk (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.37–0.89, P = 0.013; approximately 40% lower cumulative incidence), with fewer illness-related work restrictions. Adverse events were infrequent and unrelated to the study interventions. Repeated use of the study formulation was well tolerated and associated with fewer upper respiratory symptoms and work restrictions than ethanol-based sanitizers.

Article.Title: Biomechanical comparison of stand-alone interbody bone grafting versus cage implantation in ULIF: a finite element analysis
Article.Authors: Xu C.; Wu Y.; Tang J.
Article.Abstract: The biomechanical differences between stand-alone interbody bone grafting and cage implantation in unilateral biportal endoscopic lumbar interbody fusion (ULIF) remain unclear. This study compared the two strategies in a patient-specific finite element model and assessed model credibility using geometric reconstruction, published range-of-motion (ROM) data, and mesh convergence analysis. A subject-specific L4-L5 finite element model with residual Grade I spondylolisthesis was used to compare bilateral pedicle-screw fixation with stand-alone interbody impaction bone grafting versus porous titanium cage implantation. A 500-N axial preload and a 7.5-N m pure moment were applied independently in six directions. Segmental ROM, model-reported stiffness, and von Mises stresses in the interbody constructs, screw-rod system, and endplates were evaluated. ROM was calculated from the relative rotation of L4 with respect to L5. In addition to comparison with published cadaveric ROM, five characteristic mesh sizes (4.0, 3.5, 3.0, 2.5, and 2.0 mm) were assessed under identical model settings. Cage implantation reduced ROM by 30.4%-37.3% across the six loading directions and produced higher model-reported stiffness than stand-alone bone grafting. The cage model also generated higher localized stresses in the interbody construct and screw-rod system; during right lateral bending, screw and rod stresses increased by 556.6% and 361.2%, respectively. Endplate effects were direction- and level-dependent, including a 326.7% increase at the L4 inferior endplate during right lateral bending. In the mesh study, the monitored von Mises stresses for 4.0-, 3.5-, 3.0-, 2.5-, and 2.0-mm meshes were 6.820, 11.499, 9.849, 9.865, and 9.840 MPa, respectively; the maximum pairwise difference among meshes of 3.0 mm or finer was 0.25%. Within the prescribed loading, material, contact, and mesh assumptions of this single patient-specific model, cage implantation provided greater immediate segmental restraint but generated a less favorable localized stress environment in selected implant and endplate regions. Stand-alone bone grafting produced greater motion but a more diffuse load-transfer pattern. The mesh convergence results support numerical stability of the reported stress solution but do not constitute independent biological validation. These computational findings are hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as proof of clinical superiority, long-term safety, or a direct basis for patient selection.

Article.Title: Research on the mechanical properties of loess solidified via enzyme induced calcium carbonate precipitation (EICP)
Article.Authors: Chen S.; Liu J.; Li G.; Chen C.
Article.Abstract: Loess has a special structure that usually leads to collapse, disintegration and dissolution, and easily triggers slope instability, foundation settlement, and ground fissure. As a recently developed soil stabilization method, high efficiency is widely recognized as a fundamental characteristic of Enzyme-induced calcium carbonate precipitation (EICP). Cost-effectiveness and environmental friendliness render it a proper method for fine-grained soil solidification. Based on the orthogonal test method, the role of enzyme concentration within the generalization processes was assessed via specifically designed enzyme-induced carbonate precipitation (EICP) tests. The experiments mandated precise regulation of cementing solution and skim milk powder concentrations, pH value, standing time on the CaCO 3 content, and determining the optimal mineralization condition. Furthermore, to quantify the mechanical performance, the unconfined compressive strength (UCS) tests were conducted to considering the effect of dry density ( ρ d ), cementing solution content (CSC), enzyme to cementation solution ratio (ECSR), and Na-Mt content ( C N ). The test results indicated that the optimal EICP mineralization condition was that the soybean powder concentration was 200 g/L, cementing solution concentration was 1.50 mol/L, skimmed milk powder concentration was 2 g/L, pH was 7, and standing time was 120 h. For the EICP treated loess, the stress-strain curve is divisible into a slow ascending stage, a fast-growing stage, a slow growth stage, and an attenuation decrease stage. A maximum UCS was achieved at the dry density of 1.55 g/cm 3 with 4% Na-Mt content, following a trend of increasing strength concurrent with rises in both initial dry density and Na-Mt concentration. The UCS exhibited the trend of increased firstly and decreased subsequently with the increase of CSC and decreasing of ECSR, it reaches the maximum when the CSC was 14% and the ECSR was 2:3. The research results can promote the practical implementation of EICP method in foundation treatment.

Article.Title: Operationalizing biological interpretability in health-related visual stimuli using multimodal artificial intelligence as standardized non-human raters
Article.Authors: Ayman D.; Ozkan H.; Ayman D.; Tanriverdi O.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Evaluation and assessment research in health communication requires structured, construct-based approaches for interpreting visual materials. This study introduces the Asclepius Biological Interpretability Scale, developed through a two-stage modified Delphi process (a joint image-and-item panel followed by an independent item-only panel) grounded in the Biopsychosocial Model and Visual Literacy Theory, and examines whether multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) systems can reproducibly apply this framework relative to internally generated human reference scores. Six artworks (four health-themed and two controls) were evaluated by three multimodal AI models and four researchers (internal human reference) using a standardized protocol with independent researcher-operated accounts, memory-isolation procedures, repeated assessments over two days, and the final 20-item scale. Because Image Type varied across only six stimuli, health-themed versus control differences were summarized at the image level (Cohen’s d), human–AI differences were summarized descriptively at the rater level, and reproducibility was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Spearman correlations. Within this development image set, AI-generated scores were descriptively higher for health-themed than for control images on the three biomedical subscales (image-level Cohen’s d = 0.91–1.38) but not on Non-Medical Interpretability (d = 0.49); with four health-themed and two control images, these differences were not statistically significant ( p = 0.19–0.60). Reproducibility across researcher-operated accounts was excellent for the three biomedical subscales (ICC = 0.90–0.97) and moderate for Non-Medical Interpretability (ICC = 0.57), whereas agreement across assessment days was poor (ICC = 0.04–0.46). The four researchers’ internal reference scores were higher than the AI-generated scores on the biomedical subscales for health-themed images (mean differences 1.41–1.96 points) and lower on Non-Medical Interpretability (− 2.02 to − 2.19 points). These findings provide preliminary methodological evidence that multimodal AI can reproducibly apply a structured interpretability framework to controlled visual stimuli. Although day-to-day stability and the Non-Medical Interpretability subscale, which showed substantial internal-consistency problems, require further refinement, the results support the feasibility of using AI as standardized non-human raters within controlled methodological settings. Broader validation using authentic health communication materials and independent external human raters remains necessary.

Article.Title: An integrated ArcGIS Python toolbox for SCS-CN event runoff estimation and flood screening in data-scarce Ethiopian basins
Article.Authors: Yasin K.; Yuya B.; Muir F.; Hebden S.
Article.Abstract: Flood early warning in data-scarce regions is constrained by sparse gauging and limited modelling capacity. We present an integrated ArcGIS Python toolbox automating SCS-CN event runoff estimation, from curve number generation and per-event antecedent moisture classification through to threshold calibration, evaluated in a semi-arid Ethiopian basin. From four quality-controlled stations, 587 rainfall events (2010–2023) were extracted; 98.6% occurred under dry antecedent conditions, corroborated by ERA5-Land soil moisture ( p < 0.001). Evaluation used nineteen documented flood windows from disaster databases and official reports, since discharge records are unavailable. Basin-mean runoff discriminated documented floods with AUC = 0.91 (95% CI 0.83–0.97; Cohen’s d = 2.6), rising to 0.95 for the eleven events triggered within the gauged area. A calibrated 1.25 mm runoff threshold detected thirteen of sixteen floods with approximately 62% fewer false alarms than the regional 30 mm rainfall criterion at equal detection, confirmed out-of-sample by temporal hold-out. Discrimination proved robust to the initial abstraction ratio and ± 10% curve number bias, whereas absolute thresholds were not, making local calibration essential. Limited gauge coverage and a small documented-event sample are acknowledged limitations, quantified via satellite-precipitation comparison and bootstrap intervals. The toolbox provides a transparent, reproducible flood-screening framework for data-scarce semi-arid basins.

Article.Title: Coupled U–Pb geochronology of inherited and detrital zircon in the Iberian Massif: insights into its deep structure and geodynamic evolution
Article.Authors: Cachapuz P.; Chichorro M.; Bento dos Santos T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The combined use of detrital and inherited zircon U-Pb age spectra provides new insights into the crustal evolution of the Iberian Massif as part of the North Gondwana margin. In the Ossa–Morena Zone (OMZ), Ediacaran detrital zircon populations are dominated by Pan‑African ages, whereas inherited zircons overwhelmingly record Cadomian signatures, implying that Cadomian crust remained largely unexposed during the Cadomian event itself. Late-Rift igneous units of the Central Iberian Zone (CIZ) and Galicia-Trás-os-Montes Zone (GTMZ) Parautochthon present significant inherited Cambrian signals, indicating a shared cryptic infracrustal magmatism which is extensively exposed in OMZ (Early Rift and Main Rift events). Carboniferous zircon records reveal sharp contrasts. OMZ Carboniferous detrital zircon patterns reflect syn-sedimentary magmatism and active erosion of Famennian-Tournaisian igneous bodies. There is a notable lack of zircons from older magmatic sources, implying limited exposure of Cambrian and Ediacaran basement during Carboniferous basin formation. Inherited zircons from OMZ Carboniferous rocks display typical Cadomian–Pan-African and Cambrian peaks, but also unexpected signals from South Portuguese Zone (SPZ) magmatism, suggesting deep mixing of OMZ–SPZ sources. In contrast, CIZ Carboniferous sediments are dominated by Precambrian sources, showing weak Variscan signals, even though inherited zircons reveal clear signatures of Cadomian–Pan‑African, Rift‑to‑Drift, and Variscan events. Because detrital zircon spectra are strongly influenced by crustal exposure, inherited zircon patterns provide a more robust record of deep crustal processes and allow a more precise determination of the climax ages of major orogenic events in the Iberian Massif.

Article.Title: Compartment-specific soluble immune profiles associated with preterm birth, perinatal death, and low birthweight in pregnant individuals living with HIV
Article.Authors: Corry J.; Zotova N.; Tabala M.; Kasindi F.; Massamba B.; Babakazo P.; Manuzak J.; Liyanage N.; Funderburg N.; Yotebieng M.; Kwiek J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Pregnant people living with human immunodeficiency virus (PPLWH) face elevated risks of preterm birth (PTB), perinatal death (PND), and low birthweight (LBW). While antiretroviral therapy (ART) effectively suppresses viral load, it neither prevents these adverse pregnancy outcomes nor resolves underlying inflammation. Since circulating maternal markers may not fully capture local immune dysregulation, this observational cohort study identified compartmentalized immune factors associated with adverse outcomes. We analyzed 45 immune factors in paired maternal, placental, and cord plasma from 118 ART-treated PPLWH in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo. Among these pregnancies, 30% resulted in PTB, 9% in PND, and 8% in LBW. Compared to term births, PTB ( n = 35) was associated with discordant spatio-temporal signaling of T-cell-associated chemokines CCL20, CXCL9, and CXCL10. PND ( n = 10) correlated with the largest inflammatory signature and was associated with factors that signal neutrophil recruitment and activation, including CXCL1, CXCL5, MPO and S100A8/A9. LBW ( n = 9) was associated with higher concentrations of inflammatory factors at enrollment IL-18 and S100A8/A9, alongside increased postdelivery and postpartum SAA. In ART-treated PPLWH, distinct outcomes were characterized by time- and compartment-specific immune pathways. These pathways may provide mechanistic insights into adverse birth outcomes in PPLWH and highlight potential compartment-specific biomarkers for risk stratification.

Article.Title: Field-based vital-capacity changes following a 12-week athletic skills model-informed curriculum: a retrospective non-randomised comparison in one Chinese primary school
Article.Authors: Zhu J.; Bu Y.; Zhao M.; Xu L.; Zhu L.
Article.Abstract: This retrospective non-randomised comparison examined routine school records from 1,214 students in Grades 2–6 (607 per condition) in one urban public primary school in Southwest China. Curriculum allocation occurred at the level of 28 pre-existing physical-education (PE) teaching groups (14 per condition): 14 groups followed a 12-week Athletic Skills Model (ASM)-informed curriculum and 14 followed routine PE. Mean field-based vital-capacity scores increased by 114.86 ± 254.83 mL in the ASM condition and 45.66 ± 257.91 mL in the routine-PE comparison, corresponding to an unadjusted descriptive between-condition difference in change of 69.20 mL. Individual-level adjusted analyses produced point estimates of similar direction, but student-to-PE-group identifiers were unavailable and empirical cluster-adjusted inference could not be performed. The exact device make/model, manufacturer-specified accuracy, formal test–retest reliability, and testing time of day were not recoverable from archived records. Accordingly, the observed contrast should be interpreted as an exploratory descriptive signal rather than evidence of curriculum effectiveness or confirmed physiological improvement. Prospective multi-school studies should preserve group identifiers, pre-specify analyses, independently monitor fidelity and intensity, and use standardised or blinded outcome assessment.

Article.Title: A hybrid deep learning and circuit-theoretic framework for module-level fault diagnosis and localization in pv arrays
Article.Authors: Abdullah A.; Sadeh J.
Article.Abstract: The rapid global expansion of photovoltaic (PV) systems necessitates robust fault management for minimizing operational downtime and enhancing system reliability under fluctuating environmental conditions. Current diagnostic methodologies, however, often lack the necessary robustness and generalizability to data-driven scenarios or to differentiate sub-string faults under dynamic partial shading conditions (PSCs) and realistic irradiance gradients. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a hybrid diagnostic framework that is evaluated under non-ideal operating conditions, specifically accounting for realistic cable and busbar resistances. The proposed pipeline decouples discrete topological classification from continuous physics-based estimation. In the first stage, a hybrid CNN-BiLSTM-Attention architecture classifies the topology, resolving ambiguities in electrical profiles at critical healthy-to-PSC boundaries with 99.76% classification accuracy. Subsequently, the identified topology is fed into a deterministic circuit-analysis framework to perform module-level fault localization. The proposed non-iterative mathematical core directly maps terminal metrics ( \(\:{V}_{i}^{cal}\) , V 1PVi , I i and I Endi ) to physical fault location, achieving a discrimination accuracy of 100% for variable-resistance line-to-ground (LG) faults and 100% for zero-resistance line-to-line (ILL) faults within solid intra-string bypass configurations. Furthermore, due to the analytical nature of the localization equations, the proposed technique remains invariant to fluctuations in irradiance and temperature, provided these environmental parameters are uniform across the PV array. Simulation results on a 3 × 5 PV array confirm that the proposed approach sustains high diagnostic accuracy even under measurement noise and parameter uncertainty, demonstrating its promise as a robust diagnostic method for PV arrays.

Article.Title: Enhancing lavender productivity in sandy soils using combined applications of poultry manure extract, humic acid, and dry yeast
Article.Authors: Aboud F.; Abd-Rabbu H.; Khalid K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Lavender is an important aromatic plant valued for its essential oil in pharmaceutical and food applications; however, its cultivation and productivity are frequently restricted by the unfavorable properties of Egypt’s sandy soils. Organic biostimulants offer a sustainable approach to improving lavender productivity under sandy soil conditions. Therefore, this study investigated the effects of poultry manure extract, humic acid and dry yeast, applied individually or in combination, on the productivity of lavender plants grown in sandy soil. Two harvests were conducted at 75 and 195 days after transplanting, and the data were analyzed using two-ways (ANOVA-2). At the second harvest, the combined application of poultry manure extract, humic acid, and dry yeast reached its highest values for all measured traits, including fresh and dry weights (243.3 and 65.4 g plant -1 ), chlorophyll a , chlorophyll b , and carotenoids (1.1, 0.9, and 0.8 mg g -1 , respectively), essential oil content (2.6%), essential oil yield (1.7 g plant -1 ), eucalyptol (276.2 mg plant -1 ), carbohydrate (25.5%), protein (17.8%), phenol (22.2 mg g⁻¹), flavonoid (9.9 mg g -1 ), and free-radical scavenging activity (61.3%) and N uptake; while, the maximum values of NP and k (2.9, 0.8 and 1.1%); P and K uptake values (0.7 and 0.9 g plant -1 , respectively) were recorded with the same treatment at the first harvest. Chemical fertilizers at the first harvest recorded the lowest values for all measured traits, including fresh and dry weights ( 102 and 25 g plant -1 ), chlorophyll a , chlorophyll b , and carotenoids (0,3, 0.2, and 0.3 mg g -1 , respectively), essential oil content (1.1%), essential oil yield (0.3 g plant -1 ), eucalyptol (213.2 mg plant -1 ), carbohydrate (18.5%), protein (14.7%), phenol (14.9 mg g⁻¹), flavonoid (5.8 mg g -1 ), and free-radical scavenging activity (44.3%), as well as N, P, and K contents (1.7%, 0.2%, and 0.3%, respectively), N,P and K uptakes (0.4, 0.1 and 0.1 g g -1 , respectively). The use of organic biostimulants in reclaimed sandy soils effectively enhances lavender productivity and quality, offering a sustainable approach for cultivation in arid regions while increasing its value as a natural source of food and pharmaceutical products.

Article.Title: A MATLAB-based AI-IoT simulation framework for LSTM-driven smart solar irrigation and renewable energy management
Article.Authors: Mashaly A.; El-Sehiemy R.; Elgohary M.
Article.Abstract: Smart irrigation offers a great avenue for better water use efficiency, and farming sustainability. However, most of the studies conducted so far tend to concentrate on the monitoring systems and platforms of the Internet of Things (IoT) or on the prediction models based on Artificial Intelligence (AI) (but not on both). To address this gap, this research study proposes an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Internet of Things (IoT) system to predict the water consumption requirements and control the energy produced by a PV system along with a battery State of Charge (SOC) management system, Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm, adaptive pump-speed control, and conceptual IoT communication architecture. A dataset of real environmental data from the NASA POWER database was used to test the framework for Egypt’s New Delta region. The LSTM model was able to classify the irrigation pump operating states with an accuracy of 96.11%, a recall of 0.9820, a precision of 0.9100, and an F1-score of 0.9446. It had a better performance than the two models, Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) when compared and robustness testing with various independent training runs showed a stable performance in predicting. An estimated annual water-saving rate of 28.57% was obtained relative to the assumed conventional fixed-schedule baseline, while motor energy use was reduced by 74.74% through adaptive pump-speed control. A sensitivity analysis was also performed, showing that the model was stable to moderate variations in environmental and operating conditions. Combined, these findings suggest that the use of AI-based modelling for renewable energy management in the context of an irrigation simulation model built in MATLAB could be a valuable asset in improving irrigation efficiency and lowering water and energy use, which is a promising start for future implementation of hardware versions of intelligent, solar-powered irrigation devices.

Article.Title: Concentrations of uranium, cesium, and rubidium in drinking water and Monte Carlo–based age-specific health risk assessment of uranium
Article.Authors: Mohammadpour A.; Golmohammadi A.; Dehbandi R.; Shahrokh M.; Hashemi H.; Gharaghani M.
Article.Abstract: Freshwater is essential for life and the economy, yet its scarcity is worsening due to population growth, climate change, and unequal distribution. This study measures concentrations of uranium (U), cesium (Cs), and rubidium (Rb) in drinking water supplies across Arsanjan County, Iran, and evaluated the associated carcinogenic and non-carcinogenic risks of U using Monte Carlo simulation. Uranium concentrations were consistently below EPA and WHO guideline of 30 µg/L. The maximum Cs concentration was 0.63 µg/L, whereas Rb concentrations ranged from 2.04 to 13.94 µg/L. Non-carcinogenic risk assessment using Monte Carlo simulation showed that hazard quotient (HQ) values were below 1 for all age groups, indicating no significant adverse health effects. Children under 2 years had the highest hazard quotient values (HQ median = 0.028; HQ 5th–95th centile range = 0.012–0.061). The estimated excess lifetime cancer morbidity risk (ELCR median :1.58 × 10 − 6 ) and excess lifetime cancer mortality risk (ELCR median :1.02 × 10 − 6 ) were estimated across all age groups. Sensitivity analysis further revealed that U concentration was the most influential factor for both non-carcinogenic risk and excess cancer risk. Although concentrations were below WHO and EPA guideline values, the findings highlight the importance of continued monitoring and incorporating age specific vulnerability into regional water quality management strategies.

Article.Title: Ancient terrestrial forests reborn as modern marine ecosystems under shifting sea levels
Article.Authors: Lebrato M.; Shannon J.; Russell T.; Jordan A.; Jije-Goncalves M.; da Graça M.; Caputo M.; Lillis A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sea-level rise and coastal erosion can submerge terrestrial carbon-rich landscapes, yet the ecological fate and climate significance of such relict coastal carbon deposits remain largely unknown. We report the discovery of submerged tropical peat reefs in the shallow coastal waters of the Bazaruto Archipelago, Mozambique; a legacy of ancient coastal forests now transformed into benthic marine habitats. Radiocarbon ( 14 C) dating reveals ages spanning ~ 300 to ~ 5000 years BP, indicating mid- to late-Holocene origins as coastal peat swamps and forests subsequently submerged by rising seas. Sampled peat material contains up to 40% organic carbon by dry weight, indicating an organic-rich legacy coastal peat substrate rather than a quantified habitat-scale or areal carbon stock, and δ 12 C values around − 27‰ confirm a predominantly terrestrial carbon plant origin. Peat reefs are shallower and exhibit greater variability in physicochemical, environmental, and physical properties than adjacent hard scleractinian coral reefs, influencing biological structure and habitat function. Biodiversity surveys across multiple scales (benthic quadrats, invertebrate, small fish, and megafauna transects) showed that these carbon-rich peat reefs support a biodiverse and distinctive assemblage of marine life, significantly different from nearby coral reefs. The peat substrate is colonized by diverse sessile and mobile invertebrates providing structural complexity for fish communities and as nursery habitat, with richness comparable to coral reef ecosystems. Importantly, overlapping communities highlight ecological connectivity across reef types (41 and 44 small fish/megafauna shared species), even as habitat composition differs markedly. Unlike adjacent hard coral reefs dominated by reef-building corals, peat reefs host no living corals and are instead characterized by seagrass, macroalgae and sponges using the peat as substrate, creating a carbon-rich system, and a detritus-based food web. Our findings illustrate how ancient terrestrial systems can persist and support contemporary ecological functions, and the ecological “reinvention” of Earth’s landscapes under shifting sea levels. This underscores how substrate-driven ecosystem baselines shape biodiversity, calling for the inclusion of such relict ecosystems in emerging coastal habitat mapping, conservation frameworks, and legacy coastal carbon assessments.

Article.Title: A phase 2, randomised, placebo-controlled study to evaluate once-daily oral Travelan for the prevention of Travellers’ diarrhoea
Article.Authors: Casey J.; Poly F.; Porter C.; Lamberti K.; Beckett C.; Islam D.; Laird R.; Isidean S.; Testa K.; Chapman V.; Shindler A.; Franks A.; Tennant S.; Chen W.; Al-Ibrahim M.; Kanellos J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study evaluated once-daily oral dosing of Travelan (IMM-124E), a bovine polyclonal antibody product, for prevention of Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC)-induced diarrhoea. In this randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial using an ETEC-controlled human infection model, 60 healthy subjects received 1200mg Travelan or placebo once-daily for 7 days. Two days after dosing commenced, subjects were challenged with ETEC strain H10407 and monitored for diarrhoeal symptoms. Travelan was well-tolerated with a significant 50% reduction in ETEC challenge-related adverse events ( P = 0.0001). Efficacy outcomes did not reach statistical significance, largely due to a lower-than-expected placebo attack rate (33% vs 70% anticipated); however a strong trend consistently favoured Travelan, including a 40% reduction in moderate-to-severe diarrhoea (primary endpoint), a 50% reduction in severe diarrhoea, a 44% reduction in all diarrhoea, and a 71% reduction in early antibiotic use. These findings were supported by significant reductions in intestinal inflammation markers (faecal myeloperoxidase and calprotectin) 4 days post-challenge. Significantly lower O78 lipopolysaccharide IgA and IgG titers were observed but over 80% of subjects in each group seroconverted by day 15–29, indicating Travelan did not hinder immunity to ETEC. Although underpowered and limiting definitive interpretation, these findings suggest a potential protective effect of once-daily Travelan, warranting further investigation in a larger adequately powered trial.

Article.Title: Active abdominal compression-decompression cardiopulmonary resuscitation versus standard cardiopulmonary resuscitation for adult cardiac arrest: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Article.Authors: Cui R.; Liu X.; Yang X.; Huang Y.; Yang X.; Zhang S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the clinical efficacy and safety of active abdominal compression-decompression cardiopulmonary resuscitation (AACD-CPR) compared with standard cardiopulmonary resuscitation (STD-CPR) in patients experiencing cardiac arrest (CA). We systematically searched 11 databases from inception to November 2025, including eight randomized controlled trials. Outcomes assessed included return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), survival, neurological outcomes, hemodynamic parameters, arterial blood gas parameters, oxygen metabolism parameters, and adverse events. Data analysis was performed using RevMan 5.4.1, and certainty of evidence was assessed using the grading of recommendations assessment, development, and evaluation (GRADE) framework. AACD-CPR was associated with a higher return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) rate and a shorter time to ROSC, whereas 2-week survival did not differ significantly between groups. Several exploratory physiological outcomes showed between-group differences, but substantial heterogeneity was present and many estimates were based on only two or three small studies. Rib fractures were less frequent in two studies, while evidence for other adverse events was limited. The certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate. AACD-CPR represents a promising resuscitation approach, but the current evidence remains insufficient to support broader clinical implementation. Larger multicenter randomized trials involving diverse populations are needed to evaluate clinically meaningful outcomes, including survival to hospital discharge, long-term survival, neurologically favorable survival, and procedure-related safety.

Article.Title: Energy consumption analysis of three-layer prefabricated composite wall panels: an integrated forming process and comparative study with cast-in-situ construction
Article.Authors: Xu J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The construction industry accounts for approximately 36% of global final energy use and 39% of energy-related CO₂ emissions. Prefabricated construction offers potential energy savings during the construction phase, yet limited studies quantify actual on-site energy consumption for multi-layer composite prefabricated wall panels. This study develops an integrated forming process for a three-layer prefabricated composite wall panel (structural concrete—EPS insulation—recycled aggregate concrete outer layer) and compares its construction-phase energy consumption, thermal performance, and mechanical properties against traditional cast-in-situ methods over a 100 m 2 wall area. Experimental results show that the proposed panel achieves a compressive strength of 36.2 MPa for the structural layer and 28.5 MPa for the outer RAC layer, a flexural strength of 4.8 MPa for the full composite panel, and a thermal transmittance (U-value) of 0.38 W/m 2 K at the center-of-panel region, which is 86% lower than conventional 200 mm solid concrete walls (2.8 W/m 2 K) and 85% lower than 150 mm solid prefabricated walls without insulation (2.5 W/m 2 K). It should be noted that these comparisons are made against uninsulated solid walls; when a conventional 200 mm concrete wall is equipped with 80 mm external EPS insulation, its U-value reaches 0.32 W/m 2 K, which is lower than the composite panel's 0.38 W/m 2 K. The U-value of 0.38 W/m 2 K meets the recommended threshold for passive house standards (U ≤ 0.4 W/m 2 K) at the panel center, though it should be emphasized that this applies only to the center-of-panel region and does not account for thermal bridging at panel edges, joints, and connections to structural elements. Construction energy monitoring indicates that prefabricated systems reduce on-site energy consumption by 27.3% (from 46.9 to 34.1 kWh/m 2 ), primarily due to lower machinery energy (59.6% reduction) and curing energy (45.2% reduction). However, a sensitivity analysis reveals that if electric curing blankets were not used in the cast-in-situ wall (i.e., natural curing at ambient temperature), the energy savings would be substantially smaller—approximately 7.3% instead of 27.3%—indicating that the reported savings are partly dependent on the curing method employed. Transportation energy increases by 68.8% (from 3.2 to 5.4 kWh/m 2 ), but the absolute increase (2.2 kWh/m 2 ) is outweighed by on-site savings (13.6 kWh/m 2 ). The integrated forming process eliminates secondary insulation installation, reducing labor time by 40% and avoiding thermal bridging at the panel center. Energy distribution analysis shows that factory production accounts for 42.5% of total prefabricated construction energy, followed by on-site lifting (27.0%), transportation (15.8%), and joint filling and finishing (14.7%). A sensitivity analysis indicates that the break-even transportation distance, at which the on-site energy savings are offset by increased transportation energy, is approximately 320 km round trip. These findings support the adoption of multi-layer composite prefabricated wall panels for low-carbon construction and provide quantitative benchmarks for construction energy assessment.

Article.Title: Uncertainty-aware adaptive fusion with graceful degradation for trustworthy cervical cytology
Article.Authors: Chaabane S.; Bushnag A.; Oyouni A.; Massoudi W.; Abuzneid S.; Aluneizi S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Trustworthy cervical cancer screening requires not only accurate classification but also reliable estimation of predictive uncertainty to identify cases that should be referred to clinical experts. This study presents an uncertainty-aware deep learning framework that integrates an ensemble image encoder comprising ResNet50, DenseNet121, and EfficientNet-B0 with dedicated clinical and genomic encoders through an adaptive fusion mechanism. Modality-specific predictions are subsequently combined using a convex weighting scheme driven by predictive entropy estimated via Monte Carlo Dropout. As paired patient-level multimodal data were unavailable, clinical features were derived from an independent risk-factor cohort and genomic features were synthetically generated. The proposed framework serves as a proof-of-concept for uncertainty-guided multimodal fusion. When auxiliary modalities are uninformative, the framework automatically suppresses their influence, maintaining identical test-set predictions across all image-containing configurations, while a static equal-weight baseline reduced the AUC from 0.993 to 0.982. Evaluated on a combined SIPaKMeD and Herlev benchmark of 6,849 cervical-cell images, the framework attains an AUC-ROC of 0.993 (95% CI 0.988–0.997), 97.08% accuracy, 98.07% sensitivity, and 96.08% specificity, with well-calibrated probabilities (Brier 0.025; ECE 0.014). Cross-dataset transfer experiments revealed a notable generalisation gap, highlighting the need for external validation, while confidence-based selective prediction demonstrated the framework’s potential for human-in-the-loop triage.

Article.Title: CytoDNNEnsemble: combining cell-level and distribution-level representations for flow-cytometry classification
Article.Authors: Gniazdowski T.; Markowska-Kaczmar U.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Flow cytometry is a cornerstone diagnostic technique, but manual analysis is laborious, subjective, and prone to inter-operator variability. We propose a parameter-efficient deep ensemble model, CytoDNNEnsemble, for automated analysis of high-dimensional flow cytometry data. The architecture consists of two smaller, independent subnetworks that process blood samples from complementary global and local perspectives. This design reduces the reliance on expert gating, captures complex cellular patterns, and improves diagnostic consistency. Extensive experiments on relatively large real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of accuracy and robustness while keeping the parameter count low, highlighting its potential for clinical deployment.

Article.Title: Integrating multi-omics analysis reveals shared genetic architecture and spatial correlations between heart failure and osteoporosis
Article.Authors: Liu R.; Sun C.; Li Y.; Li J.; Jiang N.; Lu Y.; Yang G.; Tan Y.; Zhang F.; Meng C.; Xia X.; Liu Y.; Yang K.; Wang M.; Yu M.; Qi X.; Huang X.
Article.Abstract: Heart failure (HF) and osteoporosis (OP) are common age-related disorders with established epidemiological associations, yet their shared genetic architecture and molecular underpinnings remain poorly defined. We performed an integrative multi-omics analysis to elucidate genetic links between HF and OP. Polygenic overlap was quantified using the bivariate causal mixture model (MiXeR), while shared loci were mapped via conditional/conjunctional false discovery rate (cond/conjFDR) analysis. Transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) with MetaXcan, Bayesian colocalization (eCAVIAR, fastenloc), and tissue enrichment analyses were applied to identify candidate genes and regulatory contexts. Spatial mapping of disease-associated cells was conducted using Genetically informed spatial mapping of cells for complex traits (gsMap). MiXeR estimated that approximately 447 ± 114 variants had non-null effects on both traits, corresponding to 52% of the estimated non-null variant count for OP and 21% of that for HF. Despite this extensive polygenic overlap, the genome-wide genetic correlation was weakly negative (rg = -0.091, SE = 0.024, P = 1.07 × 10 − 4 ), and the estimated correlation of effect sizes within the shared non-null component was also negative (rho_beta = -0.295). Cond/conjFDR analysis identified five pleiotropic loci and three novel HF loci. TWAS and colocalization consistently prioritized HOXC6 as a shared transcriptomic candidate across multiple tissues. Spatial transcriptomic mapping using the E16.5 mouse embryonic reference indicated enrichment of HF-associated genetic signals in embryonic muscle regions and OP-associated signals in cartilage and cartilage-primordium regions, with GRB10 emerging as a shared candidate gene. Our study delineates a shared genetic architecture and distinct spatial correlations between HF and OP. HOXC6 and GRB10 were prioritized as candidate shared genes by transcriptomic colocalization and spatial mapping analyses, respectively. These findings generate testable hypotheses regarding potential regulatory links between cardiovascular and skeletal traits and highlight candidate genes and tissues for future functional validation.

Article.Title: Tribocatalytic degradation of cationic dyes using Na₀.₄K₀.₁Bi₀.₅TiO₃: influence of friction pair materials and reactive species
Article.Authors: Rahul N/A.; Rajeh S.; Alsaiari N.; Chauhan V.; Vaish R.; Kushwah H.; Amari A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study explores the tribocatalytic activity of cationic dyes (Rhodamine B (RhB) and Methylene Blue (MB)) using Na 0.4 K 0.1 Bi 0.5 TiO 3 ( NKBT) as a catalyst under various conditions. The degradation efficiencies of RhB, MB, and binary (RhB + MB) dyes were examined, revealing that RhB exhibited higher degradation (~ 90%) compared to MB (~ 44%) at 600 rpm over 360 min. However, in the binary dye system, MB degraded more (~ 53%) than RhB (~ 9%), contrary to the results of individual dye degradation. The observed results may be attributed to the steric hindrance caused by the planar structure of MB molecules, which interferes with the Coulombic attraction between RhB dye and the catalyst surface, thereby reducing the degradation efficiency of RhB dye. Kinetic analysis showed rate constants of 0.00684 min − 1 , 0.00142 min − 1 , 0.00022 min − 1 , and 0.00208 min − 1 for RhB, MB, binary RhB, and binary MB, respectively. The effect of different friction pairs on RhB dye degradation was studied using polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) disc (homemade) with glass, polypropylene (PP), and PTFE beakers. The PTFE beaker-PTFE disc pair showed the highest degradation (~ 93%), followed by PP-PTFE (~ 89%) and glass-PTFE (~ 77%) at 600 rpm over 180 min. Optimal RhB dye degradation (~ 96%) was achieved in the PTFE beaker at 1000 rpm within 120 min.

Article.Title: Characterisation of mycotoxin-producing Fusarium species associated with maize ear rot and its pathogenomics and mycotoxin gene profile
Article.Authors: Pallavi K.; Prasannakumar M.; Harish J.; Karan R.; Manjunatha C.; Devanna P.; Sarangi A.
Article.Abstract: Maize ear rot is a major constraint to maize production, causing yield losses, grain deterioration, and mycotoxin contamination. This study characterised the diversity, pathogenicity, mycotoxin-associated potential, and genomic features of Fusarium associated with maize ear rot in Karnataka, India. A total of 54 isolates were analysed using morphological, multilocus phylogenetic, pathogenicity, toxin-gene, and whole-genome approaches. Six Fusarium species were identified, with Fusarium verticillioides predominating (43 isolates; 79.63%). Most isolates exhibited high pathogenicity (> 75% disease severity), while tested representative isolates of F. verticillioides and F. graminearum reduced seed germination to 65% and 62%, respectively, and caused substantial stalk and ear rot symptoms. The predominance and pathogenicity of F. verticillioides were further associated with its fumonisin-related genetic potential, as FUM1 was detected in all 43 isolates, and LC–MS confirmed high fumonisin accumulation in kernels infected with the tested isolate. In contrast, the tested F. graminearum isolate contained trichothecene-associated genes, including NIV-associated TRI7 and TRI13 . Whole-genome sequencing of F. verticillioides PMER18 produced a ~ 40 Mb genome with 98.0% BUSCO completeness and identified putative pathogenicity-associated genes, CAZymes, transporters, and candidate effectors. Together, these findings integrate pathogen diversity, disease development, mycotoxin risk, and genomic features, providing a framework for risk assessment and integrated management of maize ear rot.

Article.Title: Simulation of servo control system for photovoltaic cleaning robot based on multi-motor synchronization and precise PWM control
Article.Authors: Shi Y.; Huang K.; Wang F.; Zhao F.; Wang K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The walking and cleaning modules of the photovoltaic cleaning robot rely on the cooperation of multiple motors; however, traditional control strategies are prone to issues such as asynchronous motor speeds and phase deviations under complex working conditions, leading to robot motion jamming and uneven cleaning performance. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a simulation of a servo control system for photovoltaic cleaning robots based on multi-motor synchronization and precise pulse-width modulation (PWM) control. A path tracking control strategy utilizing error components is introduced, in which the linear velocity and yaw rate of the robot are regulated by a proportional-integral (PI) controller and a proportional (P) controller, respectively, thereby achieving accurate tracking of the desired path. Precise PWM control is employed to adjust motor speed by varying the duty cycle of the DC pulse sequence. Experimental results show that under disturbance conditions, the deflection angle of the photovoltaic cleaning robot can return to the expected value of 0 rad. The time delay data for multi-motor synchronous control remain relatively low, fluctuating between 0.46 s and 1.43 s, demonstrating the system’s capability to effectively correct synchronization errors among motors.

Article.Title: DC-link-stress-aware DVR–supercapacitor scheme for voltage restoration and transient energy stabilization in PMSG wind turbines
Article.Authors: Nori A.; Abdulabbas A.; Saleh A.; Számel L.
Article.Abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG)-based wind energy conversion systems (WECSs) are known for their high efficiency and full-scale converter interface and are widely used in variable-speed wind-power applications. However, grid disturbances such as voltage sag and swell degrade terminal-voltage quality and impose transient stress on the shared DC-link. To improve voltage restoration while maintaining DC-link voltage stability, this paper proposes a grid-connected PMSG-based WECS configuration incorporating a dynamic voltage restorer (DVR) in conjunction with a supercapacitor energy storage system (SCES). The SCES is coupled to the shared DC-link through a bidirectional buck–boost DC–DC converter (BBBC) to provide fast transient-energy support, and the DVR is connected in series at the generator terminals to compensate for grid-voltage disturbances. The DVR is controlled using a DC-link-stress-aware deadbeat control strategy, while the SCES control is based on a PI controller synchronized with the GSC to regulate the common DC-link voltage and manage the supercapacitor charging and discharging process. The proposed DVR–SCES system is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink R2024a and evaluated under 20% and 50% voltage sag conditions, as well as a 20% voltage swell condition. In addition, a comparative assessment is carried out against D-STATCOM–SCES configurations rated at 3 MVAr and 6 MVAr. The proposed DVR–SCES scheme maintains the terminal voltage at approximately 1 p.u. for all considered disturbances. In contrast, the D-STATCOM–SCES configurations restore the terminal voltage only to 0.90–0.96 p.u. during the 20% voltage sag and 0.58–0.66 p.u. during the 50% voltage sag, depending on their ratings. During the 20% voltage swell, the maximum terminal voltage reaches 1.12 p.u. and 1.06 p.u. for the 3 MVAr and 6 MVAr D-STATCOM–SCES cases, respectively. Furthermore, the proposed scheme has a maximum output-current deviation of approximately 0.4% and a maximum peak-to-peak DC-link voltage deviation of 2.17%, while the D-STATCOM–SCES configurations have corresponding maximum deviations of 21.9% and 4.00%. Finally, the simplified, indicative cost–performance analysis suggests that the proposed DVR–SCES configuration provides a more favorable cost–performance tradeoff than the investigated D-STATCOM–SCES configurations.

Article.Title: An interpretable ANFIS-NSGA-II framework for evidence-stratified modular wearable risk fusion in elder-health monitoring
Article.Authors: Leonid T.; Londhe G.; Theivadas J.
Article.Abstract: Wearable health monitoring spans fall, cardiac, oxygenation, sleep, mobility, behavioural and long-horizon neurodegenerative indicators that arise from different sensors, labels and time scales. This study presents an evidence-stratified Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System optimized with the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-II (ANFIS-NSGA-II) that fuses module-specific actionability scores into an interpretable monitoring-priority index (MPI) without treating heterogeneous risks as equivalent disease probabilities. Because no synchronized seven-modality older-adult cohort was available, the complete fusion mechanism is evaluated in a controlled subject-indexed synthetic benchmark of 240 subjects and 2,880 observation windows, while real datasets provide module-level evidence and prospective validation targets. The full 3 7 antecedent grid is reduced to a training-derived 64-rule library by an explicitly specified ranking criterion, and the Pareto-selected policy retains 20 active rules. On 48 held-out subjects the frozen policy achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.914 (95% participant-cluster bootstrap CI 0.871–0.948), area under the precision–recall curve (AUPRC) 0.888 (0.824–0.935), sensitivity 0.868 (0.779–0.935) and specificity 0.751 (0.639–0.832). Paired participant-cluster comparisons show that logistic regression, a generalized additive model, a random forest and a quality-weighted mean all reach discrimination that is statistically indistinguishable from the proposed model after correction for multiple comparisons; the proposed model is significantly better only than a max-risk rule. Ablations show that the 17 mandatory anchor rules alone are significantly worse than the selected policy (AUROC 0.861), that relaxing the anchor requirement lets the optimizer reach significantly higher discrimination with only 8 rules, and that quality-weighted marginalization is preferable to zero-filling but significantly inferior to simple imputation when signal quality is uniformly high, the alternatives converging only when quality is genuinely variable. A scenario analysis that varies interaction strength, interaction identity, label noise, target functional family and the share of escalation propensity driven by unobserved latent state quantifies how much of the reported performance reflects recovery of the authors' own generating mechanism: without label noise the target is deterministic conditional on the seven scores and the generator's subject-level offset, the model attains 72–98% of the oracle discrimination computed from the true propensity, and it exceeds logistic regression in only 1 of 14 scenarios. The contribution is therefore an auditable, reproducible fusion and policy-selection architecture rather than a gain in predictive accuracy, and every quantitative result is a proof-of-concept methodological finding on synthetic data. Prospective synchronized multimodal validation with clinician evaluation remains necessary before any clinical use.

Article.Title: Association between baseline hypertension and cisplatin-induced nephrotoxicity in patients receiving short hydration
Article.Authors: Saito Y.; Kobayashi M.; Sakamoto T.; Takekuma Y.; Sakakibara-Konishi J.; Shimizu Y.; Kinoshita I.; Sugawara M.
Article.Abstract: Cisplatin (CDDP)-induced nephrotoxicity (CIN) commonly arises during CDDP-based therapy. Hypertension (HT) has been identified as a potential risk factor for CIN, although other possible covariates cannot be excluded, without sufficient CIN prophylaxis. This study evaluated the association of baseline HT and CIN, utilizing the short hydration method, considered the most advanced CIN prevention approach, in a real-world setting. Patients with thoracic cancer undergoing CDDP (≥ 75 mg/m 2 )-based treatment with the short hydration method ( n = 244) were retrospectively evaluated. Patients were classified into the HT group, including patients requiring pharmacotherapy at baseline, and a control group without HT. CIN was observed in 18.0% of patients in the HT group across all treatment cycles, significantly higher than the control group (6.0%, P = 0.008), meeting the primary endpoint. The maximum changes in serum creatinine levels and creatinine clearance from baseline were notably worse in the HT group compared to the control group ( P = 0.009 and P = 0.0496, respectively). Similar outcomes were observed in the propensity score-matched cohort. Even after excluding patients concurrently administered bevacizumab, consistent results were obtained. In summary, patients with baseline HT complications are at high risk of developing CIN with short hydration.

Article.Title: Assessment of content and quality of thyroid nodule management information on Chinese video-sharing platforms
Article.Authors: Li R.; Zhou Z.; Zhu Y.; Xu J.; Li M.; Wang X.; Wang G.; Ma W.
Article.Abstract: Abstract As short videos have emerged as a promising medium for disseminating health information, the quality and reliability of thyroid nodule (TN) management content on video platforms require critical evaluation. On November 12, 2025, the top 120 videos returned on each platform using the prespecified composite search were screened. Ultimately, 151 eligible videos were included in this cross-sectional study (Bilibili, n = 76; TikTok, n = 75). Five distinct quality-related domains were assessed: overall educational quality and usefulness, information reliability and balance, source transparency and accountability, patient understandability and actionability, and coverage of selected TN-specific management elements, using the Global Quality Score (GQS), modified DISCERN, Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) benchmark criteria, Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT-A/V), and the study-specific Video Integrity 5 checklist, respectively. Spearman’s rank correlation was used to analyze relationships between video characteristics and quality-related scores. Videos on Bilibili were significantly longer than those on TikTok (median, 2.46 vs. 1.35 min; p < 0.001). In unadjusted comparisons, TikTok videos had higher GQS, JAMA, and Video Integrity 5 checklist scores than Bilibili videos; however, none of the six predefined quality-related outcomes remained significantly associated with platform after adjustment for uploader category, publication age, and video duration. Videos uploaded by medical professionals scored higher than those uploaded by non-professionals in overall educational quality, information reliability and balance, source transparency, and TN-specific management coverage. A large proportion of videos lacked key transparency indicators, with 88.74% lacking literature citations and 82.78% lacking conflict-of-interest disclosures. Associations between audience engagement metrics and quality-related scores were generally weak and inconsistent across platforms. Although 76.82% of the sampled videos were uploaded by medical professionals, limitations in source transparency, balance of presentation, and coverage of key TN management elements remained. These findings may inform future efforts to improve the transparency and clinical contextualization of patient-facing TN management information on short-video platforms.

Article.Title: An adaptive behavioural zero-trust security framework with proactive cryptographic caching for continuous authentication in 5G non-terrestrial networks
Article.Authors: Sankeerthana N.; Dakshayini M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract 5G non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) are key to future global broadband and military communications, but their high latency and dynamic topologies require security approaches beyond perimeter defences and static authentication. To overcome these vulnerabilities, we propose an adaptive behavioural zero trust security framework (BZTSF) for continuous 5G NTN authentication. Our method continuously evaluates node trustworthiness using network signal information processed by an isolation forest machine learning algorithm. A proactive cryptographic caching mechanism reduces re-authentication latency to 7.2 ms with 99.5% session continuity (evaluated under warm-cache rule-based conditions), compared to traditional 1600 ms handover peaks. When subsequently integrated with the ML engine, the framework demonstrated a highly efficient signalling overhead of 0.75%, well below the 8% target. A policy decision point engine instantly translates anomaly scores into access control decisions. Evaluating 50,000 simulated NTN telemetry samples (4:1 class imbalance) yielded 88.00% accuracy, 0.9856 average precision, and a 0.9969 ROC AUC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve). Within the simulated environment, the framework delivered 100% live spoofing detection and 1.0000 attack recall with zero false negatives. Feature importance analysis reveals that physics-based kinematic metrics-specifically velocity deviation, GPS distance, and Doppler shift-drive the zero-trust scoring. Ultimately, this framework serves as a proof-of-concept demonstrating that adaptive, low-overhead security integrations are theoretically viable under orbital constraints, paving the way for future physical validation in next-generation 6G networks.

Article.Title: A prospective pilot cohort study of hydrocyn gel as a dressing agent compared with conventional flavin-based pin-site care for infection prevention
Article.Authors: Md Yusoff B.; Jasmin L.; Nik Kamaruzman N.; Mohamad N.; Ramlan M.; Azwan Aziz M.
Article.Abstract: Pin-site infection (PSI) is a pervasive complication of external fixation, whose prevention is hampered by a lack of consensus on optimal care. This study aims (a) to generate preliminary estimates of pin-site infection rates associated with Hydrocyn gel compared to conventional flavin dressing and (b) to characterize the pattern and severity of infections (using the Checketts-Otterburn scale) in both groups over a four-week follow-up period. A prospective cohort study was conducted from April 2024 to December 2025. Sixteen patients with external fixators were included: 10 used Hydrocyn gel and 6 used conventional flavin dressing. Patients in both groups performed self-dressing every three days. Patients were followed weekly for four weeks, with pin-site infection diagnosed and graded using the Checketts and Otterburn scale. Due to the non-randomized design, small sample size, and retrospective trial registration, no inferential statistical tests were performed; results are descriptive. The Hydrocyn gel group had a lower pin site infection rate of 20% (2/10) compared to 66.7% (4/6) in the flavin group. In the Hydrocyn gel group, two patients developed Grade 1 infections; one resolved spontaneously, and one had worsening infection that required surgical debridement and pin removal. The flavin group experienced earlier and more frequent infections, with one patient requiring early debridement and multiple cases progressing to Grade 2 and 3. No osteomyelitis was reported in either group. Hydrocyn gel was associated with a lower observed rate of pin-site infection n compared to conventional flavin dressing in a trauma population. Because treatment allocation was based on patient consent rather than randomization, the observed association between Hydrocyn gel and lower infection rates should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of treatment efficacy. Trial Registration : TCTR20260302001 (Retrospective study registration: 02 March 2026).

Article.Title: Multimodal speech perception in noise after multisensory perceptual training in autistic children and adolescents
Article.Authors: Möde L.; Ghaneirad E.; Szycik G.; Worthmann H.; Bleich S.; Borgolte A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Autistic children and adolescents exhibit alterations in multisensory processing of simple audiovisual stimuli and complex speech stimuli. Multisensory perceptual training improves audiovisual simultaneity perception in typically developed adults, thereby facilitating speech comprehension in noise. We hypothesized that multisensory training would enhance audiovisual integration and speech comprehension in noise in autistic youth. A brief simultaneity judgment task (SJT) with feedback as the training paradigm was administered to a sample of autistic participants (aged 8–17). Simple audiovisual integration and speech comprehension were assessed before training (T0), immediately (T1), seven (T2) and 14 days (T3) after training. For simple audiovisual stimuli, changes in simultaneity judgements were observed at T1 and T2. At T1, these changes may reflect a shift in response criteria, whereas at T2, a narrower TBW and a steeper slope may indicate improved simultaneity perception. In a Word Recognition Task (WRT), no significant improvements were observed. This study suggests that multisensory training alters simultaneity judgement in a SJT in autistic youth, with the effects persisting seven days. Future studies should determine whether these effects reflect changes in response criteria or genuine improvements in simultaneity perception and determine how training paradigms must be adapted to enhance speech comprehension in autistic youth.
