Article.Title: Evaluation of the clinical performance of two new onchocerciasis rapid diagnostic tests in districts targeted for elimination in Ghana
Article.Authors: de Souza D.; Ashong Y.; Afatodzie S.; Dogbe M.; Nyarko A.; Logonia B.; Frempong K.; Moore C.; Hundley L.; Kutjok P.; Prince-Guerra J.; Elder E.; Won K.; Vedrine C.; Leissner P.; Duvoix A.; Adams E.; Biamonte M.; Boakye D.
Article.Abstract: Current diagnostic methods for onchocerciasis lack sufficient utility, sensitivity or specificity. Two new lateral flow assays developed by Bioaster and Global Access Diagnostics (BA/GADx) and Drugs and Diagnostics for Tropical Diseases (DDTD) multi-antigen test Biplex Version C (DDTDc) were evaluated in Ghanaian communities that have received mass drug administration for many years or are considered non-endemic to assess their potential for point-of-care use. Both tests detect IgG4 antibodies against the Onchocerca volvulus -specific antigen Ov16, while the DDTD test further detects antibodies to the O. volvulus -specific antigen OvOC3261. The study enrolled 1,700 participants (≥ 5 years) across seven communities. The tests were evaluated on whole blood in the field and on dried blood spots (DBS) in the laboratory. The results were compared with the O-150 qPCR on skin snips and the existing SD Ov16 RDT test on DBS. O-150 Skin snip qPCR identified only 26 positives, limiting the assessments. However, the sensitivities of the DDTDc and BA/GADx RDTs evaluated in the field and in laboratory compared to the O-150 qPCR ranged from 76.9% (95% CI: 56.4–91.0) to 69.2% (95% CI: 48.2–85.7) and 71.3% (95% CI: 52.2–88.4) to 69.2% (95% CI: 48.2–85.7), respectively. The specificities of the DDTDc and BA/GADx RDTs evaluated in the field and laboratory compared to the O-150 qPCR ranged from 68.3% (95% CI: 65.1–71.3) to 69.5% (95% CI: 66.4–72.6) and 72.5% (95% CI: 69.4–75.4) to 68.2% (95% CI: 65.0–71.3), respectively. The sensitivity and specificity of the SD Ov16 RDT based on O-150 qPCR were 65.4% (95% CI: 44.3–82.8) and 72.9% (95% CI: 69.8–75.8%), respectively. The concordance between the new tests and the SD Ov16 RDT was above 92%. There was substantial agreement between the DDTDc test in the field and the SD Ov16 RDT (Kappa = 0.63; SE: 0.03; 95% CI: 0.57–0.69), and between the DDTDc test in the laboratory and the SD Ov16 RDT (Kappa = 0.76; SE: 0.02; 95% CI: 0.71–0.80). Similarly, there was substantial agreement between the BA/GADx test in the field and the SD Ov16 RDT (Kappa = 0.79; SE: 0.02; 95% CI: 0.76–0.83), and between the BA/GADx test in the laboratory and the SD Ov16 RDT (Kappa = 0.76; SE: 0.02; 95% CI: 0.72–0.80). Both tests demonstrated field usability and adequate sensitivity, meeting the WHO TPP requirements for onchocerciasis mapping decisions but not for MDA stopping decisions. These advancements represent progress toward diagnostic tools available for elimination programs but underscore the need for continued diagnostic innovation to address the challenges of evaluating new diagnostic tests in disease elimination settings with a low number of true positives to assess the diagnostic performance of the tests.

Article.Title: Object groups mutually bias each other’s perceived average size, as evidenced by neural and behavioural data
Article.Authors: Memis E.; Fink G.; Weidner R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract The human visual system simultaneously computes summary statistics of object features, such as average size, across groups of objects. Evidence suggests that summary statistics across groups of objects (ensembles) are not independent but influence one another. We investigated whether an ensemble’s average size affects the perceived average size of another ensemble, and whether such changes are reflected in altered activation patterns in the visual cortex. Distractor ensembles’ average sizes altered the perceived average size of target ensembles in a contrast-like manner: Large distractor ensembles decreased the target ensembles’ perceived average sizes; conversely, smaller distractor ensembles increased target ensembles’ perceived average sizes. These contrast effects were reflected in more activated voxels in retinotopic regions when target ensembles were perceived as larger. Distractor ensembles’ voxel counts were similarly modulated by target ensembles’ average size, suggesting their perceived average size was also altered. Additionally, individual differences in the magnitude of the ensemble-size contrast effect covaried with activation in higher-level regions, including the left intraparietal sulcus (IPS) and middle temporal gyrus (MTG). Together, these findings suggest that ensemble summary statistics are contrasted, resulting in changes in perceived size and altered retinotopic activation pattern, with involvement of a network including left IPS and left MTG.

Article.Title: Explainable machine learning for shear capacity prediction of reinforced concrete deep beams
Article.Authors: Meghdadi Z.; Shabanlou M.; Shiravand M.; Khaloo A.
Article.Abstract: The shear capacity prediction of reinforced concrete (RC) deep beams remains a challenging issue in design of concrete structures. Although the code-based strut-and-tie method is widely accepted, it is often time-consuming for routine design applications, while existing empirical equations are unable to fully capture the highly nonlinear interactions among material properties, geometric characteristics, and reinforcement variables. To address this limitation, this study proposes an explainable machine learning framework for predicting the shear capacity of RC deep beams. A comprehensive database of 419 experimentally tested specimens was compiled from the literature, and eight supervised machine learning models were developed with hyperparameters optimized using the Optuna framework. Comparative analysis showed that the optimized Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT) model achieved the best predictive performance, with a test coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 0.93. A synthetic Gaussian input-perturbation study was conducted to assess the numerical sensitivity of the models under progressively disturbed inputs. To interpret the black-box behavior of the model, Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) and three-dimensional Partial Dependence Plots (3D-PDPs) were employed. The resulting feature-response patterns were broadly consistent with established deep-beam behavior, particularly the positive effect of concrete compressive strength and the negative influence of the shear-span-to-depth ratio, along with important nonlinear interactions among key variables. Finally, a user-friendly graphical user interface integrating the optimized GBDT model was developed to provide rapid and interpretable shear-capacity estimation for practical engineering applications.
Article.OpenAlexKeywords: explainable machine learning; reinforced concrete deep beams; shear capacity prediction

Article.Title: Effect of features burdened with classical error, misclassifications, Berkson error, and group-summary assignments on machine learning performance and interpretability
Article.Authors: Mohamed Z.; Oraby T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Measurement error is widespread in modern data pipelines, but its influence on predictive modeling and variable importance assessments in machine learning is often underestimated. Our study examines how input measurement error affects both prediction accuracy and interpretability across four common additive error types: classical error, misclassification of predictive features, Berkson error, caused by algorithmic or model-based assignment errors, and group-summary (aggregation) assignment errors. Using controlled Monte Carlo simulation experiments that cover regression and classification, we evaluate five popular machine learning models: generalized linear models, support vector machines, random forests, XGBoost, and multilayer perceptrons, across various error levels. To distinguish the effect of the error from optimization issues, hyperparameters are tuned separately for each dataset, and performance is measured using standard predictive metrics and permutation feature importance. Results show that measurement error generally reduces predictive performance and can significantly alter the ranking and estimated contribution of highly predictive features, with different degradation patterns depending on the error type and model. These findings clarify when performance declines might be mistaken for distributional shifts, among other things, and highlight the importance of diagnosing and correcting measurement error before drawing conclusions about model robustness, generalization, or variable relevance.

Article.Title: Fabrication of superhydrophobic and superoleophilic copper oxide nanostructures without organic modifiers for oil–water separation
Article.Authors: Velayi E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Superhydrophobic and superoleophilic hierarchical urchin-like copper oxide powders were synthesized by a facile one-step method without the use of low-surface-energy modifiers. The selective wettability of the powders toward water and oil makes them suitable for oil adsorption from oil-in-water emulsions. In addition, the hierarchical CuO structures were grown in situ on a stainless-steel mesh, which was used for the separation of heavy oil–water mixtures. The synergistic combination of micro-/nanoscale roughness and a reduction in the polar component of surface free energy through hydroxylation of the copper oxide surface likely leads to a significant decrease in wettability and the development of superhydrophobic and superoleophilic properties, as evidenced by a static water contact angle of 161.1° ± 2° and an oil contact angle of 0°, measured on the CuO-coated mesh surface. The superhydrophobic copper oxide particles demonstrated a high oil adsorption selectivity greater than 19. The immiscible chloroform/water mixture was separated via a simple filtration method using a superhydrophobic/superoleophilic copper oxide–coated mesh filter, achieving a separation efficiency of approximately 98% and a chloroform permeation flux of about 7300 L m⁻² h⁻¹. In addition, copper oxide powder showed promising potential as a selective oil adsorbent for the treatment of oil-in-water emulsions and the cleanup of oil spills when used in the form of sorbent booms or pillows.

Article.Title: Performance and emission analysis of a diesel engine fueled with rice-bran and lemon-peel oil biodiesel blends
Article.Authors: Rangari V.; Deshpande H.; Bhosale S.; Kebede A.; Majumder H.
Article.Abstract: The growing demand for sustainable energy and for emission reductions has intensified the search for alternative fuels for compression-ignition engines. This study presents a novel experimental investigation of the combined use of eco-friendly biodiesel derived from rice bran oil and lemon peel oil, as well as their hybrid blends, in a CRDI VCR diesel engine. Unlike conventional studies that focus on single-source biodiesel, the present work uniquely explores the synergistic effects of dual biodiesel blends on engine performance and emissions. A hybrid Taguchi–Grey relational analysis (GRA) approach is implemented to evaluate the influence of key operating parameters, namely blend ratio, engine load, and fuel injection pressure, while addressing the inherent multi-response optimization challenge involving performance parameters (brake power, brake thermal efficiency, brake-specific fuel consumption, and mechanical efficiency) and emission characteristics (CO, HC, NOx, and smoke). Hybrid biodiesel blends demonstrate competitive performance and lower emissions than conventional diesel, highlighting the potential of waste-derived dual biodiesel fuels. The optimal parameter combinations indicate that blends such as D75RB25 (blend ratio of 25% RB and 75% neat diesel), engine load of 100%, and fuel injection pressure of 500, D80LP20 (blend ratio of 20% LP and 80% neat diesel); and D90RB5LP5 (blend ratio of 25% RB and 75% neat diesel ) at full load and 500 bar injection pressure can serve as viable substitutes for diesel fuel. The novelty of this work lies in the combined application of dual-source biodiesel blending and multi-objective optimization using the Taguchi-GRA method, providing a comprehensive framework for enhancing engine performance while reducing environmental impact.

Article.Title: An optimized majority-feedback QCA D-latch and SET/RESET-enabled SRAM cell for compact, low-latency nanoelectronic memory design
Article.Authors: Wani P.; Kassa S.
Article.Abstract: Quantum-dot cellular automata is a contender to replace the scaling of semiconductor technology as it hits physical limits of complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology, with its ability to switch faster, take up less space and consume less power. In this study, the design and functional verification of compact QCA data latch circuit and a memory cell suitable for SRAM operation are presented, which are designed, implemented and simulated in the QCA designer (QCAD) 2.0.3 software. The main contribution is a single-layer 14-cell D-latch with a 0.007 µm 2 footprint, reducing the layout area, latency and QCA cost compared with a similar design previously reported in the literature. Another 15-cell variant is proposed, incorporating SET and RESET control, for SRAM-type applications, reducing peak energy dissipation by approximately 22% from the 14-cell baseline. The circuits are found to be compact, low-latency circuits for next-generation nanoelectronics memory and different logic circuit design applications with reduced power dissipation. The power dissipation and polarization map of proposed circuits are implemented in QCAPro Software.

Article.Title: Problematic internet use is associated with poorer health behaviours and peripheral serotonin levels in young men
Article.Authors: Kożybska M.; Rył A.; Tomska N.; Raczyński G.; Rotter P.; Rotter I.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Problematic Internet Use (PIU) is associated with difficulties in psychological, social, academic, and occupational functioning and is associated with unhealthy behaviours such as poor diet, inactivity, and sleep problems. The post-pandemic period has intensified PIU and Internet addiction, especially among young men, who are more prone to risky health behaviours. This study aimed to assess the relationship between health behaviours, PIU, and serotonin and dopamine levels in young men. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 325 men aged 18–30 from the West Pomeranian region of Poland. PIU severity was measured using the Internet Use Test (IUT), and health behaviours were assessed using the Health-Related Behaviour Inventory (HBI). Blood samples were analysed for serotonin and dopamine levels using ELISA. 17.7% of participants exhibited high or very high PIU. One-third led unhealthy lifestyles. Higher PIU correlated with lower health behaviour scores, with a small effect size. The overall HBI score was moderately negatively associated with non-work Internet use during weekdays and weekends. In the low PIU group, healthy eating habits showed a moderate positive correlation with dopamine levels. The linear correlation analysis, after adjusting for age and BMI, revealed a weak correlation between IUT scores and overall HBI scores, HBI healthy eating habits, HBI positive mental attitudes, and serotonin levels. PIU was linked to poorer health behaviours. These findings underscore the importance of addressing both Internet use patterns and health behaviours in interventions, as they are closely interrelated in this demographic. Further research should explore the neurobiological mechanisms behind these associations.

Article.Title: Taurine is a functional regulator of transthyretin; implication in transthyretin-induced hypothyroidism and amyloidosis
Article.Authors: Krishna S.; Khan S.; Singh L.
Article.Abstract: Transthyretin (TTR) is a homo-tetrameric, 55 kDa, transport protein synthesized mainly in the liver, retinal epithelium, choroid plexus, placental villi and uterus. The main function of TTR is transport of thyroxine (T 4 ) and retinol-binding protein, while it also plays a crucial role in neuroprotection. The binding of thyroxine assists in maintaining the stability of the native tetramer, which is crucial for its functionality. Eventually, dissociation of the tetramer to its monomer results in the formation of toxic oligomeric TTR species and their deposition causes diseases such as cardiomyopathy, polyneuropathy, dementia and preeclampsia. While current kinetic stabilizers occupy the hydrophobic thyroxine-binding pocket, identifying endogenous modulators that maintain TTR homeostasis without impairing hormone transport remains a key objective. In this study, we investigated taurine—a vital neuronal osmolyte and endogenous chemical chaperone—as a functional regulator of TTR dynamics. In the present study, we have systematically evaluated the effect of taurine on the structure-function paradigm of TTR using various biochemical, biophysical tools and cellular model. We discovered that taurine exhibits preferential binding to TTR leading to functional enhancement of T 4 -binding affinity and exhibits anti-aggregation potential towards TTR amyloidosis. Further examination of the mechanism revealed that taurine exhibits preferential binding to TTR microstates and restricts local conformational fluctuations, without altering the global native structure or thermodynamic folding. Together, these findings identify taurine as a trans-acting allosteric chemical chaperone of TTR. This discovery of functional regulation of TTR by taurine offers a promising, non-toxic therapeutic strategy in repurposing of taurine (an FDA-approved supplement) for TTR amyloidosis and TTR-induced hypothyroidism, especially in neuronal and gestational impairments.

Article.Title: A QMIX-driven routing protocol for dynamic Underwater Acoustic Sensor Networks
Article.Authors: M A.; Lokam A.; Dasari K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Reliable and energy-efficient data collection remains a fundamental challenge in Underwater Acoustic Sensor Networks (UASNs) owing to limited battery capacity, high propagation delay, dynamic network topology and unreliable communication links. To address these challenges, we propose a Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (CMARL)-based data routing framework for dynamic UASNs. The routing problem is modeled as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP), where each relay node acts as an autonomous routing agent using locally available information. The framework adopts a Centralized Training and Decentralized Execution (CTDE) paradigm, in which cooperative routing policies are learned using the QMIX algorithm and executed through trained local Q -networks. Each agent constructs its local observation from residual energy, relative forwarding progress towards the sink, estimated link quality and neighboring node availability, while the action space consists of cooperative next-hop selection. A UASN-oriented reward function that jointly optimizes packet delivery reliability, energy efficiency and network lifetime by encouraging reliable packet forwarding and discouraging inefficient routing decisions. Extensive simulation results show that the proposed framework consistently outperforms representative routing protocols across key metrics - packet delivery rate, end-to-end delay, and network lifetime, providing an effective, scalable and intelligent routing solution for next-generation UASNs.

Article.Title: Physicochemical quality, molecular composition, tocopherol profiling, and in vitro activity of cold-pressed Sacha inchi (Plukenetia volubilis L.) oil
Article.Authors: Shanmugam G.; Sahadevan R.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sacha inchi ( Plukenetia volubilis L.) oil is among the richest plant-derived sources of alpha-linolenic acid (ALA), offering vegetarians a plant-based route to omega-3 fatty acid. This study encompasses around the characterization of cold-pressed Sacha inchi oil (SIO) combining physicochemical quality assessment and molecular composition. GC-FID analysis quantified five major fatty acids, with ALA as the predominant fatty acid (49.61 ± 0.05%), with total PUFA content of 84.25 ± 0.07%, with a ω-6:ω-3 ratio of 0.70:1. LC–MS/MS analysis revealed a total tocopherol content of 492.685 ± 0.049 mg kg⁻¹. SIO exhibited concentration-dependent DPPH (IC₅₀ = 24.94 ± 2.58 µg mL⁻¹) and ABTS radical scavenging activity (IC₅₀ = 31.99 ± 1.13 µg mL⁻¹). In RAW 264.7 macrophages, SIO showed concentration-dependent effects on cell viability, with IC₅₀ values of 213.40 ± 5.73 µg/mL in LPS untreated cells. SIO also reduced LPS-induced NO production by 6.05–49.62% at 10–75 µg mL⁻¹. And exhibits cytotoxicity against MDA-MB-231 triple-negative breast cancer cells (IC₅₀ = 15.08 µg mL⁻¹; 95% CI: 14.14–16.06 µg mL⁻¹) and HEK-293 cells (IC₅₀ = 45.53 µg mL⁻¹; 95% CI: 43.02–48.02 µg mL⁻¹). These findings highlight the compositional richness of SIO and support its potential as PUFA-rich functional food ingredient.

Article.Title: Pesticide health literacy and preventive behaviors among greenhouse operators in Northeastern Iran
Article.Authors: Mahmoodi A.; Pourhaji F.; Naseri M.
Article.Abstract: Greenhouse operators face high pesticide exposure risks, yet the cognitive pathways translating health literacy (HL) into preventive behaviors remain unclear. This study examined the multidimensional construct of Pesticide Health Literacy (PHL) and its association with preventive behaviors among greenhouse operators. This cross-sectional census study was conducted among 115 greenhouse operators in Neyshabur County, Iran. Data were collected using validated PHL and preventive behavior questionnaires. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent samples t-tests, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), and hierarchical multiple regression. Participants exhibited moderate PHL (mean: 61.92 ± 16.96 out of 115) but significantly lower preventive behaviors (mean: 8.90 ± 1.74 out of 21). Hierarchical multiple regression revealed that PHL was the strongest independent factor associated with preventive behaviors ( β = 0.63, P < 0.001 ), followed by educational attainment ( β = 0.37, P < 0.001 ). Sociodemographic variables alone did not significantly explain variation in preventive behaviors (R 2 = 0.084 , P = 0.140 ). PHL, particularly the critical information assessment domain, showed a stronger association with preventive behaviors than the sociodemographic factors examined in this study. The findings suggest that interventions addressing pesticide safety should extend beyond basic information provision and include skills for critically evaluating pesticide-related information, particularly among operators with lower educational attainment. Such an approach may help address the gap in HL preventive behaviors in high-risk agricultural settings.

Article.Authors: Tafti A.; Mirjalili B.; Basharnavaz H.
Article.Abstract: In the present study, a convenient and greener synthesis of a series of naphtho[1,2- e ][1,3]oxazines was accomplished via three-component one-pot cyclocondensation between β -naphthol, formaldehyde, and various amines using nano-eggshell/B(III) as a natural catalyst in aqueous medium. This approach is totally non-polluting and several advantages, such as shorter reaction time, mild reaction conditions, simple workup, and reduced environmental impact. The experimental results are consistent with the data obtained from the DFT calculations.

Article.Title: Bearing capacity and safety factors of ring foundations in spatially variable soils: a hybrid FELA-machine learning approach
Article.Authors: Mohammadizadeh M.; Mohammadizadeh M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Ring foundations efficiently support axisymmetric structures like silos, storage tanks, chimneys, and cooling towers with reduced concrete volume compared to solid circular foundations. Their ultimate bearing capacity is strongly affected by asymmetric loading and spatial variability in soil properties. This study presents a hybrid machine learning framework to predict normalized bearing capacity factors and safety factors for ring foundations in spatially variable cohesive-frictional (c-φ) soils. Datasets were generated via finite element limit analysis (FELA) in OptumG2, incorporating random field modeling of effective cohesion (c’) (lognormal, depth-linear mean: µ c’ = 10 kPa, k = 1 kPa/m, COV = 0.3) and friction angle (φ’ up to 40°). Four loading configurations (complete, internal half, middle half, external half), inner-to-outer radius ratios of 0–0.9, rough/smooth interfaces, and nine anisotropic scale-of-fluctuation cases (horizontal: 10–60 m; vertical: 2–8 m) were analyzed. A Convolutional Neural Network processed random field images and parameters, achieving R² > 0.95 and relative errors < 3%. External half and complete loading gave highest capacities; internal half reduced them by up to 40%. Spatial variability in c’ and φ’ contracted failure envelopes by 10–25%, emphasizing reliability-based design. The framework dramatically reduces computational cost versus traditional FELA/Monte Carlo while retaining accuracy, supporting preliminary design, optimization, and risk assessment.

Article.Title: Trajectories of cardiopulmonary adaptation and executive function in elite endurance athletes receiving transcranial direct current stimulation with interval training
Article.Authors: Dai C.; Zhang L.
Article.Abstract: This study examined how transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) interacts with high-intensity interval training (HIIT) to shape cardiopulmonary fitness and executive function in elite endurance athletes across an 8-week protocol. Sixty-six nationally ranked athletes were stratified by training tenure, competitive level, and baseline maximal oxygen uptake, then prospectively allocated, with participant and outcome-assessor blinding, to one of three intervention arms: real-tDCS plus HIIT, sham-tDCS plus HIIT, or HIIT-only; 59 completed the programme. Both stimulation arms alternated between a left dorsolateral prefrontal montage and a bilateral motor montage, and cortical target was carried through the analysis as a within-subject factor rather than folded into a single stimulation label. Cardiopulmonary indices, executive function (Stroop, N-back, Flanker), prefrontal hemodynamics via functional near-infrared spectroscopy, and heart rate variability were measured at four assessment waves, with female athletes tested inside the early follicular window at every wave. Nonlinear mixed-effects and generalized additive mixed models resolved dynamic trajectories at the individual level, while a second-order partial derivative quantified the stimulation × load interaction. End-of-study allocation guesses did not depart from chance in either masked arm, so blinding held. Because masking held only for the two stimulation arms, the real- versus sham-tDCS comparison carries the causal weight of the trial, and the HIIT-only arm enters as a partially unblinded reference rather than a second control. Against sham, the real-tDCS arm showed a delayed but steeper rise in maximal oxygen uptake and an earlier separation in Stroop interference. A modelled cumulative exposure-response surface exhibited a non-monotone shape with an interior maximum whose geometry, but not whose coordinates, survived leave-one-subject-out cross-validation; because intensity and duration were fixed and exposure varied only with session completion, we present that surface as exploratory. Cross-system coupling between prefrontal oxygenation and ventilatory threshold strengthened under active stimulation, consistent with, though not proof of, a bidirectional central-peripheral regulation account. Adherence captured the largest share of individual response variance, with BDNF and ACTN3 variants contributing modestly. As exploratory findings, these patterns are consistent with a stratified, trajectory-aware view of neuromodulation in elite training, though claims about an optimal dose must await confirmatory trials that deliberately vary stimulation intensity.

Article.Title: Physical activity and blood pressure as predictors of cognitive function in the all of us research program
Article.Authors: Okusaga O.; Lin Y.; Atkinson E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Physical activity (PA) is positively associated with cognition, whereas elevated blood pressure shows a negative association. However, most studies relied on subjective, self-reported measures of PA. In this study, we examined associations of PA (daily step count from Fitbit wearable devices), systolic (SBP) and diastolic (DBP) blood pressure spanning 14 years, with end-of-study cognitive performance in 3,093 participants in the All of Us Research Program (AoU). Cognition was assessed by the Gradual Onset Continuous Performance Task (Grad-CPT), Delay Discounting Task (DD-Task), Multiracial Emotional Recognition Task (Emorecog-Task) and Flanker-Task. Baseline PA metrics were positively associated with Grad-CPT (β = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.18 to 0.44), DD-Task (β = 0.05, 95% CI: 0.04 to 0.07), and Flanker-Task (β = 0.26, 95% CI: 0.17 to 0.35). Baseline SBP was negatively associated with DD-Task (β = -0.01, 95% CI: -0.02 to -0.004). Longitudinal k-means clustering identified 3 clusters of individuals—A, B and C— with mean daily steps of 5108, 8875 and 14,161 respectively. Individuals in clusters B and C had higher scores than those in cluster A on the DD-Task, Grad-CPT and Flanker-Task. These findings underscore the potential role of PA promotion and optimal blood pressure management in supporting cognitive health.

Article.Title: ECG-based automated detection of sleep apnea using deep neural networks and hidden markov models
Article.Authors: Qnatyan S.; Ghimatgar H.; Keshavarz A.
Article.Abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a common yet underdiagnosed disorder, and current diagnostic methods such as polysomnography are resource-intensive and inaccessible for many patients. Electrocardiogram (ECG)-based screening offers a more practical alternative, but the nonstationary nature of ECG signals and substantial inter-record and physiological variability limit diagnostic accuracy. Here we propose a deep learning framework that integrates multiple surface ECG-derived features—R-R intervals (RRI), ECG-derived respiration (EDR), and R-wave amplitude (RAMP)—from the PhysioNet Apnea-ECG database. Using a combined Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)–Transformer–Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architecture with a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) as a post-processing module, our method achieves an accuracy of 90.33% and specificity of 94.91% under record-wise five-fold cross-validation, while the record-wise A-Test robustness evaluation across K = 2 to K = 36 yielded an accuracy of 90.68% and a specificity of 94.26%. HMM post-processing increased accuracy by approximately 3.7–4.0% points, with larger improvements observed in sensitivity. These results demonstrate the feasibility of a computationally efficient ECG-based framework for OSA screening, while further validation on independent external datasets, prospective clinical cohorts, and real-world home or wearable recordings is required before clinical or home-based deployment.

Article.Title: Methane bursts during spring thaw in the permafrost region of Northeast China
Article.Authors: Xia H.; Guo Y.; Shan W.; Zhou S.; Cao S.
Article.Abstract: Spring thaw in permafrost regions is associated with episodic bursts in atmospheric methane concentration. In this study, these methane bursts were investigated across different permafrost types in Northeast China. MODIS data and Sentinel-5P methane observations were used to derive the thaw onset date and methane burst timing, respectively. Results showed that methane bursts exhibited distinct spatial and interannual variability. Methane burst date was delayed with increasing permafrost stability, and median burst dates occurred in early to mid-April in unstable permafrost, late April to early May in semi-stable permafrost and stable permafrost. Meanwhile, methane bursts generally occurred within 15 days after thaw onset. There was a consistent positive relationship between thaw onset date and methane burst date across all years, with regression slopes of 0.78–1.07. Notably, the median lag tended to shorten from 15 to 22 days in 2020 to 11 days in 2024, suggesting an increasingly rapid temporal response of methane bursts to spring thaw over the study period.

Article.Title: CFD investigation of a novel gabion-based porous medium configuration for energy dissipation in ogee spillway stilling basins
Article.Authors: Aminvash E.; Daneshfaraz R.
Article.Abstract: Ogee spillways which provide very large discharge rates are extensively employed for civil engineering applications, but high velocity flows generated by Ogee spillways can be seriously harmful to downstream structures. This numerical investigation is conducted to assess the potential of adding porous media (uniform gabions and cross shaped gabions, with varying porosities: 30%, 40% and 50%) to the stilling basin at the bottom of ogee spillways to dissipate energy. The maximum improvement in relative energy dissipation compared with the smooth-bed configuration reached approximately 65% for the uniform gabion configuration and 46% for the cross-shaped gabion configuration. In addition, the addition of porous media led to significantly low downstream Froude numbers as much as 91%–98%, showing the flow can be reduced from supercritical to subcritical flow regimes. Moreover, use of gabion based porous media provides a new cheap and hydraulic effective alternatives to the concrete stilling basins and their hydraulic efficiency can significantly contribute to construction cost saving.

Article.Title: An antimicrobial cyclic peptide with multitarget efficacy for acne
Article.Authors: Yu N.; Guo G.; Zhang L.; He T.; Zhang M.; Wang J.; Wang J.; Yao R.; Wang G.; Wang J.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Acne vulgaris is a complex inflammatory disorder, and current treatment options are often limited by antibiotic resistance and cutaneous irritation, underscoring the urgent need for safer multi-target therapeutic alternatives. In this study, a novel antimicrobial cyclic peptide (AMCP) was systematically evaluated for its multidimensional anti-acne efficacy, and a penetration enhancer was developed for improving the topical dermal delivery. At a concentration of 20 µg/mL, AMCP inhibited dihydrotestosterone (DHT)- and linoleic acid (LA)-induced lipid synthesis in SZ95 sebocytes by 40.0% and 29.1%, respectively. Furthermore, it exhibited potent bactericidal activity against C. acnes (MIC or MBC at 0.5 µg/mL) and S. aureus (MIC or MBC at 1.0 µg/mL). AMCP suppressed key inflammatory mediators (IL-6, IL-8, IL-1β, TNF-α, and PGE₂) in a concentration-dependent manner in both HaCaT keratinocytes and SZ95 sebocytes. Additionally, it promoted keratinocyte migration, upregulated the expression of epidermal differentiation genes (FLG, IVL, Claudin-1, and KRT1), and downregulated KLK7 expression. Notably, the combination of 2% propylene glycol and 0.1% sodium surfactin synergistically enhanced topical dermal delivery of AMCP, resulting in a 5-fold increase in cumulative permeation at 8 h. In conclusion, AMCP exerts anti-acne effects through a multi-functional mechanism involving sebum control, antibacterial activity, anti-inflammation, and cell migration, while also overcoming the bottleneck of topical dermal delivery. These findings provide a new cyclic peptide with anti-acne efficacy, positioning AMCP as a promisingly anti-acne ingredient.

Article.Title: Enhancing network science with large language models and federated artificial intelligence
Article.Authors: Kumar L.; Solanki S.; Jhariya M.; Wadekar S.; Manzoor T.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Sixth generation (6G) networks require intelligent and privacy-preserving solutions to handle traffic complexity, resource allocation, and security challenges. While Large Language Models (LLMs) offer advanced reasoning and Federated Artificial Intelligence (FAI) enables distributed learning without directly sharing raw data, their combined application in large-scale network science remains limited. Key issues include non-IID data, decision latency, and limited robustness of centralized models. To address these challenges, this work introduces FALCON-6G (Federated AI and LLM-Oriented Cognitive Optimization in 6G Networks), a novel framework for distributed anomaly detection, traffic prediction, and adaptive resource management. Experiments conducted under federated learning settings with 50 participating clients and 200 global communication rounds on two Open RAN and four intrusion detection datasets show a 22.7% average relative improvement in throughput prediction accuracy and a 17.6% reduction in decision latency compared with FedAvg, along with up to a 23.9% relative improvement in intrusion detection F1-score over FedAvg and a 34.0% reduction in communication overhead. These results demonstrate the potential of FALCON-6G for privacy-aware 6G network optimization. The current evaluation is primarily based on benchmark datasets, and validation in live large-scale 6G/O-RAN environments remains an important direction for future work.

Article.Title: Dietary acid load is associated with quality of life in overweight and obese adult in Iranian women: a cross sectional study
Article.Authors: Rasaei N.; Samadi M.; Bahrampour N.; Daneshzad E.; Gholami F.; Tavakoli A.; Clark C.; Mirzaei K.
Article.Abstract: Epidemiologic investigations have shown that dietary acid load (DAL) is associated with some limited quality of life (QoL) markers; however, according to the documents available so far, the association of this dietary pattern with QoL among overweight and obese women is not clear. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the association of DAL and QoL among overweight and obese adult women. This cross-sectional study included 377 overweight and obese women. A validated food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) was used to assess dietary intake. DAL was estimated based on potential renal acid load (PRAL) and net endogenous acid production (NEAP). QoL was assessed using the 36-item Short-Form Health Survey (SF-36). Linear regression models were applied with progressive adjustment for potential confounders including age, body mass index, physical activity, smoking, marital status, education, occupation, supplement use, and total energy intake. In crude analyses, both NEAP and PRAL were positively associated with the General Health and Physical Functioning domains of the SF-36. After adjustment for age, body mass index, physical activity, smoking status, marital status, educational level, occupational status, supplement use, and total energy intake (Model 2), higher NEAP remained significantly associated with General Health (β = 3.23, 95% CI: 0.05, 6.40; P = 0.04). The association with Physical Functioning was no longer statistically significant (β = 2.72, 95% CI: -0.33, 5.78; P = 0.08). Higher PRAL also showed a borderline positive association with General Health (β = 3.15, 95% CI: -0.11, 6.43; P = 0.05) and Physical Functioning (β = 3.09, 95% CI: -0.05, 6.25; P = 0.05) after adjusting all confounders. No significant associations were observed between DAL indices and total SF-36 scores after multivariable adjustment. In this cross-sectional study, higher dietary acid load was associated with better general health and physical functioning among overweight and obese Iranian women. These findings should be confirmed in prospective studies.

Article.Title: Person-independent and cross-dataset evaluation of convolutional and recurrent architectures for eye movement classification
Article.Authors: Akkaya A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Classifying eye movements into fixations, saccades, and smooth pursuits is a basic step in the analysis of gaze recordings. Deep models are now common for this task, but they are often evaluated on windows that share participants between training and test sets, which leaves open how well they work for people the model has not seen. This paper reports a person-independent comparison of three architectures—a one-dimensional CNN, an LSTM, and a CNN–LSTM hybrid—for four-class eye movement classification on the GazeCom dataset (54 participants, 250 Hz, expert frame-level annotations). Each model is trained and tested under leave-one-person-out cross-validation, so every participant is held out in turn, and each architecture is run with two input representations: raw gaze position and a derived set that adds velocity, acceleration, and angular change. Model differences are assessed at the participant level (paired tests over 54 folds, Holm-corrected) rather than on overlapping windows. Two findings are consistent across the study. First, recurrent modeling is what separates the strong models from the weak one: the LSTM and the hybrid reach a macro-F1 of about 0.82 with the derived input, while the CNN reaches 0.71, and the gap holds for every participant. Second, adding the convolutional front end to the LSTM does not help: the hybrid and the plain LSTM are statistically indistinguishable with the raw input and separated by less than 0.01 macro-F1 with the derived input, so the extra component is not warranted by the data; the hybrid carries about 70% more parameters than the LSTM for no measurable gain. The derived input improves every architecture, most for the CNN and for the smooth-pursuit class. Three non-learned or lightweight baselines (velocity threshold, velocity–dispersion, and a Random Forest on kinematic features), tuned per fold and evaluated under the same protocol, stay near 0.53–0.54 macro-F1 on the fixation/saccade/pursuit task, well below all three deep models. When the GazeCom-trained models are tested without retraining on the Lund2013 recordings and scored against both expert raters, accuracy falls as expected, but the ordering of the architectures is preserved. The plain LSTM is therefore an adequate model for this task; the smooth-pursuit class remains the main source of error and is the most useful target for future work.

Article.Title: Quantifying and mitigating explanation drift under INT8 quantization in plant disease image classification
Article.Authors: Khandaker S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Deep learning image classifiers are routinely compressed to INT8 for edge deployment, yet the effect of quantization on post-hoc saliency explanations has not been quantified at scale. We define explanation drift as the systematic change in a saliency map between a full-precision (FP32) model and its fake-quantized INT8 simulation, and measure it with three metrics reported against explicit random-overlap baselines: top- k Intersection-over-Union, top- k Dice, and Spearman rank correlation. We evaluate four explanation methods (Grad-CAM, Grad-CAM++, Integrated Gradients, LIME) on three architectures spanning distinct design families (EfficientNetV2-S, ResNet-50, MobileNetV3-Large) fine-tuned on the Paddy Disease Classification dataset (10 classes, 10,407 images), yielding 3,240 paired saliency comparisons per operating point on a stratified 320-image subset of the validation split. A central methodological finding is that the choice of Grad-CAM target layer, not quantization, governs whether attribution appears to survive: for all three architectures the last module returned by a naive “final layer” heuristic emits a $$1\times 1$$ spatial tensor, which forces a constant saliency map and produces spurious attribution collapse in up to $$61.7\%$$ of images. With architecture-appropriate target layers resolved by an explicit spatial-dimension criterion, no collapse occurs in any of the 3,240 comparisons, and drift is substantial but bounded: mean top- k IoU ranges from 0.366 to 0.790 across architecture–method pairs (4.5–9.7 $$\times $$ the random-overlap baseline of 0.081) with median Spearman $$\rho = 0.850$$ . Drift remains strongly method- and architecture-dependent, with Integrated Gradients least preserved and MobileNetV3-Large most affected among architectures. Calibration choice dominates deployment fidelity: on the full validation split, MinMax calibration in ONNX Runtime reduces FP32–INT8 prediction agreement to 0.644 and 0.641 for EfficientNetV2-S and MobileNetV3-Large, whereas percentile calibration restores it to 0.927 and 0.915. Explanation-aware quantization-aware training with a teacher–student CAM consistency loss improves MobileNetV3-Large (top- k IoU $$+16.3\%$$ ) but degrades EfficientNetV2-S ( $$-8.5\%$$ to $$-26.0\%$$ ) relative to post-training quantization; a $$\lambda = 0$$ control isolates the cause, showing that the direction of these changes is present in standard QAT, while the consistency term improves top- k IoU in all nine architecture–method cells relative to that control ( $$+0.6\%$$ to $$+14.4\%$$ , six significant after Holm correction). Stored full-validation CAM summaries differ from the primary subset by at most 1.4 percentage points in IoU; matching per-image records are unavailable, limiting independent verification. Finally, the auxiliary ground-truth localisation summaries (with incompletely verified execution provenance) for annotated SIIM-ACR chest radiographs report low mean FP32 and INT8 overlap with expert masks, illustrating why explanation similarity under quantization must not be read as explanation quality . Analysis code, figure-generation software, and derived result tables are openly archived.

Article.Title: Correlating InSAR-derived ground movement rates with landslide activity class and causal factors: a case study from Cyprus
Article.Authors: Tzampoglou P.; Loukidis D.; Tolomei C.; Svigkas N.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This study investigates the statistical correlation between ground movement rates in landslide areas, as derived by Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) results, with geological, geomorphological, environmental and geotechnical causal factors in southwestern Cyprus. The analysis examines ground velocities derived using Multi-Temporal Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (MT-InSAR) for both active and inactive landslides that are recorded in an existing inventory, using ascending and descending orbit datasets. The results show that the largest Line-of-Sight (LOS) velocities are observed in landslides characterized as active, followed by dormant and relict landslides. The largest displacement rates correspond mostly to outcrops of fine-grained clastic rocks, such as marls, radiolarian mudstones and mélange, due to their weak shear strength. An analysis based on Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) identified rainfall as the primary factor influencing the increase in LOS velocity. The Plasticity Index (PI) generally exhibits a positive correlation with the velocity, while the Geological Strength Index (GSI) demonstrates a weak negative correlation. The findings suggest that, while geological and geotechnical characteristics are crucial in the emergence of landslide phenomena, the rate of the ground movement, once initiated, is predominantly influenced by the precipitation height.

Article.Title: Paraprobiotics suppress bacterial virulence and promote anti-inflammatory tissue repair in a murine infected burn wound model
Article.Authors: Salimi A.; Torkamaneh M.; Haghighatshenas Z.; Sakaki F.; Chiani M.; Sohrabi A.; Aghamohammad S.; Rohani M.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Burn wound infections are a significant clinical problem that requires effective therapeutic interventions. Paraprobiotics, a non-viable form of microbial cells or components of probiotics, retain some health benefits while eliminating the risks associated with live microorganisms, thus providing a safe and natural alternative treatment approach. This paper investigated the therapeutic potential of paraprobiotics for treating second-degree burn infections and promoting wound healing in a mouse model. Twelve groups of mice ( n = 3 per group) with burn injuries and bacterial infections were treated with paraprobiotics, antibiotics, or respective controls. Wound size, bacterial virulence factors, and levels of proinflammatory cytokines (IL-1, IL-6, TNF-α) as well as anti-inflammatory and repair-related genes (IL-10, IGF-1, SMAD2, TGF-β) were evaluated through quantitative gene analysis. Paraprobiotic intervention had a major impact on wound healing and suppression of bacterial virulence factors. Quantitative gene expression analysis showed that proinflammatory cytokines (IL-1, IL-6, TNF-α) were significantly downregulated, while anti-inflammatory and tissue repair genes (IL-10, IGF-1, SMAD2, TGF-β) were upregulated in the paraprobiotic group compared to the control groups. Paraprobiotics possess strong immunomodulatory and regenerative properties that enhance wound repair, making them promising agents for safer and more effective management of infected burn wounds. The results support the development of natural therapeutic approaches to maximise patient outcomes in burn care.

Article.Title: Autotaxin induces fibrosis in lamina cribrosa cells in glaucoma
Article.Authors: O’Regan A.; Irnaten M.; Eivers S.; O’Callaghan J.; Wallace D.; O’Brien C.
Article.Abstract: Lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) and the enzyme that generates it, autotaxin, have been shown to play a role in fibrosis in the trabecular meshwork in glaucoma, contributing to increased intraocular pressure. We wished to investigate the role of LPA and autotaxin in fibrosis of the lamina cribrosa (LC) of the optic nerve head in glaucoma. LC cells from glaucoma patient donors (GLC) and normal controls (NLC) were cultured, and expression of autotaxin and LPA receptors were determined through real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR), western blotting and immunofluorescence. Autotaxin activity in cell media was measured via a phospholipase assay. GLC cells were treated with an autotaxin inhibitor S32826, and the rate of cell proliferation and ECM gene expression were assessed. GLC cells showed significantly increased autotaxin mRNA (3.84 ± 1.71 fold p < 0.05) and protein expression (1.54 ± 0.41 fold p < 0.05) compared to NLC. The LPA receptor LPA 3 was also significantly overexpressed (2.73 ± 0.23 fold p < 0.001). Treatment of GLC cells with S32826 significantly reduced autotaxin activity, cell proliferation and expression of ECM genes COL1A (0.51±0.06, p < 0.05) and FN1 (0.64±0.12, p < 0.05). Inhibition of autotaxin decreased cell proliferation and ECM production in LC cells, and therefore could be a potential target for fibrosis in the LC in glaucoma.

Article.Title: Marital satisfaction and parent-reported emotional competence in Chinese preschoolers: serial indirect associations through mindful parenting and parental involvement
Article.Authors: Wang T.; Qu H.; Wu P.; Xu Z.; Li M.; Luo M.
Article.Abstract: Guided by Belsky’s parenting process model, this pooled cross-sectional study examined a theory-ordered pattern of statistical associations linking marital satisfaction, mindful parenting, parental involvement, and parent-reported emotional competence. Participants were 5,303 married biological parents of kindergarten children in Hubei Province, China, most of whom were mothers. A latent-variable structural equation model adjusted for data-collection batch and relevant demographic characteristics; classroom-cluster-robust re-estimation was used to evaluate the nested recruitment structure. Marital satisfaction was positively associated with mindful parenting and parental involvement; mindful parenting and parental involvement were each positively associated with parent-reported emotional competence. The theory-ordered statistical indirect association through the serially specified parenting constructs was positive (β = 0.038, cluster-robust 95% CI [0.029, 0.046]), whereas the adjusted direct association between marital satisfaction and parent-reported emotional competence was nonsignificant. Covariance-equivalent directional specifications fit identically, indicating that temporal and causal ordering could not be established. Because all constructs were reported by the same parent at one time point, the findings describe theory-consistent statistical associations and do not show that one parenting process preceded another, transmitted an effect, or would improve the child outcome if changed. Longitudinal and multi-informant research is needed.

Article.Title: Physical activity and incident hypertension in relation to anthropometric and liver-related indices during 5-year follow-up in the Azar Cohort Study
Article.Authors: Haghshenas R.; Somi M.; Faramarzi E.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Hypertension (HTN) is a major global public health concern. This study examined the association between physical activity (PA) and incident HTN, focusing on the mediating roles of anthropometric (AI) and liver-related indices (LI) in the Azar cohort. Data from 11,754 adults without baseline HTN were analyzed. Fifteen anthropometric and nine liver-related indices were assessed using standard protocols. PA was measured via a validated questionnaire based on metabolic equivalent of task (MET). Generalized Structural Equation Modeling (GSEM) was applied to evaluate direct and indirect associations. Results Individuals with HTN were older and had higher anthropometric and liver-related measures, while PA levels were lower (P < 0.001). Higher PA was associated with a lower risk of HTN (RR = 0.91, 95% CI:0.89–0.94), whereas higher AI (RR = 1.92, 95% CI:1.81–1.99) and LI (RR = 1.21, 95% CI:1.19–1.23) were associated with a higher risk of HTN. AI and LI accounted for part of the observed PA–HTN association, with a stronger contribution from AI than LI (53.64% vs. 34.95%). After accounting for the mediators, the association between PA and HTN remained significant (RR = 0.94, 95% CI:0.91–0.96). The association remained significant after adjustment; each one-unit increase in MET was linked to a 6% lower HTN risk (RR = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.91–0.96). PA was inversely associated with HTN risk, with anthropometric factors accounting for a greater proportion of the observed association than liver-related factors. The partial mediation suggests that other factors may also contribute to this association.

Article.Title: Lymphocyte-predominant inflammation refines lung histopathology scoring in preclinical respiratory viral infection: support from deep learning analysis
Article.Authors: Seok S.; Kim H.; An H.; Lee Y.; Lee N.; Yoon G.; Kim J.; Lee H.; Yoo W.; Seong J.; Park J.
Article.Abstract: Respiratory viral infections such as influenza and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) remain major causes of morbidity and mortality. Although lung histopathology is a major endpoint in preclinical studies, conventional H&E-based grading primarily evaluates the extent of inflammatory-cell infiltration and may not distinguish progressive from resolving disease. Here, we investigated whether inflammatory-cell composition could refine lung histopathology assessment using convolutional neural network (CNN)-based analysis. In SARS-CoV-2 mouse cohorts, systemic disease severity was classified according to body-weight loss and splenic white-pulp atrophy. H&E-based inflammatory-cell infiltration scores and CNN-derived inflammatory-cell-rich areas did not fully correspond to systemic disease status in several infection and vaccine-challenge settings. In contrast, lesions associated with lower disease-severity or recovery-phase states were enriched in lymphocytes and CD8⁺ T cells, whereas higher disease-severity or lethal-phase lesions showed macrophage- and neutrophil-rich patterns. A two-step CNN workflow that detected inflammatory-cell-rich regions and subsequently classified them as recovery-like or lethal-like supported this composition-based distinction across independent SARS-CoV-2 cohorts. Similar lymphocyte- and CD8⁺ T-cell–enriched inflammatory patterns were also observed during recovery in influenza A infection. These findings support lymphocyte predominance as a practical histopathologic parameter that complements conventional inflammatory-cell infiltration scoring in murine respiratory viral infection models.

Article.Title: ECO-EDGE: joint DAG offloading and fabric routing in Multi-AP MEC via conic optimization
Article.Authors: Alymani M.; Almutairi A.; Alhayan F.; Alnori A.; Al-Dayil R.; NEMRI N.; Ebad S.
Article.Abstract: Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) enables low-latency services by migrating computational resources closer to end-users. However, as mobile workloads increasingly adopt complex Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) topologies, system performance is strongly affected by interdependent data shuffling across the inter-server fabric and synchronization constraints during uplink transmission. Existing models frequently neglect physical fabric capacity limits and decouple communication from computation, leading to inefficient energy usage and increased latency. In this paper, we propose a coupled Mixed-Integer Non-Linear Programming (MINLP) formulation that jointly optimizes multi-AP association, task placement, Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS), and explicit inter-server routing under per-application deadline constraints. To address the inherent non-convexity and combinatorial complexity of the joint problem, we introduce the ECO-EDGE framework. ECO-EDGE decomposes the original MINLP using a Block Coordinate Descent (BCD) architecture and solves relaxed subproblems via tailored convexification techniques, including McCormick-based convex envelopes for bilinear placement products, a “Bits-per-RB” formulation that maps communication constraints into exponential cones, and power- and rotated second-order cone representations for computation and fabric delay modeling. The resulting relaxed BCD scheme exhibits monotonic objective decrease under exact block solution, while deterministic rounding and topological list-scheduling are applied to recover feasible schedules, which are subsequently verified for deadline satisfaction. Simulation results in dense multi-AP deployments show that ECO-EDGE reduces total system energy by up to \(81.8\%\) compared to a Local-Only baseline and achieves an empirical deadline satisfaction rate of \(97.9\%\) , outperforming heuristic, fabric-oblivious, and disjoint optimization baselines.

Article.Title: Intelligent adaptive energy management framework for hybrid solar-grid EV fast-charging stations with energy storage and time-based demand response optimization
Article.Authors: Govindasamy D.; Rathinam R.; Zneid B.; Bereznychenko V.; Touti E.
Article.Abstract: The rapid expansion of electric vehicle (EVs) is significantly increasing pressure on the conventional electrical grid and introducing new challenges in load management, peak demand, and grid stability. Conventional grid systems, dependent on fossil fuel-based generation, contribute to greenhouse gas emissions and limit the environmental benefits of EV adoption. Although several studies have integrated photovoltaic (PV) systems with EV charging networks, most have not addressed real-time coordination between multiple power sources, time-of-use (ToU) pricing, and dynamic demand response (DR). To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes an Intelligent Adaptive Energy Management Framework (IAEMF) for a 1 MW hybrid solar-grid EV DC fast-charging station equipped with a 600-kWh energy storage system (ESS). The framework incorporates a time-adaptive multi-mode control algorithm that dynamically allocates power among PV generation, ESS, and the utility grid based on irradiance, electricity pricing, and load demand. The proposed system supports five operational modes PV-to-ESS, PV-to-EV, Grid-to-EV, ESS-to-EV, and PV-to-Grid facilitating fully bidirectional energy exchange across the DC bus. A variable-step Perturb and Observe (P&O) MPPT algorithm is implemented to maximize solar energy extraction, while the adaptive allocation strategy continuously adjusts PV distribution factors according to ESS state-of-charge (SOC) and demand variations. Time-of-use (ToU) pricing enables cost-effective energy management by shifting grid charging to off-peak periods and the demand response (DR) enables priority-based scheduling during peak periods by balancing user urgency, PV utilization, and grid cost simultaneously. MATLAB/Simulink simulations demonstrate that the proposed IAEMF achieves 87.8% renewable energy utilization, a grid export-to-import ratio of 4.2:1, and 71.8% average daily solar contribution, while maintaining stable DC bus voltage and efficient ESS utilization. Furthermore, the proposed system achieves CO₂ emission reduction of 659.5 tonnes/year by minimizing through grid imports. In addition, the total PV generation-based CO₂ offset reaches 1,853 tonnes per year. The results validate that the proposed hybrid architecture provides a scalable and sustainable solution for next-generation EV fast-charging infrastructure.

Article.Title: Optimization of UV-C irradiation time for biologically treated saline wastewater using artificial neural networks and a hybrid multi-criteria decision-making framework
Article.Authors: Omidvar M.; Farahbod F.
Article.Abstract: Biologically treated saline industrial wastewater may still contain residual organic matter, nutrients, petroleum hydrocarbons, and dissolved constituents that limit the quality and potential reuse of the treated effluent. Ultraviolet-C (UV-C) irradiation is a chemical-free polishing technology with potential for further improving effluent quality; however, its treatment performance depends strongly on irradiation time, and excessive exposure may increase energy consumption without providing proportional improvements. Moreover, optimization based on a single water-quality parameter cannot adequately represent the simultaneous changes and trade-offs among multiple effluent-quality indicators. Existing approaches commonly evaluate UV treatment using individual quality parameters or conventional statistical analyses, while artificial neural networks provide prediction capability but have limited interpretability for selecting an operating condition. Conversely, multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) approaches can support transparent optimization but are generally restricted to experimentally investigated conditions. Therefore, an integrated framework that combines experimental UV-C treatment, predictive modeling, and interpretable multi-criteria optimization is required for systematic determination of the irradiation time. This study aimed to experimentally investigate the effect of UV-C irradiation time on biologically treated saline industrial wastewater and to develop an integrated ANN–MCDM framework for predicting wastewater-quality responses, identifying influential quality parameters, and determining the optimum irradiation condition. A laboratory-scale reactor equipped with a 30 W low-pressure mercury lamp emitting at 254 nm was employed at irradiation times of 40–320 s. Prior to irradiation, 4.8 g of dry ice was used for pH conditioning. Nine wastewater-quality parameters, namely COD, BOD, phosphate, nitrate, dissolved organic carbon (DOC), total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH), turbidity, total dissolved solids (TDS), and pH, were evaluated. A 64–32–16–9 multilayer perceptron ANN was developed for simultaneous prediction of the normalized quality parameters. In parallel, Min–Max normalization, K-Means clustering, principal component analysis (PCA), a Composite Wastewater Quality Index (CWQI), TOPSIS, and sensitivity analysis were integrated to classify treatment regimes, determine parameter weights, evaluate overall treatment quality, rank irradiation times, and identify the most influential quality indicators. Wastewater quality generally improved with increasing irradiation time, with the most pronounced overall improvement occurring between 240 and 280 s, followed by a saturation tendency at longer exposure. The integrated analysis identified 280 s as the optimum irradiation time , yielding a maximum CWQI of 0.977 and a TOPSIS score of 0.966 . At this condition, COD and BOD reductions reached approximately 41.1% and 17.5% , respectively, while improvements were also observed in DOC, TPH, phosphate, nitrate, turbidity, and TDS. At 320 s, the CWQI and TOPSIS score decreased to 0.925 and 0.894 , respectively, indicating that prolonged irradiation did not provide a corresponding improvement in overall treatment performance. PCA identified phosphate as the most influential parameter, with a normalized weight of 0.168 , followed by COD ( 0.149 ), DOC ( 0.139 ), and BOD ( 0.125 ). The sensitivity analysis produced the same parameter-importance sequence. The ANN achieved an average test RMSE of approximately 0.12 on the normalized scale and provided predictions for irradiation times not explicitly included in the experimental dataset. The ANN and hybrid MCDM approaches provide complementary capabilities: the ANN enables simultaneous nonlinear prediction at untested irradiation times, whereas the hybrid framework provides greater mathematical transparency through clustering, objective weighting, composite quality assessment, ranking, and sensitivity analysis. The agreement between CWQI and TOPSIS in identifying 280 s demonstrates consistency between two independent multi-criteria evaluation approaches. From a practical perspective, the results indicate that extending irradiation beyond the optimum does not necessarily improve overall effluent quality and may increase irradiation time and associated energy demand without proportional treatment benefits. The proposed integration of UV-C polishing, ANN-based prediction, and an interpretable hybrid MCDM framework provides a systematic approach for evaluating and optimizing biologically treated saline industrial wastewater. The methodology enables simultaneous consideration of multiple water-quality parameters while retaining predictive capability for untested operating conditions. The identified optimum of 280 s provides a data-driven operating condition for the investigated laboratory system and establishes a basis for further studies involving repeated experiments, uncertainty analysis, explicit UV fluence measurements, microbial inactivation, and scale-up toward practical wastewater reuse applications.

Article.Title: Prioritizing climate-resilient housing recovery in conflict-affected Yemen: a district-level MCDA and uncertainty framework
Article.Authors: Al-Azazi S.; Alezi K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Yemen’s housing recovery requires choices among districts where flood exposure, conflict, displacement and humanitarian need overlap. This study develops a district-level multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) framework to identify districts that remain high priorities for early climate-resilient housing recovery under alternative assumptions. The model combines seven dimensions: flood hazard, human exposure, built exposure, climate stress, conflict fragility, displacement pressure and humanitarian severity. Four weighting scenarios are tested, and Monte Carlo perturbation examines rank stability when normalized inputs and scenario weights vary. The model does not estimate direct housing damage; it screens districts under combined physical and social pressures and compares the national ranking with heterogeneous city-level evidence. The highest-ranked districts are Ma’rib, Ma’rib City, Sirwah, Al Marawi’ah, Khur Maksar, Ad Durayhimi, Tuban and Bani Sa’d. Flood-gate, missing-data, internal-weight and sparse-RDT ablation tests preserve the leading pattern, although uncertainty increases near selection thresholds. The framework provides a transparent national screening tool for recovery sequencing, subject to local engineering assessment and stakeholder validation before implementation.

Article.Title: Device-assisted calf-raise training combining high-speed and eccentric exercises improves gait speed in older adults
Article.Authors: Kanayama A.; Ueba R.; Yamamoto S.; Kinoshita S.; Nagao H.; Yano Y.; Kamimukai C.; Doma K.; Iwata A.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Plantar flexors are critical for mobility in older adults. Although movement velocity contributes to gait performance in addition to strength, few interventions target both plantar flexor strength and velocity. To address this gap, we developed a novel device to support a program incorporating both high-speed and eccentric plantar-flexor exercises and examined whether this device-assisted program improves plantar flexion strength, movement velocity, and gait speed. In a nonrandomized controlled trial, 40 older adults were allocated to either a training group ( n = 20) or a control group ( n = 20). The training group undertook a 10-week calf-raise program using a custom-built device, whereas the control group continued usual activities. The program was performed twice daily, 5 days per week, and included high-speed calf-raises (20 repetitions) and eccentric calf-raises (30 repetitions). Of the 19 participants who initiated the intervention, 18 completed the program (retention rate, 94.7%), and all achieved the prescribed target dose (adherence, 100%). Compared with controls, the training group showed greater improvements in gait speed (+ 0.17 m/s) and plantar flexion strength (+ 7.5 kgf) and movement velocity (+ 104.9 °/s). These findings suggest that device-assisted calf-raise training may improve plantar flexor function and gait performance in older adults. Trial registration: UMIN-CTR, UMIN000052504; 15/10/2023.

Article.Title: High-pressure processing and thermal pasteurization of blueberry purée-based baby food differentially modulate polyphenol bioaccessibility and intestinal cell responses
Article.Authors: Mazurkiewicz B.; Matusiewicz M.; Wojcik-Gront E.; Krucon T.; Uhrynowski W.; Jeznach N.; Jaworski S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Proper processing of baby foods, ensuring both safety and the highest possible nutrient retention and bioaccessibility, is of particular importance for the health and development of infants and young children. In this study, blueberry purée-based baby food was subjected to conventional thermal pasteurization (TP) and high-pressure processing (HPP) at moderate temperature, and their effects on sensory quality and the availability of bioactive compounds were compared. Polyphenol stability and antioxidant bioaccessibility were evaluated during storage and simulated gastrointestinal digestion, while intestinal cell responses and prebiotic-related activity were assessed separately. HPP-treated purées showed significantly higher phenolic bioaccessibility, whereas differences in antioxidant bioaccessibility and anthocyanin recovery between treatments were not statistically significant. Caco-2 cell viability varied with treatment and incubation time, whereas intracellular reactive oxygen species levels were not significantly affected by processing treatment and decreased with incubation time. The effects of both preservation methods on microbial growth were dependent on bacterial group and incubation time. Positive PAS values were observed for Lactobacillus after both 24 and 48 h, whereas Bifidobacterium did not show a selective growth advantage over Enterobacteriaceae under the applied experimental conditions. Short-chain fatty acids remained below the detection threshold in the fermented purée samples and the inulin control, although several unsaturated fatty acids were quantifiable after fermentation in both processed purées. These results demonstrate that HPP and thermal pasteurization differentially modulate the functional properties of blueberry purée-based baby food and highlight the importance of preservation strategy selection in the development of foods intended for sensitive consumer groups.

Article.Title: Tribological performance of PTFE/polyimide pulp/GCNT composites
Article.Authors: Zhou J.; Sun X.; Zhao D.; Si C.; Wu S.
Article.Abstract: Abstract Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) is widely used as a solid lubricant but suffers from poor wear resistance, limiting its application in demanding mechanical components. In this study, PTFE-based composites reinforced with polyimide (PI) pulp and graphitized carbon nanotubes (GCNTs) were prepared via a cold-press sintering process. The tribological properties were evaluated under different loads (2 N and 10 N) and frequencies (1 Hz and 4 Hz) using a ball-on-disk tribometer. The results show that the composite with 5 wt% PI pulp and 1 wt% GCNT (designated as #3) exhibits the best overall performance. At 2 N and 1 Hz, its coefficient of friction (COF) reaches 0.025, which is 69.3% lower than that of pure PTFE. Meanwhile, the wear rate is reduced by up to 75% under 10 N and 4 Hz. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) analyses indicate that the improved tribological performance is mainly attributed to the formation of a continuous and uniform transfer film on the counterface. PI pulp constructs a load-bearing fibrous network that enhances mechanical strength, while GCNTs promote the adhesion and stability of the transfer film, effectively changing the sliding contact from composite–steel to film–steel and reducing both friction and wear. This work offers a practical route for developing PTFE-based self-lubricating composites with balanced mechanical and tribological properties.

Article.Title: Higher plasma oleic acid is associated with slower progression from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer’s disease in men and women
Article.Authors: Dakterzada F.; Jové M.; Cantero J.; Mota-Martorell N.; Pamplona R.; Piñol-Ripoll G.
Article.Abstract: The contribution of sex differences in lipid metabolism to the pathophysiology of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) remains under Investigation. This study aimed to investigate sex-stratified associations of fatty acid (FA) profiles in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and plasma across the AD continuum, and their associations with AD pathology and progression. FA profiles were analyzed in 198 CSF and 286 plasma samples from AD, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and control subjects using GC-FID. The MCI subjects were followed up for 58 (± 12.5) months. Analysis of FA profiles of control subjects revealed minor sex differences in both CSF and plasma biofluids. In men, a higher CSF anti-inflammatory index was associated with lower odds of AD than MCI (OR = 0.025), whereas higher CSF α-linolenic acid (C18:3n-3) levels were associated with higher odds of AD (OR = 2.826). In women, higher CSF levels of palmitoleic acid (C16:1n-7) were associated with lower odds of amyloid-β (Aβ) positivity (OR = 0.500). Higher plasma oleic acid (C18:1n-9) levels were associated with lower odds of MCI-to-AD progression in men (OR = 0.666) and a longer time to progression in women (HR = 0.404). Our results suggest that higher plasma oleic acid levels were associated with slower disease progression in both men and women, whereas higher CSF anti-inflammatory index and α-linolenic acid were associated with AD diagnosis in men. These findings may reflect differences in lipid metabolism associated with AD across men and women, although reverse causation and residual confounding cannot be excluded.

Article.Title: Nature-inspired antenna design using hybrid ANN and Bayesian optimization techniques for biomedical applications
Article.Authors: Sharma M.; Jhajharia T.; Rawat S.; Saraswat K.
Article.Abstract: Abstract This paper is presenting a systematic approach for designing of antenna resonating at 3.18 GHz with an impedance bandwidth of 3.10–3.285 GHz which lies at the lower edge of the UWB spectrum used in IEEE 802.15.6-based Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) research. The proposed compact antenna becomes more suitable for WBAN-assisted healthcare monitoring and microwave biomedical sensing applications. The antenna designing is covered in two sections. First one deals with the non-linear regression analysis with correlation analysis to achieve final design for patch. The surrogate modelling for reflection coefficient parameter for complete 50 samples of the patch design is presented and compared with other techniques. The non-linear regression based surrogate modelling along with correlation analysis by Pearson and Spearman techniques helps in making prediction of the patch design structure by selecting most featured and significant design parameters. The second section caters the process of ‘Artificial Neural Network (ANN)’ modelling with optimization techniques to achieve optimized design of ‘Defected Ground Structure (DGS)’ structure. The optimization is performed by ‘Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II)’, Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO)’, ‘Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO)’, and ‘Bayesian Optimization using Gaussian Process Regression (BO + GPR)’ techniques. The optimized antenna having size of $$0.2968 {\lambda}_{0} \text{m}\text{m} \times 0.318 {\lambda}_{0} \text{m}\text{m}$$ at resonant frequency of 3.18 GHz, is fabricated on FR-4 substrate. The excellent agreement is observed between simulated results and practical results which confirms the robustness of the proposed systematic approach for the antenna designing and making it suitable for biomedical application.
